On the negative side, two different couples staying on my floor (4th) decided to have a fight among themselves in the hallway between 1230-1am. The night before, my colleague who stayed at the hotel said that the fire alarm malfunctioned in the hotel and caused a periodic beep almost the entire night. Also, the shades are not great in the room and let in a lot of light in the early morning. To top it all off, they charge $7 to park your car in a lot with hundreds of extra spaces. Not joking.

“Great stay” I was in town for a convention during this stay. I stayed a total of 4 nights. The staff was friendly througout my stay. I was always greeted with "have a nice day" or "have a good night". My room was spacious but the bathroom was small. I ordered room service one night and the food was delivered promptly and tasted good. I only had an issue one evening with the maid service. I arrived back to the hotel one night and the bathroom was not cleaned and the towels were not replaced. Aside from that incident, I had a fine stay.

“Good location great staff” This hotel is close to the White House, the Mall, and a couple of blocks from the Metro. The staff all went out of their way to make our stay a pleasure! We will be staying here on our next trip to DC.

“2nd time staying at lucerne” We have stayed twice at the Lucerne. Both times were great. the 1st time we had a suite with pull out sofa. good for a small family since it gives people space. the frig was great since we go to H & H for bagels and get lox & cream cheese at zabars for breakfast. Just got back, booked a room over the internet for a queen (least expensive) but wanted 2 beds. got there and just asked for 2 beds and it was no problem. great location on UWSide. We have stayed at excelsior, empire, and On the Ave and choose Lucerne. But with a big crowd we always rent apartments on UWS. It is a neighborhood, good restaurants, and a real feel for New York. Never would stay anywhere else but the Upper West Side.

“Beautiful hotel in great location” We unfortunately arrived right at check-in (3 p.m.) and it was very very slow. The staff was friendly, though, and I think the issue was because a few people had problems with their rooms (room type they wanted not available, etc.). Our room was on the 8th floor and had no view. It was stylishly decorated and spacious, especially by NYC standards. There were motion-sensor lights under the bedside tables, which became rather annoying pretty quickly. One didn't seem to be working properly and never turned off so we just unplugged it. This feature is much more convenient in the bathroom. I loved the full-length mirror inside the closet; wish more hotels had these. The rate for our room itself was pretty reasonable, but parking is outrageous at $65/day. There are plenty of much cheaper garages within walking distance. There was also a $15/day fee for wi-fi access which is a bit steep... and room service prices were ridiculous. Again, there are plenty of nice restaurants in the area with much more reasonable prices.

“Decent place to stay” The physical location isn't the best - it's surrounded by wig shops and hair extension palaces. During the day, there were several people we passed on the way to the subway who made us feel a little anxious. At one point, we had to walk through a pretty intense argument. The hotel itself was fine. We arrived several hours before check-in and they stored our bags at no extra cost. The NWRQ line is only one block away, which was very convenient. Our room had two twin beds and was very comfortable. There were three of us total in the room and while it got slightly crowded at times, I really can't complain. The best part was probably the very large, very nice bathroom. As others have mentioned, there is a continental breakfast on the 4th floor in a very small room. Every time we visited, there were a ton of people standing around. Rather than fight the crowd, we took the breakfast back to our room. They served several types of donuts, bagels, and fruit, as well as juice and coffee. The doormen were extremely helpful during our stay, and patiently answered our many questions and gave recommendations when we asked.

“Loved it-” I absolutely loved this hotel. It was really cute. I was given an upgrade to one of the suites and that was really wonderful, I loved the large jacuzzi, and the soft comfortable couch. I also ate at the Grand Cafe next door and the Mason Cafe around the block and both restaurants were incredible. The location is great, walking distances to the Moscone (about 10 minutes) and tons of nearby shopping, bars, restaurants.... Christine- the front desk manager was very helpful with helping me with my logistics. The entire staff was friendly and polite. I can't wait to continue staying at Kimpton Hotels!

“comfortable modern rooms, average rates, nice staff, near supermarket” I had stayed at a pricer hotel for a conference downtown but decide to try something less expensive for the remainder. I had the King room which included a sofa, frig, nice work desk, etc. It was very comfortable. I liked that the supermarket was within walking distance. Also, the shuttle took me to the transit center where I was able to take the metro train downtown. Thus eliminating the cost of parking and the traffic. The bistro menu is very limited in selection but the food wasn't bad. There are resturants in the are that the shuttle can take you to also. I don't know if they have a swimming pool because I didn't use it but there was a fitness room.

“Jeckyl and Hyde experience!” Stayed at this iconic hotel for four nights at the end of August. The hotel is beautiful and the communal areas are maintained to a very high standard as of course are the rooms. My only moan is because it is the hotels low season that over the weekend of my visit the hotel was absolutely packed with families and groups there for the weekender special deal. As a consequence the pool areas were packed to the rafters and any sense one had that they were staying at an exclusive beautiful hotel quickly evaporated. It was more like staying at Butlins). This sense was further underlined when a significant delegation of tattooists arrived to commence their conference. Lol.

“Good value for the $” Very nice, clean hotel that must have been recently renovated. Great location, exception for being right next to the L train (very loud). That's the biggest negative. Other than that, excellent service. Paid $171/night for a suite on the concierge level. Well worth the money.

“Extraordinarily noisy rooms, mediocre service.” I was really surprised by my experience at the Palomar DC given the TA ratings. I'm a frequent business traveler and stay at a lot of Kimpton hotels, and my experience has generally been that the Palomars are the nicest among the Kimpton properties. Unfortunately, not so this time. I'll preface this by saying that I had a cold when I was staying at this hotel--so while I'm not someone who's generally hypersensitive about hotel noise, I guess it's possible I may have been a bit more noise-sensitive than usual. In any case, I really needed to get a good night of sleep. I checked into my spacious room on a middle floor and was initially pleased--it was clean, in good condition, and attractively furnished. However, when I returned from an evening meeting I was unhappy to find that there was an intermittent loud banging noise (like someone in the adjacent room nailing something into the wall) every few minutes. I called the front desk, and they said there wasn't any maintenance happening on that floor and they didn't know what the noise was. So they moved me to a room on the 2nd floor. The move was handled poorly by the bellman they sent (who disappeared for >20 minutes with the keys) and was an inconvenience--I would have been much better off if they'd just given me the keys and let me move myself. So there I was, in my new room on the 2nd floor. The room was in fact practically at ground level, facing the sidewalk, and there was significant street noise. On top of that, people in the hallway quite literally sounded like they were in my room and speaking at high volume. On top of *that*, there was a frequent sound from overhead like a chair being scraped loudly across a floor. I sat there trying to convince myself that the noise wasn't so bad because frankly, I was embarrassed to complain again--but it was that bad. So I called the front desk again. They were not particularly apologetic for all the inconvenience, but did move me to a corner room on a high floor (I insisted on moving myself this time). That room had a poor layout with an extremely cramped bathroom, but it was (finally!) a quiet room and I was able to sleep. I previously had a fabulous stay at the Hotel Monaco, another DC Kimpton hotel, and already have plans to stay there again. However, I won't be visiting the Palomar DC again despite my frequent DC visits. Disappointing experience.

“Flawless Stay!” My compliments to Marriott for such a well-run hotel. Every staff member we encountered was friendly and helpful. Check in/out and the valet parking service were very efficient. Evening service in the bar and breakfast both easily met expectations. The room was extremely clean and well-appointed, though I do agree with a previous reviewer that I expected it to be just a tad more upscale as a 'JW' property. The central Cherry Creek location was ideal for walking to nearby restaurants and shopping (we especially liked dinner at North, just half a block away). I do think it's a little pricey ($300/night), but we wanted to stay in Cherry Creek and it's by far the best neighborhood option (and perhaps the best overall Denver option). We'd go back without hesitation.
“立地がよいです” タイムズスクエアから歩いて10分以内です。部屋も清潔です。朝食はバイキングですが、食事の内容は満足のいく品揃えというわけではなく、まあまあですが、あまり期待しないほうが良いです。食事を取る場所がとても狭く、混んでいて座る場所に苦労して食事を楽しむ余裕は無かったです。日曜にチェックインしたのですが、週末は安くなるのか、格安でした。

“All around great experience” The Fairmont Olympic was a great experience for our family. From the helpful valet parking attendants, concierge, check-in staff, luggage valet to restaurant staff - we were greeted with smiles and given wonderful service. We stayed in a 2 bedroom suite that was large and beautiful - lots of space for everybody. The yellow hallways and bright rooms are always welcome in the often cloudy Seattle. The hotel is in walking distance of anything you need to see in Seattle - or a short cab ride. The dining room is one of the most beautiful ones I have ever seen - and the food matched its beauty. The Fairmont is a large hotel - but provides all you need to make Seattle a fun place to visit.

“What else can I say?” I have to write about our stay at the Salisbury Hotel even though many others have written great reviews and rated this hotel very fairly and favorably. I stayed over our spring break (Apr 13-18) with 2 teenagers and had a 1 bedroom suite. I booked it after spotting the $173/night on hotels.com. I dropped a previously booked hotel (Radio city apartments) in favor of this one due to price. Sure this hotel is old (70 years) with lots of character, but we got a lot for the money-2 double beds with a pull-out couch, very large living area and kitchen, microwave, refrigerator, great location, clean and comfy overall. Our hotel requirements were 3 beds, in order that we could all sleep well, and a kitchen to help us save money on food, and great location. The beds were firm with very nice sheets on them and my son was thrilled to have the whole living room to himself along with a very large flat-screened TV. The furniture looked new in the living room as well as the carpet. As noted in previous reviews, one elevator was out for most of our stay. You can take the freight elevator if you'd like a real flavor of old New York, which we used exclusively since it was by our room. When checking in I asked for a rear room and was given an end room-long and skinny with the living room at the street and the bedroom at the rear. The bedroom was quiet, but the front was noisier with the street noise. We did not try the hotel breakfast since we went to the store (Morton Williams Marketplace) a block and a half west to get supplies. They have fresh produce, groceries, a deli, pizzeria, and a hot and cold buffet. We saved lots of time and money by eating breakfast in the room each day. We usually stopped somewhere nice for lunch and then had soup or leftovers for dinner. Our total food/restaurant bill for the 3 of us was $400 for 6 days. We had Angelo's pizza delivered which was very good, Tony's di Napoli by Time's Square served family style and was a very fair price for great food, Lansky's Deli was a great lunch place with local flavor (try the mazza ball soup). Hated Maxie's by Times Square-very expensive, very poor service, poor food. We enjoyed all the the city had to offer especially the plays. We had decided to see Avenue Q, but the tickets for many plays are offering 40% off on broadwaybox.com so we also saw Mama Mia and 39 Steps. All were great plays and we had a really wonderful time at them all. The hotel is so close to the subway you can get anywhere quickly with minimal walking if you prefer. We also took the bus easily to the UN (M104, no transfers needed). Don't let cost slow you down from visiting this great city. Our hotel was a real deal that fit our requirements perfectly, our flight from Detroit to LGA was $135 roundtrip, our food costs were reasonable with very little effort on our part to minimize them, and our entertainment costs were low compared to other times I have visited. We had a fabulous time, and I would highly recommend this hotel and a visit to the Big Apple.

“Waste of time - awful place” The Standard looks like it was decorated at kmart -- all plastic and not really clean. It was noisy, really odd and missing essentials that business travelers need. The hotel staff in general portray an attitude that they are better than their guests. Wake up call was 20 minutes late without an apology. The ironing board was a desk top (hard to iron the suit), the bathroom was just hard to deal with (no kleenex, not sparkling clean tile, no place to put your toothbrush). The bedroom was decorated in inexpensive grey carpet and walls were blemished. The all around step to the bed (without box spring and low to the ground) was easy to trip on (as I did at least twice). I quickly checked out after one night and moved to a more suitable hotel for business travelers.

“Good Location for Fishermans Wharf” We have stayed here on a number of occasions, we use the hotel only as a base and our days normally start early and finish late after having been sightseeing and then visited some of the restaurants and bars. As such we view the hotel as being clean and the hotel service is professional although at time the check in areas can be very busy. We have not eaten in the restaurant (there a loads of other options close by). The hotel is in a good location for the F-Line and the two cable car routes, although we have found that although not a scenic the No. 30 bus stops outside the hotel and is considerably quicker (at busy times) to be able to get into Union Square.

“Hotel is a must for convention center events!” The Omni Dallas was much more than I expected. I've stayed in other Omnis, but this one was far above the others. My 16-year old daughter and I were in town for a volleyball tournament at the Convention Center, so there were A LOT of people in town for the weekend. The location was so convenient- the hotel is connected by a skybridge on the 2nd floor- which made our lives so much easier. And the rooms were full of little surprises (and not the kind that scurry on the floor). There was a TV built into the mirror in the bathroom; a motion-activated light came on under the bedside table to illuminate the floor; the TV was hidden behind two sliding panel mirrors; beds were VERY comfortable; and we had our own Keurig coffee maker, with all the supplies, as well as a safe and refrigerator. The group rate was a little higher than we usually pay ($159/night), but the convenience was worth it. They offer both valet ($19/night) and self ($15/night) parking. I valeted since it was only a few more dollars (not counting all the tips!), and the service was excellent. They even allowed us to leave our car after we checked out, which was so helpful since the tournament wasn't over until after 2:00 pm. The pool was very cool (located on the 4th floor) and at night the outside of the hotel is a big light show! I didn't eat at any of the restaurants, but did visit The Owner's Box (Sports Bar) one night. It's full of TVs and they serve a great Bloody Mary; but if you don't like a lot of noise, I'd skip it.

“OK for Day or Short Stay” We spent a few hours to catch up on sleep before our next flight, and the Travelodge was convenient . Interesting, different 60s style building with traditional motel layout. Rooms not flash but OK. Close to runway so not overly quiet. Can take the blue bus to Santa Monica, or private bus to Manhattan Beach if you have time for a quick look, or take blue bus to rapid train station if you want to go further afield, but it is not really a good location to be based for a few days. Overall fine for a brief stopover between flights but wouldnt stay for any length of time.

“May Trip to Seattle” We stayed at the W for two nights in late May 2012. It's a nice hotel in a good location. The light rail stop is about a block away (down a steep hill), and it's convenient to the monorail and pike place as well. If you're going to chinatown, a baseball or football game or the space needle this is a convenient hotel. The staff was friendly, but didn't go out of their way to help or provide advice. The bellman did go up quickly to get our luggage, that was the one bright spot on service. The room was nice and about what you'd expect for a W. The view wasn't great, but it wasn't the worst either. One thing to keep in mind is that parking is $37 per night. If you have a car and are taking the ferry to Bainbridge or Bremerton it's very convenient for that too since the ferry dock is just a few blocks away. We would stay here again if coming to Seatlle as it was a good location with a comfortable room.

“Nice Hotel Near Seattle Hospitals” Nice, clean, attractive hotel near several Seattle hospitals. I had appointments at Virginia Mason and this was very convenient. You can either walk or talk their free shuttle. I think that the shuttle is a great touch and helps give guests reasonable access to downtown. However, this is definitely not what I would call a downtown hotel. There is not much in the immediate area except medical facilities and the Seattle University. Rooms are well furnished and reasonably sized. The free internet is a great touch. Room service is from Jimmy's on Broadway which was pretty good but expensive. Please note that they add a service charge and an 18% gratuity but still have a spot for tip on the bill. I always hate that as it seems a sneaky way to get a double tip. I was able to get the room for $137/nt which seemed very reasonable for hotels in that area. Based on reviews, this appears to be the best hotel in the area. I would stay again if I unfortunately have to visit the hospitals.

“Hotel Lobby, rooms, and staff are all warm and inviting!” Our entrance through the front door was a pleasant welcome by the door staff, Front desk staff were friendly, Concierge on staff Konni Godley was pleasant, warm, and friendly. She asked us what brought us to the Palomar, I replied, for an Adult time out! She advised of the events that were in the area and on the property. We went out with friends of our to dinner nearby, and was suprised by a bottle of red wine and sweat treats at bedside. The entire hotel welcomes you, either by sight, touch, sound. You have a sense of being very comfortable in your own skin, and with the one you love. Found out through a source of mine that Konni was recently voted "Concierge of the Year" by her fellow concierge's in the Dallas area. What an honor to be served by such a geniune person. When you arrive, don't forget to ask for Konni, she will make you feel like you never left home, which in turn makes you never want to leave the hotel.
“Have stayed twice and would return” This is a very nice hotel, with a solid restaurant and bar on-sight. It's well-lit, appointed and staffed with nice people. This is B+/A- property.

“Great rooms, boring restaurants” I stayed in this hotel recently, and was very impressed by the front lobby and ballrooms. My room was also quite pleasant. But the restaurants and registration areas were strangely bland and formulaic. This is undoubtedly due to the convention nature of the hotel, but I was still disappointed to note that such an obviously historic hotel was lacking any distinctive bars and restaurants. With that said, this is a very clean and attractive hotel with a great staff. Upper level rooms have amazing views of both the lake and city. This is an excellent choice for either convention or business travel.

“Nice hotel and ok location” It is what I would expect of a St Regis hotel and this was no different. The room was of a very good size and the quality of the facilities also quite good. However, I do have some recommendations to warn you about if you are staying at this property. 1. If when you check be sure to ask which side of the buiding you are on. If you are on the Mission side the amount of noise which bounces off this highrise and the building across the street is loud and constant and it feels as if your window was left open. 2. We were in room 709 and again ask where your room is and avoid any room ending in 09 because that is where the service elevator is and where all the staff come in and out for any flor service including butlers. The service door from that elevator was adjacent to our door and the constant opening and closing and slamming of the door never stopped. I called downstairs to ask that at least have the staff softly close the door when going in and out. They did but the talking and trays and noise still made it sound as if my door was wide open to the hallway. Other than that it was a nice room and good hotel.

“Nice Older Hotel in Great Location” The room was clean, extra-large and very comfortable. Their staff is very pleasant and helpful; the breakfast deal is terrific; we had a great stay. Our room was on the front of the hotel and, even though we were on the 11th floor, it was a little noisy but it didn't prevent us from getting a good night's sleep.
“Charming and easy.” Great find in Wall Street area. Walk to Bankruptcy Court. Nice bar. Reasonably priced restaurant.

“Perfect Location” Stayed at the Holiday Inn Washington DC for a week in late July, As other posts have said it is very easy to get to by subway, the L'Enfant Plaza station runs 5/6 routes. Close to the mall and all the Smithsonian museums.. Yes, eating can be a challenge at night, but after a full day a quick dinner is sometimes all we wanted. Rooms were great, although the train tracks were behind the noise did not bother us and was minimal. There is a full service Starbucks in the building, which was a great plus for our famil. Would recommend to anyone who wants to be close to all the action of DC, and a block walk to the subway for everything else outside of the mall area.

“部屋は広かったです” 今回のニューヨーク旅行では、アンダズのウォール・ストリートとフィフス・アベニューに宿泊しました。ハイアットのポイントを使って、ANDAZ SUITEに無料アップグレード。フィフス・アベニューがかなり洗練されていることもあり、ウォール・ストリートの部屋には少々野暮ったい印象を受けました。ただし、ウォール・ストリートの方が部屋は広かったです。シャワー・スペースの排水が悪く、水が浴室の外まであふれ出るのには閉口しましたが、その点以外は素晴らしい部屋でした。周辺には観光スポットが多くありますが、フィフス・アベニューの方が買い物には便利です。アーリー・チェックインを希望してましたが、残念ながらチェックインできたのは3時半ごろでした。

“Updated, yet still rough around the edges.” This hotel is nice - simply put. Getting there isn't 'easy' as you have to U-Turn when coming in off the interstate. The front desk staff is polite, friendly, and is more than accommodating. The rooms are in decent shape, but a little rough around the edges - however they are clean. Well appointed and spacious, they provide enough space to relax and work. The beds aren't the best - but they aren't the worst either, a little on the hard side. My favorite feature had to be the king size pillows on the king size beds. The pillows were great and the linens were soft and fresh. I stayed three nights and had no problems until the final night. I returned to my room around 5:45 and the room was around 75 degrees. Considering the temperature outside was 100+ with the heat index, I wasn't ready for the temperature to increase more than it had already. I had even closed all of the curtains before I left to assure the heat didn't creep in the room while I was going - but alas, I had no way to plan around mechanical issues. The air coming from the A/C unit wasn't chilled - so I checked the thermostat and didn't see anything incorrect. So I called the front desk. After about 10 minute a less than friendly maintenance employee arrived to assess that the thermostat wasn't set correctly, and sure enough - cool air streamed from the unit... for the next 15 minutes. Then the temperature in the room began to climb again. It was 82 when I woke up soaking wet in the middle of the night, and then freezing when I woke up when the alarm clock when off. So I'm not exactly sure what the problem with the unit was - but it definitely wasn't functioning properly, of that I am sure. After three nights I am pretty sure I would definitely return to this hotel, I enjoyed the stay - and the property was up to par on nearly all accounts.

“perfectly fine hotel” arrived for 4 day visit to chicago with my 19 yr old daughter and good friend. stayed in a suite, very decent price, on 24th floor. room was fine for 3 of us. hotel staff were friendly and accomodating. perfect location for shopping or sight seeing. would certainly stay here again for location and price alone. we signed up to be a "select" omni member before our stay and we got free coffee in the morning plus papers as well as free wifi. highly recommend becoming a "select preferred" quest. just sign up on web site. We have stayed at Talbott before and loved it until construction caused lots of noise. cafe lux around corner as well as try "tempo" for a great breakfast. have fun and enjoy.

“Great City-Great Hotel” From check-in to check-out another great stay. From my request with attaché, to one of the cleanest hotels in NYC, and, of course, the food at Nougatine , it was a wonderful stay. Everyone should try the hotel at least once....

“Surprising Center City Find” Stayed for two nights on business. While work colleagues had told me the Courtyard (next door) would be better, I can clearly vouch that the Residence Inn was far superior. There are two reasons for this: the service (everyone is extremely friendly and helpful) and the breakfast (which was better than anticipated). The common space on the floor where the breakfast is served was quite large (for a city hotel), nicely decorated and well thought out (and TV's in the breakfast bar greatly appreciated so I could catch up on the news). The room had an odd layout to say the least, but had all the amenities one would expect from a Residence Inn (fridge, popcorn for first night, etc.) Great location within five minutes of Center Ciry offices, City Hall, Reading Terminal Market and top restaurants. Would definitely stay here again!

“Good Value in Great Neighborhood for Unpretentious Travelers” Stayed at Wyndham Garden Inn Chelsea seven nights, from December 23 to December 30, 2009. Most all hotels in Manhattan considered the last few nights of our stay as part of the high priced New Years Eve week. We were getting decent rates for the first 3 or 4 nights, but the last few nights tripled! We ended up calling hotels directly to ask for a lower price for those nights since we would be staying so long. Wyndham Garden Inn Chelsea was the only hotel that would adjust their prices. So we paid $149 for the first six nights and $229 for the last night, before taxes of about $20 a night. We paid about $40 for a taxi from LGA. The hotel is on 24th Street halfway between 5th and 6th Streets (a little closer to 6th), just one block over from the major cross-street in Chelsea, 23rd Street. There are subway stations all along 23rd street. The closest to the hotel is the FV station at 6th Avenue, but the 1, RW, 6 and CE stations aren’t far within 1⁄4 mile. The location of the hotel is its best feature. There is quick access to all parts of the city. But Chelsea/Flat Iron is full of interesting shops and incredible restaurants. We walked to all of these restaurants... we had breakfast at Murray’s Bagel (on 8th Avenue south of 23rd Street), had the best BBQ brisket ever at RUB (on 23rd Street between 7th and 8th Avenue), had an excellent European brunch at Markt, enjoyed incredible soup at Pipa’s inside the ABC Carpet Shop on Broadway, indulged in old fashioned diner-style meals at the Lyric Diner on 3rd Avenue, and even sipped shakes at Burger Shack in the Madison Square Park. The area has really fun for people watching. The hotel is obviously newly re-constructed. All the materials and fixtures are new. There is essentially no lobby. The doors open right at the front desk. There is a sofa and a couple ottomans but it’s not a spot you would spend time. A ticket desk/concierge is squeezed into a corner. The restaurant is supposed to be a part of the hotel, but it didn’t really seem that way. We never ate there. Room 903 is steps from the elevator and faces the front of the building. The small room was adequate for two people who travel well together but don’t think of sharing a room with someone who get’s on your nerves. It has a desk and chair, big flat screen TV on the wall, arm chair, two nightstands, a luggage rack and a closet equipped with an iron/board. There is no dresser. The king sized bed has a good quality mattress topped with a comfy feather bed. The sheets are good quality (probably 350-threadcount). The duvet and comforter are nice and cozy. The pillows are decent foam. The heating system was a little quirky; it made a lot of noise whenever it kicked on. But we got used to it and slept through the repeated ruckus. The bathroom is well equipped with a good-sized shower, decent towels, enough counter space and True Blue Spa soap, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. The water pressure and temperature were good. Except one morning there was no hot water. By the time we went down to the lobby, the repair truck was already parked in front of the hotel and they were repairing the frozen boiler. We had plenty of hot water when we returned that afternoon. Our room was cleaned completely and promptly when we’d leave in the morning. Although no one knocked when we had the do not disturb sign on the door, the cleaning crew was very noisy. Two of them even got into a screaming match about who wasn’t working fast enough! But everyone on the staff was very friendly to the guests. The hotel worked for us because we don’t need a fancy lobby, an onsite restaurant or other services. It was a good value for the price compared to other hotels in Manhattan. It is in an area that we like and has good access to public transportation. If you travel like we do, you’ll like this hotel.

“Probably Boston ́s best Hotel” First of all I have to mention that this was our second stay at the Mandarin Oriental Boston. Our first experience was somewhat "mixed" so we were courious about this second stay but in the end never regreted the decision. We were fortunate to stay 7 nights during early May and really enjoyed our stay from the arrival until the departure. Since we are frequent visitors to Boston as well as New England we had stayed in almost all 4 and 5* hotels in Boston and I have to say that the Mandarin Oriental Boston is probably Boston ́s best hotel. The location on Boylston Street close to the Prudential Center and Mall as well as Newbury Street is absolute perfect. Especially during rainy or snowy weather. You will be able to exit the Hotel directly to the Mall without getting wet. During sunny weather all the nice shops and restaurants are only a stone throw away. Our favorite seafood-restaurant Atlantic Fish is right above the street from the Mandarin Oriental Boston so after dinner you literay just have to fall in your bed. Service at the MOBOS was at its best. We were always smiled at and greeted by name and everybody was super friendly and welcoming. We had booked the lowest room category or Lifestyle rooms on the 4th floor, but personally we liked this room much better the the Deluxe room category we previous had stayed in. Lifestyle rooms have a hardwood floor as well as a day bed below the window. Absolute fantastic rooms in terms of size, cleanliness and and equipment. Twice daily housekeeping made our room always look and feel like brand new. in regards of sleep quality I have to admit that I had the best sleep for weeks during this stay. Beds with Frette linen are like heaven and the sound proof windows guarantee almost no noise from busy Bolyston street. Really amazing are the Concierges Correy and David who were extremley helpfull with almost all reasonable and unreasonable requests. Also a nice touch is the courtesy Mercedes Benz limousine service within the Boston area. Overall we really enjoyed our stay and would absolute recommend this hotel.

“Can't beat the location!” Spent two nights here while on vacation with wife and sons (8 and 5). As stated in other reviews, the best attribute of this hotel is the location. All of the important stuff is within one or more blocks - you can't beat it. There are restaurants 1-3 blocks away on Market Street and in other directions - see more below. The Market St & 5th St subway station is only a block and a half away. Be advised that this subway station doesn't have elevator or escalator - a bit of a challenge with luggage, but we made it just fine. The room is typical 1970's Holiday Inn size, though it has been updated. We had a two-double bed room and it was a squeeze for the 4 of us, but again, it's about the location here. Everything was clean and worked well, including the wireless internet (free). The pool was very nice - only got crowded once - there were a couple of family reunions going on in the hotel. Pool is good-sized, but no hot tub. We had breakfast in the restaurant one morning - did the buffet - I had a free coupon and the kids were supposed to pay a lower price on the full buffet (they can eat for free on a kids' menu or limited buffet), but they didn't end up charging for them. Food was pretty good, but fairly limited in variety. I would not have paid the full $12.95 for each adult and whatever for the kids, at least not two days in a row. My 5-year-old lost his stuffed panda he got in DC on the same trip. I asked the concierge to look into it before we left, but there were no signs of it. When I arrived at my office a couple of days later, there was a message they had found it - they shipped it (charged me, but that's okay - they didn't lose it. I was really impressed that they found it and tracked it down to us and notified us. Lesson learned though, don't use DHL - they had a hard time finding the address that it was shipped to and didn't get it to us in the promised time! Try the Snow White Diner on Market at about 2nd for breakfast - be advised that it is cash only, though. It was a great breakfast experience and reasonable prices. For dinner, try DiNardo's - great seafood, though a little pricey, but not outlandish. (Kids' menu is about nine bucks). It's around 3rd and Race, I believe. Definite walking distance - we did it with the boys. For a cheesesteak - go to Jim's - 4th and South (straight down 4th from the hotel). It's a medium walk or a short cab ride. Be sure and look at the board and order from the choices offered - the cook taking the orders doesn't have patience for questions or odd orders! We did okay, but others in front and behind we told "look at the board!" The Riverlink Ferry to Camden is fun, but there isn't much to do in Camden. There is a Children's Garden - it looked like fun in the brochure, but we opted out at the kids' request. We went to the Battleship New Jersey, but it would have been close to $80 for the four of us. If the boys hadn't just seen four ships in Baltimore on the same trip, we might have done it.

“room with a great view” Hotel was very nice. Elevators were strange but easy to work and get around. Our room was very clean and the view of TImes Square was amazing especially at night. Location is great. We were able to walk to the theaters and all the main site seeing attractions. We visited the View Lounge after a long day, the drinks were excellent and the view amazing. Would definetly stay at this hotel again.

“It will do, but...” This hotel has many flaws. However, it has a great location at 52nd and Broadway, the northern end of Times Square. My room was of a decent size and the bed was comfortable. I had a nice view of Times Square and I suspect, as the hotel begins on the 8th floor of the building, most rooms have good views. The furniture in my room was badly scratched. The chair looked like something that wouldn’t sell at a yard sale for 50 cents. The wallpaper in the bathroom was peeling and there was mould on the wall. The bath/shower was a plastic unit reminiscent of Motel 6. Perhaps worst of all, there is only one working elevator to haul guests and their luggage from street level to the 8th floor lobby. As this hotel must have about 300 rooms, there is always a delay, a line and a cramped ride. Forget about it at “rush hour” in the morning or evening. My room had no phone service. It took three calls on my cell phone to the front desk to get an engineer to come up to the room. He told me that the problem was that the line was dead and that the phone company would have to be contacted. He assured me that the hotel would keep me apprised of the status which, of course, they did not. In fairness, the hotel did make an adjustment to my bill at checkout to compensate me for this. It’s amazing how little you get for $500 per night in New York!

“If you have a disability do NOT stay here!” Gorgeous room, great location, F- for Accessibility. I wrote a letter. To enter and exit the building you have to go through a back alley, and the hotel laundry facilities. They also do not have any rooms with accessibility features. Will not return, am warning my friends...
“This place should be blown up” This hotel is so dated it should be blown up and rebuilt. Stay is OK. Meeting service is lacking.

“Good budget hotel” We just stayed one night here and although it isnt the fancies hotel, it has everying you could need. The area is quiet and a little bit out of the way but not so far that it was inconvenient. The rooms are a but dated and dingy but clean and supplied with everything you could need. I found the wifi connection not very good. The breakfast area is tiny with just a few tables but the breakfast was satisfactory. Toast, waffles, eggs, sausges, yogurt etc were available and although may not have been of the best quality, they did the job. The best thing about this hotel is the staff, they are great, very friendly and helpful. I would stay here again and can recommend it but be aware it is a buget hotel so dont expect the ritz.

“not a bad choice for airport stay” Older property, which does not look like much from the outside. Inside the rooms were clean and furnishings were new. Double queen room was nice size - no squeezing around the room with suitcases on the floor, lots of space. breakfast was very nice - in a restaraunt they have on site. 4 waffle makers, hot hard boiled eggs, oatmeal, biscuits and gravy, sausage links, cereals, breads, yogurt, etc... and lots of seating even when crowded staff did a great job of keeping breakfast stocked and clean airport shuttle was on time and frequently runs. indoor pool was clean ping pong table and table shuffleboard was nice diversion for kids small workout room with 3-4 machines - but never saw it crowded. freee coffee and apples in lobby some CONS: not much in the area - an IHOP .25 mi down the street is only other restaraunt close not a pretty or touristy area - a few auto parts stores, some old rental car locations, a boarded up lounge/restaraunt - you get the idea.

“A historic hotel with a room that took me back to the '80's” The lobby and location are tremendous but the room (18101) was tired beyond belief to carry the Hilton badge. The room was small with a bathroom that was too small to turn around in and the wired internet is ridiculous since many business travelers are ditching their laptops for Ipads. The carpet was coming up in the doorway of my bathroom and the furniture looked like 1989 wanted it back...oh and the retro television (tube type) was another drawback. The slow service of the elevators almost caused me to be late since they were so slow. I've stayed in many historic hotels and really love the atmosphere but they shouldn't get a free pass with a room this tired.

“fantastic service” we were staying in a hotel in santa monica and we were extremely unhappy with the service so we decided to check into the hilton at universal city as we were spending the next day at universal studios then flying out to san francisco. it was a perfect location for visiting universal studios and all city walk. we found that we were over at city walk both nights and even though it is only a short walk over there from the hotel, they actually offered a free shuttle service that took us across to city walk. the service was execptional and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay here. Next time we visit los angeles we will be basing our selves at the hilton. fantastic hotel.10/10

“Lack of Customer Service means everything” I have waited almost 3 weeks to write this review as my experience and stay the the Renaissance Los Angeles was not a pleasant one, and as you can see from my many reviews I am usually an upbeat and positive type of guy. As a Marriott Gold Member I am a dedicated Marriott patron. We had reservations for my son and I for one night before flying back home. Our reservation was a guarantee for 2 beds and was paid for on a Marriott Certificate, one they gave me for staying so many nights in a designated period of time. From the time I walked into this hotel, I don't know if it was because I had my 10 year old son with me or was a "non-paying" guest, but we were treated like second class citizens. The front desk clerk didn't say more than two words to us during check in and when questioned, answered in a curt, unprofessional manner. They told me that my room only had one bed - even though we had a guarantee for 2 beds. When I questioned her, she laughed at me and told me those guarantees didn't mean anything. We had no amenities explained to us, like location of Club Lounge, restuarant options, etc. Frankly they had no interest in making sure we had a pleasant stay. Feeling a little frustrated I emailed the hotel after my arrival home and questioned their policy on the guaranteed room. While they couldn't answer me directly, they were kind enough to say they would refund the certificate we used and the $46 we spent on dinner in their restaurant. I was feeling much better and ready to move on. However, now over 2 weeks later, no refund, no re-issued certificate and no response from the hotel. While not every hotel employee can be the tops, I am seeing a patern of employees who really have a lack of customer service. I have stayed several times at the Marriott LAX next door and found it to be a wonderful property. Next visit to LAX will not be at the Renaissance, even with a free Certificate.

“Good Times Close to Union Square in San Fran” I read the reviews, I always check out TripAdvisor before traveling. The Hilton at Union Square IS big. The front desk workers can be a little "snobbish." But overall, it was a very nice location and the positives far outweighed the negatives. First off, we arrived late as we had flight issues. We originally planned to take BART from Oakland. Not a good idea. Not the best neighborhood in Oakland and too far to walk with luggage in San Fran. The hotel location was easy to find via GPS. I wanted to use Valet for parking as we were arriving late and would not be using car until we departed. After waiting 10 minutes, I asked a police officer in front of the hotel and he said there was no Valet service. Parking was around the other side of the hotel. We found entrance easily and managed to get a parking spot near hotel entrance. A short walk was made to the lobby. Contrary to a lot of comments, no lines but then again, it was around 10:30pm on a Sunday night. We had our key within seconds and we were on our way to Tower 1 with a City View. Nice enough room. A few stains on floor. Older room. Could stand some updates and touchups. Room had balcony and provided a very nice view. We could see Coit Tower, the Bay and Union Square. Bed was comfortable. Comfortable bed. For two people in the room, it would have been nicer to have more than one towel per person. Amenities were nice. For breakfast, we had the free Hilton Continental breakfast coupons. we skipped the first day in order to eat at a favorite restaurant (Sears Foods). The second morning, we had breakfast at the hotel's restaurant. We were seated quickly and helped ourselves to a very nice breakfast of baked goods, smoothies, juice, coffee, etc.. For $10 more, we could have had the works. We also used second set of coupons for road food and that got us a fruit, bakery item and beverage (iced green tea). Wait at the Starbucks was not long, as many have commented. We did see long lines at various parts of the day. Hotel is within 4 short blocks of Union Square and Cable Cars. Walking is good for you and we enjoyed the atmosphere of all that is San Fran. Checkout was as fast as check-in, no wait. Room bill was around $350 for two nights and parking was an additional $98 plus tax. You will find the Hilton has many friendly staffers. We were regularly wished a good morning by many workers from housekeeping staffers, to security workers.

“Great Hotel and a Great Location” My wife and I have been going to Chicago for quite some time. This is the first time we've stayed in the Gold Coast district and it is a wonderful location. There is a grocery store around the corner and a drugstore one block north of the hotel. There are many restaurants and pubs in the area as well. The room was well maintained and very spacious. The staff was first rate, kind, and helpful. The only problems we experienced were the shower drain was too slow and the hallway noice was a little loud. The free wi-fi via the tv was great as well. Stay here, you won't regret it.

“Great Experience!” We used Hotels.Com for the first time, and I was a bit apprehensive about how we would be received; have read/heard that many hotels treat consolidators as second class citizens. Didn't need to worry! From our very gracious greeting at our early check-in (and arriving around 11 a.m. after flying all night), we received nothing but first-class, ***** star service. We asked for a renovated non-smoking room when we checked in. One wasn't available at that time (one in smoking was) so we accepted the non-renovated room. (They did tell us a renovated room would possibly be available a little later in the day.) Lovely room, large, good city view -- but very poor air conditioning. We went out for lunch, and when we got back, it was apparent the room hadn't gotten any cooler. My husband went down to the desk and came back with new key card to a non-smoking renovated room on another floor -- GREAT air conditioning, lovely room -- even bigger -- with a partial view of Central Park! Enjoyed our 5 night stay SO much! Tried room-service once; expensive (as are most meals we found in NYC!) but excellent food, presentation and service. The hotel is right next-door to a major subway line, which made commuting to the U.S. Open in Flushing Meadows very easy! All in all, we loved the Helmsley Park Lane and hope to make this an annual tradition!

“Spectacular property, great service, but a few kinks with housekeeping” This hotel is brand new. We booked at the last minute and needed 2 beds, so we had to book a studio suite. Boy were we glad. We were only on the 10th floor, but the room was huge. Not just big by NYC standards, I mean huge. Close to 1200 sq ft. Decor was sleek and modern. Beds very comfy and the bathroom was magnificent. Large double sink, soaking jacuzzi tub, shower with 3 different heads, including the popular rainsoaker head. The fitness center was also top rate. Service was extremely attentive. From the doorman, to the porter, to the concierge (called "personal assistants"). Room service was great, both quality and the personnel. Only fly in the ointment was housekeeping. The room was immaculate, but for some reason, each day's service missed something. One day it was clear they did not vacuum. Another the bar ware was not replaced (and one dirty glass was replaced). When we called, the problems were corrected, but it was a bit of a surprise given just how on top of things everyone else seemed. Would stay there again.

“Great Room But Not Set Up for the Late Night Airport Arrival Guest” I booked this hotel at the very last minute when an emergency business meeting was called in Denver. I landed at Denver International Airport (the hotel is near the airport) and arrived at 11pm. Unfortunately, despite the airport location, the hotel is NOT set up for the airport-arriving business guest. Room service was dead, the restaurant was closed. I went to the bar and ordered a glass of milk and fajitas (limited menu). I received four strips of chicken drowned in something that looked like fake Tabasco Sauce. If it had been, it would have been marginally edible, though not fajitas. Instead it was indescribably bad. I returned dejected to my room. Our meeting was cancelled and I had to fly out first thing in the morning. Well, there is no room service at the crack of dawn or any restaurant. My room was beautiful (but I was awake in it for 15 minutes). Bottom line: This would be a A plus business hotel if it catered to the segment of weary travelers who land at Denver Intl Airport late or have to leave for DIA early in the morning. This hotel serves neither group. Manager: Please add 24 hour room service.

“At The Centre Of The Universe” I love New York! I usually stay in Midtown because it's close to everything I want to see but this time, a friend talked me into trying the Lower East Side, and we chose the Nolitan after reading its terrific reviews here. It's true what they say on Tripadvisor - the staff are wonderful: friendly, helpful, polite, good humoured. We arrived very late at night after a long flight, and still received a warm welcome. I spent the first night on level 3 in what to me was a very small room. My best advice for anyone who is going to be a new guest, is request a room that is higher up as there will be less street noise. It will be worth the extra money. Go for a corner room if you can. After the first night, I complained about the noise (I am quite a light sleeper) and was offered a corner room on the top floor at a discounted price. I took it! My NEW room had a divine free-standing bath and a gorgeous view of the Williamsberg Bridge. The bed was superb, however all this does come at a price. I paid $477 a night (online) for the room on the lower floor and $75 more for the discounted room on the top floor. The Nolitan is situated in easy walking distance between THREE different Metro stops, which is by far and away the best way to get around New York. The hotel really is in a good position and it is only a few stops up to Midtown. One stop south is the beautiful Brooklyn Bridge over which I highly recommend a casual stroll. The hotel is also situated in the middle of an astonishing number of cafes, restaurants and bars in and around NoLita. There is a brilliant little Japanese restaurant around the corner (ask the staff to recommend it), a great cake shop and a really well-stocked bookshop for those of you who need a relaxing read. It would be difficult to ask for more. Oh, and there is free wine and cheese in the afternoon. That sold me. My one tiny criticism is that the continental breakfast could be a little bit more extensive. So, to sum up, if you can afford it, do it. The Nolitan is everything people say it is.

“Near the airport and nice...” Surprising hotel near the airport. Friendly employees. Nestled between two highways. One side is nice and quiet. The other is livable given all the action happening outside. Never interrupted my sleep cycle. Club floor is a work in progress. At least the elevators are being renovated. Interesting from an engineers point of view. Not a lot of dining options in the area. Car may be needed.

“Great hotel, great location, fantastic deal” My husband and I stayed here the night before an early flight to avoid having to drive up to BWI from northern Virginia super early in the morning. We got a great deal on an AAA stay and park package that allowed us to stay for the night and then leave our car there while we traveled (up to 8 days). We were only gone for three days, but it was comparable to what we would have paid to park at the airport. The room was much nicer than expected, with a comfortable bed, nice desk/work area and a big flat screen TV. The bathroom was nicer than expected as well. The only problem we ran into was that the hairdryer didn't work, but they brought me a new one within 15 minutes of calling - at 5am! The shuttle service to the airport runs 24 hours and was very convenient. When we returned to pick up our car, the shuttle came right away after I called, even at 1am! I would not hesitate to stay here again if I had an early flight.

“Very nice stay in a very pleasant hotel” The hotel is in a great neighborhood. Some good restaurants, shopping, easy to access the rest of the city via subways. The room had two queen-sized beds, good free internet access, and was reasonably well equipped. The shower was fine as well. Nothing fancy, but all nice and clean. The elevator at busy hours was slow. The free breakfast was pretty good. Again, not fancy, but good omelette-like breakfast the first day and so-so scrambled eggs and bacon day 2. Cut up fresh fruit, bagels, etc. and coffee. The breakfast room and general ambience was nice. I personally love not having to pay extra for every little thing (breakfast, coffee, internet, ...). Also, they had hot cider and cookies out in the afternoons when we returned. We didn't really ask for much from staff, but when I stayed on after breakfast to work on my computer, they cheerfully worked around me. When my daughter realized an hour after we had checked out (we were sill in the city) that she'd left her ipod charger in the room, we called and left a message with housekeeping, who brought it to reception by the time we checked out. I wrestled with four stars or five and decided to go with four. While it met my expectations (or better) for an affordable NY hotel (I used HHonors points this time), it is not the same as a great hotel that also meets my expectations (e.g., the Grand Bretagne in Athens). So, I am giving it a four star recommendation. I think it is similar to but slightly better than the Sheraton Four Points in Chelsea, for which I don't appear to have written a review. We will return to this hotel.

“STAY AWAY!!!!” The 1st problem with this hotel is that it is in the middle of nowhere. The cab fair from the airport was $58!!! Once I arrived there they said that they were full even though I showed them my printed out reservation. After trying to speak to the manager about finding me a room at a nearby hotel, he asked me to leave and began swearing at me. An Absolute Nightmare hotel!!!!!

“Great staff and located right in the action” Tracy (front desk) and Kevin (doorman) were just a few of the team members that provided excellent service. The location is the best in Times Square. All suite rooms are very large. Just stay here and you will be happy

“Unbelievable stay at this W - even from a jaded traveller” I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. I took advantage of the SPG program and paid through points. Keep that in mind for the rest of the review. I am a SPG Platinum. I checked into this hotel on a Thursday night, just before the July 4 weekend. On the drive up, the hotel is located adjacent to UCLA and a very residential area. I almost didn't notice the hotel until my wife pointed to the "W" on the side of the hotel. The exterior looked nondescript. The valet was extremely courteous when I drove up beside them as I wasn't sure where to "stop" the car. I arrived early, around 11 am, and didn't expect to have a room ready. The pre-allocated room wasn't ready but a simliar room on a lower level was. I declined in favour of the higher floor room and had them hold my bags while I went out & about the local area. I returned many hours later and found out they had upgraded me to a 2 room suite. Unbelievable! The lobby areas and the front of the hotel was super chic. It was in line with other W's. The elevator has a built-in camera that "plays" with a photo of the elevator occupants. Kind of a fun and unassuming way to ensure privacy and security. Upon arriving to my suite, I immediately noticed it was huge. Not beside the elevator (which I hate elevator and associated guest noise) but in a recessed corner. The furnishings are funky. They are modern, without try to hard to look it. Lots of art around the rooms. There was a full-size LCD in the living room and a smaller LCD in the bedroom. The 2nd room was more of a workspace which mainly comprised of a sofa and workdesk. Hey, works for me as I can't get enough desk space. There were several thermostats around the room controlling ambient temperature in each. The A/C units were more than able to handle the July heat. In fact, I had to turn up the temperature as it was getting a little frosty. The bathroom was very large. Good counter space. As opposed to a shower curtain, I got a funky half-glass with a hole. While aesthetically pleasing, you can probably imagine it was tough trying not to let out too much water from the mssing half of the glass. Interestingly enough, Thurs night was super busy due to some event happening. Having said that, even though I could hear some noise in the living room, it was completely quiet in the bedroom. Fri night was extremely quiet in comparison. The service received, from everyone, was literally incredible. Everyone introduced themselves and remembered and greeted me by name every time. Am I in a W or a Ritz Carlton?. I mean that in a good way. Front desk - excellent. Concierge - excellent. Valet - surprisingly excellent. Anywhere, anything phone service - excellent. Before you think I'm a shill working for the W, do note that I've been a SPG Platinum for many years and have tried hotels all over the world. This is probably one of the best, if not the best experience, that I've had in any hotel in North America. Certainly better than most European luxe hotels and certainly on par with Asian luxe hotels. In comparison to the W Seattle, which I stay at frequently, this W is clearly superior. Would I return? Absolutely. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend? I'll do that even without them asking me. Was it all perfect? No. An extra charge appeared on my CC after checking out. However, a quick call to billing and it was sorted out. Another problem occurred when they brought up my bags. They only brought up one and both tags were attached to that one. I was getting worred they had lost my other one but, no problems, as it was shortly brought up. I enjoyed this stay so much, I even emailed Starwood corporate. I never do that. Ever. Tips: 1) The restaurants in the nearby village are high quality and not that busy. I got into Palomino without any problems, unheard of in Seattle. Good food at decent prices. 2) Free internet in the lobby for guests. 3) If your room faces the BACKYARD, you might find an interesting WiFi signal. 4) There is a Best Buy and a Ralph's a block away.

“Unimpressed” As a gold marriott elite member I expected more. I was upgraded to the concierge floor with a balcony over looking the parking lot. I heard every car horn and screaming kid. This was still better than the noise coming from the above floors where they are doing refurbishing. The front desk was unable to answer what time they start and finish work, when I mentioned moving rooms they looked stunned. The walls/doors ar thin so you will be able to hear others talking. The rooms lack a safe so when I went to the front desk to use the hotels that said they don't have any left, unacceptable for a hotel in a resort area. Honestly for what they charge there should be a room safe. The room is typical Marriott flare or lack of flare (and I think my room is "updated"). The bed is comfortable, flat screen tv, outdated bathroom, popcorn ceiling, central AC. For the price there are so many better choices in San Antonio such as the Westin, Omni La Mansion, Hotel Contessa, or my favorite hotel Valencia. At best this is a 3 star hotel. Also you will have to walk to get to a decent part of the Riverwalk. A plus of this hotel is self parking where you can come and go as you please for a $23 fee.

“Just perfect” This hotel was such a nice surprise in every way. It is beautiful, clean and cool. The staff was really sweet and helpful. I have read some reviews here saying that it is quite a walk in to central San Antonio so when came there we were really surprised of how close it was to everything. Riverwalk is just outside so you can walk on it. This part of the riverwalk is very nice to, not as hysterical. Parking is 17$ per night but it was cheaper than many other hotels. Don ́t miss the hotelbar "Ocho". It was lovely and had such nice light. Just a really cool place that I would go to even if I didn ́t stay in the hotel. The only bad thing i have to say is that there is nowhere to hang your clothes. No closets or hangers. One more not so good thing was that the AC was really really loud. That brings down the rating on the sleeping quality.

“Hands down one of the best values in Los Angeles” Having stayed at this property probably about 7 or 8 times since their opening, I can fully recommend your next Hollywood visit to be at this uniquely charming hotel. The rooms are spacey; 750sqft minimum for each room as the property was originally built to be condo units. Great amenities from washer/dryers in each room, 2 flat screens per room, available complimentary I-Pad uses, amongst a plethora of other great treats & treasures. In it's first year of opening, prices were much more reasonable; as of late, the price increases seem to be a little much but the quality of rooms & service still makes it one of the best values in LA. The off-putting things about this property are that room service comes from the in-house restaurant Cleo and next door's Katsuya (both great restaurants); both charge a delivery fee in addition to the hefty gratuity which is odd since Cleo is in-house? I can order to-go, travel down 5 floors (the hotel is only 5 stories total so it's not far no matter which floor your room is on) and just bring it up to my room rather than pay that delivery fee: it's more like a "if-you-are- -too-lazy-to-come-get-it-yourself-expect-to-be-charged" type of fee. The ice-machine is a pain; there is only 1 ice-machine located on the 4th floor but I consider a small price to pay for traveling through the hallways in discovery of neat features this hotel has to offer. Quiet sleepers beware: the property sits next to Avalon Nightclub which is known for their ongoing heavy bass electronic music after-hour parties (yes low frequency bass waves travel through walls): Friday & Saturday nights this club will go strong until after the sun comes up which should be more of a reason why they should consider keeping the prices slightly lower for the weekend because if you are stuck on the Avalon side of the building you might not be getting much sleep or if your neighbor in the room next door just so happens to be that world famous DJ that just got off his set from the club and decides to continue the party in their room for the night. Since it's opening the hotel has done an excellent job in keeping it's cleanliness but with so much detail involved you can see a little wear starting to show finally. A chipped tile in the shower; scuff marks on some of the hallway and room walls but nothing to complain over since again, the value of this property is still one of the best deals in LA. Small renovations every year should be mandatory given then amount of detail and traffic this place sees. Overall, the best times to truly enjoy this property is on the week-day nights when their aren't so many party-goers involved; walking through the dark halls provides a plush but eerie feeling of being transported to a different time and place where you'll be more than satisfied that you have this place to yourself for the night.

“Over-rated” Recently stayed at the Hyatt Capitol Hill for four days of business. There’s no denying that the hotel is very well decorated, clean, and upscale. The rooms – namely the appliances – are as well. But there are several “little things” that took away from the experience. The first is that the so-called free wired Internet service doesn’t exist. I could not find a LAN plug in my room to save my life so I was forced into buying three days of wireless service. And, the comfortable factor of the bed was surprisingly average for the excessive price at the Hyatt. Did I mention the space at the bottom of the room door that allowed hall noise (from loud guests returning no doubt from a night of drinking) into the room? Or perhaps I should mention the $20 breakfast buffet that was on par with Holiday Inn Express? OK, I understand that you’re paying for location (it was nice to be so close to the Capitol and Union Station) here but I clearly felt the Hyatt is overpriced and doesn’t live up to the price tag overall. If you want to be close to the Capitol, then go for it. Otherwise, you can do much better in D.C.

“Pleasant Stay!” I stayed in the Hyatt Regency Boston for a night and it was a good experience. We got early check-in into our room and we couldnt be more thankful for that. We got a room on level 5 and we was greeted with a pleasant scent along the corridor to our room. The hotel is conveniently near to the subway, less than 5 minutes walk. It is also very near to Chinatown and the

“Hotel has potential” I recently stayed at the Crowne Plaza Hotel in downtown Dallas. As far as location is concerned, it is walking distance from several eating establisments. I highly recommend going over to Market Street, where there is everything from a Sonny Bryant's, Spaghetti Warehouse, TGI Friday's, and a Butcher Shop Steakhouse. The hotel is also right down the street from the Texas School Book Depository at Dealy Plaza. To check into the hotel, you must pull into the self-park garage and get a ticket. There is no valet parking. When you get inside, mention to the hotel clerk that you are parked in the garage and they will activate your hotel key for entry and exit into the garage. The hotel has a nice restaurant, which I used every day at lunch. The food is good and reasonably priced. There is also a hotel bar, and a nightclub which is open on the weekend. This can be a plus or a minus, depending on your perspective. I found it to be a minus. The nightclub patrons practically take over the hotel, from the garage, to the lobby, to the elevators, to the rooms and they make plenty of racket. I awoke one time at 4am to revelers on the pool deck, even though it is clearly marked that it should be closed at 11pm. I also witnessed several club goers horsing around in the elevators, which can be rather annoying. They must make a lot of money from the club, but as a hotel guest I would suggest closing it down because it detracts from the overall hotel experience. The room was very nice and clean. It had the standard hotel amenities, as well as a mask and earplus so you can sleep better. You might need them on the weekends when the nightclub is open, although they may cause you to oversleep your alarm. The internet connection was very flaky at first, but improved during the week. The staff told me they were in the process of changing from one internet provider to another, and that they had to change the router that they were using. My room included a refrigerator, but no microwave although I heard from other guests that the hotel could lend one if you requested it. We were also working at the hotel, and generally speaking they were easy to work with. The first thing that concerned me were the amount of maintenance they were doing on the floor where we were working, and the noise was rather distracting. The second thing that concerned me was that a hotel staff member interrupted our session and "Shushed" us to keep it down, even though we never spoke above a normal conversational tone. Overall, it's a nice hotel, but I really suggest they close that nightclub.

“Absolutely Perfect in Every Way!” We recently stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth while visiting BU with our 16 yr old. ( Note to parents of BU prospective students or current ones, this hotel is directly across the street from campus. Very well located for visiting!!) From the moment we pulled up to the moment we departed, everything at this hotel was perfect! The front desk was wonderful, our room overlooked Fenway Park, and we had a huge room with two large beds and a sitting area as well! The women at the front desk were very friendly, helpful, and very welcoming. If I could live at Hotel Commonwealth, I don't see why I would live anywhere else! ha Book it now. You won't regret it. ( yes the parking is steep, but it is Boston. We paid a little bit more for NYC the next day.)
“great hotel” always a pleasure to stay here. clean rooms, easy access to freeway, fine gym and great staff!

“Customer service exceptional, rest mediocre” The biggest pro is definitely the customer service. Exceptional. High class treatment. Lots of staff standing around offering assistance, "Do you need assistance with your bags? Is there something I can help you with? Can I get someone to get your car? Do you need help with directions?" Staff was very helpful, friendly, and professional. I really felt pampered. Fitness room had plenty of good equipment and pool looked just right, although felt a little warm. But, I didn't have time to use either. Shower was nice. Bed was comfy. Big fluffy queen pillows. I slept well, except that I kept getting up, because I couldn't seem to get the temperature controlled right. I had a nice view from the 11th floor. I didn't love the room. My biggest complaint was how small it was. It was tiny and tight, and I'm a small person. I had a queen bed. I was by myself and couldn't imagine 2 people trying to share the room. The bathroom is especially tiny. No counter space, although there's a glass shelf you can put some things one. There's absolutely no way 2 people could be in the bathroom at the same time. The bathroom was well lit for putting cosmetics on. The floor looked like it didn't get vacuumed well enough. The sheets has what appeared to be rust stains on them. They also looked pretty worn. I got the room on Priceline, so I got a great deal, $60. If I could pick, I would stay at the Hyatt where I stayed the last time for $60 on Priceline. Lots roomier, etc. Although the customer service was not remarkable, like at the Omni. I'll be staying at the Omni Charlotte, NC next week. I hope I enjoy the room better.

“Very Nice After Room Change” My wife and I recently spent a night at the Mandarin Oriental to celebrate an anniversary. We ended up having a very nice time with the staff and the spa being the highlights. To begin with, however, we were placed in a room right next to some kind of a service entrance. We had paid for a relatively nice room so I was disappointed when my brief afternoon nap was interrupted every 3-4 minutes by the sound of a door closing. After a call to the front desk, we were quickly relocated and loved our new room. The spa is among the best that we have been to and the staff throughout was exceptional. Breakfast in the room was excellent the next morning. I would have given five stars except for the initial room placement. Avoid room 520 and you will have a wonderful time at this lovely hotel in a very nice location.

“Hidden gem!” Stayed for 5 nights on business. This hotel is excellent - location is not necessarily the best but that's the only thing. Ordered room service as soon as I arrived and the food was absolutely fantastic. Internet connection was provided free of charge. An iPod player was provided. The room was spacious and the staff were very courteous.

“Disappointing... they'll need to try much harder” I was sceptical about booking the hotel as it's new but I phoned in advance and the manager also emailed me to confirm that our requirements would be met, we'd be well taken care of and that he'd personally make sure we got a great room. Well, of course, none of that actually happened. We arrived late afternoon and although we had specifically requested a quiet room on an upper floor, we were given a room on the 2nd floor which had industrial drying machines right outside the door. Presumably to dry out a leak of some sort. We complained and they managed to find us a room on the 6th floor. Although the room was a decent size by New York standards, it was an odd shape, the tv on the wall was miles away from the bed, the aircon didn't work properly and it was noisy, the room phone had no information on it and all the pillows were absolutely terrible - cheap foam - which meant I woke with a crick in my neck. On top of that, and worst of all. wifi didn't work. Something that was essential as we were on business. The staff really were very nice and they tried to help out but of course they couldn't really do much so we checked out the next day despite having originally planned to spend 7 nights there. To be honest, it's more of an upmarket hostel than a hotel. There are a couple of chairs in the hall where you check in but there aren't really any facilities. The location is ok.... a bit too busy and noisy for my liking... but if you enjoy the hustle and bustle of New York and want to get a cheap Louis Vuitton or Rolex, then it's perfect. It is however only a short walk to Soho and to Tribeca which is great. Would I stay there again or recommend it? No.

“A Rare Good Deal in the Loop” I was excited to win this hotel on Priceline given it's good reviews. It does live up to the reviews. The hotel is bright, clean, and modern inside and out. Hotel staff was friendly during my minimal interaction with them. Our room was large, and appeared even more spacious due to the high ceilings and large bathroom. There is a large stand-up glass shower. We had a king room with mini-fridge and microwave. Our room looked over Franklin street. The only complaint I had was that the room doors slam shut very loudly and can be fairly bothersome if you're nursing a hangover early in the morning. You could loudly hear people talking in the halls. There was also some traffic noise from the street, even 5 floors up. Otherwise, the hotel was very good. I would highly recommend.

“Great place to stay in San Antonio!” We loved the charming and historic atmosphere of this hotel. It combines its historic heritage with very modern comfort. The location is simply great on the Riverwalk! Highly recommended for your holidays in San Antonio.

“Convenient, new residence inn” This is a new residence inn and a ltlle different from the normal 2 story townhouse properties. Its 4 stories, and the suites are a little smaller, and the kitchens not as nicely doine as they used to be. Still, its pretty nice. The suite worked well and the location is very convenient: its 10 minutes to the zoo downtown in one direction and 10 minutes the other way to seaworld. Mission valley is retail heaven with several malls and all the big box stores (including an IKEA -- cheap modern furniture and household stuff) The pool is a big one for Residence Inns and theres a separate kiddie wading pool, and a decent exercise room. The breakfast room is big, and it fills up toward the end of breakfast.

“Very nice but don't bother unless you are R-C Status (not Marriott Status)” Stayed at this hotel for one night. Originally planned to stay 4 nights. I am Platinum Marriott but had never stayed at a Ritz. I checked the website carefully (I thought) and even called and inquired as to what my elite status conveyed at the Ritz - specifically upgrades and the executive floor lounge. I was told yes to both and the website indicated as much. When I arrived I inquired as to lounge hours and was told (politely) that that was not part of the deal. So I decided to stay anyway and forgo the access. I was placed in a mid-floor room with western view - meaning street view. The room was noisy without the a/c on - fortunately if you left the fan setting on - it provided enough "white noise" to drown out the street noise. Room furnishing are dated - bed was VERY soft. Property was well maintained and I found ALL of the R-C staff pleasant, friendly, and interested in my experience. However, I work very hard to sustain my status (travel in excess of 200 nights per year and split fairly evenly between Marriott & Hilton) and frankly have come to expect that a relationship like this promotes some sort of expectation - if Marriott owns the brand, then Marriott should honor the loyalty I bring to relationship. I do not feel that to the case so I won't be staying at any R-C again until this policy changes. My dissapointment was hightened by the fact that I did the checking before hand and found out the information provided was misleading. If you stay at this hotel just recognize your perks from Marriott Rewards DO NOT convey.

“Perfect location” Stayed here while lobby under renovation. Room 2826 very modern and comfortable. Nice king bed, electric shade, and fridge. IPod charger in room. Restaurat in hotel very nive for the view and worth a splurge. Spent $120 for 2 with no alcohol. Location is excellent. Close to everything union square has to offer. Try lori's dinner down the block for a cheap meal to take back to the room.

“Just... Wow” I had to travel to San Francisco for business on short notice. All hotels were sold out due to a citywide event. I usually stay at the Fairmont San Francisco, so thought I would try their new property. The hotel did not have any single rooms available due to the event. My two colleagues and I decided to book a three bedroom apartment. Since we are all pretty private, we were hesitant to do so. We should not have worried. This apartment was absolutey stunning. Each guestroom was humungous and featured a king bed and bathroom. The living room and kitchen were sleek and modern and perfect for entertaining. The best part of the apartment was the balcony - it had the most amazing view, overlooking Alcatraz. There was also a fire pit. Absolutely wonderful. The service was great as well. I arrived really late in the evening due to a flight delay and was exhausted.
