I told the front desk this and they refrained from giving me a brief overview of their services, delivering me and my bags to my room quickly and offering an overview in the morning. Additional perks - there is a free continental breakfast AND the business center is free. What a rarity in a luxury hotel! Other hotels should take notice. Your guests are willing to pay a good rate for a good hotel, but they would rather not feel as if they're being "nickled and dimed". Although I usually prefer to stay in a more central location (this hotel was located in Fisherman's Wharf), I would certainly return given the chance.

“NYC Marathon weekend - a great hotel” spent a night in the city with my son to see some sights and spend some quality time together. The staff at the hotel were helpful and very nice. It was Marathon weekend in the city and we were able to get a great rate (by NYC standards) Check out Mustang Sally's down the street for a burger and a beer. Room service for dessert was a great treat.

“Number One Choice for Chicago” The hotel, formerly the Le Meridien, is conveniently connected to the Shops at North Bridge mall, easily accessible from the hotel's fifth floor lobby and a short elevator trip. As such, despite the main lobby being on Rush St. the shopping drag of North Michigan Avenue is easily accessible from the hotel. Despite arriving at a busy period of the day, check-in was handled swiftly and politely and key cards were handed out in no time. We reserved a junior suite for our two night stay and as you can see from the pictures, it was more space than we actually needed. Bottles of water were provided and were replenished daily, there was a jogging map provided with the different recommended routes depending on the distance run, wired and wireless internet was available and it was complimentary for our stay. Despite the boring interior design, the room was comfortable and airy. The bed was certainly the highlight of our stay and it easily ranked as one of the best hotel beds I have every slept on. The bathroom had separate shower and bathtub which I truly appreciate, and the toilet was in a separate room within the bathroom, something my wife truly appreciates. Toothbrush, toothpaste, combs and mouthwash were provided, a rarity in the age of cost-cutting. Something which I think is lacking from a hotel such as the Conrad is the in-room coffee maker. Instead, the hotel has replaced it with a limited self-service table of coffee, tea, water and newspapers, located just outside the restaurant in the lobby. They quickly run out especially on days with high occupancy. For a more detailed review, please go to http://playingforpici.com

“Very Pleased” I am a Priority Club member and have stayed at the other Intercontinental property in midtown but find it to be showing it's age so I gave the new Intercontinental a try and came away very pleased. This was my second stay at this property in a three month time frame. I returned due to my positive experience on my initial visit and was just as pleased with my second stay. I had business to do in the Times Square area and this hotel is only one block away. Consequently, I didn't need a cab to get to my meetings. Front desk and valet staff are pleasant and accommodating. Check in and check out were a breeze. I was out of my cab and into my room in just minutes. Rooms are sized nicely by New York standards and housekeeping was spot on. I heard no noise from the hallway or adjacent rooms and slept wonderfully on the comfortable bed. I used the in-room computer terminal and enjoyed the convenience. Lots of channels available on the TV. I did not use room service but very much enjoyed lunch in the Todd English restaurant just off the lobby. Room rates are very favorable compared to other popular midtown lodging venues. This is now my hotel of choice when I need to stay in the Times Square area.

“Great place” Stayed here with my hubby who was in on business... very nice hotel, great view from pool area and gym. Great service too... wonderful location right on Lady Bird (or Town) Lake. The beds were comfortable, and we enjoyed the convenient Starbucks on site. Many good places within walking distance... the onsite self-parking is also very convenient.

“Very Nice” My stay was three days on a business trip. I took the train from the airport to downtown and the hotel was a nice, 3 block walk from the Suburban Station. I was very pleasantly surprised by the vibrancy of downtown Philadelphia and there was lots of shopping and restaurants within easy walking distance of the hotel. The hotel staff was very polite and accommodating. Room: Pros: big flat screen TV, comfy bed, nice shower separate from tub, Koenig coffeemaker, and safe in room. Cons: ended up with a crummy view, and like many hotels...they could move the furniture to vacuum edges more often and they could have accessible electric plugs near the bed/bedside stand.

“city views” The hotel is located in a very central spot in downtown San Francisco, convenient to almost anything you would want to do. The room was comfortable, nice, and spacious. bathroom was very small good stay overall

“W Review” We were a family of 3 wanting to stay in an upscale hotel. We got upscale but did not expect snobby. We were greeted by snobbish front desk and checked out with the same. The rooms were nice and the bed is wonderful as you would expect from a starwood property. I liked the furniture and decor of the entire hotel. I do recommend you check the honor bar and snacks in your room for any missing items. We never saw the honor bar but did see the snacks and WE DID NOT EVEN TOUCH THEM. # days later our credit card was charged more than our 1 night stay. I called and I was told it was for the snacks and honor bar that was eaten/drank. The manager did remove the charges and it was painless to call. It was just annoying. From now on I will ask for those items to be removed from our room prior to check in so this will not happen. This hotel is walking distance to the ACC and many other attractions. I would stay there again.

“Great location but very average for the price” I stay at Hilton hotels across the country when I travel for business. All of them have nice beds and linens and various levels of quality on everything else. This location is very average in terms of furniture and room quality. The location of the hotel was great and the concierge was very helpful in finding a delicious meal nearby. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again for business but would struggle to justify the high price and average room quality if traveling on vacation.

“Purgatory Point Would Be More Accurate” I would echo the previous review in every detail. "Prepare to be gouged" is spot-on. $20/day for a parking spot (see photo) -- not even for valet parking, but just to park yourself next to your room. $15/day for the tiny exercise room. Yes, that's per day, not per stay. You get one day's fee off if you book one of the overpriced "spa" packages. Big deal, since the spa services themselves cost many times what they would cost in the outside world. And the prices at their "casual" outdoor restaurant are what you would normally expect from a fine dining experience. My wife and I spent $73 for two appetizers, two soups (nearly inedible), one order of luke-warm, flavorless coffee, and two salads that we split -- no main course. Our room was nothing special, though the rate was what we normally spend in Hawaii. The bathroom paint was disintegrating and peeling off, the hinges on the door were completely rusted, and the furniture was shabby at best. What the previous reviewer didn't mention is that this is one of those resorts where everything is inconveniently located -- it's all spread out over many acres. Your room is likely to be in a little building far from the main lobby, spa, exercise room, pool, meeting rooms, and restaurants. To do anything, you have to walk outside and walk or drive to the facilities. So if you want to be overcharged for the room, charged extra for every amenity, and inconvenienced in accessing any of them, this is the place for you.

“Great Stay at Hyatt Regency Chicago” Was here just one night on a business trip. Perfect location downtown. Check-in was fast and efficient. Was even asked if I'd like a lemon-scented water while waiting a few minutes in queue. Scored a newly-remodeled room in the West Tower. At first, I found the bed in the middle of the room with desk behind the headboard to be a little odd. But quickly appreciated how it used the space quite nicely. Checkout was just as easy. I'd definitely recommend to anyone staying downtown Chicago.

“Excellent stay in a beautiful historic building, PERFECT LOCATION. Breakfast? Meh.” This was a great hotel stay. The location couldn't be better - it's just a short walk to anywhere in historic Philadelphia and lots of great restaurants. The room was cute and had ample room for us (two of us), and it was very quiet (top floor, courtyard side). It's a modern bathroom and you even get Comcast digital cable on the TV. Parking is available across the street for a slight discount off the parking garage normal rate. Breakfast was the only thing that let this place down. It was literally a bowl of raisin bran, and some terrible pastries and plain bagels. For this price and this elegant of a hotel, I expected better. It was a real disappointment each morning. I wish they simply hadn't mentioned on the website that breakfast was included and we would be figured that into our budget. Anyway, I do highly recommend the hotel and the staff was always very friendly and helpful.

“Not a place to stay unless someone else is paying” To chime in with the rest of my fellow reviewers, do pick a better place for your stay in San Diego unless someone else is paying. My employer sponsored a seminar, so I had no other option but to stay at the Town and County Resort. My room on the second floor of a two-story building must have had zero insulation, since I could hear my next door neighbor on his cell phone at all hours of the morning and evening (I was not in the room during the day). The room was terribly dated with a well-worn, navy carpeting, old bed linens and covers, all of the above of questionable cleanliness. On the day that I was to check out, I called the front desk several times to inquire regarding any additional charges and was placed on hold for what seemed like 10 minutes at a time to be told that no one could help me at that time and that there were "many other guests" who needed assistance. In short, poor service coupled with mediocre amenities equals zero appeal for any future consideration.

“Great value” The Club Quarters Chicago (Central Loop) was quite chic. It was close to the museams and millennium park, but far from the bars and clubs. The rooms were standard size and had either two twin beds or one queen. My only complant is that they don't provide any blankets, so bring your warm pjs!

“A very pleasant surprise” I didn't have extremely high expectations as I got a favorable rate through Priceline, and while I am a Gold SPG member, I didn't think that would matter. I was wrong on both accounts. First, the lobby is light and extremely appealing, with touches you wouldn't expect. I was placed on a Starwood Preferred Floor, and the rooms were decent sized, with extremely large and renovated bathrooms that, to be honest, were much nicer than most higher end hotels. The bed was a bit hard, but I prefer that to too soft. The fitness center was also a pleasant surprise, with ample machines and weights. I ate at the Cherry Lounge, which was also extremely pleasant with good food. The icing on the cake was that the front desk was kind enough to give me a late checkout the next day due to my SPG status, although they probably didn't need to. Was it the Ritz? No. But was it an unexpected gem in this price range? Yes.

“Beautiful and unique!” Bar scene was hopping on Saturday night. Chef is fabulous. We were attending a wedding reception and couldn't get enough of the food. The staff was very hospitable. Rooms are all unique. Some are cheaper than others, but you get what you pay for. The way rates in DC have skyrocketed lately, this place is a steal. It's a short walk to the Dupont Circle metro. The neighborhood is filled with great restaurants and bars.

“Good value for HHonors member with no car” I stayed here as a Gold Member using Point Stretcher and did not need to park overnight so was very pleased with the value. Pros: Large, quiet comfortable room with great western views. Upgraded to executive floor. Complimentary WiFi, bottled water, and breakfast buffet which offered hot and cold cereal, fruit, cereal, and pastries. Executive floor lounge with computer and cold drinks in cooler. Comfortable decent size pool with excellent towels. Friendly staff at front desk and restaurant; also when encountered in hotel. Cons - got to assigned room on 10th floor and discovered electricians were working on installing new internet wiring, door of room was propped open, worker said it needed vacuuming and wasn't sure if Wifi would be working. Also room overlooked highway. I called down and was immediately assigned another room on the 9th floor facing west. Second room was fine except only had one hand towel and no wash clothes; I had to call down for some. Also realized I hadn't been given my cookies (!) which I did get from the front desk the next day. I agree that charging for parking should be unnecessary. There was even a minimum $6 charge just for short term and only a handful of free spaces for check-in. My son dropped by a few times and twice had to park across the street in the office lots; they do patrol for overnight trespassing but it wasn't a problem otherwise. Overall I enjoyed my experience but might have chosen a different Hilton property if either (1) I had to park a car overnight or (2) they hadn't offered Point Stretcher.

“J'adore” Nous y avons séjourné plusieurs fois,en couple,avec des amis,avec les enfants et moi J'ADORE!!! Trés classieux,les chambres sont soignées,literie excellente,belle vue surtout plus vous montez en étage. Ambiance trés New Yorkaise au bar,petit déjeuner un peu cher mais top,avec pancakes,gaufres,pain perdu.... L'hotel est idéalement situé sur Times Square,accés facile pour tous les points stratégiques de la ville que ce soit a pied ou en métro. A Noel un énorme sapin vous attend en haut de l'escalator,assez impressionnant! J'y retournerais sans hésiter.

“Excellent hotel” I can't believe this hotel has not had a review in 4 years. Stayed here for 3 nights on a room/golf package. The hotel is across the street from the Texas Motor Speedway. It is "out a ways" from most other landmarks. However its right off 35W and only 30 min south to Ft Worth or DFW. This is a very nice Marriott. The lobby area is great, good bar, and the breakfast buffet was average. The rooms are good size with very comfortable beds and large bathrooms. There is a LARGE outdoor pool / hot tub. The attached golf course is a mixed bag. The layout / design is very nice. Its a Troon course. However, the course is not maintained well. I don't think it sees a lot of play and its just not kept up like it should be. Its a shame. Still worth playing (we played twice in two days) but with a little effort it could be a much nicer course.

“4-star experience for a 2-star rated property” Not in a so-fancy neighborhood, not surrounded by beautiful views, just a simple and convenient place to stay for a cruise-goer. We booked a one-night package which included a free week of parking for a very reasonable price. The GM - Shiblee Ahmed was proactive and helpful from the day we arrived, the day we left for the cruise and was the first person to greet us back after the cruise. An all around good guy. Rooms are typical for a Vagabond with all the very basic needs - decent bedding, bathroom toiletries, and TV. AC worked well and WiFi was great. Breakfast seemed to be limited to donuts and coffee and was cutoff at 9am sharp.

“Definitely worth considering” It seems to be getting harder and harder to find decent business-style hotels in New York at a reasonable price. When I am travelling alone on business I don't really want to spend many hundreds of dollars per night staying in uber-luxury places on my own - I'd rather save my cash for when I'm vacationing with my family. But I want a level of comfort that doesn't make me totally miserable to be on yet another long business trip. In this regard, Kimpton hotels seem to hit the mark pretty well. I've stayed at quite a few recently and the Eventi is definitely close to the top of their range in quality terms. The hotel is located at 30th & 6th which is not an area I've stayed in before, and isn't that convenient for me frankly as most of my meetings are generally in mid-town but what it lacked in convenience it definitely made up for in quality - plus as an added bonus it is right near Korea-town where I had one of the best Korean meals I've ever tasted (and that includes several trips to Seoul!). There is also a subway very close to the hotel which meant midtown was literally minutes away. Arrival was very straightforward, no waiting in line, no long forms to fill out plus they remembered to offer me the $15 complimentary credit for the mini-bar which I get as a frequent visitor to Kimpton hotels. As usual they were also offering complimentary wine 5pm-6pm in their verandah bar which I think is a nice friendly touch. The room was a very good size for New York which nice bathroom and very comfortable bed. Wardrobe was fine and as usual they offered free internet. The hotel seemed to be something of a hot-spot as there was some sort of fashion event going on one night which looked like fun. I didn't use the restaurant. Check-out was very easy. Will definitely be back.

“Bad Housekeeping But Otherwise Nice Hotel” I'm of two minds about the Hilton Austin. My overall sense is that the staff by and large are fantastic but that some wayward housekeeping staff are putting the whole business at risk. I'd never paid much mind to housekeeping before. They leave new towels, I tip them--what could they possibly screw up? Well, they left a dirty cup among the clean disposable cups by the coffee machine. Evidently someone had left a bunch of pens in it, judging by the ink stains at the bottom. Of course, pens can get pretty germy, since people's filthy hands touch them all the time. I'm far from OCD, but my fiancee drank from this cup without checking it first (who would?) and vomited about 2 hours later. A call to the housekeeping manager did nothing; she was defensive and wanted to know what we wanted her to do about it (which should be her problem, not ours). The security people, however, seemed to take it quite seriously. They were very apologetic and professional. They said they'd even have the cup tested for whatever it was that made my lady sick. (We have yet to hear from them, but we'll give them more time.) But why didn't the maids check the disposable cups to see if any had been used? The other weirdness from housekeeping was that they kept banging on the door despite the presence of a "do not disturb" sign posted by my fiancee, who stayed in the room while I was at a meeting during the day. She was on the phone, and they just kept knocking. This never happens anywhere else. Guests are not obligated to vacate the room at 10 AM for the convenience of the maids! Another odd thing was that I'd asked for, instead of the ubuiquitous and obligatory USA Today (a slightly more cerebral version of People Weekly), the New York Times. The next morning we got two of the latter--and one USA Today, which we ignored. The morning after that? No New York Times! (When did USA Today become the de facto national newspaper instead of the NYT or the Wall Street Journal? But I digress.) It's time I said some good things. The bellhops are super friendly. The location is good--close to South Congress--where you will find the affordable and delicious Manuel's and (a short drive away) Threadgill's--the gorgeous and rococo Texas State Capitol building, and the famed and racuous (at least at night) 6th Street (though be aware of various panhandlers on some nearby streets). The rooms themselves are nice, albeit fairly small. Hopefully the management will have fixed the housekeeping problems soon. If so, the Hilton Austin will be far more deserving of its (gulp) $289-per-night (plus tax!) rate. But you owe it to yourself to check out the very nearby Radisson, Mariott Courtyard, and (for probably around the same high price) Four Seasons.

“Safety Issues at the CP Houston” My wife has stayed at this property several times now, as it's proximity to the Anderson Medical Center and treatment of guests, combined with a fabulous rate is ideal. Upon the last visit prior to this one, my wife noted that the plastic stool used to assist travelers in the Hotel Van to dismount had cracked. This visit, the stool is gone entirely, leaving van occupants to dismount as best as possible. Many of these riders are senior citizens, who cannot make that step down very well. My wife also mentioned that on a recent ride in the van, a gentleman from Oklahoma noted to the driver that the turn signal appeared to be broken. Lastly, over the Holidays, the van was not in service to provide complimentary rides. It was not being fixed. The driver was not available to drive it. The Hotel's choice was to direct passengers to taxi's at their expense. That was a shoddy choice in my estimation, as it would have been very customer oriented to at least pay for the taxi rides when the promised van was not available. While we will still use this property for all of it's other aspects, we and all others should be aware of the issues that should be dealt with in the complimentary van service offerred by the hotel.

“Close (but not quite) perfection” The Peninsula in Chicago is an adventure in extravagance. Our suite was charming; spacious, and with the most extraordinary bathroom I've ever encountered in a hotel, complete with an enormous soaking tub overlooking the Chicago skyline...and a built-in television behind glass, so you could catch the news while indulging in a bubble bath. (It became my habit.) Our bedlinens were crisp and soft at the same time; and control panels for the lights, the radio, the television, and the front door "privacy" light were well-placed throughout the suite, always a finger-touch away. The hotel's public areas are unapologetically grand; amazing vistas, endless ceilings, and gleaming marble floors. Our only complaints? Room service could be a bit time-consuming; it often took forty minutes to an hour (a far longer wait then, say, the Four Seasons in Beverly Hills or the ever-speedy Covent Garden Hotel in London). Once we even placed a simple order (a pot of coffee) and it never arrived. And the valet wasn't too speedy delivering our luggage upon departure; we must have waited fifteen minutes. If the staff can learn the value of alacrity, then this hotel will rapidly become a true favorite of mine.

“Really bad experience” At first glance the Hotel Whitcomb seems like a beautiful old building that offers rooms at very reasonable prices for San Francisco however my experience with this place was beyond sub-par. I don't recommend it to anyone. For starters, I walked into my room and the light switches did nothing and it was pitch black. I held up my cell phone for a source of light, fumbled through the door with my bags and searched for a lamp. I quickly noticed that a large portion of the ceiling was peeling and the room felt dusty. I went to the bathroom and turned on the light and could barely look in the mirror. The light was terrible and made you feel like you were in a morgue. I proceeded to find hair in the sink (GROSS) and promptly tried to get some sleep. As I went to set the alarm I noticed that the clock was off by about 6 hours (helpful). The street noise was pretty bad (which on some levels I would expect...it's in the middle of the city on a busy street) but my room was by dumpsters or something because there was a lot of extra noise directly outside which made sleeping incredibly difficult. The next day I asked the front desk for the free wi-fi code and he informed me it was down and I should try again in the morning. When I went back into my room, I experienced the same issue with the light switches and was immediately frustrated once more. Later that evening after I had finally fallen asleep the people in the room next to me came back and I learned just how thick the walls were. It was a 2nd night of terrible sleep. I woke up feeling positively exhausted and unable to focus well at work. Since this was a business trip I felt really deflated by my stay. Do yourself a favor, research research research and spend the extra cash on a place that promises to give you a decent night of sleep.

“Could use an upgrade” I stayed here for a few night while in business in DC. The hotel was nice enough, but could use an update. I found the decor to be old and dated. I've stayed in some really nice Homewood Suites such as the one in Baltimore, and this one is not up to that one's standard.

“Perfect airport hotel with great shuttle!” Perfect location for our needs...we stayed here 1 night at the beginning and 1 night at the end of our recent vacation to Iceland. The flight times didn't match up for us, and so we needed a place to stay for the night. Their airport shuttle runs 24 hours and was quick and clean. You can sign up for the time you need it in the morning - makes it very convenient, and it's right on time. We also asked if they could take us to a restaurant down the street, and they said he could since he wasn't busy. A nice tip got us a pick-up as soon as we called after we were done. The rooms are nice for this class of hotel, I think they were recently remodeled. They have free wifi and also free long distance calls. They offer free coffee just off of the lobby, but it was basically black hot water. Also, check out the Ginger Palace for a nice breakfast...just a short walk outside of the hotel. We had Domino's Pizza delivered and it came very fast!

“Great hotel - great location” I stayed at the Gansevoort in the Meat Packing District for 4 nights for a recent business trip. I was very pleased with everything about this hotel. Service was fantastic from the front desk to the chambermaids. The room was modern, clean, large for NYC, new, and had a very comfortable bed. The cafe downstairs was great for a morning coffee and the lounge on the main floor was nice for an afternoon drink. Although the wait staff service at the bar was not as good as the rest of the hotel. I did not use the pool or go to the lounge upstairs- I did take a peek and it looked pretty trendy and loud so I went downstairs. I also went the japanese restaurant in the hotel- it was very good. I recommend this hotel- it was my first time in the Meat Packing district (I have stayed in Greenwich Village and Midtown on past visits) and it was my favorite. Great little boutiques, fantastic restaurants (Spice Market!).

“Top Notch Hotel” Overcoming a rocky start due to a reservation mix-up, the Intercontinental Boston won us over with their professional, courteous staff, and a clean, well maintained, comfortable property. Our "Harbor View" room was exceptionally clean, modern and visually interesting. The room featured a nice flat screen television, high quality bedding, a nice work area, your typical over priced "mini-bar" and unique features like special "accent" lighting alongside the bed. The furnishings and carpeting looked new, and the in room artwork gave the room some personality. Hallway and adjoining room noise were minimal, despite the fact our room was next to the ice machine. While technically you could see the Boston Harbor from the window if you contorted and leaned properly, charging extra money for such a limited view seemed gouging. Likewise, the $14.95 a day for in room wi-fi internet seemed a bit steep as well. One interesting feature of the room was the separation between the sleeping area and bathroom. In this case, the two areas were separated by a half wall behind the bed, which featured two sliding frosted glass/wood panels. While it gave the room a modern feel, I would guess that persons with bathroom privacy issues may be uncomfortable. The bathroom itself was ultra clean and large, featuring a deep tub and a glass shower enclosure. I especially appreciated the fact the shower head was over 6 ft. high, with nice water pressure! Complimentary bath products and plush robes were also provided. The hotel lobby provided ample seating areas, and the hotel offers an array of dining/drinking options. We did not visit the pool/spa area, but we were told by other guests it was nice, but not fancy. Hotel staff were pleasant and helpful, even calling our room the first night to inquire if we needed anything to make our stay more enjoyable. While not the most centrally located hotel for Historic Boston, the "South Station - T" stop is a short three minute walk away. From there you can access most attractions within the city in a matter of minutes, including taking the "Silver Line" back to Logan Airport. My wife and I bought $9 all day passes for the "T", easily figured out the route system and which trains to take, and quickly became "T" pros. All in all, I would certainly stay at the Intercontinental Boston again! It's clean, comfortable, safe and quiet...with a efficient, knowledgable staff intent on making your stay enjoyable.

“Merry Christmas - Had a great time here over Christmas !” We arrived on Christmas Eve and stayed her over the festive period - we are so pleased that we picked this hotel. Great location, very contemporary and the staff were welcoming. Our room had a fire which was great, you phone down and a staff member brings you a log, lights it for you, checks that it is OK and then he leaves you to it ! Perfect for the season and the weather outside. We would definetely stay here again and highly recommend this hotel. The only negative was that they do not always have someone to help with your luggage which can be difficult sometimes with the steps and our tip is do not look for the Red door when you drive up the street for the first time, they have painted it a different colour !!!

“Zweckmässiges Hotel an guter Lage” Standardmässiges Holiday Inn Hotel an guter Lage in Manhattan. Zimmer zweckmässig, allerdings sehr klein, und auch das Badezimmer war winzig. Aber dafür war der Preis für NYC-Verhältnisse sehr gut und damit das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis sehr akzeptabel. U-Bahnen und Shopping ganz in der Nähe, das Hotel ist damit auch von den Flughäfen her sehr gut zu erreichen.

“OK Hotel for City Center” We recently stayed for one night here. The hotel appears to be a renovated, retouched older property and most likely needs another touch-up. Its main attraction is that it is close to the baseball stadium and Inner Harbor - within walking distance or a short taxi ride. Rooms are standard size which look smaller than they are because of the massive furniture which has seen better days. The bathroom is European size cozy. However, bathroom towels and all the linen is clean and fresh. The bed and the mattress are very comfortable for a good night's sleep; and it is quiet. The staff is quite pleasant too.

“OK - but could be so much better” The variation in the standard of rooms at this hotel is enormous - some look really nice and some are barely OK. This, sadly, means that the customers with the loudest voices will get preferential treatment and upgrades - if you like to avoid confrontation, you will most likely have to put up with a shabby room. Room 1431 is definitely one of the poorer rooms - air con/heating was madly noisy even when switched off! (and didn't work that well, either); decor was really tired with torn wallpaper, scuffed paintwork and worn carpet. Bath did not drain properly, meaning you take a shower standing in 6 inches of water! On the plus side, the room was quiet (apart from the heating!) - no sounds from other rooms and traffic noise not a problem. This is a budget hotel, and unless you get a really poor room as I did, it does offer a very good deal for a NYC stay. Location and cleanliness were both excellent. Rooms were cleaned very efficiently every day. However, the service is very impersonal - even downright frosty at times. Check in desk staff are admittedly busy, but could make an effort to be more friendly - it doesn't cost anything, guys! And in 5 days, not a single doorman offered me so much as a smile, never mind a 'hello'. Apart from one very nice and efficient man who organised a car to the airport for me, no staff member made any effort to offer me any more than the barest minimum of politeness. The diner (Park Cafe) attached to the hotel is great. Efficient, friendly staff and excellent basic diner fare, served with a smile until 1am. The elevators worked fine and I never had to wait more than a few moments. The lobby has hardly any seating, and at busy check-in/check-out times, it can be quite chaotic and unpleasant. It reminded me of being at an airport where all the flights have been suddenly cancelled!

“One table in breakfast area” Stayed here one night. Close to Hobby but neighborhood is scary; includes 24 hours check cashing store and homeless people. Room was OK for one night. Didn't have any WiFi problems. Breakfast consited of a waffle maker, coffee, juice with one table/6 chairs. I certainly do not want to sit next to people who just woke up unshowered. It was tight like 737 seating. Will spend the extra $ for a Holiday Inn Express next time.

“Good Bargain” Our stay was an unplanned trip, and we didn't put much thought into where we were staying. Rooms were paid by the company, and we picked it based on name and location. We were happy to see that the choice was a good one. Service was great at check in, and the lounge service was excellent as well. Rooms were spotless, and breakfast buffet was very good. I would recommend this hotel for any business travelers. The only thing I would recommend would be to leave with a little extra time to allow for traffic, since the location is near the airport as well as several busy highways. Overall, just a good experience for the rate we paid.

“A good option” We booked through Hotwire and got a rate of $58 which made the stay seem very reasonable. I would be hard pressed to pay the $129 a night found through their website. The location is central to the galleria and right off the tollway (you can avoid paying the toll by staying on the service road). We were able to park right out front and enter into what is an enormous lobby. The staff was friendly but I did think they were trying to upsale us. Upon check-in we were asked if we wanted to spend $15 to upgrade to a "remodeled" room. They just need to do all the rooms remodeled and up the price for all rooms. The facility and public spaces are very nice. The room itself that we got was big by normal hotel standards. The furniture and room itself was clean and not run down, but does look a bit tired. The best part of the room was the down top mattress, water pressure, and size of room. The amenities of coffee and toiletries were adequate as well. I would stay here again at the hotwire price but not over $100 a night.

“Best W ever!” The best W we know! The Front desk staff was so helpful and caring especially the manager. I broke my ankle while in town and they were so amazingly helpful and accommodating! Normally, W's kind of fell like a night club, you have to look the look or they'll shrug you off. This W still looked like the night club, but the acted like the St. Regis. Thank you!! The rooms were very nice and had great views of the city. Surely the best value for your dollar in town.

“Fitzpatrick - lovely on the inside” I stayed in the smallest room, which was still relatively large and very nice. The rooms seem like they have been renovated recently, and they are very tastefully decorated. I had a room in the back (2707), and I faced directly into the windows of an adjacent office building that was a short distance away. I hope that the more expensive rooms have a better view.The hotel looked rather plain on the outside as I approached from Michigan Avenue, but it turned out to be very nice inside. The location is great - only a block and a half from the Water Tower on Michigan Avenue, and only 3.5 blocks from the Red Line Chicago subway station (not the Blue Line Chicago station). The neighborhood felt very safe, and there are a number of restaurants nearby.One review I read said that rooms have VCRs in them, but mine did not. Also, the TV was relatively small - 20 inches, I think. The room did have a nice CD player and radio, however.I would definitely stay there again.

“Great Stay” This is a wonderful and innovative hotel. The arrival is concierge style. Guests have a seat while the very friendly representatives check them in. We were helped by Sako. She was mindful of our anniversary, friendly and efficient. For New York, the rooms are enormous. There is a walk-in shower with waterfall head (practically a room of its own) with a separate bathtub enclosed in the tile area. The sink area and separated toilet are across the foyer. The room itself features a small refrigerator with free nonalcoholic drinks and a few snacks. The design of the room is different than anything else I have experienced. Next to the sink, there is a large piece of furniture that works as a closet, full-length mirror and cabinets. Turns out the piece of furniture spins around. Wonderful feature. The flat screen is on a long desk/table that is separated from the wall. There is seating on both sides. The windows also have seating and a comfy chair is in the corner. The bed is on the firmer side with a nice duvet. We admittedly got a kick out of the lighting/shade panel. Lighting around the room can be shut off completely, set to a relax mode or turned up full in addition to other settings. The blackout shades are also controlled on that panel. There is a wine hour from 6p-8p with snacks. Muffins are served in the morning and coffee is complimentary throughout the day. Wonderful touches! It is only fair to mention the negatives. The modern faucet continues to drip after being turned off which can be an annoyance. On a more imporant note, the staff is super friendly, but lacking in local knowledge. Coming out of the Holland Tunnel, we asked for directions and the agent at the other end had to look up directions. Any staff member answering the phone should know that. We wound up finding our own way. We asked a front desk agent (not the one who checked us in) for an Indian restaurant nearby. Again, she did not know and hit google maps. The result was one restaurant no longer in existence and another that changed names and was a dump. Overall, I would definitely stay at the hotel again. I would just not rely on the staff for recommendations.

“So So” There now. Its ok, clean, small rooms, no microwave/refrigerator. Low end breakfast, limited cereal selection, only 1 waffle maker. No problems with staff. If driving, I did see a sign indicating allow 40 minutes for valet retrieval, parking is evidently not on site. Not exactly in the middle of things, in fact, I wouldn't go too far noth or east after dark. Not a bad walk to metro in the other direction tho. Likely one of the more reasonably priced properties around so its full of school groups. Its principle redeeming point as far as I'm concerned is its the only Choice hotel in the district after a few years without one.

“Above average corporate hotel” I've spent an extended weekend at the Radisson Blu Aqua. Impressive architecture, not so impressive interiors, although some effort was clearly put in the design of the lobby and rooms. The lobby is unattended, and serves as an over the top waiting room. Not really my idea of a lobby, but it was comfortable and had an inviting fireplace. The bar and restaurant is across the hall should you want something to drink or eat. Regular food, decently priced, nice-ish design. I got a somewhat small standard room, comfortable and practical, but nothing special. The sparkling floor and countertops were a bit disturbing, as they produced a "disco ball" effect on the walls. The closet, in all its shiny silver glory was way too small. Great bed though. Service was average throughout, with the exception of the doormen, who didn't greet or respond to greetings, and pretty much just hanged around the door. There was a nice little executive lounge which resembled a dentists waiting room, probably the liveliest place in the property. To sum it up, hospitality wise the experience is as bland as you can imagine, and If the building wasn't the architectural gem it is, the entire hotel would define the word banal.

“O.K. if you do not use room service” I found that the check in was efficient, friendly and cordial. I really liked the welcome green tea. The front doorman was especially considerate of the fact that it was cold out. My room was pleasant and well appointed. My big disappointment was breakfast room service. Room service just could not get the order right, even though I ordered only things that were on the menu. Even lunch room service was not right. I checked out one day early as I just was not looking forward to another breakfast being botched. Also, when all I wanted to do is report the error, room service insisted on sending a manager to talk to me. It told them no that I was busy, which I was. They would not listen to me and sent a manager anyhow. I could not believe how much emphasis room service put on not giving me what I requested and only giving me what they decided was good enough for me to have. Although the mall is convenient by accessing it from the third floor via a hallway, I also believe this is a security risk for the hotel. There are no live eyes that can see this hallway. The fitness area is pleasant with the light from the windows. Swimming int he lap pool was excellent. Windows on three sides is quite pleasant. The location is too far of a walk from Fifth Avenue to my liking. Others may like it being near Time Warner. I paid over $2,600 for two nights. I would have to rating this a five star with all five star rating to say that it was worth the money.

“Great bargain, unique decor, "security" obnoxious” This is a great hotel in a great location in that rotten cesspool called NYC (Never going there again, ever! Suck it, NYC!) People were generally polite, the gift shop pricing was actually reasonable (compared to the shady tchotchke shops on the rotten streets of rotten NYC), rooms were clean and remained clean, and the art deco decor was a wonder to see. The excellent location ensures that you can just get on the bus or train and go anywhere quickly. The only bad experience came from the rent-a-security douches who insist on stopping you every g-d time you tried to get to the elevators to get to your room. May be this was for some imagined security concerns but it made a nice hotel feel like a darned prison - not cool at all. Still, very highly recommended - this place is pretty cool.

“Good place to stay, but it could be better” Overall, I had a good stay. I did not purchase anything at the hotel restaurants so I can't say anything about the food there. I was disappointed that the gift shop did not have milk, and I wasn't about to pay what they wanted in the restaurant for a glass of milk. I didn't try the swimming pool and workout area. The main reason is that they were in a separate tower. It seemed a little inconvenient to take the elevator down, walk across the lobby to the other tower and then take the elevator up to wherever that was located. I was also disappointed in the internet service. I tried to connect from my room, but the connection was slow and did not work for very long. I eventually went downstairs to the lobby to use the free internet which worked much better. The hotel was very good about refunding the price of the internet service that I had paid for, but if they are going to make you pay they should at least offer dependable service. Another thing that I didn't like is that they did not give me all of the credit for my stay with the Starwood points program. I only got credit for $2 worth of expenses for a 4 night stay, so I had to send proof of my expenses to get credit for the rest of the expenses. Otherwise, I was satisfied with the room. It was a good size, and everything was in working order. But I definitely wouldn't call this an "Excellent" stay.

“I'll be back” I go to San Francisco really often for work or leisure reasons and this time I wanted to make an hotel change. Before I went to Mandarin Oriental and then Westin St. Francis, both wonderful hotels but, this time, I've been really surprised by Grand Hyatt San Francisco. Starting from the hotel staff, helpful, kind and so professional. Anne S. and Oscar L. tks a lot for your warm welcome. The hotel is totally renewed, the rooms are amazing and the beds really comfortable. I had a room at the 28th floor and the view of the city skyline from my full-size window was stunning. The hotel is located in the best position in SF, near all the city tourist attractions or financial district if you're there for business. I'll be back! this is my new choice because... I left my heart in San Francisco and Grand Hyatt helped me on that.

“Great Location” Stayed here on a last minute staycation. The location is perfect! Although the hotel is not fancy.....it is very clean. This can be a challenge anywhere near the beach, but the room was immaculate and didn't smell musty. Our patio opened up to the pool and hot tub...which was awesome! Definitely a great place to stay to be in the middle of it all!

“No Complaints” Stayed over night for a visit to TCU. Received a TCU discount. Everything worked as expected, room was clean and upgraded. We asked for a room further away from I20 and didn't have any problem with freeway noise. The location was convenient and easy to find. We didn't eat out there, but there are several nice restaurants within walking distance, and it's not far from downtown. Free WiFi worked without a hitch and was fast. Not much else to say. We literally just slept overnight then left. Skipped the breakfast but it looked like the standard quick-eat setup at all the hotels in this class.

“Good service and location marred by high noise levels” The Henley Park is in a great location at the very heart of Washington, no more than a few minutes walk from many attractions. The lobby, with its pleasant dark wooded interior, looks more like a university college than a hotel. The room was small (mine had no table to work on) and the bath was pretty tiny, but the shower was good and the water was always hot. I liked the bed. The service was low-key and efficient. I ordered a fresh green salad at 9 pm and it arrived in less than 15 minutes. In the morning I explained to the restaurant staff that I was in a hurry and needed to eat breakfast quickly. They delivered my food inside five minutes and it was excellent. The rather large drawback was the noise. My room (607) looked out right over the air conditioning unit of a building on the other side of 10th and the din was so loud I barely slept. A colleague of mine in 307 had exactly the same problem. There is no insulation in the rooms, so even the smallest noise carries. Just as I did start managing to nod off I was woken up at 6:30 am (this happened every morning) by a large gang of construction workers and their loudly beeping vehicles. If this hotel could sort out the noise issues it would be a winner.

“Nice hotel, but some problems...” The Grand Hyatt Washington is a nice, modern hotel located in downtown Washington, D.C. The lobby consists of a multi-level atrium with ample food opportunities, including Starbucks Coffee, the Grand Cafe (which is the hotel's restaurant), a sports bar, and a deli. There were also a couple of gift shops. Upon check-in, the staff were very friendly, promptly directing me to my room. When I arrived in my room, I was met by a nice, spacious room. The bathroom was nice and clean. The main problem with the room was the cleanliness of the bed and the carpet. The carpet appeared older and dirty. The bed also had at least two (2) hairs on it, and a stain here and there. This may bother you (as it did me) if you are highly concerned about cleanliness. (The room wasn't disgusting, but it wasn't spotless...) Also, when the air-conditioner would come on at night, it would make a loud click as it switched on. (Slightly annoying if you are trying to sleep, but you'll get over it.) Overall, my stay at the Grand Hyatt Washington was adequate, but not spectacular. The lobby/atruim was nice, the staff and concierge were very friendly and helpful, and the location was good. The main problem was the cleanliness of our room.

“Darn great value !” This is an older hotel that offer great value for a clean and comfortable room. The hotel is clean, quiet and neat; though the layout and is somewhat dated. The staff is friendly and couteous. The hallways and elevators are somewhat small and cramped. The guest rooms are plenty spacious. The bathrooms are also very small; typical of older hotel designs. Each room has a 4-cup cofee maker, a small fridge, and a safe. The work desk and chair are adequate size and comfy. The HVAC system is very responsive (though a little bit noisy) - it cooled the room from 76 to 69 in just a few minutes. The free wifi has a very week signal on the floor I occupied (9th); also, the internet service was S L O W W W W W. Between 4PM and 10Pm, it is impossible to use the internet service in any expedient or meaningful way. The lobby level bar is small but friendly. There is a restaurant, but I did not get a chance to try it. This hotel is located in a convenient and seemingly safe area, it only cost me $6 to take a cab ride to the Whitehouse each day. I never waited more than one minute to catch a cab any time of the day or evening. There is a wonderful Whole Foods store just around the corner, nearby other various local neighborhood restaurants.

“Classic - Pure DC” We hosted a business meeting here. Fantastic meeting room, and great service from the staff, they were flexible and fast with last minute changes. The hotel oozes history and elegance. My room was much larger than expected for such an old hotel, especially the bathroom. The location is prime for anyone wanting to explore the city. Expect to pay a lot for food and drink.

“Convenient Location” Good location across Faneuil Hall, Quincy Market and the Government Center. The staff was very helpful and courteous. The room was clean and comfortable although it was quite small for a suite. Our room had a nice balcony with table and chairs. Although the bath anemities were generic, they were a decent quality. The bathroom was very spacious. We were on the 8th floor and there are only 5 rooms on that floor which made for a very nice and quiet stay. Decor throughout hotel is simple and minimal. Room service was excellent - the English muffins are made at the hotel and are wonderful. The hotel restaurant was also very good with very reasonable prices. Cons: Our towels were pretty shabby and should be replaced; our balcony had tacky "plastic" greenery in the planter boxes; in order to reach our room on the 8th floor, we had to take two different elevators - the first lets you off on the 7th floor and you wind around the 7th floor to reach the elevator that takes you to the 8th floor. The hotel does not have a gift/sundries shop. Valet parking is $45 a day.

“Great hotel in an excellent location” We stayed in the "historic" part, which got us a rather large and comfortable room. Hotel was reasonably quiet, very convienent, and the room was large, comfortable and clean. No complaints, would stay here again. We did not eat at the restaurant or use any of the other services.

“Good room, pity about the bar staff” Rooms are compact, but fine for a couple of days. Not sure that it was really "times square" but not too far off. Bathroom was a little disconcerting, with a calico (read see through) curtain across the shower area and a glass door that didn't close flush with the wall for the toilet. Nothing much was left the imagination of the other occupant of the room. All that aside the room was everything that was promised by the website. Pity about the bar staff - they clearly want a certain type of customer, of which a couple in their 30's who don't want to get overly dressed up (jeans & t-shirts) to have a beer were not the type. Service was slow (not a busy time). In summary, stay at the hotel, but find another bar, of which there are plenty around, to have a drink after a day of sightseeing.

“Decidedly mixed reaction for the Hamilton CP Washington” The Hamilton Crowne Plaza is well-located to McPherson Square and directly across the street from Franklin Square, This makes in a nice alternate in that area if you have events at the Grand Hyatt or the Renaissance Washington, two larger convention hotels that are within about a six-block walk. The finish at the CP Hamilton is nice and housekeeping seems decent, but the hotel's overall culture of service seems to be spotty. (Don't expect any extras for being platinum PC, for example.) On the plus side, we liked the streetside outdoor seating for the restaurant and we were able to the get toothbrushes replaced that the maid kindly threw away for us after the first night. There was a $109/night weekend rate available during our stay which is certainly a bargain for this quality of property in Washington DC. It is convenient to the metro system, too. The neighborhood itself has some amenities such as places to eat or grab a cup of coffee, but it is certainly not as well-blessed with these as the Dupont Circle neighborhood. Negative aspects include the internet service provided by Wayport Access, a third-party vendor. We found it very intermittent and at $9.95 per day, certainly no bargain for the very mediocre service. We could open the window in our room, but it is one of those annoying systems that maxes out at about two inches. In summary, the Hamilton Crowne Plaza is a decent hotel, but not one that we would put on our "must return" list in Washington. For a good rate, it's not a bad choice.

“Nice hotel, airports veRy loud” This hotel is your basic Sheraton, good service, reasonable rates, and the rooms are good.....nothing to brag about but, good. The airport does get loud but that's what you should expect from a hOtel in this area. Basically the hotel served my needs

“Convenient, Quaint, Affordable and a Great Value for your money” I was only in New York City for one night to celebrate a birthday with some friends and found this hotel through a great deal on a discount hotel website (I am all about the discounts and moderately priced hotels). While the lobby is incredibly small and the elevators can be slow, the room was decently sized and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was amply stocked with some nice amenities and the towels were very plush. The closet space is incredibly SMALL. I was only there for one night so this was not an issue for me. I would not recommend staying more than a weekend here. It seems best for short stays. The staff were SUPER friendly and called my room 30 minutes after I checked in to see if everything was OK.
“Great location and beautiful spacious rooms” Even during lobby construction, had a great stay, wonderful front desk personnel.
“Very average, convinient locatino for business traveler” Average stay, clean...good, comfortable bed. TVs need updating.

“Clean & Modern” Valet parking: $32 Self-parking garage: $24 but no in/out priv. HOWEVER, we were able to save tons of money bc we checked in past 6pm so we parked across the street. Meters don't get checked until 8am so we just put in quarters ($.025 for ever 12 min) until we checked-out at 11:30. Cleanliness: Perfect Customer Service: Professional & upgrade given @ check-in Gym: Perfectly adequate and new machines Pool: Small & narrow but cool if you like city views A couple blocks from Horton Plaza (Major mall & theater), Gaslamp District (restaurants & stores) Noise level: Can hear police sirens from street (we were on 16th floor) and people talking in the next room. This wouldn't be my first choice for families or those looking for a romantic weekend. I felt it was perfect for business travelers.

“What a Great Place!” What a great place! The neighborhood seemed a little dicey at first, but it's lively and crowded and very New York and very safe. My room was huge, immaculate, and quiet with great views and (more importantly) a great shower. The staff couldn't have been more helpful and friendly. The hotel is walking distance to anywhere - and do walk if you get the chance; it's the best way to experience the city - and if you can't walk to where you're going, the subway is only a block away. I'll definitely stay there again.

“This is a fine place to stay in SouthPark” I see a lot of mediocre reviews on this hotel and I really don't understand them. This is a Courtyard. It's not a Marriott, it's not a Renaissance, and it's not a Ritz. It's the Courtyard part of the chain. So OF COURSE it's not going to be one of these higher end hotels. But if you're wanting to stay in the SouthPark area at a GREAT value, this is an outstanding choice. Actually, it's the BEST choice. None of the other hotels nearby come close to the value of this hotel. Are the rooms clean? Yes. Was the stay quiet? Yes. Did I feel safe and comfortable? Yes. Yes to those 3 questions makes this a solid 3-star hotel. The fact that it is such a good value and the great area that it is in gives it another star. I will GLADLY stay here every time I'm in the SouthPark area of Charlotte.

“Very Good Service and Accommodations” We stayed here as part of a conference in town; the conference sponsors had already booked us here. Our experience was excellent. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was spacious, large enough for us to have a meeting before our presentation. The countertops were granite with a wet bar and fridge, and the TV was huge. The room oozed comfort and thoughtfulness, and it was clean. When we reported that our coffeemaker was not working, Josh, an employee, courteously brought a replacement to our room within five minutes of our call to the front desk, and he plugged it in and tried it out to make sure it worked. That's service! The continental breakfast was adequate. The whole idea of semi-fast food for purchase in the lobby seemed a bit awkward, but I suppose it would work well for a harried traveler. Also, highway noise was noticeable but not overwhelming in our room.

“Sehr freundliches Personal, ordentliche Unterkunft für Urlaub” Das Personal - sogar der Bellman - ist SEHR freundlich. Man nimmt sich Zeit, gibt Tipps, sehr persönliches Ambiente, man fühlt sich - trotz des Großststadthotels - sehr willkommen. Die Zimmer sind zwar nicht sonderlich modern, bis auf die Badewanne aber sehr sauber und für ein paar Nächte wirklich gut. Preis/Leistung stimmt hier wirklich. Nachmittags gibt es immer kostenfrei eine "Weinprobe" im Hotel, sodass man auch auf andere Gäste trifft. ZuRr Fishermans Wharf kommt man mit dem Bus für 2 Dollar in 10 Minuten, die Bushaltestelle liegt etwa 300-500m vom Hotel entfern, sehr einfach zu finden! Das Wifi ist leider sehr langsam (aber kostenfrei), nicht einmal Sprachtelefonate per Skype klappen hierüber. Ich würde hier wieder übernachten!

“Nice touches that made it special” We stayed here for an Anniversary weekend getaway in Dallas and we were very impressed with the rooms and the service! We were treated to excellent service, including some perks at Charlie Palmer's and PM Lounge. I could not have had a more relaxing anniversary weekend. Front desk even followed up to see how everything was going with our stay. They also have an Escalade car service to take you to dinner reservations or anywhere within (I think) 5 miles of the hotel. Even with it being first come, first serve, the service only had about a 10 minute wait on a Saturday night. The room details were well thought out. Although the room we were in was a bit small, they had really nice decor and details that you would not see a Marriott or a Hilton, IMHO. The photos were interesting, the bathrooms unique, and the bed was really comfortable. It was essentially a "funky" modern look that suited us great. The only drawback was that the room faced a dilapidated building next door and they were doing construction on that side to extend the hotel (no construction noise on the weekend, just a view of the construction and rundown building!). Valet was pricey, but much preferred over worrying about my car in one of the nearby parking lots overnight. I will hopefully be back -- as the revitalized Main St. has a lot of action on the weekends and this hotel sits right in the middle! BTW, the pool and PM Lounge are really cool!

“Decent stay. Good price. Nothing bad to report.” Stayed overnight on a Saturday. Front clerk wasn't very nice, but it didn't ruin my stay. Room was clean and had everything in it that was needed (micro, fridge, cable, internet, a/c, etc.). Bed was ok. Didn't hear much noise. Breakfast was basic. Pool was small but clean. Located directly off I-35S. Decent stay overall. Would return for same price (less than $50).

“Good Option for Denver, CO” Stayed in a corner room. Quiet, clean and comfortable. Frette sheets, nice pillows. Nice bathroom and sitting area. Would defn stay here again. As far as upmarket hotels in Denver, there appears to be two options, the Ritz Carlton and Hotel Teatro. This is probably a better pick. I would think the Teatro is less corporate and homoegenous. The staff seemed friendly, well mannered and happy.

“A Little Gem in the Big City” I had picked this hotel to stay after a late-ish arrival at PHX the day before our American Southwest Roadtrip, mainly on the reviews here. However, the reviews on Tripadvisor do not do it justice. This hotel is truly a little gem in a huge city such as Phoenix. The impressive service started at the airport where our shuttle driver offered us cold water from a cooler. It went down very well considering we had arrived in the early evening and temps were still hovering around 100F. On arrival, the evening desk clerk was extremely welcoming and friendly, even throwing in a free breakfast buffet when we asked. Warm freshly-baked cookies were also offered as well. The room was a decent size, and nicely decorated with an extremely comfortable bed. The only downside is when we arrived to our room, there were dirty dishes and trays from breakfast on the hallway floor right at our door. When we mentioned it to the clerk, they were taken away promptly with apologies. Location-wise, it is in a deserted area maybe bordering on seedy. However, it is very safe walking around the area, albeit a bit deserted. Other reviewers noted there is an In and Out Burger "right across the street" when in reality, it is 5 miles away. There is really nothing nearby food-wise within walking distance, except for a Bill Johnson's Big Apple a short walk away, which offers decent diner food with good service. We didn't try the hotel restaurant other than the buffet breakfast in the morning. The breakfast is excellent with great choices and the hotel serves one of the best omelets we've ever had, hands down. From check-in to check-out, the staff at this hotel can't do enough for you, always smiling, pleasant and professional. In reality if Phoenix were our destination we would probably choose a more central hotel, but for arriving at the airport to go to other destinations this is absolutely going to be our go-to place to stay. Kudos to the management and staff for such a great accommodation.

“Bravo to Drury Plaza Hotel!” After comparing hotels for price and proximity to the Riverwalk, I chose the very new Drury Plaza Hotel for our 3 night July 4th holiday trip. We couldn't have made a better choice, and recommend it highly! On arrival, we were immediately impressed with the historic building, which was previously a bank. The 23 floor hotel has a perfect location, and one can access the Riverwalk by taking the hotel's elevator or stairs to river level. We booked a King room for 2 adults and a toddler, and to our pleasant surprise, received an upgrade to a King two-room suite. The room was fresh, clean and spacious. The view of the city was great. The complete breakfast each morning was a good way to start the day, and had something for everyone. Afternoon cocktails were nice as well. All of the Drury Plaza Hotel's staff members were friendly and courteous. I applaud Drury for making a great addition to the Riverwalk.

“Excellent Service” The staff at the Century City Hyatt make this a delightful place to stay. The service is highly professional and very attentive to detail. Every single interaction was delightful. The rooms are also large, very clean and well appointed. I very much enjoyed sitting on the balcony and watching the sunset in the evenings. I was at the hotel for a conference and the meals at the conference were defintely well above average. The only thing I could really find any fault with was that the price was high (over $300 / night), however this is Los Angeles and this is a prime location. Great hotel, great staff, great location and the price tage to go with it.

“Ok hotel, horrible location” The hotel is nice, same level of cleanliness and service as all Renaissance hotels. The front desk staff (girls) were really unfriendly and caty and unhelpful, so I had to go back a few times to request something until someone was nice enough to listen to my request. Besides them, everyone else at this hotel was SUPER friendly! The hotel's location is not really great, it's in a rather shady area. Next time I go to Denver on a business trip, I'll stay in downtown.

“Not sure why it's called a luxury hotel” It was just fine but no where near luxury. Husband and I stayed July 23-26, 2009 with our 4 yr old daughter and booked this place b/c it has a kitchen. When I booked the junior suite on quikbook.com at $212/night I was thrilled. I called to confirm and was told the bed room was separate from the living room, which to me means there is a door separating them. Not so, at least not in our room, 2105. The sofabed was very shabby looking, circa 1970s. I noticed a few rips in the fabric. My daughter slept on it and did not complain. She was happy to have her own bed to jump on. The kitchen was a plus though we only used the fridge. The bathroom was fine. My daughter and I both fit in the shower with plenty of room for her to play with the water. Our bed was comfy enough. I really can't complain about the place other than being told our bedroom was a separate room. One minor complaint: their website says they have flat screen TVs. Not in our room! It was fine but I wouldn't go back. I'd rather spend my money at a place like the Grand Hyatt with much nicer furnishings.

“GO TO NORMA'S” Okay so I consider this hotel much more than a hotel and that is why I love it. The room's have been slightly touched up recently (carpets and wall paper). Also, for NYC the rooms are spacious. The best part is what the hotel has on site... Norma's - The best breakfast... ever. Moonshine - The coolest/unique spa... ever The gym is HUGE. Its a urban resort...Enjoy!

“Average Hotel with a great location” We were expecting a bit more when we saw the hotel's website. The room was average. I am still wondering what the ammenities are. The bathroom clearly needs updating. A plastic shower curtain? No room to really move at all. The lighting is awful in the bathroom area. However, the room was clean. The elevators were quick. Our first night, we called down for more towels. When we came back, they never came. There is no turn down service, but the sign said that we could call at your service anytime. We did love the location....across from the Galleria. It's the fourth largest mall in the US. There are lots of restaurants nearby. Some are walking distance. The hotel offers a shuttle. They were great the first day. The next day, we called three times to get picked up, not even a half mile away, and were told the first time the shuttle was available. The next two...they are on the way. We ended up taking a cab, as we had an appointment to get to. The staff was very nice. We did ask for a neighborhood, area to check out restaurants, shops. We wanted to see more than just the galleria area. No one had any ideas. We found that unusual...but the concierge was not there that day. She did call our room the next day to offer assistance, but we were locked into plans with a group. All in all, a great location...just don't expect anything more than an average hotel.

“One night stay” This was a very nice hotel with a few issues. There were issues with the hot water not getting to my room, so they had to move me. They were very nice about it and gave me a gift basket for the inconvenience. The room is a studio suite and the layout is very nice and open. The bathroom had been remodeled, so now it is a large walk in shower instead of a bathtub with a shower. There was a coffee maker and a refrigerator, but no microwave. There is a nice desk area, but the plugs for the computer did not work. The hotel is a not easy to get into or out of and there was some construction. The lobby and the breakfast were both nice and the help was very nice. Now that I know how to get there, I would stay again.

“Boston's Best ! The Westin Copley!” A quick getaway to Boston from CT was needed, so I checked the prices to stay the weekend of 11/10 and sure enough the prices were through the roof... $350 + for anywhere. Have no fear priceline was near! www.priceline.com, went on, booked the Westin for $175.00 Whooo hooo! My weekend getaway was complete! We checked in early...about 10:30 a.m. Very easy check in. For people wanting to know about the area. You cannot go wrong booking this centrally located Boston hotel. It is in the middle of EVERYTHING, whether you want to shop, walk, eat, Duck tour it...etc. Our room was on the 30th floor! The views were to die for! The bed was all dressed in white linens and was the most comfy thing ever! After checking in we went for a bite to eat... we walked through the mall and went to the Pour House. (Boylston Street) We have been there before, so we knew it was good. We walked to Fenway because I had to get an Ellsbury T- shirt! GO SOX!!! We also shopped around a little on Newbury St here and there. At night we chose the Cactus Club, very good Mexican Restaurant for some drinks. We stopped by Lir a bar/restaurant. We also stopped by Whiskeys bar/restaurant for a quick bite and Solas an Irish Pub outside the Lenox Hotel. The BAR 10 inside the hotel was definitely hoppin', but we opted to go to bed when we got back. Wait... actually, we ran out to the 24 hr Shaws, which is right next door for some snacks and then to bed it was! The Westin is great! The employees are nice, the pool is small, but I would've jumped in! The workout area seems very legit as well. Nice equipment! You have tons of restaurants to choose from and the mall is under your feet! The next morning we took a walk to Gov't center- Quincy Market... about a 15 minute walk or so. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. And if the price seems to steep, try priceline. Enjoy your stay!

“Great Amenities in New York” We stayed just a few nights ago and were very satisfied. It is not the typical "suburban" Staybridge rooms but they do have kitchenettes as opposed to kitchens. Free reception three nights a week (Tues-Thurs) and breakfast daily which were both sufficient. About 2 blocks north and 3 blocks east from the heart of Times Square. The hotel is connected to a Fairfield Inn and a Four Points. The staff were friendly and the hotel very clean and modern. The location on this street is next to a few adult stores which wasn't ideal but people kept to themselves. We were booked at another hotel until the night before we happened to check and got this for $105 AAA plus tax. VERY GOOD RATE for New York. Overall would stay again and would recommend.

“Clean, comfortable, and a great location” Stayed at the Courtyard this week. From arrival to departure, my stay was flawless. The room was clean, very well layed out, and the bathroom was large. The lobby looked busy for breakfast, I did not get to try it. Internet service was good in the room.

“Disappointed” This hotel is not up to Hilton standards. The decor of the hotel is very dated and run down, espicially in the hallways with guest rooms. Service at the front desk was very rude, I felt like I was bothering them when I called to tell them the room they had given me had a clogged shower. I feel they could swap the sign on the hotel with that of Comfort Inn and no one would notice. I was very disappointed.

“Top drawer!” Absolutely perfect! Great location near the metro and walking distance to the zoo. Right on RockcreeK Park. Very nice area to run in cruise down the park and up Embassy Row. Hotel staff was great. Upgraded us to a very nice suite with balcony and great view.

“Business hotel, no personal attention, they ignore your requests” Good location. I had Room 2967 from June 6 to 11 for a weeklong business trip. Good value for corporate rate. My flight was delayed until after 4 am and room was held for me with my Amex guarantee, albeit with two beds. Fast service, other than room service which could use some more efficiency. I ordered my 2nd night and got the wrong plate and decided to eat dinner before returning the other nights to avoid a 45 minute wait for someone else's order. What annoyed me is that when I checked in, I noted my room was dark and had a very large burn mark on the carpeting (a foot long). I did not care as I was exhaused and it is a business trip. However, my safe was also locked and I had to call Security to open it for me so that I could use it. When the security man arrived, he saw the burn and asked me what I did very accusingly and rudely. I told him I had been at the hotel for less than ten minutes and it was a sign of poor maintenance by the hotel and he should report it so that he problem could be fixed while I was working on Tuesday. No one ever came to fix it, communicate to me about the problem, etc. This, after a hotel employee accused me of burning the rug. I was just a faceless guest and I had no time to waste at the front desk, etc. On my final night (5th night), I had a voice mail from a desk clerk calling me by the name of another guest asking if my room was OK. As I was checking out in less than 8 hours, I did not bother to return her call. I liked the voice mail checkout as whenever I am in NY, I take an early flight out and the cashiers are never ready in any hotel for me. Odd - no mini bars. Room service trays that I saw at 7 pm were still in the hallway at 8 am, little attention in the evenings to cleaning. I would stay again if the New York Palace, where I prefer to stay, is sold out again the next time.

“Was fantastic for me” I stayed here for four nights in late October using Hilton Honors points. Advertised room rate for that time period was around $399 per night--not completely tragic but that would start to add up after a few nights. Room was the biggest I've ever had in NYC. It was a true suite with two separate rooms and a nice sized bathroom. Living area had a full sized desk and couch, large TV, wet bar, and mini bar. Room was very quiet--I would have never have known I was in the middle of Times Square had I not looked out the window at all the neon lights. Curtains were more than able to block out the light however. My one complaint with regards to the room is the in-room paid internet access. I had constant problems with connectivity. I found that the signal was "fighting" with the complimentary Hilton signal. The Hilton signal would override the paid internet but then was blocked since I was in my room. Lesson learned: just go down to the lobby and use the free access. This is a bit of a limited service hotel however. The lobby is on the third floor, which necessitates two elevators to come and go from your room to the outside. The lobby lever is somewhat small, with a small but sharp bar with friendly bartenders and free internet in the lobby. The restaurant where I had a free breakfast each morning wasn't better than O.K.--however I was not looking to the hotel to provide my nourishment. Overall, I would definitely come back. The location is great, the rooms are very comfortable, and the functionality is perfect for my needs.

“Nice, but beware if you are not into "uber-modern"” We stayed here for three nights on a recreation trip. First impressions: Very modern building, obviously newer. (When I looked at Google Maps, it still shows a dirt lot, so I guess it's that new.) Front desk was very polite and helpful, as well as knowledgeable about the area. The room was very good sized and quite "modern", but that can serve as a downfall for some, which I'll explain later. The good: Bed was large and comfortable, lots of pillows. TV was large enough for the room size, with decent amount of channels. I don't know what some of the other reviewers had for breakfast, but we had NO issues with food quality or selections available. I think sometimes, people expect Bob Evans quality (which is right next door, btw), but want if for free for all of their family, instead of dropping $$$ at said restaurant. There is a VERY cool outdoor sitting area off the main lobby, with a small waterfall and a gas fire that burns at night. We went out and sat there for awhile each night, instead of being cooped up in our room. WiFi available in all areas of the hotel, although the signal was a little weak in that outdoor area. No need for that to be the case! We needed info on the bike path, which is just across the river from the hotel, and the front desk person knew all about it. LOVED that! Also, was recommended to a very good Mexican restaurant, which was probably four miles away. Loved the fact that he told us about what he thought we'd enjoy, not just what was "around here". The parts to be aware of: The bathroom is separated into two parts, one with a toilet and a sink, the other with shower and a sink. If you are with your spouse or sig other, not a real problem, but if you are sharing a room with others, or there are kids/teens involved, it does cause a little privacy issue. Second, the doors on these are VERY cool, but again, lacking in privacy. Instead of traditional wooden doors, they installed sliding doors with translucent glass! Very chic, but some travelers will be VERY turned off by this. The room doors all shut very loudly, if you don't catch them with your hand, so you can constantly hear the slamming of other doors from the hall way. As someone else noted, there are train tracks directly behind the property, but other than the rumble of the engines, it was really not a problem. (No whistles, just engine noise.) The hotel is in a great location, but that means (especially during rush hours) lots of traffic. It can be difficult to get around, but you are right next to a college of OSU's size.
