You have to be realistic. There are lot's of things within walking distance, and never once did we feel unsafe doing this. Pool was basically a lap pool, not a traditional place for kids to play. HVAC did a decent job of holding the room at the temp we desired, but the fan was not nearly loud enough to drown out hotel noise. Bring your own fan, or other white-noise creator! Overall, absolutely would recommend this hotel, as long as you are aware of those items above and they are not going to surprise you!

“Great location, great rooms” I stayed at this hotel overnight on a business trip and am glad I did. The room was on an upper floor and had a balcony, which was definitely worth the extra price. The views of Lady Bird Lake and downtown Austin beyond it are great. The location was also very good--just a few blocks (about 8) from 6th Street and the heart of downtown. Definitely walkable (but for the 101 degree heat on the day I was there). Some guidebooks stressed as a top site the bats of the Congress Street Bridge and the balcony looked directly out on the bridge--less than a block or so away. But be warned, although I hung around the balcony for hours waiting for the bats (they were supposed to come out at sunset), I never say any. A slight disappointment. The room was clean, large, and the bed was comfortable. I liked the clean, crisp style--typical of Hyatt hotels. The soaring atrium and glass elevators were also nice--a signature style for Hyatt Regencies that I always enjoy. There were a good range of things to order from room service and my dinner was particularly good. Prices were reasonable. I also enjoyed a nice pre-dinner drink in the lobby bar and it was very nice. Good views out the windows (again, too hot to sit out on the terrace) and service was quick and friendly. The SW restaurant ( think that was the name of the lobby restaurant) looked like a nice place for breakfast, but I was running late and regret that I didn't have a chance to try it. I used the valet parking and the staff was very quick in getting the cars. I called from my room and it was always waiting for me (which is not true in every hotel I've stayed at). Service in all areas was good. Check in and check out were quick (of course, that could be because there were no long lines) and every staff person I ran into was friendly but professional. This hotel met all my expectations and would definitely stay here again on my next trip to Austin.

“We have a winner folks!” This place is great...has a real cool vibe, in addition to great service and amenities. We didn't even get a chance to experience the wine bar and had to leave for the airport before breakfast (although the nice young man putting breakfast together had some things out early and we got to grab some yogurt and a bagel), but we experienced enough to know we'll be back. The room is large, comfortable, beautifully decorated and well-equipped. The A/C fan runs constantly, which is great for blocking out unwanted noise. I agree with another reviewer who mentioned needing more outlets (I found a couple on the BACK of the desk lamp!). The modern sink was more fun than functional for me. But I loved the nice big sink and counter, and want to say thank you to the designers who put lights BESIDE the mirror instead of just above only. You can tell everything about this place was well thought out. I kinda hate to see it turn into a Hampton Inn this fall. Hope they don't change much.

“Such a convenient and safe location for those who are sightseeing” Wow - this place is amazing. A friend suggested that we stay in Olde City since it was convenient and very safe...I'm so glad we took his advise. The hotel is conveniently located right on Independence Park and is as luxurious as you'd expect from an Omni hotel. The staff was very friendly, accommodating and knowledgeable. Many hotels in the Center City/downtown area can be a bit seedy at night, even though they may look okay during the day, but hotels in Olde City are great at any time since they are very safe and the area is clean and pristine. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Philly for business or pleasure. While this hotel can be expensive, it's worth the money since you are staying in 5-star excellence and in a very nice neighborhood.

“Great location, great hotel” We stayed for 3 nights at $119 per night. Great rate if you can get it. At this price the hotel is a bargain as it includes breakfast. The room we had was a 1 bedroom, with plenty of room. The bed was very nice, but the sofa bed was not very nice. We had to put the mattress on the floor. No big deal. The valet parking at $20 per day was fast and efficient. The breakfast was typical average selection, but adequate. No complaints. The hotels location is great and walking distance to some great attractions. Yes would stay again

“Cookie Cutter Hampton Inn” Nothing bad to report...it's JUST a Hampton Inn. I've been very spoiled staying at many other hotels with much better breakfasts. I can’t stand “powdered” eggs and “Hampton Inn/Holiday Inn Express” breakfast foods...but the hotel here is clean and convenient to the Interstate. The rooms are clean and the beds are fresh...so if you’re looking for an inexpensive stay, this location is your place.

“Great experience at the four seasons chicago” Where to begin? Everything about the hotel was amazing. From the beautiful rooms to the breathtaking views, our first four seasons experience was fantastic. Having stayed at many other upscale brands before (mandarin oriental, ritz) we decided to try a four seasons for our trip to chicago and we weren't disappointed in any way. The hotel rooms were spacious and very modern. LCD flatscreens were found both the living room and bedroom. The bed was exceptionally comfortable and the large window sill was covered by a cushion that you could relax on with your laptop and enjoy the great views. The staff was equally outstanding. Very polite every time we encountered them and the concierge recommended an outstanding steakhouse (david burkes) that everyone in my family loved. The location was also very nice, sitting right across from the john hancock building on michigan avenue. Curbside at the hotel had lots of heaters that helped tremendously when waiting for a taxi in the 20 degree weather. My first experience with the four seasons chain was outstanding and i've already made plans to stay at the four seasons paris this summer.

“Great place to stop at the airport” We spent one night at this Radisson,which we chose from many as it seemed to be the most convenient and best deal. We normally stay at Hilton properties and this was the first Radisson for many years after a poor experience in St Louis, MO! Well, our expectations were met. Very convenient. Easy, free parking. A great room with separate sitting area and couch. FS TV, if not HD. The hotel has a nice terrace area and bar which served as the breakfast area in the morning (not sure, but think they served snacks, or even more in the evening). Unusually, the (included) breakfast was served at the table having chosen from a menu and cooked to order. You could only order juice or coffee but then were allowed to take coffee "to go". Breakfast was great. Best of all, and I'm not sure if this applies to all Radisson properties, the bathroom items (shampoo, lotion AND body wash) were all in easy to use squeezy tubes with the contents labelled in large LETTERS. Hooray. A chain that considers its older clients. No peering at tiny bottles in the shower trying to fathom out what they contain and then fumbling to open them with soapy hands. These tubes worked! Hilton and others, please take note. And, another pleasure was china mugs and glasses supplied for drinks (along with coffee maker etc). It is depressing when you go to even quite up-market hotels, to be presented with paper mugs. Mugs and glasses are nice and they're green! And there are two restaurants at least within easy walking distance. An Applebees and The Cattle Baron which is where decided to eat a delightful dinner. It's difficult to fault this hotel, which is the 14th on our current trip. Near the top of our list!

“Keep Your Pants On...this place is boring and uninspired” This joint is a ho-hum hotel that is more suited for business travelers than for couples on vacation. The service is what you'd expect from Westin, but nothing about this hotel really stood out. We were here for a formal dinner in the large conference room and I swear my shoe leather was softer then the beef. The front desk personnel were fine, the valet was fine, the room was fine. This hotel was so fine that I'm getting bored writing this review, so I'll sign off. (This place is a far cry from the Chicago Westin.)

“Great Business Hotel With Good Prices On Weekends” We recently stayed here for 5 nights to attend a wedding and got a great price of $99 per night. We thought the hotel was well situated for our needs but you have to remember that Woodland Hills is not downtown LA. Parking was $13 a night in an adjoining garage and ther is a nice mall across the street (try Ruby's for breakfast or lunch). There is a PF Chang's across the street and Kate Mantilini, a chic LA type fancy diner in the complex, as well as numerous other restaurants from fancy steakhouses to fast food and Chinese. There is a larger upscale mall also within walking distance. This Marriott has a nice little indoor pool and fitness center and an outside pool as well, with a small bar. There is a tiny sports bar inside and a dining room serving breakfast, lunch and dinner. There is a small business center that charges exorbitant prices to use their computers although you can print boarding passes for free. Wifi is available throughout the hotel and you will see many people sitting in the lobby using their computers. Maid service is very efficient and helpful, as is the entire hotel staff. The hotel was an excellent base for our five days here, which included visits to Simi Valley, Santa Monica, etc. You can get around the area very easy, usually avoiding the horrendous LA traffic. All in all, a great place to stay if you want to avoid LA congestion. Calabasas, only a couple of miles away, is a nice choice for a quaint town with good restaurants and shops.

“Nothing amazing, but decent” We found it very hard to find reasonably priced accommodation in LA. We didnt have any specific agenda for our time there, so we just picked a hotel that seemed ok for the price. That's pretty much what the Clarion Hotel Downtown was. The room was nice, the bed comfortable, and everything was clean, but like the majority of hotels we found in LA, was overpriced - especially for the area it was in. It's really not in a very nice location at all - very dirty, very old and run down, and not filled with the nicest people. There is public transport nearby, but I wouldnt recommend using it - like everyone says, you really need a car in LA, and I think had we listened and hired one, the location of the Clarion wouldn't have been so important because it would have just been our base, as opposed to the area that we were mostly confined to. So all in all, decent hotel, not bad for the price - but if you're going to LA to experience the glitz, glamour or even just a friendly face and a semi-clean city...this area probably isnt for you.

“An Oasis in Time Square Chaos” Stayed 2 nights (award) and found the hotel just as good as my last stay several years ago. The place was fully booked as there was a jewelry and fashion accesories convention occupying 9 floors. As a result, did not receive any upgrade for Gold status. PROS: -spacious 2-room suites with 2 TV's, microwave, small empty fridge, touch-sensored honor bar, and small safe. -free wireless HSIA for gold and diamond members (no wired access available) -complimentary full hot breakfast buffet for gold and diamonds (normally $28) at restaurant -quiet despite outside chaos; comfortable beds. -central location: multiple subway lines within 2 blocks, close to all theaters, endless dining options CONS: -bathtub spout is overpressured like a firehose, as was the showerhead--major need for a flow restrictor. Would be very effective for interrogating terrorists, probably better than waterboarding. -fitness center: dated Precor equipment that seems to shake and rattle. The room is very warm despite high ceilings. There is no bathroom on the same floor--have to go up 1 floor to the restaurant level. -business center: temporarily located on lobby level in a tiny room the size of a closet. The least they should do is PUT UP A TERMINAL FOR PRINTING BOARDING PASSES at the front desk (plenty of room)

“Good choice of hotel but a bit noisy due to construction next door” I stayed at this hotel with family for 3 nights. The hotel is located in lower Manhattan, very close to the world trade center and battery park. You can go for a short walk by the river and get a great view of the statute of liberty. The hotel is somewhat far from Times Square and a couple of blocks away from the closest subway station. Beware that this hotel is right next to the World Trade Center construction site and I found it very very noisy starting very early in the morning (7AM and on) and through out the day. There is drilling, hammering and loud construction noise. It did not bother me a whole lot as I did not plan to sleep in, but if you have young children or if you want to sleep in bring ear plugs. Also knowing the reason for the construction, I was more saddened than upset (RIP all 9/11 victims). The check in process was easy, the staff were very accommodating. Parking is $55/day which allows for in and outs (rare in NYC) and it took them about 15 mins to bring the car up upon request. The room was clean and the cleaning staff did a great job cleaning the room every day. There is a Starbucks on the main level which is very nice. The internet in the room you have to pay for, but there is pretty reliable free WiFi in the lobby which was very good. Overall, I would recommend this hotel but I may not return again as I found it a bit too far from Times Square and the main shopping hubs. Otherwise the hotel is great.

“Fairfield Inn Downtown is a BIG inconvenience” Normally I am down with Fairfield Inn's by Marriott. They're clean, serviceable, and have a warm breakfast everyday. This one however was a BIG diappointment. Check in was easy and the staff was really nice. From there though it was down hill. The parking at this place is TERRIBLE. We were there during the city's lame answer to Mardi Gras, "Fiesta", which had locals and others parking at our hotel without paying or staying. This property claims to limit the number of riff raff parking at the hotel, not so, otherwise the lot would look empty like the Courtyard by Marriott next door. The staff at that hotel had security guarding the lot so only guests were allowed. The Fairfield Inn, not so much. My business has lots of heavy equipment that I must haul to my room after work every night and this was a collassal pain. This also was troublesome because the elevator is REALLY, REALLY slow. For a property with only four floors this machine should operate a little more efficiently. The maid service here is average at best because it seemed I had to ask for more soap and towels on a daily basis. One other thing is the internet service here is extremely slow and doesn't work a lot of the time making a business stay nearly impossible to pull off, unless you use the computer in the lobby, which of course is always being used. One other thing about the lobby is when you exit there are usually smokers right outside the door and its so great to get a big whiff of their cancer sticks when you enter and leave the hotel. This place is close to the highway and Riverwalk, but if the costs are the same stay next door at the Courtyard because you'll have an easier time parking and the internet service is much better.

“Stellar Customer Service” Though I was confused by the advertising (I thought the Omni was directly on the St. John's river from the appearance of the professional photo), I was not disappointed. What the Omni lacks in views (a room with a "water view" is being able to see a slip of water from between buildings), it makes up for in every other way. The service of this hotel rivals that of the legendary Waldorf-Astoria of NYC, in my experience. They went above and beyond the call in every way...from the front desk management to the maid service. I cannot imagine anyone being more than satisfied with their service. Further more, the hotel is impeccably clean and the design is tasteful and luxurious. If you stay here, and understand it isn't directly on the river, you won't be disappointed.

“Great value, very clean” I've stayed at several SF hotels in the past and this is a great hotel for the price. We upgraded our room to a room with a mini fridge. Our room was about the same size as many rooms I've stayed in other SF boutique hotels. So it was small as I expected but comfortable. We had breakfast and dinner once at the Elephant Castle next door. It's a little expensive but it's a good. There are several great sandwich shops around but most are closed on the weekends. We walked 10 min to North Beach for some good italian dinners a few nights. Viva is our favorite for Italian. The Specialty Bakery & Cafe on Sansome St had the best sandwiches and cookies. The area around the hotel is very safe and very quiet on the weekends. The Bart station is just a few blocks away or walking to Union Square, North Beach, Chinatown, etc is about 10-20 min walk. The Club Quarters is a great hotel that fits my budget and we'll be back again soon.

“Pretty Nice Hotel” My husband and I stayed at the Le Meridien from June 20-24, 2008. We checked in around 11:00 p.m. and the lobby bar was hopping and the front desk staff were very friendly. We stayed on the 10th floor in a studio suite. It was a great room. We had a bathroom that had a separate tub and shower and our views from our two windows were of the bay bridge to the right and one of the Transamerica building (pyramid shaped building) in the financial district. I enjoyed the separation of the living room from the bedroom with the big flat screen TV. I did notice something in the shower at the bottom of it. It felt slimy all the time, but I tried to wipe it off, but it never went away. Not sure what the slime was, but it looked and wiped up clean??? We stayed at the end of the hall and never heard one person coming in or out of their rooms. Super quiet! We did eat breakfeast on the 3rd floor and it was fine. I did have room service and they were very accommodating with my order. Fast and friendly service. Oh by the way, I made the housekeeper on the phone laugh until she cried when I called down there and told them I needed a new hairdryer becuase I dropped ours in the toliet (long story) :) The location of the hotel was also fabulous. You are three blocks from the Piers and the start/end of the street cars (trolly's). The staff and location was great and I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Happy traveling!!!

“So bad we did not stay” Of my many years basing my hotel choices on Tripadvisor reviews, this is the first time it failed me. Granting it is not the Four Seasons or Marriott, I have stayed at good/decent Days Inns before. I booked through the official website, called multiple times to specifically reserve a nonsmoking room because I was traveling with family and my sister was pregnant and I have allergies and asthma. We were given a "convertible" smoking/nonsmoking room. (I have traveled enough to know there is no such thing). Rooms were small, interior and exterior needs updating. Window screen was barely attached, needs a nail or 2. After pitching a fit because the manager initially had no plans of giving back the room deposit (he finally agreed after I threated to call the BBB on him and file a formal complaint), we just left and had to look for another hotel to stay for the next 3 nights. The only advantage that I can see if people want to stay here is the free parking and for smokers. Otherwise, there are many other comparable (price range and hotel class) options.

“Ahhh... For the budget conscience traveler only.” I was in Jacksonville last week for business and booked one night on Hotwire.com for $65. I enjoyed the hotel and needed to extend my stay at the last minute, so I booked another night at the same price. I was assigned a different room and had an unpleasant experience. Because of this, I am going to break my review into two categories: Good night and Bad night Good night: - Check in was really easy, the front desk folks were pleasant - From the outside of the hotel, it looks older, but the lobby looks like it got an upgrade a few years ago - My room was spacious and had a nice. "home-y" feel Bad Night: - My room was DIRTY. The headboard on the bed had oil/grease marks all over it, the sink did not drain and had someone elses hair and toothpaste all over it. I literally did not take a shower because I was afraid that the hotel staff did not clean the shower - The "sleep number" bed did not work either night. I think that the batteries were dead in both beds. Overall impression: My first nights stay was GREAT. I left thinking that I'd found a little gem in Jacksonville. My second night stay was absolutely repulsive. I got the very last hotel room when I checked in, and my guess is that the house keeping staff was not prepared for such a large crowd. Would I stay here again?? Probably not. I have not been that impressed with the hotels on Butler Blvd (check out my review of the Hampton Inn).

“Great hotel deal in downtown Chicago” This hotel is only about 3 blocks from the heart of Michigan Avenue or the lake putting you in a great location for shopping, taking the train to other parts of Chicago, or enjoying the lake area of Chicago. The price is reasonable and includes a great self-serve breakfast that includes waffles and breakfast sandwiches. The accommodations are not fancy, but clean and well-appointed. The staff is fabulous offering and providing excellent service. We love to stay here because of the price and location. We will be back.

“Very pleasant experience - would stay here again” This hotel is right off I-45 at the intersection with FM1960. There is a Krogers in walking distance, as well as a shopping mall. Check in was the fastest experienced in a long time, very efficient. The room was attractively furnished, lobby has a fresh appearance, breakfast area was clean, and buffet breakfast was good. Windows in room can be opened, but there is road noise from I45 even when shut. Not too bothersome if tired though. Ample parking. Yes, would stay here again.

“Third Stay and Second time have seen bugs!” I have to stay here for business. I have stayed in older side twice and both times saw bugs. The first time ants, the last time a roach crawled out of the bath mat. The newer wing room was bug free. The front desk just says sorry and that is it. I would not stay here unless have to- like me! Basically dated property that you would not think is a Marriott. They have a captive audience and seem to know it.

“Service Excellent; Pool Area Nice” It's the service here. Compared with other Four Seasons some of the physical/decor wow factor not there but the Four Seasons bed, L'Occitane bath products made it comfortable. Large room just needs a little color-pizzaz to freshen. Pool service excellent and area was very relaxing and more resort like than a downtown hotel property. Good gym. Very prompt service retrieving car. I went for a party nearby but can see this would be a good choice for business trips. It was also an incredible value-- weekend rate was very very low and enjoyed the deal

“Hotel tres bien situe proche de Alamo et du riverwalk , parfait pour visiter San Antonio” Accueil tres agreable et souriant , une tres grande chambre claire avec un lit king size , une excellente literie , un hotel tres calme , une grande salle de bain avec une fenetre..toutefois toutes les chambres ne semblent pas etre ainsi , il y en a de beaucoup plus petites et moins agreables Une bonne adresse

“Soviet Westin: Not for Business Travelers” This hotel was a great disappointment for a business trip. First, the air conditioning was not adequate for a late September afternoon in Chicago. I arrived in the room at about 230pm and had to work. The AC had been off. I fired it up, but it took hours on a not very hot day to make the room tolerable. I was sweating through my business shirt --- something that wouldn't happen at the Days Inn or Embassy Suites -- chains not usually mentioned in the same breath as the Westin. I was unable to get the Front Desk to answer or Conceirge, despite repeated calls. The hotel simply does not have enough staff to handle the crowds. Check-in was a 15 minute ordeal at an off hour. My breakfast was botched. I asked for Special K, at Soviet Westin I got Total. I asked for Grapefruit, but at the Soviet Westin they do not have fresh grapefruit. Odd. My telephone lacked its base, so it slid across the glass table constantly -- bad for business calls (manager: check it out - Room 1107). The good points: 1) Gold Coast location is superb; 2) Heavenly Bed still good. The gym is B-plus; but completely full at 6AM -- Manager, it needs expansion. This is a hotel with a great brand and location and very poor execution.

“Lots of Bang for the Buck” Excellent hotel - the second time I've stayed here. The rooms are very spacious, and immaculately clean. Very comfortable bed. The front desk staff and concierges are friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. Its location, one block from Union Square, can't be beat. Small quibbles - the bathrooms are small-ish and somewhat dated, and I personally prefer a down comforter to a heavy bedspread. But all in all the Donatello offers you a large clean comfortable room, an excellent stay and great value.

“Fine for a few days” I stayed here for a few nights for a conference at a neighboring hotel and compared to the other property this one was very average. The rooms are fine, if not a bit dated and in need of a refurb. The bathrooms could definitely use a makeover! Fitness centre is tiny and the pool is starting to show its age, along with the rooms. The dinner served here was pretty good and the service in the restaurant was really friendly which makes up for the generally average state of the property itself. This is not a bad place to rest your head for a few days on business so long as your expectations are set correctly.

“Great Stay” Used my Marriott Points for my stay at this hotel. Nice, super clean room - seemed like it was brand new! The bottled water and the trail mix they left for me was a nice surprise since i didn't check in until after 10:30 pm. Convenient location to the airport and a shuttle is provided from 5AM to 11 PM which saved on cab fare if not renting a car. Hotel seemed to be in more of a residential area with the closest restaurants a little distance away (the hotel does offer a shuttle to Easton Town Centre if reserved in advance). Overall, a great stay, a nice staff, and all the amenities that they list on their website are available just as they advertise.

“Subpar...definitely not a 3.5 star” The Tudor hotel is certainly not the hotel for those who like big brand name hotels. Even the holiday inn is better than the Tudor. The Tudor is a decent place to crash if you need a clean bed in a quiet hotel, but the little details that make a hotel stay enjoyable and luxurious are seriously lacking in this hotel. First I'll touch on the positives. Cute lobby, great doormen to greet you, and helpful front desk staff. Our maid was kind, she left us extra towels as requested, although she left us no shampoo for our final day - so we couldn't wash our hair. They offer bath and body works products, which is a nice touch, too. The air conditioning in the room was fantastic, and the tv was big, flat, and functional. The room itself was small and dingy. While the bed area was clean, the bathroom smelled horribly of mold. Our sink wouldn't drain properly and the stench of the moldy bathroom made our room smell awful, too. Everytime I had to go into the bathroom I dreaded it! The phone in our room didn't work, either. I truly felt as though I was in a bathroom that had been surface cleaned but not properly sanitized for decades. Those blacklights they use on CSI would have forsure had a field day! As for the location, I can't comment much on it. We cabbed everywhere because it was pouring, but it's definitely a rather far walk from 5th avenue shopping (probably 20 minutes). We paid $125 per night on priceline, however, I would say that this hotel was only worth 100, not 125, and I wouldn't call it a 3.5 star. Also, for those booking on priceline, this hotel charges a fee of $50 per night if you want 2 double beds, so make sure you're aware of that before bidding. I cannot imagine anyone paying full price for this hotel...I felt a tad ripped off at $125. All in all, if you're looking for a clean and quiet place to rest your head for the night (with no extra ammenities or luxuries), then this hotel will do just fine. If you are scared of germs, hate mold, and in general want more than dingy basics, I wouldn't recommend the tudor. Did it ruin my trip? Not at all. Did it add anything exciting to it? Definitely not.

“Excellent stay at Marriott, Copley Place” We flew to Boston on jetBlue. I was able to get a ridiculously low air fare and was impressed with the quality of the aircraft. The hotel is in a lovely location. It is a smart looking hotel. I would definitely recommend it to other visitors who travel to this great city. Overall, we were impressed with this hotel. The check-in at the Mariott Copely Place was smooth and quick. There was only one mishap during our stay which occurred as soon as we arrived and it involved the elevator service. Just before the elevator reached my floor the inner door opened. The elevator was a foot short of my floor and the outside door was still shut! The bloak I was with tried to pry the door open but it refused to open. This totally freaked him out – We were stuck dangling up 20+ floors and unable to exit and it was upsetting. We were stuck on the elevator for 7-10 minutes while sounding the alarm bell for help. A very helpful security staff member, tried to calm us down as he spoke to us from the other side. Finally the elevator door was able to open. We were told that there was no mechanism to open the outer elevator door from the inside in case of emergency, which remains concerning. The security staff member was sincerely apologetic and sensed how disturbed we were to be stuck. To make up for the traumatic experience he ordered a wine and cheese tray to be sent to our room. In addition, he arranged for us to use the concierge services on the 28th floor, courtesy of the management of Marriott. Without a doubt the view of the Charles River and Back Bay from the upper levels of this hotel is a marvel!

“Excellent Overall !” Overall I was very pleased by this hotel. After reading some review's I was a little worried about staying there because of the service rating and some of the room ratings. When i called the actual hotel to confirm that it was only a King bed and not two queens, the lady at the hotel was extremely rude and hung up on me before I could get her name, however when I arrived at the hotel I was pleasantly surprised at how nice the hotel staff was. I received excellent service from the people at the front desk and the entire staff was really friendly and always said hi. The room was excellent and really spacious, the bed was extremely comfortable and the desk area was nice. Although the internet is not free. I liked the fact that the parking was free and you could park in the little garage also. Overall the hotel is somewhat of a hidden gem to me at least. It is tucked away from major business and other disturbances just a little, but not too far from attractions or restaurants. I never heard a peep from my room, pretty good sound proofing considering the freeway is right next to the hotel and my room was facing the freeway. I would definitely stay here again, I definitely agree with there 3 star hotel rating although I was a little hesitant at first. Trust me, try the hotel, you will like it.

“Overall good” My husband and I purchased a deal from living social that included stay, 2 drinks, and free breakfast. The hotel itself was really beautiful and very unique. It's location is close to the Riverwalk and other fun spots. The bar is very unique, due to the low lighting and candles. The complaint that my husband and I have is the price of parking, $17, and the breakfast. Luckily our breakfast was free but it's very over priced and was not tasty. Overall it was a great stay.

“Exactly what I expected for the price” I was in NYC for 4th of July weekend and I was catching a show on Broadway and going to the Harry Potter Exhibition at Discovery Times Square. This hotel was a 2/10 of a mile walk from both. Obviously - the location of this place is top notch. It's exactly where I wanted and needed to be since I was traveling alone. The hotel is perfectly fine. Nothing special. The rooms are exactly the size you'd expect for NYC. I only had one problem. I called down for an extra pillow and was delivered one with long black curly hairs all over it. As if it was just taken off a used bed and handed to me. I called down and told them and there was no apology - just a promise for a clean pillow. I would still stay here again. I got the clean pillow. All was well.

“Good location and value” As a business traveler, I found the Warwick to be located well; close to several subway stops; and near many restaurants. Moreover, it was away from the masses of Times Square, but certainly close enough for me to take a walk there.

“Nice stay at Tuscan” I found a great mid week deal that included a discount on parking. The front desk staff was efficent and friendly. The lobby area is decorated nicely with nice chairs and sofas to mingle at before heading out to have fun. Tuscan offers complimentary glasses of wine at 5 which is a nice touch. The room I stayed in had two doubles and a slight view of the Coit tower. Nice flat screen tv. The room was very clean and the beds comfortable. The room also has free wireless which I've read other hotels nearby don't. It was nice visiting SF during the off season and really enjoyed the stay. This is the nicest BW I've ever stayed at. It should have a higher rating on TripAdvisor. Perfect location to Fishermans Wharf.

“Going ..under a major renovation - great service” First floor was just beginning to undergo renovation, second floor was completely closed and nearly finished. There were not a lot of guests when I stayed here because they didnt have a lot of rooms available due to the renovations. I had a newly renovated room on the third floor. Of course the room was very clean, good A/C, nice bed, good TV...The room had a small refrigerator..which I really appreciate. The shower was VERY clean..all white..decent water pressure...bathroom was a little on the small side. What sets this property apart is the service, Philip at the front desk (Borger, TX) is great. I utilized the Van service to get to and from the airport and had them take me to a restaurant..the service was VERY prompt and the driver was very friendly (even at 4:15 in the morning going to the airport!). Didnt eat breakfast, use the pool or exercise room. This property is close to the airport..not much around here within walking distance that I could see and the area gets pretty "Industrial" as you head west down Universtity..not sure I would walk down that way very far. The area immediately around the hotel has lots of office buildings and you see a lot of traffic, but the room was quiet.

“quaint, cozy and excellent location” it's like a european hotel. the elevator was tiny. the room was small and clean but when your in sf why do you want to stay in your room? quiet but no view. excellent location two blocks from chinatown and one block from union square. staff was nice and helpful. if you want ice they will bring it to your room. did not get to take advantage of the complimentary wine. plenty of cafes available. even a walgreen across the street. nice place to staff that won't break the bank. i would consider it on my next visit.

“Good Choice if You are Staying in this Part of Town” I booked my room for the Memorial Day weekend when Indianapolis hotels are filled for the 500 Race. Although this hotel is on the opposite side of the city from the speedway, it was very easy to get to this hotel as it is very convenient to freeway access. It is a typical Hampton Inn, with very comfortable beds and an adequate hot breakfast in the morning. This hotel has a large indoor pool.
“Average Stay” Clean rooms, good staff, good location, lots of parking space, average rooms, good sleep. Might stay there again when visiting Houston.

“Great location for traveling to NYC!” The location of this DoubleTree is what makes it a gem. I don't normally stay on the upper east side, but this was a great experience - away from the noise and lights of mid-town. There is a subway station right outside the hotel to take th 6 train north or south, and 2 blocks away is the E train to get you everywhere else. Great experience!

“One night stand” Stayed here to attend a company Christmas party. We had some difficulty finding the hotel as it's behind another hotel. We kept driving around in rush hour, Christmas shopping traffic. Only when we called the hotel and got a recording that it was behind another hotel were we able to find it. Daphne at the front desk was very friendly & printed us out a map on how to get from the hotel to the Christmas party. Room itself was fine, quiet, comfortable bed, lots of hot water, hot drinks served in lobby. We requested more feather pillows and was glad we did as they were small, so we used two each. Walked the next morning to the Galleria mall - this would be a great place for shoppers planning to shop to stay!

“Super Cute hotel- perfect for travelers, great location” Stayed at Hotel Diva for Labor Day Weekend- got an awesome rate- $159/night. This place is great- on Geary just a short walk from Union Square. (It's also right across from the Clift hotel). Hotel furnishings were very cute and our room was a nice size- two double beds, nice huge flat panel TV and a sitting area. They also gave free wireless and had a small business center on our floor. The only downer was we did hear noise throughout the night...one night it sounded like huge dump trucks came by to unload dumpsters or something... it woke me up for a good 15-20 minutes in the middle of the night. ..NOT pleasant. (We were on the 4th floor). Overall though, I'd stay here again...and request a room on a higher floor. There is also a Starbucks attached to the hotel which was convenient and a nice looking Mexican Tapas place attached on the other side. I didnt eat there but it was packed everynight. I'd definitely recommend this hotel for a weekend trip up to SF for a reasonable price. :)

“Clean and New” This place is great for business travelers who want to be close enough to walk and grab a bite to eat, but also have a clean place to stay. The breakfast offering is very Southern so don't expect any healthy fare however the staff are delightful. I even left my expensive jewelry on the bedside table and it was there when i came back at night. I was totally surprised and impressed. Try this place and you will be pleased you did.

“Only for reunion tower! Hyatt as a hotel is a disappointment” This is my second stay at Hyatt regency dallas. (my prior stay in May 2011). Both times I felt disappointed. We had a great start- valet very attentive, and carried our bags to check in. Then the trouble began. Hyatt is trying to be a "pet friendly" hotel, it has a "few" rooms which it made pet friendly. We had tried for two days the week prior to make a reservation for a pet friendly room. When we called, they said the manager was out and this person was the only person who could make it. Then we called central reservations, same thing, called and left a message with no return call. We went ahead and booked online and left comments about a small pet and how we weren't called back. We also upgraded to the city view "VIP" program. When we got to the desk, the CSR did not have a king size bed, then did not have a pet friendly room on the city view. Only left with the 4th floor (which we had already stayed at, before they became pet friendly). I understand they only have a few pet rooms available, but how about the fact that their customer service is so poor they don't even return your calls? I told them we could wait no longer and went ahead and booked reservation. If they would have called me sooner, i could have booked at another place, They are not the only hotel in this town. But it was too late! Checking in at 10 pm, where else were we going to go? we got stuck on the 4th floor. The rooms are a disappointment. Again being a 4 star hotel, you would expect everything to be modernized. The hyatt is an old hotel with some minor covers to make it look "updated." the furniture is so old, its probably from 1980, old wood, and the desk looks like something I had in 5th grade. I am not sure if the upper level rooms have better furniture, but I was depressed when I was in the room. At least this time the bathroom was clean. Like other reviewers, the previous stay, the bathroom was so dirty, with mold growing on the tile- needed major cleaning of the caulk. The bed was comfortable, the TV a large LG, no DVD. We had breakfast as compensation after I told them they were not the only hotel in town. The breakfast was good but on the greasy side. We ordered egg white omlets, side of bacon and coffee. Food was brought up promptly. We visited wolfgang puck 560 and def agree, it is the highlight of the stay. The food is definitely overpriced and the bottle of champagne as well but you are paying for the view. I understand. The food was very good though. I would recommend the bar area, where you don't have to make reservations and you can just plop down on the couches and enjoy the view. We had also asked for late check out and paid the extra fee. Upon check out, we scrutinized our bill, good thing! because they tried to charge an extra day of valet parking and an extra day of pet fees. Be careful and ask for your final bill. It saved us 70+ dollars and hassle of phone call to argue. All in all, go for the reunion tower/wolfgang puck's view, but skip the 3 start trying to be 4 star hotel and stay somewhere else. bleh.

“Good deal in Midtown for $160” Days Inn Hotel New York Broadway was once grander: notice the checkers marble lobby, where boorish tourists now straddle the couches, and the polished brass mail chute, the internet of its day, which is now largely ignored. A shadow of its former grand as it may be, the hotel offers a convenient midtown location and surprisingly roomy accommodations. Service was an expected from such establishment, sleep was average due to street noise, but at $160 a night (after AAA discount and including decent internet signal), it was a bargain. And the mail we sent from the chute made it all the way across the oceans.

“Fix that elevator” I only stayed at the Holiday Inn Express on Salisbury Road in Jacksonville, FL for one night so I won't write a lengthy review. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful, so check in and check out were great. The room rate was reasonable at $62/night. The elevator was awful. When I got in to go up to my room for the first time, the elevator buckled and started going up before the door completely closed. It sounded like it was struggling to move and it stopped rather abruptly when it reached a floor. They seriously need to have the elevator serviced because it's terrible. The room was nice and spacious. It had a fridge and a microwave, which were nice even for a one night stay. The bed was very comfortable. Overall, this would be a great hotel if they could fix that elevator.

“Great Location” Stayed here for 4 nights for a conference. Hotel staff was extremely knowledgeable of the area and quite professional. I was upgraded to a 2 room suite on the 25th floor upon arrival with access to the club lounge on the 26th floor. The view I had from the 25th floor was amazing. Could see the water front from one window and the Space Needle from the other and what a spectacular sky line Seattle offers at night. This hotel is located about 1/2 a mile from Pikes Place Market the Water Front and the First Starbucks. The walk down is great and when I say down i mean down. Returning to the hotel was straight up hill but worth the effort in my opinion. Despite having complimentary breakfast in the club lounge I did eat one morning in the restaurant and it was a basic buffet or you could order off the menu if you have the time I would recommend walking to the water front to find breakfast. Did have room service one night. A basic Turkey Club with Fries and water. Was about 20.00 including tip so not so bad for room service. I gave the server a couple of extra bucks but he was not expecting it. My only complaint with this hotel was the Elevators seemed to be running slow. Not sure if they were all working or what but it was a small inconvenience. This will definitely be my hotel for future stays in Seattle.

“Honesty And Excellant ” Stay 7/1-7/8-06 Every thing was just as displayed on web site Very large room,.clean room hotel is spotless Staff is top notch,breakfest in lobby very good All of the items i requested were done When i checked out on 7/8/06 i left my camera on the robe hook in the bathroom and did not remember until i was on the plane going home, when i lande i called the hotel and they already had my camera in security and said they would send it to my home on monday. Honesty and a great hotel what else could you ask for, this is the place to stay,thanks to all at the hotel.

“This rooms are not very good, the lobby is nice” The lobby of this hotel is historical and beautiful. It's not really a high-class hotel though. The rooms are far from high class. The carpet is dingy and old-looking. The room did not have a coffee maker. I don't think I have ever stayed in a hotel that had a coffee maker. This hotel does have a Starbucks as many hotels do of this type. The rooms are also small. There is little room between the beds and the tv and the bathrooms are small. You wouldn't be able to close the bathroom door if you were sitting on the toilet. You would have to get up so your knees would not hit the door. There was no room to put anything in the bathroom. The bathroom door had peeling paint. The lobby had a lot of people and the ceiling was beautiful. I booked this through hotwire at $79/night ($189.30 with taxes and fees for 2 nights). I asked for a room with two double beds and they said no such rooms were available. They asked if I wanted a rollaway bed for $35/night, and I declined. As with most hotels in Chicago, parking is very expensive, so if you drive in, call some places around and you can get overnight parking at less than half the price of the hotel. The Millenium Park garage is nearby and is much cheaper. The room had virtually no view other than being able to see part of the Jersey Boys sign from a theater.

“Don't believe the management's responses.” The hotel's downstairs common areas are compelling. The desk staff was nice. I took a dekko at the pool. It's upstairs and outside, which should be fun. But it turns out to be mean. I'm a little hesitant to write this review, since the management seems to respond to all negative reviews about experiences similar to mine. I don't especially want to be tracked down. However, management's claim that we-are-really-really-sorry-for-your-negative-experience-and-gosh-we-are-renovating-as-fast-as-we-can, well it just ain't so. It annoys me because I believed it, I thought any management that cares enough to respond on tripadvisor.com must run a hotel with a heart. Not so, folks. Stay away! The problem is the room. Or my room, perhaps they're not all quite so disgusting. Huge and scarcely furnished, it seems appealing until you squint to stare at the medium-sized TV and fail to sink your toes into the indoor/outdoor carpet. The bed was nice enough. The bathroom is a real trip. It has old and rusty plumbing (e.g., the visible part of the sink’s drain) and the sink couldn’t be turned completely off no matter how hard I tried. The tub/shower was in the far end of a 15’ long bathroom, and the dim lights were both in the near end. I showered with the curtains open, ready for a quick escape should any pop up at me from the drain. The tile grout had lots of black mold, and, yes, the plumbing was rusty, old and crappy. I wish I'd brought a camera to record the squalor. Oh, yeah: a first for me. The room’s wastebasket still had trash in it when I arrived.
“Fantastic hotel.” Loved my stay here. A little hard to get into though as there is no street entrance. Staff were very attentive.

“If your not attending a convention here, stay somewhere else” If you are attending a convention at the hotel, then this property is for you, beautiful common areas and convention space. The hotel itself is ancient, was previously a Adam's Mark and Raddison. The bathrooms are the smallest bathrooms I have ever seen in a hotel, and I have stayed in 500 different hotels on several continents. Yes the rooms have been remolded but it is still old, it even smells old in the rooms probably due to the AC/Heat units from the 70s, except they installed the handy interface that turns off the AC/Heat when u leave your room wether you want it off or not (Bad in the Hot summer or Cold winter). Calling guest services for a request or wake up call takes forever, sometimes you have to hang up and try again, they don't seem to have enough staff operating the phones. If your not attending a convention here do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else, there are plenty of properties within a block of the 16th Street Mall where all the shopping, bars and restaurants are.

“Very Nice West End Hotel” We have stayed at this hotel several times while visiting our daughter who is a student at Georgetown. Having stayed here before the renovation and after, I can say with a great deal of conviction that they really spruced the place up! The rooms and the service were top notch. We enjoyed the afternoon tea. The hotel is convenient to Georgetown and Foggy Bottom. All of this comes at a price, however. The only "issue" is the constant issue in Washington: construction noise. I lived there for many years and had forgotten about the constant construction, reconstruction, renovation, and remodelling that goes on in that city!

“Great Alternative to Normal Downtown LA Blah Hotels” I've been travelling to downtown LA for years and have always bemoaned the lack of interesting, high-quality hotels that caters to business travellers downtown (i.e. Kimpton-type of hotel). Tried the LAAC on a recommendation for 3 nights and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The rooms are well-appointed, free wi-fi, and the bed was absolutely fantastic. Small niceties include a complimentary plate of fruit and cheese/crackers in your room upon arrival. I really enjoyed free access to the excellent fitness facilities this full-service gym has to offer, including more equipment one could ever dream of in a typical hotel fitness center (if you are a swimmer, the LAAC includes an indoor 5-lane, 25 yrd lap pool bathed in sunshine - fabulous!). An excellent cooked-to-order breakfast buffet is included in the cost of room. Downsides include a somewhat inattentive staff (tipping - at least for food services - is not permitted apparently) and there are some areas that are showing a bit of wear and tear. If you wouldn't enjoy a clubby, throwback ambiance, the place isn't for you. Overall, I thought it was a great value and I have booked a return trip next month.

“Great Experience” Like others have mentioned, I was concerned when I first won this hotel on Priceline because of all the negative reviews posted on this website. In my case, the Wellington turned out to be one of the best hotel experiences I've ever had in NYC. I arrived in the middle of a drenching rainstorm and was so happy to just get inside that I didn't ask for any special room type, upgrades, etc. Maybe the check-in clerk took pity on me because I was soaking wet but she upgraded me to a king-size room at the back of the hotel. The room decor was all blue and yellow and was just lovely. This was one of the few occasions when my room actually looked like the one in the hotel brochure! The location of the Wellington was perfect. I was attending shows in the the theatre district and Lincoln Center and both were an easy walk from the hotel. The variety of restaurants in the area was incredible, anything you could have wanted was within a few blocks. I was extremely pleased with every aspect of my stay and would gladly stay here again or recommend it to friends. My overall experience at the Wellington was better than some of the 4* hotels I've received in the past from Priceline.

“Noisy but Tolerable” The walls must be paper thin because I could hear everything and everyone. It seemed pretty clean and I actually had an acceptable meal. The bathrooms are quite outdated and the decor is - interesting. I would probably choose somewhere else next time. But, having just come from a stay in one of the worst hotels ever, this seemed pretty good at first. It's disappointing because of the great location. They really need to pay attention to these reviews - the staff does not really seem to be that concerned with service.

“Wonderful Location, Fantastic Staff & Service” Wonderful "home away from home" on the West Side--within walking distance to great restaurants and shops (you must spend an hour in Zabars!). Nice to be away from tourists and in a real neighborhood. The beds, shower and room were great. But the best thing was the attentive service from the staff and management---when they found I had left my pocketbook in the room safe, they called me to let me know, and sent it back UPS the next day! They also extended a warmth and friendliness rarely encountered at larger hotels. The doormen were a wonderful addition, and friendly and helpful. Liked locked hotel after hours, felt very safe--and evenings were quiet to sleep. Free wifi. Will stay there again--for sure.

“Impressive” This is a lovely hotel, very clean, very quiet and all employees were very courteous. The room was perfect. Breakfast the next morning was delicious. My dad and I stayed here since it was near St. Joseph's Hospital where my mother was staying after surgery. We were informed that we could take advantage of the hotel's shuttle service to/from the hospital if we so desired. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone spending time in downtown Houston. It was a nice hotel at a great price. Close to the George R. Brown Convention Center, Discovery Green Park, the Toyota Center and Minute Maid Park.

“Decent Option” The Sheraton is a massive hotel, I believe the 3rd biggest in Chicago from what the Architecture river tour told us. So if your looking for any charm or personalized service this isn't the place. There's a queuing line at check-in but we're Starwood Preferred Guest(SPG) so we got to bypass it. Another queue greets you at the concierge......we never needed them so that wasn't an issue. The staff is plenty friendly but your just another of the 1000 or so people staying there this week. It's also a convention hub so the lobby and elevators can become quite crowded at a moments notice. On several occasions we waited well over 5 minutes for an elevator. The Location is central to many things you want to see in downtown, however it's quite a walk from any train stop. So going to/from airport on train or a Cub game or anywhere outside the city isn't as convenient. A never ending line of cabs is available 24/7 though and can take you anywhere, just at a higher price than public transport. The hotel bar was nice and you never drink alone with so many people there for the conventions. A Shula's Steakhouse is located in the lobby but with all the good food choices in Chicago we were never tempted to go there. We stayed on the 30th floor which is for SPG members only. Views were beautiful looking down the river and at the new Trump Tower. The rooms were very basic and clean with no frills. Bathroom was dated and had no flare. Carpets were clean. Beds and pillows were to my liking, but they have a weird plastic like middle sheet that was somewhat uncomfortable. Rooms have nice, big HD TV's with plenty of channels, coffee pots with Starbucks coffee, and complimentary newspapers and water. The room was equipped with the smallest safe I've ever seen in a hotel room, not even large enough for a laptop. Overall I enjoyed my stay at the Sheraton and would stay again. I just nit pick in reviews to give an overall sense of what your going to get.

“Patio on lake” It is probably a man made lake, but the outodoor patio with bar service was a preasant surprise. Beautiful and relaxing. Great property. Far from airport, about 45 minutes. Taxis must be called, there is not a taxi stand where they are waiting to take you anywhere. Both times it was about a 10 minute wait. Great restaurant off lobby with very good service. Front desk staff were also very accomodating. Lobby provided free lemonade and water all day, coffee in the morning. Free internet in lobby.

“LEFT OUR HEARTS IN SAN FRANCISCO” Upon arrival, it was pouring down with rain & we thanked the gentleman who worked there, who helped us in to the hotel from the cab. The hotel receptionist were busy when we got there, with a long line of people checking in, however they did a fantastic job & were extremely welcoming & friendship to us. We got upgraded & received a $20 voucher to spend at the inhouse Starbucks - For no reason? We didn't ask for an upgrade or voucher, so we found this was lovely. The room was clean - a bit old fashionished but it had character. Central to everything & safe. Would stay there again & have told others that its a great place to stay for a decent price.

“Doesn't disappoint. but oh those elevators” We have stayed here 4 times now and still love the Marquis. We had good service from front desk, in lounge, and from housekeeping. Admittedly we weren't there all that long this time so didn't use all services. But nothing beats the 8 fl lounge for nice cocktails, maybe the cheese platter, and a fantastic view of Times Square. You can also get literally ANYWHERE you want to go in just minutes from this hotel. I did call the concierge for show tickets as I was told they can do that, but they forwarded me to a ticket service without saying that was what they were doing. The Marquis is also pretty overpriced. We paid about $550/ni and it is nothing more than a nice Marriott room. But we did have a nice flat screen tv, plenty of room, and a view of Times Square. So we just swallow the cost and enjoy the superb location, nice room, and good service. The only thing is tha tthis trip the elevators were HORRIBLE. We had thought since they put in the new elevator system it was better, but we almost were late for a show after waiting sooooo long for an elevator. When one finally came to our floor we just squeezed in and held our breath. I would stay again. And hope the price doesn't go up....

“Gute Lage, aelteres Hotel, sehr teure Parkplatze” Das Hotel ist gut gelegen, direkt hinter dem Fishermans Wharf. Direkt an einer der beiden Cable Car Linien. Trotz Diamond Status bei Hyatt habe ich nur ein ziemlich schaebiges Zimmer erhalten. Zimmer sind eher dunkel. Die Parkplatze des Hotels sind mit USD 45.-- pro Nacht + Taxen und Tip (somit dann > 50 USD) viel zu teuer. Ich wuerde alternativen Suchen,w enn ich nochmals hier waere.

“fun, yet sophisticated” Just enjoyed an in-town getaway here. We wanted a base from which we could reexplore such shopping/dining areas as: the Beverly Center, The Grove/Farmer's Market, Third St., Robertson Blvd., Melrose Ave., La Cienega Blvd., and Beverly Blvd. The choice came down to the SLS and the Sofitel; the new Montage Beverly Hills was enticing but too far west. We opted for the SLS because it is newer, a Starwood Luxury Collection property, nightlife guru Sam Nazarian's first hotel, and home to The Bazaar by Jose Andres, only the second restaurant to ever receive the highest four star rating from the Los Angeles Times (the first, Bastide, is now closed). Monkeys are the SLS's mascots because, a front desk staffer told me, they are "fun, yet sophisticated", which is the hotel's aim. Designed by Philippe Starck with typical whimsy, humour and modern style (sometimes at the expense of practicality or function), the hotel also tries to provide a high level of service. For the most part, it succeeds. The staff is young, friendly and largely professional, but certainly less formal than at a Peninsula or Four Seasons. On weekends, there are lots of young partying beautiful guests usurping the pool and restaurant/bar, causing commotion in the hallways and rooms (think HBO's "Entourage"), but come Sunday, the place settles down. There are separate entrances to The Bazaar and hotel, which has its own quiet restaurant, Tres. The hotel's lobby lounge is actually outdoors. Typical Starck touches abound--mismatched furniture everywhere, long tall communal tables in the restaurants, mismatched glassware in the rooms, all varieties of chandeliers and huge mirrors. The front desk area is dark. The meeting rooms are named after famous monkeys. A room key is needed to ascend any elevator. Each floor has a pool table with a silver floor lamp shaped like a rifle. Throughout the lobby and restaurant are myriads of shelves filled with books and tchotchkes--a housekeeping nightmare! THE ROOM. I had reserved a veranda room, but the very accommodating receptionist quickly upgraded me to a Signature Suite with terrace when no veranda rooms were available. It was large and so very chic. The terrace rooms all seem to be on the 2nd floor with the terraces exiting onto 3 different garden courtyards. As mentioned in numerous prior reviews, the rooms are dark, with many tinted, almost useless reflective smudgeable surfaces/mirrors (even in the shower)--another housekeeping nightmare--I was compelled to leave a larger than usual tip out of sympathy. The desk lamp looks hand-blown but is insufficient. I'm sure the floor lamp styled like a tree trunk and the lighted makeup mirror in the bath were added in response to guest comments about darkness. The sofas and chairs in the living area were chic but not cushy/comfy/plush. There were several design elements that did not seem durable: the white upholstery was stained, the handles on the heavy mirrored sliding doors to the bath were loose, the leather pulls used to open the unique closet doors were frayed and weakened. The large safe is situated too high. To encourage a festive atmosphere, the minibar is very amusing and complete--large bottles of booze plus interesting mixers, a martini shaker, 2 bins of treats labeled Saints and Sinner. The bed was queen size, low (to fit into the sleek custom headboard/nightstands), not quite Westin Heavenly. The terrace showed evidence of past revelry and lack of maintenance--many cigarette butts on the ground, a cigarette burn in the sofa. The shrubs by the wall were dead (hopefully not from urine), but the bamboo was alive and the potted Meyer lemon trees were bearing fruit. There are W Hotel-like catchphrases all over, some of them "SLS", like "Scribble Little Secrets" on the pen, "Society's Latest Scandals" on the newspaper bag. In the bath, several common items were forsaken for style--no wall towel racks (just 2 stylish hooks), no bars of soap, no soap dish, no luggage rack. There were, however, huge Costco-sized bottles of hand, face and body washes, plus body lotion, shampoo and conditioner. The guest directory will tell you these are green because they are refillable. I asked the housekeeper if people take them like they do the usual mini-sized ones--she said yes, so we did. The shower is slate, mirrored, huge, with a concealed drain. I found the towels a bit small and thin, though they are custom made by D. Porthault for SLS/Starck. We could hear others guests through the bathroom vent. The guest directory makes for a fun read, is titled the "SLS Illustrated Dictionary of Services" and includes such listings as " 'Tight Buns'--see personal fitness training" and " 'zzzzz'--see linens, mattress and bedding". THE RESTAURANTS. Dined Sunday evening at The Bazaar. We had peeked in on Saturday night--the place was teeming with foodies and revelers, the noise deafening. Sunday was much calmer (the NBA finals, which the LA Lakers clinched on this night, probably contributed). All four venues--Rojo, Blanco, Bar Centro and the Patisserie were accessible. There is an outdoor terrace, but it faces the valet drop-off area. Apparently about $22 million was put into The Bazaar alone. I was expecting a molecular gastronomy experience along the lines of Alinea or Moto in Chicago, where a meal is a 3-5 hour, sometimes solemn affair. But The Bazaar is different--tapas (traditional and modern) with some molecular gastronomy elements like liquid nitrogen, trompe l'oeil presentations, specific instructions on how to eat a particular dish correctly. Very theatrical and playful, but serious and delicious. And fast--we were done with the tasting menu, presented in "waves" rather than one dish at a time, in under 2 hours. I was a bit disappointed that the tasting menu was simply dishes off the regular menu yet cost a bit more than if ordered a la carte. The food is much better than it has to be--this place would be popular even without the foodies and four star review, and it meshes so well in atmosphere with the hotel. Apparently, there is a "fine dining" restaurant within the restaurant (it is mentioned on the website) that serves a set tasting menu 3 nights a week. There is an outpost of Moss, the great New York Soho design store, here. Hotel guests also apparently have special access to Nazarian's other restaurants/clubs/lounges. The other restaurant, Tres, is a quiet retreat, never crowded. The menu was quite similar to the room service menu, with some prices identical as well. Tried the continental breakfast buffet one morning and it was fine, included cheeses, chacuterie and aguas frescas. THE POOL. Located on the 6th floor. Reminiscent of the pool at the Starck-designed Mondrian Hotel. Quite See and Be Seen on the weekend, with the pools, one no more that a foot deep, secondary to the cabanas, lounge chairs/beds, and restaurant, named Altitude. The fitness center on the 2nd floor is large and well -equipped. Did not try the adjacent spa. The business center charges for internet use. Overall a fun, relaxing stay. We were able to walk or bike to all target areas, with the Grove being the furthest (1.2 miles) away. It doesn't seem too business oriented (except probably show business), nor too kid friendly. It is a decent value, especially compared to the luxury hotels in Beverly Hills proper (SLS is one block away from BH), though perhaps not quite as pampering an experience. Would definitely stay here again, and in fact plan to do so. Kudos to management for reading TA reviews and responding to each individually. This is especially important since a guest comment card is not offered, although I did receive a thank-you email from the hotel afterward, and there was a link for comments.

“Great location, attentive service, good value” stayed june 13, 2004, ask for top floor room, quiet, roomy, view of mtns, good location to freeway, shopping, movie theaters. staff is excellent, helped with reservations and directions, attentive. pool was so so, dirty. breakfast has waffles and hard boled eggs, fruit. free wireless internet in lobby area. great rates too!

“Unless you are staying at the property for a convention I wouldn't recommend it.” The lobby area is fantastic. The guestrooms are outdated. I would not recommend this property to those who are not there for a convention. The property sits far off from all the "action" of Chicago so if you are into walking to the attractions, this hotel is not that convienient. My experience wasn't horrible that I wouldn't stay there again, I just feel there are better situated properties that are not as outdated.

“Great service; amazing beds; superb location” Location: I was hesitant booking this hotel based on location alone, not being in the heart of downtown. But Little Italy is a really happening place in the evenings, and seemed busier than most areas downtown at night. Service: Customer service was excellent at this hotel. Dealing with a situation in our first room; the free shuttle to the zoo; holding onto our luggage after early check-out; and answering our questions - all handled very well in a customer-oriented manner. Roof top area: There are a number of areas within the hotel, especially on the 5th floor, from which to sit down and enjoy the view. I really looked forward to my evening cigar and scotch while taking in the view of downtown, Little Italy, Coronado, the airport, and incoming planes. Rooms: Initially we were in a 'Comfy Queen' room at ground level next to the parking lot, storage, and utility areas. These rooms are small and dark. If we had stayed here the whole week, I would have given this about a 3/5 review instead of the 5/5. I'm not one to complain as you get what you pay for. But a couple of days into are stay, we woke up to dripping water. I ignored it thiking it was the shower. But it was actually a fast leak from the ceiling pouring down into the open toilet, which splashed everywhere on the floor. There was a flap of ceiling plaster that had popped open where the water was pouring from. The excellent customer service mentioned above is what led to a room change into a King-size on the top floor. Beds: In both rooms, the beds were extremely comfortable. I looked forward to sleeping every night. And we needed it after very full days of excursions, sight-seeing, shopping, and eating. Other: -I was surprised to see the work-out room. Nothing fancy, but enough to get my quick work-outs done in the evenings. -The free Wi-Fi service in the rooms is hugely appreciated. This permitted us to plan our days, map destinations, and book excursions. -I like what they've done with the style of the hotel. They've taken an old motel and turned it into something trendy.

“Excellent location” We were a bit nervous due to previous reports, but the location was so darn great...right by Carnegie & Stage Deli's for cheesecake after a show or a close walk for a moonlit carriage ride in Central Pk. We admittedly do alot of tourist stuff when we're in town & this location is great for subway or walking. We had a group who used 2 rooms. They were clean & nice. The stay was just fine. We had a blowdryer go out & it was fixed within minutes! The check-in & out had lines, so go a few minutes early. But nothing outrageous. Yes, it's aging a bit & not super fancy. But you're not paying the super fancy price either! This is a fine value for the City & we'd stay again.

“The W in DC - Very Nice Hotel” I had to attend to some business in Washington and last time stayed at the St Regis and was totally beyond impressed and was planning on staying there again next time I came to town but I was meeting up with a friend who is a W fanatic and insisted we stay here. (in fact we are still here as I type) It does not live up to the St. Regis but then again it is several hundred dollars a night cheaper so..... ;-) Anyway, It is a great hotel however, it is maybe, just a little "too hip"??? is that possible, LOL?? I don't know how to describe it, almost trying too hard? I guess I just don't get the whole W concept, I know many people who adore them. Anyway, the service is spot on, the hotel is beautiful (if you like hip and modern), and the roof - top lounge is absolutely stunning and filled with Washington's beautiful people, very interesting to enjoy a evening up there. The room, a Fantastic Suite (actual room name) is medium size for a suite, but plenty big for Washington. My friend is flying out tomorrow and I am moving over to my old stand-by the Willard in the morning but I expect I might try another W out again in the future.

“Don't stay here if you actually want to sleep” I'm not a precious traveller. I swear I'm not. But when you can hear every cough, footstep, door opening, door closing and elevator ping that happens, ALL NIGHT LONG, then you tend to get a little fed up. This hotel isn't soundproofed. At all. Maybe the good reviews, below, are from people who stayed before the hotel was full. Because if there's more than one person on the floor, it's ridiculous. And the elevator ping is way too loud. My room was the furtherest away from the elevator yet every time it arrived, I heard it. A doubleping. When you're standing next to it, it's geniunely deafening. Room service arrived promptly - food was middling, a 'main' salad was the size of a side, arrived without any bread or anything like that. The people are young, goodloooking, charming - but you can get that at any Soho hotel. And the room is tiny, cold, and beautiful. All in all, this place is severely style over substance. Why someone would build a potentially beautiful hotel and then give it the soundproofing qualities of an open hospital ward is beyond me.

“Good location, good people” Everyone here is pleasant and really seems to appreciate your business. In the bistro area, there are booths with a TV and outlets so you can work and not have to worry about your battery. Very nice feature that is not mentioned anywhere. The room was clean and of nice size. You may be able to hear the traffic on I-% as the hotel overlooks the Interstate. Parking is available primarily underground. It is a short 2 1/2 block walk to the main drag of old town for restaurants. Took around 5 minutes r so to get there. I would use this hotel again. The air-conditioning in my room was a bit loud when ti was cooling which might affect a lite sleeper.

“No more free parking.” Standard large Hampton Inn with 6 floors. Great housekeeping, but parking has been raised to $15.00 a night from free. With these charges it's best to stay at another Hilton property in the area and avoid the ripoff.

“OK hotel, basic room, no free internet” I stayed here on a business trip. Meeting facilities were excellent but the room was very basic considering what I paid and the fact that internet was $12.95 per 24 hour period. Too bad our meeting organizers cannot see clear to try the Holiday Inn chain where internet is free and the rooms are on par or better than this particular Marriott.

“Location is nicest aspect of Doubletree.” I stayed at the Doubletree in downtown Philadelphia for three nights in mid-August while on a business trip. In general, the nicest aspect of the hotel is the location - squarely in the middle of downtown Philadelphia within walking distance of many restaurants, etc. There was really nothing negative about the hotel but little to offer in the way of positives either. The lobby is small but fairly well appointed. Check-in was quick and easy. The hot cookie was a nice touch. The rooms appear to be have been remodeled within the last few years. They are decorated in a "contemporary" style - not my taste but at least the room was not run-down. My room had an odd shape - long hallway opening into a modest bedroom area. The room and especially the bathroom have nice ameneties. I ate only one time in the hotel restaurant - for breakfast. The meal was ok, fairly typical for hotel fare. I did not try room service but they have an extensive room service menu. The pool and hot tub area were not very impressive. The hot tub looks like something you would have on the back of your house - complete with a wooden deck around it. Very out-of-place in an urban hotel. The pool was very small and does not give the impression of being well maintained. A water pipe feeding the pool was barely hanging on with some duct tape. They have a nice but small exercise area. The business center was small and you have to pay for the internet usage after 15 minutes of "free" time. I find this irritating - the nearby Park Hyatt offers free internet usage. The conference rooms were very comfortable, nicely appointed and easily accessed from the elevators. I nearly rated the Doubletree an overall 4 stars, but the hotel just doesn't quite rise above mediocre - average in most categories.

“The Good and the Bad” Okay, all things considered this wasn't a bad hotel, but I wasn't overly impressed either. The good news about the room--up to date furnishings, carpet, tiles, walls, etc., strong air conditioner, good bed, mini-fridge and microwave. The bad news about the room--it was narrow and undersized, had a lovely view of an air shaft where you couldn't even see the sky, had NO cell phone reception, and had a budget flat screen television with a ridiculously undulating volume that surely disturbed neighboring rooms. Also, don't you hate hotels that give you a sheet and a fat down comforter with no blanket in the middle of the summer? Who uses an inch-thick comforter in July? With a strong air conditioner in a tiny room, a blanket would be a welcome addition, but they didn't even provide one in the closet, so you either freeze or burn up when sleeping. This hotel also likes to brag about "free hi-speed wireless in EVERY guest room." You can ping a wireless hot spot, but unless you want to wait 20 minutes to load a Web page or email, forget about it. Thankfully, an Ethernet connection is provided on the room's desk, which worked fine and is the only real way to get any work done. As for transportation, arriving at and leaving this hotel was a major challenge. There is only one three-car pull off for the entire hotel, which is always full, on one of the busiest streets in downtown DC--14th Street leading directly to/from I-395. The hotel has NO public parking and you have NO access to your own car--everything is valet only, which means tipping each and every time you drop off and pick up your car, to say nothing of the $30 daily parking charge plus 10% garage tax. That's right, $33 a day for parking if you bring your own car. The good news about transportation--they aren't kidding when they say the McPherson Street subway station is right across the street. It is. What is not advertised about the DC metro, though, is the lack of air conditioning in stations, which in July was a bit like descending the escalator to hell. Add to that, ongoing summer track maintenance with fewer trains running all summer long, and it's so not worth waiting 15-20 minutes in stifling underground heat when you could walk to the National Mall and Smithsonian in about 10. In other words, if your sole reason for staying at this hotel is metro access, I personally don't think it's worth all the negatives.
