Food in the hotel was pretty average--typical Hilton buffet breakfast with hots and colds. We had comp breakfast coupons, so I don't know what the actual cost would be. Probably not cheap if the daily parking charge was any indication. Typical big city hotel--nickel and dime you for every cent they can squeeze out of your pocket. Sorry, but I was not impressed. Will never stay here again with many other options in the same area.

“A Winner!” Just returned from our 2nd stay at this hotel and once again, everything was outstanding. As others have pointed out, the location can`t be surpassed. Some have griped about the tiny lobby, but this is a triviality. Upon entering the hotel there are 2 check in/check out kiosks. You swipe your credit card, your reservation information comes up and it gives you your room key card. Very easy......no waiting in line. Elevator access requires the key card so security is a priority here. The youthful, smartly dressed staff is perpetually smiling and helpful. To appease those disgruntled souls who have issue with the lobby, the 7th floor Terrace Club more than compensates. There is a spacious sitting area, restaurant and gratis computers so you can check your personal email. As others have also mentioned, there are filtered water dispensers with bottles in the Terrace Club and on some other hotel floors. The hotel is only 3 years old and our room still looked new. We had a very comfortable queen bed, kitchenette, a great bathroom with a huge shower, flat screen televsion, comfortable sitting area with sofa bed and all the amenities of a much more expensive hotel. Requests for exptra pillows and an iron and ironing board were honored withing 5 minutes. We got all this for a great rate of $159 per night. We shall return!

“A little hiccup, but they took care of it right away” Really nice hotel in a very convenient location in Printer's Row, just about a 10 - 15 minute walk from Michigan Avenue and the Art Institute. Nice rooms and friendly, capable staff. We had a slight problem with our room - after showers, there was a strong sewage smell - the front desk took care of it immediately and moved us to another room - providing a free upgrade and even complimentary drinks at the bar that night. The hotel is undergoing some construction, which may have been the cause of our issue, but otherwise, you wouldn't know they were working - we never heard a thing coming from the construction area. The breakfast, as others have mentioned, is not great, but enough to get you going til you can get over to the nearby Starbucks or Dunkin Donuts. I would definitely stay in the Blake again.

“good holiday hotel would stay again” stayed here 5th-8th sept with my wife hotel was good no problems,perfect location for all amenities,short drive to fashion valley transit station to get tram/train into downtown sandiego best way of getting around save yourself a lot of hassle looking for parking.car parking at transit station is free so perfect for sightseeing,day pass 5dollars great value.hotel amenities were fine breakfast was adequate cereal,porridge,waffles toast and different breakfast breads,yoghurts fruit and different hot and cold drinks.would stay here again.

“Definitely not normal Marriott quality” Very big complex which knocks this hotel down several grades. We were there recently for a 3 night stay to attend a conference at this location. The room we were forced to take was in the Park Tower. This is the back end of the hotel and apparently dug into the hillside as you are more or less in the basement. The room would have been good for a Super 8, but I was staying at a Marriott and expected much better. The whole complex is aged and we have a couple of issues with our room which took multiple calls to the front desk to resolve. I can not really speak specifically to value as our room was paid for by work, but I know what the rate was and I would not call it any sort of value for the price and what our accomodations were. I do not know the DC area and can't really speak to the location with much authority. It seemed to be in an okay location, the zoo nearby, we walked about 2 miles to J. Pauls in the Georgetown area and the Metro is vey close which we took for about a 1/2 hour ride to a Nationals game. I would not stay here again unless I was on a free ride.

“Great location 2 blocks from the White House” This is a very nice hotel. It has just undergone a major refurbishment, and the rooms are spacious, well appointed, very comfortable, and very nicely decorated. I stayed here for 4 nights with my mum over New Years, 2012, and we both very much enjoyed this hotel. It is a great location. You see the White House as you step out of the hotel, just down the street. It is easy to walk to all the attractions from the hotel. It is also easy to walk to Dupont, and eat in the many cafes there, or into downtown. The restaurant staff at breakfast were very excellent. Our waiters were all excellent, and provided great service. The breakfast was very nice. The lobby bar staff were also exceptional, and made lovely cocktails. Concierge, and the doormen were also great. The Executive Lounge is typical for American Hilton's, nothing that special. It had limited hours, and provided minimal service, and food etc, and all alcoholic drinks had to be paid for, which is very different from in Asia etc.. The lounge itself is quite a nice room. All in all, we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. The only reason it hasn't received a 5-star, excellent rating, was due to the front desk. The staff were adequate, but the service standard wasn't what we were used to experiencing at Hilton Hotels, and it often seemed very understaffed. Housekeeping standard was very clean. We received suitable upgrades as Diamond guests also. Would recommend this hotel.

“Westin does it right” I stayed at the Westin Phoenix downtown for a convention I was attending. The main hotel was the Sheraton but the Westin is a quick 2 block walk. From the minute I arrived, I felt a different vibe compared to other Westins I have stayed at. This has a small hotel feel and every single staff member talks to you! The rooms are huge and the Heavenly bed is super comfy. Plenty of space for hanging clothes, small fridge, couch, etc. As a Platnium member, I had access to the club lounge which is open 7 days a week. They offer a light breakfast and hot options at 5pm. I ate in the restaurant for lunch and dinner. Make sure you eat outside with the firepit and get the Hawaiian tuna. I loved this hotel and am so happy that it is downtown. Starwood, you did good!

“It could have been a better experience...” The grounds were beautiful, the rooms were immaculate and the staff were friendly. The food at the Veranda (their casual dining restaurant) was but pretty good - love their pizza. Based on all of these, I would have given my experience 4 stars; however, one item really soured my experience. I called the front desk on Thursday morning - very early - asking if they could schedule a couple of spa services for me for the next day. I was informed that I would have to leave a voicemail for the spa as they are the only ones who have access to the appointment book. That made sense - so, I left the spa a voice mail. I never heard from them all day and upon returning to the hotel, later that evening, inquired again. I was informed the spa was closed but that the front desk would send them an email to contact me first thing Friday morning. I was on conference calls until about 11am on Friday morning and never heard from the spa. I left a voice mail with the manager of guest services informing her that the spa lost out on approximately $400 as no one had gotten back to me. I specifically stated I wasn't looking for anything free, but just wanted to make the Inn aware of the matter. I left the resort to go and enjoy the day in La Jolla. Around 2pm, I received a call from the spa asking me if I wanted to book my services for Saturday. I told them that I had left that voice mail the prior day and that I had wished for spa services on Friday. The response I get is "oh, I'm sorry, we can book you now". I retorted no thanks since I'm in La Jolla - 25 minutes away. BTW, I never heard back from the guest services manager either, which I do believe is poor customer service. I'm still giving this experience three stars because, other than the spa mistake and lack of responsiveness, everything else was really nice.

“Good location if you are attending an event at Moscone Center” The room was fine and a good size. However, from the first to the last time we walked into the room it smelled. Almost a weird soap smell. I am not a W fan though a big Starwood fan. They want to cater to being cool and hip. Focus on customer service and a delivery model. I only stayed there because I was attending a conference at the Moscone Center across the street and for that it was perfect. For some reason the room just did not feel clean. Dingy is the feeling. But that was just me. Oh and in very small print they put a $5 price tag on a small bottle of water in the room. Avoid their snacks and waters. Overpriced. You can buy all the water and snacks you need one block over at a food store on Mission St.

“Old Hotel right on the expressway” We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights from 13th January to 15th January 2007. The room was a good size with a king size bed and balcony overlooking the pool and car park area. The room has no fridge or microwave but has an ice bucket and coffee maker. There is only in room dining for breakfast. They have sports bar downstairs named Cassidys that looks inviting but when you go in there is plenty of tables chairs and TV's but they don't sell any alcohol as they don't have a licence to sell alcohol. We couldn't believe it. They would lose such much money with guests going elsewhere. The pool is indoors and open 6am - 10pm. The hotel also has a fitness centre and business centre which offers free internet. The room ahs a reverse cycle air conditioner. The bathroom is a bit small but functional with an extra bench with mirror located just outside the bathroom. Good for us women to get ready while hubby is in the shower. There is a McDonalds, Popeyes chicken , KFC and Pizza close by or a 5-10 min walk. Hotel is old and elevators are very slow. they have a coin operated laundry.The bed was comfy. We ordered feather pillows from housekeeping which helped us sleep.The hotel is right on the expressway and the noise of traffic and sirens kept us awake all night. We wouldn't stay here again as the hotel did not make our standards that we are use too.

“Union Square area for under $80” Have stayed here on 5 occassions now, its a good deal when you can't get a 4 star hotel under $100. This property fits the bill, its in a decent area, close to everything and offers a pretty decent continental breakfast(muffins,donuts,bagels, juices,milk, fruits) I look forward to visit #6

“Excellent staff and a great location” I had an event where we needed to book a conference room for the day. The day before, I shipped a Fed-Ex package of equipment that I was to pickup at the front desk upon arrival. Well, the rental car line was 20 deep at Hobby so I had to haul it in a cab. When I arrived, the hotel had already set everything up for me. The event went without a hitch and I had a bedroom and couch to lounge in for the rest of the day before my flight. (Beats waiting at the airport!) The guy at the front desk was very pleasant. He called me "sir" and helped me immensely when I realized that some of my items didn't get packed. (Packing tape, empty box, etc.) After we paid the bill, we were notified that we had overpaid by $30.00+ and were being issued a refund check. The location is great. I was able to do a 10 minute walk and eat at Beck's Prime in the underground city a few blocks away. The hotel itself was very clean. The only complaint I had was that their wireless was extremely slow. I also couldn't get a good 3G signal from the room. I'm not a fan of $10 parking, but it's downtown...so what are ya gonna do? I wouldn't hesitate to stay here if I found myself back in Houston.

“a resounding "eh"” This is an old-style hotel in a historic building approximately five blocks from the Inner Harbor. Although reasonably well kept, the hotel will disappoint guests who prefer modern styling. On the whole, the public spaces are a bit dark and grim, and furnishings in the public areas were outdated and overused. The room itself was fine: the bed was excellent (sleep number) and the bathroom was clean, but the room was small, the heat was weak, and the windows leaked in frigid air. Soundproofing was good. The front desk staff were agreeable and helpful. A business center has two terminals with complimentary internet service, and rooms have free WiFi. The neighborhood is an unappealing and commercial area that, to some, may appear to possess an uneasy air of danger.

“Gutes Mittelklasse-Hotel, etwas außerhalb gelegen” Das Doubletree Denver ist wirklich ein gutes Mittelklasse-Hotel, das meine niedrigen Erwartungen mehr als übertroffen hat. Zunächst bietet das Hotel einen kostenlosen Shuttle-Service vom und zum Flughafen und bei der Ankunft im Hotel gab es zur Begrüßung einen frischen Cookie. Unser Zimmer (wir hatten ein Doppelzimmer mit getrennten Betten) war ausreichend groß, nett eingerichtet, und sehr sauber. Der Zimmerservice war einwandfrei. Morgens ab 6 Uhr konnte man im zum Hotel gehörigen Café/Restaurant gut frühstücken, entweder à la carte oder Buffett (zum unschlagbaren Preis von 15 $, inklusive Kaffee, frischer Omeletts und Waffeln). Das Hotel verfügt außerdem über ein gut ausgestattetes kleines Fitneßstudio, einen Whirlpool und einen Swimming Pool (letzterer war leider wegen Renovierungsarbeiten geschlossen). Eine Hertz-Autovermietung befindet sich direkt neben der Rezeption. Einziger Nachteil: das Hotel liegt etwas außerhalb an einer großen stark-befahrenen Straße, direkt neben einer Strip mall. Eine Taxifahrt nach Downtown Denver kostet ca. 20-25 $.

“A great trendy and hip hotel!” While in SF on April. 2012, my 2 friends and I attended a function held on the terrace. It was very nice and kept it at the front of my mind for a future stay. That stay came at the beginning of Aug.2012. And it did not disappoint! :) The same 2 friends and I enjoyed our stay. The room was lovely and had a view of the bay and bridge. The bed was comfortable and there was ample space in the room and bathroom. We visited the bar and snacked on breaded chicken bites and some beer. The bartender was cool and was of great help. If you want internet access, they do charge a fee to access in your room but you can get some free Wi-Fi in the lobby downstairs. Everyone from the bell hops to the front desk clerks were very nice and professional. They greeted us w/a cordial and friendly attitude. There are restaurants and stores within walking distance. We will DEFINITELY come back to the W Hotel. It was great!! :D

“A nice place to stay” We enjoyed our stay at the Westin. Our room was very nice with a great king bed. Staff were very nice and helpful. Good location near airport. Would stay again and recommend to family. Thanks Westin.

“Perfect” Clean rooms,great location and great rate too,no complaints,really. My new home when in San Diego. The lady at the front desk was a bit cold and completely unsmiley tho,I guess she was just having a bad day. Other than a great hotel and I look forward to go back.

“great value/service/amenities for location!” one of best places i've stayed! grounds lovely, good fitness center, cozy comfy rooms, good toiletries, food at breakfast stellar (salmon, oatmeal, eggs) and wonderful snacks available! distance from city is downside but shuttle to train nice but not efficient if on schedule...we werent; we stay here when in seattle if dont need to be downtown for business

“hotel incroyable” Un hotel qui a apporté un atout majeur à la réussite de notre voyage. Tout dabord, il est central, proche à pied et en metro de toutes les attractions, personnel à l'écoute et au service, vue sur central park epoustouflante, grande chambre à la décoration moderne, belle salle de bain, piscine audernier étage avec solarium au 42ème. Hotel calme, je recommande le soir de diner au snack en bas ou il serve un hamburger mmm! un régal.

“Clean & Good Location” This hotel is not very far from Sea World but be aware that Sea World is not close to the downtown river walk area. If you are spending most of your time downtown then stay down there but to be out near Sea World this is a great location. There are a lot of restaurants, a mall, shopping, and a theater right across the street for any down time. The facility was extremely clean and all the staff no matter what their title were very friendly. They have a nice typical continental breakfast. The only negative is they only have one small very slow elevator...very slow.

“Second stay just as great as the first!” This was our second stay at the Marriott in the last six months. We booked the room through Priceline and got a great deal despite it being the first weekend of pre-Super Bowl activities in Indy. For attending those activities, the location could not be better! Right across from the Maryland Street leg of the Convention Center and just half a block from the zip lines and activities on Capital, we were in the heart of everything just half a block away. The valets at the Marriott were so cordial and up front about valet vs. self-parking in the garage under the hotel. Valets at some hotels lose interest in you if you decide to park yourself, but these guys were very nice, helpful with directions, and also very welcoming each time we went in or out of the hotel. The elevator from the parking garage goes straight up to the end of the hotel lobby--very convenient. When it came to checking in, Alex at the front desk could not have been nicer, answering my questions about a possibly extending our stay (we didn't but only because one evening of the Super Bowl stuff was enough) and arranging a late check out for us. We asked for a room at the end of the hall with a king sized bed--and that's what we got. Great view of the State Capital, too. The room was a standard King room and not overly large, but certainly big enough. The large flatscreen had a wide selection of channels, including HBO. Having a refrigerator would have been nice (we did not use the minibar). Although there was a national sorority convention at the hotel, we had a very peaceful stay and slept quite well (very comfortable bedding!). This is also the first hotel in a L-O-N-G time where we weren't awakened in the morning by hearing "Housekeeping" and tapping on the door of a nearby room. Although the housekeeping staff was working just a few doors down from our room, we weren't aware of them until we were ready to leave and went by the cart. Internet is free in public areas or in the business center (2nd floor). Guests can print 20 pages for free in the business center. The cost for Internet in the room depends on where your provider is located; if it is a local provider the connection fee is $1.00. Otherwise long-distance phone rates apply. We were able to use the business center for about 15 minutes to look up restaurant info, etc. The only negative for me: parking fees are high--$28 to self park for 24 hours and $34 to valet--but that is a city-wide issue in downtown Indy. The toilets in the rooms are also incredibly loud--similar to airplane or cruise ship toilets. The menu for the restaurant on the first floor looked amazing, but we didn't get the chance to try it this time. Definitely plan to next time--and this is a place we will be going back to again.

“As airport hotels go this is a good one” Hotels right in the airport terminals - like the Marriott Houston Airport -- are particularly convenient for connecting travel as there is no need to deal with hotel shuttles and other issues. But they can be expensive and sometimes are not terribly nice and can be noisy. At the Marriott Houston, yes, you pay for the location but here's what you get: - Reasonably quiet facilities - Decent facilities including nice rooms, a revolving restaurant at the top and good regular restaurant and a good exercise room. - Good service The problem with the hotel is the same as the problem with Houston airport overall - space. The place is big and you might have to walk a decent distance to get to your room. The layout of the circular towers with four radiating hallways from the center can be confusing too with its symmetry. I've stayed at a number of hotels around Houston airport and yes, the hotels not directly in the terminal offer a lot of value as they have lower prices than this hotel. Yet overall if you are willing to pay a premium for being in the terminal, the Marriott Houston airport should not disappoint.

“Wonderful Philly overnight!” My husband and I booked this Radisson for a weeknight stay via a Travelzoo offer including valet parking. The hotel also permits pets ($50 cleaning fee/stay and $10/night), which sealed the deal for us! We were impressed from the moment we pulled in front of the hotel. The valet staff was courteous. Check in was quick and pleasant. And yes, we were excited about the chilled fruit-infused water in the lobby to cool us down on a very hot day! I find the criticisms of the decor in some of the previous posts unfounded, as I loved the look of the hotel in general. We were put on the 4th floor, which I suppose is the pet-permitted floor but given room 423 which was a corner room and very large, airy, and bright, thanks to the two huge windows. With it being a corner room, foot traffic was minimized, and thus my dog was less jumpy as he heard people pass by. The bed was a sleep number bed and took a while to figure out but was fine. The free wireless internet was fast. The bathroom was small but adequate and most importantly, clean. Shower pressure was good with plenty of hot water (via an oversized showerhead). I enjoyed the toiletries, especially the almond-scented soap. One minimal criticism was that the toilet didn't seem to flush very powerfully and thus the handle needed to be pressed down longer. Another disappointment was with the 32-inch flatscreen. We were ok with the fact that the picture quality was not HD, but the sound had lots of static. We did not address this with the hotel as we just shut the TV off and called in an early night. I did hear garbage trucks and sirens pass by but it didn't bother me too much...it goes with the territory of being in a city! Location-wise, the Radisson Warwick Plaza could not be beat; we were just minutes from Rittenhouse Square, which my dog loved! We had made reservations for dinner at Tinto and that was only a 15 minute walk away. We enjoyed walking around the neighborhood for window-shopping and felt completely safe in the neighborhood. The bellstaff at the hotel was very helpful in giving us walking directions to Reading Terminal Market. We enjoyed a great value at this hotel. I highly recommend it for location and the level of service the staff provide. They were even able to accomodate a late checkout for us, which allowed us to truly relax and enjoy our stay even more! I definitely would not hesitate to stay at the Radisson Warwick Plaza in the future, should I be offered a similarly-priced offer.

“alright for a quick trip, noisy and nothing speical” it was nicely located down town, half a block from the lake, and a $3. cab ride the the nice shoping areas and resturant. had the switch rooms when i got there. the windows were only partly covered by the unattractive curtians and there was a parking garage 6 feet away from the building... the bathrooms were all brand new and nice. def the best part of the hotel. bed was alright, nice to have kitchenet, tv half worked. staff wasnt very helpful or friendly over all. house keeping either took all the towels and washed them everyday-because they dont seem to follow the 'if its hanging you'll use it again' policy that they have posted everywhere. orrr iw as using towels that other peple had that they just fold up and put back on the rack...

“Beautiful hotel in the Northwest” Family and I absolutely loved the Olympic hotel. From the swimming pool that was a good size for young kids (6 yr old) and the cookies and milk they brought at night, it was a complete, comfy experience. We plan on heading back to Seattle soon and would make this place a must stay. Room service is pricey, so take the 10-15 min walk to the market (Lowell's has an awesome crab omelette) or run down to the French bakery on the first floor for some tartlettes and coffee for a nice change.

“A cozy spot in Chicago” This hotel is very well maintained. The rooms are cozy and clean, and the beds are very comfortable. The front desk staff was very helpful with directions and suggestions, and we asked a lot of questions! There is a wide assortment of items for breakfast, both hot and cold. I would stay here again.

“Sheraton figured out how to do it right.” You can't help but notice a large trophy on the twelfth floor lobby desk of the Sheraton. The staff is proud of their service and intend to keep the trophy by staying friendly, keeping the rooms clean and attractive, providing internet access/boarding pass printouts in the lobby, taking care of problems right away such as replacing batteries in the TV remote. There is one set of elevators from street level to the lobby and a second set from the lobby to the rooms. Reminded me of Tokyo hotels that occupy a few floors of a high rise. Always wanted to stay in one and now I feel like I have. We hung out for a little while in the small lobby sipping complimentary lemonade. Central location. Weekend street as well as hotel interior parking. It's a new hotel and Sheraton figured out how to do it right. The suites are very well designed to maximize space while providing kitchen area, sitting area, sleeping area, desk and bathroom with tub. Coincidentally a friend was staying at the hotel the same nights we did. We were all raving about how nice the hotel was. Nice workout room on the rainy day. Quick drive up 163 to Balboa Park for a run on the sunny day. There were very small problems such as occasionally hearing our neighbors and dry air.

“Clean Room, Soft Bed, Free Breakfast” All the basics are there; Simple check in, very nice and clean room, an excellent night of sleep (I heard no sirens as per other reviews and I am a fairly light sleeper) The free breakfast was nice; nothing over and above but still very nice. Was asked how the meal was when I got up which was also something that made me feel that the staff actually cared about the customers. The one thing I will warn business travelers of; Getting a cab in the morning is a nightmare, I called 10 minutes prior got out front to witness three people diving for a single cab (that was most likely the one I called) all claiming they had been waiting for upwards of 20 - 30 minutes. I ended up having to call a car service which took 30 minutes to arrive only to find that only two cabs showed up during that period.

“A Value Hotel, But at least it's worth the money!” I stayed at this hotel 3 times this summer as a result of Priceline bidding. I'll try to keep this one short....so here's "the skinny" as they say: - The location is EXCELLENT!!! It's just outside of Times Square's major hustle and bustle ..you can't much beat it unless you are directly in Times - The service is so-so...during the day..there's usually a wait at the front and bell desks. The front desk being the more irritating of the two as there is usually only 1 or 2 people there even during its busiest times.Last time it took me nearly 20min to checkout on a pre-paid reservation. - My major complaint....this hotel needs big time updates. It appears that they don't attempt to renovate or take the time to spot check for issues like paint or broken furniture pieces. The rooms are rather drab...it's great for school groups or when you aren't planning to stay in your room much. However...if you're paying between $95-$115/night like I did...it's worth it for the location. - Crazy complaint, but one none the less-- The TV's take awhile to respond to the remote control...almost like when your batteries are dying in your home remote. I thought it was a 1 time thing, but happened on all 3 of my stays. Oh, and the selection of channels is pretty limited. That's about it....good if you look at it as a value hotel.

“Unbelievable A/C noise. Very clean, but not Starwood” This hotel is clean, updated , and staff very helpful. Hotel situated right behind a strip mall and is actually hard to see. The neighborhood is in transition and not nice, however, I do not think it is unsafe. Rooms are tiny. Would never try and stay here with more than 2 people as even this would be cramped. One small covered chair, one small desk, and a TV stand with drawers. What is truly stunning is the air conditioning systems in the room. The low frequency rumble off of these units is unbelievable!!!! Shakes the room when they start up. No whinning engine, or squeaks, just tons of low frequency rumble that hurt my ears a little. Absolutely reminds you of a train going by, or the 1200 watt subwoofer on some cars. You have to turn the TV up while it is running. if you are a light sleeper, you're done, as these cut on and off all night (thank you Ambien) . What idiot purchased these things. Beds are very comfortable, If the rooms were larger and they replaced the A/C with something acceptable sound-wise, this place would be fine. The A/C units would prevent me from staying here again.

“Nice Homewood Suites” As far as the property goes, it is pretty much what you expect from a Homewood suites, nice big rooms, decent but smallish pool, free parking, breakfast and (non weekend) dinner included, the usual homewood stuff. It was a crowded hotel, the place was full and I have never seen it so busy at the pool and the meal service, esp breakfast, it was very crowded. The location is good for a San Diego visit, all the attractions in the area are within a 1/2 hour, and the beach is just 5-10 minutes away (and the hotel will rent you beach chairs and other beach stuff). So, since these properties are all pretty much the same, it is the staff that can make or break your visit. It's a bit of a mixed bag here. The food service staff was over the top great, skillfully handling the hordes of families (mine included), and providing customer service above and beyond what you normally expect at a free buffet style meal. The front desk staff was a different story. By no means did I have a problem with them, they just seemed a bit disinterested in the customer service aspect of the job, you got a vibe that they would like you to stop bothering them with your questions and or needs. Not rude, or unhelpful, just not warm and receptive, as I have come to expect at most hilton family properities. I'd stay again, it's a nice property that suited my needs.

“Great location but not the best” Great location in downtown Denver, close to everything that you need to do downtown. Hotel is clean and well maintained, the lobby opens up into a Peets Coffee, and the Yard House, so there is no problem getting coffee early or enjoying a late night meal if you are arriving on a late flight into Denver. What was annoying is that some rooms are located far from the elevators and you need to walk and walk and walk... Well priced and great downtown location.

“Stylish hotel” Rooms are beautiful. We were staying with our 2 kids and felt we had lots of room in our King Suite with 1 kid on sofabed and the other in a cot. The King Bed was super comfortable. The rooftop pool is fantastic, very stylish. Fantastic location right on the Riverwalk and in the middle of downtown. Valet parking is expensive but there is a cheaper carpark opposite. Occasionally had to wait at front desk for staff but all in all excellent service.

“Sopra ogni aspettativa” Stanze (vere e proprie suites) e bagno enormi ed eleganti, due televisori al plasma, mobili in stile e moquette. Prezzo veramente conveniente se prenotato con anticipo. Quando siamo tornati dopo una settimana, senza prenotazione, abbiamo pagato il doppio: comunque una cifra modesta per il livello dell'albergo. Servizi impeccabili e personale gentile. Da non credere.

“Absolutely Loved Club Quarters Chicago” My friend and I absolutely loved Club Quarters Chicago. We stayed for 3 nights and have nothing bad to say about the place. We were a little nervous after reading some online reviews, but were completely impressed. The location is SUPER convenient to the El--the red and blue (O-Hare) lines are about a block away and the orange line (Midway) is about 2 blocks away. The rooms are fairly small, but not the smallest I've ever stayed in and on a vacation you're not in your room much anyways. The room was tastefully decorated with helpful ammenities like microwave and fridge. Someone else commented that the beds don't have blankets, but they're easily available if desired. The staff was WONDERFUL and very helpful with suggestions of places to eat, both nearby and farther away...in fact we took all their suggestions and were pleasantly surprised each time. The pub attached is cute and a wonderful place to end the evening, although it was pretty hopping after work! One of the best pluses to the hotel were the treats provided in the lobby/guest area. Coffee in the mornings, homemade cookies and soda in the afternoon, and water all day long. They also have computers with Internet and printers available 24 hours a day, which is very handy to check-in with the airlines. Overall, we were completely happy and couldn't have imagined a better place to stay--we highly recommend it.

“Not worth it” Positive: good enough location, double room was quite large, pleasant enough staff Negatives: I think, especially at these prices, that there simply was not enough value. Staff certainly never went above and beyond, everything (internet, bottled water, gym) was an extra cost. The decor was not nice and quite fussy and dated. The restaurants in the hotel are not worth trying either. There are much better values in nyc.

“A welcome return to it's best!” This is a hotel that I have stayed at on many occasions for both personal and business and it had generally been very good but on my last stay lets just say things " fell through the cracks" but they have certainly turned things around. I had a 3 night stay last week and it was great. I must commend Anika Joseph who has looked after me very well on this occasion and the stay was great. They are renovating at present so the lobby is rather small but still you would not notice if you did not know how great the real lobby is. Great location and the place just works. Most staff very welcoming including the doorman, front office and housekeeping staff. Concierge did rather rather busy most times and a bit " busy " too often but still all round good. A good job guys and well done don- a ship well on course! Bruce

“Great Hotel and Friendly Staff” I had a great experience here the past week. The hotel was spotless and the staff from the doorman to housekeeping seemed to be friendly and willing to help. I stay in Hyatt Hotels a lot and this was as good if not better than many. The hotel is great for anyone on business or just for leisure. The rooms were just your standard Hyatt rooms, its not the Ritz but its a solid 3.5 star hotel that's clean safe and a good experience. The hotel bar is actually priced very well at 6 bucks a 16 ounce beer and the bartenders were happy and nice.

“Gem of a place” Very good hotel in Midtown Manhattan! Still walkable but a tad removed from the theaters on 40s streets. Otherwise, two blocks away from the best strolling and shopping opportunities, and less than a $10 cab ride to the Met and other fantastic museums. Of course, if one is ready to brave the subway, there is not a problem at all. Good restaurants all around. As indicated by others, the front desk personnel are very helpful and kind, and we tapped on them for sightseeing ideas, restaurant reservations and confirmations on several occasions. Prior to our arrival, Monica in sales was very helpful in responding to questions and assisting with show and dinner options. We stayed five nights in a nice and spacious room on the fifth floor with two large corner windows. Nice bathroom with all the necessaries fully replenished every day. We found the aircond to be noisy. Not terrible, but noisy. Very generous breakfast is served from 7:00 until 10:00 weekdays and until 11:00 on weekends, meaning one does not have to be up at the crack of dawn. Items included coffee, tea, several fresh juices, bagels and breads, fresh sweet rolls, hard-boiled eggs, cold and hot cereal, and a large, beautiful fresh fruit salad! In addition, wine and cheese are served every afternoon from 5:00 until 8:00, again, plenty of opportunity to make it and mingle with other guests. Unfortunately, there is no wine and cheese on weekends. Coffee, tea, cookies and fruit remain available until midnight. There is a guest computer in the library and free internet access. Very nice - I highly recommend.

“Great if your used to staying in a crackhouse” Although I booked this room on hotwire and thought I was getting a great deal, I was surely disappointed after arriving. I called the hotel 2 weeks prior to my booking to request a non-smoking King room. The gentleman who answered the phone was more than happy to satisfy my request. When my wife and I arrived, we were less than impressed by the surrounding area. Although there was an on-site security guard in the parking lot, he seemed distracted and was sleeping near the front door. Shame on him as there was a car filled with gang members cruising throught the parking lot, looking for an available victim. Upon checking in, the desk agent asked me, "So, I have you down for a non-smoking king." I replied in the affirmative and after about 15 seconds of looking through her computer, the desk agent said to me, "Is a non-smoking double okay?" I told her that I had previously called to request a king and she told me, "You booked on hotwire and nothing is guaranteed." I told her, "I guess I have to take what you have." She rudely pushed me 2 room keys and my wife and I made our way up to our room. Upon entering the room, my wife expressed, "What is that smell? The room trully smelled like a senior nursing home. It smelled like a colostomy bag exploded. We immediately called the front desk and we were told we would get another room. My wife again inquired if there were any king rooms available. We were informed that the only king's available were smoking rooms. Hindsight is 20/20, but I should have taken it. Upon entering our 2nd double room, it smelled just as bad and it appeared as if the carpeting hadn't been vacuumed with trash and crumbs all over the floor. The bedspreads were circa 1978 and appeared dirty and unkept. The towels in the bathroom were paper thin. Come on, does it take much to stock the place with new towels. This isn't the Motel 6 and I would expect a little more from a chain like the Holiday Inn, especially their flagship brand. Furthermore, the drapery was ripped, the television had basic cable channels and the bathroom fixtures appeared old and unkept. At one point, my wife needed to go to the car for something and I actually said that I would escort her for the first time in our 7 years of knowing eachother. When I finally tried going to sleep, it was impossible. The smell permeated the room, my feet were hanging off the bed (doubles, come on I'm 6'2,) and I couldn't get the curtains to hide the light from the bright lights outside in the parking lot. This hotel was absolutely horrible. The staff was less than helpful and when I checked prices on their website, I found that I only saved myself 5 bucks by using Hotwire. Not worth it!!!!

“A Bit Disappointed” The Fairmont is a beautiful, older (but modernized) hotel in a prime Seattle location. The hotel is walking distance from most city sights, including the waterfront, aquarium, shopping, Market and many more. The lobby is old-style, large and comfortable, with oriental rugs, lots of wood, etc. Check-in was quick. Getting to the room -- not so quick. The hotel has four, quite small and quite slow elevators, one or more of which was almost always out of order in the two days we stayed there. Thus, at peak times such as mornings and dinner-time, there was a 5-10 minute wait. And, when the elevator finally did arrive, it was filled, because it only holds 5-6 people, without luggage. With luggage, it's crowded with 3. Our room was disappointing. Knowing that older hotels have a hodgepodge of rooms, many of which are smaller than modern hotels, I didn't expect much. Still the room was VERY small with no view. Queen bed. Only one chair -- thus, one of us had to sit on the bed to watch the very small TV. Of course, because the chair and bed were directly opposite (and the room was too small to move the chair next to the bed), we both could not watch TV at the same time w/o craning our necks. There was almost no place on the floor to put our suitcases and we ended up tripping over them. Room decor was ok -- not memorable -- and bed was comfortable. The A/C worked well and I believe there was a mini-bar (didn't use it). However, the room was so small that we didn't want to do anything there but sleep. The bathroom, by contrast, was a good size with lots of marble and nice amenities. Rooms were very well-insulated and there is an in-room safe. Wakeup call was timely and staff was very friendly. The concierge desk was well-manned and provided excellent suggestions. We tried the hotel restaurant for breakfast. The food was good and served fairly promptly. Cost was about what you'd expect for a high-end hotel. Workout room was modern and there was plenty of staff to assist. Overall, the stay was ok but, if coming again, for the same price I'd stay down the street at the Hotel Monaco or just try another hotel in the city.

“A true classic” If you can - stay at the Drake. This place can be expensive but I got a good price and I am glad that I did. The hotel is just amazing inside. You will feel like you have walked into a different era when you enter. The rooms are smallish but normal for Chicago. The service is spectacular - this is the standard against which other hotels should be judged. Bottom line - if you can get a good price stay here. If you can't get a good price but everything in Chicago is expensive then stay here and at least enjoy the cost. If you can't stay here, then stop by and walk through the lobby so that next time you visit you will know where to stay.

“Rooms will make you smile” August 2011- Hotel is undergoing a bit of a face lift. Not a major remodel. Does not affect rooms or noise, in my experience. Check in : Very quick and friendly, however there was no :"preferred" line for SPG members. It was very busy, but the staff was moving as fast as they could. Room: This is my 3rd stay at this hotel. Room is on the smaller side, but very cheery. soothing walls with added pops of color, art, and accessories. Accessories need to be noted as they are things like little lamps, a Budha nightlight (that changes color) books. staggerd shelving, vases. I had a corner room and the corner couches had decorative pillows with a round coffee table. It made for a nice sitting area and overlooked the city. Windows have nice wide shutters. Location: Located 2 block South of Market Street. A less than 10 minute will have you enjoying great shopping, or easy access to the BART system. Room Service: Food was excellent. Ordered what was recommended. Local salmon cooked to perfection, one of the best I have had. Arrived in less than 30 minutes, with a smile. Bath: Large Bathroom with a tub/shower combo. Lots of vanity space and shelving to hold extras. Robes provided and plenty of towels. Bath line is from "Bliss". What I find interesting is that you can go shopping without leaving your room. Room is stocked with items for sale such as wine by the bottle, hats, robes, Ipod docks, candy, nuts, chips, first aid kit, tote bags, and items for "adult safe encounters". There is a fully stocked mini bar also. Enjoy!

“Kept expecting Bette Davis to walk by” When I first walked in at street level I was a bit skeptical--right up against the L, marquis lights at entrance, bustling, and then an escalator to the lobby--but holy toledo! The ceiling is many stories high and painted with murals like a cathedral somewhere in Europe. The lobby is dark, with marble and velvet everywhere, 20's or 30's feeling...and crowded and busy...I felt like I was in Vegas for some reason. The front desk service was great, I even had an apple while checking in, and my room, renovated on the 19th floor was lovely...fresh, clean, large, with two big windows so lots of light. The elevators were a bit slow but fun, and dessert and a drink in the lobby was quite delightful. I'm not sure I would stay again, I prefer smaller boutique hotels, but I had a very pleasant stay.

“Poor service, beautiful views, nice space” How many people does it take to notice that a light is burned out and get it fixed? At the Arizona Biltmore apparently it takes a lot...The light in our bathroom was gone when we arrived late on a Wed pm. We first mentioned it on Thursday. Didn't get fixed. We called housekeeping on Friday. Still not fix. We spoke to housekeeping in person on Saturday. We talked to a manager Saturday afternoon. Finally, on Saturday night we called the manager again. We were promised it would be fixed in 10 minutes..I guess time stands still at the Biltmore because 10 turned into 20 which turned into 30... Housekeeping in general is pretty poor too. Our trash never got emptied one day. The shower had scum in it, the minibar was never replenished and somehow the housekeeper broke the toilet, never notified the maintenance department, and it stayed that way for over 9 hours. The architecture is nice. The views of the mountains are beautiful. But with the plethora of resorts in Phoenix to choose from I would aim for one where service is more of a priority. Ritz? Four Seasons? Hell, even the Hyatt Gainey Ranch.

“Not Bad...Not Bad at all!!” I stayed here during the last week of October. The property is pretty new so the rooms, the lobby, and amenities are completely up to date. I believe every room is equipped with a mini-refrigerator. The hotel provides complimentary shuttle service to and from Union Station. However I had to contact the hotel a few times because the shuttle was never on time picking up at Union Station. The neighborhood is not the best for taking a leisurely stroll. The staff is helpful and friendly. The hotel also provides free parking, which is rare for hotels in major cities.

“OK place to rest before flying” It's an easy drive from this hotel to the airport, so a good choice if you're flying out early. Checking in after midnight, I felt a little uneasy as I drove back to the large, tenement-looking building in the rear where my room was located. The parking lot was overly crowded and the building looked really run down, the corridors shabby and ugly. However, when I entered my room, I found it entirely satisfactory for a night's stay. The bed was comfortable and the shower worked well. I'd recommend this place, especially if you can check in before dark and avoid the very creepy ambiance.

“Nice hotel, but some problems” As with most Embassy Suites, you get a good value here when you think of the space you get, the 2-hour cocktail hour, free breakfast, and nice atrium area for meeting with family or friends. Rooms were clean, staff courteous, and a better than average breakfast for an Embassy. However, we did have a few problems. The indoor pool is nice, but the water was cloudy and all four kids in our party coughed all night long. After we checked in and were in our room, we checked on the Internet to find they had charged us $40 more than the quoted rate including taxes. I went to the front desk and they said they do that for incidentals and would be credited back to us after check out if we didn't use the telephone or pay movies. I know they do this sometimes when you use a debit card, but we were using a credit card. They should at least tell customers what they're doing! Didn't say a word to us. The breakfast line was very long on weekends if you get there after 9AM. Not sure I would stay here again unless the price was right.

“Great view of cathedral.” Upon arrival I was offered and upgrade which I gratefully accepted. After a long flight to NYC from Australia and my first stay at this hotel I felt very much at home. The room was a good size, well decorated in the classic style and it overlooked the cathedral and beyond. The restaurant wasn't open on the Sunday night so I went to the Gilt bar instead. Location on Madison Ave between 50th & 51st is really convenient to all things like Central Park, the MOMA, a couple of delis, and eveything else!

“Feels Like an Apartment!” If you like being just outside the city, then this is not a bad place to be. It's about 15 blocks from Cheesman Park -a fantastic park to run, picnic or take a walk. You are 45 minutes from most mountains for hiking and just 10 minutes from downtown. The hotel is quaint. The air-conditioner in the room as noisy. If you like to feel like your a local, this hotel feels like an apartment. You have a kitchen, living room, dining area, a decent bathroom, comfortable bedroom and two sliding glass doors to the balcony. I didn't use the amenities or the restaurant. I was completely satisfied with my 4 night stay. The price was nice too! About an hour from Denver International.

“Nice Hotel & Great Staff” My only complaint is that I picked the 4th floor for my stay and it is half smoking and half non and the entire floor smells of smoke anyway, I'm not sure every floor is like this though, I may have just picked the stinky floor. Stayed here for 4 days, there is a free breakfast served every morning (muffins, danish, cereal, bagel, toast, juices, fruit and a few hot items, one being waffles. My husband left a little earlier then the time breakfast was served every morning (I think breakfast starts 5:30am) and the staff allowed him to take cold items like juice, pastries, fruit every morning. There is a gym with 1 bike, 2 elipticals, 1 treadmill and weights. The machines have tv's attached to each one. There is a decent pool that is 3ft on the shallow end and 5 ft on the deep end. This is a newer hotel and is right off of the freeway, close to shopping and dining... ate at Mellow Mushroom & Pita Jungle in the area while staying here. Close enough to the big city but just far enough on the outskirt to be able to breath the air. :) Would stay here again if I needed to.

“Grungy, no internet for 3 days, charging for internet after this, no one takes responsibility” For the price, this hotel is not a good value. I smell faint cigarette smoke intermittently in my room, the cleaning seems grungy (sticky lamp switches - WTH!), and for the past 3 days the internet service (wired and wireless) has been down. Finally it comes back today somehow and they have the temerity to demand their 12.95 pounds of flesh/day (oh, 5.95 pounds of flesh/hour if you are not careful with the nasty "web" interface) after 3 DAYS+ of downtime! No one at the front desk or management takes responsibility and just passes you on - the internet support has no clue and tells you to keep trying. I have previously stayed at Parc 55 and it was awesome in terms of service, ownership, and amenities. Hilton, OTOH, is nothing like Parc 55 - I am sorry to have given these people my business.

“I enjoyed the MIllennium Boston Hotel” I stayed at the Millennium, Boston from 1/12-1/15/07. I was very excited to get the $109 travelzoo rate that I just discovered a week ago. It was perfect for me. The location of the hotel is incredible, directly across the street from Faneuil Hall in Boston's waterfront area. There are a number of restaurants and clubs that are right on the street below, as well as in the Faneuil Hall complex. If you are someone who does not party hard at night, having a room directly on the street(blacony rooms) might be difficult with the news and commotion that I witnessed at 1am on Friday/Saturday night. My room had no view whatsoever, but it was very quiet. The room, itself, was one of the best that i've ever had, not to mention for the price of $109. When I thinnk of the dives that I have stayed in during my trips to Manhattan, I cannot beleive the luxury and the cleanliness of the room, as well as the two-part bathroom with an incredibly big tub. There were some annoying parts of my stay. There is no shuttle to the airport. There is coffee only during the week and not on the weekend when I desperately needed it. When I quesitoned the staff about this slight imperfection, I received two different explanations(at two different times). The first was that they needed the restaurant staff for the morning breakfast,. What??!?!? The second was that, on the weekend, there is a fresh produce market in front of the hotel and people walk in off the street to have coffee. What?!?!?!?! An upscale hotel like this does not offer coffee to its clients. Why can't they put the coffee on the fourth floor where the breakfast restaurant is located? This was disappointing. Thank God for the DUNKIN DONUtS next to the hotel. A positive and a negative was the free internet wireless access only in the lobby. To have internet access in the room, there was a DSL line which was not free. Why, in 2007, is there no wireless access in a hotel room, in a luxury hotel? I did spend time in the lobby doing my business when I needed to be in my room. There is a very nice bar/restaurant off the lobby and a breakfast restaurant on the fourth floor. The buffet was not at all attractive in the breakfast restaurant and I would have expected much, much more for the high price of $24. The staff, however and the decor were excellent. The service, apart from the quality of the buffet, was otustanding with very friendly waiters. There is no gift shop and no refreshment machines, so be prepared to purchase what you need in Faneuil Hall, before reutrning to your room. The convenience of the mini-bar was nice, but I could not afford any of the products sold. Overall, the proximity to the T line and the location of the hotel made my trip an interesting one. The hotel room, bed and facilities in the room were very comfortable. The woman who served as the concierge was very helpful and the desk staff, for the most part, were wonderful. However, it's hard to find someone in the lobby in the middle of the night, and you have to call out behind the desk area to get someone. Do not expect an expanse of a lobby, if this is your thing. There is a quiet area near a fire place that is nice. My checkin was very quick, in spite of the hotel having only two desks to check in clients. I arrived at 6pm and that made it helpful. frankraffa@ aol.com

“Sheraton should be ashamed” This probably is without a doubt the most pitiful example of a Starwood brand that I have ever stayed in. It is dirty, dated and appallingly understaffed. This is my second stay (and last) at this hotel in as many weeks. Each week I have been awakened between 1:30 & 2:30 AM to discover that it is 76 degrees. There is only central controls for the climate control so there is nothing they can do for you. Last week when I checked out at 10 AM I asked to speak with a manager only to be told that there was no manager on site because "He had not come in yet". I asked to have him contact me and never received a call. I called back the next day and once again was told he was not in. The following day I received the same message. Tonight (at 1:30 am) I asked yet again for him to call me. The bathrooms are dirty and dated. The linens are threadbare and pitiful. The carpet in my room this week have stains that are 6 inches across. The lampshade in my room has been broken by a previous occupant and never replaced. The staff is apathetic at best and difficult and rude at their worse. The property rarely has more than one person at the front desk at any given time and they generally don't care if you have a problem. This hotel is not representative of the Sheraton or the Starwood brand and should not fly their flag. This evening I asked for the name of the management company or ownership group so that I could lodge a complaint directly with them only to be told that it is an individual owner. Three guesses, but I am fairly positive this is the mysterious GM that doesn't return calls. Early tomorrow morning, I will be at our local offices strongly suggesting that we search for a new hotel. I strongly recommend that if you are in the area you find a better hotel to stay at.

“Good, good, and good.” I really enjoyed my stay here. A new hotel: crisp decor, spotless, good service, comfortable, quiet. I am a frequent Marriott customer and this is one of the better Marriott's that I've stayed at. It's close to the airport, but not a great spot for sight seeing. Decent restaurants within walking distance. The hotel restaurant has an over-priced lobster roll that wasn't that good, but otherwise, I like my whole experience. As a Marriott person, I received free Internet and concierge level, but if I wasn't the Internet was $16.95 a day.

“***** Star Service” SO much has been said about this property already, but I am happy to report The Hotel Vitale is my new found fave in San Francisco. I'm usually a creature of habit, but decided to give Hotel Vitale a try. I always love walking along the water, visiting the Ferry Building and Farmers Market, Dining, Shopping, Exploring-and this property makes a great base to experience the best of San Francisco. The service was incredible from the moment I arrived. I felt genuinely welcomed by the Valet & Bell staff, Front Desk etc. The Concierges are !!outstanding!! and every recommendation was spot on. The Vitale attracts a nice diverse all ages mix of people (singles, families, couples) and is such a comfortable place to stay and relax. I was truly surprised at the quality of staff, quality of food, and water view/s at reasonable prices. The Vitale has a cozy Lounge and stylish Restaurant offering some truly delectable food and delightful service, and let us not forget about the simple comfortable rooms complete with every amenity.

“Decent hotel, crowded bar” Stayed for a couple days before flying back home. The hotel is decent, quite new. The suite was good size with two 37 in flat screens. There was the door separated the living area and the bathroom to the bedroom. Bed/bedding was decent. The breakfast was crowded in the morning, especially the egg line. The evening cocktail hours were packed with long line and noisy customers. Only one bartender to tend the crowd so she was quite abrupt. The manager stood watching but did not help. Will not come back to this hotel even though the breakfast and happy hour drinks are included in the rate. Rather have complimentary internet connection which this hotel charged 9.95 USD for 24 hours.

“Pleasant one night stay in NW Indianapolis” We were able to use a Roomsaver coupon for $42 at this place right off the Interstate. We got a quiet room in the rear, away from the main road, There were two beds, 2 pillows each. The lights over the beds were a good touch. No breakfast included, but there is a McDonalds right behind the motels. Free Wifi.

“Awesome Marriott Excellent Service” The Marriott Phoenix Airport is an excellent hotel with extremely comfortable beds. The staff was friendly and eager to accomodate requests. The business office has free internet, but there are charges for printing, faxing, copying. But if you need to get a boarding pass, those of you who like to get up at 12:01 to get that "A" Southwest pass, they do have a computer at the front desk to let you use and print those for free. The rooms are very clean and appeared to be new. The bedding felt like at home, my wife is very particular in this area and if she liked it, I know it is good! The hotel restaurant had excellent food and friendly service. The servings were larger than any human should eat, but the food was great! Nice outdoor pool to cool off from the AZ heat. Workout room is cramped, like any hotel, but the equipment is new and up to date. Shuttle service to and from the airport is free and prompt! Overall this is a fine hotel and very well managed.

“Big rooms, decent breakfast, noisy freeway” My queen room had lots of space, a flat screen TV, and a good size bathroom. The lamps had sockets which was very useful. Next time I'll request a room that doesn't face the freeway, as the windows don't filter out the noise well. I still got a decent night's sleep, as the bed was quite comfortable. They charge $12 for parking, and there is metered parking on the street also.

“Drury Inn Northeast 4900 Crestwind Drive” Some of the previous reviews are NOT for the Drury Inn Northeast, but for the Drury Inn on the Riverwalk. That being said, this Drury Inn provides the basics for a traveler: clean room with a hot meal in the morning. We arrived Sunday night, Jan. 30, and there was a hot meal. Monday morning, Jan. 31, there was breakfast. Again, the basics, but good coffee, scrambled eggs, cereal, yogurt, bananas, etc. The room was very clean, and the staff was friendly and courteous. I would stay here again. Don't get confused by the other Drury hotel in front of this one that sits directly on the I-35 access road.

“Very nice and comfortable business hotel” The rooms were nicely appointed and spacious. The bathroom was a little tight, but had a separate shower stall and bathtub. The bed was comfortable. About what you can expect from a decent business hotel

“Very Average Hotel...” This hotel is an average hotel in a great location.. The rooms are quite large for New York standard, but other than that I dont think it has much going for it... Very basic and average hotel... I think the 3.5 star rating of this hotel is very generous.

“Ah-ah-hhh! The Watermark” We have stayed at the beautiful Watermark Hotel in San Antonio a couple of times. The first time was when we booked 3 nights at the La Mansion across the river and had a terrible experience all the way around - messed up/lost reservations, filthy, dusty room (not appropriate for our asthmatic child who was unfortunately ill at the time). They promptly moved us to this "sister" hotel and set us up with 2 connecting rooms. It was beyond lovely. Very spacious - the bathrooms were to die for. Being that our children took the double queen room in the corner of the hallway (adjacent to our King room), their bathroom was HUGE. We could have fit 4 people in the tub, alone - no need for the pool! Very elegant/conservative/comtemporary decor which was very calming. The beds are very comfortable - a big plus for a traveler who has back issues like myself. The location is fabulous. We have yet to get a river view, but no matter, the river is a step outside the door. A wonderful way to experience the very special River Walk is to dine at their signature restaurant, Pesca. We've dined there many times since the hotel opened and are NEVER disappointed. They even whipped up something for our finickiest eater (plain buttered pasta, fresh strawberries on the side) which seems silly, I know, but many restaurants would not bother with even such a simple task. Pesca has fantasitc, friendly service, a wonderful menu and wine list (not cheap, but so worth it!). It's a favorite place for us to celebrate a special occasion when in SA, even if we are staying out in the hill country. The conierge desk has never steered us wrong with dinner reservations outside the hotel as well. And if you are with your kids, there is a Johnny Rockets right next door. A favorite of our crew. The second time we booked for a spa weekend for an anniversary trip. The spa was wonderful and relaxing and is quite beautiful. Our room, service and dinner reservations were as perfect as we expected and had experienced in the past. This is not a place - nor are there really many on the River Walk - for a swimming pool type vacation. It is HOT in Texas in the summer and the small roof top pool can become quite warm. However, we still enjoyed it, with or without our children. There is pool side service from a small cafe next to the pool which has good food and drinks (good margaritas, etc). You will get excellent service for the price of what you would expect at a 4 or 5 star hotel. Also worth mentioning is the workout facility. Very nicely done and clean (empty-no other patrons around) with all updated equipment. We enjoyed this, as well. Book the Watermark if you find yourself in or near SA even for one night. You will truly enjoy the experience. We will definitely book it again - for one night or for several!

“THE BEST HOTEL IN SAN FRANCISCO!!!!!!!!” I have stayed at this hotel several times now over the years, I ALWAYS LOVE THIS HOTEL!!! The location is great, the staff are the BEST!!! I will be back again soon!!!

“Noisy Noisy Noisy....if you stay here bring EARPLUGS!!!!!!” Ok, I am not a princess or a diva, in fact read my other reviews - just down to earth and practical. This by far was the NOISIEST hotel I have ever stayed at. Yes, it was on the Riverwalk and you could hear the partyers on their way home, but it wasn't them that kept waking me up, it was the San Antonio BUSES roaring down the street that did it. The hotel is in a great location on the Riverwalk, and it is well appointed and if you don't mind noise, you won't be disappointed. It does need some fine tuning.....like the valets/doormen who don't bother helping you with your luggage if you choose self parking (valet was $29.00 per night - self $9.00). Here I am pulling 2 suitcases, and carrying a beach bag, my purse and laptop to check in while my husband parked the car. Hello??? Doorman???? You can't see me strugging???? Our room was spacious and I found beds and pillows comfy. Once again the picky little things.....like not getting more shampoo on day 2. And the tap in the bathtub is preset to lukewarm (I want the CHOICE of a hot shower). And why didn't they put 2 sinks on the huge valet, oh, and the design of the toilet....eww, flushing problems, and poor lighting. YIKES, I'm sounding like a princess! My last gripe was in attempting to pour water in the crazy 2 cup coffee maker that doesn't pull out enough from the cupboard and it spills all over the place. And Wolfgang Puck..........your name is all over the coffee and the coffee fixins.......do your really want your name associated with plastic creamer???? Not that it was replenished day 2 either. Oh well. I did have a positive experience printing 6 flags tickets through concierge (Saved $20 per person buying them in advance on line and printing them at the hotel) and the hotel bar serves yummy strawberry margaritas (we had to beg to sit on the empty patio......in which all the tables were reserved for dinner patrons - who never showed up). So, bottom line we had a great time due to our friends, but given the choice would try any other hotel first before going back to the OMNI - like the Sheraton Guenter - we liked that one!

“Somewhat dated; not Hyatt's best” Travelled here on business. I frankly expected a little more than I got. Booked a "suite" at more than double the deluxe room rate, with a sitting area. What I got was 2 rooms where they had knocked the wall down, and put a dated, nearly tacky couch and cheap coffee table opposite the bed. I would NEVER invite a client or colleage to meet in the room. Looked great for the 1980's or 1990's. Hyatt could, and should, do better. They need to reinvest some money in this location...

“This was perfect for us!” We wanted to stay near, but not IN Boston, and this was great. I had read on Trip Advisor that the hotel had a shuttle, which we needed. It worked GREAT for us, both in going to Boston Common, and to Harvard Square. We used the shuttle only, and not our car. The rooms were nice, the restaurants very good, the staff terrific, the beds comfortable, the room quiet, and we had a nice view of the Charles River. We would definitely stay there again. Boston was thrilling and we're glad to have taken the Trolley tour; great meals at Legal Seafood in Boston, and Sandrine's at Harvard Square.

“Good value and Close to Airport” It is a good value and has a gated garage which is nice in the city. They have food/bar on site and it was open until 11:30. The room was clean, but you tell it has been a while since they've been updated.

“A top place” This is a special place, it was advertised in the Centurion magazine and had a few perks to attract new clientele. I was treated in the most polite and professional manner throughout the 5 days I spent here, the Front Desk Manager really went the extra mile to give me and the two friends I travelled with a wonderful experience. He locked off two of the end rooms so we had 2 suites to ourselves with interconnecting doors. You can complain about price but this is New York, there isn't really a massive difference for the area. One thing that always appeals to me is when guests dress up a little even for breakfast, that was the case over here - very classy. The breakfast buffet has all the things you would expect and there is a Ramsay restaurant I believe. The location is pretty dead on perfect, a few blocks up from Times Square, you don't get to see all the foot-traffic passing the hotel which is nice. You have the proximity to Central Park and the shopping on 5th Avenue, Hells Kitchen is just round the corner. When I went, there was a sudden snowstorm on the 1st of March - I will never forget the experience of NY with a carpet of fresh white snow - I wished the planes were grounded so I could stay another day....shame but a beautiful memory. Take a punt and go for this hotel - you will not be disappointed. Enjoy!

“Convenient hotel for business travelers” I stayed here on a short business trip, found it convenient to the metro. good amenities for business travelers. It did not have the best soundproofing from the street noise but otherwise a very comfortable stay.

“Good for a night's stay” If you are looking for a clean, comfortable place to stay in Indy for one or two nights, the Ramada Inn-Airport is a good option. Although some of the public areas, especially the elevator, could use a good cleaning/sprucing up, the room itself was fine. Despite the proximity to I-465, everything was quiet. Breakfast was good too--waffles are available. Nothing fancy here, mind you, but the price was right (a special rate), the hotel was very convenient to the airport.

“Good to stay” Chose this hotel because my friend was a HHonor Gold member, and I am too. The room price was fairly good and the location was not far away too. Generally speaking, it was a good hotel with beautiful scenery and convenient location. They didn't provide the airport shuttle service unitl Mar.12th according to hotel tele-operator. Upon arrival, my friend was upgraded to a higher level with balcony as a benefit of gold member. He also told me the front desk representative who was learning Chinese, was very helpful and humorous. The room was good but no refrigerator in which caused a trouble that we had no cool place to put our take-out. The internet was 11.95/per day which was expensive and we wanted to use our Gold member account to login but failed. We had to choose bill to my room option but finally the hotel waived this. We visited 2 of the lounges in this hotel, the window and the fountain. both of them were pretty good. The window lounge is a good place to relax. The hotel provided self parking which charges 16 per day. One might find one outside the hotel at less cost.

“Adequate but No More--Clean, Good Service, but Crazy Coffeemaker” I stayed here a total of 6 nights, checking out just this morning. Overall it's a decent business hotel, with a few quirks. Here first is the get-to-the-point rundown, followed by something for you more wordy types (like me). GOOD: Very good housekeeping--they even left extra shampoo and extra regular coffee; good attitude on the part of the front desk; 3 blocks from the convention center; free bottled water in the room (!); plenty of outlets; no street noise (because my room [904] faced an alley, which I requested). The bed was comfy--neither firm nor soft. Nice pillows. Good TV channels, though I don't think there was any HBO. Room was average in size. BAD OR AT LEAST ANNOYING: Weak (but adequate--barely) shower pressure; constant slamming of doors by guests (and (possibly staff); air conditioning occasionally not cold enough; weird, temparamental single-cup coffee maker; generic commercial-grade coffee, rather than the Seattle's Best promised by the takeaway cups and the entire TV channel devoted to said brand 24 hours; very small fitness room; small pool; awakward car access to curbside due to one-way street on one side; no active blower vent in the bathroom; elevators get busy sometimes; air in room so dry that my nose dried up overnight; USA Today rather than the Washington Post--what's up with that? Bellman did not give me receipts for my bags and did not hang up my two hanging bags but instead draped them over something. FOR YOU LITERARY FOLKS: Shall I compare thee to a Hampton Inn? Thou are less lovely and equally temperate. Weak rains doth barely cleanse the guests each day, and your java pot hath all too small a (hot) plate. As business hotels go, this one is adequate. I think "Four Points" must mean "four points out of a possible 10." The most irritating thing was the door-slamming, which sometimes went on as late as 11:30. It baffles me that anyone would be this inconsiderate. I would urge the management to install some type of felt weatherstripping-type stuff along the door frame to muffle the sound a bit--maybe even ask guests at check-in to be sure not to let the heavy doors slam. And the coffee maker--it's almost worth your staying here for one night just to see the World's Most Annoying Coffee Maker. Mine would not drip straight down and so made a total mess. And the capacity--one cup! Why on earth can't hotels just give you the standard Bunn-O-Matic with the 12-cup carafe? Surely any number of kitchen-device companies would jump at the chance to supply a reliable, familiar, and economical hotel coffee maker to these chains. Or how about a French Press? Durable, easily cleaned, easily figured out, with a name like a wrestling move. What's not to love? To top it off, the little cups say "Seattle's Best," and there is a TV channel touting the deliciousness of said coffee and the ocial responsibility of the company--which makes you feel a bit cheated when you see this package of some stuff from Illinois. They should call it Ill-Annoy Coffee. At the same time, this hotel (unlike the comparable Hamilton Crowne Plaza two blocks away) had plenty of outlets and a pool. The pool is on the roof, in a kind of penthouse. That sounds fancier than it really is. It's a small pool. But refreshing. The pause that refreshes! Sometimes there was water in the elevator from people who had just been swimming. There was also a small fridge. The fitness room is tiny and has maybe 5 treadmills and a universal gym crammed into the back end. If you're a runner and traveling in DC, you'd be better off just jogging down to the National Mall and running there in the early evening. The 9th floor is supposedly for "Starwood Preferred" members, but I got a room there just by asking for something quiet. I noticed that two rooms on this floor (919 and 920 I think) were themselves behind another door--and given the constant slamming, it might well be worth any extra cost to get that extra layer of sound-deadening. But then, they might face the street, and with early-morning deliver/trash/recycling trucks, you don't want that. TAXI TIP: The taxis in DC are now (glory be!) on the same meter system used in the rest of the world. They kind of stick it to you on the drop fee ($3.00) and for any extra passengers ($1.50 each!), and there's a $1 gas surcharge in the summer. But it beats that horrid zone system of yore. EATING TIPS: This hotel is close enough for you to walk to Chinatown--but it's kind of a forlorn walk, with a few homeless here and there. Not truly scary, and if you're in a group, don't hesitate. If you go to Chinatown (at H and 9th and thereabouts), go to Eat First. Delicious and cheap! Also consider Ten Penh, on Pennsylvania and 10th. Fantastic (though pricey) fusion Asian. Just across from the FBI. And of course, DuPont Circle is a quick Metro ride, as are the restaurants of upper NW DC and Clarendon (in Arlington). There's a restaurant in the hotel, but everybody knows that hotel restaurants are to be avoided. I have no firsthand experience with this one, so I could be wrong. But why risk it? There's also an ESPN Zone on 12th Street, very nearby.

“Ist und bleibt unser Stammhotel in Hollywood!” Nach 2006 waren wir heuer zum 2. Mal im Beverly Garland HI. Und auch diesmal haben wir uns hier wieder sehr wohl gefühlt. In LA braucht man sowieso ein Auto, daher ist es auch kein Drama, dass man das Hotel am besten mit dem Auto erreicht (Anbindung mit öff. Verkehrsmittel ist eher schlecht). Das Personal ist durchwegs sehr freundlich. Die Zimmer wurden seit 2006 offenbar renoviert, wir hatten ein schönes Zimmer mit Kingsize-Bett, Balkon Richtung Pool, einfach schön! Das Hotel bietet neben dem Pool auch noch einen Fitnessraum, der auch seit 2006 erweitert und verbessert wurde. Parken kostet pro Nacht $ 15,--, ist man Mitglied bei Priority Club Rewards wird für das Parken $ 12,-- verrechnet. Das Hotel bietet merhmals täglich einen gratis Shuttle zu den Universal Studios an. Im dazugehörigen Restaurant "Tulas" kann man am Vormittag gut frühstücken (Buffett kostet $ 15/Person) - leider war das Servierpersonal etwas überlastet, sodass sich am ersten Tag schon eine Schlange bei der Tischvergabe ergeben hat, obwohl mehrere Tische bereits frei (nur nicht abgeräumt) waren. Alles in allem war es wieder ein mehr als angenehmer Aufenthalt und wir kommen sicher wieder!

“Very close hotel to UT Stadium” We stayed here the night of the Thanksgiving game of Texas vs TCU. It is about a mile walk to the stadium and is very convenient because they have free parking. Most of the parking lots are about the same distance from the stadium. This is a very nice hotel despite the complaints that it is locate next to a cemetery. Both my wife and I grew up within walking distance from each of our childhood homes from cemeteries and played in them so this was not a concern of ours. There is a Denny's located next door and the hotel also has a restaurant on site, plus a small bar.

“Great stay in spite of Irene visting.” Stayed at the Sheraton Tribeca the last weekend of August, 2011 for a wedding. Irene, the hurricane, was not invited but she came anyway. We drove our car to the hotel and were a little surprised that there wasn't a better entrance for guests arriving. You're lucky to get a spot on Canal Street to unload your car.
