Valet parking was $60/day. Upon arrival, I thought we'd be bombarded by bellmen who'd help us get unloaded, etc. but not so much. My husband ended up taking our car to a local garage that was INDOORS and ABOVE GROUND to make sure we'd be okay if the hurricane hit. It ended up taking him about 20 minutes to go around the block and I attribute this to the mad rush of commuters getting out of the city before the storm him. Still, kind of a pain to deal with. Otherwise, check in was smooth. We were in the club level as our reservation was booked with my Starwood points. The bellman who took us our to our room, was extremely knowledgable, full of information, and eager to give us a great experience. We were taken to our room on the 17th floor. Our room was beautiful and roomy for NYC standards. One wall was all windows looking right towards the the Empire State building. Fantastic views and the rooms are brand new and well designed. Because of the impending hurricane, many of the guests were basically stuck at the hotel since all of Tribeca shut down. So the bars was full, the computers were being used and there was a lot of activity in the lobby and restaurant. I have to give the staff a ton of credit. No one seemed annoyed by the questions, the stress or the influx of guests. They kept a bulletin board with storm updates in the lobby and a flyer on each floor. Overall, the hotel was fantastic at providing news on the storm, what roads were open, what their plan was, and what we could expect if we got hit hard. Fortunately, we only lost cable for a an hour or two. Power never went out. And I have to mention how comfortable the beds were. We slept so well during the height of the storm and the linens kept us warm and cozy. Upon checkout, right after the storm, we decided to hit the breakfast buffet to get some food in us before our drive home. If we could actually drive anywhere. The buffet left a lot to be desired. The eggs were old and cold, there was no more toast left and none of the staff seemed concerned that they were busier than usual and guests were in line waiting to eat. However, I have to say that the Sheraton staff managed the storm and its inconveniences really well. I loved that there was a Starbucks in the lobby to get some morning coffee. And the lobby was bustling with travelers who made it a communal meeting space. The staff accomodated. The rooms are extremely comfortable, the views are amazing and the location is central to everything in lower Manhattan. Would definitely stay again.

“Not bad but Valet people are not friendly” I booked our stay in this hotel via Priceline bidding and paid 292 dollar for 2 nights which is not bad. We arrived in the afternoon and they gave us a room on the 6th floor. First thing we noticed was that the airconditioning made a lot of noise so after we parked our car in the Common Garage (cheaper and nearby) we called the front-desk and they send someone who switched the airco off with a hidden button. Our stay was OK but the VALET people were not friendly at all. According to the hotel it's allowed to park for 15 minutes during check-in and check-out. They seemed not so happy when you ask for this and they directly tell you that if you're not back within 15 minutes they start charging you. I explained that I will be as fast as possible but that I depend on the front-desk-lines... No excuse... "we will charge you if you're not back in 15 minutes" Location is perfect and there are some nice restaurants nearby.

“Great location for seeing San Fran from the top of the hill!” I often stay at the Fairmont chain since the locations are excellent for work/sightseeing and I used to get nice upgrades when I was traveling for work on someone's tab (sniff, sniff... miss those days!). I stayed at the Fairmont during my recent San Fran trip for 5 nights - I love the Nob Hill area and it's the most reasonably priced of the hotels at the top of the hill. Super convenient since 2 major cable car lines go right in front of it. Lovely historic decor and lobby - they serve lemon, lime and cucumber water in the lobby which are yummy! Rooms are a bit dated as most Fairmonts are (smaller bathrooms in standard rooms), but I love the history of the chain. On the plus side, water efficiency isn't that established with the showers so you can an amazing spray!! If you want modern, this is not the place for you. Customer service is good and concierge staff are helpful. I didn't eat at any of the restos but hubby went to Tonga one night for an overpriced $26ish burger that was quite good. Solid 4*.

“Can't wait to go back!” I went to Chicago for an Car club event and decided to stay at this hotel instead of the host hotel becasue of the great price I found on their website. Since the moment I was greeted at the door I experienced great service, all the staff was friendly, helpful and I have to say good looking ;) I was promptly checked in. The room was somewhat small and I felt almost claustrophobic in the bathroom, but it was clean and very nicely decorated, the Bliss products provided were also of good quality. They have iPod docks so I listened to my own music while getting ready to go out. The Acura experience is a great plus, they take you anywhere in the downtown area. Valet parking is 40.00 a day The bar area is very trendly and is really easy to charge drinks to your room!

“holy cow...what a fabulous hotel” stayed with 2 of my kids and their families--they put us all on one floor which was wonderful....my son had an amazing city view and my dtr & I had a view of the hancock....the room was fab....little touches like a nightlight that popped on in the closet when you walked by & gorgeous roller shade that really blocked the sun....a "pillow menu" that included an i pod pillow....great staff that made us feel right at home....a beautiful bar with a great view... bonus is Ginos east is right next door...michigan ave is 1 blk away.... not one complaint!!

“Excellent cheap option” Luckily I ended up at this property at 1 am after leaving another hotel that had bed bugs (ew!) Jose, the night manager, set me up in a fabulous and clean room for very cheap, and even helped me treat my clothing from the previous hotel experience so I had something to wear the next day. Their breakfast is fabulous and the rooms are extremely quiet for being so close to the airport. I was very grateful to the whole staff that salvaged my stay in houston. Two very big thumbs up!!

“Good stay at the Lexington” I was in Manhattan for two nights for business, and was booked in to the Lexington. I arrived really late in to Newark (courtesy of all kinds of airplane mechanical problems) and ended up taking a taxi instead of the airport bus. The taxi driver had a good time finding the entrance (which is actually on 48th instead of Lexington), but all was well. I received a friendly greeting from reception and checked in. My room was on the 12th floor overlooking 48th street. Street noise was low, but noticeable (as it would be more or less anywhere in Manhattan). My room was small but comfortable, with a new bed and a bathroom where everything worked. It was clean, tidy, reasonably recently decorated - and as I wouldn't be spending much time in the room, perfectly fine for two nights. The hotel is convenient for almost everything - subway, buses, museums, shops, Grand Central. You can walk to Grand Central in about 5 minutes, if you want, and to Central Park in about 30 minutes if you get a move on. The hotel was very busy - it's in a great location, and its prices are reasonable for Manhattan - so there are always loads of people in the lobby (moreover, wifi is free in the lobby, and $16 in the rooms). There's a bar and several restaurants, none of which I tried, but all seemed to be thriving. There's also a Starbucks off the lobby, and about 5 billion other coffee shops within walking distance. Overall, I had a good stay - I slept reasonably well for Manhattan, the staff were friendly, and I found the location extremely convenient. The rooms are small (but normal for Manhattan). I'd probably stay again.

“All the good details.” I stayed four nights at the Pearl hotel and it was a great stay! The location is fantastic both for walking and for using the subway. The hotel is fairly new so every thing is in perfect shape. But what makes hotel so good are the little details: the staff is very helpfull, the breakfast is a great addition, the free WiFi is very good, there are umbrellas in every room, two bathrobes, great bed and pillows... I will definitely recommend staying at the Pearl.

“Good Value at great location but cramped” Got a good price for a great location, just a block off Michigan Avenue on Ohio. This is an older hotel so the elevators are small and the rooms seem smaller yet. If you are somebody who likes to spread out your "stuff" in the bathroom, forget about it. No counter space to speak of. This didn't bother me for a one-night stay but if you care... My companions complained that the wifi was slow. Bottom line: if you are looking for an OK place to crash while sight-seeing in Chicago, this is a great place. If you are looking for a romantic weekend or "spa experience," keep searching! Oh yeah, parking was $36 a night, I believe. I came in by train/taxi.

“Great location - Great hotel” I will quickly duplicate everything that has been said in other reviews. The hotel is centrally located, staff is helpful and the rooms are clean and quiet. One negative that was mentioned in reviews is the slow internet. They offer free wireless and wired internet along with a higher speed paid service. I just plugged in and used the free wired connection and it was fine. I uploaded google maps and lots of other things on my old lap top that I travel with. I did not see in reviews of speed complaints whether the reviewer used free wireless or the free wired connection, maybe wireless is slower. I never tried to see. I also have to mention breakfast at the Dutch Eating Place at Reading Terminal Market. It is really good and inexpensive. They just have counter service, no tables. I even saw couples sharing an order of pancakes because the portions are so large. The hotel faces Juniper, but there is a back entrance at 13th and Filbert. If you go out the back the market as well as Market East train station are only one block away. The $45 nightly valet parking makes this hotel perhaps not the best option if you have a car. If you are relying on public transport you could not ask for a better location. I used city buses instead of the Phlash because the service is so quick in this central area wher several bus lines run up and down Market. I had an early flight home, so I appreciated the free printing of my boarding pass at the business center in the lobby, next to the elevators. I have attached a picture looking east at the front of the hotel. City Hall would be to the right and the building in the foreground on the left is the Masonic Temple. To the side of the hotel is Filbert Street and the Reading Terminal Market and Market East train station at the far end of the block.

“Big Room in NYC” This is a convenient location, walkable (but not close) to Times Square and Central Park and not so loud and busy at night. We stayed at a room with 2 queen beds. The room is very big and comfortable with a sofabed and queen bed available for the 2 kids. We were on the 29th floor and traffic noise was minimal. Sound insulation between rooms however, could be better. We could hear the neighbours talking and showering. Wireless internet worked well. Staff was helpful and fairly prompt. There is a variety of restaurants close by to suit kids and adults. Lots of places for quick bites in the morning which is probably better value than having breakfast at the hotel. A Starbucks and Subway are right around the corner and a drug store right next door. A good choice and value for families travelling in NYC.

“Not a great experience” As Hampton's go this was a little disappointing. First off I had to make a special effort to close the door - it did not close firmly and lock if you just let it go. Bathroom lighting was a little dingy and towels were threadbare. Breakfast is chaotic - between 7:30 and 9 count on a big crowd and a challenge finding a seat. Also, they are running a charitable promotion and tagged a $1 dollar donation onto my bill. They happily removed it when I was checking out, but if you're a traveler that takes the bill from under the door and goes, be sure to double-check. Positives- parking is immediately next door if you drive. Central Park is an easy walk a few blocks north. Bed comfort was decent, internet is easy to access and the a/c worked very well.

“good location but that's it.” The location of this hotel is excellent but that's about it. I stayed on the first floor with windows facing I don't know what. The room was pretty small and the service was not so good. The place looks good but does not function well. It definitely is not worth the money as you can find other hotels around D.C. I am a Marriott elite member and I was disappointed.

“Ok hotel, connected to a mall which was great!” Room was small. The bathroom sink counter was tiny with very little space to put my toiletries. Food was excellent...try the "Mighty Mo" sliders with fries and the chicken quesadilla. The breakfast buffett Saturday was delicious with lots of choices. I found the hallways freezing, but it was 85 outside so this may be normal for Texas hotels. Walk out the lobby door and turn left and you will be a at Macy's. The mall connected to this hotel was not fabulous, but was acceptable. The Riverwalk is very close so no taxi is needed. No food vending machines, but soda and ice were near my room door. Free newspapers (USA Today, Wall Street Journal) were available at concierge, but you must pay for the local newsaper ($1 weekday/$2 Sunday). A shoe shine area is in the lobby. Local police were in the lobby often so I felt safe. Like most downtowns, homeless men were on the street and I had one on Commerce ask me for change and my phone number, while another a few yards away begged for coins. Across the street from the Marriott Rivercenter is the smaller Marriott Riverwalk...and across the street from there is the convention center, which is connected to the new large Hyatt. A taxi ride to the airport is about $25. When asked, my cab driver told me he accepted debit cards. At the hotel, he told me my MasterCard debit card could not be accepted, only MasterCard Visa debit cards were accepted...because of this, I paid with cash and he lost his entire tip...and I let him know it! Check-in and check out were quick. Plasma tv in room had lots of channels. Maid service was early and quick.

“A nice suprise.” As a Starwood Platinum member I have generally avoided the Sheraton chain in the past because of some bad experiences, but decided to give the Sheraton Suites in San Diego a chance. I was very impressed. The rooms are modern and clean and I can't say enough about the comfort of the beds and pillows. Wow, what a great night sleep. This is an older building, but they do a great job maintaining it and keeping it clean and fresh. The hotel has a nice pool and fitness center, although it would have been better to see a set of free weights in the fitness center instead of a clunky old weight machine. I have stayed at the W hotel on a couple occasions, but I may actually prefer the Sheraton Suites over the W. I read that parking is a bit of a haste here so I just opted to park in one of the nearby lots for $5 per night and never had a problem. The front desk met all of my requests with a smile. Sorry W Hotel, I think I will be coming back to the Sheraton Suites next time I'm in town.

“They REALLY look out for guests” This hotel is close to the "RED" Subway line in Boston and it is very comfortable. It stands out because the rest of the area is... well... not the nicest part of Boston. As usual with Courtyard, the room was just right and very comfortable and clean. I happened to be there the weekend of ComicCon and there were come interesting characters staying there. The staff informed me that the ComicCon guests were asked to sign statements that they would be quiet and not do anything to disturb other guests. I was also told when I checked in that if I heard ANY noise to report it to the front desk immediately. I didn't hear a sound and slept like a baby. As I checked in pretty late and didn't want to go back out, they gave me the menus of several local places that delivered to the hotel. I enjoyed on of the best Calzones I have ever had... I wish I could remember the name of the place. Great hotel.
“In the heart of Time Square” Very convenient, great service, great views. The rooms large fir NY and acutely represented accurately from their website. Overall, great place with a hip scean.

“An economical option close to SMU” I'm pretty picky about my accommodations, but I think some of the negative reviews here are unwarranted. While we had a minor hiccup upon check-in, all in all we had a decent stay, and plan to return. After reading some of these negative reviews, I had some concerns about staying here. The hotel was completely full, due to weddings and a big football game, but the staff seemed prepared to handle it. At check-in I observed a Diamond member struggling to get a non-smoking room, followed by our getting assigned to a room that was already occupied, which caused some initial concern, but the rest of our stay was just fine. We were assigned to a room on the 18th floor, which we were told was an "upgraded" floor. I'm not sure if that meant recently renovated or what made it upgraded. We reserved a standard King bedded room. The room had a good-sized refrigerator with a freezer compartment that actually froze ice! The room a/c, however, seemed to have difficulty keeping up with the Texas heat. We were comfortable with the thermostat set at 65, but we normally keep it at 75 (in Texas!) Housekeeping needs to better focus on the details, with dust evident on the bathroom fixtures, but the room was otherwise clean. The bed was comfortable, and we slept very well. No outside noise was heard from the 18th floor, which was very nice. Even though we were close to the elevator, we were not disturbed by dinging or hallway traffic, even after the wedding reception ended. For the price (about $89 some weekends) it is a great value for a full-service hotel in the SMU area. If you are HHonors Gold or Diamond, it is an even better value with the breakfast buffet ($15 pp) comped. We were very impressed with the quality and selection of the buffet, with fresh fruit, smoked salmon, made to order omelets and a variety of other options. I've already made more reservations for future SMU visits!
“If you need to stay in this area,” This is it! Almost perfect accommodations! River view rooms have telescopes!

“Great friendly Marriott in big city” Stayed several days at this hotel. Large rooms for NYC. Standard and good Marriott amenities. A bit south of all of the activities in NYC but so close to good subways and cabs zip up the west hwy to get you anywhere fast. Staff was ten plus! Great rate for the quality and being in NYC! Just can't figure out the crazy expensive price for breakfast at the hotel restaurant/bar..... Crazy even for NYC! And come on Marriott get with it and stop charging for wifi! Otherwise I loved it!

“Quaint but small rooms” Of all the hotels we stayed in a cross USA trip this was the smallest room with the highest bed. They even provided a step to stand on to get into the bed. That said it was clean, in a good location - short walk to Capitol - and had a good Irish Bar/eatery attached..

“No complaints, good value chain hotel” We spent 3 nights in this hotel & generally were happy with our choice & it seemed good value for the price in terms of LA. The room was spacious & clean with large flat screen HD TV with very good picture quality. Room had microwave, fridge, tea/coffee maker & there was an ice machine on nearby landing. There was no safe in the room, but receptionist agreed to hold valuable items for us. Free parking. Free Wifi (unsecured network) but intermittent and problematic connection with apple devices, but seemed fine with pc laptop. No laundry facilities on site but launderette across the street. Staff were friendly & breakfast was better than average, with good selection of different options (hot eggs & bacon as well as waffles, toast, spreads, fresh fruit, yoghurt, cereals, juices, tea/coffee). Dining space was limited to 3 or 4 tables, so you may have to wait. Location seemed a bit out of the way and rather run down, but appeared safe enough. Bus stop to downtown was across the street but could be a long (20-30 mins) wait for a bus. It took approx. 20mins to travel downtown.(NB returning from sightseeing we often experienced very long waits for a bus & on one occasion the bus was so crowded that passengers were almost hanging out of the doors. This was about 7.30pm). The Hotel ordered a taxi to take us to Universal Studios- the taxi was quite late and seemed overpriced at $35. If I could I would give this hotel 3.5 rather than 4 out of 5 to reflect lack of laundry facilities, no safe in the room, quality of WiFi connectivity & location.

“Excellent stay” Stayed at the Four Points Philadelphia Airport this weekend. No problem finding a parking space. Many handicapped spaces offered. Parking only $5. Parking attendant helpful with local directions. Front desk staff friendly. Free internet and printer use in the lobby for those not travelling with a laptop. Clean, decent hotel. My room was large and well-kept. Free bottled water in the room. Very comfortable bed. Alarm clock and wake-up call both in working order. Airport shuttle was quick. Shuttle bus could hold at least 16 passengers.

“Small rooms but good overall service” My boyfriend and I just returned from a 5 night stay at the Baltimore Marriott Inner Harbour. We were not all that pleased with the size of our room, bathroom or closet space. We also didn't have that great of a view. However, the staff including the concierge and doormen were great and very helpful. The convenience to inner harbor and its attractions was a short 10-15 minute walk away. Also, the concierge recommended a great restaurant Kali's Court (a 10 minute taxi ride) which was first class! If we do return to Baltimore on vacation, we may try the Renaissance or the Marriott Downtown. Hopefully the rooms will be somewhat more spacious. Overall a good experience.

“Convenient to convention center, easy access to airport & highway” Recently stayed here for a convention at the Convention center. So convenient to just walk a few minutes across the bridge to convention. The airport is very close, yet we heard no noise from our room. Hotel parking very easy and competitive pricing. This was really an excellent location for the Boston business traveler. We would definitely stay there again. Our service was excellent, so I can't relate to some other comments posted here.

“Love the renovation” The renovation that's going on with the hotel is fantastic. Rooms are now fresh and very comfortable. With regards to available space in the room it's very spacious (compared to other SF hotels). There is now a blackout blind over the main windows, in place of heavy blinds, and you will easily sleep late with how dark it makes everything. Nicely done Hyatt

“WONDERFUL stay!! Gong back ASAP” We had booked another hotel weeks prior to our visit to Austin. We booked a Sat & Sun over Labor Day weekend. Last minute we decided to go on Friday. So I tried to book the same hotel we had reservations at, but the last minute price had gone up considerably. So the hubs suggested we try Priceline. So, I did the name your own price option, chose 4 star in the downtown Austin area & offered $100. Kowing the city, I knew we'd get a good hotel. We got the Hyatt Regency. We called after the reservation was made to verify that we had a King room (always need to do that). So, we arrived & the property is fantastic. Gorgeous landscaping, it is located on the south bank of Lady Bird/Town Lake, (not really what I call downtown Austin, but close enough).Check in was a breeze, I asked if we could be upgraded to a King Riverview on a high floor. They said yes, but there would be a $30 upcharge. We paid it. They gave us room 1101 which was on the 11th floor, corner room. We walked into a huge room with large windows all along the wall looking out to the river & downtown, & there was another smaller window on the side, looking toward the west (up river). We were so excited with the room & our view that we decided to for-go our previous plans of making it a night on the town, to just run down S. Congress, eat a bite & run back to catch the Bats evening flight (we had a perfect view!) The restaurant was packed, so we missed the bats, but came back to our room & went to the pool (which was awesome). We sat by the pool with an adult beverage & enjoyed the peace & quiet. When the pool closed, we went back to our room, turned out the lights, pulled up two chairs & sat in the windows, enjoying the FANTASTIC view. How WONDERFUL that was for us. The bed was comfortable & the bathroom big enough. We didn't eat at the restaurant, but SHOULD have. The bar is nice & they have a covered patio to eat, drink or just chill on. The river activities are right there too. We hated that we had to leave, (we could have stayed at the same rate we had booked thru Priceline if we had wanted, but had to go to the "other" hotel since our reservations could not be cancelled). Would we stay here again? YES! YES! YES! It is now gonna be our "go to" hotel when we visit Austin (3-4 times a year) even if we can't get the $100 Priceline deal........it's a fantastic hotel.

“Internet service very spotty” I have stayed here several times and really like this hotel. It's downtown, close to the ballpark and next to Vic and Anthony's. The service is excellent and the rooms are stellar. This time I was disappointed in the internet service. I had a lot of work to do and the wireless was very, very slow. I called the front desk and a very nice man came up and re-started the router...but the service never got better. I was in room 815, maybe others were better. Still a very nice hotel, just wish they could get this fixed.

“Basic hotel” The hotel is in a great location and for me, that's about all it had going for it. It's a standard business hotel connected to the convention center, but it does have an inside connection to the Pru shopping mall and is a short walk or T ride from Fenway. I stayed here with a certificate and I'm very glad that I didn't pay. Honestly, the rooms are so small and the property so depressing, I can't imagine making the decision to stay here with the Marriott and the Westin right across the street. As for the property, it's very blah. Beige, brown, worn out rugs and furnishings. It looks like it's been trampled by thousands and thousands of convention attendees. It needs to be updated and refreshed. The room was so tiny that only one bedside stand fits next to the King bed. The other part of the bed is just about up against the wall. We had a large entry way that was a waste of space. The bathroom was very, very small and almost impossible to maneuver in. The Front Desk was abrasive and distracted when we checked in. It was midnight and both agents seemed to be closing out their drawers or working on reports. They barely pointed us to the elevators. As a Starwood Preferred guest, I expect a lot from Sheraton properties and this one misses the mark. If attending a Sox game, I might check the rates here...but with hundreds of other options that are much better, I'd try a few dozen other places before even looking here.

“Not so special.” I didn't think it was that great. Guys at front desk were a little snotty. The room they gave us was in a really weird part of the building-- a floor below the lobby (aka technically the basement) with a view that looked out at the rooftop of the building next door, and all the debris on that rooftop. Maybe if you get to go "upstairs" it's a fabulous experience, but come on-- our money is all the same color green. There were some pretty accents and decorating details to the room, but for the money, and for the feeling that the front desk staff communicated of "you're lucky to be at this hotel, that's the only room we have left, sorry sucker" I would never recommend this place to anyone.

“Good Hotel Close to Capitol” This is a very nice hotel near the Capitol Building and about one block from a Metro station. It seems rather expensive, but then, it's D.C. Not sure it was worth $219 a night, but again, the location was excellent. The rooms are decorated nicely. Unfortunately, the free wifi was slow and cut out frequently. The staff was top-notch and bent over backwards to accommodate you. You do have to pay for breakfast, but it's excellent and includes made-to-order omelets. This hotel has a bar and small restaurant, too, which is unusual for a Courtyard. It was decent food and nice for the weary traveler who didn't want to go out on their first night in D.C. I will likely stay here again when I go back to D.C. in another month.

“Of 4 stays, by far the worst--could consistency be an issue here, even for Diamonds?” Very disappointed with my stay this week. Just stayed one night, and the reasons I like this spot are: Diamond upgrades to 1 BR with Studio reservations; fan on stove top (helps me sleep, I know there are others out there like me), Bud Light, and icemaker. Also the bed and location. Well, bed and location were good. My Diamond upgrade was to a Handicapped studio (without being warned by FD clerk); fan did not work at all (so I got to listen to the kids screaming in their room), and a fridge totally frosted over. Oh...and I went down for a much needed drink, and they were out of Bud Light 15 minutes into the social hour. I can't stand dark beer, but was told the Bud Light would come "when we run out to the store". Shower, handicapped-accessible, was horrible. Positives? Bed was fine. Man at front desk who I requested a bucket of ice from accommodated me, but after I told him this was my least favorite stay at this hotel, did not seem to ask a lot of questions. Front desk clerk was cheery, and the room was quite clean. Any different than what you can get in the Galleria for under $200/night? Rare, but possible here. I was sorely disappointed, but might give this spot one more chance before heading back to Sheraton Suites with their horrid traffic.

“Very nice but try to avoid rooms on first floor” This is a beautiful historic building, very convenient to many attractions in Washington including the convention center. The extremely wide hallways are elegant. My only caution is that first floor rooms in at least one part of the hotel are below grade level, so they have no view and if you look out your window you're staring at the legs of pedestrians. They can also stare in at you if the curtains are open

“Excellent service and close to airport” Hard to recall a more truly hospitable front desk clerk at any other hotel at which I’ve ever stayed. She was truly friendly, and made me feel as if I were staying with an old friend. When I arrived at the Jacksonville airport, I called the hotel to see about a shuttle pick-up. It turned out the shuttle happened to be at the airport at that moment. I heard the clerk call the shuttle driver and arrange for him to wait a minute so I could climb aboard before he left. The room—clean, spacious, well-equipped—certainly met my expectations for a Courtyard by Marriott. They gave me a free coffee as a Marriott Silver Elite member. A number of other hotels are available in the airport area. I wonder if any can match the level of service I experienced.

“Does not always live up to its potential” Great location. Rooms are very clean but average. As a Marriott Rewards Gold member, my upgrade options are nothing special. The Lounge is first rate, however, and I usually start and end my day there with a nice breakfast and a decent bite for dinner. Large fitness facility, and Marriott is generally good about not charging guests to use the fitness center. Lots of cardio, lap pool and free weights.

“Pretty, historic hotel that misses on a few key amenities” Stayed for 2 nights on a business trip with meetings at the LA Convention Center. THe hotel is in a good, central location for Downtown LA destinations. The valet and bell staff are very friendly and attentive as are the front desk attendants. The lobby is small with an average size bar and restaurant making up the majority of the ground floor. The restaurant serves decent, California cuisine, but is overpriced for the quality and selection of menu items. My biggest beef with the restaurant was breakfast. I received the Diamond complimentary breakfast voucher and decided to use it the first day. I have had varying experiences with complimentary HHonors breakfasts, but the norm is usually a continental buffet bar with pastries, breads, cereal, fruit, etc. At the Checkers, I was offered the choice of a basket of bread or toast. I received (for by $12-14 value) exactly 3 miniature pastries that were defrosted within the previous hour. I recommend here taking the extra HHonors points and going to Starbucks across the street. The rooms were nicely appointed, but the large flat-panel lacked high definition feeds. The picture was too grainy on that nice, expensive television to justify it being in the room. The room amenities are typical for a Hilton, bed is comfortable, and climate control worked well. I just wish they would figure out how to give away free wi-fi to all staying with them. The fitness center/ pool/ spa is a nice retreat on the balcony. It was the highlight of the hotel. A great little heated pool oasis in the middle of the city. Great views of the city. I probably would opt for the Marriott or Ritz by the Convention Center next time.

“LaQuinta, In the shadow of the Willis Tower” Stayed at LaQuinta Downtown while visiting family. There was a convention in town that weekend and the rates for hotels in The Loop were averaging over 350/night. I booked for 239/night and was not expecting much. I was pleasantly surprised. I had a very spacious , king room with a microwave and mini refrigerator as well as coffee maker in room . Large desk area with free wifi, nice flat screen TV. Nice bathroom with large shower. Basic decoration but clean. Breakfast included was heavy on carbs but adequate with waffles, cereal, toast , muffins, coffee, juice ,milk and yogurt. Argo Tea was just a door way away in the lobby and a deli was also attached to the lobby. I recommend Argo Tea. Try the spiced chai. The Willis Tower was about a block away. The hotel was a block away from the river and well located with several resturants in close proximity, including the Billy Goat Tavern. This was a comfortable hotel with helpful staff .

“Large comfortable room, nice stay” This hotel looks like an apartment building, which I think it used to be. We stayed three nights in a studio--bed, bath, and kitchenette. The bed was comfortable, and the room was clean. A lot more space than is usual in a NYC hotel. Front desk service was extremely pleasant. The location, on E34th Street near Lexington Avenue, is outstanding. There is an all-night deli/grocery on the corner and many decent restaurants nearby in all directions.

“Very good family hotel; Superb F&B” Very impressed. We also had a 2 bedroom suite and it was very spacious and tastefully appointed. Food and beverage is above average and their home-made ice cream, pizza, and Saturday afternoon chocolate buffet were all excellent, as was their Julienne restaurant. We enjoyed the baby crib with the stuffed animal and the milk and cookies they delivered our first night. Staff was mostly very friendly; once we couldn't get seated in the dining room and we were instead seated in the lounge but comped on the chocolate buffet for the inconvenience. Service is not impeccable but certainly quite good. Example: We sat for an hour without any food being served in the Julienne; they misplaced our order and nobody came to check why we weren't served. It was only after I got up and asked where our dinner was that the food began to come forth. There were less than 10 people eating in the whole restaurant so someone was obviously asleep at the switch. The piano bar is a very nice place to sit with the old bank decor all around you, and even dance a bit. We also liked the location which was convenient to Faneuil Hall; on Memorial Day Weekend their street performers festival makes it a great family place to be. Prices for spa services onsite such as massage are quite reasonable for today's market.

“Hey, this is a GREAT Hotel” I spent a weekend here at the Embassy Suites while in town for a football game. This hotel is very new, clean and extremely comfortable. It's an Embassy Suites so the rooms are larger with separate living and sleeping areas. The staff was very friendly and the hotel is well located for walking to a few of the major attractions in downtown Denver-- and just a few short blocks off of the 16th street mall. FYI, included breakfast was fantastic -- one of the best I've had at an Embassy Suites, you won't leave hungry!

“Recommended” My wife and I booked this hotel on the basis of TripAdvisor reviews. Vacation. Three nights. Spacious and comfortably furnished room. Clean, comfortable and quiet. Adequate breakfast included in rate. High speed internet. All staff courteous and helpful. Location is convenient to Beale Street, Museum of Rock & Soul and shuttle services to other attractions. This new hotel and neighboring hotels are in an area in transformation with a number of building undergoing restoration. At night, we did not feel particularly safe walking to and from hotel because of loiterers and panhandlers on corners and near trolley stops. Note that many restaurants in area are closed on Sunday and Monday nights – not very tourist- friendly. As result, you might be forced to walk to Beale Street for dinner. Beale Street a real disappointment after visiting Bourbon Street. As development continues in the area, the “edginess” should lessen. The concerns expressed relate to Memphis generally rather than this hotel specifically. We recommend this hotel; it has much to offer at a reasonable price.

“A good base for the larger family” We had a double room but our friends had a large family suite with a kitchen in it and it worked well for them and their family. Only downside was only 1 bathroom when there were 6 sharing. The door men were very helpful and staff were friendly in general. The area above reception was great for sitting reading, catching up with emails or playing games. There were lots of food options nearby and it was a good base. I have stayed at another Affinia Hotel and this would encourage me to try another again.

“Kimpton never fails” I booked the Muse based on the reviews here and the fact that it was a Kimpton property. We've always had good luck with them in the past. Once again, the reservations process was a breeze. They bent whatever rule there is about grownups in a room and let me book adjoining rooms...a king for myself and my husband and a queen/queen for my two teenage boys. The rooms were lovely. The boys' room was enormous...particularly for a NYC room but even compared to standard rooms in other cities. I was concerned about street noise from experience with past visits and had requested rooms on a higher floor. I was dismayed to be assigned to the floor 12....right next to the elevators. You know what? No noise at all! Our adjoining rooms had an additional, lockable foyer door that blocked any and all noise from the hall and whatever street noise was completely blocked by high quality insulated windows. Very nice. Lovely linens. Comfy beds and a selection of pillows. Decent toiletries. Good lighting in the bathroom.... and so on. Our boys were disappointed with the fitness room, but if they didn't get enough exercise walking with us through the city that's not the end of the world. My only complaint was a problem with the electrical relay on our a/c system...it kept clicking as it turned on and off...even more noticible in the quiet room. I mentioned it upon checkout and I'm sure it's already been repaired. We'd rebook in a heartbeat.

“Gorgeous historic hotel” The Brown Palace is one of the most beautiful historic (1890s) hotels that I've seen--and I've seen quite a few, because I particularly enjoy staying in historic hotels. The atrium lobby is spectacular. And, despite its age, the hotel is in great shape. My room was lovely, very comfortable and well-appointed. (Not everyone may appreciate the reproduction Victorian-style furniture, but it goes with the hotel.) Unlike so many upscale hotels, the room had a coffee-maker, which I appreciated. The bathroom, obviously recently re-done, was particularly nice. (The shower had two shower heads, one in the wall and a second in the ceiling, which was a new experience for me.) The only small drawback to the room was limited closet space. I was at the hotel for a meeting so didn't take advantage of some of the amenities, such as the spa or having tea in the lobby, but the meeting rooms were nice, and the service provided for the meetings was good. I'm very glad to have had the opportunity to stay at the Brown Palace, which I've admired during previous visits to Denver.

“Get the Deluxe King Suite if you can....” I stayed in a Deluxe King Suite for my birthday and it was amazing. I have added some pictures of the room, but I will start with check-in. We checked in about 3pm and the front desk person by the name of Chalang Hassan was very helpful. This is the only hotel I have been to where the front desk person tells you how much they will be holding on your card for incidentals. Just so you know, they only hold $50.00 per night. Chalang gave us all the info we needed and also mentioned there was some party going on later on that night that we might want to check out. From there B.C. the bellman had taken everything out of our car from valet and followed us up to our room. Mr. B.C. told us about all the hotel had to offer on the way to the room. Once we got to the suite he put are clothes in drawers and hung our nice clothes up that we were wearing to my wife's company party later. He even gave us a tour of the room. YES a tour of the room, because there was so much in there. As you can see from some of the pictures, it was an amazing room. The room had french doors that you walk into from the hallway, and there was a entryway with a table and across from the table was a small bathroom. Then you walk into the living room. The living room had 2 nice size couches, a smaller table and a huge flat screen TV. The dining room had a large marble table and around the corner was a bar. Not just a little bar area, but a actual bar were you could serve drinks (which we did later that night), a fridge and a sink. There were even cabinets were you can hold extra bottles if need be. The bedroom had a large cozy bed, with a work desk and a chair with an autumn. The master bathroom was the only thing that was normal, except for the dual shower head. The suite had a hall closet and another closet in the master bedroom. We had a few friends over later that night, but you could have hosted a nice size party if you wanted to. If you would like this room, it was room 1802. AMAZING. We did not drink in the lobby bar, because we brought a case of birthday beer and champagne with us. We did eat a specialty pizza from the restaurant which was good. NOTE. If you get room service they will charge you 18% plus 2.95 for delivery. If you just go down and get it your self, you save all that money. Just charge it to your room and take it back to the room with you. Over all this hotel and staff met and surpassed all my expectations. I had a great birthday and I will probably try and stay in the EXACT room again next year.

“Very Average” Over the past weekend we stayed at the Crowne Plaza for our friends wedding. The property is listed as close to $130 a night, but with the wedding we got it for $89/night. On arrival friday night from the outside the property is grand, almost fancy in appearance. Once we got inside it was a whole different story. This hotel happens to cater to many conventions, unfortunately this past weekend was the "Frozen Bull Semen Convention." The lobby, bar, elevators will packed with drunk rowdy people. Even when we got to our floor, the hallway must have had 50 people with beers in hand, screaming at the top of their lungs. As we were passing by, people were asking us if we were the [-] that complained on them. It was not the most inviting situation. Once we got to our room the noise in the hallway continued until about midnight, before we could no longer hear screaming drunk people. The room itself was very very average. A standard bed with a small console tv. The furnishings, bathroom, lighting were all very average, honestly in need of an upgrade. The staff at the desk were EXTREMEMLY friendly. I had called ahead to arrange for a fridge/microwave, and on arrival we had a fairly large fridge/freezer and microwave that had been on and already nice and cold. We did visit the bar the following night (the semen convention and finished) and the food and drinks were quite good for a reasonable price too. We did not get a chance to visit the restaurant, but the menu looked appetizing. Some friends of ours had tried the breakfast and said it was quite good. Overall, this hotel is again average. We may have had a better experience if there were fewer drunk people present. I think it is probobly worth staying there is you can get a rate < $100. Honestly in Columbus Ohio, for $100-$150 a night, I expect much more than what we experienced at the Crowne Plaza.

“Awesome location, varying room quality” Having stayed at the St. Francis many times, I still very much like it for its location. Right at Union Square, plenty of dining and shopping options available on foot yet still not too bad to get in/out of the city if you’re there on business. Room quality unfortunately varies greatly: Rooms in the older part of the building are of good size, but bathrooms tend to be old and walls are thin. Rooms in the tower are more modern, but if you’re on a low floor you might be looking at a wall or another window just a few feet away. Rooms on the higher tower floors are best, especially when facing north: Awesome views including the Golden Gate Bridge, Coit Tower – or the Union Square if you’re facing east. Very welcoming staff, great concierge service. The hotel does participate in the SPG Green program, so if you skip cleaning for a day you get a US$5 food/drink voucher and extra SPG points. The Clock Bar is a nice place for that nightcap after a long day at work. P.S. If you’re a SPG Gold/Plat Member: The free water is sometimes “hidden” in the minibar fridge

“Still love the Desert Ridge” This was my third stay at this hotel. We had a most enjoyable time here last year and I was hopeful that it would prove to be as good this year. I was travelling with my twelve year old son so requested a room with a computer (rather than travel with a laptop) and this was granted with an upgrade to a room with a great view over the pools and mountains. The rooms are a reasonable size - with two queen beds, a spacious bathroom with shower and a balcony. We ate breakfast in the Blue Sage most days - buffet with my son paying around $9 and mine being $19.50 - a relaxing way to start the day - especially when suffering from jet lag and waking very early in the morning during our first few days in arizona. We spent some time by the pool most days and these were rarely crowded - but were noisier at the weekends when large groups of 'young (ish) men and women' would drink (a fair amount) and generally get quite loud as they turned pink in the arizona sunshine - golf parties or conference attendees - i don't know. There were many 'local' families on one occasion being allowed into the pool area by residents - you need a room key to access the pool area, they just asked if they would open the gates for them! It didn't seem to be a big problem really as the hotel pools are large and this is the off season. We ate pool side on several occasions and the food was fine - although one server over charged us on several occasions (the hotel put this right when I checked out). We had one meal (on our last day - and the server then told us that on purchasing one drink from the pool area (soft) we were entitled to refills all day (news to us) - I wonder if that will be the case next summer? - although we'd never been told this before. We ate room service often - my son prefers it, and it was usually pretty promptly delivered and generally warm. There is a 20% charge + $3 and tax added to each order - ouch! We were able to order using the inroom computer and confirm availability online - so my son was able to order the food for us this year - a nice touch. Check in and out of the hotel were easy and my special requests were met (computer and fridge). Most of the staff are attentive and helpful - always polite and friendly - the pool staff less so this year than last. We made use of the complimentary laundry service - with soap and softener provided - and left with clean clothes to finish our arizona holiday in the marriott canyon villas. We will be back here next year - we love the location, scenery and the service you get in the off-season. And as Brits we LOVE the sun......

“Good and Bad Reviews are true” Before posting this, I read the previous 8-10 reviews before me. I can say that I agree with them all - the good and the bad. But when the bad ones are true, they truely do overshadow the paper-thin physical appearance of the hotel. The room had beautiful fixtures and decour, and the rooms had lots of modern chic. Great detail, even down to the Plantation shutters in the rooms - and we stayed in two over two nights. That's because the noise was horrible. The hotel should be embarassed and ashamed at the oversight. Sound-proof windows are a necessity on busy downtown streets. The Valencia has none. It sounded like there was a construction project going on outside. The manager the next morning played dumb, saying he had not been informed of a construction project. Have you ever heard the garbage men when they grab a big Dumpster with the big robot arms then turn it upside down into the back of the truck, rapping the bin over and over to jar out garbage at the bottom? That was the sound that went on all night between midnight and 4am. The manager had no clue such a thing existed in their little neighborhood. So he moved us to another room on the 12th floor. My wife, a light sleeper as it is, never slept more than 2 hours. We were already tired from lack of sleep the night before. Then we heard our neighbors talking in their rooms all night, with blaring noise from the TV and what must have been a boom-box stereo. At one point, a woman loudly scolded either her son or husband in front of our room for 15 minutes. And when I say outside the door - I mean my wife looked out our peep-hole and saw the people standing one foot in front of our door - absolutely oblivious! She beat on the door and they left, but the noise from within the other rooms persisted. Even the bed (propped up on some wooden box) made too much noise. We tried to drown out noise with the AC fan, but as another reviewer posted, it only runs for a few minutes before kicking off automatically. I know certain hotels overprice their place for image and to keep out riff-raff, but this place is attracting riff-raff with money and their image is taking a blow. Breakfast buffet was ridiculously over-priced for being so average and offering so little. If you judge a hotel stay with your eyes alone - this is the place for you. If you judge it strictly as a hotel, the Riverwalk has far too many other competitive places than to waste your time here.

“Average” First time in NYC for my daughters 18th Bday. Room was small (but I believe on par for NYC). Location was excellent in Times Sqaure walking distance to a ton of stuff). Bed was comfortable, view was incredible (corner room overlooking times square). Did not use onsite facilities such as restaurant etc so no feedback. Overall rating average, nothing impressive besides location and view, but then again nothing to complain about.

“Great location, Good service, some amenities not impressive” The location is amazing, if you're planning to do a lot of public transport or walking. The service was great throughout the stay. I was disappointed with the quality, size, and ventilation in the gym. And I was bummed at the limited/expensive Internet options (no free wifi in the lobby, $15 fee for in-room Internet PER DEVICE).

“Peaceful with terrific service” This was our first stay at this hotel. Located in a residential area within a short walk from great shopping, this boutique is a gem. Even though there is no lobby, there are lots of nice touches. Hot cider or chocolate near the concierge desk served along side holiday cookies and welcome beverage delivered to the room on arrival. The standard rooms are spacious with enough room for a work table, a side chair and plenty of space to accommodate a room service table setting for two people. The bathroom is very l large with tub, separate shower and flat screen t.v. What makes this property heavenly is that it is quiet allowing for a wonderful nights sleep. We stayed on the fourth floor and it was very peaceful. Room service was quick and the food was delicious. Zero complaints. I see no reason not to return to this property. It's lovely.

“Very nice hotel in a great location.” All things considered we were very happy with our recent stay here. The room was nice, the service was good. The heater in our room did not work right and the man who came to fix it was very helpful. It's a short walk to Dupont Circle and the Metro. The staff was welcoming. I would only ding them for two small matters that keep them from "excellent." It's an upscale boutique type hotel yet they only provide free coffee in the lobby for a few hours in the morning and they have tiny little paper cups. You have to keep running back to fill them up. It's as if they're afraid you'll drink too much of their coffee. And also, for a nice hotel they surprisingly provide very cheap scratchy kleenex in the rooms. But these are minor and we'd stay there again.

“Typical TPS, could use a little refresher!” Hotel was okay for the price, however it seemed like there were quite a few college aged kids staying at the hotel. They were not loud, however hallways and elevators were not the cleanest. The bedding was fine in the room, and carpet, etc was clean. Just could use a cleaning or paint job.

“Comfortable Retreat” A one night stay for business turned out to be a pleasure here. Everything went well for me: check in, parking, clean, quiet and spacious room and balcony with a nice view of the harbor, good air conditioning, comfortable bed--oh and did I say clean? The restaurant staff were particularly nice as all meetings took place there--both inside and outside. I would stay here again, especially with the great rate I was given (instead of booking with one of the companies, I called the front desk because I had some specific questions about the accommodation and I was treated with over-the-top kindness).

“Won't ever come back” First, the positives... we arrived at 10:45 a.m., and they had a room for us shortly. The people at the desk were friendly and helpful. Now the negatives... After inching our way through terrible Boston traffic, the parking garage was full, so we parked a couple of blocks away and walked through the rain to the hotel. The room, at $169/night, is small and tatty. The bathroom is a knee-banger. There is a deionizer/heater running in the room, possibly to remove smoke odor. There is broadband internet connection, but if you're on the fifth floor as we were, expect a very weak WIFI signal. Supposedly you can hard-connect, but the receptacles in the room are the old style telephone connectors - no Ethernet receptacles and the hotel doesn't furnish cables like many. Don't count the nearby galleria food court as a plus; it's a cattle stampede at noon. Lest you think we're just overly-critical, we stayed at two wonderful chain motels on the way to this one, and reviewed them both positively. Parking, by the way, is $18/day, free at most motels. Bottom line, if you're a patient at one of the many area hospitals, perhaps you don't care about any of this. But if you're in Boston on business or pleasure, take a pass. Find a chain motel outside the inner city where the expense is less and there are more amenities.

“Decent value but not a 4-star hotel” The room we stayed in did not offer the luxurious feeling that the hotel's photos imply. Room lighting (mostly fluorescent) was terrible and depressing. Hallways felt especially run-down and not in keeping with the stylish lobby and elevator decor. Room was a good size, but the layout was too tight -- we could barely get around the bed and past the dresser. The bathroom was clean but very clinical and non-luxurious. Overall, it didn't feel like a nice hotel. On the positive side: Staff were friendly, polite, and genuinely helpful. Bed was comfortable. We got a good rate (Surf & Turf) that included free wired Internet access and self parking, which saved us more than $30.

“Great family stay at the Holiday Inn during Cherry Blossom Festival wknd!” This was an excellent Holiday Inn to my surprise. As mentioned by others, a great location for walking to many museums and attractions - within walking distance to the Smithsonian Museums, National Mall, Washington Monument, Holocaust Museum, & the Tidal Basin, for which we were there mostly to check out what was left of the Cherry Blossoms. Our room was very clean, the double beds were comfortable, and had plenty of towels too as we stayed on the 6th floor facing the inner courtyard. It was very convenient for my family to walk around to the sights and then relax in the hotel room afterwards. There is also a Starbucks in the hotel and a McDonald's less than 1/2 block away from the hotel that are open since everything else is closed during the weekends in that area. We were able to take advantage of the Bed Breakfast Beyond package that we booked which included buffet breakfast in the mornings, 2pm late checkout and 1/2 price discount off of parking ($17.50/night instead of $35). We also had dinner at the Capitol Bistro (which served breakfast too) one night and were impressed with the quality & variety of selections offered. Same goes for the breakfast buffet too! My family and I were very satisfied with this Holiday Inn and would definitely stay there again on any future DC vacations!

“Kudos to Hyatt Place!” Stayed here for one night in November 2008. I had heard about these newly renovated Hyatt Places and their aiming at Gen-Y, but this was my first time to stay at one. I must say they did an excellent job. The lobby is open and has lots of seating for small groups. There is an open kitchen that serves prepared meals 24/7 as well as a small snack bar serving Starbucks. We didn't use any of this, but were impressed. The room was huge with a great setup. It had a very green, modern feel to it. The color palate of the carpet, walls, bedspreads, etc was very eye-pleasing. There was a big flat panel tv that could swivel towards the living area or towards the beds. The beds were very comfortable as well. And perhaps the coolest thing was a panel with just about any electronic hook-up you could imagine. Ethernet, s-video, RCA, etc. So you could plug in a laptop and view it on the huge TV. My only complaints were the old, slow elevators which clearly weren't replaced with the renovation, and access, which was very poor coming from the south (downtown). There was nowhere good to get off coming from the south, so you have to take the access road like 2 or 3 miles before you can cross back under and go back south to where the hotel entrance is.

“Stay away from this dump” I also booked this hotel based on previous reviews. Either the reviewers have different standards, or management went downhill since. The room was filthy. Hair on the sheets and the sink. Mold in the bathroom. The pull out bed was so filthy (crumbs, peanuts, pieces of tortilla chips...) that we gave up on it, also because the mattress was thinner than the pillows. How is someone supposed to sleep on that mattress? Beats me. We ended up using an air mattress we had in the car. Service was below average. The young woman who checked me was not even listening to my questions, the man who checked me out seemed not to know what he was doing. Only one woman seemed to have a notion of "customer service," and was prompt and helpful when our room key stopped working. The water pressure was adequate, but the shower curtain is wafer thin and it's easy to flood the bathroom floor. The bathroom door did not lock. Last but not least, the boors above. A family with kids whose parents apparently did not believe in controlling the little lovelies, who as a result screamed and stomped most of the night. I cannot blame the hotel for the rudeness of certain American families, but be forewarned that this is the crowd that hangs out at Best Western. Needless to say, we will NOT be back.

“Not Such a Good Experience” Checked in on a Friday for a long weekend in Mid October. Arriving around 230PM we were made to wait until around 5PM to check in - due to late check outs. We were offered one complimentary glass of wine in the bar while waiting, were charged 10.00 for the additional glass. Upon checking in I enquired if the Sofitel chain was affiliated with either NWA or BA for frequent flier miles and the front desk rep had no idea. He did not volunteer to check on it for me either, just a simple I don't know. I would find it hard to believe I was the first person to ever ask about frequent flier miles but you never know.After we checked in our bags were not brought to our adjoining rooms like we were promised. Still more time wasted waiting for them. I was not given a key card for the outer door of our adjoining rooms, unfortunate for me I did not discover this till my friend and I split up to do different errands. The key kerfuffle was not handled well by the front desk...even more waiting while they got someone in security to make me the proper key. Around 1030PM Friday night I was awakened by Room Service entering my room. Apparently they had been knocking but I did not hear them ( the beds are very comfortable ). I did not think it was appropriate for them to just enter, especially when they had the wrong room. The coffee bar in the morning was nice. The last thing I did not appreciate was that on Sunday when I enquired about a late check out by 2 hours I was told NO, they had guests arriving that afternoon and needed the rooms ready by 3PM. That was interesting since it did not matter to them that I sat in the lobby about 2.5 hours on Friday due to late check outs. I have written well over a month ago to Sofitel Guest Relations with these and other concerns from my stay but they have yet to respond. I was unimpressed with their service and would not choose their hotel again. After spending 500 per room ( 1000 total ) for a weekend I expected a little more.

“Friendly and helpful staff, property in need of refreshing, decent location” The hotel is in a good downtown location, a few blocks from upscale shopping opportunities and a few blocks from the waterfront shops and restaurants. Property is due for a facelift, my guess is that the last one was ten years ago or so. Hotel is quiet on the room floors but the door latches are loud. It is almost impossible to open and close the doors quietly. You may wait for one of the four elevators as there are 40 floors to cover. Fitness room was crowded and a little too small for this size property. Large meeting room chairs were the typical stackable type, not very comfortable. Staff was pleasant, helpful and efficient.

“25 degrees and concrete floors not a good match!” I have stayed at the San Jose before and decided to give it another try. I love the zen like garden along with the wine bar and Jo's coffee next door. Parking is ample and free. I love the amenities in the bathroom, very hip. However this is where the charm ends. I want to love this place but just can't, the rooms have paper thin walls, and the light manages to shine in your eyes at the crack of dawn. The worst is the concrete floors. Who wants to wear shoes when the weather is cold?! A carpet runner would be nice. The bathrooms are as basic as the YMCA. The beds are ok but not like the heavenly bed or even the Sheraton sweet sleeper bed. Some paint and pictures on the walls would go along way, mininalistic is one thing but they take it to the extreme! The location is too far to walk into town where all the activities are. Don't confuse the front desk arrogance as intentional I just think they are not the brightest bunch. I have stayed at the Austin Hotel next door and although it is much older it really has some charm, although it to is too far from town.

“Ask for an upgrade” I discovered this Red Lion hotel on Quebec street because it shares the airport shuttle with the Hilton Doubletree. I have been here twice in winter and in summer on week-ends. There seems to be a regular budget seeking customer on the week-ends, mostly young families with van loads of kids, or college student athletes traveling to Colorado for competition. Yes, it is an older hotel, and some of the rooms are being renovated. And, the freight trains blow their whistles as they pass at night. It is just two blocks from a great shopping area with fast food restaurants and plenty of stores. The on-site restaurant is okay, and serves a buffalo burger. I joined the Red Lion frequent guest club, and ask for an up-grade when I check in. So far, that has worked to put me into one of their better rooms at rack rates. It's just a little hard to find the access road leading to the hotel from the Quebec Street North access road.

“Great location, as long as you're 5'8" or shorter” This is a remodeled 1920's hotel in the heart of Seattle. Great location, but the rooms are so small and confining that you have to be a person of smaller stature. We're both tall and over 200 lb, so bit of a challenge with suitcase storage, and general space! We had a king, and there was less that 18" between the edge of the bed and the wall. Thin walls. The bathroom - nice, but if you were in the Wizard of Oz as an extra Munchin - it'd be fine and spacious. Even with only one person in the room, it was confining. Also make sure you get a room on the street side as garbage trucks roll in about 3 am in the alley behind the hotel. High expections - but they werent met.

“Good value for the money” A lot has alredy been written about this hotel, so I'll try to cover some different ground by saying that it has definite pros and cons. Pros: clean, located in a good neighborhood, lots of space for the money, free breakfast. Cons: Felt a bit like a college dorm, in that it is efficient but has no ream charm or character. It's pretty far from a metro stop, in a kind of "in between" neighborhood between Dupont Circle and Georgetown. However, I should note that the nieghborhood has come up a lot in the past twenty years and has a lot of much more expensive hotels nearby (Ritz, Fairmont, etc) The free breakfast is extensive but is somewhat of a zoo with a lot of people packed in and milling around. The suites have those awful flourescent lights in every lamp, which I really hate but which are becoming ubiquitous, much to my (un PC) chagrin. All that being said, it's a decent place to base a sightseeing trip with the family, so long as you don't mind a good walk to the subway. I don't think I could recommend it for luxury travelers or even business travelers, but for sightseeing, it's OK, and good value for the money (although I was surprised they charged for internet access)

“Adorable hotel for solo travel in NYC but don't plan an event here.” The hotel's inability to handle a small convening was a nightmare, but the hotel was very cute. What can I say? I thought that I had found the perfect boutique hotel for a client's convening but boutique hotels sometimes come with a price: inefficient systems, lack of response, etc. It didn't help that there was a portage fee for each box and the sound person had lunch break scheduled for noon (as union members should) but the AV company of record for the hotel didn't send in a replacement for that hour. Where does that leave a convening? Without someone to set up mics for the lunch panel! But, if you are just hanging out in New York and you are looking for something off the beaten path, it's a good, rather inexpensive, alternative.

“Nicely furnished, poorly managed. Stay elsewhere” First, this review is for the Washington Hilton. Some reviewers of this hotel appear to be talking about the Capitol Hilton. Don't stay here, but if you do, make sure you're clear to cab drivers. (Locals call it the Hinckley Hilton, a reference to its grim historical role.) The place looks great and has some nice amenities. Rooms are clean and feel new - paint carts were all over the place when we visited, so seems like they're committed to keeping them that way. Sparkling, large fitness center and a nice pool (though don't expect the lifeguards to let you stay in it to the posted closing time - they shut it down nearly ten minutes early, apparently eager to get home). The nice interior is the only thing keeping this from getting a "Terrible" TA rating. The problem is service, and I don't mean the people providing it. Everyone, literally everyone we met was excessively nice and seemed dedicated and experienced. But the people managing them don't seem to have it together and/or they haven't hired enough staff. I could offer a number of examples. Expect long waits for someone to pick up the guest services line. At least twice it took more than a dozen rings for someone to even answer, and neither was at an odd time. I asked around later and the hotel wasn't even full that day, so just imagine what it would be like if there's a big convention or something. At another point, there was a major mechanical problem in our room that required maintenance to fix it, which caused severe inconvenience. At other hotels, for much more minor issues I've been offered a room upgrade, bottle of wine, something to make up for the hassle. The maintenance guys were super nice and took care of the problem the same day, but management didn't even send an apology note. I'm told the interior was recently renovated. But until there's better management of the nice people working there (and maybe more of them hired), this is a no go unless you're forced to or find a truly unbelievable deal.

“PAMPERED AT THE INDIGO” I travel constantly for the university that I work for and I must commend Hotel Indigo for combining both luxury at a pleasant price. When in San Antonio I choose to stay downtown because that's where all the fun is and because I know that I'll be pampered. LOL Ive stayed in different hotels north near the airport and they're okay. Ive stayed at cheaper places and have never been back. At the Hotel Indigo near the Alamo, I know that I will get great customer service and the staff goes over and beyond to make sure that I'm happy. This hotel is both historical character with a touch of luxury because it has been beautifully renovated with gorgeous wood floors, striking colors, flat screen TVs and awesome AVEDA toiletry products. There's a nice workout room downstairs where you can watch TV while you work up a sweat. Why stay anywhere else when you can be pampered with french toast , orange juice after sleeping like a baby.

“Okay hotel and Beware of charges” Thought the hotel was decent price for what it included which was the free breakfast and happy hour drinks/finger foods but it's really not worth it. There is always a long line for the breakfast, happy hour drinks and food, difficult to find empty seating to eat. The location was okay. The bedroom blankets are bad, it's a thin blanket and not comforter or heavy blanket to keep you warm. The pillows were so bad that it kept my husband awake all night long and he didn't sleep well with the mattress either; I didn't because of the blanket or lack of. If you're used to staying at Marriott and Hiltons or even any bedroom with decent thick covers and pillows, you will hate staying here. I also found a hair (not ours) in the sheet. The bedroom we received was very small facing a concrete wall of some building so we asked to switch rooms being first time here so the guest services happily did so and the room was bigger with separate bedroom with lots of traffic noise at night. However, this is where I give it one star. We prepaid the room since it was booked on their site at the best internet rate. When they gave us another room, we were charged for it so double charged! It's been 3 weeks, 3 calls and still no credit!!!! Very frustrating, much time wasted, and stressful because every time you call we have to wait and explain the situation again. ABSOLUTELY NOT WORTH IT!!

“Ok but not worth the money” The location is great right in the heart of things and a short walk the the convention center. The rooms are small and the price is veyr high compared to major hotels. They are not very well organized especially for check in. Three PM is the check in time I did not get my room u til 4:30 and I was one of the lucky ones some people were still waiting at 5. The Tv is very small and mine was dark. Wifi was ok. Next time, for the price, would book one of the major chains in the same area.

“Great little hotel” Great location, walking distance to everything (except the sports fields and the Space Needle but this is a nicer area of town anyway), across street from Seattle's new library. Unique room decor - funky, colorful, assorted patterns, but fun and very comfortable. Aveda toiletries, spacious bathroom counter with room for all your personal stuff. Friendly staff. Parking expensive at $27/day + tips. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was excellent at $8-$11, nearly 1/2 what the W Hotel's restaurant across the street was charging. Room 420 was not a suite but was quite roomy and had everything you'd need. Fitness room has Precor bikes, a treadmill, stair stepper, and free weights - ask for headphones at the front desk before you go down there if you want to hear the TVs mounted at each station. Tulio, a Seattle favorite restaurant, is one block away --try the sweet potato gnocchi for an appetizer and the risotto - both excellent, as was the grilled lamb. Not cheap though - about $100 for 2 with 1/2 bottle wine. This was my first experience booking through Hotwire so was worried we'd get one of the worst rooms, but it was as nice as any I think, except maybe the suites. We paid $130 (Hotwire 4-star rating). If you don't like the big chain hotels, this is an excellent alternative.
“Better places in Midtown” Yes, great location. But there are better places nearby - The Library, Dylan and Roosevelt for example. For the price, the Bryant Park is far better.

“Horrible rip off from Priceline” I booked this hotel for over $200 a night on priceline. When I got there they refused to give me a nonsmoking room and were completely un helpful. The room they showed me was stinky and disgusting and they insisted it was my only choice, telling me i had requested a smoking room which is not true since I'm allergic to cigarette smoke. Since it was with priceline, I paid for 3 nights ($775) and couldn't even stay at the hotel because of the smoke, and they refused to give me a refund. What a huge rip off and disappointment. Bottom line, do not book through priceline for a 3 star hotel in georgetown or you might end up with this horrible place.

“Best Bath Robes of ANY HOTEL... EVER” Last minute stay at the Hotel Vitale... and it was amazing. The panoramic suite featured stellar views of the Bay Bridge and the Ferry Building. Room service was good, service from staff was excellent. I also used the business center, which was small but perfect. Well appointed. Highlights: - Walk in Shower - Giant Bathtub with View - Windows - Mini-Bar - AMAZING BATH ROBES Hotel bath robes are usually nothing to write home about... but these robes are exceptional. I have no idea what type of fabric is used on the exterior of these robes...it is like UnderArmor or something... I have no clue... Great robes- feel and look incredible. Inquired at the front desk the cost of the robes and they are only $100. What a steal for the best bath robe on the planet.

“A disappointing experience” Have just returned from a ten day trip to the US, which ended with five days in NYC staying at Affinia Shelburne - have mixed feelings about this hotel. Firstly, we got an excellent price (40% discount) through Hotels.com. I emailed hotel twice to give them a chance to price match - no response. In the end I called from UK, but they wouldn't do this, so booked through Hotels.com. The hotel is very nice indeed, although a different part of the public area appears to be being dug up each day! Also, the housekeeping trolleys were kept in the corridors all the time, which spoiled the look, and made it difficult to navigate past with all the luggage when we arrived and left. The room we had was the quietest we have ever had in NYC and was very comfortable indeed. However, to call it a Studio Suite is a misnomer - it is an ordinary hotel bedroom with only one chair , a bed, a TV and a desk with minibar - most definitely not a suite. The hotel offered a hot buffet breakfast for $12 for the first three mornings which was excellent, but on the fourth morning it changed to a la carte where a slice of french toast and a coffee would have cost more than this and the 18% gratuity was added automatically to the bill - even though half of the dining room was being (very noisily) dug up at the time we wanted breakfast. The charges for wi-fi and computer access were, I thought, steep, particularly as I have usually had free internet access in New York hotels previously. The staff (with the exception of a couple of the doormen and the really pleasant chambermaid) were uninterested to the point of rudeness and the front desk staff didn't adjust our bill as they promised to. When I asked if they had bathrobes as pictured on their website, I was told that the website room photographs were not real room settings, just made up ones! They did however then provide me with robes. When asking about the rooftop bar, we were told it was on the 14th floor by one member of staff, the 15th floor by another, and finally correctly the 16th floor by the third. When we visited it we were short changed by $10 by the barman and offered no apology - only told by the manager that it was our fault because we didn't get a check (weren't offered one!).
