I have stayed in the Affinia Manhattan previously where it is much more noisy, but the room (studio suite) was huge, had kitchen facilities and the staff were very gracious. I have also stayed in the San Carlos which is far superior and the Courtyard Marriott (several times) where the customer service is absolutely excellent. Would I stay there again - no probably not, and definitely not at the full prices. The overall feeling given by the staff at this hotel was that they were interested in getting every last dollar out of us. Whilst I have no problem in paying for good service and amenities , this hotel did not provide either of these. This is not a 4 star hotel, and the service is certainly not 4 star.

“Gutes Hotel in guter Lage” Das Hyatt Regency, Bosten ist ein typisches Hyatt Hotel, direkt an der Haupteinkaufsstrasse von Boston. Vom und zum Flughafen sind es rund 20 Minuten. Der Check-in verlief schnell, das Personal war sehr freundlich, obwohl es nur eine provisorische Rezeption gab, da die eigentliche Rezeption umgebaut wurde. Der Umbau hat den Hotelbetrieb aber nicht gestört, es war weder laut noch dreckig. Mein Wunsch nach einem ruhigen Zimmer wurde entsprochen (bei Buchung angegeben), leider war der Ausblick nicht solo prickelnd, aber man steht ja auch nicht den ganzen Tag am Fenster. Das Zimmer selbst war standardmässig eingerichtet, gross und geräumig, wie man es von Hyatt erwartet. Über Sauberkeit kann man sich auch nicht beklagen, tägliche Reinigung und Auffüllen der Goodies im Badezimmer. Die Lage der Bar ist nicht wirklich gut gewählt aber OK. Ein kleines "Lowlight" ist das Frühstück (gebucht). Für Europäer könnte es etwas mehr Brot und Marmelade / Honig geben. Nur Toast ist ein wenig eintönig. Ansonsten kann man aber nicht meckern. Omelettes werden frisch, nach Wunsch zubereitet. Das Restaurant ist auch zu empfehlen, wenn man am Abend nochmal einen kleinen Snack möchte. Ansonsten sollte man die Restaurants in unmittelbarer Umgebung nutzten. Hier gibt es eine grosse Auswahl und die Preise sind niedriger als im Hotel. Die Lage ist, wie schon gesagt, ausgezeichnet. Vom Hotel aus kann man Boston bequem zu Fuss erkunden. Boston Commons ist gleich um die Ecke und zum Hafen braucht man 10-15 Minuten zu Fuss. Über die Garage von Hotel hat man auch direkten Zugang zur Bostoner U-Bahn ("T") - 2 Linien halten hier. Alles in Allem kann man das Hotel sehr empfehlen, sowohl für einen Städtetrip als auch für Geschäftsreisen.

“Phoenix can be a Nightclub w/ rooms” The Phoenix is a bargain with a catch. On weekends, speakers, bouncers, a DJ, and clubbers can be right outside your door until the wee hours. The staff is great, the atmosphere is cool, but be prepared. Free parking, people watching, and transvestite hookers outside are added bonuses. It is easy to catch a cab.

“Decent not awesome” We came here for a conference and was very happy with the room. Very roomy and comfy. The food in the am was pretty good. The conference room was good, although the seat we chose was right beside the temperature control and my husband had to adjust every ten minutes because the room either got very cold or very hot. The location was ok of flying in but not if you wanted to do a quick run out for dinner. Nothing right there at hotel. Staff seemed flustered with the amount of people at conference for lunch and everything was disorganized and they seemed irritated. And we were giving them business? Hummmm.....

“Satisfactory but we'll keep looking for our next visit” Our family of four stayed at The Warwick on July 28, 2005. The hotel was older but well-kept from what we saw. We had room 2601/2602 which ended up being a sort of junior suite. Unfortunately, we had two young children with us and the sofa was not a sofa bed as I had booked. The front desk however did send up a rollaway bed when asked. The location is good as mentioned and we walked to Times Square and FAO Swartz near Central Park. There is a Hilton right across the street at which we stayed on Jan 1, 2004, which is probably more preferable for us in the future. The Warwick's elevators (as would be expected in the historic building that it is- built by William Randolph Hearst for his paramour Marion Davies) are indeed small. The service could use improvement, particularly the front door staff. The bellhops were helpful storing our luggage however. The best element by far was the restaurant, Murals on 54. The food was okay, but we had great service. The staff were WONDERFUL with the three kids we dined with at breakfast. The staff were attentive, courteous, couldn't have asked for better. It also didn't hurt that the buffet for the 1, 3 and 6 old children were free. The recent remodel was very nice.

“Beautiful decor and artwork” My brother's rehearsal dinner was held at the Canterbury this past weekend. The lobby and reception areas of this downtown hotel are beautiful- a colorful mix of both traditional and contemporary artwork with large, overstuffed sofas and chairs. It was a really nice choice for a rehearsal dinner. I didn't sleep at this hotel but the guests who did said the rooms were lovely and comfortable, tho small.

“Hotel Near Getty” I booked this hotel for a room with a King bed because we were staying at Marriots on this trip to Los Angeles for our Marriots Rewards program, and this hotel was close to The Getty. It is about 15 miles away, but it may take longer than 15 minutes depending upon traffic. The rooms are small, but the beds are comfortable. The first room I asked for had cigarette butts and was dirty. They quickly changed us to another room; it was on the sixth I believe. It had been changed from a smoking to a nonsmoking floor when I opened the door it smelled horrible. My daughter was helping us check in since she lives in L.A., but she had to leave because the room smelt so bad. My husband was even bothered by the smell, and he never complains about hotel rooms. I was getting discouraged, but the front desk was really nice about it. Our third room was great! It was still small, but it was clean. The hotel has a nice modern lobby with a Starbucks, and the Mall across the street has several restaurants accessible from outside entrances. This mall had a nice Macys, which was great I did a little shopping at their sale. The Cheesecake Factory is suppose to be close by, but we did not go looking for it. The Getty was easy to access from this hotel, but we thought the 405 would be easier on a weekend, not so. Many of the guests seemed to be associated with events or businesses.

“Ein Hotel der Mittelklasse” Das Zimmer war im großen und ganzen in Ordnung. Nur leider liegt dieses Hotel in einer nicht sehr ansprechenden Gegend, da es hier viele Obdachlose gibt. Alleine hätte ich mich abends nicht mehr auf die Straße getraut. Der Service im Restaurant war absolut in Ordnung, man hat sich sehr um uns bemüht.

“The "Stephen F." falls short of InterContinental standards” Summary: On our second stay at the "Stephen F." we were sad to find that things have gone down hill dramatically for this property. Definitely a low-end member of the InterContinental chain. I would recommend the Driskill as an alternative. PROS: excellent location with much to do within walking distance, good water pressure, plenty of hot water, nice bedding, pretty lobby, and oddly enough I was not put off by the $18 daily unlimited valet though it would be nice to have another option, they didn't charge us for the "welcome amenities" we purchased (it was a special occasion) though if they had we would've complained because the quality was extraordinarily poor for the price ($25 plus service charges for a couple of apples, an orange, a few grapes, a bottle of water, and four tiny, waxy, totally inedible truffles) the guest services manager did--on request--unpack flowers sent ahead and place them in the room. CONS: we basically felt shamed for booking our room on Hotwire, this was a special occasion so I called beforehand to inform the hotel and to request a complimentary upgrade if available (this request is routinely filled when we travel elsewhere for a special occasion...birthday, anniversary, etc.) but were told we couldn't be upgraded because we purchase though Hotwire; however, on arrival the others in our party (who also booked through Hotwire) were upgraded...we were told that we could "purchase" an upgrade, our particular class of room was extraordinarly tiny...more like what I expect in New York City or San Francisco (our friends who had all been upgraded came to see our room and began to refer to it as being in "steerage"), the bathtub had numerous areas where the glazing had come off, the retractable clothesline was broken and hanging down, the picture in the bathroom was filthy (toothpaste residue, etc), there was a broken lamp that flickered on and off when you opened and closed the drawer of the table it was on, it was unnecessarily difficult to operate the alarm clock (which, incidentally, went off at 4AM as set by the previous guest...housekeeping should know to turn off the alarm function after each guest), uneven housekeeping...they often failed to replace toiletries and even failed to replace the towels once, only a teeny-tiny indoor pool, the toiletries were of very good quality but every person in our group encountered two rather bizarre problems: first, the caps are made of two parts (way, way overdesigned) and they kept coming apart leaving the bottle sealed while you were holding the top part of the cap, and second, it was impossible to just get a small amount of product out of the unusual little bottles...you got nothing or half the bottle...like I said everyone in our group noticed this issue so it wasn't just us, the front desk manager is impeccably dressed and totally professional but his perfectly clipped British demeanor comes off as more aloof than courteous and lacked any warmth...this is Austin not Buckingham Palace.

“Mega-hotel, but personal service” Because I called ahead, my room was ready for an 8 am check-in. Rooms, especially in The Towers, are lovely with all the amenities. Great location, right on the 16th Street Mall and lots of dining options in the hotel and nearby. I was attending a conference and the meeting spaces were gigantic and the A/V staff very helpful.

“Pretty good, not excellent” The Fairmont San Jose was a great deal at the room rate we had ($160/night) for a nearby conference and expo. My room was large with a proper work desk, loveseat, chair and plenty of floor space. The bathroom was large and clean, as was the closet. I also really liked that there was a separate WC room and a vanity area outside the bathroom, which makes it easy for multiple people to get ready in the morning. I found the lobby lounge lovely with really friendly, down-to-earth staff, as was the onsite restaurant, the Grill. I also had very pleasant service from the front desk, concierge and housekeeping. I didn't try the pool, but the gym was above average for a hotel. The location was also perfect for easy walking to the convention center and many Downtown restaurants. However, a few things should be noted that keep me from giving this a higher rating: 1. The trash bin was not empty when I checked into my room, though I saw no further evidence of poor cleaning throughout my stay 2. The shower stall was a little small for my taste. i would rather have given up the separate shower and tub than have something this size. 3. There was a weird smell in my room sometimes. Kind of like sewer, to be frank. I noticed this same smell wafting along First Street during parts of some days, so I think it's not the hotel's fault, but rather it just gets sucked in to the ventilation system when the wind blows a certain way. It wasn't constant or strong, but any hint of such a smell is really unwelcome. So, all that said, I think the qualification I first made - for the room rate of $160 - makes a difference. I don't think this hotel is worth $200+

“Disappointing Room & Service” An Omni frequent guest program participant, I stayed here recently and was disppointed in the service and the quality of the room. The room was traditionally furnished and elegant but very small. There was very little counter/desk space throughout the room and bath. The TV was mounted on the wall; this was fortunate because there was no table or desk space for it! While I have never before used drawers in hotel rooms, this time it was necessary because of the lack of open space. The desk was too tiny for work (and cluttered with the coffeemaker, room service menu, etc.). Per the front desk staff all the rooms have similarly small desks. Not a good choice for business travelers. The complimentary morning beverage never arrived at the designated time. The room service salad was small and pricey. All room service food here is pricey. If you want rolls or bread with your dinner you will be charged extra (you would think that at the Parker House Hotel Parker House rolls would be provided). On the positive side, the location is close to several historic sites. As a frequent business traveler in Boston I have stayed at the Omni, Eliott, Hilton Back Bay and Commonwealth Hotels. Of these four the Commonwealth is by far the best!

“Decent budget hotel” We spent nine nights at the Wolcott. Overall, the hotel was quite nice considering the rate. The lobby was quite grand, nicely restored and ornamented and the rooms were moderate, but clean and the bed was firm and ok. TV worked, some trouble with the signal with some channels. Complimentary muffins, coffee and tea were served in the lobby, which was a nice surprise. Location is excellent, just a couple of blocks from the Empire State Building, Macy's and Penn Station. The two elevators were small and slow, and one of them malfunctioned one evening, but it was repaired before the next morning. The hallways seemed somewhat worndown. Maid visited everyday. If you want a clean,basic and affordable place where to stay and rest your bones in a good location in Manhattan, then I guess the Wolcott is just fine. Don't expect anything fancy or room service or anything like that. There were no problems (except the one elevator one night) during our stay. Overall we got good value for our money.

“Sleep in the car” The room was not really fit for paying customers. The staff was arrogant and rude. We tried to check in at 2:50 and was told that the rooms would not be ready for 10 minutes. Based upon the room, I know they were not cleaning my room. The security latch was broken, the faucet leaked, the chairs had giant stains, the closet doors were missing, you only get a bar of soap (no shampoo), the sheets are sandpaper quality, and the towels smelled of chemicals. The toilet did work.

“Good value at a convenient location” We stayed here for one night before flying out from Phoenix, so it was very much a quick stopover where we weren't looking for a ton of amenities, just a clean room. Crowne Plaza delivered on that score; and we got a nice rate via Hotwire. Rooms are arranged a very large atrium which includes an indoor pool. It didn't bother us at all, but guests who are sensitive to chlorine odors might find this a drawback. The hotel seemed nice but strangely empty of decor. I think we may have come while they were in the midst of a carpet cleaning of the main atrium--no furniture, no plants in the gravel, just wide open emptiness, which gave it a strange feel. The front desk staff were generally nice, but on check-on the clerk failed to notify us that there was a happy hour. We learned of it only after we were walking through the lobby and heard another staffer apologize to a guest that he was checking in too late to be a part of it. I wasn't sure if this was because we were Hotwire guests, or plain forgetfulness, but we were disappointed with that. If they had breakfast we didn't hear about that either! The indoor pool was bitterly cold--we had no problem coaxing my son out of it because he was turning blue. Hotel is in the midst of a corporate park area; there are some restaurants & shopping nearby (driving distance) but nothing you could walk to. The front desk staff have a list of local restaurants they will share. That's helpful. Cute gift shop in hotel, small but some worthwhile items. Hotel is in North Phoenix area, right off Interstate 17, so it's a quick jaunt to downtown, airport, etc. I would stay here again for a trip of this purpose--just a place to crash for a night while we were in transit.

“Comfortable but very dated” Spent 3 nights here - location is not so bad - close to the Space Needle and about 15-20 minutes walk from Downtown / Market Place. Rooms looks very dated indeed as does the whole hotel. Service relatively good.

“Creaky Noise Disclaimer Should be Required for North Tower” If you stay in this hotel, bring earplugs and anti-nausea meds. The North Tower sways rather dramatically in the wind (significantly more than any other towering hotel I've visited), resulting in very loud creaking through the walls. The noise was so loud we thought rats were scurrying through the walls and called the front desk, all due to a 6 mile per hour (mph) wind. When the gusts hit 23 mph every inch of the walls sounded like they were creaking. Although the noise issue is apparently a regular problem, the front desk couldn't be bothered to tell us themselves what the problem was and instead sent up the "engineer" to explain that earthquake retrofitting was the cause of the loud noise. When the engineer called the front desk from our room to see if we could move to a quieter room, the front desk denied that any additional rooms were available in the hotel (this after they tried to up-sell us on an upgrade upon check in after noting that the hotel wasn't full) - not impressed. It's too bad the hotel does not warn guests of the creaking noise, too, because the room itself was adequate and had a decent view, and had we expected the noise and swaying we might have been more impressed with the hotel.

“Hello, I thought I was at Trading Spaces” So you walk in the lobby, I thought it looked like Rob and Laura Petrie's livingroom from the Dick Van Dyke Show. I know Trendy, 60's is in, but come on folks work with me here, its UGLY, it was UGLY in the 60's. The Wi-fy, less than pleasant. I couldn't connect in the morning. The WATER PRESURE in the bathroom was worse than SUCKY. There is none! The bathroom sink is nice to look at, but you need an owners manuel to work the faucet. The safe to store your laptop, would not accomodate mine. The ICE machine is in the frickin BASEMENT. The signage on the hotel is not visable unless you look up. The neighborhood is really sketchy at night. 1 block with a wrong turn and you are in the bad part of the tenderloin. Lastly, there is NO AIRCONDITIONING! Our ceiling fan had a mind of its own, it comes on and off by itself, I understand that the remote controls from other rooms will activate your ceiling fan 1-4 rooms away.

“overrated, overpriced” I've stayed at the hotel as well as attended luncheons and meetings here. Room: - I got a particularly small room and it wasn't the most comfortable. Remarkably, my friend's room, at the same rate, was about 2x as big and more luxurious. Hello - The hotel has a long, storied history and it's reflected in the decor and service. - The food served at the luncheons is probably the best i've ever had at any luncheon. - Otherwise, a very staid hotel where the older crowd definitely hangs out. I'm probably one of the youngest people roaming around

“Great place to stay near Little Italy!” Stayed at the Hampton Inn for 2 nights to attend the Little Italy Festa. If you are a fan of the Hampton chain and what they offer (free airport shuttles, complimentary breakfast, business traveler-friendly touches) I am happy to report this hotel doesn't break from tradition. Check-in was quick. They get bonus points from me because I arrived around noon and there were a number of people in front of me from the cruise ships--but my room ready and I was able to check in early. The staff was very friendly and very helpful in giving directions. The location was ideal for me since I did not have a car--it's in a safe area, just a quick walk to Little Italy and all the major bus and trolley lines. Also a 5 minute walk to Seaport Village area and the Broadway Pier if you need to catch the ferry to Coronado. I was really impressed by the workout room. While small, it had a number of cardio machines in good shape (including the elliptical--which is hard to find!) and sturdy free weights and a stability ball, and a water cooler. To address the issue of the train--I only heard it once during my stay. But I am used to living near trains so it probably did not bother me for that reason. All in all, a good stay and made my first time visit to San Diego a good one.

“Very Accommodating” We spent 2 nights here waiting to fly out from visiting our daughter and family. Nice, spacious room, clean. Better than average breakfast fare. We came down from the mountains on a shuttle and the CI&Suites driver took us to the rental car agency. Very nice people at the front desk and all personnel that we encountered were very nice and helpful. Got a great rate too!

“Top shelf. Leave the kids at home.” VERY, VERY nice property. The staff was very courteous and helpful. Location wasn't the best and looked a little scary out on the street at times, but no issues while out walking before dark. The pool (or Poule as they call it) is as nice as any you will find, glass on the end which extends out at 10 stories high. As an order of french toast was around $20 I decided to walk down the street (out the front, down one block to left, take a left and Seven Eleven was on the right) and get a donut and some milk. The fitness center again was as nice as I've ever seen. I would not suggest bringing kids here although there were no problems we were the only family we saw. The adults at the pool were making out to the point a few of the couples should have went back to their rooms, needless to say we didn't stay at the pool long.

“Expected more, not the greatest choice in the area” I was in town for the Nike Women's Marathon this past weekend and shared a room at Nikko with another runner. I was originally booked at Orchard Garden, but in the interest of saving some money decided to share a room with a friend instead. She was already booked at Nikko - the proximity to Union Square (and the starting line) was better and the price was cheaper. On first appearance, the hotel is extremely nice. Marble foyer, great valet staff, front desk was extremely helpful and kind, as was the concierge. Huge compliments to the staff. Unfortunately, the rooms cannot compare. The beds were soft and the bedding was nice and comfortable. The room was a little small, but I believe this is the standard in San Francisco, so I can't complain. The separate tub and shower are nice, but my biggest complaint is about the shower. The shower door would not stay closed. The water pressure continue to get weaker and weaker as I showered. As a runner, I appreciate an awesome high pressure hot shower after a marathon. . . it was a shame that the shower went to a light drizzle a few times (was EVERY runner showering at once?) and didn't stay very hot. The worst part was the mold and mildew all over the shower stall. I have attached pictures because I don't want readers to think I am exaggerating. I was so disappointed to see that the cleaning staff didn't make enough effort to prevent this much growth. This is not four star, $225/night quality. There are much nicer hotels in the area for this price. Choose wisely when going to San Francisco and opting to stay near Union Square. Hopefully Nikko will clean up their rooms and then the stay will be much more well-rounded. It is a shame the room quality doesn't match the superb staff.

“Decent hotel, nothing luxurious” I stayed here over the Thanksgiving holiday while visiting family in the area. The hotel was decent, rooms were of average size, clean, and the staff at the front desk was very friendly. They accommodated our family, as we had reserved 5 rooms, and they made sure to put all of them next to each other. My complaints would be the area of the hotel. It is not easily visible from the street, gets very dark and is next to the woods. Our car was broken into the night before we left, and Im sure the dark secluded are helped that. Also, the walls are very thin so you can easily hear people above, below and on either side of your room. This included the kids that were running up and down the hallways all night. The beds were TERRIBLE. They felt like concrete and I had to take Tylenol for back every morning. The tvs were also very old and need to be replaced.

“Very Good Hotel” This hotel was overall very good. The concierge as well as front desk receptionists were very helpful and kind. The bellman as well as the doormen also went out of their way to make sure our stay was enjoyable. We have stayed at other high end properties in D.C (such as the Ritzs) and this one has the best location for sightseeing. However, I must critique several aspects of the hotel. I think it may have been the time that we were checking in at (as many people were checking in at around 5PM) but the receptionists seemed somewhat disorganized- we were handed another guest's welcome. Mind you, they were very kind; however, a third receptionist might have been needed to better serve all the guests checking in. I just thought this should have been a bit more smooth. Also, paying for a higher category room is well worth the $40. We started off in a deluxe room that had a tiny bathroom with very little sink room, a very small closet by the TV, and very little room between the bed and the TV area. We then asked for a larger room, which was much better. It had 2 sinks with a large counter area, a spacious seating area, and plenty of closet space. So worth the $40 extra a night! I also think the turn down service was a bit bare, perhaps slippers and bed mats should be included. Overall though, an excellent stay and I would stay here again while visiting the D.C area!

“Nice place in a good location” I stayed in the Avenue Hotel Crowne Plaza for one night for a conference. My experience was nearly completely positive. The room was nice and big with a pretty good view. It had the usual amenities (flat screen television, desk, etc.). The room and bathroom were clean and well-maintained. The furniture and bed were in good condition. There was a minibar I didn't use (just like all mini bars, the items were ridiculously overpriced). One great feature was free wireless Internet that was reliable and fairly fast. The location is ideal if you want to be in the neighborhood surrounding Michigan Avenue. There were a ton of restaurants and stores within easy walking distance. I had a drink in the bar in the lobby of the hotel, and it was quite nice. I only had three small complaints The room rate was not a bargain, but I'm sure that was partially because the conference was going on (I booked too late to get the conference rate, which was only $20 cheaper than what I paid). Travelzoo had deals at comparable hotels in the neighborhood for less than half the price I paid. Also, I found a small candy wrapper in the closet when I was hanging up my coat. The rest of the room was clean, but it did make me wonder about the housekeeping. And room service took longer to deliver my breakfast than the amount of time I was told when I ordered. Luckily, I was running early, so the delay didn't make me late for the conference. But over all, I had a positive stay at the Avenue Crowne Plaza, and I would be happy to stay there again (depending on rates at comparable hotels in the neighborhood).

“Amazing” Beautiful,Amazing,This motel is one of the best motels you have to stay at this place even if its just for fun or for business.Very nice area with tons of things to do,resturants,gifts,loved this motel

“Love love loved it!” We stayed for two nights and paid a little over $100/night using our AAA discount. This was an incredible value. I highly recommend this hotel. The rooms are large and immaculate. The bathrooms are luxurious. The staff was extremely gracious. I cannot say enough about the beautiful decor throughout this hotel. We had drinks at the lobby bar (fun!), coffee in the lobby (free!) and brunch in the restaurant (so-so but the ambiance made up for the mediocre food).

“Perfect stay” Spent 3 nights in room 726 in the new tower. Terrific stay. Beautiful terrace overlooking the marina. Very nice room with very clean lines. Great shower. Concierge was very helpful. Housekeeping was top notch. Great hotel on the water and within a half a mile of the airport. The planes can be loud but the sight of them taking off and landing so closely was a fun aspect of our stay. Top notch exercise equipment in 24 hour gym. Self park was $22 a day but easy. We'd very likely stay here again. Nice, large waterfront pool as well.

“Simply the best” Wow, this is a really great hotel.I stayed here twice in Feruary in two different rooms. I don't feel any need to stay anywhere else in LA (Unless budget is a constraint). This is a real five star hotel with great character and a tremendous level of service. The rooms are stunning. Huge high ceilinged suites with marvellously decadent decoration and a four poster bed. Each room is equipped with a vintage record player and a selection of albums! The kitchen is beautifully equipped and the bathrooms are great. Each room also has a spacious balcony. Room service arrived in 5 minutes with a meal ordered from the excellent mediterranean restaurant. The selection of drinks and snacks in the room is imaginative and extensive. Check in staff are super helpful. I overheard one of them sending out a taxi to find a guest who had got lost somewhere in LA ! Of course all this comes at a price (overnight parking is $37!) and the rooms come at around $320-$350 a night, but in a way it is excellent value for money and nothing here is done on the cheap. There is even a washing machine hidden away in one of the cupboards. The one draw back is perhaps the noise. Avoid the rooms that give onto the club next door on the North side. On my first night there was a live concert going on until midnight. Luckily it was a great concert which we enjoyed without having to pay for tickets! The rooms that look out onto Vine are also a little noisy at night. The quieter rooms look out onto an internal courtyard, but then they don't have the great views from the balcony This a really great experience and you could happily live here for an extended period if you had the money!

“Mandarin vs The Setai” The Mandarin is a beautiful hotel. Having lunch overlooking Central Park is amazing. The room was small but comfortable. The spa is just okay. The services are lovely, but the spa amenities are lacking. When comparing luxury I prefer The Setai the room are much bigger with espresso machines and internet included. The turn down service brought gourmet pretzels and candies. I love their spa with water lounge. Its the little things that matter. The Mandarin did not even put a chocolate on the pillow and charge for internet. I hate feeling nickel and dime-ed on my vacation.

“EXCELLENT!” This was the last hotel we stayed in, during our two week road trip. We only stayed for one night, from the moment we checked in, till the moment we checked out, everything about this hotel was perfect. The staff are excellent, always smiling, always helpful. The rooms were fantastic, spotlessly clean, smartly decorated, and the funky animal print roles were a riot! The location was great, nice safe, vibrant area. We ate at the Hotel restaurant, David (our waiter) was excellent, friendly, informative and very professional. This is without doubt, a great find, thank you tripadvisor!

“excellent hotel !!!!!” sheraton gateway was an excellent hotel in los angeles. it was in a good location. its a big hotel with many rooms, nice ambience. staff were very friendly. i stayed 3 nights enjoyed alot. big rooms and finally had a nice stay

“Slightly Tired Elegance with Terrific Views” We had a very nice stay at the Fairmont, and whether you love it or not depends on point of view -- this historic grand dame was elegantly renovated -- but ten years ago.... So, the furnishings are far more luxurious than an average four star, but slightly too worn for top ratings. The beds, however, are very good and the linens are Frette -- wonderful. If travelling with children; this would not be my top choice -- stay at the waterfront! The Argonaut is a terrific, fun, hotel with kids, and there will be far more to entertain them. Likewise, for a young adult, there is nothing hip or cool about the Fairmont. But for the business or adult traveller, the location is central for business and restaurants and quietly above the fray -- no cheap t-shirt shops on Nob Hill! And the Fairmont is truly a beautiful historic building. The best thing about the hotel per se, are the views -- so book a tower room (this is admittedly not the old part of the hotel, but you can still hang out in the historic marble lobby). Another decent choice are rooms in the front of the hotel overlooking the roof garden, which is lovely. By all means avoid the interior rooms - there is no point in staying here at all if you are looking out at grey interior walls! On a clear day, go across the street to Top of the Mark (at the Intercontinental Hotel) for breakfast or drinks.

“I would MAYBE stay here, again.” I got an amazing deal($100) with Priceline for this hotel, I got lucky! I stayed here for one night and it was a good experience. The only downside of it was that my bath tub got clogged while I was showering. The weird thing is that it must have been for a while because my hair doesn't really fal out. I didn't tell them because I wasn't staying there another night, but the tub was still clogged when I checked out the next morning. The beds were beyond amazing, I always thought Marriott had the best beds but this hotel beat them. It was very vintage looking but it was really nice. The staff was very friendly, the area is perfect for people who like to be near everything. You have Times Square a block down and 5th Avenue two blocks up. Good location!

“Over priced and over rated but bettr than some” I really like to stay in Marriott properties when ever possible but I woudl have to say that I was seriously disappointed in this hotel. Don't get me wrong, the location was great and the staff were fantastic, especially Edward the elderly Concierge who was beyond helpful everytime we would see him Now for the no so good - the entrance of the hotel smelled like urine everyday, many people even commeted to the Valet staff about it and they just joked, saying "they must be used to it by now". Here's an idea, how about breaking out the pressure washer. The hallways also smell very musty as if the carpets were wet and in the 5 days we were there it was not uncommon to see big fans blowing in the hallways to help dry things out which added more noise in the halls For the most part the hotel was just OK and simply not worth the $300+ per night they were demanding. Again - location great and service good, quality of hotel was just bad
“長期滞在もOK” ダウンタウンからは少し距離がありますので、レンタカーがある場合だけ宿泊していました。部屋は広く、長期の滞在でもストレスは少ないと思います。クイーンアンの一角にあるので、徒歩圏にもレストランやスーパー(セーフウェー)、ピザ屋、クリーニング店、コーヒーショップ(タリーズなど)一応のものはそろいます。キーアリーナ(NBAの本拠地)やスペースニードルへも歩いて行けます。

“Not a boutique hotel” The lobby is misleading. The rest of the hotel is strictly on a par with your average clean motel in a regional city. The hotel basically has no amenity that would be expected of an establishment that claims to be a "boutique" hotel. Though reasonably clean and comfortable, the rooms are basic and bare bones when it comes to the little things. Not even drinking glasses. The mini bar is strictly soft drink in cans, and that's it. And the little plastic toiletries in bottles appear to be replenished rather than replaced when new guests occupy the room. Most off-putting for me was this weird smell—like an artificial scent of rancid buttered popcorn—that wafted through the halls. Won't return, even at rates that are substantially cheaper than what I could find elsewhere in the city.

“立地とお部屋からの眺めが素敵なホテル” ボストンのパブリック公園の目の前にあるホテルで、ボストンの市内中心部の観光をするのには、徒歩で可能だし、地下鉄で移動する場合にも最寄りの駅まで徒歩2~3分の距離にあるホテルで、立地はとても良い場所にあるホテルです。 またパブリック公園の目の前に建っているホテルですので、ガーデン側のお部屋を希望すれば、ホテルの部屋からは、緑が生い茂っている心が和む公園を眺めることができます。 公園のお隣にはボストンコモンがあり、フリーダムトレイルの出発点があり、トレイルに沿って歩いていけば、ボストンの色々な観光名所を巡ることができ、また公園の反対側のニューベリー通りの方へ歩くと、ジョン・ハンコック・タワーへも徒歩圏内で行くことができます。 こちらのタージホテルは、以前はリッツ・カールトンだったそうで、現地では「オールド・リッツカールトン」と呼ばれているホテルとか。 お部屋の広さも十分で落ち着いて過ごすことができましたが、バスルームは、バスタブ+シャワールームで、固定のシャワーだったので、そこだけがちょっと古さを感。 でもそれ以外は水回りも問題無く利用できました。

“Good for families but don't expect a good night's sleep” We stayed here last weekend for a wedding. We were in a studio suite which was in a courtyard sandwiched between two other suites. The night we arrived around 11 pm our neighbor who shared an adjoining door had his TV on so loud that we could hear ever single word the person on the tv was saying. There was no seal beneath the door so you could see the light of the tv and the shadows of the people walking back and forth. We called the front desk and asked them to have them turn the TV down and about half an hour later the volume was lowered but still kept us awake. The next morning we were awoken at 6:30 am by the neighbors on the other side of us in a yelling match. Once we finally got back to sleep after that, the TV on the other side of us from the night before was on again at full blast. This TV situation happened two nights in a row and we went to bed pretty late both nights. The decor of the rooms were very outdated and need to be redecorated - they look like they haven't been updated since the early 90s. It was great to have a kitchenette and washer and dryer and when we called housekeeping to ask for laundry detergent we got some right away, so that was a positive. The pool is awesome but for how many units they have at this resort they need to add another pool. The restaurant is also very outdated but the food was decent. The beds were comfortable but the bathrooms weren't super clean - I found a few hairs in the shower and on my towel. The wallpaper in the bathrooms also needs an update. A pamphlet in the room said we could get free newspapers at the front desk so I went there very early on Monday morning to pick one up and was told they were all out and I had to purchase one from the newspaper stand for $2 around the corner. The location is in a bad area of town in South Phoenix only about 8 miles from the airport; not close to any good shopping or nice restaurants. If you want to sit by the pool all day or golf and are not bothered by outdated rooms and large crowds at the pool, I would recommend this place, otherwise go elsewhere.
“A good solid place to stay” You should be pleased with you stay here. I always am.

“Really Amazing Location” I will admit to being a little weary of this hotel before we got there. We were traveling with our 16 and 8 year old sons through four cities (DC, Philly, NY & Boston) with only a couple of days in each city. Location was everything to us in every city and the location and price of this hotel was excellent. This is not the place to stay for people who are snobby about hotels. It is not a fancy place. But it is charming, affordable, located practically right in Times Square and perfectly acceptable for family travelers. Our room (#402) was bigger than I expected after reading various reviews. I'm giving this hotel a very good rating because it worked out perfectly for us. There are undoubtedly some downsides, but none of them overshadowed how glad we were to be in that location. The free internet service was awful and mostly didn't work and when it did, it was so slow it almost wasn't worth it. Neither of the beds in our room were comfortable and the pillows were terrible. One of the beds was actually almost collapsed. The elevators were sometimes a little scary. The air conditioner never actually cooled the room to anything a person would call cool. The hotel itself is a charming little building. We actually had a "view" of the street, so unlike some other reviewers, we were not looking at a wall or an alley. The location is just amazing. We enjoyed going to the Irish pub Connolly's right next door both for dinner with the family and for drinks later when the kids were in bed. There is a Starbucks right down the street and a fruit stand on the corner. Check in and check out was easy. Overall, I would certainly recommend this place to my more easy-going friends who wouldn't mind that it is not The Ritz.

“NICKELED AND DIMED - NOTHING SPECIAL” The Omni is a standard mildly upscale hotel, nothing special. The beds and pillows are fine, the rooms clean and conservative, and the staff nice is nice, albeit mildly inept. Here's what soured me on the place: The wifi in my room was spotty so I had to move to a less desirable location. Apparently routers are only on every other floor - they may want to correct this, it's pretty easy to do. The business center charges $28/hr for computer use (?!), an obscene fee I've never experienced at any hotel I've stayed at, usually it's free. The last straw was when they wanted to charge me $175 for accepting pre-paid packages I had shipped to the hotel. All they did was store them in a closet for a day. I refused to pay and they relented. There's lots of choices in downtown Indianapolis and you'd be wise to stay somewhere else. I cannot recommend this place --although clean and comfortable it left too many bad tastes in my mouth.
“客室は狭く、壁が薄い” 立地重視で宿泊したが、B級ホテル感は否めず。まずホテルエントランスが狭すぎて、ホテルを探すのに苦労した(ビルの勝手口のような入り口だった)。泊まった部屋は狭く、8畳一間にベッドが置いてある感じで、窓も小さく全体的に薄暗かった。それ以上に困ったのは壁の薄さ。隣の部屋の音が丸聞こえで、落ち着かなかった。

“Nice stay but not a value” We stayed here over the weekend, as it was the site for our conference. After reading the reviews about valet parking, we opted to self-park (very easy but expensive). Our room was on the 15th floor, dead center of the building, facing east and looking straight through the “window” of the office building across the street. (That is, the building’s design has a square “cut out” and you could look beyond to the mountains, with downtown to the southeast.) The spacious balcony was a great place to relax; our room was comfortable – the bed was incredibly comfortable; but the TV had very limited channels. Not even a decent cable TV package. The bathroom was nice but I couldn’t believe the sloppy glass tile job along the walls – wow, Hyatt paid for and allowed for this type of workmanship (or lack of)?! I am an early riser and had to wait with other guests for Starbuck’s to open downstairs (employees arrived late too). If the hotel doesn’t include coffeemakers as part of the room amenities, at the very least, they should have Starbuck’s open earlier than 6:00am (guests from the East Coast or abroad would agree). We had breakfast at Breeze out of convenience. We ordered the continental breakfast buffet (good) and off the menu (just okay). In general, the hotel was fine, the staff were all very courteous and professional, but the lack of amenities – not to mention paying to exercise at adjacent Equinox – is not worth staying at this particular hotel, considering other options in this part of LA.

“good location, so-so hotel” Stayed at the Hotel Pennsylvania for 3 nights for a conference in NYC. The location was great for the ease of transportation options but less great for noise, particularly on saturday night. I waited an hour to check in, but the staff were friendly and courteous. I enjoyed the vintage bathroom but the older beds and decor were a little depressing.

“Needs some work” Room service was quick, but the food was not very good, even for room service. My room was not cleaned properly - dirty towels weren't taken, or dirty towels were taken and then not replaced with clean towels. It was daylight savings time and no one bothered to change the clocks back, even days later. If it weren't so close to the Hynes Convention Center, I would have stayed at the Marriott.

“Excellent service but I miss the old bar” The Mark has been renovated to within an inch of its life; it's now very modern with lots of black and white and carrera marble. The old bar has been replaced with a standard, much smaller bar. I think this is a huge loss as the old bar had an old "club" feeling, but the drinks are still excellent. The rooms are very, very comfortable with lots of high tech gadgets. Service is excellent and the room service breakfast is one of the best I've had. The in-room bar is fabulous.

“Not great, but not bad” I was in Chicago with my daughter on a hot Sunday in July and needed a one-night stay downtown. So my wife booked this hotel online for us from home. She didn't have my AAA card number but was assured it could be taken care of at check-in. Well...at check-in I was told that nothing could be done about the rate and that I would have to pay the rack rate. Also, we were checking in at 5:00pm and our room still was not ready! We had to wait about an hour. The room was fine, although one of the remote controls was missing. Also, as with most Embassy Suites, it was pretty noisy, with children running around and looking over the balconies and such. But that was to be expected. So...although there really wasn't anything bad about our stay or about the hotel, I was entirely satisfied. I think there are better places to stay in Chicago, at least for me.

“Faded, wilted flower” I have been staying at the Arizona Biltmore for over 20 years. I love the location. I love the setting. I love the architecture and the sense of history. I even owned a condo on the Biltmore grounds for many years after opening my PHX office and so my wife and I often dinned at the property’s restaurants or used the spa when we were staying in the condo. But, I am sorry to see what is becoming of this once elegant, sophisticated property. My most recent stay for a short business trip will, unfortunately, be my last until the owners of this property start working to address its service and maintenance issues. It seems that the focus is on the transient conference attendee rather than the repeat high- end resort visitor or the independent business traveler. Some examples of poor serviced. On my last trip I arrived late. Though I am Hilton Gold the type of room I requested was not available. By the time the rather uncaring receptionist got the room issue fixed as best he could (which was not too good at all) it was nearing 10 p.m. Before going to my room I asked which restaurants would be open. He indicated that the café was open until 11. So, I went to my room, unpacked and then returned to the café at about 10:15 only to be told that they closed at 10 but that I could get a diverse selection at the bar. I went to the bar only to be told that the kitchen was closed. I pointed out that the bar menu indicated that serviced was until 11 and was told “Oh yeah – we have to fix those menus – we stopped serving until 11 some time ago. If you want something to eat you can go to your room and order room service.” All was delivered with a rather “not my problem” attitude. Good grief – all you can get at this “high end” resort after 10 p.m. is a limited room service menu. ‘Nuff said. The room itself was in sorry need of maintenance. Stained carpets, a rather unpleasant “these carpets have been here too long” smell which one also encounters in many of the hallways. Scratched furniture. And just a general feeling of boy, could this place stand a makeover – a big makeover. I had a drink from the mini-bar. We all know this is not the most economical way to have a drink but it is convenient and so we pay the $10+ for a jigger of whatever. Imagine my surprise on checkout that there was a “service fee” – I believe $2.50 – for using this item – not to mention tax. Now I don’t really care about $2.50. But the idea of being assessed a service charge for taking a small bottle out of the frig – well, really now – talk about nickel and dime. So, I’ll not be staying at the AZ Biltmore in the future – there are so many fine resorts to chose from in PHX. Pity – I really loved that property. I hope the owners will take note and rehabilitate this resort that has played such an important part in PHX hospitality history. I hope the Waldorf Astoria Resorts line will also take note. This property is no longer worthy of the brand.

“Fantastic combination of recent renovations in classy historic building!” Stayed for a few nights after reading about how this older hotel had recently undergone a full renovation - and how well liked it was by most visitors. I was not disappointed. My room was extremely usable and I highly recommend it to business travelers staying for a few days or more (the deluxe level room). It has a large walk-in closet and a very comfortable bathroom with a rarity these days - the bathroom had its own window. Combi tub/shower with excellent water pressure and nicely finished faucets. The room itself had a very comfortable bed and there was a dark wood center console in which was mounted a large flat screen TV with tons of cable channels. Free wireless internet is a lovely bonus and really should be included at all 5 star hotels - thank you to Stoneleigh for doing that right! I ate breakfast at the restaurant and was quite pleased with the gracious service; the food was also lovely (although hard to judge well by breakfast). I asked about the history of the hotel and if I could see some of the older areas in the penthouse, and the concierge took me for a 20 minute tour of the penthouse common areas as well as the two grand suites. If you are going for romance, you couldn't do better anywhere in Dallas than the presidential suite on the penthouse level (the one without the outdoor terrace). But the real deal is that for a 4-star price, you get 5-star quality and service in every room. And this hotel is a wonderful example of renovation gone right - a historic building made even better by having modern systems, modern bathrooms, and lovely finishes. The folks at the Stoneleigh have done very well, and I will happily look to stay here whenever in Dallas - choosing this hotel over even the Ritz-Carlton or the Rosewood hotels. I did not use the Stoneleigh Spa, but visited it to buy a gift for my wife - and the it looked quite welcoming; an added bonus!

“The best!” Wish I could give them 6 stars. We've stayed here twice for weekend getaways, traveling with our dogs on both visits. The staff truly couldn't be nicer--and not just the front desk staff, I mean *everyone* we've encountered. We saw lots of familiar faces on our 2nd visit, and some of the hotel staff remembered us too (or at least our dogs, who are pretty darn cute). For those who don't know, the Kimpton hotels are probably the most dog-friendly anywhere, and the Palomar Philly is especially welcoming. They even have a brunch in the warm weather months with a special doggy menu. (And yeah, that's ridiculous but it's a lot of fun and our pups loved every minute!) The rooms are lovely and very well kept; we had a spa king room on our last visit and the enormous bath was a nice luxury. We love this place and hope to return again and again--the wonderful staff really make it feel like home (except fancier and with room service)!
“Great Location” Great locacation but! Small rooms, tiny bathrooms. Small bed or beds, No coffee facilities. Lots of clean linen daily Long queues at reception. Expensive bar. Would not return.

“Quiet, clean, comfortable and very friendly service” I stayed for one night in January to attend an event at Cobo Hall (which is a short three-block walk from the hotel). The room was spacious, clean, and well-equipped. The bed was a bit too soft for me, but others may like it. The walls were solid -- I couldn't hear any noise from adjoining rooms or the hallway. The front desk staff was incredibly friendly, offering tips for my visit and ensuring that I had everything that I needed. I would definitely stay here again.

“lovely, clean and well run hotel” We stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott Downtown Baltimore arriving late into the evening. There is parking attached to the hotel (not included) and the elevator brings you right into the lobby. The Front Desk staff greeted us warmly and welcomed us to the hotel. I had requested adjoining rooms on a high floor which we were given and the rooms were very spacious and clean. We ate breakfast in the hotel and there was a very nice selection of food which was delicious, well presented and the staff was very nice, accommodating and anxious to please. I would recommend this property and return in the future.

“Westin NYC was excellent” We visited NYC over Labor Day weekend and stayed, for the first time, at Westin Times Square. We have stayed at several hotels in NYC including W, The Londoner, and Sofitel. Westin stacked up quite well. Our room had a view of the Hudson River and was on the 39th floor. It was very quiet. The bed was comfortable, the room was ample size, furniture in good condition, and the double showerhead was great. Also, the rooms come with a ipod docking station built into the stereo, so bring some tunes. The only disappointment was the fitness center & wi-fi were extra $$$. Can't complain though -- we received a AAA rate of $229/night. We flew into Newark, and found the Liberty Express Bus to be very economical ($25 roundtrip!), quick and comfortable. It drops you off less than one block from the Westin Times Square, at the Port Authority. Of course the location of the hotel is perfect for easy access to theatre, subway and is a nice jog away from Central Park. Also, plenty of Starbucks' nearby. In fact, the Starbuck's in the same building is open 24 hours, which was a nice, quick breakfast.

“We had a great stay!” We used Priceline and got the hotel for 4 nights for $85/night (over Memorial Day weekend). We were given a large two bed, two bath (tiny bathrooms) room w/a loveseat + coffee table. The location was FABULOUS (red line stop outside the door, orange line 1-3 blocks away depending on your destination) and the staff was super friendly and outgoing. Our room was cleaned very well and we would not hesitate to stay there again, in fact if we return to Chicago we'll hope we get this if we use Priceline again. It was a great stay for our family.

“Clean and attractive hotel, wonderful location” The son and I stayed here when he was visiting the University of Chicago. We arrived late evening and friendly Carolyn made our check-in easy and fast. She also was very helpful when I asked about transportation to the university, and we found it easily accessible via the Metra. The room was great: clean, spacious, attractively decorated with an eye for whimsy and featuring a gorgeous view of the river. The window seats, though a bit high off the ground, were wonderful, and one was the size of a small bed. The housekeeping staff was also really helpful during our stay, which was greatly appreciated. We found the hotel's location to be excellent for a walk to Millennium Park and other attractions. Definitely a recommended property; I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Easy place for business in Cambridge” Nice hotel on the Charles River. Located on a bridge, so you can easily get to Cambridge for work. Exit from parking lot puts you on an Eastbound highway, so you must go east to go west. (unless there is a simpler way)

“You'll be sad to leave!” We stayed at the Commonwealth for a long weekend for the Red Sox last regular season series - an annual tradition. However, this was the first time we stayed at the Commonwealth and we were very pleased. My review might be biased by the fact that it was some kind of nirvana for me to wake up in the morning and see Fenway Park outside of my window. But, I am a hotel dork (dork, snob, connoisseur...take your pick), so I'll try not to let my that cloud my assessment. The things you would expect to be exceptional for this level of hotel did not disappoint - comfortable bed, outstanding bedding that feels like silk, large bathtub with rainfall showerhead, quality bath products and, of course, a stocked minibar (for that ritual snickers and Heineken!). There was also a luxuriously large bathroom that allowed two people to get ready without bumping elbows and the restaurant (Eastern Standard) is quite a draw all on its own. We were eternally grateful they were still serving food at 1 a.m. when we finally arrived from the airport - a delightful gift of St. Christopher, the patron Saint of travelers. Everyone on the staff that we encountered was very nice and helpful. I needed to send some things back home which they cheerfully helped me with. The restaurant staff was great, and we never got that feeling like, "oh, you're just hotel guests." They treated us like regulars, but that could be because we spent a lot of time at the bar in between baseball games! The neighborhood is great. It just doesn't get easier to walk to the game, but it is really easy to walk down to the public garden, do some (window)shopping on Newbury St. or pop over to Copley Place. The green line is right outside the door to Eastern Standard if you don't feel like walking to the North end (we do, but we walk a lot). Overall, this is a great hotel...whether you decide to venture no further than your room or make it your base from which to explore the city.

“Great inexpensive hotel” 6 ladies stayed in 2 double rooms at this hotel for 2 nights before a cruise out of NYC. We had absolutely no complaints. 1 room overlooked the pool and was very quiet and the other on the 5th floor overlooked the street but we didn't find the street noise bad. Safe & clean. Walking distance to everything we wanted to see. Evangaline in gift shop made arrangements for a van to take us to our cruise and saved us about $50. Unless you really want to pay "big bucks" for a fancy hotel, stay here. We will again.

“Nice hotel. Very friendly staff.” Just stayed here for two nights on a business trip. Upgraded to club floor (12th floor). Club lounge offered free beer and wine at night. Concierge helped me map out a 6 mile run along the river walk and thru town. Rented a car for the day from the Marriott river center just a few blocks away (hertz). $20 cab ride from airport to hotel. Staff was very nice everywhere I went in the hotel.

“Quality, but no personality” I stayed here 3 times between November and January on business. The rooms are comfortable, clean and tasteful. They also are reasonably quiet, despite the fact that you are in Times Square. The staff is courteous and professional, and they run this behemoth hotel like a well-oiled machine. Even when the hotel is crowded, I never have had to wait to check in. The breakfast buffet was absurdly overpriced, but excellent, especially if you are on an expense account. Same for the room service. However, like the crowds outside in Times Square, the crowds inside the hotel can be overwhelming. If you are trying to get into or out of the place during a peak hour at a peak time of year, prepare to cram yourself into an elevator with the masses to get to the lobby. At or near full capacity, this hotel has a population that exceeds many small towns. Because everything is on such a large scale, the hotel felt impersonal. If you are looking for a hotel with charm or personality, look elsewhere.

“Centrally Placed Delight!” I arrived at an un-earthly hour of 07:00 after my flight from São Paulo arrived at Newark at 05:15. I asked if I could check in and leave my bags with Concierge and was told yes (Check-in is for 16:00 on the day and check-out is at 11:00), but we don't have your room ready but we have another free if you'd care for it. Thanks I said, and went up to the room to shower and change. How many hotels would be so kind as this? Effectively, I got an extra half day at the place for free! I was here to see New York and didn't want to stay in my room. The room was a very nice size, clean with all the creature comforts that I needed and was on the 25th floor, overlooking Lexington Avenue, in the shadow of The Chrysler Building. Grand Central Terminal was below, what more could I want to explore the city. I had a great two days in New York and got to see so much from base at the Grand Hyatt. It's position is so central that you can easily get anywhere from here, either on foot (my preferred mode of transport in New York) or by Subway/Bus/Cab. I would recommend staying at the Grand Hyatt without any hesitation, it has all that you need for a great stay.

“Good option for overnight stay” Pros: - Convenient access to airport - Modern, clean rooms - Good gym Cons: - Limited nearby food options - Thin walls/noise It's a pretty lengthy and somewhat confusing walk from the far terminals if you don't want to take a shuttle. Still, for a short stay in the city, you can't beat the convenience of being on airport property. The room was modern, clean and smelled fresh. I also had a nice view of the harbor. The walls are thin though, so you will hear every noise in the hallway- talking, drunks laughing, doors closing, etc. The gym was large, nice and fairly well-equipped, except that for some reason it lacked a water dispenser, and instead had a fountain that was kind of gross... I would recommend bringing your own water. Your nearby food options are limited, but they do have a shuttle to the subway. If you are visiting the city on vacation, I would probably look for something closer to downtown. For overnight or brief business travel, this is a convienent option. Overall, this was a very good experience and I would stay here again.

“Great Price and Great Location” This was our second stay at the Hacienda, but it has been a couple of years since our last stay.We had a queen bedroom on the Plaza level. It had a microwave and refrigerator and free wifi. We paid $109 a night for 2 nights. Breakfast was included but it was nothing special and I would not go out of my way to have breakfast included. The property is lovely and the room was not very spacious but it was very clean and the bed was extemely comfortable. The best part was the free transportation to and from the airport and the cruise ship port. We would stay there again . We ran into a couple that could not get room issues regarding faulty plumbing and other issues resolved. I think there needs to be a little more participation by management in getting issues resolved while the customer can still be placated. The front desk staff seems to lack any authority or confidence to correct problems in a timely manner. Just an observation

“Great service” I have stayed at this hotel a few times, and normally have average or sub-par service. BUT, I am glad they have all new people working the front desk. Omar is a super nice guy, and really good at running the front desk. He makes people feel right at home. As far as the hotel itself, I don't really agree on paying $22 a night for parking (valet only), so that means it will cost you more with tips. Also, there is a sign in the bathroom if you use any of the towels to remove make-up or clean your shoes, there can be up to a $35 charge. Really? I was in hotel management and know what hotels pay for towels, and I can tell you, it is about $2 a towel. Sounds really petty to me. It is an oddly laid out hotel, if you are on floors 6, 7 or 8 - you will need to go to the 5th floor, make two turns and go up another elevator. Strange

“Uncomfortable Beds” The standard design of the Amerisuites rooms is efficient (half wall separating sitting area/ kitchenette from bedroom/ bath area with tv viewable from both areas). The staff was friendly upon check-in. Our internet worked just fine. However, we found the beds to be very uncomfortable (lots of springs in your back). The room needed an update (worn looking carpeting). And the free breakfast was marginal at best. Finding the hotel upon leaving the airport was no easy adventure either. There are other hotel options that would have been far more convenient to IAH (with restaurants closer by). Still, our Entertainment rate of only $53 a night made this hotel a bargain!

“Great location for 5th Ave and Central Park” This location is great for the theater, central park and 5th avenue shopping.Although not huge, rooms are clean, contemporary and well featured with great showers. No on-site lounge or restaurant but options abound within walking distance. Desk staff was very attentive and helpful with directions and even offered an umbrella on a rainy night.

“excellent location, OK hotel for business stay” Excellent central locatoin with restaurants and shopping a short drive away. The hotel is very old and shows its age. I didn't see any activity in the hotel restaurant. The room was tired but OK. There was mold and discolortaion on various surfaces in the bathroom. The bathroom had a very low ceiling due to an access hatch that was in the ceiling for some reason. Check-in and Check-out process were OK. Parking was free and convenient. Although this property looks very intriguing from the outside with it's gold reflective glass, the inside is nothing special. Overall, it's an OK place for an overnight stay for a business traveler.

“Noisy!! and Special Request for Adjoining Rooms Unfulfilled” Perhaps this rating is overly harsh, however I consider the ability to sleep essential to any hotel experience. This hotel, despite a great location, considerable charm in the common areas for the price, and a delicious breakfast, did not provide a decent night's sleep. Several months ago, my 4 newly or nearly 40 year-old friends and I booked two suites for a reunion weekend in San Antonio. At the time we made the reservation we were told that special requests for adjoining rooms were "nearly always honored." (And, in fact, we paid a higher rate for the room - - $209 a night - -by booking adjoining suites directly with the hotel than we could have found online, where we couldn't guarantee adjoining rooms.) When we arrived, we were told there were no adjoining rooms available and we were put on the same floor instead. If that wasn't bad enough, at about 3:30 am on the first night we were awakened by wretching and groaning from the poor stranger in the adjoining room who apparently "drank the water" - -or too many margaritas - - in Mexico that day. Because there is no insulation between the rooms, It sounded like he was in our bathroom. This, unfortunately for him and us, continued off and on all night long. In the morning, we complained and were moved to another room for the remaining 2 nights. This new room, likewise, had paper thin walls (as did the second room for our goup). Allthough nobody was throwing up in the room next door, we could still hear our neighbors talking at normal volume - -and our friends could hear their neighbors as well. (And I'm sure our neighbors could hear us!) I would not recommend this hotel to others unless they were deaf.

“Great location for an overnight business trip.” The hotel is new, clean and efficient. Staff are pleasant and helpful. Short walk through the Philadelphia Convention Centre to get to Walnut, Chestnut, Market Streets. Steps to the Reading Market for a great breakfast or lunch. Rooms are standard, LCD TV is good and there's a nice big shower. Typically annoying Sheraton low-level lighting in the bathroom so close detailing of those chiselled features may be challenging. Why doesStarwood do this in their newer hotels...I want my bathroom bright or at least with the capability to make it bright. If you're working late and need something to eat late they do have a decent-looking room service menu until 10:00PM. Otherwise Chili's, Maggiano's are about a block away. Bar is adequate and friendly. Free wifi in a Starwood property is unexpected these days and great. Would definitely use this hotel again at $155.

“good chicago hotel at the right price” We normally stay at another competitor in Chicago. There was an unusually good special so we decided to try the Peninsula. We had a 1 BD suite. Views in this hotel are not as good as the FS where we we usually stay but we did have a nice view of Water Tower, and a little bit of the lake. Main bathroom is a little small, suite had low ceilings and the TV was outdated. Our mini-bar was not refilled during our stay once....no diet sodas after the first day. The restaurants were empty or having special events during our stay, so even though we were offered a discount we could not use it and try them. Hotel was nice enough to credit toward the stay. Concierges were very good at getting basic info, though they push the restaurant of a former chef that we thought was a poor suggestion. The bar is old school but really smells of smoke even though it is non-smoking. The pool/ spa is nice. The location is central Michigan Ave near the major dept. stores. I would return only if I found a great deal again.

“It's a convention hotel” The Grand Hyatt is large and fairly impersonal. The South tower is older and the rooms are smaller (although management swears this is not true, but it is. I moved from one suite in the North Tower to a "larger" and more expensive one in the south Harbor Tower and it is significantly smaller.) The southern view, however, is much better if you are on the outside of the building, and there is less noise and street traffic. The rooms are okay, but lack some of the amenities touted on the website and some things show lack of attention to detail... (non-working desk phones in both of the rooms I had makes me wonder if that is a coincidence or the norm). It seems the recession has slowed business down and a staff member told me that renovations are being deferred until business picks up again. The location is nice, although the touristy Seaport Village that surrounds the place seems mostly closed due to the economy and time of year. The food is very good. We ate in Sally's Seafood on the Water and it was quite a delicious lunch. The restaurant, however, was empty. Going to try Top of the Hyatt on the 40th floor tonight and see how that is. Impressive lobby and first floor. The rooms are pretty much standard-issue Hyatt. Fast elevators, which is nice, although this is hardly full occupancy, so I guess that is not a good time to determine elevator speed. The owner was a vocal supporter of Prop 8 in California and that has prevented some groups and conventions from staying at the hotel. Possibly that explains the lack of business as compared to the much more bustling hotels in the area. Overall, it is fine. Good location, near the airport, water views, within walking distance to most business traveler needs. I have stayed in several other hotels in this neighborhood, and liked them more, although this quite sufficient....

“Do not stay there even if you are desperate.” We booked a double hotal room, arrived late to find it was a small air tight box 1.2m x 2m x 1.2m ceilings. There was not enough room to close the door once you put one suitcase in the room. There was no air, no amenitied of any kind except one bed with a used sheet and wet towel screwed up in the small cupboard. Management would not come and check and told us it had been cleaned. They then charged another $22.95 to upgrade to a room where you could at least get inside the room. Wifi did not work. There is no lift and rooms are on 5th floor. Do not stay here.

“Best hotel on Chicago and we have stayed at several!!” Great location! Close to navy pier and michigan ave. We stayed with our 5 year old. They have a guppy program where they will bring a goldfish to your room! Huge hit! Also brought a kids robe and a kids gift bag! Also the hotel offers a free wine tasting at 5. Chipolte is across the street an mcdonalds is close too. Room was very spacious And the pool was great too!

“Absolutely fantastic” The hotel claims to be a 'home away from home' - they're wrong about that - it's much better. Although it markets itself for longer stays, we booked in for 2 nights while traveling the East Coast. Arriving very early in the day so we could explore Philadelphia the hotel took care of our bags and when we returned to check in properly the hotel had already moved our bags to our room. This is a very simple thing to do but so many hotels fail to do this. The hotel sits on the corner of Rittenhouse Square, between two of the main shopping roads in Philadelphia. This was my first visit to Philadelphia and the city surpassed my expectations. Within short walking distance of the hotel were many good restaurants. It's a lively, vibrant city and the hotel is a short walk from all of the central attractions including the Liberty Bell and Reading Market. Pleasantly the hotel had upgraded us to a 2 bedroom suite and the suite was beautiful. The suite comprised of 2 well sized bedrooms, both ensuite, a good size livng area, a dining room with table suitable to seat 6, a fully fit kitchen with 3rd bathroom of it. Full HD cable set up was available with free high speed wifi. In truth the suite had more floor space than my house. In fact the only downside of the suite was that we didn't want to leave it. All this for less than the cost of a standard sized New York hotel room. While there we did see a standard room and these were very good sized too. The stay itself at the hotel was quite eventful. On the morning of our second day contractors cut an electric cable outside the hotel leaving the hotel without power. This drama, on what must have been a very trying day, was dealt with by the hotel staff with poise and patience. They were incredibly accomodating going out of the way to ensure that this did not spoil my stay and kept me up to date with events by telephone while I was away from the hotel. This hotel has raised the bar for accomodation and any other hotel is going to have to be really special to top it.
“リーズナブル” 立地はまずまず、眺めも高層階だったので良いと思います。ただ、窓が防音ではないので少しうるさいです。建物は古く豪華ではありません。

“Sleep 101 -- Go back to school” While the Hilton Indianapolis North is a nice, clean, updated hotel located within a few miles of TONS of great shopping and dining, the hotel fails in what should be its prime objective...SLEEP! My husband and I stayed for a nice, weekend getaway. We booked through Priceline, so I really didn't have a choice for the hotel, but the price we paid was very good. We requested a king room, which they were able to accommodate even though the hotel was completely booked for all kinds of sporting events. There was a college basketball team there, as well as, what seemed to be HUNDREDS of kids for some kind of soccer tournament. Anyway, our room was very satisfactory. It was spacious, clean, and everything seemed to be in working order. No complaints. Then we heard teenagers goofing off in the hall. I thought they'd move on, but they didn't. Pretty soon, I heard music playing outside my door, so I opened the door and went out. There were three teenaged girls just sitting around on the floor outside my room. One licking a sucker, one playing a radio and the other just standing there. I didn't say a word, I just looked at them like, "Why are you guys sitting outside my door?" One of the girls obviously read minds, so she offered, "We're just sitting here waiting for someone in 'that' room." She pointed to the door next door to mine. I just walked back into my room without saying a word, but thankfully, they got the point and moved along. All weekend, there were kids running up and down the hallways. I don't blame the kids or the hotel...this is just irresponsible parenting (there were parents everywhere, too). Anyway, my room was nice enough, other than the obvious, and even with the noise, I was still okay with the hotel...until it was time to go to bed. The bed feels soft and squishy, which at first feels okay, but me AND my husband woke up stiff and achy in the middle of the night! Also, the A.C. doesn't cool well enough. There is scientific PROOF that the ideal sleeping temperature for the human body is 64 degrees F. I can't stand it when hotel A/C units don't function well. If you are the type of person who likes it COLD when you sleep (like me), get ready to sweat. Plus, the bedding was VERY warm, so the room really needed to be much cooler for comfort. My husband doesn't like it as cold as I do, but even he was hot. He completely took the covers off himself. So between the soft mattress, warm down bedding, and the warm room, we were pretty miserable at night. Which is too bad because this could be a great hotel. They need new mattresses and cooler bedding and/or better A/C units. They have a restaurant downstairs that is pretty decent. An indoor pool. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The location is near two Indianapolis shopping malls, and dozens of restaurants. It's also about 30 minutes from a casino off I-69, if you like to gamble. Parking is also FREE which is a huge plus! If I got this place for a great price (like I did), I'd probably be okay with it again, but I would not pay rack rate for this place. No way. Too many other hotels around to be miserable.

“Very Nice” We only stayed one night, but was very impressed with the service. I love good service. Front desk was friendly and helpful, as were the door men. We had happy hour in the bar Food was innovative, good and quick. Told the wait would be 20 minutes, went up to our room, came back down and maitre'd spotted us and lead us to a nice couch. Finished in time to attend a show at Jazz Alley. Nice job Hotel Monaco.

“Great Location, Great Rooms” Stayed here for 5 nights from June 5 -June 9. We booked through the hotel web site and got a great deal. It appears that the only problem here is the check-in staff. We had reserved a room the same day that our friends had reserved their room, we chose the same catagory and requested in the comments that we be placed on the same floor near each other. When we checked in we were on two different floors. This was handled quickly and changed so we could be near eachother. This is not a big deal at all however, the employee that checked me in was quite rude and either inexperienced or just didn't care. The employee that checked our friends in was quick and friendly and resolved the issue. Our check in was pretty quick, about 15 minutes, however this hotel caters to the airlines it seems and there was always a large amount of flight crews there. Numerous days we saw check-in lines at least 20 deep and only 2-4 employees working. We heard numerous people complaining about waiting over an hour to check in. So only problem seems to be the check in. We had a room on the 27th floor with amazing views of the city. There was noise in the room but what do you expect when you are in the middle of a large city. We heard police sirens all night long but once again what do you expect! The room was amazingly clean and we always had turndown service with a chocolate and the next days weather left on our bed. This was wonderful. The shower had awesome water pressure and it seems that they are still using the Marriott soaps and shampoos. Our room included free breakfast and afternoon snacks. The breakfast was simple but great. Always had free juice, water, and soda. There was always fresh bread and some pastries. There was meat to make a sandwich and lots of cereal with fresh fruits.
