The afternoon snacks were not bad. We only went up there twice, once was chicken wings which were ok and the next time there were little pizzas. I thought that alcohol was included in the afternoon snack but it isn't, they have an honor bar. The workout facility at the hotel is not bad. An area of barbells and a couple multi exercise machines. Several treadmills. Nice towels to stay clean and that have a steamroom. THe only thing that is missing is no pool or hot tub. The hotel location is awesome. I would say the best around. You walk out the front door and take about 100 steps to the cable car, or BART. The booth to buy the MUNI tickets is right there at the cable car so just wait and buy it there. You are within a block of all the major shopping stores and walgreens and what not. Parking is expensive, $40.00 per day plus and extra $5.60 per day tax but it is very nice to have your car safe and right there at the hotel. THe valet employees were excellent, friendly, and brought the car very quickly. IF you are debating between fishermans wharf area and union square area, do union square because there is nothing to do at fishermans wharf. This is the first time staying in the city and when I come back, I will only stay at the Parc 55 hotel. The stay was wonderful!

“Great Hotel - But Meeting Space a little Cramped” The Indy JW Marriott is a great hotel and certainly warrants an excellent rating. The lobby and rooms are modern and in great/new condition. The JW is decorated in a very "contemporary" style so if you like conservative/traditional styling you may prefer the Conrad. The exercise facilities are very nice at the JW - lots of machines and no waits. Dining at the formal Italian restaurant was a great experience - delicious food but expect slightly small portions. I was staying at the JW for a small conference - our group had about 30 people and I felt the room was too narrow for our size. However, everything else about the conference was great - meals were especially good during the day. For a high-end hotel in Indy, you can't go wrong with the JW Marriott.

“Finally......a Hyatt that gets Customer Service Right” I had previously stayed at this hotel last year when they were in the midst of their renovation but decided to come back after the renovation was complete due to a points offer for GoldPassport members. My previous experience was okay with just middling service from the staff and nicely redecorated rooms that were comfortable but not spectacular. Both times I received a "partial" ocean view or "Marina" view I think is what they call it. As others have said the pool area is nice but definitely meant for families and kids. There is a nice bar area near the pool and a highly rated restaurant (Red Marlin) on the grounds but I never took advantage of them due to the price. If you feel up to walking, Mission Beach is about a 20-30 minute walk west of the hotel (or 5 minute drive) where you'll find plenty of restaurants and nightlife (parking is difficult there so I usually walk---besides, you've already paid $20). There is also a seafood restaurant next door that has more reasonable prices but is also more "divey" looking. Rooms are comfortable with the Hyatt Grand Bed but beware if you're a light sleeper with a marina-facing room as on both occasions I was able to hear the seals barking even at night. My biggest surprise here though was the massive improvement in customer service. I'm not sure if they got a new GM or just better training but I was very impressed with the friendliness, smiles and genuine willingness to help provided by the staff. At check-in, I chatted with a nice young lady who genuinely seemed to be happy to be working there. If you've ever stayed at the Hyatt in Irvine or Orange County, you'll see a marked difference in the staff (especially among the sour/dour Irvine staff). Even when passing by maint. or housekeeping staff, they acknowledge you and smile and sometimes joke with you making you feel at home and relaxed. I only wish that Hyatt would transfer this to most of their other properties as this is what customer service should be for this level of a hotel. Let's just hope that this Hyatt can maintain it going forward........

“Awesome Westin” Stayed at this hotel for only one night on a day trip into Boston. The hotel is so big and the rooms are really spacious. The staff are very helpful and there's a bar in the lobby with seating area which is a great way to start the night with a few drinks before heading out. The bathroom is one of the cleanest bathrooms I've ever seen. The shower has two heads and the soap products are not harsh for your skin at all! The bed was really comfy, best night sleep! Can't complain about this hotel at all.

“Better than the average Embassy Suites” I am not a fan of Embassy Suites (except for the one in Bogota, Colombia, which is outstanding). Commonly they are big, noisy (and often smelly) barns, often with screaming children running up and down the halls and scruffy people in line for free popcorn (or such) and free low-quality drinks. Breakfasts are usually "by the pound" (a lot of low quality bulk & fat). Rooms are marginally comfortable, and sleeper sofas are unfit for sitting and severely unfit for sitting). For family budgets, they are great (if not essential) -- the included breakfast saves $10/person from a travel expense. For business travel, they usually suck. However, THIS Embassy Suites, perhaps because it is adjacent to a freeway, in the midst of an office park, and of a less cavern-like design, is clearly different. The staff are friendly & efficient. The breakfast was better than average. And the rooms are more quiet than most other Embassy Suites. Significantly, the price is quite affordable, especially considering it includes the morning meal. Receiving Hilton points is a real plus, and the proliferation of Hilton brands makes it easy to accumulate what they call Hhonors points (and Hhonors rewards). The free parking is also a sanctuary from the latest gouging tactics of even suburban hoteliers. This is a good hotel, well-managed, and surprisingly appealing for the business traveler. I will stay here again, if I'm in the area.

“Lousy Location but decent rooms” This hotel has tiny rooms and the carpets don't look as clean as they should, the lobby is also small but what bothers me most is the location of the place. You walk outside and you feel like you can't possibly be in NYC. The place outside the doors is super smelly and dirty. Not a great place for you to ask guests to meet you or to feel that you can wander and locate great eateries close by either. The rates are also costly so for a better location and cheaper sleeps maybe try somewhere else.

“Great Hotel....” We loved it! Large Retro rooms w/ nice view from the upper floors. Plus FREE bike's to use! We spent all morning biking down to the water-front and along the Seattle bike-path. Its a 15-20 min. bike ride to the water-front w/ a few busy intersections; but once you get down to the water-front its really a great way to see the city. Coming back is slightly up-hill. And the restraurant just down the block from the hotel (The Portage) is Fantastic. In fact, the Portage does a FREE wine sampler in the hotel eatting area a few nights a week. They also serve tasty appetiziers which we made a meal out of.... FYI: Once you are down-town, on bikes, it's a 1 or 2 block walk uphill to see the Pikes People Market. Lock the bikes up where everybody else does.... Great Breakfast here too! Plus they offer a FREE "cart" service. ie" We wanted more books to read, at the end of our trip, so they sent up the "Book Cart" which had like 20 books and we swapped out a few. They have a video cart, a computer cart, a kids cart---etc....15 different carts.

“Not so bad, not so good” This is a plain old motel, with pretensions. You will be hard pressed to find better at the price near to the middle of Boston, and they have parking and a shuttle service to the nearest T station. If you need a place to stay, as I did, it will work. The shuttle to the T runs on time and the drivers make an effort to be sure that people running from the station either get on, or are assured that another shuttle will be along soon. All in all, getting into downtown is fairly easy and doesn't take too long. I wish that the quoted price simply included the shuttle cost...they add it on to the room cost whether you use it or not, so they might as well just put it on the room price in the first place. My room had a typical low cost hotel disinfectant smell that, as a person with low tolerance for chemical smells, I found barely tolerable. Otherwise the room was clean. The neighborhood is not the best, but not the worst. I was not worried about my car in the parking lot. I don't like that the supposedly secure doors into the hallways leading to the rooms are not secured (I walked in and out of a couple of them without having to use my key card). I would make sure that my door is locked at night. The Deadwood Cafe and Brewery next door is not a place that I would want to hang out in, mostly because there is no there there. I wanted to enjoy a good beer in a nice pub atmosphere, but it is a bowling alley. What's worse is that I have had good times in some bowling alley bars, but I can't imagine having a good time in this one. I didn't even sample the beer, the place was so unappealing. On the other hand, having a bowling alley/pool hall next door might be good for some people, and that part of the establishment looked appealing, especially if you are travelling with young people. I will likely stay there again. I will hold my nose.

“Luxury hotel at a great price” We stayed one night at this hotel and found it very comfortable. The beds were huge, the bathroom had both a shower and a bath tup, and the mini bar included all kinds of things that you could possibly need. The staff was friendly and the dinner we had at the hotel restaurant Noé was quite good. The truffle butter is fantastic! The hotel has a pool area, but is seemed that it was shady most of the time. We paid USD 179 +tax for one night which is not expensive at all for a hotel like this.

“close to everything downtown Austin” I stayed here for a meeting for 2 nights. They are currently remodeling. My room was remodeled--very contemporary with lots of pillows, flat screen TV and reminded me a bit of a Westin (including the catalog in the room where you can order everything in the room if you like it that much.) They are still working on the patio by the lake and the lobby. They told me the cowboy mural behind the registration desk (that has been there the 15 years that I have been going to the hotel) is coming down for a more modern look. I didn't eat there so I can't comment about the food. The cleaning staff seemed to do a good job. Lotions and potions are the usual Hyatt stuff. The best part of the hotel is the room's huge windows that look out on Town Lake (if you can get on the north side); they offer a great view as you look north onto downtown Austin.

“Excellent Value for the Area” I selected this hotel due to the rate being approx $200 - $250 cheaper than other hotels, even a Hampton Inn. I was impressed with what I received. Service was good. My room was a nice size, quiet and comfortable. I am heading back to NYC in Feb and will certainly check out this hotel again.

“fabulous hotel and fabulous location” I have stayed here twice now and cannot fault at all - everything has been thought of and the service is superb. I love the location on Ghiradelli Square with a great view out across Bay and Alcatraz. The hotel provides everything you want. There are quite a few restaurants around but the hotel has a house car which will drop you off at other locations close by.

“We enjoyed our stay” The lobby and public areas are as interesting as I had been lead to believe in all the previous reviews. I even stepped into the empty Crystal Room to look around. This is the room that was used for the Academy Award ceremonies in the old days. On our morning of departure the room was closed with a sign stating movie filming in progress please do not disturb. Our room was adequate. The queen bed was comfy and the bathroom plumbing worked okay. The TV was small. The odd thing about the room is there was no dresser to put clothes in. There was a huge walk in closet with only about 8 hangers. I used the ledge of the closet for my folded clothes. There were a few small shelves in the TV unit that my companion used. There was also a safe in the TV unit. The room was large, so there was plenty of space to add a dresser. The bathroom was also very small, not uncommon for old hotels, but frustrating because of the wasted space in the room and the walk in closet. We could hear people talking in the hallway, but it was not a big issue because we were at the end of the hallway in Room 368 and not many people walked by. If you were closer to the elevators you might be more bothered by noise in the hallways. Of course, the hallways are very long, so the downside of being at the end is you have a long walk from the elevator to the room. We had the buffet breakfast at Smeraldis in the hotel. The cost was $ 20.00, not bad since it includes coffee and juice. Menu offerings were around $ 15.00 without drinks. The buffet included made to order omelets, fresh fruit and some very yummy pastries among other offerings. Try a chocolate croissant. If you want a lighter breakfast walk to 6th street, on the side of the hotel between Olive and Grand. There is a bagel place plus another coffee shop. There is also a convenience store in that block. We did not find the area around the hotel very intimidating, even after dinner at night. There are homeless people, and a few asked for money, but most just minded their own business. The subway station is just a block away and was convenient to get to Hollywood. We also used the Dash bus to get to China Town. The concierge in the hotel gave me a Dash map. I enjoyed wandering around downtown, the ST. Vincent Jewelry Center, Angels Flight and Grand Central Market were all worth a visit. If you want a good happy hour place try the Weiland Brewery a block from the Hotel at 505 S Flower. Just cross Grand and walk past the library from the hotel, cross Flower and take the escalator one flight down to Weiland. They had cheap beer and wine and we mixed with some local Angelinos there. There were enough people walking around at night that the area did not seem as intimidating as some may lead you to believe. We past all sorts of interesting restaurants and bars as we walked.

“Happy wiht the Holiday Inn Express” I initially booked 2 nights at this hotel, due to speaking at an Educational Conference. The hotel was SO quiet and COMFORTABLE, that I stayed a third night. I spend 75 plus nights per year in hotels and am thrilled when I have a good night's rest because the hotel is QUIET. I even chatted with the front desk about this concept and was told that they screen their large groups to make sure there is a responsible adult that will ensure the children will get into their rooms and not run wild. I was SO impressed! They certainly recognize their business clients. I had a paper on my door every morning and used the business center and the laundry facilities....super! There are quite a few restaurants within 3-5 miles and also a FED EX and Post Office...perfect for shipping! I WILL stay here again...thanks so much! Oh. they also have a Wednesday night BBQ ....FREE!

“Elegantly Modest, Comfortable, and So Worth Experiencing” My extended family and I were in Boston to attend a college graduation and occupied four rooms. We stayed for five days and are completely delighted with the experience (except the restaurant which was mediocre at breakfast, service was good, food not really). Part of me wonders if any of the tepid reviews about the size and quality of the rooms caused me to go in with lowered expectations. But having stayed there for five days I feel that the hotel is very well managed. The rooms are comfortable and well appointed; the staff is attentive and caring. When the doorman saw, for example, that I was headed for the elevator, he pressed the “up” button for me. I was greeted with “good morning” but only when I made eye contact, otherwise my privacy was respected. The internet is $9.95 a day but I didn’t pay because I enrolled in their rewards program online (free of charge and qualifies you for free internet access). We booked our rooms through Priceline and didn’t get any inkling of second class service that others have commented on. If you are educated, especially in the social sciences/liberal arts area, you will find the experience staying here glorious, surrounded as it is with so many artifacts of our nation’s historic past. I call this place elegantly modest because as richly appointed as it is, there isn’t the slightest hint of snootiness about it and it welcomes all kinds of guests, there was even a family who took out dominos and sat at a table in the lobby to play a game. Shopping, dining, theater, pubs, whatever you want, it’s all within quick distance and usually best in class (definitely go to Sam Lagrassas, best sandwiches, Google it and see, it’s just around the corner, so good that they are only open from 11am to 3:30pm M-F). I'm a professional in my late 30's and I took my senior-aged parents who sometimes liked to wander off on their own and I felt comfortable knowing there were so many places within a short walk that they could sit at for hours to drink coffee, people watch, or just read (e.g. Irish famine memorial park, Bruegger's, Starbucks, Borders café, or, their favorite, the hotel lobby). Very close by is a CVS, 7-11 for any of those runs for food and sundries that are part of every good vacation.

“Great Staff !” Stayed here in June for 2 nights . From the moment we checked in the staff at the front desk were amazing . We were given a room on the second floor and when we woke up in the morning our bathroom door wouldn't open . We'd placed all our toiletries in there the night before and were unable to retrieve them . After calling reception they sent up a service man who eventually got the door open . The front desk then organized for us to be ugraded to the 18th floor with amazing views of the Empire state building and as we were heading out to explore NYC made sure all our belongings and luggage were waiting for us in our new room when we returned . The room itself was excellent . Very clean and the bed was extremely comfortable . Strong WiFi in the room too. The location is ok . Subway lines on the corner and some pretty cool restaurants close by too .

“Not the best place I've ever stayed at” Stayed here for one night on my way to University of Texas - Austin. While the university is a mere 5-6 minutes drive to the campus, the motel is nothing special. Rooms are basic (and clean). Wi-fi is available in all rooms at a small fee (2.99 usd for 24h). While the motel is not bad, it's nothing special as well. I was waken up at around 1 am by my noisy neighbors, and a series of frightening screams creeped me out a bit... Let's say I wouldn't recommend this place and area in general to women who travel alone. All in all, an ok place, especially ok given the under 50 USD rate you can get on motel6.com website.

“best place to stay near Central Park” We stayed in this hotel for four nights. It's an excellent location when you like midtown Manhattan and don't mind some street noise. Our room was spacious and we liked the magnetron, coffee maker and the fridge very much. The hotel is not glamourous or luxurious but very comfortable and clean and the staff were friendly. I checked several other hotels in the neighborhood before booking, but there is no other hotel that offers so much for such a reasonable price.

“Great stay for a special occasion” We stayed here once before several years back and enjoyed it. This time really enjoyed it also. We walked everywhere and so the location is perfect. We left the car at the valet when checking in. The room was nicely done. Compared to most hotels it was very quiet - which was so great because i wake up to every noise. Tv was a large flat screen and there is an iPod docking station. When booking online I shared that we were celebrating my husbands birthday and so they made some gestures that were very thoughtful - at checkin they gave us a thing for 4 free local beers that they brought to our room. When we got back from dinner they had left champagne and a fruit and cheese plate. Some very nice touches that were appreciated. We really enjoyed our stay and will come back.

“Comfy beds, mixed service, broken (and expensive!) wi-fi” In town for a big conference, and as we all know with conferences, you truly are at the mercy of when you book your hotels to get the best. This isn't the closest to the conference center nor is it the nicest, and I got mixed service. Some folks were extremely kind and nice, including the bagel shop attendant and gift shop attendant, but I received some of the rudest service by the front desk attendant and I called the manager on duty at the time to let them know they may want to give the gentleman a break of some sort as he appeared very upset and never received a call back to at least know I was acknowledged. The rooms are great and I like the touches of the shower pouf, but the wireless, as others mentioned, is really just unacceptable. Not only is it expensive, but it was unreliable. I tried purchasing three times and it charged my credit card but did not work and when I called to inquire, I was told it was the vendor's fault and I had to walk to the convention center to get wireless. The manager must realize that often times conference-goers and business people don't have time to go set up shop in "The Link" business center. Parking is also atrociously priced-- take the bus if you can.

“Great hotel and great service” I recently stayed at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge for a conference. I was there for 3 nights. The hotel is very nice! The common areas were nicely decorated and there were plenty of seating areas. The rooms were well appointed. The beds are very comfortable and the bathrooms were a great size, with separate tubs and marble shower stalls. I only wish the tub was a soaking tub! There was also a nice balcony with a table and chairs, overlooking the putting green and some outside seating. One of the best things about this hotel is the service! Everyone was very professional and very courteous. Even under the pressure of serving that many people (over 1000) lunch at the same time, the service staff always came through with a smile. The shuttle to the mall across the street was very helpful. The only problem I had with service was with a young girl at the front desk. She didn't seem to know what she was doing and wasn't very courteous. The other cons are that the hotel is huge and caters to conferences. Since that is what I was here for, it didn't bother me. But, I did notice vacationers trying to get through the crowds, and I don't think I would like that if I were on vacation. Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

“Well situated, Decent Hotel” Stayed here on business for a couple of days and found that the this is a pretty decent hotel with its own charm. On first sight, the hotel is pretty dated but the rooms are well appointed and maintained. I got a large corner room at the very end of the main wing (where the reception is situated) and it was lovely. My only complaint is that the window faces one of the airport roads and it gets noisy during the day - but that is not a problem at night. Breakfast was great and they have a great (and reasonable) room service menu - which is good to have after a red-eye flight! All in all - I liked this hotel and its convenient location right next to BWI. Would I be back? Yes for the convenient location but for a holiday? Probably not.

“Downtown Delight” My husband and I stayed at the Andaz on a trip to NYC in February. I wanted a cool place to stay in case the weather took a really bad turn and we got hotel bound. We had a large king bedded room with a nice soaking tub and separate shower. Can't fault the room at all, very modern and comfortable. The stocked mini bar wasn't all that impressive but it was nice to have for a quick snack and a bottle of water. The complimentary happy hour in the evening was great. Good wine and very attentive service. The staff at the hotel are friendly and helpful but I wasn't too keen on the check-in with handheld devices. I thought it was very awkward standing there with luggage in the middle of reception waiting to be attented to. I don't know how they can tell who is checking in and who is just in the lobby with luggage waiting for a cab or something. The Wall and Water Restaurant onsite has a fab breakfast. They have a buffet or you can order a la carte which was quite affordable. I would definitely return if the price was right.

“Impeccable Service” This was our second stay at the Soho grand. The service was impeccable, people could not seem to do enough for us, from the manager, who changed our room and upgraded us when the a/c did not work, to the room service people. And of course, the location cannot be beat and the linens are fantastic. BUT, the rooms are very much in need of fixing up. Our bathroom ceiling was peeling and the room ceiling desperately needed paiting. We were in an executive king which is bigger by not much than the regular king and oddly enough contains no additional furniture. There is no desk, just one small table that barely fits a tray from room service. One small desk chair, and a small, uncomfortable arm chair and that's it. So would I stay there again? For a decent price for the executive king, I might. But I am more likely to go back to the Bryant Park which, althogh not in Soho, is maintained beautifully with good sized rooms.

“Spectacular Hotel!” Awesome hotel! Great views of the water and Canada (be sure to request a water view room). Friendly staff. Housekeeping was timely and the beds were very comfortable. It's within walking distance to Greektown (casino and restaurants) and river walk. The hotel dining options were plentiful and the main lobby bar stayed open very late. Overall a fantastic hotel!

“worth the money savings” I stayed at the Marriott Courtyard to save some money. I was attending a conference at the convention center and the conference hotels were up to double the cost of the Marriott. Since I was going to be in meetings all day, I decided to get some exercise and save some money. the hotel is an old bank, I forgot this until I walked it. Brought a smile to my face. The check in is at a teller stand. Hilarious. Being a bank means the rooms were solid and I heard no noise at night, but it also meant the internet didn't reach your room (but you could go to the lobby). The walk to the convention center was a hike, but it was fun going through the Gaslamp district. I felt safe and was amused by the all the partying going on (stayed thurs-sun). I would not bring my kids through this madhouse though. Service was functional but not outstanding. I could have stayed closer but the lovely weather made the long walk a pleasure. The hotel didn't have a lot of the stuff that the big hotels do, but if you want to save money, walk or take a taxi and have a nice room, then this place is for you.

“Good, but Hotel Burnham is better” We stayed at the Monaco recently and it was very nice. Usually we stay at the Burnham, another Kimpton hotel in Chicago, but decided to try the Monaco given that its web site indicated the room was quite a bit larger in terms of square feet. It wasn't larger. Most of the Burnham rooms have a nice street view of State or Washington. At the Monaco we overlooked an alley. The Monaco is very nice with an excellent location. Just south of the river with great access to the magnificant Mile, the Loop and the El. If the Burnham was booked, I'd stay again at the Monaco.

“great priceline rate and large room” We live in a Seattle suburb and wanted to stay downtown for a wedding. I selected a 4 star in downtown Seattle on priceline for $99. The reservation was accurate and there were no problems at check in. We were given a king bed in the old tower. The room was large with a comfortable bed. However, under the duvet was a traditional old blanket. Who knows when it was last washed...I was surprised to see that in such a high end chain hotel. The other motel like feature were thin and rough towels. Valet parking was $35 and wired internet was $10.

“Fantastic top notch property” Brought two soccer teams here to stay for the weekend for a tournament. The hotel staff was outstanding from minute one and never once dropped the ball. Had stayed here once before and had a good experience so chose this hotel again for that reason. The property is beautiful, kept immaculately clean and very well appointed. The staff is outstanding and the level of service is better than many larger or competitor properties that I have stayed in. Rooms are comfortable, have microwaves, refrigerators and coffee in the rooms. Nice fitness center and even a guest laundry. Good location and easy access to the highway and the businesses in the area. I will stay here again and again anytime I am in the area.

“Great Value in Prime Location” Totally comfortable, large room with nice decor two blocks from the harbor. It's a converted bank building with high ceilings, attractive common spaces and good architecture. Our room had pristine bedding, soft pillows and a large flat screen TV. When people in the next room began to throw a party around midnight, the staff immediately paid them a visit and solved the problem. Complimentary breakfast was ample and well prepared with fruit, eggs, bacon, oatmeal, bagels and much more.

“Looking for value and classic old school vacation feel, this is it.” Perfect location on South Congress near all the food, bars and music of SoCo. Rooms are small with literally 4 walls and a small restroom. Not much interms of service or room amenities but you can expect a small room, clean, safe and perfect for a few nights in Austin. Best feature is that parking is included in your rate!

“Location, style and Service” The AKA White House is 2 blocks from the White House, Quiet, well appointed rooms with excellent amenities. The decor is great, the rooms clean and comfortable. Melody Short on the front desk was excellent, and provided excellent recommendations for food and access to public transport. Two small gripes: a) The closest grocery store is a 20 minute walk, and without a car is a hassle. CVS Pharmacy is close by for the emergency stuff, but not for a main shop, its a cab ride. b) Food options for breakfast on a Sunday and Saturday are very limited, and you really need to try out options further afield via the Metro or a cab ride. But we loved it, and I am returning.

“Pleasantly Surprised” I was a little hesitant, given the mixed reviews, but this hotel was secured at a reduced conference rate, so I went for it. I stayed in room 1483, which I would highly recommend for 2-4 travelers. It's a room with very nice double beds, a lovely desk and sofa, and a small, but very clean bathroom w/excellent water pressure. The view out of the room was stunning -- a view to the condo gardens, with the treetops of the Boston Common in view, as well as a panoramic view of the river and T-lines. There's a very useful business center, an ATM, and an Au Bon Pain restaurant onsite. The staff were polite and helpful at all times. The only wrinkle was that the hotel safe kept malfunctioning, which the security folks were able to sort out twice, but was mildly inconvenient. On the whole, I truly enjoyed may stay, as did my friend. We are both seriously picky about hotels, and we had a blast.

“Expected More” I've stayed at most of the Hilton properties in the Bay area, but this one in particular was a disappointment. It was typical Hilton, clean, convenient, nice staff, etc., but fell short of a downtown San Fran hotel of this stature. We arrived very late, 12:15AM on a Thursday night. I was surprised on several counts; namely, no valet, no bell man, no 24 hour room service, no bar, no mini bar, no food service whatsoever. Please, in a 30+ story hotel in one of the largest cities in the US? The young man at the front desk was polite concerning the inadequacies, but could hardly offer much. He gave us a number for a pizza delivery service, and told us we could walk three blocks up the street for a bottle of wine. We had pizza and wine in bed at 1:30 AM. All I could think of was the Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton within shouting distance. Had it not been so late and had we not been so tired from a horrendous day of travel, we'd have left.

“Great little hotel for business travellers” Fantastic hotel for business travellers. Love the free wireless and breakfast. Gym area is sleek and well-located. Beware, if you're in rooms 108 or 208, you're windows face the pool so that could get noisy during busy summer months.

“The 2 1/2* hotel it claims to be” These reviews made me worry that I had landed a one star hotel for two and a half star prices. The hotel isn't as fancy as the three star DoubleTree across the highway, but it is fine. Room 510 was by the ice machine and the maids' room. Neither was a problem. There was some road noise, as to be expected in a hotel by a highway. So what if the parking garage turns are narrow? It's a parking garage. Room was clean and attractive, with coffee machine, balcony, two beds and sleeper couch, and all the usual amenities. The hotel has a fitness room and restaurant. Entree to the running/hiking trails on the hillside behind Hotel Circle South is from the road to Hillcrest beside the Holiday Inn. My travel companion liked the room a lot, and that was after a night at the Omni. The coffeemaker is Sunbeam instead of Cuisinart. Not a major problem.

“great location, noisy, good eaterie downstairs” We were upgraded to a 10th floor king room by Eric over the phone after booking thru Hotwire ( paid $ 125 per nite ), hotel gave it to HotWire for $ 89.... poor quality linens, Dell flat screen so so quality, bathroom needs a rug ( very cold marble floor), and window box style heat/ac was noisy, and had to be kept on since single pane windows are used, but it masks bigtime traffic noise below, the hotel is on a main street, so easy to walk to many places. The restaurant downstairs on premise had a delicious breakfast, also try nearby Lola's for breakfast/dinner. Front Desk staff is a bit green, need some customer training, often just stand there looking into space, or more interested in talking with each other than assisting guests. Bellcap was ok, but didn't explain the room's features like the included mini frigerator, or that internet is $ 10 a day with no free areas, or that most everything in the room, candy, etc is spendy, like $ 3.25 for a Snickers bar. All in all, the small room, and very comfy bed ( needs better linens, and using fitted top sheets so they don't come off in the night ), bath shower was good, but hot water wasn't there most of the time even after compaining. We had stayed here when it was the Vance hotel, it's spiffed up, but rates doubled too. It's a cheaper version ( in quality, service, etc ) of the W Hotel chain.

“Good business hotel” This is a good business hotel. The rooms are just fine and good for the business traveller. Concierge is helpful. Check in and out is efficient. I don't know that I would stay in this location for a personal trip but for business it works.

“Good choice” One night only here. Hotel was very busy and there was normally a wait for the lifts. Location is great - very central downtown amidst the shopping area. Lobby is very nice and would appear to have been recently upgraded. Bedrooms a litte tired but fine. Staff friendly. Would certaininly recommend.

“Fab!” Great stay - large room with comfy bed, really lovely salt-water pool and jacuzzi, staff very accommodating, breakfast delicious. A little too much noise from the hallways was the only drawback. Would certainly return.

“Beautiful and Modern!” This is probably the best Hilton properties in the states. Located right on the bay, you get amazing views of the city and Coronado Island. The hotel is clean, crisp and the staff from the valet to the front desk were accommodating. We were given a room in the 19th floor overlooking the city/bay area. The hotel loses points for having a giant ad on the north facing side of the hotel. It made our room darker as it prevented sunlight from coming in. HH rejoice! Free appetizers in the Vela bar for each night stay. You also get the standard continental breakfast from the Starbucks on the ground level, however for $10 you can upgrade to the Buffet. Overall, a very good experience and I would stay here in a heartbeat. The hotel is situated next to the convention center and across the street from the Stadium. Easy to walk in Downtown or a short cab ride.

“Very Comfortable Hotel” The Grand Hyatt in downtown Denver is a very nice hotel that is located about a block and a half off of the 16th St. mall. The rooms are spacious for an older building, nicely furnished, comfortable bed, walk in closet, nice views, with indoor pool, work out center, rooftop (above the parking garage) tennis courts and running track. We were in town for one night so we didn't get to spend a lot of time at the hotel but the time we were there we were pleased with the accommodations. There is a piano bar in the the lobby and a restaurant, we didn't have the opportunity to try any of the amenities but it was nice to know that they were available. There were a couple of things that we weren't crazy about and for some it would be good info to have before hand. The hotel offers wifi in the rooms at a cost, there is no business center in the hotel. There is a computer that has internet access but there is no printing available and wifi in the lobby . The only issue that we had is we assumed that we would have the ability to print off some tickets to a show that we were attending that evening as well as my husbands boarding pass for the next day. We were told by the bellhop that the concierge would be able to help us with the printing of those items. When my husband called down to the concierge they seemed a little confused but said that if I wanted to come down to the desk I could use their computer but the boarding pass would have to be printed out at the FedEx/Kinkos that is in the same complex. For our tickets I was able to log on to my email at the concierge desk and print out the tickets. A little later my husband went into the kinkos check into his flight and print the boarding passes and he found out when he got there that it would be $21 to log on and print... when he mentioned that he was told by the hotel to go there for the service they said that it was still $21, he opted to do it at the airport. That wasn't a big issue, it was more that we assumed rather than making sure they offered that service. My only other complaint, and again, not a big one, is that when you have your car valeted, you don't pick it up out front where you drop it off, you go through a doorway across the lobby, down a hallway and out a service door into the garage. It just gave that feel of being a second class citizen now that you've checked out. It wasn't a problem with the few bags that we had however, if you had larger luggage or several bags to balance I would recommend having the bellhop pick them up and take them down. My husband and I got the corner king room while my daughter got a regular king room. What makes the corner king room different is that it's at the end of the hall. My daughters room seemed a little larger as a whole, I preferred the layout of the corner room more because the bed was facing the large window. Short of that feature there wasn't enough of a difference to make the king room more special than the regular king. Short of the two rather minor issues we really enjoyed our stay at the Grand Hyatt and would stay again.

“Convenient, Friendly, Fashionable” I can't say enough about Hotel Abri. This was my second recent visit, and once again I was impressed with the friendliness of the staff and the size of the king room. The location can not be beat, big TV's and working desks are great, and if you want a gigantic room with a huge bathroom, ask for a king corner room - you will be amazed.

“New York elbow room” This is my second visit to the Times Square Westin. After staying at various W locations, the Hudson and the SoHo Grand, these are by far the biggest rooms I've had in NY. Some of the other places are just a bed, plus 2/3 ft. around it. Last time I was here, I had a corner room that was especially large. It has everything you'd expect from a Westin, with clean contemporary rooms and good bedding. The views vary widely – but some are quite nice. It's a fine place to be if you want to be near Times Square or the Theater District. As you might imagine, so close to Times Square, there can be mobs of tourists and many chain restaurants. If you're looking for a romantic oasis in the city, This part of town probably won't be your first choice. Our trip was short, and built around theater tickets, so it worked fine for that. I'm not sure if this is really true, but it seems like a rather large Westin, and the service feels less focused. The mini-bar fridge wasn't working, so I let the front desk know. They said they would send someone up. When I returned later in the day, it still isn't working, and there's no message or update on status. Obviously, not a very big deal, but unusual for a Westin. By contrast, the concierge was very insightful/helpful in arranging dinner reservations.

“NOT The Best Westin” Reservations: easy using the Starwood Website. Check-in: polite efficient and prompt Room: Quiet enough, pleasant furnishings although a little scuffed up. Nice sized room and bathroom. Heavenly bed and shower are still fantastic, especially the bed. Nice bath products as well. Hotel gym: only open 8 am - 8 pm on weekends, which is a little odd. Check-out: fast efficient and accurate. Chief Complaint(s): 1. There is nothing particularly special or memorable about this hotel. It is a large convention/tourist hotel that you will forget as soon as you check out. 2. THEY CHARGE $14.95 per day for internet service: this is a TOTAL RIPOFF. Chief Attribute: If you shop around you can get a nice room in a great location just off of Times Square for a reasonable price by New York standards.

“Smooth Stay” On arrival the valet were friendly and continued that way throughout my 3 day solo business stay. Check in was smooth. Room service was great and I do not have anything negative to say about the hotel. Valet parking was a little steep at $38 per night, but I am not familiar with other hotels in Philadelphia as it was my first time. I do not know if this is standard or high for the area. Considering in LA I pay around $25-30 I thought it was higher than average. The room was clean and had good decor and ambience. It wasn't the largest of hotel rooms but they used their space well and it did not feel cramped. The bathroom was spacious, it had a shower only which suits me fine. I had breakfast once in the restaurant and room service once. Room service was perfect. Amazing food, great service, it arrived in 20 minutes. Breakfast in the restaurant wasn't so great. They mixed up my order and then brought the wrong style eggs. I wasn't in a hurry that morning so wasn't a huge problem. They were apologetic and resolved the issue, and also brought some complimentary fruit. Overall the stay was good, perfect location walking distance to stores Macy's etc, and an efficient valet service. Make sure you call for your car before time if you are in a rush aanther say it can take up to 20 minutes although I always got mine in 10. The hotel also gives you a $10 credit if you go green and do not have maid service that day which is also a bonus. I loved the outdoors in feel they have in the corridors with the exposed bricks, and they have lovely elevator music. I would stay again.

“'Yes ma'am, you'll be safe round here... and I was!” Arrived at the hotel, book in was quick and effortless, Emilie was the very friendly and most helpful girl, she gave me a room with a fantastic view of the ground zero monument buildings and other amazing skyscrapers. Lovely room, very clean, modern and comfortable. I haven't stayed downtown before, and I have to say, it was a nice change, lovely tree lined streets with town houses and local deli's, which were open 24 hours. I fell asleep as soon as I got in, woke up at 2am, realised I hadn't booked transport to the airport, the concierge was a huge help in arranging a lovely big mercedes to take me. I was hungry, he pointed me in the direction of the deli at the top of the road, I asked if it was safe for me to walk, hence the title of this review. I usually stay midtown, but this area is so peaceful but also typically like the New York you see on the telly. I will definitely stay here again, and would recommend it to anybody.

“Great Location” The Westin Seattle has a great central location that is a 10 minute or less walk to all the things we had planned including Pike Place, the Monorail (90 second ride to the Space Needle), the flagship Nordstrom store, and lots of great restaurants (we went to Serious Pie, Palace Kitchen, The Crumpet Shop, Le Panier, and various Pike Place spots on our Savor Seattle tours). The room is what you would expect from a Westin and at the price I paid (under $90), it was perfect!

“Grand old hotel with very modern amenities.” This Omni is in an ideal location for touring Philly's most historic sites and offers a very welcome level of comfort and service. The building is older, with a grand and elegant lobby, while the rooms are very modern with comfy beds and luxurious bathrooms. As an Omni loyalty program member, I enjoyed having complimentary coffee delivered to my room each morning at my selected time. It was simple getting a cab (waiting outside) to head out to the train station after my visit. Breakfast overlooking the square was a real pleasure! The staff was very friendly in a professional way, which is always helpful. I travel often and tend to stay in the ultra modern boutique hotels, so this was a nice change.

“Solides Hotel in Dallas” Das Hotel liegt im Nordosten von Dallas. Es ist ein solides Mittelklasse Kettenhotel. Nicht besonderes, aber gutes Zimmer mit guter Ausstattung. Auch Parkplätze waren genügend vorhanden. Das Hotel liegt direkt am Freeway und so ist man in kurzer Zeit überall im Großraum Dallas. Das Hotel bietet ein gutes Preis/ Leistungsverhältnis und ist für einen Kurzaufenthalt in Dallas zu empfehlen.

“Great Unique Rooms” The rooms as the Beverly Laurel can't be beat. First, they are huge, or at least mine was. Second, they have a lovely set-up, with a kitchen, bar and seating area. The location is also great, right in the middle of LA, in a clean, safe neighborhood and everything is a short drive away.

“Great hotel!” I really liked the hotel - they allocated us a large room on the 4th floor which was spacious (for 2 adults & 2 children sharing), clean and well equipped. Breakfast in the restaurant was a welcome change from the buffet type meal served in so many establishments. Good location - I would definately come back here

“Excellent place to hold certain functions” My stepdaughter had her wedding reception in the penthouse of the Hudson last night. I declined to stay in the hotel, as I had read the reviews and knew that it was not right for a middle-aged couple, but I have to say that the Hudson has the ability to hold a first class event. The food and service were fantastic, and the hotel organizer, Marta, was on hand for the entire event and was very hands on and anticipatory, I wandered around the hotel with the reviews in mind, and I would say that the hotel does a good job of taking care of the euro-hip, and a substandard job of taking care of the older and/or family crowd that booked on Priceline. It's just not designed for that.

“Wonderful room, jazzy lobby, friendly service” I spent only one night at this great hotel. It's LEED certified, modern, and comfortable. Upon entering my large room, saw two bottles of water and a box of jelly beans with a nice hand written card, thanking me for my business and platinum status. Free wifi, great tv, very comfortable bed, large walk-in show, Aveda products, etc. made for a very enjoyable stay. This was my first Hotel Indigo stay and it certainly won't be the last.

“You can do better!” We stayed at the Hotel Penn because of its proximity to the Westminster Dog Show. I am occasionally back in Manhattan and spend the night, and I would NEVER choose this place again. We didn't see any vermin, but there was definitely a dark, dingy quality to the halls and the room. To be honest, we thought the beds were comfortable and the shower had good water pressure. Other than that, there are only lowlights. The front desk staff must be the slowest people in New York City - and possibly the most unmotivated to help you. The security guard sitting by the elevator seemed to be more of a tour guide than a actual safety measure. What shocked me was that the hotel charges a $4/bag fee to store your luggage if you want to tour the city after your 12noon check-out time. I have travelled fairly extensively and never encountered this absolutely small-sighted, cheap measure. Don't write this off to "It's New York - it's all expensive." It's never happened to me at other New York hotels - so it's more that "It's just Hotel Penn, it's cheap." We could only guess that the hotel is too large to renovate and enough people stay there to keep the management from wanting to - certainly the location is nice, but there are better hotels in more interesting neighborhoods closer to better restaurants. Keep looking.

“Expected more” I just stayed at this hotel for a work conference. Rooms are clean- no issue there- but I found the staff less than helpful in general, and very little in the way of amenities. For example, no gift shop to buy toiletries, etc., no room service. Also, the "internet" wasn't working for 2 nights- even though the hotel charges an extra $9.95 to cover this and phone calls.... The place was not horrible- but I wouldn't rush back at all.....

“立地はよい” 行きも帰りもシャトルバスで向かいました。マンハッタンまでの道が混んでいるので往復とも1時間半以上かかりました。 20ドル強かかりました。 ロビーは1階にはありません。 フロントの対応はよいとは言えませんでした。 鍵をもらっただけで、なんの説明もありませんでした。 部屋は狭く、トイレのゴミが片付けられていないということでクレームを出しました。 6月だったからでしょうか、ヒーターが一切効きませんでした。なので部屋で洗濯しても冷風ではなかなか乾きませんでした。 冷蔵庫はありませんでしたがアイスマシーンがフロアにありました。 部屋の中に金庫がありました。 ブロードウェイミュージカルを何本か観ましたが、歩いて帰れる距離なので安心です。自転車タクシーに乗ってエンパイアステートビルまで行きましたが、25ドルでした。 駅から近いし、駅を利用しなくても歩けるので立地はすばらしいです。ただ52ndを9thの方に夜向かうのは多少危ない雰囲気です。 ただ、この近辺は警察があちこちに立っています。 レストランは景色がよく、タイムズスクエアをみながら食事することができます。滞在中、1人で3回そこで夕飯を食べました。14ドル程度ですが、パスタなどを食べることができました。 インターネットは自分でHot Spotの画面からクレジットカードで契約してから使うというものでした。 最終日にシャトルバスが迎えに来る時間まで荷物を預けましたが、一つにつき1ドルでした。 フロントの対応をまったく気にしなければよいと思います。

“Average, despite upgrades” I stayed at this hotel in January 2008 to attend a weekend professional meeting. My room was not in the tower, but a two story building attached. The staff was excellent and helpful. The room was quiet (I understand construction was going on but I stayed on a Saturday night and nobody was working on Sunday morning.) The bed was new and comfortable, the furniture was good but not great, and there was a flat screen t.v. The room was clean. However despite the $65 million in upgrades, my bathtub did not drain properly after I showered. If two people are sharing the room and each wants to shower this could be a problem. The fit and finish of the bathroom was poor, although I want to stress it was clean. What was puzzling was that in order to use the internet you had to pay a fee -- either for a cable connection or to log in to wireless. Something that is provided free at Starbucks should be likewise free at a hotel that considers itself first class. Paying more than $10 per day to connect is just annoying. Room service ended at 10 p.m., a problem for some of our group that got in late at night. Our meeting room was not signed -- I mean how difficult could it be to put up a sign saying "Palm Room" on the door of the Palm Room? When I checked out using the express machine, my receipt indicate that the food I had ordered was liquor. Obviously, my professional group was not going to reimburse me for drinking my dinner. I had that changed by the front desk, but it took a while. Others have mentioned that this hotel is out of the way. It is if you want easy access to downtown. If you have a car you can drive to downtown, the gaslamp area, etc. fairly easily. If not, a cab ride is going to run you $25 or more. There are virtually no restaurants in walking distance, again a problem if you get in after they close room service. So rent a car.

“Wonderful value” Very good location. Close to buses (which can take you to the subway) which go east and south to the National Mall and north to the National Cathedral. Full kitchen in every room (that's a full-sized stove with oven, full-sized refrigerator with ice-maker, dishwasher, disposal, microwave and toaster!) There's also a complimentary continental breakfast. Friendly, helpful staff, although housekeeping was a little confused. They ask you, as many hotels do these days, to put the towels you want washed on the floor and hang up the ones you don't need to have washed. Our maid had a habit of taking the towel on the floor and not replacing it--she also often took all the towels--even those not on the floor--without replacing them. We had to call the desk twice to have towels brought up. It's a neighborhood place and gives you a feeling of really being in Georgetown--and the Four Seasons is two blocks away and I'm sure MUCH more expensive. You can get decent deals by going to the hotel's website. Just one caution, though--DON'T GO TO DC IN THE SUMMER!
“大型ホテルですが、ゆったりとした部屋とフレンドリーなスタッフ” ショッピングにも観光にも便利な立地です。大型ホテルでロビーもとても広く人でにぎわってました。部屋はスタンダードな感じですが結構広く、プールが見え、ちょっとしたリゾート気分でした。

“Good Choice” This hotel is just steps from Hollywood Boulevard, but amazingly quiet. My room overlooked an apartment block, which meant the view was not great, but there was no noise from the shopping centre. As previous reviews state, the place is a little tired, but that can so easily be overlooked with all the advantages. The place is beautifully clean with a pleasant pool and roof terrace. The rooms are very well equipped. There are two double beds, iron/board, hotplate, fridge, coffeemaker, cutlery/crockery, roomsafe, TV, clock/radio and hairdryer. There were always loads of coffee, sugar & creamer. Buying a few basic supplies made it very easy to prepare breakfast in the room There is a huge double mirrored wardrobe and very clean bathroom with bath & shower. I had a small problem with the bath plug & maintenace came to repair it within minutes of reporting it to reception. Very slight negative were the very thin dividing walls meaning next door conversations could be overheard. The hotel is a few yards from the subway & the Hollywood & Highland shopping centre. Also many tours leave from the front of Grauman's Chinese theatre, making very convenient. This is a well located, reasonably priced hotel & I would recommend it for a visit to Hollywood

“Overall, OK hotel, despite a few glitches” We visited to celebrate my wife's and our daughter's birthdays. Room was spacious and comfortable. Lots of,closet space and a nice balcony. Room service was good. Had a few maintenance issues and the doormen aren't overly friendly. Great location.

“Perfect Service at the Omni” We stayed at the Omni San Francisco for 3 nights at the Labour Day weekend. It was the last stop of our honeymoon to the US and we couldn't have made a better choice. We were upgraded to a Bay View Room on the top floor (17th floor). My wife was given a rose at check in, they brought us a bottle of champaign and chocolate-coated strawberries and had arranged our bathrobes with another rose the first evening. Room service was simply outstanding. I highly recommend joining the free OMNI Select Guest programme which entitles you to complimentary WIFI, beverage and newsparer service. Staff was charming, attentive and helpful with the exception of one gruffy bellman. Dined once at Bob's Steakhouse (belonging to the hotel), waiters so so, but great food, had a perfect filet mignon. Cable Car line runs just in front of the house. The only minor drawbacks: - WIFI service doesn't work on the 17th floor which they "somehow forgot" to mention at check-in (however, as Select guest you can use the cable internet free of charge) - walls are quite thin (the same old story everywhere...) - parking: as usual in SF, street parking is a mess and the hotel charges a hefty 40$ valet fee for 24 hours + 6$ city tax. Hotel is within walking distance of Ferry Building, Embaracadero, Coit Tower, Market Street, Chinatown and SOMA. Would highly recommend and always return there.

“Great time!” We had a great stay. We found the beds very comfortable and the room was clean. Good location to catch subway to other locations. It was our first stay in this location and we not impressed. It would be helpful if they could provide a small area map with places to visit. We were somewhat disappointed in the availability of nearby restaurants. Day staff seemed knowledgable but afternoon evening staff lacked the ability to assist with restaurant locations, advising that we should travel at least ten blocks north to eat. We were also frustrated with their restaurant. Appearance is impressive but it felt as though we were bothering a non-busy staff. We only ordered dessert and coffee which took forever. The coffee tasted stale and the cheesecake had been microwaved so that some was soft and warm and other parts cold. Thanks to our plans to in the city, we did have a very enjoyable visit but my experience at the Distrikt left me a little disappointed based on all the great reviews.

“Location fantastic” Good value for money, close to pike st market and lots of good bars and restaurants on your doorstep. Rooms clean comfortable, excellent staff on hand to help with maps ect and where to go. Easy choice for around 100 dollars a night.

“You have a choice - choose an alternative” If you know and like Westin - you won't like this. Austin has many better properties. Question the validity of the other reviews on the site? Corners have been cut to create a small contemporary version that removes the concierge lounge on the SPG floors, free internet for SPG members and any decent parking. Service delivered by anyone over 17 with authority doesn't exist. Room service failed, the single phone in the room didn't work and a wireless connection took all night . While it's adjacent to the Domain Center... you have to drive over and park again. They've cut every corner, then overcharge for the basics. Shame on this limited partnership owner.

“The hotel guests are coming!” This hotel is in a great location and has a number of nice features/amenities. To skip to the punch line, I would absolutely stay here again and look forward to my next opportunity to do so. Pros: - hotel appears to be new or newly renovated - check-in is quick, efficient and courteously staffed - rooms are tastefully appointed with hardwood entryway, carpeted bedroom, desk, reading area with chaise lounge and designated lighting - iPad speakers - complimentary slippers - extensive and varied room service menu - TV works with the LodgeNet app for iPhone, which is a cool and fun feature - complimentary WiFi Cons: - elevators take quite some time to come and some have not yet been renovated - no alarm clock in the room. While I'm sure the average guest has a watch or phone to tell time, it's nice to have a clock in the room that is visible if you awaken during the night - no minibar - no bathrobe. This isn't a big deal but most hotels that offer slippers have bathrobes. - the bathroom toiletries are bolted to the wall. This is undoubtedly more green than manufacturing the miniature sized bottles but is much less convenient for guests. - located near a number of great restaurants The pros more than outweigh the cons so I wholeheartedly recommend a stay here.

“Good bur far from Great” We came to this hotel with high expectations. We have stayed at the Kimpton Hotel Allegro in Chicago several times and absolutely love it. However, our experience at the Eventi left some room for improvement. For starters, the lobby is tiny. As others have said, there was really no room to sit and drink your coffee in the morning. This leads us to a huge disappointment for us – there was no coffee maker in the room. My husband and I love a piping hot cup of coffee in the morning while getting ready for the day. What a hassle to get your clothes on and go down 18 floors to stand in line and bring two small cups back up 18 floors. Several times when we got downstairs they were out of coffee so we had to wait. Finally on the last day right before checkout we mentioned to the front desk about how we really would have liked a coffee maker and he said oh, we can bring one up for you. How would we know we could get a coffee maker – there was no sign in the room? There was a sign saying we could get a curling iron or toothbrush, but nothing about a coffee maker. And, we could not have called for one if we wanted to because guess what – our phone did not work for the entire stay. We brought this up to the front desk and they sent someone up who said he would have to do some major work and would come back the next day, but he never did. And we did not have the energy to futz with it when we were there to enjoy the city. One other thing that we really missed was having a concierge – especially in New York City. The front desk folks seemed put out if you asked for a restaurant recommendation. They did not have a book of menus or other materials that would have helped us plan our days. Also, due to a glitch in the reservation system, you have to make two separate reservations is there is a sale going on for a portion of our stay. Thus, our room keys did not work after the first night and we had to get them reprogrammed. On the plus side, the bed was very comfortable and the room was clean. The floors to ceiling windows were nice. The complimentary internet for Kimpton in Touch Members is a must. We did have one beer, one coke, and 1 bag of pretzels with the “raid the mini bar” $15 coupon for In Touch members. We were only able to enjoy the wine hour one night out of four since it was only offered from 5pm to 6pm. We arrived on the first night right after it closed and thought they might have offered us a glass of wine since we just missed it but even though we mentioned it, they said come back tomorrow. I think a two hour time period would offer more of an opportunity to enjoy a glass depending on your schedule, or simply have a bottle in the room since the lobby is so small there really is not a lot of space to drink it. Overall, we had a nice time at the Eventi Hotel despite the little inconveniences but would most likely stay elsewhere next time.

“Good Sleep and Clean Shower” I stayed at this hotel only because the price was right and the location was good. It was indeed old with ragged carpet and scratched surfaces. But we don't spend much time in the room when we visit Chicago, so I was happy that it was clean and the king bed was extremely comfortable. The first night was very quiet but on night two the room next door was occupied and it sounded like they were practically in the room with us, as the connecting door did not filter much noise. The rusty air conditioning unit was a little icky but the air that came out of it was just fine. I've stayed in several hotels at a similar level in Chicago and this one is about par for the course--some good points and some bad.

“Great Package rate” The "Date Night" package was awesome. It included cocktails in the very cool Lantern's Keep bar and continental breakfast delivered to our room. The room was fairly small, but very comfortable and quiet. We were celebrating an anniversary, and the hotel sent up a bottle of wine, some chocoates and a note. Great location in Midtown. Only complaint is that the bathroom was small, and there was not much room for personal toiletries. If you're driving into the city, the hotel has a great rate at the parking garage directly across the street. The staff was all very professional and friendly. Would definitely stay at the Iroquois again.

“Excellent City Hotel Living Up to its Reputation” I've never seen this hotel before so i can't compare it to the old version and I have been quite a fan of the Beverly Hills Hotel. I was very happy with this property and it would be a hard choice between the two Dorchester properties on my next visit to LA. The arrival gardens makes a great first impression (although I never did see the swans). The premiere canyon suite 269 was gorgeous (i was upgraded thru Andrew Harper)-- i really liked the decorating and the airy feel of the place. I didn't have any issues with the electronics in the rooms and I'm pretty dumb in that area. The terrace with the pool and the view was excellent. The bathroom was large and functional; the bedroom and living room and closets were all primo and I liked the Swiss-based amenities in the bath. The Wolfgang Puck restaurant for dinner and breakfast were both excellent; i really liked the menu, the food quality and service. The spa was fine and the treatment good. The grounds are all lovely on the landscaping and the color and ambiance of the place is very pleasant as you stroll about the property. The only disappointment I felt was in the gym; there are a few free weights and some cardio but not more -- I was expecting a hotel of this sort to have a really good gym and I can't understand why they skipped over this.

“Stay Elsewhere” Don't let the public spaces fool you; the rooms are a joke. Even an upgraded room was way too small for comfort and lacking in amenities. The poorly designed bathroom was all about looks over function--it failed on both counts. Do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere.

“Ordinary” Although it is highly rated in these reviews, and you pay a premium price compared with other airport hotels, there is nothing special about this hotel other than its proximity to SEATAC. If you are thinking of staying here, pay attention to the Trip Advisor comments about the hideous views of HVAC equipment from the windows on one whole side of the hotel. Although my room was on the top floor of the building, the view looked like an industrial site, just because of all the equipment on the roof of a lower wing of the building. The room itself was spacious, the bed was comfortable, and the bathroom was functional. But during a rainstorm in the middle of the night, the ceiling leaked. The club lounge, for which I had paid extra, was about as modest as any I've ever seen. But it did have good food at breakfast. The best part of the hotel in my experience was its restaurant. The room itself was extremely ordinary, looking like a roadside restaurant on a freeway, but the food and the service were first-rate. Bottom line: I slept well here. But even though I collect Marriott points, I don't think I'd return to this hotel.

“Very nice Hotel and great location” I liked this hotel. the place was very clean. the check in staff can use a little more training on customer service, but all in all, a great hotel. The only problem I had was with the parking lot which appears to need some extra people to help get cars. Great bar and service people.

“Excellent” The room, at $179, was a great value considering this is a full service hotel. Unfortunately for me the hotel was not in the most convenient location, but most other locations were booked up already due to the marathon. Everyone was very friendly and helpful and with a shuttle service to the subway station, I did not personally need a car. There is also an enclosed walkway that directly connects the hotel to the airport. The only problem I had was that my room had neither microwave nor a refrigerator. I don't stay in full service hotels very often, so maybe this is just their way of trying to get you to eat their overpriced food.

“Location, location, location” This Kimpton has a great location with a lot to do nearby, especially in Westwood. The rooms are good and show their age but are well maintained and comfortable. The staff is both professional and courteous. They have a wine hour that is fun but oenophiles might want to bring their own. This is a good, if not great property, and I would not hesitate to return.

“Indy 500” We went to Indianapolis to see Indy 500 and we totaly recommend this hotel. The hotel has a very good location next to Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Rooms are good, very clean and nice staff.

“Sehr angenehmes Airport Hotel” Schöne Hotel 5 Fahrminuten von LAX. Shuttle-Bus fährt im 15 Minuten Takt von allen Terminals zum Hotel. Dort angekommen checkinn in 1 min. Schöne und saubere Zimmer mit Gratis-Safe. Sehr gut eingerichtetes 24 Stunden Gym mit allem was das Herz begehrt. Außerdem bietet das Hotel eine sehr schöne Poolanlage mit einem beheiztem Pool. Im Hotel befindet sich ein Starbucks und leckeres Restaurant (mit ca 50 TV`s). Dort kann man für ca 10 Dollar sehr lecker essen. Warme Küche bis 24 Uhr. Also ich komme wieder.

“Wonderful wedding night stay” I stayed here with my husband on our wedding night in late August, a few months ago. It is a wonderful property, modern/swanky/low profile feel. Due to a corporate rate I have, we stayed here at $300/night for a "Spectacular Room" (I think Kimpton may have changed the room names now), but were supposedly upgraded to a nicer room since it was our wedding night. The room was beautiful, with large windows and a gorgeous view of Boston from the bed. The bathrooms were very roomy and nice as well. I am very surprised about the complaints here about the service. Service was over the top excellent during our stay, and we asked for a lot of different things. I thought they were great and seemed accustomed to providing high level service. We ate at their Spire restaurant for brunch with our families the morning afterwards, and it was great. The only hassle at all was that they accidentally billed us twice for the room and on wrong credit cards (we used different ones to reserve), but it was quickly fixed with a phone call. Regardless, I'm very glad I stayed at Nine Zero on our wedding night and am eager to stay there again.

“Beautiful Hotel” This hotel looks brand new. It is lovely. The suites were clean, spacious and had very nice amenities. The couch is a king sleeper. The location had a pool and hot tub. The staff was very nice. The breakfast was good although very crowded on Saturday morning. The only negative was the wifi was not working properly. Great location.

“Fun for fun people” I ended up sleeping two nights at the Roosevelt, poolside bungalow ( not really a cabin by the lake), and it was amazing! Great environment for fun loving people, and the best food ever! Please have the breakfast bagel with salmon!!! great service and music is always playing. Not for business!!!

“Okay place” The hotel is in a nice location - just in front of The Domian. But there is a railway track behind the hotel and if you are a lite sleeper, then this is not the hotel - though you could request a room that is not facing the track. Good: free wifi, decent sized rooms, free breakfast, free parking, easy access to freeway Bad: Noisy A/c, railway track behind the property,price/day for this class of hotel

“Very clean. Nice stay.” If you need to be in this part of Houston, this is a good choice. It's clean and quiet (make sure you request a room not facing the highway). It didnt look all that full, so try and get a good rate.

“Got such a great deal! Hotel exceeded my expectations!” Stayed here for 3 nights before heading north to Vancouver. Got an amazing deal on Expedia for only $138/night, which is unbelievable for a busy July weekend with several Alaska-bound cruises departing and the Red Sox in town to play the Mariners. The hotel is in a great location b/c it's on the periphery of Downtown, Belltown, Lower Queen Anne, and South Lake Union, so it's easy to get to many of the sights/attractions in Seattle. It's a 10-minute walk to the Westlake Center to catch the light rail, about a 20-minute walk to Pike Place Market, and is about a 10-minute walk to the Space Needle. There are also several bus lines and the trolley that go past the hotel, so getting around was easy. The hotel has a gorgeous lobby, a nice hotel bar, and having a Whole Foods underneath the hotel was fantastic for grabbing a snack, water, etc. without resorting to the minibar. Our room was average-sized, but beautifully appointed and very comfortable. We had a higher floor room facing north, so we had a great view of Lake Union as well as the Space Needle in the corner. The highlight of the room is definitely the large bathroom w/ a great glass shower, deep soaking tub, and plenty of space. Given that we spent our busy weekend sightseeing and didn't spend very much time in the hotel, the Pan Pacific Seattle met all of our needs in a very comfortable fashion. I don't know if others may luck out and get the deal we did, but regardless, it's definitely one of the best hotels in Seattle and I would definitely stay there again when visiting Seattle!

“Do Not Stay Here For Now” Be aware that the hotel is undergoing extensive renovation and that there is no special consideration given for the guests, except that the check in staff wear silly hard hats. They'll still charge you rack rates, and you have to step around the work men that work during the day. There dust and debris on your way to your room (and it follows you). There are no signs telling where the safe areas from the construction areas are (OSHA violation???)Valet/self parking is $15/day regardless.

“the quietest hotel ever” We were in town for the Denver Bronco/Pittsburgh Steelers game. Booked this hotel because it was the "cheapest" place to stay in the Downtown area on a football weekend - WOW - what a great surprise - it's a really nice hotel !!! We arrived close to 1230pm - asked about checking early so we could head to the game - they said YES. (Thanks Sara - you made our day !!!) The rooms are large, very clean, very comfortable, and the QUIETEST hotel I've ever stayed. The pool and fitness center are great. The staff was generally nice - other than the girl at check in it appeared that everyone was "doing their job." The hotel is a short walk to 16th St Mall area - and you're note dodging a lot of bums/homeless/beggars like you are at other Downtown Denver hotels. A short walk up 17th Avenue you'll find some great local places for food/drink !!! I would say the only negative - breakfast - both mornings the were out of food - and the guests had to wait - that's unacceptable with a hotel that has high volume like this property - happened both mornings. The parking situation is confusing - there are lots nearby - that I found out after the fact I could have parked overnight for less - the hotel valet parking is expensive - and the front desk staff takes care of the car - the staff would leave the desk to park/retrieve car. This is really a great hotel - I was very pleasantly surprised - I would stay here again !!!!!!

“Great Hotel with Amazing Service, My favorite in DC” I have stayed at this hotel a couple times over the past month and each stay was excellent. The staff is extremely friendly, but not over the top, and all of my requests were handled promptly and politely. I had a park deluxe room on one stay and a park suite on the other and each room was very large and tastefully decorated. The hotel is modern, but not over the top. I had breakfast each morning in the Blue Duck Tavern and the food was great. The service was a little slow, but after mentioning I was in a hurry the service greatly improved. This is my new favorite hotel in DC and I will definitely be back. Positives: Large rooms Luxury hotel without a stuffy feel Friendly Staff Amazing Restaurant Negatives: Far from the metro if you are taking public transit Not enough outlets around the desk area No HD channels

“gutes, hervorragend gelegenes Hotel” Die Lage sehr nahe zu Fishermans Wharf ist hervorragend. Es gibt ausreichend Parkplätze, die allerdings mit einer Extra-Gebühr zu Buche schlagen. Der Service ist hervorragend, man wird äußerst zuvorkommend bei sämtlichen Anliegen (und davon gab es einige) und Extrawünschen behandelt. Leider wurde dei Kreditkarte mit dem fälligen Betrag bereits per Vorkasse zum Zeitpunkt der Buchung vor etwa 10 Wochen belastet. Kostenloses WLAN ist vorhanden. Das Frühstücksbuffett sowie der Service dort waren sehr gut. Leider war es nachts etwas laut vom Pool her, der sich auf der zur Straße zugewandten Seite befindet und leider auch von der Straße selbst. Die Zimmer sind sehr groß, erscheinen aber etwas abgewohnt. Aber alles in allem eine gute Wahl.

“Excellent Value” The Newton Hotel fully deserves the reputation for being top value in NYC. After a lot of research, we chose the Newton for 2 stays in June 2010. I wont go into all of the advantages as they are many, and well documented in other reviews. We had a junior suite on the 8th floor for a week, and one on the 4th floor next to Broadway for 3 days. Both were a good size and very confortable, but had slightly different characteristics. The 8th floor room was better designed, but the A/C was very loud. We couldnt turn it off as it was hot and humid in NY at the time. However, it did had an advantage. The room was not very soundproof, so it drowned out the noise of the hallway and other guests. The 4th floor room was not laid out as well, but the A/C was a lot quieter and the location at the end of the hall was also a lot quieter. I was aware of the lift situation before I booked. I used it as a character building excercise and tried to think of the money I saved staying here, but I have to admit that after 1 week of putting up with it, I was a bit fed up. The lift is slow and is busy often enough to require tolerance. However, it is not enough to stop me from staying again. Overall, despite some minor little things (and the lift,) the Newtown has so much going for it (especially location and price), that I would happily come back again. Would recommend a junior suite at the end of the hall on a lower floor.

“super location/ below average service” I have stayed at the worthington numerous time over the past few years. I am always attracted to the location ( right off sundance square and near reatta and several other great dinning spots). The hotel is average at best for what you spend. Average size rooms, nothing luxurious and i would say falls in the middle of the renaissance chain vs. recently remodeled properties. Concierge lounge is a joke. Food was poor, attendant was not in attendance. It's a great pit stop on the 8th floor to grab some free water and possibly a WSJ ( since they didn't drop one at the room).
