Just depends on what you expect, as someone who travels 200 nights a year this is disappointing. If your grabbing a room on priceline, you would be happy.

“Average, but met my needs.” The hotel was hard to find. It's hidden behind a small shopping center in a very congested area. It took two times around the area to locate it due to poor hotel signs. The hotel was nice, suite was very clean, and the breakfast was bland in taste. It is located in a nice area very close to shopping and eating establishments. I consider it as an OK stay. Good luck finding the hotel and entrance.

“It felt great to be back” I had not stayed at NY Palace in a couple of years and it felt great to be back. Rooms are nicer than I remember and the lobby remains the place for the powerful to roam. Gilt is a fabulous addition to the NY restaurant scene (2 star Michelin:) I can hardly wait to return. Only things I did not like was desk clerk insistence that I booked a smoking room (I did not) and then she tried to hussle a higher rate for a room with a view. I wound up on the 34th floor with a river view after saying no so I cannot imagine what she was peddling.

“Very comfortable, smaller choice in NYC” We booked a suite upgrade using spg points, arrived at four, and were treated to a very nice cocktail when our room was not quite ready. Our one bedroom suite was really two interconnecting rooms with the Murphy bed folded up in the second room, which, after reading the reviews left me feeling a bit let down ( no terrace, big bathtubs etc), but hey, it was a points upgrade so what the heck? At check in there was the usual Starwood platinum theater of "what newspaper would you prefer in the morning?". Oddly, never did get a newspaper without asking at the front desk. And then when the Sunday Times was all consumed, the front desk further asked our room number and said they would find and deliver one. Alas, no NYT. Enough of any criticism. But at the rates The Chatwal commands, I trust management raeds thses review and puts them to constructive use. Staff were uniformly friendly and very helpful. Ali, our room butler was great explaining the very high tech room controls and hotel features. I am not sure what else a room butler does for a guest, but Ali was both enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the property. Ali clearly prides himself on his workplace and the hotel. Nicholas Mullen, the concierge, was both accomplished and excellent. He obtained very difficult to obtain restaurant reservations at Le Bernardin for a civilized hour, and was knowledgeable and very professional. The Lambs Club is a good restaurant, with a nice wine list, excellent service, and good menu. For prix theater, it was a great choice. Breakfast was similarly well done, at reasonable, for this property, prices. The Kashwere Spa is small aka intimate with three treatment rooms, but the staff were excellent, the treatments superlative, and while expensive, we received great value. The hotel architecture is appealing, with the subtext of Stanford White and Thierry Despont interiors. Your room will compare favorably to the very best in terms of decor' and technology. We have enjoyed the Four Seasons, various Affinia proprerties, and others. Matching the boutique nature with Starwood benefits means that this hotel will likely do well. Thank you to Ali, Mr. Mullen, the spa staff, various bar tenders (mixologists), housekeeping et al. We enjoyed our stay. Mrs. Rowingman thought it was a wonderful spot, and isn't that what counts? Please read my criticisms as "the little stuff". But at the room rates commanded by the Chatwal, it is always the little stuff isn't it? I look forward to our next stay.

“Nice!” Opened just a few months ago; the hotel is located in affluent Lincoln Park neighborhood and very close to down town with a magnificent view of the lake and the park. The rooftop bar is great and the food and service are excellent. The rooms is clean and the bed is cozy and comfortable. Although my room was on the 10th floor, I still could hear the street noise especially on Friday and Saturday nights, but expected if you are staying in and busy city center like Chicago so bring you ear plugs. I enjoyed the stay but I feel it is a bit overpriced.

“Very nice” Stayed here for three nights in March. The guys at the door were really nice and helpful about getting cabs, into clubs, advice etc. The clerks were quite nice too. The single room is small as the massive bed takes away most of the space. The bathroom is super small considering the status of the hotel and room rates. The room itself is mostly white and comfy, but it sure is small. Theres not a lot of luggage space if it'd be two people in there. I worked an entire day on my laptop in the room and it felt comfy, so no complaints really. The food at the restaurant was allright, but hella pricey, but bar is nice. We went there friday night and as usual to get a table, you gotta buy a 300 dollar plus bottle. We just went in and sat at one of the free tables and no one came to bother us. The bar gets very full and it's not exactly a party vibe, but its a good chillout spot. The hotel's not in a particulary rough area at all, its the usual SF street scene. The location is superb, almost everything is a walking distance and the hotel is just a block or two away from the hustle and bustle, so it's not so busy there. Lots of good cafeteria's and restaurants around the premise.

“Awfull place with poor staff, dated rooms and lobby and not worth it!” I stayed here over New Years to visit Times Square one year and have to say it was a disaster! This place is close to Times Square like a block away but that is the only good thing about it. The place looks like it is straight from the 1930's with a dated lobby and poor staff not helpful at all and just all around bad service. The rooms are like closets and the price is outrageous. I would look around if you are thinking of even stepping into this mess since there are about 50 hotels in Times Square alone. The morning of check out the lift broke at the garage that had our car and we waited on New Years day literally 6 hours before they fixed it and got us out of the city. Never again would I go near this place or recommend it to anyone!!

“Loved the Affinia” We booked this great little boutique hotel thru Travel Zoo at a very reasonable price. It was rated at the time the number 2 hotel in Chicago. The Affinia lived up to the ratings. The decor was very modern and simplistic . I have never stayed in a hotel that had real HD TV. The location was great - just one block east of Michigan Avenue in the high rent district. The staff was very helpful and friendly.

“Wanted to rate it higher, but just couldn't...” You can't beat the location of the property. Located on Mission Bay, the ocean front property offers a nice pool, ocean access, a great beach path to walk the bay, nice grounds and conveniently located to a large number of San Diego's tourist attractions. I stayed at the hotel for 3 nights for a conference. The conference facilities were fine, but the the nice decor, linens and artwork in the rooms couldn't disguise how old the building is. It showed its age by having ill fitted doors(closet door wouldn't stay closed), few and poorly located outlets, and other inconveniences that newer properties don't have to worry about. Several(if not all, not sure) of the accommodations buildings are only stairs and accessed from the outside. Makes it challenging when you have a lot of luggage or event related items to pack in and out. The food in the cafe was really good, and overall service seemed fine.

“One of the Best Ever” After being bumped from the W Lakeshore because they were oversold, hotels.com helped secure me a room at the Trump. It was like dying and going to heaven. As dank and dismal as the W is, the Trump is nothing short of one of the finest properties I've ever stayed at. In addition to large, spacious, luxurious, sumptuous rooms and bathrooms, the real story here is impeccable service from the most professional staff I've experienced and interacted with. From top to bottom - the doormen, the reception staff, the concierges, there is AAA quality that is so rare these days. This must be the nicest property in Chicago these days, if not the nicest in the country. Absolutely 10 out of 10 experience for the discerning traveler and I highly, highly recommend. It is one of the few places that is expensive and worth it. My only regret is staying for only two nights. I would've loved to stay for a month.

“Biz travel with family along” stayed here bz of my marriott affiliation, but also because of the reviews. Clean, free wifi, coffee machine in lobby and rooms. more room than typical NYC hotels. Wasn't cheap by any stretch but the rooms was great, service was great, and location can't be beat for tours. My only complaint is the gym is really lacking outside of cardio equipment. Free weights are dumbells up to 25lbs only. no universal type machine. Staff very friendly, room was clean and view was awesome from 29th floor. would stay again.

“Loved the free wine!” Found this hotel with a great review on travelzoo.com when it was going for $100 a night - definitely a steal! My sister and I enjoyed the complimentary wine bar from 5-6. They were very generous pourers, and we quickly found ourselves talking to the other guests and sharing stories and tips about the city. The rooms were a little on the small side, but comfy, especially the beds and the down comforters and pillows! Aveda ammenities were also a nice touch. If breakfast is not included in the rate, I suggest skipping the hotel's b-fast and head out to one of the many dinners on your walk to union square. It will cost you less. Location is great and not too noisy. There is a section near the hotel that you shouldn't cross into at night, but we didn't have any trouble. Definitely would recommend the hotel, especially at $100 a night!

“Would Definitely Come Back” This was my first time in Denver and was in town for a mix of business and pleasure. The main reason for booking the Four Seasons was the price (I was able to get a corporate rate) and the positive reviews here on trip advisor. I took a taxi from Denver International Airport (Note that it is a flat rate coming from DIA. The taxi driver attempted to charge me the metered fare, which also happened to some of my coworkers.) I arrived around midnight and there was no line to check-in. After check-in, the front desk employee made the extra effort to come around the check-in desk and show me where the elevator bank was. I appreciated this extra effort. I stayed in a Deluxe room on one of the higher floors. Although my room was across from the elevator, I did not experience any noise issues at all. The room had a spectacular view of the mountains, which I could see from my bed. The room was also spacious and had a very contemporary feel. The bathroom was quite nice with a large glass shower and a tv in the mirror. There is twice daily turndown service which can be declined using the Do Not Disturb button next to the door handle. The towels and bath products are good quality. I experienced a couple minute wait while checking out and was only able to secure an hour extension to my check-out time. I would definitely consider returning to the Four Seasons the next time I am travelling to Denver for business or leisure.

“Good for families” First and foremost, this hotel is great for families. And that is why it's packed with families. If you really don't like children and want a peaceful breakfast, I recommend staying elsewhere. The breakfast was great, particularly for a family. The buffet was wonderful and the coffee nice and strong the way we like it. Watching the carp swim in the pools while eating breakfast is a lot of fun with young children. The restaurant on site has terrible service and I don't recommend it because of that reason only. The food was actually decent, if they remember to bring it to you. We went twice and regretted it twice. Other families had the same problems on different days so it wasn't just an isolated experience. The pool was fun for the kids and they also show movies in the afternoon for kids. Given the outreach to families, I wonder why they don't have a separate play area for younger kids. It would help keep them from running around the atrium. As a gold vip, I can tell you that there are no additional perks worth discussing (I did get two bottles of water, but for a 4 night stay, that's not much). Not even late checkout when I tried. Kevin or Keith (sorry, I can't remember his name correctly) is a wonderful bellman who is friendly to the kids and adults alike.

“NOT a Value” This property reminds me of a converted rooming house, and NOT a motel. While it may have had a slight facelift within the past 10 years, it could use a good cleaning. The rates are competitive with other properties in the neighborhood, but a far lesser quality of room. Add to the fact that all rooms are on the 2nd and 3rd floors, so bags must be carried up the stairs.

“Slebst für diesen Preis nicht zu empfehlen” Das Sub Bright Hotel ist eines, wenn nicht das schlechteste Hotel, in dem wir je waren. Das Hotel liegt in Chinatown und damit ziemlich zentral in Manhattan, der wohl einzige Pluspunkt des Hotels neben dem (verständlicherweise) günstigen Preis. Das fensterlose Zimmer war äußerst eng und schmutzig - überall waren schwarze Harre sowie diverse Flecken auf der Bettwäsche. Außer den Betten waren ein kleines Regal mit dem Fernseher, ein Waschbecken und ein einfacher, billiger Ventilator die einzigen Einrichtungsgegenstände im Raum, wodurch dieser auch schon gefüllt war. Das (shared) Bad war im Verhältnis zum Zimmer sauber. Obwohl wir nur beim Check-In und Check-Out mit dem Personal zu tun hatten empfanden wir es als unfreundlich. Im Zimmer war kostenloser Internetzugang über W-LAN verfügbar. Außerdem war es möglich einen hoteleigenen PC für den Internetzugang zu nutzen. Gegen eine Gebühr war es des Weiteren möglich Taschen und Koffer an der Rezeption abzugeben.

“It's okay.” Pros: *Convenient midtown location away from Times Square and close to Herald Square subway stations. Walking distance to Penn Station. *It's only been open for 6 months and everything for the most part feels new. *Although the bathroom is small, the shower has an upscale feel. *Contrary to a lot of the reviews, the front desk staff was mostly professional. My only gripe would be I requested a late checkout and don't feel this was handled correctly. I believe normal checkout is noon. I needed 3pm but would have been happy w/ 2pm. The front desk's original answer was a 12:30 checkout. I politely asked if my platinum status w/ Priority entitled me to something later than 12:30. I was given 1pm. Gee thanks. *It was kind of neat to have a view of the Empire State Building. *There's a free business center on the C level w/ two computers and a printer. It came in handy a couple of times. Cons: *The phone randomly rang a few times for no apparent reason. I called down to the front desk and asked why. They had no idea. *I've read a few reviews about having a mini-fridge and microwave. I had no such things. *Maybe I'm just spoiled, but the rooms are small. I know rooms in New York are generally smaller. I've stayed in close to a dozen hotels in New York, and with the exception of the Indigo in Chelsea and the closet I stayed in the at Herald Square Hotel, this was the smallest. *The surrounding neighborhood is kind of blah. You need to walk a few blocks before you find any restaurants/bars of interest. It's kind of disconcerting at night when all of the surrounding businesses have metal guards over their doors with random graffiti. I never felt like I was in danger or threatened. I just felt kind of deserted at night. Totally different story during the day. *Housekeeping failed to show up on twice even though the do not disturb sign was taken down before 1pm on both days. *The elevators could be painfully slow at times. I know there's not a freight elevator because the housekeeping and maintenance staff are constantly in the same elevator w/ the general public. Maybe if they had their own elevator it would speed things up.

“Good but not as great as other reviews” We had a fine stay here. The location was great. It was nice having the breakfast there, but the breakfast was more crowded than in other Homewood Suites and did not have as much of a selection. We had good service, but were not thrilled with our room. We had a view of a roof, and the room smelled like smoke. Management told us they thought it was coming from a nearby restaurant. The closet door was not working which made it hard to open and close. It did not seem as clean as other Homewood Suites. But overall, our stay was fine.

“Nice place to stay” Very nice property, rooms were a little small and view of heat vents on roof, but very clean and the staff was friendly. The perfect place to stay if going to a baseball game and also an easy walk to the inner harbor. The most comfortable beds I have every slept in at a hotel!

“Great Value, Super Location Friendly Staff” I have stayed many times in the Capital and Residence Inn more than meets my basic requirements and does so at a great price. This hotel is not fancy and has no frills but the service is above average, the breakfasts - which are included are much more than a cold bisket. There is a light meal 3 days a week. All support is near by from a deli, small grocery store, laundry (no hotel costs) two blocks to the metro and many many resturants with in walking distance. If that were not enough two great book stores near by. I will return!

“Great Stay!” We went to a Cowboy game and decided to stay at this hotel after the game. My wife and I were both suprised with how much we enjoyed our one night stay. The room we stayed in was very big and clean. This hotel has a very modern look. Normally I don't like that look but this hotel looked great and it was clean. The staff was very friendly. We had breakfast in the lobby and it was outstanding. If your staying in the Galleria area of Dallas, stay here and you won't be disspointed.

“BUG !! on the bed” We booked through their website, pick this location due to our business purpose check in at 5pm, all was OK it seems the manager family also living in the property. Our room is at 3rd floor, all seems fine, everything worked as advertised, just at bathtub there was some crackk that have been repaired but of course leaving some white stain unless replace it completely. when I woke up in the morning, found little bug on the pillow which I immediately squashed it ... but after my husband took shower there's another one !! I took the picture of it & will upload it once I have the time. we leave immediately & breakfast didn't open (next to reception) until 7 am, no time to alert the manager.

“overall good but not excellent” spent 3 nites 7/4-7/7. got an incredible deal on travelocity- $160/nt including parking. Had a room with a king sized bed- room was nice sized with a window seat facing lake shore drive and a partial lake view. pluses- location- excellent- millenium park- art institute a/c worked well- and it was 100 degrees every day partial lake view room concierge- very helpful minuses- valet for car- they said 10 minutes from calling for the car to delivery- one time it was 30 minutes- they forgot to put the request in - so we had to wait another 15 minutes once we arrived; one time it was 20 minutes. the other times it was 10-15. don't tell me 10 minutes unless it is 10 minutes. check in- very nice - but they neglected to give us a mini bar key- once we requested it- they sent it up immediately lobby- circular and a little confusing- felt we were walking in circles at one point. hallways- a little dingy for a fairmont would stay again if the price was right- like it was for us.

“Do not stay here. Do not book this hotel. Stay away.” WARNING, DO NOT STAY OR BOOK THIS HOTEL: This hotel will overbook its rooms (in other words, breach your hospitality contract and sell your room to someone else, even if you fully pre-pay your stay) and then attempt to waive its responsability. In some jurisdictions, selling the same thing (the right to occupy the room) twice, is considered fraud. Would you like to stay in a hotel that behaves in this manner? I did not think so... In my many (over 30) years of travelling, many of which have been for business travel around all continents and staying at hotels of all levels, from small family owned hostels to high-end Asian ultra-luxury palaces, I had never experienced such an unethical and illegal behaviour as the Hilton Boston FInancial District. This hotel does not honor its basic contractual obligations, even when stays ave been pre-paid. Leaves no option but to sue in court. The hotel does what is equivalent to you staying at the hotel and, then, in the end declaring that you are not paying for the stay, despite the contractual obligation to do so. Do not run the risk, stay elsewhere. There are plenty other ethical options in Boston. DON'T SAY I DIDN'T WARN YOU!

“Good deal- Great view” I stayed at the Westin Seattle for one night on business. It must be noted that I got a great rate of $110/night on Priceline. My feeling is that it was well worth the money and would have felt fine paying more. Check-in was a breeze. I checked in around cocktail hour and the lounge in the lobby looked to be full of people having a great time. I wish I would have had time to pop in for a drink. It would be a great place to have a business meeting or meet up with friends before dinner. Lots of comfortable seating arrangements. Room 3462 has an amazing view. (See pic--sorry it's so dark...but you get the idea. :)) I thought the room and the hotel were clean, modern and up to Westin standards. As always the toiletries were great and plentiful (no need to check your luggage.) I always love their robes, linens and pillows. It was also very quiet up there and that's a bonus in a city setting. The internet is not wireless in the room, but did work perfectly for a fee. Sitting at the desk in the room overlooking the city and water was really nice. The sofa/sitting area was another great place to lay out all my papers and use as an additional work area. The restaurant in the hotel does close at 9:30PM (which I thought was a little early for a downtown, business hotel.) I had to opt for room service. The food was very tasty and they have a good selection. It was priced very typically for this type of hotel in this type of location (not cheap, but you know going in it is going to be pricey.) I assume in that location that most people are eating out as there seems to be many hotels in the area. My only criticism would be the valet parking. I checked in at 5:30PM and left 11 hours later at 4:30AM. Looking back at my bill I realized I was charged $31 for valet parking. I'm not one to typically complain about hotel charges, but $31 for 11 hours seems excessive. I have no idea if they have self parking (I didn't see any), but that would certainly be worth checking out. I wish I would have had more time in Seattle. The shopping in the immediate area looked terrific. The big Nordstrom is within walking distance. I noticed that if you forget anything...the hotel has a personal shopper from Nordstrom that will deliver anything you need during normal shopping hours. It a good service to have in a pinch.

“A real architectural gem” Stayed here recently fo a meeting. The first thing that strikes you as you enter the hotel is the architecture and the space. It is clear this hotel has history in every corner of the buidling. Although historical the hotel is comfortable and welcoming. Check in was qucik and friendly, The elevators quickly whisked me to my high floor room. It was upon exiting the elevator and seeing corridors disappear into the distance that you realise that this is a BIG hotel a feature that is not so obvious at ground floor level. My room was thankfully a short distance from the elevator lobby and was well appointed and furnished. The bed was comfortable and the room had all the amenties that you could wish for. The hotel has a large numnber of meetings rooms of all sizes and decor - ranginf from a room in which Al capone allegedly played poker to a room that looked like a room in a medieval castle. these rooms are thread throughout a couple of floors and commuting between rooms was always an interesting orienteering exercise. I would certainly consider Palmer House if I were in Chicago again but I also really like a couple of other hotels in Chicago so it might come down to price on the day.

“HUGE hotel but well-organized” Enormous hotel located in downtown Dallas. Nice access to nearby eateries through a skybridge connecting the Sheraton to the Marriott next door. Eateries close around 5pm so prepare accordingly if you wish to eat outside the hotel. I was here as part of a convention of 3,000 and the hotel handled the crowds superbly. Very well-organized and orderly. Internet access is free if you use the hotel wireless in the lobby and about $15/day if you wish to purchase service in order to access the Internet in your room. A bit pricey but pretty standard for these larger scale hotels. Five banks of elevators are a bit confusing at first but once you gain an understanding of which one leads to your particular room, they are much more efficient that standard elevators which access all floors of a building. Comfortable room and nice soft bed. Starbucks coffee packs in the room made for a comfortable wakeup as well. I would recommend the Sheraton if you have a need to stay in the downtown Dallas area.

“Not that nice for a Sheraton” I stayed at the Four Point Sheraton next door to this hotel last year and it was horrible! I tried the Sheraton Suites on this trip and it was better. The staff was nice and the rooms were spacious. The hotel reminds me of an old embassy suites. The hotel is showing signs of wear: carpets in the rooms, walls in common areas, etc. I have stayed at much better and much worse. This property is the middle of the road. Next trip I will try the Hilton that is beside it.

“OK stay” Stayed 3 nights while visiting my kids who attend college in Boston. The lobby is small, nothing fancy, but clean. There don't seem to be too many people working at this hotel, just the front desk clerk and a guy to take your car if you opt for the valet parking. The room I had was spacious and clean, with a nice sized bathroom. Mini-fridge was a nice touch, as was the coffee pot in the room. There is a breakfast served, and it's ok, but seems a little pricey (buffet is $18). Walk over to the Lenox Hotel for amazing waffles, pancakes or french toast for about $15; or the Pour House pub on Boylston St. is open for breakfast; good meal for surprisingly cheap (less than $10 gets you pancakes, eggs and coffee). Overall, if you need a clean good-sized room in a nice location in the heart of Back Bay, this place may have a good price; compare deals with the many surrounding hotels. But don't expect anything else. Parking across the street at Prudential is convenient but expensive. If you're willing to park a few blocks over on Westland Ave, you'll save $15 per day.

“Great Location But Use Caution Regarding Noise!” I've had a love-hate relationship with Radisson Hotels for decades. The price point at most locations matches many upscale brands (Hilton, Marriott, etc.), but in the end my experiences suggest that the Radisson brand is only average value for the price point. The Seattle Airport location is great if you are doing business at/near the airport. You can literally walk from the terminal to the hotel in under five minutes. The property is clean and well kept, but by no means spectacular. Rooms are generous and well equipped. However, the TV's are old tube sets that are not on par with most other brands. Beds are comfortable. NOW FOR THE BAD PART!!!! This property has, without question, THE LOUDEST ELEVATOR I HAVE EVER HEARD! I arrived at the hotel around 11 PM and noticed the right-side elevator was closed for the night with a sign in front of it that read "Closed for Energy Conservation." Well, that may be true, but the REAL reason they close the elevator is because when it is operating the sound is deafening! I had a room on the 6th floor a few doors down from the elevator and was awakened by the noise when they turned it on around 4:30 AM. I asked to move to a different room and even though the room was considerably further away, you could still hear and feel the noise. Management confirmed that they are aware of the problem but had no idea if they would ever fix it. If you decide to stay at this property use caution and insist on a room far away from the elevator.

“Amabilidad y excelente zona” Sólo estuvimos 1 noche en este hotel porque éramos una familia de 4 y la habitación nos quedó un poco estrecha pero lo recomiendo ampliamente para 3 o menos personas x habitación. Me quedé gratamente sorprendida con la amabilidad del personal. La zona es perfecta, Georgetown a unas cuantas cuadras y por el otro lado Dupont Circle, en ambas zonas existen buenos restaurantes. Lo recomiendo ampliamente.

“A very good stay at the Grand Hyatt Washington” The hotel is a beautiful facility with very large rooms and bathrooms. We were given upon check in a King Room in the 11th floor over looking Downtown DC. The room was very clean and had very nice amenities. There were only two minor issues with the room. It is so dark in the shower that it is hard to tell if you got all of the soap off. And the King Bed was quite uncomfortable. It was very used and had not been updated in a while. I recently stayed in a Hampton Inn which had a new Pillow Top mattress which was ten times as comfortable as the Grand Hyatt Mattress. It was also ten times as inexpensive.

“Loved It” Planned a long weekend in NYC...partial work, partial girl's weekend and partial couple's weekend. Loved the hotel. A lot of room. Good ammenties. Excellent fitness center. Was treated very well by the staff. Twice given use of the house vehicle. Not cheap, but highly recommend. Also great sushi restaurant one and half blocks away from the hotel.
“UNIMPRESSIVE” While there was nothing glaring unappealing, I would not choose this property again as it is "worn" and in need of rehab. Pricing is on the higher end and isn't a value.
“Great location...” Location, location, location! Too bad the rooms and service did not exceed my expectations...there was no "wow" factor here, other than the location.

“Bei dem Preis unschlagbar, ansonsten okay” Ich kam dazu dieses Hotel zu buchen, da 25 EUR pro Zimmer/Nacht einfach unschlagbar war. Insgesamt ist die Lage nicht sehr zentral, jedoch durch den Central Park sehr schön. Mit der Subway ist man dann in bis zu 15 Minuten an Times Square, Grand Central oder 5th Avenue. 25 Minuten sind es bis zum untersten Ende Manhattans. Wir hatten zwei verschiedene Zimmer, da wir an zwei Wochenenden gebucht hatten: Zimmer 612 (glaube ich) Die Zimmer sind klein, aber nicht eng. Die Möbel waren okay, könnten jedoch mal wieder renoviert werden. Der Schrank war - wie bisher überall in den USA - ziemlich klein. Das Bad war verhältnismäßig groß, mit großem Spiegel und viel Ablagefläche. Ausgestattet war das Zimmer mit Fernseher, Telephon, Föhn, Klimaanlage, Bügelbrett. Die Fenster konnten auf beiden Zimmern nicht geöffnet werden. Zimmer 1102 Die höchste Etage des Hauses hat ein Besonderes Gimmick: Beide Zimmer hier haben je einen kleinen Balkon mit perfektem Ausblick über den Central Park auf die Skyline Manhattans. Ansonsten war das Zimmer größer als unser erstes Zimmer, jedoch stand hier auch noch zusätzlich ein Doppelstockbett drin. Das Bad hingegen war kleiner: weniger Platz, kleiner Spiegel, wenig Abstellmöglichkeiten. Das Zimmer war gleich ausgestattet, der Fernsehempfang war jedoch ziemlich übel - lag wohl am Fernseher. Minuspunkt in der Sauberkeit ist, dass meine Freundin beim zweiten Aufenthalt im Bad zwei kleine Härchen gefunden hatte. Der Service an der Rezeption war tadellos. Die Koffer wurden am letzten Tag bis zum Abend für uns kostenlos aufbewahrt. Leider gab es kein gratis Internet, was wir in NY sowieso nur im Applestore finden konnten. Wir würden dieses Hotel, mit entsprechendem Preis, auf jeden Fall empfehlen. + unschlagbarer Preis + schöne Lage - nicht soo zentrale Lage - in die Austattung könnte mal wieder investiert werden - kein gratis Internet - Sauberkeit beim zweiten Aufenthalt nur mangelhaft

“LOVE this Westin!” I stayed at this Westin for one night while tagging along on my boyfriends business meeting. We usually stay at Westins at this is definitely one of the nicer ones we have stayed at. The location can be pretty easy to miss due to construction but its fantastic (great for shopping) I forgot a pair of heels and the concierge directed us to Nordstrom just a few blocks away (and mapped it out for us) She said there was a Macy's and Filene's Basement in the opposite direction but I believe that was a few blocks further. The concierge also made a recommendation for a great Italian restaurant within walking distance (Coco Pazo) and made reservations for us as well. She's friendly but a little too chatty... The lobby is open to the restaurant/bar but the entire area gives off a trendy vibe. Check-in was quick, everyone was friendly and within just a few minutes we were in our suite. The suite (I forget which kind) was large - a wetbar area, living room/office, with seperate bedroom, and a huge bathroom. The entry way/wetbar had a wall of mirrors that led into the living room. There was ample seating (3 person couch, chair) flat panel tv, desk with Mac desktop and the room was so large it didnt feel cramped. The bedroom had a Kind bed, flat panel tv, seperate sitting area with chaise lounge and was still very roomy. The bedroom closet had more than enough hangers (I'm a stickler about this) The bathroom was HUGE - seperate stand shower, tub, but i do with there was a bit more counter space. There was more than enough towels in the bathroom and two bathrobes too. I absolutely love this Westin and hope we stay here again next time we're in Chicago!

“Great location but hotel disappointing” Location can't be beat. Lobby is welcoming and a variety of eateries, including a Starbuck's, are appreciated. Bellman and valet were excellent. Beyond these positives, the stay was disappointing. Hotel was frumpy and worn. Hallway was dingy. My room had a yucky stain on the chair, cobwebs in corners and did not smell fresh. "Free" web access was unreliable and paid upgraded web access was not much better. Room service was inaccurate. Very noisy at night, could hear everything from room next door and footsteps from room above (and there was a child who spent long hours between midnight and 4 am running and banging toys). Mini bar was never replenished. Noting all these things in the hotel provided survey did not elicit any response from the hotel.

“Don't Confuse The Hilton Club with the Hilton” Prior reviews lead me to believe that some travelers are confusing The Hilton Club with The Hilton. Yes, they are at the same address, but The Hilton Club is a hotel-within-a-hotel as well as a timeshare-type property and consists of suites located on the 37th and 38th floor with their own private check-in desk (and other services). You bypass the ground floor big front desk and ride dedicated elevators directly to the 37th floor. Hence The Hilton Club provides small hotel personal service in the context of a large hotel in a super central Manhattan location. I first stayed here years ago and liked it, but I always hunt up a luxury-bargain and The Hilton Club had not been turning up with favorable rates until a recent prepaid offer for $215 for 2. Not the best deal in mid-town you say? Check again; the rate included complimentary breakfast, complimentary wireless access, complimentary daily cocktail reception, plus gym and business center. The smallest room, the "euro-king" is neither huge nor cramped feeling; it's rather ship-like in that it makes really good use of the space, with lovely built in furnishings. The bed was terrific, a small table and chairs was okay for working, but not comfortable for sitting to watch TV. The large glass-walled shower had a rainfall head and also side jets with excellent water pressure. The stall was spacious and had a seat in the back. Aveda amenities and plenty of shelves complete the nice, if a little compact, but shipshape bathroom. The welcome desk always had two friendly attendants. The breakfast offerings were very nice and well presented; fresh fruits, yogurt, hard boiled eggs, cereals, super selection of baked goods, coffee, expresso, teas, juices, etc. Can't say what was offered at cocktail hour. All in all a very satisfying choice of lodging. A couple of caveats when you are hotel-shopping; be sure you are comparing apples to apples--what are the extra charges? If you shop for a rate and enter 2 adults, 0 children, when a list of options appear, be sure the "second person" is included. With Hilton and some other hotels, it may not be and when you proceed to booking there will be an "extra person charge." Be aware of what you are getting and what you are paying for in every case. At hotels.com, the extra person fee for this Hilton Club was $30/night; through Hilton directly it worked out to $17/night. If you need luggage storage here after check-out, be prepared to pay $3.50 per bag per 24 hours, plus tips.

“Beautiful hotel” I stayed at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront with a colleague while attending a conference at the San Diego Convention Center. The hotel is conveniently located right next door. Check-in was a breeze. Our room was roomy and extremely clean. The bathroom had awesome deep drawers in the vanity, which made it much easier to unpack. The pedestrian bridge over Harbor Blvd is open, pretty and a great asset. We used it several times to cross the street to get to the Gaslamp. if you want to see a Padres game, you are right across the street from the stadium too. The women we worked with at the concierge desk were extremely helpful. They made us 2 dinner reservations for exactly the time and place we wanted. They provided me with a handy jogging map. I personally watched them work with multiple guests at one time and it appeared that they were keen on satisfying all reasonable requests. We originally planned to check out the morning of our departure, but our flight was a redeye that was not leaving until 10:30pm. We contacted the front desk about extending our stay, and they made it possible for us to keep our room until 8:30 that evening. Although we had to pay for an extra night (because we were staying past 5:30), it was nice that they were able to accommodate our request at the last minute -- it took all of 5 minutes. One note for business travelers -- the UPS Store runs the hotel's business center. You will be charged an extra fee to send or receive any packages at the hotel in addition to your regular shipping charges. This can get pricey depending on your needs, so be careful. All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel to any business or leisure travelers who want a modern, upscale, conveniently located hotel near the Gaslamp/Convention Center.

“Amazing” We stayed in the king suite. It was huge. The doors were thick and we could put our light sleeping toddler down each night in the living room and retreat into the bedroom and she slept soundly. Enroll in the rewards program before making your reservation to get free Internet and $10 towards the mini bar. For all there is free hot cocoa in the afternoon and wine in the evening. Location is fantastic but still quiet enough. Restaurant on site was convenient and has nice filling breakfasts. The only negative was the metallic thump in the bathroom, which when we asked we were told was from flushing in others bathrooms. We closed the door and slept through it...noticed it most in the morning and after dinner.

“Great family run motel” Stayed here again with the family, 3rd time. As usual check in was seamless and the husband and wife team ensure the place is well kept. Not too near downtown and all the better for it as you can drive or catch public transport easily from here. Thanks we will return.

“Fabulous” If location is important..this hotel is fantastic. Walk directly into Macys from the hotel. Great shopping in walking distance of the "magnificent mile". The hotel: Check- in was a breeze even though our room was not ready (our fault..arrived too soon.) The desk clerk walked out from behind the desk and literally escorted us to the restaurant where we waited for the room and had a fantastic lunch. How about a "pork belly flat bread pizza"? A "cherry smash cocktail"?. I know...sounds a little funky but what flavor! And the wild salmon was cooked to perfection. Service was perfect. We were not yet checked in and the servers knew our names...typical Ritz standards. We had a suite with two bathrooms...wife loved that. AC was quiet and able to cool to 68....we like it cool when sleeping. Entrance to the hotel is a little congested but the valets handled it efficiently. As a matter of interest, the Hotel is not part of the Ritz Carlton family...only the name licenced some years ago to Four Seasons to provide the Ritz Carlton branding in the Chicago area. It's a little pricey buy hey...it's a Ritz...or a Four Seasons...either or, it's a winner!

“Un brin viellot” Trés bien situé,proche de Central Park. Hotel un peu viellot,je trouve,mais bon rapport qualité prix. L'ascenceur fait un peu peur,le plancher grince,mais leurs suites sont grandes et bien aménagées. La literie est bonne pour les grands lits,en revanche les canapés convertibles offrent beaucoup moins de confort! Petit déjeuner copieux et pas cher environ 6$. C'est bien pour les familles car les chambres sont grandes,dotées de nombreux rangements et on peut y prendre le repas(petit coin kitchinette). Why not??

“Location, location, location and the hotels great too” We always stay at Westins when we have a choice. The Dallas Westin Galleria never dissappoints. It is a great stay. I booked the room on a third party website and reserved 2 queen beds. Upon arrival the reception said that there were not any of that type room available. I told him that it was what I had booked and he said those were only "preferences" on third party sights. I told him I knew the difference and that this was not what I booked. He asked to see my confirmation. I showed it to him and he made a way to honor my booking. The beds are the most comfortable stay although I do not prefer the sliding glass door on the bathroom. It has no lock therefore when it accidently slides open it can be quite awkward for a son-in -law when sharing a room with your mother-in-law. Unlike the other Westins we have stayed in this year, the a/c seemed to work very good and keep the room cool. The location of the hotel was excellent. Being connected to the galleria is great for having an infant. When my husband or myself need a little extra sleep in the morning, the other one of us had a great place to take the baby on a walk. The restaurants in the area are great. We love the Westin Galleria.

“Good stay” We stayed here one night when we saw Bon Jovi at the Arena. Hotel was easy to get to. Safe walk to and from the Arena. Room service ended at 11 so we couldn't get anything after the concert. We decided to get it for breakfast but found out you had to have your order marked and outside your door before you go to bed. Just weird. The room was clean. The hallways are confusing as well. We twisted around turn after turn to get to our room.

“Super location, design, (almost) everything” We are a small family of two adult and one 9 year old child. We were in New York to celebrate my (I'm the mom) 40th Birthday. From home, we could not decide between this hotel and the Thompson LES, so we had originally booked 4 nights at Crosby and 3 nights at the LES. But we fell totally in love with the Crosby, and after 2 nights we asked if it was possible to stay for a full week at our lovely Junior Suite on the 10th floor. At first, it seemed as if they were fully booked, but the staff did everything they could and we ended up staying 7 nights in the same room. The room: Upon arrival, we were given a room on the 4th floor overlooking the courtyard. We are big fans of light and views, and asked if they could put us in another room. Again, staff did everything they could and finally gave us the most perfect room located on the 10th floor - great views over the LES, Soho and Brooklyn Bridge in the distance. Big window, beautifully designed, enormous bathroom with tub and shower. The room was not ready for us, but we were treated to a drink on the house in the lovely library room (hotel guests only) while they made up the room for us. The hotel is gorgeous - we love the Firmdale hotels in London, but this hotel really beats them all. The restaurant, the library room - every-where's quirky and beautiful and a real treat to the eye. The location is (in my opinion) the BEST in NYC! Restaurants, galleries, shops, cafes - all are within walking distance. And the subway is just around the corner. What really makes this hotel stand out is the staff - nothing was too much trouble... they even remembered my birthday and gave me a tray of cupcakes. The only thing they need to straighten out is the service at breakfast. The breakfast staff seemed confused and disorganized. We had to ask several times for EVERYTHING - But everything that finally did arrive on our table was delicious, and we had it included, so this is just a minor comment, but someone ought to help the staff organizing the routines at breakfast. There was a lot of running around and forgetting everything on the way... That said, we really did enjoy our stay and will not hesitate to recommend it! It is expensive, but worth it if you appreciate beautiful designs and comfort and a small hotel in a superb location. We are looking forward to coming back.

“Needs Updating” My wife and I just spent three nights here. The hotel is in a very good location near the Convention Center and 16th St. Mall. The staff is very friendly and the hotel is clean and quiet. However, the room was drab but adequately appointed. Housekeeping service was efficient. The public areas on the first floor are outdated and in need of a total renovation. The "business center" consists of two pc's and a printer that did not work when we were there. The restaurant and bar area are dreary. We have stayed in several Crown Plaza properties but this one did not measure up to most in appearance and amenities. However, we got a very good deal on Priceline so the value was certainly there.

“Great place for the money” Hey, for the money it’s a great place. In the right neighborhood surrounded by other big chain hotels. Within minutes by taxi from the Westlake Center, where the Light Train to and from SEATAC Airport stops ($2.50 each way) also with a great Food Court at the station. The Inn has a large inviting lobby, rustic style with a real-flame fireplace. Exceptionally friendly reception (by Chris.) Rooms are small but adequate for sleeping but not much else. You don’t go there for romantic encounters or to impress Mama how far you’ve made it in life. Bathroom tiny but sparkling clean. Continental breakfast on the house even includes scrambled eggs and sausage. Wow. For a one or two night sleep for the money it seems unbeatable.

“Outstanding!” On a spur of the moment impulse I decided to "kidnap" my husband and take him to Philadelphia for our anniversary. We go there a few times a year -- and have stayed at the Sofitel (loved it), Four Seasons (liked it), Ritz Carlton (loved it but we were on the concierge floor and that made it special) and the Hyatt Penn's Landing (eh?). The Rittenhouse, at a starting price of $450 for a standard room, has always been outside our budget. But oddly -- and it must be said we wanted a one night stay over Memorial Day weekend, not a high season time for Philly -- i got a $300 rate, using Kayak.com (of course the Ritz Carlton was offering rooms at $225 or so; you could tell it was a dead weekend). So, sorry for the long story, but I booked it. And as said -- outstanding. Not perfection but close enough and, value for money, worth the cost. At $300 that is. Like others have said, we were greeted on check in with champagne and strawberries -- nice touch (never stayed at a Four Seasons or Ritz Carlton that does that). They welcomed me "back" and either they were able to pull up a stay some seven years ago (and pre-husband) or they were just being...nice...but the first impression was absolutely lovely. And even for our cheapie fare, we were given a lovely room, fronting the park. Overhearing that it was our anniversary, a waiter shortly after we got to our room delivered fruit and Fiji water. Nice touch. I remember staying at Kennebunkport's pricey White Barn Inn for our actual honeymoon and management didn't as much offer a "congrats". The service continued to be exceptional throughout (and I'm alas picky and just was...purring). The location right on the Square (and there are some neat bistro/restaurants behind, on 20th Street, worth a look). Perfect. The room was big enough (and the bathroom was sumptuous, separate bath and shower, thirsty towels, flat screen tv (which we never used). All in all, very very excellent. Only criticisms: the rooms are big though oddly shaped and that wasn't a big deal but I was surprised that the furnishings were so dated. Dark replica mahogany furnishings, etc. Clunky "old fashioned" television in clunky dark armoire didn't fit the hotel's vibe (or price point; there should have been a DVD player). The mini-bar carried really cheap wine by the half bottle; again, not fitting. Will say we loved the iPod dock! The only other downer was its in-hotel bar; the Boathouse is alas, dark and claustrophobic (but honestly the neighborhood is so vibrant it wasn't a big deal). We didn't get to Lacroix (went to Le Bec Fin instead and that's another story). Also didn't even know about the pool until it was too late. Good excuse to go back but wouldn't spend much more than $300....

“...hat die besten Zeiten hinter sich” Das Hotel ist von der Lage sehr zentral und hat von der Zimmerausstattung das Gefühl hoher Individualität. Ein Gas-Kamin auf Knopfdruck hat wirklich viel Charme insbesondere vermutlich in den kalten Herbst- und Wintermonaten....an einem warmen Tag heizt das Ding sonst etwas zuviel. Die Zimmer sind super aber sehr dunkel. Wer es hell und freundlich mag, ist in diesem Hotel falsch. Das sollte man sich bei 500 USD pro Nacht schon genau überlegen. Der Lobby-Bereich sowie das Engagement der Mitarbeiter hat die besten Zeiten hinter sich. Das angegliederte Restaurant ist definitiv nicht empfehlenswert! - Zum Frühstück dann noch lieber zum Dunkin Donut und der ist auch nicht toll....

“Unexpected stay due to the hurricane.” My friend and I were travelling Amtrak from Arizona to Washington, DC. I saw this coming, but we were notified that our train from Chicago was cancelled on the day we were scheduled, due to all the disruptions from Hurricane Sandy. I tapped out a reservation on my Smartphone for a one night stay at the Allegro. ( I was looking for an excuse to stay at another Kimpton in Chicago, having stayed at the Palomar and Monaco. ) I see the previous reviewer's complaint about parking, which should not be a surprise. I parked a couple of years ago at the Monaco, and it was around $43 per night at that time. I agree, these charges make me wince, but that is to be expected when parking at a hotel in a major city. However, we were blissfully without a car and the tension of driving into such places and the Allegro is walkable from Union Station. As evidenced by some of my other reviews, I am a big fan of Kimpton hotels. My travel companion and I certainly enjoyed the Allegro, which is the largest of the Kimpton chain, with 483 rooms. The staff, as always, were most hospitable and we enjoyed the restaurant. The room was fine - my fault with it was that it was large enough to have some kind of lounge chair. The only chair was at the desk. Also, there was no arrangement with a health club for a gym and use of a pool, which was the case last year at the Monaco. Otherwise, all was fine. We were rebooked on the next day's Amtrak train to Washington and went to the Hotel Rouge, another Kimpton, and had a fine time there.

“Top notch mid-town hotel” Stayed for one night only after a disaster at another chain - i found it excellent - i booked on the phone via their reservations - having told them my woes the girl was very friendly and said i'd be much better looked after - which i was to be fair! - super friendly check in girl looked after me very well, had heard about me leaving the last hotel, and gave me a free upgrade - huge room with very comfy bed and plenty of nice touches here and there - great bathroom with massive tub, good shower - and lots of towels which is something of a rarity these days superb midtown location - very cool lobby bar, with lots of beautiful staff - i found them efficient, but not exactly friendly - not unusual for this type of hotel in NYC - yes its very 'hip' and may not be to everyone's taste - but i really enjoyed my stay and would look to back

“Lovely huge suite - great weekend value” Just completing a quick visit to Chicago with the kids. The hotel has a great location - Michigan avenue just north of the River. Our suite was a high floor tucked away in a corner and was huge with a huge bathroom and separate powder room. The suite is easily close to 600sq ft but feels much larger. The bedroom could easily accommodate two king beds instead of one and still a loveseat, a desk, etc. The bathroom was lovely as well. My kids were there Thrilled. In their minds, the only negative was the lack of a pool. The weekend rate made our stay a good value. Usually for quick trips with kids I stay in a Residence Inn, Embassy suite, etc. For this trip I wanted to feel like more a vacation for me as well. As my kids told me, "Mommy, whatever you paid extra for this hotel, it was worth it."

“Worth staying here if you can get a good rate” We stayed here for one night during a frigid and snowy January weekend after seeing a concert at the Fillmore Theater. After seeing the weather forecast, we decided the weather was too bad to make the drive back to Lansing and to stay in Detroit overnight. We made the reservation the same day naming our own price using priceline. This hotel was rated a 3.5 star and we bid $70. We were really surprised we got this hotel for that price considering this was also the auto show weekend. For $70, we felt we got an incredible deal. This hotel is located in the center tower of the massive Renaissance Center. Our room was on the 54th floor and we got a birds eye view of downtown Detroit. The windows are floor to ceiling due to the hotel being housed in a glass tower. Due to the cold temperatures, however, we had to keep the drapes drawn most of the time to keep the freezing cold from infiltrating the room. The room is a little oddly shaped due to the circular tower it is housed in but it felt spacious enough. Our room also had a large closet and a flat screen tv. The furniture and decor looked recently updated. One nice part about the circular design of the hotel is that there are no long depressing corridors when you get to your room and there are only about 25 rooms on each floor. Another nice thing about this hotel is that it is easy to get to the people mover, which will get you just about anywhere you want to go in Downtown Detroit . The people mover can be used to get to the convention center (Cobo), Joe Louis Arena, Ford Field, Conmerica Park, or Fox Theatre and it only costs 50 cents one way. I highly recommend the people mover to get around downtown Detroit as it is much easier than trying to walk or drive Detroit's confusing jumble of streets and it is well patroled and safe. The Marriott has valet parking for $20 but if you are there on a weekend, you can self park for only $6/day. The self park garages are located on your left, just after you turn off of Jefferson into the drive that leads to the hotel. The skywalk connecting the garages to the Renaissance Center is located on the third floor. As other have commented, the massive Renaissance Center can be a little bit confusing to get around. Besides housing the hotel this is also the headquarters of GM. However, there are tons of signs as you walk around and if you follow the signs, you should have no problem. Anyways, you can't get lost since the buildings are circular. The worst that happens is you come back to the place where you started. Overall, if you can get a reasonable rate, I highly recommend the Renaissance Center Marriott.

“Good Location, Good Value” I have stayed at this location twice. Once in 11/05 with family and once in 1/06 on business. Pros - Good price (for New York) - Great midtown location - Marriott quality and service - All rooms appear to have been recently remodeled with new Marriott look. - Awesome TVs - large flat screens! Cons - - Small rooms - Lower floors get lots of street noise - The lobby has limited storage for luggage so storage is a tough job for the bellman. They are usually grumpy about it - but they have good reason to be! Plan a few extra minutes to store/retrieve your luggage.

“Hands-Down Best Budget Hotel with Best Location” I frequent NYC often (as it is the best city on Earth) and when it comes to affordability without sacrificing cleanliness and location the only place is the Edison Hotel. No other property can possibly beat this location while still offering a sane price. It is old, and some rooms are aged.....if you can handle this then there is no other. You walk out the doors and you have a Starbucks to the right and one to the left. All Time Square attractions are within footsteps. You will live, taste and feel what New York is all about while staying at the Edison....for you are in the heartbeat of the City. An added feature,one not even offered at some 5 star properties is that they require you to show a room key before entering the elevators. You have a lobby and a 24 hr. deli next door. Rooms they call double/double are a must for families since these are much larger than their ordinary rooms which are a bit small.

“Loved This Resort!” We stayed at this resort from 6/15-6/22 it was our first time staying at this Marriott Vacation Club. We own at Marriott Shadow Ridge in Palm Desert Ca and thought we'd like to try a different resort for a change. We were not disappointed. although Canyon Villas is a much smaller resort. we actually liked the compact layout w/ the resort. We stayed in a 2 bedroom villa overlooking the courtyard and future construction it was a quiet area near the b-b- q area. The rooms were actually slightly larger than what we have at our home resort and everything was new and updated. The pool area was close by and worked well for our family. The bar area there is very small and the lobby/marketplace/maze was also much smaller than what were used to but everyone who worked there was friendly and helpful it really didn't matter. Also, there were several group activities planned for the children daily with a great staff. The JW Marriott was a short drive or even walking distance if its not too hot. Our children enjoyed the lazy river and we spent a couple of days enjoying that resort as well. It was convienent that we could charge drinks and lunch there to our Canyon Villas room and they had our names on their resort list for towels which was nice. The Desert Ridge shopping Ctr is close by for everything from supermarkets, movies, to nice restaurants you really don't need to go far for anything if you just want to stay close to the resort. We would highly recommend this resort to any family who enjoys a good timeshare resort. I believe in reading other reviews here some people with higher expectations don't fully understand how a timeshare resort works. It is not an all inclusive resort with room service, 24 hour activities, restaurants, bars etc.. It is however a great place to bring your family ,stock up your fridge and relax and enjoy your stay!

“Amazing Back Bay and River views” I've stayed at this property a few times now. The hotel is attached to the indoor mall that runs along part of the Back Bay which makes it convenient when the weather is bad or you need to get to and from the conference or office quickly. From our mid-floor room we had very good views of the Back Bay and the river. At night is was quite beautiful to see all the buildings lit up. The room itself was okay. The bathroom was quite small for the size of the room we had (junior suite). Also, the room had adjacent doors to the next door room which made noise transfer from the other room quite loud (there was a 5 year old in the room next door who like to yell and jump around). One of the biggest issues I have with this hotel is the lack of water pressure. I think several other reviewers noted it as well. It's definitely noticeable. Also, specific to our room, the bed was very squeaky as if the box spring was broken. Last but not least, if you drive your vehicle to this hotel, beware that valet parking overnight at the hotel is around $50 (I think it's like $47 and change).

“Great Location in Northwest Washington” While rooms are small (as with most in DC), the beds were extremely comfortable and the service was outstanding. From check-in to breakfast to checkout, the staff really seemed to be going out of their way to make our stay a very pleasant one which is just what I want from a hotel!

“Huge convention hotel, comfortable” Wear your track shoes to get around this place, especially if you use the self parking. Nice service and rooms. In lobby they had folks offereing glases of lemonade or ice tea which was nice. Not sure if that;s usual or for the state Democratic convention that was starting while we were there. Location ws convenient to Minute Maid Park. We walked the 6 blocks to the Astros game, and caught a pedi cab back. Price would have been too high but we got a deal through a discount site which made it worth it.

“Poor Choice” I arrived at this hotel in the morning after a long red-eye, eager for a rest. I asked at the front desk when my room might be ready. I was told "Check-in time is 3 p.m." Of course, I knew that. I asked again whether I might be given some idea when the room might be ready, since 3 p.m. was hours away, and it seemed very reasonable to think it might be ready earlier. The clerk sniffed,"I don't control the room cleaning." I groped for some shred of accommodation, to no avail. I returned at 3 p.m. I was led to a room was about as small as could be and still contain the beds, dark and with virtually no decor or artwork, no view, no anything--absolutely minimal, like a cut-rate motel room. And the price was by no means a bargain; the Excelsior two blocks away was a little more expensive for a much nicer room in a much nicer building with a more accommodating staff. I'll never stay at the Park 79 again.

“Nice updated property, sketchy area” The lobby area is all new and the breakfast was one of the best I've seen at Hamptons and I travel weekly. The rooms are large but you can tell this was an older hotel that is being refurbished. Some of the tiles are replaced, but the wallpaper is still old as are some of the fixtures in the guest bathrooms. This location is very close to the airport, Old Town, and the highway, but the neighborhood is still a bit sketchy with a strip club about a block away. No surveillance system yet outside, which worries me a bit. Good prices for the location just keep your kids close.

“Trendy Bar, for the Beautiful people ( and Me )” Hotel Bar with a nice quality feel, great service with a great range of cocktails, not overpriced for the location, no real views, but a screen with a camera viewing outside from the 5th floor. W have a style and New York W is no exception, plenty of seating and private areas, nice feel, nice tunes, not too loud, def worth a visit, for cocktails and not the same same Irish or Sports bars. Probably had a few older men leering.. probably had ladies that cater for that market.

“Lots to like.” Yes, it's older, but there's a lot to like about this Embassy Suites property. We like the self-catering possibilities, with a microwave oven and fridge in the room and a gas barbecue available, dining in is easy (housekeeping provides dishes). The pool is well laid out for sun and shade. Custom-cooked breakfast and "happy hour" are included in the price. Ask for a room on the side without a parking lot for the quietest night. While there isn't much to walk to in the neighbourhood, there's a handy grocery store a block west and a decent Italian restaurant a few blocks east. Beer and wine are readily available at a market a block east.

“Nickel and dime” Rooms dated and old, then they nickel and dime you to death. Fee for gym, fee for internet but a free newspaper! Friendly helpful people at the front desk. Free printing for the boarding pass...but watch the fees!

“Very nice for the price” This hotel is definitely worth the price. The customer service is excellent, and the shuttle is very convenient. The hotel has been recently updated and is very clean, which is most important. The breakfast is also good. As others have mentioned, the area isn't the nicest, although I wouldn't say it was scary. There just isn't a lot around until you get to Old Town. The hotel is right on the freeway, but we didn't hear it from our room, which was on the other side. The complimentary parking was also a bonus. On the negative side, the wifi wasn't the fastest, but it was definitely better than nothing and was free. My biggest complaint is that you have to call to have the shuttle come pick you up at the airport. This wouldn't be a big deal except it doesn't say that's what you have to do anywhere on the website. After waiting a half hour at the airport, which is the last thing you want to do after traveling for 6 hours, we called and the shuttle came. It would have been nice to know that before though. Despite this, our overall experience was good and we would definitely come back.

“Best place to stay in Philly” I was attending a conference at another hotel, but chose to stay at the Sofitel because the TripAdvisor reviews were better. I wasn't steered wrong. The entire hotel was spotless and the room was beautiful. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the food at the restaurant was delicious. All of the staff were friendly and helpful. I would suggest taking the package they offer which includes the parking and breakfast. It's a much better deal than paying for each separately.

“Plush and historical; poor network access.” This is a very nice hotel located a short walk away from the Woodley Park Metro stop, which makes sightseeing throughout Washington very easy. The long list of prestigious guests and the use of the site in a feature film were impressive. If you're planning to stay here or at another Omni property, be sure to sign up for membership in their Gold program. You receive free internet access and bottled water. The network repeatedly dropped me throughout the visit. The nature of the conference that we were attending meant that just about every participant had an electronic device, but you'd think that they'd have a more robust system. I was initially assigned to the wrong type of room, and the door locks didn't work properly on the second one. These minor problems, which were quickly addressed, are accounted for along with the inadequacy of internet service in the "Service" rating.

“Bad experience, no follow up” Typically, I enjoy the old world charm of the Waldorf Astoria in New York. My room was of a decent size, but unfortunately, my experience was a disaster this time, including a horrible brush with customer service. The tv did not function in my room, and I immediately called to have it fixed. When I had returned to my room 3 hours later, it was still not functioning. Another call to the manager on tap, and I was assured that a) it would be fixed in the morning or b) I would be moved to another room (it was already past midnight at the time). I was also offered a free night stay to make up for the inconvenience; an operable tv in the room is not really a big ask. The next morning, I went to have breakfast at Oscar's included in my room rate. The woman who assisted me that morning was an absolute nightmare. The front desk had given me a single voucher to cover two days of breakfast for the duration of my stay. The waitress at Oscar's yelled at me, grabbed the voucher, and told me that I would have to wait on line to go get a voucher for the second day. It was a horrible experience. I went to the front desk to complain, and again, I was assured that a) my tv would be fixed and b) they would send me a voucher for a free room to compensate for the horrible service I had received during my stay. Well, the tv was finally fixed, a full 24 hours after I had arrived. The voucher? It never arrived. I have never had such horrible service in my life, and it's doubtful that I will return to the Waldorf Astoria in New York -- so many other options in the neighborhood.

“Excellent hotel in the heart of Philly” We stopped over Philly on the way home from the Carolinas. This hotel came highly recommended. The staff was super-friendly and helpful. The location is excellent - right in a residential part of the town - not too noisy, but still bustling with life. Their breakfast was adequate and healthy - we liked the fact that they used real plates, cups and utensils - minimizing waste. The parking is about 5 min. away - a bit inconvenient for us because we had small children. There was also no ramps at the entrance for a stroller to get into the hotel. Minor things, though. We still think the hotel is a great find in the city.

“Great value” Stayed 3 nights at this hotel near Lake Shore drive north of downtown Chicago. Great price for its location. The hotel is old, with an old fashioned elevator that is charming but very inconvenient when you have luggage. The rooms and furnishing are old but the rooms are clean. A generous breakfast is complimentary. Some of the staff are more helpful than others though all I encountered are friendly. This hotel has an arrangement with a parking garage next door which made parking a breeze. Overall I had a pleasant stay for the price and would recommend this hotel to people not seeking luxury.

“Great location - how do they keep out the street noise?” This was a cool, modern, clean hotel in a perfect midtown location - just a few blocks from Rock. Center. It is hands down the quietest hotel I have ever stayed at in NYC. I heard no street noise and no hallway noise (even though my room was right on W. 45th St. and right across the hall from the elevator. Bed was super comfy and the shower was one of the best. The mini bar had all this Dean and Deluca stuff - I spent $16!! I booked this place through Travelocity's secret hotel search - I couldn't have been happier with how it ended up!

“Great stay at Windsor Suites” My family (husband,10 yr old son and myself ) spent 4 nights at the Windsor. Everyone was very nice and helpful from the front desk to the engineers. If we asked for something it was always there within 10 minutes The hotel is within walking distance to quite a few historical sites also. The only thing we didn't like about the location was that everything was closed by 6 pm so you had to go out of the area to find something at night. But all and all it was a nice stay and I would book there again.

“Mixed feelings” We stayed for one night during a recent trip and I have pros and cons to report based on our experience. Pros- The shuttle was prompt picking us up at the airport. Check-In was fast and courteous The hotel lobby and exterior is very inviting and clean Indoor pool looked very nice Room, although dated, was spacious and offered several amenities(Room 509) Room service was prompt and reasonably priced Breakfast was sufficient in the morning with made to order eggs. The front desk was very helpful when we picked up our Rental Car and need to park for a little while before checking out. The Budget Rental Car is directly across the street from the hotel Cons The room was clean but dated. I don't know if other rooms have been updated. There was an extreme amount of noise coming in from the street. I am actually hearing impaired but the amount of traffic noise and airplane noise made it difficult to sleep soundly. We liked the Embassy Suites but the dated rooms and the noise level that we experienced would make me shop around next time before booking here again. We are Hilton Honors Members and choose this hotel for the points.

“Great service & hotel” Had an easy check in check out at this hotel. Front desk was extremely pleasant ( i believe her name was Ali). Hotel room is very modern and typical morgan hotel style. Sleek & contemporary. Loved the bathroom, no tubs ladies. Bed was SUPER comfy. Was only there for one night but will be coming back again. Location was great walking distance from South Station. Unfortunately left my favorite belt in the room and I have yet to hear back from housekeeping and security if they have found it :(. Overall great hotel. Lil pricey but your paying for the amenities.

“Nice Place” I was in for the Phialdelphia Marathon & this modern hotel was great. It is right across the street from City Hall and a walkign distance to the museums, the marathon start and even to the Reading Market (which one must visit). The location is well worth the price and we chose to park the "car ourselves" which is the same parking lot the valets do. This saved us a lot since parking is 45 bucks a night. The parking lot has a weekend daily rate of $5 bucks for 24hrs and it is about 4 blocks away, just ask where. I loved this option and thank the doorman for telling us. The hotel's "check-in" was the only place needs work, the ladies in the front need to be more "open", smile just a little more, suggest more, I didn't find the concierge at all while I was there so they had to be the back-ups & they really didn't have much to suggest. My hubby used the gym and liked it, did it's "job" as he stated. The rooms were a good size and you need to ask for what you expect out of your room, they are pretty open to assign what you need. If you need more privacy then ask to be away from the atrium, if you want quiet, ask to go up and in the middle...a city view is not needed but it's nice since most rroms there don't have one. The lobby is cool to but remember to go left when you land, that is where the "check-in" is as the bar is actually the center of the lobby. Overall, a good choice with a good location, an okay block (walk out of it) and a good vibe.

“Great hotel - would definitely return (if I can afford to!)” Having moved away from NYC after years of being a true "New Yorker," I've always found it difficult to stay in a hotel when I come back into the city, and have been able to, for the most part, avoid it by crashing at friend's places when they are out of town. Recently though, everyone was staying local when we came to visit, and I booked a room at Gild Hall for a surprisingly low price online at quikbook.com. The site had the warning caveat that the hotel was under construction (thus the low rates, no doubt) during renovation. We assumed, safely, that there would be little interfering noise on a weekend stay and booked a standard king room. New York City hotel rooms are notoriously tiny with variable amenities and equally variable staff attentiveness - imagine our surprise to enter into a quiet little world of wonderful. I almost hate to write this review and "out" the hotel, a supreme gem hidden waaaay downtown, but I feel like I should share our experience. The entrance is on a tiny side street, off Gold St, a 5-7 min walk from the Fulton St subway stops which serves nearly all major subways lines one could want for. While the hotel undergoes renovations, the lobby is the size of a cubby, but who needs more than that for check in? We were double upgraded, they informed us, to some sort of deluxe king room, compliments of the hotel, and whether it was a line or a true upgrade, the sentiment was kind and the room lovely - unbelievably high ceilings, even spacious by NYC standards. The bathroom was huge and came with 'fresh' brand toiletries - quite highbrow, actually, and a thoughtful addition. The room had the requisite and now ubiquitous iPod docking station and flat screen TV and an extremely comfortable bed. As we were getting ready to go out, turn down service rolled by, and while we declined, it was a nice touch for a fledgling boutique hotel. The room was quiet, dark, and blessedly free of radiator rattles, construction, or hallway noise even though we were right across from the elevator. The water in the shower was hot, the robe in the bathroom sumptuous and everything clean and orderly. Quite honestly - what more could you expect or want for?? I know the hotel will grow, the Todd English tavern will move in, and I imagine it will become quite the hot spot downtown with prices to match (other Thompson group hotels are NOT cheap!) but in the meantime, its well worth booking a room (even if its further downtown than you might normally consider!) in order to have the little quiet luxuries that Gild Hall offers before everyone else finds out about them, too.

“Mixing Business and Family Fun- Not too Shabby” This was a quick weekend trip to a destination not too far to home. The Marriott staff was welcoming upon our arrival. The doorman and the lobby staff were friendly. We experienced an effortless registration, which was a good thing as we were unaware that there was a college-group convention scheduled for the same time we stayed. Registration staff offered several good non-hotel dining options for us (we traveled with kids.) Unfortunately, our baggage got lost from the bellhop to delivery to our room and it took a few phone calls for the staff to find it and deliver it (they were very apologetic) Room Pluses: Our room was on a high floor as we requested when we made our reservation, and we had a remarkable view of the entire inner harbour and city. Amenities in the room were typical Marriott: "Bath and Body Works" toiletries, somewhat rough (but abundant) towels, Kurerig coffee maker and soft and warm bedding. The Room Minuses: Housekeeping earned some kudos (from the kids) and sighs (from all of us)...towel animals fashioned and left on the bathroom vanity...but woke us up early one morning thinking the room was unoccupied... Overall it was a typical Marriott room, somewhat small with double beds. The furnishing were somewhat dated; but who goes to a hotel for the furnishings?!? Hotel Amenities: -The pool was great for the family. It was clean, clear, \warm, and a had a lifeguard on-duty all day long (where do you find them now-a-days?). There were plenty of towels for everyone. With a lifeguard present in the pool area the wife was able to relax. .- The fitness center was mediocre.
