In my humble opinion the Marriott chain has fallen behind other major hotel brands. The fitness machines were creaky. Towels were tough to come by. There wasn't a natural flow to the layout of the fitness center and it lacked adequate free weights. Several of the aerobic machines were out of service. - BIG plus was the working and clean hot sauna... - There was quick elevator service to all floors. Hotel Restaurants: We have nothing but good things to say about the hotel restaurant/bar...Kosmo's. There was plenty of room for our family to spread out. Nooks, crannies and huge comfy chairs for the kids to play in. The staff was attentive, accommodating and VERY kid friendly. Although it's not health food teh kids liked the french onion soup, buffalo wings and crab cake sliders. However,don't eat the pizza (ugh). The other places we ate were the typical middle America specialty chains McCormicks and Schmicks, ESPN Zone, Ruth's Chris...all were just Ok We went to the National Aquarium, it was crowded, but fun and informative. With a few kids we were somewhat harried but would definitely visit it again Overall I would stay at this hotel if I had to go to Baltimore again.

“Nice UWS Hotel” Location is great. Away from the bustle of Times Square but close to subway. Lots of eateries close by. Rooms are small but well appointed. Bathrooms adequate - great NYC water pressure. Our second time and we will repeat! Comfy beds. No pool or spa.

“(Not quite) Perfect” I was very impressed with Trump Soho. As a city hotel it scores very highly on key points: - big room - comfortable bed - charming staff - attractive architecture - location. So why not 5*: - not enough lifts. There is a rush hour around 6pm when you can wait for over 10 minutes for a lift. Madness made worse by the hotel "privatising" some lifts for functions. - our maid cleared cash off the desk (albeit having left a thank-you note!). Strange to assume that any cash in the room is a gratuity. Hotel handled it fine - but very embarassing/awkward for everyone. I had no idea how much I had left so had to report it. - paid-for wifi. I know some hotels do it but my wife and I travel with 5 wifi devices between us (laptop, iPad, phone etc). Which means $15 per device per day - you can't alternate a log-in between them. So, of course, I just connect one which is then inconvenient. If the hotel wants paid-for access, it should be useable between different devices. Would go back - really liked it.

“Ups and Downs” I stayed here with my partner on a long weekend in Chicago in December 2012. Overall, it was a pretty good experience, and I would return. However, there were some things about the hotel that would prevent me from giving it a 4-circle rating. First, the room needed some maintenance. Although very stylish in its decor, there were some flaws: the desk chair was broken (it's height function was snapped off), which made using the desk uncomfortable. The sink and basin were small, so there was limited space to put toiletries. The closet was oddly designed: there was very little full hanging space because a chest of drawers had been put in the closet. So, we didn't really have enough space for coats, pants, etc. The lighting in the room was really terrible -- at night, it was very dark. The worst part, however, was (a) thin walls and (b) connecting doors on either side of the room. The result was that on the first night we heard the neighbors to the right (who were having loud conversation and drinks) and, on the next morning, we heard the neighbors to the left. The hotel is a large convention facility and has that feel -- two towers, long walks to fitness center and lobby, etc., but I knew that when booking. I did think that, for such a large hotel, service was responsive: when we needed a couple of things in the room, they were brought quickly; check-in was efficient and welcoming; getting a cab was pretty easy, etc. The hotel was doing some renovation in public areas, but it wasn't hugely disturbing. We didn't use any of the hotel's bars or restaurants; I passed a couple and they had a pretty hotel-ish feeling. The fitness center, in the basement of the east tower, was excellent: lots of equipment, good selection of equipment, clean, etc.; I only wished it had some windows. The hotel's location is great; it's on Wacker, a block off Michigan, with easy walking access to Michigan Ave. shopping, the Loop, the park, etc. I was given (due to my Hyatt status) access to the club lounge, and I thought that as lounges in the U.S. goes, it was well done, with pleasant evening appetizers and a pretty nice (continental) breakfast. Overall, I would return, but I also think there are better options in the same vicinity, many of which have a similar price point. (Although, for the record, the rate I paid for the room over my stay was very reasonable).

“A competent hotel in downtown San Diego” The Doubletree Hotel San Diego Downtown is an older property that has been remodelled. Remodelling is a good idea. Whenever I go to California, I am disappointed when I encounter older buildings in general, unless they are historic masterpieces. I just have a mental image that California with it's wonderful tech base, should have the nicest newest buildings. This is not always the case. The remodelling efforts at this property should go further. It is nice overall, but there are warts. We rented a mini van b/c we had 4 adults with large pieces of luggage carrying delicate equipment. When we pulled into the parking garage, we found that the ramps were too narrow to navigate. We ended up using the parking lot across the street, but it would have been nice to avoid the parking garage altogether. The newly remodelled lobby is kind of swanky hipster in terms of style, like a W for example. However it doesn't match the 70's/80's feel of the rest of the property.

“Disappointed. Our discount applied to our service too, I guess.” My wife and I came and stayed here for business meetings (not held onsite). The property seems charming enough, some might consider the 50's/60's California Ranch style "dated" but I consider it classic, but truthfully we didn't have time to explore beyond our room, main lobby, and veranda (restaurant & bar space), and we didn't play golf, use the spa or enjoy any of the property's amenities, including what appears to be a nice kid's program. So why are we disappointed? By the weak service of waitstaff and lack of service by front desk/security/valet staff handling (or lack thereof) of our complaints over two nights. Our first night was marred by a car alarm that went off ALL NIGHT LONG, a beep-beep-beep that cycled on for a couple minutes, off for maybe 10-30 minutes, then on again. First call to front desk was they'd send security. My second call was answered by someone who had just come on and didn't know anything about it but would send security. I slept through the alarms until the one that woke me at 5:30 am but my wife had not slept. So I walked to the front desk and the gal there said she didn't know anything about it but then jumped on the radio to someone saying "what do you know about that black Honda Civic in Valet with the alarm that's been going off?" Nice. Second night, and unbelievably, another car alarm was going off into the night, this one being one of those with six different alarm sounds. Thank God it ended sometime after midnight, maybe that's when the offender who had self-parked his pickup truck in the valet lot and left, returned. First call, they'll send security. Second call was met with hostility, "there's nothing we can do, valet doesn't have a key, we've looked in the bar and asked everyone if it's their truck. Sorry, let's just hope the owner comes back." Third was an in-person visit to the front desk who says I'm the only one complaining about it. He radios the valet who says sorry, he didn't find keys or the owner and he's off in 5 minutes so he can't help" but they'll send security, give them a little more time, and they'll call me and tell me what they're going to do. No call... ...no apologies, no offer to move us to another room, or comp us, or offer SOMETHING. We (including coworkers) had cocktails on the veranda 3 times and 3 times waitstaff was inattentive, one time disappearing with my wife's credit card and had to be located after we waited 30 minutes.for her return. We stayed at a corporate-discounted room rate. I guess that's why we ended up in the "Terraces", the rooms that are outward-facing, towards the parking lots, on the perimeter of the resort (and why we were not offered a relocation?). Nice rooms, well-appointed, with attractive casework for dresser, desk and 42" plasma with digital LodgeNet, and another nice piece which set the king bed at a 45-degree angle, and with integrated night lighting. If the rest of the resort has this level of appointment then you'll be fine. But rooms 801-831, with their single-pane windows, should be avoided, due to poor proximity to parking areas.

“Nice hotel” Nice hotel with very comfortable beds. Wood floors are a nice feature. Nice bathroom with extra large shower. Immediately next to Galleria so very easy walk to shopping and food. Only complaint is that exercise room sucks! All equipment is worn and very old. Also not a big fan of popcorn ceilings in the rooms. Overall a great place to stay.

“Room for Improvement” I would like to give the Pointe a great review but unfortunately I can’t. I grew up on Phoenix and the Pointe was always someplace nice but I think maybe it is past its prime although the issues we encountered could easily be remedied. Pros: 1. It is very centrally located and convenient to two freeways and downtown. 2. The location itself is beautiful. 3. The pool seemed nice (but a little small). We did not use the pool but I did check it out. 4. We were able to get a Presidential Suite for a very reasonable price and the room itself was VERY large and more than met our needs. 5. Bell staff & concierge was otherwise very nice & knowledgeable. For the price we paid I guess I really should not complain much but it certainly was not a 4 star hotel. Cons/Issues: 1. We checked in at 9PM. The hotel is very convoluted and confusing. The bell desk told us the wrong building to go to and we drove around for 15 minutes in the dark (lugged our suitcases and 2 tired kids up and down stairs) before we found our room. Room numbering is completely erratic. (ie Room 2164 is in building 18 but 2163 is in building 20) 2. When we entered the room the desk chair was askew, the chairs for the table were on the table and the bathtub was half filled with water and there was a soaking wet towel in there. My daughter asked “why is the carpet wet?” I took off my shoes and realized that the carpet in the bedroom area was soaked. I don’t mean damp, I mean squishy, sloshy soaked. I called the front desk, who seemed completely unconcerned by the cause of the water and offered to send up a fan. I told them explicitly not to worry about it that night but that we’d be out all day the next day and to have it fixed. I explicitly stated that I had 2 small kids I needed to get into bed as it was nearly midnight their time. My husband noted that the carpet under the bed was dry and that there was a carpet cleaning machine outside another room down the way. I figured someone didn’t finish their job. At 10PM a worker knocked on the door and asked if he could come finish cleaning the carpet. I sent him away. Please remember, we checked in at 9PM, a full 5 hours after check-in time but our room was obviously not ready, yet we were sent to the room anyway. The carpet was dry by the next morning. 3. For 3 days the neighbors wine glasses sat empty on the walkway railing outside our door and housekeeping never took them. 4. Our room was VERY far away from the Falls pool. It was literally a hike down there and we were closer than a lot of other rooms. So if you're looking to enjoy the pool be prepared to walk (it is set in the side of a mountain so by "hike" I'm not kidding). There are smaller pools around the hotel as well. 5. Our room clearly was not part of the recent renovation as there was plenty of peeling paint, peeling wallpaper, stains on the table, peeling stain on the table, and closet doors that didn’t work right. 6. Last but not least, I was SHOCKED that Disney channel was only available On Demand as a pay channel. For kids there was only Cartoon Network or Nickelodeon for free so there was nothing age appropriate for my 6 year old to watch as she wound down for bed at 8-9PM, as both have gone pretty adult by that time. Seriously, if you’re going to tout yourselves as a family friendly resort, at least have some family friendly TV available for free. I’m not about to pay $3 to watch an episode of Phineas and Ferb. Noggin, Sprout or PBS Kids would even have been a good option to have available.

“Our New Favorite NYC Sheraton - but beware of cab problem” This new ( about 10 months old in July 2011) Sheraton is located on Canal Street riight in the heart of one of my wife's favorite shopping areas. It is in Tribeca and very near SOHO which means scads of good restaurants to choose among. It is very close to many of the most handy subway lines. The staff are great! The club lounge is huge, and includes a great outdoors area....actually designed to be able to easily eat in...instead of having mostly sofas and soft chairs like most other lounges. Breakfast was a bit erratic but at least is supposed to include eggs, sausage, bacon and potatoes plus normal continental breakfast stuff. Only real complaint was that it was suspicously difficult to to get a cab at 4 PM...we gave up after 20 minutes and had to take one of the relatively pricey ($50 to LaGuardia was quoted, but we negotiated down a bit) limos the bellmen offered "right away".

“Nice Hotel with Good Service” Lovely hotel with nice rooms and a very comfortable bed. The check-in staff are very friendly as well as efficient. The bathroom is modern and I love the Aveda toiletries. The concierge really knows his way around good restaurants. I will be back.

“Average at best” This hotel has gone way downhill since my last stay a year ago. The three rooms that I looked at before choosing the best of a sad bunch all had a moldy smell. The carpets lloked old and stained. There was noise from other rooms. The bed that I slept on had a cheap, stained mattress. The valet took 40 minutes to get my car. The oncierge never called me back about a restaurant reservation. On the plus side, the location is great, and some of the old time employees still remembered my name. e-mail me for any questions.

“Hip, Eclectic, Nightlife” You should be aware there are 2 Dream Hotels in NYC. One is Uptown the other one is in Soho. I learned this the hard way but the front desk gave me a free room upgrade (queen bed to a king). Needless to say, the price difference was significant. On a Saturday evening the Dream Uptown was 209.00 (w/taxes:about $280.) P/n compared to the $900 p/n at the location in Soho. The lobby of this hotel is a bit small yet it has a very trendy feel. From the large floor to ceiling circular aquarium to the giant statue in the seating area. Quite eclectic if you like that. The hotel ambiance is blue....that is a theme throughout that is carried into your hotel room. As the elevator doors opened to my floor, I am exposed to a very large mural of several woman with their breasts exposed. After your eyes adjust & you wrap your mind around that moment of unexpectedness, you head to your room. My room has a very cold feel to it, all white, minimal yet it is still considered to be a medium size. There is a desk, queen bed, large plasma tv, walk in closet, nice art work, of course blue neon lights all around. The bathroom is small but has that black/white checker flooring, not a lot of sink or shelving space for your essentials. If your two women sharing this room, you will have to use the desk to store your stuff. All in all, the room grew on me . There is a nice bose sound system as well. The walls are very thin and it can get loud. I heard every word of the batchelorette party. By the way, this seems to be a hot spot for them. I stayed on a Saturday, when I looked outside my room I was happy to see the farmers market right at the end of the block, a big plus! If you are hungry for lunch they have a great restaurant attached to the hotel w/ an entrance to the lobby. They are known for their pizza’s and have indoor or outdoor dining. After getting ready for the evening I head up stairs to the roof top club Ava Lounge. Full of couches and nice seating areas but no bar only cocktail servers & a DJ. As a single person standing at the high top table felt awkward especially since it took a while before getting a drink. However, the cocktail waitresses were kind & said I could sit at the reserved couches until these people showed up. Late night this place only can be accessed by a guarded elevator & doormen with red velvet ropes await the crowd outside. Dream 55 is next door for more night life. The lounge is a dimly lit ambiance with a sexy glow also w/ an entrance inside the lobby & out. If you are looking for night life, fun, sexy in the city with many options without leaving the hotel or going far, this is for you!

“A good choice for a stopover.” A good choice for a stopover. Conveniently located between Burbank and LA it was a good choice for a night. It was an older hotel with some older furniture yet it was clean and well maintained. It's location is odd sitting behind a Denny's restaurant, but don't let that bother you, the place is O.K. for a night.

“great location, worn out hotel” this hotel has a fabulous location on Park Ave. a block from the best shopping on Madison Ave. Prices are pretty decent for the size of the room, location and NYC in general. Staff are courteous and friendly by NY standards. We had a verly large 1 bedroom suite. The hotel just was not well-maintained or clean enough. There were two phones in the room that did not work. A doorknob was falling off. The hallway carpet was stained and worn and the room was dusty. Housekeeping was very weak when we were there - i.e. they do not throw out an empty soda can unless you put it directly into the trash. Bathrooms are very small....we did have two. I would pay more and stay in a better hotel next time....or even the pay the same and stay someplace like a W that would have a newer, fresher feel. This place is really stale. It's a shame. It has real potential b/ of the location and size of the rooms..

“Enjoyed a 2 night stay here....” This hotel saved me from a terrible experince at Aloft across the street. 2 nights in town for work, given a king room on floor 5. Unfortunately this room had been smoked in similar to the Aloft but they switched me to a better room on same floor. Nice layout, hardwood floors, Keurig coffee maker is a bonus, had view of lake and pool, nice open shower, nicely appointed room, pillows a bit lumpy but soft and they worked. Workout room was suitable, not great for weights but cardio is fine. Pool is very nice, loved taking a dip after a long day. Serfvice was excellent here, overall a great stay, great location for me, lot's to eat and shop for in area. Highly endorsed.

“Budget Friendly” Ok let me get this out the way. This is not the Hilton, Hyatt, Marriott or anywhere else FANCY. This is Kings Inn. Now having said that, the hotel is overall very average run of the mill Bates Motel knock off. The rooms for the most part were clean and cost efficient. Of course it doesn't have all the bells and whistles as a five star but it is somewhere safe, clean and reasonable to lay your head if you are in a money crunch. NOTE: Please be aware that this motel offer a very resonable weekly rate and some people call this place home. So if this is not the right surrounding for you, please go somewhere else.

“NON IL MASSIMO” Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel per una notte nel mese di novembre 2012. Ottima posizione, si trova in pieno downtown a Fort Worth, vicinisimo a tutte le attrazioni e agli uffici, a soli 5 minuti di auto da Stockyards. L'hotel necessiterebbe di una bella ristrutturazione sia interna che esterna. Camera molto spaziosa e pulita, ma piuttosto datata. Personale gentile ma non particolarmente ecciciente. Piscina interna troppo piccola rapportata alla struttura, e comunque troppo corta per nuotare. Palestra ben attrezzata e pulita. Centro congressi veramente grande e funzionale. Parcheggio costoso. Rapporto qualità prezzo non buono.

“旅慣れた人にはお勧めのホテル” 都会的ながら、冷たさは感じない。温かなサービスとは言えませんが、旅慣れていて、別にホテルに色々とサポートを求めるのでなければ、逆にこうした都会的なホスピタリティの方が居心地の良い場合があります。 ベルボーイからフロントスタッフまで長く勤務している人が多く、さりげなくwelcome back! という挨拶も嬉しい。 定期的に訪れて、常宿として使うには良いホテル。 ロビーフロアのカフェメニューはなかなか秀逸です。

“Suited All Our Needs” Stayed here for 3 nights. We loved the breakfast and happy hour - three alcoholic drinks per person. Rooms were simple and met our standards. Nothing fancy - the hotel gets the job done. Employees were pleasant and very helpful. I loved the business center amenities - free internet, printing, wireless internet and a few office supplies for your use.

“At least it's clean!” I thought the Vagabond was okay. The room was clean. The people that run the place seem nice. The free breakfast was at least adequate (coffee, fruit, waffles). Not bad. There are two swimming pools (which is a plus if you want some privacy and don't want to be with a group at one pool). The drawbacks were: they should put double pained glass on the windows and better security windows. When I walked into the room, the window lock was open. There is a vibe in this part of the valley that it isn't 100% safe -- which is why the easy-open windows and balconies seem a bit unsafe. BUT... having said this, I spent the night in another hotel that was a block away and it was MUCH worse than the Vagabond. (It was the King's Inn -- which by comparison is a total dump and was about $30 to $40 more expensive). The Vagabond by comparison seemed like Shangri-la because it was CLEAN and it actually HAD a free breakfast and GOOD service. It isn't a high-priced hotel and not something for people who are used to first class accomodations. But it is a bare-bones hotel for someone who just wants to have a place to sleep for a reasonable price. I would rate it a C+ or B- for its price range. Not bad.

“Elegance and Bliss” I love this hotel. It is classy, gorgeous, and truly 5*. The rooms are beautifully appointed and the toiletries and bathrooms elegant. My only minor complaint is on the size of the room, which was not substantial, but given that it was just me in the room, this was fine. All of the personnel are attentive and anxious to help. I wanted a ticket one night for a Shakespearean performance and the concierge managed to score one with no additional service charges tacked on and no "hotel fee" for booking it for me. This is a rarity. One afternoon I noted one of the personnel taking a beautiful display of Belgian chocolates on a plate to a room. I commented casually, "I wouldn't mind one of those in my room!" He asked for my room number and within minutes a complimentary chocolate platter decorated with lilies appeared. The hotel's cafe served spectacular breakfasts and its signature restaurant, "Kevin Taylor," is amazing. Every dish was perfection. We ordered a bottle of red wine that I still dream of. A warning: this place is not cheap. It is a classic example of getting what you pay for, so if you are up for a splurge, this is most definitely the place.

“Comfortable, great staff, excellent location” I stayed here for the weekend. I was given a corner room--which had a very nice view, a comfortable bed, and a nice bathroom with plenty of hot water. The staff were the highlight here. Check-in was swift--and when I arrived early they already had my room ready including the small refrigerator I requested. (I am on a special diet and the refrigerator makes it easier for me to at least stay close to it!) The concierges were always friendly and gave me good recommendations and directions. The location was excellent. Plenty to do in the area--museums, shopping, restaurants...all within easy walking distance. There was also god running in the area along the river. All in all--an excellent stay and I will return, if I return to Boston.

“Nice location for restaurants and sights.” I stayed here while attending a meeting at the McCormick Convention Center. While rather inconvenient for the Convention Center (several miles away), the hotel was in a very convenient location for an easy walk to Millennium Park, Navy Pier, and the Art Institute of Chicago, plus many excellent restaurants. The room was spacious, nice desk for working, nice shower. The breakfast in the Club Lounge was very good, it had a reasonable selection of food (pastries, hard boiled eggs, cereals), plenty of well-spaced seating, several choices of newspapers, it was never very busy, so a nice quiet place to eat and read a newspaper or work on laptop. Wireless is not typically free but I had complementary internet access, which was excellent, good speed. I did not get a chance to check out the exercise facilities. The staff was friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

“Great Location” Staff were really friendly on arriving, took our bags as we were early. Coffee all day and breakfast was a bonus. A short walk from Times Square and lots of other sights in a quick walk. Room was small but big enough for two adults, safe area and a great pizza place a few doors down.

“Very nice, new facilty” Positives: Still has the brand new smell Nice, slightly different layout, plush carpets, nice fixtures Two large HDTVs with a good amount of HD channels Usable wireless signals with decent speed Accommodated my stay, despite my booking agent getting the date wrong Good value for money Very close to the airport, but little noise pollution. Negatives: Large stain on the futon, made me think a child had slept there and urinated on it Hand prints all over the inside of the glass on the bedroom window (who puts their whole palm on the glass, or puts their face on it?) Had a late start but received an unsolicited wake up call at 7am
“Just right” Right where we needed this hotel to be! Dog friendly, comfortable room and good breakfast. Friendly staff a plus!

“Great Experience” Great place to stay on Riverwalk. Everything from check-in to check-out went extremely well & staff are friendly & responsive. We were in a 2-room suite on quiet 5th floor, which was a good size. Adequate drawer space, which is unusual for most hotels these days as they are more interested in selling minibar items than where you will place your clothes. Free high speed ethernet in room convenient with plug on top of desk so that you don't have to crawl underneath. Free local and long distance phone calls. Hotel is a converted historic building that was done very well. Lobby is beautiful [historic looking murals were actually put in by Disney for a movie that was filmed there about 10-15 years ago]. Breakfast is large & good. Happy hour offers free drinks and enough food that families with kids were making it their dinner. We just had a couple of drinks before going for dinner on Riverwalk. Although there is no concierge, there is a large book with menus for area restaurants. Retrieval of car from valet was quick. $18 for parking was low in comparison to other Riverwalk hotels. Rooftop pool area offers views of the city. Although this was first time at a Drury, we will definitely check out others in the future. Only complaints were that on 1 day the room wasn't cleaned until after 3:30 pm & it is a little tacky to have windows covered even if there isn't a view from them.

“Beards, beards, beards” Get ready for a packed, loud, groover lounge upon arrival of this steampunk type hotel. Rooms are a bit on the small size but so what else is new in New York City. I had a "small" room that was just that...small. Bed was very comfortable. The television media was very interesting. They have their own sort of network. Easy to navigate. Bathroom was well equipped and I especially liked the small handsoap on a rope (no, it's not what you think). There's enough white noise in the hallyway, room to dull the outside street chaos. Staff is very friendly. You will notice that everyone with the exception of the females are sporting beards. Stay tuned on that phenomenon. Great restaurants are a part of the scene as well. Breslins and John Dory. There's also Stumphump for coffee. I'll come back if it's for a couple of nights. Any longer and I'll probably look elswhere. I'm an old codger and like my sleep. Happy trails.

“Best budget hotel in San Diego” The good: After much searching for a cheap hotel in San Diego that was in a decent location it brought me to the Dolphin Motel. The staff here are very friendly and print things for you and also help you out with any problems you have. The location is great and parking is free. You are around 5-10 minutes from downtown San Diego and all the attractions. The breakfast was okay- we had some muffins,coffee,yogurt, and orange juice but it was okay. Most importantly, the price was great and it is very clean. The bad: The rooms are not very soundproof. I stayed on the 1st floor and was able to hear a lot of the footsteps from the room above me so that was a bit annoying. Also, if someone was outside your room talking you could hear them without much of a problem. I think that if the hotel was quieter i would have given it a 5 star rating.

“Good hotel, pleasant stay” Enjoyed staying there on business. Beautiful room but it would be great if they provided bottled water and had the clock next to the bed instead of behind it. Walls are a little thin. The bed was comfy and the room was spacious. the place is mostly very nice and well run. Like the workout center and lobby bar.

“Another great stay at the Hampton Inn” Went to Seattle over the Christmas holiday for a weekend getaway. Booked at the Hampton Inn Downtown because my husband and I have had great experiences staying at Hampton Inn properties. As expected, this one did not disappoint. The hotel is a short walk from the Space Needle and Seattle Center and within walking distance to downtown, albeit about a 30 minute walk. If heading downtown and you don't want to walk, you can take the bus located right out in front of the hotel. Be advised that this hotel is not located downtown. We got a great rate, $89/night. Our king bedroom was large, clean, had a large tv and very comfortable bed. Breakfast had a great variety of foods (a hot dish, bagels/bread, fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, cereal) and something to please everyone. The lobby had 2 computers with internet access that were free to use. The hotel was very quiet in terms of city noise, no horns honking or general commotion, though we did hear footsteps and movement in the room above us but this wasn't too disruptive. The front desk staff wasn't as informed about how to navigate the city and I would have expected but we still managed to get around with no problems. Overall, great value for the money and I would definitely stay again.

“Ok for a business trip” This is not a tourist hotel. The Hyatt McCormack is off the beaten path and you cannot walk to any shops or restaurants from the. I was staying at the Hyatt for a 3-day convention which the hotel was suited perfectly for. Rooms were clean, service was good and the beds were comfortable. The reception offered automatic rooim key card kiosks for check-in which was really convenient. The health club is mediocre, not nearly as nice as other properties. The lounge/bar area is adequate with TV’s for sports and basic pub food. Chicago is a wonderful destination - I would just recommend a more convenient location if you are going for a fun filled visit.
“Very Nice” Spent one night here while traveling through. Room was large and comfortable and quiet. Good location with a huge mall and many restaurants near by. A free breakfast would be nice.

“Excellent service and perfect location” We were in town for a graduation and the staff was exceptional. Everyone in our group was very impressed with customer service at this property. Included in our group were several road warriors who travel frequently so this was no easy feat. Its location cannot be beat, easy access to attractions, Reading Terminal Market, transportation and shopping. This is our place to stay in Philadelphia!

“5 Stars hotel and 5 stars staff. Truly enjoyable !!” Spend 5 nights in this great Intercontinental location in Washington. I have to admit that it is one of the best Intercontinental hotels I have encounter and not only for the nice facilities, but mainly because of the positive and attentive attitude of the staff, all of them. From the front desk staff, the Concierge, to the Cafe servers, to the room service staff, cleaning lady and "at your service" phone operator. All these members of the Willard family really understand the meaning of "service" and "high standards of attention". My sincere congratulations to all of them, who many our vacation extra special. The hotel is nice located within walking distance to all the principal landmarks. Nice restaurants are close by and the French Cafe at the hotel is nice for breakfast or a quick lunch/dinner. The up/down trolley stops in front of the hotel, which is very convinient. A few nice stores are also near by, CVS, Borders, Macy's and other. The rooms are ample and well decorated, new TV's, comfortable beds and linens and lots of space. The room service menu is very complete and a good alternative when rest is needed. Overall, a 5 star hotel with 5 star staff can only mean a 5 stars experience. High recommend this hotel to all.

“recomendable” las habitaciones del hotel son bastante amplias, en comparación con el común estandar de las habitaciones pequeñas en la mayoria de los hoteles de nueva york... además de ello, es un hotel sin mayores pretensiones lujosas, pero realmente agradable y muy bueno en cuanto servicio... diagonalmente tiene una tienda tipo supermercado que abre las 24 hrs, lo cual es una ventaja tremenda para comprar alguna cosa de comer cuando estas de vuelta... el restaurante del hotal tiene menu variado en la mañana para desayunar bien, el cual debes pagar aparte (como casi todos los hoteles en NY no incluyen el desayuno) y si no es de tu gusto pues apenas caminando al salir tienes múltiples lugares para desayunar como es propio de esta ciudad... el personal es muy amable, tienen personas de habla español... el único detalle a considerar es que está ubicado en la décima avenida, lo cual resulta distante para quienes no gustan de caminar tomando en cuenta que las distancias entre cada avenida son bastante largas y generalmente la vida de Manhattan comienza a partir de la 7ma, por ende, son al menos 3 avenidas que debes bajar para ir al times square como centro para moverte hacia lo demás y, honestamente que en la noche, al salir de algún musical no dan ganas de caminar tanto (ademas algunos trayectos son bastante oscursos y solitarios) asi que terminas tomando taxis por el cansancio de la jornada de caminatas conociendo nueva york... creo que esto es un factor importante para conocer y considerar...

“Needs Updating” The hotel lobby is definitelyi beautiful, however, I switched rooms a few times as the carpets were very stained, and stiff in parts, in each. The drapes and baseboards were very dusty too, which is hard for me as an allergy sufferer. The concierge was so gracious and went out of their way to ensure I was comfortable. I will definitely stay here again as it's in a great spot for the business district, but my advice is to make sure your room is clean enough.

“Fabulous location, fabulous service” We stayed in the Allerton for 5 nights in September. I had booked through Hotels.com and got a great rate but I didn't realise at that time it was a small room. That's certainly not the hotels fault, and although we may not have had much space, the room was immaculate as was the bathroom. We had a view of the Water Tower from both the room and the bathroom. On checking in we were told of the free wine in the lobby bar mid afternoon--that was a nice surprise. The staff were lovely during the whole stay, I really could not fault any single aspect of the hotel. The location is great, we made full use of the CTA pass and used the buses up and down Michigan Ave.
“近くには素敵なレストランも” 全てにおいてなかなか大きな造りのホテルでした。特に高さのあるベッドはバネがきいていて全体的に設えが大きかったです。壁が薄いのか、廊下を歩いていると部屋から物音がよく聞こえてきました。坂を下っていくと流行りの素敵なレストランが軒を連ねていました。良いエリアにあるホテルだと思います。

“Under renovation” We enjoyed our stay with this Hilton. Our room was being updated. It was very clean. The main pool really made a positive impression on my 5 and 8 year old girls. There were a lot of lifeguards, a big plus given its size. The "attractions" surrounding the pool were run down. It was not clear if that part is going to be renovated. All in all, it has high potential I would stay here again.

“Fabulous Boutique Hotel” My favorite hotel in San Diego is now the Hotel Solamar. We took advantage of the upgraded King Corner suite with jacuzzi tub. This tub was AMAZING. I've stayed in lots of great places all around the world and this tub was fantastic. My girlfriend got a huge kick out of it. Room was clean and spacious. Only drawback...not enough drawers to put clothes in. Parking is expensive, but there is a public parking lot directly across the street that'll save you some money. This is a dog friendly place and you will see plenty of them! Secondly, the J Six Lounge is located on the 4th floor so be prepared to hear music until just after midnight. This fact didn't bother us and we enjoyed every minute of our stay there. Food at the J Six Restaurant is quite good. Location is prime. Gas Lamp a block away with countless shops and restaurants to enjoy. Will definitely frequent this hotel again.

“My new favorite hotel” I got a deal online and loved every minute of my stay here. It's the perfect hotel for a solo traveler, but I wouldn't recommend it for families-- unless they have significantly bigger rooms available. For example, a huge window separated my bed from the bathroom. There was also about 2 feet around the bed on all sides (aside from the wall side. However, as a solo traveler this made no difference to me.) I also enjoyed the daily free water and champagne in the entrance from the street level. Also, the hotel is around the corner from a 24-hour CVS and across the street from Whole Foods and the Columbus Circle subway. I'd definitely stay here next time I'm in NYC for work or leisure!

“A great stay close to everything” We just spent a long weekend at the Hilton Times Square. We were in a corner King Room and really enjoyed the extra space. As others have noted, this hotel is conveniently located to the shows and restaurants of Times Square. The hotel is surprisingly quiet, despite being so close to everything. The bed was very comfortable and the breakfast buffet was delicious. The staff at the front desk, at the bar, and at breakfast were professional and courteous. We'll definitely be back! The only suggestion for the hotel is that they need to update their wi-fi policies --- $13.99 for inroom wi-fi is old school for a modern hotel, especially when they are charging per device.

“Nice hotel, great location” Had a wonderful weekend stay at the Sofitel. The location is very convenient to midtown sights, and more importantly, shopping. Despite being on the edge of Times Square, the area was generally quiet and free of the typical TS chaos. The room (610) was very spacious and despite being just around the corner from the elevators, it was more or less quiet. The bathroom was also quite big, but the doors bothered me. I’m sure they’re simply for aesthetics sake, but instead of a standard door, there were two skinny doors that opened from the center and the one always swung shut. I'm all for sleek design, but only when it's practical, too. Also bathroom-related, the toiletries were surprisingly generic; glad I had brought my own. We had little interaction with the staff, but they were friendly/helpful in those few instances. Overall, a really nice stay.
“便利で安い” ロケーションがよくにぎやかなところなので夜も安心です スタッフがとても優しく感じが良かったです 高級ホテルではないですがニューヨークの高級ホテルでもひどいところがあるので 色々泊まっているホテルの中では安いホテルの割にはまた泊まってもいいかもって思います

“Fairly good deal, but too old school” I stayed at this motel because I needed somewhere for one night, close to uptown, and inexpensive. It was average but I was hoping for a little more. I have noticed in the past few years that some of the sleep inns I've stayed at in the Charlotte area could use some updating. This one definitely fell in that category. There was no fitness center and the pool was extremely small (indoor). The computer was absolutely archaic and didn't work. They claimed it had been knocked out by a recent storm but it looked like it hadn't been used in quite some months and maybe even a year. There was no info in the room pertaining to TV stations or any area info that would be helpful to visitors unfamiliar with Charlotte. The breakfast was meager but what was there was fresh. The pocket door to the bathroom did not close all the way but since I was traveling alone I did not request any maintenance or to be moved. TV stations were somewhat limited for a motel offering cable. As for points in their favor the room and linens were clean and neat and the staff was polite but not overly helpful or friendly unless they were pushed for assistance. Really needs updating though.

“Exceeded my expections!” This hotel absolutely exceeded my normal expectations of a NYC hotel room. The location was very well situated in the Chelsea neighborhood and a subway stop was just a half a block away. The lobby was small but very modern and not overly colorful as some Hotel Indigo is. The rooms were actually very nice, bright, new, and a great size for a New York City hotel room. The internet was free and worked at an excellent speed. It was a little weird that the internet would log off after about every hour or so if you are working on something make sure you save often. The staff was very friendly and helpful as they greeted us each time we walked into the hotel. Overall I was very pleased with my stay here and I would strongly recommend it to other travelers.

“Old world luxury” Stayed for just one night at the Towers of the Waldorf and it was an extremely pleasant stay. Lori at the front desk could not have been more helpful upon check-in and all the staff we encountered during out stay was courteous and helpful. The suite was beautiful in that traditional style with floor to ceiling drapery, large fireplace, comfortable dressing area and bath. It was like you were staying in a plush 5th avenue penthouse. I was only disappointed that I had to check out the next morning!

“A wedding night to remember” We held our wedding reception in the beautiful grand ballroom at the Millennium Knickerbocker. It was quite a throwback for some guests who remember high school proms or weddings from decades past when this hotel was very en vogue. That meant that even people who had been to events in the space were still awed by it's beauty and elegance. We truly blew our guests away with this one. The catering manager, Lauren Haver, was there all night to make sure everything went off without a hitch and the head waiter treated us like royalty. Our glasses were never without champagne and our guests were waited on hand and foot. Although Lauren isn't employed by the hotel anymore, we still go back each year of our anniversary to have a celebratory drink in the hotel's sleek bar. I love the old school style and swagger this hotel evokes calling out to the roaring 20s and 30s without the cheesy-ness of a 'theme' hotel. The suite we had was immaculate. It's was bigger and better appointed than our condo. Lauren even went out of her way to give us a wedding night price when we decided to stay for two nights instead of one halfway through the reception (the first night was included in the package). The staff even helped us lug all of our little odds and ends (left over wedding programs, gifts, etc) to the room late that night. The next morning my husband lounged on the super comfy bed while I watched TV in the bath tub. Yes, there's a TV mounted on the wall in the bath tub. Its location is also great, so that when we had to leave to let them clean the room we grabbed a quick bite to eat without having to navigate the throngs of tourists on Michigan. I would highly recommend this hotel for a truly posh stay or amazing event, but if you're searching for a bargain with breakfast included and drink waiting for you when you walk in keep looking.

“Convenient downtown hotel” This is a conveniently-located downtown hotel. The lobby is large and rather confusing, and at the time of writing it was undergoing renovations. My upgraded room was luxurious, and included a bar-style dining area, sitting area and kitchenette. Decor was understated. contemporary and fairly new. Service was good. Recommended.

“Good location, Good people, Good Value” The hotel is from the 70's (and before) but they have done a great job with the updates and the rooms are comfortable. If you need a a desk for work, ask for a room with one on check in. This time I had a small table to work from, which is fine, but a desk is better. Ask for a room with a bay view - truly relaxing.

“Great location and Beale” The Westin was nice - good room and great location. I had been on the road for a while by te time I stopped here and was able to take advantage of the nice gym facility a couple times. Hotel staff were generally helpful. The location I pretty convenient for walking around downtown but I def recommend driving anywhere beyond a few blocks as the walk is not always that great. The parking garage allows hotel guests in and out services which are handy only if you will use them - otherwise do not pay for parking through the hotel. The location is right on Beale for fun evenings out. This did fuel a couple noisy next door neighbors but after they woke me up, I was able to fall right back to sleep on the pillow top mattress

“Great hotel... not so friendly staff” I stayed here one night on a recent trip to Phoenix. I loved the basic room. The room was HUGE. My room was not in the best location... it faced an office building... however, the room was very nice. The front desk staff woman who checked me in was not friendly. She was not helpful... did not make me feel welcome... I felt like I was bothering her. Not so good. My rating would have been higher for the hotel had it not been for her. I may or may not stay here again in the future.

“Convenient stay” Due to an early morning departure and late night arrival, we spent a night here both before and after vacation. The rates seemed reasonable, so we took the commuter bus from Milwaukee, which was very convenient (the "bus terminal" is right across the street) and allowed us to avoid the hassle of constuction on I-94. Check in was quick and painless. It wasn't busy either time, so we used the front desk. One clerk was quite indifferent while the other was more friendly and outgoing, though both were very efficient. The room was smaller than I expected, but suited our needs perfectly. It was clean and quiet. I was a little too tired both nights to give an unbiased assessment of the beds, but I did sleep well both nights. We had evening snacks to hold us over at the sports bar. The waitress warned us about the small portion sizes, and she was right, but it was probably what I should normally have anyway. We enjoyed a very good breakfast at the restaurant (not the buffet) which, like everything else here was pricey, but that's expected. Given this experience, I'd use this hotel again in a similar situation. The convenience of being connected to the terminal is just too good to pass up.

“Great location for theater district” Very clean, very quiet hotel. Excellent restaurant and shopping downstairs. Nice breakfast. Staff extremely pleasant and helpful. Beds are super comfortable. Get steps from most of the theaters and the Kimmel Center. Discount parking

“Thank you, Hilton Bayfront” I went to San Diego this past weekend with my family and friends to celebrate my birthday. We booked three rooms together and were traveling with three toddlers in total. This was our first stay at the Hilton Bayfront. Normally, we stay at the Omni next door to Petco Park. I thought it might be fun to try someplace new. I'm so glad we did! The hotel has an amazing location to start. It is the last property located next door to the convention center. Thanks to the bridge that connects it back to Petco Park, you have immediate access to everything. In comparison to the other hotels in San Diego, it is not too pricey for what they are offer. Overnight parking is actually cheaper than a few other hotels in the same vicinity. Since the property is only two years old, the rooms are very nice, clean and comfy. When traveling with little ones, that's important. We enjoyed the Starbucks on the first floor and ate at the hotel bar as well. The pool is great and we spent time there also. From the hotel, you can even make the walk up to Seaport Village. It's relaxing as a walk on Sunday morning. Because of the marina, the children love it as they can see all of the boats. The service we received at the front desk was exceptional. Thank you to James and Robert. Other than that, the service at the rest of the property was good, but not memorable. When I say 'not memorable', I mean I didn't go out of my way to remember their names to say thank you. I think that's pretty much on par with everywhere else. Since the property is larger than that of places like the Omni, you don't necessarily see the same faces over and over again. That's not their fault, so you can't criticize them for that. All in all, I would definitely stay at the Hilton Bayfront again. In fact, I already have reservations to stay there again twice in the next six weeks. I can't wait to go back.

“This place is a dump!” OK so we recently were put here for comic con thru the hotel lottery....couldn't move because town was booked...did it serve its purpose? a place to sleep and shower, yes. However, I can not believe this place is a 3 star?! I have traveled a lot and have stayed at many hotels...I can not in my right mind imagine how this place rates 3 stars? First off, we checked in around 4pm and were given a room in the "motel" section i.e outdoor hallways and door access. After commenting on said room clerk responded since we were checking in so late(since when is 4pm late) we couldn't be moved. Clerk didn't seem to want to offer any info on much just gave me the keys, had me sign papers, and that's about it. Upon getting to the room after lugging all our luggage up flights of stairs boy were we disappointed. Even my two young sons, thought this place was a dump and asked if we could leave! Never would I recommend or stay here again.

“Not Too Bad After All” Not to sound snobby but I don't normally stay in this type of hotel. However, I needed to stay in the area and the Renaissance, a few blocks away and no great shakes, was $200 more. So for $179 a night I decided to give it a try. It is a busy hotel with very little character but the staff were very nice. There was a manager's cocktail party (no thanks) and an ok free buffet breakfast. The rooms were clean but, you know. Why they bother with plastic flowers is beyond me. There are two tvs and a coffee maker but that's about it. I don't love the location but it is close to the convention center and a few restaurants. So all in all, it was not an unpleasant experience and at least they are trying.

“LOVE THE ROOF TOP POOL” Great location for the Back Bay, the park and Newbury St. kind of a hike if you want to hang out at Fanuiel Hall. Staff was friendly and our room was clean with a nice view on the 11th floor. The beds and pillows were heavenly, we had breakfast at the restaurant and it was very good, wish we would have eaten there for dinner. The absolute best was the roof top pool. I believe it is the only hotel in Boston with an outside pool and the outstanding service by the pool made it even better. One suggestion would be if you have more than two people staying the in the room, pay for the upgrade to a larger room. I would definiately recommend.

“Smart hotel that lives on it's reputation” The rooms are comfort and the staff accommodating however the food is not what you would expect from a hotel of the Hilton's standard. My biggest grip are the extra charges. I have never been charged extra by any hotel to receive a small parcel (book from Amazon) or store my bags on check out whilst waiting for the bus to the airport. They also charge for the internet $35 for 5 days. The advise from the concierge on trips, where to eat etc was not great as talked out of buying a go-card with the price of the attractions included to a trolley bus pass with no attractions included on the grounds that the go-card finished at 5.30. Only to find the trolley bus pass also finished at 5.30 and you were not able to queue jump as you would with a go-card.

“Do consider this hotel in Chicago!” Since this hotel is right next to the McCormick Place Convention Center in Chicago, it is the ideal location for attending any meeting at the Center. When all the other delegates have to catch a bus in the monring, you will just walk 50m - luxury! Even if you are not attending a convention, this hotel is in my opinion quite a good choice for Chicago. The next door Convention Center has a Metra station underneath - so train to Chicago's downtown is simple and quick. The hotel itself has good facilities and is only 200m from the lake shore. Taxis into town cost little from here - and compared to some of the downtown Chicago hotels, the McCormick Place Hyatt is modern and well fitted out. I walked around the local area during the day and felt safe, but most of Chicago's attractions (museums, shops, architecture) are a short taxi ride away.

“Great place for a convention” Stayed June 2 - 5, 2011 on 12 floor. This is a great hotel and an excellent site for a conference/convention. Ours had close to 700 attendees from all over Texas. Located right across the freeway for the Dallas Market Center you could walk there if you were so inclined. Rooms were nice although the A/C was a little cantankerous. Would liked to have had a mini-fridge but I guess you can't have everything. On the downside the restaurant, cafe & coffee shop were quite expensive but there are lots of great cafes and restaurants within a 10 minute drive.

“great stay” This Hilton lived up to the Hilton reputation. Located on 6th Avenue it is in a great location. The Hotel is large however I still felt that persoanl attention. The room and bathroom were nice and comfortable. The concerige lounge was spacious and well cared for. They accomodated my request for a late check-out. The only thing I found to be a bit unusual for a hotel of this size is that they did not have coffee available until the restaurant opened at 6:00 or 6:30. I am used to there being a Starbucks machine in the lobby of most hotels. I could have walked down the street however that is a bit of a pain at 5 in the morning. The room coffee is never any good plus I did not want to wake my friend.

“Thumbs up” To me, the two biggest things the Jewel has going for it are location and price. Now, pretty much any hotel in Midtown between, say, Third and Eighth Aves is going to offer easy access for many of the things most tourists want to see. But the Jewel's proximity to Rockefeller Center and Fifth Ave. shopping makes it even more appealing, and there isn't a ton of traffic noise at night, unlike places closer to Times Square. As for price, I got an upgraded room for $209/night with my AAA discount. That is really hard to beat. By American standards, the proportions of the place are tiny. Were I claustro- or crowd-phobic, I wouldn't want to spend too much time in their itty bitty lobby during 3 pm check-in. Even the hallways feel small. By Manhattan standards, these dimensions aren't unusual, and I suspect that the many, many Europeans who stay here aren't phased by it at all. Because of the great rate, I chose a "superior" room, which offered a bit more space. Granted, the bathroom is still very small, but the rest of the room was comfortable (again, especially when compared with nearby hotels at this price point). Another advantage to springing for a bigger room is that having the bed farther away from the door probably meant a quieter night sleep for me. The room itself was pleasing and contemporary... nothing particularly remarkable, but clean, aesthetically appealing and comfortable. I did notice that the TV didn’t have the greatest picture, but then again, being holed up in one’s hotel room is not the best way to spend time in New York City! The Jewel is a very good place to stay.

“Nice FS Marriott, good location, outstanding Concierge Lounge” I've stayed at this hotel many times over the last year and have had a good stay just about every time. The location is great for Inner Harbor access. My Marriott Platinum status gets me access to the Concierge Lounge, and this lounge has one of the best breakfast spreads of any CL in the US. It rivals international lounge setups. All in all, a very nice hotel.

“Great hotel but can be pricey” After learning never to stay too far away from Logan when you have a 6:00 AM flight, the Hilton Boston Logan has become my "go to" hotel when flying home. It can be a bit expensive but knowing that I can wake up, walk across the skywalk to my terminal and not have to fight Boston traffic is so worth it. Rooms are nice and have been updated. The lobby still looks like it's stick in the mid 90's but that's no big deal. Fitness center features a good bit of Precor equipment and is maintained fairly well. And while I never have a big need for hotel staff, they're always friendly and welcome me back since I usually stay here 4-5 times a year. Only downside is the restaurant (Connoly's Public House).It's meant to be a British type pub but it's just a sports bar with lots of wood. Food has gotten worse each time I've dined here. It's not bad and I know it's an airport hotel so they've pretty much got you trapped but they could at least try to make a somewhat decent meal. I think the guests who stay here expect better food and are willing to pay for it.

“Modern, Clean Hotel in a convenient location” I booked this hotel for my parents for an overnight stay on June 2, 2007. The front desk staff and housekeeping were really instrumental in assisting my parents with checking in at 1000 (much before regular check-in time) so they could freshen up. The hotel and room are modern, well-kept and a good size for NYC. Their room was an internal room with windows and yet it was quiet. The location is great for conveniences, about 3 blocks to Central Park and the Natural History Museum, right on Broadway with a 24 hour diner across the street (which provides the room service for the hotel) and a Starbucks around the corner. There are lots of restaurants and shops right outside the lobby and parking next door, across the street and around the block. The concierge was helpful in planning our visit to the Statue of Liberty with regard to parking and suggested we eat breakfast near the hotel on Sunday morning before heading to Battery Park (where we wouldn't have found many, if any, breakfast options). A nice hotel. I wouldn't hesistate to recommend it or stay there on a subsequent visit to NYC.

“Comfortable Stay on the Edge of Downtown” No complaints on the room. It was large, comfortable and well-appointed, with the plushest bathrobes and great bath amenities. The hotel is also conveniently attached to a Whole Foods, making it easy to get cheap bottled water and some munchies. Staff were very pleasant and friendly. While the hotel is located downtown, it's about a 10-15 minute walk to where all the action is (restaurants, shopping, bars). We also drove to Pike Place Market because of the distance from the hotel. Since we only had one night we felt the need to maximize our time by driving but for anyone with the time or inclination to stroll, this is a nice place to base yourself.

“Third Room was Close enough to the Charm” I had a great stay here in October and reviewed the hotel very favorably back then. I was in town with 15 colleagues in January and we had gotten a great group rate to stay at this hotel, including upgraded rooms (which should have been the same room type I stayed in back in November). The hotel has a great location near our office and with hotel rates so high in NYC, we were happy to find an affordable option, especially one I could recommend firsthand from my last stay. Unfortunately it was an absolute disaster. I arrived at about 1am Monday morning, got checked in, went up to a room and straight to the bathroom only to find it had not been cleaned (see photo). Whatever was in there had been sitting for a while and the bowl looked all around. There were also hairs on the bathroom floor, several, which just made me feel that the room had not been cleaned. I immediately went downstairs and said that room was not acceptable. Btw, the room size and quality was MUCH worse than what I experienced in the upgraded room before. I was given another room, no apology for the problem in the first room, although I was told to call downstairs to let them know if the room was okay. But that point I was exhausted and just needed to get some sleep, so when I got in the room and the toilet was clean (although there was still a hair on the bathroom floor), I just made sure to check the matress and sheets for bedbugs (no signs of everything) before going to bed. Overall, both of the rooms were smaller than I had been in and overall looked very dingy, old and in general like they need a good cleaned (for example, don't lose the remote behind the nightstand, it's filthy back there!, I didn't want to walk on the carpet barefooted). If it was only me, I probably wouldn't stayed in the second room without an issue. I have never changed rooms for such a problem in the past and I spent more than 50 nights a year in hotels of all star levels. I was mortified when I got to work though and heard that nearly every colleague I was staying with had had pretty bad problems. I couldn't believe this had happened after my good stay before! I took notes of all the problems and called my hotel contact at lunch to say we all needed to be in better rooms or we'd be checking out. Here are the problems that were shared with me: toilet wouldn't flush (2 people, one it was fixed for), shower wouldn't drain (several people), hair on the floor, generally not up to a clean standard, phone was broken, remote was missing from one of the rooms, sheets were dirty and had to be changed on one room. I was shocked that there were such problems. My colleagues and I have reasonable expectations of having a clean room where things work -- nothing fancy, just that. When I called, and all throughout my dealings with the hotel, I really don't have many complaints. They seemed shocked to hear about the problems and really tried to help. While it did take a bit of back and forth, and it still wasn't great when we moved rooms, I have to say that they handled it pretty well. I first talked to my contact who I had negotiated the rates with. I found out that only a few of us were in the negotiated deluxe rooms -- i said we all needed to be in the rooms and she said that she could upgrade me to a suite, but they were sold out of deluxe rooms... what?! that's what we PAID to be in! I told her she needed to refund our entire bill and we'd be moving hotels... well, then the GM called back and said he would move us all Not sure where the rooms magically came from. I got put in a nice suite, clean, good size, I had no complaints. Some of my colleagues were fine with their new rooms, although there was still a handful who said there was no apparent difference between the Deluxe room and the other room they were in (no cleaner, no newer, no bigger, etc), although at least everything worked in the room. This was pretty disappointing. I met with the GM and we did work out a better deal, but overall it was such a disappointing experience that the hotel just was not up to a good standard. If it was just my room that needed to be changed, that would be one thing. I know things happen, but when 90% of my group was appalled by their room, had to change rooms up to 3 times, that's just unacceptable. It's too bad b/c I need to plan a lot of trainings in NYC and we're not taking any chances this time and staying at the W instead. Even in the suite I was in, there was a dull sound of a dishwasher/washer just outside of the back corner of the room (24th fl). If my husband was with me, he probably wouldn't have had any problem sleeping, but it was obnoxious to me and I had to wear earplugs. Overall, I feel that once the issue was elevated, they were trying to help and were quick in responding and trying to find a solution. Definitely made concessions that helped but at the end of the day, we weren't in the rooms we were supposed to be in, and even when we were, there were problems with them, even several days in and after talking to everyone. Management has to clean up for poor front desk and housekeeping staff. checkout was fast and were able to stick to what they promised. bottom line, really depends on the room. i've now stayed in two very solid rooms for the price, but also saw 2 that were unacceptable, along with all those that were unacceptable to my colleagues.

“Good experience” My wife and three boys stayed here at the end of August. Our one bedroom suite was much larger than typical and the staff was great all the way around. We had some minor complaints, the furniture was pretty tired in the living room, the pullout couch was a full rather than a queen but nothing serious. The room did have a quirk, no windows in the bedroom. It was a good hub for exploring and walkable to many things, even with a 5 year old. I wouldn't recommend it for the young and cool but for a family of 5 it worked very well.

“Poor service and pests!” I stayed at the Hotel Indigo at the Alamo midweek for three nights as part of a business trip. It was a return visit, as I had stayed there twice before in 2010. The previous two visits were great, and I looked forward to the stay. I was placed into a tiny room facing away from the street. I was surprised somewhat by the size, given my repeat customer status and my Priority Gold status. However, I decided to accept the "fault" as my own for booking a queen bed room instead of a king. On my final night, I crawled into bed around 11:30 p.m. following a late dinner. That's when I noticed a "crack" on the wall that seemed to move. Upon closer inspection, I discovered the crack was actually a trail of ants. They started at the bowl of chips on the desk and trailed past my headboard to the window. I obviously couldn't sleep at this point and contacted the front desk. "Hi, I'm staying in room XYZ and am checking out tomorrow, but there are ants all over the walls." "OK." "So, I'll need to move to a different room." "Let me see if something's available." AVAILABLE?! I just told you that you have a pest problem. How are the first words out of your mouth "Oh, I'm so sorry" or "Let me get you another room right away." I was told that another room one floor down was available, so I quickly packed up my things and went to the desk to get my key. Again, no apology. When I opened the door to my new room, I discovered that it was unmade. Back to the front desk I go! It's now past midnight. "The room that you just put me in hasn't been made up." "Oh, my book showed that it was." WHERE'S THE APOLOGY?! I kept silent at this point, given how furious I was. I was finally placed in a larger, made-up, ant-free room where I got a grand total of 6 hours of sleep before leaving the next morning. I left a follow-up voice message to the director of sales later that day expressing my frustration about this stay, the fact I was offered no compensation or even an apology, and that I had stayed prior. I requested a callback and never received one. Quite unfortunate, given my previous two stays in 2010 were good. But there's plenty of other hotels in this area of the Riverwalk, and this property has lost my business for good.

“The Best We've Tried for Convention Center, Petco Park or Gaslamp” My husband and I have stayed at several of the downtown San Diego properties and this is our favorite to date. Pros: 1. Rooms, clean, modern with comfy beds, good down-style pillows, and a large window with pseudo seat to take in the view. 2. Location, PERFECT for a convention,and a bridge to Petco park, right on the bay with fantastic views of Coronado island, a walkway along the waterway connecting you to the convention center, marriott, hyatt, sea port village, and eventually USS midway if you are a GREAT walker. However, only on site restaurants are there, everything else is a bit of a walk. 3. Pool, nice heated pool and jacuzzi with view of the bay (and a large Dole Freighter while we were there) and a Huge TV playing the NCAA basketball tournament. 4. Noise, this is the kicker, some of the other hotels are really near the trolly or worse train, that blows its horn throughout the night. I didn't hear much of anything from my room except some howling wind, but we were in the midst of a heavy winter storm. 5. Views, the lobby bar and various other vantage points have really pretty views of the bay, and had the weather been nicer we would have enjoyed our drink on the deck. They even have a fire ring outside that looked like a fun place to enjoy a drink. Cons: 1. Parking, was $27, I think, my frugal husband did free street parking blocks away, not sure how he found that but he was determined. 2. Service, we only interacted with the staff at check-in and check-out: check-in was luke warm and check-out was really slow due to a couple of guests with prolonged transactions Tips: 1. We bought the bed and breakfast package for an extra $30/nt for 2 buffet passes because I read on Tripadvisor the cash price is like $24? for one so I thought we'd just commit ahead of time. 2. Made a reservation for breakfast buffet, which was great because we caught a huge line from the conventioneers and were able to buypass the line.

“Despite Trump, I loved it” The last name on earth I associate with is Donald Trump, but I decided to give this a shot. From the second you enter the door, this is a true 5 star experience, the likes of which I don't think I've ever had anywhere. And I commonly stay at places like St. Regis, etc. etc. You enter the door, you're welcomed, asked your name and escorted to a very discreet desk in the minimalist lobby. In seconds, you have your room, and at least 5 people welcome you by name. The room was a one-bedroom suite, and it was breathtaking. Not only a large living room, but attached to it is a full kitchen, in exquisite style. You can actually cook in this room, although there isn't an oven. Everything is decorated in perfect taste, very expensively, but not ostentagious at all. The bathrooms were beautiful, there's even a flat screen tv built (somehow) in to the mirror! The only negative was the fireplace, which I was looking forward to enjoying. It's completely fake, electric optical-illusion flames, no heat at all. The bar is also magnificent in the hotel, complete with very finely made drinks and a luscious bar menu, with awesome sushi. I am sure that everyone of the highest taste will be pleased with this hotel. it's a truly premium class experience.

“Great location - traveler be ware” I have stayed at the Omni Shoreham three or four times in the last two years. The hotel is mostly a conference hotel, which means they are often discounting rates to attract guests during slow periods. While published rates are very, very expensive, I have never paid more than $100 a night for the Omni on Priceline. Most of my stays have been pleasant, but after my most recent stay, I doubt I will stay here. For the record, it has a great location and has nice amenities. Unfortunately, the service just isn't at the level you would expect partly because it is a conference hotel and a significant number of the guests will never return -- so there isn't an incentive to provide good service. When I stayed in February, the service was downright awful. I ate at the restaurant, but had to wait 10 minutes for a menu and drinking water. My dining party, which included two prominent politicians, was seated at the worst possible table -- in the far corner just outside the bathrooms. It took another 20 minutes for our meals to arrive, but the orders were wrong. Shockingly, the waitress took the meals back to the kitchen and the chefs scrapped off the wrong items instead of replacing it with what was ordered. This was totally unacceptable. And the manager's reaction? A basic apology and 5-percent reduction in the bill. Perhaps most disturbing was when I posted a comment about my experiences at the Omni on Twitter. This led to a hotel employee confronting me in the lobby and harassing me for my comments. I don't know if these are isolated incidents, as I never experienced anything like this on my previous trips to the Omni. While it is nice hotel in a great location, there does seem to be a trend of poor service.

“Dirty filthy disgusting!!!” My partner and I recently stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. Firstly when we arrived at reception, the staff were rude. The gentlemen seemed to find something strange about the fact that I wanted a king room for 2 men. When I arrived at room 711 it was blatantly obvious that it had not been cleaned and hadn't been cleaned thoroughly for some time. There were no towels and very little toilet paper. We told the man at reception who shrugged it off and said "I'll get some sent up". A few hours later some towels but no toilet paper had arrived. One of the towels was filthy and dull of holes. It looked like the rags I use to wash my dog! We were forced to leave a $50 deposit at reception, Why? Who on earth would want to steal anything? The entire room was dirty and the walls were stained. The furniture was falling apart, the shower was hanging off the wall and the phone didn't look as though it had been moved or cleaned for 30 years. The photos on your website are very misleading. I spoke with several other guests who said their rooms were just as bad. When the cleaners came to do whatever it is they do they didn't replenish the shampoo until the final night when I left a note requesting some. The staff couldn't even be bothered to place the fresh toilet roll on the stand, instead it was left still packaged next to the dirty sink. The one lift in operation was also faulty. DO NOT STAY HERE!!!! The only positive is that there is a fabulous donut shop and an ihop nearby.
“fabulous” Great place in a beautiful location and really nice staff. Also, two great restaurants on either side of the hotel. Well worth it.

“Ok, but nothing special for the $$ they charge” I am a Diamond Member at Hilton but decided to give this chain a shot when I had my 20th Anniversary in Seattle. Well to start off I booked a suite and paid extra and then found that their website description is not what you get. A suite has more than a bedroom and a bathroom (standard hotel room). When I took my printed reservation down to the front desk and showed them that it said things like two TV, a couch, ect, the desk clerk told me "oh, they mixed two suites into the same description on the Kimpton Website - sorry about that how about a free breakfast". You got to be kidding me! Even Embassy Suits has a sitting room, bathroom and bedroom unlike what Kimpton calls "a suite". I was here for a 5 day stay and this was how they offer to correct false advertising? I send the Kimpton preferred guest website an email asking about the failure to provide a suite as advertised on their website (my reservation description) (also furnished a hard copy of the reservation printout (from their website) to the front desk manager on duty) and did not get any reply or solution. I also send an email after the trip (guest survey) and once again did not get any follow up via email or mail. So I guess that tell you how concerned they are about guest. The staff ranged from indifferent to not helpful. I asked the front desk if their was any good breakfast spots in the neighborhood hood and was told, no only the hotels. Gee I found one of the best breakfast spots in Seattle 1/2 a block away, how convenient that the hotel does not know they exist. We arrived late the first night (11 pm) and had to go inside and run down the bellman who busy chating on his cell phone to get any help with our bags. Prior to my arrival I had emailed the hotel to inform them that it was my 20th Anniversary as my other half is really picky so I wanted to make sure everything was good to go. I got a nice email back saying they would like to deliver a bottle of champagne and some chocolate covered strawberries to our room upon arrival to celebrate. I also told them we needed foam pillows. So upon arrival no champagne or strawberries, no foam pillows and we had a great room with a view of an alley and high rise building -nice! Now the good - you will not find a better housekeeping staff or a cleaner room than this property. We were very impressed that when we left each morning to go out shopping that they made up the room before we got back (even short trips of 2 hours or less). The beds were comfortable. Not so good - the AC-Heat control has a 4 x 4 inch screen that is bring green and will shine directly in your eyes all night. If you are light sensitive, you will have to tape something over the controls. This is not a 4 start hotel, it a very clean business hotel with super high rates. You can do better at any of the chain hotels in Seattle.

“Ok if you don't want to sleep” The room was clean and updated. There was plenty of space for me, my wife and 2 daughters. The problem is that it is right off of a very busy road and it was nearly impossible to sleep. Also the breakfast buffet was horribly inefficient even with three breakfast attendants. Most Homewoood suites I've stayed at only have one and do a much better job. Trash was overflowing, they were constantly out of hot items, and finding a clean table was impossible. These are all the things that kept me from giving the hotel a higher rating. As I mentioned before the room itself was great.

“Nice hotel, nice location” The Grand Hyatt is what you think a big chain hotel in a big city will be; filled with business and tourist folks alike. This is no surprise either, the hotel's location is downtown,close to the financial hub for the suits, and for the fanny pack crowd, only blocks away from great shopping on Market or the odd smells of Chinatown. As with a majority of our personal travels, my wife and I secured a great rate using Priceline. Gotta love that William Shatner!! Our room was larger than what I expected of a major downtown hotel and it was clean. The bed wasn't "heavenly" or cloud-like, but I slept well and that's all I really need.
