The one mildly disturbing room feature were the paper thin walls. If you're a light sleeper, bringing ear plugs will remedy the situation. We didn't have car, so I can't tell you about parking. If you can avoid having to rent a car (i.e. you're staying in the city), do so. Parking in SF should be an Olympic sport; an EXPENSIVE Olympic sport performed only by those highly trained in the craft. Besides, SF is a great city to explore on foot and the Muni bus system and the BART (use it from SFO into the city) is one of the best public transportation systems in the country (relax, NYC yours is still the best). Oh yeah, and the California cable car line is about three blocks from the hotel. It will take you to within a block or two of the Ferry building and all it's restaurants and gourmet shops. I'd stay at this hotel again without question.

“Severely outdated!!” I am a frequent traveler to NYC -- I was having trouble getting a room on a recent trip and a colleague said "try the Roger Smith" it is a no frills boutique hotel. Immediately I was concerned, but I don't have to be all about the frills. Ok, the good -- excellent location, walking distance to everything, the staff was great. I got in 20 minutes after the restaurant had closed and just wanted a glass of wine before bed. The manager said no problem and brought me glass, no charge. All really good. BUT the room was outdated. It had really bad furnishings -- starting with Kelly Green carpet and drapes. I felt like I had stepped back in time into my grandmothers guest bedroom. It wasn't bad for one night and I might stay here again in a pinch but I won't make it my regular spot.

“Problems with the internet..” My husband and I spent the nights of 12/6 and 12/7 "won" on Priceline in a double room on the 32nd floor of the north tower, room #3286. The valet staff swooped upon us the moment we pulled in under the awning and responded in a helpful way when we explained that we wanted to self park ($21 -vs- $29 a night). Check in took probably about 20 minutes. We checked in about 4pm and there was a bit of a line with only two front desk staff members on duty. The front desk staff was quick and friendly when we finally made our way to the front of the line and honored our request for a double room on a high floor. She gave us excellent instructions on where to park in the garage to have the easiest access to the north tower elevators. The parking garage was easily accessed by our room key. The garage is set up a little differently than most garages and the parking spots are very narrow. The garage is littered with post missing chunks and holes in the walls at the front of the parking spaces where people have attempted to park in the tiny spaces. I guess I expected a little more comfort in my parking experience for the price that was paid. Our room was spacious and very nicely decorated. The beds were pretty comfortable. We had many channel choices on the television. The bathroom was a comfortable size and offered typical hotel amenities including a blow dryer. There was a small rust spot in the tub, but everything was very clean. There was one big problem with our room... we were never able to connect to the internet. On the first evening we were there we were able to access the web far enough to be offered three different internet packages ranging from $14.95 a day to $21.95. On two different devices we agreed to the lowest priced plan for two days and after a few minutes were never able to get online again in our room. We called the tech support number and followed all of the instructions given, but it did not work. We were given a code by the tech and took it to the front desk and they removed the charge with no problem. The web is available in public areas of the hotel but it was super slow with lots of time outs. I walked all over the lobby area to try and find a better signal, but it was slow everywhere. We ate breakfast in the restaurant the first morning and it was way overpriced! The food was okay, but $4 for a Coke.. seriously? We had two meals in the sports bar and both times we had a very good experience. The food is more reasonably priced there and pretty much everything we ate there was very tasty. The service in the sports bar was amazing! I would stay here again of they resolved the connectivity issues.

“Free Concert (all night long)” I spent one night at the Omni last weekend after a full day of traveling and didn't rest very well at all. First, the hotel cancelled my reservation. I was traveling with a large group and although they confirmed my room with the trip coordinator, somehow my name was "erased" from the hotel's nightly manifest. After being told that I'd have to get a room at another nearby hotel (apart from the rest of the 100 people in my group), a manager finally "found" an available room. Even after being accommodated, I got no rest. The hotel is located in a prime downtown area and it seems ( as experienced by other reviewers) to be right next to a nightly open-air concert. I mean, I was on the 10th floor and I could clearly hear the bass beats and words of every song sung until about 11:30 PM when I finally just turned the TV up to drown out the sound and fell asleep. Ultimately, my rest was anything but restful at the Omni.

“Great for the Price” The Parc 55 is a great hotel for the value. We took a gamble and booked on Hotwire, but were pleasantly pleased with what we got for $110 a night. The checkin was smooth, room service was good and the valets were fast and helpful. The concierge was a bit snotty, but hey, it happens. The only bad thing was the Friday night we were there, some drunk morons were down in the street yelling and doing their best to get hit by taxis at 1 a.m. We could watch them from our room and wished we could have thrown water balloons at them or something to make it more interesting... Even though we were nine floors up, it made sleep tough for a while. No wonder they have complimentary ear plugs in the bathrooms! Overall, a nice hotel with a great location.

“Great service” We stayed here for a week and very much enjoyed our stay. It was clean, modern, and the staff was terrific. They were very helpful with everything we asked for, especially with our plans for visiting local attractions. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Dirty, dingy with miserable and rude staff” After posting dozens of reviews on tripadvisor.com over the past couple of years, I hope I've established a bit of a reputation as a reliable source. Trust me when I tell you this: For me, the Dupont Circle Residence Inn has a very special place in the Marriott lineup. I am sad to say this property is far and away THE worst hotel I have stayed in during many years of business travel. Don't even think about staying here. There are many better choices in central Washington, DC. I'll keep this short and to the point. I arrived just before 11 PM on a recent Sunday night. Instead of encountering the usual Marriott professionalism at the front desk, the night clerk ("Andrew") greeted me with sarcasm and contempt, the likes of which I have rarely encountered anywhere...ever. The entire check-in was steeped in condescension as Andrew responded to my normal questions about facilities, services, and hours with adjectives, adverbs, and tones overtly hostile and annoyed. He even argued with me about my elite membership status (gold), insisting I was silver and apparently unworthy of his professional courtesy. I was tired after a long trip, so I trundled up to my room (#802) through the abused elevator and filthy hallways. My room proved wholly inadequate. It had not been cleaned properly for a long time, appearing to have been only cursorily wiped down. Furniture was over the hill, dirt and grunge lingered in and around the cabinets, door hinges were broken, and shelves were falling out. The queen bed was terribly uncomfortable and a far cry from the bedding at every other Marriott property I have been in during the past couple of years. The handicapped-accessible bathroom felt more like a dingy locker room. One appeal for Residence Inn is the ability to cook for yourself. Here you can pretty well forget about making any "real" meals on the tiny two-burner stove and microscopic microwave. They were the worst I have seen at such a place. The ice maker in the refrigerator had been turned off, so when I called the front desk to ask where an ice machine may be, Andrew gave me a sarcastic lecture describing how, in its great corporate wisdom, Residence Inn had no ice makers, because the refrigerators had them instead. Yes, I explained, but mine was off, and I would have to wait a long time for ice. I wanted a cold drink before retiring. Eventually he stopped arguing and agreed to bring some ice from the kitchen downstairs. Within 30 minutes, I had had enough and resolved to find another hotel for the next four days of my trip. I called the Marriott reservations desk immediately. In the morning, another desk clerk proved totally unprepared for a simple question about directions: "Quickest way to Arlington?" Instead, after much consternation, I received a map and directions to I-95 and an unrelated place 20 miles out of the way. "This should get you close," she said. I spent over two C-notes for a miserable eight hours in this dump. It's not worth a single Jackson. Stay away. Period. End of story.

“Best in Venice” Been to Cali 2x in past year.... Stayed in the VBSH BOTH times and LOVE the place.... First time was a shot in the dark and i loved it so much i made it a point to go back..... If you want straight-edge high end & pristine take a hike down to Manhattan Beach and you'll get the Hamptons west.... if you're into activity, life, and real people stay here .... the beach is at your doorstep as is music & art and people skateboarding, rollerblading, bike riding, walking and people just living the cali life.... Yes there are homeless people living on the boardwalk buts thats the nature of trhe business down there.... During the day they just blend in w/the crowds.... and at night I have never been bothered at all.... The beach does get quite and dark at night but thats b/c its the beach and theres not much else around except for lots of water! The staff is awesome.... tell you exact where to park on the street so walk the 2 blocks it's no big deal.... the bottle wine is a nice touch and the rooms are very nice.... you can just settle into your small apartment for a few days.... very relaxing.... def worth the rooms above the first floor so you get a view of the water/boardwalk....

“it will be my "go-to" place to crash in austin. cheap. clean. comfortable. freebies.” so i booked at the Ramada one late night on a Saturday night. After working 13 hour days all weekend and staying in the Motel 6 up the street for 3 nights, this was a nice upgrade. its not 5 star by any means but is about the nicest "cheap" hotel/motel your gonna get. the step down is a Motel 6 / Super 8 and the step up is something along the lines of Holiday Inn. this lays right in between the two. you'll pay about the same amount to stay at the Motel 6 or $100 more to stay at a Holiday Inn. Stay at the Ramada, its the best deal. Its an older property but still gives you the most bang for your buck. I scored my room for only $65 on a Saturday night. where everyone else was charging more. Motel 6 wanted $80 so I left. Hotels/Motels fluxuate prices during weekends and by vacancy so i guess I just happened to be staying in a packed Motel 6 and the Ramada was a little less full so the price dropped. Even though they were only about 3 miles apart. Anyway, the rooms are nice and comfortable. Clean linens and very comfortable beds. You get in-room ironing board and iron, a small closet area to hang clothes, coffee maker, cold a/c, cable tv (older model tv- not flat screen) some other motels have already upgraded to flat screens. (i travel alot), mine had a small desk and office area that was nice to sit down at and hammer out some emails. oh, there is free internet their as well. Or there was when I was there. The place as quiet and chill on a saturday night even though there was a biker rally going on in austin at the time. maybe i just got lucky because i scored a room on the top floor and in the back corner. so it was silent, peaceful and comfortable. the bathroom was clean and tidy. little travel size grooming products were offered up in the bathroom shelf so that was good. mouthwash, soap, lotion, there was even a small bottle of travel size hand sanitizer. they have a fairly decent continental breakfast but nothing to write home about. its basic stuff. cheap cereal, donuts, bagels, muffins, juice, coffee, milk, maybe a banana and apple or 2. it wasnt all that good but its really nice to have the option. i just packed up this little bag with donuts and bagels and hit the road. filled up my thermos with juice too. hey, one for the road. Overall, i had a nice stay there for the same price as a cheaper quality motel. got way more for my money and felt more comfortable during my stay. i'll be back there this month to stay while on business. cheap stays equals more per diem for my pocket. rock n roll. thumbs up ramada

“Pretty Good” This is a decent hotel in a great location. Our suite provided a good amount of room and was very clean. Check-in was efficient, but very perfunctory - can't say the front desk staff was overly friendly or welcoming, but they were efficient. There were a few minor negatives - some of the doors in our suite had holes in them, the water pressure wasn't particularly good, the drain in the tub was very slow, and the wine and beer during the "happy hour" were atrocious (they could do much better for not much more money - and maybe even less). But, the food during happy hour was plentiful and quite tasty (you could make dinner out of it) and breakfast was excellent with lots of choices and very good service from the staff. Staff during "happy hour" was also very nice - friendly and looking for ways to be helpful. The couch in the lobby could use replacing as it's pretty saggy and threadbare. Overall it was a very good choice. We'd definitely stay here again - good value for the money.

“Blah....but great staff and good location.” I've stayed at this hotel before for the annual Hustle Up the Hancock, so I had to look back to see if I posted a previous review. I had not. And, I think that I know why: the rooms do nothing for me, but the staff makes a good impression. I don't want to ding the hotel because I like the staff, but then I never look forward to staying there either. Pros: Really personable staff. I only stay there for the event, so perhaps they put their best foot forward at that time. When staff members are able to deal with families carrying multiple bags, stuffed animals, and a talkative kid, I give them kudos for the extra effort. Also, the rooms were clean.... Cons: Room decor. The rooms didn't have a personality. They were too functional (barren), even for a mid-range hotel. There were also lots of bare walls. They need to have a good interior designer come in to make some quick fixes. Finally, I think that I really wanted to be at the Westin next door, although from being in its lobby it doesn't seem as kid friendly as the Hilton!

“Always a fun place to stay!” We stayed at Pointe Squaw Peak from Monday, July 13 to Wednesday, July 15. We enjoyed ourselves ~ we had stayed at the resort a few years ago and were pleased to see the updating that had been done! The room was quite comfortable, the front desk staff extraordinarily kind and pleasant, and the housekeeping and maintenance staffs never failed to stop and move out of the way for guests ~ as well as share a pleasant greeting. Used the workout facility (treadmill only) and was pleased with it ~ it's a short walk across the parking lot. The River Ranch water park was great ~ loved the water slide and lazy river. Since we were there during the weekdays, there weren't any problems with too many people or rowdy people at all! (The lazy river is DEFINITELY lazy ~ get ready for a long, meandering tube ride!!!) The water is warm, but, hey folks, this is Phoenix in July and the air temp is 110 degrees at 8 p.m.!!! The Hole in the Wall restaurant was fine ~ not impressed with the waitstaff whatsoever, though! Try Aunt Chilada's, a Mexican Restaurant a short walk from the main lobby (5 minutes?). Also, if you're not interested in a daily newspaper, call over to the front desk and get the 75 cent/day charge removed from your account ~ every little bit helps!!! All in all, a fun experience for the family ~ you have to try really hard not to have a good time!!!

“Wonderful respite on top of Nob Hill” I am a fan of Fairmonts in general, and though the brand is not absolutely consistent, it has often delivered high quality service and physical facilities. The Fairmont SFO is no exception. A very nice property and generally courteous and professional service. Location is great. It's right on top of Nob Hill, so the view is quite spectacular. I was in the Tower, and my room had a harbour view, which means I could see Alcatraz from my room. At night the lights of the city below are quite enticing. I was in SFO for business in the Union Square area, which is only a quarter of a mile from the hotel. But because the hotel is up on the hill, it's away from the noise and crowds below. I consider the location of the Fairmont to be ideal -- close enough to things but a place to escape to after. But it's on a hill. A steep one to boot. I like walking, but still going up gets tough especially if you do it two or three times a day. Of course you can also do the cable car, or take a cab. But I thought the walk would do me good after all the nice good in the city. The room is spacious. It's called a deluxe room in the Tower. Marble bathroom. Separate shower and tub. Miller Harris toliteries as usual. Bathrobes, etc. Large Flat screen TV, though reception is a bit iffy. No stereo equipment, other than an IPOD docking station/alarm clock. No coffee/tea making equipment in the room -- this is disappointment, since I have always enjoyed a cup of their nice Fairmont selection of teas in my rooms. Electronic safe in room, which is very nice. A/C works, if not extremely powerful, it is effective enough. Good closet space, though if you have a lot of overcoats etc it may become a bit cramped. Room in very good condition. I encountered none of the worn out conditions that some other reviewers mentioned. As is, my room, at least, does not even need a reno job. It's nice enough for a Fairmont. Breakfast in the Laurel Court. It's included in my rate. Very wide selection of foods for breakfast buffet. $28 per person. Given what's available and the quality, it's a bargain. I did not have other meals at the hotel. The lobby is probably the grandest part of the hotel. Impressive. All in all, a very nice hotel. If I go back to SFO, I'll definitely check out this hotel first.

“You'll be seeing red, but in a good way” Love the Kimpton Hotel properties and this one didn't disappoint. Great spacious rooms with a cool vibe. Love the big, fluffy robes. If you're looking for something a bit different, this is a good choice. Food at the bar isn't bad either but I'd pass on the overpriced breakfast buffet. Only complaint is the limited channel selection on the TV, should be better for this type hotel. And the gym equipment could use an update.

“Unexpected Surprise” When traveling, I like to look at myself as a realist. When I put a bid in for a NYC hotel for $100, I know that I'm not going to be staying at a luxury hotel. I get what I pay for. So after having my bid accepted for a $100 a night for two nights, I didn't want to have unrealistic expectations. Upon checking in, I asked to see the room or have a choice of rooms. The attendant seemed puzzled by this so I ask her if there were any upgrades available. I was moved from a standard room to a deluxe room for $50.00 a night. Though I never saw a standard room, the deluxe room was a pleasant surprise. My room (1755) was on the 17th floor and a corner room with three windows ... including one in the bathroom. My room faced E. 28th and Madison and I loved the view. The room also had some character, including a large bathroom with tub/shower and a little "nook" in the room that that had two carpeted stairs leading to it. I enjoyed my morning coffee there while I decided my daily plan. Though the room did have some signs of wear (marks from luggage, etc.) it was a delight and I fell in love with it. There were only a few rooms (six I think) on the 17th floor. This was the top floor and I would recommend staying higher if possible. There is a water main being repaired from 8:00 PM until 4:30 AM each day, though the air conditioning system blocked that out and I wasn't interupted. I was interupted by the housekeeping staff that talked loudly and we opening and shutting doors, but it was after 8:00 AM. In conclusion, I would definitely stay here again. There appears to be two hotels in one, which travelers should be aware of. The bottom floors are standard rooms and the top floors are deluxe rooms. You will notice this when the elevator opens as the carpeting color is different. Four elevators are available and rarely had to wait. There is a bar, which has a nice happy hour from 5-7 with 1/2 priced cocktails. Loved that! The service at the hotel wasn't poor. They weren't overly friendly, but weren't rude either. I've been treated like royalty at other hotels, but this hotel keeps things low keyed. This didn't bother me, but others might want the red carpet rolled out when they arrive followed by a glass of wine ... that just won't be the case here. I was disappointed in the doorman though. I never say him helping anyone with luggage or opening and closing the door. Wasn't really sure of his purpose. Subway is about a ten minute walk. Grand Central in about 5 blocks north where you can catch the S, 4, 5, and 6. The 33rd station is located about 5 blocks south where you can catch the 6 train. If you prefer a close subway line, you may want to look elsewhere. I hope this review has helped you. It's honest and from my heart. Give the Jolly Madison a try!
“NYC business trip” The views are great. The restaurant is pricey and average.

“Good Location” We enjoyed our stay at the Grand Hyatt. It is in a good location to get on the underground subway which will take you anywhere. A trolly tour company is located on a corner outside the Ford Theater (which is also a very close walk from the hotel). The only complaint I have is the lack of windows to the outside. The hotel is built around a large inside courtyard, and light comes in from the top of the glass ceiling. I like more natural light than what the courtyard provided. Other than that minor detail, I would recommend this hotel when you are in the D.C. area.

“An oldie but a goodie!” I have to tell you I am not a fan of Sheraton hotels in general but this one could change my mind. I stayed at this hotel 20 plus years ago and recently stayed again on business. I realized this when I checked in. The hotel has been re-done inside (don't panic!) It is not dingy or have an old feel to it. The hotel staff was wonderful. They were fast to respond and VERY pleasant and accommodating! I was shocked my room service was delivered by the head chef. The food was delicious and hot. The sleep was VERY relaxing and restful. I highly recommend this hotel and WILL stay here again!

“Convenient, contemporary” This is a contemporary hotel, conveniently located in the heart of downtown near City Hall in a building that is famous as one of the first "skyscrapers" in the US. The interior decor is contemporary and understated, and the restaurant is good, if somewhat uneven in its level of service. My room was satisfactory if nothing special. Recommended.

“Wonderful Hotel and Staff” My husband and I stayed at this hotel just this past weekend. It was really a wonderful place and highly recommended. We did ask for a room on a high floor before we went and they had one all ready for us. It was on the 15th floor and was a very nice size. The bathroom was large also. It had a huge window with shutters. The weather was perfect and we were able to open the window a bit and let some fresh air in. Even though we were on the 15th floor , we still heard noises from the people outside on the streets below but it didn't bother us. And if we would have closed the window, we probably would not have heard anything. We had a view of some tall buildings and also it looked like some apts with rooftop terraces. Very nice! The staff was excellent and did anything for you. We highly recommend the breakfast buffet at the restaurant on the premise. Asked for extra towels and tissues and got them. Nothing was a problem. We will stay here again when we visit Boston.

“Lovely hotel” Stayed at the Georgetown Inn June 29-July 2. Was a perfect spot for touring Georgetown University. An easy walk takes you directly to the front gates of Georgetown University. the hotel itself was very nice. Clean and comfortable and well located in charming Georgetown. The rooms were a nice size and the air conditioning was plentiful. The staff were very nice and helpful. The doorman was always there with a smile, ready to help with the bags, open the door, and hail cabs. A nice added bonus is the Gray Line hop on hopoff tour bus stops directly in front of the hotel as does the DC circulator and Metro bus. Cab fare from the hotel to Union Station was about $14. The hotel has a great resaturant. We enjoyed both breakfast and dinner there every day. Huge portions of good, hot food for a reasonable price. Stay away from Martin's Tavern on the corner unless you like an abundance of flies with your mediocre meal. I would defintely stay here again. We were traveling with teens and seniors and everyone was well accomidated and happy.

“I agree that this is a great hotel” I have stayed at this hotel many times and just love it! The staff is great and the service is fantastic. Love the upstairs pool! As a Platinum HHonors Member they offer me a choice between points or a breakfast and I love my points. I know some are ticked off not getting the breakfast (yes people it is only for Platinum members) but I love my points. Thank you to the team and i recommend this hotel!

“Why would you EVER want to stay downtown again!?!?!” I found this place on Tripadvisor after despairing of the current high cost of downtown accommodations. The Ocean Park is the perfect antidote: affordable, laid-back, uniquely charming, immaculately-kept, and smack-dab adjacent to one of the MUNI Metro lines that takes you directly into the Market Street subway. Furthermore, it's not only handy to San Francisco State Univ. and the airport, but within walking distance of the Zoo and the magnificent Pacific Ocean beach. It's easy to forget that the Ocean Park is 70+ years old. My second-floor room was both spacious and cozy; with a warm-colors decor, a flat-screen TV and an amazingly comfortable bed, a clean, bright black-and-white tiled bathroom and a full walk-in closet. Though it's true that there are only a couple walking-distance diners, there are some wonderful neighborhood resturants, including authentic Chinese, and the unique Bashfull Bull Too a short hop (via driving or trolley) away on Taraval. Being a guest here is like having a special refuge, out by the beach, to which you can retreat after spending a busy day in the city. I've stayed in many many places in San Francisco; from high-end Union Square hotels to independent 50s-era two-story motels. None has given me so much basic satisfaction as the Ocean Park Motel. Oddly enough, I recently found a photo of one of the MUNI trolleys that I'd taken while on a visit to the Zoo in 2000. I've attached it with this review, along with a similar shot from Sept. of 2008. Despite being so close, I missed out on staying at the Ocean Park while on that earlier visit. I know better now.

“The City Never Sleeps ..... And neither will you!!” Handy Mid-Town location right at 48th between Park and Lex. Easy access to Grand Central, 5th Ave retail, Roc Center, Diamond Alley and if you want o stretch your legs Times Square. Lobby is nice - big and well appointed. Front desk staff was efficient but generic - gets you smoothly checked in - but running off the script. Rooms are fine - decent size by NYC standards - nicely turned out but tight. Could use some updaes - tv is small w poor picture - you get used to nice flat screens and these are not - no place for your stuff in the bathroom -comforter is thin w no extra blanket in the room. Wireless s really fast - but expensive at $16 a day -yikes Biggest issue is the noise -bell hop whistling for cabs, guy walking down the hall dropping off papers, room next door flushing toilet - you name it. It is New York and there is going to be some noise but this was a bit crazy. Was on the 8 th floor -maybe going up will help w street noise but the hall and neighbors are a problem.

“Rescued by the Hilton Garden Inn” After booking into a horrible well-known chain hotel in Chelsea, we moved the next morning to the Hilton Garden Inn. The room was twice as large as the previous room. The bed was comfortable and the furnishings looked new and well maintained. The breakfast offered was delicious! The restaurant in the hotel is one of many French restaurants owned by a single company. They are all excellent restaurants. The staff was friendly and took care of all of our needs quickly. When I informed the front desk that the lock wasn't working on our room door, someone was there to fix it in less than 2 minutes. Great timing! The conceirge was able to get outstanding tickets to a musical for us. Overall, a PERFECT stay. I wish I would have booked with this hotel from the beginning! Sadly, we couldn't stay longer because the hotel was booked for the last two nights of our trip to New York.

“Excellent Crash Pad” I stayed here for 1 night for business after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor. The room was spotless and quiet (it was not facing 8th Avenue.) The room was very tiny, but there is plenty to do in the vicinity. The staff was accommodating and friendly. I would definitely go back.

“Great business Hotel” Conveniently connected to the prudential tower. If you are taking the train in from the airport. get off at the Prudential stop on the green line and you go right into the mall. Short walk to the sheraton. The hotel was packed when we visited, though we still managed a upgrade to the starwood preferred floors. The room though had a small closet for hanging your coats and clothing. Mattress was slightly worn, needs to change soon. Bottled water complimentary 2 per day. A continental breakfast was offered, fresh fruit, yogurt, pastry, cereals and beverages. Pretty much the same spread everyday. Computers (2) were available to use in the lounge and at the lobby but for some reason they were very slow in loading the pages. Took the taxi back to the airport, was about 30 dollars.It was a good stay here at the Sheraton Boston. Will visit again,

“Good Business Stay” Staying on business, we had a couple of unusual requests that the front desk was happy to accommodate. The rooms were nice. Upgrades were apparently in progress as one of our rooms had an updated shower stall and the other didn't, but both were fine. The wifi worked well. The Jacksonville Landing and riverwalk are just a couple of blocks away with touristy, but decent, restaurants. I had lunch at the hotel restaurant and needed something quick. They told me that even a sandwich would likely take more time than I had, so I got the buffet which was good. You would think they would have a choice or two for those in a hurry, however. We also had their breakfast buffet which was pricey, but good. One problem which is just symptomatic of Jacksonville and not the fault of the hotel is that the tap water tastes awful. It's the same way in St. Augustine. The other problem occurred when I asked at the desk where I could print my boarding pass. The clerk was helpful, but told me that the front desk prints them for guests rather than having a self-serve kiosk. Well, okay, but I also had to select my seat on the flight and the clerk had to lift up the computer monitor and put it up on the counter for me to be able to see the choices. She was nice about it, but she shouldn't have to do that and I thought it was an unnecessary nuisance. That's really my only criticism or suggestion for this solid hotel.

“Fantastic Hotel” Upon arrival to the hotel, we were informed by the front desk manager that our room had been upgraded. My daughter and I were quite happy. Our room was much larger than expected, very clean with (2) flat screen tv's. There was free wifi and a complimentary bottle of water. The front desk staff were also very helpful with recommendations. I would highly recommend this hotel for families, business or overnight stays.

“Not Bad for An Older Property” This Hilton has just undergone a huge renovation. I had a room on the 16th floor and it was nicely remodeled. It had the feel of a European hotel with the decor and bathroom fixtures. The balcony was nice, as well, since the weather was great when I was there I spent some time out there. Room service was good and the breakfast down along the Riverwalk was decent, too. The meeting rooms were adequate for the conference I attended. The people that worked here were very friendly and helpful. The only real complaint I had was the valet parking was very, very slow. You better call down way ahead of time otherwise you will wait a long time. There was quite a bit of construction going on around the hotel including in the lobby area.

“Gorgeous, Stylish, Comfortable....even though it was for work, felt like a spa.” I am a big fan of the Holiday Inn family of hotels so I was pretty excited to try out their new concept hotel. It was fabulous. The rooms are gorgeous. Wood floors, uber-hip fabrics and textiles in the troom. I loved the Kuerig coffee maker and the Aveda bath products. The bed was super comfy and the whole hotel just had a fun vibe. The rooftop bar and fire pits are stunning. I would definitely stay here again. Plus it is only about 4 blocks over from the 5th street restaurants/bars.

“Comfortable, but not outstanding.” We stayed two nights at TownePlace at Arrowood; we had two small kids and four adults. The property is conveniently situated right off of I-77 but is tucked away behind a few other hotels, so there's less traffic noise than you'd think. The property itself is nice and well-kept; somewhat dated in spots. The lobby is very small but has a nice little mart with snacks and drinks if needed. The rooms are just OK - they're fairly cramped (even with two bedrooms, living area and kitchen, it felt REALLY tight) and the walls are paper-thin (could hear people coming up the stairs all night, and it sounded like the folks above us walked like a marching band). Our first room didn't have working AC, so we needed to switch (I should note - they gave us extra Rewards points for this inconvenience). Breakfast was minimal fare - bagels, bagged muffins, cereal, juice, yogurt and waffles. Better than nothing but I've seen MUCH better at Marriott properties. All in all, I wouldn't steer someone away from here as it's not terrible, but there are lots of other places to stay in Charlotte that are better than this.

“Noisy 5th floor” Only stayed one night; 5th floor hallway has some sort of AC/chiller noise towards the east end of the hallway - sounds like a jet engine. Fairly quiet with door shut. Room was ok, carpet did not look good, multiple spots, small bathrooms. Staff was exceptional though.

“Historic hotel, great location” We stayed for one night in a suite in the main building-we were upgraded to a signature suite upon check in for no apparent reason-love that! The suite was huge - 2 rooms with a large wrought iron balcony looking out towards the tower. We were very impressed by the room. We had room service dinner that was very good as well. The location of the hotel can't be beat, you're on top of Nob Hill with beautiful views, tons of things within walking distance, Grace Cathedral right there plus the Mark Hopkins and Huntington Hotels. At the Fairmont SF you really feel you're in SF not just another Hyatt or Hilton in any city. We'll be back!

“Super Hotel direkt am Union Square” Das Westin St. Francis liegt zentral in San Francisco am Union Square. Zur Starwood Kette gehörend, erhalten Gold und Platinum hier wie bei allen Starwood Hotels ebenfalls die bekannten Annehmlichkeiten wie Zimmerupgrade oder kostenlosen Internetzugang. Wenn möglich ein Zimmer im Tower buchen mit "Cityview" oberhalb des 20ten Stocks. Von dort hat man eine super Sicht auf Downtown San Francisco mit tollem abendlichem Lichtspiel. Wenn man mit dem Auto unterwegs ist, sollte man bedenken, dass Parken am Tag USD 50.- kostet, also nicht gerade ein Schnäppchen. Sonst kann das Hotel nur wärmstens empfehlen.

“Doubt you can beat this for value in midtown Manhattan: highly recommended” My partner and I stayed in a deluxe room for two nights, while visiting NYC for a friend's 40th. We travel a lot and are pretty demanding about the places we stay, and are pleased to say we found it pretty much impossible to fault this hotel. Above all, it's outstanding value: you get real quality and friendly service, for what's a relatively low cost for midtown Manhattan. We were particularly impressed by the comfortable, enormous bed, and by the well-equipped bathroom. The deluxe room had a small living room area included, which added to the sense of space, and is worth paying a little bit extra for. The bathroom was of a very high standard - nothing to write home about, but had everything you'd want while away from home. Check in and check out were extremely efficient and friendly, the free breakfast was simple but perfectly adequate, and the common areas in very good condition. All in, it's hard to fault this hotel. It may not win any awards for originality or being out there, but nevertheless it's very very comfortable, and we recommend it highly.

“Business Hotel. Very clean” I arrived for check-in at 10pm and there was a very short (less than 5 minute wait). The person at the front desk was very nice. The hotel was in reasonably good condition and the room was perfect. I say reasonably good because the carpet in the hallway was a bit dirty. The lobby looked very busy (Friday night 10pm). The only beef I had was parking which was 20 bucks. There is plentiful airport parking all around the hotel for about 12-14. Parking is four floors below ground and spaces are VERY limited. Drivers were circling. I only got a spot because another person was affraid to squeeze into the one I took.... Tiny spaces!

“Location and not much more” Located right on the San Diego Bay and next door to the Convention Center, Petco Park and Gaslight District you can not beat the location. The lobby is very striking but for a brand new hotel it is sad to say that is the only plus. The room was, while not tiny, surprisingly small. The bathroom was servicable but, again, small, with barely adequate lighting. It was impossible to get the right temperature in the room - it was always either stifling hot or too cool. Perhaps you can blame this on the hotel being new but it pretty much fit into the overall feeling that this was built for the masses who come to San Diego for an event. We tried the breakfast buffet. It was, again, adequate, but for $23 per person plus tip you can do better by walking a block or two. You can't beat the location if you are attending a convention or going to the ball game. If you want a nicer room there are plenty of other choices.

“Decent place but not over the top” We found the place somewhat cramped for the group of six that we were but it did have all the mod cons --however with one bathroom the going was tough ! Breakfast however was the best we had in the entire west coast US trip with good variety --- we were there for three nights and it was a decent stay but could have been better.

“Can I take the pool home with me?” Usually I laugh when I read the “great pool scene” rating on when I’m putting together a review. Swimming is my preferred exercise and the pool is generally an over-chlorinated, overheated pit in the basement. Not here. The Marriot has a huge pool, and the poolside is so popular there’s a sign prohibiting reserving beach chairs. The patrons were mostly 20-somethings, hanging out with each other and enjoying the great poolside bar. THIS is a great pool scene! Our room, on the 21st floor, was comfortable and kept clean (although sometimes it wasn’t serviced till early afternoon). We had the City view (Bay View is a little extra) and even on the 21st floor, noticed a few sirens and commuter train whistles. If you’re sensitive to those, bring earplugs. The room did appear to be well-soundproofed against noises in other rooms. The hotel is convenient to everything- a short walk to the waterfront, including Seaport Village and multiple museums and exhibits. If you head down First Street you’ll find Ralph’s, a 24/7 grocery that has everything including a full liquor department and pre-made sandwiches, wraps, sushi and a salad bar. Who needs Room Service when you’ve got Ralph’s? The toiletries in the room were high-end; citrus-scented shampoo and soap. My only problem with how the room was equipped was the usual undersized wastebaskets- our 2 were perpetually filled since we got newspapers and threw them out when done. Check-in and check-out were efficient; I asked them to remove the high-speed Internet charge when I couldn’t get it to work and it was removed with no problem. I got by with dial-up and was happy to find that I was not charged for the access through toll-free numbers. The hotel has an automated wake-up call servuce; they connect you to it and you punch in your room number and wake-up time. A bit impersonal, but it worked flawlessly the 3 mornings I used it. We were here for a business meeting but came in a day early at our own expense just so we could enjoy San Diego. The Marriott was well worth the price.

“Perfect for solo traveler” I traveled to NYC on a Friday to catch the last showing of a Broadway musical, and I am glad that I pick a hotel in financial district instead of midtown or Times Square. This hotel is away from the police siren and all the hustle bustle you would typically get in Manhattan, especially on the weekends. I was given the City View room on 44th floor (The highest floor), but I didn't encounter any problems regarding the wait for the elevators. Again, probably it was because I stayed during the weekend. The staff was helpful and the room is clean, I would definitely recommend to anyone who is traveling solo or on business.

“High Quality Hampton Inn - new carpet” I got a chuckle when researching hotels in the Jacksonville Area on Trip Advisor - there is not one REAL hotel (eg. Marriott, Hyatt, Westin, Hilton, local boutique hotel, etc) in the entire top 20! So - compared to what is available in the area this Hampton Inn should be rated a 5 star hotel - but for those who travel a lot it is what it is: a really high quality Hampton Inn experience. The staff is excellent, the rooms are clean and spacious (mine had brand new lovely carpet), the lobby area is clean and modern, the breakfast is basic and nutritious. The hotel is located close to corporate campuses and shopping areas. I've stayed here twice so far and will stay again when in the area - it really is the best around - hard to believe!

“Expected better” I really wanted this to be a great hotel. I've stayed at the Westin in Boston before and had a very nice stay. This was just ok. We stayed for two nights on the 15th floor. Pros Close to Pike Place, Chihuly, Space Needle, EMP Great restaurants in walking distance. $5 coupon to be used in restaurant for not having linens changed- great incentive!! The beds were very, very comfy! The pool and gym were both good sizes. Cons Parking costs= daylight robbery Lines at check in Discourteous desk staff- I seemed to be inconviencing them when I passed through the lobby and asked if I could have some coffee sent to my room. I was told that next time I should call Service Express so it could be put in the system. Room not serviced- Although we didn't need our sheets/towels to be changed after just one night we assumed that coffee would be replaced, the toilet roll would have been replaced etc. I expected better from this hotel.

“Great for Business” I am a frequent user of this hotel in my travels to El Paso. Its localization is extremely convenient as it is in the route to the border to Mexico. The rooms are clean and comfortable and my only concern is regarding the air conditioning that is too loud and not efficient. The breakfast in the morning is very good and their "travel bags" are excellent when you are in a hurry.

“Decent Family Hotel... but 'Resort'?” I stayed at this hotel last night, mid-week in June for 1 night on business. All staff members were very friendly and helpful. Free easy access parking and my internet access was free, it said the first 24 hours only but I am not positive... there may be a charge for access after the initial 24 hours. Grounds were nice but not much like the resorts I have been to, just a nice hotel with nice grounds. Room was clean. It appeared that the bathroom was pretty new or has held up very well. The bedspread was a bit tired but the select number bed was great. I was really sick when I arrived and went straight to bed at 130pm. The curtains blocked the sun, the a/c was cold and it was virtually silent. I went to my event around 6pm and returned to the room at 10pm. I noticed it was a bit noisier but nothing bad. Ask for the 5th floor if you are a business traveler! I would not want all the kids above me, that's for sure. LOADS of children at this hotel. Logical, it is just down the street from Sea World. They are really cute, all excited to see Shamu. I did not find them annoying at all. B'fast buffet was pretty normal fare. Nothing great but it was fast, and that's what I was looking for... the made to order omlette station was good and again, the staff exceptional. I would stay here again. It was a nice hotel with a nice atmosphere. The beds were good and the bathroom clean ~ that's enough for me!

“Gorgeous and Charming” My wife and I loved our 3-night stay at the Royal Palms in April. The property is just gorgeous, with beautiful flowers and landscaping, and interesting architectural details around every corner.We stayed in a casita near the back of the resort---very cozy and romantic. We had breakfast and dinner at T. Cook's---both great. In addition to outstanding food, T. Cook's has a lively lounge for cocktail hour. We spent a significant amount of time at the small but lovely pool. My wife really enjoyed the small but very nice spa. Service was outstanding all around. They happily gave us a very early check-in at the Front Desk. Although we had a few dinner reservations at other restaurants in Phoenix, we really never wanted to leave the property. It just felt like a perfect oasis, and left us feeling very relaxed. Definitely out favorite hotel where we have stayed in the Phoenix area---its top Tripadvisor rating is well deserved.

“Great for families with kids.” Right on the river, great for kids. Each of our kids received an adventure backpack that had toys, games and a plastic canteen that came in quite handy at Seaworld. Toys were great for down time in the room. Valet parking is very expensive, but private parking lots are available nearby. Bar and restaurant are high end with prices to match. Fantastic pool, fantastic location. We would stay there again.

“NINE ZERO - very positive experience!” I have been a huge KIMPTON fan for years! Stay at KIMPTONS whenever I can and get very annoyed when my business travel location precludes a KIMPTON reservation. I just gifted my son and his fiancé one night for a special occasion at NINE ZERO and what a positive experience!!! Thomas Burke, was so very responsive and made sure all the details were so very special - they had a wonderful time. I just want to thank you and all the great staff at NINE ZERO. Just when I think a KIMPTON experience could not get any better, I am always amazed that it ALWAYS gets a notch higher! Thank you KIMPTON!

“An Excellent Starwood Property” I travel a lot and try to stay in Starwood properties like the Westin. On average they meet expectations and often exceed them - such was the case during our recent stay in Memphis. The staff were knowledgable and friendly and made a point of remembering you as a guest. The location for the average tourists like us was perfect. The guitar program was very cool. The room was perfect and how can you not love their beds and linens. Usher was staying the hotel while we were there, but somehow neglected to invite us up for a drink! The internet charge is amongst the lowest I has seen in any major chain. Seven dollars a night is reasonable. While such basic services such as that should be free,that is not often the case. The price was considerably lower than at the Madison where we spent the second half of our stay and far better value for money (and even without the economic assessment is a far better place to stay as my Madison post explains). In both cases we booked directly with the hotel (no priceline or other internet engine).

“very nice hotel, if attending the Mccormick center” This hotel is very nice, very clean, the staff goes above and beyond to be accommodating. They are extremely friendly. If you are working at or attending anything at the McCormick center, this hotel is perfect. If you want to see Chicago, this isn't the best hotel. It is about a $8 cab ride to the loop and a $12 cab ride to Michigan street. There is little to nothing around the hotel, and overall not the nicest neighborhood in the evening. The hotel itself though is very nice, very clean, and very large. The rooms are clean and comfortable. and again, if attending the Mccormick center this hotel is perfect. The $33 self parking fee seems very excessive for being in the outskirts of town. Space is not at a premium here and this just seems very very expensive in my opinion.

“Only worth it if the sleeping room rate is severly discounted” Paid $169 p/night -- booked online through travel wholesaler (Expedia). It's an old hotel so some latitude needs to be extended in certain areas. We specifically asked for a room away from the elevator and we were placed RIGHT NEXT to the elevator in what was little more than a converted closet. Still, it is hardly the value I was seeking. Small cramped room, miniature bathroom but I nice big closet. Good thing as there was nowhere to put any clothes; too bad that I had to turn on all the lights in the bathroom and the near the bed to see anything inside the closet. the hotel has had an upgrade to the HVAC system but hasn't bothered to remove the air conditioner from the window. The hotel rooftop also opens itself up for Wednesday night "clubs" so getting to your sleeping room is like accessing the Pentagon. The queue line is supposed to make the hotel guests feel like they are prioritized but it just makes it all the more ordinary. One more inconvenience in a city where choices are plentiful and the desire to ever return to the Sir Francis Drake becomes non-existent. Too bad that they cannot capitalize on their history in a manner that would make a guest want to return.

“Excellent choice for auto show.” Stayed one night for auto show, very convenient location. Room was very clean and nice, used people mover to go to Cobo center. Front desk staff very friendly and helpful. Many plaeces around to get a nice dinner. Will come back again. Stayed January 2012

“Stayed with the family. Can't wait to come back.” I stayed here in a room with 2 double beds. The room was clean, comfortable, a decent size for manhattan, good amenities, and good size bathroom. The hotel was furnished nicely and has an amazing location. It's pricey but so is every other nice hotel with this proximity to time square and other attractions. There are theatres on the same street, a subway station entrance on the corner, stores, restaurants, and nightlife all within a few steps (literally) of the front door to the hotel. I'd definitely stay here again. A couple of things to note. I drove here and when I pulled up there was only one staff member outside and he was handling the cabs so there was no help with our bags. I left my wife with 3 kids and the bags. I asked the staff member where the hotel parking was since it's half the price of the valet ($27/day vs. $55 with valet) and he said just park at any lot. However before I arrived I asked the hotel if they had parking and they said they had a lot with an agreement for a discounted rate. The staff member was of no use so I called the front desk from my cell and they gave me directions. I found it no problem. Too bad the doorman was too lazy or incompetent to provide decent instructions. When we left we just walked a block to the parking lot with our bags down the street since it was less of a hassle than going to get the car and trying to find one of the limited spots in front of the hotel. I'd go back for the location alone. I also go free wifi, not sure, but when I checked in they told me it was free. I had to accept the charges but I never got charged. I am a gold preferred guest so that might be why but it was a bonus.

“SoHo Style, SoHo Price” You know you're in SoHo when you pull up to a hotel that's discreetly marked and you are greeted by a handsome young man dressed in business casual, all black attire...across the street from a bodega. The SoHo Grand is decorated with the urban chic-meets converted industrial loft style that New Yorkers have been overpaying for since the 80's. The room looked great but had a few notable drawbacks: the bed was hard, the water pressure in the shower also. I also noticed the sink dripping and found the TV far more complicated than a TV in a hotel room should be. To the hotel's credit, I did not report these problems--the visit was short and in true NY style there just wasn't time. Pleasant surprises: each floor has a common area with ice machine, magazines and a FilterFresh coffee maker. Smart alternative to in-room coffee. And the doormen are friendly and helpful in a way one would expect from a luxury hotel. And if you want to shop SoHo, you will not find a better location.

“Decent hotel but not great” This place was a mad house when I stayed this summer on business, but I guess that is to be expected in New York. The room was nice and clean. The biggest issue I had was with room service at breakfast. They did not enter the order, when I called to inquire it was obvious that was the case. The breakfast arrived so late I didn't even have to time to finish it before my business meeting. I brought this up at checkout and after multiple phone calls to the restaurant they did give me a small discount, I would expected more than that given the lack of service and how it took an hour and a half to get the food. I probably wouldn't go back to this specific hotel.

“Fantastic Stay....wish I could have stayed longer” we only had one night in Chicago, and regret not being able to stay longer because the hotel was awesome. The valet guys were extremely helpful and were right there when we pulled up. the cost is $46, but you are in the city. I had gotten an email a few months back before their opening and was able to get the room for $89! What a deal for this hotel, it was definitely worth a lot more. Upon check in, we also received a "raid the minibar" coupon for two items up o $10. It was beautifully decorated with flat screen tv. We did not get to enjoy the wine reception at night, but did go down for coffee and tea the next morning in the beautifully decorated lounge area. There was a nice pool on the top floor and also a rooftop bar which was very nice. We did not eat at the restaurant Sable, but it looked very nice. We had dinner across the street at Rock Bottom Brewery and I would highly recommend it. The red line was right next to the hotel and we were at the White Sox game in 15 minutes. There were shops and restaurants in walking distance.

“Luxury hotel, great meeting place” This is a top notch hotel located on the campus of the university of Texas. Texas Longhorn theming is everywhere, so if that nauseates you -- consider yourself warned. The meetings are nicely appointed with higher end finishes, and reasonably quiet. I didn't hear any room to room noise despite the place being sold out. My room faced the capitol along MLK blvd, so there was a little road noise, but it wasn't too bad, and the view of the capitol more than atoned for the mild noise in my mind. It's a bit pricey, but it's a great location in Austin, and that typically is something you have to pay a little more to get. The conference facilities are very nice, which is the real purpose of this hotel. Food was above average, but nothing to write home about. My one complaint is that the floors in the conference level are labeled by letters according to purpose (LL for lower lobby, M1, M2, for meetings and mezzanine, etc., none of which are very intuitive at face value.) Every time I got on an elevator people were perplexed and did not know what button to push. It would be much better to simply number the floors and put small labels on the elevator panel to remind people where the lobby, mezzanine, parking, or meeting rooms are located. That's probably not that big a deal, but given the consistency of the problem, it's a fairly conspicuous oversight for a conference center.

“Dated but very comfortable” I believe I recevied the rate for this hotel from Hotwire due to the massive construction project currently being done on I-76, it took me quite a while at 3:00pm on a Saturday to get to the exit. Arriving to the hotel it does not stand out and there are not automatic doors from the parking garage, $33 per night to park, to the lobby. That said, once to the desk a very quick check in and a fast elevator to my floor. Once inside the room the room looked old but the flat screen TV looked good and the bed was a standard Crowne Plaza comfortable bed. At 1am I ventured down to the lobby and noticed a very good time being had in the bar, this seems to be a pretty popular place with kareoke and a lot of laughs late at night. The room had good water pressure but the sink was outside the bath area, I never like that. Check out was as simple as check in, all in all an excellent stay at the Crowne Plaza on Market Street.
“Very Nice Hotel” Great locaion, and everything was very nice at this hotel. Great View from the pool area.

“Too busy for renos Westin?” If you are visiting Houston to shop the Galleria - you can't beat this Westin for location and convenience. Be forewarned: This is a popular hotel and nearly always fully booked and as a result, it appears that Westin hasn't been able to implement a regular refurbishment program. The rooms are tastefully decorated - but are beginning to show considerable signs of wear. The Heavenly bed was just 'OK' - not very plush / no featherbed and limp pillows. The dual head shower head leaked terribly. Weak water pressure and the toilet did not flush completely (took two - three flushes). Thankfully, Westin has not sealed the patio doors leading to the small balconies. I hope that when the time finally comes to renovate the guest rooms that they don't seal the doors shut like other hotels have done.

“Avoid the "taxi" service” I stayed at the Mela for one night - Saturday, March 27th. The hotel is fine and even though I've never stayed here, the rooms seem to have been updated recently. Current stylish furnishings in a decent sized room for Midtown NY standards. The bed was great. One big complaint... upon check-out the bellman asked if I needed a taxi and I said yes. He told me he had "taxis" standing by outside. I saw a black town car pulling up and asked the front desk if these cars cost the same as taxis and was told they do. When I asked outside what the fare was I was told $40 flat. When I scoffed the bellman offered me the car for $35 and said that the average fare from Midtown to LaGuardia is $40. This is completely false!!! I take cabs from midtown all the time and they NEVER cost more than $30 WITH the toll and the hotel staff knows this. I hate that they take advantage of unknowing tourists with this scam. Don't take their town car service.

“Funky, Modern, Fun Hotel” I stayed here for a bachelorette party and it was great. The rooms are big enough to hang out in - plus I love the bench seat that was in the room. They have Kiehl's products (reason why we chose the hotel). The location is awesome as it's only a block away from the Magnificent Mile and while we were there - a famous R&B singer was also staying there. If it's good enough for a celebrity... :) The el stop is about 2-3 blocks away - it's not a bad walk (Red Line - Grand stop)

“Great for visiting Suffolk Law School” I stayed at Nine Zero for a workshop in June at Suffolk Law School. You cannot beat the location if you want to be near Suffolk Law; it is a short two blocks walk down Tremont Street. The hotel was very nice for the conference rate; I don't know if I would pay some of the higher room rates described in other reviews given the other hotel options in the area. It seemed like a low-key W Hotel, but probably not the "happening" and "hipster" vibe it. The lobby and reception area is very small. And although they advertise a "wine hour" I did not see many people gathered for it. Overall, I think it is a great choice if you need to be around Suffolk but you will want to step out on the town for any type of socializing.

“Top Lage - schlechter Service” Ich war voriges Jahr für 10 Tage im Hotel The Roosevelt in New York untergebracht. Gebucht habe ich direkt auf der Hotel Homepage, da ich über Twitter einen Code ergatterte, der einem einen sehr guten Preis bescherte. Wir bezahlten etwa 120 Dolar pro Nacht für ein King Luxury Room, die zweithöchste Zimmerkategorie. Das Hotel liegt direkt an der Madison Avenue - also in bester Lage direkt neben der Grand Central Station. Der erste Eindruck des Hotels war atemberaubend, die Hotellobby versprüht einen ganz besonderen Charme und ist sehr gepflegt. Der Check-In war eine Katastrophe: unfreundliches Personal liess uns lange warten. Unsere Zimmerkategorie war nicht verfügbar, so frachtete man uns in ein ,,billiges" Zimmer mit der Option, einen Tag später zu wechseln. Einen Gutschein für's Frühstück o.ä. bekamen wir auf Nachfrage nicht. Man meinte nur, wir hätten keinen Anspruch auf unsere Zimmerkategorie, da wir einen Spezialpreis bezahlen würden. So etwas ist mir noch nie passiert! Naja, das Zimmer für die erste Nacht war eine Katastrophe - also runter zum Front Desk und etwas energischer nach einem Zimmer unserer Kategroie gefragt und nach dem Manager verlangt. Siehe da, es hat gewirkt. Wir bekamen unser Zimmer, das wirklich sehr, sehr Groß war (ca. 20 qm). Auch das Bad war Riesengroß. Das Zimmer war sehr sauber und gepflegt. Alle Annehmlichkeiten vorhanden. Alles, ausser einen kostenfreien Internetzugang. Den lässt sich das Roosevelt fürstlich entlohnen. Schade eigentlich, da dies in jedem Durchschnittsmotel on the Road zum Standard gehört. Das Zimmer entschädigte für den Trouble am Check-In. Am ersten Morgen gingen wir zum Frühstücken im Cafe in der Lobby. Dort wird Starbuck's Kaffee gebrüht und man kann Kleinigkeiten zum Frühstück kaufen, wie Bagels, Sandwiches usw. Die Tage danach gingen wir dann immer in die Zahlreichen Cafes in der Umgebung. Im Roosevelt sind auch noch ein paar Restaurants, Bars und Geschäfte untergebracht. Haben wir aber alles nicht genutzt. Auf dem Dach ist eine Rooftop Bar mit toller Aussicht auf die Stadt. Alles in allem verbrachten wir schöne Tage in New York und im Roosevelt, obwohl der Service für so ein Hotel zu wünschen übrig liess.

“Wonderful Omni!” We stayed at Omni Shoreham at the beginning of February and we were more than pleased. Our room overlooked the garden and had a nice balcony. We found it to be very clean and the staff very friendly and accommodating. Although it is not in the centre of Washington the Metro is literally no more than a 2 minute walk away and gets you to the centre in no time at all. We ate at Open City which is just across the street and constantly had people queing to get in - well worth the wait!

“Compact rooms but location, location, location” This is really an ideal hotel location, right in the middle of Michigan Avenue. Totally convenient to everything you would want to do downtown! I found that the rooms are quite a bit smaller than comparable hotels in the area. You definitely wouldn't be able to do yoga in the room :) The bathroom in particular is incredibly small. That said, the rooms are very well appointed, beds are comfortable, flat screen TV's, etc. Oh, and yes, there IS a Starbucks in the lobby level! That was a huge plus :) Biggest issue for my stay was mobile connectivity. Unless you choose their daily internet access (and why would you at $17.95 a day!), getting to the internet through your mobile phone or tablet is really slow. They must have a double firewall for those who don't pay :) Also be prepared for spendy valet parking - $57/day! That's about $5/day higher than other hotels in the area. It does allow for in & out privileges however.

“Typical HGI” I stayed here in November 2011 and had a decent experience; it wasn't the best Hilton Garden Inn I've stayed in, but it was satisfactory. The decor is on the older/dowdy side, but my room was clean. Generally, service was satisfactory; it was a bit slow in the restaurant, but very nice, and my food was good. The business center was fully equipped. One major complaint: the fitness center. Its equipment was terrible and needs to be updated. The fitness center was below the standard I expect from the chain. Location is right by the exit to the airport; there's not tons around it, but you can't ask for anything closer to the airport.

“One of the nicer Courtyards” Very friendly and helpful staff. Parking has high, but this is Chicago and it was less than many places. You just don't get free parking in big cities. Good internet that was free. Room was comfortable and clean. Very large and made the stay very nice. Restaurant was not the best. The food was good, but the selection was limited at best. Starbucks there offered another choice.

“lovely hotel with excellent staff” i stayed here a few nights on business. i really enjoyed the "old-world" charm of this place. Some of the older hotels tend to have that old architecture, fixtures, wallpaper, etc and it shows. This hotel did not have that. It is now a hilton owned hotel, my understanding for several years now... It has been cared for in a very nice fashion, where the older touches are in very good shape - the elevators with a small bench and light fixtures with little shades. The hotel uses high quality toiletries, and the room was clean and reasonable sized, especially for an older hotel - built in 1920's i believe... The staff was awesome here - informative, welcoming, etc etc. The bell captain was very welcoming, the desk staff was welcoming and informative about the hotel history, all in all very nice touches... The gold coast room you should take a peek there floor to ceiling windows and magnificent views to boot. Really enjoyed my stay away from home. I was able to get a room at a good rate for this week, and wish i could afford to stay here more frequently!

“Quiet and convient area.” We enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Manhattan East. Our room had a king-sized bed. The room was small, but this is to be expected in Manhattan unless you are paying big prices. However, the room was big enough and we weren't bumping into each other or anything like that. Our room also had a chair, small table, flat screen TV and small business desk. The bathroom looked like it was just recently redone. There was a coffeemaker, but unfortunately no fridge for storing beverages. My only complaint is that there were no towels or washcloths in the room when we arrived, but we did check-in quite early so maybe the room wasn't 100% ready yet? The rest of the hotel is quite nice. It had a modern/retro feel to it. Everything was clean and in good working order as far as I could tell. The elevators are quite small, but it wasn't a problem. I'm a Hilton Silver member, so we had a free continental breakfast and it was quite good and filling. All the staff that we came in contact with were very helpful and pleasant. The hotel has valet parking for $51.00 a day. We decided to park in one of the lots a few blocks away and we saved some cash that way. I really liked the location of the hotel. I have stayed in Times Square before and it was quite noisy and crowded. It was nice to be within walking distance (about a 20-25 minute walk to Times Square), but in a more quiet area. I only heard one siren at night that woke me up and I'm a light sleeper. I found the hotel to be very quiet. I only heard neighbors when they closed their door and even then it wasn't that bad. The hotel is a short walk to Grand Central Station and a few blocks from the UN. We walked all over the area and felt safe at all times. I'd stay here again if we were in the area!

“great rooms, great price” A fellow friend and I stayed here booking a room with 2 double beds. The room was fantastic, kept very clean by housekeeping and the free breakfast was ample, the only downside to a fantastic stay was the front desk whom we likened to Fawlty Towers. It seemed that no one had a clue. We did however only find this amusing and added to the charm. Our rooms were thoroughly modern, very comfortable beds and yes as in other reviews the breakfast room is small but they are in the process of updating and they provide a great service and at no time did we see it as an inconvenience. Location was excellent and so handy to everything.

“Never Again” I've stayed at this property several times. Unfortunately, my most recent stays prompted me to write this review. The hotel is not very clean and the front desk staff are often surly. While I realize this is a Starwood Category 3 hotel, it operates as if it were a Category 1 hotel. If you need to sleep, I suggest you book another hotel. The air conditioner is so loud when it cycles on and off that it will wake you up throughout the night. The floors in the room often appear very dirty. On my most recent stay, the toilet had human waste in it (someone forgot to flush). The hallways are also dirty and there are room signs just left on the floor of the hallways. While some of the front desk staff can be pleasant, most act as if you are interrupting their day. The front desk is consistently unmanned when I go to check out in the morning. If there is a positive, the shuttle bus drivers are very pleasant. Also, the fitness center has nice treadmills with tvs built into the machines. Overall, the fitness center is nice, albeit small. Stay away. I know I will.

“Perfect!” This was our second time at this hotel at the beginning of February for two nights. We loved it the first time and when we booked to go back to new York we didn't even think twice of another hotel. Upon arrival were given a room on the 42nd floor overlooking ground zero with fantastic views over the river and skyline of new york. Rooms were very comfortable, not at all small compared to alot of new york hotels, with a very large comfortable bed and lots of bathroom toiletries. Check out was at 12 but unfortunately my husband was ill so after letting the conceirge know, they very kindly said we could stay in the hotel at no further cost until he was well enough to leave which was much appreciated. Overall fantastic hotel, great views and very accomodating staff!

“Great...but not sure all the packages are worth bothering with” Mostly great with a few islands of relatively minor problems. First the good: Outside of the hotel and lobby were decorated like a winter wonderland, as befitted the season. The restaurant service was absolutely flawless ( servers who don't write orders because they are expected to remember them, remember clients clearly from one day to the other, and go above and beyond consistently). Rooms are comfortable: yes the beds are great! The gym is well equipped. Second the slightly off putting: mmmhh...we got the "I love chocolate package" which advertized: bfast every day, dinner once, snack once and...a gift. And we have an A-Club favorite guest membership, which also advertized " a gift". So, no gift...either for the chocolate package or the favorite guest membership. Upon enquiry, "the snack was the gift". Not at all what the package suggested. That said, bfast was sublime and the chocolate dinner outstanding as well. Some problems at checkout though: we got charged for all dining despite having booked the package and it took quite a while for a polite but seemingly less than informed front desk staff to correct the problem. Would absolutely go back, but probably not on a special package.

“Better than I expected” Stayed for one night. Staff was extremely friendly both on the phone and in person. Hotel was clean and parking was good. There is a covered garage in the back. Wife and I had the breakfast buffet and here's the only place where from a people perspective there could have been improvement. Seemed like they didn't have enough staff and we repeatedly had to ask for things that with proper staffing, would have been out. My wife didn't like the bed also. It was her Goldilocks moment. The beds are very soft. She felt like she was sleeping in quicksand. With that said, for one night, we would stay again.

“Great location. Busy lobby but comfortable stay.” Stayed over busy summer weekend. Lobby was always hectic with both guests of hotel and just passersby. Location is popular for those coming to/from Riverwalk, so Lobby can become a madhouse at times. But up in the room and elsewhere has a nice quiet feel. Rooftop pool was packed with kids and it is nothing special...a bit like an oversized hottub. But with the Riverwalk out the back door and the Alamo out the front, this hotel makes everything convenient and saves a lot of time and hassle. Didnt try any of the hotel restaurants/bars, because you have a plethora of dining options right outside along the Riverwalk. Good place for families, probably not best for business or romance travelers.

“Had a great time. Great Location.” I stayed here 2 nights over a weekend for business. It was a great location close to everything downtown. Their rates were more reasonable then some other hotels. I had some minor problems with the internet access but was able to get what I needed in the business center. The staff was helpful with downtown information. I also got a good pizza recommendation to go to Uno down the block.

“Close to LAX But Too Many Issues for a Return” Drive up to valet parking and got out of car. Waited as valet finished his ten-minute chat with a lady in a nearby car. Probably not a guest, as he kissed her when she left. Did not like waiting. Front desk clerk seemed annoyed that I was there. Apologized to her for my interruption. Did not know hotel was undergoing renovation (web site only mentioned lobby). Food and beverage service now offered in hotel conference room. Average room with view of construction site next door. Probably would not stay here again.

“Would definitely stay again” I had a great stay at the Comfort Inn. First of all, while the neighbourhood may not seem like the greatest, I never felt uncomfortable or like I wasn't safe. Which isn't to say that I was necessarily right about that, but I had no qualms about walking around at any time. The inn is right next to the N. Vermont/Beverly metro station which was so convenient. It took you to Universal Studios in about ten minutes and to Hollywood and Vine in less time than that. Plus it could connect to downtown very quickly. There was also a bus on that corner that went very near The Grove and further towards Beverly Hills. If you're driving, you're a block away from the Hollywood freeway. The staff was very helpful. The free breakfast provided more than made up for not having a restaurant. Also, and this was maybe just our luck, all the other guests that were there at the same time as us were also friendly and would give us tips on where to go. The only downside I could see was that if your room was facing N. Vermont, it would probably be a little noisy. As ours didn't, we had peace and quiet. Also, of the three Pepsi machines, only one was working at the time, but it was fine because the Circle K across the street provided all of our snacking needs. All-in-all it was a great stay, especially for the low, low price, and I will totally return next time I'm in L.A.

“spacious room and convenient location” stayed here 3 days for my son's graduation at johns hopkins university. very reasonable price. i was surprised with how spacious the room was. we booked a double bed and stayed at 2505. there was kitchenette with mini fridge, microwave, coffee maker (didn't use it), plates and silver wares and some extra tall glasses for wines, etc. there's also 2 free bottled water everyday which is a nice touch. i slept like a baby, i love their mattress(on a firmer side,not soft/hard) and pillows(6 in each bed,luv it!) the safe was locked when we got in the room, called front desk and less than 5minutes the guy came to open it. that's service! we ordered room service one night, delicious (crab cakes, strip steaks, fries,etc) and price is reasonable as well. we use their valet parking through out our stay for $25/24hrs(unlimited in and out). check in was a little slow, but, check out was a breeze. i can stay here again.

“Great Service. Hotel bit tired but absolutely fine.” I found the hotel staff exceptionally helpful. I think it was the restaurant manager who even opened up the sports bar out of hours so that I could watch an English soccer game. Nice little pool and jacuzzi. Very convenient for airport and 15 minute drive to downtown San Antonio.

“The OK and the Not So OK” This property is more like a 2 3/4 star but that isn't an option. First the good. Even though this is definately an older property, the room wasn't bad. It's large enough and the bed is comfortable. It's got a CRT TV but it is probably a 25 inch, maybe a 27. It's large enough and there are plenty of channels. Check in was fine. The lady who checked us in was very nice. There is an indoor pool and an indoor hot tub by the pool. 20 oz sodas are available from machines for $1.50 I believe. It may have been $1.25 but I think it was $1.50. I've seen smaller sodas sold for much more at hotels. The air conditioning unit in the room wasn't real quiet but it wasn't real loud either. I'm glad it wasn't any louder but it was okay. Now for the not so good. In the bathroom, I could easier hear people in the next room. I couldn't hear them when I was in the living area, only the bathroom. There is no fan in the bathroom so after a shower, the mirror of course is fogged up for awhile.
