The elevators aren't the fastest in the world and thankfully there weren't too many people staying there so we never had to wait. I could see where it could become very backed up if there were numerous people staying there. We stayed on a weekend and the free breakfast is not served on weekends but for $9.95, you can have breakfast in the restaurant. Room service ends at 11:00. We ordered room service one night and the lady demanded payment immediately which was not a big deal. However, she didn't have change so I gave her $30.00 and she stated she would leave the change at the front desk. The next morning, I went to the front desk and she had kept $5.00 for herself. She didn't leave any change at the front desk nor did she even turn the ticket in to the front desk. It's as if I never ordered room service. Thankfully, the front desk staff did give me my change but if this employee will attempt to steal funds from customers, it makes me wonder what else she would attempt? The food was okay, nothing special. It's convienent, that is the best part of the restaurant located here. All in all, this hotel is okay. Above average in some areas and below average in some areas. When Comfort Inns and Holiday Inn Express offers free breakfast on weekends and this place can't, that is below average. Room service staff trying to steal money from customers, that is unacceptable. If you are looking for a professional, full service hotel, you can do better than this. If you are looking for something a little nicer than an economy hotel, this fits the bill.

“A nice place to stay.” When I got in after 10PM (after Amtrak was even later than usual), the front desk, which I had warned via cell phone in advance, told me that since the remaining rooms in the price range I had reserved for faced the street, they would give a larger room on the 9th (top) floor instead. The staff seemed this eager to please throughout my 4-day stay, quick with directions and advice. The room itself was a decent size with a walk-in closet, in-room safe, and lots of sunlight. I only used the restaurant once for breakfast, which was pretty good if pricey. (At that, it wasn't any worse than the famous places around Union Square.) It is a bit of a trek to Union Square, and you'll need transit to get almost anywhere else, but bus stops are right nearby and the Muni will eventually get you where you want. There's also a good Internet cafe, Quetzal, about two blocks away. One caveat: you really don't want to venture south past Geary St., two streets down, even in the daytime. You'll run into panhandlers anyway, but that happens in lots of places in San Francisco.

“Location, location, location” The Embassy Suites at 600 State Street in Chicago is in the heart of where you want to go downtown. It's a short walk to theatres, Lake Michigan, the riverwalk, Chicago Tribune Bldg, Magnificant Mile and Nordstrom. the staff is fabulous; everyone was friendly; , from the front doormen, to the desk staff and the conceirge. The rooms were large and the beds were great. They plan a redecorating of rooms which will make this an even nicer hotel.

“Definite Upgrade Over the Standard ESA” I was awarded this hotel via Hotwire.com. On paper, I saw that I was getting 2.5 star with a pool and breakfast, so I was stunned that it was an Extended Stay. No matter, the hotel was fine. The hotel was in a great location, situated in a very popular shopping district. The restaurants were mostly of the cookie cutter type (Carraba's, Smokey Bones, Chili's, etc), but I know that's OK with most people. The lobby was very nice, with a business center and breakfast area off to the sides. The breakfast area offered excellent complementary coffees 24/7. The rooms were small, but well laid out. The kitchenette contained newer appliances. With regards to the television area, the easy chair had a pull out bed for one, situated in front of a smallish TV. The bed itself was small for two, but that is typical for ESA's. My wife and I used the pool. My wife has a background knowledge of pools, and she noticed that there was enough algae on the pool stairs to leave footprints. That bothered her a little. Overall, it was a solid, if forgettable stay.

“Great hotel in an excellent location” I booked at the last minute through Priceline and paid $75 per night (versus their standard rate of $200 per night). The hotel is about 5 minutes walk from Union Square and Market Street and also about the same distance from the Montgomery Street BART station. It was about ten minutes to the Ferry building/Embarcadero and also 10-15 minutes through Chinatown to North Beach and the Italian restaurants. Having booked on Priceline for such a low amount I wasn't expectlng much, but was given an excellent room on the 6th floor. I didn't have any problem with street noise as mentioned in earlier posts. The room was small, with a queen bed and not a lot of room around, but it was more than enough for me. The bathroom was equally cozy, with just a shower although it was well-kept and clean, with Aveda shampoo and lotions too. The sink was in the bathroom; other posts suggest that in some rooms the sink is outside of the bathroom. The room was well-furnished and clean although I think if they replaced the large cathode ray television with an LCD screen it could then be wall-mounted and the hotel could do away with the large television-and-minibar-containing cupboard, which dominates the small room. Other highlights include a zebra-striped bathrobe (the black stripes on mine were purple, presumably as a result of bleaching while washing), an iPod docking station, reliable WiFi, clean, comfortable white bedding and also the wine/beer hour from 5-6pm. This was really nice to take a couple of beers up to the room after spending the day walking around San Francisco. I had breakfast at the adjacent Cafe de la Presse which attempts to recreate the ambiance and service of a Parisian cafe, with prices to match. I think the rack rate charged is too much for this hotel, but if I were to be assigned it again through Priceline or Hotwire then I'd be more than happy.

“Terrible hotel, only thing decent is the Dome Bar...” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Camino Real over the Thanksgiving weekend. I grew up in the area and so I figured I would pick this place having been there for nice formal events. Well, I guess I'm thinking back 10 years too long because this place has gone down hill. That probably happened when the Westin company left... The rooms are very run down..furniture is beaten up...the beds are uncomfortable, the bathroom, also not great...and the place just felt filthy. You're better off staying at a nice hotel near the airport..or stay in a budget hotel in the area that is newer and cleaner. This place needs a BIG makeover. Oh..and don't even think about using the pool...it's really small and you won't want to sit at it..trust me. The Dome Bar is there..it's nice but not worth it.

“Its ok!” + Location breakfast at only 4 dollars(big selection) Big rooms with a lot of space - The crew: most of the crew was not so friendly The rooms feel a litte old. The rool was very hot and dry we stayed at 17 floor and the noise from the street was not so high. The hotel is ok if you find a reasanable price, otherwise you can find better.

“Awesome” Booked my parents at the Four Seasons for their 50th anniverary. The hotel staff was a 10 on a scale of 1 to 10. Arranaged for a driver with the hotel to take them to and from SFO perfect service. Used a tour company from the hotel, it was a 10. Everything about the place is a 10. My parents gave it a 10.

“Rich Uncles Estate” Booked online Marriott rewards member weekend rate for Superior Room w/queen. Saturday night check-in politely asked if any king beds were available, we received a 2 tier upgrade to Executive Room. Front desk even asked if it was ok that our room was near elevator, we didn’t mind since we were getting free upgrade (Thank you Marriott Gold). For base rate of $163, we got a the deal of the weekend. Room was over 300 sf, great bed with miniature reading lamps built into the headboard. Room also included a long bench a foot of the bed as well as a full sized sofa and coffee table. Bathroom was large, included 2 robes and nice Molton Brown amenities. Flatscreen was huge mounted on the wall. Hotel feels like your staying at your rich uncles huge estate. Bar was large with plenty of seating, it was empty (memorial day weekend) but barman was really nice, drinks were good and an order of warm mixed nuts addictive. There’s free coffee and tea 24 hrs in business center. Neighborhood is safe and tons of restaurants within 10 min walk, we tried LaFollia on 3rd Ave and 19th and really enjoyed it. I wouldn’t hesitate to tell anyone to stay here, we had great weekend.

“Outstanding choice!!!” We went to NYC for a long weekend, to enjoy a few Broadway shows. This hotel is 1 to 1.5 miles from the theater district (depending upon which theater) and is a reasonable walk. Note: A cab ride to the theater is only about $7 + tip, if you don't want to walk. The subway (E train) is right across the street and will get you very close to your theater, too. Pros: VERY large rooms by NYC standards. VERY clean rooms and bathrooms. Very friendly hotel employees. A quiet hotel. Much quieter than being near Times Square. We were on the 23rd floor. Very reasonable rates for NYC. We booked months ahead of time. $237/night. Free use of computers in their business center, which was never busy. Subway station is very close to the hotel. A good CVS/Walgreens type store is right next to the hotel. Cons: No large beautiful lobby, if that means anything to you. We couldn't care less about that. That's it!!! Note: This property is a typical 3-star Courtyard Marriott. If you're looking for the Four Seasons, this isn't it. We could not have been more happy with this hotel. Kudos to the management of this property!

“Your paying for a name” Fairmont Hotel San Francisco The hotel is a 4 star hotel that I got at the rate of $207.00. Rates went up to $695. Parking was $52.00 p/n & breakfast in the main café in the mhotel is $30 per person. No coffee in the room so you are forced to purchase in one of the cafes. There is a $!5.00 charge to use the fitness center. My partner used the sauna and was very disappointed in how dirty it was, old and had broken fixtures. He has planned on showering & getting ready down there after his steam but couldn’t bear it. No free wifi unless you are a President’s Club member (I am but forgot to tell them at check in). Show them your foursquare check in & free room upgrade if available. The room 259 has no view. Because of my rate, I got this terrible view. I tried to change it but it was going to be $30-$75. The hotel was almost sold out so, they couldn’t upgrade. The room has very large ceilings, a walk in closet, small counter space in bathroom but it’s nice. I wouldn’t come back here if I was just using the room. The hotel is gorgeous otherwise and very historical. Be sure to go on a Wednesday so you can go to the Tonga Room which has a pool in the middle of the restaurant. The hotel is in a great location, 3 blocks down from China Town. We ate a R&N Lounge which was very busy and had good food, especially their spareribs. It’s located 25 minutes from the SFO Airport and about 15 minutes from the Golden Gate Bridge. There are two Fairmont Hotels, the other is in Ghiradelli Square and is three times the rate.

“Disappointing stay” I stayed here for five nights and had high hopes after a great stay at the Hampton Inn in New York. However, there are several problems with this hotel, which could be seen as minor when taken individually, but which overall add up to the fact this hotel "could do so much better"! The positives are free coffee, free WiFi and a good location for exploring downtown/attending the convention centre. The negatives were: : Rude staff. With the exception of a couple of people on reception, I found the staff in general to be unhelpful, and many avoided eye contact. : My room had had a "touch up" paint job, with the marks clearly visible all over the walls. The hotel in general feels worn and needs a revamp. : It took ages for the water to heat up for the shower and there are only two tiny towels in the room. : There are no bathrobes and none available on request either. : There is no recycling anywhere in the hotel, which is a disgrace in this day and age. All the cutlery, dishes, plates and cups at breakfast are made from plastic or polystyrene, meaning the amount of waste going through this hotel every day must be enormous. : The breakfast is plentiful if you like cheap, processed food. There are some fruit options but not really enough healthy foods. : The air con in the gym is on far too low, making for a sweltering workout. When I asked if there was anyway of turning it up to cool, I simply got told "no, I don't know how to do that". And she wasn't interested in finding out either. Overall, there is not enough attention to detail at this Hampton Inn, which is a shame as I expected more from this brand.

“Very good overall but expensive” Spent one night at the Westin as a family in July 2008. We paid full price (> $400 / night) but were given a room on the top floor (45th) with an amazing city view. Pros: - great location, just close enough to Times Square but not right in the madness of it - friendly welcome at the reception (they even spoke some french with us which was a nice touch) - super view on Times Square (+ Empire State bldng) - windows that actually open - steps to the theaters - fast and efficient elevators Cons: -Boutiquish look and feel, a bit too cold and trendy for our taste - too business like - weird and inconvenient bathroom - weak air conditioning We would go back but only if given a lower special rate.

“初めてのNYC観光を無難におさえたい人むけ” 日本人の観光ツアー発着場所に指定され、飛鳥クルーズのカウンターも設置されたり、日本人ガイドもうろちょろしているので、初めての海外や初NYCで不安な人にはお勧めです。 ヒルトンらしく、NYCの中では部屋も広い方だし、アメニティも充実しています。 MOMAは目の前。地下鉄は歩いて1ブロック分、シェラトンの方が近いです。 近くで映画のプレミアが行われることもあり、スパイダーマンの撮影が行われていたときは、セットの瓦礫や紙が飛んできていました。 話題性、利便性、安全性でも無難にNYC観光を押さえたい人にはおすすめです。

“Great Place in a Revitalized Fort Worth” Having lived in the DFW area a few years back, I was really reluctant to stay in Fort Worth. But when I turned the corner and saw the area and the hotel, I was amazed. The Omni is a brand new hotel in a new part of Fort Worth that I haven't been to before. Once I got to the hotel, the bellhops were extremely friendly - they always opened the door for me when I came through. The front desk staff was helpful. There was a large crowd checking in when I got there, but the lobby was very specious and inviting. Off to the corner, I could see a Starbucks in the hotel that also had sidewalk seating. And there was also a restaurant with very cool and modern decor that was separated from the lobby with a fireplace. It looked like a very comfortable place. Walking to my room, I didn't feel like I was in a hotel. The hallways were decorated well with pictures lining the wall. I felt like I was in a high-end residence. (Which, apparently, there are condos to the other half of the hotel) Once in the room, the decor was pure Texan. The beds were VERY comfortable, and the bathroom was very spacious with plenty of towels. There was a hairdryer, ironing board, coffee maker, etc. Nothing out of the ordinary, but all the basic amenities were there. When I went to bed that night, I slept really well, just sinking into the bed and being surrounded by pillows. The view from the room was nice. It overlooked a garden on top of the lower roof and onward towards the Texas prairie. The pool was nice. There was a bar that wasn't opened yet, and outdoor restrooms. The pool is on top of the lower roof on the third floor, so you don't hear too much street traffic. The gym was really nice. There was a good assortment of cardio equipment and free weights. There was also a supply of bottled waters and towels. You have to pay for Wi-Fi and use of the business center on the third floor, but you can check in and print your boarding pass for a flight for free. One night, I spent some time in the wine bar not too far from the lobby, it was decent. Coming from New York, I was expecting the wine prices to be a bit cheaper, but it did seem expensive. Overall, my stay was enjoyable. The staff was friendly, the rooms were comfortable, and the location is great. The Omni is across the street from the Convention Center and the Water Gardens. Sundance Square is about a ten minute walk, and there are a lot of bars and restaurants in the area. I would definitely stay at this hotel again... and I recommend you stay here!

“Great for business travelers” I go to NYC on business every other month. I just need a quiet, safe, clean place. I travel by myself so I need to stay in a safe neighborhood. The Kitano is probably the quietest hotel in NYC. In other hotels you often hear sirens, etc all night. Here it was silent. The hotel lobby itself is quiet. The people that work there are soft spoken. The service was excellent, especially for NYC... no attitude at all. The room was modern and extremely clean. Bed extra comfortable. The downside....Pricey. If you are going for fun, I'd stay somewhere like the W but if you need clean and quiet, try the Kitano

“Nice hotel & GREAT staff.” I had stayed at the Madison a few years ago and remembering it as an upscale hotel went for it again for a 4 night business trip this past week.The lobby area is just beautiful. Be warned that the hotel is undergoing renovation in some rooms but that wasn't an issue at all for me during my stay. I was placed in one of the newly renovated rooms & it was quite nice. The bed was VERY comfortable and there was good space in the new vanity in the bathroom. The chair in the room was new in an elegant style & very comfortable as well. The shower was newly redone & very clean. The main reason to me that the Madison really stood out was the staff. ALL of them were very friendly & helpful. The doormen were always cheerful & the desk staff were great especially Kaouthan (sp) who checked me in. She even remembered me from my previous stay! I didn't have a car or eat there so i can't comment on the restaurants there or the parking situation. For someone on a business trip I highly recommend the Madison!

“Mostly positive” We stayed three nights in January 2009. The positives: good location, free parking, friendly staff, very easy beach access, rooms clean, big (30"+) flat screen tv, bathroom recently remodeled, free coffee, juice, and muffins in the lobby each morning. Now it's time to get nitpicky: room 28. Two light switches at front door, could not figure out what they controlled.They did nothing each time I flipped them in either direction. Electrical outlet under view window: dead. Light switch in large walk-in closet did not work. Floor lamp in closet worked if you unplugged the microwave or refrigerator in there. Coffee maker in closet, but never received coffee, filters or cups (so why bother putting a coffee maker in the room?) There were four items in the closet that needed electricity, but only two outlets. Bathroom newly remodeled and nicely tiled, but shower head was mounted at least 10 inches too low and room had a strong mildew smell that did not go away. The two beds in the room did not seem to be queen sized. More likely full size, so you will be very snug sharing the bed. So there are details that the management needs to work on, but even with all of the minor annoyances I would still stay here again. Good value for the price and location.

“Indifferente” Abbiamo soggiornato 3 notti all'hotel Mark Twain a luglio 2011. L'hotel non è niente di che; l'arredamento è abbastanza vecchiotto e le parti comuni sono tinteggiate di un color vinaccia che, complice anche l'abbondanza di moquette e velluto, rende l'ambiente molto buio. Pulizia della stanza discreta. L'ubicazione però è comoda perchè in downtown e da lì numerosi punti di interesse sono raggiungibili a piedi; la via in realtà è abbastanza sporca. Non c'è parcheggio (puoi solo sostare per il tempo del checkin) ma ti offrono un servizio di valet parking che, come normale ovunque tu vada negli states, costa parecchio ma almeno ti parcheggiano loro l'auto e ad ogni richiesta te la riportano nel giro di 10 minuti. Personale alla reception non scortese ma nemmeno particolarmente cordiale.

“Great room, front desk not up to usual Kimpton level” The room was great and just what I expected - clean and with a great view. The front desk provided less that usual Kimpton service. No one on the door, had to ask about valet parking, a seemingly disinterested desk person - poor social skills - not what I've come to expect at Kimpton.

“Nice hilton in good location; great view of Camden yards” Stay here just about every time for conventions. Room overlooking camden yards is awesome, particularly if they are playing! Typical clean and comfortable room. Restaurant is located in building across street. I dont like having to pay for internet on top of the expensive rates, when other Hilton family hotels (Hampton Inn) can provide it for free.

“Nice hotel, Great location, great service” Le Parker Meridien is a great hotel from several aspects: 1) Location - can't beat it for midtown. Convenient to everything. 2) Service - service was friendly and helpful. My key got demagnetized and the front desk immediately sent someone up to help me instead of me having to go back downstairs 3) Overall - the rooms were nice. I would even say a little larger than the typical NYC hotel room. Bath products were very nice as well. My only complaint is that the elevators were ridiculously slow. I think maybe only one elevator was running for the entire tower side of the building but this problem persisted for both days I was there. This just made you have to leave a little earlier than you would normally but overall not too big of a deal. I would definitely recommend Le Parker Meridien to anyone wanting to stay in midtown.

“Very accommodating staff!” We love Homewood Suites, have stayed at many of them, and will continue to do so. Our room was very comfortable regarding the bedding, temperature and living room furnishings--and it was VERY quiet. We brought a bottle of good wine to celebrate just being able to get away for an overnight--life is busy. As we packed, my husband asked me if we needed to bring a corkscrew and I told him no, because they always have those in the kitchen, as well as wine glasses. All HS we have stayed at have offered place settings for 4 in the kitchen, including wine glasses and a corkscrew. Hmmmm....not here. I suspect this hotel caters more to business people who take advantage of the light meal and wine/beer Monday-Thursday. Our kitchen didn't have 4 of anything, and the one cooking pot looked rather sad. I have to compliment the staff though---when I went to the desk to inquire about it, I was told someone would bring what we needed to our room---within 10 minutes, we had 2 wine glasses and a corkscrew. The breakfast area is very comfortable and has plenty of seating. The food was plentiful and good....the scrambled eggs were cooked but had cooled off.... but they have microwave so we took care of that. The coffee was GREAT!! Due to road construction in the area (no fault of the hotel--they probably hate it too), we did not want to venture too far for dinner. There is a wings place in front of the hotel...never been to a wings place but we LOVED it. It's not just wings.....so many choices of other foods and it was delicious and only a 2-min walk to the entrance.

“Great value, great location” Picked up this hotel for Saturday night on Priceline, and got it for $57/night + tax... not bad for the Saturday night after Thanksgiving. The hotel was fantastic... check in was great and we got two free cookies. The rooms were very nice. Plenty of street parking since they don't check the meters on Sunday. I'm not sure how much parking is otherwise. My only gripe was that they haven't upgraded their TV's to plasmas or LCD's, yet. Other than that, I was very pleased.

“Spacious rooms with window seats” Nice hotel in the middle of downtown Chicago with a lovely Art Deco style reception area. Rooms are quite large - if you can, get a river view room as high up as possible. If you do, there's a window seat that is quite large - it's basically a twin mattress in the window, and quite pleasant to look at the river and Chicago skyline. Very close to Michigan Ave, Millennium Park, etc. Free bikes to borrow, which is an added bonus. Only negative is that this section of Wabash means the wait for cabs can be long, so you need to walk a short distance to Wacker or State if you don't want to wait that long.

“Second review, if that's OK for the same hotel.” I stayed for the third time in two years at the Biltmore, and reviewed it in 2010. I am writing this additional review to respectfully disagree with some of the other reviewers. My friend and I enjoyed our stay at this hotel, and found our room spacious and comfortable. I did tell the hotel that some touch up paint was in order, the carpet was frayed around the edges of the room, and the old keyhole in the bathroom door looked shabby. OK, folks, there was not much shelving in the bathroom. Other than that, we thought our stay was just fine. While I would not give these rooms five stars without some upgrading, I fail to see why others are so picky. The employees were great and I love the " movie star " swimming pool in the basement. The prepaid rate was fairly reasonable and a big plus is that it is within walking distance of Walt Disney Concert Hall, where we went to hear the LA Philharmonic. I was discussing this topic with one of the bellmen, who sighed about the recent reviews and commented " Some people just don't like old hotels. " This one dates from 1923. Frankly, i like the place and will return. Case stated. Goodnight! ( P.S. - I seldom ever order room service, but we placed a food order late at night and it was promptly delivered. )

“Meets expectations for Homewood Suites” This is your typical suburban hotel. Free parking is easy with 2-3 entrances from various points in the parking lot. The breakfast was also free and had an adequate assortment of continental items including a make your own waffle bar. The suite was nice with a door that closes between the living room and bedroom. The kitchen refridgerator was a good size and the kitchen was well appointed. Location was good for us as we were there for a wedding on the NW side of town, location quality would differ per hotel guest. There were many, many restaurants within walking and short driving distance and a nice mall is literally across the parking lot. Also, the pool and hot tub were indoors which made them useful in early March even though it was cool outside.

“Good hotel oriented towards conventions” Staff was helpful. It's clean and comfortable. Not on the most busy part of the riverwalk but it's better than walking several blocks on street level. Good pool and hot tub. Parking is free with AAA card.

“Sassy” Loved the hotel- looks completely new, very clean, functional and the service is excellent; location great for shopping, but not close to downtown austin; pool-super small, but sexy lounge area; great for b-travel, short stays.

“Good location and staff” This is a very convenient location with a excellent restaurant and bar next door (Elephant Bar). This is now a Holiday Inn Express, no longer a Holiday Inn as of January 2012, even though it is still listed as a Holiday Inn. The property has been recently remodeled and the breakfast only restaurant, has been converted to a HIE eating area. This is a new conversion so not everything is to HIE standards, namely there were no cinnamon rolls or the new pancake machine. The staff is good, and they made the effort to bring me a new room key when mine didn’t work. I didn’t have to slog up to the desk or wait long for the bell man arrival. The rooms are average, and the TV has poor reception on some stations, but they have been upgraded to flat screens so it was acceptable but not ideal. The bathroom had two lotions and shampoo instead of conditioner, shampoo, and lotion. I didn’t find this out till I was already in the shower. Just a little disappointment, but a easy oversight by the staff. Again I have found that the bathroom central exhaust is not functioning. It leads to steamy showers, and in wet climates mold. But in this area since it’s so dry the only downside is steamy showers. Good property and will improve after the complete transition.

“Great place to spend time-lovely amenities” We stayed here for 3 nights while visiting colleges nearby. It was a great location for stanford and ucla berkely. We spent the afternoons here relaxing. The pool is beautiful with a hot tub. Lots of palm trees and lovely vegetation. The breakfast was fantastic. There was a business area with a compter with free internet. It was upstairs above the lobby. Kind of hard to find. No one was hardly using it. They had cookies and bottled water all afternoon in the lobby. The room was modern and comfortable. We had a fridge and microwave and two sinks. Great for getting ready in the morning. There were great restauraunts right across the street and a starbucks. The bus stopped right across the street to go downtown. Even though we were near an airport, it was quiet. The shuttle bus was quick and on time.

“Good room, fantastic location” This is our third year staying at the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf during the month of July. We travel from out of state each year for a family reunion and we have found this hotel to be a good value in a very expensive neighborhood. That said, here are some pointers if you pick this hotel for your Fisherman's Wharf location. The parking is pricey, currently running at about $32.00 a day. There are cheaper public parking lots nearby so you will need to self park to save on parking. The hotel's restaurant is OK but there are so many very good restaurants in the area that we always eat elsewhere (even breakfast). Ask for a room that has been refurbished. Maybe all the rooms are done now but last year some of our relatives had "old style" rooms. Our room this year was fantastic and faced the pool. We loved it as the bed was very, very comfortable and the room was quiet and restful.

“Location, Location, Location” We usually don't stay at hotels around the airport. Not much to see and not much to do, noisy, congested and often not the best of neighborhoods. But the Hilton at Logan Airport is so convenient....it's like another terminal - you and your luggage can walk there without so much as taking a step outside. You can take the hotel shuttle to the train station, or the free airport shuttle. A short train ride takes you just across the water to the heart of Boston. The best part of this stay? Not having to wake up at 4AM to make our morning flight to Chicago!!

“Great Location but very run down!” During recent stay for a meeting that was being held at this hotel I found the property very run down. The worst of it is the hotel has a critter problem...Bugs and mice! The meeting room had nats flying around, one of my co-workers had bugs in the carpet in his room. Another co-worker had to have her room moved because a mouse was in the room. No critters in my room but I was on the top floor. It seemed like the whole place needed a good scrubbing. Stay at the Hyatt, Intercontinental or new Hilton right by the ballpark instead. They are right in the same area

“Totally enjoyed my time at Marriott's Canyon Villas resort” This is absolutely one of the best Marriott vacation resorts in the States. The suite is luxury and well maintained. My husband, my 6 month old and myself just love the swimming pools dotted throughout the resort as well as the exotic desert plants everywhere you see. Highly recommended for family vacationers.

“Chambres luxueuses et bon emplacement” Les chambres sont très très spacieuses, le service est impeccable! L'hôtel est proche du quartier du Rittenhouse square et ses petits restaurants. Vous êtes à 5 minutes de la mairie et à 20 minutes (à pied) du centre historique (Independence Hall...). Le bar de l'hôtel est très sympa. WIfi gratuit.

“Kitschy yet comfortable” I felt like I was staying in an Anime set design, but overall it was an ok experience. The room was clean and somewhat spacious for San Francisco. There must be something wrong with the window as the echoing of wind blowing was annoying and constant due to a big storm that arrived while I was in town. The bed was surprisingly comfortable and the room was very clean. Overall, it was a decent experience, but probably would not stay again due to the location and style not really being my personal taste.

“A Period Piece in Downtown LA” Hollywood loves a good period piece...and Hollywood seems to love the Westin Bonaventure because a ton of films have used the Bonaventure as a backdrop. The Westin is quite proud of their fame. The question for the modern traveler...Does the fame live up to the Westin experience? The first question from many is...WHY would you stay in DOWNTOWN LA?? Downtown LA has a bad rap for being riddled with crime and homeless throngs roaming the streets. I went to school at USC just south of downtown, so I know the old reputation well. I also know that downtown LA has changed. It's the home of significant urban renewal...and renewal can't get more urban than this part of LA. The old garment district warehouses are now semi-luxury lofts. While it's no parade from the nearby Disneyland...Main Street LA is now in the overwhelming shadow of the gorgeous new Disney Music Hall. The theater complex and Museums have really taken root and make the area very enjoyable...and easily walkable which is a real treat in Los Angeles. But...about the hotel...the architecture was tres avant garde back in the day it was built. You're faced with basically 5 giant room-filled columns. From an architectural vantage, that was probably pretty cool. As a guest, it's not an age of architectural glory that you're trying to remmber. Instead, you're faced with sometimes challenging task of remembering which elevator ascends the column that will take you to your room, and if you're wrong, it may be a while before you find your heavenly bed. I read a lot of reviews about the Bonventure being dated, and I have to disagree. Our rooms were very nice. The toiletries in the bathroom were sparse, but I thought that the room was generally very nice. The trademarked Heavenly Bed was heavenly, and the decor wasn't dated at all. An odd function of the cylindrical architecture is that an elevator ran literally within an arm's reach of our windows. Noise was never a problem, but if you're not an exhibitionist, you might request a room away from the view of elevators. We didn't bother changing rooms, so read what you will into that. Finally, there's a rotating lounge and restaurant on the top floor... and it's really a must see. It's pricey, so I wouldn't recommend dinner, but it's certainly worth a drink...sunset if you can!

“updated and renovated route 66 era motel” There is no way I would've given this place a chance if I had not discovered that they were Ramada's property of the year for 2011. This old gal has completely had a makeover, but all the property charm has been kept. The grounds are simply divine--lots of grassy places for kids to run around, and there was even a little bunny on the premises! The rooms were impressively clean for my persnickety mother and we appreciated the fridge and microwave. The interior design is pleasing, and the electrical outlets are ample for all your electronics. Keep in mind: no breakfast, so if you include the cost of this, plus the hassle- you might save more money going somewhere else. This hotel could really go over the top by trying to advertise that they are Hawaii without the plane ticket price...they could provide poolside drink services, or room service with the restaurant on their property, and make lots of happy customers. I'm not giving it a 4 because the things that reminded me it was an older property were the things that mattered to me: the jacuzzi had only 3 out of 6 jets working, and there was only a shower with no tub. You simply can't beat the price, though, for what you get. It was the only double queen room we could find in this price range. If you are a family with small kids on a budget...give this motel a look: there is plenty of room for them to stretch and run around. The pool is sweet even if the jacuzzi is lacking. Another plus is that it is located around a lot of interesting Asian eateries, as well as a plethora of shops and chain restaurants. Simply a good option for sensible people.

“Overall very nice ambiance, terrific location, gracious service --but some uneven bits” We stayed at the FS/SF for a mini-vacation. Overall a great value with the extra night free and some preferred partner benefits (breakfasts plus one lunch). Everyone was very nice and gracious. The doormen were particularly welcoming and helpful --snagging cabs and providing useful dining advice. The concierge staff were very nice and helpful with directions but didn't really come up with anything i hadn't already found on on open table or interested in getting reservations to places i couldn't. The room was clean and spacious, lovely bathroom (pristine deep soaking tub-- but no bath salts) and great shampoo products. The room darkening drapes actually overlapped (most hotels seem to have an annoying gap)- big plus. And the window seat was just delightful. Cozy spot to read and look down at the kaleidoscope of Market Street traffic. As manager noted in response to another reviewer, coffee makers & teapots were available on request (but if you don't think to ask... ). Unfortunately the turn down people don't seem used to the idea-- they'd take away dirty mugs but didn't replace them (promptly remedied with a call to housekeeping, but i'd already made the coffee when i noticed...) Oh, another nice thing that could be better-- lovely new TV but many channels not HD. And the written channel listing provided was out of date-- the channel guide on the tv itself was more extensive. And charging for wifi is probably a big profit center but tacky. Less expensive chains provide it gratis. Restaurant was also a bit uneven. The smoked salmon benedict was absolutely perfect. In fact the breakfasts were all lovely, foodwise, and generally timing wise. But one day service was less attentive --maybe it was one particular server who was inattentive--the day she was serving it took forever to get breakfast. We also were disappointed with lunch -- (same day, same server)--- we ordered the soup, asked if it was vegetarian, were assured that it was. and it came served topped with distinctly unvegetarian bacon! We sent it back (i hate being put in the position of having to send food back!) but we could overhear the cook being upset that he hadn't been told to omit it. Waitress seemed indifferent to the error. the rest of the lunch was adequate but not up to the list prices on the menu. it may have just been a bad day or the A team on vacation. Overall a very nice property, comfortable public spaces and service orientation. And great location. But the handful of glitches were surprising.

“Beautiful room, but inconsistent service” We stayed for a week in early July--two adults and a teen on a rollaway in a Madison King room. This room is very large--tons of room for yoga, and is quietly luxurious as noted by previous reviewers, with a fabulously comfortable bed and pillows (although the rollaway was not so great--why do they charge $50/night for these?), thick towels, a remote that controls every electronic item in the room, including the blind, etc. We loved the room. The bathroom was equally beautiful, except that the shower is badly designed so that every time you get out of the shower there is a mini-flood on the bathroom floor--very bizarre and annoying, given how carefully designed the other elements of the room and bathroom are. We didn't like the spotty room service, which sometimes left clean water and wine glasses and sometimes didn't, as well as sometimes leaving Maison du Chocolat macarons and sometimes not. You'd expect consistency and thoroughness at a hotel like this. We also didn't much enjoy the lobby, which is very Esme Squalor--that is--loudly and painfully stylish, with rather unfriendly reception and a very silly bar (go and see it yourself if you have a chance--it's worth it for the wow, that's just silly factor). However, the doormen were all very nice, and the location makes almost anything at all worth it. What a fantastic spot, especially in the summer when the trees are in full leaf. Central Park is half a block, the Frick is a few blocks south, the Met is three blocks north, and the best espresso I've ever had at Saint Ambroeus is around the corner. Plenty of buses and cabs, as well as a subway stop nearby. It was always a joy after a long day walking around the city to come back to this quiet and beautiful street and to the cool, heavenly room.

“Nice Residence Inn” uthis is an updated Marriott property.Flat screen TV, stainless steel appliances. Full size refrigerator and oven, dishwasher. Granite tops with a fireplace. It is clean. What you would expect from a Residence Inn. Good breakfast. Friendly staff. Walls are a little thin.

“Wonderful stay” Absolutely wonderful stay, start to finish (I stayed 6 nights). I booked by calling the hotel, and got a much better rate than on the internet (I paid $205 per night, plus tax and parking). All personnel were kind, polite and helpful. The hotel size is just right- not too big, not too small. The lobby makes you feel like you're in a European city. Restaurant, bar and pub all outstanding. Location perfect. Gym is much better than most hotels. Free WiFi everywhere, and if you need a computer, there are two, with printers, free, along with stationary supplies in the 'business center'. Mini-fridge in room was a nice touch, and they give you all the free bottled water you want, both in your room and in the gym. i would definitely stay there again.

“Un peu décue” C'etait mon deuxieme séjour a l'hotel Colonnade, globalement l'hotel est toujours plutot bien mais j'ai été un peu decue cette fois-ci. La clim faisait beaucoup de bruit (meme éteinte), il y avait une tache sur mon dessus de lit et la vue sur le parking manquait de charme. La piscine sur le toit de l'hotel est sympa s'il fait beau, mais elle n'est ouverte que de 8h du matin a 20h. Par ailleurs, l'acces Internet est payant ($13.95 pour 24 h) ce qui me semble peu compatible avec un hotel d'affaires.

“Great value, reliable hotel choice for midtown” I had stayed at Hilton Garden Inn Chelsea in 2008, and having just stayed at Hilton Garden Inn W 35th st. for one week, I can safely say Hilton Garden Inn's in Manhattan are reliable, safe hotel choices and a great value for your money. The location of the hotel is perfect—Yellow and Orange subway lines right out the door and a short walk to others. Within walking distance to many major attractions. Safe street. I had the continental breakfast in the hotel restaurant one day. A decent selection of baked goods, cereal and fruit... but you can find many inexpensive breakfast options right outside the hotel on 6th ave. I really appreciated the free coffee in the morning by the hotel bar. Lovely to pour a cup and go! The room is very clean and well-appointed with Direct TV, coffeemaker, microwave, minifridge and Free in-room WiFi. However the lack of an in-room safe is a letdown for me. Lower levels get a little bit of street noise at night. Housekeeping is very thorough and non-intrusive. I will definitely consider returning to this hotel in the future and recommend to others.

“Ok but loud on a friday night” My husband and I stayed at this hotel on a Friday night. The valet parking is very nice given the traffic and craziness of downtown. We did have some trouble finding it and had to circle the block. Our room was on a very high floor and was a little dated. But the view was amazing! My only complaint was the noise from a local club or something. We could hear clubbing music well into 3 am. I don’t know if sound carries or what but it was the first time I’ve had to fall asleep with a TV on to drown out noise! We chose this hotel for its location to the convention center (its about three blocks away). It was a nice place to stay and I think will be very nice once the renovations are complete (the pool was closed when we were there).

“Pleasant stay at the Stanford Court” We arrived in San Francisco Thursday morning and took BART to the Powell station. We decided to bag the cab and just walk up Powell to the Stanford Court hotel - with our luggage. (Yes, I know it’s at the top of Nob Hill....but I knew we’d be eating a lot of delicious food and welcomed the exercise) We booked our room about 2 months before our stay on Marriott’s web-site. They had a deal – Super Savvy Weekend rate for $159.00 and we stayed 4 nights. The Stanford Court is a nice, clean hotel with a very friendly staff. We arrived around 10:30AM and to my surprise, the room was ready. I’m Platinum with Marriott so we selected our arrival gift: Bottled water...(quite parched after the uphill trek) and brie/crackers – plus it came with a side of grapes – yum. The size of the room is a bit bigger than most San Francisco hotels (but many SF hotels have tiny rooms). The room was clean but very traditional, almost antique looking furniture but the room had everything we needed. A king bed with down comforters and pillow top, separate vanity from the bathroom with full length mirror, open closet next to the vanity/sink with bench. Our room was on the 8th floor with a partial city view. I noticed the walls in the room needed a fresh coat of paint but I could smell fresh paint in the hall-way and noticed they’d painted other areas around the hotel, so I’m sure room will be refreshed soon. The bed seemed very comfortable at first but at night as we slept the bed sloped a bit in the middle. We’d wake up right next to each other and we’d have to scoot back to our sides. It may have been the mattress or maybe an old bed frame? We loved the chocolates on our pillows with the turn down service and hot chocolate with our wake-up call. As a Platinum member, we got the healthy start buffet on weekday mornings in the restaurant. They had oatmeal, granola, cereal, croissants, pastries, fresh berries, toast, etc. It was good. The location is perfect – walk down Powell to Union Square or walk down California to China Town and the Embarcadero or walk down Powell to the North to North Beach and Fisherman’s Wharf. Sometimes the walk back up the uphill was a little difficult after a big meal but we loved the exercise. If we’d had enough exercise for the day, it was easy to catch a cab for a few bucks. The trolley stops at the top of the hill – but it’s not worth $5 a person. A cab is much cheaper. Just down Powell, a street or two is a liquor store/market. The prices are better than other similar stores closer to Union Square. It’s a great place to stock up on water, snacks and beverages for the week. Just down from the market is a great little Mexican restaurant. I don’t remember the name but it was really good an in-expensive compared to other nearby restaurants. Other days/nights we ventured to North Beach for lunches and dinner. North Beach has better restaurants than Union Square. We always felt safe walking back to the hotel at night. The staff was pleasant and we did not have any problems. I would stay at this hotel again.

“Very decent hotel - would recommend” Pros: We were puzzled by all of the negative reviews. This is a very good hotel with a nice well kept lobby area, good restaurant for breakfast, friendly staff, clean, well appointed rooms, decent bathroom, clean hallways. More upscale, than the Crowne Plaza down the street. (Where we have also stayed and would also recommend) We got a very good value on priceline and would definitely stay here again. Cons: the pool was very small and was unheated; we found on street parking but otherwise parking lot is not right there and you are charged every time you leave; they charge for internet access (just ridiculous - really think the Hilton needs to change this if they want to build loyalty).

“Loved it!!” While my family is usually a Marriott family, we decided to stay Westin this time around because the Marriott propertes are just too much in the middle of everything in the Riverwalk - constant crowds. I will stay Westin at every future Riverwalk stay. We are only gold level but were treated like royalty. It was insanely busy that weekend (sold out) but the service never faltered. The rooms were clean, the location on the riverwalk is great (within walking distance to everything but out away from the drunken loud crowds). We did not eat there other than visit their breakfast bar (grab & go) in the mornings. We also had drinks in the bar 1 night. The entire trip was fantastic. Thanks for the tips on requesting self-parking. $15 per day is much better than $45. But we loved it so much, we may lean more towards starwood properties in the future.
“Great, fun place!” We have stayed at the Modern B&B many times. Each time has been wonderful. The rooms are very comfortable and the location is over the top. We look forward to going back.

“Excellent Hotel!!” My husband and I spent three nights at this hotel and could not have had a more enjoyable experience. We always try to stay at a Kimpton hotel if the city we are traveling to has one and this is one of their better properties for ambiance, quality and outstanding service. It is certainly a beautiful hotel. Having read some past negative reviews I was somewhat apprehensive but either the reviews were wrong or the hotel has greatly improved. Check-in went well, our room was perfect, our stay was without any problems and check-out was easy. The hotel atmosphere is very relaxing and lends itself to having a great time. The wine hour was enjoyable and two of the evenings the manager circulated the room to make sure the guests were pleased with the hotel. Housekeeping did an excellent job each day and never caused us an inconvenience. Every staff member was great. We tried the hotel restaurant for breakfast and it was excellent. Went to the fourth floor outdoor bar. The area was nice but it was too cold to stay. The fitness room was so-so - not very big with limited equipment. The location of the Hotel Solamar is convenient to both the Gaslamp District and the Convention Center area. Public transportation is nearby and the city bus to the airport is a few steps outside the hotel. We took it back to the airport and it took about thirlty minutes. We would definitely stay at this hotel should we visit San Diego again.

“Solid Airport Option” I just spent one night here and got a great deal so value-wise, I was impressed. I arrive about 11pm and it was pouring rain. I drove around to the parking lot (uncovered) hoping there would be a back door I could go in through, but the back lot is a bit shady (or at least in the rain) and I drove back out to the front and decided to valet which wasn't much more expensive. I was checked in immediately and went up to my room. I'm Starwood Platinum which usually means I'm upgraded but I'm not sure there are upgraded rooms here. There was a nice note from the GM stating that they are re-doing the Preferred Level, and there was also a plate of cookies and grapes, which I felt was a nice touch for this level of hotel. There were also several bottles of water. The bed was comfortable and though the room was a little bit dated, it sounds like they are making improvements. The bathroom was fine, had lots of counter space and decent bath products. Location-wise, it was great for the airport and for the price I paid, I would definitely consider this hotel again in the future. The staff were also very nice.

“Terrific Location” We stayed at this hotel for two days with our 16 and 8 year old sons. The location is wonderful. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room was perfectly comfortable and had a nice view of the courtyard. The location of this hotel is really great as it is within a short walking distance of the Mall. We were disappointed that the pool wasn't yet open as they told us it would be and that was one of the main reasons we chose this hotel in the first place. We had been hoping to let the kids swim and relax after long days of sightseeing. The gift shop was tiny and the staff there was not very friendly. The room where you can store your bags before you can check in was uncomfortably disorganized but the people working there were very nice. The business center seemed to be very busy and there was often a line to get access to a computer. I loved the little courtyard which was a comfortable place to sit and relax with a cup of coffee in the morning or a glass of wine in the evening. All in all, we were very satisfied with our stay here and would gladly stay there again and recommend it to others.

“NIce views, good hotel.” Not my first visit to the Lake Union Silver Cloud Inn. Staff are always incredibly helpful and polite: a real plus to the hotel. The rooms are a little basic (certainly there's no luxury here,) but they are completely serviceable. No bar or restaurant in the hotel but there is a shop where you can buy essentials and charge them to you your room. There is a continental breakfast provided which is reasonable and very popular and included in the price of the room. There's a pool (never used it) and a very small fitness room (one treadmill) but at the time of my visit they were busy expanding the fitness 'centre' which I think was long overdue The location is slightly out of the way of downtown (for example, you can't do one of those van shares to the airport from here) but there is a great new tram service taking you to downtown which terminates right outside the hotel. But Seattle isn't a big city so being 2 miles away from downtown isn't a big problem. A real bonus is the fantastic free hotel shuttle service to downtown and the Seattle Centre (and some other locations). So the hotel isn't luxurious and not necessarily cheap given the accomodation quality, but all the little extras they provide make it worth checking out as a hotel when in Seattle. Do check out the lake view rooms as the view is fantastic.

“I have stayed here about 20 times” And The Peninsula never ceases to amaze me. It is one of the very few places where you can stay and be assured that your entire experience will be PERFECT. Frankly, when paying the rates at a 5 star hotel like this, one should have perfection. You will. I have stayed at many of the other 5 star hotels in Chicago, and none can compare to the Pen.

“Gutes, traditionelles Hotel” Das Madisson Hotel in Washington ist ein gutes Hotel, wenn auch mit einer relativ guten Lage.Man ist zwar nicht direkt am Regierungsdistrikt, der für Touristen den interessanten Part der Stadt ausmacht, sondern muss sich erst ein Stück erlaufen. Zum Capitol ist es sehr weit, etwa 45 Fußweg, zum Weißen Haus dagegen nur etwa 10 min. Das Hotel an sich ist in amerikanisch, trditionellen Stil der 40er Jahre gehalten, wobei es nicht heruntergekommen oder vernachlässigt aussieht, sondern immer noch gut renoviert ist. Die Klimaanlage hingegen war leider sehr laut und das Bad für meinen Geschmack ein wenig zu alt, was die Ausstattung angeht. In der Lobby gibt es kostenloses WLAN, auf den Zimmern kostet dieses jedoch Geld. Ansonsten ist das Madisson ein gutes und schönes Hotel mit einer akzeptablen Lage.

“Perfect stay in this Hotel” We stayed in this delightful Hotel. Who provide wonderful stay, friendly service and an extraordinary breakfast. The room was beautiful, sunny and clean, and we were made to feel at home at all times. It’s a breath of fresh air because of the stunning landscape outside with beautiful flowers. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this hotel.

“Pleasant Stay” Very polite and attentive staff, prompt valet service, clean rooms. The business center offers free airplane boarding pass printing. Rooms are clean and beds are comfortable. The bathroom is a tad small, but it's not terrible.

“Enjoyed the Hyatt” I booked rooms for our family of 10 over Labor Day weekend. Even though the hotel was very busy I never felt neglected or as if the staff was overwhelmed. The Hotel was well kept and the rooms quite nice. I slept very well on their mattress which was divine. The concierge was accomodating. He made us reservations and offered coupons for a great restaurant on the Mall. Overall our experience was terrific for all 10 of us, no easy feat.

“You really can't beat the location” I stayed at Crowne Plaza Times Square for 2 nights, while on a bussiness trip. Perfectly located in the heart of it all, it is a very short walk from everything - theaters, fine restaurants, great coffee. My co-workers and I dined at Pigalle (5 minutes away on foot) twice in 2 days. The rooms have been renovated and the lobby area in nice, modern, sleek. I had somewhat of a problem with my bathroom fixtures (faucet was leaking and the sink was cracked, which made the water drip until the floor was full of water. The maintenance person came right away and offered me to change rooms, which I declined, since it was midnight. However, he cleaned everything and promised to come the following day to replace the sink. This didn't happen, but I was not really disturbed by it. I did mention this story briefly at the front desk as I was checking out and... apart from apologies, the clerk also went ahead and removed the only charges on the room bill, 2 nights worth of Internet use. My intention was strictly to inform them, but the lady was extremely nice and I thought her reaction was great customer service. I would definitely recommend and I would also come back.

“Good location” Gee, Charles C wrote most of what I was going to say. It's a good place for the price and it is in a convenient location. From here we were able to walk up to Kerry Park (slowly), over to the Space Needle, and wandered to downtown and the waterfront. Nice sized, clean room. Friendly and helpful staff. Microwave, fridge and sink in our room. We'll probably stay here again on our next visit to Seattle, as long as cool temperatures are in the forecast!

“Quite, comfy, safe” This property in the financial district offers lovely views. The desk staff is friendly, the concierge well informed, and the room warm and cozy. Towels we nice, sheets were soft, the bed was like clouds, and the room maintained in good order. I was here on Christmas and enjoyed my stay. The TV is appropriately positioned to the bed so that I could watch TV until my eyes glazed! Give this property a consideration your next trip to SF.

“Very nice airport hotel” I bid on priceline.com and paid only $116 (including tax) for one night in this 4-star hotel. It was definitely worth it. It is a true 4-star hotel with all the style, comfort, and space. I asked for a room with double beds, but the hotel clerk told me that they ran out of such rooms and upgraded me to a room with a living area, and a pull-out sofa. It has plenty of desk and storage space, a large bathroom, two TVs, and a king-size bed. My mom and I had a very restful night between flights. Though it was near the airport, we couldn't hear the airplanes at all when inside the room. It doesn't feel like an airport hotel at all. There is a Burger King right across the street, so you can save money on food if you don't mind fast food for one day (we didn't.)

“Save $, great location, but room temp?? Aaaaghhhhh !!!” Attending a conf in D.C. Decided to try and save my company some $. Had a rate of $109 at HH vs $240 - $300 at conf-recommended hotels. Here's the low-down. THE GOOD: Excellent location in downtown D.C. Less than 1 block from Metro. Plenty of varied restaurants within easy walking distance. Front desk staff was decent enough. Room was clean. Fairly quiet. Didn't eat at hotel restaurant, but there's two connected to the hotel. THE BAD: Closet space/depth is no more than finger-to-elbow deep (see pic). But the big prob is that room temp is centrally controlled (there's a knob in the room, but it's disconnected and front desk will tell you room temp is central controlled at front). My room was SWELTERING. They sent up maint guy, who fiddled with the heater, but that did nothing. Late Oct, so wasn't too cold outside. So I had to open my windows. Unfortunately, 2 floors down on adjacent roof were the HVAC units, so the noise was overwhelming. Very disappointed in this area. Took a bullet for the company, but never again.

“Very Chic Hotel! Great Location!” The W Hotel in Times Square is a very chic hotel, in a great location! It's perfect if you will be taking in Broadway show! The staff was very friendly and courteous. The rooms are small, but nice. I was there on the weekend and the bar in the lobby can fill up and get pretty noisy, but it's part of the ambience of the hotel. The club in the basement of the hotel was cool and had decent music. I would recommend the hotel, but search around for a good rate as it can be expensive. It's a nice hotel, but don't overypay. We spent around 234.00 a night in November. The hotel restaurant, Blue Fin, is excellent but expensive. If you want ambience, and a great location, then I would recommend staying at the W Times Square!
“Waste of a great architecture” Great exterior facade as well as for the lobby and outlets. The rooms are a dive; service is sh1t. Never staying here again ever!

“Great location, great price!” Being that Hotel Circle contains a wide array of hotels, I think it may be just personal preference as to where you stay. On a previous trip, I stayed at the Holiday Inn (Hotel Circle) but this time decided to try something else, I was not disapointed. The hotel welcomed us with a lounge area in the lobby (big screen tv included) and because we had arrived so early in the morning, they were more than happy to hold our bags while we went galavanting. Upon check in, the staff was very helpful and welcomed us with two warm chocolate cookies (VERY good). Our room was very spacious and clean although there wasn't much of a view. The parking area can be a bit of a walk and the ramps leading up and down the parking levels are VERY narrow. If you drive a big SUV or truck, you may want to park elsewhere. The location is awesome, few minutes away from Sea World and Qualcomm, and a couple of minutes away from Fashion Valley Mall (a very nice place to shop). Getting to and from the hotel is very convenient as it is located right next to the freeway. Sports Arena Blvd., which contains tons of eating places, is also just a hop and a skip away. There is internet access ($5 for about 1/2 hour) in the lobby and a nice swimming pool / jacuzzi which is open until 11 pm. Great place to stay!

“Awesome location, no extras” Stayed here one night at a discount rate--would have been really annoyed if I'd paid full price. It may be the best location in the city, between Times Square and Central Park. Room was clean, bed was comfortable, and shower was good. But don't expect any extras--the TV remote didn't work, the thermostat didn't operate, and the cold water knob was partially broken. Fortunately, you don't spend much time in the room when you're in NYC. Wish I'd had some street noise to drown out whoever seemed to be bowling over my head until 1am.

“NORMALITO Y CARO” Estuvimos en The Surrey desde el 28 de Diciembre del 2011 hasta el 4 de Enero de 2012. Hicimos la reserva directamente en el hotel, las noches del 30 y 31 de Diciembre costaban más del doble del resto de los días, que ya era bastante caro. La situación es regular, está a tres manzanas del metro más cercano, y es necesario transporte para llegar hasta el centro, eramos tres, y habíamos pedido una suite, con sofa-cama, y una habitación silenciosa, y se pago de forma anticipada, porque había descuento, la habitación estaba en el 3o piso, y daba a la calle, así que no era muy silenciosa, porque además no está bien insonorizada, la calefacción no podías manejarla tú, lo hacían de forma central, y había noches en las que hacía bastante frio, no había sofa-cama, nos pusieron una cama supletoria, y el día que fuimos a hacer el check-out, nos cobraban 300 $ por la cama que nos habían puesto. El punto más cutre, fue que todas las noches nos daban botellas de agua y galletas, pero la noche antes de irnos, nada!!!! Lo mismo con el champú, suavizante, gel, etc... el día antes, nos quitaron todo lo que sobraba, supongo que para que no nos lo llevaramos. Eso sí, el personal del hotel era muy amable, y casi todos hablaban, más o menos español, pero no creo que repitiera.

“Strange Hotel - not great location” The hotel had signs in the elevators advertising the upgrading of rooms but it was hard to tell if this had happened yet. The room I stayed in was functional but drab as was the hotel itself. It is beside a YMCA that it uses for its health club - the street outside is non-descript and the overall location is not very convenient if you are staying here as a tourist. Overall it is an uninspiring place, a little on the ugly side and best for a one-night passing through stay otherwise I would skip it. I was on business and there for only the one night and it was ok for that - just!

“Hilton quality, but this one's not my favorite” I stayed here for an overnight before an early flight out of San Jose Mineta Airport. Overall I have no major complaints - but with all the choices in the area, this probably won't be my first choice on my next trip. First the location is right downtown - if you're unfamiliar getting to / from the freeway, it can be difficult especially in high traffic times. Secondly, it is directly below the flight path to the airport, so there was some noise from the jets. Finally, the hotel has a very "industrial" style in the rooms - just not my taste. I thought it made the room look like it was in a much lower tier hotel chain - but that's just my taste. All Hilton staff that I encountered were very professional and courteous..

“A little tired - Look elsewhere!” Stayed here on business back in January and it was fine for one night. Much more likely would have driven me stir-crazy. Room was decent - good-sized and clean - but certainly could have used a facelift. Parking was - as noted in other reviews - a bit inconvenient. Look elsewhere in the neighborhood if you're staying near the Medical Centers. I certainly will next time.

“Great Comfortable Hotel” I loved staying at this hotel. The service was outstanding and you should not miss the free chips and guacamole (and margaritas) in the lobby in the evening. The rooms are well thought out and very relaxing. I had a chance to experience the club level and found that to be amazing. Great service and food. I was only sorry I did not get upgraded for the level. No worries though as my room was wonderful. Near a nice choice of dining and close to everything in Dallas

“Nice location and beautiful hotel.” Check in was easy, very helpful front desk. Nice, clean rooms with beautiful views of the city. Good size and nice bathroom with all the essentials. Check out was easy via telephone. I'm looking forward to staying here, again.

“Wonderful stay” Location is unparalleled, and the hotel has an old-world feel with all of the amenities you would expect. I was upgraded to a great suite on the 31st floor - must have been bigger than my house - what a fantastic surprise. Had dinner at Bourbon Steak - the french fries are to die for. (The steak wasn't bad either.) It was a quick trip - but a great oasis in the city. Nice job to the staff.

“Renovation fantastic” Very contemporary hotel right by the Prudential Center, terrific and pleasant staff. The rooms are newly decorated and good sized, though the construction is not over yet, leading to noise during the day. Rooms at the front of the hotel are larger than the backside. Room service from Brasserie Jo was excellent and very quick. Great hotel to stay at in the back bay area.

“Fabulous hotel” I am just back from Chicago and the Hilton. I was there with my three girlfriends and found the hotel great. We got upgraded because I am Hilton Gold, so we were able to use the Executive floor for free breakfasts, and between 5-7pm free nibbles and an honor bar. We had booked a room with two bathrooms, which was very big and had a partial view of the lake. The hotel is straight across the the road from Grants park, and further up the Millenhium Park, which was stunning with the trees changing colour etc. The Executive floor staff were excellent, booking restaurants etc for us, and were very helpful. The swimming pool is huge, and has windows all around which was another plus. To shop, it is just around a slow half hours walk to North Michigan Avenue, which we did quite a lot, or you can take the free shuttle there, leaves every hour and returns every hour. We checked in and out with no problem, no waitin etc. We thoroughly enjoyed the hospitality of the Chicago people and staying at this hotel, and would definately stay here again. Chicago is just beautiful.

“Very good under right circumstances” I have always wanted to stay at the Omni due to its proximity to the Convention Center. I attend a conference there annually. Its location turned to be ideal, better than the new Hiltion or the Marriott (which are at end sides of the Covention Center, while the Omni lies in the middle). The hotel accomodations are good, but not "excellent" for the price (if you get a government rate, then they would be fair). TVs are old, channel options are not great (in fact, my HBO went dark after the second day). If you do decide to stay at the Omni, I highly recommend that you register for their Loyalty Program. It's free and it does provide some good perks (such as 2 complementary morning drinks delivered to your room, and other extras that are saved on your profile). Overall, a very good hotel (I know that it is a high commodity, due to its proximity and bridge connection to PETCO Park [Baseball Stadium], on that note, if you would like to see your favorite baseball players, you can usually find some in the lobby about an hour after the game).

“Great for family group, lots of room” Directly on Times Square, front door adjoins the front door to Legally Blonde. Right in the middle of the action, but crowds and pace on the sidewalks may be a bit intense for some, and particularly for anybody with a stroller or walking aid. Definitely worth upgrading to a package that includes the complimentary breakfast buffet. The buffet included fresh fruit, hot oatmeal, hot breakfast meats, omelettes and eggs made to order, pancakes and waffles to order, cold meat and cheese selection, smoked salmon, juices, breakfast pastries. Something for everyone, and open until 11:30 each morning. Our suite had two double beds plus living room and pull out couch. Decor very pleasant, kitchenette was helpful. Extra sink and large mirror in kitchenette area doubled as an extra vanity. Three women and all their stuff fit nicely, not crowded, very comfortable. The fitness center is under construction, temporary quarters are crowded but servicable. The business center had three computers and servicable printer, all worked well and was convenient. No complaints, great stay, will return if travelling with family. For a romantic holiday, go several blocks away from Times Square for a more calm and relaxing experience.

“Loved it and I will definitely will stay here again” I am very particular about hotels and this was absolutely one of the best experiences I have ever had, especially for the bargain price. I booked the room on the Marriott website for $159 a night and even received a gift card for $25 visa card per night, making this an amazing deal. I took the blue line to the hotel, which was a short walk and from the moment of arrival, I was in love with the historic Blackstone. The bellman was instantly available to help me with my luggage up the stairs. Upon checkin, I was given an envelope to log in for my visa vouchers. At the check in desk, the clerk spent the time to talk to me and welcome me, even walking me right to the elevators. The next day, another clerk was very helpful giving tips on sightseeing neighborhoods. I felt that the hotel itself was absolutely beautiful and newly redone in a stylish old meets new look. The room was so comfortable and I loved the italian marble in the bathroom and throughout the whole hotel. Amenities were Aveda and there were bathrobes in the large bathroom. There was only a shower with fair water pressure, but it was certainly acceptable. I ate twice at the restaurant, Mercat, which was AMAZING for lunch and brunch. I appreciated the business center with free internet access and a printer for boarding passes For the price, i can not think of a better experience in all of my travels.

“A sound pre-flight option” I have transited so often over LAX that I could write a book about the hotels along Century Blvd leading up to the airport. But, until recently, I had not stayed at this Courtyard—and I can honestly say, I’ve missed a real gem! Situated a stone’s throw from the airport (but not directly off Century, so you miss the constant hum of passing cars), this newly renovated, sleek hotel is really a great option for those late night arrivals and/or early connections from LAX. The staff is efficient, the rooms clean and well-outfitted (fluffy beds, lots of space, good lighting!). There is a complimentary computer ‘center’ with free coffee to the right of the main entrance (and free WIFI in the rooms). There is also a café on offer in the main lobby, offering drinks and light eats. Maybe I was swayed by the new ‘facelifting’ of this hotel (hey! This is LA!), but I wouldn’t hesitate to stay here again, particularly given the very reasonable price we received (booking through the website directly). Sweet dreams, travelers!

“Average Hotel...” When I visited Chicago for the first time, the "Hilton" brand seemed like a safe bet. I remember having seen it in that Harrison Ford movie (Fugitive?)...and it looked nice. When I arrived, I was surprised at how old it was. It is an extremely old hotel...but appears to have been relatively well maintained. The line at check in was LONG...but I was impressed at how quickly the line was moving. Kudos to the front desk staff. The room was average. Not great...not bad. It was quite large -- I got one with two double beds, as I was staying there with a friend of mine (not my spouse). Didn't eat in the restaurants...just got orange juice and a danish at their coffee counter. Service was quick...prices were fair. On my next trip to Chicago, I would certainly explore other hotels before I would return to the Chicago Hilton.

“Excellent hotel!” the final stop in my multi-centre trip and this hotel was by far the best hotel we stayed in! modern, chic, contemporary... you name it. It was beatufiully decorated and elegant. The staff were excellent at customer service providing maps information etc. The room was clean, bright and spacious. It was about a 20minute walk to Union Square which was excellent and it was also accessibe by buses that run near by. We did not try to breakfast or the food there, but that was our own choice, not to reflect on their restaurant. Fusion cuisine doesnt float my boat hehe! But overall, this is an excellent boutique hotel.

“Not luxurious, sometimes problematical, but I keep coming back...” I've used this hotel some 15-20 times over the past ten years for business travel. I've experienced management changes and the good/bad/ugly of two-star hotels. But during the past three years I've seen a definite improvement in all areas, from customer service ("uncaring" has become "very friendly") to room condition ("shabby" has become "modest but clean") to free breakfast in the dining area ("cold packaged danish" has become "hot, real food"). This location IS older, and it shows. There are no inside hallways, all rooms open to the elements. Heating and A/C units can vary from room to room, as does WiFi connectivity. But over the years I've used this hotel I've learned a few basics that make each stay comfortable for me: 1) Check out the room before settling down, and if there's any problem let management know; they'll most likely try to accommodate a polite request. 2) Don't expect five-star quality for two-star prices. 3) If you really must have quiet, ask for a second floor room away from I-10 and not facing the pool. 4) If wi-fi is really important (it is to me, a wired business traveler) check it out from your room when you first arrive and ask to be moved if you're not satisfied. And why do I keep coming back? Because it's an easily accessible location with comfortable beds at a decent per-night price and (since about 2008) friendly, helpful employees who make me feel welcome. Oh...and the Tony Lama store next door is a great place to get some new boots at a great price.

“Needs a little work” We got this hotel through Priceline. The rooms were comfortable and the location was adequate but there were definitely some (minor) issues with our stay. First, the good. The hotel is very striking when you first arrive. The decor of the rooms is good. We really liked our beds. We ate at the bar the first night we arrived and although we thought it was a bit pricey at first we were pleased with the portions provided. The bad. The hyatt tries to come off as this upscale hotel, but really they are trying to pinch every penny they can out of you. The mini bar is computerized, so if you try to move things around (i.e. put something of your own in there) you will automatically be charged. We didn't know this and had been moving things around all night. The next morning we saw the tiny notice on the mini fridge and called the front desk. Thankfully, they removed the charges. If you want to use the fridge for yourself it is a $10 charge. Also there are no vending machines because they want you to take the overpriced products in the minifridge. This was a bit annoying. Next issue was that our coffee maker was broken. It took over an hour for someone to come and replace it. The hotel is located on the edge of the embarcadero right across from the Ferry Building. It is a bit of a walk to most sights, but if you don't mind a walk it is not too big of a deal. There are bus stops right at the corner. If I were to go back to SF I would probably look for a different part of town to stay in as this is the Financial District and dead after dark. Still, a good deal for Priceline.

“Good all around!” I used to live around the corner from the Hilton Garden Inn so I knew the area and chose this hotel for its location. It is 1 block from the subway that goes to the airport (JFK), close to all subway lines, 1 block from a grocery store (Food Emporium), and close to affordable, less touristy restaurants on 9th Avenue (between 43rd and 53rd-ish). I was upgraded to a room with 2 queen beds which were quite comfortable. The room was clean, had a desk, flatscreen TV, microwave, refridgerator, iron and ironing board, free wi-fi and they gave me two bottles of water for free upon check-in.
