They offer cookies in the afternoon, and use of the business center is free, and printing is also free! The staff was wonderful - consistently friendly and helpful. They held my bags the day I checked out. This is a great location and a hotel that offers good value. I didn't have time to use the gym, but there is one. I'll definitely come back to this hotel.

“Disappointing! Disclosed photos does not portray faithfully its simplicity. Nothing but a simpleton hotel!” Disappointing! Disclosed photos does not portray faithfully the simplicity of this hotel which is classified as a "boutique hotel" (not a "charming place”). In fact, that ́s nothing but a simpleton and ugly well-located hotel in Georgetown! Additionally, we find a cockroach in our room and the staff were worried in being discrete with other guests instead of, at least, excuse themselves with us. The breakfast is “on foot” in a small hall next to the reception – "an arm to arm fighting among guests trying to survive”, because there ́re no tables and chairs to sit! The guests must serve themselves and choose to eat on foot or take the snaks and breads to the room (to feed cockroaches?). Regrettable. We do not recommend.

“Excellent hotel and The French Room is dining at its very best.” My wife and i have stayed at the Adolphus several times and it is a great hotel in downtown Big D. Rooms are big and very clean, staff is courteous and helpful. The French Room is without equal in dining pleasure. Food is unequaled, waitstaff is highly trained and knowlegeable. Wine list is extensive. When we are in Dallas going to the Adolphus and The French Room is a must.

“My new favorite NYC Hotel” Stayed at The Bowery for a Saturday night of fun with my husband and some friends. We normally book with points at the W Union Square but decided to try the Bowery for my husbands birthday. We were not disappointed! Great old feel to the hotel and amazing, friendly staff. Didn't have the 'corporate' vibe most front desks have these days. Rooms were bigger than I expected and had a unique feel to them. Bed was fantastic, so comfortable. The location is perfect! We are not as familiar with this neighborhood so we had fun exploring! So close to Bleecker and great nightlife. Neighborhood is a little gritty but somehow it's in a good way. Very laid back hotel/neighborhood and I would recommend it in a heartbeat! Can't wait to go back.

“Nice - our first stay at a Hyatt Place” Nice place - our first time there. I liked the size of the rooms. The kids loved the TV - it's a nice sized flat screen that you can see very well whether lying in bed or sitting on the sofa. The hotel was clean, and the staff friendly. The beds are doubles. I prefer queens, but that's not a dealbreaker. I think we hit the breakfast area during a rush - it was very crowded and the food kept running out. The staff was doing their best to keep up, but probably could have used even more help.

“Hotel that Works” Enjoyed a get-away weekend at Westin Chicago River North. Great first impressions as we could not expect more professional and courteous service from the doorman, front desk and bellman. Throughout our stay every staff member made us feel welcome. We stayed in the standard king room which was very roomy and included a sofa, chair and large desk. The room had a limited view of the Chicago River. The bathroom was large and can easily accommodate two people, loved the “Heavenly Shower”. We did not have any noise issues and their “Heavenly Bed” is very comfortable. As stated in all of the previous posts, the location is great. Negatives: two of the treadmills in the fitness room were not working, extended wait for our car from the valet service and why do they have to charge for internet usage. Would definitely stay again.

“You Get What You Pay For. But That's OK.” If you keep thinking "value" during your stay at this hotel near 96th and Broadway, you will be fine. Otherwise, you may be disappointed. There Newton is clean, well tended, safe, bed-bug free (According to the "Bedbug Registry.Com), cordial and well-staffed by helpful and knowledgable personnel. How many hotels in any part of Manhattan can make those claims at $139 per night! (Plus taxes, of course). In fact, there are few other hotels in the city of any description where you can get that price. At that rate, you do have to share a bathroom down the hall with a few other guests, though for a little more you can get a room with your own toliet facilities. The shared bathrooms are meticulously maintained and, to be honest, I only saw one other guest who used the bathroom ever so breifly in 2 nights at the hotel. Besides, there are 8 floors, each seemingly with one shared bathroom per suite of rooms. So, if your floor is in use, you have 7 more to try. The clientele is a largely European crowd attracted by the bargain prices. Obviously this place is touted in European guidebooks of America. The clientele is quite varied in age, but mostly quiet, patient and travel-savvy. And best of all, you are in New York City, a walk away from some attractions and a brief subway trip away from almost all the major places. The Newton is just across the street from the IRT line 96th Street stop. OK...so what do I mean when I say you get what you pay for. Well the rooms are very small...probably equivalent to a 2 star hotel in Paris. In our room, the closet was not too ingeniously placed right next to the front door, so you couldn't open your closet and the front door at the same time. Plus, the closet was placed where the bathroom would have been...only big a problem for very drunk guests in the middle of the night who forget there is no bathroom. Let's see...one morning at checkout time the only elevator broke down. This was no problem for us at a lower floor, but I feel sorry for guests who had to lug their belongings down in the extreme heat from the upper floors. To be fair, the Hotel staff was quite willing and able in assisting guests with that task. There are two computers for guest use in the lobby (For a price...20c per 15 minutes...not bad). Naturally one of those computers was out of order. And the worst part...while rooms are non-smoking...the previous occupants of our room had ignored this rule. Cigarette smoke clung to everything in the small room. Despite the fact that we kept the very efficient air conditioning blasting for our 2 day stay, the stale cigarette odor never completely washed away. The Upper West Side neighborhood near the Newton is largely residential with the usual array of shops and services that grace a good residential scene. There has been a moderate uptick in panhandling over the past couple of years, but the neighborhood is well policed and largely hassle-free. There is the problem of finding a good comfortable neighborhood bar/restaurant in this area. "The Regional" with decent, sturdy Italian cooking and a really fine bartender comes closest to meeting this need. Otherwise, there are 2 taverns in the area which literally names themselves "dive bars"...which,unfortunately, in my opinion...is an all too apt description of those 2 establishments. You need to walk about 10 blocks up into the Columbia University neighborhood to find the right kinds of pubs. Again, since this is New York, I don't have to advise you on where to go to find anything and everything you want. But in this particular neighborhood, that walk to Columbia is worth it. The campus architecture and the whole atmosphere of the place is quietly outstanding. It is also cool to walk through Riverside Park at 95th Street and make your way to "Hudson Beach" a sprawling outdoor cafe of random tables overlooking the river. Sunset there is especially eye-popping. Children and dogs and all kinds of recreational venues add to the festival atmosphere. The service is slow, so avoid the Cheeseburger unless you enjoy stiff and lifeless cheeseburgers that failed to make their way from grill to your table in anything approaching a normal time.

“Very, very average...” Due to a contract that my company has with the Wyndham, I stay at this particular property about 50 nights per year. If you stay at this hotel without high expectations, then you will be pleased. It is just very, very average. Some high points: -Rooms are always very clean. -The common areas are nice and don't appear worn. -Free Internet with Wyndham By Request membership. Some low points: -Front desk staff needs some serious training. Invariably, I check in with the same 2 or 3 people each time I stay and it takes them 5 minutes to complete a task that should take 30 seconds. Each time, I am asked for my credit card, which is not necessary as a WBR member. I am also constantly amazed that, given the number of nights I stay in this hotel per year, that I am never recognized. None of the employees here are terrible, but none are that great. Just very average to below average. -As has been mentioned, the water pressure in the sink faucets is lousy. -Unless you are a heavy sleeper, you will be woken up each night between 12-1am as they loudly throw the newspapers up and down the hall. -Room service doesn't offer any options that aren't soaked in butter or oil. -Bed and bath linens are of the kind of quality you would expect in a Hampton Inn or similar. -The workout facilities are pitiful. The lone treadmill is a relic of the past and the remaining equipment is sad. Fortunately, I am a member of 24 Hour Fitness, so I just drive a couple of blocks to the nearest gym to workout. Honestly, the only reason I stay here is because of the contract my company has with the property for a $94/night rate. If it was my own dime, I would choose to stay at the Marriott next door. I would avoid the Hyatt across the street as the rooms there are showing their age.

“Nice enough hotel, great condition, and friendly staff” I enjoyed my stay here over the weekend for the UT game. The hotel was in good condition, the staff was pleasant, and my room was very nice. Definitely would recommend this to business travelers because it was nice and quite with a comfortable bed.

“I liked it” I liked this place, it has a cool log cabin feel to it in the lobby. Due to Amtrak problems we didnt arrive until really really late at about 5:30am the morning after we were supposed to arrive. The staff were helpful, though wouldn't refund us or offer a discount even though we'd pretty much missed a night even though it wasn't out fault. That was ok though, i didn't expect them to really. The room was nice, clean and comfy. The area has plenty of convenience stores and fast food places. A little on the shady side the further you walk down the street but nothing major. Good location, and got a free taxi service from the hotel downtown. There seemed to be lots of services at the hotel, pool, shop, resturant, but i didnt use any of them. I'd stay here again.

“Quasi perfetto” perche quasi? solo perchè non ci hanno dato i coupons del nostro package che comprendeva soda e pop corn gratuiti e neanche quelli per le due colazioni comprese nel prezzo fino ad un massimo di 50 dollari, così le due mattine abbiamo sempre dovuto dire al responsabile di sala che avevamo il brakfast incluso e lui doveva controllare.. per il resto veramente perfetto, a partire dall'arrivo con il servizio di valet parking per noi incluso, alla calorosa accoglienza alla reception, alla splendida camera, pulitissima e bellissima e lussuosissima al 12mo piano con vista sul petco park (stadio del baseball). Situato all'inizio del Gaslamp District, quartiere pieno di negozi e ristoranti, vicino al convention center e al trolley che ci ha comodamente portato all'old town park, comodo anche per andare, in macchina, a coronado beach. A fine vacanza dopo più di 5000km sulle strade dell'ovest due pernottamenti con valet parking e colazione per 4 persone 220 euro a notte a camera direi PERFETTO!! Per la connessione gratuita internet in camera, fate l'iscrizione gratutia al programma select guest member e vi arriveranno anche gratuitamente due bevande al piano al mattino.

“Good location, good convention hotel” We stayed at the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile March 31 - April 3 for an Resident Anesthesia Convention. Although this was the Convention Hotel, the rate was $160/nt + tax. I was able to book on Priceline for $79/nt + taxes/fees. For this price, the hotel was a good value. It was a typical Marriott Hotel, though the bathroom in my standard King room on the 22nd floor seemed a bit cramped. The hotel is 3 blocks from the Grand Station on the Red "EL" train line. It was extremely convenient to use the train to get to the hotel from Midway. We used a combination of trains and walking to see many sights in Chicago including the Field Museum, Art Institute, Millennium Park, Navy Pier, China Town, Greek Town and Hancock Tower. The pool was standard, the jacuzzi was closed. The Cardio fitness center had new equipment - several elipticals and tread mills with personal TV screens - very nice. Some colleagues said the view from the upper floors (28 and higher) were quite good. My room was on the 22nd floor, we could see the Navy Pier just fine and look down Michigan Avenue. I think that using Priceline you can book a 4 star hotel in this area for less than $100/night incl. tax. There are quite a few 4 star hotels that are very nice and I was just lucky that the hotel I got on Priceline happened to be the one at which my convention was held.

“Wow....what a place” All the five star reviews about this fine hotel are accurate. Top notch in all respects. The rooms are superb, with a high intention to detail. All the additional amenities are the best, multiple pool options, the Fazio course is beautiful and extremely playable. Dining covers the entire landscape from a very high level to casual. Clearly, one of the top hotels in the west. You need to stay here and experience it....as someone who travels extensively this is one of the best.

“A Unique Hilton Property” I stayed here on a college visit with my daughter. I chose this hotel because it was significantly cheaper than the downtown hotels. The drive time to get into the city is not bad. There are a few stoplights but usually were not a problem. The proximity to the airport would be great if traveling in/out of AUS. There was not much if any noticable jet noise in our room and we were on the airport side. This hotel is a unique round shape which I found to be very appealing with the massive center courtyard, restaurant and coffee shop. The front desk staff were VERY helpful in suggesting places to eat off of the beaten path including a memorable trip for us to Lockhart, TX to Black's BBQ. The room was trademark Hilton quality and comfort. As a diamond, we received free breakfast in the restaurant which was top of the line offering us the buffet or the ability to order from the menu. They did suggest that there might be a parking fee. There was a booth for an attendant but it never was staffed. There is ample parking but I imagine airport travelers could take advantage of it. I think it should be monitored but would have been dissapointed if there had been a charge for it given the amount of space they have available. I was in Austin this week and as I flew in and out of AUS, seeing this property made me wish I was staying here all over again! This is a top notch property!

“Is this really a Hyatt?” Requested a quiet room. I got one right above the railroad. They did accommodate a room change and gave me points for the inconvenience. My new room? Above the freeway! Their location is poor and noisy. Room service is extremely expensive (21% service charge) and had to return the full tray. Their coffee shop claims starbucks coffee, but it's not, it tastes bad. Valet parking is $20 a night and they take forever to bring your car! They have 6 elevators but had 3 stops everytime i took a ride and i was on floor 15. Maybe just 2 or 3 were functioning. Escalators from Lobby to 2nd floor was broken. If you need to connect your laptop, ipad, ipod and smartphone, bring your own extension, there is 1 AC outlet in the room and 2 in the bathroom. I read the hotel GM replies to concerns and i understand his philosophy and it shows on the level of this hotel....too bad.

“Great Choice” The rooms are very large for an in New York hotel. Stayed in a king room that had a sofa which converted into a bed. The bed was very comfortable. The room size gave room to live in while in the room. The bathroom was some what small but had a seperate dressing area. The tub was small. The whole facility was always clean and well maintained. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The location was just a few steps away from a subway station which made it very easy to get around the city. I would rate this a 4 star hotel and would stay here again.

“Better Places to Stay in Phoenix” I stayed here in the summer of 2003 because a friend had a free voucher. Visitors to Phoenix and Scottsdale, please note: there are MANY, much better resorts to stay at than this one. This is an old property, with some maintenance problems. The water features are nice, but just average for Phoenix. This resort is kind of far from most tourist attractions, etc. For the money (about $100 a night from Memorial Day to Labor Day), try the JW Marriott Desert Ridge (which is a beautiful new resort in north Phoenix). All of the Phoenix and Scottsdale resorts have water features and most have golf courses, too, so shop around. It is a buyer's market with resorts in Phoenix during the summer.

“Huge Disappointment - Won't Stay Here Again” While the lobby impressed, it was all down hill after that. The room smelled musty, the carpet was somewhat damp and the bathroom was decaying (toilet seat was all chipped up). Room service was slow and didn't have all the items we wanted. Contacting anyone was slow. The worst part was the night. There was a train going by that rumbled the room every 5 minutes or so. We had the worst sleep there. The last time we went to Baltimore, the Intercontinental was sold out, so we had to settle for the Hyatt, but after staying at both, we will be trading UP to the Hyatt from now on. What a let down for a hotel chain that we've always enjoyed.

“What Matters Most is What They Do When Something Goes Wrong” I booked at this Hilton for a very short (barely 24-hour) visit to make a presentation at a conference. While I was surprised that this Hilton's lobby isn't as opulent as others I've seen, I realized once again that what matters most are the facilities in general, the room and its cleanliness, and how the staff members conduct themselves when things aren't right. I checked in, the nice young woman found my reservation, and then she said, "My goodness. I see that the room we have set aside for you hasn't been readied yet by housekeeping. Let me check." She was embarrassed, as she should have been--it was 6pm!! Before she went to check, she said, "Please go over to the Starbucks and get a cup of coffee and a snack as a gesture because of the inconvenience; they will charge these to the front desk." When I did so and came back to the front desk, she said, "I'm going to give you an upgrade--to a King corner room--because we weren't ready for you when you arrived, and here's the coupon for free WiFi in your room." I was reminded that this kind of customer service is what really matters--and, of course, that the room is very clean, very large, and with a small balcony. In short, I'm very pleased with this Hilton, and if this young woman was any example, the management has done a tremendous job in hiring and training its staff.

“great place to stay” we had a weekend stay and had a great time. the room is spacious, and clean, the service is great. We are not sure about the decor style/color, but it is kinda fun to be there. We liked the location, it is a 3 min walk to Wholefoods and bars!

“Dowdy, overpriced, uncaring” My room was tiny, shopworn, and downright musty. But the real problem started at 9:30 when an apparently large group of people started partying in the adjacent room. They got progressively louder and louder, and the walls were so thin that I had no difficulty whatsoever following their every word. At midnight I finally got fed up with the gales of drunken laughter and called the front desk. They said they would "take care of it immediately." They did NOTHING. No one knocked on the room's door, and no one called, because I certainly would have heard it clearly. I spent an entirely sleepless night tossing and turning. The next morning my complaint to the front desk was greeted with a shrug. No regrets, not even a tepid apology. I put all of this down on the comment card provided and sent it to the corporate office. I got a form letter back two weeks later saying they were glad I had enjoyed my stay at the Driskill! Save your money. Get some sleep. Avoid the Driskill like the plague.

“Comfortable Hotel” I stayed here in November while visiting my daughter. My room was small, but comfortable. I found the staff to be helpful and friendly, which is always comforting. The fitness center was well equipped and convenient to use. We enjoyed dinner in the restaurant one evening, and had a great bottle of wine that was recommended. The hotels location is ok, we were able to walk to restaurants. Parking is expensive, but we were able to find a spot to park in the street. I visit D.C. quite often, and this hotel is on my list of favorites.

“Beautiful hotel, but service needs a bit of fine tuning” I recently stayed at the Intercontinental with my husband and 2-year-old. My husband was in Boston for a conference so we tagged along. The hotel is very nice and is especially geared for business traevlers. I wouldn’t describe the hotel as necessarily family –friendly, but we knew going in that it was more of a business hotel so that was o.k. The furniture in the room was very contemporary. Everything was very clean. The bathroom is very large and has a great separate shower. The room also included a very nice marble entry. Only downside to the room was the view, or lack thereof. We looked into the offices of the next building. (see picture). The location was great. We were only a couple of blocks from the children’s museum (highly recommended) and the Aquarium. The Boston Common, where we rode the swan boats, Fanueil Hall, and the Freedom Trail are also all within walking distance. In addition the South Station, with train and bus connections and a reasonable food court if needed, is only a couple of blocks away. The Convention Center is about a 15-20 min walk or a $7-9 cab ride. We walked to all the restaurants as well. Barking Crab was very good and fun. Legal Sea Foods is near the Aquarium. OK, but a local chain, so that was to be expected. Ate a couple of times at the Flour Bakery & Café, which is a couple of blocks behind the Children’s Museum. We saw it on the Food Network and it ended up being great for breakfast and lunch – excellent food, reasonable prices for a simple meal. There were three problems we came across at the hotel. All had to do with service. The first thing was that the service was slow at times. My husband grabbed dinner at the restaurant and the service was very slow. We also met someone in the lobby outside of the bar for a drink and the waitress failed to acknowledge us on several trips even though others were helped. Probably because we had a child with us, but that doesn’t mean we didn’t need a drink. The second problem was with one particular doorman, if you can call him that. Many times we would come through with a stroller, bags, etc. and he wouldn’t open the door for us. Sometimes he would say “hi,” but he would never offer assistance. Third, the concierge was very nice, but, when we asked for a child friendly recommendation for a simple restaurant the first night we were in (in need of a simple and quick meal where a potentially fussy child would not be an issue), we were sent to a higher end restaurant that looked very nice (and not child appropriate) with $40 entrees – this made no sense.

“Disappointing” My first impressions of this hotel were not good. The hotel has long-since sold its ground floor space for retail on the Magnificent Mile, and therefore you enter the hotel via a less-than-impressive small side entrance and have to wait for an elevator to the lobby on the 3rd floor. My suitcases were taken out of the truck of the taxi and I was handed the baggage receipt stubs - at no point was I given a choice about whether or not I wanted or needed assistance! Check-in was a disaster zone. I waited in line for 15 minutes, although people were cutting in and the check-in staff served them and didn't seem to care. Several guests in front of me were having problems checking in and I soon found out why - when I checked in, they mistook me for another guest in spite of having my credit card with my name clearly printed on it. My room was, in my opinion, very small, as was the bed, and only had a shower, no bath tub. After a long flight I had been looking forward to a bath, so this was also disappointing. The decor was dated, and I would not have wanted to stay more than one night. My room faced out onto the Magnificent Mile which, be warned, is very noisy! The Christmas shoppers were making a lot of noise when I arrived, and I was woken up regularly in the night by emergency vehicle sirens. Maybe Chicago needs to impose fines for noise during the night hours as they do in Manhattan? Of course, the proximity to the Magnificent Mile is also an advantage and you are in a great location with this hotel. Overall, I found this hotel disappointing compared to other Crowne Plaza properties and would not stay there again.

“Good clean rooms, but elevators are huge problem” This is a good clean place to stay. It is close to two convenient subway stations. The rooms are clean and decenly sized. The problem is the elevators are HORRIBLE. I waited at least 20 minutes, multiple times for an elevator. I'd keep looking if you're staying during a busy time. If however you want/need to be in the financial district, this is a great location, just avoid elevators during peak times.

“Great for a ball game but nothing special” Visited with my family to see a Tigers game and it was the perfect location -- two block walk to the stadium (and a nice stadium at that). The hotel was nothing special -- clean, basic rooms, small and occasionally crowded pool -- but everyone I met was attentive and friendly, including Darrell at the front desk. I would have probably given the hotel four stars instead of three if I had paid, say, $99 a night instead of the $179 (+ $20 parking) I did pay. I am sure that is dictated by the downtown Detroit hotel market but I considered the $225 total I paid for one night (no free breakfast) expensive for what you get. If you can get a good rate here however, I recommend this hotel, especially for Lions or Tigers games!

“4 night Stay” I stayed here on a 4 nights break from england and chose the hotel because i got a great deal through orbitz and wanted to stay central with a hotel brand. Union sq shopping wasnt my thing but it took 10-15 mins walk. The hotel is next to friscos landmark building the Transamerica pyramid which you cant appreciate until you view it from a distance. Chinatown in next door up a hill, broadway and the many adult clubs are like 2 minutes walk away ;) The hotel itself was clean as hilton standards expect, staff were always helpful giving directions etc. I got a 'bay view' room which was awesome, if i hadnt then i would have been faicing a building and oit would have been bland so request bay view. Room was spacious, had the usual amenities, bathroom was very nice and modern, shower great. Ididnt eat in the hotel but had a few late beers and the bar staff were nice and liked to flirt, expecially the women! Its a bit of a trek to fishermans wharf but an enjoyable walk. took 20 minutes to walk to pier 33 for the alcatraz ferry. use taxis if you must but you wont get the frisco experiance. I would stay here again definately as its far away from the castro area if you get my drift!

“Friendliest Staff in Chicago & Perfect Location!” Just returned from a 4 night stay at the Hampton Inn Majestic. The hotel is located directly above the Bank of America Theater (aka Lasalle, Shubert, & Majestic Theater at various times in it's history). We attended Jersey Boys (highlight of our trip!) which is playing at the theater. The hotel is also just a couple of blocks from Millenium Park and Grant Park, so we were able to walk to Taste of Chicago & the fireworks, so it was an ideal location for our trip. What Hampton Inn Majestic lacks is a grand entrance lobby, restaurants on site, a pool, and concierge. Our small travel group felt these "missing" items were more than made up by the hotel staff who were the friendliest and most helpful staff any of us have encountered in our travels! Everyone, from housekeeping to valet to front desk staff, went out of their way to answer questions and provide excellent service. The hotel has been open only a year or so. The rooms are fairly small and decorated in dark colors (carpet is brown, walls are burnt orange), basic but yet comfortable and functional. We all slept "heavenly" on the beds, and the pillows were the best we've had in a hotel setting. Soundproofing was extremely good for a downtown location in the Loop, which can be a problem for other hotels in the area. The breakfast in the lobby area was good, with typical fare for a complimentary hotel breakfast. Just a block or so from the hotel is Italian Village. It's kind of a landmark restaurant & recommended for that reason alone. The Palmer House Hilton is just a block away, so make sure you walk into the lobby to marvel at it's beauty. Macy's on State Street is a couple of blocks away---if you like to shop, make sure you go there, since it's the flagship location of the former Marshall Fields (boo-hoo). Take the escalators or elevators to the 7th floor and peer into the Walnut Room and go the Visitor's Center. If you're hungry for a relatively inexpensive lunch, try any of the restaurants on the 7th floor---a nice switch from some other fast food joints. I would recommend the Hampton Inn Majestic for anyone who wants a location in the Loop for business or pleasure. It's ideal for theater goers and for those wanting a location near Grant Park. The free trolley stops are only a couple of blocks away, and you can easily get around without a car.

“Same Four Seasons experience but rooms a little tired” I just returned from a quick one-nighter. This Four Seasons is everything Four Seasons is about except for one thing. The room decor is very tired looking. Nice bathroom with fresh orchids and marble top but the armoire was a very dull old wood and there was a regular TV in it and an old JVC boombox! This is 2009 for crying out loud. Besides the room being this way, the service was impeccable and everything else was beyond my expectations as it always is at any Four Seasons. I was told the room decor is 21 years old and they're hoping for a rennovation starting in June which keeps getting pushed back.

“100% Great Experience” This review is for a one night stay (March 3 - 4) in room #1128. Upon arriving at the hotel (friend and I walked from Powell Street BART Station), I immediately noticed that they had finally put a sign on the exterior (metal letters, set discreetly on the front of the building by the entrance). When we started walking past the tree pots set on the outside Geary Street wall of the building, my friend said, "I already think I am going to like this place" due to the understated but stylish exterior vibe. Upon entering the fantastically designed lobby, we encountered no line at check-in. My friend went off to ogle the spectatcular design elements while I dealt with check-in. The woman handling that was friendly and welcoming...in fact, none of the snottiness pointed out in some other reviews was encountered by us with any of the staff during this visit. But we are smiley, friendly people so maybe that's what we got back? Who knows -- I just felt very welcome the entire visit. We then took the opportunity to enjoy a drink in the Redwood Room before the party scene started -- it's a stunning space, and the redesign of several years ago was sympathetic and successful. Going when it is quiet may not be a party highlight, but it is certainly an opportunity to enjoy the magnificence of this space -- and a good cocktail! When we got to the room, we discovered that the management had delivered a bottle of sparkling wine (Gloria Ferrer blanc de noir) and a lovely flower arrangement, with their compliments. Most kind of them! Our purpose for coming to the Clift this time was to host a 40th birthday party for a friend, including 10 guests, so we had booked a 925 square foot one-bedroom suite with living and dining area. It was spectatcular -- very large, private, quiet and beautifully designed with loads of windows and large wall mirrors to keep things bright and several pieces of custom Phillipe Starck furniture that are unique to that room. There is an 8-place oval dining table covered with a custom cut piece of orange mirror glass. Wild! But very sophisticated, too. It's "freaky-chicy" as one of our guests said. The room service team arranged everything perfectly -- four hot appetizers had been ordered a week before-hand, as well as red wine glasses, Champagne flutes and iced Champagne buckets (we bought our own wine at the very well-appointed wine shop two blocks away -- Moet & Chandon White Star and Stags Leap Wine Cellars "Artemis"). By the way -- we got NO bad vibes at all about bringing our own wine and the people in room service, in the days before our arrival, were a pleasure to work with. We asked to have everything set up by 6:30pm and it was done by 6:40pm. Pretty good! The room is great for entertaining, and after two hours or so, we all left for the Vivienne Westwood party at the DeYoung Museum. Upon returning close to midnight, some of us enjoyed cocktails and appetizers in the Living Room area, which was dark and private -- the Redwood Room is a great place to party, but we were too pooped to deal with that scene. We slept soundly in the excellent bed and in the morning were shouting for joy over the strongest water pressure from a hotel shower either of us had experienced in quite some time! The bathroom has ample space for personal effects and the dressing room outside the bathroom has a table-with-mirror and huge closets for even more storage. We requested a late check-out at 2pm which was immediately approved. Then we went downstairs to enjoy our breakfast. The Asia de Cuba french toast was amazing -- it had a veritable mountain of whipped cream -- and bravo to the restaurant for also offering "design it yourself" egg-white omelettes for those of us fat-averse types! Breakfast was not cheap but we had a couple Mimosas, so it was our own fault! LOL And if you want cheap, there are a couple greasy spoons a block or two up Geary that serve good diner food (I think one is called the Olympic Flame and I've had good eggs-toast-and-bacon brekkies there). Check-out was a breeze and there were no "hidden charges" on the bill. Once again, the staff just could not have been more friendly -- even the cleaning staff one passed in the halls smiled and said "Hello." I had some fears about the complexity of the expectations I had of the hotel -- the food, getting it set up, making sure it was a memorable and flavorful 40th birthday for my friend -- and I just could not be more pleased. They got EVERYTHING right. I will most certainly be returning to The Clift....in fact, I have the same room booked for July 6! Good job to everyone at the hotel and thank you for making my friend's 40th birthday truly special.

“Typical Westin” Westin's are usually a good bet for a business hotel, and this was no exception. The staff were all very friendly. Service was good both in terms of room service quality, and in the restaurant. The $22 breakfast buffet is a bit over priced for what it is. The Corner Bakery, on the side of the hotel is equally good for much less and a much wider selection. But the price of the buffet breakfast was the only real draw back. The rest of our stay was pleasant, with no unexpected surprises or problems to make note of. The location is great in that you are only two blocks from Larimer Square, which has many great dining options. The Denver Visitor's Bureau and others will taut the 16th St. mall, which is in front of the hotel. It's nothing to get excited about. It's lined with touristy, semi-cheap stores and attracts a fairly large homeless population. Larimer Square is much nicer! If we were to return to this area, we'd probably come back to this hotel.

“Very Nice Hotel” I recently stayed at the Holiday Inn Express West Intercontinental located at 1330 N. Sam Houston Parkway East conveniently located near the George Bush International Airport. The hotel is very nice with comfortable rooms and wonderful front desk staff. The breakfast buffet is above standard for most Holiday Inn Express Hotels, and the restaurant recommendations are excellent I would highly recommend this hotel to either business or leisut=re travelers who want to be close to the George Bush International Airport.

“Lord, Don't Make Me Go Back to Hotel Hell” My employer booked this hotel for our entire traveling party via Priceline (I think). We had a crew of about 10 traveling to NYC to cover the Rangers playing the Yankees in the ALDS. The good: The location of the Roosevelt is great. Right in Midtown, near Grand Central (Hello, Joe's coffee!) near an Equinox at which I like to work out, nice little location. Granted, I'd prefer to be on the UES, but I digress. My maid, Bonaventura, was lovely. She cleaned the heck out of my nasty, crusty room and was as sweet as could be. That's about it. I'm a service gal I just like nice people. It's the Texan in me. The staff couldn't even muster basic niceties that a random cabbie in the city offers. Seriously. Front desk attendants wear buttons with the letters "WIT". I asked one what it meant and she replied "Whatever It Takes". That's supposed to refer to their willingness to be helpful and accommodating. Didn't happen. It would have made more sense had they worn buttons with the letters WTF because that's the attitude most of them had. The bellman did not offer to help us when got out of the cab. I don't care, I travel with just one bag but our photographers carry around 5, many of them weighing 50 pounds or more. No offer of help at all. I could go on: front desk people had nothing, upon checkout a woman refused to give me a receipt b/c we paid on Priceline. I just wanted the blank sheet in case my employer needed something for their records (you never know) and she fought me for 5 minutes! The bellman who held my bags for my after I checked out ASKED me to tip him before I even had the chance to get my money out of my purse. The valet asked if I wanted a cab (i usually just grab my own) I said yes, he goes to the street and starts talking to a town car driver about their night out the previous night. After 5 minutes I looked at him and he replies "It's not happening". No, it's not. The rooms apparently haven't been updated since 1947. They are small, have wobbly furniture and crunchy carpets. The bathroom was so small that the door hit me in the knees when I had to use the restroom, eclipsing the postage stamp sized Italian train, I once had to take. It had absolutely no counter space, save for a tiny little glass shelf. I had to put my products on the toilet seat to get ready. I could go on but don't want to relive the experience. The thing is the Roosevelt is always packed with a lot of overseas tourists and price-conscious travelers. It succeeds on price alone. I'm not sure what we paid but no doubt it was cheap. This hotel was at full capacity throughout our stay. Forget botox, it needs a full-on facelift but undoubtedly it will continue to operate with its wrinkly, shriveled miserably facade and terrible service.
“Solid” A good solid hotel, friendly staff etc. Poor breakfast but otherwise excellent!

“5 Stars. Best Memphis Hotel For All Around Value. My Favorite.” I have been to memphis about a dozen times and stayed in at least 9 different hotels - everything from roach motels for $20/night up to 5 star suites for upwards of $250/night. This is by far my favorite. I'm on the 2nd night of my stay and I don't have a single complaint so far. I booked on priceline (77, memphis east) and I would gladly pay $100. The value is fantastic here, especially when compared with the other hotels in the Memphis area. Check in was a breeze. You can either check in via an automated touch-screen kiosk right at the front door, or the "old fashioned way" at the front desk. The clerk was incredibly polite and actually stepped out from behind the counter to shake my hand and introduce herself and offer her services. I was very impressed. The lobby/foyer area is very handsomely decorated and comfortable, and also serves as a bar/lounge/breakfast area. My room was on the 4th floor and was very nice, much better than I had expected. I've stayed at the holiday inn, doubletree, 4 points Sheraton and Marriot and this was the best room. Very spacious - even with 2 beds. There is a large open area with wrap-around sectional couch, a wet bar with mini-fridge, desk, and a wall mounted (large) flat panel TV. The tv was very cool as it provides user friendly hookups for external audio and video inputs (VGA, SGA, HDMI, etc) and buttons to change the input. The bathroom is just the toilet and shower (shower by the way was very nice - great pressure and flow) and there is a 2nd sink and counter right outside the door. Beds were clean and comfortable, and I have yet to detect that awful musty smell that every hotel has in the world. The room was also absolutely immaculate Amenities were great. Free internet, free parking, and free breakfast buffet. Breakfast has fresh breakfast sandwiches, oatmeal, blueberry waffles, fruit, juices, and all the other breads and such. Haven't had to use the business center but it looked fine, and the fitness room was good as well (2 treadmills, an eliptical, and a bike - all with built in tvs). My only gripe is that the fitness center didn't have any weights or resistance equipment. The hotel is also located in a very nice area where I don't have to worry about the security of my vehicle at night - much unlike the rest of memphis. Also very easy to get in and out of (unlike the four points). Again - this has so far been my favorite hotel I've stayed at in Memphis and I plan on returning here many more times. I plan to speak with the manager before checking out to see about arranging a rate comparable to priceline's so I don't have to gamble on the bid process every time. For $77/night, this is the best value one can get in memphis.

“overpriced; thanksgiving day parade buffet nice;cust service could improve;” Arrived and room not ready by 3pm; was told to have drinks and snacks on the house while room worked on;( husband came later on in the evening) 2 daughters and I ordered tea and a snack tray for us to split; took about 45 min to be served our snacks/beverages. It ended up showing up on our bill at check -out;Room very small but nice; not thouroughly cleaned however; fridge covered in sticky spray and popcorn on floor, rug and on furntiture; not told about hotel accom. at check in so missed out on rules for using elevators at night-(need card to operate it); no coffee machine in room or comp. coffee in lobby which would expect for paying 1 K a night. gym just ok; nothing special and quite small; nice access to mall and shopping on lowever levels, however; no discounts or anything for stores in mall; nice location for madison ave and macys parade. we were repeadedly asked if we were staying at the hotel whenever we used facilities including elevators. this became annoying. ordered room service breakfast on thanksgiving day so that teenage girls could eat and get out to get spot for parade viewing; 100 $ for two mini sized cereal/milk ; one hot cocoa and one order of fresh fruit and one coffee; clean bathroom with nice bath salts,shampoos, etc.beds comfy; very tight space though for price paid. our anniversary and member of their frequent club but no upgrades provided. no free wi fi even! asked for and received a 2pm check out; got to room at 1:45 and maidsin room and cleaned bathroom and part of room already- some of our personal things like toothbrushes, makeup, etc tossed in garbage already. they were not notified of the late check out. so i was quite upset- wanted to use facilities and freshen up before our departure. this should NOT happen in a 5 star hotel.

“Lovely” The Eliot is the way all great boutiques should be. The staff exemplifies courtesy and graciousness. If you stay more than once, they somehow know your name when you arrive. The tiny but elegant lobby is a good indication of your stay - character, history, and intimate. The small older elevators are perfect - I love them because they remind me that I am not in a Marriot or a Hilton, but rather someplace different and special.. The rooms are tastefully decorated, well-sized (I've stayed in both the junior suites as well as the standard rooms), and very comfortable. I'd say this is my favorite hotel to come home to after a long days work or travel.

“Excellente situation et vue sur Central Park (en étage élevé)” Idéalement situé proche de Central Park, beaucoup de chambres offrent une très jolie vue sur le poumon de NYC. Hotel grand aux standards habituels Meridien. Pas le grand luxe mais pas de reproche majeur. Petite piscine sur le toit. Hotel très fréquenté par les sportifs de l'US Open. Pour un tarif en dessous de 200 euros la nuit, c'est très acceptable.

“Nichts besonderes aber okay, klassisches U.S.-Hilton” Relativ zentral gelegen, 10 Minuten zu Fuss vom Dupont- Circle oder noch näher an der Metro gelegen. Zimmer sind etwas klein, Badezimmer extrem klein, die Toiletten sehen aus als ob sie nachträglich ins Bad eingebaut wurden. Service ist sehr freundlich, es gibt eine Executive Lounge für Statuskunden von Hilton oder Gästen die auf dem executive Floor gebucht sind. Insgesamt ein sehr typisches Hilton in Nordamerkia, empfehlenswert.

“Ottimo hotel e posizione” L'hotel ha prezzi alti, a meno che non trovi qualche offerta (per questo ci siamo riusciti ad arrivare :) ). A 50 metri da times square, vicino ha tutto. Non vi allontanate troppo verso port autority (circa 100 metri) perchè di notte la zona non è ben frequentata, anche se ci sono molti poliziotti. Camere ottime, pulite e ottimi i prodotti da bagno. Bella la hall e i piani. Non ha internet gratuito, ma basta scendere in strada e trovate tutto.

“Decent - some good and some bad” Stayed at the Doubletree for one night. The good: Room is spacious - rather large for New York standards. Had a comfortable bed, nice desk, nice loung chair and a flat screen TV. The shower was wonderful, lots of pressure and hot water. The bad: Room was noisy. I could hear everything going on on my floor. Could hear doors slamming down the hall. So sound proofing is a big issue here. Secondly, the shades on the windows are bad. They do not completely block light coming into the window - there is a nice gap in between the shades. Thus, you can't get total privacy and block out light. Other bads, service was pretty terrible. Didn't get my wake up call. Unenthusiastic check in. Overall, if you need a clean bed and a hot shower, stay there, but otherwise, look around

“My Favorite Business Hotel in San Francisco” Listen, I've stayed at the Ritz and I'm sure the Four Seasons and Omni are nice as well, but I personally prefer the Meridien for it's low-key feel and Embarcadero Center location - plus if you're SPG, this is your best option in SF. The best description I can come up with is "just really, really nice." This hotel is nice and contemporary without being too cool for you like the W. Restaurant and bar are nice, and the staff are very friendly and helpful. Rooms are very nice and spacious, and the entire hotel is very well maintained. This is one of those hotels that you always feel glad to arrive at. The rooms facing the Bay have a partial view of Treasure Island, and the suites that face that way are amazing. I will always try to stay here.

“A Hidden Gem in Boston” I stayed at The Onyx Hotel for 7 nights in December 2005 for business. Since I was there for a conference, I spent a lot of time in my room afterward working on my computer. The walls were pretty thick which helps and the street noise was minimal. The Onyx is in an "Urban Renewal" type neighborhood, which is exactly the type of neighborhood I prefer over highly tourist-filled areas like those near Prudential center (Westin, etc). The T is right up the street and there are many restaurants and ammenities nearby (an Au Bon Pain is located directly across the street, a Dunkin Donuts 3 blocks away, multiple bars/eateries within 3 blocks). I did have one incident where there was a concert at nearby Fleet Center and drunken guests were throwing themselves against my door at 2:00am and carrying on like they were in a frat house. Management was quick to both acknowledge and apologize for the disturbance. The front desk staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The rooms are averaged-size (for an urban hotel) and very clean and comfortable. Housekeeping gets 5 stars. I had a Deluxe King smoking room, which was located on the second floor. Kimpton seems to be punishing us smokers more and more these days by providing fewer room choices and the worst rooms availale. However, I would stay at this hotel again.

“Inadequate dining facilities.” I just spent four days, three nights at the Loews Hotel in Philadelphia while attending a convention there. There was no question about where to stay because of the convenience of being in the same hotel where the meetings are held. The hotel was comfortable and clean, however I do have a few complaints. First of all, my family tried to get in touch with me and were told I wasn't registered there. They were almost frantic wondering what happened to me. I learned upon checking out they had my last name spelled wrong, which was really inexcusable because I gave them a credit card upon checking in and my name was clearly spelled out. Also upon arriving there I was told my room wouldn't be ready until 3:00 P.M. I said I really needed to get into my room because I am leaving for a city tour at 2:00 and after traveling for many hours to get there I would definitely like to freshen up before going on the tour. After I insisted, they did let me check in shortly before 2:00 P.M. My main complaint was the hotel only has one restaurant, Sole Food, which is small with a very limited menu and certainly not adequate to service all the hotel guests when the hotel is full. The first morning I had room service, which arrived on time and was very nice, but very expensive. The second night I found the maid had failed to leave a room service card to fill out and hang on the door to get breakfast the next morning, and as it was late I thought I would just call in the morning. The next morning it was raining buckets outside so I didn't want to leave the hotel for breakfast so I called for room service and was told they were running an hour and a half behind. I said that would be unacceptable as I had to be in a meeting within an hour. They suggested I go down to the restaurant for breakfast. When I arrived at the restaurant I found I was not the only person needing to eat. There was a long, long line and waiting list. I waited as long as I could and finally ended up asking if I could grab a muffin and be on my way as I could not wait any longer. They said sure, but they refused to put the charge on my room and I had to pay cash. (You'd think they would comp that since it was impossible to get anything to eat in the hotel.) That day I found a maid in the hallway and asked for a room service card. (They didn't automatically leave one). That night I filled it out and my breakfast arrived on time the next morning. A very important thing but I'm almost reluctant to mention because I can't prove it is that I became ill in the middle of the night on Friday night after eating food at a reception but served by the hotel. I only ate one meal away from the hotel and that was on Thursday and I felt fine all day Friday, but something definitely upset my stomach after that Friday night meal at the hotel. I would stay at this hotel again if I attend a convention there, but I would hope the weather would be nice enough to get out to get something to eat. In a four-star hotel you would expect adequate dining facilities.

“Loved It!” I travel to New York for business on a regular basis. I chose this hotel based on the reasonable rate and was very impressed! The room was spacious and clean. The decor is inviting and the furnishings are comfortable, clean and gorgeous (I really want one of those green velvet chairs for my home). The hotel has a classic feel but with modern upgrades. The bathroom was modern and clean. The elevator are very tiny as I have heard other travellers mention, but I did not find the wait to be long. What stood out for me? I found the staff to be friendly and helpful! Although this should be the case, it is rare in NYC in my experience. I was given prompt, accurate walking directions when I asked for them without a side order of attitude - thank you Warwick staff! I often find the restaurants in these older hotels very dark and uncomfortable. Although the walls in Randolph's are dark wood, the large windows overlooking Avenue of the Americas make every table in the room inviting, even when dining alone. Food was pretty good, especially the soup of the day (cauliflower). I worked in my room for several hours and found the desk and internet access met my needs very well. My room was on the 7th floor. This is lower than I would normally chose as street noise can be a problem in NYC but I found it was not an issue in this hotel. Did I mention the location? Very, very convenient! I actually had some shopping time on this trip and 5th Ave is very close by. I hope to make it to the Museum of Modern Art next time, which is across the street. Overall, this was a pleasant surprise. It is very well restored/ maintained and I hope to return soon.

“Convenient stay and decent service” Rooms are ok. Good location and convenient near the airport. Has a small bar with good food but its kitchen closes at 11, bar is good to unwind. Front desk staff can be very helpful and accommodating, or just not give a dam; depending on who you run into at the front desk. Big )++ for the outstanding shuttle staff willing to go the extra mile. BTW, rooms have paper thin walls and you can hear the conversations of people in the next room... and more. :) Room service was prompt and on the dot.

“The best part is the lobby!” This is a sexy hotel somewhat similar to the Ace but less authentically cool. My room here was tiny with an even tinier bathroom (the smallest I have encountered off an airplane). Most people staying at the same time as us appeared to be in their twenties and thirties and the restaurant was enjoyable with a great deals at happy hour. The front desk called several times to tell us we were being too loud, something that rarely happens at hotels. The location is less desirable than some and most rooms overlook a boring parking lot. The 24hr room service is extremely limited and takes about an hour to arrive. At one point our shower stopped working and we called the front desk who responded about an hour later and made the necessary adjustments. They provide lots of attractively packaged in room items with hefty price tags. If you want something like, say, a razor, call down to the front desk and they should have free ones... using the option available in room cost me nearly $20! However, the lobby is glossy, modern and really just too swanky.... it couldn't make a better first impression!

“Still Understaffed” Stayed here with wife for a convention. The hotel is huge with numerous outstanding amenities. The pool area may be oversized for the staff/plan, however. Like 2 previous stays here, the property is still understaffed and undertrained. In the summer, the Schlitterbahn-like pool area is a zoo with guests competing for the few poor overworked servers' attention. This was completely unlike similar resorts in Vegas, Phoenix, etc. where the service is practically falling all over you with help. Unfortunately similar issues with front desk and maid service not up to the standards of a destination resort hotel. So all of this tends to stress up your getaway time, especially considering the price and "resort fee" you're paying. Let's face it, most of us just want a comfortable spot to lounge with a book or adult beverage, without having to fight for it. As is written by others, the hotel is about 30 minutes from the River Walk, in a residential neighborhood on the outskirts of San Antonio. If you're taking a family trip, the Hyatt Hill Country (adjacent Sea World) or Westin La Cantera (adjacent Fiesta Texas) offer better locations. The JW Marriott is more of a golf/convention meeting hotel.

“The Most Elegant Hotel In New York” What can I say. This is the very best in NYC. My husband and I celebrated our anniversary at The Lowell. I will never forget it. Marble kitchen and bathroom, crystal, frette sheets, the hotel has a person that just changes the orchids in yoour room daily....our terrace overlooked The Pierre... Everything thing is just done in such good taste. It is perfection!

“The best hotel in America-redux” I have had the good fortune to stay in this wonderful property 6 times. I have been so spoiled by each experience that I am always terrified that there is no way it can live up to my expectations. I just spent 5 nights there with my 20 year old son (before he returns to college) and I'm delighted to report that, as usual, The Pen exceeded all of my expectations. This hotel has it all. An unbelievable staff, a phenomenal location, 4 great restaurants, a terrific bar, and perhaps THE best fitness center/pool in the world. The cardio machines are beyond state of the art and the pool is gorgeous and inviting. Every time you interact w/a Peninsula staff member, you are greeted with someone who meets your gaze and wishes you a good morning/afternoon/evening. These folks are genuinely vested in your visit and consistently go beyond and above the call to insure that all of your needs/wants are met. The staff, from the doorman to housekeeping to room service are all professional, warm, unpretentious, and wonderful. The director of guest relations, LeeAnn Brown, has become a family member and friend. She is genuinely concerned about our well being and has-miraculously- found a source for "Chuckles" which are sadly, very difficult to find for all but Ms. Brown. I travel a lot. Nobody but Ms. Brown has sought out and procured "chuckles" for me. Thank you! On this visit, we had a wonderful experience in the Shanghai Terrace and another in the street level restaurant. I'm really picky but this place is beyond the call. From the size and weight of the towels to the TV/radio in the bathrooms to the free wi-fi and water that is set out for you each night, this is THE place you want to come home to. I cannot recommend any property, anywhere, with greater enthusiasm than I do the Chicago Peninsula.

“空港の直ぐ傍で夜遅くとか朝早くのフライトを利用の際には大変便利です。” Sheraton hotelは時々利用しているが、空港からのシャトルサービス(無料ー荷物あるときにはTip 一ドルをドライバーに渡すとよい)。スターウッドメンバーであれば、最上階にあるラウンジで簡単な朝食とドリンクも。 ベッドも大きく長時間のフライトの疲れを取るにはお勧めです。 ホテル内にはレストランも数件、小さいショップもあります。 急ぎで市内に泊まる時間の無い時には、ホテルでの打合せにも利用しています。 ビジネスマンであちらこちら飛び回る方にもお勧めホテルです。 車で迎えに来て貰うにもわかりやすい場所にある。

“Excellent hotel” This hotel is a very classy establishment near South Station and China Town. The rooms are large and very modern, with nice touches such as an iPod dock. The hotel has an excellent gym and good bars/restaurants.

“So nice to find a quiet hotel in NYC!” I stayed at this hotel last October, and it was a true delight. A friend and I took a taxi from JFK, and although the driver had issues finding the hotel, we were able to get there pretty quickly. Our room wasn't available when we arrived (roughly 8am), so we got excellent directions from the front desk clerk and headed uptown to see about getting SNL tickets. The hotel held our bags for us, and allowed us access to a nice bathroom to change clothes and freshen up in. Our room was really nice with 2 comfortable double beds and it overlooked a patio area at the end of the block. What amazed us most is that it was so quiet! After staying in midtown and Chelsea on previous visits, it was a nice change! (I should note that we stayed there on a Saturday night, so it was pretty slow on that end of town.) We were able to take public transportation around the city very easily from here. Wonderful hotel, I'd stay here again in a heartbeat! I really liked the Andaz's modern touches and amenities. As a younger traveler, I greatly prefer hotels like this to the stuffier hotels like the Waldorf.

“Gem in Times Square” This is my favorite New York hotel. It can be a bit pricey, but is a lovely, very safe property. Their customer service is excellent and you absolutely cannot beat the location. Very close to the subway, Broadway and some excellent restaurants.

“Enjoyed the stay very much” We came to Philly to see My Fair Lady, and booked a package rate at the RC for $389 which included bfast for two and a $50 dining credit. From the moment we drove up to the hotel to the moment we left, service was excellent, and fully met our expectations from an RC. Was the best ever customer service we got? No. But I'd be overly picky if I were to be critical. Everyone was very courteous and friendly. The room we had was a corner room XX02, so there was lots of light. It was spacious too. The furniture was good quality. Color scheme subdued yet classy. Bathroom was large, with separate shower and bath. Toiletries first rate with Bulgari. Flat screen TV, likely 32 inch. Wired and wireless internet. Two phones, one cordless. Coffeemaker in room, and lots of (we hope) complimentary bottled water. In-room safe. Some furnishing not 100% perfect, as the photos may show, with one a/c vent loose and some wires dangling from the shades in the bathroom. But really, folks, nothing really serious. The room was very nice. Turndown service came when we were still in the room, but the nice lady offered us chocolates. With a smile. We had dinner at the Grill. First rate. Menu was simple. But very nicely done. Service was very good. Breakfast also at the Grill. Can't complain. Lobby is being renovated right now. But we knew that going in. All in all, a very good stay.

“rock solid business hotel” i got this hotel through priceline. the site puts it in dupont circle, but it is actually a metro stop away, a good 20 min walk probably. this is a convention hotel. it is big. service is polite, efficient and quick. the rooms are not the newest, but are kept very clean and nice. the bathroom is a bit on a small side. there is nothing particularly great about the room, but nothing bad either. the common areas are huge, as this hotel was built for volume. i got lost once going to my room. all in all, rock solid.

“No longer on my list of SF hotels” The hotel itself is just fine and the staff is polite and helpful. Rooms are noisier than the average SF hotel. Regardless of which street you face, noise loud enough to wake moderately heavy sleepers continues until the wee hours and begins 5-6am. The breakfast is as sparse as others have commented, but that was never a problem for me. The problem is the neighborhood. I travel on business to 8-12 cities a year and always ride public transit at these locations. I am not easily made uncomfortable even though I am something of a target because I'm obviously a visiting businessman with a laptiop slung over my shoulder everywhere I go. When I stayed at the Bijou 1/2004 and had employees stay in 2004 and 4/2005, they commented that the area was rough but manageable. If you walk straight up Mason towards Union Square, then you aren't going to have many problems once you make it a couple of blocks. The walk to/from Powell St. BART is edgy and the walk to Mosconi Center is edgier still. And even the hotel staff warns against walking the other two directions (the front desk clerk scratched it out in red pen on the map when I checked in and I didn't even ask since I travel here all the time). I am not talking about panhandlers, which are everywhere and do not bother me. This is another matter altogether. For an extra 10-15%, stay in another hotel in this boutique chain called the Maxwell Hotel, just a few blocks closer to Union Square.

“Decent Location” We walked to Independence Mall, and decided a closer location would have been nice. Self-parking (we saw no sign of valet being available) was difficult. The tower is tall and narrow. Finding a spot and navigating the other cars exiting were equally difficult. The "welcome cookies" we were given at checkin really are a nice touch and were delicious. Our room and beds were very comfortable. Unfortunately, the pool was closed for painting, so our children were disappointed. We got this hotel for a great rate through Hotwire, and were very happy with the value.

“Perfect location - lovely hotel” This hotel is perfectly located for exploring the interesting city of Seattle, about half-way between Pioneer Square and Pike Place Market and only two blocks from the waterfront. The hotel is in a lovely old building and the rooms are decorated beautifully. My room , 401, looked out over 1st Avenue. If you keep the windows closed, you will not be bothered by the busy traffic below. If you want to keep the windows open, ask for a room away from that street. My room had a living area with a fireplace, couch, two chairs, coffee table and a second TV. It was very nice, although somewhat dark because the room was a narrow rectangle with windows at the narrow end. Fortunately, there were plenty of lamps. The bathroom was not large but was adequate and was nicely equipped with a great showerhead. Towels were thick and fluffy. I have learned that I must ask to have a coffee maker brought to the room as they are not furnished as a standard feature. I also always have to ask to have more than the one or two coffee packets provided each day. The staff was friendly and efficient and responded promptly to any request. The breakfast, which was not included in the room rate, was first rate. Because the servers at breakfast do double duty as hosts/hostesses, on two of my three mornings there I had to wait for some time for someone to acknowledge me and seat me, because they were busy serving people or in the kitchen. A host/hostess would be nice. This was only the second Kimpton I have stayed in and I am quite impressed with the level of service and the uniqueness of the properties. You never feel like you are staying in a large chain hotel. I highly recommend it.

“Return guest, would go again” I am a return guest to this location. Rooms are modestly updated. Clean, good AC, comfy beds. A bit overpriced as there are no frills, but for the location you really can't beat it. Good pool as well. I did not have a car, but it is mandatory valet $12 per night. Most of downtown is pay parking though. 1 block from Capital, 5 blocks from 6th street bars and 12 blocks from south of campus, you really can't go wrong. Service was friendly. Stock up on water or pop and bring your own as the machines are always sold out, and it was 100 degrees to have no water bottle! The closest quick stop is about 4 blocks away.

“"SITUATION ET PRESTATIONS EXCELLENTES"” Nous sommes arrivés le matin à 10H et nos chambres étaient prêtes. L'enregistrement a été rapide et avec le sourire. La chambre est spacieuse avec deux grands lits, un coin salon et un bureau avec vue partielle sur le parc Millénium. La salle de bain est également très grande avec douche et baignoire ainsi qu'un peignoir! La cerise sur le gâteau est la cafetière Nespresso avec ses capsules renouvelées chaque jour et gratuitement.La concierge est là toute la journée pour vous conseiller quoi visiter et où manger. Elle se charge également des réservations. La situation centrale de l'hôtel permet de visiter la ville à pieds. Nous avons loué une voiture pour passer une journée en dehors de la ville et le hic était le prix du parking: $54 par jour. Un plus pour le Bar Eno où nous avons dégusté d'excellents vins. Leur cave a une renommée internationale. Nous avons quitté l'hôtel une nuit plutôt pour partir à New York. Une surcharge de $150 nous a été alors facturée, mais remboursée après un mail de réclamation :)

“GREAT LOCATION, decent, if average hotel” We stayed here for a long weekend in July 2010. You can't beat the location! Very close to subway stop, Central Park, shops. The hotel isn't very close to alot of great restaurants, we found ourselves heading over to 42nd St area for something decent to eat after 9pm. Lobby was busy, decor is nothing special. Only 2 agents working the front desk, surprisingly since hotel was quite busy. We stayed in a newly "renovated" room which was very nicely laid out, beds were extremely comfortable. My only complaint was the bathroom size, no room to put your toiletries around the sink area, and door JUST about closed around the toilet. The shower, suprisingly, was very nice sized!!! But no tub, so that means no place for us ladies to rest your foot to shave your legs! We put a request in online BEFORE we checked in for extra towels through Hilton website, and of course, never got the extra towels, and had to request them at the front desk again.

“Super Service, Great Location” My husband, myself and my two older children stayed at the Monaco over Christmas, and were totally delighted with the service. It seems as if the hotel's employees truly enjoy working there - they not only are consistently upbeat and friendly, but they really go out of their way to ensure your stay is pleasant. The decoration is true to the photos - funky, and distinctively Monaco. The only negative for my family and myself were the beds - they were not particularly comfortable, and the feather pillows were really flat, as if they were lacking in feathers. We've stayed at the Brown Palace in the past, and think that the Monaco is more conveniently located to the theater, Larimer Square, Lodo, and just generally in a nicer area. All in all an almost perfect stay!

“Enjoyed my stay!” The room was clean. The bed very comfortable. No backache. The A/C fan stayed on all the time. No on and off to wake me up. The staff was friendly and helpful. Told us about a Chinese restaurant and printed out a map. The welcome key packet had a list of restaurants within walking distance. The breakfast was good. Cereal, toast, bagels, waffles, juice, fruit, hard boiled eggs, etc. The grounds were well kept. The parking spaces were a bit narrow.

“History and Wi-Fi” My stay in the Palmer House was memorable, in part because they just don't make hotels like the Palmer House anymore. Watch the hotel TV channel for a fascinating account of the hotel's history. I also very much liked the free Wi-Fi (and the price I got by bidding on priceline). Lastly the doormen are very friendly and helpful.

“Decent stay- could be better” Don't worry about the very busy gas station that shares a drive w/ the property- I was a little concerned, but very few people cut thru the parking lot, plus there's a security guard on duty after 11pm. The property is older, & shows its age. There were a few broken floor tiles, & most everything needs updating. Bed & pillows were comfy, ac was cold. Room had an odor to it, like stale cigarette smoke. Not overpowering enough to change rooms, but it was noticeable. Carpet looked like it needed vacuumed. Breakfast was slightly less than at most Fairfields, but was ok. Staff very friendly. With a little updating the property could be great, but was good enough that I would stay again. There's a cheddars restaurant/bar across the street that's open late.

“have stayed for a week/year for 10 years and love it” We have stayed here for a week in October each year for 10 years and love this hotel. Four Seasons just knows how to run a great hotel, even though it sways in the high wind. Best in town, we think. Love the rooms and restaurant and spa.

“LOVED this beautiful hotel!” Wow- I wasn't expecting much when we pulled in but when I stepped inside my jaw dropped. A gorgeous lobby that has been designed with dark wood and contemporary furniture and carpet. Room was beautiful - big, comfortable bed with fluffy duvet. Awesome bathroom with modern stand-up shower and sink. Room included a nice refrigerator and was so clean. This is everything the Chicago Downtown Marriott should've been. My only complaints are that we were really looking forward to hitting the pool and hot tub after a long, cold drive from Chicago and their pool and hot tub are OUTSIDE on the roof and only available in summer! That was a huge disappointment. The other one was the lack of any standard pub-type food in-house. The weather was awful so we stayed in for dinner. We thought the bar would offer more laid-back options but the menu was just as snotty as the snotty restaurant. The food was nice but hardly comforting or filling. I went upstairs to check out the in-room dining menu for a late snack and it was more of the same.

“A true 5 star experience !!” What can I say; anything less than 5 stars just wouldnt be fair. I stayed the last weekend in May and as a Platinum Ambassador member, I was upgraded to a lovely suite overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The staff were all consistent in their level of impeccable service and respect without that stuffiness, sometimes apparant in 4-5 star hotels. It would be unfair to pick out one exemplary staff member as everyone was exemplary from the time I arrived to when I finally departed. The Valet service for my car was always speedy. The room and its furnishings were top notch. The bed was one to die for, I even checked what brand the bed and the topper were as I want the same for home. Well done IC-CC, I will be back !!

“great value and big rooms for NYC” I stayed here with a friend of mine. Very good value for New York City. The hotel was getting a bit of an external face lift but it caused no inconvenience. Great service, quick check in and check out and ideal location. I recommend this place and the doubletree on 51st and Lexington for good value and location in NYC. This is a great place for business or just having fun in New York. It would not be my first pick for a couples getaway but really - no complaints.

“Excellent Stay, should be much higher in ranking!!” We stayed at this property for 4 nights the end of October with our two older kids. Our entire experience was really, really good here. It is a convention center hotel and you do have to pay for things that come standard at other hotels, but the location, the staff and the hotel itself really can't be beat. We also got our stay at a fantastic rate of $160/night via Priceline. Our room was 907 and faced the interior (not the street) so it was VERY quiet. The room had been recently renovated (most of it) and was really, really clean! It is older and the bathroom fixtures and tiles showed some wear, but again it was really, really CLEAN. The staff couldn't have been nicer at all times. We arrived about 11:30 p.m. and the staffer behind the counter was counting cash. I said, "should we step to the next person?" He quickly put the cash aside and said, "No problem at all, I can help you!" He also gave us a room with a fridge for no charge when I inquired if any were available...how nice was that??!!! The hotel roomkeepers did a great job, too, and left whatever supplies (Keurig coffee and creamer, more shampoo) that we said we needed. We did leave tips for them, but not huge ones. There was always someone available in the lobby to answer our "how do you get to??" questions, and they were always sooo nice! The lobby is really jazzy and contemporary, the rooms are a bit more standard, but still nice. The metro is within a couple of blocks, the White House is a 10 minute (at most) walk. GREAT location.

“Nice, but rather corporate Westin” I stayed in The Westin Market Street on November 23rd for a pretty good non refundable internet rate of $129 through the hotel website. However, if it hadn't have been for the fact we were just three stays off making Platinum with Starwood, I would have preferred to have paid less than $100 using Priceline for an equivalent 4* hotel. This is a perfectly acceptable nice, clean and comfortable corporate hotel but there is no wow factor about it at all. The decor is all a bit grey and gloomy and lacks the charm of many Westins, although it is no where near as dismal as the recently renovated Westin Galleria in Dallas (which I have also reviewed). The room and bathroom are well sized and from the Starwood Preferred Guest Floors, you get very good views of the city. It is conveniently located a block away from the Bart, MOMA and The Moscone Centre and two blocks from Union Square. If you are attending a convention at the Moscone Centre then it is ideal, but I would not recommend it for romance or fun and would suggest the more historic Westin St Francis on Union Square instead, or one of the many chic city centre boutique hotels (eg The Hotel Monaco or Palomar). I will say though, all the staff were extremely nice, friendly and helpful.

“Good hotel” The main drawback was the location. Close enough to the airport to hear the noise and it's kind of in the barrio. Everything else was great. Breakfast was decent and hot. The staff was helpful. The rooms were very nice. I would stay her again if I had a car to get around.

“Very Nice but not crazy about the Location” I got this hotel off of Hotwire. It was a great price and it said it was downtown. If it was downtown, it must have been on the very edge of downtown. It was just over 2 miles away from US Airways Arena. I was hoping to be within walking distance of downtown activities but could not due to the distance. The hotel does offer a shuttle service that will take you to downtown and pick you up. The driver was really cool. I wish I could remember his name. We talked basketball during the drive to and back from the arena. He also worked at the front desk. The staff at the hotel was really nice. I needed to purchase something out of the gift shop which was closed and the first desk made a quick call and they opened it for me. Room service was fast. I placed a breakfast order late in the morning, and my food was there in less than 20 minutes. I enjoyed the bed and my room was very clean. The parking garage is a little funny. When first parking in the garage, I found the setup a little confusing. They share the garage with a few businesses nearby. All in all, I enjoyed my stay but I was not too crazy about the location. There was a BBQ place within walking distance but that was about it. You need a car, use the shuttle, or catch the Light Rail that's across the street if you want to do anything outside of the hotel.
