“Friendly, clean and comfortable place to stay” I spent 3 nights in the Hyatt and was very pleased with the accommodations, the staff's friendliness and the cleanliness and comfort of the room. The room was more a small suite with a sitting area separated from the sleeping area by a half wall. A nicety was the traveler's size tube of toothpaste I found waiting fro me in the bathroom, one that was replenished twice during my stay. Breakfast was very good, offering an array of cold cereals and hot foods. The property is conveniently located near the Hwy 183 and Mopac which gets one into the downtown area in about 15 minutes (barring any traffic problems) There's also a small shopping mall which houses the Mighty Fine Burger restaurant which is worth the visit especially if you like thick milk shakes like they used to be made in the "old day."

“Not up to Westin standard” My husband and I stayed at the Westin for 1 night on our annual trip to take in some Seattle Mariners games. We have stayed in many downtown Seattle hotels, and this was the most disappointing one we have encountered. As Starwood Preferred members, our king room was upgraded to one with a view of the water, but on checking in at 5 p.m. we were informed that our room was not ready yet, as the people in the room from the night before had not left it yet, though check-out time was 3 p.m. As we were on our way to the ball game that evening, we just wanted to drop our things off in the room and head out for dinner, so we opted to take a room with 2 double beds rather than wait for the king room to be available. Disappointing, but not a big deal. The biggest disappointment was the cleanliness, or rather lack of, in the room. There was a used bar of soap in the bathroom, hair all over the bathroom floor, a layer of dust on the telephone - the room had not been cleaned thoroughly at all. When we checked out and went to get our car from the valet, we handed over our ticket and waited 20 minutes, but no car appeared. We finally questioned the valet attendant, and it turned out that he had simply forgotten to ask someone to get our car, which was then retrieved promptly. There are many hotel options in a similar price range in the downtown area that I would recommend over this one. We will not stay here again.

“Two nights at the Copley Square” We recently spent two nights at the Copley Square hotel. We stayed in Boston for 2 nights on our own prior to a business meeting I had which required me to switch to another hotel. Overall, the Copley is very nice; although a little difficult to get to if you are unfamiliar with Boston! Staff was very nice. Checkin was a breeze. The room we had was a little on the small side (think NYC-sized rooms) but the bed was extremely comfortable and the room was clean. The bathroom was very small as well; no room to put your toiletries. Our room did not have a tub; only a walk-in shower but the shower was nice. We had continental breakfast included with our room, which was pastry/fruit/juice/coffee. Good enough; prices would be a little steep if you were actually paying for breakfast. Be aware that valet parking is costly; again, think NYC prices. We did enjoy our stay and would consider a return stay if we were to return to Boston.

“Great service, a bit islolated location” Overall, I experienced a great stay at this hotel during a recent conference. The staff was helpful, by room was clean and comfortable and the food during conference was great. The only negative was the relatively isolated location. I am a big fan of walking, and you really needed to take a cab to get to town (although it is an easy walk from the airport). The hotel itself is clean and up to date. I was given a small suite with a little balcony where I could see downtown and the water through the trees (I was on a low floor). The bed was the usual very comfortable sheraton bed, and the linens were clean and fresh. Lunch at the hotel restaurant was tasty (I had a nice seafood cobb salad), but everything on the menu is $15-$20 for lunch before drinks, tax and tip. There are no other options to dine nearby, other than walking to the airport for fast food. The other hotel facilities were good. The gym contains several bikes, treadmills and ellipticals, as well as weight machines. The pool looked great. Lots of places to sit. There is a very nice club level lounges, with a great view. The lounge included cold breakfast choices each morning (cereal, oatmeal, pastries, fruit and cold cuts). Unlike some other Sheratons I visit, there were no hot choices. There is a free shuttle from the airport, and it is only about a 10 minute walk, so I did not experience parking. It looked like overnight parking was around $20. The property itself consists of several buildings, so the experience might depend on which building you end up in. The main tower houses the restaurant, bar, lounge and a much nicer gym than the other tower. The other tower is not right next door- it is a bit if a hike. There are also some annex buildings where the rooms have exterior corridors and doors. The overall value varied. My conference rate was over twice the auto club rate I paid the final night., so check around for deals.

“Small, tired rooms, but decent staff and a good location” I stayed at Hotel 57 during January's Snowmageddon. On the whole, I found the staff to be equal parts delightful and helpful. The rooms, on the other hard, are a bit banged up and poky. Upon check-in, I was upgraded to a larger room because so many rooms were unoccupied. All I have to say is that if this is what passes for a larger room, then I would hate to see how small the smaller, normal rooms must be. One other quirk: the room I was put in had no in-room safe. When I reported this to one of the receptionists, I was told that there should be one in there. Odd. By the way, there might be some collusion between the doormen and certain cab drivers. One driver, who gets a lot of business from a certain doorman, immediately pressured me to agree to a flat rate $30 fare to LGA. The doorman told me that I should be suspicious of anyone who tries to charge me any more than $30; that $30 should be about right. Given the agreement between the sums quoted by the two gentlemen, I wonder if the doorman isn't getting a cut of that $30 to keep referring fares to the driver in question. Now, I know that it isn't unusual for cabbies to give themselves a bit of an income boost by doing off-meter runs, but this seemed to be a bit too cute by half. I wonder if the fare would have been any less had I told the cabbie to run the meter?

“Recently renovated Marriott property nice choice for Manhattan's mid-town East side” I attended a conference at this property. The hotel rooms and common areas obviously have been fairly recently renovated. The rooms are actually quite spacious for New York (where a walk-in closet is the usual rule of the day). Front desk, concierge, bell and housekeeping staff are attentive and friendly. There are many key attractions, great restaurants and world class shopping in the immediate environs. The 525 Lex lounge is cheerful, with great bar service. Depending on ones proclivities, the call girls at the bar may be either an annoyance or a welcome "feature."

“Esteticamente perfetto” è veramente un hotel bellissimo, se vi piace lo stile moderno. Ristrutturato da Stark pochi anni fa, è quantomeno da visitare per scattare due foto. Se si è clienti dell'hotel si ha accesso alla veramente splendida terrazza che si affaccia sul fiume. Questa è dotata di amaca, lettini, poltrone e via dicendo. Veramente bella. L'unica pecca, a mio avviso, sono le camere: o spendi molto e prenoti una camera superior oppure ti ritrovi in una camera che io definirei più che altro un loculo. Non c'è lo spazio per una valigia, figuriamoci due. Ecco, se avete problemi di claustrofobia o pagate di più oppure cambiate albergo, è il mio consiglio. Le camere superior invece di spazio ne hanno davvero molto, forse anche un pò troppo rispetto al necessario. I bagni sono comunque piccoli e poco arredati. Secondo me hanno risparmiato molto sull'arredamento delle camere da letto. Il ristorante/sala delle colazioni è fenomenale, con armadi alti fino al soffitto, che è altissimo. Pietre a vista. La stanza con il biliardo/biblioteca è altrettanto gradevole. Così come la hall. Insomma andatelo almeno a vedere! è vicino a Central Park, in linea d'aria è parallelo più o meno alla 5th ave, all'Apple store.

“Comfortable stay......” I recently stayed here for one night last week. My flight was earlier than expected so I proceeded to the hotel in hope's of being able to check in. The front desk gentleman was very kind and attentive. He gave me a room on the second floor and I was given a breakfast voucher as I was there early enough to have breakfast. The hotel is a smaller Hilton property, feels more like an Embassy Suites to me. The halls were clean and well kept. The breakfast buffet can be upgraded for 5 dollars if you are a gold member, which is a really good deal. No such thing at the Union Square property. The location of this hotel is great and it was the first time I have stayed near the wharf. It felt more like a neighborhood to me. There is a Safeway and a Trader Joe's walking distance and of course you have all the tourist traps (wharf) two blocks north. You can also catch the Powell trolley that will take into downtown (short walk from hotel). Overall a very good stay and I would certainly consider returning. I did noticed that the shower head was broken and I didn't mind since I was there for one night. However, management should inspect the rooms. The other thing that needs improvement is the internet access. No wi-fi in room and speed of access in the lobby was not much better. The connection felt more like dial-up than DSL. It may have been that they were upgrading their TV systems to serve more HD channels. However, if you are staying there for business, you may want to inquire about the speeds. It certainly was an inconvenience for me.

“Great place” I travel a lot and stayed here on business. The hotel staff is quite friendly and helpful, the adjoining restaurant has excellent service and food, and the location couldn't be better. The hotel is steps from the Farragut West Metro stop. Yes, the room is small, but it's efficiently designed, as is the bathroom. Plumbing was modern, linens were excellent, mattress was very good, and I heard no hallway noise. Outstanding hotel.

“Roomy and Relaxing” Spent a week here on a time share exchange the week before Xmas and enjoyed every minute of it. It was dark when we arrived, but the resort was colorfully decorated for the holidays. Check-in took less than a couple minutes and we were on our way to our 2-bedroom unit for some much needed rest. The suite seemed very new and was spotless. Each bedroom had a king bed, comfortable bedding, and lots of storage space. The main bedroom had a large soaking tub along with a separate large shower. The suite had three flat-screen TV's each with a DVD player. Lots of channels along with a few HBO and Encore channels. The kitchen is functional with full-size frig (there's a small one in the guest bedroom), microwave, full stove & oven, dishwasher, and washer/dryer. They give you enough dishwasher soap, but you'll need your own laundry detergent. A nice touch was a water feature on one of the walls which added to the relaxing ambience. We were on the first floor so we were only steps from our car in the parking lot. The property itself is quite large. To the east (which is the direction our villa faced) is a golf course and the JW Marriott is probably less than one mile away. To the north is some more of the golf course and some desert landscape. To the west over a wall are some homes, but you hardly notice them. To the south, they've begun construction on the next phase of the resort so I would imagine the villas at that end will be somewhat noisy in 2008. The hotel provides a regular shuttle to the JW Marriott and Desert Ridge Marketplace. The small gift shop really has very little in it. There's also a nice pool area with two waterfalls, whirlpool, large scale chess set, outdoor barbecues, playground, grass volleyball court, pool table, and ping pong table. There is something scheduled at the resort every day for every age group so you can choose whatever you might be intrested in. Being so close to the Desert Ridge Marketplace was a big plus. We ate there, shopped groceries there, saw movies there, and did a little last minute holiday shopping. The resort is close to the freeways, but still feels like it's in a very quiet area which was nice. We all really enjoyed our stay and I'd strongly recommend this place.

“Needs Major Renovation” We have a lot of family in Philly, so visit often. Tend ot stay at the Starwood properties as I think they are the best. Westin and Le Meridien are A+, and Society Hill Sheraton is pretty good, love that location. This Sheraton however is the weakest of the bunch. It's a large, convention style hotel, but needs a lot of renovation. The arrival experience is poor, the driveway is not particularly attractive and the main entrance doors are not befitting an important upscale hotel. The lobby and rooms are just good enough, but rooms need better TVs. You can't check into a Sheraton at the end of 2011 and still have old tube TVs. The gym and pool however are abysmal. Low-end YMCA quality. Ownership needs to renovate ASAP.

“Nice upgrade” When we arrived we were immediately y assisted with our luggage and it was taken to our room as well. Check-in went smooth by forthcoming staff. Due to my Diamond Hhonors status we were upgraded to a 2-room suite. It had a wet bar with fridge and microwave, a living room with sofa and chairs and a bedroom with good quality King bed. The bathroom was fantastic, spacious with a separate shower (with an enormous rain shower unit) and a whirlpool (seemed new). From our windows we had only view on roofs, but we didn’t mind at all, we were very pleased with our upgrade. There is a relaxing pool area with 3 pools and comfortable sun beds with thick cushions. It can be crowded with many children playing around. We had dinner in the café, they had only simple meals, but it was reasonable priced. The waitresses were very friendly. In the morning we had breakfast in the restaurant. They have a good breakfast buffet. When we were there we only got vouchers for a continental breakfast, so we had to pay extra for the buffet (this is the first Hilton where we had to pay!). I do hope that they have changed this policy for Diamond (or Gold) HHonors members

“decent hotel with some drawbacks” Check in was helpful but the first room they gace me had not been cleaned. The key didn't work for the second room. The room itself was small but comfortable. The views of the city were nice as the fog rolled in. This is a big inner city hotel. Noise comes with the territory. The location is great for buses or cable cars. Buy your passes from the gift shop. Hotel had good security. This is an adequate hotel when you want to be right in the city. Upper floors not facing Van Ness are less noisy

“Great Value” Great price for a small apartment type room. You get way more than a standard hotel room for the same price. Quality room with nice amenities...just make sure you ask for a non-smoking room/floor.

“Great concept, horrible execution” The hotel itself is fine. The property, while maybe not as lush as the pictures on the website show, is fine. The location is great, and despite "Sugar's" being next door doesn't really feel unsafe. However, I have never stayed at a property of this size that didn't have management on site 24 hours. This proved to be a major problem. Returned to the hotel after seeing a concert at Stubb's in Austin. The key didn't work to our room. This shouldn't be a big deal, however it was after 11 pm and there was no one in the front office to assist in getting a replacement key. Was given 2 keys at check-in, of course the first one worked fine, but the other was still in my wallet, so I didn't bother grabbing the other. This isn't the first time, and certainly won't be the last time I've been given a key that didn't work. This was the first time I wasn't able to get a replacement. It was roughly 12:30 AM, had a dead phone after spending most of the day in Austin. I literally had to kick-in the door to the hotel room. This may seem drastic, however there weren't any other options. Once I was able to access the room, did call the number they give in case of after-hours emergencies. The person answering was extremely unprofessional, and gave no indication that they were employed by the hotel. After the frustration, didn't even stay the night.

“Great .. will definately stay again” WJ is an excellent hotel for budget travellers. Its in a superb location.. agree it is a little noisy, but hey, its NYC! If its peace and quiet you want, you're in the wrong city! Just use ear plugs at night and you're fine. WJ has everything you want for a great stay in Manhattan.. *very* comfortable **huge** bed (we had Deluxe room - 387). Nice, warm bathroom with very powerful shower and gorgeous, thick, white towels. Staff very friendly, welcoming and polite. We had a great time at this hotel and will definately stay there again.

“Great location” I stayed here right after 9/11 when it was under different ownership and was very impressed with this hotel. I wasn't disappointed this time around. The rooms are gorgeous. Big and spacey. The bed is super comfortable and the ambience is fantastic. This is a great hotel. The location is also great and walking distance to the meetings I needed to be at. The one draw back was that the wifi didn't work but they brought up the longest Ethernet cable I've ever seen and I wasn't stuck the small desk. They also forgot their wake up call and luckily, I made it to my meeting on time.

“If Only Location Were the Only Thing...” I decided to go the Priceline route and see what my bid would get me. I guess you get what you pay for. I was looking for a hotel convenient to UTSA and also a variety of restaurants, and this locale didn't disappoint. Unfortunately, the hotel had a bit to be desired. Though hard to desribe, the hotel common areas had a 'cheap hotel' smell that may have been related to the garbage cans placed on each floor for the guests to dump their trash cans into. As the name suggests, the rooms are geared for longer stays and though the bed was comfortable enough, the balance of the furnishings and the condition of the bathroom were barely up to the 2-star rating I requested. The small TV was a good 10 years old and was about 20' away while laying in bed. At least the pool was refreshing, though bring an extra towel for the lounges. Though not advertised ,the hotel did offer a 'coffee bar' and some bagels in the morning. Not a standard continental breakfast, but better than nothing. Got a good night's sleep, but luckily my wife wasn't with me...especially when a couple crickets found their way into my third floor room. Probably wouldn't stay there again at any price.
“Great Staff and Property” The front desk staff were super friendly and very helpful. Rooms were large, clean and comfortable. Great location for an airport hotel. Hotel will validate parking.

“Perfection” This hotel is just amazing. I stay at a lot of hotels and this one is up there with the best. Super quiet rooms, tons of staff there for your every need, beautiful, well kept furnishings, nice bathrooms with good water pressure, free WiFi. Make sure you sign up for their Select Guest program - amazing as well. I don't give out 5 star ratings very often, but I had no choice with this one. Several others from my group stayed here and I got a personal thank you from two of them on the "great selection of hotel". You won't be disappointed.

“Convenient, but incredibly dark rooms” It's OK, but the rooms are incredibly dark. Also maintenance wasn't great. For whatever reason, they put very dim lights in the lamp. Thus, the bedside lamp provided insufficient light to see my watch. The shower leaked and the switch on the bedside lamp fell off. It's convenient to Grand Central Terminal though and the rooms are quite large. This is yet another hotel that pipes analog signals into digital TV's. This results in a distorted, grainy picture.

“Convenient to Seattle University” Very convenient for parents of Seattle University students. Literally across the street. Room was clean, but a little small (we had odd shaped room next to elevator). Highly recommend the on site restaurant (Nicks???). Breakfast was great and I had wish I had known about the great beer selection on tap. It's a little pricey for a Silver Cloud, but better rates than most places in the vicinity.

“Totally Loved the Hyatt!” My partner got our stay at the Hyatt from Priceline - $100 a night!!!! for Tuesday-Thursday. The hotel exterior was beautiful. Getting our room was pleasant, but when we entered the room, it didn't face the koi pond as promised by the clerk - it faced the parking lot. Plus, it was smoky, and it was supposed to be non-smoking. We went back to the desk, and the clerk apologized about 100 times and upgraded us to the junior suite in the towers. Man, what a difference! Huge room, great balcony overlooking the koi pond, wonderful big bed, table with chairs, just great. Everyone who works here greets you warmly, even the maids! they are all trained very well - even calling room service was nice! And food was great and fast. I used the gym on the second floor, and it was the best gym i've ever seen in a hotel. New workout equipment - aerobic stuff, and free weights, and other equipment! towel, water, tvs, mats... the whole nine yards. Great! The grounds are amazing - so tropical and lush, with the aforementioned koi pond, big swimming pool and big hot tub - great to get into at night. The hyatt is right by the marina - all the boats are steps away! it's just gorgeous. Plus there is nothing right beside it - it's all by itself, away from downtown but only 10 minutes to get into the city. A little bunny rabbit hangs around the grounds by the koi pond, just eating grass and being happy. It was perfect weather, a nice breeze and sunny, and just so nice to hang out in the tropical little paradise here. yes, the hotel is a bit old - not exactly up to date - but it is still nicely decorated and lovely. and i bet if you don't stay in the main tower, you won't like it as much - but if you do stay in the main tower, and especially if you get upgraded to a suite, you will enjoy your stay.

“Very convenient, polite staff” I travel frequently to Baltimore and this is my usual place to stay. It's been fairly well-maintained with attractive rooms, many with great views overlooking the Inner Harbor. Very centrally located and everything from Camden Yards to Harbor East are a 10 minute walk. Staff has always been friendly and responsive. The only negative is that it is very much a convention hotel and feels it - it is large-scale, busy, and at very busy times it can be hard to get attention.

“Great service, beautiful building, excellent restaurant.” In the old B&O Railroad headquarters building. High ceilings, marble staircases, etc. Very friendly staff. Took a suite with a great soaking tub. Was disappointed by the furnishings in the suite, management could have done better there. Sort of suited a hotel a little bit downgraded then the impression this gives. Staff referred to me by name during my stay and very polite. Don't miss the B&O restaurant.

“Tries too hard to be trandy” I have been here twice now, but probably won't stay again. There is nothing really bad about this hotel, it's just that I felt like a fish out of water. I hate to complain about hotels clientele, but both times I have been here I have been met with rude behavior, snobbery, impatience, arrogance and bad manners. This is not from the staff, but from other guests. It is a trendy hotel and as a result I feel that a lot of the guests feel they are a cut above other people. I have experienced pushing and jostling at check in, noisy behavior from neighboring rooms, people cutting in front of me in the line for the taxi. I have never experienced this kind of behavior at other hotels and I travel for business about 30 times a year with about 15 of those trips to NYC. I want to like the hotel, but with customers like the ones I have described I don't think i'll be staying again.

“Not bad, but not good either” Upon check in we had the usual issue of not having a double-bed room available, even though we'd reserved two rooms with a double bed, and got there early to ensure we weren't left out. So I did have to share a bed when it would have been desired to have my own. The room still had someone's forgotten belongings in it when we let ourselves in, but housekeeping was there soon after to collect them. The room was otherwise clean and comfy. The hotel is located within a short driving distance to the light rail, which was nice. We were headed downtown for most of our stay so this location was convenient. It was also close to a lot of excellent dining options, and away from all the crowds of downtown. We did try eating at the hotel restaurant one night, a decision we quickly regretted. Our dinner of "pizza and fries" was quite gross, and likely came out of the microwave. But there are lots of other dining options nearby, so just remember to visit those instead.

“Stayed here for Indy 500 weekend a few times - it's ok” We've stayed at this hotel the past few yrs for Indy 5 weekend - great location, right on the circle downtown. Rates usually are 400-500/night with a 3 night minimum as it's usually booked and sold out 9-10 months in advance for this weekend. Of course, getting a hotel in Indy that weekend you take what you can get and usually we book our reservation for the following yr when we check out. Rooms are ok...not very big - clean though. TV's are flat screen, but grainy and not the best HD. Also, the higher up you are, the hotter it tends to be - can be very hot in indy end of may - not sure if the AC is the best. I believe one yr we had to move rooms b/c the AC didn't work in ours Hotel does have a starbucks and room service is really good - have ordered room service multiple times each yr we've stayed here - very quick -and very good. it's approximately 30/day to park your rental car as well (I believe). Pros: LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION - easy access of 65 as well Cons: nothing overtly negative...

“?? Not getting the 'dirty, awful' reviews” ?? I didn't think this place was that bad at all. Was really braced for the worst after reading the reviews, so thank heaven it didn't live down to my expectations. I got this hotel on Priceline after picking a "two star" accommodation...apparently it had formerly been rated one star. Paid $75 plus taxes. Firstly, yes, it's an economy hotel. The furnishings weren't opulent but they were decent enough. Looked like someone went to Ikea and bought out the place (although it'd be basic, no frills Ikea stuff, not the fancy rugs and decor.) The bed was very comfortable, I thought (and I'm used to the plushy digs at Hampton Inn, Sheraton, etc). I slept like a log. No loud noises in the hall, the light blocking curtains worked great, lots of good water pressure, air conditioner ran like a champ. Plus my room at least was spotless. Plenty of close, free parking, a relief when you arrive in the wee hours and are walking into the lobby alone. The night watchman let me in well after the lobby closed and gave me a key, no problem. Honestly? I'd gladly stay here again. The free coffee in the lobby was great. The only item I'd add: there's another Extended Stay nearby. Be sure you're at the right one before you unload all your bags.

“Maybe not a TOP Westin, but Nice” This is a very nice hotel. It seems that some of the people on here are judging this hotel against some pretty high expectations which, I suppose, is quite reasonable considering that it's a Westin and not cheap. Still, some strike me as overly critical. Although the hallways seem a little dark and dingy, the rooms and public spaces are nice. I like the Westin Galleria in DALLAS more and, as I recall, the Westin Post Oak over on the other side of this mall seemed a little nicer. Still, I had no complaints about my stay here.

“My favorite hotel to stay...EVER! Kimpton Hotels are amazing” Kimpton Hotels are my favorite. They are so lush and cozy. Every time I am in LA I HAVE to stay at this location. The rooms are like pillows, the TV is huge, the bathrooms are nice, the staff will bend over backwards for you, and even the hallway smells amazing! I mean come on. This hotel is perfect for business, romance, solo, anything. This is my second trip to Cambodia. My first trip I splurged and stayed at a pricey resort. Since I was going for a month this time I was on a budget. So for $20 a night I picked this place based on the reviews and am glad I did! LOCATION: The hotel is located right across from UCLA campus which means you have great access to Whole Foods, Rite Aid, tons of restaurants, and bars at night. Not to mention the cemetery where Marilyn Monroe and many other famous people is located right around the corner! RECOMMENDATION: I would (and do) recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to be comfortable and well taken care of. I love this hotel. PROS: - Lush Rooms - Delicious food in the restaurant - Enormous flat screen with tons of channels - Quiet - Friendly and helpful staff - Romantic dark feel to the hotel itself CONS: - You have to valet your car

“a great deal!” I have booked this hotel approx. 10 times. It is great for business and here is why: The hotel is completely renovated- everything is new and fresh. The staff is very professional- I have never experienced any problems whatsoever. And the price is beyond a good deal- check hotwire for the best price! I stay here all the time for business. One negative is that the area is not super fantastic (lacks restuarants and cool stores) but head over to South Park for any gourmet needs! A great favorite!

“Great Location” This was our 4th trip to NYC and I am always looking for a good deal on hotels without getting a bad room. We read several of the previous comments from other guests left on this website. We saw that there were both good and bad comments and decided we check it out for ourselves. The lobby is very nice and yes the staff seems unfriendly but that is what the work ethic is like with the people working in the hotel. They are helpful and give you information as needed and it is their culture not to be friendly because they only are there to do the work. We were given information and never was anyone rude. When we entered our room we were happy with the conditions. It was clean and small but most of the rooms in nyc are small unless you want to fork over $400-500 a night in a swanky hotel. I have stayed in hotels with smaller rooms and not as clean in NYC before. For what I paid and the location of this hotel it was worth the stay. We went through La Quinta to make our reservations and fiqured if we were not satisfyed with our stay we would have contcted the corperate headquarters and asked for a refun on our rooms. Well we didn't have any complaints where we could demand a refund.

“(4.5) After an exhausting trip, needed this place to recuperate” Good service from getting out of the cab at the front door, check-in, room service, and late check-out. A bit impersonal, when compared to similar hotels (JW's, Conrad's, etc.), which is why it doesn't make the excellent rating. The room was fantastic - not only was the design new/modern with classic touches, but it was very functional. The food (room service) was delicious, I tried the pulled pork sandwich with mac+cheese and fruit plate. The gym was fair sized for NYC and didn't feel claustrophobic - it had about 5 treadmills, 5 ellipticals, free weights, and machines. Location was great, many good restaurants close by. Overall, the room was so relaxing and comfortable that it alone would make me come back to this hotel again.

“Great Experience at a Convention Center Hotel” Fantastic staff, wonderful service, great view of downtown, Lake Michigan and Soldier Field! As an exhibitor at a medical show in January, I had a Regency Suite for my 6-day stay. The suite was spacious and clean, although the furniture in the living/dining area was a little dated and worn. However, the bedroom was a nice size, comfortable betting and nice bathrooms. The staff was courteous and very helpful for my entire stay. Our company had a lot going on in the suite, which served as a meeting room and hospitality area as well, and the food was good and delivered timely. I was able to check in early and when checking out, the complex billing (split between two credit cards) was handled with ease. A special thanks to Jimmy in the package area, who went beyond the call of duty to retrieve a mis-shipped package. I ended up with over 15 packaged shipped to my attention at the hotel, and Jimmy was incredibly helpful in alerting me and allowing me to keep some of the boxes in the holding area.

“Good for a Fordham or Lincoln Center Visit” The Empire will seem familiar for those who like European-style hotels and the color brown. Translation: smallish rooms, understaffed fron desk, narrow corridors, dim lighting, and lost of brown decor (rugs, wallpaper, furnishing). I was housed here while on a business visit to Fordham University and it's super convenient to both the campus and Lincoln Center and Columbus Circle. My room was smallish, although not the micro-room (#1137) one sometimes sees in NYC. However the odd trapezoid shape made it look larger than other rooms on the floor diagram. It was perfectly comfortable for a short stay, but oddly configured. The bathroom was long and narrow with aa very shallow sink. athere was no desk, but rather an 18 inch by 4 foor table under the falt screen TV covered with stuff for sale (wine, candy, etc.). The room was clean, bed comfy, and air conditioning adequate (kept room at 73 degrees when set on max as outside temp passed 95 degrees). The staff was okay, but the front desk was often crowded at check in times with only one or two people on duty. Bottom line: an okay place to stay in this part of town, but don't go out of your way to stay here.
“Cool hotel, but very basic” Cool trendy hotel, but very small rooms, and not very modern. The hotel has had a light refurbishment, but still has far to go

“Cannot fault this hotel” We spent the ifrst 2 nights of our fly drive holiday at this hotel last month and loved every minute of our stay. Stephen on the front desk was a pleasant smiling asset to the hotel, the chambrmaids did a great job of cleaning and replenishing the bedroom each day, the restaurant staff always had a smile on their faces and the food was great and the bar area was a nice quiet place to enjoy a glass of wine at night - the whole hotel was incredibly clean and a delight to stay in. We had a complimentary breakfast as part of our package and it rated as one of the best and most comprehensive breakfasts in any of the 10 hotels that we stopped at over our 16 day holiday. Nice large free car park and only a 10 minute walk to the Cherry Creek shopping centre. We were impressed with Denver and even more impressed with this hotel - if we were ever to visit Denver again this hotel would be our first choice.

“Love the Benjamin” This is the fourth time I've stayed at the Benjamin and continue to LOVE this hotel. The hotel is well maintained and service is superb. Rooms have a small kitchenette with a fridge, microwave, dishes, glasses and flatware. Perfect size for grabbing snacks or simple breakfast food at a near by Duane Reed or CVS. The hotel has a pillow menu with nine different pillow types. The bathrooms are not large or have lots of counter space, but it's a classic New York hotel. Another reason I love this hotel, location, location, location....it’s on the east side but steps away from the subway where you can catch the 4,5,6 and E,V. If you fly into JFK and want a true New York experience, take the Airtrain to Jamaica Station and then grab the E train and hop off at the 53rd/Lex stop. If you have lots of luggage and want an easy ride to street level, follow the signs to the elevator. Once at street level your two blocks away from the Benjamin. One way trip on the Airtrain/Subway from JFK is only $7 bucks. Save the $60 taxi cost for dinner or shopping. Each time I leave, I can't wait to get back.

“Great location and rooms clean!” This hotel is right in the middle of Times Square, so is in a great location. On my last trip to NYC, our hotel was awful. It was worth spending the extra money for somewhere clean and nice. Although your not usually in your hotel often, you still want somewhere clean. I would absolutely say here again,

“Not as bad as many Reviews I've read, but nothing special” Found the hotel neat and clean upon entering through the Metro, but also found the same uninterested greeting at the front desk as noted by others. Another person walked up just when I did, and one of the two people at the front desk, who was dealing with paperwork or something but had no guest in front of her, didn't acknowledge either of us for more than 90 seconds. I have no issue with saying "I'll be with you in a few moments" or something, but we could have been ghosts for all I knew. Room was in very good condition, very clean, although the corner interior room was oddly-shaped though not cramped. AC unit seemed to struggle to keep the room comfy, though it was only in the 80s during the day (and again, an interior view). If I had paid what others noted I'd probably have been more agitated. But for $99 and a Hyatt Gold member, it wasn't bad, just poor service.

“professionalità e confort” hotel posizionato in maniera eccellente, il personale è gentilissimo, molto disponibile e parla italiano. E' l'unico albergo della citta di new york che include nel prezzo della camera la prima colazione anche se leggera. Le camere sono ampie, ben climatizzate e molto pulite. Lo consiglio vivamente per un soggiorno pieno di confort.

“Disappointed in this Affinia” I'm a big Affinia fan so decided to try the Affinia Manhattan, especially after reading about the renovation. The upside is location: pretty much across from Penn Station so it's very convenient. Staff at the front desk were friendly, but it took me three tries to get the room I asked: one quiet and high up.The first room backed onto the elevators and overlooked a courtyard where there was jack hammering going on. Second room was across from the elevators, where people were talking. Third try got me an upgrade to a 1BR, which was a nice gesture. But I would have preferred the right room on the first try. Yes, the rooms have been renovated, but the overall affect in the 1BR was of a dentist office waiting room: laminate cube table, chrome with glass. Very antiseptic. Big bustling lobby, impersonal feel. Couldn't seem to control the heat (way too hot) but the cold air leaking through the window air conditioner compensated. And I had to call to get my bottle of wine I had received through a promotion. I think next time I'll take a cab across town to the Affinia Shelburne or the Affinia Dumont. They are in the E. 30s

“Be sure to stay here on your trip to Seattle” This is a great hotel and offers terrific value for money. It is in a lovely location and is a safe neighbourhood. We found the staff to be extremely friendly and helpful throughout our stay in the city. I loved the room. It was clean, spacious and comfortable. Our room overlooked the inner courtyard which didn't bother us at all for 2 reasons. 1.) There is no noise when you are trying to sleep. 2.) The view from the rooftop terrace is magnificant so that's where you go for the great view, not looking out your window! There is a starbucks attached to the hotel which was great. We enjoyed buying our breakfast there and then taking it up to the rooftop to eat it there and relax and enjoy the view. Be sure to walk up the hill to get to Kerry Park on Queen Anne Hill - stunning views there too. In the reception area there is a couple of computers with internet access which are free to use for guests. There is no in room safe however there are safety deposit boxes to use at reception. Some great places to eat round about the hotel. Easy to get downtown with buses right outside the hotel, or walk to the space needle to get on the monorail or even just walk the whole way. Next time I'm in Seattle this is where I'll be staying!

“Great Hotel” Great hotel. Booked it online for an early morning flight out of metro airport. The beds were the best hotel beds I have ever slept on. The showers were fantastic as well. Plus, I had a cool outside view to the tarmac where I could watch planes pull up to and leave the gate. Pricing seems to be hit and miss. I booked it for $80 online (a fantastic bargin) when I stayed. However, 5 months later, I had a late international arrival at the airport and wanted to stay the night before driving home. For the same room, the price was $240 (way too expensive).

“Great location and perfect for families” This hotel offers the standard "Embassy Suites" experience with great customer service. The location is very convenient to the L. We were impressed with the staff who took the time to find out how our stay was going and what could be done to make it better. We'll be back.

“100% Satisfaction?” Upon arrival it appeared to be a in city Hampton Inn. Was expecting the typical Hampton Inn Service people have grown accustomed too. Well, not quite. As soon as I came thru the door I was a little put off by the people hanging out in the lobby chatting with the front desk clerk. I should tell you, it was 1:00 am and the 3 men in the lobby chatting with the Night Clerk were local and obviously friends or the employee. We were checked in. I was a little more concerned when I realized the elevator was not a security card entry. You can just walk in, push a button and choose any floor you want to go to... and no one will stop you. Then I came into the room or should I say cubby. Small, very small. But at this point I just got ready for bed and fell asleep. It was the next morning when I realized the condition of the room. Tub was dirty with hair, vanity was cracked, ac/heater vents were broken, and what should of been a warning when I came in was the Hampton Inn sign mangled and in need of repair. There are several of this style hotel in NYC now that seem to be build by the same company. But I have to say, the Fairfield Inn by Marriott over by Times Square or the Four Points in Chelsea (which looks exactly the same as this hotel) are in much better condition and quality than this Hampton.

“Good value in an expensive city” It is hard to find acceptable accommodations in New York for less than $300 per night. $200 is a steal. So when we secured a junior suite at the Eastgate for less than $150, it was too good an opportunity to pass up. Yes, the decor needs a bit of freshening. I was told that starting in January, the place would be undergoing renovations. Meanwhile, the furniture is serviceable and the space is very generous. All is clean and the beds are triple-sheeted so you won't see the blanket at all. There was a full kitchen and a comfortable seating area with sofa, chair and excellent lighting. We only had a view of another building but that meant there was minimal street noise. Bathroom was small but clean. The location is very convenient for most things. We had to take a train leaving from Grand Central Station which is just a short walk away. There are plenty of restaurants and shopping nearby. Our one peeve was that we could not turn off the heat. Thankfully, the window opened so the "fresh" air coming in cooled things off to a comfortable temperature. There is virtually no lobby. All the workers we encountered were friendly and helpful. We even parked in the garage in the building. This cost us $34 per 24 hours including all taxes. Not bad for this expensive city. We'll be interested to see how the renovations affect the pricing. Meanwhile, like other Affinia properties that we've tried, this is a well-run establishment.
“ロケーション最高!” タイトル通りBARTの駅からも近く、何をするにもどこに行くのも便利でした。 部屋はあまり広くないので二人だと多少窮屈かもしれません。 部屋にあったコーヒーはスターバックスのものでした。 冷蔵庫はなかったように思います。 高層階の部屋だったため窓からユニオンスクエアが見えてきれいでした。 値段も手ごろでまた泊まりたいホテルです。

“Ok hotel, great location, wifi and TV didn't always work” The hotel is ok; the rooms are a little small, but other than that a pretty standard chain hotel set-up. But it's in a great location in Chelsea. On the first morning, the hotel's Internet connection was down for two hours; just when we were trying to plan what to do for the day! On the next morning, the TV signal went down.

“Very nice stay!” Great place- fantastic views, nice pool, a short stroll to Bunker Hill, 15 minute drive into Cambridge, just across the bridge from the Italian district. Very friendly and helpful staff.

“Fun hotel, good value & central location” After reviewing the Yotel web site and other reviews I was apprehensive, but it turned out great and would totally stay there again. Be prepared for an ultra modern property catering to the solo traveler, tourists and younger/trendy people. Staff, restaurant, bar and night club all provided exceptional service and value. Areas that need improvement: No shampoo, conditioner or lotion provided. Motion sensors are slow to pick up movement. I don't like walking into a dark room when I left a light on... TV picture is too dark and not alterable. Lighting around bathroom mirror is not bright enouph. I would not recommend the Yotel for older couples, families with children or anyone sharing a basic room do to the bathroom configuration.

“Too busy” There are things that are great & nots so great. Great location, view, quiet rooms for the most part, shopping & food close by and walking distance, entertainment. It has everything. The things I don't like about this hotel is: 1. sometimes it is very difficult to get an elevator due to congestion! And I'm not even kidding! You are at a convention center. 2. The rooms are very used and average. Occasionally I have gotten rooms that were not cleaned well or needed repair. But they have always gotten me better room if I had a problem. I have gotten rooms that the HVAC didn't work well. I changed rooms. Sometimes a stale odor in the room like mildew or something. This hotel generally has an extra room to move to if you get a bad one. The staff has ALWAYS been friendly and accommodating. However, they get so much business that if you were to threaten to move to another hotel because bad service to whatever degree, they don't really care. It is a big hotel. Staffers are friendly, upper management not so much.

“Fine but not a luxury hotel” This is not a bad hotel. It's just old. I was really looking forward to staying here but left underwhelmed. The service is worthy of a Waldorf but that's where it ends in my humble opinion. The rooms were spacious but dated. The grounds were nice but not overwhelmingly beautiful. This is a very solid 4 star property. The history of this storied property is interesting. If you can catch a rate go ahead and check it out. This hotels' biggest asset is it's past though, so please adjust expectations. The Biltmore area of Phoenix offers quite a variety of high-end distractions. It's a nice place to visit. Enjoy your stay.

“Hotel normal, próximo a LAX, para pasar una noche” Este es un hotel típico de viajeros para pasar una noche. Esta al lado de LAX, nosotros lo escogimos porque nuestro vuelo salía temprano y está al lado de la zona de coches de alquiler. También nos decidimos porque el parking era gratuito, frente a 10-20$ que te pedían en otros de categoría superior. El sitio está bien, la habitación era amplia y limpia, pudimos disfrutar de la piscina, y la verdad es que el poco tiempo que estuvimos nos quedó una buena sensación. La única pega fue la atención de recepción, tanto para entrar como para salir, totalmente apáticos y sin mirarte a la cara. Lo recomiendo sólo si tienes pensado coger un vuelo. Para pasar unas vacaciones en Los Ángeles está muy alejado de cualquier punto de interés.

“Surprisingly Nice” It was only one night so I decided to stay at the Union League Club based only on it's proximity to my meeting. Room 1030 turned out to be small but nicely appointed. The bathroom had been renovated fairly recently in marble. The shower was really beautiful. Gilchrist & Sames toiletries completed a nice experience. On the minus side the bed spread and padded bench were both stained. The carpet was just beginning to show wear but was clean. The service was good and the ambience was even better. This is a little gem that I'd rate 3 stars overall with some 4 star touches.

“Very nice hotel, very good location” Stayed at this location on a weekend trip to Chicago. Right in the heart of downtown near several restaurants, House of Blues, Ruth's Chris, etc. The rooms were very nice with a small minibar with microwave and small fridge. The breakfast was pretty decent and a plus if you don't want to venture out of the hotel for a morning meal. Free wireless internet for guests. There is shopping nearby, you can catch a trolley to Navy Pier nearby and Michigan Ave is within walking distance. At night the neighborhood turns into a barhoppers/clubgoers dream. All the restaurants in the area pretty much turn into nightclubs so just be prepared for the change in scenery on weekends at night. We got a steal of a deal at $109 when Marriot.com was running a special. The only downside was $40 per night for parking which added $120 to our hotel bill. Other than that everything was great!

“Great for the price” For 50$ a night (from priceline.com), this was a real bargain. Yes, we got a small lousy room near the ice machine. Yes, the air conditioning made the noise of an idling truck. However, it was not hot, so we turned it off. The bathroom is very small, with little counter space, but everything was very clean and in working order (even the kind-of-hard-to-figure-out coffee machine). The hotel has a pool and an adequate fitness center. Even next to the ice machine the hotel itself was quiet. Overall, for the price, quite a bargain. For the standard rate of 134$ a night, I would have been quite unhappy. Self-parking was extra, but at 14$ a day it wasn't too bad. The hotel has access to one of the extremes of the Riverwalk (which is currently being expanded), so if you are tired of walking and don't mind waiting forever, you can get there by watertaxi.

“Quirky hotel” Stayed here for business twice now - restaurant is very overrated. The rooms are nice with high ceilings, and the hotel itself feels unique with its wide hallways and high ceilings. Service was just average.

“Pretty clean and comfortable- bad location” Not much to say. This place was very decent, clean & comfortable. It is situated not too far from a sleazy strip club in a bad location. I would recommend this place to a single business traveler who has no interest in seeing the nice parts of Dallas. Good hotel for the price.

“Van Ness -is- the way to the Golden Gate...” I echo recent comments that this is a pretty good place. The bathtub drain was blocked when we first got there but repaired the next morning. Internet was slow when all guests were there, likely since many of them were at the geophysicist's conference and heavy users of laptops/internet. That is about all I have bad to say and those are minor things. I did eat in the sports bar on the last night and it was fine. The Polk Street area offers a lot of other options (plus there is the gem in the rough of Tommy's Joynt on Van Ness). As mentioned, the New Village Cafe is a good breakfast choice, much cheaper than the hotel itself. I found all staff I dealt with very friendly, but the bell captain seemed hard to find at times.

“Good Value For Seattle” I've stayed here before and yes it is a bit outside the city centre. The hotel has a free shuttle and we used that as well as public transport and walking and didn't find it any problem. The secure parking was free which you don't find in the city centre and with breakfast, internet and laundry all included it was a good deal for a fairly pricey city. We did have a bit of street noise but our room was clean and comfortable and I would stay here again if I return to Seattle.

“Nice rooms, cold shower” This hotel is very clean and the rooms are great like all Hyatt Places I like the suite feel that the rooms have and the large TV's. The staff was friendly and helpful. The only issues wtih the hotel were a lack of hot water in the shower in the morning and the shower area is extremely small. the TV reception was also spotty. The the networks were in HD and great, after that it went downhill quickly. ESPN never came in at all and the oterh channels were SD which is not great on a 42in flat screen. Overall the hotel was nice and I would stay again but I hope they fix the TV issues and pipe in some hot water.

“Expected cleaner, more contemporary room for the $$” Nice amenities, fantastic location, disgusting bedding. It was probably clean but the stained bed skirt squished me right out. Overly aggressive early morning room service loud enough to disturb anyone on the floor regardless of privacy requests was also extremely annoying. I would expect this in a cheaper hote. Not worth the money.

“Hôtel parfait pour visiter NYC” En visite le temps d'un week-end, le Comfort Inn fut d'abord un excellent rapport/qualité prix. La proximité de Central Park (réellement moins de 5 minutes à pied) en a fait un choix très intéressant pour découvrir le poumon vert de la ville. En traversant Central Park on peut rejoindre la 5ème avenue en moins de 25 minutes, le métro reste conseillé pour s'aventurer plus bas dans Manhattan. Reste que le quartier est idéal pour ceux qui veulent dîner a proximité de l'hôtel ou faire du shopping (Colombus Avenue à deux pas). L'opéra se trouve également a proximité et le musée d'histoire naturelle est à une station de métro. Les prestations de l'hôtel sont bonnes et l'équipe est très accueillante. Certains pourront trouver la chambre petite mais les chambres standards sont propres, claires et très fonctionnelles. Le wifi est gratuit tout comme le petit déjeuner. C'est peut-être le seul bémol, la salle pour se restaurer est minuscule et le choix pour le petit déjeuner assez sommaire. Lors de ma prochaine visite, j'espère pouvoir obtenir de nouveau une chambre dans cet hôtel de qualité et abordable (ce qui n'est pas toujours le cas à NY)

“We Knew This Wasn't the Ritz, and Liked It A Lot” OK, the rooms are small. But this is NYC, and The Mave is a value. You've got to know when you come to a boutique hotel such as this you're not going to be staying in the Ritz. I've read other reviews where people complained about the room smell and view. Our particular sixth floor Madison Double was bright and fresh. And most importantly, the bed was as comfortable as any that I've slept in recently at hotels. We love the location, off the touristy path. Very close to SoHo, NoHo, Grammercy, Union Square and the lovely Madison Square Park...but uptown is very accessible, too. Loved the friendly staff

“Great historic hotel” This hotel is a step back into history with every modern amenity. You cannot beat the location if you are visiting the stockyards or want to have a late night at the bars or rodeo. The bed was extremely comfortable and the old fashion sink/toilet/shower was impressive. The staff was very courteous and helpful. If you are looking for a historic hotel in a fun area of town this place cannot be missed. We are locals who booked a night so that we could do a nice dinner and night out without worrying about driving home. This place is literally 15 minutes from my house and I am looking for a reason to book to stay here again.

“Excellent,loved staying at this Hotel.Great Location.” Huge rooms,great beds,separate area for the kids,friendly staff.Cant complain at all.The location is superb next to the brillant Quincy Markets.We loved staying here and in Boston.What a beautiful city and lots of Irish pubs.Highly recommended.

“Makes Business Trips Into Vacations” I want to say that my second stay in this hotel was better than the first two years ago, but that would have been impossible, as the first was so good nothing could top it. This is a dream hotel. The staff are really kind and helpful and full of good ideas about interesting things to do in the area no matter how much or little you have to spend or what your tastes are. When I explained what sorts of things I wanted to do and see and that I like to walk, they gave me amps that made it all easy. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the beds are great. The food in the hotel is quite good. I'm a somewhat fussy eater and vegetarian, but despite the proximity of terrific restaurants, I ended up eating in the hotel three times because the food was so tasty and inexpensive for what you get. The location is wonderful, you can easily walk to many fascinating places, including museums and parks. Every hour I was able to take off from the conference I attended I could spend having fun -- and I did.

“Good place to stay if working at OSU” I stay at the hotel every time I come to work at OSU. It is close to campus and within walking distance to several good restaurants, the best being the Mexican place in the same parking lot. The draw backs are the price, a little high, and no free breakfast or even coffee for that matter. The business center is great for the business traveler. I would not stay here if I was with my family, it is much more business oriented.

“Renovation has begun - Floor 5” Stayed at Marriott El Paso near airport for 3 nights. Requested and received a room for disabled with king bed. It was not yet renovated (and needs it) however it met all our needs for this type of room, except for the aesthetics (which will be addressed in the renovation). The hotel renovation should be completed by mid-summer (according to front desk staff). Room service was prompt and tasty, but the order was not fulfilled accurately. Room service was necessary because the hotel restaurant is closed for lunch! But no harm. It was still enjoyed. Service staff was excellent in all respects (but that might be because I'm a Marriott Platinium). The breakfast daily in Concierge Lounge was above average. Hot cereal daily and good continental breakfast choices. Evening snacks in the Lounge were definately above average - nice choice of hot foods, top shelf liquor and wines and good desserts after 7 pm. The pool area is functional but tired and also in need of renovation (massive amount of paint peeling near the skylights above the jacuzzi). Pool chairs show dirt stains. The fitness room is open 24 hrs with decent variety of equipment. Overall, at $175 per night (mid-week), I overpaid but it's the only Marriott full service hotel in town, and I'm a Marriott junkie. Once the renovation is completed, I'm sure $175 will be a much better rate.

“Cruise Ship Bath” Pod51 is a decent location. plenty of restaurants and bars. quiet rooms but you have to be ready for the smallest bathroom you've ever encountered. you can reach your bedside table while sitting on the toilet. i'll leave it at that. quiet setting. nice window AC unit that you can control. comfy bed and while the room is small, it's well designed. so, i recommend the Pod, as long as you are ok with the cruise ship bathroom.

“fantastic stay!” I had arranged a number of rooms for an industry conference (our professional group was composed of one woman and nine men), and heard afterwards from each of my fellow travelers that they were most impressed by the Riverwalk Vista. We certainly appreciated the afternoon wine, lemonade and fresh cookies. Breakfast was bountiful, fresh, and tasty, the rooms very attractive (pets are provided in the form of fish), the bed marvelously comfortable, and the (wired) network access worked quickly and easily. The bath was clean, and while I chose to move my very fancy coffeemaker from the counter onto the floor (since I was staying for over a week), it didn't really pose a problem. Yes, there is street noise, especially on a Saturday night, but if one travels often and is familiar with the variance in ambient noise levels at hotels, one usually brings along some form of earplug. White noise generators are provided in the room, which worked quite well, such that I only needed to use my earplugs a couple of times. The hotel is located a mere five minutes walking time from the convention center, and is thirty seconds from the Riverwalk. Good food is abundantly available nearby. If one wants to park a car, there are parking lots within a couple of blocks, and there is a 30-minute "offloading parking area" in front of the hotel. I felt quite safe in the neighborhood, and the hotel is additionally secured by a keycode locking system. Our little group is already planning to return for our next exhibition in San Antonio. Many thanks to Catherine, Anet, and especially Patti, who made us feel so very much at home.

“Awesome Amentities & Lovely Location” This hotel has 4 different eateries, a humongous convention center, and a few great pools, not to mention the many other enhancements. The rooms are kept very nicely with soft carpet! We had nothing go wrong with our stay and I surely recommend this hotel!

“Nice Conference Venue. OK Hotel” The hotel has been extensively refurbished, but the age is still aparent in the rooms and some of the facilities. It's a nice hotel, located in a wonderful area of D,C.

“Cheap but you get what you pay for” From the gecko in my room (quite cute, actually, but I prefer not having wildlife running around!) to the horrible WiFi, room smelling like a brewery, and the disinterested staff, this was an interesting experience. I stayed here one night merely because of a recent Carlson hotels points promotion, and to be fair, did receive a partial refund when I complained about all of the above. However, I would not recommend this place unless you're really stuck with nowhere else to go.

“Good Value” The rooms itself are not especially great, but they are clean and serve the purpose. However, the location (short walk to transportation/attractions), friendly staff, and free parking make up for it. I would stay here again.

“Pleasantly Surprised” My husband and I stayed here for 2 nights free, using Starpoints. This was our first time staying at a Meridien. The lobby is nicely decorated and clean. There is also a small indoor pool and a large gym. The gym costs $10 a day and has racquetball and a dry sauna, in addition to a lot of equipment. There are three restaurants. There is valet parking, but we self-parked in the same garage (still valet) with a $30 a day parking coupon. The business center is small and really expensive. Check in was easy and we were pleased to get an upgraded room with a Central Park view, even though we did not pay anything for our stay. The elevators were a little slow to arrive. The decor in the rooms and hallways is modern. Our room was large by NYC standards and light-filled. The bed was really comfortable. The room was quiet. There were two small closets, a safe, and two desk areas -- perfect for business travel. There was a large TV with DVD and VCR. The bathroom was clean and had Peter Thomas Roth toiletries. Maid service was pretty good, but our washcloths weren't replenished. There is no coffee pot, but there is a Starbucks directly across the street. There is a minibar that can't be used to store food, as it apparently contained sensors inside it that would charge you if anything was moved. Checkout and luggage storage were easy. They were fully booked and could not offer us late checkout. The location was pretty good and within walking distance to many attractions and good restaurants. It's also less than a block away from two subway stations. All in all, we were pleased with our stay and would stay here again.

“Barely 3 Stars, nothing fancy..” I travel twice a year to Seattle on business. Stayed for 6 days. The good stuff: $85.00 per night is a steal for downtown Seattle. Pleasant staff. Everthing worked in the room and the bed (bedding) was good quality. Clean, well maintained public areas and bright hallways. Great location to shopping, convenction center and Pike Place Market. Area's of disappointment: No bellman. No conceeair. 5th floor restaurant; slow service and food was cold both times I ate there. Inadequate light and dark furnishings make rooms look poor. No lotion provided in bathroom or full length mirror. Very loud, room doors have no seals. You hear all voices and other doors slamming shut. TV must be replaced! Dark picture tube and bad reception. No HBO and/or Showtime. On Demand options are very limited.

“Nice Place, Fine Staff” We moved to this hotel after a bad experience at the Tempe Sheraton Four Points. What a difference, like going from purgatory to heaven. Staff was friendly and helpful, room was beautiful and spacious, pool was very nice and relaxing. No complaints at all.

“Great Location BUT....” Beautiful hotel, excellent location, great service. But......cell phone reception is awful or non-existent (we had to go outside at all hours of the day and night) and the same is true for wi-fi. However, if you're here on a romantic getaway and don't WANT to use your cell phone, then the Park Hyatt is the place. I'll leave my cell phone and laptop home and stay here again.

“Like The Yankees in The Postseason” The Chatwal is the only luxury boutique hotel in the Theatre District and it shows some promise, but the symbol of the hotel—an archer with the bow pointed directly over his head—sums it up. The arrow just might come down and hit the archer. The Chatwal has a habit of shooting itself. I have stayed at The Chatwal a half dozen times and the bellmen always remember me and greet me by name. Then, there is the front desk crew. On my last visit I was the only guest checking in and the bellman greeted me by name and welcomed me back within earshot of the front desk clerk who did not greet me by name and demanded that I present identification. I do not mind being asked for identification by the TSA, but when I have spent thousands of dollars at a property and the bellman knows me, I should think that the front desk crew might stop treating me like I intend to make off with robes and ashtrays. The Chatwal staff has an annoying habit of wanting to help you when you have no need of it, reminding you that they have helped you before, and being unavailable to help you when you really need it. Recently, one of the butlers interrupted me in conversation and held my elevator to tell me that she had put some pressing in my room. Since I am able to see the pressing hanging in the closet, was that really necessary? The décor at the Chatwal is art deco and very impressive. The rooms are small but opulent. The bathrooms are amazing and feature Toto heated electronic toilets that are black lit at night. It makes you want to get out of bed for a trip to the bathroom. Most bathrooms also feature TV’s built into the mirrors. Heck, you may never want to leave the bathroom. My only complaint about the bathrooms is that the vanities are very small and not large enough for two guests. Be forewarned if you have ATT cell phone service—there are rooms on the interior of the hotel where your service will not work. If you need to use your cell phone and you have ATT service, ask for a room on the 44th street side of the building. The fitness center is very small and a small (4 feet deep and 6 feet wide by maybe 10 feet long) adjoins it. The fitness center is about the same size as the pool and features two treadmills, two cycles, and an elliptical. The built in TV’ only have a limited number of channels that must have been selected by someone who does not watch American TV. There are no networks channels. There is no CNN. Worse, yet, on my last two visits, only three of the dozen bad channels actually worked (MTV, ESPN and USA). The fitness center at the Chatwal is among the worst I have ever seen in a luxury hotel. Perhaps they should get rid of the pool which I have never seen anyone use and build a real fitness center worthy of the room rates they charge. The Chatwal is home to the Lamb’s Club which is an extraordinary restaurant. The food is good and the service is attentive. They have the New York restaurant affectation of telling you that you can only have a reservation at a time that is about 30 minutes different from whatever time you might request. They have done that to me a half dozen times and I have always arrived at the time I wanted and never observed a need for this silliness. Lest someone reply and tell me I do not understand the restaurant business and it is a timing issue that impacts the reservations later that night, let me call “bull” on that now and reveal that I worked in gourmet restaurants for a decade. The bar at the Chatwal is on the second floor and it is beautiful and excellent in every way. The service is fantastic and they even hand cut their own ice cubes which is amazing in this day and age. The Chatwal is like the Yankees in the postseason—it is very good. My frustration is with knowing that the Chatwal win the Series with a little more attention to detail and some training for the front desk folks that focuses on putting the guest first.

“Great place for an OSU visit” Stayed for one to take a campus tour with my son and was very pleased. Check in was smooth, room was very clean and nicely furnished. Breakfast buffet was average. Valet and lobby staff very helpful. Even though we had a car, it never left the garage. Everything on the OSU campus is within walking distance of this hotel. They also offer a free ride service to anywhere on campus which we used on one occassion.

“Hilton New York - EXCELLENT!” What a place! I am glad I chose such a fine hotel to stay at whilst visiting New York for the first time. The location is excellent, central park and times square a mere 5 minute walk away. I chose the executive level which meant a room between 37th - 44th floors. I got 43rd which gave some unbelievable views towards central park!The staff were extremely friendly and the hotel was very clean. Well worth paying that bit extra for executive level. Go on, give it a try - you won't be dissapointed!

“Poor location in downtown.” This hotel is up on 11th and not near anything. In summer weather, you don't want to be out hiking it 6 blocks or so to get anywhere. The hotel underwent a major renovation a couple years ago, and while the lobby is nice looking the rooms are still dated....complete with low popcorn ceilings. No Platinum SPG upgrade. Front desk also forgot to give us our b'fast vouchers since we bought a package that included b'fast. They said they would bring them up but two hours later we've not seen them. This is an average hotel at best. Thankfully we only paid $100/night. I wouldn't want to pay more, especially to be in this location. Homeless shelter is a few blocks away so a number of colorful people in the neighborhood. The club room food service doesn't start until 6 pm in the evening! Big deal, it's limited service isn't worth the wait. Sheraton should drop management on this property because it doesn't do them any favors, or at least rebrand it with a lesser quality name. I would hate to be a manager saddled with this property. We're here in the middle of a magicians conference which has well over 300 rooms blocked. Quite frankly when a conference as large as this books the hotel, they take over and it was a huge disservice to book other guests, unless you're into packed lobbies with magicians of varying qualities and levels or craftsmanship all talking about the newest card tricks or the barrels of their trick canes. They even had "magic camp" for the kiddies in the group. Whoopee, I would have just as soon booked myself into a clown convention. Austin is a great city with lots to see and do. We'll definitely be back, but not in this hotel even for $100/night.

“Good stay at the Holiday Inn Select” My wife and I stayed Labor day weekend at the Holiday Inn Select. The Holiday Inn Select is located on I410 close to 280. There is a Holiday Inn Express almost next door. The Holiday Inn Select's sign is not as visible from the access road. We almost went to the wrong hotel. When we checked in we were give a room on the 11th floor which is their club level. We were happy for the free upgrade. The room looked like it had recently been redone and was in good shape and clean. The AC was set on 65 degrees, but never got bellow 73. We like it cold at night. My wife loves to take hot baths, but the water was only warm. The free wireless Internet did not work in our room for 4-5 hours the first day, but we were able to go down the hall to the lounge and get a signal there. It worked great the next day. The hotel was remodeling their bar and cafe. Curtains were setup to hide the work which narrowed the path to the front desk to 2 to 3 feet wide at times. It was difficult to walk through with bags. A temporary bar and cafe had been setup in another room with very limited selections. Service at the front desk was great.

“It could be a much better hotel if the housekeeping staff did not try to get guests up every morning” I have stayed at this hotel dozens of times, and each visit, however good, has been marred by what is clearly intentional conduct by house keeping to get us all up and out of our rooms by their schedules, not ours. I have stayed in every part of the hotel and on every floor. It never fails. That the management does not stop this is crazy. I know that the housekeepers work hard and everywhere else I stay I always leave a gratuity on the bed. At this hotel, however, I want to practically scream as the daily cacophony begins when housekeeping arrives on the floor. I stay in hotels every week, just about, but this one is unique for this bad feature. I have complained but truly, the management does nothing to change it over the years so why bother anymore? It is like the hallways were a mall or a private home where anything goes at any volume. The rooms are fine, generally spacious and clean. The location, while certainly not downtown, has a Metro stop at the bottom of the driveway and that gets you anywhere. The meeting space is good, and older rooms are always being renovated and freshened up. If yours seems old and tired, ask to be moved. They will do it. The restaurants are fine but even better dining is right outside on Connecticut a Avenue and nearby streets. There is underground parking, and the neighborhood is very safe. Proximity to Zoo and Metro makes this a good place for families. The walls are a little thin and rooms with doors between them are a bit noisier than they should be, but this average rating I have given would be much higher if only someone trained housekeeping that guests want to wake up on their own schedules, not those of the cleaning crew. It really is quite amazing and the worst on a routine (not isolated) basis of any hotel at which I stay. Shameful lapse of management... or maybe they want everyone up and in the hotel restaurants?

“Great Location, Acceptable Accommodations” The Millennium Hotel Broadway is in an ideal location for tourists. It is in the heart of the Times Square area and within easy walking distance of many attractions. Access to the NYC subway is just a block away. The accommodations are acceptable, but marginal for a 3 1/2 star rating. The hallways and rooms are a bit run down looking. The room was clean and everything was in working order. I would recommend Johns Pizzeria (44th st between 7th Ave and Broadway) for excellent pizza. There are a few inexpensive cafes on 45th street directly across from the hotel that are good for breakfast and lunch. Overall, if you plan to spend minimal time in the hotel this is a good choice simply for its location.

“Still a great place to stay Downtown In Philly” Recently, I just stayed at the Mariott Downtown. It is a very large convention hotel conveniently located close to everything! The staff is extremely pleasant and the staff is very responsive. The rooms had been redone since my last visit. Across the street is the Flagship Macy's with decent shopping. In this location you are central to everything in Philly! Both bars had fast service and the food was above average for a Marriott. I would absolutley stay there again. It was a pleasant experience!

“Enjoyed The Ritz-Carlton, Battery Park” I stayed at The Ritz-Carlton, Battery Park with a business colleague for 3 nights in Feb. The hotel is modern and the bar is especially cool for drinks w/ spectacular views. The rooms are comfortable and very large (for NYC). Beautiful bathrooms w/ seperate bath/ shower/ toilet. Upgraded amenities- typical Ritz beds/ linens (frette, high thread count, etc. The hotel is terrific. We had Sunday brunch in the dining room. It was a great experience; awesome selection of freshly prepared foods and seafoods- pricey, but great for hotel guests. Excellent service. Smart- realistic- funny concierge was very helpful: got us broadway tickets, restaurant reservations, etc. The only negative about this hotel for weekend guests or uptown/midtown business travelers is that the hotel is located far from city center. Hotel is very near to wall street, financial district, statue of liberty--but you'll need to use the trains on the weekend to hit the park, 5th ave, soho, greenwich, etc.

“Great Room” This is a nice hotel with a surprisingly good location. Lots of neat restaurants nearby. My only complaint was that I had a concierge floor room and it shut down on the weekend despite the fact that the entire floor was occupied.

“pricy, but in walking distance of most everything” I stayed here for business purposes. They stored my bags since I arrived early and stayed late. The rooms were very spacious by NYC standards and there are plenty of good restaurants within walking distance.

“Amazingly well-done plush eco-hotel in heart of San Francisco.” Quite new at the time of my visit, the Orchard Garden Hotel was more than just a great moment of pampering, it was a moment of pampering where one felt they were doing good to the earth instead of dumping harmful chemicals in one's wake. The bed was infinitely comfortable, with top quality high-threadcount linens and duvet. Very modern TV, electronics and stying within the room. The "green" bath products were plush and wonderful smelling. The restaurant in the lobby was nothing short of San Francisco excellent. (Were it not in this city dominated by competitive cooking and foodie-ism, it would be a high standout on its own.) Staff was incredibly welcoming and warm, clearly proud to be a part of this hotel.

“pleasantly surprised” to be honest I wasn't expecting much for $175 in Manhattan bt i picked it based on the proximity (across the street) from Penn Station. However the room was large, with a nice sofa and a desk, in attractive, contemporary design (they must be upgrading the rooms- some reviews talk about run-down rooms but mine was fresh and beautiful).
