Nice touches were the iPod docking station and the windows that open for some fresh air (and NYC noise). The gym was adequate. I wouldn't hesitate to stay again, even if I don;t have to be at Penn.

“Room for improvement” Things I liked about this hotel: 1. Nice bedding and towels. 2. Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries, when left in room. 3. Pleasant demeanor of staff. 4. Decent exercise facilities and warm pool water. Things needing improvement: 1. Sleep quality. If you stay here, expect to hear the constant rattle of the freeway and the televisions on either side of your room. Even if you move to the couch, you can expect to hear noise from the atrium. I do not think the noise from the other rooms was excessively loud, rather the noise was due to thin walls. 2. Connection to guest services/front desk from room. On four different occasions, I tried to phone guest services from my bedroom. Other colleagues tried to phone guest services as well, and no one ever picked up. We learned to walk to the front desk to ask our question. Even then, guest services did not always follow through. One evening at about 6pm, I walked to the front desk to ask for an extra blanket and lotion (as the maid never left any in my room until the last day I was there); the person at the front desk gave me some lotion and told me the blanket would be sent shortly. I waited two hours, but the blanket never arrived. 3. Rooms. My room looked like it was damaged from a boy band party. The bathroom door was clawed at the base, there were multiple stains on the carpet, and some of the furniture was dented. Old florescent lighting overhead. 4. Shuttle. Make sure you reserve the shuttle well in advance; otherwise, you may need to arrange a taxi or will have to wait a long time. 5. Business center has sloooow computers, and if you wish to access the internet from your room, prepare to pay $10/day. 6. Restaurant menus - greasy food. Not many healthy options. You can probably find better, healthier options at Whataburger or Subway, which are within walking distance. I have stayed in the Market Center district on other occasions and can recommend better hotels within a two-mile radius. I know people love the free breakfast and happy hour (well, if you are really into bacon or like a margarita served in a plastic cup) at Embassy Suites, but I would rather pay for breakfast and get good sleep at another hotel.
“Really poor” $12.95 for very slow internet. Rooms dated. TV an old relic. Beware of making toll free 1800 numbers. They hit you $2. Food horrendously overpriced. Give this hotel a BIG miss

“Quoting Ferris Bueller "If you have the means, I highly recommend picking one up"” Oh what a night. Spent my 40th birthday downtown and stayed the night at the Waldorf. Hands down best urban hotel experience. Fantastic service from check-in all the way to check-out. Received complimentary upgrade to a Waldorf Suite with luxurious amenities including a gas fireplace, deep soaking tub, and Gi-Normous shower. Wonderful linens and bedding made for peaceful slumber after a late night out on the town. Room was opulent, cozy, and comfortable. Complimentary hotel car service to our dinner location - driver wouldn't accept a tip. Neither would the bellman who helped us with our bags. Breakfast in the restaurant was delicious - and great service. Easy to understand why this hotel is tops in Chicago.

“Decent hotel- Great Location” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Indianapolis for business. The best thing about the hotel is the location. It is right in the middle of everything. I love a hotel that is connected by covered walkways to a mall with a Nordstrom. There are many restaurants within walking distance. I tried the Palomino and it was quite good. It is a good place for people traveling alone. There are lots of tables and places to sit at the bar. Arriving at the hotel you would think it is a dump. The valet area is all crazy because of construction. All things considered they were quiet accommodating and the service was quick. Parking was $25/ day. The hotel was still under construction when I was there on 10/17/07. They were doing their best to keep it closed off. It didn't really effect my stay. I will say that the elevators are slow and typically crowded (especially when one of the conferences is going on---which seemed often.) Add a little extra time when going or coming from your room. The rooms are quite spacious with typical Hyatt decor. Both the bedroom and the bathroom were well maintained. I stayed in room 1511 and had a nice view. It was a quiet room. The bed and pillows were all very comfortable. The linens, towels and robes were all of nice quality. The bathroom amenities were the typical Portico brand for Hyatt and were well stocked. There is a safe and an empty refrigerator in the room. The wires in the room is TMobile and it didn't work when I arrived. I called down and they wanted to send an engineer, but I opted to go with the high speed ($9.99/day.) I woke up the next morning and both the high speed and the wireless weren't working. I managed to get on the wireless for about 1 minute and half and it still charged me. The front desk person wanted me to pay both charges. I explained that I would not be doing that and they finally took one off my bill. Overall, the Hyatt is a decent, clean place to stay in a good location. It is a fine business hotel or if you are going to the stadium. It isn't glamorous, but it gets the job done.

“Very odd property” The property is convenient to the airport. and has a nice pool/ That is where it ends. The property was under construction and to get to and from the room I had to go through tunnels of clear plastic. The elevators were very oddly placed for customer flow. The halls were very dark and did not make me feel safe. The room was very dated.

“Comfortable hotel, but expensive and nothing amazing . . .” This hotel was comfortable, and the service was fine. It was fairly expensive (booked at the last minute for business travel at $249 for one night and $299 the next night). The lobby was funky, but not large. I had stayed at the 71, which is right around the corner on an earlier stay. The room I got at the 71 had a fabulous view, and I'd probably try the 71 on my next stay if I end up in the same section of town. One cool thing was the yoga channel on TV -- an endless loop of a yoga class. Unfortunately, the yoga gear that was promised (mat, accessories) was not in the room, and I didn't bother to request it.

“Aging Dowager” Booked by my company at the Helmsley Park Lane, I was excited, as I had never stayed there and looked forward to the experience. Set on Central Park South, this hotel is in a great location. My room (4315) had a "partial view" of the park. Not bad really. I was encouraged by the attentive and friendly check-in staff and, aside from some construction work going on inside the lobby, we were off to a great start. Once onto my floor, I noticed that the wallpaper was in need of repair (not to mention that it was gaudy and quite dated). Could this be a sign of things to come??? Yes! My room was large enough and high enough to get a good view, but was obviously aging and in need of a major upgrade. The wallpaper and paint were peeling away and the furnishings must have been grand...in their day. The bathroom was small, but with a large tub. However, it was shoddy and unkempt. The vanity was out of a bad 60's movie and the caulking around the tub was moldy and pealing. Even where things were "repaired" it seems that no attention at all was paid to detail. The repaired grout in the floor for instance, did not match the original. The bed was large and comfy, but not a "Heavenly Bed" by any means. Finally, the windows did not fully seal, so street noise and wind were easily heard. Now, this IS New York, so I didn't spend a great deal of time in my room, but when you are staying at a hotel with the famous Helmsley name, you expect a little more. This room was a little less. I hear that they are remodeling and that my room may be one of the last to be done, so this review should be tempered with that information. I'd say that, despite the decor and shoddy repair work, I actually had a comfortable stay at the late Leona's place. It's not the best, but it's not the worst either.

“Great location, beautiful architecture, hit or miss staff” A group of friends stayed at the Marriot Courtyard downtown San Diego this past weekend for a bachelorette party. The hotel it self is very cool, it’s the old historic building that used to be a bank that was renovated into a hotel, but they kept a lot of the original architecture, even the teller signs at the check-in are still there. It’s a beautiful property, the rooms are fairly spacious and aptly decorated, and there are some great views of the city if you are in one of the upper floors (we were on the 7th and still had good views). Valet is expensive, $33 a night, but pretty standard for city parking. The location is superb, withing easy walking distance from a ton of awesome restaurants and the Gaslamp district, we didn't need to take cabs the first night everything was so close. Also, the beds are amazing! We were a little disappointed in some of the service we received, we had requested a mini-fridge for our room early in the day and had to call back 2 more times (in addition to when we originally requested it at check in) before it arrived. Also we had booked three rooms and the hotel policy is for room check-in at 3pm, we did not get our last two rooms until after 4:30. I did speak with the manager and he was extremely contrite and helpful, however the front desk clerk was not so much. The other rude staff encounter we had was with the server in the breakfast area who treated us a little better than garbage, snapped at one of our friends for accidentally picking up the water he laid down for the person to her left, and split coffee inches from my elbow without the hint of an apology, it was very weird. I was also disappointed that there was no pool, and the beach is about an hour and half round trip by walking to the pier and taking the water taxi over to Coronado, so a little inconvenient for the sun-soak-seekers. All in all it is a very cool hotel, great location, however the staff were very hit or miss, some were awesome, some were rude. I would take my chances here again however, and would just try to keep in my the areas that I could expect some underwhelming service.

“Your standard Marriott” It has been almost 8 years since I was last here and amazing how little it has changed but that's not a bad thing. The rooms have had a mild upgrade in those years but there is still little character to the place. Still the rooms where very comfortable and clean and the beds where wonderful. I ordered room service which although fine was very expensive for what it was and perhaps I'll think again regarding eating in the hotel again. The gym was great and the staff in the lobby, bar and Starbucks very helpful and the free shuttle to the nearby Gallaria mall was a life saver considering the cold weather during my visit! All in all a very comfortable stay although nothing spectacular!

“Good for airport hotel” Stayed here 2 nights as part of a business meeting last week. Check in line was rather long, however I am Hilton Honors member which had an expedited line. Otherwise waiting on that line would have been a bummer. Check in process was ok, there was an error on the rate that they had but they addressed the problem when brought to their attention. Room was fine though a little smaller than what I would have expected for an airport hotel (i usually expect smaller rooms in city hotel) but for 1 person it was ok. Bed was very comfortable and flat screen TV with HD channels worked well (so many places boast their flat screen tvs but then have crummy reception). Bathroom functional with good shower. I ate in sports pub one night, burger and salad were good (meat done on the rare side so take note, my medium came red and my friend's medium rare came back very rare). Location is this hotels strongest point. Easy access to airport and easy access to the blue line. For $2.25, I was in downtown Chicago in about 35 min. I had dinner downtown on the second night and getting to/from was a breeze.

“Very nice hotel, and close to the Victoria Clipper Ferry Dock” We stayed at this hotel our last night in Seattle before departing for Victoria. The hotel was great and so was the staff. Very short taxi ride to the ferry. Would stay there again.

“Nice Business Atmosphere” The rooms were clean and the lobby is one of Marriott's newest lounge renovations. Overall a very nice place to stay. My only complaint was the old-style air conditioner without a thermostat, which kept running all night. However the beds were very comfortable and the bathrooms were very clean. A nice business hotel, but like all other Courtyards the breakfast is not complimentary. The hotel is also very close to popular restaurants and the Dallas downtown and uptown.

“Quite Acceptable Midtown Hotel” My one-night stay was paid for by the organization whose meeting I was attending, and they had a conference rate of $239 which is reasonable for a good Manhattan midtown location. With a good rate, the Radisson counts as perfectly acceptable in all crucial ways. • Room: my "business class" room was small but not claustrophobic. Bed was new and comfortable, nice flat-screen TV, desk and chair. Everything clean and tidy, and the climate control responsive and efficient. No obstrusive street noise. • Bathroom: small but this is an older renovated hotel, so fixtures not brand new but clean and okay. Good lighting, hair dryer on wall, good shower head and quality towels. • Location: At Lex/48th an easy walk to Grand Central Station and subways in all directions; a subway stop at Lex/51st very convenient. Easy walk to a number of shops, museums, etc.. • In general, this is a good visitor's hotel if gotten at a good price.

“Omni on Michigan is a Dream.” Got a good deal on a weekend pacage in this Hotel and have to say it is the nicest stay I have had in more than a dozen business trips to Chicago. All rooms are Suites, staff is friendly and professional, Restaurant is out of this world and all the extras like a great health club, turn down service, complimentary morning beverages delivered to room and on and on. Room was very clean and every need was attended to without feeling intruded on. Will definately stay here again.

“Great convention hotel” We stayed here for a meeting at the convention center. The hotel is directly adjacent to the convention center at easy walking distance. I believe it was built in mid 80s but has had very recent renovation and upgrades, does look and feel very new. I had my reservation months in advance but due to high volume receptionist first told me they could not accommodate our request for a king bed. Upon my protest and reminder that I am a Marriott rewards member we were given a king room in the north tower with a beautiful view of the marina. Rooms and facilities were above average compared with other marriott properties. Elevator service was quick since we were just on the third floor. Valet was pricey, but pretty efficient. You can text message to retrieve your car. We did not try any of the food services. Location is just minutes walking to the gas lamp quarter with a variety of breakfast, lunch, and dinner choices. I would stay again.

“Nice hotel, just noisy” I spent two nights here on business and have mixed feelings about the place. Overall, it's nice -- very clean, the rooms are well-appointed, and it's close to the airport, downtown, shopping, beaches, and anything else you would want in San Diego. However, the proximity to the airport means that sleeping in is a problem, because a bank of flights departs starting at about 6am, and at least on the side of the hotel I was on, it was pretty loud. And if you want to sit outside near the pool and have a conversation, you'll be pausing periodically to let the planes pass overhead. The rooms are also rather small and cramped -- it would have felt crowded with another person. My room on the third floor had a rooftop view and the housekeeping room was nearby, so I heard lots of noise from that also. And there was only one small elevator at my end of the hotel. I'm not sure if there was another one at the other end, but it did get slow and crowded in the morning when people were checking out. Most of the staff was friendly, and the shuttle to the airport is free and quick. It's an okay place to stay if you need convenience, are traveling with one or maybe two people, and aren't going to be there for more than a night or two.

“Great Location” Check-in took about 10 minutes, but the upgrade to the river view room was fabulous. The views are great and this hotel is attached to the Prudential center and is in close proximity to shopping, restaurants, and tours, etc. Elevators didn't take a long time even though there are about 36 floors. I would definitely stay here again when I am in Boston.

“A pleasant stay in a boutique hotel with a great location in the Loop” I stayed two nights in May 2012 and was overall quite pleased. Would not hesitate to return and would recommend it, provided you don't need a full service hotel with a grand lobby. This hotel has a great location, helpful staff, modern and clean rooms and public areas, and a compelling price (booked through Travelocity's 'mystery hotel' arrangement). There are actually two hotels sharing the same building and entrance, the Central Loop Hotel and the Chicago Guest Quarters. They have a common lobby and some of the same facilities, but the rooms are on different floors. The name of the hotel aptly describes its location: It is about as well located in the Loop as one could imagine. If you are coming in from O'Hare, take the CTA Blue Line to Monroe or Jackson and walk to the hotel in five minutes. If it is rush hour, you will get there quicker than a taxi. In any event, you will save yourself a bundle on the cab fare. The reception staff were friendly and efficient. There are kiosks for self-checkin, but the staff handled it for me. My room was on the sixth floor. Each room shares a small side corridor with another room, which is off the main corridor. So, your room door is very close to the other room door, and a noisy neighbor coming and going could be bothersome, but that wasn't the case for me. The room was smaller than most hotels, but well laid out and equipped. Furniture and furnishings looked almost new. Large stall shower in the bathroom, but no tub. Bathroom lighting was terrific. Room had a built-in desk, minifridge, microwave and coffee maker. Fast and free Wifi. Very comfortable bed with lots of pillows. Housekeeping did a great job before and during stay. Room was spotless. The room is well lit, which is important as it doesn't get a lot of natural light from its one window. I did not utilize the restaurant. There are plenty of restaurants of all types and price points in the neighborhood. There is a 7/11 across the street with a good variety of hot and cold breakfast foods. The exercise facility has four treadmills, two elliptical trainers, one all purpose weight machine, free weights, and a stretching area. The room and equipment were very clean and well maintained. There is an unmanned business center with PCs and printers. No charge to use. Overall, I think the Central Loop Hotel presents a very good value proposition: A good, clean, modern hotel, with free wifi, exercise room and business center, but with smaller rooms, no gift shop, no grand lobby, no room service, no minibar, etc. If you don't need the frills you can save yourself a lot of money.

“Needs Remodeling” Pro: The Westin's famous Heavenly Bed. Love the comforter, and all the pillows. Cons: Very out-of-date. Needs to be renovated badly. The wallpaper peeling off the hallway walls was our first indication that this Westin was not up to Westin standards. The room did not contain all the amenities listed on the website, such as a CD player. We were told that none of the rooms have CD players, so why is it listed on their website? This Westin will not leave you feeling pampered. The Fairmont is across the street.

“Three Day Stay - Great Hotel Excellent Service” Stayed here for my godson's and his twin brothers graduation Friday to Monday 4 to 6 June. Wonderful stay! Room was clean and ceiling to floor windows gave great light and cheerfulness. LCD TV was at least 42 inches, swiveling for viewing from couch or bed. The mattress was great. The breakfast buffet was EXCELLENT! Besides cooked to order omelets and fresh made waffles, included fresh strawberries, fresh pineapples and smoked salmon. The pool was very nice and included iced water at the towel location. Saw a number of children with their parents. The exercise room was large and include a full set of ten pair of dumbells in 5 to 50 pound gradations. There were at least 5 machines. Room was clean. Examples of excellent service: 1. As a Hilton Gold, was given breakfast coupons normally good only for cold buffet, but I was offered the full buffet. 2. The waitress the first day when I was finishing breakfast asked me if I wanted a cup to take with me. 3. Asked at the desk where I could buy a newspaper over the weekend (normally USA Today only on weekdays) and was offered a free Houston newspaper. 4. While waiting for my omelet, the obvious manager asked me if I was being helped. I saw him walking around the restaurant, apparently inspecting, each morning I was there. The ONLY two small negatives, and the first is typical of many Hilton's, I had to ask for room upgrade and the internet connection was slow. Great hotel!

“Classic lines with a few wrinkles” RECOMMENDED. I'm only giving this AVG not because anything was wrong, simply that for the money it's an avg stay. As others have commented, this is an older hotel that has been renovated several times. Paint is thick on the wood from many years of service. Ceilings high from years were A/C wasn't invented. Furnishings of good quality but a bit worn. Check-in was prompt. Room was nicely sized, quiet, bathroom was moderately lighted with marble flooring. Basically the hotel is like a well worn shoe. It's certainly in an excellent location so if you get a good deal on the rate, it's worth a stay.

“Nothing Special” My husband and I stayed for four nights at the HIlton Austin. He attended a conference at the hotel and I was along to explore the city. If you don't mind sterile, chain hotels, then this place is OK. It offers good-sized rooms with modern bathrooms and robes. Our room had two double beds, a desk, two chairs and a flat-screen TV. The bathroom lacked a fan, though, so it was necessary to open the bathroom door after showering to get some air circulation. We were on the 23rd floor so there was a view of the surrounding area. But even at that height and with permanently closed windows, we heard music coming from noisy 6th Street, a block away, at night. We experienced maintenance problems. Our first room had an air conditioning unit that whined and groaned, so we complained and were given another room. This second room had a broken lamp, which we reported. A man came and took it away, indicating it would be replaced with another. That never happened. And there was a Housekeeping problem. One night, a piece of used chewing gum (my husband and I don't chew gum) worked its way out of the duvet on the bed. Guests crowded this big hotel, attending conferences on site or staying for a 3-day music festival. Thus, the elevators moved slowly, stopping at many floors, and the lobby was often exceptionally noisy. Reception seemed poorly prepared for check-in at times. For example, at 12:30 p.m. one day, I counted 35 people standing in line to register. Access to the fitness rooms requires a fee and it can be impossible to find available equipment early in the morning. The swimming pool is free. The hotel is easily accessed from the airport by bus (75 cents) and leaves you off a block away. Major tourist sites can be reached comfortably on foot and good restaurants are nearby. If we returned to Austin totally on a leisure trip, we would look for a smaller hotel with character.

“With old-school grandeur comes wear and tear” This is a large (900 beds) and historic hotel, and because of the latter it has a lot of charm that more contemporary properties lack. On the downside, many of the fittings and furnishings are on the old side. The elevators, for instance, are ancient, and the air conditioning in my room was highly ineffective. There is no doubt that this would be a fantastic hotel if it underwent a major refurbishment. On the plus side, the beds are very comfortable, there are plenty of TV channels to watch, and the location is excellent. I probably won't stay here again, but I'm glad that I did.

“A Mixed Bag! Gotta get a deal to balance out pluses and minuses” My wife and I just returned from a 2 night stay for a baseball game at Camden yard and booked our room through hotwire for a great rate. Pros: The bed was very comfortable for both my wife and I. The fitness center was larger than most I've been in with plenty of equipment. Checkin was very quick with front desk very helpful. Our room was clean and check out was very quick. Cons: The room didn't have a safe or a mini fridge. The absence of the safe being way more important. They did offer a safe deposit box downstairs but we didn't use it. The hotel location at night definately has the criminal element. I'm a police officer in another city and I felt uncomfortable at night but I did see police presence so that was good. I joked with my wife that when we were walking around the harbor i felt like we were on vacation but when we got back around the hotel I felt like I was on duty. No free wifi. Additional Info: We read previous reviews about parking so we didn't bother with valet or self park with hotel. The first night we paid $18.00 for 24 hrs. in the garage that runs underground. The second night we moved our car to another garage on Baltimore ave. for $12.00 for 24 hours. Previous reviewers mentioned cheaper options for parking but they neglected to mention where exactly these places are.The garage we used was on Baltimore between N. Liberty and N. Howard Streets Summary: If you get a great rate and don't need a room safe, free wifi or a mini-fridge and don't don't mind the location then you will be just fine here. If you spend more than $75 a night then I wouldn't recommend it.

“Great location, but lacking in other areas” You can't beat this hotel's location. Very central to the top attractions/restaurants/things to do in Boston. However, it is a VERY large hotel, so if you're not lucky, you may end up needing a lot of time to check in. Also, their room service is not the greatest. It took forever for them to deliver fresh towels to our room (~50 minutes from the first call). I stayed at the Towers level, and it was great to have breakfast and the space, but the staff in the lounge isn't the friendliest. The hotel/rooms are also a bit outdated, though, if you look at the pictures before you book (on TripAdvisor), then you shouldn't be in for any surprises. I'm undecided on whether or not I'd stay here again. It is SUPER convenient in terms of location, and if I was able to book a room at a good price, then maybe. Otherwise, I'd think about some of the other hotels in the vicinity that are on par or nicer.

“Not Up to Intercontinental Hotel Stadards” The Hotel itself has amazing potential. The location is great and the staff is very pleasant. The check in was easy and fast and they were very efficient. The rooms are VERY outdated and old. They need to refurbish them. The TV's were old and the reception on most of the stations showed static lines. The furniture was worn and used past its life. I was very disappointed that as a Platinum member that they charged me 15USD for Internet that was slow. I do not think any hotel should charge its elite members for Internet usage and I told this to the front desk upon check out and he just said, sorry but it is our policy. I realize that at this particular hotel it is policy, I just think it is bad policy that needs to be revisited. The one good thing about the hotel was the restaurant inside. It was great food and reasonable prices. I have stayed in at least 30 Intercontinental branded hotels in the last 10 years and this one was at the very bottom of the list for hotels that I would recommend to others. In fact, when I go back to Austin in a few weeks, I'll be staying at another hotel chain that I normally do not give my business to. The great thing about this hotel is that the potential is unlimited. They need a good management team in place that will spend some money on upgrades and staff customer service issues and they will be a 5 star hotel again. I wish them great luck as I love the brand but this hotel is not up to the name Intercontinental Hotel.

“Can't Say Enough Good Things About This Hotel” We had a total of three rooms at this hotel for three nights, and everyone in our party had a wonderful stay. There was a little snafu at check-in as two of the rooms were supposed to be Club rooms, but that was quickly rectified to our satisfaction. This hotel is only about 6 miles from the airport, is in close proximity to the convention center, and there are places nearby that you can walk to when you are ready to eat. Having said that, the restaurant in the hotel is great. Ten of us ate there on Saturday night and everyone enjoyed their meals as well as the service. Sunday night we attended a gala in the ballroom that included a sit down meal, and again the food was very good. It is not easy to serve that many people and have the food be tasty as well as the correct temperature, but the Sheraton pulled it off. Our room was 2145, the last room at the end of the hallway. It was extremely quiet, roomy and comfortable with a pretty view. The only suggestion I would make is that it would be nice to have more than two bath towels in the room, but that is a minor detail. The water pressure was more than adequate, and we appreciated the recycle bins in the room. We rarely had to wait on the elevators, but one very annoying feature is that you have to insert your room key before it will let you push the button for your floor. Sometimes the key would not work and you would miss your floor. While I realize this is a security measure, it is a big hassle for the guests. I did make use of the fitness room, and it was probably one of the best appointed facilities I have ever seen at a hotel. In addition to the assorted treadmills, bikes, etc. there were fitness machines and free weights. This hotel also has a lap pool which is rare as well.

“Good Hotel, but some customer service issues.” First the good: the Hotel's location is excellent right next to Boston Common. It was our first time in Boston and it was perfect for walking around the city. The rooms were clean and very large. The beds were comfortable. Service started out well with a very friendly bellman who was excellent throughout our stay. The front desk also had our room ready with dog bowls and a bed. Unfortunately, our view wasn't much to speak about as we were on the 14th floor so mostly saw the top of an adjacent building. Tried to get an upgrade as we did at the Palomar and Eventi on this trip by saying the secret summer password, but they said there were no view rooms available which was fine. This is where the problems started for us: first, I was told that I would be sent something to our room for the special perk, but asked if I could just get valet parking credited to my account instead. The front desk attendant said she would take care of this, so we left our car with the valet which at $42 on a weekend was clearly overpriced for the area since parking garages nearby are only around 10 - 15. Unfortunately we were only credited $18 out of the parking, so obviously there were mixed messages. The one downside to the room was that you could hear a lot in the hallway. In the morning there were lots of people talking and loud bangs from housekeeping staff. You also heard this in the evening, which became a problem for our dogs. We have taken our dogs to many Kimpton hotels and stayed in 3 on our trip without a problem. Apparently something startled our dogs and they were barking when we had gone out for a short dinner. The hotel called us, but unlike their policy states, did not leave a message. We were two minutes from the hotel and when we got to the front desk the person I was talking to said the dogs were at the front desk since they were barking, but they weren't there. Apparently we had gotten back so quickly that the person had just gone up to our room to check on them. My partner found her in our room giving the dogs treats which was just leading to further barking, etc. making our night a little stressful. A bit more of a quiet room like in the Palomar in Philly and Eventi in NYC would have prevented this problem and also would have led to a better night's sleep. Finally, the elevator's in the AM were extremely busy and took forever and the bathroom while very large lacked hooks for towels which was weird. I also was charged for minibar usage that should have been credited to my account because of the Kimpton In Touch program. It was taken care of when I discovered the charge, but I still had to call the hotel back which was annoying. Overall a very nice hotel in a good location with just a few customer service issues that could have made our stay more inline with our other Kimpton stays. Would definitely go back due to location and just hope for better luck with customer service.
“Excellent Value” Stayed here twice two weekends in a row. Great location close to the Beltway, good restaurants close by.

“Good Hilton choice” Good stay. Requested online and called ahead for early check-in and didnt get it. This was the only "blip" in our stay. They held our bags while our room was getting ready which was nice. Check-in was a breeze and room was in good condition. Restroom door was a bit worn but no worries there. Nice downtown view (was on 15th floor). Not centrally located so walking around was a bit much since the heat was killing us!! Overall a good stay and great customer service. Great cookies and coffee available in the front lobby.

“Nice hotel, good location” Stayed for 3 nights. booked via hotwire, upgraded to historic tower. Got a big room, with a nice view.Service was great. Valet parking was efficient, but you expect it for 53 doller/night. But the location was the best

“I made a good choice to stay here” I had a marvelous experience! Beautiful hotel, ideal location, friendly staff. The room (I was upgraded to the 12th floor, executive level) was clean, bathroom beautiful, and the view not bad either. Near Chinatown and within walking distance of the White House, National Mall, museums, restaurants, etc. (If you like Lebanese in a chic setting you MUST try the mezze restaurant Zayatanya, which is just 3 blocks from the Hyatt.) The breakfast buffet was a bit expensive ($19) but there was an excellent selection, and the atmosphere was quite tranquil. Omelettes made to order, homemade granola, yogurt, fruit, cereal, oatmeal...worth the splurge. I'm glad I gave it a chance and didn't listen to the people who gave this hotel such a bad rating.

“A Plus Hotel, Conrads Never Disappoint” This is a superb hotel. The rooms are huge, including a luxurious bathroom. It is clean and service is first rate. Breakfast was excellent (and complimentary for Hilton Honors members). Hotel is in a good location, and is connected to a mall, which I imagine would be a great asset in the Chicago winter. Next time I go to Chicago, I will stay here for sure.

“Business type hotel thats not worth it otherwise” My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights as a birthday getaway for myself. We got an ok deal off of priceline, or so we thought. As it turns out it wasn't worth the price we paid, not necessarily because of what we paid, but because we didnt spend enough time at the hotel. When you read reviews below you may get a distorted view of what to expect from this Hyatt. Yes the valet is a rip off, but you only have one other choice, a self parking lot behind the hotel for 24 rather then 35, so maybe the valet really is worth it because you can do in and out. If you need to stop by the hotel during the day, just park at the shopping mall that is right next door for 2 hours free parking, problem solved. They of course charged us for 4 days of valet parking even though all we did was pull up and leave our car upfront to check in. They removed that from our bill, but I have not checked with my credit card yet to see if they messed that one up yet. I would suggest giving a bogus name to the valet if you do that so you don't have to fight them about it later. Service was acceptable, but not worthy of a 4 star rating. We had no special needs, so couldn't really judge the 'above and beyond'. When it comes to the room, many other reviews seem to dislike it. Its a very typical business hotel. Everything is ok, nothing spectacular. The balcony is great though to sit on in the morning. The tv in the room is big enough. Don't even think about touching the minibar. And yes it really is $5/day to have the contents removed, if that isn't the dumbest charge I have ever seen, then I would love to get your emails. As far as noise, well, the hotel was built probably in the 60's so its horrible. You can hear anyone in the hall, anyone above you, below, and any vehicle driving by the hotel. We were on the 9th floor, so maybe that contributed. My only suggestion, get to sleep early because traffic in the morning will wake you. The bed was not comfortable for me (too hard) but my wife said her back felt great in the morning, so it evens out. There were 5 different pillows on the bed to chose from, so that was nice. A/C works well, shower was fine, only one sink (again, the business hotel thing). There was a nice desk if you need it, as well as a chair and ottoman. On the negative, there was mold in the bathroom and the towels never get dry. The quality of tile work in the entire hotel is horrendous, especially by the elevators, they should be ashamed of themselves for keeping even a day. The hotel only changes the sheets and towels if you call down to ask (we dont change our sheets and towels daily at home so why would we at a hotel) People that complained about the "no coffee maker" didn't read the sign in the room that said if you want one all you have to do is ask and they will bring you one. Wifi costs more in your room (yet another perk of a business hotel) but is free in the lobby. We were on the 9th floor and connected to a local hotspot, CAA guest it was called, so we were happy. Pool looked nice, but we didnt use it, and it was shady in the afternoon, good suntanning...haha. The location is great if you want to see all of LA. Any meal you want can be found at the mall next door, but please, eat local, not chains. We went looking for food trucks and found several that were outstanding, thats the fun of being in a new city. Funny thing about this hotel, on old maps its a Westin, and the Intercontinental that is on the same road closer to Fox is the old Hyatt. Interesting choice since people seem to like the IC better. Can't confirm, but have read this Hyatt is not corporate run, which is probably why they just don't care about the quality and what they offer like the other Hyatts I have stayed at in the past. Summation. It is a business hotel. We were not on business. We overpaid (thanks priceline) for what we got, the location could have been better, the hotel should have been better, and not worth a dime over 90 bucks (thanks LA). I do love LA though. I can't imagine anyone actually picking this hotel of their own free will, either priceline or hotwire sticks you there, or you have a conference at this hotel which is a matter of convenience.

“Spacious room in great location” Was in Chicago on business for 2 nights in early November. Appreciated the proximity to the State/Lake station, as well as to many locations of interest. Best part, though, was being able to kick back in the suite-style room in the evening. Appreciated the kitchen, extra lounge space, and comfortable bed with a fantastic view. Will be returning next month and will definitely be staying here!

“Above Average, but bot great” one block to Magnificent mile, only the hotel itself is not so magnificent. location,view all very impressive decoration,exterior not so much so i guess 4 out of 5 is fair oh wait, the internet? 5 out of 5 sucks.

“Excellent choice for value and location!” We always spend the hoiidays in NYC and most often stay at another hotel. This year, our regular was all booked up, so we tried the Hampton Inn Times Square North and it was great. Have two teenagers, so room size matters - and this was fine. Very clean, comfortable beds and a very courteous staff. Breakfast was an added bonus and, in the end, saves lots of money for other shopping. Good access to Internet (free wireless in the room). Location is outstanding - one block from the E train (perfect for access from JFK) and one additional block for other north/south access lines. Right off of Times Square - but without the noise and crowds that you might expect. One piece of advice - if you're having breakfast, go early because it gets very busy around 8:00 a.m. In addition, the elevators get a little crowded in the morning. Nothing that can't be overlooked though. Overall, a great stay at a great hotel.

“Good choice if you get a deep discount” I won the Prescott Hotel on a Priceline bid of $85/night for a 3-night weekend stay in mid-November. I was a bit concerned about previous TA reviews citing musty-smelling rooms, dirty carpets, old bathrooms, noise, non-functioning wi-fi, etc. Fortunately, I didn't experience any of these problems during my 3 nights there, and overall I was happy with my stay, esp. considering the discounted price I paid. My late night check-in was quick and painless. I was given a room on the 6th floor. It faced the elevators, but noise from the hallway was never an issue. The room's only view was of an internal airshaft and other rooms, but the upside to this was that it was quiet. A street-facing room would have been much noisier. The only noise I ever got was an occasional creaky floorboard, as you would expect in an older building; this never bothered me. The room itself was compact but well laid out and well decorated, in a sort of Ralph Lauren brown paisley theme. I think two people with two large suitcases would have felt quite cramped in the room. Since I was staying by myself, I rather liked the room's snug and cozy proportions. Thankfully, there was no evidence of the musty smell that other reviewers had referred to. Also, the carpet was perfectly clean and the free wi-fi worked great throughout my 3-day stay. The bathroom was very spacious, and must have been recently renovated, as the tile, grout, wallpaper and shower curtain were all pristine. Everything was gleaming and spic and span. Water temperature and pressure were perfect, and the bathrobes and the L'Occitane toiletries were nice touches. The "living room" in the lobby is well decorated and a great space in which to relax with a cup of coffee and a newspaper. Complimentary coffee and tea are served 6-10 AM every day. It's too bad this service isn't available all day long, as is the case with some other Union Square hotels. The range of complimentary newspapers, including the NYTimes and the Wall Street Journal, was much appreciated. I never tried breakfast in the Postrio restaurant off the lobby; it offers a very limited menu and is seriously overpriced. Instead, every morning I took my free cup of coffee and headed off to the unpretentious, casual and welcoming Honey Honey cafe just 1/2 a block away, at the corner of Post and Taylor. I didn't need any special services while staying at the Prescott, so only had superficial contact with the staff. I would say they ranged from gracious and efficient to just passable. The housekeeping staff was lovely and did an outstanding job cleaning my room. Some of the front desk staff seemed more interested in gossiping and joking among themselves than in helping guests. One morning, I (very politely) let the young woman at the concierge desk know that the coffee carafe was empty, and she said not one word to me the whole time she replaced it. No "good morning", no "you're welcome" when I thanked her; not a word. A few minutes later, I saw her give another guest the silent treatment, so it seems she wasn't allergic just to me. Quite a weird, off-putting experience more befitting of a hostel or budget hotel than one that bills itself as a luxury boutique hotel. I was able to shrug off the service lapses by reminding myself about my great Priceline deal. I'd definitely stay at the Prescott again for less than $100/night. But, for that weekend, the best rate available from the Prescott's own web site was $194/night - if I were paying that rate, I would find another hotel with better service standards and larger rooms.

“Wonderful Place to Stay” This hotel is awesome!! We stayed here for 2 nights and were absolutely delighted with the service, the hotel location and the excellent staff. We received a call 15 mins. after check-in from the front office staff to see how our room was- I was very impressed by this customer service touch. The breakfast buffet is great with fresh food (and lots of it). We plan to return to this hotel again and would highly recommend others to experience the ambience it has to offer.

“Beautiful room, noisy neighbors” The room would have been perfect, only marred by cigarette burns here and there. The pillow top mattress would have provided a nice rest, if it weren't for the very loud and generally inconsiderate displaced New Orleanians.

“Very Average Hotel” The hotel is located good area attached to the Prudential Center which gives great access to the convention center, restaurants and shopping. The rooms are on the small side, and the bathrooms are really tight. Housekeepers are very inconsistent, and do not have much of an eye for detail. I had a huge dark stained hand print on my shower curtain that went unnoticed for my entire stay. There were always lines at the front desk even at odd hours during the day. The concierge was no where to be found the two times I approached the desk on two different occasions.

“Loved this hotel... great location, excellent service. Perfect for work or just for fun.” I was looking for a hotel with a great location, clean and service focused, but I didn't want to break the bank. A friend suggested I check out the Kimpton loyalty program to find a good special (its free to sign up and I got free wireless). I ended up at the Serrano Hotel, and loved it. The staff was great... super friendly and ready to help. Already a great first impression with the character of the lobby and smiling front desk staff. I was working and needed some assistance, they could not have been more helpful. The room was comfortable and clean...everything I needed and right in Union Square. I didnt get a chance to eat at the restaurant, but I heard great things about it... and admittedly it smelled amazing when I walked by. Just not enough time this trip... but next time. I would go back for sure... and plan to.

“Excellent accomodations, service, hospitality.” Michael A. Miller - 8/22-23/07 This is just an excellent hotel, no compromise in accommodations, hospitality, and general staff. Location is perfect for transportation and walking if you choose. Close to airport. Food is excellent as are hotel services.

“Needs Major Renovation, There are Better Options Nearby” Many recent reviews have pointed out that this Westin is undergoing a renovation. That renovation, however, is limited to the lobby/check-in area. Many more renovations are needed! The corridors are dreadfully dreary. New carpeting, new wall coverings, lighting all are needed. The wireless internet is an added fee, and functional. The fitness center is adequate, but I would expect better from a hotel in the Westin tier of properties. One small positive is that there is a real Starbucks in the lobby. That and the potential for low rates are the only things I see recommending this property. I stayed at it because it was the site for my meeting, and therefore I got an extremely low rate. Otherwise I would opt for either the Hyatt or JW Marriott nearby.

“Very SPG Elite Friendly. Great Rooms and Front Desk Staff” We have stayed here 3 times recently. Two of the three times we were upgraded to very nice suites and given concierge lounge privileges every time – even though I had only Gold status the first two times. Front Desk staff always was very helpful, with Brian Scruggs being the most recent very helpful staff member. Parking is very expensive (more than $50/day...but that seems to be true for all downtown area Chicago hotels). Cheaper ($30/day) parking is available next door, but one has to either climb 2 flights of stairs or (as I eventually found out) enter hotel’s lower level on riverside of eastern side of hotel through or next to Chicago Burger restaurant and use an escalator. Also even when not crowded, doorman needs your car keys when you check in or checkout. The concierge lounge is huge (two stories tall!), and has, in my SPG hotel experience, a pretty minimal breakfast buffet. Aside from hard-boiled eggs, milk and some cream cheese, the only protein available is in sugary yogurt. You can get plain yogurt, but you have to ask in advance. No complaints about room- great bed, lighting, electric outlet availability, Internet, desk, temperature control and bath room facilities. Décor was pleasing

“Very nice, but isolated.” Large, bright, clean room. Looked like it had been recently painted. Bathroom large and very clean, but showing its age. We had a bayview room with a peek a boo view of the city skyline. Impressive. Quiet. Staff was helpful and professional. Very good valet and bell service. Ate at the restaurant. Decent wine list, but expensive. Food was good, but barely warm. Service very good. Good place to stay as a destination, but isolated from the city and almost everything else.

“The Standard has evolved into something special” I have been staying at the Standard for years but I have never been compelled to write a review because of inconsistencies in service, room quality, and stays. However, I think they are either trying to ramp up their quality or I was there over a slow weekend. Nonetheless, aside from the super stylish rooms and ambiance, the hotel was "on" this past weekend. Room service took less than 15 minutes and other services were excellent and timely. Every inch of the hotel was clean and tidy and the rooftop pool was fantastic. No complaints this time around. The Standard has definitely made its mark in downtown LA as the stylish business hotel of the moment.

“Nice Place - Enjoyed my stay” I stayed at this hotel for two nights during a business trip. The breakfast buffet which includes omelets, pancakes, bacon, fruit, cereal, sausages, biscuits, etc. was a nice touch. To top it off they also offer a Happy Hour with snacks which usually lasts approximate 2 hours in the evening. This is a nice atmosphere to unwind after a busy day. The bartendars are so nice and willing to accomodate you on any drinks that can be made as long as they have the ingredients on the mini bar. The Front Desk and Concierge staff are willing to assist you with any thing to make your stay at the hotel more pleasureable. These employees made my stay even more memorable with the pleasant smiles and lovely attitudes displayed on a daily basis. Hats are off to them for the job they do everyday. The hotel provides a shuttle bus and offers rides within a 5 mile radius of the hotel. No, they do not pick up from DFW airport, this is out of range. There is also a restaurant located on the premises with a friendly bartendar to keep you company.

“A Good Stay” I stayed here on a Monday night to catch an early flight from Intercontinental. I got the room on Priceline for a great price and was pleased. The shuttle service was great - allowing me to avoid an additional days rental by returning it in the afternoon before departure. Check-in was quick and efficient - and was permitted to check-in at 1:30, facilitating the rental car return by 2:00. I thought this was a very nice gesture on a Priceline room. The bed was extremely comfortable. The only negative was the room, which was both nice and clean, did have a musty smell on the order of a smoker having been in there before me. Did not complain since it was not overpowering.

“Wonderful relaxing stay” I am trying to go through all the Kimpton Group hotels and this was my first stay at the Monaco in Seattle. Everything was a breeze, from check-in to check-out. The beds were incredibly comfortable and the room (a double queen room) was spacious. I especially liked the l'occitane shampoo and conditioner, it's a nice treat when the toilettries are nicer than what I use on a normal day. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants an upgrade to the other nearby downtown hotels.

“hang out in this beautiful hotel” If, like me, one of your hobbies is luxury hotels, you might like to see this one. The grounds and the public areas are georgeous. So many palm trees! We were there during the great weather in March, and the huge hotel lobby was open to the outside pool area, making it feel very spacious and inviting. You can sit around fire pits, near the pool, in the lobby, or back by the golf course. A great hotel for hanging out, and at these high spring prices, you want to and get your money's worth. The "lazy river" is perfect for kids. The spa is beautiful, and you can spend hours there just relaxing. Just across a street is an upscale shopping center with many restaurants and a grocery store, so it is great for families. The only thing I would not rave about are the rooms - the bathrooms are wonderful, but the rooms themselves are slightly above standard Marriott. But most have incredible views! I have stayed at many nice hotels and this is one of the most pleasant for just spending time.

“Efficient Service, Good Location” Check-in service pleasant. There was a printer and computer in the lobby for boarding passes which is a convenient touch. Elevators weren't crowded. King size bedroom nice and big. Bed very comfortable. Wake-up call worked. 2/3 blocks from Westlake Centre so convenient location.

“Good - but won't stay again.” This is a two part review. We stayed here prior to a return flight to the UK in May 2011 - the night they caught Osama Bin Laden! The hotel is well located hotel at LAX which makes for a very comfortable overnight. The shiuttle from LAX may not be the most frequent but its a short ride to Airport Blvd. The interior of the hotel is a huge atrium with rooms facing in. It was something of an oasis from the bustle and general madness that is LAX. Rooms were, as you'd expect from Embassy, well appointed and comfortable. Ours had a mini balcony although the only thing to see outside was traffic. Soundproofing could have been better. I think I'd rather have had a fixed soundproofed window than one that opened onto the balcony. Hotel facilities were also good. There was a small indoor pool and a business suite with two PCs and free internet access. next to reception there was a 24 hour shop witha selection of drinks, snacks and last minute items. Drinks were also available from vending machines on each floor. The atrium was the location for the breakfast buffet. It looked really attractive for a relaxing breakfast although it was crowded and teh organisation of teh cooked to order items made service slower and more complicated than it needed to be. Overall it was disappointing but could be aesily improved. We returned the rental car before arriving. The car parking charges were rather high. In fact, if they'd been a bit lower I'd probably have stayed here for 3 days (instead we spent two days at the Raddison Residence Inn at Manhattan). Staff were helpful and efficient. Check in and out was quick. Overall, it was a nice place to relax before a flight home. So why won't I stay again? When I arrived home I found I'd been charged $5 for a bottle of water we hadn't used. mainly I was annoyed that they thought I was stupid enough to pay for an overpriced bottle of warm water when there was a refridgerated vending machine at teh end of the corridor that charged half that! I used the Hotel's online web form to advise them that the charge was incorrect and could they reconsider it - but didn't get an answer. I suppose I could have disputed the charge with Visa but, to be honest, life's too short to waste over a $5 overcharge. Instead I'll stay somewhere else when we visit LAX next (normally we pass through twice a year). Embassy Suites may be $5 up at the moment but they'll lose far more in turnover.

“Bad hotel experience - would not recommend!” I was truly disappointed in all areas regarding this property. My room was not very clean and poorly maintained. It had a musty smell that I could not get past - new carpet needed. The staff were slow to check-in and were not vey friendly. I was hungry and asked for a restaurant recommendation - they suggested the Jack-In-The-Box across the street. This hotel is literally on the street entering the airport - plane noise is constant. The hotel gift shop was not open from the time I arrived until I left. I would definitely not stay here again. I stay in hotels about 200 nights a year - this one is in the bottom 10 of the year. I have stayed in Motel6 properties that were nicer. If the rate is below $35 go for it, but otherwise pass or you will be disappointed.

“Good not great” Stayed here one night for business in September because the normal Chicago hotel I use was booked. The location was convenient. The check in was fine although the staff wasn't as friendly or helpful as I was hoping. One thing I don't like about Crowne Plaza's in general is no water in the room, and having to resort to the vending machines on the floor. For business travelers that is pretty annoying. I ordered room service and it was quite good and have no complaints there. The fitness center was small, and multiple machines were broken but there was one working elliptical and one treadmill.

“Great location, good hotel” We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights over the weekend. We were greeted at the taxi by the door staff and helped in with our luggage, the check in was good and then another guy took us and our luggage to our room. The staff were very helpful when we were trying to make decisions about where to eat, what tours to do and how to get there. The room was nice, nothing out of the ordinary, mini bar, safe, loads of hanging space and coat hangers, TV etc... The bathroom was quite small and there was no where to dry wet towels apart from on the rack above the toilet....I didn't like that. The shower was over the bath, which isn't a problem normally, but it was annoying that you couldn't get in at the bottom on the bath as it was too sloped, so you have to get in the tap end and get straight in the water...again..not a massive issue...when the shower stopped I could hear water under the bath but not drained away, like there was a layer between the floor of the bath and the bottom? weird. Breakfast offered is tea, coffee and hot chocolate and there is a wine reception every evening 5-7pm. This was the 2nd time we had stayed at A kimpton hotel and we received a $10 mini bar voucher to use because of this. Location was excellent, 2 mins from union square, cabel car stop, subway lines..etc All in all it was good.

“Impeccable Service” I was here on business again and they really took care of me. I had a great corner room. The housekeeping staff was so friendly and helpful. I arrived in my room and realized that they have gotten rid of all of there fridges in the hotel. I was going to be here for 3 weeks and needed one. I am a diamond member so I called down to the front and they accomidated me :-) This hotel is so central to everything and our go to place when we are in the city.

“Amazing Service” The number one thing that stuck out at me was the amazing service from every single person who worked at the hotel. From the bar tender, to valet, to front desk, they all were on top of their game. I have to say the valet is one of the best I have experienced in town. They were by far the quickest at bringing my car up than any other hotel in the area. The rooms were nice, nothing amazing but still very nice. The bed was very comfortable, got a good nights sleep every night. The bathroom was good, with a rainfall shower and 2 sinks. There was no bathtub, just a walk in shower. The one thing I did not like was the hardwood floors in the room. You could hear the people above and beside you whenever they walked. It wasn't a huge deal but that would be the only negative about the stay. A few other random things...The location was great with easy access. There is a grocery store and starbucks across the street so you have everything you need within walking distance. Parking is $35 per day but that is about normal for any hotel in Beverly Hills. The complimentary wifi was a nice bonus though.

“Completely Medicore, Older Hotel Which Is Good For No More Than 1 Night” Okay, so I understand you don't go to airport hotels for their fabulous accommodations and amazing dining and incredible customer service. You pretty much know they will be high-volume hotels which offer the basics. Due to my job, I am put in this hotel often. And it's fine. It's good for a shower and a night's sleep. This is an old hotel....like 1970s old. But they are in the midst of a room renovation (sorely needed), which is making it a little more liveable. The old style tube tvs are being replaced by large flat screens, the stained carpeting is being replaced by a fresh new design and the overall new room style is modern and boutique-ish. The bathrooms do still feel old, but they are clean and offer the new Peter Thomas Roth bath products. This Hilton offers 2 dining options - a 24-hour cafe that offers pizza, salads and sandwiches, and a full-service restaurant. Both are not that great, but there is nothing to eat in the area (except for fast food). The Landings Bar also offers some food options. I've never had the room service, but that is available as well. The bartenders in the Landings Bar make great drinks and are friendly. There are large crowds at this hotel. There are often lines for the airport shuttle and the hotel hosts large conventions with weird people - just imagine a hotel overrun by people dressed in anime outfits, stuffed animals or wizards. Most of the staff are pretty friendly and handle the weird crowds well. However, the front desk staff are a little irritable at times, and you can tell they are tired of the chaos and just want to go home. Eventhough the hotel is located right at the airport with views of the runways, it is fairly quiet. I've never had trouble sleeping here, except for some of the noisy rooms next to housekeeping closets. I have also had a couple rooms with heat that didn't work. On cold nights, it kind of sucks. Both times it was late and I was tired, so I had to run the shower at full heat to steam up the room since it was so cold. This is a perfect hotel for one night before or after a flight. Any longer than that, you will be unhappy by the crowds, old feel of the hotel and lack of anything to do in the area.

“Great stay and wonderful complimentary incentives!” This hotel provided us with the perfect location for dinner, access to the American Airlines Center for our event, and nice picture moments due to the Christmas decorations near the hotel. The hotel offered a nice cocktail hour that Saturday from 5:30 to 6:30, which included two complimentary cocktails (beer or wine) per occupant. It also offered cookies and milk from 8-10 PM, but we were unable to participate in this due to plans. A complimentary breakfast was also provided, which offered more than what I thought it would. I enjoyed it! I would have liked more than one mirror in the room besides the one in the bathroom, but that was manageable. I would stay here again if I were attending an event downtown.

“Outstanding NYC Nightlife” I was a guest of a member of Soho House NYC club. As a result, I enjoyed the benefits of well mixed drinks on the uber cool rooftop deck on a hopping evening in the Meatpacking district. A very memorable experience, and one I relished, and will relish in memory.

“Good DC Choice” With many different options in DC the Park Hyatt is a good choice. The location is great being near both DuPont Circle and Georgetown and not far from K Street and the museums. The decor is modern and fresh and the room was designed well with a spacious bathroom and living area. Service was good but not great but overall the hotel exceeded my expectations. Also the Park Hyatt is a good value compared to the Ritz or Four Seasons in Georgetown. I liked this hotel and would return.

“Average” It has comfort of being in main area of the manhatten city and close to times square. It's small but neat room, free internet wireless facility with morning breakfast & gym. Little congested.but still good option for one who want to stay in the heart of the city and travelling for business or leisure. Location is just perfect. Jet Previlage Membership No. [--]

“The Best” There is little more to say about this hotel other than it is absolutely superb. For some reason they gave me a unit with two rooms, and one could easily get lost... State of the art appliances, first class amenities, helpful and unobtrusive staff. And the view of Alcatraz from my room was amazing! It must be said that their free breakfast is a real continental offer with fresh juices, cereals and fruit, not the ordinary coffee and pastries offered at some other places. Fisherman Wharf itself is not that attractive, with an endless row of souvenir stores. But you do get a wide choice of very good restaurants nearby, on all price ranges, which the staff will be happy to reserve for you. Would love to go back here anytime.

“Outstanding overall experience” Our stay at the newly renovated Public Chicago was outstanding. I was hesitant to book with a hotel that opened within the last month with new staff and still working out operational kinks. From the moment the bellman unloaded the luggage from the taxi, too the personal greeting from the front desk attendant, it was very evident the staff had been expertly trained and already functioning as if they were open for years. After seeing my initial room which was beautiful and well designed, I inquired if a larger room was available for my 3 night stay and my request was handled within minutes and a bellman was there to happily move our things to the new space which was exactly what I was looking for. During our stay we used every food service offered by the hotel, from the bar to the restaurant to room service for breakfast lunch and dinner on various days; in every situation our expectations were exceeded. The food and beverage quality as well as the service were top notch and most surprisingly fairly priced. The hotel had the new hotel buzz and was full of beautiful people, both employees and guest. Our only regret was that we did not get to spend more time in our room and in the hotel. I have stayed at every 5 star hotel in Chicago and although the other hotels have much more visible staff standing around to open doors and greet guest, Public Chicago's service far exceeded that of every other hotel in the City. I know some of the luxury hotel chains pride themselves on "anticipating" guest needs, every need cannot be anticipated. For those needs or special request which always come up no matter how nice the hotel as they did at Public Chicago, the staff at Public fulfilled every request quicker, more efficiently and with happier staff than any service from any hotel I have experienced. The commend the owners and management from doing such a tremendous job with the Public Chicago, you have created a truly sheik environment that allows everyone enjoy it at a fair price with outstanding service, congratulations!

“Great place to stay!” We stayed for two nights with our 2 1/2 month old and it was great. Our room had plenty of space to spread out in, great furniture and lighting, and free wired and wireless internet. Everything was very clean and it was great to have a kitchen to use for dinners. The staff was so friendly and helpful and the hot breakfast (eggs, sausage, potatoes, oatmeal plus all the normal continental stuff) was a nice perk. The pool is on the 27th floor and has great views over the city, they also have a nice exercise room up there and a laundry facility. The only thing I would warn about is that it's about a 10-15 minute walk to get to Michigan Ave, which for us with a baby made it difficult to get out and shop a lot. Overall a great hotel!

“Central Modern Boston Sheraton” We stayed in this central modern (next to the Prudential Center tiwth cafes and shopping mall) hotel for two days on the 25th fl, North Tower which has updated recently refurbished rooms. Riverview is spectacular, elevators are fast, and the K and Q rooms are the same size, having tried both. There is free internet for guests in the lobby by the Starbucks and a separate boarding pass printing machine. Breakfast provided by the function we attended in Apropos was a nice buffet breakfast, but less expensive and better options available on nearby Newbury Street-try Charlie's. If you are an art & architecture fan seek out the free tour at the public library two blocks away and make sure you view the reading room, hammer beam ceiling on the third floor, and the EA Abbey murals on the 4th floor; currently, nice small Toulouse Lautrec show at the MFA. Metro is nearby, reached thru the Prudential Center-from the airport, change at Govt Center to Green Line, Heath St.

“Like the revamped lobby” Choose this hotel because of a Marriott Rewards bonus offer. Overall a pleasant stay. This is a new property and was my first experience with the newly introduced lobby that Marriott has been pushing at it CY locations. Spacious, plenty of TVs, full service eatery, convenient business center, three different newspapers (gratis). The location is great, right between downtown and the JAX beaches, walking distance to a brand new wal-mart, nice pool with hot tub. A really nice touch is a fire pit by the pool which you don’t usually see at CYs and the landscaping was impressive for this type of property.

“Nice Stay” Okay, as a San Diego native, there is no question that the Sheraton still retains that California feeling. In fact if you take your self (Walking) outside of the hotel and to the East you will see an amazing view of downtown that even I did not know existed. In fact, you usually have to go to to the other side by way of the Coronado Bay Bridge to enjoy such a view. Minutes from the very best of San Diego: Balboa Park, San Diego Zoo and Gaslamp Quarter. I find at times that the hotel transported me to circa 1970's, but the pool and grounds more than made up for this. I do agree with the other reviewers: For a grander experience, the Marina Tower has exceptional service and closer to the middle of all of the action.

“Delightful stay!” What a pleasure it was to stay overnight at the San Carlos last week! I am in New York every other month or so, to visit famliy, and none of us had ever heard of the San Carlos before! I usually like to stay in midtown, and the location, at the intersection of 50th and Lexington ,is central to many NY attractions (although it is about a $13 cab fare to downtown). Check-in was a breeze. The lobby is small, but simple, elegant and quiet. I booked a Corner Superior Room for $399 a night (mid week) and found out I had been upgraded to a Corner One Bed Room Suite! Sweet!!!!! Our room (701) was on the 7th floor. It had a mini kitchenette (microwave, sink, table, chairs, coffeemaker, plates, glasses, etc.), a very generous size sitting room, a nice size bedroom with a large queen bed (maybe a small king, we couldn't quite tell), a full bath (large by NY standards) and 2 generous closets. In addition, we had 2 flat screen TVs, fully stocked mini-bar and Aveda bath products. Our views of 50th St. and Lex. were great. You can hear a bit of street noise from the 7th floor, but I am a very light sleeper, and it did not disturb me. The bedding was very soft and comfortable, but the bed was a little harder than I like it. As I was getting ready for bed, I noticed a little sign on the nightstand that said that housekeeping will has various pillows and bed toppers to chose from. I was too tired at that point to see if they has a pillow top for my mattress. The room and bathroom were spotless, as were all common areas. I never had to wait for more than a minute or so for an elevator. My room rate included a continental breakfast, which was served in a room off the lobby. The breakfast was adequate. All tables were taken, so I took my cottage cheese, yogurt and pastry up to my suite, and enjoyed it there. All of the staff I encountered was super friendly and helpful. Someone at the front desk got my husband and I a dinner reservation at Avra for that evening, after we had called ourselves, and were told they were all booked. I don't even think she was a conceirge, but like I said, the staff was wonderful! There is an Indian restaurant on-site, but the room service menu was very limited. If room service is very important to you, this is the one area that this hotel seems lacking in. As a veteran NYC traveler, I 100% recommend the San Carlos hotel.

“Great Location, Great Place to Party” This hotel was in a great location, right at the entrance to the Gaslamp District which has a tonne of shopping, eating, and partying spots. It's also right across the street from a trolley car stop which will get you around town easy without renting a car. The hotel itself was very nice. Rooms were clean and trendy, bed was supper comfy and the bathroom shower with two rain shower heads was great..... The two clubs within the hotel were also good. Super busy on Friday and Saturday nights if thats what you are in to. The club on the main level causes the hotel lobby to get extremely loud. This didn't seem to affect us at all as we were on the 6th floor. The club guests also have to cut across the lobby to get to the washrooms, so later at night theres lots of drunk people stumbling thru the lobby. Not the place to take the family, but a great stay for a guys, girls or young couples weekend.

“Close to TCU, good shopping” This is not the most elegant Residence Inn you will find- the building is older and yes, a little dark, but there are plenty of amenities: a nice workout facility, lovely pool, a great cafe/bar that was always bustling when I was there, and direct access to the river. It is also just a few minutes walk from great shopping and restaurants, and is quite close to TCU. The biggest problem with the hotel was noise from the railroad. It didn't bother me too much, but my husband had trouble sleeping. The trains are noisy. The staff was pleasant and the facilities clean.

“My Favorite of the W Hotels” I have stayed at here several times (5+) for business. The W Westwood is my favorite W Hotel in the US. The service is impeccable and the location is great! This particular W has the largest hotel rooms (standard room) of any W Hotel I've ever stayed at. I would recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to LA - business or pleasure.

“It's fine” Good business location. It's starting to look a bit dated. it's clean, rooms are fine. Not special. Great views. Good luck finding a bellman or valet. Never could find help at the front door. Front desk staff were helpful. Lobby bar seemed understaffed. Starwood needs to give this place a facelift. I always stay here when in town, I still will, just wish the little things were better

“Location, location, location” If the title didn't tip you off, this hotel is probably in the best location in the city. Located on 15th St., you are exactly 10 blocks south of UT campus and the Drag, and 10 blocks north of the Historic 6th and 5th streets. You can literally spend your entire stay without getting into a vehicle. and all of the rooms have views of downtown since you are smack dab in the middle of it. I stayed here with 4 friends for New Years a year ago. It was perfect for our needs. The two room suite featured a living room with a fold out sofa bed and a small kitchen, and a bedroom with two queen sized beds. The room was very comfortable for 5 people and even featured a walk out balcony. The staff was very friendly and the cost was very affordable for our group. It would be a little on the expensive side for a single or couples getaway. Be advised that you do have to pay for parking (I believe $16 a night). I highly recommend it is it fits in your price range.

“FORGET THE TROUBLE.” Recently we reserved a room on the hyatt web site and since we were Diamond members we used one of our suite upgrades. Arriving at we were give a suite on the sixth floor and the only view was a massive gravel roof. So much for status. . Initially we had asked for a harbor view but they pay no attention to requests and the room assigning person does not look at status or requests. After 1 1/2 hours waiting we were finally given our room which was a small suite with a semi harbor view. Which was fine. The next day the fun started. You have to have your key to get up in the elevators and I forgot mine MY BAD! I went to the desk and asked for a new one. The front desk clerk Adam said since the room was in my husbands name i could not have a new key made even with id. He should of sent someone up with me and i could verify something in the room but he just said no and that i would have to wait until my husband came from his conference at 6 o'clock and 4 blocks away to get into the room to get in the room. .. Be prepared to have the clerks be totally unhelpful and our right obstructionists! . Finally after a temper fit the manager was called and he said it was ok to give me a new key. It was my mistake to leave the key in the room but it should have been resolved like most hotels do it . #1 The first key didn't work in the lounge which is nice to get water and cokes.. #2 I went back down and got the key re-keyed. It didn't work in the door to the room. #3 Went back down and re-keyed again. which didn't work in one of the doors. #4 Found a helpful supervisor and she took keys down and a manger finally came up with the re-keyed re-keyed re-keyed keys.. #5 Husband has old key and since their keying system stinks I will have to go down again to get him up in the elevator and into room.. So if you want to spend your vacation hunting keys and not getting into a room this is the place for you.

“Great hotel, great location, very family-friendly” I stayed here in Oct 07 and Dec 07, each stay was for one night. Both times I enjoyed my stay and found the hotel to be top-notch.
