The Oct one was for a girlfriends' getaway weekend. We had two double-queen rooms right next to each other. We were in one tower, and used the jacuzzi/pool in the other tower. You do feel a little silly walking through the entire lobby wearing a white bathrobe, but oh well! The Dec stay was for our annual Christmas night in Seattle with the kids. When we checked in they had run out of kids' goodie bags, so they gave us a free in-room movie credit. We had an Executive Suite, which seemed more like two rooms they had joined together. There was a living room area with a sofa, tv, desk, and a pull-down bed, as well as a full bath. You open the adjoining doors (two sets) and enter the bedroom, which had a king bed, desk, and sofa, and also another full bath. The kids loved having their own "room" and they thought the pull-down bed was pretty cool and comfy. They brought up a little crib for our 2 yr old to use, too, which was nice. We donned our bathrobes (alas, no little robes for the kids, like the Fairmont does) and used the pool/jacuzzi--kids had a blast. We bought some snacks at the sundries shop downstairs, which were actually reasonably priced. After spending the evening out on the town we all came back for a good night's rest, as we had a Santa brunch the next day at Macy's. The kids sacked out pretty well; the rooms seem well-insulated from hotel noise and street noise (we were on the 35th floor). We sacked out on our own bed, and they don't call these Heavenly Beds for nothin'! It was such an incredibly comfortable bed, holy cow. We kept the curtains open and the downtown views were fantastic. We watched the flat-screen tv from our bed, which has really cool personal lights for reading, and it was great. Good for romance, good for resting :) The hotel staff was friendly and helpful, and they stored our luggage for us the next day when we checked out and did some shopping. The location is great: the Market, Westlake Center, the big department stores, Pacific Place, and Belltown are all within a few blocks. I'd recommend eating at Lola, just two blocks over. Top Pot Donuts is also just a few blocks. We would definitely come back! During the holidays they had a special promo: Executive Suite for $350, incl a $200 gift card to Pacific Place that you can use at any shop there! It felt like you got the room for just $150 :)

“No room service ... vending options drab; sat in my room gnawing my arm” Its a few year since I stayed here and it has improved. The gym set up is excellent with a nice indoor pool. The room was adequate. The actual catered food for our meeting was very good. Thank goodness it has not been seismically shifted away from the convention center, otherwise would not have a basis for existence. I arrived on a flight from the West coast and got to the hotel after midnight. The check in was good and the lady friendly. The key did not open the door at the first cut, not her fault but was a recurrent issue, I found out later. I asked about food and was handed 2 take out menus ... also offered vending machines. I explored and could not do, selection limited, not even a sandwich to toast or a salad. (Twinkies give me childhood flashback episodes if I eat them for dinner). So I went to sleep like a couple of billion people on this earth - hungry. I awoke in the early hours thinking I had eaten my right thumb. Actually I was gnawing on my forearm above the wrist while my arm had gone dead from the elbow down perhaps as some sort of archaic primordial preparation so if you eat a limb its anesthetic .... I woke and despite a bad hair day looming, found the Corner Bakery that opened early and got a muffin and coffee. Afterwards in my meeting, while concealing my right forearm like an embarrassing tattoo, I got online and donated to Worldvision, Unicef and Save the Children's Fund with a pledge to do more for the worlds poor and hungry. Notwithstanding this, meanwhile back in Chicago at the Hyatt, McCormick Center they need a food option 24 hours a day if they are going to be a serious contender with competition opening close by in 2012.

“Great workout facility” I was here on a business trip. I am very tall and they gave me an accessible room, which means my jacket hits the floor in the closet and all the light switches are lower than my waist. The beds are very nice and they offer you a $5 credit if you opt out of housekeeping for one day. It is very close to the convention center and The Cheesecake factory. The gym is on the 35th floor and has two levels with enough treadmills and ellipticals and weights for all. The bathroom in this room has very little counter space. If I had my husband or family with me, there wouldn't be enough space. And there is no bath in this room, just a shower. The shampoo and conditioner is low quality, so bring your own. It is right next to the elevator, so you have to hear the noise all night. There are plenty of tv channels and the mini bar is well stocked. They gave me a free bottle of water, which I refilled in the gym. The drapes seemed to keep the light out, but it was still pretty early when I woke up. The Internet accommodates up to four devices, which is nice. There is a cool remote button to press to turn the floor lamps on and off. Overall, a typical hotel room in a convenient location. Parking is $44 a night so be prepared.

“pretty nice” stayed overnight for a next day meeting. it's located in the middle of downtown and just a quick walk from the red line subway. i've never stayed at a hampton inn but thought it was quite decent. it's not a 4 star hotel or anything, but it was nice enough. i got a room w/ 2 double beds, and the room provides a computer lap desk so i could work on my laptop in bed. they have free internet which is a big plus for me. i did notice that the walls were thin as you can hear people in the hallway or the doors slamming, and the sirens from the street coming from the window. They have an automated wake up call which was prompt and on-time. they called to check if the room was okay after settling in for 5-10 mins. the bathroom was clean, nothing too fancy. there is a chinese restaurant that is zagat rated on the corner called Ben Pao. their black pepper shrimp was excellent, but not so much for the mongolian beef (i've had better). there was a line for ordering take-out, but you can also order to-go online on their website. it seemed to be a somewhat fancy restaurant.

“Like a movie theatre only with a bed” The Bijou is a movie theme hotel that while small is fun and clean. The rooms are all named for film shot in and around San Francisco and the small theatre just off the lobby shows a San Francisco double feature every night. The deep rich colors in the lobby are carried through to the rooms where the colors are bright and rich. The beds are comfy and the closets large and stocked with an iron and ironing board extra pillows and an extra blanket. I had a room on the 6th floor with a queen bed, much larger than I had expected with a full bath. The one criticism I have of the bath tub was that due to the spigot being at one end and the drain control at the other it is not usable for soaking as you'd either be hitting your head or being poked in the back. Being a city dweller I am used to noise and wasn't kept awake by the busy streets on either side of the hotel. But in any event, the hotel provides ear plugs in the room. The neighborhood is grity but most of the street people are not dangerous and can be quite friendly when treated like human beings. If nothing else think of your interaction with them as an interesting cultural experince. Though the staff warns visitors of walking west from the hotel, the area is safe durning the day and as long as you are aware of your surroundings you can walk the streets at night. The continental breakfast while not lavish is enough to get you going in the morning. The staff is friendly and the little extras offered at all Joie de Vivre hotels [free staff authored city guides, access to a Golden Gate Greeter] along with the special services for movie buffs make this budget hotel a cut above most.

“Great!!” We loved the Bulfinch. The only negative things that I can say are (1) a couple staff gave us some bum advice about ATMs and convenience stores (they are both available just across the street), (2) the bathrooms can be cold in the summer – with blasting air-con there that you cannot control, and (3) there is almost no closet room. But these are such small things. All else is great at the Bulfinch. The location is great. There are nice conveniences kiddy-corner - - a convenience store with ATM and a nice little place where you can grab breakfast. It is a short walk to the State House and Faneuil Hall, and in the other direction the Garden if you are here for a game or concert. It is a short walk (5 min) to the Haymarket T-station - - and about same distance to North Station, though Haymarket is a better walk at night (I guess unless there is an event at the Garden). The young staff is very friendly and helpful – it is a hotel where you feel a personal touch – after just a day the staff will know you as you walk in. The building itself is also very quaint – sort of a Boston version of the Flairtron Building. The rooms are cool and if you can afford – definitely get a “nose-room” suite. While the room may seem narrow - - but it is long and you have windows everywhere with some nice views. I love natural light and these suites definitely have them everywhere including the bathroom (we could see the Garden from the bathroom – and when we showered I could even see the State House looking into the living room). The bed was big and comfortable. Overall, I really loved staying at the Bulfinch - - I love Boston and the Bulfinch is a great way to stay in this great city.

“Molto buono” Un 4 stelle praticamente in centro, fermata della metro appena girato l'angolo, un clima amichevole e un buon profumo che ti accoglie nella hall e nei vari piani. Per chi usa la macchina c'è anche il parcheggio sotterraneo. Buoni prezzi per un 4 stelle.

“Good but nothing special” I stayed here for one night on business in November 2003. No real complaints with this hotel. But it wasn't anything special. On the plus side, my room was more spacious than the average hotel room. No high speed internet access in the rooms (surprising since this hotel seems to cater to a business crowd). Staff was very friendly and efficient.

“This hotel is in a great location” I stayed at the Sheraton Downtown for five nights during a recent convention. This hotel is in a great location - right on the 16th Street Mall so there are plenty of bars and restaurants within easy walking distance. This hotel is made up of town buildings located on opposite sides of Court Street. I stayed in the Towers and it took a while to figure out how to get from building to building - without going outside. Many a guest was confused upon arrival but once you figured it out, it was easy. The staff was very pleasant and helpful. My room, Tower 520, was a bit on the small side but very clean. I stayed in the room myself and found the storage to be somewhat lacking. Small drawers but lots of closet space. I imagine if you had two folks sharing the room, it may be a problem. The bathroom was also small but had a full sized tub which was nice. My room was a bit noisier than I prefer. There wasn't a whole lot of traffic, but I could hear the odd siren going down the street. I could also hear music blasting from some bar on 16th Street. This was only a problem on Friday and Saturday nights. There was a pool outside but it was chilly the day I went out to look at it so no one was swimming. Went to several large meetings at the hotel itself. Some of which were catered. The food was very good and the staff again very pleasant.

“Above and Beyond - Olympic Service” Our group of 10 stayed at this property before and after an Alaska cruise departing from the Port of Seattle. One night before the cruise and three nights post cruise. We booked through the AMEX Centurion Card, so we received a number of perks. PROS: Location is ideal for walking about without being in the middle of the fray at Pike Market. There is a great restaurant across the street too, sort of a trendy tapas/wine bar, but the food was wonderful, fairly priced and despite the initial air of pretense they were very welcoming of the five children in our group (including three wee lads). Town car service was handy and freely offered. Food in the Georgian was perfect, really, perfect is the word. From fresh local cherries to the best chicken hash you could imagine the breakfast food was divine. We had room service dinners and the food was equally outstanding. Rooms were on the "charming" side, but the furnishings and finishes were first rate, the bed was of the top of the line nature with down comforter, fancy sheets, pillow top mattress. The windows actually open which is a very nice feature in Seattle with the refreshing sea air. The fitness/pool area was a little oasis in the city and hit the spot. But beyond everything else the service in this hotel was as good as the best hotels in Europe or Asia. We were greeted by name throughout our stay, we were "remembered" on our return visit a week later. Servers were great with our three small children in the restaurants, not to mention the milk and cookies and toys. The best example was the kitchen fire on the day of our departure (10 guests mind you) that set off the smoke alarms throughout the hotel and put their emergency announcements into action and elevators were turned off for safety. We were on the 4th floor and needed to depart as our shuttle van was at the front door. We called the bell desk and at first were told that they could not come for our bags due to the elevator issue, I then explained our deadline to get to the airport and 4, yes four, bellmen came immediately to our room and brought our bags down 4 flights of stairs with smiles and good spirits. CONS: The Shuckers Restaurant had very slow service, it was almost like the staff there were not on the same channel as the rest of the hotel, I think it may be a concession. The entry from the main street requires going up a level from the lobby, minor issue, part of the charm of an older hotel. We will only stay at the Olympic on future visits.

“No flat screens & $40/day parking” Had to pick this hotel option based on my company's travel partner preferences. The two big problems were the 29 inch old style tv instead of flatscreen, and the $40/day parking. The things I liked about the hotel were the views (I was on 18th floor), and the grab-and-go breakfast area in the lobby, which was a nice alternative as I did not have time to sit down.

“Ridiculous overnight parking fee” The hotel itself is nice enough. Nothing spectacular, but conveniently located if you have to be in Philadelphia. I will begin by saying that the valet overnight parking fee is $50 per night. I didn't realize this until check-out. Needless to say I was less than impressed. The rooms were decent, but nothing out of the ordinary. I would certainly not go out of my way to stay in this hotel again. The doorman was always pleasant, but I can't say the same for the concierge. Be careful walking around at night alone. The neighborhood takes a turn for the worse after the sun goes down.

“very good service” This is my second time at the Hampton Inn in Manhattan. I returned because it is a good price for its location, and the free internet and breakfast save additional money for my budget-conscious company. This time I noticed a concerted effort to improve service. Staff were very courteous and went out of their way to help. The breakfast is not the greatest, but it is free. There is always a hot item (example: sausage and waffles), as well as cold cereals, yogurt, and pastries. My room was a bit noisy because some door nearby kept slamming, and Manhattan always has lots of sirens and honking. Overall, though, this hotel is a very good value.

“WOW, I LOVE this place.” Stayed in room 2215. Needed to be close to the airport and out at 5am. I expected the typical airport hotel feel. Boy, was I wrong. This place ROCKS! It's like staying at a 5 star high end lodge in a peaceful, tranquil setting. No lack of amenities. And the restaurant, wine list, food menu, bar, etc. were all a 10...... KUDOS to you. You nailed it......

“Good choice” This is a very nice hotel. It is located in the Times Square area, and several Broadway theaters are within 1-3 blocks. There are plenty of restaurants in the area as well. The hotel itself is nicely decorated. I stayed in a corner city-view room, which offered impressive views of the city. The room was average in terms of size but above average in terms of decoration and comfort. The shower features 2 shower heads. It might not be good for the environment, but it sure felt good. The air conditioning was not able to keep up with the 100 degree weather as much as I would have liked, but the room was fairly comfortable. Overall, this is a very nice hotel in a good location. Pricewise, you'll pay for it, but this is still a good choice.
“A very good hotel” We have stayed at the Marriott at least four times while in SF for a long weekend. It is good hotel for a three day weekend in SF.

“If you like sleep, stay somewhere else” Featuring some of the thinnest walls in the hotel industry, the Peabody Memphis looks great from the lobby and that's where it ends. I heard the guy in the next room yapping on the phone until about 3 a.m. And he wasn't even talking that loud, it was just the paper-thin walls. God forbid if it had been an amorous couple in the next room... Needless to say, I didn't get any sleep and it ruined my next-day. Forget the ducks, they're not worth the trouble. Stay somewhere, anywhere else and you'll almost be guaranteed of having a better night's sleep.

“Disappointing for a Courtyard” I have stayed at Courtyards throughout the country and this was probably one of the worst. I had to wait about five minutes to check in since the only desk clerk was helping someone else. Then, I had key card trouble getting into my room. Next, I hit the fitness room. The machines were either old or just beat up. I did go for a run on a treadmill. However, the room temp was showing as 127 so it was either broken or poorly venilated. When I returned to my room, this time I couldn't get in so I needed to return to the front desk to get a new key card. Besides this, the room was fine. I didn't use the cafe since I had plans outside of the hotel. I will not use this Courtyard on future trips to Dallas.

“Great breakfast and gym” I spend 5 days attending the conference in Chicago. The Hyatt Regency Chicago locates in a good location downtown, easy walk for shopping and restaurants. The bed and pillows are super. However, what I like the most is the gym, which has state-of-art equipments and it opens 24 hours. Breakfast is very good and nice to get good energy for the day.

“Another visit and still just as wonderful” This is such a great hotel in downtown chicago, just a few blocks off Michigan avenue and close to everything. I try to stay here once a year on business and it's just as good as before. The rooms are comfortable, clean and in wonderful condition. But my favorite is the crepes for breakfast! Service is still outstanding throughout the hotel. I'd highly recommend this hotel.

“DO NOT STAY HERE until they renovate.” This place needs MAJOR renovation. An entire face lift. Was in D.C. for a conference last week (3/11). This was the overflow for the conference hotel, The Mandarin Oriental. I walked into the room, and literally walked right out, called The Mandarin begging them to find me a room. Thank goodness they did. I was honest with Mesfin at the front desk and he didn't charge me the one night for leaving. He understood... The rooms are dingy, old (no, I mean REALLY old), there was actually rust in areas of the room. It looks like no one has touched it since 1960. There was NO WAY I was spending the night in there. Trust this review, DO NOT book here until they have renovated the entire hotel. And, thanks for understanding Mesfin!

“Well-appointed and friendly, but noisy and cold” My wife and I stayed in a suite on the eve of a conference held at the hotel. Service is friendly and efficient, and the Hard Rock theme is cool, but the decor is very modern and cold (we like a more traditional, warm atmosphere), so the room does not feel at all cozy; there is no tub, just a shower, with tile on the walls and floor of the entire bathroom area that makes it a bit hard and cold; lots of electrical and medical outlets, nice TV/audio equipment, well-appointed. The PROBLEM: while the windows are thick and entirely blocked out all noise from the game at the stadium right outside our window, noise within the building carries right into your room - voices, doors, etc. - and there is a loud fan over the toilet that you cannot turn off and is a bit annoying. This hotel must be fun for those who want the Hard Rock experience, and I might recommend it to those folks, but it just is not for us.

“Ok hotel with cheap parking” We stayed here for one night while my boyfriend attended his last day of school before we left for our trip to the UK. The lobby of the hotel is all marble and seems impressive on the outside but when you get a closer look you see the hotel is in need of some updating. We had a king room and the bed is decently comfortable. The pillows were kind of flat but they were ok too. Linens on the bed were fine. Towels were a bit thin but nice and white. The room showed its age in furniture but they had a brand new flat screen tv in the room. Working the tv with cable box is a little confusing at first. The bathroom is old and showing age. You don't get much in the way of toiletries. The shower is fine but dark as the light doesn't shine in much and the curtain is dark. You can tell the culture marble and tile need new grout and caulking. The location of the hotel is good for businesses and colleges in the mid-Wilshire area but not good for touristy things. You'll have to navigate the bus system to get to touristy stuff. I took the 720 part way to the Beverly Center and back. I would stay here only if I had to stay in this area for a specific reason. They have a good deal on parking and a better rate than some other hotels in this immediate area.

“Wonderful Stay!” I stay at a lot of hotels and I RARELY designate an "Excellent" rating as I feel that there is always room for improvement. However, I think that the W TImes Square has it right. The hotel itself is in the perfect location. Close to many midtown office buildings and smack in the middle of Times Square with great views (from certain rooms) of the "crossroads of the world". The staff could not be more friendly. It is so nice to encounter staff members at an upscale hotel that do not act stuffy and better than everyone else. I had fun with one of the doormen picking on some of the more stuffy guests as they walked into the hotel. The bell staff is wonderful, the front desk assigned us the perfect rooms and even made the extra effort to get them adjoining which only took an extra hour past check-in time and even called me on my cell phone to let me know the room was ready. I came back to my room to find a welcome amenitiy of wine and fruit and was just made to feel welcome in every aspect of my stay. This hotel is fantastic and well-worth the room rate. I hope that in choosing this hotel, other travelers will have the same positive experience as I did.

“Convenient, but typically costly” This property is a typical high-end, full-service, in-airport hotel. It is located in the Delta terminal at Detroit Metro, so if you are flying out very early in the morning, it's a great spot. In fact, there is a security checkpoint just for Westin guests that allows you to enter the airport bypassing the main security line. My buddy was flying Delta, so he had no issues. However, be aware, if you are flying a different airline, allow an extra 20 minutes to get to the North Terminal. You must take the Westin shuttle to get over to the north Terminal and between the ride itself (huge airport) and actually waiting for the shuttle to leave, don't expect to just walk out of your room and get to your gate. Not surprisingly, the extra costs can sneak up on you. Internet $10, rollaway bed $20, bottle of plain water in room $4. We checked in late after the football game and were out very early, so didn't experience much in the property, but it was sure nice not to have to get up early and drive in on day of departure.

“Very nice stay” I can't seem to figure our why there are so many negative reviews about this hotel. My one night stay was very pleasant, staying on the preferred floor gave me a nice room with a great bed and bathroom with bath and shower. The furniture was nice and while some part of the walls were cracking in the corners, it had a classy feel to it. The staff was usual DC, burned out from too many foreign guests and snotty tourists. The breakfast was nice and location, for me, was perfect. For tourists, it's a bit far from the metro, but reasonable. The biggest problem I encountered, and one that is becoming all too prevalent at high-end hotels, was the alarm clock. I prefer the radio to wake me rather than ringing telephones. However, I (being an adult with a PhD, serving as an officer in the US Army Corps of Engineers, knowing how to fly a small airplane, program my VCR, write statistical script, and change my oil) could not figure out how to set the alarm clock. The service staff was of no help and the desk clerk said they could not put instructions in the room (she never explained the reason for this impediment). Still, I really like this hotel and the gym was excellent. The other reviewers must be used to the Ritz or Four Seasons.

“First stay at a Kimpton a good one, thanks fellow reviewers” We stayed at the Kimpton Palomar for two nights after reading other guests' reviews and were delighted with the location, the room, our reception. Our two cats were welcomed, our van with its car-top carrier was parked safely in an outside lot by the very patient valet ($38.00 & $6.84 in taxes per night). True, full breakfasts were a splurge at $39.05 before the tip for my eggs benedict and my husband's steak and eggs, but the coffee and service was excellent, the ambiance fresh and un-crowded. We were shy about attending the evening wine reception in the lobby but it just solidified the over-all friendly tone. The two persons with whom we chatted definitely enhanced our visit, suggesting places to go and sharing some of their backgrounds. I particularly liked the multiple ethnicities of the staff--Ethiopia, Sierra Leone, Equador, Vietnam--also a cosmopolitan New Yorker--and their general sweetness--great hiring. Our standard King room was extra spacious, the bed among the most comfortable ever (my husband has back trouble, so this is a constant concern), the sheets and duvet smooth but crisp cotton. We didn't have a chance to use the leopard-patterned robes in the closet, or the sock-slippers, but appreciated the non-standard design. By signing up for Kimpton's loyalty program, we had free wifi--not sure if this is standard if you don't sign up, so definitely take a moment to sign up, and you are also likely to get a coupon for $10 worth of goodies from the in-room bar--we chose the $6.00 pop-up map of DC--very handy-- and a Dagoda chocolate bar, also $6.00--without the coupon, would never have opened the bar. Desk and lamp with built-in outlets made computer use easy. DuPont Circle location is easy walking to multiple restaurants--we wandered into Ping Pong @ One DuPont Circle for dim sum one night, Raku for a late afternoon lunch of yellow curry and coconut noodle soup with beef; and a late-night snack at the hotel's Urbana restaurant. The metro entrance is only a couple of blocks from the hotel, but we had good weather and walked to the National Museum--three subway stops worth of walking, $2.20 each to return by subway.

“Basic Room with Motel Feel - Close to Hollywood Sites” The hotel is walking distance (a couple of blocks away) to the most popular Hollywood sites - the Walk of Fame and Mann's Chinese Theater. One can also walk to Melrose Avenue and Sunset also. It's a safe area and you see other people walking outside. The hotel is a 10-minute drive to Universal Studios too. Price includes free wifi and free parking (spaces are small so if you have a big car, it'll be a tough squeeze). Reception was very nice - felt like a real hotel but once you get to the rooms, it starts to look more like a motel because it's open air so your door opens to the outside. It's not a bad thing - looks worst if you arrive at night as the corridors are lit with fluorescent lighting. The room is in good shape - not rundown. Our only complaint was that there were small ants in the bathroom - on the sink counter and a few on the floor. They seemed to coming from behind the bathroom mirror. Other than that, the rest of the room was fine. Breakfast is not included but there is a tiny restaurant connected to the hotel that serves breakfast, lunch and dinner. There is a Starbucks a short drive away in a mini strip mall. There is a pool but it's adjacent to the parking garage.

“Love the Location” We stay at this hotel several times a year, and really love the location. It is within walking distance of: the magnificent mile shopping, just across the river to the theater district, sears tower, and the art museum and the park. It is also convenient to the red line train which we take out to popular spots such as the second city comedy club, and cubs baseball games. On our last visit we had a room on the 12th floor, and it had been recently rennovated. It had a wood shlef that went the whole length of the room which was nice for storing stuff. It was a decent size room with a small couch, ottomon and a desk. It also had a fridge. Typical courtyard style. The room was nice and clean. It is also within walking distance of lots of great restaurants.

“Great hotel” My teenage daughter and I stayed here for 3 nights. Great hotel for tourists. Very quiet and location was excellent for siteseeing. Easy to walk to TimeSquare and the subway station a few short blocks away. We even walked to the Theater district. Rooms were spacious for NYC and kitchen area was very nice even though we did not use it. Bed was very comfortable. Bathroom was very tiny but nice. Included breakfast was convenient but not great. They were often out of food and the staff seemed to have trouble keeping things stocked. Pretty much the same bland items each morning with little variety. The usual scrambled eggs, sausage, waffles , some okay looking muffins, toast, bagels, cereal, yogurt, and some fruit (which they always ran out of). The oatmeal would usually be out or almost out also. We never had a problem with the elevator or had to wait long even though the hotel was quite busy. Hotel has a computer and printer for guests in the lobby area and a concierge desk.

“Spectacular hotel in truly pristine condition” Really impressive hotel. Head and shoulders above the hotel across the street, in my opinion. Spotlessly clean. Gorgeous property.. seemingly old world and brand new all at once. Was especially impressed because I didn't like the first room they gave me, and they immediately moved me -- I thought they'd be hesitant because I was paying their bargain basement rate. Not so -- they moved me right away. Only negs -- no coffee maker in the room, and during peak hours, there was like a 25 minute wait at the coffee shop in the hotel. Also, like many hotels in SF, rooms over the main entrance are noisy because all of the bellman use this loud whistle to call cabs for people.

“Who was saying Hotel 17 is a "gem"???” Wow, where do I start? The positives--quiet street (but not the hotel). The negatives--cramped rooms; cheap, uncomfortable bed. An army cot would have been more comfortable. But the worst was: uncaring service staff and construction on the next two rooms to mine, BANGING, DRILLING, SCREECHING EVERY day from 8 am to 4:30 pm. When I complained, no apologies, no ability to move me to another room. And the piece de resistance, bathrooms in the hallway, so I'd have to wait in the morning to get in line to use bathroom or take shower. Off the beaten path as well--not convenient to many parts of town. The clientele seemed to be mostly European. Our standards and theirs I suppose are not the same. This isn't Dubrovnik or Prague, this is NYC. In summary, probably the worst hotel I've stayed at in about the last 10 years. Spend a couple more dollars and find a decent hotel, in a more convenient part of town. Down the street though, great little diner open 24 hours, called Gramercy Diner, on corner of 3rd ave, and 17th street.

“Average Courtyard” I have stayed in many Courtyard properties that outshine this one by far. This one is definitely on the average scale...but it is not a bad hotel. Nothing really stands out about this hotel in either a bad nor good way, it serves its purpose well and without disappointment. However, the pool is indoors. It would be nice to see an outdoor pool in Texas. The hotel is directly on a service road to the highway so your options of what is around is limited, although the shuttle may be willing to take you where you need to go.

“Superb Hotel. Great location depending on what you are there to do.” We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and just loved it. Our room was extremely spacious. The bathroom was huge. Hotel amenities were outstanding. The lobby bar was always a great starting or ending point of our day. The hotel is a bit isolated from retail and dining, but, very close to the National Mall and all of the Smithsonians. There are really minimal shopping and dining areas around the National Mall anyway. We always went to Dupont Circle for bars and restaurants. There is a Potbelly Sandwich shop next to the hotel which was great. Around the corner is the Cafe Twelve, great casual sandwiches for breakfast and lunch to go. Starbucks across from the hotel was nice. CVS is across from the hotel as well. That is ALL that is close to the hotel. I'm not kidding. Also, just a short walk to the waterfront. Be prepared to walk ALOT.

“THE GRANDUCA DISAPPOINTS” I have been a frequent guest at the Granduca. I guess I kept hoping it would improve, but it hasnot. The Granduca has disappointed me for the last time and I will not return. 1. Do not order room service. I called and ordered a chesse plate one evening when I was working late. The menu desribed three types of cheese and grapes. An hour passed- no cheese plate. I called. The woman who answered the phone promised to look into it. She never called back. Another 15 minutes passed and I called. She said she was looking into it. She never called back. After another 15 minutes, I called. The waiter answered and explained he had delivered it to the wrong room. I suggested he make another and he seemed surprised at my suggestion. Finally, he brought me the "cheese plate" -- three large hunks of some white cheese a few crackers and some relish. When I complained that it was not what was described in the menu, he shrugged and left. I called the front desk and ask them to have the General Manager call me. She never did. 2. Do not use the laundry service. They are incapable of accounting for clothing. Most recently, they lost my navy blazer for a day before finding it and they lost all of my laundry for the last night of my stay and then argued with me about whether I gave them any laundry. When I explained that I personally gave the bag to the front desk at 7 am, they acted as if they did not believe me and began calling people who were on duty at that time. After three more calls, I walked down to the front desk and asked to see where they kept the laundry. They refused me. The finally found my laundry at the clearners they use. They told me I would have it by 9 am the next day because it was "in a machine and wet." I explained that a suit should be dry cleaned and it best not be "wet.". They again said I could get my laundry by 9 am--small comfort since my flight was scheduled to leave before they wanted to return my laundry. After makiing me wait for a couple of hours, they finally brought me my laundry. It was not wet. It was finished and hanging. So, they kept me up for a couple of hours waiting on my laundry and they did not seem to care. Again, I asked to speak to the General Manager. She did not call me. 3. Do not use the mini bar. They only re-fill the mini bar when they want to do so. During my most recent stay, they tried to do so only once-- when I had the privacy sign on the door. Indeed, they just opened the door and attempted to come right in. They never tried to re-fill it again. On the last day of my stay, I took a soda bottle from the mini bar and when I tried to open it, it exploded and glass cut my lip. I grabbed a towel and tried to stop the bleeding and when I finally got it under control, I called the front desk and explained what had happened. They said they would send a maid to clean up the glass and a first aid kit if I needed one.The maid did not arrive in the 30 mins that passed before I had to leave. Nice eh? If I ran the hotel and a guest had a soda bottle explode from the mini bar, I think I would have gone to the guest's room and apologized and expressed concern. The General Manager never called me to explain how a soda bottle might explode or why and they charged me for the beverage that exploded. 4. They are greedy. I stayed for almost a week before the Final Four in Houston and needed to stay for five more days starting on the Sunday when no game was played, including Monday-Wednesday nights. I have a regular corporate rate with Granduca that is reasonable and I am a frequent guest. Yet, the Granduca jacked up my rate to $650 a night for Sunday and Monday and refused to reduce it claiming the Final Four generated demand for the rooms. That might have been true before Butler and U Conn won their semi-final games and there were cancellations all over Houston by fans of other larger programs who hoped to see their teams in the finals. The Granduca has no customer loyalty at all and they took advantage of me and they know it. 5. There is no management. I have asked the front desk staff to see a manager on a half dozen cocassions. Most of those were met with blank stares. The only place I ever saw the General Manager was on the hotel channel on the TV where she promised to take care of my every need. I have never seen her on property in any of my visits and she has never once responded to any of the messages I left at the front desk to have her call me to discuss each of the aforementioned experiences. 6. They are unresponsive. If you call the front desk, the standard reply is "I will look into it." Apparently, "looking into it" rarely involves calling you back to let you know what they are doing about it. There is no sense of urgency in responding to my requests. 7. They are unreliable. You might get business packages addressed to you or they may end up in another guest room. It is a crap shoot. Sometimes, your TV's work and sometimes, they do not. Sometimes, your bedside clock is right and sometimes, it is not. Occassionally, the bedside clock alarm goes off because they forget to clear it before giving you a room. The Granduca has good bones-- a nice building; great rooms with lots of space and small kitchens; and a good location. But bones do not make a great hotel. A great hotel is about the service and there is no service at the Granduca.

“Great place, good value” My husband and I stayed at the Adagio in April 2004. We lived in the Bay Area for 3 years and have also stayed in several SF hotels. We loved the hotel and decided to stay there again at the end of our trip. The hotel is beautifully designed, has a great restaurant and friendly staff. The location is excellent, there are homeless people everywhere around Union Square and you just need to accept that. There are a few downsides - lack of air conditioning is rarely a problem in SF but we did have some freakishly hot weather and felt it! The valet parking service is poor and service is a bit inconsistent. However for a hotel in this price range it is an excellent value, especially for lovers of modern design.

“A Good Hotel, Conveniently Located” I stay at the Grand Hyatt at least once a year when I visit DC on business. The staff is friendly, the beds are comfortable, the rooms are clean, the internet wifi service is good, and the location is convenient both for walking and taking the Metro. The room decor is conservative and unmemorable, but works. If you're looking for special or trendy accommodations, you're probably better off elsewhere. However, if you're looking for a quality hotel for a business trip, meeting, or visit in the city, the Grand Hyatt is a good choice to consider.

“Good option near 6th Street Entertainment” I chose the hotel based on location, price and prior reviews. The location is great being only a few blocks from the 6th Street entertainment area. The hotel itself seemed to be an upgrade from a typical Hampton. There was a nice breakfast / evening reception area on the second floor which included a New Orleans-inspired balcony with tables and chairs overlooking San Jacinto Blvd. The hotel also had a very efficient and friendly valet parking staff. My room was clean and very spacious. The refrigerator was a nice surprise. Like most (all?) Hamptons, there was free wi-fi and free breakfast. The only real drawback seems temporary in that there is a great deal of construction in the immediate area. The construction barricades seemed to limit pedestrian traffic and made me at least a little uneasy walking in the area, alone after dusk. But, once the construction impact lessens, I would not hesitate to recommend the hotel.
“Fun but loud” This hotel is central, but stay on the first 10 floors so you don't hear the club upstairs.

“good value in nyc if you want to stay out of busy downtown” The Milburn offers good value for stays in NYC. The building appears to be an old apartment house that has been coverted to a hotel. We had a 2 room suite for less than $300 in NYC. The bederoom and living room are quite large. The bathroom and kitchenette (sink, refrigerator, coffee maker and microwave) are small. Everything was quite clean and well-maintained. There is a continental breakfast included in the rate. The hotel is right off of Broadway and a short walk to the 72nd Street express subway stop to everywhere else. It is a healthy walk to times square. It is a very good location to stay if you are visiting Columbia, Barnard and other UWS colleges. There afe lots of restaurants in easy walking distance. Apparently they have delivery room service arranged wih some. Parking is discounted at a garage about 3 blocks away...if available. If not there are other garages.

“Posh and Convenient” The W is in a great location, central to most anything you'd do in New York City. The rooms and lobby are modern and offer all of the conveniences you'd expect for a hotel of this caliber. The only negatives were that the wait to check-in was quite long, and the swank lobby/bar area (which offers great people watching) was always completely full, but all of these are signs of a hip hotel. All the staff I encountered were helpful, the room was clean and the fitness center was quite large for a midtown hotel, with a great view on the treadmills and just about any equipment you could want.

“Unfortunately, the reviews are right...” I was concerned when this hotel came up on Priceline - we usually get the Marriott since I had read the reviews about noisy rooms, but I've never had trouble sleeping with my sound canceling ear buds.....until now. Pros: Beautiful, historic public areas, friendly service, for the most part, exceptions noted below. Room safes, walk in closets, nice architectural details in rooms, comfortable bed. Good rate on Priceline. Cons: 1) Generator noise that can be heard in the corridor of the 3rd floor, nearest the courtyard. It got worse when the bathroom light/fan were turned on, and when the air conditioner was turned on. Management should not be renting rooms, in which it is impossible to sleep. We asked to be moved the next morning & no questions were asked as to why - they already knew why. 2) Second room on 3rd floor over alleyway, had barely audible hum, and street sounds...until bathroom light or airconditioner was turned on. Street sounds were louder in this room, but one expects that in a big city. 3) Thin walls - one can hear your neighbors & housekeeping (especially when they stand & talk in front of your door for 5 minutes) 4) Parking is $40 - park at Pershing Square for $15 if you don't need to go in/out 5) Restaurant was good, but a bit on high side 6) Valet forgot about me for 10 minutes, after unloading our car. 7) Husband complained about small, out of focus TV. 8) Inadequate bathroom shelf space for more than one person. 9) Crowded, outdated, stuffy fitness room. Don't know what to recommend if you use Hotwire or Priceline - usually bidding on 3 1/2 stars gives you the downtown Marriott - bid on 4 star hotels to be safe? I wouldn't stay here again.

“liegt zentral im MD Anderson Medical Center Gebiet” das Hotel bietet alles für einen Aufenthalt im Rahmen eines Besuches im MD Anderson Clinic Bereich. Kostenlose Shuttle verbinden das Hotel mit den unterschiedlichen Clinic Bereichen. Die Zimmer sind geräumig und mit allen Wichtigen ausgestattet. Frühstück ist landestypisch bietet aber auch alles Nötige. Zimmer sind ruhig und angenehm.

“Super Cheap Hotel Downtown Chicago” I have stayed at this hotel 2 different times. Can't beat the price!!! Paid $80 for a room with a king size bed. The room looked like it had been recently remodeled and was clean. Location is great! Walking distance to Michigan Ave and tons of restaurants. Bonus: FREE PARKING (first come first serve for guests of the hotel). Only downside is that it did not have a fridge.

“Real Nice Hotel - Stellar Service” I probably would have given this hotel a 4 out of 5 - but the amazing customer service I experienced put this place over the edge. Everyone, the bellman, front desk, servers, room service etc. went out of their way to make sure I was happy and taken care of. The roof top bar is not to be missed. There was a local musician doing a show in the lounge on Friday night - nice touch. This is an older hotel, but they have really made an effort to update the guest rooms with nice dark wood and granite. However, the windows are old and a bit drafty. My room on the 25th floor had a fantasic view of the harbor and other nearby builings. There isn't a lot in the immediate few blocks, but I was easily able to walk to the Seattle Art Museum, Pioneer Park, the Waterfront and other tourist sites.

“On a good way to become a luxury boutique hotel” Don't let the facade and the state of the surrounding buildings shock you. There is still construction going on, but not as bad as elsewhere in the city. And the street itself is very quiet at night. I would not yet call it a 'luxury' boutique hotel, it still needs some work done. BUT: the rooms are very spacious (at least the executive guest room I was in), with high ceilings. The workstation is sufficiently spaced and there is an extremely comfortable office chair. The 'minimalistic' interior still has everything you need: flatscreen TV, microwave, fridge, coffeemaker, good assortment of snacks. (First time I have ever seen an 'intimacy kit' (condoms) and First Aid kit in a hotel room !) While some have commented that the beds are very hard, which is true, I appreciated that and found it to be just right. A MAJOR plus: free WiFi in the rooms (I really don't understand why most business hotels, including high priced ones, are still charging for it. These days it should be part of the room amenities.) Although the hotel has recently been renovated, the room already showed some wear and tear, including water damage on the bathroom ceiling and floor. But don't forget, this is a very old building. The lobby is modern, so is the bar area. The staff is very friendly and extremely helpfull. All in all a very good place and if they keep up the renovations it is well on it's way to become a true luxury boutique hotel.

“Yes, the rooms are big....” The Salisbury has a great location and nice big one bedroom suites at a decent price, But the bathrooms are in dire need of an upgrade. They have ground-in dirt and don't feel clean. The door on ours was peeling badly. Also, one fo my pet peeves, lightbulbs were all 40 watt, even the three way bulbs. We only used the staff when we checked in (I'm from NYC and know my way around), but they weren't particualrly friendly. And, don't be fooled by the "continental" breakfast "voucher" as they call it. It's $6. We didn't use it since NYC diners are the way to go for breakfast. Wifi is $12 a day. I'd say the Salisbury makes you feel like you would have been better off staying at a reliable chain. We will not stay there again.

“Wonderful surprise--older hotel near downtown, free parking, free shuttle to downtown” We knew northing about this place until visiting Denver we needed a place to stay 2 nights. There was a hotel coupon for $49, so we read Trip Advisor reviews and tried it out. What a pleasant surprise. Friendly, helpful staff; free wifi, free parking, free shuttle all day to any place within 3 miles (and with a call they come and pick you up) and they accepted the coupon for 2 nights. Thiis not the Ritz, but it is a clean, pleasant hotel with comfortable beds, an exercise room, coffee maker in the room (no microwave or fridge). The hotel is near Mile High Stadium,the football field, and within a mile or two from downtown. There is a restaurant on the top floor with a great view of Denver. Food was good and prices were reasonable. We would strongly recommend this hotel if you want to avoid high prices of many hotels or some motels that are less than adequate around the Denver area.

“Comfortable, Well Maintained Property!!” Very well-kept property with free parking. Hotel room was quite large with plenty of pillows and huge windows (with blackout curtains). Staff was courteous and helpful. The hotel was pretty quiet (not a race weekend), and the other reviews are correct in that it is not within walking distance of anything. But for an extra 5 to 10 minute drive you get a much nicer hotel for the price of central Fort Worth.

“Pleasant staff, the rest OK” Found the staff to be very pleasant. The hotel is newer, but doesn't feel new. Small lobby. Decor in lobby and halls are dragged down by beige industrial type steel doors more suitable for a parking garage. A tall skinny building with very narrow corridors. 25 floors/2 small elevators. Yes, you will wait. Rooms are fine by New York standards; not big, but adequate size. Internet service was faster than in most hotels. In a more gritty part of Chelsea with numerous cheap handbag and junk jewerlry stores.

“$40 charge for a free night” I noticed 2 $20 charges on a free nights stay. Staff didn't have a clue when I called. "Give me your secret code on your credit card," one staffer demanded. I said: reverse the charges. This marred an otherwise great stay. Close to SJC, VTA Metro, free bus to SJC and Santa Clara Cal Train. 3 restaurants literally in the parking lot. Room spotless. Only annoyance: a blinking red light behind the TV when I was trying to sleep. RECOMMENDED.

“Funky modern hotel with Hacienda style twist” Wow, what a cool hotel. Some of the reviews on here say about the low light being a problem, but with the 100degree heat outside and dazzling sunshine it sits perfectly. Cool, modern, sleek, en trend, yet with the Spanish and hacienda feel whereever you may be in the hotel. The design is fantastic, the location excellent and the staff are amazingly friendly & efficient. The rooms are big and well equipped, the bathrooms are large too, and the lighting is just right. Whilst I was there we had a few storms and the hotel power was knocked out for a few hours, but this didn't phase the staff at all. Instant contingency plans kicked in and they were up and running. Couldn't have been friendlier or more efficient. I will definitely go back to this hotel. I'd booked 5 rooms for myself and 4 colleagues and everybody had a great experience.

“Nice hotel for business trips” I stayed here for 5 nights for a leadership training class that was being held in the building next door. Overall, I thought this was a nice business hotel. The staff was exceptionally friendly and service oriented -- everyone from the front desk to the valet to the housekeeper was very pleasant and helpful. There was never a line at the front desk. Valets were very helpful with directions. The location is convenient -- it's right off the freeway. There are several excellent restaurants right across from the hotel in case you don't want room service (Flemings, Japengo, Melting Pot, etc). They have a deal with a full-service gym that is located on the property, so you have to pay an entrance fee to get in. The entrance fee was included with my training, but for others that could be annoying. The gym itself is excellent, with classes and large quantities of fitness equipment. There is a small coffee shop to the right of the lobby. The room is decent, your average business hotel. The first room they gave me had a bad odor, but when I asked to be switched, they moved me right away with no hassle. The soundproofing between rooms isn't great -- I could hear my next door neighbor coughing in his room. However, they do have complimentary earplugs at the front desk, which took care of the issue. Overall, I think this hotel is a fine business hotel -- I wouldn't mind coming back for business, but would definitely not recommend for a weekend getaway.

“Great!” The Indigo in San Diego was absolutely amazing. We stayed for 3 nights and had a great time. The room is very modern, with hardwood floors, great art on the walls, large high def tv, very comfortable bed. The bathroom is great, love the stool in the shower. The Aveda products are great. The 9th floor deck is amazing, a great place to have a drink and enjoy the views. Overall one of the best hotels I've stayed in.

“Style and Substance! A definite 4” Some hotels are all style and no substance. In certain isolated cases, it's the other way around, lots of substance but severely lacking in style. (Of course, when push comes to shove, one should always take substance over style.) Nonetheless, having a little style thrown in is always nice. Which gets me to the Andaz Wall Street. I definitely dig the Andaz's style. Great lobby exuding understated elegance with a nice homey touch, nice large elevators, wide hallways and minimalist rooms. As for substance: (a) the room (basic King, without the peek-a-boo tub), it was huge, lots of space to roam! I love the electric roman shade, the bedside lighting controls (all off, relaxation, work, etc.) and the ability to control the brightness of the lights. The TV was an LCD and had to be at least 42 inches. I liked the little eraser with "oops!" printed on it. I liked the full length mirror that slides out. That the TV channels on offer were all standard definition was a let down however. (b) I liked the bathroom, done in black marble (or granite), the huge shower area, the rain shower, the toiletries on offer and the huge soft towels. However, I don't get the absence of a towel hook or the glass sink that's way too shallow. (c) Free mini-bar that was restocked daily! I had sparkling and still Saratoga water, orange juice, diet and regular coke, Terra chips and a granola bar. Not bad at all. (d) Free snacks at the lobby. As another reviewer has noted, the muffins are tasty indeed. And coffee too. (e) Free Wifi. Though the speeds did seem to vary quite a bit from hour to hour. (f) Cleaning and housekeeping standards, a bit uneven. Housekeeping missed a small face towel that was lying on the floor. On one day, I did not get a new set of toiletries (which was not a big deal since I had plenty of the C.O. Bigelow soap, shampoo and conditioner left), on the next day housekeeping gave me a completely new set notwithstanding the fact that the old one's weren't completely used up. The upper portion of the rainshower retained splatter marks - how the last guest even got that part wet, I don't really want to know. (g) The left side of the platform bed sported a clear gash where someone (or something) bumped into it and tore off part of the wood. (h) Staff were nice. Treated guests with respect and with a friendliness that did not seem to come from reflex alone, which is a good thing. A word regarding Wall and Water, the restaurant. I had the hot brunch there on Sunday and while pricey at $27 was quite tasty. The items on the cold part of the buffet were definitely higher quality stuff. The hot entree was tasty (though having to chew on the thick applewood smoked bacon did cause a sensitive molar to flare up :( Location wise, it's the only hotel on Wall Street. It certainly does not feature the crowds one gets when staying in a hotel at Midtown and Wall Street isn't as dead on the weekend as it used to be. Close to the WTC site, Century 21, CIty Hall, Battery Park City, and the Brooklyn Bridge.

“Great location if you like Time Square” Literally on Times Square. We had a nice room which overlooked the square. Noise didn't bother us although i thought it would. Check in was very quick, arrived at 1pm and no problem getting a room early. No problems with the room, very comfortable. Next time we will stay in Soho or Chelsea - Times Square isn't for us - but if you want to be in the middle of all the tourist activities then i would recommend this hotel.

“Great option for downtown Detroit” Stayed here for the second time during the ALCS (Detroit-Texas). From the outside this Doubletree looks a bit run down, but inside it is very nice. They defintely did a nice job renovating this property. Rooms are very nice and spacious (bedroom and living/desk area). Plenty of room. There is also a coffee bar and regular bar off the lobby. There is a free shuttle to take you around downtown so you don't have to take a cab. Only downside is lack of self parking. Each time I have stayed here the valet parking take a while.

“Location and Great Service ....with a smile!” We checked into the Argonaut on Nov 11th for 3 nights. My wife and I wish it could have been longer. Upon arrival our (my) expectations for a view were greater than could have possibly been delivered. The bellman , Sam, very patiently escorted me from room to room until my expectations were met. The manager Mark was concerned enough to make sure everthing was as expected. We had a bay view suite as a pointe of reference. This is a two room with dining area and jacuzzi bathroom. The room also had a telescope for viewing. There were two flat screen TVs, plenty of comfortable couches and chairs. The lobby had a nice gas fire place that was used as nightly gathering for wine tasting. The location is near shopping, the Buena Vista bar, Pier39, bike rental at Blazing Saddles, was ideal for the active tourist. A very safe area. My only complaint is a minor one. The bar/rest closes at 9pm. So if you come back to hotel for a night cap use your honor bar or leave for local watering hole. P.S. Ericka and Ed were very helpful as concierge. Use them they are helpful.

“Unhappy Guest” My manager likes Country Inn & Suites and was happy to find the Austin North location. The hotel in general was in good shape and the staff was nice, but his room was not clean at all. Moved to Hampton in the next morning.

“Great location, great rooftop bar” This hotel has a great location. Very modern lobby. I loved the vibe. Room was very nice. I paid extra for a late check-out, but housekeeping was banging on my door and trying to enter all afternoon--even when I called down to confirm I had asked for late check out. Front desk is extremely snobby. Do they realize they are working the front desk? No reason to act rude. I was there for baseball, and went to the rooftop bar after. They close at midnight, and then room service also closes at midnight. That is ridiculous in a city as big as San Diego and downtown. THey told me to go to the grocery store across the street. The valets are awesome! They make the hotel. Very cute and funny. Great attitudes. THe front dest should take a lesson from them!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

“Convenient Conference Hotel in all respects” I recently stayed at the Hilton Austin for a four day conference. Because I arrived early, I was checked into a parlor room, which was described as having a bed low to the ground. I was a little nervous. But, the room (1103) was wonderful, VERY large, nice view, with a dining room table, sitting area, bar area with sink, and huge bathroom. The conference areas of the hotel were easy to navigate and the food was delicious. I took advantage of some of the amenities. The exercise room is large and better equipped than most hotel gyms. I enjoyed a manicure and pedicure in the hotel spa, and while pricey, was an enjoyable experience because the technician was such a delight. Everyone I encountered in the hotel was helpful and friendly, from the valet, to the concierge, to the front desk staff. The location was good, as downtown Austin is not huge, and it has many fine restaurants within walking distance and is close to the music district. We also walked to the University, to the bats on The Congress Street Bridge, and took a bus to the South Congress Food Trucks. All in all, no complaints.

“Top class will be staying in this hotel again!” Having read differing reviews on this hotel didn't really know what to expect however from the moment we checked in we weren't disappointed. The reception area was very smart and the staff were very friendly. Our room was initially a 'city view' room on the top floor however when the porter opened the door it hadn't been serviced so he quickly found us another room which we didn't like. A quick call to reception and we were immediately found another on the 38th floor overlooking Central Park! The room was large with quality furniture and flat screen TV, the bed was very comfortable and the shower was the most powerful we have ever had in any hotel anywhere in the world. The maid was very efficient and the room and bathroom were spotlessly clean. The hotel is ideally located with all the main shopping areas, Broadway etc within easy walking distance. Will be going back in 2008 for sure couldn't fault it.

“Excellent location, great facilities” We've stayed here twice with our younger girls. First time was about 4 years ago. The room we were given was looking a little 'tired' and in need of some updating, but the pool area and common areas were excellent. The fire pit by the pool was a great touch (this whole area has been renovated since our last visit). Getting to other areas like Old Town, Mission Beach and La Jolla was super quick and easily. You need a car though to get to any of them. We found the service adequate but not overly friendly, which was surprising for the price we paid, plus the fact that it's a resort where you'd expect people to spend more time there compared to a regular hotel. Overall, a very good experience!

“Great rooms” Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. Fantastic views (we were on the top floor) and absolutely quiet. Room was spacious, well appointed and good options - including DVD, CD, etc. The lobby area is small with options for fine dining or bistro. Bistro food is good but the staff are a little inconsistent (good and bad ones). The fine dining is good, simple and well staffed. As is the front desk staff. Overall, enjoyable hotel, easy access to everything (and walking to most sites and locations as well), subway stop about 5 minute walk away, and well located slightly north of the Whitehouse.

“Great customer service-Mr. Villa is awesome!” I reserved one queen room as a surprise for my parent's 38th anniversary. From the time of booking- to planning a surprise - to checking out - they have been great and efficient. I can't be there but from my parents feedback - they were in awe. They loved the place. Thanks to Mr. Sam Villa- he called me back and I asked him to put together a surprise for my parents. He made sure they were taken cared for. They brought them a strawberry dipped in chocolate and a bottle of wine. They also included a 2 morning buffet breakfast all for $50. I thought it was a great deal. I love the fact that i don't have to do anything. My parents were soooooo happy and felt truly special. Thanks to .my Villa's dedication.

“What a suite deal” All I wanted was an inexpensive room for a one-night stay so my daughter and I could get a head start on shopping before we joined other relatives for a stay at another hotel. A Priceline bid was accepted and we were the winners of a room in a very clean, comfortable hotel in a fantastic location just off 5th Avenue- the one with all the stores. The very charming Grace checked us in efficiently, smiled mysteriously, and whispered that she had given us "a little upgrade". The "little upgrade" was the Diplomat Suite, with a sitting room, bedroom and -*eureka* - TWO bathrooms. Need I tell you how nice it is for two women to have two bathrooms? The rooms were smallish, but clean, quiet and very enjoyable. We felt very safe and secure in the hotel and (did I mention that we wanted to shop?) we were just a few blocks from Rockefeller Center, Saks, the Garment District, and Lord and Taylor's. The hotel seems to be designed for the frequent business traveler, and we didn't have the opportunity to check out all the amenities because we had other plans (did I mention shopping?), but if I'm ever fortunate enough to stay at Club Quarters Midtown again, I'll do so with delight. Thank you, Grace, for getting our annual Girls' Week off to such a nice start. We hope to see you again....so we can do some more shopping.

“Very nice stay right in downtown” I always enjoy staying in downtown San Diego. It's a great walking city. This is a very convenient hotel. We walked through Gaslamp and all the way down to Seaport Village and the harbor area. The guys out front were very helpful with directions and even helped us find a good dinner spot in Little Italy during one of our many walks. Room is a good size...we had 2 queen beds. I liked that I could work in the in the room and close the french doors while my daughter slept in the bedroom. Wi-fi was the best I've experienced in awhile. Only went down a few times. Room is very quiet....slept like a baby. The only improvement I could suggest is to update the bathroom...that door has just got to go, and the whole bathroom could use a makeover. Really enjoyed my stay and would highly recommend to others.

“Fabulous corner room upgrade” I had a wonderful stay in San Diego for a work conference this fall. I had a newborn baby at home, and the hotel staff upgraded me to a corner room so I could have a fridge. The room was very nice, and the view was spectacular. I enjoyed morning runs on the marina, and I will definitely recommend this hotel to others.

“Help me get out of here!!!!!” Are you brave? Are you foolish? Want to make all your nightmares come true? Well then.........stay at the place where you can hear the screaming all the way out on the street - yes folks.......welcome to..........The Hotel Pennnnsylvania. Certainly they must mean Hotel Transylvannia. No...even Dracula wouldn't stay here. If your budget concious, do yourself a favour - get a sleeping bag and sleep in the park instead of here - you'll thank me. This isn't a hotel. It's hell........living hell.

“Excellent - my second stay.” This hotel is so nice. I just love the convenience of basically being right in the airport, no need to take a cab anywhere. I recently stayed for my second time for a one day business meeting. Our group remarked about how nice the hotel was for an airport hotel. This hotel is just great, has a nice cocktail reception, beautiful rooms with all the amenities you could want. Love that you can leave your meeting and be at your airport gate within a few minutes. No hassles of a shuttle or cab needed. Our group meals were all excellent. Meeting rooms fantastic. Just great.

“Great staff, great room, great service” We spent 5 nights at this hotel with a great location close to the freeway. Easy check in and check out. Being Marriott Gold members we also had access to the concierge lounge where they serve a good breakfast & hors d'oevres in the early evening. When we asked about breakfast on Saturday, since the Concierge Lounge is closed on weekends, we were given certificates for a free breakfast in the restaurant. Nice touch, Marriott! We had dinner at the Limestone Restaurant with good service and good food. The room was the usual well decorated, well maintained, great bed that is found at all Marriotts. Another great reason to stay at Marriott.

“Ignoring price: a really great hotel” We ended up having to book a hotel during the Oracle conference, and we ended up paying more for that room than any of us (including two senior execs) had ever spent on a hotel room in their lives. THAT aside: the bed was incredibly comfortable, the staff was friendly and helpful, and it felt more like a suite than a room (even though it was standard). Plus it had free wifi if you were willing to hand out your email address and answer a few questions.

“Trendy, fun hotel” We got a great intro price on the hotel's website so decided to try it out. The hotel is very trendy and modern. If you've stayed at the Ivy, it is very similar. The shower is very nice with a dual showerhead. We had the King Suite, and there were two large LCD TV's along with a vinyl couch and two bar stools. The Sweetwater Saloon at the hotel is fun, definitely not your typical "saloon." It is more of a club. Other than that, we had room service which was pretty good, and then breakfast at MaryJane's coffee shop which was a standard good breakfast. One thing we were not aware of that I would watch for. There is an "IN Charge" on your bill for $15.00. They do not inform you of this until you ask at checkout (if you even do ask). This charge includes all the VOSS water in the room, the copy of Rolling Stone Magazine, some CD I never could find, use of the gym, long distance and local calling, and turndown service at night, which we did ask for, but never got... It would have been nice to know this stuff at check-in, but I guess if they don't tell you, you probably won't use the items, but they can still get their $15 from you. Interesting to say the least... Other than that, we had a good stay and would stay there again - as long as they don't rack their prices up too much after grand opening.

“Excellent Airport Hotel” Well appointed rooms and triple pane glass make this hotel an outstanding choice. You can walk thru the parking garage from any terminal in 10 minutes. Friendly and helpful staff. Great workout facility full of the latest equipment which is well maintained. A 10 min walk or 2 min van ride to the T gets you downtown in a flash.

“Sauber, gute Lage, nette Zimmer, leider Umbaulärm!” Wir haben hier 2 Nächte rund um den Independence Day 2012 verbracht. Die Suites sind sehr geräumig - mit Vorraum und Kücheneinheit, das Bad ist im Vergleich zum Zimmer recht klein, aber ausreichend. Leider fanden gerade große Bauarbeiten statt und es wurde bis 21 Uhr lautstark gebohrt! Sogar auch am 4. Juli, obwohl von der Rezeption aus gesagt wurde, dass es an diesem Tag keine Arbeiten geben wird. Der Lärm hat den Aufenthalt etwas gestört! Toll war das Frühstück - frische Omeletten, Speck und scrambled eggs! Die Auswahl an Joghurts, Obst, Cerealien, etc. war groß und ausreichend. Der Kaffee war für amerikanische Verhältnisse ok. Der Fitnessraum ist geräumig, 2 Laufbänder, 2 Crosstrainer, 1 Ergometer, einige Kraftmaschinen. Top ist, dass es direkt vom Hotel aus einen Zugang zur U-Bahn gibt. Außerdem befindet sich im Erdgeschoss des Hotel eine Cheescakefactory (gutes Essen, gute Cocktails!), ein Starbucks, sowie ein Schuh- und Bekleidungsgeschäft. Gleich vis a vis vom Hotel ist ein Einkaufszentrum sowie in unmittelbarer Nähe ein Whole Food Market. Mit Ausnahme des Baulärms war der Aufenthalt hier sehr angenehm und wir würden hier sicher wieder Urlaub machen!

“Nice details, room, and location” I'm currently staying in this hotel (room 1011), and am really pleased. First, I arrived around noon, before official check in time. The staff checked me in promptly, and upgraded me to a king bed on the top floor (my preferred location). The room is small - rather like a New York-size hotel room. However, the details of how the room is appointed make up for the size. The linens and mattress are terrific - very comfortable, and I'm a linen snob. Plenty of pillows are on the bed, which is great since I tend to do a lot of reading and work on the bed rather than the desk and use them to prop myself up. I slept quite well, which is unusual for me, I don't often sleep well when travelling on business. The room had it's own thermostat, which I appreciate and nearly always change - the system was responsive, and turned off right away when I changed the temperature. A large flat-screen TV with DVD and CD player allow for playing your own DVDs - I always watch movies on my laptop in my room, so I'm really looking forward to watching a movie tonight on a much larger screen with a better sound system than my little laptop. For those who don't bring their own, you can still purchase movies through the TV. Clock radio has an iPod port with charger. The room has a nice size desk, and internet is wireless. Good news: although they charge $10.00/day for access, you can sign up for the Kimpton InTouch membership at no charge, and get free wireless - I did this, and it works well, am on my second day. The bathroom has a decent sized tub and great fixtures - again, smallish, but well appointed. The towels are VERY nice - really thick and soft, am soooo interested in buying some from the Kimpton website if they are avialable. A large closet is provided, with complementary robes in thick animal print terry (animal print is their brand signature). Toiletries are Aveda (nice), and the bathroom has a shaving mirror. Then there are the usuals - iron, ironing board, hair dryer, etc. No coffee maker in room, alas. I do not have a key to the mini bar, but a maid showed up yesterday to refresh the bar and it looked like some really great stuff, not the usual Pringles and almonds. Maid service is good - I went out for a while and my room was pretty clean when I got back (The flat screen could have used some dusting - black shiny surfaces=noted dust collectors). The location is close to the Metro, and the the neighborhood is terrific - lots of great places to eat, and Starbucks is right next door. The restaurant in the hotel (Urbana) is also well thought of, and the room service I had yesterday was very good - great flat-iron steak salad, dates with prosciutto and blue cheese, and a really good gazpacho with heirloom tomatoes for dinner. A bit pricey, but worth the delivery and good flavors. There is also a wine happy hour, and a business center with an ATM. There is a small pool which looks nice, and a workout room I didn't check out. Price for my room is $240/night, but the details make up for it.

“Small rooms great location, hard review to write......” I find this VERY hard to write as this hotel has a lot of potential, we LOVE Kimpton, and the location is AMAZING. People who come here should keep in mind that this is a historic building and things are old and might come apart. Our toilet paper holder and shampoo holders broke off. Also note that these were NOT big deals I am just trying to be honest. The rooms are tiny that is true but the location makes that unimportant in my eyes. You are right on Union Square and can walk anywhere easily. OUr view was in fact of the square with the musicians etc. This hotel though does not offer what all the other Kimptons do: $10 mini bar credit for In Touch Members, wine happy hour in lobby nightly, goldfish in room for kids, kids toy chest. That being said the front desk manager gave us drink coupons when we brought this up so this is not a big deal either. I think the hardest things about this hotel is the paper thin walls (I am sure people hated being by us as well) and how hard it is to get the car from valet (we tried for an hour at one point and no one answered then when they did they said it would be another 20 mins for the car so we just took a cab). The Beefeater down stairs is charming and a great and unique piece of the hotel. They do seem to need more people down there though. The bar is always hoping and seems to be a place to be. I hear they are renovating some rooms here but I cannot speak to if we were in one of those but we had a flat screen so maybe. There is no mini bar or shop in the hotel but a Walgreens across the street for things like Coke and Juice. This is a very hard review to write as I believe it should get a 3.5 but didnt have that choice. This hotel is best for people without kids who want to stay in a great area or for business as each meeting wouldn't be far I imagine. We had the Please make up room on our door for two days and never was serviced which might mean they are understaffed.

“Cool, different hotel.” Cool hotel in Hollywood. Walking distance to Chinese Theater. We stayed in a suite and it had a working record player and actual records (if you are under 25 you might not know what this is, he he). Full kitchen, etc. Again, a cool hotel, but it is a little worn--nothing that would make me change my mind about staying here, but I see them needing to make some renovation in the next year or so. Nice experience, nice location.

“Worked very well” Extremely well located (and yet not noisy) downtown, this is a reasonably proced hotel with small but comfortable suits and a large bathroom. The staff were extremely helpful and the breakfast worth going down for.

“Great atmosphere and theme” The "Tuscan" Inn is recognisable from all directions and inside the theme continues - lots of dark red. But the decor and furniture really was nice and well co-ordinated, it felt like you were staying in a much higher class hotel than it was. Comfortable beds and good water pressure. Very close to the old fashioned trolley rides and the alcatraz ferry, lots of nice walks to be had from the hotel. Downsides are disinterested staff, bordering on rude and quite small rooms. Also we may be two men, but we are a couple. We were put in a room with two separate beds (they were not quite doubles but slightly bigger than singles) - and this is San Francisco of all places! Every other hotel we went to in the USA and Europe asked if we wanted one bed or two when we checked in. The Fisherman's Wharf location is a bit over the top touristy. But it suited us as we were in the mood for a bit of escapism. It's an easy city to get around anyway, so you can easily escape. They pride themselves on their Italian and Chinese food which must mean a lot of entrepreneurs try to cash in.
