Because we ate out both nights and the food was appalling and overpriced compared to here in Melbourne or compared to some of the great spots we found in New York and West Hollywood. Bad luck I suppose. Contrary to all the reviews here, we were on the top floor facing out and noticed no noise! I even had a family member stay here who warned me about the noise but we noticed nothing. Disclaimer: we live in an inner-city apartment at home so may be used to it.

“Lake Union Residence Inn did very well for my family...” Just finished a 5 day stay at the RI in Lake Union with my family...many good points, a few bad ones, and no deal breakers... The Good: We were in room 737 and were delighted with the view of the lake from both rooms and the balcony. Wonderful!! It is worth spending a little extra for this view. Simply stunning. It was great to sit on the balcony and enjoy the sunset each night. The rooms were what I have come to expect from the RI...the kitchen was fine, things were clean and acceptably updated. Wireless connection was fine. Breakfast each morning was solid...not much variation from day to day but, in truth, so what. Light dinner three nights each week was offered but we didn't take part in it. The location, besides the view, is great. The street car is steps from the front door of the hotel. Many sites are walkable...the Seattle Center (Space Needle, Museums, etc.) are less than a mile away. Lovely park across the street with a museum to open in December 2012. We took the street car daily (literally didn't need the car we rented!) and were able to take it to the largest Whole Foods market I have ever seen. While I am not usually impressed with stores, this one was pretty impressive. Staff were on their game...all requests met with immediate attention (nothing major but good to know that they took attending to our creature comforts seriously). Nice touches included having my favorite newspaper delivered each morning without my asking (ok...I am a Marriott Member but not all of their properties have paid attention to the data they have!). We got solid suggestions regarding local eats and things to do. Pool was nice...lap pool for those who are serious, kiddy pool for those who are kids. Gym was small but accessible. One great touch was gas grills on the patio...it was actually very nice to BBQ one night rather than venturing out with tired kids. The Bad: Others have mentioned the construction but unless you really walk the area, you can't fully appreciate what is going on...the nearby roads are being redone, there are some improvements to the park and tram line, and there are a number of office buildings being put up nearby. The neighborhood will be amazing in a while--right now it is a bit messy. The Ugly: Nothing at all ugly about this location... To Do's: Seattle Center was a great day...you don't need to do all of the museums. Bainbridge Ferry was outstanding. Really loved the walk around there. Ride the Ducks...seriously. I thought it would be silly--it was, in the best possible way. Kids loved it. (So what if there was a thunderstorm going on.)

“This is an old gem of a property!” The Palace Hotel is a classic older hotel located in San Francisco. It is high end, and well maintained by a professional and courteous staff. The suite was very nice, I couldn't believe that rooms this large were available in SF. The suite had a large bathroom, a bedroom and a living room. It was very comfortable and well worth the price. The dining room in particular is stunning! The ceiling is glass and gets great sunlight. It is wonderful to be able to see the clouds roll by as you eat. My overall impression is that this is an elegant older place worth visiting.

“Why Ancient Bank Buildings Don't Make Good Hotels” In a way I feel sad for the Langham in Boston. It's a great brand with a great heritage, but its Boston property has a distinct problem: INFRASTRUCTURE. There is nothing that can be done about that, given the fact that the building was the old (in Boston, that means really old) Federal Reserve Bank building. So it has a massive girth, squat height, and wave upon wave of granite facade asking with all of its might that you stay away. The end result, once you do find a way in, is a forced imposition of elegance which, to my experience, did nothing to fight back the overall impression of claustrophobia. Not helpful is the window treatment I found in my room: a relatively small double hung window with an insulating pane screwed in to keep away any access to fresh air and a huge awning covering almost half of the visible exterior space, resulting in a bunker-like view. The location of the building in the continually deadening old center of finance in Boston leaves one with the simple impression that better hotels are to be found. Everything about the service levels during my stay were superb; cheerful and efficient checkin and room service. Welcoming all about. Again, however, I can only feel sad that nothing can be done about the structure and its enveloping gloom...

“Nice hotel” I traveled here for work, which was really close for me fortunately. The hotel was pretty much what one would expect from a La Quinta, the room was comfortable and the bathroom was adequate. The A/C worked quite well and cooled the room nicely, even in the summer in Texas, and it didn't keep me up at all during the night. The pool looked quite nice, although I didn't get a chance to check it out personally. Breakfast was awesome, and it had Texas shaped waffles! Excellent. The front desk lady when I checked in was quite helpful. I asked for a Whataburger, a necessity in Texas, and she found me directions and printed them out while I took my stuff to my room. That was quite nice of her to do, and something you'd expect from a much nicer hotel. Really made an impression.

“the best of all the choices” since our daughter recently began school at USC, we have stayed at the Hilton Checkers 3 times in the last 6 months for various trips there. It is apparently the best of the downtown LA choices. USC recommends various hotels on their website- we have only used the Hilton because it is the only one with two queen beds in the room vs. two doubles (we are a tall family) and we are Hilton Honors members. We have been very pleased by the hotel overall - yes, the shower water is a little unpredictable temp wise (switches from hot to colder randomly), but as with all Hiltons the beds are awesome, the rooms are modern (they just put in flat screens), and the carpet was brand new in the hallways in January. Closets are huge. The lounge is very nice with dinner service available at the bar, the restaurant is fine (I wouldn't eat all my meals here, but breakfast is fine) Workout room is small but acceptable with a nice view, parking is expensive but this is downtown LA. Yes, there are only two elevators, but this was not a problem any time we were there and the hotel was sold out each night. My biggest complaint was that the bathroom counter did not have enough space for three adults' toiletries. Staff is friendly and tries hard to please. Water Grill across the street is one of the best in LA. Based on the reviews of the other hotels downtown I have read on this site, I would not stay anywhere else.

“Customer Service took the weekend off...” Hotel is beautiful and most of the core services are top notch, but customer service took the weekend off. General observations: took multiple attempts for someone to answer the main operator number (appears the hotel was understaffed at the front desk and in other front line service areas), wireless internet not working in our room nor in the Tai Pan club, complete lack of follow up from the on duty manager over two nights, and white dust/dirt all over the driver side floor mat/console area of our vehicle at valet checkout. Background: called main operator number regarding wireless internet problem, transferred to an offsite help desk (between hold and trouble shooting time wasted almost 30 minutes), an unidentified hotel employee called the room around 2100 and told us IT was unable to repair the problem and we would need to change rooms for internet access (move my 9 month pregnant wife at that late hour? after more back and forth, told it would be resolved the next day), after a relaxing morning at their beautiful spa returned to the room and still no internet, stopped at the front desk on way out of the hotel for the afternoon (no knowledge of the internet problem and the lady explained it was probably my fault for not accepting the charge during the wireless configuration process...she had no clue and clearly did not understand anything about the issue, but assured me it would be resolved and someone would follow up....NO follow up...NOT even an explanation after my third contact). I finally gave up and did my business over the telephone. Upon checkout, my driver side vehicle floor mat was covered in a white dust/dirt. Valet was very apologetic and explained someone probably made the large mess the night before during a rainstorm...valet cleaned up the best he could with some towels/water and I departed with a very messy vehicle. Only plus for their weekend customer service was their Club Concierge who was pleasant and helpful. Minus that positive impression, a complete customer service failure! We selected Mandarin for relaxation, but departed with frustration. We will definitely consider going back to Georgetown Ritz before spending another $1,500 weekend at this Mandarin location. Not the norm for Mandarin's other properties...

“Room was dingy, disappointing” Start with the positives: The lobby is stunning. The location can't be beat (especially for my visit). Every member of staff I interacted with was friendly (though a note on this below). Outweighed, unfortunately, by the bad. The room was worn to a shocking degree. Peeling wallpaper, insects in the bathroom, a very worn and stained carpet, stained floor in the bathroom and cracking grout, peeling paint and a door nob about to fall out in the bathroom. I found the bed linens to be scratchy--something I've never run into in a Hilton--though some of that could be psychosomatic. The room felt dirty, not helped by two long dark hairs left on the fresh towels. I got to be serenaded by the couple in the room next to me when it was time to sleep; the walls were paper thin. As I said, folks were friendly. I was a bit surprised that they had two people working the line for check in. One trying (awkwardly) to make conversation, the other with cold water (a very nice touch on a hot day). Had they trained one of these people to help with check-ins, though, we wouldn't have had as long a wait. As it was, the check-in process was slower than it needed to be, even after I got to the counter. I chose the hotel based in large part on the positive reviews here on Tripadvisor, and on the location. I had been here for a conference a few years back and been unimpressed by the meeting rooms, but figured I'd give it another chance based on the generally good reviews here. I suspect that had I gotten one of the renovated rooms (I was on the 21st floor), I would have had a much better experience. I've lived in NYC and Tokyo, small doesn't bother me. I guess I could have requested being moved, but I was exhausted and had no way of knowing if this was actually the standard of the hotel. I guess the take-away is that Chicago has a lot of very nice hotels, and hotels that cost less and provide a nicer stay. For me, at least, I doubt I'll give the Palmer House another chance, Honors points be damned. Happy to come and have a drink in their beautiful lobby, but otherwise I'll pick one of the other nearby hotels that provide a much better value. If you do decide to go here, make sure when you are making your reservation that you have a renovated room.

“Bumped out on a flight...get a free room” I was "volunteered" aka bumped out for my flight in Charlotte to my home. In their comps, I was given a free hotel for the night (without my luggage). On the upside, the room was clean with a smaller bathroom. The water was fine. However, on the downside, the mattress was a basic motel stuff, hard springs throughout. There are a Crackle Barrel and Waffle House is walking distance plus a gas station if the tank is empty. For the money, I stay there again. But then, it wasn't my money.

“Pass on this one” I stayed at this hotel with a group of folks for a convention and none would return. Everyone changed rooms but there was still problems. Fresh coat of paint and new carpet just seemed to be a cover for something dark and dirty lurking below. The hotel bar/lounge was the best part (we had to drink before we could subject ourselves to the rooms) but very pricey. Found out way too much from the locals about what goes on in this lounge!! I would recommend that you check out a kimpton group hotel fairly close...the hotel rouge!! One of the best!!

“Great hotel and can't beat the location!!” Just spend a two night weekend stay at the hotel with partner. This was my first time visiting Denver and the hotel couldn't be in a more ideal and convenient location. Everything is within walking distance of the hotel. Shops and many great choices of restaurants. We arrived on an early morning flight and they were nice enough to let us check in before noon. The hotel is obviously an older property and it does show a few signs of wear but I read that a major renovation is coming soon. Still the property was absolutely spotless. The fitness center and pool are were really great. The room had all the standard hyatt amenities you would expect. Dined downstairs for breakfast and I usually avoid hotel breakfasts because they are always so mediocre. The breakfast buffet at Pub 17 was excellent. Pancakes and french toast made to order. The staff was very friendly and attentive service. As always this hotel reaffirmed my past Hyatt experiences. You can always count on Hyatt to provide you with a great experience. Next trip to Denver this will definitely be the hotel we choose once again.

“GRAND TRADITION” The "Suite Celebration" promotion could not be turned down ; we would have loved going back to the Four Seasons, but with a price tag in excess of $1100+ for the smallest room at the time of our stay, we decided to try a new place instead. New might not be the right word, though, to qualitly this stately Grande Dame towering over Central Park. Everybody that counted in the 20th century stayed there; you can feel it, like being handed a chance to stay there. We had booked a Premier One-Bedroom Suite, and were allocated one on the 27th floor. A corner suite, really large, probably larger tha our Paris flat, with the focus on the living room and bed room, which were huge. Beautiful city views to the east from both, with an extra voew to the south from the bedroom. Massive heavenly bed. Admittedly, the bathroon the bathroom was on the smaller side, still with a tub and a separate shower stall, but no separate WC. Those were the days ... Bathroom perfectly up to date, with great pressure, wonderful full size Molton Brown amenities. Housekeeping is fantastic : it was never to be seen, and did a beautiful job. Nice friendly operators in the elevators, some of which could use better airconditionning (the elevators, not the operators). Fantastic concierge whi went out of ther way to locate some stores, and did some follow up on it when we got back. They seem interested ! Both on check-in and out, valet obliged and hold our rental car for a little while, not actually taking it away. Breakfast is good, but the selection is limited. No smoked salmon bagel in the ciy where it was created. Drawbacks ? Not really. We checked in on my birthday, and although I had made it clear when booking, this was never acknowledged in any way. There is one house car, probably a single one, which was NEVER available to us : it had either just left, of was stuck somewhere ; and when it was parked in front, the driver could not be located. And last, why is it that none of the non signature suite has a park view ? Or perhaps non of them was available ib the Suite celebration.

“Hotel designed for business conferences - NOT family travel” I just returned from a stay at this hotel for 4 days/3 nights. It was an "OK" hotel. My company paid $450/nt for this hotel, and I don't consider that a fair rate for an "OK" hotel. I have stayed at many JW Marriott's and this just doesn't compare. The good parts... The hotel is beautiful and huge. Everything is spotless in the lobby and public areas. Lots of hotel employees around waiting to assist you. The room had a nice big flat screen tv and the bed was very comfortable with lots of pillows. The location is perfect; within a few blocks, you can be at the White House, Smithsonian, National Aquarium, National Archives, Washington Monument, Ford's Theater, Monaco, and more. The bad parts... Prepare to be nickel and dimed A LOT. Despite the hefty price tag, you don't get anything complimentary in this hotel. No free internet service. No free local or toll free calls. I could not connect to the internet during my entire stay. The only option they offered was one of the lobby computers, at a rate of $6.00/min. I was on the phone with the ibahn IT help desk trying to connect to the internet, and then the hotel charged me for the phone call to the help desk (I complained and they did remove the charge). The room was fairly small and just not up to JW Marriott standards. It was a typical hotel room, nothing nice about it except for the extra large tv. The restaurant and room service are exorbitant. One morning for breakfast I got special K, a banana, and tea and it was $25.00 after the tip. One evening at the restaurant I got shrimp cocktail, soup, and a wedge salad and it was $45.00 after the tip. There are not a wide variety of choices for eating in the area if you don't want fast food or cafe food, so sometimes I was just stuck paying these prices. Bottom line - if you are not paying, then this is an ok place to stay, mostly because of the location. If you are footing the bill, definitely stay somewhere else more friendly to casual travelers.
“大きい、便利” マンハッタン最大級のホテルです。 ですので施設、サービスの内容は充実しています。立地も何処に行くのも便利で、とくにタイムズスクエアに寄り道しながら行くのにはいいと思います。 しかしこのホテルに限ったことではないですが、マンハッタンのホテルは費用対効果が低いですね。

“Excellent location” Stayed in one of their better Club rooms which was nice and large with a good wardrobe area and nice bathroom. We had breakfast in the attached bar/restaurant and the food was very good. Perfect location right on Union Square and only a few minutes walk to Chinatown which has some very good restaurants, hotel also has a nice indoor swimming pool which unfortunately we never had the time to use. Very helpful staff on reception although for some reason one particular concierge was almost snooty, totally without a smile on his face and you felt like he was doing you a favour just helping you with information. Would stay here again.
“Grand Hotel but way overpriced!!” Stayed at the Soho Grand for 3 nights. Very nice lobby and bar area. The rooms were very clean and very small. Overall I liked the hotel but it is overpriced.

“Attention to Detail Is Paramount at the Willard” I stayed at the Willard when I was ten years old. I had passed by and had even attended a black tie event there in my 20's, but hadn't stayed there again until I ushered my mid-30's in there. My husband, daughter, parents, and I celebrated my birthday weekend at the Willard this past spring. We had side-by-side rooms. Unfortunately the rooms didn't connect because of a wiring problem with the door. However, that was the only "problem" we encountered during our stay. The Willard was the first overnight hotel experience we had with our baby. She was four and a half months old when we stayed there. The hotel not only had a crib for her, they included a plush Ralph Lauren blanket for her to lay use during the stay. In addition, we requested a microwave to sterilize her bottles in the room. The hotel provided it at no extra charge. The room was beautifully appointed and very large. We were thrilled with the size of the bathtub, which allowed us to bathe our daughter with ease. The Willard's location is wonderful when you're in DC. While you have to walk a few blocks to get to the orange or blue Metro lines, it's so centrally located and close to the Mall that it's a perfect place to stay when in DC.

“Nice suite hotel in the heart of Greektown” I stayed at the Atheneum for a Friday and Saturday night in July 2010. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I stayed in a deluxe suite. I won the room on Skyauction.com for $270 for two nights, taxes included. The room was HUGE! A seating area with a large screen TV, and bathroom, and then the sleeping area with another large screen TV. I didn't watch much TV, but if you like to watch two programs at once, this would be the hotel for you! The furniture was kind of "funky", but comfortable. Free Wi Fi in the room. maid service was very prompt. I was never bothered by outside noise or noise from other rooms. I guess there is a MIchigan law which says you cannot bring alcohol into the hotel if the hotel has a liquor license. I read some earlier reviews about not being able to bring alcohol into the hotel. I think as long as you weren't trying to bring two cases of beer through the lobby this wouldn't be a problem. I was able to bring my own bottle and mixer in with no problems. There was a "Peoplemover" stop right next to the hotel. The hotel also offered a shuttle service which I didn't use. Being right in the heart of Greektown there were all kinds of restaurants and bars within easy walking distance. Greektown is a pretty lively place on Friday and Saturday nights. The Greektown Casino was across the street. I was going to do a little gambling, but with a $15 minimum bid on the tables, I decided to save my money. ;-) I walked to the transit center and took the tunnel bus to Windsor, Ontario for a few hours on Friday night. The hotel was also within walking distance of ComericA Park to watch a Tigers game, which I did on Saturday afternoon. Overall, I enjoyed my stay here. If you could get the room for about what I paid, I think it would be a good value, as the rack rate was about $200 a night + taxes.

“Beautiful hotel! Will stay again.” Living in the Chicago suburbs, I've stayed at this hotel twice in the last year for quick getaways in the city and I will definitely return. The staff aims to please here. At check in, they give you a warm towel for your hands and kids receive a Trump backpack with a stuffed animal and a baseball cap inside. I don't really enjoy corporate advertising, but the kids enjoyed the goodies. On both visits (one with kids, one without), we stayed in a suite. I don't recall the floors but the rooms were high enough to have great views of the Chicago River and a partial view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. Floor to ceiling windows maximize the view. The beds are phenomenal. I've stayed in many high end hotels and these beds and pillows were top of the line! I never wanted to leave that bed. The bathroom is granite throughout and quite nice. In the smaller suite, the tub was contained within the shower. In the larger fireplace suite (fireplace wasn't real), it was separate. My kids enjoyed the TV screen that was contained within the mirror. I thought it was an inconvenient location and made it difficult to see in the mirror. My biggest disappointment with the rooms were the towels, robes and toiletries. I really would have expected higher end from Trump Tower. The towels weren't that large, nor were they very plush. The toiletries seemed like something generic with the Trump name on them. The toiletries are something I look forward to trying at higher end hotels, so this was a big disappointment. I did enjoy the kitchenette feature in both rooms. Very convenient. You have to access the pool through the spa (which smells wonderful!). It was a bit on the small side. Having cold water with lemon slices available was a nice touch though. The concierge couldn't have been better. The staff goes out of their way to make families with kids feel comfortable, but I didn't want to take my three kids to the hotel restaurant on a Saturday night. Although they are well-behaved, I never want to take the chance of disturbing other diners at a high end establishment on a Saturday night. The concierge was helpful with recommending a more kid-appropriate, non-chain restaurant with food and drinks that the adults could still enjoy. On our visit without kids, my husband and I really enjoyed the hotel bar (blanking on the name). The martinis, while a bit overpriced, were fabulous and the views made up for the price! We did try the hotel restaurant for breakfast with the kids and I have to say, we did not like it at all. We really appreciate well prepared food and this was not it. I would think breakfast would be a tough meal to mess up, but I was wrong. We like to stay at different hotels when we head into the city, so while I may not rush back to Trump Tower, I would definitely visit again, and recommend it to out of town friends.

“Not boutique.” Rather than stay at the hard rock hotel I decided on the ACME for 5 nights, based on the Stella reviews on here. All through my stay I kept wishing id stayed at the hard rock. Who on earth thought to call it ACME, a silly name, I just don’t get it. Appearance wise it doesn’t stand out and its right next to a grotty hostel. I walked past it twice when trying to find it. The check-in area is literally a room and a desk but hey its cool as it has graffiti on the walls to draw you attention away! I was assured id be upgraded when I checked in however they couldn’t as the manager wasn’t there. I emailed him and had no reply. My room was a king on 15th floor, very cramped sidewise even though it was their biggest king. Two people would struggle to move around each other. The water pressure is poor, the tap and shower dribble, very disappointing as it’s a lovely styled bathroom. Hairdryer barely dries you, it’s pathetic. The air-con is also poor, very noisy and doesn’t give off much cool air. What annoyed me is that they advertise super fast blazing internet. This doesn’t exist, just wifi that’s only ok. I enquired at reception and the guy didn’t know what I was talking about! Also, there is no ‘wireless audio system via a bowers and Wilkins system’ like they advertise. I had a small cheap iPod dock. I had one window that looked into someone else’s room so I couldn’t have the blind up so it felt dark 24/7. The TV channels are also poor, no HBO or movies, just a basic cable package. Breakfast is basically a holiday inn express style buffet, good luck finding a table to sit. I sat on some stairs. In the room there is nowhere to put your luggage and no closet! Just wire racks with 3 hangers either size! Overall I was hugely disappointed and will not be going back, I paid allot of money, this is no way a boutique hotel. It is a glorified holiday inn express with nicer fittings and fixtures. Start scratching under the surface a bit and you’ll see for yourself what I mean.
“Nice Place” This hotel is in a great location-off union. This place is a great choice.

“Stayed here several times” Always like staying here. Place is new, modern and very clean. I am a Platinum Member and this hotel ranks in the top 20% of Holiday Inns I stay at. There is an Outback down the street. Area is nice, right off the Interstate. Good place.

“My new 'go-to' hotel for Jacksonville!” Amazing, from start to finish! Plenty of parking - covered deck. Lovely pool + hot tub (super-clean, very pretty courtyard setting). Entire hotel EXTREMELY clean & staff (ALL) were just amazing. Full kitchen with cook-to-order breakfasts plus a buffett if you so desire. I cannot say enough great things about this location, althought he Jax downtown area can be a bit overwhelming/confusing, just ask the desk for a special downtown map - makes for easier navigation than GPS even. If you do not like road noise (it is in downtown next to the HWY) ask for a pool-view room as this may help, noise still was not bad at all regardless. This is my new GO-TO spot for Jax!

“great value; great location” This hotel is located in the middle of the Galleria area, an excellent area to stay in Houston. The hotel was clean, the staff friendly and helpful. The room was a nice size, not fancy, but offered all the basic amenities making our travel stay easier. There was a wedding party at the hotel so the manager put us on a different floor, facing the courtyard, respecting our desire for quiet. The breakfast was just adequate, but having a kitchen offered options. Overall a great choice for a Houston stay!

“Unbelievably Bad” Due to the Oklahoma State Cowboys being invited to the Holiday Bowl, we started making plans to drive to San Diego and make a three day road trip. I found a 3 star resort on Hotwire and decided to give it a try. When we arrived at the hotel, we found total chaos at the front counter. We were given instructions to our room and when we opened the door, we found a king size bed with bed taking up the entire room. Because there was 3 of us, 1 being an 11 year old, I called Town & Country after I booked on Hotwire and was assured we were given a no smoking room with two beds. We drove back up to the front counter and explained that we needed two beds and we were given a king size bed. The employee stated since Town & Country was a resort, they only guaranteed a room, not anything else. I asked why I was told by an employee of Town & Country that we were given a no smoking room with two beds. The employee changed her story to our room being occupied by some people who wouldn't leave. Right beside me during this exchange was a lady who was at the counter when we checked in which was about 30 minutes ago. Turns out, she booked on Orbitz and Town & Country was claiming they didn't receive the reservation. All evidence was pointing to Town & Country overbooking and now they didn't have enough rooms. I told the employee that she was going call Hotwire and explain to them that they did not have the room that was promised. She did call Hotwire and told the employee that I did not find the facility acceptable so the Hotwire employee asked to speak with me. I explained the situation to Hotwire and was told they would refund the price immediately and asked to speak with the Town & Country employee. The Hotwire employee asked the Town & Country employee if they were going to find alternate arrangements for us and was told no. By this time, I had been lied to so much that I just wanted to leave and never come back. As I was leaving, I noticed the lady who had booked through Orbitz was still there without a room. Luckily, I had joined AAA before I left and had their California book with us. We called several hotels in the area and eventually found a Comfort Inn Hotel & Suites not far away. This room was much nicer and larger than the room at Town & Country plus parking was only $5.00 a day instead of the $14.00 charged at Town & Country. Why Town & Country Resort survives is beyond me. Worst service in the world, rooms that are no larger than a king size bed, furnishings that could be found at a flea market.. There is just no reason to stay here when there are so many other choices in the same price range.

“A good stay in DC” The location is excellent. Service was friendly, attentive and helpful. Food at the Biersch restaurant is nicely done, and so is the beer. I'll be staying here more often when I'm in DC.

“Great location, very good hotel” Stayed here for 2 nights on business. The location is ideal, you are about a block from the State/Lake L stop, so a trip from Midway will take you 30 minutes and cost $2.50, much better than a cab. I requested an early check-in, and got it with no problems whatsoever. My room had no view, but it was clean and comfortable. My interaction with staff was minimal, but I found the door-people to be helpful and pleasant. Easy walk to the Magnificant Mile, and the proximity to the L makes everything else easy to get to as well. Would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Old, gross, and sketchy” Was in a pinch. Needed to be in NYC at the last minute for business but my usual hotels were booked solid and this was the only spot even remotely in the neighborhood. This hotel shows its age. My room was dingy with broken furniture and rusty fixtures in the bathroom. The halls are dark and poorly lit. The place is massive and filled to the brim with busloads of students. I would not recommend this hotel

“Great location in D.C.!” We stayed here over the July 4th weekend, and we really enjoyed our stay. The hotel is conveniently located, within walking distance of most of the major sites and monuments of Washington, D.C. The hotel itself is comfortable, as you'd expect from a Courtyard Marriott. I appreciate the in-room coffee maker and the free wi-fi, as I was there on business. The concierge is very helpful. In fact, I found all of the employees happy to go out of their way to assist their guests. The fitness center is small, but functional. The pool is quite small--much too small to swim laps in, but it would probably satisfy small children who need some pool time. This hotel does not try to be a five-star hotel, but it performs very well in the market segment that it does target. This was my second stay at this hotel, and I will definitely stay here again when I am in the D.C. area again.

“SMALL” Small rooms ,small bathroom and no drawers to store your clothes.Constuction outside starts early,around 5AM I found small bites on my arm one morning I think caused by bedbugs but not 100% sure.Plusses are easy walk to many of the sights you want to see,easy access to Metro system and very helpful front desk.I received good price for room but would never stay at this hotel again.

“Good hotel outside of city” We were frustrated by traffic getting to the hotel and found the parking garage to be both expensive and difficult to maneuver around. Not a good start for our stay but the rest of the stay was very good. Everything was clean and well taken care of. I didn't look into it but there is probably an interesting history to the building. The older section looks very interesting. I had no complaints at all over the four days we stayed. Several options on site for eating. Prices seemed on the high side but really pretty typical for the area. There are some good options for restaurants a few blocks away. Wireless in rooms is not free so be prepared to visit the lobby for free access or pay for Internet. Conference facilities are good if staying for business. Fitness center was one of the better ones I've been in at a hotel. This is one of only hotels in the area. Right next to Metro.

“Nice hotel, okay location for tourists” Very nice hotel with large rooms and large bathrooms. We had a corner executive king with a partial view of the Golden Gate Bridge. We took a cab from the airport that was around $50. We stayed two nights. The first night I heard a lot of street noise but I don't live in the city so I don't know how that affects others. We were on the 20th floor. Breakfast in the concierge lounge was okay but the coffee machine (espresso, latte, etc.) was wonderful. The appetizers in the evening were not hot (cold beef skewers? ick). There was a nice cheese plate though. $7 for wine and around $9 for cocktails. Lots of water and granola bars. Parking is $50 per night so we took a cab from the airport as I mentioned and then rented from the Avis down the street (675 Post St) at the end of our stay. There is a Hertz in the hotel but it was significantly more expensive. The concierge gave us great recommendations for dining and directions to various attractions. Although I liked the hotel I would consider staying at the Marriott Fishermans Warf next time just because of the location. We were sightseeing and spent a lot of time getting to where we needed to be. On the upside we were able to ride the cable cars quite a distance which was a fun experience.

“Clean and convienient” Spent one night in Philly en-route from Washington to New York and found the hotel to be a very decent hotel. Friendly and welcoming staff, who were very accommodating when arriving a few hours before check in time. The room itself was a fair size and clean. In simple terms, it was the sort of hotel room you would expect for £80 per night near a tourist area/city centre. They also offer a complimentary breakfast buffet though this was fairly 'basic'.

“gutes Hotel - tolle Lage” Auch hier war ich vor drei Jahren bereits, meine Bewertung erneuere ich hiermit. Das Hotel liegt am Fishermans Wharf, also sehr zentral in San Francisco. Die Zimmer verteilen sich über vier Stockwerke. Nachmittags gibt es in der Lobby kostenlos Wein. Das Publikum ist quer durch den Garten von jung über alt, von Business über Touristen. Die Lage ist absolut Top, fast alle Sehenswürdigkeiten sind zu Fuß oder mit dem CableCar zu erreichen. Da ich bereits zum wiederholten Mal da war bat ich um ein Zimmer, dass nicht direkt zur Straße liegt. Man sagte mir dass es leider nicht anders ginge, ich aber am nächsten Morgen direkt umziehen könnte. Dies erübrigte sich allerdings, als ich feststellte, dass das ZImmer zum Innenhof, und nicht zur Straße lag. Bilder/Videos zur Hotelbewertung (Zur Vergrößerung einfach auf die Bilder klicken!) Frühstück gibt es im Restaurant. Bei uns war es eingeschlossen und wir fanden es ziemlich armselig. Tee oder Kaffee. O-Saft, Buttertoast und Konfitüre ODER ein Croissant, dazu etwas Obst. Für 5 USD kann man das Frühstück upgraden! Achtung, die 5 Dollar-Gutscheine, die man für das Restaurant bekommt, wenn man sein Zimmer NICHT reingen läßt, gelten nicht für das Frühstück. Die ZImmer sind recht geräumig und geschmackvoll eingerichtet. Es gibt Flat TV, Telefon, seperates Bad und WiFi.

“Poor first imprressions.” Booked into Room 110 for 2 nights. Only one light/lamp worked and TV was out of order. Called front desk and they sent someone to fix everything. TV still had some issues on ocassion. WiFi signal was week and cut out alot of times. This is a very busy property so don't expect early check-in. Pretty convenient to freeways and the motel sits up the street from a Starbucks and gas stations.

“Pretty Sneaky” This property is a new Sheraton, and was very recently remodeled. The new decor looks snazzy, with the new era look. The carpet is cool, but the room, and bathroom were small. The bed was comfy, while the pillows were not. This property charges $10.95 for Internet access, but they do not disclose the local phone charges anywhere in the room. If you access through a local ISP, they actually charge you more than the $10.95. Parking is expensive; self park is over $12, and Valet parking is over $18 per night. I forget my cell phone charger in the room, and I attempted to reach the hotel. I left messages for lost and found, and Housekeeping. I even had Starwood Preferred call them. They never called me back. This is the hotel where cell phone chargers go to die! This hotel has a great location, with a old building that has been successfully remodeled. The negative is the extra charges, and complete lack of customer service. Even the check in was an ordeal.

“Nice area” Not a Holiday Inn EXpress so no free Breakfast.. but i like this location and plenty of places to eat. the hotel is very big, very nice bar area to enjoy a drink, I had a nice room with a nice view from my window and clean bed, Bathroom is a very old style with the toilet right at the door when you go in, some tiles a little loose that i reported. which i reported and offered to move me to another room which i decline since i like the one i was in. a lot of residential buildings across the street and a Starbucks a block up so lots of pretty woman walking bye :) sorry got off track. very nice hotel on my list as a choice during my Layovers in New York City

“Surprisingly Nice and Very Convenient” I just got back from a business trip to Chicago. Because of a large convention in town, the only hotel I could find in the area I needed to be in (River North) was the Best Western Plus. Although I have nothing against Best Westerns, I usually stay at what are considered full-service hotels and I think of Best Westerns as roadside inns for families. I was so pleasantly surprised with this property! There is a good Italian restaurant and bar just off the lobby that has killer Chicago style, deep dish pizza. There is a small but serviceable fitness room on the roof with an indoor pool. Although I didn't use it, the hotel offers free WiFi and FREE PARKING (unheard of in downtown Chicago.) My room was pleasant, rather large, and well equipped with extra pillows, blankets, coffee maker, hair dryer, etc. If you are looking for exceptional value in Chicago, you need to look no further than the Best Western Plus River North Chicago Downtown!

“Runtergekommen und dunkel, nichts positives zu berichten.” Das Hotel liegt nicht sehr weit weg vom Stadtzentrum in Denver. Ueber das Hotel selbst kann ich leider nichts gutes sagen. Die Zimmer sind alte, stinkig, klein und dunkel. Eine Renovierung waere dringend ueberfaellig. Was mich besonders stoert, ist das hier versucht wird alt und modrig als "historic" und "boutique zu verkaufen. Ich wuerde hier nicht wieder uebernachten.

“Did not impress” I travel quite a bit to Boston on work and usually stay at the Intercon or Langham... Always seen the Boston Harbor Hotel and thought about staying there so this time around I did and I was less than impressed. Next time I am going back to the Intercon or Langham.

“Xanadu” The Ritz Carlton Dallas is perfect. the property is new and extraordinary. the rooms are spacious. the baths are marvelous and some have TV's hidden in the mirrors. They get it and they designed the hotel for comfort for high end business travelers. The fitness center is large and has windows. There are a number of new Precor treadmills and elipticals, each with it's own TV. They also have a nice circuit of top quality weight machines. The pool is lovely and private on an upper floor off the fitness center. The spa completes this floor with a full blown salon, a dozen treatment rooms,and locker rooms that are the envy of every other high end hotel. The food is remarkable. The hotel is home to Dean Fearing's restaurant where they prepare innovative Southwestern cuisine. the lobster nachos are a must. Dean is on site and is likely to visit your table and chat. his passion is what makes his restaurant a breed apart. His staff is exceptional. They great you by name, they remember what you like to eat and drnk, and they genuinely care about your comfort. As one example, the staff knows what I like for breakfast and that I like to sit at the bar. They find out when I am in house and the set up is waitin for me each morning along with the NY Times at my usual seat at the bar courtesy of Linda who is amazing. The bar staff is at the very top of the game. The bartenders-- Jamie, Jillian, Sedrick, Ryan and Amir are pros. They will remember your drink and your name and greet you like an old friend. Johnnie doubles as a bartender and cocktail waitress and she is wonderful and Rachel, another cocktail waitress is one of the best in the business. Mary and Samantha are the guardians of the gate at Fearing's and they will try to accommodate any request. The folks in the spa are wonderful too. Stephanie cuts hair as good as anyone in Beverly Hills and sings in a band on the weekends.Sheena does nails and she treats you like family. Aryn gives a great deep tissue massage and she is a sweetheart. Julie rinse the spa and she will attempt to accommodate just about any reasonable request, even finding me an extra large bathrobe! Kent is the conceirge. He can accomplish just about anything on short notice and with a smile.He can also get the house car--a Bentley-- to take you up to 3 miles away. Nice touch rolling up on your friends in a Bentley. The front door staff is great. DiDi and Melvin great you like an old friend and Steven does a great job and he enjoys his work and it ahows. I know I am leaving out some great people, but they are all excellent. Andrea at the front desk always greets me with a smile and they often upgrade their best customers without you having to ask. There is a wonderful club. room with great food, so ask them about the club floor when you check into the hotel. I have stayed at most of the t hotels in the country and all of the Ritz Carlton hotels in America and the Ritz Carlton Dallas is the very best because the people are passionate about providing outstanding service.

“Great hotel if you get the right rate.” I've got a stunning rate of 109 USD per night plus tax while the standard rate would have been 189.00. On top of 109.00 or 189.00 whatever the hotel charges you a 48 dollars per day for the parking !!!! Outrageous !! Do yourself a favor at park around the corner on Mission street for 32 per day. Nice rooms and mattresses,I really like the Westin style. WIFI was extra at least at my rate,I really hope for 189 per night you would get that for free....

“Worn, Dated and Dirty Hotel past its heyday” I have stayed at this hotel many times for a conference. Each year it gets worse. This year, the room was filthy. There was a dirty napkin in the made bed, the shower had hair in it. Every day there were housekeeping problems (no soap, missing towels, etc.). The rooms are worn and dated (from the 90's) and this place is in desperate need of better service and remodeling. If this wasn't the only place to stay for thisannual conference, I would stay elsewhere. Note: Banquet food was good, but temperature control in meeting rooms was a problem -bring a sweater.

“very nice, but should have been a little nicer” We stayed here before and it has always been great. But this time I have a few little nits. There was never a bellman to help us get our luggage out of the cab from the airport, or help us hail a cab while we were there, or help us load our luggage back into a cab when we left for the airport. Also the concierge was never available either in person or on the phone, and he/she did not return calls left on the answering machine. There were also only 2 bath towels in the very teeny bathroom, and there were 3 of us. And the dvd player didn't work, but it was replaced the following day. Gee, I sound really crabby. It really wasn't a bad experience (the room was clean, the location is great, the front desk was super, the free wifi and happy hour appreciated), just not as great as previous times at this hotel. Maybe they were short-staffed for the holidays.

“another visit to the Sax...and it didn't dissapoint!” This is our fifth annual visit to Hotel Sax and although I have reviewed it before, I feel compelled to do so again. We booked our trip on travelocity and it was extremely reasonable to fly and stay over Labor day weekend. as always, the concierge, front desk, and the bell men were helpful and friendly. We stayed on the 10th floor in a room with a king bed. The room was clean, spacious and the bed was comfortable. The only complaint is that the bathroom sink was tiny and there was no room to set anything on top of it without it falling in the sink or on the floor. The maid service was slow but i would imagine they were full for the long weekend. we had wine and cheese purchased from Bin36 in our room during two nights of our stay and it was awesome. the people are friendly, helpful, and quick in getting you your order to go. we had never done this before and will definitely do it again next year. the hotel is close to everything and is in a great location. for breakfast, there are many options since room service is expensive (starbucks, einstein bagel accross the street, and the huge mcdonalds down the road). i love the hotel sax!

“Dated and Enormous” This place has an exceptional staff - very kind and helpful. They need to be, because this is a tough hotel in terms of layout. It is enormous, and the signage isn't great for finding rooms. No wireless Internet in rooms (even for a fee), and many of the rooms have a funky odor. The place needs a serious upgrade. If you do have a room here, ask for one near the front desk (I think that would be in the towers) to save a hike. It's also easier to find your room in that section of the hotel.

“Didnt want Logan area but it turned out OK anyway.” I went on Priceline at the last minute and figured if I could snag a room cheap I would stay over, if not, I would do the drive home. I forgot to uncheck "Logan" as a search area and put in my very low price for a 4 star hotel within Boston. Yep, as soon as it said Congrats I knew at 79 it had to be something near Logan.. UGH!. It's way out of the way if your kicking around downtown and want to stay around the sights. But all in all, it turned out to be a nice place to stay the night. The staff at check in were great, very friendly. The front desk agent seeing my 7 year old boy asked if we wanted a Boston view, or one of the airport. My 7 year old yelled, "airport" so we had a lovely view of runway 44 LOL... . My kids liked the lap pool but I could tell that there were some serious swimmers waiting for the kids to get out so they can do their workout. To get to the pool you have to go through this narrow gym with people doing all of these stretches on the floor and your walking over them pretty much... strange culture those health clubs.. But, in the end, if your staying downtown and your doing the swan boats, etc., this place by the location only isnt where you want to be. However, if you are flying out in the early a.m., it's ideal.

“The suite life!” I stayed at the legendery Waldorf Astoria two times in May 2010, and have the following tips to the HHonors Diamond tier members. The hotel will upgrade you to suite subject to availability. However they will not mention that you are entitled to another benefit as per rules. I would recommend that you explicitly ask for the USD20 voucher for beverages. Also try asking for suite 25R which is very spacious and relaxing. The Sunday brunch at the hotel's Oscar's American Brasserie is not to be missed.
“I ́ll return” Pros: Rooms completely restored. Ipod docks. Kindly Staff. Good location (Broadway and 77th.). Internet wifi free in rooms. Cons: Too small rooms.

“Excellent use of cash&points” This hotel is a bargain for a Starwood hotel, if you belong to their Starwood Preferred Guest program. We used 4800 points and paid $90. We found check-in very efficient, got a slightly upgraded room too. Our room on the 8th floor was on the Lexington Ave. side of the hotel, there was significant traffic noise as a result. The room was modest in size, which is not unusual, in my experience, in New York. The lobby area is quite attractive. The elevators were a little on the slow side, and required the insertion of your room key to operate.

“Nice hotel, but it was the staff who made it so.” I attended Comicon here this year over the Memorial Day weekend. The hotel was just across the street from the convention center, so its location is what brought me to the hotel. The lobby is nice and comfy, with a southwestern decor. The giftshop has many fine AZ souvenirs. I didn't go to the Compass restaurant due to its prices, but the Einsteins Bagels was great for drinks and inexpensive salads and wraps. Terrace Cafe had good breakfasts. The Networks Bar and Grill was great for evening meals, with the drinks being especially good. Our first waitress, Valerie, was the best! It must have been good food since I gained 2 pounds even though I walked all over the convention center 4 days straight. I did not use the pool area but my friend did, and said the pool and spa were wonderful, as well as the workout room. The floor carpeting was showing wear, but it must be a busy hotel. There is no free Internet but if you buy food at Networks, we were told we'd get free connection, and there are computers in the lobby to use, 30 minutes for $5, if you must access your email. There is also a computer to use to print out airline boarding passes, a nice convenience. My main gripe with the otherwise adequate rooms was there was no mini fridge, as many hotels are adding now. There was a coffee pot and hairdryer though, both appreciated. Now to the staff: from the man who checked us in (gave us a 19th floor room!) to the engineer who fixed our shower to the desk personnel at the front desk to the wait staff in the Terrace Cafe, all were friendly, helpful and this while maintaining their nerves during a crazy sci fi convention where zombies and other costumes walked the hotel at all hours. I would stay here again if the location warranted. Thank you, Hyatt Hotels, for making our stay so nice!

“Edles Hotel” Das Millennium Biltmore Hotel in LA liegt im Geschäftszentrum von LA. Um nach Santa Monica oder Hollywood zu kommen, braucht man ein Auto, aber das braucht man sowieso in LA. Das Hotel ist sehr nobel, hier fanden früher die Oskarverleihungen statt. Die Zimmer sind teilweise etwas antik eingerichtet, aber schön. Das Frühstück war uns dort zu teuer, aber gleich unten gibt es einen Starbucks.

“Very Polite Staff But Noisy Hotel And No Late Check Out” The staff does try had and the hotel is in a very good location. However I would not stay here again. I was kept awake until 4am by the guests next door. The were not being loud or rowdy. It is just that they were awake talking in normal voices and moving around. Due to what must be very very thin walls in between rooms I could hear every word and even put in earplugs and could still hear them. I could also hear everything going on in the hallway. Due to the lack of sleep I asked for a late check out of only one hour which was denied. It was the day of New Years Eve but they had rooms left in every category on their web site. The room was tiny even for NYC but it would have been acceptable if not for the noise.

“New hotel, great rooftop restaurant, clean and comfortable rooms” Although this hotel was a little hard for our driver to find the location proved to be quiet and convienant. We travelled with our baby and asked for a crib upon arrival. The room was perfect, a little small but new and compact. The crib was there as we asked. The restaurant upstairs be came a fast favorite with views over the construction of he freedom tower. Would stay again and again

“Pretty nice stay at Midway” We had a late flight into Midway and needed a place to sleep before a day of fun in Chicago, so I booked a room through Priceline, and ended up at the Courtyard. For the price I paid, it was a great value. If I had paid full price, I might have wanted more pizazz. But the room was roomy and clean, with very nice comfortable beds and bedding. I left behind my eyeglasses, on the floor of all places, and the staff was very helpful in getting them back to me in perfect condition. No noise problem, even being close to the airport. Shuttle service from the airport was great, even with our 1 AM arrival. A number of eating options attached to the hotel, or within walking distance. Features I saw but did not use: Nice looking (smallish) indoor pool and very basic fitness room.

“Not Bad for the Money” As others have noted, the area is "colorful" - chock-a-block with street vendors during the day, and black plastic trash bags at night. However, the vendors are not insistent; a polite "no thanks" is all that's needed. These are not panhandlers! As for the hotel, the staff was very pleasant, and our room on the 11th floor was clean, quiet and boasted views from all four big windows of the Empire State Building. Quite impressive. The room furnishings were motel-standard, and the a/c worked very well. Next time I go to NYC I will probably try to find something in a sllightly more upscale environment, (maybe on a street with a couple of trees on it!), but the Broadway Plaza is a good value in my opinion.

“Fantastic” I've stayed at more expensive and fancier hotels but I never had been treated better than at the Embassy Suites Arboreum in Austin, TX. Everyone from the front desk, bartender to housekeeping was super friendly and helpful. I didn't like the firm pillows so feather pillows were brought up immediately. There was a problem with a closet door rather late in the evening but the maintenance man (nice guy with a Russian accent) came immediately and fixed it. The free reception each evening included fresh fruit, chips, salsa and a hot appetizer. The bar was not only free but included any drink you wanted. In short, everything was done just to my specifications. Of course, with Embassy Suites you usually get a nice room and free breakfast, but recently in Nashville (airport location) alcoholic drinks were not free.

“Great hotel for a park and fly package” I used their park and fly package that included 20 days of free parking. I enjoyed the free wi-fi in the room. Nice restaurant for dinner and breakfast buffet in the morning. The complimentary airport shuttle service is a great addition.

“Perfect location” We were delighted to find that the hotel we booked through Hotwire at $100 per night was the Omni Downtown. Excellent location, walking distance to 6th St, Warehouse district. Our room was huge (907), overlooking the atrium and, despite the fact that the hotel was busy with a wedding, it was really quiet. Nothing negative to say at all. Very unusual for me! We didn't eat at the hotel as we were so close to so many options but the lounge area was very pleasant and there's a sports bar too if you want to meet up before hitting the town.

“Decent value, some rooms better than others” Overall, the staff was friendly and the location to downtown was good. For the value it was okay. Unfortunately, we stayed during a convention and it seemed like everyone was showering at the same time...no hot water until mid-morning. We had a roach on our bed at one point...thankfully only the one. The doors to the back parking lot don't let you in (no handles and the card readers don't work, so naturally everyone props them open...hence bug problems). Our bed was uncomfortable and sunk inward to the middle. Although some friends of ours also stayed here and they had no problems with their room.

“Excellent in Every Respect” I'm a Sofitel frequent guest but it was my first time at this hotel. It does the Sofitel name proud. I arrived at 10 AM and was immediately given a room bigger than the one I paid for with lots of closet space and the bathroom was far from the bedroom (unlike a previous reviewer's expereince). Bed was the standard ultra comfy Sofitel bed with lovely sheets and duvets. TV had loads of channels and latest movies for a surcharge. Very fast WIFI available for a surcharge or you can use one of three Apple computers and printers in the business center off the lobby for free. Restaurant serves a great breakfast and has a veggie friendly menu. On a sunny day eating on the sidewalk is a treat. Service is exceptionally friendly and helpful. They really work as one Team to deliver service. Example, I needed help carrying my luggage down upon checkout at 11 AM and the porters were all busy helping other guests so the receptionsist came up to help me instead of making me wait. The gym is very well equipped and the location is perfect for jogging as you can run to the Lincoln Memorial and the Mall, etc. easily from the hotel. Next time I'm in DC I will stay here again for sure.

“Good Hotel, Great Location” The hotel is situated in a great location, close to many attractions without having to pay for parking. The room was clean, the staff was friendly and helpful. I didn't rate the Rooms a perfect 5 because of the old TV's, which I am sure they are in the process of upgrading. The sleep quality for me wasn't the best as the guest room doors slam shut which woke me up during the night and early morning hours. Overall I would definately recommend to others.

“Nicer than your average Marriott” This Marriott is larger than your typical Marriott with some nicer touches in the lobby and main floor areas. It doubles as a small convention space though. Very close to the mall and short walking distance to Bricktops and Paco's Tacos both of which are good. The hotel has a nice workout facility with several treadmills and a few ellipticals as well as freeweights. It also has a small outside pool. Parking is free. Would stay here again. The Wifi coverage though is not good as I only had a spotty signal in my room. It was free though.

“Exceptional service from a New York classic” Enjoyed a one night stay in June. Arrival and check in were handled very smoothly and Guest Liason was professional but down to earth. Room was as expected of a New York hotel- not big but comfortable. I do agree with other reviewers that light switches old and bathrooms typical of the classic marble type. I personally don't have a problem with these but note that newer hotels bathrooms can be more comfortable. A package arrived after I checked out and Kevin, concierge, was kind enough to contact me and offered to send it on. This kind of service from all of the staff is to be commended.

“Enjoyed my stay at The Prescott” The Price: I went on priceline to look for a hotel deal in San Francisco. I paid only $500 for 5 nights (normally goes for $200-300 per night). It was worth every penny. The Room: The Prescott has a very upscale feel. The rooms are clean, quiet, and beautiful. The bed linens are soft and mattress is very comfortable. The room itself is small, but they make good use of the space. My only complaint about the room is that the water pressure in the shower isn't great. The Staff: The hotel staff was very helpful. They had great tips... where to dine, what to see, how to get around, etc. Also, there is a private club on the 4th floor of the hotel that offers a complimentary breakfast and happy hour (full bar & appetizers). We didn't pay for the club membership, but the front desk slipped us a key pass anyhow. Location: If you want to be in Union Sq, this hotel is perfect. There is lots of shopping, restaurants, and other things to do. The Prescott is one block from the heart of Union Square. There are some homeless in the area, and a suspicious massage parlor around the corner, but overall, the neighborhood feels safe. It's close the to BART and the Powell St Trolley. It's a $7 cab ride to Fisherman's Wharf, The Ferry Building, and AT&T Park. $35 cab ride (plus tip) to the airport.

“Clean, Friendly, Pleasant” I booked this hotel at a conference rate of under $200. I wouldn't have thought of this hotel except that it was on the conference list choices and the price was great. I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms were exceptionally clean, the service was very friendly and prompt, and the Internet service is free. It's a great hotel for all the basics. There is a restaurant attached called Salmon River that offers room service. It's okay for a quick bite or drink, but New York has more to offer for food. Great location, walk to Penn Station, Grand Central, shopping galore, midtown a hop away. Also, I was put in a handicap room when I checked in. I asked for another as the sink was akward and they upgraded me to an extra large king after one night. I would recommend for no frills if you get a decent price and good for business travellers.

“Great location and friendly” Chose to stay here when visiting New York after good experience at Palomar in Los Angeles. Very friendly hotel with nice welcome and very helpful front of house staff. Super location for my business visits and also just a couple of blocks from the bus to JFK and to Grand Central Station. Free wine hour in the evening, and fresh fruit always available, plus plenty of morning papers. Nice if compact room, beautifully clean and well air conditioned and soundproofed, and good sized TV and fast Wifi as in other Kimptons. Also great minibar and snack offering. I had a great view across Park Avenue. If you arrive on a Sunday beware that the restaurant can be closed on a Sunday evening, although there are plenty of nearby places to eat. I had room service as I had arrived after a long flight and was not that impressed with a turkey breast sandwich, although the ingredients all seemed fresh. Later in the week I had an excellent dinner at the bar at the Silverleaf Tavern - the hotel's restaurant and bar - including wild mushroom risotto which was yummy - and had friendly company there too. Breakfast was OK - a bit expensive and not a very exciting range of things to chose from in the buffet - It was interesting to observe that it is clearly a destination for working breakfast meetings for nearby business people. However the staff were attentive and plenty of nice fresh coffee available, regularly refilled.

“Adequate” Booked the hotel "blind-folded" via Priceline at $130 per night plus taxes for 3 weeknights while on business in Chicago. Started with a standard room with no view, later changed to one with gorgeous view of the river, for $10 extra per night. Very much worth it. Beds are nothing special and the covers are the old kind. Although Holiday Inn prides itself on its pillow menu, I found them all to be very hard. Rooms were in average working order; had problems with the drain plugs in both rooms and had to rip them out of the sink to make it drain. First room wasn't cleaned properly; found a luggage tag right next to the desk, but didn't have a single bar of soap. Quick response from housekeeping though after I called. Front-desk staff was always helpful, and room service was on time and as expected. Large portions (breakfast at least). Wifi works well and is complimentary. Finally a downtown hotel that doesn't charge for this everyday amenity. Pool was very nice; large and deep. Just too bad parents can't control their kids these days and believe that 100 db screaming is "cute." I didn't try the exercise room, but it looked modern, spacious and well-equipped. Not the hotel's fault, but I had severe cell phone problems in both the rooms I was in: T-Mobile signal kept coming and going. Was mostly a problem on the southward facing side. Odd. Overall, I would return here if I was in a crunch or just on vacation. For business, I would prefer the Wyndham. :-)

“Mostly Good News” Stayed here one night while on a business trip - was great to be able to walk from Terminal B straight to the hotel without requiring a bus. Was even better the next morning being able to walk right to the regional septa train and get to downtown philadelphia in 25 minutes for less than 10 dollars - much cheaper than a taxi! Room was typical Marriott style and no complaints about the service. Only concern was the price - it should not cost more to stay $50+ at the airport versus the Sofitel in Center City

“Nice clean hotel, friendly staff” This is an older property but is well maintained, clean and comfortable. Hotel associates were friendly and helpful. This location (Rt 23 and I-270) is an extremely congested high traffic area and difficult to drive around during rush hour.

“It's a big, impersonal conference hotel” I've stayed here before for conferences and it was just as I remembered e.g., big, expensive and impersonal. The room was very attractive, a bit larger than many of Marriott king-sized rooms, but freezing. When I arrived the air conditioner was going full blast and the room temp was 62 degrees! Needless to say, I turned off the air conditioning unit. After a few hours, I was chilled and looked around for a blanket but there was no extra blanket in the room (several of my colleagues also remarked on the frigid temps and the lack of an extra blanket the next morning). I prefer to take a bath, but the tub drain wouldn't work, so I put up taking a shower for a few days. The continental breakfast with our meeting was ordinary and skimpy...they didn't even have any fruit, much less fresh fruit, just orange juice. The Maryland crab cake I had there was quite tasty-and full of crab meat! The location is fantastic, e.g., close to the Metro, lots of restaurants, and within easy walking distance of the National Zoo.

“No free internet!” Amazing and well preserved hotel. Rooms and public areas are well kept and of high quality. Location is a bit away from the busier areas of downtown, but still walkable to Grant Park and close to an L station. I really liked this hotel, but the major downside was that there was no free internet, not even in the lobby. This is the only reason I wouldn’t stay here again – everything else was great!

“Very pleasant stay” Stayed here in October for the Georgia-Florida game ...wireless internet was out all weekend, but that is my lone real complaint. The beds were comfy, the room was very clean and pleasant. The towels were not that great, but i mean, this is a Travelodge, not a Doubletree, so you have to be realistic. Best part was the breakfast. Very solid and above expectations. Bagels, fruit, waffles, muffins, cinnamon rolls, it was a quality spread. I'd stay here again if I was in the area for sure.

“Outstanding service & location” Selected this hotel after reading Tripadvisor reviews and I was not disappointed. At $263 (inc tax), I thought this was pricey but I liked the location. From my entrance into the hotel, I felt that the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. My room was very spacious and well appointed. I had an excellent stay and I would stay here again.

“Big and old” We reserved the Radisson at Cross Keys but had to move the Radisson Lord Baltimore downtown because a recent storm had affected the electricity in all the area. The building is old and in need of better maintenance. We stayed only one night and checked in just in time to watch the final Eurocup match on an old model TV. Our double twin beds room was big but the AC was barely enough to keep the room cool. We didn't see any breakfast service but found a cafe nearby. We had to take down our suitcases ourselves at checkout because there was only one cart and there were a line of guests waiting for the bellman. I think that a hotel of 22 floors of rooms needs more than one luggage cart. The location is in downtown, walking distance from the inner harbor. I used my points to pay part of the hotel costs, so for $46 a night I think it was a good deal.

“Average at Best” The room was spacious however needs to be updated. I have stayed at MUCH nicer Renaissance hotels - not sure why this one wasn't up to par. I was happy that they had a "real" hair dryer in the bathroom - I am not a fan of the ones attached to the walls. The Aveda hair products were also a nice touch. I had the crunchy french toast for breakfast - it arrived promptly for when I ordered it (put the order card on my door the night before) in the morning and it was quite good. Probably would try a different hotel at the Philly airport next time I stay there. Other hotels seems closer to the airport and easier to find. Though ok, this one didn't win me over.

“Great location, unacceptable service for the level of hotel” This is a hip hotel in a great location with a good restaurant. The rooms are extremely small and have a poor layout. I was here on a business trip and had no where to work beside essentially sitting in the bathroom. On that note, forget room service unless you want to eat it in your bed. My biggest issue is the service. A hotel at this price point should have flawless service all the way through from the doormen( which there was often none and the ones when there didn't want to help with bags and were noticeably irritated when they had to help get a cab) to the desk to the room service. None of these people were terrible but none seemed to be trained as to the level of a superior hotel.

“Awesome in all the right ways” Stayed for the ACTFL convention. .8 miles from the convention center so not too far away to walk. the bed was SO comfortable! rooms are spacious. Staff is friendly. lobby very comfortable. the fitness center was great, fresh oranges every day (love that!) not to mention a great view of the city from the 15th floor. wifi is $10 which i didnt like and breakfast is pricy at the restaurant but whatever. i would stay here again in a hearbeat. rate was $159 a night b/c of the convention.

“Great in many ways!” This hotel was totally comfortable, clean and accommodating. The staff couldn't be nicer! Very nice full breakfasts in the morning added to the positive atmosphere. I truly recommend this as a wonderful place to stay! I only wish all my business travel met these standards!

“An average value” My wife and I stayed at Edgewater Hotel for two nights. We chose the Edgewater because we were coming from Victoria on the Victoria Express ferry which arrives at berth 69, right next to the Edgewater at berth 67. So we wheeled our suitcases the short distance to the Edgewater. Location The hotel is not near stores or areas of interest. Probably the closest shopping area is Pike Place, about a 15-minute walk away. We soon realized the hotel was too remote for us. We had booked for Saturday through Tuesday nights, and we checked out on a Monday. They charged us half of the estimate for all four days. Sadly, if we had booked for only Saturday-Sunday (much cheaper weekend rates), then we would have wound up paying considerably less for those two days. The halls The long halls can be entered from only one side so you do a lot of walking if your room is far from the entrance. The long narrow corridors don't seem to fit with the premium rooms on the fourth floor. The halls are narrow enough so that it's difficult to navigate a suitcase past the maids' cleaning carts, and people who are sensitive to scents will feel the hall does not smell fresh. The sense of mustiness is enhanced by the hunting lodge motif and squeaking floorboards. Room We were in room 430 on the fourth floor. There is a sofa against the foot of the bed with cassock in front of it that could be used for a breakfast tray. There is an enormous plasma TV screen can be watched from the bed or sofa. In one corner a gas fireplace goes on if temperature controls changed suddenly from cold to hot. Good bathrobes, umbrella in closet. The bed is comfortable and inviting with lots of cushions and a little stuffed bear that we named "Ed" wearing the Edgewater T-shirt, propped against the pillows. The posts of the four poster bed are made of raw timber, probably for effect. There is a writing desk by the bed, and the floor is carpeted. There are more than enough electric plug outlets. We liked the location of the air conditioner/heater. It didn't blow on the bed or sofa. Good selection of teas with the tea and coffee maker. The refrigerator had a freezer compartment, so we could freeze our ice pack. Bathroom The wide bathroom with entry way takes up a quarter of the room-bathroom area. There is a stand-up shower. There is no more than one double hook to hang towels, bathrobes, etc., so we wound up putting them on back of the toilet even though hooks could have been installed in many places on the wall. View The view from the rooms on the fourth floor (see photo) is similar to that from Six Seven Restaurant, but the view is broader, including a view on clear days of Mt. Ranier hiding behind the red fingers of a container port crane. A porch runs the full length of the room with access through two sliding doors. We were in room 430, close to the Norwegian Cruise Line berth. NCL passengers could look down on our porch, taking away some privacy, but the cruise ships made a pretty view for us, and we missed them when there was no ship in the berth. The view from the fourth floor may be good for Seattle, but it is no match for the view at, say, the Pan Pacific Vancouver. Quiet enjoyment We could hear the couple in the room next to us banging suitcases around on Sunday morning, and about an hour later in the same room there was such a lot of commotion that I went into the hall to find the source, and I found it was the housekeeping lady. I have no idea what she was doing. There is a function room on the 4th floor by the elevators, and the decibels get pretty high during receptions. It’s best to avoid room 484. It is the guest room nearest to the fourth floor function room. They have a heavy door that can be closed against the pandemonium when guests are trying to sleep night. Service Service at check-in, check-out, housekeeping, and concierge was polite and efficient but not exceptional. Restaurants The restaurant Six Seven is so outstanding that we ate there twice. They provide half-plates, so instead of sharing, I had a halibut, and my wife had pork loin. Both were excellent. The desserts were tasty with distinguished presentations. I had a panna cotta with blueberry topping, and my wife had a lavender honey creme brulee with a glass of Red Mountain Kiona ice wine. It was an extraordinarily satisfying meal. We recommend Six Seven Restaurant whether you stay at the Edgewater or not. We had breakfast in the room, and the food was very good and delivered promptly. We ate in the room rather than on the porch under the gaze of cruise ship passengers. Internet Edgewater's unique Internet policy seems a bit grasping. If you want wi-fi (no LAN), you pay an additional $4 an hour, $10 a day, or $25 for three days which is annoying. If you are using two devices, such as a computer and a smart phone, the charge is doubled, and if you use three devices, the charge is tripled, which is annoying to the power of three. We were charged for using two devices in one day. We felt the hotel was good for a day, considering its view and location near the Victoria Clipper and cruise lines, but we prefer to be in the middle of shops and restaurants, and we felt a wee bit ravaged paying for Internet access on a per-device basis. We moved to the more central Pan Pacific Seattle Hotel where LAN and wi-fi are free for all guests. The hotel offers a lot, but the pluses and minuses divided by the price would yield an average value.

“Very disappointed, won't return” I stayed here with my family several years ago and loved it...a spacious room in a lovely part of town with a great (hamburger) restaurant (Rare Grill) downstairs and a rooftop bar. This time was a disaster...they have recently renovated so the rooms are nice but now more typical NYC small. The rate that was advertised on the website (grand opening) was completely not true--we did not get upgraded, we did not get coupons for hamburgers at Rare (although I asked repeatedly during my three night stay), the bell men just watched as we struggled with our bags, and the manager was no where to be found. We also were charged a much higher rate which it took a couple of days and several emails with the manager to correct--he should have given me a free night, but...this is the state of customer service. Sad to say, never again, in fact, I will now avoid all Affinia and go back to the Kimpton and Starwood properties. Too bad, it is a great location. (But there's a Kimpton, Muse I think, and a W nearby). The restaurant, Rare, is still good with great service.

“Above Average, Great Location” Stayed here for 3 nights on business. I did not choose the hotel, and likely wouldn't have simply because while I love the neighborhood, the Hilton where I have points is right across the street.
