That being said, I was pleasantly surprised with how enjoyable my stay was. The exterior and lobby harken back a few decades and seem somewhat dated. My room had been recently renovated and was spotless with nice furnishings, including a couch and coffee table. Only problem is that with the new multimedia panel built into the dresser under the 40" HDTV, there is very little in the way of drawer storage. I had to use the drawers in the two night stands - something I've never had to do before. As I'd read other reviews that indicated noise was an issue (I had absoluetly no problems during my stay), I found it interesting that the bathroom amenities included a pair of ear plugs! Staff were friendly and helpful. I found the breakfast buffet to be over-priced for what it was - even in SF - but the coffee was delicious and the service outstanding. Best part about this hotel is the location. Assuming you want to be in the Union Square area, it can't be beat for convenience to all transportation and shopping.

“Inn at the Market--superb location, feiendly service” Husband and i treated ourselves to a three-day Seattle blowout with a townhouse waterview suite at inn at the Market. Our first room wasn't so good--room 502 overlooks the vents from the restaurant on the ground floor, with the associated grease odors and loud noises, and the sharp wire struck around the borders of the wall to keep the birds from landing on the building, along with some scraggly-looking potted arborvitae on the deck. So I asked to be moved to another room, which the staff gladly accommodated the next morning. Room 602 and the upstairs bedroom is a lot nicer, with good reading lamps, good water pressure cleaner white wall-to-wall carpeting(why anyone would furnish any living space, especially hotel rooms,with white carpeting is beyond me). Stairs are steep and take concentration to negotiate--they do have a rail on one side of the wall. It is inconvenient to have a bathroom only on the top floor, and my husband fell down the stairs while schlepping stuff down, but didn't hurt himself much.--We decided the 5th floor unit would be a lot more usable if it were divided into two smaller rooms,one upstairs, with a commanding view of the sound, and one downstairs, with a little kitchenette(and a bathroom add-on, or even in the hall), for a lesser rent. The doors that appear to divide these units are obviously old hotel doors, so they must have been separate soemtime in the past. The 5th-6th floor suite also needs some fairly easy-to-do fixing--three-way lightbulbs that work, lampshade screw-on tops, water-pressure increase, carpet cleaning. The pluses are many--lovely room service from Cafe Campagne(bit cheesy),Marche, and Basso(delicious fruit smoothies), great water pressure in the 6th floor room, super comfortable bed with nice linens, fantastic location, right on top of Pike Street Market, windows that open, quiet hotel, pleasant staff. Inn of the Market is nice--just keep in mind that fifth-sixth floor townhouse waterfront suite really isn't waterfront on the living room floor, more back-side of deck, and cooking vent view.

“zentrale Lage, preiswert. Sauber” Liegt nicht "direkt" am Times Square, wie der Name vielleicht vermuten läßt - in 10 min ist man aber zu Fuß dort. U-Bahnstation nahe gelegen; verschiedene kleine Restaurants in der Umgebung. Check-in war professionell und problemlos. Während meines 5tägigen Aufenthaltes mußte ich nur ein einziges Mal länger auf den Aufzug warten. Von meinem Zimmer im 31. Stock hatte ich einen guten Blick - auch auf den Hudson River! Das Zimmer war sauber; super bequeme Betten. Kostenloses WLAN. Das Frühstück war in der Rate eingeschlossen: ausgezeichneter Kaffee, ansonsten amerikanischer Standard in dieser Preisklasse. Hätte keine Bedenken, dort wieder zu buchen.

“Large room and great location!” We had 3 people on our group attending a conference at Easton. The hotel was having their grand opening with an Ohio State theme (players in attendance and media) with free snacks and wine! We had no problem checking in and we had a suite with two queen beds and a pull out sofa bed. The room was bigger than the Hilton at Easton we had the last time we attended the conference. Rooms had a modern flair with the sink area outside the shower area. We also had a fridge. The breakfast was average. The location is just across Morse across from Easton (north of Easton).

“Yech!” Supposedly an airport hotel, but it is the next (sketchy) exit down. Hotel is hidden behind Shoneys and is NOT what you expect to see when you see this hotel chain. This hotel is very old and gives you the creeps. Front desk staff was very nice and aimed to please, but room is gross. Pink something stains on walls, carpet has mysterious stains, tile floor in bathroom was dirty, dust on baseboards was gross. The beds were in good condition and were the best part of the hotel. TV was small and very old. Fitness room treadmill is a lawsuit waiting to happen. One time, it speeded up so fast, that it almost threw me off. Then I turned it off and tried it again and after another few minutes, the belt slipped and I grabbed the handles to keep from falling. TV in the fitness room had no remote. Asked for one and was told that there wasn't one, just reach under the bottom of the tv to make it work...The breakfast room is large and clean, but all the food was cold. There is a sign on the areas where hot food is supposed to be served that says "hot food coming January 2012" Final note, if you don't get one of the 10 or 12 parking spots in the front of the hotel, park at Shoneys is better than parking in the scary back of the hotel.

“Decent big hotel with some rough spots” Came to this Sheraton for work. Generally, this property performed well. But there were a few things that just rubbed me the wrong way. First - the positives: the staff were very friendly and helpful. The bed was comfortable and the TV worked. The room was clean and there was plenty of counter space in the bathroom. On the other hand, the bathtub was very slow draining and the "sleep" function on the remote did not work. There were only two lamps in the room so a floor lamp by the easy chair would help. My biggest problem was with the 4 packages that had been sent to me for our training classes. When I went to the business center to get them, the "handling" charge for them was more than $60! And they weren't even very big boxes! Most hotels that I've dealt with would not charge for boxes that small. Our event was held in their Majestic conference rooms on the 37th floor. The physical layout of the area was excellent with lovely views of downtown Dallas. One problem was that the first morning the air on the floor was very stuffy. It felt like the a/c had been turned off overnight. Walking in first thing in the morning, it felt a bit like walking into a Singapore street market - stuffy and odors coming from the breakfast that they were setting up. We had problems all day long with the WiFi. It would randomly cut in and out and was a burden on our facilitators. The food for the event was imaginative and decently prepared. I was not prepared to see the coffee cup at my place as well as the one next to me both with lipstick stains. The location of the hotel is a bit out of the main stream. It is a 4 or 5 block walk to areas with restaurants. The DART light rail trains do stop right outside the hotel, so if you are into public transportation, you are in luck. So the Sheraton has its ups and downs in my opinion. I wouldn't avoid it were I to return but it wouldn't be my first choice either.

“Really nice luxury retreat in NY” Where to start... I'm here for business which usually means a long boring trip without the mrs. spending most my time in the room. So what I want is a large room, nice luxury and a place to separate work and bedtime. Well you're not going to get that in most NY hotel rooms... Generally small and hominess... Enter the Hyatt 48 Lex. Probably not the cheapest hotel room but like I said its for biz and I'm a platinum. At first, the booked terrace room wasn't available so I got a regular room much smaller and w/out a balcony. So the review really is about the corner suite w the balcony... I'm not entirely happy about the downgrade at first but the regular room is really nicely laid out and well furnished... Didn't bother me for long. Pros: Huge room separate living, bath, 'kitchen', wrap around balcony, and bed. Modern but elegant finishes... Dark woods, sleek steel, nicely done... Great standup shower w tiles...Typical Hyatt in my experience so far... Two 37/42" flat screens Great customer service... Clean rooms, helpful concierge, available lounge area in lieu of lobby... Everyone is Super helpful and always has a smile... Clean and updated room, from wooden furniture to drapes to tvs and amenity kits Turndown service w chocolates Lex lounge offers fruits, coffee, tea, in addition to some pastries in the morning and cheese at night, free PC/biz center on a working Mac with printer... Nice "free" space for all Free Internet for plats otherwise is 15/day w ability to swap device, only one per room at rate. Although I didnt use... Small out of the way fridge, dish washer, minibar, wine bar, yes in room wine selection...and second 'kitchen' sink Cons; Prob due to the only two elevators the wait can be kinda slow since it services the entire bldg plus cleaning crew during peak hours Location is a bit far east for my liking, but it's not awful... Waldorf and Interconnential is nearby, so you'd have to say the same about them... Doors are heavy but the sound is kinda bad... Try not to stay near elevator or exit doors, but oddly enough it seems like this hotel is quiet as a mouse after 10... Dif type crowd id say... Fairly priced, a bit higher than mid tier but worth it. 10/15 min to central park, 5/7 min from fifth ave Would definitely stay again, lex brass restaurant was quite good, you could do a lot worse for hotel restaurant... Didn't mind eating here at all. Wait staff seem really friendly.

“Good resort feel with limited food options” This property is awesome. Friendly check in and personal escort to our room. Room's patio walked out to the golf course which was just too cool. Huge hd tv, spacious room, two chairs, and plenty of room for activities. Aveda bath products are always nice. This was one of the best rooms I have ever seen. Staying here 4 nights was way too much because of the limited food options. There is really only one bar that serves substandard cuisine and some I the restaurant menu. We came in expecting several distinguished dining options but it all was blah. We were forced to sculp out the surrounding area instead of doing the true "resort" thing by not leaving. For over $600 in breakfast lunch dinner for 2, we left feeling like the food was a ripoff and trust me it was all average. You know the feel when one chef cooks for several menus. Even room service served the same menu options! However, room service was a life saver as it rained all day Sunday. Food was delivered perfectly each time, props to their staff for this! How you deliver cold salads, hot food and appropriate condiments every time AND in the rain is astonishing.

“Great deal, great location and good hotel” Stayed at this hotel on a Saturday night. Arrived at about 11am and the hotel had a room ready for me to check in. Overall the hotel had a few kinks but I would still recommend it. The hotel is huge and it faces Market Street which is one of the main thoroughfares downtown. Took advantage of the valet service. Was about $35 for the night and you can keep it with the valet until the evening of the day you are checking out. The room I got was a corner room on an upper floor. Two double beds, huge flat screen TV, desk, chair, table and bathroom. The hotel charges extra for internet service. Was at a Courtyard by Marriott in Boston the week before and high speed internet was included. I paid the $12 they require for 24 hours of service however the service was beyond slow so I upgraded to the high speed service which was only a couple dollars more. That service was horrendous too. The room smelled of cigarettes even though smoking is not allowed in the hotel. I told the front desk and they offered to change my room but I had already settled so I declined. They did send someone up to deal with the smell. Didn’t help that much. The TV is great however sometimes it wouldn’t turn on or it would randomly turn off. Seemed to be a problem with the cable maybe or the picture tube in the TV - no idea. The location is in the heart of downtown - steps away from City Hall. The hotel is also a short walk from shopping at Rittenhouse Square, the historic district, and all of the city's museums. I walked everyone. Perfect location. Only downside to the location and this has nothing to do with the hotel itself and more to do with Philadelphia - Center City has a lot of homeless people. At times they can be everywhere. They seemed to be centered in Center City. I live in NYC and have to say we have nowhere near as many homeless people. Just be careful of your surroundings. I did speak with the hotel and they didn’t charge me for the internet service which I had problems with. I would recommend the hotel though I got a deal on Priceline which helped.

“It's OK for the center of New York” I was originally booked here by a client for an event, then stayed an extra night for business. The rooms are a good size for the center of a major city, but dark and with the usual limited lighting so common in US hotels. I've always thought they cut back on lighting bedrooms to pay for the ice vending machine that rattles on through the day and night on every floor. The only real irritation was the location of the coffee machine, safe and mini bar. They couldnt have picked a darker corner just by the door without any lighting. Mr grumpy the bell boy seemed not to like helping out guests. I asked which was the direction to Times Square. Shortly after I overheard him saying to a colleague "Is it my job to give directions". No not if you don't want buddy. And you don't have to work there either. New Yorkers can be the most miserable, possibly the worst city in the US for service, yet the expect some of the highest tips! The lack of breakfast facilities for such a large hotel is consistent with the "eat and walk" culture, so I did...and breakfast elsewhere. The only real screw up was my laundry. To be told I hadn't called it in so it missed the 9am same day service as a little irritating. I know how it works, I stay in enough hotels every year, and that morning I called it in at 7am. Still they didnt charge me for the overnight express service, so the Starwood chain keeps my vote and my business. Is it expensive? At $310 per night without taxes...most certainly but this is New York, and it is in a great location.

“Cool hotel but doesn't quite hit it” I was booked here by someone else and the reviews I read talked about how it was hipper, cooler and generally just better than the W in Seattle. I haven't been to the W in Seattle, but I've been to plenty of them in other cities and I don't think I would put the Hotel Andra in the same category. It's fashionable but it's more trying than executing on the urban chic measure. The location is pretty good - just a short distance to all the fun in Pike's Place, shopping on Fifth Ave, and tourist entertainment near the Space Needle. It's also right on the edge of some dodgy blocks and alleys too - I had the opportunity to breath in urine, pot, BO and garbage on the several short walks I made to the nearby attractions. My room was spacious, modern, clean and comfortable. The hotel is about 9 stories high (the exterior, by the way, is nothing special) and many of the rooms are on the busy streets, but the city traffic noise is muffled. The king bed was great and there was a small fridge and sink as well as an office desk space and small couch with coffee table. If you like a bathtub, you don't get one. Also, there's no shower door or curtain, just a partial glass covering, which I think is chilly! The bathroom generally was small and the lighting on the moody side - flattering, but difficult for applying makeup. I'd say the room is nice, the bathroom just average. The Lola restaurant in the lobby serves up great Mediterranean food and you can get it to go for your room if you like. I give the 4 rating because I didn't think it quite hit the mark on the hipness, location is good but near some seedy stuff and the bathroom was average. A few other things that make it fall a little short - the service is funny (there's plenty of help but they don't necessarily get the door or offer to deliver your luggage) and the details were missed (eg my ironing board legs were smashed and broken; my toiletries and coffee supplies weren't refilled; I had to call at 2pm to get my room cleaned). These things said, the room was very clean, modern and comfortable and the location is handy.

“Nice stay -” I grew up in LA and since the Bonaventure opened, I always wanted to stay here. Decided to spend a day or two in LA on my way back to SF from San Diego. Now that the 70's vibe is back in vogue, the place is more fabulous than when it was first built. We were able to check-in a few hours early and were given a renovated room on the 31st floor with a sweeping view of Hollywood and the famous Hollywood sign in the distance. The room, though a little small was well-appointed, comfortable, and quiet. Spent the afternoon at the pool, which was a perfect place to relax and nap in the glow of the LA sun before it went behind one of the nearby buildings. I highly recommend this property. While the signage is not very clear for those driving up and wish to park their car, I'd still stay here again. The rooftop rotating bar is FAB straight out of 1978 - but with 2010 prices. $31 for to two cosmos. OUCH!

“Nice week at the W Dallas” I stayed at the W this spring for one week while on a business trip to Dallas. The hotel is very new and modern and the rooms were well appointed. My room, perhaps a Wonderful?? had a modern bathroom with a walk-in rain shower. The room service was great, and there was fully-stocked mini-bar in the room. All-in-all it was a great place to spend a week in Dallas on business.

“Good Experience at Large Hotel” Very nice property centrally located, adjacent to Oriole Park at Camden Yards and the convention center. Only a block from Camden Station (commuter train station) and a Light Rail stop. Service is inconsistent, ranging from indifferent to good. Has a very large fitness center. Rooms are decent size and still showing the relative newness of the hotel. Self parking is available in hotel garage, but payment is seperate (not charged to room) which is unusual and inconvenient. NOTE: Many rooms face into Oriole Park at Camden Yards, which is interesting even if there isn’t a game and affords a view, albeit from a distant vantage point, of the game. However, note that the ballpark lights will be on until an hour or so after game time and this additional lighting may be bothersome to some trying to sleep.

“Good choice...if you get a good rate” I just returned from a 2 night stay at the London. I had stayed at the property several times when it was the Righa, so I was well aware of the hotel's terrific location. As for the hotel, the preceeding reviews seem accurate. There are very attractive common areas and the service seemed consistently good. The rooms are spacious and very nicely appointed, especially if you like contemporary decor. That said, our rate was over $600/night and the place is not worthy of that rate. If you can get an attractive rate, you won't be disappointed. Its a 4 star property in my view, so the nightly tariff should reflect that. A couple final pros/cons: The fitness center is superb - one of the best I've seen at a non-spa hotel. The restaurant (Gordon Ramsey's) is flawed and very expensive. I won't go into details, but NYC has far too many great restaurants, especially for the price. Settle for drinks in the bar and go somewhere else.

“Capital Hilton is the perfect DC location!” I stay at this property on a regular basis. It is in a great location, the service is excellent and rates are competitive to other corporate full service hotels in the area. I often arrive late, so 24 hour room service is important to me. The guest rooms can be small but the hotel updates the soft goods on a regular schedule.

“Perfect location for Smithsonian and Capitol” Perfect downtown location on the edge of a gorgeous residential neighborhood. One block from the Capitol South blue line, easy access to anywhere. The staff was always courteous and the room was quiet and clean. Continental breakfast is somewhat weak; however, there is a Starbucks on the other side of the block if seeking out a stronger coffee, etc. I would stay here again.

“One of my favorite Hiltons” I stayed at this hotel for the first time for one night recently and it surpassed my expectations. I used to live in Philadelphia, and I had a business meeting at this hotel, so I stayed there for that purpose. I was a little disappointed not to be in Center City, but that changed when I checked in. The hotel is very nice and has some real university charm. It's also connected to the Penn bookstore, which has a Starbucks inside, so I was happy about that. The front desk staff is extremely welcoming and helpful. When my room key did not work upon my first attempt, I went back down and they fixed it for me. They told me that if it happened again there was a house phone on the floor I could use so I wouldn't have to walk all the way back down again. Not to worry, the key worked fine on my next try. The king room was comfortable. The bathroom was clean and spacious. The Evolve power system is a bit annoying. Because I traveled alone and for only one night, I only got one room key. I should've gotten 2. You need to put a key in the Evolve receptacle to have electricity in your room. It was close to 100 degrees outside & every time I left the room, the A/C turned off. It was kind of annoying. I could've remedied this by getting 2 keys & leaving one in the room. I know that defeats the purpose, but it was hot outside!! The other neat thing in this hotel is the room iPad, which provides free wifi. I ordered room service for dinner, and I did so very easily using the ipad. It had pictures of the food & even tallied up my total for me before I ordered. It also gave me an estimated time for delivery. The food and service were excellent. Bottom line, if you need to stay near Penn, choose this hotel. It's really top notch.

“A high 3... a 3.8” First the pros: (a) brand new, (b) free guest laundry, (c) good sized rooms that come equipped with a full sized refrigerator, stove, microwave, plates, glasses, and utensils, (d) free WiFi, (e) LCD TV with over 200 channels (many in HD), (f) friendly staff, and (g) free breakfast. Cons: (a) quality of food on offer for breakfast was so so... I still can't get over the horrid scrambled eggs - I found the eggs such a turn-off that I ate breakfast in area diners for the remainder of my stay, (b) food choices in the breakfast buffet were likewise fairly limited, (c) breakfast room was small, so small that it gets very crowded during breakfast, (d) the hallways are narrow, (e) only three washers and dryers in the guest laundry, it was not an issue for me but I can imagine that as the hotel fills up with longer staying guests, it may become very hard to come by an unused washer or dryer, (f) housekeeping, cleaning standards seemed to vary from day to day, and (g) location, right beside port authority on a not very nice side street. Not to say that the area isn't safe because it is but aesthetics wise it could be better. A word about the rooms, I booked a high room with a NYC view and got one on the 13th floor facing the hotel on 39th. Bit disappointed there. At least there was sufficient separation between the two buildings to allow sunlight in. My room was located right beside two elevators but I didn't hear any elevator noise. Amazed (and thankful) for that! Design wise the rooms were functional but not very stylish or cutting edge. A bit more pizazz would have been nice. Overall, Staybridge Times Square offers very good value for the USD250-300 per night price range I paid. Shorter staying guests would probably have less use for the in-room kitchen or the guest laundry but it's nice to know the're there just in case one needs it.

“Excellent Accomodations and Location” What a great hotel! The rooms are huge - excellent for families, or if on business/getaway a great amount of living area. Everything is in walking distance including restaurants, grocery, water taxi, inner harbor, etc. Flat screen tvs in both the living room and the bedroom. Great service and check-in. I would definitely recommend this to others and plan on staying here again. This stay validated my commitment to the Hilton chain. They have really spruced up the inner harbor since I was here last - I would consider coming up just to do a fun weekend with family or significant other.

“Overall a Satisfactory Stay” Stayed at the Mariott Del Mar for three nights while in town for sightseeing and visiting family. Found it to be very nice for the price I paid (booked through the Mariott website). A little off the beaten path for tourist activities and mostly geared to business travel, but a very well maintaied property, attentive staff and very comfy beds (especially the comforters). Only problem was a forgotten room service coffee order one morning.

“Tolles schickes Hotel im Yachthafen” Sehr schönes überdurchschnittliches Best Western! Es ist zwar leider auf dieser "Insel" ein bisschen "abgelegen".. und ein Supermarkt o.ä. ist nur mit Auto zu erreichen, aber ansonsten ist es traumhaft, schöner Pool, superedle Lage, schöne Zimmer. Direkt vor den ankernden Schiffen gibt es auch so Art Grillplätze. Haben wir zwar nicht genutzt, aber wer das mag, kann dort auch ganz romantisch und erlaubt grillen und den Sonnenuntergang geniessen ;o)) Preise variieren auch ein wenig. Wir hatten einen Superpreis für nur 130 USD inkl. Tac..beim derzeitigen Kurs unter 100 Euro.... also absolut zu empfehlen!

“Just off MI Ave and on the Lake” Swissotel Chicago is on the corner of the river and lake, just about 2 blocks off Michigan Ave. Be prepared for slightly uphill walk if you are shopping MI Ave. That is the only downside to the location, but you may enjoy the access south to Millenium Park. The Chicago bus does come in front and along with El (rail) very easy to use. Rooms were good, nothing spectacular about them except the views. The building is tirangular shaped, and we could see Millenium Park. Bath is roomy with separate shower. Single sink and tub were nice also. Room included desk & chair along with casual chair & ottoman. Overall good but not great 4* hotel. The rate we received on travelzoo special $159/nt for labor day weekend was ok. If you want to be in the middle on MI ave shopping, this is not the best location, but a nicer hotel at decent rate (less than $200) this is a good choice.

“Superb downtown hotel” What a wonderful hotel. When I checked in, I was told there was no longer a regular room with one king size bed, I was then upgraded to a deluxe! The room was superb, it was huge, clean, comfortable. Location is perfect it's near everything. The trolley is one block away, Gaslamp District, and the Harbor are close by, Balboa Park isn't far. Staff extremely friendly. An excellent choice.

“Best Addition to Baltimore's Lineup of Hotels!!” My parents and I decided to take a weekend getaway to Baltimore at the last minute. We always stay with Hilton Family hotels as we are HHonors members. Many of the hotels were booked solid for the date we were to stay (8/23/08). However, I was reading about a new Hilton that was to be opened in Fall 2008, and decided to check it out. It turns out the hotel had it's grand opening the day before we stayed!! They had an incredible discounted special rate as part of the celebration, so we took advantage. This hotel is very conveniently located to Inner Harbor, and is directly across the street from Oriole Park at Camden Yards. This makes the hotel THE ideal place for baseball fans to stay. The lobby is rather simple in design, but features contemporary furnishings and art which add a hint of elegance. The staff were very friendly, and always eager to help with any concerns we had. The room decor is basically cued to the lobby in terms of the furnishings and decor, with exclusive Hilton Serenity bedding and toiletries. The lamps and furniture in the rooms help to create a futuristic, but laid back, atmosphere. The bathrooms are very large, and each room features a large flat-panel HDTV. Of course, since this was the hotel's second day of business, the room smelled fresh and brand new. There is a small bar in the lobby which provides a great selection of beers and cocktails; perfect for unwinding after a day of sightseeing. The hotel is connected via skywalk to the Baltimore Convention Center, which provides ease of access for those attending conventions. Inner Harbor is about 3 blocks down from the hotel, and so it is within easy walking distance. Overall, this has to be the best hotel in Baltimore. The service and accomodations are top-notch, and the location cannot be beat. Thank you Hilton for providing a great new hotel in Baltimore!!

“Reception staff... What a Joke” I stayed at this hotel for 4 Nights in March. Got to the reception only to find out we had only been booked for one night. The man said he would look into this and call us tomorrow. Got to our first room 1205.. the phone rang.. they wanted us to move rooms as this one was getting re decorated!!! Got to the second room to find only one of the beds have been made. Called room service they wanted us to move rooms AGAIN. We said no and just wanted the bed made. The lady was really nice and said she didnt think anyone would be checking into this room. The second day we came back from a day out and couldnt get into our room, we went to reception who said they only has us booked in for 3 nights. This made no sense... why couldnt we get into our room? We never had a call from the man who checked us in. We spoke to the manager who didnt even apologise until we asked her to. We showed her the proof we were booked in for 4 nights and still she didn not believe us. After a long argument she offered is free breakfast for our stay. We then got a phone call the next day to say we were booked in for 4 Nights. The staff were very unproffesional and not very happy to sort this matter out for us. We booked the hotel through get a room.com I will not be booking through them or staying at this hotel again!! Apart from the reception staff the hotel is in a good location in Times Square. The breakfast is lovely but expensive if you were to pay for it. Rooms The rooms are a good size for New York rooms. However the walls are really thin and you can hear everything that is going on next door and in the hall. I have also stayed at the Millennium Broadway which I found a much better hotel overall.

“This is not a traditional Embassy Suites, I would avoid it” The rooms are big , however dated. Not what we think of when we think of an Embassy Suites. This is more like an old Double Tree. There is no court yard, they are under staffed. Took 30 minutes to get our car from the valet and the cost is $38. Line for breakfast was an hour long and it is in a TGI Fridays, again not what you would expect. The elevators are slow, managers reception area was cramped and the a/c wasn't working. Asked the service desk for a resturant suggestion and they suggested a food court across the street and walked away from us. My wife and I looked at each other in disbelief. We have stayed at embassy suites in at least 15 locations and have never experienced such disappoint.
“ゆったりとしたソファ” 部屋にはソファが3人掛け1つ、1人掛け1つ、そしてカウチ付きが1つあり とてもゆったりとできるスペースです。 ベットも大人3人が悠々眠れるほどの広さでした。 また朝食も吹き抜けで欧州貴族の宮殿を思わせるような素晴らしいところで 思わず映画の中にいるような感じでした。

“Excellent” We stayed over a long weekend and got a very good rate on a corner room overlooking the river. Two rooms, a large bathroom and another toilet with washbasin; the facilities were excellent for the price. The restaurant overlooking the river has a very good view and a substantial and varied good quality buffet for breakfast. The dinner was fine but not the best food I have ever eaten. All the staff we met were friendly and very helpful. We both liked the ambience of the hotel and would stay again if visiting Chicago in the future.

“It's all good!” We only stayed one night and found it to be very good. The receptionist was helpful. At the rear of the hotel there is an outdoor eating area with several different restaurants. We had dinner at the Dubliner which was at best, very ordinary. The location was good for walking to ground zero and the stock exchange. The receptionist arranged for a fixed price taxi to take us to the airport. We were lucky with our visit to New York to find this hotel and the Herald Square through trip advisor.

“Good enough” We stayed at this hotel over Christmas, Dec 24-27. We got a cozy room on the 5th floor, which is very small - not unusual for New York. No coffee maker in the room. View is of the furnace and another building. Bed is very comfortable. Room is clean and modern. They gave us free internet. Nice lobby and lounge. Expect to pay for coffee and hot water. Location is good - near a subway station and walking distance to 5th Avenue, Rockefeller Center, etc. After checking out I used their Acura service to get to Penn Station - nice service but I recommend reserving the day before as it fills up quickly. All in all, the hotel was good enough for the price paid but I wouldn't pay full price for that room.

“Fantastic Hotel in Millennium Park and the Loop area” I am so glad that Carlson group decided to opened up its first Radisson Blu property in the US and they picked Chicago. The hotel's wave-like structure is second to none, quite impressive the first time I laid eyes on it. The sleek and modern interior design distinguishes itself from the pack of upscale hotels in Chicago. I stayed in the Park Suite for one night before Thanksgiving day, overlooking the Millennium Park on a brisk sunny fall afternoon, and I thought, "It doesn't get better than this for spending a November day in Chi-town". The bright colors in the room and light wood floor complement each other. There is a Nespresso machine in the room which I fell in love with saved me from walking to the Starbucks across the street at the Aon Center. The service was phenomenal but I did not try the restaurant that night. Keep up the good work, I would not be surprised if this hotel made it to the top 10 list in Tripadvisor for Chicago hotels in the first quarter of 2012.

“Rooms are renovated, service remains terrific” The rooms have a fresh coat of paint. There is some new art on the walls and you walk on pristine carpets. This is a nice thing. The views are still terrific, with high views of city and sound. The service at this hotel remains one of it's strongest attributes. The people are friendly, quick to help and easy to be around. Ideal conditions for a good stay. It's a relative value given the quality of the stay and the location.

“Great Deal for NYC” Nice hotel for a reasonable New York City price. Clean rooms, friendly staff, good continental breakfast (muffins, cereals, yogurt, etc.). Rooms are TINY...so be forewarned. A double room is nothing more than a double bed with little extra room at all - we couldn't even open our bathroom door all the way w/o hitting the bed! (Bathroom is very small, as well - no tub, just a shower.) BUT...excellent location, great pizza just a few doors down. Surrounded by Irish pubs & bars, within walking distance of all NYC tourist spots. Definitely check out the view from the rooftop terrace. It makes the stay worthwhile!!

“Great value for its class in Boston” This has been my third stay at this Hotel and the location,fitness and indoor pool make it a great choice.The club rooms on the high floors with its own express lifts are quite with spectacular views of Boston and the club lounge is very adequate. I was upgraded to a suite as a spg platinum member and was given complimentary high speed internet which was great. The bed very comfortable and for a great suite with a view ask for 2722

“Best hotel in our 5 day, 5 city trip” While we only stayed here one night, it was the best value of all the cities we visited... NYC, Washington, Chicago, Seattle & LA. The front desk and all the staff we met were both friendly, helpful and efficient. The rooms were modern, nice sized and very comfortable. Flat screen TV (but mostly all analog channels). It was great to walk outside and have great restaurants all within a 4 - 5 block radius.

“Consistent Marriott which we love!” We are avid Marriott loyal fans. So this place was of course to our liking. Very nice room and great location! Would stay here again!! We walked to an awesome awesome steak house. Our waiter had worked there for twenty years!! Very clean place and easy to get in and out even in car.

“Posh public spaces - puny rooms” Even though we could barely move around in our private space, we enjoyed our one night stay. Our room was ready on check-in, a bit early. The service from the front desk, to the bar, to the restaurant was very good. The public spaces in this historic hotel are beautifully restored and a pleasure to enjoy. The Boston Cream Pie and the Parker House rolls lived up to the hype. The location is perfect for business or tourist - easy to get anywhere.

“Good for overnight for an early flight!” We booked this hotel as we had an early flight to catch & we are priority club members. As a platinum member we are meant to be upgraded. upon check in we were greeted with an unfriendly male who would not even make eye contact with us & said the hotel did not upgrade & then when we asked for details about transfers to the airport we got one worded answers. When we checked out another male staff member on front desk only mumbled when we asked about a receipt & he said no to us!!! Funny we are now at the Holiday Inn in Washington & got an upgrade no questions asked & a heck of a lot more courteous & helpful!!

“Nice hotel, but facilities not up to Kimpton Standards” The location off Union Square is very convenient for leisure or business travelers in San Francisco. The staff was friendly and helpful. Despite an oversold situation, I was able to get early check-in following a very early morning flight from the East Coast, which was very helpful. I didn't partake, but there was a nice happy hour off the lobby with very inviting staff. The room was good - decent size, clean and reasonably well appointed, but the design standard wasn't up to the level I've seen in other Kimpton hotels. The bathroom was very small (couldn't get into the tub without closing the bathroom door first), and while it had possibly newer granite counters, the shower was old and very basic. The carpeting was on the older side and not flat on the floor in some places. I suspect they bought this hotel and haven't renovated given how much more modern and over the top other Kimpton's I've stayed in were. Pretty good value, but not a wow experience.

“Pleased with my stay” I stayed there during Labor Day weekend. Unfortunately the room wasn't ready when I got there at around 5 PM. Besides that, the location was great and pretty quiet. There was a subway station about 2 blocks away for the 7 line. I didn't find that one until after I had got off at Grand Central Station. Room was clean and nicely appointed. Only negative to the hotel was that the walls are thin and you can hear your neighbors.

“Beautiful Hotel, amazing bathroom” We stayed at the Fairmont Olympic for New Years, the room was beautiful and comfortable. I especially liked the vanity area, it was a perfect spot for getting ready without getting in each other's way. Ordered room service and our server was SO nice but the food could have been a little more fresh. Overall it was an elegant hotel, but not my all time favorite.

“Great hotel for an SF stay” Spent two nights here over July 4th break. It was a great location - perfect spot in Nob Hill to connect to the wharf, union square or elsewhere. Would be good for business or vacationers. Room was clean, comfortable, and well appointed. We had an excellent east side view across downtown to the bay. Service was responsive and helpful arranging us a great early am town car to the airport. On east or north side of hotel you will hear the cable car all the time. We loved it and didnt mind a bit, but light sleepers may feel otherwise. Room was a bit cramped, only real downside, more like an NYC hotel room. And elevators were one area not renovated so they ran quite a bit slower than newer, updated ones with better technology. All in all a great hotel.

“Great location,very nice rooms, attentive staff” I've stayed at this property twice. For someone that does not know Boston well, it's a great place to stay. The property is huge and Copley Place is a landmark so even if you get turned around walking, someone can always point you back in the right direction to the hotel. There are restaurants of every type within walking distance or a short cab ride. We ate both off and on-site. They actually have pretty good food on-site. If it's freezing when you visit, just go to one of the bar on site...plenty of food..yes quality food or junk food, a dozen flat screens and the most talkative, lively people ever. I loved my room, and am thankful that I was upgraded to a higher floor so I could enjoy the view. My room wasn't huge, but I had plenty of room to be comfortable. Sometimes the rooms can be VERY expensive, but it also depends on the time of year and the day of the week you're checking in. But this is a quality hotel so it many people believe paying a little extra is worth it. Attention shopaholics: While I am not crazy with spending money all the time one of the BEST things about this hotel is it's attached (via indoor catwalks) to TWO indoor malls. One is a midpriced mall the other mall is very high end. So you can catch a bargain or wield your black card with ease. Don't want to spend $$$? Use both malls to get some great walking exercise. It's air-conditioned in the hot summers and heated in the cold winters - and very safe at night. The staff were very professional, but genuinely nice. If you stop at the concierge desk and tell them what stores you plan to visit, you might luck out and get a coupon. Be sure to check out the theater district. That was a lot of fun and there are some great shows. I didn't rent a car either time. With moderate traffic it took about 20 minutes one-way. Supershuttle was cheaper than a taxi, but neither was very expensive. Of course if you are in a hurry or don't like sharing a ride either rent a car or take a taxi. I imagine though, that parking at the hotel isn't cheap. I would definitely stay here again.

“Loved it and hope to come back” This hotel was beautiful and the staff was extremely friendly and very accomodating. I've been on business in San Diego for about 6 weeks, moving around to different Marriott Hotels (I have Platinum Elite Status) and this one had to be one of the best. I am a history buff and this building has a lot of history behind it and they have kept the beauty of the 1920s alive. The room was great, bigger than I thought it would be (had a king size bed) and hotel was very clean. If you want a fridge and microwave, just ask, they very happily and quickly bring one up for you (and there is no charge). Speaking of no charge, internet is included as well. Anytime we asked for anything or needed anything extra, the staff was very quick with helping us out. The bellman, Nick, was awesome, helped us out a lot and even had coupons for a free appetizer at a good Italian restaurant nearby. Don't forget to ask for a tour of the hotel by the bellman, especially to go up to the tower and see the great view of the city! We valet parked and the valets were great with giving us directions and were very fast with getting our car (I have had problems with other Marriott Hotels nearby and their valet being slow and actually damaging co-workers cars). The location is great, easy to get to and from the city and one block from the Trolley line. It is located at the start of the gaslamp district so there are tons of places to eat, drink, and shop all within walking distance. We ate in the restaurant for breakfast and it was great, I especially liked the french toast. I highly recommend this hotel and if am I back on business will defintely try to stay here again (and would stay here even for a vacation as well). The only downside is no pool, but I knew that coming in. Fitness center was very nice and clean and I also did laundry while I was there (only 1 washer and 1 dryer, so you need to have good timing as there was a line for laundry on a friday night).

“Faded elegance” This of course used to be the old Ritz and (for good or ill) has not seen much if any subsequent renovation. Nonetheless the charm remains, as does the good service and great location. The bathrooms are tiny relative to what we expect nowadays but spotless and with nice Molton Brown toiletries. Finally - the price is around 60% of the new Ritz so it does reflect its faded grandeur. Room smelled a little stale but (hooray) the windows open. I warmed to this hotel.

“Great new hotel” As usual with my NYC trips, I booked this hotel based on room rate and location. The hotel is new and modern and any Ikea fan will feel right at home there. The location was excellent - we stayed there for several days, ventured both north to Central Park and south to Tribeca (not on the same day) and never once got on the subway. Do avoid the bar adjacent to the hotel - way overpriced, plenty of better alternatives nearby.

“Best hotel to ensure a pleasant nyc stay” We love this hotel and if we end up somewhere else we always wish we were at the Affinia Dumont (better than the other Affinia's as well). It's convenient but not in a crazy area and very accessible to everywhere--Times Square, Central Park, shopping--and you can get to trendy restaurants within 15 minutes. We visit about 3-4 times a year, and have brought our dog to the hotel as well. Rooms are spacious and mini kitchens make the whole visit a lot more relaxing. Do check your bill carefully. I have booked at special rates and then charged differently at check out. Once i proved my rate via my email confirmation they happily adjusted.

“An adequate stay” I stayed at the Jacksonville Hyatt for one night for business, and it was just what you'd expect from an older, large Hyatt Regency property. Everything was perfectly adequate, but nothing was stellar. My favorite things about the hotel were the bed, which was quite comfortable, and the staff, who were all extremely friendly and helpful.

“Elegant, Contemporary, Good Value” Not a St-Regis fan, more of a 4S fan in general. We do not like the St-Regis in New York despite the fact that rooms are super comfy and beds even more, but the typical St-Regis traditional type decor is not our type. We are not fans of super modern W types either but we do enjoy contemporary styled hotels with a classic, timeless feel. The San Francisco St-Regis is an elegant and contemporary style hotel, not classic and timeless, a bit more "au goût du jour" which means "taste of the day". So its nice, not timeless. Its elegant, very clean, comfortable, the suite we had was well designed, view was great. Service is ok but nothing to remember or make you go back. Now if we look at the experience we lived as tourists in San Francisco for the price we were paying at the St-Regis, the value was great. It was a great hub to be in. We could walk to several places, even a great ball game on the Friday evening with fireworks and an interesting victory. The big question... would we go back? Honestly we could go back because the overall value was great. The 4S is always on our list but in SF it is getting old so that's why we opted for the St-Regis.

“Chicago Business Travel” I scheduled a business trip with the additional purpose of entertaining clients in the evening. Overall I found the hotel clean, good location, helpful staff. But what made this trip the most worthwhile for me was dining in the Michael Jordan Steakhouse in the hotel. Definitely a top notch experience all around.

“Convenient, centrally-located and close to public transport” This is a good hotel for those looking to be centrally located in Seattle, as this hotel is within half a mile of the city centre. It is also close to the Light rail link terminus, which runs all the way to the airport. So getting here from the airport is child's play, and will cost you less than three dollars. There is an airport bus (number 124, with one change to be made at another station) which you can board from a neighbouring bus stop, so the hotel is also very convenient for public transport. The Sky Needle and the Pike Place market are also both within easy walking distance. There is no breakfast here, but there are lots of places in the streets around the hotel where you can eat for a small sum. The room was tidy, clean and spacious enough. I remember the receptionist on the morning of my departure was kind enough to offer to change a twenty dollar bill so that I had change for the bus.

“Intimate Hotel-Recommended Hilton propery in the area” I've stayed at all the Hilton properties in the mid town area from the Waldorf to the hampton inn and I'd say this is my favorite. You almost feel like a local here, indiscreet from the outside, a small lobby with a door man that you feel you know well after a few days. The rooms are nice, fridge, robes and pretty big for new york. I believe this property was set-up as a timeshare and I kept waiting for someone to try a sales pitch, but it never happened, in fact I found the service impeccable. Only down side is was the TV had this surround sound speaker set-up that is overly complex for the quality of the sound...

“Very poor example of a La Quinta - My Fault!” My Fault, I again tried to cut corners and book cheap on Hotwire.com. They said 3 star for $60 and I jumped at it! I had room 614, very dirty, awful bed, 1980's TV. I had clean white socks on, and after walking on the carpet they were brown on the bottom. At 2am due the awful bed, I went to my car - Ah, the comfort of a reclined front seat!

“Great access to Easton Shopping Center” Very convenient to Easton Shopping Center. Modern, clean, nice new lobby, room was clean, looked new and very well laid out. We liked the convenience of walking to the shopping area with everything so close by.

“Loved my stay!” I would have given Doubletree 5 stars but the bed wasn't good for my back. The hotel is great, the service is wonderful and the location is perfect (minutes from the airport). I would recommend this hotel, if you plan to come to the San Jose area. And don't forget the cookies!

“Very happy with this hotel!” My son was visiting Seattle Pacific University, and we chose this hotel for its proximity to the college (about 2 miles away). I wasn't sure what to expect, but I got a good online rate ($129) and the pictures looked nice. We were delighted with our room! We had a two-queens regular, non-view room (we knew we weren't spending much time there, so why splurge for extras this time...) and it was very spacious! We had a hide-a-bed couch and coffee table, huge flat screen tv with a good selection of channels, two sink areas and very nice amenities (Aveda bath products, Tully's coffee, and a GOOD blow dryer!) Towels were large and fluffy and plentiful. We were given a copy of the Seattle Times in the morning, which was a nice alternative to the usual USA Today! Everything was spotless and the beds were very comfortable. My only complaint would be the heating/air system. It didn't seem to have a thermostat, (I could be wrong about this, as it was late when we went to bed, and I didn't spend a whole lot of time examining it--just turned it to a cooler temp) so it was just on or off and it was hard to get a comfortable sleeping temperature going. The fan wasn't overly loud, but it was a constant hum. It was nice to have free underground parking (particularly when I saw plenty of ice-covered cars on the road in the morning!) and free internet service. There was also a small business center which was free to use. We didn't use the pool or exercise room, but we looked at them and they were nice enough. The breakfast room was LOVELY with a fireplace, view of the lake and plenty of seating. Breakfast options were good (wafflemaker, bagels, pastries, muffins, hard-boiled eggs, fruit, cereal, yogurt, coffee, tea, hot chocolate, milk, juices). I was surprised at how many people were in the breakfast room, since we'd barely encountered anyone while we were there and the hallways and room were very quiet. We never had to wait for an elevator and there were plenty of parking spots in the garage. The location was convenient for the college visit and also very convenient for freeway access, and close to downtown. The staff was professional and helpful. I would definitely stay here on future visits.

“Nice option...downtown.” I've stayed in this neighborhood a few times, so I took a chance on the Fairfield Inn for one night. As a platinum elite, I would have expected a nicer/larger room or possibly a suite, but I was stuck in a corner room that seemed "small" to me. The room layout was enteryway, straight ahead to small sink (with very little counter space) - then a small bathroom; to the left was the drawers and bed/bedroom. Even though the room was small and hard to manuever around, everything was functioning and there was minimal street noise. The neighborhood was nice, tons of mid-level food offerings are steps away. The free breakfast in the morning was adequate, but there were quite a few people, so seating was limited. I ate quickly and departed. Service was good. The staff is very friendly. Overall, I'd give this an average, just because I expect a little more space in a room and I was not "wowed".

“Good place to stay” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Tech Center on a fun trip with my son recently. It was a perfectly good hotel for our purposes and I would recommend it to anyone and would happily stay there again on another trip to Denver, despite having a few issues with the property. The hotel was nice and clean and in a good location if you do not have to go downtown. Traffic was relatively light in the area (we were there over a holiday weekend; since this is primarily a business district, I imagine it is busier during the week) and there were plenty of restaurants within driving distance. The Tech Center area is a pleasant business park area that is well-maintained and clean. The hotel had a decent (but pricey) breakfast and a nice indoor pool and hot tub (very clean and well-kept). The bed was very comfortable. There were a few downsides during our trip. First, the walls seemed to be somewhat thin as there was a group of spanish-speaking people that were up late talking loudly one night and I could hear everything they said (but not understand it!). I almost called the front desk, but they finally quieted down about 11:30 p.m. Also, the staff failed to clean our room one day. We left the room about 10:30 a.m., and did not come back until 6:30 p.m., so they had plenty of time and there was not a sign on the door telling them not to disturb. So, I was disappointed in that. Finally, when I made my reservation with Hyatt, I bought an upgrade package that included breakfast, parking and internet. Before I bought it, I called Hyatt's customer service to make sure it would include breakfast for both me and my son. They told me that my son would be able to eat free, so it would not be a problem. But, when I arrived at the hotel, they told me that only kids under 5 eat free. My son is 10, so he was not free. When I politely explained the situation to the front desk personnel, and that I had been told something different by Hyatt customer service, they offered no apology or even a token gesture to make up for it. In my opinion, a top-notch property tries to at least offer a token gesture. Especially since I am a Hyatt Gold Club member. But, nope, nothing from them for this misinformation. But, those negatives aside, the property itself is nice and the staff were generally courteous, so I would recommend it.

“Great location and comfort for large family!” Hotel is easy to find - right off IH45, convinient to many restaurants and shopping and, best of all, 5 minutes from Johnson Space Center, 10 min. from Kemah Boardwalk, and 5 minutes from Armound Bayou Nature Center. We did all 3 plus San Jacinto Monument and Battleship Texas in 4 days/3 nights with 3 children and grandmother. A great hotel and area for a family vacation! We had a 2 bedroom/2 bath suite with separate kitchen and den and had plenty of room. Complimentary breakfast with mini omlets, biscuits, potatoes, cereals, pastries, waffles was excellent. Complimentary weeknight dinner and drinks was adequate. Tip- Look in nearby places like McDonalds for Space Center discount coupons as we could have saved $42 with a coupon we found after our NASA visit!!!!!!!!

“Well above average - as airport hotels go” One must remember that this is not a resort, it is an airport property. That said, it is comfortable, clean, well located, and with decent amenities. They don't quite have the Diamond level service honed, but other than that is a very acceptable night's stay. I asked to speak with the GM regarding my concerns (and they were minor), and although the night clerk did not relay that message - he came to see me as soon as I repeated my request in the morning. The GM was receptive to the comments, and gave a genuine promise to investigate. Finally, the restaurants on site are good a reasonably priced. Go figure!

“Great location and quiet” Just completed a three day stay at this hotel. Upside was that the location is perfect, 1 1/2 blocks off Michigan Ave., and one block from Lake Michigan. On a quiet street (Walton) which gets virtually no traffic. Staff was very friendly, especially Mark at the front desk. Breakfast is included and is standard Residence Inn fare. Room was pretty standard as well except that I noticed the rooms around mine were bigger. I was on the 15th floor and it was quiet.. Internet was free, parking was $45 but I didn't have a car. On the downside, the rooms don't have safes, which most Chicago hotels I have stayed at do; and the elevators are a little smaller and slower than some of the other hotels. Workout room was "standard." a few Precor cardio machines, a few dumbbells but no mats or stretching equipment. I was told that I could use the Marriott at 540 N. Michigan which I checked out. It had more cardio equipment but no weights. On the dining side, I ate one night at the Rosebud Steakhouse across the street. It was very good. Also, I used the GO shuttle to get to O'hare airport and it was $29 vs. $45 for a cab. If I got the same good rate, I would most likely stay here again. Cheers. Marius

“Relaxing Stay!” I stayed in the Bay Tower for one night, booked by a travel agent for a conference I was attending. I really enjoyed my stay. I arrived at around 10 AM due to an early flight having worked through the night before boarding the plane. I was planning on just checking my bags and going out to explore the city. Amazingly, they had a room available and I was laying in the bed within minutes of arriving. It was great to spend the day resting. The room does have an interesting layout but it works well. Room feels spacious and was quite clean. One of the unique aspects is that each room has a balcony. Mine faced the marina and airport but I still appreciated the fresh air and sunlight. Loved the pool with the best aspect being that some of the lounge areas are semi-covered in case you do not want a lot of sun. I was able to comfortably nap by the pool without fear of burning myself. It is only a mile or so from the airport but I was not bothered by any noise even though my room faced the airport. If you are a light sleeper, it may be an issue for you. Try asking for a room facing the harbor. This location is not ideal for tourist activity. It is about a $15-20 cab ride to the Gas Lamp District if that gives you an idea. The staff were very friendly and eager to please. They were readily available with dining or entertainment options. I had a great stay at this location and would consider staying there again. However, if I was in San Diego to have fun and see the sights, I might find something a little closer to the action.

“Great Wall Street hotel” I stayed one night at this hotel to attend a work meeting in the World Trade Center area and was pleasantly surprised at how nice this hotel was. The main thing that really impressed me was how well laid out the room was. Although somewhat small, the room never felt that way as every inch was well though out and designed efficiently. The room was tastefully designed with modern furnishings and had all the requisites for a business traveler: free wi-fi, plenty of outlets for charging electronics, ample desk. One really nice touch was the espresso machine in the lobby's "great room." If I had a longer stay I could see lounging in the great room as there was a lovely fireplace and lots of comfortable chairs. Instead after I checked in and got situated, I headed to the lobby lounge (in my socks!) and helped myself to a cappuccino. It was definitely a little treat that made my stay a little nicer. One other thing I thought was a good idea was the self check in/out. You just go up to a kiosk and check in and check out. Saves time waiting for a desk clerk especially for business travelers who invariably are either tired from a long trip or in a rush to head out of town or to a meeting (as I was the next morning when I checked out). The one small negative is the construction across the street on the new World Trade Center memorial. The construction noise started quite early which was not too bad for me since I had to get up early for my meeting but I can see how it would be terrible if one wanted to sleep in. The hotel is definitely geared to business travelers so I wouldn't necessarily stay here if I was in NY for fun but if I had meetings in the area, I'd definitely return to this hotel.

“Love the Burnham” Hotel Burnham is a jewel. We stayed two nights the weekend before Christmas. We found the location to be excellent ( across the street from State street Marshall Fields). The staff is helpful and courteous. My only gripe is the room size (which is normal for old renovated boutique hotels) my suggestion is to upgrade to a suite which we will definitely do next visit. The restaurant serves a great breakfast but the bar is way to small.

“Good location but tired property” We stayed here primarily for the pool scene and location. Pool scene had a bunch of people trying really hard to be cool, and sipping on their $16 drinks. The people checking you at the pool would even take your bottle of water so you couldn't bring in anything from your room. Room could definitely use a remodel. Paint was chipping. Closet was huge, but bathroom was small (they were about the same size). We were able to negotiate a decent rate for the location, but I'm really glad we didn't pay top dollar for this very average property.

“Nice Hotel, great location” The Palomar is a nice hotel. The rooms are spacious and the bathroom is well laid out. The complimentary afternoon wine and morning coffee are a nice touch. I ate dinner at the bar and the food was delicious and nicely presented. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Didn't use the pool, but it looked very nice. I would definitely stay here again.

“Refreshing” Just spent four nights at Monaco. Great location for a visitor to Seattle. Refreshingly different, over the top but successfully carried off. Large comfortable rooms, well equiped with CD players and thoughtful amenities (but at a price). Very well stocked minibar too! Wacky decor but it worked - leopard print towelling robes humourous touch. Luxury bathroom marred by a cheap sliding door - let the side down there. Efficient friendly check-in staff and savy concierge. Only thing to spoil picture was the over priced and limited menu in the Sazerac Restaurant on the hotel premises and the miserable surly staff that worked there.

“One of the worst hotel experiences ever!” I came to this hotel to visit my husband who was training at one of the military bases nearby. The first thing I noticed was that this hotel is directly across the street from one of those "checks cashed here, money now places" but I reserved my judgements and figured it would be fine inside the hotel. I arrived alone as my husband was not off until the following day and I was immediately harassed by a male friend of a girl at the front desk. He followed me not once but twice to my room and even got on the computer after me and searched the history to see where I went....CREEEEEPY! The second time he came to my door and wanted to talk to me I decided it was time to check out. because I was scared. I packed my stuff, went down to the desk, told the staff that I felt unsafe and that I would like to checkout immediately without charge, which they allowed me to do. I was actually so scared from the situation that I left without another hotel even lined up. Thank God the Hyatt Place had rooms avaialable. In all fairness, the hotel allowed me to check out and the management called me and offered me to come back at a reduced rate to make up for it. But knowing that guy was the friend of a worker there and was allowed to roam wherever he wanted made me feel unsafe. I wouldn't go there ever again but I would suggest women traveling alone strongly consider going somewhere else. The hotel seemed cute, but I was in and out within an hour and it's unfortunate that bad decisions on behalf of the staff made it so that I wouldn't find out what kind of hotel it really was at all.

“Generally Good” We have just returned from a weekend in LA at the Elan hotel. The hotel generally was great. The positives are: the location was good, the staff were super friendly and helpful, the cheese and wine reception was nice and the breakfast was fab...In the US I find that the breakfasts are generally a coffee, a piece of fruit and a muffin, but at the Elan it was bagels, pastries, cereals, eggs, cheese, yoghurts, tea, coffee and juices. A really nice surprise! There was only a couple of negatives and that was the weird smell in the hotel...it kinda smells like bathrooms (clean ones, but bathrooms none the less) and nappies (or diapers).... We smelt it as soon as we entered the reception and it's something that stayed with us throughout the hotel. The other one was the pillows, they are quite bobberly and hard. Aside from that, I would stay here again because everything else was good and the price for the location is ace.

“Say hi to Pete the Peacock!” As part of my job, I toured about 10 of the hotels in San Antonio. Of all of them, this way by far my favorite. They are just completing a renovation of the property (rooms are much nicer than the pictures they have on their website). This hotel has a lot of style and has much more personality than your standard Marriott. Be sure to request a room with a balcony! They are awesome. The courtyard is amazing. The pool area and various lounge areas (complete with rocking chairs) is gorgeous. The health club is OK, but not spectacular. However, they have bicycles guests can borrow as well as a tennis court, so you have a wide variety of options. Parking is pricy at $15/day, but much more reasonable than the other Marriotts and the Hilton, which are all $25-30. The hotel has some resident birds that live in the courtyard - about 6 peacocks, some pheasants, and other assorted exotic birds. Kids (and adults!) will enjoy wandering the grounds trying to hunt them down. (Hint: If it's hot, look under the bushes.) This property is much more affordable than a lot of places in San Antonio. If you are on a budget, it makes much more sense to stay here than some of the other local hotels. (Just avoid the $15 breakfast buffet!)

“Heaven in San Francisco” We have been staying at the SF St Regis since it opened. We have stayed at several other hotels in SF and always return to the St Regis. The staff is cordial and professional without being stuffy. Rooms are roomy and well lit, with good work areas. The location is excellent and within easy walking to shopping, dining, and the financial district. The rooms are starting to see a bit of wear, but not nealy as much as most other business hotels. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Hotel Aweseomness” There's little not to like at this downtown Courtyard by Marriott. The location is perfect -- along the 16th Street Mall with its free buses in the heard of downtown Denver, a short walk to the Colorado Convention Center and a short walk to Larimer Square where you'll find some of the city's best restaurants. Unlike most Courtyard by Marriott's, this building has plenty of character. The building was once a department store and the lobby is ironically within a small courtyard built into the building that has been enclosed. The old building is nicely restored combining aspects of the old (high ceilings and large windows in the rooms) with modern luxuries and conveniences. Unlike most downtown hotels, Internet access if free (and reliable). The staff accommodates professionally in typical Marriott style. The bedding and rooms are spotlessly clean and very comfortable. The Rialto Cafe, located within the hotel is a casual restaurant and bar, but nonetheless a big step up from the typical hotel restaurant. It faces 16th Street and unlike other hotel restaurants, seems to attract locals and others off the street.

“What a view!” Enjoyed my recent stay here. Had a room on the corner with a lake view. Saw the Navy Pier fireworks, the Buckingham fountain, and the museum complex -- just a super view! Bathroom was nice, staff was friendly and helpful, and Mescat restaurant was really good for both a breakfast and a dinner. Only one complaint -- the easy chair with ottoman in the room may have been the most uncomfortable chair I ever sat in. Obviously, chosen by a designer for the great look, but not meant as a place to relax and read or watch TV.

“Nice, but loud” Room was fine, standard Hilton fare -- excluding the TV which hasn't been upgraded to an LCD yet. The only real issue I had was the noice level. Even with my windows shut up on the 19th floor, I could hear everything on the streets. If they can make the Doubletree in Times Square soundproof, you think they could make a little effort and upgrade the windows in here. That said, I still haven't found a quiet hotel in SF.

“Wouldn't stay there again.” We selected this because it was near the airport and the price was good. The hotel itself was okay (although the walls are paper thin) The problem is the neighborhood. We felt safe in the room, but outside the room didn't feel safe at all.

“Clean, comfortable, modern - did the job” Stayed one night on a layover at a rate of $214 + tax booked off the Marriott website. Booked this hotel due to airport proximity. I had a very brief stay. Arriving at around 11:00pm and leaving at 6:30am. The shuttle can take a long time. It drops at the Marriott first and we had a very full shuttle all going to the Marriott. Took ages loading and unloading everyone. The good news is, of course, that you are the last stop on the way back to the airport which is literally a couple of minutes to terminal 1. En route to the hotel from the airport it's probably quicker to walk especially if you are in a 'low number' terminal and have to stop at all the other terminals collecting people. Wifi worked fine. The little 'mini-market' sells beer and wine which is great if you are arriving late and want a quick drink. My only complaint is that there were no glasses in my room and I ended up drinking my wine out of a mug. Brought back memories of camping trips I've known. It works well for a layover due to airport proximity.

“Freaky, Weird, Fun!!!” What an oddball of a hotel. In fact, it's even kinda weird to refer to this place as a hotel, as it's part night spot, part people watching place, part mini-mart, and part hotel. Arrived after getting a good rate on a pre-pay a couple days before I left Indiana. Hotel is VERY near Times Square and has lots of lovable features: -Mini-fridge and in-room safe (fridge is CLEAR and safe is candy apple red!) -My room featured sleeping quarters for 4, with 2 sets of plush bunk beds, and EACH having it's own separate television that could literally be pulled up on a wall mount until it was inches from your face as you lie in bed. Yes, there were FOUR separate tv's in my room. -Rainfall showerheads, and separate room with toilet. -Included continental breakfast is FANTASTIC!!!! Fresh croissants, ham and cheese, blueberries and raspberries, cereals, yogurt, OJ (not the murderer, but the juice!), and a good selection of breads. -Included is a top-of-the-line cappacino machine that you'd find at Williams-Sonoma stores for probably $2,000.00. Free lattes, espressos, etc are included in the free breakfast. -Awesome steam room, tiny but fun pool, with little workout room and sauna. -Gotta love the free internet!!! Among the few negatives at this hotel: -Breakfast room gets VERY crowded with insufficient seating. -Lighting in hallways of hotel is VERY dim. Actually hard to see and a bit depressing in hallways, to be quite honest! -Because of how tv's are set up, actually difficult in some rooms to watch tv together. -Staff is friendly, but somewhat aloof unless you're going out of your way to engage them in conversation. The next comment is NOT a criticism, but merely an observation. Hotel caters to a fair amount of gay couples and international tourists. Again, not a criticism! Just as a frequent traveler, this is the kind of stuff I know some people would be interested to know as they plan trips. Never did that make me feel funny or uncomfortable, it just is what it is. I'd be more than happy to stay here again in the future provided rates are again reasonable. LOTS of character and uniqueness that makes it a memorable experience worth giving a try!

“Just Ok.” Had to stay at the airport hotel because the downtown Marriott sites were sold out. This is an older Marriott with a convention center. The staff is extremely nice and the rooms are older but clean. There is a nice amenity of a robe in each room. For single ladies traveling stay in the rooms numbered 10-30 to stay safe. NOTE: when I checked in, they had a sticker on my key envelope to not leave valuables in the car. This is an okay hotel if you are doing an overnight, but any longer, I suggest the downtown hotels. Note: After you check in, park closer to the convention center entrance as that entrance is closer to the guest rooms side of the building. You will need a room key to enter that door.

“The devil is in the details but overall experience was great” We had a recent family vacation here and overall we really enjoyed it. The bungalows were spacious and the grounds lovely plus the hotel is in a location that is convenient to many attractions including Sea World, Old Town, Downtown and Balboa Park as well as boasting it's own water activities. I travel frequently and I was a little nervous after reading many of the reviews but I think this hotel is better than many people said it was. It wasn't a 3 star hotel. It had all the 4 star amenities, the issue is that many of the details aren't as polished as many 4 star hotels and the clientele felt more downscale than you'd expect to see at a 4 star resort but it had everything we needed: nice pool areas, a solid restaurant (on the bay), a nice spa, quick room service, and comfortable beds.

“Hip Hotel with a Great View” I had the opportunity to stay a couple of nights at the Conrad in NYC recently. It was my first time at a Conrad, and actually, my first time staying in the financial district in NY. I have to say that I was impressed from the start! The lobby itself is a work of art. Upon check in I was given a double room upgrade to a really chic suite. Since I was traveling on my own it wasn't a big deal to me but it was definitely a nice touch. After check in I popped up to the rooftop bar for a drink since the weather was favorable. What a fantastic view! The bar overlooks the Hudson river with a nice view of the Statue of Liberty. In addition to that I enjoyed the quaintness of the rooftop bar. I wasn't all "clubby" like 230 5th ave. The service was good there too. I was able to enjoy a local Brooklyn beer and snack on some nice appetizers. I would definitely recommend the Conrad for business or pleasure. It's also close to the WTC memorial which is something to be seen.

“Deeply Satisfied” We stayed here at the suggestion of a friend who uses it often. Found a good rate on a discount website and did three days over a weekend. Large corner room with three windows (that opened!), very quiet, all amenities you'd expect at somewhere like the Ritz but without the stiffness. As our pal said, this is a lovely staff, warm and pleasant helpful. Excellent bed and nice linens, heavy bathrobes, comfortable armchair with an ottoman. Central location near the art museum, the Koolhaas library, and about a 5 block walk to Pike Place Market. We did not have a car, but our pal usually parks in another garage the next block south and finds it less expensive. And a great recommendation for the bakery-cafe on the ground floor on the west side; fabulous pastry and coffee as good as you'd expect in Seattle. I can't tell you when I've been as happy with a hotel as this one.

“Good Location and landmark hotel” Stayed at the hotel for four nights at a discounted price of $205 per night (and another $32 local tax per night). Probably this would not have been my first choice in the hotel; however the conference which I was attending was also taking place in the hotel, I decided to stay here. The room I got was on the fourth floor. I did not notice upon check-in; however, it became apparent later that night. The constant noise of the trolley cars and construction trucks until midnight and it restarts again around 6:00 AM. Had I known of this, I probably would have asked for a room on a higher floor. The hotel should install double panned window to reduce the outside noise. The room size was OK -- per San Francisco standard. The mattress and pillows were soft so if you want hard mattress -- ask of this before check-in or better yet, before you reserve the room. The shower water pressure was low and there was mold at various places on the grout. My room rent has included breakfast. However, there were few people who were bit upset after finding out the morning buffer breakfast cost was about $35 to $40 (incl coffee and latte).
