So if the cost is an issue, you may find other hotels nearby. The hotel did not provide free wi-fi. You will have to pay for it. Don't bring your car to the hotel for overnight parking. They charge $51 per night for valet parking. Unfortunately there is no close by parking garage so use public transport including cable car, BART or taxi. The hotel's famous restaurant is on the 16 floor -- it is scenic when there is no fog. Unfortunately during my stay, the weather was not cooperative. The hotel has three elevators for guests use; however, only two of these reach the 16th floor. You won't know of it until you are in the elevator and try to select 16th floor. (The other famous San Francisco hotel – Fairmont – is right across from this hotel.) The hotel staff was friendly and I did not use other services to comment. There are lots of restaurants in the city so you will have plenty of choices. The only downside is that either you will have to use taxi, cable car ($6 for each way ride) or walk. Walking down is easy; walking back to the hotel -- it is hard.

“Grand Old Lady in great location” Beautiful old hotel with updated amenities like LCD flat-panel HDTV. Stayed for business and within walking distance of most things downtown. Like most old hotels, rooms are not large but perfect for the purpose. Booked a AAA rate for under $200. A steal. Definitely will return if the opportunity (and price) presents itself.

“It's a terrific Hyatt. A real one.” First off, I am not a chain hotel guy at all, but if my favorite boutique hotel is sold out in LA, I always choose this Hyatt. It's old-school top-notch Hyatt Regency. Great amenities and classic service. Yes, you pay a bundle for valet, and breakfast costs a lot, but this is LA, baby. Account for that in your budget. The rooms have great balconies, they're very nicely appointed with all the fancy fixin's, and it's in the most business-friendly location there is in LA. Easy to get to Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, Studio City, several networks (across the street), and the FOX lot is a 2 minute drive. It's also not typically a "scene" in there with scads of people milling about with their flip-flops looking for the "Homes of the Stars" bus. Whew. If you're NOT in LA on business, you'd still like the hotel - I just wonder why you'd stay in Century City. So if you make that mistake and wonder why you're paying 20 bucks for your eggs, then that's on you. I like it.

“A really nice hotel that feels more like a condo than a hotel.” A very large suite - large living room/dining room, full kitchen, big bedroom, 2 bathrooms - all in a wonderful location. I booked 2 months in advance and for just over $300 a night, we were very satisfied with our accommodations.

“Good hotel if you get a good rate” Got a great price through a convention rate, however when you do that be prepared for a total mob scene!! The taxi line downstairs looked like the ones you see at the airport, YIKES! Hotel was fully booked so only had 2 double beds despite my king bed reservation. Again when you have a big hotel like this that is packed be prepared to wait for alot of things (elevators, coffee, etc...) Room was nice, great mega flat screen tv (but no HD???). Bathrooms need a bit updating but not bad, however, be warned the shower pressure is TERRIBLE (packed large hotel usually equates to bad water pressure). For the $$ it was a great value, would not pay more than other comparable hotels in the area as I dont think you need to.
“Suites, dinner and breakfast, allright!” Very nice accomodations. New, free "dinner" and free breakfast near all the companies and the beach.

“A beautiful place to stay in a perfect location in the heart of the city” I stay at the Palace on a frequent basis for work. Most recently, I came back on a leisure trip and loved it just the same. The staff is very friendly, from check-in to housekeeping, the lobby is ornate and gorgeous, the rooms are very large, clean, and bright. The windows in the room are huge and open up for nice fresh air. The bathrooms are fine, nothing special, although I feel like I have been in rooms with fancier bathrooms than the one I had this weekend. Room service is usually pretty good. The beds are super deluxe and comfy. Across the street is the Sentinel, with the best muffins you have ever eaten. Unfortunately I found that they are closed on the weekend. Along with a cup of their coffee, you will save a ton of money versus eating at the hotel. I will keep staying here over and over. Definitely a good find.

“Cant go wrong with a Renaissance” I stayed here on a business trip which was at the same time as Lolapalooza. The location is good, the staff is nice and friendly. Ikram at Guest Services and Abraham at the Front desk really stood out and were great! However next time I think I'll stay at the WIT across the street as that was a really hip hotel or at the Marriott Downtown which is a better location.

“Good location, plenty of room” We stayed here for only one night with our 4 kids when they had a random long weekend. It's within easy walking distance of the Inner Harbor (and that's with a lazy 4-year-old in tow) and close to TONS of shopping and restaurants. We usually stay at Residence Inns because we need the room and this one had plenty of space for us. We didn't use the kitchen since we were only there one night and breakfast was included but we have in other hotels. Breakfast had enough choices for us but we aren't picky. What I loved is that their breakfast room had plenty of tables...especially tables for more than 4. Nothing is harder than having a bigger group with little kids and a) not finding any tables or b) finding two tables for three. This room had tables for eight (at least 4 sets). That made my life SO much easier than pretty much every other hotel I've ever stayed at. It could be because were there on a quiet Monday morning but no one was bumping into each other or waiting in line for the waffle maker. The downside of the hotel is that you have to play over $30 for parking. And then you have to wait for the valet to get your car. It didn't make us miserable but for suburbanites (remember, 4 kids to corral) it was a little inconvenient. We also had to use the pull-out couch which was fine except the linens weren't in the bag. Only the comforter was stuffed in so when we got home late, I had to call down for the sheets. When we made the reservation, I asked for extra towels and a crib in the room. That wasn't there either. So they lost a star for those minor annoyances.

“W Ideal for Moscone Center visits” The W hotel is the closest hotel to the Moscone Center for those heading for conferences at that site. The hotel itself is very well kept up, adjoins such features as the Yerba Buena part, the SF Museum of Modern Art and the Metreon, a theater-shopping center combination. Nordstroms and the BART are nearby, The W is a relatively small place, lacking the shops associated with larger hotels, but it's relatively quiet and has an adjoining restaurant, naturally called the XYZ.

“Elegant Hotel” Great hotel, good location block from Union Sq.Lots of Asian type decor. Great restaurant, the Pacific (high side) delicious food and good service.Staff at hotel especially bell boys, valets, car service exceptional. Reception could stand some improvement and the bathrooms were on the small side and no coffee machine. A very pleasant stay with great internet rates.

“The least impressive 'W Hotel' in the US.” We stay at all Starwood properties when we travel and have stayed in most of the W Hotels across the country. Although the hotel lobby is beautifully decorated and the service is above standard, the Dallas crowd at this hotel left us feeling like we had crashed a bachelorette party for a few hundred of Britney Spears best friends. This is definitely a hotel to 'be seen in' for Dallas-ites and the loud, techno music and scantilly clad guests weren't quite what we were looking for for our anniversary getaway. If you're in your early twenties and like to party, this is the hotel for you! If you're used to the smooth and sexy, more sophisticated W Hotels on the West Coast, you'll be very disappointed in this property. PS. You might want to bring a flashlight to maneuver the hallways to your room!

“Wonderful experience” What a great hotel. Rooms are very comfortable, and well thought out. All of the staff was accommodating, and very helpful. Ate at both restaurants there, and was really impressed. Very quick walk to the mall(Smithsonian castle).

“Really nice room, great staff” Recently stayed here for business, using reward points. Booking the reservation on the web site was effortless. I was upgraded to a small corner suite on check-in, which was a nice gesture. It included a sofa, large work desk, and a minibar. The bedroom had great views from the large panel windows. The location is perfect for Mag Mile access. The property is nicer than the Allerton next door, where I've also stayed, and my guess is the rooms are more spacious. Staff were exceptionally helpful and friendly. I enjoyed breakfast in the Sky Lounge on the 40th floor one morning when it was pouring rain outside. Set up as a lounge rather than a restaurant, it's a casual and relaxing setting, (serving breakfast only), with nice views on 3 sides. The hot breakfast buffet is $18, a reasonable value and cheaper than a room service full breakfast. A full service restaurant/bar is also located at street level (it closes at 11pm weekdays though). Parking is valet only, $48 per night, which is pretty standard for the downtown Chicago hotels. My only complaint is that the TV was an older-CRT style unit that had a poor signal on some channels, and I couldn't enjoy one of my favorite shows. Otherwise a great stay and I look forward to returning in the future.

“WOW does not even begin to describe this Hotel” I am not even sure where to begin with this review so lets start with the beginning. We were planning a short get away to San Diego and we have had very good luck with the Kimpton chain. So when I started to check out the San Diego area, i noticed that there were 2 Kimpton hotels in San Diego. I places a note on the Kimpton InTouch facebook page to reach out to others for some recommendations. I got one reply from a member of management at the Palomar. She asked me to email her my needs and wants and she came up with the perfect room suggestion for us. At Check-In, the desk staff and valet staff were attentive and friendly. When we got to our room, there was a complimentary bottle of wine left for us since they new we were they celebrating a milestone. The room had everything we could ask for and more. It was close to everything we wanted to go and see. The concierge recommended several nice places for us to have lunch and dinner. I can not say enough good things about the staff as they went out of their way for me several times during out stay. This is a definite 5 star hotel in my book!!!

“Only one working elevator for 32 floors” I had a business trip in Manhattan, and being a Hilton Diamond member, but also being on a business trip budget, I chose the Hampton Inn Manhattan Time Square South hotel. I orginally wanted the Times Square North location, because it had better reviews, but the south location was $40 less a night, closer to the train station, so I figured how bad could it be? Pro's Close to the train station Clean rooms Friendly Staff Con's Two elevators for 32 floors - ONE WAS OUT OF SERVICE Tiny hallways Only two check in/out clerks at the desk - One was working when I checked in So, only 3 Cons - not bad, right? WRONG. My check in was over 30 minutes since one check in clerk was not at the desk. The line was to the door. The elevator situation, if both are working is an issue. When one was out of service (per the front desk clerk), it can take more than 20 minutes to get to/from your room. And I was lucky - my floor was a high one, so I could sqeeze in to get down to the lobby. The elevator stopped at almost every floor, and many unlucky guests couldnt fit on. I will NOT stay here again

“Great Service and Convenient Location” The ugliest Embassy Suites, but the service from the front desk to the housekeeping staff to the restaurant employees are top notch! Rooms were very quiet, large and clean. The courtyard and pool area was very nice and the property is well maintained. A great location in midtown close to airport.

“Expected quality, not the best location” You will find in this hotel everything that you will expect in a Hilton. The hotel is huge and it affects the quality of the service; there is just too many people. Room and bathroom were according to expectations. The lowest point of the hotel is the neighborhood. You will be OK walking towards Powell St but if you walk the other way, you will find two or three very rough blocks with people dealing drugs, asking for money, etc. Great transportation, though. Close to the BART Station, and the Cable Car.

“Middle of the Road” Location: Mid-town East; not the most central part of Manhattan. I personally despise the East side- it takes longer to get everywhere, and most of the sites of the city are on the West Side. Hotel: Rooms are small(ish) but well laid out. However, there was a wall panel missing (entirely) from my room. Definitely needs some further renovations as everything feels very Marriott and in need of revamping. Staff: I'm assuming this is a labor union hotel- staff is average and not very helpful; also not very professional in back of house or on guest stairwells. Lobby/Bar: Best part of the hotel - gorgeous entry lobby and the side bar is dark, cool and sophisticated. Love the classic and modern combination. There are so many new luxury boutique hotels in the city. This hotel, just recently merged with Marriott, is just ok. If you are on a major budget, stay here as the rates are decent. Otherwise, look for something newer.
“Great Location” Nice Hotel, best of all the staff. Very helpful. Good area to walk to the waterfront and some nice restaurants. We found absolutely nothing wrong with this hotel.

“Fresh Fairfield Inn on the West Side of El Paso (small glitch with room)” Arrival experience: Arrived mid-evening on a Wednesday. Very friendly staff. Room (general): Typical Fairfield Inn/Marriott room, fairly clean carpet, large flat screen TV. Bathroom: Good size, in generally good condition. Tub was clean. Bed: Good bed. Houskeeping: average but the hotel is fairly new and fresh Restaurants: n/a Free breakfast in the lobby was OK. Bagel selection could have been better. Bar: n/a Grounds: No real grounds to speak of, just the parking lot. Pool: Available, but we didn’t look at it Staff attitude/service: overall good, but see MISC section for a discussion of a complete nightmare. Perks for status: Platinum gift/points offered at check-in. Parking: Ample free parking Misc: The Marriott by the airport was fully booked. So I went out of my way to stay at this Residence Inn (it’s on the West Side of El Paso), and it’s a decent drive from the airport. There is a good Mexican restaurant (Leo’s) within walking distance. Walmart only 1 minute drive away. Warning- Door problems! For the first time in my many travels, I had a problem with an electronic key. I had a very early flight to catch from El Paso to DFW Friday morning. I ate breakfast and returned to my room to collect my things. When I tried my key, the door would not unlock. I ran to the front desk and it took a while to locate a staff member. After a few minutes, she generated a new key. But that key didn’t work. I ran back to the front desk and again could not find the staff member immediately. She eventually appeared, and I was in total panic mode. I explained I had a flight to catch and that I needed to gather my luggage from my room. The staff member brought a little machine that looks like an old, portable credit card machine. We went to my room’s door, and she connected the machine. It took nearly 5 minutes for her to open the door. This was stressful to say the least, but I made my flight. I can understand random door problems, but staff members should be up front and present in the mornings to assist guests.

“Nice hotel in a pinch” We asked for and got the airline distress rate ($63 pn). Of all the airport hotels it's probably furthest away. Shuttle service came and did pickup (~15 mins drive). As others have mentioned staff were pleasant, though couldn't find our telephone reservation and had to start all over again. No cots were available for our 15 mo old daughter. The rooms are pleasant, with an interesting design. Everything is simple and well labelled. Room was clean. Only downside were the extremely loud air cons, which we had to turn off. Pool is small and alongside the car lot. Free wifi was slow. Shuttle available for our return to airport at 4:30am which was appreciated. Overall good experience.

“Decent downtown hotel, great value with convention rate” This seems to be an older but nicely remodeled 12-story downtown hotel. Not an elite property, but not bad either. About a 5-minute walk to the convention center, and not far from the entertainment of 6th Street. It sits right along the river, adjacent to the Congress Street "bat bridge" (bats nest there and flock out every evening). There are trails along the river if you like to take a morning jog. About 15 minutes from the airport. The lobby includes a Starbucks, TGI Friday, and small lounge with occasional live acoustic bands. The check-in people are very friendly, professional, and helpful. Same is true of the housekeeping staff and facilities people. Parking garage is attached, costs $15/day for self-parking with unlimited in and out privileges. Typical for downtown hotels. Valet parking is extra. There is a separate elevator for the parking garage, making it a little inconvenient. Breakfast was not included in our convention rate, but TGI Friday's has a breakfast buffet for $12 per person, with a nice selection of breakfast food along with a lady making awesome omelets. I somehow got a suite, which was very nice and roomy. My colleague got a regular King room, which was also decent sized. They offer tiers of wired Internet service: 1Mb/s is included in the room rate, 3Mb/s is an extra $10/day. The free service was fast enough when working, but it seemed to have many periods of unresponsiveness, which was annoying. I guess that helps them upsell the higher internet tiers. The room was very clean and included a fridge, flat screen TV (two in the suite) with plenty of channels, apartment style air-handler A/C that worked very well, and nice bath amenities. An unexpected amenity was the sleep-number bed. Never had one of those before, and was able to find a very comfortable setting. It was quiet and I got good night's sleep here. The upstairs halls have more of a motel feel -- one of the things that makes this property seem a little less than elite. Not sure what normal room rates are -- it's probably an average downtown hotel for the price. But at the conference rate we got (just over 100 bucks), even with the extra-cost parking and breakfast, it's a very good value.

“Very cute!” Very cute and hip. Rooms are small but darling. THey said we had 2 queens but it was definately 2 doubles. Bathrom small. Not enough towels. Had a freeway side room but wasn't that bad noise wise. Lounge up tp was GREAT. Food was delicious. Pretty expenisve, but it is LA. Bed veryt comfy. Why don;t they just put parking in the price of the room? Great location. Close to Rodeo and Robertson. Would stay again.

“Still has some bumps to be worked out” Having heard (on Flyertalk) & read about all the improvements that have been made at this hotel recently, I decided to give it a try for a one-night layover. The lobby & restaurant areas have had major renovations, especially the restaurant-couldn't believe the difference in there! Unfortunately, there is still no place to park the car during check-in & bell stand refused to take my bags, so I could go return the rental car, because one of the bags was a computer bag. Staff seemed to think rooms 'next to each other' is the same as 'connecting', which we had specifically requested at the time of booking, leading to a room change after arrival. Beds are still comfortable, but be sure to ask for a room on a higher floor to avoid street noise. This hotel shares an airport shuttle w/the Westin LAX, which is the first stop after leaving the airport. Other shuttle options to the hotel, w/o the stop at the Westin, would be the Budget rental car shuttle since the Budget lot is directly across the street from the hotel. Be sure to give yourself enough time when returning to the airport to have to wait for a 2nd shuttle to come if the first fills up before you get on-the morning of my departure, the shuttle did leave several people behind & this was despite several pax standing, or sitting on a suitcase, in the aisle of the bus.

“Good but expected more” Went to this hotel over Thanksgiving weekend on friend's recommendation. Generally was very good. The room was very nice with a good view. Felt very comfortable in the hotel. Parking was expensive but expensive; also seemed very isolated where guests park. The hotel is in the midst of the harbor area; very good for walking around. You don't need a car for most of the downtown sites so perhaps that car would not be needed if you came in via train/plane. The area around the hotel has many restaurants and attractions. Did not like the panhandlers we saw in the area; some were on the aggressive side. There were dark areas that could be on the scary side late at night. There is a Whole Foods and CVS drugstore very close. At the Whole Foods shopper before us put her money in her stocking; not a good sign for the neighborhood. For the price we paid could have had some coffee (free) in the lobby in the morning. Restaurant and bar in the hotel were OK. Though friendly enough staff did not appear to know of anything in the area.

“Amazing service” I stayed on business for two evenings and from check-in to check-out came across the some of the most professional and helpful staff I've ever encountered. There were no rooms ready upon check-in and yet the front desk person made several calls, upgraded my room, and made sure I did not have much of a wait. Additionally, she apologized for the wait - a real rarity and very much appreciated. Everything I requested, including a fan (yes crazy, but helps me sleep through the evening), they were able to meet. The valet and room service were always prompt. I took two early morning classes in the gym and both instructors were wonderful - I believe their names were Josh and Nikki. They were very helpful, patient, and great in explaining everything. The gym was large, very clean, and modern. I didn't encounter the thin wall issue (whcih is often tough) but I was upgraded to one of the top floor rooms which was very large. This is a wonderful hotel which I highly recommend.

“Superb stay” This is a perfectly located hotel – only steps away from Port Authority Bus Terminal where the NYAS dropped us off, so no need for connecting transportation. It’s not until you get up to the lobby you appreciate how wonderful the hotel is. The front desk was very helpful and welcoming as was all staff we encountered. Our room was on the 35th floor with a great view (well, as good a view as you can get in NY!). The rooms are huge! Not just by NY standards but generally. And the beds and bedding are divine! We had breakfast at Applebees which is linked at the ground level to the hotel, very good value and very good food. We only had to cross the road and basically we were in Times Square – couldn’t have been better located.

“Elegance as always !!” Loved the Westin Waterfront !!! great lobby. bar, workout facility and pool. Service was excellent as always. Although I believe that the Westin at Copley Square is a better location for tourists, closer to shopping, bars, and restaurants. As always the heavenly bed is amazing and the bar was wonderful. Staff was extremely accommodating. As always Westin made for an excellent weekend get away !!! This hotel is across from the street from the Institue for Contemporary Art and next a convention center.
“42丁目の隠れ家” こじんまりしたホテルで42丁目にありますが、中央から 離れているので静かです。 となりに墓地。 フロントも簡素で個人の家におじゃまする感じでした。 部屋は狭くなく、シックなインテリアです。 カードキーの不具合には黒服セキュリティーが、 シャワーカーテンがなければメイドさんが、すぐに 来てくれました。 財布と相談の上、隠れ家的ホテルとして泊まってみる のも良いと思います。

“A good hotel but not a great value” The hotel was OK for a short stay, clean, reasonable walking distance to Old City attractions and restaurants and the blue line subway is OK for getting across town. Hotel is $40/night for self parking and a long haul from hotel with bags so use valet. The dining room seemed disorganized at breakfast .
“Pretty Dang Good” My wife and I stayed both at this hotel and the Courtyard at the Warf and based on just hotel quality, cleanliness, and comfort the downtown Courtyard is far superior.

“Great Place to Stay” I stayed at the Travel Inn Manhattan on December 4, 2004 and I was very pleasantly surprised. Given that it was a weekend during the very popular holiday season, I had a very difficult time finding a hotel. I has originally booked a room at the Super 8 Times Square ($329), but based on the reviews here about bed bugs, I looked for something else. I paid $190 per night at the Travel Inn and for this time of year, that was a good price. I've also stayed in much worse hotels in Manhattan and paid more. The other reviews here about the Travel Inn are very accurate. Positives: Hotel was clean, the lobby was attractive, the people at the front desk were friendly, the reservations process was smooth, the hotel was quiet, the room (double-double) was the size of an average hotel room which is large for a city hotel, the elevators were large (again, for an older city hotel) and fast., and the bathroom was large enough to have some counter space. The pool looked nice though no one was swimming since it was December. There was an area in the parking garage to check bags between checking out and leaving town. Negatives: the towels were quite thin...I thought that the hand towel was a wash cloth
“一度は滞在したいホテル” サンフランシスコ繁華街の中央にあるこの街を代表するホテルです。ロビー階の豪華さは旅人を豊かな気分にしてくれます。 当日宿泊した部屋には豪華なシャンデリアがありました。ただ壁が薄く、隣室の声が筒抜けです。

“What a place!” Nothing can beat the location of this property! Attached to a shopping center with Nordstrom department store and other shops as well as a food court. Walk one block and you are right in the center of the Magnificent Mile with its myriad of shops and restaurants. Most of the best restaurants and steakhouses were all withing easy walking distance of the hotel. Check in was swift and the staff at the front desk are such lovely people. Being a Gold member I was upgraded to a deluxe city view room which was facing Michigan avenue. The room was of a very good size and the bathroom was enormous with separate bath and shower. Toiletries are of high quality. Drinking water bottles are placed in the room and replenished regularly. Bathrobes of high quality and room slippers are provided too. There is no executive lounge in the hotel but breakfast vouchers are given to elite card holders and can be used in the restaurant. The breakfast is ala carte type and the voucher equals to 19 dollars. So you can either use it for a set full breakfast or order other items as you wish and the amount will be adjusted by the voucher. The staff at every level are excellent - be it the doorman or housekeeping or restaurant or front desk or the concierge. I was really very happy with this hotel and strongly recommend it to anyone going to Chicago and looking for class and perfection.

“Absolute Zero Customer Communication and Poor Systems” If you can help it, never stay in this hotel. I've stayed a few times and the rooms are small and the hotel mirky. The only thing redeemable about this place is the location. My review this time has to do with their complete lack of customer service, not with anyone working in the hotel per se, but with their systems and policies. I received an email from them in August about special rates because I had stayed before. I booked a room for a September weekend, noting on my calendar when it had to be cancelled. I cancelled it online, but they charged me anyway. Their computer systems are woefully inadequate. The screen gave me a confirmation that they cancelled, but no number was seen. Unfortunately, I did not go any further thinking it would be fine and long story short - yes, you guessed it, I am stuck for a no-show fee of $255. They claimed I never cancelled. Of course, this is going through my credit card which can do nothing to help me after 2 months of investigating. Don't bother trying to contact anyone in billing. They are never there and they don't return your messages. I tried in vain, which is why I went through the credit card company. I hope my review of their property via customer service holds merit and prevents someone from booking there. If you look at my reviews prior to this, I only like to review when I can give high ratings. Unfortunately, I feel so betrayed and used by the Milford Plaza that I had to write this.

“Just what we wanted” This hotel is fantastic and the only negative points to call them that way would be the cost of parking and the location, but, like everything in life, depends for who. I chose this hotel knowing it is located in Fishermans Wharf which for many may be convenient and for many others not. You need to know where you want to be and then choose the hotel. In some other visits I have stayed in central SF, near Union Square, you name it. Hyatt, Intercontinental, Chancellor, etc all of the great and centrally located. But for this quick stop I had what I needed. The hotel is very well located in Fishermans Wharf, which is no more than 15 minute walking from Embarcadero, the end of Market Street. I love FW and I enjoy my Cioppino at Sabellas Tower. Knowing where I was going to dine the decission was easy. Hotel is well located, the building does not make justice to the rooms which are spacious, very clean, big and nice appointed. No complaints whatsoever. Bed very comfortable. Breakfast quite good and if you want to go for more you pay an extra 5-6 USD and you get what you want. Went for a run from the hotel to Bay Bridge and way back; fantastic. Parking is a problem, mainly because being that touristic its expensive. But, very near the Argonaut hotel you have some streets and parking spots where is free of charge to leave the car overnight. If not just park it in front of the hotel and "insert coin". If I go back to SF and I dont mind staying 15 minutes from Union Square I would pick this hotel again. Yes or Yes.

“Great place for football fans!” I booked this hotel for a preseason game that my husband and I went to while in Dallas. I was a little nervous staying here since the other reviews are kind of old. But what a deal! We got our room for $85 for the night. We had a king sized bed that was a 'suite' with a pullout couch and microwave and fridge. Our room was clean and the bathroom was a good size. The hotel is very close to Cowboys stadium (it was a little tricky getting into the hotel so luckily we had some good maps). The hotel is just one exit away from the red parking lot. The breakfast was ok....I did have some old milk that didn’t taste quite right but once i mentioned it, it was immediately replaced. The pool is outdoor and very nice. The workout facility looked pretty new. The hot tub looked a little dated but was still good. This was an excellent value for its location and I will stay here again :) :)

“good for visiting Georgetown University” We stayed here for one night. Our aim was to stay as close to Georgetwon University as possible and this hotel is actually really on the campus. Our room faced a pretty courtyard and we enjoyed seeing the students relaxing in the sun. Otherwise, this hotel is in need of a MAJOR overhaul. We did not get a good rate and I wish I had known about priceline before arrival. Parking is $25 a day in an adjacent deck. You can NOT pull up to the hotel and unload your bags. There is noone to help you with your luggage. You have to haul it all by yourself from the garage to the room. This involves going up stairs. Our room had peeling wallpaper, a mildewed bathroom and thin walls so we heard our neighbors during the night. The TV is from the 1970s I think. The reception on the TV was poor-very grainey to say the least. We paid $9.95 for internet service from noon to noon. But...don't pay for internet as we discovered you can actually access the Georgetown wireless internet for free. I am surprised that Marriott allows its name on this hotel as it is really on older feeling Holiday Inn from the 1970s. It is a great location for seeing Georgetown University but not for touring DC. We found cabs to be expensive to just take us a few blocks up to M Street($13.80). If you get a good deal, then stay here. Just be aware of what to expect. On the plus side- the hotel staff is very nice-especially Joseph who is at the front door greeting everyone. The beds were comfortable as well.

“Hands down - my favorite Marriott affiliated property in SF” I travel extensively on business and spent a good portion of October / November in San Francisco. After trying several other properties, I happened upon this one and fell in love. This will be my first choice going forward when I need to be in San Francisco. Check In The checkin experience was smooth and efficient. I had no issues. When we discovered that my Marriott number had not been included in the reservation, it was added and I was given an upgraded room. Room Regular rooms are a little on the small side, however, are definitely adequate. The corner rooms they use for upgrades are great! Although hallways are a little worn, the rooms are newly redone and have a modern flair. Beds are comfy and bathrooms spotless. Beware of rooms on the lower floors on the California side of the building -- you'll hear quite a bit of trolley noise at all hours. Concierge Lounge While I was staying this fall, they opened their new concierge lounge. It's an excellent amenity. Breakfast options are the standard eggs, fruit, bread, pasties, hot / cold cereal, etc, but the service and staff make it so much fun! Views from the lounge are great, especially at sunset. Happy hour appetizers are very nice. There were 1-2 hot items, veges, cheeses, cold cuts, etc. I really enjoyed this lounge, and I've gotten to where they don't generally impress me much. Location / Transport From it's location on Nob Hill, it's a quick cab or trolley ride down into the financial district. The hotel also has a complimentary car service they'll let you use if it's available. Atmosphere / Character What I like most, is the feeling. The property is small enough that people know you. They remember you and are very friendly. This very much feels like a little boutique hotel with the Marriott / Renaissance amenities. I'd definitiely stay again!

“A great hotel and great employees” We stayed at this hotel from 6/7 - 6/9. We booked a 2 queen suite for 3 adults (one of the adults was 16 but 6 foot and over 200lb) and 2 kids (7 &9). The hotel was easy to find, right off the highway, walked right in and check in was a breeze. The lady who checked us in was very nice, even though I could tell she was tired. Every employee I met all had a smile and was very nice. That always makes for a pleasent stay. We went into our room on the 6th floor and we walked in and there was a recliner, a love seat, a desk and a TV in the what I would call the living room. As you walked through the living room there is a full size frig and then a counter top that has a microwave, a small coffee maker and a sink. Then it goes into the bedroom that has 2 queen size beds and another TV. There is also a clock radio, iron and ironing board and a full size mirror for closet doors. The bathroom was right across from the frig and it is a normal bathroom, sink, tub, toliet and a blow dryer. Not the biggest bathroom but it worked out just fine. There was a indoor pool and hot tub and there were places to sit outside of the pool area with windows looking in. When you check in they give you drink cards, one for each adult over 21 and this will get you 3 free adult beverages each, between 5:30 - 7. We were able to do this the night we checked in which was great. They also served I guess what they called snacks or maybe a light meal, but this was what I would call dinner because that is what it ended up being. They had pizza slices, nachos, baked potatoes, salad and soda pop, everything was nice and fresh. The next night they replaced the pizza with chilli dogs, we missed out on that. There are fast food resturants right outside the hotel, you could walk to them if you wanted, Taco Bell, Wendy's, Jack in the Box, etc..... and other resturants down the highway. Breakfast in the morning was great. Make your own waffles (awesome) biscuit and gravy, sausage, donuts, eggs, breads, cereal, milk and juices. We are very glad we booked the suite, there was plenty of room for our family. Oh there is also free internet room (2 computers) and free hour of long distance. You do need you key card to get in and out of the hotel if you park in the back, but there is a buttom for an intercom if you cannot get in or out. This hotel is 20 mins from Sea World. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. Great hotel and great employees!

“Second Visit This Year” My husband and I spent June 18 at Rittenhouse 1715, our second visit this year. This time, we selected Room 220 on the second floor which faced north and thus had no view (which was not a problem as we arrived well after dark). The room was tastefully decorated in blues and browns, with a large “rainforest” shower head. The room was very quiet, and we only briefly heard footsteps overhead. Check-in and check-out were both very quick, and the front desk personnel very friendly. Be sure to grab a fresh cookie from the lobby area. For brunch or lunch in the neighborhood, our favorites are Noble (2025 Sansom Street) and Marathon (19th and Spruce), although there are a number of good restaurants a short walk away. We also recently stayed at the Hyatt Bellevue which I will soon review. Between the two, we prefer Rittenhouse 1715 due to the more personal feel of the hotel and the room décor.

“Nice stay” Really enjoyed this property, very nicely decorated. Lounge area is tasteful and elegant. Couple of minor issues with housekeeping; failed to deliver requested items twice, so I gave up asking. Next time, I will request these items in advance since there seems to be a communication breakdown between front desk and housekeeping. Not enough to keep me away though, I will definitely be back.

“Beautiful hotel. Double check that you have your luggage when you leave” We travel and stay in hotels in Dallas about every other month. Each time we try an new hotel. We have stayed at Rose Crescent, Adolphus, ZaZa, Westin, Intercontinental and are getting ready to stay at the Gaylord Texan in a few days. The Ritz has so far been the nicest one with the best service. The only problem that we encountered was when we were leaving. The bell boy took our luggage and stored it while we ate breakfast at the restaurant on site. After we were finished the valet went to get our car and the bell boy said he would put our luggage in while we checked out. We live in the Oklahoma city area. We stopped in Ardmore to get more gas and realized that our luggage was not in the trunk. I called Ritz Carlton and they said they would ship it to us. I was happy about that, but was surprised that we were not given a free night or something. Especially since my luggage had all my make-up and things that I would need for the next morning. I'm not one to be pushy so I didn't make a big fuss over this. I just thought for the reputation that Ritz Carlton has, they would want to make sure everyone was totally satisfied with their visit.

“decent value for a night or two...” I've stayed at this property three times in the last twelve months and I have found it more than acceptable. Convenient to the airport and the freeways, satisfactory service, and great beer bar. After staying at the hotel I decided to check the reviews and was shocked to see the bad reviews. I am a Starwood Preferred Guest and perhaps I get a better room and better treatment, but I did not have the experience the other reviewers mentioned. You get what you pay for and this is not a place to spend your honeymoon, but if you're on business and need a airport hotel for the night this hotel is fine.

“Great Hotel, made up for mistakes.” We stayed here twice in the last week. Let it be known, I am not a picky with my hotels, you can check my other reviews. However, our first stay was less than desirable with some fairly serious cleanliness problems of the room. After contacting the front manager Robbie and sending some pictures about the issues, he assured me our second stay would be much better. He was right. Our second stay was next to perfect and I am pretty sure he personally made sure it would be better which was a nice touch. I always value the hotel's interest in their customers and this hotel puts that at the highest priority. Our second room made us feel like we were celeberties. Very clean, A/C was perfect, clean as a whistle and friendly staff. Bunker Hill is a great location with the Red Line to Hollywood just a few blocks away. The Omni Select program is superb with drinks delievered right to your door. They did forget the newspaper (or someone else took it), but I just went to the desk to get one. The only thing our second stay lacked was a DVD player that we could rent, but that is not a big deal, nor did they advertise they offer that service. Overall, the second stay was one of the nicest stays at a hotel we have ever had. Book here, it's the best in LA.

“a decent hotel, but way overhyped” OK, so to preface this, I live in Arizona, I travel all over the globe for work and have stayed at many many hotels worldwide. The Az Biltmore just does not impress me. The Hotel itself just seems dated. and not dated in a classic kind of way. I think it just feels old. The rooms, (in which I have stayed in at least 7-10 different ones in the last three years) all seem tired and rundown. The cleaning staff does a great job with what they have but the rooms seem like they have not been renovated in ages. It is a great place for conventions though, they have a ton of great meeting space. Stacy Shapiro (one of the convention managers) is one of the best in the valley, if you have a choice ask for her, some of her colleagues do not have a clue about their job, but she is amazing. Do I recommend this hotel, well the history of it is amazing, the architecture is very cool, it just seems overpriced to me.

“Für 1 Nacht ok” positiv: - kostenloser Flughafenshuttle - unmittelbare Nähe zum Flughafen ohne Geräuschbelästigung - Nähe zu (günstig, einfach) öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln - große Zimmer mit TV negativ: - das gesamte Gebäude macht einen abgenutzten Eindruck - Zimmer hatte sichtbare Wasserschäden an der Decke - Preis-Leistung stimmt nicht (überteuert) Fazit: Für eine Nacht ok, dennoch sollte man die Preise vergleichen. In der Nähe gibt es ein großes Hotelangebot.

“Can't beat the location or the bar downstairs.” If you are not familiar with the city but want close access to great food then this is the place for you. Have great happy hour tequila specials in the bar and whole foods around the corner. Need to pick up a baby shower gift so try Schneider's Juvenile not too far away. Lots of access to Zipcar too which makes touring the city fun and easy. Rooms are basic and a little tight but fir 1 person it is fine.

“Central Location, Friendly Staff” The hotel is conveniently located near Greek town and The Loop with a Blue Line stop just outside the parking lot. The staff is always very friendly (my second time here) and accommodating. The rooms are quiet, but definitely in need of a makeover. Bed was ok in comfort, but certainly not the softest I have slept in. Only two annoying things happened, one is that the bathroom was not stocked with shampoo, conditioner, lotion and two soaps and the light switch next to the bed stopped working. By no means did the seriously detract from the overall experience, but it did show that the hotel needs some work. Especially the elevators.

“Friendly Checkin, Valet and nice room” We just stayed at this hotel over night as we were going to a concert at Billy Bob's. Our stay was very nice, room was clean, nice view of the trains from the 10th floor which I like. Even though we could hear the train horn a couple of times it did not bother us at all. Even housekeeping seemed very nice showing us where our room ewwas when I misread the info writen on the card Overall it was a nice stay

“Stylish HGI” I stayed here one night over a weekend. The property is very nice; in its amenities, it's very much a standard HGI, but it's style makes it one of the better HGI properties that I have seen. The lobby is quite large, with a good working area and the standard HGI cafe. The restaurant is not the typical "Great American Grill;" rather, it's a more upscale restaurant that's attempting (I think) to fit in with the many upscale dining options in the Cherry Creek community in Denver. The business center was very nice, with multiple computers, printers, etc. My room was the standard HGI room, with a desk, bed, chair, coffee pot, microwave, fridge, etc. Although its style was superior to other HGI properties, it was also a little smaller (although not horribly so). My only objection was that the window was relatively small, which meant the room had less natural light than many other hotel rooms. Service-wise, the hotel was on-point; check-in was fast and polite and the driver to the airport the hotel arranged for me came on-time. Location-wise, Cherry Creek is a great part of Denver, with lots of shopping and dining options. This HGI is a bit removed from the major shopping/dining area, but not too far away. There are some more standard stores (i.e., Target, Panera Bread, etc.) within walking distance of the hotel. There's also a lot of construction right behind the hotel; I'm not sure when this will be done or what it will have, but it'll be nice to have the construction complete, as access to the hotel is somewhat restricted right now because of the construction. I'm sure that's temporary, however. Overall, I'd definitely stay here again.

“Blah and more Blah” Stayed here for a conference. Horrible wait staff at meals. Food is overly expensive and not very good. Pool is drab and the rooms are downright boring. You'd think for the price that you pay to stay there that the rooms would at least have nice beds and duvets...but oh no...they don't. I'd never go back.

“Our Texas "2nd Home" Hotelier keeps us comin' back!” Our Texas "2nd Home" Hotelier keeps us comin' back! Once again, the Drury Inn and Suites chain was host to our needs for a good, safe, comfortable "2nd Home" location while enjoying time away from Home. And, in usual fashion, the Drury didn't let us down. This is, I shall say, once again one of those instances where I wish I could give half-stars, because it would be more like 3.5 (*** 1/2) stars! Although a wee bit confusing with all the driveways in the area, we were able to get right on in and registered in no-time at all. Ok, so the area isn't very "pretty", with what you might agree with as a lack of "greenery", but greenery is becoming harder and harder to find just about anywhere - with explosive growth and lack of sufficient rain. Par-for-the-course. Parking is ample - and even though it was relatively busy, we always managed to find a spot out front of the main traffic area. We quickly noticed a greater-than-usual Police drive-through presence in the area, which kind of drew some concern. So, in respectful fashion, I stopped one of the "driving-through" officers and asked him about that, and he explained that their presence was in a Pro-Active position, to notice valuables in plain-view, and to actually notify the hotel to have guests who have left valuables in this way to come down and better secure their belongings. History around this area precluded that, and I can't complain with Law Enforcement's response. For the record, for our one night, there were no issues! Quickly, a bit more about the outside area: Marie Callendars has a restaurant feet from the hotel, and across the parking lot is a strip mall with Ross, PetSmart, Office Max, and a couple other stores to help with incidentals or those with that sudden urge to just have to buy something! The rest of the area is mostly residential, however, there is a Home Depot across the road as well. You're right off of 35, with EASY access to the 410. You're there, or there, or THERE in no time at all! We were very pleasantly greeted (as ALL Drury's do when we arrive), and offered a pleasant room almost exactly where my pre-arrival request had been made to. The room was clean, the beds were comfortable, and I was even able to sleep the night in the fully reclining chair (yes, I sacrificed for the wife and daughter, so each of them could have their own bed). The TV worked fine, the AC did its job, the bathroom was clean and appointed as needed with plenty of towels and toiletries. Honestly, I could not find something that didn't work or didn't meet our needs. Pretty good wireless internet, and a small, yet sufficient, work-out room to allow for those calories you're about to take in! You see, we're not folks that demand a lot from our hotel - just a good, clean, safe and comfortable place to stay for however long the stop is. But what we do recognize, is that our room is simply meant for a few short hours, because we're ready to get out and get busy! Not to stay all day in the room. Of course, I definitely won't forget about the tremendous spread of INCLUDED breakfast offerings in the morning, nor will I keep it a secret about the 5:30 Kickback. Hot dogs, baked potatoes, salad, carrots/celery, chips, pretzels, nachos, salsa, sodas and popcorn - ALL INCLUDED! Ok, and I know you'll want to know this - 3 FREE alcoholic drinks per adult - PER night! For us, it's a non-issue, as none of us drink alcohol. But, it's ALL INCLUDED! So long as we keep having these positive stays with Drury, we're hooked! We've got 2 more stays already booked with Drury - November and December. Can't wait! And neither should you! Safe Travels!

“AMAZING location for families!” We stayed here for 2 nights and loved every minute of it. We were able to get a fabulous rate (really - a GREAT rate!) and when we checked in we were greeted by a great front desk staff in a grand lobby. Anthony was able to place us into a room on the 28th floor with sweeping views of the harbor and city. Our room was spotless and spacious. It was a solid 4 star quality. We slept with the window open all night which was a great treat for a family from AZ. The hallways were kept clean & clear and the elevators were as speedy as they could be when servicing so many floors. The pool area was wonderful (2 pools - one adult, one family). There were 2 spas and one LARGE pool in the family area. And an extra special treat for the kids - fire pits with s'more kits and a "playground" area with fooseball, horseshoes, etc. The location can not be beat - we walked everywhere with our 7 & 10 year olds. The only place we had to drive was to SeaWorld and home. 100% recommend this hotel!

“It was a little dated, but nice hotel” I will stay at a different hotel next time I need to stay near the airport. IT wasn't bad, just not as nice as some of the others in the area. Plus, I couldn't get cell phone service in the lobby.

“Decent” We stayed here for 3 weeks as a young family while relocating. It is more of a long stay type of hotel than a hotel with all the standard amenities (bar, restaurant etc). That said, it was clean, rooms neat and in good condition and in a good location for this part of town. You can walk to restaurants etc. and there is a nice bayou park nearby to go jogging in etc. The hotel feels quiet (which we liked) and the pool was decent. There are not lots of staff but those that are there are helpful and polite. The breakfasts were ok for standard American style. They were also serving free light meals on week nights (one specific meal per evening, nothing fancy) which was an alternative to eating out every night. Car parking is free too. I would stay here again if working in the Energy corridor.

“First-rate accommodations and a great location!” We just returned from another 4 day/3 night stay at the Hotel Palomar in Washington, DC. My wife and I have stayed at this hotel 3 separate times - three nights in July 2008 (in a King Spa Room), three nights in January 2008 (in a Queen/Queen Deluxe Room) and one night several years ago when it was the Radisson Barcelo. What an improvement since the property has been acquired and renovated by Kimpton! The Hotel Palomar's lobby contains a variety of modern artwork, vases, sculptures and murals. The staff is well-trained, courteous, helpful and professional. There’s a complementary local shuttle available through the concierge, complementary coffee/tea in the lobby each morning and a fun, complementary wine reception in the lobby every evening. The concierge was very helpful with dining/shopping/sightseeing suggestions, etc. Room: During our stay in January 2008, we had a very nice Queen/Queen Deluxe Room. The room was large with attractive décor and very comfortable furniture, bed(s) and bedding. The bathroom was clean and functional with a standard tub/shower combination. However, there was very little clearance between the shower curtain and toilet. I booked directly with Kimpton and got an "Internet Spoiler" nightly rate of $202 + tax for our Wednesday through Saturday stay. During our most recent stay in July 2008, we had an amazing King Spa Room that was spacious, modern and very chic. The bathroom was large and attractive with a granite countertop, marble floor, a two-person spa tub and a separate glass shower. Our requested “quiet room” was located on the back-side of the hotel across from an apartment building (no street noise except for a lone garbage truck on weekdays at around 6:30AM). While we did hear the occasional door slamming in the hallway, we didn’t hear anyone in the adjacent rooms during our entire stay. I booked the room at www.kimptonhotels.com for $220/night + tax for our Thursday through Sunday stay. We both agree that the room rate was an incredible value! The Hotel Palomar’s King Spa Room was definitely the best “$200” city hotel room we’ve ever stayed in. In both rooms, the toiletries, animal-print bathrobes and in-room amenities were superb. The hotel also provides nightly turndown service and complimentary wireless and high-speed Internet access. Hotel Location: Dupont Circle is the epicenter of avant-garde culture in Washington. The Hotel Palomar's location is ideal, just 2 blocks west of Dupont Circle (and the Metro), close to Georgetown and Embassy Row. The hotel is near the northern edge of the "wealth and power zone" of Washington, close to many great restaurants, nightlife and shops. Safety: We lived in nearby Fairfax Virginia for several years and visited Washington about once a month, so we learned our way around the city prior to our most recent trip. Although Washington is one of the most crime-ridden cities in the US, we feel relatively safe walking in the neighborhoods northwest, west, southwest and south of Dupont Circle (known as "Sheridan-Kalorama", "Embassy Row", "Foggy Bottom" and the "Golden Triangle" respectively). The revitalized “Penn Quarter” neighborhood is also relatively safe (the area bordered by Union Station on the east 15th Street NW on the west, Pennsylvania Avenue on the south and New York and Massachusetts Avenues on the north). The neighborhoods around the Hotel Palomar are upscale and more or less safe. A good rule of thumb for walking in Northwest Washington (during the day) is this: Stay south of Connecticut Avenue from Rock Creek Park to Dupont Circle and south of Massachusetts Avenue from Dupont Circle to Union Station. These are the main tourist areas anyway. Anything west of Rock Creek Park is also fine. Sightseeing. There are many lesser-known museums, galleries and historic homes along Massachusetts and Connecticut Avenues and in nearby Georgetown. While many of these quaint sights are off the beaten path, they're definitely worth seeking out and visiting. For more well-known destinations, the White House is about a mile away, the Washington Monument is about 1 1/2 miles and Capital Hill and many of the Smithsonian museums are over 2 miles from the hotel. We suggest taking the Metro Red Line from Dupont Circle to Metro Center, transferring to the Blue Line and getting off at the Smithsonian Station. That puts you right in the middle of the National Mall and saves you a 2-mile walk. Dining. Washington is becoming more of a culinary destination these days and there are many very good restaurants to choose from near the hotel. There's also a Starbucks adjacent to the hotel and a bagel place and small grocery store right across the street. The hotel’s wine bar (Urbana) is a great place to hang out and people watch. Summary. We've found that Kimpton hotels consistently provide first-rate accommodations, service and amenities and offer great value. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Palomar and we'll definitely stay here again the next time we visit Washington, DC.

“Worst Customer Service Ever” I booked this hotel as I needed a place close to the Amtrak station as I arrived in San Antonio at 730pm and my train did not leave until 7am the next morning. I booked my hotel with the Best Western 800 number and made my way to San Antonio by bus. When I arrived I took a cab to the hotel and arrived at 732pm. First of all I had to wait at the front desk for 17 minutes before anyone came to help me check in. No one was there. The phone was ringing off the hook. Finally a young lady came out of the restroom. She walked around the corner and said "can I help you"? No apology for me having to wait. I advised her I was checking in. First thing she said was I need ID and a credit card. I gave her a credit card, not the same one I used to book the room by the way. I started to give her my drivers license and realized at that point that the Greyhound agent in Houston had kept it when I purchased my bus ticket. I advised her that I had my work ID with a photo, voters registration card and birth certificate among numerous other forms of ID, just not my drivers license. She said "well you must have a state ID to check in here". She then got on the phone and called the "manager" who approved for me to check in. She was very rude and made me feel very embarrassed. I paid cash and was made to feel like I was some sort of criminal or something. She swiped the credit card I gave her for incidentals and gave me my key. I went to my room which was very nice by the way. I then came back downstairs and check my credit card account to see how much of a hold she had put on the card. Zero, nothing. I checked our bank account to check the card I had given the 800 number to hold the card, which was our debit care and she had authorized the full room and tax on that card which I never physically presented. I asked her about this and she said, we always run the card before the guest arrives for one night room and tax in case of a no show. I advised her that I would have not been a no show until 6am the next morning. She said there was nothing that she could do about it. I asked her that since she had already authorized my card to simply refund my cash and charge the card. She refused. I asked for directions to the Spaghetti Warehouse. The directions that she gave me made me walk through the almost empty parking lot when she could have given much better directions. The business center as they call it closes at midnight. A very cute hotel but the customer service is horrible. They also said that the manager would call me and it has been 5 days and no phone call. I would not advise anyone to stay here. Also NOT pet friendly. They tell you at check in if you smoke or have a pet your card will be charged $200.00. Again very rudely.

“Noisy HVAC and Noisy Neighbors” This hotel needs some updating. Great location if you like Times Square. horrible HVAC system which cycled on and off constantly and it's one of those units that you can't really control the temperature no matter what you do with the thermostat -- it's always 70 degrees. it rumbled like a jet all night. the doors to the rooms do not completely line up with the jambs, so there is a lot of light that comes in from the hall, and hence, a lot of noise -- banging doors, elevators, drunks. i stay in NY every week for business and will not return here.

“I suggest you avoid this hotel at least for a while...” I stayed at the CY Hobby on February 16, 2012 and I think I was in room 142. The hotel is going through construction right now and it is causing some very large problems that they are trying to limit the disruption. That being said, I would not choose to stay at this hotel again. Pros: 1. Close to Hobby airport. Less than 5 mins to drop off a rental car. 2. Bed and pillows were pretty comfy. 3. Room was recently remodeled. 4. Staff seemed apologetic to the current state of the hotel 5. Quiet for a being so close to the highway and airport. Cons - Hotel: 1. Construction is reaking havoc on hotel operations: Check-In was in a conference room, Gym relocated to a dimly lit room, getting from one side of the hotel to the other required going outside. 2. Recently remodeled room was less than impressive. The AC unit was very loud and would NOT shut off at all. Mirrored closet didn't have door handles to open the doors. Room was very small. Hot water took forever to come on. 3. Parking is very limited. Most of the parking is in front of the building which is very inconvenient considering you cannot enter the hotel in the front of the building. You have to enter the side or back of the building. 4. Room internet was very slow. 5. Only one working ice machine in the hotel and they could not tell me exactly where it was. Cons - Location: 1. Scary neighborhood. Enough so that they have the parking lot gated off but apparently not scary enough that they ever lowered the gates! Makes you feel really safe. 2. Difficult to get to if you are not familiar with the area. It is a "You can see it but cannot get there from here," situation. It is located on a one-way access road that runs beside the highway. You need to exit the highway to the north of the hotel to get there or circle around on a different road to hit the access road. It might be a better hotel when all of the construction is complete, but I was in a new room that still had lots of problems. No matter how much construction they do, it will not change the neighborhood. Hopefully their attitude toward their guests safety will change. I am a loyal Marriott member and I wont be back to your hotel. Sorry...

“Nice Hotel with everything you need, but a bit of a hike from the Metro if you have luggage” Quick one night stay for a business trip. A pleasant half a mile from the DuPont Circle red line Metro stop, the hotel is large and has shops, several bars and restaurants. There are tables in the lobby set up for laptop use and the staff was helpful but not overly friendly. My room was nicely appointed and very clean. Any type of food at any price point can be found in the restaurants between the Metro stop and the hotel. If you have lots of luggage, it would be easy to grab a cab from the Metro to the hotel and vice versa.

“Half the price of the Hilton with more of the perks!” I was in town for a conference being held at the Hilton. Given that the rate quoted there was twice what I had booked for the Hampton Inn, I wasn't expecting much. Indeed, I was mistaken. Not only was the staff very accommodating, the room was large by Manhattan standards, and very comfortable. And, unlike the Hilton I got free wi-fi and didn't have to pay $3.75 to check an item for storage. Some people at our conference did that everyday just to check a coat. Oh, and I got free breakfast too. I'd stay there in a heartbeat. The subway stop is within a block of the hotel, so getting there is a breeze.
“Comfortable upmarket hotel” spent one night here - everything went well, staff are friendly, hotel and room was clean and nicely furnished, quiet with no view

“First time I stayed at a Westin and Last” First of all, I think they gave me the worst room, only a queen size bed, and a room that seemed to be part of a larger suite as there was a adjoining room b/c I got a deal on hotwire for $89... check in, lady was indifferent to me checking in, told me they had no king, just queen or double, I chose double, little did I know it was a Murphy bed! An uncomfortable murphy bed in a westin, like come on!!! Room wasn't clean, used stir stick on the floor, hair on couch, carpet dirty. Washroom was small. Elevators were dirty, writing on wall, fingerprints on doors, buttons worn out. If this is what a westin is like, I'll never go back, I feel like writing in and getting a refund. I parked across street for $30 as cheaper than valet at westin. I don't know, there's so many nicer hotels in this place.
“Fantastic place.” Charming and quiet room. Very helpul staff and great breakfast. No doubt, our next trip to Memphis we ́ll stay here again.

“It is what it is.” For long term stays, the price is good. Weekly rates are about 36 USD per night. A kitchenette, full bath, and a bedroom. The wireless is good. If you are relocating and need a very small apartment, this will work.

“Paradise Harborside” My first Fairmont experience and it was just as I had hoped. The service is top notch and the rooms are large and modern. We went to the gold building and that gave us access to complimentary beverages and hor'douerves. The view of the sunrise over the harbor was spectacular. Out new getaway Boston hotel. Love it!

“Nice staff, great location” This hotel is located right between the Convention Center and the 16th St. Mall in downtown Denver. Nicely updated, nice rooms, wish the air conditioner worked a little more (but it was 100 degrees outside). One rude housekeeper in the elevator, but other than that very nice staff. Front desk staff extremely friendly and helpful. The location is great and would definitely stay here again!

“Tiny room with no internet access” Booked this hotel for its location for a meeting, and was initially impressed by the entrance and lobby. Great service, checked in just before midnight, the warm welcome did make a good start. Then it starts to go down hill from here. When asked for late check out, they only allow for 1pm instead, they start charging by the hour after that, not so friendly really (it's not like they are fully booked the next day, I checked). Anyway, moving on, the room is tiny, is just a bed with no room for luggage, not to mention a closet. Once you have the luggage on the floor, you will have difficulty moving around in the room. Shower is also tiny, small sink and everything. Then there is no free internet, not even a bottle of water, they charge every single thing. This is not very helping for business traveller who arrives late after a long flight. In conclusion, they only give a good image at the lobby, that's all you can expect here.

“The best thing is the location” My title says it all, the best thing is the location. I stayed here just for one night, as I got a good deal through Facebook that was a lot cheaper than my usual NYC hotel. I had stayed here previously before the renovations, in 1996, 2005 and 2007. The renovations are still ongoing, in the lobby and the outside. The main entrance on 8th Ave is closed off because of this, so you enter from 45th St and have to use the stairs to get to the lobby--no elevator or escalator. It's not so bad if you don't have a lot of luggage. Check in was quick and I went to my room on the 25th floor, a queen bed renovated room, room number 2531. I remembered it being small from my other stays, the only change now was what the room looked like. I expect NYC hotel rooms to be small, but this room, it was really small for 1 person, if 2 had been in it, there would have been no room at all. There was the bed, which was most of the room, a small bedside table, the flat screen TV on the wall, and an armoire type thing that was meant to be the closet. It had a safe, ironing board, hairdryer all inside it and about 5 or 6 hangers for clothes, very small. There was no chairs, or desk, and no luggage rack so I had to put my suitcase on the floor, which I don't like to do. I didn't watch my TV much, but had to sit on the bed to do so, also late at night I brought McDonald's back to the room and used my suitcase sitting on the bed as a table because there was nowhere else to put anything on! The bathroom was small and narrow. They had wireless internet--$14.95 a day! That is ridiculous, when it's become such a standard amenity, it should be free! They charged for internet use in the lobby too, except to print off boarding passes (I don't know the charge, though). The Marriott Marquis doesn't even charge for internet now! I refused to pay it, especially for one day, so if I had to look up anything, I just used the 3G through my phone. There was an ice bucket in the room, but no hotel info guide or anything, so where the ice machine was, I wouldn't know. I didn't see it on the floor anywhere. They must have rushed also in painting the rooms because there was areas behind the bed where the green paint was that weren't painted well and you could see uncovered areas. The back of the door also wasn't repainted, as there was old grey paint chips that had fallen off. The room was clean, except they could have vacuumed better. The bed was comfortable. There wasn't much of a view, and the windows were dirty. They have two shades on the window, which they have a sign up about by the elevators, advising that you close so people can't see in for privacy so they don't see you undressing! My view was mostly of the rooms across the way. The elevators are slow for how many they have. Their system, where you push in your floor number and they tell you which elevator to take should be quicker, but it wasn't. The Marriott Marquis has the same system, at least twice as many elevators, and is way more efficient! The hallways also when you step off the elevator are so dark and dreary! The location is very good, it's close to Times Square, the Broadway theatres, lots of restaurants (Shake Shack--one of the best cheeseburgers I've ever had!), subway stations and the Port Authority bus terminal. It was good for me as the show I went to was only right around the corner. The hotel employees weren't overly friendly. They didn't really greet you, the doorman never offered to get a cab, the front desk people weren't too welcoming. My key didn't work one time but they were quick about getting me a new one. I don't think I would stay here again. I think I'll stick with my usual place, the Broadway At Times Square Hotel on 46th St. I am glad I got a deal for my one night here though, as it wouldn't have been worth it to pay full price.

“To be honest, not impressed” I know it was a busy weekend in New York for the Marathon, but because of budgets I was almost forced to go for the Moderne without reading the reviews here first - boy, do I wish I had read them! Almost from the start I had problems. The room I was in smelt musty, the toilet didn't flush properly and the sink didn't hold water because the plug was faulty. My view was of a wall, and the air conditioning was noisy. If you get a room on the ground floor beware - because this will be the same. The video was also missing a cable, which took almost two days to fix. So why not one mark? Well, the staff were very helpful and I get the feeling I would have got a room change had it not already been fully booked. The bed was extremely comfortable, and the room clean and of good size. It's just the bad memories of the Moderne will always outweigh the good ones. The hotel needs improving .... and fast!

“此処の経営者は改装&改築は念頭に無いのか” 立地と料金はいいですね。只それだけ。後の項目は全て最低点。何度か泊まったけど改装やリニューアルなどは考えていないようで旧態依然。宿泊料金も最近は3桁に乗ってるようでそれならやめた方がいいでしょう。$15くらいなら1泊なら???。 ロビーは暗く暗いのは廊下も部屋も。部屋の窓からの眺めは良くないのはニューヨークのホテルなら珍しくはないがかび臭くシーツもいつ変えたのかわからない状態。 エレベーターが旨く作動できないことも(これは私は感じなかったけど友人が言ってました)。バスやトイレの場所も最低限の設備。ここ数年は泊まっていなけどもう泊まることはないでしょう。$15キャンペーンでもやっていて部屋が改装されてたら、考えてあげましょう。

“Plutôt bien” Hôtel situé juste à côté de Union Station, je garde plutôt un bon souvenir. C'est vrai que les chambres ne sont très grandes mais si on voyage seul cela suffit. Le resto de l'Hôtel, un pub Irlandais, est vraiment bien.

“Great Location @ LAX & near Culver City & Santa Monica” This is a great location within walking distance of LAX. Free regular shuttles to from all airport terminals. Parking available ..... check details with hotel. Most airport terminals have undergone a great makeover since 2007. TBIT (Tom Bradley International Terminal) has an excellent "new" food court (public access). It has a new & unique Airport lounge (reLAX) accessible to all for a fee ($15US for 1 hour ++ ... 2011 prices). TBIT is being expanded to provide space for Airbus A380 Super Jumbo departure gates. Completion due in 2013 ?. Hotel room was large clean comfortable in very good condition. Great hot and cold buffet breakfast. Coffee bar available. Gift shop available. Tour info and desk in lobby. Convenience store is less than 10mins walk. Public Transport Bus Interchange is about 10+ mins away. TAP stored value card (Metro) may be good value depending on the length of your stay. ~ Metro Bus to Union Station & or Long Beach. ~ Big Blue Bus to Santa Monica. Has its own multi trip pass. ~ Culver City Bus. Its own ticket system LAX ~ any terminal has departing from arrivals level the following:- ~ Santa Barbara Coach. Please google for details. ~ DisneyLand coach to DisneyLand Hotel Anaheim. ~ ~ Good way to get to Anaheim with day return. ~ Flyer Coach to Union Station. US$7 one way ~ Huge variety of hotel shuttle vans to various parts of LA & San Diego. ~ LAX local airport hotel(s) shuttes Recommend it and stayed again at LAX. First visit was in October 2000.

“great locations, swanky, friendly staff - best concierge EVAH!” i stayed here with two friends the first weekend in april for a girls' weekend. my husband i stayed here in june 2008 and were very pleased with everything about it. this time around, we arrived in chicago at 9a - upon arriving at the hotel we were checked in and in our rooms in less than 15 minutes!!! timmy the concierge was the most helpful person on earth to us that weekend, helping us with everything from directions to shopping discounts to letting me use his computer to order delivery for dinner. his recommendations were spot on. we had a small problem with the bathroom lights being out, and this problem was resolved within 30 minutes of a phone call to the desk.

“Great location, NOT great service” This is my 2nd visit to the Hilton New York, and it may be my last. The location is fantastic - walking distance to Central Park & Columbus Circle, as well as walking distance to anywhere in Midtown - Macy's, Rockefeller, Times Square, etc. Great, great location. The beds are comfortable, but I found the sheets to be hard & crunchy - and very loud each time you moved. For the price you pay, I think the sheets could be of higher quality, as well as the service could use a lot of help. I'm a Hilton Diamond Member, and used the Diamond member check-in, and still received lackluster service. The people at the desk were bordering on rude, and just completely didn't care about me or anyone checking in before or after us. I don't expect to be fawned over, but a friendly greeting and kind attitude would be appreciated. The hotel was extremely busy & full this weekend. Our room was not ready before 3pm, and the luggage room was full at check-in, so we had to leave our luggage in a sectioned off area in the lobby - not the safest feeling, but it did have someone watching over it, luckily. Our room was also not completely clean - we found leftover food & newspapers in the cabinet when we got up to our room - that's just gross, and again, at $400+ per night, seriously, attention to detail needs to be a top priority. I called customer service about the outlets in the room not working, and never received a response during my stay. The room itself is nice enough, there are plenty of elevators, and it's mostly quiet. I was on the 15th floor and you can still hear some street noise, but not nearly as loud as many other NYC hotels. I'd recommend this hotel on location, but not on service or quality of the rooms.

“Great Location in Downtown Austin” We stayed three nights at the Radisson for a wedding on a group rate. The room was of moderate size with all the amenities required for an enjoyable stay, however, the public areas and hallways could use some updating. The sizable staff was very attentive to our needs. Self-parking is available for $16 a night and valet parking for $23. The hotel has an excellent location on the river and within walking distance of many restaurants. Starbucks and TGIF Fridays are located within the complex and provide casual meals and snacks. If the rate is reasonable, then the Radisson should be considered for a stay in the heart of Austin.

“Updated, but Missed The Mark” This was right on the board-line of average and very good. The location is excellent for my work - just a few blocks from my office and an overall nice area. The bed was comfortable, but the AC didn't seem like it ever cooled the room, so despite the comfortable bed it was difficult to sleep. If you're looking for a business hotel, be warned that it doesn't have a traditional desk, but rather a table in front of a couch, so very difficult to do any work in the room. (The room overall is also quite tiny, but not much smaller than many other NY hotels.) The bathroom is where they missed the mark. The bathroom is very small and cramped. Our room just had a shower, the sink was small and there was a counter over the sink so it was almost impossible to lean over to the sink without hitting your head on the counter. The toilet paper dispenser is behind you when on the toilet, the water came out of the sink when on high at a trickle, and the shower drain was constantly clogged and backing up. I was confused with why they made such a small bathroom when the closet was huge! The lobby in this hotel, which can be a refuge, is just a big empty space with some chairs. I've never seen such an unimpressive lobby area. The highlight of the hotel was the front desk staff, who were alway pleasant, happy and efficient.

“Obviously water issues on site....” The con's: Two separate rooms booked, two toilets overflowed/stopped up. The last day they had to turn off the water (leaving a message at 9:34 a.m. that the water would be off from 10 - 3) and there were 3 Rotor Rooter trucks on site.
