It ended up being ok, but I had moments of panic when we returned from the pool at 10, got the message and then took the quickest shower of our lives as we had a plane to catch that evening. The air conditioning in the room sucked. We had a west-ward facing room that caught a ton of afternoon sun but I immediately closed the heavy blinds and set the temp at 58. It ran CONTINUOUSLY while we were there but never felt really cold in the room. Our room location (2050, main building) also backed up to the staff/laundry area and we were woken up at 7:30 a.m. by the staff talking and banging as they transferred laundry/bedding to the carts) The food prices are outrageously overpriced. The pro's: The Falls water area rocked. My kids (7 & 8) were in heaven and it was very relaxing. The water slide was fun (we tried it too) and the water was downright chilly/refreshing. We also visited the family pool and it was nice. We booked through Hilton and got the Dining Special so we received 2 $50 vouchers for food per room (2 rooms) so we had $200 to spend on food. We thought it was $50 per stay so that helped offset the food prices and since you have to eat, it was easy to sit back at the pool and order on a tab rather than get dressed, run out for lunch, etc. You did have to use your $50 at one sitting. We ate at La Cantina for dinner (tortilla soup for 2, 1 kid's meal, fajitas for 1 and 3 margaritas + a Shirley Temple) and we paid $12 over the $50 (plus tip). We used another at the pool for 2 iced teas (free refills), 2 kid drinks, a pretzel, nachos, wings, kid chicken tenders and a beer + pina colada. Another for lunch at Point in Tyme (3 beef sandwiches, kids meals + soft drinks) and one for breakfast (not sure what they ordered that time). The food was all good (not great, but definitely edible and convenient).
“Great old school DC hotel” Family stayed at Omni Shoreham for Passover. Wonderful hotel with terrific outdoor pool. Overnight parking is a bit expensive but there is some on street parking nearby.

“veramente un bell'albergo” Niente da eccepire. Ottimo albergo, ottimo servizio, personale cordiale. Si trova immediatamente a sud del centro nella zona di una grande centro commerciale, con vicina la stazione della metro di St. Andrew (che conviene senz'altro usare, 5 minuti di viaggio per il centro). Indubbiamente da raccomandare

“Nice renovation ... shame about the service” The renovaton at the Grand Hyatt has certainly made a big difference to what had become a very tired hotel. The room decor has been modernized and has a much better use of space. Bathrooms as ever are small, rather cramped and with a minimal number of amenities. The wireless internet is also not included in the price but is reliable and fast. The best part of the hotel is the Gold Passport Lounge which serves a good continental style buffet and evening snacks. All of these improvements are ruined by staff most of whom are miserable and surly. There are a few of the staff who stand out as being helpful and welcoming (e.g. Kenny) but the rest make the stay average at best.

“In Need of a Facelift” The Sheraton Suites San Diego is, in the words of my wife, "a fine hotel that just needs a major remodel." I think that sums it up perfectly. The hotel is really a "fine" place - with a convenient location and nice views of the harbor, but the decor and the general public spaces of the hotel are really wanting for a little TLC. The room was very clean (we stayed on the "Club Floor" - originally floor 27, but because we had been given a room with two queen beds, we switched to the 26th floor where we had a king bed). The amenities in the room are standard Sheraton - from the Starbucks coffee to the shampoo. The Internet is fast and reliable. And, finally, by report from my wife - the food in the hotel restaurant was decent enough. The hotel is, however, older and the decor in the rooms really shows the age. Don't get me wrong - it is not a threadbare situation by any means. It is just that I have come to expect a little more from Starwood properties. Would we stay here again - probably not, as there are a number of really nice Starwood hotel properties in the San Diego area that have been updated and remodeled. In closing - this is a "fine" hotel; but, there are better places to stay in San Diego that still allow you to take advantage of your SPG status and points.

“Great Location to Downtown” The location to downtown boston can not be beat. It is a five minute walk to the common and maybe ten to quincy martket place. The room we had faced the golden dome and was very big with a desk, couch and chairs. Had a flat screen TV with a nice king bed. They do give you a couple of water bottles for free which was a nice touch. The hotel is very clean. The lobby is small and the parking can get expensive at 42 per day for valet. With valet you can come and go all day with the car so it is cheaper that way.The hotel room was quiet during my two day stay.

“Nice place, not-nice neighborhood” This is a nice little hotel with small, European-style rooms. The staff was super-friendly and helpful. My room was clean, simply furnished and a bit noisy due to the round-the-clock hubbub in the street below. Despite being just a block or two from some big, swank hotels, the Bijou is in a somewhat dangerous neighborhood. I'm a New Yorker, so I'm not faint of heart, but I certainly was upset when I was physically accosted by two men on the street--on a Sunday morning! So, if you stay here be careful... walk up the hill and toward Union Square, but not down the hill or back toward the Tenderloin.

“La storia passa di qui” Arrivati in hotel sarete accolti dalle storiche foto dei presidenti che qui hanno alloggiato e del governatore dell'Illinois, Barak Obama, che eletto presidente, tenne nelle sale di questo hotel il suo primo discorso post elezione. Anche se l'ambiente è elegante, la clientela è informale. Il ceck in è rapido, le camera ampia, con due bagni (per noi che eravamo in 4 una comodità) e un computer a disposizione del cliente. Per chi vuole risparmiare sulla colazione è presente uno starbuks all'interno dell'hotel, mentre all'esterno, a cento metri di distanza, si trova un dunkin donuts. Unico neo dell'hotel è la posizione, comoda per le visite ai musei e all'acquario ma abbastanza lontana dalle vie dello shopping e dei ristoranti, ragion per cui ci si deve preparare a delle lunghe passeggiate per raggiungere le mete desiderate. Come posizione è sicuramente meglio l'altro Hotel della catena Hilton (Palmer House), che però ė più distante dai musei. Insomma bisogna che valutiate quali siano le vostre priorità (cultura o shopping?).

“Quaint Downstairs bedrooms terrible” We were booked into this hotel for 7 nights, downstairs is really quite nice there is complementary sherry and biscuits available in the afternoon. Most of the furniture looks to be antique and it’s all very quaint. The problem is that the furniture in the room we were in was also of a similar vintage and should have been replaced a long time ago as basically it’s all worn out. We had breakfast included in our room rate and it was very poor quality, the breakfast muffins were mouldy and there were slug or snail tracks over the carpet in the dining area. The staff in the hotel reception were helpful and friendly, but the bedrooms really let this hotel down
“Great Value...” lovely clean room, nice flat screen tv, decent breakfast, excellent value for money...will stay here again.

“Two Words-Top Notch!” Stayed at this hotel as a birthday getaway with my husband.The room was one of the nicest I have ever stayed .They made you feel welcomed and honor whatever your celebrating !.Room was large and comfortable.Any what is esp. nice its so close to the Riverwalk.They have a nice bar in the evening to unwind.The staff was very helpful as well.Loved the bath products and esp. the towels. So if you want a special night to remember and are celebrating a happy occassion (let them know ahead of time) or want a top notch hotel check out the Hotel Valencia!

“Great pick if you want to stay at the Venice Beach” This is a lovely and comfortable hotel. The place is walking distance (3-4 min.) to Venice Beach and there are several restaurants near by. We found the staff to be incredibly welcoming and helpful. 2 caveats though i) if you are looking for a romantic gateway, Venice Beach might not be the best venue overall. Although it is walking distance (30 min) to Santa Monica, it is not as hip and romantic. It is more geared towards street-ball, tattoo shops and street vendors. A very eclectic area but not a romantic gateway. ii) throughout our stay, there has been weird noises coming from our sink. not horrible, but can wake you up at night.

“Wonderful time in Chicago!” This Four Seasons put my faith back in the 4 Seasons. After a disappointing trip to Lanai we had a wonderful time at the Chicago 4 Seasons. The location is perfect, we could walk or take the subway everywhere. The little treats they brought the kids every afternoon was much appreciated and they were very helpful when I forgot my prescription sunglasses at home I was able to go right downstairs and have a pair made in 24 hours! We had a wonderful time traveling with our 3 sons to visit the midwest ballparks and this was a wonderful location and hotel to stay in. Would highly recommend! Oh and the milkshake from room service was REALLY good!!

“First rate location...” Sometimes a hotel can ruin the first impression of a newly-visited city, especially after a long Transatlantic flight. Well, the Chancellor didn't. A comfortable hotel, excellent location and helpful staff created a good feel immediately and it formed the bedrock of a great first time visit to San Francisco. Hotels in downtown San Francisco can be very pricey but, with the breakfast and parking package (we rented a car), the Chancellor was very good value. (You must have a car to experience driving down Lombard Street! ) Unless you arrive very early in the day, suggest you buy a bus/trolley ticket on the day of arrival and use it the following day. This ticket is not valid for 24 hours from the time of activation - it is valid for a calendar day only. But it is good value for money and great for the essential trolley (and old-fashioned trams) rides.

“Laid back boutique who gets the formula right every time” This was my second stay at The Maritime and I must say that it is a hotel that I have really warmed to. Initial impressions may not be a glitzy as some hotels in New York - but once you settle in, the hotel is a fantastic choice. Firstly the rates are excellent - very good value for money. The hotel also has a good location - close to Chelsea, Meatpacking District and The Village - so good for shopping, nightlife, restaurants and central for getting around the city. Rooms are small with queen size beds (but this is the norm in NYC), but well designed with lovely bed linen, tv/dvd/stereo, complimentary wi-fi, fantastic shower (but no tub) and the best mini bar selection you will ever come across. There are two restaurant choices. Matsui is one of the best Japanese restaurants in the city and La Botega offers a good breakfast (love the oatmeal and latte) and a nice selection of Italian cuisine. The full menu from both restaurants are also available on Room Service, which makes a pleasant change from the 'club sandwich & ceasar salad' options that so many hotels offer. There is a also a nice 'laid back' bar with a DJ at the weekends (not the most happening place in town, but a good vibe). Staff are very friendly - a little informal at times, but it suits the style of the place. All in all, this is a great option for both a leisure trip, or low maintenence business traveller. Thumbs up for The Maritime.

“Big room, river view not worth the extra money, and customer service needs improvement.” For anyone who doesn't want to read all of this (it's a lot), here are the key points: spacious rooms, substandard staff, incredibly slow and aging elevators, tiny bathrooms, not the most stable power grid (was without power for an hour in the middle of a movie in my room). The price is too high unless you consider that parking is plentiful at this hotel - self-parking is free. River view cost is NOT worth it. Only get it if it's only a few dollars more (and I mean less than $10 more; it's not worth more than that). Sure, you get a balcony, but there's nothing -- I mean, nothin' -- to look at. Except a few ducks. That's it. Stay at another hotel. I love Hyatt, but this one flopped. Unfortunately, I may be a bit overly critical as I had previously stayed at a Hyatt resort... I don't recommend this for the picky / classy traveler -- Regency or Grand Hyatts (and resorts) are more appropriate for people like you and me. All right. I'm going to try to be as honest as possible here. I love Hyatt - I could never stay at another type of hotel chain - I love my Hyatt rewards points, but this hotel needs some improvements. First off, let me tell you what they did right. The manager and I were unable to reach each other via phone as I tried to get my rate adjusted because it had plummeted by 25% since I had first placed the reservation, and not only was it adjusted but I was given complimentary breakfast coupons (for hot items -- cereals, bagels, and fruit along with OJ and coffee are free; eggs/bacon/french toast/etc are not) for each night that I stayed. The rooms, wow! Very nicely sized, except the bathroom... The bathrooms are UNBELIEVABLY SMALL. You have to stand to the side in order for you to be able to close the door -- I've never seen that small of a bathroom in ANY hotel or motel, for that matter. Nice lights, the TV is decent, even though it's an HDTV yet a lot of the channels appeared in standard definition with black bars on the top and bottom, and gray bars on the left and right side. The beds, WOW! I was able to sleep like a baby (I normally do at home and not at hotels). Highly recommend the beds. Room was AMAZINGLY quiet! Really, really quiet! That's about where my compliments stop. The staff, though friendly, was, at times, unhelpful. I felt like there was a lot of potential, but there are a few reasons that I will never stay at this hotel ever again: 1) Painfully slow elevators that beeped madly at you if more than five people get into an elevator at one time. On average, I probably waited about one minute each time for the elevator. Keep in mind there are only TWO for the entire seven floors, and once it gets to your floor, you have to wait another 20 seconds for the elevator to align properly then for the doors to slowly open. They take longer to close. I was almost embarrassed to bring my partner to this hotel, but the rooms made up for it. Terry is an awesome (assistant) manager. If you ever have a problem, talk to him -- he'll take care of you. 2) The rest of the staff (Terry not included) is a bit unfriendly (and I'm a really friendly person! Really!) and the maintenance team didn't really seem like a maintenance team but a bunch of guys that fixed stuff when it went wrong... which brings me to number... 3) My power went out. I tried to turn on a light in my room and poof! I called down to the front desk (this is where number 2 makes more sense) and said "My power in my room is out" and they asked "Are you sure?"... Yeah, I'm pretty sure, guys -- here in the dark, everything's dead. "Well, you're talking to me, so it's not all out! *slight laughter from front desk rep*"... "OK, well can you send someone up here?" It took almost an hour to get my power back on, and no, I wasn't using an iron or a blow dryer as the "maintenance team" suggested. It was almost midnight and I was enjoying a movie when this mess happened. 4) What's up with the tiny bathrooms?... That's all I can say about that one. 5) The "river" view is definitely a joke. You stare at a minuscule stream of water... the colors a bit awkward, there are a few ducks, and there are only other hotels to look at on the other side. That's not a view. The extra cost is barely justified by a balcony, but if you're going between late April and late August, you'll barely use it because it's so grotesquely hot. We were outside all of three minutes during our entire three-night stay. Overall, the room was spacious, and that pleased me. Once I stepped outside, though, it was just disappointing overall. Elevators are scratched up/beat up, too, and it made me feel a bit ghetto. I recommend this for anyone who isn't going to stay in San Antonio to enjoy everything it has to offer. I know that Hyatt Place caters to "business and weekend travelers" as I was informed by four different Hyatt telephone reps, but I don't recommend it for anyone but the business travelers. For business, wow... a fantastically sized room, but I recommend staying at another nearby hotel for a lower rate. Aloft is a newer chain and seemed to hold some promise -- I almost regret not going with that one, but like I said, I'll probably always stay with Hyatt -- just not a Hyatt Place in the future - only Regency or Grand Hyatts. It was a great effort, but just not worth it. Better luck for me next time.

“Great NYC Choice” I really enjoyed my stay here. I booked a twin/twin and had a good-sized room with two twin beds, microwave, refrigerator, and flat screen TV. The bathroom was small but was new and clean. The rooms and bathrooms were redone about a year and a half ago so everything was fresh and clean. The Hotel Newton is located in a real neighborhood on the Upper West side. The subway is in the next block and the M104 bus runs up and down Broadway. There are many dining places nearby, a drug store at the end of the block, and a coin laundry around the corner. I didn't have a view as my window looked out at the back of other buildings but this was probably a good thing as the room was very quiet. There was very little room to room noise. As others have mentioned, there is only one elavator and it is pretty slow. The only other possible problem is that the mattresses are very firm but guess they are good for the posture. I'll definitely be returning as the Newton is a real bargain for a hotel in a very expensive city.

“Value for money hotel” Looking a bit tired in places, limited breakfast choice. I had a queen sized room, paid well under $100 per night, Cable TV, but not great quality, Room, Shower and Bed were all OK, Built in Safe, Microwave and Fridge in room, but no coffee making! bit of street noise, and a bit of noise from adjourning rooms, but compared to most Boston Hotels, Good Value For Money

“Cheap prices and good service, BUT... smells like raw sewage!” My friends and I stayed here during the San Diego Comic-Con last weekend. Here's a breakdown of this hotel: Positives: -The prices were very affordable (~ $89/night). -The housekeeping service was prompt and very thorough. -They had a pool, but we never used it. -There was plenty of parking. -The air conditioning was FREEZING cold (thank goodness!) -Our room also had a microwave, a mini-fridge, a blow dryer, and a coffee maker. -Free cable TV! Negatives: -Although we arrived at around 12:30 and the room was already made up, the front desk told us it would be "about an hour" until we could move in. (We moved in anyways.) -There was a perpetual smell of raw sewage in the room; especially in the bathroom. Nothing was leaking and we couldn't track it down to a source, but the smell never went away. -The two beds weren't firm enough, and the pillows were too thick. -There was no free shampoo or conditioner; they want you to use a single, unlabeled, wall-mounted soap pump in the shower (like at an auto body shop!) -The cereal dispenser constantly jammed at the continental breakfast. The maid had to use tongs as a work-around.

“I love this place. Good to be back!” Couldn't secure a room at Hyatt Regency for entire length of my DC stay so moved to Henley. Have stayed here before pre 9/11. Was quaint then, but rooms need freshening. My cab driver told me on the way over I would like the Henley. I told him I had stayed here before and was looking forward to a little charm on my last sleep in town! The hotel is adorable. It is in the British style and exudes charm. There is always a good crowd in the bar. My room is quite pretty a great change from the tired room of yesteryear. Big countertoup, free wireless, great space, quiet and bed is calling to me...

“Very good value, pleasant stay.” I was in SF for a three day meeting, and stayed here because it was close to the Moscone Center. Long and short: a recently renovated, clean, quiet business hotel. Everything worked as advertised. Room service arrived in 20 minutes, and was piping hot and fresh. Not a super luxurious hotel, but very comfortable, functional and affordable. Very pleased with my stay.

“Repeat guest” I always try to stay here if possible--must book early. It's the best value in Chicago. The room is basic but comfortable. It's in a great neighborhood--good restaurants, shops, Trader Joe's, free access to Ballys Fitness Club, and a very nice indie movie theater around the corner. Steps to the EL and a manageable walk to DePaul University. Good breakfast complete with waffles is included. No complaints.

“Pleasantly Surprises” I read the reviews about mice and hoped for the best and did not see any! I booked this hotel using Hilton Honors points, and it only cost a little more than 50,000 points for a 3-day stay thanks to point-stretcher awards. I assume they are doing this to build up clientel after having the problems detailed on this website. I was a bit apprehensive, but it was a great deal and as we were attending a wedding I figured we would not be in the room much. Using my points I was able to secure a junior suite. Our room was very nice and fairly large with a sitting area and a small fridge, which was great. The location was ideal, only about 2 blocks to great restauants/bars on Logan and Dupont Circles (go to the Logan Tavern for brunch and enjoy their Bloody Mary menu!), a Whole Foods, a liquor store, and the metro. All that said, the hotel is not great. We were in the "nicer" part of the hotel and it lloked like they had even remodeled the hallways down the hallway we were staying in, but not the hallway going the other way on the same floor. I think their "normal/non-suite" rooms might not be that great. The common areas were not that nice and service was pretty bad. House keeping called us both days we were there to say that since we had a "do not disturb" signout they weren't going to clean our room! Meanwhile the one day we had left at 12:00 ish and taken the sign down, and there was a message on our phone at 3:30 telling us this. They ended up cleaning it, but not very well. New towels and the bad was barely made and that was about it. But no biggie. Front desk was useless and barely noticed you when coming or going. One evening we needed a taxi and the doorman drove us in the shuttle for free (we were going to a friend's about a mile away), which was nice and we tipped him very well. One night we were exhausted so we ordered room service and the food was excellent. All this said, by using my Hilton Honors Points the stay was free, so it was great bargain for us! If I had paid $260 a night for the suite (which is what they were going for when I looked) I would have been disappointed. But otherwise a pleasant mouse-free stay!

“No Frills Clean Hotel Close to Convention Ctr & University” My sister and I stayed at this hotel while on a trip to see the Dalai Lama speak at the university and Convention Center. It's an average hotel when it comes to amenities and decor, but it is in a great location (about 5-10 minute walk to the university and 5 minute walk to the Convention Center). The price of the room was decent at about $70/night and the room was clean. Overall, this is a good value hotel if you don't care about the decor and fancy amenities.

“Great location, but not up to usual Hilton quality” I usually stay at the Omni Parker House or the Ames when visiting central Boston. However, being a Hilton Hhonors Gold Member, I thought that I would give this Hilton a try and spent two nights in a King suite. The good: 1. The staff were very friendly and helpful. 2. The rooms were clean. 3. The bed was comfortable, as were the pillows. 4. Location. Like the Parker House and the Ames, the Hilton is centrally located. The bad: 1. No in room safes. For a Hilton, this is totally unacceptable. When I called down to ask where the in-room safe was, I was told that there weren't any because "there wasn't room for them". No room for them? Please .... my suite was quite large and there were at least half a dozen places where they could have installed an in-room safe. 2. The building is art deco and you get the feeling that they have tried to buy art deco style furniture for the rooms. In my opinion, it hasn't worked too well and the rooms appeared a bit cold. 3. I'm not a lush, but it's convenient to have a minibar in your room. It's certainly something that I would expect in a downtown Hilton. However, there wasn't one. Instead, there was a dirty looking empty fridge in the TV console, which wasn't working and which had a tired sticker on it saying something to the effect that it was more of a "chiller" and would not refrigerate properly. 4. Although Nix's Mate downstairs is a hip and cool looking bar/restaurant with decent food, it didn't seem right that this was the only offering in a downtown Hilton. It would have been nice to have had a slightly quieter (Nix Mate was very loud on the Saturday night), more dressy, place to eat as well. I'm a fan of the Hilton chains, but this is one Hilton that I will probably not stay at again. For the money, it doesn't come close to comparing with the Omni Parkerhouse or the Ames in downtown Boston

“The Only Hotel I have ever been too where I could live Fulltime” I live in Western Michigan and flew out of Chicago on a trip to Jamaica on the return trip instead of driving back home after a late night return flight. We decided to spend the weekend in Chicago at the Waldorf Astoria. Oh Boy.. This is the best hotel I have ever stayed in.....and I’ve stayed at Trump’s hotel in NYC and Chicago and the Peninsular in Chicago, along with the New York Palace. The service here blows the others away. We stayed in room 2403 a suite, I could live here the view was of the Miracle Mile. All of the shopping is nearby along with great places to eat. We ordered room service the first day and the coffee was delicious. The Alafia containers they kept the coffee in kept the coffee hot for 3 hours. The room had a drop dead gorgeous bathroom with Ferragamo toiletries which are the best! The mirror in the bath had a flat screen TV in the mirror. Along with two other top notch flat screen s in the Living room and bedroom. The linen was so soft and modern. The bed was very comfortable and the suite had 1 1⁄2 baths which made for a happy Mrs. . The shower was huge and the water was nice and hot quick. The Valet’s, door man and desk staff were all professional and friendly. This place could be stuffy but it is not. The spa and gym were to die for..First rate new equipment with a killer locker room and spa. The décor of the hotel is first rate and very calming and relaxing. If I were a Pro athlete playing in Chicago, not living there in the off season I would live here during the season. Now the bar here is very nice with all of the high ends liquor.. I mean high end. Pappy van Winkle bourbon at $300 a bottle and $50 pours. The room is nicely decorated but a little on the small size, my suite was larger than the bar. All of the suites have balconies, so no cigar smokers outside in front of the hotel because you can smoke in your room on the balcony. During our stay there were two weddings we ran into one of the brides on the elevator.....Her dress must have been in excess of 20 grand she looked beautiful. This is a special occasion hotel. For romance or business. If you take a client here they will be impressed in an impressive city. I am spoiled after staying here it is all downhill for other hotels I may stay in especially for work. This hotel is rated the number one hotel in the USA, I see why now! The only downside was the Sunday brunch with a limited menu and bad espresso. However the prices weren’t bad. There are better places in the area...one disappoint is that there fine dining restaurant was closed for breakfast this is a mistake as the room is beautiful. The food and service for Brunch is better at the Peninsular and especially at the Trump. Stay at the Waldorf and eat elsewhere.

“Gorgeous hotel close to Amtrack station” This hotel was visually impressive - upon entry the lobby is incredible - I was checked in promptly by very friendly personnel. The hotel is located very close to the amtrack train station (2 blocks away), Seaport Village, the cruise ship terminal (5 blocks), the gas lamp district; clubs, bars and restaurants (7-8 blocks), large mall called the Horton Complex, buses, trolley system and light rail system. I would reccomend if this is your first time in SD as you are close enough to everything and in a pretty safe area (lots of other hotels in the vicinity). As a solo female traveller I felt perfectly safe. The hotel did have a restaurant and a bar which I didn't visit as it looked expensive. The hotel also featured a 24 hour fitness room and pool (not 24 hours) which I checked out and it all looked very well kept, and a massage studio. I paid $350USD for two nights for a room with a King Bed, my room was very well kept, extremely clean, including luxurious toiletries and a robe, I didn't hear any noise and was very comfortable. The only thing the room didn't include was very internet which was a shame however it is available in the lobby area (you have to resign in every 30 minutes). There is a great cafe which appears to be attached to the hotel but is actually an independant business - highly reccomend going there for breakfast - yummy and 1/3 of the price of the hotel. I was by myself so the room was quite large for me and I wanted to stay on in San Diego and not pay as much so I moved to a smaller hotel (2 blocks away - the Sofia - see my review on this). I would stay here again but only if i was able to split the cost with another room mate or if I could get a cheaper rate. Another nice area to stay in would be La Jolla - gorgeous upscale area about 1/2 hour away from downtown on transit but not sure how much rooms would be out there.

“Great Value, Just what I expected....” I stayed during July 2008. When I researched hotels during this time (peak season) I was lucky to get a room with no bathroom, and all the hotels for the same amount of money (269 a nite) had reviews that included bugs in the hotel and rude people. When I got there I was given my room key and was able to pay for the ' in case of incidentals' with cash instead of having to put up a major credit card. This was great for me because I dont have a major credit card - my fiance did but he would not be with me until he got done working later that day. The room was clean, it had a safe and it was cleaned each day. The walls are thin but I had no complaints for loud neighbors. Its stylish and its cute. There were no drapes on the windows so the sun came in strong each morning. We were on the 10th floor and had a great view. Its about 6 blocks from Rockefeller Center. I liked this hotel and I am definitely referring it to other people who don't want to spend 600 a night at the waldorf.

“Great location and good beds. That's about it.” The hotel really needs an update! But if you want to be in a central location it will work. The problem is that there are so many other nice hotels in this area. The room is dated and the bathroom is old and tiny! So many little things that are a turn off..plastic cups like in a motel, plastic shower, the ac didn't work. The bar was so worn out and the closed at 11:30pm..even though it was packed.

“Well-located - but not quietly located” The hotel is near George Washington University, close to shoppinig, accessible to the subway system. The units are suites - with fully equipped kitchens, perfectly adequate baths, good closet space, and a sitting area. A problem - and one about which the staff is honest if you inquire is that a 'quiet location' within the hotel is a difficult - to impossible- need to meet. The hotel is located next to the Georgia Washington University hospital, and the ambulences, with sirens, run night-and-day. So . . if a suite with kitchen outweighs the importance of a quiet location, this can be a good place -- but if quiet is a priortiy, this is probably not the right spot.

“Great Conference Hotel” Stayed June 24 to June 27 for a conference. The rooms were large and clean. All had a balcony. The service was great except for Blue Sage where the service was horrible, not one order was correct. The common areas were beautiful.

“Can't Really Find Anything Wrong” We wanted something close to the Toyota Center and this works........but it is also just minutes from major freeways AND close to most downtown attractions. Great location. The place was also very clean and well kept with a spacious lobby. It was also in a very open location with police stopping in for breakfast every morning and coffee all day long. Clean and Safe. The rooms were large enough that our family felt comfortable all the time. No one had to move around if somebody else moved. They also had cookies and milk everyday at 4, nice gesture. But what saved us $40 every morning was the hot breakfast. I don't eat breakfast except on vacation. Every day I had cereal, bacon or sausage, eggs, biscuits and gravy and either french toast or waffles. We left every day fortified. The staff was friendly and helpful. I don't ask a lot of a place, but this one surpassed my creature comfort requirements. Oh yeah there is a small indoor pool that others used and looked like fun and a small exercise room, but that's not what we were there for.

“Good four-star hotel, comfortable & pleasant” Stayed here in mid December 2011 on a direct booking at rack rate, on business. Standard room was perfectly adequate, and comfortable, if a bit small, with good climate control, good ventilation in the bathroom, comfortable bedding, pleasant shower experience, clean towels and good bath amenities. Clean carpeting, ceiling, walls, even the grout and flooring in the bathroom and the shower curtains were clean. The furniture is showing a few dings and some wear, but nothing major. In-room internet service (which should be free) was at least affordable, and is actually free in the lobby. Staff was helpful, the lobby clean and pleasant, and the meeting rooms, electronics, and catering were top-notch. Room service dining was fast and expensive, but acceptable in a pinch. I also found the airline boarding-pass printing station in the lobby to be easy and convenient-bravo! Definitely recommend and would stay here again.

“good hotel in great location but a little pricy” This was a nice Westin, very much up to the Westin's standards, very clean and great service across the board from everyone, and the hotel is in a great location. It's on the river in river north, and is a short 2 block walk across the river to the blue line (which takes you right to O'Hare - extremely convenient!) and is about 5 or 6 blocks to the red line (which takes you up to Division and on to Wrigleyville, Andersonville, etc.) which is a little bit of a longer walk but still not too bad. It's also right across the street from the House of Blues on one side and a CVS on the other, and is just 2 blocks from Frontera Grill and Topolobampa, two awesome Mexican-style restaurants by Rick Bayliss. Also just a ten minute walk to Michigan Avenue. I'd stay here again. My only concern is that it was a little pricy, so I'd still shop around.

“Nice Rooms; Spotty Service” Location: Shopping arcade with high-end retail connects this property and others to the Hynes Convention Center. Located in the heart of Back Bay, the Westin is also close to several T (subway) lines, the Boston Public library, and some great running and biking trails. Accommodations: Very nice rooms with breathtaking views from the higher floors. Great beds. The clock radios have iPhone docking stations so if one forgets the plug-in charger, no worries! Service: okay -- not great! I checked in to find pubes in the bathroom and a room phone with makeup on the receiver. The breakfast buffet had good food but the service sucked just about every morning. The servers were so slow with drink refills that I had to refill my own juice and water two mornings in a row. And, for $20 the buffet should include an omelette station, it doesn't. Only my 15 percent conference discount made the price tolerable. Lastly, I want to commend management for keeping the hotel guests apprised of developments during the little East Coast Earthquake. The tremor caused the all but one of the hotel elevators to shut down making my 33rd-floor room tough to access after lunch. The manager sent no less than three voicemail blasts to guests during the afternoon, the last of which let guests know when all elevators were back online. Overall, a pretty nice place, I would stay here again if I needed to be close go the convention center.

“'Heavenly' is exactly right!” My mom and I were in town for the San Diego R&R marathon. I needed something centrally located that was also going to be the perfect place to crash after the race. From the moment we pulled up to the valet to the time we retrieved the car on our way to leave for home the service, the amenities, the whole experience was WONDERFUL! Sincere kudos to the concierge service - extremely helpful and accommodating, knowledgeable and even knew who we were each time we approached the desk. The rooms were very nice. I can't say enough about the bed and the double headed shower. A runner's dream. Transportation, food, and shopping are all within walking distance. . . the views are spectacular, the outdoor pool is great, and the special massage service that was brought in for the marathon was so perfect. What a great treat for my first race and my mom's birthday. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone that will be in town for both business and vacation. The trolley station is a very short walk, putting the whole city within easy access. Enjoy!!

“great service, great location” We stayed at this hotel the first week in April. The staff was courteous and always willing to help us. Service was always with a smile. The Grandview restaurant was excellent with attentive service from Richard our waiter. Great location, close to shopping. Would stay at again.

“great hotel, lousy location” we took advantage of a one-day sale, basic room for just $99 ($150/night + $50 food/room service credit). for a 5 star hotel that's amazing. and the hotel is fantastic but for it's location. noise all night, homeless people milling around all morning. now i understand why it was so cheap! we'd rather not deal with the urban blight on our vacation, BUT if you can take it...it's an amazing hotel otherwise.
“Third Stay & A Pleasure Each Time” Helpful staff, friendly service, comfortable room. Business friendly. Hotwire rate, but always treated like full paying guest. Thanks very much.

“Ok but some drawbacks” I stayed at the HGI for business. The staff was helpful and nice and the room was clean. My biggest complaint is that the food was awful. The room service had portions that tasted spoiled. The breakfast buffet was also sub par and there is no room service option for breakfast. I've stayed at a lot of HGI's and this one is the worst I've been too. on the plus side, once I brought the room service issue to their attention they did credit for part of the meal. everyone there was pleasant and attentive. If I had to come back i would probably venture out for better food options. Front desk staff very nice.

“Excellent hotel--but watch out for the upcharges!” This is a brand-new hotel, opened 2/28/08, and, at the rate I paid, $160 a night, you won't find a better value (without Priceline) for a true 4* hotel. The rooms are very comfortable and quiet. I didn't even hear people in the hallways. The room size is fairly large for a big city center, although there is only room for one person to sit at the desk, so I think it would be difficult for more than one person at a time to enjoy room service. There are eight fast elevators. The gym is huge, with individual headsets for TV, apples, and free bottled water (a better option than the $8 they want to charge you for the bottle in your room). There's a long 3-laned lap pool with swim goggles provided. The pool is indoors, but there is an outside sunning deck for those rare days (such as today), when it's warm enough to work on your tan in SF. There's also a small whirlpool tub, and a spa (which I didn't examine). One unfortunate aspect of this hotel is that almost all rooms either have views of downtown or the bay, but not both, due to the alignment of the hotel. The odd-numbered rooms have downtown views and the even bay views (I would give an edge to the downtown views). The only room which would have views of both would be at the end, i.e. rooms ending in XX19. I would also note that the hotel has no 2nd or 13th floor, so you need to subtract 1 or 2 from your floor number to know what floor you're really on. As often happens in high-end hotels, they seem to make a lot of extra bucks on non-room-rate fees. Using the internet will cost you an extra $14/d. The parking charge is $50 a day, although since we stayed a Saturday night, we found street parking across the street for free, and there are a number of less expensive parking lots around. A simple room service breakfast will set you back over $30. A regular drink (cape cod) will cost $10 (plus tax and tip). The minibar charges are also astronomical (it's one of those which charges you if you so much as move an item). The location is excellent for the Moscone Center, MOMA, or the Metreon. It's two long blocks to BART and MUNI (Powell St. Station--which can also get you into the airport if you don't have too much luggage to lug around two blocks). Union Square or the Theater District are a 10-15 minute walk. So as of this time, this new hotel is a great deal for a modern, comfortable 4*. The caveats are that the views aren't as great as you'd think (we were on the 24th floor), and the extra charges can really get you if you're not careful. Oh, and there are no bathtubs in the regular rooms.
“Very nice” Great hotel, very conveniently located to the Moscone center. Very comfortable rooms, good service, nice bar. All-in-all, a very nice place to stay.

“great hotel but a bit disappointed” Good location, nice staff, very very good restaurants. But the room was a bit too noisy (probably because of the pool's ventilation) and we could only sleep 5 hours. We appreciated the fact that we did not have to check out before noon as we got up at 10 am and we could enjoy a delicious continental breakfast. We chose the "staycation" option. Breakfast and parking were included which was great. But when we picked up the car, the attendant said we had not paid for the parking and he refused to let us go. So we had to go back to the hotel and get from the receptionist the proof of our payment. That was a bit annoying since we were in a hurry. But overall, we enjoyed our stay there and we might come back but not to stay in the same room.

“Excellent, Excellent is the Only Way To Describe This Resort!!!!” The Westin Resort is amazing and beautiful in all aspects. Everything from the first hello at valet to the front desk to room service to dinner to the pool attendants - everything is finer than fine. I'm also a platinum member with Starwood and received a free upgrade to a beautiful suite. If you are wondering where to stay - then the choice is a no-brainer. The Westin La Cantera offers more in a resort than I've seen in years. The majestic views, first class golf course and incredible facility all tucked into one simple yet elegant package. This exemplifies why Starwood is the preeminent choice for all travelers. This is another reason why SPG has won the "Freddie Awards" so, so very often over their competitors who do not hold a candle to them. Be a Starwood guest and start enjoying all the worldwide exclusive benefits.

“Very nice, very convenient” I’ve stayed on Capitol Hill in Washington a number of times over the last several years for various business meetings and conferences, but none of the hotels at which I’ve stayed measure up to the Washington Court. When I arrived at about 1 p.m., I was offered a room with two double beds immediately, or the option of waiting until about 4 p.m. for a king room. As this trip was only for a single night and I had some things I wanted to accomplish before my meeting (including reviewing some documents and getting in a light workout), I took the room that was available. The room, which opened into the interior courtyard area, was beautifully decorated and included a desk, a reading chair, and an alarm clock one did not need a manual to figure out. The bathroom, which has a small black-and-white TV and telephone, was nicely decorated with the usual amenities. The only drawback was the main bedroom's rather tired 27” television with a picture that got fuzzy every few minutes. I certainly wasn’t going to pay to watch a movie on that television... Service was very good. In addition to accommodating my (very) early arrival, housekeeping brought a robe within minutes of my request, and everyone I encountered was friendly and helpful. The lobby bar served as a nice meeting place. The service was good and the prices reasonable. Only a few negatives (in addition to the television issue I mentioned above). The fitness center is a little light on cardio equipment, though it does have plasma TVs to watch during your workout. It would be better if the plasma sets were in the rooms. The business center was also somewhat sparsely equipped and, unlike the Hyatt across the street, did not have a kiosk offering complimentary airline check-in. A colleague said it cost him about $14 to check in, counting computer time and the cost of printing out the boarding pass. I’ll admit it: I walked across the street to the Hyatt (where I have stayed recently) and used their complimentary kiosk. This area of Capitol Hill offers quite of few restaurants (some of them very good, like Bistro Bis in the nearby Hotel George), and is convenient to Union Station and the Metro. The homeless residents get a bit more aggressive after dark, but such is the case in many large cities. The biggest challenge, as with virtually any hotel in the District, is getting a favorable rate. The father in advance you can book, the better – and it’s likely to be better still if Congress is not in session. If you can get a competitive rate (or if money is no object), I’d highly recommend the Washington Court Hotel.

“Great location and pretty good value for money” The location of this hotel is it's major selling point. Put simply it is close to just about everything whether you are walking or plan on using public transport. The rooms are nice and clean and quite spacious, especially the one bedroom suites. All rooms are well equipped and come standard with a large refrigerator and kitchenette. The only real let down is the complimentary breakfast, which although it is complimentary it lacks any real variety and is lacking in the taste department. The only taste that does exist is pretty much pure sugar. Overall the family thoroughly enjoyed our stay, the Comfort Suites were family friendly relatively well appointed and certainly in a fantastic location

“Great place for spending a night while passing through LAX” My wife and I spent the night of February 25, 2012 at the Sheraton Gateway LAX as part of our 29 hour trip from Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada to Santiago, Chile. We found our room with king size bed, at a cost of $104 plus tax, to be clean, the bed and linens comfortable, and the flat screen television in good working order. My only complaint is that there was a $12.50 daily fee for wireless internet usage, so we elected to utilize the free computers in the hotel's lobby area. Of note: My wife and I enjoyed excellent nachos at the lobby bar. We also had the concierge book us a 7 hour tour of Los Angeles and Beverly Hills ($79 per person with VIP Tours -- pick-up and drop off at the hotel). Overall, I must say that I am very pleased with the Sheraton Gateway LAX for an "airport hotel". On a scale of 1 to 10, where 1 is terrible and 10 is excellent, I give the Sheraton Gateway Lax a rating of 8.

“Immer wieder FANTASTISCH” Wir waren schon öfter im Mandarin in New York. Aber es ist jedesmal super. Das Hotel liegt direkt am Columbus Circle im Time Warner Gebäude. Man hat auch vom 3.Stock Zugang zu einem Teil des Time Warner Centers welches eine kleine Shoppingmall beherbergt. Es gibt einen kleinen Empfangsbereichunten, aber die eigentliche Lobby ist im 35 Stock. Wenn man aus dem Aufzug steigt ist die Aussicht ein Wow. Es gibt in diesem Stock eine Bar eine Lobby Lounge und das Asiate (das Restaurant). In der Lobby zu sitzen ob beim Frühstück das am Wochenende auch dort eingenommen werden kann oder nachmittags oder abends ist ein Erlebnis. Die Aussicht ist einzigartig. In der Lobby Lounge gibt es auch eine kleine Snackkarte. Die Zimmer sind für New Yorker Verhältnisse extrem groß.Jeden zweiten Tag stand immer was anderes im Zimmer. Obst, Pralinen, Kuchen.... Die Aussicht ist je nach Kategorie unterschiedlich. Wir hatten das erste mal eine Aussicht auf den Hudson River aus dem 51. Stock. Wunderbar. Das Bad ist sehr groß mit Wanne und großem Fenster. Im Zimmer befindet sich alles was man von einem Luxushotel erwartet. Der Service im allgemeinen ist bestens. Außer die Kellner im Asiate und in der Lobby Lounge sind teilsweise nicht gut genug ausgebildet. Fitness ist klein aber relativ gut sortiert. Neben dem Fitness gibt es ein kleines feines Schwimmbad mit toller Aussicht. Es ist zwar irrsinnig teuer aber ich finde jeden Euro wert. Da das Hotel praktisch erst im 35 Stock beginnt ist es auch so außergewöhnlich. Fazit: Wenn man einmal da wohnt ist es sehr schwer woanders zu wohnen wenn man in New York ist.

“Others too Big, Others too Small..This hotel is just right!” A visiting friend came in from Atlanta for a much needed vacation and got an excellent deal on this hotel....It is smack in the middle between LAX, Santa Monica, Beverly Hills-Hollywood and Downtown...He didn't drive ( a sin in LA but he is a New Yorker) but was able to get around to his vacation destinations via cab/bus and sch Now I know West LA and I can say it is hard to find a good solid hotel at a decent price... I like Century City but in this are you have a Lackluster Holiday Inn Express, A small roomed medicorce Courtyard, and TOO BIG trying so hard Century Plaza...all all usually run you $200 but I know you can get a deal on this place on hotwire/pricline if you look The Pros: The ROOM: If you love lots of light and window, this place will suite you with their floor to ceiling windows. Spacious Desk. The bed looked comfy.Bathroom was large with a separate tube from shower ++++BALCONIES...if you smoke every room in this place has a balcony which is hard to find in LA..The only other I know in this are is the Sheraton Delfina. I liked how the bed was not the first thing you saw when you walked into the room ( ie, away from hallway and bathroom blocked having to hear people or maids). Plus, it just makes the room feel bigger...my friend loved that they had lounging robes for him. If you are Middle Eastern/Arab...they adore you. Okay this is just an inference to the 4 or five television channels they had available...Oh and the hotel is also CLOSE to UCLA..I would recommend it for a stay if you are visiting someone there. FOOD/SHOPPING: You are close to the Westfield Century City Mall...and restaurants. my friend said their food court was gourmet and delicious. You are also quite close the Beverly Center where we went to Dinner at the Grand Lux (YUMMY) (The Sofitel is ok but I think I preferred this one for a West LA location base if you don't HAVE to be in Santa Monica). The hotel does have a quaint little bar but I didn't really check out the facilites When I walked in the hotel was quiet..now this is sorta an industry/biz area so it would make sense that is wouldn't be crazy busy on the weekend unless it has shopping ladies. CONS: They only have valet which runs 30 or so a night but they do charge less for visits which is nice...Some places in Hollywood ( see my Ramada review) are $30 no matter how long you stay. After you park, it is straight up to the room...no crazy 20 minute walk to your room elevators like downtown la hotels. When I went to get my car it took a bit longer then I expected BE WARNED: You could miss the hotel from the street...I did miss the small entrance the first time around. If you want a busy/happening hotel this is not for you...but for people staying in the area it is the best of the choices... Cheers, Bella

“Smallest Hotel Room in the World!” My sister always teases me when I check a room's size before booking. Well, I didn't do that this time, and it was a mistake! I didn't measure the room, but I'm certain it was about 12x9! The bathroom was about 6x6, there was one very small closet, and no dresser. The room was comfortable and clean and hotel staff were very cordial and helpful, but the room is way too small for two adult women! No wonder the price was a little more reasonable for midtown.

“The true test is when something goes wrong” The hotel is beautiful and you can't beat the location for getting to the most popular tourist sites. The front desk staff are attentive, the bar area is comfortable and breakfast is a bargain compared to the prices of even Denny's down the street. I checked into the hotel on a Friday for a restful weekend. The first evening something went wrong with the phone system and it was intermittently sending calls to my room from the outside. According to staff the system had just been worked on. This made for a disruptive first night but I got through it. The next morning they comped my breakfast which I thought was nice. Later I mentioned it when I got the Marriott survey, a day later I received an email from the hotel manager apologizing for the incident and crediting off the first night's stay. It's easy when things go right for hotels to take care of you but the true test is when things go wrong. This hotel is focused on taking care of it's guests. I would stay here again in a minute.

“Cheap, cheerful, compact – great location.” TRANSIT – free shuttle FROM airport. We had dropped a FOX car rental off and walked down the Promenade. LOCATION - Gaslamp area is where action is. Easy walk to trolley lines, restaurants, waterfront. Parking fees apply. Lot of weirdos wandering around talking to themselves. CHECKIN – efficient but impersonal. ROOMS – stayed in Rm 414 initially. Shewn kind enough to offer us another room as some alarm going off all night external to the Hotel. Mattresses in each room were squeaky (old) – ok if you don’t move in your sleep. Cheap & cheerful. This is central city so be prepared for road noise – did not interrupt our sleep though. BREAKFAST – good selection but no toast.

“Hotel was average / acceptable (AC/DC were better!!!)” Stayed for 4 nights in October and was reasonably pleased with this hotel. Okay, it's a bit pricey for what it is but get a good rate and its more than acceptable. It's a clean and safe place to be. Guests were a mix of tourists, business people and conference attendees. Big room (one bed) was very comfortable, but bathroom was small. Great location for Union Station, Capitol Building, the Mall and the Verizon Centre if you're going to a concert/game (as we did). There is a shortage of eateries in the immediate vicinity, but Union Station is more than accommodating for a cheap breakfast and is only around the corner. In my opinion not as good as other Affinia hotels (as in New York city), but it did the job. Tip: ask for a non-connecting room if this is not required - connecting doorways do not appear to be well insulated. Didn't use the bar or restaurant - they seemed a bit pricey. I agree with other reviewers about the lack of free bottled water and coffee/tea. Its these little things that people seem to remember most!

“If you want in the Middle of Times Square, this is the place” Great location in the middle of Times Square. As others have mentioned, elevators can be confusing, however, once you get the hang of them it’s all good. The elevators can be slow at times especially in the early evening when people are headed out to shows. Make sure you leave yourself enough time. We waited over 10 minutes and were almost late for our dinner reservations at an off property restaurant. The other thing and this is no fault of Marriott, as people are waiting for the elevators, they tend to crowd at the elevator doors and makes it very hard to get off once the elevator stops at your desired floor. Rooms were very comfortable and clean. We were on the 30th floor. Had dinner at The View one evening before a show. Great views of Manhattan, food was good. Went back to The View for drinks after the show and service was less than desirable. There were several folks that left because the server was hit or miss. The next evening, had the dessert buffet at The View. Not worth $19.00 per person. If you are not a hotel guest and just want a few drinks, there is an $8.00 cover charge with a 1 drink minimum per person. Wi-Fi in the room is horrible! As Marriott Platinum members the Wife is complimentary, so even at no charge, it was bad, could not imagine paying for it.

“Good room for the price” Pear Tree is a good place if you are on a budget and need a room for a good value. This is a slightly older property but still well maintained. The staff is very courteous and helpful. Check in was easy and quick. The hotel is located on 410, not far from Northstar mall. There are a few restaurants close by and a short car ride will get you to many more restaurants. As we were there in the winter we didn't get to try the pool. THE ROOMS - They are pretty roomy and our room had the mini-fridge and microwave. The bed was reasonably comfortable, I wish it was a little softer but for a weekend it will suffice. The bathroom is average sized and like most hotels seems to fog up quickly if you take a hot shower. The floor gets slippery so definately law down a towel to keep you from slipping. CONTINENTAL BREAKFAST - This was the best thing about the hotel. They had a good supply of food. The bagels were fresh and the waffle maker a good touch. It gets packed (especially the waffle maker station)because everyone staying there eats the breakfast so expect a crowd. BUILDING - It was nice and tidy. Not extravagant or posh, but well-maintained and not musty smelling like many Ramadas. It could use some new carpet in the hallways and maybe in the rooms too. However, the carpet is an old style but not dirty or dingy. The building is well insulated from sounds and it was surprisingly quiet. This hotel is a good deal if the price is right. I recommend it if you are looking for a nice room and are not concerned with needing a lot of luxuries.

“Location Makes It Work” I did not choose this hotel. It was the site of a conference that I was attending. I expected not to like it very much, but I was wrong. Yes, it is large and somewhat impersonal. Yes, the Sheraton lacks some charm. But, there was a lot "right" with the hotel. First, it is located right on the river and within walking distance of Michigan Avenue and the Navy Pier. Second, the rooms were decent size with comfortable beds, quality flat TVs, and nice views. Third, for the most part, the staff were accommodating, friendly, and helpful. Fourth, there was a pleasant riverside place to have a coffee or a drink and lots of services from restaurants to business center to Fedex location to even a quality shoe shine service.

“Priced Right for Weekend Getaway” Our room had a king size bed, very comfortable, flat screen..seemed to be newly updated and very roomy. We had a street view, but we're here to see the sights of DC. Very friendly people from the Valet, front desk, bartender, and room service...my only complaint was the loud neighbors with childred who felt the need to slam their door other than that ..the location is great...,you are just a few blocks from the capital and we walked everywhere. BRING COMFY shoes if you like to walk, cabs are nice and the valet will assist in grabbing one for you. If you like spanish tapas, you MUST go to JALEO. My boyfriend and I were in DC to celebrate his 30th b-day and had just an amazing time seeing the sights, going to the muesums and taking in great food and drink on 7th ave. Have fun, enjoy DC and take in our GREAT history..perfect for family and couples and singles (if you're coming by car, there is a fee for overnight parking) I booked throught ORBITZ and felt the price was very fair for the value experienced

“a good return experience” My second stay at this hotel, much like the first the year before - very pleasant old-fashioned environment, good amenities in the room and in the hotel at large, quiet but convenient neighborhood, excellent value for New York. I did request, and was granted, a room facing the street rather than an air duct. Though still the standard room, it was not claustrophobic, and had lots of sitting/ storage/ counter space. I have the same caution about the young desk staff I had last time, though. This time they actually gave me wrong information, both about what was provided in the room and about where the nearest store was. They still need training!

“super Appartment - aber nicht ganz billig” Der Zimmerpreis ist zwar nicht ganz billig, wenn man sich aber ein Appartement mit mehrern Leute teilt, kann sich das trotzdem rechnen. Die Zimmer sind sehr großzügig. Man kann dort locker 4-6 Personen unterbringen. Die meisten Zimmer sind mit einer vollwertigen Küche ausgestattet, so dass man sich auch selbst was kochen kann. Das halte ich allerdings für nicht notwendig bzw. einen Fehler, da in der Umgebung eine Vielzahl guter Restaurants in allen Preisklassen zu finden sind. Überhaupt ist die Lage sehr günstig, da man nicht weit zu nächsten Metro-Station hat auch Central Station als einer der Haupt Verkehrsknotenpunkt ist in 10 Minuten zu Fuß erreicht. Die zentrale Lage kann auch ein Nachteil sein,wenn man lärm-empfindlich ist. Ich empfehle einer Zimmer in den oberen Etagen oder nicht zu Straße hin (dann hat man aber auch weniger Tageslicht - ist halt ein Kompromiss). Im Hotel gibt es auch eine kleine nette Lounge mit freiem Internet Zugang und täglich einer "Happy-Hour" mit kostenlosen Getränken und Snacks. Sehr positiv ist auch das Personal das immer sehr freundlich ist.

“Best service by far” I recently stayed at the Sheraton for two nights while attending a conference in Phoenix. I was blown away by the services. This is by far the best service I have received while staying at a hotel in recent years. I received a room on the 15 floor. Room was what you expect from Sheraton. The view from the room really sucked!! I got the room with a view of the hotel satellite and communications towers. TV quality was good and room had Starbucks coffee. Room also came with a refrigerator. I would like to see Sheraton move to Nespresso machines. After a long day attending a conference was great to relax at the hotel lobby bar. The desserts are yummy. I didn’t get a chance to try the restaurants in the hotel. Hooters and Starbucks are directly across the street. My work colleague used the gym. He said the pool was really nice and gym had everything you need. Next time!!! Wireless worked well. Wireless should be free. I would definitely stay here again!!

“Not bad” We got this hotel on Hotwire for $65. The room was clean and comfortable, with a mini fridge. The wifi was a little slow, but it worked. The breakfast had a lot of good choices. The only thing I would change is the location of our room - we were right next to the elevator and heard a lot of loud conversation. Kids traveling for a soccer tournament and a gymnastics meet were there at the same time - at least they weren't loud all night.

“Nice hotel behind the Coke sign.” My sister and I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. The Renaissance is a nice hotel in the middle of Times Square. The rooms are an ok size for NYC, although the bathroom is a bit old and small. This hotel is very convenient to everything from the subway to the shops and of course Times Square. I have stayed at a few different hotels in Times Square, whilst this hotel is not my favourite of the ones I have stayed at (loved the size of the Doubletree Suites) it is still a good choice and was great value for money at the time we stayed. The location of the property does make it feel a bit like you are staying in the middle of the road which for me was a bit weird but the convenience made up for that. The staff were friendly and helpful so this property is definitely one to consider if you are coming to Times Square.

“A little over the top...and a few trip-ups” I stayed here for a business trip, arriving late after a long day of travel...i hadn't been the one who booked the hotel so was not expecting the atmosphere or decor...i found it to be a blast to the senses and not very relaxing....so in other words not of my taste. The room was fine, not particularly upscale, though functional. I was very disappointed in the lack of water pressure in the shower, and the lack of timely room service. i'd ordered a few items, hoping to get a late meal, only to be called back much later that my items were unavailable. the front desk tried to make amends but it was very disappointing to not have gotten timely service. one more thing, the hotel sits on a residential street so it is inconvenient to get a cab walking out the front door.
“Genuine staff” Great staff....really feel they look after you... Rooms wonderfull,cosy and clean Free good coffee,and wine hour

“Un buon indirizzo per visitare Manhattan” Abbiamo soggiornato di recente in questo hotel che pur non avendo un gradevole aspetto esterno, si è rivelato una buona struttura. Camere non molto spaziose (ma a Manhattan è la regola), ma pulite e curate. Colazione compresa nel costo della camera, di buon livello. La posizione non è centralissima, ma si può raggiungere Time Square in 15-20 minuti a piedi, o più comodamente prendendo l'autobus n. 11 che passa sulla 10th Ave davanti al Duane Reade e cambiando sulla 42th st, prendendo il 42. Abbiamo apprezzato soprattutto la comodità dei letti e la silenziosità della zona nelle ore notturne. Il personale della hall si è rivelato gentile e disponibile.

“Great, roomy suites - Omni Loyalty program is terrific!” If you hate small hotel rooms lacking amenities in the so-called "fancy" Chicago hotels (like the Drake and Knickerbocker -- and I've stayed in both), you will love the Omni. The suite had two TVs (bedroom and living room), a desk, closing doors to the bedroom, nice bar area and vanity. Also the Omni Loyalty program, which you can join for free, provides real benefits, like free internet, a bottle of water, and a breakfast beverage delivered to your room. Very nice service here as well. The only thing the Omni lacks is one of those grand lobbies. You actually take the elevator from the ground level to the lovely check-in lobby. This is now my hotel of choice in Chicago and I'm looking forward to trying it elsewhere. It is so nice to stay at a hotel where they understand that providing good service and not charging for every service is a way to keep your customers.

“Perfect location and lovely spa” My girls and I stayed there while we were visiting Seattle to tour the UW. We were able to walk everywhere in the city (except to the UW). The room was nice. I really liked the comfortable furinishings and the bathroom was very well appointed with nice products and decor. The pool was very nice...salt water. My only complaint was that we had noisy neighbors with small children, but that cannot be helped. Also, the elevator call tone was loud enough for me to hear it in my room, so next time I will request a room further away from the elevator. I still give it five perfect stars because it really was a great stay!

“Classic, Convenient and Cool” Normally, I would not stay at hotel this ridiculously expensive ($350+taxes) but since it was for work, everything else was booked, and the boss pre-approved the expense there I was checking into one of the nicest hotels in Boston. The hotel is gorgeous, rooms spotless and elegant without being overly gaudy. Lobby had plenty of seating for quick meetings or private calls. The bar soap/shampoo was top of the line! (With airline “carry on” baggage rules it’s just easier NOT to pack those items and use the hotel offerings for these over night trips.) Being a young business traveler, and looking younger, the staff was a bit more relaxed with the formalities. The kindly noted that I dislike being referred to by my last name. I'm giving this a 5 star review b/c it deserves it. But I will note a few odd things that could have really annoyed some guests paying out of pocket. First, as I was washing my hands in the bathroom sink the water kept filling up. Apparently, the stopper came off from the hinge in the down position. I had to go under the sink and push it up. Second, the bedside clock (which was an iPod/mp3 docking and charging station!) was set to the wrong time. For the life of me, I couldn’t figure out how to change the time! I got back to my room so late I just wanted to sleep in the compfy king size bed, so I used my blackberry for the clock during the night and requested a wake up call. For a business traveler this is a very comfortable hotel. Laptop/internet hook-ups in the room. But for all the money you spend (as a tourist) there is no free business center to check emails or even a free cup of coffee in the morning. You’re paying for ambiance...and you’re getting it. But you’ll also pay for everything else. (Except the complimentary NY Times left at your door in the morning!) Note: I did have a friend lucky enough to get this hotel on Hotwire over the summer for an amazing deal!

“The Long and Winding Road” Stayed at the Hilton in early December 2011. Booked a "Garden View" room and not realizing that it took over 5 minutes to walk from Lobby to the room itself. The hotel is only about 4 storeys high, and the numbering of the rooms basically reads "1" + "floor" + "room number (on that floor)". If you have a lot of luggage with you, I highly suggest that you emphasize on getting a room closer to the entrance. I had 5 pieces of luggage as I checked in, and the receptionist handling the check-in assigned one of the furthest rooms possible which took me over 7 minutes to push the luggage trolley all the way to my room. After getting all my luggage into the room, which I'd expected to be a larger size considering I was supposed to be paying for a "deluxe garden view" (the room is smaller than what you would find in a Hampton Inn), I headed out to get food as their restaurant was closed. Along the way I asked the receptionist why I was given a room so far away when I had all that luggage. The girl just frowned and said the hotel was fully booked and that I should have made the request earlier. When I told her that I had requested - as I booked on-line - that the room not be far from the elevator, she then said "can I send someone to help you then?" Being a Hilton Gold VIP member, I am entitled to either a free upgrade (where available), or breakfast, or a 1000 points HHonors bonus. I had an early flight out so I skipped breakfast. Upon check-out I asked if she would note on the bill that I should get the 1000 points, and the girl (a different undertrained person) looks at me and smiles as she recites, "oh, just tell the Hilton Hhonors people that you didn't have breakfast and they should give you the miles." What Hilton Hhonors people? It was unfortunate that I didn't have time to speak to her more, but perhaps that's a blessing as I don't think it would have helped me, but possibly only help her learn that I don't work for Hilton, nor are there Hilton Hhonors people standing around me to hear a plea about me not having breakfast at one of their lesser properties so they award me with 1000 miles. Being a Gold VIP member, and having to deal with this kind of lack of service, I don't recommend staying at this hotel unless you're travelling with over 400 other people and all of you want to stay in the same property. While the hotel is very near the airport, and that right out the back-door of the property is the lightrail stop, downtown Seattle is not 15 minutes a ride away as their website claims. The best thing I have to say about this hotel would be the shuttle bus drivers as they were the most helpful of the lot.

“Pleasant stay, nice staff, average establishment” There's nothing particularly remarkable about this hotel. It's a neat, clean, cookie cutter TownePlace Suites hotel by Marriott. The staff was very friendly. Kudo's to them for helping my stay a good one. Another reviewer stated it quite well, it's a Fairfield Inn with a kitchette. It's a less expensive Marriott Residence Inn without the hot free breakfast. My only complaints about this establishment are placement of the flatscreen TV on the half wall between the bed and the kitchenette (I walked into it in the dark and thought I nearly ripped it off the wall); noise transmission between the rooms (yes, that's code words for thin walls); and a shower head that's mounted low on the wall (beyond eye level...and I'm only 6 feet tall). It's convenient to a couple of decent restaurants next door. Easy access to Mo-Pac highway and any location in Austin.

“Top o' the World” Perched atop SF's famous Nobb Hill, the Fairmont San Francisco's views are incredible. Walk down one direction and you're in Union Square, walk in the other direction and you're staring at Alcatraz from fisherman's wharf. I would absolutely return. Best Parts - location. in the centre of everything you'd want to see and experience in SF. - the tonga room. the hotel's tiki lounge is reminiscent of a glamorous time. set around the hotel's old (1930's) indoor pool. the tiki band plays on a boat floating on this old pool. - hotel is old, but rooms have been nicely updated Know this - no pool - the climb up to this hotel is significant. if you are wearing nice shoes or want a break, take a cable car. - free internet if you join fairmont's loyalty program

“No, thank you.” I stayed here for a night. Wow, really not nice. Small room. Felt dirty. Stained. Grungy. Towels were like sand paper. I think a 13 inch television. I would never recommend this hotel.

“Rather nice boutiquish hotel” Fashion 26 is located on W. 26th, a few steps from 7th Ave. not really within walking distance of midtown, but quite near the 28th St. stop on the 7th Ave. line. It has a boutique feel, but, given its 22 or 23 stories, it isn't really. Its dining room, Rare, serves a really nice lunch for an average price (for NYC). It has a rooftop bar (covered in winter, of course) that's quite pleasant. The rooms are small but nicely appointed. The TV is one of the few hotel TV's nationwide that really does have HD, although it offers only 17 channel, which is strange, given that NYC cable TV offers more than 100 channels. There was no pen or paper at the room's desk, and it wasn't replaced even after I mentioned this to the staff. I was on the 19th floor, and cell phone reception there was lousy. The reception staff is clearly a bit small and can be overwhelmed by guests checking in and checking out, resulting in delays. The hotel's checkin time is 3:00 PM, but they allowed me to check in at 10:00 AM without complaint. The internet speed was 1;8 M/sec. That is good enough for checking emails and the like, but not enough for serious use. (Why do guests tolerate hotels choking down internet service like that?) It can be expensive though, depending upon the season. All in all, I liked it.

“Loved this hotel- great experience” I stayed here for one night for business and it was wonderful. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The rooms are incredible! Flat screen tv, awesome decor, COMFORTABLE bed, beautiful marble sink, coffee maker, large dresser, huge desk, overstuffed chair and footrest. Easy to use alarm clock, lights by the bed on the wall with outlets - which is always nice for charging cell phones, etc. Ate at the restaurant and the waiters were great and the food was pretty good. Overall, a great experience - wish I could have stayed longer.

“The Liberty pays homage to its past” As someone who lived two blocks from this property in it's former life as the Charles Street Jail, it was a distinctive and unique opportunity staying here. The interior public areas reflect those of the original building in a quite attractive way. The lobby is an amazing spot when the bar scene gets going, the Saturday night we stayed, it was jam packed. While we had a fantastic dinner in the restaurant on the lower level, Scampo, the noise level in this fully occupied restaurant made it very difficult to have a conversation with my dinner companion. Also, the lighting made it quite difficult to read the menu, thankfully we were given extra candles, which helped somewhat. Our room was modest in size, the furnishings attractive, but despite being a part of the "Luxury Collection", it did not feel up to that designation in our room.

“Pleaseant surprise” Came here with colleagues on a business trip. I'm from Memphis but had never stayed here and was impressed with the stay. It was a bit busy when we checked in and our helper was somewhat overwhelmed. However, the other two workers helped us out and were very pleasant, engaging, and professional. The room was nice, bigger than expected. I have NO COMPLAINTS about this hotel. Great location downtown too. I definitely recommend staying here.

“Business travel” Stayed one night at the Westin Copley. Corporate rate but reasonable by Boston standards. Clean, up to date room. Only complaint was lack of plugs at desk area. Many electronics to plug in. Breakfast at Hotel restaurant was good but pricey as most are. Would return on next trip to area.

“Good choice in Times square area” My husband and I stayed here for one night earlier this month. The location is a short walk from Times Square, but away from the hussle and bustle, and down the street from a nice grocery store. (The Food Emporium). Our room was large and clean, except for the rug which could have used a shampoo or needed to be replaced. Breakfast was okay, nothing special, but I liked the fact that coffee and tea was served all day. I also saw a bowl of apples. What sets this hotel apart, beyond the size of the room and location, is the staff, who were very friendly and helpful. They get an extra star just for that.

“Modern, fresh, and elegant” Our 10th floor room was well-appointed with an incredible view of the city. The bathroom was modern and sleek, with a frosted glass sliding door and all new fixtures.
