Be aware that the glossy tiled floors are slippery when wet. Put a towel down for traction. We were able to have breakfast in the Executive Lounge each morning before setting off into the city. There was a wonderful variety of food and beverages laid out beautifully. Traveling with one adult, one teen, and a toddler, we were glad to find a selection of items appropriate for each of us. The valet staff was very responsive and patient, even when we needed to get into our car to find some missing Halloween costumes. The gentleman who waited with me was a great conversationalist as I tore through suitcases to find an item. And the cold citrus water near the lobby entry was refreshing after a long day sightseeing. The only unfortunate encounters were with the security staff. Once, a security staffer rolled his eyes and refused to answer when we asked him a question. Another time, a guard hinted we should leave the elevator as he brought on a VIP. If he had outright asked us to leave for security reasons, we would have left. But he instead made a snide comment that we should get off because he was going up to the Executive Floor. Well, so were we. This VIP got to ride up with our family and guess what, he survived his encounter with the hoi polloi. Interactions with *all* guests should meet a minimum standard of courtesy, no matter what their rank or title. Overall, our experience was positive, and I would stay again at the Washington Hilton. We are loyal Hilton guests and Diamond Elite members with over 100 nights per year at Hilton properties across the country -- this is a lovely property that we recommend wholeheartedly.

“Very nice hotel” We arrived at 9:30am and were cheerfully allowed to check in. A king bed was reserved, but switching to 2 beds was no trouble either. Even though we were right next to the elevator, we never heard it or another guest. The room temperature was easily controlled. HDTV was perfect. We did the obligatory bedbug check, practically undressing both beds and the mattresses were clean as a whistle - in fact they could have been brand new they were so clean. The bathroom was bright and roomy. The towels were large, plentiful and plush. It was a great stay! Nice room, friendly service, good location.

“Okay, but pricey” I stayed for 3 nights recently at the Hyatt Mission Bay resort in San Diego. I wasn't sure what to expect as had read some bad reviews on this site. I guess I was pleasantly surprised - the hotel was attractive, rooms nice, clean, pretty views, and great vegetation - lovely lush greenery, well maintained. On the downside, rooms were expensive and the on-site restaurant equally so. We ate a couple of cheap fish meals at the fish-fry place within walking distance along the marina. Even the wine wasn't too bad there for $3 a glass! I didn't have time to get into the pool but it looked nice and there were some nice poolside areas. The staff was helpful and welcoming. Internet connection in the room was expensive but reliable; they had a very roomy business centre where you could print your boarding pass free - useful. their conference catering, set-up and food were all fine. Being a northerner, I enjoyed the ease of drifting from indoors to outdoors for meetings and networking. Overall, though, not sure it was worth the $200+ nightly rate and it was also out of the way, requiring a $12-15 cab ride to get anywhere in the main part of town. Morning sun glistening on the marina waters is a sight that will stay with me though!

“Loved our experience here” We chose this hotel for it's location to the Hippodrome Theatre which is literally 1 block away. We do not think the area that the hotel is located in is "shady" at all. We live in MD and are familiar with what constitutes as "shady" in Charm City. We had a great time walking to the Theatre, and since we booked a romance package, the front desk had chilled Champagne and chocolate covered strawberries waiting for us in our room. We paid only $150.00 a night and it was well worth it. The deal included the romance plus dinner and breakfast at the hotel cafe. Our meals were great and a fun time was had. I highly reccomend this hotel during baseball season since our room had an outstanding view of Camden Yard. I can only imagine what it would be like with the stadium lit up.

“Está bien, podría ser mejor si el servicio mejora.” Está clasificado 4* aunque hay detalles que creo que no le hacen estar a esa altura. Es un hotel inagurado en Febrero de 2010. Está situado en la 37th st. entre la 5a y la 6a Av. En el lobby se encuentra la recepción y una pequeña zona de sofás. Los recepcionistas fueron muy amables y hablan español. Un problema que le veo al hotel es que sólo dispone de 2 ascensores y son lentísimos. El edificio tiene 20 plantas y normalmente se tiene que esperar bastante al ascensor. Tampoco dispone de ascensor de servicio y a veces te encuentras con los trabajadores cargados con la ropa o la basura... eso a mí no me molesta pero la verdad es que se ve raro Nos han dado una habitación en la planta 12. La habitación es pequeña, enmoquetada y con una cama muy grande. Hay un armario enano con 8 perchas. Dentro del armario también está la caja de seguridad, el secador del pelo, la plancha y la tabla de planchar. La tele es plana y también hay un puerto para el I-pod. El baño es también muy pequeño, aunque luce porque es todo nuevecito. Se compone del lavabo, el WC y una ducha grande. De amenities sólo ponen gel, champú y body milk. El minibar es de estos modernos dónde se carga la consumición en el momento que tomas el producto. No hay espacio para poner algo que traigas tú de fuera. Hay wifi gratuito, aunque la conexión no es buena. Nosotros pedimos el cable para conectar y sin problemas nos lo trajeron y así hay mejor conexión. El desayuno es un cachondeo. Está incluído en la tarifa y está situado provisionalmente ( a la espera que acaben las obras del restaurante) en la planta -1. Están las mesas bastante juntas ya que la sala no es demasiado grande. El desayuno es bueno, pero la saturación de gente en el espacio reducido lo torna en una aventura el conseguir una rebanada de pan Hay diferentes panes, bagels, muffins, cruasans, bocadillitos... También quesos, embutidos y huevos duros. Frutas, yogurts, cereales. De bebidas hay cafes, tes, leche y zumo de naranja ( que aunque no es natural está bueno). El desayuno se sirve de 7 a 10 de la mañana. Tiene un roof bar en la planta 21 con buenas vistas al Empire. El techo es trasparente y supongo que de cara la buen tiempo lo deben abrir para hacer una bonita terraza. Los precios de las consumiciones rondan los 10-15$

“We loved it!” The view was awesome! The rooms were good sized. It's an all suite hotel with one bedroom, a living room with a pullout, and a kitchenette. Steps from shopping and restaurants and Quincy Market. Short walk to the subway and harbor. One bonus was the mini-concerts/shows at night. After dinner, we would sit and relax with one free complimantary drink. Conveniently located. We walked everywhere (historical district) and when we got tired, walking back to the hotel was easy enough. The subway was also right across the street. There's a convenient store close by as well.

“Got a deal on Hotwire, Pleasantly surprised” Great deal on hotwire ... Bed was soo comfortable, room was clean, the only downside was that our view was of construction and another building ... guess that's why we got the great deal. We weren't in the room that much so it was alright. Also our TV was not working and it took 3 hours for somebody to take a look at it.

“Beautiful Old Hotel located in the loop.” There are times when we prefer to stay in the loop over the Magnificent mile, and at those times, this is the perfect location. It is only a couple blocks from the old Macy's, and easily accessible to all 'L' lines. We arrived at 10:30, and made a special room request, which the desk clerk said he could easily honor, but that we'd have to wait to check in until 2:00pm. This was not a problem, and we enjoyed Chicago activities until 2:00pm. The desk clerk knew nothing about our previous arrangements, but said he could help us. He said we'd have to wait no longer than 45 minutes for our room, and that they were already cleaning it. We returned to the desk at 2:45pm, and again the clerk knew anything about our previous arrangements. She apologized and actually made work of finding us a room. By 4:30pm, we were finally checking in. I felt like the first two clerks had just tried to get rid of us, but the third clerk was amazing. We were granted our request, and were pleased with it. I must say though, that the last 45 minutes dragged a bit as we waited in the Lobby with our grandchildren. A second inconvenience was a large wedding that was celebrating in the entry, and made it impossible to get through. I'd have expected the hotel to rope off a path for incoming and outgoing patrons. Having said that, this is a beautiful hotel. We've visited it often and love the lobby. When you register, or make your reservation, be sure you aren't getting a small room. While a large room isn't necessary, the small rooms here have barely enough room to walk between the bed and other furniture. I'd not give the small rooms a 4 star rating. The larger rooms however, and nicely decorated and very pleasant. The staff varies widely from the best ever to below average. I've not read other reviews, but I'd guess the reaction to the hotel varies greatly. I'd love to see this beautiful old hotel return to the excellence it once enjoyed, but budget cuts may make this difficult. When you stay here, be sure to visit the new beautiful Millennium Park, the Cajun restaurant, heaven on seven at 111 N. Wabash, and visit the cultural center on Michigan Ave, between Randolph and Washington to learn about attractions available during your visit.

“good hotel with some issues\” was scared of the reviews about the size of the room, but we got a decent sized king bed room. had enough space for rather large luggage. bed was ok. feel a bit worn as it was mushed near the waist area. the closet was too small. the bathroom was oddly big compare to the rest of the room. great pressure, but the shower curtain kinda threw me off. not nice. could have used a ref in the room. coffee and tea was available in the morning at the lobby. valet took a long time when you wanted the car. the concierge was very nice and friendly, front desk not rude, but generally disinterested. also had housekeeping knock at 830 am on a sunday, which was annoying. all in all, good with tiny service issues, and some minor refurbishments needed.

“Value for money in New York” Stayed with my family for a week in February. Things we liked: Location - 8th Ave near to many attractions and the subway. Staff - Very pleasant welcome from the front desk Complimentary Breakfast - very convenient when getting 2 small children fed in the mornings Room - Very comfortable beds, spacious living area (for NY), kept clean daily Complimentary coffees, cookies and apples round the clock Free internet access - I picked up the wireles signal from 2nd floor, otherwise would have used ethernet connection The price - considering the location and comfort on offer - this is my fourth trip to NY and this place takes some beating Could have improved: We had no view to speak of with the room and the rumble of the subway was detectable, but not really a major nuisance Some of the fixtures and fittings around the place are showing their age, but again not a big issue Dining: If you arrive and need a quick eat (take away/delivery) look no further than directly opposite the hotel at Ray's Pizza - really very good indeed for everything and always busy. Even the likes of John Travolta and Keanu Reeves have been known to drop by, the photos are there to prove it! Other nearby local eats for those with young children include Ellen's Stardust Diner complete with singing waiting staff. Mars 2112 (the food ain't great, but the kids still remember the experience fondly. The Carnegie Deli, check of the "Woody Allen" sandwich, but leave room for the famous cheesecake because it's the best. I would also recommend a trip down to Lombardi's in Little Italy just at the junction of Spring/Mulberry, always great Pizza and atmosphere. Out and about: For sightseeing with the kids, a trip on the Q out to Coney Island, Brooklyn, to the Aquarium is a fun day out. Top of the Rock(efeller Centre) beats the Empire State. Central Park Zoo is always good as is the rest of the park (we were fortunate to get plenty of snow). American Museum of Natural History with it's awesome dinosaur exhibits and the Hayden Planetarium. Disembarking the ferry at Ellis Island is more rewarding than Liberty Island. Shopping: Macys is great, but the place is huge so take regular breaks at the cafes on each of the floors and don't forget your tourists discount card at the visitor centre. Bloomingdales also operate a tourist discount card. If Dept stores are not your thing, just walking along 5th Ave, you'll see lots of upscale and everyday outlets. For the small ones, shopping at FAO Schwarz and of course the enormous Toys R Us in Times Square should round things off nicely. You can always stop for a delicious Hot Chocolate and pastry at the former in the imaginatively named FAO Schweetz !

“Could be worse, could be better” This is a downtown hotel with a downtown price and a recognizable name, so expectations tend to be fairly high. In some ways it's good, but overall it left me cold. The location is across from the minor-league ballpark, a couple of blocks from Beale Street, and about a half-mile from the convention center. Needless to say there are a ton of great restaurants within walking distance (I recommend the Texas de Brazil). There is the usual rip-off valet fee ($20/night) that you expect in downtown hotels, but at least they give you unlimited ins and outs, and it's the same at all the big hotels in Memphis. Be warned, they don't have enough valets so in the morning you'll wait a while to get your car, and in the evening there is a line of cars on the street waiting to get in to the overly small driveway. Check-in is fast and friendly with a complimentary warm cookie. The hotel is an inner-courtyard style, with glass elevators and a nice area to meet with your colleagues. It seems to be either a renovated old hotel, or an homage to some old-time hotel. There is a TGI Fridays off the lobby, which is unremarkable except that they give you a coupon for a complimentary breakfast buffet there each morning, and it is excellent. There's even an omelette guy. Upstairs, the hallway carpets are kind of worn and decrepit. The room door was very hard to open probably due to swelling in the humidity, but when I complained they fixed it right away. The room was very small but had a kind of elegant/modern/deco decor to it. The bed was comfortable, but the 7 assorted pillows all flattened to nothing when you put your head to them. The A/C was effective but had some annoying clicks when it kicked on and off. The bath amenities were very nice. The wireless internet worked very well, and while there were very few outlets in the room, there was one on the work desk which was nice. There was a flat-screen TV, but there were only like 10 channels, and not the ones you'd expect. Translation: have stuff for the kids to do, cause the TV isn't going to occupy them. The room was clean, but the window situation ... there were horizontal wood blinds that had no open/close control (it was broken off); there were drapes, but the pull-thing to open and close them was broken off and laying on the window sill; and there was a disgusting old towel stuffed in around the window frame. So, overall I'd say it's "okay" but not great; I'd stay here again but only if the company was paying for it.

“An experience back in time” Spent three days at the Alexis in early June. The hotel is located in a great location, near Pike Place Market and Pioneer Square. Lots of touristy things to do within walking distance of the hotel. The Alexis has a historic feel, but is extremely well maintained. The staff was very helpful and friendly. We enjoyed our large room with a very comfortable bed. I'm not usually a fan of boutique hotels, but the Alexis was a perfect fit for a visit to Old Seattle.

“Perfect!” Spacious, spotless clean room! My favorite feature--a bathroom dimmer switch--you can leave the light on without lighting up the whole room. Friendly, efficient service. Our favorite at this hotel though...the wine hour! Fabulous sangria takes the edge off of a long day of driving or whatever. This is our favorite place to stay in Phila!

“Perfect Location To Explore New York City” We stayed in this hotel for four nights and it is in such a great location that we were able to explore all of Manhattan. Only two blocks to Times Square and most subway lines within a few blocks. The hotel is nice but no frills and well worth the price. Breakfast had a large selection to choose from including eggs, bacon, sausage and waffels. They will store your luggage for early arrival or late departure. Would definitely stay here again.

“Small but clean, friendly staff, close to Northwestern Law” We were very pleased with the staff who were helpful with our many questions as first time visitors to Chicago. The room was small but clean and the internet service was free and fast. The proximity to Northwestern Law and the downtown Chicago area, including Navy Pier made this a great location with good value for the price. We would definitely stay again. The breakfast was included and had good variety (waffles, cereals, fruit, bagels, yogurts, etc.)

“Best free breakfast” The most impressive thing about my stay at this Residence Inn was the free breakfast - it was far superior to any other area hotel (or any others that I can think of period). Potato pancakes! I also had the good fortune to stay on a night when they had what I think they called a manager's reception, or maybe it was just a beer night. Anyway, they were serving good beer and BBQ sandwiches. So I didn't need to eat out, but if you do, there are plenty of options in the adjacent shopping areas (I recommend China Fun across the street). My room was large and clean, with good TV's (I seem to recall they were upgrading to FIOS or something like that at the time, so the channel selection should be improved by now). The price range is a bit higher than other hotels in the area, and also as far as I could tell there was no wifi internet, only wired.

“Can't beat it... BEST place in NYC” I've stayed here before and wanted to bring my husband back to celebrate our 8th anniversary. We had a 11th floor corner king. What a GREAT stay. Without exception, every single person who worked here gave us flawless service - warm, professional, responsive, friendly. That's hard to achieve for a hotel, and I'm generally a very picky consumer. We had dinner at Gemma's twice, and the food was fantastic. It was a most wonderful stay and HB is now our "go to" place when we're in NYC. We've stayed at Blue Moon, Waldorf, and used airbnb for apartments, which is great when we bring our kids. But if it's just the two of us, Bowery Hotel can't be beat. Thanks to the staff for a wonderful job!

“Great 4 night stay” My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights over the New Years holiday. I agree with the positive reviews below on the details. First class experience the whole way. Yes, the hotel can seem almost overly stylish (typical W), but we as not overly stylish people never felt out of place. And the entire staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel is on a truly quiet residential block, but we could easily walk to the restaurants, cafes and shops of Westwood Village. Finally, we loved the central location: easy to drive to all the L.A. sights and hotspots, then return to our hip oasis.

“Another Fantastic Stay at the Back Bay Hilton” I was a frequent visitor of the Hilton Back Bay when I traveled to Boston for work frequently several years ago. Recently I had an opportunity to return to Boston and stay at a long time favorite hotel in Boston for three nights with my wife. Once again the stay was fantastic. The thing that always sets an hotel apart for me is the staff, at the end of the day lots of hotels in Boston are similar to the Hilton, but the staff takes very good care of you here. One example was when I was returning to the hotel at night and because of a party there were no parking spots. The doorman talked to the manager and found us a spot in the "permit" parking area, going out of their way to assist us. The rooms have been recently renovated and were very nice. They were a good size, very comfortable bed, sofa, desk area and HDTV. I liked the updates to the room with the exception that they have bolted the balcony doors closed so you can't go out anymore. One thing I do like about the rooms however is you can open the window for fresh air which is rare downtown and something I always appreciate. The hotel is a perfect size, not monolithic and crowded like some of the surrounding hotels so you never feel crowded. They have a great workout area and indoor pool and a starbucks in the lobby. The location of the hotel is perfect for getting around, just across from the Pru Center. Always look forward to returning to this long time favorite.

“WOW WHAT A GREAT RENOVATION JOB!” I was amazed at the beautiful room with new everything!!!!! It is sooooo much better now than it was before!!!!! Great going!!!!! Isabella is so sweet, helpful and a great people person!!! I love it when I feel like I'm coming home to family because the folks at the front desk treat you so beautifully! You are such an asset in hotel business, Isabella and a joy for all of us who stay there. The gentleman on the night shift was finely dressed and wonderful as well. This is a first class establishment now, thanks to all the fine folks who work here and the fine accommodations! Blessings to you all!

“A great addition to TriBeCa” This is a very nice hotel. A smallish, boutique-style hotel similar to a lot of others that have been popping up in NYC over the last couple of years. I like this one a lot. It's a mix of new, modern flat-surface styling and old, worn furniture. Very nicely done. I had a nice corner room with plenty of light. Staff was nice and efficient. Location is brilliant if you like TriBeCa and work Downtown (like I do). My favorite detail was the rock radio station blasting when I returned to my room. Wireless internet didn't reach my room and I do feel it was a tad too expensive, but I would definitely recommend it and I will most likely come back.

“Small cousy hotel in Georgetown” Small Cousy hotel in Georgetown. Perfect location, nice rooms, friendly staff, valet parking and light breakfast included. Free wifi access. Located close to M street where you will find small antique shops, restaurants and pubs. Nicely decorated rooms, king size bed, nice bathroom. I think I paid around $ 180 pr. Night which I think was reasonable. Have stayed there twice for business, but the hotel is a good choice for couples as well.

“Outstanding hospitality, live up the reputation” Front desk folks consistently were extremely helpful, patient, and knowledgeable. From the front door to the concierge, we were really impressed with their professionalism. Will be back again.

“New Construction, big rooms, service-friendly staff” This Courtyard is pretty new construction and is very up-to-date. They have a wide selection of available snacks for purchase, a nice breakfast area serving evening faire as well. Even though I booked the room on my credit card points, somehow my reservation was still matched up with my Gold Marriott Rewards status, and was thanked at check-in for staying with Marriott hotels on a frequent basis (nice touch). Nice LG flatscreen TVs in the rooms, although most channels were analog rather than digital. The free "highspeed" internet could seriously use improvement - it's slow to the point of borderline useless at time. It seems to "take naps" and go totally non-responsive, and then it will start working again. I had to access my email through the web email application rather than Outlook. I stay in this area very frequently, booking rooms through a couple of popular on-line booking sites, and have seen a very noticeable increase in vandalism and burglary of cars in the hotel parking lots in the City View area, so be sure to try parking near the front doors of the hotel, or at least in an area with security camera coverage.

“Decent hotel” Went to this hotel for a concert at the Verizon Center, which is about 15 minutes away. I travel alot and for the price we paid ($90), which is a steal for a Hitlon. Overall the Hotel is clean and the rooms are average and comfortable. A few minor issues : 1) we could hear almost ANY noise the kids in the room next to us made all night. 2) $9.95 for internet, I mean, really? I guess I am just surprise these days when hotels still charge for interent...not that $10 is an issue, its just the point. 3) Elevators are super slow It has a decent location to restaraunts and there was a pretty large mall just a couple minutes away. If you are going to a concert in the area or need to be in the part of town, this hotel is just fine.

“Average Sheraton, One of Downtown's Good Deals” I stayed at this Sheraton approximately 5 weeks sporadically from Apr - Sep 2008. I never had a bad experience and enjoyed the amenities. It's exactly what you would expect from a newer Sheraton. The hotel recently (within few years) renovated and went through a brand change to Sheraton, and they did a good job with the decor and comfort. I stayed in a variety of rooms including a suite and every time they were outstanding. You're not going to get the bright modern look of a Westin, but you do get the modern decor and comfort you'd expect from a newer Sheraton. The elevators can be slow at times, but only during peak periods. There is not fitness center, but you do have access to the Bally's next door... however that is a bit outdated. The rooms are nice and clean, and you don't have the issue of running into an old stinky outdated room that you could find at the Westin Bonaventure. If you are an SPG member and need to stay in Downtown, I'd recommend the Sheraton over the Westin for its consistent performance and great staff. Compared to some of the other Downtown hotels, you are a bit closer to some of the seedy areas, but I was never worried.

“Great Room & Location” Spent one night at the Willows. The staff was very helpful. Needed to stay past regular checkout time and the staff was very accommodating They even let us stay in the parking garage at no extra cost. The continental breakfast has a nice variety of cereals, bagels, breakfast sandwichs and juice. The location is in a nice residential area and very quiet.

“One of the nicest largest suites in a simply gorgeous and grant hotel.” My family recently stayed at the Drake and frequently make Chicago trips). We stayed in room 511 (a family suite) and I swear it must have been at least 800 square feet! It was absolutely gorgeous! It was a corner looking out on Michigan Ave. My husband and our 2 kids (ages 8 and 14) stayed two nights in January. This hotel is a gem. It is magnificent and did not look the least bit shabby. It's old, certainly, but it is grand and old in a good way, nice architecture, crown molding, etc. We ordered from GrubHub Thai food and ate it in the room - what fun! We also received full breakfast with the suite. We had a king bed and a sofa bed, but they also brought an extra nice large rollaway for one of the kids as well as 2 extra feather duvets. I was a bit worried after having read some reviews nut was so pleasantly surprised by everything. The TV is free on regular channels and there are many many channels, but the internet is $12.95 and is only available wired, which is fairly common and was not a disappointment to me - just info for you. The breakfast buffet was fantastic! If you are accustomed to Ponderosa then go somewhere else. This is a gourmet buffet with smoked salmon and capers! Of course they do have the standard scrambled eggs and bacon also, as well as muffins, pastries, fruits, cheeses, yoghurts, cold cuts, cereals, pancakes, Nutella, peanut butter, juices and etc. Loved it! The staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome. Anything we needed we were greeted with a can-do attitude. I even went off and accidentally left my train tickets in the room ($160!) after having checked out and when I called, Cynthia from housekeeping went and found them for me! I am surprised anyone even made the effort at such a large hotel. Believe me this is not the first time I have left something at a hotel but it is the first time the staff at a hotel cared to find my item. I won't soon forget this hospitality. We have recently stayed at the Sofitel, Dana Spa, Monaco, Rafaello (lost PJs there), all in Chicago, and now I feel my loyalty should be at the Drake and when possible we will stay there from now on. THANK YOU AGAIN CYNTHIA!!!!!

“Loved the place!” I usually prefer staying on the West Side because most of the places I go are there, but I had to go and add downtown to the Priceline location list and voila. I was a little nervous that the East Houston would be too out of the way, but with a subway stop right around the corner that could bring me right to Herald Square, the worries evaporated. As for the hotel itself, I loved it. I was in Room 205 and I don't know if is was bigger or laid out differently because it was a wheelchair accessible room, but I found it quite comfortable. The bathroom was cavernous and while the lighting was a little iffy, I didn't mind. The continental breakfast in the basement was the usual assortment of muffins, breads, cereals, fruits and yogurts, but it certainly did the trick both mornings I was there and there's access to water, coffee and tea all day. There was also a Whole Foods about two blocks down the street that I used to good advantage. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Mostly good, some things to consider” We stayed here over New Year's Eve, wanting to be down in the thick of things for the festivities and weren't disappointed. The location is superb and our compliments to the doormen for pointing out the $30/day parking behind the hotel. (The Hyatt charges $50/day) We stayed in the West tower, 17th floor. The room was nice and when we checked in they offered an upgrade for $20 to a room with a "water" view, which we took. This is probably NOT worth doing as it's just a slice of the river if you angle your head to one side. Not much to see. FYI- The west tower is the one to be in on NYE. The main building had some traucous party going on and all guests to he hotel had to wear wristbands to show that they were staying in the hotel. Things were much quieter in the west tower, where we were happy to get a good night's sleep after walking back from the fireworks at the Navy Pier. Yep, the pier is a close walk.

“Good Hotel Choice” We stayed at the Beverly Garland Holiday Inn for one night, Dec. 23rd. Our party included 2 adults, 2 8-yr old boys and a 5-yr old boy. I had reserved a room with 2 queen beds. Upon check-in, Angel, the desk clerk, informed me I was "Guest of the Day"! She presented me with a gift bag of goodies (2 water bottles, M&Ms, almonds), a certificate, and A ROOM UPGRADE!! to a "children's room suite." The room was a regular-sized room with a king bed, but Holiday Inn built a "room" around a bunk-bed with it's own dresser and TV. The "room" looked like a fort or a castle. How perfect for little boys/kids? I thought the "Guest of the Day" promotion idea is absolutely fantastic as a way to promote guest-loyalty! The room was clean, the bathroom was clean, the employees were very helpful. the decor was very contemporary. My only "minor" complaint was that our room was located on the first floor, and at about midnight or so, employees on a shift change or break, were being loud outside our room. Not a big deal. I heard them, but *not* the highway traffic nearby. And although breakfast was not included in the price of the room, our children did eat free. And the parking was free as well. I would definitely stay here or recommend this hotel to friends.

“Dissappointment. Behind the times and needs to be updated” Not much more to say. The room was only fairly clean, and the carpeting was very stained and seen better days. Internet access in room is an additional $15 per day. TV was old tube type, thus no HD either. The Hilton Boston Financial District needs to be updated and amenities brought up to meet today's travelers expectations. This does not appear to be a 4 star hotel, 3 at best- and that is a stretch without today's expected amenitites.

“Great hotel in a fantastic location” I was really impressed with this hotel. The hotel is located on Park at 38th just a few minutes walk from Grand Central Station. The service at the Kimpton was great. The staff really seemed to care and make sure the guests were well taken care of. The hotel had a lot of nice touches such as happy hour each day with free wine. I'm not sure if all guests get it but we got a $15 credit for the mini bar. You can't buy much with that but it's a nice touch. if you sign up for the frequent traveler program you get free wi-fi so it's worth signing up for the program if you aren't a member already. The room was typical of NYC, small but comfortable enough. It's NYC so you're not spending too much time in your room anyhow! The beds were comfy and the rooms were nicely soundproofed. From our room on the 15th floor we had a nice view of the Empire State Building. Overall, a very nice stay at the 70 Park.

“Good value, good location” We arrived at the Harbour Building of the Georgetown Suites on a rainy, miserable evening and were greeted by the friendly front desk employee who quickly checked us in and went over the details of the free breakfast with us, gave us coupons for local restaurants, and suggested close (it was pouring!) seafood restaurants as we specifically asked for those. We had read mixed reviews of the hotel, and were sort of worried when we stepped off the elevator into a dimly lit long hallway with little atmosphere, but when we swung the door open, we were delighted with the room. The bathroom has been updated with an attractive granite countertop with plenty of space for our belongings, but the bathtub was older. However, the tub was clean with gleaming tiles and caulk, and a new shower head. The shower knob was a bit clumsy and I discovered it was highly sensitive when a lot of people used the water at once, but I mastered it and it was fine. The hotel supplied quality conditioner, shampoo, shower gel, moisturizer, and the usual kit of items you see you in good hotels. Two large closets were in the room, although one didn't have hangers, but another held two comfortable bathrobes. A king-sized bed was comfortably made up with a cozy comforter and bright white linens with an excellent thread count. The pillows were of varying types to suit all sleeping styles, and I found one to nestle into each night. We had a kitchen in our room with only two of each item (dishes, glasses, cups), which was kind of odd, and no dish washing liquid or dish washer powder as we had a dishwasher. However, I discovered housekeeping washed the two wine glasses and one coffee cup we used in the dishwasher, which seems a waste of water. Perhaps she placed the dishes in the dishwasher to dry? Either way, they were washed. The next day she washed them again, and placed them on the small kitchen table with napkins poking out of the wine glasses. Nice touch. While the kitchen cupboards were definitely dated and ill fitting, they were clean. We really didn't need the kitchen. We enjoyed the nice complimentary breakfast, which had healthy options as well as delicious pastries, and the Washington Posts and USA Todays available to read. We did use the Internet and agree with everyone's comments on how slow it was, and delight in the fact the hotel is upgrading. A small business center is available to print boarding passes. We never met a rude employee at the hotel. I can understand the negatives of staying in the rooms that face the highway. Luckily we faced the courtyard, but since we were on the fifth floor, this allowed us to hear suitcases rolling over the cobbles early in the morning, or drunk co-eds returning from a night out in Georgetown with exceptionally loud lungs. (This only happened one night and the girls were quiet once they got in the hotel.) Either of these experiences is preferable to the noise of the road. Other than that, the courtyard side was quiet. If you are visiting Georgetown, the location is excellent. If you are venturing to the Mall, you'll need to walk six blocks to the Foggybottom Metro, or ride the convenient Circulator or Metrobus. The six blocks to Foggybottom is not that big of a deal if you don't have luggage, but could be challenging bumping over cobbles, sidewalk cracks, and the crowds of Georgetown when moving suitcases. Of course, there is also a taxi which the hotel will get for you. We will definitely put the hotel on our list as a place to stay again.

“Great building, inconsistent service” This is the hotel that was featured on the opening credits of the TV show Dallas for many years, and remains the epitome of the mirrored glass architecture from the late 70s/early 80s in Dallas. That, and the trademark atrium, date this hotel somewhat. Still, they have done a nice job of updating things. Rooms are airy and sizable--and placing the beds overlooking the view (as opposed to parallel to the windows) make the room feel bigger still. Good beds, and enjoyable showers, with noteworthy water pressure. My room, 2321, had a good view of the skyline, and many of the rooms on that side of the hotel do--request one. The hotel is well located for highway access, particularly for a downtown hotel. Valet parking is $19.50 a day, and can be slow for car retrieval. Internet is $10 per day--obscene given margins on this service, and outrageous given that many less expensive hotels no longer charge for this. Fitness center is well maintained, and though some equipment could use updating, it is nicely furnished and free to guests. There is a pool and hottub on 3, but can't say it looked very welcoming. . .overlooks the back side--a rather desolate view--of the hotel. What is frustrating about the hotel is the service--while always pleasant, it can be lacking. Housekeeping just made my bed and replaced my towels one day--no tidying up. Another day, they neglected to come, altogether. In fairness, the hotel recouped well, and I got follow ups from the housekeeping manager and the assistant rooms manager--both of whom attempted to make amends. While recovery was good, there were sufficient lapses to disappoint. Yes, got this room for $59 a night on Priceline, but still expect good service from a 4 diamond Hyatt Regency. . .with work, perhaps I would be impressed next time. Building, overall, is a pleasant surprise--and if service had been at the same level, this would be a great find, particularly at the Priceline rate. Would still return, but would caution those paying full price that you may or may not get 4 diamond caliber service during your stay. And note to hotel--seek ways to eliminate internet fees. . .it feels as if you are nickel and diming your guests. Bad.

“Excellent San Diego Gaslamp Quarter Hotel!” We stayed at the Hotel Solamar for a two-night stay and enjoyed both the Gaslamp Quarter location and the hotel itself. Having handed over car parking duties to the valet (at $36 pn the one irritation with the Solamar, to be honest) check-in went smooothly & professionally and we made our way up to our room on the 9th floor, high up with a view as requested as part of the online booking. We both thought the room was first-rate, with a lovely & comfortable large bed, great decor, good quality furniture & fittings, plus a large, clean, well-finished bathroom. No coffee maker but there was a fridge and the wi-fi internet was quick and easily accessed. We didn't eat in the hotel but we did avail ourselves of the wine reception on the first evening and it was lovely to sit in the beautiful lobby area in comfortable arm-chairs drinking a couple of glasses of very acceptable Californian wine. The hotel location is great for the restaurants on Fifth Avenue a short walk away and we also made the short stroll to admire Petco Park on the final morning. Driving up to Balboa Park was also easy. In summary, we enjoyed our stay at the Solamar - Margot liked the 'ambience' - and should we return to San Diego in the future we would probably stay here again, perhaps even catch a Padres game!

“Not perfect, but plusses outweigh minuses” First the plusses: This is a beautiful and stately hotel built in the early 1900s that exudes character. The desk and bell staff were friendly and helpful. It is in a great Dallas neighborhood - Uptown. Within walking distance are fine dining and casual restaurants, bank ATMs, convenience stores - all the things travelers look for. My room, 801, was a spacious corner room with a large comfortable bed. The bathroom had plenty of room, too. Free wireless internet was included. The minuses are mainly nit picks, but there were enough of them for me to give the Stoneleigh a qualified review. First, the desk in my room was useless. It was a narrow table pushed up against a wall and had no lamp and no electrical outlets nearby. To use my computer I had to rely on the glow from the bathroom lights and stretch a cord across the entrance to the bathroom. The desk chair was uncomfortable. The room needed a place where one could get some work done. One of the lamps next to the bed has no light bulb in it. That should have been remedied in advance of a guest checking in. The beautiful flat screen high definition TV didn't work. I called the front desk who said that engineering would be sent up. They never came. The next morning the TV worked, so perhaps they fied it remotely, but they never told me. I checked in at 7:30pm and was told that the dining room was closed for the evening. Huh? I was happy enough to walk down the street for dinner, but come on! I'll go back. I hope when I do management will have paid a little more attention to detail.

“Great location and nice hotel” I'd never been to Austin and really enjoyed being walking distance to 6th Street. The hotel is comfortable, fairly clean and well priced. Nothing exciting but I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again either.

“Excellent price, in the heart of Hollywood!” My parents stayed here when they visited me last fall. PROS: -dirt cheap (approx. $100-$120/night) -located a block from Hollywood Blvd., walking distance to all the popular tourist attractions -free parking -free Internet kiosk in lobby (warning: the PC is loaded with spyware) -free continental breakfeast in lobby CONS: -small rooms; you have to turn sideways to fit more than one person at a time in the bathroom! -despite being recently renovated, the rooms still seem "dated"; cheap carpet, paint, linens, etc.

“great hotel- room a little too small” friendly staff, nicely appointed room, nice sized bathroom, great location but the room itself was a little too small. a king sized bed, a comfortable chair, a desk with chair, 2 nighttables, a dresser and not much room to maneuver.

“Nice Room and Hot Breakfast!” Stayed at the Residence Inn Lake Union for one night on 10/27. I was lucky to get the rate of $60 through Priceline. With taxes and fees it came to $76.45/night. Check in was quick and easy. The front desk people were all very nice and pleasant. Self Parking is an additional $20.69/day (this includes sales tax). I didn't want to waste time looking for street parking. There is a separate garage for SUV/Trucks and sedans. We had a mini-van so we parked in the SUV/Trucks garage. Parking stalls in the garage seemed small. So, I can't imagine what the stalls in the sedan parking lot look like! At least the parking lot felt safe and secure as you needed a key to get into the garage. The room itself was spacious. I had a one bedroom with a king bed. Small kitchen with full-size refrigerator, stove, and microwave. The bathroom was a little on the smaller side, but it was OK. The bathroom sink was separated from the shower and tub and there was plenty of counter space. There were two TVs, one in the living area and one in the bedroom. The free internet worked and we didn't have any problems getting a connection. I could smell the hot breakfast in the morning from my room so I knew it was time to get up! There was a wide variety from bagels, toast, eggs, sausage, yogurt, cereal, fresh belgian waffles, etc. All in all, a very nice stay at the Residence Inn and I would definitely stay here again.

“Great location Great service!” You couldn't ask for a better location when visiting New York City. Located on 41st and 5th Ave right smack in the heart of the Big Apple. The hotel has a small feel to it. The staff is extremely friendly and enthusiastic. Upon arrival you are given a great deal of one on one attention. The rooms are large and comfortable. I was upgraded (thank you) to a suite which provided a great deal of room to stretch out and relax. Rooms are stylish and extremely comfortable. I know from the their website some have views of 5th Ave mine did not but I prefer I quite room which it was. Complimentary mini bar (non alcohol) and snacks are also included with you stay. I also had dinner at the hotel restaurant The Shop and is was very good. They also do a very good breakfast. The Andaz is not cheap but what is in New York? I would highly recommend this hotel before shelling out more money for some of the other 5 star hotels that are in the general area.

“Very good business hotel in downtown Chicago” There aren't very many Conrad hotels in the USA and that is honestly a shame as they are very valid competition to the other high end hotels of other chains (i.e. JW Marriott, Westin, etc.). This particular hotel is a very fine business hotel. I was upgraded to a Jr. Suite, which is basically one large room in a sort of L shape. By big city standards my room was huge, complete with a Bose 321 DVD system and high def TV WITH HD programming. The bathroom was also a highlight as it was huge and had a large walk in shower in addition to a big tub. The Conrad Chicago has a very unique service (no additoinal charge) as they present you with a "pillow menu". I choose several different pillows (relaxation, clod and flu and magnetic) and they were cool. The magnetic probably the worst of the lot but the relaxation was wonderful. Their location is terrific. It is one block off Michigan Ave and on Rush very near to Ontario. It is connected to a mall (by big city standards). You can easily walk to the Loop. There are a ton of restaurants within walking distance as well. The valet parking is a rip off though as it is $51/night. There are cheaper parking alternatives in the neighborhood. Thankfully I work for a company that is OK with that sort of parking expense so it was more convenient to park at the hotel. They have a little outdoor bistro type restaurant on the fifth floor. It is in a great setting and the food is terrific. I would highly recommend it.

“Very new, very nice, airport noise could be a problem” Stayed one night on a long road trip. Arrived after midnight and departed right after breakfast, so impressions are somewhat limited. Parking was limited and some cars were parked far down the entrance road, though the front desk attendant told me to feel free to park at the front door, as long as I left room for the shuttle bus. It was a windy and brisk night, this was appreciated. The hotel is very new and the king room was nicely appointed with flat screen TV, very comfortable bed, sleeper sofa. The hotel is adjacent to I-465, so there was some road noise, although with the AC fan on it was not objectionable to me (I am a heavy sleeper, normally). I like it when the HVAC system fan can be turned on and left on. Sometime early in the morning the Fed Ex jets from IND began to leave, and this was a bit more noticeable. Light sleepers might have issues here. The breakfast bar was similar to other Comfort Suites I have visited. Large dining room, but only five tables, they could use more. The hostess attending the bar was not very attentive, some items took a while to be replenished, and the biscuits and eggs were cold. My son likes the fresh waffles, and I am basically a bagel and oatmeal guy, and these were fine. If you value clean and comfortable you will like this hotel, but light sleepers might beware.

“Great family-friendly hotel in a perfect location” We stayed in San Francisco with our three kids (13, 9, and 6) for five days over President's Day weekend, and Hotel Nikko was the perfect place for us to stay. I booked an Imperial Club Queen-Queen room via AAA, which is the best deal you'll get at this hotel. We had free daily breakfast and afternoon wine/snacks in the Club lounge, free Wi-Fi, free rollaway bed, and free access to the health club/pool for about $310/night (plus tax). The room was wonderful -- on the 23rd floor, in the corner, and very quiet. Roomy enough for a twin-bed rollaway to fit. The Club level rooms are bigger, which is one of the reasons we upgraded. The furnishings are contemporary and the colors are soothing; slate blue/white/dark wood/neutrals. All the usual stuff for a pretty nice hotel room: iHome alarm clock, flat-screen tv, double-layered light-blocking drapes, large bathroom with separate toilet room and shower/tub room. You can even watch tv on the bathroom mirror :) There was a complimentary fruit platter and large water bottle upon our arrival, and nightly turndown service includes little chocolates. Breakfast: You actually get a couple of breakfast choices; either the free Continental one in the Club lounge, or use the two daily passes for brunch at Anza, the restaurant downstairs. The first morning we all ate at Anza because we got to the Club lounge within 5 minutes of closing, and the guy was already putting everything away. Anza has an expansive, varied brunch buffet, which included Japanese-style breakfast items (e.g., miso soup, rice, etc.), as well as the usual American-style items. The brunch is normally $25pp, but my husband and I ate for free with our passes, and the kids' buffet was $10pp. Not too bad. The next few days my husband took the kids to the Club lounge for breakfast (they eat fast!), then brought them back to the room, where they watched a couple of cartoons while my husband and I went downstairs to Anza for the full brunch. Nice for us to get a little quiet time before a long busy day gets going, now that our 13 yr old can watch the younger ones for a bit! And you get two brunch buffet passes per night, per room, so you may as well use them. Pool: Very nice heated pool in a large, heated atrium. Kids loved it. The only problem is the VERY slippery tiles all around the pool area. Holy cow, I almost busted my head open! The kids were sliding around, too, whether barefoot or in flip-flops. Hotel Nikko, please upgrade/change those tiles soon, before someone really gets hurt! There is also a small Jacuzzi there, which I enjoyed. Lobby/atmosphere: The lobby is nice, the staff friendly, the place is high-end all around but not fussy; more modern. There is a Starbucks in the lobby; always a bonus! Location: We did not rent a car, so location was crucial, and this place was awesome. 1.5 blocks to the Powell St BART and cable car stop. MUNI stops everywhere. We only took a taxi once (other than the ride from/to OAK airport). Recommend: If you are going with kids, I highly recommend the CityPASS. What a deal! It just turned out that everything we wanted to do was part of the pass -- for some cities it is not that way at all. We made huge use of the unlimited MUNI (bus) rides and cable car rides. Would definitely stay here again, with or without the kids.

“Most basic business hotel” Stayed here a while ago. Room is small but clean. Window faces the wall! Restaurant breakfast is so so. The only great point about the hotel is free internet. Okay, one more great thing was on the following day when I needed to catch a cab to a business as well as later on needed another cab to go to a different hotel, they had a town car waiting for me as complimentary! Of course when I needed to go to the airport a few days later I called for the service and gave them a big tip!!

“Great location, some awkward moments.” The location is great and the staff were friendly and helpful. The concierge/tour desk/whatnot shop is convenient and is efficiently run. The place is very popular with tourists, and unfortunately this sometimes creates awkward moments such as the two obviously drunk older British women knocking on my door at 2 AM and cussing me out for not being the person/room they wanted. My thoughts went to Mrs. Slocombe and Mrs. Axleby, but I digress. I called the front desk and they handled the matter quite tactfully. It is definitely more of a tourist hotel than a business-oriented hotel. The only complaint I had is that one of the bartenders didn't know what a Manhattan cocktail was, but that was easily resolved. Four night stay in downtown SF at a great location for an excellent rate. Wth the exception of the drunks and the inexperienced bartender, I give it four stars out of five. I would a half-star if the bartender reads up on classic cocktails.

“Predictable, which is a good thing” Room was spacious and comfortable. Bright (lots of windows). Clean. Bathroom modern and well appointed. Great shower. Bed and pillows as comfortable as one should expect of a FS property. My only criticism of the hotel is that the public spaces feel a bit dark and cold (there was enough marble to clad a mausoleum), more for passing through, but not terribly inviting if the aim is to relax. Perhaps I did not scout around enough, but for some reason I felt self-conscious poking around.

“Great spot near Brooklyn Bridge!” I've stayed here 4 times, & each time I am glad I did. There are many nice restaurants nearby, as well as an open air market a block away. Not too long a walk to subway. Parking lot across street too. Our room last time had a decent view as well. Our friend booked a room here also & had a very nice stay. The rooms are nice & we always sleep well. Some typical banging of doors as guests check-out, but I've found this to be common most places, sadly, that people can't be aware they're being rude. I like staying here as it is a bit off the beaten path & quieter. If I want noise & late night out, it's just a short taxi ride! Tho' my 2nd time here my taxi ended up going over the Brooklyn Bridge instead of turning onto Peck Slip. lol. With GPS, it's much easier to find now. =)

“Best place to stay in Keystone Area” Great location. Was here on business. Clients office was near by. Took about 25 mins to get to and from the airport. No real traffic issues. Covered parking onsite. Nice lobby. Rooms were in great shape with comfortable beds. Plenty of good restaurants close by. Had a great stay. Sheraton has done an excellent job with the public spaces and lobby areas. Great fitness room and a pool. They even have a sun deck to hang out on. Only complaint...it was 105 degrees in Indy the day I was there. Management could do nothing about it...

“Beautiful building, great location, small room” Stayed here with my husband in January on a short trip to Boston. We booked a Classic room so weren't expecting anything fancy but it was smaller than we expected. The bed was really comfy and the linens were of the high quality you'd expect in such a hotel. Reception staff were friendly and the porters were very accommodating, explaining features of the room when delivering our bags. Good restaurants on site and lots of options in the surrounding neighbourhood as well as the usual room service options. The building itself is beautiful and feels very welcoming with an open fire roaring downstairs for you to sit by and warm up after a wander in the Boston weather. The real benefit of this hotel is the location - perfect for wandering this great city.

“OK Hotel” I stayed at this hotel while attending a conference in Oct. 2007. The hotel locagtion is superb; 1 block off of Michigan Avenue. The room itself was ok. Nothing fancy, but nothing dull and drab either. The room was a good size and the bathroom was modern and updated. I would stay here again for a couple of nights. If you are looking for a luxurious hotel, this isn't it. If you are looking for a good room, at a good price, and a great location then this might be the place for you.

“Fantastic - Loved it” It was my 3rd time in NYC and i have to say that this was the perfect stay! Before i checked in i was worried about the noise - the usual for NYC but I was given a room at 15th floor that was just perfect. No noise, very clean, super confortable bed, free WIFI, superb service (from check in desk, concierge all the way to room service). I had a problem with my hair drier at 6AM, I called the front desk and in 5 min they were upstairs with a replacement. I was impressed. Location is great as well – approx. 10 - 12 min easy walk to Time Square, lots of restaurants around. I would definitely go back.

“Not bad but not good either.” I stayed here for two nights after a wonderful stay at the immaculate Renaissance Harbourplace in Baltimore. I chose this hotel because 1) it seems to be the most reasonably priced in downtown DC, 2) its close to a metro station, 3) its not far from where I had my meetings, 4) it has in-room safe, and 5) its a Crowne Plaza. Unlike other chains hotels in downtown, its a "historic" rather than a modern hotel. But it has been refurbished to a good standard. The location is OK, but like many downtown area in US cities, its not a particularly exciting place. The restaurant is reasonable. The problem with the hotel, is the staff, maintenance and the upkeep. Here are a few: 1) I am a Platium level Priority Club member, and I believe I get complimentary upgrade, although I have never experienced this yet. So on check in, I asked if I am to get an upgrade. And she said yes and told me she'll give me a room with a good view over the square. Hardly an upgrade but good view. OK. Then, the next day I asked the counter, and the staff told me the club/executive floor is closed for refurbishment. But told me they should have offered me free drink tickets, which I wasnt. Then I overheard at breakfast that the guy sitting next to me was in Club floor. What club floor ? I thought it was closed ? 2) The room they gave me was tiny but bright. Unfortunatley, the key for the safe in the room was missing. Yes, in-room safe need a key rather than the usual key pad. They told me they were in the process of replacing it so I had to be moved to another room. 3) The room they moved me to was at the back of the hotel, with no view, and faces the back of an office block, and worst, the fans of the hotel's air-con system was only 2 or 3 floors down, immediately below my window. It was noisy. The noise went on all the time. The room was about double the size of the first room but dark, and noisy. 4) the room window relies on two little "chocks" to keep it in place. One of them was engaged, but the other one wasnt. So there was a gap between the upper and lower half of the sash window. Called maintenance to get it closed. They managed to close it, and the noise was reduced, but still, noisy. 5) I hate hotels which rely on wifi for in-room internet connection. WIth my laptop which has a weak receiver, it seldom works. After trying for half an hour, calling reception, which put me through to AT+T technical support, I had to get a "high speed bridge" from the reception. 6) The first high speed bridge didnt work. It was dead. They promised to send up a second one but after 15minutes, it didnt come so I had to collect it myself. It worked some further fiddling !! These "high speed bridges" were in their slightly worned out original postal boxes (with stamp and address etc) tucked in a drawer under the reception desk. 7) the towel hook behind the door was bolted to the door with two bolts. One was missing. Surely the cleaner would see that everyday, but why wasnt it repaired? How about wrinkly (i.e. water damaged) piece of in-room menu ? Its not a bad hotel, but in a good one, everything works ! I probably wont be staying here next time I visit DC.

“Always A Nice Experience” It is always a pleasure to return to this hotel. Staff is friendly and welcoming. Rooms have recently been refurbished and the new carpet, paint, furniture, and TWO flat screen TVs (in the suites) are wonderful. Breakfast buffet could use some attention to detail and a better menu but service and comfort are nice. I will return.

“Loved the décor – Everything clean, comfortable & classy” The first thing you will notice is the clean and classy décor of the Eventi in NYC. The staff were all very cordial and welcoming, without the pretentiousness and coldness of a typical higher end hotel. When we initially booked our reservations, no double queen rooms were available only a single king. The day of our arrival, the check-in attendant worked tirelessly in an attempt to accommodate our request. Alas, his efforts were in vain, but we found our king room so comfortable after the first night, that although we were sleeping three in the bed, we decided to stay in the room the remaining four nights. We requested an additional small refrigerator since the room refrigerator comes completely filled with bar items, and this request was honored promptly. The neighborhood is rather dirty, but the NYPD station is in the same block, so we felt safe. Times Square and the Theater District is only a short walk away, and the Eventi offers a much better value than some of the Times Square hotels. As is the rest of the hotel, the complementary morning coffee and tea offered in the lobby is of superb quality. As a frequent traveler, I congratulate the management and staff of this hotel on a job well done.

“Excellent Hotel - Excellent Staff !!” Traveled here on a business trip. Super nice hotel right on the river. Clean rooms and excellent meeting space. MORE IMPORTANTLY, the staff was superb !! Always went out of their way to help out when asked and sometimes for no reason at all !!! :) They even had a Wednesday Night Reception with free food and drinks. The only downside is that there aren't alot of places to eat around the hotel within walking distance

“good location” We stayed one night at the Hyatt Regency, booked on Hotwire for a total rate of $105.29 . Room was comfortable, good beds,flat screen tv, desk and office chair (no other seating in room) coffee maker (the new pod one that makes a cup at a time and only two pods= 2 cups of coffee) good sized bathroom with good lighting and the first time I have seen toothpaste as one of the amenities in the bathroom. The view was one of the other towers of the hotel facing us. The restaurants were all very pricey so we didn't eat at any of those. This is basically a hotel for business people, The teens would have been happier with a pool and with something for breakfast before we headed out for the day.If you get a good price it is a good location for everything in downtown Chicago with a bus stop right outside the entrance. I would stay at this hotel again, but probably not with teens or younger children. I like to have breakfast at the hotel before we start the day, and this hotel the breakfast was too pricey, I would prefer the breakfast be included with the room rate as some other hotels do. So basically, it was a good place to sleep for the night.

“Never again” The staff was great but the hotel has two main flaws. 1) if you have at&t wireless you will have zero reception here. Zero. This is the only place in NYC I have ever experienced this to this extent. We are talking zero bars. 2) the bathroom shower is glass and the room has a view. Aka you can sit on the bed and watch everything your partner does in bathroom. Everything. Call me old fashioned but I like my phone to work and a little privacy. We checked out after one night. The gym was very small also and the furniture was very college dorm ikea

“Yes and No” Pros: historic old hotel, larger rooms, central location, clean, nice bedding Cons:minimally staffed, elevators from the tower of terror (lurch a lot, 20 minute waits from top floors not uncommon, only hold 8 people), very dark rooms (one window facing a wall and very few lights), high speed internet bogs down after 6am (?DSL line) to <1mbps, desk chair well below working level unless you are over 7 feet tall

“Good Value” The quandary: visiting NYC during the holidays with no advance planning -- with two adults and two adult children. The solution: YOTEL. So we needed three beds and wanted to stay near the theatre district and we wanted to spend less than a fortune. For less than $200 per night we stayed in a bright, clean room with unique pull up bunk beds and a comfortable queen. The only real complaint is the silly glass bathroom door that insists on slamming every time - and does not go all the way to the ceiling, making it . . uh . . difficult to . . . uh . . . USE when nature calls and there are others in the room. The pluses are many: the windows actually open, the shower is huge, it is well-insulated for sound and feels very secure. The staff are genuinely friendly and seem concerned that you will like their place. As for the bland restaurant, main lobby and bar . . . who needs 'em. This is NYC and anything you want is steps away.

“Not the place for a good night's sleep” This place is definitely stylish. And location is pretty good; right on edge of trendy Soho scene. Rooms are cute, albeit very compact. I stay in NYC a lot for work and have basically stayed at most downtown hotels. It's also very new, so that's nice. BUT I stayed here on two separate occasions and it is the noisiest place I've ever slept in NY. It's on a relatively busy street and theres a fruit store that apparently starts receiving deliveries at around 4 am -- honking, truck engines, garage door opening ... Too bad, because the place is stylish and feels much cleaner and newer than Soho or TriBeCa Grand. Not nearly as luxe as Trump Soho, though, which is where I would recommend staying if you can afford it and want to be in this area.

“Terrible” I was scared to stay here, based on the reviews, and sadly, they are right. I didn't have much choice . The woman at the front desk was the rudest person I have ever experienced in the hospitality industry. I was shocked. Room was not very clean. The only place to eat is a Subway...honestly. And the hotel is behind a very tall iron gate, that is both comforting, I guess, and disconcerting, as well. I didn't sleep well and left very early. Never again.

“Great place!” We stayed at the Columbus West Hampton Inn..found it to be very nice. The new bedding was great! There was a microwave and frig in the room. The breakfast was good. Our only complaint was a minor one.. the dining room was very crowded at breakfast. We had to take our food back to our room. We will stay here again in the future.

“As good as it gets” Let's be honest. It's not fare to compare this hotel with Best Western and Hampton Inn hotels because they don't have the same budget prices. It's a small hotel with a great location. The room is quiet, although there's no view (not at the first floor), but there's a safe box and free wireless internet (fast). If you like asian food you just turn left on fifth ave. and left again on 32nd st. New York city is great for shopping and you could start at fifth ave., but don't forget the shops at 34th st. and Union square (one Best Buy openned for 24 hours). As I said, it's as good as it gets.

“Great location for Boston, Just OK, overpriced!” We stayed at this Courtyard by Marriott for 5 nights while attending a convention at the Hynes Center. It's in the heart of Boston's Back Bay and Copley Place which is central to all of Boston. The rooms are clean but do not offer the amenities that the other comparably priced hotels in the area do. Again this is an average/OK hotel by Courtyard standards, just that the price does not measure up to what is offered. For example, we stayed on a Sunday through Friday. We were charged $120 extra for the Wednesday and Thursday nights ($229 vs. $349 possibly because the Boston Marathon and opening day of Fenway). The restaurant is overpriced for breakfast and offers typically what you would get at a "complimentary breakfast offering". Lots of history to this hotel (over 100 years old). Not a bad place for Boston if you want to be "in the heart of things". Just be aware there are better places for the pricing and value. I'd look around at the other hotels in the Back Bay/Copley Place.

“High End Hotel at Summer Rates” In Phoenix, when the temps touch 100 and above, sometimes the high end hotels and resorts offer summer rates and special deals. This was the case for our stay at the historic Arizona Biltmore and we had a beautiful room for about $100 per night, plus tax and resort fees, for a very reasonable cost of $180 for a one night stay (also includes parking costs of about $15 for self parking or about $28 for valet). The hotel is a classic and the building and grounds alone are worth the stay. Our room was on a the second floor with a nice patio/balcony, soft and comfortable beds and a huge bathroom with double sinks and a tub and separate glass shower. Several pools through out the hotel grounds and our room overlooked a smaller but good size pool that was quiet and felt like our own private spot. We never left the hotel, explored the grounds and buildings, admired the architecture and design of Albert C McArthur, with influences by Frank Lloyd Wright, enjoyed all the old pictures of past guests (US Presidents and film stars), had a drink in the lobby bar and listened to great piano music and had a nice dinner and breakfast in "Frank and Albert's" restaurant (very good, but expensive to be sure). Almost every employee was happy and helpful, with the only exception being at the front desk. The one major negative of the stay was a surly and rude front desk person at check-in. Not a welcome to the hotel and never even made eye contact, a very poor ambassador for a unique hotel. We did not let this person spoil the trip and we enjoyed the stay.

“Needs Some Updating” The St. Regis is in a perfect location. Literally The White House is just a stone's throw from the hotel. There is a Starbucks across the street and restaurants all around. The property itself needs to be renovated. The lobby couches appear stained from years of wear and tear. The restaurant, albeit fantastic, has stained carpeting throughout. The actual rooms themselves were best described as tired. We had two doubles, which seemed more like two twin beds- very odd. Both beds had wheels on them and they would easy move. The wheels made the room feel more like a nursing home. Just odd. Would I stay here again? No. There is no wow factor here. I have stayed at other St. Regis' and this one is sadly worn down. And please know that I wanted this hotel to be great.

“Perfect location” My partner and I stayed at the Parc for 3 nights in late August. Love the location and the hotel although being remodeled at the time was in very good condition. Check in was quick and smooth. Loved the room. Very comfortable bed, great shower. The hotel is close to all the great downtown shopping and restaurants. Also there is a small bakery right outside the door for a quick breakfast. Across the street is a BART station and very close to the Cable Car line for a jaunt to fishermans wharf. My only complaint was the cost of internet in the lobby - I believe it was $5.99 for 20 minutes-I bit too steep for me! There is a sports bar and an asian restaurant on premises. Overall a great experience.

“Lovely Stay” Stayed in the Whitcomb Hotel in March this year for 4 nights with my daughter. A lovely historic hotel central to most places. Trolleys and BART on our doorstep.Our room was lovely and large if a little dated but that added to the charm of the place The shower was great and the beds were very comfortable. The room was spotless. We ate in the Market grill one night and had a fab meal there. A work of art came out on my plate, I had the chicken and my daughter says her seafood pasta was the best she had ever eaten. The food was delicious, the restaurant was very comfortable and there was a fire burning in the fire place which was lovely as we had a window seat and it was pouring out of the heavens outside and it made us feel really nice. There is a Starbucks attached to the hotel which opened really early and it was great to start the day with a nice coffee. Yes there is a lot of homeless people in the area but at no time did I ever feel threatened by them. I spoke to a few of them, most were ex Vietenam Vets who were thrown on to the streets by Ronald Regan in his wisdom. It actually really upset me to see how these people were treated having fought for their country they were nothing but respectful of me. Sams diner is across the road and does a really good breakfast.All in all I had a wonderful stay here and would definately stay here again when I next return to San Francisco. Thank you Whitcomb

“Georgetown's Best Deal?” We stayed at the Georgetown Suites 30th St. building for three nights last weekend while we visited our son at Georgetown University. We thought it was a very good deal. We had plenty of room, with a king sized bed, comfy chair, table with four chairs, bathroom and well-equipped kitchen. Everything was clean, spacious and comfortable. The decor is dated in style, but not worn or tired. The staff was helpful. There is free WiFi in the room or you can check email for free in the lobby business center. Great location, right in the midst of the Georgetown shops and restaurants, about a 15 minute walk to the University (uphill). The Circulator bus can be caught just up the block for going to the Mall. Great bran muffins at breakfast, among many other choices. The only down side was that the heat/air conditioning duct was a big vertical grid on the wall that blew right on the bed. Apart from that, it was a great deal for $150/night.

“Thanks for the awesome upgrade!” My family and I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights for the Boston Marathon. The rate ($189/night) was certainly right considering just about every hotel in Boston was booked during this period. We were upgraded to a huge one bedroom suite, which was AWESOME because my husband was running in the marathon and we were travelling with our one year old son. I felt like the hotel really took extra special care of us because my husband was running in the marathon. Having the extra space made a huge difference for us so that everyone could have their own space and get a good night sleep. I thought the bed was really comfortable and the linens were nice and soft. The suite itself was certainly in need of an update, but it had everything we needed (except central heat/air). It had a living room, dining room and kitchen. Our room faced the construction side, but we did not hear any noise at all. The only noise we heard was from ambulances. This area of the hotel we were in (entrance from inside of the galleria/food court) was very private and quiet. Speaking of the galleria/food court, it was great to have some quick food options in the hotel and there is a CVS right there too. I thought the overall location was good because it was close to a few different T stations and you could easily walk to Fenway Park (as well as the route to the Boston Marathon). I also thought the service at the hotel was good. All of the employees I interacted with were polite and pleasant. There were a few things I didn't like about the hotel, but they were relatively minor. 1 - The water pressure in the shower was just sad. 2 - I didn't like how the room had in-window AC units. It was almost 90 degrees while we were in town. 3 - Someone in the room next to us put a finished tray of food outside of the door (presumably from room service) and the tray stayed outside the door for over 24 hours. It may still be sitting there now. 4 - The internet service in the hotel was complimentary, but the signal was very weak and I had a tough time connecting to it and staying connected to it. It was a good experience overall. My husband stayed at this hotel (alone) for the 2011 marathon and had a nice experience then too, which is why we stayed here again this year.

“Basic Hotel, good location” Stayed here for 1 night. The hotel is clean and neat. It looks like a former apartment building that had been converted to a hotel. The room was large -- with a kitchen. Everything worked fine -- toilet, fridge, shower, A/C, etc. It lacks the niceties of the nearby Affinia properties -- no pillow menu, no fancy toiletries, no fresh fruit and juice in the lobby. Small, lobby -- can get crowded quickly if 3 or 4 people are there with baggage. Just a large, clean NY hotel room. It is in a good location near a lot of restaurants and stores.

“Weekend Trip” I have been to San Francisco many times but I have not stayed at the Omni Hotel before. We arrived on a Friday at 11:00 am but our room was not available. The staff told us they would call our cell phone when our room was ready. They did not do this but we were happy to enjoy the city and when we returned at 5 pm our room was ready for us. Our room was 726 which looked out on the street. The room was quiet although one of the evenings we could hear our neighbors fighting and this woke us so the walls are not so solid. The room is fairly standard offering in room coffee and nice bathrobes. The location of this hotel is excellent. The trolley stops outside the door of the hotel. We took nearby public transportation to the Japanese Tea Garden and Botanical Garden. Many activities are within walking distance of this hotel as well. Concerning breakfast, there is one restaurant in the hotel, which is a steak house in the evening. Breakfast is pricey and ordered off a menu, no buffet. Granola/yogurt is around $16 so I would recommend going to one of many wonderful breakfast places nearby. The menu was limited as well. We utilized the concierge service of the hotel and a word of caution here. We found several of the staff not well informed of restaurants that were within two blocks of the hotel. We were fortunate our last night in the hotel to meet Lex Doherty who was excellent and well informed. So if you can ask for him, I would highly recommend it. Overall this is a super hotel, super staff and great location. I would without a doubt stay here again..

“I expected more from an Omni” This hotel was just so-so for an Omni. The location is not the best for San Antonio. I went there for a banquet and stayed the night. Banquet food was very dry and not that great. The rooms were a little small. The hotel itself had an older feeling. On the plus side it is nicer than all the other hotels in the area. There is a small fitness center. The military rate is very good.
