“Great stay over New Years” Stayed at hotel (for the second time in two months) with some friends in a suite for New Years 2009/2010. Having stayed in regular room in November, I knew what to expect from hotel. This time was in a suite on the 6th floor at front of facility. As mentioned elsewhere, the hotel is just a very short walk from aquarium 't' stop. Just 2$ from logan airport. Check-in was a breeze. Suite was big enough for us all - 3 adults and 2 teenagers. Small kitchen area, although no microwave or fridge, which would have been useful. So close to everything, very good for new years fireworks, on Common at 7pm, and then a very short walk to habour to welcome in the new year. As I've written before, I usually stay at the Omni, but if the deals keep on at the Hilton, then it's a good choice.

“Did not feel ripped off at a NYC hotel for a change” Having been spoiled with frequent suite upgrades (particularly in Asia) with most of my hotel stays, I found the Andaz Large King room to be one of the rare cases where a non-suite room was respectfully adequate. No issues on this Friday night stay in March, save for the inconvenience of not being able to tune in to the Knicks game (no MSG on TV and no AM radio on the bedside alarm clock/radio). The resourceful long table with three seats functioned as a working surface, TV stand, and mirror vanity set. The other ingenious design is the closet/full-length mirror/countertop which rotates 360 degrees (see picture). No complaints from me about the bed, bedding, bath, nor shower, the only thing that was an annoyance was that the sink seemed to splatter a lot while the water is running. The one-category room upgrade was provided along with breakfast (since it was the weekend, brunch for two was complimentary up to the mid-afternoon, unfortunately I had other obligations so was not able to take advantage of this) for my Gold Passport Diamond membership. After check-in around 6 pm, I entered the room and soon noticed that the time displayed on the alarm clock/radio was incorrect (as it is often the case at hotels), just as I noticed it, a knock came on the door and a maintenance staff asked to come in, to specifically adjust the time on the alarm clock/radio – I never realized (or it did not seem) that hotels made an effort in this regard!

“Excellent Hotel” This is an excellent hotel. As other reviews point out, the lobby is nothing to write home about, it's fairly poky. But that really is the only criticism I have. While there I put the hotel through a number of tests. The first one was: I'm very noise sensitive, and although they gave me the kind of room I'd requested, very high up, with a wonderful view, it had a connecting door to the next door room, which was a potent and irritating noise source. I asked to be moved to a quieter room. At first they told me the only quieter room they had was on a smoking floor (I'm a non-smoker). When I said I didn't care, I just wanted a quieter room wherever, they found one on the same floor I was on, which was a non-smoking floor. It wasn't a better room, really, and was in some respects less good. But it was quieter, and served me well for the rest of my stay. Full marks on that. The move was executed within half an hour of my initial complaint. Secondly: I ordered a DVD from Amazon, and by mistake Amazon left my name off the package. In spite of that, the hotel staff ensured that it got to my room. The service in the Affinia was universally excellent. The concierge, bellhops and reception staff were extremely helpful at every turn. One word of advice: whatever you do, don't bother going to the Barking Dog, or whatever the hotel's adjoining restaurant/bar is called, for breakfast. For better value, and a more authentic experience, go to the Murray Hill Diner just round the corner on Lexington. The service and the food is much better.

“Nice hotel, great location” I visited the Langham with my bf for one night on November 14-15, for a job offer trip. The location was perfect, right down the street from One Int'l Place, where he had his meetings. The room was on the second floor and was comfortable, though nothing over the top. The bellhops were kind of hit-or-miss. They graciously helped me figure out which cabs accepted the vouchers I had, however, when we arrived one of them pulled a backpack out of the trunk of our cab and placed it on the (wet) sidewalk. I wasn't too happy about that. Similarly, the concierge staff were great when I checked in a bag, but took a long time for no apparent reason to retrieve it when I returned. I'd probably stay here again if I needed to be in this area of Boston.

“Thought it was a great hotel, but.....” My first impression was what a beautiful hotel this is and how very nice and helpful the staff is. I still think this. The beds are so comfortable, however in the middle of the night my husband woke to something crawling on him. We turned on the lights and sure enough bed bugs. My husband is in pest control so he knew immediately . We took the bed apart and there was more evidence, so we had our rooms switched and no more problems. We were told that it was the first time, however now I see another review that mentioned it. We checked my daughter and son in law's bed in the morning and even though they didn't have bugs currently, my husband could see the traces that showed there had been. The hotel handled this, but when they were supposed to call hotwire to let them know, they didn't plus had no record, so I had to call the manager and find out what was going on. They comped the rooms so I appreciate the great service, but not the lie about there never being bed bugs before or the fact that the manager didn't call hotwire to take care of this. It is a beautiful hotel, great location and great staff, but be aware and check the bed when you get into a room. I'm going to say yes to recommendation, but with a warning.

“Can't recommend it enough!” My boyfriend and I booked a double room at the Magic Castle, for our week long trip to LA in June 06. When we arrived we found we had a *huge* suite. The staff were absolutely lovely, friendly and funny and very attentive. It had a great pool, a laundry room, and tasty breakfast was available every morning. The suite was great, complete with a good sized kitchen and balcony. The only slight let down was the bathroom, which could have done with a lick of paint, and the carpets could have done with a bit of a clean, but generally it was excellent, and extremely good value for money. The customer service at the hotel was really good, they left Hersheys kisses next to the bed every day, and in the evenings left us a card with the next days weather forecast on so that we'd be prepaped. The staff always had time to listen to you, and were full of suggestions and recommendations. The hotel is in a great location, just next to the walk of fame, right in the centre of Hollywood. I really can't recommend it enough. One night we went for dinner at the Magic Castle club, which is next door, and while it is a beautiful building, and the magic shows were spectacular, the food was overpriced and not very nice. I'd recommend going for the shows, but definitely not for dinner.

“Flawless” Booked a room using Priceline and was lucky enough to get the Omni San Francisco. The hotel pays attention to every detail, and I mean EVERY detail. Upon arrrival at the centrally located hotel, we were greeted by the doorman and others willing to help with baggage. There was a bit of a line at the check in desk and one of the bellmen quickly realized the need for additional resources. After advising those waiting he would secure additional help, he did just that. Soon the line was gone and everyone checked in quickly. The reservation was under my name but they allowed my wife to check in while I parked the car, simply asking that I return to the desk with my ID and credit card at some point durign our stay. Now that is service. When we arrived at the well appointed room, there was a hand written note from the housekeeper welcoming us. That is a first ever! That evening the room was turned down, chocolates were left and the television was tuned to a station that was entirely soothing music and beautiful scenes. Again, what an amazing touch. When we returned to the hotel on day 2, another hand written note from the housekeeper indicating she hoped we had a wonderful day, this time the note was personalized to us (vs. Dear Guest). We visited the bar as well and while the drinks were quite pricey ($15 for a martini) the atmosphere and service were perfect. I would highly recommend the Omni. Many others before me have given high ratings and I completely concurr. Excellent, absolutely excellent.

“Always a great experience” This is my second time staying at this hotel - both times for business. It is close to everything. The staff is always professional and easy to work with and the rooms are clean and well appointed. I would highly recommend this hotel as a great place to stay in Indianapolis.

“Love this place!” Excellent location, friendly staff, very interesting design of a hotel within a train station. Some parlor cars are made into bedrooms, very well furnished and elegant. There are life size characters all around (white statues really) depicting people one would see at a working railroad station. Some rooms are interior, i.e. windows do not open and overlook the pool or corridors. Hotel parking by valet OR self parking in underground garage right across the hotels entrance way; presently $18 per 24 hours. Free WiFi in rooms but somehow the TV reception in our room was mediocre; printed channel guide in room did not correspond with actual channel as appeared on TV set. Large bathrooms, fine bedding and central location make this a winner!

“Excelent Value” My first stay at this hotel in west LA. Read mixed reviews and glad I took a chance, because it was excellent all round. Service from staff was superior and all the rooms are in fact suites so even the basic accommodation has style, equipment and comfort. I particularly enjoyed the pool area and private jacuzzi - just what business travelers need at the end of the working day.

“Very Impressed” I was very impressed with the Ritz San Francisco. Beautiful hotel, great location. Room was very spacious and set up like a suite. Special cudos to the Concierge who set up some special requests including an exotic car rental and a tour of "hard to get access to" winery. Just what one would expect from the Ritz. Only misstep was that they promised to send a special chocolate desert to our room to make my wife's birthday, but it never came. Since they were 'on the money' with all the services we actually paid for I won't hold it against them.

“Fantastic Choice” This is my favorite hotel in the area...brand new and in a good central location. PLUSH beyond belief bed and beddings & attention to detail is a priority.Considering the value, this is better than a 4 star location. I would definitely return, as this is a wonderful hotel.

“Not so bad” I stayed here in January of 2007. This hotel is okay if you can get a good price. The room was small but in decent condition. The bathroom was in good condition and kept very clean. The room was drafty which is not good in January. Some people's reviews are very unrealistic. It is obvious that they don't travel often to NYC because they don't know how expensive it really is. That being said, I would not pay more than 150 a night to stay there.

“Okay” Located 2 blocks from space needle. This area is not central downtown so whilst it is probably quieter there's not much going on a felt a bit creepy - maybe just the time of year? Easy access to main downtown by monorail though which was good. Breakfast more than adequate. We didn't park so can't comment on that. Like all motels Walls a bit thin. If you need this area can recommend otherwise next find we would probably pay a bit more to be downtown

“Good hotel” This is a well-run hotel in a good location. Staff are friendly and attentive. The room was well-appointed with a very comfortable bed. Good quality toiletries are provided. The well-equipped kitchenette was a real plus. The subway, ATMs, grocer/food market, bakery, wine merchant, delis and restaurants are all close by. Next door to the Beacon Theatre but there were no noise issues. Would definitely stay here again.

“Great Location; Average Hotel” The best things going for this hotel are: - Location (very handy for Wall Street) - Free bottled water The rooms are small, but a good use of space. My room had a small TV, desk, a window unit a/c (which was good for white noise) and a clean bathroom with shower-only. I would actually stay here again, but I would request the following: - The front desk staff will push you to check in/check out at a selfservice kiosk For the amount you are paying for the room, you should be checked in/checked out by an actual person. This is important because during my stay, the kiosk would assign people to smoking rooms ... I had to spend my first night in a rather smelly room (I checked in late .. by the time I realised the smell was the room and not the entire hotel, I had to wait until the next day to swtich to a non-smoking room.)

“Very pleasant stay” I arrive late afternoon and the check in was quick and pleasant. The room was clean big and comfortable. I had a really nice sleep after a long flight. The only downside was the WiFi was not free, If you are a transit passenger in LAX it is really worth to stay here.

“Perfect location in Chicago” You simply can't beat the location of this property. It's only a couple blocks from Michigan Avenue and easily accessible to everything in the heart of Chicago. The atrium is impressive and remarkably clean. The breakfast omelette station was pretty slow and the lines at the managers reception were lengthy. The property is great though overall.

“Avoid like the plague” This is just an awful hotel. It's difficult to know where to start. Too few, too slow lifts. Internet that doesn't work properly,. Expensive food of very average quality. Noisy rooms. An unstaffed business centre that didn't have any paper for the printers and copiers. Oh I could go on and on. The staff try their best to overcome what clearly is a design and management crash site - but it is an uphill task.

“Good location and reasonable rates” This hotel is located adjacent to the RCA Dome and near the convention center. It also offers free parking for guests, which saves you anywhere from $12 up per day if you're driving. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The free continental breakfast is fairly standard. It's an easy walk to most downtown attractions. I stayed in a king studio suite, which is a very large room with a good work space and a refrigerator. Free internet was another plus. If you don't need the amenities of a fancier hotel, this place is an excellent value in downtown Indianapolis.

“Great location and service” Stayed at Westin for the second time in the last year. Service was very professional in the lobby and very polite when requiring a taxi or help with luggage. The maid service was excellent, our daughter was ill some of the time and they took really good care of us in the room. One minor issue is the handling of packages. If you order something to be delivered by post to the hotel it is dealt by the adjacent business centre who added $20 a package for the items that we had delivered. Technically the business centre is separate to the hotel but the fees were a disappointment.

“Nice rooms” We arrived at the hotel to learn that the reservation desk scheduled our arrival on Fri instead of Sat, so we did not have a reserved room but we had been charged for a no-show. Not a good way to start off a stay. No one could help with the erroneous charge until Monday, which is not good for customer satisfaction. Then, the Sat. night rate was higher than the Fri night rate, which was frustrating. To add to that, there is a $24 per night parking fee, even on weekends, that we were not aware of until we arrived. Adding $24 to the great rate I negotiated originally made it a not-so-great rate and adding it to the higher Sat night rate made this hotel a place I would not have stayed in considering I was going to be there for a total of less than 20 hours. All of that aside, it is a nice place. There was a wedding going on and the wedding party was taking over the lobby and bar area taking formal photographs (the wedding party was loud and using very colorful inappropriate/offensive language, but this was not the fault of the hotel) but once they finished the photos the area was open again to hotel guests. We ate dinner at the bar and the bartender, Steve, was great. The food was tasty but pricey (two cocktails, a burger and a garlic shrimp pasta dish cost $80). The room itself had a great desk area that would be ideal for a person on a business trip. Towels provided were for one person (one washcloth, two large towels) more were quickly brought up to the room when requested. The cord on the blow dryer was tied up in to some sort of knot -- that was inconvenient and took time to fidget with in the morning, The shower was large and had glass walls and doors and a great shower head. In the living room area of our suite I could hear all the hallway noise (there was a large, loud group next door) but the noise could not be heard in the bedroom area, which I was very happy about! The room charge for Friday could not be discussed or handled until Monday which tied up funds on my credit card but upon speaking with the accounting dept. Monday afternoon, the Friday charges should be off my credit card in 48 hours. Not ideal but better than never coming off my card. We were repeatedly told that for security reasons the front desk could not remove charges from a guests account, they could only charge the account. Something is wrong with a system that allows charges to be placed on an account easily but makes it difficult to have incorrect charges removed - just my opinion. If I was in the area again, I'd probably stay at the Courtyard, so I would not have to pay for parking and not have to deal with the wedding crowd in the lobby.

“Cold & Impersonal” Stayed three nights on business. First, the positives. 1. Location. Hotel is next to trolley station and close to public transportation. Cabs are right outside. No need to rent/bring a car. Easy walking distance to a lot of great restaurants as well. 2. View. My bayview room had a very nice view of the water. Some rooms clearly had spectacular views. Others obviously didn't. But if you have a water view, it's special. 3. Service. The service was generally good. No waits or lines, even though this very large hotel was hosting a convention. However, I couldn't escape the "plastic smile" syndrome. Everyone said & did all of the right things, but I couldn't get over the feeling that I was nothing but a number among a very large number of people. And now for the negatives. 1. Hotel Decor. You either love or hate the lobby. I agree with the reviewer who described it as 70s modern and cavernous. To me, it only added to the cold and impersonal qualities of the hotel. 2. Rooms. Nothing special. They are clean but have that somewhat dingy/not remodeled look. The sink area (outside of the bathroom) had been redone but they forgot the bath. It's tiny and in need of updating. You sort of want to get in and out of the tub/shower as quickly as possible. It really looks like a Motel 6. Amenities are bare minimum and mine weren't replaced for 2 days. Also, my room was oddly laid out. Sitting in the desk chair, you could not see the TV. Sitting in the lounge chair you couldn't see the TV. You either had to rearrange furniture or sit on the bed to watch TV. And, some rooms are a LONG way from the elevators. 3. Speaking of Elevators . . . there aren't enough and they are tiny. If two people with luggage get in the elevator, no one else can join them. 4. Club Level. Don't do it. You get continental breakfast, which is okay when they are prompt at replenishing food (sometime yes, sometimes, no). However, there aren't nearly enough seats in the "lounge." As a result, one morning people had to eat their breakfast standing up. The evening hors d'hoeuvres are weak and all service ends at 8 p.m. Soft drinks are free; alcohol will cost you (apparently due to CA law). 5. Internet. No wired service; only wireless for $10. I know a lot of folks mentioned problems with noise. I had none. Not sure if this was because I was on a high floor or if the crowd was quieter than usual. Overall, I came away with two impressions. First, they were trying to nickel & dime you to death. (Water in room is $6; fees in club lounge; they serve you coffee and OJ immediately upon being seated at breakfast -- before you find out it will set you back $8.50 + tax/tip). Second, it was just another huge hotel and you, the guest, are just another traveler passing through. I've stayed at several other SF hotels and, if I came again, would stay at one of those rather than return to the Hyatt. The experience wasn't terrible, it just wasn't terribly good.

“Very nice hotel - enjoyed our stay” We stayed for one weekended at this hotel, and it was a very pleasant stay. The room was large, clean, and furnished with modern new furniture. The kitchen was a good size for a hotel and had everything you need to cook and eat meals. There is even a 24 hour grocery store within a few blocks of the hotel. The hotel is not in the most busy part of downtown and requires a good bit of walking to get to those areas. However, it is in a very quiet area and there are plenty of good restaurants within a block or 2 of the hotel. An average continental breakfast is served daily consisting of bagels, danish, hard boiled eggs, oatmeal, etc. We thought it was good and sufficient. I would definitely return to this hotel.

“What every hip hotel should aspire to be...” Do you like the style of a W or small boutique hotel but you are sick of being treated like if you are not beyonce you have no right to exist? Then this is the hotel for you. Rooms are incredibly stylish (some of the nicest I've been in and I stay at 5* hotels), very comfortable with all needs thought of, no nickel and diming (free wifi, snacks soda and water in room), and a great attitude with the entire staff. Very nice gym ad rooftop bar / restaurant.

“Not bad for an airport hotel.” My flight was canceled and I had no choice but to stay over for the night. Going back into Seattle was not an option because I was re-booked for a flight departing at 5:40am. Given that it was already 10:30pm by the time my original flight was canceled all I wanted to do was go to sleep. The area at SEA_TAC where you wait for the hotel shuttles is full of fumes, ugly and overall unpleasant. This is no fault of the hotel but it does make for a good impression. Also, the wait for the shuttle seems like it took too long. Although the shuttle driver was quite pleasant. Check-in was a little slow as 10+ people exited the shuttle at the same time and all headed toward check-in. It would have been nice if there was a swing person at the front desk to accommodate the sudden influx of guests. The walk to the room was ridiculously long. The corridors seem to go on forever and ever. The carpets are hideous. Who designs those things?! The room was a amply sized with king size bed, nightstand, desk and chair, lounge chair, flat screen tv, and console. The bed was surprisingly comfortable with soft sheets, good pillows and a nice weight comforter. If it were not for the bed I would give a 3.5 rating to the hotel but the bed was so comfy that I boost the rating to a 4.

“A reliable choice” I usually stay in the Westin Waterfront when I stay in Boston, but it was full so I tried the Marriott on this occasion. This is a modern, elegant Marriott located on the Boston waterfront. i was given a large room with a king-size bed (internal view only - this won't suit everyone, but it was fine for me). Everything worked well, very clean and quiet, and lots of space to work and relax. The staff were friendly and efficient. Check-in was handled quickly. Had dinner when I arrived in the lobby restaurant. Had chowder and mussels - all fine and certainly better than many hotel restaurants I've tried.

“Nice little hotel in the Village” Hotel has a terrific location right on Washington Square in the Village. Rooms are NYC small. I had a Deluxe Queen which was about 11'x14' and faced out onto the Square--could be noisy at times but loved having a street view onto both MacDougal and Waverly. Free continental breakfast in hotel restaurant was an added plus. I paid $275/night in peak September period when other hotels were charging in excess of $300-$400 per night for basic accomodations. So, this wasn't a bargain but was a relatively good deal for that time of year. At other times of the year, better deals and accomodations can probably be found elsewhere. Hotel is one of the few family run properties left in NYC. Good management, some friendly employees and some not but not a deal breaker. Rooms are clean and generally well maintained. This is a good choice, if you can get a room at the right price, if you want to spend time living in vibrant Manhattan neighborhood, convenient to all the city has to offer. Not luxurious, but comfortable and clean.

“Nice stay, good Loop locaton” I stayed just one night for a business meeting. It's a very good location for business in the Loop, the Merchandise Mart, and is a short walk to the Art Istitute of Chicago, theater, and the opera. Macy's in the grand olf Marshall Field's building is a short walk away. It's not a bad walk to the tony mega-shopping district of North Michigan Avenue, although some may prefer a cab. While there are glitzier hotels, you can often get a good rate here since it is so large. You can spend the savings on a good dinner. The room felt recently renovated and very fresh (deatils below.) The public rooms are beautiful in a turn-of-the-last-century grandeur. I have visited the hotel a number of times over the years, and the most recent lobby redo is very welcome. There is a convivial bar and lounge area that makes for a very sociable atmosphere - some past years, the lack of furnishings made the place feel less inviting. Now it's back to being a social venue. Room 13157 had only a double bed as requested (usually there's more floor space when I ask for a smaller bed when I am staying alone than if the bed were larger or with two beds.) Very comfy bed and an assortment of pillows. The room does not set records for spaciousness, but it felt like a good size as a result. There is plenty of drawer and storage space, although the closet felt small with the retro-fit safe. The view of was of an alley and airshaft, but it was also quiet, if dark. The room ALMOST has all the typical business-class amenities (ironing board, hairdryer, toiletries, etc.) EXCEPT a coffee maker, which I miss having. Also: no minibar or fridge, which I don't miss. Spotless housekeeping throughout. Annoying things: there is the situation of the duvet without a top sheet, but you can remove the inside comforter easily if you are too warm and use the wool blanket stored in the closet. Also: there is an internet charge approx. $15, which I always find annoying, but less so since the rate was good. The bathroom is very small, although it also felt recently renovated. There is good counterspace to spread out. The tub doesn't fill as fast as I'd like, but at least there is a tub, contrary to the shower-only rooms that seem to be a renovation trend at other hotels. Very professional and friendly service throughout. The hotel had a nice promotion when I was there for guests: a $50 credit for any spa services at the on-site spa. Unfortunately, I was too busy to take advantage. There is a Starbucks at street level, and a newsstand/gift shop. Some complain about the high cost of parking at hotels and lots in downtown Chicago. Get used to it. It is approx. $40 self-park and $50 valet at this hotel, which is in line with many other hotels. The City of Chicago tries to discourage ANYONE from driving car in, and charges high rates even for city lots. There is the odd open lot here and there where you can get away with under $20 for an early-in or late-in rate, but its how it is downtown. While this hotel often charges a higher rack rate that you expect to Hilton policies, they often have very good rates at the last minute since this is a BIG hotel to fill up.

“Great location, nice room” This is a very nice (not exceptional) business class hotel in a great location for shopping on North Michigan Avenue. The room was fresh-feeling and not very spacious, but not cramped, either, i.e. typical of a renovated hotel from another era. The bed in room 1842 was comfy; the heat was "responsive" on chilly nights; the bathroom is good but not luxurious, although there was a nice range of toiletries and counter space to spread out. Exellent housekeeping. There were all the other things you expect of a good business-class hotel, e.g. in-room safe, coffee maker, etc. Since we were at leisure on a short stay, we did not test the internet connections or the fitness center (lots of power shopping and museums instead.) There is a $48/night parking charge, which is very typical for this area of Chicago. There are in/out privileges. I don't understand the complaint of another Tripadvisor poster re: having to wait in a cold garage -- the car was quickly brought around to the front when we wanted it. There are various restaurants and a Starbuck's on-site. We only used the Starbuck's and the cafe for breakfast since we were in the mood for eggs, panakes, etc. The latter was fine, and service excellent, although they should improve the coffee (can I bring in a Starbuck's?) There is also a more lavish breakfast buffet, but we generally don't go that route. The Eno wine/cheese/chocolate bar looked nice, but we were busy with other things. My usual complaint about these places: the music was grating Euro-techno-loud something, not conducive to sipping wine. I would have asked them to turn it down (or off) had we stayed for a while. The other complaint is minor and happens: we had difficulty checking in when the desk could not find our reservation, and this was one of the few times when I had the confirmation number buried somewhere. 'Can't say whether it was their fault or the cedit card tgravel agency we booked with (we used bill-back miles, using a good room rate) but even after checking both my husband's and names, there was still a no-go. We booked a spare room, and then settled it with out CC company and the hotel afterwards. For some reason, we were booked using my husband's first name as the last name. Someone should have thought about this possibility. The room in general was quiet, but it faces North Michigan Avenue to the north. The holiday lights were ablaze, but we could also hear the occasional siren going by. Still, the room was ready, and we could check in early. Everyone was very nice and polite. While not in the same league as a Ritz or Four Seasons, we'd be happy to stay here again. But then again, we good a good rate, not the posted rack rate that would put it in league with those other hotels.

“Beautiful Views” For a weekend trip to New York I decided to stay somewhere other than the usual Times Square area and decided to try out Ink48 in Hell's Kitchen--a great decision. The hotel was beautiful with excellent service. What really made it the perfect choice though was the room. I chose a Hudson River Suite and could not have been more satisfied--definitely worth the price. It had three "rooms"--a large bedroon area with a very large and comfortable bed with good lighting and a large tv, a living room area with a very comfortable couch, a desk with chair, and a comfortable chair, and a large bathroom between the two (with a hallway separating the bedroom and living room areas--no separate door; an opaque door closing off the bathroom. The bathroom was very large with 2 sinks, a separate shower and very large tub and a little nook with the toilet. The shower was very large with a rainforest shower-head but the star of the bathrrom was one of the largest tubs I've ever seen. Usually, I limit myself to showers but the tub was pretty inviting and I tried it out--it was great; had to force myself to get out to get to a show. The highlight of the suite, though was the incredible view. There are floor to ceiling windows along the entire length of the suite (except for a closet that is opposite the bathroom) and there were incredible views of the river. The hotel looked down on the Manhattan cruise terminal and the USS Intrepid (aircraft carrier museum). Beautiful views of the river and the city beyond the river--it really made for spectacular scenery both during the day and at night. (One downside is that although there are very effective shades to block out the sun, there are gaps between the shades to early morning light does get in.) The location proved to be particularly convenient for going to the Jacbo Javits Convention Center, the Intrepid Museum, and the Manhattan cruise terminal (I would definitely stay here for a pre- or post-cruise stay) but it also turned out within easy walking distance of Times Square and the Theater District (which I found out when I had difficulty getting a cab after a Friday night show). About a 15-minute walk down streets that did not seem unsafe (always had some pedestrian or car traffic). The immediate area around the hotel did not have much in terms of restaurants, but there were quite a few a block or so toward mid-town. One thing to watch out for is that the late-night (all day) menu is very limited and dinner service ends at 10:30 pm, so don't the mistake I did of waiting until after a show for a late night dinner (but I found a cheese plate and salad worked out okay). An earlier room service dinner I had the following night was fine--quick service and good food. Breakfast in the restaurant was also good. They have an afternoon wine reception (5:00 pm-6:00 pm), which I missed both days I stayed in the hotel, but it seems a nice amenity. I also missed on my chance to visit the bar that is supposed to have great views (it was closed one night for a private event, which is probably not that rare), but with the great views from my room I enjoyed a nice glass of wine from my room and enjoyed the views anyway. The suite has two closets--a relatively small one across from the bathroom and another one in the entry hall (which I used to staff my coats). There are also very comfortable bathrobes for use (in fact I had already bought one from a prior stay at a Kimpton hotel in Baltimore--another hotel I enjoyed). I drove to NYC and the hotel was pretty close to Lincoln Tunnel; parking is expensive ($55 a night--valet) but I found that it worked out well to just park the car and take cabs and walk to get around town. This turned out to be a great hotel choice; beautiful room and what turned out to be a very nice location.

“Meeting” Used this for a meeting and had good results. Easy to get to, staff helpful and friendly. Always plenty of parking and well lit, hotel grounds clean and well maintained and the value is very good considering all the services this hotel provides. Have always liked the location, it's close to airport, dinning and major highways.

“Great historic hotel which has been modernized.” The Hilton in downtown Ft Worth many years ago was known as Hotel Texas -- the hotel where JFK spent the night the day before he was killed in Dallas. The hotel is conveniently located, and everything in downtown Ft Worth is within walking distance. The rooms are large -- I had a king room the room included a couch, table and desk -- and was not crowded or cluttered. The bathrooms have lots of granite and plenty of room. The view is not much to brag about -- but that's often the case when you're in a downtown area. In addition to the regular New Year's Eve crowd, there are 2 football bowl games in town so the hotel was full!! The bed was wonderfully comfortable. The hotel staff very accommodating and of course TX friendly! Only valet parking is available -- unless you want to park a couple blocks away and walk over . . . but even then in the long run you'd probably end up paying the same $20 for parking, and not near as convenient as valet. Everything was spotlessly clean and we look forward to the opportunity to stay at this hotel again. The only drawback I experienced is a diet coke was $3.00 -- get real! And the vending machine only accepted credit cards.

“Super Lage, toller Preis” Wer ein Stopp-Over macht, um vom L.A. aus seine Kalifornien-Tour beginnen will, oder ein günstiges Hotel sucht, um ein wenig L.A. zu erkundigen, der ist hier genau richtig. Sauber, guter Service, tolle Lage direkt am Flughafen, große Zimmer, tolle Betten. Kein Super-Luxus-Hotel, aber bei Preisen deutlich unter 80 Euro ein tolles Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis. Starbucks ist unten im Hotel, damit ist auch für guten Kaffee gesorgt, in der Lobby war Internet kostenlos... Was will man mehr?

“Great Location; Will Stay Here Again” My wife, 4-year-old son, and I used Hhonors points and stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn for one night on October 19, 2008. We arrived around 11:30 am and were able to check-in. As a Gold Hhonors member, I was given a choice between Breakfast or 750 points. I chose breakfast and was given 6 coupons for breakfast, which I believe was a mistake, since you typically only get 2 per day. I also received coupons for 2 free bottles of water from the “snack shop”. Even though I only had one wheeled duffel bag, the use of the bellman was “pushed” on us. ROOM: We were in room 1107 which had 2 extremely comfortable queen beds. In addition to the beds, there was a desk with office chair, a cabinet with drawers, and a cabinet with a refrigerator, microwave and coffee maker. If you use the refrigerator, make sure it is turned on. I think they turn it off to conserve energy. There was a smaller than expected flat panel TV that had PPV movies available. There was also complimentary Internet in the room. Our room was in the “back” of the hotel, on the opposite side of 8th Ave. There was no view as there was an old building a few feet from our window. Although the hotel is across the street from a fire station, we didn’t hear any sirens loud enough to wake us at night. There is a safe in the room, but it uses a Key rather than a touchpad. The bathroom was small but clean. The toiletries were Neutrogena and consisted of Mouthwash, soap, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. They had switched the heating/cooling system to heating for the season, so even though it was a little warm outside, we could only use the heat and couldn’t get the room as cool as we would have liked. FOOD: The complimentary breakfast was in the restaurant attached to the hotel. When we entered, they asked if we had vouchers and gave us a separate menu that listed our choices. This was good because you knew exactly what you could order and there was no confusion. They had many choices including: pancakes, eggs, omelets etc. The food was good and we thought it was better than the free breakfast we had gotten a few months ago at the Hilton Times Square. There also seemed to be a lot of non hotel guests eating at the restaurant as well. OTHER: The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance to Central Park and Times Square attractions. There are also several different subway lines available within a few blocks. There is a parking garage right next to the hotel. Get your parking stub validated at the front desk for a discounted rate. Our rate would have been $68 (for ~28 hours of parking), but was discounted $13 to $55. We were able to have our bags held for us after we checked out. After picking up our bag later in the day, we planned on using the lobby restroom, but didn’t know it required a room key to enter. I would definitely recommend this hotel and it will be our first choice for future trips to New York City.

“I died and went to hotel heaven” After reading the horrible review, I was a little worried about this hotel, but was heartened by the other very positive experiences that the other past travelers had at the Ritz, and hoped my stay would be as good as theirs. I have to say, my stay exceeded all expectations. Upon arrival, due to the corporate rate my firm had paid, I was upgraded to the Club level. Because I was in town for a series of meetings that were all going to be held at the Ritz, this was a god-send. I never left the premises! Ate breakfast in the Club twice, lunch once, and did evening cocktails with a colleague who was also upgraded. It was fantastic, and I must recognize Darcy who was there both evenings and who could not have provided better service. One night, I even had my dinner delivered to the lounge on her excellent suggestion that I might be more comfortable eating there than from a tray in the room. And oh, what a room. The bed was heavenly (move over Westin) and the bathroom sublime. The only thing I don't care for at Ritz Carlton are the bathroom amenties -- a little over scented for me. The meeting space there is second-to-none, and all the food service was wonderful. I had nothing but excellent service from the front desk, to bellman, to concierge. This may have been one of my top hotel stays of all time.

“Excellent Price, Excellent Location!” Have stayed here before and was not disappointed, the stay this time was no different. The maid service was great and free muffins and coffee in the morning saved on breakfast. The staff was great with info and directions, save for the night-time emplyee who left much to be desired in the personality department, and no free internet, I would stay again.

“Agree with positive reviews” Our experience at ZaZa was great. The place is the refurbished Warwick hotel, enjoying an excellent location near several major museums and the medical center. The staff was friendly and attentive. We had a suite which, while not cheap, was good for the price. In other cities a suite with this much room and furnishing would have been much more expensive. It was clean and in good condition, although the couch bothered my wife and mine's allergies (we're allergic to dogs and the hotel does allow pets though they charge a fee for cleanup after they leave). We brought 2 small children and enjoyed ourselves even though the hotel appears to cater to a more adult clientelle. The pool area was excellent but we were there before mid-morning when it became swamped with adult guests. It might be a different place at different times of day. I had a deep tissue massage in the spa which was great but did cost more than it would have in other spas. The spa itself is beautifully decorated and was heavily booked with guests so be sure to reserve in advance if it's important to your stay. Some free amenities and treats in the room were appreciated given the overall cost of the place, giving a welcome feel. The food in the hotel is excellent. We're looking forward to going back soon but I don't recommend this place to anyone who's trying to travel on a tight budget.

“Comfortable” This hotel is built in a strange configuration so you end up taking long walks on long corridoors on different levels to reach you room. However having got there it was worth it - I had a suite which had a Kitchen and sitting room with a fireplace. Bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was a nice size - No safe in the room was the only amenity that I was wanting for, Complimentary breakfast in the lobby was no frills but fine. Great location near the Space Needle and the Gates foundation , just a 15 minute walk or so into the City . Happy to recommend.

“Good hotel, if not terribly interesting” I stayed here during a business trip and was satisfied overall. The staff was accommodating and helpful. Rooms were clean and neat. I liked the use of rock motifs in the decor in homage to the famous Austin limestone. The hotel was rather standard otherwise, which is fine for business, since you want no-frills competence. Decent breakfast buffet. I wish elevators were not so slow. I lived on the 20th floor and sometimes had to wait close to 5 minutes for the elevator and then had to stop on every floor. They should make separate elevator banks which go to 10 floors each.

“Enjoyable stay” Stayed 3 nights over Labor Day, large hotel, nice corner room on high floor. Internet was $13.63 I believe, try facebook word of the week, for a free day. Nice bathroom, though no hook for towels, only underneath of cabinet folded, so they can’t dry. Hotel will only change towels & linens, if you ring and ask, no leaving them on the floor. Good desk area, location good a little too far east could be more central.

“Nice weekend visit - but packed with conventioneers!” Stayed here for the weekend to go to a Cubs game and visit family and friends. We were very pleased on arrival - front desk staff couldn’t have been nicer, noting we were SPG members and thanking us for our stay even though we booked a low rate through Hotwire and weren’t in the SPG system for this stay. Our room was ready when we arrived on a Friday morning at 10am, so we were happy to be able to drop our things, do a little work, and freshen up before the game. The room overlooked the city with a sliver of Navy Pier visible in the distance, though the weather was so foggy we hardly saw it all weekend. Rooms with two double beds were comfortable enough, though a hotel of this quality should really have two-queen rooms instead. Bathroom was old with standard fixtures – didn’t feel like a four-star hotel bathroom, honestly – but was clean. Room overall was fine but there seemed to be a layer of dust on everything – housekeeping could definitely be more thorough. “Sweet Sleeper” beds were as comfortable as advertised and we all slept very well. Big-screen flat screen TV was great, but the clock-radio was old-style with no iPod dock. There was a party going on in the room next door to us on one of the nights and we heard some noise but it definitely could have been worse. There were several conventions in the hotel while we were there, so the huge lobby was always hopping. There are a couple of ‘game tables’ with built-in video games – including old school games like checkers – that were declared the highlight of the place by the youngest member of the party. We didn’t even notice the internet café on the bottom floor until our last day when we were permitted to print our boarding passes there for free – looked like a good place if you needed to jump online for a few minutes but I don’t know what the fee is. In-room internet was $12.95/day, I think, so we used the hotspot in our smartphone instead. Overall, totally fine for a weekend stay, and would probably be great for a convention. We’ve stayed at other hotels in the neighborhood that are more suited for families but had problems finding a good rate for this weekend, so the Sheraton did just fine. We didn't rent a car until the last day when we left to visit people in the suburbs and go to the airport because at $49/night, parking was much too much. It's just a few blocks from public transportation which was just fine. The hotel is just a few blocks from our favorite breakfast spot West Egg Cafe, and we visited Sue the Dinosaur at the Field Museum while we were there, too.

“Find another hotel!!!!” I travel a lot and am used to very few places being perfect. But do yourself a favor and find another hotel in Washington. I signed up for the Washington Plaza because it was supposed to be close to the convention center. It really isn't, you'll need to take a cab anyway. The staff wasn't rude, they just were not helpful at all. The room was poorly furnished with the lowest quality furnishings, bed covers, curtains...everything seemed very, very cheap. My window looked right into apartments next door. There was major constuction going on each morning at 8 am in the area and it was very noisy. I had to pay $194.00 a night and felt totally ripped off.

“Good hotel” This hotel is a standard Hyatt Place and everything was as expected (free continental breakfast, HDTV in room with nice couch and ottoman). Only complaint is I reserved king room and received 2 queens because they were out of kings.

“Good for what you need” This is a great location, it is right in the Fashion District, so in the evening after all the wholesale stores closes, you don't have alot of traffic or noise around. This location is close to Madison Square Garden, down a few blocks from Whole Foods, and easy access to subway on both sides. If you're too early for check-in or you're not leaving a while after check-out, they are kind enough to lock up the luggage for you. They have 2 elevators with 25 floors of guests, so it may take a bit when you call of the elevator but it's not intolerable. The hotel front desk staff were friendly, but the housekeeping staff never remembers to give us wash cloths. I've called them 3 out of the 5 nights to ask for it and while they do deliver them, they do not keep any at the front desk. The concierge has an agenda to push the boat cruise, but can tell us nothing about it and was giving it a hard sell too. When asked about show tickets, they quote us the highest price. Of course, that's because they're going thru an agent so you're paying 2 commission essentially. Go to TKTS or do the lottery at the box office of the show. Popular show or not, they always work.

“Sehr gutes Hotel mit tollem Blick auf Ground Zero” Hotel allgemein: Das Hotel beansprucht die ersten 30 Etagen eines auch zu Wohnzwecken dienenden Gebäudes aus dem Jahr 2010. Wie für W-Hotels aus der Starwodd-Gruppe üblich wird hier der Schwerpunkt auf das Thema "Design" gelegt. Durch den Eingang an der Albany Street gelangt man it dem Fahrstuhl in die Lobby in die 5. Etage. Von hier aus stehen dann weitere Aufzüge zur Verfügung. Lage und Umgebung: Ausreichend zentrale Lage am Ground Zero; die Subway "Rector Street" (Linie 1) ist unmittelbar um die Ecke; weitere Suvway-Stationen sind fußläufig erreichbar. Bedingt durch die zahlreichen Baustellen um den Ground Zero herum, muss man teilweise Umwege (zum Beispiel Richtung PATH am Worl Trade Center) hinnehmen. Service: Stets freundliches und sehr bemühtes Personal; die Zimmerreinigung war stets ohne Beanstandungen. Zimmer: Sehr schön eingerichtete Zimmer im "Designer-Stil". Die Zimmergröße von rund 30qm geht in Ordnung. Das Bad ist zwar recht überschaubar, jedoch mit einer schönen Walk-In-Dusche ausgestattet. Die Aussicht aus den "Spectacular-Zimmern" auf den Ground Zero ist sehr gut; die Lärmbelästigung durch Bauarbeiten hält sich (bei geschlossenem Fenster) in Grenzen bzw. in einem kaum mehr wahrnehmbaren Bereich - New York ist halt nahezu überall eine recht laute Stadt.

“Needs an upgrade” I booked this hotel with the idea that Sheraton Hotels, in general, are usually 4/5 stars in quality. I was, however, quite disappointed in this Sheraton Hotel. Coming from Canada, the Sheratons generally appear to be more consistently of a higher quality. Part of the Starwood group of hotels, the Sheraton hotels are branded alongside the Westin and W Hotels. If you have the cash, I would suggest you would have better luck in getting consistently high calibre hotels by selecting the WESTIN brand of hotels. Both the Sheraton and Westin Hotels co-exist in major cities around North America. During my leisure trip to Dallas, I stayed in three hotels. In order of enjoyment: 1. Four Seasons Hotel Resort and Club Dallas at Las Colinas 2. Hyatt Regency Hotel Dallas 3. Westin Galleria Hotel Dallas 4. Sheraton Suites Market Center Hotel Dallas My ranking of the Sheraton at the bottom of this list does not indicate that it lost by a WIDE margin. It cannot be even categorized in the same CLASS as the other hotels I have mentioned. When I checked into my room, I was disappointed to find the furnishings of a 1970's/1980's-era. The same kind of furnishings (sofa, for example), could be found in a used-furniture bargain center. The style and quality of fabric was poor. While the room did have a small fridge/cooler, there was no mini-bar to speak of. The interesting thing was that there was a sink in the "bar area". The quality of the washroom was disappointing. The shower/tub was pretty old. My sink faucets were dripping/leaking water. The sink faucets were very old and cheap-looking. The sink/bathroom quality reminded me of cheap rental housing you would find in bad parts of town. The only thing to redeem the hotel is the quality of the bed. The sweet sleeper bed is probably the only thing this hotel has in common with the other Sheraton Hotels. I used the small fitness room on the main floor of the hotel. The equipment was pretty standard-fare. Compared to other above-average hotels, the equipment was pretty low-end. At the time, I only saw cycling machines and no elliptical machines (which I prefer). There was a television in the fitness room. The indoor swimming pool was pretty small. Not long enough for good lane swimming. Neither the fitness room nor the pool looked very used. I did visit the restaurant/pub in the evening. It had pretty standard American food. Nothing really fancy on the menu. They had a big screen television in the background. The restaurant shared a common area and entrance with the "pub" which is where the television was located. At the time I went to the "pub", the restaurant was closed. Service was acceptable. When I called the front desk to discuss the leaky faucets in my washroom when I checked-in, they said someone would be sent up to fix it. Nobody came. I mentioned this to the hotel manager at check-out time and he proceeded to reduce my bill by about $40 USD. I ended up paying about $90 USD + taxes. When reading the other reviews of this hotel, I cannot believe people can possibly rate this as their "#1" favorite hotel in Dallas! While the price is much better than other hotels (like the Westin Galleria Dallas) I stayed at, this hotel does NOT deserve the Sheraton brand name. It would be more suited as a Holiday Inn Express or something in the 2/3 star category. Hope this helps. If money is not too big a concern, a Westin Hotel will always be better than a Sheraton Hotel. Westin Hotels also feature the "Heavenly Bed" AND the "Heavenly Bath"... which feature dual-shower heads. A great plus for comfort and luxury. Although this hotel is convenient if you are travelling for business (it is across from a conference center), people travelling for pleasure/fun should stay AWAY from this hotel. I hope this review helps your decision-making.

“Great Business Hotel near Hutchinson Cancer Center” I came to town for two nights to give a lecture at the University of Washington and the Cancer Center. They put me up here. Overall, I'd give this hotel very high marks. The staff was friendly and helpful, the location is excellent (on a street car line, next to the cancer center, with restaurants across the street). The complementary breakfast was excellent, the rooms clean and fully functional. Mine had a kitchenette, although I had no need for it. The hotel also provides an evening snack that could count as a light meal with free beer/wine (while inviting a voluntary contribution for a local charity). Free internet access was also provided. There's also a refrigerated display case of foods and deserts (for purchase) in the lobby (great if you have urgent need of an ice cream fix at 10 pm) and a nice lobby lounge with three sets of newspapers daily (local, WSJ, and USA Today). One tip, a private car service offers airport transportation from the hotel to SEA airport. It's about $10 less and easier to schedule than a taxi. The front desk can set it up.

“Groovy Bed and Fine Room” I got this room for less than 1/3 the rack rate from an online auction site. I was in town for my sister's wedding and the wife and I did not want to stay with my parents who had gone crazy with wedding stuff. The location is great - right off the highway in an upscale suburb next to HP's local headquarters. The room was large and clean and the bed was the bed we've ever had in a hotel. We would highly recommend it, especially on weekends when its normal crowd of HP trainees isn't there.

“A true Experience” The entrance is not like almost every other hotel I have been. It's hip, trendy, feng shui, it's a warm welcome. The rooms are big and well decorated with sofa's, good quality off beds, and spacouis. The wine reception at Krimpton Hotels every day s a great thing to give the customers a great feeling. It's hard to explain sometimes, but it's the feeling you get when you stay in this hotel. The restaurant Urbana has delicious food. And every morning free coffee and tea in the lounge, that's their entrance called.

“tucked away gem” bathrobes are cheetah print -not plain white. yoga mat, pilates block and band avail for workout in your room. healthy room service menu also a plus for the business traveller who wants an option other than homefries! they can also arrange a pet goldfish for your stay if you get lonely. good wifi if you signup to kimpton loyalty program which is free. not the best location (close to TD Garden & T stop) but not that much else around apart from pizza places. staff friendly and helpful!

“Optimales Preis-Leistungsverhältnis” Ich kann mich den anderen hervorragenden Bewertungen nur anschließen. Ich war für fünf Nächte dort, 90$ plus Tax bezahlte ich. Das Zimmer war ausreichend groß, zumindestens für mich allein. Die Lage ist gut, eine Buslinie, die quer durch San Francisco führt, fährt direkt in der Nähe los. Das Zimmer wurde immer tip top gereinigt. Das Personal an der Rezeption war immer hilfreich. Für den Preis einfach unschlagbar.

“Very Nice Place!!!!” I stayed in a 3-bedroom suite at the Granduca to visit my father who was having treatment at the nearby MD Anderson Cancer center. The suite was very spacious and just about everything in it was great. The master bedroom was huge as well as the master bath and space is definately not a problem in this place. We stayed in the 2nd master bedroom and were very comfortable. The bed was huge and very soft, but the pillows were very uncomofortable and we brought our own from Kansas City. The shower for the 2nd master is shared with the 3rd bedroom and is pretty nice. There are 2 vanities in the master bathroom and only 1 vanity in the 2nd bathroom, which is not that big of a deal if you do not have a fully occupied suite. However, you would think that a place with the quality of the Granduca would have a bathroom for each bedroom. The dining room and living room were great and had tons of room. The TV in the living room was HDTV and was huge and great for watching sports or movies on the DVD player. You could even order movies in HDTV through the TV if you wanted to. The full kitchen was also a great feature and it is a great thing to have the ability to cook your own meal if you wanted to. I used to excercise room once during my stay and was very impressed with the equipment. All of the equipment was top of the line and it was nice to be able to watch TV while I worked out on the elliptical. The pool and hot-tub were right outside from the main lobby and looked very nice. However, since the weather was cold and rainy we never got to take advantage of the pool facilities. Each morning a complimentary breakfast was served near the bar area and it was pretty basic. They had all of the basic stuff (cereal, fruit, bread, eggs, tea, coffee, etc.) and it was not very impressive. However, the breakfast was complimentary and it was nice to have a free breakfast every morning. There was no restaurant in the hotel which I found quite odd for a hotel of this stature. You could order room service from the restaurant next door for some pretty hefty delivery charges if you really wanted room service. Overall, I would have to say that this hotel is a great extended stay hotel and does not have all the features that a full service hotel might have. If I were staying in Houston for a short amount of time I might stay in a hotel that is fully featured.

“Modern and fun” My family and I did an overnight in NYC and got a very good deal at Eventi. Although they had overbooked and didn't have the room we'd reserved, they did give us 2 rooms instead. The rooms were great - a little small, but that's normal in NYC, and for what we paid (about $230) it was a great deal. The rooftop terrace on the 5th floor was a good place for coffee and to take in the view. Foodparc next door, which belongs to Eventi, is a fun place to eat with kids, you order your food at touchpad kiosks and pick up. The food was ok, nothing great, but prices were reasonable. The service staff in the hotel was friendly, but seemed a little distracted when there were large crowds in the lobby. Overall we enjoyed our stay and would come back here.

“Wonderful service” My partner and I stayed in a King room for one night in September predominately so we could go to the Magic Castle, and the hotel didn't disappoint. After staying in 4 other hotels during our holiday in the US, it was the only place that felt like home and we both slept like logs.The service is impeccable - from the drink offered at checkin, to the special touches like a free mini bar service, 24 hour access to the pool and the extra efforts the staff go to ie. allowing us to return to the hotel to have a shower before our late night flight home to Australia and even driving us up the small hill to the Magic Castle due to me wearing heels! It's not the cheapest hotel in Hollywood - but definitely the best value for money, and you can't beat the location. I'd thoroughly recommend and will definitely be back

“Typical Holiday Inn Express” This hotel is right on the edge of downtown and is easy to walk all over the area-even into Juarez. It has a nice SW look and is what you would expect from this chain. A couple of door showed signs of battle fatigue but still would close. It is clean and everyone is friendly and helpful.

“Good value for a Good price” We had a Travel Zoo deal for $109. a night. We stay in Boston a lot and this was our first time at this hotel. Room & bed were comfy, smallish, window opened, which is a plus. We parked in the lot across the street for 24 hours for $24.00. Easy walk to Fenway Park about .5 mile. We went to the Rolling Stones and the location was fine. We'd stay there again if we could get that price. I don't think I'd [pay more than $150.) because there are alot of great hotels in the area and if you look around there are alot of deals, (weekends, anyway).

“everything you need in NYC.” I'm not sure if Nicolas who checked us in could actually be any nicer or more helpful. He was a delight to encounter and a real asset to the reception team. Upon check out the team were also very cheery which I feel is a good reflection on the management. you would imagine that this is the standard through the chain - but believe me - it isn't. As SPG platinum members we were given an upgrade to a higher floor room and given a small goodie bag with a copy of Time Out, a bottle of water and some cookies. a very nice start to our stay. The rooms are not overly big but they are very comfortable, clean and with a very comfortable bad and coffee facilities. There are the standard toiletries plus mouth wash, cotton wool, shower cap and dental floss which is leaps and bounds better than some of the other Four Points hotels we have recently stayed at. There were only 8 rooms on the floor (I think) so it was very quiet and we slept very well. There is a bar and an Italian restaurant on the ground floor with a small sitting outside area, we didn't try these as we already had plans. The hotel is very convenient for shopping, restaurants/bars and for the metro. I'd definitely recommend this hotel and we will probably be back. You guys did a great job. Thank you !!

“Nice hotel on a great location” We booked at the last minute just for one night. What a great choice this was. The rooms are nice and well appointed. The front desk staff is very cordial, efficient and accomodating. What a location this place has Broadway, Time Square you are a block away from the center of NYC. We have found our new home base when going to NYC!

“Great location and hotel” This hotel is in a great spot for walking along the Embarcadero waterfront, catching the F tram to Fisherman's wharf, or using the Bart to get other places (including the airport). There are also convenient buses to get out to places we like to visit such as the deYoung Museum and the associated Legion of Honor Museum. It's walking distance to SFMoma and either a hike to the Museum of Asian Art, or 3 Bart stops. Many of the rooms have great bay or Bay Bridge views (they usually cost extra). There used to be a revolving restaurant on the top of the hotel, but now it is the hotels Regency Club space. For us this is well worth the extra cost since one can get free continental breakfast with a good selection, coffee and soft drinks are available all day and cookies are available in the afternoon. From 5 to 8 there are substantial hors d'oeuvres and an honor bar with reasonable prices (beer $4, wine $5 and hard liquor $6). In spite of San Francisco's great food reputation our recent restaurant experiences there have not been as good as in some other places we visit (New York, DC, Paris, London) and since the main purpose of our visit is to suck in the atmosphere and re-visit a few sites (especially museums) we have taken to getting some lunch and using the Regency club for a light dinner and several glasses of wine, which makes its additional cost a bargain. In the past we have only stayed at this hotel using Hyatt Gold Passport points but we recently ran out since I have found that the Hilton group program is better for us because it has far more hotels around the world. However, even at $450/night we decided this was a better choice overall in SF than the Hilton options. Incidentally, if you are going to use local transport for several days (buses, trams, Bart) it might be worth while getting a Clipper Card, which avoids having to get small bills or change. Except for the Cable Car, the fare on a bus or tram is currently $2 - or only $0.75 if you are a senior. I think you can order a regular Clipper card online. You can only get a senior card (or youth card) at a designated service center - there is one in the Embarcadero Bart station, right outside this Hyatt. We bought one each for future use. (The regular one-way fare from the airport will be $8.25 after July 1, 2012, while the senior/youth fare will be $3.05.)

“very disappointed” Nice lobby disguises the motel rooms. Outdoor balcony leading to the rooms overlook the trash area of the restaurant and loud employee entrance. Free wireless internet doesn't work in the room nor the lobby. Hair in the bathroom and non-working HVAC. Never again.

“Lovely :)” Stayed there with my boyfriend on the 11th of September. The hotel is very well kept. It makes a great impression from the outside - all from gold and very clean. Valley parking. (a little pricey - $44 for one night). Room rate was a good price - i think $130 for a night - considering the quality & location you cannot complain. Room very very spacious - we got a corner room maybe thats why? very clean - bed so comfortable - had an amazing nights sleep! maybe because i ve been in 4 different hotels in last 3 days so... but no bed was amazing. bathroom spacious enough. shower - heavenly shower - enough said! you do not want to leave. view was good - there was no late check outs, although you can store luggage for free which was a nice touch & also the bellman brings your luggage to you on a trolley. very classy. The funniest about our stay was that we were trying to open the window and we hit the drapes by accident and a mini bottle of vodka fell out of it! we done the same to the other drapes just for fun and we also found vodka there! we found it really funny - seemed like an easter egg hunt! apart from everything else the hotel is HUGE! the only drawback is that someone on out floor was smoking.....weed. i mean even if somene hasnt done it before they were deffinitely passive smokers. i mean smell was everywhere!! nothing else to say - lovely hotel to stay in - especially for my last night in America with my boyfriend.

“Great hotel and a decent location” I stayed here for three nights on business in early January 2005. I would highly recommend staying in this hotel if you are in the DC area. It seemed to be a very new hotel (as opposed to an old one that has been renovated). The suite was spacious and the bed was quite comfortable. The staff was friendly and courteous. The free breakfast buffet was very good (hot and cold items). I did not partake in any of the evening meals, so I cannot comment on it. There are 2 subway stops within a reasonable walking distance (do not pay attention to a previous review that says 6-8 blocks, it is incorrect). The McPherson Square station (orange and blue lines) is about 3-4 blocks south (brisk 8 minute walk). The Farragut North station (red line) is about 5 blocks southwest (brisk 11 minute walk). The hotel was nice and quiet (but my room was at the very end of the hall). Nice work area with free high-speed internet access (wired). I would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Impossible to Overrate This Hotel” I love everything about this hotel. To me, it feels like home. The lobby, the staff, the rooms, the location, the food & drinks... everything is perfect here. It is the picture of old southern hospitality. The ducks are cute, they are not why I stay at the Peabody. I stay here because it makes me happy, there is a warmth to the people here, to the atmosphere, to the decor even. It is worth every dime, and anyone who complains about it simply has expectations that are unrealistic - and I work in the hotel industry and have stayed in the best and the worst - and I tell you, this is the BEST. I cannot imagine why anyone would not love it here.

“suprised” I was surprised here. For the PRICE... As it was a good deal on a very last minute stay. Room was good.. but small lobby was clean. service seemed okay.. only a night... hallways are old ... but overlooked

“would definitely stay again” I have stayed at this hotel twice now and really like it. I find it relatively quiet and has wonderful views of the river-- so try to get a room with a river view!! I have switched from the loop W which was a bit to kinetic and like this hotel's convenient but not right in the middle of everything location. I tend to take the blue line in from ohare and is a very short work from the clark an lake stop. My room has always been spacious, and very attractive but as someone else wrote not over the top. The hotel was formally a Nikko and still has a slight zen asian look.

“Great location but very busy” We stayed here 4 years ago. Same great location, and they've renovated some rooms. On check in as Marriott elite, it was very fast with a truly separate line for elites (3 check-ins as a matter of fact!) I was there on points, and got a nice room. The main problem with this hotel is the vast number of people. There about 15 elevators, but they are often slow and jam-packed on the weekends. My main problem was the group of very loud and obnoxious drunk girls in the room next door. Had to call security 3 times: 2AM, 3AM, 4AM. Got moved to another room the next night, which was much more quiet! I'd return again.

“Nice place on the Riverwalk” This is the 3rd time I have stayed at the Marriot RIverCenter for a conference. This is a very nice, but pricey hotel. Its nicer than the older Hyatt down the riverwalk and the other Marriot across the street. The food was very good. I had a room service steak on the first night and it was excellent (for room service). The staff was very pleasant and Courteous. The room was small thsi time, but I have had larger rooms here I think. One nice thing for a conference hotel is that its not all spread out, so the walking is pretty minimal. Also the HDTV FLat Panel was nice, but they need more chanels. The only minor issues I had was some trash left in the room and that they charge for internet access ($10.71 per day). But I am sure Ill be staying here again and always look forward to being at the riverwalk.

“Disappointing Experience” i arrived with 16 yr old daughter and her friend on Friday of Lollapalooza around 12:30. They went to concert, hotel was a zoo and rooms were not ready till 3. I had been up all night. I sat in the lobby for 2 hours where it was horribly loud, crowded and the muzak was screaming. Finally I went to a small room off the lobby, put down my 3 pieces of luggage and put my head down for 30 min. I was awakened by a security guard who told me I could not 'sleep on the floor" I explained that I was exhausted, waiting for a room, but he made me move. Next, i checked in with my HHonors number. The clerk replied" you haven't used this in six months". That's all he said. not welcome, nada. I checked into the small dark room on 13th floor room 244 where I had a view of a brick wall. The room had no coffee maker, nor did it have a refrigerator. The next day, the room attendants did not replace the dirty glasses, nor did they dust the furniture or vacuum beneath the bed., I went to the workout room where I was charged $10 to use a treadmill and bike. The pool was too short to do laps. The hotel also has no free internet, just free boarding pass. The final straw was when I checked in my luggage the last day. The tall fellow said in a rude way "THANKS SO MUCH" when I didn't have a tip. i was out of cash and came back with money to tip on picking up the luggage. However, he was quite rude. I stay in Chicago every year, sometimes twice. This hotel is no different than a Motel 6 for what it offers. The food and drinks are overpriced. The employees are rude. I will never ever recommend this property to anyone.

“A gem!” I frequently stay at Starwood properties, but I believe this was my first stay at a Luxury Collection hotel. The US Grant was definitely worth the 16000 points per night. We came for a one night stay, and were very impressed by the beauty of the lobby and our room. The robes, slippers, and toiletries were great, and the bed was extremely comfortable. What was most impressive was the friendly and helpful staff, including the coffee barista, the restaurant staff, the front desk personnel, and the concierge. The location is great, with a lot of wonderful restaurants and shops within walking distance. We hope to come back some day.

“Clean, Decent, pleasant” Spent one night here on business. Easy check-in, clean + pleasant room, convenient location, nice low-key italian restaurant downstairs. Low-frills, probably best for business. Lobby is quite bare. For $200 a night, there are much better places to stay in New York.

“Clean and modern hotel close to the airport.” A nice option close to the airport, but they do not offer room service. You can order from local pizza or Chinese restaurants and will deliver right to your room.

“Comfortable Hotel in a Quiet Neighborhood” I spent one night in the Kitano on my way home from an international trip. Having previously lived in the city I wanted a quiet hotel with easy east-side subway access (Grand Central is a few blocks away). Wary of tiny NYC hotel rooms I booked a premier room. I didn't realize I'd been upgraded to a junior suite until now; the check-in agent should have told me as upgrades always make people feel good! The suite looks exactly like the photos on the hotel's web site and is very large for 1 or 2 people. The room was quiet and the bed (and especially the pillows) extremely comfortable. I had no problem getting the room quite cold, the way I like it, and the water pressure in the shower was amazingly powerful. Like another reviewer I appreciated the electric kettle and green tea. (If you want coffee but want to avoid Starbucks there is a Joe's in Grand Central or Aroma Cafe on 42nd.) The hotel is in a residential area but easily accessible to Grand Central and the Empire State Building on foot; a short subway ride puts you at Union Square or SoHo. There's many great restaurants nearby, including Wolfgang's for steak, Artisanal for a bistro with a huge cheese selection, and Saravanaas in Curry Hill for amazing south Indian vegetarian (81 Lex at 26th - don't go to the imitators). I didn't interact with the staff too much, the but desk agents and bellman were friendly and welcoming.

“Hotel is fine, not as great as other Le Meridiens” I stayed previously at Le Meridien in Dallas and really enjoyed the hotel, and decided to try out the San Francisco location. It was fine but did not meet my expectations, unfortunately. I expected modern, clean, and new. The SF hotel is more dated, with older furnishings, slow elevators, and a stuffier feel than I expected. I stayed in 2 different rooms over 2 weeks, and while the 1st had floor to ceiling windows in the bathroom (odd location) and a balcony with a view of the bay which were nice, the 2nd room I stayed in had a weird odor like cigarettes when you entered the room. Luckily it didn't linger and the room smelled fine otherwise after you entered. There are high-end finishes, but they look dated. The mattresses seemed old, as you could clearly feel the divots on either side where everyone previously had slept. The lobby and elevators do play a fantastic mix of music though, which I really liked. It's in a good location within the financial district, and you have easy access to great restaurants, touristy sites, and a lot of corporate offices (for the work traveler). The people working at the hotel were very friendly and helpful and remembered me when I checked in the 2nd time. While it was conveniently located near the office I was visiting, I didn't see many other reasons to stay at this hotel again. It was fine, but not great.

“Some good,some not so good..” Good location and very easy walking distance of practically everything you'd want to see in Boston. We had a good room overlooking post office square. Nice touches like roses and chocolates (it was our wedding anniversary). Breakfast was acceptable but not memorable for $25 a head. Reception on arrival was impersonal and overly formal which contrasted sharply with all other staff we came into contact with who were delightful,friendly and helpful. My irritation with the Langham is their charging policy. Charging for the internet in these days of high technology where Wi fi is freely available in cafe's and public places appears stingy. Charging $4-8 dollars for " small bites" with drinks in the Bond bar ,when other high end hotels will give you small plate of nibbles with your drink, appears mean and the $42 per day valet charge is eye watering.I am aware they are a business and need to make a profit but if there is a perception in the customer's mind of profiteering rather than making a profit, they are getting it wrong.

“Great value for NYC” I'm giving it 4 stars because for the money, you can't do much better. First, the front desk staff was nice, and they paid attention to the comments I made when reserving.
