Our room was small, but it was a good use of space and the layout was very functional. It was clean, modern, and well kept. We were facing another building, so there was no street noise at all. We had some noise from the hallway at times, but that's kind of the luck of the draw with hotel "neighbors". In-room lighting could have been better, but other than that, there was nothing to complain about. Location was fine. We walked to and from Grand Central Station, and from Times Square at night after seeing a show. The street the hotel is located on was a little more "dead" at night than I felt comfortable with, but we didn't experience any problems. I did feel as though the front desk should have been checking ID's at night, as they've done in the other NYC hotels I've stayed in. However, the bottom line is that I'd stay there again.

“Nightmare - stay away ” After reading all the great reviews here, we decided to try this hotel. It was a complete nightmare!\ First, they tried to charge me for an extra night despite the fact that the manager had communicated to me that would be happened. Then she (the receptionist, one of the rudest people I have ever met) refused to honor the rate I had booked the room at. Thank goodness I had printed out the confirmation. She was nasty about the revised rate. Then she gave us a room that barely fit our luggage, much less a rollaway-again, the confirmation showed we had requested a rollaway. So she pulled a bait and switch and offered us a suite for $75 more, we were exhausted so said we would take it. What a disaster! The pullout couch had a huge hole in it, there was no one to make up the bed and the air conditioner didn't work (which she also refused to believe). It was worn, small and smelled. We left, went to the Fairmont where they treated us like royalty. Just goes to show you get what you pay for

“Got the Best Room in the House--4036!” My husband and I just returned from the Marriott Marquis in NYC today. I wanted to write this review while I still remembered every detail of our visit. We stayed for 4 nights and had a fabulous time. The hotel was very clean, quiet, and not any more expensive than the other hotels in the Times Square/Broadway area. If you are looking for a hotel to spend New Year's Eve in, this is the place. They have "Ball Drop View Rooms" available for New Year's Eve that can be booked by calling the hotel directly. I am sure they are EXPENSIVE, but this hotel by far has the best view. Actually, the ball drop is filmed for TV from this hotel! I was torn between rating this hotel as "excellent" or "above average". We only had two problems during our stay. The first was at check in. After navigating the subway from JFK, we arrive at the check in desk only to be informed that the room we reserved was not available. Well, let me explain. It was available, but it would be "$60 dollars more per night." When we reserved a room, we called the hotel directly. My husband was on business and got a special rate that was offered through the company he was coming to visit. The lady on the phone said that the rate quoted was for a "city view room." Well, when we got there, ready to check in, I asked if they had any rooms overlooking Times Square. The man at the desk said, "Yes. For $60 more per night. You can't have the Times Square view room for this company's rate." And, I said, o.k. then, we'll just take the "city view room" that is included in the rate. And, again he says, "No, the Times Square view room is $60 more per night." And, I say, "Well, what is a "city view" room?" and he doesn't answer. He just stands there looking at me. Now, I know there is a difference between a "city view" and "Times Square" view room. I knew that much going into it. There are 4 different faces of the hotel, some looking in directions other than Times Square. But, obviously, this man thought they were one in the same-that "city view" and "Times Square view" were one in the same. I had just heard (via TripAdvisor) that you could ask for upgrades sometimes, especially if you were a Marriott Rewards member-which we are, and they would let you have them. The man at check in acted like I was a complete idiot for mentioning that I was a Marriott Rewards Member and said, "You don't get an upgrade for that!" Well, according to TripAdvisor, lots of people do. But, we must not have been one of those people. So, if you expect to be getting freebies just because you are part of the "club", I wouldn't count on it. Well, the guy at the desk finally asks if this is our first time at the Marquis. When we said yes, he said, we'll I'll go ahead and let you have a "Times Square View" room then since it is your first time here. Well, finally......Again, I wasn't asking for the best room in the place or anything, I just wanted the "city view" room we had reserved. Meaning, I would like to look at SOMETHING within the confines of New York City. Considering that some on this website have said they got rooms over looking steam vents, I just wanted to make sure we got a room with an actual view. Well, the poor guy must have not understood what I meant, but my complaining paid off! When, we stepped into Room 4036, I about died! We were on the 40th floor, looking DIRECTLY at where they drop the ball for New Year's Eve. Two days before this room would have cost $1000 bucks or more! We had the best view ever and I was so glad I had a bit of a tiff with the guy, if this was my reward! We could even see the Statue of Liberty from this room, as well as Battery Park, and even a slight view of the river from the right side. A few nights, my husand and I turned the couch around to face the window and just sat and stared! Very cool! The other problem is that we were charged more for our room, by about $50 a night. Then, when we checked out, the charges had been corrected. We didn't even have to say anything. But, it did put a hold on our bank for more money than we had anticipated. I would check into how much money they are going to put on your credit card/debit card before you leave the desk. Our rate was $215, but we were charged more than the standard tax and fees. But, miraculously, it cleared itself up. We didn't bother to ask what had happened. As far as the elevators go, they were not a problem. I think people bring the elevator problems on themselves. If you expect to leave 10 minutes before your show and get there on time, you are pushing your luck. We never had a problem with the elevators, save for once, and that time it was only a 10 minute ride or less. We went up and down the elevators at various times of the day too, 7 a.m., 12 noon, 5 p.m., and all throughout the evening. The bed is nice, the couch is nice. Hated the pillows. We came back with sore necks because all the pillows were feather and go flat as soon as you lie down on them. The bathroom and room were both very spacious. The towels were some of the best hotel towels I've ever used. Very fluffy and soft. There is a fitness center, but we never used it. There is no pool, which could be disappointing to the kiddies. But, the view was fantasic and we would go back--just for the view and location of the hotel alone.

“Actually, nice surprise but 11 AM checkout? Really?” Well, I thought that I would loathe this Hilton as I know it to be ginormous. Yes, I had a very long, and I mean quite a long walk to my room which was on the edge of Rock Creek! No, it was not that bad but I thought that this hotel did surprise me for being so huge. First of all, the interior has been reworked a bit and the rooms are much improved. What is not friendly or convenient if one has AM meetings is the 11AM checkout. I thought it was pushy. I see the batallions of cleaning ladies but still. This is not hospitality, nor is the recorded robo message about sustainability. Check in was a bit rocky as I had to wait for a bit but it was smooth sailing. The line of questions about who wold come into the room with me was odd and the way it was done was off-putting to say the least. However, the rooms are so nice now. The bathroom is very clean and smart with a light-up Connair mirror and better toiletries than what they used to have before. The matresses were great but my only complaint is the AC which is bizarre. It turns on and off loudly and it made me get cold and then hot, repeatedly. I awoke with a sore throat which scared me until I could have some coffee. It happens sometimes with hotel air conditioning but this was not great as I had to speak here in DC. The free internet in the lobby is a great idea as it encouraged me to have a drink down in the " Direct Line" and get my affiars in order. If you are coming to DC, you may cinsider this hotel if you have children because I beleive it may be spacious enough. The location is a bit rough as it is a ten minute walk from the Dupont Station but the 42 bus stops right in frontof the hotel. The bar Maclellans is open late and I would have had something there if I was awake. They are soon opening up a coffee bar which is sorely needed. If it was not for the 11 AM checkout, I would have to say that the Washington Hilton is a great choice for DC.

“Pleasantly Suprised” My husband and I just returned from a company-sponsored vacation at La Cantera. We also brought along our two children, ages 7 and 4. When we learned of the location of where we would be staying, I looked up the reviews on this site and was disappointed. I read many horrible reviews about service. Since it was company sponsored, we had no choice on where we stayed. Well, I was pleasantly surprised by our time there. The staff was incredibly friendly. We didn't encounter any rudeness at all. This is a large resort that caters to golfers and corporate gatherings. I do not play golf, but we found enough activities to keep us busy for the two nights we were there. We ate lunch at the Palmer Grill, breakfast at the restaurant right within the resort, and two catered meals in the ballroom. The food was very good. The price of the restaurant meals was reasonable for the type of resort that this is. The decor of the public areas is beautiful, as is the landscaping. The room was standard. The pool area is very large and well maintained. There's also a large workout room with high end equipment. My two complaints: 1) There is no communication between the cleaning staff and the front desk. On the first day we arrived, I was exhausted from the plane trip so I took a nap. Since we had just checked in, the room was obviously clean. It didn't occur to me to put up the Do Not Disturb sign to keep out housekeeping. Well, I was woken up by the maid entering the room. This also happened on our last morning before we checked out. 2) Internet service is $17.50 an hour. That's highway robbery. (We also stayed two nights down on the Riverwalk at the Contessa, where internet service was free.) Aside from those two things, our stay was very pleasant. I would highly recommend this hotel to corporate event planners and to avid golfers. If you don't fall into those two categories, you would probably be happier down on the Riverwalk. I also want to reiterate that I found the staff to be very friendly, and nothing like what was written in other reviews.

“Good Stay” Stay was pretty good. I booked the Plaza and thought I was actually going to stay at the Fairmont. However, when i figured out my mistake, i was a little disappointed. Then i checked in at the park plaza and was overall very happy. this is a nice hotel in a good location.

“A Renaissance? Hmmm....” The Renaissance brand is my favorite of the Marriott brands. I like their unique character, most often find the service above average, and generally find them one step above most mid-brand hotels. Not the case with the Worthington. The valet service is friendly, the lobby is attractive...and then it seems to go downhill. I have stayed here 5 times or so - and check-in has never gone well. Either my Marriott number is missing, my room is not ready, I did not receive the room I booked -always something. Rooms are tired, furniture is scratched and worn. At the rates charged, no excuse. The location IS great- and I suppose that is what enables them to deliver such poor value. Sad really, this hotel could be a true asset to Ft Worth - and the Marriott chain!

“Rip Off ” After a crazy room rate $400 for a king room... this isn't MONTE CARLO, rate and for get having a $10 cocktail Check this out: Package Handling Policy There is a package handling fee for all incoming and outbound packages. Please contact the hotel directly for the exact fee. I was charged for a FEDEX.... an envelope Boycott - stay at the MONACO across the street

“OK if you want a suite and kitchen when downtown” Stayed here because my favorite (the Sheraton) was fully booked. Its an average and quite acceptable residence inn. The parkign is expensive but we elected to use the public lot behind the hotel for $5! The kitchen is good if you need it, I didn't. Breakfast OK and overall the hotel is pleasent enough. The rooms are quite boring, but clean.

“There are better alternatives” Went for an overnight stay this week. Staff is very friendly. Food was interesting but not spectacular during meeting. The room is tired. No outlets for computer - had to unplug wall lamp - room becomes very dark. Bathroom not completely cleaned - stains on counter. Went to use public bathroom on meeting level and it was worse than a baseball stadium or beach bathroom. No soap in dispenser.. Clearly not cleaned or checked.

“Not cozy or romantic, but problem free and friendly staff!” I stayed at this hotel for the final 2 nights of my trip. Upon reflection, there was nothing special or unique about this hotel and I know I wont really think back on my stay here or remember it down the road. There was no nice view. No pay-movies. No restaurant or bar. The room was small and clean. It didn't look as slick as the pictures on the website, but it was pretty close. On the flip side, there was a complimentary water waiting for me when I first arrived to the room, there was complimentary breakfast available in the morning, and there was pleasant and professional staff working at all times of the day. So although there really isn't much I'll remember about this hotel, this might just be a very good thing to some folks. Contrary to some people's opinions, we did not find this hotel convenient for the subway. We had to walk for 15 minutes to get to a subway, and 25 minutes in the evenings. This hotel is near the South Street Seaport which is fun in the day, but in the evening this area pretty much shuts down. Would I stay here again? Yes, but only by myself or for business. I would not recommend this hotel for families or for those looking for a romantic or relaxing place.

“Chambers - Stylish reasonably priced mid-town option” I stayed at the Chambers Hotel over Memorial Day weekend. The room was stylish, modern, comfortable and quiet. Check-in was friendly and quick. .As others have commented, the rain-head shower is a great touch. Requests from housekeeping were answered promptly and front desk staff was friendly and helpful. The price ($250/nt) seemed reasonable for the location and services offered. Lotsof small restaurants and shops nearby and of course Ma Peche if you felt like a restaurant splurge. Easy access to public transportation as well. I would recommend this hotel to couples visiting NYC who want a smaller, stylish hotel in mid-town.

“I'll definitely be back!” My boyfriend and I went to Chicago for Christmas and New Year's. Over the course of the stay I stayed at 3 hotels in the city. The Courtyard was by far our favourite out of the group. We stayed only one night using my boyfriend's mom's points. We checked in around 2pm on the 28th and the room was ready for us. We stayed on the 20th floor. The room was a lot more spacious than I expected. The bed was nice and there was a little living room area with a couch and a coffee table. The bathroom was okay. The shower was fine but it took a while for the water to go down the drain. The sink and mirror area is a bit small as mentioned before (I have too many toiletries and make up!). There's free internet which is awesome. It's so hard to find free internet. There is also free internet in the 24 hour business centre. We didn't use it but that's what they said. There's a pool on the 10th floor but it's only open till 10pm so we missed it because we went out for dinner till late. The workout room which looks good is open 24 hours a day. There's a mini-Starbucks downstairs as well as a restaurant called Viand. Didn't eat there but would if we had more time. Menu looked pretty good and it looked like a cool space. There's a lot of stuff nearby with Michigain only a block away. I would definitely come back here again.

“Sheraton City Center Baltimore: Standard Big-City Convention Hotel.” Stayed in the Sheraton Baltimore City Center on a soon-to-expire free night. The hotel is a pretty standard big-city convention hotel. We had a corner room on a high-floor, so it was pretty big and spacious, though the bathroom was tiny in comparison. The location is pretty good, about eight blocks south of the Mt Vernon neighborhood and about five blocks to the Inner Harbor. The streets are pretty dead at night, which may be off-putting to some people because it gives the area a sketchy feel. One tip: try the B & O American Brasserie around the corner in the Monaco Hotel.

“Fabulous!!” We're locals, and booked an event in the Onyx Room. The location of the hotel is ideal, and the hotel itself and room were great, but we knew all this coming in. What pushes this from a "good" to "excellent" rating was the staff/service. Everyone we dealt w/ was friendly, helpful, and had a sense of humor. If we ever get to plan another event or just want to spend the night someplace where we treated like royalty, this hotel is the top of our list.

“Near Virginia Mason” Visited a relative staying there during his wife's stay at Virginia Mason. The hospital is owned, apparently, by Virginia Mason. Can't believe it. It is like walking into a 1960's downtown cheap flop house. The appliances and furnishings are, seriously, out of the 60's. They still use bedspreads. During my visit there, I didn't even consider checking out the bathroom. I would not stay here for any reason, ever. I think that it is time for a extreme makeover.

“A Few Kinks To Work Out.........” This is a very new property. It has great potential, but we encountered a few problems. First of all, don't get directions off their web site. The directions are wrong. Even the phone number that prints out with the directions has two numbers interposed so some poor guy got a phone call at 1am when we couldn't find the hotel. Where is it? It's directly behind Comfort Suites, but I guess they can't tell you that in their directions. There is no sign visible from the road and no portion of the hotel can be seen from the road. They really need a sign. The room set-up was nice. You enter into a living room type area with a sleep sofa and large flatscreen t.v. The bathroom is between the living room and bedroom with another nice t.v. Unfortunately, our unit was on the freeway side of the building and I could hear the freeway traffic. There were two closets, but both had the closet rods laying on the floor, kind of like they'd fallen down. Breakfast was excellent. Waffles were a treat.

“Need a car...” Definitely not in the heart of San Diego. Like most of California's car culture, it helps to have one here. Cabs were not plentiful making getting around difficult. The trolley was just a short walk away. The ATM was broken the first day I was there, so I didn't have the cash to use the trolley (which was getting set to accept credit cards - but as yet didn't). The bartender took $5 out of his tip jar and lent it to me so that I could use the trolley. Of course, I paid him back and tipped him well the next day - but, it was still very nice of him. Rooms were typical for what one would expect of a Marriott. The pool was always crowded. Although there were hammocks around in the shade that were unoccupied on occasion. Conference facilities were fine. Again, typical for what one would expect. The trolley provided easy access to the YMCA (2 or 3 stops down) as well as to City Center.

“Great experience” This is a wonderful hotel, reasonably priced given its location a stone's throw from the Capitol. The rooms, for Washington, were large, comfortable, and well-appointed. My room was right above the bar, but the thumping dance music stopped every night by the time I bedded down. Staff was helpful. No complaints.

“Truly Historic Hotel - Almost Five Stars” Driskill can best be summarized as a hotel with great history that is not sacrificing comfort to make the experience more "authentic." Recent multi-million dollar renovations have proven to be a wise and valuable investment. The lobby is grandiose, with the 1886 Grill offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner to diners inside and outside. Plush couches and chairs abound, including miniatures for toddlers near the check-in desk. The mezzanine lobby has more Texan charm with cowhide print couches and the like. ROOMS I suspect these rooms are not cookie cutter. Narrow, well-appointed hallways connect the accommodations. The rooms have plush chairs/beds with plenty of lighting. The raised ceilings are painted appropriately in burnt orange. Plenty of pillows were to be found on the beds - perhaps too much - but the owners have truly spared no expense to make stays comfortable. The desk setup was convenient and functional but could have used an Ethernet jack given the wireless Internet issue described below. Bathrooms were oddly shaped but functional and perhaps less updated than the rooms and public spaces in the hotel. The Driskill has provided much of what you could need - hairdryer, toiletries, etc. More shelf space around the two sink areas would have been useful. BUSINESS CENTER There are two computer terminals with ample desk space and printer access in the business center, located off of the main lobby. This is perfectly situated for you to grab boarding passes before leaving the airport and a nice feature for a business traveler who might otherwise opt for a chain hotel. Wireless access was spotty in the room. Enhancements in this area would make the Driskill more attractive for high-paced business travelers. VALET PARKING I did not experience any delays with the valets. My only complaint is that they do not promote a self-parking options, but, hey, that's business. Perhaps it makes sense to up the rack rate and make the valet parking complimentary. Given the busy nature of Brazos Street during some hours, it goes without saying that caution is the order of the day. OVERALL The danger with historic hotels is that not everything will work, and I had the same experience here, but less so than your run-of-the-mill historic hotel. Improvements to the Internet service and functionality of some of the room features (lighting) would turn this into a five star quickly, and I am a tough critic. Hats off to the owners and staff.

“Not exactly what you would expect” My partner and I chose the Hotel Madera from the reviews from tripadvisor. We booked a last minute vacation through a website and this hotel was one of our choices. We read the reviews and decided this would be the best choice for us. First off, it is not a bad place to stay. There are just a few little things that people should know before booking to stay here. Kimpton prides itself on being a very gay friendly hotel. The hotel is a little bit of a walk from the gay area, but not too bad. The only problem we had was asking about where to go in the gay neighborhood. The desk staff were very nice, but didn't seem to be knowledgeable of the gay lift on DC. We had called ahead and asked for a quiet room on a high floor. They booked us on the 10th floor, which is their highest, but it is not quiet. You can hear all of the air conditioning and other equipment on the roof. Ask to be on floor 9 or 8. Also, if you like the room dark in the morning, ask for a room on the front of the hotel. The rooms in the back have older cooling units and so your black out curtains do not reach to the floor. Our first night there, we didn't get into DC until around 3 AM. At around 7 AM the fire alarm went off. This continued for a couple of hours sporadically. The front desk staff never said anything really to us about it. Also there is not really a concierge there at the hotel. We actually got more help from the other staff than from the front desk staff on finding neighborhoods to explore and places to eat. Overall, it is not a bad place and the people were friendly, just not really what we were expecting. We would probably try another Kimpton in town such as the Rouge or Palomar the next time we are in town.

“Not the best place to stay with your dog” We live in Wisconsin and often take overnight weekend trips to the big city of Chicago with our dog. Be warned that the pet friendly rooms at the Palmer Hilton are old, run down, next to the elevator and a little smelly. Even though you pay the same rate as other guest, don't expect the same treatment. You also have to take the service elevators up/down with the dog. Thankfully Sasha is a toy poodle so we snuck her on the regular one without notice. The nearest green space is blocks away on Michigan Ave. Not ideal for that last outing of the night. Oh - don't even think about letting your dog do any business on or near Centennial Park. The guard actually yelled and ran after us. This was quite entertaining considering the guard weighed about 350lbs. House of Blues is much more pet friendly and there is more green space nearby.

“Bring your earplugs!” Loved this hotel, room, the location and everything about it...but you definitely notice that it's the city that never sleeps! During the renovation, unfortunately they forgot to upgrade the windows (and...I was on the 12th floor--and...am not a light sleeper). As long as I remember my earplugs, I would definitely stay here again!

“Horrible place to stay” We stayed at this hotel for one night on Dec 25. The hotel was running some Christmas buffet for non-guests that day so all the guest parking spots were taken and we had to park quite a distance away and lug three suitcases through the rain. Our first room seemed ok. That is until we flushed the toilet. Next thing we see is water flooding the entire bathroom, seeping out into the room and under the adjoining room door and into the next room. By the time maintenance came, the entire room and part of the hallway was covered in water. We got a new room on another floor, and the toilet broke again. We couldn't flush for the entire trip. Horrible plumbing in this hotel. Hot water takes quite some time to come in and the pool area is not stocked with towels. I guess you have to bring bath towels from your room in order to go swimming. The pool is nice, but we didn't even get to enjoy it. The staff is friendly, but the hotel has an out of date feel. Very old fashioned. Bottom line: if you don't flush the toilet and don't require hot water or towels by the pool, this is the place for you.

“Friendly, interesting, historic and well-located hotel” I bought a 3 one-night packages at the Algonquin on RueLaLa, $200 per night including 2 cocktails and 2 breakfasts per night. I knew about Dorothy Parker & the Round Table, but I wasn't sure what to expect now that it was a Marriott. It couldn't have been a better experience. The rooms aren't huge (kind of typical for NYC), but the beds are comfortable, & there are some older historic touches I liked. Each door has a little quip or saying from people like Dorothy Parker, and there is the "legendary" Matilda the cat roaming the lobby, both adding to the charm and history of the hotel. It was so clear that the staff truly care about the place - rather than a "standard Marriott feel", they were interested in each guest individually & everyone was friendly, kind & helpful (not always the case in NYC). We ate dinner in the restaurant (not the Oak Room which is closed for the summer). I was concerned at first because there wasn't a huge selection, but the dishes were fabulous! I had probably the best tuna I've eaten in NYC (& I've eaten a fair amount there). Our waiter Boris was amazing to chat with, & knowledgeable, & took pride in the restaurant. There are 2 free bottles of water in the room - a huge plus in the heat, and I appreciated not being charged for them. They'd emailed me a "virtual concierge" page where I could ask for certain pillows in the room, other amenities. I wanted only foam pillows & that's what I got. Having the breakfast & cocktails as part of my package was a big plus, because while both were delicious, they were pricey - cocktails were upwards of $20, but they did use unusual ingredients; breakfast was $15 for a pretty basic continental, though a lot of fresh fruit. One very small annoyance - my daughter couldn't eat most of her $20 fruit breakfast, so we asked to have it packaged, & they charged us $3.50 - I've never had that happen. But other than that, it was a great experience.

“Beautiful room, great service” The hotel is beautiful. The room is well appointed and the bathroom is very nice, especially the shower. All the staff was welcoming and accommodating, from the front desk to the room service man (not sure of his name but he was very friendly) to the concierge. The only negative in my opinion is having to pay $9.95 a day for internet access.

“Great place to ring in the New Year” We went to the Ritz Carlton to visit friends and ring in the New Year. We had a terrific suite and were impressed with the hotel amenties. My wife had a wonderful massage and enjoyed the spa. We had New Years Eve dinner in Elways and enjoyed the festivities, magnificent food and wonderful service. The General Manager does an exceptional job at getting to meet and know his guests. We look forward to our return.

“I love Priceline...” ...because I end up in hotels like this. This is a very well-managed HI Express property and I was happy to have gotten this for an excellent rate on Priceline. Staff Uniformly excellent...some a little more friendlier than others, but always had good information and took care of any questions I had (especially regarding billing...I had pre-paid through priceline but still got a bill slipped under my door with the priceline account info on it...reception assured me no problem). Receptionist even got me to sign up for reward program. Room Large room, decent bathroom, walk-in shower. Large desk (always good for business travel). High bed (which I really like) and nice firm (but not hard) mattress. My only complaint is that the TV system (dish) is way more complicated than it needs to be. Accidentally ended up off network twice and had to fiddle with the TV itself to get back on. microwave and mini-fridge rounds out the room. I was in room 217 so on the back side about three doors away from elevator. I heard occasional foot traffic, but no traffic noise or trains that others talked about, so being on the back side of the hotel does make a difference. Housekeeping Uniformly excellent. vacuumed and cleaned every day. very clean bathroom. the only oddity was that my ice bag was never replaced. Location Very convenient, right off I-30, if no traffic, 12-minute drive to downtown. Located across from a mall with a wide-range of dining options and a WalMart so you could pretty much get whatever you needed across the street.

“Classy hotel but in a tough neighborhood” We stayed 2 nights recently. Very nice hotel with friendly and helpful staff although the hotel is not in a very good neighborhood. It is a long walk to fisherman's wharf and generally a few blocks away from most things you would be looking to do from a tourists perspective. The hotel itself has an upscale restaurant and bar located off the lobby, the bar menu is reasonable priced but the choices are lacking. We also felt paying for the Club level was well worth it as the Club offers a free breakfast, free appetizers and drinks in the afternoon and free internet access (you have to pay a $15 daily fee to use the internet in your room). The gym is adequate with a few treadmills, machines and an indoor pool. No locker room or health club type amenities. If you want to be right on top of fisherman's wharf or other trendy areas of San Francisco, I would not recommend this hotel. If you are looking for some exercise and really an easy way to see all the city has to offer by walking through the city, I would recommend this hotel to you.
“Very good value” This hotel offers a good location for Hollywood. Rooms are clean and unbelievably spacious. Nice beds. Staff is friendly. Good breakfast.

“Right near Universal” This is decent hotel. The service was excellent and the hotel was clean. The rooms are a bit small and the hotel is dated. There was a lot of street noise from my room (377). Give it another 10 years and it will benefit from being nostalgic. It is RIGHT in the Universal City property.

“Tolle Lage” Hotellage ist ienfach klasse. Die Grand Central Station vor der Tür und alles in Midtown ist zu Fuss zu erreichen. Sehr schöne Lobby nur die Zimmer könnten mal wieder renoviert werden.Sehr Freundliches und zuvorkommendes Personal. Die Zimmereinrichtung ist nicht mehr die neueste aber die Zimmer waren sehr sauber. Auch der Zimmerservice arbeitet sehr sauber und gewissenhaft. Alles in allem ein Hotel das ich jederzeit weiterempfehlen würde.

“Priceline bargain near the airport” The area around LAX would not be my first choice for a location when visiting Los Angeles, however, this was the most convenient location for a family visit. I've stayed at the Radisson, Westin and Hilton near LAX now and they all rank pretty evenly for my purposes. I bid for a 3* at LAX, and got the Hilton Los Angeles Ariport for $60 per night plus taxes. The Hilton is one of many hotels located along Century Boulevard just a few minutes away from the airport. They run a free shuttle to/from the airport. The check in process was quick and they gave us a 2 bed room as we requested, for checkout they slip your room charges under the door and you can just leave the keys in the room. The room was spacious and clean, the beds comfortable. I requested two double beds ahead of time since I was staying with my dad and they accomodated my request. There was a TV with a limited number of stations, iron and ironing board. No in-room safe or refrigerator. The shower was fine with plenty of hot water and pressure, toiletries included shampoo, conditioner, lotion and soap, towel were thick. There was a hair dryer and coffee maker in the bathroom. There was an outdoor pool (too cold to use it) and a health club in the basement with treadmills, stationary bikes, ski machines, climbers and some weight equipment. I grabbed a very expensive snack at the coffee bar one morning, $5 for a muffin and water. Dad had breakfast at the hotel every morning and it was over $20 each day, you can obviously do better going outside the hotel. Parking, as with most of the LAX hotels, is an extra $14 per day with in and out privileges.

“Cool Boutique Hotel” Although a little too far downtown for my business meeting(s), I had no regrets about staying at this cool boutique locale. Typical small NYC hotel rooms, but a nice lobby area and good staff

“Overpriced, typical conference/business hotel” Was there for a conference in November 2007. Had a $225.00 (tax not included) room with two double beds. Not only is the room small, so are the beds. Bathroom is very, very small. Construction across the hotel, so view was not delightful at all. Plus, construction noises started very early in the morning! Not much perks with the room. There is a food stand on the 1st floor, but you'll pay for it! Try the Starbucks down the road or Boudin a few minutes down. The lobby remains mostly packed during conferences. This is more of a business/work oriented hotel. Not a good family hotel or for romantic getaway. The good thing about the hotel is that the staff members (e.g., folks at the counters, housekeeping,etc.) are friendly despite the number of hours worked or rude people encountered. If you need help finding things, the information desk gives out maps and tourist friendly directions. If you don't spend much time in the room or care much about room quality, then it's a decent place.

“Would stay again...at Hotwire rate!” My best friend treated me for my birthday to an overnight in Boston!! I checked out the site and was stunned at the rates!! I was sooo glad she mentioned the sweet rate thru Hotwire she got. She booked it on a Tues. and we stayed the Saturday of the same week (last minute sweet deals do happen for Boston). We valet parked overnight for $36, typical fee for Boston hotel. The room had two doubles, and was comfortable for us. The funny thing was that the bathroom door kept getting stuck on the toliet. The sink/counter was nice and made of granite stone. The hotel was only a 15min walk to Faneuil Hall, perfect! (We felt comfortable walking in this area.) The hotel staff were very sweet and so accommodating. We even got a courteous call to make sure the room was okay. As we went out for the evening of fun, we needed a cab. The valet was so sweet, he left his station and ran down to the corner to get a cab for us. Also, I forgot a blouse in the closet, I called hotel and was promptly connected to Lost and Found. Housekeeping returned my call within the hour, they will mail it to me via UPS. I would definitely stay here again.....at Hotwire rate! ;-)

“Jumping the Shark” Jumping the shark My stay at the FS in Boston was a great letdown. Let’s talk about the good features it still retains: a very good concierge service and tideness of rooms and common areas. But: when I checked in I was given a room right in front of the AC vent which, apart from being really noisy it cooled the room too much and it made entering the room a bit of a challenge as, servicing the whole seventh floor, it blasted out freezing air right on your back. I went right to the reception complaining about it and a young gentleman at the reception told me ‘nobody has ever complained about it if it still bothers you tomorrow morning we’ll turn the AC down’. Well, one of the reasons I really like this hotel chain is that everything is always perfect and they take care of problems asap. I hate having to complain, move around once I’m settled down so I never went back. Breakfast the following morning was a challenge. I asked for a continental breakfast plus yougurt and eggs but I got the bill instead of the eggs. Strange I though let’s see tomorrow morning! The day after I chose the American breakfast, same story: after a 45 minute wait I still hadn’t got my eggs so I just paid and left. On the third day they finally managed to deliver the right order in a decent time. I also had lunch once day and it was decent but not the excellent quality I was used to at the FS. Besides you eat on plastic table mats which is really a let down for a high end hotel. What a difference from the FS in Paris where they iron the table clothes before setting the table! I remember they had them also the other time I was there but being service and food excellent you don’t really mind. This time though it bothered me a lot, maybe because I spent a lot of time staring at them waiting for my breakfast. I had to be back for another two days but I cancelled ny reservation and decided for the Fairmont instead. While I was there the hotel was celebrating its 25th birthday: an old dame living on fame and memories!

“Elegant boutique hotel near UT campus” I love this hotel ! Have stayed 3 times when in Austin to visit my son ; they are very friendly folks; very dog friendly too as they provide doggy beds and bOwls ! Comfy beds, quiet area and very close to university of Texas campus.

“Great hotel, great location” The Edgewater is a fine hotel built on a pier over the ocean. The magnificent lobby is built like an upscale north coast fishing lodge. That theme is carried into each guest room. We booked on Priceline and stayed Friday & Saturday night while we walked & shopped downtown. The first night we stayed in a city view room and moved the next day to an ocean view room; though the room furnishings are really no different; it was like moving to a different hotel. The ocean view is simply fabulous. Here’s my plus/minus assessment of the Edgewater. +Great location on Alaskan Way; a 3 minute walk to the cruise ship terminal, a 5 minute walk to Pike’s Market, a 10 minute walk to the Space Needle or a 15 minute walk to the downtown shopping core. +The rooms are heated with the fireplace and the aura is great. +Flat screen TV (37” in the city view rooms and 42” in the ocean view rooms). +2 comfortable easy chairs to sit by the fire in. +A comfy ottoman fashioned out of wool in the shape of a bear. +Great linens, high thread count sheets make for a good sleep. +A teddy bear in every room +Funky modern bathroom with large walk in, dual head showers. +Homey lobby with inviting chairs to enjoy the fireplaces and ocean view. +Very nice fitness facility with 2 treadmills, 2 ellipticals, a resistance device, and free weights. +A complimentary business centre with 2 computers and a printer. -Parking is expensive, we paid $31 per day including tax.

“Very Nice Hotel” This hotel was awesome, one good thing is you didn't have to pay for parking, but you did have to pay for internet which was a pain. $12.95 a day. I stayed in a king suite, it was very comfortable and a very large room. My bed was in a different room from the common area room, and both rooms had 42" or 47" TV's!!! Hotel was great, I loved it, will stay here again, plan on dining out because hotel restaurant is pricey.

“This one is a keeper!” This River North area hotel is about 2 months old, and is one of the best i have been to. Staff i sooooo friendly, and willing to cater to your every need. Happy hour wine hour every day is a bonus and an unexpected treat. The design is trendy chic. mattresses are so comfy. lighting levels in hotel are on dimmers! bathroom is luxurious, but the bathroom door is a little awkward as it is a sliding panel, but does not close all the way and does not lock. outdoor terrace on the 17th floor and indoor pool. overall, this is such a great hotel! Sable bar & kitchen adjoin this hotel, and is also a new place to dine/drink, and very trendy chic. I will definitely go back!!!

“Superb Hotel in semi noisy neighborhood” Really great staff and great hotel accomodxations near chinatown and the convention center. Depending on which side of street your room faces, it can be a liitle noisy with cars and occasional sirens ... but all quiets down after midnight.

“Great location..clean rooms” Just returned from a 4 night stay. Great location and extremely clean rooms. Connected to a mall with a ton of shops and restaurants which was great so rainy days. Walking distance to Fenway. We were traveling with a group of about 400 people and the only complaint from myself (and others) was that the AC didn't seem to cool too well. No major issues so would stay again.

“Cool new hotel @ reasonable rates” Hotel staff friendly and welcoming, funky vibe. Spacious rooms, robe, free Internet if in the Kimpton club, all typical of a much more expensive hotel. Parking is pricey though the staff did say you can park ovenight on the street, if you can find a space!

“Average” So like the title this hotel is pretty average I mean for the price it's a good deal the only thing I didn't like was the bed its soft but not to comfortable. It kept me tossing and turning all night other then that it was an ok stay

“Great experience!” My family traveled to Dallas for Thanksgiving this year. We met up with family that was already there and we all stayed at the Adolphus. The hotel was very nice and was very family friendly. We had adjoining rooms which meant we could put the baby down in one room to sleep without being seperated and enjoy spending time with the rest of the family in the other room. The beds were comfortable and the bathrooms were nice. We ate breakfast at the hotel. It was excellent. One morning we ate in the restaurant and the other we had room service. Both were well done. The Rodeo Bar and Grill was open on Thanksgiving night fortunately because nothing else was. The turkey dinner was surprisingly very good. The hotel staff was very friendly, especially considering they were working on a holiday. The hotel is in a great location. We walked from the hotel to the American Airlines Center one night for hockey. During the day we walked to the Dallas Aquarium from the hotel also. There is a Starbucks on the corner across the street from the hotel and within a half mile walking distance there are many restaurants such as TGIF, Spaghetti Warehouse and Chipotle. We enjoyed our time at the Adolphus. They serve afternoon tea in the lobby and it was a very nice atmosphere. The only problem we encountered was a slight problem with out hot water. We should have notified the front desk immediately but we did not. I am sure they would have takend care of it.

“Nice view and Neighborhood” The view of the city from the top rooms is really nice. The hotel is clean and service is very good. The room are medium size and the bed is comfortable. My only complains is that the hotel is too big and they have a lot of events and conventions, so it can be noise, and the metro is not that close.

“Needs some TLC” I stayed at and reviewed this hotel back in 2006 when I was last at this hotel. At the time I gave it 5 stars. Unfortunately for the Hotel Carlton it seems that times have changed. A once lovely and well maintained hotel has been left to crumble. Walking into the foyer was the same as last time, and as many other reviewers have noted the staff are very friendly. One of the staff, Edgar had a humor that was not to my taste and said a few things to me that were borderline offensive. It however did not detract from the front desk staff being very accommodating and helpful all of the time I was there. The 2 lifts are very slow, particularly noticeable at busy times as they are also quite compact. I had a room on the 5th floor and was told I had a view. I however could not work out what view I supposedly had other than the adjacent building's roof. What I did have that was unexpected was noise. A lot of it. There was street noise, neighboring guest noise (hearing a guest in the next room urinating is quite unpleasant, sorry gross I know but this is true) and a lot of hallway noise. I also had two other guests come into my room on separate occasions when the front desk accidentally checked them into the same room as myself. Fortunately I had the chain on the door each time but it was still a bit awkward. I also had two instances over three days where my access card did not work in the room door. This was a nuisance to go in the slow lift to the lobby to explain the situation each time. There was also a sniffer dog that came into the rooms on at least one day that I was there, apparently he was sniffing for drugs. Makes me wonder what kind of hotel this is! Other than the noise and lack of air conditioning (there isn't any, just a ceiling fan) my biggest issue relates to the bathroom. There is a lack of space in the bathroom, there is no shelf to put your stuff on so all of my stuff had to go on the toilet cistern. Yuck. The bathroom was also unclean. There was mould on the lamps above the mirror (likely as there is no ventilation) and the bath was FILTHY. I know the general manager reads these reviews so I will be attaching a photo of the bath with filth clearly visible. Hopefully she will address these issues. The lovely smelling bath products of 2006 are gone and replaced by a dispenser in the shower. So impersonal and reminded me of the dispenser from a public restroom. An unexpected and unpleasant change. The bathroom also had patches all over the wall and mould in between the wall tiles. The mirror above the basin had 3 lamps above it with lampshades covered in mould. Not a good look at all, extremely unhygienic and this urgently needs attention. This hotel used to be a beautiful and great value hotel. Now it is a very sad shadow of its former self. This was such a disappointing experience. If it wasn't for the staff being as engaging and warm as they are, this property would be a 2 star property. I sincerely hope the manager addresses these issues and brings this once lovely hotel back to its former glory.

“Always Great!” Spent a wonderful weekend in San Francisco (2/24-2/26). I am never let down by The Four Seasons SF. Great Location. Clean rooms/suites. Friendly and engaging staff. My only dislike is that the in-room internet service is very poor, slow, and often unreliable. I have been staying at this hotel since it opened and it has always had the same problem. They should consider not charging for the service anyway. Beside this one issue, the property is terrific! The Sports Club LA is located within the property and hotel guests have full access to the club. This is a fantastic amenity; the club is really wonderful. The adjacent spa is terrific and the hotel salon is equally as great. The hotel restaurant and lounge are pleasant and pretty good. You really don't need to ever leave the property. But, let's face it, it's San Francisco, and there is so much to see right out your front door on Market St. Point off for poor internet in rooms. This is tech crazy San Francisco, common guys, get with it!! Other than that - GREAT!

“It's getting better all the time” I wrote a review of the Hyatt Regency a few months ago, but felt compelled to write another on my recent return visit to Chicago. This time I stayed in one of the renovated West Tower rooms, and I've got to give the hotel its props. The Hyatt rooms have always been spacious by downtown Chicago standards, but the makeover makes them seem even more so. The new rooms have an elegant modern minimalist look, without taking it to annoying extremes like some boutique hotels. The room furniture is sleekly elegant, and the flat-screen TVs are nice. The bathrooms too have gotten the mod makeover, with cool sinks. (My only gripe is the awkward placement of the toilet paper spool.) My big king bed was a tad bit firm but overall very comfortable, and the Hyatt thankfully has taken away a few of the pillows they tossed on the bed in the older rooms. (There were way too many). The public areas are as busy as they ever were, but for such a big hotel check-in is a relative breeze and service is about as efficient as it can be. I didn't eat at any of the in-house restaurants (I never do) but there are plenty of them. Location wise, the hotel is in a prime spot about a block from Michigan Avenue on the south side of the Chicago River. It's connected to the Illinois Center and its ersatz collection of fast-food outlets and offices. If you're smart and taking transit, the CTA Jackson bus (no. 6) and several rush hour-only buses stop right across from the hotel entrance at Wacker & Stetson. The numerous bus lines that use Michigan Avenue are a block away, and the Wabash/Randolph & State/Lake CTA stations are about 4 blocks away.

“Not that impressed....” First of all, the parking fee is ridiculous. We had two vehicles so parking for one night was $60.00. I will not stay here again. The hotel itself was nice, although small. The good deal you get on websites goes away considering parking.

“Decent at Best” PROs: Huge Rooms and Balcony, Nice View (Probably Much Better in Other Rooms), Very Courteous Staff, Terrific Location, Good Bath Products, High Quality Feather/Down Pillows and Duvet, Has Kitchenette, Housecleaning Staff is Thorough, Lots and Lots of Clothes Hangers, Maintenance Staff Arrived Very Quickly to Repair Broken Light Switch, Accomodated an Early Check-In, Rate of $116 (plus $8/night for parking) is a Good Value for This Area of LA CONs: Cheap Decor (Very Ramada Inn Circa 1986), Only Basic Cable (No Premium Channels), Very Small Television, No High Speed Internet Access or Dataport in Room (There Was a Sign About Wi-Fi at the Sister Property Way Down the Hill But No Indication in Our Room About Internet Service), Chipped/Peeling Paint in Bathroom (on Walls, Ceiling and Door), Warped Bathroom Floor, Just a Generally Run Down Feel to Room and Furnishings, No Top Sheet on Beds (Fitted Sheet and Covered Duvet Only), Hard Beds, Shower Pressure So Intense it Reminded Me of Scene from the Movie "Silkwood", Uneven Water Temp in Shower Required Constant Adjustment to Prevent Scalding or Freezing, Tiny Table-top Ironing Board Instead of Full-Sized One, Weird Arrangement of Kitchenette...Had to Pass Sideways Through a 10 Inch Gap Between Corner of Cabinet and Corner of 'Fridge to Enter (a Large Person Simply Wouldn't Have Been Able to Go Into the Kitchenette), Assigned Parking Isn't Monitored by Staff and Our Space Was Often Occupied by Other Guests or Visitors, Weird "Shed" in Parking Lot Filled with Old Furniture and Matresses, Continental Breakfast is Served Down at Sister Property Making it Highly Inconvenient (Even if it Hadn't Been Raining) My partner and I recently (February 2005) stayed at the Hollywood Hills Hotel and were greatly influenced in our decision to stay there by the reviews on this site. Neither of us can imagine what could possibly lead someone to give this property a four or five star rating unless that person simply hasn't stayed in a nice hotel before. This is not a Four Seasons, Westin, or "W" Hotel. This is a decent hotel, tops. Nothing extraordinary about it save some lovely views and the unusual size of the rooms. Though we can't say enough kind things about the staff there are definitely numerous flaws and shortcomings. Overall we'd say this property is shy of being "average" when compared it to huge number of places we've stayed througout the USA and in Europe. Is this hotel "fine" and an "okay" choice? Absolutely. With some additional work this property has the potential to be superb. But until that happens keep your expectations modest.

“Loved the art deco decor of this "boutique" hotel.” This hotel wraps you up the minute you walk in from the parking lot. The subtle lighting, artwork, floor to ceiling mirror, fireplace, deep chairs can all serve to distract you when checking in. Polished steel elevator doors and deep blue plush surround you on the way up to your room. Lots of nice touches in the room are a bonus, and for a change there is a view, even if it is of the university district of Seattle where this hotel is located. Classical music softly accompanies your exploration of the room. There is an umbrella, in-room safe, gorgeous artsy decor, the special Noble House pencil, a delightfully preserved bath, and ear plugs for a nice, quiet sleep in a comfy bed. Downstairs the District Lounge serves patrons with a pint evenings and breakfast at 7 AM. On site parking is reasonable. This is a lovely hotel if your business takes you to the University district of Seattle.

“Nice, but the price...” Stayed her for a conference from July 24-27 2011. Nice rooms, excellent customer service. I had one problem, the conference rooms are utterly confusing. I spent time walking around not finding any of the rooms I needed. It was also a great value in terms of price, because it's right in the middle of all the great things in Chicago. Also, the internet was $21.00, and that's just ludicrous.

“Westin Riverwalk Is Perfect” I've been 3 nights on Sept 19 to 22nd for an Oil Exhibition. Room is big, clean, bathroom is excellent, comfortable for shaving, for a shower, wi-fi in your room (not free), everything works well. The staff is also very friendly. Breakfast is just good. The restaurant should be considered OK, average, nothing special. You can find better restaurants outside. Also the location is excelent.

“A simple hotel.” As far as the Hilton portfolio of hotels goes they should turn this into a Hampton Inn. It doesn't quite seemed hit the doubletree mark for me. There was really nothing to set it apart from anything else. It's not overly far from the city, it's right on the T, it has views out over wasteland or road. There is no room service and the reception is more like a Super8 than a Hilton brand. Definitely one of those hotels built for vocational functional purposes i.e. serve UMass rather than the general happy wanderer . You won't be disappointedwith your stay but you may sit in your room and ponder what other places downtown would have been like.

“I've seen the future of the Kimpton brand...” Kimpton used to buy interesting, older buildings and rehab them. However, with their rapid growth the past few years they've clearly lost that vision and, in Los Angeles, rehabbed a 70's-era Communist-looking building in a decent location with rooms smaller than most in New York City. That's "the story" this hotel tells...which isn't much. In my opinion, just a bad business decision. I'm sure they also want to create a "hot scene" around the dreary pool squeezed between 2 buildings. Again, not inviting. As many have noted, the AC system is old and dusty. The room is nicely decorated but can't make up for the small size especially if you get a double room. But It's Los Angeles! One of the most expansive cities in our country. We ended up leaving two nights early and headed to the London. I hope they halt their agressive expansion and return to their roots. Otherwise, same old, same old.

“Posh, but not Perfect” I stayed three nights at the reconstructed Hotel Bel-Air in December. After being closed for more than two years for upgrading there should be major changes and there are. Building exteriors and the wonderful gardens are either untouched or faithfully restored. The swans are still there. Inside everything is new. The lobby, restaurant and bar are in the same locations, but have no resemblance to their former versions. The quality is very high and pleasantly appealing. Rooms have been completely redone and are very modern. Baths are large and swank. All furnishings are new. My first impression was good. But as my stay continued I found that function and comfort had not been given the same attention as appearance. The rooms lack comfortable seating and a good light for reading. Some things just don't work. For example, it was not possible to open the door to the toilet compartment without moving or rolling up the bathroom rug. It was not possible to place the bathmat in front of the shower door because opening the door swept it aside. Counter space in the bath was a bit skimpy. Lights can not be individually controlled--switches control groups of lights or lamps with settings of on/off, low or high. The shower has a choice of a rain shower that drenches the entire enclosure or a hand-held shower head. I could not use the shower head in place on the wall, because it sprayed on the door and I could not adjust its height--it was mounted too high and I was unable to lower it. The phone contains a control panel for the room, including the thermostat, that takes a bit of time to learn to use effectively. Valet parking costs $38.50 per day. Internet access costs $15 per day. Valet service was excellent. The wall-mounted TV is about 3 feet square, but only the upper half contains the screen which is equivalent to about a 37-inch TV. The TV controls are complex. The staff was uniformly polite, welcoming and well trained. The restaurant, now operated by Wolfgang Puck, is outstanding. Rooms were clean and quiet. There is a new added section of rooms that blends in well and looks the same as older sections. Of course, the great location in a residential section of Bel-Air, just off Sunset Boulevard is the same. There is a large new spa, but I did not visit it. In summary, I enjoyed my stay and probably will return. But I wish someone with authority had insisted on creating rooms with more functionality and that provide a comfortable place to sit and read under a good lamp.

“Typical Chicago overpriced hotel” It was recommended that I stay at the Hilton in order to quickly make my flight the next morning. I was surprised at the small size of the room and the average nature of the room for the price. The room cost nearly $300 for one night and the room tax was nearly $50. I suppose one has to pay for the convenience of being next to the hotel. I did not think that the room was anything special. The hotel was very crowded. When I went to print my boarding pass, there was no paper in the printer and I was directed to go to the opposite end of the hotel in order to start the process all over again. I was definitely unimpressed by this Hilton hotel. The next time I'll find something a little cheaper and take a shuttle. The night before I stayed in a wonderful hotel in Downers Grove that was a suite for literally half the cost.

“Efficiently excellent” This is a far more pleasant place to stay than the nearby, very expensive Ritz Carlton, at one-third the price, where we stayed several days before sampling the Club Quarters on our return trip. True, you don't have tje R-C's snotty help condescending to extend faux cheery "good mornings", but you have more comfortable rooms at one-third the price. Instead of a sterile, incredibly expensive dining room ($65 for a mediocre breakfast for two), you get a reasonably priced meal in a cheery adjacent pub. The exercise room is not as fancy, but it's free, as opposed to the R-C's $25, and you optionally can have a stationary bicycle or elliptical machine delivered to your room, for free of course. If you enjoy in-room coffee, forget the R-C, which doesn't have it, and go to the Club Quarters, which has an unlimited supply. True, the R-C has fast 801.2g wifi, while the Club Quarters has (rather inexcusably) only the slow (11 mbs) 801.2b wifi, but the R-C charges $10 a day, while the Club Quarters provides it for free. Anyway, the R-C's nominal fast internet frequently slows to levels slower than dialup (10-15 kps), so it doesn't matter. The Club Quarters is not perfect, of course. Something is wrong with the TV system (which is the exact same as at the R-C), so that it is hard to find services other than the standard TV stations. It says it offers HD TV, but I couldn't find it.. However, the Club Quarters offered two wide-screen plasma TV's while the R-C has one, standard TV. While the Club Quaters TV has extensive inputs for PC's, they appear to have been disabled. (The Ritz Carlton had no such inputs). Exterior lights bathe the windows, so the curtains must be drawn at night. The Air Conditioning is quite noisy. But, even without the associated major savings, the Club Quarters is the superior hotel.

“If you are planning on doing some midtown exploring - this hotel is ideal.” I have stayed at hotel 70 Park several times and each stay has been wonderful and the service consistently friendly and welcoming. They have recently remodeled/updated the rooms and lobby and the changes are great. The aesthetic is modern, but warm, not severe. I really like the physical location of this property. If you are planning on doing some midtown exploring (Rock center, 5th ave, theater district, empire state, etc.), this hotel is ideal. It is easily walkable, but feels removed from all the congestion (and noise) that you can run into in much of the area. And if you are not a Kimpton InTouch member - you should join. The perks are great and if you are a member you will get free WiFi and a coupon to take a few items from the minibar. Also - some rooms on high floors on the back of the hotel have views of the empire state building. Worth checking to see if one is available.

“Gorgeous, classy, great service!” Wow. After spending 2 nights at the crappy Executive Pacific on the company's dime, I moved to the Monaco for an extra night on my own following a business trip. I had done Priceline and scored the Monaco for only $95! THIS is what a Kimpton Hotel should be (I had lost faith in the brand after my stays in DC). The lobby is AMZAZING. Really stylish and well-decorated and a great place to hang out. I actually got to take advantage of the free wine reception, and it was really nice!! Front desk staff was amazingly friendly and helpful-you can tell they are well-trained. (Alec checked me in and was very pleasant, sort of a weird gal on the overnight shift though). Doormen/valets were all really nice; got a great tip for breakfast (Bernard's on Seneca around the corner-cheap and good!) Then I get to the room. Uh, wow. It was more like a studio apartment that had been decorated by HGTV or something. Really stylish and cool, and ironically matched my own style (I would love that tripod lamp!). Super comfortable bed. Large bathroom. The entire room was IMMACULATE and it seemed that no detail had been left unattended. I'm not sure what their usual rate is since I got it off of Priceline, but I would pay up to $40 or $50 extra compared to other hotels just to stay here. I thought the parking was a little pricey at $36, but I guess that goes with the territory with a city. They had a Business Center that allowed me to print my boarding pass for free. Walkable to downtown shops, light rail and Pike Place Market. VERY pet friendly (though i didn't have pets). Really a very, very nice place. Thanks for a great stay--wish I was there longer than one night!

“Will be back - great experience - not typical hotel in a good way” Reading some reviews about this hotel (mostly positive) I have to offer my perpective as a mid 30's business traveler and why I really like it. First - this hotel is in a great location and a new building, a good start for any hotel. It is well decorated in a modern/stylish look and feel, a stodgy Ritz Carlton this is not. The staff is on the younger side and very friendly - not old and formal like many 5 star hotels. During my stay they were professional and one woman went above and beyond to make sure a last minute request I made was done. I had room service and ate in the restaurant and both were high quality and worth the price. The shower in the room I had was huge and nice - all glass and stone, nice shower head etc. Beyond this what hit me was that they are not nickle and diming - internet is included in the rate, the water and basic snacks in the minibar were complimentary. While it seems small - this matters to me and says they are in tune with what people want. I will pay for a nice room service dinner - but don't charge for internet and a bottle of water. My complaints were really minor: the lights in the room were controlled by a fancy pad that was a bit tricky to use and the desk chair was a bit uncomfortable (looked nice). I will be staying there again on a future stay. As a frequent and global business traveler - this place is a solid hotel on all fronts. If you can afford the rate - try it. The NYTimes review which I read after seeing others on this board mention it is off track and probably written by an oldster for whom this hotel is not designed. Plus aren't the WWII generation they only people that subscribe to papers anymore?

“Excellent choice for DIA” This was an excellent choice for being close to the airport. Great price, great location, very easy to find, quiet & comfortable room, and -- best of all, by far! -- a very comfortable bed with comfy linens & pillows. Most hotels of this type, I have sadly found, have rock hard beds, thin sheets, ratty blankets, & springy pillows you could bounce on. Not here. This was a great bed! When I made the reservation on their website, I requested extra feather pillows & a blanket, & they were on the bed when we checked in!! Amazing ... I haven't gotten that kind of service from Hilton or Hyatt or Mariott. The rest was what you would expect -- clean, large room, simple bathroom with average towels. The only issue we had was with the toilet, which continually cycled on & off. We didn't think it was a maintenance issue, so we didn't report it ... but perhaps we should have! We simply kept the door shut & it wasn't a big deal. Poor water pressure in the shower, but do-able. We skipped the buffet breakfast, so I can't comment on that. Didn't use the pool, either -- I really hate those small indoor pools that reek of chlorine. We did use the free business ctr (3 computers) to print our boarding passes. Free parking, free airport shuttle, great restaurant accross the street (Ted's Montana Grill -- the buffalo pot roast was outstanding!). I would defintely stay again & I heartily recommend it!

“Friendly Helpful Staff, Not a Good Location” Stayed here for a conference. Stayed on the top floor in the round tower. The rooms are not bad. My room must have been updated, because the furniture and decor was pretty up to date and new. Keep in mind that this is not a Marriott or a Sheraton, but it is probably one of the best Holiday Inns I have been in. The Good: The staff is very friendly and helpful. Every request was met. The conference facility was good. The room service is very prompt. I used room service 7 times and had no problems. There is free wireless internet. Close to the airport (10 Min) Adjacent to Town Park. Gret for walking, jogging, etc... The Not so Good: The hotel is not downtown, and is a 1 mile walk each way minimum to downtown. There are no places to eat within a 20 minute walk. You will have to drive and park downtown. There is a small Chevron gas station next to the hotel that sells all the basics. Beer, candy, snacks, etc... Hence, this is why I had room service 8 times. The food in room service was OK. Not bad, but not as good as the great eateries in Austin! There is no plug in internet, you must have wireless capability in your laptop. The hotel is right on I-35, and unless you have a high floor, you may be bothered by the traffic that goes all night. I had the AC on, and it drowned out the traffic. All in all, I would probably stay at either the Marriott, Hilton, Embassy Suites, Four Seasons if I come back. Primarily for the proximity to downtown, not because of the service or hotel facilities.

“Great hotel” After having stayed at another Kimpton property in San Francisco, I was expecting something special and I wasn't disappointed. This hotel is charming, and the staff clearly had been well schooled in customer service. My room was small, but very well appointed. The view wasn't anything special - but I just closed the blinds. If I wanted to see the city, all I had to do was walk outside. It is very convenient to the Metro and Union Station, within walking distance of the Capitol and the Mall, and only a $15 cab ride from Reagan National Airport.

“mixed feelings but location could not be beat” When I saw this inn had opened I was excited. I was a former resident of Boston and recognized this place as being nothing short of perfect in terms of it's proximity to all the sights, shopping and restaurants in the back bay. The minimal staffing is fine for me since I really am a low maintenance guest and would rather not pay for the "pampering" in city locations. The room was nicely decorated and comfortable but the television never worked. We brought this to the attention of the management who could not fix it so I ended up just telling them to forget it since we don't watch tv at home so saw little need here at the inn. A big problem I had with the room was that the bathroom was exceedingly cold. There was no forced hot air supply in there. I understand construction limitations in retrofits but a towel warmer or radiant electric in the floor would have made it bearable. I always consider the price I pay when rating lodgings so when it's a cost effective stay my expectations are lower. I probably would have given the place five stars had the bathroom not been freezing. I may have forgiven the TV since the manager did offer to have the cable guy come fix it. I would only stay here outside the winter months or in a room with a heated bathroom.

“Very Nice” I've stayed her a few times now and what a great hotel and in the perfect location. The decor is awesome...very different. The king bed room was very large with lots of open space. The bed was very comfortable. There is a nice large desk with very good wireless internet and a large flat screen TV. The bathroom was a bit small and there isn't much room to lay out your bathroom stuff, but the shower is excellent. The air conditioner was a bit disappointing. It didn't seem to keep the room very cool even with the shutters closed and the fan set to high. Overall a great place.

“a conventioneer's dream"” For the money, and I emphasize that fact only; you can do much better in San Diego's fabled Gas Lamp District. Located conveniently across the street from the SDCC, this hotel is a short walk to comfortable hotel rooms (beds), a smoking Oasis, friendly bartenders (and head-chef), and Fox News playing in the Lobby at all hours (unless you wrangle the remote from the staff - and they will relinquish it easily!) . I did not like the bathrooms in this hotel: I had to clean my bathtub with Chlorox and the narrow tub's pitch, is uncomfortable for showerers. The bathroom door is auto-close, and the light is motion sensored. And you cannot turn it off! The meeting rooms are accommodating – but the chairs are not comfortable. Internet is available, but we’ve still not found a hotel that gets is – yet – without many phone calls and a lot of extra conversation. Since you have to get up and walk, often – it’s nice to have a lovely historic “patio” to escape to. Comfy outdoor couches for the consistent SD temperatures make the uncomfortable meeting room chairs bearable! A quick walk – just a block - to Spaghetti Factory, The Oceanaire and Nobu and the 5th Avenue corridor makes up for the steep rack rate (barely). One more thing; if you are not a train/trolley fan, don’t stay here. The train announces its arrival day and night and you can hear the train whistle through the hotel. There is a card in the room explaining why; but there’s no preparing for that first 4AM whistle!

“Perfect location, comfortable room” I was looking for a hotel close to Penn Station, Chelsea and Times Square and this literally put me in the middle of it all. The room was good size (much bigger than the cubbyhole I had last month at the Ramada New Yorker), the breakfast a nice addition (although the waffle maker was always either busy or out of commission) and the service efficient. Only negatives are minor. Cell phone service was non-existent in my 4th floor room and I was unable to print anything from the business center computers, one of which was so infected by viruses that it was completely unusable.

“Hipsters’ Heaven; Purgatory for Others” Here’s the problem with hipster hotels: there aren’t that many hipsters in the world, so a lot of faux hipsters show up, bad looks and all, and act as though the rules of hotel civilization do not apply to them. Welcome to the Hotel Palomar, Kimpton’s latest entry in high chic/low service warehouses. Located off DuPont Circle (and convenient to a Metro stop), the renovated building opens on P Street between 21st and 22nd. P Street is two-way, but there’s no entrance drive to the hotel, so you’re looking at a U-turn from the 22nd Street side. Since there’s a single valet and no one to take your bags, your first move is frenetic. The group in front of us retrieved their own bag carrier from the lobby, but the apparatus would not fit into the cramped elevators (they wedged it, with one teenager sitting on top of the bags; rest of the family rode with us, otherwise, we weren’t getting our own elevator to open.) Do not attempt check-in between 5 and 6 PM. A single desk officer handles all inquiries and check-ins, which can mean torture if you’re competing with the slightly sloshed gratis-wine-tasting lobbyists asking idle questions of the poor guy for entertainment (“If I wanted a late check-out, would I be able (slurp) to get that (slurp)?”) You will be carrying your own bags. My room was advertised as I guess an executive suite (two cuts above a junior suite on the Internet offers, $439/night.) My deskman described it as a “motion room,” leading to my question and the answer I only understood when I unlocked the door. A high-end suite means a standard sized room, single basin bath, and a 6x8 foot alcove with a flat screen tv and a step-climber (whatever.) Shower water never got hot; some lights in the room were inoperable, and I had a delightful view of some building backs. But it was so trendy. His and her robes in zebra and leopard, dark rugs, geometric wall coverings, sleek furniture, a very comfortable bed. Complimentary hi-speed Internet. Call it a slightly toned-down W lacking the techno-pop in the lobby. Staff wore brown instead of black. Room service was timely and high quality. Fact was, when you got a live body to deal with, the experience was pleasant. It’s just that the company probably elected to hold prices down by keeping the staff as minimalist as the décor. But at the end of the day (literally as well as figuratively), a hotel above the first few floors is a place to sleep. This concept has not penetrated the Palomar guest list. From roughly midnight to 3AM I listened to the serenade of the hard partying folks in the seventh floor hallway, one of whom vomited in mid-sentence. House security was unresponsive. By 9AM, it was time to escape, not depart. Of course, the check-out clerk may have been programmed to avoid asking, “How was your stay?” Hence the importance of TripAdvisor.

“Fairmont Copley...Wonderful!!” Stayed at the Fairmont Copley this past weekend. Great hotel and location. Across the street from Copley Place, Prudential, Hynes Center. There is also a Shaws supermarket about 2 blocks away. Pharmacy (CVS) across the street. Boston Public Gardens and Common are a 15-20 minute walk away. Within walking distance to Downtown Crossing (Macy's, Filene's, etc.). Green line (T) right across the street. Newbury St is about 3-4 blocks away...have lunch at Stephanie's. The hotel is older and charming. Room was in great shape, comfortable bed and large well-stocked bathroom. Stay at the Copley...you won't be sorry!

“Holiday Inn works in a pinch” We used Priority Club points for this three night stay. As a Priority Club member you can get $5.00 off the current parking rate (either self parking or valet). The rate was $23.00 with the discount which is excellent for self-parking in this area. The hotel itself is fine, although I would MUCH prefer two queen beds instead of two doubles, but we didn't have a problem sleeping. Pros -- during work hours you have inside access to the CTA brown and purple lines. Otherwise, you do have to go outside for a block or so to reach the CTA stop. Nice pool, but alas no hot tub! Cons -- we were there over Thanksgiving and it is a pretty chilly walk to the shopping areas. It would be great in summer weather, not a bad stroll at all. The rooms all have a pretty decent view. Our daughter who lives in Chicago, said we faced Oprah's apartment building, we were on the lookout but she didn't use her terrace... haha. Would I stay there again? Probably, if the price is right, but if I had other similar options I would try those. The hotel is nothing special, the CityScape bar on the 15th floor is a nice small bar with a great view.
