If you would like to sit somewhere in the city for a view I would highly recommend it. I think they have free appetizers on "Hump" day so Wednesdays would be a fine place to hang for a couple of hours! I did ask about rollaway beds because of the double bed situation, but the extra charge was $20 which I thought was unnecessarily high. It is an adequate hotel in a great city..........

“Could use an instruction book or manual for the room otherwise a very enjoyable stay” Positives: Amazing location, where Lower East Side meets East Village and SOHO. Great restaurants, entertainment, culture and shopping nearby. Room 1403. King Jr. Suite (I think). was spacious with sitting area, large flat screen TV, and great view (southeast) from the 14th floor. I was told this was an upgrade from a Deluxe King. Bed was comfortable. Trendy appearance to room. Modern design. The bed had an attractive lit landscape. The slate or marble bathroom was attractive and functional. We had a large shower with a rain-type spout. Service Front desk was excellent. We needed an ironing board and iron in a hurry and they sent one right up. There is a concierge service and we received an excellent restaurant recommendation. The daily NY Times was appreciated Public Areas We did not eat in the restaurant, but the cocktail lounge looked attractive. Second floor lobby was confortable. There is a trendy rooftop lounge that had a DJ. The lounge is for members only and hotel guests. I thought that was a nice gesture because I remember another trendy hotel in the meatpacking district that cleared the guests out of their top floor lounge at 9 PM so that others could be rejected at the velvet rope. The treatment here is a bit more standard among good hotels. The crowd was mostly in their 20s. It was not for us, but looked like fun. Negatives The tower looks like an eyesore to me. It stands out in stark concrete. A north-south view would have been more interesting so that one could view the skyscrapers in midtown and the harbor below, but the orientation of the building is a minor criticism and the view was interesting to explore. The room also looked a bit stark and industrial with the unfinished concrete ceiling. I guess that is a matter of taste. I couldn't for the life of me figure out how to use the hotel phone and the complicated shower. The bed had a lit landscape above it. I had to fumble around with every light switch Some instruction would have helped. Free internet would be nice. The hotel is pricey but not out of character for the area. I would call it an average value. All-in-all, we would like to stay here again.

“Hotel is Makes Customer Service a Priority” I just spent one night at this Marriott. The location is great with many restaurants nearby. The hotel seems to cater to the business community and in fact I was conducting a conference at the hotel is everything went smoothly. The front desk staff are very helpful. I do want to say a special thankyou to the front desk manager. My cell phone had fallen between the seats of my can and since it was dark I could not locate it. The front desk manager used this cell phone to call my cell phone several times while I loated it fromt he ringing. Thank you!! I received a room on the club lounge and again found the staff to be friendly and helpful. The sleeping room was fairly standard, with the bedding showing some wear. Even though I was near the ice machine, the room are quiet. I did find it odd that the room did not have a flat screen TV, but rather the old model. There are many elevators and getting to the higher floors is quick and easy. The food in the club is pretty standard for a Marriott. The intent is not to make this a meal. It does seem lately that that Marriott is cutting back in their food quality. Getting to the hotel is easy, just off the interstate. When I am back in Memphis I will probably stay at this hotel.

“Best Hotel Stay” I just loved staying at Hotel Vintage Park. Great service. Great rooms. Located next to Seattle's library the hotel is very centrally located. If you are up early they serve coffee and the in the lobby 5am - 9am. They offer complimentary turn-down service. The offer a wine reception every evening at 5pm. This hotel is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at.

“Just great” Stayed there for 5 days and it was just fabulous! The rooms are very stylish and the beds super comfy. I loved the bath bliss goodies. Check-in was very quick and friendly. A big thanks goes to the great concierge she did everything to feel you welcome at the hotel. Even organized us the hotel car without asking - what a nice surprise. The fitnessroom was also well equipped and really clean. The complimentary morning coffee was a nice thing too. The only con to mention is the club and the appendant poolarea. The club employees are so snoby and there is hardly ever any space at the pool.

“One of the best hotels!!” I travel alot and this is one of the best hotels! First, the service is like a 5 star hotel--every request met with "certainly" "can do"; instead of the usual impersonal "can't do" or "don't know anything about it" like most hotels these days. My request to change to a quieter room was met with giving me exactly what was needed-- a room on the end on a top floor, away from the elevator and vending machines. So many times I have requested a quiet room at check in and have been given a room near a vending machine or elevator. That is the type of drone at a front desk that I often encounter where you request something specific and they nod and then don't take any of what you said into account. At this Hyatt they actually LISTENED and gave me what I wanted. The room was beautiful, contemporary decor, plasma tv, lovely bathroom. Room service I had each night and they told you when it would arrive and by God it did, usually within 20 minutes and there was a large convention here at the time. The room service food was really, really good and I had the Halibut, Filet Mignon, Hamburger, dessert over the many nights. The bar on the 27th floor had a fantastic view and the drinks were strong and relatively inexpensive considering the view and service. A shirt sent out for pressing arrived back on time and was lovely. All staff could not be more accommodating. The staff seemed well trained, trained to actually be helpful. I have stayed at other Hyatt properties and really didn't care for them, so this was a pleasant surprise. I can't say enough about this hotel. I would go back there again if in the Denver area. They were kind to the teenagers who were here for the dancing convention and didn't get on their case for hanging out a bit late at night in the lobby, just sitting and laughing together. They provided a very large practice space in the hotel and didn't yell at the kids for dancing all around the hotel, which many other hotels often do. What a lovely, lovely hotel!! the hotel is right across the street from the convention center, just a couple blocks to downtown restaurants like Mangionno's and to shops like Forever 21 and PacSun etc. Elevators were fast and plentiful. Lobby and hallways as well as rooms had fresh, current, contemporary decor. Bell staff was great on check in and check out and Justin was great at arranging transportation for us at 4am to airport. THANKS to everyone there!!

“Big hotel small rooms! Rude security” This hotel Is Huge But The rooms are EXTREMELY SMALL and unconfortable when I was trying to seat at the desk I almost dont have space to open the chair since the bed is right behind. ALL DAY AND NIGHT security is at ELEVATOR like if you were getting inside a night club and if u have a visitor it's a hassle to let him go up to your room. I didn't like that hotel at all it's a boring old hotel where u won't be treated kindly, Probably you might need to WAIT IN LINE untill the security check you keycard at elevator, every single time make sure you have your keycard out in your hads while getting inside the elevator: so they know you are a guess and not going to steal the expensive decoration and art they have inside the hallways. Ah! something good, they have a nice Gym and a room to do your laundry right beside the gym. ! Lol you'll see!!!

“A very basic hotel; cheap, hard beds” The tiny reception area in the smallest lobby I have ever seen, clues you to what's ahead. Room trimmings are modest--a basic curtain, coffee maker, and a smallish bed to go with the smallish TV. Noisy airconditioner and a layer of dust on the furniture that housekeeping just wasn't able to get. All rooms have only the spring mattress option--it was difficult to get a good night's sleep. No in-room safes and paper delivery. Bathroom faucet in my room was loose, but it did the job. When departing, front desk attendant did not ask how the stay went, which is such a crucial opportunity to make a good impression on the guest. A lofty name and premium pricing doesn't make this Jewel a standout. I'd pass on it if I had the option.

“Excellent Customer Service” We stayed at the Omni April 19-25. The customer service was exemplary. The hotel is within walking distance of most things, many good restaurants, etc. Complimentary morning beverage service and choice of USA Today, Wall Street Journal and/or local newspaper each morning was awesome.

“great hotel, great location” This is a fantastic property. they were very helpful when my laundry was misplaced and were able to locate it very quickly. When we had a car die in the parking garage they were able to help us contact a company to quickly and expediently relocate the dead vehicle. The sushi was surprisingly good for a city in the middle of a state which is thousands of miles from an ocean.

“Great location” I was doubtful when I got this hotel for half the price of the other major players in the city but it will now become my regular Philadelphia hotel. Its most outstanding feature is the location, so central for everything, whether its business or pleasure yet set in a nice, quiet tree-lined street. Check in by Kimberley was fast, efficient and very welcoming and the staff were great throughout my stay. The rooms are standard fare but my King room was a good size, well-furnished with decent quality furniture and a small but nicely decorated and spotlessly clean bathroom. The bar couldn't tempt me with its pretty standard fare and I ate the same breakfast elsewhere for about $15 less and no queues. This is a very acceptable hotel.

“Nice accomodations in center city” Great location and comfortable rooms. Yes, rooms are a little on the small side-- but the price more than makes up for it. Friendly staff, free wifi, free printing, free bottled water, fridge and microwave in the room. I'd totally stay here again. If you just need a place to crash in Philly, this is a great option!

“It ain't what it used to be” The Bonaventure isn't the luxury hotel that it used to be. It's shabby despite the lobby upgrade, weirdly empty (like the set of a scary movie) and the food is awful. But the rates reflect its reduced station in life, and the location is perfect for downtown business trips, and lets you walk to the library, Disney, MOCA, even Nokia Theater with ease. I've stayed here 5 times in recent years. The beds don't seem to have that Westin loft any more (or maybe it was just this one) but in other ways the service was fine. Parking is outrageous, so park nearby instead. Or even better, take the FlyAway shuttle to Union Station and then walk around downtown. Lots of good restaurants in the area, so no need to eat in the hotel. Especially avoid the overpriced LA Prime, where the food is just plain bad.

“Hideous decor” With all the lovely hotels in Chicago there is no reason to stay here. My room was not a suite and there was no kitchenette. The lighting was outrageously bad and the decor is too ugly for words. The hotel attracts loud groups so beware.

“Affordable Convenience” This was the best Coutrtyard by Marriott in which I have ever stayed. In fact, I was lucky to even get a room during the week of the UN session - and I had a reasonable price (roughly half that of my colleagues). The bell staff was extremely helpful, the concierge fantastic and the room amenities were superior to many other NYC hotels in which I have stayed. It was everything you expect from Courtyard with additional convenience (Time Square station on the corner) and world class service all in the heart of Manhattan.

“Liked my stay at the Court, great location and friendly service!” I stayed at The Court for 4 nights, after bidding for a 4 star hotel on Priceline, as The Court is considered a 4 star property on Priceline, even though it is considered a 3.5 star property on Tripadvisor. I was happy to see I was given a southfacing room, with a nice view. The bed was very comfortable, and the sheets were high threadcount. This is an older hotel, so some aspects of the hotel showed its age, such as the ceiling in the bathroom and the worn dresser in the closet. The carpet in my room, and the tiles in the bathroom were new. The room I had was very large, and quite a bit larger than most hotel rooms I've had in New York. The mattress was very comfortable. I found my room to be very quiet for NYC. The doormen, cleaning ladies and the front desk were very friendly and courteous. While this hotel isn't as luxurious as many of the other 4 star hotels, I was perfectly happy at the Court, especially considering I paid half of what I would have been paying for a room at the Iroquois. The neighbourhood is well-located, and has lots of services, including several 24 h diners and delis nearby. I would choose to stay either at the Court or another hotel in Murray Hill on future visits to NYC.

“A Decent Option in the Flower District” Located within walking distance south of Times Square – about 16 blocks – and a couple of blocks from the subway lines at Madison Square Garden, and a few blocks from the Empire State Building, and Macy's, the Doubletree Chelsea was a good choice. Like most rooms in Manhattan, the room was very small, but it was decently appointed, with a small closet, a safe, a flat-screen t.v., and two comfortable queen-sized beds. The room still was not ready when we arrived at 5:00 p.m., but the staff was apologetic and courteous and made every effort to have the room available for us. We sat in the lobby and took advantage of the wireless internet for about 15 minutes before the room was ready. The bathroom, like the room, was tiny but well appointed. Towels were large and thick and there seemed to be plenty of hot water. There was just no place to put down anything larger than a toothbrush. We were on the 23rd floor and it was very quiet – there only seemed to be 10 rooms on a floor – and the elevators were reasonably prompt except around the peak hours. All in all, the location was acceptable, the hotel was comfortable but not lavish, and we'd stay there again.

“Pricey for Dallas. Comfortable room and excellent service.” Spacious well appointed room with nice hotel amenities. Excellent customer service. Phylicia at the front desk was delightful and went out of her way to make me feel welcomed. She is a star. Pricey for the region, but if you are looking for service, this place comes through!

“Ditto on the Food Poisoning (norovirus?)” We were at La Cantera for Thanksgiving with extended family--14 of us in all. Early on our third day my mother in law became violently ill. Early the next morning (the day we were to leave) I came down with the same horrible symptoms. My mother in law was well enough to travel home but my family of 4 had to stay as I was in no shape to make the 5 hour car ride home. We extended our 2 rooms for the night ($500.) telling the front desk that it was due to my illness. Imagine my shock when I got home and read the previous review about the group suffering from food poisoning. I phoned the hotel and was informed by their executive offices that between 11/2 and 11/12 a number of guests and employees had shown symptoms of the norovirus. They assured me that they had contacted the San Antonio Health dept. and they inspected and gave them a clean bill and that the problem had been taken care of. Obviously it was not. We were denied a refund but were offered a one night stay which I refused. The only other remedy was to credit our spg rewards card for a nights stay which I reluctantly accepted. I am most irritated that after informing the front desk staff of my illness no one bothered to check with us to see if the symptoms were similar to what others had experienced--if for no other reason than to alert housekeeping to take extra precautions when cleaning my room. In addition to the horrendous end to our stay there were also some other issues 1. Our room keys kept "decoding". We made every effort to keep them away from cell phones etc. but were constantly having to have them re keyed (a very long walk to the front desk) 2. When making our travel plans repeated attempts to contact the hotel via email, phone and fax went unaswered. Luckily we checked our 3:00 Thanksgiving dinner reservation on Wed. as the last seating was at 2:00 and it was under a completely different name but with our phone number 3. For holiday weekends they really should have some activities (movies, crafts, etc) for kids. The lobby was like a gymnasium most nights filled with bored children running around and banging on the piano. We stayed here last year for Thanksgiving and it was a much more pleasant experience. Ironically one of the highlights of my stay this year would have been the fabulous steak dinner that I had in the hotel restaurant if I didn't think that was the meal (salad bar) that made me sick.

“nice” Not a big fan of boutique or trendy hotels , but was booked here for a few days by clients. This was really a very positive surprise and experience , much better than other trendy hotels i have stayed in . Located in a great neighborhood with lots of local flair and history, plenty of coffee places , restaurants and old famous delicatessens - have to spend the weekend next time. The service is excellent , from the doormen who were very helpful and knowledgeable about the area, to the check in staff. The bar is nice if you can use the outside deck , inside not so fun. The restaurant has a good menu , but questionable lay out and decor . Rooms are comfortable , a bit on the dark side for me , beds are very comfortable, slept like a baby.

“NICE PLACE TO STAY IN SEATTLE” While the room is dated, the price, location and staff make stay worthwhile. This a great area to stay; within walking distance of Space Needle; quick access to public transportation; and worth price. Staff were efficient at check-in. Grocery a block away; could have prepared meals in room, but did not.

“This is one of Washington's best!” Had a great stay at the Grand Hyatt Washington. The location simply cannot be beat. It was raining the day I flew in, so it was especially nice to be able to get to the hotel via the Metro without ever having to get wet. Rooms were average sized and the bed was comfortable. I received the hotel for $80/night + tax via Priceline, which I consider a steal. Even with a priceline bid, I was given a room on the 11th floor (Gold Passport Floor) and my non-smoking king request was granted. My only complaint was the gym. While very nice, they are actually part of Washington Center, not the Hyatt, and the cost is $11 per day (no comp for gold passport members). However, the gym is very complete with a multitude of cardio machines, machine weights, and free weights, as well as an indoor pool. You can't beat the quality or location.

“Buen hotel en una zona no tan agradable” El hotel resulta bueno,edificio victoriano, con mobiliario no tan moderno, cómodo, limpio con excelente personal tanto en el front desk como quienes sirven los desayunos. Lo que resulta negativo es fundamentalmente el entorno que durante el día es agradable, (está a 1/2 cuadra de la öpera, y de los edificios gubernamentales (Civic Center) ,por la noche se complica por los mendigos, homeless, alcohólicos, drogad entre otros, que rondan la zona, (como en otros lugares de la ciudad). Aunque reconozco no haber tenido problemas directos, intimidan un poco. Supongo que por negocios debe ser ideal por la zona.

“Absolutely Wonderful!!!” When looking for a hotel in Philly I reasearching using TripAdvisor and they did not steer me wrong. Doubletree was an outsanding!!! The staff was great, they knew exactly how to explain where to go, and the rooms were spotless. The AC was cold, the rooms were big, the beds were very comfortable, the bathrooms were clean and the location was perfect. You are 1 block away from some outstanding bars and restaurants in the area. The parking garage was connected and the blocks are short...not like the long NYC blocks. The hotel is about 5 miles from Citizens Bank Park and in the Arts district where it is clean and safe. As an added bonus, Doubletree is only 1 mile from two of the most famous Philly Cheesesteak places (Pat's and Geno's). Next time I go to Philly I am going to go right for the Doubletree!!! Very impressive and very reasonably prices. You will not go wrong staying here.

“Mix Feelings” I was here on a Saturday night in May - fairly busy weekend night in downtown Memphis. LOCATION - Really doesn't gey better. Right across the street (you can touch it, it's so close) from the ballpark. Bealle Street is only 2-3 blocks away. Restaurants, bars, shopping, sights....it's all very, very close. NOISE - Bring your earplugs.. This is a noisy place. The noise level (at least the night I was there) was deafening. No way you could have even thought about going to bed before midnight. The ballpark across the street had the music blaring very late. There is noise from the street, too. Maybe there is a quieter location than what I had. SERVICE - Wasn't a fan. Not rude, but staff definetly was indifferent. You get the idea the employees aren't very valued there...... FACILITY - Beautiful atrium lobby with glass elevators. Very social in the lobby. Great gym for a hotel. There is a TGI Friday's in the lobby. Avoid it. Several of my colleagues had bad experiences there. ROOMS - Ugh. Mine smelled like a nursing home. This is a very old hotel and you got the feeling there was layer after layer of paint on the walls. The bedding and room were nice, but something was just off. I think that it SMELLED old. For a quick stay, this place isn't bad. Keep your expectations low and I think you'll be happy.

“Go Elsewhere Unless You Like Noise and Bad Attitude” There are two big problems with this hotel: bad attitude from the staff and noise. I booked a lengthy trip, and when I checked in the front desk manager said that there were only 2 rooms available: one right next to the elevator and at the corner of two busy streets, and the other right next to the electrical equipment room, where you hear the elevator rumbling by constantly. The next morning, the day desk manager said there were many vacancies and moved me to a room where I could hear the constant rumbling of the subway. I'm not kidding. Then he told me that for the rate I paid, that was it--despite the fact that entire floors were shuttered because "business is slow." Well, it's no wonder that business is slow. My request to speak with the General Manager was ignored. Who needs this type of treatment when you're trying to enjoy your vacation. Do yourself a big favor. I've traveled to SF many times, and you can find many better places to stay. I got a very good price on my reservation--but there's no such thing as a free lunch.

“"Stay Classy, W Hotel San Diego"” Reservations: made through the booking agent for the conference I was attending. Price: pretty good because it was a conference rate. Check-in: fast efficient and very friendly. None of the "attitude" I have encountered at other W Hotels. Room: large modern well-furnished, with a great TV and DVD player, large comfortable bed, modern sparkling bathroom, excellent linens and towels, superb Bliss bath products. Amenities: excellent scene in the lobby although the music was a bit loud for my taste, typical W Hotel bar scene, great restaurant in the hotel (Rice), small but nicely appointed gym, small pool, and a spa (which I did not use so I cannot comment about it). Check-out: accurate and friendly. Parking: valet only; pricey but prompt and responsive. Down-side: $12.95 per day for in room internet is ridiculous; this should be free/part of the basic room price. It is 2007, not 1999. This is like a surcharge for electricital lites!!! Come on W, get with it!!

“Wonderful Property, Comfortable/Large Rooms” I stayed at the Hotel Monaco Chicago for two nights this week for work. It was my first experience at a Kimpton Hotel and I absolutely loved it. The rooms were trendy but not overly-so; they were large and nicely decorated and I didn't want to get out of bed in the morning because it was so plush and comfy. The bathrooms were also large and the shower head was spa-like. I loved the free Aveda amenities and animal print robes. My coworker had a room on the train-side of the building the first night and asked to be moved the next night because it kept her up all night. My room was very quiet but it faced another building and had no view whatsoever, so that was the only drawback. There was complimentary coffee, tea and newspapers in the lobby each morning and a wine hour each evening. The staff that I encountered were all very friendly and the hotel was impeccably clean. The location is in a perfect location near shopping, the Chicago theater district and famous Chicago marquee, and Millenium park - all are walkable. I'd highly recommend it for business or pleasure!

“This hotel is the worst of the worst” We checked into this hotel on Saturday the 3rd of September. My boyfriend had to attend an event at Universal Studios on Monday so we came up early. We called the night before to make a reservation and mentioned that we had rooms under a particular reservation. First they said they didn't have the reservation. We figured we'd sort it out when we got to the hotel and just booked a room. We got there and of course they charged us the more expensive rate. We had to get the manager on duty to come out and explain what the deal was. We gave up trying and just checked in. The hotel is kinda old and musty. Definitely bring a travel candle to get rid of the smell. We had a non smoking room but it still had this weird smell. So Sunday morning we called down to the front desk and asked them about the room situation. We had a room under a block and wanted to keep the same room. The guy said they couldn't do that so we'd have to pack up our bags and store them until a room is available at 4pm. It was 11am and we wanted to go shopping for the afternoon. No way I was going to pack up again and then move into another room. I called the manager on duty again and explained that we didn't want to have to do this. She said we could keep our things in there and she'd sort it out. So we left to go shopping for the day. We got back to the hotel after a couple of hours and decided to go for a swim. We sent up our friend to go grab some drinks from the room and when he went up we had a problem getting back into the room. The door wouldn't open. We went down to the front desk and called down from the hallway phone several times. Finally I waited at the front desk until someone made a call for someone to go up to our room because we had been waiting for 45 minutes already. They finally sent security to open the door manually. They said it was an engineering problem as the battery on the door swipe was out. After that our key card also took about 10 swipes each time before we got a green light. Oh and the hot tub is disgusting. It's brown and murky. The pool is okay. It was the saving grace. When we checked out of course, we were billed incorrectly. The manager on duty hadn't sorted out our bill so we had to stand at front desk and argue for a bit again. This hotel is a nightmare. I recommend people to not stay here. It's totally dingy and not worth over $100. Stay at another hotel close by or at the Sheraton. I'm sure it's better.

“Nice Hotel w/Old San Francisco Feel” This is a solid option in San Francisco, if you get a deal. We spent a night here before we moved into a new apartment. It reminded me of the older rooms at the St Francis. I like the old San Francisco feel but some of it can be a bit dated like the bathrooms. The water temperature was off and would only be boiling hot. The location is good, easy to get to the financial district and to the touristy sights near union square. The room was spacious and the bed was very comfortable although the lighting by the bed was a little off for reading in bed. Overall a good option for SF, but only if a decent price is available as it can get quite expensive. Service was friendly, although we only had a few interactions.

“Great value and decent location” Great price for New York City. Location is convenient to subway stations and Penn Station for trains. Room and bathroom fairly small but clean and comfortable. Cold continental breakfast is fine. Free computer use in downstairs business center for those travelling without their own laptop.

“Fantastic all round :-)” Great hotel in a great location - good shopping, bars, restaurants etc nearby. Easy cabs, subways, walking etc. People complain about room size here but it is NYC, all rooms are small. If you don't like it, book a suite. This hotel could benefit from better leisure facilities but that's it really. Other than that it's intimate and cosy but with all the amenities you need really. Highly recommended.

“Nice hotel, centrally located” I only stayed for one night whilst on a brief trip to Chicago. The staff are fantastic, very friendly and helpful. Rooms are large, well appointed and comfortable. Location is right on the river near the Trump Tower and easy walking diatance to Shops and Restaurants. The bar looked very good but sadly didn't have a chance to use it. A small mixup on the pressing service, information in the room said it was available until 2000. My suit and shirt was collected but didn't come back, I phoned down and after some confusion I got theme back (unpressed) as the service isn't available apparently. All in all, highly recommended.

“Great City Hotel” I have stayed in a variety of Chicago hotels but for value and location the Springhill Suites Downtown River North is hard to beat. For those arrriving from ORD it is a short straightforward 5 min walk from the Blue Line direct from the airport. Check in was good and I had a corner suite on a high floor. Room was bigith a seperate sitting area. The bathroom had a double wlak in shower. The bed was really comfortable and I slept really well. Hotel has a great location with most attractions within walking distance or accessed from the L. The great advantage of this hotel is that the rates are often significantly less than surrounding hotels which makes it great value. Definitely be back !

“Five stars is not enough for this wonderful hotel” From our arrival to the departure seven days later there was not one thing that was not of a five star standard or beyond. The door staff, reception staff, especially Ashley and Meghan were outstanding! They could not have been more helpful or friendlier. The location in relation to Newbury Street, the Metro, sites and shopping is extremely convenient. The Prudential Centre, Lord and Taylor, Saxs on 5th are all within a very short walk. Our room was whisper quiet, large and comfortable. It was spotlessly clean and well equipped and refreshed each day. Bottled water was provided daily and there are fountains on each floor to minimise the plastic bottle use. Evening turndown provides Lindt chocolates as well. There are bananas and tea and coffee in the foyer by the open fire each morning, hot chocolate and cookies each afternoon. The business centre and gym are excellent guest facilities as well. We ate in both restaurants, the chowder in the bar was delicious, the more formal dining food was very good too, as was the service. The cocktails are delicious! We were so sad to leave this hotel. They certainly have the needs of the guest at the forefront. There is not one thing they could improve. Continue to maintain your standards Lenox staff, other hotels should visit and learn from you.
“Bathroom with a window” Great place to stay with a fantastic gym. The restaurant could be a little faster in service. The room was very spacious and had a bathroom with a window. Very cool.

“Everything was great at this Hotel !!!” It was our first visit to this hotel. The staff is great, they have a great sense of what Customer Focus is. The rooms are big and clean with excellent views. The swimming pool area invites you to spend the whole day there. The Hotel is about 2 miles from the Galleria Mall and it provides an efficient free shuttle. The Lobby is fantastic, a great place to have a good conversation and a good drink too.

“Four star premise, service and amentied need a little work” This is a very nice hotel with thoughtful staff. Well decorated with spacious rooms, the location near the White House puts it in the heart of the District. It is nearest the McPherson rail station (Blue Line from DCA and Orange Line to other points). If you've stayed in one of the better Grand Hyatts, you'll have a good idea of the Sofitel experience. My room on the second floor was spacious, bright and quiet. The toiletries and related items were very complete with several unique items probably more appreciated by female guests. There were abundant and conveniently places plugs so recharging my stash of electronics was no problem. There was a minibar, but no in room coffee, a fact I detest. C'mon folks, you stock a room with liquor but no coffee? Really? Unfortunately, this is a common practice with higher end hotels. Bizarre. There were other shortcomings. The bed had a bottom sheet and a duvet containing a comforter, but no top sheet. During the heat wave we had, this meant either cranking up the AC all the way and sleeping under the comforter (still too warm), or sleeping with no cover at all. There was no middle ground. Personally, I could not get comfortable with this arrangement. Others attending the same conference had the same complaint. Since the Duvet is fairly elaborate, one wonders how often it's actually laundered. Mine smelled fresh and looked clean, but I did not see replacement duvets on the maids' carts. The lack of in room coffee was a problem. Having a European employer, I'm apt to be on the phone early in the morning. In this case, the room service line was busy so I could get neither coffee nor food until lunch due to the length of my calls. Surely, this is not normal, but this was not the only example of service problems. After checking in, I had to leave immediately for a speech and tried to find water. The room wasn't ready yet (I arrived early in the day), but there are no water fountains in the lobby. Other hotels have self service water stations, but this one requires you to go to the concierge and ask. He was intently engaged on a phone call, and not even the bellman could go behind the desk for a bottle. I left without. In fairness, the bellman caught up to me half a block way and brought me a nice cold bottle of water, so kudos to him. Overall, the hotel is very nice, very elegant and very welcoming, but it seemed a bit understaffed at times. In room internet is $9.95, so I used a Verizon aircard instead. My schedule prevented me from using the fitness center or restaurant. The location is terrific near business, tourist, and dining locations. The Sofitel is ranked #2 in DC on TA, but I can't agree. I prefer the Grand Hyatt nearby or (especially) the Mandarin Oriental (location not nearly as good).

“Excellent Service, Wonderful Location” Accompanied one of our friends to Austin and stayed at this hotel for a night. Although we are Omni Select Guest Members, we booked our stay through Priceline this time and our price bid went through, so we were able to get the hotel for $105 a night, a big savings (especially for downtown Austin). This hotel is located about 2 blocks away from 6th street on the quieter end. The hotel staff were very friendly and courteous. In the past, I've noticed that you are treated differently, if you book your room on a different website from the hotel and they do not give you credit for the stay. I'm not sure if they gave us credit as a stay on our Select Guest Membership, however, they did give us all the perks. So I did receive the room preferences that I choose as a Select Guest and first dibs on the room, instead of waiting to see what was available. The room was nice and clean. We checked in at 6:45 p.m., went to dinner, and came back later to see that they turn down the room. Very nice touch. The concierge was great. On the way to the hotel, I called ahead because I didn't know the number the San Francisco Steak House and I wanted to get reservations. The concierge told me they would look up the number, make the reservation for me, and then call me back on my cell. Turned out the number listed on the internet and phone book were not working numbers and I later found out on the way driving out of Austin, that the restaurant was closed. Not sure why. Anyhow, when I got to the hotel, they referred us to a really great steak restaurant 2 blocks away called Dan McKluskey's and also gave us a card with the Chef Special. When we got to the restaurant, we found out that that meant $6.95 off an appetizer. You never know what the Chef Special is until you get to the restaurant. The food was good as well as the service. The ribeye steak starts at about $29.95 for a 10 oz. but it worth it. Overall, I would stay at this hotel again. It made for a nice getaway and the service just made it even better!

“Comfortable with a good breakfast” The rooms are similiar to most Embassy Suites but appeared a little smaller. The included breakfast was very good, with a good selection of fruit, made to order eggs, etc. again this is typical of Embassy Suites but this one seemed to have a better slection. The evening menu, however, was not as good. The manager, however, contacted me when I left via email and apologized. The location is not too far from downtown, it is about 10 minutes by taxi and about twenty five dollars.

“Consistently excellent service” This was my first stay at this hotel and I was very pleasantly surprised with the consistently excellent service I received at every point of my stay. The door person quickly opened the front door and welcomed me with a warm smile/greeting. The front desk was efficient and friendly. They made a dinner reservation at a wonderful, nearby restaurant. I booked a junior suite and was very please with its spaciousness and comfort. Clearly, this property is very well managed!!

“Excellent Location, Bathrooms are Lacking” We selected the Sheraton Boston Hotel for a 3 day trip primarily for its location, which is in the heart of the Back Bay neighborhood. The nightly rate was $275, which seemed rather high, but comparable to the Hilton, and cheaper than both the Westin and Marriott Copley Place. The lobby is really nice, but unfortunately, the corridors and guest rooms are not as nicely decorated. The first room we were given was at the end of the hallway on the 23rd floor of the North Tower. It was tiny, only accomdating two double beds, a desk, and chair in the corner. The bathroom was plain and clearly needed renovation. Unfortunately, within the hour we could hear a couple being intimate next door. It was very loud, and the soundproofing wasn't very good. We called the front desk, and were moved six doors down the hallway. This room was larger, but still had the plain, although clean bathroom. One very good quality of the room were the "Sheraton Sweet Sleeper" beds, which were extremely comfortable. The view was surprising nice, of the South Tower, Christian Science Plaza and surrounding neighborhood. We could see the pool from the room and it even had a sliding roof which was opened one day. The lobby has a restaurant, bar and Starbucks. In addition, there were 7 computer workstations in the lobby where hotel guests could access the internet for free. We took advantage of the computers everyday, as did many other guests. The hotel is a 10 minute walk from the Amtrak station at Back Bay and down the street to the Prudential Green Line T station. Visit the adjacent Prudential Center Mall for great shopping and restaurants such as Legal Sea Foods. Overall, the helpful employees, great location, and comfortable beds make this a solid choice when staying in Boston.

“Good Location” The hotel is in a good location with an helpful staff and decent dining choices, but it is very old and needs a renovation. The room I stayed in was on the small size with old furnishing and TV(very limited channels). I am not sure I would stay here again.

“What a gem!” Stayed here for a week in August. Rooms were small, but this is typical for NYC I guess and doesn't bother me personally. Staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Location is great - two blocks from the subway, very close to Central Park, and with a few nice restaurants in the neighborhood. Would definitely recommend this hotel and also stay here again.

“Simply fantastic - my new Chicago favorite!” It's all about the bed. Amazingly comfortable. I usually wake up 3-4 times a night in hotels due to the unfamiliar room, bed, etc. The feather fiesta that is the Sofitel bed is unbelievably comfortable, and I slept soundly through each night I was there. I think that is quite a tribute to their bed's designer! The hotel itself is beautiful in that 21st century clean, colorful Euro sense. You won't find anything with a floral design here, thank goodness! Very chic, down to the hallway carpets and the in-room lighting. The bathroom was huge and spotless, with a separate stall shower and very good French toiletries (I admit I brought the leftovers home!). Frette bathrobes, too. Location is phenomenal - walked everywhere from the hotel. Usually I stay at the Westin River North, which is very good. This is better, and I will stay here from now on. Can't wait to get back into that featherbed again!

“Pleasant, luxurious” Did a last minute overnight in DC on a Friday night. Got a $235 rate for a standard room! The rooms are consistently elegant, comfortable, roomy, and elegantly appointed. Marble bathroom. They've recently upgraded to flatscreen TV's (they used to have big tube TV's). Very quiet room. You can use the spa facilities as a guest of the hotel, whether or not you get a spa treatment. The locker room has a really nice big hot tub, steam room, sauna, and a "treatment" shower with tropical rain, side spray, etc, settings. The last time I stayed here, I stayed on the Tai pai level -- if you can get it cheap, go for it; otherwise, it's not worth the extra $$. The buffet is just okay, and the rooms are the same lay-out as regular floors. The concierge service in the Tai Pai Club was sluggish and unexceptional. The location is not great. Somewhat convenient to the southern edge of the mall, but there's almost nothing in the immediate surroundings of the hotel. Parking is $38/night. A litle steep for the location. Also (my major pet peeve) -- they charge for internet. At very upscale properties, I really appreciate complimentary internet service, and resent the nickel-and-dime charge for such a basic, universally need; it seems a bit like charging $8 for air conditioning.

“What every 5 star hotel should be!” It is rare that I give such a glowing review but this Ritz really does have it all done perfectly. The rooms are spacious and very comfortable. The decor is luxurious without being over the top. The views of the City are great. From checkin to housekeeping to the restaurants and doorman, the staff is wonderful. They are inviting and friendly. You get the feeling that if you needed something they would do just about anything the help you. But since they thought of everything you don't really need to ask for anything. The location is obviously terrific. The hotel is in a very busy area of the city but once inside it is like an oasis of calm. I had both room service and dinning at the restaurant on the 12th floor lobby. Both were terrific - food and service alike. I wish that every hotel experience was like this one at the Ritz. It was absolutely wonderful.

“Worth a stay” I am staying at the Hampton Inn in Washington DC and am quite impressed with this new hotel in Washington DC. Room is clean with added amenities like a microwave, refrigerator, room safe, free internet access and free morning breakfast! Add to this a swimming pool and fitness center and you have all of special benefits of a four star hotel at three star price. The hotel is a ten minute walk to the Gallery Chinatown Metro stop and across the street from National Public Radio.

“Very good” This obviously is a premium location right downtown. Took a room on the executive floor. Small but very nice room and view on the city. Very Good concierge service – they kept our luggage for more than 12 hours and called us a taxi on our way to another hotel. Good breakfast but still standard (Hampton Inn style)– no omelettes or such fancy I would expect from the executive floor breakfast room. Downside = had to call 4 times the front desk to get toiletries delivered.

“Time Square” I am in New York approxomately every other month and try to stay at different Hilton hotels since the city has so much to offer. This hotel is off the beaten path of Time Square but still within walking distance of it all. Very beautiful, safe and upper class hotel. Will stay here again.

“It's what you'd expect from a W.” Some people love the W and some dont. If you are a younger business traveler like myself, you'll love it. Great location, great onsite amenities, and quality living space. However, this is not a place I would bring a young family. The lobby is connected to a bar and the music goes late into the night. That aside, our company used the event space and brought in roughly 100 clients. The hotel staff was exceptional! I travel a lot and they were one of the most accommodating staffs I've ever worked with. For business, I highly recommend this hotel.

“Second Stay- Much Better than First” We stayed at the Intercontinental a few years ago and had were disappointed with our room. Last weekend we stayed again and had a wonderful room. We realized that there are 2 towers to this hotel- the rooms in one tower are updated and very comfortable, the rooms in the other are small and in need of updating. Both times we booked through Priceline, I don't think whether or not your book on a discount website determines your tower. Our last room- the bed was very comfortable, great bathroom and very comfortable room. We did not have any kind of view, but being right on MI Ave, who needs one? The hotel itself is GORGEOUS. The hotel bar was nice with great service. Our favorite part of our experience was the wine, cheese, and chocolate bar attached to the hotel. Very fun place with great wine. They sell discounted bottles/glasses when you take up to room.. Will definitely come again!

“Beautiful hotel but at a price....” I've stayed in may different Philly hotels. This was my first stay at the Four Seasons. While the public spaces are grand and beautiful, the rooms are no better than those at either the Westin or the Sofitel. And while the bed was comfortable, it did not match the comfort of these other hotel's beds. The location is just slightly off the beaten track. In short, the other hotels that I mentioned charge considerably less than the Four Seasons so if you desire grand public spaces, then stay here. Otherwise, there are better choices for the money.

“A really 'classy' spot” The Regency just feels right. From the friendly doormen, the welcome men at the desk, the hustle & bustle of savvy travellers and professional New Yorkers, it's New York elegant. Even the smaller rooms are lovely, though the bigger ones and the suites are even better. It's the epicenter of the Power Breakfast- (if you can afford it.) They close next January for a year of renovation, so it'll be missed, but even better -- maybe more expensive? - when it reopens. Watch the rates - sometimes the prices are 'over the top', other times, you can get a great 'deal'. We were just there for the weekend, and got a good rate, + free parking and free wifi (both of which will add a lot to the price, when it's full price.)

“Review” Pros: 1. Location: The hotel is right on the Freedom Trail and in easy walking distance of most tourist locations. 2. Hotel was recently renovated and in good shape. Cons: 1. Rooms are very small, even for this New Yorker's standards. I guess that's what you get for a Downtown Boston hotel. 2. Room was generally clean. However, there was spilt coffee on the desk. While this was a minor problem, this made me uncomfortable in the room initially, even though the rest of the room was spotless. 3. While the hotel is historic, it also had a very stuffy atmosphere.

“Great location and service” Located in a renovated apartment building in the Back Bay one block from Boylston, and 2 blocks from Copley Place and Newberry St. The staff are all pleasant, helpful and seem truly interested in your visit enjoyment. Free wi-fi throughout. The breakfast is OK and has a variety of items from eggs and waffles to fruit and cereal. The rooms are attractive and have windows that actually open. Street noise is minimal. My only issue was the bed. The bed was comfortable but the linens seemed thin, "limpy" and there was no good blanket or comforter. You can't beat the location and price, I'd stay there again.

“Best W in New York!” You get the best of the W here - the trendiness, high caliber of service from the staff, and a good quality room product and overall experience. This hotel is trendy. The entrance is located right off Times Square, and you don't get the same pretension from the doorstaff that exist at other W's within the city. It's low key, but the doorstaff are helpful, and the Acura car ride service is also located here as well. The check in is located on floor 7, which is also the "Living Room," filled with young socialites. The staff at the front desk are fun, passionate, energetic, and welcoming. There's a nice store with W products off to the side of the check in desk. The elevators are super fast, per what you find at U.S. W's. They also have the distinct W smell, which is wonderful. The rooms are a great size for New York City (at least 300 square feet), with modern amenities, comfortable beds, waterfall showerheads, etc. I LOVE the sinks that the hotel uses...the design of the sink and incorporated faucet is so modern. Some minor cons about the rooms: the quality of the tv's is not great (may be more a function of the program quality than the actual hardware itself), and great views of the square are not found in all of their rooms. In terms of service, their staff is fantastic. The Whatever, Whenever line is courteous, prompt, and responds to your every need. The in-room dining folks take the time to answer your questions and remind you that they're available all night - couldn't be better! The managers are also present at checkout, and they're helpful, kind, and response. One helped speed up my checkout by taking my keys, printing me a bill, and sending me on my way. I also emailed the GM after checking out to share my experience with him, and he quickly and courteously responded. It really reflects the overall responsiveness of the management at this property, and their pride in their great product. I've stayed here a handful of times thus far, and any time business brings to or near Times Square, you can certainly bet that I'll be staying here again.

“Disappointing” Stayed at Menger last week for an overnight getaway with my husband. I think I expected too much ahead of time. It is advertised as a beautiful historic hotel. It is historic and has some impressive antiques. The downside: musty smell, thin carpets, old plumbing, and no insulation/sound proofing. I could hear every time a faucet was turned on, a toilet flushed, etc. The televisions were old 20 inch dinosaurs which would be just fine if the picture wasn't covered in snow. It was clean, bed was comfy, good service...just needs serious renovation.
“One Night was NOT enough” Really great buzzy place – one that I will visit again and again.

“Surprisingly Nice!” My husband and I booked a last minute room here for New Year's Eve (we live in Dallas and were spending NYE with friends in Ft. Worth and didn't want a late night drunk drive!). Our room was rather pricey, but I suspect that was just NYE price inflation. When we arrived at the hotel, there was a long line of people waiting to check in, but it moved very fast and check in was quick. The room was surprisingly nice and the beds were covered with very cushy, lightweight duvets. I've noticed this trend recently at hotels and I really like it. The bed was one of the more comfortable I've slept in at a hotel. The bathroom was decent, if a bit small. We returned to the room around 2 a.m. after a night out (and after dinner at Duce, which was excellent). Despite the hotel still being fairly busy at that hour due to NYE, our room was very quiet. We ordered room service, which was actually quite good and arrived warm, which is always an issue with room service food. The ceasar salad and grilled chicken club were great and so were the fries! Overall, this was a surprisingly pleasant experience and this hotel is highly recommended.

“Great Place to Layover While Traveling Through LA” We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights prior to a cruise on the Paul Gauguin. It was a good idea to break up the long flight from Chicago to Papeete. The hotel itself is very nice. The only complaint would be the very small and not so bubbly hot tub. We did eat at the lounge during Happy Hour and had some excellent drinks and food. The restaurant was quite expensive, but if the bar good is an indicaiton of the restaurant food, I am sure it is excellent. There is a Burger King across the street that we used for breakfast. We met a couple in the bar who had a layover and visited the bar while waiting for their flight. What a great idea! We had a great deal at this hotel booking through Priceline. I think we paid about $70. We woudl certainly stay here again.

“Couldn't have been better” After reading all the positive reviews of Inn at the Market, I'm having a difficult time adding to the accolades. We were there for six nights and thoroughly enjoyed every minute. Our room was beautiful (fantastic bed linens) with a breathtaking view of the water. We were in room 804, and the picture on the website of the water view room is entirely accurate. There was even a complementary bottle of wine waiting for us when we arrived. The service at the hotel is also wonderful. I had to buy flowers at the market (couldn't resist), and the hotel provided a vase. Also the hair dryer was not working properly, but within a couple of hours of letting the desk know, a new dryer was installed. As everyone has said, the location is perfect--many lovely restaurants, wine bars, shops, as well as the Market are at your fingertips. When we returned home, we watched "Sleepless in Seattle," which we hadn't seen for many years. We were delighted to see views of the market, the Athenian where Tom Hanks ate with his friend, and--to make it even better--we saw the Inn at the Market! It made us wish we were still there.

“The Yin & Yang of The Affinia Shelburne” So, here's the scoop on this place: Rooms: The basic rooms are a good deal at $ 200.00 or under. The suites are above average deals, if that's your thing, at $ 500.00 & up. Hotel is very popular with Europeans & Brits. Service: very good, very responsive, very friendly. Neighborhood: safe, residential area known as Murray Hill, plenty of local restaurants around that are open all hours on the weekends, walking distance to basics such as the Empire State Bldg, Herald Square, Grand Central, much more; plenty of cabs cruising Lexington Ave & 3rd Ave. Room service: prompt, fairly accurate (forgot all the condiments & the salad dressing), expensive as hell (I get it, this is NYC, but $ 80.00 for a salad, 2 burgers & 3 drinks was interesting). My Experience: our visit began oddly, as the amenity package that I had paid for wasn't in the room & had to be requested (2x); then, it was discovered that the sink wouldn't drain; up to our room came a maintenance gent who worked diligently for 90 minutes to resolve the issue on a Friday night; with my help, issue resolved. Not exactly what you want to do after traveling all day, but stuff happens. Next day, the flat screen television failed; ended up watching Winbledon tennis finals on a dilapidated, old tv in the hotel-affiliated bar named 'Rare.' Front Desk Manager Warren Herrera came through for us - - re-located us on Saturday to the suite up on 12. Suite was very roomy & had the feel of an apartment. The AC struggled to keep up with a 95 degree day, though, and didn't cool the living room area until well after dark. BTW, the hotel doesn't AC the hallways. You come out of your room on a hot summer's day & wait a few minutes for an elevator & trust me, you melt. Just thought that no AC in the hallway of a major hotel in mid-town, especially after renovations, was odd - - and off-putting. Staff: Very professional, very friendly, very responsive to issues. Eats: recommend Zengo's on 3rd Ave for Asian Latin fusion (try the duck appetizer, very good); recommend Scottie's Diner on Lex (open 24-7 & the best corned beef hash I've ever tasted); Nirvana is Indian food on Lex, basic nothing special; Sushi Yasuda a few blocks away for excellent sushi & great service; the little corner deli on the corner of 40th & Lex for that NYC classic, the egg, bacon & cheese on a hard roll sandwich, damn, now that's a tasty & inexpensive item for a quick breakfast. The little pizzeria around the corner from the hotel (Royal Pizza? Imperial Pizza?) on 3rd Ave isn't very good. Two Boots in Grand Central is much better, as are many other places for pizza in NYC than Royal or Imperial whatever the name. Kips Bay movie theatres are only a short cab ride away on 2nd Ave @ 31st, or walk to it if weather permits. The towels in the basic rooms aren't as plush or new as the towels in the suites. Toiletries are above average, can't recall the brand. 'Rare' is the restaurant next to the hotel lobby. Known for their burgers, which are quite good & which will set you back $ 15.00 or more per burger. Pricey food, drinks are good & priced like the rest of the area. Would recommend staying here because the management strives to get it right.

“Great customer service--wonderful hotel” You just don't expect to see triple sheeted beds at a Fairfield Inn (at least, I don't), but that's what you get at the Cherry Creek Fairfield Inn and Suites in Denver. The hotel was recently renovated and it looks and smells fresh and clean. We stayed in a King Suite and it was perfect for our needs. The outer room had two easy chairs and a pull-out sofa, television and CD player, plus a computer desk (free wireless), microwave and fridge. The bedroom was separate and had its own tv. The bathroom was small but had a nice granite countertop. Loved the fireplace in the lobby and the breakfast was nice (various pastries, bagels, muffins, cereal, toast, yogurt and waffles). The front desk staff knows their customer service--extremely friendly and helpful. We were having trouble wheeling our overloaded luggage cart to the elevator and a young man insisted on taking it up to the room for us then refused a tip. The location can be noisy, since the hotel's on busy Colorado Blvd., but we requested a room on the opposite side and it was nice and quiet. I would definitely return.

“Very average, but I would stay here again” 1. Breakfast & Dinner Free hot breakfast is included and they also serve dinner on weekdays. The selections are nothing special, but I didn't expect a fabulous buffet in the first place so the breakfast & dinner was just fine with me. 2. Exercise facility The exercise room was VERY small and the equipment was very limited. I didn't use it, but they have indoor pool which seems very nice. 3. Self service laundry As far as I know, there was only 1 self laundry room in this hotel with only 2 washing machines and 2 clothes dryers. Sometimes both machines were in use or someone's clothes were still there. 4. Room Kitchen and a fridge are nice and room was spacious. No flat screen TV.

“Great value!” This is an older Holiday Inn & Suites. But very nicely kept and clean. The staff is outstanding, over-the-top friendly. This was the cheapest 2-room suite in downtown Chicago, which is why we chose this hotel. It's not luxury but it's nice. Our room had 2 large-screen TV's, a refrigerator, and a micro-wave oven. Wireless internet was fast. This hotel is not walking distance to Navy Pier or to the shopping district but it is walking distance to several great restaurants and coffee shops. It's also connected to a great pizza restaurant where we ate 3 times. They served a great breakfast too. Overall this was a great value as we saved several hundreds dollars over a long weekend vs. other downtown Chicago suite hotels. We'd return.

“First class” I've been staying at the Lenox consistently for several years as part of extensive business travel. They are so good to me I made it my businesses "team hotel" and my persona. "family" hotel of choice as well in the past (although I've just moved back so the family stays will be at a minimum now). The manager, Daniel, is first rate, as is all of the people that work there. The place was renovated the past few years and it is clearly one of Boston's hidden gems. HIGHLY recommend the place. I love the location when I'm going to Sox games. The irish pub, Solas, is first rate. Can't say enough positive things about the place. This review probably sounds like an employee wrote it but I assure you this is legitimate.

“Comfortable stay. Good location.” Stayed here one night in Feb while in town for a swim meet. It is an easy one block walk to the Mecklenburg Aquatic Center. The location is also convenient for all downtown and will be across the street from the new NASCAR museum which is under construction. It was mostly like any other Hampton Inn (which is a chain we like) but I must call out that the breakfast staff was exceptional !! The lady came by to every table and offered to cut up and serve an orange or some other fresh fruit to the customers. That was something I have not seen before !

“Give Inn to the Market!!” We ended back-to-back cruise vacations with an overnight stay at Inn at the Market. Although we had access to the Inn's sedan service (there are certain caveats that exist around that service attribute), we chose the quick cab from the cruise ship terminal to the Inn. My partner was having mobility problems and we advised the hotel in advance that we might be an early check-in. When we did check-in, the front desk rearranged our full waterview suite to a room that was close to being refreshed. We were able to get to our suite 608 with ease. The view was breathtaking with a grand view of the bustling marketplace and waterfront, the room well appointed and Gilcrest and Soame bathroom amenities were most welcome. It's always a good sign when there is little need to leave the comfort of a suite the first evening. At dusk we mingled with several other guests on the terrace, which lent itself to a nice little wind down to our vacation. The bed was extremely comfortable and made for a great night's rest. At checkout in the morning, one of the desk clerks who met us temporarily the previous day recalled both our names. We thouroughly enjoyed our stay and wouldn't hesitate to stay here again, but it must absolutely be the waterfront view. It currently is our favorite accomodation experience.

“Its about the smiles” New hotel so expect some teething problems. The Cable TV is not the best and has issues from time to time. The walls between rooms are thin ( typical of most NY hotels). The housekeeping and cleaning of the rooms leave much to be desired. But the overall pleasantness, hospitality and smiles of the staff make this a great value for money hotel. Location is conveneint , though a bit seedy (this I think will change over time(

“Wenn die Lage passt, dann sehr empfehlenswert !!!!” Wir kamen von Deutschland kommend erst am späten Abend am Phoenix Airport an und wollten schon ein wenig in Richtung Grand Canyon fahren, was dann am nächsten tag auf unserem Reiseplan stand. Daher hatten wir uns das Garden Inn Happy Valley ausgesucht, denn es liegt am nördlichen Rand des Großraums Phoenix unweit des Interstate-Highway Richtung Grand Canyon. Möchte man jedoch die Städte Phoenix oder Scottsdale besuchen, dann ist die Lage eher ungeeignet, da man schätzungsweise 45-60 Minuten bis in die beiden City Center braucht. Das Hotel an sich ist jedoch sehr empfehlenswert. Es macht einen sehr modernen Eindruck. Scheinbar ist es erst vor kurzem eröffnet oder zumindest renoviert worden. Die Zimmer sind sehr schön und sauber. Das Business-Center ist kostenlos. Das Frühstücks-Büffet sehr reichhaltig und bei den meisten Zimmer-Raten inklusive. Das Personal war während unseres kurzen Aufenthalts sehr zuvorkommend. Wir erhielten sogar zwei kostenlose Flaschen Wasser, da ich Mitglied im HHonors-Programm der Hilton-Gruppe bin.

“Excellent choice for NYC” This is a great hotel for a trip to Manhattan; especially if you're going to be spending any time in the Village. It's also a quick cab ride to Midtown and all of the theater's. It's not your typical hotel - there's no front desk. Instead you're greeted by an employee who will invite you to have a drink while they grab your room key. I checked in on a particularly cold and snowy night and there was a roaring fire near the bar; it was perfect. The room itself was very clean and modern. The lights took me a second to figure out but once I did it was a great place to stay. I love a good shower and the hotel had excellent water pressure and a steam shower built into the bathroom. There were plenty of towels in the bathroom, they did smell a tad bit like they'd been through an industrial laundry facility. The bed had a very comfortable down comforter and mattress. I could tell it was real because there was a feather or two that poked me; however, it wasn't bothersome or excessive. The views of the city were nice and made the room feel much bigger than it was. They've done a great job of turning a small space into a cozy space. There was a nice iPod / iPhone dock by the bed to charge your phone (or iPod) and play some tunes as well. The one minor complaint I had about the room was the lack of readily available electrical outlets. In this day and age, people are going to want to plug in a laptop and cell phone. My guess is as the hotel works through the opening kinks, they'll solve this issue. (There were plenty of outlets, it just took some time to find them and get a plug to them). Despite my fewer minor nit-picking items, this hotel is a great bet; especially for NYC. I'd recommend it to anyone.

“Nice New Hotel~!” Booked this hotel via Spg website. got an excellent deal for 149/night on a busy weekend. stayed at this property twice, both time got upgraded to a nice corner room (xx25 and xx01) as spg gold. If you are platinum you'll get upgraded to the corner suite (more likely). but the hotel sold out pretty often b/c its right next to the convention center. its an easy 5 mins walk (and safe too) to the bart station and also there are lots convinent /fast food store nearby (quiznos, starbucks, McDs, taco bells and 7-11). CPK is right across the street too. SF shopping center and Union square are approx 2-3 blocks away. There is a big cinema right behind the hotel too. Easy access to the Ferry building/fisherman's wharf via bus / cable car. The room on 22 floors and UP are consider "grand deluxe/premier" room so they have a better view of the city. As other reviewers suggested. This hotel has a nice , new gym at 4th floor, no swimming pool tho (Very common in norcal). But this hotel is mostly business travellers so not likely people will have time to really use the gym facilities. Afterall, this hotel IS a business hotel, so don't expect too much from it. The service was prompted but slow. Most of the people working at the front desk are young so their knowledge could be limited and their attitude certainly needs to polish some more when dealing with the customers. Afterall, this is still a nice hotel, very comfortable bed and AC works great in the hotel, a perfect place for travellers whos visiting SF for the first time!

“Nothing like staying in the mall” Two of us stayed for 1 night at the Westin Galleria Dallas in June 2011. We chose this hotel based on its location within the mall. We have previously stayed at the Westin Galleria in Houston. The hotel is nicely renovated and we had a great room on one of the higher floors. What we loved the most was being able to walk straight into the mall. The Galleria is quite good although I prefer NorthPark. The front desk staff were fantastic. I cannot rate them highly enough.

“Boutique Hotel in middle of busy city” The Teatro has elegant rooms and a first class staff.(An example being the valets who offered to take our car to a wash and detail center a few miles away when we simply asked about the closest carwash.) The hotel rooms are tiled in marble and the comforters are down.(Worth the upgrade to a superior room). While the location is a short walk from 16th Street mall - I think it is much nicer to be located at the Teatro which is only a few steps from the theatre district and Lamier street! This hotel deserves between 4 and 5 stars.The restaurants located within are critically acclaimed but I feel possibly overhyped. Definately consider having breakfast off property if you are looking for more than continental dining. Overall, our favorite romantic escape.

“One of the best in Dallas..” Beautiful hotel with 5 star rooms,,, Nobu's bar was cool at night. The lobby bar is a bit warm during the day because of all windows but weather out side was nice enough to have a drink outside. The hotel also had a Lexus which drove us to dinner one night.

“Excellent customer care” The hotel wins high honors for taking very good care of its guests -- from check-in to check-out, they try to make everything pleasurable, easy, professional and comfortable. Room was comfortable and immaculate; view was spectacular. Very quiet. Very upscale. Only downsides: valet parking (the only choice available) was very expensive but was also very well run; room service was very expensive as well, but staff is wondereful; air unit was a bit noisy. Fortunately I booked via Priceline!

“Excellent business class hotel” If you travel frequently for business, most hotels start to look alike. The Hilton Indianapolis stood out and is an excellent value when rooms can be had for around $150. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms are much larger than the typical hotel room. My room, which seemed to be a regular one (not a suite) had a separate sitting area with sofa, desk, two chairs, and a TV. The bed had both foam and feather pillows--a nice touch. I also really like the Peter Thomas Roth bath products. On the down side, the decor, especially in the halls, is tired. But I found the entire hotel to be clean and well maintained. I would stay there again.
“Business Visit” Room was comfortable and hotel loaction convenient for work and leisure. Hotel staff is very courteous and helpful. Have stayed several times in past and will do so again.

“Besoin d'être rafraîchi...” Bon, pour une nuitée d'étape, cet hotel est fort convenable mais néanmoins, pas mal de soucis d'entretien pour cet hotel situé en périphérie de Houston. La réceptionnisme avait beau être souriante, celà n'a pas suffit : problèmes divers dans plusieurs chambres de notre groupe, l'hotel a beau afficher "hotel 100% no smoking", plusieurs chambres puaient la cigarette, quelques soucis d'électricité et un environnement très "banlieue". Les chambres sont correctes mais quelconques. Cet hotel ne sera pas inoubliable, heureusement Houston nous a laissé de bons souvenirs...
“Greenspoint Preference” I prefer this hotel when staying at Greenspoint. Rooms are big and recently renovated. The executive lounge has breakfast and a buffet in the evening.

“Great conference hotel” A huge hotel designed for conferences. I have been there twice for conferences. They are very pro. When it comes to such arrangements. Nice rooms, huge beds and clean bathroom. Staff is nice and polite. Valet parking. I would rather stayed at a small boutique hotel if I had not attended the conferences. It is in my opinion better to choose a hotel in Georgetown. WIFI is not free, breakfast is around $ 25.

“Nice Galleria hotel” The Courtyard is far and away better than the one on West University- clean, modern, professional staff and all amenities. Close to mall and restauarants. i will be back I'm sure as my company got a great corporate rate here. No complaints.

“Good location, comfortable rooms” This hotel is almost too hip for itself, given it's location in the middle of tourist central. The staff is friendly and helpful and the rooms are very comfortable and well sized for NY. The bathrooms, in particular, are very generously sized for the NY area. Noise is kept to a minimum with good sound proofing and hallway noise is minimal. One minor complaint is that while the alarm clocks look nice, they aren't very functional given they don't light up and are completely invisible in the dark.

“Great brand new hotel!” This is a brand new hotel in a nice area near Point Loma. It is on an old military base that has been completely redone into a really nice retail/residential space. The hotel is in a very convenient location; plenty of surface parking. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful. The pool and hot tub were nice. There is a HUGE park and walk along the river immediately behind the hotel. Don't miss the opportunity to take a stroll around - it is wonderful! The room itself was tastefully decorated and everything was new and clean. The free internet was good; my only complaint was that the free internet was a little slow because of course they want you to upgrade to the paid internet.

“vergogna” veramente indecente, sporco con capelli lunghi in bagno nel pavimento e nella doccia, un cattivissimo odore in stanza, pulizia inesistente. Non lo consiglio a nessuno anche perchè non è per niente economico. posteggio a pagamento in uno spiazzo abbandonato senza nessuna custodia, veramente pessimo, mai più !!!

“Always wanted to stay....” I stayed here for a night just yesterday with my wife and 20 something children, location was great right on the best part of Hollywood Blvd. I loved the lobby and pool area and being a fan of Hollywoods history I found the hotel fascinating. But if you want to sleep forget it! Doors banging in the surrounding rooms constantly and the people in the room next door partying all night, and this was mid week! I can sleep through almost anything but it was like a war zone on the 6th floor. I would not stay again.

“Better than expected...” I was really expecting the worst during my stay. I was surprised to find a nice hotel especially for the period it was built. Was able to open balcony door and sleep at night to the wonder piece of the man-made brook. Nice conferencing capabilities. You will need a car.

“Beautiful rooms, nice views of LA” Our room had a great view of the hills and Los Angeles. We could see Beverly Hills and Hollywood. The bed and sheets were very comfortable. The bathroom was spacious but only has a shower. That wasn't a concern for me, but if you are looking to take a bath, you may be out of luck. Service was efficient and polite. Many French people work at the hotel which was interesting to be in the heart of LA. The valet service sometimes took a while but the staff was extremely courteous. The mall across the street is great if you forgot something at home, but the variety of shops is nothing special. Room service was quick and tasted great. You will want a car in LA, but this hotel is on major bus lines and easy to walk to various cafes, drug stores, malls, banks, bars, etc. I was able to find a discounted rate online, but the rack rates are expensive. Would definitely stay here again. It's not as luxurious as the Beverly Wilshire, Peninsula, or Four Seasons but the staff is just as well trained and works hard to make you feel at home.

“Could be much better” Stayed here recently for two separate non-consecutive nights for both catching and returning from flights. There are good things and bad to consider. Overall I would likely not chose to stay here again. We chose this place for their great online rate and the proximity to the airport (5 minutes) and they offer a free airport shuttle and free airport parking (maybe ?). Upon check-in we were told that they were now charging a $10.00 a night airport parking fee ! This came as a shock as we had done our research and even spoken to one of their associates to confirm this. When we complained we were told it "was new" and they "just started" charging ! and that the information was not yet posted on their website ! What ?! We had to argue the point and then by coincidence the clerk / associate who had actually helped us with our reservation showed up and we explained the situation. When he was told of the "new fee" he replied to his own co-worker "since when ?" The first clerk was either clueless or trying to scam us. Nonetheless we did not end up paying to park there for a few nights. As for the airport shuttle, the early morning shuttle to the airport was fine, but there were problems on the return flight pick up. Like one of the other reviewers had suggested we too waited 40 minutes for our pick up - even after calling twice ! (Its about one mile - 5 minutes in traffic). While we were waiting at the airport the other hotel shuttles came and went three times ! And when he finally arrived the van smelled of smoke. Overall the room was nice, clean and comfortable. However, we never had enough towels or wash cloths. There always seemed to be missing something. One should also note that they do post ominous warnings in the rooms about not leaving items in your car due to potential theft. The warnings were so well posted that it gave me an uneasy feeling. When I asked the desk clerk when was the most recent theft he replied "just last week." Yikes. And like the other reviewers stated the breakfast is disappointing for a Marriott. I expected a higher quality. They also posted that breakfast is served until 9:30 am, but one morning it closed at 9:10. Glad we had gotten their at 9:00. If you are a fan of Spring Hill because of their bars and cocktails, please note that this one does not have a bar. They have applied for their license as that was posted, but currently they do not have one. They do have a nice snack bar / sundry counter near the front desk.
