We found our rooms to be clean, which is most important. And I do like the two sinks and separate toilet if you are a couple and both are trying to get ready at the same time. Even though the room was clean, we found the lobby and grounds in need of cleaning, trash pick-up, vacuuming, etc. So, there was some good and some bad, but there was more bad so we will not likely stay here again.

“Quaint little oasis in the mist of a bustling Chicago” I booked a room using [---] for my daughter and myself and we stayed 5 days over the Labor Day weekend. We booked a hotel/air package. I called from the airport as we were leaving to check to make sure they were expecting us and talked with a very NEGATIVE lady! I asked if we could have a queen or king if not two double beds and she told me that since we booked through an internet website ( arrogance in her voice) we would be supplied with a double!! She was very short with me. As I was telling her that was fine and we'd make do, she transfered me to the front desk. I told the gentleman, that I'd just called to make sure we had a room and had just inquired about beds and had been informed that there was NO way we could change from a double to a queen, king or two doubles and that was FINE. No problem. I was really not upset about it UNTIL the lady was so rude to me. Anyway, be that as it may, we did have a very postive experience at the Whitehall. Freddie, who greeted us at the front desk is THE PERFECT representative for a hotel!! I apoligized for the misunderstanding and told him a double would be fine to which he agreed that we'd be more comfortable with more space and presented us with a king room! I have to say, his generosity and graciousness, along with the friendliness of the staff is what any hotel should strive for in order to add that extra touch often missing in the larger nonpersonal "super-mega" hotels. We stayed on the 8th floor. Unlike a previous review, we didn't have hardwood floors but carpeting. The bath and bed were spotless! I said before in other reviews that I love the covered comforter and the white bedding. You know you're in a clean bed because it's a little hard to mask spots on white linens. The furniture in the room was a bit worn but tasteful and the hallway carpet needs to be replaced. Having said that, I need to agree with my daughter that I'm glad the hotel took care of the most important things to renovate first, like the bath and beds. I can live with the other. There are no ice machines but the hotel provides ice which is complimentary (when you call room service ). We didn't use this service but I'm sure if used, a small tip would be appropriate. We did take advantage of the free coffee and tea in the lobby each morning. It was brewed perfectly. They offer REAL cream and not creamer which was a nice touch. There are only two elevators but we were there during the Labor Day weekend with an abundance of guests and we only had to wait a couple of times with the elevator being full and it returned to our floor within a few minutes. The location of this hotel is one of it's best selling points. It's a half block from Michigan Avenue and half block from Rush Street. You can walk everywhere from here if you're a walker and if not, there are cabs and transportation right out the door. This little hotel is unique. I hate hotels that are so large, you feel like you're lost on a cruise ship! This hotel isn't for everyone. It's older, therefore historical which is just another reason I love it. It's not lush, but is tasteful with a bit of European charm thrown in. The rooms aren't memorable but the beds are spotless and clean as well as the bathrooms. Our sink had a small back up problem in the mornings when everyone was using the plumbing but it eventually drained after a few minutes. You couldn't ask for a better or friendlier staff. Also, my daugther and I had a man follow us into the hotel and into the elevator and before we figured out what he was doing, he followed us out of the elevator. The moment we stepped out of the elevator, I put it all together and as the doors were closing I told the man on the elevator. He called the security. Also there was a maid on our floor and we told her as she was standing near our door. I had already confronted the man and she did too and told him he needed to leave if he wasn't a guest. The security were there within minutes to deal with this man and talked with us in order to make a report . We should have been more aware of our surroundings and I hadn't realized that he'd been trying to touch my daughter on the elevator! If I'd known, I'd never have gotten off and would have stayed on with the other guests ( a man and his wife) and reported it with them. (safety in numbers) This could have ruined our stay but didn't as it was handled very professionally and quickly and we felt safe and stayed more aware for the rest of our stay.

“Nice Hotel In a Good Location” Great location for visiting downtown Houston, baseball games, good restaurants, conventions and the theaters. We drive into Houston for a date night about once a month and try to stay at this hotel. The hotel has pet friendly policy so our small dog enjoys our date night in Houston. The restaurant serves a good breakfast, a buffet, menu or continental. The steak house restaurant is also very good. The staff was friendly to us and our pet. The room was a standard king nonsmoking and very clean. Valet parking though expensive is very convenient. The free shuttle service to restaurants, stores or events provides friendly drop off and pick up so you can leave your car parked at the hotel.

“Beautiful hotel, but a little off.” This hotel is one of the oldest, most historic in chicago. The hotel itself is very aw striking. the rooms were remodeled{good thing} but, they were done super modern which does not match the hotel. the standards rooms are a shoe box and the front desk service is very lacking. helps to be a diamond member where your treated like very well. but other people its a wringer.

“OK, but does not meet Hilton standards.” OK, but does not meet Hilton standards. Right on U. of Texas which has +'s and -'s but is aprox. $100 less then the Hilton Med. Center which is about 5 miles away. There's no gym on site, but you can use the campus gym. There's a good game room and fast food directly across from the hotel at the student center and the campus is nice, but the hotel rooms are old and don't meet the standards of the upgrades Hilton has been making. OK option for a business stay, but I wouldn't chose this a get away destination.

“A fine hotel but value and price don't meet” The Affinia Shelburne is a fine hotel if it was priced $100 to $150 lower per night. I picked this hotel simply for it's proximity to where I needed to be in Manhattan, it was two blocks away from my meeting place. Having never stayed at an Affinia property I had no expectations other than I new it cost $400 per night and they called themselves a Boutique hotel. The management has served themselves no service by referring to the property as a "Boutique Hotel", with that term certainly comes some expectations which the Affinia Shelburne could never meet. The front desk were certainly bothered by being interrupted by a guest. The room was comfortable, clean and in good repair. I received 2 emails prior to arriving from a concierge asking if any assistance was needed prior to arriving and what kind of pillow I would like, I was impressed. Then I arrived and realized they must have been automated emails because there was no sign of a concierge on site and when I requested a some additional pillows, I had to call twice and thirty minutes later I was told the two pillows the brought to the room were the only two left in the hotel, so take them or leave them. Someone in the hotel brand management team needs to change the branding or majorly adjust the property staffing.

“Nice attempt BUT...” Stayed here 06/24/05 - 06/26/05 - room #209. The rooms seem to be fairly nice with extras including microwave, fridge, high speed internet and lots of plugs at workstation desk in room, ceiling fan, separate sitting area in room. Hotel includes small exercise room and indoor/outdoor pool. Front desk staff is extremely helpful. Lots of restaurants in area and very close to FM 1960 / Sam Houston Tollway. Problems I encountered: Toilets clog very easily (saw toilet plunger outside a room), train track immediately across the street with trains that go by the hotel all hours of the day and night. Television had less than 10 channels and one of the channels provided could barely be heard. Summary: The area has many hotels and you could probably do better than the Best Western Suites.

“Welcome home!” The Affinia 50 is a truly wonderful place to stay. The rooms are extremely clean and spacious, esp by NY standards. The beds are so comfortable as are the pillows-I loved the pillows that were on my bed, so didn't make use of the much mentioned "pillow concierge" although I have to admit that paritally sold me-good marketing! There is plenty of closet space, two full length mirrors and a small fridge. The bathroom had enough shelf space. Real hairdryer, and an iron/full ironing board also. My room was on the 2nd floor, I was originally facing the street but I asked to be moved b/c I am a light sleeper. The room I ended up in was perfectly quiet, also on the 2nd floor, but might be off-putting to some as it had a basement apt feel b/c the windows were high up and had no view to speak of but my personal preference was to have quiet compared to views. The staff at the Affinia are what make it such a special place. After a long day of touring or business it was so nice to come back to "welcome home" and "cheers!" They learn people's names quickly and use them. From the front desk to the bell people, they seemed to be genuinely interested in our well being. Just a very nice group of people to be around. I also loved the punch at the front desk! The club floor is very comfortable, a nice place to relax, and stop for wine and cheese in the late afternoon. The hotel is located very close to two subway lines, including the 4,5,6 and E,V trains. A couple of room for improvement items-the internet access is $9.95 per day or $49.95/week- with so many hotel offering this for free, competitively speaking, I would think the Affinia would too. I did not look at the breakfast at $14.95, so I can't say if it was worth it or not, but it said "continental" and I've never had a continental breakfast worth $14.95. Ess a Bagel has the best bagels ever and is right across the street! One other drawback is there is no bathroom fan. Those were minor drawbacks, however, in comparison to how nice everyone was and how completely comfortable I felt in the room and hotel, especially getting a good night's sleep every night, being warmly greeted upon check -in, and being warmly greeted everytime I came and went. Highly recommended!

“I forgot how nice it was to stay here” So well located in the heart of soho, walking distance From it all. Great staff and amazing restaurant service. Very cool people everywhere. The beds are super comfy and the elevators fast. Lobby is on the first floor so don't be confused. Pretty much a hotel you don't want to l

“Enttäuschend Renovierung” Es ist schon ein paar Jahre zurück, ich hätte zuletzt blieben und aufgrund der guten Erfahrungen, die ich wieder für dieses Hotel entschieden. Der Service war gut, aber ziemlich enttäuschend und ich werde erklären, warum. Wenn Hyatt Diamond-Mitglied gibt es bestimmte Privilegien wie einem dedizierten Diamant-Schreibtisch für Check-in und fragen Sie, Sie sind also nicht in den Warteschlangen. Allerdings wird dieser Diamant-Desk nicht besetzt kontinuierlich. Als Ergebnis jedes Mal, wenn Sie kommen den ganzen Weg und müssen nur länger warten, als ein regelmäßiger Gast. Das Hotel befindet sich auch ausgiebig in der vergangenen Periode renoviert, was aber viel enger geworden und weniger persönlich und gemütlich. Der Service ist immer noch gut, aber unsere Suite wurde gerade angerufen eine Suite mit einer kleinen Sitzecke.

“Time to try a new hotel” We've made an annual trip to Indianapolis for the last 4 -5 years and we always stayed at this hotel. The location is great for downtown activities. But this stay was pretty mediocre. There were good things such as the friendly helpful staff. But there were many minor annoyances. We arrived to find that the one queen bed room we had reserved was not available because a previous guest had hung laundry on the sprinkler causing massive flooding. So we were upgraded to a king suite. It was a true suite with 2 rooms with a door between. But it was quite cold in the room and we discovered that the heat in the bedroom was off. Odd for a day when the temp never reached 40. But we turned it on and went out to dinner. The room still felt chilly when we returned and we kept turning up the heat all evening. It's an old building and the room was on the corner with windows on both sides so seemingly it was hard to heat. The room never really felt comfortably warm. Through the night I was awakened repeatedly by the noisy rattling whenever the heat turned on. I usually travel with earplugs just in case but had forgotten them and the front desk didn't have any. The shower head was way too high, at least 7 feet up making water pressure poor by the time it got down to me. Breakfast the first morning was okay but the second morning there were no bananas and the bowl of cut fruit was mostly empty. Time to move on to a new hotel!

“Nice while its new, good views” I stayed here for a quick weekend stay. Normally I don't stay in Hilton's for non-business but I chose the location for convenience to the Baltimore marathon. The hotel itself is nice because its new. I like that it had plenty of elevators whose doors closed quickly...thats normally a pet peeve of mine in Hiltons. Pros: Very new, clean comfortable rooms, fast stable internet Walkway to convention center, close to everything downtown, easy to get a cab Great view into Camden Yards if you are on that side of the hotel Cons: Check-in isn't great, the HHonors line wasn't really being followed and I had several people cut in front of me, would've been quicker to just stand in general line. The Diamond Tavern is a building over, and they boast being a classy sports bar, but their 20 tvs don't have any sports packages and very limited local stations so they had virtually no games on. Definitely not worth it given all the true sports bars a street over. If my company wants to put me up here again thats fine, but given the similar proximity of the Hampton Inn I wouldn't spend the extra dime out of pocket.

“Elegance in Boston” As stated in other reviews, I generally like modern and contemporary hotels. That said, we spent a very enjoyable six nights At the Taj Boston (Business and Pleasure). The hotel is the former Ritz and lives up to the elegance of a Ritz and now Taj reputation. Boston has many areas so it is hard to say what is the best. It all depends on what you are looking to do. The Taj is in Back Bay, overlooking the Public Gardens and the Commons. Great location for shopping and business. It is on the corner of Newbury Street which has some great shopping and galleries. It is walkable to the business center and walkable to the waterfront/North Bay on a nice day or a short cab ride. The Taj is what you expect from an older, traditionial hotel. Excellent service and staff (although the reception area was always a bit of a cluster) with lots of friendly, efficient, and helpful staff. Room service was quick and the food was hot, and The Bar was comfortable and relaxing after meetings and shopping. We had a room with a park view. It was amazing with the fall colors. I highly recommend requesting a park view. An associate was there and had an air conditioner view. The view definitely added to the experience. The bedroom was fairly large for an old hotel. A pleasant surprise was the lighting in the room. One of my biggest complaints is the lighting in most hotels is not bright enough to work. The room was very bright. The two downsides were the small size of the bath room and the lack of outlets near the desk. The bathroom was tiny! Older hotels have small bathrooms, but this was one of the smallest I have had in quite some time. You could not fit more than one person in at a time, truly tiny. On the plugs, in todays world of lap top, mobile phones, iPads, etc, we need outlets. There were only two near the desk without unpluging a light. While these were inconveniences, they are not deal breakers and wouldn't prevent me from staying there. My only complaint would be some of the wear and tear. The carpet was filthy and stained, and the comforter and sheets were torn. You expect wear and tear at all hotels, but I do expect a higher standard at the Tag. All the above said, I highly recommend the Taj if you are in that area of Boston.

“OK but for the price would check elsewhere first” We stayed here 2 nights for leisure activities in downtown. Its a very big hotel, rooms are on the small side. In addition to the room charge, you are charged approx. $50/night for parking ($44 + taxes) and $13 for internet if you choose to use it. The pop machine on our level was out of soda pop both nights so we had to go to other floors to get a soda if we desired one. There is no pool at this hotel which was a bummer for my two teenagers. Stamps in the gift shop costs $1.99 x tax for two - I thought stamps were $0.48/each? Things add up pretty quickly here so if business is paying go ahead and stay. If its coming out of your own pocket and you aren't a millionaire, I would look elsewhere first.

“Decent hotel” OK location, a bit further from IAH than one would like. The area is also in a bad area of the Houston Metro called Greenspoint or as locals call it "Gunspoint". There is security in the parking lot. The room are laid out a bit funky and they rooms have very very heavy doors, wonder why? There is nothing within walking distance to eat or pick up a forgotten item.
“A reason in itself to visit Chicago” Always perfect. Period. One of my favorite hotels in the world.

“Great Location” When we arrived at the Hotel we had someone offering to help us out with anything we needed until the time we left. You could not walk anywhere in the hotel without a staff member saying hello or asking if there was anything we needed help with. I had never been on a subway before and the concierge took the time to explain everything about the subway. He never made me feel like I was bothering him. The location was fantastic. The subway was close by. The Grey Line Tour buses were two blocks away. The ABC studios was across the street and the NBC studios was within walking distance. We did not go to any Broadway shows but they were all around the hotel. I won't bother sending any pictures because other people already have. Our room looked just like the pictures other people have submitted. We never had to wait in line for the elevators. If we ever go back to NY this will be the place we will stay at.

“not all hiltons are the same” was staying her for a conference, so those facilities are huge. and confusing. but can really accomadate huge functions. The concierge, while they gave good recommendations for restaurants, where always rude. never saw a smile, they appeared quite cocky. you really felt like you were asking stupid questions, as if you didn't trust their first response. Exploring ideas and options really appeared an inconvenience to all 4 of them that we used. we were there for a week, so that service was consistent unfortunately. The room was to hilton standards, but as i had made reservations 10 months in advance, and asked for a room with a view, i was put in a room with a tiny window on th 11th floor. i think the building has 40 floors or so. the location is quite central but RIGHT next to the meat packing district. while i can easily handle such run down neighborhoods i highly caution the average person.

“Rainy & Windy outside, warm & toasty inside” The weather outside was frightful, but our stay at Hotel Triton was delightful! We were taking a 1 night foray into San Francisco and I checked the hotel's website and the price was reasonable. After they sent me an email if I would like to upgrade for $9, I did it and we ended up with a corner room on the top floor with a view of the entrance to Chinatown! The room was cozy, but clean and comfortable. The employees were helpful and friendly from check in right through advice on which way to bring the car for a fast getaway in a driving rainstrorm!

“Not bad, not great” We stayed here on the last night of a 3 week trip from Ohio to Yellowstone and back. We picked the area because we love to dine at Ruth's Chris' Steak House and this was the least expensive yet decent hotel nearby. We paid $123 before tax and that included happy hour and hot breakfast buffet. (The Courtyard nearby was $159 and didn't include either.) We arrived just after happy hour ended, but they were nice enough to give us each a cold beer, which was appreciated after 8 hours on the road! They had served dinner that night too, which I guess they do on weekdays, which we found interesting because there are a lot of nice restaurants nearby. The room was nice. The only bad part was the lighting at the sink. The staff is friendly and the pool was nice to sit and relax by. You do have to walk outside to get from the rooms to the lobby/pool. We'd most likely stay there again.

“Hotel Wales - a gem in the UES” We had a lovely stay at the Hotel Wales. Large clean room with nice details, comfortable beds, and lovely tiled shower made the visit perfect. Hotel staff were professional and friendly. Loved the patio on the roof - it seemed to expand the size of the room. On weekends, they served drinks and bar food. Valet parking was expensive and it took a while to get our car. Hotel staff called the garage for us to see what caused the delay. Close to museums, central park and the subway. We would stay there again. The hotel offered suite discounts. Hotel also offered a discount to use the 92nd Street Y, a short walk away.

“Just OK” Used this hotel for a business trip. Called in the AM to get a reservation and was directed to their system that took my reservation using Hilton Honors information. Upon arrival they had lost my information. They did find a room with two beds. The beds were awful, lousy mattresses. I could never get the air conditioning adjusted properly as the room always felt musty. Bathrooms were actually very good I think they have remodeled them. The flat screen TV was very dark and I had to turn off lights to see the program. Furniture was in good shape and in general the room was clean. Never delivered papers in the morning, which is not a big deal but it is one of the services that you get use to at Hampton properties. Breakfast was not up to standard. They served egg rounds that were tasteless and under cooked pork sausage patties that were really greasy. No fresh fruit available and one of my pet peeves using artificial creamers. I opted for a bowl of raisin bran. For a quick trip to the airport this Hampton is OK but if I was staying in Houston for more than one night I would find a different place to stay.

“Great location, should have free wifi” We stayed here for one night after getting a great deal on a late rooms website. Its perfect for the USS Midway (highly recommended!) and the Gaslamp district which is a lot of fun. Our rooms had a fabulous view of the bay, and the champagne and snacks in the bar at the top of the hotel were really reasonably priced and worth it for the view. A hotel of this calibre and cost shoulld have free wifi though!

“Another great Kimpton hotel” My husband and I had a gift certificate for a free stay but I think this hotel is well worth paying for. Check in was very friendly and attentive. As stated in previous reviews, the rooms are small but very comfortable. The bathtub is nice and deep, great for soaking. The afternoon wine reception was fun with red and white wine and organic beer. We had some appetizers and drinks at the attached Ponzu restaurant and were very pleased with the quality and the service. For anyone wanting to rent a car for the day the hotel is right around the corner from the car rental agencies on O'Farrell St. For people who like a great breakfast, the hotel is also only a block from Max's at Geary and Mason and the famous Dottie's True Blue Cafe on Jones.

“Decent, budget hotel” Given our budget, I'd say we made a good pick. Location is good, a couple block to Penn Station, the Empire State Building, Macy's and the Mall of Manhattan. The Staff were attentive to our needs. We called up once for help with the Safe and they showed up immediately. The couple of issues we had, which were not deal breakers, was the poor water pressure. I ended up taking baths most nights instead of bothering with the shower. The water would be nice and warm then there would be a loud bang of pipes then a cold burst. It was mildly annoying. The other issue we had was with the outside noise. Several nights we slept with the window open. Our 11th floor room was very warm so despite the 20degree weather outside we did leave our window open most nights and man, it sounded like somebody was out there banging at the pipes with a hammer. I assume this was the pipes expanding and contracting in the cold air. It got real bad some nights, luckily we had brought ear plugs with us. Other than that the hotel room was nice and spacious, with a comfy bed. I would stay here again.

“Pros and cons of a landmark hotel stay” I stayed here for my second time in a decade as a captive hotel-conference attendee, but found the hotel to have the usual pros of an upscale historic property -- and one located at the heart of Chicago's Loop -- and the usual pros and cons of a big convention hotel. I was placed, for some reason, on a Hilton Honors floor, so my room was huge, pretty, beautifully maintained, and very comfortable, with armchair, windows that opened (though facing the El train), multiple HDTV channels, big bathroom with nice lotions (though no robes), and, upon request, a coffeemaker. The long and nicely furnished hallways assured that the room was undisturbed by neighbors. There were extra charges for wifi, parking, minibar, etc. Despite the conference crowds, the desk and room service staff were fast, competent, and friendly. The public rooms are turn-of-the-20th-century elegant, all carpet and gilded ceiling. However, with conference crowds milling about, one's focus was more on avoiding being trampled than on admiring the decor. While I did not try the well-known hotel restaurant, a quick room service meal was good. On the other hand, drinks and dinner at the informal bar-restaurant off the lobby proved frustratingly slow and mediocre. The hotel's lower level has a Starbucks and informal cafes and stores, which come in handy when the weather is too terrible to venture out. However, it is worth it to make the effort, since Chicago is full of wonderful eateries and shops.

“Freeway noise” It is 3am and I cannot sleep here because of the freeway noise. I am on the tenth floor and I can still hear it. this hotel is at the intersection of two big highways, so good luck getting any sleep if you are a light sleeper.

“To Each His Own” We stayed at the Muse for 5 nights from 8/31 thur 9/5 and contrary to the last review we were quite pleased. We booked the Muse based on a very good rate found on Travel Zoo and the reviews of others at this website. Our room located on the 14th floor was on a front corner of the hotel giving us windows on two sides which made it both bright and we had a satisfactory view down 46th street. The room was large enough and very clean although somewhat sterile. The bathroom was more than satisfactory with nice soaps and lotions. Our only real compalint was only one chair in the room. Of course, with two people, one person must sit on the bed if you spend any time in the room. According to the receptionist, Kimpton plans on refurbishing and upgrading to their standards towards the end of the year. which hopefully will improve the decor and fix the chair situration. They don't need to do anything with the bed, linens or pillows which are all above average. Also, the room was made up promptly every day. The wine reception every evening and free coffee in the hotel's restaurant(except Monday's) were nice touches. We would definetly return to the Muse and highly recommend it with the caveat that a higher floor might improve your overall perception..

“Good facilities -- some service issues” Stayed at Hyatt Regency with a colleague for 2 nights in August for a conference. Griselda was friendly and helpful at check-in, and we liked the hotel itself (carpet in room looked a bit tired) but had some service issues: -Bath amenities were not replenished -My colleague left clothes to be drycleaned and they were returned dirty with a rude note regarding what the cleaning folks thought was on the clothes (I won't repeat what the note said as it was vulgar) For what we paid, it was a good value, but not an outstanding stay by any means

“Very nice hotel. We'll be back!” Spent a night at this hotel because we had a dinner thing to go to. Used my Hilton HHonor points for it. Loved it. Will definitely come back. Check in was efficient. They had our key and coupons ready by the time we got there. It wsa around 2:45. No problems. Nice cute little cupcakes at the check-in counter too. Elevators were fast and quite spacious. Lots of uniformed folks greeting people and smiling. Very nice. Made guests feel welcome. I liked that a lot. Room was small. But not too bad. Just enough for two. Cozy would be the right word to describe it. I will not justify it and say it's New York, blah blah blah. That's bull, because I've stayed in many NYC hotels with pretty spacious rooms. But this one was just fine. Not big by any means, but it's fine. Must be the layout. Anyway, simple but nice furnishing. Hey this is NOT a 5-star hotel, so don't go looking for the St. Regis. It's tasteful and clean. And all you need is there. Flat screen TV. Wifi and wired internet. Ipod plug in. Walk in shower. In safe safe. Keuric coffee maker. Efficient A/C. And I do like the new Hilton toiletries. No complaints. Check out was efficient as well. Courteous. And people continued to be cheerful and all smiles. I will definitely be back.

“cool but could be better” We were having the interior of our house painted and did not want our children to breathe in the fumes. I have been wanting to stay here since it opened and was super excited about our stay. The check in was really nice, we were greeted with a drink upon arrival. Your room key has an imprint of an old jail key on it which is pretty cool and the interior of the main hotel retained many features of the original jail, like the layout, or the prison door on the entrance to the kitchen in the restaurant. The view was nice but the hotel was very noisy at a variety of times, late at night from people leaving the nightclub or screaming in the hallways because they were drunk to people running up and down the hallways in the morning and the sound of people talking. The people in the room next to us were loudly playing music. I also didn't like the computerized system for things like a virtual gift shop, etc. I found it difficult to find what I needed and when I did order something it took forever for it to arrive. I felt like once I checked it, we were completely alone with no customer service at all. If they could fix that as well as the soundproofing it would be a 5 star hotel.

“Cute Hotel - Great Location” I enjoyed my stay at the O'Brien. Its has a small lobby and there was always someone at the front desk to greet us. Both the day and night staff were very friendly & helpful. I get sick of the big box fancy hotels that all look the same. This hotel was great, it had character and it was refreshing. It offered comfortable beds, nice big flatscreen, big bathroom, cozy general meeting area on each floor. I LOVED the balcony.........even if it overlooked a parking lot. It was nice to sit outside and read the morning paper. Breakfast isn't fancy, but there are enough choices. All in all a charming little hotel.

“Improved” We'd stayed here about 3 years ago, and since then they've refurbished some. Very clean, but you need to expect a basic American indoor-halled motel. Lots of foreign visitors taking advantage of the budget prices and the auto-friendly location. (Free covered parking, although the parking is tricky for the beginning driver - but that's true all over San Francisco, isn't it?) We like the Lombard Street location, since we enjoy exploring the various neighborhoods by car. However, it does create some noise; this isn't a place for a light sleeper, although the rooms that face away from the street may be quieter. Some front desk staff isn't completely easy in English, but it's a very small minority of the staff, and only a problem on the phone. Breakfast is (good) coffee, OJ and various pastries that always seemed to be brought in fresh. Plan on carrying them back to the room, since there's no dining area. Large rooms, decent towels, so-so mattresses. And on those rare days when the city gets hot, there's AC as well as heating in the individual units. We averaged less than $100 a night, and that's a real bargain in San Francisco, where parking at one of the fine hotels, regardless of their discounted rates in this economy, can run $35 a night. Quite satisfied, all things considered.

“Great place and GREAT service!” I love this shiny new hotel in Soho next to the Holland Tunnel. The only reason I am not giving it 5 stars is because they CHARGE FOR WIFI. Shame on them. What luxury hotel charges a daily wifi rate anymore? Don't nickel and dime me, just add it into the nightly rate somehow. We had a lovely 1 br corner suite overlooking the Hudson River, building tops and Varick Street below. The service was Four Seasons quality from check-in to check-out. There is nothing guest services won't do for you. Lovely, articulate, warm staff. Can't say enough good things about the people who work there. I guess they are afraid of the Donald saying "you're FIRED!". Great location, in walking distance to Tribeca, Soho, Lower East Side and the W. Village. Great price too for the quality of room we stayed in. Nice thick walls, you can't hear anyone above you or next door to you. Ok, I have said enough, I just wish they didn't charge a daily rate for the internet connection. Stay here!

“Top quallity hotel” I would stay in this hotel anywhere in the world. This was my first visit to Indianapolis. My client -- a large local business -- suggested this hotel. There may be equally nice hotels in town, but I cannot imagine one more pleasant than this one. The room amenities were top-class. The staff was attentive. The location seems very central. The business center is right off the lobby and unstaffed -- 3 computers and a printer. I personally enjoyed the modern art throughout the public places in the hotel. The wine bar was a pleasant surprise. I got to try some wines from some new places, e.g, Uruguay. Here are the two worst things that I can say about this hotel: having to use the room key in the elevator was is bit annoying and the fax machine in the business center would not connect with my office. I will stay in this hotel on my return trips to Indianapolis.

“Park Plaza-Boston” The Park Plaza was just as good as it looked online. What a great location too; it's easy to walk the whole Freedom Trail and explore the city. It's in a convenient location with tons of great restaurants. We had a wonderful brunch every morning. We will definitely stay here again when in Boston.

“Total Lack of Service!” I have to start this review off by letting you all know that I'm NOT a diva! I posted a great review of The Stoneleigh a while back. But I have since changed my mind, and this is why: My daughter, who lived in Dallas, got married last September. I must've made a trip to Dallas at least once a month for a year and always stayed at The Stoneleigh because of it's convenient location, great rates and it was a nice hotel. We booked 40 rooms for the weekend of my daughter's wedding and held a party the night before for over 100 people on their penthouse floor-using The Stoneleigh's food and beverage. Even when I wasn't staying at the hotel, we would go there for drinks either in the bar or on the patio. We also referred many friends to stay there. I don't know about you, but I think that added up to a LOT of $$$$$. My youngest daughter and I stayed at The Stoneleigh last weekend while visiting my middle daughter. When I arrived, no one offered to help with my bags, upon checking in, there was no recognition that I was a return guest, much less having spent thousands of $ the past year at the hotel. I was pointed in the direction of the elevator, not shown to the room, etc...(not that I needed that, but it would've been nice for someone to ask). During my entire stay, the toiletries or mini bar were never refilled or replenished. There obviously were 2 people staying in the room, but only 1 bed was turned down. I couldn't get the free wifi to connect and called reception to help. I was given some instructions that I had already tried, I said I would just figure it out, she said OK and hung up. We met some friends in the bar for drinks and the staff were unfriendly and rude. I had breakfast in the Bolla Restaurant the last morning before checking out. I was pleasantly seated and then waited and waited for a waiter to acknowledge me. I had to ask a bus boy twice to send my waiter-and I was only 1 of 2 parties in the whole restaurant. After my food arrived, he never came to ask if everything was OK. I also had to flag him down to get my check when I finished. At this point, I was boiling. At least the food was good. The Stoneleigh Hotel is a gorgeous deco hotel-the public rooms are beautifully decorated, and the guestrooms are large and spacious. The only thing this hotel is lacking is SERVICE. There is none. I should say that I was told by one of the valet's-with a scowl on his face, that new management had stepped in about 6 weeks ago, and things had changed for the worse. I will give a shout out to the Valet guys-they were the best part of my visit. They were courteous and called me by name and always knew which car was ours. I'm not asking for special treatment or want to be a VIP, but it seems that somewhere, someone would see a guest profile and recognize that we've been regular guests of The Stoneleigh and would, at least, be welcomed back. I was very disappointed with my visit. I'm not sure I'll return.

“Nearly perfect” There comes a time when a hotel is praised so much that it can't possibly live up to its advance billing. I almost wish I hadn't read so much about the Sorrento before I arrived, because I was expecting perfection! Having said that, this hotel is impressive on a number of fronts. The bed linens are wonderfully comfortable, and there's an assortment of pillows catering to every preference and allergy level. (I thought the mattress could have been firmer, though.) The robes are Frette -- very luxe. I stayed in a standard room that had a view of downtown Seattle. If you're there on business, there's free internet access, and a fax machine in the room. There's even a generous supply of office stuff -- pens, paper clips, etc. -- in the desk. (I was on vacation, so I didn't look too hard at all that stuff, but there was a lot of it.) Overall, the service was efficient and friendly. I had no trouble at all getting my car from the valet parking; it was always there within two minutes. I used the town car once, at the last minute, when it started raining and I didn't feel like driving. The wait was only about 5 minutes, and the driver gave me a card with the hotel's phone number, so I could give him a call when I was ready to return to the hotel. I had dinner at the Hunt Club. What a cosy place, and the food was good, too. The hotel isn't perfect, though. As everyone has mentioned, the standard rooms are small, and the bathroom felt tiny. I might splurge for a suite next time. Also, I could clearly hear the people next door. Thank goodness they seemed to go to bed early because I didn't hear them late at night when I was trying to sleep. And that view of downtown Seattle? It comes at a price: a steep climb uphill from all the tourist sites! If you're into getting fit, it's a cool experience. But it's not so great when the weather's cold and rainy, and you're carrying shopping bags (from Nordstrom, of course.) There's always the town car, but you'll probably have to wait. Still, I'd give the hotel a five because the staff is well trained and friendly, the bed is super comfortable, the hotel has a historic ambience that's hard to duplicate, and it has a well-regarded restaurant. In other words, it does what a boutique hotel is supposed to do. I'd stay at the Sorrento again. But I'll be sure to bring earplugs and a good pair of walking shoes! P.S. The hotel guarantees that you'll get the lowest rates on its website. I paid $169 for the standard ("deluxe") room.

“Okay Stay” The front desk people were quite friendly. Even though there was a host of people arriving for a convention, the desk person was calm and treated me as If I was the only person he had to see. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. My biggest complaint was the heat. The thermostat read 68 degrees, but the room had to have been closer to 75. the temp would not go down despite my turning on the AC. I did not sleep well due to the heat. The restaurant staff was very friendly, but service was slow. Food was just okay. Within walking distance to Capital and Denver civic center. The hotel parking was closed, but there was public parking is close by. Overall not a bad stay, but for a comparable hotel in downtown Denver, I would recommend the Grand Hyatt over the Sheraton.

“reasonable rates, nice accomodations, helpful staff” We stayed for three nights in late July. While the room rates varied each night, the weekend was very reasonable. We asked for a high floor room when we checked in early and the staff complied. We had a splendid southern view from the 30th floor. The rooms are spacious and well-appointed, nice bedding, cabinets and closets, good lighting, nice bathroom. The only oddity was an old-style, non-flat-screen TV. The neighborhood has some nice restaurants and is convenient to both mid-town and downtown.

“Adequate Hotel - Not Horrible, Not Spectacular” During my stay in Seattle, I had the opportunity to stay at the Hotel Vintage Park and the Hotel Monaco Seattle. I would say that, between the two, there is really no comparison as Monaco was much larger, well-appointed and helpful. Both are in a good location and about a block from one another (the length of the Seattle Public Library in between). I have nothing to complain about with Vintage Park, only the observation that my room was rather small (but just fine for a solo traveler) as was the very small lobby. No one offered to help with my bags to the room, though I managed despite quite a load. Another observation was that the hotel staff - bell vs. front desk - seemed very competitive with one another which I thought odd, or at least to be so obvious about it. I would stay here again if I got a good deal on the hotel - the location was fine, room interesting and clean, and no glaring problems. It just doesn't beckon you back like some other hotels. I loved the Monaco Seattle, as well as the Monaco Chicago. You can tell a big difference between Vintage Park and the Monaco.

“A matter of taste” Recently modernised with spacious and comfortable 1 and 2 bedroom units, with kitchen facilities. Breakfast, evening snacks/drinks (sometimes dinner) and internet access are included in the price, although parking at $13 a day is not. This hotel is ideally going to suit families with a couple of children - the hotel has a pool, and is the right side of town for going to Sea World and the Zoo. It is also going to suit small groups of people looking for multi-occupancy units - for example, those going to Qualcomm Stadium, which is easy to get to. If you belong to one of these categories, you will likely be very appreciative of this hotel and probably rate it 4 or 5. Other travellers (including ourselves) will be less enthusiastic. If you like a hotel that is potentially reasonably quiet, the Residence will inevitably seem a bit noisy. Depending on your neighbours, it could be very noisy, although we noted that the sound insulation is reasonably good. I believe the hotel does a very good job in providing accommodation of a certain type. It is just not going to be to everyone's taste.

“Be a Select Guest and reep the benefits!” I took my 18 year old niece for a 3 day weekend trip to New York City for her high school graduation. I've been to New York 6 times within the last couple of years and like to try different hotels in Manhattan. After realizing the prices were definitely much higher than my last visit I decided to try Hotwire. I landed the Omni for $237 per night. Other hotels I was considering were in the $300 range, so I was pleased with the rate and hotel chosen. I stayed at the Omni about 8 years ago and truly loved the location. We were treated very well by the front desk personnel upon check-in. We arrived at 10 a.m. and still one of our rooms was ready. The rooms are relatively small, but nicely appointed. (My stay at the New York Palace last year included a room twice the size of the Omni's.) The bed was comfortable with top of the line linens. The bathroom was functional and elegant with a marble shower and granite countertop. We had unimpressive views from both rooms. (I overlooked St. Patrick's Cathedral from my room at the Palace.) The housekeeping staff was efficient and helpful. The most important point to share about the Omni is their "Select Guest" program. I signed up for this free program after making my reservation. I received a "Select Guest" card in the mail with various coupons that included room upgrades and 50% my next Omni weekend stay. As a "Select Guest" member you receive complimentary morning drinks delivered to your room, a newspaper of your choosing, late check-out until 5 p.m. when available and preferences noted of your pillow type and floor you'd like to be on in all Omni hotels. I was thrilled with these perks! I enjoyed freshly squeezed orange juice and hot tea each morning and the New York Times. I also utilized the late check-out since our flight didn't leave until 7 p.m. Most importantly, I've noticed that when other travelers book their rooms through a discounter like Hotwire or Priceline when they check-in they are treated like Hobos on holiday. As I said, our front desk person treated us kindly and respectfully. She was a great introduction to New York for my niece who had never visited this fine city before. Overall, we had a wonderful time. The hotel is centrally located. The rooms are nice and clean. I've stayed at the Palace, the Benjamin and The Waldorf Astoria. The Palace is my favorite, but the Omni still ranks high in my book. If you decide to stay at the Omni, you MUST be a "Select Guest!"

“Nice and Quiet” Very close to subways (1/2 block to #1 train and 1 block to N,R,W trains). Quiet and safe neighborhood dominated by flower shops and Chinese imported goods shops. Numerous coffee shops/drug stores nearby, along with some restaurant choices (including a great $1/slice pizza shop at 6th and 25th). Less than 10 minute walk to Madison Square Garden/Penn Station. Free internet (wireless and wired) and a restaurant (breakfast) on premises with a small bar should you like to have a casual drink.

“What a place to grab a drink!” I have traveled the world and seen many a bar in my life. The Oak Bar in the Fairmont Copley Hotel is absolutely amazing! Style, class and service are exceptional here. I recomend it for an after dinner cocktail while out on the town. The drink list is extensive, the service was great, the band was incredible and the atmosphere was A+.

“perfection has a name: "Four Seasons in Beverly Hills"” We stayed two nights in a suite in this hotel. When we arrived we met one of the most friendliest receptionists ever. He was very interested in Europe and The Netherlands. We were escorted to the room together with our luggage, this is very efficient. The room was beautiful decorated. A large living room and a large bedroom. We had two bathrooms. In the room they have an Ipad so you can order roomservice, concierge assistance etc. from the Ipad. The spa area is beautiful, but without rest area. The swimming pool is heated, the service is like the rest of the hotel perfect. I went to the gym and sauna and left my bracelet in a locker. The staff from the spa did not know my name, but when I was in the lobby the receptionist came to me and said that I left my bracelet in the spa. So they could describe me and reception did know who I was. The spa reception excused because they did not know my name. I said that I liked the service a lot as they knew me. All the staff know you immediately. For example when we had breakfast on our second day the lady in the restaurant knew what we ordered the day before. Another lady in the restaurant (she served lunch the former day) knew us and came to us for a small talk. This is service we appreciate and like. One thing that was not top was the reservation for a restaurant. I gave 2 names to the concierge for a restaurant. Thought it was one restaurant, but by accident gave 2 different restaurants. I also said that if they did not have a table I wanted to go to another trendy restaurant. They made reservations for one of the two I gave, unfortunately this was not a trendy restaurant. Partly it was my fault as I gave two names, partly the concierge could contact me and asked which restaurant I was more interested for. The food in the other restaurant was good, but I expected another restaurant. We liked this hotel so much. If we return to LA we definitely will come back. This hotel is known for the service. We got the best service in America in this hotel!

“Worst hotel ever” Don't be sucked in by the Hollywood idea of this hotel. The bathrooms have no counter space and the shower is terrible. There are a type of spanish rounded tile on the stairs, which are everywhere and it's very difficult to walk in business heels let alone fashion heels. Unless I have to for an event, I will never stay at this hotel again.

“Loved it” I asked for a quiet room and was given an inside room on the top floor. I never heard a sound the whole time I was there. The room was big, and I ran the fireplace in the evening and in the morning just because it was there. The common room is quite nice. I missed the wine reception, but I stopped in after and finished the leavings. The morning breakfast was excellent. I had quiche, yogurt, oatmeal, and fruit, but there were also pastries, hard-boiled eggs, cereal, and more. The staff was friendly and helpful. Here are a few nitpicks - you decide if any are important to you. 1. The building is old, e.g., you open and close the accordion door of the ancient elevator yourself (I thought it was fun, but it doesn't make for quick trips to the room). 2. The rug in my room was not a sparkling hotel commercial carpet, but it fit the feel of the place. 3. The coffee both in-room and at breakfast is Folgers-ey. 4. The shades in the room don't block out all the light - I brought my eye mask and I was fine. I had a great stay at White Swan Inn, and I recommend it.

“Very nice downtown hotel” Stayed at the downtown Indianapolis Marriott for one night in mid-July. Traveling just with wife for pleasure. We originally stayed at the Marriott due to its relatively low internet rate and were pleasantly impressed by the hotel. Originally, we were scheduled for two nights but decided at 3 pm the next day to check out - they did not charge extra for the late check-out. The lobby and room were equally nice - very well furnished with nice amenities. I disagree with a previous reviewerer comparing this to a Motel 6 - this Marriott is a very nice, higher-end hotel typical for other full-service Marriott hotels. The valet, bellhop and check-in staff all provided great service and the check-in experience was smooth. Used room service for breakfast - food quality was excellent but a little on the pricey side. Concierge was very helpful and friendly. I agree with a previous reviewer that the pool is too small.

“A Very Pleasant Surprise!” We stayed here for 3 nights on business, March 5 – 8. As Marriott Platinum Rewards members, we always try to stay at a Marriott, but we couldn’t get a room anywhere downtown, and grudgingly stayed at the Omni instead. Wow! What a pleasant surprise this was. Although we are not members and haven’t stayed at an Omni in over 20 years, all of the staff, from the front door all the way up to the Concierge Lounge, treated us as old friends. The service at this hotel is absolutely top-flight. The Concierge Lounge at this Omni is truly “concierge” style. Unlike at the Marriott, alcoholic drinks are complimentary, mixed for you, and served to you at your table. In the evening, the Concierge Lounge staff always offers to make dinner reservations for you and to help in any way they can. The hotel had a very nice bar area on the 3rd floor. We found the restaurant Noé to be highly overrated, but it was slightly better than most hotel restaurants. Our room (1724 Club Room) was tastefully decorated in warm shades of beige, taupe, gray, & charcoal. Although the bed was very comfortable, it was too high for me (5’2”) to easily get in & out of. We appreciated the extremely light duvet, which enabled us to sleep comfortably. There is a thicker duvet draped across the bottom of the bed if you need it. Lighting was excellent & bright. There was a large desk with comfortable leather chair, and an armchair with ottoman. The view was over Olive Street at the front entrance of the hotel. The bathroom was large enough in which to comfortably move around and had separate shower stall & bathtub. In addition to the usual shampoo, shower gel, conditioner, lotion and soap, there were also Q-tips, cotton balls, sewing kit, toothpaste, mouthwash, razor, shaving cream, shoe mitt & shower cap. The bar of soap was much larger than normally found in a hotel, which we very much appreciated. I have only a few minor complaints. (1) We originally booked (in October) 5 nights at $284 on the hotel website, but due to changes in our business appointment schedule & flight changes, we had to reduce our stay to 3 nights. (These changes were made a week in advance). The hotel did change the reservation, but bumped our nightly room rate to $379. (They told me the price had gone up because the hotel was fully booked)! However, at the same time, I also reduced the stay to 2 nights for a colleague traveling with us, and his price stayed the same. Go figure! (2) We arrived in the room to find a used towel on the floor of the shower, so we were not convinced that the shower had been cleaned after the previous guest. We called this to the attention of the front desk, and housekeeping did come to take care of it. Still, it was a rather yucky thing to see upon arrival. Otherwise, housekeeping was generally good & pleasant. (3) The location was a bit far from the Convention Center. We had to take a taxi to & from everyday, costing us $9 plus tip each way. Also, it was quite a climb up a steep hill to get back to the hotel on evenings when we went out to eat. The escalators between 5th & Hope Streets do make the climb back to the hotel a bit easier, but we were told they stop running at 9 or 10 pm. These minor complaints account for my lower rating in Value, Location and Cleanliness. The lower rating for Sleep Quality is due to to extreme height of the bed. Nevertheless, it is a 5-star hotel. All in all, we enjoyed our stay and were very pleased with this Omni Hotel. I highly recommend it.

“Excellent choice, great hotel” Just back from a long weekend trip to NYC with family. We had 3 rooms total and each were different and excellent. Location cannot be beat, just off Times Square as well as a close 5 minute walk to Rockefeller Center and 5th Avenue. Close by subways can take you everywhere in Manhattan. Service was great, bellman was wonderful and always asking if he could assist. We were all upgraded, even with a great rate from Travelzoo. rooms were a great size, bathrooms varied. Ours was on the smaller size, but workable. Only (small)issue was I could never figure out how to shower whithout drenching the bathroom floor. Will sasy the bed and pillows were a little too soft for my tastes, but still comforatble enought o sleep. The half glass wall just did not do the trick! Other than that would recommend this great find to anyone heading to NYC.

“Disappointing From Start to Finish” My wife and I stayed 2 nights at the Loews in late July while attending a professional conference in the city. Our problems with the hotel began with check-in. We had received an e-mail telling us that check-in commenced at 3pm, so when we arrived at the hotel shortly before 3pm we weren't too surprised to find that our room wouldn't be ready for a little while. When we checked back about 30 minutes later they told us it would still be a while and that they would call us when it was ready (in fairness the desk person did provide us with a couple of drinks coupons for the bar). An hour or two later we still hadn't been contacted and so we checked back with the desk only to be told that it would still be a while and to await their phone call. Finally, approximately 4hrs after first arriving at the hotel and desperately needing a room so that we could get ready for a 7pm reception we checked back with the desk and were told that our room was ready - no phone call, no nothing. We later found out that people who had arrived at the hotel an hour or two after us had no problems getting a room even though we were still waiting! During this 4hr wait we looked around the hotel to try to find somewhere comfortable to pass the time, however the only space appeared to be in the restaurant/bar and once we finished our drinks we felt obliged to move on. After wandering around other parts of the building it became evident that there just aren't any good social areas in the hotel, even the lobby area doesn't really lend itself to hanging out. When we were finally given key cards to the room they were incorrectly coded so we had to rush downstairs to take care of that. Our room (822), once we did get into it, was also a little disappointing. While the view was nice enough, a glance around the room revealed that it needed some freshening-up (rust stains in the sink, scuff marks on the ceiling, etc). It just gave the impression of a room that had seen slightly better days. Coupled with this there were at least two occasions during our stay when the wait for elevators was very long. Additionally, it appears that wifi is not available for free and parking is very expensive (NOTE: a very short 2 blocks south at 12th & Sansom is a Central Parking facility - they usually have a coupon online which means that parking there costs 1/2 the price of the hotel parking). Overall, our short stay did not give us a good impression of this hotel. While I think this is an interesting, historic building I'm not convinced that it makes for a great hotel space. The mismanagement of our check-in process definitely didn't get us off to a good start, but the hotel and its services did little to help win us back.

“Good basic hotel in a good location” This is a motel-style building with indoor hallways, located on Third Street. It is across the street from Park La Brea, a large apartment complex. It is about three blocks from the Farmer's Market and about two blocks from The Grove, a large Las Vegas-style outdoor mall. The hotel is clean and quiet, and the staff are friendly and helpful. There is a small swimming pool but no spa or exercise room. The staff told me about a nearby gym on Wilshire but I was not able to find it. The rooms are small and the decor has a 70s feel. Not rooms you would want to spend a lot of time in but OK for sleeping. A small table and chairs, but no desk. I did not try the internet service. Plenty of hot water and towels but the amenities are a bit chintzy. The room had a refrigerator and coffee maker. Our room tended to be cold; the only heat was a window heat pump unit which at least was not too loud. There is a nice, friendly restaurant on the premises and a coffee place across the street. Parking is safe and convenient in the alley at the back of the hotel. This is a reasonably priced, comfortable, and friendly hotel, perfectly adequate for travelers who are not interested in paying big bucks to get a mint on the pillow.

“One of the worst travel experiences ever” We arrived at 12:40 am last night to find a very old man behind the desk (I am not an ageist but this individual looked like he would struggle to even stand). I was informed that my room was given away, no other rooms were available in the nearby area, and I would have to stay at a downtown hotel in Jacksonville. The desk person was completely overwhelmed when I even asked to see whether there may be more amenable nearby options. Later I found that the manager had called me at 12:28 to ask me to call her (she did not mention the room was given away). I gather reservations at this location are first-come, first-serve, catch-as-you-can. The hotel they booked us in required valet parking, was an isolated high rise with very expensive breakfast, and charged $ 9.95 for internet. In total, not including the round trip inconvenience - we had traveled 1.5 hours to the hotel, arrived exhausted, and we had a 7:30 am meeting that was no longer nearby - the lack of sleep, the extra gas, etc. this little glitch cost us $40.00. I travel frequently for business, and the last hotel chain that did this to me - a Holiday Inn Sunspree Resort in Florida during the 1990's that relocated us to another Holiday Inn with no amenities - I have never frequented again. While this was expensive for me, in the long run, this will be more expensive for Marriott

“アメリカらしいホテル” 表玄関からエスカレーターでワンレベル下がったところにフロントがあります。フロントの近くに 無料で使えるインターネットもありますが、セキュリティーが緩いなと思いました。フロント近くにはバーもあり、いろいろな国の言葉が聞こえてきて、客層が多様な印象でした。 お部屋は広さは確保されているものの、設備がなにしろ古い。水回りに特に古さを感じ、タオルまでも何百回洗ったのかと思うほど、使いこまれた感じです。肝心な冷蔵庫やセーフティーボックスがありませんでした。 机の上にウェルカムの手紙とスナックがおいてあったのが嬉しい心づけでした。

“IMPRESSIVE!” From the minute I checked it, I realized this not the usual Candlewood. The lobby is bright, clean and the front desk associate was extremely pleasant and friendly. The room (studio) was very spacious and very clean. The bathroom was better than a few full service hotels I've stayed in. The room is equipped with everything someone on an extended trip will need. Everything was good quality and well kept. The bed was comfy and it was very quiet despite being that close to I-10. This is a good choice for short or long trips to the area. There are several restaurants in the area and everyone is eager to help should you need advise on dining or directions. This one just a gold star for being squeaky clean and for having some of the friendliest staff I've encountered at any hotel.

“Nice and comfortable hotel.” Stayed here for a function. Hotel and the room was nice. Overall, a very good stay. The one negative is parking. Only street parking and some garages are available. I thought the valet parking ($41 a night) was high but I hear other hotels charge the same. Either way that is high.

“Nice enough hotel. Big rooms, a bit dated.” The Washington Court has a great location near Capitol Hill and not too far from the Canadian Embassy. If you're not going to a place in the area, there are much better located hotels nearer the Dupont Circle area. I was only in the hotel one night. The room was comfortably furnished and rather spacious, as was the bathroom. The hotel is showing its age and is looking a bit dated.

“Great Clean Newish Hotel” I recently stayed here and enjoyed this hotel. This hotel is less than 2 years old and has that newish feel and is clean. Staff was super nice. Room was quiet and I didn't hear anything (I am a lite sleeper). There are a lot of business folks around, especially in the morning for the free breakfast. Breakfast was good, hot and cold items.

“Great Soho location, nice rooms, limit service” Stayed for a weekend in May 2009. If you are aware of the Soho layout, it's a great spot. Near many restaurants, shopping, subways. Easy to find just off 6th Ave and Canal. Rooms were new and nice, normal NYC small. Shower only in our room which I like, but some may not. Service staff was friendly, but WAY understaffed. They just couldn't keep up. However overall the stay was very nice if you are just looking for a good location and nice bed before heading back out into the city.

“che spettacolo!!!!” albergo meraviglioso in posizione eccellente,camere immense e pulite.io non avevo la colazione ma la facevo al bar della hall e ve la consiglio caldamente perchè le pastine so eccezzionali...spesa 2 paste e cappuccino sugli 8 dollari!!

“Solid airport hotel--exceptional for the price” I had a very early flight from Boston and had been looking for a good hotel near Logan. Everything was up in the $300 range so I decided to try Priceline and was shocked that I got the Hilton for $90!!! This is an above-average Hilton. The lobby is airy and immediately inviting. Check-in (and check-out) was quick and friendly. I was given room 360-- a smoking room as I'd requested. I understand the anti-smoking issues, but I admire Hilton for still accommodating those of us who can't quite kick the habit. The room was large, sleek, clean and had a nice view of Boston. The tv was brand new, flat-panel with great resolution, although the choice of channels was a bit limited (about 25) when compared to some other hotels. I couldn't quite master the a/c system which I set at 68 but kept bouncing back to 74. It didn't matter much because the glass captured the cold outside, but on a hot day, I would've called maintenance. I ordered room service, chicken quesadilla and a turkey panini with fries. The food was good quality, especially the fries which tasted fresh-cut. It wasn't a culinary extravaganza, but it did the job. As for the walkway to the airport, it's really only useful if you're flying in/out of terminal A (Delta). Otherwise, use the hotel shuttle which runs 24 hours. Highly recommended hotel for travelers needing to stay near Logan.
“Almost decent location, with bad pillows” The rooms could use much better pillows. Front staff very nice. Avoid rooms near elevator, it's very noisy!

“Possibly a former Embassy Suites?” The rooms are huge suites and the layout of the building with the huge atrium reminds me of most Embassy Suites I've stayed in. Unfortunately, the Crowne Plaza Suites doesn't include the wonderful ES free omelet bar or even a buffet breakfast. Although the building is mere feet off from a very busy freeway, I was pleased that the room noise was minimal. I was unable to find a way to turn of the outside light on the 1.5 sq. ft balcony, but the curtains did a good job darkening the room.

“Huge Rooms” On all previous trips to San Antonio I have stayed on the Riverwalk. This trip I didn't need the touristy things and the Hyatt Place was perfect. It is very convenient to the airport, shopping, Trinity University, and downtown. The room was enormous and quite clean. Plenty of towels and the beds were fine. The air conditioner makes a strange noise, thumping after it cycles off. The internet seemed to be hit or miss. Sometimes it worked, other times I got no connection. Staff were all very friendly and helpful. Plenty of parking. The breakfast has enough choices.

“Nice resort hotel with fine restaurant” We enjoyed three days off during busy business trip at this hotel. I rarely dine at hotel restaurant as they are usually expensive and taste are just standard. Though the prices are bit high side, the main restaurant served variety of interesting menu and taste was outstanding. In addition, daily fireworks starting at 9pm added good taste for dinner.

“Nice hotel, but some blips” I stayed in this hotel for business. The conference was held at the hotel. In terms of the room, it had a nice style to it and it was clean, quiet, and comfortable. However, the telephone did not work well in that whenever I put the line on mute the other party could hear someone else talking. In addition, the Internet service in the hotel room was extremely unreliable (even though I paid for "premium" Internet); note: it was wireless only. Both of these things together did not bode well for the presentation that I was giving over the web. (However, the front desk did give me a credit for Internet service since it virtually did not work.) (There also is a computer in the hotel room. I did not use it, but I found it interesting that there was one. So, in case you forgot your computer at home or you wanted to browse the web, I suppose you could have used that.) The television in the room was just fine, although I did not have much time to watch it. The hotel restaurant was fair. It was very expensive and some things were good and others were not. The wait for service was sometimes quite awhile. The hotel also has a Starbucks on the first floor. It was pretty decent and I was able to get "convenience food" (e.g., fruit and cheese cubes, etc.) during lunchtime as I was pressed for time and I did not have time to sit down and eat lunch at a restaurant. I called the front desk asking about breakfast and how I can get it in the morning. I was told that the breakfast was on the second floor, but the front desk person did not mention that room service was available or that there was a card for ordering breakfast (to schedule room service ahead of time). The former is pretty obvious, but the latter was not. The breakfast card was neatly tucked away in the desk drawer and I did not notice it until it was too late. The conference facilities were so so. The restrooms were not conveniently located and seemed to be in odd locations. On the other hand, the Internet for the meeting rooms was excellent (as opposed to the dismal experience I had connecting from my room). A mall is right across the street from this hotel. In addition, there are several Walgreens stores within walking distance. This hotel is located in the Magnificent Mile area and so it was very convenient and safe. Most of the time, the bellman was able to assist with getting a taxi. I also learned that you do have to wait outside for the airport shuttles as they do not come into the lobby. I got back to the airport by taking a taxi (about $45 to O'Hare) rather than taking the shuttle (Go Airport Express). (On the other hand, getting to the hotel using the airport shuttle was a great deal and convenient, even though it seemed to take forever.) I was able to store my luggage for several hours on my last day. (Thanks Clive for your kind service.) While my stay in Chicago was primarily for business, I did have the opportunity to visit the mall (as I mentioned) and also the Art Institute of Chicago. 1. The Shops at North Bridge At first, I did not know that a mall was across the street (520 N. Michigan Ave.). I thought that it was just a Nordstrom's store. I entered the North Bridge mall (across from the hotel) and I was very surprised. It was beautiful inside with three levels of floors for Nordstroms, Nordstrom Spa (got my Jane Iredale makeup there), an opitcal shop (called Optica), a Bose store, and many other stores and restaurants. 2. The Art Institute of Chicago This place was amazing. I have visited many museums throughout the US and this was one of the best. (I found it comparable to the de Young museum in San Francisco. It was almost as awesome as MoMA in NYC.) This museum had a very extensive collection of Asian and European art. Unfortunately, I did not have time to see the Roy Lichtensetein exhibit (even though I would have loved to see it). However, the admission price was very reasonable. (I believe I paid $9.) And, the museum was open until 8PM on Thursday. (While I took a taxi to the museum from the hotel, I ended up walking back to the hotel from there. It took awhile, as I believe it is just a little over a mile, but is certainly walkable.)

“Excellent Family Hotel” Great, safe location. Helpful staff. Spacious suites for a family of five, nice complimentary breakfast and weekday complimentary lite suppers. Highly recommend this property for families wanting space and convenience to all of Washington's great sites!

“Perfect location, average Hotel” Overall, you can't find a better location for a hotel in DC, especially for business and/or Mall walking. However, this hotel is a typical, older Holiday Inn. The lobby is small and is always jam packed with people. The lines for the desk are usually long and the service could be better. The rooms are not always very clean and their is a musty smell throughout the hallways. The restaurant and bar is average. All that being said, I will continue to stay here, mainly due to the perfect location.

“Great Location and Breakfast!” Very convenient, not only to the airport, but also to drive into Philly, and get back out of town to stay. The complimentary breakfast was also great. Chef's on hand to take orders (omelets, pancakes, french toast, etc), as well as a great buffet. Comp. newspaper at your door, nice fitness center. $5 to park, per day. One complaint: Just coming in town, ready to put your feet up. Check in time is 3:00pm. We got there at 4:15, and they did not have our room ready. We sat in the lobby for 30 minutes, before our room was ready. They did apologize, and were nice, but sure did not offer anything. That is nearly two hours after the listed check in time.

“Superb Hotel and Staff--Will Recommend and Return” The Sofitel is a superb hotel that met and exceeding our expectations. The Sofitel is located in the heart of Philly and within walking distance of most major attractions, great restaurants, and business center. Check-in was flawless and expedient, and we were welcomed by the hotel's wonderfully trained and professional staff. Parking was a bit expensive, but well worth the price knowing our car was safe and we could access it, quickly, at anytime throughout the day (for no additional charge). Our room was elegant, clean, and spacious. It included a large, immaculate, modern bathroom complete with spacious shower, separate tub, twin sinks, and granite and marble appointments. Our king-sized bed was incredibly comfortable. My only complaint was that the bed was made with only a sheeted, heavy duvet. It was impossible for me to control my body temperature without blasting the air conditioning. A separate sheet would have been most welcomed. Our modern room included a flat-screen TV, a desk and chair, two spacious closets, a safe, two fluffy robes, a Bose stereo system, and free bottled water, My husband would have welcomed free wifi, but it was available for a fee. The hotel is quiet and pristine. The on-site restaurant was excellent, and I would recommend it for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or an afternoon cocktail/snack. The concierge was most helpful--providing us directions and eating recommendations. We will definitely return to the Sofitel. One of the best!

“Boutique Hotel With Lots of Class” An absolutely beautiful hotel in an old 1920s building. First class, white glove service the whole way (excellent employees). Our corner room had 2 walls that were nothing but floor to ceiling windows, affording great views of the city. Top of the line furnishings (ivory silk bedding, granite top tables, mahogany finished furniture with matte polished silver handles, cd / clock radio, flat screen tv, art deco lamps) and super-comfy soft pillows and bed! The windows actually open fairly wide to let in fresh air. Big bathroom with only 1 sink. Excellent restaurant, great breakfast w/fresh squeezed orange juice. Negatives: The only parking option is valet parking for $23 per day. High-speed internet access is available for $10. The roof top pool is very tiny (big enough for 2 people tops) but it has beautiful city views (and a hot tub). This is truly a first class hotel and I recommend it to everyone!

“SFO without charm, but eficency” Its a regular Hilton: big, well located, nice rooms and busy. The plus here in SFO was the service. Check in guy really seemed to care about my stay, altough the lobby were chaotic due a conferece goers. Great choice,

“A Fine Hotel” This is a fine, casual hotel that's centrally located. A friend and I stayed in a one bedroom suite and it was basically like a one bedroom apartment, with a full kitchen and a small balcony. The decor is hip and contemporary but not pretentious. The breakfast buffet was great, too, with make your own waffles, yogurt, eggs, pastries, good coffee, etc. All in all, highly recommended!

“部屋が広い。” 体調の悪い中、どうしても仕事でNYに行くことになり、それでこのホテルを選びました。3泊しました。securityはとても厳しく、安全でした。何と言っても部屋が広い。確かに値段も高いですが、部屋の広さは充分で、しかもお風呂がとても綺麗で大きく、連日の雨で冷え込んだ体をあたためるには最適でした。 locationは地下鉄の駅がすぐなので便利。でも環境が良いかと言われればまぁまぁでした。とにかくホテルの外は騒がしいです。あと5番街にもあるいて行けますが、寒い中歩くのは大変かなというくらいの距離です。 冷蔵庫はないので、持ってきてもらいました。あと日本からくる人は必ず、歯ブラシとスリッパが必要です。これはついてないことが当たり前だと思った方がいいと思います。 ロビーも比較的ひろいですし、スタッフの人もとても親切です。 いたってシンプルですが、お金に余裕がある時に行きたいです。 ちなみに隣接されているレストランのステーキは絶品です。

“Attracts voyeurism” This hotel attracts young, successful, creative types who appreciate the high end design and want to be located in the trendy meat packing district of NYC. There is superb bar on the 18th floor which offers stunning views of the city and a roof garden which is a must see. Each room, while compact boasts a minimalist feel with all white furniture. You may also be surprised to see a glassed walled shower in the middle of you room. What makes The Standard's rooms so exceptional are the floor to ceiling windows which offer guests an wonderful panoramic view of the NYC skyline. Be warned, these windows allow office workers in the adjacent building a great view into your room, so don't get carried away and forget the blinds.

“Excellent choice in the heart of downtown Seattle” The Hilton Seattle is located a block away from the Sheraton where all the action downtown begins - by action, I mean, shops and restaurants and everything else. This location puts its guests close enough to everything yet far enough from the hustle and bustle of a busy pedestrian area. Granted it is an older property, much older from the outside when compared to other hotels, such as the Sheraton but the rooms and the service provided is sufficient enough to make up for the age. Rooms have been renovated and while it is nothing too out of the ordinary, it is comfortable (albeit, the rooms, and especially the bathrooms are pretty small). Being another Hilton, one can come to expect reliability! The Downtown Airporter bus stops at this hotel (they only stop at a few select hotels) so that's another added bonus - there is no need to transfer to another bus to get to your hotel! All in all, a solid choice in Seattle.
