“Typical Renaissance - high quality and service” Stayed April 2nd and 3rd while in DC on vacation. This hotel is typical of Renaissance facilities - high quality, very nice rooms with comfortable beds, attentive service and a convenient location. Rooms are not unique, but very comfortable. We had a king bed desk and sitting area, nice bathroom. Great, spacious lobby as noted by others. Starbucks on site is a plus. Location would be excellent for Convention Center business or dealings with EPA, IRS, Dept of Justice. For tourists, the Mall is 6 blocks south, with Metro stops within 4 blocks of hotel. Chinatown is 2 blocks away, MCI Center is also close by. White House is about a 15 minute walk, Capitol and Lincoln Memorial would be closer to 25. Hotels in DC are expensive compared to much of the nation. Compared to other DC hotels, the Renaissance is a very good value. If you want a DC dining experience - go to Zed's in Georgetown for a great Ethiopian meal.

“In heart of Georgetown with renowned restaurant but pricey & cramped” While the staff went out of their way to accomodate an extra night stay on a very busy weekend, and the location could not be better, the hotel is small, with small rooms and is a little worn and could use a makeover. Of course, Citronelle, one of the best restaurants in town, is located within the hotel, which also makes it very convenient for dining and room service.Given the smallness of the rooms, the real estate is quite pricey. Being in Georgetown, it is also not the quietest place to sleep but that is the tradeoff.

“Should of Stayed at Westin Across the Street” The Westin offered me a suite across the street. I thought it would be best to try a new hotel. I booked a very expensive room at The US Grant during Thanksgiving with a friend. As an SPG Gold member, we received no upgrades, only late check out. This was a four night stay and our room was way too small for that period of time. The staff had an attitude. I was so mad I asked the GM to give me a scissors as I tried to cut up my Gold card. He stopped me and we sat down for a chat. I explained our room was too small for the visit and that an upgrade should have been given. I also explained that I did not like how they treated us seeing we were a younger clientele. We felt looked down upon. Whenever we go to hotels we are respectful and usually never make a mess. He gave me bonus points to make up for it. The tub was fantastic, but I still wonder what the suite at the Westin looked like.

“good service, good location, good value” I stayed here because it was convenient for an event i was attending. The room was small but clean and well equipped (flat screen tv, robes, magnifiying make up mirror, ipod dock).there was no coffee maker, but they do serve breakfast). Staff was helpful, friendly and i was delighted to have room available even though i arrived early (noon). Breakfast was fine-- juice, coffee, fruit, croissants/breads, yogurt, cereal. More robust choices (eggs, smoked salmon, etc.) for an extra charge and the dining room pleasant enough. The air conditioner was a window unit so it was a little noisy but as i always take ear plugs with me that was not a showstopper. All and all, great location (Babbo is across the street, subway and starbucks around the corner, and the Square of course and NYU) and reasonable prices for new york. internet pre-pay was particularly good deal, though not refundable.

“Great hotel - under renovation though” Palmer House Hilton is in a good part of downtown Chicago, within a block of the train and is a great old hotel. It is under construction, so the fitness center / spa is non-existent, but eventually should be a good addition. Price was good for a downtown hotel, but this can change day to day. I've stayed here several times and it's consistent. The Hhonors executive lounge is good.

“Renovated Ol' Granddaddy Hotel!” Excellent staff. Lightning fast valet service. Easy to get to the Medical Plaza. Ruth Chris Steakhouse IN the hotel. Clean comfortable room. Free wifi with HiltonHonors!

“This is the perfect modern hotel. Faultless!” I can't find fault with anything! Well done Andaz! I've stayed at the Andaz on Sunset Strip (LA) and had a great experience there. This is even better. The check-in was casual and fast with helpful, friendly staff. The building is a superb piece of modern design with high ceilings and a minimalist sensibility. All the usual Andaz touches were in place... free drinks in the lobby, a trendy and interesting bar, free mini-bar contents (not alcohol) and free wireless. My room was probably the best New York city room I've stayed in for anything close to this price (under $200). High ceilings, a huge amount of space for Manhattan, amazingly quiet, a great comfortable bed, ultra modern and flawlessly designed furnishings. The bathroom was superb with a powerful ceiling mounted shower head in its own "shower room". The lighting is particularly well thought out, offering atmosphere and style to the whole room. The best touch of all -- a button that electronically opens or closes the blinds - with the option of total blackout or a lighter curtain that lets in sunlight. I loved being on Wall Street and walking distance from subways and lots of history and great restaurants. The guest services agent was helpful and gave me advice on where to get lunch one afternoon. I had a tour of the spa and wish I'd had time to use it - the staff were friendly and I liked the services on offer. This really is a first rate hotel and I don't think you can find a better deal in Manhattan for the kind of rates I paid.

“Middling” I had just a so-so expereicne at this hotel. The room was okay and spacious by New York hotel room standards but the hallway was dimly lit and felt drab. The location – right in the middle of Times Square – was too overwhelming for me, but that's just personal preference. Some of the front desk staffers weren’t very friendly and actually kind of brusque. The lobby was also dimly lit and felt like a library (I like a more bustling kind of atmosphere). I’d opt for a better place next time.

“A Convenient Stay for the Price Paid” My wife and I just returned from a five night stay. The property is well located from a visitors perspective. Walking distance to the Space Needle & Chihuly Garden along with Pike Place etc. Several bus lines stop across the street from the hotel. A five minute walk to Central Link light rail that serves Sea-Tac Airport. As noted in other reviews, this is an older property. It appears to well maintained. The television in our room was hit and miss in terms of channel quality. The hotel claimed they have no control over it - blamed it on the cable company. The pool and whirlpool area are in the basement of the hotel and a little on the small side. The Concierge was helpful. The Business Center has two computer terminals and one printer. Wi-fi is not free - as stated in the previous review. A full american breakfast in Brasserie Margaux was included with our room rate. It was fine. Some days it appeared that the restaurant was short staffed and managers filled in as servers. Our room on the 14th floor had a great unobstructed view of the Space Needle. As noted in other reviews, there's a new building under construction across the street from the hotel. They start promptly at 7am. If you are sensitive to noise, you might want to request a room facing the opposite side of the construction. Nice quality bedding. Bathroom linens are on the this side. As the title of my review - the hotel was convenient for what we paid. For a future visit, I might consider another property.

“A Great Hotel!!” I just got back from a dental convention in Chicago and decided to stay at this Hilton Garden Inn. Let me start by saying this hotel is perfectly located in the heart of downtown, close to the red line train, shopping and numerous great places to eat. The check in was polite and fast. I got up to my room and was surprised how clean and modern the room was. Flat screen T.V. king size foam bed, comfortable enough for me but if you like a bed that is on the firm side you may not like this one. The room also had a fridge and microwave which was nice! The bathroom was spotless! There were two concerns though, one was the common halls had an echo and some guests don't seem to think of others at one o' clock in the morning yelling slamming doors etc. Second the AC/HEATING UNIT kept coming on for 10 or 15 seconds at a time all through the night! Annoying! And very loud! This was after I switched it off! After the first night I went down to the front desk to notify them of this problem and they sent somebody up to the room(I guess while I was out) to try to fix this, but the second and last night I stayed the same problem happened again. The front desk staff did ask me if the problem was fixed but after I said "No" she didn't seem to care to much. I would recommend this hotel if your a "deep sleeper."

“Great Location - Nice Hotel - Disorganized Front Desk” We stayed at this location for one night while visiting Austin. We wanted to be near the nightlife and entertainment so chose this location. . The location was easy to find and the hotel in a commercial area next to the convention center and a 5-10 minute walk to all the action of 4/5/6th street & Congress. You have the choice of valet or self parking. Self parking is in a connected garage with easy elevator access. ($18/day in and out) The only negative I have to say about this hotel is that their Hhonors check in is a joke, they do not follow the pre check in procedure, and they are very disorganized mismanaged and uninformed at the front desk. (At least the day we got there.) Asked for the manager to call us but we never received the courtesy call. There is a nicely decorated, large and inviting lobby with a large front desk and nicely appointed common area. There is free Wifi available in the lobby area. In room Wifi is for a fee. The hotel has a nicely appointed gym, for which I believe there is an additional charge. (It was comped for us as HHonors Diamond Members.) They also have a full service spa. There is nice outdoor pool, hot tub, and and sunning area on the 8th floor overlooking downtown. They have business center with several computers, but I believe there is an additional charge. There is also a UPS Store in the lobby, and annoyingly the hotel contracts them to receive any packages for which there is a $5 per package fee. The rooms are nicely decorated, relatively large and still seem new. The beds are typical Hilton (nice beds) and they have nice HD TV's and plenty of channels. The climate control works well and it seems the blower motor stays on for white noise while the climate control is still functioning. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space. There is a tub with shower...if that is important to you. We did not experience city noise inside the hotel, but we were on the 25th floor. (25th and 26th are the Executive Lounge levels) The room was quiet for the most part, though I could hear doors slamming in the morning from time to time. Even though they put us near the elevator and ice machine there was no noise associated with either as they were well divided from the room area. As for the executive lounge, (if you are on one of those floors) there was an evening reception with veggies, chips, and cheese. They always had bottled water, juice, soda, tea, coffee, etc available any time we went to the lounge. (I believe hours are 6a - 10p) In the late evening they have a small desert selection. The breakfast has nice pastries, cereal, drinks (as per above), hard boiled eggs, oatmeal, and whole fruit. There was always plenty of seating in the executive lounge. As a note they do charge for liquor.....and they do not offer free internet in the lounge, which I find odd, though the hostess did let us use her computer to do a hotel check in. The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We did not partake of any of the hotels dining venues.....too many good choices nearby to eat in a hotel. I would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if we wanted to stay in the area for a personal trip. Room rate seemed a bit high, but we were on a reward stay. Had we been on a paid stay we would have looked at either this Hilton or the Intercontinental, both very nice options and similar in their offerings and the prices seem to vary wildly from day to day. They were agreeable to late check out when we asked which was nice. Our room was non smoking, but they still offer smoking rooms, which I think is odd in a new hotel like this....

“Unmetered taxis still an issue-I got scammed” This is an old hotel that if it wants to really live up to the HIlton name, needs some major refreshing. My first thought upon arriving was that this was not going to be good, it just looked past its prime. It actually turned out much better than I thought. The room was big, which I liked, but I wouldn't have sat on the old worn out sofa if my life depended on it. It badly needs replacement, as does the carpeting. That being said, I liked having the kitchen and the bed was very comfortable, ceiling fan was a nice touch, big screen TVs in bedroom and living area a very nice touch, wireless connection worked great. The breakfast and happy hour food was very good, but they don't really have enough room for all the guests to eat. If I were a family, however, I'd make a beeline for this place, you could save a fortune in meals. The hotel is not near the Metro at all, it's quite a walk, so if walking is an issue, I wouldn't stay here. However, the retvitalized 14th street area right around the corner is fantastic, lots of great restaurants, stores, cafes, Whole Foods. I loved it and the ambiance. But like so many others, I got scammed with the cab deal. It only cost $16.75 to get to the hotel from Reagan National, and the cab I got at the hotel charged me $25.00. Shame on you Homewood Suites! I think of Hilton Hotels as being a step above. Not here.

“Stylish and fun” A chic, slightly hard-edged hotel in a quiet, revitalized area of offices and residences within walking distance of the harbor and downtown. Though relatively small, my room was well equipped, with a great bed, a wonderful shower, good electronics, and many stylish touches. The only downside was the lack of a comfortable reading chair. The "beach" bar, a lively outdoor sandy space with an open fire, is a hoot; but the "pool" is just for dipping, not for swimming. Room service breakfast was fast and accurate. Dinner in the hotel's restaurant was excellent -- creative food really well prepared and presented -- though some in my party thought there weren't enough choices. As in most W hotels, your fellow guests are a major part of the show. Beautiful, stylish young people alternating with aging People in Black working hard to be "with it." The noise level in the public rooms is high, but the bedrooms have perfect sound-proofing. Overall, I really enjoyed this place. Paid a lot for the experience, and loved almost every moment. But I would not recommend it to people who want traditional comforts. Go for the adventure!

“Great rooms, great location, great pool, great service” With our family, we had booked three double rooms in Jan 2009 and were fully satisfied with the Grand Hyatt. A highlight was the well-heated pool and the outdoor spa. Location: As others had said, excellent location, close to everything. Rooms: Spacious, beautifully furnished and decorated. Beautiful bathrooms with massage shower. Public areas: Everybody enjoyed the gas fireplace in the lobby after coming out of the freezing coldness outside. Breakfast: We had a rate with buffet breakfast included which was very good with a good selection of cooked items and cooked-to-order omelettes. Pool and gym: High-tech gym with Life Fitness machines, a large and well-heated indoor pool and a steaming outdoor pool which was especially enjoyable since it was freezing cold. Breathtaking views of the mountains from the spa. Service: Bellstaff and recipionists were extremely helpful and friendly. We did not eat in the hotel's restaurant but walked a few steps to the Ship Tavern in Brown's Palace Hotel and had a most enjoyable, reasonably priced dinner there.

“Convenient to Metro and DOT” I recently stayed at this hotel the night before a business meeting at the DOT, which is only 1 block away. I parked in the garage ($29.50 per night) but there is a Metro stop within a block of the hotel. This hotel is clean and well maintained. My room appeared new. The layout is a little odd as the bed faces the window. The TV is facing the couch but not the bed. I am not a fan of Courtyard beds....I don't find them comfortable and the bed at this hotel was no exception. Internet is complimentary. The hotel has a restaurant with a breakfast buffet, which is a little overpriced at $12.95. They also serve lunch and dinner. There are very few restaurant choices within walking distance; however, the accessibility of the Metro opens up many options. Overall, this is a nicer than average Courtyard that I would use again if I need to be in this area of DC.

“Great hotel!” My wife and I stayed at the Omni for a night when our building's central air conditioner was broken. Overall, we really liked this hotel. :) This hotel has a long list of pros: + WONDERFUL sound insulation from the street. There was no traffic, no concert sound, no sound at all coming from the outside. + The rooms are in good condition. Maybe a little dated, but spotless nonetheless. + The beds are comfy. + The restaurants are good (we've been there separate times). They are extremely popular during the week, but + Free juice | coffee in the morning, free paper, etc. Lots of attention to detail, high marks here. The only downside to our whole visit was really our mistake; we forgot to specify that we didn't want an adjoining room. As a result, and some inconsiderate loud teenagers yelled a long time and ordered room service. Our room smelled like burgers around 2am. =\ However, this wasn't the hotel's fault. Highly recommended!

“Great view and great locaton” I stayed here during a conference. My room was free as part of that. I liked the room for the most part, but wish it had had a bathtub. The view was wonderful. The bed had many pillows, which made it easier to sleep, but I found the clock radio to be too bright. I did like to fridge sans minibar. I was able to store some leftovers overnight as a result. The pool area construction was someone disruptive, but I knew about that beforehand, so it was no big deal.

“Good hotel, great location” Stayed here for 5 nights before joining a tour. Hotel was in a great location, easy walk to Times Square, subway and 5th Avenue. On a pretty quiet street. The room was good size for New York standard, Bathroom was big enough and was clean. Breakfast was good, cereal, pastries, pancakes, juice, toast, coffee & tea. Although the breakfast room was very small & often very crowded. Front desk were helpful and gave out maps of the area. Free internet was an added bonus. Overall enjoyed our stay and would return again.

“Impressive new ICH in San Francisco” We stayed at this property and booked the California Staycation package that they are offering to CA residents through the end of the year. The package includes free parking, a $20 gas card, and breakfast for 2 at their restaurant in addition to the room. We had booked a regular room but at check-in on a Friday night, were offered an upgrade to a club room for an additional $40. We decided to do the upgrade since we were feeling peckish and were pretty certain we could get our money's worth in free drinks and snacks at the lounge. As it turned out at checkout they did not have a gas card to give us, so they gave us the room upgrade for free instead -- OK by us. The hotel is very modern looking, quite striking really. The check in was pretty quick and efficient and we found our way to our room easily enough. We were on the 32nd floor, and found the floor-to-ceiling windows a great touch. The room however was a bit on the small side, and the bath was one of the smallest we've had at an ICH property that we've ever stayed at. Still, it was very clean and comfortable with great bedding (as usual). The lounge is the smallest we've experienced, too, at any ICH property, although there is a big outdoor area so when it's not cold or raining one could escape the slight clausterphobia of the indoors by sitting out on the patio. Being on a higher floor ended up being slightly annoying, at least when it came to the elevators. Even though there are 4 of them, it seemed that whichever elevator came up to get us would also be the one to stop on each floor going down along the way. We learned to not take the first elevator that would come up, so that we could avoid stopping literally 5-10 times on our way down to the lounge or the lobby. It's a very nice property, despite previous posters if you know SF it's a good location. It was a particularly great deal getting the Staycation package, since $50/night parking is ridiculous (though tip for anyone who doesn't know: there is a parking garage charging far less right around the corner on Mission). We'd definitely stay here again.

“Eine grand Dame in Sachen Hotels” Sehr zentral gelegenes und exclusives Hotel, zuvorkommender Service und schöne grosse Zimmer. Als HHonors Gold Mitglied bekommt man weder Upgrade noch Loungezugang, aber das reguläre Frühstück ist inklusive und das kann sich sehen lassen, erst recht für amerikanische Verhältnisse. Internet funktionierte im Zimmer nur per Kabel, das Fitnessstudio ist rund um die Uhr offen, aber ganz seltsam in 3 verschieden Räume aufgeteilt.

“The Service Made the Difference” We just returned from a 4 night stay at the Public. We'd booked with an excellent rate from Hotels.com for a 2 night weekend visit. Due to Hurricane Sandy, we needed to add two additional nights. The staff was exceedingly helpful, understanding, and accommodating in working out our extended stay at an appropriate rate. With the uncertainty and stress of the situation, we were most appreciative of their readiness to assist in any way possible. The Pump Room is superb and priced accordingly. If too pricey for some, there are numerous alternative dining and breakfast options within a couple blocks of the Public. The location, in a lovely neighborhood just a few blocks from lots of city life activities, offers a nice respite from the busier areas. We had no problems at all with elevators, noise, toiletries, etc. Loved the spacious walk-in closet and the modern furnishings and details.

“Standard Homewood, excellent service !!” The Homewood Suites experience is pretty standard nationwide and obviously the look and feel of the hotels are likewise. While I have ever to have a bad experience with this chain, from my experiences so far, the staff at this location was exceptional. There was not a single time that I ran across an employee in this property that I was not greeted and asked if they could be of help. Housekeeping was helpful and very attentive as was the front desk staff and the morning breakfast staff. Kudos to all.

“Happily Surprised!” We stayed here around New Year's and I was very pleasantly surprised with the quality of the room. It was beautiful with a great view - far from Hampton Inns I've seen elsewhere. We even enjoyed free breakfast. (It was nothing spectacular but nice to get some food in us before sight-seeing.) If you want that times square location and a great NYC value... I would highly recommend this.

“Perfect base for exploring downtown Denver” My fiance and I stayed here for one night at the beginning of our trip to Boulder and RMNP. The hotel is in a good location for exploring the 16th Mall and nearby attractions. It's a historic property so the lobby and rooms reflect the period in which the hotel was built. It has a nice ambiance without feeling stuffy or outdated. Upon check-in we were given complimentary bottles of water, which we gulped down since it was about 100 degrees in Denver that day. They also offer complimentary tea, coffee and apples. Our room was quite large and very clean. The shower was a bit small, but totally manageable. We did use the gym. It's in the basement so there aren't any windows, but the equipment is fairly new and well maintained. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would definitely recommend it.

“Nice and roomy, great location” Stayed here from June 4th to the 7th on a business trip. We checked in around 12-1 in the afternoon and had no problems. I was actually expecting something much smaller, as it is New York and space is hard to come by here, but I found the room to be very spacious. Much bigger than the trendy boutique hotel I last stayed in. The room was clean, there is a small refrigerator and microwave, and free internet (don't know if this came with business traveler reservation or if it is standard). The wireless internet was a bit up and down, but I guess that's what you get for free wireless. You can also plug in directly. The first night, like someone mentioned below, I thought the room didn't have a blackout curtain. However, as I discovered, behind the sheer curtain, there is actually a thicker blackout curtain which I made use of the second night. The location is great.. The hotel is very close to a lot of places and restaurants as well as the subway stop. If you want to go down to union square, there is a station only a block away. I would avoid the retaurants in Times Square as they'll cost an arm and a leg and the food is just ok. Lots of Starbucks nearby if you need a coffee fix. I tried to make do with the hotel coffee, but it really wasn't very good. There's also a grocery store on the next block (Food Emporium) if you're there for an extended stay and want to stock the fridge with water and snacks. All in all, can't really complain. Staff was friendly and helpful, room was spacious and clean. It seemed pricey, but it is New York., and you could easily get half the space for a higher price in another hotel. (A friend in NY at the same time on business stayed at the Hudson Hotel, which cost more, and the room only had enough space for the bed)

“One of the best Courtyards for customer service” I had business for three weeks in Malvern PA, so I would leave Malvern on Friday afternoon, turn in my car and catch the shuttle to this Courtyard. Yes, there is a Marriott right at the airport, but this Courtyard is quieter than the airport hotel. Before I even arrived I received an E-mail from the manager of the hotel and since I had a question about shuttle bus from the airport I asked..not really expecting any response because you seldom get one, and within a couple hours the managers E-mail told me to contact them as soon as I got to the airport and the shuttle would come right over. The second week the front desk staff greeted me by name, even though I had not identified myself when I requested the shuttle, same for the third week. All the staff were friendly, even at 4:00am in the morning when I had to catch the bus to catch my flight. The Bistro was a nice place to get dinner for the evening, nothing extravagant, but better than going out. The only two issues I have with the site is no wifi in the rooms, but I carry a cable and had no problems with it, and also in the Bistros booths not all the channels worked on the TVs, but since I was not there to watch TV this didn't bother me. I have many more weeks like this coming up and my plans already include a Friday night stay at this Courtyard.

“Beautiful hotel, some detractions for me” I stayed at the US Grant for two night recently on a business trip. This is really a beautiful hotel, extremely tastefully decorated and centrally located. It was explained to me that none of the rooms really have good views, and I was given a room that overlooked the roof. So I had no view, but also no street noise, which was good. The bed was super comfortable as well. Two things bothered me though about my stay; one was the extremely loud air conditioner which would kick on and off constantly throughout the night. It was so loud when it would come on that I needed to use earplugs on my second night so that I could sleep (I got very little sleep the first night)! Secondly, the faucet design in the bathroom sink was such that it would splash everywhere when I used it. The entire sink area was constantly wet. Because of these two nuisances I probably wouldn't stay here again - but it was a beautiful hotel.

“Great, traditional hotel in excellent location” We booked into the hotel for 2 nights as the base for some sightseeing in Dallas. The hotel is beautiful, and has a real traditional feel to it. The staff were very friendly and courteous, and we were given (as requested) a high room with good views of the Dallas skyline. The room was a great size, with a large bathroom and good closet with ironing board. It was clean and the bed was fairly comfortable. The hotel has a great bar, although it is fairly small so get there early if you’d like to get a seat. When we were there, there was two weddings going on at the same time, and that meant a lot of people spilling into the hotel bars once the weddings finished at midnight. The hotel is in a great location for exploring Dallas, and the JFK museum and Dealy Plaza are within walking distance, as are a section of shops and restaurants. If you have time when you’re in Dallas, we’d recommend eating in Wolfgang Pucks restaurant at the top of Reunion Tower; the food and the views are amazing.

“Location Saves The Day” The location of this hotel right smack in Times Square can make you forget a few of the realities - pricey for tired-looking rooms and average house keeping. They do well because of their location but must become more aware of the importance of quality and service.

“Nice Hotel” Nice hotel - clean, comfy beds, little old (popcorn ceilings, etc) but overall good stay. People very friendly. We ate breakfast in the restaraunt and it was very nice. Nice that you don't have to pay for parking! I don't have anything else to say but it says I have to have 200 words so bubble gum, bubble gum, bubble gum, bubble gum

“A pleasant surprise” Visiting our college age daughter in Boston for the weekend is always expensive. Let's face it -- hotels in Boston are expensive. Since we drive to Beantown, this hotel was a fine choice for us. Easy to park and its free. Rooms are smallish but very attractive and well appointed. Overall, a very good value.

“Worth the convenience” We had an early morning flight and decided to stay at the hotel with a direct tram into the airport. The room (in the south tower) was typical ~ nice. Room service was fast, good and with huge portions. Getting into the airport couldn't have been easier. Take the hotel lobby elevator down to tram level, the tram is then just a few steps away! My absolute favorite part was the parking. We left our car there for 5 days and they had an extended stay rate ($16/day, I think). Airplane landed; we picked up our baggage from baggage claim; we took the airport elevator down to the tram level; tram off at the hotel stop; up the hotel elevator to the lobby and within a literal, total 10 minutes we were on our way home!

“Very nice hotel in great location” This is a newer hotel, and it is very clean. Its location can't be beat: a couple of blocks west of the John Hancock building. I stayed in a "city view suite." My view wasn't as impressive as I would have liked, but it was still pretty decent. The room was very large, including the largest bathroom I've ever had in a hotel room. The toiletries included a nice brand of soaps/lotions and a body scrubber. The bed was fairly comfortable. The only odd thing was that there were no blankets; the bed contained a sheet over the mattress and a comforter. I thought that was odd, but it wasn't a problem. I ordered breakfast via the room service menu, and it was enjoyable. Even though the hotel is 30 plus stories tall, there are several elevators, and I never had to wait more than 30 seconds for one. You won't go wrong with this hotel.

“Sans attitude” We enjoyed our recent stay at the Taj - Campton Place. Like many top-tier establishments, they have a beautiful facility, but they actually go a bit further. For example, there are packets of almonds and fresh apples in the gym, multiple newspapers available for guests and a very helpful staff who know their stuff, including where I could get a necklace clasp repaired locally. Even better was their professional nature, but without the attitude that one sees far too often. We stayed in a deluxe room which was small but certainly sufficient for two people and has the usual lovely linens and bath products. The restaurant/bar are very expensive and given the plethora of outstanding restaurants in SF would encourage a look elsewhere. Breakfast, while expensive, is lovely and the coffee and jams are downright amazing. There are multiple parking garages on Sutter which offer far better rates in this tight economy. I know hotels are reevaluating the expense of fresh flowers, but the flowering quince branches in the lobby were lovely and I would hate to see this luxury lost. Overall, location and customer service are Camptons strong suits, but one must be prepared to pay dearly for these privileges.

“Another renovated hotel with very air conditioning.” This is a lovely well located hotel with really nice staff and a free Lexus to run you around.However, we were put in a courtyard facing room which picked up a jet engine style air conditioning exhaust system outside. For the first time in 35 years of travelling I asked to move at 1.30 in the morning. I have had a run of decent hotels, either brand new or those operating in renovated altered buildings in recent months where the air conditioning has been loud and not "tuned" properly.At the end of the day a hotel has to provide a good bed and a quite environment or else it fails.

“Great Hotel in Great Location” Went to Boston with Wife, daughter and dog to look at colleges. This is a pet friendly hotel. The Eliot is on the corner of Commonwealth and Massachusetts Avenues. If you like shopping, half a block away is Newbury Street. We stayed on the forth floor in a suite-no road noise and had two restful nights of sleep. The fitness center is a sports club on Newbury Street (1 min. from Hotel) and free of charge with pass from front desk. If your lucky, you may find street parking but recommend the valet parking. This in an upscale property that is very well done. The hotel staff was very professional and attentive. I have no complaints and when we return to Boston we will stay at the Eliot.

“Rates 4 stars in comfort and amenities.” Comfortable and roomy with a great bath and shower. Excellent bedding. A parking fee is charged and hotel must park the car and keep keep the keys due to limited space. In all a very enjoyable stay.

“Enjoyable weekend celebration” This is a busy hotel. Constant activity. We were there during a city festival weekend. The hotel was booked full and most of the crowd was younger. There was quite a bit of "rules" placed on the hotel guests. There was crowd control by the hotel. The elevators had a line with the queue ribbons and crowd control in place. The guests we found to be patiently willing to wait through all of this. The crowded festival must have pre empted this mentality. We were on the 17th floor but found that the steps were a better choice than waiting to one of the six elevators to go down in the mornings. It would have assisted us best to have the floor clearly marked when you got to the lower floors. There seemed to have several sub floors and we past the lobby floor on several occasions as did the many of us who choose this means of travel through the hotel. I would recommend to post in the stairwells which floor is represented by level.

“Too bad the rates aren't as cheap as the decor” This was my first stay at Room Mate Grace and I doubt I will stay again. The room I had was an upgrade which would make wonder what kind of room I would have been given. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was large, those were the best features. The remote control didn't work, neither did the high speed internet. Some lightbulbs were just exposed, not the classiest look and the furnishings were very cheap in design. It was also a challenge to open and close the curtains, you have to climb up on the bed to do this, also to turn on one of the lights. The room and the hallway were poorly lit. The decor in my room and the hall were not my taste, like something out of a 70's mod themed movie. That alone would not bother me except for the other issues. Also, the bathroom lighting was so poor it was hard to apply make-up even with the cheaply designed make-up mirror. On a positive note the staff was friendly and helpful, the pool is a fun place and the complimentary breakfast was good. It was overall a clean hotel ,but kind of dismal and the "mood lighting" throughout the hotel made it seem like evening all day.

“Less than average” Stayed 5 nights in this hotel while in Philly for a work meeting ... I wished I had stayed somewhere else. The room was fine, very basic, but the walls are paper thin (the guy in the room next to me was having a conference call for his work and i heard the entire conversation). I actually liked the location ... in Center City, but not right in the middle of everything and a subway station entrance right beneath the hotel was super convenient. However, when it comes to customer service, this has to be one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in. On 3 different occasions when I went to front desk to ask a question the response I got each time was a tilt of the head and a shoulder shrug. Even if the person at the front desk staff didn't know the answer to my question, she didn't even bother to help me or offer to refer me to someone else who could help me. And 2 of them were simply rude. Then in the restaurant not only was the service horrible, but the food was incredibly bland and not worth the prices they charge. I would definitely not stay at this hotel again the next time I'm in Philly. For a comparable price, I know I can find a much better place to stay.

“Trying for trendy - the Palomar 2 blocks away is better” This hotel is right next to SMU - great if you want to be right next to SMU. It's 3 blocks from the interstate so easy access. The entrance is strange and hard to find. The place looks like an old apartment or other type residence building. The staff are great. The bartender is superb. The rooms are uncomfortable. Too much stuff in them and the space is too tight - doors bang into things when you open them etc. Breakfast is a disaster - do yourself a favor and skip it. The menu is limited - the food is below average - the service is terrible. Unless you have an hour to kill so eating microwave food seems like a good idea you'll want to eat elsewhere. I've stayed at the Palomar 3 blocks away and it is far better.

“Great value, location, stayed here several times” Set your expectations for a B&B not a chain hotel, and then you'll see what a find this is. Convenient neighborhood for dining shopping and strolling. Hotel staff is a little amateurish but well intentioned. Renovations look almost complete. Good restaurant adjacent to the hotel.

“Great place, great location” This hotel was built in the summer of 2008. Rooms were spacious and clean. The staff was very helpful and pleasant to chat with. The property is located about 10 minutes from the airport and about 20-25 minutes from downtown if there is no traffic. There are several restaraunts within walking distance including Ted's Montana Grill, Outback, Uno, Applebees and a few more. I will definitely stay here again.

“Nice Lobby, Friendly Staff, But Otherwise Mediocre Hotel” Not sure what it is about Ritz Carlton's- they seek to compete in the same market segment as Four Seasons and Park Hyatts, but, on avergae, they're never quite to the standards of those hotels. The Dallas Ritz Carlton is Exhibit A. Impressive lobby when you walk in-beautiful flower arrangements steal the show, with what it is (allegedly) one of Dallas' trendiest bars to the left. The staff is exceeding friendly, but in that superficial obsequious tradition typical of middle America that becomes grating within 2 minutes. The room, however, left something to be desired. The design was the aspiring mcmansion look from that old TV show Designing Women that American suburbanites aspire to. The Wallpaper was something from another era. The toilet flush has to be held down for some time in order for the toilet to actually flush. The handset of cordless phone on the desk didn't work when the phone rang, and by the time I fiddled with it and then rushed to the bedside phone, the call was missed. The wireless internet was maddeningly weak (come on people- this is the 21st century!). At night there were noises of unknown mechanical origin rattling in the background from time-to-time. On the plus side, in the morning they delivered a Financial Times without me requesting it upon check-in - high marks, at least, for an actually readable newspaper. Memo to management: you have work to do.

“Not bad for a conference hotel” The location was pretty great--can't beat walking out onto the Riverwalk, but being far enough off the main drag to miss the bar crawlers. I hear the hotel was booked solid while we were there for a conference, and the service was slow and overtaxed. There were several account mistakes, and there was always a line to speak to concierge or the front desk.

“Beautiful Hotel - 90% Excellent, 10% Ok” I arrived at this hotel on June 19, 2010, staying one evening. I am a Silver Hilton Honors member and impressed by this beautiful hotel. I arrived early and was able to get to my room around 11:00 a.m. Tom, who was the front desk professional, helped me in this regard. Tom was also helpful in acknowledging my birthday that same day and gave me waters and cookies. He also helped coordinate a shuttle ride, I needed. My room was #506 and was clean and bright and overlooked the pool. I used the business center on two occasions and found it quiet and helpful. The pool area is very beautiful and relaxing too. This particular weekend was super busy because of the San Diego Fair. I was told that the shuttle driver was taking me directly to the Fairgrounds. Halfway through the ride, the driver, whose name I did not get, but he was a young man about 26, he informed me that he could not take me all the way to the Fairgrounds that he was dropping me off at a bus stop at the Horse Grounds and I would be driven by another bus to the Fair. That he had to get back to the hotel to drive other guests. It is a shame he couldn't have told me ahead of time. I was stressed out because he was truthful from the beginning. Otherwise I would have taken a cab. I am from Florida and am not familiar with this area. I ate breakfast the next morning in the restaurant. I had the buffet and it was okay, not great. Cynamon was very professional. Upon check out, Ramez was the front desk professional and helped me to my destination of Camino Road by driving the shuttle there. So kudos to Tom, Cynamon and Ramez for helping me in their fair city.

“Convenient & a little Charming” Spent six nights in a single room, and feel as though I got what I paid for. While it wasn't the smallest room (with bathroom) I've ever stayed in, it would be in the top three for sure. Definitely not much space to stretch out or store stuff, but if you travel light it shouldn't be a problem. Those expecting Holiday Inn-sized rooms need not apply here. Being on the first floor I was uneasy about the window without bars that looked onto the adjacent alley, but that was no issue. My noise concerns were also unfounded, even with the nearby theatres. While the room & rest of the hotel could have used a bit of sprucing up here & there, it was clean enough for me. Location was convenient...about a five minute walk to the Orange Line & a bit under ten to the nearest Green Line stop. Plus being two blocks south of the Common means that the harbour, Back Bay, South End, Downtown, Freedom Trail, etc. are already within walking distance. Made my reservations via booking.com which seemed to come up with the cheapest price. As others have mentioned, there is something charming about small, older hotels that make it easier to overlook the minor rough spots. Set your expectations accordingly and you'll be happy with the Milner.

“The Belvedere Hotel NY - Ottima scelta!” Hotel in ottima posizione per visitare NY, raggiungibili a piedi sia Times Square che Central Park. Vicino alle stazioni delle linee 1, C ed E. Nelle immediate vicinanze ci sono Starbucks, minimarket, ristoranti e negozi di souvenir e tantissimi teatri. La nostra stanza era una deluxe con 2 letti queen, decisamente molto grande per gli standard newyorkesi. Bagno un po’ vecchiotto ma pulito e con tutto il necessario. Cabina armadio spaziosa con all’interno la cassetta di sicurezza. Avevamo anche un piccolo cucinotto con lavello, microonde, frigorifero e macchina per il caffè (comodissimo per la colazione!). Ottima la vista (11° piano) su Time Warner Center e Hearst Tower. Servizi: concierge per info turistiche e ogni tipo di prenotazione (musei, sport, visite guidate...ecc...); un piccolo negozio di souvenir, cold drinks e snack, fitness center (non usato da noi) e business room con internet gratis solo per le conferme dei voli, navigazione a pagamento a 3$ per 15 minuti pagabili cash o carta di credito. Ascensori: i principali sono 2 e c’è sempre abbastanza attesa...ce ne sono altri due sempre disponibili agli estremi di sinistra e destra di ogni piano (loro dicono che sono quelli di servizio ma li possono usare anche gli ospiti). Alla reception sono collaborativi e cortesi, abbiamo segnalato che il lavandino del bagno non scaricava bene l’acqua e al nostro ritorno era già tutto risolto. In definitiva hotel sicuramente valido e consigliato.

“Nice even with significant construction going on” This is a very nice HGI with a great modern decor. The rooms are exactly what you expect to find at an HGI. The on-site bar and restaurant are nicer than what you usually find at an HGI. The staff are friendly and attentive. There are also a few restaurants adjacent to the hotel. Good location in the Cherry Creek area of Denver.

“Great new hotel” Hotel is brand new, so everything is in great shape. The room was very clean, nice, and new. The size of the room was not that big, but it was not unusually small. Based on previous reviews, I thought my room would be the size of a closet, but it was not bad. The TV did not have the annoying pitch to buy TV movies that is common in most hotels. The high-speed Internet connection is free and easy-to-use, and they even provided a cable that reached to the bed. I stayed in Room 801, which is configured for a handicapped person. The only possible negative is that the shower, which makes up the rightmost one-third of of the voluminous bathroom, is basically a showerhead and a shower curtain. This means that it can get water on the floor rather easily, as a bit leaks from under the curtain. The staff was very friendly, and they gave me directions to several places. The room was extremely cold when I arrived, so I suggest that you call from the airport and tell them to turn on the heat before you arrive, if it is the wintertime. The restaurant is supposed to open in a month or so.

“Great location, pleasant stay” I was a little bit leery about booking this hotel due to noise and bathroom size issues mentioned in other reviews but I am so glad I did.. The studio with 2 double beds was huge, the bathroom with tub shower a good size, and the kitchenette so useful! Every staff member we encountered was helpful and friendly and our request for a higher floor was no problem. Yes, we did hear sirens but it reminded us we were in the Big Apple, and it did not affect our sleep at all. If you are using intercity transportation, the location is perfect. Megabus and Boltbus stops are a couple of blocks away, and Penn Station is across the street for train travel or easy transport to JFK via LIRR/Airtrain. Proximity to shopping, good restaurants, subway, sights, is great especially when it is so chilly outside. Minus 1 star for not having free WiFi but we can't complain too much because the room rate was very reasonable. Also, you are able to print out your boarding passes in the lobby at no charge. We would not hesitate to stay here again. Such a convenient location, nice, large room and good value made for a pleasant stay.

“Very comfortable with central location” My wife and I stayed two nights (one week apart) at this hotel in early July 2012. The rooms were pleasingly appointed (see photo) and the bed/pillow was as comfortable as any I've slept on. The hotel is at a downtown corner, so I heard noises from vehicles as early as 6 am, but there are thick curtains to block the light. The A/C was quiet but effective. The elevators were responsive and the staff were eager to help with directions and suggestions. We found it a short walk to the pier area (coming back up the hill was our exercise for the day) and to the monorail. If you hail a cab be sure to only get in from the curb side as it is dangerous to try to get in from the street side. We noticed a sign that the hotel was being purchased by someone else? Don't know if that will change anything.

“klasse Basis für einen Stadttrip durch Chicago” Das Hyatt liegt direkt am Fluss mit Blick auf Lake Michigan und den nördlichen Stadtteil. Am Besten nach den renovierten Zimmern mit "Lake-" oder "River View" fragen. Die Dimension des Hotels ist immens, aber wer damit leben kann, ist sehr gut aufgehoben. Von den Sevice- Einrichtungen haben wir nur das Restaurant genutzt, dass Essen war ausgezeichnet und das Ambiente mega- es gab sogar live Piano- Unterhaltung. Wir hatten über Priceline gebucht und dadurch war das Preis-/ Leistungsverzeichnis mehr als ausgezeichnet und wir wurden deswegen trotzdem nicht anders behandelt als die anderen Gästen. Wir würden. Insgesamt klasse Hotel und dazu super Lage, auch um während einem Städtetrip dazwischen auch mal gemütlich zu entspannen.

“Good As Always” After reading some of the really nasty comments on TripAdvior, I was a little hesitant about bringing my family back to the Queen Anne, but I couldn't have been more pleased. We've stayed several times in the past ten years and this visit was no different from the others. A clean room with a kitchen and tons of storage space is so welcome when traveling with kids and doing back to school shopping. Yes, the beds are old and the pillows could be newer, but there are plenty of them and more if you ask the desk. I love the old fashioned bathrooms with comfy little tubs, the great toiletries, the beautiful courtyard, and the location, location, location just steps away from shops, restaurants, buses (we took the 18 all the way to Safeco Field and it stops near the hotel coming and going) and the post office. We fill up the 'fridge, breakfast in the room and hit the shops and sights by 10am, returning late in the day to watch a little TV before dinner or change to play in the Seattle Center fountain.The big closets are great for drying clothes and storing new purchases, but there is also a spotless laundry on site which we always make use of. Yes, this is budget lodging, but there is absolutely nothing wrong with it for its price point and lots of things right.

“It doesn't get any closer to BWI than this.” You are right at the airport, and they have a shuttle that will pick you up at the terminal and drop you off there, as well. Because you're so close, you do get the noise of the planes, so light sleepers should consider that. Not a problem for me. I ate dinner on site when I arrived, and it was excellent. Had a nice spinach salad and two amazing crab cakes. I also ate breakfast there the next morning. They had a buffet for $13, and it was average. From check in to the restaurant to the guy who drives the shuttle, the staff are all courteous, friendly, and welcoming. My room was on the small side, but nicely appointed. Flat screen TV, king sized bed, and a desk to work at. The Wi-Fi was excellent. I've flown through BWI dozens and dozens of times over the years, and never stayed here before. It will be one of my top options from now on.

“Good Value Close to the Airport” I spent a night at this Fairfield, which is conveniently located near the airport. Check in went quickly and the front desk personal was very pleasant. I was upgraded to one of the suites that were available. The room and bathroom were very clean. The suite included a lounge area with a refrigerator, couch and TV while the sleeping area had a very comfortable bed and another TV. The bathroom had the normal amenities of soap and shampoo along with a coffee maker with 2 packets of regular and decaf coffee. Breakfast was included with the rate, which included bagels, fresh fruit, yogurt, muffins, coffee and juices. I would stay here again if in the area.

“Great Hotel in best location” We are a family of 4 and stayed here early June 2011. Upon checking in, the desk staff were extremely helpful and whilst we had booked a standard Double-Double room, the staff helped advise us on an upgarde and then worked out that it was cheaper to Join the Ambassador Club (as we were staying 5 nights), after which we got a free upgrade, free in room internet, a free movie and free use of the fitness club, so for us, we thought this extremely good value. You could not beat the location, being right next door to the Tribune building and opposite Nordstroms on the Magnificant mile. From here, we could walk to the shops, downtown, millenium park, navy pier, restaurants, beachses and just aabout everything. We stayed in teh historic tower, as whilst we could have got a better view in the new tower, we were advised that the rooms were much bigger in the historic tower and they were. We had 2 doubles and a rollaway bed and still had plenty of space to open out suitcases and walk around...the room was huge. We didn't try any of the dining options, as the Michael Jordan steakhouse was still under cosntruction and whilst I liked the look of Eno, it probably wasn't the place to take young teenage daughters, as it is the more adult, winebar type place, that appealed to me and the win list looked great. We hate Starbucks coffee(as most Aussies do), so we disn't use the starbucks eaither, but found a great cafe (Baci) atound the corner in east Ohio st that made Lavazza Espresso, which is where we had outr breakfasts. The concierge recommended a great Breakfast place (Yolk) within walking distance towads Navy pier. We also ate out at other concoierge recommendations, such a sa great d=restauarant next door and portllos and Unos, both Chicago institusions, and only a couple of blocks away. Parking was very pricey and we used a salf park station behind the hotel for overnight parking at $25 rather than the $55 the Hotel charges, but teh hotel allowed multiple re-entry valet parking. As we only had a car for 1 night, this was fine. Close to public transport, with busses both north (to the zoo, Lincoln Park, beaches) and south (downtown, the museum campus, Hyde Park (miuseum of science & industry/University/Obama's house) outside the front door. The 12th floor art deco former olympic athlete pool form the 20s was fabulous and in keeping with the whole art deco Chicago theme. The gym, whilst smallish, was reasonably well wquipped, but a bit clasustrophopic with no windows, and having cardio equipment on carpetted floor isn't probably the best idea when people sweat on it. Overall, we loved the place and would definately stay there again and recommend it highly.

“Just stay here - it's great!” Love the Magnolia. Stayed first in Houston and loved it so Dallas was next and they did not let us down. Friendly staff. Got in on the suite package and felt like I was in an apartment it was so big and nice. Cookies were great although I may have taken too many - sorry :) Location is really good for all things downtown Dallas and I like that they are practically attached to the Iron Cactus - a must for margarita fans. This hotel really cares about its guests and I will try to ALWAYS stay here when in Dallas and pretty much anywhere else they have a hotel.

“great hotel and great location” i had a lovely room in the old tower. good internet connection and eveything was very nice. great 24 hour gym and a fabulous lap pool. too bad i did not bring my swim suit. great location. walk everywhere. nice staff. room was nice sized and bed very comforable. .

“Great Nob Hill Views of the Bay” Tthe Stanford Court provided me with a very pleasant stay and introduction to Nob Hill. If you get a bay view room on a high floor, you'll be treated to a visual panorama of boats on the bay, as well as the cityscape of the nearby skyscrapers. Not all the rooms appear to have such views, however. The bathroom was a long galley-like structure with sliding doors between vanities and closet space outside the main bath. The desk and bell staff were pleasant and efficient, and a housekeeper brought three toothbrushes to my door from which to choose my favorite color when I inquired about their availability. The parking is always pricey in San Francisco, but the valet service offered at the Stanford Court is courteous and efficient. Nob Hill is a good hike up from Union Square to keep fit, and ladies who favor stilettos such as myself need to pack a pair of block heels or flats to negotiate the uneven streets and pavement. Walking downhill in heels is not for the faint of heart! The fitness center is small without much of a view, so bring music. There wasn't much to offer for a quick breakfast to go beyond coffee and pastries, so be sure to try Sears, a century-long brunch institution with lots of history, just down the hill. Another favorite is the Cheesecake Factory in the Macy's building. Alcatraz, preferably at night when you can tour the Birdman's Cell by flashlight, is a very interesting tour. Check out theater options before your stay as well.

“Great Stay at this new Spring Hill Suites” Brought my niece and her two young children to Indy to see the Zoo & Children's Museum. This was a great location for the Zoo and a short walk to the Monument Circle. Everyone was very impressed with Indy and with this hotel. The layout of the room worked out great for us--Everyone seemed to have a "private" place to change, etc. The kids spent a lot of time in the pool and it looked very cleam. Breakfast in the morning was very abundant. I appreciate the key-operated elevator and didn't find it difficult to use at all. In fact, the kids enjoyed activating it with the key. The hotel is located a little off the beaten path, but Indy's downtown is so vibrant, that we felt comfortable walking several blocks at night, as well as walking the canal. We used valet parking and found it quite convenient. We'll stay re again.

“Wonderful hotel, great location, sweet people” Wonderful time here in a great location. The price was right, the location was right, the lobby was lovely, the easy early check-in was right, the bed was great, the pillow menu is FAB. The bathroom was tiny and the room service only so-so so I can't give it five stars, but it's a great hotel and we'll definitely go back any time we're doing business in that part of town. Thank you, Affinia staff; you made our stay great!

“Not as Bad as Some Reviews - Quite Good” Stayed at the MO in DC overnight midweek. The bell staff were incredibly gracious, after chatting on the way to our room our bellman called the front desk and asked for a better room. A better room was provided promptly. The bellman did this on his own accord after we mentioned which other MO's we have visited. The front desk staff were also gracious and provided hot towels at check in. Concierge was helpful too. The room itself was nice with a great bathroom with separate tub and a large shower. The bed was very comfortable, the internet was fine (unlike other reviews say) though its cost $15/day, the decor was simple but elegant. The bath products were good. We had drinks in the Empress/lobby lounge. The drinks were good, as was some food we had but the service was sluggish. The staff here seem annoyed at the world. We missed breakfast but had a quick bite at a sandwich place next door. Some downsides... 1. The location is far removed from most things. This would be an issue for tourists or those inclined to walk or take the metro. 2. There is noise from the trains and from jets going into Reagan National airport. 3. Price are high for everything and room prices are high for the inconvenient location and noise issue. We booked a special rate from as an American Bar member at $295 midweek. That said for the quality of stay we had I can overlook the downsides. Of course, at published rates of $565+ I would be upset as there are better choices for those prices.

“Not Walker-Friendly” The beautiful lobby and great service is somewhat offset by the small, older rooms. The location is at the top of Nob Hill, which means it's just two (VERY steep) blocks from Chinatown, and two of the main trolly lines pass just outside. There's not much within walking distance because of the steep hills, and the on-site restaurant prices are very high ($30 pp for breakfast). I would have been very pleased to get this on a Priceline stay, but at regular prices I'll be happier next time somewhere more walker-friendly.

“Première expérience dans un SOFITEL : excellente !” Séjour de 4 nuits en mini suite. Première expérience de ma vie dans un SOFITEL et vraiment pas déçu, loin de là ! De l'accueil au jour du départ. Je ne sais pas pour les chambres mais les suites sont très confortables et spacieuses. Le personnel est vraiment très agréable et très prévenant. Le restaurant est de très bonne qualité. Pour les petits-dej je pensais que çà serait plus cher; le "Continental" est à 20$ pour une boisson chaude, un jus de fruit à volonté, un basket de pains et viennoiserie par personne, beurre et confiture. Rien à dire. Et surtout, un emplacement de folie, prêt de la White House ! J'adorerais y retourner.

“Very good!” Check-in: Well started off with a little hitch. They have those throw down type rugs by entrance so when I walked into the lobby I tripped on it. Caught myself so alls well. Mentioned it at check-in and the clerk was apologetic. Just need to do something to make sure it stays completely flat. I wasn't looking for it. Check-in : quick and efficient. Everyone I saw.. said hello, how are you, anything you need? From housekeeping to random employees I ran into being nosy walking around the hotel Room: I requested high floor away from ice machine/elevator. Got it. I had a 1 bedroom suite for 2 nights. Room was very clean and trust me I look. I liked that it was set up as a small apt with kitchen/living room, hallway then bedroom, not a fake suite with a little wall to separate. Very spacious with tvs in living area and bedroom. Nice tray in living room to carry food, eat from, dvd player. TV channels were less than I would have thought. Maybe 20 and 2 are hilton channels trying to get you buy movies. No FX or USA...Full fridge, 2 burner stove and microwave. Silverware, plates, and pots all there. And a dishwasher. Good job Pool/breakfast: Now it's late fall here but the weather was about 80 all weekend so I went to pool area to stretch out and read. My goal was to get a lil sunshine however, the way the building is set up, the pool area is completely shaded by afternoon which is good in the summer but kinda bad on those indian summer days like now. Breakfast Saturday was good. Omelets, sausage(not that good), waffle maker, potato pancakes(look like hashbrowns, don't be fooled), fruit, coffee and juice.They also had muffins with nuts in them in. Bad part is they post their breakfast available items on a board by the entrance. Now as I and many others have peanut/nut allergies, would have been nice to post that the muffins have nuts in them. It was a dark muffin so not very apparent that they are there. Sunday morning for some reason is PACKED with people unless you get there early so I grabbed coffee and banana and hit cracker barrel. Express checkout: Slid under your door, leave keys in the room.This is what I love about Hilton. I do not like stopping at desk when I signed for approval at check in. Waste of time I would definitely return. I love this side of town. Nice area with lots of restaurants but you do need a car.

“Great service, but tries too hard to be hip and trendy” I stayed here for business and it lived up to my expectations based on previous reviews. Staff was very friendly and I was offered a drink upon checkin. The room came with a well-stocked bar and almost all of the nonalcoholic items were complimentary. I did find a couple of things to be a little strange. First of all, the room had no drawers. I ended up putting items that could not be hung up on a shelf on the top of the closet. Since I am short, I had to step up in the closet to reach. More puzzling was the giant glass wall that separated the bedroom area from the rest of the room. There was very little space between where the wall ended and the table under the TV began. I kept imaging myself walkimg into the wall, especially half asleep. I will say that everything looked clean and modern and both the sheets and mattress were very comfortable. While the room had enough space for 1, I think it would have been cramped for a couple. My parents came out to join me at the end of the trip and stayed in a larger room. Their room was similarly furnished with one important difference - there was a glass enclosed tub/shower in the middle of the room and no, it was not frosted glass. I would have felt like an exhibitionist, although my parents said that the glass fogged over when in use, so it wasn't much of an issue for them. It did strike all of us as a little odd though. When a couple of issues came up (thermostat not working) they were handled quickly and courteously. The rooftop lounge and pool were very nice. You could see the baseball games on the big screen in the stadium. I would recommend bringing your own beverages - a thimbleful of Bailey's cost $12. Noise from the club was not an issue for me, but my parents heard it in their room. Nice hotel if your young and want to go clubbing. Probably a little too much for me.

“Nice business hotel in the center of Washington DC” The Marriott Washington Convention Center is a nice hotel located in the heart of Washington. The Convention Center is located in the next block and can be reached within in minutes. Also important sightseeing sides as the White House or the Smissonian Museums are in walking distance. There is also a metro station close by. The room are very spacious and well equipted. For executive rooms a special lounge is availible with nice breakfast and dinner and drinks round the clock.

“All this and a free shuttle to the airport. What a deal.” Great deal, great stay. I had a very comfortable bed, something I needed after a long travel day. For other women traveling alone, this is a great choice, because they get you in or out of the airport easily, and the accommodation is better than at many in the chain. The hotel was quiet, which may have been the season. I was sorry I didn't book more time in Jacksonville, and hope to do so again. I'd return here anytime.

“Steer Clear” I've stayed in this hotel many times - never again. The place has become dated to the point of dilapidation in some areas. The room furniture is worn, scratched, chairs were threadbare and the bathrooms are old, stale and dingy. The 1980's style TV belongs in a museum, not to mention the poor reception that accompanies the relic. We had access to the Club Floor which was a total joke. The offerings in the club room were meager. For one who drinks a lot of water however, this might be a good deal in that the Club Room offers bottled water complimentary, which is a far cry from the $4.50 charge for water in the rooms. Another major rip off is the $35 valet parking - the highest in San Diego that I've encountered. Service, or lack of, is another issue. The staff is indifferent to rude. Our room was not made up one day. I called "At Your Service " twice and still no results. At 6:00 that night I"d had enough and went to the front desk to complain. A shoulder shrug and telephone call later, the problem was corrected. It was almost 8pm by that point. The toilet barely flushed, and there was a continuous back-up of black/gray material sludge material in the bathroom sink that reeked of raw sewage. The AC system barely cooled the room, and the carpet was dirty and well worn. We couldnt wait to leave, never to return. This is the worst Hyatt I've ever stayed in, and as a Hyatt Platinum member, I feel more than qualified to complain.

“Agree with previous posts - average” I was here as part of a large coporate conference. As already stated - the location is good - you can access the riverwalk and easily go to dinner or shopping. You can also pick up the water taxi from here. Average mall across the street. About a 10 minute walk to the Alamo. Roughly a 15 minute ride to the airport. That said - even looking around at other average hotel brands - their facilities appeared to be more recently built. Even this brand has a newer facility directly across the street, Marriott Rivercenter. Rooms were "ok" - comfortable and clean, but worn. The beds were a bright spot as they have upgraded all the linens and pillows - which made for a comfortable sleep. This hotel is far enough down the riverwalk to be away from the noise. As part of a corporate trip - or if you get a good price on Priceline.com - this is a decent place to stay. Breakfast buffett looked good. They have a quick cafe downstairs which serves Starbucks - inlcuding speciality drinks and muffins. Don't book this location if you are going for a destination/special event as there seems to be plenty of other charming hotels further down the riverwalk with tons of charm.

“Nice Enough for Corporate Travel” My husband needed to be here on business so I came up to meet him for the weekend. If we travel for fun we do not normally stay at the airport, but as this was a business event for him the room was selected by his company. The hotel was nice and clean. The lobby is marble and updated and I would rate it at the level of 3.5 stars. The rooms are large and clean, but are badly in need of updating. They still have tube televisions and the furniture looks like a very traditional home from the eighties. The bathrooms are much more modern than the rooms themselves. They are on point with most 4 star hotels. We stayed here the same weekend that Hurricane Irene blew up the East coast, and while the hotel could use some updating the service is 5 Star all the way. We were originally in a suite on the 12th floor, and as the storm approached they moved us to a suite on the 2nd floor for our safety and convenience should they loose power during the storm. If you are staying here without an impending storm then I would recommend that you ask for the 12th floor as they offer concierge service with a nice breakfast and evening appetizers. This hotel also has an indoor pool which is small and loud, but also very nice. There were several children in the pool when we viewed it and it was a little to rowdy for my taste. The food was overall fairly good with the exception of the hamburger. No seasoning at all. I would stay here again because it was clean, and the staff was incredible, and that really makes for a nice experience more than modern decor and flat screen televisions.

“Its the best, Jerry, the best!” Spent three nights in the Andaz and have to say this was the best hotel I have ever stayed in while in NYC. Everything was perfect, the reception, room, design and staff. The mini bar and wireless were free not to mention a great coffee bar and a wine reception in the evening, also complimentary. I'm looking forward to my next visit very soon.

“Best hotel I've stayed at in NYC” I stayed here for four nights in June 2011. Got a very good advanced deal through Expedia. The rooms were spacious, stylistic, clean, and quiet. Service was really friendly, breakfast was pleasant and there was free WiFi. I've stayed at about 10-15 hotels in New York and this one was by far the best. Would recommend it without any hesitations.

“One of the best sleeps of my life” We came in the night before the most recent snow emergency; and the staff was wonderful. The check in process lasted less the five minutes, and in that time they made sure I had the room I wanted and had made me reservations for Italian just down the street. The room itself was wonderful. Very well maintained with a very modern look to it. What made the room was the bed and the assortment of pillows and bed coverings. I hit the bed after dinner and was out like a light. The service was excellent; calling down for the car from valet was a snap and by the time I came down they had it waiting for me within ten minutes even with the terrible weather. Great location, great service, and wonderful sleep.

“Great value and location” We left our luggage and went out for lunch when we arrived, then had to wait another hour for our room to be ready at 2pm. Nice waiting area in lobby with CNN. Great location one block off Connecticut between Dupont Circle and Farragut metro stations; lots of restaurants and shopping. Our room at the end of the top floor had a view of the other buildings and Scott Circle, so much light that we had to close drapes at night. Nice bathroom, but only a tiny ledge for toiletries. Good shower, but NOTHING to hold on to getting in and out, and slippery enough that I had to put a towel on the tub floor for traction. No mini-fridge in a regular room. Staff was efficient and friendly and helpful on a busy weekend.

“An Elegant Octogenarian” Wow, I hope I look this good at 85+ years old! Consider this. Tens of thousands of twenty-somethings (and younger) descended upon Grant Park, directly across from the Hilton Chicago, to participate in the annual music festival known as Lollapalooza, and thousands of those revelers camped out in the rooms of the Hilton Chicago. Although the lobbies were always filled - and from the looks of things, all the rooms, too - my business-class corner room was totally quiet. I heard nothing but music from the festival grounds. The view was fantastic, facing east toward the park and the Lake. To the north I could see Navy Pier, allegedly Chicago’s number one tourist attraction. The bed was incredible; I didn’t want to leave it. The shower worked perfectly, the amenities were quality, the Wi-Fi fast, and the room itself quite spacious. In the bathroom was a built-in night light (see the photo). Ah, such joy. Don’t you hate to turn on bright lights in the middle of the night for a short run to the facilities... All of the hotel personnel were polite and thoughtful, and bearing in mind the pressure of a hotel filled with what seemed to be mostly kids on spring break, they were accommodating beyond the call of duty. The hotel is perfectly located – easy walking distance to all sorts of public transportation, a variety of restaurants, Millennium Park, Navy Pier, shopping, theaters, everything. The Hilton Chicago itself has a fascinating history. Read about it here in Wikipedia. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilton_Chicago

“Obviously, luck has a lot to do with it” Having read the other reviews of this hotel, I feel we were unlucky... I accompanied my husband on a business trip last week. We arrived to a charming welcome and told we had been upgraded and put on the 7th floor instead of the 3rd. Well, it was late at night, so what did we know about it until the morning when I found both windows (a corner room) looked out on dark walls. I dreaded to think what the third floor was like. Then after four nights we unexpectedly had to stay on one more night. I had vacated the room early, but at 1pm (their usual checkout time) I was told by phone the new room was ready for me and my bags were in it. Not quite true. Although the usual check in time is 3pm, my room wasn't ready until 5pm. And it was on the 3rd floor (also dark but not noticeably worse than the 7th). When I asked to check out the next day at 3pm, the answer was a great big 'No'. I didn't feel very loved after spending several thousand dollars with them over the week. Basically this hotel is beloved of anyone with a room or suite on one of the upper floors, and rightly so, because if the room is right, everything else follows. Both our rooms were large by New York standards, but size isn't everything. Service was great and the location is fine, but give me the Four Seasons every time. Oh, and charging for internet access in the 21st Century???

“pretty awesome” got an incredibly great deal on priceline last minute. was happy i got this hotel as i wanted to try it out. the lobby looks great in photos and even better in person. did not expect it to be as high as it actually is. might be the best lighting ive seen in a hotel. asked for double beds as was traveling with the sister, and they did give me stress over it, even if the two double room is a room category up as i saw in their website. the room itself is sparse and clean. all in all it was incredibly soothing. beds were comfortable. the bathroom worked. there was a large walk in closet. valet and concierge were helpful and accommodating. we had some fax issues and the front desk staff were very cool about it which i again appreciate. the location is a bit father north end of the busy area. the area is mainly fancy residential, but transportation is close by, and there are a lot of bars just a couple of blocks down. would definitely want to stay here again.

“Nice airport hotel” I stayed here in March, 2006 before an early morning flight. The rooms were clean, large, and quiet (important when you have an early morning flight). I had the breakfast to go bag which was nice to take along to eat on the plane (cereal bar, muffin, water, and apple). The only negative was the mattress was soft and the fitted sheet was too small so it came undone. I guess another negative is that it was expensive because of the Final Four. I paid $177 (including taxes) per night.

“Not Bad, with one caveat” I would rate this hotel as excellent except for one thing. I was travelling on state government business, and had a govenment check to pay for the stay. My office had even called beforehand to give them information and get the hotel listed as a vendor. However, when I arrived the front desk refused to accept the check, saying in needed to be sent in several weeks before. The front desk personnel were polite, and recited that this was their policy. He said he would speak to the manager. he walked away, and in a few minutes came back with another employee, who instead walked out the front door.
