He said he had just spoken to the manager and reiterrated that they would not accept the check. I said I wanted to speak to the manager. He said that she had just left for the day. Obviously, the person I saw walk out was the manager. This was terrible cutomer service. I would expect the manager to come over and speak to me about the issue. What type of manager leaves for the day when they know they have a customer service problem at the front desk? That being said, the hotel has a good location, and my room was clean and well equipped. The rooftop patio was a great place to have a drink and watch the sunset.

“Great stay!” Had a work christmas party/event in Seattle and wanted to stay the night in the city so we chose Inn at the Market after hearing great things about it. We are very happy we did. What a nice hotel! The checkin process was easy and they even had warm freshly baked cookies at the desk to eat. The room was pretty nice with everything we needed. The bathroom was a nice size. We had a city view room due to all the water view rooms being taken already. The only odd thing about the room was that the bed wasn't facing the tv. But certainly no biggie there. Both the room and lobby were very clean. Location is nice despite the many homeless people you tend to see outside the hotel. Not a bad place to stay at all. I'd recommend it to anyone staying in Seattle.

“Consistent but Overrated” I decided to try this on a recent combo trip up to Seattle for business and to see friends. Since it was “highly” rated by TripAdvisor Contributors I decided to give it a go. I have to say I was a “little disappointed” from what I was expecting for a Grand Hyatt (their flagship property). By no means is this a “bad choice” so don’t get me wrong, it really just depends on your likes and dislikes. Here is a summary of my experience and my opinion on this property: Location – I give it a 50/50. Yes, you are semi-in the heart of downtown Seattle (but on the edge, close to the freeway). You are near shopping, businesses and the convention center BUT you are also close to the freeway so many of the rooms have “freeway view”. My room/suite actually had a combo-freeway/water view (peek-a-boo on the water side)...I honestly expected more water and less freeway for what I was paying. Now, you don’t really hear the freeway too much but you do get to look at it depending on where your room is. For a comparable price, there are several hotels in the area with much better views that are much closer to the water and sites. Charm – There is not much “charm” to this hotel but I don’t know that is the objective either. It’s fairly corporate with clean lines but so many properties in downtown Seattle have special touches like wine tasting in the lobby, fireplaces in room, etc. where they really make it feel special (think the Monaco, or Mayflower or Vintage Park, etc.). Food - Well yes there is a Ruth Chris on property but while that is a nice high end place, it’s a chain. Give me something with true “Seattle” personality. Seattle is such a “foodie” town, I can go to Ruth Chris in any major city in the U.S. Rooms – The best part is the bathroom in my opinion hand’s down. Spacious, modern, clean, etc. Sure that’s great, but how much are you really in there? The bedrooms while fairly standard for Hyatt and most the chains these days (comfortable beds, flatscreens, etc.) the furniture was a little worn. Some of my furniture had lots of nicks and scrapes. Additionally the "attractive leather" chair at the desk was not adjustable nor that comfortbale so I could not really utilize the desk in comfort as I could with an ergonomic chair many hotels provide these days. The bedroom portion of the room itself reminded me a bit of the size you find in NYC at a “W” or something similar. There is not much area between the bed and wall/dressers so if two of you are trying to pass to get to the door or bath at the same time, it will be tight. Realistically that is not untypical for an urban hotel but in many of the Seattle downtown properties, they appear to be a bit more generous in the size of the bedroom itself (in this case, a decent amount of square footage goes to the bathroom). Perhaps it was just the layout or usage of the square footage but I was not that excited about it. Gym – Well I am always fairly happy with the Hyatt facilities for their gym and one of the reasons I come back. Maintaining a workout on the road is important to me and they are always well equipped, clean and spacious and are more like a real “gym” than just a small “fitness room” that many properties offer. All that being said, I probably won’t come back to this particular Hyatt. I think Seattle has a lot more “interesting” properties in this price range and location with special touches you just don’t get at the larger corporate chains. Ahhh....consistent but boring.

“Forget This Place” It's a new hotel so you would expect better, but maybe there's a reason it was so empty during my 3-night stay. This despite cashing in on a Black Friday online deal for 50% off. The receptionist was incredibly rude to me when I checked in. I've never arrived at the counter to be asked "what's your reservation" so abruptly. This was followed by being given a room facing the highway, then a room that had been smoked in, then finally a decent room. Each time with much rudeness in between and zero courtesy. Breakfast also royally sucked considering the brand and price of this place. Nothing hot, nothing fresh...just stale bagels, prepackaged donuts and cakes (real healthy!) and mini cereal boxes. Other hotels in the area serve much better breakfasts, with scrambled eggs, hash-browns, fresh cut fruit, etc.. so I was very disappointed. Not to mention breakfast is only served until 9AM, even on Sunday!! Small Peeves... Advertises HBO, but there is no HBO (I even called the desk to ask which channel)

“small but perfect” staying here for 2 nights before my return to Sydney I found the hotel to be just what it should be, I had a single pod which meant shared bathrooms. Never being a fan of Hostel type accomodation it was purely a budget choice for me but what a lovely suprise. I adored this hotel and it really was perfect. Not once was their an issue with the bathrooms. A light goes on in your room if they are occupied. They were spotless and well appointed. My room had a little desk and corner window and the bed was firm and comfortable. The staff were lovely and the location was fabulous. Less than a minutes walk to the subway and no more than 10 mins walk to Central Park. There is a McDonalds close by as well as a great little deli with easy meals. I would definately return and look forward to doing so soon.

“Great Staff and Location” I purchased this hotel through Priceline. The location of this hotel is great, there are so many things in walking distance from this hotel. There are also plenty of subway stations in walking distance to get you to other parts of the city. I took the NYC transit bus into the city instead of a cab, which takes you to Grand Central and from there it's only a 5 minute walk to the hotel. The Hotel itself is small and on a relatively quiet street which helps with the nose in the rooms. I called a day in advance to let them know I would be getting in early and they had a room waiting for me when I checked in at 1pm.The staff is great, very helpful, especially Sophia at the front desk. There was one bellman, that was a little crass, other than him the rest of the staff was wonderful. The lobby is small, nothing fancy but perfectly clean. There are only 7 rooms on each floor. I asked for a quiet room, and was given a room on the back side of the hotel at the end of the hallway, next to the housekeeping room. It was perfect, I didn't need a view, there where no guests room next to me, so I didn't hear people in the next room. I will say the doors to the room are a little thin, as I could still hear people talking in the halls at night. But since there are only seven rooms on the floor there isn't much noise in the hallways. I actually never saw anyone on the floor. The room (807) was actually pretty big for NYC standards. The bathroom is your typical Courtyard Marriott bathroom with a hairdryer, soaps, shampoo, conditioner, lotion, shower gel. The room had a small safe and plenty of desk space with a coffee maker and TV. My only complaint for the room was they don't have the Bravo channel. There was free wifi in the room, I didn't try it though. The beds were supper soft. I do wish that Marriott would get longer sheets so that the sheets cover the comforter during the night, or put a duvet cover on the comforters. I really didn't like waking up in the middle of the night to readjust the sheets so I didn't touch the comforter. Other than that this is a great hotel and would recommend.

“Decent place to stay” I was in town for a VFW meeting over a weekend. The Ramada, where the meeting was held, was overbooked again(basketball kids). The Clarion, about 2 miles away was the overflow for us. I traveled with two other ladies and shared a double room. The room was clean and the beds comfortable. The a/c was noisy, but that's about the same everywhere. We were missing a bath mat the first night only. The second day, we asked housekeeping for a couple extra towels but didn't get them. The breakfast in the morning was good. Boiled eggs, cereal, yogurt, toast, bagels, potatoes, sausage gravy & biscuits, and belgian waffles and beverages. All in all, the Clarion was a good place to stay and I would stay there again.

“Overall, Not Bad” We arrived in San Diego expecting to stay at the Town & Country Resort but had to change plans after they didn't honor the reservations we booked weeks in advance. We thankfully had an AAA California book with us so we called Comfort Inn to see if they had a room with 2 beds at a reasonable price. At $89.00 a day and a parking charge of $4.95 a day, we decided to give it a chance. When we arrived, we found the parking spots were real tight. In the second enterance/exit, there is a spot by a light pole which is by the street that is wider than the other spots so we parked there. Check in was fast and when we got to our room, we were happy to see a very large room with two queen beds. The TV was an LG flat screen, probably a 37 inch model. The heater was quiet for a window unit. The mattresses were comfortable. There was a very small refigerator in the room which came in handy. The bathroom wasn't large but was adequate as the sink is outside the shower/toliet area. There is a heated pool outside with a hot tub by the pool. All in all, very pleased with the room. There was only a couple of negatives. The breakfast room is on the 4th floor and this room gets really crowded with people. There is one waffle maker and there was a huge line of people waiting for it. They were out of toast and bagels. They had various kinds of muffins and boiled eggs. No hot foods like eggs were served. The employees were just overwhelmed with the amount of people in the breakfast area. There was a lot noise in our room. We were on the third floor and I could not tell if the noise was from people walking above us or if it was coming from the hallway or maybe from rooms beside us. There just seemed to be more noise than usual. Like I said earlier, the parking spots are really tight and you have to watch for the pillars, other cars, ect. All in all though, we were pretty happy with the stay. We wouldn't have a problem staying there again.

“excellent stay overall” I was somewhat worried about the minimalist decor/coolness of this property, but it quickly won me over. Our Bryant suite was nicely appointed, if slightly stark. The bed was of excellent quality and the linnens were divine. The flatscreens in the LR and bedroom were perfect. The lighting/heating systems and controls were extremely fine and tremendously appreciated. I have never enjoyed a hotel bathroom so much...from the heavenly tub to the stereo system to the plush robes (which I normally don't use). All care has been taken to provide top quality modernity throught the hotel. My only beef was service. While the staff is quite friendly and natural, some kinks need to be worked out. We had made it clear that we had a special celebration during our stay. While we greatly appreciated being given a very good rate on a Bryant Suite, not even a congradulations card, much less flowers, wine or chocolate were in the suite. We quickly ordered Godiva chocolates and were brought the wrong kind. Only later that evening could we look forward to finally digging into the replacement. When we returned to the room we found a small box of quite boring flat chocolate squares...not exactly what we had in my mind. We laughed about the $30 or so we were paying for it and let it go. The remainder (most) of our continental breakfast was removed from the room despite a note I left on it to please leave it for us. A series of calls and miscommunications ensued (including a call to us at 7 a.m. the next morning) which I was not in the mood for, just to have those things replaced. That said I feel the staff truly wants to be top notch and with perseverance and committment to it, they will in time.

“Great Place” This hotel is a wonderful find. it's very clean, the staff members are on the ball and very helpful. Our only complaint: the smell of someone's cigarette smoke coming through the vents into our room and into the bathroom when we arose in the morning. I'm not sure what can be done about that, however. We didn't have the opportunity to have the complimentary breakfast, as we had to leave early, but it looked very good.
“Good location, nice staff and great view” The hotel staff were all nice and the view was amazing. I stayed on the weekend and noise was not a problem.

“Hampton Inn Poplar - My favorite Memphis spot” It is centrally located in East Memphis to lots of shopping and restaurants. It is a relaxing hotel and has a great price. I can't say enough for the staff; always exceptional and the housekeepers ALWAYS say hello!!! We only live 60 miles from Memphis, but when we need a get-away, this is the spot!!! Thanks!!

“Great views, great place if you're up for the crowds” I've stayed at the Hilton Times Square a few times but my most recent stay was the best yet. I had an upgraded room on the 44th floor and the views are just spectacular. There are no obstrcutions for South-facing rooms so you just have an incredible view of the city. The hotel has nicely updated rooms that are a very nice size. The beds are extremely comfortable and everything is very modern. My room was very quiet, being on a high floor, with almost no noise from the streets below. The restaurant is good, but expensive, especially compared to all the options you have within a few minute walk. I like the fact that there's a lobby bar as well. It's small but it's just great to have a spot to grab a drink before heading out. Drinks aren't cheap but it's really convenient. The location of the hotel is good and bad. It's a great spot if you're up for dealing with the insane crowds around Times Square. The sidewalks near the hotel are simply packed. For kids (of any age) Dave & Buster's is right next door as is Madame Tussauds. However, that also means lots of pushing through the crowds. The 42nd St subway station is also right there so it's a breeze to get away from Times Square quickly. I'd definitely recommend it to anyone that wants a central home base while in NYC with great rooms, views and beds. As long as you can deal with the crowds everytime you walk out the door. One simple way to avoid that is to head out the south door onto 41st.

“Great location, clean and stylish rooms, free Wi-Fi” I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn recently with some extended family for a weekend in Chicago. I will definitely be back. The rooms are a great value and the Free wireless internet is great. The rooms are nicely appointed for a midrange chain with updated furniture, Aeron desk chairs, comfortable beds with clean white duvet covers, and flat screen TV's. (see my photographs) They have an extended cable line up including HGTV. There is a microwave and refrigerator (not a mini-bar) in each room--it is right across the street from a grocery store. No safe provided. Wi-Fi is free and works well. The pool is small and there is a whirlpool. The fitness center contains a few basic machines; there was a sign on the door saying free guest passes were available to Crunch fitness a block away. There is a parking garage right next to the hotel...self parking was about 25 per day...a bargain for downtown Chicago. The hotel is right in the River North district, two blocks off Michigan Avenue. Close to River North restaurants and nightlight. Near Nordstroms for shopping. Weber Grill restaurant is just off the lobby. I would recommend this hotel.

“Friendly staff and quiet location” My company booked me at the Hampton Inn Chelsea when they couldn't get me in a room closer to my client's site. I've stayed at other Hampton Inns in Manhattan but never this one and I must say that this property was fantastic! I usually take the train into the city but ended up driving this time due to traveling with colleagues and time constraints we were under. They have valet parking only and it's $45 for 25 hours (yup -- twenty-five hours). We checked in quickly with no problems and were offered freshly baked warm cookies. The front desk staff was so very friendly!!! The hotel is located not even half a block from Starbucks in one direction and half a block to Jamba Juice and Whole Foods in the other direction. The subway stop is just around the corner and so convenient! Breakfast was the usual Hampton Inn bfast with hot and cold foods, pastries, yogurt, fruit, etc. Bathroom was clean, everything was very tidy in the room. Didn't hear any street noise at all! I will stay here again -- even when traveling for leisure. The rates we got through my company code are fabulous for Manhattan!

“Awesome” I got a great expedia deal on this--under $200/night before tax. Stayed here for the San Francisco Marathon, which starts literally right outside the doors of the hotel. But there's a lot else right outside this hotel's doors--Ferry Building, Farmers Market, Whatever The Name of The Giants Stadium This Year...the entire Embarcadero is right there. Room was fantastic, even though the "city view" is little more than an office across the street. Needing an early night's sleep, silence was crucial to me and the construction of this place didn't let me down. The BEST aspect of this hotel, as you'll see from my photos, are the multiple outdoor sitting/drinking/dining terraces on all the higher levels. Great in the afternoon which tends to be sunny and warmer in this SF microclimate. The restaurant is above average, but certainly don't hesitate to go out to eat. Lot of great dining spots in SF. Finally, they may have the friendliest hotel staff I've ever encountered. Just outstanding service! I've stayed at half a dozen hotels in SF and this has been the best, hands down. I was always a Harbor Court fan, but this place has that beaten, and at a better price.
“Great hotel” Great rooms - very comfortable - great service and food. Gym is fantastic though opening hours are a little tight at the weekends.

“Great Location” We stayed at the hotel for six nights over New Year and were very impressed with this hotel. The location of the hotel was excellent, it is across the road from Rockefeller Plaza and half a block from 5th Avenue. Check in was very quick and the staff very helpful. The room was very clean and comfortable and was average size for NYC. There was a fridge and microwave in the room and bottled water was available to collect from every other floor in the hotel. The bathroom was on the small side but on our experience of staying in NYC before the rooms are generally small. Computers and printers are available in the hotel. We found the staff at the hotel very helpful. The only negative point of the hotel was the lift, there were two lifts in the hotel but the wait could be quite lengthy. There were stairs which a few people did walk up but our room was on the 19th floor so it would have been quite a walk. The hotel was excellent value for the price we paid. We would definately recommend this hotel for a stay in NYC.

“Zimmer nicht wie gebucht verfuegbar” Als wir in der Rezeption (in der seit unserem letzten Besuch vor mehreren Monaten immer noch das Wasser von der Decke laeuft) ankamen standen zwei Mitarbeiter hinter der Theke und haben sich unterhalten. Wir wurden gesehen - und ignoriert. Als wir endlich einchecken konnten wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass die gebuchten und bezahlten Zimmer nicht verfuegbar sind. Wir koennten nur ein King Zimmer und ein 2 x Double Zimmer haben obwohl zwei 2 x Double Zimmer gebucht und bestaetigt. Toll, wenn man mit 8 Leuten uebernachtet. Uns wurde aber zunaechst jegliche Hilfe verweigert mit der Aussage, die zentrale Reservierung haette die Buchung falsch uebermittelt. Erst nach extrem hartnaeckigen Druck wurde meinem Verlangen nachgekommen, uns ein zweites King Zimmer kostenlos zur Verfuegung zu stellen. Ich wuerde das Hotel in Zukunft meiden!

“Below average spa - two thumbs down” My experience at the spa was average. The spa service itself was good however the amenities lacked. The spa didn't offer much by way of food/snacks. The lounge area was small and basic. Overall, I would go somewhere else for a spa service.

“2nd Night redeemed 1st night's stay” My traveling partner was having a procedure at a Beverly Hills office. This hotel was recommended as being moderately price for the area. I booked one night's stay thru Priceline. I worked that day and drove 5 hours and arrived about 9pm and was given a room on the 3rd floor.. After showering, I pulled the bedding back on my bed and the sheets just didn't have that crisp freshly laundered feel or look to them. As I inspected further there were stains on the top sheet. I called the front desk and told them. I was told he would send housekeeping right up to change the sheets. Initially I said ok but then started thinking what else hasn't been cleaned? (the other bed's sheets had obviously been changed. So maybe the maid thought no one has slept in the 2nd bed in the previous occupant?). I called down and asked if another room was available. I was told the room right across the hall was and "a bellman will be right up with the keys. 20 minutes passed-no bellman. I called again and it was a different person who answered the phone and didn't seem to know anything about it. By now its about 10:15. After that call, about 5 minutes later someone arrived. In the meantime, I looked around one of the chairs, and there were little papers-obviously the room had not been vacumned I realize people try to pull scams in order to obtain freebies, but I was very surprised that nothing was offered to offset my inconvenience. However, in the morning I went down to the desk before checkout and explained what happened the previous night and asked if my parking could be waived and he said "Absolutely". Thank you Ryan for your service. My traveling partner had to stay another day that we didn't expect. The clinic then told me that the Crowne Plaza gives a discount if you mention the Clinic's name when booking. I did and got a far better price than Priceline. We were given the same room accept on the 7th floor with sweeping views of downtown and mountains. We rec'd a newspaper in the morning vs not receiving one the night before. The room was very clean. The beds were very comfortable. The pool area is fairly large and attractive, Bus stops close. Although there didn't seem to be any restaurants right outside the door, walk about 4 blocks up Beverly Blvd and both sides of the street are lined with chain stores: Chilpote, Starbucks, Peets etc as well little local's cafes. Cute area. Rodeo Drive about a 25 minute walk. Because my 2nd night was so much better, I would definitely recommend this moderately priced hotel for this area.

“Top notch family resort!” This is a great place to vacation! The standard room is an embassy-suite style standard suite (separate bedroom/living room areas, nicely decorated and very comfortable). The staff if very friendly. The grounds are beautiful and there's tons of stuff to do! This is the most kid-friendly resort we've ever been to... there are free activities throughout the day for the kids and on Saturday nights they have a free pool side "dive-in" movie, there are about 8 pools, a water slide, and water falls and fountains located throughout. The kids get a free welcome gift. The only drawbacks are the cost of food (although this is typical of these types of properties), and parking is a bit of a hassle... but you can valet for the cost of a tip if you chose. They could use a few more strategically placed elevator too (depending on your room location you can be in for a bit of a walk if you need to use the elevators). Overall this was a great experience, and given the great deal we got through Hotwire at $75/night it was pretty amazing!

“Good location, easy parking across the street, nice views” I enjoy staying at this property as check-in is easy, the rooms are bright and the bed comfortable. The parking garage is right across the street. The front desk staff makes sure to make you feel welcome. The rooms are typical of sliver size hotels in Mnahttan and not particularly large, but has everything yuou need to ensure a pleasant stay. The location is close to Macy's and the Empire State Building for those visiting the area. I'd stay here again. You can often find good rates during the winter months.

“Great Location” The St Francis is one of my favorite hotels in San Francisco. If you are traveling for business, shopping or night life this is a great location. They seem to have several upgraded rooms and I have been able to stay in both updated and the ones that have yet to be updated. The views from the upper floors are incredible and that staff always seems to be welcoming. The greatest asset to the property is the location and many of the hot spots are within walking distance from the hotel. I would rate the non suite rooms at 3* the hotel a 4* and the stays in the suites as 5*. the rooms are spacious considering the age age of the hotel and the location. This isn't your typical NYC type downtown hotels with micro rooms.

“Decent but there are better W hotels” I stayed there for 3 nights. My whole stay was uneventful and I got an upgrade to a nice room. There is just nothing that really stands out about this hotel. But sometimes no news is good news. The location is great. If you get a good rate, I would recommend it.

“Grosses und ruhiges Hotel” Die erste Nacht nach dem Flug habe ich im HILTON LAX übernachtet. Im Normalfall erwarte ich nicht viel von einem Flughafenhotel. Dieses Hotel hat mich jedoch überrascht. Die Zimmer sind gross und sehr geschmackvoll eingerichtet. Die gesamte Hoteleinrichtung wirkt überaus elegant. Das Frühstücksbuffet war überdurchschnittlich, würde es jedem empfehlen. Sehr angenehm ist auch, dass sich im Hotel eine Mietwagenstation von Hertz befindet. Ich könnte mir dieses Hotel auch für einen längeren Aufenthalt vorstellen.

“Nice hotel, just don't try to book a taxi from here!” We picked this hotel because of the ratings here on TA and as far the cleanliness etc goes, we were not in any way disappointed. The novelty Texas-shaped waffle iron at breakfast was indeed cute - even if we're not waffle aficionados! I would endorse what has been said elsewhere about the friendliness of the staff, though add a caveat to their 'helpfulness'. We were in Austin over a weekend (Saturday & Sunday night) during the Pecan Street Spring Festival - awesome fun, by the way. We asked at reception about getting a taxi into town for this and were supplied with a couple of numbers to call from our room - though warned it could be a while. Fair enough. After numerous attempts, we finally managed to get one booked and headed down prior to the alloted time for collection to wait.....and wait....and wait. At this point, the guy on reception told us all manner of nightmare tales about the difficulties of getting taxis on a Saturday night. My fiance asked if he could call to chase from reception, conscious it was a freephone local call, but was told he would have to go to our room to do so. Why? Especially given our room was a good distance from the main entrance. We were then further regaled with what sounded a lot like excuses to us, about how the hotel staff never got involved in helping guests arrange taxis because of the difficulties that were experienced....blah blah, blah. Well, maybe the local taxi firms are appallingly unprofessional/overworked. Yet surely if that is the case, the hotel should build a relationship with one so that it can (a) ensure that firm gets the work; and (b) improve service for its clients, instead of palming them off with flimsy 'good luck with that' asides? A small grumble in what was otherwise a really enjoyable stay - just be warned if you're not willing to drive everywhere (restaurants, downtown etc) that you are in a pickle!

“Favorite hotel so far by the galleria” I really liked my stay at this hotel. They hotel staff was very friendly and accomodating. This is one of primary reasons I like the Marriott hotel brand. I booked this hotel with priceline and they offered me a choice of king or double beds which not all hotels will do if you book with priceline. The room was smaller than some I have had but extremely comfortable. I really liked the bedding and the bed, extremely comfy. The layout of the room and bathroom was also very nice. They have self parking at 13 dollars a day which is cheaper than many hotels in the area (there are some free ones though). The only complaint I had is the hotel bar is way overpriced. All hotel bars are pretty pricey and I expect to pay about 7 bucks for a jack and coke but they charged 9 here... ouch.

“Price can't be beat” Our family of four spent one night here in June. This was by far the cheapest hotel in the Inner Harbor area. Location is very convenient to the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. Staff was very helpful. Hotel was nice enough, and worth the money. Room was very small. Probably could not have spent more than one night here without getting on each other's nerves.

“Terrible Bristol Lobby Lounge” We were hoping for a night of fine dining and good drinks.Arrived in a mostly empty lobby lounge to be told there are only tables in the middle of the room but we would be reseated closer to the window when a table came free-they are half full for those tables at this point!.We are given menus (naturally astronomical-this is the 4 seasons after all)and 5 minutes later having been told we would be reseated the waiter tells us to "Move if we are not eating as we are getting busy" .Still half empty at this stage.I am not sure where the 4 seasons train their waiters these days-we just laughed, gave up on anything good happening here and moved off to the absolutely lovely Bistrot du Midi which boasts staff who understand hospitality.

“Back for a second time, still great!” Very clean residence inn close to Beverly Hills. Great breakfast, really nice servers. Rooms are clean and quiet - hotel is very well kept. Only negative is lack of pool. Avoid parking fee (I hate these extra fees) by parking on the street - right down from the car wash on Beverly!

“Very average.” Compared to other Westin properties I've stayed at, this one is somewhat below average. The rooms needs some cosmetic upgrades. My room had an overall "musty" odor. My room included "free WiFi" and "free bottled water". When I arrived, I had to call and request a bottle of water and only once during my 6-night stay was the water bottle replaced with a new bottle. There was an overall lack of consistency with housekeeping services as well. Some days, they skipped giving me wash clothes, other days they shorted me a bath towel. Some days the room was cleaned by noon; other days it wasn't ready until later (I tried to eat in my room on a lunch break, but it was in the middle of being cleaned). There is also a dog kennel on the south side of the building, so every day and many nights I heard barking dogs, even from the 10th floor.

“Nice hotel, large, needs some room updating” Guest rooms could use a little overhaul. Beds were comfortable, but some areas of room/ bathroom were a little shabby. Room was a decent size with nice double-sink vanity area in bath. Hotel is very large. Service was good by all staff. Friendly. Good food at several of the bar/restaurants.

“Best Super 8 Ever!!” Agree with all the previous excellent reviews...this family do a FANTASTIC JOB! The place is spotless, comfortable, breakfast was good, Owner is friendly, even offered us desert when we arrived! There's even a LCD TV Monitor in the elevator! The business centre has clean laptop computers and a good laser printer, just what you need to print off your boarding passes. 10/10 for The Kumar Family.

“Nice hotel for price but check CC statement carefully.” Stayed here $69 for a one night stand after flooding in Houston caught me in East Houston in not the best of areas off I-10.Nice hotel small suite room comfy beds renovated nice rooms.Breakfast was outstanding with waffle iron that would make you homemade waffles in the shape of the state of Texas pretty cool the high point of my stay.Tried to slide a second charge in on my credit card 2 months after the stay hoping I would not catch it reported the charge "error" got a refund so be careful there.

“Even more good stuff” All the good stuff the other reviewers say about this place is true. What's more, the rooms are very quiet and relaxing. They encourage recycling. What a concept! They have coffee in the rooms which is rare these days. Free local telephone calls and parking. The staff is gracious and accommodating. The front desk staff and housekeepers couldn't do enough for the guests. It is was unreal. Guests hung out in comfortable chairs in the lobby like they were in a second home. I would not stay anywhere else if I am near Queen Anne. They have ruined me for other places.

“Just what we needed” The location is just perfect, and the rooms are fabulous. We stopped here for one night on our way home from Dublin. It was well worth recovering from jet lag in such comfortable surroundings.

“Not 4 star” I won this hotel on a priceline bid. I am beginning to realize that hotels register with priceline for a reason. This was billed as a 4 star hotel and it is not even a 3. The check in was easy and the employees were helpful though the front desk clerk mentioned to me she was at the end of a double shift. The hotel is centrally located. There is no breakfast though there is a coffee service in the lobby in the morning. The valet staff was good and the employees really do a good job at this hotel. the room was very small, old, drab, and the bed sagged. the room had only one DOUBLE bed and I am 6'4'' so it was rahter short. the bathroom was small. There is quite a bit of outside noise that makes it into the rooms and I was awakened at 06:00 by a dumptruck below my window. I travel to Seattle often and there are a lot of good solid 3 star properties in the downtown area (Red Lion, Crowne Plaza) so I would probably head there next time unless I wanted to srping for wht is one of my favorite hotels of all...The Grand Hyatt Seattle.

“Close to Perfect Hotel!” Cleanliness and Friendliness must be their mission and they excel in both. The location is great. Rooms are spacious, amenities are good, but more than that - every single person on staff greets you - smiles and makes you feel welcome, of course, we felt that throughout San Francisco. They appreciate and understand the value of tourism dollars. Didn't eat at the restaurant - too many choices close by and didn't want something ordinary. Love the fact that the fitness room is open 24 hours unlike most hotels who experience the 6am rush and then there is not enough machines for everyone. Wouldn't even think of trying another hotel after such a nice experience.

“Great Hotel! Our 2nd stay..” This is a great Hotel! We've stayed twice, and will return again. Great location downtown. Walking distance to everything. Staff is courteous and helpful. Pool on the roof is fabulous! Great views!

“Great Staff” I booked this hotel for two nights with mixed feelings given the reviews on this site. Our experience was much more positive than some others. The staff here is extremely friendly and go out of their way to meet guests' needs. Our room was clean, comfortable and extremely quiet. The breakfast buffet was very good. We appreciated the indoor garage (it isn't that far from the lobby) because it poured with rain much of the weekend. Parking was free in our reasonable AAA rate. You can avoid some of the traffic congestion from the Galleria by coming in the back way off San Pedro. The front desk recommended Le Peep on Westheimer around the corner for a late breakfast - excellent food at reasonable prices and lots of parking.

“I will be back...” I had to spend one night in San Diego before moving to a hotel inland. I chose the Dana because of other reviews and the location of the hotel. I really wish we had more than one night here. I was with my 13 year old daughter. We arrived later at night. Front desk was efficient and organized. As we were only there for one night, I didn't really care about the view. As it turned out, the room looked out onto the cove pool. NIce...although could probably be loud if there were lots of people in the pool. Room was nicely decorated, 2 queen beds...comfortable, smooth sheets and fluffy towels. There is a microwave, coffee maker and small fridge. Coffee packages were Wolfgang Puck brand. We decided to order room service for breakfast. Came to $20.00 (including tax, mandatory gratuity and service charge) but for cereal, fruit, orange juice, eggs, toast and hashbrowns I would say it is really not much more than one would pay at a decent restaurant (not talking Denny's or IHOP). We left the car at the hotel and took the shuttle to Seaworld. Stayed the day and then left. Staff at the front desk were very informative about directions. The setting is beautiful and the grounds nice. Sure there is a parking charge, but majority of the decent hotels in the area do charge. If you don't want to pay it, stay at a cheaper..yet no way near as nice hotel, in a different area.

“great base for conferences & conventions in downtown Phoenix” I just finished a two night stay at the Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel. This is a very large hotel (close to 30 floors; 1000+ rooms and 40-something suites), situated a block or two away from the Phoenix convention center. The 10 minute cab ride from the airport is just under $20 before the tip. This hotel can accommodate a lot going on: during my visit, there were not one but two big events happening at the hotel concurrently (a meeting of DSW shoe store managers and a forensics conference). When the two disparate groups were meeting up for a social time in the sizable lobby, it still didn't feel so overwhelming to where I couldn't easily navigate around the various groups to get where I wanted to go (to the front desk, to the restaurant or to the lobby bar). Check-in took only a few minutes (delayed only because the front desk manager had to run to the back office to grab some breakfast vouchers for me), and I was given a room on the 23rd floor, which is one designated as a "Starwood Preferred Guest" floor. Unlike the "club" level floor (which gets the more dramatic upgrades and perks), there are a few subtle perks to a SPG room: free bottles of water in the room, a robe in the closet, and daily USA Today newspapers could be found in the elevator lobby. My room had an empty mini fridge and a room safe deep enough to store my MacBook Pro in. The closet also contained a couple small drawers along the bottom if you are the kind of traveler who wants to take clothes out of the suitcase and drop them into some place more orderly. A large flat panel screen was on the wall facing the bed. I was happy to be able to leave the little in-room A/C unit on "high" all night long and it generated enough white noise for me to be able to sleep comfortably. The A/C unit was also a little too weak, as it never seemed to diminish the humidity in the room or get below a certain temperature. Internet (which I paid for out of pocket) was $15 for 24 hours for both Wired (Ethernet, on the work desk) or Wireless access. One nice perk about paying for Internet is that paying for the 24 hours allows you to connect three separate devices (i.e. your computer, a colleagues computer, an iPhone, an iPad, a smart phone with a WiFi connection, etc.) to the same 24 hour period. I was thankful that my SPG Preferred Plus status allowed me to check out of the room at 4 p.m. (perfect for my 6:30 p.m. flight time). I did both breakfast ($18 per person for the buffet breakfast if paying ala carte) and dinner at the hotel's sizable restaurant. The entree I enjoyed was Pan Seared Halibut (on a bed of white bean puree and topped with an olive tapenade or salad; reasonably priced for an upscale place at $24). Other choices include a couple different types of steak, organic salmon, etc (i.e. a good selection for both light and heavy palates). I also had some time to try out some exercise routines in the massive gym space on the 4th floor with a variety of cross trainer and treadmill machines and a separate room with free weights. There's an outdoor lap pool on a patio next to the gym (the only pool on the property; no full size or kid-appropriate pool here). Would I stay here again? For leisure... well... Scottsdale and it's luxury spas are literally down the street, so I'd have to think about it. For business, absolutely! My rate of $178 (including breakfast vouchers & taxes) seemed a wee bit high, but the hotel was full of conference and conventioneers and I was happy to be in the center of it all, so I think this stay was definitely worthwhile. Hopefully this information helps you out. And if you did find useful information in my review, please let me know by clicking the "Helpful" link down below. Have a great stay!

“Great overnight location; little attention to details; parking a disaster” [This note to Priceline & other third-party guests precedes all my reviews of hotels I purchased through a 3rd party vendor] Like everyone else, 3rd-party customers read reviews and arrive with expectations; high attentiveness to guest needs is what distinguishes one 2-3 star from others. Third-party prices fill rooms, and provide the business with opportunities to sell services and win future customers. My advice to Priceline customers: pay attention to reviews, articulate your needs clearly (both in advance and on arrival) and speak directly and immediately to management if your expectations are not met. If basic room needs are unmet and you bought from Priceline, ask management for adjustment; if unresponsive, tell Priceline in writing; use snail mail to the company’s street address and direct to Customer Service VP. I’ve found them responsive. Talk to local management directly and pleasantly: they value meaningful guest feedback and often can use information you provide to correct persistent problems. Whatever rate you paid, be courteous and civil to a fault: it never helps to be confrontational. Commend with care what is commendable.] OVERVIEW and COMMENDABLE: For airport convenience, and if you don't need to park a car, this large (500+) hotel is tops; it’s situated at Century and Sepulveda, right at the LAX entry. An airport shuttle runs every 15 minutes. Management was promptly responsive to my pre-arrival inquiry about parking, guest laundry and refrigerator. There’s a top-story lounge with a great view. There’s 24-hour room service, a fitness center, outdoor heated pool and free wireless internet access that (a) works and (b) loads with reasonable speed and is easy to access. I was situated at my request near the guest laundry, which is small but reasonably priced and efficient. The room was adequate but outdated; upper level rooms are better quality. Bedding including pillows was very comfortable. Despite proximity to airport, and facing Century Boulevard, my room was very quiet. QUESTIONS: It may be possible to check-in online 7 days ahead of arrival; an employee told me guests who do this are often upgraded, which means a nicer room and nicer bedding (floors 5-8 and above). An attempt to research this at the chain’s website turned up a dead FAQ link. PROBLEMS: The hotel seems to cater to groups more than to individual travelers. Of course, this makes economic sense. The touted lobby concierge is often absent, and long lines at check in are common. The hotel operator and front desk seemed overwhelmed and telephone inquiries (made necessary by the absence of amenity information from the room information guide) go unanswered. At check in I asked for a refrigerator; a crib was delivered and it took about 30 minutes to correct this. The services directory claims newspapers will be provided each weekday at your room, but this does ot happen; USA Today is at the front desk. Hot water runs slowly. Parking is a disaster: (a) $20 a day, plus taxes. (b) It is operated by a vendor, Quality Parking. (c) Valet is the only option. You are given a ticket, which you retain for your entire stay. The car is retrieved by presenting the ticket to a cashier station. (d) You then wait, and wait, and wait. I made the mistake of giving the valet my ticket one day, and he made the mistake of not telling me to keep it. This error, which was eventually corrected by cross-referencing my room number to the car, cost me 1.5 hours of waiting, calls, and frustration almost to the point of calling to report the car stolen. At one point, the cashier asked me to identify the key--of a rental car, from among hundreds in the case. Had I been on an important schedule, or needed to retrieve the rental car to return it, I would have missed my connection.

“Nett aber kleine Mängel” Anlässlich eines privaten Aufenhtaltes in New York haben wir im März 2010 6 Nächte im Hotel The Tuscany verbracht. Das Hotel wirkt sehr "privat", die Public Area ist sehr durchgestylt, das Team an der Rezeption chic und sehr freundlich. Das Zimmer war wie der Großteil des Hauses in warmen Violetttönen gehalten, es verfügte über zwei große, mit excellenten Matratzen ausgestattete Betten, und einen grandiosen Blick auf das Chrysler Building. Leider war das Badezimmer veraltet und nicht gerade ein Vorbild an Hygiene, aber was solls. In der näheren Umgebung des Hotels befinden sich zahlreiche Filialen von Starbucks und kleine Restaurants. Sehr gut: im Hotel gibt es jeden morgen kostenfreien Kaffee. Ansonsten sind die Preise (auf die Gastronomie bezogen) im Hotel wirklich hoch.

“outstanding bargain!” I just returned from nine nights in the Hotel Mela, and I highly rec this hotel! It's brand new (opened in Jan 2007) and extremely clean. The beds are very comfortable, with fine/soft linens, and the towels are divinely soft Turkish towels! I stayed in one of the "Superior Queen" rooms, which is one of the smallest. However, it was well organized and more spacious than I expected. It was also very quiet! Even though the hotel is 1/2 block away from Times Square, I was NEVER woken up at any point by noise--that's amazing in NYC! The Spa bath products are wonderful, and it was nice to have the mini-bar fridge when I needed to keep something cold as well. The staff are are excellent--everyone is very friendly and welcoming, without ever being obsequious or condescending, as some other hotel staffs may be. I never had any problems at all when I was there! There are a few things this hotel doesn't have--it doesn't have a restaurant, although they do a room service at night from a local hotel. I never used it, because NYC is great for exploring, so it didn't bother me. However, if you're the kind of person who enjoys lounging in your room enjoying yummy room service, this isn't the place for you. They don't have coffee makers in the room, either, although the manager told me that they are getting them this fall--that will be great! They do have a nice exercise room--I never used it (NYC is my exercise!) but I did check it out and it was clean and had great equipment. The safes in room are great, and the flat panel TVs really save space. The alarm clock also allows you to plug in your ipod, which is awesome. They are also perfectly located, close to the Times Square subway, Bryant Park (and its subway), etc. I highly rec this hotel and hope they will be a big success--it's a great addition to the NYC boutique hotel scene!

“Overall, very nice hotel and location!” Overall, we found this to be one of the better Hiltons we have stayed out. The location is pretty good, at the foot of Fifth Avenue and the edge of the Gaslamp (night-life and shopping area). There was a sleek, modern feel to the hotel. We found the staff to be helpful as well. Our room was exactly what we had requested! There were no signs of wear, bedding was comfortable and the bath was more than adequate with La Source toiletries. There are two complaints (one of which nothing can be done about): 1. Freight trains hitch up in front of the hotel. Being that it's downtown with lots of road crossings, they blow their horns a lot. Fortunately, they seem to be done by midnight. On our Saturday night stay, we did not hear them at all. 2. The hotel charges $30 per day to park your car! That's simply OUTRAGEOUS! Especially in light of there being $5/day lots around the corner for weekend parking (which is when we were there). But for those two inconveniences, everything else was perfect! And because it's almost impossible to get everything perfect, this hotel rates very high on our list of those to return back to in San Diego!

“Great location - great stay” This hotel is located across from the Alamo and is also located in a great area of the river walk - close to all of the restaurants. Comfortable, spacious rooms. We had a balcony room and it was perfect for us and our daughter. Friends had a standard room and it was equally nice. Rooms were spotless and updated with new everything. Super large, swiveling flat screen TVs and a decent size refrigerator for beverages. We will definitely stay at this Hyatt again.

“A tired hotel for tired business travelers” This hotel gets well-used, and it shows. Unless you look out a window, you could be in any well-used Doubletree anywhere. One upside is that rooms here actually have windows to the outdoors, which isn't always the case in other Doubletree hotels. The chocolate-chip cookie at check-in is so quaint - why do they still do that? The rooms are fully functional - ironing board, closet has room for a couple of suits and shirts, bathroom is adequate size and lighting, tv works. Furniture is slightly soiled and pretty worn. Beds are OK, and no bedbugs on this visit. Breakfast bar is way over-priced, and even the "fresh" food looks tired!

“Still Great!” Just stayed at the Nine-Zero and am happy to report that it is still a great destination when visiting Boston. I haven't been there since the first year they opened and was delighted to see that most things are still up to par. The most alluring feature of this hotel is the location - I can't imagine a more convenient hotel in all of Boston. It's sleek/hip design is also very cool. But, like all trendy hotels, it seems to tire from hipness. While still sharp, nothing really has changed since I've been there 4 or so years ago. The room is very comfortable and stylish but was showing slight signs of wear (minor wall scuffs, slightly aging furniture). Also, on my first visit the robes and towels were Frette and that was no longer the case. The Mario Russo products were great but seemed to be smaller in size. And the cheap plastic made it difficult to actually get the shampoo or conditioner out. And, as mentioned in another review...it is a little tacky that there are so many things for sale in the room. The bed was super comfortable and very roomy. A luggage rack would have been nice. One great addition from my last stay was the evening cocktail hour. Nice wines were served in the lobby from 5-6. A nice touch. Staff was friendly and helpful. Needed some extra soap and it was sent up promptly. As instructed, when I needed my car I called about a half hour before hand. I came downstairs and it was ready and waiting. Although the $38 fee is quite steep! The Nine-Zero is no bargain but look around the web. I got a great rate through one of their promotions and it was actually a little cheaper than comparable hotels such as the Hilton.

“Great Location and Great Hotel” I stayed in DC at several hotels over the months of March and April and this was by far the best hotel that I stayed at in the area. Great location and a quick walk to the Dupont Metro. Many restaurants close by and free wifi with good speeds for Kimpton In Touch Members. I just with I was able to stay at this hotel for all the nights I had to stay in DC.

“Great end to 2011” Spent New Year's weekend 2011 here. Great stay--the rooms are cool, ours had a little window seat overlooking the street that was nice. Did add some limited street noise, but the sun and air were worth the tradeoff. Walking distance to everywhere we wanted to go, good neighborhood with lots of local flavor, close to bus line, etc. The cable TV wasn't working and they fixed it quickly and also hooked us up with a late checkout. All systems go.

“Good location, no complaints” We traveled on pleasure, not buisiness. I don't like being nickeled and dimed, however, this buisness hotel didn't do that. I'm a silver member and had two free night certificates, and was upgraded to a 25th floor corner room, with the hotel booked solid for a convention . . Only complaint came waiting for the elevevator, in the morning when biz folks were off to the show. But the view as worth the wait. However, this corner did not have the balcony. Slightly smaller than the other king beds, for more room get a double bed Nice pool, small out side deck. The whirpool , although small, packed a good power punch to work those muscle knotts out. The small gym was well equipment and 'sweat-smell free'.Great central location for getting around. we walked to everything. Boston common, fenway, Beacon Hill. And the subway is 5 blocks, far enough that the homeless are not at the hotel door, but not far enough to work up a sweat.The hhonors floor is 24, the gold room is nothing to rave about. I walked in and saw fresh fruit, coffee, and some dry goods. Far cry from the free breakfase at a hamption inn. You can cross the street and eat in Prudential center, or better yet, outside on newbury st. NO problems with staff. Front desk was fantastic. At 9pm I ran out of milk for my comp. in room coffee, and the manager opened the frig up at the starbucks which just closed. Then housekeeping appeared with more creamers and coffee. I would stay here again,if the price was right. And it seems more updated than the busy , croweded 5000 room Shereaton across the street.

“Basic, classic and a tad bit spooky!” The Moore is one of Seattle's two truly historic hotels and is a great deal for downtown Seattle. I checked in at midnight and got one of the less desirable rooms, tucked away int he back overlooking the alley. It had a private bathroom with a non functional shower and no mirror and in the morning we woke to some insanely loud construction type activity in the alley. That said, I would definitely recommend the Moore... Everyone we interacted with was friendly, the maintenance guys even took my boyfriend and I down to check out the Olympic size swimming pool in the basement (it's empty)! Positives: -Super central location -Minimal, modern guest rooms -Very affordable -Laid back and likable employees Negatives: You can't have visitors in some rooms Not all rooms have private baths 11am checkout Slow elevators All in all a great old hotel, and the only one with rooms available the night of the Yankees game this month!

“Not your typical NYC shoebox hotel” I have stayed in many NYC hotels where the rooms are the size of a shoebox. The Benjamin in that regard has good sized rooms, even a fridge and microwave meaning you can snack in front of the Tv without needing to eat out. The hotel has some age and charm. Food is catering form the restaurant on the ground floor - good quality, reasonable variety. Drinks are expensive but its New York. For location, room size and in room facility at the price, this is a bargain
“Good Hilton Garden Inn in a great location” This was a nice Hilton Garden Inn at the north end of Tribeca. The room was good size for New York and up-to-date. Would stay again.

“Very surprised, and that is not good!” I am writing this two days into a five day stay. I am on a company sponsored trip beginning tomorrow, but I arrived two days early to sightsee. This evening, after a day of sightseeing, I called to request a bathrobe since it was an amenity listed on the website and I deliberately did not pack one because it was listed that it was provided. It took over two hours to get a bathrobe. While relaxing in the tub after my second day of sightseeing, I noticed gross neglect in cleaning around the tub. On my first day, yesterday, I did not have hot water after another long day of sightseeing and took a very cold shower. I have read about all of the dignitaries that stay in this hotel and although impressive to read, I find this inferior to most hotels that I frequent and stay. The dignitaries may stay where they like, but I can't imagine they find this to be very impressive...I certainly didn't . Very disappointed to date, but I still have three more days to stay.. Perhaps it will improve and I can update my review!

“Great location to visit the set of "Sid Roth's ' It's Supernatural' "” Having secured tickets to the taping of Sid Roth's It Supenatural TV show in the new location of Charlotte...I needed a hotel and delectd this hotel based on location. It was sooo perfect. to drive to and from the studio. The hotel was very nice, had a list of places to dine and directions.the was a golf tourney going on so the hotel was packed. Breakfast was a buffet with options for a la carte. I would return.

“Really nice hotel” We stayed for a few nights on business. We loved it. I don't have anything to compare it to as I've never been to Indianapolis before but if I go back, which I'm sure I will as I have clients there, I will stay again. I appreciate the complimentary internet, the excellent device ( Marriott sure knows how to hire- great service at almost every property), comfortable, quiet, clean rooms and close proximity to restaurants etc.

“Nice Rooms but Shady Managment” May 2010. We had the opportunity to spend several nights at this property when we were in the area. The hotel off of a side road off of the toll way. Be careful about driving on the toll way or you could get fined $25.00 each way. I recommend staying off of it. This property is near Rice University, the Galleria is not too far by car and it is near the River Oaks area of Hourston. There is plenty of free parking in the parking lot. Check-in was very fast but I knew something was wrong when the front desk person take my Marriott Bonus Bucks coupon. Our room was comfortable and your standard Big Box Residence Inns. The bed was comfortable. Lighting in the room was good. , The work desk was moderate and the office-style chair okay.. My The room had a sleeper sofa and a comfortable arm chair. The bathroom was clean.. Lighting was good, the towels were plentiful, and the shower worked well – immediate hot water with plenty of pressure. Bath amenities include shampoo, conditioner, lotion/ The breakfast buffet featured scrambled eggs, hot oatmeal, and all the other things you would expect on a breakfast buffet. The hotel public areas were clean and well-kept, but could use an updating to the style of the rooms. When checking out and settling my bill, the front desk management processed Marriott Travel cards first before the Residence Inn Bonus Bucks. This left with a difficult choice because if I used the Bonus Bucks I would not able to use the face value. This is awful strange since on this trip the Residence Inn at Alamo Square in San Antonio had no problem accepting the full amount of the Bonus Buck. Also after this trip I used a Marriot property bonus buck at the Renaissance Madison in Seattle and they had no problem accepting it. I had used a Bonus Buck at the J.W. Marriott Union Square in San Francisco and they had no problem accepting it. This property and it's managment was sneaky in what it did just to make a few bucks! I have a future trip scheduled for Houston and it is fair to stay I won't be staying at this property again!

“Luxurious older hotel in downtown Dallas” Stayed at this wonderful hotel Labor Day weekend and what a grand experience it was. The hotel is in an excellent location in Downtown Dallas, close to shopping, restaurants, pharmacies. The staff was incredibly friendly and the lobby is incredible. The French Room Restaurant off the lobby is a must see. I was assigned Room 1703. This was an executive suite, and it was huge. The room was so well appointed--the furniture beautiful, and the bathroom spacious. The carpet was beautiful. The beds were very comfortable with high thread count linens. The towels in the bathroom was thick. The soaps the Adlphus used are great. Also did breakfast in the Bistro Rstaurant. I had the breakfast buffet for $15.00, and it was filling and very good. The Adolphus Hotel is a grand old hotel, and it makes for a very memorable experience. By the way, parking is valet only and it is $26.00 daily. I left on an incredibly busy morning, and the valet had my car to me in 5 minutes and gave directions to I-30.

“Great location, clean, affordable and friendly.” Stayed here for a few nights for business last week. Hilton Garden Inns have become my first choice in business travel and this hotel didn't disappoint. Very pleased with the hotel, the amenities, cleanliness and the location. The Polaris fashion place is across the street offering lots of shopping and dining choices. Also a quick ride to Easton and Dublin if you want to visit those areas. If you don't have a car no worries - there's a restaurant and bar in the hotel and other places within walking distance. Hotel staff was friendly and helpful. Would definitely stay here again.

“Superior staff, great room!” I stayed here last summer on business. When I arrived, after a long, intl flight, i was told my room would be ready in 2 hours, if I wanted to go walk around. I told them I was exhausted and just would wait (or maybe sleep) in the lobby. They then asked how important a view was to me, because my proposed room was overlooking the hahbah. I was happy with a room sans view as long as it was quiet and had a nice bed. They then got me another room. The girl at the desk was incredible. Not only did she help me with my suitcase (which I could have done) but she showed me my room, how to operate the electronics and even let me know which of the nespresso capsules were her fave. I then realized I forgot my power cable to my laptop (I'm not normally this bad), and asked if by any chance someone had one I could borrow while they were working? Well, within ten minutes a guy came in with two to try. And luckily one worked! The team here rocks and they made my stay so enjoyable and special. The room was also great - quiet, large, great bathroom, comfortable bed, fast wifi. Perfect in every way. They also have a gym nearby which, while small, is adequate. Definitely good for a business or personal trip.

“prefect NYC hotel ... great location, great staff, great vibe” 1 of the better NYC hotel stays i've had. location was perfect if you like a downtown ... proximity to west village, meat packing, soho, etc staff was helpful/friendly & we rooms were specious with all of the amenities. it was also quite affordable. about the only complaint i had was that the bar was bit tired, but then again, i'd rather have that away from my hotel anyways

“Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Time” I cashed in some Marriott Points to stay here. Very Nice Hotel with lots of amenities. In the heart of NYC times square and walking distance of the Theaters. I traveled with my mom and she has a walker now and no issues getting to the plays for her. The hotel has a great handicapped rooms with support bars near the toilet and shower. Big bathroom too. The view we had was not great but could see a bit of times square. They have a nice buffet $29 for breakfast lots of Fresh food. we ate at Juniors across the street ($8.95) better pricing. They have two Starbucks on site one at street level and one at the 8th floor level. The elevators do not have buttons in them. You press the floor you want and then the system tells you what elevator to go to. They have high traffic at peak times for the elevator. Remember this when going out pre theater dinner. They also ding you $16.95 for internet so remember to bring your wireless router for free hooks for the rest of your friends and family. The standard rate at this stay was $299 plus tax. in 2007 the rate was 517.00 per nite. this is a category 8 hotel for Marriott with 40,000 points per nite. The clock radio had the wrong time and was not lighted at night. Remote worked well and flat screen TV was good too. No paper in the morning unless you request it. Thats a bummer. Staff was great with the few requests that we had. business center was awesome, concierge staff gave real help versus sending you to affiliates that charge too much.

“Perfect Stay!!!” Once again Hyatt has lived up to its name. I am a huge Hyatt fan because of the consistency of their product and great customer service. The Hyatt Regency Boston was yet again another flawless Hyatt property. the hotel is in a very convenient location only blocks from the Boston Common in the heart of downtown Boston. Upon entering I was immediately greeted by friendly doormen. Check in was fast and most importantly the front desk associate was extremely pleasant and welcoming. My room was on the 15th floor with a great view of the city. The room was spotless and very nicely decorated. The bed was amazing. Slept like a baby both nights of my stay. Hotel also had a nice indoor pool and great stay fit gym. The only things I could find wrong were very minor flaws like some of the public spaces are in need of renovation and the shower in the room could have been better quality. Still overall it was a perfect stay. I was highly impressed with the 5 star customer service I received from all of the hotel staff. I definitely will stay here again on my next trip to Boston.

“Great location and free laundry” Great location-- walking distance to the Galleria mall, across the street from a couple great restaurant-bar spots, and a few short blocks from a 24-hour CVS. The biggest plus for me was the free laundry, especially since I stayed for almost two weeks. I'd stay here again.

“This is a very chic hotel in a great location!” This new hotel is in a great location. It is right by the airport but is slightly off the beaten track where the traffic and noise are very tolerable. It is surrounded by great restaurants and upscale condos and office buildings. It is just a few blocks from the subway as well. The hotel is clean, modern and chic. The rooms are pretty cramped which is not uncommon for a big East Coast city. While we were there, there was a huge singles convention, so it was not exactly peaceful and quiet. The walls are paper thin and the sound insulation is somewhat lacking. However, the service is friendly, prompt and professional. The gym is well done but very hot! There is a small pool. If you want a new, trendy clean hotel in a great location, you would be hard pressed to find a better place.

“Once again excellence!” Second time here this year. The room was super, 29th floor with as good a view as it gets in Houston. The room was spacious, well appointed, and had wifi for free. The drawbacks were a $5 bottle of water, but on the plus side, 2 coffee packs NON decafe, yea! Relatively cheap car parking, $24 a day, I think. Nice staff, from the parking guys to the front desk to the bartender. I highly recommend this joint as one of the best in downtown Houston.

“Last time I will ever stay here!” I have have stayed here at least three or four other times in the past. The first two stays I had little to no problems. The last two have been bad, and I will never stay here again! Problems: *Checked in around midnight and it took forever to get a person to the desk. *Shower head was all messed up and they supposedly had no other rooms avaible. I ended up fixing the shower head myself after showering in another friends room. *The kitchen sink plumbing was broken and was collecting in buckets under the sink. *Light was out in the refridgerator. *Cobb webs hanging from the ceiling. *Room key kept deactivating. *Could hear people talking outside the building while staying on the second floor. *Lastly they charged for me for the night after I checked out, but thankfully I was refunded!

“Sie sind (nicht) willkommen..!” So oder so ähnlich, war das Gefühl, dass einem die unfreundlich Rezptionistin vermittelt hatte - satte 30 Minuten Diskussion, bis endlich geklärt werden konnte, dass ein Internet-Ausdruck aus "roomsaver" dem Original entspricht und dass die Internet-Seite extra dafür da ist, da man sie zum Ausdrucken nutzen kann, falls ein "roomsaver-Magazin" nicht greifbar ist. Dann wurde uns mitgeteilt, dass wir pro Übernachtung einen Voucher brauchen würden ("O..k. dann drucken wir noch eine Seite aus"), dies hatte dann dazu geführt, dass wir dann letztlich nur eine Nacht gebucht haben - "als eine Art Strafe" mussten wir dann auch noch mit der Kreditkarte zahlen, weil man keine America Express Checks annehmen wollte - im Gegensatz zur nur 2 min. entfernten Tankstelle. Fazit: Das Hotel ist an sich gut gelegen und verfügt über eine halbwegs vernünftiges Preis-Leistungsverhältnis, aber mangelhafte Mitarbeiterqualifikation lässt hier eine Reservierung zum "langwierigen Diskussionsexkurs" werden.

“Good Location” Stayed 4 nights in October. Great location for the Metro and main attractions. The room was a good size, with a large comfortable bed, nicely decorated and clean. The bathroom again very clean with adequate towels and shower accessories. A room safe a good touch. The lobby always appeared busy with coach loads of visitors appeared to be arriving daily. Didn't use the restaurant,but had breakfast next door for less than half the price. A bit surprised when they charged $7 to store the cases for a few hours after checkout. Overall a good hotel and would stay again. Watch out for the mini bar ( very pricey) and top tray. Items picked up will be charged to your room if not replaced within 20 seconds.

“Perfect hotel for LA” This was an excellent hotel! We booked through their website for $161 per night (AAA rate) and opted to choose our room when we arrived. This was a great idea, as we ended up getting a MASSIVE room overlooking universal studios, with a seating area, and a very comfy king size bed! The hotel itself was great - the staff were extremely helpful, it had a good coffee bar for the morning, a large bar, and a restaurant with a big buffet breakfast (although we did not eat there). The hotel was in a great location - within walking distance to universal studios, and very close to the City Walk, which was fun at night! We drove to downtown LA (grauman's chinese theatre) in 10 minutes, and were at Rodeo Dr. within 15. This hotel is beautiful and is a great choice if you're looking for something a bit more reasonable priced in central LA. I highly recommend it! Parking wasn't too expensive (I think $17 per day), and the lot was easy to use! I highly recommend this hotel. I have stayed at the Sheraton Universal and this is just as good, if not better.

“Great bathroom.” We stayed just one night at the intercontinental on a quick trip down to see a show. I booked through hotwire so got the room under $400 for a saturday night, was a good deal for that weekend. I was pleased with the front desk, very warm and friendly welcome. Our room was not ready yet so we went to lunch, and had a message that we were all set to check in before we finished eating. Hotel is easy walk to time square, but I suggest walking the other direction for a great selection of restaurants in easy reach. I am pretty pregnant and this location was good because I could walk short distances easily, and there was always a cab available for whenever I needed to go more than a few blocks. The room was a good size for New York, certainly bigger than I expected from previous stays in the area. Well appointed for a 4 star hotel, bed was comfortable, everything was clean and orderly. But I need to talk about the bathroom, because that is where this hotel stood out, in my opinion. Bathroom is NYC hotels arent always the best. This was more like something you would see in Las Vegas, to be honest. It was not huge but certainly larger than average, and very well designed. Glass tiled walk-in with a rain shower... I love rain showers. There was a hand-held too if you want that. No tub, but this shower was worth the loss :) Nice amenities in the bath too, good products that were good sized, plus a little box of the extras you sometimes need to ask for (sewing kit, q-tips, showercap, etc). We did have breakfast at the hotel but I wouldnt repeat that, it was very expensive for what it was. Good, but pricey, and there are so many options so close by... if I am paying $22 for my eggs I expect my waiter to keep my water glass full, at least. Overall I would stay here again.
“Average Hotel in excellent location” LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!! The hotel is average in every sense, other than that. We booked through hotwire and got a relativly low price.

“Good location, lovely & spacious room, OK service” I stayed at the Hotel Madera for one night during the week on a business trip in March 2006. Upon arrival, I was slightly confused because there was no valet to be seen outside and I had to parallel park my car in a tiny spot on the street in front of the hotel. Also, I had to carry my own bags inside. This is not typical for me on a business trip, but I had booked the Hotel Madera knowing that it is a small, boutique hotel and that reviews of it on this board had said that service was lacking. However, once I got inside to the front desk I had very good service from the woman staffing it. She immediately radioed down for a valet to move my car. While my room wasn't immediately ready, she had the valet also store my bags. While I camped out on the lobby sofa across from the front desk to check my email and voicemails, my room became ready and she sent me upstairs. My bags arrived about five minutes later. As I am a Kimpton in touch member, I did enjoy the bottled water and fruit basket, along with handwritten welcome note in my room. The room was incredibly spacious for the city, with a full size sofa in front of floor to ceiling windows that opened out onto a small balcony with great views of New Hampshire ave. The bed was comfortable and they let me select pillows from the pillow menu. I was disappointed that the high speed internet connection was not wireless, however. All in all, I had a nice time at this hotel and would stay again for business. However, if you have a car that needs to be parked, be prepared for slow service from the valet. Next time I am in DC for business I will probably just take a cab from the airport. There were almost always cabs out front and the metro is just two blocks away in Dupont Circle.

“Little too trendy but GREAT service” My mom and I stayed at the Gans last summer for 4 nights. It's a very trendy hotel that is right near my NYC office. I was there on business and my mom tagged along to see New York. Every evening we sat out on the rooftop bar and she told me about her day over $14 drinks. We would leave for our evening activities and were often surprised by the long line to get into the hotel upon our return. Fortunately, guests of the hotel did not have to stand in that line. I don't think they would have let my mom and me into the lower level spa that turns into a night club. I was annoyed that there was not a coffee maker in the room and that I had to order a $20 pot of coffee every morning. I was became even more annoyed when I discovered that I could purchase a "personal satisfaction" device from the mini bar but could NOT make myself a cup of coffee in the morning. Maybe the average guest has other priorities. The rooms was excellent. The beds were comfortable and I enjoyed the view from the window. The shampoo, condition and lotion provided are awesome. The concierge really went above and beyond in assisting my mom in planning her visit. She wanted to see a lot and they helped her map out some things knowing that she was going about town on her own. Whenever I am in NYC and unable to stay at the Gans I always make it there for a cocktail on the roof. I do recommend crossing the street and having dinner/drinks at Pastis. It's my home away from home rest/bar in NYC.

“If it weren't for the staff, it would have been perfect” After reading previous reviews, I thought we could bypass the staff altogether and attempt to check-in via the computer kiosks. It said "Room not ready, please ask for assistance." The staff member told us our room would be ready in 5 minutes, then he disappeared and we did not see him again. 20 minutes later, when we asked another staff member about our room status, he replied "I don't know" and did not offer to check for us. It took us being a bit proactive in asking about our room in order for someone to get back to us, but 30ish minutes later, we were finally called back and given a key to our room. The room itself is lovely - simple, small, clean. It is quiet and has all the amenities you could need, including a small flat screen tv, hairdryer, closet, toiletries. The shower does not have a bath, but it is a large stand-up stall which I thought was fabulous. The location of the hotel is great - next to a dead end corner which, I think, might add to the quietness factor. On the other hand, it is so centrally-located that it is a perfect spot from which to launch into your NY exploration. I would, however, recommend doing your homework...my "let's wing it" approach to finding this hotel wasn't successful, and strangely enough, three out of four cab drivers did not know where Albany street was. For the price I paid, I would certainly go here again, with hopes for the same nice quality of room and hopes for a better interaction with the staff.

“Mega-sized historic hotel w/ga-jillion people during convention, but ok” Our rating, if available, would have been a 3.7 vs. the 4.0 we had to select for this hotel. This is a giant hotel right on South Michigan Ave, with a historic, grand, still-trying-to-be-opulent lobby-entry.
