The hotel is located further south than many of you Magnificant-Mile shoppers may want, though walkable/bus-able/taxi-able, but also convenient to the Field museum, and all the others nearby, as well as the park for those with families/kids, history buffs, etc.. For us, the location was fine. We've already done the museums from prior trips, and we're not big shoppers of the Mag-Mile. It was however limiting in terms of nearby good restaurants, bars. Let's go to our review: Good stuff: The room was a generous size. A tad-bit dated, but not too bad. We got a corner room, though facing back side of hotel vs. facing the park on East side of hotel (b/c we declined the upgrade charge for our Priceline deal). Plenty of room with our double beds, to get comfortable, featuring club chair & ottomon, LCD TV, credenza with drawers, writing desk, usual over-chargeable snacks/drinks, good-sized bathroom with nice toiletries. So much room, that they could have put another double bed, and still have plenty of room. The room was very quiet, even though we could see the "EL" subway rumbling nearby. Beds were fine, and room cooling was very comfortable. Additionally, there is a separate flat-screen on the desk to offer information or local places to visit. We didn't find it useful so really didn't care for it, and it took a few attempts in order to turn off. We were worried that the room would be very dated, old, musty, etc., but were pleasantly surprised it was fine. The location was just ok...but so reachable via bus or extended walking from other parts of the city. It is a few minutes walk to the museum area further East, if so inclined. It is however, not very close to the Art Institute museum, or the "Bean" sculpture, so please note there will be some walking or other options needed. If you're into fitness, lots of good walking. We were also told of large pool and fitness center, but did not utilize (chargeable?). Bad stuff: Like we said, the location was just ok... away from Mag-Mile shopping, good restaurant options, and other parts of city. A bit remote, but not truly. If you don't mind walking/public transit, not as big a deal. Given its size, there is a large check-in reception area with the long requisite felt-ropes, to queue up in a snake-like route, to a fairly indifferent staff. Everything seemed to be chargeable. We asked for a room facing the park, chargeable. Fitness center, chargeable. You get the idea. We were there over a weekend, with a convention for good measure, and sure enough, there were lots of people. This made the elevator area crowded & noisy, and the waits for elevators was long. Once you get past the lobby/main floor of the hotel, much quieter. Summary: A good hotel for the price we got (well under $100/night). It was a good-sized room with comfortable beds and basic amenities. Yes, needs a little updating, but fine as-is as well .. depends on your tastes. As mentioned, the location may be an issue for some...depends on what you're doing/visiting. We wish it was closer (walkable) to some good restaurants, but this city has plenty of transportation options. Would we recommend it as first choice, no. There are so many other fine hotels that we've stayed at, closer to the hub-bub that is Chicago. Of course, the price goes up accordingly (?) We would recommend this hotel as a fall-back option if others (based on location) are too expensive, or fully booked. It's a back-handed compliment of the hotel, but we had no major issues with staying here. It's a fine hotel. (Sorry, forgot to take pix!) Happy Hotel-ing !

“Still Recommended” I've probably spent 75 nights in this hotel in the last four years. It has a good location, is an attractive and comfortable property, and the staff are generally pleasant. The lady who runs the afternoon hospitality session, Kelly, makes an exceptional effort. This hotel, and probably most Residence Inns, are relatively egalitarian. I didn't get any special treatment for being a Platinum member and no one seemed aware of the room preferences in my profile. Not a big deal but I'm not sure if this promotes brand loyalty. I also have a minor complaint with the room. The air conditioning compressor is in the bedroom wall and very obstrusively cycles on and off at night. This would be ok if you set the fan to run all the time but it won't run unless the compressor is running. I finally would just cool the room as much as I good before I went to bed and then would just turn it off for the night.

“Clean, Comfortable and Convenient!” I stayed at the Radisson in mid-December for 3 nights. I was very happy with my choice and would highly recommend the hotel to anyone going to San Francisco. First, the location is excellent! It is the closest hotel to the wharf and Pier 39. If you go out the back way, it puts you right in the heart of the wharf/pier area. Of course, there are many restaurants and shops to choose from all along the wharf/pier area. I found the area very safe to walk in, including later at night. There were always people out walking around enjoying the restaurants etc. If you go out the front by the lobby, you are on Beach St. There are two trolley stops in front of the hotel, one to the right and one to the left. It makes it very easy to head into downtown/union square and is only $1.50 each way. On the way back in from downtown, you are also dropped off right in back of the hotel, couldn’t be any easier. I would not recommend getting a car, as it is not needed and San Fran has great public transportation. Also around the hotel are a Safeway and Walgreens, which makes it convenient to get snacks etc and save a little money. There is also other national shops close by, and attached to the hotel building is an IHOP, Johnny Rockets and a Subway. The hotel its self is a 4 story “U” shaped building with a wing in the middle. The lobby is very small but functional. I arrived at about 7pm and there was one person ahead of me checking in. I did use there online check in option, which is supposed to save you time etc, however, at check in, I still had to sign and present my credit card. According to the website, checking in online is supposed to save you from doing anything except presenting your ID to get your keys. Oh well, check in only took about 3 minutes. I had requested a king size bed non smoking online and received one on the 4th floor of the hotel. There are two main elevators in the lobby, with a few others scattered around the building. The hallways did have a unique smell I suppose, but nothing too bad. The hallways sort of reminded me of an old cruise liner. The room itself was perfect for one person (for a couple it would be fine as well). The room was probably about 300 sq ft at most, however, it was functional and clean. The bed was WONDERFUL!! They all have the sleep number beds, with down comforters and down pillows. You can set the bed to whatever number suits you. There was also a small desk and an armoire with a TV and storage. The air/heating unit was a little loud, but it worked perfectly. You can also open the windows to let in the fresh air. The bathroom entrance was right next to the bed, which was a little odd, but again, for one person, it was fine. The bathroom was of good size though (bigger than the one I had at the Crowne Plaza union square). It had ample space to move around and place your things. The water pressure was fine as well as the temperature. The room was cleaned everyday while I was out sightseeing and they did a great job. I did manage to see the rooms with two double beds and they seemed a little bigger, so space didn’t seem like a problem in those rooms. Overall, I loved coziness of the room and the bed made it well worth it. I would definitely stay there again next time I travel to San Francisco. Everyone I came into contact that worked at the hotel was friendly and would always greet me. The location is perfect for travelers visiting the city. I also had a good view of one of the hill areas, the wharf, and even a view of Alcatraz and the water. I couldn’t really ask for more. The other hotels in the area are close by, but for the price, the Radisson was the best option. It is definitely a solid 3 star hotel.

“Déceptif” Un hotel cher (pres de 350 USD la chambre par nuit) pour : - une chambre en etat tres moyen et daté - un coffre de chambre ne fonctionnant pas - une climatisation défaillante (pres de 24 degre celsios avec la clim poussé à fond) - un service de pressing qui froisse les chemises - un ménage à 14 heures ! - une réception très impersonnelle et blasée Cet hotel s'est endormi sur ses lauriers bien passé avec des couts excessifs pour un service très moyens ! L'hotel meriterait une renovation generale et un personnel plus attentif. Je n'y retournerais pas et vous conseille de rechercher ailleurs.

“Best Luxury Value in Houston” This hotel compares favorably to the Four Seasons and the St. Regis. Consistently excellent service, very high quality bedding and food service. It is hard to believe this is available at $129 for a weekend rate. Join the frequent guest plan and get free internet and free coffee to your room. Those alone are worth $30 at the Four Seasons.
“Central Downtown Location 1 Block From Sears Tower” The pricing coupled with the newness and the location, make this a comfortable value.

“Perfect hotel.” I really enjoyed my stay here for several reasons. The hotel is attached to the Galleria and has easy access to some pretty food restaurants. The rooms are large and offer good workspace and the best part, the hotel has an Escalade and the most pleasant and polite driver I have ever met. Our Driver, Joey, was the best and a great asset to the hotel. I am looking forward to my next stay there. As a side note, the hotel does not have a restaurant but the Daily Grill is located in the Galleria, just a few steps from the hotel. Highly recommended.

“Old style for old money” Though everyone in the office was impressed I was staying there (they seem to have a strong brand!) I would not stay there again. The room was expensive and not that big. Sure there was a separate bath and shower, but the bath salts were 50 bucks a pop. And the water was far too chlorinated - not a DC thing, definitely a hotel thing. I smelt like a swimming pool most of the time. You have to pay for internet and for the gym - the hotel's best feature and the reason I booked. It's not cheap - 15 bucks a day. When I left I found some clothes in the closet had gotten wet due to a leak. They offered to dry clean them, but it was too late. There was mold on the carpet in the closet. The service was impeccable and there was free coffee/tea in the morning and sometimes hot chocolate or lemonade in the evening. But for the same price you can go to a number of equivalent or better hotels (hyatt next block over for example) that don't charge you for everything.... and give you loyalty points too (you can use marriott points there but not earn them). I conclude that it must have an old and loyal clientele!

“Apparently Sheraton are indeed getting better !” What a difference a renovation and a new focus could do ! I never thought I would say anything good about Sheraton. To me it was a bunch of outdated properties, some badly, with rather ordinary to poor service. The newly renovated Sheraton Boston proved me wrong. The redone lobby is inviting, calming, nicely decorated with plenty of seating and places to hang out. Nicely done. It has a Starbuck Coffee and some computers available free (Links at Sheraton, they call it). The lobby can become a really busy place at times. The check-in was friendly and quick. Since the room was not ready they offered to call me on my cell when it would be ready. Nice touch. I was upgraded to an executive suite. (I'm SPG Gold, but that doesn't typically give you a suite). The room was a nice corner corner obviously recently renovated. It had a flat screen TV, a confortable working desk and a very confortable bed. The decor was really nice with pictures of Boston on the walls. Unfortunately no wi-fi access in the room and a rather high fee for wired internet. This hotel is well located in the Back Bay neighborhood a few minutes walk from the restaurants of Newbury St and the shops of Boylston St. A great stay. I will reconsider Sheraton. Renovated ones !

“First Rate but not very good value” As with all Peninsula's Michael Kadoorie, the obsessive owner, has made this a first rate experience. I found it expensive, despite getting an excellent corporate rate, and the rooms rather small - akin to a london hotel really. I found the room a bit "fussy" also. Fantastic location and service as to be expected. If your budget stretches, streets ahead of most similarly priced competitors.

“Affordable Semi-Luxury Hotel in NYC” I took the recommendations of fellow trip advisor travelers and booked this hotel for a 1 night business stay in Nov 2008. I was not disappointed. Excellent price for the room quality and amenities. The room was very clean and the room was on the larger size for a NYC property. The hotel offers a decent complimentary continental breakfast, but wi-fi/internet access is an additional $10/day. The entrance to the hotel is a narrow hallway to the front desk, and counter space in the bathroom is limited, but again, the room was very clean, a good size, and the bed was excellent. The staff was also very helpful. The hotel is located about 1 block away from the 28th street WR train station, and located close to the Fashion Institute of NY. Overall, a very decent quality boutique hotel for about $300/night.

“Awesome Hotel in a Great Location” Just stayed here as an SPG Plat and was upgraded to a suite on the 15th floor. Was nice and spacious, with 2 full baths. The view was excellent, staff was excellent and the location is perfect! I have no complaints whatsoever, except for one, which comes with the territory of staying on Michigan Ave, and that was the $55 charge for parking a car overnight. All in all though, highly recommended and I'll be staying here again. Most favorite aspect would probably be the lack of pretentiousness that often comes with other hotels in the area. For dinner, you can walk across the street to the Cheesecake factory, and for lunch or breakfast, stop by L'APPETITO, a great little deli/bakery.

“Enjoyed the W - it's not your father's hotel!” The last couple of reviews are really off base in my opinion. This place is not for everyone - let's get that out of the way. It is hyper-modern, and yes, the rooms and hallways are painted a dark color. So what, it works! Very dramatic effect. The lobby is like a really cool movie set, and has very different feelings at night and in daytime. The guy who checked me in could not have been nicer, a really pleasant fellow who was not in the least bit snobby. The doormen and every other staff member I encountered were unfailingly pleasant and polite, always with a smile and a hello. The elevators have piped in music. The hallways are dark but not in a dangerous way. Maybe other posters are exaggerating a bit? I was upgraded to a "Spectacular View King" on a higher floor. It was a big room, with the bathroom just inside the entrance, tiled in charcoal gray. The shower was great, and the Bliss toiletries are very nice - worth bringing home. There was a big plasma, a nice sized desk and a big, comfortable backless sofa in front of the window. But the highlight for me was the bed - wow was it comfortable, even better than the Westin Heavenly Bed. You will not want to get out of bed in the morning. Best.Bed.Ever. Oh, as for the "hidden" electrical outlets, there are two behind the TV and one in the base of each nightstand lamp. So what is the issue, people? The wake up call was a live person, always a nice touch, and she was on time for the firs and follow-up and was very pleasant. Also pleasant was my server in the bar restaurant, Tara. She was very sweet and very efficient. That was nice after a long and delayed flight. Valet parking was fine, unlike other posters' experiences. Just call down from the room before you need the car. Altogether, a very nice experience. I will return when next in the Big D.

“Great babymoon weekend” We were looking for a quick getaway from Dallas for the weekend, as my wife is due in about 2 months. This hotel met our needs as a place to relax and spend some time in a nice hotel within driving distance . We booked through FHR (AMEX program), so we got an early check-in and got upgraded to a balcony room. It had a nice view of the city side, although I must say I am not very impressed with the SA skyline (is there one?). The only issue we had was they forgot about our perks for booking through AMEX and I had to stop at the front desk 3 times to make sure I got the "envelope" with our benefits. It seemed they were very overworked with all the people coming in over Memorial Day -- but they were friendly and helpful when I did talk to them. Chairs were hard to come by the pool the weekend we went, but we got lucky and snagged some chairs in the morning both days in the adult only area. I did see a lot of people looking for chairs though and felt bad they did not have enough. However, less chairs meant the adult area was relatively quiet and away from the craziness of the kids' pools (which we never went). Servers came out every 15 minutes or so the check on any orders or anything we need. The restaurants were excellent. Brannon's food was pretty good, but our server was excellent and made the meal better. Francesco's at Sunset was even better as they had a table with a perfect view of the sunset (fitting name). The food was prepared well and service was just as good. Expensive though, but I guess it's a hotel, right? Pretty much the only resort "activity" we found is the pool area. I know there was a nature hiking trail, but we did not try that. Since our goal was to relax -- I would only come back here when there are less people (offseason) and if I was planning on golfing, which I heard is amazing from the people there.

“Wonderful Stay” The rooms are nicer than any homewood I have ever seen. My family stays here every time they visit us now. There is free parking if you park in the spots at the hotel instead of the garage. It is close to a lot of great places to eat, not even a mile drive. San Marco area is close with great places to eat. The front desk will tell you where to go. Bistro AIX and La Nopalera are some of our favorites. Of note: The studio rooms are nicer than the 1 bedroom rooms. The 2 bedroom rooms are amazing!

“Great Midtown Hotel” This was my second stay at this hotel this year. Came to town just after superstorm Sandy. This was no typical time in NYC. Staff was wonderful and managed to accomodate those of us traveling while providing shelter to many of New York's own who had no power or worse. This is a huge hotel, however, I always felt the service was personalized. I was somewhat disappointed that the Executive Lounge was no longer on the 44th floor, however, was pleasantly surprised that the quality of the lounge was just as good albeit without the view. Found the staff to be kid friendly as we were traveling with our three children. Location is perfect and almost everything you will want to do is walkable. We will most definitely return and once again I cannot compliment the staff enough!

“Good price and location, but room size is laughable” My husband and I were arriving late and only staying one night so we figured the bunk rooms would be fine, plus we stay in private rooms in hostels a lot when in Europe. They were impossibly small, smaller than I expected. The problem is not just that they are small, but they could've done a better job with using the space. There was a tiny shelf above the door which was about 8 inches deep. The shelves could have been bigger to store luggage, because if you travel with more than a purse, you have to put the luggage on the floor. There were hooks along the mirror to hang things though. There were TV in each bunk, for the top bunk, that space could've been used for luggage. If you have back problems to do not take the top bunk b/c the mattress is thin and you can feel the boards. The rooms and hall are carpeted and the hall reeked of stale cigarettes, prob from pre-smoking ban days. Allergy suffers beware. So why a 3 star and not a 2? well, the location is great. The bar is beautiful. And the price for NY is decent. However, with priceline, you can pay $10 more and get a real room with bathrooms.

“Why the hype?” Pros: Good location with entrances on both sides of the hotel and located across the street from a Starbucks. Plenty of restaurants and Central Park within walking distance. Service was good helping me resolve billing issues. Beds and noise level were fine as well. Cons: To turn down the blinds in the room we had to jump on the desk to reach the cord. Don't move anything in the mini bar or they will charge you. The burger place downstairs was overhyped as well. Pricey and bland. My husband and I made a joke that they were happy meals. They accept cash only, no credit cards. Overall it's ok. Nothing that was horrible but nothing that was awesome either. I'd like to check out other hotels in NYC when I return.

“Large room, good location. Decor is...” Large room, good location. Decor is bland. Checked in late and bedding was dirty and stained so had to sleep on it until the next day. Front desk could not change a $50 bill.

“Loud, but convenient” I have stayed in all types of NYC hotels from high end luxury to budget basic. This hotel is a nice surprise. I stayed 5 nights during a recent business trip and found the hotel to be perfectly suitable for what I needed. First the pluses--the location can't be beat. Easy walk to Herald Square for those who love to shop, great neighborhood walking for those who like that, and quick in/out to either LGA or EWR. Several subway stops are accessible within a couple of blocks with 6th Avenue close by for cabs uptown and 7th Ave to go downtown. Whole Foods 1 block away makes up for the lack of good deli take-away on the street, but 7th Avenue has plenty of other good restaurants. I did not try the hotel restaurant but the roof top area was quite nice. The front desk staff was terrific. I had an issue with the reservation reflecting the wrong room rate and it was handled on the spot to my satisfaction. They do have luggage hold and I appreciated the security at the elevator banks making sure nobody without a room key was going up. In the guest rooms the beds are comfortable and clean and the bathroom is spacious enough to actually have a counter--often hard to find in a NYC hotel room. The shower had good pressure, the towels were thick, and everything was clean and modern. The desk area provided plenty of power access and enough surface space to make up for not having a separate dresser. There are drawers in the desk for people like me who are staying several days. End tables on both sides of the bed also had power outlets--great for charging a phone overnight and still using it as an alarm. Heat/Air in the room was reliable and efficient. The closet is small, but adequate and there is an in-room safe--a must for any NYC hotel I stay in. The CONS: Construction on the restaurant meant my 4th floor room was very loud well into the wee hours of the night. One night off-loading of scaffolding lasted until about 4 am. This was incredibly disruptive. I strongly encourage a high floor room. The room does not have a microwave or mini-fridge, which for short-stays is probably not a big deal but it would have been nice to have as I don't eat out every meal. The nearby Hilton Garden Inn does have these things and having stayed there as well for an equally long trip it gets my vote over this hotel. The decor is not my taste. Very dark and metallic. That doesn't impact anything other than personal preference. I would recommend this hotel for anyone who is traveling to NYC for business or pleasure.

“Best Stay in a Long Time” I had been placed in a poor property before moving to this locale, adn was hesitant. The property is is a very "office area" locale, difficult to navigate or understand at night. This is the onl negative about this property. It is actually very close to Fajitas andOutback, less thn a mile from ajor shopping, etc I had a 3 room suite, a nice small apartment with a full size kitchen and living room area. The bed was "newish" and had a selection of pillows. The "water closet" room of bathroom could not be occupied without a loud fan, but somethings you d not need light for!. The front desk staff was eaer to help, and filiar with area allowing for great suggestions. The breakfast areawas above standard,with fare such as omelets, sausage and bacon, the usual cold offerings.In the evenings, the reception from 5-7 was a complete meal, not happy hour snacks. There is a small conveniene store in lobbby area. Daily housekeeping is provideded, something usually not offered in the "apartmen/long term" stay hotels. A great stay and will be back. Was pleasantly suprised when I was given bill, as this place could charge more and get away with it. Another great Hilton property!!!
“Disappointing” Paper thin walls. Very careless housekeeping; dirty dishes multiple times in the restuarant. Very low performance for a Hyatt. Very high room service prices.

“Convenient location” This is the 2nd time we've stayed at this hotel - this time we were on our honeymoon. Again, we were completely satisfied with our stay. The hotel is clean and the staff were friendly and helpful. We stayed for a week and purchased a 7 day Metro card for the Subway... it was so easy to get around Manhattan with the ACE line right out the front door and other Subway lines an easy walk away. Easy walk to Chinatown and some delicious restaurants. I would not hesistate to stay here again when in New York and definitely recommend this hotel. In fact we recommended this hotel to others - they didn't stay there and were disappointed with their other hotel in the area! Free wifi too!

“Outstanding Customer Service” We checked in early and they were able to find us a room. We had trouble with the wifi and they were on that too. We went out to eat and brought back leftovers and they provided us with a fridge and microwave. When our cruise was delayed today and we requested late check out, they have us until 3pm. The beds were comfy. Easy access to highways. If there is a sporting event traffic can get a little rough but that isn't the hotel's issue. Parking is $19. No free Wi-Fi. Overall, outstanding customer service.

“Gorgerous property with very poor services” I picked W Boston and The Liberty Hotel during my recent trip to Boston since I want to experience both design hotels while The Liberty hotel is certainly the winner at the design and comfort but the level of service is light years behind. Location is ideal for tourist since it is right across from the Metro station. Being as a formal jail, the property owner successfully restored the jail into a beautiful artwork. As you walk into the hotel onto the atrium lobby, you will be stunned how beautiful it is. No hotels nowadays have such a GRAND lobby like The Liberty. Even if you don't stay here, you should come in for a drink or tour. Situated by the river makes the hotel have some rooms with awesome river view and luckily the suite that I stayed at included even better view being on the corner location and the view is spectacular day and night. Rooms are plush and tastefully decorated while still comfortable. I love the high quality MOLTON BROWN product that they use in room. Their sheets and towels are better than average hotels, which is totally in-line with the luxury hotels name. The only issue that I had was the housekeeping. Turn-down service was one of the worst I have seem in years. Whomever turned down my room just leave towels wherever she wants, hang the wet towels on the shower door and it was just bad. I called the housekeeping supervisor over and she was trying to convince me that they did they because I hang my towels etc. Wrong. I stayed at hotels few hundred nights already and I know how it should work. It was just bad. She did the turn down again but however, no followup recovery service was done. I wonder if this ever reached to the in house duty manager? The service that I received at this property was quite SPOTTY. I have had good Concierges the day that I checked in and yet I had ones who just kept talking on his phone for personal purposes while flipping through his cell phone at work. Front desk agents ranges widely too. There is a classic gentlement who seems eager to help and offered guests welcome drinks without asking while others just try to hand you the key card and send you out of your way (which was the check in agent that I received). I have seem quite a few negative reviews before on tripadvisor, mile points, flyertalk and yelp before my stay and I now do believe that some of the negative reviews are indeed true since I have experienced personally. The property is beautiful but the level of services demonstrated by the front desk staff, concierges, and housekeeping teams makes me wonder when will the management team take some serious effort to re-train some of the staffs to provide a more uniform, courteous, professional services to their guests to claim themselves as a five stars property?

“Decent Doubletree” Front desk staff was very welcoming upon arrival to the hotel, and our check in process was efficient. The lobby is very large with a great amount of leisure seating, so a good gathering space for groups. The room itself was fine - comfortable and clean...my two top priorities. The bathroom was a bit small. We were at the end of a hallway on an upper floor, so a bit surprised to hear kids (?) running in the corridors. Surface parking lot with security present. The Doubletree in downtown Detroit offers larger rooms, but this property appears to better kept (based on my room to room comparison in recent stays). Another plus is the number of restaurants nearby, a mall, and best yet - The Henry Ford Museum and Greenfield Village!

“Excellent hotel for the price -- great value” The bottom line: I have stayed in a few dumps in NYC, and this hotel is NOT a dump. Yes, the rooms are very small like in most New York hotels. The renovations a few years ago were kind of slapdash in some ways with too much caulking around the sinks, etc. But to be fair, this is not a "boutique" hotel costing $350/night. It's a budget hotel in an old building. The lobby area has a lively bar and a nice little lounge with free coffee and tea and an internet terminal (charge applies). During my two visits (Sept. 2005 and March 2006) I have found the front desk staff to be professional and polite. Speaking of which, I traveled this time with a colleague who was given a ground-floor room. She heard a lot of noise from the lobby and from the smoking terrace behind the hotel, so I would avoid a ground-floor room. The furniture and bed linens look just like the photos on the hotel's website. The beds are very comfy and clean. I stayed once in a room facing 50th St. and once in the back of the hotel. I slept like a baby in the back room, though I got a lot of street noise in the front room (mostly drowned out by running the window a/c unit). The neighborhood is safe. There are delis and a subway stop just footsteps away, and you can walk to the heart of Times Square in about 2 minutes. I had a rental car for my business trip and paid $35/night to park across the street at a theatre's underground garage. Shocking? Yes, but that's the going rate for garage parking in midtown Manhattan. If you're traveling with kids, just be aware that there is an "adult novelty" shop on the same block. Frankly that is part of the history of the Times Square area, a holdover from the old seedy days before Disney came to the neighborhood. But the store is fairly low-key and you can't see much from the sidewalk. Overall this is a pleasant place to stay. I not only recommend it -- I was happy to return six months after my first stay. The Amsterdam Court ain't the Pierre or the Waldorf-Astoria, but it costs a fraction of what those hotels cost.

“Contemporary Ritz” This is a very nice Ritz, which is pretty conservative and not overly luxurious – more contemporary than most. The rooms are a good size with comfortable beds, nice work desk and marble baths with separate showers. The main restaurant is good, although very casual for a Ritz. The location is close to Boston Commons, not really close to the major tourist or business areas, although Boston is small and easy to take a cab anywhere. I found the service to be good, but not as friendly as usual.

“a nice hotel on the edge of the gaslamp” We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights for a family vacation. The hotel really stepped up and honored an internet rate package that offered via Hilton.com in error ($99/night + free parking +$35/night hotel credit to be used in anyway we liked!). The breakfast buffet is great - kids ate free with adult purchase, I highly recommend. The rooms were comfortable enough and staff was friendly. You have to walk across a bridge over the road to get to the Gaslamp, trolley, or really anything, but that was a minor inconvenience.

“Acceptably Nice” Stayed at the Williard a couple of times during the Summer season of 2011. It is one of the Intercontinental hotels that do not honor the suite upgrade policy of the Royal Ambassador program; they did not even bother to try to find a room with a view of the Washington Monument at my request. Fortunately, the free minibar program privileges were still intact. The bathrooms in the rooms are spacious and I like the white hue of the stone cladding in the bathrooms. The first time I stayed there, there was a dirty wet wash cloth sitting on the side of the bathtub. The following time I stayed, the desk surface was unnaturally sticky. And on the first night of each stay, holes in the linens were spotted on prominently visible parts of the bedding – this was particular shocking, as it was not a lone incident and this hotel supposedly keeps to very high standards. We also experienced reception problem with the television stations and in-room pay movies on each stay – which was annoying. The location is convenient and the building beautiful, but this Summer, I would probably give the hotels on either side of the Williard (JW Marriott or the W Hotel) a try for comparison.

“Good Location” Second visit to NYC & chose this Hampton Inn. Very well located, easy walking distance to pretty much everywhere (30 minute walk to Soho, 10 minutes to Times Square) & lots of eating options nearby. Small room, but that's to be expected, was clean & quiet, except the pillows were fairly awful. Breakfast was ok, nothing to write home about, cookies & lemonade in the afternoons was a nice touch. The lift was very slow at times which could be frustrating. The front desk staff were really helpful & friendly. Would probably stay here again

“Another Great Stay” Stayed here for the first time two Christmasses ago. Had a wonderful time. Back again, this time with our 17 year old daughter and we appreciated the Doubletree even more. This time, our mission was to shop for a prom dress and the Doubletree's location makes it easy to visit all the major department stores in NYC. We didn't have to take a cab even one time during our shopping expeditions. Highly recommend the Crumbs bakery (down the street a bit from the hotel) for breakfast or a late snack. Also, even if you don't have a teenager with you, you should go into the Forever 21 store that's just a few steps away. It's four or five floors of amazement! As always if you are going to see anything on Broadway, this hotel is close to all of the theatres and it really is an excellent choice.

“Great location” My husband and I stayed at The Standard Hotel for a few days. We live only 40 minutes out of the city, but now the best way to really enjoy and area is to stay there. We were able to walk to so many great places to shop, or window shop in the Meatpacking District. Your only blocks from the Chelsea Market, a block long, indoor, shopping mecca for all gourmet foods, wines, candy, oils, and more. A great place to grab a lunch, or an afternoon snack. The High Line is right below the hotel and offers a great walk with a beautiful view. We rented bicycles from the hotel for $10 for the day. We peddled down the The World Trade Center area, the turned around and rode to the bottom of the George Washington Bridge, all on a newly constructed path. As you ride, you have the Hudson River the entire way, and the occasional restaurant where you can park, grab a bite, and continue on. Great thing to do, and great hotel too stay in. Beautifully appointed, European feel, get a corner room and you will never want to leave the room and its amazing view!

“The best service I've ever seen in a NYC hotel!” This was a perfect option for me and my friend, visiting friends in NYC. It was located centrally, but not annoyingly touristy like Times Square. The front desk staff was exceptional! I even felt like the room service order taker really felt bad when I asked him if he had any aspirin because I had a headache. The deluxe studio room I had was actually on the moderately big side, compared to other hotels, like the W up the street, which is TINY. We also had a microwave and empty fridge, in addition to the minibar! Clean room and nice toiletries, although it wasn't a brand I recognized. Beds were so comfortable and they had like 12 different choices of pillows! I can't believe I didn't know about this hotel before. I booked on Hotwire and got a great deal for my money. I'm recommending it to all my friends now.

“Loved It!!” We spent the weekend here to do some sightseeing in Center City. The hotel itself is super cool- the round rooms and unique layout only add to the charm. The view from the balcony and the bedroom was great- it overlooked the museums and the BFPKWY. The bedroom was seperated from the general living area, which was nice- gave it a very homey feel. The kitchette had a mini fridge and microwave, and there was even a sink. The bed was wasn't too bad- luckily we had our own pillows because there were only feather pillows. The only real issue I had was the bathroom door- it didnt close completely- very awkward!! The location was perfect- centrally located- close to the museums, CityHall, Chinatown, historical sites, Reading Terminal, and loads of bars and restaurants! Overall, I would certainly go back and I would recommend it to friends.
“Cannot say enough about this hotel. It is wonderful” Stunning rooms, location, views, service, food and experience. Cannot wait to go back!!

“Large rooms, great location... so-so service.” I've stayed here a few times over the past couple years. I really like the Columbus Westin Hotel, but I try to stay as loyal as I can to the Hilton brand. This hotel is in a perfect location for seeing the nightlife or catching a Blue Jackets game. And the rooms are a very generous size. Finally, the breakfast was better than expected and the server was an absolute delight. So, for the most part, this hotel is draped with positives. I do, however, have a few gripes. - as a Hilton gold member, it would be nice to be occasionally upgraded when the hotel has an open room... higher floor, better view, larger suite, etc. Hilton and Hilton Garden Inn almost always upgrade me if they have availability. It's one of the reasons I stick with them and have let my Marriot and Starwood accounts dwindle recently. - I ordered $60+ of room service 'snacks' during my last stay. The food took an hour to arrive and was mediocre at best. The steak sandwich was not only cold, but was priced at $22 on the bill even though the room service menu listed it at $14. After tipping the room service attendant an extra ten dollars (on top of the included gratuity), I was even more disappointed by the lackluster dishes. The front desk was nice enough to remove the steak sandwich from the bill, but I thought they probably should have done a little more. Other than that, the hotel is a great choice for Columbus. In fact, I'm going to be staying there again next weekend, so the positives apparently outweigh the negatives for me. I'll just avoid the room service this time around.

“Surly Staff - Noisy Room” Very disappointed with this recently renovated hotel. At check in - 4pm - our room was not ready (!?!) so we were given an upgraded room - next to the elevator. Got very little sleep. Staff - with the exception to the concierge - were very aloof and argumentative. There are plenty of hotels in this city that will appreciate your business more than this hotel - we will not be returning.

“Don't let the outside fool you - great Hampton Inn” I booked the Hampton Inn when the Hilton Garden Inn up the Street was full. Although, I've stayed at many properties along this stretch of I-10 and like Hamptons in general, I've never chosen this Hampton because the property looks a bit old. This hotel was absolutely perfect for me. It's very clean inside from the lobbies to the rooms. The staff was friendly. The decor is contemporary throughout. They have a nice business center. I so appreciated the scanner - most hotels do not have one. The fitness center is adequate - not the best equipment, but I used it and was satisfied. The breakfast was good, as all Hamptons provide a decent buffet. The room itself was very comfortable. Great layout, lots of outlets in the right places, AND thank you for having a decent hair dryer 1875 watts instread of the typical dinky 1500 watt. I will definitely stay again.

“Love this historic hotel” My husband surprised me with a weekend in Philly at this boutique hotel. It was our first time there, but we absolutely loved it. The room was huge with a big bathroom complete with tub and shower, kitchen, living room and bedroom. The bed was very comfortable and we enjoyed our stay. All of the staff we dealt with was very friendly and helpful. Based on previous reviews, we didn't waste our time with the breakfast so I can't speak to that, but we did enjoy the cookies the couple of nights we were there which were very fresh and delicious. Also, the location is close enough to all the action of center city but also in a quiet neighborhood which is a nice balance. I definitely will be returning to the Morris House.

“Expected more. No attention to detail and more bed bug comments” I have stayed in other holiday inn's before so I was concerned about the reviews posted. The bed bug comments are all true. A group of us had 3 to 4 rooms where we found bed bugs. After discussions with the hotel, they offered to wash the clothes and luggage and offered other rooms. However if we would have stayed quiet, nothing would have happened. No initiative from the hotel regarding bed bugs. Time for a deep cleaning of all rooms. My room was fairly cleaned everyday, but for some reason the bathroom was never "detailed" cleaned. If the bathtub was cleaned. Then then soap dish was not or the uses bottles of shampoo were left where I left them. Sometimes I only had two shampoos and one conditioner. The front desk staff was completely average. No smiles or worked at their own pace. The shuttle service was slow. They needed more drivers or altered their schedules to accommodate the high demanded hours and service, especially to the airport. I don't know I think I was expecting more. The location and sizes of the room were good. The complimentary service to the mall and Walmart were greatly appreciated. Coin laundry was great. The restaurant "good eats" had better staff service. The housekeeping dept always greeted guests in the hallway ( that is nice). If I had to come back again, it will have to be because my company is paying for it. I am concerned of the bed bug situation and by the multiple comments, it probably won't stop until the hotel takes care of it

“There are better places” Recently had a one-night stay here, courtesy of Priceline. Was not very impressed. Room was tiny, but in good condition. Desk lamp (one of only 2 light sources in main part of room) was burned out. TV remote did not work. Nice clock radio/CD player (much better than typical hotel's), but a little difficult to figure out. No high-speed internet. Worst problem was that sink had not been cleaned from previous guest; contained dry toothpaste and hair. Ick.

“Nicer than a lot of hotels in this city but don't expect the regular fancy doubletree” I stayed here with a group of friends for a big party my family was throwing nearby on New Years eve. I have to say that it's okay, restful, clean but it's an old hotel that they renovated, gutted out etc so it still has the quirks and layout of an older property. It's not bad and decent little bar downstairs but it's not the nicer luxury type of Doubletree so make sure you lower your expectations. The people are friendly and helpful. The chocolate chip cookies are delicious at check in!

“Great accomodations, location and value. Service could use improvements.” I stayed for 5 nights at this hotel for the first time and it was great. The room is very spacious for NYC standards. This was my 2nd trip to NYC in 6 months. I booked the studio suite with 2 beds and it was more than enough for me and my 2 cousins. The kitchen comes in very handy and very functional for storing food. The bathroom is big and clean. Hot water goes in and out at times but not a problem and water pressure was good. I have nothing bad to say about this hotel. It's a great find. It's very close to Penn Station and Macy's, within walking distance to Times Square. A lot of restaurants nearby as well as banks and Duane Reade. Everything was within reach from this hotel. The only interesting thing that I find about this hotel is that when I checked in, I didnt even have to sign for anything. I already know how much the entire stay would cost so I had a certain amount of money to cover the cost of stay. However the front desk did not inform me that incidental charges would be added on top of that. I will admit that I've traveled a lot and stayed at a lot of hotels and incidental charges is not new to me. But dont u think it would have been nice if the front desk could inform u about that kind of thing, especially when it comes to money? Long story short I found out that my account went over the limit when incidental charges were added on top of the certain amount of money that left in my account for the total cost of stay only. As u can imagine, this created a lot of problem with the bank. Who would want to pay for overdraft fees, right? So I went down to front desk and told them about the situation and they called the bank to release all the charges that were made to my account. After that I gave them another card for incidental charges. Problem solved, right? Yes, for a few days. The day before I checked out I checked my account and saw that they have taken the money out for my entire stayed which was expected but then I was surprised to see that they still have incidental charges on hold on that same card, and I thought to myself, didnt i give them another card to cover the incidental charges? Now my account is overdrawn again? So i basically gave up talking to them about this and went to Wachovia to take my money out of my Wells Fargo account to cover the amount being held for incidental charges because my Chase account gets charged for overdraft fee. So all in all I never get charged for overdraft fee, but this problem could have been avoided if the front desk could have informed or asked me a few questions before they charged my card right? Every hotels that I have stayed, they show u the total cost of ur stay and have u sign on the dotted line signifying that ur agreed to pay the amount shown on the receipt, but this wasnt the case with Affinia Dumont. Long story short, they ended up putting a hold for incidental charges on 2 cards that I gave them. If you dont run into the same problem I did, you will have a great stay all around and I'm planning on returning to this hotel on my next trip.

“Yo Yo Yo, Check This Place Out.....” Let me first tell you that I would never knowingly book a place like this. The uber-hip, trendy, vibe-y hotels like this are usually big on style, and short on substance. I definitely prefer a more traditional hotel experience. However, I ended up booking here thru a blind site, and was immediately disappointed when I received the confirmation and saw what I got. With that being said, this hotel far exceeded my expectations, and I must say that not only did I enjoy it, I admired it! Most New York modern hotels are heavy on the black and dark color tones. This place is bright, and white, and it's also immaculately clean. You check in on the ground floor, thru an automated kiosk. This is the fastest check in I have ever had in an NYC hotel. From walking thru the front door to my room in about 2 minutes! It was also during a peak check in time of 7pm. You go up to the 4th floor ( which is called Mission Control) and then catch another elevator up to your room floor. All of the social action is on the 4th floor: the Outdoor space, bar, restaurant, and gym. The rooms are tiny, but very well laid out and with high ceilings so they don't feel claustrophobic. The bed is actually a couch, but folds out to a bed with one button. The bathroom has all high quality soaps and comfy towels.The only beef here is the lack of privacy in the business part of the bathroom. There is merely a curtain which separates your sounds and smells from whoever might be on the receiving end in the adjoining bedroom. Overall, the rooms are very comfortable, and very laid out. I will warn you that the location is off the beaten path and there is not much around the hotel. You are definitley not in the action, or that close to it if you stay here. You will get a very comfy and cozy experience if you do stay here, and Yo, if you're not that hip like me, it might help to make you one cool dude!

“Fantasic stay” Overall fantastic experience. I arrived at 10:30 in the morning and received great service from the first hello. The front desk staff was very cordial and found a room for me. The room was very nice and well appointed. Bed was very comfortable. Sean at the Concierge desk was very helpful on two fronts: dinner reservation and getting me an appointment with a fantastic barber. Overall nothing but positives. Looking forward to my next visit.

“Pretty good bargain hotel” We stayed on the top (6th) floor, with a window facing the Bay. Thus our room was quiet, day and night. The room was clean and the price was right for a ten day stay in this expensive town. We chose it for price and location (near our family at Liberty Station). Underground parking was a nice touch. Gripes: The light over the bathroom mirror didn't work and could not be fixed. The breakfast is the worst I've encountered in my travels - even the fresh baked waffles came out like rubbery wonder bread. The bar on the first floor does not attract the high society crowd - it is very noisy. The desk staff is often absent, though they are helpful when they are there. I guess you get what you pay for.

“enjoyable stay” We stayed here for four nights at the beginning of february. We got a good deal online prior to our arrival. Check in was nice and quick. Our room was a nice size, especially by NY standards. Breakfast and wine/cheese in the evenings was great to have at the hotel. It's our third hotel that we have stayed in from the hotel chain and overall we enjoyed our stay however we will return to the hotel library again for our next stay. We found that the staff were friendlier there and we prefer the more modern decor at the library hotel. If you get a good rate online though I'd definitely recommend staying here as the location is great and the Monkey bar is great to go to for a cocktail before heading out for the night.

“Convenient, but bring the earplugs” Stayed here recently while on business. Because it is located between highways it is fairly convenient if you need to drive in various parts of Houston. However, you will hear highway noise anytime you in your room.Bathrooms could use some updating. The staff was friendly and the bed comfortable, but they should offer earplugs at bedside.

“Pretty Average Kimpton Property” First let me say I love Kimpton hotels. They have an amazing hospitality program that includes free happy hours, free Wifi, and even mini-bar privileges. Every Kimpton is unique in it's style and a fresh change from boring hotels. That said, this particular Kimpton felt pretty mediocre. When I pulled my car in, I was struggling with all of my stuff and no one offered to help me (there was no one out front so it's possible they just didn't see me). Normally I always take my own stuff to my room but this is one time I might have actually let the bell hop do it, however no one even offered this (despite the fact that I put my clothes and bag on the bellhop cart...). The room was not super clean (I found a hair berret next to my bed on check-in) and they took my soap after the first night without replacing it. I understand they are going green but having pump soap dispensers in the shower (instead of the typical small one use bottles) felt a little ghetto. The property itself is in a great location and I got a great price for a popular time of year in DC. The Helix sent me an itinerary of things to do in my stay (live like a local) which was cool, and even emailed me during my stay to see if they could help in any way (I don't like to complain, I just like things to be right). Overall, again I can't say enough about the perks around Kimpton, and there is nothing better then someone handing you a glass of free sparkling wine after a hard day of work, but this particular Kimpton could use a few tweaks to make it better.

“Nice Hotel” Very much enjoyed this hotel. A few things to point out. The rooms are small - but like most large city hotels. The rooms though are very well appointed and have many amenities. This hotel is great for buisness travelers or singles - not for families and more than 2 people in a room. The decor is very contemporary, is new and comfortable. In fact, immaculate! The hotel offers many extras like free bottled water (as much as you wish), free wireless or wired internet, and several other nice amenities. The location cannot be beat. You may not have a great view, but I found the hotel to be very quiet. I would definately recommend this hotel!

“Needs some updating” I stayed at the Hiton for one night for business. The hotel was easy to get to as they have a complimentary shuttle from the airport. It runs every 20 minutes or so and is only about a 5 minute ride between the hotel and airport. The downside is that the room needs some upgrading to the door locks. I just was not comfortable with the flimsy locks. There was an adjoining door to the other room and I was never quite sure if the deadbolt was latched or not because when I tried the door to open it, the whole knob just swung around in the hole. The main door to the room wasn't much better. The room included an iron and ironing board, no blowdryer and free broadband internet access. Overall, the price is a tad much for what you are getting. I would recommend looking at some of the other hotels in the area for a quick hotel stay near the airport.

“Enjoyed it” We spent 6 nights at this hotel with my parents and my husband's parents. All of us really liked the hotel. We had standard rooms and although they were a bit of on the small side they were absolutely fine. The best part of the hotel is the location, perfect distance to Central Park and Times Square!

“Stay was SUITE!!!” Excellent location, top notch service, then add in the suite upgrade and I cant say enough about the US Grant. As a Starwood Platinum member, I ususally get upgraded but this time the Presientail suite made it that much better. I have stayed here many times and also around the corner at the Westin Gaslamp. I prefer this hotel as it is much more personable, the management and personnnel are freindlier and more helpful. I will always stay here when doing business in San Diego.

“Very Decent Hotel” This is a fine hotel. Location is excellent not too far from Gaslamp and convention center. Staff is professional and friendly. Restaurant and bar are nicely priced and the food is very good. Rooms are spacious, clean and very confortable. Keep in mind this hotel is new, so everything is still shiny. Internet connection is NOT free! My room had a nice view. The hotel overlooks the water and does have a nice swimming pool but no access to the bay..

“Well Located/Great Staff/Very Nice Room” Stayed during a business trip to San Fransisco and was very pleased as it suited my needs perfectly. Located in the financial district and walking distance to many attractions. Staff was excellent and the room was very comfortable and clean. Only negative was that there was not a restaraunt on site for breakfast but many others within walking distance. I would stay again for a business trip but if with my wife may try something different.

“Pleasant surprises abound” I needed a spot for an overnight layover and chose the Hilton at O'Hare for various logistical reasons. I expected a hotel that was long of tooth and possibly noisy due to its proximity to the airport, but I got none of that. The room I was given appeared to have been recently updated and at no time did I ever hear a plane engine. The staff was courteous and there were several restaurant options within the hotel property. (In this regard bear in mind you're kind of a captive audience so food and drink are a bit spendy, although it's nothing that will shock experienced travelers.) The train station is very close to the hotel entry, so a cheap trip to downtown Chicago is right at your fingertips. I enjoyed my stay here thoroughly.

“Perfectly Serviceable in Uptown Charlotte” Having stayed in most of the Uptown properties in the past, I expected more of the same at the Omni while staying there for a wedding weekend. While they throw around the word "luxury" on their website, I was expecting and received a nice but not outstanding room... Ceilings are a bit low, but everything was clean and in good repair. I had booked a "premiere executive king room" for the larger square footage, but because of the odd shape of the building, the room didn't feel that much more spacious. Additionally, all of the rooms in this category are close to the elevator, and as I prefer quiet, I would NOT choose the same room again. Now, the bad: the hotel had been booked for the weekend by a college fraternity for their "formal"--in addition to drunk college kids in the lobby and elevators, they came up to their rooms (so glad to be by the elevator!) VERY late and VERY loud. I thought the commotion had ended by 2:30, but was sadly awakened again as someone was violently ill in the room next door. Charming! That said, normal activity in an adjoining room would probably have gone unnoticed. Guests talking as they passed the room in the corridor would be overheard from within guest rooms. The good: the bride had wisely advised everyone to join Omni's loyalty program before booking... Select Guest gives you free wifi, evening turndown, complimentary shoe shine, complimentary pressing of two items, and ... my favorite! Morning beverage service--two beverages per guest delivered to your room. We of course grabbed some pastries as well, but this service made the stay leagues ahead of the Hilton and compensated for a more dated property compared to the Westin. Of course, for me, a pot of hot chocolate and a croissant IS breakfast, so I may be biased! Most impressively, they were always ON TIME, which is rare with hotel room service... All in all, I'd stay I'd stay there hands down over the Hilton. I love the Westin, but... if there was a large price discrepancy, I'd probably stay at the Omni, particularly as it's location adjacent to the Epicenter makes it much more walkable.

“Call ahead if you need to check in before 4 pm” I was wondering why this hotel is ranked #21 out of 189 hotels in Dallas. There is nothing special about this hotel but the employees are highly motivated and professional. My hotel saty was pleasant, the bed was comfy and the shuttle service prompt. Looking at other reviews on here,it is true that the elevators have a mold issue. The odor was so strong that I could not wait to get to my floor. There is also an issue with the check in. I arrived at 3:30 p.m. and the cleaning lady just finished up in my room. My wait was minimal but I was a bit surrpised that the front desk could not assign another room, especially since I enjoy Hilton Diamond Status. I strongly recommend that you call the hotel if you plan on checkin in before 4 p.m.

“Clean, Safe, and Pleasant” I picked this hotel on a recommendation, and I'm sure glad I did! Walking distance from a shopping center with some quick and easy restaurants and very safe area. The courtyard was very pretty and pleasant. It was a comfortable and nice room. The breakfast was also good and very convenient. It's on the outskirts of the "Los Angeles" area (in San Fernando Valley) so it's less expensive, less noisy, and safer. I was very pleased with this hotel and I would definitely be back!

“Il mio motto: "non puoi dire di essere stato a NY se non sei stato almeno una volta al Chelsea Hotel"” Ho soggiornato al Chelsea con un'amica. La nostra stanza era la 402, di certo fascinosa, ma per niente in ordine... tutto il quella stanza, dalla moquette, ai letti, al bagno aveva sapore "antico" e durante la notte siamo certe di aver sentito il respiro di "qualcuno" provenire dal termosifone... un fantasma? suggestione sicuramente, ma le numerose storie accadute in quelle stanze (es. l'omicidio della fidanzata di Sid Vicius dei Sex Pistols per mano sua) hanno fatto del Chelsea un albergo dal fascino unico.. dappertutto ci sono opere degli artisti che vi hanno soggiornato... Certamento non è un albergo economico, soprattutto per i servizi che offre, ma per me quei soldi li vale tutti. Unico! Strepitoso! Dal fascino indescrivibile!

“Wretching experience with room service food!!!” My husband and I stayed at the Raddison on an overnight layover the night of June 29th 2005. We got the property for a $53 Priceline bid. The shuttle service to and from the airport was great and the rooms were pretty with a great view. However, because of the soundproofing on the windows there was no air circulation and our air conditioner kept freezing up and turning itself off so that the room would become hot and stuffy. The food situation was the absolute worst! There is not a single vending machine onsite to get a little snack, so having arrived at midnight we were completely dependant on room service. We ordered up some steak and eggs for $21.50 a plate and when they finally arrived about 45 minutes later (Thank God Taxicab Confessions was on TV to help pass the time!) the food was cold and pathetic, with burnt fried eggs topping teeny tiny dry looking steaks, sans the promised breakfast potatoes. We called up to inquire about the potatoes, and they simply said they were out and there would be no substitutions., We told them we wanted to send the steaks back and order something else and they agreed, so we got 2 pasta primaveras, which was so foul tasting my husband didn't eat his. About 2 hours later I began to get sick and had to fly back from LA to Denver with, without going into sickening detail, what I suspect was a fairly raging case of food poisoning which has lasted 2 days. To add injury to insult, we were charged the prices for the original meals, which were almost twice as much, and the front desk refused to give us a breakdown of the food bill so we could see what we were actually being charged for!!! We will NEVER stay at this property again!

“Hôtel design et fonctionnel, bien placé !” Hôtel tout neuf, encore en travaux en partie mais ça ne gêne en rien. Les chambres sont vraiment petites mais fonctionnelles, tout est optimisé au maximum pour gagner en espace. Les lits sont très confortables et bien grands. Bien placé pour découvrir la ville, l'hôtel est à 2 minutes de Grand Central (lignes verte, mauve et shuttle). Personnel très aimable et serviable. Petit déjeuner gratuit servi dans le hall chaque matin ! Quelques points négatifs : - Certaines chambres sont très bruyantes, on entend fort la climatisation de l'hôtel dans le plafond ou la climatisation qui est sur le toit de l'immeuble voisin. N'hésitez pas à demander une autre chambre, le personnel a l'air de savoir que certaines chambres sont pires que d'autres. Si vous le demandez, aucun problème pour avoir une autre chambre. - Dans certaines chambres, il y a une fenêtre dans la salle de bain mais pas de stores, donc impossible de faire le noir complet. Un petit détail à améliorer...

“Gorgeous” We stayed here over Christmas and New Year 2010/2011. This hotel is beautiful. The rooms are lush (if you are able to get a room that is not in-facing that is). The staff were great and nothing was too big or too small. We didnt find any attitude or snottiness from any staff member - it was all great! Don't miss out on the restaurant downstairs - especially for brunch!

“Boutique Hotel...” If you are used to the amenities and styles of the larger franchise hotels then I'd not recomment this for you. If you are not into the chain hotels then definitely worth a stay. Pros: Right in the heart of the Gaslamp District; easy walk to more food and entertainment than can be described in a book! If you can't find it, it doesn't exist! Friendly staff and good restaurant Fireplaces in rooms a nice touch Cons: No coffee maker Tiny (versus full size) ironing board Nightclub across the street will definitely be heard if a band is playing late hence my "poor" rating for sleep quality

“10 anniversary - great place to stay!!” Hubby & I stayed here for 3 nights. We were placed on the 20th floor, in a corner room with windows facing West & South....what amazing views!! The room was spacious and incredibly clean. In fact - I place on calling the hotel in the AM to give kuddos to the housekeeper for our room. Was there noise? yes....you are in a city...in a hotel. When a firetruck goes by our neighborhood at home, I hear it. When the kids take a shower upstairs....I hear it. Why people think that you wont hear that here is beyond me. One night we slept with the vents under the window open but did need to shut them as it made a huge difference in noise. We also chose to keep the fan on (the fan on the a/c controls) to help drown out the street noise. We slept great all 3 nights. The only downside was the concierge that was on duty on Fri. night. We stopped by to talk to him twice - he was the least helpful person we met in SF. The concierges in general seemed to assume that "everyone knows how to use public transportation". Thats not always the case - hubby and I come from a large city - that has NO form of public transportation....trying to find a bus/street car in crazy Union Square during rush hour, is a daunting task. A little guidance - or even a step-by-step how to guide would be incredibly helpful. We spent 4 great days here - we stayed out of the "touristy" traps and really SAW SF. What an amazing city. If anyone is looking for any casual, easy, fun ideas for a 30+yo in SF...hit me up! I'd love to share what we did..

“Underrated Hotel in a Good Location” I wasn't expecting too much from the hotel when I booked it given that it was in the bottom half of the hotels in Manhattan on TripAdvisor's ratings, but I was pleasantly very surprised. The rooms aren't gigantic, but have nice flat screen TVs with DirectTV and good closet space. The bathroom was very clean with quality toiletries. The location is a bit dead on the weekend, but there are some nearby restaurants and bars.

“Great hotel, secluded from the action, nice family atmosphere” If you are looking to party, meet people, see the hot crowd that Phoenix has to offer, it isn't here. Mainly seniors, families and goofy tourists. That said, this is a wonderful hotel, sedate, beautifully landscaped and designed and has good access to Biltmore Park. For the purpose of getting to Scottsdale or Chandler, where I was doing business, it was quite a bit less convenient since it is not in either of those places, but it IS central to the entire city. The staff was very responsive, the room very clean and in good condition. Only disappointment is the pool ran out of pool floats, people were hoarding them, then next day they were out of one type and charging for another. Ugh. The food at the pool was very good, you get paid attention to reasonably well by the service staff. Would definitely stay here again, bring the family.

“Huge rooms, great location” As mentioned in other reviews the hotel rooms are huge! The decor is modern but not high end, more mid level luxury. The shower in the bathroom was gianormous. The hotel gym is also large and full of top notch equipment. The front desk staff is lacking in any service training. Staff is only real detractor in my stay.

“One of the best hotels I've ever stayed in.” We had a rough day traveling and weren't in the best of moods when we were cheerfully greeted by a wonderful clerk named Vanessa. As she checked us in, she explained to us breakfast times, available parking and that they had complementary dinners as well. The best was still yet to come. Both of our rooms were way more than we expected. Full size refrigerators and a stove top made it easy for us to prepare our lunches. The rooms were very clean and smelled wonderful. Breakfast was wonderful. We didn't get to partake in the free dinner. Although parking was not on the site, it was just a minute walk away. I don't think we were charged for parking. Vanessa and another clerk named Toni greeted us and made us feel at home each and every time we walked in the door. This may have been the best place I've ever stayed. This hotel was an easy 12 minute drive into the heart of Philly and even closer to Fairmount and the zoo. Still great location for the price.

“Great stay, great staff, great spa” Capella is doing something right at The Setai. We first discovered Capella's commitment to service last year at their property in Cabo. The stellar service in NYC lived up the high expectations that were set in Cabo. The entire staff were warm and friendly from the doorman to the receptionist and attendant the wonderful spa. Housekeeping was great- we inadverdantly tracked-in some sand/salt from tramping around a snowy city. When we came back to our room after turn-down the carpet was magically cleaned (in addition to the delightful turn-down treats/housekeeping mentioned in previous reviews). Spa is well-appointed- with a nice (smallish) lounge/waiting area with tea/water and a couple of selections of light spa-type snacks. Our massages were lovely and therapists professional and competent. The beautiful Hammam is the star of the spa. It is in the co-ed area of the spa so bring a swimsuit. Nice spacious gym. We hope to enjoy a drink at the bar on our next visit - it looked like a nice spot for a drink with a Jazz trio on the night of our visit. We have already booked our next stay with Yolanda at Jet Luxury. We booked our January visit with them also, very professional, answered email's promptly, and we got a great rate on the room. We are looking forward to our return visit!

“Great, Modern, New NYC hotel” Loved it from the minute I walked in. Friendly service, modern furnishings, great location right off of Herald Square. Extremely clean and nice finishes in the decent sized guest room. Comfortable bed and the neatest pressed sheets I've ever seen. This hotel snob was impressed!

“Good Airport Hotel” Stayed here for 1 night. Hotel: Very un-Sheraton looking. Sleek & Modern on the inside. Doormen did not offer to help with the bags but I guess we looked like we did not need assistance. They were pleasant though. The front desk was very helpful at check in and check out. Nice pool area with whirlpool (had leaves in it) as well. There was a bar and 2 restaurants (1 AM and 1 PM) and a Starbucks. Shuttle to the airport very early in the morning was spot on. Room: Very nice. Horrible noise from the air con that the maintenance man fixed straight away. Comfy bed. TV had some sound issues. I could not get the broadband to work but that was my computers fault. Good size desk. Very little outside noise noticed. USA Today at the door in the morning. Adequate bathroom facilites and good towels. This is a good choice if you need a hotel at LAX.

“Old school with modern amenities” Denver prices have always been high but I saw special offers that the Oxford was running and booked. Closest to Coors Field. Arrived at DIA at 9am, took the RTD arrived by 11am. Walked to the Oxford to see if I could drop by bag off and the young lady, Jennifer, said two rooms were ready to choose from. WOW, after taking a 6am flight, of course, I'll check in now. Snoozed for a few hours. Hot hot day, AC worked fine. Modern amenities in an older hotel that still uses a real key. Bed was comfortable, a block from the 16th St Mall bus. The fitness center is the building next door and is shared with a spa. I have stayed at the Monaco, Hyatt, and Hilton property near the convention center as well as a Townsplace Suites on Speer which I think has changed names. I would say the Oxford is the best for the Coors Field RTD DIA route if that was the plan.

“Great location, typical Marriott amenities. Not the best management.” Overall, we enjoyed our stay at this JW. Like many JWs, it was a step above regular Marriotts in Union Square. We enjoyed the location--- it was centrally located to shops, restaurants, and some attractions. As other reviewers have noted, there is no free internet--- even in the lobby (if you have stayed with Marriott before, you are likely used to this). The concierge level amenities were impeccable, with great breakfasts and snacks on weekdays. Seems like it would be ideal for business travelers or those willing to spend a bit more on leisure travel. As one caveat to my review: we had the unfortunate experience of having noisy (i.e., yelling, screaming, perhaps tipsy) neighbors for one night. The management seemed reluctant to take care of this, which was clearly less than ideal. We had to threaten to call the police ourselves to have them take care of the noise next door.

“Wonderful welcome” Spent three nights of fun at hotel prior to trip to LA for business. Upon arrival from airport by taxi we were meet by the doorman who had our bags out and into the hotel before I could exit the cab. Quick service. Once I got to the front desk to meet my wife there he was to hand us each a glass of wine. Timing was perfect, it was free wine hour. What a great way to start this short vacation. Check-in staff were very nice and we got our bags delivered to the room shortly. The hotel has a very cozy feeling to it. Everyone who works at the hotel seems happy. The hotel and room as expected are in a nautical design. Room had a plush king bed with a large flat screen TV. Room was of average size and very clean. Location is a key plus of this hotel. It sits directly on the waterfront. All of the sites and resturants are outside your front door. It really does hit you how beautiful San Franicisco is when you when to walk out the front entrance of the hotel. When you are in San Francisco you want to stay in either Union Sq. or the waterfront. They are the end points of the cable cars. So the Argonaut is the perfect choice. The Argonaut is beside the turn table (end Point) of the Powell - Hyde cable car line. Just walk around the corner of the hotel and jump on board. You should buy the 3 day metro pass. It gets you on and off the cable cars, buses and subways as many times as you want. You will save a ton of money this way. The best restaurant I found on the waterfront for dinner was Castagnola's. Great calamari, swordfish and Mac & Cheese and service. The best breakfast place is also around the corner next to the cable cars. The place is the Buena Vista. Known for there Irish Coffee but the breakfast was great. Use the cable cars to see the sites. I used them and get on and off close to what I wanted to see. In China town, the best Dim Sum was the The Great Eastern on 649 Jackson St.. Visit the amazing lobby of the Fairmont Hotel on Nob Hill, it also has many of historical photos to see. Be sure to study the fescos on the first floor of Coit Tower. Painted in the 30's there are alot of hidden details. The Blue and Gold fleet tours of the bay are informative and affordable. Free wine happy hour in the lobby with a fireplace, happy staff, very comfortable room, along with a perfect waterfront location the Argonaut is the place to stay.

“Great Quality, Price and Location!” Made a reservation last minute and got a great deal on a great room! The staff meant all of my requests (a quite upper room with foam pillows) and gave me also a free upgrade. The bed and room was very comfortable . . . a topnotch boutique hotel! I work in this area a few times a year and will look forward to stay here again!

“Nice stay in good location” We recently spent a long weekend at the Palomar in Chicago and found it, overall, a good experience. We informed them ahead of time that we would need an early check-in but, upon arrival, that wasn't available. They did hold our luggage while we went out for brunch and some sight-seeing. The room was nice although not very large. The bathroom was very nice with a great shower and tub. The location of the room on the 12th floor and the end of the hallway was very quiet as far as hotel noises but it is hard to escape the noise of the nearby fire station! The free coffee in the morning as well as the wine hour in the evening was a very nice addition to our stay and gave us some time to socialize with the other guests.

“Not bad, all in all” Generally, I dislike almost everything about Crowne Plaza hotels. It's definitely my least favorite "mid-scale" hotel brand. But I was pleasantly surprised by the Crowne Plaza-Union Square in San Francisco. All in all, this property is not bad. For starters, the rooms are relatively spacious, at least by San Francisco standards. The location is excellent. And the rate was relatively inexpensive by San Francisco standards. (I was fortunate enough to qualify for a corporate rate that was about 40% less than the hotel's standard rack rate.) To top it off, the view from my room on the 23rd floor was outstanding. (Rooms on upper level floors with views of San Francisco Bay command a slight rack rate surcharge. But the surcharge is apparently waived for some corporate-rate guests.) My dislikes about the hotel: A very bland, uninspiring decorating scheme, which seems to be highly typical of most Crowne Plaza locations. Inadequate air conditioning in the lobby, elevators, hallways and other common areas. (The weather was unusually warm during my stay, with temperatures in the mid 70s.) Somewhat worn and outdated room furnishings and carpenting. Would I stay here again? Yes, if the price was right. Would I stay here if I had to pay anything close to the rack rate? Definitely not.
