“Found a new place to stay in NYC!!!!!” I'm almost tempted to write a really crappy review of the Jewel so that people won't know about this place, but I can't! Stayed here on a weekend visit to Broadway and were VERY happy with everything here! The location could not be better - walk out the front door, cross the street and you're in Rockefeller Center! The rooms are nicely furnished and offer a good bit of room (by NYC standards!) And when you factor in the price, it was one of the best deals we've come across in NYC in years! Will be back!

“Great service, but issues elsewhere” Stayed here for a full week on a split family/business trip, so feel like I got to know this hotel pretty well. Pros: • Location strikes a good balance for S.D. area attractions--easy access to La Jolla, near enough to the 5 freeway that beaches, Balboa Park/zoo and downtown are all surprisingly reachable with S.D.'s fairly moderate traffic, even Torrey Pines relatively close. • Typical strong Hyatt service at the front desk and in housekeeping. A rollaway bed was brought to our room and set up promptly after a single request. • Room was nicely furnished--not exactly luxurious, but clean and contemporary. • In-closet safe big enough to hold a widescreen laptop. • Wonderful free basic laundry/pressing service for up to 12 items. • Outstanding large pool area. Cons: • Thick pillowtop mattress and heavy comforter horribly mismatched for the San Diego climate. We woke sweating every night, even with the A/C cranked down to 64 and just a sheet on. • Bathroom was dingy and not up to snuff. Old beige-y tile never really looked clean. Shower/tub pull and temp control required Herculean effort to operate, and even then tended to leak water. Toilet flush was deafeningly loud, to the point where we thought twice about flushing at night to avoid waking each other up. • Ridiculous parking. $20 a night for self-parking in a far-off garage with narrow spaces. Even after ComicCon was well over, never seemed to have anything available until you wound down a couple of floors. From the giant, car-killing speedbumps on the way in, to finding a space, to navigating the long hike back to the hotel, to actually making it to my room was a good 15 minute process. Every. Single. Time. If you go, I'd recommend hunting for a free space on the street near the north entrance. Unfortunately, the cons impacted too much of the important aspects of our stay to be able to fully recommend this hotel. Especially at $250 or so a night (really $270 with the parking).

“OK but nothing special” We stayed here one night over labor day weekend while meeting up with my in-laws and our son in college. We had three rooms total, which were all good size. The king suite was actually two rooms combined into one. We wanted to stay downtown, but nothing was available in our price range. This hotel is not a bad location, just one block off I-240 and 10 minutes from downtown. I really don't have anything good or bad to say about it. The staff was friendly, the hotel was clean and safe. I would stay again for one night, especially if I had a flight out the next morning, but I don't think I would make it a base for a multi-night stay.

“Funky, cool but still a motel.” I came up from Orange County for a 3-day conference. No complaints really. This is a very stylish and chic motel makeover. The room was a little dingy (i.e, it still had the motel smell/feel even after a very solid makover). The restaurant was fantastic! I'd say the best in SD; seriously. The pool area is also very cool and very stylish. If you're looking for a perfect little getaway in San Diego, this is definitely the place. The Pearl has character and outdoes the cold, mega hotels of SD very nicely. Good work to those who made it into what it is today!
“Great” Booked via Sheraton.com. I have stayed here twice, and loved both stays. I love the Starbucks in the lobby, and also being so close to the center of Boston.

“Excellent hotel, fitness center and business center” Off course, it is a bit special to stay in a marine memorial hotel. However, it was a very good experience : - staff and concierge are helpfull - rooms are clean - breakfast is excellent, great choice and very good view on the city - fitness center is unique : a lot of appliance, plus a real swimming pool : 25 yards ! - good business center. The hotel decoration is old fashioned, then does not expect a design hotel, this is the only weak point in my opinion. Location is very convenient, close to Union Square a few minutes walk.

“A pleasant experience” I spent 3 nights here and I was very surprised. For the price, the Azul Inn was great. They were in the middle of renovating at the time so I did expect some inconvenience but the bed was so comfortable that I didn't notice the ongoing construction. I would definitely stay there again. The only complaints I had was the dark hallway that made me a little cautious as a female as the Inn is very open to foot traffic of non-guests and if you have more than one wifi device (i.e. phone and laptop) you are given one password to access their free wifi network so only one device can access the network at a time.

“Best Marriott in San Francisco” I arrived in San Francisco via the Amtrak Thruway Bus from the Emeryville train station. I arrived early but the friendly front desk person was able to find me a room on the ninth floor. Check in was smooth and fast. There was a makeshift lobby on the ground floor because the main lobby on the 2nd floor was being remodeled and was scheduled to open sometime that week. My room was good size by San Francisco standards. The rooms had recently remodeld so there was none of the decor and furnishing from the properties previous version, the Pan Pacific. My room was clean. I was a bit concerned about hearing street noise on the 9th floor but the street noise did not bother during my entire stay. Besides a desk and chair in the room there was a flat screen t.v. and chair and ottoman. The t.v. featured many cable channels. There are no ice machines on the floor so you press a conciere button for them to bring up the ice. There were two complimentary bottles of water which were replenished each day. Their a good size closet on the on other side of the wall from the sleeping area with safe in the closelet. I really like properties that offer safes in their rooms. Also a bathroom that features marble and granite and also features both a separate shower and tub. The room was cleaned well each day. the water pressure and temprature were fine. The king size bed was comfortable. I was attending the Human Resources Planning Society workshop on Succession Management and Leadership Development at this property. Continental breakfasts and lunches served during the workshop were good. The conference room was long and narrow a bit of odd shape for a workshop. The HRPS workshop had both hits and misses. I'll look foward to their Fall Executive Forum in October at the Renaissance in downtown Chicago. I ate breakfast one day in the temporary dining room in the basement. Excellent service there and very good food. For they buffet they will even prepare you pancakes, waffles and/or omellets. The pancake as well other breakfast items were fine. One of better Marriott buffets with superb service! All of the folks I came into contact were very good. The door men and bellhops were all friendly and attentive. I even was able to use to the house Lincoln towncar. The driver was friendly and nice. The gym is a good size facility which was well lighted and ventilated. I used the gym on three occasions. Just down the street west on 700 Post st. is a very good Indonesian restaurant called Boroudur. Attended by many Indonesians. I also recommend in the basement of the San Francisco Shopping Center on Market Street between 5th and 6th. is a food circus with many great affordable choices. In particular I can recommend Sorabol Korean BBQ & Asian Noodles. Also good is Tom's cookies in the food circus On one evening, some of us went to Alcaratz for the night tour. You get a wondeful view of the city but the place is a bit depressing. I can highly recommend the J.W. Marriott property in San Francisco as one of the bettter places to stay. I received both a special group rate and the HRPS rate as well! I'll stay here again!

“If you want a real hotel. . this is NOT the place to stay.” I was NOT impressed with this hotel. Yes, it is new. Yes, it is close to the airport. Yes, there are amenities. But I felt like I was at a hotel aimed ONLY at the Teen and Twenty something crowd. They boast on their website NINE FOOT ceilings in all the rooms. Too bad the ceiling is so bad looking. Rough, painted, cement. Maybe it is nine feet away because they hope you can't see it well. The luggage carts the hotel provides are airport style carts, which means you have no where to hang clothes, and you have to push the handle DOWN while pushing the cart forward. It is awkward and doesn't hold as much luggage as a standard Hotel Luggage cart, so. . . if there is more than one person, then you are going to need two or more carts. And, all the square footage going up to the ceiling would be nicer if the room was bigger. It is a tiny room. The desk chair is small, and the only other place to sit in the room is UNDER the TV that is mounted on the wall. Or, I suppose you can watch the TV from the bed. The bathroom has NO DOOR, so if you are with someone in the room, there will be no privacy. The bathroom has no tub, but a fairly large walk in shower. Furthermore, in the shower, the wall opposite the shower head is a frosted glass. . .that backs up to the bedroom. So if someone uses the restroom in the night, the light floods the bedroom. The spend a lot of money on Bathroom supplies. . but you get plastic and paper cups. The lobby looks like a teen or college "rec room". . .which is nice if you are a teenager or college student. . .but if you are an adult older than 30. . this is really NOT the Hotel for you. It is not really a "business friendly" hotel. It may be GREAT in a beach or vacation setting, but as an airport hotel, it really REALLY misses the mark. Other reviews state that it is a "bit funky and non traditional" and that is certainly true. I stay in hotels a LOT. . .and yes, this hotel was new and clean. . but not what I was looking for in a hotel. "Funky" is not what I want when I am traveling. I am looking for a "home away from home" and the Aloft was NOT that. That being said, there will be some that will like this concept. The room was just too small, and laid out to weird for my tastes.

“立地は最高、建物はちょっと古い” 立地は文句無し!ケーブルカーにもBARTにもチャイナタウンにもユニオンスクエアにも近い。 観光にはベストロケーションですね。 夜出歩いても、変な場所さえいかなければ安全です。 中の設備で朝食のバイキングは、3泊しましたがほぼ一緒でしたね。さすがに飽きました。というか他のホテルでもほぼ一緒。 確か米とみそ汁はあったような、、(あまりおすすめしません) 喫煙者ですが、確か喫煙部屋ってのが無くて「吸いたければこの部屋で吸って良し、ただし$300クリーニング費用を払え」って感じでしたよ。

“Great for the rate!” We stayed here because we didn't want to pay over $140 a night for a room. The Comfort Inn isn't new but it is clean and the people were pleasant and helpful. The hotel sits above a parking garage so parking was never an issue (and is half the price of other hotels in the area). The trolley runs behind the hotel and you can ride it to Beales St. We walked (day and night) and enjoyed the walk to Beales St. We have been to larger cities (Chicago, NYC, and San Francisco) and never felt unsafe at night. We were upgraded to a better room because I mentioned we had never visited their city and ended up with a view of the Mississippi and a large corner room which looked like it had been remodeled recently. The bed was comfortable and we had a microwave, fridge, and coffee maker. The breakfast was average hotel food with waffles. The only issue I had with the hotel was that the elevators needed to be more secure (you could access them from the parking garage but didn't need a room key to access the floors the rooms were on so anyone that parked in the parking garage - which wasn't just used by the hotel or walked into the parking garage could access the floors the rooms were on).

“High expectations from lobby crushed in the hallway...” USAirways gave me a voucher for the Four Points at PHL after a flight delay. The hotel is located across from several other hotels - a brand new aloft by W, Sheraton Suites, and Hilton. Do be advised, however, that there are virtually no restaurants in the immediate area. I did take the shuttle to/from PHL and found it on time and reliable. Upon arrival, I noticed the lobby looked great. Very open and pleasant and appeared to be recently renovated. The bar/restaurant was nice, and my dinner was prepared well. The staff at the bar were all very nice. Once I got off the elevator to go to my room, I started getting suspicious. The hallways are dank and musty - totally opposite of what I would have expected from the bright lobby. The room was adequate - bathroom with separate vanity space, large flat-screen TV, king sized bed (somehow with only one pillow...), desk, and chair. The bathroom itself was a little small but fine for a solo traveler. For the most part, the room was clean. However, I was a little appalled at a dust buildup on the air vent. I thought the room was a little musty, but wasn't going to put much thought into it - until I went to change the thermostat, and the air filter cover protruding from the wall caught my eye - it was completely covered in dust at least an inch thick. That kind of buildup has been there for quite some time. Finally, Starwood has some bizarre thing that turns on the TV in unoccupied rooms to run the in-house channel...somehow, mine came on at 5 AM and blasted me out of bed so I could learn about pay-per-view movies.

“Small, Old and Won't Return” Came here on the recommendation of a friend. Used Marriott Rewards points and it was the cheapest (pointwise) of the full service Marriotts. Was convenient to the subway and buses. The gym was excellent (with excellent views) and the concierge room was above average. However, the rooms were small, cramped, and the hotel itself is very old. I have found other Marriott properties in Manhattan better, so I won't return.

“Great Location” This hotel is in a great location, minutes to China Town, Little Italy and seconds to the subway. Had free internet connection but was very slow The room was a little small but more than OK for NYC, the staff was great and very helpful, I had a car, it costs $60 to park for 24 hours and the parking area was 6 blocks away, if you want to stay there I suggest parking your own car for half the price in the parkade around the corner. This is a good value, we got it for $199 per night (internet rate thru Holiday Inn website) that was one of the best prices we could find in that area for a hotel of this quality.

“Great Location, Great Place” The Monaco is just a great hotel. The room was a great size and we loved that we got to have a goldfish for our stay. Our room was on the top floor and the giant window looking out on the river was so lovely, especially because it had a window seat that we could sit in and watch the city in the rain. The location is great...right next to the river in the theater district. It's very close to shopping areas and the Chicago Institute of Art. The room service food we ordered was overpriced and mediocre, but other than that I loved everything. The staff was really welcoming and accomodating too. I would definitely stay here again.

“Stylish hotel with friendly staff” We stayed at the w on our honeymoon - on arrival Claudia at reception made us feel so welcome and special by upgrading our room and giving us cocktails and breakfast vouchers because we just got married! Our room was modern and stylish, very clean, bathroom had a combination bathtub/shower and bliss toiletries. The lobby was lively and a fun place to have a drink - the crowd was quite young but there were a few older guests and a couple of families. Only downside was no complimentary wifi in room but wifi was free in lobby. We liked the location too-close to Westfield and union square. A great stay!

“Good hotel” Good hotel for folks passing through. Rooms could be a bit bigger but well decorated with modern furnishings. Staff was generally helpful but restaurant service left a little to be desired. I stayed here with Starwood points and I believe it was either 3,000 or 4,000 per night depending on if it was a weekday or not. For this amount of points, it was a good deal. For my last night, I did cash + points and it was like $30 plus 1,250 points I believe. Again a very good deal. One thing I appreciated is that there is a wired internet connection (ethernet) in each room.

“Wonderful” This is what I expect from a St. Regis. A very new hotel South of Market that is tastefully done with excellent service. The whole place exudes a certain pleasantness and leaves you walking out saying "wow, that was a really nice hotel." Rooms were modern, clean and very nice. SPG platinum got an upgrade to an executive which had more space, a desk and a corner view. Lobby is well-done and cozy with a great bar and wonderful large gas fireplaces - I would be very happy to sit there for hours. Gym is nice and well-equipped. Two minor nits: unlike Asian St. Regis hotels, the coffee in-room is not complimentary, and breakfast is a la carte instead of the amazing buffets I've seen at other St. Regis hotels, and not included with the room - again unlike other St. Regis. If you can swing this on your trip, do it.

“Great Location, But Otherwise Disappointing” The location is fantastic--close to Broadway theatres, excellent restaurants, shopping, and museums. I would've appreciated the Central Park South location much more if I'd have a park view, but instead I had a view of brick walls & ventilation ducts. I tried to use my Starwood points to upgrade my room, but Starwood makes it extremely difficult to do this--you have to wait till 5 days before arrival to even try to get an upgrade, and of course by then all the good rooms are gone. My room was sufficiently spacious, and the bed was very comfortable. The hotel decor is very dark & conservative--way too Ralph Lauren for my taste. The housekeeping staff members were very noisy, intrusive, and overly aggressive. I had to call to complain because they were slamming doors and making way too much noise in the morning. They also kept calling and knocking on my door, even though I had the "Do Not Disturb" sign on my door--it was incredibly irritating, & far below the standard I would expect from such an expensive hotel. I was really looking forward to staying at the Essex House, but overall, other than the great location, I'd have to say that it was a disappointment.

“Weird Review Here! Didn't Love It, DIdn't Hate It!” This review ain’t going to get me too many “was this review helpful” clicks because all you need to know about this hotel has been said repeatedly on this board. We stayed here President's Day weekend. I gave it four out of five stars. The pictures of the place here on TripAdvisor are extremely representative (but I’ve posted a couple more including the construction outside of the window! And the construction was NOT an issue for me and my son, I thought it was kind of cool to watch a construction site from such a great angle but not all travelers will agree. Check out the photos... when's the last time you say a "flying porta potty?" Just ask about the construction as you check in!) It’s a reliable choice for Washington, DC especially if you’re a visiting tourist. Close enough to everything and the bus (“Circulator”) stops nearby and the Metro is a few blocks away. Also a great location for anyone visiting the Convention Center. Hotel is safe, clean, functional but charmless. And expect to have many groups of visiting kids and tourists coming in and out because hey, it’s the nation’s capital, and this is where they come on school trips! Can’t say anything bad about this place. If you’re booking blind from far away you’re making a good choice. Check in was smooth as was checkout. Everyone I dealt with was wonderful and efficient. The restaurant there is extremely expensive and swanky, so don’t expect any family-pricing there and local restaurants are few and far between. The hotel is located in a business part of town so nights and weekends it’s kind of dead. But the hotel itself is quite good and with all Embassy Suites the manager’s cocktail reception and breakfast are huge perks that must factor favorably into your price/value equation. Didn’t love this place, didn’t hate it but if you’re traveling with a family and a suite is a priority you can’t go wrong with this choice. So how’s that for a wordy but ultimately not that helpful review! I think everything that needs to be said has already been said on here.

“Exactly what I hoped it would be” As you can see there are so many positive reviews of this hotel so I figured I couldn't go wrong. I'm glad I chose the Pod. I was in the city from July 30 - Aug 1 on my own so I knew I did not need a large room. My twin bed was the perfect size. I liked the fact that the room had a sink so I didn't have to go to a bathroom to brush my teeth or wash my hands. Housekeeping was provided daily with fresh towels. The bathrooms were very clean. I checked out 3 of them on my floor ( I was on the 5th floor). The showers were wonderful. I do have 2 minor complaints about the bathroom though. There were no paper towels or even paper towel dispensers in any of the bathrooms. I found this very strange b/c there was a soap dispenser by the sink. Weird and inconvenient. Also, I had to pull the doors with both hands to close it. It seemed as though the doors had swollen so they were very hard to close. Once I put the deadbolt on it was fine though. I read a few negative reviews about the front desk staff being rude. I never encountered this. The 2 gentleman that checked me in and out were friendly enough. The concierge was also very helpful in recommending lunch options for me. I highly recommend this hotel if you are only looking for a clean, safe place to sleep and shower while in NYC! I will be visiting again.

“Hotel physically beautiful, but where is the customer service?” We stayed on the 25th floor harbor view and it was an amazingly large corner room. The bathroom was a little tight, but everything was in working order and decor was up to date. We had to wait a long time for the roll away bed for our daughter, but it eventually came. The wi-fi wasn't working correctly for the first few hours, but after a couple phone calls, it was fixed. (And, they apologized with chocolate, too). I guess they have a concierge, but two emails and two phone calls prior to our stay were never returned until the day we arrived with just an e-mail. I saw the concierge stand, but never saw anyone manning it - it always had a sign that said the concierge had stepped away. So, don't know if they really have one. I had a few questions during my stay, but no one I ever spoke with knew the answers (easy ones like, what is the movie tonight you are showing, and how can we book a shuttle somewhere, etc). The restaurant was the best part. The food was great and the service was awesome (they even knew answers to general easy question) and the physical environment is beautiful.

“Not My Usual First Choice for Austin, But a Pleasant Stay for SXSW” I stayed at this hotel about ten years ago, and it was okay at that time - I believe not run by Hyatt back then. The property has been upgraded quite nicely, with a good restaurant, a comfortable bar and lounge area, and room decor. It's important to note that I was booked into this hotel by the conference coordinators at SXSW based on housing availability for their speakers, so I didn't have a choice of locations. I must have smiled at the right person at check-in or something, but I ended up with a corner room, two queen beds, looking over Town Lake and the entire skyline of Austin. The room itself was well-appointed, with flat-screen television, wifi and ethernet in the room (for a fee, alas) - plenty of desk room and good task lighting as well. Bed was very comfortable and fresh with cotton linens. During my stay I enjoyed a meal from room service - it was very good, and one night some very tired colleagues and I went to the hotel restaurant which was quiet and relaxing. We enjoyed our dinners, the menu has some interesting local items such as venison and quail (I had the quail, very nicely done) with a strong tex-mex influence. My only suggestion for the restaurant would be to add some more generic dishes for those without daring palettes. There were soups, salads and sandwiches on the room service menu that fulfilled this, so perhaps it's simply a matter of making diners aware of options. The service was generally pleasant if not impressive, one of the bartenders was less than helpful when I was trying to find my colleagues but it wasn't anything worthy of getting upset over, just a sense that she could have been more service-oriented particularly as the bar at this point was practically empty and she didn't seem to be particularly busy or hurried. The view and general refresh of the hotel, its proximity to downtown Austin for events and the lake location make for a very pleasant stay. On the other hand, had it been a different time of year where there were more hotels to choose from in the downtown area, I wouldn't have chosen the Hyatt, despite its very nice location. The on-site services for business, including Internet, add substantially to the cost of a stay, and there are many other hotels in the area of the same or better quality for very reasonable prices and more inclusive amenities, such as free Internet.

“Convenient Location” Stayed on The Hilton Honors Floor 19 of Tower 3 overlooking the pool. 1 room had 2 mini sized beds and was too cramped, the other had a king bed and was a much more comfortable arrangement. Both rooms were nicely refurbished and we enjoyed free internet as an Honors perk. As has been mentioned by others, great location (although some adjacent streets do house a lot of homeless people). We weren't troubled by noise of any kind throughout our 3 nights. I gather that a lot of rooms are still awaiting a refurb and so it could be a bit hit and miss what you end up with.

“Nice building” The hotel is very grand and very beautiful, however it's location was less than appealing. I felt unsafe once outside of the hotel and whether that was just my impression or actually was the case, didn't change the fact that I didn't feel able to go out after dark. The staff were welcoming on arrival, but when I had a problem logging onto the internet, I felt that I was a bit of a nusience. They had in fact given me the wrong log in details, twice.

“Great experience!” We have stayed in a lot of hotels in Midtown East and this was by far the best experience. I would definitely return. The front desk staff and bellmen are friendly, professional, and courteous, everyone makes an effort and seems really on the ball. The lobby is very pretty and welcoming. We stayed on the 18th floor, the room was clean and comfortable, decent size, and relatively quiet for NYC. It was a treat to have a small balcony where we could step outside and enjoy the view. The TV was a modern flat screen and worked well. I liked the mini-bar and mini fridge. The hotel is in a terrific location, one block from the subway station and Starbucks. The front door guys really went the extra distance to get us a cab. We loved The National restaurant (part of the hotel) for breakfast and a late lunch. Some caveats: The bed was a bit too soft. The air conditioning was loud and the vent was right next to the bed, which made it hard to sleep with cold air blasting in my face, but at least it worked. There was a dog barking in the room next door for a bit while its owners were out. But overall, I would highly recommend this hotel as it is well run and in a great location.

“Mixed experience at the Grand Hyatt” I just completed a three night stay at the Grand Hyatt in Denver (for a business trip.) I traveled alone. I had a reservation for a non-smoking room with a king size bed. Upon arrival I was told that the only non-smoking room available had two standard sized beds (and that a king was not available even in a smoking room.) I took the two standard sized beds. I stayed on the 7th floor. There was obvious smoke smell in the hallway outside of my room as I first moved in, but none inside of my room. The room was clean and the bed very comfortable. I had hoped for a room with a view of the mountains but instead got only a view of the hotel or office building across the street. Oh well. The doors were very loud when they closed but I was never kept awake by them. I saw very little activity on my floor, even though the front desk claimed the hotel was completely booked. I ate in the 1876 restaurant downstairs for breakfast one morning around 9:00. I had the buffet but many of the buffet items had been depleted earlier. It took awhile for replacements to be cooked. Buffet was around $16 as I recall. One evening I ordered a cheeseburger from room service. I had ordered it prepared medium-well, but when it arrived the bottom of the patty was charred beyond being edible. I called room service and they offered to make me something else (with a 45 minute wait), or to remove the charge. It was late and I had them remove the charge and I ate what I could from the meal. The night before I checked out I called to check on the bill and the room service charge had not been completely taken off. The front desk did take the charge completely off my bill at that point. I'm glad I called a night before. On the plus side service was excellent, from the friendly maids to the front desk personnel to the folks helping with cars and taxis... lots of smiles and a sincere attitude of wanting to make your stay exceptional. One note: there is another Hyatt only 3 blocks away, and it is located directly across the street from the Convention Center where my conference was being held. I would have preferred to stay at that more convenient location (my trip was booked through a travel office in my business) and I mention it to caution others traveling for events at the convention center. The walk was not difficult or time-consuming at all, just not as convenient. I walked through the lobby of the other Hyatt once and it seemed very nice.

“Hotel Ok; Disappointed in Houston” This hotel is your average Hilton Garden Inn. If you have been in one built in the last 5-10 years then you've seen this one. The room was clean and comfortable, but not worth the jacked up price of $250 I paid during the Final Four in April 2011. The pool is about the size of your living room, so when the hotel is packed (as it was when I was there, the pool is a man stew). Also, if you have kids, keep in mind that with Houston's complete lack of zoning laws, there is a strip club RIGHT NEXT DOOR. This hotel is in the Galleria area, which is supposedly Houston's nicest shopping enclave. In addition, this city is so spread out that to get to Reliant Stadium from the Galleria takes about an hour and there are no cabs available for a return trip. There are also no restaurants within walking distance other than a cuban nightclub. In all, this hotel is average, but the strip club next door and the the city itself make a return trip unlikely.

“Another Great Kimpton Hotel” The first thing to be aware of about this hotel is that they have weird gimmick if you book on their website wherein you can apply for an upgrade for a very modest nightly fee after confirming your reservation, and if any of the rooms you applied for are available upon check-in, they will upgrade you and charge you the extra money. Therefore, I suggest you book the cheapest room possible and apply for the upgrade. This hotel does not give the appearance of being overly busy (it's slightly out of the way, although still a decent Midtown location) so you will probably get the upgrade for a lot less than if you booked the room outright. We did! That little tip out of the way, on to the review. This hotel is slightly out of the way of the hustle and bustle of NY. It is located directly across from a car dealership, and its Hell's Kitchen location is not particularly upscale, but it is perfectly safe. The hotel itself is very spacious and nicely appointed. The lobby is beautiful and there are lots of little places to sit and sip your complimentary morning coffee. Check-in was a breeze and very friendly. We were upgraded to a CityView Studio King Room and it was HUGE by NY standards. Plenty of room for my sister and me and our many pairs of shoes to coexist in comfort for a weekend. Floor to ceiling windows provided a great view of the city at night, and we loved the double sinks and the separate vanity area. One complaint if you are traveling with anyone other than a domestic partner is that the wall between the bedroom and the shower is only semi opaque and if you had the light on in the shower area you can see the form of the person taking a shower. The soaking tub was completely out in the open so that if you were sitting in the tub, you could see and talk to the person lying in bed. The rooftop bar has great ambiance, good cocktails, and a stunning city view. Don't be intimidated by the reception desk that they move in front of the elevator leading up to the rooftop at night - guests have priority access to the rooftop bar. The hotel was about a mile's walk or a quick, inexpensive cab ride from MoMA and 5th Avenue shopping.

“one of the better ones in NYC” Mixed feelings since I had a memorable, good stay as being upgraded to a junior suite (USD 330) but my colleague had a standard room which was too small and dated. My suite was large, newly refurbished, king size bed but too soft to me. Large TV but very old came along with VHS player and a CD player. Lovely but expensive breakfast (USD 45), I had a crepe with spicy salsa, and a plate of berries. Really great food. The service was too pushy but okay in NYC standards. On the top floor (42nd) there is a tiny swimming pool, too salty and warm water but I still enjoyed it.

“Back again, and will be back again!” Simply my favorite hotel in the area. Next door’s Hilton Garden Inn, which offers a decent dinner and it is just across the Homewood Suites parking lot (they share). The breakfast at Homewood is substantial, the coffee decent and the rooms are spotless. Love the beds. Plenty of pillows. Staff friendly, efficient and personable. Not my first stay here nor my last. I came here with my teenage daughter and hubby on a college road trip, but have stayed here for business too. I get free wifi with Hilton Honors. Within minutes of major San Diego attractions and San Diego State University, but not “too close” if that makes sense. So free parking, not overloaded with people. My preference, may not be yours.

“Clean easy to walk to places hotel” This is our hotel when planning gatherings. This last stay was for a friend's 40th birthday party. We ate at the resturant on the river walk on the first night as people were coming in at different times. It is primarly a topas type place. I also ate their buffet for breakfast and everything was fresh. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable. I like the sitting area each room has. This allows you to have a place to have others over without sitting on your beds. My only complaint is that the sink, toliet and shower are all in the bathroom. When you have multiple people staying in a room it is nice to have the sink on the outside of the shower. Small compliant. Valet parking was fast and easy. I never had to wait more than 5 minutes for my car. Front desk was nice and friendly for the many questions we had. We will be staying here again. Probably not being using the pull out coach for anyone but children moving forward but that is typical. Pool and fitness area are on the top floors and seem nice. Pool a tad small but fitness room above average for a hotel. Thanks for a great weekend.

“Comfortable stay at the Pointe Hilton” I chose to stay at this Hilton property due to my first and second choices for accommodations in the Phoenix area being sold out at the time of my visit. However, this ended up being for the better, as the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort exceeded my expectations in many areas. First off, this resort is designed with the "old-school" layout in mind - a sprawling property requiring the use of many a golf cart by hotel staff members. There isn't necessarily anything wrong with this, but if you're expecting to walk in the lobby, hop on an elevator, and walk 50' to your room, you may be slightly disappointed. My suite was located in the "North Pointe" area, which was a considerable distance from the lobby, restaurant, and fitness center. However, this wasn't an issue for me. The suite itself included a living room area in front (with a sofa, chairs, desk, and flatscreen HD TV) and a bedroom area in the rear (with two queen-sized beds, nightstand, walk-in closet with ample space, yet another flatscreen HD TV). The living room and bedroom were separated by the bathroom in the middle. The bathroom was 'split,' with the toilet and shower located separately from the sink/mirror/counter area. The room was very nice, with plenty of space to spread out. The beds were comfortable and clean, and the bathroom was adequate. I did not visit the water park area of the resort, but I did make it to the fitness center. By hotel standards it was quite large, with plenty of treadmills, free weights, and machines. I would definitely recommend this property, not only to families looking for a kid-friendly resort, but to business travelers alike. With accommodations like this, you really can't go wrong.

“Can't be beat” Frequent traveller so I know good - no - great service when I see it. This hotel has it all. Best service of ANY hotel I've stayed in. Without exception, every person you come into contact at this hotel will impress. Used to stay at Sorrento - but like this location, lobby, restaurants, fitness center and rooms better. This hotel has it all. Close to everything; comfortable, spacious rooms; incredible fitness center w/ every amenity possible, impressive lobby and truly accommodating staff. Restaurants are great - gorgeous main dining room or the cozy Oyster bar @ Shuckers. Hotel pays close attention to every single little detail. It's the only place to stay in Seattle.

“Disappointed in Love Field Embassy Suites” I've stayed at this Embassy Suites quite a few times over the years. This was undoubtedly the worst visit. When I checked in the counter clerk was unfriendly and seemed almost offended that I was bothering her at check-in. The room was okay (they actually upgraded the TV's), but it was a little warm because of the hot temperatures that Dallas was having. When I woke up on Saturday morning they had a power outage. I called the front desk and asked if she knew if this was going to be a long outage. She was extremely rude to someone who spends more than 60 nights at the Hilton family of hotels annually. I took a shower in the dark (at least I had hot water), but the maid didn't leave any shampoo in the room. I went downstairs and they had very little to eat - not of it hot. I thought this was okay so I went to get a bowl of cereal and they had no milk. Of course, they were out of coffee. When I checked out on Sunday it was still the same old poor attitude ... no thanks for staying ... no apology that there was a power outage ... it was like "don't let the door hit you in the axx" I don't know if I'll ever go back to this Embassy Suites. Like I said I've stayed here over the years, but this one instance was enough to get me to think about staying somewhere else in the future.

“A tad disappointed” We stayed here for 4 nights in October 2012. Overall, the hotel didn't quite measure up to our expectations, resp. to its status as a "Small Luxury Hotel of the World". The reception was kind of snippy; they just checked us into our room very quickly without giving us any explanations on the hotel or even saying welcome (the concierge on the other hand was very friendly and helped us with all our requests). As for the room, it was a tad on the shabby side (again, measured against the expectations that one might have based on the hotel category and price). We had heard that you have to be lucky to get one of the newer rooms here, so maybe it was just bad luck that we ended up in one that looked clearly dated (for what it's worth, we were in room number 707). Bathroom was nice, but pretty small. The spa is nice, but nothing out of the ordinary. One great thing is the hotel's location.

“Off the tourist track, but great for NHL/NBL at The Garden” This small hotel is a little off the tourist track, so if you're expecting tourist attractions at the doorstep, look elsewhere, but is in a perfect location across from The Garden for NHL or NBL games, as well as North Station (for commuter rail and T-subway). It is within walking distance to North End (Italian village), Waterfront, Beacon Hill, Faneuil Hall, and for the energetic to Boston Common/Downtown Crossing. While it's a little quiet at night, I didn't feel unsafe. There are a few pubs/restaurants on the same street as the hotel (but better to go to North End), as well as Au Bon Pain and 7-Eleven. Free morning coffee/tea was no longer available while I was there, but they happily supplied me with a coffee percolator. The staff were friendly and helpful. The entrance is a bit crowded in the evening when there's free wine/cheese, but I didn't partake in this, nor use the bar or room service. My room was on a high floor, was bright, clean and of average size, and decent comfortable bed. I was initially a bit concerned about having pets as neighbours, but was reassured they're sequestered on allocated floors, and I didn't hear a peek out of any pet/neighbour during the stay. The CRT TVs were replaced by large screen LCD TVs while I was there. Overall, it's a decent convenient hotel.

“Hilton Universal: An Excellent Choice” We stayed at the Universal City/Los Angeles Hilton from March 14 till the 17th and on March 19th. From March 17th to March 19th we stayed at the Residence Inn San Diego. Please see my review on that hotel too. Introduction/Location: This Hilton property is located in the heart of the touristy Hollywood/Beverly Hills/Universal Studios area. The area is very nice and safe. This hotel attracts the more civilized (but not snobby) guests rather than the sloppy and messy people which are better suited for a cheap motel. You enter on Universal Hollywood Drive. There is also Sheraton property located on the same street and there is an elevator which takes you between the two hotels. There is a hotel shuttle which takes you to Universal Studios and City Walk. It runs about every 15 minutes and the trip takes no more than a minute or too. It is very convenient for travelers without a car or people who don’t want to pay the money to park at Universal. The hotel has 24 floors. We stayed on the 18th for the first part and on the 11th for the last part. Features: This hotel was built in 1986 and seems to have been renovated recently. When we were staying there I overheard one of the desk clerks telling one guest that they are replacing the carpet starting with the top floor. We were given room 1872 for the first part of our stay (March 14th-March 17th). This floor/room had newer looking carpeting which was clean and did not have any stains. The desk and night table also looked to be in good condition. There was also an armoire which contained the television, a mini bar drawer, a minibar fridge and a small safe with a key. The television had the basic US TV channels plus the standard hotel movies, internet, games, etc. Everything worked fine. There are also many banquet/meeting rooms which are used quite a bit. There were a lot of parties/conferences and functions are held at this hotel. All were kept at a reasonable level (the people here are civilized). On our last day after we returned from San Diego we were given a room on the 11th floor which was not in such a good shape. The carpet was older (but clean), the night-table/armoire was worn/scratched and the beds were quite soft and creaky. I believe this is because they had not yet replaced the carpets/beds in this room since they had been working from the top floor (24th) down. Luckily it was just for one night and we managed. Amenities: Standard Hilton amenities are present at this hotel. People who are HHonors members with high status usually get a gift of some sort. We are not members but we still received a nice fruit/snack/water tray. I believe all the guests get this, although I am not sure. On the lobby level (Fourth floor) there is a nicely equipped fitness centre which has working and new machinery such as treadmills, stair climbers, bikes, etc. The place is split into two rooms which have difference types of equipment. One room had a TV and the other had a stereo with speakers on the wall. Also on the 3rd floor is a gift shop with travellers’ supplies and food/drink items. The prices are quite high for the drinks so I suggest you just pick up some from a local variety store. The access door to the outdoor pool is on the first floor. You need to use your keycard to open the gate. This is to prevent non-guests from using the pool. The pool area has a large pool with shallow and deep ends as well as a smaller whirlpool which has an adjustable massage/bubble control. The whirlpool was nice and warm (actually HOT) but once you’re in for a few minutes you get adjusted to it. Both the pool and the whirlpool were clean and heated. There are towels provided for you on a table as well as a basket for used towels. Surrounding the pool are chairs for tanning and poolside resting. You must pay to park at this hotel. Self Parking in one of their two underground garages is $11 per night and $16 for valet parking. Remember, to access the self parking you must take one of the elevators near the meeting rooms as the main ones do not service the garages. Service: Right from the start I was treated with care and attentive service. Upon pulling up to the door the attendants help you with unloading your luggage as well as holding the door open for you as you enter. Staff the front desk were incredible and helped us with driving directions as well as the locations of the different attractions in the area. The travel guide suggested tours for us and helped us choose the right one. Housekeeping came to make the beds daily and to replace towels, toiletries, etc. Everyone in the hotel was always there to help you. Dining: The hotel has a restaurant called “Café Sierra” which serves breakfast, lunch and dinner. Each morning we ate the breakfast buffet there which cost $15 per person. The price was a bit steep but the breakfast buffet was so filling we didn’t eat until dinner. Some of the food included the normal breakfast food such as bacon, sausages, pancakes, eggs as well as a nice fresh fruit and 2 or 3 dim sum dishes such as shrimp dumplings and BBQ Pork buns. If you want to save yourself some money and spend your time touring the city, take the buffet for breakfast. It will keep you full until dinnertime. On Friday/Saturday/Sunday they had a very large seafood buffet complete with hot/cold crab/lobster/shrimp/fish as well as sushi, dim sum as well as roast lamb and beef. The dessert selection was also quite nice with fresh fruit, cakes and cookies. It cost $38 per adult which is worth it if you’re a big seafood lover (like us) but if you don’t eat seafood it is not worth it to eat at this buffet. Also available Monday to Friday from 4pm-6pm is a happy hour snack in the lobby. A different hot hors d’oeurve was served each afternoon as well as a selection of cheeses, spreads and breads. Drinks were available for a nominal fee. Value: We paid $159USD per night which is a fantastic price for the quality and service we received at this hotel. This was for a standard guest room. The suites with whirlpools and the rooms on the executive floor were in the $200USD+ category. Overall: This hotel is an excellent choice for anyone who is going to be touring the Hollywood/Universal area that doesn’t have a car. Tours information is available from the concierge and there is a free shuttle that runs every 15 minutes between the Sheraton, the Hilton and Universal Studios. Location: 10/10 Amenities: 9/10 Guestroom: 8/10 Dining: 8/10 Service: 9/10 Value: 9/10

“Best Kept Secret in San Francisco” Wow is all I can say! This was my 3rd visit here, and it just keeps getting better with each visit. The rooms are great, the amenities are nice, the Staff is incredible. The free breakfast was a treat. In the previous stays, I missed it due to my sleeping late. This time I made sure I went and ate. I love the fact the hotel is eco friendly! It was great to walk into China town, and be right there. It's very close to Union Square as well.

“Excellent location and best service!” Located in Manhattan's Heart, it may look small from the outside, but it is compensated by the excellents staff, and the luxury of every room. You can walk to the rock from here, or even timesquare, without spending too much time. And if you have a specific need for tickets or any information, the concierge it's alway avaliable and knowledgable so you do not have to worry about anything in the big apple, except of enjoying every single minute.

“Excellent property in Downtown L.A.” I came to L.A. to visit friends and family and to attend performances at the Music Center and the Walt Disney Concert Hall. The Omni is the closest hotel to those locations, and it was fortunate that I could get a reasonable weekend rate that included parking and their breakfast buffet, both of which are usually pricey. The hotel itself is wonderful. The public spaces are open and lovely. My king bedroom was spacious and clean, with a view of the Museum of Contemporary Art (next door) and the Disney hall. Service throughout was quiet, cheerful and exemplary. This extends to the breakfast room, where the cook at the omelet station will fix eggs any way you please. Things to note: the TVs have not yet been upgraded to flatscreen, and sheets are changed every third day unless you specify otherwise. They will try to nickel-and-dime you if you're not careful, not just at the mini-bar but with the snacks lying next to it and that bottle of mineral water in the bathroom. Also, the computers in the lobby are $6.95 for 15 minutes, plus more for printing. However, boarding passes are free, and the concierge will print out directions to local landmarks for you on request.

“All I Can Say Is Wow!” Hotel Adagio is a gem of a hotel. We got an excellent rate for our stay, impacting my value selection above. Our room, on the 14th floor, had a view of the SF skyline that was lovely. The bed and linens were luxurious. While the rooms were somewhat small, our room was well appointed, providing all the little details that good boutique hotels have become known for. The cleaning staff was attentive and meticulous. My only complaint was that it seemed like they didn't dust very often. The closet and bathroom were both roomy, and our floor was pretty quiet (even though it seemed to be almost entirely full.) The front desk staff were all awesome, and the restaurant and bar are good alternatives for a nightcap before heading up to the room for the night. I would definitely stay here again when visiting SF, as I was able to walk all over the place (from the Ferry Building to Golden Gate Park) pretty easily and with minimal uphill. The street outside is still urban interesting and diverse, something I always find fun.

“Really great hotel and amazing price!” I walked in with a coupon and they gave me a nice large room with a comfortable king-sized bed, sofa, flat screen TV, fridge, microwave and stocked bathroom. The hotel has free parking (unless like some other hotels in the area) and is really close to the Mayo Clinic, where a free shuttle service was provided by the hotel from 6 a.m. - 8 p.m. The hotel also provides free WiFi which was fast and reliable, a nice breakfast buffet, free newspaper in the morning, and also close to a golf course where I went jogging in the morning. And lastly, the hotel has a Ruby Tuesdays, Publix (super market), Burger King, and several other restaurants and gas stations right next door. For the price, location, amenities, cleanliness and staff, I was pretty happy staying at this hotel and would do so again if I need to return to the Mayo Clinic.

“One of the best hotels in Phx” Check-in staff was exceptional. The rooms were well appointed. The hotel was clean and modern. The spa was large and of all the latest and greatest equipment. The grounds were well manicured and the lobby area thriving. The pools and lazy river are great for families. Great value for the price.

“Excellent value, awesome location” Stayed here for an impromptu date night using hilton points. Great little hotel, we had a beautiful suite with a comfy bed, great breakfast in the morning. Very conveniently located. A gem!

“Great location near 16th Street Mall” We stayed here for a convention so not much choice on the location, but found the staff to be absolutely professional and courteous at check-in. As a platinum Marriott member I got a corner room upgrade. Then room was large but the bathroom was the smallest I have ever seen! No towel racks anywhere and the door barely cleared the toilet. Not sure if a regular room would have been better. Concierge lounge on the 17th floor had a good breakfast selection of scrambled eggs and bacon, fresh fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, juices, and breads. We would stay here again, all things considered.

“Convenient location but somewhat overpriced” Just across the street from the Amtrak Station, the Marriott Copley Place in Back Bay is an ideal location for business travellers. The hotel is within steps to the Copley Place mall with shops and a supermarket. It was quite an enjoyable walk to the Copley Square and the bustling Boyston Street lined up with restaurants in the evening. Room was clean with comfortable bed but the decor was a bit old fashioned. Tried to book the hotel for other times but price had gone up considerably. Can get better deals at the Fairmont Copley or other brands in downtown.

“Great location, great hotel in Chicago” It's my second time at the Hard Rock Chicago and thought it deserved a review. I really like this hotel. It's in a great location -- plenty of shopping and restaurants around. Most importantly, the staff at the hotel is very welcoming --- they make you feel right at home. On my first trip, I scored the Penthouse suite because there was an issue with my room -- that was a treat. On this trip, I got a regular room but it was still spacious and very comfortable. There was nothing to complain about.

“I love this hotel!” This was a "leisure" trip for me and a "business" trip for my spouse. Although we have been frequently to Baltimore, we had never stayed at the Renaissance Harborplace. It was a delightful stay. The room--8115--faced the east (not south to the Harbor, which is an additional fee), but we could see part of the Inner Harbor, but also we had an unrestricted view across to the area where Barnes & Noble and Hard Rock Cafe and ESPN are located. (See my pics at www.flickr.com/donwest48). The room was sizable and completely clean and comfortable. I was fascinated by the "inner court" of the hotel. This might not appeal to everyone, but our hall was glassed-in, and faced the inner court of the hotel. I found myself admiring the lines and the colors. I took numerous fotos of the view. Who was the architect? He or she did some good work. Service was good. My housekeeper was a bit fussy the first day, but I am a counselor/listener and don't object to hearing such. You can learn a lot more about a hotel by listening to staff-persons than you can from the hotel's brochure! We ate a couple of meals at the Watertable restaurant. Excellent and easily recommended. Tips! Oh my....I handed out multiples of $1 and $5's like crazy! Valet Parking is $36.00 per night! (I noticed walking by the new Kimpton Monaco that the rate was the same.) Baltimore "downtown" is strange. The Mechanic Theatre, for instance, is atrocious. Is it used these days? I would never go into such an unbelievably ugly and nasty looking building. *yuck* Just keep in mind that your hotel might be a bargain, but you might be in a block or two of.....nothing! (For example, I would not recommend the Radisson Lord Baltimore unless you are on a tight budget.) I heard rumors of crime in downtown and even the touristy Inner Harbor, but I saw nothing that would frighten even the scariest tourist or conventioneer. Renaissance Harborplace? Absolutely recommended!

“Great location” This was a great hotel. Full service for a reasonable price ($249/night for me). The room was very nice. I had a 42" LCD in the room which also had a dock/speakers for my iPod. They also had a nice little box that you could use to hook other components to the television if you had brought them. Be sure to sign up for the Fairmont President's Club before you go, even if you don't stay at a Fairmont often. It's free to sign up, but it will allow you to make local and toll-free calls from your room for free (there is normally a charge) and use the internet for free, which is normally around $16 for a 24-hour period. The only thing I had an issue with was that they did not have an airport shuttle, and should you drive your own car, parking is $49/night. Otherwise, I really liked the place, and it was convenient to most everything that downtown Chicago had to offer. Millennium Park is directly across the street, as is a place to rent bicycles and Segways. Navy Pier is a short walk, as well as the Sears Tower. Depending on the side of the building and floor you may even be able to see Lake Michigan. I was on the 30th floor on the east side of the building and could. If you are on the North or West side of the building, you may be able to see the Navy Pier fireworks from your room, which are every Wednesday and Saturday evenings (I believe, maybe Sunday) between Memorial Day and Labor Day.

“Modern hotel with great facilities” We were lucky to stay here at a discounted rate through Priceline. This hotel has a great location in downtwon Seattle. It has modern furniture and excellent fitness center and swimming pool. We had one unfortunate incident when we checked in. We discovered unclean pillows on our bed. I assume this was a rare finding in such a upscale hotel. After our complaint, they changed our room. However, we did not receive any other compensation for inconvenience. The hotel also does not have free Internet. In these days and times, you expect to find free Internet everywhere.

“Glorified IKEA” I stayed here on business in April and was looking forward to it based on the photos online. Overall, sadly, I wasn't impressed...while the service hit the mark, the quality of the room was below the mark. I've had far better experiences at a similar price point at several other Chicago properties within the same area. It wasn't horrific. Like I said, the service hit the mark...fast and polite check-in, helpful doormen and bellmen, desire to serve. Very well done on that front. The gym, while in a basement, was complete with a great range of equipment. The bed was quite comfy. But there were issues. The rooms are glorified IKEA. Totally cheap furniture that was badly worn. Chips in the coffee table, hinges broken, scuff marks, etc. And the room had no desk! While that might be fine for a leisure traveler, it is annoying for a business traveler. Rooms also had a barren look..all white, no wall hangings, brown carpet. I love modern design, but this place was put together on the cheap and the result is that it is showing wear and tear very quickly. Lobby is also a "scene." Not to the point where you don't feel welcome as a guest, like at some places, but combine the cramped quarters with the noise and I didn't find it very relaxing.

“Excellent Stay for Spring Training” We recently spent 2 nights at the Fairfield Inn Phoenix Airport. Our visit was to attend a couple of Angels Spring Training Games. The hotel was only about 5 minutes from the stadium. The hotel was clean and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The breakfast was much more than an ordinary continental breakfast. There were egg sandwiches, waffles, cereal, hard boiled eggs, lots of breads and pastries, juice, and coffee. It was a bit light on fruit. But, that is really a minor complaint. We checked out the pool for an hour or so. Very small, but at least they had one. The room was very comfortable, the Internet was easy to access and included in the room rate. Yes, we will return next year.

“pleasant business-traveler hotel” If you have business in downtown San Diego or are there to see the array of popular sights that are scattered around town, it's a pleasant hotel in a reasonably central and walkable location. I like the hotel; we were comfortable there, and I have absolutely no complaints, but I see it more as a normal business hotel than something vacationers would be dazzled by. Vacationers might prefer some of the properties along Harbor Drive (or the Gaslamp district for those who like the Gaslamp district, which is not everybody's thing.) The turns and lanes of travel in the Doubletree self-parking garage were extremely tight.

“Beautiful Lobby overshadows a a few issues with room” As many have said already, the lobby is right up there with the best of the old grand hotels of the 20's. It's simply beautiful. The room was fine in terms of size and comfort. If it were not for the lobby and the fact that hey, this is a 80 year old property, I might be a little more upset over the water damage that was evident on the ceiling (room 1518). It wasnt anything that occured recently, from the mold and cracking paint, it was pretty clear that it had been left unrepaired for some time. The second issue was the worn spot in the rug about 5 feet into the room. It appeared like a dog chewed the rug. As strange as it sounds, I excused those two flaws because the place otherwise was great. I think when you stay in older properties, you have to take the good with the bad. Overall, the good far outweighed the bad. The concierge was great and the front desk person was helpful during check in and upgraded us to a double bed as I went through Priceline and would have had to go with a bed cart for one of my two children. Parking was steep at $5 a day but not outrageous for NYC. I opted to park the car at a cheaper garage ($23/day) but it was a bit of a walk back to the hotel... but then again, I'm kind of cheap that way.

“Enjoyable” Hilton does a fine job with all their hotels. This Hampton is well maintained, appointed and managed. The staff was always available to assist and offered suggestions to guests. Depending on where you need to be, however, this may be out of the way. I found the room to be very clean and cared for...A/C filters were clean, bath and floors scrubbed.

“Stay for the location and valet parking” The last time I was in Seattle was October and the previous year in October as well. Kept seeing Hotel Max on the corner and thought it looked funky and an awesome location close to everything. This much is true. Location cannot be beat. In summer weather, this place is perfect to walk to everything; from the market to the Space Needle and Westlake Center shopping. We stayed Friday to Tuesday am and the valet parking attendants (sorry, but I didn't catch names and hate to label, but there were two African American and one Somalian gentlemen, who were AWESOME!) Front desk was average at best. Looked asleep and the guy who checked us in didn't even tell us that you had to stick the key card into the slot in the elevator to make it go to your floor. After going back and forth, we figured it out...kinda funny. Our room was on the fourth floor facing out to Stewart and it's LOUD. I have stayed all over the country in every major city and this place is LOUD. If you stay here request a room on the other side, or you will never sleep. The walls are so paper thin that we could hear people talking (every word!), having sex (my 15-year old niece got educated.), and taking a shower at 2:00 am and hearing them drop the soap in the shower!!! Not lying...we turned on the window heater/air to drown out noise, but then that was like having an airplane hangar next to you...wow. This is like having your own little efficiency apartment in the middle of downtown Seattle. Yes, it is funky, the art is cool, but that lasts a minute and then you're like...oh no, this is loud and really small. If you are over 6 feet tall, you will have a difficult time using the bathroom. I'm not joking and I think our bathroom was larger than most. My knees almost hit the wall when going potty! The shower wouldn't drain (we asked twice for it to be fixed!) and so by the time you got out you had water ankle deep! Every day we had to ask for more toiletries, since there were three of us and we actually needed them! We weren't taking home for future use...didn't do that. Valet parking is $30, but since we rented a car and it was raining the entire trip, for us it was probably more cost effective, since we could come and go many times and not have to pay. The lot across the street was less expensive, but once you leave, that's it. So for us that could've been $100 easy a day! And the above mentioned valet guys were sweetie pies and talkative and made the whole stay! They should be at the front desk taking care of people...awesome! We ordered room service one night and it was horrible!!! So gross...ordered two sodas and they just slapped the dirty-topped cans on the tray with no glasses of ice. We ordered three separate meals; got one set of cutlery...wha??? Wierd and gross...mistake. Stay else where...hate to say it...really hate to say it.
“JW's never disappoint” Attended for a conference, good rooms, quality bed, nice grounds and a great restaurant

“`GROOVY`” no complaints about this hotel,good area,close to all tourist spots free internet in the lobby,comfy beds and nice staff very friendly.5th time in new york and have stayed and done nearly eveything and this hotel is a nice base even if you are going to new york for the 1st time you will enjoy staying at the hilton garden inn.

“Comfortable hotel friendly helpful staff, clean comforatable room.” Enjoyed this hotel. It was close to everything we needed; subway next door, great shopping a short walk way, plenty of decent restaurants, Macy's very close and very close to Union station which was really handy for us as we trained it with Amtrak, from New York and then again to Washington. Staff were very friendly, helpful and welcoming and the choc chip cookies were a definite bonus. (they keep them in a heated drawer and hand them out when you register and again whenever you come back into the hotel, if you ask. (which I did. Lots!!!) the room was a good size, quiet with a decent shower and the bed was terrific. There is a Starbucks on the ground floor of the hotel as well with free wi fi. There are no tea or coffee making facilities in the rooms (seems to be the norm in America) but we were forewarned and took a travelling electric jug with us, and our own tea bags. (Gotta have a cuppa first thing in the morning and last at night!) We loved Boston, it's a great place to get around and we'd thoroughly reccommend the 'duck tours' - novel way of seeing a city by both road and water and the tour guide was very knowledgeable and amusing. Learnt a lot about Boston, it's history and heard anecotes about buildings, cemetaries, statues etc. We also used the Greyline double decker bus tours. Pay for two days and get on and off wherever you like, whenever you like. Great way to see a City and learn about it's history and secrets. (we'd used this tour company in New York as well and later in San Francisco, probably the best of any of those kinds of tours). We also felt comfortable using the subway and did so often. It's an easy system to use, cheap and efficient. Harvard was amazing. Always wanted to go there and it was as I imagined - beautiful old buildings that just reek of history and the famous people who studied there over the centuries. Shopping is good, restaurants were excellent and it's a beautiful city with the gas lights and all the different churches giving it a lovely feel. It reminded me a little bit of Melbourne. Would stay at this hotel again. If you want professional, friendly staff, a comfortable room and bed and to be central to all the major tourist attractions and restaurant and shopping precincts, all at a reasonable price, then this is the perfect place!

“Great value for almost anyone staying here” I just spent 3 nights at this property. I received excellent value, (as I had an extremely favorable industry rate). Still, the Hampton Inn Times Square North would provide excellent value in any case. My room was comfortable, very decently sized, all necessary amenities, and very clean. Staff was cordial, and helpful, when I needed something. Though the hotel was busy, there were no tremendous lines, as I had expected on a busy post-holiday weekend. This hotel has a very convenient location, just a block from the subway, walking distance to the theatre district and Restaurant Row on West 46th Street. While it was expected breakfast would get very busy, I appreciated the suggested time advisements, helping me to plan. Would I return?--in a New York minute.

“Second Time Visit! Great!” We booked two rooms at AAA rates and received a great price for New Year's eve. As a Diamond Hyatt memeber, I kindly asked for upgrades and received them for both of our room! We got upgraded to an executive suite and a corner suite. We also received complimentary snacks and drinks in the room as well. This is our second time staying at the Grand Hyatt and have enjoyed it again. The staffs are always friendly and the views from the bedroom are spectacular. PROs: a. Have always received upgrades b. Great security in hotel during New Year's Eve c. Regency club provided good food and drinks d. Rooms are very modern and clean. e. Bathroom are large and comfortable CONs: a. They seems a bit understaffed during the holidays b. The extra charge for valet parking was very very very $$$ c. Regency club did NOT have hot breakfast, was only continental breakfast d. Regency club charged for beer unlike most other Grand Hyatts Overall we enjoyed our stay, rooms are modern, views are always great, good location for shopping and restaurants, and the price was good.

“Excellent Location, Elegant Atmosphere” I stayed at the Blackstone during Lollapalooza 2012 and it was a great stay. Very expensive, but that's understandable given it's prime location for the festival. The bathroom was huge. Modern in style with white/grey marble throughout. The room itself was not huge, but not bad at all for a downtown hotel in a major city.

“Fantastic Location.Very good value.” Staying on the 37th floor we didnt hear a thing from the streets below.Leave the lobby and your in the heart of Times Square.Such a busy place.The rooms are huge.Great for 2 x kids in the other room.Beware the sofa bed is a disgrace.Hard,lumpy,totally unuseable.We just put the matress on the floor and the kids are happy.Great blackout curtains,nice staff.Just a good value mid price Hotel.Its all a bit dated but comfortable.Would stay again.Great cookies at reception.

“Walk to Ballpark/Free Parking” Chose this hotel because of it's proximity to Chase Field, was about a 10 min walk with a few eating establishments along the way . The Hotel itself was a little over priced but with the free parking and free breakfast it all washed out. The room was large,it was clean,but it was starting to show it's age but at this point it's not a deterrent in your decision to book there.

“Nice Chicago hotel” This location was great for someone visiting who did not have a car. I was able to walk to most of the places I wanted to go or get a taxi for a reasonable price. The rooms were clean and nicely appointed. I have stayed here twice while in Chicago and would definitely stay again.

“Great hotel but a little bit out of the way if you're a tourist” I travel to NYC every month for business. My business is in the garment district so the event is in a perfect location. If you are a tourist, this might not be the perfect location for you, it is close to penn station and the empire state building but not really close to the theater district and tourist favorites. The nightlife and dining options in event's neighborhood are scarce so If it's your first trip to NYC , I'd opt for something more centrally located such as the kimptons other hotel The Muse. If location is not an issue for you, here's the lowdown on Eventi Check in was fast and efficient. Lobby very hip Room: I had a standard king room which was around $400 a night. It was small but most NYC rooms are tiny. Bed was comfortable. Room was very new and in perfect condition. Had floor to ceiling windows and I could see empire state building from my room. Nice bathroom with large shower and rain shower head. Nice toiletries from etro. It was quiet and nice There is no lobby bar but there is a restaurant somewhere on the property. There is a fitness center and a business center. Next to hotel is a place called foodparc. I think it is owned by the hotel but you can't charge to your room. It's like a gourmet food courtl I has Asian food from there for lunch and it was the most disgusting thing that Ive ever eaten in NYC ( I'm not picky). This city is full of the best food so you may want to keep walking around the corner to pert a manger..a yummy lunch choice. I'd definitely return to eventi if the price was right because of its location but as I said before,there are much more interesting neighborhoods to stay in l

“This is a gem - great location, friendly, updated rooms, and art deco lobby. What more could you want!” I love this hotel. I loved it before the renovations and now that the rooms have all been redone I still love it. The neighborhood is perfect. Metro is close, Beds are super comfy. The in-house food service is OK but with lots of nearby options that doesn't much matter.

“Great family hotel” We stayed a week at the Homewood Suites in April 2005. For two adults and two children we had a fair amount of space. The room has a full size kitchen (stove, refrig/freezer, microwave and dishwasher). The living room is a little small, but the bedroom with two queen beds was nice size. There was plenty of closet and drawer space. The bathroom was average size. The living space has a door to the bedroom. There is a TV in both the living room and bedroom. For a family, it was nice to have the kitchen. My daughter was given an antibiotic that needed to be refrigerated. Very handy to have a regular size and cold frig. A few nights we ordered deliver Chinese food and pizza, from the hotel book. Good food that was promptly delivered. We were able to keep the leftovers. There is a Whole Foods about 10 minutes from the hotel. My son has food allergies, so we bought some soy yogurt and soy milk, again so handy to have the frig! The hotel offers a great free hot breakfast and light dinner. We didn't partake in the dinner, but the breakfast was really nice - bacon, eggs, toast plus cold items. The metro is a 10-15 minute walk, to the Orange Line McPherson Square stop. The hotel is in a business district, with no coffee shops or restaurants immediately near by. We walked to Dupont Circle for dinner one night. The room was clean and comfortable. A great escape from a busy day, with room to spread out. We didn't interact with the hotel staff much. We needed a cab very early on our departure day. The hotel found a car service that called to confirm and was prompt for our ride to the airport. I would recommend the hotel.

“They do the basics, miss the details” Had to switch rooms during my stay because there was no king room first night so they put me in a suite just for that night. The suite was awful btw - the "window" was actually a sliding glass door that opened up to the pool and bar (also means it was noisy later than I wanted to be awake. There was almost no light in the suite, and the furnishings were hideous. Transferring rooms mid-stay doesn't work if you had planned to store anything in the safe while out on business... The room where I was transferred was nicer than the suite. Reasonably comfortable. However, no in-room tea or coffee facilities in a hotel advertising that all its rooms have the amenities of home...? Apparently guests are expected to intake caffeine only in the morning, and certainly not in their rooms. That's just wrong. Also I did not understand why a room in San Diego California would be furnished with a duvet on the bed. Duvets work wonderfully in Germany in the winter. But not in SD. You are left with the choice of being very warm or very cold when you sleep. Someone who was obviously not a guest in the hotel - and much larger than me - tried to con me out some cash in the hotel elevator after everyone else had exited. My inner city upbringing saved me there, not Solarmar's security.
“Perfect location” But the hotel is just ok. Rooms just ok. If it wasn't for the location...

“Great value, great location, no pretense” Just returned from a 5-day stay in New York City, and had a great stay at the Hilton Garden Times Square. First of all, the "pros" of the hotel --- and there are many. The price was outstanding for New York City ($140.00/night can't be beat). The location was outstanding - literally one block west of Broadway along 49th - steps away from Times Square. The room was spacious enough for New York - even a family of four survived in the same room for 5 days! The staff of the hotel was extremely friendly and helpful. We requested extra pillows - no problem at all. We needed help with airline checkin prior to departure - no problem. They willingly gave directions as required and the concierge was very helpful to find restaurants on Christmas Day. The "cons" of the hotel are relatively minor in nature - the heating vent clicked at night so we had to turn it off (OK since the weather was perfect for a December visit). The toilet ran one night and the windows didn't tend to keep the sound out, even though we were on the 6th floor of the hotel. In general, the hotel needs a little bit of a "facelift" - a can of paint, new carpet in the hallway - just a little bit of elbow grease will bring this back to a wonderful place to stay. No need to overstate these negative points though - in general this was a great hotel, a great value and a superb find for Manhattan. I would recommend it to friends who will travel to New York in the future.

“Nice hotel - some problems” Had to change rooms on the first night at 8:30pm when I tried to take a shower and had only scalding hot water. To their credit, they sent someone right up, but it could not be repaired. I got a new room, but when I checked out, there was no adjustment on my bill.
