Manager called on Sunday after I arrived home and took that night's stay off the bill. Temp was in the 80's, but hotel closed the pool with 8 hours notice to do concrete renovations. I would have liked to have known this in advance. My replacement room had no microwave - it was in the hall and was not replaced. I did not, however, ask for a replacement or complain, but housekeeping should have known. Otherwise, it was quiet despite being in the direct air traffic pathway of SAT. McDonald's next door, and several restaurants within an easy drive. Of course, for my stay, Route 410 was demolished between the time that I arrived and when I departed. I was sent on an "interesting" detour through the city at 4am to make my 6am flight. A word to the wise: This is a BUSY airport. I spent a full 1 1/2 hours checking in and getting through security for a 6am flight on a Sunday morning. Get to the airport early.

“You'll enjoy it more than the swans do...” Not the least expensive property in the Arboretum, however for what you get it is an incredible deal. The staff is excellent, amenities cannot be beat, and the location is great if you want to do any shopping at all (and I do often!). Unlike many hotels it is easy to get to from all directions and plenty of self parking (good if you're driving around town.) Best of all, the beds have great pillows on them. Only drawbacks are: you pay for wifi, the swans look a little cramped in their fountain, and the pool is a skinny box that is heavily chlorinated. Overall, my favorite place to stay in Austin.

“Really Nice Hotel” The hotel is beautiful. It is an excellent location. There was a few minor issues. The hotel is clearly geared toward the convention and business crowd. There were charges for almost everything, although I did not incur any of these. Our room was a little small for the class of hotel, but not overwhelmingly small. Not a true complaint, but the elevators were very slow. My comparison was that we stayed in an equally aged hotel in a different city during our trip, and the Intercontinental's were significantly slower. That's it, no more little nit picks. The staff was excellent, the doormen being the highlight. The hotel bar was also very nice. The hotel was immaculately clean. I would definitely travel to this hotel again.

“Great hotel wonderful ammenities” This is a great hotel. The location is perfect. You can walk to anywhere in downtown Chicago. It has great views. The rooms are spacious and very confortable. There is a great bar in the lobby. The staff are exceptional and go to any length to make your stay memorable.

“素晴らしホテルです” 数年前に経営が変わりましたが、良いサービスは引き継がれており満足しています。 宿泊した当時は改装後一年程で奇麗で快適でした。 フロントスタッフをはじめ、みんなフレンドリーで感じの良い方ばかりでした。 部屋も改装後で奇麗で良かったです。 別途はクイーンサイズで私一人で宿泊でとても快適でした。 ホテル周辺にレストラン、日常品の買い物なども出来便利だと思います。 屋上にあるバーからの眺めも素晴らしいです。 インターネットはワイヤレスで用意されていました。

“Great property for the price!” Nice large clean rooms! Excellent for the price due to bein somewhat hidden. If you're a Marriott rewards member, they have great sales on rates! Would highly recommend and love staying here whenever I fly into Austin.

“Love this hotel!” Stayed here at least once a month between Feb and June 2011. GREAT Hotel! Super friendly staff - they remembered me after the 2nd visit and always put me in a corner room. The lobby bar is wonderful, low key, quiet and classy. Everyone I encountered was helpful and friendly. I really enjoyed the history of the place. Be prepared, the bathrooms are kind of dark - but very well appointed. French press in-room coffee was an appreciated touch. Wish work would bring me back to Seattle again!

“where Pets are VIPs” Decided to spend the July 4th holiday in downtown chicago with our dog Jimmy. You would be surprised how few hotels will accept dogs. This one doesn't even charge a pet deposit! From the moment we checked in, we felt right at home. The hotel's decor is reminiscent of a vintage office building with the marble walls and wrought iron staircase/elevator facade. The rooms are very comfy and have chaises in front of the bay windows, making the room feel bigger than it is. Our view was right down State Street. The proximity to Millinium Park made our dog walks a pleasure and everytime we returned to the hotel, Jimmy got a warm welcome from the staff as well as the other guests. Would definitely choose this place again!

“Hilton Airport Hotel” Hotel was nice and if you need to be very close to the airport, this is the hotel that puts you in the middle of the airport. You don't hear much noise which was nice. Parking is very expensive like most airports. Room was clean, with a very professional look to it. Had a nice desk to work from and the internet. Staff were very helpful and attentive.

“Nice for Downtown LA” Recently stayed at the Westin Bonaventure while spending time in Downtown LA. Location is good for downtown businesses, but a few blocks away from Staples Center and LA Live. Room was very clean and spacious, recently renovated. Bed was comfy, and staff was very attentive. For the money, it was well worth the price.

“Great Hotel and Great Stay” I chose this hotel since it was right across the street from the Marriott Eastside, where we had a free room for the night. When I checked several weeks in advance, the W was booked. But, when I checked a week before the trip, more rooms opened up, which was good. Unfortunately, we had already booked at another hotel and were issued a cancellation charge when we booked with the W instead. I thought the hotel was in a great location. The lobby was very nice and relaxing. While some people don't like the nightclub vibe and music, I thought it only added to the hotel. The front desk staff were efficient and courteous. We had one of the least expensive rooms on a high floor, but it had a good view and was just big enough for two people. Although, there was not much room to lay out luggage. The furnishings were very cool and the bathroom was very nice. We especially liked the Bliss products. When I was at the Bliss spa, I saw the same travel kit runs for about $20 if you purchase it there. The bed was pretty comfortable too. And, the elevators ran pretty quickly without being too crowded. All in all, I would stay at this hotel again.

“A Pleasant Surprise” I must preface this by saying that we might have gotten lucky on our stay. We were returning from a 5-day trip to Vancouver Island, arrived tired and cold into Seattle for a short night's stay before heading to the airport at 6am the next morning. However, after too many hotels with nice-looking lobbies whose rooms look like they're out of grandpa's fishing cabin, this was a pleasant surprise. We were given a near-top floor room with views of the Space Needle (not a huge deal, we've been to Seattle before). The room wasn't huge, but adequate, and all of the "little things" (TV remote, heating unit, shower pressure) worked as they should. There was even the nice little touch of a Sony Dreammachine CD player/alarm clock - which only took 2 minutes to learn how to operate thanks to an instruction card by the bed. Room service was prompt - food was so-so, but as expected for a 3-star. High-speed net access for $9.95 in the room. Lower level non-water facing rooms could get loud as hotel is right off the interstate ramp. Would defintely stay again for either business or leisure.

“Huge hotel but great service” Gigantic hotel, located 10 min from Dupont Circle up a hill. The property is gigantic and a bit older but well kept, and the rooms are consequently huge. Others have indicated that it was noisy; I found it to be absolutely quiet, even too quiet. The room wasn't made one day for unclear reasons, got a prompt turnover and a gift certificate for the downstairs restaurant comped. Left my phone charger here by accident, and had it mailed to Canada pro bono. Service was top notch.

“5-star service and architecture, 3-star room” The Biltmore is stunning in its architecture and grounds and a fantastic place to plop down in Phoenix during the spring. If you're a fan of mid-century modern, you'll love exploring. Be sure to peek into the conference room spaces, some with soaring gold peaked ceilings - truly unique in design. I encountered true 5-star service from all staff during my stay, including a charming houseman who greeted me in English and then, when I asked for directions to the spa, provided me precise information - in Spanish! Because of his friendly body language and gestures, I was able to infer where to go and when I confirmed it with him ("Oh, across the pool...I see!") he smiled and said "Yes sir!" This kind of interaction is sooooo much better than the typical eyes-down, mumbling "no englais" response one might receive at other properties. As others have noted, the Biltmore is a bit pretentious when it comes to pricing. Even in the gift shop, a 12-oz. can of soda fetches $2.50 - God knows what it is from the minibar. The Biltmore's biggest opportunity for improvement is in the room itself. Once inside it's as if you're suddenly transported to a typical Marriott in a city center location. Large armoires hold a smallish 20-inch tube TV; if they'd banish the armoire and install a proper 42" flat screen, they'd gain substantial psychological space in the rooms. The rooms aren't tiny, but they're below 21st century standards for space. Bathrooms are somewhat cramped, but at least the tub/shower combo is a roomy six-plus-footer so even men can lie fully in the water if they choose. Rainshower heads help when taking a shower. Only a single sink but a wide vanity and an extra full-length shelf above help store toiletries over a multi-night stay. Closets are ample and lighted by opening the door automatically. Beds are new Serta mattresses in the same quality range as the Westin Heavenly Bed, and they include a substantial down topper (removable if too hot during the summer). However, the Biltmore ruins the effect by using cheap 60/40 blend sheets instead of the all-cotton sheets virtually every 5-star property uses these days. Furniture in the rooms is somewhat dated, with a craftsman style but worn and de-laminating tops on many surfaces. Decor is very desert-style but lacks color - too much beige/brown/terra cotta, not any bold color to break up the palette, even in the artwork or accent pillows. Despite the build date of 1929 (or perhaps BECAUSE of it), the room was quiet - and I was in the main building above the lobby. If in the main building, third floor, odd numbers will provide a reasonable view. In-room dining also falls far below a 5-star standard. No roll-in cart here - it's delivered on an uninspired tray with the single indulgence being a fresh-cut whole flower and long stem adorning the side. I ordered a pizza; it came in a delivery cardboard box. 5-star properties that get this right deliver on a silver platter with cover. For its central location and local history, the Biltmore is a hotel you should stay in at least once. You'll have to decide after that if it's worth returning.

“Such a cute hotel!” I stayed in NYC for the dates of 5/11-5/14 on a business trip. I chose the 70 Park Avenue due to its location and decor. Overall I was very pleased, and my impression just got better and better throughout the week. I have broken my review out below into different categories: HOTEL: The lobby is very nicely decorated inside, although I thought the spot between the elevators and the restaurant were very cramped. I was never able to take advantage of the wine and cheese reception because it ended at 6 and the timing was never right. RESTAURANT/BAR: The women who was the supervisor of the morning breakfast was awesome! She was very accomodating and always went out of her way to make sure you had everything you needed. In the bar, the evening bar tender (girl with short brown hair) was GREAT! It was nice talking to her while I dined solo at the bar. BELL STAFF: These guys were amazing! They always opened the door for you and were always there to grab a cab. ROOMS: Very nicely decorated. Small, but that was okay with me as I wastraveling alone. I had no view, which I would've loved to have had. The only major complaint I had about the rooms was that they were very dim. Overall, great stay and I would definently stay again. This hotel is in a great location for business or a relaxing romantic weekend. If you are looking for more of a party atmosphere, I might choose a different neighborhood, as Murray Hill is very quiet at night.

“Nice location” Just returned from a 3 night stay. Hotel was nice but the rooms were very small. Only 2 double beds for 4 people which I find surprising in nicer hotels today and we could not get a rollaway for my teenager due to fire code (even though they list this as an option on their website). But the beds were comfortable which was a nice surprise. Furnishings were a little dated but clean and in good condition. Pool was warm and excercise area was nice with good equipment. There is a Starbucks onsite and the onsited Hertz rental car was great for renting a car for a day or two to explore the area. Room service was prompt and cost reasonable. Desk clerks were a little snooty and not terribly friendly or helpful. Location was easy to find and there is a small mall across the street with several very nice restaurants, a movie theater, and a Macy's. Easy to walk to with the family for dinner and shopping. A Denny's is down the street for a good breakfast if you don't want to pay a fortune at the hotel. Overall I would stay here again.

“Best hotel in Philadelphia!” I have stayed at many hotels in Philadelphia including the Westin, Four Seasons, Ritz Carlton, And Le Meridian. None of these hotels come close to the Sofitel in my opinion. The bed is very comfortable, the down comforter is the best. The rooms are very spacious. If you upgrade to a Junior suite it is 500sq ft. It has 2 plasma and has bath and shower. The soap and shampoo are designer. Checking in was smooth, friendly and efficient The breakfast was a little expensive but very tasty. The service was attentive and fantastic. Overall a great experience. I will return again.
“Nothing special” I had a room on the 7th floor - it was very noisy! Aveda amenities were the highlight. Towels were cheap. Nice gift shop

“Very Nice For The Price” My wife and I stayed at the Whitehall Hotel April 5-9. Yes, it is an OLD but the halls and rooms have been referburbished. The place was clean and the staff very helpful. The rooms are small, after all it is a circa 20-30 hotel, and are very comfortable. If you looking to camp out on your hotel room, this is not the place to stay...go to the Hyatt or Ritz and pay the BIG bucks. You can get a nightly rate at the Whitehall for under $80.00 if u shop around. AND !!! it's located perfectly between the Mag Mile and Rush St. TRY IT. YOU'LL LIKE IT ! Though, I'm not sure it should be a four star...maybe 3.5.

“The Lodge is a nice oasis” Spent two nights here for a corporate event in the Lodge, which is different (and much better) than the main hotel. It is separate building, smaller and more homey, like a real Lodge even though it is in the middle of a busy office park. They have large rooms with high ceilings, which are both modern and classic - well thought out work areas, comfortable bed, but in "classic" style furniture. The rooms overlooking the golf course are FAR superior to those overlooking the parking lot, since there are large glass windows and decks. Although we did not use it, there is also a small "house" that has three or four bedrooms just adjacent to the main building (and this is where Obama stayed during the Democratic Convention). The Lodge has a large living room/fireplace area common, nice decks and patios, and overlooks a pretty golf course. The staff are very friendly and helpful. While this is not a place to go for a true "lodge" experience, if you are staying in south Charlotte this is a comfortable place for work and fun.

“Horrible lapse in service” This is a competent central-city business hotel by and large, but suffered from an INEXCUSABLE lapse in a key service: the business center. At 7 a.m. on a weekday, the center had NO computers with an active internet connection, and the staff who blithely informed me of this took no steps to find me a substitute means of access. They blamed the problem on their vendor of (exorbitantly priced) desktop connectivity, which apparently remotely reboots its subscribed computers.

“Really Great!” Everything about this hotel is great. The rooms are very big, the baths are huge, the bed is super comfortable and the staff isn't just good, they're fun. The ninth floor has a great rooftop deck and the lobby bar is a very nice place to start or end your evening. There are at least 100 restaurants and pubs within a five minute walk and you're just up the street from the Padre's stadium. Imagine a bright and cheerful W, with much bigger rooms, that's the Indigo. The only thing I didn't care for was the band they had in the lobby bar Thursday night. Too loud for the setting, didn't fit the hotel mood or style. Great Mac's in the lobby for your use, free. Did I mention the price? Hundreds less than what I have paid for a comparable hotel. Even with valet parking, $35 per night, it's a steal! This hotel was perfect for our stay and we'll be back.

“Wonderful property if your budget allows” Stayed here for 3 nights while attending a meeting at the convention center. Very sleek modern hotel, spacious room, nice bed, beautiful view, well equipped for the business traveller. Very pleasant service from the staff. Only one slight disappointment, the don't have a Gold/Diamond Concierge room which seems a bit surprising to me for such a large property with a heavy business clientele. The location is right next to the convention center, parking is ample but expensive ($27/night). Has an excellent sports bar and Starbucks on premises. Room service food was excellent, but very expensive. Gaslamp district restaurants are a 5-15 minute walk. Note of caution to families, not much in the way of cheap eateries nearby. Overall, a wonderful hotel as long as your budget allows.

“Great Location and Great Rooms” In an old bank building and right by the riverwalk stairway. convience store right across the street too. also a bus stop nearby for those who need public transportation. the nightly snacks and drinks along with the breakfast are an awesome perk. nice rooms and we had a great time
“Nice hotel with great food” The room was very nice, comfortable bed and spacious bathroom. I stayed at this hotel to attend a conference and the food provided was very good.

“What a view!!” Stayed here during Sept '10 as part of my every-other-year-or-so visits back to NY. This place is located super close to the Empire State Building and Macy's. Also a couple of train stations a few blocks away. It's a nice little walk to Bryant Park as well. Got this place at the last minute and was pleasantly surprised as I didn't really know much about it other than it was a 3 star hotel. For the price, the service, amenities, location, and the room were worth it. Although my room was on the seventh floor out of a possible 20 floors or so, still had a nice clear view of the Empire State Building. The room wasn't necessarily the largest, but there was enough room for a king bed, a desk with chair, and TV console with flat screen TV. The bathroom was good with no problems. Towels and bedding were comfy. The complimentary breakfast had everything, including a waffle maker (my fav). Front desk even gave me a complimentary water bottle before I headed out (had some leftovers I think). Really, there was nothing to complain about and will check this place out first next time I go back to NY.

“Maybe yes, maybe no....” NB: If you are "sleep in after a long night out" kind of person, there is a large construction site right across the street from the hotel. And they start up at 7:30 AM on weekdays. We got up about that time every day, so no big deal for us but take note! If you are the type of traveler that stays at three or four star hotels, skip this place. The bathroom fixtures are ancient, the shower heads low, the water pressure lower, and the heating & cooling is out of the 1950s (steam radiators and window AC units). If you must stay in the neighborhood, try the Mediterranean, which is a block away. It is no 3 star hotel but it is a step up in comfort. If you are a veteran of hostels or public houses, the large rooms, kitchenette, and nice staff will make your stay at the Inn pleasant. (The wi-fi is free but clunky.) There are two large grocery stores nearby, so you can do a lot of cooking if you wish; otherwise, the area abounds in ethnic eateries and pubs. This is an old, fairly rundown place in a funky neighborhood. You are right next door to a cheapo hamburger joint that attracts people looking for a $4 dinner (Dick's). While there, I've seen more than one person pay for lunch with quarters and dimes. If you don't want to rub elbows with the hoi polloi, then you are better off staying at the Roosevelt or Red Lion downtown and taking the monorail to Seattle Center/Key Arena, etc. So, bottom line? We come to this neighborhood every year or two from the Midwest. We usually stay at the Mediterranean but I got a Priceline flight & hotel deal at the Inn. Would I stay here again? Maybe, depending on the price differential, etc. I'd sure consider it.

“Not my favorite W hotel” They upgraded our room from a corner to a suite. The room was still small and the bathroom didn't have a tub. The location was great but not worth the money compared to other hotels we have stayed at in Boston. This W was missing the wow factor I'm used to from this brand.

“Contemporary, Clean, City Hotel” There was very little not to like about the InterContinental Hotel in Boston. It's an imposing new glass structure on the border of the seaport and business districts. It has an entrance on the busy Atlantic Avenue just a few shirt blocks away from South Station, and in partial view of the harbor and channel. The rear entrance is directly on the channel, with beautiful views of the water, federal court house, and children's museum. On the rear patio, there are relaxing places to sit with music and a outdoor bar. The hotel's interior design is contemporary and bright, not stuffy or gawdy. The registration desk could've used a third person, but the line still moved quickly. Bell hops were very helpful. We valed-parked the car at the hotel entrance. To retrieve the car, it was necessary to take a separate elevator to the underground garage and office, which was a little strange, but not that inconvenient. Parking was expensive, but not terrible compared to city hotels. The hotel common spaces were extremely clean and comfortable, as were the banquet areas. Hotel staff, including security guards, managers, bell hops, and room service attendants were all very pleasant. The rooms were a decent size. We had a view of the building under construction next door, as well as a sliver of the channel and Atlantic Avenue. In a nice twist, the bathroom is about as big as the rest of the room. There is a full glass shower, as well as a tub. Very spacious. One interesting feature is a window between the bathroom and the rest of the room. It can be slid closed, but light can shine through at night if someone is in the bathroom. Not a big deal. the room had a huge flat screen tv, plenty of drawers and closet space, a desk, and several chairs. It was a very comfortable, beautiful room. The mattress was not as comfy as I would've expected, but the pillows were nice. I think the best elements of this hotel are its proximity to South Station, the business district, and Quincy Market/North End; its contemporary design and appeal; and its cleanliness.

“Pleasant Hotel” Our room (1525), had a king size bed, flat screen tv and nice decor. The bathroom was a good size with the shower over the bath. Room had coffee making facilities, fridge and microwave. We found the air conditioning too noisy, so we turned it off at night. Breakfast was not included, but went to the breakfast room which had a very poor choice of cereals. There is no free internet. Staff were friendly and helpful. Location of hotel is good, near Hells Kitchen, can walk to many sights.

“Good value for the money, but not a great place - weird location!” I attended a training class in Austin last week and stayed 3 nights at the Summerfield Suites. For what we needed - a place to sleep, basically - it's fine. And we got the "Entertainment" price of $70/night. So overall, we were satisfied. That said, the hotel is on the north side of town in the suburbs, there are really no extras, and we did have a few problems. Summerfield Suites is a converted apartment complex near a mall in north Austin. It's in a basic neighborhood and close to a major bus hub. If you're in building 10 or 11, you get to listen to buses with engines idleing. Not great. The units themselves are large, but very dark. The living room in mine had only 1 window. On the plus side, it had a wood burning fireplace and full kitchen. Breakfast was quite good - full, hot meal and a lot of extras. A definite plus. They also offer a happy hour, but my group never made it. The property seems to be in a bit of disrepair. The spa was out of order the entire week - and I never saw anyone work on it. My unit had quite a few cosmetic blemishes and some plumbing issues. All in all, this was a good value for the money, it was clean and comfortable - just a bit "faded" and in a weird location.

“Third visit in two years, and keeps getting better! Can't wait for #4” My first visit to Palomar Philly was very nice. I have stayed in Palomar's in San Diego, DC, and SF and had high expectations. My second visit had some challenges. This visit was OUTSTANDING. Everything from my early check-in (I was on a red-eye from the west coast), to my fantastic room, to the welcoming service, to the delicious late-night meal in the restaurant. I am now unabashedly in love with this hotel.

“Clean rooms, but very small and cramped” We stayed for one quick night only...checked in around 10:30pm on a Friday night after a looooong, traffic-filled drive from Houston. I was so looking forward to the delicious warm cookie Doubletree always gives at check-in...was very disappointed when we weren't offered one :( Check in was quick and we were given a room on the 3rd floor, facing the elevator...room 314 I believe. I was worried it would be noisy, but I never heard anything that night as I slept. We were surprised at how TINY the room was...and I mean TINY. Smallest Doubletree room I've ever stayed in. There was a closet to the left and bathroom to the right as you walk in the door...bathroom was also very small, but well-lit, which I appreciate. The sink even looked smaller than normal! The rest of the room was nicely decorated with a modern design and dark toned woods, but it was just so cramped because the room was so small. On the far side of the room, between the window and the bed was a stuffed, upholstered chair...literally squeezed between the window and bed so that if you wanted to get in bed from that side, you had to do so from the foot of the bed and crawl up to the pillows, because there was just no room to get between the chair and the bed...they were butted up against each other...and you couldn't move the chair because it was against the window on the other side. There were also 2 nightstands, a large desk, dresser and small side table next to the dresser with a few shelves...I think this was where the coffee pot was? The size of the furniture and the amount of furniture was just too much for a room this small. Fortunately, it was just two of us for a very quick over-night stay. Any longer than that, and the lack of space would have been unpleasant. There was also a microwave and mini-fridge in the room, which was helpful for us since we were in town for a running event and needed a place for our sports drinks to cool down. The front desk was nice enough to grant us a late, 1pm check-out time after we explained we were in town for a running event and could use the extra time to get back and clean up after our race. We appreciated not having to drive back to Houston in sweaty, stinky running clothes :) I'd consider staying here again for a quick trip only though...if we were staying longer, I'd find a different location with larger rooms.

“Always First Rate!” Deciding to do something a little different, we booked our weekend at the Prescott Hotel around the corner. We lasted five minutes before returning to the St Francis to beg for a room! We have stayed in the newer tower with spectacular views to Golden gate, Alcatraz, Bay Bridge... but this time we overlooked Union Square park in a HUGE room with smaller bath. Still... it far exceeded the size of the Prescott, whose hallways, elevators, and rooms (at $400/nt) are uninhabitably small. We will NOT be experimenting again. Why argue with perfection?! We LOVE the St Francis!

“ich war enttäuscht” bin sehr häufig in den USA und auch häufig aber diesmal war ich wirklich enttäuscht. Das Hotel hat wirklich ein Probelm und das ist das Personal. Schon am Checkin war der Mitarbeiter sehr unfreundlich und hat es nciht fertig gebracht die schlüssel richtig zu probrammieren. Beim Frühstück dann waren sogar beim Brot Teile dabei die geschimmelt haben. UNglaublich das hab ich in den Staaten noch nie erlebt. Das Zimmer war wie immer einwandfrei und hatte jeden Komfort.

“Did I stay in a different hotel than the past reviewers?” I normally stay at the Airport Marriott, however for various reasons I stayed at the Renaissance for the first time. Yes, it is in the middle of nowhere, but it is an airport hotel. I did not find any of the age and wear and tear as did the other reviewers. I was greeted very warmly, arrival gift was not an issue, and given a lovely suite (220) which had slightly worn carpet, but looked fresh and was very clean. I did not find magazines, nor anything else in the bed which did not belong there. The wireless internet was quick, quicker than many properties at which I have stayed. No, I don't think you are going to choose this hotel if you are here for the Liberty Bell, but for a quick stop and to be close to the airport it is great. The Airport Marriott still beats it though as it is IN the airport!

“Enjoyed our stay...not an inch of space wasted here.” We arrived via Port Authority and were pleased to find the hotel one block south of the station. Well situated in the Garment District. Convenient walk to Times Square attractions and most of the midtown touristy stuff. I've never stayed in a tri-branded hotel before. What you get here is a 32 story hotel split up into 3 different hotels, the Hampton, a Holiday Inn Express and a Candlewood Suites. Each segment has its own interior design and lobbies, breakfast rooms, etc. Brand new and fresh looking, but I think the building is a few years old. The cramming in of 3 hotels makes for some VERY compact spaces. The hotel room floors have only 6 rooms on each, which was weird as the entire floor felt smaller than my house, but cool in that our room was literally four steps away from the elevators, and going to the ice machine (with a water button!) was like running to the fridge from my living room when I'm home. Now, the room we had up on a mid-20s floor was ultra-compact. I measured it to be approx. 200 sq. ft. It felt quite small, but everything was there and in new-ish condition. Hampton added some nice touches like a bud vase with faux-flower in it on the desk, and TV with HD channels (which made watching the World Cup especially good). The bathroom was tight and useful vanity space was limited. There was only a shower unit in the room (fine by us) and it was decent, except for being quite narrow to the point that an average sized person WILL bang his/her elbow on the wall at least once during your shower. We had a good view of midtown south, featuring the Hudson River, NJ and the Empire State Building. I thought that was very cool. The staff was awesome. Super friendly and playful even...a young bunch of professionals that seem to really enjoy their jobs. It was fun interacting with them. Breakfast was good with a wide selection of quick foods. The title of my review....Not an inch of space is wasted here...can refer to an experience I had on the lower level of the hotel. The level below the lobby features a weight/exercise room, public unisex restroom and a couple of vending machines. That same tiny footprint of the hotel room floors comes into play here as this compact area also is home to the laundry facility, staff rooms and various other hotel functions. Waiting for the elevator to take me back up to the lobby, I shared the tight hallway with two large laundry carts, a housekeeping employee and maintenance worker moving back and forth around the carts, and although I'm not a claustrophobic person, I felt uncomfortable and in the way. The employees were friendly and had a smile, but I couldn't help thinking it is a pain in the butt for them to try to do their jobs literally inches from the general public spaces. Just seemed weirdly intrusive. Oh well, I guess that's life in New York. The Comfort Inn down the block was equally as slim and tight, so I'm sure that's not as unusual as it seemed to me.

“Perfect Hotel For a quick overnight” I was given an airline voucher to stay at this hotel due to a cancelled United Airlines flight. The shuttle picked up from the airport frequently and on-time. The drive to the hotel from the airport takes about 30 minutes, as the shuttle is shared with the near-by Doubletree. Check-in was swamped and slow, but the two agents working it were friendly and doing their best. The bell-man, while waiting in line, came by offering amenities such as toothbrushes, razors, etc. The security officer thoughtfully arranged return shuttle timing to the airport for the morning, both to speed up the line and to ensure that no shuttle would be overwhelmed in the morning. I received a room with 2 queen beds. Upon check-in into the room, I noticed bugs crawling all over one of the beds, and given how short-staffed the check-in was, I didn't bother calling to get a different room. I decided to sleep in the other bed and slept well. The free wireless internet was nice. The bathrooms and amenities were adequate. There was a refrigerator in the room. I noticed the bar was open late, though apparently room service ends at 10pm. There are lots of shops and restaurants in the mall next door.

“Stayed here several times” My wife and I have stayed here several times in 2006. We liked it. Staff was friendly and helpful. We had the deluxe room each time, and it was comfortable. Continenatal breakfast was good. Location is excellent and is in walking distance of the orchestra and theater.

“Great location - recommended if you can swing a good price” We managed to get an excellent third party deal ($135) for this very well located upmarket hotel. I wanted to stay here again but thought $450 was a little more than it is worth and found a better deal elsewhere that night. I was expecting something less than we actually got based on other Tripadvisor reviews but was very pleasantly surprised. Certainly the room we were given was very clean, very comfortable, quite spacious, reasonably quiet and well finished. One of the better NYC sleeps I've had for awhile. Nice touches included fresh fruit in the lobby, very comfortable beds, good bathroom and free wifi. The location is excellent, across the street from Carnegie Hall and a short stroll to Columbus Circle, Central Park or Times Square. There are so many excellent dining options nearby that we didn't actually utilize the hotels restaurant (although it looked great and always busy) Front desk staff were efficient and pleasant and knew the area very well. Curiously, there is a charge for storing luggage (about $3.50 per bag I think). This a hotel I highly recommend if you can chase down a good third party deal....it is very well located and great value if you can swing a good deal.

“Average at Best” My family and I found this hotel on Priceline at the last minute and were pleased with the location and the price, but I'm glad I didn't pay any more than I did. The website gave the impression that they had double rooms with queens, double rooms with doubles, and king rooms. When I arrived, however, I was told that I had been given a single queen room. I asked if there was anything else available and was told that I could have a double queen room for an upcharge. When I asked if I could have a rollaway bed, also indicated on the website, the women at the desk said, "It already has two beds" and offered no other explanation. When I asked why that mattered, she said that it was against the law to put another bed in the room. Overall, she was very condescending and rude, a stereotypical "city snob." The room was nice but showed some wear. The fitness center had a diverse collection of equipment that was well-maintained. The best part about the hotel was its very convenient location. The only convenient parking option was the valet garage next door. The garage clearly gives discounts for patrons who get their tickets validated at about 10 nearby stores, but hotel guests pay full price--$37 for 24 hours. Rude staff, good location, but there are definitely nicer people and better places to stay in Chicago.

“A lovely hotel with a soul” Stayed there for three nights. Central location, perhaps not in the best neighborhood. Hotel parking, restaurant. This is a small hotel with a soul. I got a wonderful room on the 3 floor in the main mansion. Big bathroom and a real Cousy room. Nice hotel staff. Complimentary wifi and free parking. I will mot likely stay there on my next visit.

“Things Just Don't Change” Although the date of stay notes March 2009 (it would not allow you to go back more than four years) we actually stayed there in September 1981 on a tour and the place was a dump 28 years ago too. My wife fondly remembers the cockroaches in the bathroom which didn't help since she was pregnant with our son who is now 27 years old. The rooms were dirty and the staff was rude. At least we spent very little time there as we were out during the day touring NYC. The only thing good about this place is the location and price which is probably the only thing that has allowed it to survive this long.

“Very good stay, excellent location” Stayed for several nights recently while in SF on business. At check-in, I was pleasantly surprised when I learned that the hotel had taken note of the preferences I indicated when I booked - high floor, quiet room. As it turned out, I was on the 11th floor, and my room was amazingly quiet. It was quite warm for a couple days, and it was possible to sleep with the window open - very pleasant. Staff were friendly, the room was clean and had everything I needed, good housekeeping service - overall a really solid choice. The location is excellent - right across from Union Square, just about 3 blocks from the Powell Muni station (BART and streetcars) and the cable car runs right out front. Tons of shopping and food choices in the area.

“Great hotel” I was in Phoenix for a conference. I enjoyed the hotel: nice rooms, great outdoor hot tub and pool. I was in the hot tub before dawn every morning. Good fitness facilities as well. I wanted to make sure I got a chance to see the town while I was there. The hotel has great running maps that take you through the historic district. I recommend a walk or run to see the architecture. It is also in good proximity to local attractions and public transportation.

“Much Appreciated Upgrade!” I have stayed at the Chicago Hilton before for the Cubs' convention in January. It is a great hotel right on Michigan Avenue, close to all the Chicago attractions. This year we stayed there because we could walk to Soldier's field from the hotel and enjoy a Bear's game. I used a reward stay coupon for the stay, and I knew the hotel was sold out due to the Bears' game. I was shocked when they told us at check in that we were upgraded to a suite! The truth was that they put us in a suite on the executive floor that was the size of an apartment. It had a kitchen, living room, large bedroom and bathroom. The view was spectacular! The staff was over the top great to us. I felt like Mayor Daley! Thank you, Hilton Chicago!

“My new favorite hotel in Chicago” One of the BEST hotels I have ever stayed in. Its in a tie position with the St Pancras Renaissance in London. I conducted a very large meeting here with over 120 attendees. This place was incredible, from start to finish. My meeting planner could not say enough positive things about how easy it was to work with this staff. We held our meeting in the historical ballroom, and we invited the hotel "historian" to come in on one of our breaks to present to our audience about some tidbits on the hotel. EVERYONE loved it. Not only is Ryan a great presenter, but just the sheer history of this place, the architectural design, and its location just make is a true pleasure to stay at and the story just rounded out the experience for all attendees. My room was beautiful. I gave it 5 stars, even though it did not get cleaned on one day. However, I ended up having to have my birthday during my stay, and the hotel brought me a bottle of wine and cupcakes. I mean, booze and sweets will make up for any minor discrepancies. I only had a few hiccups in service, which is very rare for Renaissance hotels (I am a Marriott Platinum member, and these are my favorite places to stay). The front desk did not have my Marriott number on file, even though I called in ahead of time to add it to my reservation, and my travel agent had already added it (it was on my confirmation sheet). And, when I asked the concierge about the club lounge and breakfast, she said it was served until 10. When I went up to the club the next morning at 9:30, I found out the food disappeared at 9:00. So,,,,I went back downstairs and asked for local places to go for breakfast. I explained I was gluten intolerant. She suggested breakfast sandwiches at Starbucks (apparently, when I told her I couldn't eat bread, the synapses failed to connect), or eating at the hotel restaurant (which I had already done the night before, and I wanted a change of pace). When I asked for other near by locations, she gave me nothing to work with. Despite my little hiccups, the service, ambiance, and appeal of the hotel made up for it all. The food for our meeting was truly wonderful. AV services were top notch. All the meeting staff were fantastic. Check out my separate review for Mercat. I would recommend a meal here during your stay. You would remiss if you did not sneak a peek at the Ballroom, and the Art Museum on site. And, the fitness facility is one of the nicest I have seen in any hotel.

“Great airport hotel” Came here to spend the night before a morning flight out of IAH. The room was great, although they just changed out the TV when I was there. The breakfast was decent, but not close to the best I have had at a HGI. Parking was ample and driving to the rental car center in the am was a breeze. It was a bit hard finding the place because of its closeness to the Route 8 interchange, but managed to do OK. Definitely better than my other hotel experiences around IAH and would definitely return.

“Nice overall stay” I am a frequent traveler and often seek out Marriott properties and had the privilege to stay at the Residence Inn in mid-October. The hotel has a great location and is close to many good restaurants and bars. The fitness facility is located on the 27th floor which was a nice change to other hotels where the views from the gym are less attractive. Four treadmills and four elliptically to use. Dumbbell weights only went up to 50lbs, but works. I stayed in room 2606 which offered a great view of the city. The room provided a nice king size bed, strong hot water and water pressure in the shower and plenty of space to spread out. The only negative was the slow drain in the sink, but a simple call to the front desk and it can be fixed.

“Lots of annoyances at a good hotel” I've now stayed at this hotel two times. My first stay, two years ago, was much better than my last. The Omni's convenient location could not overcome the numerous small problems that I encountered during my recent stay. It all began at check-in. I arrived late at night because of weather delays, so I was hoping to go straight to bed. Unfortunately, the room I had been assigned had not been cleaned by housekeeping prior to my arrival. So, I headed back to the reception desk. The gentleman there apologized & gave me another room. This room was very nice & probably a little larger than the premier level room I had reserved. The room was clean and very comfortable. Unlike other guests, I had no noise issues whatsoever. I did, however, have other annoyances. The Omni Select Guest program gives members a complimentary morning beverage. You fill out a card & hang it on your door at night, then room service brings the beverage in the morning. At check-in, the clerk told me that unfortunately, they were out of the cards. I found this odd. The next morning, they still didn't have them. Finally in the afternoon, the cards arrived from somewhere. It may sound small or petty, but in the hospitality industry, little things mean a lot. The rest of my stay was thankfully uneventful. My involvement with the Omni did not end at check-out. When I checked my credit card balance a few days later, I noticed the charge on my account was more than my actual bill. After several calls to the hotel, the accounting department determined that I was charged for someone else's stay and they, in turn, were charged for my stay. I guess we checked in on the same day and had similar names. The whole thing was bizarre. At least they eventually figured out what happened and my card was credited for the difference. As an additional annoyance, Omni Select Guest has still not awarded my airline miles after almost a month. Overall, the hotel is nice, but the rooms are really showing their age. The staff is friendly and the location is great. The numerous annoyances I experienced, however, have led me to believe that I will search for a new hotel during my next stay in New York.

“Excellent location!” Stayed for a night at the Grand Hyatt New York. This was my first stay here since they finished renovations, and I have to say I really liked the result! Arrived the hotel early at 10 am in the morning, and did not expect to be able to check in so early, but the hotel had a room ready, and I was upgraded from a Grand King room to a Grand Deluxe King, staff in the reception was very friendly. The room was nice and pretty large by New York standard, and everything was clean. As a Hyatt Gold Pass Diamond member I also had access to the Grand Club on the 16th floor which also has been refurbished, and had a good selection. Late check-out was also not a problem, had the room until 2 pm. Overall it was an excellent stay, to bad it was only for one night. Will defiantly be back here next time I am in New York!

“Nice!” The location and service at this hotel are top-notch. Like many other Kimptons and similar hotels, the design aspects are important to some people. Not so much for me, although I did enjoy the unique and creative style of both the room and the common areas. While these are nice, they are not something I would necessarily pay extra for. That said, the things about this hotel that did matter to me, i.e., location, cleanliness and service, were all very good. The staff do an excellent job in all respects. The location is about 1 block from Boston Common, with lots of dining, bars and other attractions nearby, and the room was immaculate. The hotel is also one of the pet-friendliest I've ever been to. It's not inexpensive, but for what you get, I think it's a good value. My only complaint relates to sleep quality. The A/C never really cooled all that well, and the weather was hot, so the room was a bit warm. The bed was a bit too soft for me, but I realize that's a matter of personal preference. But for the A/C issue, I would have rated it as excellent.

“New hotel, OK” The hotel is new. Staff is pleasant, breakfast is fine but not outstanding. I had booked nine nights, but left after two, because the windows are sealed and I like to sleep with an open window. A few things were irritating, such as a bad fax number on the web site. No fridge or microwave in the room. Expensive for what it is.

“average” Spacious rooms - mine was larger than a 4 seasons suite. However, the furnishings are ordinary and a bit tired and service is a bit indifferent and spotty. Dont expect a concierge. I noticed a lot of noise outside the hotel and discovered it was the fire department responding to a call in the hotel. Curiously, the alarms never rang - not a comfortable safety situation. I had breakfast one morning and was totally ignored - i visited the buffet, ate, read the paper, wrote some notes and finally left. Nary a hello from anyone and the place wasn't busy. I suppose the amount paid (zero) was commensurate with the quality of the service. The dinner band is very loud and food is ordinary. The hotel is generally acceptable and within an easy walk to the downtown area.

“Not a business friendly hotel” If you need to come to San Francisco or work reasons... stay far away from this hotel. Hilton is so concearned with collecting $10 per day, per device ... that they have forgotten to provide quality, always on internet access. Sending an email can take 20 minutes... downloading a file can take an hour... if it it works at all! Printing any document will cost you... money and lots of time. It would be cheaper and faster to buy a printer in SF and through it away when you are done. Hilton should be embarrased for having this badly run property with its name on it.

“Nice location and room with great view” Westin Seattle is located only 4 blocks from the Pike Place Market. You can find plenty of shopping and dining in the area. My room on the 33rd floor had a direct view of the Space Needle. All the staffs were friendly and helpful. I will stay here again next time in business or for fun.

“Ci tornerei! Ottima posizione, accogliente” Ottima posizione, vicinissima a Times Square ed ai trasporti pubblici. Abbiamo soggiornato in due diverse camere, entrambe con bagno grande, una camera di dimensioni piu ridotte, ma comunque accogliente ed elegante. Staff molto disponibile. Unica nota negativa il servizio internet a pagamento con tariffe di ca. 8 dollari per 15 minuti di connessione e stampe a pagamento nel business center.

“Very nice hotel” This was the second time I have stayed in this location. I like it because it is away from the noise and congestion of downtown Austin and Sixth Street, but within a short drive of all the attractions. The rooms are clean, very large and the free cooked-to-order breakfasts are better than what is available in most restaurants. Daily newspapers are complimentary as well. The two swans (Butch & Sundance) swimming in the lobby adds a touch of class. The room has large-screen HD televisions in both the living room and the living room, a work desk with free internet and a wet bar with refrigerator and microwave oven. The bed was very comfortable and the hotel very quiet in the evenings. For the shoppers, there is a mall practically across the street and several others nearby. I highly recommend this hotel when traveling through Austin.

“Older, ornate hotel, but I didn't love it” I was pretty excited to stay at the hotel, and I'll say that I was a bit let down by it. My room was very large and clean, but it felt old and outdated. The entire hotel has an older feel to it, but at some point the bathroom and the room appointments should be updated. The bed wasn't exceptionally comfortable, but the room was quiet and I had a pleasant stay. The service is terrific, especially at the gym, where I was greeted and offered towels and snacks. The gym itself has limited machines and a pool. The hotel location is just off of Market St., which was convenient, near plenty of restaurants and stores. Given the volume of hotels in the immediate area, I'd probably stay somewhere else next time, as I didn't find this hotel to be worth the price tag, but if you're looking to experience a regal hotel, this would be a good spot to do so.

“Great location for NYC!” We stayed here for 5 nights from the 29th Sept - 4th October 2012. We booked one room for 4 adults. We found the hotel to be extremely well located, we got the Air Train from JFK to Jamaica followed by the Lond Island Railroad to Penn Station and the hotel was 2-3 blocks fron Penn, really easy to find and brilliant access for the subways/trains. We arrived early and our room was ready we were able to check in straight away, the staff were very efficient and helpful. Our room was very clean and well stocked, it was a bit of a squeeeze having 4 adults in so next time i'd book 2 seperate rooms. The bathroom was very nice and great shower. We had to wait a day or so to get a safe deposit box as they were all full, so that's my only real complaint, but still very minor. I didn't experience any problems with the lifts, if any staff were waiting for the lifts also they w ere very curteous and would let us take it first. The breakfast I thought was great, just a buffet but a good selection of items from, cereals, breads, pancakes, cooked breakfast and fruit, more than what you need to fill up to start your day, we never really had a problem finding a seat, althought i can imagine in real busy periods it'd be a bugger. Free internet access and printing services, bargain. Stay here again? Sure I would, we had a blast.

“Second time here - love this place!” Spent six nights in NYC with my 17 year old daughter checking out NYC colleges. We wanted a centrally located hotel that also offered us some space. This hotel met our needs beautifully. Check-in was easy and they were happy to watch our bags until our room was ready (we got there around noon). The warm choc chip cookies were a nice touch. Our room was very spacious with a living room area (sofa, easy chair, big tv, storage for clothes, desk and chair, wet bar, mini fridge, safe and microwave), and a bedroom complete with tv set and very comfy king sized bed. Bathroom was accessible from both rooms which was nice - my daughter could easily use the bathroom at night without disturbing me. Being right on Times Square means a lot of light comes into your room at night if you leave the blinds open. The thick blinds provided did a good job of blocking out the light. The room was relatively quiet too - only heard the odd siren at night. Didn't eat in the restaurant but had drinks in the Ad Lib bar a couple of nights. Reasonable prices especially if you take advantage of their happy hour. Went before going to a show and got lots of food for, I think it was, half price. Location is fabulous. Walk out the door and you are right in Times Square (by the TKTS booth). The subway stop is right by the door. There are tons of restaurants close by - just walk a block or so away from Times Square to find more reasonable prices and smaller crowds. We both agreed we would stay at this hotel again without a second thought.

“Andra was sophisticated, comfortable and friendly!” I have always stayed closer to the financial side of Seattle (W, Fairmont, Monaco) but I decided to branch out and try a new hotel in the hip Belltown neighborhood after seeing a great offer on Travelzoo. What a pleasure it was to stay at Hotel Andra. Very friendly non-assuming staff immediately had my luggage inside before I got out of the cab! If one thing stands out about Andra it is the details. High end furnishings, bedding and great service combined with Plasma TV's in the rooms made for an enjoyable new experience in Seattle. The bartenders at Lola's (hotel restaurant) were very friendly and open late. I also enjoyed the four block walk to Pike Place Market on Sat. I will definately go back to Andra on my next trip.

“Very Satisfied with The Omni” My fiancee and I stayed at this hotel from January 6th through January 9th and we were both very satisfied. I experienced my quickest check-in ever, about 45 seconds (no kidding). First, the hotel offers a free shuttle to and from the airport, which saved us money on cab fare. If you do not rent a car, a cab will cost about $25.00 to downtown with tip. The room was a little on the small side, but still very nice. I liked the two sinks and the bed was very comfortable. We accidentally broke a lamp in the room through our own negligence and we were concerned that we would have to pay for it. When we returned to our room later that night we had a new lamp and the Omni never charged us. The Omni was within walking distance of a few restaurants so that made things easier for us. The indoor pool was awesome. I've never swam in such a warm indoor pool before. The indoor hot tub was being repaired, but we used the one outside. What I liked most about the Omni was the fact that the pool areas and fitness center were open 20 hours a day (5 am to 1 am). The only minor complaints I had were low ceilings in the bathroom (I'm 6'5") and the distance to downtown. Other than that, the staff was very friendly and courteous. I will definitely stay here again and now I see why guests of the Oprah Winfrey show stay at Omni Hotels.

“Good Hotel For Business” I stayed here for two nights. I was VERY VERY THANKFUL the hotel allowed me to check-in early in the a.m. Some hotels just will not allow this even if space is available. They saved the day for me. The room was large clean and well appointed. VERY comfortable bed. No extra fee for internet, water, and use of facilities. The Molly Trolley stops right in front of the hotel to take you to the downtown eateries for free. All of these things make a difference to me in figuring out if I would return. The only con is that I found the front desk to be sort of lukewarm towards our business group. No smiles or emotions, just getting the job done. After they would get off the phone with a guest, they would roll eyes, make curt comments, shake head, etc . . . I would definitely stay here again for business if the price is right.

“Pretty Darn Nice!” First of all, I am a huge fan of Embassy Suites when I am travelling on business. I like the fact that you have two rooms, a microwave, a little fridge, and free breakfast. I don't expect charm, but what's charming about a business trip? To my way of thinking, this is an especially nice Embassy Suites. I arrived at about ten o'clock on a freezing cold, snowy night since the United flight was two hours late (shocker!). Yes, the lobby is cavernous and barn-like, but the room was nicely and cheerily decorated, with five fluffy pillows on the bed, a yellow velvet duvet and yellow velvet bolster pillow. Everything appeared to be brand new. The room was very quiet (amazing for an airport hotel) and the sheets were nice and soft and didn't feel as if they had been washed a million times. Breakfast is available beginning at 5:30 a.m. so you can zip down and get a cup of coffee as soon as you get up. And the breakfast looked pretty good. Boston hotels are astronomically expensive these days, so to find a comfortable place to stay for way less than $200, and only a 15 minute cab-ride from downtown is pretty nice!

“Great hotel, great location” This is an excellent hotel. I booked it after a couple of recommendations and finding it in a couple of places I use to find cool hotels and I'm happy to say it didn't disappoint - when I spoke to some friends in Austin they said 'ooh - that's the coolest hotel in town'. And I'm inclined to think it might be.... So the style - well, it's an old motel that's been seriously remodelled. So it's mostly single storey and the rooms open onto courtyards and outdoor walkways - much nicer than the usual lightless hotel corridors. There's a nice (small) pool and a great covered courtyard for breakfast, a beer and wine bar and a seriously good coffee joint (Jo's) in the parking lot. We stayed in a standard room, the smallest one with it's own bathroom, and it was great. Kind of a shabby-chic vibe (bare concrete floors, vintage-y bathroom) but cute, comfy and relaxing. Location is excellent - right in the heart of South Congress, opposite the excellent Continental Club, super-close to some great shopping and restaurants and seemingly 10 minutes from anywhere we wanted to go Downtown. Some people have complained about noise from inside and outside the hotel but for us, this was no issue at all. Downsides? The room was a little dark, the airconditioner was the noisiest thing I've ever heard, there was no in-room fridge, the bar closed at 12 and the shower was a bit weedy. But the up-sides? Great location, comfy bed, great styling, excellent coffee from Jo's, fabulous room service breakfast (the cracked egg sandwich is brutal, but amazing), cool staff and a very relaxing place to come back to. The perfect place for someone wanting all-services 5-star business travel? No. But if you want somewhere cool, memorable and likely to make you want to stay around, stay here. Vibe by the bucketload - and isn't that what Austin's about...?

“Check the Hotel Web Site First” First of all, make sure that you check the hotel's own website for special rates and packages before scouring other hotel discount websites. I could have saved a lot of time by doing so, as I found when I discovered a lower rate than the one I had obtained on Priceline. I did get a refund from Priceline to match the hotel's lower rate, but there were still certain limitations to having booked on Priceline versus directly through the hotel (e.g., I couldn't use my Wyndham Rewards card for points and free internet). The hotel itself was good- lovely, spacious lobby and friendly, helpful staff. Concierge was great. The lobby bartender was particularly helpful and pleasant but the prices were kind of hard to swallow. I agree with other reviewers- the location is quite central, especially for conventioneers, although you have to be careful how far you wander because you can be in rough area very quickly.

“Loved it” We booked a Deluxe 1-bedroom Suite and it was gorgeous. There was a separate bedroom and lounge and a huge bathroom with a two person jet tub, which was wonderful. The lounge had a huge sofa, separate comfy chair and a desk. The bedroom had a huge bed and a fridge style minibar. No kettle / coffee machine, but tea and coffee are available in the foyer in the mornings. There were loads of lights, all on dimmers, and plenty of plug sockets. Also loved the animal print bathrobes - grrrr! Service was very friendly throughout and the hosted wine hour is a delight. The location is very central with lots of shops nearby. We ate breakfast in Square 1682 and it was delicious, with good service. We also ate lunch here on one day, and the Pulled Pork Sandwich was the best I have ever had. Would definitely stay here again.

“Good hotel, would use again.” Good hotel and reasonable price for the downtown area. Within walking distance of several visitor attractions, though Houston is a bit spread out. Better breakfast than at the Magnolia in Dallas, we thought. Free wifi. Expensive valet parking (again) - found we could park in the garage in the same block for considerably less, without the wait for someone to fetch our car. Why do people put up with valet parking?

“Nice Historic Hotel in Uptown Charlotte” The Dunhill is a small, historic hotel located right in the heart of Charlotte's uptown area. It is in a great location as there are dozens of bars & restuarants within several blocks of the hotel. The hotel is small and the lobby is elegant but not grand. There is a small bar near the entrance and their restaurant Monticello (which was great for breakfast and previously have a very good dinner there). The rooms are decent size, clean, well lit, comfortable and equipped with an HD TV. Uptown Charlotte has lots to do and we went restaurant / bar hopping for the one evening in town. Whiskey River was fun for a club and we enjoyed a nice jazz band at Blue. Overall, a pleasant stay. The Hilton, Omni, Westin and Hilton are much larger hotels and have a more varied environment (I like the Hilton the best of that group) but Dunhill is great if you are looking for quaint, quiet but close to the action.

“Der 3. Aufenthalt und wieder sehr zu empfehlen” Das Hotel gehört zwischenzeitlich zu Holiday Inn hat aber an seiner persönlichen Note nichts verloren. Die Lage ist für verschiedene Ziele in LA hervorragend. Das nicht im Zimmerpreis enthaltene Frühstück ist nun perfekt und sehr zu empfehlen, die Zimmer und die Hotelanlage waren sehr sauber. Das Personal war sehr freundlich, die Vorbuchung sehr persönlich. Ein kleiner Wehrmutstropfen war dann nur die Abrechung eines falschen Buchungsbetrages der jedoch nach einem Hinweis schnell korrigiert wurde.

“Great Value” This hotel is nicely located and well kept. The service was fantastic all the way from the check-in, house cleaning, food service and check-out. Given the cost in comparison to the other nearby hotels, this is a thumbs up. What you can expect: 1) Mostly clean rooms. I would say that the carpet is a bit dated and could be replaced, but the hotel staff does it best to keep the rooms clean. 2) Great location on the Marina. 3) Comfortable place to stay. 4) Friendly smile and helpful attitude from front desk.

“Nice and convenient property” The Country Inn & Suites was where I spent a night recently when a tropical storm was forecasted for our area. I used gold points for a free room. This particular hotel is located in a very convenient location adjacent to I-295, with multiple restaurants, gas stations, and shopping nearby for those of you who like to spend. The hotel itself is right on the edge of I-295 but the location is not loud. It is adjacent to a La Quinta Inn and a Denny's restaurant. The grounds are not particularly attractive but it was neat and groomed. Check-in was relatively easy, although the room I was originally given was still undergoing cleaning, so the front desk clerk intercepted me and gave me a new room and key prior to getting to the room. The room iteslf, a standard 2-queen bed guest room, was clean and relatively new. The bed was extremely comfortable with some sort of pillow-top pad. The room had a microwave, refrigerator, high-speed internet (free), and a good TV with about 60-70 cable channels. The bathroom was clean and modern with a marble-type countertop and the shower worked well. Most notably about this hotel, on the night I stayed (and all Wednesdays) there is a manager's reception in the evening with free beer & wine and snack foods. The snack foods turned out to be more than snack foods...they had it catered from Carrabba's Italian restaurant, so there was chicken marsala, meatballs, plus nachos, and other appetizer-type foods. It was really impressive. You could have made a meal on it. I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone spending a night in the Jacksonville/Orange Park, FL area.

“Great hotel, quiet and comfortable.” We stayed in a junior suite, no kitchen, for one night when moving our son into GWU. The hotel is reasonably close to the school. The positives are a comfortable, clean, quiet room with lots of seating. The king size bed was comfortable. The bathroom was large and well appointed. We didn't use the hotel restaurant or room service as there were plenty of restaurants (and a CVS) within 2 blocks. I would stay here again. The one negative, and the reason I can't give this hotel 5 stars, is that when we checked in we asked if we wanted a kitchen. I asked if there was a price difference and was told yes so I declined as we really didn't need it for one night. Then we were told we would get a room with a balcony. Great. Except when we checked out there was an additional $10.00 fee for the balcony. We didn't notice the charge until we were getting into our car, and we were in a hurry because we were trying to leave before the hurricane hit, so we let it go. But I feel that it was sneaky. We should have been asked if we wanted to pay more for a room with a balcony but it seemed like they just wanted to get a few more dollars. Other hotels have been much more forthcoming about their pricing and upgrades. Oh - and they put us on a floor where they were changing the rugs and the hallways had a noticable chemical odor. Considering that because of the hurricane they were pretty much empty it seemed like poor form on their part. I['m sure they would have changed our room if we asked but it had been a long day and the itself didn't smell. I think if I stayed here again I would be very careful and specific with the pricing etc.

“Worn-out Kimpton” We stay at Kimpton hotels often. Agree with other review--furnishings bordering on shabby, carpet stained in hall, finish in tub chipping, rooms are small, bathroom really small. Bed was comfortable, wireless worked well, room was clean. Great location, nice lobby & very nice bar in lobby. Service at front desk not up to up Kimpton standard. We had trouble with reservation which I had changed online. Change had disappeared along with reservation. Front desk person charged us walk-in rate. Went into room & onto the net. Net price was over $50/nt cheaper (even lower than it would have been originally for our 3 nt. stay booked online). Ultimately fixed this over the phone in acceptable way--but expected more from front desk (at least some commiseration with our plight after having traveled 8+ hrs. to get to lobby). Some housekeeping issues as well--non-allergenic blanket looked like came from summer camp. Elevator delays. This is first Kimpton that we have not wanted to go back to. Sad to say.

“Great Location” Check-in was quick and friendly. Room was on the 13th floor. Rooms are quite small, but accommodate a large king bed, chair, and desk. The bathroom was large and very clean. Since this is an old remodeled building the hallways are quite wide. Nice flat screen TV with many channels, and free wifi. The weekend I stayed the hotel was very busy and yet there was little to no noise from the outside into the room. Lobby is nice, there is also a restaurant attached to the property and there is a small mini market located in the lobby for purchasing of snacks etc. There is also a business center, swimming pool and fitness center. The hotel is located about 5 minutes away from the Seattle Metro Transit Tunnel.

“great place!” We stayed for a weekend and had a weekend package with good rates. The room was spacious and clean and the bed was very comfortable. Our package had breakfast included in the restaurant and it was good. The hotel is in a good location, near a Metro stop. We didn't have a car so parking was not an issue for us. I think the hotel is a little pricey during the week, but for the weekend, it was great. I would definitely stay there again.

“Beautiful hotel, great personal service, but charge for wi-fi” Here for a business meeting. Checkin, bag handling, room all very nice. Beautiful room. But...and a big but, there was no high speed Internet access in the room, and there was a charge for wi-fi! I was completely dumbfounded and asked just to be sure. Despite the great location, customer service, and impeccably clean room, I would go somewhere else if this was on my dollar...it was not. It is amazing to me that a hotel of this high level would be this backward.

“Great Stay” I just got home from a great stay at the Larchmont Hotel (Stayed 2 nights 13th & 14th of September, Room # 1W2). After reading previous reports on the rooms with the shared baths, I reserved what they have lists on the web site as a “Family Room” ($199 & $229, total with tax $492.23), because of the rate I thought the room would be little more than a walk in closet, but for the rate I mentioned, I was willing to gamble. In my humble opinion the gamble paid off in spades, first the positives: (1)Location, it’s located on a fairly quiet street two blocks north of Washington Square Park (which I think is the coolest neighborhood in NYC) (2)A Nice Sized Room, (see photo’s) there were two separate rooms both small, with 10’ ceilings (3)What looked like brand new window AC units (one in each room) and both rooms had ceiling fans. (4)Both rooms a small flat screen TV’s (5) Good size closet with robes & slippers, four sets of towels and extra blankets and pillow And now the negatives (and when I say negatives again in my opinion these are all very very minor issues): (1)They only give 1 set of keys and it takes 3 different keys to get from the street to your room (2)The rooms only had 1 twin bed and 1 single with a roll out under it (3)Small chest of drawers (but a decent size desk with drawers in the front room, but all furniture seemed to be new and in good condition) (4)There was construction going on right next door (started a 9:00 AM) (5)It’s a little bit of a hoof to the subway stations (3ish blocks down on 6th or 4ish over to Union Square park) The bathroom: (1)Small but adequate (see photo’s) (2)Good supply of toiletries (good quality soap, shampoo, conditioner & sewing kit) (3)Instead of a small little shelf or having to use the toilet tank as a shelf they have a full size mirror medicine cabinet over the sink The staff: (1)Other than check in/out (we got to the hotel at noon expecting to just drop the bags, but they had the room ready and checked us in) and having to ask how to find my room and how the locks worked (god did I feel like and idiot) I did not have any contact and cannot speak of any rude behavior (2)Chamber Maid, did a nice job on my room (clean and neat, no complaints) (3)They do offer a continental breakfast (did not partake so I can not give an opinion, but it did sound a little goofy that you had to go to the desk show your key and then they would take you to the breakfast room) Again, in my opinion there is no reason not to stay in this hotel, as in previous post I would stay away from the rooms with shared bathroom, though the price is attractive. Next trip to the big city you can bet I will be staying at the Larchmont on West 11th.

“Stay here if you HAVE to be somewhere nearby” I concur with others who say that the staff here is very nice and helpful. Indeed! But..... this past week was my 3rd or 4th stay in 4 years and while the rooms have finally been repainted and renovated there are still issues. I rate this "below average" as compared with other Hamptons. Here are the issues I had: a) door lock to room was so difficult to actually lock that there were times that the door appeared to be locked but wasn't. In fact, when I arrived to check-in to the room, the door was unlatched! b) The breakfast was dismal. To be fair, the Hampton Inn corporate brand standards have been steadily diminishing over the last three years but the egg-pucks are just nasty. I was surprised that neither morning I was there was there any breakfast meat. Poor form. (The ventilation system in the hotel needs upgrading; for 1/2 the day whenever you got on the elevator, you were hit with greasy-egg smell) c) The internet was the worst, by far, of any Hilton HHonors property I have ever stayed in in 12 years as a Hilton Gold or Diamond. I did several speed tests and at no time was it faster than 56K (e.g., dialup would have been faster!) d) The breakfast area is the smallest of any Hampton I've ever stayed in. e) The "business center" is one computer right across from the front desk in the path of traffic. The hotel needs some very serious refurbishment which would include tearing out some walls and adding some junior or better suites. I needed to be literally 1/8 of a mile away so chose to stay here again, but if I am less geographically restricted, there are lots of much better and newer (and often cheaper) HHonors options within 15-20 minutes. I hate being this critical, and the staff really and truly is nice and helpful, but the property is just not up to its Hampton peers these days.

“Fantastic Hotel” Fantastic hotel, couldn't have been happier. Excellent, courteous staff. Great suite, lounge area, kitchen, balcony and separate bedroom, and great bathroom. Spent two nights there and wished we stayed longer. Breakfast was included and was delicious, lots of different choices. Office with computers and printers was included which was great. 5.30-7.30 was happy hour and we certainly enjoyed that. If you are going to Philly and not sure where to stay, do yourself a favor and stay here...one of the best hotels that I have stayed in.

“Even a princess like me liked the Wellington” Due to a miscommunication between my husband and me (and a lightning fast click on Priceline!), I found myself booked into the Hotel Wellington for 5 days. I was nervous about this because I had read the mixed reviews on Trip Advisor (even though we got the room for only $200 a night). The Hotel Wellington has several things going for it: 1. Location, location, location. Within walking distance of SO much. 2. Service-oriented employees: the receptionists were helpful with so many questions. The bell hops were personable and helpful. The manager gave us a free upgrade for the asking. 3. Clean and safe. Very clean, and no safety issues. 4. Decor is pleasant (sort of old glamour, slightly faded). If you're looking for a reasonably priced, clean safe place in midtown, give the Hotel Wellington a try.

“Very Nice, standard Hyatt fair” Hotel was very nice. We had a semi corner room that could see the bay bridge. Ammenities were all there and standard fair for a upscale business hotel. One downside however was the rotating restaurant. Wasn't really worth it for the price and the wall was a tad dirty, so ever full rotation, we would see that black smudge on the wall. There are so many great restaurants in SF that I would recommend that you look elsewhere for either drinks or food. The bar downstairs in the lobby was also a bit wanting. Not too many people, and tried to be a little too hip for what it really was, a lobby bar.

“Returning next Month - superior service, terrific location” Stayed at this hotel specifically because I liked responses from hotel general manager. I am returning because I liked the service, price, experience and location of the property. My Marriott loyalty was acknowledged with an appreciated complimentary suite upgrade. The consistently available concierge provided excellent dining suggestions, etc. Pricey parking should be expected. The bell staff took excellent care of my oversized Hertz SUV. Saturday was personal expense - meters close by allow you to pay during the evening in advance for an hour or so the next morning.

“Oldie but goodie” Downtown hotel located conviently within short walking distance of the last light rail stop. The hotel in nice, clean with a very helpful staff. Many old hotels have large rooms but it's not the case here. We had a king bed but the room was small, not a major deterrent in staying here. From here, you can walk most places in town including the Pike St. Market. Light rail takes you directly to the airport or Mariners or Seahawks stadiums. A great location if you plan to be in Seattle without a car.
