“Just okay. Trying to be a scene, but the scene was missing...” Nice enough, as W Hotels go. Lobby interior was lavish and fun, but just felt cavernous for the few people who were lounging around. Cool and a bit antiseptic, seems designed for a big crowd to bring the fun out. If the crowd is there, I can see it happening. But as it wasn't... Rooms were fine. Beds fine Staff was fine. Nothing memorable.

“Not very impessed - from a diamond member” After checking in, I was sent to a non-smoking that smelled like an ash tray (usually I just grin and bear it - but I couldn't hang). You would think that whomever stuck my diamond treats (candy bars, chips, etc) would have walked in the room and said "crap, this room smells terrible, we shouldn't stick a diamond member in here". Well that didn't happen. I called down and asked for a new room, and the guy said "we have plenty of other rooms" and then started choosing a new room while I was on the phone. He should have said "come down to the front and I'll have your new room key ready", instead after a minute of listening to keyboard clicking I came up with that solution on my own. I guess these things can't be helped, but there must have been some young girls sporting event in town, as it was crawling with loud girls, music pumping in their rooms. The phone at my desk (room 339) sounded like I was making a phone call from outer space. It was hot outside, but the AC struggled to keep up and I would have preferred it to be 3-4 degrees cooler in the room, though the temp was set low it never seemed to achieve it. Also, the icemakers are outside, and you can imagine that they aren't very efficient in 100+ degree heat, so there seemed to be a lot of ice hoarding going on given the many families staying here. I did not have a great experience and would choose to stay elsewhere next time.

“Made it! Yes...it is possible to stay here 3 nights and it's OK! :)” Just completed my 3-night stay while attending a conference nearby. It started out pretty decent, and finished with a pleasant conclusion. The middle...nothing that I couldn't live through. As several have mentioned already, this "motel/hotel" is extremely well situated to the famed, historical Gaslamp District. However, being that close and being downtown, you will be exposed to plenty - and I mean PLENTY - of homeless, even less-than-desirable locals. It's a fact of life in a big city - but perhaps that would be the deciding point of whether you stay at this location with children. Yes, the CI is old - obviously old - but they are doing what they can to maintain and upgrade. You could hear it start early in the morning, and last most of the day. You best look elsewhere if you're going to be concerned about dusty/musty corners of bathtubs where they meet the bathroom walls; you best look elsewhere if you're concerned about window-installed air-conditioners; you best look elsewhere if you're not pleased about the awkward setup of the "sink" being literally beside the beds, completely off-situated from the bathroom. You DEFINITELY can stay here if you're open-minded, willing to accept age and not-so Pot Purri smelling carpets, noisey ceiling fans, noisey air-conditions (but at least they WORK!), and the occassional less-than-chi-chi local hanging around the front. Keep to yourself, do your thing, enjoy the Gaslamp, a ballgame (within minutes of walking out the front door I might add), catch a movie (literally feet out to the west of the front door), or hit Buca for a fat, sodium and CARBO-infused fill-your-face-a-thon right next door. Dorine was really pleasant, as were the rest of the front desk staff. Soda machines on 1st (didn't work) and 4th floors (bill slot was jammed/coin slot worked). Just be forwarned...the "20oz bottle" appearing on the front of the machine is NOT what you're paying $1.50 for! :) Snack machine on 3rd, ice on 2nd... Breakfast is ok - I mean, for what you're paying and what's available at other "motels/hotels" in the area, it's probably about as good-as-it-gets (bagged eggs - warmed-up; sausage links, bagels, english muffins, peanut butter, cream cheese, yogurts, 5 cereal dispensers, waffle-maker, and so on. Finally...upon checkout (contrary to what is currently advertised on their website), I was provided a taxi voucher to get me back to the airport. Nice touch... free round-trip I guess you could say. Oh, and speaking of out-dated website....there isn't any popcorn... :( But you can pick-up a box of microwave popcorn at nearby convenience stores. I can't say I didn't survive the stay. Will I bring my wife and 11-year-old daughter to my next visit in San Diego...ummm...no, not at all. But if I have to come for business or a conference again? Heck ya! I'm good with it...and even ventured out on my own at most normal hours of the day and night with narry a problem. Lots of Law Enforcement and even Private Security folks on bikes to ensure the Tourist Trap keeps'em comin' back! Bon Voyage!

“There are trade offs - but it's cool & the location is amazing” If a big room or an amazing view is what you are after - you won't be happy here. But if you are willing to compromise space & light for a super cool Manhattan experience in a fantastic location - then this is perfect. We read all about the small rooms so "upgraded" to a superior queen - which was still super small but workable and I think the bathroom was marginally bigger and thus small but again workable! It is very dark - but that's OK as when in the room we were sleeping or relaxing anyway - and there are so many options in terms of bars to go and sit and enjoy (although the drinks are SUPER expensive). We were on the 5th floor so at night there would be loud music from the bar on Level 1 - BUT - we were so exhausted from walking around all day - we fell asleep without issue. The service was great - concierge were VERY helpful with restaurant recos etc - but we did wait a while each time (as they are thorough with each customer). We loved the uber cool environment & bars - and the location was fantastic (a few blocks from Colombus circle subway / shopping mall & central park south west corner). We would definitely stay again next time we are in Manhattan for a weekend.

“Average at Best...” The Westin Oaks is one of two Westins anchoring the Galleria mall in Houston (the other being the Westin Galleria). If your business is in or near the Galleria area, then this is a good location. You might never have to go outside. I liked that the front desk clerk inquired if I minded being near an elevator (yes), rather than just stick me there and hope for the best. In general, I found the front desk service to be very cordial and helpful. On the other hand, the "Service Express" line left something to be desired with calls dropped and unanswered, and a general sense that the staff was eager to get on to the next call. There's free self parking available in an underground deck if you don't mind competing with the mall parking - probably not a great idea around Christmas. I appreciated the computer kiosk for airline check-in that's available in the front lobby. I ended up in a large corner room (518) with a big bathroom... both so big they looked like they needed more furniture. The decor was plain and nondescript. The hallways leading to the rooms were musty smelling and in need of renovation. My window looked out onto the hotel's outdoor swimming pool, which is at the same level as my room. This was fine in the wintertime, but the noise might be a problem in the summer. Housekeeping was hit or miss, especially when it came to replenishing the in-room coffee maker and cleaning the ice bucket. There's nothing like drinking coffee out of a glass because you have no cups in the room. Room service for dinner was adequate. I'll probably try a different hotel if I ever get back to Houston.

“Christmastime Wonder” In early December, my husband and I stayed with our 6-year old son for one night in a junior suite to view the impressive Christmas lights by river boat at night. The room had a balcony overlooking the river and historic buildings. We ate dinner on the Riverwalk and only used in-room dining for late night desserts, which were very good. We enjoyed the Starbucks coffee shop on the river level and took a nice long morning walk before checking out. The Christmas lights are the most beautiful I've ever seen. I didn't give this Westin an Excellent rating because I found the pillows to need freshening. My son wouldn't even sleep on his because it smelled like cigarettes. We stayed at the Contessa right next door the year before and I found both hotels to be comparable.

“great views and service” Spent 2 nights. was given an upgrade, could have early check in and late check out with no charge. Our pre-arrival requests where absolutly fulfilled. You will need to catch a bus or subway unless you prefer to walk some minutes in and out.The area is perfect for those who want to avoid hectic areas. Very nice to walk around. Queensboro bridge views are amazing, ask for these rooms! Mini bar with every kind of non-alcoholic or alcoholic beverages, sanks, chocolates, etc. Internet not included in the rate, to me should be a must nowadays everywhere. Confrats to the staff and managers who gave us such a pleasant stay.

“Great Hotel” The Willard is one of the oldest and most notable hotels in a city full of notable hotels. If you like the amenities of a large, chain hotel, but still like a little character and charm, then the Willard may be your place in DC. It is a very nice hotel, and the price reflects that, so don't go looking for a bargain here. The service is first-rate, as befits a fine old hotel, and all amenities are expensive. I have to admit that it seemed sometimes that some of the staff were "resting on the hotel's laurels" a bit, just sort of an attitude to the effect that, "Hey, you are at the Willard, we don't have to be nice. Just be glad we let you stay here." But that attitude was not pervasive, and for the most part, everyone was very pleasant and helpful. Michael, the concierge, was especially nice and helpful. Rooms are spacious, and a bit dated, but still nice. The restauraunts are fine. We enjoyed Cafe du Parc most of all. Casual French bistro, with friendly service, very good food, and a nice wine list, both for bottles and by the glass.

“It's WAY more than just the ducks.” There are grand hotels. And there are also great hotels. The Peabody is both. The total package is so beguiling as to be almost seductive. Of course the ducks are the centerpiece, literally, in the marble fountain, in the magnificently carved lobby. The "duckmaster" schtick at 11:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. has become not-to-be-missed viral youtube theater. And the ducks are everywhere: on the floor mat in the bathroom, on the stationery, on the marble floors in the elevators... Even the bathroom soap and dinner table butter are molded in the shape of a duck. It's all so broadly kitschy that it's utterly charming. But then there's the rest of it; the countless little touches: a huge new flower display atop the lobby fountain every day, glittering Versailles-style public function rooms, wake-up calls from a live person who asks if you'd like that day's weather, scratch pads, stationery and pens (emblazoned with ducks, of course) replaced each day, laundry returned in wicker baskets, extra staff at the front desk at check-out time in order to deal with exiting conventioneers. And speaking of staff, one certainly gets the impression that the staff really IS delighted to know that you're pleased with the experience. There's something to be said for the old saw about the Mississippi Delta starting in the lobby of The Peabody. It's a constantly busy place, with people from around the world coming and going, flowing out to the elegant horse-drawn carriages on Union Ave., or down the alley to the Rendezvous for ribs, or walking a few blocks to Beall St. and the Civil Rights Museum (i.e. the Lorraine Motel). The place is quintessentially Memphis. But it's also quintessentially the South: elegant, but also casual, proper and sophisticated, but earthy and whimsical at the same time. I've stayed at the Peabody three times, and each time seems better. Some places just do it all right.

“Tired Travelodge, pleasant staff” This hotel is bad need of an update. The room was as clean as it could be, but the carpet was extremely old, so was the bathroom, and it was silly that the only curtains we could close were sheers, and we could see through them to the hotel behind us (I'm guessing ditto for those guests looking in to our room!). The staff were very nice, though, there is free internet in rooms and there is also a decent free continental breakfast (fruit, cereal, toast, waffles, hard boiled eggs, sausages, coffee, juice, tea). The gym was also decent for the hotel. Parking is $10 a night. Location is perfect - a block from the space needle and monorail, walking distance to downtown, and most importantly, to Top Pot Donuts (you MUST go here). Also only a few blocks away from an Airport Bus pick up (we walked about 5 minutes to get to it). You get what you pay for - we got a deal online, and since we were only there to sleep, it wasn't a big deal, but even for a Travelodge, it was not the nicest place.

“When in Phoenix....only stay here !” Stayed here two nights with my wife and 13 year old son. Check in was quick and the staff was very welcoming and made us feel right at home. Assigned a nice 4th floor room overlooking the pool. The interior of the hotel is beautiful with flowing ponds and lots of places to sit and relax. The room was very nice and clean and included a big living room with a connecting bedroom. More than enough room for all of us. In the evening they had happy hour along with healthy snacks. Breakfast included a lot of choices and again was presented in the beautiful atrium. Each morning the front desk provided a cup full of koi food that our son used to feed the fish and turtles. We used the the pool both days and our son kept saying this was his favorite hotel of our 6 day trip in Arizona. Overall, the staff was really nice and helpful with directions and the rooms were terrific. My family really enjoyed our stay in Phoenix and this hotel had a lot to due with it.

“Great Staff” Just returned from a stay at this hotel. The staff, as always at this property, were friendly, accomodating and helpful. The room was clean, as were the pool and lobby areas. The carpet in the room really needs to be cleaned and/or changed but overall the property is clean, friendly and the pool is awesome. I have stayed here about five times over the years and I see the same staff each time.

“You can find better options downtown” We stayed overnight arriving from Europe and heading back to Canada. I choose this hotel because of its location downtown, close to the piers. The hotel in general looks outdated. This feeling really takes form in the rooms that look more like a late 70's than a modern downtown hotel. Everything was in working order and clean, but areas like the bathroom make you think twice about how well maintained the hotel is. Service overall was good and staff was helpful. Pool is a nice touch. The worst part was the noise. We were in the 10th floor and you would think it was enough to shield you from the (un)expected downtown experience. Not the case. We were hearing everything (and I mean even people talking in the sidewalk). Some noise isolation is clearly needed in some rooms. You can hear everything that is happening in the aisles outside the room, doors closing, elevators arriving, etc. Overall, I would have paid a few more dollars and stayed in another downtown hotel.

“Everything you should expect” I've always liked this chain and the Muse didn't disappoint. We just finished 3 nights at the Muse (first time there) and we'll be back. Everything mentioned in earlier reviews is consistant with what we experienced. The lobby is still under construction but it didn't impact our trip at all. The room was spacious and very comfortable. Friendly, professional staff at every level. Location, location, location adds points to this property. Good job Muse!

“Good location, great service” We spent 4 nights here in mid-November and had an excellent experience. I've stayed in six or seven hotels in SF and this ranks with the top of the boutiques. The service was excellent and the rooms very comfortable. Join the Kimpton frequent stay club (forget what it's called) and get a free daily paper and personalized treatment. the hotel is close to Chinatown, Union Square, and the Embarcadero. Even better it is only a block and a half from the Montgomery St. BART station and thus only about 40 minutes total from SFO or OAK. Skip the breakfast coffee for the many bakeries in the area (but not the one right next door) but the wine hour (5:30-6:30) is definitely worthwhile.

“Excellent service” I am platinum Marriott rewards member and stayed here last week on business trip. Great location if you are wanting to be near Time square. All the staff I talked with were very helpful and friendly. Not sure if they have upgrades but rooms were nice and clean with comfortable beds. Flat screen TV but signal is not HD. Central AC so no noise there. Must say that the rooms are some of the quietest I have ever stayed in. Only complaint is that I could not get any Cell signal on my phone so no phone calls and No messages. Guess that is because the building is surronded by other tall buildings. I had to go to lobby to get signal. The WiFi is strong and very fast. dont think I received anything in terms of my Paltinum status like breakfast or upgrades. I would stay here again if the location worked but would request room that might have better reception for Cell services. My phone is ATT.
“Nice Hilton” Very nice hotel. The health club is well equipped and rooms are updated. Most rooms have great views. This hotel is centrally located so you can walk to dinner, bars, etc.

“Great Hotel in the Heart of Dallas” I am a loyal Marriott traveler, and when I was scheduled to work in Dallas for two weeks, it wasn't hard to decide which hotel to stay in. I was at the hotel for twelve nights, and found the staff to be very friendly and the facility to be updated, clean and everything a business traveler would need. The rooms are large and well equipped, with very comfortable beds and furnishings. The room had a refrigerator which was very convenient to have water and drinks in the room. I can't say enough about the housekeeping staff - they were very friendly, efficient and did an excellent job servicing the room. On one occasion I needed something, and they delivered it to my room very quickly. The concierge lounge is the largest I've ever seen in a Marriott, and they offer excellent breakfast and evening food. Andrew was our Concierge attendant each evening, and he was super friendly, accommodating, and just an all around nice guy! If you're there - make sure to get to know him and treat him well. The only problem I had during my stay was one morning the elevators were not working - and being on a high floor, it was not a good thing! However, hotel staff operated the service elevator between floors to make sure guests weren't significantly inconvenienced by the outage. Next trip to Dallas, I'll definitely stay here again!

“Convenient Hotel for Sightseeing” We stayed for 2 nights at the end of June. When we checked in we were offered an internal or external room and asked whether we preferred a high or low floor. We chose an internal room because I was aware of the construction occurring outside (thanks to fellow TA reviewers). The room was clean and well appointed, the king bed was comfortable and we had a pleasant stay. We booked a "weekend rate" at $125 a night which I thought was very good for the standard of accommodation.The proximity to the metro station was convenient and we used the trains to get around and to take us to the airport at the end of our stay. Only issue was one of the escalators wasn't working and it is a bit difficult to navigate with large cases, but we managed. Staff were friendly and we had no issues. One thing worth mentioning, which may be quite common but I have never come across it before is that there are no in room safes but they provide you with a safe for no cost at reception but you require a staff member to access it with you. This was not very convenient for us as we like to lock up ipad, passports etc that we are not taking with us when we are heading out, and to have to line up at reception each time we went out to lock our stuff away was as I said, not convenient.

“Amazing Acoustics in This Hotel” This hotel was not bad, and I would stay here again. It is in a very good location, staff is friendly, and in general, no comlaints. The rooms are TINY. And the bathroom shower is set up such that you have to get soaking wet with freezing water to turn on the shower. Also, the bathrooms echo everything, so I heard all of my neighbors bodily functions in the morning, as well as their evening conversations. This almost went away when I closed the bathroom door, but it certainly wasn't an ideal situation! I would stay here again because of the rate and location. Where else can you stay for $166 a night? Oh, and there are three pieces of cardio equipment in the "gym." I found it a little lacking.

“Our Great Weekend at the Langham” It was high time we revisited a friend- that is, what used to be Le Meridien. The Langham turned out to be quite a class act, from it's efficient, friendly check-in, to an upgrade to a corner room on the upper floor, it was the promise of a great weekend in Boston. The room we had was spacious, clean, and quiet. The bed was very comfortable. The bathroom had all the basics, was very well lit, and there was always a hot shower. We got the bed-and-breakfast package, which we recommend. it includes a wonderful breakfast each morning at the venerable Cafe Fleuri. And the one thing that hasn't changed is this wonderful breakfast spot with one of the best breakfast buffets in Boston. The old Meridien had a nice piano bar where a couple could get a drink and listen to fine piano music, in the comfort of big, easy chairs and sofas. The Langham has replaced that with Bond, a lively bar spot, which is noisy, crowded, and a veritable meat market. We really wish that the Langham would provide an alternate bar setting which is more conducive to relaxing conversation. And the weather in Boston was the best we've encountered yet. Fair and mild, very conducive to walking.

“Loved it” Stayed for two nights in July. The hotel was beauitful and and very well kept. The location in Nob Hill is great location in walking distance to Union Square. Although the hotel is in a busy area the room was very quiet, even with the trolley cars running on the street right beside it. The room was a nice size. The bed was comfortable, and the shower had better than average water pressure. The room was very clean and like the rest of the hotel was very well kept. The complimentary breakfast was simple, but a nice way to start the day. Had a great stay and will most certainly stay there again the next time we are in the Bay area. Recommend it very highly.

“Fly and park special” My honey and I stayed one night in room 520 and then parked the car for 14 days at the Red Lion Hotel at SEATAC airport near Seattle. What a deal! Check out the Red Lion website for their specials and the park and fly packages. The rooms at this Red Lion are very spacious and the bed is the best. The outstanding breakfast is served at the restaurant next to the hotel and can be included in your room rate. Free wifi with a strong connection is part of the services offered at the hotel. The staff at the front desk are eager to help. There is a new Subway restaurant across the street from the hotel and one block south for a quick and reasonable meal. Great location immediately across the street from SEATAC that can be walked in under 10 minutes from the terminal. Free airport shuttle is also offered.

“Would not recommend or stay again :(” I stayed here recently for a group conference and I wish I could have checked out and gone somewhere else. The rooms are run down, carpet pulling apart and dirty, the beds were uncomfortable and linens didn't fit on them so they kept pulling off, the iron melted black something or other onto my white blouse ruining it, the furniture is damaged, the coffee pot was dirty, there is no fridge or microwave in the room and there is warm bottled water available in the room for $3.50 ea. One day I came back to my room as room service was there and I caught the maid cleaning the coffee pot with the bar soap that I had been using to clean my hands with for 2 days....BEYOND GROSS. When I turned on the air a whole bunch of flying bugs came out of the vent (see picture below) GROSS. Two colleagues had the same thing happen in their rooms. And it made super loud cranky noises for about 40min. each time. The elevators were so slow I took the stairs up and down from the 9th floor atleast a half dozen times in 3 days. Internet in the room was so slow and had so many problems I had to use my aircard the entire time just to get work done. The ONLY saving grace that got this hotel 3 stars is the staff - EVERY employee I came across the time I was there was extremely nice, courteous and friendly. The hotel itself is just a skip off the entrance to the riverwalk at Pecan St but it's about a 10min walk down to the restaurants, about 15 to the Convention Center and Riverwalk Mall. Unfortunately I would still not recommend this hotel to anyone and I wouldn't stay here again.

“Loved the Drury Inn Northwest” Stayed at the Drury Inn Northwest San Antonio on Memorial Day (May 29th) for one night. We had two rooms. One room was a non smoking 2 room suite with a king bed and the other room was a non smoking 2 room suite with 2 queen beds. Both rooms were a little worn down and not the cleanest. But, it was good enough for our night stay. My 3 year old son was able to play in the living room area and sit on the couch to watch TV. There was also another TV in the bedroom. The bathroom was nice and bright, a little small. There was a kitchen sink and also microwave and full size refrigerator. That was really nice and convenient. The Drury Inn had free soft drinks and popcorn from 3pm-10pm. There was also an evening cocktail reception from 5:30-7pm. However, I didn't try it out. The hot breakfast was excellent. There was scrambled eggs, sausages, bagels, toast, biscuits, gravy, make your own waffles, cereal, apples, bananas, orange juice, apple juice, coffee, milk, jam, donuts, etc. Definitely a good variety for everyone. The waffles were yummy. The hotel is located off the freeway, although I didn't hear any freeway noise or traffic. There is also some fast food restaurants nearby - Jack in the Box, Wendy's, Church's, and Taco Cabana. There is also an HEB grocery store down the street. The hotel is about a 20 minute drive to Sea World. I would definitely stay at the Drury Inn again. Parking was free. We got a good rate of $99/night using the SAVE promotion. Just enter SAV in the promo code to get this rate.

“Small rooms but loved it anyway” Loved my stay here with my girlfriend. Yes the rooms are small, but they're very nice. The beds are amazingly comfortable. I wouldn't call it centrally located but it is fairly close to many things, we walked everywhere just to absorb the city. Train stations are nearby and will take you anywhere. Do not take a cab to or from the air[port, it only cost 2 bucks to take the train versus a $60 cab ride. The downstairs bar is very trendy and the crowd spills over into the lobby. It is very swanky and trendy, filled with young professionals out to have a couple happy hour drinks, we loved that our hotel was the place to be seen. Room service brought us the most delicious burger I've ever had, but it was exspensive.

“Good Value for the Price” We stayed for 5 days with our two teenage boys in a 2 bedroom suite. The hotel was very clean, the staff courteous and helpful and the room was very nicely appointed. In the morning, there is a complimentary breakfast. Some reviewers seemed to feel that the selection was lacking. I am pretty picky (healthy food, low fat etc.) and felt that there was always something there to eat. Plus, the coffee - Starbucks - was good! Before dinner, there is a complimentary cocktail hour. Again, there was also somethin gthere to nibble plus wine, beer, soda. Since it was on the house, no complaints. We paid $225 nightly and felt that with 4 breakfasts and light dinners included that it was a great price. The hotel is about a 20-25 minute ride from downtown SD - not exactly proximal but fine if you know what you're getting into. It is in a suburban area near lots of restaurants and strip malls within a 5-10 minute drive. My only complaints were that the bed was a bit soft for my taste and our upstairs neighbor was noisy. But, when we called the front desk to complain about the noise, they were responsive and always took care of it quickly. Overall, I felt this hotel with its nice clean facilities and free meals was a really good value for the money.

“Boutique atmosphere in DuPont circle area” This Starwood hotel has a boutique atmosphere and I found it very charming. My room was small but comfortable. The bathroom was small too, but very nicely designed and functional. The room was very clean, quiet and pleasant. I slept well. The only complaints I had are that my colleague and I, both in separate rooms, couldn't get the wireless internet to work. I was able to get on for about five minutes late at night, but it quickly dropped me. My room had an Ethernet line, but that forced me to work from the small desk tucked in the corner. Also, I asked to receive a newspaper and only got one on three out of six mornings I was there. But, I really liked the atmosphere. The hotel is very nicely decorated with an historic feel. The breakfast included in my rate was a selection of fruit, pastries and yogurt. It is located close to the Metro, but not in close walking distance to the convention center, Smithsonian and other tourist spots.

“VERY GOOD HOTEL, GREAT LOCATION!” Our second visit to NYC. We stayed at the Crowne Plaza in Times Square the first trip but I received a great deal via Hilton (on two executive rooms) this time out and we were not dissappointed. Check in was quick, the kids had been placed on a different floor and that was changed (with a smile) within seconds! The rooms were clean, spacious and had all the bells and whistles! The executive lounge was smartly furnished and well stocked at breakfast time. The room service was a little pricey but the food and the service were great! The hotel is about five minutes walk from Central Park and the same to Times Square, it is a great location! If you can get a good rate, this place is perfect!

“Very average Chicago mega-hotel” My twelve-year-old son's church group stayed at the Sheraton the first weekend of May, 2006. I made none of the arrangements but just went along as a parent chaperone. The lobby is indeed very nice and large, but our room was totally average (maybe even below average). Very drab brown decor, small bathroom, nothing particularly nice. Check in was horrible and slow (and we were checking in late at night when there was no line!). No one seemed very interested in getting us all checked in when our leader was not yet with us. Good location, but not the best I've stayed at. And as one other reviewer said, why stay here when there are so many wonderful hotels in Chicago? I agree!

“A bit of shabby class in El Paso” The beauty of this hotel is primarily in the lobby. There is a circular dark wood bar below a gorgeous, enormous tiffany glass dome. There was good live jazz one night that we were there. The lobby/bar furnishings are elegant and comfortable. I imagine this hotel was the hieght of elegance at one time, and it retains quite a bit of this. By contrast, there is a newer, starker and cheaper looking lobby area near the elevators with tacky shops. The elevators themselves are warm wood inside, a lovely hotel feature, so why haven't they fixed the significant amount of scuffing that makes them look so bad? Don't go for the pool-- it's just an awful concrete highschool-gym-looking thing in a corner on the roof. Service from the staff was excellent with one exception: We were iniitally put in rooms on the 4th floor that had only tiny windows way up at the top of the wall, out of reach, making them feel like a jail cell. Later, we realized these were the only rooms with this defect in the whole hotel (many stories tall). It was clear that the numerous other rooms could not have been full, so we couldn't understand why we would be put in these rooms first. We complained and were moved to other rooms with normal windows. These were excellent. They were good sized with beautiful wood furnishings, and they were very clean. Overall, this hotel was well worth the $90 AAA rate . Go to Cafe Central, across the street, if you get a chance.

“Unique property w/ large comfortable rooms” This is a large property spaced near many office buildings in the vicinity but not next door to the airport. Rooms have a living area next to the bedroom and bath. All rooms have doors for privacy. HDTVs are small, but had a great channel selection. TVs are in bedroom and living area. There is a small fridge in the living area. Shower is huge and very nice. Starbucks in on the lobby level. Rooms are quiet and on-site restaurant was good for dinner. One item of criticism. Upon checking out I requested to use Marriott gift-cards to pay for my stay. The check-out person said that it would "take 15 minutes" to process. It did not take that long and I could not help but sense that they simply used that line as a ploy to not have to take the extra steps to process the gift cards. Its an isolated incident that just was poor customer service. It did not ruin the stay, this is a property worthy of many repeat visits.

“THE place to stay in Washington,DC” With a view on the White House it is simply magical, especially in the evening. The service is top-notch, the rooms luxurious, bedding sublime...everything exactly as it should be. The Black Angus burger is to die for, even at its seemingly high price. The gnocchi is also delicious. Indulge yourself and you will be back again and again. Thank you Hay Adams and The Lafayette!!!

“Rooms are very nice, but LOTS OF NOISE from Ground Zero work” I have stayed at this location many times, and the service is always good, rooms are nicely done, great A/C, and good sized rooms for NYC. Gym is very adequate, and the restaurant on the 3rd floor is good as well...BUT the noise level is late at times for construction work being done at the adjacent Ground Zero. I had noise both nights till 2 30 am which was difficult for 6 am starts in the morning. Also no food is served at bar (weak bar scene) in lobby which is frustrating. Location is Financial District so at night there is hardly anything to do, but I would check out the brand new W around the corner on Allen Street as their "Living Room" bar scene is very good. I got a corner room at this Hilton once and that is spectacular. Lastly the business center is great, but VERY PRICEY at .99 cents a page b&w and double that for color.

“disappointed” My daughter made reservation through hotwire, so not sure of the exact total, but was around $150, I would have been very ,very upset if we had paid their usual room charge. Reading the reviews I was sure that the hotel would be great, a little different, but good .This used to be a days inn, and that is what it looked like, a cheaper hotel that they had tried to make look elegant and hip, but failed. The good was their bar, didn't go there but it did look inviting with a view. Location was very good if you wanted to go to Navy Pier.Indoor pool, on the small side, no hot tub. Comfortable beds, plazma tv. The bad, Small rooms, city view of roof tops, black ceilings in rooms, drab colors,not even enclosed closet, just a rod, such as you would find in Days inn. Bathroom,not enough water pressure, not enough hot water, color was grey with one wall red, not enough lighting, a pocket door that did save some space, but then they added a wood shuttered window opening from bathroom to bed area, that you could open from both sides, some might think that is trendy, but I did not. The hallways were on the dark side, with small rocks placed on both sides, the entire length of the hall , very different, I haven't saw that done in any other hotel. But I doubt if anyone would say they wanted to stay here because they had rocks in the hallway. I get really ticked off about bottled water in the rooms, I feel that if hotels place water in the room it should be complimentary, the W charges $3 for a small bottle, and $6 for the larger version. I was hesitant to make the coffee in the room, not sure if they were going to charge a fee for that also. Coffee in the morning downstairs was over $3, that is not a good thing. We have stayed at numerous hotels in Chicago, for the money this one was very disappointing. There are lots of better looking hotels in this city, with more services offered for the money. I would have to say I won't be staying here a second time.

“great views, great hotel, superb location....” Location is great- within walking distance of Seaport Village - right out the back door. Close to stops for city tour buses too. Views of the harbour were excellent. Large hotel - rooms were great, and clean. Nice rooms.

“preiswertes Motel am Hotel Circle” Durch verschiedene Aufenthalte in San Diego haben wir schon öfter am Hotel Circle übernachtet. natürlcih nicht die schönste Gegend, aber deutlich günstiger als ein Hotel Downtown z.B. im Gaslamp quarter. Das Travelodge hat eien Moteltypische Ausstattung (WLAN...) und ist sauber. Die Zimmer sind nicht überragend groß, aber auch nicht zu klein. Wer also nur mal eine oder zwei Nächte günstig in Sasn DIego nächtigen möchte, ist hier gut aufgehoben.

“Save a bucket by staying at this hotel” We stayed here for three nights after reading Tripadvisor and noticing that it is a short walk to the train. We are very glad we did. The hotel staff were very helpful and friendly, especially when the room they initially put us in stank of cigarette smoke and I requested a new room - they obliged immediately. Free wi-fi here and free cookies - nice touch. Internet terminals were a little slow, but big deal. The breakfast was fine with different options daily and the subway station was only a few stops from the centre of town. Our room was fine, no issues there. There is also an enormous outdoor mall next door with eating options and shopping so you don't want for anything (no restaurant on site). Stay at this nice HI Express and save downtown prices - you won't regret it!

“Great Service And Nice Rooms Needs To Be Remodeled” A pretty nice hotel with friendly staff. Once again it needs to be remodeled. The restaurant is good and priced right. I satyed there for two nights and paid $60 through Hotwire. I wouldnt pay over $80 for a room there.

“Nice lobby; rooms not so much” The lobby is attractive as you walk in, but service and cleanliness has some to be desired. They had no hotel room keys when we checked in, so they had to escort us up to our rooms to be let in. Received room keys the next day. Room smelled like it needed a good cleaning. Breakfast the next morning was barely ok. A few of the staff were kind and helpful, but overall, wouldn't recommend it.

“The Good, with a little Bad” Let me say upfront that this was for a business affair and I didn't have to pay for the room out of my own personal budget. Having said that, after reading the reviews from tripadvisor, I anticipated several negatives such as late check-in/late servicing of the room, noisy room/hard to get sleep, no in-room coffee maker/bathroom vent, and distant employees. I also anticipated really cool decor, really good food at Citrus, and awsome bedding. Here is what I experienced - Room not ready - well we arrived several hours before the 4 p.m. check-in so I wasn't surprised a room wasn't available. At 4:10 we were told the room was being inspected and would be ready in 15 minutes. 30 minutes after waiting in line (again) we were finally given a room. Time - 4:45. Our expectation of this falling on the negative side was unfortunately met. Late servicing of the room - each day during a break in meetings I would go back to the room to check email, and the room was serviced prior to 2 p.m. on all three of the days. Myth for us was busted. Noise in the room - street noise was fairly easy to mask as long as the air conditioner was running. Unfortunately, even though we continued to set the thermostat lower, it stopped running long before it reached the desired temp, which means I was unfortunately awake several times a night due to street noise. Also, I had an adjoining room and can tell you with great certainty that the guy in the next room worked for a software company and I had to turn up the TV to avoid hearing details of some interesting new contracts with a vendor. In-room coffee maker/vent in bathroom. Surprise - there was a really cool one-cup coffee maker in the room, it was nice! Unfortunately, the vent was indeed missing from the bathroom which really only bothered me on occasion, but it was kindof weird. Distant Employees - Well, after my third time in line trying to get my room, I think I was a little tense, and the employee waiting on me who was very friendly earlier was a little distant - but I was really beyond ready to be in the room. I take the blame on this, because EVERYONE else during the three day stay was really very friendly at every encounter. I didn't realize there wasn't a pool before we went, and also I didn't see any gift shop so if you forgot some vital important item. For the good - loved the minimal decor, very cool. The Tivoli radio had some great quality of music, although it was a struggle trying to figure out how to set the alarm. The turn-down service was classy, the robes appreciated, the food at Citrus delicious the one time we ate there for lunch, and the bedding was exactly what I expected - awesome. Would I stay here again? Yes, but at the conference rate, not at the published rate if paying for it personally.

“Cool little boutique hotel on the Embarcadero, and I mean LITTLE!” Really enjoyed the Hotel Griffon, very nice room furnishings, friendly staff, a great restaurant (Perry's) but you need to know that some of the rooms are really, really small. So is the elevator. Still, everything in the room is quality and tasteful, from the exposed brick walls, the extra bed pillows and monogrammed cushion (with a Griffon, what else?), to the iPhone/Pod clock radio, to the Direct TV on the flat screen mounted on the wall high above the sink. You'll find chocolates on the bed as an evening turn-down treat. And my particular room had frosted windows looking out on an air shaft. Apparently there are other rooms with views out over the bay or the street below. The staff are very friendly and helpful. I wouldn't say it's the least expensive hotel in the area, but it's very special and unique - you'll enjoy staying here.

“Nichts besonderes” Dieses Hotel ist eingerichtet wie eine europaeische Studentenwohnung: mit Moebeln im Ikea Stil. Als gehoben kann ich das nicht bezeichnen. Den Preis der Uebernachtung jedoch leider schon. Die Concierge Lounge ist ueberaus schlecht. Stets ist das Essen aus. Ruhig war es jedoch, und die Betten sind sehr gemuetlich.

“Friendly staff, great value” What stands out is the friendly staff. The rooms are a little outdated, but plenty of room and clean. It was quiet as well. Great value for being so close to the inner harbor which is a quick block walk away. We would consider staying here again! By the way, the $9.95 daily charge is clearly stated on the hotel website and check-in, so no surprises there.

“Excellent choice” When we first arrived in San Diego (at the end of a loooong cross country road trip), I thought perhaps we had made a mistake and that we might have been better staying at a hotel closer to downtown or to one of the beaches. But I was wrong - this hotel was perfect. We had to wait a while for our room to be ready (5:30), but when we got to our 2-bedroom suite, we were very pleased with it - although slightly disappointed that the view was of the car park, rather than the water. The suite was very nicely furnished, spacious and comfortable. The A/C was a little loud and if you turned it off, you could hear other peoples' - but that was not a big deal to us. The staff were very friendly and helpful - the breakfast was good - and the location was excellent, being close to a myriad fast food restaurants, Trader Joe's etc. The seating area outside was beautiful. We stayed for 3 nights and were very sad to leave.

“Nice property, okay room” The Westin is in Boston's up and coming Waterfront area hence you will see a lot of young professional types and a relatively lively lobby scene. The hotel is new and the lobby area is beautiful. I found the room to be disappointing though. It had an apartment complex look to it. There was a large grey metal panel cover in the room, like a circuit breaker type that distracted from what could have been a lovely room. The wall paper did not look high end enough, it honestly looks like a chain apartment builder did the rooms. The bed was not as heavingly as I have experienced with the Westin and the bathroom was just okay. It was a girls trip for my birthday and I was a bit dissapointed with the experience.

“Great stay!” We've stayed at the Dana twice--and this has become our "go-to" hotel in Chicago. Both stays have exceeded expectations. The location is very covenient, rooms are modern, staff is accommodating. The restaurant is excellent,too, particularly for breakfast. Can't wait to go back!

“almost perfect convention hotel” Marriott now hosts 100% non smoking in the guest rooms, however upon checkin my room absolutely reeked of stale cigarette smoke. Thankfully, I was quickly switched to another room which was just fine. Best qualities of the room included the bed and shower. Room size was a bit small, but as a single business traveler, this was ok. Had family been with me, we would have been really cramped. The River Cafe ( their main hotel restaurant) was disappointing both in service and food quality. Many colleagues were voicing hopes that they wouldn't have to return to it anytime soon! The 73rd floor, however, features an incredible restaurant, Coach Insignia. The menu is much like Ruths Chris or Mortons, but the food quality is even better. Wait staff is wonderful. For quick and casual dining, there is a huge food court down on the 1st level. Nothing special, but convenient. The scariest part of my visit was the need to get a taxi for the airport. I made the mistake in thinking that cabs would be lined up at this luxury, downtown hotel. Ooops--not so! I had to wait for about 15 minutes (at 7:30am), Cab fares are $45-50 one way, inc. tip, depending on traffic, etc.

“These Guys Are Amazing” We spent two days with these folks, and it was delightful. Their front office manager Riz Marfani acts like a good will ambassador. He will do anything possible to make your stay enjoyable. I had read about Riz in other TA reviews. He was complimented consistently. These reviews did not do him justice. He helped us select a restaurant among a list of about 40 on the hotels list. The place was ultimately outstanding. The room were nice, bright, clean, and comfortable. The bed had a nice pillow-top mattress. We slept like logs. The window insulation is great. The dining room service was superior at breakfast, and the food was tasty. This property is at least 30 years old, but appears much newer inside. There's lots a space for convention business here.

“Union Square a nice option. W is Lovely” We were in midtown for two nights of US Open action, and decided to stay one more night over the hoiday weekend. Had stayed in W hotels before but not the one in Union Square so I secured a reservation and down we went. Our experience was mostly pleasant and positive. We arrived hours before check-in but they did have a room ready. The room was typical, sumptuous-looking W style. Down pillows, purple satin bedcover. Sleek furniture. We had not upgraded so this room looked out onto a building which gave it a slightly dim appearance but it was a decent size, with high ceilings, a very comfortable bed, lots of amenities, comfortable clean bathroom. Great shower. The common areas are beautiful, the staff was friendly. Olives is a great restaurant but it wasn't open because of the holiday so we walked to a cozy and delicious little Italian place (Crispo) in Chelsea. The only two things that were a negative during our short stay: 1) the hotel we'd just been in offered free wireless; as soon as I turned on my laptop at the W a screen came up asking me to confirm a $16.95 24-hour charge for the internet. That irked me. I think that kind of thing should come standard now 2) When I was checking out, I noticed that our bar had not been restocked after the previous occupants. I called the front desk to inform that a lot of things appeared to be missing from the bar and I didn't want to be charged. The man I spoke with said not to worry, but I've just noticed an odd, extra charge on my credit card bill so I guess I'm going to have to deal with that.....

“It was OK...” Yes, the room was clean and the bathroom was OK. The room was very small. I think i'ts a good price, we paid 99 USD/night for a twin bed room. But the staff was very unhelpful and no service minded at all.

“Very cool spot” This is a great spot to stay in Austin. It's in the middle of town, which is always a good thing, the rooms and beds are real good, and the food is alright. I prefer staying at the Driskill next door, but this is a great choice too. Oh, and someone won a trip to this hotel on Wheel of Fortune last year, by the way. Just FYI.

“Excellent customer service!” Hotel staff provided excellent service. The accomadations very comfortable. The only ty negative I can report is the fire alarm system went off on two different occassions.

“Excellent...” One of the nicest hotels in NYC for its price range. Not a Ritz Carlton, but, it's not meant to be either. Rennovated in last few years. VERY convenient to NY destinations/landmarks and being in middle of Times Square is a definite plus for eating, taxis, etc.

“A true gem a few blocks from midtown” Always looking for the quietest hotel in New York I had tried a lot of placed until I found the Ink48. Staff is adorable. I was upgraded to a Hudson View the first time and really loved it. Have been here 3 times already and hopefully next time the spa and rooftop will be available (coming back in October ;) Rooms are well appointed. Bathrooms are not your typical tiny New York "closets". They even have a yoga set if you want to do your poses in the morning. A great starting point if you want to stroll along the Hudson. Simply love this one...not changing! Tried the Plaza Athenee and the Muse, another Kimpton hotel but the latter was not even half as good as the Ink38 and the former has a great name and location but rooms are extremely tiny, though staff is making up for it, almost. One more thing: the restaurant is serving top food and this comes from a traveler who travels to taste food :)

“Top Lage, schöne Zimmer, tolle Aussicht” Wir hatten dieses Hotel über Hotwire gebucht und wirklich ein Schnäppchen gemacht. Für 109 Euro pro Nacht bekamen wir ein tolles Zimmer mit Blick auf den Central Park. Die Zimmer sind recht groß, sehr hell und auch sehr gemütlich. Wir hatten ein paar Probleme mit der Aircon und auf Nachfrage bekamen wir dann einen Heizlüfter ins Zimmer gestellt. Das war schon supernett. Das Internet kostete (17 $ Tag), klappte aber überhaupt nicht. Wir hatten kein Frühstück, aber in NY ist das ja kein Problem, da es Kaffee an jeder Ecke gibt. Toll ist der Pool im obersten Stockwerk. Gerade bei Nacht hat meinen einen tollen Blick Richtung City und Richtung Central-Park. Beliebt scheint auch die winzige Burger-Bar zu sein - wir haben aber nur einen Blick reingeworfen. U-Bahn Eingänge und Bushaltestellen sind in der Nähe. Ich würde wieder dort übernachten.

“Nice place to rest your head.” When people say this hotel needs updating, trust me: that is all they mean. The kitchen and bathroom tiles and fixtures are a little worn. Nothing was broken or dirty or in disrepair. The only complaint I had was with the dirty, threadbare ironing board cover. The room was spacious, bright and clean, and the bed was very comfortable. They charge for Internet usage, but you can print your boarding pass with no charge. As everyone has said, the doormen are very friendly and helpful. All in all, it cannot be beat for $125 through Priceline. I was not crazy about the location, although the 51st & Lexington Metro station is nearby. Many nights after the theater, I simply walked down 45th, then up to the hotel. Greenacre Park nearby is lovely and peaceful, and several restaurants and drugstores are nearby. I only go on at length because some of these reviews make the Beekman Tower sound like a run-down dump. That is very, very far from the truth.

“Good experience” Stayed here and got put on SPG floor with nice view. Room very clean, beds comfortable. Good location near Chinatown, shops, restaurants. Was in town for phillies vs giants game, it is about a 20 minute walk to AT&T park. Elevators fast for such a big hotel. Reading other reviews while staff was not rude to me, service is a bit impersonal given such a big hotel. Rooms were bigger than I expected. Could have stayed at the w hotel across street for $25 more (had fantastic experience there a few years ago), would still prefer the w truthfully as it is more hip/ modern but this westin is very nice, would come here again. Took BART from airport to Montgomery and walked here, but beware if you have a car as valet expensive.

“Great room with fantastic staff/service” My fiance and I stayed at the Omni Hotel in Philadelphia on the evening of Friday, March 10th. We had a wonderful stay and would highly recommend this hotel to anyone. We pulled up out front in our car and were immediately greeted by a valet and bell man. They loaded our luggage onto the cart, asked my name, and then the valet whisked our car away. The check in was a breeze! I'm a member of their select guest program as I travel extensively for business, and as at other Omni's that I had been to, there was a room waiting for me early (we arrived around noon) that they had already checked me into. They just handed me the key and we were on our way upstairs. Eric the bellman accompanied us upstairs to our gorgeous room on the 8th floor and unloaded the luggage in the room. The room was very spacious, with a king bed and a full size sofa. The view across Chestnut Street to the park was also very nice. The bathroom was all marble and granite, with a nice shower with good water pressure and ample hot water. The toiletries were also very nice. Later that evening, we returned with some friends who live in the area and a bottle of wine. We realized that we didn't have a cork screw, and with one call to the front desk we had a cork screw up in the room in under five minutes. We received our turn down service as promised and the free morning beverage (coffee and OJ) for select guest members arrived promptly. My only complaint about this hotel is the temperature control in the room. It was a very warm day and when we entered the room it was 80 degrees. We put on the AC but the coldest you could set it to was 68 degrees. We are Bostonians and were armed with warm weather clothing so that was quite warm for us. We normally like to keep our house around 65 degrees in the winter so I wish I could have made the room colder. We did not have any of the problems that other posters have mentioned. This hotel is truly a 4 star establishment that I would highly reommend to any traveler looking to stay at the historic district in Philadelphia. The rooms were spacious and comfortable and the staff all bent over backwards to please us. I especially would like to commend the valet and bell staff.

“Great hotel, great rooms, great service..what more can you ask for?” My family and I just got done with a brief stay at this hotel. We weren't planning on staying in Denver but we were in Breckenridge for 9 nights and were flying to San Diego. We rented a house for our entire stay but we didn't want to make the drive and then fly so we decided to overnight in Denver. I booked via Hyatt's website as I'm a Gold Passport member there. As usual booking was quick and easy. I booked with my AAA membership and got free breakfast included (although I wasn't able to take advantage of it as our flight left really early). The hotel is quite nice and the lobby i expansive. The hotel staff were all really great and friendly from the lobby staff, valet cheek in guys, etc. We booked online and requested a baby crib and this was one of the first hotel stays where they already had it in our room by the time we arrived. Usually we have to call and request them to bring it up again. A nice touch. They put us in a big suite on the 11th floor. The room was quite big with 2 comfortable double beds and a large LCD TV. Something that was VERY helpful is they put in a very big refrigerator/freezer in there that isn't cluttered with hotel stuff. When you have kids, things like this are essential to have to fit juice, milk, etc. Some people complained about the location. While there isn't too much around the hotel if you don't have a rental car, if you have flexibility and have a rental car it's fine. We easily went to Cherry Creek Mall and it wasn't too far away. If you want to be in the heart of the action, definitely I'd say this hotel isn't for you. But if you have flexibility then definitely I'd consider this hotel. Valet parking is $18 a day. I'm not sure how much self parking is but they did have that option as well. I can't say enough great things about the hotel and the staff there. I'd suggest room #1127. It was great.

“Much better than reviews made out” Stayed here with my partner and mother. My mother had an excellent king room on the 16th floor with a north facing view. We had a good double on the 9th floor facing south. I expected to find this hotel rather shabby based on some of the reviews and was surprised how great it was. The public spaces are great, the service is excellent. Our rooms were fine though not as gorgeous as the public areas. I agree the bathrooms are a little tired, specifically the showers, but we enjoyed our stay a great deal. I'd also add that the pool area is great and the gym , though I did not use it, looks quite impressive. I disagree with a comment about the directions to the hotel - we had no problem finding it. Dallas generally has appalling road signs, and an awkward one-way system, but that's not the fault of the hotel per se. Suggest they have a larger, 'enter here' sign from the road but that's it. Will definitely stay again. Oh, got my room on priceline.com for about $60 per room per night - great value.

“Nice hotel for the money.” I stayed at the government rate. Friendly and nice staff. The halls are dark brown and dark. The room was nicer than I expected. The only issue was the toilet kept running after flushing. Strangely, there was carpet cleaning machinery in the hall during our entire stay and a housekeeping cart parked between the bathrooms in the lobby all morning. I think the hotel may want to put these things away when not in use. There is a free breakfast buffet, but the options are limited to sandwiches, cereal, toast and bagels, oatmeal, and juice. All in all, however, the rooms are clean and comfortable and a good value.

“Quite a good choice” This hotel surpassed my expectations, I arrived early (around 10am) and it was no problem to check in and get my room. The rooms were quite spacious, very clean and tastefully decorated. Whilst the hotel did not have any luxuries (coffee maker or mini bar) it did have a fridge in the room. Its location was reasonable, a good place to access public transport the Metro and buses are available from Union station. There is a Subway next door and a petrol station over the road - so at least you won't starve. The management were helpful and friendly.

“Excellent Stay & Awesome Location” This has to be one of the best hotels that I continually stay at...the main reason is for it's very upscale look from the inside and the rooms and the staff... I made some special requests before arriving at the hotel, since I was going to be arriving very very late (like 2:45 a.m.) the hotel front desk checked me in that afternoon before I arrived so as to not interfere with the audit that night...since when doing the audit. they can't do anything to check-ins or getting keys..so it was done beforehand.. I arrived at the front desk and they welcomed me as they do all clients... I was given a room on the 15th floor and had a nice view of the city and such.. The room is nicely laid out, has a full kitchenette, regular size refrig and king size bed with full sofabed... The hotel boasts a very nice full complementary breakfast each morning with omelet stand... The only negative to the hotel is that if you are parking a car they only offer valet (since it's run by a third party) and costs $22 per night...which is higher then most hotels in the whole city.. The location is also A+ to Time Warner Arena, it's connected to it...a mere one block walk to the huge EpiCentre and a three block walk to the Nascar Hall of Fame... There is a nice children's museum (Discovery Place) located about a 10 minute walk from the hotel... Also, is the LYNX (Light Rail) that is a mere half block walk from the hotel... All and all this hotel is great and is run very nicely.. Another nice touch, a small outdoor heated pool (located on the 7th floor) with sofas, fireplace and such in the pool area... Always an enjoyable stay and always will return...
“Great experience!” We stayed three nights on the Club Level of this classic hotel. Great breakfasts! Concierge is there to provide services. An outstanding stay for the money.

“Location isn't enough” I recently spent two nights at the Park Central hotel in New York City while there for business. The location is excellent for business in mid-town Manhattan, but that's all this property has going for it. The room was supposed to be a king, but they could only give me two double beds. It was tiny, with tattered furnishings and worn carpet. The common areas are unappealing and old. The bathroom is barely serviceable, and the water took at least 2 - 3 minutes to get warm, and came out in more of a trickle than a stream. There was constant noise from the hallway and neighboring rooms, which led to two terrible nights of poor sleep conditions. The room rate was well over $350 per night, so it's not as if I shouldn't have been expecting a higher quality property. I also found it irritating that the room was on the south end of the building, but I was forced to take the north end elevators. There are nicer hotels in Manhattan at this price.

“Nostalgia at its best!” This wonderful hotel located close to shopping on 5th Ave, close to Broadway to catch a show, or just to stay in the hotel lounge and people watch is definitely a must stay. This is a very nostalgic hotel and although the hotel has some age on it; the rooms are spacious, clean, and have very comfortable beds. If you can't stay at this hotel; you must at least go into the lounge for a drink and enjoy the beauty of this fabulous NYC hotel!

“Lush” This hotel is the mutt's. The room decor/layout is great and the service/willingness of the ground-floor staff to help is huge. The social space is excellent and the quality of the food in all areas cannot be faulted. There are too many MacBook users bobbing around, wearing horn-rimmed glasses and talking loudly about how awesome they are. Similarly there are a good quantity of interesting characters to liven things up. All of this is to be expected in this part of Manhattan. The rooftop bar is great and the staff who work the area are hardworking and speedy. The top floor cocktail bar is underwhelming (although decadently decked out). The seating hostesses are very haughty and the service is no way deserving of the huge service tariff (you should know how to make an Appletini!). Wind your neck in! Yours is a margins business. I'm not going to pay you 30% more for a glass of wine so you can sneer at me and give me a crap seat when the bar downstairs is cheaper, friendlier and more fun. I stay here regularly for work. It's not my £. If it were I might notice more. But I am always struck by the quality of the welcome and the comfort of my room. Can't ask for more than that.

“Wonderful location” The location was awesome, the beds were soooooo comfortable, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay and we bought 7 day metro passes and got to see an awful lot from Harlem to sign the Michael Jackson tribute wall next to the Appolo theatre to Coney Island to sample Nathans hot dogs, Greenwich Village with its market is worth a visit on Saturdays and Canal Street Chinatown on a Sunday for handbags, watches and dvds, what an exciting city.

“Airport hotel but not walking distance” Good hotel and not far from the airport building but not close. Bit hard to get to the hotel by walk, especially for those carrying big suitcases and passge is complicated through the parking area and no good sign board for direction which is not fault by the hotel but hotel should better discuss it with the airport authority. Room is OK and comfortable. Some kind and unkind reception staff.

“Great place to stay” Just want to say that I enjoyed my stay here a lot. It was clean, updated and the staff was extremely helpful. The Breakfast was also really nice. Not sure if I'll be returning to Jacksonville anytime soon.... but if I do, I would love to come here again. Book it.... you can't go wrong.

“great value in Waldorf suite” We were in NYC for college visit, needed sleeping arrangement for three in three separate beds. For about $500 got a 1BR suite with two doubles in the BR and a pullout sofa in the LR. Beautiful furnishings, fireplace, comfy seating in living area, nice bathroom if smallish for a suite. Sofa bed was ridiculously uncomfortable, we folded it back up and made up the sofa into a bed, which was fine for my teen son. Love the public areas and bar, loved the room. Do wish they would give you a break on a slightly early checkin, we arrived about an hour early absolutely drained from a long drive in really bad weather, they would not budge on the time. All in all a good experience and the suite was cheaper than two standard rooms in another hotel,which would have been our other option.

“Nice, friendly staff...but tired rooms” The staff at the hotel was super friendly and very helpful. The location was excellent too, not from my the historic sites and on the subway line. However, our room (#3109) was a bit worn and tired and a bit on the small side. The furniture and bathroom had numerous nicks and chips and needed some TLC. We stayed on the Club Level but the Club Level no longer provides breakfast on the weekend. Good view of City Hall from our 31st floor window. The hotel restaurant was OK with more friendly staff members.

“Great location & Views” I recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency at the Colorado Convention Center. It is located directly across the street from the Convention Center and within a few blocks of the Denver Center for Performing Arts. It is one block away from the 16th Street Mall and walking distance from the RTD Market Street Station. I stayed on the concierge level with a fantastic view to the southwest. Mt. Evans and Pikes Peak were clearly visible and beautiful panoramic sunrises each morning I was there. One of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in with perfect pillows and luxury linens. Excellent lighting. Could not hear people in adjacent rooms. At least these upper floors appear to have undergone recent renovation. I especially appreciate that the rooms at this Hyatt have a small window that opens for ventilation-I even like hearing the street noise below. Lots of hot water and no plumbing issues. Appreciated a rubber bath mat available. Many hotels I stay in do not offer a mat and the tub/shower can become slippery and dangerous. The check in process was very quick as was check out. Entire lobby, bell service, concierge was highly efficient and well run. Friendly, professional employees. Food was excellent in Altitude Restaurant on lobby level. Reservations are probably advised when attending an evening event at Convention Center or DCPA as I was. Only negatives: Housekeeping did not get to my room until 3:30p.m. A notice in the room informs the quest that housekeeping may come as late as 4:30. In my opinion that is too late in the day to have the room serviced. No evidence that the very long hallway on the 36th floor was vacuumed in several days and items were collecting on the new carpeting. Also in my opinion room service needs to cover glasses of wine, water, tea, butter plates etc. with plastic wrap or paper covers when making deliveries. Finally, the peep hole in the door was positioned too high for me to see out of. I would have needed a stool to stand on. I am not a short person. This needs to be fixed somehow for security reasons. I rarely give a hotel I stay at a five star rating but the concierge level of this Hyatt deserves it. It doesn't get much better than this in Denver.

“A Gracious Oasis” My visit was wonderful. I enjoy staying in this area as it is an oasis from the hustle and bustle of the rest of New York. It is a great place to start and end the day. The Park on the waterfront is great for a walk. The bed was very comfortable. The Club Floor is a great bargain and allows you to also welcome and end the day with great food and drink. Everyone at the hotel went out of its way to serve you. It was a big improvement over my last visit. The Hotel is in great shape. It was very easy to get a cab to and from everywhere we went.
“Clean hotel for the price” Not a newer RI, however it was clean and quiet for my one night stay in Austin.

“A really hidden gem” This hotel is on a New York theater district street known as "restaurant row." There is just a doorway on the street and it would be easy to pass by without noticing. There is a tiny lobby, too, but the hotel functions very well. There is always someone knowledgeable and welcoming at the front desk willing to take you up to your room. The space looks as though it was fully renovated just a year or so ago and everything looks clean and fresh. A continental breakfast is included in the room rate and this is served in the bar of the restaurant the hotel sits on top of. With nice spring weather we were able to have our coffee on the large rear second floor terrace adjoining the bar. A very unusual space for a NY hotel!

“Nice Airport Hotel” Booked a room for a one night layover on my way home from Asia and apparently the hotel was hosting an annual Furry convention, so there were lots of young people dressed in costumes. All in all it was a decent Hilton – comfortable room and decent service. The staff was friendly and accommodated my early arrival request. There was a fair amount of noise throughout the day both coming from the courtyard and from the hall way, but it wasn’t all that obnoxious or unexpected given the convention happening I guess. They certainly have an overzealous housekeeping staff that really wants to do their job. I put the “do not disturb” sign on the door so they didn’t bother me until they caught me leaving (and returning from) my room for lunch and asked if I wanted my room cleaned. I politely told them (both times) that I just checked in and wouldn’t require any service. The hotel is right across the street from the airport and it’s about a 15 min walk, most of which is covered. Just follow the signs to the light rail station, cross over the street to the bus stop/parking lot and turn right.
“Humidity problem” Upon check in, one of my collegues had to change rooms 3 times before she got one that working plumbing and no mold.

“Our place in LA” This was our second stay here and it was even better than the first in 2010. They charge $5,- a day now for parking but I think this is a good decision because last time we found it hard finding a space to park when coming back late at night. I guess there were just too many people parking at the hotel and not being an actual guest. In the parking there is an old abandoned car which I really like and definitely not should be removed because its part of the charm of the hotel. Both times there was a film crew shooting at the hotel which immediately gives you the Hollywood feel. Bruce and Roberto from the front desk were both very nice. We had package shipped to the hotel and they took care of it which was really nice. Price is a bit high for my budget but reasonable because the location is perfect. Walking distance to the Beverly center, Melrose for shopping, Wholefoods market and Petersen Automotive and Lacma museums. I asked for a top floor room at the back and we got room 310 which felt more like a small appartment than a hotel room. It had 2 windows, a kitchen, 2 queen beds, a table, two chairs, large closets and normal size bathroom in it. Beds were clean, comfortable and heating was working fine (there weren't extra blankets and it was cold at night so I had the turn the heater on, so putting extra blankets in the closets will save energy). Also the pattern of the bed covers was very nice. Our other room had purple which was a bit dark but these were yellow. And it was super quiet! We felt like moving in immediately and staying forever :) Tv channels were poor and they charge extra for wifi but this didn't bother us because you're only there to sleep. There were only 2 lights in the room this was a bit dark when you need to repack and reorganise your stuff before going on the plane. No breakfast included but try the Swingers diner in the same building, they have everything you need. Can't wait to stay here again, Beverly Laurel is the best !

“Zentrale Lage, kleine Zimmer” Das King George liegt sehr zentral unweit des Union Squares, nahe der Cable Car, Metro und Street Car Routen. Es hat somit eine perfekte Ausgangslage für Erkundungen. Es handelt sich um ein altes, etwas verschachteltes Haus, was sich in schmalen Treppen und Gängen und kleinen, dunklen Zimmern ausmacht. Unser Zimmer gab uns ein wenig das Gefühl des Gefangenseins. Wir hatten keine wirkliche Aussicht und noch dazu massive Gitter vor dem Fenster. Es war ziemlich dunkel und klein. Der Komfort war ok. Wichtiger für uns war die Lage und das Value Package, das wir gebucht hatten. Dies beinhaltete neben der Übernachtung auch Frühstück im nahe gelegenen Max's Cafe und Parken in der O'Farrell Garage gegenüber. Letzteres sparte uns 96 Dollar für die drei Tage! Der Frühstücksdeal hingegen ist nicht empfehlenswert. Man erhält einen Gutschein, der ca 10 Dollar umfasst. Tax und Trinkgeld können aber nicht verrechnet werden. Wir wählten eines der günstigen Frühstücke (Pancakes mit Kaffee) und zahlten letztlich doch noch 9,28 Dollar. An den folgenden Tagen entschieden wir uns für ein nahes Starbucks-Cafe. Ein Stück Kuchen und ein besserer Kaffee als im Max's kosteten uns weniger und es entsprach mehr unserem Wunsch. Das King George würde ich speziell mit dem Parking-Package weiter empfehlen. Man muss aber einfach wissen, dass die Zimmer sehr, sehr klein sind und das Bad recht spartanisch mit wenig Abstellfläche.

“Fantastic!!!” I recently stayed in this hotel, having purchased a package deal on another travel site. I wasn't sure what to expect of the hotel when I first booked it, but I was pleasantly surprised on arrival. I was one of the last people to check in that day, my flight hadn't arrived until after 10pm, and when I arrived at the hotel - they informed me that they had no more rooms available, but they were going to put me up in a suite. The only thing was, that the suite was booked for the duration of my trip. However - they moved me into a top-floor room the next day, with a fantastic view of Twin Peaks and the Castro, and there was a bottle of wine waiting in the room for me. The room was decorated nicely, very elegant furnishings. The management and staff there are just fantastic. They really make you feel like a family, and upon departure, they arranged for town car service to the airport for me (as my flight was at 6am). The guest services manager was especially fantastic. He was eager and interested in my experience visiting San Francisco, and he went so far as to provide me with his business card and the invitation to return soon. I will most definitely be staying here again, and I strongly reccommend this hotel to those of you who are looking for a pleasant, unique San Francisco experience without a lot of pomp and pretention.

“Got a bad vibe, left without spending the night.`” I recently blind booked this hotel through Hotwire. The hotel was incredibly cheap, but it wasn't worth what I paid. The hotel is located in the Continent area of Worthington/Columbus. There are at least a dozen hotels at this exit, ranging from very bad to adequate and above average. This hotel definately brings up the rear. It is located directly next to a Gentleman's Club. That, by itself, wouldn't bother me, but it added to the bad vibe. I pulled up, and found a lot of broken down cars in the parking lot. The exterior of the building looks non-threatening, but not the interior. When I walked in, I saw a lot of Travelodge logos still up. (Evidently, it lost its franchise.) The breakfast area was to the right, and it was sealed off. There was a raunchy smell coming from the air conditioner, which looked like a rusty, barely functioning contraption. The front desk person seemed nice enough. The desk area was shabby and disheveled. She checked me in and I went back to my room. The walk back had the most nauseous smell coming from the stairwell beyond the front desk. It smelled like burning human waste. I actually had to hold my breath as I walked by. I walked through the stairwell and down the hallway to my room. As I walked by rooms, I heard yelling couples, screaming children, and more strange smells. At that point, I didn't feel like I was in a hotel, but rather a run down boarding house straight out of a Bukowski novel. I opened the door to my room. It seemed dingy and depressed, and had a new, but equally strange and nauseous smell. The bathroom was beaten up, but somewhat clean. The bed had threadbare sheets. I looked for bedbugs, but didn't see any. Without bringing my luggage in, I left to get dinner. While I was gone, I thought that this place was too depressing for me to have a relaxing night's sleep. I couldn't bring myself to return. Given that I paid so little for the place, I left and checked in to a neighboring hotel where I've stayed in the past. I'm glad I did.
