“not too bad” First time staying here, must say that the building is begining to show it's age, from the cracked sink to the old carpet. place was clean and the staff very friendly, just not upto the standard I expected from Fairfield.

“立地がよい!” サンフランシスコのホテルの中ではかなり安く、さらに立地もいいので、空室があればいつもここを利用しています。部屋自体は古いですが、この価格なら問題ありません。昨年泊まった方の書き込みではインターネット接続無料ということでしたが、私が5月に泊まったときは一日15ドルと言われ、7月に再度泊まったときはフロント係から「近くのスタバを利用してください」と勧められ(^^;)、ホテルでネットはできませんでした。。。

“Well presented hotel - Superb location !” Just returned back from a great weekend at the Westin. My husband booked this hotel for an Anniversary break as it was close to the Lucas Oil stadium where he had booked concert tickets, for the Saturday night. Once I knew the hotel, I logged straight on to trip advisor and the mixed comments really had me concerned. Getting to the Hotel. We didn’t really have any problems finding the hotel, it is located just off S. Capitol Ave on Washington Street. (opp the Capital State Building). Car Parking Not too sure what all the fuss is about regarding parking. Basically you have two options, self park for $25 a night. If you are using this option your car has to stay put for the duration of your stay. Should you wish to take your car out then use the valet parking at $28 a night. We chose the self-parking option and the entrance is easy enough to find, the car park is called Capital commons and just before the hotel. I know other hotels in the area are charging $32 plus a night for parking. For me living near Chicago, where parking is far more expensive I really did not have an issue with the parking rate. I felt my car was safe where it was parked and that was all that I cared about. Room. We had a gorgeous suite with sitting room, bedroom and bathroom. The décor was in calming shades of cream and green. Very serene and relaxing. The king size bed was heaven to sleep on. We felt as though we had full panoramic views of the Capitol state building and downtown Indi. Very clean, presentable room. The bathroom once again was well appointed, the only negative was that it was rather on the small side. But I loved the double showerhead and the illuminated vanity mirror. Towels were a little course but the bathrobes luxurious. Wi-fi Free in the reception area, although a fee to use in rooms. There is a business centre available, but once again a charge is made for that service. Location. For us the location was perfect, only a very short walk to the shops, restaurants and bars of downtown. The lucus Oil stadium only 10 minutes away and numerous museums very close by along with the central canal, which is a very enjoyable walk. The city was so accessible that we left our car in the lot and went everywhere on foot. Restaurants/Room Service We did not eat in any of the restaurants as we chose to dine in town. We took advantage of the room service for Breakfast. Eggs, Bacon, Hash Brown, Choice or bread, tea or coffee and fruit juice priced at $18.50 plus 18% service fee. We enjoyed breakfast and it was very well presented. Not the warmest breakfast I have ever eaten and maybe not the tastiest either and at a total of around $55 for two, I guess it was not the best value meal I have eaten!!! Negatives On our second day at the hotel, we were out all day and only returned to our room for one hour to get ready for the concert in the evening. This was at 4pm and we were surprised to see that our room had not been cleaned. We left for the concert and returned at 11;45 pm. Our room had still not been cleaned. I called down to reception and she was very helpful and apologetic, but it made me laugh when she asked me if I was sure that my room had not been cleaned! They offered to send a member of housekeeping up straight away, but at this time of the night I just wanted to get into bed so declined. Our bill the following day believe it or not was incorrect, not sure I have ever checked out of a hotel yet and not been overcharged, they were trying to charge me $7.80 for 2 bottles of water which had a complementary tag around their neck in our suite. Reception put the mistake right for us with no fuss. Summary I know we had a couple of problems, but I would stay at this hotel again without any hesitation. The public rooms and bedrooms were well appointed, beautiful décor and very clean. All the staff we encountered were very friendly and knowledgeable and the location could not have been more perfect.

“Ottimo!” Hotel molto curato, in stile resort, che affaccia sulla marina di San Diego. Le camere sono spaziose, ben arredate e pulite, anche se un po’ rumorose. Se possibile chiedete una stanza al secondo piano perché sotto si sentono i passi, le voci e tutti i rumori di quelli che stanno sopra. Ci sono due piscine, entrambe con bagno turco, gli spazi comuni sono ben tenuti, il parcheggio gratuito e il personale molto cordiale. La connessione internet wi-fi è gratuita in tutta la struttura anche se in alcune zone la copertura è migliore rispetto ad altre. La zona è tranquilla e ci sono alcuni ristoranti dove servono ottimo pesce.

“so cool, but so way overpriced” I did a two day leisure stay at the W San Diego in July. One of the first things you're likely to notice as you drive over from the airport is that you're only a block away from the courthouse and county jail. Some of the streets along the way to the Gaslamp district are lined with Bail Bond shops (and drunk / cracked out homeless people). The safest way to get to Gaslamp is to walk down the street from the W is on State Street and then make a left at Broadway. As many of the other reviews have noted, the W is absolutely not for everyone (specifically, families with kids of any age, people over 40, etc.). The average age of the staff appears to be in the mid-20's, and I believe this is the clientele the W is catering to: young people with massive disposable incomes. If you fit in the demographic though, you're very likely to love the stylish decor. The lobby has a 2 - 3 story atrium overlooking a bar area that gets cleared out weekend nights for DJ's to spin music. The "Beach" rooftop bar is accessible from the 2nd floor. The elevators are surprisingly dark, lit only by some dim LED lights. We were given a room on the 13th floor (nope, we weren't superstitious). No room upgrade or anything extra for having a Starwood Preferred Guest Gold card (and we arrived at 1 or 2 p.m.; maybe this W doesn't care about loyal SPG customers?). We were able to get a slightly later checkout set for 2:30 p.m., though. The room itself was very stylish. A huge king bed with soft (350-thread count) sheets. A ledge in front of the window has a day bed/cushion where one can lounge there and read or do whatever. The downside to our room was that the carpet appears to have seen better days (definite stains and wear & tear), and the in-room air conditioning unit was really good at keeping one wall cool, but the rest of the room felt stuffy or warmer. The bathroom shower has a European-style window covering half the shower area, with a porthole in the middle so water can still spew out onto the floor depending on how close you are to the shower nozzle. The shower knob controls only the temperature, not the flow of the water. As another review noted, the toilet paper holder is not next to you, it'll be a twist and a reach behind you. Instead of some art or print, I liked the chalk board in the room. Perhaps this room was designed to host weddings and bachelorette parties. Combined internet / local and long distance calls are $25... a rip off, when compared to Marriott's typical $10 all inclusive rate at their resorts and hotels. Internet access (by itself) is $13 for 24 hours. Parking is $28 per day now. If everything you're doing is within San Diego, forget the car and take a cab to & from the airport and around town (or bicycle cab, they hang out in front of the entrance, too). You'll save quite a bit of dollars that way. The attached restaurant, Rice, serves very delicious dinners, but just as in the hotel lobby, there's ubiquitous stylish music in the restaurant as well. We were seated right underneath a speaker so that was a wee bit distracting. Overall, I thought this was a very unique & stylish place to stay, I'm glad I did it this one time, but I don't think I would stay here again. but if you're not doing Priceline or some other super deal, hold onto your wallet, this place is likely to drain a lot of cash. For our two day stay, plus parking and one night's dinner at RICE, my bottom line bill was just over $750.

“A fantastic boutique hotel in the heart of Midtown Manhattan” I stay at the Muse on a regular basis for business. I LOVE this hotel. The location is fantastic. Close to Times Square, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Bryant Park, Broadway theatres and all of midtown Manhattan. The rooms are a really nice size by NYC standards and the beds and beyond comfortable!! As with all Kimpton Hotels, there is a complimentary wine reception in the lobby every evening. The staff at the Muse are extremely friendly and helpful and the bar/restaurant in the lobby is great. The hotel is very modern, hip and stylish. I cannot recommend the Muse enough.

“Nice, but a little dated” I recently went to Paradise Point for a convention. The place was built in the early 70's, and is made up of many bungalows on its own small island in Mission Bay. The rooms are updated inside, but it still feels a little old. My room smelled kind of musty, but the air conditioner helped somewhat. That said, the facility is very quiet and peaceful, and seems like a great place for families with lots of ponds, pools and birds. The meeting facility was surprisingly nice and is right on the water. The biggest complaint I had is that the hotel is well away from anything else, so you would need to take a taxi in order to see anything. Another option is to take the local tour tram for a $30 fee that allows you to get on and off the tram throughout the city all day (a good deal if you ask me). I did not eat in any of their restaurants, but food that was served at the convention was fine. If you want a quiet "family" kind of place to stay and can get a good rate, this would be a reasonable choice for a stay in San Diego.

“Nice place to land after a long trip” This is a very nice hotel just a few miles from Charlotte airport. The rooms are large, and nicely decorated. Parking is free and abundant, since this is a convention hotel. (There was no convention when I arrived.) For Marriott Gold members, there is a Concierge Level, which is nice. I stayed one night on a Saturday and the lounge was closed. But I was given tickets for free breakfast in the hotel restaurant. I stayed here after arriving in Charlotte after a late arrival from the west coast. I would have rated the hotel higher except for the reception. While everyone else at the hotel were friendly and receptive, the frist person who greeted me did so curtly in asking form of payment and id. She was so rude that another reception agent added, "please" to the end of her request. She attempted to recover when she realized that her causticness was inappropriate, but the damage had already been done.

“The Basics Plus Just A Little More” I stayed at this property in July 2011 for an overnight prior to an early morning flight from DIA. The room was priced at $81 for a king. The property is located on Tower Road. Numerous restaurants and other hotel brands can be found here, each in various price points. The exterior of the property is clean, attractive and there appeared to be an adequate amount of parking. The lobby was also found to be clean and attractive. It is a large space that could accomodate a many guests for breakfast. Check-in was prompt and efficient and staff members were polite. There is one main elevator on site which initially caused concern. Given the size of the facility I anticipated extended waits for service. This did not prove to be the case as service was consistently prompt. Elevator cabs were clean but showed evidence of wear. Interior hallways were found to be clean but poorly lit. There seemed to be long distances between fixtures. When combined with dark wall coverings it seemed to be a long, dark walk. The room was found to be clean with everything found to be in working order. The area was spacious and there was ample work space. Wireless internet service was speedy with good download times. Fixtures in the room were found to be in good shape and were typical for the price point. Bedding was of average quality, again, that which I would expect. The bath area was found to be clean, but not stocked well. Towels were adeqaute but soap, shampoo etc. were in short supply. It appeared to be a miss by housekeeping staff. The sleep area was quiet during the overnight. Noise was absent from the hallway and outside areas. The room ventilation system was quiet as well. One strong suit of this property is the manner in which the early traveller is cared for. With breakfast beginning at 4:00 AM even those with 6:00 AM flights can travel to DIA on a full stomach. This is rare and appreciated. Check-out was a quick affair and I was thanked for my business. I travelled via complimentary shuttle to DIA in about ten minutes. The driver was polite and courteous. This is a nice, basic motel-like facility. For the price one can get the essentials plus just a little more. While not a typical coice for me, I would stay at this property again if the opportunity arose.

“Conveniently located and comfortable” The room was a decent size for a downtown hotel. We had a room with 2 double beds. The refrigerator was a plus. Hotel is only a couple blocks from the el and even closer to bus routes. Great restaurants are all around. Loved Pops champagne bar. Definitely worth it if you can get a good rate.

“Terrible experience! Worst hotel I stayed at all year.” I had such high hopes for this hotel. I was on a week and a half long swing through California and decided to stay here while in Hollywood. I love historic hotels, so this was going to be one of the hotels I was most looking forward to. This hotel claims to be a luxurious class of hotel ... I found it to be everything but. For tourists who (for some reason) want to stay close to the drag queen hookers, pan handlers, drug addicts and cheesy t-shirt shops that is Hollywood Boulevard, it is a great location. But aside from being right across the street from the Walk of Fame and the famous Chinese Theater (which is a curse and a blessing), this hotel was one of the WORST HOTEL EXPERIENCES I HAD ALL YEAR! First of all, there is almost NO service attitude here. The hotel hires the typical 'Hollywood type' ... young, attractive with an attitude. Almost every staff member I encountered at this hotel had a terrible attitude. They really seem put out having to work there and treat the guests rudely. When I went to the concierge desk (a late 20s - early 30s guy) he didn't even look up at me while I was asking him a question. He was writing some notes and kept his head down the whole time and answered in short, clipped sentences. And gave me some pretty bad recommendations to boot. I reserved a suite and asked if they had any upgrades for frequent Thompson guests while checking in. I was told that the room was upgraded already, which I thought was good. Until I got to the room and found out it was exactly the type of room I booked. When I called down and asked about this they explained that the 'upgrade' was that I was put on a high floor. Hmmm ... I didn't realize that a hotel upgrade literally meant 'up on a higher floor'. Even the bartenders had a 'dude, im going to be a famous actor one day, don't bother me' vibe. The single biggest rip off in this hotel is the Beacher's Madhouse scam. The only time the staff here go out of their way is to hawk this terrible club. Apparently, someone figured out along the line that Teddy's (the now closed for rennovation uber-guest list club in the Roosevelt) was a great way to get young 20 something year old drunken LA kids to wait in line to pay $15 for a beer. So, they opened Beecher's Madhouse and paid Kelly Osbourne (previously David Duquette until he bailed) to put her name on it. Beachers claims to be sold out for years in advance. However ... surprise ... surprise ... they slide fliers under every hotel guest's door that offer the the opportunity to get into Beachers for $150 cover ... or $500 - $5000 for table service (alchohol not included). I peeked into the club (know some people in LA who got me in free) and it seemed like it was 'over the top' crazy ... as if someone on acid designed a club and put things in for shock value. Maybe cool for the first 5 minutes but after that, you would need to take acid to forget how much you paid to get in. Total scam. One thing I was VERY dissapointed with is that the hotel is PACKED full of non-hotel guest 20 something year old Jersey Shore kids. They are all drinking at the clubs and bars ... decked out in their True Religion jeans and high hooker heels ... hanging out in the lobbies taking up all the furniture in the public spaces and swearing like truckers/sailors. Def. not a place I would EVER bring a family. The public spaces are nice (if you can get past the jersey shore trash all over the place) and are made up to look like 1920s Hollywood with big tufted leather couches and dark wooden beams and ornate painted ceilings. There are bars everywhere ... it didn't take me long to figure out this hotel caters to the young, jet set party crowd. The pool is awesome, but is almost always closed for photo shoots. At night the best time to go is around dusk when they turn the space heaters and firepits on and it is not crowded with the Situation and JWoww look-a-likes making out on couches. However, $15 for a mixed drink served out of a plastic cup or $8 for a beer is a bit much to charge. And the fact that most nights the pool bar closes at 10 p.m. in order to give business to Beacher's Madhouse is lame. As for the room ... again, think young, hip 20 something crowd. The walls and ceilings of the hallways are painted dark grey so it looks like you are walking down the hallway of a haunted house. There are paparazzi photos on the wall in black and white. We had a suite, which was very spacious but it almost felt like someone moved a ton of furniture out. There was a small coffee table, cheap looking microsuede couch, and a mini-bar with no coffee maker. The bedroom had a bed and a tv stand and a night stand. There was TONS of empty space in the room where most hotels would have put an arm chair in the bedroom. It was obvious they saved money on furniture by making the rooms empty and cavernous. We saw the maid cleaning a standard room and were literally amazed at the size of the rooms ... they looked like a closet. Smaller than a dorm room at a city college ... seriously, you really need to re-think booking a regular room unless you don't mind a closet with a bed. The bathroom was incredibly small. Literally the toilet/sink were in a space the size of an airplane bathroom. There was a shower/tub with cheesy tile walls and half a glass partition which made the floor all wet anytime you took a shower. The view from the hotel was good, overlooking the Hollywood sign and Walk of fame. There was no car service and cabs are pricey in LA. Parking was expensive as well ... I might be inclined to skip the valet and park my car elsewhere to save time and $15 - $20 per day. There are nice, safe places for $10 per day in the area. Overall, this was a very dissapointing experience. The room was cheap looking ... drab, depressing and dark. The service was beyond reprehensible ... rude and non-existant. At $200 - $350 per night, they have a lot of nerve to provide such bad service. The only good part of the hotel is the lobby area and pool area, which is unavailable at night because of all the drunk club kids taking up space before leaving the hotel after the clubs close. There should be a guests only area/lobby. This was a total dissapointment. If I had it to do over I would have booked at the Rennasaince across the street, which is cleaner, nicer and doesn't have a Jersey Shore infestation. Or the Hollywood Hills Hotel. Avoid the Roosevelt. I am very dissapointed in Thompson as a frequent guest to the brand and very dissapointed at the management of this hotel.

“All in all about average” This hotel was ok, we found some of the front desk staff a bit abrubt. We arrived 20 minutes before the check in time and he was pretty short in telling us our room wasn't ready, in all honesty everytime i spoke to this guy he was pretty weird. The room itself was ok, nothing to rave about. There was a pool and free wifi and a breakfast of sorts. The room was quite noisy as it faced out onto the pool. The location is ok if you're up for a walk. We always walked to fishermans wharf and it took about 15 minutes. Union Square took about an hour. I'd reccomend the alcatraz trip and a hop on hop off tour even if it's just to get to the golden gate bridge which is worth walking over (took us about 40 minutes) San Francisco is a beautiful cith that we really enjoyed, we were hardly in the hotel so it was fine for a base.

“A good choice when location is more important than the room” I stayed at this Marriott for a conference. The location couldn't be better - the hotel is in the middle of everything. The service was good, as was the food served at the conference. There was a Starbucks on site and a busy, fun lobby. My room was okay. It was clean but a little dated. The bathroom was small. I might want a nicer, more updated room if I were vacationing, but this hotel was a good choice for a conference.

“I want to live at the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower” This was such a nice hotel. the rooms were large and comfortable and the staff were amazing! The location is just a few blocks from the Mag Mile and we walked everywhere. You're also just a couple blocks from the Red Line which got us to The Green Mill and Wrigley Field and shopping in Lincoln Park for just $2.25. The restaurant and bar had excellent service and great food. I would go back to Chicago just for this hotel. It was the best hotel I've ever stayed in. I loved it!

“Great Place to Stay Near PHL and the CIty” I spent about a week at the aloft Philadelphia Airport and was really impressed with just about everything. To begin with, the staff is very helpful and courteous. The rooms are clean, modern and obviously set up with a business traveler in mind - plenty of power connections right where you want them, and also a device to connect iPad/iPod/iWhatever to the flat screen TV. The gym at the aloft Philly is very well equipped, including free weights and benches, a couple of elliptical machines, stationary bikes and two or three treadmills. The indoor pool is conveniently located near the gym. But the front desk staff is the difference-maker at this hotel. I highly recommend this place for a reasonably priced, comfortable and well equipped stay within in minutes of PHL airport.

“Excellent for a great price” My job frequently takes me to L.A. for work, and I have stayed at the Radisson approximately 6 times in the past year. This hotel really offers more than your typical Radisson. The rooms are relatively new with nice furniture. Most are large. Be sure to request a non-smoking room. I was stuck in a smoking room once and it was not as new or nice as the non-smoking rooms. Despite the amazing view of LAX's runway, the noise is not noticeable. The shuttle service to LAX is very convenient. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to or through LAX.

“Gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis” Das Palomar ist ein gutes, modernes Hotel zu einem bodenständigen Preis (Frühbucher!!!) wenn man die Nähe zu Beverly Hills berücksichtigt; zwei Straßen weiter Lokale, Restaurants für jeden Geschmack zu Fuß erreichbar; Personal aufmerksam und sehr freundlich, Zimmer neu und modern eingerichtet; hier macht man nichts falsch;

“Great stay!” We stayed here with a total of 8 girls (over 2 rooms) for my sister's bachelorette party, and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay! The rooms were decently-sized, with well-sized bathrooms. Rooms were clean and well-decorated. The location, as had already been mentioned, was terrific. They were very accommodating of us and tolerated our silly annoyingness (i.e. forgetting our keys several times) with complete grace and kindness. Would highly recommend this hotel for any traveler; would also like to mention that those who are not familiar with NYC will enjoy the very short walk to many local restaurant, as well as those wonderful boutique shops in Soho!

“over-priced for what you got” I stayed at the Marriot Marina in June 2007 for a convention and then stayed a couple of days for leisure. Since it was a large convention, the room cost me $299/night. For that lofty price, you got a decent room but nothing special. My room had a view of the convention center instead of the bay (more $$$). The bathroom was decently sized but the toilet was not in its own partition. Also, the bathroom didn't have any ventilation fan, so it was steamy after a shower. The shower head was a Grohe (expensive German brand), but the volume of water was not very high. I believe a major advertising point for Marriott are their "perfect" beds. For me, the mattress was much too soft. They certainly give you a lot of pillows though - two small ones and two larger ones per bed. Some bright points: I had ordered food from room service a few times during my stay. One time, I had ordered a plate of steamed veggies (not enough healthy food while on the road) and what I received was a very nice combination of small squash, cherry tomatoes, broccolini and asparagus - I was impressed. For their beds, they use down comforters instead of plain blankets. There's a gym and small pool system on the bay side of the hotel but I didn't have time to use either. The main reason that I chose this hotel was its location - right next door to the convention center. Given the amount of walking I was doing those days, I was grateful that my room was close by. If I were to go to this convention again, I would choose this hotel for the small reason - location rather than anything special about the rooms.

“good spot for the night” I Arrived very late from a long flight and was welcomed by Friendly staff. The room was nice and the bed comfortable. Since I had a meeting all day the next day, I was very pleased that the room was also quiet. While the hotel is listed as at the airport, it is actually about five miles away and required me to use a taxi, since the shuttle had stopped running much earlier, 10pm. Mind you, my flight was not late -- just a scheduled late flight from Newark, but no shuttle. The taxi driver was not thrilled, either, since he did not get a good fair to town -- so I tipped him extra, thus making the short drive a bit pricey. The lobby is comfortable and spacious, but is not updated to new bistro model.

“My last stay at this one!” Stayed here at here last week for some meetings on Thursday and Friday. My Thursday meetings canceled but I still decided to go at my scheduled fight time due to last minute airline change fees. My thought process was, I could work (on-line) from my Sheraton room until my Friday meetings. Wow was I ever wrong, I will say that they upgraded my room to a 2 room suite but when I walked in the living room air condition was broken and blowing at 60 degrees causing very cold air to blast into the bedroom thermostat and blow heat at 82 degrees. Since I could get anyone to answer the front desk phone for 30 mins i i i just picked up my luggage and went down to the front desk. They moved me to the Dallas Suite.....now I am Platnum at Starwood AND Marriott and I never have Wifi connection problems however in this room I had nothing but problems even after they "directly connected me to DSL" which of course knocked out my iPhone and blackberry Wifi connection. After a very long useless day of getting nothing done the managers solution to my problem was to comp my Internet (which I get free as a Platnum guest), no points, no cards no drinks, how gracious. This hotel caters to big conventions and not a place for individual guest (not to mention its run down and service is questionable) . I'll just stay at the Marriott (across the street) or Sherton Suites just outside downtown in the future.

“Good Airport Hotel” We had a good stay at the Doubletree and would return if needing to be by the airport. We chose this hotel, as we had to return a rental car, and didn't want the hassle of trying to find our way to the airport. We received warm Chocolate chip cookies on arrival (sort of out of place, it being close to 100 F outside, but the gesture was well appreciated.) Curiously, the exterior of the building is downright ugly, being a cinderblock-looking color and construction. However, the lobby and rooms are done in modern but warm style and the staff are extremely friendly, professional, and helpful. The hotel seems to cater to convention and business types. The suites are divided into two rooms; the living area has a kitchenette area with a good, cold fridge, microwave, and bar sink, but no dishes or utensils. Maybe you have to ask for them, as we didn't bother to ask, not needing them for an overnight stay. There are nice waffle-cloth robes available, but you have to phone and ask for them. Very handy for going to the lovely outdoor pool with. The surrounding landscaping is also very pleasant. My only beef is that the payphones ( I am NOT paying 60 cents a minute to use the room phone) are located right smack in front of the public washrooms. As I was using the phone, the cleaning lady started cleaning the washroom, and proceeded to flush the toilets several times, and the person I was speaking to couldn't hear me. The hotel restaurant is quite decent, and the buffet breakfast is not bad, and is included in your stay. No airplane noise WHATSOEVER and we had a great sleep on the comfy, firm bed.

“Not a four star hotel” I have no idea why this is a four star hotel. The rooms are small and guests can hear every little noise in adjoining rooms and the hallway. I was upgraded to a junior suite but it was still smaller than a regular room at the Westin or Sofitel. If you choose to stay here request an outside facing room. My room looked out on an air shaft that smells like the New York subway. The stench was so bad I could not use the heater because the smelly air was drawn in. The bathrooms are also small with a tiny sink and a shower, no tub. The best thing about my stay were the H2O bath products. As far as services and facilities go the "fitness center" is tiny as is the lobby. There is a restaurant next door but there is none in the hotel. This is a three star property all the way so that's what it should be compared to when choosing a hotel.

“My favorite hotel in the world!!!” I absolutely LOVED this hotel! The minute we arrived we were greeted warmly by handsome doormen in stylish uniforms. The young ladies at the front desk were very sweet and helpful. I asked for a room with a view and they gave us room 1211 - a corner room. We walked in and it took my breath away. The design details, the floor to ceiling windows, the pristine bed, the huge tub with a view.... I couldn't believe it. I took more pictures of this room than anything else on my trip! The rooms are so unique and have so much character and great amenities as well; an iPod dock, a convenient place to recharge cell phones etc. During our stay, housekeeping came to the door with an offer for a shoe shine and a small tray of beautiful cookies. The newspaper was delivered the next morning in a cute canvas bag hanging on our doorknob. Even our toast for breakfast was placed in a tidy box inside a Bowery Hotel monogrammed bag. So much attention to detail and style! We loved the bar and the cozy seating areas in the lobby. We also enjoyed having a cocktail on the patio. Very quaint and romantic. Our waiter was excellent and so friendly and funny. I feel like I'm gushing, but really this hotel is worth it. I would recommend this hotel again and again. Thank you for a fantastic stay and I can't wait to return!

“Pleasant stay, a bit dark” The Argonaut is situated in the middle of all the action, close to the Wharf and some rooms have splendid views of the bay. The decor was whimsy and fun, a bit dark. We found a great rate online so booked several rooms for all the family, including the dog. The staff is very friendly and accomodating! The parking fee is high, especially if you've a SUV. Also, I'd categorize the Argonaut as a fun, family-friendly, clean, touristy place, not sophisticated-class.

“Just Ok...” I only stayed one night at this hotel, and though it was far from bad, it never felt special either (especially for a 5 star property). Check in was smooth, but when I inquired on a specific room type, I was told "sorry" before the front desk person even took the time to check (and the hotel was empty!). I found out hours after I checked in that my husband had emailed the hotel and requested that a bottle of champagne be waiting for my birthday in the room upon my arrival, but I never got it or anything to acknowledge a celebration. Not a big deal, but not 5 star. The south tower suite we had was nice, but just that... nice. Nothing special. The bathroom was big, but the bathtub was small. Room service was fine, and the delivery people were all very nice, but the food was just average. The gym was a bit of a disappointment too. It had some old cardio machines and weights, but again, it just wasn't anything special. I'd stay here again if it were about half the price we paid per night. Otherwise, there are better options.

“Awesome Marriott” This hotel was excellent. The location is perfect. It's surrounded by bars and restaurants, plus its right near the water. The rooftop bar here is beyond unbelievable. The breakfast served in the hotel was great as well. The price was reasonable. The best Marriott I've ever stayed in.

“(half review) Good budget option in Chicago” First, I was here for a sleep study, so my room was arranged and paid for by someone else, and we were on the lowest floor. All in all the rooms are clean compfortable and no frills. On te two times I stayed there, the tub drained slow and the showerhead was leaking. (you get a nice movable showerhead, but the joints leaked). The WiFi is spotty. That said, if you're looking for a break on price, it's a good option in Chicago. You're between a drug store and a grocery store. You're in Greek Town and steps from Randolph St, so no shortage of great food, but you will need a super short cab or bus ride to access the other keyspots of Chicago, assuming you don't want to drive and/or pay for parking.

“Townplace is pretty good” I've stayed here on two separate occassions. Once, we got a suite with 2 bedrooms. This was VERY nice. In addition to the 2 beds, the sofa pulled out. Large, comfortable, clean room and bath (kitchen too). The other time we had a single bed, but there was a pull-out sofa also. This was more like a standard hotel room with a kitchenette. Again the room was very clean. We definitely prefer the separate bedrooms, but either way it's a very decent place to stay. The staff was very accomodating when we needed extra pillows and blankets.

“Internet not working---complete mess” Upon Ck in I was handed a letter regarding issues with the Internet but was told its spuradic and doesn't last long. So I decided to ck in. Big mistake wasn't working at all! Went to front desk told them of my dissatisfaction and they offered their satisfaction guarantee refund. The girl at the desk was very understanding that my work requires Internet and called her mgr to cancel my stay which was nice. Hotel room (king suite) seemed a bit old to me, not really up to my standards. Prob won't come back, but their svc was good. Stayed at another hotel.

“Average at best” First of all this hotel is in a great spot as far as sightseeing goes but that is where it ends. The rooms are very small and not that fancy. I was quite shocked that you had to pay for Wifi in your room, which was very expensive for what you get. It was only free if you sat in the lobby. In comparison all the Holiday Inn Express hotels i stayed in offered it for free and their rooms were just as good to be honest. The gym was also out of action for renovations, but was not told about that when i booked the room. Over priced and underwhelmed was my overall opinion. It is not that special and offers nothing that the cheaper hotels don't. My advice is save your cash on the room and go for a nice meal in DC instead.

“Nicht schlecht, aber nicht perfekt” Der Marriott Charlotte City Center liegt wirklich direkt in der Innenstadt von Charlotte, die Uptown heisst. Von hier sind es nur ein paar Schritte bin in die Restaurant Meile, oder zum Stadion der Bobcats. Das Hotel ist schon ein paar Jahre alt, aber ganz gut in Schuss. Am Wochenende ist das Parken umsonst, in der Woche kostet es 14$. Das Frühstück ist sehr amerikanisch und fettig, das ist nicht so mein Fall. Die Zimmer sind nicht sehr gross (ich hatte ein Concierge Zimmer) welches normalerweise Aufpreis kostet. Die Badezimmer sind meiner Meinung nach eine Frechheit. Sie sind sehr klein und haben mir gar nicht gefallen. Die Zimmer sind sehr hellhörig, besonders wenn der Nachbar die Toilette benutzt hört man auch unschöne Details... Ich bin auch eine Nacht in der Executive Suite gewesen, die ist zwar sehr groß, aber nicht sonderlich schön. Das Bad ist übrigens genauso klein, wie in den normalen Zimmern. Alles in Allem okay, aber wenn man die Preise betrachtet zu teuer für nur durchschnittliche Leistung.

“Convention Hotel” I stayed in this hotel for a 3 day convention in mid April '05. The location of the Hyatt in the West End of downtown Dallas is terrific. It's not really within walking distance of anything, but a short shuttle or cab ride is easy enough. The hotel lobby is nice. There are plenty of restaurants and an underground walkway to Reunion Station. There's a ton of meeting space. If you're staying here on vacation, keep in mind that it's likely to be crowded with conventioners. Rooms are average. Stayed in the Skyline section of the hotel overlooking the train station. Let me start by saying that it took a day or two to get used to the trains blowing their horns all night as they passed by. I don't know if it would be any better on the other side of the hotel. Woke me up several times. The bed was nice. It sits up high and I had to almost climb into it. But the TV sits low in a cabinet and I couldn't see it over my feet. There's really nothing special about the rooms. The cost was $175/night for the cheapest room when I stayed. You're paying for the location. There's no breakfast, happy hour, etc. High speed internet access is another $10 per day. For what Hyatt considers to be a higher end hotel, it's too bad they nickle and dime you for these extras. There's a fee for parking, but I'm not sure how much it is since I took a shuttle from the airport and didn't get a rental. I know it's fairly expensive. The valets are terrific. There's a ton of them around and they do a good job of securing cabs. In fact, there are usually a dozen or so cabs lined up outside the hotel. The front desk staff was pleasant, but nothing special. Housekeeping was adequate. Overall, this is not a bad hotel, but nothing special except for the location and meeting space. I'd certainly stay there again if my company was paying for it for another convention. But I wouldn't vacation there.

“Nothing special” Stayed here for one night with my wife, and 3 kids. (10, 7 and 2) Room was clean, a little tight on space for that many people, but it was just for the night. Not sure what Holiday Inn is doing with their PILLOW SELECTION they say they have a variety of firm to soft pillows for you to choose from, but they were all awful. And small. Whatever ploy they are using to cover up being pillow aficionados is a hoax. And to top it off, the beds are AWFUL too! Stiff and small! Two FULL sized beds? Queens would have been nicer. But not available. Made for a very unpleasant evening. No breakfast, unless you want overpriced and poorly prepared crap from their restaurant. Parking lot is small and tight as well. Pool was enjoyable.

“Outstanding!” After reading all the great reviews, I wasn't sure if the Residence Inn would meet my expectations. It did by a mile. Where do I start?... - Friendly staff - Quiet, CLEAN rooms - Right in the middle of everything - LoDo, Coors Field, 16th Street Mall, Denver Pavilions are all within walking distance - Large rooms with nice kitchens - Free wi-fi - Really good breakfast each morning If you want over the top "style" and cold, modern furnishings, go ahead and pay $400 a night at the Westin or a W hotel. I'll take this Residence Inn anytime. If I ever make it back to Denver, this will be my place to stay.

“Spacious” Stayed here earlier this month for five nights over Easter break. Room is spacious,, a little dated, but clean. Great location in a quieter part of the city. Plenty of restaurants nearby, didn't even try the cafe in the hotel. Shower pressure is a nice change from California's water saving shower heads.

“Top-Lage, Top-Hotel” Super Hotel in bester Lage zum Times Square. Innerhalb weniger Minuten ist man zu Fuss an der nächsten Subway-Haltestelle, dem Times Square, Restaurants,... Direkt gegenüber vom Hotel ist ein Supermarkt und ein Deli. Das Zimmer war für New Yorker Verhältnisse sehr groß und komfortabel eingerichtet. Geräusche von draussen (z.B. die Feuerwehr) waren zu hören, aber gestört hat es nicht. Die Zimmer sind gut isoliert. Die Sauberkeit von Bad und Zimmer war bestens. WLAN ist gratis verfügbar.

“Coolstes Hozel in Chicago” Das Elysian wäre mein neues Lieblingshotel in Chicago, noch vor dem W Chicago - Lakeshore (wenn da nicht das Sofitel wäre das viel güntiger ist). Aber der Reihe nach: Das Elysian ist kleines, feines boutique-Hotel. Modern, sehr schöner Innenhof, schöner Pool, tolle Einrichtung, tolle Betten. Einziger Nachteil - es ist sehr viel teurer als das Sofitel. Das Sofitel (siehe mein anderer Review) ist auch modern, auch gut, aber leider leider zu groß und zu stnadardisiert um mit dem Elysian mithalten zu können.

“My one night stay” This former Radisson is now a Holiday Inn. I stayed here on a free hotel voucher given by my airline. Like many other passengers, I was stranded at Denver this past Wednesday due to the snowstorm and was rescheduled to fly out the next day. The free hotel shuttle picked up from the airport every 5 and 35 minutes after the hour. That also happens to be the same departure schedule from the hotel to the airport. The ride took about 25 minutes, a bit farther than expected for an airport hotel. The check-in took a while since there were only two people staffing check-in and everyone got off the shuttle at once. The open interior atrium helped with the spacious feel. My room was clean and the furnishings were in good condition. I had a nice night view of the Denver downtown buildings from my room. The lighting in the room was not adequate; it still felt dim even with all the lights on. The bathroom lighting was good. I was glad to see my room still had the Select Comfort bed that the Radisson chain used. I love the ability to adjust the amount of support with Select Comfort beds. Needless to say, I had a great night sleep. I did not use any of the other hotel amenities since it was a short overnight stay but overall I was happy with my stay.

“Great Location and Comfortable Room” Located within walking distance to the White House and a Metro Station which will take you anywhere in the City, this place makes for a great place to stay while in DC. Front desk was helpful and the Concierge assisted us the entire time we were there with what to see, where to eat, etc. . . Room was clean and the bathroom was large - bed was the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in while at a Hotel. The Restaurant downstairs was excellent but a bit on the high side. If the weather is good try sitting outside. I would not rent a car unless you are venturing outside of the DC area - The Metro will take you anywhere you want to go and the week pass is $35 if I remember correctly. Great stay in DC

“Great location” Ok, so what has been said about this room previously is correct, the rooms are small - tiny. But aside from that and sometimes a weird smell in the lobby & lift, there is nothing else negative that I could say about this hotel. The location is fabulous, easy walking distance to shopping in Soho, surrounded by great restaurants of all price levels, many bars & the subway. The neighbourhood has a fantastic local vibe which is the biggest plus. Forget uptown or midtown, downtown is so much more interesting! Staff were always helpful & friendly and kindly let my friend have her room early on check in as she was sick. The roof deck is amazing, and the free breakfast more than enough..am severly missing bagels & cream cheese! Did not see any bed bugs, room as always clean & the bathroom was really nice. Would definitely recommend, although perhaps would not suit those with children.

“execellent to stay in NY” Beautiful hotel and execellent area for stay. Hotel needs to improve on having a much bigger choice of foods - too many politically correct foods at hotel!! Employees are execellent. No swimming pool at hotel.

“Great girls weekend shopping” This was my 2nd visit to Hotel Diva. The location is perfect for shopping at Union Square, within walking distance to BART and across from Curran Theatre. The front desk staff was friendly and helpful. We got into the city before check-in time and they had rooms available so we were able to check-in early. The rooms are small but they are clean and cozy, they offer some sake & champagne in the lounge during the evening. Perfect after a long day of shopping. There is a Starbucks right next door and a Mexican restaurant on the other side. There is even a "walk of fame" in front of the hotel with the signatures & handprints of some famous "divas". Always a great stay at the Hotel Diva, will definitely be back!

“Extremely Friendly Staff” My colleagues and I, who frequent Chicago often for business, stayed at the Marriott for six nights in May. This was our first stay at the Marriott and it was extremely pleasant. All of the staff are friendly and super helpful. The woman who maintains the lobby space during the breakfast hours is extremely nice, a little over the top, but well intentioned. We each stayed in a suite, which came with two rooms—bedroom and living room, and were well decorated with couches, desk and chair, flat screen tvs in the living space and the bedroom, and a great kitchen for cooking, including dishes, pots/pans, and utensils (if only we actually did such a thing!). Overall, great room with more than enough space to place our things. Hotel is in a great location, access to all that downtown Chicago has to offer, including restaurants and shops. The fitness room is also nice, which is attached to a small pool, which kids seemed to like. While the hotel is very business friendly and occupied by various professionals during the week, the hotel got extremely crowded over the weekend and there was nearly no room to sit down and eat breakfast in the morning in the lobby as a result. Besides the crowded breakfast lobby, our only complaints were that: 1) the rooms facing the east side (I think) of the hotel are right next to the garage which undergoes cleaning at some time during the early hours (1-2a), which can be heard in the middle of the night. This disrupted our sleep on more than one occasion and lasted for at least an hour...it didn’t happen every night, but more than once; 2) the hotel was packed, and with only four elevators, we had to wait a little longer than we would have liked for an elevator. This is a minor inconvenience, but noted.

“Great Hotel, Good Location, Would Stay Again” We stayed at this location for one night while visiting Austin. We wanted to be near the nightlife and entertainment so chose this location. The location was easy to find and the hotel is in a commercial area between 6th street entertainment and the convention center and a 5 minute walk to all the action in the warehouse district as well. You have the choice of valet or self-parking. Self-parking is in a connected garage with easy elevator access. ($21 self with in and out) There is a nicely decorated inviting lobby with front desk and nicely appointed common area. Across the elevator bank is the Residence Inn, which shares a common building. There is free Wi-Fi available in the lobby area and rooms. The hotel has a large, nicely appointed gym. There is small indoor pool, but unfortunately no outside deck space. We did not get the opportunity to check on a business center. Check in was quick and efficient, and they did an excellent job of noting our request for a quiet room (away from the 6th street noise) and put us in a room facing 4th street on a high floor. Though we were there for the nightlife of Austin, it was nice to be away from the hectic side, and we were really appreciative of the hotels strong stance on no noise. They have prominent signs stating no parties are allowed, and that only registered guests are allowed at the hotel. When we came back to the hotel Saturday evening, they had security at the door to ensure that only guests were allowed in. This is a nice touch. The rooms are nicely decorated, relatively large and still seem new. The beds are comfortable and they have nice HD TV's and plenty of channels. The climate control works well and the blower motor stays on for white noise while the climate control is still functioning. We had no noise from adjoining rooms nor outside city noise. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space. There is a tub with shower We could hear doors slamming in the morning from time to time. Though the adjoining Residence Inn includes breakfast, the Courtyard by Marriott does not. This is the norm for the brand and we did not expect any free breakfast. The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We did not partake of any of the hotels dining venues.....too many good choices nearby to eat in a hotel. We would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if we wanted to stay in the area for a personal trip. Room rate seemed appropriate for the area, especially with our AAA discount. Having also stayed at the nearby Hilton and Intercontinental hotels in the past, I would feel comfortable choosing any of these hotels based on who has the best price at the time. All of these are very nice options and similar in their offerings and the prices seem to vary wildly from day to day. They were agreeable to late check-out when we asked which was nice. The entire hotel is non-smoking which is always a plus.

“Great Stay” I was in town for a business meeting, and spent 2 great nights at this property. My colleagues all stayed at the JW Marriott just down the street, but I decided on the West Loop to save some money. I definitely made the right decision. Upon checking in, I was upgraded to a concierge level room with access to the concierge lounge for breakfast, hors d'ouevres and desseert. At check-in time, the hotel placed a large fruit platter and chocolate fondue fountain in the lobby for all guests. So basically, I paid 1/2 of what my colleagues who stayed at the JW did and got a lot more for my money. As for all the complaints with freeway traffic, ask for a room away from the freeway and it's not an issue whatsoever.

“A beautiful, pristine old hotel in the heart of Hollywood.” This is where the first Academy Awards ceremony was held and of course, many famous faces have stayed in probably every room. The common rooms are splendid to look at and if you want to see a building from a bygone era, in California, this is a very good example. Also, Grauman's Chinese Theater ,directly across the street, is a beautiful movie palace & one of the best I've seen thus far. Also, not to be missed is El Capitan Theater, on the same side of the street as The Roosevelt, about 1/2 a block away. The good: we paid for a standard room, in the lower price bracket (with 2 queen beds) & were rewarded with every thing I asked for in the notes section, when reserving & received a large room overlooking Hollywood Blvd. The bathrooms are circa 1927 however, so don't expect an spa tub or as many square feet as we are used to these days. The bathrooms have been redone and are nice, but not luxurious. The linens were nice also & the beds comfy. The check in staff was excellent & Mark, the head of the valet battalion was, well remarkable & was "on it" as far as I could see. We did have an instance where our keys were left if in our car, unlocked, which was alarming in a neighborhood where most anything can happen & most likely does. But, it was fine in the end. Just waiting for your car, at least when we were there is a genuine Hollywood who's who experience there, so time passed quickly. They even offered the managers safe for my valuables, after we checked out & put our luggage in storage. Room service was an unexpected surprise in that the food was good, the staff in the kitchen & deliverer's quite pleasant, plus the prices were reasonable. Amazing! The not so good: the carpet in our bed chamber in room 915 was in my opinion gross. It was rippled & felt crunchy under foot & this is the first 4 * & above I've sadly had to say that about. At $300.+ a night I expect to feel I am in a luxurious space & I didn't, when it came to the overall feel of our room. The hotel has undergone renovations & the rooms are meant to have a modern feel, which they do, but unfortunately (again) the furniture looks worn & nicked and in the case of the desk chair, really bad. Plus there was no place to sit for breakfast in our big room. That was a miss on the designers part for sure. One more thing, that is in no way controllable by the hotel staff is even on the 9th floor, the noise from people on the street on Hollywood Blvd. goes on into the wee hours. If you have kids or you sleep lightly you may consider something faces away from the street or a super high floor. All in all, we enjoyed ourselves while we attended the AFI Film Fest & seeing all the red carpets being layed down everyday at Grauman's Chinese Theater, from our rooms view, was wonderful. Everything I requested we received with a smile & you cannot ask for more than that from a hotel. My husband gave it a thumbs up & if the crunchy carpet issue is resolved, I will too. Enjoy as always!

“Clean hotel & central location” I stayed here for a couple nights while attending a conference at the convention center. The location was perfect - less than a minute walk from the convention center and just a couple blocks to the downtown area. A bike path along a small river for running was also very close by. The hotel was clean and seemed to be renovated recently.

“Extrem laut” Dieses Motel war diesmal das Schlechteste auf unserer Reise. Der Wifi Zugang war eine Katastrophe... und gerade an einem der beiden Abende wo wir dort waren brauchten wir dringend Internet.... Dann hatten wir um uns rum 2 Familien mit Kindern, die über usn rumtrampelnten, das man dachte die Decke kommt gleich runter... danne in Geschrei und Getobe bis in dei nacht und morgens ab 6 Uhr. Die Wände waren megadünn... so was hatten wir bisher in keinem anderen Hotel.. Gut vielleicht lag es auch an den Familien die vielleicht besonderns laut waren.. Frühstück gab es auch nur bis 9 Uhr... und dann war der iniraum um 08.30 total überfüllt..wieder aufgrund der Kinder ein Gematsche überall.. Zimmer waren auch nur Durchschnitt... hatten zwar einen Kühlschrank, der war auch so megalaut (gehört vielleicht zum Konzept die Geräuschkulisse ..haha). dass wir ihn nachts ausgestellt haben. insgesamt würden wir hier auf keinen Fall mehr übernachten

“Good value, nice breakfast included” We stayed at this hotel for only two nights, but were pleasantly surprised. In such an expensive city, this hotel's price was really decent. Nice rooms, very clean and quiet. Breakfast was included and had a good variety to choose from, but best of all was the laundry room! We had just arrived from almost a week in Ottawa and had a LOT of laundry to do before our cruise leaving from Baltimore. Yeah! Going to a laundromat is always depressing and can be scary, especially in an unfamiliar city. (And we will never pay $3.00 per pair of ginch!) The hotel's location was decent, but when we asked the concierge how long it would take to walk to the Capitol, (we had a tour at 0850), he was super wrong by saying 15 minutes! We had to hail a taxi mid-way there, and we are a pretty fit family. Oh, well, we made it!. When we go back to this amazing city, we would definitely stay here again!

“Downtown Denver” Stayed here one night on business, the hotel is very nice. It is a bit confusing with the two buildings. I stayed in the Tower Building, but there are hotel employees around to help you out. There is an outdoor pool open year round (heated I am assuming) and this hotel is close to all the shops and restaurants and a short walk to the Pepsi Center.

“Very good....however, not great for 5 star property” Ritz Carlton properties are always of high quality -- which is what you expect of 5 star hotels at this price point. The hotel is quite nice - rooms are large & comfortable. The in-room coffee service is higher quality than most & I always appreciate when evening turndown service includes bottled water. The bathroom is ok, not great. Surprisingly, the comfortable chairs have no lighting so need to rely on light on bedside table or natural light during day (yes, I know this is a nitpick). In room safe is small. Hotel service is, as expected, very good. Staff is helpful and accomodating - & a lot of staff available to help. Gym is nice sized & well equipped. Being in Nob Hill - if choosing location for proximity to local sites, need to be aware of the hills. On the positive side, walking to/from the local attractions provides an opportunity to elevate the heart rate & burn off a few extra calories.

“Nice Stay” I love the Magnolia - its always clean and comfortable. I just got back from a 3 night stay. I had a spacious room with two queen beds. The bathroom has a big soaking tub and a great shower. They offer 2 complimentary cocktails - which I enjoyed - a night. The breakfast is not that great, but its also included. I did not have the milk and cookies. The only negative would be the sheets had a lot of pills and were a little scratchy, but once I asked for clean sheets, they were fine. Another negative, no wireless in the room and a small TV. The pool is on the roof - and I did enjoy that. The hotel is very accomodating to the business traveler - they even gave me a small gift the last night - a nice box of candies and two bottles of water. It was a good trip.

“Ideal for stop-overs and short trips. Great business hotel.” I did not choose this hotel by choice "per se". Using Priceline, you are obligated to stay at the hotel they select if you "bid your own price". DATE OF STAY: - December 26, 2006 PRICE: - Our price was very good ($93 USD including all taxes, $75 pre-tax/fees). CONCIERGE: - Very helpful and friendly. I arrived at the hotel around noon and was able to check-in right away. The concierge agreed to watch over my car in the main entrance area so that I could freshen up for about 30 minutes. Service was friendly and they made the specific effort to remember my name so they could greet me courteously upon my return. FRONT DESK: - Very helpful and friendly. They were able to check me into a room despite my early arrival. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: - Lobby was very modern and contemporary. Reminded me of a high-end office complex foyer/lobby. There was a café in the lobby area where you could surf the internet for a $15 fee. - Elevators were clean and modern. HOTEL ROOM: - Clean, spaciously and well-equipped. - Free Starbucks coffee packs available with the in-suite coffee maker. - Decent toiletries. - Television with pay-per-view capability PARKING: - You could opt for valet or self-parking. I chose to self-park. The parkade is adjacent to the hotel and connected to the lobby. It was well-lit. FACILITIES: - I did not explore the hotel swimming pool. My hotel room overlooked the pool and the LAX airport in the distance. Aircraft noise was not a concern. OVERALL: - I would stay here again for the convenient location and high calibre of facilities. If you want a romantic hotel, this is not it. This is an ideal business hotel for the busy traveller who wants good service and no nonsense. Booking over Priceline yielded very good prices.

“Clean, comfortable, great location and not too pricey” Stayed four days and found the location to be perfect. The room was clean and comfortable and fairly large. The lobby restaurant was superior to most hotel offerings, and there were many more within a ver short walk. I would definitely stay again.

“hotel da favola” l'ingresso e la hall meravigliose rispecchiano il lusso che trovi anche nelle camere,grandi e pulite!sembrava di essere in un film!!non a caso ci ahnno girato anche "natale a new york"di De Sica!posizione buona per muoversi a piedi e vicina alla metro!!di meglio non si potrebbe chiedere!

“superb” Not much to add to the other reviews other than to say that most are right on target. We stayed there the evening of pole day at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. For $103 (including taxes) we had a big room, couch, mini-fridge, HD TV, free wireless internet, continental breakfast. If I had to complain, there didn't seem to be many restaurants nearby, but the front desk had menus from a Chinese place that delivered to the room.

“Lives up to expectations and exceeds” When reviewing a Four Seasons hotel you start out at a very high level of expectations. The Chicago Four Seasons meets those lofty expectations. The hotel is located in a nice area close to Lake Michigan and near the John Hancock tower. Starting at the 8th floor of the tower in which it resides, views are stunning in every direction. Rooms are impeccably furnished and clean. The shower is fountain of relaxation and the bathroom stocked with L'Occitane products. The gym and dressing rooms were spotless and the hotel's pool, while not ideal for lap swimming, was beautiful and still did the job. If you do use the gym or pool, bring the clothes down with you as lockers and even a bathing suit drying machine are available. The staff is courteous and the whole environment is lush and refined.

“Will Return Again” We stayed at Hotel Metro for the very first time a couple of days before Christmas in 2006. The room that we stayed is smaller, and the view from our room faced the alley. Not the best view but it's very Hopper-like. Our room was located next to the elevator, which was a little loud but not problematic. The hotel staff members were really friendly and helpful. The best thing about the hotel was the breakfast! A wide range of selection everyday! Kudos to the chefs and cooking staff! The hotel is located just down the road from great shops, like Macy's! Also, check out the Korean restaurant (Hanbat restaurant) near the hotel. It opens late, service is fast, and food is so yummy and inexpensive. Bryant park also is a few blocks from the hotel. The hotel is in a great location, but it's quiet at night. We definitely will return again!

“Price up by $30/night for no reason” I have stayed here for work before at a certain rate, that is usually LOWEST in summer since AZ is so dead for tourism in the summer. However, during my recent three day stay, I was charged $30 more per night than ever before. The only reason I stay here over other competitors in the arear (Courtyard or Homewood Suites) is the great rate. However, next time I will pay the same rate and stay at Homewood Suites. They also offer a free breakfast and I won't have to deal with a hot room because Homewood as central air- this hotel has a box airconditioner on the window. Shop around before you book here. This once great deal is gone.

“Excellent service, great room” I was really impressed with the attitude of the bellhop and valet as we arrived. They were so friendly and full of information. We had a lovely big room with very spacious bathroom. Only a few blocks walk to Chinatown where we had dinner and then walked on to North Beach for drinks. We love San Francisco and prefer this location to Union Square.

“A special treat and moving experience” When I enter this establishment, I feel like I am stepping into hallowed ground. The first obvious difference from any other hotel in this area are the displays commemorating the proud history of the US Marine Corps; if you are lucky, you may be greeted by two bulldogs wearing Marine uniforms, or the pup who has already outgrown his first uniform. The third floor hallways have extensive bios displayed for every commandant since the Revolutionary War. The 11th floor has a memorial to all Marines who have given their lives defending the country. On every floor there are tributes to the sacrifices and accomplishments of the Marine Corps throughout their history. On this trip, a small plaque caught my attention; it had the names of six 15-16 year old Marines killed in action in several different wars. I increase my knowledge of and appreciation for the Marine Corps on every visit. There is a superb gym with every conceivable piece of workout equipment in the basement, including a serious three lane lap pool. The top floor houses the superb Leatherneck Grill with breathtaking views of San Francisco, great breakfast buffet, delicious dinners (had the rack of lamb this time), and outstanding service(!). I am not a Marine but I believe everyone should spend some time perusing the displays and increasing their awareness and appreciation for this great branch of the military. The arrangement of the rooms make you feel more like you are staying in someone's very comfortable home than in some kind of commercial property. I suspect that all of this great hospitality and service is attributable to a staff truly dedicated to the mission of maintaining this tribute to the Marine Corps and their members; it starts with the "landlord", Major General Myatt, USMC (ret.) who served in two wars. I highly recommend this hotel experience!

“Terrific location, classic Ritz service” I'm quite surprised to read some of the negative reviews that preceeded this. My impression is that some people just can't be pleased. I was there the same night as the last reviewer - true, there was a technological problem that meant the room keys didn't work - big deal?! The hotel posted staff on every floor to escort you to your room and open the door. By the way, it was a problem at other hotels in Boston that night too (not a Ritz problem, but the key vendor). The location is fantastic, steps from the Common, close to downtown, public transport, good restaurants, etc. Staff is polished, responsive, available and nothing short of what I would expect at a Ritz-Carlton. My room was spacious, comfortable, quiet (I'm a very light sleeper), bathroom has a deep tub and stall shower. Absolutely no complaints and I'd stay there again.

“Sehr schönes Hotel für Erkundungen.” Das Marriott in Philadelphia Downtown ist ein (riesen)großes Stadthotel. Das Hotel befindet sich direkt an der Market Street. Das Hotel wird unterteilt in einen "Neuen Trakt" und einen "Alten Trakt" der dann über Rolltreppen zu erreichen ist. die Zimmer sind im typisch amerikanischen Stil eingerichtet. Im Neuen Trakt wirken die Zimmer "normal" im Alten Trakt sind die Zimmer sehr groß mit großen Fenstern etc. Das Zimmer ist Sauber!. In der Lobby findet man auch einen kleinen Starbucks. Leider ist der Internet Zugang im Hotel nur über Kabel (laptop) möglich. Von ́diesem Hotel aus kann man wunderbar die Stadt zu Fuss erkunden !!

“Very good hotel near museums and parks” We stayed here in December to attend the Joffrey Ballet at the Auditorium Theater (just 2 blocks away) and visit the Art Institute (about 6 blocks away). This is a great location for the South Loop, and also reasonably close to the Loop north of the river. It's a very large, older hotel, but the rooms are in good shape and well furnished. Our room with two double beds also had two full bathrooms. Room service food was excellent, and the breakfast buffet was way beyond the normal -- well prepared eggs, french toast, etc, delicious pastries and an omelet bar. The room rate was reasonable for Chicago. We had an interior room, and it would be worth asking for a room with a view of the lake. Parking was expensive but convenient.

“Clean & Comfortable” Overall we were quite impressed with this hotel. The rooms were extremely clean for my fiance (who is ultra picky about cleanliness) & the bed was ultra soft (even better than Westin's Heavenly beds). We liked the colour & styling both of the rooms & of the entire hotel. We had a 29th floor harbour view which I could have sat staring outside for hours. The location was perfect for walking to the harbour & for driving to "Captain James Landing" which is a must-go for any crab lovers! Only issue we had was that the price was quite steep as we paid almost $400 (after tax & parking) for one night. I wouldn't quite put this hotel as a 5 star...like Ritz Carltons & Four Seasons so charging that much is a little crazy for me. However, if you are able to find a promo code for this place & to stay here for under $250, defnly book it immediately!

“Previous reviews were accurate--very nice hotel and stay” My wife and I traveled to Chicago this weekend for a short getaway over the Labor Day holiday. I read many of the previous reviews and feel like they give a very accurate depiction of the Residence Inn River North. First, the location is great. You are about 3 blocks north of the Chicago River on Dearborn and about 4 blocks west of Michigan Avenue. You are only about 2 blocks from the redline station on State and Grand. Tons of restaurants within walking distance. We had no problem getting anywhere we wanted. Safety/security was no concern. I felt totally comfortable walking around at all hours of the day and night. Will mention what others have said about being near a fire station--one block to the north. Yes, you can hear the sirens. Since we read the reviews, I requested a high floor and stayed on the 21st. Had no issues with noise from street bothering us. But the lower the floor, the higher the risk of you being bothered by street noise. Room was very spacious and comfortable. Had a decent kitchen setup--full fridge, microwave, dishwasher, sink and 2 burner oven. Nice look to the kitchen too with cabinetry and stainless appliances. room had a couch and full-sized chair in sitting area. Full wall was total glass with a nice city view. Commercial property directly across the road. Did have smaller building across as well that allowed for a full view to the NE. We could see all the way over to Marriott on Michigan Avenue along with several other highrise residential units. I thought the view was decent (we faced towards dearborn and looked North ). Bedding was good. Not the top of the line Marriott mattress though. But I had no problems. Shower was above average. total glass door and plenty of room. Only downside of bathroom area was only single vanity. The vanity was located next to bed in nook before entering bathroom/shower. Double vanity would have made for much more room for two trying to get ready. TV was situated next to window in middle of room. some may not like this setup. Normally the TV is placed in front of the bed. Can't do that in this room setup. But wasn't a big deal to me. i wasn't there to watch TV. TV channels were Direct TV Satellite. Ok selection with HBO too. Lobby entrance is on second level. Saw where some people complained about this. Dont really understand this. Yes, you have to go to two different sets of elevators to get to your room. I assume they do this for security reasons and logistics of property. Its not a big deal. I thought service was excellent. All of the workers that we encountered were pleasant and helpful. Service was not a problem. Complimentary breakfast was a madhouse. It was extremely busy and crowded. But...you are getting a free breakfast at a downtown hotel. Food selection was good--waffles, sausage, eggs, potatoes, bagels and donuts. If you don't want to mess with the crowd, go down the street and pay for breakfast--pretty simple. You do get free wireless internet at this property, too. In case you haven't read other posts, this property does share the building with a Springhill Suites. When you come up the street level elevator, the Springhill lobby is to the left and the Residence Inn is to the right. Residence Inn does have three computers downstairs that you can use as well. Just a couple of more points--does have workout room and pool on top floor. No room service or restaurant. Valet parking or self park. I think $48 and $38 per day. All in all, I was very happy with this property. It was exactly what I was expecting--maybe even a little bit better. Is this a 5-star hotel? No. Don't forget, this is a Residence Inn--a few notches down the Marriott food chain. But it is a very nice and clean property in a fantastic location. For the price, I think it is very difficult to beat in downtown Chicago. Read the reviews and make your own choice. Are you looking for luxury like a Michigan Avenue hotel? You will probably be disappointed. But I wasn't thinking this was going to be the Ritz Carleton or a Four Seasons. This is a top of the line Residence Inn with quality service, clean rooms and a fabulous location.

“Not recommended” I am a regular guest at this establishment and stayed there most recently for a week in July for business. The hotel has declined from its earlier days and the rooms show signs of aging and lack of maintenance. Other things that made me wonder whether this is a Westin or a Motel 6 include: 1) the horrific sound the toilet makes is enough to encourage me to drink/eat less. 2) The carpets on my floor (43rd floor, starwood preferred floor) is littered with debris and uncollected room service trays with left-over food. 3) The bed sheets never got changed during my week long stay there. I suspect my newly developed itching is somewhat related to the not-so-clean sheets. 4) The fire sprinker in the room has its base detached from the wall. 5) Had to call housekeeping to tidy up the room twice. 6) They no longer have wireless access in the lobby and make you pay $15 a day for internet access. The only plus is the location. But there are other nice hotels nearby as well. I would not stay at this hotel again.

“What a let down!!” Friends have been staying at this place for years and you always hear stories about it. It was a major let down for me. The ceilings had chipped paint, the room was dark and ugly, painted in a rust color. The furniture was straight out of the seventies and the television was so small you had to sit 12 inches away to see it. The room had no air conditioner and was extremely hot inside, even though it was rather chilly outdoors. Calls to the front desk went unanswered several times and when we finally got someone on the phone she said she was too busy to answer. It ended up that our heater was broken and was stuck on, but it took close to five hours to get the maintenance person there to make the repair. I will say that the maintenance staff (orlando) was very knowledgeable and helpful. The rest of the staff was just RUDE, The price was rather reasonable and the room is above average size for San Francisco. The location is amazing and you can't beat it. I wouldn't stay there again. The rude staff, dirty, ugly rooms and overall total experience was sad.

“Very close to GW University and Foggy Bottom Metro” We stayed here for 2 nights for a visit to George Washington University. We were on the highest floor and the rooftop outdoor pool was above us and it leaked so the carpet in the hall was soaked. They did clean up the water, but the next day the carpet had a musty smell. The room was clean and spacious, but the shower didn't have a lot of pressure and the beds were on the soft side. In general, the staff at the front desk was not overly friendly or helpful. I'm a Hilton Honors Gold VIP member and it is not unusual for a hotel to provide complimentary amenities (like room upgrade and bottled water and breakfast and free internet) that are above the required complimentary amenities, however, this hotel only provided the basic upgrade of either a free breakfast (Continental delivered to the room) or free internet. The kitchen cupboards and the furniture was a bit worn. The kitchen included a hodge podge of dishes and flatware. The best part was the location. It was no more than a 3-minute walk from the Foggy Bottom Metro (go up escalator, do a 180, and walk thru the plaza, cross 24th street, go to the far side of the block and take a left and the hotel is at the end of the block). It is also a short walk to the Kennedy Center and Watergate. It was a great location for visiting George Washington University. The area is quite safe as the GW police patrol the area.
“Exhaust fumes at the pool” Beware of the exhaust fumes at the pool. They have a loading dock directly underneath. And very loud. Very, very loud.

“Good value, good service and good location” Stayed here for 4 nights on a business trip. 1) Hotel has a small footprint with 8 rooms per floor. 2) Rooms are average size for NY, (smaller than other cities). 3) Staff was very efficient and friendly. I had a couple of minor maintenance issues with the room which were addressed efficiently and speed. 4) I had a 3rd floor room facing the street, but street noise was not an issue 5) Had breakfast at the restaurant one day...typical overpriced hotel fare, (a lot of better values in the neighborhood).

“Old Style!!” Posizione a parte,ovvero alla partenza del Cable Car sulla Powell,l'hotel non e'il massimo!meglio,le camere sono pulite,grandissime e comode....ma e'tutto vecchiotto e si vede!il personale,cinese,e'gentile e disponibile,il grosso difetto e'la colazione,povera e arroccata nella hall....in compenso vi potete rifare con uno stupendo Lavazza Point all'interno dell'hotel stesso!...occhio ai parcheggi che,come in tutta Sfo sono abbastanza costosi!

“Good family hotel but a bit isolated” This property was much nicer than I had expected. We were in town the weekend of the marathon and rates in other Boston hotels were astronomical. A Sweet Dreams rate of $189 for our family of 4 seemed downright cheap in comparison. It included a great breakfast buffet for 2 adults and our 11 year old son--our 13 year old daughter was considered an adult for purposes of breakfast, although kids under 18 stay free with parents. Parking was another $20 and, if we wanted wireless, we would have had to pay another $10 per day. However there are computers in the 2nd floor lobby where we could access the internet and that met our needs.
