The bedroom was large and had a comfortable bed, desk, TV/amoire and a phenomenal view of the Charles river (we were in a corner unit on the 11th floor). The sitting room had a sofa bed (not so great) and room for a rollaway (nice one--$10 night) so it was perfect for our kids. They were excited about the plasma screen TV, but it was on the wall in an odd place given the furniture layout. There was some wear and tear obvious and some older looking fixtures, but anything that could be easily updated had been done (furnishings, linens, etc...). The concierge service varied a great deal; however, William was very helpful. The concierge arranged the shuttle service which we utilized each day because even with a car, we only drove when necessary (such as to the conference I was attending). It took 10-15 minutes to Copley Square and 30+ minutes to the Aquarium--through heavy city traffic. Though technically in the city of Boston, the hotel is much closer to downtown Cambridge than to any of the interesting parts of Boston and on a nice day, it would be a lovely walk to Harvard Square (about a mile). The shuttle also goes to Harvard Square. We didn't mind the location because we had stayed down in the heart of Boston the week before and felt less compelled to stay downtown. Harvard Square is a very interesting area with lots of restaurants and pubs and the Coop--Harvard's great bookstore. All in all, a good family hotel in a beautiful, but somewhat distant location for a visit to Boston.

“A Fine Weekend!” Stayed the weekend at a great weekend rate (from the hotel's own website!) in two rooms. Good, central location. Beautiful, large rooms. Both (even the single) had a sitting area. Big bathtubs, all ammenties (including double window shades to keep out the aggressive street light. ) Tinkling chandeliers in the evators, very good service. New York Times delivered to the room and an accessible, high speed computer for guest use in a lobby alcove. Helpful concierge. The bar/breakfast area off the lobby was very nice, but I would steer clear of the restaurant--too pricey for the level of the cuisine. The breakfast I had included over-cooked sausage and dry, almost stale toast. They should stick to the hotel business.

“Not bad” I booked through Hotwire at a great rate. The hotel was about a 20 minute walk to century city mall, and wasn't near much of the happening area. This could be a good thing or bad thing depending on the person. Good Things: I liked the fact that it was a quiet hotel. Valet was very quick and efficient. Very comfortable beds, good size room. Bathroom towels/linens were clean, and loved the separate shower and tub. Bad Things: Knowing I was 1 person, I got a room with 2 doubles. When asked to switch rooms to a King it became a lot of hassle for them. After going into 2 rooms (that apparently was only available) that smelt like smoke, I opted to stay in the 2 Double Bed room. This hotel I believe is supposed to be smoke free. Bellhops are pretty bothersome, trying to take your luggage even when you say you're fine. The pool area, although beautiful and comfortable, is in an area where you get high winds. It is therefore an area that ends up being cold, so you can't enjoy sitting outside by the pool. It's VERY chilly on a hot day. Maybe when it goes into the high 90's and above it won't be as bad. I was there during mid 80's where Santa Monica Beach was hotter. Even though I had a lot of bad things, I might stay again. I guess it depends on price. The room itself was fabulous, the front desk could have been more accommodating. I'm hoping that if I end up staying here again, I will have a better experience. Just to finalize this all, I've been to the Hyatt down the street which is a great hotel and probably prefer that over the Intercontinental when it comes to the pool area. It is, however more of a family hotel and louder than the Intercontinental. Intercontinental also does have more of a luxurious feel than the Hyatt Century City Plaza.
“すばらしい” はじめてボストンに行くには一番いいホテルかもしれません。 近くの川からの眺めも最高です。 ホテル内のレストラン、雰囲気、どれをとっても最高です

“Really great hotel...mediocre restaurant.” I love this hotel. The public areas and rooms are beautiful. The staff are great. Extremely comfortable. Great TV's. Great bathrooms. Great toiletries. On this last visit, I was surprised to find a very ratty, frayed and TORN towel in my room. It seems impossible that someone could have folded this towel and not noticed that it should be retired. The restaurant...OK "hotel food" but not a good value. If you are trapped in the hotel, the menu offering are "ok" and nothing more, and the prices are high. The breakfast buffet is nothing more than adequate--it's really over-priced for the quality offered. $13 a day for the internet access is, IMHO, highway robbery. This is the highest price I have ever heard off for internet access. Total rip-off. This is a terrific hotel with a beautiful restaurant that serves food that does not live up to the atmosphere. Order delivery or drive out. Maybe enjoy the restaurant/bar area with a cup of coffee or a cocktail before or after your meal. And try to avoid paying for the internet here...maybe if enough people say "no"...the management here will get the message.

“Nice friendly clean hotel” Last minute trip to spend time with family so I turned in some points and this is where we ended up. The hotel is friendly and clean. I was surprised what a great experience we had because it was an airport hotel. We ate dinner with the family there and it was good. It was nice to actually visit where it wasn't noisy and we didn't have to stand in any lines with children. The next morning we had breakfast for $10.00 and it was good. It's not a buffet and selections are limited but to start the day off we felt it was just right. I would return to this hotel without hesitation. It was only 4 miles to the Awesome shopping center and my only regret is we didn't have more time to stay longer.

“Very pleasant stay at the Fairmont” We stayed at the Fairmont recently while moving our eldest into his dormitory. Service was top-notch from the doorman to housekeeping, and the rooms were spacious, very clean and very comfortable. Our younger child, who had to spend one night on a rollaway bed, said that even that was quite comfortable. The room included both a coffee maker and an electric kettle for tea, amenities that were quite appreciated in our family. The room service breakfast was fairly pricey for what we received, but we had a light meal one night in the piano bar that was really good (try the Bee-tini while it's available. It was surprisingly refreshing), and the young woman who served us was just delightful. The hotel is well-located on M Street, and just a brief walk from Georgetown. I would most definitely return.
“Simple propre et grande chambre” Ras un bel hotel chambres spacieuses et propres belle literie.Free bus pour l aéroport.

“Satisfactory Experience” We stayed at the hotel for two nights and found the location excellent, the staff very nice and the breakfast excellent. The hotel could have been cleaner and the room, while nice, was dark and the furniture outdated. In addition, the pool was closed for renovation- something we did not find out until we arrived. We were able to use the pool at the Hilton a block away but it was inconvenient to go over during the winter. In general, it was a positive experience.

“Staff not very friendly...just okay experience.” Stayed for one night prior to an early AM flight out of San Antonio. Found one of the front desk staff to not be very helpful at all; came back later and different staff members were much better. Had trouble using the free WIFI - took forever to get it connected based on the way they had it set up. Airport shuttle was fine. Room was clean - could tell that it had been recently renovated so everything was clean and new. Had a room that said 2 - queen size beds, but they didn't feel like queens to me - for as small as they were, it felt more like 2 doubles.

“It's ok if you're traveling for business” The staff is so helpful and friendly. Couldn't be better. But the hotel leaves a lot to be desired. After I checked in, my bellman (new at the job) pointed out the giant cockroach near the elevators where we stood. For the price, it's fine for a night on business, but it's location is a bit odd for vacation travelers--it's in the middle of a business district with high rises but no people out on the sidewalks and no restaurants or cafes near by. It reminds me of downtown Los Angeles many years ago. But maybe it's partly because its 104 degrees, and humid, and who would want to be outside? I chose this hotel because it was very close to my business meeting. Maybe I should have chosen wiser. In the restaurant downstairs the plastic was peeling off the banquets but the food was surprisingly good. The room is pretty nice with adequate room to move around in. For the price, I can't complain about the room.

“Central property that does everything it says on its website” This property is good value and very central just off the magnificent mile, all of the main shops and attractions within walking distance, the John Hancock tower is next door. The river walk is only minutes away, Navy Pier slightly further but still within walking distance. The hotel matches its website perfectly, the amenities in the bedrooms are exactly as decribed on the website - microwave, fridge, safe, etc. there are even bathrobes (this is regularly stated on websites but on arrival nowhere to be seen!), the bedroom was large although the bathroom is quite small, no storage space other than one small shelf. The staff were very friendly however some of the concierge weren’t as knowledgeable about the area as I would have expected. The only negative I would have about this hotel is the lift(s), we were lucky to be on the 6th floor which meant we could on occasion take the stairs as the delays (at certain times) were quite lengthy! The 18th floor bar is nice, the views over the city are lovely at night, again be aware of the lifts, the bar does not serve food but there is a restaurant on the ground floor. For those that enjoy breakfast there are two options room service or donuts in the ground floor coffee shop (only open in the mornings). I would recommend this property and will stay here again on my return to Chicago.

“Firing on all cylinders” I stayed 2 nights at this property for work in September 2012. I really enjoyed my stay. The hotel was nearly full but I still felt like I was very well taken care of. Here are the plusses: +terrific location, easily walkable to lots of attractions +friendly front desk staff - they assisted me with reactivating my Starwood Preferred Guest account so I could transfer my points to Southwest +lovely lobby design with lots of places to hang out and get online, or have a drink/coffee +fresh, updated design in the rooms +VERY comfortable beds and pillows +easy in and out parking with friendly valets (though very expensive, $51/nt with tax) +safe neighborhood overall A couple ever-so-slight negatives: -curtains in the room. There was no gauzy curtain to let light in but prevent people from seeing in. Either the shade was up completely (and people can see in from the hotel across the street) or the blackout shade was completely down. This is a really small negative, but wish there was some kind of light filtering window covering. -parking is pricey. The garage across the street is half the price, if you need to park a car.

“I've never been this disgusted in a national chain...” Checked in on a Wednesday afternoon, worked out, showered and then headed to dinner. After getting back to my room and getting ready for bed, pulled down the comforter to find blood stains on the bedsheet. I'm not a particularly needy traveler, but this is the most disgusting thing I've ever seen in a national chain. When combined with the smell of the hotel (I'd bet someone was cooking curried goat on a hot plate in their room), this is by far the worst experience I've ever had with Courtyard, or any other Marriott or national hotel property. I'll give the staff credit for being responsive. 3 people, including the GM, showed up to "fix" it, but I don't think I'll stay here again.

“Excellent value!” TA reviews can nv be wrong! Booked a 2 nights stay at the Dolphin Motel and my stay throughout was pleasant! Felt safe sleeping at night knowing there will someone at the desk 24hrs with security cameras all around! The rooms are small but very clean! There're also free Wifi and the speed was fast! Wasnt expecting that since it was free! Do not hestitant to stay here when u are in San Diego!

“Perfect hotel.” We bought a package through a travel company at a great deal - such a great hotel, location, etc. The staff was wonderful and helpful. The room had a very cool bathtub - complimentary wine, thick bathrobes and a French press for coffee in your troop! Felt pampered. Ask the conceriege for suggestions - so knowlegeable. We loved it and will return.

“Great Location” The location of this hotel for visiting the mall was excellent. The staff, room, beds and bath were great. Pool was small, but ok. We signed up for the Priority Club (free) when we reserved our room online without really thinking about the benefits--we were glad we did so. We were given early check in at 11am on request. We overheard other people being told they could leave their bags with the bellman, but they would have to wait till the regular check in time. We probably could have paid less for a different, but comparable, hotel not as convenient to walking the mall, but for us it was worth it.

“Great location for shopping, nice rooms, service non-existent” I like staying at the Westin Oaks and Westin Galleria when I go on shopping weekends to Houston. The location cannot be beat. Take the elevator to the mall. Rooms are nice and comfortable. I spent the Mexican holiday weekend of December 10-12 here and it seemed like so did the rest of Mexico. Service does not exist. Front Desk is a disorganized mess. Bellmen disappear forever and this trip I saw three of them delivering a blanket - no wonder why they are never in the lobby. Rooms are comfortable, but not very clean. I was not bothered much by the smell of cigarette smoke in my room (520) or the butts on the tiny terrace. However, my first morning, I sat in the comfortable chair to read the paper and drink the in-room Starbuck's coffee and found that the smell came from a dirty ashtray on the table next to the chair. I had not noticed it, even when I opened the terrace door to air out the room. (I also kicked the butts off the terrace and as this room was right above the main hotel entry, did not do much to improve image.) WATCH YOUR ROOM BILL CHARGES. I had US$27 for parking even though I had no car and US$30.12 for one Sprite I drank from the mini bar. There is no hassle when you point out such issues, the staff takes off the charges right away. It must be common at this factory hotel with minimal service to mischarge guests and thus, there is no arguing needed. Would I stay here again? Yes, the location is great, rooms not bad and for a weekend of shopping, I really do not need the hotel staff. Do I think the hotel can improve? Absolutely, but they clearly do not care, this is a cash cow. Also, elevators are slow, especially when there are banquet events. There is no service elevator so prepare to ride with luggage, maid carts, etc. The Westin Oaks to me is in a slightly better location in the mall than the Westin Galleria, but we are talking meters of walking. All else is the same.

“Great Position, nice hotel .....but” Everything about this hotel should be great. The position on Shelter Island is truly wonderful with the large yacht harbour. The suite we had was marina-front and spacious. The "but" is that everything about the hotel was "not quite". The hotel charges luxury prices and everything we experienced was really good.....just not our definition of luxury for $300 a night. Nothing was particularly wrong and if you are paying $170 a night, you might consider the place fantastic. Nothing at all was wrong, it was just "not quite" Do please note that we had a really nice time in wonderful San Diego and the Red Sails restaurant along from the hotel is great

“Excellent location, okay stay” We travel to downtown Chicago once yearly and have stayed at a number of hotels near the Magnificent Mile over the years. Got a great rate through Travelzoo and decided to stay at the Doubletree. It wasn't my most favorite hotel in Chicago, but the location is excellent if you're spending the day on the Mag Mile or at Navy Pier. The hotel itself was nice, rooms were spacious, and even though our room was just off the elevators, we didn't hear any noise from them at night. Staff was very friendly at checkin and checkout as well. Our room overlooked a neighboring office building -- and looking out our windows, we could see reflections of others staying in the hotel if their curtain wasn't closed! A little odd... Also, the heat/AC unit in the room drove me a little nuts, because it shut itself on and off all night. It was January and we needed heat, so we couldn't just shut it off. Despite that, if we got a great rate again, I'd consider staying there again.

“Great boutique hotel, spa room is worth the upgrade” Stayed here for business and had standard king room which was very nice and love the decor. Had opportunity for extra $40/ night to upgrade to spa room. Definitely recommend if u like pampering. Huge glass shower with massive soaking bathtub as well. Window to the outside in shower/ tub area so tons of natural light. Nice to bathe and look out over city at night. I loved the modern, animal print decor and robes. Highly rec'd this hotel for a nice stay away from standard corporate chains.

“Great view of airport for us. Service good. Gym good. Location close to LAX.” I was upgraded to the Exec level and that may have played a role in the view. For me sights and sounds of airports are wonderful. As this was. The lounge was small for the crowd, but great view and nice service. Breakfast not amazing but fine. Gym good. Large hotel. But given that, service was above average.

“Really good Four Points with clearly better service” Four Points generally offers good hotel-business-category rooms: desk, chair, comfortable and inviting bed. Plus you get a free bottle of water. This hotel is well located in Washington. Although a bit far (for walking) to the Mall, but provides easy access to transportation (public and tourist). The service is a clearly better than most Four Points. You get warmly greeted outside, assisted with your lugages and helped to the front desk. There reception was warm, professional and quick. The lobby is stylish and inviting with confortable seating and an internet access. The room was up to Four Points standard, which means a lot (typically better than most, I find). It was clean, reasonnably spacious. It probably was renovated not long ago. The ventilation is a bit old and has problem keeping your requested temperature. The fitness center has an usual variety of apparels compared with other hotel. In front of each is a personnal TV. Cool. Breakfast at the restaurant was ok, but menu had a rather small choice. In all a smart, confortable choice in Washington. It stands the comparison to more expansive hotels. Like most Four Points.

“Great hotel!” This is the hotel we choose to stay when we are in Austin, the location cannot be beaten! I like going out to 6th street and not taking long to get back to my room after going to the bars. The hotel is gorgeous! The front staff are nice and so are the servers in the bar/grill. The room was so gorgeous, we had a corner room so we had a double view. I liked the ambiance of the room when we walked in, lamps with a dim light on and soft music to greets us. I highly recommend the Driskill, worth every penny and cannot wait to return.

“Convenient Luxury” Elegant art deco lobby. Beautiful entrance - especially from Park Ave. We had the corner room on the 12th floor and it was lovely. Only complaint is that it is a huge hotel. (you don't get that "personal service" feel like from small boutique hotels - there is a long line at the check-in, long wait on the phone, etc.) Great location - centrally located. LOVED telling the cabbie - "Take me to the Waldorf!"

“Great Hotel, Awesome Service” Wonderful location. Lots of bars, restaurants and hotels within walking distance. That said, everything you need for a great stay is in-house. The bar/lounge is top notch-- lovely cocktails and great snacks. In addition, the overall service is exemplary. The men at the front desk, Daniel and Aiden, really went the extra mile to make my stay special. Although this was a business trip, their extra care made me feel like I was on vacation. Kudos!

“Not bad, but nothing memorable” The location is on the north side of town with easy access to the highways. It's pretty easy to get to the UT campus or downtown from the hotel. The service was great. Very friendly staff that went out of their way to make us feel welcome. The hotel itself is worn. The rooms smell musty and there are stains on the carpet and curtains. We had 2 rooms and both had the same problem. Large bathrooms and a strange shower head that rotates when water comes out. The mini fridge was very poor quality. The TV was actually pretty nice. The elevators are extremely slow even though there are only 3 floors. Breakfast is standard fare for Country Inn. No surprises and a good value with hot meats and biscuits. We got what we were expecting out of our stay. It's a nice hotel for families, but that's where it ends. I wouldn't stay here if I was traveling solo.

“San Francisco Gem!” We stayed at the Westin one night for our friend's wedding. I made a reservation through the Rooms Reservations Manager- and he was wonderful about a great rate, and he attempted to upgrade the room. HOWEVER- at check-in- the front desk agent decided to void the upgrade to speed us through the line! I was very disappointed that he never even asked us if we'd like to wait for the upgraded room!! When we arrived at our room on the 11th floor, the door was OPEN! The room was clean and ready for us, but it was VERY disconcerting that the door to our room would be OPEN! The room was nice- the bathroom was typical San Francisco- VERY petite! The chandelier in the sleeping room was a nice touch.. The "heavenly" bed was a little less than heavenly- but it did the trick. For the location in San Francisco, if I was a tourist, this would be an impressive place to stay- but being a local, I expected a bit more!

“A big room with a comfortable bed” I stayed here because of its close proximity to UCLA. Traffic in LA is really bad (especially the 405 freeway) so proximity to where you'd want to go is a must. We reserved a standard room with a king size bed but what we got was like a suite. The living room was big. The room has two TVs plus kitchen and a refrigerator and a microwave. A walk-in closet was equipped with a safe. The bed was extremely comfortable. These positive have more than made up its slow internet connection and so so breakfast (Starbucks and Peets are only one block away).

“Mega-hotel overlooking the river & off Michigan Ave; clean, comfortable” A massive, convention-y hotel, characterized by a large glass-covered atrium-lobby, with ample space for lounge/dining area, gift shop, bar & restaurant, water pond, and the oh-so-80s metal rigging for lighting and hanging out ... maybe for evening disco too(?) ... but a very nice, convenient downtown hotel! Check-in is at the 2nd/mezzanine floor via escalator ... with a very nice welcome, and warm smiles at the front desk. We stayed 2 different times at this hotel within a span of a week, so we gave it a good test-run. Both times requesting King size bed, getting 2 different views. We liked both rooms, each slightly different in set-up and views (see attached pics). The Good: As we said, warm welcome checking in each time, but maybe given we are Platinum members of their loyalty program (hopefully, true for all guests). We stayed in the "West tower" each time, which offered high-floor, wonderful views from our rooms... first stay was facing the river below, tour boats, the Navy Pier and Lake Michigan, and the second stay, faced North with beautiful views of the river below and Wrigley building & others, up Michigan Ave. Rooms were modern, simple, comfortable, and most importantly, very clean. One stay, we had a glass-enclosed walk-in shower, and the other stay was standard tub/shower. They arranged one room differently than other, but same basic amenities & furniture. Bathrooms were clean throughout our stay, which included basic toiletries. The rooms were uber-quiet, with no hint of neighbors (and we knew there were people next door, and on our floor). We did not try the restaurants or room service in the hotel, given so many options in Chicago. There is an ample fitness center, with all expected equipment, but no pool. Even with its size, the hotel was very comfortable and nice. Internet was included as complimentary, but if not loyalty member, chargeable. Service beyond the check-in was adequate, especially given the size of this hotel. The hotel is right off Michigan Ave, right by (2) bridges that cross over the Chicago River. It's very convenient to walk North to Michigan Ave shopping, or East toward Navy Pier, or South toward the wonderful Millennium Park (Bean sculpture), Art Institute of Chicago, though a maybe for some, a little far (for walking) for all the other museums (Field, Shedd, Adler, etc) clustered further South. We found it very, very convenient, as there are tons of buses on Michigan Ave to take you anywhere, the EL subway somewhat close also, and plenty of taxis if preferred. Park the car for this city ... unless going to further outreaches! The bad: it's a busy atrium, with busy entrance of taxis, cars, and people going in/out. This is normal for a large sized hotel like this one. Gratefully, the West tower where we were, has its own entrance, and sped us to our rooms without having to go through the main lobby, and a bridge that connects the East tower (where lobby is) to our West tower. Do expect conventions to occur during your visit. The hotel has large meeting rooms, banquet halls, and ballrooms, to accommodate many activities, so it could be busy with people, loud (with music), and cordoned off areas. It was not a big deal for us, as we did not encounter any problems. Summary: It's a good, large convention oriented hotel, but suitable for all kinds of visitors, families, couples, etc.. It is a very clean, efficient, comfortable, modern hotel, with enough warmth for those who travel enough and do not need full service/hand-holding by staff. They were fine. Stay in the West tower if possible, as it is closer to the river, and offers great views of the Lake and city. Happy Hotel-ing !

“More like LA than SA...” My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary. This hotel is nice, but not my favorite. It is very contemporary and very dark. We prefer the Watermark hotel's design. The Valencia is a good value for a nice room. However, our room smelled like a smoking room and it was non-smoking. The bell boy told us it was the new fragrances being used to scent the rooms. The hotel is in a quiet part of the riverwalk which is nice. Don't stay here if you want a pool, there isn't one. If this is your first visit to San Antonio, I would stay elsewhere to get a true Texas experience.

“Stay here only when you can get a good rate (under US$200) and watch out for construction” I have stayed at the Mayflower before, typically when I accidentally end up with it through a bid on Priceline. This time, however, I was there for a conference (in another location) and booked because the hotel is generally solid and I could get my Marriott points. I had a decent size room (9th floor), but the location was slightly awful. It had a view of an internal courtyard which, on Thursday night, had the most infernal noise coming from it that sounded like construction. And there was a lot of it there during late November / early December. At 1am, that noise was a highly undesirable sound. I called the front desk but they couldn't do anything (other than offering to change my room which wasn't great at that time of the morning and I needed to be awake and functioning by 6am). Suffice to say, I put pillows over my head, used earplugs and took a sleeping pill. It worked eventually. The next night (Friday), however, had no noise. I also note: be careful about the minibar. It is very sensitive and even bumping it (or accidentally opening a door) is enough to result in having you charged several fees. So watch your bill. On the upside, the lobby is great, the location is superb, and the gym is free and quite good! And, if you're an elite Marriott customer, so is the internet. I'll be back under the right set of conditions.

“Comprehensive Review for Those Considering a Long Term Stay” Stayed at this hotel for 5 weeks for business reasons. Since I was a guest so long, I feel that I need to leave a comprehensive review. If you are just looking to stay here a night or so, it is a fine, if a bit dated, hotel and you could definitely do worse. Since we met so many at the hotel who stayed here for extended periods, I will systematicaly review the hotel with my opinions on the different aspects aimed at those considering long term stays. RECEPTION/CHECK IN The lady that checked us in was rude and unhelpful which got us off to a rough start. Thankfully, the vast majority of our interactions with the reception staff were very positive. Most are friendly, helpful and kind. Unfortunately, there are just a couple that probably need to improve their attitude. ROOM I was notified when we checked in that this was one of the original Residence Inns and there were no units that had partitioned rooms. Every room is a studio style. The set-up is much like an apartment complex with buildings with several units and everyone has their own walk up door. This is quite different than other Residence Inns that I have stayed at. We were hoping for a suite with a separate bedroom since we have an infant but that was not an option here. We stayed in a penthouse suite which we would highly recommend for guests with children. There is a common living area with fireplace, TV, couch and chairs; full kitchen with all appliances including dishwasher and disposal with a small breakfast nook and pantry; small dining area with 4 chairs and table; a pull down double bed across from dining table; desk diagnonal to the dining area and next to where the bed pulls down then a full bath. We actually put our daughter’s pack and play in the hallway to the bathroom as it was the only quiet and dark place. They supplied a very loud fan that helped with the noise. Upstairs is another double bed, small desk, another flat screen TV and full bath. The rooms are very drab and probably have not been updated in 10-15 years. Furniture is functional but well worn. The beds are ok but the pillows are super soft so be warned. I had to sleep with 3 of them. The upstairs gets VERY warm during the day even with a large fan they supplied and a ceiling fan both on high. We usually just didn’t go upstairs during the day. CABLE/INTERNET Cable is pretty decsent with 45 channels, all the ESPNs, movie channels, and HGTV. Missing the Food Network though. Internet was pretty slow and quite inconsistent. Pretty frustrating aspect of this property. BREAKFAST/RECEPTIONS Breakfast is served daily and there is a reception Monday-Thursday evenings with snacks and drinks. We were impressed with breakfast. I am not sure I would want to eat at my favorite restaurant every day for 5 weeks. So the fact that we would still go after 5 weeks is a testament to the variety and quality. The staff are incredible. Most of the reception food is like tortilla chips and nacho cheese but they have some days with cheeseburgers. Nothing great but if you are crunched for time or money, it is an option. HOUSEKEEPING Gems of this hotel! Nice, attentive, hard working. No complaints here. POOL Really nice pool area with two basketball courts, volleyball courts and a grilling area with two gas grills which we took advantage of a couple of times. They have balls and grill tools at the front desk. The pool is even 8ft at its deepest. The grounds crew sprays around the pool every day so it stays very clean. LAUNDRY Five washers and dryers that are large and efficient. Loads are $1 for both W or D and I never had to run a load twice in either machine. SHUTTLE Shuttle is operated by Blue Diamond and is shared with several other hotels in the area. I found it to be very frustrating: long waits, often spent over 30 minutes on the shuttle, drivers barely announcing that they are taking off, etc. The hotel is a 1.3 mile walk to the closest buildings of the medical center (Texas Children’s Hosptial) and takes 25-35 minutes depending on your pace so it is often faster to walk if you are able. I occasionaly rode the shuttle if it rained or I just happened to catch them but found overall that it wasn’t worth the trouble. One of the most frustrating experiences was waiting over an hour for a shuttle but they always go the same route so they kept filling up before they got to us. After calling the hotel a couple times, they agreed to pay for a taxi to get us back. I viewed the shuttle like I viewed the hotel’s the slow and inconsistent internet: if it works it is a bonus. I would not recommend this hotel if the shuttle is a main attirbuite that you are looking for. There are also several rental car companies (Avis, Hertz, Enterprise, Dollar and Thrifty) a mile or less away. LOCATION As above, not too far from the medical center campus but you can get closer with other hotels. You can function here without a car as Kroger (grocery) is next door and a CVS and Target are less than a half mile walk away. There are plenty of restaurants within a 15 minute walk (Spicy Pickle, Long John Silvers, Chipotle, Panda Express, Which Wich, Schlotskys, Wing Stop, Papa Johns, Taco Cabana, and many more). Hope this helps. Happy to answer individual questions if you want to private message me.

“The London could teach The Pierre a thing or two- great stay” I just returned from a trip to NYC with my adult daughter. We split our stay between The Pierre and The London as I wanted a classic hotel stay for part of our visit and then a modern decor. The Pierre was stuffy, room was hot ( ac was not working correctly and engineering could not fix) and the price outrageous. Breakfast for 2 came in at over $100. Room was small and the bathroom was too small to turn around with no counter space.Shower door did not close completely so the floor flooded each time we showered. I could't wait to leave. The London- staff excellent, and our room was amazing; 2 seperate areas for sleeping and relaxing, huge bath with all the room you needed including counter space, etc. Room service excellent; on time to the minute and reasonable compared to The Pierre. The best part was they let us check out at 4 pm- no questions asked and no hesitiation. We had a 7 pm flight home so it was extremely helpful. I will stay at The London again . Perfect location for Times Sq theatre and Madison Ave shopping.

“Easy access to BWI, but rooms need renovations” Convenient location next to BWI with complimentary shuttle service. Front desk staff was friendly and accomodating, but guest rooms were old and in immediate need of renovations. Bed was very uncomfortable and room had feeling of not being as clean as it could be. I've definitely stayed in nicer Four Points!

“Dupont Circle Hotel” The Topaz Hotel was a nice hotel with unique decor which I liked but, in places it felt a little tired/rough around the edges, for example, the hallways. When we first arrived outside our room the door handle/lock mechanism was loose and wouldn't latch or lock properly. In fact, we didn't even have to use the room key to get in, the door just pushed open as I tried to insert the key card into the lock! We thought it was a little funny that the staff had not noticed this problem before we brought it to their attention. However, once it was brought to their attention it was looked at and fixed very promptly. We appreciated that, almost by the time I had put down the telephone receiver, the repairman was knocking on our room door. The room was a funny "L" shape so, in places it felt large, for example there was a spacious sitting area with sofa and easy chair and an office space with large desk and chair but, it was a little tight when walking between the foot of the bed and the cabinet that housed the TV and minibar. In fact, the door to the minibar wouldn't open the whole way which impeded the pulling out of the drawer which held the minibar snacks and the opening of the minibar fridge door. This was a very minor problem though and in general we were very satisfied with the room. A nice "freebee" included with your stay is the use of free wifi in your room. When you sign up for the free wifi, as a reward for signing up, you get a $10.00 "raid the minibar" coupon which I thought was a nice touch. The bed was a king and was extremely comfortable. The bathroom was a nice size and even included a vanity area. The location couldn't have been better. Situated very close to Dupont Circle but, tucked a short distance away on a quiet residential street. Very close to two metro stations: Dupont Circle and Farragut North. Overall, we were happy with the Topaz and enjoyed our stay there.

“New rooms are very small” We stayed here in the past and had a good stay. This time we were on the 5th floor in the north tower which I think is a new addition. The room was clean and modern but very small. There were two double beds and barely room for anything else. We're average size people buy in the bathroom we had to squeeze in order to close the door, and only then be able to stand and face the sink comfortably. Bathing the kids was nearly impossible. I wasn't too comfortable sleeping, although my family thought the beds were OK. One thing I can say for sure was that the blankets were very noisy... I know it sounds strange but I guess is the waterproof material or something in their detergent, we could hear every move and turn and it was quite annoying. The parking is pricey ($42/night). On the positive side - the service was good, the location is great, and the hotel overall is nice with good facilities.

“Needs renovation” Aging hotel on Century Blvd very convenient to airport and freeway. Service was friendly and the lobby was nice. A Starwood Gold upgraded room was spacious with a good view, but was too long without renovation. The climate control was only crudely adjustable (fan speed and warmer/cooler adjustment, no temp reading or setting). The bathroom was small with an old shower and no ventilation. I had to prop open the bathroom door to get rid of the steam after a shower. The bed was not firm. The casual restaurant had good service and wines by the glass, but the food was really mediocre. Overall not a good experience.

“Fantastic property but needs some updateing” I have always loved the Rancho Bernardo Inn. The staff goes out of it's way to be friendly, the rooms are spacious (some a little dated) and the food is generally creative and well prepared. What I found lacking on this trip was the fitness center- only 4 treadmills, one not working and TV's not working (or missing) on one bike and one eliptical. All of the exercise units are dated and only a few have working pulse monitors. Needs a refresh!

“Fantastic service” A group of friends and I stayed here one night as a base for a low-key "bachelorette" evening. While I was familiar with the hotel in general, having been to the restaurant on site (Poste), and am a big fan of Kimpton hotels, I was very impressed by our stay and, in particular, the service. Upon check-in, the ladies at the front desk asked about the occasion of our stay, and 30 minutes later, as we were getting settled in our room and changed for the evening, a knock on the door signalled the delivery of a bottle of champagne in celebration of the bride-to-be. They were also more than happy to share recommendations for places to go nearby. This was certainly going above and beyond our expectations. The room was very nice, typical "boutique"-y decor for Kimpton hotels, and double-paned windows so there was no problem with noise from the busy street below. The location is good for sight-seeing, being steps away from the National Portrait Gallery, Spy Museum, and tons of good restaurants (check out Zola, Zaytinya, Oya, Oyamel.. just to name a few). The street in front of the hotel is frequently closed for markets and art festivals, as it was the weekend we were there. I would not recommend this hotel for families - although I'm sure they would be treated fine, it doesn't appear that kid-friendly of a place.

“A friendly, trendy dorm” I liked the hotel, but I booked a medium room, with king bed. I'm a small person, but the room was very cramped, not that comfortable. There was no closet, and no drawers, so for one week, I had to take things in and out of suitcase. The cleaning staff was prompt, friendly, and did a good job. But the heat was either too hot or cold; seemed very budget. The bathroom had no heat, and was freezing. The shower head couldn't be adjusted, so the water would stream straight on your head. The elevators were frequently out of order, and when I arrived with two suitcases and no hands, there was no doorman to help with luggage, and I had to call them three tines to get someone to come out. The restaurants were very hip and trendy, and the hotel crowd was interesting. The staff was very friendly-the halls are very dark, and could be creepy. Aside from the non usefulness and size of the room, I enjoyed my stay, although it did feel like a hip dorm room-

“Swank” I stayed here for one night on business, I was surprised by the hotel. I have never stayed at a Renaissance property and this was a really nice hotel. Close to restaurants and a short walk to the US Airways Center for the Suns game. I would stay here again.

“Hipster vibe without the attitude” Had a short stay (2 nights) at the Ace Hotel in July 2012. It's an older hotel building in the NoMa (NOrth of MAdison Square Park) neighborhood that has been given a hipster makeover. Think dark lobby, skinny jeans, Buddy Holly glasses, direct-trade coffee, hoof-to-tail dining, iPhones... it's an Instagram photo in real life. At the same time, the young staff was friendly to me despite my non-hipster appearance. Rooms are part dorm room, part retro New York. My room had a SMEG refrigerator (well-stocked with assorted beverages; there was an assortment of other snacks in the room for purchase) and an old school Polaroid camera on the rough wood table. From the window I could see the Empire State Building. The robe is designed by Wings + Horns. Bath products are by Rudy's Barbershop. Free WiFi access, of course, as I imagine the hotel's regulars are part of the Wired generation. While the hotel is certainly suitable for the young and the hip, it's not unappealing for others. I saw some families with kids, some European travellers, and some older folks, as well. For those who are non-scenesters, it's a risk-free chance to delve into another lifestyle while in the big city.

“Great Stay, Great Location” We had a great stay at the Silver Cloud Hotel on Broadway at Madison. Having lived in the neighborhood before moving away, we didn't know what to expect from this hotel in a neighborhood underserved by hotels. We were very pleased with our stay. Our room, located on the top of six floors was of decent size with a king size bed. The wall-mounted flat screen TV was great. Although we didn't use it, the hotel has a pool and fitness center in the basement. Also included with the rate is a continental breakfast which we never saw as we had morning meetings during the entire stay.

“Great hotel! More than just a "quick" walk to historical sites” We stayed in Spa Suite 539... which includes a great big bathroom with a hot tub. PROS: Wine happy hour Knowledgeable concierge Lots of windows Hot tub SPACE - king bed as well as a couch, desk, and lounge chair. Nice Robes Downstairs breakfast and bar is fab. Nice Touch: umbrellas in every room - you never pack one and always need one! CONS Less-than-private sliding bathroom doors. It is not a “quick walk” to the historical sites. It is located closer to Dupont Circle, which has it’s own benefits, but if you are looking for a museum get-away, this is not the hotel for you.

“Standard airport hotel, but it did its job!” Not much to report here! It's a clean, well-run airport hotel. Not surprisingly, it's very convenient to the airport. Staff were friendly. Rooms were clean, if not huge. The hotel met all of my expectations for a Marriott. The staff were willing to accommodate my last minute request to change from a 1-king room to 2-queens, even though the I had booked the cheapest available on-line rate, which was the 1-king room. So that is definitely a positive.

“Good Value, nice quiet Location” Our first hotel in the U.S on what is to be a long trip. We found the hotel to be fantastic. We loved the location, as it was a tidy area, with lots of interesting things to watch from the balcony. We saw a movie being filmed across the road one morning. The valet service was good (but $35)and all the staff were impeccable. The location across the road from a shopping mall and supermarket was also handy for travelers with children who needed essentials. Overall, a great experience, and a perfect location near Santa Monica blvd if you have a rental car.

“A bit shoddy in the service dept.” My daughter and I stayed here recently. Center City is a great location with lots to do and see. The hotel check in was efficient and timely. We ordered breakfast in the room both days, and had missing food items both days. On our first morning, I discovered that we had not been left any shampoo; just mouthwash and body lotion. After pouring mouthwash on my head (I don't see well) I found this out. We used the coffeemaker in the room, and when the room was made up, none of the coffee supplies were replaced. The service express people quickly arrived with coffee, but we had to request a second visit with half and half. The beds are the air type, where one dials a number and the bed becomes as firm or as soft as one wishes. The only problem is that it is necessary to wait 5 min. before getting into bed each time an adjustment is made. The employees at the lounge/breakfast area were very attentive and accurate with our orders. The maid staff was sloppy and annoyingly forgetful. I probably would not stay here again.

“Lovely people but needs renovation” We've stayed at this hotel about 4-5 years ago and liked it, though the room was small. We've stayed (since then) at the nearby Willard Intercontinental and Hay-Adams and liked them a lot, too.This time, however, we had our 9-year old with us and - thinking this would be the most family-friendly of the three hotels - we booked a suite. We were extremely disappointed with the facilities, though the people were terrific - especially Cecila on the desk. The management sent up a complimentary dessert tray that was superb. Also, a gorgeous orchid plant was in the room. However, the rooms have grown old and a bit shabby. Ours faced walls ("inner court"), so it was dark on sunny days. We probably wouldn't book this hotel again.

“Great and Interesting Hotel” Stayed here in mid-April, and found most of the negative reviews here to be without merit. Had a very pleasant stayy. The hotel is what you would expect from a Westin. Good and prompt service. Well-appointed rooms and bathrooms. Staff were quite pleasant and helpful without being obtrusive. I agree that the cost of parking is steep ($25) but it's in line with other garages in the area. Contrary to some refviews, the buffet breakfast is $17 -- not $25 -- again not cheap, but in line with what you would find in most any similar hotel. The only legitimate complaint is the hideously overpriced restaurant (LA Prime) so have a drink in the bar -- for the view -- and then dine elsewhere.

“Very good value for what we paid!” This is definitely not a four-star hotel. HOWEVER, it was a very good deal for the price we paid---$101 for a double. The building is old and historic (in the National Register), and it has a little bit of a shabby chic feel, but our room was HUGE and had been recently redone. The bedding was very comfortable. The bathroom was the least impressive feature---clean but not updated or particularly modern. The toilet was hard to flush, but this was just a problem with the handle itself, not with the plumbing. The breakfast buffet in the hotel's "grill" was also an excellent value. I'd stay here again for the same price but would not pay much more. Very good harbor and convention center location.

“Actually Not So Bad Except for Parking Cost” Got a <$100 deal for a night here via one of the bidding-type sites and was pleasantly surprised. A few reviewers have mentioned confusion or disappointment regarding the hotel's two buildings (and being surprised on check-in that they're in the "other building across the street" which admittedly sounds bad) but the skybridge between the two buildings makes it not a big deal, seriously. More importantly, this other building houses both the pool and the gym, and the latter, although located around a corner and down a long hallway, is one of the best free hotel gyms I've had the pleasure of using, with a huge range of equipment and weights. The room appeared to be recently updated with a cozy and modern dark gray/black color scheme with a few red accents. Comfy bed, big TV, electrical outlets on lamp bases, responsive thermostat. One significant drawback is parking. Other reviews complained about the $24 cost for garage parking, so I thought maybe I could outwit them and find street or cheaper nearby lot parking. It's not possible. Nearby lots have midnight expirations so you can't park overnight, and most nearby streets have overnight and early morning restrictions. After looking around for 15 minutes i gave up and drove into the $24 garage. It's a little silly to think of my $100 room having a 25% parking surcharge, but if I just think of it as a $125 room, nicely appointed and with excellent amenities in downtown Denver, then it actually seems pretty good.

“Customer Service is #1 at Hotel Indigo” My husband and I have just returned from a four day stay in the Hotel Indigo and I cannot say enough good things about the exceptional service we received during our stay. We booked on Hotwire and got a fantastic deal. Before heading off on our trip, I contacted the hotel directly and asked for a non-smoking room with a king sized bed. My request was responded to by Angie, and honoured immediately - this was a great start to our vacation. When we arrived at the hotel we were greeted with a warm smile and very attentive service by Lisa. If you are looking for something a little different than the large, impersonal hotel experience - then you cannot overlook this gem. Our room was a good size, very clean and bright. The king-sized bed was very comfortable. The bathroom had Aveda products - a nice surprise! We had a sitting area with current magazines, two chairs, t.v., and desk. I was pleased to find both an ironing board and coffee maker in the room - as some boutique hotels do not offer these. If like me, you like to be treated like a valued customer, then this is the hotel for you. Everyone, housekeeping, reception, concierge and security were friendly, personable and made you feel welcome. On our way home I discovered my husband (men eh!!), had left our GPS in the night table. I called the hotel and was immediately transferred to Anna who assured me the GPS was safe with her and they would return it to me via mail. This is service I have simply never experienced before!!! I highly recommend this hotel to you if you are looking for something a little different that will not cost an arm and a leg, yet with all you could wish for - that perfect get-away.

“Friendly staff but a little too much info . . .” This is a lovely Hilton in a great location - great for business or a trip to the Galleria. I ran into a couple of problems at check-in, including the computer system being down so that I couldn't check in. While the front desk manager kindly bought me a drink in the bar while we waited for the system to re-boot, it was 11 pm and time for bed, not waiting for a room. The staff shared a little too much information about the frequency of this problem and a couple of other things related to their relationships with surrounding hotels that their General Manager probably would not have wanted me to hear, but they were also friendly and demonstrated sincere caring about their work. The room was a very nice business room - good linens and mattress quality, flat screen TV, and complimentary bottled water which I appreciated. There were plenty of outlets in all of the lamps for charging gizmos, but nothing compares to a Marriott in Dallas I stayed in last spring that had a console with lots of outlets consolidated. Bathroom had plenty of counter space separated from the toilet and shower. I was delighted to see energy efficient lighting throughout the room! Overall a very nice hotel for business.

“Not a problem to be had...” Got a great deal for a 500 square ft room on the 22nd floor for $95 through Orbitz. Would go back there is a second. They had a perfect location and great staff. ASked the concierge about a good sushi restaurant. He gave us directions and the name of his sister who worked there, who would take care of us. Room was perfect to relax and sleep. I woke up at 930 saturday morning thinking it was still the middle of the night it was so dark and quiet in there. We were out on the town most of the time so we didnt eat at our hotel, but friends told us they were very good. Dont let negative reviews steer you away from here. They are 1 in a 100. Get a good rate, go to the Hyatt to sleep, but go enjoy Chicago instead of complaining about taxis and noise.

“Good stay in ideal location” Great location, two blocks from 16th Street with walking mall and free rail service. We were able to visit the Denver Art Museum, park and 9/11 ceremony with the Beach Boys on one end of 16th, and bookstore and contemporary museum on the other end without needing our car. The hotel has retro decor, short-wait elevators, a parking garage. Our room on the 16th floor was large with desk, easy chair with foot rest, and plenty of space to walk around. It was very comfortable. We went to our free Sunday buffet breakfast with our tickets as Hilton Honors members and entered the restaurant from the hotel. We didn't see a hostess and walked the length of the long, narrow restaurant. The hostess stand was at the other end, near the street door, and next to the buffet. When we showed her our tickets, she took us back the length of the restaurant and seated us next to the hotel entry. Thus, after we were served coffee and juice, we walked back the length of the room to the buffet, and back the length of the restaurant to our table. Apparently, hotel guests, or at least Hilton Honors' guests, are not as valued as customers who come in off the street. The waitress who got our drinks did an excellent job of being attentive and kept track of our needs, both Sunday and Monday. Wish I knew her name, but she was the only waitress with a ponytail almost down to her waist. Thank you. The hotel is across from the performing arts and convention center. Some may not care for the themed floors, but the hotel had numerous guests in their 20s and 30s who seem to like it, and the location, as well as the hotel itself, is a good bet in downtown Denver.

“Much better than expected” The reviews led me to believe that this was a poor excuse for a Hilton. I strongly disagree. Located a nice walk from Fisherman's Wharf this is a 3 star hotel. After a very easy check-in I spent 4 nights in room 274 and really enjoyed it. The carpet was clean but not new. The bathroom was a decent size and equipped with a very nice grade of toiletries. Avoid rooms above the pool to avoid noise. I opened the windows (they only open about 5 inches) to enjoy fresh air.

“Nice Stay...and Nice Matin” Our family of 4 (two adults and kids ages 12 and 16) stayed in a suite that had 2 queen beds and a very small living area with a loveseat, desk, and refrigerator...although big enough even if you were there on business and wanted work space. (I could not figure out how to open the twin mattress contained in the loveseat, but it didn't matter.) The bedroom was generously sized for a NYC hotel. Bathroom was also small, but again, that's to be expected. The room was nicely appointed and very clean, as were the common areas. The overall look was upscale but not flashily so. We found it to be a very convenient location, with the subway only a very short walk (a minute, maybe less) away. It's in a pleasant business district, with shops of all sorts nearby in case you forgot to pack anything. It was also quiet, which can be a rarity in NYC. The only possible downside I can see is that the beds are VERY firm, although for me that's a positive. If you like a soft mattress, though, this is probably not your place. Plus, the hotel restaurant, Nice Matin, is fabulous! We had a reservation, but were at least 15 minutes late because our plane was delayed. It wasn't a problem, though; the friend we were meeting there had already arrived and was enjoying a glass of wine at our table, which was held for us. The menu is interesting with many unusual choices, and the execution on everything was superb. Service was just what you want...understated but attentive. For those who are less adventurous (like our 12-year-old), the burger and fries were also out of this world. All in all, a very pleasant experience, and I would gladly return.

“A great location and I would stay again” A perfect location for the City with friendly reception staf who were helpful. The restaurant for breakfast was a little chaotic some mornings and we were overlooked on two occasions. The room was well appointed and comfortable. Plenty of parking further down the street for overnight at sensible prices. We stayed a couple days on for some leisure trips.

“Excellent experience in every way possible. Would highly recommend this property over any other hotel.” I am a platinum Starwood member so I have stayed at plenty of W hotels across the country. The W Boston is no exception to the excellence this brand stands for. I was given a free upgrading to a lovely and spacious room. Everything from the front desk to room service was perfect. I can go on and on about all the details that other hotels wish they could claim. This is one of the finest W's that I stayed at, plus make sure to sign up for the Spg loyalty program. Stay at this hotel and see why the W experience is like no other. Afterwards, please write your review.

“Excellent Location” I have stayed at this hotel numerous times. I like it because the hotel is clean, the Lobby is very attractive and the location is excellent. Just steps away from the rivercenter mall and the riverwalk. Additionally the staff was friendly from the time we arrived until checkout. Would definitely stay here again!

“So comfy....” This hotel might not be located right smack in the midddle of the tourist area's but I have to say my stay was wonderful. The bed is super comfy and the size of the room is just big enough even for 4 of us. We were celebrating some birthday's at the new restaurant complex and the walk is probably not even 5 minutes. The staff checking in was great and so friendly. I never have my starwood number and I like the fact that they remind me and look it up. After dinner and drinks we came back and hung at the City Bar. Again, the staff was great and the drinks kept coming. I'm also addicted to Starbucks and it's pretty cool that you have one right down stairs. Great night sleep and I would stay again for sure.

“Cool, Quirky Boutique” After falling for the Kimpton brand last year, we chose the Rouge for our first trip to Washington DC. It's a great little hotel with a funky, red retro feel and is located in a nice neighbourhood. Loved the sparkly, red floor in the lobby! And the canine guests we bumped into during our stay. Also, Kristin and Scott on the front desk were very friendly and helpful. Couldn't fault anything. Tip: Try a meal at Firefly, about a 10 minute walk away. Quality food with a contemporary twist, including awesome burgers and truffle parmesan fries.

“Excellent Stay” This is a really nice hotel. Is it the 19th best hotel in Seattle? I’m not sure as this was our first visit to Seattle. We had two rooms, one was booked through Marriott rewards points, and one was secured at an AARP rate. Our reward’s room was arranged in a typical Residence Inn layout (i.e. one bedroom with King Bed, and one living room with sofa bed. There was the usual kitchen area with a small eating table. The room was spotless, and the bed very comfortable. The second room had a lovely lake view and was one of the nicest rooms we have seen in any hotel. One huge room with beautiful furnishings, king bed, wood floors, love seat and chairs, with an open kitchen, and balcony. Truly a 1st class experience. Every staff member were very helpful, and the breakfast was a step up from the usual full Residence Inn breakfasts. Food was refreshed often, and nothing ran out, be it drinks, pastries, hot items, coffee or juices. Breakfast can be eating on a number of tables located in the open atrium, or in a more private area with free newspapers available. The hotel is located across the street from a number of good restaurants. We would recommend Duke’s Chowder House. Tip: Order off the daily specials menu for lunch and enjoy some “just caught seafood”. On our visit it was Halibut fish and chips. All in all we highly recommend this hotel, it is a 15 minute walk to the space needle, but a taxi is probably the easiest way to reach the Pike Place Market.

“Nice Service & Better than describe” This is a nice hotel. Staff was excellent and made sure I was taken care. Breakfast would satisfy growups and kids. I just never could get my waffle correct. Nothing bad to say. I just wish they would offer transportation to MD Anderson even if they offered it with a charge. Still would stay again.

“Great Location, good service” After reading some of the reviews here, I was prepared for a so-so stay at the JW. I'm glad to report that I had an above-average stay. I was in town for business only for 3 days, taking a red eye back to the East Coast on my final day. When I arrived, the taxi let me off on the street instead of pulling into the main area. This caused trouble for me because I was in a walking boot for my foot. However, the bellman saw me getting out and was quick to offer his help with my luggage. He greeted me warmly and told me where to check in. He would meet me upstairs with my luggage (he took a separate elevator than the glass enclosed ones). Check in was somewhat slow. It was near noon and there was only one person on staff. The person was doing his best to be efficient yet friendly. I asked for a room near the elevator (which I had requested when I originally booked the room) and he assured me that my room was close. I was on the 7th floor. As previous reviewers noted, all the rooms open up to the atrium. However, in the three days I stayed there, I did not have an issue with the noise from the bar and restaurant below. My room was a nice size for a downtown San Francisco hotel. It was clean and smelled fresh. One reviewer commented about the pay-for-bath amenities, but this wasn't the case in my room. The concierge lounge was nice and the food was above par for a lounge. The staff was efficient. I ate at the bar several times and had excellent service. Yes, things were priced high but the food was good and the was a nice variety. The location of the hotel, as others have mentioned, is excellent. I only wish I was more able-bodied to enjoy it! I'd definitely stay here again.

“Highly recommended for a superior class hotel at reasonable rates” Tastefully furnished, although, the carpet is abit loud and busy on the eye! Despite that Courtyard Seattle is an impressive hotel well located in Pioneer Square and close enough to downtown attractions. Good value for money and above par compared to other Seattle hotels we've stayed at. Only stayed a couple of nights, wanted to stay longer, but, hotel was fully booked. During our stay, there were major street repairs and construction so abit noisy in our room during the day. But can't fault the hotel for that.
“loved it” i have stayed at several different hotels in NYC but i would have to say this is my favorite. Close to everything,the staff was amazing. i would ask for a room away from the street.

“Woodland Hills” Gutes Hotel, ziemlich ruhig, kostenloses und reichhaltiges Frühstück, Parken kostenlos, Los Angeles Attraktionen ausserhalb Rush Hour relativ schnell zu erreichen. Alternativ über Topanga Canyon/Malibu, Internet Wifi kostenlos, Supermarkt und einige Restaurants über die Straße, Denny's direkt nebenan, Zimmer sauber, Poolarea ebenfalls

“Beautiful Lobby, lots of history, better options for the price” We were in town for a friends wedding. We frequently travel to Austin, usually staying at the Hilton, Hilton Garden Inn, Courtyard, or Residence Inn. Since the wedding was being held at the Driskill we decided it would be neat to stay here. While the hotel is beautiful, the service and offerings do not live up to the high prices for the hotel. You can not live on the history of your hotel alone. To be honest, the best part of the hotel is the lobby. Nothing was particularly bad, but nothing was particularly outstanding either. For the price of the Driskill compared to the other hotels nearby, I expect outstanding. The location was easy to find and the hotel smack in the middle of the 6th street entertainment and a very easy walk (5 minutes) to the convention center and warehouse district as well. You only have the choice of valet and pay a premium for that. The lobby of this historic hotel is beautiful with with front desk and nicely appointed common area. There is no free Wi-Fi available in the lobby or rooms. It seems like most hotels in the 4-5 star category are at least offering complimentary access in the lobby. There is a bakery and café in the lobby. We tried to eat here twice, but the wait was in excess of an hour and there are many other good options in the area. They really should give priority to hotel guests! We never took the time to check out their gym, and I am unsure if they have a pool. Check in was quick and efficient, thought they made no attempt to accommodated our request for a quiet room, but quiet may not really be possible where they are located. When we asked for foam pillows and extra towels they brought them promptly. Though we were there for the wedding and the nightlife of Austin, once you went inside the hotel at night you do experience a respite from crazy 6th. The rooms are nicely decorated, but as expected in a historic hotel they are somewhat small. The bathrooms are relatively big for a historic hotel, with a sink both inside and outside the bath area. We had no noise from adjoining rooms but experienced a lot of outside city noise. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space. There is a tub with shower We could hear doors slamming in the morning from time to time. Many small items in the room were tattered or dirty and could use a refresh. The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We did not partake of any of the hotels dining venues other than trying to eat breakfast there.....other than the banquet food at the wedding. (though the food was good, some of it was cold) We would not likely stay here again if we were in the area for a personal trip. Room rate seemed too appropriate for what you get. The Intercontinental (which we3 also have stayed at) is just as nice and less expensive. They were agreeable to late check-out when we asked which was nice. I love historic hotels, but unfortunately in this case, the price - payoff is not there. But, more power to them if they can continue to get those rates without providing anything stellar. That seems to work for them.

“It's not a Westin. It's a Holiday Inn.” Many Westin amenities are missing: no bath soap, plastic cups and Styrofoam mugs instead of glass, no “heavenly bath” towels or robes, no newspaper delivery and no easy check out. The rooms are severely run down: when my a/c fan ran, it sounded like the wind was blowing; veneers on the furniture were peeling or chipped and the TV could not be turned to face the bed. The management simply doesn’t care: it took them 1.5 hours to find me a room that didn’t have either significant burns in the carpet or construction noise, and 2 hours and several phone calls to deliver a robe. Keep in mind that this was the *third* room I’d been given, and I’m a SPG Gold member. From what I can tell, you’d be better off staying at the Biltmore, Hilton, Standard or Marriot. All hotels I could see from my window.

“Beautiful lobby; not much sleep” We booked this hotel at the last minute solely based on its proximity to family. We had zero expectations, which was good, because our stay was only so-so. As others have noted, the lobby, bar and Pump Room have all been beautifully re-done. The sitting area near the coffee bar is great. But at night, because this is basically all one big open space, the bar ends up taking over the place and people crowd the whole area. Not a big deal, but it did make coming and going a bit annoying as you're pushing your way through people just to get to the elevator bank. (I'd also say that though we saw some families with young kids, it definitely does not have a family-friendly vibe.) Our room was very spacious, but the design doesn't make very good use of the space. There is one tiny closet and 2 drawers for all of your clothes—no dresser. Also, the bed, which is very hard, is basically on the floor. We were on the 13th floor (yes, the first place I've ever stayed where they actually have a 13th floor!) which gave us a nice view and we appreciated the black out curtains to block the sun in the morning. Bathroom was fairly small, but nicely done. The real problem is the noise: the doors and walls are basically paper thin. We heard people at all hours—talking in the hallways, talking as they came off the elevator, talking (and more than that) coming from the room next door. We had to be up early pretty much every morning we were there and felt exhausted by the time we left. On the plus side: The Public has one of the nicest hotel gyms I've ever seen. Brand new equipment, nice view, very light, the room the right temperature. We also enjoyed a breakfast at the Pump Room and loved the convenience of being able to grab a quick to-go breakfast from the coffee bar. All in all, though the location is ideal for us, I probably won't stay here again. I value my sleep too much!

“Great Location and room” Just returned from a quick one night stay at the Belvedere and was quite impressed. We booked directly through their website and received an unbelievable rate of $159/night (taxes etc included) for an executive double (2 doubles) so right of the bat I was happy! The location couldn't be better - within easy walking distance to Broadway shows and Times Square and a couple of blocks from the subway. Lots of choices to eat nearby (we chose Lillies for dinner on 49th between 8th/Broadway - excellent food/atmosphere/price!). Our room was on the 9th floor facing 48th St. and on the larger size for an NYC room. It was clean, well decorated and beds were comfy. A/C was nice and cold. TV worked but channels limited (but who goes to NYC to watch TV?). There was a microwave, fridge and coffee maker, hair dryer, safe, and iron. You can hear trucks/cars but that doesn't bother me... Everyone at the hotel was friendly and helpful from the check in desk, to the valet, housekeeper and doorman. Lobby was nice and had lots of couches to sit. Two minor things: 1) The elevators were very small and extremely slow, even though there were 4 of them (one on each side of the floor and 2 in the middle). 2) There was a big house centipede (with the long legs) in the bathtub -- yuck! Overall a great stay. Would definitely stay again if we could stay for a similar price!

“I Love To Stay Here When in NYC” When in NYC, this is the place to stay. It is a quirkly boutique hotel that has excellent service, spacious rooms and good location for exploring the city. We've always stayed on the top floor and the room are comfortable, funky and very roomy (especially for NYC). The beds are extraordinary and the work station is more than adequate for the traveling business person. The staff is accomodating and kind are always willing to recommend the non touristy places to eat and to do. This hotel is a hidden gem.

“A Kimpton in Name Only” First off, we love Kimpton hotels. We absolutely adore them. We have given the Allegro two chances now to win our business and both visits have been less than stellar. Looking at our most recent stay, we chose their largest room, a King Suite with 2 person Jacuzzi. I had asked the concierge if they could assist with some champagne and chocolates in the room when we arrived and was assured it would be taken care of. I even offered to pay for them and Anthony assured me it was on the house. We arrived a little after 5 in the evening and proceeded to wait about 20 minutes to check in. It was a Friday evening and the hotel was quite busy, but they only had 1 individual working the check-in desk. We finally got checked in and went upstairs to the room. We walked in and though the room was nice, it was quite worn. The tabletops were full of scratches and water marks and the carpet had some stains. It was overall very clean though. One thing missing though, was the chocolates and champagne. I was assured they would be in the room for the surprise. Well I went downstairs and the concierge was nowhere to be found. I went to the front desk and waited through the line again and explained. She looked it up and said, "oh yes I see that amenity was added, I'm sorry they must be on their way, wait a bit and they should show up." I went back upstairs and we got changed for going out and still no amenity. I tried calling the concierge and finally got through. He apologized and said he would send them up right away. When they arrived we received 4 bon bons ina plastic container and a bottle of brut. OK, I get it, it was a free amenity, but I would have paid for something a little more extravagant, and if it would have been on time. Our next problem was they gave us an adjoining suite with the baseball weekend revelers from you-know-where. They were so loud and obnoxious we could hear every word of their vulgar conversations. Ultimately I decided to go say something at the front desk. They said they would send security up and that they had no other rooms, I would have to just wait and see if security could quiet them. We went out to dinner and came back to you guessed it, party central next door. I called the front desk again, and they said they woudl send a friendly reminder up to them. They quieted down for about 20 minutes then back at it again. Luckily our sleeping quarters were on the other side of the suite. The next morning we could hear every word of the housekeepers' inappropriate conversation next door. Think slurs and sexual innuendo... The next day the front desk manager sent a cheese and wine amenity up to make up for the hassle but again, I would have rather had a quiet night than cheese and bubbly. Alltogether, it would be ok for a business stay or quick overnight but I think we are done attempting the Allegro Chicago experience. We will take our business to Palomar or Monaco, or on further up to the Gold Coast hotels.

“Great location + free internet + low prices = good value.” Lets see the pros safe location just 1 block from hollywood blvd. 2 hbo channels- was able to watch a boxing match free high speed internet- was able to watch Big 12 championships since i was watching boxing on hbo. Hook 'em horns! Room was clean, bed was fairly comfortable. cons no shampoo, so make sure you bring a small bottle from a hotel that did provice you shampoo. hopefully nothings goes badly, as the front desk guys are basically just there to get paid and as they are likely making minimum wage, expect the minimum from them.

“Buena ubicación relativa” Ciertamente si uno anda en automóvil no hay problema para movilizarse. No obstante no tiene muchas opciones de restaurante cerca, y el riverwalk queda a más de 1 km caminando. Las opciones de parqueo por el Riverwalk son difíciles así que son poco recomendables. El transporte público esta en la esquina muy cerca y eso lo conecta con todo. Se puede tomar la línea amarilla que lo conecta con la línea roja y azul y así conoce todo San Antonio por menos de 2$. Nosotros llegamos para competir en la maratón de San Antonio, y por la hora y el lugar de inicio por el Riverwalk, se complicó un poco el arrivo al lugar. El hotel está bien. El personal es muy especial y es lo mejor que hay.

“Great Stay but under Renovation.” The room I had was fully renovated, new everything. Modern black cabinets in bath and kitchen with glass fronts, very modern looking. Full size kitchen which is always a plus for the long stay, not eating off styrofoam every night. there are 2 main complaints for this hotel...#1 being no business center. The front desk staff will do all printing,faxing,etc.,whatever you need, but sometimes you just need a keyboard to do work. They will turn their board around so you can use it, but when they are busy this becomes an issue. No one ever complained or looked like it was an inconvenience, but you know it is. #2-the air conditioning. The maint. dept. put in 3 seperate units, but none would actually chill the room. Thank goodness it was very cold outand the windows did open allowing me to control the air! There is the standard "convenience store" cuboard which is great for soda,snacks,etc., on the honor system,along with endless coffee since there is no breakfast offered. When reno is complete I feel this place will have a little more of the upscale "luxury" feel they are hoping for in an extended stay facility. I would have no problem stayin here again when in the area. Note-if you are using GPS, it will be hard to find the first time, as driveway into facllity is one block away from address, through a giant graveyard. A great little find as soon as the air works! Weekly maid service, so keep your room clean and it will be like a second home!!!

“great place to stay, with some nice extras” Kimpton's only LA hotel is situated in upscale Westwood, a few blocks from the UCLA campus and a short distance off the 405 freeway (about 30 min from LAX if no traffic).
