The property is in good shape, very clean and somewhat more modern and larger than other Kimpton hotels I've stayed in. Check-in was efficient and I was in my room on the 16th floor only a few minutes after pulling up out front. Valet is the only parking option here ($30/day) but the valet staff are on the ball and very helpful. Rooms are nice sized; I had a great view looking northwest over Wilshire blvd with only minimal traffic noise. The bathroom is larger than average, spacious really, and well lit. My only complaint is that the shower had a handheld spray head that wouldn't stay in place on its vertical bar and was placed too low for anyone over, say, 5'5" in height. Amenities included a flat screen digital tv, minibar, ipod docking clock radio, and a large safe. The closet includes a full size umbrella for guest use, and the infamous leopard-skin pattern robes. There are no coffee makers in the room, but complimentary coffee is available in the lobby each morning (though you do have to get dressed to go down and get some...maybe wearing one of those robes). Wireless internet access was fast and reliable. For loyalty program members, internet is free, and you also get a $10 coupon per stay to "raid the minibar" -- a nice touch and appreciated, though of course $10 won't get you much! An evening wine reception is also offered for all guests. I had breakfast at the in-house restaurant , which was very good but expensive, even for the setting. Service was prompt at first but refills on coffee lagged. I didn't visit the bar/lounge but it looked like a fun place to hang out. There is a small pool out back; it's very private but in shade much of the day. Probably perfect for those hot days but too cool for the moderate temps on my trip. Finally, they do have a useful service I've not seen before, which is to have your airline boarding pass printed out and delivered to your room with breakfast in the morning if you order it the night before, or you can pick it up at the front desk when you check out. While most smaller hotels will do this if you ask the concierge, it was nice to see it offered directly through in-room materials.

“Get A Good Rate And You'll Be Happy” $200/night average on Expedia. Institutional-style hotel: very big - many rooms, several elevators - all older (permanent-style signs posted "pardon our elevator upgrade" though no upgrading was apparently going on), odd-shaped rooms (was this an office building? my room (805) was about 10 feet wide and 30 feet long), etc. In need of updgrade, but centrally located to the Park/midtown/subway. Though on 8th floor, could hear some street noise and jackhammering: get an upper floor (23 floors). Also, get a good rate and you should be satisfied.

“A bit disappointed” I was a little disappointed by the stay. When I checked in the girl did not seem very knowledgable. I had a question and she told me I had to call the rewards line. Fortunately someone then stepped in and was very helpful and knowledgable. Hotel has no shuttle unless going to the hospital. It does seem like an older property based on the old loud air conditioners in the room. The carpet in my room was also pretty nasty with many stains. TV could use an update too. I did get a very good rate so no complaints there. I had stayed in a Courtyard in Bossier City the nights prior and this property just did not show as well.

“Nice stay - nice hotel.” I recently stayed for two nights at the Westin and had a very nice visit. The updated rooms were very nice after a day at Cobo. The hotel has all the amenities you need for a nice stay. The location is great if you are attending an event at Cobo, or anything else downtown Detroit.

“Outstanidng service, elegant decor” I stayed here for a short business trip. I selected this location because of reputation (stellar), proximity to Metro (station at end of block), and price (good deal for this historic property). The staff provided outstanding service, as one might expect. After a long flight and metro ride from Reagan National, I was greeted and checked-in within 5 minutes. There is free printing of boarding passes in the business center in the lobby. The fitness center is huge; there are ~10 treadmills so no waiting even at peak times, exercise bikes, weights, complimentary earbuds in case one forgets to pack those, etc. My room was a corner room with a great view, and it was very clean. Bathroom space is tight, but I expected as much in a historic property. Overall, excellent accommodations in DC!

“Stylish with all the touches you'd want while travelling” I decided to go "off the grid" and book outside of the conference hotel for a conference at McCormick and booked a room at the Palomar based on tripadvisor. I was not disappointed. This is a very stylish hotel - rooms are very tastefully decorated, large, with all the amenities you'd want (comfortable desk / chair, nice lounge chair, iPod docking station, large flat screen), comfortable bed. It is simply a pleasure staying here - you are not nickeled and dimed. If you are a Kimpton InTouch member you have free fast internet. The gym is stunning - large, high floor overlooking the city, great equipment. Food in the hotel restaurant, Sable, is very good. Nice free coffee and sweets in lobby. Location is a bit off beat and path, but actually is close to Miracle Mile and I grew to like the neighborhood

“Pretty good hotel” This is a pretty good hotel. It's good value given its location and features. However, "good value" means that you get a lot for your money, it doesn't mean that you get the Four Seaons at Motel Six prices. I stayed on the 13th floor and I don't know if this was a pre-renovation room but it could certainly use some updating. The furniture looked a bit old and worn, and the decor was okay, but not what I would consider a 'boutique' hotel. Having said that, everything else was above average. The bed was great, the windows provide very good sound insulation, and the bathroom was just fine. As to noise, yes, you can hear the street and you can hear your neighbors if they cough loudly. If you're sensitive to noise (I am) I recommend bringing ear plugs (I did), which will easily blank out the noise. I didn't try the restaurant or bar, so I can't comment on those. I was very impressed with the staff, who were unfailingly friendly, helpful, and efficient. They're probably this hotel's greatest asset. The location is also very good, close to lots of shopping and Chinatown, right on the cable car route, and a 5-10 minute walk to the Powell subway station. I would recommend this hotel if you want a good base to explore San Francisco from without paying too much, but don't expect luxury.

“Less black turtle neck, more do your fing job” At that price, you'd like to not be treated like the dirt. I understand the trendy cooler than human W attitude but unless my bed is made, my bathroom clean, the door opened, my bags carried and the towels not frayed, stfu.

“Nice upscale option on the Riverwalk” Most hotels in downtown San Antonio are of the predictable chain variety. You get what each chain typically provides (though at higher prices than usual because of area demand). There are also several local hotels that offer you historical eloquence at a price that is comparable to the high-end chains. But then there is Mokara. Also pricey but so much more contemporary and comfortably up-scale than anything we have encountered before in the downtown area. At last, San Antonio has gotten its first 21st century hotel and we look forward to staying at it again for another in-town getaway. It is ideally situated on the riverwalk, just south of the main channel, and a short walk from the noisier and more congested parts of the river area. Access to the riverwalk is provided by way of a nice bar and restaurant in the hotel itself. The décor in the hallways and bedrooms is tastefully done and has a nice, airy feel about it. The bed and furnishings are stylish and comfortable, and the bathrooms are amazingly large and accommodating. But there were a few blemishes. The size of our one-king bedroom was adequate for two people but less spacious than we might have liked. And our window looked out onto the brick wall of adjoining building – so now we know to ask for a room that looks out over the river. All in all, one of the better hotel experiences we have had and hard to believe it happened in our own backward. Highly recommended as long as price is not an issue.

“Suit up for breakfast battle” This hotel has a great location in Chinatown and is near Metro and numerous attractions. Limos were disgorging teased-hair Brittney Spears fans at the Verizon Center when we stayed here. The are plenty of good restaurant choices nearby and I'd suggest Kanlaya Thai across the street. The hotel was busy but served its purpose. I probably won't be back. The free breakfast in the morning was a full contact sport and, frankly, we weren't up to taking out somebody to grab the last muffin or bagel. For a low price this hotel is a good deal.

“Can't beat the location” The Courtyard is located right downtown in a great location. The hotel and rooms were very clean and modern with friendly staff and valet. They have a business center with a few computers and free wi-fi which was very convenient. Sam's #3 right next door is a great place for breakfast and there are several breweries, restaurants, and shops close by to enjoy as well.

“very nice hotel” nice people at front desk, room was good, nice trails nearby for walking/running. A little bit of highway noise, so choose your room carefully. nice outdoor grilling area that was getting a lot of use

“Hotel Solamar is Not to Be Missed” This hotel is beautiful and to be experienced. It is one of the very creative Kimpton hotels -- the difference here (as explained by the staff) is that this hotel was built from the ground up instead of being a rehab in cool old buildings like most Kimptons. The result is a super-cool pool on the fourth floor that has a cocktail lounge that goes late -- it was crowded every night and fun to watch from my hotel room or to join. Outside firepits by the pool really give a great ambience for cocktails with friends. The rooms are very funky, functional, and fun. It is located near a lot of activities downtown. The staff are friendly and helpful. Kimptons are boutique hotels and a nice break from big chains when you want high class and comfort in a smaller setting. The two criticisms of the Solamar are (1) it seems inconsistent that they would charge for web access -- a hotel of this class should provide it free, and (2) their frequent stayer program is VAGUE -- they simply notice how often you stay and then award you with awards. I much prefer getting points and seeing them add up, such as a Hilton or Marriott program.

“Really nice hotel” Just a short overnighter at The London NYC this time but have stayed here last year for 3 nights. Traveling with young kids (10 & 12), the location can't be beat. The central location to all the major museums, attractions, 5th Avenue shopping and Times Square is super convenient. The hotel's small boutique hotel vibe and room decor is young and hip which my kids preferred over the older and grander NY hotels like The Plaza Hotel which we've stayed in the past and cost twice as much. They especially liked the huge bathroom shower! Thanks to the American Express fine hotels program, we booked the London suite which included early check-in/late check out, continental breakfast and one afternoon tea. I would've given the hotel an excellent rating but both times we've stayed there, the staff seemed too preoccupied talking to each other rather than helping guests. They looked great but they're not very helpful.

“Loved it!” We stayed here for three nights at the end of October 2007. Although the ladies Nike marathon was being held the same weekend we arrived, the staff on check-in still found the time to find us the best upgraded room as we were Hilton Hhonors members. On check-in they gave us free continental breakfast for all four of us, which we didnt realise was so good until we arrived the first morning to have breakfast and was met with an amazing 360 degree view of the whole of San Francisco - this was worth it in itself even though the food was good also. Although we didnt have a great view from our room, this was more than made up with the view we had at breakfast and the rooms themselves. The rooms were very nice with lots of little extras and finishing touches, plus plenty of free Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries. Location was great with a short 5 minute walk to get to the centre of Union Square, and a taxi to Fishermans Wharf was only about $10 and 10 minute drive. Would definately recommend this hotel!

“Great Location - Has a fly problem in Room 204” We stayed in this hotel November 15 - 18th. You cannot beat the location and the price for Manhattan. I was traveling with my incredibly spry 83 year old mother. When we checked in - the only room available was the handicapped accessable room - which is just fine with us - and especially in Manhattan where this usually results in a larger room. (Room #204). We checked in the and bathroom had flies. Many flies. My mom felt certain these came up through the sewer drain in the unusual shower set up for a wheelchair. She was probably right. We reported this and asked for the room to be sprayed while we were out to dinner. Still had flies. Next day - reported the fly problem - received a lovely apology and breakfast coupons and a promise to spray - still had flies. Next day - flies. Reported again. Checked out with flies. Simple bleach in the drain would have cured the problem. I am a frequent Marriott "stay-er" and reported this on the web site. No response. Good thing I am a hardy girl from the Midwest and not afraid of bugs.

“Excellent, almost Outstanding” This is the first time I've stayed at the Rittenhouse. Check-in wasn't available in the morning but the front desk staff took my cell phone number and called me when the room was ready. An upgrade room was provided that was roomy and comfortable. The bathroom was large, well appointed, and inviting. I didn't care for the bath amenities but I do realize that they were high end and quality nonethess. I liked the fact that the elevator was nearby my room but not close enough to here the cars going up and down. The food was excellent, and I highly recommend the buffet breakfast. Interestingly, when I arrived at the room, there was no plant in the room. Later that day, a large indoor plant arrived to liven up the room. I suppose they only put them in the room when a guest is actually assigned that room. The only complaint I had was that the shower handles to control the water actually needed a sign (that was actually provided!) to get hot water to issue. After following the sign's direction in the shower on how to turn on the hot water (first time I've seen such a sign in my many hotel stays), I still could not get hot water to come out. I actually had to call maintenance and voila, the hot water worked. Goes to show that if have to put a sign in the shower stall to learn how to get hot water, then a simpler faucet would be better. The food was superb, well presented, and delicious. The wait staff was incredible. I had a petit filet mignon and it was one of the best prepared pieces of beef I've ever had. The service staff throughout the hotel were cordial, polite, and helpful. Check out was fast and efficient. I would definitely stay here again on my next trip to Philadelphia.

“Great deal & Nice Stay” My husband and I stayed for three nights in September. We booked a great special which turned out to be about $170 per night with a full breakfast. The food quality and service were excellent. We loved the location and our room was extremely comfortable. The bathroom was huge and the bed was extremely comfortable. The fitness room and indoor pool were first class. The charge for internet access is ridiculous especially since it's free in the lobby. I also had a strange run in with the maid that resulted in a call to security and the need to provide ID to the front desk. These were the only drawbacks to an otherwise nice stay.

“Loved this funky little hotel in a great area” Love this hotel and it will definitely be my go-to in San Francisco. One because the staff was awesome, but also because it was clean and is a fantastic location. Can you say Toronado 3 blocks away? The location is great with lots of restaurants and shopping at your doorstep, what more could you want? The price is also very affordable, okay, so there's that! The room was a very odd shape, but it had two beds and they gave me a air bed for our third. The bathroom was huge as well. As people have noted, this definitely isn't a cookie-cutter hotel; I'm sure every room is unique.

“Bright, Modern and Clean! Great Value!” We had a great stay with my wife and 3-year old son. The rooms were designed well with a living area and sleeping area separated by a desk and room divider. The bathrooms are split; one side features a walk-in shower with glass doors, the other side had the toilet. Both sides had sinks which made showering with two people in the room a breeze. The sofa featured a pull-out be which was perfect for my son (although I found the pull out uncomfortable for a full-size adult). The beds and linens were average -- about what you would expect from a mid-price hotel. The best part of the hotel - other than the fact that it's new an everything is sparkling clean - is the value. Free wi-fi (which, in my opinion, should be free at every hotel regardless of price), free hot breakfast that included scrambled eggs and sausage, and free parking. The other big design feature that is appreciated is simple, yet lacking at so many newer, more expensive hotels -- outlets! There are outlets in the rooms everywhere there needs to be: at the desk and on the nightstands on each side of the bed. You don't have to move furniture around and search around bending over to find a plug for your cell phone and iPad. Thank you, thank you, thank you! Overall a great spot to stay. I'm looking forward to our next visit!

“everything fine but the overall decor is a downer” All the basics were fine - comfortable bed, nice front desk, great shower...only problem with the room was it was too hot and even though it was 25 degrees outside, the fan didn't cool the room down. (I'd hate to turn the AC on in the winter.) The reason I would not go back is the decor is no fun and just dreary and old fashioned. The competition is beating them badly on this and it makes a difference when you're looking for a fun get-away.

“Love the Loews, nicest people working there” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Loews the last weekend in April while we were visiting family in Philly. Our room was gorgeous and spacious with the best view of the Philadelphia skyline you could ever ask for. Everyone working there was SO pleasant and helpful, best staff I have experienced in a while. We also utilized the pool and workout facility and was very impressed with the number of machines they had available in the gym. Location was perfect as well, everything you could ask for is in walking distance, (most notability: the Reading Terminal Market.) Would definitely recommend this hotel to a friend.

“A Great Weekend Visit” We chose the Westin because of the combination of price (AAA rate), location and accommodation quality. We were initially a bit hesitant due to some TA reviews stating the hotel was showing some wear and tear. Upon arriving we didn't notice anything like that at all. Our room was on the Starwood Preferred Guest floor and was clean, comfortable and quiet with two double beds. The only quibble with our room was the placement of the television which was at an uncomfortable angle to view when lying in bed. Service from the hotel staff was courteous and professional, including the front desk personnel and concierge. Our room was promptly cleaned everyday although we never saw the cleaning staff. One morning we left for breakfast and returned a bit over an hour later to find our room already cleaned and serviced. Location is perfect for downtown, close to the Westlake Mall, Pacific Place, downtown stores, the monorail, Pike Market and convenient to Qwest Field. The underground bus line, free in the downtown core is a great way to get to the stadium. There are many good restaurants in the immediate area and we walked to every one during our visit; Serious Pie, Shiro's, Lowell's and Elliott's Oyster House. We enjoyed our stay at the Westin and would not hesitate to book a room there for our next visit to Seattle.

“great stay at the hotel indigo” Stayed a weekend at the Hotel Indigo and had a great stay. First thing is its location. It is right across from street from the Alamo, appx a block away from the Riverwalk, and 3 blocks from the Market. Parking in downtown San Antonio is quite an ordeal, but if you book the room from their website, they have valet parking for 5 dollars and its worth every penny! The valets were attentive and gave me spot on directions when I asked for them. The hotel is in an older office building and they kept some key elements from the old and mixed it with a modern twist. It has a really cool office vibe and it works very well. The king room we had was large, and very nice with a comfy bed and a large 32 lcd tv. The room we had only had a shower, but that didnt bother us any. The rooms in this hotel are shoehorned in there, but they work very nicely. Here are the only real bad things I noticed. The air conditioner is LOUD. Me and my wife are heavy sleepers, so it didnt bother us, but I can see why people would complain. The one thing that did bother us was that while the room was clean, it needed to be "cleaned". A hotel of this caliber shouldnt have dirt rings around the light switches and caked up gunk in the shower cracks. Every area had a handprint or a smudge or random dirt on it. It needed a good mom style cleaning and I am sure more attentive housekeeping could cure that. The bistro was very similar. Very nice looking and attentive service, but the breakfast bar was messy and unkept. Again, a little more attentiveness to cleanliness and it would be great. For the price point and location alone, this hotel is worth a stay.

“Bellhop service extremely good or extremely bad” I stayed at the Wellington for three nights in May after having stayed previously at the Comfort Inn at 442 W. 36th St. in the same general price range. The location of the Wellington was slightly better--right by a subway entrance, close to theaters, etc., and the nearby streets more traveled at night (for safety). However, the rooms were not much better. I had great service from the bellman at check-in. I had been given a smoking room by mistake, and he carted my suitcases back to the lobby, got me a non-smoking room and escorted me back up to the new room. The day I was checking out I needed help with my suitcases (packed for three casual days in the Finger Lakes area and three urban days in New York City plus had wine I had purchased). Despite promises from the front desk, the bellman did not arrive at my room. I struggled to the elevator in two trips but the elevators did not stop at my floor or were completely full with other passengers checking out with their luggage. I finally got help from a German lady and got on an elevator. Barely made it to the lobby in time to catch my shuttle ride to the airport. Congested elevators is one of the problems of large hotels with tour groups, etc. I didn't encounter this at the Comfort Inn. Also thought the staff at the Comfort Inn were friendlier and more helpful with the exception of the bellman at checkin at the Wellington.

“not your average HI Express” Stayed one night at this property and really enjoyed it. The rooms are HUGE, comfortable, clean and quiet. You can't hear the noise off I35. Flat screen tv and vintage mirror were great touches. Nice comfortable king bed with famour HIE pillows. The ballroom was super clean, with granite shower walls/vanity, tasteful wall paper and a shower drape. Bath products by HEI are great and always get the job done. Breakfast was good with fresh options. Didn't have to wait for 5 seconds to get anything replenished and the dinning room attendent was very friendly. Infact everyone, front desk, house keeping etc were very pleasant. No complains with this one at all. Stay here, you'll like it!

“Nice Architecture” This was a beautiful hotel when built and the architecture still is. Unfortunately it is now in need of a lick of paint and new carpets. The service here was good and staff friendly and helpful. The hotel bars and restaurants were overpriced. The location makes it good for people on business but not so good for tourists.

“Modernes Hotel mit guten Verkehrsanbindungen” Zu Beginn unserer Neuengland-Reise hatten wir uns das relativ neue IC Boston ausgesucht. Die Anreise erfolgte vom Flughafen kostenlos mit dem Shutle- Bus 66 zum Logan Ferry Terminal, ab dort mit einer kleinen Fähre für 10 USD/Person direkt zum IC Boston. Im Intercontinental superschnelles Einchecken, als Royal Ambassador bekamen wir eine riesengrosse Suite mit Speisezimmer, Schlafzimmer mit 2 King Size Betten, großem Bad mit Badewanne und Dusche sowie separater Gästetoilette. Club Intercontinental war sowohl für die bezahlten, als auch für die Reward-Nächte kostenlos. Im Club gab es ein ausreichendes Continental Breakfast, am Abend Bier und Wein und kleine Snacks. Hotel liegt ca. 200 m von der South Station für Nah- und Fernverkehr entfernt. Auch das Terminal für Fähren und Ausflugsschiffe liegt nur ein paar Minuten weg. Alles in allem ein hochwertiges, verkehrsgünstig gelegenes Hotel.

“Good stay for a reasonable price in Phoenix” We read all the reviews good, bad, neutral and given the price we received from Expedia.com decided to take a chance for our one night in Phoenix. We are glad we did. The woman at the reception desk set the tone when our credit card was denied (out of town travel--not over use!) when she calmed us down and talked us through another credit card (jet lag is my only excuse for the nerves--my husband was calm). Check in was smooth after that and we got to our room to find music playing. It was a biggish room, very clean, with a nice sized, clean bathroom. One little glitch, the air conditioner was not working at 100% as some people have stated in their reviews, but there was a fan in the room, it was early evening so cooler than the heat of the day, so we were comfortable and didn't complain--so we didn't really give management a chance to respond to our concerns. It was dinner time so we asked about Delux Burger which I had read about in other reviews. The woman at the desk quickly printed out directions and gave us her review--great! We had a wonderful dinner at Delux which is about 10 minutes (by car) from the hotel on Saddleback (I think). It is open until 2:00 a.m. and is apparently popular as an after evening eatery, but it was pleasantly busy and very attractive. Upon our return to the hotel we went to the rooftop bar and enjoyed a wonderful view of the Phoenix sky line and the stars. Slept very well, had a nice breakfast in the dining room (we were the only ones there for the most part). I would recommend the Hotel Clarendon for a moderately priced stay and the clean, modern rooms. We took a beautiful picture of the view from the roof top but it came out blurry! Sorry I can't share it with you.

“Okay, but not recommended for extended stay” I was here for a trade show and stayed a week. I was on the 2nd floor, train-side. The noise was loud sometimes, but not deafening. Room was clean and basic. My colleague's room was on the ground floor and smelled of mildew- awful. If you're passing through Denver on the highway, it's okay, but if you need to do business here, forget it.

“Great Experience, P:leasant Stay” We had a one night stay at the hotel for a show at the Gibson Theater at Universal City Walk at Universal Studios. Other than staying at the very pricey hotels adjacent to Universal, staying at the Holiday Inn Express was a wonderful choice. I was concerned about the negative remarks on this website, but found that the hotel was much better than I thought it would be. The hotel is conveniently located at the 101 South (Hollywood) Freeway. Across the street is a Chevron gas station. Within walking distance, there are a couple of quaint restaurants. When we checked into our room (Room #310), we found a large basket of complimentary chocolates, cookies, and 2 bottled waters. The room had a view of an alley - it wasn't offensive, but it wasn't the best, either. However, I would take the alley over a hotel roof. The room itself was immaculate. There were two Queen beds along with a desk, executive chair, lounge chair, and bench. We had ordered a rollaway bed ($15 extra cost) but it would have been too crowded to have the rollaway in the room. The room also had three phones in the room (one on the nightstand, one on the desk, and one in the bathroom). The bathroom is spacious and clean. The tub is one of the cleanest I have ever seen, and I have stayed at many hotels. It has a very nice Kohler shower head, and the curtain is on a rod that is curved for more bathing space. The towels are of high quality,. The room and hallway was quiet even though the hotel was full. With regard to the "bleach smell" - I would say the smell is more like a cleaner smell with a floral scent. It is not offensive and is actually pleasant because you know the hotel and room is clean. The carpet was in excellent condition - very clean with no tears and no worn spots. The ice machines are modern and dispense ice quickly. Hotel is well maintained. The hotel room card must be used in order to access the elevator. The breakfast is nice and is served from 6:30 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. We did not experience any crowds at all - there were only 2 or 3 at any given time. There is a nice selection of bagels, cinnamon rolls, crossaints, hard boiled eggs, dry cereals (several choices), oatmeal, muffins, donuts, and a variety of juices and water along with hot tea and coffee. Universal Studios is 1.5 miles away. It is challenging to exit the hotel because there is a three way signal light at the hotel. The signal is confusing. You cannot walk to Universal, but the hotel is one of the closest other than the very pricey ones adjacent to Universal Studios. Internet access is free, however, guests must obtain a cable from the front desk. You must connect the cable to your laptop at the desk, so it is not so convenient, as you must be at the desk to do work rather than any other part of the room. Lastly, the parking is limited. Guests must place a paper placard in the window to show they are guests at the room. In addition, latecomers end up parking next to the office rather than in a spot. Otherwise, I feel the room and the hotel was a good deal (I booked two months in advance) and was well worth what we paid. I would stay there again and recommend it to other travelers.

“We loved our dog-friendly stay!” Our stay at the Palomar exceeded our expectations. My husband and I stayed her in October while in town for the Daily Show/Colbert rallies. The city was definitely crowded that weekend...also because it was Halloween. The vibe in the hotel was lively and fun....especially during the wine happy hour! Our room was clean, spacious and comfortable. It was nice to have some space to hang out since we had friends coming over to the room. I love that the Palomars are dog friendly. Unfortunately our dog loves people, but not always other dogs. We called ahead to request a room on a lower floor/near stairs and they were able to accommodate us with no problem. Once we got in the room, we noticed our dog was getting rock star treatment as well! she got a huge dog bed, water/food bowls and poop bags. Too bad the dog ended up lounging on our bed the whole time! We parked on the street, which was no problem. The hotel is in a great location near lots of shops, food, train, etc... We even hit the Trader Joes a few minutes away on our drive back to NY!

“Had two great stays at the W Lakeshore” I have to say that I have not been disappointed with a W yet! This hotel was very reasonable when I booked it for 110 per night and used starpoints on a couple of other nights plus cash (4,800 starpoints plus $60 per night). I had a great room overlooking the lake and with a good view of the Navy Pier. The rooms were very modern but very warm during the bleak winter months of December and March in Chicago when I stayed there. The beds were very consistently comfortable across the W's I have stayed at in Montreal and New Orleans. Service was excellent and I was always addressed by my first name. On my way to the gym the bell man that assisted me with my luggage said hello and wished me a good work out. I did have a wonderful work out in their nice gym overlooking the lake. This is my favorite hotel in Chicago. I would like to try the city center some time when I return to the area. The only complain I have is the location is often confusing for some people. It took one of my friends a while to find the place but we got there eventually. The bar on the top floor and the lobby lounge are always filled with great smiles and beautiful people. I highly recommend having a drink on the top floor (I'm a sucker for a sky line view!). It is not quite the Hancock building view but it is worth a cocktail or two and what's the worst? Your room is within stumbling distance :)
“38m2” 窓がとても大きく、窓際のカウチの寝転び具合も良く、街中を見下ろしていると時間を忘れます!室内はとてもシックで落ち着けますが、何せ狭い!カテゴリーは一番下のスタンダードルームだったと思います。 (約38m2) 立地がコロンバスサークルなので地下鉄にバス、また観光や買い物にはとても便利です。次回機会があったら、少々お高くてもParkViewに泊まりたいです!

“A little disappointing” I formerly lived nearby, and have driven by the MarQueen hundreds of times, and I really wanted to love the place. The exterior and lobby are gorgeous, and the hallways have a warm-and-cozy air, but our room didn't feel nearly as inviting unfortunately. It was large, but it felt cold. The furnishings were more 1990's-Bombay-Company than antique; an update wouldn't mean giving up old world charm, and I think it's time. Bed was jiggly, sheets were old, and the burgundy coverlet was flat and dated. (The one single thing that would have improved the room, a LOT: new, fresh linens.) In the bath, they've done a fine job with old plumbing, but I had to bend-double to reach the faucet while avoiding smacking my head on the wobbly glass shelf. And while the fixtures were clean, the walls are so textured that dust and mildew are gaining ground, and little things like the wainscoting/frames/hairdryer-plug were coated with dust. We had reserved a King room, but after opening our door to two queen beds and a trip downstairs to clarify, we were told they had oversold them. The clerk was breezily apologetic but it was kind of a bummer. We also weren't asked at check-out how our stay was, and I think it's just good policy to ask. Either way, I have to admit I was ready to go. (I'm sorry, MarQueen!)

“Hip hotel” Our first room had a horrible odor. We were immediately upgraded to a city view room. The rooms are a good size with a nice sitting area. There is a refrigerator as well as a coffee maker. Free breakfast is offered downstairs. A good variety of foods. A real plus is the shuttle service which will take you a few miles to and pick you up from. The lobby is large and modern. Convenience-wise, if you like to walk, it's a bit over a mile to Pike's Market. On a nice day it's a great walk since you pass through several different areas. Great value for the money!
“自転車を借りれます” スペースニードルのすぐ近く、クイーンズアンの坂のふもとの近くにあります。清潔できれい、また、Wifi込みのパッケージ(たった$7のサーチャージ)を加えると、宿泊中、ホテルが保有している自転車を借りることが出来ます。私達は自転車でダウンタウンやフレモントなどほとんど近場の町は回りましたが、とても楽しかったです。

“A Fine Experience in Downtown LA” As luck would have it, Priceline got me a great rate ($90.00 a night) over a holiday weekend in downtown Los Angeles. The front desk was very supportive, from small tasks like cleaning my window to generous favors. The clerk gave me complimentary Wi-Fi and put me on a high floor so I could photograph the panoramic view of the city. The breakfast buffet was fresh and reasonable, the night time revolving restaurant was very impressive, the view and the service. Valet parking was swift and always courteous. The surrounding neighborhood has many attractions and the freeway access close by gets you anywhere you need to go. They were filming an action film just outside the hotel in the middle of the night, so "Hollywood" was even closer than normal!!! I had a great time.

“Excellent Airport Hotel” Very pleasantly surprised by the quality of this hotel. Reception was friendly, received upgraded room, room in fine shape with excellent shower and nice bed. Restaurant food was very, very good, especially for a hotel, and regional wine list was fine. Workout room did not disappoint either. Would stay here again.

“ok, but a bit noisy with the construction....” The hotel overlooks Ground Zero, where the World Trade Center Towers used to be, and in your room you hear the construction noise from the work that is going on to build something new there. It starts early, even on the weekends. This was the first time that I had been back to the hotel since 9/11. The hotel rooms were renovated after it and are well designed and equipped, especially for the business traveller which I guess due its location are the main guests. The desk for working at has a proper work chair which makes a huge difference. There is a great, modern coffee making machine (which I wish more hotels had) and a really huge flat screen TV. The bed is large but not as comfortable as those at the Sheraton or Westin. There is a surprising lack of choice of places to eat or drink. There is only a very small bar in the lobby and one restaurant on the 3rd floor (which did a satisfactory but not stunning buffet). There is a fitness centre but I did not get to it on this trip. The hotel is right next to the famous Century 21 discount label department store and an easy 10 minute walk to South Street Sea Port area with its shops and museums and the major drop off and pick up for the round Manhattan bus tours. But overall, it is not a very handy destination for tourists as far from the shopping areas and Central Park etc. Overall, I liked the room a lot but the noise of construction did wake me up earlier than I would have liked so was glad my stay was so short. When the World Trade Center was across the road there was much better eating and shopping etc, and sure there will be again. You can often get good deals at the hotel as the construction puts a lot of people off. It is not massively troublesome but more of a minor distraction in reality.

“Perfect for a Solo Traveler - Very clean, nice location!” I went to Chicago last weekend for the Ryder Cup (Golf Tournament) and everywhere I usually stay was completely booked! Rooms were going for crazy rates, so I started seeking out some options that were 'off the beaten path'. I discovered the Central Loop Hotel, and I knew where it was, as I used to walk by it from time to time when I still lived in Chicago. The hotel is very well kept, and has cheap valet ($34/night with in-and-out access!). THe check in process was a little strange to me because you check in using a machine like you would at the airport. Some people might love this - but i missed talking to a real person. The machine printed my room info and key card and I headed up to my 6th floor corner room. This room was perfect for my needs. Very comfortable bed, sparkling white linens, beautiful widows that overlooked some fantastic Chicago architecture (post office). But - this room was TINY! Again, it was just me and I knew I would only be spending time in my room sleeping, but the bathroom was very small (no tub, shower only) and the closet was tiny. Almost felt like a ship's quarters. If you are going as a couple, or even attempting to bring kids I would def. upgrade to a larger room or suite. The rooms have free wifi (yeah!), lots of cable channels, free in room coffee and a friendly concierge staff. Free bottled water stations on each floor are also a nice touch. I will stay here again if I'm traveling alone.

“OK, But Not Fabulous Hill Country Resort” Hyatt Wild Oak Ranch is a Hyatt Vacation Club property that also rents rooms by the night. We were there for two nights because we had received an invitation for a cheap package if we did the timeshare tour. It was a very good value deal. However, I can't say I really recommend this place. It is not a country resort at all because it is located in the San Antonio suburbs, close to Seaworld. When we checked in, the receptionist asked us which floor would we like to be on. We asked what he recommended and he said that the 1st floor was convenient but the 3rd floor had the best views. We chose the 3rd floor. The first room we went to had stunning views over - the parking lot! So we changed rooms and then got a stunning view of the suburbs and the freeway (and boy was that freeway noisy). Please see my pictures. I would suggest you stay on the 1st floor where you overlook landscaping and trees and thus can maintain the illusion that you are in the country. I can't say I was overly impressed with our studio room. There was a nice big bathroom which could have easily accommodated a big tub, but the tub was narrow and shallow. The bed was one of the most uncomfortable I have slept on in a long time - surprising for a high end chain. On our tour we saw the 1 and 2 bedroom apartments and they were much better appointed, with full kitchens, big flatscreen TV, whirlpool bath and separate walk in shower. I would suggest staying in one of those instead. The rooms are located in 3 story blocks that look like cheap apartment buildings with a lot of unfinished steel and corrugated steel balcony partitions. It's just not very pretty. There is a heated indoor/outdoor pool with water slides and an unheated lazy river with a beach and surrounded by hammocks. That was fun and would definitely be good for kids. The kids will also like the gamesroom with its arcade games (but which you have to pay for - a bit cheap for a vacation resort). I also liked the firepit area where there are several wood burning pits which the staff will light for you. For golfers, the resort has its own golf course. Being a timeshare resort, it doesn't have the bar/restaurant amenities that you would find at a regular resort. There is a smokehouse restaurant that is open for lunch and until 7, that serves perfectly acceptable comfort food. There is also a shop that sells basic food items for your room. There is an actual Hyatt Hotel Resort located about a mile away where you can go for full service dining. We visited this nearby Hyatt hotel to see how it compared and it is a lot prettier. Also, it has been built in a dip, rather than up on a hill, so you cannot see the suburbs and freeway. I think it is unlikely I would return to Wild Oak, even with a cheap deal, but I can imagine returning to the hotel sometime in the future. On our final night we went to eat at Grey Moss Inn which is in the village of Grey Forest, about a 25 minute drive into the country. The atmosphere, food, wine list and service was excellent. When you pull into the parking lot and all these little deer scatter off, you are already charmed!

“What a Surprise!” Selected this hotel based on Trip Advisor reviews and the great AAA price. First impressions? Large room with two very comfortable queen size beds, strong air conditioning, good location, fast free WIFI. The surprise? There was a mouse in our room! Need I say more?

“Good - and not so.” First the good: They are updating and with many rooms done you should insist on a newly remodeled one. Our 'double double' turned out to be a freshly redone mini-suite on the very quiet 12th floor. There was ample hot water, nice toiletries and fluffy robes. The bedding was posh, plenty of closet space, and the room was really BIG for a city hotel room. The doormen were polite and prompt to be helpful. The not so good: Internet costs $10.00 a night. Access to a lobby computer to print boarding passes was $4.00 (didn't use it when I found that out) Continental breakfast in their breakfast room will set you back $12.00 a person (nice coffee shop catter-corner across the park opens @6am, and is 1/2 the price) No fridge. The desk staff ran warm-and-cold. The concierge was only in from about 9am to 3pm - never when we were at the hotel and needed something. We had to dodge workmen on walpapering the halls on our floor the last day we were there - then they started up @ 8 AM. Other Things to know: These 'double beds' are not for two people unless it is two small kids, or you are VERY friendly. They seem a lot narrower than standard doubles. Our beds were very soft, and my daughter had a hard time sleeping on them - ending up on the floor wrapped in the comforter. The Hotel is very close to the Subway, Cabs are easily found, and the 79 crosstown bus stops just across the street. We walked around the neighborhood pretty late at night, and it felt safe - but very quiet - lots of families and dogs running around. Conclusion: If you get a good deal, love Central Park and the museums, don't require a lot of help finding things to do, like quiet and comfortable places to crash - this might be the place for you.

“Very nice but not the nicest” This hotel is very easy to get to, clean, and very helpful staff. The pool area is very nice. The hot tub was ok but could have been hotter. Rooms were clean, but small. Bar was good, food was ok. Better than the Hyatt Tech Center. The Marriot in the Tech Center is better for overall stay, but the Four Points pools is a lot better. Thats the only problem with bidding for rooms, you can't select the actual hotel.

“Great value for money” After a brief problem with the card key maker on check-in that wasted about 10 minutes of my day, I had a positive stay at the Days Inn on Connecticut Avenue in DC. I spent three nights there and only had some trouble with a group of children, who I think were from France, making a hell of a racket, but that had calmed down by the time I actually wanted to go to sleep after coming in late from an NHL game. The big plus point about the Days Inn was the price, which came in about half of what the rest of the over-priced DC hotels were looking for. Of course this meant being out in the 'burbs, but it is still barely more than a 15-minute subway ride into the heart of things and Van Ness-UDC is a mere stroll to reach. There are plenty of options for eating nearby (chains mainly like Burger King, Quiznos and Potbelly) and a few family restaurants plus the odd store. The rooms are decently sized - I had two big beds even though I was on my own - but I am not a big fan of the small pillows on offer, the small square ones some chains seem to be edging towards. Give me a rectangular pillow any day of the week. The other facilities in-room were just fine, although the power in the shower was a little lacking, but these are just small things and shouldn't take away from the positive nature of my review.

“Convenient Location - But a Few Service Issues” I usually avoid Marriotts but was recently booked to stay at the Marriott Metro Center in DC by Priceline for $150 per night. The location is the major selling point: Perfect for easy access to major tourist destinations (Smithsonian museums, etc), and a metro subway entrance is just steps away. The clerk was most gracious at check in and, in response to my request for a quiet room, was able to find me a bright corner room on a high floor. The room was comfortable and very clean. Good shower pressure. Large number of cable tv channels. Comfortable mattress and plenty of pillows. A number of guests were attending a business meeting during my stay (name tags gave them away). Problems: - walls very thin; I heard the kids constantly chattering nearby for several days, then on the last night only got 2 hours of sleep before an early flight after listening to my neighbor's tv until the wee hours - some kind of maintenance (drilling, hammering sounds, and workmen chattering) next door during part of my stay - the hotel uses down pillows, comforters, & mattress pads, which are very comfortable but set off my allergies; the staff changed these the next morning at my request (although I realized later that the replacement mattress pad also had feathers!). The staff really should ask guests whether they would prefer down or non-down bedding on check in to minimize the inconvenience for both guests and housekeeping staff. - "high-speed" wired internet (no wireless) in the room was VERY slow (at $13/day), and the internet connection cord was very short - housekeeping did not service my room for 2 days of my stay. The first day was my fault, as I had the "do not disturb" sign on the door until 3:00pm and did not notify the staff when I was ready to have the room serviced (since a sign in the room said that their normal service hours were 8:00-4:30). The next day, since I had the "do not disturb sign" on the door until 2:30pm, I made a point of asking at the desk when I went out to be sure to have the staff service the room, and I was assured that it would be taken care of. When I returned late in the evening, the room still had not been serviced. - no safe or refrigerator available in the room (not sure whether available in other standard rooms of the hotel) - parking over $30 per day (although I did not require it) Given these problems, I would not stay at this hotel again if the price were more than $180 per night.

“modesto” la stanza più piccola che abbia mai visto. per aprire le valigie abbiamo dovuto metterle sul letto una alla volta. Abbiamo richiesto una camera king e invece il letto era al massimo un qeen, non c'era spazio per muoversi, non c'è il climatizzatore e abbiamo dovuto tenere la finestra aperta sentendo così i treni che passavano lì vicino ed il rumore della strada. il parcheggio è sotterraneo, strettissimo e le auto devono parcheggiare occupando 2 posti con la conseuenza che non c'è posto per tutti, abbiamo pagato 20 dollari per 2 giorni. Comunque è pulito e la zona, little italy è carina, per una notte va bene anche se lo trovo troppo caro (circa 100 dollari a notte)

“Noce, yet old Hotel in a very good location” Stayed at the Windsor Park when I got a really good price in a neighborhood I used to live in and love. Equal distance, possibly a tad closer to the Woodley Park Metro than Dupont (I walked downhill to Dupont in the morn and got off at Woodley Park and walked downhill back to the hotel). Great location across from the Chinese Embassy, parking looks a bit difficult, great ethnic restaurants w/in walking distance and actually a very quiet stay. As other reviewers have mentioned, at a good price, this is one of the bext values in Washington, DC but if you are at all particular about hotel and luxury being tied together this is not the hotel for you. However, if you are at a convention in the Woodley Park complex or on a per diem target for a major corp, etc. this is a very good hotel to deliver a good, safe stay. Personally my stay was good. Slightly updated room, noisy but very good air conditioning, wireless that worked, comfy bed and small but clean bathroom w/ a nice hot shower. Very safe neighborhood and easy to transportation as well as quiet. Did I mention quiet....

“5 Stars” I just arrived home from 5 days at the fairmont olympic hotel in seattle and i would have been content to move in their permanently! i was fortunate to be booked in on a convention rate ($250 per night--and they didn't have the basic room for 5 nights so for $25 more i had a suite!).....that is $25 well spent!! i had a huge king sized bed and a separate living room with sofa, 2 overstuffed pillows to rest my head after a day of shopping, a desk, chair and 2 tvs.....there is a separate dressing area and the bathroom was nice with 2 robes to use..... the hotel is first class all the way....the staff cannot do enough for you!! i had requested a coffee maker, which for some reason the fairmont does not provide.....when i checked in, there was no coffee maker in the room, so i phoned the front desk.....the head of catering told me that he would get one for me, even if he had to buy it himself.....sure enough, within 1/2 hour they brought me a coffee maker on a silver platter with all the acoutrements!! i was very impressed.....the doormen greet you when you leave the premises and when you return--a nice touch!! coffee and tea is served in the lobby in the early morning.....the carpet is starting to look a bit dated in the halls, but that would be my only complaint--and a small price to pay for a marvellous hotel.......i can't wait to stay on the "gold floor" on the fairmont in boston--where i am going in 1 week!! by the way, seattle is a great city for shopping! it is small--all of the shops are within a 2 block radius--macy's, nordstroms, brooks brothers, coach, yves st laurent, etc. etc.! heaven for this visitor from canada!

“Overpriced for quality” I booked a room online through the hotel website, and got a rate of $179/night for 3 nights. I was going alone to Houston for a business trip, so I wanted to be near some type of attraction for the evenings. I requested a refrigerator for my room when I booked online, but when I checked in I was told that the person who would take care of it was already gone for the day but they'd make sure it was taken care of the next morning. I returned to my room the next evening, and there was no refrigerator. I did not make a complaint about it, but I was hoping for a little follow through. When I got into the elevator after checking in, it looked rough. There was a big sign on the wall apologizing for the ongoing renovations...so I was concerned. It turns out floors 2-3 are undergoing renovations currently and are not being occupied. I was placed on floor 6, and would suggest anyone coming here to request a higher floor (6 is highest) to avoid any construction noise. I didn't have any issues with noise during my stay, but there was a fair amount of construction traffic in the lobby/elevator areas. When I got to my floor, there were no directional signs coming out of the elevator to direct me to my room, so it took me a minute to figure out which way to go. The room has a tile entryway/bathroom followed by a carpeted "bedroom" area. There is a flat panel swivel TV, which was nice. The comforter was lumpy and there weren't any electrical outlets near the bed to allow me to plug in my laptop and type in bed, which would have been nice. However, the bed was comfortable and there were ample pillows. There is a business center, but one of the two computers wasn't working so there was a wait to use it when I went in to print my boarding pass. I did like the breakfast--there were quite a few options of pastry, bagels with sausage/cheese on top, cereals, yogurt, etc. as well as "to go" breakfasts in brown bags by the check in counter. As for what's convenient, there is a starbucks and Jack in the Box within walking distance, as well as a Target. To get to the Galleria, the huge and well known shopping destination, requires a vehicle. I imagined it would be walking distance, but unfortunately that was not at all the case. It's definitely a high end shopping mall, but there are lots of restaurants inside so it was an ok way to spend the evening. The hotel is very near I-610, which makes it a convenient location. I felt safe at all times here, even when I arrived later in the evening. There was a security guard on duty, though I'm not sure if that was a preventative measure or because of safety concerns. The area was mixed commercial and residential, and while it didn't have a lot of character, it felt safe. While I didn' t have any significant issues with my stay here, it also didn't stand out as a memorable experience in any way, either.

“Great Location - Reasonably Priced” Rate: we secured a reasonable rate by booking in advance. Checkin: a little challenging getting to the lobby on Level 2 as we arrived at a busy time. Reception gave us a few minutes to arrive at our room and rang to follow-up to see if we needed any assistance. Liked having security on the ground floor. Rooms: Comfortable, clean, nice view overlooking Bowery St & the Manhatten Bridge. Bathroom has been renovated and had a heated floor. Wifi works well. Bed is comfortable and mattress has a special bug protector. Extras: it would be nice to be able to make your own tea in the lobby to the strength of your liking. Complimentary breakfast – bagels, croissant, toast & eggs - is adequate. They are obviously short on space as the bag storage fee is quite steep. Location: central to Chinatown, Little Italy, Soho & The Village. We stayed a few days near Times Square (Distrikt Hotel is fabulous) then relocated to BW to cover Downtown & Brooklyn area. We walked everywhere but the subway is also handy. Shopping: if you are looking for T-shirt souvenirs avoid the tourist traps & try Yellow Rat B*stard in Soho. Century 21 is nearby at Ground Zero but we preferred the boutiques in Soho – especially for lingerie! Food: The Cupping Room Café has fabulous food, has great value & ambience! Things to do: don’t bother with the Staten Island Ferry. Brooklyn bridge is a must as is the 3hr Circle Line tour if you are new to NY. Transit: we took the Subway $2.25 + Airtrain $5 to JFK. Can use Metro card. We would stay again.

“Location and bed were the highlights” This hotel is definitely in a great location few blocks from everything. Check in was speedy and staff was helpful. The room was fairly big but the bathroom was small with the outdated tub and shower combo, and the TV was old. The bed was good. Now the fees at this hotel are outrageous $52 for overnight parking and room service was very expensive too with poor quality food.

“Fantastic experience” The previous postings do this hotel justice. Fantastic experience. Great customer service...Jerry Hume, Concierge, is top notch and everyone else provided nothing but top level customer service. Room was clean, bed was great, and loved the french press coffee service in the room. It is the little things that make a stay great. Sorrento does a great job.

“Nice Hotel near the White House” Stayed here for 2 nights on a short trip. Nice hotel. The room (and hotel) were nicer than the usual Holiday Inns I've stayed in. The room itself was large and spacious with an empty fridge for your own use. There was also free wifi which was a nice added touch. Breakfast was lovely in the restaurant, either buffet or from the menu. On arrival I received some dicount vouchers for use at breakfast and dinner in the hotel as I am a Priority Club member. Don’t forget to look on the back of the voucher wallet as I missed a few additional vouchers (one of which was free soft drinks if you ordered a pizza from room service) – the discounts add up :-) The starbucks next to the hotel was also a nice feature. Tours etc are available from the hotel. White house is walkable in 20 minutes. I arrived by the blue shuttle bus from the airport $27 one way (which is more expensive than NYC!). Be aware of the rude staff at the counter who seem more interested in talking to each other or reading magazines. My name is quite a long Indian name and most people mis spell it. I offered the girl at the counter my hotel reservation which had the spelling on it and she refused to look at it...ended up spelling my name on the receipt as Carpenter...way off! When I showed it to her she got in a strop and apparantly doen't like having pieces of paper shoved in her face (which I didn't), she then advised she would have to cancel and re book if I wanted it changed which meant waiting another 30 mins...wasn't gonna happen! Anyway, the hotel was great (just beware the shuttle bus reservations people at the airport!)

“Geniales Designer Hotel” wer das moderne designer mässige mag und verückte zimmer liebt, ist hier gut aufgehoben, wie verrückt das ganze ist?? rufen sie mal an im hotel, aber bitte nicht wurdern wenn plötzlicher der schwarzenegger oder bruce willis drann ist :-)) also das hotel hat keine kute lage wenn man mit der metro kommt, fussweg ca 15 min und das mit koffern geht nicht, also taxi...jedoch zu fuss ist man schnell am dupont circle.... der check in ist cool und ghet rasch. freundliches personal, geniale bar in diesem bereich. die zimmer sind verrückt, jedoch genial...modern riesen flt tv, einfach geile betten . frühstück war inklusive jedoch !!! es wird genau erwähnt wieviel stück und gläser man sich vom buffet nehmen darf, also ja kein gebäck mehr *lach* sonst geniales hotel ihr werdet es auch lieben

“Excellent hotel” I stayed at this hotel on my way across America to Houston. The reception was nicely decorated and well kept. Staff could not have been more helpful. As expected breakfast was self service but had a better than average selection of food. Although this Holiday Inn Express did not provide food in the evening there was a shuttle service which allowed me to visit restaurants elsewhere and once again the service was excellent. My room was very well appointed and immaculately clean. Five star hotel for a much lower cost.

“Beautiful historic hotel in great location” Got a great rate for a weekend in Aug through Priceline. Rooms was of reasonable size by NYC standards. Beautiful public areas. Only negative is wifi only free in public areas and not in rooms.

“Residence Inn with Ritz Carlton service” This was without a doubt the best Residence Inn experience I have ever had. For the record, without some sort of a deal, a night in a downtown Denver hotel is going to run you $150-$200+/night and the Residence Inn is no exception; however, what you get is exceptional. Parking at the hotel was $20/night which is cheaper than most other downtown hotels. Further, with garage self-parking you're never waiting (and tipping) each time you get your car. Compared to a downtown hotel room, the rooms were huge and nicely appointed. The smallest unit (a studio suite) had a full sized fridge, a cook top, microwave, and a dishwasher. Everything you'd need for an extended stay even if you just want to save and re-heat some leftovers. The bed was great with a sheeted comforter (my preferred bedding) and the iPod/MP3 alarm clock is definitely the way to go. Free internet (both wired and wireless) was also a bonus. The hotel is in a perfect location. Next door to the Hotel Monaco, it's a block or so away from 16th street and four blocks from the convention center. You can also easily walk to nearly every restaurant downtown. The light dinner and limited open bar served nightly hit the spot when you just want to sit down, have a snack and drink a beer or two. The morning breakfast was great with a good selection of hot foods including eggs, oatmeal, waffles and a variety of pastries, fruits, and yogurts. For a quick weekend trip, this might not be important, but for a somewhat longer business stay, these perks add up. The fitness center was more than sufficient, there's a hot tub (no pool), and for a hotel that permits pets, I couldn't smell a thing. The best part of our stay was certainly the service. As other reviewers mentioned, service was absolutely top notch. From dinner reservations to grabbing a quick snack for you when you're a few minutes past meal times, the front desk staff seem ready to do whatever they can to make sure you have an enjoyable stay.

“Excellent service, nice location” I stayed here with my best girlfriend from childhood. I had requested separate beds and we we accomodated. The room was large and well furnished. The bathroom was also very large, clean and marble. Everything was very clean as well. The service was excellent and the staff extremely friendly. Since I had paid for the cheapest price room the view was just so-so but not horrible. We were on the consierge level so breakfast was included and was held in a nice big room overlooking the park. There was a wide choice of breakfast foods. I did not check this room at other times of the day but I think there were different things in the afternoon, for instance. We did see a couple of well known actors so this must be one of their favorites. We had massages and the only negative in this hotel is the spa could be a bit larger. I would stay here again just for the staff.

“Great Hotel- Great Rooms- Terrific Location” Magnificent Mile Area of Chicago is one of my favorite cities to visit for business with the added benefit of the great city of Chicago-its food- buildings- museums- shopping- This hotel is perfectly situated in the heart of all of it. I had a beautiful room on the 17th floor (1705) Nice suite. Living room view is a shot toward the lake and bedroom the John Hancock Tower and Delaware Pl toward Michigan Ave. Spacious room- Could not expect more. The restaurant next door is terrific homemade Italian and I seriously suggest eating here! I booked through Expedia - so if the rates are consistant I will absolutely stay here again!

“Horrible service” The rooms are decent and the location is ok but the service is just horrible. Room service never is open even when it's supposed to; front desk staff spends way more time talking to each other than helping others

“Great value, great location” I can only agree with the previous reviewers. The big +++: Location in Georgetown, near circulator bus line (but not metro) Well equipped, spacious room Price hard to beat Good coffee and free breakfast Helpful and efficient staff Free wireless and troublefree internet Nice touches (toiletries, daily paper) The few minuses (didn't really matter to us): Carpet stains Workout facility hard to get to and some equipment broken Slow elevators cause waiting Matress needs overhaul

“Great Hotel-- Best Holiday Inn Express Ever” Nothing bad to say about the stay or the hotel. It was one of the best Holiday Inn Express hotels I have ever visited. Recommended for that price range of hotel.

“Very nice. Windows may not open.” In agreement with other positive reviews for this property. I was eligible for an upgrade to an executive suite, but those were all full. My stay was for just a single night so this did not matter to me. I had a room just above the fitness room and just about spitting distance from the bar in the middle of the lobby atrium. The bar looks like quite a happening place, but I was too exhausted to check it out. The room was very quiet and comfortable nevertheless, but this interior location had no openable windows. Air conditioner was a bit loud and I don't sleep well with air conditioners on so I would personally not spend a night here again. The restaurants and service are all extremely good, and I would return for those reasons, but not to stay another night unless the windows open to the outside somewhere. Savannah Bistro in particular, has by far the best hotel breakfast that I've ever had in a chain hotel in the US. I had the breakfast buffet there. Dinner buffet was good too.

“Well-run” This hotel was well-run and met my expectations, with the exception of room size. The suites were tiny compared to other Homewood Suites I've stayed in. They were comfortable, but definitely on the cozy side. The sitting room felt rather cramped. But service was good, the staff was nice, and I was a fan of the kitchen amenities. Location is great--I was attending a conference at the Marriott across the street, and I think I got a better deal than the people staying there. It's a five minute walk to all the attractions of the Inner Harbor. Also, breakfast and the Welcome Home dinner were nice perks. There's no concierge, but the front desk staff made a good recommendation for dinner. Unfortunately, there's not much of a view from any of the rooms, but since I was hardly ever in the room, it didn't matter much.

“Nice stay at the Four Seasons” Stayed one night at the Four Seasons. The hotel is located near the art museum. The location is ok depending on what you plan to do in Philly. For us, where our time revolved around Rittenhouse Square, it wasn't ideal. For a touris, it is likely fine. The hotel is well maintained and the rooms are nice and clean and well maintained. The room was large and had a soft fluffy king bed. It had a small desk and sitting area, a flat screen tv and a mini bar. The bathroom was large and was the typical old-style Four Seasons with lots of marble and a normal tub/shower. The towels were huge and fluffy. Really no complaints at all on the room. The service was ok at the hotel. The hotel was at full capacity and the staff seemed a bit overwhelmed. For instance, the valets were very busy and didn't open our car doors. The check in desk was overwhelmed and we had to wait to check in. Overall, it was a fine stay. If I were visting Philly and the location was good, I would consider the Four Seasons.

“Well Worth the Stay” So, I just had to see for myself: How can a nice hotel look like a prison? Well, with a little imagination, I could see the connection. However, that funny novelty aside, this is really a pleasant, refreshing place to stay with many nice attributes. The hotel itself is well maintained with a newer, bright, modern decor in a quiet parklike setting (even though it's next to a small airport, the plane noise was barely noticable). And that "prison" design actually helps give the place a bright, spacious feel (no long, dark corridors). To top it off the staff was great, the restaurant was solid (for hotel fare), the wireless internet was free (it worked most of the time), parking was free, the bed was comfy, it had a nice pool area, and the central location was great with about 10-20 minute drives to downtown, the zoo, Mission Bay, and La Jolla (plus you were out of the way of the hectic hotel corridors). A stay at the Four Points helped make for a great weekend getaway and I would definitely put it on my list for a return visit.

“Nice Hotel, don't park your car” Valet staff is horrible they lie it takes half an hour to get your car when they screwed up so bad they ended up paying for my parking for over three weeks because he couldn't get my car up in time before I had a flight to catch if you stay at the hotel which is great get a taxi do not valet your car!

“Average or Below” The Marriott Wardman Park is an at best average hotel in an excellent location. We stayed during a conference when rates at this hotel were quite high, certainly far beyond the quality of the rooms or hotel amenities. Our room was small with an adequate bathroom. This is a large hotel with little charm. In the future, I will plan to stay elsewhere because there are many nicer options in the area.

“Location -Location-Location! Great Hotel” We stayed at the Charlesmark, Nov 10 - Nov 14, for 4 nights. We arrived at the hotel at 10:00 am from our flight, too early to check in. We were traveling with another couple,so we asked to have rooms close together on the top floor, after reading other reviews about street noise. We left our luggage and headed out into the city. We walked the freedom trail and the entire city all day, and didn't get back to the hotel until 5:30 pm. We checked in no problem, and our luggage had already been put in our rooms, on the 6th floor. The rooms are small but nicely appointed, and spotlessly clean. Our room was very quiet, I would defiently recomend the top floors. The only concern I had was the floor was a little squeeky , it didn't bother us but I wonder if the room below could hear it? We enjoyed the complimentary breakfast, always had lots on hand and kept it refilled. Free internet in the lounge area was a bonus,and useful for checking out places and making reservations. As my title says, we loved the location. Boston really is a walking city, and such a beautiful one, take advantage of that. The Blueman Group is great, Prudential Skywalk Wonderful,Body works2 art show WOW. So much to see so little time, can't wait to go back, and would gladly stay at the Charlesmank again

“Delightful, Delicious, Delovely” A blast from the past The Barclay was an absolute bargain. Having secured tickets to The Book of Mormon, we traveled from Atlanta to New York for just one day. Since we used miled on American, we were able to book the hotel through them. Interestingly enough, they use Travelocity for their hotels, BUT, you get to see who you are booking with. Ours was a pre-paid deal. $200 for one night in a Deluxe room. The lobby is regal and grand, in the way that only older hotels can be. Beautiful marble, mohogany, antique furniture. Makes you just say, "aaahhh." We arrived at noon, and they were more than happy to check us in and let us in the room. The room looks exactly like it did in the pictures on the website. The beds have featherbed toppers on them, which makes the bed super-high and VERY cushy. Although I prefer to sleep on a plank, I had no trouble drifting off to dreamland. I slept like a log. Also, the hotel, although being full, was quiet. No traffic noise, no neighbor noise, no elevator noise. Just quiet. The cable is extensive, and not just with news and sports, they have expanded cable, so you can watch Law and Order if you just want to relax with something familiar. The blow dryer in the bathroom didn't work, a call to housekeeping brought one in about 1 minute! Seriously. The coffee maker is a Keurig and they provide 2 pods of decaf and 2 pods of regular. I brought filters and grounds, so had I known, I would have just used what they had. The coffee package provided was in a cute cardboard box, so I don't know if they have powdered creamer or real cream. I brought some mini-moos and used them. The mini-bar was stocked with the usual assortment of outrageously expensive crap. Speaking of outrageously expensive, the room service menu. I mean...really? $42 for breakfast, $3.75 per person delivery fee AND 18% service charge. Uh, when they think up these prices do they blush??? Get some pastries while you're out, Magnolia Bakery, or any of the little shops you see in your travels through the city. The closet was a walk in, with padded hangers, slippers and lots and lots of plastic laundry bags. Two suitcase holders. Just...WOW! A/C was controlled with a thermostat, and we were able to keep the room cool and comfortable, even in a record breaking heat wave. Because this is an older hotel, the bath is not palacial, but it is VERY usable. There is a pedestal sink, but plenty of shelving to store your toiletries on. The shower has very strong water pressure. There are amenities aplenty. Body wash, shampoo, shower-cap, sewing kit, shoe buffer, stuff I haven't seen in years! The tub is rather deep, my husband enjoyed a nice soak after walking to Times Square and back. The staff is great, offering good suggestions for dining in the area (The National). The doormen were friendly and helpful in getting cabs. Everyone was super eager to do whatever it was that needed to be done to make our stay enjoyable. Honestly, we paid $200 for one night for a luxurious hotel in New York, in a great location, with a terrific staff. What more could you ask for?

“As Expected, Good Place” Stayed here 3/2012, booked thru priceline ($65 memphis east). Check in was very fast and smooth, which was appreciated. Room was very large and comfortable with a king bed. Big bathroom, very spacious. Place was clean, AC worked just fine as well. There is no fridge in the room, which was a surprise. Breakfast was good, but I had a problem with payment. They insisted on charging the meal to my room, but for my business expense purposed I need to pay for it on a company card. Their credit card system was not working so they charged it to my room, which I was not happy about. But, breakfast was good. A big turnoff is a large train that is located across the street. It came barreling through at 5am and was very loud and shook the entire room, waking me up. I've stayed at the Hyatt directly next door and did not have this issue so I probably won't stay here again. But that being said, this is a nice place and the value was good.

“The worst Sheraton ever” Being an SPG Platinum member I naturally gravitated to this hotel a short distance from IAH. I arrived and was checked into a room the first had no AC I was moved to another but this room was like the other only with AC but had a moldy smell and definatly did not look the the new Sheraton branding inspite of their multi million renovation . You waited forever for the elevator, the restaurant food was of poor quality best to pass on by this hotel to the brand new hotel a mile away.

“Drive on to the next hotel” Stayed here for one night before flying out of Baltimore - it was late at night and we needed somewhere to go and we were passing here. I would not stay here again. The hotel is out of date and has a really funny smell. Our room was on the top floor and when we eventually struggled up with all our bags we thought our key didn't work. But then we could see the card was being recognised and got the green but the door still wouldn't open. In the end we literally had to push our bodies into the door to make it open. I felt a little uneasy in case of an emergency that the door wouldn't open but we were so tired we didn't bother doing anything about it. On first look the room looked ok and the bathroom looked like it was recently re-done. On closer look the bed sheets were dirty and had hairs that were not ours all over the sheets. The same thing with the towels. Disgusting. Breakfast was as expected, nothing special but enough to get you started for the day. There seems to be loads of guest rooms at this hotel but the car park was empty at night so it seems it has hardly any guests - so no wonder they are charging too much...they have to get the money from somewhere. They have the usual tourist leaflets in lobby but the ones I saw were all out of date from years gone by. I wouldn't stay here again - there are plenty of other hotels around that I'm sure would be better - with no funny smell!

“wish i had had more time to enjoy” I was in and out of boston this week. stayed at the langham. very good service from the moment i was in the door. very comfortable bed and extremely quiet. not the cheapest place on the planet. definitely would return.

“Great hotel” OK, here is the true scoop...The Palomar is a great hotel in a great part of town...I'm not quite sure how it got the number one rating on TA(what happened to Mandaran Oriental or Ritz Carlton?)..but it is certainly a very fine hotel....First, the neighborhood....this is THE place to stay in DC....very nice area with shops and restaurants...fairly quiet..and less than a 5 minute walk to the metro which will take you everywhere..except Georgetown which is a 15 minute walk from the hotel...you can purchase a metro ticket and put $15-20 dollars on it which should last 3-4 days....Now, the hotel...drove in from PA...parking is a little high($42 for 24 hrs), but who wants to search for public parking...very nice reception at the front desk. The standard room(that I got for $141 on Hotwire) was a small queen room...if you upgrade(which we did after becoming a Kimpton member online-it's free and easy)to a king room you will love it!!! Comfortable bed, large room and bathroom and great shower....clean and roomy!!!
