Each nite there is a "happy hour" from 5-6 pm where they serve free wine and sangria..saves on the restaurant bar bill!! There is a nice pool, albeit small to relax in the afternoon! There are so many fun things to do in DC..do go to the Newseum..it is definitely worth it!!! Take advantage of the free Smithsonian museums, of course....I would clearly come back here for a repeat visit...you may want to avoid Georgetown for dinner..I found it overpriced and a bit touristy, but fun to explore!!

“W is for WOW” Okay, so this was my first W experience. I heard so much going in. Good, bad, or indifferent Im well traveled enough to wait and make my own decision. Within 5 minuates I was impressed. I caught an early train and felt guilty asking for an early check in. Hey, this is NYC I get it. But shockingly the front desk wasn't pretenious like I heard but hospitable and gracuious got me in before 11am with no hesiation WOW. You forget sometimes but little things like that really can make someones day. I was able to decompress from a rough night and early morning, take another shower, press my suit, and get ready. I was in town for he Puerto Rican day Parade. I loved everything about it the look, style, & service. The "Whatever Whenever Wish" business model is ground breaking and and a game changer Starwood really figured this thing out. You have a fan for life. My only small ripple was the Concierge. She seemed preoccupied I asked for an asian restaurant with a happy hour. She abruptly mentioned one and when I asked again if they have a happy hour she said "yeah". We go to find $40+ entrees (which is totally okay Im a foodie and value quality but this wasnt the occasion for that) I was embarrased when I asked for the happy hour menu and the bartender said they never had one. It was too late to walk out so we dined anyway. Thankfully the food was delicious but I'd suggest slowing down and pay attention to what the guests asks. We rely on your local expertise to avoid this very thing. Otherwise an amazing introduction.

“Unique Hotel in a Great Neighborhood” As a fan of Kimpton hotels, I was pleased to take advantage of the "Weekend Play Dates" package which amounted to a $129 a night rate (good, but not the best part) and FREE parking (that's the best part) at this hotel. My husband, teenage daughter, and I stayed here July 16-19th and had a very good experience. Our room (two double beds) was a nice size - adequate for three, but would have been crowded with four...very convenient having a separate dressing area outside the bathroom. The beds were very comfortable and the bed linens were of a high quality. One never knew what to expect when coming into the lobby; it was definitely the meeting place for guests. One afternoon we came in to find guests/staff hula-hooping, another time we came in as the dog walkers were taking some of the four-legged guests out for a walk (note - this is a pet-friendly spot...many dogs were there during our stay...fine with us, but maybe not for everyone). Offering popsicles in the afternoon was a nice touch, as was the sangria hour. In addition, they served individual portions of grilled shrimp and oysters during the happy hour. Overall, we were extremely happy here - especially for the price. Our only complaint would be the fact that we were unable to get an Internet connection from our room. The staff was aware of this and offered to help, but unfortunately it could not be corrected during our stay. We didn't have any problem connecting from the lounge, though. We did encounter one front desk employee that just happened to be a little too "hip" to be truly helpful to guests; she acted as if any question or request was just "below" her to have to deal with. All the other staff members were truly outstanding - more than willing to help and always had a smile for each guest, so we won't hold that one individual's attitude against the hotel. Lots of great dining in the area - we enjoyed Lauriol Plaza, Pizzaria Paradiso, Luna Grill, and for a special evening - The Iron Gate across the street (lovely intimate dining beneath a pergola lit with tiny lights). Enjoy!

“The only thing that saves this property is Alizee Restaurant” I stayed at this property as part of a New Years Eve package that included a 5-course dinner at Alizee and $59.00 for a king size suite. The dinner and service at Alizee was impeccable as was the case when we dined there for Thanskgiving. However, the Doubletree check-in service left much to be desired. The gentleman who checked us in was unimpressive and we simply felt unwelcomed. The room was acceptable, but we were disappoined that the king size suite did not contain a refrigerator (as is custom in all of the Hilton King suites I've stayed). On New Year's Day we awoke to barely have hot water to shower and used it as an opportunity to share a shower. I reviewed my bill to find I was charged $24.99 for valet service that was included as a part of the package. This was removed from my bill, again by a staff member who again was unfriendly and seemed bothered by my request to have the charge removed. As a Hilton Honors Status Member, not a property I would ever recommend.

“Very Nice” We were stuck in Charlotte during the blizzard and stayed at the Hilton Executive Park on Feb 16 and 17, 2003.I thought it was a very nice hotel with a comfortable bed, large bathroom and internet service in the room for 10 dollars a day.The location of the hotel is not very desirable unless you have a rental car but the hotel interior had much more character than I expected for something in an office park type setting.

“Classic Palomar” We chose The Palomar for a one night stay at the back end of a trip to California because it was a new hotel, in a convenient area, and we enjoyed a stay at another Kimpton property earlier this year. Overall we enjoyed our time here and it offered good value, but we would not want to stay at this hotel for more then a night or two. If you have stayed at a Kimpton hotel, you know the room décor is always unique and a little different. At this location, we did not love the look of the room. The colors were mostly black and brown, with some splashes of brighter colors thrown in. There were too many patterns in the room including a snake skin pattern on the face of the dresser. The room came across as too dark and busy, and not very relaxing. As others have mentioned, the room was a little small as was the bathroom. South facing rooms have nice views, North facing rooms overlook busy Wilshire Boulevard and condos. I believe the hotel used to be a Doubletree before Kimpton took over, and was not built from the ground up as a new hotel. The rest of the hotel is pretty nice with a good boutique hotel feel with a little clublike atmosphere thrown in. We did not use the restaurant but we did check out the pool. The pool is decent size but the pool area is long, narrow, and lined up very close to the building. There are two attractive conversation areas but only five or six oversized lounge chairs for sitting in the sun at a hotel with over 200 rooms. We were at the pool late in the afternoon so some were available, but this is not a hotel for very many people to hang out by the pool. Overall The Palomar is a nice hotel with a central location. The staff was also very friendly and the happy hour is a nice touch rarely found at big city hotels. But not everyone will like the rooms and in a great weather city like LA, the pool setup is not large enough for a hotel this size.

“A+ for Affinia” We stayed here on NYE & enjoyed every minute. Clean, modern room - very spacious. Aveda bath products. Friendly, very accommodating staff. Comfortable beds. Love the fact that you can make special requests for pillows, rooms, views, etc. - all of ours were honored. (Go to the hotel website to customize your stay.) We had a great view & even a partial view of the NYE fireworks over the lake! Valet parking is $48/day, but you can park yourself in the garage across the street for $38/day. Hotel is next to a hospital, so if you're a light sleeper bring ear plugs! Only one fully operating elevator, but staff was extremely helpful in finding alternate elevators to get you up or down. Our only complaint was the clock radio which had background noise when trying to play an iPod - we asked for a different radio & the second one they brought had same problem. Otherwise, nothing to complain about - we'd go back in a heartbeat! (Oh yeah, great location one block off Michigan Ave. Also a Gino's Pizza right next door.)

“Hyatt Harborside Boston Logans Airport” I was very impressed with the comfort of the rooms. The location is always great. There is a perfect view of the Boston Harbor from my room. The shuttle service to and from the airport was very prompt and the drivers were very accomodating.

“Don't be fooled by the pictures” I would have given this hotel a poor review if I were anywhere else besides New York. The rooms are small which is to be expected but the walls are paper thin. I've stayed at the Renaissance Hotel 57 in Midtown and it had more ambience. The Marriott Marquis has larger rooms with less noise above the 30th floor. But the Renaissance Times Square is my favorite! I checked in at 3am and I wasn't offered a platinum arrival gift. I'd have forgiven the desk clerk if the other people in my party were also forgotten, but I was the only one. There was a half filled glass on my desk and an ice bucket full of water. The shower had an open bottle of hair conditioner and a used bar of soap. One robe was neatly tied but the other was thrown over the bathroom hook like it'd been worn. I would have switched rooms but I was tired from traveling. I wouldn't stay here again.

“Great For the Short Term” We stayed here overnight during the Christmas holidays. Very convenient to the freeways, but there's noise from the passing cars. Ask for a room away from the traffic. The breakfast buffet was more than adequate. All in all, a fine place for the short term. Rooms were basic but clean. Adequate free parking and a gas station next door.

“Rasch im Zentrum, rasch wieder weg” Hier kommt man vom Flughafen rasch an und auch rasch wieder weg und wer sich nicht fürchtet, durch leicht verfallene Innenstädte ind en USA zu laufen, ist auch relativ gut zu Fuss rasch im Zentrum. Die Stadtseite ist indes ziemlich laut, um die Ecke ist ein Feuerwehrdepot und die müssen halt auch mal nachts raus. Internet-Kosten sind hoch (20 USD/Tag), Zimmerservice okay, aber hat auch einr relativ schlechtes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis. Wer dieses Hotel bucht, sollte ein Zimmer zum Meer raus bestellen und nur auswärts essen (z.B. im Steakhouse "Houston", Faneuil Sq.).

“Over-rated” I have only stayed at this hotel when I have purchase the room for a bargain price on Priceline. This is NOT a 4-star hotel. It is, at best, a 3-star that happens to be in a great location. If you stay here be prepared for a massive, impersonal hotel populated by conference and convention goers. On my recent 2-night visit they were overbooked (good for them, must be the only hotel in the land in that position these days) and they offered to comp me for 1 night at the Swisshotel next door. I would have jumped at the chance, but my schedule was hectic and I couldn't afford the time to unpack and repack and schlep back to the Hyatt for the second night. Because of their over-sold position, they had to put me in a smoking room (I didn't realize those still existed) for the first night. It reeked. My clothes still smell. As compensation they gave me a $100 Hyatt gift card which is probably fair, but all things considered, I would have much preferred to have gotten the non-smoking room I booked, and for which I prepaid, for 2 nights. Because it is discounted so heavily on Priceline, I will probably wind up here again, but I hope not.

“Great big rooms in a tremendous location - will be a gem once they work out the kinks” My family recently stayed at the Comfort Suites on Michigan Avenue in Chicago and had a great time. I can start out, though, with what it’s not. It’s not a 4 star hotel. We stayed at the Swissotel around the corner during our last visit to see our family and there’s definitely a difference in service, amenities, etc. So if you’re the type who has to have fine linens, fluffy towels (though these were pretty impressive for this class of hotel), turndown service and chocolates on your pillow, skip this hotel. But...if you’re traveling with family and looking for a great value and unbelievable space, in an unbeatable location - this is your hotel. We also got an incredible Travelzoo special grand opening rate which made it even better. We had a queen suite with a separate bedroom (though no door) including a flat screen TV. There was also a living room with a pullout sofa, chair, desk, dresser and another flat screen TV. There was a full kitchen: refrigerator, stove, microwave, toaster, dishwasher - the works. The kitchen was outfitted with basic pots, pans, dishes, glassware, flatware, etc. You could actually eat there, though there’s no table and chairs, there is a counter with two stools. Best of all, there’s an in-suite washer and dryer, which was such a novelty that we did laundry every night. We were on a high floor and had a spectacular view up Michigan Avenue over the river; what a bonus. We were there over Memorial Day weekend, just a couple of weeks after they opened, and they were still working out a few kinks, but the front desk staff was so nice and helpful and really tried to fix things as they came up. When we arrived , our room safe in the closet wasn’t working and it was fixed within half an hour. Housekeeping was spotty at best - they didn’t show up until we were back in the room at 4pm the first afternoon and wound up cleaning around us while we got ready to go to dinner. On our last day, they randomly didn’t leave any washcloths. Breakfast and internet access (wired) are included in your room rate, which is nice. But on Memorial Day, we showed up at breakfast at 8:45 and all the hot food was gone already - and breakfast was supposed to go until 10am. All the furniture in the rooms is brand new, which is nice, but clearly everything wasn’t redone. There was a “weird alien handprint” (as dubbed by the 6 year old) on refrigerator - some kind of disturbing red stain. The bathtub had a big sticker covering discoloration in the tub - we decided to steer away from baths for the weekend. There was a mysterious locked closet in the suite which turned out to be storage for towels, as we discovered when we wound up being there with the cleaning crew on Saturday. Though the guy who appeared to be the lead on the crew assured us they wouldn’t come in and out for towels, another woman on the crew let herself in to get some later on. A little unsettling to have your room used for storage, but we put up the Do Not Disturb sign anytime we were actually there and tried not to think about it too much. Parking is a big, big problem in downtown Chicago these days, and the Comfort Suites does not, at this time, have a contract for a garage - though they tell us they are working on it and the website says they do. After spending a fortune on parking the first day, we found an outside lot around the corner between the Corner Bakery and the Club Suites hotel. If you don’t mind outdoor parking, it’s a deal at $17 for 12 hours ($12 on the weekends). Or don’t rent/bring a car at all and get yourself a CTA pass a block south at the CVS drugstore. There’s a bus stop that’ll get you just about anywhere right in front of the hotel. There’s also a Walgreens and a Chipotle Mexican restaurant (one of our favorites) on the same block. There’s a very basic workout room with a bike, treadmill, elliptical machine, and weight machine, as well as towels. This is also the same room where the vending machines are. There’s no TV yet though they promise there will be. On the whole, we'd go back again - even with the bumps. Tips on sightseeing: we got to see some amazing Chicago museums, including the new Oceanarium at Shedd Aquarium, the Harry Potter exhibit at the Museum of Science and Industry, and the new modern wing at the Art Institute. All are not to be missed. We also enjoyed a quick visit to the Lincoln Park Zoo (always a favorite) and the Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum in Lincoln Park - both great for families with kids.

“Great location, good hotel overall” We stayed here for five nights and felt very happy with our choice. We loved the fact that it is a little out of the main centre (but within easy walking distance) and right on the bay. We upgraded by 20 dollars per day for a better view over the bay and city skyline. Nice room, great view, clean and modern with comfy bed. Didn't use the pool but it looked lovely. The only let down is the service which is patchy. At the bar in Vela the staff were disinterested, gum chewing and unprofessional. The staff in the restaurant were pleasant enough but there were not enough of them. This was a pity as the food was good and deserved service to match. This was also true of the concierge service which was very hit and miss. Check your bill. We had a "fall fun" package which included 35 dollars per day spend which had not been taken off our bill. Take a Flagship harbour cruise early on in your stay as it is well worthwhile and is a pleasant way to get orientated. Also do visit USS Midway for a fantastic day out. Overall a great stay in San Diego.

“Good value” Stayed here during a convention in NYC for three nights. Basic hotel but staff very friendly and helpful. Rooms are basic but if you are nOt spending much time in them it's fine. Mine was very noisy.

“Worst Service and No internet” Hotel has potential, but the front desk staff has no clue what hospitality is. They were overall rude (Not only to me, but t oothers who had similar problems with their room/internet connection) Don't think they staff meant to be rude. They are just not qualified to be in charge of a front desk. Alsom, there was a language barrier which make things weven more difficult. Hotel grounds look like a constriuction zone. Forget about the internet which is very spotty and only worked for 2 hours during my entire stay. Staff was clueless as to how to fix, even though all they neeeded to do was tro turn the modem on and off. I ended up moving to the Super 8 next door. Less hassles.

“WTCから近く便利、新しく部屋が広い ” <立地> ニューアークからのPATH TRAINの終点のWTC(World Trade Center)駅からハドソン川方面に向かって、工事現場脇の歩道を抜け、広い通りを渡る歩道橋を渡るとすぐです。徒歩5~6分です。地下鉄のWTC駅も10分はかからないので、ニューアーク空港からのアクセスや地下鉄で観光する方にも便利です。 建物は、直接ハドソン川に面してはいませんが、川の方角は前に公園があるため、運よくリバービューの部屋になれば、景色は良いと思われます。朝の川沿いの遊歩道の散歩はとても気持ちが良いです。 ホテルの建物のの1Fには、Pick a Bagle(ベーグル店)、Shake Shack(ハンバーガー店)があり、特にShake Shackはとてもおいしいのでお勧めです。 <部屋> ヒルトンポイントで、1 KING SUPERIOR SUITE に泊まりました。ニューヨークのホテルとしては格段に広く、入ってすぐにリビングスペースがあり、まん中に洗面台とトイレ、独立したシャワーブース、デスクコーナーとミニバー。奥に寝室がある細長いレイアウトになっています。ミニバーに小さな流しがあるのが便利。バスタブはありませんでした。ラグジュアリールーム以上だとバスタブがあるようです。キッチンもありませんでした。明るいブラウン系の内装で、オープンから日がたっていないので、大変綺麗でした。アメリカのホテルでは多いですが、ベッドが少々やわらかすぎたのが残念。南側の部屋だったので残念ながらリバービューではありませんでした。隣室との間の防音は良いですが、扉の防音性が低いためか、夜中にロビーで大きい声を出しているお客さんの声が、部屋の中まで良く聞こえました。 <朝食> 朝食付のプランの場合は、2Fのレストランで食べるることになりますが、この朝食メニューが少々問題です。コーヒー、紅茶、オレンジジュースと、以下の5種類のメニューから1つ選ぶことになります。1Pastries(マフィン・クロワッサン・デニッシュ) または、田舎パンのトースト 2ギリシャヨーグルト+シリアル・フルーツ 3季節のフルーツ+キャロットパン、4生ハムメロン+ルッコラ、5オートミールと温かいフルーツコンポート。 滞在中123を食べましたが、1の田舎パンを選ぶと、薄いトースト4枚だけでボリュームが全然ありません。アメリカではありえないサイズです。1のマフィン等のセットか、フルーツ好きなら3がお勧め。ヨーグルト好きなら2も良いと思いますが、いずれにしても、ビュッフェの朝食に慣れた方には、さびしい限りの内容です。 <サービス> フロントやレストランのスタッフは、きちんとした対応で、さすがはコンラッドと思わせる丁寧な応対をしてくれます。ただし、日本語ができるスタッフはいなさそうでした。 朝食とドアの防音、ベッドの柔らかさに少々難ありですが、部屋の広さとスタッフの丁寧さ、立地の良さでお勧めできます。

“No smiles at the front desk. Lobby, lounge public area is nice. But rooms need major update!!!” No frill front desk girls. No smiles, both gals at check in and out. Gee.. I thought I did something wrong. As a diamond hhonors, it is hard to see front desk personnels so cold and unfriendly. I was about to say to them..... "it doesn't hurt to smile, u work at a hospitality job, and guests need to feel welcome." so, with that said, minus one star. Parking:$14 a night which is ok... Garage a little hard to find, but once park, ash locate the elevator to lobby. Lobby area:it is nice and big. Very clean and expensive looking. Looks modern. Nice business hotel. The room: okay upgrade to regular king room on executive floor. Nothing special. The room needs some major renovations, feels like in the 80s. 90s. Minus one star. Rooms are comfy but just old. The executive lounge: it is very nice view. Breakfast is good. Good choices. Overall... It is an okay stay. Not so welcoming and a bit disappointed...at the front desk gals that set the tone of my stay. No frills. Worth mentioning: the housekeepers are extremely friendly and happy. They deserve a mention here. They do start cleaning around 10am. Thank u housekeepers... Much better than front desk gals.

“Nice Staff, Clean Rooms” Bathrooms very clean, room ok (rugs old), bed ok comfort, housekeeping staff is super nice, front desk peeps ok. I'm not sure why this hotel has gotten such high marks bc it's just ok. My room was very small, but, wasn't bad. Nothing to write home about but not terrible either. It was inexpensive and clean, and that was enough. The free wireless was SUPER slow.

“Best Hampton Inn I've Stayed At!” Hampton is my most stayed at location and I've stayed at a lot of them. This one is hands down the cleanest, visually attractive (Inside), and has the friendliest staff in my 10+ years of business travel.

“Not the best” I am usually ok with M6 properties, but this one is rundown and in a dead area of town. I stayed here a few years ago when the stores were open and it was good. But now, I'd go on down the road.

“Location” If you wish to travel on public transportation bus subway or taxi this hotel is perfect. The hotel is very nice and clean the hotel staff are helpful and the dining on site is very good. We had no problems with the room of hotel would stay again. TIP buy a metrocard for bus and subway travel

“I would go back!” Fabulous hotel. Close to everything. Amazing shuttle service that takes you to Union Station. Reasonable, good breakfast and laundry rooms, and the staff is incredible. They even had a barbecue for Priority Club members and David Cook did a wonderful job. Brian helped us quite a bit with our directions and he and David and the rest of the staff were just great. Location is fine. I would stay there again if in D.C.

“Great location to mix business and pleasure” Location - The location of the London is great if you are in NYC for business (if your business is in upper Manhattan) but also want to mix pleasure and/or have someone traveling with you that is not on business. You are close to the business center of upper Manhattan while just a few blocks from the theater district, Central Park, and shopping of 5th Ave and Park Ave. Also a block or so from MOMA and easy walk to the Met. Room - The room was large, with a good size bedroom and a very nice sitting room. Comfortable bed and pillows. The room was very clean and housekeeping was friendly. Two downsides were 1) the bathroom, very small, only room for one with a single vanity. My wife has stayed here before hand said she had rooms with large bathrooms and double vanities, so if there are two of you, you may want to check. And 2) smell of smoke. To cater to foreign visitors, there are two smoking floors. We could smell smoke coming through the air vent. This is an issue at any hotel that allows smoking. Management said it was impossible to smell the smoke, not true, I know what I smell. Either it was from the smoking floor or someone was smoking in a non smoking room. Service - The service of the hotel from bell hops, valets, room service, and desk were all great. Check in and check out was quick, and we were able to get a cab quickly when needed. Restaurants - We at at Maze (the casual side of Gordon Ramseys) and the food was excellent. Service was horrible and we walked out a second night because we could not get waited on. But that is for a different review, not a reflection of the hotel. I do recommend the London. The smoke and small bath rate it a four instead of five star review.

“Nice, but it was a free night...different opinion if I paid” Let me set up the scene for this conference trip. 4 hotels, 4 nights. Everything that could cause hotels to be booked (U2 concert) was going on in Chicago...and several idiot wedding parties here at the hotel mid September. Our night at the W City Center was a Sunday. This area of town is DEAD after dark, and almost uncomfortably so when walking about. There was very little to do, so we went out on the town. A little back story: I have stayed in countless W Hotels. I have gotten past the wannabees and glamouratti set, the sex dungeon and Abercrombie store decors, and I just like the general service level at the W. So continuing on, the hotel graciously upgraded us to a Spectacular SMOKING room 1904, which was nice. The room was big enough and had enough windows to be acceptable for smoking. I would not have paid the rack rate of $429 for this Ikea furnish spartan room, but it was great for free. The room was spacious and comfortable. The beds were standard W fare. The Whenever/Whatever accommodated some odd requests we had, although one of my friends was mildly offended that he kept being referred to as ma'am on the phone. The lobby is a beautiful beaux arte building with the W style. The bar was small...I mean small. The champagne still tasted the same, but there wasn't even nightlife in the lobby...which is my usual quip with W, but this place was at 100% and still dead. Everyone leaves the hotel, as there isn't anything around...well at McDonalds and the ever present Charbucks on the street corner. My big complaint, lame as it is, HBO wouldn't come on, and we wanted to watch the season finale of True Blood. We used the heck out of the Acura Experience! It is free up to 3 miles for hotel guests, I would recommend tipping the drivers. Arthur was super. Likes: big room, SMOKING big room, better lobby coffee than Charbucks (if it is from there, don't tell me), Acura experience, and the staff. Dislikes: I would have found things to complain about for rack price, location, location, and the out of place guests that should have been at the HoJo (not the hotel's fault), paying for INTERNET

“All about the Belvedere” As a travel agent I always get the low down on the best places to stay and usually I recommend this place to my clients. I love the location being only a short walk from Broadway/Times Sq/Central Park. For NYC it really is all about the location. Rooms are clean and comfy, as are the lovely beds and fluffy pillows! I have stayed here many times and find this hotel always used to pride itself on service. I feel the standards are slipping but I really hope they get it back on track. I really would recommend for value and location, as you shouldnt be spending all your time in the hotel room!!

“AMAZING!” So this is one of those hidden gems that you are loathe to write about because you don't want everyone else in the world discovering it (so you won't be able to get in the next time you want to go back!). With only a limited amount of rooms, you get the charm of a staff at a country inn (that remembers who you are and what you're up to) and couple it with the modern asethetic and service of a high-end big city hotel. We found each and every employee helpful from the moment we arrived (several hours before check in and were immediately given an upgraded room since ours was not yet available) until we checked out and the doorman asked my daughter how she had enjoyed her trip to the zoo (three days before). Every time we needed something from late turn down service (they called to check on timing since we had not called them at 9:30pm) to a restaurant recommendation, we were not transferred or told to "talk to someone else" as often happens at large, highly rated hotels. So aside from the terrific service experience and unbeatable midtown location, for me, the best part of the rooms themselves had to be the showers...this was the BEST hotel shower that I have experienced in a hotel. In addition the nicely pressured rain shower, the shampoo and conditioner and soap were full size so you did not run out and have to call for more after one person showered. The evening amenity at turn down was a glass bottle of Saratoga water and a Lindt chocolate...just the perfect thing to complement a lovely stay. We will be back to this hotel each and every time we are in NYC.

“Great Location” We stayed at the Westin recently for a girls weekend. It is in a great location and convenient to all the downtown activities and riverwalk. We chose to park with the valet at $30 a day. Although more expensive than I would like to have paid, it was spring break weekend and traffic was very heavy and parking was crowded. We never used the car again, so it worked well for us. The hotel is beautiful, the staff were very friendly and extremely helpful. Our a/c didn't work the first night so we were moved to another room the next day. The bell hop John was a great help in getting our things moved and even provided us with drink vouchers to make up for the inconvenience. Every time we left the hotel one of the staff would ask if we needed directions. The only complaint I would have is that the pillows were too soft and lumpy and the bed was not comfortable for me. The heavenly bed killed my back, but that's just me. Housekeeping didn't restock the coffee or cups, but I was able to get what we needed eventually. There were several conferences going on and Spring Break, so I am sure they were swamped. Overall, I would recommend the hotel and would go back.

“Ideal location” I went to grad school in Boston, so I knew I wanted a hotel near a T stop so I could easily get to and from the airport. This hotel in a traditional/old building with contemporary design is just a few steps from the Copley T stop and right across the street from the Boston Public Library. You can walk to the Public Gardens, shopping, and much more. Staff were friendly and helpful, the room was clean, and they had jazz playing on the audio/video system when I walked into the room. (How did they know?) I reserved the cheapest/smallest room for the last night of a business trip but got a slight upgrade when I arrived. Rooms are compact but perfectly adequate unless the visitors only are comfortable in Midwest Best Westerns. There's a small desk and chair, but it's probably not the most comfortable if you're trying to work all day from your hotel room--but then, why would you? Take your computer to the library, a bar, the park, anywhere.

“All round nice hotel..” I got this hotel through priceline.com and paid $70 a night. This was a great deal because it was priced at $199 - $299 on the website. Hotel was clean and modern enough. Located in the heart of downtown Boston and sandwiched between Chinatown and the Theatre district, the Hyatt provides easy access point to these two locations as well as to the 'T'. The hotel room was smaller than the Hyatt's I have lived in but the room was nice. The bathroom was smaller than I was used to as well. So, with two people wanting to use the bathroom at once could be quite cramped. However, room was clean, had a coffee making machine, a TV with all channels working (not a flat screen) and equipped with Nintendo 64 gaming (at $7.00 an hour!). Also had a bar, iron and board and a robe to use (if going to use the swimming pool). Decor was slightly 80's style mixed in with the new furniture. One thing to be aware of is the LOUD banging of the doors! Around 9-11pm, 7-9am, you will be woken up for sure by other people so bring some ear-plugs if you are a light sleeper! I got a room on the 16th floor and got nice views around the city. Staff were super friendly at the check-in desk. Couldn't say the same for some of the concierge/bell boys. Other slight criticism is the funny layout of the hotel. You enter the side of the hotel and go down a few steps to the Lower Lobby only to have to go up 3 floors to get to reception and to get to your room. Overall, a nice hotel although slightly weird in design and layout. Great value for money (for what I paid) and location for a great night out in the town. Recommended!

“Nice, Clean, Contemporary, Close to UCLA & Beverly Hills” As a preface, I travel to a limited degree to review rock concerts, and have begun to include hotel and resort reviews as well, which I am republishing here is modified form. This review is for the Hotel Palomar Los Angeles, a Kimpton Hotel in Westwood, California, during a trip to attend a charity event at UCLA. Room Type/Class: Deluxe King Room Date: August 3-4, 2011 Overall Rating: 4/5 With this stay, I was looking to stay somewhere newer, clean, and contemporary, that was within reasonable walking distance to UCLA for a concert and not too far from Beverly Hills (via car) where I also had a meeting scheduled. Based on reviews on Trip Advisor, I selected Hotel Palomar, as it seemed to fit my criteria. The property is easy enough to find, and they offer valet parking. Check-in was smooth. The hotel is very hip and modern in appearance. The room had more style than most hotels (how many places have you stayed that try to pull off some leopard print?). The room was of a decent size with bed, dresser, and desk, and the bathroom was consistent with the decor throughout. My room faced out toward UCLA with related views. UCLA is walking distance, but it is quite a walk - probably better served driving. It was a short stay, so I don't really have any additional thoughts to share. It was a nice, clean hotel, and I'd stay there again.

“Great Location - Spacious room” 3 blocks from Central Park, 1 block from the Metro, around the block from Carnegie Hall, 15 minute walk to Times Square -- all these add up to one good reason I will re-book (stayed 8 days) when I return next summer. Do Expedia or Priceline otherwise, you'll be paying a lot more if you go through the hotel...unless you do the 90 minute timeshare presentation, in which case the discounted price is about the same. Manhattan Club is far enough away from the maddening crush of tourists but close enough to everything. Area is safe. The kitchenette in our one bedroom was great to have -- there is a supermarket 2 blocks away and of course lots of restaurants all around. Skip the continental breakfast on the 26th floor. It's overpriced. Room was spacious enough for 4 people. The pullout sofa bed in LR was comfortable. Service was good. Asked for 6 extra pillows (3 of us have back problems) -- housekeeping balked for a second then sent them up within 2 minutes. Our room, 2513, was 104 degrees when we arrived at 10:30 pm. Called down for service and an engineer was up in 2 minutes. Meanwhile housekeeping sent up a fan and two bottles of chilled water with a note of apology for the inconvenience. Took a while to cool down but it finally did. Stingy with the coffee -- asked for extra packets and they wanted to charge us. Complained to Asst. Mgr -- left voice mail -- never got a call back. Leaving really early? Go around the corner and grab a cab. Don't let the bellman tell you there may not be any cabs at 4am and convince you to pay $50 for a private car to LaGuardia. This is NY after all! Take advantage of Concierge service if you're looking for hard-to-get Broadway show tickets. They have a runner ($25 service fee per tix) who will grab tickets for you at group rate, no higher than mezzanine seats...so you're not sitting in nosebleed seats. They call you on your cell if they were able to get them and you pick them up at the Concierge desk at end of day. No waiting around. You end up paying full price with the service fee but it beats spending your entire morning in the heat, lining up for cheap tickets at Time Square. Forget the tour buses. Grab a guidebook and walk. Much more interesting and free! Friends took us to Spice Market--trendy, with excellent cuisine, in the Chelsea Area. Take the bike guided tour in Central Park if you've never been there. We negotiated our fee and got an hour's ride for their usual 30 minute tour (must've been a slow day--did it on a weekday, later in the p.m.).

“A Fine Stay for One Day in DC” I've read a few reviews and while I had some similar experiences with poor lighting, and loud music in the lobby bar at night, we had a gigantic room. The person at the desk asked us if we wanted a view or size, and we voted for size. We were given room 939, with two queen size beds and a chair and chaise. This was a great room but it had not view, just some decoration on the windows to block out the back of the hotel. We had excellent door service, our room was clean and we had those nice Bliss amenities. The floor was quiet and I slept well on the W's modern platform bed. The lighting for us was a somewhat low and we had to use all the lamps to see what was in the room. There are these odd colored led lights over the beds and they gave off a strange tint to the room. We went to dinner on Thursday night and passed through the lobby bar that was filled with young professionals having a merry time. Off course there was that pulsing music that hip hotels seem to like. After dinner we went upstairs and saw the POV lounge which was only busy on the bar side of the room.The downstairs group was already gone so it was quiet when we walked in. Over all it was a good stay and the location was perfect for our touristy activities. I want to add that we are SPG gold members so they gave us free bottles of Fuji water which we appreciated and the large room. Ws are very modern hotels and they tend to attract younger "cooler" people but that does not mean that two seniors could not enjoy their stay. If you want a more tailored, traditional look then the Willard (across the street) might fit you better.

“Great hotel in a great location.” The Sofitel Chicago is a great hotel .... clean, upscale, etc. We stayed just one night in February, and it is in a perfect location for shopping on both Rush St. and Michigan Ave. The room is a nice size with good views, a large bathroom and comfy bed. There is nothing to complain about at this hotel. And, we asked for a late check out, and they allowed us to stay two extra hours with no extra fees. We also requested an early check in, and it was honored with no problem.

“Shhhhh . . . don't tell, but this is a GREAT place to stay!” After traveling to SD for years and never quite finding the best location to stay for a reasonable price, we finally found the Courtyard by Marriott - Liberty Station. The room was a typical "Courtyard" room with the basic amenities and reliable daily maid service. The pool was a great place to "hang" since it was quiet and not crowded at all. There was a park across the street with plenty of space for the children to play basketball and throw the football. With the small in-room fridge we were able to store all of the fruit and water from the nearby Trader Joes. Mostly, we were impressed with the great location . . . we had easy access to everything! From the SD Zoo to Brockton Villa in La Jolla . . . we had no issues with getting to places without a lot of traffic. As mentioned in other reviews, we were a little concerned that there would be airplane noise since the hotel is "in the flight pattern," however, the A/C makes the room a quiet oasis. And, let's face it . . . one doesn't travel to SD to sit in a hotel room . . . the outdoors awaits!

“Good but with a few issues...” Convenient to the airport. Very Very short walk from terminals. Nice rooom, refurbished. Nice public spaces. Awesome gym with a big weight area including free weights and machines. Couple of issues. First was the elevators. They have about eight elevators but only three were working when I was there. Long waits which sucked. Another issue was being overcharged for breakfast. There were four of us at breakfast. it was a business meeting where two people ordered the buffet one only had coffee, and one had coffee and asked for an english muffin. The person did not get the muffin from the buffet but ordered it off the menu. The bill camae and it was 85 dollars. The waiter had charged everyone for the buffett even though only two people ate off the buffet. The waiter did not handle the inquiry very well and it is my opinion that he deliberately charged us for four buffet's as this was a bsuiness metting and we were all very involved with discussion. I think he thought we wouldn't bat an eye at the bill. Besides this, the hotel is OK.

“Excellent Motel with a great location” I would recommend Jerry's Motel to any person considering visiting Los Angeles. The motel is small with ample parking and a great location. You have access to the all major freeways within minutes. It is simple, quiet and very clean. The owners are very accommodating and knowledgeable. If I go to LA again I will stay there in a heartbeat.

“Clean and convenient” Stayed here for 4 nights. So convenient for getting around LA using the Metro system. Used a 4 day pass which cost $5 per day and we went everywhere. Also used the Dodger Express to get to the game and the LAX flyaway bus. The hotel is clean and the rooms large. Yes the soap is marginal but its such a minor thing. We found a wonderful ribs place just up the road, also ate at Phillipes and a couple of chinese restaurants all within two blocks. Only negative is the wifi. Yes they have it but it only works in the lift area and in the foyer and breakfast room. I initially asked to be moved to a room where wifi worked but after some lengthy discussion with an inscrutable chinese guy behind the desk he admitted that the router was not strong enough to get to the rooms. That was the only frustration in a great stay.

“Not Grand” Stayed here a while ago, but forgot to put up a review at the time. Don't come here expecting the same standard as say, a Grand Hyatt in Asia (e.g. Shanghai or Hong Kong), because it's completely different. Apart from the size of the place, there's nothing grand about it. Tried to check in at 3pm, but the room wasn't ready, so had to hang around one of the cafes in Grand Central. When we got to the actual room, it was a bit underwhelming - dingy. The walls, as many other people have said, are paper thin. Hard to sleep if your neighbour is watching TV. The bathroom was a decent sixe, but there wasn't much hot water on the first night I was there. Service alright, but nothing special. Overall, give it a miss. it seems unfortunate that this is the only Hyatt offering in New York City. Yes, New York hotels are expensive, and what do you expect $350 per night etc, but this place is poor.

“Great Location BUT....” Even though I was on the 23rd floor I heard the sounds from the street which included car horns, ambulances, and people laughing! I can't imagine what the lower floors might hear! The condos are small, no counter space in the bathroom, bedroom small. But, if you don't mind a little closeness, you can't beat the location - near all tourist attractions and commerce. The architecture alone makes it worth staying here for a very unusual experience.

“A Refurb that Works” I travel to Jax regularly both for family visits and business. I had purposely avoided this hotel over the years because of reputation based on opinions of business associates and it seemed to have fallen on hard times like other older Holiday Inn properties. Recently this hotel underwent a major overhaul and instead of the usual nice lobby but tacky rooms, this one works. We stayed here because it was a Priority Club Point Stretcher hotel and we were please that we did. Beds were comfortable; rooms were quiet; and the pool and jacuzzi were nice and clean. At any rate below $80 this is a nice place to stay. Only real negative was absolutely no view ... either interstate or gas station. Staff was attentive, knowledgeable and helpful.

“Nice hotel in the UW area!” I had a great first impression of University Inn, where I stayed for one night. I called to ask about transportation from the airport and the receptionist was very friendly and helpful with directions. She described exactly how to get from Sea-Tac to the Westlake Center where the complementary hotel shuttle will pick up guests. I had no problems getting to the hotel. Indeed, everyone at the hotel was very friendly and helpful. I was assigned to a room on the fourth floor in the north wing. There are two separate wings, which are only connected on the ground floor, so be sure to get on the correct elevator. The north wing is older, but the property is lovingly cared for. Everything was clean and comfortable, just not spanking new. My room had a great balcony overlooking the parking lot. My one issue was that the complementary wireless internet connection was not working well in my room, which admittedly was in the furthest corner of the hotel. I was also using a very old laptop. I didn’t mind working in the breakfast area downstairs, where it worked fine. There is also a computer with a printer for use in the lobby. Breakfast consisted of the usual continental breakfast offerings. There are delicious mini pineapple cupcakes offered as snacks between 4-7pm. In short, I had a pleasant stay at this retro chic hotel in the University district. It was convenient for my purposes in town. The UW campus shuttle stops across the street, and the main drag offers many dining options. However, someone I met on the bus told that the Watertown hotel one block away, also managed by Pineapple Hospitality, is much nicer, so it might sense to compare the rates.

“Last Minute reservation - Last Stay” I was forced to make a last minute reservation on a busy weekday in San Franicsco. The location seemed ideal for me but every thing else was subpar, Evan for one night the hotel had an uncomfortable feel. From a shappy lobby, creeking elevator, to a very basic room with one hard chair and a worn bed the experience will not be repeated, Sure it was cheap for San Francisco but you got what you paid for so I can't complain too loudly. I will chalk this one up to desperation.

“Great Hotel, I'll be back!” I was very impressed with this hotel's location, service, and amenities. I used Radisson's new online express check-in service and thought it was great. Check in LITERALLY took about five seconds (even quicker than Hilton's kiosks and you get to talk to a real person!). Valet service was quick and easy. I was on an upper floor overlooking the lake and the view was beautiful. The outdoor pool looked very inviting as well. The hotel is located right downtown, but not too near all of the partying and noise. There are lots of places to eat and shop at within walking distance. The entire staff was friendly and helpful the whole time. I had a very nice suite with good furnishings and the BEST bed I have EVER slept on. All Radissons are installing the sleep-number beds in their rooms, and the experience is pure luxury and comfort. I actually used the high-speed internet in my room to visit the company's website to look at a sleep-number bed for my own home. WOW! All of the other amenities were also present (coffeemaker, iron/board, etc.). There is a TGI Friday's in the hotel open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. I had lunch there one day and the food was really good. The hotel was pretty busy during my stay, but never too noisy because of the clinetale staying there. I would definately stay in this hotel again, and look for Radissons in the future. Seems like they are going through some very positive changes!

“Good Base for a Tourist Trip to Boston” We booked this hotel as we were looking for a comfortable and convenient base for our trip to Boston. It is not right in the centre, but the Silver Line T (an express bus) has a stop just by the hotel and this is a very quick way of getting to South Station - it takes just a few minutes and generally runs every few minutes. From there the T underground system gets you to most parts of the city very quickly. There is also a Silver Line T link to the airport which takes about 10 minutes and costs just $2 - a cheap way to travel if you do not have too much luggage. The hotel itself is what you would expect from a luxury, recently built establishment. The public areas are extensive with a very large bar area and restaurant. Staff are helpful and friendly. The rooms are large and our bathroom had a very large walk in shower rather than a tub. There is valet parking, at quite an expense, and also a car park nearby which was considerably cheaper. In the hotel restaurant, the tasting menu is good value and very good food. They really put an effort into it. Worth taking the flight of wines with it for a fun experience. So overall, no problems with this hotel at all, and provided you can cope with not being right in the centre it works just fine.

“Hope the internal construction is finished!” Never sure what to expect from American hotels..... room was fine (club level), but the lounge was totally ridiculously overcrowded thanks to the hotels internal construction happening ie no bar or proper restaurant facilities. A bit stupid to hold a 'conference' during such time but I guess you get what you pay for. Would I go back? Doubtful it seemed a very depressing place overall.

“Fantasic!!!” From the minute we stepped into the Hyatt the staff was there with a smile and a welcome. The Inner Harbor with so much action and entertainment is really just steps away via an overpass from the hotel. Our room over looked the harbor and I don’t know what I enjoyed more waking up to the harbor view or going to bed seeing all the lights. The bed – ah, comfort at its best. Don’t miss the breakfast buffet; it is wonderful and the pool is a perfect place to rest and relax. The only thing I would change is the price of parking. If you are staying at the hotel I really think it should be half of what they charge. Don’t hesitate though – call the Hyatt and try the roof top dining.

“Fabulous. So impressive. Great location. Impeccable service and stunning rooms” This hotel really delivers. I checked in at around 11am without any delay at all. The rooms are stunning and are as large as they look and as on the website. For the price (I paid $360 + tax) I paid it was fantastic value for money. Bathroom was huge, generous toiletries, plenty of storage space (there is also a microwave and Nespresso machine). Turndown happened every night no matter what my schedule was. In my 3 nights and 4 days there and I never saw a housekeeping cart or bag of laundry on the ground. Somehow everything just happens! Super comfortable bed, wonderful sitting area, I could have spent the whole weekend here and still have been happy. I fully expected an overpriced hotel breakfast but the prices were very reasonable in relative terms ($10 or so for large bowl of oatmeal with berries, $12 for bacon and eggs) and the setting was very nice. Just for comparison I have paid $20+ for bacon and eggs in the past at a Fairmont Hotel). Doormen were friendly, always helpful and eager to help people get a cab. Checkout was just as easy as checkin. We saw the pool - small but certainly lots of people looking very relaxed on the lounge chairs. Never used the spa but looked nice. I was very impressed with the decor in lobby, hallways and the room. Granted that comes with being a brand new hotel but it was very impressive.

“Thank you Virgin. Watch out for reception staff.” We didnt want to stay here. We arrived at Logan to fly back to London in the middle of the August Security Scare. As a result, several flights were cancelled including our Virgin flight to Heathrow. Whilst it was not Virgin's fault, they realised we had 3 small children and put us up in the Embassy for 2 nights. By the time all of this was sorted, we were very tired and just wanted to get to the hotel. We asked for a crib for our baby. When we got to the hotel, we were met by a very grumpy receptionist who treated as though we shouldnt be staying there for free. Despite the fact that Virgin had promised us a crib, he advised the hotel didnt have any and we should go back to the airport and speak to Virgin to sort it out. Got to the room and spoke to Duty Manager, John, who was fantastic. He drove around all the local hotels to find us a crib and brought it to the room. I am a gold HHonours member and this is the kind of service I expect. Turning to hotel, it is above average airport hotel. Excellent breakfast although big queues, good pool, free internet (a godsend as we needed to know about flights home), great rooms. Easy to get back into Boston as well from the 'T'. Nothing in local area though. If you need a hotel at Logan you could do a lot worse, just pray you get a smile at reception.

“Great Style, Great Location, Tiny Rooms” Situated on the corner of Michigan Avenue and Erie, with a view of the Water Tower from our room, I couldn't have asked for a better location. I truly enjoyed my stay at the hotel. The decor was chic without being overdone. The room was also tastefully decorated, although incredibly small. Having stayed in many hotels in Europe, I'm used to small rooms, but this felt especially cramped. We had ordered room service for breakfast the first morning and quickly realized how much of a mistake that was. We were balancing plates on our laps on the bed in order to eat. For two people it just really didn't work. I think the room would have been perfect for one person. I was also a bit disappointed in the charge for internet in the room. With two people, both with laptops staying three nights, that would have really added up. While wireless was free in the lobby, it is inconvenient to pack up the laptop and bring it down there. Plus it was a challenge to find an outlet near seating areas. I would have rated it a five on cleanliness except on the first morning that I woke up, I went to throw away something in the trash bin under the desk, and there was a pop bottle and chip wrapper in there that did not come from us. Overall the staff was welcoming and helpful. My one complaint would be at the bar in the lobby where the bar tender acted as if he were doing us a favour to wait on us. I wasn't too impressed with that. Nor was I impressed with the 18% gratuity automatically added to our bar tab. The tab accidentally got charged to our room twice, but that was quickly remedied upon check out. I did like the hotel and would definitely stay there again, but would try for a larger room if I'm travelling with my partner again.

“Perfect location for football, conventions, bars and restaurants.” First time I have stayed here and was very happy. Located downtown adjacent to the convention center and closest good hotel to new Colt's stadium and within walking distance to many restaurants, bars and nightclubs. Located at old train station they also have real train cars as rooms. Regular rooms clean and roomy. Everyone friendly, will stay here again.

“Hippest @ LAX” I have been waiting for The Custom. Until it came around there was a major lack of hip hotels at LAX, and why should travelers be forced to stay at standard-issue hotels at the airport? Why not stay in style at a converted building {designed by same architect as the Capitol Records building} channeling the Jet Age? I checked in early, as well as requested a slightly later check-out, and the staff gladly accommodated my request with a smile. What's more, when you're waiting for the shuttle, to check-in or to check-out, the lobby has been thoughtfully designed with ample seating and lots of standing-with-suitcases room. The hotel is in a perfect location: 3 mins from LAX, 10 mins from Venice and 15 mins from Santa Monica. All in all, it's a convenient, a reasonably-priced and a mod addition to LAX's hotel offering. I would absolutely stay again, and if I only had a short stay in LA, The Custom is the perfect take-off point for exploration, beach time or relaxation by the pool. What I liked - size of safe, big enough for a lap top - staff extremely friendly - cardio & weights gyms - shuttle to/from LAX runs every half hour - lemon water in lobby - cafe in lobby - bar33 restaurant - design of the entire hotel, especially the pool area {they took a basic pool and made it fabulous with graduated tanning areas, comfy couches, cool plants, shaded cabanas, gas fire pits = bravo} - the hotel is also right beside a Ralph's grocery store and 30 steps from a Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf cafe which ups its convenience factor What to know - rooms are large and decor is minimalist - it's a older, converted building, so soundproofing isn't the best---sleep with earplugs

“Great hotel!!!” We stayed at the Renaissance for 3 nights in March 2007, the hotel was beyond expectations. The staff were personable and helpful for tourist info.. We arrived very late after many delays and the staff checked us in quickly and gave us our room keys. The room were spacious and clean. Our room's view was of the Chicago river and the theater district on the 21st floor. We had breakfast at the hotel one morning and they had fresh fruit, great service. The "L" was aroung the corner for easy transportation around the city. I would definately recommend staying at this hotel and we will be returning in the future.

“Great Location - Would Stay Again” I am a big fan of the Monaco hotels (have stayed at them in San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver), and would happily stay at any one of them again if I had the choice. Location was awesome. I also love the boutique-y details (pet-friendly, that you can have a goldfish delivered to your room to keep you company, the jazz music playing when I arrived in my room, the wine in the evenings).

“A good hotel, but a bit frantic” I love Klimpton hotels, I'm part of their loyalty program, and I have stayed in multiple properties around the country. In some ways, this hotel SHOULD be my favorite, because it is located near many of the shopping, dining, and entertainment facilities that I enjoy. However, the reception area on the day I checked in was a complete zoo, the toilet was blocked, and the view was less than stunning -- and this was in an upgraded room. I'm going to try this hotel again this winter, and I hope for the sort of experience that other reviewers have mentioned so far.

“Good water views and pool area” I have stayed at this W Hotel and the W Chicago City Center. Both stays were for business. I'd recommend the City Center location for business travel as I thought it had a quieter, cooler atmosphere and also better rooms. Both locations offer free internet in the lobby, but you have to pay for internet access in your room. The Lake Shore location rooms were more plain and I thought the lobby was incredibly crowded and noisy. The rooms do have great views of the water (if you request a water view room). Additionally, I stopped by the fitness center and it's really nice and modern. There is a great indoor pool and sundeck area. The location seems like a perfect spot if you're vacationing and also want some time to relax within the hotel.

“LOUSY Location 2 Star Hotel” This is NOT a downtown location. It's 20 minutes walk through a nasty neighborhood or down along the river. Plan on taking cabs. My room on the 3rd floor was next to the hotel A/C units. Lovely noise. Some of the rooms look directly into one another because there are two towers side by side. The old tv had static on it. There was no hair conditioner, just shampoo and soap. The pillow were not feather but synthetic. If you like sleeping on cheap sheets this is your place. No bath robes. Services? Ha! Newspapers for Priority Club members only. This is a two star hotel at best. Priceline it, but don't be silly enough to pay what they want on the website. We got a $60 pline rate and felt ripped off when we experienced the product. The worst part was being so far from downtown. There is a gym and a pool. There are plenty of cheap hotels downtown with far better locations, so why put yourself in this property.

“Thank you!” Got a room lat minute after 2 cancelled flights. Diana at the front desk was excellent and extremely helpful. What I've come to expect from my second Hilton stay this week, consistency and comfort. So confidently located across from Terminal 2 at Ohare. Try to grab a corner room away from the busy hall ways

“Mhm” Nice hotel from outside and the lobby is very warm and - let's say it - luxurious, somehow. It's like an bee hive when you get to the rooms. Rooms. Ok, they are large enough and equiped. But a little bit dusty. Walls are a little bit strange...look like caves. Moquette non in perfect condition. Door is too thin...I mean, you can hear everything happening in the corridor. 6th street is not around the corner but you will get there by crossing the bridge with a nice 15minutes walk. There's better in Austin, a lot better. But if you find a good rate (I did) this hotel can be a good compromise...

“Very good for central Austin” Stayed here for two nights and it was perfectly located for 6th St (couple of mins walking) while also far enough to avoid the noise should you wish. It's a nice hotel with good rooms/bathrooms, free wifi. Parking was expensive so we opted to park for free on the street as it was the weekend. There's a cheap lot next door though. Good breakfast selection, served in a nice balcony area. Our room had an adjoining door (are they really necessary??), a pet peeve of mine as you can here the neighbours through it so doesn't feel so private!

“Danke für den super Service und tollen Aufenthalt” Wir waren für 4 Nächte im Ritz Carlton San Francisco. Wir haben den Transfer über das Hotel organisieren lassen. Hat jeweils super geklappt. Der Fahrer hat uns vor der Gepäcksausgabe abgeholt. Wir hatten ein Clubdeluxe Zimmer. Die Clublounge befindet sich auf der 8 Etage im Hotel. Das Frühstück in der Lounge war sehr fein mit ausgewählten Produkte. Man hate hier den ganzen Tag die Möglichkeit was zu trinken oder auch was kleines zu essen. Das Hotelzimmer ist klassisch und sehr elegant eingerichtet. Die Badezimmer sind sehr geräumig mit Bulagri Kosmetik. Ich kann das Ritz Carlton nur allen empfehlen. "Und bucht das Clubzimmer, der Aufpreis ist es wirklich wert. "

“Easy Walking Distance to anywhere in the Harbor, Little Italy and Fells Point” We took the subway into Baltimore to avoid the high parking fees and traffic and congestion for New Years eve. The subway is only about 6 blocks from the hotel (Shot Tower). The hotel is located about a block from Pier 6, great location to the Harbor, Little Italy and Fells Point. We were able to walk everywhere and was glad we rode the subway due to the amount of traffic in the city. Checkin was a breeze (when you enter the lobby there is a line for Homewood Suites and Hilton Garen Hotel). We were given a one bedroom suite located on the 9th floor. The room was clean with no complaints. Typical Homewood Suites with the kitchen, living room and bedroom. The view was spectular of the city (especially at night with it lite up.) We were able to watch the traffic coming into the city from 83 which was very heavy. We were able to walk out of the hotel and go about two blocks to McCormick & Schmicht to watch the fireworks along with water edge which were spectular. We went back to the room immediately afterwards and were glad we choose to stay in the city and not have to deal with the traffic. My only complaint was hearing a band until about 2 in the morning. I read about this problem on the board and was not expecting to hear it with being on the 9th floor, but since we were up so late it was not as bothersome as if we would have went to bed earlier. The breakfast the next morning was one of the best we have had at a Homewood Suites. Everyone we ran into at the hotel was very pleasant. It was a very enjoyable stay and would look forward to returning again.

“Five Star rooms and service at the Omni” Honestly... One of the best hotel experiences I've ever had and this was my first time at an Omni. From the moment we walked into the reception to the moment we walked out the door two things really stood out...the service and the room. Everyone we encountered was very nice and seemed to really enjoy working at the property. The room reminded me of a Ritz Carlton or the St. Regis in DC. Plush furnishings, classic elegance, great bathroom. I really could not have been happier with my stay. Additionally, I had left my cell phone in the room after check-out and upon my return the housekeeping staff was overly helpful and located my phone in the laundry room wrapped up in the sheets. Whew!.... thank goodness for the great service. Travel tip: SF parking can be expensive but on the weekend we found St. Mary's parking garage one block away for only $6.50 a night. We quickly used the money we saved by splurging on the mini bar. Cheers!

“Solid Embassy Suites” Stayed one night....efficient check in. Room typical of Embassy Suites. Separate vanity/sink outside of the bathroom (in the bedroom area) which made it easy to get ready in the morning with more than one person in the room. Room was clean. Breakfast was good -- the lady at the omelette station was friendly and efficient -- but no waffles. Good value for the rate.

“excelente atención” es un muy buen hotel, tal vez un poco alejado y la atencion es impecable, todos fueron muy amables. el desayuno es mu bueno. sin dudas lo mejor del hotel es el personal. las habitaciones son tipicas de los hilton. muy cómodas y limpias.

“Comfortable” It's clean and the staff is friendly. The hotel is an old "Howard Johnson" type hotel refurbished w/ comfortable mid-price hotel furnishings. Note: there is no refrigerators, safes, or mini-bars in the rooms. It's comfortable and quiet, not luxurious and lively.

“Large hotel, close to mall.” This is a very large hotel, close to the Keystone Mall and other area attractions. It is very near downtown Indianapolis. The beds were very comfortable and large. We had a package that included breakfast. This was one of the best breakfast buffets I have ever had. There were many items that you could take with you if you were leaving for the day. (Bottled water, breakfast cereal bars, etc.). I would definitely stay again, if in the area.

“Great location, nice staff, great price.” We have stayed at this hotel before and really liked it - the price and location can not be beat! Unfortunately when we checked in, they said they did not have a king bed which we had confirmed and they moved us to a queen room instead. They said we should have been notified prior to coming to the hotel but we were not. The adjusted the price to a queen and then we had to move to another room the next night. I did not find this acceptable and complained and they lowered the price of the first night of our stay 20 dollars. Not a bad gesture, maybe expected a bit more. The hotel is very clean and yes the rooms are small but nice for Times Square. No complaints there. We moved into a king room the next day and then the air conditioner did not work so had to move again - have to say the staff was very nice, especially the hotel manager Anna who listened to my complaints. She moved us into another king with a working air conditioner (as it was 100 degrees in NYC that day much needed!). They did give us a fruit plate and a letter and some water for our troubles which was nice. There is no free wifi in the rooms but is available in the lobby. The bar downstairs is sooo loud you can hear the music thumping all night - we were on the 4th floor and could hear it very well. The bellman at the end of our stay tried to get us to take a limo to the airport instead of a yellow taxi which we wanted and was a little rude to us as well. It was not a good beginning or end of the stay at Stay, but the hotel is so reasonably priced it may be worth a future visit.

“Hip small hotel in unique location” Very close to city center (across from city hall), but sandwiched between a court of lesser offenses and an interesting night club leading to some unique characters around both after and during business hours. Rooms beautiful and comfortable. 10th floor corner room was quiet. Great breakfast and lunch at restaurant. Small but decent gym. Slow $10 Internet. Nice staff.

“Understated Elegance” Stayed during the July long weekend and fell in love with this hotel. The Four Seasons lived up to its reputation in every possible way. Checked in early at around 11 a.m. not expecting a room until later on; however, service was prompt and the front desk immediately showed me to a room without making a fuss. In fact, it was only upon checkout that I found out they had upgraded me from a Superior room to a Premium room in order to accommodate my early check in. I liked that the person who checked me in did not make a fuss and did not make a huge presentation of upgrading me. The room was large and comfortable. Housekeeping was very competent; forgot to lock up my jewelry and did not have to worry that any would be missing. Turndown service was also very efficient. My only complaint would be the lack of complimentary bottled water. The Ritz Carlton would display them freely and replenish as needed; at the Four Seasons, only one bottle was provided during turndown. The location was convenient and easily accessible to Union Square and other attractions. Everything was within walking distance... providing great exercise without having to go to the gym! The gym is an external sports club, so there is no 24 hour access. However, it does have great classes and the equipment are state-of-the-art. The business center in the hotel provides complimentary internet access for an hour each day, which is sufficient for me to check in quickly with the office. All staff were polite and helpful. Service was efficient and I had a feeling that I was well-taken care of. Doormen would always greet me and call a taxi for me. Those at the Concierge Desk were very helpful with directions and recommendations. Front Desk always greeted me with a smile and provided me with whatever I needed. I particularly appreciate them for being polite, but not over friendly or intrusive by asking me personal questions. Highly recommend the hotel for all visiting San Francisco. (The only reason I gave a four star for value is due to my inherent reluctance to pay almost $500 a night for any hotel room.)

“Great location, otherwise just ok.” I recently stayed at this hotel for two nights while in Charlotte on business. It is at a great location in the center of downtown Charlotte. It was close to the office where I needed to be, and it was close to many good restaurants. Parking was adequate, and easy to get in and out of. The check-in went smoothly, and the common areas were ok, but not impressive. Then came the room. The bathroom smelled bad, and the toilet ran. It just felt a little worn, and not terribly clean. For $219 per night, I expected a little more.

“Funky cool if you have a few bucks to spend” I have to admit that I was a little turned off by the fact that we had to wait for our room to be ready (at 6pm at night), and being told that we were being given a free upgrade which turned out to be false. Add to that we had a room that smelled like smoke all night long (it was a non-smoking room but must have been beside a smoking room), and I probably wouldn't go back to this hotel for it's price (nearly $400 Canadian with taxes). All the bad out of the way now, I have to say this hotel has got it all if you don't mind the price. The rooms are incredible. We love the flat screen tv, comfy bed, and stylish bathroom. The lounge is so hot and trendy we felt like celebs having some pre-dinner appetizers and drinks. The food, by the way, is out of this world there too!! Breakfast in the restaurant was top notch. Can't complain about atmosphere, location (soho!), nor the food.

“Great Manager Happy Hour” So we really enjoyed this hotel. It is in a safe area and is nice and clean. You save a lot on parking staying here vs staying at the embassy suites downtown. The rooms are very spacious and clean. The restaurant is good as well. The hosted breakfast and manager happy hour are nice little treats. The only thing we did not enjoy about this hotel was we were there for business and there were a lot of locals staying that had gotten rooms and were using the place to party. They had large ammounts of people in the room and were all traipsing around the hotel in swimsuits. The kids were running around leaving wet trails in the hallways from the pool. Since the lobby is a central lobby there noises echoed. If this element was not there it would have been perfect.

“Nice comfortable hotel” I stayed here for 5 nights in December. I selected the hotel, even though I was attending an event at another nearby hotel, because I like the reliability of Marriott, especially the beds. This hotel met Marriott expectations in every area except housekeeping. My room was large, on the 10th floor and quite comfortable. There was a good work station with an adjustable chair which I appreciated. The bed was very comfortable. Check in was very smooth, efficient and pleasant. Overall, the staff was always a pleasure to encounter. The concierge level staff deserves an "extra nod" for their exceptional service. I ordered room service on a few evenings and it was prompt, delivered with a smile and the food was good. The bathrooms do not have separate showers, so it is still the older Marriott tub/shower combination. Bedding and other amenities were of a high quality. The hotel is near a major interstate and I did use earplugs at night as the traffic noise starts in the early morning hours. The housekeeping in this hotel needs some improvement. I called management on three different occasions with housekeeping issues. I would consider only one of them to be major, but the housekeeping service was not up to Marriott standards with several minor issues also appearing daily i.e., leaving used towels left on the counter unattended, not providing new shampoo or conditioner, not removing empty glasses, not putting away ironing boards etc. Managements response was appropriate and attentive. Overall, I would stay again.

“Great hotel” I often stay at this hotel when I am in Houston for business. The service is excellent and they are great when planning for meetings in their conference rooms. The location is central and they offer female guests traveling alone valet parking at the self parking rate. That is a definite plus!

“Welly Wotten” Do not stay at this hotel expecting the level of service you might receive at other W hotels, or even at a Motel 6. While the room and facilities were fine, the service was, to put it mildly, abysmal. At 9 am each day, you can hear the person responsible for the mini bar knocking on each door, loudly announcing "MINI BAR," slamming doors, and chatting with the housekeeping staff. Each day of a 4 day stay, I was asked by the housekeeping staff "checking out today?" When I said no, I was asked when my partner would be leaving the room for it to be cleaned. An answer of "10 minutes" was routinely greeted by a sigh and rolling of the eyes. A request to change rooms, which was confirmed by the front desk, and by phone the day of, was not honored. Apparently there was a miscommunication among the staff. When I confronted the manager about it, I was treated to significant amounts of "corporate speak" in which I was informed that I had met "challenges" during my stay. I didn't meet "challenges;" the hotel made "mistakes." While the manager tried to make things better, a $50 voucher for breakfast doesn't do much good when breakfast for two is over $60. The coup d grace came a week later when two separate sets of letters and DVDs failed to make it to their recipients. A call to the hotel simply elicited the response "we deliver all mail to the post office, we're not responsible for what happens to it after that." Amazingly, after 5 years of Netflix, this would be the one time that the post office misplaced 3 separate DVDs. This level of service is not indicative of W hotels in general, which have been great. In terms of rooms, you should request a room on a renovated floor. The unrenovated floors, on which I stayed, are decorated, as a nice Texan on the elevator put it: "as if by some housewife who picked up some stuff at Target."

“New, Clean, Hip Hotel” I definitely recommend this hotel for business or leisure travelers. It opened within the year and has a new, clean feel. What really stood out was the staff---they were all so friendly, helpful and efficient. The equipment in the hotel gym is brand new and the room is large and bright--it did not feel like your standard, stuffy hotel gym. The hotel lobby bar was fun and lively. The hotel is in walking distance to Newbury Street and many shops and restaurants. This hotel seems to cater to bachelor/ette parties--so on the weekends, you may hear some noise in the hallway at night. We were next door to a party and when we complained to the front desk, the hotel security handled it promptly and professionally.

“Nice Stay, Valet needs work” We had a nice stay at the Hilton Plaze (also called Hilton Medical Center) It is within walking distance to a few delis and Starbucks. We had a nice King suite and the beds were very comforable. I had requested some strawberries and fruit upon our arrival and to my delight, they were already in the room. We ordered room service late one night and had everything from pasta, steak and sandwiches... all which were great. The breakfast buffet, however, was "Icky" (as my 12 yr old put it) We definitely made the trip to Cliff's Grill a few blocks away the next morning. We attended an event at Relaint Stadium and when we returned that later that evening, there were no valet attendants. There were already 2 vehicles in front of us,parked at the valet stand. When we went to the front desk to inquire, we overheard the employee tell another guest that after a certain hour, valet is handled through the front desk. (A sign regarding this should be posted at the valet stand!) We handed our keys to the front desk employee and went up to our room. We found out later that the 1st vehicle had left the keys in the ignition for valet but because they didn't hand them to the front desk employee, security threatned the guest that the vechicle would be towed. So, she had to go move it. Wow, I am surprised at this service from Hilton! It was obviously a guest at the hotel and the keys were IN the vechicle... why not just move it to the valet parking lot? Overall, it was a nice stay but they need to work on their valet policy and put up a sign so guests will know that after a certain hour, take your keys to the front desk.

“Lovely Older Hotel” We really enjoyed our stay at the St. Regis. The concierge did a great job of getting us into some terrific restaurants. The location, if you want to be near the White House, is great. The room was nice, but I found it a bit dated and dark. I asked for a room with a tub and the only room with a tub was pretty small. Our reservation had been for a premier deluxe, which I had changed to a grand deluxe. Although it was deluxe, I would not call it grand. But it was quiet and comfortable and we did not spend much time in the room. Plus because of the holiday we got a great rate.
