“Good Stay in the heart of Times Square” The Millennium is a nice hotel right near the heart of Times Square. You'll be within walking distance of all the shops, restaurants and entertainment. Hotel rooms are nice for a New York hotel (smaller rooms than other cities). Hotel staff is professional and helpful. Some areas of the hotel are showing their age - for example, the furniture in the lounge is very worn. Nice hotel for good rate though.

“Great service, great pool, great rooms” I am a frequent traveler and was very pleased to find this hotel....it's a great location and is close to Beverly Hills and Rodeo drive while being reasonably priced. I recommend it for families and business travelers alike!

“Great location for a great SF vacation.” This place is in a good location. You are short blocks away from all the action at Fisherman's Wharf, two different cable car turnarounds, cross town and local bus stops, Ghiradelli Square, Hop on-Hop off bus stariting points and maybe most important a Walgreens. With just a little effort you can walk to North Beach and Little Italy. This place is well staffed with helpful people, clean and comfortable. Did I mention the breakfast? Bacon, sausage, pancakes, eggs, biscuits and gravy plus all the other regular free breakfast items. The only drawback I found is that there are no stairs to assist the overworked elevators.

“Views & Solid Service” Booked here, took the room (suite) facing the Hudson River. Upon arrival the staff put me in a room on the 11th floor. Tremendous room. Straight-on huge views of the Hudson River, the Intrepid, the ocean-going cruise ships coming & going, all the river activity, the Jersey side, it's really pretty day & night. The room also had a view of the GW Bridge way, way up north because the windows wrap around two walls. Almost didn't want to sleep because these are, truly, million dollar views of an incredible city. Two flat screen tv's but never turned them on. Why would I...? Go for the high floors facing the Hudson. But not too high, because the closer you get to the roof lounge the louder the noise transfer will be. Late at night I could hear the chatter buzz from the roof top lounge but just vaguely & only in the living room area, not in the bedroom. Service is professional. Not overly friendly, and that's fine, just professional. Amenity was a bottle of red wine, thanks Kimpton, classy touch. The $ 15 raid the mini bar comp was fine too (an OJ, everything else is mega-expensive). Bathroom is huge, shower is cool with all the spray jets, deep soak tub, too. Toiletries are plentiful & high quality, but I can't ever remember the name of that stuff. Tons of restaurants on 9th Avenue - - that's two cross-town blocks away. Plenty of cabs available in front of the hotel or cruising 11th Avenue if you want them. The hotel lounge is apparently frequently booked for private, revenue-generating, events. Didn't get to try it out because it was booked for one of these when I was there. Prices for room service were obscene even for Manhattan. Basic eggs, toast, juice, coffee...$ 28.00 plus room service fee plus tip. lol Is someone angry at the guests & trying to nail them for every dime. NYC taxes on hotel rooms pretty steep, be advised. Def recommended as a superb 'room with a view' in the big Apple.

“quiet, clean, comfortable” Stayed there twice in December for work. I enjoyed the comfortable beds and the very quiet area. The hotel is spread out enough that even the parties that were held in the ballrooms on new years eve were far enough from my room so that I was able to sleep.

“Average hotel made better by decent staff” The Sheraton Brookhollow has undergone a recent renovation. This is evident throughout the property as well as in the rooms. The property definitely has an upscale feel and is in a business-park, near I610. Access to the hotel can be confusing, especially as the directions are sub-par and the area is under construction. The rooms are nicely appointed, to Sheraton standards. The bedding was new, and the room had been serviced recently. In the renovation, they glossed over the bathrooms. Like typical hotels of this construction vintage, the ceilings are low and the ventilation is poor. If the renovation was recent, the climate of Houston does a number on bathrooms. The paint was cracking and there was a bit of mold in the shower area. Parking was plentiful and free, though it was a small walk, as the majority of the parking is in a structure adjacent to the property. If you have pets, this would be a great place to stay, as there is a special pet walking area (small, but convenient.) The lobby staff was pleasant, and helpful. They were not overtly helpful, though I will give them a special nod as I had left my laptop in my room and they retrieved it and stored it in the front desk for the day until I could get back to pick it up. Overall, there are probably better choices for the same money, including a Springhill and Courtyard less than a mile away. Also of note, the neighborhood deteriorates rapidly in all directions, so be sure to follow well-lit marked roads.

“Not Good!” This hotel has good bones but the upkeep and service is sub-par. The hotel certainly needs an update. It feels as if they are trying to skimp on the dollars going to refurbish the joint. Clearly way past time to do so. I ouwld not stay here again until they upgrade the rooms. The service tried to be helpful, but in several areas came up short. My stay was for three nights. I had an issue with the AC and requested help 5x. On each occasion I spoke to the front desk and each time they said they would solve the issue when I was out of the toom. AND 5x they did not! Unbeliveable. I just turned it off for the last night of my stay.

“As usual, very comfortable, great position” Small but comfortable rooms, brilliant position, efficient staff and awesome bar. The only downside was noisy neighbours and intermittent wireless internet

“Top of the Heap” This is the 4th or 5th time Hotwire has placed me at this property and I've come to rejoice every time it's revealed to me after I've made my up-front payment. This hotel is not only one of the best Four Points properties there is, I think it's one of the best Sheratons. Heck, it's one of the best hotels I've ever stayed at - period! This two-story edifice was the first hotel built near BWI. It's closest to the terminals and overshadowed by the more recently built behemoth Daily Parking Garage sited next door. There's free parking in front of the hotel (often right at the door if the parking gods are smiling down on you) and there's at-call shuttle service 24/7. By some historical dispensation, theirs are the only hotel shuttles that pull up at the closest curb to baggage claim exit doors. Check-in is always friendly and efficient. The rooms are nicely outfitted with all the usual amenities. Even the art work is aeronautically themed. Housekeeping is flawless and Michener's, the hotel's restaurant, is first-rate in terms of food and service. By all means, try the Maryland Velvet Crab soup and crab cakes for some local flavor. I had my pancake epiphany here. "So THIS is how pancakes are supposed to look and taste" I thought the first time I tried them. Take the extra step and get the banana-nut pancakes. You can add on two eggs and bacon or sausage for only $3. There are lots of nice little touches here. One I noticed were the large urns with flowers on the exterior sills of the floor-to-ceiling windows. One definitely gets the feeling that there's a real "We're all in this together" spirit on the part of the staff. Everyone is eager to please. Obviously, this "can do" attitude is inspired by savvy management. There's a real sense of pride here. Another advantage here is easy access to the light rail station at the terminal which affords an easy and cheap ride to downtown Baltimore for sight-seeing.

“Good new hotel, some flaws” New, good hotel in good location. We stayed twice in July. First time we were upgraded to 16th floor (apparently room rate is higher for rooms in upper floors). The second stay did start as smoothly; we could have had a room in upper floors only for surcharge. We declined and received a fourth floor room facing opposite wall. When we were going to bed few hours later we noted sheets weren't changed after the previous guest; there was a used tissue paper and black hairs in the bed. We went to complain in the front desk. The clerk apologized, but could only offer us similar room in fourth floor; she told there was only one room available? So we ended up changing room at 12.30 am. I wasn't very happy, but it was late, I was tired and didn't feel like arguing. To be fair, this was one time incident, otherwise our room and hotel were clean and ok. The only faults were lack of safety box and drawers in room. Iron was good but hte ironing board was very low. Canal Street is very busy and there are lots of counterfeit vendors, but there are attractive streets with restaurants and shops around the block in Tribeca and across Canal Street in Soho. Several subway lines within few blocks whisk you to around New York in no time. To fetch a taxi is not very easy in front of the hotel; taxis seemed to avoid Canal Street due to heacy traffic, so we usually walked few blocks to hail a taxi. Guests can use six computers for free in lobby, but they are very slow. Many pages, eg. Open Table could not be used; they were blocked as "adult pages". There are several laundries nearby hotel offering wash and fold for 12 $ for 10 pounds. The doorman recommended us to take a towncar to JFK, it cost the same as taxi (45$ + tolls & tips =60 $). We took it as we were leaving a bit late and to get a taxi was not easy in front of the hotel. I gave the driver 70 $ and he seemed to be very happy.

“Good value.” I booked this hotel for a business trip at $149, I am a Starwood member, but not elite. It's a short shuttle ride from the airport (with one stop first at the Westin). The property itself is older, even though it looks like they've tried to renovate it. The rooms were nice mostly, with newer amenities (flat panel tv, ac hookups). Bathtubs definitely were worn (mildew) and tile was not very clean (hair all over). I had the breakfast buffet one day and it was pricey for what I got. When you add it all up, it was $20-$30 a night cheaper than comparable offerings closeby. For that, I give it 4*'s for the value.
“Mod and hip in San Diego” It is a W hotel so of course it is cool and hip. Location is nice, rooms are clean and comfortable. I have stayed atany places in San Diego and this is one of the nicer.

“Cannot fault this Hotel” This was the second time that I had stayed at the Argonaut after visiting San Francisco last year. That time I was travelling solo but on this visit I had the pleasure of being accompanied by my family. On the face of it little had changed. This time, given there were four of us, we booked a corner suite for our 4 night stay. Apart from views of the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz this gave us more than enough room as both the living area, master bedroom and the bathroom were very spacious. There is a large dining table in the living area that adds to flexibility. My sons slept on the sofa bed which was adequate, whilst my wife and I had the bedroom. The quality of the fit out is first class. Whilst we were on the busy corner we found that street noise died down appreciably after 11. We could have shut the windows to mute the noise but we love Hotels where you can get fresh air by being able to open windows so this was another attraction. As far as the Hotel itself we have only positives to say about the establishment. From the cheerful doorman, who quickly adopted our sons, to the efficient front desk staff, all were customer focussed and sought only to make our stay enjoyable. One small story illustrated this. We put some clothing in for laundry. Shortly after I had a call from Oxana from Housekeeping asking me whether we wanted a particular service as it was more expensive (double) than one that would achieve the same ultimate result. Naturally we went with the cheaper service and were grateful to her pointing this out. To us, this illustrated what makes this Hotel so good - delivery of a product that is 100% oriented on customer satisfaction. This, and of course the wine evenings (plus hot chocolate afternoons). Our thanks to the Argonaut management and staff for helping make our San Francisco visit truly memorable.

“Wonderful hotel with relaxing atmosphere” This resort is known for its wonderful restaurant sunset view and a very nice spa; two things we enjoyed while celebrating our anniversary over a four day get-a-way. Upon arrival we were greeted by hotel staff and provided a great resort overview and room upgrade. Our bags were taken to the room while we relaxed in the large open lobby area. Once we made it to the room, the flowers I had asked staff to prepare for my wife were in place and my reputation as a caring husband were secure! If fact, I had asked the bag attendant to hide a particular gift in the closet so it was available on the big day....he hit the mark and I was again in great shape. Next up was our spa treatment...this was our first and what a great experience! We headed to the pool the next day. Although the entire pool area is quite large, it is important to remember, this place is right down the street from Fiesta Texas, a Six Flags park. That said, even during the week, there are a lot of children. So...we headed down to the smaller adult area pool. Very nice and quiet. Although the service was noticeably slow since the attendants are required to walk back to the bar at the main pool area to obtain drink orders, our experience was still quite nice. Before dinner we took a walk on the nature trail located on the expansive property. Although we are not golfers, the beautiful fairways and plush greed grass was quite a sight. Dinner at sunset was quite nice but very warm. If you are there in the summer, don't plan for dinner until after 7 PM. The sun is hot and the restaurant was uncomfortably warm. Regardless, the evening was nice and our wild game dinner was out of this world good! Once you have dinner you should be sure to try brunch the next morning. You wont be sorry! All and all, our entire stay was a great experience.

“Great place to stay to visit Graceland” We spent two nights at this hotel, it was a great stay. Easy check in and out, nice big rooms, very clean, good shower, big selection of tv channels and a good selection of breakfast foods. All in all we were very satisfied with this hotel and would recommend to anyone visiting Graceland!

“not good enough to be a sheraton/starwood” this hotel is just not good and i suspect the management just do not want to do a better job, it has cost cutting written all over it. the lobby looks great but when you get to the rooms, they're shabby and unrenovated. not nice but no-one stays in a sheraton for the room decor. however i would expect the service to be better but it failed on mutiple counts. - i asked for a room away from the elevator. the front desk woman said she would give me one. i could see the elevator from my room. strike one. - my trash can still contained the previous occupant's trash. strike two. - the two wake up calls i ordered did not happen. strike three. - the room service menu has pretty much nothing on it. i ordered a pizza that was not edible. store-bought base with fairly raw toppings. strike, um, four. - there is no gym. the ballys next door, which is available for guests, does not open until 8am. strike five. the main problem here is this is a licensed property not owned or run by starwoods. i suspect that's why standards are low. but i had expectations of better, as sheraton hotels have dramatically improved over the past couple of years. this, however, is the hotel that time forgot. i would have told the management that they run an inferior operation. but no-one asked me my opinion when i checked out. do not stay here. it's just not a good hotel and does not deserve your patronage.

“The Silver Cloud is Golden” I stay here everytime I come to Seattlel. It is hip and modern, the rooms are spacious and well maintained and the hotel overall is excellent. It is 2 blocks from the light rail, RIGHT across the street from the Stadium and near all the great downtown scene and waterffont. The restaurant, Jimmy's om 1st is a great place and the service is professional and friendly. Their shuttle service cannot be beat; they will take you to and from just about anywhere in the vicinity. Stay here next time you are in Seattle; you will not be disappointed.

“Nice Place With a Wonderful View” I spent at the NY Marriott Financial Center a couple of nights when rushed from SoBe to NYC for Justine Timberlake concert at Madison Square Garden. I decided to stay by the river in South Manhattan, and my choice wasn’t wrong. I’ve got no one word of critics on this hotel and can only numerate its positive sides. Its staffs are professional and friendly and their service is very good. It’s very well located on the West Street going along the Hudson River, near Battery Park, so this hotel got wonderful views of New York Harbor with Ellis and Liberty islands. Sounds good, yeah? It’s very close to subway station (“Rector Street”) at Trinity Place, so in some minutes you’re able to get any place of the city. A ride by cab from the hotel to somewhere around the 42nd street or back would cost near 15 bucks with tip. It’s at walking distance (5-7 minutes) from the Broadway at Wall Street which is too convenient in case you’re on business trip. Its neighborhood is very quiet and not overcrowded in comparison with the city center. It’s cheaper than the other Marriott hotels situated in the city center, but it provides customers with the same service. That means that the hotel got an appropriate price-quality ratio. Finally, it has the restaurant, indoor pool and gym, and there is a Starbucks café in the same building. The check in took only some moments and I got a standard Marriott’s room with all the necessary amenities, traditionally comfy king bed and a nice view of the Hudson River and Jersey City. Besides a nice buffet breakfast, my accommodation plan included free cruise tickets around NY harbor with stops on Liberty and Ellis islands, two day-long subway tickets and two flyers for free admission to all the museums in South Manhattan - nothing special but very pleasant. After a quick check out, I caught a cab to the JFK – in a couple of minutes we crossed the East River through Brooklyn Bridge when rushed to Queens and got the airport very quickly (not wasting a lot of time in Manhattan’s traffic jams). Oh, that JFK! We spent two hours crawling for take off in a line of hundreds of aircrafts, but this is another story. All in all, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend anyone to stay at New York Marriott Financial Center.

“Nice stay, average amenities, good value” I stay here occasionally with my sons when they need be in the area for athletic events. The best things about the Radisson CK are the location, and proximity to very good food, such as Donna's for dinner, and a little cafe in the courtyard (don't remember the name, but is not part of the hotel) which has very good breakfast, including amazing homemade muffins. The hotel also does a nice job of putting out complementary coffee, granola bars, and fruit, very early in the morning. The lobby is very nice for some early quiet time until 6 am when they have a "policy" to turn on the TVs, even though no one is there - I asked them to wait until I left, which they did, but told me that was their policy - why do hotels think we want noise so early in the morning? The front desk staff were extremely nice and accommodating, but the roll-out bed they gave us (we tried 2) was in very poor condition. Nevertheless we will continue to stay here because of the location and relatively cheap price.

“A first class hotel with outstanding service” Overall, a solid five star property. Location is good, but its several blocks west of what most think of as SoHo. That said, there are some nice renovations being done in that area and I expect it will continue to improve. Note that many floors in the building are owner occupied. Rooms are quite comfortable, with fantastic views in almost every direction. My only beef with the rooms was the lighting. The bathroom was a particular annoyance – mirror light only on one side. Made shaving my right side a bit of a chore (right cheek toward mirror, eyes staring into light, unable to actually see my right cheek!). Drinks at both the restaurant and their lounge were quite well done and the wine list is small but interesting. We did not eat on the property. What was beyond 5 stars was the service. Check in, concierge, housekeeping, everyone, was exceptional

“Good property” Stayed for 1 night. The grounds are excellent with lots of trees. Loved the pools and hot tub. The lazy river was freezing! Lots of tree leaves in the water as well. Felt very secluded yet you are pretty close to many activities. Staff was always smiling and saying Hi. Easy check in and check out. Restaurant service was very good and the prices were reasonable. Room was nice and the bed was very comfortable. Nice sized empty fridge. Good working desk and the wireless reception was good. Good lighting and plenty of closet space. Sliding door opened to a small shared patio. I just wish they had screens. Combo tub and shower. No make up mirror. Toilet had a crack in it. Coffee maker is in the entry way alcove Water bottles at $4.00. Tap water was just fine. Make sure you rent a car. A taxi can be expensive! They have free washers and dryers. All you have to buy is the soap and dryer sheets. They are less expensive in the General Store than they are in the Laundry room or just bring your own. We found this to be a good hotel but if I was to return I would want to spend a few nights downtown as well.

“Wonderland?” Here's your disclaimer - a heavy dose of opinion ahead, with a few objective comments thrown in just for decoration. You want to know whether or not to stay here? Only if you can get a rate under $200, and plan to either join the Hip And Trendy Bar Scene (TM) that overflows into the lobby every evening, or ignore them. Don't bring the young kids, but teens will enjoy the luxurious Living Room off the lobby, especially for breakfast in the morning. I will say there are better values to be had in the Big Apple. In late 1998, I was intrigued by the notion of a new, hip, innovative hotel brand spun off the Westin luxury chain. Even the name, the simple, elegant, single letter W, signified something experimental and exciting was behind the concept. Fast forward to 2004. Over the years we've seen the W brand grasped by fashionistas and celebrities as an of-the-moment place to see and be seen, with the W hotel rooms portrayed as the settings for torrid affairs, steamy weekends or all-night parties. In early July, I tried out W New York, the hotel where it all started. I booked an Expedia special rate of $135, an excellent value off their rack rate of $259. The W shares a stretch of Lexington Avenue with four other hotels: the acclaimed Benjamin right next door, the Marriott next door on the other side, the grand Waldorf-Astoria across the street, and the Inter-Continental next to that. When I arrived, I couldn't miss the W due to its more vibrant street presence signaled by the cool lighting and casually dressed bell staff handling baggage under the steel-and-glass portico. Upon entering, I gazed at the phrase "WELCOME TO WONDERLAND" projected on the floor in light. So that's what W stands for now...(I think I liked it better when it didn't stand for anything...) Check-in was a breeze with the youngest (and most confident) front desk staff I've ever seen. However, the bell staff didn't seem to comprehend that I didn't want to valet park! What? And save $50 a night? Say it ain't so! Funny how they believe wanting to handle your own car means that you don't want them to do their jobs...I rather enjoyed being looked at as if I were from Mars when I asked for my bags to be sent up to the room. The room itself, called a Preferred Wonderful, was on a 12th floor corner overlooking 50th st. between the Marriott and the W hotels. My view was mostly of other people's hotel rooms, which can be interesting...but once the novelty wears off, down go the shades. A big, fluffy W Signature King bed was the centerpiece of my room (no complaints...slept great), with the big, 27" TV sitting on top of a stocked mini-bar in the corner. My room also had a desk with an upright chair, but I found myself missing the Millenium Hilton's ergonomic leather chair...not to mention their plasma TVs. The extras shelf (towels, robes, hair dryer, ironing board coffee maker, etc) in the closet was a very nice touch. The (tiny) bathroom had a small frosted glass window, but a shower only...you must pay extra for a bathtub. At this point, I began to wonder what people would think of this room if it weren't attached to the W hotel but instead, let's say a Holiday Inn...for the same price. I did appreciate the presence of the curious extra accessories in the room, including an 'intimacy kit' (...which speaks of what this hotel was designed for...) and various (overpriced) clothing items and CDs. However, this seems to be how they really make their money. I found myself seriously considering taking home half the stuff in the box simply because it was there. That's marketing for ya. Well, now that I've had the patented "W experience", I've learned that W has become not an innovative new hotel concept, but an innovative new concept of hotel marketing. It's genius, really, and it works so well in contrast to the four hotels around this building. The trendy scene that materializes at night, good (but not great) fine dining restaurant, sleek bar (with a verrrry good whiskey, by the way), gorgeous interior design and ubiquitous presence of "stuff to buy" translate into a singular marketing language that reminds me of what Ian Schrager started to do in the early 90s, only mass-produced. I should have known what I was in for when I read phrases like "that W vibe" in reviews of other people's hotels. W has become part of the hotel lexicon, for better or for worse. This hotel is very well designed and well executed, but it reeks of five-year-old notions of Hip And Cool that I fear are beginning to wear off. Unfortunately, staying here has made me want to try out the four (four!?!) other W hotels in NYC just to see what all the fuss is about!

“Beautiful room, view and location!!” We have stayed here twice recently with our sons age 4 and 2, November 2008 and February 2009. The suites are amazing, huge and beautiful, the windows are floor to ceiling and the view is fantasitc, the only way to travel with young children. Kitchen with microwave, stove, expresso machine, silverware/plates, and a fridge you can put your own things in to. Master bath with TV in mirror, comfy robes. Staff is so friendly, remember our names, ask how things are, answer any ?'s we may have. Upon arrival to our room there were 2 plates with the boys names in chocolate and 2 huge cookies each, which of course they loved! We ordered room service twice in both our stays and the food is fantastic and there was a kitchen table we could all sit at. Pool is very nice, there are even toys for the boys to play with! The air is very warm but my one complaint here is I think the pool is cold, of course once you are in it's fine, but my boys couldn't stay in longer then 25 minutes and they were shivering and lips were blue, very minor, but thought I would include for those travelling with young children. Now for my complaints, the first time we stayed we had a prob with the tv in the bedroom, we couldn't control the volume, couple of phone calls later we had a new tv, not a big deal. However, 2nd stay, the dvd player in the bedroom didn't work, the one in the living room worked fine, called 3 times, first 2 times someone came while we were out, and the player was still not working. I think they were "fixing" the living room one which was fine. the 3rd time I called and let them know what was happening and that we would be in the room to show the broken one. No one showed up. based on this I gave a 4 instead of a 5.

“Nice location, but soooo noisy . . .” Great location, nice modern rooms. But do not even think about sleeping in or trying to concentrate on work while in your room. The housekeeping was breaking new records for doorslamming every day of our stay. The ladies from China who do not seem to understand one word of our language start early and do not prop the doors open while servicing the guest rooms. I counted a door slamming (and the doors are very heavy!!!) every 10 seconds one morning opposite our room for about an hour. Complained to management, they were quick to apologize but nothing changed. It would be so easy just to use a waste basket to hold the door open while going in and out...but what we experienced bordered on sheer noise terror. One more minus: Forget about the (extremly expensive) room service. We tried to place an order in the morning, called five times, but the phone was never answered ...finally front desk picked up and promised to have room service call us back, but that only happened after I already had left the room to get breakfast around the corner at a very nice place for a third of Affinias price. And the first night the alarm clock in our room rang at 4.30 am on a Sunday. Housekeeping did not reset it after the previous guest. I was told that this is not part of their daily duties, so beware! It`s a shame...the hotel otherwise is nice, and they could fix those problems easily.

“Great location” This hotel is the perfect location for touring the Inner Harbor. It is right across the street from all the major activity, yet not too close that you are bothered by noise. The rooms are very nice and the beds are super comfy. Everyone at the front desk was very helpful and even allowed me to check in at noon since I arrived to town early. The only drawback was the parking- super high! But, if you want to see all that the inner harbor has to offer, I would highly recommend. If you are eating out: avoid the Rusty Scupper. HORRIBLE SERVICE. Our meal was very expensive and not that tasty. Our waiter left us mid-way through the meal and never returned. I would highly recommend Legal Seafoods. Price and service great- food- above excellent!

“What's not to like?” I should stipulate that this hotel is out of my normal budget, for both personal and business travel. I stayed on a Friday night after business meetings, using a free night voucher that I had from IHG. (Sign up for their great credit card, which gives you platinum status and a free night each year.) My room would have cost around $540 including tax, if I had paid for it. The room was decently sized, not large but just right -- unlike closet-sized rooms I have had in NYC in the past. The bathroom was very large and included a huge shower stall with a rainfall shower. All the furnishings were very high-end and tastefully designed. It was just what I would expect at this price point. I also enjoyed great soundproofing to go with the fantastic view toward the Hudson River. I slept like a baby. The hotel's location is just far enough from Times Square to be out of the chaos there, but close enough to get to Times Square or anywhere else in town quickly. There is a subway station right next door to the hotel's entrance (A-C-E lines for north-south travel). 46th street "restaurant row" is a short walk away. I invited some friends to meet me in the lobby lounge, We sat near the fireplace and enjoyed a bottle of wine before going elsewhere to dinner. And of course we had to visit Times Square late in the evening. I have to tip my hat to Mayor Bloomberg. His recent land-grab in Times Square, which drastically reduced the number of available lanes for vehicles, has created a vast pedestrian plaza where taxis used to roll. I have been to Times Square many times, usually at night, and the sidewalks were always so crammed that I could barely move -- much less enjoy the view. Now there is space for thousands of people to mingle in a low-stress way. And most of the billboards are now enormous HD displays. Very impressive. In the morning, I checked out and hit the town with my friends before departing for an evening flight. The bell staff kept my bag in their secured storage room. I found all the staff to be friendly and efficient. I would happily return here if I had a very generous expense account!

“Excellent Stay at Hilton Times Square” We recently stayed at the Hilton Times Square for 2 nights right after Xmas. We had booked our room early in Sept through the Hilton Honors Member dept. and requested a room w/2 beds as we were travelling w/our teenage daughter. We called and checked numerous times to confirm we had the double room. The day before we left we were told they had us in a room w/just a King bed and would try and provide a cot. After a few calls to the upper management we were moved to a suite on the top floor. The suite was lovely w/beautiful views of the city. There was a king bed room w/ a very large bathroom and a sitting/living room w/ pull out coach and small bathroom. It was so quiet that once we were in our room you didn't know you were in New York City unless you looked out the window. We had breakfast each morning there which was buffet or you could order off of the menu. We also had dinner there the first night we arrived as we were trying to make it to a show we had tickets for. Our dinner was very good - no complaints and we did enjoy the breakfasts as well. I would highly recommend this hotel, especially if you are going to see any shows. The Nederlander Theater is right outside the 41st St. entrance of hotel. The Times Square area was not that nice of an area to walk around but it was very close proximity to everything. The room was kept very clean and so were the other areas of the hotel. We would definitely stay there again if we were visiting New York to see a show. .

“Really nice rooms - not so great service” Stayed here for business with a lot of colleagues. The hotel itself was great - really nice rooms, comfortable beds, nice fitness center and good quick service in the bar area. It was central to just about everything and connected to the overhead walkway that runs through the town. The downside - there was one man at the front desk who was so arrogant and rude. He gave us all attitude with every question that we asked AND even yelled at the poor girl who was behind the front desk for printing our boarding passes. They had a "business center" which consisted of one computer and one printer. THey actually charge you for each minute you spend on the computer. It's ridculous. I travel on a regular basis and I've never had to pay to use a hotel computer to print my boarding passes. Also, all of us had our laptops and wireless cards with us and although the hotel supposedly supported wireless connection to the internet, none of us could get it to work. This hotel needs to get with the times and stop trying to nickle and dime business travelers. If I was just basing my review on the hotel room and location, I would say definitely stay here. If you need business functions, like internet access - stay somewhere else.

“Great deal ~ centrally located” We have stayed in this hotel a number of times. With that said, yes we keep coming back and yes, there is the good and the bad! Our first stay was in Winter and our room was huge. Our next stay was during the spring and our room was on the back side over looking the street and was very very small. I honestly think this was the smallest room I have ever had at a hotel. It was okay for our short stay but had we of been more than two and staying longer than a night it would have been horrible. The staff here is always very friendly and accommodating. The parking is secure and provided by the hotel. So when taking our car this is the place we aim for! The hotel itself is older and could be called quaint. It reminds you of the old days with its piano in the entrance and you expect Bogey to come waltzing up in a white suit. My guess is that many people who are seeking a modern sleek hotel might steer away from the Opal, but it's very reasonably priced so it's great for those quick trips to the city.

“Far better than average Airport Hotel.” Good to great hotel, with a few problems. For its main market though-traveling to and from the airport-its a great option. If you have to park there it costs $18 a night and is somewhat cumbersome. It seemed silly to have a rental car there, so I turned it in at Advantage and walked the mile or so back. There is a bus stop right in front of the hotel, I used the 194 to get to SAFECO stadium for a meeting. It cost less than the car by far, was probably faster, and I didn't have to deal with parking downtown. The daily fee for net access is high, and WiFi is only available in the public areas of the main hotel. The hotel can get really busy, and at times the wait to talk to someone on the phone or at the front desk can take a longish time. The gym and pool are really good,for relaxing long haul flights out of your system, and the hot tub is excellent. The rooms are more than adequate, the staff attentive and the 2 concierges especially are really wonderful.

“Great hotel and location” I stayed at the Back Bay Hilton in early May. Room was a little old and tired looking but very spacious. Staff were courteous. As Honors gold member I was able to use the lounge for breakfast. The selection was great and wold appeal to everyone. The fitness area and pool were also very good. Great location easily accessable to most things.

“Pleasant Stay” Rooms are a little on the small side but have been renovated. A nice view on K street but if you are a light sleeper it may be too noisy. Best to ask for a room on the other side of the hotel. Staff was extremely pleasant and helpful. Metro only 2 short blocks away.

“Not for a business traveler - Everything is too expensive” This place looks nice and has some good features - rooms are nice - but it is a maze - I checked in on a sunday and its not like a regular hotel - there are 2-3 different building - when I left in the morning it took me 10 minutes to find where I parked. Internet access is a ridiculous $12 day for a very slow direct connection - water is $6 in room - TV Movies are $16....There is no lobby restaurant or breakfeast - you have to walk too far - I got a mini bar key but there is no bar - just an empty fridge - Not sure why I would come back here - Not much to do in Phoenix period - I am a weekly business traveler and this is not where I will be next time......

“Trendy Luxury” My husband and i stayed one night of the Labor Day weekend at the James in Chicago. We had our first two nights free on Starwood Points at the Sheraton a few blocks away. The James is an intimate place in size and tempermant. The service is great, the rooms spotless, the facilities small but offer all you could need. The toiletries were Kiehl's - very nice. The bed linens were crisp and white, towels larger-than-most and fluffy. The bed was a little soft for me due to the feather mattress topper, but I conked out no problem. The location is great for nightlife, music and dining.

“Immaculate!” Immaculate; spotless. Evening "happy hour" and breakfast were fine. There are NO smoking rooms with King beds! The King bedded suite is fine, but smokers are out of luck. There are smoking queen bedded rooms. The room is fine, the beds are TINY!! Bottom line is that if you are comfortable is a small bed, the hotel is good value for the money.

“A convenient Homewood Suites if driving in the San Diego Area” This Homewood is in the San Diego area not far off one of the major freeways. You are not far from the scenic areas of La Jolla and Del Mar. There is a shopping center a short drive away from the hotel with a grocery and other typical conveniences. The hotel itself is typical Homewood, so if you like what Homewood's offer, you will find this location as you expect it. They typically have a hot entree or appetizer manager's reception each evening and an upgraded continental breakfast in the morning. Basically more selections than a Hampton but not with a cooked to order or the selection of an Embassy Suites. The rooms are very convenient as typically they have two rooms and include a small kitchen. This hotel was clean and in good condition. I would call it reasonably priced for the San Diego area, but that typically means more expensive than other parts of the country. A good value for the location, especially if you want some room to spread out.

“Good location” Good location across the street from the convention center and two blocks from the tram line. Many restaurants within walking distance. Doesn't have the impressive lobby most Hyatts have. I did not sample services other than breakfast, which was good but not cheap. Rooms were clean and spacious. The A/C fan was a bit loud but almost completely masked any sound from from adjacent rooms and the hallway. Minor annoyances: the automated check-in kiosk I used froze before printing my key, and both bathroom drains were a bit slow. Rather expensive, but this was a business trip, and being right next to the Convention Center was a big plus.

“There`s a reason its so cheap” Stayed here for one night on the 16/04/12.Had to ask to move room twice,first room smoke alarm would not stop beeping,second toilet was leaking all over the floor.Plugs are hanging out the walls with wires showing,hotel is dirty and old.Cheap for new york city (£70 per night) but i would recomend staying somewhere else if you can afford it.Only good point it is in a great location (Times Square).

“Gorgeous, excellent service, not 5 star but close” This hotel is lovely is so many ways. Great service, nice location, warm staff. Having said that I will say that it's not worth more than 200-300 a night. I say that because there are many 4 star options in Chicago (Fairmont, Swisshotel, etc) and to pay extra money, I want something special as a result. The hotel is nice but the rooms are like every hotel room in Chicago. So you're really paying for the name and less about the amenities.

“Gild Hall was great except for the bed.” Travelzoo had a great deal for the hotel and I am a big fan of the Fresh brand products that the hotel stocks the rooms with, so after reading the great reviews I decided to book a room for our trip to NYC. It should be noted that although the hotel's address is 15 Gold St., it's entrance is on Platt St. Good information if you're arriving via car. Some of the nearby streets are closed for construction (the sign says through 11/08) so be sure to look for the hotel on Platt not Gold, or you'll spend a lot of time circling around the nearby one-way streets that aren't closed off. The staff was very nice, and the lobby and hotel in general are very attractive. It's a close walk to the piers, and less than a mile from China Town and Little Italy. Perfect for dinner. The next morning we also walked to Ground Zero and the Wall St. area which were very close. The nice little touches: turn down service in the evening, Fat Witch brownies left in the evening, a mini-bar fridge which had a little room for our leftovers, Fresh brand lotion/shampoo/conditioner (love them!), flat screen tv, a quiet air conditioning unit, and a plush bed. The bed reminds me of the Hyatt's Dream bed. So comfortable to relax on, but oh how my back hurt in the morning. Too soft for me, though I wanted to like it. High powered shower in the morning felt great. The glass bathroom door that some people have referred to didn't bother me. It's texturized glass, you can't see everything behind it. The muffins and pastries in the morning were nice, fully stocked until almost 10 AM. All in all a great stay, and if they had firmer beds I'd gladly return.

“Loved the Argonaut!” We're just back from a six night stay at the Argonaut and we loved it! My DH, my four year old son and I decided to stay at Fisherman's Wharf but wanted a nice hotel; we found it! We got a great rate that included valet parking; I joined the Kimpton frequent guest program and got free internet and a "Raid the minibar" coupon when I checked in ($10 off a minibar purchase). We found the staff to be very friendly and helpful, the room was a good size and comfortable and the location was great, with lots of restaurants within walking distance. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

“Relaxing Saturday” Decided to get away for the weekend evening. Found this hotel at a very resonable price and booked. Great location. It is an older facility that has gone thru several name but with this renovation is great! Bright new lobby, crisp clean rooms and baths. Only draw back was having a room that faces Hwy 59 you get the road noice all night till about 4am.

“OK hotel- not much to get excited about” I stayed here for 2 nights prior to a conference I was attending. Location is ok- on the corner of Van Ness and California, so MUNI buses and Cable Car are readily available. The room was good-sized but kind of tired. Still it was clean and the bathroom had a good shower. The major problem was I was right next to the elevator banks and it took a while for me to fall asleep due to the noise. The view from my window of Nob Hill was spectacular and it is just around the corner from Polk St, if bar-hopping is your thing. It was a decent place to stay but not especially memorable.

“great night's sleep” I traveled from Jordan to London to LA. Before I continued on my journey, I was in need of a comfortable bed a hot shower and decent room service. I found all of that and more at the LAX Marriott. There are hotel shuttle buses that circle the airport. They will pick you up at specific boarding locations outside your terminal building. Each bus goes to a couple of hotels that are near each other. The wait isn't very long, about 10 minutes. There was one person ahead of me at the check in line. I was greated with a smile by the staff member behind the counter. He was quick and efficient in giving me my room key. This hotel is huge and very busy, however, I didn't hear a single sound from anywhere in my remodeled, extremely comfortable room. I ordered room service and was told it would be 45 minutes, it was at my door in 20! The food was quite good. The small bathroom was spotless with bath and body works aromatherapy shampoo, conditioner and cream. The room was nicely decorated and very clean. My king sized bed was so comfortable, I felt as if I was sleeping on a cloud. There were 5 pillows on the bed, various sizes, take your pick.... There was a desk, comfortable chair, large TV with digital cable, a large, illuminated, bedside clock (easy to see without your glasses....LOL...) as well as good lights for reading. I slept like a baby and was ready to get up and face the next day's travel refreshed and well rested. Thank you Marriott LAX.....
“Excellent Value & Clean!!” We were impressed as soon as we pulled in to check in! The hotel was clean, the lobby was nice, and our room was spacious & clean.

“finally a chic and comfortable hotel in nyc that won't break the bank!” I was a bit skeptical when my husband and I sat down to book our hotel in NYC for a wedding. Last trip, I was less than impressed by the overpriced, small hotel room that my husband had booked for us in trendy SoHo. However, after staying at Ink48 over the past weekend, I am happy to say that we've found a hotel in NYC that I would LOVE to stay in again. First of all, we arrived a bit early, but really needed to get into a room so that we could get ready for the wedding. The front desk was wonderful--professional and helpful, and actually upgraded us so that we could get into a room faster. The room itself was heaven---floor to ceiling windows overlooking the river, a bathroom which I swear was bigger than the last hotel room entirely that I stayed in in NYC, and a soft and comfortable king sized bed. I love the bathrobes in the room--animal print could be cheesy, but it was actually perfect for the chic vibe. We had a soaking tub and rainfall shower in the room, and I've never enjoyed getting ready for a wedding more. And the location--yes, a bit strange at first--you're surrounded by all of the car dealerships in NYC, but it's a comfortable walk to times square and the rest of NYC. My only minor complaints were that there was no turn down service--so late night we were struggling to pull the shades over those gorgeous huge windows, and the next day housekeeping woke us up at 9 AM after our late night of partying to clean the room, and proceeded to come back twice to see if we were out yet, despite it being our check out day. But that's really it--overall, we loved the place, and we'll definitely be back.

“Very Relaxing!” I was going to be in the area and the Rancho Bernardo Inn had a decent corporate rate through my corporate travel office. Normally, I'm a chain hotel guru and love to get my points, so I was bit sceptical about not earning any points with my week long stay. Let me just say that this place is very relaxing and a nice change from the chain hotels. Now, its no Bellagio, but very comfy rooms, beautiful location, great food, great staff and very relaxing atmosphere! Even though I won't be gaining any points this stay from my chain hotel friends, I left the Rancho Bernardo Inn much more relaxed than when I arrived.

“Excellent Property” Very nice property. I had a grand deluxe room on the 6th floor with a very pretty view of Connecticut ave. The staff were very cheery and helpful. The bar is very classy. I have a couple minor complaints: 1) They only bring bottled water to the room during turn-down. I really wanted some water when I checked in and there was none. So I went for the mini bar... 2) ...which brings me to point #2, the mini bar is empty. It contains only a tented sign saying that if i want something I should call down to room service/front desk. Not having even one bottle of water in the room prior to turn-down is unacceptable. Also, I was kind of annoyed at the empty fridge masquerading as a mini-bar. 3) Parking was nearly $50 a night. That said, I would certainly stay here again.

“Good Weird Hotel” OK here it is. Good - Location, room layout, kitchen, water view. Bad - Certain staff feel that they are doing you a favor to help you - not Shavar sp? he was great and the reason we may stay again. Others - not so great. Rooms were cleaned well but not vacuumed well. Go figure. BUT you get a vacuum in the room so go to it. This place is in many ways a hotel in name only. It is 1/2 a converted apartment bldg shared with tenants of the apartment in the rest. The hotel staff and apartment are different. No bellman for hotel guests. Concierge is limited in scope and hours. $50 charge for late checkout. WARNING: Call ahead if checking in late - be sure you room is ready.

“Beautiful hotel” Great location, great hotel, nice staff. Beautiful view of the Baltimore Inner Harbor. Good restaurant in the lobby. Only downfall was the extremely overpriced parking. Even though I stayed over night, I went over the 24 hour limit and ended up paying an extra 14 dollars for an extra hour and half.

“Great location, service and amenities need work.” The location was great, as I prefer to be away from the madness of mid-town and Time Square, with subwayu stops within a few blocks in either direction. Countless places to eat and shop within a few blocks. The facilities were spotlessly clean. The breakfast was adequate, but some healthy choices such as fruit and yogurt would have been nice. The small kitchenette was great, but needs such basics as a sharp knife. The television and internet reception was also spotty, perhaps because my room was in the back. And the front desk was less than helpful when I inquired about such simple things as the options for airport transportation. Overall, a good deal in a good location.

“Nice stay” Stayed here for 2 nights in May 2009. I also stayed here in 2006 and enjoyed it just as much. This was an older Doubletree Hotel that was extensively renovated and modernized a few years ago into a 4 Star Hilton. I was upgraded do the executive level both for this stay and during my previous stay in 2006. The executive lounge has snacks and complimentary non-alcoholic beverages. A continental breakfast is served until 10 on weekends but the food disappears fast. Self-parking is $14/night. There is a upper level terrace pool, I did not use it but it looked nice. The rooms feature private balconies and have views of the Galleria area office and condo buildings. Rooms are good sized and with all the amenities you would expect of a 4 star property, bathrooms appear to have been modernized with the renovation and feature granite vanities. Rooms seemed very quiet. The hotel tends to have good weekend deals through its website. There are numerous restaurants and shopping opportunities adjacent to the hotel and easy access to Loop 610. You can get pretty much anywhere in Houston in 15 to 20 minutes from here.

“Great location for both business and leisure” Right next to the convention center and a short walk to the gaslamp district for night life. All of the rooms have been recently renovated, my room had a large walk in shower but no bathtub. Some portions of the south tower is still being renovated and the restaurant is still closed due to the renovation. Super friendly staff from the moment you walk in to the front desk staff, valet parking attendants, and housekeeping. Ask for higher floor rooms overlooking the marina in the newly renovated south tower.

“Impressed with the Drury” I have never stayed at a Drury Inn before, and overall I was impressed. Very clean bathrooms, free popcorn and cokes until 10PM, free wifi, and a pretty good breakfast. Beds were comfortable, and I even liked the out-of-style recliner they had in the room. This hotel is around a ton of restaurants. If you *have to be* in San Antonio, this may be a good option for you. I do think they should get a new name!!! Who wants to stay at a "Drury"?

“Not really good or bad” This hotel was very inexpensive so I decided to stay here. It really wasn't spectacular, but it also wasn't even remotely bad. The room was clean. The front desk staff was friendly. There was free Internet, but it wasn't the strongest. It is off of the highway, and it can be pretty loud due to the traffic.

“Nice hotel, very kitsh” The hotel (or is it a large B&B?) is locateed in a couple of old houses in a beautiful residential area along Balboa Park. The decor is resolutely kitsh, it is a matter of taste of course. Upon entering the room, one is struck first by the decor, and at the same time by the excessive smell of air freshener. That, too, is a matter of taste, but breathing these chemicals all night long cannot be very healthy. I did not like the envelope requesting a tip for the maid, to be handed at the desk on check-out. Don't they pay their staff? The bed was good, wifi was clear, there were a fridge, coffee machine, microwave, and everything was very clean. Continental breakfast is brought to the room, which is nice. Parking is on the street, easy to find.

“Central location convenient to all” This was my second stay at this hotel in the city, I really liked the location since you can walk to the T, many stores, bars and restaurants. The front desk staff was excellent. You feel like a local when you stay at the this smaller hotel. Check out Thornton's for a budget breakfast a few blocks away.

“Great location, not-so-great hotel” Overall, not a bad hotel - Positives : clean room, comfortable beds, nice shower. AC works great and the location is fantastic. Negatives : lobby/valet under construction which makes for loud noises during the day. The worst part of the hotel is the elevators - they seriously made us miserable during the stay. It took an average of 5 minutes to get an elevator - always big lines in the lobby, and then it took 4 minutes on average to get to the 20th floor. Very slow. The price is nice, but I would hesitate to stay here again mostly because of the elevators.

“Completely worth it” The idea of getting a 3-year old out of bed to make an early-morning flight was a little too much to handle, so I booked the Westin at DTW the night before we left on vacation. I've walked past the Westin's entrance in the Delta terminal at DTW a hundred times and was always thought it would be very convenient. I was right. What I didn't realize is what a top-notch Westin it was. The price was higher than surrounding hotels, but the room I selected had 10-days of valet parking included. It was completely worth it. The biggest plus is convenience. To get to the hotel you drive to the Delta departure concourse at DTW. At the end of the passenger drop-off is the valet station and entrance to the Westin. Best thing ever. You literally walk right into the terminal and they valet your car for the duration of your trip. This feature has to be worth at least $100 in time-savings and convenience. The hotel was beautiful, calming, contemporary and comfortable. The lobby is 4-stories tall and beautiful. Westin beds are always comfy and this hotel was no exception. My Starwood Preferred Guest Gold status got us a complimentary cocktail at the hotel bar (up to $15), and we were upgraded to the executive floor. It's the top floor and features a lounge that is open for breakfast and happy hour. My only disappointment is that there weren't complimentary cocktails in the lounge (or I couldn't find them). There were, however, plenty of snacks and soft drinks. There is a security line at the hotel (open from 7 a.m. to 7:45 p.m.) with direct access into the terminal. If you are checking bags, however, you need to access the terminal from the valet entrance (not as convenient, but still very easy to access). Since we stayed the night before our flight, we requested terminal passes to enter the terminal and have dinner and drinks. We also used that time to walk around DTW (a beautiful airport) with my 3-year old son. We watched the planes, rode the tram, walked in the light tunnel between concourses, etc. It was a great little field trip that wore him out for the night! If you want to enter the terminal the day before a flight, you need to request access at the front desk before 7:30 p.m.. They give you a pass to get through security, however you're subjected to automatic pat-down and additional screening to make sure you're not on the no-fly list. Not a big deal, but we were surprised by all the fuss at security. Upon our return a week later, getting our car back was effortless and was delivered to the valet checkpoint within 5 minutes. I have never had such an easy time leaving the airport. I had such a great experience at the Westin DTW that I'm actually looking forward to the next time I have a super early flight!

“Great Location, Crappy Staff and Old Rooms” This is a difficult review to write. I love the location of this hotel, but the staff is full of themselves and could care less about you and any of your issues. I have some very specific issues that I am not happy about. 1. I am a Platnium member and requested a late check out. I was told, we don't care who you are, we are not extending the check out time. OK...that sets the table for the rest of this. 2. Around 6 am, if you want your car from the Valets, it's next to impossible. I asked when the valet's come to work and was told they are there 24/7. Hmmm. On the Valet ticket is a number to call, however, there is no answer no matter what time you dial the number. I had to ask every day at the front desk for my car and they dialed a different number. I asked about the number to dial and they said we have our own number! I had to wait 15 +++ minutes to for my car every morning. At 6 am, I am not really interested in waiting 15 ++ minutes for my car. I am also not in a mood to play games about my car. 3. I was "upgraded" to a room at check in. I found the room to have no fan in the bathroom, also no emergency lock on the door and this is an "upgraded room". My wife would not stay in the room if the door didn't have the bar that was another line of protection. I didn't care, but I imagine that a lot female travlers would like the extra protection. The rooms are very old and the housekeeping staff doesn't replace the drinking cups in the room. In a 4 day stay, the housekeeping staff replaced the drinkng cups only once. I am guessing their attempt to save a 10 cents on plastic drinkng cups. These are minor issues, but they add up to the fact that the hotel doesn't pay attention to details. The rooms at the hotel are not the cheapest and I think for the price, this isn't worth it. I can say that upon my return to San Diego, although I am Platinum Ambassador (formerlly Royal Ambassador) that I will not stay at this hotel. I like the location, but the staff is uppity and I don't need attitude from same.

“Typical Embassy Suites Needs Some Management Focus” This Embassy Suites property is typical for this Hilton brand. One's rating of the location, as is the case for any hotel, is in the eye of the beholder, depending on why one is in DC. I would typify the location as not very close to any one thing, but reasonably close to a lot of things. Going north on 22nd, one is in a pleasant residential neighborhood, with Dupont Circle and the Dupont Circle Metro about 10-15 minutes away walking. Going south on 22nd, one is on M street, which, moving to the West, takes one by the swank hotels that claim to be but are not in Georgetown, and then in Georgetown itself. The Mall is walkable to the South. Going East on M or L reaches a lot of potential destinations. Like most Embassy Suites, the character of this hotel changes vastly from weekend/Holiday to weekday. During the week it is typically business-oriented with the usual business type travelers. One is likely to see business meetings or gatherings taking place in the spread out lobby, and all is low key and under control. On weekends/holidays, the hotel turns into more of a zoo, as families quite reasonably descend upon the hotel en masse because the suites provide an excellent way to house vacationing families and the rates are discounted. Thus, one is likely to see many, many families and children running around loudly, much longer lines at the "manager's reception" (more on that below) and the free breakfast. Whether this is a plus or a minus depends on your view of families and children. As I have seen at other Embassy Suites, the "manager's reception" has gone cheap, with a few desultory bowls of chips and party mix and maybe some celery sticks. No attempt to spend more and make this more of a broad offering of appetizers, etc. The staff at the front desk admits that hotel parking is a structural issue. The small garage under the hotel has only room for about 100 cars, so you can be frozen out and forced to use the parking garage down the street at the Ritz Carlton if it is full. Even if you get one of the coveted spaces below for $30 a night, you may end up not being able to find a space, or having to park in an aisle, etc. The front desk staff at this property is not as uniformly trained in superb customer service and customer engagement as is the case elsewhere, meaning that your interaction is a crap shoot depending on the personality of the person you get. On at least one occasion in our recent stay, the person at the front desk was condescening and not friendly. More management attention is warranted on this front. Inexplicably, the soaring interior lobby is kept dark during the day and at night; management has made the decision to keep many of the interior lights off. For breakfast, they turn them on. The exercise room is pretty good for this type of property, with enough treadmills and weights, and one universal weight machine.

“Great Place, Super Location” This hotel is a short walk to the popular Gaslamp District. The rooms are spacious and beds are comfortable. Shower pressure is great. The breakfast buffet is wonderful and at a good price. All hotel staff were very friendly and willing to help. This is a great place to stay while visiting San Diego.

“Great value, rooms feel a little outdated vs Residence Inns” Let me start by saying we had a great stay here, and you really should consider it an option. Great Central location on 34th and 3rd Street, although taxi cab drivers aren't always sure where it is!! Like other reviews what makes this aparthotel is the staff - such a warm and genuine welcome really made it feel home from home, and a can do attitude was really refreshing. They were genuinely interested in us and wanting to make sure we were ok. We had a skyline suite on the 28th floor with fantastic views over the Chrysler Building (see pic). The suite was comfortable, spacious and airy but could do with some upgrading. A really nice touch was a complimentary wine and cupcake gift to wish us a happy anniversary, which was also wished to us on arrival vy the front desk. I would definitely recommend getting a suite as it gives you a good sized lounge area, with couch and chair, (couch turns into a sofa bed), desk area, and small kitchenette which comes equipped with crockery and utensils, fridge, cooker, coffee cup machine and microwave. There are some great delis and D'Agostino Supermarkets within a couple of blocks walks which made a great change to eating out and saved $$$'s! A good size TV with channels to cater for all ages and tastes as well as the usual in room TV services. The main bedroom has a good sized king bed or there is a queen - queen option too, which would make the room feel smaller. Loved the pilliow menus which helped for a comfortable sleep. Functional and spacious bathroom with good powerful shower. Having just stayed at a Residence Inn what was noticeable was the age of the property and I felt that for $300 a night, the hotel could do with a refurb to modernise room, air con system, kitchen equipment and general security. Equally the noise insulation was poor (both from room to room - very easy to hear other people conversations, and from the general traffic noise/sirens/car horns of New York traffic) and ear plugs are provided in the bedroom drawers. What was pricey was the internet at $13.95/24hours - especially as other chains now give this as free - in fact this was the first hotel on my US trip I had to pay for internet. So be aware. Other TA reports mention problems with lifts/elevators at this property - I didn't have to wait for more than a couple of minutes at any time and this was with 3 out of 4 in operation. There were signs on each floor asking you to call front desk if you had been kept waiting for a lift so they could send up to you which was a nice touch. What particularly impressed me was security at the hotel. We had an early departure and it was like fort knox to get in and out - which was a great touch and something staff clearly took seriously. As for location of the hotel, you are a few blocks away from Empire State Building, the 6 line at 33rd and 4th Street which gets you to all the sights and attractions. All in all I'd be back but I hope Affinia do some investment to bring the rooms up to date.

“Wonderful rooms & staff, awesome full complimentary breakfast” Beautifully decorated rooms include a full kitchenette, with a stainless fridge and dishwasher, granite counters, nice living-room seating area. Very quiet - never heard any neighbors while I was in my room. The staff are extremely helpful. Great location for convention goers. Short walk to the Greater Columbus Convention Center on High St. Cab ride is between $5 and $6, which we did take advantage of because the sidewalks on High St. were icy. Overall, this is a very nice place to stay for the money!

“Westin Overnight Stay” This is a large hotel off of Times Square so it is a busy area. There are not many good restaurants around just standard fare but what is close is the subway. From the Westin to downtown or uptown was a breeze. It was also within walking distance of Bryant Park and the New York Public Library as well as both Penn Station and Grand Central Station. The room was small, but because I am a Starwoods Gold Card member it was free and they included an upgrade to a higher level floor which placed us above the street noise. The beds were great, the shower heads (two of them ) made no sense (and one was not working). Staff was friendly and provided information about places to eat and shop. If you like movies there are 25 screens on this street. It was a nice stay and the location was Terrific!

“Excellent Location...Great Value” We took the advice of others and tried the Talbott. We agree that the location is ideal,only a few blocks to Michigan Avenue, Water Tower Place, Bloomingdale's (900 North) and Rush Street. We found the staff to be very professional and friendly. The corner room we had was very spacious, with a large sitting area as well as a large bath. It was very quiet (our room was at the back of the property). The only down side is the so-called free continental breakfast. It was pretty pathetic...some cold cuts, cheese, corn flakes, juice and coffee. Do yourself a huge favor and walk across the street to Feast. Their breakfast was fantastic and they also serve lunch and dinner.

“Perfect experience at the Westin!” I got my room for an incredibly low rate on Priceline so definitely check that out when it comes time to book. The hotel is smack in the city center, near the waterfront, restaurants and shops as well as the light rail and monorail to Seattle Center and about a million trolleys and buses. I spent $2.50 taking the light rail from the airport to Westlake, and then had about a three minute walk to the hotel. Can't get easier than that. The hotel is great - try to ask for a room on the floors that are higher up so you can have a view (my view was of the monorail, though a friend of mine had a gorgeous view of the water and mountains.). They were very accommodating and allowed me to check in early and check out late without any fees, which was awesome. Internet was a bit pricey (about $10/day) but they have this deal where if you deny housekeeping you get a $5 voucher for food and beverages...I spent mine at the cafe downstairs in the north tower, which was delish. The beds were super comfortable...almost TOO comfortable. Everything was very clean. Room service (I got breakfast) was expensive but very good. The pool and fitness center were both excellent. I can't think of anything to complain about...it was THAT good. :) I'd definitely stay again and will without a doubt recommend it to my friends.

“Now I've see it all......a four star diguised as a Super 8” To put this review in perspective we live west of Austin but try to stay in town prior to trips. We normally stay at the Intercontinental on 7th street but we thought we'd try this because of the almost unbelievable reviews. We were heading to Southern Cal for a wedding which was being held at the Hyatt in Long Beach where we also stayed. Let's put it this way. With the exception of location this Super 8 put the Hyatt to shame in every area including service. In fact, when we got to Long Beach we discovered that the Hyatt had lost our reservations (another story altogether). In addition to the great rooms, free wi-fi and all the other amenities we parked our cars at the hotel cheaper than airport parking and they both dropped us off and picked us up from the airport. It's almost too good to be true. Two thumbs way up for the owners of this property.

“Location can't be beat - size is amazing for NYC” This is my go-to hotel each and every time I'm in NYC. It's smack down in the middle of everything including my favorite office and Del Frisco's Steak House. It has all the excitement of the bright lights and big city. And, the space...holy cow...for NYC, this is the biggest room you will ever find. Not much in terms of other amenities. But, as they say in NY....location, location, location.

“Wonderful Hospitality” The staff at this hotel go out of their way to accommodate guests. They are polite, informative, courteous and extremely helpful. The service in the restaurant was awesome, with an excellent cuisine to choose from. Would highly recommend this hotel and it's facilities.

“This is our third visit! Not fancy, but fabulous!” This was our third visit to the Blue Sea Lodge on Pacific Beach. During the off-season it's quiet and relaxing. We felt like we had the motel and beach to ourselves. Yes, it's crowded and pretty noisy during the summer months, but we left our door open to the beach all night during this visit and heard very little noise. Service is terrific. We checked in early without a problem. Our room was a bit small and they moved us to a larger one on the second floor right away. This place isn't fancy or glamorous, but if you're looking for a great place to stay that's right on the beach and close to lots of restaurants, bars, and things to do, you'll love it! Our room was equipped with a microwave and small refrigerator. There is a grocery store and liquor store within walking distance. My husband enjoyed sitting out on the balcony, drinking his beer, and watching the people go by. We didn't even bother to rent a car because there are so many things to do within walking distance. If you bring a car, they do charge for parking.

“Great Place to Stay” My husband and I stayed here for four nights in May 2011. I was really worried reading some of the previous reviews, but found the hotel to be perfect for us. The staff was very friendly and accommodating, the room was spacious and clean and the location was convenient (three blocks to closest metro). We would definitely stay here again on our next trip to DC.

“Nice Hotel and great staff, still nothing much in the area” Stayed here for 4 nights in June 2010 for business. The hotel which was once a Wyndham Hotel has been renovated by Hilton and it looks good. It has a vast lobby area and seems to get a lot of convention business. The hotel is used a lot by local companies like Haliburton to house personnel that are taking training in preperation becoming contract workers in Iraq and Afganistan, but there was also a convention of teenage girls that are on school dance teams (how is that for an interesting combination). The workout room was bigger and a lot nicer than the old hotel and the outdoor pool on the second floor also looked very well maintained. The lobby bar was converted from a sports bar to a wine bar, which is too bad, because the pool tables are gone and that was one of the few fun things to do there. Now it is just a bar with lots of TV's like every other bar. The area around the hotel is still bleak, although it looks like they are doing some renovation of the Greenspoint Mall across the road, which the locals refer to as the Gunspoint Mall, since there has been a high incidence of crime around its parking lots. The hotel is safe, but I wouldn't go wandering to far around the area. The staff at the hotel was super nice from start to finish. If your buisiness takes you to the Greenspoint area I would recommend the hotel as a nice place to stay, but not a tourist spot (are there really tourists to Houston?) Don't even think about going to this hotel without having a car.

“One Night Was Not Enough” We called the hotel directly to book a last minute Saturday night reservation because we were meeting friends in the North End and did not to bother driving back to the North Shore. Everything during our stay was perfect! Valet greeted us upon arrival to park our car and front desk registration was speedy and pleasant. The interior of this hotel is beautiful with warm tones and gorgeous views of Boston Harbor. The rooms are tastefully done, spacious and modern. Our King bed did not dissapoint with lots of pillows and just the right amount of "fluff". We didn't spend a lot of time in the room, however, I would definitely recommend this property to tourists and out of town business travelers. The location is perfect for exploring Boston. there is an abundance of restaurants/shops and tourist sights are all within walking distance.

“Art deco masterpiece refitted to modern use, and pet friendly” We stayed at the Palomar mainly because it is pet friendly and also located in the center city.The hotel was terrific. It is in a remodeled 1929 art deco office building known as the Architects Building. There are 28 floors but four very speedy elevators. In addition to taking our pet, the hotel has a nice fitness facility on site, really good wi-fi, and excellent room service. The lobby is a pleasant place to wile away a few hours. The only small complaints we have is that the numbers on the phone were so small as to be unreadable, and the maid service was slow one day- we usually walk the dog while they clean, and I had to be outside int the cold for a couple of hours. We will stay here again and look for other Kimpton hotels around the US. We had a favorable experience in the LA Palomar.

“Not as bad as I expected from the reviews” This hotel was chosen by someone else. We needed one near to Imperial Beach, and the one we had stayed at before was no longer there. After this was mentioned to me I checked, as always, on Trip Advisor and I was not happy. But, to be fair, the place isn't as bad as some of these reviews make it sound. It was clean, and quiet, and the breakfast wasn't great but was certainly more than some slices of stale bread or whatever a previous review said...it was comparable to other continental affairs in chain motels - hot and cold cereals, toast, English muffins, Danish pastry, juices and tea and coffee, maybe fruit (I don't recall as I don't take the fruit). Although it was too chilly to use the pool it looked well-kept and clean. The landscaping, what there is of it, was neat, trim and attractive - flowers, palms, manicured lawn. The negatives can be summed up as such: - Neighbourhood isn't great. Not really down, but a little dicey looking here and there. It wasn't enough to scare me, however...I didn't intend to go wandering. -Service is spotty. I needed a phone book for a local number and there was no book in the room, so I went downstairs and asked. I was told the book might be by the t.v., not the phone; the desk clerk told me he didn't have one (as he flipped through something that looked an awful lot like one to prove that to me). Why he didn't just offer to look the number up for me (online or whatever he does) was beyond me. When I returned later and told him no, there was no phone book by the t.v. or anywhere, he offered to have a book sent up to the room. I told him I was going out then and needed the number before I left, so there was no use in sending a book up. If there were books available, why didn't he just give me one the first time? I ended up looking up the number in a weatherworn book hanging from one of the last remaining pay phones on the planet in front of a 7-11 on Palm Avenue...the next day, however, when I went down in need of something, it was the owner at the desk.
