What a difference. He was almost military in his yes-ma'am-immediately! demeanor. If he'd been on when I needed the phone number, I wouldn't have been squinting and fighting the sea breeze with the book. - Weird Microwave Setup. The room had a fridge and microwave, both very clean. However, the microwave was not plugged in and in no way would reach the outlet from its perch on the t.v. We had to actually move the microwave at least five feet and crawl to get the thing plugged in. There was some graffiti on the bathroom wall which it was obvious they had tried to remove and traces of it remained. Otherwise the room was quite clean. For the price paid, this was not a bad deal. I give the negatives in detail so that you can see they aren't that bad.

“"We were overbooked . . ." or "Don't get too comfortable at the bar just yet, sir."” Arrived after midnight to be told no room, due to hotel being overbooked. News to me. News to my firm's travel department. Options were a Radisson three miles away or some place in Montebello (!). Ultimately got a room, on their nickel, at Beverly Hilton. Almost $100 in cab fare to that hotel and back to downtown the next day. And this from a preferred hotel for my firm. So be careful.

“Residence Inn Excellent Stay” My husband and I stayed one night at the Residence Inn. Excellent staff, rooms, breakfast. This establishment does the Marriott name proud! We also stayed at a "higher" star Marriott in Columbus another night and did not have the same experience. (very disappointed) Stay here if you want to be near Easton Mall and have a wonderful experience.

“Dirty little hotel” There was hair all over the comforter. Upon closer inspection the comforter and sheets were stained and had holes in them. Even the towels were ragged. Very skimpy on bath products. Room very small. Nice decor overall.

“Great Location/Very Busy Hotel” My husband and I stayed at the Hilton San Francisco Union Square just last night for one night. The location is great but the hotel is very big and very busy. We had a room on the 34th floor with a great view but the room (as I'm sure all rooms in San Francisco are) was quite small. We're Hilton Gold members so we got to use the Honors check-in. Had we not been Honors members, the check-in line was very, very long. The check-in process went smoothly and our room was ready when we arrived. We visited the hotel bar for a drink before bed. Very big martinis with a very big price tag! We had the continental breakfast buffet in the morning which was very good. I pressed the spa button the telephone in the room and got a recorded message telling me that there wasn't a spa and that if I wanted spa services, I should contact the concierge. If you're going to San Francisco and want to be centrally located to the main tourist attractions, this is your place. If you want peace and quite, look elsewhere.

“Wonderful Location, great check-in experience” We came here for our anniversary and were a little apprehensive. It far our visit exceeded expectations. You can't find a better place near the Wharf, Coit Tower, Tours to Alcatraz, bus and cable cars to downtown. Maybe that's because we started with a good experience at checkin. First, our room wasn't ready yet as it should have been. So we were given courtesy drinks while we waited at the Sports Bar at the hotel. That was nice and the wait wasn't long. The woman at the front desk was so pleasant and polite. She answered numerous questions we had. The room was oustanding! It had a very high ceiling, great work desk area, and an extremely comfortable bed. It was quiet although you could hear occasional street noise (to be expected at the Wharf). We even tired out the pool and spa, although it did feel you were in a fishbowl. Checkout was a little long. The hotel is close to the wharf, Shops, a World Market, Cable Cars, Columbus street for a bus to Union Square and AT&T Park - along with all the fun cafes and restaurants towards Coit Tower and North Beach. We'd definitely come back again!

“What is an airport hotel?” Definition: (A hotel near the airport. The hotel does not have to be connected to the airport (although some are) or even adjacent to it; it could be located up to five miles away. Most airport hotels have a shuttle to and from the terminals.) Well, reading the definition above, this place is for SURE an airport hotel. Nothing more actually. The person who checked me in was not very friendly. Seemed bored with his job. Bummer. My room was on the 3rd floor overlooking McDonald's. The hallways were in pretty bad shape. Did not feel much like a hotel hallway, felt more like an old, creepy, condominium hallway. The smell. Ahhh the smell. Almost all Holiday Inn's smell the same. Not bad, but not good. Just Holiday Inn "ish". Great blackout curtains in the room! But I had trouble with all the outside noise. I had NO idea McDonald's was such a noisy place, at all hours! There was SO much noise all night long. Bass bumping nearby etc.. I hate that. They need better window sealing! Free WiFi. Tried for 2.5 hours to get a wake up call. The phone just rang off the hook for over 2 hours straight. Sometimes it would go to a strange voice mail. There was a clock in the room, but it was flashing some incorrect time since my arrival and I refused to set it. I grabbed one of those "Do Not Disturb" things from the door to place on the knob and it was NASTY! I mean, gum or something on it and some disgusting looking stains. Bathroom is small, but WAY more updated than the halls. Tub looks pretty worn out. Had ZERO washcloths in the bathroom. Love the light sensors that turn the light on for you as you approach. GREAT shower head, really nice flow. And of course, skinny, wimpy towels. McDonald's really IS 25 steps away from the lobby if you are into that kinda thing. Egg McMuffin, MMmmmmm. If you can get a room here for $90/night or less, go for it, for the convenience. Most airport hotels I have stayed at are never great and that is unfortunate. But this place will do the job, and nothing more.

“Adequate lodging, horrible service with an Attitude” We stayed at the Renaissance while attending a meeting at the Convention Center. There were a number of problems with the service we received. On attempting to check in at 2 pm (stated check in time is 4pm), I was told the room was not ready. The reservation was in my companion’s name and I arrived with a signed letter from her and a copy of the front/back of her AmEx used to make the res. They requested phone authorization from her but refused to use my cellphone when I had her on the line and offered it to the clerk, instead insisting that I hang up so that the clerk could dial herself. When that was settled, I asked about putting my Marriott Rewards number on the room and was told I couldn’t do that. Then I was told (not asked if I wanted) to leave my carryon with the bellman. Excuuuse me! When my companion arrived later that evening, four clerks were standing around behind the desk, she was the only guest waiting, and nobody offered to help her. After 10 minutes, she requested and got assistance. The room was a good quarter mile from the elevator, as noted by a previous review, and had a distinct though stale odor of smoke (non-smoking room). On the positive side, the room was spacious with a comfortable bed, nothing fancy but the a/c worked well, there was always hot water, and there even was a window that opened, a rarity nowadays. The room service meals arrived promptly as ordered, and the restaurant brunch was excellent and smoke-free. The concierge (Marie) was gracious and helpful with restaurant recommendation. We had prearranged a late checkout at booking, but when we called on the morning of departure were told that it wasn’t available unless we paid for it, and then when we offered to pay were told that in fact it wasn’t available at all. After a lengthy discussion with the supervisor, who was very rude and insulting, she finally conceded to allow us to stay til 2p, not 4p as requested. As a result we ended up in the TV lounge, where I was watching sports while my companion took a brief nap until rudely awakened by hotel security (because sleeping was not allowed). We weren’t from off the sidewalk, we had just dropped $860 at the hotel for a 3-day stay and this just was the last straw. Needless to stay, on our next visit to the Inner Harbor we will select another hotel.

“great hotel, great location, great staff-easy access to Houston expressways” This is a great Marriott property. Really nice staff; we had a program glitch and they were very helpful to us with business services. Location right across from the Galleria...easy to get to from the Houston expressways. Little cafe and bar in lobby had great food and service also.

“If it's inexpensive, it's a fine place. Not amazing. Not bad.” I've stayed at better Doubletrees and at Doubletrees that aren't as nice as this one. It's fine. A portion of it is in an old building, and so some of the rooms are very small. On the plus side, the bathroom was big. The furnishings are a bit dated and a bit tired, but it was nothing to really complain about. I really found it bizarre that they consciously chose a wallpaper that mimicked painted cinder block, giving the common halls the feeling of a dormitory. The breakfast was top notch. I'd stay here again, but if the other Boston Hiltons are the same price, I'd pick them.

“Lacking in amenities and service” I stayed immediately before Hurricane Irene. The elevator set up was slow and annoying, with one reserved for the bar and one that didn't seem to be in use at all. The minibar instead of a refrigerator was useless, particularly as there are no ice machines and the ice I requested when I checked in hadn't arrived by the time I checked out. The coffee maker/minibar area was lit up with no apparent on/off switch, so it glowed all night long. The television had only basic cable and WiFi was $15 per day. The worst was the night of August 26, when airlines began to announce flight cancellations. I called the front desk to ask if I could extend my stay rather than check out as planned on August 27. I was told they would check and call me back. Thirty minutes later, I still hadn't received word so I called again and was told they were not extending any guests and were holding all available rooms for staff. This left me scrambling, after midnight, to find a hotel for the following night. The discourtesy in not extending my stay, and in not even bothering to let me know, was the last straw.

“Great hotel” Had a wonderful stay here. The room was nice and clean. They seem to emphasize good night's sleep here. Upon check-in, the guy boasted about how the beds have seven layers of sheets or whatever for extra comfort. Well, the beds are indeed really comfortable. And the room came with sleep amenities (ear plugs, linen spray, relaxation CD)... all nice touch. In-room Internet access was free, which you don't get for free usually at hotels of this caliber. The thing that really impressed me was that the reception guy had four bottles of spring water brought up to my room for free, when I asked him where I could go buy water nearby. So the service here is really good, too. The hotel is conveniently located near the subway and near the regional rail's Suburban Station. The only negative was the tiny bathroom and the shower that didn't give me as hot a water as I desired even at the hottest end of the dial. But it was still warm enough.

“Average for an airport hotel, though I expect more from Westin” On this particular trip, I stayed at both the Westin LAX and the Sheraton LAX. Typically, when I compare a Westin and a Sheraton I expect the Westin to come out on top but in this case the Sheraton was the clear winner because of the gym and pool quality; plus the Sheraton has a Starbucks in the lobby while the Westin does not have a coffee shop. Rooms at the Westin are pleasingly decorated with seemingly new furniture. The gym is adequate for a quick workout, but could use an expansion/update. There are dumbells, a few weight machines, and a few cardio machines. The pool is adequate but unremarkable, and the hot tub definitely needs an update (missing tiles, rust, etc). The hotel has a Daily Grill restaurant in the lobby, which offers pricey high-calorie steakhouse fare, as well as the requisite astronomically-priced hotel breakfasts. This is another area where the Sheraton comes out on top, as that hotel has a Starbucks in the lobby which offers lighter breakfast alternatives. As of July 2011, the hotel is in the midst of renovations, so about half of the lobby is closed off; perhaps once renovations are complete, there will be more/better amenities here.

“...das Hotel in New York” Hier ist meiner Meinung nach eines der besten Hotels in New York. Leider reichte meine Geldbörse nicht für eine Übernachtung, dennoch habe ich mir alles genau angesehen. Als Geheimtipp kann ich das Drehrestaurant empfehlen. Einfach einen Drink nehmen und über den Dächer mit Blick über ganz NY anfangen zu träumen. Untern der Time Square, dann der Blich auf den Hudson usw. Einfach traumhaft schön. Einen Aufenthalt kann ich bei Dämmerung empfehlen, wenn NY sich in sein Lichtermeer taucht.

“Beautiful Historic Hotel” Perfect stay in the city. We arrived early, and our room was not ready, but they could place us in a lower-class room immediately. We chose that, and were thrilled with the room, a standard deluxe king (no pull-out couch). The room was much larger than expected, though by the chart on the back of the door, it was definately one of the largest on our floor. Bathroom was spaceous as well, and of course the service was impeccable. If you stay, make sure to wander through the event rooms--lovely art deco decor worth exploring! they also managed to squeeze in a last-minute half hour massage, also excellent.

“OK, not great though” This is an attractive, relatively new property in Chelsea which is definitely beginning to show its wear prematurely (as well as it's less than stellar management). Rooms are fairly large for NYC standard for the price/class and the free hot breakfast is a welcome bonus. Bedroom/bathroom furnishings are modern and comfortable. Got a good rate at the time, so it was worthwhile. Chelsea location is great in my opinion, although the block the hotel is on is not the most attractive or desirable in the neighborhood. The not so good: in the 3 days & nights spent at hotel in Nov 2008, never was the room or the hallway vacuumed--and they both needed it. Room and bathroom was showing wear--marks on walls and furniture, some peeling wallpaper, etc. Nothing major or overly gross, just a bit disappointing for a property still relatively new. This is a heavily used hotel which operates with a less than appropriate cleaning/maintenance routine. It wasn't filthy, but it wasn't very clean either. For the right price, I'd probably stay here again and be willing to look past its faults. If you don't need a lot of room and only 1 bed (double or queen) will suffice, I'd recommend the GEM Hotel Chelsea first--rooms are tiny but the place is immaculate and the staff much more professional and courteous. GEM also has a better location. But it also has its shortcomings. Depends what you need in a hotel.

“Great Location, friendly staff” As its name suggests, this hotel is right on the riverwalk. Most of the city's attractions are within walking distance. The hotel offers valet parking, but you don't really need your car unless you want to explore the missions or the hill country. I really liked the interior of the hotel - lots of dark browns and reds that give it a colonial feel without being tacky. My room was spacious and had two leather chairs in addition to a desk. It wasn't a riverfront room but I could still see the river if I stood at my window. The room was very clean and confortable. The bed was soft and I slept very well. There is a cool bar next to the lobby which features one of the coolest lounges I have seen in a while. What made my stay most memorable was the friendliness of the staff from bellhop to front desk staff.

“W is No Wow but is still Kool” Check-in: Excellent. Room: Large, great bed and bathroom. Some of the furniture was scratched and needed to be refinished or replaced. Excellent TV and stereo. Wonderful restaurant for breakfast. Above average gym and VERY nice pool. One complaint: valet parking was $45.00 per nite: that is ridiculous!!!!!!!!!!!! It was the one bad note on an otherwise great stay.

“Very nice experience” Booked this hotel on Priceline and hence did not have a choice of getting a room of our choice but I certainly was very happy with the result. We stayed here when this was a Holiday Inn and the remodeling of the rooms really showed. The room was of good size and comfortable with a sofa and comfortable easy chair with an otterman. The desk area stretched from wall to wall under the windows which had modern rolling shades. The bed was very comfortable with adequate pillows. Our room was on one of the lower floors (5th) but we still had a nice view of North Beach and Coit Tower. I can only imagine what our view would be on a higher floor. Oh sure there is city noise. After all this is San Francisco. We didn't experience noise from other rooms as some other reviews complained about. There was occasional footsteps from the room above but not what I would consider excessive or bothersome. We live in the middle of several acres of land in the middle of the El Dorado National Forest with our closest neighbor several hunderd yards away so we are not used to the noise of the city but the traffic and trash collector did not bother us. The only problem we ran into was the shower took an excessive amount of time to heat to a comfortable temperature. This is really a waste of water which we can't afford to waste in Northern California. The hotel should really work on this problem as soon as possible. Since our room cost only $80.00 a night I thought that we really had a bargain for San Francisco

“Love this hotel” I think this is a fantastic hotel, and am not really sure I understand the confusion from some other reviewers about the layout. In any event, there's just something about the little extra level of service that this hotel provides that will definitely have me coming back. The rooms are a little on the small side, but very comfortable and very clean. The location is great as well -- easy walking to either downtown locations or River North, with plenty of trains nearby for some of the surrounding neighborhoods. Looking forward to returning!

“Splendid Birthday Weekend” We stayed at the Hotel Burnham in August 2011 for a birthday weekend. We loved it! The staff was excellent. We found them very friendly, personable, helpful, and all around committed to making guests feel welcomed and happy. Martin was the real standout. He went above and beyond in every way, especially in the extra touches he arranged for the birthday. Praise also goes out to Liz, Emil, Vani, Kelly, and Daniel. They were all friendly and helpful. Our room, on the second floor, was lovely. The appointments were luxurious. We enjoyed the Aveda products in the bathroom, the well-priced gourmet snacks in the mini-bar, the comfortable desk, the chaise lounge, and the lovely curtains, linens, and upholstery. Our only complaint is that the bed was a little too firm and we were woken up one night by a parking garage alarm on the other side of Washington Street. We are reasonable and understand that the bed is under the Burnham’s control, the parking garage is not. We got used to the bed, but the first night was a bit restless. The historic features and fixtures are enjoyable and make for a unique experience, but the attention to detail in the here and now are what really makes the Burnham a standout. Easily reachable from the airports by rail, the Burnham is centrally located to all the best in downtown Chicago. It was a five minute walk to Millennium Park, another ten minutes through the park to the Art Institute, a ten minute bus ride from the Burnham to the Shay Aquarium and Adler Planetarium, a fifteen minute walk to the river and a fifteen minute walk to the lakeshore. We had to take a taxi at night to and from Navy Pier, but the flagship Marshall Field (now Macy’s) was caddy corner on Washington and State Streets. The Burnham has a restaurant named the Atwood Café. We dined there one evening for dessert and one morning for breakfast. The food was good and so was the service and setting. As this was our first Kimpton experience, there were unexpected surprises like the morning Starbucks (including decaf), the house dogs and fish (Albert), and the evening wine hour. We definitely recommend the Burnham and look forward to staying there the next time we’re in Chicago.

“Great location, Noisy Rooms” Stayed here for 1 night with my parents and sister. I have to put in the disclaimer that the last hotel I stayed at was in Feb at the Conrad Chicago which was amazing so perhaps that's why I wasn't impressed. Pros: Great location right on the water, next to Seaport Village, nice pools, amazing views, comfy beds, beautiful lobby and friendly staff Cons: Thin walls in the Seaport tower (we could hear the phone ringing in the room next to us, a baby screaming for a half hour, doors slamming and the people above us stomping around), cigarette smoke coming through the vents and we were not on a smoking floor, no flat screen tv's, room decor was a bit dated. I will be trying another hotel on my next trip to SD but If you're just looking for a great location and don't really care about the room/noise so much, then this hotel will be fine for you.

“Excellent Stay” My daughter and I stayed here for 4 nights when we took in a concert in Columbus, but decided on staying in Easton as we intended to spend more time shopping than anything else. The shuttle from the airport was very quick and we had excellent drivers both ways. Check-in was very efficient and we were greeted warmly and within a few minutes we were in our room. Very spacious and clean - at first glance the beds looked terribly lumpy... turns out it was just the style of duvets they use and it was all very comfortable indeed. The comp breakfast was a good start to the day and fresh coffee was available all day from the breakfast area. Would definately recommend this hotel.

“Great location in Downtown San Jose” Stayed here and had a good time. Room was good size with VERY comfortable bed and pillows. Loved the glass Shower Stall. Nice large LCD Flat screen TV, but limited TV channels. Hotel Staff was excellent! Always available and friendly.

“Great hotel” This is a very good hotel. True Texas hospitality. Very professional, friendly staff. Beautiful "old school" interior atrium - the lobby of this hotel is spectacular. Large well appointed room. Right in the middle of downtown close to the Chevron (ex Enron) building, Continental Center, etc. afew blocks from Midtown for great restaurants and drinks as well as the basics (CVS, Rendall's grocery store, etc) The lobby bar is good. Breakfast restaurant excellent - my VP says they have the best bacon in the world. Valet parking for a fee but it is easy to park in the street at night. To me, the best downtown hotel in Houston.

“Great location. Rooms needs renovation.” I got a last minute deal at a fantastic price. The location is amazing right off two subway lines on Broadway. The staff was very friendly and iwas able to check into my room early. The rooms were very worn and tired. The rug was threadbare and the duvet cover all wrinkled. The wrought iron sink in the bathroom was rusted and the end tables were chipped. The room looked nice and long as you didn't look too close. The bed was amazingly comfortable and that's really all I cared about. I would stay here again if the price was right.

“Perfect for business meeting!” I flew into Dallas for a one-day meeting that was being held at the Grand Hyatt DFW. From check-in to check-out, the customer service was incredible. The hotel is clean and very well kept. The room was incredible and I was lucky enough to get a "run-way" view; the bathroom was HUGE!!! It was a great night sleep and a perfect experience.

“Just What We Needed” We stayed at the Sea-Tac Doubletree for one night between our Canadian vacation and our flight home. This mega hotel served its purpose perfectly. We got a super deal on it ($45) through Priceline so I didn't expect to have the Penthouse suite. We had a room on the 1st floor in the 6th wing. We had a view of the parking lot but it was very, very quiet. Bring your walking shoes and map as this hotel is really spread out. Check in was quick. The desk clerk gave great directions to our room and handed us chocolate chip cookies as we finished. This hotel must be used by flight crews quite a bit as they had their own dedicated line for checking in. When we walked through the lobby, there seemed to be quite a line up except at that check in station. The room itself was nice - what I would expect from a Doubletree hotel - although it seemed a little dated. The bathroom in particular could use some updating as it had an ancient toilet and only a shower. We took a dip in the pool and the hot tub which were in a large courtyard between several wings. Since parking was $16 per night, we decided to return our rental car a day early. We were able to catch the shuttle to the hotel after about 20 minutes but we didn't realize we could have walked there in about 10. The shuttle was smooth for ride back to the airport the next morning. What really impressed me were the employees. Every single employee we encountered said hello. This seems like an amazing feat in such a huge hotel. Congratulations!

“Good place to stay in NYC” Location can't be beat, near but not right on Times Square, walk to any Broadway theater, and an easy subway or bus ride from Lincoln Center. My room was squeaky clean, and the staff gracious. I wish hotels would supply real creamer, rather than powder. Room was on the small side, but thoughtfully equipped. I liked the internet access in the lobby. This was particularly handy for coping with the aftermath from Hurricane Sandy.

“Cool Vibe” I loved the vibe of this hotel. Very cool bar in the lobby that is visible from all floors from the open atrium. The room was comfortable with a good view. My only compliant is that the lighting is quite dark, so it's not great for make-up application! I would definitely stay here again. The area and vibe can't be beat.

“Honeymoon Night Splurge” We live in Seattle and booked the Fairmont Olympic for our honeymoon night. We booked a King Suite as we wanted enough space for our wedding party to hang out and get ready prior to our ceremony. We called the hotel directly to book and were given a modest AAA discounted rate as members. Upon booking, we advised we were staying for our wedding night and would like an early check-in if possible. The person who booked our room was very polite and professional. He noted that we were booking the "only 5-star rated hotel in the Seattle area." Check-in was okay. The person behind the counter was a little robotic with the "Welcome to the Fairmont" script and there was no acknowledgment that we were there for our wedding, which I guess we sort-of expected given the fanciness of the hotel and having given this information upon booking. We were given an early check-in without any hassle however. Our room was spacious with a bedroom and separate living area that had a couch, chair and coffee table. The decor is okay. It keeps with the old style of the hotel but we were expecting some more modern touches such as a flat-screen TV vs. the old one in the room (not that we watched any TV on our wedding night - just an observation!). The bathroom sink and faucets could be a bit nicer. The bed was comfy but not as good as some of the beds at nicer Hiltons where we've stayed in the past. The shower was very nice. The hotel did deliver a plate of chocolate-covered strawberries with a 'Congratulations' acknowledgment of our marriage. The valet parking also left us cookies & milk when we departed in the morning. Both were nice touches. After taxes and valet parking charges, we paid a little over $400 for our night's stay. In all, our stay was nice but we did not feel overly pampered or treated like royalty which, at $400/night, one might expect to a small degree.

“Not as good as advertised” The hotel lobby is very inviting. Rooms were just ok, based upon the rate we paid. The amenities were average. We "upgraded" to a deluxe king on the recommendation of the clerk in reservations at the hotel. We had a view of an alley and another building that was undergoing remodeling (glad we only had noise on Friday). When we asked about a room with a view of the Mississippi River we were told that there would be another $30 per night charge. Continental breakfast came with the room. It was hard to find a concierge on duty the weekend we were there so ended up booking our own tours. The location is good, about 1/2 block to the trolly and about 5 blocks to Beale Street.

“Decent hotel near the Phoenix airport” I probably would have given this a very good rating except our room was close to the main street and it was very noisy. It made it difficult to sleep. Ask for a room away from the main road and you will be fine. The breakfast and free internet were both good as well.

“On Chicago's front lawn” This hotel has been our choice on a couple of occasions when we have done bicycling events that started and ended at Grant Park. The most recent for the annual LATE Ride. The location is better suited for those looking to visit Millenium Park, Museum Campus or Soldier Field however it still has easy access to the loop and Mag Mile shopping. If you're looking for nightlife stick to river north and gold coast hotels. We have chosen to park our car at the Grant Park South lot a short walk north on Michigan Ave since it's cheaper than hotel parking and the in and out privilege offered by the Essex didn't concern us. Don't expect a great city view at this hotel but you can get a great lake view if you choose a east facing room. Another note is that the Chicago double decker bus tour has a stop right across the street to the north along Michigan Ave and you can purchase the hop on/off tour ticket and make a loop right back to the hotel.

“Too trendy and too noisy” This is the first time I stay in a W hotel. I thought I would love a trendy hotel like W Hollywood, but now I have a mixed feeling about it. At first sight, the hotel is very impressive with its big red logo and glamorous "living room". The room itself is not crowded in an LA standard. The bed is super comfortable, and the sound of sea is really fun. However, at night it gets incredibly noisy. I live in 11th floor, and the 12th floor is a night club which seems to be very popular. So till 3am, you'll not be able to sleep. The staff all get very anxious and angry, and I don't know why. In short, if you're looking for warm and relaxing hospitality, it's not the place. The neighborhood can get a little bit scary at night. There's a Starbucks just a block away. It gets super busy in the morning if you want a coffee and a breakfast sandwich.

“Quiet and very relaxing.” Even though we were in such close proximity to the airport (and our room faced the airport), I never heard any planes while in the room. The best way to describe this stay was "functional". The room was fine, except for the fruit flies that were present when we got there and remained for our entire 3-night stay. They weren't harmful, just annoying. Desk staff was lukewarm but OK. The did make it clear to us that they knew we booked through a vendor and not through them; not sure what was up with that. Housekeeping was OK, but probably the reason the fruit flies existed. We had each brought a glass of wine back to the room to enjoy. When finished, we rinsed them and left them to be collected the next day. Housekeeping did not remove them. The next night, the same thing and again they were not removed. By the time we checked out, we had quite a set of glasses on the settee. I've not experienced that before. We didn't complain, and actually found it a source of humor. Paying $17 per night to park was frustrating. Especially when we had to pay up front, and the gate was open half the time to any and all who wanted to park there (for free). All-in-all, I'd go back but only if the price was right. There are a lot of hotels to choose from in the area so I wouldn't go out of my way to find it again.

“Excellent and functional hotel” I stayed in this hotel for four nights during my recent business trip to Seattle. Very functional and reasonable in all aspects. Room has only shower but large screen flat TV, microwave, coffee maker and Wi-Fi are all big plus. Also I used their small gym and swimming pool. The reception people are helpful and they offer coffee and small cake during daytime. One problem is that there is no proper restaurant. They have a bar and pizzeria but they do not serve breakfast. There are coffee shops everywhere so I had no problem. I definitely come back again to this lovely hotel.

“Magical weekend stay!” It was time to leave the spouses behind and we girls decided to stay at The Iroquois, as it was exceptionally priced at one of the travel websites and a very convenient base to see the main sights. My girlfriend's first extended visit to New York City and The Iroquois made it memorable. Many thanks to Alex, who graciously upgraded our Classic Room to an Executive Suite! We stayed one night in the Classic and it was quite adequate-- clean, a good size for a NYC hotel room. Comfortable bed, fluffy towels and bathrobes and quiet. I didn't hear any noise in the hallway or from other rooms. The Suite was heavenly with a spacious living room, sofa set, desk, flat screen TV, BOSE mp3 player, complimentary half bottle of wine and sparkling water. Once again, exceptionally clean surroundings with that incredibly comfortable bed, flat screen TVr; marble bathroom with separate shower and jacuzzi tub. Turndown service was consistent with chocolates and weather card. There's a wonderful complimentary shoe shine service and that person does a great job!! We did attempt to order room service one morning and our card was not picked up; the next morning, however, breakfast was delivered promptly. Reasonable price for that breakfast, too. The entire staff is professional and pleasant. There's coffee available in the main lobby in the mornings and I could honestly say, that renovation of that lobby is finished (to give an update based on other travelers' info). This is not a large hotel (which I love) and I was extremely pleased with our stay. I recommend it highly.

“Nice Hotel with Excellent Service” I very much enjoyed my two night stay. The hotel staff is great. I stayed in a King Suite which was much bigger than I expected and had double doors that separated the room and bath from the living area. The pools were very nice and I suspect it would be a nice place to hang out by the pool. They had a pool bar that was closed when I was there in January but it looked like fun. I recommend asking for a room with a view of the pool and courtyard as opposed to the parking lot. The staff went above and beyond, I was impressed.

“Luxury Hotel in Ideal Location” Our long weekend stay at the Park Hyatt was wonderful. Arrival and check-in is very personalized and informative. We felt like they were expecting us! The common areas are more like a home than a hotel lobby. The complimentary hot beverages in the library are a nice touch. Our corner room on the 16th floor is around the corner from the elevator yet quite. The king size bed made up with featherbed and luxurious linens is remarkably comfortable. The lighting is perfect with dimmers on many switches. There’s a long window seat where you can spend the mornings watching the city come to life. The dresser and closets have ample storage. The bathrobes are fluffy and cozy. The bathroom is a delight with lots of super soft towels. The super nice shower has great water pressure. The soaking tub is fantastic. The amenities, especially the conditioner, are top notch. The hotel is located right in the middle of the high-end shopping area and right between the three most famous spots for Chicago deep dish pizza. Plus it’s very convenient for transit users. We would love to return!

“Convenient, comfortable, roomy” Overall, the room and hotel were excellent, room size was excellent, plenty of space, nice desk and working area. Wireless internet was free only in lobby area, but required a fee in room (I picked up a free signal in my room on the 6th floor which was adequate most of the time). The staff was friendly and efficient. The elevators were a tad slow, sometimes the wait was long. Nice flat screen in room, although most stations not HD, so mediocre picture quality for most stations. Not much of a view, I had a great view of a dirt lot. Other colleagues who stayed there said they were given a choice on checkin, "view or quiet". I got quiet I guess. The location is good if you need to go uptown or midtown. Overall, it served the purpose for a stay while doing business at Columbia.

“Very nice, laid back conference hotel” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency-Colorado Convention Center for three nights to attend a social studies teachers' conference. The staff was very friendly. I checked in on their automated computer system, and a staff member was present to assist me with any questions. I was able to request a higher floor and was assigned to the 20th floor. My room overlooked the downtown area, and Rocky Mountains. I was able to take some very cool pictures on the final day. The health club/spa area was very well laid out. As for the pool, it is designed as a lap pool. However, since the Hyatt is more of business/convention hotel, families are able to take advantage of it for recreational/fun purposes due to business travelers not always using it. The hot tub is outside, which I did not use because of the colder temperatures. I ate breakfast at Altitude on my final morning. It was cheaper to eat the buffet than order off the ala carte menu. Since I am not a huge breakfast eater, I was pleased with the quality of food: Cereal, fresh fruit, assorted breads, scrambled eggs, bacon, etc. Juice refills are unlimited when ordering off the buffet menu, which is a nice perk. I thought the quality of the room was of decent size. I have stayed in much smaller rooms in the past, and have no complaints of the room, bathroom or any noise. The only minor area of concern I had was housekeeping trying to get into my room before checking out (9:35am), but since I was in the room, I quickly asked them to give me more time. The hotel is a couple blocks from the 16th Street Mall; allowing the visitors to choose from a variety of shops and dining opportunities. The state capitol, art museum and CELL are only a few blocks away too. If you are coming to Denver to attend a conference at the Colorado Convention Center, the location cannot be beat. The hotel is also very convenient for attending events at Invesco Field, Coors Field or Pepsi Center. I would stay at this Hyatt again in the future for any of these reasons.

“A very nice hotel with an odd layout” Stayed one night in august on business. Location is great - close to Georgetown, Rock Creek Park, Dupont Circle and GW University. Rooms are spacious even if you are not in one of the suites. Beds are comfortable and the amenities are what you would expect for this class of hotel. This is rated a 3 star, probably because its lacking things like a pool, but if you are going for the room and not the amenities, its closer to a 4 star.

“2 Star Hotel - Safe and Clean for $60/night” Quality Inn by Choice Hotels can be hit and miss in terms of the quality of the property. This hotel property, located right by the naval station and close to the airport is a good location if you want to be on the north side of Mission Bay. This is definitely a no frills hotel - properly is quite dated and the room doors open to the outside. Bathroom was clean and the towels were thin. Internet was free as well as breakfast. Nothing to jump up and down about but the hotel is a good value for $60 a night. Would recommend for business people just needing a night's rest and moving on. May not be ideal for a week's stay.

“Brilliant!” This hotel, so close to Times Square and Broadway, is brilliant! I booked it after reading other people's reviews and I was not disappointed. We stayed for 3 nights. We had booked one king and one double. Both rooms were very spacious and nicely decorated - with some lovely photography on the walls. From my room I could see the Empire State Building and, by craning my head slightly, the Chrysler! The beds are FANTASTIC and have a lovely soft under duvet. Quiet air-conditioning and excellent double-glazing meant that the rooms were really quiet and relaxing. My kids were somewhat disappointed that I was supplied with free chocolates every night during turn-down service - but they were not! Evian water was also complimentary. Bathroom was a good size (it was so good to have a proper shower cubicle and separate tub) and spotlessly clean. Unfortunately the double wasn't quite ready when we checked in but it didn't cause a huge problem given that the king was available (so we were able to freshen up before embarking to the top of the Empire State Building). The staff on reception were pleasant (except for one rather haughty French woman) and efficient. The concierge are really good and clearly take pride in their work. The breakfast was expensive....but so good that it was worth every penny and set us up for the day. Staff were lovely - even when serving my two adolescent sons who were all kitted out in their death/heavy metal clothes! Next time I am in Manhattan I'm staying here again.

“Love it!” I need to state that I've stayed here twice but it's always been paid for my by work, so I'm not sure what they paid for the room each time. With that, I will say that I've stayed here a total of 5 nights throughout the last year and have not been disappointed. Check-in process each time was very smooth and welcoming. The staff has always asked if I needed anything and they have made sure I was taken care of. The bell staff was great as well as there was one time when my baggage was late from the airline and they made sure to update me regularly with the baggage they had. I took advantage of their wireless internet service the last time I stayed there and had no problems. Granted, you are going to pay for internet at this hotel, but I never had any problems with it. The location is probably the best part about this hotel. I loved being close to SoHo since I had to go there to shop for clothes after my airline lost my baggage for 2 straight days. There are also plenty of places to grab a drink or food nearby. I would highly recommend this place if you happen to be staying in the area.

“Average.” Massive check-in lobby. Service, not so good or non-existent. Restaurant? This is not New Orleans. Room? OK One major gripe is that we ordered breakfast for 2 people in the morning. When room service finally delivered, it was for 4 people, as we were charged for 4. After calling and speaking with the Food & Beverage Manager to rectify this situation - only after a long drawn out argument, did they refund the additional breakfast entrees. Clearly, not worth the aggravation and we're glad it was one, quick evening.

“A gem...an absolute gem” I was pleasantly surprised by this hotel. Despite all of the negative posts it turned out to be a delightful place. I am not sure why everyone is so fussy about the somewhat outdated rooms, they were clean and unique and the location could not be beat. I do not like staying in chain hotels...they are boring and very antiseptic. While here, the staff was over the top friendly and professional. I felt safe as a woman alone and my room was so funky cool. No, it is not the Marriott or Hilton...THANK GOODNESS> Any problems were quickly handled and they were minor. I made my way around town from the hotel and found it to be the best of locations. Others attending the BIO convention complained about their hotels...some four star and yet mine was perfect. The one's who complained...perhaps it makes them feel better...a bit of snobbery? For there certainly seemed to be a lot of rather wealthy folks staying at the hotel, if one could judge by the mercedes and bentleys parked in the drive and the manner of dress. I think if you like personal attention and a more european atmosphere, then this is your spot. If you like McDonalds and the same thing you have at home...then perhaps not. Thank you all who made my stay so nice. I was so nervous about the negative reviews I even emailed the corporate headquarters with my fears...they answered as did the hotel mgr within 24 hours...that set the tone for the entire trip. Never promised me anything except a nice stay and that is what I got.

“A lovely place” My boyfriend I stayed here for two nights. We really enjoyed the great location, good service, comfort environment, and elegant room here. It was a good choice and we would definitely stay here again.

“Decent hotel, great perks, kid-friendly” Stayed here for a week on business at the Medical Center The hotel is located in a business park next to an abandoned go-kart track at the intersection of two main freeways, Access around town (on and off the freeways was easy, once learned), but there was not enough parking for this busy hotel. Hotel is older, but renovations made the rooms nice. Complimentary made-to-order breakfast and manager's reception was above average and a nice perk (as were the free frozen margaritas.) I never found the business center they claimed they had - that has a computer terminal for boarding passes, but no desk or chair - you had to stand. The carpets still need to be redone or cleaned, but the room was otherwise clean, spacious, and had great temperature control (during 90+ degree weather). One of the elevators did not work and the rest were slow. Front desk staff were friendly and courteous, but failed to follow through on reported issues. The place was full of families with kids. This is not the best Embassy Suites I have stayed in but certainly not the worst. I would probably stay here again if I needed to be in this area. Would definitely recommend it for families, but not so sure about business people.

“Mixed Bag!” Stayed here for a period of 3 days. I have to say that I found the room very clean and actually spacious. AC noise tended to be a bit loud, but sometimes that comes with places that have window units. Breakfast was okay, but nicely presented. The problems that I saw were the following: the pool was really not usable. It looked murky and dirty. So, if you are going for the pool, you may be disappointed as I was! I also cockroaches crawling on some of the furniture that was in the main lobby area.

“Good service, but a remodeling is needed soon” First, the service here is quite good. The front desk and bell staff were top notch and friendly. I can say the same for the restaurant staff. There was only one occasion were service suffered -- the hostess table at the lobby restaurant was left unattended for quite some time, so I was waiting for a while, but gave up. Other staff could have stepped in to offer to seat me, but didn't. I ended up ordering room service and paid $30 for a crabcake sandwich, fries and a soda. It was a good sandwich, but $30 is a bit high for Philadelphia. (Lunch and breakfast in the restaurant were much better.) I will say the room was spacious and bright, but it was showing wear. Paint was peeling on the window sill and the veneer on the desk was breaking off. The carpets in the hallway were dated and fraying and the halls themselves were dark. The worst part -- Noise from the hallway trickled into my room well into the evening. The bathroom was well equipped -- if you like L'Occitane, you'll be happy. Also, there was a Keurig coffee maker in the room, which was a nice touch. All that said, is this a 4 star hotel? Yes. 4 & 1/2 stars? No. I do think I got my money's worth though as I booked via Hotwire and got a very good rate. I would certainly stay here again, but I would say it's a shame that such a good staff is not matched with a top notch facility.

“Right Choice for a Night Stay” Enjoyed a one night stay before an early flight out of LAX. Helpful stay, good food and service at their restaurant, and comfortable accommodations. The shuttle to LAX in the AM, very helpful. Would stay again.

“great staff, rooms need upgrade” Convenient location, nice lobby, helpful desk and concierge staff. Room service was good, on time, and delivered professionally. But boy, these rooms are getting tired and need an upgrade. Desk phone was broken in more than one way - stuck on pulse dial, for example. No desk light. Laptop power required crawling under the desk to reach the wall socket. Lights in bathroom had an electrical buzz that was really annoying. Shower curtain was a little scary. Air conditioning system was ancient and loud. Bed stood out as comfortable and relatively new, and the other furniture was okay.

“Nice Stay” My wife and I stayed at TownePlace Suites for 1 night before our flight to San Francisco. The room was clean and was very comfortable. Using name your own price on priceline we were very pleased to save over 1/2 compared to the average price. The kitchen came in handy as we had purchased eggs and sausage to prepare before our flight. Would stay again if flying out of Columbus.

“Great location, enjoyed the experience” My adult daughter and I stayed for one night, used my accrued Westin Hotel rewards points so the room was no charge, in a double queen room for the disabled, although we are not. It was the first time I have stayed in one of the older historic hotels in San Francisco. The room was large, well furnished, the beds comfortable, the view was of the alley (Ugh) but we were there only to sleep and spent our waking hours on the town. The trolley ($5.00 each person, each way) was across the street and there were several reasonable local breakfast eateries in the area. The draw backs were the hotel parking ($54.00 per night) although there was parking down the street for about $30.00 but far less convenient when you have several suitcases to haul. The room was warm and the a/c didn't cool it down, but we opened the window and slept fine. It was a bit noisy in the halls but it was quiet after 11:00 p.m. I thought the place looked a bit ghostly, definitely older decor and the place could have used some updating but it had everything needed in the bathroom and bedroom. It reminded me of a haunted hotel I stayed in a few years back but we didn’t hear any spooky noises. The lobby and the halls were beautiful, check-in and check-out went smooth and the staff was friendly

“Friendly Staff - Average ES!!” As a HH member, I they to stay at ES whenever I'm on business. This one isn't anything to write home about. Location is NW/NC San Antonio. This has to be one of the oldest ES facilities I've been to (and I've stayed in tons of em). Rooms were very clean, housekeeping was adequate, and front desk staff excellent. In fact, I'm sure it's the level of customer service from all staff that keeps this place in business. Two biggest disappointments were the Manager's reception (especially the food - chips/salsa each night) and the overall food quality. Ordered room service twice and both times the orders were at the room within 15 minutes. However, each tasted like food left under a heat lamp = not fresh. This surprised me as ES room service/food quality is one of the best kept secrets I've found when traveling. Fitness Center is small but well appointed. Elevators are considerably slow (may have something to do with age of the facility). I'd only stay at this location again if I absolutely had to. The Riverwalk location is far superior.

“Great lobby, great location” Really funky lobby and very nice staff. Bathroom in the room are also very unique. Stayed at the hotel on a sold out nice due to storms and unfortunately the hotel was very loud. Would stay again to get a better feel for what it is really like.

“Perfect in every way” My husband and I stayed at the Elysian for a quick anniversary trip and were delighted at every moment of our stay. To start, the service is second to none. Every where we turned, someone was offering to help in a genuine way. There was zero pretentiousness that you often find at hotels of this quality. Then, the room itself...wow! We stayed in a Gold Coast Suite and were swimming in decadence - large/separate living room with a fireplace and balcony, king bed, chaise lounge, iPad docking station, gigantic deep tub, fantastic lighting in the bathroom, personal full wet-bar, macaroon treats with the turn-down service, and I'm sure I'm missing highlighting many of the hundreds of details in the room. We both enjoyed the spa - my husband partook in the whirlpool/sauna/steam room and swam in their lap pool while I luxuriated with a massage. The location was in a safe area, just steps from high-end shopping and just a short walk to the subway. Our stay at the Elysian Hotel will be hard to top...until we return back and are in their care again!

“Excellent Value” Well worth the price!!! The room was a genuine suite with two bathrooms! and the sink and mirror were outside!!! Super continental breakfast, lots of choices and fresh fruit!!! Coffee avialable at the lobby when you came in after walking from downtown. THe only downside is the major arterial running outside that you must go around to cross and our weather was a little crummy. Other than that it was all that it claimed to be!! We will be back!!

“Nel complesso buon hotel” Sono stato per 3 notti in questo hotel, nell'agosto del 2012 con mia moglie; l'hotel è bello, situato un pò fuori dal cuore della città, circa 1,5km. La hall è curata e pulita, come tutto l'hotel del resto. Personale educato e efficiente, camere belle con la WiFi gratuita. L'uncia pecca è che sia nella hall che nei corridoi, il personale teneva il climatizzatore a delle temperature POLARI da tenere il maglione per uscire di camera. Nel complesso lo consiglierei.

“Traditional hotel - good but not for me” This is one, if not the oldest hotels in Boston and if you want heritage and tradition this will not dissapoint (the entrance, lobby and restaurant are all very grand). It also doesn't do anything badly - the rooms are pleasant and comfortable, the breakfast plentiful, the service also pleasant, but it didn't do anything especially special.

“Good location, busy but well organized” A one night stay with sisters. We were impressed with the friendly helpful attitude of everyone on the staff we dealt with from the valet parking attendant to Daniel at the front desk. Good location for walking to many attractions.

“Best Holiday Inn Express” I stay at 20 Holiday Inn Express hotels a year for business travel. My family and I spent a great 4th of July weekend in San Antonio and enjoyed this great Holiday Inn Express very much. We walked to Market, Riverwalk and Alamo and enjoyed the pool very much. Best Holiday Inn Express that I have yet to stay!

“Top Shelf Comfort” This hotel is a rare gem, blending elegance in both architecture and general service style with a warmth that makes one feel comfortable. Whether you're a known celeb walking through the doors or a worn out business traveler like me, the treatment is equal and attentive to all guests. My only regret is that I didn't get to try the spa, as I was short on time. Great drinks at the bar, and the appetizers were heaven. Try the Lobster Mac & Cheese - a perfect metaphor for the Sofitel in general - top-shelf comfort.

“Won't be staying again” Unfortunately, the only really positive things about our stay at the Affinia Shelburne was the size of the room and the comfort of the bed. We stayed in a deluxe one bedroom suite which was adequately furnished though lacking in asthetics and suffering from poor lighting. Our windows opened into a narrow canyon of building so very little daylight reached us. We didn't mind the lack of view as we had no intention of staying in the hotel during waking hours, but we did mind that we didn't have better lighting. One more lamp or perhaps a ceiling light would solve that problem. If you are booking the larger rooms in order to have a refrigerator and microwave, be warned that the refrigerator is mostly ice maker. You will have to remove shelves to stand up a carton of milk or bottle of wine. The unit does not come with plates or silverware but we were quite pleased that our bellman, being notified of this lack, had it sent right up to us. The Affinia Shelburne may be located in a somewhat more residential area of Manhattan, but that doesn't mean that it is a quiet area. Lexington is an extremely busy thoroughfare. And noise from the rooftop bar is channeled right down the previously mentioned canyon so sleep isn't possible until everyone else decides to go to bed and we did not stay over the weekend so it's quite possibly worse then. Also the Affinia's location means that you have a longer way to travel to most 'tourist' spots. As we have stayed in New York often, we didn't mind being off the beaten path. Make sure you are prepared with great walking shoes or lots of cash for taxi fare. There are Metra stops a few blocks away and Grand Central Station is only four blocks from the hotel. If you are interested in any of the 'kits' or other free amenities offered by the Affinia hotels, insist on ordering them in advance. We called the hotel several days prior to our arrival to reserve one of the items and were told that we could just ask for it on arrival. Unfortunately, it took them two days and repeated calls and visits to the front desk to get it. And if you want to go to the rooftop with your family for a night-time view of the city - don't. When we arrived on the 16th floor, we were rudely told that we could not even set foot through the door before we were even off the elevator. Apparently, the entire rooftop becomes a bar at night. The man guarding the rooftop was unbelievably rude, especially considering that we were guests of the hotel. Had he nicely told us that we could not go out, perhaps we would've been more accepting but his attitude was completely uncalled for. We left feeling that the hotel values it's bar patrons much more than it's hotel guests. Even though the following was not entirely in control of the hotel, the internet reception was spotty and one elevator was out of service for a time. We were looking forward to staying at the Shelburne but we won't be staying again. There is a great deal of improvement needed.

“Spitzenmäßiges Hotel” Erstklassiges Hotel mit super Service und toller Ausstattung. Trotz der Nähe zum Flughafen kann man sich nicht über Lärmbelästigung beklagen. Das Frühstücksbuffet war sehr gut und vor allen Dingen reichhaltig. Das Zimmer war geräumig und sauber. Das Hotel hat einen schönen Poll samt Whirlpool im Innenhof und ist mit Palmen umsäumt. Das Personal war freundlich und zuvorkommend, auch ein Zimmerwechsel war ohne Probleme machbar. In der Lobby des Hotels ist ein „Starbucks“ beheimatet. In der Nähe des Hotels befindet sich sowohl eine Bushaltestelle, von der wir für 0,75 Dollar nach Santa Monica gefahren sind, als auch eine Haltestelle für einen Trolley, von der man beispielsweise nach Manhatten Beach fahren kann (Tickets hierfür gibt es an der Rezeption zu kaufen).

“Clean and Friendly” This hotel provides all you could hope for from a Fairfield Inn. The rooms and common areas are clean and the hotel staff is remarkably friendly and helpful. The rooms are in need of some modernization - they are feeling quite dated. But they are roomy and tidy. The fourth floor rooms feature higher ceilings and nice tall windows. My room was quiet and I was able to work and rest in peace. I appreciate that the stairwells were clean and well-lit and basically usable -- I prefer stairs to elevators any day, provided the stairs aren't dark and creepy. In sum - nothing really remarkable, but no big, bad surprises, either. I will certainly return here in the future should business bring me this way again.

“Convenient but” This hotel is beside a poorly rated mexican drive thru and a bath house and is directly in front of a trolley stop. Its proximity to public transit means two things: you have incredibly easy access to downtown and beyond, and you hear trains all the time. And these trains don't go quietly - they honk their horns and blow their whistles as they go, and yes, you will be awoken by them. The hotel itself isn't the newest in town, but the insides are just fine. The lobby reminds me of a hostel - dorm room quality furniture and lots and lots of fluorescent lighting. The rooms are pretty much what you would expect from a hotel of this class. Breakfast was decent, all things considered. Lots of cereals, yogurt, some fruit, juice, muffins, and a hot item that seemed to vary. The coffee isn't very good. The food itself seems to be in too cramped an area given the number of people eating at peak hours. The free shuttle turned out to not be so convenient - we needed to head to the airport around 10, which happens to be when they run a shuttle to the zoo, and at 10:30 they were taking a group of senior citizens to their cruise (there seem to be a lot of people staying here for this very reason). On a side note, a previous occupant of our room left behind a pair of pants and a shirt which were stuffed behind a chair in the corner of the room. If you stayed here and are missing a whole outfit, you might want to call the hotel! Overall, this place is a great value, but you get what you pay for.

“Great little find” The Charlesmark is a fresh, funky little boutique hotel in a fabulous location. Easy walk to Boston Common and the Prudential Centre. Although my room was small, it was cosy (perfect on a snowy stay in Boston), had nice lighting, comfy bed, modern furnishings, a CD stacker and piped music!! The bar / lounge downstairs is trendy and has free internet access. Would definitely stay here again.

“Great location” As you've previously read this is a great location with the trolley running right by the hotel, taxis lined up and ready for you, Union Square right in front. We had a nice corner room on the 25th floor with 180 degree views of the Golden Gate Bridge, Coit Tower, Union Square and the Bay. The glass elevators are wonderful providing great views on the way to and from your room and they are speedy. We had a great stay in San Francisco and enjoyed this location but there were few things not up to par. The Oak Room was just ok - actually the food was pretty good but the service was substandard. Most of the staff was cordial, friendly, and wanted to help in any way they could. However the expectation of a tip was obvious every time something was done for you. Our biggest complaint would be about the mini bar (refreshment center in the room). Each item you consume is charged a 20% service charge (tip) plus sales tax - this adds up! There was also a discrepancy in the amount we were charged and the amount of things we agreed that we consumed. Beware!

“Fourth time here - I really like it” I have stayed here four times and find it to be my hotel of choice in mid-town. The rooms are comfortable for one or two and the service is excellent. The rooms are quiet and well appointed.

“New and efficient in Downtown Detroit” The Westin is a perfect business hotel in downtown Detroit. The building and location is historic, but the interior is totally updated. I found the room to be clean, quiet and in perfect working order. The staff was very friendly and all-in-all it was exactly what I would expect from a business hotel and I had a great night's rest before a meeting the next day. Valet, while a bit pricey, was efficient and I found that I never had to wait more than 5 minutes for the car to show up. About the only thing that I found strange is the fact that they didn't seem to have room service. I look all over the room for a menu and could not find one. To be fair, I didn't call down and ask -- I just gave up when not fincing the menu in the room. Overall, a nice, clean, modern and efficient hotel I'll be back.

“Nicer than expected!” Stayed at the Palmer House for one night on a recent trip to Chicago. As a HHonors Gold member, I was uncertain of what to expect, however found the hotel to be clean and the staff friendly. I was upgraded to a larger king room on the executive floor. The room was spacious and clean. The offerings in the executive lounge were above average. All the staff I encountered were friendly. The food at Potter's Lounge was good. I would not hesitate to stay here again, especially for the bargain prices you can find during the winter months.

“Nice property, good location” This property is about 10-12 years old and is located approximately 4 miles from Denver International Airport. Because of this distance, a wait for hotel pickup at the airport can be longer than normal for most airport hotels. We found the property to be very clean, staffed by professional individuals, though some hiccups were experienced along the way. The best staff member who went out of his way to accommodate our needs was within the food and beverage department and his name is Dakota. This young man was exemplary and I hope the hotel recognizes his value and rewards him accordingly. The buffet breakfast was excellent as well and I found no fault in anything experienced in this area. Housekeeping had some issues which were representative of taking shortcuts in the rooms but this was not a concern to the point of besmirching the property needlessly. I believe if you seek a property near the Denver International Airport, the Embassy Suites would certainly address all of your needs.

“Excellent stop room brand new” I got this near the airport and it was so close to my thrifty rental car as well. THe room was huge with 2 heater control units - full kitchen with a dishwasher and large bathroom. I got this on priceline and they gave me the handicap room. It looked brand new. Im not sure if the whole place is this new but the hallways looked it. There was even a continental breakfast with great coffee and a bagel. They told me they had shuttle service to the airport every half hour. THe location was less than one mile from the airport. With the esa it says the desk hours close at 10 am. I got in at 12 :15 am and luckily there was someone there. Not sure why. Also no shampoo in these esa places so bring your own and the vender machine only takes quarters- no dollars. Fantastic place would rate it a 3 star.

“Fantastic” Very nice Hilton with fantastic service. I stayed her one night while seeing a show in the area. Looks like it was recently redone with the decor and interiors high quality and elegant. Bed was super comfortable and room was quiet. Had drinks at the bar where the bartender was nice and attentive. Had breakfast at the restaurant and it was excellent. I will stay here again when I visit downtown LA. Used Hilton Honors points to get a free room. They gave me an upgrade to a jr. suite which was very roomy.

“Great place to stay in Seattle” I stayed a few days at the Watertown for a conference. I would definitely stay here again. The location is perfect for the University district, there are a number of cheap restaurants, cafes and stores nearby. The hotel has free bikes you can borrow to move around the area, and Seattle is a bike-friendly (if hilly) city. If you want to go downtown, the hotel has a free shuttle. Staff is friendly and helpful. The room is not huge but definitely large enough, and quite clean and comfortable. It could use a bit more light and water pressure is not great (though adequate). There is free Internet in the room (a cable is available). I am a light sleeper, but this hotel is very quiet at night, and the beds are comfy. Amenities such as free coffee, teas and herbal teas, cookies and wine tasting in the afternoon make your stay even more pleasant. Breakfast is OK: eggs, bagels, a variety of cereals, juices and pastries. Nothing stellar or homemade, but it gets your day started.

“Visit the lobby and move on!” This hotel is living off of its historical and modern political visitors, in my opinion. We stay in Denver semi-regularly as a quick getaway/overnight for us. I can think of multiple downtown hotels as good, if not better than this hotel for less (Marriott, Hyatt, Ritz-Carlton, Hilton, etc.). The atrium area when you first enter is indeed impressive, especially considering how old the property is, built in 1892. However, for travelers I'd recommend stopping by, maybe have a meal or their afternoon tea, take some pictures, and find another hotel. My exception to this suggestion will be to mimic what we did using Marriott points (it became part of the Marriott family a couple of months ago). The Brown Palace claims to be top-end, and prominently displays its awards at the desk, but doesn't live up to it in my mind. As a very regular traveler, business and pleasure, here are just some of the reasons it is not worth it's price point as to details expected at this level of hotel: 1-bar of soap for sink and shower, 1 coffee cup, small bathrooms (albeit beautiful and with 2 shower heads), no comfy chair in room (ours had 3 dining room type chairs even with ample room for a larger one that you might actually want to sit in), noise (as they are all about drawing people into their atrium, it is noisy), crowded check-in/checkout area (as they set up for afternoon tea by 9AM), old and stained furnishings in sitting area, disingenuous staff (I get in the hospitality world what it means to work in a property of this supposed caliber, doesn't mean you have to lose your perspective on normal and genuine kindness to all.), no pool, and the fitness center is actually across the street and shared with another property (that's less than half the price per night). On a positive note, they do allow pets, for $100 deposit, but so do many downtown Denver properties. For out-of-state visitors, drive the 70+ miles south to stay at the Broadmoor for about the same price point and a much better hotel experience! For those taking in sites in downtown Denver, there are plenty of other full-service properties that are better.

“Good hotel but rude staff” For the city of Detroit, this is a good hotel. The Courtyard and the Marriott are probably the best hotels in this area. Location is good because you have a CVS and food court nearby that are accessible w/o going outside. Plus, you have Canada walking distance away. The rooms here are big and nice, typical for a the Marriott brand. The only negative thing that I have to say is that the staff is not very welcoming. Do not expect to get a hello, a smile or even a glance as you walk in. Oh, and don't walk out of the gym w/ your gym towel because the security guard will freak out!

“Not what I expected” Upon arriving at the Palmer House, I was stunned at the rushed atmosphere. It took us a few minutes to get oriented with the lobby itself, as there is a multitude of foot traffic going either direction at any given time. After finally arriving at the check in desk, we were greeted rather impersonal. The man stayed on the phone the entire time he checked us in (which I found to be not only rude to us, but also to the people trying to carry on a conversation on the other end). We again had to reorientate as the lobby area was filled with "cocktailers" on business trips (which did not bother me, but did make it a bit difficult to navigate through with our bags). I will add that the ambiance on this level was absolutely spectacular. It definitely takes you back a century, and is phenomenal to take in. We arrived on the 17th floor only to find that our room key didn't work. Had we not been on the El, and carrying our bags with us, it wouldn't have been so frustrating, but we were worn out, and ready to drop our bags, shower, and regroup. My husband left me with the bags, and waited so patiently on the elevator that seemed to take FOREVER to reach our floor. Eventually he returned, and it turned out that the gentleman at the front desk had assigned us the wrong room. Imagine my surprise...(as he paid NO attention to what he was doing in the first place!) We got into our room, and it was clean, but not eclectic or modern in any way. Still the old TV. A decent sized bathroom. The room itself was very small, but if you're only staying a couple of days, then it is manageable. Don't expect the typical Chicago boutique experience in this hotel. It's hustle and bustle is at it's best. Concierge is pleasant, but not overly friendly. Efficiency seems key, not friendliness. We did have cocktails, apps ,and desserts in the hotel restaurant and really enjoyed those. We would only return if it was a great price that we couldn't beat.

“excellent value” if you need a lot of space try the holiday inn,,,,if you want a great deal in nyc stay here....small rooms , I only sleep there, great location, quiet, clean and cheap for nyc with tax $140 ish.......

“OK Stay - Recommend only if you want to save money” Came to Chicago for a gymnastics meet. So first of all I need to preface that I stayed at the Doubletree because our booster club negotiated an $88 per night rate and that included the use of the pool which is normally $15 per room. Overall, my experience was what I would expect for paying $88 per night. Cons: 1. Rooms: I changed rooms three times which is not something I would normally do but the paint on the ceiling of the bathroom was peeling so badly that it was depressing. Also, there was rust on the tub (I don't live in mansion but when my bathroom at home is a LOT nicer than the hotel we have a problem) and the room furniture and walls were pretty beat up and no flat screen which seriously dates the hotel. We stayed on the 9th floor and it smelled like a mixture of cleaning products and smoke and carpeting was stained in hallways which overall doesn't make for a great atmosphere - but I guess what would you expect for $88. The paint on the ceilings in the bathrooms in the second and third rooms were a little bit better but overall rooms were really worn. I expected better from a Doubletree. I normally stay at Marriotts but have stayed in Doubletrees before where the rooms were a lot better. A taxi cab driver told us that the hotel used to be a Holiday Inn which would make sense, because the rooms and hallways reminded me of an old Holiday Inn which they tried to retrofit to a Doubletree. Linens were OK. 2. No free coffee in Lobby (you get it in the rooms but I am used to free coffee that is made in the lobby) and one of the electrical outfits in the main lobby looked like it had been melted and couldn't be used. Really only saw one useable electrical outlet in the lobby. 3. Pool was a hike to get to. 4. No free wifi - although I knew about this beforehand. Also, it looked like I would have been charged to use the business center and I can't tell you the last time I have stayed at a hotel that charged for internet usage or charged for business center services. Pros: 1. If you have a group that is cost conscious and needs a block of rooms for an event it looks like you can get a decent deal. 2. I will say that overwhelmingly the staff was VERY nice. The only bad experience was that the front desk person told me that I had to bring my own towels to the pool when in fact they have pool towels behind the desk. 3. Good location. 4. Eistein Bros. restaurant in building. Not sure that I would stay at this hotel again. I am really interested in having a decent hotel room when I go somewhere and the room was barely average, plus the hallways had that odd smell that you can never get rid of. I guess I can recommend it if you can get a great deal and you don't care about a really nice room.

“Un hôtel usine bien placé sur Times sq.” Je descends très souvent dans cet hôtel pour mon travail. C'est indéniable, l'emplacement est idéal ! mais mais mais.... Vous ne serez en aucun cas dépaysé ici, j'imagine qu'un bon 75% des clients sont français. Accueil "à la chaine" en réception": " NEXT" signifie ici "Bienvenue au Novotel Times Sq N.Y" L'accueil au petit déjeuner est.........inéxistant. Je n'ai d'ailleur jamais payé mon pdj, en 45 mn personne n'est venu me voir à table....Je me suis placé tout seul.....Car tout le monde est genre débordé. La vue en revanche est top ! La chambre est standard Novotel. Rien à redire, pas le grand luxe mais de bon standing. De gros progrès sur la propreté des chambres. La litterie est convenable. Les plateaux sales des rooms service restent, quand à eux, toujours dans les couloirs plus d'une journée. Le rapport qualité prix est convenable, mais l'accueil.....ah...... la notion de service dans une enseigne française.............

“For overnight near the airport, an OK place” I was one of many travelers staying overnight to be near LAX for an early morning flight. I chose this hotel because it was close to the airport, within walking distance of the rental car return, and had a 24-hour airport shuttle. The good points are (a) the price was reasonable compared to the other hotel chain properties nearby; (b) the staff was pleasant and welcoming, (c) the rooms are adequate and comfortable with free wifi, and (d) the hotel is one of a half dozen that sponsor a single shuttle that runs every 15 minutes or so and on which this was the last stop before the airport. The hotel restaurant did not look particularly inviting, so I had a light meal in the bar, Brewster's. This bar boasts 100 or so beers, and has a good selection of wines by the glass. It is easy to fall into informal conversation with other travelers and that was fun, so I talked to couples from Dallas and London, England, respectively. All in all, I would stay here again on an overnight visit. For longer stays, definitely not -- Marina del Rey and Santa Monica beckon one down to the water.

“Really enjoyed my stay” What a nice surprise after reading the negative reviews on here. After flying in from Europe I found an oversized room with a VERY comfy bed at the Hampton Inn PHL Airport. The check in was great and efficient and the free shuttle operates 24/7. Francis at the front desk was super helpful. There is even a Ruby Tuesday restaurant next door in case you get hungry. This is an older Hampton Inn but everything was in perfect shape. My flight departed at 6 am the next morning and the front desk even gave me a travel bag with food and a water. The only negative thing about this place was this annoying lady from the hotel's management office who called twice asking me about my satisfaction.

“Incompetent, unclean, and boring” Had problems checking in and out, and in between. But first, don’t believe the hype on this hotel’s website. This hotel is near nothing. The restaurants and clubs listed as “nearby” are elsewhere in Denver, but you will need transportation. It’s a long walk to the train, despite the claim for it being near.
