Long walk to a busy intersection, then under a set of interstate bridges. There were homeless people under the bridges asking for a handout. Check in was a miserable experience with an incompetent clerk that could not understand a simple question regarding a company credit card. Three times she left and came back with answers that were irrelevant junk. Finally talked to some chubby manager that was equally clueless—didn’t even bother to check, just said “no” when he finally grasped my question. I had to use a personal card, and then was punished with the noisiest room with a view of the front parking lot—the clerk even bragged to my face that she was sticking me in that room for making her “look bad” in front of the manager. Tried twice over the next three days to resolve the CC issue, each time met with indifference and incompetence at the front desk. Another thirty minutes to check out and still wound up with spurious charges on my personal card. Seriously, this hotel is staffed by untrained workers that are indifferent and clueless. The entire place is filthy. The hallway carpet was covered with the same debris (leaves, threads, glitter, paper and other detritus) the entire four days I was there. A cigarillo butt was in one hall corner the entire time. Hard to miss, but who knows how long it’s sat there. A partially eaten box lunch sat next to the trash can near the elevator for an entire day and evening. Which explains the bugs. Ceilings in the hall and in the bathroom were cheap hanging industrial acoustical tiles, many were stained. I’ve never been in a Motel 6, but I’m betting this is the way they look inside. I had bugs in the bathroom, not surprising with a filthy hall and loose ceiling tiles. They never cleaned the in-room coffee service all the time I was there, and only provide decaf unless you beg (three mornings, then I gave up; had to ask for condiments and shampoo as well). Room walls so thin you could hear every conversation in adjacent rooms. I did visit a guest room on the west side that had mountain views-- across multiple lanes of interstate traffic. We could barely hear ourselves without raising our voices over the roar of the traffic. So much for scenery. There was a refrigerator in the room. No place in walking distance to buy anything. Believe it or not, in this “classy” place one of the cabinet doors for the ‘fridge and fallen off and they never bothered repairing it, just left it partially open with half its doors. The mini ‘fridge had an ice ball around the freezer compartment-- hadn’t been cleaned or defrosted in months. It wasn’t cold inside and it buzzed and groaned constantly. Yet they list this piece of junk as an “amenity” in the hotel room description—what a farce. Finally, (not really done with all that I dislike about this place, but I’ve spent enough time on this hole) the restaurant (glorified snack bar) and in-room dining are mediocre and way overpriced. This hotel is one of the worse deals, ever. Avoid.

“Very nice hotel, but room was just average!” We stayed qt the Peabody only for one night. The location is absolutely terrific - right near Beale Street and within walking distance to the Mighty Mississippi, but the room was on the small side and the bed as well.....as was the tiny bathroom........ We got a coffee maker on demand and there was no minibar in the room - but otherwise everything was absolutely perfect. Did we get our money's worth?...... I don't know......

“A gem (no pun intended) in Washington DC” I really like Kimpton Hotels. They are top-tier hotels, and while a chain they feel like much smaller and more intimate places to stay. As others have noted, the decorating is non-traditional and a bit off-beat, but still very tasteful. My room was large and obviously not a standard box in a large hotel. The location was near Dupont Circle and an easy walk to the offices along Connecticut Avenue. What made this trip especially nice was the outstanding service. Everyone I met from the desk to the lounge restaurant was incredibly nice and friendly. The light meal I had in the lounge was delicious and the service pleasant without being overbearing. I had a problem with my computer printer and the front desk staff went out of the way to get me what I needed. Staying here was a very pleasant experience

“Often before but never again - creepy service” I've stayed here many times before, but this was the last time (and if my wife has her way, the last time for any Omni). Used online checkin, they promised room would be ready at 1. It wasn't even ready two+ hours later, apparently because my frequent guest profile requests a feather-free room (one of the choices they claim to offer). Not to worry, they said: "we'll put you in a feather room for now, then swap everything out while you're out at the game." Returned from game and dinner only to find out no one had bothered to do anything, Desk manager then lied about how quickly he'd fix the problem, and apparently it's never ok to call them on their service failures (the first guy who showed up at the room had zero pillows to swap out the 8 that were being replaced, which someone dampened my confidence).

“ausgezeichnetes kleines Boutique Hotel am Broadway” Im Vorfeld auf eine Penthouse Suite geupgradet und dieses nicht bereut. Das Zimmer war im oberen Bereich untergebracht mit einer Terasse und Sitzmöglichkeiten. Im Eingangsbereich war ein kleines Wohnzimmer mit Ferneseher, es folgte das Waschbecken und ein seperater großer Duschbereich. Man konnte vom Bett aus den Sonnenaufgang über Manhattan beobachten (der Wahnsinn!) Das Zimmer war ausserordentlich sauber und hat eine tolle Ausgangslage um Manhatten zu erleben. In direkter Nachbarschaft gibt es tolle Restaurants und Bars, man ist ausserdem in 10 minuten am Central Park West Eingang direkt am Dakota Building.

“Clean & Comfortable... Breakfast Was Just Okay” We stayed at this hotel as a last minute unexpected stop passing through Columbus. Many of the hotels in the area were booked, and this one had availability. They had a little trouble offering us a AAA rate, but it was resolved by the time the bill arrived under the door in the morning. Our room was spacious and comfortable, with free WIFI and two flat panel TVs. The only low point of our stay was breakfast. It wasn't... bad, it was just lackluster. To put it another way, I've had higher quality food at lower quality properties. There was a long line for the custom order omelets, and no bread or bagels anywhere to be found (although it was near the end of the breakfast period, so it is possible that we missed it). They also shut down and dumped the coffee pots within 15 minutes of the official end of breakfast. From that point forward the only coffee available was from the one-cup machine in our room. Since they didn't charge extra for the breakfast, I can't say too much against it, and this property definitely lived up to the high quality standards of the Embassy name in other areas. Overall I would recommend this hotel, as long as breakfast is not your priority.

“Good location for me” My son lives in the Hollywood Hills so my choice in staying at this hotel was based on proximity to his home. The hotel lobby is beautfiul. Valet service is excellent. There are two restaurants on site, one very casual and one upscale steak house. I did not use them. The library bar is nice for a nightcap. Friendly, timely service. The poolside bar has limited offerings and was not adequately staffed on our evening visit resulting in delays in service. The rooms are well priced for LA but compact. Noise was not an issue. Room service for coffee in the AM was prompt. There is some kind of very hip club on the premises that many try to get into in order to see a celebrity. Since I was visiting the biggest celebrity in my life, my son - I skipped that part.
“普通に満足です♪” 建物自体は古いですが、中近東風で良い雰囲気です。ステイプルズセンターも近く便利です。ただちょっと部屋が狭かったです・・

“wonderful staff!” A year since my last visit and the status quo remains. In all respects an average property with the exception of the staff. Consistently above the norm from the front to room service. THEY are the reason I will return. People do make a difference.

“Nice Location” I recently spent two nights here on a business trip. The location is very nice. The hotel is in good condition and the staff were helpful and friendly. However even if you get a good room rate, the price of staying there can add up quickly. Parking was $30 per night. Eating or drinking there can be spendy. A cup of coffee at the Starbucks in the lobby was $4.00 (that's for regular coffee), and a beer at the lobby bar was $8.00. Maybe that's on par with other DC hotels but it would make sense to walk a few blocks to Union Station for much for affordable eats and drinks.

“A wonderful hotel” My family and I stayed in this hotel for 3 days. As a matter of fact, we couldn’t find anything to complain about it. It is one of the best hotels we have ever been. Everything is perfect. The room is excellent, the internet works very well, the location is very good and the staff are very polite. In a nutshell: the hotel has everything that one could expect from a 5 star hotel.

“Beautiful Hilton” We had the pleasure of staying on the executive level for two nights. The room was perfect and all that went with it. The food and drinks provided were a nice touch and the staff is as wonderful as the hotel itself. A lot to learn about the history of this place. We truly enjoyed our stay. Thank you to Mr. Temperly for all his help.

“Mixed Marriott Experience” Stayed three nights here in January with a co-worker while attending a huge convention (thousands of attendees). The overwhelming memory of the stay is that the key cards rarely worked two consecutive times during the first two days. This required multiple trips to the front desk for replacements - numerous other guests were having similar problems. Hopefully they have worked this issue was temporary. The room was fairly typical - enough room for a couple of beds, not much more. Bed was comfortable, temparature in room easy to control. Bathroom was clean and everything worked well. The best part is the concierge lounge, if you have access. Very good morning and evening food and beverages. It is right across the street from the Metro red line - that is very nice. Overall, this is a large convention hotel. It is okay, but there are plenty of other choices in town - I will probably stay somewhere else in the future. If you are a Marriott fan, this is a good choice, though. There is a CVS right across the street and plenty of interesting dinding choices a very short block away.

“Worthwhile stay unless....” This is a worthwhile stay unless you're really picky. I can only think of a few negatives with this hotel. First, is that there is no free wi-fi. You can, however, access the wi-fi for free in the lobby though. Second, there's no free breakfast. Most of us, however, need to eat less anyway. Finally, I noticed a strange smell permeating through the hotel. It wasn't great, but it wasn't overwhelming either. My spouse, however, did not even notice a smell, so unless you're sensitive to smells, you probably wouldn't notice it either. As for the positives: the first is that the hotel, which is very close to MDW, offers a great park and fly deal for its guests. We got a rate of around $150/night and it included parking for the 9 days we were gone. I doubt we could find a hotel room & parking anywhere in the area for less. If I'm wrong, please email me and tell me so. In this case, however, I don't think I am. They have a shuttle to the airport that starts at 4am (its essentially 24 hours), that is complimentary. We used it to take the train into the city for dinner AND to the airport for our flight. Second, the room and hotel were pleasant enough and clean. Our room included a very comfortable king size bed and a big bathroom with a great shower. We found the hotel staff friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. We didn't use the pool or exercise facility available, but both looked sufficient. We did use the business center, which has computers available for use, including printers to print out your boarding pass. Third, there is a Starbucks attached to the hotel. There is also a restaurant and bar. Overall, I would highly recommend the hotel. It's the perfect place to stay when you need a place the night before a flight. It, along with many other hotels, is very close to the airport. While, the hotel isn't in a great area of town (when is an airport in a great area of town), I wouldn't imagine there are many problems with theft. Seemed pretty well lit and safe.

“Just three complaints” 1. $20.00 parking fee for an out of town hotel, ridiculous; 2. we reserved a non-smoking room an ended in a room with a strong cigarette odor and had to stay on it because the place was sold out; and, 3. they sell two room suites which are not real two room suites; they are a room with an area with a sofa bed and just one bathroom. Aside from that, the place looks wonderful. They serve a pretty good complimentary breakfast.

“Very good hotel, awesome location.” The best thing was the size of the room (really big for what is NYC), and the location which is great......only 2 blocks away from Empire State. Everything was clean and neat....although the only negative thing is that they refused to provide an early check in; but they did stored our bags, so we had a walk until check in time.

“The aldol farce” We stayed in the Adolphus in August this year. Our first experience at check in was okay but she didn't tell us about the complementary breakfast that came with the room. The room itself was nice and large but the air conditioning could not cope with the 105 f temperatures. We asked for assistance and the hotel arranged a change of room but forgot to tell us. We were convinced that the concierge was so busy with his multiple roles that we seldom saw him and when we did he wasn't much help anyway. The dining room was fine and the lobby dark cool and nice. The gym was quite good for a hotel. Overall we expected more from the service considering it ranking on trip advisor. The exception was fillippe in the dining room for breakfast who was excellent.

“Great for a convention or business meetings” This hotel is lovely in its appointments (furniture, lighting, decor) in both the public areas and in the rooms. The beds are comfortable and the pillows are fluffy. The toiletries are from Bath and Body Works (standard Marriott amenities) and they smell good. The breakfast served at the business meeting was mediocre. The coffee isn't very good (the coffee in the hotel rooms was actually better) and it kept running out as did the hot water for tea (took the staff almost 20 minutes each time to refill). The hotel restaurants had decent food--hearty midwestern fare--though the service was either understaffed in both restaurants or just not very efficient as they screwed up orders at our tables and the ones near ours during two different meals. I'd stay here again though.

“Good, average hotel” Stayed at the Doubletree to be in Dearborn near the Henry Ford. Check in was great, nice room with super bed and creature comforts. Free wireless is fabulous. Breakfast in the Grill was included in our package, and it was super. NIce fitness area with adequate equipment. Only drawback, doors are thin -- and you hear all the noises in the halls. Since the hotel is right beside the freeway, that is the view. Would I stay again, that would depend on other options -- but it would be a good contender.

“Very Good Hotel” I booked the Holiday Inn I-95 by mistake, intending to book the FL-9A Holiday Inn, so we were prepared for a disappointment after reading TripAdvisor comments for this hotel. We were quite pleasantly surprised. When I checked in, I commented that some guests mentioned that in-room wi-fi access was slow or non-existent. The man at the desk checked us in to room 106 instead of 510 because he knew the wi-fi signal was stronger in that area, and he was right: the signal strength was "very good." We could look out of our window and see our car parked next to the window. Location The hotel is ideally located next to I-95. It took about 15 minutes in rush hour traffic to reach Ruth's Chris Steak House in the Crowne Plaza Hotel right on the waterfront. The river view and the meal were excellent, and parking was free. The hotel is not far from Deerwood Shopping Center where we found Mandaloun Restaurant that served delicious Lebanese food. We chose the advance booking rate without breakfast. It seemed a good value, although others said they had received much lower rates on Priceline. The freezer in the refrigerator in the room was cold enough to freeze our ice packs. We were granted a late chekout at 1:30 pm when we expected to return from a Segway tour of the Kingsley Plantation. The man at the reception desk had a problem unlocking the computer to check me in but the problem was resolved the next morning. The electricity went out in the neighborhood over a 45-minute period beginning about 8 p.m.. We assume it did not happen often because the hotel did not provide candles. Battery-operated emergency lights went on in the lobby and halls until electricity was restored. It appeared that the hotel's main line of business was hosting conferences and meetings in the numerous meeting rooms. We were sad to find that there was no coffee available in lobby, probably because this was not a Holiday Inn Express. There was a coffee maker and microwave in the room, however, and both worked very well. I suspect that different wings have different levels of service. Our 100-wing had good Internet and a very good room.

“Always a very nice stay” I've stayed at the Langham a number of time and was there again in the last month. It's gotten even better - the dining room which I always thought was a bit tired, seems to have been changed somewhat and is much more inviting. The staff is always great, from the front desk staff to the concierge desk (this staff is tremendously helpful) to room service. The hotel is located in a business district which I was initially concerned about since I didn't know what restaurants, etc, would be open in the evening but it's not a problem... the hotel is within walking distance of Faneuil Hall/Quincy Market and a quick cab ride to Boston's version of Little Italy. The hotel is great and my only negative comment, which I also made to the management, is that in a luxury hotel a guest should not be charged for internet service. In 2001 this is no different for charging for electricity in the room... no hotel would think of doing that and similarlly, should not charge for internet service.

“GREAT LOCATION AND STAFF” After bidding on Priceline for 3 1/2 star hotel we were pleasantly surprised that the Embassy Suites surpassed our expectations. Clean large suite with mini-kitchen, comfy king-size bed, and clean modern, bathroom. We had a wrap-around terrace, and the rate included a very respectable breakfast buffet (yes in the connected TGI Fridays) AND a "managers reception" each night with a very decent open bar with nibbles. Also a nicely functional business center with internet access and printers accessable with your room card. The location is great for the Rittenhouse Square, Parkway area with nice restaurants in easy walking distance. We were very satisfied and thrilled that we didn't get the Sheraton next door like we did last time!

“Standard Sheraton, great location” I stayed here for a few nights around the Super Bowl. The hotel staff clearly went out of their way to provide as much extra help and assistance as they could to make guests feel at home. Service was friendly and excellent. The rooms are standard. Clean, but the water pressure / shower nozzle was not good and made it hard to get conditioner out of my hair. The best feature is the location. It's a block of the main circle downtown. You can easily and safely walk anywhere in the area. There is a Starbucks in the building as well, which is always nice. Breakfast was fine, your standard basic hotel buffet. Plenty of great restaurants are within walking distance, and you can walk to the stadium easily. There is a parking garage at the hotel, which looks as if the ceiling is starting to fall apart. Overall, fine hotel and service. I would stay here again.

“Absolutely Wonderful Hotel” My wife and I stayed at the Benjamin June 30th for one night. We were delighted with just about everything from the location, to the very friendly and professional staff, and the large and well-appointed room. Best of all, is the care and attention the hotel gives to its guests for a chance to have quality sleep time. There is a pillow menu with a choice of nine different pillows and a turndown service with lavender spray to help one sleep. In addition, the hotel supplies a white noise machine on request and even has a room service menu featuring foods to help you sleep! Needless to say, we slept great. The doorman, Mohammad, is one of the best you will ever meet. This is the best hotel I have stayed in in New york City, bar none.

“Quaint, intimate amidst San Francisco's shopping district” Never stayed here before - but this hotel appropriately scales itself around a lot of "not nice" building facades - including the Hyatt across the street. You almost miss the Taj entrance if you blink. But everything inside is appropriately scaled to maintain the kind of intimacy that allows your mind to escape the visual noise outside. I was in their smallest room - but I was on business - and it was lovely. Staff was pleasant, although distracted sometimes - indicating a need for more staff not different staff. I may come back.

“Gelungene Modernisierung!” Das Hilton im Financial District in San Francisco hat im Laufe des Jahres 2011 einen aufwertenden Umbau erfahren. Die Fernseher aller Zimmer wurden auf den neusten Stand gebracht. Das alte und zu langsame WLAN wurde durch ein neues und zuverlässigeres ersetzt. Einige Zimmer auf der Executive Ebene wurden grundlegend Renoviert. Seit November 2011 gibt es jetzt endlich auch eine Executive Lounge im 26. Stock die ein Hilton übliches „Continental-Breakfast“ zur Verfügung stellt. Die Lounge ist geschmackvoll eingerichtet, aber für ein Hotel der Größe mit über 100 Exec-Zimmern etwas zu klein geraten. Der Evening-Snack ist nicht der Rede wert, ein „Feierabendbier“ gibt es hier auch nur gegen Geld, was eigentlich eher unüblich für Exec-Lounges der Hilton Gruppe ist.

“Große Zimmer, guter Service” Das Hotel liegt etwas außerhalb vom Stadtzentrum, aber es gibt stündlich einen kostenlosen Hotel-Shuttle zum Viertel Inner Harbor oder zum Convention Center. Die Zimmer sind groß und ordentlich ausgestattet: Klimaanlage, Fernseher, Kühlschrank, Mikrowelle und Kaffeemaschine. Das Hotel verfügt über ein kleines Hallenschwimmbad. Das Frühstück ist mit Rührei einigermaßen reichhaltig. Auch gibt es ein Business Center mit PC's mit Internet-Zugang.

“Nice hotel for fun times” My husband and I stayed at the Westin Copley Place from April 17-19, 2008, and we had no problems. Check in was prompt and the staff was nice. The room was average size, deluxe king room, had Starbucks coffee, but we don't drink coffee, and the room was very clean. It is in a GREAT location for shopping, restaurants, and the subway. It is a $10.00 cab ride, one way, to Fenway Park or it is a 5 minute subway ride to the Park. Overall we had a nice stay. The only thing I can think that would be negative were the stains on the carpet outside of the elevators, but not that big of a deal. Would stay there again. There is a mall that is attached to this hotel just in case you need to go shopping for anything. Its is connected by a covered walkway. Fabulous idea!!! Happy Traveling! P.S. The only reason we went to Boson was to see Fenway Park and see the Red Sox play :)

“After 5 months and 14 hotels in D.C., this is my new favorite hotel!” I had the pleasure of staying at the Madison two weekends ago while in Washington D.C. I have spent the better part of the last five months in D.C., mostly transiting between various hotels that were in the vicinity of my office. Though it isn't particularly far away, the Madison is NOT near my office, so it had never occurred to me to stay there. I was in town with my significant other a few weekends ago and used Priceline to book a hotel in the area around the White House. I had just spent the week in the Capitol Hilton, so that will be my main frame for comparison; until I found the Madison my other favorite places to stay in D.C. were the Liaison Capitol Hill, the Hilton, and the Winn. The room was decorated in a slightly busy but intriguing way - quirky, elegant furnishings that were the perfect place to relax after a busy day in and about D.C. A few things that stood out for me: wonderful linens, with a double-sheeted comforter. Air conditioning that kept the room at the perfect temperature (for my significant other, this means "arctic chill"). Two bathrobes in the closet. Keurig beverage maker in the room, with pods for coffee, decaf, and, wonder of wonders, green tea. There were ceramic mugs on the credenza. The wireless internet was fast and FREE (which amazed and delighted us-first time I've gotten free wireless without status of some sort at a 4* hotel). Finally, there were real wine glasses (not the kind that your two year old can hurl at the floor and will bounce, but actual stemware) provided on the credenza. I have never, ever been to a hotel that supplied actual wine glasses (without calling down to room service) in the room, just the thick-stemmed heavy glass wine glasses that are barely good enough to drink two buck chuck out of. We didn't see much of the staff, but they were polite and attentive when we did see them. This is absolutely my new favorite hotel in Washington D.C. and I will stay here any chance I get.

“Loved the Four Seasons!” We only spent one night at the Four Seasons, but absolutely loved it. The staff was very friendly and helpful from the moment we arrived and really made us feel welcomed. This is not a stuffy Four Seasons. The lobby bar is lively at happy hour with lots of locals drinking beer and enjoying an after work snack. Our room was large and very comfortable with a nice view of Town Lake. The bath products provided are L'Occitane and the towels and robes were nice and soft. Room service was fast and very good at breakfast. The hotel is in a great location within walking distance to the capitol and many bars and restaurants. Ask the guys at the valet stand where to go!

“good but at what price?” Stayed here for one night on a good weekend rate which included breakfast $215). Hotel service was good, including room service, which was prompt. Pleasant pool area,gym/spa nice spacious room in a traditional style. Ita a formal Ritz Carlton and still looks like one. The problem is there is nothing really around the hotel and it backs up on self storage facilities and freight train tracks--so you do hear the train whistles in the back "city view" rooms (and the city is in the distance so there is not much to see). DO have to say though that the train was not loud enough to really bother me. So I enjoyed my stay there to kick off a hectic business trip--and would have no hesitation in staying there again-- provided a got a reasonable rate--didn't seem worth an arm and a leg.

“Wonderful, Romantic property” The hubs & I stayed at the Omni La Mansion del Rio to celebrate our 37th wedding anniversary. We booked a King-river view with a "shared" balcony thru the hotel's reservations on the day that we were to travel. The rate was great as it was a 4th of July promotional rate (a week prior to the 4th). I told the reservationist it was our anniversary & he upgraded us to a private balcony!! We were in room 425. We checked in on a Tuesday & stayed two nights. When we arrived there was a bottle of champagne iced down & two glasses with a anniversary card signed by all the staff waiting for us! HOW SPECIAL!!!! We opened it, made a toast & began our vacation! The room was really nice & was very quiet. One whole wall was brick. We had a couch & a flat screen TV. It was a nice sized room with french doors that opened out to our balcony, a very small balcony, but just ours! There were two straightbacked chairs to sit in, but it was more comfortable to just stand & watch the happenings down on the river. The 4th floor is perfect, not too close to the river & the noises that come with it, but not too high that the treetops blocked your view. There was another door to out that opened to a "shared" balcony. Shared by three other rooms. Which would be great if you were with a larger group. The bathroom had granite countertops & wonderful large towels. Shower was great. The hotel is in a historic old school building. So it has wonderful San Antonio charm. It's laid out a bit odd & you have to walk a bit to get to the elevators. Which were a bit on the slow & HOT side. (they had record heat - 106 while we were there). UGGG. The pool was AWESOME!! We think it was a saltwater pool. The water was perfect! The staff at the pool was great. We ate snacks & had drink by the pool one entire day! Heaven!! The staff was SUPER from the second we drove up til the minute we left (sadly). The front desk staff greeted us by name the whole time we were there. The concierge was so helpful. Tony was our bellman & he was great! He recommended a restaurant off site (as we wanted Mexican)... and said we might be able to use the hotel's limo service. Great idea!! We called & were accomodated right away. Ronnie was our driver & he dropped us off at the restaurant, gave us his card for us to call him to come back for us. He was great!! The staff seems so eagar to please & make your stay a special one. This is a fantastic hotel. I WILL always stay here in the future. We ate breakfast at the hotel's restaurant one morning. We had the buffet & sat out on their patio. The food was EXCELLENT & again, the staff was incredible. $19 pp - all you can eat. I didn't think I could eat $19 worth of breakfast....but once I was done, I didn't complain about the price. It was worth it. THANKS Omni La Mansion del Rio for making us feel "SPECIAL". We will return!!

“Very Expensive Hotel and Great Location” No major complaints about the Long Wharf Marriott, except our room assignment. In fairness to the hotel though, we checked in quite early and were given the option of taking room 158, or waiting for a different room. The view was hardly inspiring given the rave reviews I'd read on here about the location. Frankly our view sucked, as you can see by the pictures, but we didn't spend much time in the room. That said, it's a solid, even above average, Marriott experience. Only weird thing was the way the bathroom door opened, more like a dish cupboard door, rather than a room door. Breakfast was included in our rate for about $429 a night, which by the time you added in taxes, it came closer to $479. But the location was perfect for Fanieul Hall and the Greenway experience. For those of you traveling to or from Logan Airport, the hotel is right above the Aquarium stop and it's about a 10 minute ride (or less) from the airport on the subway. Nice pool and a great view there of Boston Harbor. There is a nice reading area near checkin, which was stocked with wonderful books. Because of the hotel's expense, we only did one night there and then 2 nights at the Back Bay Hilton, which I've also reviewed. If you can afford this hotel, you'll be happy. It's a bustling, quality experience that one comes to expect from Marriott. Everyone we encountered at the hotel was really nice. Bottom line: expensive and good, but doubt I'd splurge again.

“A great place to stay in Austin-nice views and more!” I stayed at this hotel while visiting Austin to visit a friend;s grave who had recently passed away. The hotel was very near the airport and I had no difficulties finding it. It was convenient to downtown via Riverside Dr., or other areas of Austin via Ben White Rd. to the highways and Interstate. The staff was exceptionally helpful with suggestions for food and things to do. I did not eat breakfast at the hotel, due to my wake up time. The rooms were nice, the bed comfortable. I had an excellent view of one of the runways at the airport and enjoyed watching planes as they landed. I would most definitely plan to stay here again!

“I really Like This Hotel” I have stayed at the Hyatt Regency Capitol Hill on a number of occasions when I have had business in D.C. I stayed again this week and was reminded why I really like this hotel. First, its location is perfect. It is walking distance to the Capitol Mall with all of the monuments, so if you want to play tourist, it is perfect. If you have seen all of the monuments and want to do something else, the Natiional Gallery of Art, the Natural History Museum, and a number of other free museums are in walking distance. It is three tree-lined blocks from the Capitol, so if you have business on the hill, there is no better place. It is three blocks from Union Station, so, if you are like me and you do not want to pay for a cab to get everywhere, it is perfect. Union Station also has a number of shops (although major construction is underway this summer). In addition to being in the perfect location, the rooms are very nice and the staff seems to understand that it is its job to help you and to make your stay comfortable. There is a lounge, a work-out facility and meeting rooms as well. I, however, never use the gym because the Capitol Mall is a great place to run. The only down-side is that it is expensive. So, if you are like me and are usually on a budget, I highly suggest you stay here if you have business in the district and want to bring your family. While you work, your family will have plenty to do.

“Beautiful hotel - almost perfect” We stayed here for three nights for a major dance competition. The service was over the top amazing. Every person we interacted with was wonderful from the front desk to the army of people they had in the halls. The staff at all of the restaurants from the buffet to Stetsons were perfection. I wish I could clone that level of service everywhere I go. My only gripe was about the room, which wasn't bad, but I felt could have been better. A mini fridge would have been great. There was a serious lack of dresser space. There was something that resembled an old night stand in the closer but it only had one drawer in it. After 3 days it gets very difficult for 2 people to live out of suitcases.

“New Hypo-Allergenic Room and Same Convenient Location” The beauty of staying at the Grand Hyatt is it's proximity to Union Square. There is something for everyone in the area. Even after having lived in San Francisco for a number of years, the appeal of downtown never grows old. Theatres, spa treatments, music, art museums, and of course, shopping are all within walking distance. The Grand Hyatt is in the process of renovation. The lobby is all boarded up and it is quite crowded as there is little space to hang around while checking in. I was told all that would go away by Summer. We were upgraded to a city-view Pure room which has a hypo-allergenic environment. There is a HEPA filtering machine in the room -- yes, you can hear it but it didn't interfere with my sleep. The room also has individual reading lamps with adjustable goosenecks. The furniture is modern and sleek --with an electronic window shade that you can operate from your bedside. Modern and clean and very comfortable bed. We went on a AAA package which included breakfast. The wait staff was harried and the food was okay...you can dine on better fare elsewhere. But really, what you're there for is the gorgeous view. And on a day like we had, it re-emphasized why San Francisco is one of the most beautiful cities in the world. It can get expensive so always be on the look-out for specials or packages. If you want to try something touristy but different, go to Mason and O'Farrell and try the GoCar tours. Guided by a GPS you ride in a 2-person car, powered by an engine with controls akin to a motorcycle. if you follow the tour route, especially the one that takes you beneath the Golden Gate bridge, you're treated to wonderful sites with an accompanying narrative. You can't go over 30 miles per hour and you have to crank up the volume to hear the tour over the sound of the motor -- but it is fun nonetheless. Be sure to wear warm clothes and gloves as it sometimes gets windy. The perspective is great because you're in an open-air vehicle.

“Amazing Unique Hip Experience” This is hip at its hippest! When we pulled up to the Liberty Hotel, I thought "wow - this is going to be a place I will never forget". And it turns out I was right. Despite the fact that it was freezing outside, the minute we pulled up, a gentleman opened our car doors and helped us with our luggage. Once we went inside, we were greeted by one of the most amazing hotel lobbies you will ever see. Words cannot describe how unique the lobby is, so I am not even going to try. But take my word for it - it's an architectural wonder. Open and airy yet cozy and chic. Just beautiful. And because it was happy hour on a Friday, people were arriving to have drinks in the hotel's lobby bar. Needless to say, it was a bit crowded because this hotel is definitely a hot spot in Boston. Once we checked in (which, by the way, was very easy and quick), we went to our room and were amazed at how chic and cozy it was. A thick duvet on the bed was soft and inviting, as was the sunk-in bathtub and large flat screen television. This is definitely a room one could just lounge in for a day or two. After checking in, we went to the lobby for a drink. By this time, it was incredibly crowded in the lobby and all the tables were taken. We paid a premium for 1 glass of champagne ($25) but it was tasty! Then we went exploring in Boston! The great thing is that there is a subway stop directly next to the hotel. From there, you can get to central boston, or even take it to the JFK museum! In all, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The stay was nice, the hotel was amazing and the location was wonderful! I would recommend this hotel to young people and those who like chic and hip!

“Hollywood History and Charm” This is a great hotel. Although the room was looking just a little tired, the common areas of the hotel were amazing, and we would definitely return for the history and charm, the great restaurants, food and bar, and the exceptionally friendly staff.

“Pleasant stay overall” We stayed at the Sheraton Suites for the July 4th weekend with our Starwood Starpoints. Although it turned out to be a pleasant stay, our intial impression was not very good -- when we asked hotel staff if we could park in the parking lot, he was unnecessarily snobby and aloof. (By the way, it costs about $24 to park in the lot per day.) We ended up just finding street parking. Next, we checked in. We had asked for a non-smoking suite, but somehow we were given a former-smoking suite. The person at the front desk was very apologetic about that, but said that they would spray the room so we couldn't smell the remnants of past smoke. That was a bit off-putting, but when we opened the door to our suite, we were pleasantly surprised. It was very spacious, and the view our hotel room had was pretty nice. We were even able to view some of the fireworks from our room! I liked how the living room was separated from our bedroom with french doors. The bathroom was a bit weird -- the sink was separated from the shower and toilet area with a series of sliding doors that were sometimes hard to slide completely shut. Nonetheless, it was fine. The bed was extremely comfortable and gave us some good night's sleep! We used both the jacuzzi and the (small) swimming pool, but it was always crowded. Nonetheless, once people started leaving, it became more pleasant to use. The only complaints we had were basically the snooty staff at the entrance of the hotel as well as the noise level -- the walls seem to be very thin -- I could hear my neighbor! Besides that, I would stay at the hotel again. While it's not completely central to the San Diego sites, it was fine enough, and in a rather safe area as well.

“Good Value” I just returned from a stay at this hotel and would have no problem staying there again.It is a short walk up 7th Ave to Times Square and the Theatre District,about 15 minutes.It is also close to many Subway lines so you can get around the city easily.Rooms are small but you aren't going to New York to sit in your room.One drawback is only 2 elevators so at peek times you might have a short wait to get one.Also no express checkout from your room.I saw some long lines at times waiting to checkout.Area around hotel looks a little doubtful but I had no problems during my stay.Free hot breakfast is a nice plus.Also staff was very helpful in answering any questions .Well worth what I paid.

“Comfortable clean spacious rooms in large conference-center style hotel.” This large conference-center style Marriott in downtown L.A. is a fair bargain for the leisure traveller if you find a good price. While it is located in the downtown business district of Los Angeles, which has comparitively little interest to many other nooks and areas of the sprawling Los Angeles area, a certain amout of any tourist's time will be required in the car, driving around between these many areas of interest. And there are a few good options for dining, chic drinks and entertainment within walking distance of the hotel, as well. A big car port and valet service opens up into a soaring lobby, with wings of conference rooms in all directions. The rooms were big, spacious, comfortable, clean, modern. We had a view out onto 3 overlapping highways surrounded by palm trees, which is a very "Los Angeles" view, and I did not mind it at all, as the sound-proofed windows kept the noise out. (the highways are not TOO close to the hotel.) My top reccomendation: walk to the nearby Standard Hotel Downtown to their ultra-chic rooftop bar / adult playground. This outdoor venue, high amidst the glass skycrapers of downtown Los Angeles seen in every TV show and film depicting L.A., is complete with a bright green astroturf floor around a swimming pool, fireplace, bed-pods, well poured martinis and a uber fashionable crowd straight off the pages of Wallpaper magazine. A very "L.A." experience for the out of towner. I will certainly go back for a third time.

“Value hotel on 57th street” We stayed at the Salisbury Hotel for 5 nights over Christmas 2009. The hotel is in an excellent location on 57th street. There are 2 subway stations within minutes of the hotel, Central Park is also 2 blocks away. The hotel was exactly as we expected after reading many reviews on tripadvisor. It is a bit dated, but the rooms are a good size. We had 2 double beds, a walk in wardrobe, safe in room, iron and ironing board, flat screen tv and mini kitchen with a microwave. We were on the 11th floor facing 57th street and you can hear street noise. It wasn't an issue for us though. If you are a light sleeper then perhaps requesting a room not facing the street would be advisable. The breakfast consisted of cereals, bagels, waffles, donuts and bread. It was $6 per adult and free for children 5 and under. We considered it good value for what was on offer. We arrived at the start of the breakfast as it got busy and people had to queue to get a table as we were finishing. Before we arrived we purchased the New York City Pass. This certainly saved time in attractions such as Natural History Museum and MoMA. These museums can get extremely busy, it is best to visit early. The best investment you can make is to buy a metrocard, the subway will take you everywhere you want to go. Overall our experience in New York was superb. The city is amazing and it was made better by staying in a decent hotel with a great location. I would advise staying here as we had no complaints whatsoever.

“Inexpensive and convenient 3 star” Nothing special but at my $69 AAA rate this was an incredible bargain. Rooms are closet-sized but nicely finished, with comfortable bedding and flat panel TV's. Paper-thin walls but the couple next door went to bed to save my sleep. Perfect location for Union Station, Capitol Hill area, and a modest but friendly staff. Do NOT visit if you intend to valet ($40 overnight); I arrived by cab so felt no pain.

“Excellent Extended-Stay Hotel” The Homewood Suites Memphis-Hacks Cross became our "home away from home" when we had to move out of our Memphis house for four days due to construction. The hotel is located directly behind a Hampton Inn & Suites, and both properties are directly across the street from the world headquarters of FedEx Express. While technically in Memphis, it is on the fringe of the city, adjoining the suburb Germantown, and is in an area that has seen several retail and restaurant chains move into recently. Nearby restaurants include Outback Steakhouse, On The Border, Olive Garden, TGI Fridays, Logan's Roadhouse, McAlister's Deli, Buffalo Wild Wings and Dixie Cafe. We reserved one of the larger suites, with two king beds, along with the usual Homewood amenities: two TV's, sofa-bed, small dining table, kitchenette (stovetop, microwave, refrigerator but no oven). Breakfast each morning was very good, offering a rotating selection of hot entrees (pancakes, eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuits & gravy) as well as standard cold fare (cereal, bagels, fruit). Rooms were well-maintained and service was excellent. During our stay, we did have a problem with some ants coming in our room (to get out of the cold), but maintenance quickly responded and they made it right during check-out. While you shouldn't expect luxury (it is a 3-star hotel) it is an excellent choice, particularly if you need a suite with kitchenette facilities. Highly recommended.

“Usual Uber-Chic W Experience” This is the newest & hottest hotel in Austin, directly in competition w/the Four Seasons, which has been there for many years & is very traditional. Usual W experience: stylish people, sophisticated & very modern decor, young & hip staff, interesting menu. I had an accessible room so it was probably larger than most, very spacious. Bathroom has almost no counter space, but that might be b/c it was accessible. Kind of dark w/all that concrete & targeted lighting. I had problems w/the Internet but the IT guy was great & got it resolved immediately. Very slow service at breakfast but the food was excellent. If price is no object & you want to see the beautiful people in Austin, definitely stay here.

“Adequate” I stayed here for a meeting at the Denver Convention Center which is about 3 blocks away. It is also just about 2 blocks away from the 16th St Mall. I arrived about 2:40pm in the afternoon and waited in line for about 15-20 min to check in. One bottleneck was a person whose reservation they couldn't find. And there were 2 people inline ahead of me who were checking back to see if there room was ready (they weren't ) and mine wasn't either. I was told that checkin time was 3pm and they would call me when the room was ready. I looked for a bellman to check my bag and trudged to the meeting with my backpack. As soon as I got there I got a call that the room was ready so trudged back. I checked in with the same person I had spoken to 30 minutes earlier and he acted like he had never seen me before. I checked out with the same person and no recognition then either. The room was adequate and the fitness center was well-equipped although very crowded one morning. When i asked for a FedEx box to ship some things home, I just got a point 'There's a FedEx across the street.' I needed a bellman for something a couple of times and there was a wait both times. In contrast, when I walked out of the Hyatt Regency coming back from the convention center (the Regency is across from the conv ctr) there were several helpful bellmen, always asking if I needed help or directions. Also the Regency had a bustling lobby with nice bar, restaurant, and coffee shop. Grand Hyatt had small and quiet lobby with much smaller bar and plain looking restaurant. Would not stay at thisnGrand Hyatt again if I had a choice.

“Great location and an indoor pool too!” My family and I (wife and 6 yo son) stayed for 7 nights. We selected the hotel because of its proximity to Moscone Convention Center and the presence of a pool. The indoor pool was a big plus, because the weather in SF was about 50 degrees - the pool (and the fitness room) were well kept and opened very early (5 am for the pool) which was very helpful for travelers from the East Coast. Overall the facilities were clean and well maintained. Front desk staff were helpful and friendly. The room was clean with a decent view. The restaurant had a buffet breakfast which was good, although pricey. I ordered something off the menu (ie avoided the buffet) and it took quite a bit more time for preparation and did not come out very appetizing. The location was within a few blocks of Moscone and a few blocks of Market Street. It was about a 15 minute walk (25 minutes with a 6 yo) from the Ferry Building.

“A Lot of Style and Not a lot of Substance” A cool lounge-y vibe permeates the entire property. That being said, I found it too dark and dank. The coolness extends to the check in desk, where you'd better keep your cool as you wait in line 30 minutes to hand someone your credit card just so they can hand you a room key. Seriously, management, why is there always a loong wait at the check in counter? If you think you're the hippest hotel in town, put in a kiosk and let us self check in and be on our way! Now that you have your key, open the door to the tiniest of tiny rooms in all of NYC. Even the furniture has been imported from Lilliputian Land to fit into the toy doll house rooms. Your 7 year old might think it's cool, but wait until you lie on the bed, which is only inches above the floor. Throw me a rope and pull me out! Check out the image of the bathroom. It was so small that when I sat on the pot, I was forced to spread my legs or they would crunch the wall in front of me. I'm six feet, so anybody over average height and weight will have an issue. Here's my final take: 18-34 you might think this place is cool 35-49 you will probably not think this place is cool 50 and above you will wish you had booked the Holiday Inn Express By the way, 3 calls to the front desk to try and get a remote for the TV.....I'm still waiting!

“Great Dallas Hotel - North of City” Unique location - attached to large mall. Other reviews are accurate, hotel has everything except fine dinning and a bar (they do have a small bar and small dinning on the second floor). However, the mall has numerous places to eat and some have a small attached bar. The pool area is beautiful if the weather is nice. Would definitely stay here again! Regarding parking, you can pay for valet parking, or park in the open mall spots directly in front of the hotel.

“Perfect Location but Everything Not so Fabulous” As a frequent business traveler, I was not sure what to expect from this Wyndham as they tend to be hit or miss in my experience. As others have mentioned, this property is in a perfect location. Only one block away from Union Square, shopping along Market Street, and walking distance to all of San Fran's public transportation options. Parking at the hotel is pricey ($48/day) but there is a public garage 2-3 blocks away which charges $25/day. The entrance and lobby have clearly been renovated but the rooms have not. While clean the rooms/bathroom were clearly a bit dated. While not the best it was not the worst room I have ever seen. I also agree with other reviewers....the NOISE is striking. I have never stayed in a hotel where so much outside noise comes into your room. Even while staying on the 26th floor you can hear voices, sirens, and just about anything else at all hours of the day. We were able to secure this hotel through bidding on priceline at $120/night which was a great deal. If we paid anything more I would have been a bit more disappointed in the stay. If location is your priority this may be the place to stay; if absolute luxury is your goal definitely look into other options.

“Nice Hotel Convenient Uptown Location!” The Hilton Charlotte Center City has everything you would expect from a Hilton property. The staff is friendly and the rooms are well equipped. The hotel is centrally located and within walking distance of the NASCAR Hall of Fame and the Time Warner Cable Arena as well as numerous restaurants. Also close to the light rail. I stay here occassionally on business and have always had a great experience.

“Nice Hotel, great stay....but depends on whose paying and how much?” Overall I had no complaints on the hotel its self. As a Starwood Gold member, I was upgraded to a "Spectacular Room" on the 55th floor. Had a corporate rate of $289 which for mid week is quite good. A little taken away with some of the costs of the extras...$41 for a two egg breakfast, which was the only option first thing in the AM as the restaurant didn't open until 7 as most places didnt....$7.84 for a diet coke from the mini bar, again no other options so it is what it is when it is 15 degrees outside and didn't feel like venturing off. Bed was quite comfortable, nice shower with a modern waterfall type sink...little disappointed in the lobby...simple bar and no restuarant in the main part. Would I stay there again, depends on how much and whose paying. As a category 6 hotel requiring 20,000 points, in my opinion much better to stay at a category 5 hotel (Westin a couple blocks away or one of the Sheraton Hotels)....but for a reasonable corporate or weekend rate, would definitely return.

“Very Nice Hotel - Not Best Location” This is a beautiful hotel; especially the Fairmont Gold rooms, but the location is a little out of the way and usually ahve to sue taxis when I stay here. Would defientley recommend it if you cna get a good deal on a room.

“It's a nice average Doubletree - being remodeled” Tiny bathroom - so small you have to move the door out of the way to get in/out of the shower and you can't open/close the door if you're sitting on the toilet. Being remodeled but you can still get many touches of the old hotel this used to be. It's fine, but not great.

“Historic, fancy, central, but $$$$” The hotel overall is ornate and fancy, but if I was paying cash I would never stay here (I stayed on points). I would sooner go for a W Hotel or Westin - I prefer the more modern hotels. And for the price of the hotel, I would expect the rooms to be a bit better maintained. I subtracted one star for the hotel missing these details. Its my first time staying here and when I entered the room, I thought "that's it?" Of course I had high expectations -- its the Waldorf right? This is where rooms can cost $600+ per night. I was there on Saturday and the Sunday brunch looked amazing, though at $99/person, skipped it. Pro's -The location is very central to midtown -Very ornate and beautiful -Salvatore Ferragamo shampoo/conditioner -When I requested more shampoo/conditioner, they were brought right up to the room and someone called immediately after to see if I got everything I asked for. -The bed was *very* comfortable Con's -The rooms are just average, considering which hotel this is -The flat screen TV is a cheap Phillips model (not a big deal, I wasnt there to watch tv) -There were a few spots where the paint was peeling on the ceiling, a rusty patch about half the size of a dollar bill, on the window (I've posted a photo) -The curtain seam was falling apart -2 Bottles of water were supposed to be complimentary but there was only 1 of the "Waldorf" branded bottles in the fridge. A phone call and asking twice still resulted in no water being brought up. I left the hotel for a few hours, came back, and had to call again to finally receive the water.

“Exquisite Hotel but expensive” Overall an excellent hotel. First class service, high quality rooms, but at a price. If you can afford it I can definitely recommend it. It is right near the shopping center of San Francisco but kind of far from all the typical touristy spots. The hotel bar and restaurant were both very nice.

“Very good, but my expectations were higher” The Waldorf Astoria has built its reputation on elegance and luxury. In this case, it's also in Midtown Manhattan, centrally located for business or pleasure in Manhattan. The lobby is spectacular, the service I received was courteous and professional, and the room I experienced was spacious, very comfortable, and, quiet (important in the city that never sleeps). The hotel staff has is prepared for the international traveler, and I heard several languages in dialogue between staff and guests while there. My corporate room rate made this, all-in-all, a very good experience. BUT, I also noted that my room furnishings were 1950s era, the wi-fi was an expensive add-on, and my basic breakfast (bacon, eggs, hash browns, toast, juice, coffee) was above $50. ,I would stay again (and probably will on business at the corporate rate), but it is not the special experience that you might expect from the Waldorf-Astoria in New York.

“Pretty good” This hotel is well located near Time Square but as a result, it is pricey. Even on Priceline, it came in at over $240 a night. Rooms are functional and have all the necessities. I have to say they are small but aparently most rooms in New York hotels are. Either way, it was a comfortable room. The service was good and the staff helpful. As the location is very central, it is very busy and noisy around the hotel. Time Square is busy at all hours so consider this as most outdoor noise can be heard from the hotel.

“Convenient location” I stayed here one night after I had a minor surgery done in a nearby medical office. My sister stayed with me. Check-in went smoothly (I was even able to check-in early). The room was spacious with 2 beds, TV reception was fine, and room ammenities were quality. The hotel was very convenient--my sister went shopping in the nearby Keystone Mall while I slept after my surgery. She also brought back a take-out dinner from a mall restaurant (there are several choices). The parking was a breeze--an attached garage with a covered 3rd floor walkway. My only complaint is the fee for wifi. We didn't use it since there is a charge and we were there such a short time. We did notice there are several computers for use in the lobby--and saw several businessmen working there. I thought nowadays all hotels had complimentary wifi, but I guess not. This is the first time I'd stayed in this hotel though I have been in it for conferences before. The hotel is nice, the workers seemed friendly and helpful, & the room was clean. I would certainly stay here again!

“A reasonable option for downtown accommodation” Don't expect a spic-and-span doubletree at this location even though it costs 200+USD per night. Positives: 1. reasonable location from most downtown attractions - 20 something minutes walk from Quincy Market, boston convention center, back bay and a relatively close ride from airport. 2-minute walk to chinatown if you like cheap food (beware of the homeless population within the area) 2. reasonably clean as you would expect from this chain. Negatives: 1. received a one-bed room even though we paid for a two-beds room. 2. Rooms are old and small, appears to be converted from a college residence. There was no bath tub in our room. 3. Gym accessed to YMCA is poorly coordinated and slightly misleading. Need to go outside to access the facility (there's a walkway through the roof top but the elevator service was unreliable). And must provide personal information to YMCA upon entry, which throws customers off guard as not everyone goes to the hotel gym with a photo ID!! 4. Used questionable product to clean room - caused itchiness all over body for both myself and my partner. Overall, an ok experience.

“Long in the Tooth” This hotel was once called "the second most important address in Washington DC." Sadly, that was about 50 years ago. About the only thing going for it is location. Rooms are dark, small, old and overpriced. When the air conditioning comes on, it's like a wind tunnel. The exercise room was very good. The property is void of any energy. Look elsewhere.

“Pleasantly Surprised” The service was excellent from arrival to departure. The Front Desk Agents were extremely helpful and informative, the bellman was also great. My guest room was very roomy and comfortable. The front desk called my room after I checked in to assure everything was good with my room, a standard for their hotel that I have not experienced at other hotels. I attended a conference at the hotel and the banquet staff, audio visual staff, and catering staff were all great. The breakfasts, however, during the conference had too many sweet items. It would have been nice to have some bagels or muffins at least. I realize this may not be the hotels fault if the client selected the breakfasts, but the catering staff should keep that in mind as they guide their clients through the selection process. DFW is about a 35 minute drive from the hotel which was the only downside. Overall experience was a very pleasant surprise.

“Excellent Airport Hotel” I had a late flight from East Coast that meant I would arrive at SEATAC at what would be "my 1 a.m." so I chose to stay at this hotel. I am very glad that I did. The airport shuttle arrived soon after I had claimed luggage and made my way to the pick-up point. The driver was friendly and helpfu. Upon arrival I was greeted warmly by the front desk and had no problems checking in. The room was on the main floor and I had requested a higher floor, but it was not a problem. The room was very quiet and looked onto the interior atrium. The room was nicely appointed and the bed very comfortable. There was good water pressure but the towels did have a sour smell. Once when walking down the hallway I stopped at a maid's cart to sniff the towels on it -- same not so pleasant odor. I had breakfast in the concierge room and it was very busy and a bit cramped, but the staff was doing a good job clearing tables, apologizing, and trying to make it work. Since I was up early I took a walk down to the light rail station which is right down the hill. It was very convenient and I was pleased to use it to get downtown to the hotel I stayed in for the next night. The light rail takes about as long as a taxi into Seattle, but it is clean and pleasant. SEATAC is about a half hour from downtown so I did not want to make this my destination hotel. It was great for my purposes and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a place near SEATAC.

“Wish I could have stayed longer” On the outside, this place doesn't look like anything to write home about but the suite we stayed in was very comfortable and great value for money. Actually, the room itself was tiny, with barely any room to move about but the living area was very spacious. We had a view of the pool and the ocean. The hotel staff was very helpful in providing us with a guide of what to do in San Diego. The complimentary breakfast was great and parking was free (open lot). Locating this place wasn't easy or may be it was just my GPS' issues. Location: You need a car/taxi to get into downtown San Diego where the night life rocks but if you are looking for just calm relaxation, this is the place. I am a light sleeper and I didn't get bothered by the plane noise that some people mentioned.

“SUPER” Le meilleur rapport qualité-prix que j'ai jamais vu à NY. Grande chambre, 2 grands placards, déco très chic (petit bémol pour la SDB petite et déco plus ancienne), kitchenette avec frigo et micro-onde, le tout très récent et en parfait état. A priori un peu excentré mais quartier très vivant et station 72ème à 50 mètres desservie par la 1 mais aussi les express 2/3 qui vous mettent à 1 station de Times Square et à 2 de Penn Station! Seul bémol : internet payant, ce qui devient mesquin de nos jours...

“Excellent Hotel - Four Points” This hotel is in an excellent location and it is off the major streets so it is quiet. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay - the rooms are large, modern and well appointed. I also decided to have breakfast at the hotel & it was excellent. Restaurants are a brisk walk away, but there are many good ones which are close. I ate at Genki Sushi which was only a five minute walk away.

“Great comfort and space” We loved the Phillips Club. Our one bedroom apartment with full kitchen was bright, spacious and very handsomely appointed. It was well designed and maintained. It was great having use of the Reebok Club across the street which is a terrific gym ____much better than the typical hotel facility. Also, we enjoyed the neighborhood and good location. Of course, if you are looking for all the amenities that are provided in hotels, ex. room service, attention to your every whim, this may not be the place for you. There is no restaurant or bar. But, we found the staff very courteous and helpful. We felt as if we were living in the city instead of visiting tourists.
“Good experience, great view, nice room for SFO” The beds were comfortable, the room was basic and nice...good location in the Financial District.

“We'll be back to this one!” We had never stayed at a SpringHill Suites, and were very pleasantly surprised with this hotel. This hotel was excellant from the moment we walked through the door. We had just driven many hours on I-95 and needed a place to rest. The room was perfect - clean and spacious. The staff was one of the best I have ever encountered. The breakfast bar was also very good. There are several chain restaurants within walking distance, and we ate at a good Longhorn Steakhouse. Many days later we could not find one of our bags and thought we had left it at the hotel. I called the hotel and although they could not find the bag (we later found it someplace else), the staff took the time to look. Great hotel, and we plan to be back because of it!

“Trying for the Kimpton look but not cutting it” The hotel has excellent service. This is the best part of the hotel. Each person encountered was pleasant and helpful. We were given a 4 pm late check out on New years day, which was unexpected and very nice. The problems are with the rooms. We paid $159 for a Junior Suite. Not horribly expensive, not horribly cheap. I would argue that the room we had was a Junior Suite. A small bay in the windows accounted for the "Junior." The bed was comfortable but the furnishings which appeared to be somewhat new seemed cheap and uninspiring. The hotel is in the University District. This was clearly advertised. I guess I was expecting some charm and quaintness but it was more seedy and downtrodden, than I expected. On our next trip to Seattle, we would select another hotel.

“Modern, trendy, but smokers definitely not welcome.” This large hotel is modern in design and is aimed at the younger traveller. It is in a fine location next to the Theatre District and is surrounded by a wide range of restaurants, some of which are excellent. The staff are really welcoming and helpful, even to older customers. The rooms are large and comfortable. However if you are a smoker you will find no welcome here (or in the rest of Boston for that matter). It is the pavement for you, with no cover and no seats.

“Our new hotel in NYC” We stay in NYC at least 5 times per year, and have had our favorites over the years, which we have posted here. But the last time we thought we would stop at the Library Hotel since our trip brought us to the New York Public Library for research. What a great place. at the corner of Madison and 41st it is easy to get to Grand Central and Penn Station, as well as being just a few steps off Fifth. The Staff was courteous and friendly, as well as knowledgeable and helpful, and we were able to check in early (unusual, but not unheard of). Caveat: The rooms are small - this is not a suite hotel, but rather a well appointed, pied-a-terre in the city, where they make use of every square foot of space. Very clean, the room was perfect for us - and even with a room across from the elevator, and a very light sleeper, the room was quiet and peaceful. Good internet service, and the continental breakfast provided gratis was excellent. The prior evening there was also a wine and cheese reception, which was a nice way to unwind after a day walking the city and doing research. Will go there again in a heartbeat. Our new favorite hotel in NYC.

“Very nice” I was at this hotel as part of convention and was placed into the "secured" area as a frequent traveler upgrade. The room was spacious, quiet, and efficient for working. Excellent location within walking distance of many downtown attractions. I needed a late checkout on the day I left and the staff was very accomodating. I asked for an airport taxi 5 minutes before leavign and it was waiting for me when I checked out. Only $15 via private service. I'd stay here again.

“Close to perfect...close.” This is my second time staying here- I was there for three nights for a meeting. All of the physical parts of the hotel are wonderful. The lobby, restaurant, guest rooms, fitness center and banquet facilities are remarkable. I am very impressed at their relatively recent renovation. The food was amazing- both in the restaurant and in the catered meetings. The only reason I am giving it 4 stars is that the hotel has lost some of its attention to service. I had at least three instances of Hyatt staff apathy- something I am not used to seeing from the brand. 1. Upon check in, I asked if an suite upgrade was available due to my Hyatt Status and an upgrade certificate I had been sitting on from Hyatt. The man said that unfortunately nothing was available (which I totally understand). However, he went on to further imply that he hooked me up with a very nice room. The room was awesome, but all the rooms were awesome. I'm at a meeting with 100 of my closest friends- I soon found out that mine was the same as everyone else's. No problem- just don't mislead me. 2. I'm a fit guy and like to take the stairs to my room. I ran into an employee in the stairwell and let him know that the door to 9 was locked. This caused me to go from 6 to 9 that morning on the stairs, then back to 8 to take the elevator to 9 to workout. Seems kind of stupid. He told me that it was because of security. I suggested that they key code it from the inside and he told me that it wouldn't work. That didn't make sense- tons of hotels and even your elevators do that. It made me more irritated to discover that the hotel in the other stairwell is NOT locked on 9. So much for the security excuse. 3. Internet. My Passport should have entitled me to internet access at no charge. It did, however I had to call down to the front desk each of the first two days so they could give me a code to get on when my name and room number didn't work. I asked for them to just do it for all 3 days, and they seemed really put off but finally called me back with a code to do that. Not major stuff- the stay was wonderful. However, I know you guys read your comments and I want to help you be perfect.

“Great Deal” PROS Stayed for 6 nights. Daily Breakfasts and dinners on Monday – Thursday. Breakfast was scrambles eggs served with a rotating two of the following: bacon, sausages, corn beef hash, and potatoes. There was also the normal cereal, instant oatmeal, bread/toast, yogurt and fruit salad. Made it for 2 dinners, one with raviolis, with choice of red or white sauce. The other dinner was chicken and potatoes. There’s also green salad, and some deserts came out later. Wine and Bud Lite from tap is also served. Shopping and restaurants within walking distance behind the hotel. Business office had 3 PC’s each with a black and white laser printer (one was not working). I found this great! Lots of places usually have only one PC and no printer. Great size room, full kitchen, full size refrigerator, dishwasher, sink, plates, and utensils. There’s a large flat screen that was on the dresser along the wall in the middle. Situated so that you can swivel it to watch from the couch or turn it so you can watch from the bed. Also in the room was a work desk, a small table you can eat at, and ottoman used as a coffee table. There’s WiFi and cable for a direct internet hook up. Room looks just like the pictures in Homewood Suites’ advertisement. . Except for the WWF bout going on above, the room was quiet with the adjacent rooms. CONS 22 miles from Phoenix if you wanted to do stuff downtown. Exercise room had 2 treadmills and a stair stepper. The only weights were free weights with one bench. Look out, the location was not on my GPS. Just exit North 17 at W Pinnacle Peak Road, the hotel is just a quarter mile on the right.

“Stylish, Wonderful Location” I stayed two midweek nights at the Harbor Court ( a Kimpton property) and found the location, amenities, and design to be top notch. The welcome is warm and gracious, and staff make an attempt to satisfy your every need. I paid $224/night for a deluxe king bay view room (senior rate on the Kimpton website), and while not inexpensive the rate was better than the larger chain hotels in the city, especially the Hyatt Regency and Le Meridien that are close by. I'm normally a loyal Starwood guest, but this time I decided to try Kimpton, and the experience was gratifying. Pluses: 1) The location right on the Embarcadero is fantastic! Try for a bay view room. Over the years the Harbor Court's location has only become more advantageous as the Embarcadero has become increasingly people friendly. The Ferry Building with it's wide array of food and gift shops and restaurants is spectacular. The Harbor Court provides a jogging map with roundtrip mileage estimates from the Ferry Building to various points along the wharf. 2) Typical for Kimpton, wireless internet access is complimentary. There are two iMacs in the lobby connected to a printer. Under 15 minutes is free, and you start paying for anything over that. 3) Rooms are small, but beautifully and stylishly designed. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in, perhaps excelling over Westin's Heavenly Bed. A wall mounted LCD TV and Aveda bath amenities complete the room. 4) Morning coffee service and evening wine tasting (another Kimpton tradition) is delightful. 5) The Embarcadero YMCA is next door with complimentary access is to Harbor Court guests. Complete fitness facilities include a 25 meter six-lane pool. 6) The BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) Embarcadero stop is two blocks away; so, one can get from SFO to the Harbor Court in under 45 minutes, including walking time from the BART stop to the hotel front door. Fare is about $5 each way from SFO. The Harbor Court is also easily accessible from the Oakland Airport via the same BART stop. 7) Great restaurants within easy walking distance in the neighborhood: Ozumo (in the Harbor Court), Boulevard (at the end of the same block), Slanted Door (Ferry Building across the street), and One Market (two blocks away). Minuses: 1) As mentioned before, rooms are small, and the majority of non-bay view rooms are interior and rather dark. No other disadvantages I can think of. I'll come here again!!

“Everything but the Butler...” This property is conveniently located to the Broadway Theater District and other attractions. Our room was larger than what you normally expect in a NYC hotel, but only had one small window looking out over another building, making the room slightly dark. But, the room was comfortable, cool and quiet. However, the butler service was not all it was cracked up to be...A butler greeted us upon our arrival, showed us the room amenities and provided instructions for summoning a butler. We didn't need butler services that evening, but did call for a butler the next morning for coffee. She responded right away with a French Press pot of coffee, which was excellent, but a little small. I called for another pot, even emailed eButler asking for a second pot, and never received a response. And there were no instructions on the room phone on how to reach the front desk or room service! We finally gave up and checked out...Except for the butler service, this hotel did a good job. All other staff were courteous and helpful.

“exceljent location and service” We stayed in the hotel for 2 nights The location is the best you can ask for The room was large and comfortable and had good amenities The service was excellent and always with a smile The only problem was that we got an interior room and all we can see thru the window was the backyard of another building

“Much better than last visit” When I was here last time, I got shoved into a smoking room without being informed. Upon arriving at the check-in, I was relieved to see the jerk from last time wasn't at the reception. The ladies at the desk were very pleasant & nice. Not as courteous as the Ritz, but friendly enough. I was delighted to hear that now the entire hotel is non-smoking. Nothing against smokers - we all have choices in life. But keep the smoke to yourself if you will. I got an upgrade to a junior suite - which is nice. A lamp's light bulb was dangling off the wire though, so of course it doesn't lit up. Room plan is interesting - bathroom at the main door, then living room, then around the corner the bedroom. So to go to the bathroom from the bed, you need to walk the entire length of the suite. It didn't bother me much cause I worked in my room until 1:30am & then had to get up for an 6am East coast conference call. For the limited time I slept, I slept really well. The bed was very comfortable. The business center was terrible though. They actually charge you for internet access - although the first 30 mins was free. It couldn't log onto my work computer because the computer there lack of Java. The business center is also right next to the lobby where there's a wine bar with super loud jezz playing. Again I couldn't play on the piano. oh well. The restaurant food was mediocre for the price they charge you. I don't know if I will come back...

“Historic location in Printers Row Chicago” We stayed here from Aug 5th to the 7th. We arrived to early to check in, asked the bell captain for a restaurant recommendation, which was Blackies, (see reviews, we were pleased). Upon our return, I explained to the desk clerk, we would be entertaining friends from England and would need to have a room that would accommodate sitting in chairs, after a short discussion we agreed upon upgrading to a corner suite (with a nominal charge). We and our friends were impressed and satisfied with the room.The huge windows gave them wonderful views of Chicago. Living area had large L shaped sofa, two chairs, dining area had table with six chairs and buffet. Separate bedroom had large comfortable bed. Bathroom had separate tub from toilet. We were given drink and breakfast coupons. This hotel is located in historic printers row (history of Chicago is very interesting). We enjoy friendly staff, hotel staff here are helpful, always greet you and assist you with requests.
