It is also only a few blocks from Buddy Guys, our friends had come to the US to travel The Blues Highway, with Chicago being their last stop. They were quite pleased to be able to visit us at the Blake and be so close to a great Blues Club. I would recommend staying at The Blake.

“Very nice, great location, great for couples or business.” Spend a weekend here in the summer. Overall ambiance was very nice. Rooms were fairly large for downtown Boston, clean, and well presented. Very old-world nice. Room service costs were insane, even by the usual standards. We've done the Chocolate Buffet before at Cafe Fleuri, which is simply fantastic and worth the cost every once in a blue moon. Gym & pool/spa were very nice with modern equipment. Location was easy walk to Fanuil Hall & North End (in Financial District)- excellent. The bed was very comfortable & soft. Bathrooms are clean & functional, but thats about it. Not quite up to the overall standard of the bedroom/hotel in general. Service was excellent in general. Highly recommended.

“Design giveth, location taketh away” I spent six nights in this hotel in early October 2012. I was excited to see this property, based on the excellent reviews I'd read. Based on my experience, I feel the hotel is a solid four-star property and an excellent choice for travelers headed to Chicago. I arrived early (9am) with plans to leave my bags with the front desk. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find out that my room was already available. Up to the ninth floor where I was happy to find a very clean and colorful room. While the room was not very big, the layout was very smartly done with some excellent features. Compared to similar modern hotels (NYC's W Hotel Times Square comes to mind), the Blu Aqua is MUCH more comfortable because of the design. The decor was also much brighter and 'happier' in the room, causing me to smile every time I looked at the brilliant teal carpet and sparkly floor tiles. The bed was VERY comfortable, the equal of any hotel bed I've slept in. There was a small balcony for those who wanted to step out for some fresh (30 degree) air. The closet/desk areas were nicely done and very convenient. And while the counter area near the sink was very limited, the shower stall could easily have fit multiple people, if water conservation is high on your priority list. The rest of the hotel is equally well designed. The restaurants, bar are striking visual spaces, though I cannot comment about the food (I did not eat in the hotel). The gym is large and well laid out, with a nice extra: a basketball half-court. Downsides... the biggest potential issue is the fact that there is a fire station located directly adjacent to the hotel. Given that my room faced the same side of the building as the station, I heard the sirens more than a few times during my stay. Also, the doors are heavy and close with enough force (thanks to some amazingly strong springs) to make a resounding 'slam' that can be heard from quiet a distance up and down the hallway. I'm not a light sleeper, so this wasn't an issue for me. But, if you are easily awaken, keep this fact in mind. The location could also deter someone who wants to be RIGHT on Michigan Avenue or RIGHT on the park or RIGHT on the river. It is none of these things. If you want to be close, but not too close to the activity, this location could be a winner for you. Plus, there is an excellent CVS Pharmacy only steps from the front door, giving you convenient access to snacks and sundries. Overall, this hotel made me smile with it's friendly service and well-executed design. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a near-luxury hotel in downtown Chicago.

“Older, but comfortable, big rooms” Exhausted, and heading south, I decided on a whim to stay here for the night. At $55 and right off I-35, the price wasn't bad. This hotel is older, and you feel that inside. However the rooms are all in-facing. They are also VERY large. The bed felt newer, and was comfortable. The continental breakfast was typical, cereal, toast, pastries. The staff was very friendly. Also, it's across the street from the Miller Brewery, so the smell of beer brewing fills the air. The name is somewhat misleading, though. This hotel is not really near downtown Fort Worth, but rather several miles south on I-35.

“Price is right, but would not choose again” Just stayed here for two nights for a convention in San Fran. The event was at the mosconi convention center was was .7 miles away. Since it rained the whole time I was in town, I didn't walk but it seemed further than .7 miles and was a good $6-8 cab ride away. Not a great neighborhood as the hotel has 3 massage parlors, a liquor store and smoke shop within view of the hotel. Unless that is what you are looking for! Felt seedy to me and the hotel was dark and very small. I was supposedly upgraded to a larger room for $12 more a night and my room was very tiny. Can't imagine the non upgraded room. It had everything you need, which all Kimptons do, but most are much nicer. I had meetings at the Marriott marquis which blew away this hotel. Not even same ballpark and I was sorry I didn't pay more (double) to stay there. Especially since that hotel was across the street from the convention center. Overall, if you just need a cheap place to sleep, this is fine. If you are used to a Marriott or hyatt, you won't like this place.

“Paper thin walls, a voyeur's delight” As a Gold Starwood member since the mid-1990's, I expected a lot more. Tiny, tiny room with paper thin walls, bricks for a view. One one side, a heterosexual couple from Europe and on the other an acrobatic homosexual couple of unknown origin. Human copulation in Stereo! I guess that's one of the charms of San Francisco. Luckily, I packed my Bose headphones. Business travelers, avoid this location. There are newer hotels between Union Square and the Moscone Center to choose. They have closed the elegant French restaurant on the top floor and now it is used for special events.

“Not as good as I had hoped.” There were some issues during my stay that made me decide to check out after the first night rather than stay the four nights that I had planned. Based on their impressive website, I expected their VIP program to be worth joining. I checked in and confirmed that my VIP # was in my reservation. The perks associated with the VIP program never materialized and the front desk girl was indifferent. I went up to my room to discover it was a handicap room. I wish the front desk person mentioned this when I was discussing room options with her. I try to stay at boutique hotels and I have come to expect the quirks that come with such hotels. The room was small but very stylish. The leather chair and ottoman along with the bed were extremely comfortable. The huge glass vase is dramatic but the grime on the inside takes away from the rest of the room. Some of the blinds were broken and the faux frosting on the bathroom door was marred. I didn't see anything on the room service menu that appealed to me so I called downstairs. I asked the room service person if there were any specials. The girl said " You mean you want to know if anything on sale?"...UGH. I ended up ordering a burger medium rare but it arrived very well done. This is by no means a bad hotel but I had just hoped that the staff would have been a little more detail oriented.

“Re-done, but...” This hotel has been in serious need of a re-do for some time. It's as if it had been living off its advantageous location in Preston Center. The good news is the renovation, however slowly it's taking place, is pretty good. The room overall was a pleasant surprise - good bed and pillows, nice decor, fine TV, good climate control, etc. The furniture and the fixtures were ok but rather common. And it was sad that the toilet handle/flush valve, though new, already weren't working properly. The biggest inadequacy in the hotel related to technology. Lots of dead zones - which makes it hard for business meetings. And rather galling was the very cheap insistence that you get forced through their little connection program to get to the internet, even if you have your own 3G. To their credit, they provided us a courtesy password. BUT it didn't work, and the front desk twice had to give me alternative codes. This is getting old. Quality hotels need to let their patrons have access, or at least not override those who already have plans. Access to the internet shouldn't be part of the revenue stream for a highly rated business hotel. Having said all this, the service was friendly. And, if they deal with these problems, this hotel could be a lot better than it was.

“Stayed here twice and fantastic!” Being a Starwood Preferred Guest member, I've stayed here twice and loved it both times. The first time was in a standard room, but still very large and comfortable. The second time, was upgraded to a corner deluxe room that had wrap around windows, beautiful views of the Hudson river, and a very well equipped and large bathroom. The major plus of this hotel is location, location, location! Right in the heart of Times Square, very accessible, near Port Authority bus terminal, and the subway stop. But you do pay for the premium of location. The downside of this hotel is that the rooms feel stuffy. The windows don't really open so it is quite humid in the rooms and my corner room with a view had slight smoke smell problem, even though it was a nonsmoking room. The hotel's lobby is very nice and totally quiet/private as it's two floors up from the street level. Concierge were always busy as the hotel has many guests with families to contend with. I would recommend this hotel to families, tourists, and first time visitors to New York.

“My first stay at a Homewood was a success” The staff was very friendly. The hotel is within walking distance of Pike Place Market in one direction and lots of great bars and eateries in the other. Rooms were as expected and the breakfast was better than expected. This is where I plan to stay on my next trip to Seattle (hopefully sooner than later)

“Great Hotel, Perfect Location” I guess the title of my review says it all. This place is located across the street from the Chicago River and a few blocks from the Navy Pier. The decor is contemporary with great bars and restaurants. Despite this I must say that their best asset is their extremely friendly and helpful staff. I am actually looking forward to coming back here next year.

“Good Value: Felt Like an Old Mexican Resort” I enjoyed my stay, especially lounging by the pool under huge palm trees. It is an older hotel but the rates ate reasonable and they are close to a lot of good restaurants. The gym was ok, with mostly just cardio. I would recommend a first floor room facing the courtyard as they have real nice patios.

“great location and price” Manhattan is swamped with hotels so there is no way I could recommend this over other hotels. All I can say is that I had an acceptable experience. The rooms are a bit tired but the lobby is attractive and the service was friendly, warm and welcoming and they certainly helped me get around NYC! The 42nd Street entrance - the most attractive - is closed off for rennovation so that was a bit disappointing but the more discrete 41st entrance is just as good. The theatres are all within walking distance. No free breakfast Im afraid which is why the Hampton Inn portfolio of hotels by hilton are more expensive than this one. If you're a HiltonHhonors member then this is definately a hotel worth collecting your points at.

“Much Better Starwood Options Available, This one needs a facelift” Usually I stay at the Westin or the W in Chicago but when both of those were so expensive, I tried this place. I had actually stayed here years ago and sadly, I think the place looks the same. The public areas are fine, spacious, it's really a big hotel, but the rooms are so dated. It's your typical sheraton and doesn't have a ton of personality, but beyond that, it really needs some updating. Especially for the prices they charge, it seems that the furniture, decor, paint and bathrooms should be refreshed. It really just doesn't look like the typical Starwood quality. I did like that they had bottle water free of charge, which sometimes they do for Spg Platinum and other times they don't. The bell guy who gets the cabs is very friendly and in general their staff seemed to be pretty good, but the location is a bit out of the way and I think I'd only consider if there was a great deal and the other Starwoods were too expensive.

“Wonderful experience and best location for downtown Denver” My wife and I returned to this hotel for our anniversary, after using it for our wedding one year earlier. We were able to have the same room as for our wedding - a beautiful and very spacious king suite. The bed and linenes were wonderfully comfortable. The hotel was in the process of their Christmas season decorating and the lobby was beautifully decorated with colorful lights and garland and bright red mini-trees. What could be better than having a Starbucks and the Rialto Cafe in the same building!? Walk or jump on the 16th St bus and easily go anywhere in the city. The front desk staff were professional and friendly. I would highly recommend this Courtyard for any Denver visit.

“Posizione ottimale e ben collegato con al metro” Posizionato al centro di Boston, proprio a due passi dalla Prudential Tower dalla quale si gode di un bellissimo panorama sulla città, l'hotel è ben collegato con il resto della città grazie a due fermate della metro linea E (verde), una a circa 250m a nord e l'altra a circa 200m a sud della struttura.L' hotel, a due piani,è simile a molti altri hotel di pari categoria in America, semplice con poci fronzoli. Nota negativa, l'ubicazione dell'ascensore al primo piano, raggiungibile attraverso vari gradini,che non agevolano carrozzine di bambini o disabili. Personale abbastanza freddo e distaccato,di poche ed essenziali parole, tuttavia non ho riscontrato nessun problema di sorta. La camera, una doppia con due letti a una piazza e mezza (queen), era spaziosa e pulita, dotata di tutto l'essenziale (asciugacapelli,sapone,shampoo e asciugamani in abbondanza per quanto riguarda il bagno; mentre era presente in stanza il bollitore per te e caffè con fornitura gratuita di questi ultimi e Tv schermo piatto), presente in emtrambe i piani macchina per il ghiaccio e distributore di snack e bibite. Dato che l'hotel si vanta i prezzi migliori della città (io per una doppia ho speso circa 75€ per notte) forse è spiegata la presenza di numerose gite scolastiche e gruppi, che hanno creato qualche fastidio in termine di rumori e disturbo durante la notte,tuttavia risolto con l'utilizzo di tappi per orecchie.Stranamente, in uno dei 4 giorni del soggiorno , non abbiam oavuto nessun servizio in camera, ma per chi si sa adattare nno ha rappresentato problema alcuno. In linea di massima un buon hotel di categoria turistica che si distingue soprattutto per prezzo e vicinanza al centro e al museo di belle arti.

“Great Hotel &Location” Recently spend 4 nights at the Omni and found it to be a wonderful hotel. A bit pricy but it is new york--check for special rates-- the rooms are spacious and re-modeled and very relaxing. the baths are large for New york and are re-done in granite and all the up-to-date amenities. The lobby is small but cozy and they have a nice bar off the lobby for a quick cocktail before dinner or something late night. Food is super expensive but a nice deli across the street for snacks and bagels etc. The hotel's employees were very customer -oriented and most pleasant to deal with as was the concierge. And the location is perfect--only a few blocks to Rockerfeller center one way and central park and fifth ave shops the other. If you are looking for a nice upgradefrom a hilton /marriott type but less than a four seasons/ritz carlton then try this terrific hotel--you won't be disappointed

“Nice stay at the Hilton” Definately worth the stay if you get a good rate at the Millenium Hilton. The room was gorgeous, with huge windows on two sides of the room and stunning views. The hotel staff were helpful and friendly, and there was no street noise at all in the room.

“we will come back” Everything in the hotel was excelent The room was very big - the bed was comfortable The breakfast was rich and tasty The service was wonderful We will recomend this hotel to our friends

“So glad I got to go!” We were there during this Memorial Day weekend. I was a chaperone for our school's choir trip and they got a good deal. This is not the place I would typically stay at, as I can't afford the price. It is on absolutely gorgeous grounds! Beautiful flowers, bushes, and trees. They have a lot of family activities such as roasting smores in the evening, watching a movie on the lawn, and several others. There are 3 pools and a lazy river that was fun. One can play golf, basketball, tennis, check out bikes to ride, take a nature trail hike, play volleyball, get a massage, or play on the playground equipment. There are several pricey restaurants and we ate several meals at the small restaurant near the pools. You can take a van trip to another one of their properties about a mile away and go to their pool that had water slides. The room was nice and clean. The beds were comfortable. We enjoyed the balcony outside our room. The room did have a refrigerator. I found all the staff to be very nice and helpful. I would definitely go there again, if I could afford it.

“The rooms reminded me of a trip to a private mental hospital.” The decor of the rooms reminded me of when I was a child and visited a family friend at a psychiatric hospital- all rounded corners, nothing of true comfort in the rooms, or any real types of personality beyond over hyped purple lighting placed behind the rounded cornered tv cabinet done in white. There was absolutely no personality to the room, not even an ice bucket....lol, exactly like a mental hospital in where there is nothing left out to hurt yourself, even the bottles of shampoo/body wash are bolted to the walls and there is a white curtain hanging needlessly in the middle of the room to partition off the bathroom from the sleeping quarters that reminded me of an Emergency Room. I really did not enjoy this hotel at all, to the point that I checked out several days prior to when I originally planned on leaving the city, and checked into another hotel. They brand themselves as a higher end hotel with all of the amenities of home.... if that home is a mental hospital than they would be correct. They do not provide a mini-bar in the rooms, and the location is an odd one so going out to get a beverage or a snack in the area is sketchy and undesirable to do. There is no mini fridge provided so you cannot even keep something cool in your room, and not even an ice bucket is provided, which to me screams "cheap" and completely unconcerned about their patrons level of comfort. I travel often, I mean I am the type that is the ideal patron to want return business with, also meaning I have been to many many hotels and I have never seen one so lacking and barren before in all of my 45 years. No real shampoo or soap is provided. You must wash both your hair and body with the same items. The last I knew, they need different ingredients. There is no conditioner provided, not even in the "mission control" center (which was also annoying and I will tackle momentarily) so if you need any, you must trek out to find a store in which to purchase these items. No q tips provided, not cotton balls, absolutely nothing at all but bottles of wash that are larger bottles bolted on to the wall, which kind of skeeved me as then I also knew and thought about all the other naked people that had stood in that same shower using these same items..... yes, I know it's a hotel room, but one of the true measures of a good hotel with excellent understanding of it's patrons, is delivering a sense that no one else stayed there prior. Using the same bottles that strangers used while naked, even if in thought, was not pleasant. Oh, but they do provide you with a mini packet of Kleenex, you know the kind, that you kept in your pocket while in kindergarten. I am a grown up, staying in a place that bills itself as higher end, I want a full size tissue to use that I don't have to wrestle with to blow my nose. I wanted to jot a note down for directions to a store, so I could go buy a bottle of conditioner, and they didn't even provide a note pad to do so with. The space to store your items? There is none. Your entire time there, in this tiny room, you must stare at your suitcase, adding even more of a closed in feeling to the room. There are 2 small drawers provided under where you must place your luggage to use, which is under whe you put your luggage so you must first move your luggage if you want to access it. The beds..... how they can even refer to these as beds is beyond me. They are nothing but futons, and not even glorified ones at that. They are so hard that I would have preferred to have slept on a chair, had they provided one. The bed linens were cheap and itchy. My suggestion would be to the owners of this hotel to go sleep at the "Night" hotel for a night to see what a real bed, that is pure luxury, is about because this was nothing more than something my children may have slept on when in nap time at day care. Complimentary breakfast? While the assortment of muffins was nice, having provided hot eggs and toast would have been a nicer touch, and in honesty, probably cheaper for the hotel to provide in cost comparison. Beautiful terraces? I wouldn't know, as when I tried to go out onto one of them, I had 5, yes 5 staff members come chase me off of the terrace,telling me I was not allowed to be there. It was completely funny that it required 5 of them to come tell me this, as I am all but 5 feet 4 inches and 130 pounds, and maybe if they hadn't chased me off the only thing I was actually enjoying about the hotel, I may not have chosen to take my business elsewhere or be writing this review. The location is horrible and in a part of the city that is not convenient to other areas, it's a several block walk to Times square in an area that is rather sketchy, next to the Port Authority, read, having to deal with derelicts to go buy a bottle of conditioner that had not been provided, putting my safety into question. There is a nightlife there, that I will say is "hip" and would be my only real reason to ever return, even though it was complete chaos and not well directed. When you walk off of the elevator on the 4th floor, the mission control ( more like mission impossible) floor there is no indication on where to go and you are immediately thrust into the overflow of there events and party area, leaving for confusion on exactly where to go, once you are able to find the " mission control area" it is again filled with no real personal touches. They offer kitchy little items for sale like little miniatures of their rooms, but not much to offer in what travelers may really NEED, like conditioner, q tips, although there is a toothbrush for sale, and umbrellas, but more of what they seem concerned with is selling cheap trinkets of the hotel. My encounter with this hotel is a complete shame, as someone who truly appreciates uniqueness to a hotel, such as the architecture of this building, if I had felt like something other than a guest at a mental hospital, with it's lack of true design, and having 5 attendants come to rush me off the terrace, I might have returned with my 3 teenagers for a weekend in the city, or on one of my many other business trips into the city, I come in at least twice a month for 3-4 day stays ( can you say return money?) but I found it completely lacking in any personality. any real concern for it's guest, and a total lack of comfort. I don't even want to mention what happens when you realize that if you go down to "mission control" to find out if you can get a bottle of conditioner" if you forget your key, you can't even get back up to your hotel room on the elevator. I understand his is probably due for hotel security, but maybe try adding real staff instead of kiosks, and it would again add to the comfort of it's patrons maybe it might be a 2 star hotel. I believe half of the high markings have been done by a younger crowd with no real money or idea as to what true comfort is, which is sadly misleading to other consumers who actually understand what a good hotel remembers first, it's customers comfort, and that would start with providing amenities like ice buckets and losing things like emergency room curtains in the middle of the room to partition off the bathroom from the sleeping closet, as that's all the rooms are, a closet without any real personality.

“You could call this a Courtyard Plus” This Courtyard is a bit more than your typical Courtyard, as it has a resturant with room service, a deli, conference center, and a full bar, along with a larger pool area. It's more of an inbetween a full Marriott & a normal Courtyard, hence the Courtyard Plus I'm calling it. As mentioned in the other reviews, the rooms are very nice at this property and they keep it up amazingly well. I had to ask how old the property was, and was amazed they said 4 years old as it looked like it was a brand new & they just finished everything a few months ago. About the only drawback to this hotel is it's location. It is in a good central location, but at the same time it's not close to anything except the airport. So expect to make a bunch of 5-10 min. drives to most items. Or go park near the Old Town trolley station & ride the trolleys. That's the best way to go downtown. Two items. Jim the bar manger/bartender is a master at classic cocktails as he spent 30+ years at the Del Coronado as a bar manager and is way above what you would expect to find at a business hotel. The other is the hotel will take you on the shuttle bus to any of the resturants on the Shelter Island/Harbor Island area. Highly recommend the Bali-Hi, With the restoration, the view & the high quality food it's a great Tiki Temple, and Jimmy's Famous American Tavern is basically across from the Holiday Inn about a 1/4 mi. away is a fantasic gastropub & has a nice harbor view. Very cool decor as well and great if you want a causal dinner.

“good and bad” I've been to the Ashton Hotel on several locations, while I was attending events. I have never stayed there, nor had a reason to because I live about 30 minutes away. The wedding that I was attending was going late and I needed to be up early in the morning and be near the area so I decided to stay the night. The room rate as part of the event was very attractive so it was a win, win. It's definitely a smaller hotel and it is located in the middle of downtown, which means it is close to just about everything. The downside is it doesn't have its own parking garage so valet is a must - or you can drive around and hope for parking spot on the street or find another garage nearby. Now, finding a nearby garage isn't a horrible hassle, but I had a lot of things with me so valet was my choice that day. Well, that is -if there was a valet anywhere to be found. We had completely unloaded the car and packed the luggage cart before we found anyone. That's the thing, they are just busy there and it takes a little bit for the guys to get your car - you just have to plan ahead. On a completely positive note, I knew ahead of time about the delay and asked that my car be ready an hour and a half later and it was there, on time. I thought they might have forgotten about me and they did not. Nice tip followed, of course. The room we got was 302 and the double doors to the front of the room led us to believe it would be massive. Actually, it was quite small, but it was quite nice. The bed linens were cushy and white and overall the room was well decorated with completely soft & fuzzy carpet. The bathroom was super lovely and I especially liked the architecture, decor, and the shower. So there it is - it's a good stay and there are spurts of really wonderful service and the staff is very, very nice overall. Just be ready for a delay with the valet and you will be fine - and the room is a bit small but I only spent about 8 hours in total and most of that was sleeping. One more thing- I was very excited about having breakfast delivered to my door at a certain hour - they don't have something easy to fill out and pre-order breakfast. In fact, the menu for in room dining seemed quite dull and limited so we just opted to leave earlier that morning and get breakfast on the way.

“Noisy but good location” I stayed in this hotel for a week for business reasons and only got one really good night's sleep. The doors on the guest rooms are extremely loud when they shut and I could hear the folks around me in other rooms. Since Chinatown is so close, I understand that this is the hotel of choice after a night of clubbing. It is in a very good location and the staff was extremely attentive. The steps going down to get to the registration area was no big deal, odd ...but was told it was for safety reasons. The breakfast was delicious, Deirdre makes a great omlette. Not sure I would stay here again until they replace the doors with something more quiet.

“Classy Hampton Inn” I recently spent 4 nights at this hotel on leisure travel with my husband. At first glance I wasn't sure we were in the right place, the building facade, and lobby are pretty classy by Hampton Inn standards! The rooms themselves are basic Hampton Inn style, and are on the smaller side by comparison (but definitely still comfortable and clean). The lounge/breakfast/happy hour location is really nice, and access to the outside balcony is great. One night we bought a bottle of wine and just sat on the balcony reading and watching the traffic. The location of the hotel is ideal. We walked everywhere (dinners, tourist attractions, leisure strolls, etc.), and had no difficultly orienting ourselves and navigating the city. There are plenty of places to eat and drink within a block of the hotel if you don't feel like going further, but 6th street is a short stroll up the road. We even walked to UT, and the State Capitol. Morning breakfast was good, but basic. It was often crowded, and staff was so-so about refilling missing items. Definitely still good, but not above average for a Hampton Inn. We only took advantage of happy hour one night, and staff was friendly and the food and drinks were great. My one complaint about this hotel is the parking. The price ($23 while we were there) is steep, but I understand that's the norm in most cities. However, not having an option for self park is very annoying. Having to depend on (and tip) a valet, when I'm perfectly capable of walking into the garage and getting my car is just bothersome. The valet service was backed up and slow every time we needed the car. One evening we waited 15 minutes for our car! I'm not complaining too much about the price, but am complaining about the valet service. One tip, if you stay on a weekend, just park on the street nearby for free and better convenience (we did this the one weekend night we were in town).

“Adequate hotel close to Union Square” Hotel Rex is a smallish hotel close to Union Square. What can I say about it? - It was OK, we didn't hate it but wouldn't bother to go back. For some reason, when we checked in, we were told we had been upgraded to a better room - I've no idea why, but we didn't complain. Our room was on the third floor and at the back of the hotel so there was no road noise. The room was a reasonable size but I peeked at a normal room and they seemed a lot smaller. It was clean and well decorated in a old fashioned way, although it had the noisiest plumbing I've come across - if you like bright modern hotels this isn't the hotel for you. We appreciated the free glass of wine served in the bar between 5pm- 6pm. We didn't eat in the hotel - try Lori's diner (turn left out of the hotel entrance - 2 minutes walk) for big American breakfasts in 1950s surroundings.

“Basic place to stay” Stayed for 1 night on the 17th floor in an executive king room. Arrived late morning and was able to leave my bag was not able to check in --- ok because it was just past 10:30 which is understandable.. Lobby was small and bustling. Returned to check in around 7 pm that evening and had to wait around 15 minutes because there was only 1 person working the front desk at that time. Lobby was still active. Received my room key and retrieved my bag and headed up to the 17th floor. Room was diagonal from the elevator which turned out to be okay --- i did not hear 1 elevator all night. Walking into the room, I was slightly underwhelmed. The bathroom is immediately inside the door and is small with a small shelf and shower only. Bathroom was clean but some of the floor tiles were chipped and the towels could use some serious upgrading. The room itself is best described as efficient but there is not a lot of warmth. Everything was in good working order however the ottoman had a big rip right in the center, the dresser was nicked from too many run ins with luggage, and the thermostat is oddly placed over the desk. Actually, I could never tell whether the thermostat controlled the hvac unit or not. My room stayed the same temperature during my entire stay despite my adjusting the thermostat. I did like the big windows and could see the top of the Empire State building easily. I also liked that there was an extra chair for relaxing. Pros: location, comfortable bed, quiet on the 17th floor -- never heard anyone else on the floor even though the hotel was sold out, free internet (although it is wired-only in the rooms -- meh), and windows open slightly to let some air in. Cons: tired room, service seemed impersonal, could hear a lot of street noise even on the 17th floor, the reading lamps were too high over the bed, and just a generally cold vibe. Decision: this won't be my first choice for a repeat stay and I'm a big Starwood fan however if the price is right and I can't get into one of my preferred stays --- then this is a basic place to rest my head for 1 night.

“Like the Renovations” I stayed one overnight here on a business trip. I have stayed in other hotels in the area and, although the neighborhood isn't great, I've never had a problem walking around the area to get something to eat. I like the renovated rooms--they have nice touches like plenty of places to plug in phones and laptops. I also like the fact that there is a sofa in the room so I didn't have to sit on the bed to work or watch tv. I was a little concerned about being on the first floor with a sliding door to the parking lot, and not sure how secure the lock was, but I didn't have a problem and, although the hotel was fairly busy, my room was quiet. The outdoor sitting area looked like it would be nice but I didn't use it since it was nearly 100 degrees while I was there. I would have rated this hotel higher except for two relatively minor issues that made the stay less than ideal. First, there was no information guide in the room, so I couldn't just look up information about the facilities. Second, the man at the check-in seemed distracted and maybe a little overwhelmed/tired; while he wasn't unfriendly, neither was he particularly welcoming.

“The Grand Dame of Seattle Hotels” I had not stayed at this property since the change of management from the Four Seasons but the transition was seamless and the service is better than ever. Having been raised in Seattle, I would describe this as the town's version of The Plaza. A place to come for tea in the Atrium or an "event" meal in the Georgian Room. There are certainly newer options in town but this is old school excellence. Great place to stay during the holidays!

“Great place to stay in north LA/Hollywood area” The service at the HGI LA/Hollywood is as good as any Hilton property where I've stayed. Front desk staff were helpful and friendly and restaurant staff seemed to actually enjoy their job and it showed in the service. While the lobby is small and rooms seem a little smaller than many HGI's, given the location this is not that surprising. The pool was clean and well maintained, the hot tub was hot, the food was above average, and the hotel overall was very clean and well maintained. The $30 valet parking is pricey, and with no self-parking available is definitely a minus. The location right on a heavily trafficed street made rooms on the street side a bit noisy. These are really the only two cons from my visit. Location is great. Easy walking distance to the weirdness of Hollywood Blvd, rougly 3 blocks from Grauman's, a nice shopping/eating mall that abuts the Dolby (formerly Kodak) and the Hollywood Bowl. Less than 10 minutes to Universal Studios and convenient to Mulholland Dr for some great views of the basin to the south and San Fernando valley to the north, and 15 inutes or so to La Brea tar pits and Rodeo Dr. All in all, a great place to stay for sightseeing and entertainment.

“nichts besonderes” Hotels in San Francisco sind ziemlich teuer. Unsere Wahl fiel auf das Executive Hotel Vintage Court. Es ist kein besonderes Hotel, aber das zimmer war wenigstens für etwas über 100 Euro die Nacht zu bekommen. Das Zimmer war klein und etwas alt. Das Frühstück wurde in der Lobby eingenommen, aber es war echt nur ein Snack und es gab nicht mal richtige Tische und Stühle.

“We still love it here” I have recently returned from an extended stay at the MCV. I spend five weeks there with my son and then with the rest of my family. I had a booking in a studio for a week which was adequate for two of us but limited when it came to preparing food with only a microwave and toaster to feed a 16 year old so we ate out at the Desert Ridge Mall or used the Canyon Springs pool bar. For two weeks we had a master suite and this gave us a washing machine and full kitchen (there are washing machines for guests in studios in a laundry room which I have used in the past but did not need this year). The extra space and large fridge was much better and enabled us to relax together and separately with the living room and bedroom. The only thing I do not like about the master suites is the way the bath is not separate to the sleeping area it is open plan.It is also not a spa style bath which would be better and not out of place in a Marriott resort. There is a shower/toilet accessed through the kitchen and bedroom which is adequate. The master suite has a balcony that sits four people - this could have been cleaner tbh. For the last fortnight of my stay I had booked a two bedroomed apartment and a separate studio for my adult son and his girlfriend.We were told it would be next door and when we went to check in for that room it had been given to someone else so they were located a few apartments away - not as convenient as we had hoped. The two bed apartments have two balconies - in the older style buildings (2600) they have a lock off second bedroom but I understand that the newer buildings have two bedrooms without the lock off facility.During our stay I broke the glass jug of the smoothie maker and another was provided almost immediately at no cost.We also requested a few items that were missing from one of the rooms and these were delivered very quickly too. We had no problems with checking in the only hiccup was the fact that a room for my son was not as close as we had been told it would be. The pools are smallish but never really crowded.The basketball part of the pool is always busy but the rest is not.The larger pool is usually much cooler than the lap pool which is sometimes like a tepid bath.The hot tubs are lovely at night but very hot in the day time when temperatures ranged from 100 - 115. The check in staff were all helpful with special mentions to Scott and Robyn.The pool bar staff are all very good Mark, Matt, Jonlyn and the long serving cooks do a sterling job in very hot conditions.We ate often at the pool bar and although the menu is small my son was happy with the chicken tenders ($8) and burgers ($10) .We bought refillable beverage mugs ($15) so they proved to be an absolute bargain. We used the transport to the Mall which is better than last year and runs every two hours until 8pm (it was very much curtailed last year) and hope that next year the service will be hourly.Please Marriott. I would still recommend this resort to anyone who enjoys hot summer days and am already looking forward to returning next year.

“Newer rooms with a harbor view.” My stay at The Dana from March 24-26 was fine. I stayed in the newer Bayview rooms which have a beautiful view of the harbor. I saw the older rooms which were okay and a little dark, but still pricey. There is a Hyatt across the street (not on the bay, I don't think). The location is nice for boating and walking or jogging as it's on a jogging path which runs parallel to the water. There is a small grocery/convenience store within walking distance. The nicest surprises were the two restaurants on the property. Our dinner at the Blue Pearl was very good and the Firefly bar/restaurant was delicious (especially for lunch). The two pools looked nicely maintained. If considering a stay at the property, I would highly recommend a rental car, unless you plan to remain on the property. If the later is your plan, the shuttle to and from the airport should work fine.

“Unexpected Surprise!” Hotel Giraffe is located on an up and coming section of Park Avenue. There are plenty of great restaurants within 5 minutes walking distance from Hotel Giraffe. There is a fun energy in this section of town. There are balconies off many of the rooms - outdoor space in New York is a rarity. We utilized Hotel Tonight App on the iPhone to book a last minute hotel room at Hotel Giraffe. We got a great price at the last minute. The hotel staff at check in were very friendly. When we checked into the room, there was a bottle of Mondavi red wine, free of charge, two bottles of water free of charge as well. We had a full balcony (shared with the room next to us - but there were plants used as a divider - and we never saw our neighbors). Hotel Giraffe has a full service restaurant in-house. However, we did not frequent it to be able to review it. The Hotel offered us free continental breakfast the next morning until 11am. Overall a great boutique hotel! Strong recommendation!

“Great Priceline Deal!” Booked for $50 on Priceline for a stay on the way home from Disney. It was a great stay. The rooms were beautiful and the bed was comfy. The cookies were great. The staff was very friendly. The bath was roomy and clean. The only issue I had was since I was traveling, it's not very convenient to the interstate. Our mapquest directions weren't very good (they didn't tell us which way to turn when taking the exit) so I recommend calling ahead of time. I would stay again.

“A Great Stay!” We recently returned from a seven night stay at this property. Check-in was a breeze. We had four standard suites and one executive suite. All of our rooms were in the main building. The rooms appeared to be recently rennovated. The beds were comfortable. Good quality linens along with a nice coffee/tea maker. The concierge was very helpful in making dinner reservations. We only ate one breakfast at the Hole In The Wall. Nothing special. I'm not a huge fan of hotel dining. All of our other meals were outside of the property. There are plenty of nearby dining options. The pools looked inviting. However, with the unseasonable cold weather, swimming wasn't an option. We played tennis and basketball on well maintained courts. A great hiking area is about 1 1/2 miles from the property. The hotel provided a map. Check-out was painless. I located one minor mistake on the bill which was promptly corrected. Overall, a nice stay.

“Great location!!” Just held a 3 day sales meeting here for a group of 25. Perfect venue for this. Meeting rooms right size, staff very hospitable, very good for (forgot we were in a hotel :) ) Location is great as it is a short taxi ride from the airport and you are in the heart of Boston. 5 minute walk to many great restaurants. As a tourist, this is an ideal location.

“fun Memorial Day weekend stay in DC” The rates are great during non business days! Quite a contrast for the staff, though; as most of the clients appear to be business travelers except for weekends and holidays. The rooms are quite convenient with a refrigerator and stove top and an assortment of kitchen wares. The smoke smell is an issue though as we never did determine the cause of the smoke smell as we were located many floors above the only smoking floor in the building. The location is near the Metro and Walgreens and Dupont Circle and the associated restaurants and bars and shopping. I would stay again without hesitation but I do have an issue with the smoke smell in the bathroom. No amount of air freshener will mask the smell of smoke; and the air freshener was no more pleasant. Thank go the windows opened to air out the room. The Y across the street is great and no cost for guests!

“"Great Hotel - Quiet Location” This was a great hotel and a quiet location. All rooms either have a bay view or a harbor view so you can't go wrong. Wonderful walking path directly accross the street. Pet friendly. Town/Gaslight district is a short 5-minute drive but lots of parking so not a problem. The quietness of the location of the hotel and the great views more than make up for it's "isolation". Great staff, restaraunt and room.

“Poor experience” Stayed for business, there were many issues: 1. dirty bath, broken closet, coffee pot not cleaned, etc not remedied despite requests - the room was shabby 2. computers in business center frequently not functioning 3. as a Marriott member, was told I was upgraded to the concierge level...it has been closed however I was not informed. 4. exercise center and pool were closed

“Excellent New Years Eve Weekend” Had a great stay on the 44th floor. Room clean with good linens and towels. Staff was all outstanding. TV had too many channels to watch. Room Service was quick and items served hot. Location is perfect and security is tight. During the stay, the hotel updated and communicated all the changes that could be expected. Location is perfect. The bed was a bit softer than I prefer but clean. Would stay here again.

“Good location, reasonably priced, noisy start to day” I have stayed a number of times at this hotel, normally for one or two nights. The rooms are fairly large, with a dedicated sitting area in one large room. The staff are friendly and helpful when asked. The location is very central DC with a number of attractions nearby. Internet access is muc better than before although in my last two trips there were some issues with the wireless. It may depend on the room. The only real issue is the noise from the garbage collectors very early in the morning. They usually wake me up before dawn. Try to be as high up as you can. Plenty of good eating options nearby. The hotel does not have any food (except a snack vending machine) but there are breakfast options accross the road or a 1 minute walk. This hotel serves my purpose for a short business trip. I would not wish to stay for a longer time partly because there are no cooking facilities and partly because of the noise.

“Go only for the historic feel...otherwise, stay somewhere else” The hotel itself, like Boston, is full of historic details. The lobby is lovely, with a feeling of grandeur. The staff were fine, but not overly helpful. The queen room was small, with not much space to put suitcases, or anything else. The bathroom was decent in size, but not much room to put toiletries. The shower was older, with the showerhead loose from the wall. Although one wants the "historic" feel, it just feels old overall, making it not quite comfortable. Pros: - convenient location near the Prudential Center, and Newbury Street, Boston Public Library - 2 blocks from the Back Bay station - duvet covers...no icky bed spreads! Cons: - no free wifi - small rooms - old feeling..."historic"? (thus, not feeling completely clean) I probably will choose a different hotel with more modern amenities the next time I come to Boston

“Overall Nice, Great Location” I just recently returned from a weekend trip to Chicago with a few buddies of mine. We stayed at the Marriott Chicago/Magnificent Mile. It was a 3 day, 2 night trip: Rooms: I have done a bunch of travel in the last couple of years and have stayed at many different types of hotels/resorts and different chains. At this Marriott, I thought that the beds in the rooms were some of the most comfortable that I have ever slept on. The pillows were extremely comfortable as well as the bed itself and the light featherbed that was on it. I have been told my other people that all Marriott beds are like this, but all I know is that the beds at this Marriott were extremely comfortable. The rooms contained an ironing board, Iron, Bath and Body Works Shampoo and Conditioner, plenty of towels, with a flat screen TV, small table and chairs, and high speed internet (available for a small fee). The room itself was not extremely big but had a decent view of the city. (I heard some rooms, the view is not so good!) The carpets and bathroom was clean which is always nice. The hallways were also quiet at night which was a plus. Lobby: We stayed at this Marriott over the weekend and the lobby and lobby bar were extremely busy. The lobby is an open space with lots of tables and couches for you to sit on, relax, and have a cocktail before heading out to the city for the night. The prices were reasonable for service at the bar. It was a very nice lobby experience. Also in the lobby was the bell desk, front desk, and the concierge which was very helpful in finding nearby restaurants and bars. Location: This hotel I believe is in a great location. It is right on Michigan Avenue in the heart of the “loop.” (I hope that is what the immediate downtown is called.) It is very close to “ Rush St. ” and all of the hotspots of downtown. There is great shopping close as well as many great restaurants within walking distance. At the hotel, we valet parked our car with the hotel and never once removed it from the garage as we could walk anywhere we wanted to go or just take a short cab ride. Service: Check in was extremely quick. All we needed to do was give our last name and our reservation was pulled up. The staff was quick to have our bags brought upstairs and tell us where all of the amenities of the hotel were such as gift/sundry shop, pool, coffee bar, lobby bar etc.. The concierge located in the lobby was very helpful with making reservations and providing lists of nearby restaurants broken down by type of food and location. Finally, the valet and bellmen at the front entrance were very quick to hail us a cab, or to help us go in any direction that we needed. Pool: There is a pool located on the 9th floor (I think) but we did see or go in it. Overall, Our stay at the Marriott was great and provided a great “home base” to go and do whatever we wanted to do that night in Chicago . I would recommend this hotel to friends and family and would stay there again if I was to once again, visit the Windy City .
“Really pretty good” Good location. Trendy bar on the top floor and very accommodating staff. Door men are very friendly. Stayed here 5 times in the past year Check it out

“Not as impressive as I'd expected” After reading about this hotel online (was here as part of a meeting) I was prepped to expect something more. The meeting rooms, to be sure, are impressive. Room, however, was tiny. Bathroom was so small I could barely get in and out - even in the smallest of NYC hotel rooms I have never had such a small bathroom. They also kept putting the bath mat in the way so that you could not get the door open easily. It got to be a pain. Amenities were not replenished. Upon check-in I told the girl at the desk that I would not be staying four nights, only three. She seemed to adjust it. I was forced to actually check out in the middle of the third night due to flight changes because of the approaching hurricane. The staff was gracious in getting me a cab (all duly noted, it turned out, in my file) but I was then charged (I found out with my credit statement a week later) for the fourth night, evidently due to some confusion about my "early departure" on Night Three. They are being kind about rectifying this, but no one can figure out why it happened. Note to all: they really are on the prowl for those not following orders, One of the trustees of our group wasn't allowed in a restaurant during the week because she was wearing jeans, and I, who own a fourteen-buck Tracfone I only use in emergencies, was sitting in a far corner of the Wigwam restaurant at breakfast speaking quietly with a friend about the upcoming storm and what I needed to do when I was handed a card "requesting" me to get off the cell phone. Wow! Me? Me who doesn't even know the cell number because I use it so infrequently?! So beware: when they say the staff is prepped to make you follow the rules (I wasn't even aware that was a rule) they are, Room service food was actually not very good..at least the burger. Soup was okay. Room service guy was vey nice and the nicest and most professional employee I met there.

“Austintatious” This is a great location to watch the bats flying out of the congress Ave bridge. The hotel is a little aged but our king room was quite large and had a view of the lake. we were within walking distance of a free festival that had live music as well as many great restaurants and bars.

“Great hotel, noisy during convention” We won this hotel for $75 on Priceline for the Thanksgiving weekend. The hotel feels very new and is nicely appointed. Great location about a block from 6th St. and next to the convention center. Bed is outrageously comfortable. Unfortunately on the 2nd and 3rd nights there was a large convention that checked in and trying to go to sleep felt like I was caught in Spring Break. I called Security 3x but it really never calmed down. The Front Desk Manager was able to comp my $15/day parking for compensation due to it being a Priceline reservation.

“I recommend this hotel” I was very happy with this hotel. The room was huge, the lighting was very nice, the bathroom was fully equipped including a jetted tub. I ate lunch and then breakfast at the restaurant in the hotel and the food was amazing. I am a picky traveler and this met all of my expectations.

“Extremely average hotel” Stayed for a one night getaway and booked via Priceline for $56 - it's classified as a 3.5* hotel in downtown Philadelphia. Check-in was somewhat of a disaster - girl who checked us in barely said a word to us and put us in room 1633 - 2 double beds. Got into the room fine, but went back out for a couple of hours and came back and our keys didn't work. Went back and they said we never checked-in! After some convincing, the front desk (re) checked-us in to the room we were in and gave us breakfast coupons to make us for our issue. Rooms are just OK. Clean, but beds are not that comfortable, they still have tube TV's and the ac/heat unit is very loud and goes on and off intermittently. Bathroom is typical hotel bathroom with Bliss amenities. No mini-fridge provided, although there is a spacious work desk for the business traveller. We had a drink in the hotel lobby that night - $6 for an Amstel, $10.50 for a Bailey's on the rocks. Lobby bar is nice enough. We had breakfast the next morning at their Terrace restaurant with our coupons for the buffet. Fine and typical hotel breakfast buffet. It's apparently normally $15/pp. There is an indoor swimming pool on the 3rd floor which we did not utilize. Location is decent. We walked straight down 17th Street to the Rittenhouse Square area for dinner and drinks that evening - about a 10 minute walk. The elevators are really, really slow... It's not a bad place, nor is it great. For $56, it is worth it. Although that ac unit kept me up the entire night, so if I had a choice, I don't think I'd stay here again.

“Lower expectations” The Silver Cloud Inn- Lake Union is very nice and a surprizingly good location. Its very close to downtown without as much hustle and all the added expense. I had a very nice "view" room that I paid extra for. I was quite disappointed in the view. It was the same as the View lounge around the corner. You could only see a little lake between the buildings on the other side of the street. I'd stay there again but not pay extra or expect a view.

“Great location and great staff!” Got to stay here for the Marketing conference in October with the girlfriend and I have to say this hotel was great! The location is ideal because it's walking distance to Union Square, and about half an hour walk to Pier 39 at Fisherman's Wharf. Transportation wise, all the major buses and Cable Car is right in front of the hotel, what more can you ask for! I liked the fact that they had WiFi in the hotel room as well as cable, so you're not restricted by the length of the internet cable when you want to sit anywhere else other than the office table. The only gripe I had with the hotel was it was really hard to get a Taxi. It's actually easier to get a taxi if you walk away from the Hotel because a lot of times the taxi will get caught before it even makes it into the hotel entrance!

“The "W" Stands for Worst in San Francisco” Where to begin? Maybe I should tell you that the W hotel San Francisco used to be one of my favorite hotels in the city. The rooms were stylish, sexy, comfortable and the public areas were lively, clean and attractive. Not anymore. It’s a design disaster! The second thing you should know is that the hotel is undergoing major renovation – major. A fact that we were never informed of at any part of our reservation process. There is no lobby and the makeshift check in area is truly deplorable. There are work lights, tarps, paint and pathetic “oops” signs everywhere – letting you know that acknowledged that problem. Maybe they could tell you about the problem before you book the hotel. If the lobby wasn’t enough reason not to stay here – the remodeled guest rooms definitely are. The rooms are now a disaster of crappy furniture, white walls, tan carpet and broken plastic Buddha’s. As a designer myself, I have fallen in love with many W Hotels’ designs in the past—I understand and appreciate good design. This is not good design. The room looks like someone made a last minute dash to a Japanese version of IKEA and slapped crap on the walls, put together cheap furniture and left before it was finished. The room décor is a disaster. It is also pathetic to see remnants of the old décor still pathetically left behind: a dark wood headboard, a sink, a mirror, drapery tracks on the ceiling without drapes. None of it works. It’s hard to choose the worst element in the room. The freeform mirror glued onto the old headboard? The plastic Japanese “art” pathetically installed on the wall? Or maybe the random lamp balancing on the edge of the desk that obviously didn’t fit into its nook? The new disastrous design also makes its way into the W restaurant Trace. Before I tell you about the restaurant, let me say the staff at the restaurant was excellent and the cuisine was very good. The restaurant is also a design disaster. If the challenge was to take a great space and break it into 17 cramped and uncomfortable areas—mission accomplished! The cheap looking décor looks like it came from the same Japanese IKEA and someone has the novel idea of making black wood cages in which to place the tables. Even the waiters complain about navigating the maze of cramped tables and black wood crates. There is also a “dot” pattern on the wall and windows, a theme that permeates the new areas, and it is annoying, tedious and already dated. Whew! In short, I would never stay here again and I felt truly ripped off. Something I usually have not felt at any other W hotel before.

“Großes Zimmer, gut gelegen” Das Hotel liegt 15 Minuten von der Stadt entfernt und 10 Minuten vom Strand entfernt - mit dem Auto. Drumherum sind einige FastFood-Ketten und Shops. Das Zimmer war sauber und sehr groß. Einrichtung wie man es von einem typischen amerikanischen Ketten-Hotel erwartet. Das Continental Breakfast war auch etwas umfangreicher als woanders. Also alles in allem ein guter Aufenthalt.

“Not easy to find” This hotel was very hard to find from 95. it was 9pm, dark, and Salisbury road seems to start and stop inexplicably!. Hotel was a bit of a disappointment. Desk clerk very nice and helpful. The extra pillows I had requested when making the reservation were not delivered. As previous reviewers have stated, hotel is dated and in need of an overhaul. The corridors have a stale odor, and are not properly air conditioned. The room was somewhat shabby and TOTALLY lacking in plugs/outlets. The only plugs we could find were one behind the bed, and one under/behind the desk. Each plug was used by a lamp or clock. Bring a power strip!..So, charging a phone or using a computer was a challenge without ample electrical outlets in the room. There is an outlet in the bathroom, but I hesitate to put a phone or computer near the sink/water. The smoke detector was loose and hanging from the wall precariously; the bathroom door was scratched, missing paint and desperately needed painting. Bed has a sheet and a comforter that was WAY too big, and therefore heavy and cumbersome, and rather hot. Breakfast was fresh and good. This is a stopover hotel when traveling, period.

“Wow! Will exceed your expectations!” This Omni has been the best business hotel that I have been in all year! wow! Brand new; great design, architecture, artwork, public space. The room was incredible - beautiful bathrooms, colors, fabrics and if you have a room that faces the Reunion tower flashing at night, what a show! The food served at the conference I was attending was also top notch. This is one hotel that I was very sad when it came time to check out. Check in and enjoy! Also easy walking to all downtown attractions. My only negative is the limited amount of free wifi, only available in the lobby and not the strongest signal.

“Outstanding hotel on every level” I've stayed here before and once again found this to be an outstanding hotel. The hotel itself is beautiful and the rooms are laid out nicely. The staff, from the shuttle drivers to the front desk, to housekeeping are friendly and go out of their way to help. It's quiet. It's spotless. It's an inviting place to stay.

“Night & Day” That was the difference between the 2 rooms I had at Parc 55. As others have said, this is a wonderfully-located hotel, close to great shopping, food & the Powell St. Cable Car stop as well as the BART and Muni station. The first night I was given a room which was on a lower floor in this odd little cul-de-sac, I say odd because there was a large pole in the middle of it, making it impossible to see if anyone was behind there. It was kind of nerve-wracking as a solo female traveler. The room itself was gorgeous - it was an updated king and the beautifully appointed, the view was nothing to look at. The bathroom was oddly configured with a lot of wasted space - the towel rack was over the toilet, at least 6 or 7 feet from the tub and no hook near the tub on which to leave your towel. Huge, flat screen HD tv, not many options in terms of channel selection (I know, they want you to pay for the extras) The room was above a busy street and it was unbelievably noisy - I stayed on Bourbon St. during LSU football season and had quieter nights - someone was loading case after case of glass bottles onto a truck at midnight, bar revelers at 2; dumpster trucks at 5 - and did I mention that people were yelling in the hall in between? I called the front desk and asked to be moved for the second night. They could not have been more gracious or accomodating. I was given a room on a top floor and was able to move up early on Sat. morning. The room and bath were not updated, but the view of San Francisco bay and the blissful quiet was more than worth it. Staff throughout were warm and helpful. If you go, make sure to ask for a quiet room!

“Best kept secret (3rd time staying; still a charm!)” It may not be a 5-star, but you can't beat it. Third time we've stayed and they've increased in our esteem again! This BW caters to the business crowd, but we've always stayed for leisure (usually on a weekend). For the rate, it's perfect. Clean, "green", and if you request & it's available: a drop-dead view of the Space Needle practically across the street. (Ask again at check-in to make sure.) A mere walk to Belltown (about 5 short blocks) where too many choices of restaurants, wine (and spirits) bars, younger folks clubs (live music, pubs, etc), jazz clubs --if weather permits, a nice hoof over to even Pike's! You don't get the usual BW complimentary continental breakfast buffet, but b/c rates are lower we splurge on breakfast via room service. Parking's free in lower locked parking, which has cameras so we felt cool leaving our many shopping finds from this great shopping city discretely tucked away in back of our SUV. Check them out, for the money they're not long for best kept secret status too much longer. Kudos to the staff and management of this property; well done!

“Recommended .. clean & in great location” Really impressed with the New Yorker. Beautiful lobby (complete with piano player!) gave a great first impression. Our room was clean, comfortable and we could control the heat ourselves (pity we couldn't control our gross neighbour, who's every spit-up we could hear .. and there were *a lot*!!). Other than that, it was pretty quiet and we got decent sleep. Water was hot and the tub took seconds to fill! Just what you need after a long day shopping! Staff were friendly and polite, bed was comfortable, ample storage space. No view from window, but that was no problem. Very convenient location. Subway right outside, Macys just steps away. Business Centre and Fitness Centre (& restrooms) can only be accessed with your room key card, which is also needed to pass security on the elevators. We thought this was a great idea. Would definately stay here again.

“Nice stay in Washington DC” Very convenient location near Dupont Circle with lots of restaurants nearby. Paid using points from previous stays at Marriott, so I am not sure about the cost. Staff were nice and the breakfast was good with lots of choices and value for the money. (It wasn't included with the room.) My only complaint was that the hotel restaurant was not open for lunch on Saturday, and we were hoping to grab a quick lunch before heading out. However, it all worked out well as we had a nice lunch nearby at the Mayflower Hotel and enjoyed the experience there. The restaurant at the Courtyard is open M-F and served brunch on Sun. The room was fine, but not all that large. The TV was a fairly large flat screen model and very nice. The beds were very comfortable, and the room was spotless.

“Amazing deal for an awesome hotel!” I recently stayed at the St. Gregory over the Christmas 2011 holiday weekend. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. I also found the hotel to be extremely clean. Something that is not to be taken for granted even in very nice hotels today. I loved the two doormen that opened both doors everytime I entered and exited the hotel. I also enjoyed my meal at the 'M' Street Lounge. I had a suite with a living room, full kitchen, large bathroom and separate bedroom. The mattress was very comfortable and there was lots of closet space. I had a flatscreen tv ad mini stereo system in the living room with a cd/cassette player. Plus, there was another tv in the bedroom with an ipod radio docking station. Cool! It seems they thought of everything. There were even dishes in the kitchen and housekeeping would put them in the dishwasher for me everyday. (I made sure to tip housekeeping because they did an outstanding job!). I liked this hotel and look forward to trying out the Beacon Hotel which is their more contemporary sister.The only thing I didn't enjoy during my entire stay was the obnoxious faux 'Marilyn Monroe' statue that greets you at the front door. :o(

“A Good Choice for Business or Family” Enjoyed a large room with a great view. Microwave oven, refrigerator and balcony with chair. Downside was parking at $27 per night. Even across the street was parking for $20 per night but no in and out privileges. It has a great lobby and excellent food in the morning. This was a good value.
“tiny room, far from town” The hotel is located far away from the city center. The room was very small, with only one chair because there would not be space for two.

“The Best for a Girls Spa Getaway” 4 ladies in our mid thirties booked this for a spa getaway and we had the best time. The room was fabulous and the private spa area pool was the best - uncrowded and so relaxing. We booked a suite that was 2 rooms (with seperate entrances) adjoining a suite living area in the middle. We had sleeping for 8 even though we only had 4. There was an extra bed that folds out in the suite area. The suite area also had a full bath, so we had 3 bathrooms total. Full dining table and living area plus a kitchenette. We booked the spa package where the room rate each day includes a spa treatment and access to the spa area for the whole day. This is an area away from the main pool areas, no kids, complete relaxation. The spa treatments are top notch and the smoothies served at the pool are so yummy. We stayed 3 nights and only went to the main pool area one day. The main pool area is nice too, but just not as tranquil and relaxing. The hotel is away from everything so you will need a car if you want to venture out. Overall I love this Hotel and would go back tomorrow!

“How to get a decent sized room at this great hotel” The Hudson is an amusing, trendy hotel in a GREAT location with a friendly, efficient staff that suffers from having many miniscule rooms. To ensure a decent sized room just ask for one with two beds. The price is very little more and the rooms big enough to fit two beds are often wonderful with corner windows and plenty of room. Info from a visit of 4 days, Feb.10-14, 2005

“Great location.” We just visited the Millennium and the location was great. I wanted to join Good Morning America's street audience which was just across from the hotel. There is a decent deli as well and two Starbucks. (Word of warning: across the on 44th Osteria La Doge presents well with good service but food was not good) We did stay on a higher floor which helped with street noise. It is basically a convention, tourist hotel but our room was very large for NY standards. We stayed in a superior king room which was very clean but our air conditioner struggled a little to keep up with the high temps. Bed and pillows somewhat hard but not uncomfortable. So if you are looking for size, location and a clean place to lay your head, this is not a bad choice.

“Dirty carpet” The room is fine for the price, everything functioned but the carpet is dirty. I don't know why they can't put in laminate flooring as the new Motel 6s have done, at least they can be wiped when something's spilt. The room was clean enough and well provided for. Lovely pool which we enjoyed and the breakfast was OK.

“Loved this place” This is a small, quaint hotel in a busy area. It's updated, clean and safe. The parking is relatively inexpensive for Chicago ($18) and the garage is right next door. We had a junior suite that worked really well for the three of us who were traveling together. There's a free breakfast and free wifi. We stayed two nights and found it to be convenient for what we wanted to do. The breakfast was very adequate. It was like a little oasis in the city. I would definitely stay here again.

“Bathroom Bloopers” We stayed at the Hotel Vitale on an overnight layover, and having been to San Francisco numerous times, we like to try different hotels and picked Hotel Vitale. The staff are 20-30 somethings; overall, they very friendly, professional, and accomodating. We stayed in suite that had a view of the Bay Bridge. The room is decorated in modern minimalism, but with touches of warmth, like the cozy bed with big duvet. The bed was a bit on the soft side, but we did have a restful sleep. Extra pillows and a blanket were neatly packaged in a canvas bag, sitting on the floor. A bit odd, considering there is a huge empty shelf in the closet. Overall, the hotel promotes relaxation and serenity, and we liked the new age music and white noise cd's that were stacked beside the cd player. The room service was prompt and the food was hot, well prepared, and our meals were awesome. The choc. chip cookies and milk dessert really hit the spot. I registered for the room, and my husband has a different surname than I. He was met with extreme suspicion when he ordered for us, as the person taking our order kept questioning our differing surnames. That is perhaps why we were made to pay for our food on arrival to the room; it being late at night, we decided not to pursue the issue. We just felt badly for the room service person, who was forced to make two trips: to deliver food then to run downstairs to process our credit card payment. Something to take note of if you are travelling with someone with a different surname. Ah, now to the bathroom. The bathroom has an amazing glassed-in rainfall shower, and a handy cut-out is in the glass wall to reach in and run the shower before you get in. However, I am 5'2", and found my arm did not reach the water faucets. Therefore, my husband had to run the shower for me. A minor thing, but not very convenient if I was by myself. Also, a major thing we did not appreciate was the sliding door of the bathroom which sits about an inch above the door opening. You better be travelling with an extremely good friend or your spouse as .... every little sound carries into the room if you know what I mean. And, some things should just remain private between two people. Overall, we had a nice stay at Hotel Vitale, but would not return as the bathroom door was the deal breaker for us. If you don't care about that, the hotel is in a great location and the staff are wonderful, plus the best-tasting room service we've had yet.

“Chicago Conrad-Everything as expected” I stayed here with my son on the weekend of May 16th. Check-in was quick and very pleasant.My room was on the 6th floor,cityview. Both of our rooms were identical. The entryway to the room was spacious. The room had a large (50"?)flatscreen TV, desk with comfortable leather chair, easy chair with ottoman and a dresser with 3 drawers for storage. For the life of me, I cannot understand why this hotel does not have wifi, just old fashioned wire hookup.There was a good sized closet equipped with a large Conrad shopping bag to carry home your souvenirs. The closet was also eqipped with slippers, cloth laundry bags and an umbrella for use during inclement weather. Because of the hotels proximity to a firehouse, the area can be loud at times I never did hear anything from other rooms or hallways the 2 nights I stayed and there was a convention in town, so I was quite impressed with the quietness. The bathroom was "Kohler" branded with luxurious marble countertops and floors, a tub, and glass enclosed shower. Toiletries were Italian, but also included Q-tips, flossing sticks, mouthwash and a toothbrush with a very small tube of Colgate toothpaste included. The toilet was seperated by a door from the bathroom. The towels were very thin and worn as mentioned by others. The hotel had a bar with around 12 barstools and tables and easy chairs to accomodate another 28-30 patrons. There were more tables and easy chairs in the area surrounding the lounge entrance. The bartender and his assistant were very good at their jobs and pleasant to boot. I only used the restaurant for breakfast. I was given vouchers for a free Continental breakfast. The vouchers were worth $14.00 and could be used as credit for any item on the menu. I opted for the American breakfast which consisted of eggs, potatoes, a meat item, toast, juice and coffee or tea. The price was $19.00. The portions were on the small side and I would have definitely opted for another restaurant if I didn't have the vouchers. Onlike some other comments about the staff, I was very happy with the service I received from my waiter and waitress. The hotel itself is in a great area for shopping, and a 20 minute walk to the waterfront. It is also a 5 minute walk to the C.T.A. Redline, which is great for traveling to the friendly confines of Wrigley Field or connecting to other train lines. My ride coming into the city from ORD on Friday evening was about a 35 minute ride and $45.00 +tip. On Sunday morning, the ride took about 25 minutes and cost me $36.00 + tip. Having Diamond status in the Hilton Honors program, the only thing I was slightly disappointed about was the lack of an executive lounge. But I knew this going in. Overall, the hotel was everything I expected. Because of the lack of an executive lounge, I will probably try the Drake Hotel the next time I am in Chicago.

“Excellent Location” We stayed here for 2 nights as we were traveling around a few places in California and wanted to go to a Lakers game. The hotel is across the road from the Staples Center which was very handy and is a good base to discover downtown LA by foot. The hotel has a small pool which wasn't well heated for swimming in November. There is a business room with internet access and priner for free which came in handy. The rooms and hallways are nicely decorated and are kept clean. We were on the top floor at the end of the hallway near the fire eascpe. This is not the best place to be as you can hear people on mobile phones in teh fire escape as the walls are not all that thick. Other than that this hotel is in the best location if you want to see downtown or see a Lakers game and was a great deal for us as we used Prioity Club points, the room rates online seemed good at the weekedn which is when we visited. The subway stops close by if you are coming from Union Station or Hollywood.

“Good location. Nice hotel. Comfortable beds” We received a phenomenal rate on Priceline for this hotel listed as a 4-star in Midtown East. The location is great. It's actually right around the corner from the Waldorf Astoria. Shopping, Grand Central Station, restaurants and attractions are all within very close walking distance. Our room was on the 3rd floor overlooking 38th (?). Based on other reviews and the fact that it was Christmas week, I fully expected to have street noise. We had none. I also expected the common areas and room to need updating since the hotel is a little older. Surprisingly, most areas seemed to be fairly updated with new carpet, etc. I was pleasantly surprised. It was in better shaped than the Omni Shoreham we stayed at in Washington DC. The room was very quiet and the bed was quite comfortable. Good size room by NY city standards.
