Plenty of room to stretch out. We even had a little reading chair tucked in the corner. The work space had a lot of outlets for cell phone, camera and PC chargers. The alarm clock has an iPod docking station which was a nice touch! The bathroom was a bit small but in my experience all the bathrooms in NY are quite small. Someone had removed the hairdryer but I called down and the front desk brought one up immediately. The check -in lines were very long in the late afternoon. Since we checked in around 1pm, we had about 4 people in front of us. Everyone took an inordinate amount of time to check-in. We, however, had our keys in less than 3 minutes. The restaurant is overpriced for what you get. We had some after theater snacks (they close at 11:30pm) and were not impressed. We found out later that a 24 hour diner was right around the corner on Lex. New York is, after all, the city that never sleeps. In summary, good things: - Good location - Attentive front desk service - Nice size room - Comfortable bed - iPod docking station - Lots of desk outlets for camera, PC and phone chargers Things that could use improvement: - Check In process - Restaurant - Bigger bathroom All in all a good stay at the Barclay. Nothing exceptional to RAVE about but it was nice. I would stay again at a good rate.

“great stay” just returned from a great stay at the affinia manhatton, great location , right opposite penn station and madison square gardens concert venue, so transport throughout the city is fab, check in was quick, very friendly and we were given what we asked for, if you want a view of the city expect noise, take earplugs because it would be a shame to ask for a quiet room as you will be put at the back, nothing nicer than sitting in a chair last thing at night and looking out over the NY scene, wonderfull,, ask for a high floor, corner refurbished room, then you will have a duel oulook over 2 sides , the room was spacious and newly decorated, the bathroom unfortunatley was not, but useable, for a short stay, a beaufull 1930's building, was very happy with our stay, would recommend and would stay there again

“another night in DC” This is very run of the mill hotel, i have stayed many times due to convenience/location only. walk or a quick ride to most anything you want to do in DC. The staff is very friendly and bartender Barry is top notch and the burgers are pretty great.If you can help it at all do NOT drive here, the parking is a complete rip off and that is they even have room for you. The rooms are a little tired, there does not seem to be any difference in rooms, regardless of what so called upgrade you get. housekeeping staff seems to be in low gear. If you have a late check out they keep tapping on your door like a woodpecker, obviously they do not know what the do not disturb sign says.there is no attention to detail in housekeeping at all here, even the hallways, woodwork and elevators are dirty. so choose wisely when booking a hotel in this area, this may be best bang for the buck if you can tolerate some housekeeping issues.

“A great hotel” Stayed here for the second time on business, having previously visited with my family. I was delighted to find I once again had a huge room with a great view; the front desk staff couldn't have been more helpful and room service was able to deliver me a sandwich at 10pm. Highly recommended

“Nice place to stay” My wife and I stayed here for a major conference held downtown. The property is well-maintained and the staff was most courteous. There are many restaurants nearby, and you can catch the Trolley about a 15 minute walk away to ride downtown. If you have a car, I-8 is right out front and you can easily find your way around.

“Great value for the money” Stayed two nights at TRYP Hotel near Madison Square Garden in NYC with an excellent king bed in an accessible room. My honey recently had surgery and the only rooms with bathtubs and a shower are the accessible room. Our room 1109 was on 35th Street with a view of the neighborhood and had no street noise The hotel is within a block of the subway that will safely take you to most New York City and vicinity locations. The hotel is in a renovated high rise and was tastefully done. Our room was 268 square feet which is generous for the advanced purchase rate of $259 + tax per night. Overall I consider this rate a bargain for NYC standards. Free Wifi is included in the rate which makes the cost per night even better. If you are looking for a clean, well maintained, properly located NYC hotel, with friendly staff, without the numerous frills of a five star hotel, the TRYP is a superior value. The family rooms seems like and especially good value because of the capacity of the room.

“Had a good stay, would stay again” Gave it three stars for the great service, rooms were adequate - has a coffee machine, good tv channels, clean, good sized rooms. The only problem was a good 10 mins walk to restaurants. The restaurants in the lobby is no good. Noise from other rooms is quite loud. I would recommend this hotel.

“Great place, loved the location.” My husband and I stayed at the Farmer's Daugher for 3 nights, April 17-19, 2006. I always read Trip Advisor's reviews before staying anywhere. The reviews that are posted here are usually right on. This is a motel that has been tranformed into a very pleasant, themed boutique place to stay. We stayed in the "no tell room". We loved the decor, the copper lampshades, the amazing copper table and bar, the no carpet floors, the comfortable bed and shower. Our room was a good size and for being on such a busy street it was very quiet! We had the a/c running all night, so if there was any noise, that may have blocked it out. We walked to the farmer's market across the street, where you can find any kind of food for a very reasonable price. We took the advice of one of the reviewers and had brunch at the crepe place. My huge crepe of ham, mushrooms and cheese sauce was delicious and served with a green salad. They also serve sweet crepes with fresh fruit and toppings. One night we had dinner at the outdoor French restaurant, near the gourmet market, at the rear of the farmer's market. They serve 40 wines by the glass. Excellent food and wine! You can sample food from all over the world here, and the prices are amazing. Next door to the farmer's market is the Grove shopping mall, where which has upscale shops, restaurants, movie theatres, and dancing fountains similar to the Bellagio in Vegas. One day we went to the La Brea Tar Pits. Don't miss it! The LA County Museum of Art and the Peterson Auto Museum are also a couple of blocks away. Our reservations for the Farmer's Daughter were made online via the hotel web site. If you stay 3 nights the 3rd night is discounted. We found this to be a better price than the web daily price. The hotel has a restaurant that looks nice, but with the farmer's market across the street, we didn't try it. If you drive, you must use the valet parking for $12 per day plus tax, which makes it over $13 per day, plus tip to the valet. Add that into your price per room. If you want to use your laptop, the price for that is around $10 per 24 hours plus tax. This service isn't provided by the hotel, but by the cable company. With the extra add on of parking and internet fees, we still found this to be a reasonable hotel, with charm, and a friendly, helpful staff. The out door lobby area is beautiful, a pair of parakeets are residents of the hotel. I found myself sitting outdoors in the sun, off the lobby area, using my cell phone to call friends and tell them The Farmer's Daughter was a great little hotel!

“Great oasis in midtown” This was the second time I've stayed at the Royalton - for a week on business. My room was upgraded to the top floor because I was a returning guest; and there was a bowl of fruit and welcome note in the room too. The hotel ground floor is a pretty smart bar. Very different from your average hotel. The room was spacious with an in-room iPad a great touch. There an ok fitness room open 24/7 too, which is great for the early rising jet-lagged Brits! My only critisism was hat you could hear the lift bells from inside my room, but that wasn't too much of a problem. I'll definitely be staying at the Royalton for my next business trip.

“It's your standard Marriott - decent” This review is based on a five-night stay in March 2008 by a business traveller who frequents Marriott-branded and Hilton-branded hotel properties. Overall: the hotel is okay for what you're paying; it meets the standard full Marriott level of expectation for cleanliness and service. It is clearly an older hotel that was renovated relatively recently. Pros: + soft beds. + full Marriott standard of cleanliness and quality. + close proximity (walking distance) to every hospital in the medical district. Cons: - the sewage smell right outside the hotel. - the construction / renovations everywhere on the ground floor. - the lack of a front entrance (because of the above). - the small bathroom (just enough room to get in, close the door, and then sit on the toilet or step into the shower.)

“Dark, trendy, modern” I am on day 6 of a 7 day stay here at the W City Center. My first impression of the lobby and elevator was that this hotel would be perfect in Gotham City (my sons love Batman, I do not). Ironically, this hotel is not really one where you would stay with children. I find W hotels hit or miss. This one is a hit. The staff is typical friendly, the rooms are crazy clean. There are minimal things wrong with the room (missing door latch, partial flushing commode). My favorite feature at this location is their agreement they have with Acura providing a free drop off service. Also, it's location is closer to the convention center and financial buildings than the W Lakeshore. W Lakeshore is a great location if you are planning to shop in Michigan. Cool things about this W: - Free coffee in the bar on your way out - free drop off car service - Bliss bath products - cool under lighting under the beds - no bedspreads on the beds - multiple bars - spaceous room

“It was okay, a few problems the first night...” We were visiting San Antonio for a surprise birthday trip for my sister n law. We chose to stay at the La Mansion Del Rio because we got a good rate online. I had seen the property before and had always wanted to stay there. The location is great, directly on the river walk so we were very excited about that. Upon check in we were advised that there is a $50.00 a day charge for incidentals which we were not aware of prior to arriving. I know most hotels keep a card on file for things like this, however here at the La Mansion, you are billed automatically and refunded 7-10 days after you check out. This was not a problem for me, I was just surprised so I wanted to make others aware. We were given our room keys, we were in room 150 across from the main lobby in the other building. Now this room is directly behind the double door entrance and directly across from the elevator so we heard people coming and going all night long. The room was a nice size with two double beds and a flat screen tv. We noticed when we first went in the room was not cooling properly, we decided to turn the ac down lower while we went to dinner hoping it would cool off by the time we got back. We were gone for a few hours, when we returned the room was still hot and muggy. We noticed this in all of the hallways of the hotel as well. We decided to call it a night as we arrived late and were very exhausted. My husband did not sleep due to the heat and noise coming from the hallway all night. We contacted the front desk early the next morning to make them aware of the issues we were having with the room. At that point we were told that they would let the manager know to contact us as soon as he was out of a meeting. In the meantime they did send up a maintenance worker to check the ac in the room. Come to find out the filter needed to be changed, which he promptly did. We noticed a difference right away, but we were still not happy with the noise so we requested a new room. Taneeka, one of the front desk clerks advised they she would move us to a new room as soon as one was available because they were completely booked the night before they didn't have any rooms available right away. We were fine with that since we were leaving to get lunch anyway. Around 3:00 we were contacted by Taneeka again to let us know that our new room was ready. Tankeeka also offered to have a member of the staff move our things from the old room to the new one since we were out. She also gave us two complementary tickets the breakfast buffet for all of the inconvenience. I have to say that Tankeeka along with all the other front desk representatives were amazing to work with and went above and beyond trying to make our stay more comfortable. We really did appreciate that. Our second room was 405 with a pool view; it was clean, cool and quiet. We were very happy with this room and were able to enjoy our last night in San Antonio. Thanks again to staff for everything!!

“Always reliable; will stay again” Stayed twice at Double Tree Houston Downtown in 2010 for its close proximity to Allen Center where I was having meetings. Grand lobby and well appointed room - a bit more luxurious than the average Double Trees you would have expected. Efficient valet parking. Will stay there again.

“Great location but not much more” Stayed for a night with family to do some shopping and see a musical. The location is great! A stones throw to Macy's and the train station. Easy walk to Times Square and the Theaters. Rooms are very small and elevators a bit slow and small. It's really the location that sells this property. Nice view of the Empire State Building from our room as well.

“Zentral gelegen” Das Hotel liegt zentral. Die Market Street und die Sehenswürdigkeiten sind in Fußnähe. Die Zimmer sind sauber und geräumig. Das Internet auf den Zimmern ist gebührenpflichtig, allerdings ist das Business Center in der Lobby gratis. Vorsicht: das Parken ist sehr teuer (38$/Nacht) selbst zum Ausladen für eine Stunde mussten wir schon 12$ bezahlen. Direkt auf der anderen Straßenseite ist eine Parkgarage, die über Nacht und am Wochenende 5$ kostet.

“A glorious holiday weekend at The Brown Palace!” I have lived in Colorado for 20 years, but never stayed at the Brown. What was I waiting for??!! My husband and I booked a "Luxurious Love" package for the weekend. The price included 2 evening cocktails each night of our stay, complimentary valet, and breakfast at Ellyngtons or room service, plus rose petal turn down. We loved every minute of our weekend. From our check-in on friday night, the front desk clerk (Kyle) was very friendly and helpful and made us feel very welcome. We had selected a Top of the Brown king room, and the room was enormous - # 916. Huge, with a sitting area, desk, king bed, etc, we loved it. THe room was actually in one of the corners of the hotel, so that may have been why it was so spacious. The bathroom was bigger than my bedroom at home! We each had a cocktail in the atrium lobby that evening, and seating was at a premium as afternoon tea guests were lingering after 5pm. The waitress was extremely pleasant, and we loved sitting there listening to the live jazz combo playing in the lobby. Fun. Because we wanted to go to the Parade of Lights at 8pm, we had made dinner reservations for 6pm in the Ships Tavern. Good thing we had, because they were pretty full - I think lots of people were going to the parade. Tip - they serve HUGE portions at the Ships Tavern. Very nice dinner! We placed our room service order on our door when we went to bed, and it was delivered promptly on time in the morning. Great portions, great fun to eat in our pj's. The next day was spent shopping/seeing the sights downtown, and ended with another wonderful cocktail in the lobby. The Parade of Lights on Saturday started at 6pm, so lots of people/families left for the parade at that time. The piano player was fantastic. I don't know his name, but we spent several hours hanging out in the lobby listening to his music, and when the kids/families returned from the parade he had them all singing Christmas carols around the piano for nearly an hour. What an enjoyable evening! Our room service breakfast the next day arrive on time again, but they forgot my toast. A phone call by me, and within a few minutes it arrived with a sincere apology. Very prompt, as I can't eat eggs without toast, I appreciated their quickness. We had an absolutely LOVELY stay at the Brown. Our daughter got married at the Brown back in Sept -and the girls "get ready" room was a large suite. So the two types of rooms I've seen have been fantastic. I'm ready to go back!

“Great time at the OMNI” As soon as we pulled up in the car we were excited about staying. I am a Omni Select guest and I had a coupon for a Free upgrade for a room. I was given a very large one bedroom suite. It has a nice living room with a large table. The door staff at the hotel is great too. I was there on my first trip to DC ever. Every time I came in for the day they asked me how every thing was going for the day. My girlfriend had a 75 min massage given to her at the fitness center and loved it. The pool closes early, at 9 pm. I didnt have a chance to use it. The Metro is very close 2 min walk one block very nice to have close by after a day on the town. The room service was great too. Being a select guest they had free drinks every morning at our door for us with a paper. They have happy hour in the bar at 5 to 7. I would stay there again in a heart beat.

“We wanted to stay longer!” We stayed here for our anniversary and loved the location. It is right next to the convention center and across the street (pedestrian bridge) from Petco Park. You can easily walk to the Gaslamp quarter and to Seaport Village. There is a nice walking/running path behind the convention center with a view of the water/marina--it leads right to Seaport Village. The hotel staff is sincerely friendly and helpful--everyone we talked to -including the parking lot attendants were super friendly and nice. I was hoping when we checked in we might get an upgrade because of our special occasion, but there wasn't really anything available. Much to our surprise, when we returned after dinner, there was a bottle of champagne and some munchies as well as a note from the desk clerk Jacob who checked us in! What a nice touch and we were so happy that for a big hotel chain, they gave us that personal touch. The room was large and the bathroom actually had plenty of light! Nice size towels and room to put things down on the vanity. The king size bed had plenty of nice pillows and was so comfy. My only negative is the internet/wifi is not free and I didn't want to pay for it. We had their summer fun special-including parking and $35 per day voucher, which we used for breakfast. There is also a Starbucks and yogurt shop right outside. The pool area is nice as well as the fitness room. They provide several free activities on the weekend-including beer/meatballs one night and wine/cheese another. Just a great experience overall. We can't wait until we can return.

“Fantastic service, large rooms and sooo comfortable” Wow! Very, very nice. We had a room on a low floor but it was large and had a wonderful view of the Tidal Basin and harbor. The bathroom was very well appointed but I still cannot say enough about the size of our room. The lobby bar was a 'scene.' Nice! Every evening it was lively. Sometimes too lively. Service was slow but with the size of the crowd, I guess that could not be helped. One of best hotels I've stayed in.

“Better Than Expected” When I pulled up in the front of the hotel. The valet was backed up, hotel guest were standing out front and their children were running around to where I did not want to check in. However, once I surrender my car keys and checked in everything was alright. My suite was comfortable, clean and had all of the amenities I needed. Plus it was quiet on my floor. I had breakfast at the hotel every morning. Coffee was a great way to plan my day and catch up on e-mail. Every evening there was a little snake and the menu was posted on my fridge. The bed was so comfortable. My room looked right out over the ALAMO!
“nice hotel” clean, great location, train station resturant's close by just easy it's midtown. i recomend it.

“It was only good” Booking: I won a bid on Priceline.com. Give this option a try...if you know how to use the "Negotiator" tool, this could save you money. We got a "King Room", on a higher floor, away from the elevators. Area: This is not the "rich" side of Chelsea...still, it offers good dining options and the subway is nearby. Facilities: The hotel is new, clean...though very small. Room: The room is fine. All the furniture is new, the bed is comfortable, the bathroom (and the toiletries) are nice. Tiny...is an understatement for the overall size of the room(s) though. Good Surprises: All the diners in the area offer good food and quick delivery - they even deliver right to your room door. Strangely Missing: Rooms have everything except for the most important - TOOTHPASTE! Overall: We stayed only for 1 night...it was an average hotel experience...but the price was fair. Tip: Ask front desk for a set of menus from restaurants that deliver...this will save you money & effort. Have fun, be safe, and happy trip!

“Beautiful hotel in a prime location” My husband and I stayed for 2 nights at the Hyatt Regency in San Antonio. We booked through name your price on priceline so were very pleased to get such a fantastic hotel for just $70 per night. On check in the staff were very friendly and looked for the best available room for us. The room was exactly what we'd hoped it would be: clean, large, comfortable and tastefully decorated and furnished. Having free use of a rooftop pool (however small) and a fitness centre packed with top of the range equipment really made our stay special. After a hot day walking around San Antonio, it was lovely to lay on the sunbeds on the rooftop, have a dip in the pool to cool off and go for a workout before dinner. The location of this Hyatt couldn't be better; straight out of the doors onto the riverwalk. It was perfect for going out for dinner and drinks each evening. Once inside the hotel, all of the sounds of the riverwalk were blocked out and we got a very restful 2 nights' sleep. The only reasons I have marked this hotel down are: - if we had paid full price, the hotel would have been very good but nothing exceptional. - parking was extremely expensive (even compared to other hotels on the riverwalk).

“Inexcusable disaster. One preventable problem after another.” I don't think there's enough room here to describe everything that went wrong at my recent one-night business stay at the Fairfax. I'd stayed there before, and never had a problem, so this time was just inexcusably shocking. On the plus side, the location is great, two blocks from DuPont Circle and the Metro, right on Massachusetts Ave. The Cons. First, the room. My colleague and I both got rooms in the same line; each room was about 150 square feet, if that, not including the tiny closets or the bathroom. It was ridiculously small, and not at all what was advertised and reserved. The bedsheets were stained, and the room was so tiny I had to stand in the bathroom so the maid had room to change the sheets after I complained. At least one of the bath care products had already been opened and presumably used. The front door was not properly aligned, so at night the tiny room was flooded with light from the hall. Multiple complaints about the running toilet were ignored. The stick-on privacy glass on the bathroom was peeling off, revealing the same lovely view of the dumpsters in the alley below shared by the bedroom. Somehow the hotel also forgot to leave bottled water in my room or offer it to me, even though someone came around with a cart in the evening and offered it to everyone else (when I answered the door she only offered turn-down service and chocolate, not water). (They also forgot the ice bucket.) A number of the outlets were dead (explaining why it took the iron so long to warm up!!). One request to speak to the manager went unanswered; the other was met with annoyance and then feigned ignorance, and I was told to wait 10 minutes (I chose to depart). However, to the hotel's substantial credit, once they were advised of all of my complaints (via written letter to the hotel and Starwood), they promptly called to apologize and tried to make it right. I was informed that meetings were held and the problems addressed so they should not re-occur. I'm almost afraid to give them another chance. But as I said above, this could have been a complete aberration, as my prior stays were uneventful and enjoyable, but a hotel of this class simply should not have that many aberrations. Thus, I can't recommend the hotel, but am hesitant to not recommend it, and so am checking "no" because TripAdvisor makes us choose one or the other.

“Nice but not clean” Lobby spectacular, rooms are updated and cool but my trash can wasn't emptied and there were tiny hairs on the white bed. Used other one. Bathrooms sink new but tub and toilet were old and dingy. Great location.

“Location!” The location of this hotel is the best I've tried in Boston thusfar. The hotel lobby is newly redone and is very sharp. Customer service and detail to attention is 5 star. Rooms are 3 star. They were average size. My room had leftover piece of food on a room service menu which was a little gross. Their restaurant breakfast was very pricey, next time I'd walk to a different place. The valet people were great and very consultative. I'd stay here again.

“excellent hotel in downtown Philadelphia” Let''s say this up-front. The feather beds in this hotel are without question the best we've ever slept in. The Sofitel is located on the site of the old philadelphia stock exchange. The neighborhood looks seedy but is generally safe. When we were led to our first room, it reeked of smoke. A quick call to lobby resulted in an apology from the manager and an upgrade to a suite. The rooms are handsome, comfortable , and elegant. The bathroom included both a shower and a tub. The public areas of the hotel are attractive and tasteful. The restaurant in the lobby is reasonably priced for a big city. Don't miss the complementary coffee which is located near the hostess. If you want to dine with the locals, try the excellent Marathon Cafe just a block away. The hotel lobby bar has attentive waitresses and fine cocktails. Highly recommended. Check the Sofitel website for special deals.

“Comfortable New York Hotel.” We stayed at the Benjamin earlier this month. The location, 51st and Lexington is excellent. Great access to the subway (on Lexington Ave.) and buses. The building looks to me as if it dates from the 1920's. It is more elegant than the Affinia 50 or the Affinia Gardens where I have also stayed. The staff is outstanding. The bellman (I wish I could remember his name) was the best. He carried our bags to Lexington Ave. when we checked out "to save you 6 blocks" since 51st St. is one way going in the wrong direction. I booked a superior room and was upgraded to a suite, a real luxury in a city with too many shoe box hotel rooms. The suite included a very small kitchenette, and we made use of the fridge and the glasses and plates. There was a live plant in the room, a nice touch. The TV was high def and had a terrific picture. The bed was very comfortable. A chair in the living room had a stain, and one of the chairs was a little scuffed. The bathroom was marble and elegant, but small. There was little room to put your stuff. We arrived early. Our suite on the 7th floor was not ready, but a suite on the 4th floor was. I appreciated getting into the room early, but I wonder if it wasn't a mistake. The suite faced Lexington, and this part of mid-town is very busy. We were awakened by a police siren early the next morning. I would ask for a room higher up, or one which did not face Lex. The gym was adequate, but would have benefitted was a little more diligent housekeeping. There is a business center, but you are charged for internet time. No big deal for me, since I brought my iPad and my hotspot. The neighborhood is great, and Ess-a-Bagel on Third is a great spot for a cheap breakfast. I carried out because we had all this room to spread out. The hotel restaurant was closed for an event the evening we were there, so management had a wine and beer hour to compensate. Lots of daily papers in the lobby, and the hotel shined my shoes gratis. I liked this place and would return. I paid $272.00 for the suite, a great deal in mid-town New York. the rate would have fallen to $246.00 for the weekend. With a little more attention to detail, this place could offer a five star experience, but in my judgment, it was a very solid 4 star stay.

“Solid Hilton experience” Our first visit back in a year. Front desk welcome was great and departure was the same. Not sure if Starbuck's was in the lobby last year but it was a plus for the morning. Hotel is going thru a renovation but you would not know it as they have isolated the section under renovation. The hotel has an activities desk and we bought tickets for a Double Decker bus tour , the closest pickup was nearby at Union Square and we had a great tour. Lot's of deli/convenient stores in walking distance and tons of places to dine. A good hotel to base yourself from ( they also have rental car agencies across the street )..

“Beautiful place, excellent value” The hotel was a great value. It is located in a business park area and I believe most of their business is probably during the week so they offer fantastic rates on the weekend. We were looking for a convenient place to stay with family that had a pool for the kids. The pool was adequate and not overly crowded but the people that were there were much more rowdy and obnoxious than you would typically find at a 4 star hotel. I suspect due to the very low weekend rate. We stayed in a double queen on the corner and the room and bed were comfortable with very nice linens and pillows. AC worked well, bathroom was beautiful, spacious and clean. Overall the hotel was quiet and relaxing(with the exception of the pool) Valet parking was only $10/day which is a bargain compared to most hotels I've stayed at. And while we didn't utilize room service the prices were also very reasonable. It is conveniently located next to major highways and we found great restaurants and shopping in Grapevine only minutes away. Medieval Times dinner show was only about a 15-20 minute drive from the hotel as well and fun for the kids. If you are looking for a nice hotel at a nice price in the DFW area then I don't think you could go wrong with the Omni.

“Nice location - but not up to Hyatt Regency Standards” Pros: - Outstanding location on Embarcedero Drive and across from the Ferry Building - Large & Beautiful Atrium - Large Rooms Cons: - Rooms are dated, worn out - Bathrooms are not clean - Service was adequate We stayed at the Hyatt Regency in other cities and I would like to say that this is a nice hotel, but not quite worth the price to stay. The initial impressions of the hotel were good, an incredibly 10+ story atrium with hanging lights and global ball greeted us. The hotel location is superior with a close walk to Chinatown, Financial District, and Fisherman's Wharf. However checking into our room, I must admit that the rooms were sub-standard for a Hyatt Regency hotel. The big problem we had was with the old, worn out look and feel of the room. The carpet was stained and rough -most likely because it hadn't been replaced in a while. The bathroom fixtures were old and an eyesore. Old fixtures and noticeable hair in the bathroom didn't leave a positive impression. It didn't help that the dim lighting in the bathroom and entry way didn't give the room a "bright" look. Bed sheets were rough and not the typical "fluffy" high-thread count for linens. The room was really a big downer. We didn't try many of the on-site services except the fitness room and it was very bare with a couple treadmills and reclining bikes and light weights. The new Stay Fit fitness center wasn't opened at the time so the fitness facility could be better next time. For the dollar's worth, I wouldn't recommend the Hyatt Regency. If any reason, you would want to stay here for the location but that's pretty much it.

“2 nights in Houston” My husband and I stayed at this hotel for two nights while visiting some family nearby. The hotel was a good location for us. Our room was great, spacious and clean. The bed was quite comfortable. The only unfortunate thing about our stay was that our original booking was for three days and we had to change it to two on arrival due to change in plans. This change is length of stay ended up increasing our room rate by $80 for the first night! I am still happy with the property, but if I had known this rate would have jumped this much, I may have looked around for a better deal elsewhere.

“Beautiful” This is a great resort. The rooms are huge, clean and nicely decorated. There are lots of pools to choose from. We ate Dinner and lunch here during our stay and the food was great. This place also runs a shuttle bus down to the local shopping plaza.

“Worth Staying Here” Stayed one night and overall had a great stay. Pros --- Great location and within walking distance to all major attractions including Lucas Oil Stadium. Room was very nicely appointed -- appears to have been recently renovated. Comfortable bed, nice work desk, and flat screen TV. Room had a great view of the city lights and Monument Circle! Ask for a room on the 9th floor or higher and for this view. The hotel is about a $25-30 cab ride with tip from the airport. There is a starbucks near the lobby area. Cons --- The bathroom was clean (most important) but was very small and didn't have the new feel of the rest of the room. Just before the front entrance of the hotel and the parking garage there is a bus stop that seems to be a gathering point for homeless and transients --- this might make some feel uncomfortable like it did to my colleague. Overall i had a great experience --- this is not the Conrad (down the street) but worth staying here and you'll end up paying a lot less.

“Such a disappointing return trip” Having had a lovely time here two years ago we returned only to be hugely disappointed. The hotel is a huge conference centre and this is all they are interested in. They are simply not interested in the one off guests who are on holiday. We were staying 8 nights and didn't get the room we requested when we checked in. We got a bay view room which was a joke - you could see the bay if you stretched your neck over the balcony. The balcony was filthy. We asked to be moved but were told the place was full so they could do nothing, they could move us the next day for a few nights and then we would have to be moved again! We contacted our agent at home who are 8 hours behind but due to time differences there was no Manager on site, they left a message and were promised the manager would contact us as soon as they arrived in. They didn't and we had to follow it up ourselves. We spoke to Elizabeth who turned out to be one of the only helpful staff members and after some sorting her end she managed to get us the room we wanted. The hotel is so busy with conferences it's just not a relaxing holiday destination. There are business people on lap tops everywhere (including the pool) and talking loudly on mobiles. The place really needs a renovation as it's filthy in certain areas. The cushions around the bar area are dirty and the whole place looks tired. We loved it the last time we stayed but sadly we will not be returning. The apathy of the staff is probably due to the lack of care given to the hotel. It's such a pity

“Highly recommended, not without faults though” This is a brand new hotel with all modern amenities. The offerings were comprehensive and at a 4-4.5 star level. We booked a superior room and were "upgraded" to a deluxe room on the 9th floor with no view but were given the option to wait for a room on a higher floor which we declined. The room was huge and the bathroom had full window frontage which is rare in hotels. This made the bathroom deluxe in my opinion and the stand up shower was fine and preferred to old fashioned tubs. Bed was pillow top but on the firm side. Linens were nice. There was a huge LCD tv as well. Overall, the room was extremely comfortable and tastefully decorated. The service was excellent as well, I called down a few minutes prior to check out to have boarding passes printed and they were waiting for me when I checked out. I recall a similar experience at a Westin in NY when I was directed to the business center for a 20 minute ordeal, most of which was the staff member trying to get the hotel computer billing system to work so they could add the $4 to my bill. A big negative was that the room was adjacent to the ice machine room and stairwell (room 902). Though not often, a loud crashing noise came from the ice machine as it filled buckets. The stairwell was used aggressively, why I don't know, at around 3am each night of my stay. It was situated directly behind the headboard and the noise reverberated throughout the room and of course woke each of us up. I suspect it was a staff member checking for breakfast order cards in a manner as efficient as possible for him or her, but I'm not sure. If you wish not to be woken, ask for a room that is not adjacent to these service areas as there are two like this on each floor. This is the only reason why I didn't go five stars all the way because the hotel was truly worthy in other respects.

“Great location on the miracle mile and a nice older hotel” Booked this hotel for an absolute steal on hotwire and then upgraded for $75 a night to a top floor lake-view suite. Great hotel in terms of location and service. Extremely convenient and comfortable hotel. Loved the bathrooms and the fixtures. Its only draw back it is a really physically old hotel. Book it on hotwire (using one of those websites that decode what hotel is what) and then enjoy the luxurious accomodations for what it would cost to stay at a holiday inn.

“Nice choice in Boston” Just got back from a 3 night stay in Boston. This property is a little worn and not as perfect as some of the other 4S properties-the chair in our room had stains on it, and the tv remote was dirty. However, those were the only 2 glitches. I agree that at the prices you pay for a 4S, 2 glitches is too many, but 4S is one of the few hotels that I know I can count on, and Boston was no exception. Our room and bath were very clean (other than the remote, obviously)- no stray hairs to be found on the linens, in the bed, or in the bath (one of my pet peeves!). The service was definitely up to 4S standards, and the location across from Boston Common was great. We were given a ride by the "house car" to dinner one night (a free service) and were given excellent recommendations by the concierge on where to eat and what to see. We had an excellent stay- the location was great, the service was excellent, and our room was spacious and very clean. This would definitely be my choice if ever in Boston again.

“Don't stay at this hotel” Got this hotel on Hotwire at a 30% discount. Although hotel is listed as on the "Riverwalk", it is at least 3 very confusing blocks to get to the touristy Riverwalk area. Even with 2 maps in hand, we both got lost walking down the first 2 blocks of this deserted end of the Riverwalk, go back up to the street, ask a police office on how to get back down the main Riverwalk area. So if you want to stay in the Riverwalk area, don't book here. This hotel also has the rudest & most un-professional valet staff. Both the morning & evening crews were horrible. Their uncaring attitude were extremely unsettling. Even at $28 for valet parking & $24 for self-parking in lot across the street, it's not worth it. They ran out of valet parking spaces in the evening & you're on your own to find your own parking. Rooms were nice & comfy, but rest of hotel seems old & dated. Would not recommend this hotel for a relaxing family vacation.

“Great service!” From check-in through check-out, the staff of the Hyatt was terrific. This hotel has a lot going for it beyond service. Beautiful new bar and restaurant on the Mezzanine; very cool setup for check-in; comfortable beds; nice HVAC system in room; sliding door allows fresh air for the room; well-appointed bath. I did not provide an excellent review because internet service was very slow and there was a fee for it; high speed internet was more expensive ($15/day) but worked well. There was no lounge chair in my room and the chair for the desk was not height adjustable. Taxi service in SF is lousy in SF and even worse at this location, likely due to construction a block away. But it is a convenient walk to great shopping, restaurants and the Moscone Center. I recommend it!

“Good value but fairly basic for Sheraton” Good value for area...room with two double beds for 104 +tax. Hotel well located in Fisherman's Wharf area. Close to Cablecar stop. Beware of parking, over forty dollars per night Valet at hotel with no in/out privileges. Parked across the street for 20$ per night in parkade. If one of the reasons to choose this hotel is the fitness area, skip it. It is comprised of a few machines in a dimly lit room for which you have to go outside of the hotel.

“Great for the price” For the same price that I am paying for a room in Danbury CT, I got a great room at the Hilton. It was a prepay special and I was upgraded when I checked in. That was a great surprise. I arrived late and was happy to see that room service was still available at 12:40am. The food was expensive but the service was good. The elevators were slow but that did not bother me because I was not in a hurry. Check in/out was speedy. Would definitely stay there again. Forgot to mention that a security person was checking room keys at the entry late at night to make sure no one entered the hotel who was not a guest.

“Comfy, roomy and great staff” Enjoyed the stay in the Wingate Jacksonville South. The hotel was very quiet. Nice outdoor pool and big indoor hot tub. The breakfast room is very nice and great breakfast and service. The staff is very friendly on all fronts. The rooms are comfy (beds nice!) and clean. The decor is "florida style" and getting a little more dated - but again clean and comfy. I will be back!

“Centrally located, excellent hotel (esp for business)” I stay at the Sheraton Seattle frequently. it is my "go to" hotel in Seattle. The cross-street is Pike Street and it is a nice stroll down to Pike Place Market. There is LOTS of retail shopping and restaurants surrounding this hotel. You can also easily take the monorail to the Space Needle. The hotel's public areas are representative of a large, Sheraton-style hotel, but very nicely designed and the ambiance is warm and inviting. Once, during the holidays, they even had a Ginger Bread house 'show' in the lobby (more like Ginger bread castles!). The rooms are clean, comfortable, and 'normal' sized (e.g., a King Deluxe room). I am a Gold SPG member, and have never been upgraded to a suite at this property, so I cannot describe the suites (although they have upgraded me from a Standard to a Deluxe room - which I think are on higher floors and have (somewhat) *better* views). The exercise room is awesome, with amazing views (I could work out all day just looking at the view!), and lots of treadmills, etc. I have never had trouble finding a machine, even on the busiest of days. Also, the pool looks awesome, but I have not tried it out yet. Lastly, the restaurant 'Daily Grill' is EXCELLENT! I stopped eating pork, but I still crave their Double-cut pork chops with a local berry sauce. So awesome. The Fish & Chips are good too. Very large portions of everything...Also, it is a nice, dark atmosphere, with booth seating, that is cozy on a rainy Seattle day. The bar is a great place to meet with colleagues/clients after work too and has a variety of cocktails, good wine, etc. I also noticed that they have an extensive Gluten Free menu too. The lobby bar was under renovation end of Sept. 2012, but in the past has been a great place to relax and has a great wine selection and the bartenders are very personable.

“Excellent Downtown hotel” Right in the middle of the action I was very impressed by the Doubletree. Room was spacious but part of a 3 room suite with 2 connecting doors. One morning the people in the adjoining room were very noisy but until that time I hadn't noticed. Breakfast buffet and bar were moderate but it's so close to the centre of things I didn't give them much of my cash. Tried room service one night. pizza was almost cold but as it took 45 minutes to deliver I couldn't face complaining and the wait for a new one. The 2 empty beer bottles and the ice bucket were not cleared from the room in 3 days though. So overall great venue but the service could be improved

“Pretty But Flawed” My husband and two daughters recently spent a four-day weekend at the Ritz-Carlton San Francisco. It is a handsome building in a good location, but several annoyances make us wonder whether it's time to change our allegiance to the Ritz brand. We had wanted to stay at the San Francisco Ritz for some time and booked a one-bedroom suite on the Club level so that breakfast, lunch and snacks would be readily available in the Club lounge, primarily for our kids (easier than going to a restaurant for every meal). When making the reservation I was very specific that there would be four of us in the suite, stated the ages of our kids, and explained that we needed a pullout couch for one child and a rollaway for the other. I was told the nightly rate for the suite when I reserved, and nothing was said about any extra charges due to the number of people in the suite (keep reading). First problem: after confirming three times in advance that our suite would have a separate pullout couch and a rollaway bed in the living room, AND that they would be made up and ready when we arrived because we were getting in late, we were taken to a suite with no pullout couch at all and no rollaway in sight. After a couple of phone calls, we were finally moved to a one-bedroom suite that met the description of what I had reserved, but it was very late and we were exhausted. It wasn't a pleasant beginning to our stay. Next problem: upon reading the Club level "welcome letter", we learned for the first time that only three people per suite could partake of the Club lounge food and beverage; any additional guests would have to pay $50 per day. At no time during the reservation process was this mentioned to me despite my specifically advising the reservations personnel that there would be four guests in the one-bedroom suite. This additional charge therefore effectively raised our nightly room rate by $50 per night, to a rate we had not agreed to. We immediately discussed this with the Club manager and the reservations manager, and asked that someone get back to us with their determination on the matter. No one ever did, but upon our checkout, the $50 per day additional charge had been included in our bill. On this point, it's the principle of the thing. If that's their policy, they should tell you when you make your reservation. We had paid a significant additional amount to stay on the Club floor already, and ended up paying $200 extra on top of that (for a 12-year-old girl who doesn't eat much). Housekeeping problem: on two out of the four days of our visit, our room was never made up. We left the hotel before 9 a.m. each day and returned just before dinner time, to find no clean towels and the suite uncleaned. Each time this resulted in housekeeping rushing to our suite to make it up at the same time that we were trying to shower and get changed to go out to dinner. It is a mystery to us why this should happen even once...but twice is ridiculous. Finally, more housekeeping issues: throughout our stay, plates of half-eaten food sat outside rooms on our hallway, on the floor and on furniture, for more than a day at a time. It was, frankly, disgusting. Why wasn't this cleaned up? To see this at a hotel at the level of the Ritz is unbelievable. On the plus side, our suite was lovely, and the staff were uniformly pleasant and helpful. Still, the stay was overall a disappointment.

“Sauberes Hotel in guter Lage” Die Zimmer des Hotel sind sehr sauber, sowie eigentlich das ganze Hotel. Zimmer haben normale Größe und verfügen über einen Fernseher. Bad ist ebenfalls sehr sauber und größentechnisch ebenfalls in Ordnung. Das Hotel liegt mitten in Chinatown. Die Metro ist ca. 5 Minuten vom Hotel entfernt. Auch das Weisse Haus ist in ca. 10 Minuten zu Fuß zu erreichen. Von dort aus sind wir zu Fuß weiter zum Capitol, Washington - & Lincoln Memorial. Ist alles zum erlaufen. In Chinatown kann man übrigens ausgezeichnet essen, wenn die Chinesische Küche mag. Personal war sehr hilfreich und bemüht als wir uns mal eine Pizza aufs Zimmer liefern lassen wollten.

“The best service you will get from a hotel!” The staff at the Magic Castle Hotel can not do enough for you from the moment you check in until the moment you leave. We arrived much earlier than the advertised check in time and were greeted warmly (with a drink) and advised that we could have one of the two rooms we had booked immediately and that the other would be ready in an hour. The check in process was one of the most thorough I have received ranging from information on the complimentary breakfast, the pool, the complimentary mini bar available at reception, the free DVDs for use, free laundry detergent, the list goes on. For our family day at Disneyland one of the members of staff even researched the best means through which to travel to and from Disneyland. When this turned out to be via hire care, he then went about booking it for us and arranging to have it dropped off and picked up at the hotel by the hire car company. While the rooms are probably only 3.5 stars at best, they are very clean, comfortable and ours had a kitchenette and dining area which was great given that we were travelling with our two young children. The free wireless internet was very reliable and the room itself was also very quiet and peaceful from a sleeping perspective. The final 'magic' part of the visit was on check out when we were advised that we could keep one of our two rooms until 6pm at no extra charge given that we had a late night flight out of LA. Extremely generous and extremely unexpected. This hotel thoroughly deserves the ratings it is receiving on TripAdvisor and is one that I wouldn't hesitate in recommending to anyone.

“My only choice in San Fran” After learning this place existed, it is the only place we stay in San Fran now. Zero complaints: great location, nice staff, historic building, well appointed rooms, great breakfast buffet, complimentary evening reception. Excellent all the way around. If you military of any type, you get a fairly sizeable discount on room rates.

“Good Location, Good Hotel” I found this hotel more than acceptable. I got a good price on Hotwire and despite them appearing to tell the hotel the wrong date I was going to be there I was checked in very easily. The room was surprisingly big. It was clean and comfortable. The breakfast was ok without being outstanding and it does say that they are building a new breakfast room. If I was coming to SF again and I could get a suitable price I would definitely stay here again.

“Basically good; hardly luxurious” The room was fine; nothing special even though it supposedly was a "preferred level" room. Indoor pool was ok; a bit small. Nice workout facility. Location is really great if you're doing anything near Prudential Center/Fenway. Warning, they charge you for everything

“Trendy fun hotel” Love this hotel. All appliances are new and my room was as clean as you can get. The staff was friendly and helpful. I've stayed in many hotels in New York and can honestly say this is the best hotel you can stay at. I'm not a fan of the location only because it's smack in the middle of Times Squares but that could be a positive for tourists.

“near Joe Louis Arena” would recommend to those wanting to stay downtown. Within walking distance of Joe Louis Arena and other attractions. There is only valet parking but worth the money, they were very fast. Area recommendations Downtown

“Superb Hotel with a couple of flaws...” This is an outstanding property. The rooms are very nice with most of them especially the upper floors having good views. regardless of where you are at you'll hear some road noise and the occasional siren....It's Washington DC! You might have to walk a bit to get to your rooms but they are nice. Beds are very comfortable and TV's good size. There are many places to walk to and the subway isn't too far away just northwest of Dupont Circle so you can go anywhere you need to. Now the bad, I know the Hilton people will see this so feel free to go to room 6214 and check it out. Th ironing board is what you would call "Made in China" I actually could not get the wrinkles out of my shirt because of the badly wrinkled, extra thin covering which was very "crunched" at the edges. They also have the "DREADED" movement sensor that let's the airconditioner work as long as you occasionally move. Yes they will come fix it but you have to ask. If you find this helpful please mark it so. Thanks Berny

“A nice stay . . .” We stayed at the Marriott for a convention being held at the hotel. Service was generally good and although we had requested a king size bed and got two doubles, that was really the only issue. (And we didn't press for a change.) A few things of note: 1. The breakfest buffet in the hotel's restaurant was very good. One of the better breakfast buffet food experiences ever. (Service was slower one morning, but fine the other.) 2. Price of the room was at the the special convention rate so I thought it was affordable. Valet is about what you'd expect for a city that size I guess. No issue with valet service of any kind - Very prompt. 3. Pool and hot tub were nice and not crowded at all even though there were a number of conventions going on. 4. Close to White River State Park (Took a very nice evening walk to the park & Canal Walk) and downtown shopping center and restaurants. And obviously the Convention Center & RCA Dome are across the street. Baseball stadium a block away.

“Convenient Little Hotel” This was my second stay at this hotel. The first time I had stayed in 2002. Now, I was on a business trip to the suburbs of Dalas, but wanted to stay closer to the city so I could dine at the West End, which is a $10 cab ride away. The hotel seemed to have undergone a renovation. It is clean. The location is very easy to arrive at from the airport. Lee at the front desk was very helpful. He let me choose between two rooms, I chose the smaller room with an updated electronic thermostat. The hotel has a little pool, which is very clean and a great oasis for relaxation.

“AMAZING NEW HOTEL IN CHICAGO -- GREAT ROOMS” I stayed at this hotel for three nights in July and it is a fairly new hotel in the city's loop district. It was an amazing experience. The lobby is immaculate. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms are LARGE, COMFORTABLE and the bathrooms are among the best of any place I have stayed in. The only downside is that the valet parking was EXORBITANT, even for the Chicago prices...over $50 a night for valet and no affordable self parking options either, nearest lot is almost 2 blocks away and, while cheaper, with no in and out privileges it can add up as well. The room service and food was impeccable -- reasonably priced and great taste.

“We were quite pleased with the Silver...” We were quite pleased with the Silver Cloud Lake Union. We wanted a place close to the city with free parking and breakfast. The Silver Cloud has that. The breakfast was kind of a free-for-all, with not enough bus people or servers to accommodate the crowd, but the food was ample enough. The room was nice, with fine amenities. We enjoyed the view of the seaplanes landing. We ate at Duke's Chowder House, a short walk away, and that was very good as other reviewers have noted. We would return to the Silver Cloud.

“buon rapporto qualità/prezzo” nulla di eccezionale ma rapporto qualità prezzo favorevole. Posizione non esaltante ma...nel complesso non male. ottima la possibilità di parcheggio. Piccola colazione continentale compresa.

“Great location, really nice rooms, wifi connection is terrible!” We stayed in the Dylan for a night in October. Found the staff on check in really nice and the concierge was nice if not that helpful of where to go out to get a bite to eat! He didn't really know the area that well. The room was really nice, big king size bed which was super comfortable and impecably clean. Bathroom was big and spacious too! The only draw back was that the wifi connection was really weak and became very irritating to try and use! Would recommend the Dylan if the wifi wouldn't both you!

“Great location, rooms a bit disappointing” We have stayed at other Sofitels and found the rooms at this one a bit disappointing. I confess, I was surprised after all the rave reviews on the site. There was nothing actually wrong with the room at all, but it seemed a bit dated in comparison with the rest of the hotel. The lobby bar and public areas are all really funky but the rooms seemed fairly bland in comparison. Having said that, despite the styling issues, the room was very comfortable, had a great view and was quiet. The bathrooms were lovely - as usual for a sofitel! The breakfast room seemed very small for the size of the hotel and on one morning there was a 20 minute wait for a table - although on the other days this wasn't a problem. Food was excellent and service at breakfast was good. We didn't eat in the hotel in the evening (there are so many options in Chicago) but one evening when we were tired and tempted to stay in, we did notice the restaurant seemed quite high end and there didn't seem to be an option to have something simple like a Club sandwich in the evening. Only snacks/small plates were served in the bar. Again, I found this unusual for a hotel of this size. The location was brilliant - a stone's throw from the magnificent mile and only about 15 minutes walk from the river. We loved Chicago and were fortunate enough to see some of the Blues Festival which was fantastic. My top tip - take one of the (less well publicised) Chicago Architectural Foundation boat tours if you are even remotely interested in architecture. it was money very well spent and you get some great photo opportunities from the river.

“Old World Pleasure at a very reasonable price” My wife and don’t travel to Washington DC that often and this was our first stay at The Churchill (we always do Priceline bidding; sp we got our room for $80 per night; but there is no guarantee that this will work for you). We really enjoyed The Churchill as we felt we had gone back in time to those worldly places of yesteryear. The reasons are simple our room was large and everything worked, it had a nice desk, a place to put my laptop, and a separate alcove for more space and reading. The refrigerator worked, the bed was comfortable, the common areas were pleasant and uncrowned, the bathroom was large, the location north of DuPont circle was ideal for easy commuting. Street parking on the weekend is readily available. There was no downside for me as our room was on the 9th floor facing Connecticut Avenue and not noisy.

“Good Location to visit DC area with Metro within one block” We stayed at this hotel due to winning it from Priceline when trying to book a hotel for the DC area. We paid $78 which was a good deal for the area. The metro was very convenient within a block of the hotel at the corner of Woodley Road and Connecticut Ave. An all day pass on the metro was only $8.30. The zoo is within walking distance of the hotel. We requested a room in the newer section and was given a room on the 8th floor facing the National Cathedral. The room is very small, but clean. We moved the chair from in front of the desk in order to get by the bed. There was no refrigerator in the room, just an empty space where one should have been. The bathroom is rather small (the door would hit you if you are on the toliet). We were able to park our car along the street in front of the hotel (Sat and Sun only) instead of paying $32 for parking. Plenty of places to eat around the area or just a subway ride away. We did not use any of the amnenities in the hotel as there is so much to do and see around the DC area. Just make sure you wear comfortable shoes as you will be doing alot of walking.

“Great boutique hotel and location” My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights in July 2012 and had a great experience overall. We arrived around 11 am and our room wasn't yet ready, but they had champagne or red wine waiting in the lobby and gave us a glass to relax while they stored our bags and we figured out our next steps. The champagne and wine were available all day long to take a glass to your room or just sit in the lobby before heading out. A very nice touch that a lot of large hotels don't offer! They also had NYC maps and helped us with directions before we headed out for the day. We booked this hotel through Living Social and check-in was smooth. They already had my voucher when i arrived, so I didn't have to do anything but give them my name and a credit card for incidentals. When we got into our room later, they had left us a bottle of champagne and cookies in our room. Another unexpected, nice touch! As part of our Living Social deal, we also got an upgrade on the room, which seems to have meant we got a room on a higher floor. This didn't work out so well for us because our room ended up on the backside of the hotel, which meant our balcony overlooked other buildings and the air conditioning units. They offered to switch our room but we figured we weren't going to be there to use the balcony anyway, so we stayed put. If you plan to use the balcony, ask for a room on the front of the hotel. The room was a nice size, with plenty of room for 2 people and a large suitcase to move around. They had a lot of nice little amenities that really stand out: 2 robes, champagne, wine and highball glasses, a corkscrew, a fully-stocked mini bar (which cost extra if you took anything from it), ipod station, flat screen tv with about 200 cable channels, free wifi, and even a vanity kit in the bathroom with q-tips and cotton ball (things I forgot to bring). The bed was very large and comfortable. The bathroom has only a shower (no tub) but it came with a removable shower head if you wanted to use that. Location: Very convenient. We were about 1.5 blocks from Grand Central Station, about 3 blocks from Times Square. Lots of great restaurants and bars nearby. About a half block from 5th Avenue shopping. Service: Great! They always had a doorman there to help you with luggage, guide you, get a taxi, etc. The front desk people were very helpful. We asked for a couple of things and they got them to the room within minutes. Two nights they brought us oranges as a snack in the room. Restaurant: This is the only part that I would rate average. We had a $50 credit and breakfast included every morning. We used the $50 credit and the food was so-so. I ordered a lobster linguine and it came in teriyaki sauce, which overpowered the lobster and just wasn't the right choice. Breakfast was continental and serve yourself. That's why I was surprised at the end when I was automatically charged nearly $5 for gratuity for the one day that we ate breakfast there. The attendant in the restaurant didn't do anything - not even come by the table to give us water. I don't mind tipping but you have to do something to earn it. Business office: it was available for free but I didn't use it. In all, I would highly recommend this hotel, just go out for meals.

“An Average Marriott Property” Checked into the Marriott in late August to stay two nights during a recent business trip. It looks like they recently updated the lobby, but outside of that the hotel looked tired and in need of a facelift. Had a couple of drinks and dinner at the bar which was fine. No problems with the staff, and additionally I would say they were more friendly than other Marriott properties.

“Remarkable how good service overshadows the nits” The Marriott Executive Park is solid business hotel with excellent freeway access without being noisy. In my stays, I've been impressed with the "southern hospitality" in the hotel, with all of the staff being friendly and helpful. I've gotten excellent lunch and dinner recommendations, helpful driving advice, and just politeness from the staff. The rooms are older, but nice and functional. Lots of outlets around the room and WiFi reception is good. One nit - they have the slowest elevators in Charlotte. Seriously, the elevators there frustrate the heck out of me. But the service overshadow the elevators.

“It was nice but...I mean it is a Hyatt...what I expected but nothing stellar” I stayed at the Hyatt from Jan 24-27th for a conference The first night rate was 269 and the other two nights were 200 (conference rate)...Please also see my Parc 55 review during the same stay. 1. Location and Size: Unlike the Parc 55 hotel which has 1000 rooms compared to this hotel's 800, the Hyatt feels massive. The moment you walk off its street level you are shown a map that has all its various levels for conference rooms and check in etc. Once I found the atrium to check in ( left the luggae with the bellman) I was asked it I wanted to upgrade my room for 35 dollars a night to a bay view. I said no thank you. I figured I wouldn't get an upgrade anyway. I mean it is a Hyatt so they kinda give off the vibe they don'ty have to try and impress you with perks such as upgrades get to make you smile. Kinda like, "if you had the money you would of gotten it already". It was ok, I had had my great view the night before :). It was raining a lot so I didn't take in the locations pro/cons. Overall it was an asset. The cable car stops in front of the hotel and you can get a troplly to FWarf if you'd like in front of the Ferry building. The cons were that since it is in the financial district all the nearby stores like Starbucks, Coffe bean and tea leaf, and Walgreens closed super early. No 11pm coffee here. Staff: When I went up to my room the first time I found it has just been finished being cleaned. I noticed later that there was a sink problem (no biggie the sink just fiulled up quickly) I guess the maid from the previously must of reported it becaue the next afternoon I had a matienance man show up to unclog the sink. I just wished the hotel at notified me with a phone call because I had to wait 15 min for the facilities person to fix the sink when I had wanted to relx and change clothes for the next part of my day (post conference). The concereige had a great attitude and was fery helpful in sending me to the Ferry Building for Food which was AWESOME ( you must go|) Room: It was nice, ok view, bit of the bay. You have to be cool with your inner exhibitionist because bascically since I was on the 7th floor (or 10 by their elevator) I was smack in front of a bunch of office buildings so people can watch you if the draps are opened ( didn't matter much to me). CON: The mini-bar. If you TOUCH or MOVE anything, you WILL BE CHARGED FOR IT..the pro was that all the locals I told this story were shocked and laughed with me about how absurd it was. If you want to rent the fridge it is $30 bucks a day and the housekeeping staff must remove all the items. Other facts: Their restaurant on the rooftop is closed currently. That would of been nice. The business center charges 5.95 for 15 min of internet and 35 cents after that. You cannot charge it to your room and must use a credit card. I mean it was ok..the conference was well-organized, and I did grow to like the Hyatt. It just wasn't stellar with the exception that the Ferry Building, its food and gifts is the BEST!

“Bad service, not a good business hotel” I stayed here for one night in June, 2009 and would not recommend this hotel. To begin with housekeeping did not change the half used shampoo bottles (pretty gross, huh?) from the previoius guest and after calling the front desk three times over an hour and a half period --- each time was "greeted" by NICKIE-- she could honestly care less that I had no shampoo. Also, I am a HHonors Diamond member and there was no Diamond amenity in my room. The service at this hotel is very low end and this Nickie woman is a total joke. I would not stay here again and would recommend that you stay away.

“This place ROCKS!!!!” This hotel is fabulous!! We got the tip about it from Trip advisor and we are thrilled at the quality for the price we paid. The hotel is located near the Georgetown section very close to the Metro (4 blocks) It was a very safe area. We took the Metro to all of the spots. I suggest you buy a multiday metro pass and avoid the Taxi's which are very expensive. We took the Amtrak train from Ny and were pleasently surp[rised when the taxi pulled up to this hotel. The lobby is stunning! There is a cool waterfall and lots of foliage, Lovely! The front desk people were super friendly and asked why we were in DC. We told them it was our anniversary and that we had never been to DC. They provided us with maps and suggestions as well as directions. The room was on the 7th floor and was very nice. It is an all suite hotel. The front room was the living area with a sofa,chair,coffee table and nice flat screen tv. There was also a nice table and chairs for quick meals. The bathroom was very clean and spacious. Nice comfy towels! The bedroom was gorgous-King bed, nice furniture and another flat screen. The hotel offers a hot otch free breakfast- they had an omelet chef as well as tons of choices. Go early as it fills up quick! The second day we came back to our room for some rest and found the staff left us a bottle of wine and a card signed by the whole staff for our anniversary. They also included a complimentary book on DC from the gift shop in the lobby. The pool/hot tub was very nice as well and we relaxed every night after a long day of walking! the MOST impressive thing we found was the free managers reception every night. They comp free alcohol and munchies. We were there during the VP debate /World series and they had flat screens set up in the dining area. We both had 3-4 STRONG drinks and munchies. There is also a good restaraunt in the hotel where we ate the first night. We also got some light snacks delivered from room service one night-YUM! Overall-this was an awesome hotel and I now look for Embassy Suites whenever we travel!

“It does the job for cheap (and does the job perfectly at that)” The more I travel the more I can't understand "premium" hotels. I've been going to Houston regularly for over 10 years, and can't believe how much money I've wasted at "premium" hotels in the Galleria area. Hilton Post Oak, Sheraton Suites west loop, JW Marriott, Westin Galleria, etc. - all fine properties, and "full service" but so overpriced compared to properties like the HGI and other "second line" brands within the umbrella brands. It seems the more you spend per night for a room, the more they charge you for other stuff - parking, internet, etc. If you're in Houston, the Galleria area, on business, this is perfect. Spacious, clean rooms, friendly staff, good services, and so very close to everything in the area. Walking distance to a great Argentinian wine bar and steakhouse, and also to one of the best sushi places in town. Covered parking (only $10 a day) and free wifi & remote printing. This is now my go-to spot when I'm in this part of town.

“Perfect in every way” Best workout room ever! No doubt about it--this gym is well equipped and serious. The view from the pool and fitness area is the best! We had a great rate or whould not have stayed here ($129 on Travelocity). The bed was comfortable, room was very clean and the location can't be beat!

“Great value within walking distance to National Mall” Suite was spacious. Best complimentary breakfast I've had (made-to-order omelettes, and lots of other choices). Not being used to embassy suites in general, wasn't used to "manager receptions" so it was great to down a few pints for free each evening. All interactions with staff were great. Fitness room is very small, but adequate. Didn't try pool. In room wifi isn't free, but being on the second floor, we actually were able to pick up the free lobby wifi signal most of the time. Only took 10-15 minutes to walk to Smithsonian (natural history or american history). Plenty of restaurants you can walk to as well. Valet is pricey, but it didn't look like there was any cheap option in that part of Washington.

“pretty much as everyone says” stayed here for a trade show for 5 nights. As most have said it's a average downtown hotel, nothing really bad about it , just nothing really special about it either. check in was smooth, friendly and effecient. We got a room on the 9th floor and had a spetacluar view of the roof.......and a bit of the skyline and hills surrounding the area...... room was typical , beds comfy, bathroom the usual.......on it goes. I ate at the terrace for breakfast buffet..........it was decent for 18.00 bucks We had dessert in the compass room, it was sort of fun rotating around with a rumble with a nice view of the city and surrounding area............hotel must've been built in the late 70's If was very convenient for the trade show which was directly across the street and a short walk from our hotel to our booth....... the area has decent restaurants within walking distance. The downtown is not to exciting accept for the ball park and arena.......... again nothing special, but not really bad either........ pool area is quite small

“Good value for a one night stay. Small, but quiet room.” My wife and I stayed in the city on a Monday night as she had tickets to see Madonna. We wanted something reasonably priced given our short stay. I booked direct with the hotel and used a AAA discount. With tax, it came out to less than $200. For a hotel right in the middle in midtown, that's a really good rate. Hotel is well located for those coming as tourists or in town for business. The room we had was a queen bed standard. The room is dark and it is small. But, the bed was fine and our room in the back of the hotel was REALLY quiet, which was perfect. Bathroom had a full shower, which was a plus. Personally, a room this small would stop being enjoyable after a couple of days. If coming to NYC for several days then consider if a small room makes sense. But, if here for a night or two, this is a fine option if looking for a decent price on a midtown hotel. We thought the staff was perfectly fine. No problem on check-in and someone came up straight away when the tv remote didn't function. I don't think I'd opt to stay here with our kids. The artwork is probably a bit more risque than I'd like to expose them too. But, without them, I'd no have problem with coming back for an overnight.

“Very good staff: Helpful, friendly, always trying to contribute to a good stay.” The Sheraton Hotel and Towers is rather typical of a large downtown hotel. Very nice, clean facility but not really anything special. There is an excellent west facing view of the River and Trump Tower. Restaurant and bar prices are high, as is often the case in these places. In this regard, the Sheraton is no different from the Marriotts, Hiltons, etc. This place does stand out because of a very nice and helpful staff. The front desk, the bell men, the concierge, the housekeeping staff are all eager to help you if they can be of service. It looks to me like the management here has done a good job of recruiting the right people and keeping the focus on the customer. One more tip: I often take a cab from O'Hare but the fare has now gotte up to over $60. I took a shuttle from ORD and too ORD on this trip. It was easy, we only stopped at one other hotel and the fare was only $29. The train will get you into the city, avoiding all the stalled freeway traffic, for only $5 but you still have to get from a station to the hotel . . . kind of a hassel. The shuttle was clean easy and a fair price.

“Good One Nighter” What a pleasure to fly from the cold of London and be at the poolside at the Doubletree in 88 degree sunshine by evening.! The hotel is very convenient to the airport, offers free parking, a free cookie on check in and free internet use in the business centre. The bedrooms are rather dated, especially the bathroom, but are clean, comfortable and spacious. We were rather disappointed in the standard of food available in the Sports Bar ( the other in house restaurant was closed) but our main complaint was the amount of leaves and tree debris in and around the pool area. A couple of sun beds actually had a kind of resin gum dripping unto them from a tree and did not look to have been cleaned for some considerable time. This apart, we enjoyed our stay and would return.

“Communication could be better” Generally the service staff was friendly. At times the cocktail servers were slow to respond. The communication from the hotel could be better. They produce a weekly calendar of events which I did not receive until the 3rd day of my stay. Additionally, the guest room directory needed to be up dated as the TV channels were not up to date. I found a hair (not my color) stuck to one of the towels. I had a couple of other issues which management failed to adequately resolve which has been frustrating. Being a JW Marriott I was disappointed in some of the little things that could have been better.

“Wonderful location & modern room” Stayed here w/my husband to entertain clients in the city. Our room was very spacious & big, overlooking Huron Street. Based on the many reviews I've read, I think there are many different sized King bed rooms here. Ours had plenty of room and was not cramped up at all. We had a hair dryer, as well. This is something that most boutique hotels and pretty much all hotels have. So if you don't see one, call the main desk so they can bring one up to you! Awesome H20 toiletries, me liked. Beds were clean & comfortable. Simple white down bedding & plush mattress, what more could you ask for! Huge windows & black out curtains for those of us that like to sleep in. I am a light sleeper so being in the city there is bound to be sirens and loud late night noises. I woke up from a fire truck or ambulance once, should have brought ear plus to drown that out and my husband snoring ;) Also had massages at the spa in the hotel. It was an overall nice massage but the spa itself is SOOO TINY! The entire place has low lighting to kind of mask how tiny it is. W/that said..
