I don't think there were more than 2 or 3 rooms so it can't really get too crowded in there. The massage room I was in was a typical massage room but you could see behind the curtain in the room all the stuff they store behind there. Not the "omm" experience you want. Great massage but wish the area had more room so I didn't feel like they were hiding their toys for company. Had breakfast at the restaurant attached the hotel - yummmyyy goodness!! Wonderful coffee, yummy egg white omelette& some delicious Mexican breakfast dish my husband got. Overall wonderful stay, would definitely stay here again minus a spa visit but will bring ear plugs in case of fire trucks again!

“Incredible Value – What’s not to like!” We booked this hotel via Price-line. What a deal. Excellent staff, grand lobby, nice rooms, hopping bar, good buffet breakfast....What's not to like. Bit of a walk to the convention center, and just a tad on the far side of the Riverwalk, and the TV's were not flat-screens, but who goes to San Antonio to watch TV...and still, may be the best value there!

“Comfortable Well-Appointed Property” We have enjoyed both of our stays at this stylish, well run property. While the decor may be a little flamboyant for some tastes, it certainly provides a pleasant departure from the typical mainstream hotel experience. Monaco lobbies are feasts of color and theatrical flourishes, decked out with stylish furniture, bold fabrics and other touches which establish a cheerful tone. The presence of guests' well behaved dogs also lends a rather homey atmosphere to a clearly chic, upscale experience. Despite all the elegance, this is a mid-tier, mid-price hotel, an affordable luxury which provides quite a treat for a vacation or get-away weekend. The rooms carry on the color and drama of the lobbies and are very comfortable and well maintained. We have selected suites on each visit and find the extra space well worth the cost since the standard rooms have felt a little small at the Monaco's property in Denver. The standards of the hotel are quite high despite the moderate price point and all the amenities from the jazzy robes to large marble bathrooms to well chosen furniture reflect well on the management of this chain. The staff are wonderful and very professional. We especially approve of the room service and bar dining option at the Monaco. While the formal restaurant is there if you need it, its menu is unexceptional and there are better dining experiences all over San Francisco. The bar, however, is a very comfortable place to hang out and dine on an excellent selection of various bar foods from burgers to calamari to raw oysters. The presence of this bar dining option is a real plus in considering the Monaco since it takes all the pressure off the dinner hour when a major dining experience may not be required every night of your stay. Our one slight negative on this hotel is its location which is off Union Square rather than on it. While two extra blocks aren't a huge deal, the twentieth time you walk them could matter to you. Otherwise, the Monaco is an excellent choice near the very best part of a truly enchanting, vibrant city.

“Full Service Hotel?? More like NO service...” I was put up in this place by my airline. I knew a little of the Red Lion hotel history, once a part of the Hilton Family for a short time, Hilton converted the good hotels to a Hilton or Doubletree then selling off the less appealing hotels. Well this is a less then appealing hotel. The check in staff was slow and clueless. I was given a room with 2 beds, I said it is just me, I only need 1 bed. She told be 1 bed is more money. OK.. I walk to my room, open the door and the smell of room was overwhelming, they had to use a can of spy to make it smell "good??" There was an old post-a-note on the floor, the lamp shade was not on straight, and just musty. The 2 beds were covered in the old hotel style, with a big smelly comforter, and thin sheets. There was no remote for the TV in the room, I called the desk and was told people take them. I A/C was loud and not very cooling. The bathroom was ok but small. They market themselves as a full service hotel, it reminds me of a super 8 when I walked in. the restaurant was an add on to the side and you have to go outside to get there.. The restaurant was like an IHOP. The staff was bad, no bell man to help with bags. No service not full service. The internet was free there is a positive. Over all there is so many other places to stay around SEA airport there is no reason to stay here. Oh and the person in the room above me uses the bathroom a lot. I can here it in my room..

“Great location for Cowboy's Stadium and Arlington...” In my opinion, this hotel was a gem after a long week of travel. The staff was friendly and went out of their way to provide directions, local restaurant information, etc. to make the stay easier. I stayed on award points and was offered the Club Level with neither a request nor mention of an upgrade. The rooms are well appointed and the hotel appears fairly new. The restaurant offers ample choices and a reasonably priced breakfast buffet. The gym offers the traveler a nice assortment of equipment plus an indoor pool. Arlington attractions, including Six Flags, Hurricane Harbor (formerly Wet-n-Wild), the Ranger’s Ballpark and the new Cowboy Stadium are about a 15-20 minute drive (depending on traffic). The hotel offered a shuttle service to the Cotton Bowl and offers same to Cowboy games. This service saved time and money as parking near the stadium is challenging and expensive. Though the hotel is located less than 15 minutes from DFW, airport noise was minimal. Good central location for both Fort Worth and Dallas attractions.

“Pretty good place to stay” Just returned from a 3 night midweek stay here. Most of the recent reviews I've read have been pretty spot on. I do feel the strongest aspect of this property was their service, and that's a good thing! Location: The location can be a plus or minus, depending on your needs. If you desire to be in the center of the action and be able to walk right out the front door onto it, then the Marquis and nearby hotels are going to be a better choice. They'll also be closer to the shows. On the other hand, the Hilton is close enough that the walk is really short to the start of Times Square.. and you still feel the excitement as soon as you walk out the doors. The taxicab drop off point on 41st is a blessing b/c there is little traffic there, however once you hit 8th, you are in instant gridlock. The Hilton is very close to the 2 subway entrances so if you'll be utilizing the subways, great choice. If you don't want to stay away from all the craziness of Broadway in the heart of Times Square, this is a perfect location. Service: As I already said, the strong point is service. There was always a bellhop available to assist with flagging down a cab, always someone at the security desk on the first floor, and everyone I encountered was with friendly. Check-in was seamless. This property makes a conscientious effort to always have their staff present and visible in key locations (including the sky lobby) to greet you and guide you with any questions. That made me feel very welcome as a guest of the Hilton Room: If there was one thing I could change, it would be the room. I just felt it was too boring and dull for being a Hilton or being a luxury property. The room was clean and functional, but it can use a refresh/renovation as well as the hallways. The lobby areas and elevators have all been updated in recent years. My wifi worked fine and the AC worked great. Had no problems with good water pressure and hot water. I slept well too! The pictures others have posted on here are an accurate depiction of the rooms. I had a room on the 39th floor facing the Times Square area and it was a pretty neat view. i saw some of the lights (not all), could see the Hudson River at a distance, was right next to the Thomson Reuters buildling, and could even see the New Years ball. A pretty decent view for a downtown property. Wrapup: I didn't order room service or dine on property so I don't have any comments on that. However, if you leave the property and are considering going to the Applebee's next door, skip it. Service there was horrible! After checking out and almost at the airport, I realized I left my car keys in my hotel room. A quick phone call to the front desk and security was able to have my keys waiting for me promptly upon return to pick it up. When I return to the area and if i stay in Times Square again, I would definitely consider the Hilton again due to the excellent service and location.

“Great stay! 3/05” This hotel is pretty well located- you can get to an EL stop without going outside. The view was great, the river and downtown lights were right there! Got a good rate on Hotwire. A little hard to find by car, and parking is a bit steep, but public transit options are good. There was free WiFi in the rooms. The room itself was nothing particularly fancy, but everything was very clean and in excellent condition. I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Almost perfect - with noise as an exception” The Good: Check-in: we arrived just after noon and were delighted to find that our room was ready for us. We were in our room fewer than five minutes after entering the hotel. Room size/appointments: The rooms are generously sized and the decor is undated and elegant. We enjoyed the large flat-panel television. Gym: good selection of weights, treadmills, and elliptical machines, many of which had their own attached television. The water cooler was filled with ice water and slices of orange and cucumber. Delicious. The locker rooms and showers were impeccably clean and well appointed. Check-Out: despite being busy on the day that we checked out, the hotel was able to accommodate our request to leave an hour later than the scheduled check-out time. The Not-So-Good: Noise: we were initially placed in a courtyard-facing room (number 460). Beware – though this room faces the courtyard, it’s still noisy. The room sits across from a maid's station, which meant that we experienced fairly constant yelling/ice bucket filling/garbage bag shaking/door slamming from the early morning until the conclusion of turndown service. We informed the hotel of this issue, and to the hotel's credit, we were immediately moved to another room. Shower/Tub: as other reviews have expressed, the bathrooms are well-appointed with Bulgari products, but a combined tub and shower in a hotel of this caliber is an anomaly these days. Water pressure from the shower head could have been better. Overall impression: we’ll probably stay again, and we’ll bring earplugs next time.

“Happy” We stayed at the Omni in downtown LA the last week in May 05. Room was fine, clean, roomy, with a view - if we turned our heads - of Frank Gehry's Disney Center. What was probably the most impressive was the lower-level personnel, maids, bellmen, and the guys working the driveway, all cheerful, friendly, helpful. It was quite striking. The hotel has a car service that's available from 7 a.m. until 11 p.m. to take you or pick you up within a 3-mile radius. (That means you can go to Dodger Stadium, for instance.) No reservations, first come first served, but it worked really well. We had a car, but used the service 3 times in 5 days, and was happy with it. The hotel is walking distance of the Disney, Mark Taper Forum and Chandler Pavillion, as well as being almost on top of the contemporary art museum. There aren't a lot of restaurants, particularly for breakfast, nearby, especially on weekends. But we walked down the hill to the Central Market and had a wide range of choices, including great Mexican food. (Used the car service for a return.) If you go to the market, go across the street on the downhill side and see the Bradbury Building, unremarkable outside, but amazing inside. By the way, there are refrigerators in the rooms for the minibar, and they can be used if someone needs to store medications - no need to ask for another. I don't recall the daily parking charge, but it wasn't as much as some previous reviewers said.

“Fabulous hotel, great travel location” We found this hotel on an overnight stay during the thanksgiving holiday enroute to our destination in upstate NY. It was brand new and in the hub of restaurants and wonderful shopping mall. We were given a rate of $99.00 as a walk-in and were not disappointed. The buffet breakfast was too much for my husband and I and two teen girls, so we were offered 3 items for $3.00/per guest from the selection. The staff was so accomodating and the lobby was especially dressed for the xmas holiday. The beds were almost as comfortable as those at the Westin. On our return trip, we decided to stay here again and were equally happy. Its a great location off the interstate on Polaris Parkway and not that far from downtown Columbus. Carrabas Restaurant and the Cheesecake Factory are nearby.

“My new favorite hotel in Chicago” Loved, loved loved this hotel. Beautiful soothing decor, enormous rooms and bathrooms with great views. Terrific location no matter what you are doing. Staff very accomodating and room service was very good, as were the restaurant and lobby sushi bar. Fabulously comfortable bed. This hotel will be my first choice from now on. One recommendation - a surge protector on the desk. I had to crawl under the desk to plug in laptops, chargers etc.

“Brilliant” Had the pleasure of staying at the Alexander Inn between September 6th - 8th. Read great reviews on here so was expecting good things, and wasn't disappointed. It is in a great location, with great bars and restaurants literally around the corner, and within easy walking distance of most of Philly's sites. The staff were superb, the simple continental style breakfast was just fine, and the room (considering the price) was perfectly acceptable. The hotel attracts a mixed crowd - which for me adds to the appeal - and myself and my girlfriend met a lot of interesting people during the course of our stay. I found Philadelphia to be a great city to visit, and will definitely be returning soon. Fingers crossed there will be some rooms available at the Alexander Inn!

“Exceeded my expectations.” I stayed at the Drake July 11th for 2 nights. I booked on Priceline and was very surprised to have gotten the Drake. I read quite a few negative reviews on this site and was very worried I would get a dumpy room because of booking through Priceline. I called the hotel a couple weeks before arrival and asked for 2 beds. I was told hotel was sold out for the nights I was staying, but they'd do the best they could etc. I wrote an email to reservations indicating my Silver Hilton HHonors status and again requested double beds with upgrade request. Response came promptly indicating sold out nights again, but to inquire at check in for upgrade. Upon arrival, valet took car with a smile. Check-in was smooth. I asked for upgrade. Again told hotel was sold out and rooms had been assigned by superviser according to requests. I asked how big the rooms were, 150 sq ft? 200, 300? Clerk did not know but said room was comfortable. Was given room 219. Walked down long wide hallways with great anticipation. Opened the door and was very pleased. Room was nice size. View was very good. Faced Michigan Avenue. Extremely clean. Luxurious bed linens. My standard room came with 2 bathrobes. Large tv channel selection. Crabtree & Evelyn toiletries. Awesome deal considering I got this for a steal on Priceline. Turn down service was prompt. Received excellent service throughout whole stay. Only qualm was valet was $43/per day but it is downtown Chicago and because I was traveling with a toddler, for sake of convenience, I didn't look into nearby parking garage options. $43 rate includes in/out priviliges. Took car out several times. Valet guys were quick in getting the car. I would definitely stay here again and would pay out of pocket direct to hotel if I got a good rate. Location is awesome!

“Bar Scene: Very Cool Service: Too Cool” I've stayed at the W Hotel in Time Square and I've been to their lobby bar numerous times. The location is perfect. The bar is always full of interesting people from NYC and out-of-towners. The decor and mood is cool -- but not too cool -- it's comfortable for anyone. But this last visit, the staff -- normally a super friendly crew -- had changed. They were so busy laughing and snickering amongst themselves that they forgot drinks, had to be flagged down; and seemed more than a little annoyed to take a photo of our group. They out-and-out mocked two guests who were a little odd -- causing them to leave sooner rather than later. W Management -- Bring back the friendly, fun team you had. W Bar Scene: Very Cool. Service: Needs to Warm Up.

“Except bed linens, good hotel” This is a nice hotel that is well located and with nice room amenities. The shower pressure was great and we didn't hear noise from other rooms. My boyfriend noticed that the bottom sheet on the bed was not put on properly and the matress was exposed...see the photo. We know the sheet fits properly because we actually remade the bed just fine. So it was laziness / sloppiness on the part of the housekeeping staff...not okay in a hotel of this caliber. Otherwise, no complaints, and great warm cookies at check in as usual!

“Charming, luxurious and perfectly located” Three night stay at the Chicago Intercontinental for New Years Eve. We were given a large room on a high floor. Elevators are very fast. $161/night which by city standards is very reasonable. Two buildings; the historic building which was a mens' club in the 20s and has been restored magnificently, and the newer tower. Staff attentive and helpful. Location could not be better. I had health club, and internet for free with platinum status.

“Pleasant stay.” Stayed two nights last weekend and was completely satisfied with the hotel accommodations and services. The lobby appeared to have been recently remodeled and the checkin was a breeze. The excercise room had modern treadmills with Ipod coonections and a TV. The sauna room allowed me to relax after a long day. Checkout was smooth. Kudos to the front desk staff. Thanks for a great stay.

“Sleek, modern oasis in theatre district” Very expensive, beautifully designed, modern but soothing, inner garden. Room was medium sized, quiet (overlooking 44th St), occasional sirens of course - this is NY), with HUGE shower (no tub), excellent bed and down pillows, good lighting, computer, flatscreen tv, hairdryer, iron and ironing board, slippers and terry robe, minibar, pod-type coffeemaker (ugh), not a lot of outlets, no mirror in bedroom (many in bathroom), ok heat/ac. Strange drapes - hard to open and close if you aren't tall. The coffee from room service was terrific! And can't beat the location if you're going to Broadway shows - right down the street. Subway within 1 block, huge staircase up when coming back, but does have escalator, thank god. Personally, I prefer a studio hotel with microwave - cheaper to keep breakfast and leftovers than to have to go out or use room service. But for a plain hotel, this is fine.

“The best all around Chicago hotel” Wonderful hotel with a great location. Rooms are as shown in photos. It was very clean, exceptionally quiet and comfortable. Service was impeccable. Everyone on staff that we encountered from the doormen, to the cleaning lady, restaurant staff and front desk staff were genuinely polite and very professional. They do a great job at making you feel welcome. Further more, having the check in area on the 3rd floor made it feel even cozier. Food and service at 676 on the 4th floor was terrific with a wonderful view of Michigan Avenue below. After staying at other hotels in Chicago, I have to say - this is by the best! You will not be disappointed. We already have reservations to stay there at the end of this month. Make a point to join their Select Guest program, it's worth it. (Free beverages delivered to your room in the morning and a discounted rate on breakfast breads.)

“Very Cool Hotel - Good Vibe” Kimpton properties are usually top notch, and the Helix is no exception. Staff is exceptional, from front desk to maintenance personnel. Everyone is focused on serving the guests. The entire place has a 60's vibe. My king room was large, except for the bathroom. Large flat screen TV and entertainment center. In-room safe, minibar. Sadly, no in-room coffee maker, but there is complimentary coffee and tea service in the restaurant area, although with multiple newspaper choices. Nice sitting area in room. Free WiFi. My room was very quiet.

“Great location, great people, good value for NYC--but not perfect” This is a great little property in an outstanding location. For what you pay--it is excellent. I have stayed there twice, and find it quite adequate when i am on a budget. In one room, the window did not open and that makes ventilation/heating tricky. The bathrooms are tight, showers only, but again, good value. The bed is very comfortable which to me is an unexpected pleasure in a budget property. I did not have any trouble with the internet. The hotel is a little noisy--guests slamming doors, some noise from Manhattan. They are changing food/restaurants, but the coffee in the lobby in the morning is excellent. I would stay there again for the value and location.

“Perfectly Fine” Stayed here three nights. Perfect for going to Universal Studies, but that's also the reason I never stayed here before (too "touristy" a location for business). However, I was pleasantly surprised by the location. It's sandwiched between the 101 and 134 freeways... which means it's a good location to access the San Fernando Valley, Hollywood, or Pasadena whichever direction you want to go. From that standpoint, it's a pretty good base for exploring L.A. (only beaches are less accessible). Otherwise, it's a fairly standard Hilton. I was on a floor BELOW the lobby which gave it a subterranean feel. I would've appreciated more light and a view. Front desk staff seemed a bit clueless when the group I was with was needing to check in a little early (one staffer knew how to find available rooms while the other one had people camping out in the lobby for 30-60 minutes waiting for a room... finally, they talked to each other). Only other disappointment was that the pool was closed for repair.

“Great location to explore Chicago on foot” Fun eco-boutique hotel in a great location close to the Magnificent Mile and Old Town. Very smart design of the rooms make the space feel comfortable despite the small size. Clean and well equipped for staying in Chicago. Staff were helpful. Good price through Priceline for two nights in May 2012. Would certainly stay here again.

“A very enjoyable stay” I spent three nights at the Bristol attending a conference at the convention center. The location is excellent. The hotel is cheerful and modern, with lots of beautiful artwork. My room was large and comfortable. The housekeeping was so-so, and my minibar fridge was never cold despite my request to have this fixed. However, I found the front desk staff very pleasant and accomodating. Breakfast and room service dinner from the restaurant were quite good. The free high speed internet connection in the room was a plus. Overall I enjoyed my stay, and found it good value next to the overpriced chain hotels offered through the conference.

“Great place to stay” We loved this place, the staff were great, the beds were soooo comfortable and the location was perfect, Rochelle in reception was smashing, so helpful with great tips for getting the best out of your time in san francisco, forget the car as you can get anywhere by trolley bus or tramcar even golden gate bridge with just one change 30 from stockton street and change to 28 at laguna street which stops at the bridge car park with an $18 3 day pass you cannot go wrong, loved the time spent there.

“Lousy bathroom, but decent rate for a room with two beds and a sleeper sofa.” We had to wait for our room, so they knocked $50 off the room, which was nice. Hotel may be only a few miles from everything you want to do in San Diego, but it's not in the best area. There's a strip club a block or two down the street, but the hotel parking lot didn't feel that unsafe. There is a dive hotel next door. The AC doesn't run unless there's someone in the room, which is annoying because it was always too warm and stuffy when we returned. But the most annoying thing was the poor lighting in the bathroom. A single 65w light covers the whole room, including the shower. There's an old fashioned heat lamp too, but it heats up the little bathroom so fast that if you have more than one person showering, the room gets unbearably hot. So, if you can find something nicer for the price in the area, go for it. But this hotel is an OK value if you can't.

“Very comfortable stay in a modern room” I LOVE Kimpton hotels. Truly I do. Free wifi and $10 minibar credit if you're a Kimpton member (for free). And I love the little touches, like the goldfish in our room. The cocktail hour included delicious white wine sangria too. Service was great. Everything I expect in a Kimpton.

“Very nice Hampton Inn and good location” I recently stayed here for business. It was great and about what you would expect with a Hampton Inn. The price and location make this a good bet for the city. The rooms were not huge but it is an old building in a city center so you can't expect huge rooms. The rooms were remodeled with the usual Hampton bedding. The fitness center was terrible but most Hampton's have terrible fitness centers. I had no issue with the staff. In fact I left my cell phone charger and Tanesha sent it to me right away. I did have some colleagues who stayed at the Sheraton about 1/2 a mile away and it was disgusting. The rooms were old and the conference center was awful. So overall if you want a good location and a clean room stay at this Hampton. You are right near the inner harbor and not too far from the Camden Yard.

“Extremely comfortable welcoming” I booked this hotel because of the great reviews. It is all true. The decor is lovely, the beds are really cozy and the fitness room is adequate. Best of all is the welcoming staff that is always available to offer suggestions or provide directions. We also really liked the location.

“Great Location” The hotel is in a fantastic location for the Faneuil Hall restaurants and bars. We found the staff to be most helpful and accommodating. The room was clean and had everything we needed, but could do with a little 'tidy up', ie paintwork and doors. A 10 minute walk gets you to the centre on Boston and to the common which is a great place to start your Boston adventure. There is a fruit and veg market just in front of the hotel, so if you’re a light sleeper you may want a room to the rear of the hotel as they get going at 6am. We didn’t take advantage of the hotel restaurant but did have drinks in the comfortable bar area, which we found to be reasonably priced. All in all this is a great hotel, location and great value.

“Almost boutique in size and scale, great neighborhood” First visit to this part of Boston and the neighborhood is impressive and the hotel is right in the thick of it all with great (but small) rooms at decent rates. No Bistro lobby as found in some suburban Courtyards but a Starbucks is a 4 minute walk away and there are hundreds of restaurants and shops nearby. Flat screen TVs in room is a plus. Rooms have the feel of cramped NY size but unless you are with the family it shouldn't be an issue. The staff was great, friendly and helpful throughout. Construction on a garage across the street starts around 8 a.m. so no sleeping in if you are on front of property, which is most rooms. Historic building is well preserved.

“Solid, dependable choice in Manhattan” I've traveled frequently to NYC for business and have stayed at the Westin Times Square more than 5 times. I'm a SPG member, and try to stay at SPG hotels whenever possible, and I feel that the Westin Times Square (along w/ the W Times Square) is one of the best SPG hotels in the NYC area. The Westin is upscale, clean, and quiet, especially considering it's in the middle of Times Square. To be honest, Times Square is not my favorite, as it's so chaotic, busy, and tourist-ridden. However, the Westin is an oasis in the midst of all the Times Square chaos, and I've found it to be a dependable hotel in NYC, which is why I choose to stay again and again. The rooms are spacious for NYC standards, and comfortable with their Heavenly Beds, good work desk (one of the W hotels I stayed in NYC didn't have a work desk, which I found unacceptable since I was on a business trip), and modern bathrooms. The rooms are also extremely quiet and often have beautiful city views. Most important for me, the rooms I've stayed in are also clean. Hotel cleanliness is one of the most important factors that I consider when choosing an accommodation, and especially in NYC (which is well-known for its bedbug problems). I'd highly recommend this hotel, whether you're going to NYC for business or for pleasure.

“Overpriced and not all it's cracked up to be” The location is great, a trendy uppwe West Side neighborhood, neat restaursants, the park, museums, etc. Staff was pleasant. There is free Wi-Fi throughout. It seemed clean, but the rooms were extremely small, the bathrooms dark and really tiny. The lighting was either overhead glare or insufficient bedstand. The beds were OK with big fluffy duvets. The biggest complaint - $259 plus tax. Had it been $149 it would have been a good value. Otherwise I'd look elsewhere.

“A Hidden Treasure” A very nice moderately priced hotel in the middle of NYC (Times Square). The real hidden treasures are the hot tub rooms. Fully jetted tubs With a TV, an excellent way to relax after a long day of walking around the most amazing city in the world.

“Excellent hotel, excellent location, recommend for all...” I originally booked my stay with Springhill Suites next door (the two hotels are connected and share the same owner), but as they were oversold they upgraded me to a corner suite at the Residence Inn. I originally booked my king room for $99 plus tax (AAA rate), that was for a Saturday night in early March. Overall, I would highly recommend Residence Inn or Springhill Suites next door. This is my go-to hotel stay in the city of Chicago. ROOMS: Very, very nice. The door opens to a long corridor that has a kitchenette with a full sized microwave and fridge, along with two small stove burners. There is a desk/dining table that sits two chairs. This leads into a sitting area with a couch, chair and coffee table/foot-rest directly across from the king bed. Flat screen TV was along one wall. There were plenty of electrical outlets to plug into. Since this was a corner suite, two entire walls had floor to ceiling windows. The rooms are large and clean, and I couldn’t have asked for anything nicer. One note is that the clubs on Hubbard do keep a late-night loud crowd on the street. If you think that might bother you, request an upper floor room. BATHROOMS: Separated by a door into one section for the vanity use, and one for the toilet/shower use. It is a large area to move around. The showers are walk-in and very nice. There is no tub. HOTEL FEATURES: I did not see a restaurant on site, but they do offer a free continental breakfast in the morning. It can get fairly crowded down there, so I did not partake. Note that there is a bagel shop connected to the hotel. I also understand that there is a pool on an upper floor. LOCATION: This is a prime location. It’s at the corner of Hubbard and Dearborn. Hubbard is a great spot for River North restaurants and nightlife. There are so many restaurants and clubs within a SHORT walk I couldn’t even begin to list them, but rest assured you will not be disappointed. Michigan Ave shopping is a brisk walk or short cab ride away. This is a safe and lively area and one of the best places to stay in the city. WHO I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL FOR: Just about every type of traveler. I’m a solo pleasure traveler, and the Springhill/Residence Inn is my go-to stay in the city. I see a lot of families and business travelers as well. I don’t think anyone can go wrong here. HOTEL TIP: AAA members get a good discount at this hotel and Springhill Suites. Also note that this hotel offers free wifi. If you have a portable DVD player, the TV has composite connection on the back. Marriott rewards member are more likely to get upgrades.

“Nice business hotel” in at 4 PM and was given an upgrade to a king room on one of the towers/executive floors. The lobby is very small and in my opinion, uninviting. There are no areas to chat. There is just bascially the front desk and concierge stand. Front desk staff and bellman were very curteous and helpful. parked my car in the adjoining ramp ... self-parking is $16/day and valet is $20/day. The concierge greated me with a big smile when I arrived in the lobby and asked if I needed any help. The service at the front desk seemed somewhat dry and uninterested. If you stay on one of the towers floors, you get a choice of beverage delivered to your room in the AM along with your choice of newspaper. I was very happy to find that I was given a corner room. I'm glad I got this room because even for a corner room, I felt the room was small. I can only imagine what the other rooms are like. Ask for rooms that end in XX12 as these are the largest rooms on the floor according to the floor layout on the door. The bed was very comfortable and contained Hilton's new Serta bedding package. There was a robe and upgraded products in the bathroom. Wired and wireless high-speed internet are available in the room .. it is complimetary if you are staying on one of the exec floors. In order to use the wireless net, you need to call down to the front desk and receive an access code. I found the wireless net to be very slow and drop numerous connections. For best reception, you need to use your computer towards the center of the room. I also tried using the wired high-speed net, however the connection was not working. Since I didn't need to use the net an extensive amount, I decided not to call the front desk. I felt the exec lounge was ok. Evening hou'douvers (served from 5-8) consisted of teriyaki steak strips and various cheeses and crackers. There are also plenty of complimentary soft-drinks to select from. When I was there on a weekend, the bar was manged by the concierge. Alcoholic drinks are charged to the room. There is a few nice leather couches and some tables, but overall the lounge is not big by any means. There is also a good selection of magazines and CDs (the exec rooms have the Hilton alarm clocks with CD players). The late night offerings (8-11) consisted of fruits and cookies. I checked out early the next day, and did not have a chance to go to the lounge for breakfast. I must agree with a previous poster who stated that this lounge seemed lackluster compared to other lounges. I ordered room service that night and found the food to be very excellent. 24 hour room service is available. I also heard the sunday brunch in the restaurant is one of the top brunches in the Charlotte area. The hotel is connected to small plaza which contains small shops and a gift shop. I did not have time to explore this area, so I'm not sure exactly what types of stores were there. A few other words of advice .. when checking in, I was not asked if I parked my own car, so I needed to go down to the desk later that night and receive a parking permit. My room did have a mini-bar, however I was not given the key and needed to stop at the front desk for this as well. I was told that the hotel is removing the mini-bars from all the rooms due to discrepencies in billing. Only a few rooms still had them. They are probably not necessary if you have access to the lounge. Also, turndown service is available on the exec floors. However, you need to call the front desk and request this service. I was not told this upon checking in. I didn't realize this until it was too late in the evening. Would I stay here again .. probably. The weekend rates are great (I payed $89 dollars for my upgraded room). However, I felt the service and quality of the rooms were must better at the HGI and for what you get for what you pay for during the week, you'd probably be getting a better deal at the HGI.

“Noise from new restaurant” Choose this as thought it was away from the noise of Times Square. However, a new restaurant around the corner, 157 Lafayette apparently opened up. It is more of a club with a live DJ playing loud music through the night. Complained but management couldnt do anything. Make sure you dont get a room facing the back or you will need ear plugs to sleep. Otherwise it is a nice small room.

“Alcuni punti di debolezza. Molti punti di forza.” - POSIZIONE OTTIMA. L'hotel si trova in pieno centro a New York (Midtown) e a circa 100 metri da diverse linee delle metropolitana, tra le quali la linea E che collega direttamente con l'Air Train dell'aeroporto JFK. - PERSONALE CORTESE E PREPARATO. Il personale è davvero cortese e preparato. Cerca di venire incontro alla esigenze della clientela con stile e cortesia. Meno brillante il personale del concierge che sembra più interessato a consigliare locali/servizi dei conoscenti piuttosto che a dare informazioni realmente oneste. - CAMERE CARINE, MA CON QUALCHE LIMITE. Le camere sono carine e i bagni adeguati a un 4 stelle. Ottimi i materassi e i piumoni. Unica punta dolente la scarsa insonorizzazione delle stanze. Nelle camere ai piani bassi sembra di essere per strada. Alcune camere hanno poi problemi con il riscaldamento, aspetto che in una città come NY è tutt'altro che secondario. Nelle stanza sarebbe bello avere qualche gadget in più (in particolare le pantofole). - PREZZO MEDIO. Il prezzo non è basso, ma è comunque adeguato alla struttura, alla posizione, al servizio e alla città (una delle più costose al mondo per quanto concerne gli alloggi). - SERVIZI MEDI. L'hotel dispone di una palestra carina (non eccezionale). Mancano sauna, piscina e servizi più evoluti. Ottimo il ristorante interno.

“Are you kidding?” My corporation booked this hotel for me at my request, as I refused to stay at the standard "Hilton Garden Inn" when I knew Omni Hotels were amongst our preferred. What a mistake. PROS: -There is a restaurant/bar onsite...but good luck finding any servers. -It's in downtown Jacksonville with shops and restaurants across the street. CONS: - Most rooms have terrible views, including overlooking a large parking lot. - There are extremely few ammenities (no minibars, no good cable, etc). - The rooms were dingy, smelly and dirty. I slept on top of the sheets for 4 nights and didn't get anywhere near the comforter. - I had to explain to the waitress in the restaurant (after waiting a good 15 minutes for service at peak lunch hour) what a Pellegrino was...she thought it was a beer. Granted, this is Jacksonville. You aren't going to find any true four or five-star hotels here. But my coworkers who stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn I declined had much nicer, cleaner accommodations.

“Very Nice Choice” The Memphis Marriott is an excellent hotel for business or vacation. I requested and received a newer renovated room in the North Tower. Staff was very friendly, accommodating and helpful on check in. Beds and bedding were very nice and comfortable. Curtains and carpet could stand to be updated. Also would be nice to have a mini fridge in the room. Bathroom nice also, tub good sized and shower head great. Housekeeping was friendly but not the most detail oriented. Trolley stop right in front of hotel. Not sure where the noise was coming from but it was a bit noisy. Breakfast buffet had nice selection but considering it wasn't that tasty I thought the $15 was a bit steep. The bar had reasonably priced selections but service was very slow. Overall, I enjoyed my stay and would stay there again.

“Great stay!” My family of four (husband and 11-year old twin girls) stayed at the Nikko for 4 nights. I had booked an Imperial floor room with two queen beds both for the space and the amenities. Had read reviews about tiny rooms, etc. When we arrived we were offered an upgrade to Imperial Executive Suite for an additional $50 a night. We went for it and were glad we did. The Imperial Executive Suite on the 22nd floor had big windows with a nice view, two queen beds in the bedroom, a living area separated by a partial wall, a large bathroom, a half bath, two televisions, hallway... not huge but lots of space. Beds were very comfortable with lovely bedding, bathrooms were great-- Furniture was otherwise a bit tired as was the carpet. But the room was perfect for us and very, very quiet. We slept really well-- not a sound from the hall or from other rooms. We really like the included buffet breakfast at ANZU --since we had coupons for two people for each day, we had breakfast there twice with all four of us. The other two days we had nice continental breakfast in the Imperial Lounge which was also included. We enjoyed the 5-7pm wine and hors d'ouevres in the Imperial Lounge. And we especially loved the large indoor pool, hot tub and locker rooms with saunas and steam rooms. This, along with free wi-fi was all part of the Imperial package. Our rate wasn't cheap, but nor was it particularly high considering all that was included--We paid around $250 a night. A splurge for us, but worth it particularly given the reviews for other rooms in the hotel. We had a great stay!

“Great hotel, convernient location, incredible price” I had never stayed here, and in searching the Marriott website, saw that there was a rate of $203., if cancelled by the day before. This is haf the price of the typical Manhattand full price room, especially booked with short notice. The hotel is ideally located, a few blocks from Times Square, Grand Central, etc., but far enough away to be quiter and calmer. The front desk staff was friendly, and there is a concierge, almost a necessity in NY, who was helpful and knowledgeable. The room was spacious (you might forget you were in Manhattan) and modern. Only the expected hotel noises of a toilet flushing, etc. The wireless internet was among the speediest that I have found in a hotel. Paul Mitchell toiletries. An added bonus was the free continental breakfast. Cereal, yogurt, fruit, bread and pastries, perfect, if a bit crowded. I can't imagine that this is the usual price, but in any case I will be back!

“Perfection!” I'm a fairly harsh critic but I have nothing bad to say about this hotel. The decor was chic, the staff were efficient and helpful, the rooms were spacious and comfortable, and the location was ideal. Definitely felt like an upscale experience at a reasonable price. I was motivated to join the Kimptom loyalty program after my stay here, as I plan to try other Kimptom hotels more frequently!

“Great Place” We were in Seattle for a wedding. In addition to my family of four, my extended family took up at least 6 more rooms. We had a room with two queen beds and there was plenty of space for us and our children (ages 11 & 3). The room was clean and having a microwave and refrigerator in our room was great for the kids. It was also very easy to get around in the hotel. I didn't have to worry about my 11 year old getting lost trying to run back up to our room to get something. The staff was terrific and friendly. The shuttle service was a great way to get around to the fun places without a car and the shuttle drivers were super friendly (particularly Monica). We were able to get everywhere we had wanted to go using the shuttle. It was also nice to have free internet access down in the lobby. The breakfast was convenient and my kids loved making their own waffles! The food at Cayenne was fine and the people who worked there were really friendly. The only complaint I have for our entire trip was Cayenne's inability to divide checks at least by table (I understand not wanting to manage 20 single person checks). However, making us do the work of working out payment from 20 people was more frustrating to us than it would have been for them to divide the group in to the four tables we took up. This was the only not-customer oriented experience we had on our trip. I would suggest they change that policy and I'm also guessing that their tips would be better broken out in to smaller checks. Other than that, it was our first trip to Seattle and we had a wonderful time. We will definately stay at the Silver Cloud Hotel again. Thanks.

“Lovely Boutique in Very Convenient Location” I stayed at this hotel for three nights in April, and really enjoyed the experience. The theme is old library, each floor is a specific "section" of the library, e.g. Literature, and each room, a specific genre for that section (e.g. "Classics"). The hotel is elegant and sophisticaed, without trying too hard to be cool or trendy. The service is top notch, there is an amazing top floor with two outdoor seating areas, and an enclosed solarium type area, for drinks, appetizers, or dinner in the evenings, with really fantastic views. Beds were comfortable with upscale linens, I did not hear a sound in the evenings. And, very clean! I had free breakfasts as well as happy hour drinks and snacks, and internet. Coffee and tea available all day/night. They offer a free DVD lending library with a huge selection of titles. I would definitely stay here again. Would be great for romantic get away, but is not set up for families.

“Great location, great staff and always comfortable beds!!!!” From Check in until check out the staff was very accommodating. I had to store some frozen food in the freezer for our trade show and the Chef Patrick was so helpful and made sure that we were taken care of. He was great. The rest of the staff was also nice. The location is great, right on Michigan ave near shopping restaurants and Rush street. Great place to stay for business or pleasure.

“Nice hotel in good location” I'm a frequent traveller to NYC and just needed a hotel to stay in for 2 nights. The Shoreham was conveniently located: not too far from Grand Central or from the 4,5,6 subway line. Check in was easy- we were an hour early so we had to leave our luggage and come back, I do wish they'd have been able to give us our room at 2:00 instead of 3:00, but it wasn't that big of a deal. The hotel was nice, clean, modern, and minimalistic. The room was small (but that is very common in NYC) and there was no counter space in the bathroom. But other than that, the room was very nice. I would recommend this hotel for anyone wanting a nice hotel in a convenient location. My only real issue came at check-out, whenwe were told that we had taken stuff from the mini-bar, which we hadn't. After we explained that, the charge was taken off. Also, when you are in your room, keep the Do Not Disturd notice on your door, otherwise there is always someone knocking. It's hard to take a nap that way.

“Excellent hotel for conference” Stayed here for 3 nights whilst at a conference at the hotel. I must say the level of service is beyond what I usually experience in the US. All the staff are genuninely pleasant and seem very willing to go the extra mile. The rooms are extremely well appointed. A test I usually apply to seperate the great hotels from the average ones is if there is shower gel provided in the bathroom. And there was! Along with toothpaste in every room! I slept incredibly well on the large comfy bed. The best experience however was the food for the conference. It was superb. Very varied and very, very welll cooked / presented. Only gripes were that the desk in the bedroom had no easy to use power socket and they charged me $15 to use the 'business center' to print of 4 reports. However at $180 a night this place was an absolute bargain (conference rate). I would not hesitate coming back here for pleasure or business. The onsite Starbucks was a bonus as was the small NYC cafe (cheaper than the hotel breakfast). I didnt use the ruth and chris steakhouse but it looked very good. All in all 5 star.

“A very elegant, refined property in Central Park” The hotel has really shown vast improvement in every area. My (basic) room was spacious, immaculate, and luxurious right from the enormous flat screen tv down to the absolute comfort of the linens. Service was impeccable (especially Fatima at check-in and the whole crew of doormen.) The location is unbeatable---near lovely Central Park and the best dining in all of Manhattan. This was my 5th visit and by far the best. It was a flawless stay and I can't wait to return. Truly a 5 Star experience! Well done.

“An all-around disappointment” I booked this hotel for a short overnight leisure trip with my family (my husband and two children under the age of four). We enjoy staying in suite hotels that offer 2 bedrooms since it allows our children to sleep comfortably while my husband and I can stay up and watch television. When I looked at the available rooms at this property, I was shown "2 Bedroom Penthouse." I called the hotel directly to ask about the room and was told that it was a loft. The living room and one bedroom were located downstairs while the second bed was in a loft space that opened down to the living area. The woman with whom I spoke at the hotel assured me that the downstairs bedroom had a door that closed it off from the living room. I requested an early check-in at the hotel, but when I arrived at 1:00 p.m. I was told that my room wasn't ready. The reception also suggested that I return at 3:00. The reality was that the room WAS ready but hadn't yet been inspected. As I stood at the desk staring daggers at the receptionist, she made it a point to continually check back with the housekeeping supervisor to find out if the room was inspected and if it was ready. I waited for about 15 minutes before the receptionist confirmed that the room was ready and that she could check me in. When I arrived at the room I found that the downstairs bedroom did NOT close off from the living area. In addition, the air conditioner wasn't working properly. My husband reported the air conditioning problem to the front desk and someone came to look at it immediately. Thirty minutes later, just as we were leaving to go to dinner, the front desk called to let us know that they would be moving us to another room. After dinner my husband went to the desk to get a key to our new room and expressed his displeasure with the fact that we had been told that the downstairs bedroom had a door. It turns out that the penthouses in the main building do have doors but that the penthouses in the adjacent townhouses do not. We were given a discount on the room, but that didn't mean that my children slept any better. This is obviously an old property and shows a lot of wear and tear. My husband and I both described it as "junky." There are two other issues with this hotel. The first is that it backs up to a train track and I listened to trains all night long. The second is that it allows pets and I had to listen to the yippy dog below me all night long. I will be sticking with Holiday Inn's Staybridge Suites or Hilton's Homewood Suites, but I will never again stay at a Residence Inn.

“Excellent for business travel, great location, concierge disappointing” Spent six days in October for a conference, where due to weather I was stranded a couple extra days. The hotel accommodated my unexpected delay and I did not have to worry about making other arrangements. This property is enormous. I had a room on the 8th floor of the South Tower, no view, but still I liked the huge windows and the well-appointed room. Not as nice as some of my favorite Westins, but the location makes up for any deficiency. The staff was helpful and kind, and truly you can walk or take the light rail almost anywhere in minutes. I walked to Pike Place, the Space Needle, shopping and restaurants. Despite the terrible weather, I didn't care! What a really great city. Basic gym, decent pool and spa. Meeting space is very good, but needs some TLC. Temp was very good! Lobby bar and meet up space decent. Breakfast buffet acceptable, but pricey. Mini bar, coffee maker, robe on request. Great, reliable Westin beds. Great sleeping. However, beware to not get a room near the elevator or ice machine, way too noisy. They re-roomed me immediately once I realized this. I am irritated by a lazy concierge or one that assumes the lowest common denominator. We asked for good asian, thai, vietnamese nearby and the guy sent us to the Thai Ginger in the mall. Here's my opinion, and the opinion of every other weary traveler, if we ask you for a recommendation and you can't think of anything but the mall, say so. I would rather use Yelp.
“Packed” I've never seen a hotel so overrun with warm bodies. It was like walking through Disney. Crowded. Expensive. The room was nice. But not for the $200 I paid. Will not stay here again.

“Style over substance” A friend suggested we stay at the Palomar because of its location and restaurant. This has put a strain on our friendship. The Kimpton Group, which manages the Palomar, must believe that style is the only thing needed to satisfy its customers. The front desk staff was less than helpful on virtual every request. Don’t bother with the concierge they never return your calls. The coffee being served in Styrofoam cups in the lobby was a nice touch. I can accept a high price for a very small room if it is accompanied by good customer service. That was not the case at the Palomar.

“Go for the drinks but not the room” Just a big party - if you are under 30, get drunk and have fun and don't mind passing out on the floor. The rooms are TINY and rarely cleaned. This is not for adults, especially as service is non existent. Seems popular enough so they probably won't care about this review but in a city like NYC there are too many other good choices.

“Das schönste Stadthotel bisher” Nach einer österlichen Tour kehrten wir von Arizona kommend zum Ausklang der Reise im St. Regis, New York, ein. Dies ist wahrlich das schönste Stadte-Hotel in dem wir je gewesen sind. 1903 erbaut ist das Haus in diesem prachtvollen Stil erhalten und man hat den Eindruck, daß alles gerade eben erst renoviert und gestrichen worden ist. Dies ist wohl nicht der Fall. Der Service ist sensationell. Der private Butler - in Livree - auf unaufdringliche Art stets zur Hand. Die Zimmermädchen tragen schwarze Kleider mit weißen Schürzchen und Häubchen. Faszinierend wie die riesenhaften Blumen- bzw. Sträucher-Arrangements im Speisesaal und in der Halle plötzlich am nächsten Morgen ausgetauscht waren ohne die geringsten Spuren zu hinterlassen. Der Concierge bemühte sich unendlich für uns noch Karten zu einem völlig ausgebuchten Event zu erhalten, die mein Mann von zuhause aus nicht hatte buchen können. Letztlich gelang ihm das sogar, aber der Preis von $ 500,-- für mindere Plätze war uns dann doch zu teuer. Zum Glück hat New York ja jede Menge Alternativen. Den Geburtstag meines Mannes feierten wir im Restaurant des 3 Sterne-Kochs Becasse, das dem Hotel angegliedert ist. Auch hier gab es nicht den Hauch einer Beanstandung. (Sieht man von einer Gruppe Chinesen ab, die teilweise in T-Shirts gekleidet waren). Zum Nachtisch gab es ein Extra-Dessert vom untröstlichen Consierge, weil er uns nicht die richtigen Karten besorgen konnte. Das Hotel hat eine sensationelle Bar - die "Nat King Cole Bar" - in welcher angeblich die "Bloody Mary" erfunden wurde. Die Rückwand der Theke wird von einem witzigen Gemälde geziert, das "Old King Cole" auf einem Thron zeigt. New York hatten wir fast immer um die Weihnachtszeit besucht. Diesmal gelang ein Spaziergang durch den Central Park. Der Besuch von "Ground Zero" fiel aus, weil an diesem Tag Präsident Obama dort eine Rede hielt. Aber New York ist ja immer wieder eine Reise wert.

“All the right stuff” From the large, spacious guest room, to the 27th floor bar, this Hyatt is one of my favorites. The room desk was large with a second table on wheels, there were plenty of plugs for electronics, and even a window that opened. The bed was comfortable, linens and towels first rate. The bath was spacious and well equipped. There is internet, but also a charge for it. Overnight self parking is $25. The fitness center is large and well equipped. Plenty of cardio machines, free weights and weight machines, all clean and well maintained. It is next to the pool, and the entire area has plenty of daylight. This is a good downtown location, across from the convention center and one block up from the 16th ST Mall. Access by car is easy after a 23 mile ride form the airport. The room amenities, air conditioning, linens, etc all were up to Hyatt standards, which is to say quite nice. Elevators from the high floors are fast, so ask for a room with a view. The lobby is tall, airy, and well decorated. There is a coffee shop and restaurant.

“Great Hotel For People on the Go” This hotel is good for someone on the go. Its not an amazing hotel by any stretch of the imagination. Its in a good area for getting anywhere in NYC...close to the tube. The room is very small, the staff is friendly, and the lobby looks really ghetto. We had a problem with noise one of the nights we stayed here, because there is a club downstairs. However, the other nights we stayed here, we went out on the town, so it was not a problem. If you want a hotel that takes great care of you...stay somewhere else. But, if you like to roam the city, and won't spend much time in your room...definitely stay here and save some money.

“Deeply Disappointing - Not For Business At All” I have stayed at this hotel many times over the past several years - with excellent experiences every time - until last week. I felt like I had checked in to a dirty discount tourist trap. The hotel was loud, filled with wet towels, dirty floors, loud children, terrible wireless internet and extraordinarily slow elevators. The maintenance man advised that all of that was due to the large number of families with children who had come to swim in the pools. Kids playing in the elevators. Their gaming on the wireless slowed it to a crawl. I have hosted large business meetings in this hotel in the past with great success. Unless there is a radical change, I'll never do that again. I recommend that the Omni pull this franchise until this situation is fully remedied. A very helpful staff seemed to know all about these problems, but not empowered to do anything to cure them.

“Understated and friendly” We stayed for three nights. At first the decor and darkness are a little offputting, but the service is incredibly friendly without being smarmy. Our rooms were quiet and comfortable and the kids loved their twin room. Wifi is good. Whatever time you turn up in the bar (even if it's not during the wine hour), as a guest you're offered a free glass of house wine which we appreciated. We ate in the bar one evening as well and had great food - nothing fancy, but very well executed. The barstaff and front desk staff were all delightful. I would stay here again - it's central, comfortable and quiet.

“What a Mess!” I travel often and am a Hilton Gold HHonors member for many years. I know hotels well and this hotel is a total failure when it comes to service. I had to wait for a room to be readied despite arriving after 4 p.m, then was given a small Queen room instead of the King I booked. When I called the desk no one answered. So, check in was bad. The room lacked many advertised amenities. No Robe, no Frette linens. The continental breakfast featured unripe and unedible fruit. White bread was the only option and was too big for the small toaster. Juice was not fresh. The "Executive" level is worthless. No one answered when room service was called. Eventually the front desk picked up and took my order. Needless to say, it was lost. When we finally did get our food, much later, the chef brought it up as they were understaffed. He did not know how to serve and forgot improtant items. The food was awful, not suprising as the Chef is delivering food. I called the front desk after the room service trouble, they said the manager would be in touch the next morning. He never called. No one answers the phones here. The morning paper never arrived. When I went to the Front Desk the next day to get change to tip the valet they had none! 11 a.m. on a workday and the Hotel cant even break a $20.00. This Hotel failed from check in to check out. This would be a bad experience for anyone. Being of a frequent guest of Hilton Hotels it was twice as frustrating for me. Almost every staff member I spoke too said they were "slammed" or "understaffed." I checked out early and moved to the absolutly excellent Omni next door. I have stayed at many Hiltons over the years and this is one of the worst based on price for value. By the way, I wrote the manager a letter of complaint and never got a response. Not a surprise really. There are many better hotels in this higher price range in San Diego.

“Great Westin property in Philly” I stayed in an executive suite for a one night and was fairly impressed. The building itself is a former Ritz-Carlton location and still has much of the original hardware including the marble bathrooms. Newer Westin furniture and bedding has been added over the years and everything fits together quite well. I had mixed encounters with the front desk staff but overall they seem to be doing a good job and provided everything I needed throughout my stay. A small fitness center located on the fifth floor offers Life Fitness treadmills, ellipticals, recumbent bike, multifunction tower and dumbbells. The hotel is conveniently located to area attractions, offices, shopping, and restaurants. Will stay again when next in Philadelphia.

“Cannot wait to return! Spectacular resort!” I cannot say enough about this resort. I thoroughly researched destination spas within the US and it came down to two, Lake Austin and one in Tucson. I was sold on Lake Austin the minute I called to check availability and the coordinator was so friendly and helpful! That was so different from the experience I had when I had called the other resort and was placed on hold for 15 minutes and then rushed off the line. Grrrrrr! This resort is spectacular...rooms are clean, homey yet modern, and spacious. I thoroughly enjoyed sitting on my front porch at night reading (with the resident cats). I also loved my private, serene garden out back...complete with a tranquil fountain. The food was amazing (spa portions, for sure ;), classes were revitalizing, and spa treatments surpassed my expectations. Visiting in February proved to be chilly, so outdoor pools and paddleboarding were not options. The staff was so accommodating. I visited over Super Bowl weekend and being a diehard NYGiants fan, was intent on watching the game in a relaxing atmosphere. I felt like I was watching the game at home with family and friends. It truly does not get any better than this. I was so excited to become a Monarch Club member because I will be back!

“Great Winter Weekend Getaway” This review is several months overdue, but my husband and I visited the Ritz Carlton in January for our 7th anniversary weekend. From the moment we checked in, we received nothing but the best of service. We were upgraded to a very large suite (with a TV in the bathroom, no less) and received congratulatory chocolates and a card a few minutes after getting into the room. Our rate included club floor access, which was fantastic. We joked that the next time we stayed there, we'd just take all of our meals on the club floor. Since it was wintertime, and a weekend...it wasn't busy at all. We were big fans of the dessert presentation and champagne every evening, and the actual club lounge was well appointed and - comfortable. The valets were of great help grabbing a taxi for us when the McKinney Avenue Trolley failed to show up, after waiting for 30+ minutes across the street. One evening we had drinks in the lobby bar outside Fearing's and were treated to free samples of guacamole and Fearing's signature prickly pear margarita. I have avoided tequila like the plague since I was 23, but even I could say it was an outstanding margarita. It has taken us eight months, but we're finally getting around to actually dining at Fearing's next weekend. The hotel had only been open for a couple of months when we stayed there, and I didn't feel hardly any of the "growing pains" the Dallas area has been susceptible to with all of the new hotel openings. I found the RC employees to be friendly and helpful, and they were even the inspiration for three papers in one of my MBA Marketing courses that semester.

“Incredible hotel” Spent two nights here with wife and two sons (7 and 4) during business/vacation trip. This place is wonderful. The staff at the front desk and restaurant were friendly, very good at their jobs, and genuinely nice people. Maria in the restaurant is an angel - a true joy to see first thing in the morning. Fortunately, we were not her due to medical reasons, like many of the other guests, due to proximity to hospitals. But if we were, I would have been very comfortable. The room was very comfortable - nice bed, everything clean and in good working order. If you don't care for the restaurant (which was fine for the meals we had there), there are a Pizza Hut and Burger King in the parking lot - very convenient. The pool was large and fun for the entire family. There is a Metrorail stop relatively close by, though we didn't use it. It can get you to downtown without having to drive. The elevators can be a bit slow, and parking can be a problem (though never was for us) if the lot gets too full. If you have young children, be sure to check out the Children's Museum (not very far to the north). Our kids loved it so much, we went back a second day. You may have reciprocal admission privelages with your local museum membership. Internet service worked well. There is a business center with a couple of computers on the first floor. I would definitely stay in this hotel again, especially if I needed to be in the Medical District, Museum District, or close to Rice University.

“Gorgeous hotel but customer service is lacking” WIth some re-thinking of its customer service approach, this hotel could easily go from just OK to excellent. The facilities are by far the high point. Our room was spacious, clean, attractive, and modern with comfortable beds. The bathroom was larger than expected, well-lit, and very tastefully decorated, with a Heavenly Shower that lived up to its name. The hotel lobby is active, beautifully decorated, and welcoming, with lots of places to sit and enjoy the natural light coming in through the large lobby windows. We worked out at the gym and found it to be well-equipped for our needs. The indoor pool is next door to the gym, and the guests we saw swimming (mostly families) seemed to be enjoying themselves. Though the location appears to be in a growing part of the city that is being renovated -- lots of construction in the area -- we didn't find it to be an unappealing location. There are some decent restaurants within walking distance, and a reasonable cab ride took us to Fenway (we were in the city to see a game there). It would probably be a less appealing location for folks who wish to do lots of walking to plentiful retail outlets and fun tourist attractions. To us, the unappealing part of the hotel was something some other folks have referenced in their reviews -- the lack of "can-do" attitudes and customer service-focus in some of the employees. The restaurant is a good example -- it offers a breakfast buffet which is fairly tasty (but not cheap), but, alas, both days that we ate there, we noticed that there just weren't enough servers for all the tables and very few workers bussing tables. Tables sat with huge piles of plates on them for periods of 20 minutes or longer while other diners patiently waited for seating. Other tables remained empty altogether for long periods of time (maybe the staffing for those tables was not available?). However, the hostess stand was packed with people eager to eat (we noticed about 50 people, in addition to us, waiting to get in the restaurant, and that size crowd continued the whole time we ate). Some were frustrated that they had been told the wait was 15 minutes then had to wait 30-45 minutes. Some people left before their parties were called for seating. Meanwhile, I saw two restaurants employees in the dining room reading magazines and looking bored while guests buzzed about them, looking for help (maybe the employees were on break, but they were burning time in plain view of all the guests -- not very professional looking on break or not on break). Both mornings in the restaurant we saw these same kinds of sights. We wondered aloud how much more money the restaurant would be making with some new management on the scene and theorized that it would be a huge increase in revenue with some new direction. The whole scene just lacked efficiency and direction on the management front. The servers looked frustrated and harried. We also encountered the lack of customer service approach when it came to things like valet service, waiting about 35 minutes to get our car. When we asked two other employees out front if they could please help us track down our car, they all seemed to want to try to avoid doing any additional work. No one said they would check on it for us and see if the car had been picked up yet. Instead, they all said, "I'm sure it's on the way," and declined to take any responsibility for researching the situation. That was frustrating, as we had flights to catch and the time window was getting tighter and tighter, particularly for my flight, as we waited. I ended up bailing out and got a cab to the airport, due to time panic, and my friends continued to wait for the car. (I did make my flight, which was good! :) ) We did encounter an especially friendly, attentive bartender (I wish I had gotten his name) who seemed to take pride in his job and made us feel valued as customers. But I can't recall another employee who was as customer-service oriented. It's such a beautiful hotel -- it's a shame that the staffing/management part of things isn't as good as the facilities. I think we'll choose another hotel in Boston next time. BTW - I noticed long check-in lines as we were heading out. :(

“Great place to stay near the airport” First time stay at this hotel near the airport. I usually stay at a competing large chain down the road. This place is nicer. The interior seems to have been newly decorated. The furniture is retro hip, with lots of places to sit in the lobby. The bar and restaurant were really busy, and pretty good actually. WiFi was free and pretty reliable. Service was good. Parking was complicated, as the hotel self park lot is not well marked. Keep going straight past the hotel and park behind it for $11 a day, otherwise, prepare to pay valet rates which are more than double that. Bed was really comfortable. Bathroom was standard, these need renovating next. I would definitely stay here again. Also, there is a free shuttle to the airport, which is an easy walk if you don't have too much luggage.

“excellent location for stopping in Philadelphia” stopped with three friends (in two rooms) for 2 nights early May. Both rooms were twin rooms with ample space and ensuite bathroom. We basically used this as a base, as we were out all day and night (at night watching baseball). Excellent location, right in the middle of town, handy for the underground. There is an underground parking lot opposite underneath a shopping complex, the hotel will give a discount on the parking. For the limited time we were there, we had no problems with anything in the hotel.

“Average. Depends what you are looking for.” This is a hard one to write. If someone had recommended this place to me, I would have wondered what they were smo***, I mean thinking. It really, really depends what you are looking for. New and fancy? NO. Clean and sparkly? NO. Cool and funky? NO. Huge room? Yes. Huge bathroom? Not even close. Good price? Yes. Decor from the 70s? Formica counters? Couch from 1965? Yes. They are friendly here. The service is very good. The elevators are scary. The carpet is in bad shape. The bathroom floor is 1" mosaic tile. The lighting is not bad. The desk is adequate. The room is HUGE for New York. The area is interesting, and safe, and fairly centrally located. The price is fair. Hope this helps.

“A nicer inner city Marriott” Stayed 4 nights for a convention in October. The palce is 2 blocks from the ball park, a good 15 minute walk to the convention center, and a good 30 minute walk to the ESPN Zone at the inner harbor, The staff was professional and attentitive. There is a sports bar therein with a number of TVs which makes for good Sunday football viewing. The rooms are what you would expect at a Marriott. I have only two complaints: 1- right next to a fire station and being in the city that means sirens more often that I'd like. 2- The bell men were overly agressive in my opinion. I'd think twice about staying here again due to the fire station, if same will not bother you- then I recommend the property.

“Perfect location for the waterfront” We've stayed here on a number of visits to San Francisco and it does the job well. The rooms are spacious and clean, though a little dated. The facilities are good in the rooms not that you'll like spend much time in them. The beds are comfy and we slept well during our stays. The bathrooms are basic but clean and have a good shower. The breakfast buffet is pretty gruesome in terms of quality of food and selection but you get used to picking through and finding something. I couldn't eat like this everyday though - it's kind of what you expect in the US but coming from the EU it was really far from what we were used to being served, particularly from a quality point of view... The hotel location is perfect for the waterfront in that you can be by the water in a few minutes walk. There are plenty of bars near by but generally its better to head into North Beach for food since the water front is exactly what you normally get where tourists are found; expensive and inedible. The hotel is also very close to the drop off and pick up for the city tour. One of the nice features of the hotel was that having rented a bike for 24hrs, they hotel happily let me store it in our room over night so I could use it the following day. This was unexpected but very appreciated. They were also pretty good with getting us cabs and an airport limo etc. The hotel is definitely overprice for what it is but so are all the hotels in this location. Overall we have always had a good stay here and I'd recommend it to others.

“Great location, great lobby, ehh on the room” Perhaps industrial minimalist is your thing... then LPM is your hotel. Ive been looking forward to staying here for quite some time. Business and opportunity brought me here at fairly decent corporate rate - still it was slightly disappointing. And the opportunity to get an upgraded room is probably nil since its a common known fact that most biz travelers have the SPG Am3x card.The fact that biz travelers prefer SPG properties is going to hinder your chances at getting that upgrade or prime corner room, etc. I got a room with a shared door... first couple of days was fine... I think the person next to me was playing in the US Open?! I noticed a US Open limo waiting outside as a cart was being taken from the room with a huge tennis racquet bag... and then the problem occurred. A fairly loud couple moved in the following day. Lucky enough they sleep pretty early and I didnt hear a peep after 11pm. However, my preference was for a quiet room -- which the receptionist seemed to obliged with a room away from the elevator and away from ice machine. But shared door aside... Pros: Modern room Lack of huge furniture pieces made the room seem pretty big for NY standards Clean, lovely cleaning staff Great lobby and entrance, bar area and burger joint (slightly hidden - didnt go but heard positive reviews) TV is massive at prob 46" desk is great set against window...love that however, my room faced hilton club... with windows looking back... great for working not great for "browsing" NY sky line location is fantastic... near Central Park, but a bit of drive to hot spot restaurants in lower Manhattan... but far away from time square to give you some peace. duane reades and chase banks nearby... Fifth Ave shops one street down... great location all around Cons: felt underwhelming relative to expectations modern as in minimalist industrial cold feel... probably not my think... although i like 'modern' wifi is $17 per connection, thats right per connection, although that might be the norm around here (not sure if you can swap the 'registered' connection to dif PC/tablet/smartphone) bathroom pretty small shaving razor is $7; how about free? is that too much to ask Is there a lobby to relax? not sure... wasnt told or invited gym, $10, i suppose thats not awfully outrageous... not sure is thats entirely common here just not much to warrant an immediate return... as i type from another NY hotel room which is tiny compared to LPM but fantastically designed... review to come. Ordered room service several times... its good food... pizza is good, breakfast is great... prices are high. couldnt get the bill under $50/meal... might have been worth it to go downstairs in the restaurant. Summary... great location, great size, good layout, ok feel. New York is expensive.. your expectations should be as well.

“Perfection” I love this hotel. I love it so much I would live here if I could afford to... and I'm a hotel owner! The design is superb, the grounds and pool sexy beyond belie,f and the charming staff complete the picture. This place is just brilliant. Worth a trip to Austin to experience.

“Inesquecivel” Vale a pena ir a San Francisco e ficar no Intercontinental.O hotel é lindo, tudo funciona bem, tem segurança, o quarto é bem grande , confortavel, uma vista maravilhosa (dá para ver até o nascer do sol), o banheiro bem equipado,grande e com secador ótimo, diferente dos de parede usados em alguns hotéis mais antigos. Tive atendimento excelente desde a reserva , feita com Jennifer Gabriel, que foi super atenciosa e gentil, até o atendimento no valet, front desk , boas vindas e garçon do restaurante.O café da manhã tem um buffet caprichado e gostoso.A piscina e Jacuzi são uma delícia, assim como os roupões colocados no quarto.A localização é boa e o quarto silencioso, com um blackout muito eficiente.Foi uma experiencia maravilhosa para minha família.

“FOODIES REJOICE!” The Marriott Downtown is a wonderful property, and it's appeal is accentuated by what lies across the street...Reading Terminal Market. The hotel is updated, and very well maintained. The lobby is beautiful and impressive with loads of seating available. The rooms are clean, beds very comfortable, the baths are beautiful and well stocked. As said before the location can't be beat, it is central to almost everything.
