The staff was very professional and accommodating. The Bell captain even used his personal charger to charge my daughters i phone, when she left hers at home. The true gem for your inner foodie is the Reading Terminal Market across 12th. St. A huge train station revamped and stuffed, and I mean stuffed with local food vendors...both the eat in and take a way types. Anything local to the Eastern Seaboard, and Pennsylvania is represented. Seafood and meat, cheese, produce, bakery... Overall a wonderful experience!

“Right in the Middle of it All” The best part about this hotel is the view. You know it from the moment you take the elevator to the lobby. The only problem I've ever had is a wait at the check in desk, and a lack of SUV cabs (we had 5 in our party). The location is prime for anyone visiting the city but the hotel is professional and perfect for a business stay. Close enough to walk to Carmine's or ToysRUS, and yet high enough to miss the car horns and bustle of the city. From one side, we saw the Christmassy Empire State Building. Another side gave us a birds eye view of the street. You can walk to Dwayne Reed's for any travel necessities and you're across the street from about 5 different fast food, quick service, or sit down restaurants. Perfect for winter nights when you stay inside as long as possible. The staff is friendly and the rooms are spacious. What can I say...I wouldn't stay anywhere else!

“Interior left me cold” Atrium interior design means that probably close to half the rooms at this hotel have only interior views. We had one of the interior views. Even on a sunny day at noontime we needed every light in the room on in order to do any work/reading. The atrium interior "greenery" is all fake. Restaurant seemed moderately overpriced, e.g.breakfast buffet was $19. There is a Starbucks on site as an alternative however, especially for those not here on an expense account. Reception was slightly stiff, a little too proper for us. If not Platinum or Diamond with Gold Passport, be prepared to pay for internet access.

“Big and busy, but good” This hotel is huge. For as big as it is it runs like clock work and every employee we dealt with was extremely professional and gracious. This was my second stay in the last six months. Both times my room was in the West tower. Both times purchased on Priceline. Each time I checked in, there was no mention of Priceline and I was treated well. Each time I was asked if I wanted to upgrade for a slight fee. Each time I said yes. A deluxe room was $30.00 more a night. I really can't tell you the difference between a standard room and a deluxe room. Both times I stayed there I stayed in a deluxe room. The amenities in the deluxe room include a bathrobe, air purifier, ipod alarm clock, hairdryer, Lighted make-up mirror, down blanket, nice sheets and linens. The coffee maker with 'to go' cups is a nice touch. The room I stayed in 3024 was weird because in this room they 'floated' the bed-meaning the bed was in the middle of the room with the desk behind it. I really didn't like the design and felt it was a waste of space. It made me uncomfortable. Also the rooms are a dark earth tone. Almost too dark to the point of the room seems dirty even though it's not. I felt like I was in a cave. Because this hotel is so huge, the rooms are starting to show wear. However, it's still a great value for the money. I would recommend it. Within walking distance to North Michigan Avenue and Navy Pier too.

“It was just fine!” This hotel is conveniently one and a half blocks east of Michigan Avenue, equally distant from the Water Tower and the Michigan Avenue bridge-within an easy walk to Millenium Park and the Art Institute. It is a safe and secure place. The staff are accomodating and friendly. The hotel offers a complimentary breakfast-nothing extravagant, but plentiful and a variety (oatmeal; waffles; cereals; fruit; hard boiled eggs; various breads to toast; juices,coffees and teas). The rooms were clean and inviting. However, I would avoid room 806;906 was fine, but we had to be moved out of 806 due to poor ventilation (fumes from a restaurant's wood burning oven seemed to have access to this room's air system, causing our eyes to burn). Other than that, a fine stay-nothing fancy, but who hangs out in their room in a city like Chicago?

“Great hotel, not so great location” Excellent hotel with great service and amenities. It's location is not very appealing though. It's located right behind the parking lot of a shopping area. I guess it must be nice to be there during the day but after work there is not much to do here. If you're in Austin and want to have some fun in the evenings you'd have to find your way downtown.

“Stilvoll, gute Lage, aber unruhig” Das Parker House ist sehr stilvoll und individuell. Die Eingangshalle und der Great Dining Room sind eindrucksvoll. Der Service beim Valet-Parking und Einchecken war sehr freundlich. Allerdings wurde unser Wunsch, anstatt eines sehr schmalen Doppelbettes ein (schmales) Queen-Bett zu bekommen, nur gegen Zahlung eines ordentlichen Aufschlags erfüllt. In dem anderen Zimmer (für die Kinder) gab es immerhin ein Zustellbett kostenlos. Die Zimmer sind sauber und entsprechen dem üblichen Ausstattungsstandard, sie sind aber sehr klein. Unsere Zimmer gingen auf einen Lichtschacht hinaus, waren aber trotzdem recht laut, da in diesen Schacht unzählige Klimaanlagen hinein dröhnen. Auch waren aus den Nebenzimmern und vom Gang her viele Geräusche laut zu hören - vor allem fallen die Zimmertüren sehr lautstark ins Schloss. Die Lage des Hotels ist großartig. Ganz Boston ist leicht fußläufig zu erkunden. Das Frühstücksbuffet (22 Dollar plus Tax und Gratuity) ist sein Geld in jedem Fall wert: große Auswahl, tolles Ambiente, prima Service und Getränke inklusive.

“Booked a killer deal here on priceline” I couldn't be happier with this hotel. Even if I hadn't gotten it for a steal of a rate I would still have been thrilled with the service and amenities. Great location too. I will definitely be back.

“One of my favourites!!” I have stayed at this hotel several times and it never disappoints. Excellent top class service, beautiful modern rooms, and tasty food at Art restaurant. Wherever there is a four seasons, my husband and I will be staying at it. Whenever we wish to entertain our parents, we will be taking them here. Four seasons= top class consistent service.

“Great Renovation of a 1970's Holidome” I travel quite a bit and to my knowledge this is probably the only Courtyard in the country that is an extensively renovated Holiday Inn Holidome from the 1970's. From the outside you can really see the heritage of the building. They have done some updating of the outside structure but you can clearly tell that this was an original Holiday Inn build. The outside maintenance was great with nice landscaping. Inside they have done a beautiful job renovating the holidome area. The pool area was nicely presented. The water temp in the pool was perfect and the hot tub was hot with powerful jets and quite relaxing. The room was standard Courtyard which is meant to be a compliment. A big comfy bed outfitted with great linen. The bathroom was rather spartan but efficient. The towels were big but rather scratchy but water pressure was very good. I did have breakfast at the hotel and it was decent. The free high speed internet was just that, fast and free. Others have mentioned that the hotel location isn't in the prettiest location in Columbus. While not a bad area by any stretch it is in an industrial type of area so this is something vacationing families might want to consider before booking. Overall this Courtyard is unique, well renovated, comfortable and friendly and i can, like most Courtyards, highly recommend this property.

“Great Location. Great Hotel.” Despite some TA recommendations to go with Trump Int. Tower over NYPalace, we went with NYPalace anyway due some advantages (for our current needs) NYP has over Trump. It was the right choice and we had a fantastic stay/experience at NYP. Our room was Jr. Suite in The Tower. THE LOCATION: excellent location, across from St. Patrick on Madison Ave, with 2 entrances on 50th and 51st streets. It is 1 block from 5th Ave, 2 blocks from the nearest subway , 1.5 block from Rockefellar Center, 3.5 blocks from Broadway. Central Park is 15 minutes walking distance. There is a starbucks across the street (on 51st) and many restaurants, cafe (both expensive and affordable) around. THE HOTEL: Beautiful and elegant hotel with many great architectural details in the lobby. The courtyard (where Gilt restaurant is) is facing St. Patrick. There are different check in areas and elevators for Main House guests and Tower guests. Tower guests also have different Concierge. The common area is very clean, nicely furnished and freshly accented with many beautifully designed flower arrangements. THE ROOM: Our Jr. suite is located on 52nd floor looking down at St. Patrick. The room is spacious (650 sft) and intelligently designed with big walk in closet (with umbrella there), extra closet at the front, and more closet storage space before entering the bathroom. The furnitures are a little dated with scratches and chips. The carpet needs replacement but is clean. There is a 42 in flat screen TV, DVD player, Bose stereo system (can connect to Ipod) in the room. Therre is a fully stocked refreshment/snack center in the room but out of the way. The bed is very comfortable. The sheets are clean, fresh and crisp. amny of them are Italy linen. The marble bathroom is huge and gorgeous with bath tub and shower stand. The bathroom mirror goes from one wall to the other. There is a vanity chair in the room and everything one can think off (all Molton Brown facial cleanser, toning solution, lotion, mouth wash, mending kit, collar kit, vanity kit, shaving kit, dental kit, Molton Brown bath products and scale). The bathroom is very clean. The towels are thick, soft, clean and have the luxurious feel to them. The two white, clean, fluffy bathroom floormats are changed daily (NOW, that is the first I know of). The room has great soundproof. We hardly hear any noise on the hall or outside. Turn down service is done nightly with the delivering of bottle of water. THE SERVICE: Besides a little hiccups from the check in lady (who first told us we have to wait for room, gave us a lecture on their check in and out times since we arrived early, but later "switched" room for us after a reminder that we have contacted the hotel many times to request early check in so my young kids can eat after a long flight), everyone was attentive, professional and helpful. Many of the staff have been with the hotel for 30 years (our Bellman and Housekeeper). Some of them appear to like what they do and are always in good spirit (the older gentleman in the executive lounge). I have never tipped that much in my life...not only because everyone was deserving it but because I felt it is a tradition there. Some other hiccups was that some of our pre arrival requests were totally ignored by check in (2 double beds, hypoallergenic room). Also, the "welcoming kids amenities" (teddy bear, crayon, color books, kids bath ropes) were never seen until we noticed some being delivered to another the room and inquired. Other requests such as refrigerator, microwave, highchair were delivered within 30 minutes to our room at no extra charge. THE EXECUTIVE LOUNGE: One of the best reason to stay in the Tower, besides having free wifi in room, is having access to the Executive Lounge. The lounge is over 3000 sqt with elegant decor, nice sofa, TV, table and chairs, computer area (with printer) and IPad if you want to borrow. Breakfast is served every morning (6:30-10:30 weekdays and 7-11 weekend) and consists of scrabled eggs, bacon, sausage, potato, smoke salmon, oat meal, lots of fresh fruits, good variety of pastries and bread, cereals, milk, coffee, juices (to include fresh squeezed orange juice) and different drink choices. Light lunch (different sandwiches, soup and salad) is served daily and the h'ordeuvres (shrimp, lobster salad, Thai dishes, sushi, cheese, crackers, beef wellington...) and coctails in the evening are great hits. There is also desert from 7:30-8:30pm. In short, whether you want to stop by for the food presentation or just to get coffee and drink at any time, the EL is a great added feature for the Tower. It is worthwhile to note that their cookies are simply the best. RESTAURANT: We didn't dine at Gilt or Istana but ordered room service which was run independently from the restaurant. The food was excellent. The steak was cooked to perfection. The service was on time and professionally delivered and presented. 19% gratuity plus $7 fee per person were charged to the total bill. A tip for those who travel with babies or young kids, order grocery from Freshdirect and have them delivered to the hotel. They have everything including ready to microwave meals that designed by Chefs and are excellent. Mine was delivered to the hotel an hour before my arrival so it was kept in the package room and delivered to my room. OVERALL: Almost perfect but a fantastic stay. Great, clean hotel with wonderful service that we would definitely come back.

“One Smidge Short of Excellent” I want to preface this review by saying that my husband and I are in our mid senior years. We can afford more now than when our children lived at home. This was one of the best 5 day vacations we have been on in many years even with the small inconvenience of the bathroom size and noise. After staying several dozen times at the Valencia in San Jose, CA, we finally were able to experience the Valencia in San Antonio. We had read, on several TripAdvisor reviews, that it was noisy. We had always stayed in a Junior Suite and never experienced any noise in CA. Not so on this trip. We were originally given a Junior Suite, but had to be moved to a regular room because of the recently varnished wood in the junior suite. My asthma bothered me the minute I opened the room door and another Junior Suite was not available. I want to add that all through this experience we were given four diamond treatment. The front desk, the porter, the manager...everyone was friendly, helpful and ready to try to meet our every need. Now about the noise. When I was in the bathroom, which I might add is smaller than their CA counterparts, I could hear the lady in the next bathroom talking. She wasn't yelling, just talking. I heard her as clear as if she were standing in our room talking. It was a very uncomfortable feeling, so I kept the bathroom door shut while we were in our room and the radio or TV on. I can't actually say I heard any voices while we were in our room area. There were some bumps and knocks, but no voices. I was uncomfortable enough to keep the TV on just in case. Other than that, our stay was very relaxing. We were on the 9th floor, on the side of the building between the river and the street. We didn't hear any noise from the ground, but then our view was of the top of the building, the pool area (no one swam throughout our stay) and a parking lot. None of those make much noise. I can guess that if you stay by the air conditioners, you would hear them so if you wake easily, ask for a room away from them. After we settled into the room, we drove our car to the Market Street Parking Garage ( 3 blocks away) parked ($12.00 for 24 hours instead of $27.00 at the Valencia) and walked everywhere almost the whole 5 days. The Hotel is on the Riverwalk and within walking distance of everything we wanted to visit. The parking garage was close, well lighted and we felt our car was very safe. Each time we came and went from the Hotel, we were asked if we needed directions, had doors opened for us and our every need met, day or night. Definitely 4 star treatment. Inside it is much the same as the San Jose Valencia. The tone is peaceful, water flows inside the lobby, colors are relaxing and lights are low. It has a business center that is very efficient, dining venue (we didn't eat there) and a small bar area. The bar (V-Bar) is, thankfully, not the hot spot that is the San Jose V-Bar. All staff personnel were a friendly, attentive group of young adults and happy to be of help whenever we asked (but I'm sure our tipping didn't hurt their opinion of us). We will definately stay there again but in the future, only in a junior suite.

“Fun place to stay just close enough to the action” This hotel is a place that I imagine people either love or hate. It's very modern and as soon as you walk in, you feel like you're entering a night club. The main lobby is decked out with loads of comfy couches and chairs and has a great bar. Up a few flights of stairs is the roof bar which can get packed at night. So it's definitely a place where you can have fun. If you're not looking for that atmosphere, I wouldn't recommend it. The rooms are a great size and quite comfortable. My room had a window seat, however, it was overlooking a parking lot. The area the hotel is in is a bit odd. A block away you'll find bail bondsmen and pawn shops so it's probably best not to stray too far alone. However, you can walk to the Gaslamp Quarter from here in about 10-15 minutes depending on your pace. But if you're lucky enough, you can take the courtesy car from the hotel and have a much more pleasant trip. The hotel is at most ten minutes from the airport. This was my first time at this hotel and I'd certainly stay there again. However, not if I were traveling with my family. Overall, a great experience with very attentive staff.

“OK Hotel in San Jose” We got a pretty good deal on Priceline and checkin was fine with friendly staff. Room was fine but not great. Overall stay was good but not sure we would want to stay here again, not sure why but just felt it was a strange hotel.

“Clean, friendly, comfortable” My only complaint is that it's a little far from the metro--about 6 blocks, which doesn't seem like that much, but when you add in uphill with luggage and/or rain--it's far. Other than that, this was a lovely hotel! It was very comfortable. The room was a little small, but how much do you really need? The breakfast in the morning was great--I filled up on the waffles and everything so I didn't need lunch! Thanks for a lovely stay.

“Good value. Nice, clean rooms, quiet.” I got a good AAA rate. Nice Courtyard for an urban location. I was on a high floor but just a basic city view. I think few rooms have great views of the bridges etc. But my room was very bright, clean and comfortable. The neighborhood is pretty desolate on the weekend because it is near the business district. As a female solo traveler, I took cabs back to the hotel at night or friends dropped me off. The hotel is about a 10 minute walk up a slight hill from the Montgomery Bart station which I took from SFO airport. Good Deal! I rented a car nearby for my trip to wine country at the same rate as the airport rate. Parking is expensive so if you can try to rent a car in the city when you need it or park somewhere else. Otherwise you can get around with public transport. One thing, as a Marriott Rewards Silver guest I would expect some voucher toward my breakfast. Breakfast was not a bargain. Hilton Honors Gold gives vouchers or has free breakfast at some properties. I had a food stash from the Hampton Inn- Airport I stayed at the previous night ! A Starbucks is opening in the lobby. Not much in the immediate area for eating. Not real close to the major tourist attractions but the price was good! The hotel does provide free coffee and a free internet computer station.

“Delicious” This hotel is convenient for mid-town attractions. It's just a few blocks from Penn Station, The Empire State Building and Times Square. I was welcomed to the hotel by a friendly and energetic staff, determined to keep me happy. Their first test came when I discovered, shortly after checking in, that the air conditioner in my room had sprung a leak and water had soaked the carpet. I called the front desk and they dispatched an engineer. He arrived quickly and determined that whilst the AC could be fixed, it would take some time for the carpet to dry. He rang the front desk and requested another room. Then he went to the new room to make sure everything was in order before I moved. He then called the bellman who moved my things to the new room, which was identical to my original room, without the wet floor. This summed up my short (three days) stay at the hotel. I was impressed with the care and good spirits of the staff in every situation. My only recommendation is that they may need one or two more staff during the busy times. My room was small but well-designed with a good bathroom shower and enough storage space. The desk worked well. Wi-Fi is available in the room for about $10 a day. This is, however, per device, which I think is antiquated and a bit naughty. Paying $20 a day if you use your computer and smart phone is really over the top. Of course, like all DoubleTree hotels, you're greeted with their trademark cookie. The cookie and their service were both delicious.

“Pleasant Staff” I stayed with my husband and 2 kids ages 17 & 8. One of the nicest hotel staffs I've encountered in my trips to NY. It was reasonablly priced. It was a GREAT location - Macy's in the next block, couple blocks from Empire state bldg. Very Clean with free computer and internet use available. The Free Breakfast was really good. A slection of Pastries, bagels & cereals along with Eggs, bacon and make your own waffles. Although, if you want the best selection get there early. By 7am it was packed and by 8am most of the good stuff was gone.

“Horrible Place...” Our flight was delayed and we missed the last flight to our destination and needed a hotel room close to the airport. This one had an easter sale, but i sincerely advise you all , it is not worth to stay here. The location is not safe, there is a stripclub across it and all sorts of duboius lookiing bars around the area. The hotel itself is not safe, the doors to outside do not lock soundly , needs maintenance, and anyone can come in at night. The room is FILTHY..the toilet seat has all sorts of CRUD and SOIL on it. The lounge chair smells of urine and we dare not even walk barefoot on the carpet. One sleepless night, on the stinky bed and pillows. One lesson learned , never again trust these deals , otherwise airport would have been a better option. Same sleepless night but a cleaner bathroom.

“Old San Antonio” Das nach David Crockett benannte Hotel versprüht einen Mix aus Kolonialzeit und texanischer Geschichte von San Antonio. Ich war nur eine Nacht im Hotel, war zufrieden, aber weiss nicht genau ob ich mich nochmal dort einbuchen würde, oder lieber ein etwas moderneres Ambiente bevorzuge. Man wird hier nicht enttäuscht, aber darf auch nicht zuviel erwarten. Wer in der N♪2he der Attraktionen sein will ist hier gut aufgehoben.

“Courtyard by Airport” Very nice outdoor area. Arrived late, but there was some sunlight left and the courtyard was pretty and peaceful. The pool isindoors in its own pool house with outdoor lounge chairs facing the pool. Well kept garden and pots. Many rooms had balcony's overlooking courtyard. I did not notice any noise from airport in the courtyard. Lobby was modern. There is a business area, booths and a snack bar with wine and beer. It was buzzing with activity. Room was fine, typical Courtyard. Staff were great, very friendly. Free internet. Flat screen TV. Granite in bathroom. Free coffee in lobby. The free shuttle to the airport stops at all 3 Marriott properties, so plan accordingly. Early am (4 am) I could hear the planes taking off, but a colleague on the same side of building did not hear anything.

“They don't quite get it yet at the Renaissance” With all the Hawkeye & Cub fans in town for Labor Day games, rooms in the Loop were hard to find for the weekend of our daughter’s college move-in. So we went out to Rosement, just a few minutes up I90 from downtown. My hubby checked in Friday, while I arrived on Saturday at 4Pm. It's a good thing we had another room because the second room was not ready until well after 6PM. This is my pet peeve -- waiting for my room! And from a Marriott? Shame shame. To the defense of the reception staff, they were embarrassed. I just told them to relax because I was going to dinner and would use the other room for now. And they did try to get the two rooms near one another -- just around the corner. The hotel is large and well-placed off the interstate, only blocks from the "L." It's not far from a great forest preserve that we used for our morning walk/run. We came back for breakfast -- not include -- and very expensive for what you get on the buffet. The staff was very pleasant this morning, with a quick "good morning" and "have a good day." And there wasn't anything really bad but I just didn't get a good feeling about the hotel. Our second room smelled soooo bad. The blinds were hanging off. Our shower head was a hair away from exploding. Still, the room was clean. The baths were marble. The price was right ($119). What was my problem? Perhaps it was the design. I am not really into that European orange and beige. The living room was small as was the bedroom. But that's not usually enough for me to complain on my Trip Advisor Forum. Now that I think about it, I think it was just the little things. It felt like cheap luxury... upscale wanna be. I don't think I would stay here again, but for a family looking for value, it worked. Just don’t sweat the small stuff.

“Friendly staff - excellent location” My stay at the Donatello was excellent. The room was very spacious and the staff are extremely helpful, warm, and accomodating. I arrived very early and while they did not have a room available for me at the time, they were able to provide me with access to their club room, which had everything I needed to freshen up (shower, toiletries, etc.). The club room has a great reception room as well, really nice space to read, do some work, or just take a view of the city. There is free coffee, free internet, and a bar that has live jazz. The happy hour at the bar was really nice too - half off appetizers and discounted wine and beer. My room was excellent, very spacious. There was a nice wet bar in my room, which was great since I was staying for an extended period. It was also great to have a corner room with great views of the San Francisco streets. My only complaint would be that there is a considerable amount of noise that can be heard from the streets in the room and I was on the 9th floor. This is because the Donatello is in an excellent location - only one block from Union Square. Yet, I was awakened several times during the night during my stay by loud noise on the street. The noise was from party-goers as well as trash trucks and street cleaners. I would definitely go back!

“Best Rooms in San Francisco by Far!” The St. Regis San Francisco offers perhaps the very best accommodations in the city. I have stayed at several others including the Four Seasons, W, Mandarin-Oriental and the Ritz-Carlton, and the rooms at the St. Regis are by far the best. The rooms are innovative and luxurious, more so than most other hotels I've experienced worldwide in this class. The service was also commendable, but not quite as good as the Four Seasons or Ritz-Carlton. It's not quite as personal of an experience, but the rooms and facilities make it worthwhile. One final note: The restaurant (for dinner) has a very limited menu offering in my opinion. You can't find anything basic ie. steak, chicken, etc. Everything is "Fu fu" in my option, but lunch and breakfast in the more casual cafe are great.

“Great staff, nice welcome drink on...” Great staff, nice welcome drink on arrival (& a couple of other times during my stay!), very clean and comfortable, rooms a little small, but even on business I was only there to sleep. Nice restaurant on site. Overall a great hotel in that part of NYC. this was not my first visit here and won't be the last.

“Great location, great price, simply a great hotel” Having stayed at the Marriot Courtyard on 5th Avenue, I happen to like this one better. The hotel is superbly located. You are one block from the subway and minutes away from the theatre district. Bryant Park is a block away. This property is only 2-3 blocks away from the other Marriot Courtyard but again, I think a bit better located and somehow a bit more pleasing in my opinion. By Manhattan standards I thought our room was huge. We had a room with a king size bed. Like all Marriot Courtyard properties the bed was soft and luxiorius. We however found the bed too soft for our liking. Our room featured a vice nice and large LCD TV and large closet. It is worth noting the building the hotel is located in is exceptionally narrow. As a result there are only 6-8 rooms on each floor. Our room was very quiet and heard very little from adjoining rooms. If we had a complaint, it was the bathroom. The door had an awful creaking noise when we opened and closed it and we suspect waked others on the floor. The bathroom lacked a fan, so steam would linger in the bathroom for hours. Staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel has a small snack area where you can buy drinks (including beer) and other small items. Breakfast is served in the lobby as well but we did not try this and presume this is not included in the room rate. Overall, an excellent location, comfortable room, and having stayed in 6-8 different NYC hotels on prior visits possibly the best I have stayed in, keeping in mind I am more of a budget traveller.

“Smooth stay” I think that the parking, after tax (and valet tips) was more expensive than the expensive downtown Washington DC Hilton/HGI. Friendly Staff. Somewhat convoluted hhonors floor where you need to take an elevator up, then walk to another elevator that goes up one more floor, it's a bit like being punished for having status if you're wheeling baggage/equipment around. The room was nice, though there was a large gap at the bottom of the door that let a lot of noise in from the corridor - there's always that one guy who has to use his outside voice in a hotel corridor after 11pm I liked that the TV signal was in HD and I was glad that I got a courtyard view as the other side seemed very noisy.

“Couldn't Be Any Better” Booked this trip through "Hotwire" which I never had done before. Once I got my confirmation I emailed the hotel ref room info. Tom quickly replied stating he was able to place us on an upper floor and upgrade our room. Upon check-in very nice and accommodating front desk personnel met us. When we arrived at our room it was everything Tom had said. Nice size, clean and comfortable. Bathroom was an “ok” size, functional. Hotel itself was very clean. Great location easy in and out; would definitely sty here on our next trip. Thanks to the entire staff for a great trip.

“Good room, good location, good night!!” Stayed here for one night last week while repairs were being conducted to my home. The staff was very pleasant at checkin and during the stay. The room was decent sized for one person and the bathroom was the smallest I have ever seen. The other reviews were right when they said you could barely close the door without hitting the counter or barely turn around without bumping into something. Everything was very clean throughout the entire room and I didn't hear any noise from the street or the hallway. All in all, I'd say it was a pleasant stay and would return.

“Full of Local Bums THAT LIVE THERE” We stayed here before our vacation to Hawaii because we thought it was a good deal for 1 night stay and we also left our car parked there.First the shuttle van is filthy,the room in the back to put your luugage is very dirty.The A/C in the room did not work,no blow dryer,also NO ALARM clock,who ever heard of a motel with no alarm clock.I finally figured it out,this place has a BUNCH of people living there.When my wife and I went to get breakfast it was full of all these people that live there.Lots of kids screaming and yelling and the front desk did not tell them nothing.But it all boils down to that old saying you get what you pay for so please DO NOT STAY AT THIS DUMP,it is full of alot of local BUMS.

“OK but probably better choices out there” We booked a junior suite for 5 nights through priceline. We were bringing our 5-month-old daughter, so that's why we got the junior suite. The service started out great - they brought a pack-n-play up with freshly laundered sheets for our daughter, they emptied the minibar so we could use it for bottles. The hotel room is not gorgeous but it's better than acceptable. It's supposed to look muted and sophisticated but it's looking a little worn down. But then we had some problems. The room was overwhelmingly hot and it took them over a day to fix it. With an infant, that wasn't fun. Our cordless phone in the room didn't work at all. The front desk was sometimes unfriendly (eg, stared at me while I was struggling to open the enormous heavy front door with the stroller in tow instead of helping). The worst was room service. The menu is very limited and way overpriced. A tiny steak with some fries was $26. My husband's was way overcooked, and mine was only 2/3 the size of my husband's (and his was tiny). They never brought an extra receipt up so we constantly had to ask for them. A meal of two bowls of oatmeal was $20, seriously. Even though they have a full service restaurant, they would not allow us to order anything except for the very limited number of items from the room service menu. I even asked if we could go down and pick the food up from Cortez (the hotel's restaurant) and I was told no. This issue won't affect most people like it did us. Because we had an infant, we couldn't just run out and grab something to eat. I found the limited menu, extremely high prices, and poor food quality to be a real downer. It definitely negatively affected our experience and we wouldn't come back.

“Hampton Inn Denver - Service with a Smile” My wife and I stayed 2 nights at the Hampton Inn on Sherman Street in Denver after visiting with family in Steamboat Springs. We arrived at about 10am in the morning after an early and long 3 1/2hour shuttle ride and went right to the Hamton Inn hoping to check in immediately, drop our luggage and shower before going out to tour Denver. We were told as is all too often the case that the hotel was full and no rooms were ready to check in. I appealed to the front desk person, Angela and said we would really appreciate being able to have our room asap. Angela said she would see what she could do. 20 minutes later, Voila! Anglea and the housecleaning staff had our room ready. Her assistant Adam helped with the process too. This was excellent service and it was done with a pleasant "can do" attitude and a smile. The hotel itself is quite pleasant, clean, well located within walking distance of the 16th St. Mall, Capitol Building and many shops and restaurants. I would highly recommend this hotel and applaud the excellent service Angela provided to us!

“Consistently Good” I have stayed here a dozen times in the last two years, most recently on July 9. The hotel sits next to the old World Trade Center site and was completely renovated after 9/11. The hotel is sleek, modern and comfortable. The standard rooms are small, but very comfortable. The room decor is also modern and minimalist in a good way. Light wood furniture; glass tops on the dresser and desk; large flat screen televisions. I've eaten in the restaurant many times and have been happy with the food. The continental breakfast used to be better and has been scaled back a little of late, but it's ok. It's several years out now since the renovation, but everything is still in very nice shape. Noise has sometimes been a problem with the continuous day/evening work on the World Trade Center site, and most of the rooms face that direction. There are rooms on each end of the hotel that face the opposite direction and they are quieter (although the view isn't nearly as interesting). These rooms are also significantly bigger than the typical rooms facing the WTC site. I've stayed in four of these end rooms, and it seems to be hit or miss if you get one. I've attached some pictures of one of these bigger rooms, so for the standard room, imagine something much narrower. The staff is courteous and professional. One extra bonus of the hotel is that it is also right next to the Century 21 department store. I definitely recommend this hotel.

“OK, especially for families” Stayed at the Residence Inn Times square Dec 22-25, 2006. Its overall a nice place to stay in Manhattan, especially for families i.e with kids. The rooms are good size, slightly smaller than the average Residence Inn out in the country. Rooms are clean. comfortable and quiet. Typical of a residence inn, there is a kitchen, with everything minus a stove/oven (surprising), there is crockpot and microwave oven though. The elevators are fast but quite crowded especially during peak time, but they have a way of 'controlling' them manually for faster service. The hotel is very child friendly, positive but can be overwhelming if you are looking for a slow and quiet environment. The breakfast is average, nothing fancy. The 3rd floor has a lounge that is well furnished, the restaurant is on the same level and there is a small bar too. Staff - very courteous and professional, all of them. Check in can be slow because of the numbers, but it is efficient once your turn comes. Check out is automated. Location is very ideal. Overall a nice place to stay, good rates, would return.

“Great location, parking included, and comfortable suites” The Cow Hollow Suites are actually a companion property to the Cow Hollow Motor Inn, which in contrast is comprised of nicely appointed, large hotel rooms (check in is shared, but the Suites have their own entrance). We've actually stayed in both and now opt for the Suites as the better albeit pricier choice. Why? Well, the Suites are actually like renting a small condo that is serviced like a hotel room, and they are at least as comfortable as those offered by the large "suites" chains. There's nothing like lounging in an actual living room after a day of out and about, or even dining in if one so chooses. A significant advantage for the the Cow Hollow is that it is located in an area that has any number of dining options and for virtually any taste and budget. Moreover, the Cow Hollow includes parking in its room rates, no small matter in a town as expensive to park in as San Francisco. If there is any reason to knock the place, it is that the decor of the Suites is a bit dated, but then that's also part of the charm since everything about them in our experience is quite comfy and well-maintained.

“More than I could ask for!” This resort was excellent for me and my family and my group of 10, 5 adults, 1 teen, 2 babies and 2 toddlers. I will start out by saying my arrival into Phoenix was rocky with my 2 day old iphone being stolen...but i put all feelings aside and enjoyed my phone free vacation! Checking in was a breeze, no lines, great service, we received complimentary bottled water as well as our room preferences. The resort is laid out in several buildings that are disconnected and have seperate parking lots but you can definetly walk from one end to another in 5 minutes! We drove around to find our building which has its own grand lobby and beautiful patio and pool area with swim up bar and waiter service. I was in the north pointe building in a 3rd floor room facing the pool, yes it is loud in the evenings when people are at the pool but with the TV on i could not hear a thing! and my balcony faced a quiet courtyard area with the sounds of a calming fountain! The king suite was very spacious with a large seperate living room with pull out couch and a seperate bathroom and sink area, large flat screen tvs with lots of channels, clean bathroom and floors. I inspected it vigorously as i have a crawling baby. The best part was the french doors that seperated all 3 spaces from each other so you could be in the living room without disturbing anyone in bathroom or bedroom. The fridge wasnt cooling properly and my precious milk spoiled, i called up to the lobby at almost 11pm and they sent someone with a new fridge in less than 5 minutes! Same with towels, i requested 6 extra towels and i received it right away! The food at the north pointe pool was much much better than the waterpark, we ordered almost every item off both menus so this is an accurate representation. We ate at Rico's at the breakfast buffett most mornings, no lines, great service, delicious food, the croissants were to die for! One morning i had a spa appointment and grabbed food to go at the "starbucks" cafe and although my muffins were delicious it was ridiculously expensive $30 for 2 muffins, 2 breakfast sandwiches and 2 bottles of juice! You are better off spending $32 for 2 adults to eat in the buffett! By the way kids 3 and under eat free! The waterpark food i hated but they made the mixed drinks very strong and good! We walked to Aunt Chiladas and had great service...i wont comment on the food cause i am from texas and anything besides tex-mex just doesnt taste good to me...i shoulda known better. Waterpark was amazing...its not a waterpark per say just a collection of a large pool with waterfall area, baby pool, large slide pool, medium sized pool with basketball and volleyball and lazy river. There was also mini golf to the side, you pay one time $5 to play or a $2 per day resort fee for unlimited play. All the pools have towels! There is also a playground and if they are not in session they will allow you to bring your kids inside camp coyote and play in a room full of toys, disney movies playing on the large screen, a puppet theater...perfect for the under 4 yr old kids who could not otherwise attend camp and wake up early and get hot in the playground. There is also a public park by Aunt Chiladas you can walk to and play at. The spa was amazing, i had the best massage and wonderful service there as well! The concierge was very helpful in booking spa appointments, tours to sedona and grand canyon, discounts at rawhide for the kids. Location was great, chinese restaurant that delivers quickly across the street as well as a sports bar type restaurant, there is also a bank of america bank and atm across from the lobby down the street minute drive there is a walgreens and fast food restaurants the airport was 9.2 miles away, 15 minute drive Scottsdale was 12 miles away Rawhide was 25 minute drive One day was rainy and cold so we drove about 8 minutes out to Jamba playland an indoor carnival for kids which was also amazing and so fun for them with cheap carnival food for us to keep our mouths busy with. If you force me to have one complaint, it would be...the wifi is terrible...dont bother paying for it cause it did not work...go down to the lobby and wifi is free there or you can use the business center computers. I asked for a refund of my wifi charge and it was given to me no questions asked. I was there for 4 days and i would have stayed for 2 more if the airlines didnt have change fees, it was so much fun, perfect for me and my family, perfect location

“Feburary in the Windy City” What a great hotel. Everyone from the doorman to the housekeeping staff were freindly and helpful. The hotel has been updated and felt fresh. This is a very large hotel in two towers and the directions can be confusing, but the staff were very helpful. The only negative thing I can say about this hotel is the elevators can be over whelmed at busy times.

“Hotel Solamar is Amazing!” We went to San Diego for my birthday and we had an amazing time. Part of the reason was this hotel. We stayed on the 8th floor and the room could not have been better! The bed was amazingly comfortable, the room was large, and the cleaning staff kept the room spotless (even so much as perfectly arranging the curtains each day). The staff was friendly and the bell-staff was always ready to help with the car no matter the hour. This is a great hotel.

“Awesome Resort” This resort is really first class. I am originally from San Antonio, but had never experienced it like this. Beautiful setting with multiple pools. Shopping and Six Flags are conveniently nearby. The service at the pools really pleasantly surprised me and was consistent the several days we spent at the pool. Food quality was very high. Room was clean and very nice, although we had lots of activities planned. We would definitely return.

“Lovely, clean and a great value” This 1 year old Four Points hotel is a great value! For $89 you get a beautifully appointed room, wonderful bed, great amenities and free wi-fi! The lobby is warm and inviting, the food is great and the staff will go out of their way to accommodate you. The room decor is fun and funky and the sliding bathroom door with the frosted porthole is just plain fun. The corner rooms are HUGE! Try to get one if you can. If you get a standard room, don't fret; they are still plenty big. Nothing but compliments to the staff for their great job and for Sheraton in creating their newest Four Points product. Well done.

“Located steps from shopping” Stayed this past weekend, the remodeled lobby, restaurant and bar had all opened up only 2 weeks prior. The remodel is very nice, with 2 gas fireplaces in the cozy lobby seating area. The restaurant has been re-located to the mezzanine level, along with the bar, and these are open to the lobby below. They spent some serious money on the furnishings and fixtures, but beware there are no views like from the Grandviews bar and restaurant they replaced. They say that Grandviews will no longer be a public area, and be converted into meeting room space. Sad, as this was a very nice feature of this property with impressive views from the 36th floor. Check in was prompt, but slightly confusing, as staff each are situated at small desks with laptops. It seems they are going for a boutique hotel look, but when you have over 500 rooms and no intuitive way to queue up, it gets crowded. The doormen were always very efficient at hailing cabs and providing directions. There's also a lot of staff standing around by the elevators and I could never figure out exactly what their jobs were. The breakfast buffet is very good, and is $25 a person, though service seemed a bit unsteady. Perhaps the staff is still very new. Rooms were nice and very clean. No curtains. There are some light plastic movable shades, and then a roll down room darkening shade powered by switches next to the bed. Room was very quiet while I was there, except on Saturday night during a massive rain and wind storm the building's steel structure squeaked and groaned for hours, keeping us awake. I was surprised that no robes were provided in the room, and after 2 phone requests for 2 bathrobes, only 1 ever showed up. Also, newspapers for elite members are not delivered to the door as at other Hyatts, but are left in the elevator lobby. The bathroon did have a great shower, and hot water was abundant each morning. A very welcome touch was that the room had a mini-fridge that was empty so that you could stock your own drinks in it for your stay. No mini bar. There are a couple convenience stores within a block or two of the hotel along Sutter Street. You are also almost right on Union Square, and the heart of San Francisco's shopping district. Literally every major department store and boutique has an outlet within a few block radius of the Grand Hyatt. Overall, a nice renovation job, and I would stay here again, if just for the location. They do have a few kinks to work out training personnel, but hopefully this will be accomplished very soon. I do hope they will re-open the 36th floor bar space again someday.

“Nice place in great location” This is a nice small hotel located a few blocks from Times Square. The room was a nice size. The bed could have been a bit more comfortable and our room did not have a bathtub. Other than that, we had a good experience here.

“Excellent hôtel” Excellent rapport qualité-prix pour cet hôtel idéalement situé (les fenêtres des chambres donnent directement sur le parc historique), doté d'une belle piscine intérieure et offrant de grandes chambres (déco très américaine...) et un wifi gratuit pour un pris raisonnable. Personnel d'accueil très aimable et cherchant à se rendre utile.

“Great experience!” I had a lovely, large room with a comfortable bed. The layout of the room is a bit odd, but it is spacious and had a bed, couch, dresser and desk. The staff is friendly and helpful. It is located directly across the street from the Houston Pavilions which has dining and shopping. I can wholeheartedly recommend this hotel.

“Right on waterfront, good for a conference” We stayed here for 3 nights as part of a conference so didn't have a choice in hotels. That said, we were pleased with our stay here. The rooms are standard Marriott, but many rooms have a beautiful waterfront view, and the 31st floor concierge club lounge (closed Friday noon - Sunday 5 pm) served both hot and cold breakfast items, omelettes made to order, fruit and snacks throughout the day, and decent hot appetizers and dessert in the evening. The lounge also has 2 computers for printing boarding passes and web surfing. Rooms have a safe and refrigerator in the flat-screen TV cabinet. Bathrooms are small but there is a make-up mirror on a stand. The area around the hotel has some nice restaurants such as Fleming's and Roy's, and within a few blocks along the waterfront are Panera Bread, Hard Rock, and Houlihan's. There's a Barnes & Noble bookstore here, as well. For shopping, there are a few chains - Anthropologie, J Crew, White House/Black Market - and some local boutiques staffed with friendly employees. The harbor has "dragon boats" you can rent to paddle about, and there is a harbor cruise company (Spirit Cruises) that offers evening excursions. Given our good experience, we would stay here again if in the Baltimore area.

“Quiet on Weekends for Peaceful Stay in Downtown New York” The Club Quarters located in the Financial District of New York ended up being the perfect spot for our long weekend in New York. At first I was bummed that we were not staying in a more culturally interesting area but it all turned out for the best. Since the financial district is so quiet on the weekends, it ended up being an oasis in the city. We love walking in New York so each day we used the hotel as our base and walked to Chinatown, SOHO, etc. We also took the subway when necessary. We also got what I would consider a fabulous deal on this hotel. It only cost 175.00 per night on Priceline. Somehow (without asking) we got assigned the Diplomat's Suite. It had two rooms, two flat screen TVs, a pull-out couch, King size bed, kitchenette (though we did not really use it). The bathroom just had a shower which was fine with us. This was a fabulous deal in my estimation for New York City. To boot, we had excellent service from all members of the staff. Unrelated to the hotel, we ended up getting two parking tickets when we parked near the hotel because we did not read the signs properly, so that is a little heads up. If we could ever score such a deal in the future I would definitely be up for staying in the Club Quarters again.

“nice furnishings, good food and cloth shower curtains that STINK!” Nice big room with fancy furniture, including a sleep comfort bed, BUT, for heaven' sake, if you are going to use cloth shower curtains; take them down and wash them occasionally. They stink of mildew and urine when they get wet; enough to make you gag! Good breakfast that costs extra and parking costs extra as well.

“Loved the Bedding!” Why do we stay at a hotel... mostly to sleep. I have to say, this was one of the most comfortable beds I have slept on. It rates right up there with Westin's Heavenly bed. Room was nice and clean. Furnishings looked almost brand new. Front desk staff was pleasant and friendly. Everyone was professional but not snobby. One of the better hotels in greater San Diego.

“Hilton standard rooms but rough around the edges” We stayed here Labor Day weekend, so first of all, I was a bit jarred, as a recent ex-NYer, by the tourist traffic on the sidewalk, so that perhaps colored my stay, but I did stay in this same hotel on September 11, 2010, in a last minute booking because it was available and I wasn't as affected by the tourist traffic. So, in the next couple of weeks after the 10th anniversary, the location next to the WTC is definitely a factor to consider. Having said that, if you have a room on the WTC side, you can spend some time viewing the site in peace - both times I stayed I had a WTC view even though I didn't request it either time. However, I was disappointed by the amenities at the hotel. I didn't pay a bargain rate for the hotel, so I was a bit dismayed to find out not only is the internet access in the room not wireless, it was also $14.95 a day. I think they get this complaint a lot because when I was trying to plead my case as a Hilton Honors member to the front desk, the front desk person corrected my $15 to $14.95 and just repeated the wired complaint like it was a matter of fact. I can deal with the internet charge, but then it became about the little things. The ice machine on our floor was broken, and we called down to report it. Nothing was done to address the broken machine during our two day stay. And finally, the elevators were ...taxed. Several times we waited five or more minutes for the elevators. None of this is tragic, and if my rate was less than $300, I probably wouldn't have noticed. Housekeeping was excellent, the room was comfortable, and the tv worked well, as I would expect from a Hilton hotel. I probably won't stay here again, unless I get a good deal, because the internet charge effectively raises the rate, and for me, the hyper NYer, the slow elevator is really problematic. But overall, its a decent hotel in an interesting location.

“Quick, Clean Comfort at Rock Center” I only stayed here for one night, as my trip extended and the hotel I had been in couldn't let me stay another night, but... I got lucky, it was a good choice! Clean and reasonably quiet with a super fast and friendly check-in and out. Wireless internet was free & fast and there was a free purified water dispenser on my floor. Shower (water) pressure was good for Manhattan and the bed was comfortable. There was a little wear on the room, but nonetheless, it was clean as a pin. All in all, this hotel deserves consideration, for it is a good value and a solid choice for this area of Manhattan.

“Wonderful hotel, but not the best in SD.” I stayed here out of chance; I live in San Diego and went to priceline to see if I could get a good deal for a weekend getaway. I was able to get this hotel for $77 a night ($259 on every other website). The staff was superb, very helpful, and very friendly. The rooms were clean and well decorated; There was a minibar that was well stocked, and we had a small balcony right over the rooftop pool. The concierege, belldesk, and valet were all extremely curetous and helpful. This seems more of a business hotel, as it is directly across from the convention center. I prefer the "boutique" hotels in San Diego (Ivy, Hard Rock, U.S Grant), but for this deal I would stay again.

“Great Hotel, Nicely Located” This is a standard Hilton Garden Inn Hotel as all the others you can find everywhere. This one is very conveniently located (3 blocks from the Hollywood Boulevard and near highways), so you don't always need your car. The hotel seems pretty new, very clean and VERY helpful staff. Two downsides: parking is very expensive ($30 valet only) and AC is very noisy in the rooms. Breakfast is very good as well, but coffee is horrible as it is in all the Garden Inn's.

“Ok for a business trip , the Hilton was a little (not much) nicer” I recently stayed at the Westin Market Street and the Hilton Financial District on two consecutive nights on a business trip to San Francisco. They were more alike than different, but the Hilton felt a little nicer. I checked in around 6 pm and the place was busy. Just like my Hilton experience, there was a bit of a wait at the front desk, and just like my Hilton experience, there was not much to be gained by my Platinum Status (Diamond at Hilton). In both cases no upgrade, just a normal room, though at the Westin I was on a middle floor and not a very low floor. The room itself felt older and more dated than the Hilton, hence my comments about "nicer." The bathroom was not quite a nice, or as clean. There was some mildew on the shower curtain. the furniture was beat up. The location of the Westin was better- very close to BART and many restaurants and stores. The gym was ok, larger than the hilton, and better equipped. There is no lounge at the Westin, so the Hilton wins for having a lounge and at least a continental breakfast. Overall, there are nicer choices nearby, so it just depends on the rate whether I would return.

“Rapporto qualità/prezzo superlativo” Sarà che ormai mi sono abituato agli spazi angusti di New York, ma questo albergo mi è parso davvero spazioso. Sono arrivato una sera alle 22 e ripartito il mattino seguente alle 7, ma ho avuto modo di apprezzare la cortesia del personale della reception e del bar, l'ampiezza della camera (sarebbe più consono chiamarla suite), la comodità del letto. Era tutto nuovo, praticamente immacolato. Rapporto qualità/prezzo superlativo: cento dollari a notte. Colazione a prezzo onesto ($9.50) per un buffet non ricchissimo ma soddisfacente. Consiglio questo hotel sia per lavoro che per piacere.

“Not as strong as other Westins” Location of the hotel is great and the surrounding area/restaurants, etc. is nice. Had some water issues during my stay (no hot water in morning) and although there was apologies from the front desk and managers, that did affect my feelings about the hotel. The rooms are fairly recently updated, but still showed some wear and tear.

“We Will Be Back” This is not a luxurious hotel. However, and ths is a big however, it is one of the best NYC hotels available for value and location. Yes, you may walk a little more to get to Times Square but many of the Broadway shows are within two blocks. Plus, there is a Rite Aid across the street that has groceries and other items expected in a drug store. It is not over priced. Because it is on 8th Avenue, the crowds are not there. Breakfast was CROWDED. I mean CROWDED. One morning the line was 20 deep just to get to the breakfast area. Staff knows this but nothing has been done about it. It may be due to the popularity of the hotel. Rooms are nice. Not spectacular but nice. The concierge is dedicated and helpful. Our rooms were in the 225-250 (before taxes) range which for NYC was a value.

“Nice one night stay” I had a quick 1 night stay at this location. The hotel is downtown and near numerous attractions. The room and bathroom were both immaculate. And for a downtown location, my room was quite large. I would have given this hotel a perfect score if they didn't charge guests to use internet in their room. Are you serious? I loathe upper end hotels that charge to use the internet in your room. I don't want to go down to the lobby or the Starbucks across the street to use the free internet. I want to use it in my room that I paid quite a bit for!

“Small rooms, hot water problems, pleasant enough staff, but comfy beds and good location” Greeted by large glitzy foyer of yesteryear design (think enormous chandeliers, swirly carpets, ornate side tables and you're there) the Reception staff were pleasant and the check-in process quick. The key card worked first time (always a good start) and familiarisation with the room v easy (difficult to hide things in small box - felt NYC hotel room size). If there is one thing that all hotels need to be able to do that's have hot water always on demand - went for x3 showers: 1 v luke warm, 1 warmish, 1 hot - not good. The bed was v comfy and ultimately I was there for a couple of nights and for what I needed it for it was adequate. The hotel needs modernising though and for the price (approx 170GBP pn) was hoping for something a bit more memorable.

“clean hotel, great price” Seattle was "sold out", and this place got good enough reviews on tripadvisor, so I chose it. Good price, nice to be in the center of town. Pros: inexpensive and clean Cons: no A/C, small TV, small bathroom, no internet access Basically, a room, clean sheets, good location. No regrets... I got what I paid for and was not disappointed.

“Clean, comfortable and relaxing” I really enjoy the Hotel Indigo brand. There calm, beachy feel offer a welcome respite when traveling. The Dallas Hotel Indigo is close to hitting the mark with hardwood floors, colorful wall paper and free standing bathroom fixtures. The biggest downfall was no way to play music. The other hotels I have stayed at offer a cd player with a soundtrack and a beach fragrance. This hotel had an alarm clock and that is it. The food at the restaurant was good and their lounge was comfortable and funky. The free WiFi was great as well. If and when my travels take me to Downtown Dallas this hotel will definetly be on my short list.

“Clean, great location” Half the price of other NYC hotels if you book ahead of time, right in the middle of cultural and interesting things to do and see, no frills hotel, impeccably clean, spotless bathroom and linen, safe, friendly enough as I don't aim to befriend the staff, 6$ cab ride from Javits, 7$ from madison area, same for trendy tribeka shopping, diners, shops, street vendors... and right across the street from washington square. only complaint: horrible pillows.

“Bedroom nice, Bathroom bad.” Never having stayed in the Galleria area before, I was very confused by the two Westin's essentially on the same block. Yes, there are two. The Westin Oaks Galleria and The Westin at the Galleria. The Westin at The Galleria has better reviews by and large than The Westin Oaks. I thought I was making reservations at The Westin Galleria but in fact was booking at the other Westin. My transportation from the airport was even confused by it all. Staff at The Westin Oaks was very friendly and seemed responsive to my needs. I complained about smoking on my floor within the first 24 hours and the problem was addressed. This is a non smoking property but I never would have known that when I checked in-the smoke smell in the hallways was very thick. One advantage of this property is the elevator system-one hardly has to ever wait for an elevator and the elevators don't stop at every floor on the way up or down. My bedroom was spacious and clean for the most part. Mattress seemed brand new and very comfortable. Linens on bed were high quality. Nice views of Post Oak area and beyond. And then there was the bathroom. I was in room 1708, by the way because I read other reviews of water issues and the manager wanted to know which room the guest was in. I reported one of the problems when it occurred. A repair man came up after 30 minutes claiming that someone above me must have overfilled the tub. Hah! Just looking at the bathroom ceiling when I checked in, was evidence that there has been chronic water problems in the ceiling. The tiles were covered with furry stuff and corroding. Large spaces between ceiling tiles. What happened was water pouring in great quantities, including pieces of the ceiling from the 18th floor bathroom above me into the bathtub. Lucky for me that I was not in the bathtub when this happened. By the time the repair man arrived the water had stopped. I can't imagine this would be very healthy. But there was another issue with the bathroom and that was the very hot water in the toilet. Every time I went to the bathroom it was like a sauna on my bottom. I didn't see steam rising up but it sure felt like it and one time I thought I had been burned. I am not kidding about this. I think I could have roasted marshmallows over the john! It was very disconcerting. I never put my hand in the water because I thought I would freak out. The toilet storage tank was even hot to the touch. When you turn on the water in a bathtub it usually runs cold and turns warmer the further you turn the handle. With this bathtub it was the opposite. It starts out hot and turns cold the further you turn the handle. The wallpaper in the bathroom was stained and dirty-one area could have possibly been blood stains. Look behind the painting hanging over the toilet. So what's the deal with even renting out rooms in this condition? Does the Hotel hope to get lucky and hope the guests won't make a fuss? Does the front desk think that guests of a certain age will just suck it up? I should have asked to change rooms but sometimes the hassle of packing everything up & moving is just overwhelming. Plus I was not in the room that much. I would have had a beautiful stay if it were not for this issue. It was a major issue. Because of my experience here, I will think twice before I even book at another Westin.

“Fantastic location and great rooms!” I stayed at the Red Lion for a work conference and was overall extremely pleased with my experience. The hotel is in a great location, easily within walking distance of Pike Place, major retail outlets, ferries, etc. The rooms themselves were also large, clean and very comfortable, with nice views of the city (at least on upper floors). The shower had great water pressure too, which I always find a plus when you want to scrub the airplane feeling off! Conference facilities were adequate and the food at both breakfast and lunch was very good. I would stay away from the box lunches though, which did not seem fresh at all. Too bad, as everything else was great! The attached pub is also nice for a drink in the evening and is large enough to accomodate big groups, although the service was a bit slow (one bartender for a place with 40-50 people in it is not enough!). There is also a business center, somewhat awkwardly located in a separate building, but you can print boarding passes here for free. The staff of the hotel was pleasant enough, but I wouldn't say especially friendly or helpful. In fact, the concierge was actually quite rude at one point. Why bother having a surly concierge? All in all though, I think this place is a great option since you are in the middle of everything and the rates were very reasonable considering the quality of the rooms and location. I would definitely recommend it if you are looking for a decent place to stay in downtown Seattle.

“Good location but not really a 4 star hotel” This hotel suffers greatly from setting up too high an expectation. If it is categorized as a 3 or 3.5 stars, it would get a much better review from me. By being in a 4 star class, it became some kind of a false advertisement. The room is large by New York standard but a bit outdated with some molds in bathroom and small but visible signs of wear and tear throughout. Everything still functions well though. There are mini bar, security safe, big flat screen TV, and WiFi internet (for a fee). The lobby has free WiFi. There is no coffee machine in room. The bed is very comfortable with high quality beddings. The lobby is large but check-in and check-out can take some time since it is an enormous hotel with so many guests. I saw many flight crews staying there also. The elevator bank can get pretty busy at times. On the second day, one of the elevators was out of service and there was a long delay trying to get down seeing one jam packed elevator after another going by and couldn't get on. Location is terrific near Times Square and high floors can get some nice views. Our room on 31st floor has a view of the famous New Year's Eve ball. I didn't realize it is illuminated all year round. I took several cool pictures of it. For the priceline rate of about $180 per night, this hotel is perfectly fine for NYC. I wouldn't pay too much more for the condition it's in.

“Some Nice Cosmetic Touches, But...” I stayed at the Warwick for business (location), making my reservations through the hotel’s web site. I had been planning to stay there for some time as the appeal of the structure seemed inviting. (I have stayed at most area hotels.) I enjoy old hotels and understand that you have to overlook issues with maintenance, but the Warwick needs more attention, both to the structure and the staff for the business traveler. My suite was large, but not in excellent repair. Sure, it had a fresh coat of paint on textured stucco walls (like you see in a cheap remodel) and the decorating style was a bit lost on me. But the living room A/C made so much noise, you could not talk on the phone while it was engaged. The bathroom amenities, towels and linens were of mass-market hotel style, and there were issues with the plumbing and electrical outlets. And, you have to enjoy the flight path from Love Field, which apparently goes right over the hotel. The friendliness of the staff escaped me on this trip as there was barely a word uttered in my direction, even when ordering at the Library Bar. The restaurant was closed, which I was not told of in advance, so there was no opportunity to comment. The ‘charm’ highlight was the Library Bar – it is well done and the musicians were great, although I did not find the wait staff very cordial. Some of the old architecture is quite nice. For the money, you should go to the bar, enjoy the piano, and you’ll see what you need to see of the Warwick. The renovation at the Stoneleigh is of a higher caliber and more comfortable. From reading the other reviews, it seems like they do wedding much better.

“A Basic Hotel” We stayed at this hotel property this past weekend for one night in a Standard room category. We are Gold Starwood Preferred Guests and this hotel was not able to extend a late check-out nor was it able to upgrade our room category upon arrival. Although I understand that this hotel caters generally to business travelers, for leisure travelers, I would not pay more than $200 for a Standard Room, even during peak-times in San Francisco. We booked this room initially for over $300 per night but two days before arrival the rate lowered to $199, as went as low as $159 several hours before check-in. For business travelers that will have their expenses reimbursed, then I guess it would not matter what rate you are paying. When calling the hotel directly, it takes the hotel operator sometimes in excess of 10 rings to answer a call. I am not sure if this hotel offers its guests' Concierge services but I would be sure to inquire about it before making plans to stay here if you are going to require the assistance of a Concierge. We made no use of the fitness/spa or restaurant faculties so I will not comment on those aspects of the hotel. For your information, valet parking at this hotel is $42 per night plus taxes. Hotel accommodation taxes is 14%. You can park your car across the street in a public parking garage or turn into the Four Seasons alley way and find the Jesse public parking garage where you will pay $20 max/ per day. Be advised that the Jesse parking garage closes at 10 or 11 and DOES NOT open until the next morning. Your car WILL BE stuck until the next morning so if you will be needing your car throughout the night, do not park here. Check-in at this hotel is consistent with any other convention hotel. It was busy and the check-in staff did not honor their priority check-in line for Gold/Platinum Starwood Guest members. The Standard Room we were given was on the lower floors of this 36 floor hotel and our view was of another rooftop's A/C unit. We were looking down the alley way of the Four Seasons where their guests bring their cars to valet park. It was really a small room. Generally I prefer to stay at hotels where rooms start out at 400-500 sq ft in the Standard Room category but this hotel's standard guest room was half that size. There was a king bed, a desk/chair, a dresser with a flat screen television, and a bath with shower/tub combination. It was not very well ventilated, even with the air conditioning set at 65 degrees throughout the entire during of the stay. The toiletries are of the Westin brand variety (not really good) and all the sheets and towels are available for sale and made exclusively for the Westin hotel chain. If you are a tall individual you may feel that your head may hit the ceilings as they are set really low. We left the DND sign on our door and housekeeping honored the sign so I can't comment on that aspect of the hotel's service. You have an option of whether you want your sheets changed daily or left alone for the entire duration of your stay. We did order room service: three drinks, an entree and one order of an appetizer came up to around $80 dollars. A significant portion of our bill went to taxes, fees, and gratuities. The food was average but it did come up in half an hour. The bell-desk is ALWAYS busy. The valet brought up our car in less than five minutes. We were left waiting for a housekeeping attendant to bring down something we left in our room, granted it was our fault, but it took 10-15 minutes from when we made the call for someone to be sent down. I thought it was an excessive amount of time but maybe it should be expected. Check-out, like check-in took a fair amount of time of waiting as well even though there were 3 front desk agents and 3 guests in front of us. We waited probably 10-15 minutes to check-out. Again, they did not honor their priority check-in/out line for Gold/Platinum guests. The bill they sent up to our room before check-out was correct so there was no need to dispute anything about the bill. The location is excellent and I it would be a fair assessment to say that this hotel is able to get the job done when all you need is a clean and comfortable place to stay while in San Francisco; however, if you want a more personable hotel, this is not the place to stay. And like I mentioned above, for leisure travelers do NOT pay more than $200 for a Standard Room, I assure you unless you are upgraded to a better room, you will regret it as the price is not consistent with the value that you may expect. I know I would have been mad had I paid $300 for this room.

“Perfect location! Great Hotel! Wonderful Staff!” My husband and I stayed here last week for 5 nights. We had an interior King Suite on the 5th floor. It was very comfortable and QUIET, which according to reviews I have read of other hotels, is not an easy thing to find in Union Sq. True to other reviews, the staff was FANTASTIC! The concierge, Hillary, was extremely helpful with booking transportation, tours, special arrangements, anything I asked. And the doormen/bellmen went above and beyond and make it a point to remember you by name. They all make an effort to be the best and it shows. And they have FREE Wi-Fi.....they get big points for that alone! The location was perfect, trolley, cable car turnaround, and BART are all literally around the corner. There is plenty of shopping and restaurants within walking distance and a Walgreen's right around the corner for all those essentials you may have forgotten. There is an italian restaurant attached but we did not get a chance to eat there, although it smelled great and looked to be pretty full every night so that's a good sign. A BIG factor for me in reviewing a hotel is whether or not the beds are comfortable. If you've ever had an uncomfortable bed you know it can ruin a vacation. The beds here are outstanding in my opinion. Very comfortable and cozy. I gave the room 4 out of 5 because there were a few minor things I thought were lacking, such as no mirror outside the bathroom, and no full length mirror, and the towels, while they looked to be new, were not very soft. Also, we like it very cold when we sleep and the window AC unit struggled at times, but it did an ok job, it's not like it was hot outside so it was still comfortable. These are extremely minor things and it would not deter me from staying there again. I just feel there is a little room for improvement. Overall, for the price we paid we felt we got an amazing experience at Hotel Abri and would highly recommend it to anyone looking to stay in the Union Sq. area. I walked down to the Westin for a masage in their spa and the lobby was so crowded and noisy, I was virtually unseen. I almost booked us at the Westin but after reading the great reviews of Hotel Abri decided to go with it......SO glad I did!

“Low-end hotel, but can get good prices for NYC” We stayed on Saturday in mid February. The price is good for NYC and it's in a pretty good location if you want to be near Grand Central Station (which we did because we wanted ot get to a number of other places both uptown and in Brooklyn). The rooms are small - but if all you need is a place to sleep they are fine - clean and comfortable. Currently the hotel lobby in under construction so they were providing breakfast at a cafe down the road. For me the breakfast was good - eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, sweet rolls - but for my wife who likes fruit and yoghurt it was barely adequate.

“What is the deal with the noise?” Stayed at the Omni for 4 nights on business. A prior reviewer hit the nail on the head about noise coming from the elevators. My room was probably 6 or 7 doors down from the elevator and you could hear loud humming as the elevator went up and down ALL DAY LONG! Granted, it was less frequent late at night but an annoyance nonetheless. One expects peace and quiet and a good night's sleep from an Omni hotel. This problem alone would cause me never to stay here again and never to recommend this hotel to anyone else. I am giving this hotel 3 stars because everything else about my stay was pretty good. The room was clean and spacious and nicely appointed. Service was professional and friendly. Price wasn't bad at $100/night. The location is tolerable but you must be willing to do everything at the hotel or have a car at your disposal to get to any restaurants or shopping. It really is in the middle of nowhere. But, it is convenient to the airport and there are restaurants and strip mall stores only 1 or 2 exits down the road. It's quite a drive to downtown and Dallas traffic can be fairly miserable. If on business and needing to stay in the area, I had a much more pleasant stay at the Doubletree in Farmers Branch just down the road and would recommend that to others.

“Brand new and sparkling” This place opened in May so it's new and off to a good start. We stayed in a Towneplace in Henderson NV, and liked it so decided to try another one. This newer one addressed our previous problems in Henderson. They added a larger closet to the kitchen area and the bathroom door didn't hit the bed, but in general it might have just been a bigger room. But most of all, the AC was perfect at this location. The vents didn't blast right in your face and the thermostat worked well. We were very comfortable and slept well, especially on the incredibly comfortable bed.
