As noted in our Henderson review this chain has a well organized extended stay setup. Also at this location, they had a great patio area with new, well equipped barbeque grills. We were here for 3 nights and wanted to give it 5 stars, but some service issues lost some points. Though friendly, the staff seemed disorganized. Our keys had to be reprogrammed everyday and this was a pain, especially when we came in late and had to go back downstairs. We were told several times to make sure we didn't carry the key near our cell phones even though we're fanatic about keeping the keys far away from our phones. And it wasn't just one key, it was both of our keys. One desk clerk said it happened all the time, the other said it should never happen. Another time housekeeping forgot to give us toilet paper and we requested more and it was delivered at midnight! They just need to work out some kinks in service, but otherwise a great stay.

“Good hotel, so-so location” I was pleased with this hotel, but am not sure I would stay here again because of the location. It only took me about 5 minutes to get to downtown, which was great, but there are NO restaurants near this hotel. Next time, I'd probably stay a little further from downtown to be closer to restaurants. Plus, were this hotel not right next to the Hilton Anatole, I might say it's not in such a great looking neighborhood (unlike a previous reviewer, I did not see any vagrants in the area). My room was large, quiet, very clean and very comfortable. The bed and shower were both great. I did have to switch rooms during my stay due to a dead air conditioner (not too surprised... Dallas in August). Very few TV channels compared to most hotels nowadays. No problems with the wired internet service. Breakfast was excellent. I ordered room service one night, and it was OK. Service overall was very good.

“Ignore the bad reviews - this hotel is perfect for an airport hotel.” Just had a 1 night stay here before a flight. I was pretty pleased with the whole stay. The rooms were nicely decorated, bathrooms were new and clean. The bed was super comfy and the airport noise did not bother me at all. My brother's room had very noisy neighbours but I guess that is not the hotels fault! I got a free drink, internet and breakfast through a combination of my rate and by virtue of being Gold. Overall I would definately stay here again. aks120

“Nice place” Great value for the money - you get a whole suite! Kitchen, foyer, small sitting area, dressing area and bathroom. Comfortable bed, very clean and spacious, easy parking. Friendly and easy check-in and check-out and helpful reception. Free coffee in the lobby is nice too. Only bad thing is our room was right next to the elevator, so we heard some noise outside our room, so next time we are there, we will ask for a room further from the elevator.

“Great place” We booked this place last minute and didnt know what to expect... The location was brilliant couldn't have been better, was right next to the greyhound station, and 2 streets from Beale Street, also within walking distance to Sun Studios, the bus to Graceland and the river etc... The rooms were being refurbished when we were there, so it looked pretty run down at the front, but we were put in one of the new ones round the back, i'm pretty sure we were the first people in the room since it had been done out, so everything was sparkly clean and the bathroom was HUGE! I'm sure once the other rooms are all done (which they might be by now) the place will be awesome. The prices were very reasonable, we wanted to stay an extra night at the weekend and the lady at reception let us have it for the same price although they were supposed to be more due to the local festival going on that weekend which was nice of her. I would definately stay again!

“Great Newer Hotel Near Plenty of Downtown Attractions” On a recent visit to San Antonio for a business, I opted to extend my stay by 1 night and experience the La Quinta Inn & Suites for the first time. I was very impressed! The hotel, opened around 2005, is a new construction hotel built near the former site of the very first La Quinta Motor Inn (opened in 1968 for the HemisFair). You can read all about the brand history through a mural of collected artifacts of the last 40 plus years on display at this hotel. It was really a pleasant surprise. Upon arrival, I was checked in by a friendly but busy front desk staff. My room was ready early, so I had time to settle in and enjoy the expansive pool area and hot tub. It was mid afternoon on a bright sunny Friday, but only a handful of people enjoying the pool. The area was fresh and clean, and the water sparkling! My room was on the 14th floor (of 15), but with plenty of fast moving elevators, there was rarely a wait. The suite was spacious, clean and cool. The bed was extremely comfortable and everything was in working order. The TV service features a really nice bonus – several channels of “ambient choices”! A great way to relax. The room included a work desk, free Wi-Fi (although slow), and a coffee maker, fridge and microwave. Bathroom amenities were basic, as expected for a limited service hotel. The hotel features a rare option for La Quinta – a lounge area with light menu. I enjoyed a glass of wine before retiring, but opted for dinner at one of the many restaurants within a few blocks of the hotel. Although I knew it would be chaotic on a Saturday morning, I decided to experience the free breakfast. It was indeed ridiculously busy, a reason why free breakfast has little value to me, a single traveler in this case. I imagine it would have been far more pleasant during the business week. The dining area and lobby however were very inviting. Not flying out until later, the hotel happily held my bags for me while I explored the city once more before leaving. Check-out was slow because the front desk is always busy, and often multitasking by also taking reservations. The hotel is directly across the street from the RiverCenter Mall, and about a block from the River Walk itself. You’re less than a 1⁄2 mile from the Alamo, Convention Center and Zoo – in other words, a great location and good value in downtown San Antonio! Upon departure, the Bell Staff quickly and politely gathered my bags and called a cab. Overall, a great first experience with La Quinta, and I would definitely recommend the Convention Center location for midweek business travel, families, and easy access to many of the Downtown offerings.

“great value” Only stayed 1 nite...the last nite of a 13 day trip that encompassed an alaskan cruise and 3 different hotel stays and this was our favorite hotel. Beautiful location overlooking lake union.. watch the boats and seaplanes take off...hint ...pay the $10 extra for the lakefront room and request a sleeper sofa/loveseat, I believe those rooms may be a bit larger. Anyway, hotel and rooms very clean. nice lobby, nice indoor and outdoor pools. Great free bkfst. The hotel isn't near anything so they have a great free shuttle ( tip the driver) that does drop offs and pick ups every half hour. Free internet...2 computers. Exercise room had ex bike, treadmill and epiliptical machine. would stay here again in a heartbeat

“Needs a little fine tuning” For my birthday weekend my husband splurged on the Palace. We booked online and given the option to upgrade for $25 so we did. The valet guy was nice and offered to take our bags. At the front desk there was a small line but what was surprising only 2 desk clerks. Find that odd since it's tourist season. The front desk lady was friendly and had us checked in pretty quick. The room itself is a nice size #558 and has a view of Montgomery. Towels are nice and soft something that I really appreciate. The bathroom is a tad small but that seems the norm in SF. Nice toiletries. The bed was nice and comfortable with soft sheets. We got to check out our friends room #512 and they had a small sofa and a coffee maker. I liked their room layout better. In our room I found no bathrobes so I called and got them in a quick time. We checked out the pool and it is a pretty nice size with some chairs and tables to hang out at. We then had a drink at the Pied Piper just so we could see the famous painting and it's worth seeing. We enjoyed the dark ambiance there. We really wanted to eat at the Garden Court but we missed breakfast and it was time for Sunday brunch for $75/person!!! When we checked out on Sunday there still were only 2 front desk clerks. I am still undecided if to come back to Palace because of the pricing and the little nice details some other hotels offer. I would have liked to see some tea options in the room and maybe a discount for the Sunday brunch.

“Gut!” Während meinem Aufenthalt in Phoenix verbringe ich 4 Nächte im Hotel Westin Phoenix Downtown. Die Fahrt vom Flughafen Sky Harbour zum Hotel dauert nur wenige Minuten. Das Haus ist und wirkt sehr neu und gepflegt, die Mitarbeiter sind allesamt typisch amerikanisch-freundlich. Chek-in problemlos und zügig, die Zimmer ausreichend groß und gut ausgestattet: angenehmer Fernsehsessel mit Fusshocker, seperate Sitzecke, Schreibtisch mit 2 Bürostühlen, Badezimmer mit großer Walk-in Regendusche und optisch getrennter Toilette. Im Hotel befindet ein Restaurant (Provence) welches den ganzen Tag über eine gute und abwechslungsreiche Küche bietet. Auch das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis kann als sehr gut bezeichnet werden. Das Gym im Haus ist sehr gut und mit Geräten der neuesten Generation ausgestattet, hoch oben befindet sich ein Outdoor-Pool, welcher zwar nicht riesig groß, aber dennoch ausreichend ist.

“The 24/7 hot tub is really the only thing worth mentioning” But in case you're curious I'll dish a few more details... Good stuff: -the WA State Convention Center has these hotel catalogues (free, you'll find them on the rack of hotel brochures by the visitors booth) that almost always include a coupon good for a night or two here at just $79.99 (walk in only, subject to availability) -large hot tub open 24 hours a day -free wifi -in room microwave and free continental breakfast -practically across the street from the Space Needle -A few blocks from Whole Foods Not so wonderful: -11am check out -In a slightly shady neighborhood -Hallway noise travels into guest rooms -The weight room is very basic -Every room is identical in size

“One of the best big-city IC's, Great Base for Touring Chicago” I'm a longtime Intercontinental club member and generally have good success with all of their brands. This IC is one of their best in the system. While the "historic" tower is old, it's clean, meticulously maintained, and comfortable unlike other old hotels in the Chicago Loop. I note that some complaints here are about small rooms in the newer tower. This is the case in all big cities - they should try Tokyo or Paris to see a REAL small, five star room! Ditched the car in the burbs and relied totally on the CTA. Inner city travel in Chicago is terrific - get a prepaid card and go nuts. Two drawbacks to the hotel -- frequent sirens at night, also a "big city" thing. We were on the 19th floor and could hear them, but they didn't bother us. And the internet service, the usual grossly expensive IC hotel charge, and subsequent slow service. Wish Intercontinental would stop using the internet to gouge travelers! Staff at the hotel uber-courteous, friendly, and knowledgeable about Chicago, both the value trips and the ripoffs.

“Would stay here again” Pleasantly surprised and would definitely stay here again next time! Pro's: Great location - lots of restaurants nearby, convenient subway access, 15 minute walk to Penn Station, Greenwich Village, Soho. Comfortable room, comfortable bed, eager-to-please staff. The free breakfast, afternoon coffee/tea are always nice. Also got a great price - called 2 days before to see if they had a better rate than I had originally booked at and they did. Con's: Very minor wear and tear problems in bathroom (running toilet which they promptly fixed) and no hot water second morning. Housekeeping was close to 5:00 p.m. so I skipped the cleaning. The lack of hot water was annoying, but since it was not a problem the first day, I assume it was a one-time issue and this would not prevent me from staying again.

“Bait and switch!” The W should stand for Why? why are you mopping tread mills at 6:45 AM and not drying them? Why Invite the guest to coffee and then charge for it? Why is the hotel so unhip? 80's are over, get back to serving your business cliental.

“another relaxing night” had passed by this hotel a few times on the way to races, but never had a chance to stay until April 2012. stayed here overnight. was impressed. the hotel is very well designed. beautiful long passageways with marble and stone. several different restaurants including a great steak house. the rooms were wonderful. the service was very accommodating. the athletic center was very nice. they even had a starbucks in the hotel. that was incredibly convenient. also it is across the street from the convention center, so even more convenient. walking distance to everything. would HIGHLY recommend.

“Had a great time!” My hubby and I decided to take a staycation in our hometown of Denver. We live down in the southern burbs and rarely get out towards the Stapleton area, and we wanted to visit the Bass Pro Shop, so we decided to stay at this hotel. The Lobby area of the hotel is very nice, decorated in various lovely colors. The lobby is a large, very tall Atrium with the rooms facing out towards the courtyard. My husband is a Marriott Rewards member, so we were upgraded to a room on the concierge level, floor 12. The room was very nice, the room had nice furniture and a nice west facing view of the mountains. Thanks to all the great Tripadvisor members who commented on the train whistle that kept them up, we mentioned this when checking in, and evidently if you are facing west (which is the best view of the Mountains anyway) you don't hear it as well. I didn't hear it all! The room had a nice balcony, which since it is still winter we didn't use, but it would be great in the spring and summer. The room was very clean and the bathroom nice and well appointed with Aveda products which I love. We wanted to eat over at the Northfield shopping area which is where Bass Pro Shop is located and the hotel has a shuttle which drove us there and then returned at 10:30 pm to pick us up. That was nice as it allowed us to have a some drinks and not having to worry about driving. That was nice. There is a small but nice bar in the lobby of the atrium and evidently an Italian restaurant at the hotel, but we did not eat there. Our stay here was very nice, and I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in the Stapleton area of Denver. It would be nice for someone also going to or leaving the airport even though it is a little ways away from DIA. Thank you, we will return!

“A” We stayed from March 24-28, 2007, in two rooms. The furniture is dated but functional. Closet space is limited. The room near the elevator was quiet whereas the room facing 56th street was somewhat noisy. The maid service was excellent in one room and sporadic in the other during our stay. The check-in desk personnel were excellent. The Italian restaurant in the basement was fine. We will stay here again. Overall a very good experince.

“new hotel, large rooms, comfy beds” Great new hotel with nice staff. Got a good last minute deal rate of $357 per night for a deluxe king and was upgraded to superior king, through LHW.com (booked a few days prior to traveling). Bed was vey comfortable, room was quiet and very large for New York and was clean and fresh (hard not to be being open for only 2 weeks). We were there to see a show. The hotel is several blocks away from time square, so it was a 5-10 min walk to the theatre. But near the empire state building and Bryant park. Has a Spa and a nice gym too.

“Not what we had hoped for.” Sorry I did not read the TA reviews prior to spending over $220 to spend one night here.The main hook is it's across the street proximity to USC (the purpose of our stay). The hotel is not owned by the university but houses many USC students in a dorm like set up. Hallways, pool,etc with lots of students.The hotel is markedly outdated, has noise issues (students living there and street), and needs a major interior renovation. The Sleep Number Beds were not comfortable (each person can select there own level of discomfort) and feel like you are sleeping on an air mattress. Water presure in the shower was not great and the bathroom looked like it was out of the late 60's (yes, I'm old enough to remember!). Continental breakfast at McKay's had less appeal and variety than many other hotels which charge considerably less for their rooms. I would have never included it in my room rate had I known. We had a juice and coffee then left for breakfast elsewhere. The hotel staff was pleasant and I didn't even bother to complain because I figured it was my own fault for not doing my homework better. If you have to stay across the street from USC then ok, otherwise, you can do better elsewhere.

“Great hotel for a business trip” I was worried that the Hampton Inn would have a lot of street noise. The hotel is located near a busy street and close to the freeway. Yet, I did not have any issues with traffic noises all night. The hotel has excellent insulation. There is a lack of restaurants in the area. There is a AM/PM next door, a Taco Bell and a sit down Mexican Restaurant-Tio Leo. You have to get in the car and drive a couple of miles to get to food. Check in was a breeze. The hotel staff were very friendly. The fitness center was adequate. The breakfast room was OK for someone in a hurry. Good selection of cereals and muffins, but nothing substantial (coffee was good). The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The Hampton Inn was up to par with the Hilton brand standards. The bathroom was also clean. The room had free high speed internet. I did not use the WIFI since they had a CAT-5 cable in the room. The desk was spacious enough for work. Also, the coffee table and couch was a great addition in the room. All-in-all, I would stay here again.

“a great deal with the 30% discount” We booked a 3 night stay here because they were offering 30% off with a 3 night stay. We were in town for a Colts game and the hotel was a short drive from downtown (15 minutes). The general manager checked me in and she was most polite and helpful. She even gave me a map of the shopping areas which were about 3 miles west of the hotel. We found a movie theatre, several large stores and lots of restaurants in that area. Our room was large and included a king bed, a desk and a chair with an ottoman. There was plenty of room for a couch, which would have been more useful. The free internet was great. Our bathroom was clean, but the fixtures looked a bit dated. On the plus side, the shower had a variable speed head which I was actually able to adjust -- most of the time when you try to adjust them you end up just about unscrewing the enitre shower head. Our bed was adequate-- too hard for my liking. The HVAC unit wasn't terribly efficient either -- it was either on or off. When it was on, it was entirely too hot. If we turned it down, it did not keep the room at a consistent temperature. The breakfast was OK. They offered more hot items than most motels, which was nice. They had eggs every day and alternated between ham and sausage. There were biscuits and gravy, but one morning they ran out of gravy, another morning they ran out of biscuits. When I asked the breakfast attendant about them he answered that "someone had gone to get them". The breakfast attendant was about the only unfriendly person in the place-- he did not speak well, wore baggy jeans and even a knit cap one morning. He did not present well. A guest with a dog walked into the breakfast area one morning and no one asked her to leave. Fortunately, she did not stay long.I am glad that we didn't pay full price for this motel. But for the price we paid, it was adequate.

“Loved it!” Genuinely friendly staff. Clean rooms, nice amenities. Informative and AVAILABLE concierge. (I've stayed other places where you could never reach the concierge by phone, and then would have to wait in lines in the lobby.) Great location (near Rockefeller Plaza). Hotel program worth joining (free breakfast beverages, free internet access, turn-down service with chocolates). Will definitely stay again.

“I'd make it my home!” This has become our go to hotel when we go to a base ball game or desire to stay near the wharf or embarcadero. There is nothing that is missed by the staff and hotel. We have stayed numerous times. From the moment you drive up to the hotel til the moment you leave you are treated with respect from a kind and caring staff that is also always knowledgable. Sure parking comes with a fee but everywhere in the city does, so park your car and enjoy their town car service, the city's transit or as we do...just walk. Walk across the street and you can catch a rail. It's so centrally located to the wharf, embarcadero, a Giants game. The hotel is modernly decorated but very comfortable. You are treated to a warm cloth at check in and always a smile. The rooms range in size but are all comfortable with cozy linens and care around every corner with details. If you are seeking a quieter stay ask for an inside room. If you like the views of the city, request a room with a view of the clock tower and embarcadero. The hotel has provided a beautiful seating arrangement in the rooms that we have stayed in to enjoy these views! As a member of Joie de Vivre hotel's club (a free sign up) we always receive a bottle of wine at are room all chilled! Don't forget to sign up. The restaurant and bar is just as nice. The food is good and the drinks tasty! Its sitting area outside is great for relaxing and decompressing before heading up to your room. My favorite hotel for anything!

“A perfectly fine hotel” The XCrowne Plaza in Denver is a perfectly fine downtown, business hotel. The hotel is clean, has decent rooms, decent service adn staff, and is a great alternatie for business travelers coming to teh Convention Center but not wanting to pay the higher rates at other hotels. Our stay in July 2012 had no major problems. The safe in the room wouldn't function properly, but upon asking for help, at the front desk, a staff person was at our room before we were back to it! Concierge ws helpful, bar had a nice and affordable happy hour, and the hotel overall was more than acceptable.

“Fantastic Choice in Boston's Back Bay” My girlfriend and I spent a weekend in March at the Copley Square Hotel for a "mom's weekend away." The rate we got for our room was outstanding--Boston in the "off season."! The hotel is very contemporary, having Reception "pods" and "intuition specialists." The staff was very friendly and helpful. The nightly wine reception is a very nice touch. The decor is very chic. The room was a bit tight with 2 double beds, but those beds were extremely comfortable!! The bathroom was a great size, too. I liked the little touches the hotel offered, including the free wi-fi, the "Today and Tomorrow" feature listing, and the "Bedtime Stories." The location was excellent for us--lots of shopping, dining, and areas to walk. My one complaint is that I think our room (room #314) was directly above the bar/club. On Saturday night, I was kept up from 12am-2am from excessive noise. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

“Good Value, Good Location” I spent one night here in September 2010. Overall, this hotel is an extremely good value. It is new, very clean, and efficiently operated. It is also in a great location on Adams, just a short walk from the Art Institute, Millenium Park and other attractions. The hotel is nothing fancy and doesn't bowl you over with amenities, but one shouldn't expect that for this price in this great location. The only "ding" I can really give it is that my 9th floor single room had extremely poor wireless reception. So slow my iPad wouldn't even connect. Be forewarned: This hotel isn't smack in the middle of the action. The Loop is populated with office buildings and little else. If you want to be in the heart of the hotel/restaurant/shopping area, you'll need to take the 10 minute walk to River North and the Magnificent Mile.

“Excellent Budget Accommodation” Stayed here for four days with family in May 2012. It is adjacent to a neighborhood that I would guess houses families that economists might refer to as the "working poor." There is a small church across the road. You will need to drive to restaurants and shopping, but fast roads are close by. We never felt unsafe during our stay, even when driving through the adjacent neighborhood after dark. Noise was never a problem, and we never saw or heard of any "busts" or crime in the area. There were two "biker" couples staying at the Pinn during our stay, and when I saw them drinking outside, I thought "Oh no. I hope there's no noise tonight." We heard nothing more than voices at reasonable decibel levels. The Pinn facility is kept up so well that it looks and feels like an oasis in the midst of the more run-down structures around it, which I guess could be attractive to a potential thief, but I suspect that Pinn management keeps a close eye on the premises (and cars) at all hours. Our room was very clean, and management was very responsive. The free wifi worked well. As long as I felt confident that management was monitoring the facility at night, I would have no problems staying there again. It was a great, no-frills, bargain option that management should be commended for offering to those of us who need travel on a budget.

“LOTS OF TLC” We just arrived Nov. 17; we were early so our room wasn't ready but the young woman at the front desk was so helpful; she took all our luggage and then explained about which restaurants were close by and even had a coupon for us. When we returned from lunch, not only was our room ready but all our luggage had been taken up plus several boxes of materials which I had shipped earlier and which I needed for business meetings were also in the suite. The suite is huge and immaculate with floor to ceiling windows overlooking Michigan Ave. We have a full kitchen, big living room, bedroom, bath, washer and dryer. The amount of space is amazing plus breakfast is included. We are looking forward to this stay; with these accommodations and such a responsive staff we know we'll enjoy our time here.

“Good place to stay in SF” I stayed for two nights to attend a business conference on Market Street and was happy I did. I love that the location was really convenient to Union Square, Market Street, the Financial District and Nob Hill. I really like the gym in the basement! As you might expect for a Kimpton Hotel, the staff was perfect. Unfortunately, the pictures on the travel websites really do this hotel a disservice - it looks much better in person.

“Not Bad !” This wasn't too bad. I've stayed at most of the hotels on Shelter Island and this one is better than average. I've stayed twice recently. Once in the Casa Del Mar building and once in one of the tropical themed little huts that jut out from the other buildings. I preferred the layout of the rooms in the Casa del Mar building because they were quiet (better insulation) and also more spacious than the other "tropical" themed building. Overall the rooms were very clean and the staff were very friendly and accomodating (both times). The room service was reasonably priced (not a complete rip off like most hotels) and was a good value with tasty food (good waffles!). Drawbacks were that the room in the Casa del Mar building needed work in the bathroom (needing grouting to be redone and the wallpaper had started to peel). The "tropical" themed other building (hut) was great (had a nice little porch area that was relaxing to enjoy the breeze). BUT it was very noisy (almost no insulation between the room and the next room). It was also more cramped than the other room, as they made the bathroom too large (weird layout) yet without a bath tub! But other than that I would rate this hotel fairly well. I would give it a B+ for the Shelter Island area. Would recommend for tourists and locals alike. Would not recommend for noisy families with kids or for partiers. The location is great and the decor is pretty good. Price is about right for what you get. This is a good middle-of-the-road comfortable hotel in a great location.

“Great Hotel” This is my 2nd stay with this hotel in the last 3 months. Dan The front desk staff that night made our late check in very smooth and we got a great room on the high floor as we requested. housekeeping staff keep everything clean and all the bathroom supplies stocked. The bed is always very comfortable and I wish I can have one in my own bedroom. Great location and very close to the shopping area and attraction.

“Walking in Memphis” My husband and I stayed at the Vista Inn Motel for 3 nights in early January. The location is terrific only a couple of minutes walk to Beale St. We were visiting during the quiet season, so the streets were empty at night, however it's safe to get around Downtown on foot. Bed was comfy and the area was quiet. Only cons were had to ask for a restock of fresh towels andtoilet paper, some of the towels were old and had with the previous user's hair intertwined in the fabric, and there is a fee of $5 per person to have bags stored at reception at check out. Otherwise; everything else was fine. The hotel is pretty basic, but that's what you get for a 2 star accomodation. It was clean, safe and in a good part of town and that's all we wanted.

“It's a Days Inn...” This place is just okay. I would not have stayed here, but my company booked this hotel for show at the convention center. Right across the street from convention center, so that's good, but it's a Days Inn!!! :-( The rooms were just okay, small, cheap fixings. Tools were left in room from work I guess someone was fixing?!? Does have frig and microwave in room. Never used them. Maids service very slow, back from show at 4pm still not cleaned!!! What?!!? Very small bar area. They had a small set-up on patio on Sat., it was chilly outside so sat inside. Asked to move because outside folks not associated with inside folks. This was an advertised event at front desk!! And inside was EMPTY. In fact the restaurant was never busy! Front desk folks and bellmen very helpful and nice! The one bright spot. Don't stay unless pocketbook dictates.

“Nice hotel for a longer stay” I stayed at the Candlewood as I was visiting the University of Texas. I was a bit apprehensive reading the reviews so had low expectations. As the university had once booked me at an adorable bed and breakfast for a previous stay a few years past, I was concerned about this choice. The hotel check-in was convenient and fast; everyone who worked in the hotel were very helpful. The room was large and had all of the amenities for a longer stay—large fridge, clean oven + microwave, dishwasher and sink. Popcorn was waiting in the microwave, and the hotel provided an in-room coffee maker. The blowdryer appeared European style (rectangular head) but had surprisingly high power. Only soap and shampoo is provided of the "White Rain" variety. Several clean ribbed cotton towels were provided as well (not the frayed ones suggested by earlier reviews). The room had a large closet and several wooden hangers. I would bring more if you have more than one suitcase. A laundry basket is also provided in the closet. The hotel also provides an in-room VCR+DVD player and a CD player. I had two alarm clocks to choose from. Internet access was great-- free, no problems and had fast connections every evening. The hotel does not provide coffee in the morning, although they did offer a free dinner one evening. The Candlewood has a room that contains several items (snacks, aspirin, toothpaste, ice cream, frozen TV dinners) that can be purchased for a reasonable price on their honor system. I liked the ability to get some pop or tea at odd hours. They have a laundry room with several washers and dryers + a reasonably large exercise room. The hotel did have a smell (a bit more than other places I have stayed). My room is cleaned only once a week, which may lead to this. I think they are trying to get rid of the smoke. It was nothing intolerable. A movie theater and a nice Mexican restaurant + bar are located within walking distance nearby. I ordered a cab to the airport at the front desk, and he arrived promptly at 6:00A. I paid around $45 to the airport. I think you'd like it. I would stay here again.

“Terrible noisy room, not that clean but good hotel location.” I stayed at the Poweel for three nights from 25th June 2004 on my way to Hawaii and for the Gay Pride weekend in SF. This was not my first time at the Powell but on the other occasion I had a much nicer room. I was given a twin bedded room with two single beds when I had requested a double through Expedia.. Okay fine this happenes sometimes on a busy weekend and they could not swap my room. However the room was right next to an ice machine that kept me awake clunking away all night. I know I paid a budget price but the rooms are in desperate need of renovation and are not that clean really. A place to stay if you want to be in a good location to get around the city but don't plan to spend more time in your room than when you are asleep.

“My preferred downtown Charlotte hotel” The Hilton Downtown is my go-to hotel for business in downtown Charlotte. The hotel is convenient to all the major office buildings and other hotels downtown; it takes us less than 10 minutes to walk to/from the corner of Trade and Tyron from the Hilton (which is itself adjacent to One and Two Wells Fargo Center); the Wells Fargo Area is two blocks away. The staff is great, the hotel spotless, well equipped business center, and a nice HHonors lounge. There are no hospitals nearby and the nearest fire station is several blocks away so there is little outside noise on the upper floors. If this Hilton isn’t available there is a new Hampton Inn & Suites several blocks further away from downtown that while a longer walk, I still recommend as an alternative.

“Great Find” At the last minute I changed my reservations to the Stoneleigh due to all the rave reviews on Tripadvisor. I was very pleased that I switched to the Stoneleigh. Great location, beautiful, newly renovated, very friendly and fantastic rooms. The only complaint was the air conditioning vent was right above the bed and it was a bit uncomfortable when it went on. I do not know if this applies to all the room. I loved the decor in the lobby. It reminded me Gaudi and the Casa Fuster in Barcelona. The bar was happening at night and the breakfast innovative and delicious. We also at a massage at the spa and it was very nice. I would absolutely recommend and and repeat my stay at the Stoneleigh.

“Excellent boutique hotel in awesome location” What an awesome find! Great location right across from some of Boston's beautiful landmarks & a stone's throw from the MBTA (Boston Metro) Park Street station! Hubby & I arrived after 11pm and easily made our way from Boston airport to Park St station. The hotel was fantastic. I had been corresponding with Thomas the concierge before we arrived and he was exceptionally helpful and friendly answering my questions and helping me to plan our 4 day stay. Thomas had also assisted our request for a quiet room and a refrigerator all before we arrived! The room was lovely. Modern, sleek, tastefully furnished and welcoming. The only things we werent in love with was the queen size bed (tough when we're both 6 feet tall!) and the tiny shower cubicle! Again, tough to manoeuvre in and out of when it was a tiny square space with a door that pushes into that space barely giving you enough room to even get in! Trust me...you wouldnt want to be podgy! As mentioned we arrived late and found that there was a tiny Boston bar/cafe across the laneway called Barracuda where we were able to get some seafood for a light snack before bed. Alternatively there is also a popular bar on Tremont St right across the road too. We found the location to be right in the heart of everything. Boston is a great walking city and it was easy to navigate to see the sights. My best parting tip is a little cafe called 'Thinking Cup' on Tremont St opposite Boston Common (maybe 5-7 mins walk away) where you can get the most delicious Stump Town coffee made by the most expert baristas around! The cafe also does tasty sandwiches and breakfast and seemed to stay open later than 10pm most nights! Oh...and the Woodward Gastro Pub at the Ames hotel was delicious too! Great Napa Valley Wines (Sebastiani pinot) and ridiculously delicious duck flat bread & lamb breast with succotash! The lamb was incredibly good value at $23. Ps....7 eleven was walking distance for basics as is the Loews Cinema in case you have time to catch a movie!

“Service and cleanliness much improved” I've reviewed the Residence Inn at Dupont Circle about 2-3 years ago and given it an average rating. I must upgrade to four stars to cite major improvements in cleanliness and service. This Residence Inn has really improved its cleanliness, both in common areas and rooms. I had no problem walking around my room and to the laundry down the hall in socks and not worrying about ugly stains. I also experienced fabulous customer service from all the staff during this trip. The front desk upgraded me to a 1-bedroom, provided office supplies and equipment, greeted me every time I entered and made it very easy when I needed to re-register after leaving due to an east coast snow storm. I must give a special shout-out to the food service crew who very kindly held the complimentary evening meal for me past the meal closing time as I dragged myself in from the 7" inches of snow after my flight was canceled. Is it the absolute finest place to stay in DC? No, but the location can't be beat and the staff service was so great that I will be coming back.

“We really enjoyed our week at Millenium Hilton NYC” I stayed here on a trip to NYC with my mother for Xmas 2011. We stayed here for 8 nights. This is a pretty fabulous hotel. The views, are really spectacular, especially from the higher floors. I stayed in a Junior Suite on level 49, and my Mum was staying in a room on the smoking floor, which was on a corner and also had a very lovely outlook of the old church and the Woolworth Building. Both rooms were very comfortable and well presented, with very large wall like windows. The location is great for exploring Lower Manhattan - and the subway is just on the corner near the hotel, so it is quite quick and easy to get up to midtown also. The impact of the WTC rebuild is felt while staying in the hotel, as it really is directly across the road from the construction. My mother and I found this quite powerful and moving, and also meeting some of the staff that were still working in the hotel from the time of 9/11, and hearing there stories was a very moving experience. There was 24 hour construction that was occurred during our stay, and there was some noise, but it wasn't overbearing. One nice thing is all rooms have windows that open slightly, so even on a very high floor one can get fresh air. The lobby bar here is really great. Great bar tenders that make lovely drinks, and provide a really nice 'local' bar feel. I really enjoyed being able to come back and relax at the bar in the evenings after sight seeing and enjoy the ambience there. There is quite a nice relaxed and second home feel about this Hilton, which I really enjoyed. Not being right in the centre of NYC, and also probably being a business hotel catering to many return guests, gave it a really nice feeling. We both felt very comfortable and secure in our stay. The housekeeping dept. were fantastic. We really noticed their professionalism and attention to detail. It was a nice touch that the ice was placed in our ice buckets at turn down time. Very lovely staff we encountered there. Overall, I wouldn't have any hesitations to recommend this hotel. It is a really comfortable, and well appointed property, and we enjoyed the food and drinks we had here. We had room service several times, and dined in the restaurant also, everything was lovely. That said, even though I like the relaxed and not so uptight atmosphere here, there were some moments were the service of the front desk, operator, and concierge could have been a little tighter. The staff were always professional, though I did feel a few times the service standard wasn't quite as attentive or experienced as what I am used to experiencing at Hilton hotels, which was a surprise in NYC! The service at Hilton Times Square in these front office departments was definitely noticeably better. I think that this could be improved - a more service orientated outlook, without being to intrusive or forceful, and this hotel would be really fantastic. The breakfast sort of suffered a little from this hit and miss service quality too unfortunately. The dinner waiters were great, as were the bar staff in the lobby as mentioned. Anyway, thanks to all the staff at this hotel. The service was overall good, and we really felt at home here on the other side of the world from Australia over xmas. A special thanks to the Housekeeping and Lobby Bar staff for looking after the 'Molony's' : ) Try Andy's Afternoon - a cocktail in Liquid Assets Lobby Bar, and a must - is Century 21 across the road for unbelievable discounted shopping. Definitely by all your I Love NYC souvenir items here-- it is so much cheaper than anywhere else!

“Going Downhill - Avoid” We have now stayed at the Madison three times. The first was soon after it opened several years ago. At that time the service was wonderful. I could not have asked for a better place to stay in Memphis. When we left, we felt we had been treated well. The second stay was a couple of years ago. The service seemed to have gone downhill. The little touches that had made it so special were gone. Then, booked the zoo package for the 13th for my daughter's 9th birthday. The advertisement on the web is copied straight from the website today. Memphis Zoo Package 04/27/2005 - 12/31/2007 12/31Since the arrival of the Chinese Giant Pandas, the Zoo has become a "must see" attraction to Memphis visitors. This package includes accommodations in our deluxe room, continental breakfast, 2 adult tickets and 2 children tickets along with valet. We arrived, checked in and went to our room, which was nice, but on the small side. When we returned from the zoo and our evening outings - there was no turndown service. The only thing that was different was two small chocolates that had been tossed on the counter. Pretty frustrating for what is supposed to be such a fine hotel. The next morning we had been charged for valet parking and were told that a continental breakfast did not go with the Zoo package. It is on their website today! When my husband complained they eventually told him that they could arrange it - at this point we were frustrated and just wanted to get out of there. They did remove the valet parking charge from our bill. We won't be going back to the Madison. The service was not what it should have been for a hotel that advertises as a luxury hotel. The pool was out of order, the rooftop bar was closed for a wedding - so - I would avoid the madison. I have stayed there when the service was absolutely great - and it is nowhere near that now.

“Great location, value” I attended a conference at this hotel, staying for 5 nights. The hotel was clean and nice. I appreciated the great downtown location. I would definitely recommend this hotel. I had a special club room that had better decor than the regular rooms. The workout facility is really nice and overlooks city streets. The only complaint I really have is that some of the food that was served by the hotel for our conference was underwhelming. I ate nearly all of my meals as buffets provided by the hotel for our company. It was certainly serviceable but many of the dishes lacked flavor. It is a fun hotel.

“Nice Hotel” Quick trip to Legoland with the Grandkids, so hung our hats here for the 4 days. Great Staff, nice pool, and surrounding grounds. Good bar and restaurant area. Usual good beds and clean rooms. Thanks to Kathleen, who helped us out with a minor problem prior to our arrival. (my fault, not Marriott).

“Beautiful Hotel- Great Location- One drawbacks if your not aware of” The hotel is overall very ggod- The rooms ( King Suite) was perfect and extremely large and well aoppointed. The only drwaback was my room loaction was on the "inside" choose a room on the outside corridor of the hotel as I could hear everyrthing the went on in a wedding party several flights up! All night- it echoed throughout the inside track and unfortunately the hotel did nothing about the excessive and drunken noises... Back to the positive- staff, location, rooms ( pick the right one!) Overall with my advice you will like this hotel....

“Ottima la terrazza” Recensisco quest'holtel non perche ci ho alloggiato ma perche ci son stato a fare un aperitivo. Dall'alto della sua terrazza si può fare un aperitivo in mezzo allo skyline newyorchese in tutta tranquillità innanzi ad uno scenario al tramonto davvero fantastico.

“Be Careful, Park Centeral had no AC on an 80o Day in June!” We have stayed at the Park Central before. It's a decent hotel that is is usually good value for the price point. However this last stay we had to move on our last night, before an important performance because we were notified the night before that the AC was going to be worked on and the off from 9AM till 9PM on an 80o day. Better to do maintenance on this during the cooler months. This was not acceptable and we paid for a night we could not use, as getting ready for our special day while sweating was not an option.

“Incredibly Wonderful Hotel” I'm a frequent business traveller with elite status across most major business hotel chains. Marriott is my preference, and of all Marriott properties I've ever stayed at (I'm a Gold Elite member at present) this one is the most wonderful. We ended up here because we were appalled by the Marriott Courtyard downtown when we arrived, so we jumped in a cab and headed here. Boy, we couldn't have been happier about that decision. $60 cheaper a night and worth three times more. First, the renovations of the rooms are now complete, so the previous reviewer's issue with renovations should be history. And as this is a family-owned Marriott (ie not a franchise) the renovation has spared no expense or attention to detail. In short, the rooms are utterly gorgeous. And beds that put the normal (yet wonderful) Marriott Revive bedding package to shame - it was like sleeping on air. Very modern selection for colour scheme and the rooms were completely quiet - I didn't hear a single sound despite the property being at almost full occupancy. The concierge lounge is not yet renovated (although the plans look spectacular!), so they were offering free buffet breakfast to Gold Elite members in the restaurant instead. The buffet was not amongst the more lavish of the Marriott spreads, but it was still very nice with fresh omelettes made to order and a decent selection of accompaniments - bacon, sausage, potatoes, fruit, baked goods, cereal....and of course the always present JW Marriott oatmeal! The location is not downtown - it's about a $25-30 cab ride into the city. But it's directly across the street from a very large shopping mall (South Park Mall) with department and specialty stores ranging from high end (Neiman Marcus, Louis Vuitton) through to the normal mall fare (Dillards, Macy's, Gap, Brookstone). There's also a Rite Aid within five minutes' walking distance, so I felt the location catered particularly well for visitors both with and without cars. The staff and service - without exception (and we dealt with almost all of them during the four days of our stay) were second-to-none, and that's saying something for Marriott, where the standard is generally quite high. My colleague and I both commented that we'd never felt more welcome or "at home" at any hotel, and we travel more than 120 nights a year around the world. We will be coming to Charlotte on a reasonably regular basis and cannot wait to return to this hotel. One word of caution: The restaurant and concierge lounge are being renovated between now and the end of the year, so if this is an issue for you, defer your stay until January 2009. But personally it wouldn't cause me a moment's hesitation - this place is pure gold. Enjoy!

“not bad but not as nice as LA's Palomar, friendly staff, robes, no slippers.” Rooms were comfortable, bathroom not great. Location is near shopping but a bit to close to the seedy side of Mission st. The financial district is a short distance away. The plus is the restaurant inside which is Michelin rated on the fifth floor. Also a plus is that the Powell St. Station for BART and for the SF Cable Car is just around the corner. THe cable car takes you to fisherman's wharf and the pier. Leopard and zebra bathrobes! wifi free for Kimpton members. Bit expensive for the room and bath quality.

“Nice Hotel, Great Location” A number of business colleagues and I stayed at the Boston Harbor during a conference. I hadn't stayed there in probably 10 years. My opinion then was that it was over rated. What a difference 10 y ears makes. I arrived from a red eye flight to find my room ready and waiting. The room was huge, with a decent work space, plenty of sitting space, flat screen TV, BOSE wave radio, and a comfy room. And a great water view. I was on a smoking floor but could smell no smoke. The staff is polite, friendly, and helpful. I showed up early in our meeting room and found no coffee. When I mentioned to a co-worker that I was doing OK for a guy who slept on a plane the staff person who was setting up our room offered to go find me some coffee, and showed up with a full pot. Location is great. Right on the harbor, walking distance to downtown, and on a great running route. The only issue I had was minor - the air conditioner was shut off when I arrived, meaning my room was about 75. I turned it on and left, only to return at the end of the day to find it off again. I later learned it's on an automatic shut off. As a result I was always too hot. Otherwise it was quite a pleasant experience.

“Great stay and excellent location” I love the Topaz. And like most Kimptons, the level of service here is superb. Rooms are spacious, comfy and quiet. I love that my room had a little alcove off the bathroom to get ready in. The wine hour is a nice touch, although I was only there one night for it. They don't have a fitness center on site, but give you access to the YMCA just around the corner. The Y is a little dated, but is enormous - you can always find a machine, and the pool is great. The bar is nice and usually not too crowded - although I wish they offered more food choices - especially on a cold, snowy January night. This is one of my go-to hotels in DC since its close to my office and will definitely be staying here again one day!

“Excellent Hotel...Great Service, Comfy Rooms” We recently stayed four nights at The Surrey and loved everything about our visit. The location is great. Walking distance to the Whitney Museum, Central Park, great restaurants and lots of shopping. I love shopping in this area of NYC because it is much less crowded than other areas. Everyone at the hotel was very professional and pleasant. The room was beautifully decorated and the bed was very comfortable. The complimentary water and nightly cookies were a nice touch. Complimentary internet would have been appreciated. Don't miss the opportunity to eat at Cafe Boulud. This is Daniel Boulud's restaurant and definitely meets the expectations of quality and taste you expect from him. Great dining experience. I enjoyed an afternoon at the spa and recommend it highly. It is small but very quaint and relaxing. I nearly fell asleep during the massage. Very relaxing experience. Overall, wonderful stay and will definitely go back to The Surrey when we return to NYC.

“Repeat after me: "This is not a bed and breakfast"” The Morris House Hotel offers an experience that I hadn't had before. Old house, re-worked into big, characterful rooms with a very pleasantly eclectic selection of furnishings; spotlessly clean throughout; en-suite bathrooms with the slightly erratic water pressure, during a shower, that reminded me of how my kid sister used to flush the downstairs loo in hopes of scalding me as I showered upstairs; biscuits / cookies and tea set out in a "common room" of an afternoon, with, in the adjoining room, sofas drawn up in front of a large, cheerily blazing hearth... Windows that open for fresh air, snuggly Goldilocks-just-right big bed. Aside from a pang at the cost of parking my rental car at the affiliated garage (when I saw the posted fees I chose to leave it on the street), a perfect bed-and-breakfast - like experience. And then, the next morning, the breakfast. LOL OMG WTF. Orange juice, milk, hot water, a large serving dish of wheatflakes, a tray of non-croissants and non-Danish pastries and non-bagels (are there no Jews in Philadelphia? Quick! Get some!), a few oranges and apples (of the last, several were my first morning there, I swear it, actually rotten) -- portion-control cream-cheese and whipped-butter plastic tublets -- and, I must grant, WONDERFUL coffee. But the rest... This at a hotel with a restaurant annexe. Why doesn't the hotel pay the restaurant to send over a few trays of this and that (canapes, cold meats, devilled eggs), some breads, some proper pastries? What a good chance to show off, to attract customers for an evening meal! As it was, however, my fear that the breakfast was a foretaste of what the restaurant offered sent me elsewhere for dinner. Looking back through several years of reviews, I note the same puzzlement, my puzzlement, over and over again. Such a friendly, cosy, home-like place, guests write -- and then, breakfast. A breakfast that emphatically lets down the side. If, that is, you think that you've checked in at a B&B. Well, you haven't. You're at a hotel. A cosy, friendly, snuggly, lovely hotel. But it's a hotel. And hotels don't do breakfast. As far as the breakfast goes, you're at Motel 6.

“great hotel, great location” Travelzoo notified me of a great deal on this hotel. The rate for a basic room was $109. When I logged onto the website I noticed the rate for a 2-room suite was $179. It's hard to pass up a deal like that so I booked the suite with a king bed. We checked in early and our room wasn't ready. Not a problem since we were really just there to leave our luggage. There was a slight problem when we returned though. Instead of giving us a suite with a king bed, we were given a suite with 2 queens (which, in actuality, were 2 doubles). The front desk offered to change our room but the original one was on a higher floor, had a balcony and a better view. So, we decided to stay put. The room was large and nicely appointed. There were flat screen TVs in both rooms and the beds were very comfortable. The bathroom was also a nice size and modern. And, even though we were close to the elevator, we found it very quiet. The lobby is beautiful and there are several shops on the premises for gifts and food. We didn't eat at the restaurant or order room services but the menus looked good. We did sign up for the Omni Guest Services Program which entitled us to daily breakfast beverages and a newspaper. The Omni is close to the Zoo and Woodley Park and there are many restaurants within a 2 block area. We had breakfast at the Open City Restaurant every morning. The food was great, it was reasonably priced and the service was super fast. We also ate at Cafe Paridisio. I highly recommend both restaurants. The Metro is also just up the street from the Omni. All in all, we enjoyed our stay at the Omni Shoreham. I would definitely stay there again.

“Great Stay” I have stayed here several times and I am always pleased with the stay. It is a very busy hotel but once in your room, you forget how much activity is going on in the hotel. We love the suite vs. just a room! We will be back!

“yes, great location -- decent rooms.” We booked through hotels.com, and check-in was smooth and desk clerk/all staff friendly. There is one very small olde timey elevator (we had to go in three trips with five folks and our bags.) The hotel is attached to a little hamburger restaurant called Double Decker, which, upon closer inspection, is a much better place than it looks (quality local ingredients, good beer on tap, etc.) but you can definitely always smells burgers & fries on/around the premises. Comfy bed, good wifi speed. There are the usual San Francisco hobos on the sidewalks everywhere, but it didn't feel threatening -- even at night when we walked from the hotel to the Mission to get burritos. There are a bunch of more upscale places on Hayes St nearby -- good coffee shops, bars, restaurants. FREE PARKING was a big asset -- even our 15-passenger van was able to fit. I would definitely book here again.

“Quirliger Innenstadthotel” Immer, wenn ich in San Francisco bin, gehe ich in Marriott Marquis. Die Aussicht (von den hoeheren Stockwerken) ist atemberaubend. Die Zimmer sind fuer eine amerikanische Grossstadt sehr geraeumig und nach amerikanischem Standard sehr gut ausgestattet. Grosser Flachbildfernseher, Schreibtisch, Sessel und gute (nicht zu weiche) bequeme Betten sind vorhanden. Habe bei meinen bisherigen 4 Aufenthalten nie ein lautes Zimmer gahabt. Die Lage ist sehr zentral in unmittelbarer Naehe zu Powell St., Moscone Center, 3 min zum Union Square.

“Physically nice Hotel but poor service” Stayed 3 days in the Hilton Bay Front , San Diego. Great Location . Hotel room was standard. The room was serviced after 3pm all days except for check out when the housekeeper came at 9am . $10 to print a boarding pass.

“Great location near airport, free parking while you travel” My son and I stayed overnight here with an early morning flight out of PHX the next day. The hotel provides a free shuttle that runs every half hour, which was very convenient and on time. The hotel also allows free parking, which was terrific for us since we were gone for 14 days to the East Coast. It was cheaper to stay here overnight and take the shuttle then it would've been to park in any of the airport lots. So for those conviences, I give the hotel high marks. The hotel itself is definitely an older Hilton property, which shows its wear in typical ways: worn carpet, chipping paint, etc. That doesn't bother me as long as I feel like it's clean. My biggest complaint is there was someone else's hair left in the bathtub. Ewww. That's just gross, and should be high on the list of no-no's of housekeeping, in my opinion. But the beds were clean and comfy.

“Southern Charm and Hospitality with great food!” I love the Peabody Hotel. This hotel has a grand and gorgeous lobby. Lovely flower arrangments and I love how in the evenings you can get a glass of wine or coffee and dessert and people watch and listen to the live piano player. The lobby is such a delightful place to be. Oh and the desserts are absolutely decadent and delicious and totally worth splurging on. I also enjoyed their lobby shops; they have some great shopping in them with items that are totally unique to Memphis. The staff is so friendly and helpful. I went there to ask where the closest cell phone store was (as I had forgotten my iphone charger) and one of the staff members, let me borrow his personal one. They went out of their way to make me feel welcome. Chez Phillipe is just a great place to dine. The food was absolutely perfect. The shortrib beef dish was delicious and the creme brulee to die for. The service was top notch and they really cared to make us feel welcome and special. The room was comfortable, clean and modest (not as grand as the hotel), but I love this hotel and I will stay here again. The marching of the ducks is absolutely lovely!! What a cool tradition. The atmosphere, the location, the history and the great staff make it the perfect choice for Memphis. Southern hospitality at its best.

“What you would expect: Excellence” After visiting many Four Seasons properties, we are starting to really appreciate the consistency across the hotels: great service, great food, great rooms, great people. This feels like a boutique hotel, and if you hang around you'll see a few celebrities. Location was great---not in the middle of all the traffic like the other Four Seasons in Beverly Hills, but close enough to Rodeo Drive to walk (abotu 10 minutes). We took the house car several times---a Rolls Royce with tinted windows---which is available on a first come first serve basis. It was fun to see what life is like for the stars as people try to see who's inside the car. My one requirement for a room: to sleep. Beds of course are not a problem at the Four Seasons, but I was concerned because the hotel isn't very high, and our room was facing the front of the hotel and a busy street. But with the A/C on constantly we heard nothing all night long and slept for 10 hours the first night. Compare this with the Ritz in Laguna Niguel---a sprawling beachfront resort---where we stayed later in the week where we heard people walking above us and everytime the A/C came on it woke us up. This seems like such a minor thing, but sleep is important whether you are on business or pleasure. Only a few complaints, which of course are minor compared to other hotels: *When we made the reservation and when we checked in we asked for a quiet room. We were given the one RIGHTNEXT to the elevators. It's a pain to go to your room only to have to then go back to the desk and then wait again for a new room. *During breakfast one morning we heard two of the waitstaff complaining to each other about their manager---guests really don't want to hear that. *One morning we had a long discussion with our server about one of the smoothies, we ordered it, but never got it. We weren't charged, and decided to forgo it, but it was strange. *There is only one pool, and it's relatively small---if there were kids there, it would not have been relaxing. One thing I would like to mention is that the staff is fabulous---no snootiness like what you'll encounter in the service people on Rodeo Drive. Everyone is treated like a valued guest no matter who you are or what you’re wearing.

“Super location and top-notch hotel & service” First time at the Trump. Beautiful hotel, nice public areas. Room on 26th floor was huge, and the bathroom was enormous. Beautifully appointed, massive walk-in shower. Great views to the north, west and some east, too. Absolutely would go back to this place. Outstanding service, the best we have had anywhere in Chicago. Location just off the Magnificent Mile, convenient to Macy's (formerly Marshal Fields) and Art Institute. And a short walk to our favorite restaurant, Rick Bayless' Frontera Grill and Topolobampo.

“Great location and recently updated rooms” I've always liked this property and they have updated the rooms, new furniture and a HD flat pannel tv. It's between the 16th street mall area lodo, so you can walk to both, not to mention connected to the Tabor Center mall. Great staff and accomidatioins. During my stay they were changing cabel providors and I had no HBO, was not happy about that but it should be a tempory problem only.

“Solid property in a great location” I was surprised to see some of the really critical comments on the MO Boston. I thought the property was solid. - Bell staff, reception and concierge on the ball and very friendly - Rooms were what I would expect. Views aren't great and I don't personally like the choice of sea foam coloring for some of the furnishings but the rooms are solid. Lot's of power outlets in a convenient location by the desk - Bar and restaurant have nice modern Asian-influenced design. Food and beverage quality is very high Only negative I experienced was that the bar and restaurant staff were a bit of a mixed bag. Some were clearly grumpy and inattentive. Also, seems they don't cross train so even if someone is available they may not be willing to do something until the "responsible" person shows up -- e.g., "let me find my colleague so that she can seat you" in our empty restaurant. I'd choose the Four Seasons over this property. The service is much better there.

“Nice hotel. Clean/new rooms, comfortable bed, very central location” I found a great air/hotel package online and stayed 3 nights. As others have already mentioned, this hotel's rooms are on the small side, but they are well thought out and not claustrophobic. The king size bed was very comfortable. The bathroom only had a shower, but it was spotless. I think it's a great home base in midtown if you're sightseeing, or in town on business. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful, the maid did a great job each day. There was a bit of a traffic jam in the breakfast room my first morning. The layout didn't seem to be as well designed as it could have been and for some reason the coffee urns are hidden outside the dining room area next to the business center. But the food was plentiful with the fairly standard offering of cold and hot cereals, waffles, bagels (toaster available), pastries, yogurt, fruit and fruit salad. Other than needing to improve how the food is laid out, the only other minor complaint is the rooms aren't wireless... you can only access wireless from the 1st floor (although there are internet cables for laptops in the rooms). I recommend this hotel and would definitely stay again.

“Designer's Choice Hotel for Washington DC” Washington DC is infamous for its wide variety of upscale hotels, most of which maintain ties to their historic past. The Park Hyatt Washington DC however defies this rule by introducing a hotel that might be one of DC's trendiest. In 2006, the entire hotel received a 24 Million Dollar floor to ceiling renovation, which now delivers a product that is impressive by almost every five star standard. Location: When choosing a location in "the district" as locals call DC, the Park Hyatt is situated just a few short blocks from historic Georgetown (which features some of the city's best restaurant and shopping options) as well a short cab ride (or 15-20 minute) walk away from the White House and other neighboring attractions. I found the location to be quite ideal. Guest Rooms: Almost 50% of the guest rooms are Park Deluxe accommodations, which are oversized rooms with king size beds. These rooms feature the spa bath, which has a separate soaking tube and over sized open rain shower. (the bathrooms were spectacular!) If you can't score the Park Deluxe Rooms, the standard rooms are quite nice as well, but do no feature the generously large spa baths. The beds in all the rooms are amazing, with spectacular linens to match. The overall room decor is warm contemporary; and exude a very residential feel. High Speed internet is complimentary (there is a fee for wireless) Service: The service throughout was amazing, yet not at all imposing. It was nice to have great service at your disposal, yet never anything too overbearing. There are small touches throughout the hotel that are reflective of the "Park" designation (which is Hyatt's more upscale brand) Dining: Although I'm not generally partial to hotel dining, I would suggest trying at least one of the hotel's restaurant or in-room dining options, as the food is absolutely spectacular! The presentation on every item was fantastic. I would also highly recommend trying one of the hotel's famous cheese selections, either in the lobby or in-room. Gym: The fitness center is full of great equipment, but some might call it a bit on the dull side. It certainly does the trick with lots of modern equipment, but nothing that says wow. The pool and jacuzzi are located adjacent to the fitness center. We had a wonderful experience at the Park Hyatt Washington DC, and are certain to return on our next visit. I have had the opportunity to explore many of DC's hotel options, and this is one that stands out as a unique take on the Five Star experience. Yes, there may be many others to choose from, but this one is fresh, contemporary and just right!

“Top Value Hotel in a Great Location” Stayed 4 nights at the Holiday Inn Midtown 57th St just before Christmas. After searching the net for good deals, I finally chose this hotel primarily based on the nightly rate, but also for its location. This hotel is great value compared to many similar hotel brands in New York. On arriving at 7pm, check-in was fast & efficient. Front desk staff & concierge were all polite & helpful. Rooms are extremely spacious by NY standards, with plenty of space for suitcases etc. The bed was very comfortable & never had any problems sleeping at night. The decor is ok & room amenities just fine. Housekeeping was efficient. The hotel is well located & within walking distance to the main tourist spots. Central Park is just a couple of blocks away, & Times Square, a leisurely 10-15 minute stroll. We walked everywhere, apart from to the financial district, when we used the subway. Always felt safe when walking around, even at night. There are loads of great traditional Diners near to this hotel & most are open 24hrs. This means you can always get something good to eat & you dont need to rely on the hotel, where the restaurants are on the pricier side. I would definitely choose this hotel again as it really was a good value for money base to explore NYC. This is not a luxury hotel, but then it doesn't pretend to be. Its a clean & affordable option with spacious rooms & friendly staff. If you're going to New York to shop & do the tourist thing, then the Holiday Inn Midtown is a good choice. Why spend loads on many of the other big chains (Hilton / Renaissance / Westin etc) when you can get the same amenities for much less. Since you'll hardly ever be in the room, save your money - stay at this hotel & shop til you drop...!!!

“The Chancellor--Why Go Anywhere Else in SF??!!” Stayed at the Chancellor in Dec. '06 thanks to such good reviews on TripAdvisor.com & loved it! Great staff--the front desk, housekeeping, and the bellmen; nice clean rooms; great cookies & coffee in the lobby. A year later the place is still outstanding! Front desk was so friendly---gave us great restaurant & pub recommendations & tourist ideas. Room was spotless and quiet! Free wireless and a decent room rate, too! We highly recommend the Chancellor--will make a return visit ASAP!

“BIG DISAPPOINTMENT” This is an incredibly average hotel with apparently very little in the way of oversight. First the good; Very good location, large rooms, comfortable bed. Now the bad; The absolute worst valet, bellmen and front of hotel staff I have ever encountered. Ive spent roughly 150 or so nights in hotels over last 5 or so years so that is saying something. Zero help with doors, zero inquiry about bags, an absolute abomination parking vehicles and a completely apathetic demeanor. The front of hotel was hanging out, yelling and laughing like it was a house party while people 20+ are waiting to park or get taxis. Now based on how comfortable they seemed acting like this it has to be normal operating procedure. That means NO OVERSIGHT. Its a shame because its in a very good location across the street from Reading Terminal Market which is a fantastic place to get lunch with 50+ diff options.Not as good as Quincy Market in Boston though. Its also near at least a dozen good restaurants like Capitale Grille, Amada etc. Its also a decent looking hotel w a pretty good lounge. But unless you get a great deal $159-$179(very rare) its definitely not worth a look. This will most certainly be my last visit to this Marriott. PS- The front desk person we dealt with was professional and pleasant.

“Clean hotel” We stayed here with 4 teenage girls. most of the hotel staff was friendly. The morning gal needs to smile. The evening staff was very friendly and helpful. Our rooms were roomy, comfy and clean. The hotel is located with in walking distance to the T. There is a Target behind the hotel which was very convenient. You can get to downtown on the T in 15 min. We went to a Red Sox game and took the T. It takes about 30 min from hotel to park. not too bad. The pool room was very hot! made it uncomfortable for us watching the girls swim. they had a little lounge area with a small bar, pool table and sitting area.

“Clean and comfortable” This is a clean and comfortable hotel. Chicago is a great city for walking, so we certainly did not mind the distance to attractions. Otherwise, there is indoor access to the El.. Because it is located on top of the Chicago Sun-Times building, it is very quiet. I don't think i would pay the premium for rooms with the city view again. The lounge has great views. On the negative side, I would echo other comments regarding the internet connection - it was incredibly slow. If you are on business or otherwise need internet access, this could be a real problem, Water in the pool was surprisingly and uncomfortably cold. .

“Stay and Park deal a very good value” Stayed one night prior to flying out of BWI on a very early flight. While the rooms have been updated the hallways remain a little dated. The staff was very friendly and efficient, including the check in, housekeeping and shuttle bus employees. If you will be parking at BWI airport for about a week the hotel offers a stay and park deal that is very reasonable. We booked the “AAA stay and park deal” available at the time on the hotel’s website. All in all the most convenient hotel location to BWI airport, with regular shuttle service running at least every 10 to 15 minutes. Pick up at the airport is currently in area D near baggage claim.

“Classic Hotel with some nice modern touches” The hotel has a nice lobby. The lounge was somewhat disappointing. I went there after 10 and the kitchen had closed down. Restaurant is not a foodie destination. Basement space could use better configuration. As I recall, you can only enter the cafe from the street. Room comfortable and bathroom updated. The highlight for me was taking a Pilates class in the fitness centre Sunday morning. Since I'm a President's Club member, I can borrow an Adidas outfit.

“Good deal at the location” The property is close by LAX, it is reached through common shuttles shared with the Hilton (several of the LAX hotels use this system). Perfectly adequate rooms, satisfactorily clean, very comfortable beds. Bit of an issue with soundproofing, you may overlook parking lots and delivery docks where trucks backing up will be heard clearly, and some sound filters through from nearby rooms, but not specially noisy. Definitely a business hotel, many meeting rooms. Restaurant is OK for the price category. ACE Rental car desk in lobby. The shuttles nominally make the run on a 15-20 minute interval but traffic and number of passengers may affect it. On departure there was a large family group with lots of luggage and the Hotel got dispatch to send a shuttle specifically for the 4Points rather than share with the Hilton passengers, good call.

“Great place, great location.” Just got back from a weekend stay. What a great room. We ended up in one of there corner rooms which have three picture windows in a baywindow shape giving you an incredible panorama. Unique. The service was great and the price was $119 including parking. (You are very close to the T-stop, and right off from Boylson St.. Newberry St. is just 2 blocks away, and coming of the Mass. Pike it couldn't be easier to find. We walked to the commons and Downtown crossing, which took about 25 mins total and it's about a good 15 min. walk to Fenway. Swimming Pool is small, no sauna or hot tub. Weight room is nice. But Boston isn't about staying in your hotel. We didn't try the hotel dinning, but the bar is very nice. Very clean and although our room only had a shower it was very large and had a double shower head set up which was very nice. I very much recommnd.

“Neat - O” I stayed at the Farmer's Daughter last Saturday night. This place is a trip! The lobby is really cute, with the farm theme. It cracked me up when the clerk emerged from behind the back wearing overalls and a checkered shirt. This hotel appears to have been a converted 50's LA motor/hotel. The way they modernized it with the country/hip theme is quite neat. I loved the picture of the hound on the bedroom wall. Yes, as other reviewers said, there is no view. I didn't go for the view, I went for the location - and it is a good, central location. There is valet parking steps away from the registration desk.

“Good Views, Bad Service” Stayed in one of the Central Park Suites....The suite did not have much space for the price, don't get me wrong it was not small, but for $2,100 a night, I expected a larger living room and bathroom. Room service takes forever as does check-in.. Also the hotel charged me twice for room service, had to get it taken off my credit card..Next time I think we will stay at the Ritz-Carlton on Central Park South.
“Indifferent staff” Bottom line- had to sleep on the floor. The room, ammentities and property don't warrant its 5 star status. Better can be found in a better location for much less.

“Great for Leisure; Bad for Conferences” This place has a bipolar personality. The hotel was excellent; the conference center -- not so much. The hotel has a great, central location, blocks from the great restaurants of Fisherman’s Wharf and North Beach. We received five different dinning recommendations from the hotel staff. All were very good! The hotel is smallish so no Regency Club exists at this property. Surprisingly, the restaurant had the lowest prices I have found at any Hyatt and conference guess receive and additional 20 percent off! Knuckles Restaurant service was good except Friday morning when we had to wait a good while for our server to show up. When she did get to our table (after we got our own drinks) she said they were having a meeting. Unfreakinbelievable!!! You would think the meeting would have happened BEFORE Knuckles opened. Don’t drive a car here unless you are traveling on business. No self parking. Moreover, valet is $45/per day. If you park overnight on the street, you will be sorry. We found lots of broken of glass from car burglaries along the curb on North Point Street just east of the hotel. The rooms are very nice and the housekeeping is outstanding. Although there is no turndown service, the rooms are apparently freshened twice per day. I would dash up to the room at lunch to change for a quick workout and shower then return in the evening to find fresh towels, a clean shower and my workout clothes stowed away. Many reviewers complained about the “doorless” showers (a glass partition only partially separates the shower from rest of the bathroom).
