Though some reviewers said the bathroom floor got wet, I believe one would need to try really hard to get water on the bathroom floor. The staff was friendly. Everyone smiled and gave the greeting of the day. The conference center is nice but the service is horrible. We had a great continental breakfast set up every morning and cookies or some other confection in the afternoon. Unfortunately, ice water was rarely available. To make matters worse, many times we had no water at all! A co-worker told me that the coffee ran out too! I complained to the servers or hosts twice and complained to the front desk also. The situation did not improve throughout the week. This is totally unsatisfactory! I do not recommend booking a conference here.

“Challenged when busy” From other reviews you know that the location is great, balconies overlooking the Riverwalk are worth the upgrade. Staff is very good except that when the hotel gets busy service falls apart. The hotel just does not have enough staff when the hotel is fully booked. During a recent weekend stay the hotel was busy with Christmas events and parties and management did not have extra staff on call. Room was not serviced until around 5pm. You could not get near the front desk or concierge desk. Waits for elevators were extended. Valet parking appears to be outsourced and the service is hit or miss depending on your timing. The wait to just pull into the car park on a recent Saturday afternoon was 20 minutes. Bottom line is to be careful booking this hotel if you are going to stay during a busy time. The hotel just can't handle being busy.

“Really nice and with a wonderful Senior Price” Stayed one night a the Comfort Suites North. Convenient to I-35N and the restaurants along I-35 and over into San Antonio. Very clean, good wi-fi and the price with Senior Discount was UNDER $60. I couldn't believe it. For those wanting amenities, there is an indoor pool, laundry and exercise facility. What is not to like?

“Clean but outdated rooms” When we booked our hotel through hotels.com it was the best priced for the location and the amneities. Upon arrival at the belvedere the doorman david greeted us verywell. The check desk was very nice and they found us a room at 10.00am and the check in time 4.00 pm. When we got up to the 7 floor we got in our room it was nice and the entrence way had nice tile.The beds were very low and to soft the room was a little out dated but very very clean. The bathroom was nice and clean. The amenites were nice workout room breakfeast etc.etc.... The problums we had were 2 elavaters for a 17 storie buildingand they were very small. This place was a little pricy but very convienynt. The consiare was helpful (when there). So if you are looking for a good location and clean rooms.STAY HERE

“Nice, clean business-class hotel” The rooms are clean, the beds are comfortable. Standard room size, standard bath tub, comfortable bedding, and wi-fi worked fine. TV is flat-panel but not Hi-Def. Be prepared that parking is valet and expensive, and that it takes 15 minutes to retrieve your car, but they warn you this as you check in.

“Generic Hotel...” Stayed here for three nights while visiting friends and doing some sightseeing in San Francisco. Great location, but otherwise a little disappointing: Pros: - Location. Located in the heart of downtown SF. Easy to access public transit or taxis from the hotel. - Staff. Everyone who I came across was very professional/friendly. Check in was a breeze. - Housekeeping. The room was spotless when we arrived, and they did a good job of cleaning each day and replenishing toiletries. - Concierge lounge, particularly the breakfast offerings, were better than some of the other properties where I've stayed recently. Cons: - No wireless internet. It's almost 2011...and no WIFI in the rooms. A little ridiculous since most lower priced hotels offer complimentary internet/wireless internet. - Requested a room on a high floor. Instead given a room on level 21...hotel had 39 levels. - Nothing really stood out about the place. Very generic/somewhat outdated rooms, nothing unique to being in San Francisco, etc. - The hotel had some sort of bar/lounge on the top level, which probably had great views of the city. Limited hours though...this place closes very early. One other thing...parking here is over $50/night. I can't complain about that since it is San Francisco, but you can park on your own for much less at other garages in the area. Check that out and save yourself some money if you make the mistake of having a car while staying here.

“A Pleasant Surprise” After reading the reviews from people claiming this property was subpar, I hesitated to make a reservation. However, it seemed everything else in the same area and price range was rated even worse. There was a slight check-in delay when the desk clerk claimed my room wasn't ready (well after check-in time.) This was easily resolved by offering to cancel my reservation and go to the Fairfield next door, when a room magically became available. Aside from that, a nice room, certainly on the high side of Hampton standards. TV was an old CRT model (with no Fox reception) so that was a minor disappointment. Free shuttle to the airport, which I didn't use. The location is off-airport, in an office park behind a bank ops center, which means you shouldn't expect anything scenic outside the window. There is a Ruby Tuesday in the area but not much else. But you're probably considering this property because you need to be close to the airport, and this more than fits the bill.

“a good value for new york city” We stayed at Marrakech Hotel on a weekend trip to new york because it was only $99 a night. The hotel was well decorated with a Moroccan (I think?) theme throughout, quite beautiful. The rooms were small but clean and the tv, a/c, shower, everything worked. The hotel is only one block from a subway stop, and there are a few 24 hour delis near by for snacks, though beyond that there isn't much to see in the immediate area. The staff was friendly and offered us advice on where to go, and gave us a late check out. The downsides (expected for a hotel in Manhattan for under $100): the mattress felt old and was squeaky, there is no elevator (up to four flights of stairs), and no wifi. Overall, I would definitely recommend this place to anyone wanting to explore the city on a budget.

“more historic and charming hotels nearby” Typical stylish hyatt, but only in the rooms. The building it is in shares space with other offices---though there is a starbucks inside and covered access to other building outside. So you can avoid the weather. If you are looking for charm, look at the other hotels near by. Hotel is around the corner from a historic area and the capitol. However, where this hotel is lacks any charm. Great if you are a sports fan though. Also, you have to pay for parking---the hotel doesn't have any special arrangements or airport shuttle. Taxi to airport was $30 not including tip. Super close to the airport (15-20 min) and very walkable area with restaurants near by. So you do not need a car. Good location for business. Internet cost is not included in hotel rate. Like the others complained, a vent is over the bed, that keeps constantly coming on and off. My option was to turn off the heat, which isn't really an option most of the winter.

“Mala Porto Vista” I stayed here for three nights during a recent trip to SoCal, and even though I got a pretty good deal, I don’t think I would stay here again. The building itself looks very modern from the outside with a cool, chic lobby and friendly staff, but when it came to the rest of the hotel, I was not impressed. My first view after stepping off the elevator on my floor was one that reminded me of an old motel because the rooms were entered from the outside. They all had large windows that could be viewed in to, and each room had an air conditioner that stuck out of the wall next to the door. Even though the carpet was a little worn, the furniture in the room was nice. The bed was very plush and very comfortable, the armoire looked pretty new and was large, and the dresser was good. My only complaints about the furniture were that the television was outdated, and there was a desk right next to the dresser without a chair. So, it was unusable. Overall, the room was just too small for all the furnishings. The bathroom was adequate. Although I was not impressed with the room, I will say that the hotel had a great view of Little Italy and beyond. Go to the top floor for a relaxing view and fresh air. It was also in a great location being so close to dining, bars, and the trolley.

“Excellent, clean and comfortable.” Stayed for 6 nights and really have no issue with this hotel. DIdnt use it much in terms of facilities,but it's location was excellent for a top notch hotel. A couple of minutes walk from Dupont Circle Metro station. (15min walk to the White House) Used the bar in the hotel and it was nice way to relax after walking the sights of Washington. Everything is close by, shops, bars and all the restaurants you want in terms of price. We were on the 4th floor, and it was nice and peaceful. Room was excellent, comfortable bed and seated area and a fab flat screen tv. The bathroom was huge and plenty of toiletries, bigger towels maybe. We did alot of sightseeing, so really the hotel served its purpose for a restful night. Checkin was stress free and the doormen always pleasant, no matter what time of the day we walked through. If I was to stay here again, would make more use of the hotel. Glad I stayed here on my 1st trip to DC.

“Good location, nice hotel” My wife and I stayed here for one night. Overall, the hotel was nice and comfortable. My biggest complaint would be the size of the rooms. For a hotel of this caliber, I would have expected a larger room and bathroom. Service was friendly and the parking garage was convenient ($18 per night). The hotel is a couple blocks away from a restaurant/shopping area but right next door to the Convention Center and NASCAR Museum.

“Excellent location and wonderful staff” The W Time Square reverses many of the negative stereotypes about hotels in Time Square. The service is EXCELLENT at this property (not the case with other hotels, even SPG properties). The hotel staff really knows how to treat a guest, very accommodating. There was some upgrades being done near my room. The hotel staff immediately informed me that they could either upgrade me to a "noisy" room or keep me in my original room. I really appreciated them giving me the option and most of all being honest with me. I chose the "noisy" room....didn't hear a peep. The other stereotype undone by the W is the rooms were actually quite large. I thought they were basically the same size as other SPG properties around the world. Of course the hotel was clean and well taken care of. The bar on the 7th floor is a cool place to hang out. The location of the W is on 47th and Broadway, literally right in the middle of the Time Square action. The "gold standard" for years in location in Times Square was the Marriott Marquis. Well, the W is literally 10 feet away, just to give you an idea. If you are going to Times Square, stay at the W!

“It's how the problem is handled!” I am excited to report that after speaking to Roger Millar and Jennifer Tinkler of the Hampton Inn (downtown Austin) that I am a completely satisfied Hampton Inn customer. Jennifer was wonderful, she listen to the issue and shared with me the training that has happened since my stay and that the security issue was immeadeately resolved by the GM (Mr. Millar) personally. I appreciat the fact that when you make management aware of issues they are addressed and corrected. A huge thanks to the management of the ampton Inn of Downtown Austin, I will be back, SOON!

“Average Hotel, Good Location” I stayed here this past weekend with some friends to go to an event in the city. I was satisfied, but the hotel has some things to work on for sure...read on: -I used Hilton's "Requests Upon Arrival" system online where you can order things like extra towels, pillows or beverages to have delivered to your room before you even check in. I knew that there were going to be 4 guys in 1 hotel room, so some extra towels and pillows would be great. These items were NOT in the room, even though I specifically requested them months prior when making the reservation. What gives? -3 bath towels in a room that is meant to hold up to 4 guests. That's the hotel being cheap right there, clearly. -We did not find out the hotel has an indoor pool available to guests until we checked in so we did not bring our swim suits. Why is this information not on the website? -Housekeeper tried to enter our room on Sunday morning without announcing herself when we had a Do Not Disturb sign up. Thankfully the room was locked, but still...come on now. -After returning late from a bar one night, we got in the elevator and had a security guard come in after us. He did not say a word to us, but just followed us to our room and then left. SO CREEPY. I am really not okay with this...made me feel like I was a criminal or something. -Location is very good...just maybe 2 blocks from Mag Mile and a few more to other good areas like State Street and the Red Line CTA. We could also walk to Vision/Excalibur where our event was at. -The hotel has been renovated and brought up to date with contemporary furniture, but you can still tell it was once a Holiday Inn back in the 80s just by the architecture and layout. The remodel really did do a good job though and it's on par with other Doubletree hotels, although they did not replace the TVs. Rooms really could benefit from some flat-panel TVs. Really like the window-seats in the room, great for storing luggage or extra clothes. -Friendly bellmen, always saying hello and seeing if we needed a cab. -Easy access to 7/11, McDonalds, bagel shop and Dunkin Donuts for quick bites. -Free WiFi in the lobby SO, all in all, I would stay here again if I got a really good rate; however, I think there are better hotels in this city with more personal service and a better attention to detail...two things that are very important to me as a guest. I would welcome a management response to my comments.

“Buon hotel ,un po' caro nei servizi ma consigliabile....” Hotel a 5 minuti da una delle stazioni metro più importanti della città ( Dupon Circle) che permette di raggiungere tutte le destinazioni Utili della città. Grande entrata circolare per le auto e taxi con Hall ampia ed accogliente con servizio Touch Screen per info sulla città , metropolitana, attrazioni locali ecc. ecc. Personale tutto sommato disponibile e cordiale. Camera Pulita, ampia , con un bel bagno funzionale e ben tenuto( parecchi asciugamani ed accappatoi) con vista frontale sul quartiere di Georgetown. Wi- Fi gratuito nella Hall ma parcheggio Valet piuttosto caro (74 $ per due notti...) Nella zona intorno,tranquilla e frequentata, parecchi ristoranti ( italiano , messicano , russo , greco, fast food, Steackhouse ecc..).

“Above average stay. Great location.” Stayed three nights for a conference. Gorgeous view of river and lake from West Tower. Very nice hotel with some subtle signs of aging in the rooms. Clean rooms and staff very friendly. Great location - lots of walkable attractions. Recommend Volare for authentic italian food - walkable from the hotel. Definetely would stay here again.

“Just not up to Marriott standards” I had an early flight out of Houston and wanted to stay near HOU. The hotel is certainly close. Check in went smoothly and I was assigned a room on the second floor. As I was walking to my room, I noticed a thick build up of dust along the edges of the walls. Upon entering my room, the bed and television looked nice and new, but the rest of the room was shabbly. There was mold in the tile of shower and bathroom floor tile was not clean and had loose hairs. (not mine) I ordered room service for dinner and only one type of soup was available (black bean). Noise was very loud from atrium at night. Drapery had a hole in it. Window wall had peeling paint and black granite nightstands were dusty. I probably will try the Hilton next time.

“Enjoyed our stay” The staff and service are second to none. We would call from the room to the valet and the car was there by the time we arrived. Room was excellent, and the entire hotel is gorgeous. Based on other reviews, we did not eat here. Cannot say enough about the staff. The noise level in the room was acceptable (better than other hotels I have stayed at in San Diego) and turning the fan in the room to medium drowned it out. My one big complaint is $12.95 for internet access. When I can get free wifi at rest areas, coffee shops, etc. this fee is ridiculous. And the $2.00 charge to make an 800 call was a bit petty also. Some reviews spoke of the shady neighborhood. Our room did face the Plaza Hotel, which appears to be a flophouse, so not the best view. But we used the front entrance on Broadway and did not have any issues at all. We walked to the Gaslamp several times from the hotel. Brians 24, a few blocksaway and an easy walk, has an awesome breakfast. If you are arriving by car from the airport on Broadway and using the valet, be aware the entrance is off of 4th Ave and not easily accessible from Broadway.

“Nice stay at Palace Hotel” I stayed at Palace Hotel for 5 nights, and found it a very enjoyable experience. The staff is excellent, and Debbie Law is hands down a sensational concierge. This is a Luxury hotel with great service and amenities; the rooms are a bit retro, but still lovely. Would stay here again.

“Good value, clone of Eastgate Towers across the street” Stayed a single night recently at the Murray Hill East Suites. I've previously stayed at the Eastgate Tower, across the street and a block east of here, and had a pretty good idea what to expect from this converted apartment building. In fact, the Murray Hill East Suites was nearly identical physically to the Eastgate Tower -- my room was a mirror image of the one I had at the Eastgate Tower a few months before. My general perception was that the furniture/drapes/carpets at the Murray Hill East seemed every so slightly newer/cleaner than at the Eastgate Tower, but the furniture itself was identical, and there wasn't much difference overall except for the bathroom; the bathroom in the Murray Hill East appeared to have been remodeled with completely new fixtures, tile, etc. sometime in the last year or so. The room itself was large and comfortable, with a dining table and chairs, sofa, end tables, arm chair, coffee table, TV stand, and dresser, along with a double bed and one nightstand, arranged in an L-shaped room with the dining table at the top of the L near the door, the couch along one wall, the TV near the angle of the L, and the bed/nightstand in the base of the L. The small kitchen is in a separate room near the entrance door, with a half-sized fridge, full four-burner (albeit small) range, coffeemaker, sink, etc. The bed itself was nothing much -- at the low end of acceptable -- and the pillows were barely there -- I had to scavenge the two extra pillows from the closet to make up a decent place to put my head, and the first time I looked in the closet for extra pillows I mistook the two pillows for folded sheets -- they were that thin and flimsy. I ended up not using the high-speed internet access -- I couldn't find any indication of a hotel-provided wireless signal, and there was no wired connection of any kind in the room. Since I didn't start looking until late in my only night there, I decided I could live without it until morning and didn't pursue it. Neither here nor there, but this was the first hotel I've been to in the US in fifteen years or so where I was given an actual, honest-to-god metal key for the room, instead of a magnetic card key(another vestige of the building's days as an apartment building). If you're particularly concerned about security and the possibility of someone duplicating the key, I suppose that might give you pause. Service, in the limited interactions I had with the staff, was courteous and professional, if not effusively friendly. All in all, this seems like an excellent option in this part of Manhattan, particularly for the price. If I were to return to this customer's location for several days, I'd definitely consider it. Having room to spread out and a kitchen where I could store and prepare meals would be welcome.

“HANDY FOR EVERYTHING” We considered staying somewhere else, just for a change, but were glad we didn't. East Grand is just off North Michigan Avenue, a short walk along State Street takes you over the bridge to south of the River. The Weber Grill is attached to the hotel, and has great good and Rock Bottom Brewery is right across the road, also with good food. We had some rain and wind when we were there, and it was great to be so close to everything. An additional bonus is that the entrance to the subway is a few yards from the hotel too. Great beds, like all Hiltons, and loved the new "bumpy" feathered duvets.

“Great stay at The Alex” We stayed at The Alex Hotel for one day in June. As Leaders Club members we're upgraded to a spacious one bedroom suite on the 29th floor. The room was great with a full kitchen which we unfortunately didn't use due to our short stay. Overall a very nice hotel with wonderful views of the Chrysler Building and I wouldn't hesitate staying at The Alex again

“Great value and location - would stay here again!” We chose the Donatello for it's combination of location, space, price and favourable Trip Advisor reviews; last time we stayed in the Westin Market Street. Jesus checked us in into a great room at 1130 when we were expecting just to drop our cases - what a great guy! In fact, the desk staff, concierges and maids were all super friendly and helpful which made The Donatello a welcoming place to stay. The room was generously sized and being on the back of the hotel, very quiet indeed - we didn't hear a thing from either inside or outside the hotel at night. A kitchenette area allows for snacks or breakfast in the room which was an added bonus. The hotel is just two blocks from Union Square and a few blocks further from cable car and muni stops (The F line tram is quietr than others and a great way to see the sights from The Castro, through Fishermans' Wharf to the Embarcadero) and there's even a parking garage right next to the hotel if needed. I think we made a good choice with the Donatello and would say that it fully lives up to it's positive billing on Trip Advisor and would recommend it without reservation!

“Clean , peaceful night sleep near Broadway” We stayed here for one night on points for my husbands birthday. The location was ok, short walk to get to Broadway. The bed was super comfortable and slept great. We usually stay at Crowne Plaza on Broadway and are up all night listening to sirens. I had the free breakfast at the hotel, quite impressive not just cold cereal and muffins, they had hot items as well. The only complaint I had was no bath tub. Other than that a great place to stay.

“最高でした” だんなの仕事の関係で泊まったのですが、いやーよかったです。場所も良いし、地下鉄の駅はすぐだし、大満足。帰りの飛行機に行くのにタクシーをポーターに頼んだら、リムジンを呼んでくれました。リモじゃなくて、タクシーで良いんだけど...と言ったら、フラットレイトでタクシーと同じ値段で良いとの事。ポーターと運転手は知り合いらしく、まあつまりはコネみたいなモンでしょうか。とにかくよかったです。ビジネスでも、ハネムーンでも安心しておすすめできるホテルです。

“Very good stay... with the right expectations” End of the quarter budget time and could not get to where I wanted to go with Priceline but instead found this hotel a few stops out of downtown on the Red line metro and I had a very good stay. i usually do not stay out past the Woodley Park stop and this is at Van Ness which is a couple of stops past Woodley on the Red line but it was worth the extra 5 minutes. The price was very reasonable and was close to anything ($$) I could have gotten on Priceline ( w/o knowning which hotel I would get). It's a very safe neighborhood and the hotel is literally 2 blocks from the metro. I had dinner(s) from the Giant Food store across from the metro and ate healthy all week. I did try the italian restaurant directly across the street and it was good/not great. I also ate lunch from the Potbelly Restaurant which is on the way to the metro and that was also basic but good. Front desk was friendly and helpful when I checked in, free coffee and tea but no breakfast, Room was a bit on the small side but very nice and updated. I was on the backside and it was quiet all week. Shower was hot in the morning and heat worked great during the very cold week outside. Pillows were plentiful but way too small and I ended up waking every night w/ either a stack of them or laying my head directly on the mattress as they had slipped out. Lobby is very small w/ very limited seats but I did slip into one of the chairs one afternoon and drank tea while watching the news and it was comfortable. I did hear a couple of complaints about having to pay for parking but I am a public transportation guy. I also overheard the manager solve a parking problem for a road crew that had stopped overnight w/ a very large truck and she was very good laying out the solution to the problem and the crew walked away happy. i did not pay much at all for a DC visit and for the $$, this hotel is a GREAT value and I will book it again.

“a noticeable step down from the peninsula...” after three nights at the peninsula, i ended up staying another night because the weather was crappy, and i have traveled enough times between NYC and chicago to know that any little hiccup in the weather will affect all flights, especially the last one out. as a result, i decided to stay another night, but this time at the four seasons, as i was able to procure a better rate than the peninsula (the peninsula was cheaper with the third night free option, but another night would have resulted in the full rate). i wish i could say that the four seasons is in the same category, but it isn't. the rooms are smaller (i had an upgraded room at the four seasons, but an entry-level room at the peninsula), though with much better views because of the height of the hotel. i found the service at the peninsula to be exemplary in every way--the four seasons was not nearly as good. as i write this, it's been 30 minutes since waiting for two bottles of water from housekeeping after missing my turndown service (i had the "privacy please" sign outside the door). i would not be surprised if it took another 30 minutes to get the two complimentary bottles of water. good thing i didn't ask for ice, too. the rooms are nice enough here, but after three nights at the peninsula, it was a letdown. the rooms here are smaller, and the bathroom is a little too compact. the toilet is right next to the shower/tub, whereas in the peninsula they are in two separate compartments with their own doors. the design of the shower is not great. the water pressure was much better here than in the peninsula, with much better control over the temperature, but the two doors that kept the water in the shower and off the floor did not serve the purpose well, and you had the floor covered in water. not a big deal, normally, but again, the toilet is right next to the shower, so your feet are covered in cold water as you use the toilet. also, the TV is much smaller, though most channels are in HD and much better quality than the peninsula, where the TV is larger, but many channels are not HD. as another reviewer pointed out, the design of this hotel is such that it sways and creaks when you have a windy night (common in chicago). so as i write this review, the building is creaking, and it's hard to tune out. now, i understand the hotel discloses this on some card or correspondence, but i don't see it in the room, and the idea of earplugs, while nice, doesn't help me because i am afraid i would oversleep as a result of them. the views here are spectacular, though, so that is a plus, and it is still a better hotel than most other places i stayed. as far as five-star properties in chicago, though, the peninsula is still top in my book. the trump is great as far as facilities, but the whole building is non-smoking, so that's a minus for me. the four seasons and peninsula have smoking rooms, which is nice because sometimes all i wanna do is light up a cigar at the end of the day. i know the four seasons takes their work seriously, so i do plan to address this with management.

“Great location, good value” My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights while visiting our children. The location is great, and we had an AAA promotional rate ($125) that was well below anything else that I could find in the area. As mentioned in some other reviews, the room was a smaller than most hotel roooms, but was still fine. The room was very quiet; we didn't hear a sound from outside or in the building; the window was double pane, with an additional storm pane, which eliminated all street noise. There is a cafe in the basement, and a neat-looking restaurant and bar attached to the hotel in what was once the ornate high-ceilinged lobby of the bank that formerly occupied the building. Within a couple of blocks are various eateries (including a Starbucks and a Subway for a quick breakfast and coffee), and a CVS as mentioned in another review. The free in-room internet was quite slow. We would stay there again.

“Great location!” First, nothing can beat the great location of this hotel. Right in the middle of down town and literally next to a metro station, which means you can easily get everywhere. The hotel was very clean, rooms were tastefuly decorated and in great condition. Staff was super nice and the breakfast we ordered through room service was excellent!

“Always a Winner” This was my third visit to this fine hotel in the last year and I'll always go back. A perfect location in the Short North arts district and next to the Arena Entertainment District, I like it because it's right in front of Columbus' North Market. I always enjoy a visit there too. Hotel front desk staff are always welcoming and friendly, especially my favorite "Taylor". She always does a nice job. The hotel is clean and has very nice rooms. Housekeeping does a nice job and the guys in valet parking, this time it was Nicola, are always on top of their game. Whether you're attending a convention (the convention center is across the street), on business travel, or with the family, this hotel is always a winning choice.

“Very nice” Hotel was very nice, enjoyed my time at this place, Hotel was first class the only problem was that at check out all four of our rooms had additional charges that we had to have removed. Almost all other at the meeting at the same problem.

“Loved every minute of NY. Great Location” Great location, fantastic staff and awesome rooms. I loved this hotel so much and would definitely stay here again! The staff all over the hotel were amazing in particular the bar staff. They were so friendly and helpful and made staying there that much more enjoyable. The Grand Hyatt is perfectly located to see everything only a short walk to Central Park, an even shorter walk to awesome shopping in particualr H&M which is just down the road and there are also really lovely restaurants nearby. I thought it was great value for money and would recommend it to anyone. New York is an awesome place and I am sure you will love it no matter where you stay however if you want a centrally located base which is great value for money then you really should stay here. I will stay here again for sure :). TIP: make sure you go to the Hotel Gansevoort roof top bar - it is amazing and the crab pizza is delicious!

“Great location, but only average hotel” The location of this hotel is excellent but unfortunately the hotel itself is only average. Positives were: location, ok sized room, big bed, big tv, mostly clean Negatives were: noise from the street (despite having asked for a quiet room), small bathroom, no bottled water in the room, charge for internet, pretty decrepit curtains

“Good deal in Midtown” Hyatt is definitely business oriented, but an excellent hotel if you can get a deal online through Priceline or Hotwire on the weekend. Was here for the Gates exhibition. Great location next to Grand Central Station and the buses to/from LaGuardia, Liberty-Newark, and Kennedy were practically across the street. Internet access available for minor cost in the business center. Rooms standard size for NYC, comfortable beds, nicely done renovation. Would definitely stay here again for anywhere to $170 a night.

“Not what it used to be” This was my 5th (and probably final) time staying at the Palmer House. My family and I stay here the week after Thanksgiving every year. There is a very large medical conference that a family member of mine participates in and my husband and I join for some exra time we would not otherwise get with the family. My first few years I was highly impressed with the Palmer House and it's offerings. At the price we were paying, I would expect to be impressed. Even last year amidst all of the renovations (which were only extensive to the "street level and pool/spa) it was still impressive. We always stay on the "Executive Level" because of our "status" with Hilton Hotels (HHonors). On this level you need a special key to access the floor and it's executive lounge. In the lounge (in years past) we were greeted with a nice amount of options, both hot and cold, for breakfast. Large bagles, fruit, hot oatmeal, fresh bread, eggs or something similar and wonderful Douwe Egberts coffee, Tazo teas, hot chocolate and a fridge full of sodas and juice. All free for the taking. This year there were no hot offerings, not even packets of oatmeal. Only toast, small bagles, small dried up muffins and pastries. The coffee has been switched to Lavazza (which sucks), the soda is still available but they are small bottles. The small botles were not the bad part as they are still a good amount. The problem is that in the week I was there, I was never able to open a bottle. I did not see one woman able to open a bottle the entire time. Not even the bar tender. I was told by an employee in the executive lounge that they cut-backs were made because of the economy. That... I can understand. Read further. Part of the new renovation is the spa and pool. The pool is average but by no means looks like it has been remodeled. Not to mention you have to walk and walk and walk down all types of back hallways past conference rooms to even find the pool. Odd since they frown upon you wearing a swimsuit around the guests. Not sure how to get from your room to the pool otherwise. Maybe that's why theer was never anyone at the pool the whole time I was there during a week the hotel was completely sold out. Which is another point. There were NUMEROUS things that the hotel has cut-back on to save a dine here and there but the price of the closet size, paper thin walls have gone up. My king size bedroom closet size room was $221 a night. They have taken all of the coffee makers out of the room (which they had installed brand new the very week I was there last year). Even a budget hotel offers a coffee maker in the room. They said this was part of the cut-back. So, now you are forced to buy their coffee from room service, which we did one night. 2 cups of decaf = $14 plus a tip. Did I mention that if you are one of the lucky few to get executive level status, there is no decaf? I had to call and ask why there was no decaf because the employees of the exec. lounge just said "it's not offered" every time I asked. It was eventually brought up the last 2 days of my stay. The concierge recommended a restuarant called "Tavern at the Park" which is just next to Millenium Park our first night there. But my husband and I received a healthy dose of food poisoning. I don't recommened this place to eat. The second day, a couple moved into the room next to us. As mentioned above, the walls in the hotel are seriuosly paper thin. The couple began having sex at 5pm on Sunday and didn't stop until 7am on Monday. They were anything but quiet. I tried knocking on the wall, slamming my door, slamming a closet door (which they also did frequently) and at 5am I called security and told them to handle it before I did. The couple quieted down from 5:30-6 when they picked up where they left off. Security stated that they have done alll they can do. Now we are talking two nights with no sleep. I did go to the front desk the next morning and complained. They happily moved us to another floor and a bigger room. We were told it was a 2 bed, 2 bath. It would have been had the second bath not been under construction. To conclude this long review (and I could certainly go on and on)... if you are new to the Palmer House, you will not know anything is wrong (except the rooms were absolutely freezing the whole time). If you are a returning guest... you will most definately notice some serious changes.

“Great location and very good experience” Booked this on Hilton points. Six nights on Diamond reward so had a king suite on 28th floor which was a great view. Breakfast buffet was very good although exactly the same all six mornings. Had to meet my driver at 6:45 so opening at 6:30 was a challenge. Staff made sure i was fed and I appreciated that. Very busy week in NYC with the fleet and Memorial Day but well managed by the hotel. Have stayed here several times before and it was better than I remembered. Good exercise room. Convenient to everything. Nothing truly amazing but a very comfortable stay with only one disappointment experienced by my wife. The refrigerator was not working and we lost $50 of food from a steak house and a sushi bar. It took all day to get it working and she lost the only sunny day waiting in the room for the repair man. Staff tried to recover and provided several options which we accepted with satisfaction.

“Excellent location and service” I stayed at the Westin Times Square while on a week vacation in NYC in August 2012. My experience and recommendation can be described by the below: Location The hotel is definitely at one of the best locations you can stay at in NYC. Located in the heart of midtown it is exactly at times square with all major attractions and entertainment facilities located in a radius of 2 to 3 blocks: 5th avenue for example is only 3 blocks away while avenue of the Americas is 2 blocks down. As soon as you step out of the main entrance, you are on 8th avenue, 43rd street just seconds away form a variety of restaurants and bistros from all around the world. (Shake Shack is just in front....just cross the road). Furthermore, the hotel is at really close distance from all artistic attractions of Broadway. the Minksof theater where Lion King is playing is just two blocks ahead and all other theaters at a walking distance. The Intrepid museum is on 12th avenue accessible on foot or 5 minutes by cab including the NYC traffic. The hotel really has one of the best locations to be in while "touristing" in NYC. Hotel and rooms The building is really nice both on the outside and on the inside. Main entrance on 8th avenue is lavish and holds the security and baggage claim desks. A large escalator takes you all the way up to a grand front desk and concierge services as well as a really cozy and elegant seating area. The experience starts really well at the hotel the minute you step inside the lobby. The hotel also has another entrance from 42nd street which is equally nice. Rooms are quite large and very well decorated. I was in a two double bed that was very spacious and really comfortable. It was on the 24th floor boasting a great view on the Hudson river and the surrounding area. The bathroom is neatly decorated and equipped with all services you would expect. The only drawback is that on some floors the halls are a little complex and intertwine with one another. Halls are all greyish so some light or colors might make things look way better. But it is not a note that will push you away from the hotel, it is just a small note I picked up while there. Service Service at the Westin can't be described by nothing other than just perfect. You are greeted with a beautiful smile that makes you feel welcome every single step of the way. I would like to extend the best compliments to "Sarah" at front desk who was just wonderful in making the check in process one of a kind knowing that my room was not available at time of check in. She was really great in the way she reassured me and greeted me at the premises. I truly recommend that you ask for her if you check in at the Westin. As for room service and house keeping, they are also very nice. I have been provided with all my requests and more by really great personnel who never refrained from being there whenever they were needed. Security and bell boys are extremely helpful, they were great in helping me with directions and booking of cars and taxis. Service at the Westin is one of the best I have ever experienced in a high end hotel Prices Well to be honest it is not a cheap hotel. I ended up paying USD 370 a night and that was a discounted rate. But I think it is a perfectly explained price for such a hotel, location and time of the year (high season). It is really worth every penny. I strongly recommend the Westin times Square for your next stay in NYC.

“Perfektes Hotel für einen Städtetripp” Das Hotel liegt unmittelbar an einer der grossen Subway Stationen (Columbus Circle), wenige Gehminuten vom Centralpark entfernt und Nahe 5th Avenue. Die Zimmer sind sehr sauber, jedoch wirklich recht klein - was uns nicht wirklich gestört hat, da man den ganzen Tag unterwegs ist. Dafür ist der Schlafkomfort sehr gut. Einzig die Nasszellen sind ein wenig zu klein; fast keine Platz auf dem stillen Örtchen! Tolle Sky Terrace, unschlagbar. Bedient mit Liegen und einer Hängematte, Lounches. Auch Abends sehr schön! Alle Sehenswürdigkeiten sind - wie fast überall in Manhattan - sehr gut zu Fuss, Taxi oder mit der Subway erreichbar.
“Sofitel shines again...” The service is prompt, the rooms are clean and tastefully decorated and the beds are comfortable. The location in DC is tough to beat.

“A pleasant surprise!” I did not know what to expect when I walked into the lobby - it seemed old world and perhaps had seen better days - but I was pleasantly surprised when I got to my room - the bathroom was large and the room itself was large and very clean - I had a terrific view of Soldier's Field from my window. The hotel itself is across the street from Grant Park and the weather was hot so it was nice being across from a park. We had a dog with us so it came in quite handy - oh yes, the hotel is pet friendly! The outdoor area on Michigan Avenue are terrific whether you are grabbing a quick coffee or eating at the restaurant there.....the gym was nice too and open 24 hours...The architecture in the lobby definitely gives an old world vibe but the rooms are definitely top notch!

“Amazing lobby, nice rooms , awesome staff!” I stayed 5 days at the Renaissance hotel. The check-in was a breeze and the people were so nice. Every time i met someone in the hotel , i was greeted politely.My room was very clean and big and there was a small fridge also. The lobby of the hotel is so unique. It is very trendy and a fun place to have a chat with friends. If you dont want to pay for the internet , you can also relax on the confortable chairs and tables next to the sports bar. There is a starbucks, a deli market, and a little convenient store inside. I know there is more stuff on the lower level but I never went there. I mostly ate at the deli market, fresh sandwiches , salads and fresh from the oven cookies. The location is good , lots of restaurants very close and 2 blocks from Chinatown and 4 blocks from the Verizon center. I did walk all the time to visit all the museums, memorials and White House but it might be a lot for someone who doesn't like to walk. Your walks are never boring since the archictecture of Washington is just stunning. I can say that I was surprised a bit with the hotel. It deserve a 5 star rating for all the efforts they have been putting on the decor and the amazing service.

“Not very clean!” My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights, paid for through Priceline. The lobby is fine, but when we got to our room, it was filthy! You could tell the carpet had not been vacuumed as there was paper, coins, and food in it. My bed had several strands of hair in it and stuck in the pillows. The shower was moldy and had soap residue caked in the little soap trays. I asked for a different room, and although the front desk clerk was friendly and accomadating, she didn't apologize for the dirty room or for the inconvenience of having to change rooms. The second room was a little better. Overall, this hotel is not very clean. The hallway carpets were very dirty, and there was always room service dishes left outside rooms practically all day. I would not stay at this hotel again.

“Pretty Good for a Holiday Inn” Spent just one night here while attending a convention nearby. Good location along Wisconsin Avenue with many restaurants a few minutes walk up a short hill. Asked a pedestrian at the corner for a restaurant recommendation and she pointed out a place called "Bourbon" with no sign outside. Only locals could have possibly known that it was a restaurant. It was an excellent find. The hotel itself has recently remodeled all of its rooms. From other reviewers, it sounded like this was well overdue. Everything in my room was clean and fresh. Oddly, I was missing a desk that other rooms included. The front desk clerk said they were still getting new furniture delivered and distributed. I have two main suggestions on how to make an average stay maybe above average: the Internet, while free (much appreciated!) was incredibly slow. I suspect the entire apartment building directly next door gets free Internet since the connection is not protected, thus eating up bandwidth. Second, the heating/cooling system cycled on and off all night with a big "clunk" each time. If would just stay on constantly it would have been better and helped to block out traffic noise. Breakfast buffet has good selection of hot and cold but quirky. For example, great biscuits but no gravy. Huh? I'd recommend this hotel if you're in the area.

“Wonderful Choice” Enjoyed our stay at the Park Hyatt. An elegant hotel, beautiful lobby area with a helpful, efficient staff. Nicely appointed rooms and very comfortable beds. A short walk to the Foggy Bottom metro station. Would definitely stay here again.

“Didn't even take shower because we were so grossed out” Stayed in hotel Pennsylvania during a family trip to New York. Conveniently located, yes, but you have to ask yourself what type of quality you want to sacrifice for a low price. The hotel advertises having rooms with "city views", do you know what part of the city we saw? The brick wall of the adjacent building. I think the only way this hotel still functions as a business is to mislead potential patrons to stay here and lure people with lower prices. I've stayed at really nice hotels, and I've stayed in a sleeping bag on cold wet leaves too-I know not everything can be the Ritz Carlton; but I personally did not care for this hotel whatsoever. Do yourself a favor and spend a little more to give yourself a vacation that's you're going to remember for the great things you did, not for the sub-par hotel you stayed in.

“ausländischen Standort” Chicago ist eine Stadt, die weitgehend problemlos zu Fuß besucht werden kann, aber das Hotel liegt etwas ganz Besonderes. Obwohl nahe dem Zentrum, fühlt es sich weit von der Route. Es hat sogar so etwas wie ein Motel. Das Hotel selbst ist nicht schlecht, aber nicht ein Ort, wo du schon etwas Zeit im Laufe des Tages zu verbringen. Die Club Lounge war enttäuschend, aber dank diesem Raum war die Nutzung der Sportstätte verantwortlich. Die Zimmer sind nicht besonders, aber man kann Glück mit der Sicht. Insgesamt nicht zu empfehlen.

“Great hotel, great value!” I planned a week-long trip during New Year's with a friend from Italy and we stayed at the Washington Hilton (1919 Connecticut Ave). Great hotel!! The price was excellent, the staff was extremely friendly, the room was clean and comfortable, and we had a lovely view of the Washington Monument right out our window. The location in Dupont Circle is nice, only about a 10 min walk to the metro, and surrounded by nice restaurants and shops. We walked to everything but took the metro mostly towards the end of our trip because we were tired. Overall, an excellent choice if you're planning a trip to DC! I'll definitely stay here again!

“Beuatiful Hotel in Great UT Location” This was my 3rd stay the the AT&T Conference Center in 2009. This is a beautiful property with big well-appointed rooms, comfortable beds and upscale toiletries. The street level restaurant serves a nice if pricey breakfast. The staff was very helpful. When I checked in at 11pm, I realized that needed to have my shoes shined for the next morning's meeting. The person at the reception desk took the shoes. They were shined and delivered to my room within 15 minutes. Ask for a room with a view of campus/the tower.

“Great and less than great” It's the Ritz but I need to give it three stars. Very snooty but very professional. Rooms are great, bathrooms very great. Restaurant is way expensive and when room service finishes adding on their extra charges the price almost doubled. It's a ten minute walk to Georgetown. There is no view from your room. Prostitutes come in the bar late at night looking for business. I'm not joking as I saw them work the bar every night for the week I was there. You share the elevator with people going to the connected gym so it always has extra people not part of the hotel coming in and out.

“The Plaza was great!” This summer we've stayed at the Plaza. We are a family with two children (teenagers) and we go to NY once a year. Every time we try another hotel! We've stayed at the Waldorff Astoria too, but this time we really liked to stay at the Plaza, after the renovation. Well, we were nicely surprised! The room was spacious and the bathroom even more! Everything looked very luxurious, really great. The lobby was beautiful too, with the nicely decorated bar. The only annoying thing was that the last day there was a 'doorman' who asked everyone if they were hotelguests before they were allowed to enter the lobby. He did this in a very impolite way, and when my son had to go back, so he had to enter the lobby twice in about 5 minutes, this 'doorman' asked it AGAIN! That was a little silly.. But for the rest we had a really nice stay!

“Central location; decent accommodations” My husband and I stayed at the Ren Cen for a family wedding. The location was very central, and being on the river was nice. The room size was adequate, but the bathroom was small in comparison. Although relatively clean, it was clear that the hotel is due for a renovation soon. The room and the hallways definitely show signs of wear & tear. Clearly, the hotel wasn't soundproofed sufficiently to block out the techno concert next door. Overall, not bad, but I would consider another hotel if we return to Detroit.

“unresponsive & unprofessional” I have never stayed at this hotel; however I did block 15 rooms for my daughter's wedding this May. I called and spoke with the Reservations Manager who emailed me with a nightly rate and I emailed back thanking her and asking the date after which our block of rooms would be released. She replied with this info and said they looked forward to having us--or words to that effect. This was all done last October. Last month I asked my daughter to email this woman and ask if any of the blocked rooms had been booked. The reply came from a man in a terse message--no explanation of why he was replying instead of the person with whom I'd corresponded. His tone was unprofessional--he said we didn't have rooms blocked because I'd never signed anthing--I'd never been asked to sign anything and would have if I had been asked and he added that the room rate I'd be quoted was no longer valid--now it was higher. I forwarded the original correspondence and said that I didn't know who he was or why he was replying instead of our original contact there. He never responded! I read in another review that management is unresponsive. I'd agree. I'd recommend staying at another hotel where they understand that they're in a service business.

“Worked well for the needs of our extended family” We stayed here two nights, one on each end of flights in and out of Sky Harbor. It is very convenient to the airport and the shuttle service worked great for our different family members needs. The first night we had a one bedroom and since there was not a lot of extra room in the bedroom, we put the play and pack in the living area where baby comfortably spent the night. Used the light above the stove as a night light and could easily check on sleeping baby. The bedroom had a good sized vanity outside the bathroom and a spacious closet. Very nice to have the fridge and extra sink. We did bring our own bottles of water and kept them nicely chilled. During our second night stay we had a 2 bedroom unit and the 2nd bedroom had room for the play and pack. Had a much smaller vanity and it was also outside the bathroom. Nice closet. For some reason the AC was much louder in this room but it was consistent and gave a white noise effect which worked fine for sleeping baby and us.The main bathroom on this stay had hair in the tub when I pulled back the shower curtain. Until this everything appeared clean. After dinner, we arrived back to a power outage in the hotel and area. We had a case of bottled water + groceries and a baby. An employee who was helping another guest as well, jumped in to carry our water and give us a glow stick to find our way to the 4th floor (no elevators, of course). The room was already getting warm (108 that day in Phoenix). Within an hour we were very relieved to have the power restored but it did take quite awhile for our unit to cool down to our comfort level - sometime during the night. Renovations were occuring in the public areas while we were there so the breakfast/reception area seemed a little makeshift but it appears it will be nice when finished. Breakfast included several hot options - oatmeal, eggs, waffles, and the usual accompanying fare. It was not a large room but we had no difficulty securing a table either morning. Did pop into reception but soup (August in Phoenix?) was the main entree so we just enjoyed good cookies. All the employees were very cordial and accomodating. I look forward to be able to stay at this hotel again.

“OK-but some glitches” Ok stay-bathroom is very small and basic for the nice furnishings throughout the rest of the hotel. Bed wes comfy-air conditioning very old and noisy, and since the thermostat is right next to the vent it kept turning off and on all night. Restaurant was ok. Room service B'fast was horrid! And they were late in delivering it. Bigguyinpasadena

“Stayed 3 months” I stayed 3 months at this hotel on business. As a platinum status member, being on club level and having a good concierge lounge is important. I love the rooms. They are like new, well maintained, clean, and large. The lobby is big and decor is modern. Overall, this is my hotel of choice in this area if the price is right, and it was. The downside was concierge lounge. The hot food was useless for all 3 months. They never had anything I liked but the cheese and crackers, and the dessert. When they put the aged cheddar out, my weight becomes an issue. Great cheeses! But lousy hot food, and the lady was not friendly to me for all 3 months. You would think that after 3 months, she would go out of her way to be nice. She was usually watching TV and was too busy. In contrast, the morning staff in the concierge lounge were very friendly, and the food there was as expected. If they cleaned up their act on the night time concierge lounge, I would give them 5 stars. The front clerk staff is friendly and professional. The one Asian room service lady was awesome. She was very nice and I looked forward to seeing her. Room service food is good but nor great. Fish is always fresh and tastes great. They can also prepare it the way you want, not just what the menu says.

“Nice place to stay in the city” My daughter treated my wife and I to an overnight stay in New York at the Hampton as well as a dinner cruise on the Hudson and East River. We took the bus up from the Jersey Shore to the Port Authority and walked the ten easy blocks to the Hampton on 51st and 8th. We arrived early on a Monday afternoon. We were able to check right into our room, so we were able to unpack and go exploring. It is always nice to get an early check-in. We had a cheap but filling lunch at the beer bar around the corner on 51st. Good burgers and some good brews on tap. I had the ten dollar beer and burger special. It came with a pickle and an ample supply of fries. The burger was home made (not a patty). Back to the hotel. One of the elevators was out of service for our whole stay. The one elevator that was in use was definitely overworked. When we arrived we were taken to our room by way of the freight elevator. People were using it during our whole stay. From a liability standpoint, I am not too sure on the advisability of this practice. My wife and I preferred to use the stairs to our 6th floor room. It was good exercise. The room was of ample size. It had a nice 32 inch flat screen tv. The king sized bed was very comfortable. Plenty of pillows and sheets with a good thread count. The bathroom was small though. There was really room for only one occupant at a time. The shower was hot with good water pressure. The heat - air worked well. There were no loud noises or wild parties. The morning breakfast was very well attended. There were waffles as well as all the other items that one expects at a Hampton breakfast. I wish there were some eggs and bacon though. Perhaps they rotate the menu from day to day. The workout room was small but well stocked with treadmills and other equipment. All of the workers we came in contact with seemed to do a good job. The desk was quite professional. I think we will make this hotel the base of operations for any future New York overnight stays. It seemed very popular so one may have trouble getting a last minute booking.

“location location location” This is a trendy, modest sized property in an upscale part of Boston near the government center. The rooms are sytlish and somewhat minimalist, the bed comfortable, the bath modern and mid-sized. The value here is reasonable for Boston and the location outstanding. The gym, though modest in size, is clean and modern also. The folks at the front desk were very helpful and engaged at both check in and when I confirmed directions to a restaurant. The sytle is not overbearing or pretentious. Did not eat at the hotel but within a five minute walk are a number of fantastic if pricey restaurants on Beacon Street. I was going to the Orpheum theatre that night and it was COLD with some icey sidewalks so this location was ideal. I would definitely go back if I was going to another show at the Orpheum in less than ideal weather, can not beat the distance or proximity of great food.

“Nice rooms” The Greektown Casino Hotel is a good option if you are traveling with a large party and require decent and easy accommodation. I found the service to be excellent and the rooms to be contemporary and clean. The only drawbacks to this hotel are that it is part of a casino and the heavy traffic associated with that as well as the limited healthy food options in the adjoining restaurant(s). Valet parking is included with your hotel stay and the friendly staff are more than happy to make whatever accommodation you may need. I do know that my traveling companion did have difficulty when he requested an earlier check-in - tho I would attribute this to the fact that this is a casino centered hotel.

“3 Day Trip To San Diego” This is a great location. Down the street from the Petco Ballpark. Location is great Parking: Valet Only Place had a gym with water cooler. Terrace near the gym. The 9th floor had the gym, the terrace, the bar/lounge area. The grass area for the pets, and another terrace with the firepit and view. There was a bar downstairs/eatery with a business center. Very clean place and pet friendly. The rooms were excellent and clean and modern style. Did a segway tour with the "Another side of San Diego" Did the Balboa Park tour, it was fun since I have never been on a segway before. Recommended for everyone.

“Best Value in Midtown Manhattan if all you need is a place to sleep” The Courtyard New York Manhattan / Midtown East is a great choice if all you need is a place to sleep, but if you are looking for a full service hotel this is not the place for you. Our room was large for a Midtown Manhattan hotel, and the rate was low. There's a subway stop nearby, Central Park is a short walk, and there are plenty of restaurants nearby if you want a simple meal after a long day in the city. Overall, this hotel provides excellent value as a base for a visit to NYC. Many attractions are a short walk away, and all others are easily accessed by subway or taxi. Will not hesitate to use this property again.

“gorgeous” Just got back from a 4-day stay at the Desert Ridge. Really gorgeous place with great service. Was there for a conference and all of the conference sessions were fantastic. The hotel was cool and never too warm (no easy feat in Phoenix in August!) and refreshments were always stocked. Food at the banquet meals was fantastic, and I usually hate banquet meals. Food service staff was great. Hotel was very clean and fantastic service throughout. Gorgeous pool area with several pools and very ample chairs/shade available. Really nice patio/lanai area. Rooms were nice and very clean. This is a resort experience. My only gripes: housekeeping staff never quite caught on that there were 4 of us in the room and never left enough towels/washcloths so we had to keep asking for them. Prices at bar were very high. Bad wireless connections and had to pay to have it in room, but free in lobby. Not much to complain about, but had I been paying for this myself (and it is pricey), I probably would not have been more annoyed about these minor things. Room has everything: alarm clock, TV, toiletries. Very large shopping area with great stores/restaurants across the street (about a 10-15 minute walk I would guess). Very nice place with great service. I would go back.

“Hotel in guter Lage in Chicago” Das Hotel liegt direkt am Chicago River, nur 3-4 Gehminuten von der Michigan Avenue (Haupteinkaufstrasse) und ca. 10 Gehminuten vom Navy Pier entfernt. Ein gutes Mittelklassehotel, mit vielen Serviceleistungen, für Touristen und Geschäftsreisende geeignet. Die Zimmer sind teilweise renoviert, gut eingerichtet und sauber. Einziger Negativpunkt, in den renovierten Zimmern steht das Bett jetzt mitten im Raum, was zur Folge hat, dass die Klimaanlage die in der Decke angebracht ist, einem mitten ins Gesicht bläst. Die Klimaanlage lässt sich nicht abschalten. Das Hotel hat mehrere Bars und Restaurants, sowie einen Starbucks. Leider alles etwas teuer. Hier geht man besser in eines der zahlreichen Restaurants in unmittelbarer Nähe. Das Frühstück im Hotel kostet 25$, im Restaurant direkt nebenan bekommt man ein Frühstücksbuffet für 10$. Zu den Hauptcheck-in / - out Zeiten ist es an der Rezeption sehr voll. Lange Wartezeiten sind einzuplanen auch wenn die Rezeption teilweise mit bis zu 10 Personen besetzt ist. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich, offen und hilfsbereit. Aufgrund der Grösse des Hotels und der vielen Gäste ist es immer ein wenig unruhig, wer Erholung sucht ist hier fehl am Platz.

“Basic hotel in great Seattle Center/Queen Anne location” I recommend my visitors stay in this hotel when they visit me in Seattle because it is cheap and in a great location near the Space Needle and waterfront. It is definitely basic/no frills, so if you're looking for something really nice, I wouldn't recommend it. But if you don't plan to spend a lot of time in the room this place is perfect. The rooms and bathroom are very large and very clean, but the beds are a little hard and the bedspreads are thin and nothing special. The common areas are nice and clean and the receptionists always friendly and helpful. The great thing about this place is that it is literally in the shadow of the Space Needle and a few blocks from the Olympic Sculpture Park. It is about a mile from downtown shopping and Pike's Place Market. It is located in Queen Anne, which is a very cute neighborhood area just north of downtown. I would highly recommend Peso's Mexican Kitchen for a late night drink or dinner, and they have amazing breakfast (best in town). You should also visit the top of Queen Anne and browse the shops there.

“Decent, but not as depicted on website and in photos.” The Curtis is a nice enough hotel in a great location. My problem with the hotel is that it's nothing like what they depict on the website and in photos. It's really just your average, aging Sheraton hotel that they've tried to add a few gimmicks to and increase the price. That being said, the location of the hotel is nice.

“Wonderful Hotel...” Wonderful hotel that is all we needed for a trip to The Big Apple! This hotel had friendly staff and clean, REALLY clean rooms. Yes, the room was small but so is all of the other rooms unless you have an endless bank account to splur on the MORE expensive hotels. There is a beautiful bathroom that gives a shower or bath. The king sized bed was absolutely wonderful. The air was great after a long day of sight-seeing and shopping. The breakfast bar is great. The negative is that there is little room to sit down. What's a little standing? I think we go the best hotel in the area. It is right around the block from Times Square, all the Broadway shows, and plenty of shopping. There is no view from any of the windows. The pictures that you view here or on the candid photos doesn't do the room justice. I wouldn't bring kids but is great for two!

“Best Westin in Chicagoland!” I stayed hear when my apartment was being painted after moving to Chicago for work. When I got to the front desk (SPG Gold member) they automatically upgraded me to a corner river view room on a high floor. I also had access to their club upstairs. Great hor' dourves and free softdrinks. It was basically my dinner by the time I left. I had a lovely night watching 4th of July fireworks from my window. Slept great and left with late check out. The next year I went their to find a quiet place to talk on the phone and they let me borrow a conference room. AMAZING!!!

“Beautiful grand Hotel” I've been stayed there for 4 nights. it's a wonderful hotel. It's a huge hotel, very friendly staff and great location. Nice clean room, good proximity to shopping area. Close to the park. Good ambience.

“Great location for a conference or pleasure trip” Stayed seven nights recently for a conference. Most convenient hotel to the city conference center. Great views from higher floors of either the harbor or the Gas Lamp area. Above average fitness center on the ground floor of the north tower was open 24hrs. Very nice pool area. Close walk to light rail/trolleys. Concierge lounge is on the 24th floor of the south tower and is very nice but a little crowded. It overlooks the water. Nice large shower and pillow top bed with good quality pillow options. On-site meals and drink costs were high, parking was $26 for self park, more for valet. Not the place to stay if you are looking for a bargain, but extra nice location and property overall. Only problems I had was a very loud Saturday night on-property night club that I could hear clearly on the 24th floor, and housekeeping repeatedly turning my room temp down to 68 degrees from where I had it set at 72.

“Comfortable, sort of by the bay” Having read a bad review of a place near Civic Center I have stayed in a couple of times before, I changed at last minute to Comfort Inn by the Bay based on reviews here. The recent reviews are quite accurate: this is a decent place to stay, somewhat convenient to Fisherman's Wharf, a little inconvenient for other locations. Room was small but fine; loud noise from rain falling on the air conditioner can be forgiven since that day was the heaviest rain on that date since 1838! Room faced a wall, so no view, but hardly ever in it during the day, so that was also no problem. Upgrades available for a fee. Wireless internet handy and free. Surprisingly, hard to find a late night snack on Lombard, but pretty good snacks in the snack machine on the third floor. Breakfast was quite good, especially the waffles. Was there pretty early every day so can't comment on them possibly running out of things. From one block north (Chestnut) there is the #30 bus through North Beach and Chinatown to downtown, takes about 20-25 minutes. To come to the hotel, cable car to Lombard, then walk downhill. To make the return trip that way would be a bit brutal since it is quite a hill. As usual, for a stay in the SF city area, a Muni Passport is a good idea, I don't think they have them at the desk though. This is especially true if staying at this hotel since only Fisherman's Wharf west area (Ghirardelli etc.) is really within walking distance. Staff, as mentioned in other reviews, was quite friendly and helpful and the area is better than many.

“Good hotel - Good location” My company and I stay in this hotel a couple of times per year on business trips to the area. This location is always clean and the people at the desk are always friendly. The beds and linens are not 5 star quality but they are very nice. It is easy to get on and off of the freeway to this location and the parking is good. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the area.

“Un buen hotel” Nos alojamos en este hotel dos noches. La zona del hotel no esta en pleno cento de Dallas, como a unos 5 kilometros. Vamos que desde la habitacion tienes unas vistas preciosas del Downtown de Dallas. El parking del hotel era gratuito, asi que eso esta muy bien. La habitacion era muy amplia y las camas muy comodas, ya que estuvimos en dos camas queen size. El baño estaba muy limpio. Vamos que estaba dentro de lo que puedes esperar de un Doubletree. Por cierto, la zona tiene poco alrededor asi que lo mejor es coger el coche y marchar a ver el Downtown. Solo hay un pequeño Wendy ́s enfrente del hotel. Pero bueno, no esta mal el hotel teniendo en cuenta que el Downtown de Dallas es bastante caro. Resumiendo, me alojaria aqui de nuevo.

“Overnight getaway” My wife and I live about one hour's drive from Boston, and wanted to grab a couple of days in Back Bay during the holiday season. I agree with other reviewers that the location is supurb for experiencing the best shopping that Boston has to offer, and as long as the winter weather is cooperative, puts you within walking distance of many charming and interesting attractions. Indeed, in warm weather, I've even walked to Fenway Park from this location. With a AAA room rate and mid-December hotel slump, the price was right. Extremely accomodating staff and classic (meaning not modern) decor, was just right for us. The attached City Table Restaurant is a plus, particularly on a cold and blustery evening. The noise level is a bit high, but the food is of excellent quality and the prices put it into the $$$ range. The upscale Copley Place Mall is just a few blocks away, and the shops, galleries and restaurants of Newbury Street are one block north. If you like to browse libraries, as I sometimes do, cross Exeter Street to the Boston Public Library. Just one night and two days like this can really do wonders for one's spirits. There was mention on another review of the $43.00 valet parking fee. That can be avoided by clicking onto www.boston.centralparking.com and printing out a certificate for the Prudential parking garage, which is just a bit further down Exeter Street from The Lenox. The discounted fee for 24 hours is $25.00, and there is no one to tip.

“Pass on this one! A DOG WITH FLEAS!” They really don't care. I called Hilton to complain! This is the POOREST service I have ever encountered! If you are on business STAY SOMEPLACE ELSE! THEY ARE HORRID!

“Good Experience With Park & Fly Option” My wife and I used this hotel recently to fly out of the Indianapolis airport. We drove up late the night before our flight and then used the shuttle to the airport. The car stayed for an additional 4 nights. Hotel was nice, what little we saw since we got in so late. Room was clean, bed was extremely comfortable, front desk staff was nice. Shuttle ran on time, both to and from airport. I will note, however, that the park & fly rate was approximately equal to the basic room rate plus what airport parking would have cost, so it's not a free lunch. However, the convenience of getting a gate drop-off, etc., was worth something to us, and it more than offset the little bit of waiting/scheduling necessary for the shuttle.

“Nice Hotel” I go up to Seattle a few times a year for business and mostly stay at the W Seattle. If I have some spare time, I like to take a walk down to the shopping area, its pretty close to restaurants. Easy to find, valet parking available. The lobby is a little funky at night, but in a cool way. I've had drinks in their bar and lounge area before, nice vibe. The room was comfortable, nice flat screen, bathroom was a good size. Although they need to do something about the shower curtain. Its too short and has no weights in the bottom of it and is constantly blowing back on me. Next time I'll make sure to ask for a room with a separate shower stall. Plus it has a straight shower bar, they need to install the curved ones. Apart from that, the stay was great. Definitely going back.
“Great Location, Average Room” Great Location, Average Room. We have stayed at this Hyatt twice - it is is fine if you get a good deal, but really needs to be updated. Staff is friendly and helpful.

“Good Hotel for Family Visit to NYC” There is nothing flashy about this hotel, but it more than gets the job done. For starters, there are not a lot of options in Manhattan for a family of five. This hotel fits the bill. Also the location is great. It is a long, but doable walk to Times Square for example. However with that said, there is a Subway E/M station steps from the hotel and more lines within another block away. There is also a Duane Reed drug store essentially attached to the hotel (which has a sizable grocery section) and a CVS a block away. Both are 24 hours. While there does not seem to be a lot of fine dining options nearby, there are other chain/intriguing options (like Essa Bagels a block away). While the rooms are nondescript, they are functional with very comfortable beds and a great TV. There is a restaurant onsite, but only breakfast is served. Finally the staff all seemed very helpful and friendly. Overall, I would recommend this property for a no-frills NYC family vacation.

“Very clean spacious room” My husband and 1 year old stayed here for two nights while visiting Boston. The room was very spacious and clean. The staff was very friendly and even allowed us to check in early and upgraded us to a king size room (instead of queen). The pool and workout room was impressive -- the pool roof retracts so the indoor pool can become an outdoor pool and the weight room seemed to have a lot of equipment. The hotel is connected to the prudential center shops which is very convenient. Also, it's stop number 11 on the Old Town Trolley which made our sightseeing very easy. The only complaint was that the doors to the rooms had about an inch shaved off of the bottom so you could hear everything going on out in the hall and everyone in the hall could hear everything being said (or screeched by our 1 year old) in the hall.

“just OK” My daughter and I spent the weekend at the Sofitel. We checked in Friday night and thought the room, a delux with double beds and a city vew for $219.99 per night, a good value. The room was spacious with a sitting area and nice marbled bathroom with a seperate shower and tub. The furniture in the room was a bit worn but the beds were comfortable. We left the room on Saturday from 10-3 and housekeeping had not cleaned the room upon our return. They did call at 5 asking if we would like the room cleaned. The hotel advertises turn down service each evening, but that service was never rendered the first evening. Room service was timely and tasty. The hotel is located very close to a Metro station and the doormen were on their toes throughout our stay. On the day of our departure I had asked for a late check out at 2 PM . Upon our return to the hotel at 1 we found that our keys would not open the door to our room and I had to return to the desk to remind them of our request for late check out. They graciously re-programmed our keys. With all of the boutique hotels availablr in DC I think I might try another one next time.

“Great location” Stayed here for one night. Very impressive facade and lobby, but unfortunately the rooms were only so so. There was warning on the mini bar that if you put personal items in there they would charge you a hefty fee. If you wanted the items removed they woul charge you a fee etc. Water bottles was 4 Dollars. This is usually free at hotels costing 300 Dollars pluss. Rather unusual and not very customer friendly with this minibar warning either. PS Pool is only 3 feet so only suitable for kids. Otherwise OK

“"The Purr-fect Property for Passing Thru LAX!"” I live a good bit of my life at 35,000 feet or in hotel rooms, and when I step off the plane in LA, the last thing I look forward to is having to sit in LA Freeway traffic to find a comfy bed for the night. The Custom is just purr-fect for nesting nearby LAX, has a bowling alley within a baseball toss, a great pub across the road, 24 hour grocery shopping and that's just to mention a few of the local seductions; like good Italian food, walks in the park, or great Thai you'll be pleased to meander away from the hotel's very trendy pool club and meeting place settings. The furnishing are all trendy, and my bed was lower to the ground than I'm accustomed but I had a great night's sleep and the Staff is "ta die for!" The cherry on the top of the hotel's attraction is the fact that they'll 'send a sleek black car to collect me from the airport' and its a whopping 12-14 minutes from the curbside of LAX before I'm in the lobby, asking for a room with a view. Mark Sheehan, author of "America Over Easy!" The KNOW BEFORE You Go Guides.

“Exemplifies the luxury of Four Seasons!” A return, and too short, visit to the Four Seasons on E. Delaware Place at N. Michigan Ave. What a great neighborhood! What a great hotel! It's pricey, but so worth it. There is no "warm & fuzzy" feeling here, but staff are consummately professional and efficient. I took a city-view room this time, on the 33rd floor, just to have a different experience from looking out the other side of the hotel. It was just fine. The beds are so comfortable, the closet is large, the bathroom is top of the line.
