Had a little problem with dropped internet connections one morning, so the front desk person volunteered to remove all internet charges for my whole stay - unexpected but kind. This hotel makes you feel as comfortable as at home, even when you're far from home.

“Consistent Service and Pleasant Staff” Overall a very nice stay. The checkin staff were helpful and efficient. Room was the standard Embassy Suite, with ample storage and hanging space. Breakfast was freshly prepared, and the pool was very large. A very good business stay with no hassles.

“Won't Stay Again” This was a stylish hotel. But my room was dirty and that can pretty much ruin it all. When I arrived it was clear that there were rings and spots on the bathroom sink/countertop and it was evident that the desk had not been cleaned in a while. I had work to do so the idea of setting my paperwork on what appeared to be coffee stains was not appealing. When the manager came to check on this and clean it, he first indicated that nothing needed to be cleaned, but he would try. He said the spots were hard water, old stains, etc. Whatever... miraculously they all came off when he sprayed the surfaces with cleaner and wiped. The next day, it seemed that the housekeeper was not too attentive to her duties. There was no attention to detail. Also the robe hanging in the bathroom was worn enough that I did not want to put it on. The best thing about the place was the restaurant attached to the hotel. Now that was good. But it's more important for me to feel like I'm in a really clean room, so I wouldn't choose to stay here again.

“Nice public spaces, meh rooms” We stayed 2 nights here in April. We traveled with extended family, so I was able to see a couple of different rooms. All struck me the same way--frumpy, tired, kinda cheap looking, poor use of space. They reminded me of the rooms in the old historic hotels I used to visit as a kid. That said, the bathrooms are all large and gorgeous. It is quite a disconnect. The concierge service which gives you access to a large room serving breakfast-snacks-hors d'oeuvres is fantastic. I also found the service throughout the hotel to be good--helpful and pleasant. The lobby of the hotel is a converted 1908 bank (the rest is a sky scraper built off of it). It is well done and the public spaces of the hotel are all pretty neat. The location is terrific. That area of town does have a lot of street traffic and noise. We were on the 8th floor and still had some noise. It didn't bother us--we like a bit of noise in a city--but if you need a really quiet sleep you would be advised to go higher up. I would be willing to stay here again, but for my next visit to Philly (in 2 weeks) I have decided to try the Four Seasons. They had a report on the Bedbug Registry, which is why I tried the Ritz-Carlton this time, but I am going to take my chances. As I recall, the rooms there are a bit nicer.

“Labor Day Weekend Trip” Stayed here over Labor Day weekend and it was fantastic! Right in the financial district, walking distance to ferry plaza farmer's market (20 mins), union square (15 mins), Cobb's comedy club (25 mins) and Chinatown (30 mins). The rooms are standard courtyard type, nothing special, although I did have a great city view. They have a bar right on-site which seemed nice. They have a business center where you can print your boarding passes for free and an indoor pool and whirlpool (open until 11) If you are here during the weekend, go check out Ferry Plaza Farmer's market. We went at 8am on saturday and we had zero crowds. The fruit samples there will melt in your mouth, especially the pluots! From the Market you can walk to Fisherman's Wharf area, which sucks, but is close to the ferry you take to Alcatraz. Alcatraz is one of the most interesting places I've ever been, and if you don't believe me go check out the other reviews. We bought our tickets 2 weeks in advance and were able to get any time we wanted. Go eat at Osha Thai right down the street. Great atmosphere, reasonable price, and the lemongrass chicken will blow your mind. ============= AIRPORT INFO ======================== You can figure this out on google maps using public transit, but if you are flying in and out of Oakland you can get to and from this hotel in about 30-40 mins for really cheap. Take the airbart shuttle from OAK to the Coliseum ($3) and then take the Bart train ($7ish) to the montogomery street stop. The hotel is about 2-3 blocks from there. Just take the bart back to the coliseum and the airbart will pick you up from there once you are heading home. SFO you won't need to take a shuttle, you can just buy a bart ticket straight to the montgomery stop.

“Still one of my favorites” Having stayed at the Hyatt Regency Century Plaza when it was a Westin, I was looking forward to returning again for business this month. It did not disappoint - although there is some wear and tear to the property, it continues to be an excellent choice for the area. It is very conveniently located and the staff is very professional. It is also wonderful to have a Starbucks on the property. I do agree with other reviewers that the bathroom is on the dark side (which you'd think they would notice in LA of all places) - it made getting ready for our full schedule of dinners and meetings a bit difficult. I would definitely stay at the Hyatt again but recommend that, due to the intense hotel competition in the area, that hotel management fund some upgrade to what is a great property.

“Perfectly nice and reasonably priced” We stayed for one night for the Bulls vs. Pacers playoffs. I was a little nervous after reading the reviews, but the hotel was perfectly fine. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was nice, and there was an extra sink and vanity in the bedroom, which allowed my husband and I to both be getting ready at the same time. I love having the extra sitting room with another TV. I had read complaints about the rooms being too hot at night, but ours was quite comfortable and there was an overhead fan. I had also read complaints about noise, but we were on the 7th floor and we didn't hear a thing from outside or from the inside of the hotel. The manager's reception and breakfast are always a pleasant touch. There's a really nice fitness center that's open 24 hours. The location is great, in the middle of downtown with lots of shopping and eating options steps away, and easy walking distance to Conseco field. Only a few small negatives - the rooms show a little bit of wear and tear in areas, the indoor pool area wasn't great, the pedestrian entrance is kind of strange, and there's a $20 parking fee (which actually isn't that bad for the area). But for $120/night on the weekend, we were really pleased with our stay.

“A Wonderful Find in The Heart of Downtown Charlotte” This was my first experience with the Hyatt House concept, and I liked what I found. Service was excellent, and the property has a new, modern feel to it. The rooms are comfortable and well appointed. The one thing that keeps me from giving this property an excellent rating is the parking situation. There is on-site valet parking, but all other parking is across the street in city lots. And, the drop-off or check-in location for this Hyatt House is virtually non-existent. In other words, the arrival and parking situation is confusing and not at all customer friendly. The location is great for doing business in downtwon Charlotte, and for walking to many fine restaurants. Will most likely return here when doing business in Charlotte.

“Beautiful people -- efficient and greatly located. Expensive!” Just what you'd expect from a W - modern sleek rooms (not huge though). Very hip lobby bar (and super expensive, but who cares when in NY?) It's worth it just to watch the cool people lounging. Great location, can get to everything NY has to offer. Concierge staff the best! Great diner around the corner (exit hotel, go right, to corner, go right 1/2 block) for breakfast.

“Very Good Older Hotel near Union Square” My family of 3 stayed at this hotel this past week. I have stayed at Kimpton Hotels in the past and they have been very nice places with friendly and helpful staff. They are usually pricier than I typically like to spend but when I find a good online deal, I have been very pleased. The hotel was in a good location just a short block from Union Square although fairly close to the dicier elements of the Tenderloin with an equally short walk in the opposite direction. The hotel is older but very clean and quite comfortable. The staff was very friendly to my 2 year old son, although when I asked the front desk and the hotel doormen about less expensive parking options for our rental car, they were very coy about letting me know that the lot just a few doors down from the property had indoor parking for much cheaper than the hotel valet (less than 1/2 the price from Sun through Weds.). The hotel has a relationship with Postrio (Wolfgang Puck's faded entree into the SF restaurant scene in the 1990s) for breakfast, but there is a decent place (Honey, Honey) less than a block away which was much better and far less expensive. The hotel provides a Happy Hour/wine tasting in the comfortable lobby, although we did not partake this time. Computers are also located in this common room but they are not free; however, joining Kimpton In Touch benefit program gets you free WiFi throughout the hotel. The room we stayed on faced Post St but was pretty quiet. We stayed in a room with 2 comfortable beds with adequate room to put a pack and play for our young son. The beds were comfortable and clean. We had no complaints about the bathroom either. For public transportation, there is a bus which runs downtown on Post Street with a stop just up the street within less than one block, the Powell Street Cable Car is just 1 block away and for BART and MUNI (subway) an easy downhill walk to Market St. All-in-all a very nice place to stay in SF.

“Cute rooms, but service needs work” After a super-friendly check-in (I wish I had the clerk's name, since she was the only good one we encountered) we were quite pleased with the room. The design is inspired and we really liked the separate sitting area with the sectional couch, as well as the nice little work desk. The mini-fridge and sink area were also a big plus (although our fridge didn't cool sodas much beyond room temperature even overnight). The downside here was the "Gallery Host" concept in which the front desk clerks are also responsible for getting drinks and preparing snacks and hot food 24/7. In theory this is great -- we were delighted that we'd be able to get meals and snacks in the evening, right at the hotel. But the front desk people seemed really to dislike this part of their job and, in our stay, treated it as a nuisance and a bother. Hyatt Place has a great free continental breakfast set out buffet-style (as well as hot items for purchase). But, again, its success is dependent on staff. On our two mornings there the front desk clerk was deep in conversation with the shuttle driver before, during, and after breakfast, not refilling items in the breakfast area, clearing plates, or cleaning up spilled food from previous guests. Another morning a second clerk was shouting across the lobby to her colleague about some sort of custody or childcare problem. On check-out, a woman I assume was the manager (she wasn't wearing the sweater-set uniform of the other clerks) gave us a really hard time about a food item on the bill that we asked to have removed (it wasn't ours). Considering the many other items on the bill, most more expensive, that we weren't disputing, I was surprised at her response: she insisted mistakes were "impossible" because of their automated system. Our overall bill was several hundred dollars, so why she wanted to go five rounds about a $4 charge was beyond me. Again, we really liked the rooms and the breakfast, as well as the WiFi and the fitness room, but this was a pretty lame staff all around, with the exception of our young check-in clerk and a friendly airport shuttle driver. I'm not sure if we would stay here again or not, but I hope the management can get up to speed and get everyone on-board with the Hyatt Place "concept," which is indeed super and creative.

“Mediocre customer service, great location” The hotel is in a fantastic location in Boston, at the South West cornert of Boston Commons, and walking distance to Chinatown and even places like Fenway Park. Boston's a small city, so walking almost anywhere is possible. The building also houses a couple of restaurants. We tried Finale, which is an incredible dessert place. At first, the prices seemed a little high for dessert, but they were worth every cent. I wanted to go back every night. Apart from that, the hotel was a bit of a disappointment. We had problems with check-in, parking, room service and the lobby restaurant. At check-in, they said no rooms despite a reservation, and the manager had to be called. With parking, no valets were available, so we had to find a garage on our own near the hotel. For room service, they forgot a few items and delivered well past the promised time, and the lobby restaurant service was bad - a lack of waiters, and drinks took half an hour to arrive. The room was small and very subdued looking. Very clean and tidy, though. I've seen better furnishings in comfort inns. The in-room internet service didn't work and we were still charged for it. The view was into other people's hotel rooms, a few feet away.

“Nice Hotel in a Great Location” The staff at the Dana is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are trendy with a minimalist style, although we were not fans of the exposed concrete. The bathroom is large, with a great shower and nice bath amenities. The lighting is romantic, so if you enjoy reading at night, be aware you might need a booklight. We found the TV to be a bother, as it is very slow to change channels. We had breakfast in the restaurant one morning and found the food and service excellent. We enjoyed the hotel, but prefer any of the Chicago Kimptons for our frequent stays. Do check out the Farmhouse Tavern on Chicago Avenue - we had a great dinner there. We also enjoyed Pizzeria Via Stato, a block south on State, and the Purple Pig on Michigan Avenue was great at lunch.

“Great stay and would come back again” Stayed on the front and back end of a business trip. Great location off of Highway 805. The hotel is about 12 miles north of downtown San Diego. Large King size room with dresser, desk, flat screen tv and free wifi. Room was clean and had rooms on the second floor which were quiet. Comp. hot breakfast in the morning which consist of eggs, bread, breakfast meat, cereal, juice, fruit, coffee, milk, yogurt. Outdoor swimming pool, fitness center and business center (took a peek but did not use) Free parking but lot does get full around dinner time as the hotel shares a lot with a restaurant (Chili's). Numerous eating locations/retail strip mall east down Mira Mesa Blvd. All are within a 5-10 minute drive.

“Luxury with your pets” This is the first time I've ever taken my beloved dogs to a hotel and it was as much fun as I thought it would be based on the Palomar's website. When we arrived, we had great little dog beds. The staff brought bottled water, dog bowls, and dog treats. And, we got to let our dogs go downstairs with us to wine hour, which was much fun for a rainy night. We couldn't have loved the location more with shopping right across the street as well as a movie theatre. It was about a $10 cab ride into downtown, which was nice since it was raining (p.s. I loved Dish for dinner). And, everyone on the staff was very friendly. Hooray for Hotel Palomar for knocking it out of the park! I'm going to knock off one star simply because the rooms were super small compared to other Palomar properties I've visited. But, I wish there was a half a button because it wasn't that big of a deal.

“I would not stay here again!” Checked in late after stressful drive over pass. Check-in gal was so very nice and that was the only plus I can attest to. Elevator to room was dirty, and was dirty at 10 next morning when I left...in that amount of time I would think someone would have noticed how yucky it was and cleaned it. When I got to room it was very warm, I adjusted temperature to cool down, quickly prepared for bed as it was late and noticed toilet seat was up and toilet paper wasn't folded like it usually is in a freshly cleaned bathroom. Everything looked clean enough, so I didn't worry a lot about it, until next morning when I got in shower and there were half empty shampoo and conditioner bottles still in shower! That just struck me as really gross! Half way through night woke up to room that was possibly 90 degrees, tried to adjust temp again, open windows, hold curtains open to get air, anything to cool down room...finally after several attempts to hold curtains back with chair, I realized there was a cooler under window (it was 2 in the morning and I got in very late, so I admit I wasn't too observant!). I turned AC on lowest temp possible and it cooled room down. I had cold air blowing from one direction and hot air blowing out of an overhead vent on other side of room and it balanced out to comfy temperature, but still last thing one wants to deal with at 2 a.m. with flight the following morning. I couldn't wait to get out of there. One thing to note: hotel approximately 20 miles to airport. Also, hotel description said rooms were newly remodeled...that is not the case. As I said earlier, air system is antiquated, carpet was all stretched out and lumpy, micro was on some sort of movable cabinet that was inches from the wall and awkwardly placed at best, there was a little closet with strange shuttered accordian door that was old and off the tracks, just funky to say the least. I will say the bed was comfy and the sheets were clean and well fitted; also lots of pillows. Besides the suspicious bathroom situation, the room seemed clean. I would not stay here again.

“Great choice for New York City” We stayed as a couple for 1 night in January on the 17th Floor. This is a great little hotel, nothing too flash but everything is as it should be. Pros: Excellent location in soho with easy access to the metro and local bars and restaurants Nice spacious and clean rooms with really comfortable beds Very friendly staff Excellent value for NYC Cons: None!

“Would stay again!” Check in was fast & friendly, room was clean with fun decor and a desk with enough space to get some work done. The bathroom was very clean (although a bit tight) but at least there was counter space to set toiletries, toothbrush and hair brush. This is a historical/old building so spaces are bit smaller but it's completely modern and has great charm. The staff is excellent and they provided really nice extra touches. My hint would be to sign up (free) as a Kimpton member to get those little extra goodies they offer.

“L.A. Comes to Austin...Ideal for Hip Young Travelers” Excellent Service- when I asked for the best route to my SoCo destination, the staff member went online and printed out a map and directions. The decor is more like a nightclub with a dark charcoal grey as the primary color in the lobby and the guest rooms. Grey is punched up with bright accents everywhere including the overhead lights in the hallways which made me think of airbrushing. The room had dark grey walls, platform beds, a walll unit of a built in desk and a covering over the ac unit which reminded me of old style motel units. The beds were backed up by a divider wall between bed and bathroom. The beds were comfortable, the pillows a bit lumpy since they were that shredded styrofoam feel. My only issues with the place were a mini refrigerator that was so noisy we ended up unplugging it and the view from our room was two big trash dumpsters on a paved drive and directly below our window as a big construction scene...concrete mixer, construction dumpster and building materials. We were gone during the day when construction was underway (even on the weekend) so it really wasn't a problem but it certainly was ugly. To park in the free lot down the street you had to walk past a bar wing under construction and sealed off with yellow caution tape. The elevator interiors were hung with grey padding like movers use to protect walls, but these were a design element.!???? The "breakfast" was somewhere between convenience store and fast food ambiance. Although my reservation was to include complimentary breakfast, I was a bit surprised to learn at checkin that it was only for one and I was given a plastic card valued at $7 for each morning of my stay (and a $5 bar card). I was also told there was a chef on weekends who prepared omelets...turned out the "chef" heated up an english muffin and a premade triangle of scrambled egg in a microwave. The experience was more odd than unpleasant. We rested well, the staff was excellent, the location was great and the price was good. This place seemed a pretty good fit for Austin since it was clearly aimed at a young, relaxed audience (Wired magazine in the rooms and a dog bowl set at the front entrance). Overall it was a good hotel in a great location and my only recommendation would be to know what you are getting.

“5 Stars for a great price - great hospitality, location, home away from home” I stayed at the Sofitel the 3 days before Thanksgiving in Nov 2011. From the moment we walked in to the time we left I felt like I was in as close to a 5 star hotel as possible - without actually paying for one. Unbelievable holiday decor - modern and orignal. Our first room did not have windows that opened, so all I did was ask and they put us in a room 2 floors up with "french doors" - which opened to the tiny balcony and was a very nice touch. Apparently all the rooms with 2 beds face the Beverly Center, but I didn't mind because everything else was so great! I think our first day there LA got about 5 hours of steady rain - and even with the doors shut, the water seeped in onto the carpet. I don't think LA in general is equipped for heavy rain so I considered it a fluke. Coming from Boston this is nothing. The bathrooms were very nice - lovely glass enclosure - rainmaker shower, L'Ocittane products, hairdryer (without having to ask). The Robe was so so comfy too! No fan though. I thought that was weird. The beds Crazy Comfortable! Feather beds and soft sheets were such a nice luxury away from home. The hallways were lovely. The Concierge / Valet so helpful. Complimentary umbrellas for the rain. The Restaurant Bar very appealing for both Dining and Drinks. The gym was fully equipped with machines and food/water! Le Spa is a "Must Do". We got a $25 off with our reservation which was a nice surprise. Very decadent. The pool is so-so compared to all the other ones in the area, no view and sun fades away by 1pm due to the Beverly Center blocking it. When we were there the pool was out of service, so the hotel allowed guests the use of the SLS pool which is supposed to be excellent! This location was perfect for me. Facing Beverly Center, 10 min walk to Robertson St and the Ivy, 25 minute walk to the Grove. Close to public transportation if necessary. 5 min walk to Hertz rent a car, 5 min walk to Melrose Ave. Across the street from the tour bus pick-up (Starline and others). We actually even walked home from the Comedy Store one night from the Sunset Strip! About 30min walk downhill. I really loved this European hotel, and the luxury it exuded. Normally I am not in the room a lot while traveling due to sightseeing, plans etc - but here I didn't want to leave! We were supposed to get the "I love chocolate" package, but we never did. I was so impressed with their other services, hospitality and room service though that I forgot about it until after I left. They allowed us late check out which we really appreciated. Overall I would absolutely stay here again - highly recommended for just about anyone. I cannot compare to the Four Seasons or the Peninsula, but I will say I felt like a VIP the entire time I was here.

“Was given a choice, not sure I made the right one...” My new employer brought me down for business and I was given a choice of 3 hotels in the area. I chose this one, but I'm starting to regret it. First of all, despite my room being prepaid, they did an additional authorization on my card, and a third card. This has greatly inconvenienced me, and even though the girl looking into it was very nice at the front desk, she never got back to me to let me know if that was resolved. Then, for two days straight I got no replacement coffee in my room, despite calling the first day and letting them know. Finally today I called again and it was brought to me. Tonight, because my room has a kitchen, I bought a bottle of wine. I called down to get a wine opener, and was informed they had "one", but the guy never brought it back". A hotel has ONE wine opener? Really? The dirty coffee mug in the cupboard was just icing on a bad, stale cake. I'm here for 9 days, and come back regularly. You can bet I will reconsider my decision next time. Very disappointed.

“No longer as it used to be” Just completed my fourth stay at this hotel and they have changed over the past 6 months. This hotel has become all about taking your money and giving as little as possible in return. As a Hilton Silver Elite member I maintain a profile of room preferences and these are generally respected by hotels, unless of course the hotel is fully booked. Hilton Times Square doesn't care about this: You ask for a high floor, they'll give you a low floor; you ask for a room far from the elevator, they'll put you next to the elevator shaft and so on. Most hotels in the world will leave a complimentary bottle of water in the room for its elite members, give free Wifi access or breakfast, not this hotel -- no perks whatsoever. In addition, on site services are expensive: WiFi they charge $14 per device (computer and Ipad, that's $28), breakfast is $27 for a poor buffet. Finally, the fire alarm went off at 10:30 PM and the communication from staff was very poor. The PA system did not function well and all announcements were cut short, very poor performance.

“Mucho lujo y Pague un exclente precio” Excelente Hotel muy amables, llegamos yo y mi familia con niños, y ya nos esperaban, el hotel tiene mucho lujo, la habitacion casi perfecta solo comentar que ya le estan pegando los años, pedi servicio al cuarto para cenar dos noches, la cena fue excelente, el personal , excelente desayuno , camas muy comodas muy amable y lo mejor que logre un excelente precio, ubicaion perfecta caminas al Galeria y muchas tiendas alrededor, jabon cremas shampoo , wow...

“Winter Classic” I stayed at this hotel the night before the Winter Classic and barely got any sleep. I am somewhat of a light sleeper and generally sleep through most noises, but I had much difficulty enjoying a restful night sleep at this hotel. There are a couple of things that contributed to my lack of sleep. First of all the convention center loading dock was directly across the street from my room and was very loud with trucks backing into the dock all night. I would constantly be woken up by the beeping sound that trucks make as they are backing up. Secondly, the window heat & ac unit was very noisy and allowed the sound of the traffic down below as well as the trucks in the convention center loading dock in very clearly. I hoped for better from this hotel, but was disappointed I was unable to sleep well here. If I had a room higher up and not directly across the street from the convention center loading dock it might have been a different story. However, the window heat & ac unit was still about as noisy as they get and would have probably have woken me up as well.

“Have to agree with others........” The hotel is in a great spot has a great look to it the lobby and the Ruby Room are very nice. The room is decorated very modern styles with a nice flair about them. Typical Kimpton Hotel which is why we choose to stay there. But the room is very small 2 adults and we felt cramped. With the wife ironing and me showering and getting ready was a challenge. The shower water pressure is poor and avoid the $13.00 each all you can eat breakfast. The hot food was dry and the bagels and cereal are just not worth it. Parking was $32.00 a day which is typical for a downtown hotel, but I found cheaper parking myself and walking one short block. Ruby room at night is very nice. Nice Martini specials. But when all is done and said we have stayed at better rooms for this price it was not worth it.

“Fantastic bargain” What a pleasant surprise. Never stayed at a Drury before, but it was fantastic - great rooms, very clean. Internet availability in the lobby. Free soda fountain all day. Big breakfast, free alcoholic beverages each evening with pizza, nachos, baked potatoes, salad - amazing bargain!!!

“An absolute pleasure to stay here” My husband and I were in LA for a long weekend. I had never been to LA, and a friend recommended this hotel. It is located in Westwood, right near the UCLA campus. Westwood is a pretty quiet residential neighborhood, with Westwood Village being just a 5 minute walk away. Pros: 1 - Beautiful hotel; modern, clean look; very LA! 2 - Spacious suites 3 - Excellent service all around (front desk, conceirge, housekeeping, valet) 4 - Beautiful poolside dining 5 - Bliss Spa on 2nd floor 6 - Great restaurants within walking distance Cons: 1 - Bathrooms have little counter space and no storage space. 2 - Could get loud if there is a party going on at the bar 3 - Tiny on-site gym 4 - Expensive ( I didn't comparison shop to other hotels in LA, but $35 a night for parking seems like a lot) I would definitely stay there again and recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the LA area.

“Close to the airport and light rail” I have stayed at the Radisson a few times in the last five years, for both business and pleasure. With the construction of the light rail, staying near the airport is a cheaper and more convenient way to spend the night when attending a Seahawks or Mariners game. The hotel is located across the street from the airport...I mean literally across the street! The hotel does provide a shuttle, but I saw a number of pilots and flight attendants walking to work from the hotel. The hotel is also about 4 blocks from the Airport Light Rail station, which is the cheapest and sometimes fastest way to get to downtown Seattle. The staff has always been friendly and helpful when I have stayed there. A few times they have only had one person working at the front desk, and I have had to wait in line for five minutes or so to check in. The rooms at the Radisson are comfortable and well furnished. Some of the furnishings are a bit dated, but does that really matter? The rooms are equipped with large flat screen TVs, a desk and chair, sitting chair as well as a luggage table/rack. The bathroom has granite counter tops, and an adjustable "butterfly" shower head. There are a number of eating establishments within walking distance from the hotel...Subway, Mango (Thai), Jack-in-the-Box, Denny's, Sharp's Roaster, Gregory's Bar and Grill, Spencer's (at the Hilton), and a Seattle icon, 13 Coins (24 hour dining) right next door. Overall, I give the Radisson a "thumbs up". I will be back .

“Perfect for business” I stay here frequently. It took the staff several visits before they started to recognize me as a regular, but now they help make this a great stay. Very strong value, not strong on a amenities.

“Great hotel” We have stayed at the Drury on the Riverwalk several times. It is a beautiful hotel, and a good value for its location. Our only suggestion is that the staff could be somewhat more gracious and welcoming.

“Elegant hotel” Hotel is beautiful and large and is a few blocks from Michigan Avenue. Concierge level room was very spacious, clean, and comfortable. Concierge lounge was usually too crowded and seating was at a premium. Concierge personnel in the lounge were rarely around when you needed them to ask a question. However, the concierge in the lobby was excellent and offered numerous wonderful restaurant choices.

“fantastic hotel and excellent service” Stayed to attend a conference being held at the hotel. Arrival experience was great. Valet's were quick to assis as soon as I pulled up to the driveway. You have the option of doing the self serve check-in, but I opted for the face-face interaction with an agent. Was given an option of a King bed with a street view, or a dbl/dbl with a view of the pool. Chose the view as I was only there for a couple of nights. Room service as ok, but the food andservice at the restaurant for breakfast was better than expected. Large outdoor pool and with plenty of lounge chairs, Front desk was very flexible with extending my checkout so that I can relax in the outdoor pool before I left. Would have been a 5 star review if it wasn't for the very long wait to have my car brought up. There was an event that had just finished and there was a long queue at the driveway. There weren`t enough valets on duty at that time, and there were customers who requested their cars brought up after I gave my ticket to the booth, who for some reason were getting their cars brought up before mine. I suggest calling for your car well ahead of time (30 minutes) to avoid this, or doing self parking. Shopping mall across the street, and Starbucks in the lobby. Plenty of staff in the lobby offering assistance with luggage, directions, etc... Will stay here again when in LA.

“Hotel d'alta classe nel centro di Washington D.C.” Ottimo hotel a 4 stelle nel centro di Washington D.C., stanze grandi e ottimo bagno. La posizione, vicino alla Casa Bianca e alla fermata da dove partono i pullman per girare la città con la formula sali e scendi. La qualità si vede tutta della catena Marriott e c'è pure lo Starbucks all'interno dell'hotel...nella grandissima hall.

“Fantastic” Marriott Gold member - loved the concierge lounge views, atmosphere and service. Front desk clerk was great at check-in and check-out. Great location, very pleasant, spacious room with incredible view ofr river and beautiful lobby. Great fitness center. Only complaint was overly priced drinks at Nico.

“Trying hard to be hip (by DC standards), and mostly succeeding” I stayed at the W four nights with a group of colleagues in DC on business. Since I used to live in DC, I was elected to choose the hotel, and sold this one to the rest of the group based on its fabulous location literally across the street from the White House and fantastic rooftop bar. While it may have been a bit too "hip" of a hotel for some business purposes (the heavy bass of the loud music played in the lobby in the evenings was a bit jarring as my colleagues were checking in), the rooms were swanky enough to make up for it. Luckily, my colleagues found it entertaining rather than off-putting, but just know what you're getting into. As mentioned, the rooms were fantastic, with luxurious beds and a great shower. Of note is that one "wall" of the shower is a frosted glass panel that is partially see-through into the bedroom, so I wouldn't recommend staying here if you're planning to share a room with someone you're less than fully comfortable with! Also appreciated was an iPod dock and extra storage space/areas to put luggage. I was worried about noise given the previously-mentioned heavy thumping of bass in the lobby, but on the fifth floor I couldn't hear any of either the lobby music nor the rooftop lounge. The same was not true for one morning when there were not one but two groups protesting/picketing on the street below my room and I could hear their voices with the windows closed. I was given a room "with a view" although this was really just a typical DC street view. Again, the location is great - steps from the White House and a few minutes' walk to the Mall and the plethora of museums and views it has to offer. There are a range of restaurants nearby - check out Old Ebbitt Grill just the next block up 15th for a "historic" DC restaurant, and plenty of Starbucks and CVSes in the surrounding blocks to keep you powered through your day. One tip on internet use: Wifi is not free in the room, but you can get two hours of free wifi in the "lounge" in the lobby. While this is a nice enough place to hang out, and I did on several occasions, a couple times I really just wanted to lie in bed and surf the internet. I found it worked to go downstairs, log on, then keep my laptop open and logged on while carrying it back up to my room - voila, no extra charges on my bill, although I of course cannot guarantee this will work for everyone.

“Good Location!” We stayed at the Washington Plaza from 5/21-5/24. It was in a great location and that was a big draw for us. It was walking distance to about everywhere we wanted to go. The rate was very good for the location, we paid $89 a night. The room was average size and it was clean. The bed wasn't extremely comfy, kind of squeaky, but it wasn't super uncomfortable. The bathroom was also clean. The t.v. remote was broken or needed batteries, and I'm sure all we would have needed to do was call and get a new one, but we were too lazy to do it! We weren't there to watch t.v. anyway as we were out exploring almost all day and night. The parking is pretty steep (I think $28 night) but I checked and it's about the same at all the other hotels. I would recommend going to a coffee shop or somewhere else to use free Wifi as their rates were very high. We didn't eat at the restaurant but had a drink in the bar one evening. They have a nice pool area and we were going to have a drink at the pool bar, but ran out of time. Overall a decent place to stay for a quick visit.

“Great location but nothing special” We had a group of 8 in 4 rooms for 3 nights. Hotel is in a very convenient location close to Michigan Ave. and all shopping with tons of great restaurants close by. Check in experience was very slow due to front desk personnel- both shortage and lack of ability. Rooms were clean but the bathroom had the weirdest swinging door on it that was a big hassle if you were coming in or out. I have stayed at a lot of Embassy Suites but never seen a door like this one. The bed had been updated but was nothing but a standard Embassy Suites room. Breakfast was very good but the logistics of how they had this one laid out caused a lot of confusion by guests and traffic issues. Cocktail hour was good. We ate one night in the hotel restaurant since we were wiped out from a long day of shopping. Food was ok but would not eat there again. There are too many great places close by for the same money.

“Nice location” The lobby and room were very nice and clean. We stayed on business so I can't comment on the cost or value. It had a gym and pool which I did not use but enjoyed the free fruit in the bowls there. The rooms had thermostats which I like very much and a big screen new TV. The bed and linens were very nice and comfortable. If you don't like traffic noise request an inside room. We did and did not hear a thing. Evening turn down was often late or non-existent, I called one evening 3 times. This hotel has the annoying feature of charging for the Internet except for in the lobby. Even willing to pay for the Internet I had trouble connecting my iPad and the telephone help was not at all helpful.

“抜群のロケーション” グランドセントラル駅からほど近い位置にあり、徒歩でエンパイアステートビルディングやタイムズスクエアなど様々な観光場所に行けます。パークアベニュー沿いなのでマンハッタンの中心にも関わらず比較的静かでゆっくり休めます。豪華さや派手さはありませんが、スタッフは皆親切で対応がいいです。朝はコーヒー、紅茶がロビーラウンジで無料で提供されます。夜はワインが無料で楽しめます。おすすめです。

“Perfect” Greeted by very friendly and professional staff upon arrival,quickest check in ever,hotel is in a great loacation,close to Grand central station,Times Square,Rockefeller,3 block walk to Central Park. The rooms are of nice size and lovely plush clean bathrooms,one of the niceset rooms we have stayed in New York,the view was of office buildings and was the only negative i have of my experience,but we spent all day marching around Manhattan so we were not too disapointed. We only went in the bar to have a drink so i cant review the restaurant,but the whole bar area had a lovely french feel to it and was modern,i did find the prices a bit steep but this is New York. The concierge was very helpfull,waiting at the front desk only too happy to help,we definately recomend this hotel

“OK Hotel- needs updating” During a reunion I stayed here. The desk personnel were super. The people in the restaurant were very accomodating. There is both self and valet parking. The hotel is fairly hard to get to from the south unless you are familiar with Austin.. We did not have our room cleaned one day due to the maid coming at 4:30 when it was very inconvenient; but she came early the next day. The rooms need updating - peeling walpaper, old TVs but I enjoyed our stay

“As expected.” The Dallas Grand Hyatt is about what I expected from a large city Hyatt. I did not find any of the negativity expressed in other reviews (kids, noise etc.). The food is expensive, as is food in all major hotels in major cities. Rooms were clean, staff friendly and beds very comfortable. Kennedy Book Repository museum walkable and train station very close. Was there for a meeting and the hotel proved a nice venue.

“Very good for the money in NYC” I stayed in the Holiday Inn Express last week and was nicely surprised.. It is exactly what it is supposed to be..clean,no frills, good location, and nicely furnished with a decent bed. I was impressed that they didn't gauge people like other places in the area did due to Hurricane Sandy. Extra bonus points for that..Plus they had complimentary computers and printer in the lobby which was nice. Did I mention how nice the staff at the front desk was,... Very good value in NYC.

“Big corporate hotel...good location but otherwise so-so” I stayed at this Marriott property for a conference. It was a mixed experience. The main positive is the excellent location in the heart of downtown Philadelphia; numerous restaurants and bars are within walking distance. Taxi trip to the Philadelphia International Airport is about 15 minutes; $30. There is also a shuttle for $10 (not recommended unless you are okay with multiple stops around the city). I did not have a good experience with the front desk service. First of all, the process was slow, and the desk seemed unprepared to handle a large volume of people coming -- strange for a large hotel. As a Marriott Platinum member, I was also surprised when my request for a high floor was ignored, even though I had booked my reservation two months in advance. When I checked in, I was assigned to a low floor, interior room with a view of a massive heating/cooling unit. I hadn't planned to spend a lot of time in the room, so it was largely moot, but it was annoying on principle. When I asked about this snafu, I was told that the hotel had run out King rooms on high floors, so this was the best they could do. The manager was apologetic but the experience was really inconsistent with what Marriott claims to strive for with respect to their frequent business customers. I didn't make too big deal of it, but was even more surprised that no attempt was made to offer a different room, or maybe even a free drink, or some complimentary points...nothing! Otherwise, this property strikes me as the ultimate large, corporate hotel. It is reasonably clean but showing wear in spots; the rooms are rather bland; it is generally an impersonal experience overall. If returning to Philadelphia and needing to stay downtown, I would probably seek a different hotel. I was not impressed with this place.

“vieil hôtel dans un un bon emplacement” La situation de l'hôtel est très bonne car à proximité de tous les magasins et à 7 minutes à pieds de la rue principale (Market street) avec ses trams, bus et centre commercial. En face de l'hôtel, vous avec le CLIFT HOTEL, hôtel très branché et design. bar et réception à visiter. Ca vaut le détour. Le personnel à la réception est agréable. Les chambres sont très rustiques et chargées, mais bon, ça ne m 'a pas dérangé plus que ça. L'hôtel est lui aussi assez ancien et les photos sur certains sites sont trompeuses, voir retouchées. Les chambres ont encore des clés à l'ancienne, c'est dire :) mais le tout est bien entretenu et propre. La chambre possède un écran plat, un frigo très ancien, un réveil très ancien et un coffre très ancien aussi. WIFI gratuit. Pas de clim (il faut dire qu'on en a rarement besoin ici). Demander une chambre vers l'arrière, elle sera sombre certes, mais calme car il y a bcp de trafic sur la rue principale et aux Etats Unis, on ne coupe pas les sireines d'ambulance, police et pompiers pendant la nuit donc vous me comprendrez :) Le dernier soir malheureusement j'ai trouvé un cafard dans la chambre ... Personnellement j'ai payé moins de 90 euros la nuit et je n'aurai pas donné plus. A certaines périodes ou les weekends, ils ont les chambres à près de 200 USD la nuit, ca ne les vaut pas du tout. San Francisco est la ville californienne la plus chère pour les hôtels et préférée des touristes, donc ça reste raisonnable. C'est aussi la ville avec le plus de clochards, il y en a bcp. Tard le soir, je recommande de ne prendre que les rues principales ou même un taxi car pas bien fréquenté. Mon coup de coeur de cette fois-ci: DOLORES PARK à proximité de Castro: magnifique. il faut monter dans la partie supérieure et il y a une super vue de SF. Petit conseil pour ceux qui viennent pour la première fois à San Francisco: le soir (été comme hiver) il fait assez froid et bcp bcp bcp de vent. Prévoyez donc une veste épaisse et un pull, croyez-moi !

“Quaint hotel, price was right” We booked this hotel through hotwire. We got an AMAZING rate, but the room we had was quite small. Which, worked out just fine because we were on the tail end of a week long east coast trip, and after all the sightseeing every day, just zonked out. The bathrooms, however, were almost "paris-sized" SO TINY. Both of us could not be in the bathroom at the same time. Service was great, especially parking services. We were in and out quite a bit, and the staff never huffed once when we asked for our rental car- a bulky ford expedition. All in all, this hotel was very nice for the price, especially being in georgetown. ALSO- one of the only places with a pool, which was nice for the balmy june afternoons we spent walking around sweating. :)

“This used to be a great hotel - but...” it has really gone downhill and takes advantage of travelers with extremely high prices. I used to always stay here. I have not traveled to LA in a few years, and stayed here on an overnight before a flight. The rooms have not been modernized (with the exception of the beds. I was on the club floor, and at the bar there I heard someone order a gin and tonic -- and it was $11.00 - usually hotel club floors don't gouge their clients. I have to believe there are better hotels around here.

“Great suprise through Hotwire!” My family stayed at the Crowne Plaza Airport for one night before our flight out of Phoenix to Atlanta. I was amazed at the value we received from our $50 Hotwire purchase! A quiet, extremely comfortable room on the 10th floor with a terrific view of the south mountains of Phoenix and the busy airport area. Nice quiet hotel, very attentive and friendly staff at every turn, and we left our car in the hotel garage during our week-long trip for $7 per night, a dollar cheaper than the OPEN parking at the Phoenix airport! Great hotel! Thank you Crowne Plaza Phoenix and we'll definately recommend to our friends.

“Overpriced compared to others” The HI is really overpriced. The hotel made a quite run-down impression. Even though having been on the priority club level, the room wasn't really great. We had a stunning view onto the.... air-condition system, on the roof in front of our room there were lots of cigarettes which could also explain the strange smell of smoke in our room as well as on the hallways. Smoking seems to be a real problem. The TV was extremely old, not really what one can expect for the quite pricey stay. I would prefer other hotels nearby in the future as i.e. the Sheraton, where I have stayed recently.

“An almost completely delightful experience” I was in DC for several days vacation, following a work conference in the area, and had a truly wonderful time at Hotel Rouge. In summary: My room was spacious (the sheer square footage was as much as I've had in suites in other hotels), the Bar Rouge a valued perk, and the location near DuPont Circle ideal. The rooms are quirky, but pleasant. The bathroom showed some wear and tear, but still did the job. The AC worked well - important in summertime DC. My only problem with the L shaped room I had was that the television was not conveniently placed to watch from the bed. Although there was a very nice and comfortable seating area near the TV, we couldn't comfortably watch a movie from bed. It's a very minor point. Bar Rouge has good courtesy coffee in the morning, and a good evening food and drink menu. The breakfast may be wonderful too - I don't know. Hotel Rouge is a few blocks from the hub of Dupont circle, which I liked - a little bit of a walk back and forth was welcome. There are quite a few decent restaurants in area of the Circle, and several VERY good ones. It was a longer haul to museums and monuments, and in the heat we relied more on cabs than our feet for the longer trek. A last word: My initial impression of Hotel Rouge was very poor because of the incredibly rude front desk person who greeted us. He gave the impression that he was doing us a favor by talking with us at all, and our exchange was in every way inhospitable. In fact he was so unpleasant we half expected him to tell us there was no room for us at all. But beyond that one person, everyone else was absolutely welcoming and charming. Every time we came in or left we had a pleasant smile or word from every person on staff.

“Loved it!” I was in San Diego for 6 days to attend a conference. The convention centre was right across the street from the hotel which made it extremely convenient. Hotel staff were friendly & helpful. The room I had was comfortable with a king-size bed and adequate room & bathroom amenities. Only negative point is the train that runs by a couple of times at night- for some strange reason the driver sounds the horn loudly and that was very irritating. The hotel's location is perfect! I enjoyed exploring the Gaslamp Quarter and especially enjoyed the Horton Plaza Shopping Mall several blocks up the street from the hotel. Take a leisurely stroll along the MLK pathway right outside the hotel towards Embarcadero Marina Park North, Seaport Village, the USS Midway Aircraft Carrier Museum and the pier along North Harbor Drive. I could have walked on forever in that gorgeous weather!

“Great Hotel” This was my first stay at an Omni Hotel, and I was really blown away. The service was outstanding, and the property was tremendous. The room was very large with a comfortable bed loaded with pillows. The bathroom was large as well, with a full compliment of luxury amenities. The location is excellent, close to the convention center, the water, and the Gaslamp District. There is a nice restaurant on site, but there are better ones nearby, such as Acqua Al 2 (pronounced acqua al due) for great Italian food. If you’re looking for luxurious accommodations in San Diego with a great location, the Omni will exceed your expectations.

“No frills, good service, good value” The Crowne Plaza met my expectations for a hotel in this class. The customer service was outstanding (Merle at the front desk stood out), and the price was great. The room was nothing special, though it had a flat-screen TV. The bathroom, as other reviewers stated, was pretty small, though big enough for me (and I'm an urbanite used to small bathrooms, too). The best thing about the hotel was the parking situation. I was very happy to be able to park myself in a garage (located on the lower floors of the hotel) and get in and out easily, without the delays (and tips!) of valet service. The restaurant is not good and very overpriced--skip it. Overall, I'd stay here again if I can't find a room Uptown, which is where I prefer to stay.

“Unique, wonderful and well located” The James offers many strong points making it an excellent choice for a centrally located hotel. As for location, its right at the intersection of Ontario and Rush - very close to great bars/restaurants and two short blocks off Michigan Ave. While some nice properties are right on Michigan Ave,, I think its preferrable to be close, but just off of it for diminished noise and traffic. The hotel itself has a unique, comtempory design, which carries from the lobby into the rooms. Style preferrence is a personal thing, but if you lean toward the less traditional, you'll enjoy the look of the James. I was fortunate to have an upgraded room, which landed me in a suite on the top floor. Not much of a view, but the room was very spacious, contained 2 couches, had 2 flat screen tvs, very comfortable king bed, well stocked bar, and a bathroom complete with Kiehl's products. Not bad! Service at the counter and door was prompt, professional and friendly. Maid service was well done and included turn down service. Another plus is the fitness center which rivals many stand alone gyms for equipment selection and quality. I only have two minor criticisms to offer. One, the hotel is an older building and there are a few worn spots in the common areas that should be touched up. Second, and this is very minor, there is not gift shop in the hotel, so if you need toiletries or a bottle of water, you'll need to go across the street. My recommending of the hotel is enhanced by the relative value it offers. Considering the location and amenities, I think its hard to beat, especially if you compare the cost of elite Chicago hotels such as the Park Hyatt, Peninsula, or Four Seasons. For a quick business trip or a fun weekend, the James should deliver what you need.
“Hampton in need of renovation” This property is in need of renovation. Furnishings seem very dated. No restaurants within walking distance.

“Good stay at the CP, but it could be better” Was on business in Denver and they booked several of us at the CP downtown. Overall my stay was fine, but I did expect more for the high rate we paid. It is conveniently located next to the 16th St. Pavillions Mall so there are lots of nice shops, restaurants and things to do nearby. The CP is an older but well maintained and updated property. The rooms are large enough, but not quite as big as new ones today. It was well appointed and updated. There is in-room coffee (that is not so good), large flat screen TV, in-room safe, but NO microwave, mini fridge or other amenities. Local calls are still .50 cents each (i am amazed that some hotels still charge for this) They do provide glasses and mugs as opposed to paper cups which is nice. The maid service was good and attentive. All of the staff were friendly. After a couple of encounters with the night concierge I felt he was trying to push my group to the places he recommended which was totally opposite of what we were asking for. (Think beer drinking young men directed to quiet high priced eateries when we were asking for a brewery/sports bar). They do not provide a complimentary breakfast, snacks or anything like that. They want you to eat at their restaurant, which is overpriced for what you get. Most guests ate at the many other choices on the 16th street Pavilion next door. One nice thing was they have "quiet floors" for business travelers during the week. These are kid-free quiet zones which was nice. The elevators are also room key controlled which makes the floors safer. They have a nice fitness room too. One important thing to note is that the entire downtown area is sadly covered up with homeless people sleeping in doorways. It made for an unpleasant situation. I'm surprised the businesses there don't do more as it surely has to impact their business. Also, the hotels recommended we travel in pairs at night for safety. While I never had any incident, this alone would make me not want to stay at any of the area hotels. Overall it was a nice place. Overpriced for what you get and a bit scary due to the homeless downtown. I will stay somewhere else next time.

“Nothing Short of Spectacular” Whenever we check in at the Grand, we take a deep breath because we know we are "home." The resort grounds and rooms are utterly amazingly out of this world. It's hard to fathom that a resort of this size has less than 300 rooms, suites, and villas because the Grand emphasizes detail, impeccable customer service, and nothing short of making one's stay a perfect 10. We love the idea that the hotel remembers our favorite room so every time we come down, they immediately put us in that room. We come to San Diego now just to stay at the Grand Del Mar! From the time we arrive and the time we depart, there isn't a minute that we don't feel pampered or treated like royalty. So many staff members recognize us and address us personally which is hard to find these days at many large impersonal hotels. But then, the Grand Del Mar doesn't fall under that category because it is in a truly 5 star category of its own. This 390 million resort is one of a kind -- over 30 types of different rocks and over 30 types of different wood. Once you have stayed here, I guarantee you that you will not want to leave. At least, that is how we feel each time we are here because we have found our "paradise on earth."

“Below Average Residence Inn” I frequently stay at Residence Inn properties across the country. This Residence Inn does not meet the standards of most of the other properties in this chain. My room was partially renovated to look like a typical updated Residence Inn room, but with close inspection the room was pretty shabby and dated. The breakfast was not well stocked, and they even ran out of forks one day (although one evening the dinner reception was quite nice as far as being well stocked). Some of the towels in my room smelled odd...almost like gasoline. My phone didn’t work upon check-in. The internet connection in my room was poor, making it impossible to compose lengthy email messages. The TV was frustrating as it was slow to respond after pressing the channel change button on the remote. There were no towels to be found around the pool area. The employees mostly lacked polish and finesse. My stay wasn’t awful, but it was nothing special.

“Loved it! Great staff with a family feel.” We stayed here our first two nights for Comic-Con (it was 100% booked for the remainder). Got an incredible rate on Expedia, and they did not mention it when checking in. Cons: * Parking is expensive ($26). But it's expensive everywhere in San Diego. * Slow elevator. Yes, singular. They're in the middle of an elevator upgrade -- much needed. * One computer in the lobby as a "business center". Gorgeous and stylish lobby with the glaring exception of an inexpensive desk with a computer and printer, and duct tape against the walls. * No breakfast. There is a restaurant that people were raving about, but nothing complimentary. Management did put out a fruit basket, so kudos for the attempt. There isn't really a place to put a breakfast bar, but a coupon toward the restaurant breakfast would be great. * Scenery. Or, lack thereof. It's downtown; I didn't really expect any. Pros: * Beautiful mix of the old and new. Red, black, and white, but they completely made it work! Very stylish deocr in both the lobby and the rooms. The marble floor is stunning, and the furniture chosen to complement it. The designer was worth whatever he charged. * Excellent staff! We really felt like they operated as a family. All were warm, enthusiastic, knew their jobs, and genuinely seemed happy to serve. * Very comfortable beds. * Large rooms. Our neighbors had "several" in a King suite, and they said they were all comfortable. We felt there was plenty of room for us to stretch out, work, or sleep without noise. * Immaculate rooms. 5 stars for housekeeping. * Location. 6 blocks straight down to the convention center. 1 block from the major bus artery, and a block the other way from the trolley. Hard to beat the convenience. Overall, we loved it and will make it a first choice when we're in this area.

“Solid budget hotel” Stayed here one night, were given a room on the 4th (top) floor. Lobby sterile looking and plain, was not impressed. Got to room, was surprised . . . nice room. We had room 429, very large room with 2 dbl bed, dresser, mini refrig, microwave, medium round table and two chairs, big tv, iron/board, tile floor, large balcony. The bathroom was small but had a good tub/shower, wall-to-wall counter, hair dryer. The room/bathroom were really clean. Houston is a damp and moldy city, mildew is common but our bath had none. The room needed updating, but it was very clean and comfortable. About the smell . . . our floor smelled like fabric softener, it smelled fresh and clean. I was really surprised when I read all the terrible reviews. This was a solid budget hotel and I would most definitely stay here again. BTW, we are two senior ladies, very well traveled. Sandy (in Denton)

“So convenient to all public transportation” We flew into Seattle to spend the night before our planned vacation to Victoria, Vancouver Island and San Francisco. This hotel is so convenient and the staff is very welcoming. From SEA/TAC airport we took light rail to Pioneer Square which arrived 1-1/2 blocks from the hotel. We literally walked down the street from the exit, turned right on Yessler Way and the hotel was about 3/4 a block down on the left. Our room was spacious, very, very clean and the breakfast the next morning was Continental along with waffles. We walked to the Space Needle for dinner and rode public transportation back - really easy. The next morning, the Victoria Clipper, Pier 65, to Victoria was just 1 mile from the hotel. On returning to Seattle from Victoria, we stayed a 2nd time at the Best Western (great, clean accommodations again) and took Amtrak the next morning (0.3 miles from the hotel) to San Francisco. We would definitely go back to the Best Western on a return trip to Seattle.
“使い勝手のよい2部屋” 1階の入り口にはセキュリティーが常駐していて、予約確認書を 見せて上階のフロントでチェックインしました。 午前9時前でしたが、ホテル会員だったので入室できました。 リビングと寝室からバスルームに行かれ、洗面はダブルシンクで 便利です。 電子レンジ、冷蔵庫も完備。 家族がゆっくり休みたい派と動き回りたい派に分かれたので、 ここは正解でした。

“Best staff” Times Square is crowded, noisy and smells bad so, you likely don't want to stay right there but, about four or five short blocks away is the quiet, low key but elegant Micheangelo. A sort of refuge. An easy place to come back to after a hard day working or sight seeing. I picked this hotel because of the rating on TripAdvisor and because it was in the middle of two trade shows I attended and it was the same price as the two hotels where those trade shows were. Nice, elegant little bar. Friendly, accommodating staff. They comped me on the Internet connection. I left my phone charger in the room when I checked out, called them about it and two days later UPS delivered it to my door.
“Fantastic!!” Absolutely huge hotel, big comfortable rooms and great location. The pool was great.

“Good Location & Value” I stayed here for 6 days while doing business for the county. The location was walking distance to a trolley line. I also walked to Beale street a couple of times when the trolley was late. Do not depend on the trolleys to run on schedule at night. I was told the days were not much better, but I did not use them during the day. They are good cheap transportation when available. There are also many pan handers along the trolley line at night. This can get aggravating every night when you go out. The hotel lobby and halls are dated. The rooms seem to be more modern but I would rate them as average. Mine was clean. The staff was helpful with tourist questions and will also help arrange tours. The internet was free but down one night during my stay. The breakfast was basic and none of the item change during the week. But it is free and convenient. Overall a good location and a good price. I plan to write a separate review on some of the places to go.

“Great Hotel but still needed earplugs” I've stayed at ths hotel before and thought it was great. Maybe it's just that it is a year older now or we just had back luck. Out suite was plagued with strange noises. Although these rooms have "central" airconditioning with a thermostat, the blower unit was in a utilily closet in the bedroom. It woke me everytime it cycled on and off. Fortunately it was not that hot while we were there and I simply turned it off at night. The worst offender was the refrigerator from hell. I've never experienced an appliance with such a variety of loud and annoying noises. I own four refrigerators and realize that all refrigerators make some noise but there was something wrong with this refrigerator. The manager offered us earplugs or to move us to another suite. I know she was trying but I think she should have taken our word that something was wrong with this refrigerator and either fixed it or moved it to another room as opposed to asking us to move all of our stuff. Aside from the refrigerator from hell, this is a nice hotel. The afternoon social hour is particularly nice. Kelly, the lady who runs it, is great. We were in a group of about 20 and this gave everybody a nice opportunity to meet their peers who are spread out over the country.

“Great hotel, but not for everyone” The Clift is a wonderful hotel, but as the reviews reveal, you either love it or hate it. Here's my take: If you like to dress in Nikes, cargo shorts, T-shirts and baseball caps, you'll hate it. If you booked online with price being your only criteria and didn't do your homework, you'll also hate it. The decor is an acquired taste. It's pretty "out there" when you first walk in, but that's the point. Very dim lighting, and the furniture looks as if Tim Burton decorated it with leftovers from the set of "Beetlejuice" They really stress form over function, but the crazy seating in the lobby is really quite comfortable. From our experience, everyone on the hotel staff was friendly and professional, from the doormen to the bartenders in the Redwood room. The rooms were very comfortable also. Bathrooms were on the small side, but this hotel is not about hanging out in the bathroom, or watching TV, for that matter. Again, I think ones experience at the hotel depends totally on perspective. If you embrace the quirkiness and have a positive attitude, you will love the experience, from the atmosphere to the staff, but if you walk in and immediately feel as if it wasn't what you expected of a 4 star hotel and you don't fit in, you will find things to complain about.. To those people, I'd suggest that they do a little research next time and stay somewhere else.

“Exceptional place to stay!” When they say suites, they mean suites! There was a separate bedroom with its own tv and a sitting room with a sleeper sofa, tv, microwave, fridge, and even a sink. Clean and nice and for $72 best place we stayed on a 2-week trip-ask for the senior rate if you qualify. We would stay there again in a heartbeat!

“Great hotel with a Great location!” We booked this hotel prior to Hurricane Sandy and was contemplating if we should switch to a mid-town hotel after seeing/hearing the damages that took place in Lower Manhattan. Thankfully, the Hotel posted updates on their Facebook group page so we knew they had everything back up in order by the time we arrived for our vacation. We stayed on the 10th floor facing WTC. Not the highest floor but it was nice getting a free upgrade to a King size room. Check-in was a breeze as they had a room ready upon our 12pm arrival. We stayed there for 4 nights and have no complain at all. Room was clean, curteous staff, nice view, great location. I'd definitely recommend this for anyone who is looking to stay at Lower Manhattan. It's close to the major attractions with various subway stops close by the hotel. Due to the aftermath of the Hurricane, the PATH via NJTransit to WTC stop and the Cortland St. subway station (two steps from the Hotel entrance) are currently not in operation. But the Fulton St. subway station is just around the corner from the Hotel and it's a major stop for 3 subway lines that took us all over Manhattan.

“Not glamorous but a nice place to stay” I stayed in a first floor room which was nice. I'd stay here again. The location is about half way between JAX and the I-95, yet the room was plenty quiet from an aircraft noise. Airport shuttle is $3. Refrigerator. Microwave. No gym. Pool. Yes, the lobby computer has a very nice internet connection. The property grounds are kind of odd--not glamorous, like a real estate layout from some bygone generation. Room doors all open to the outside. Complimentary hot breakfast was good and basic. For a Choice Privileges location next to JAX, this Quality Inn is a much better deal than the Clarion which is opposite the parking garage from the terminals. Lobby is nice and spacious.

“Clean & Convenient” My husband and I stayed here during Memorial Day Weekend, and found the hotel to be quite pleasant. This hotel was great for the price and location. It's almost on the corner where Diversey, N. Clark, and Broadway meet. Just up the street from the El Train, and bus stops are a hop, skip, and a jump away. The hotel staff was very nice and always helpful. Also, their continental breakfast was pretty good. They served coffee, juice, donuts, bagels (my husband really liked the bagel slicer), cereal, and milk. Best of all, they have their own parking lot with a reasonable $10/day fee, but get their early in the day 'cause they go fast. This fee was a lot better than paying $20/day at one of the garages. The rooms are small and could use a little more lighting. But who wants to stay in their room all day when you have Chicago to see? Also, watch out for that step in front of the bathroom.

“A Good Stay” Across from the Capitol and via skywalks connected to the Convention Center and Shopping Mall (and then seemingly everything else). Starbucks in the hotel lobby, but not 24 hours; and the only restaurant is a steakhouse ( so on the pricier side). Better off doing the 10 minute walk to Downtown. At the time of my stay the gym was being renovated... Room of the standard sort; although the bathrooms were smaller than usual. I was on the Club Floor and the Lounge there had a smaller selection of food items that usual Starwood Lounges. For the price and the endless number of hotels on the area, I an not sure it was the best deal around. The hotel itself was good; however, again the price seemed high for what I received.

“Big bugs a problem” Three of us stayed at the Homewood Suites Biltmore for six nights at the end of April. The breakfast buffet and use of the computer with free internet access was very nice. The staff was very helpful. The location was good for us, and close to shopping and many chain restaurants. The problem was the three big bugs we had in the room. One night there was a dead one on the floor near the beds; another day there was a live one running around on the ceiling; and another day there was an almost dead one on its back near the door. These were not small bugs either -- I would say they were 2 inches in length. The front desk person called them water bugs. Whatever they are, they are gross, and I would not stay there again without assurance that the bugs were gone.

“A Great Oasis in the Concrete Jungle” I rarely write a review on a hotel - well, other than my personal hotel blog. But the Homewood Suites in Downtown Chicago was such a pleasant stay that I decided to make this one my first official TripAdvisor review. I was in town (my first time to Chicago) for a conference and chose the hotel mostly because I could cut my business cost with the complimentary breakfast. I was also pleasantly surprised to find the hotel also had a dinner as well! The breakfasts, while quite crowded were well staffed and very well prepared. We especially enjoyed visiting with the always cheerful and helpful Connie each morning. From start to finish I was pleased with this stay. The front desk clerks were just delightful (Starr was wonderful!) and extremely helpful. If I had to register one less than perfect aspect of our stay it would be with the strange occurrence each evening on our wireless internet. It kept kicking us off and asking us to sign in with the Hilton Garden Inn. Of course we couldn't sign in at that hotel, so we had to keep logging in and out until it recognized us at the Homewood Suites. Inconvenient, but not a real problem. We slept well, we dined well, and we will chose this hotel again if we return to the Windy City!

“Loathed the W” The front desk staff were very pleasant and helpful. But, the hotel is too trendy, too dark and too noisy. The corridors are poorly lit and narrow. The room was shabby and not very comfortable with a terrible view of a tall parking lot. The window covers do a very poor job of keeping out light from the parking lot which was well lit all night. Also, the windows do not open at all and the air conditioner made loud noises all night. The food was mediocre in the dining room. And , it was overpriced. I will not return.

“Out of this world fantastic!” From the moment we arrived, we felt welcome and well taken care of. From the reception to the concierge to the bell staff, there was nothing lacking in our first impression. Our daughter was given the "Trump Kids" bag as we checked in - it contained a stuffed animal and a coloring book and crayons. Based on our booking, we had a "space available" upgrade and we ended up getting a beautiful suite overlooking Lake Michigan. Our suite had a full sitting room, well equipped kitchen as well as a large bedroom and bathroom (and a second small bath). In the room, each time I went looking for something thinking to myself, ... oh, they should have put in...I would find it a moment later. There was not a thing that one could want while traveling (especially with kids) that was overlooked. The staff was incredibly accomodating setting up sofabeds and bringing extra pillows and featherbeds. The beds were perhaps the most comfortable I have ever slept in...ever. Our dining and spa experiences were similarly noteworthy, and even if there was a slight imperfection, the staff more than made up for it without being asked. I believe that truly defines a top notch property. For example, I had a pedicure scheduled and the nail tech had a family emergency. Rather than simply having me wait the 45 minutes until my next service started, they offered me a complimentary foot reflexology treatment. In the restaurant, they went out of their way to accomodate special dietary needs and split portions. Hands down, the best U.S. hotel stay (although a very close second to the Four Seasons in Seattle).

“Great for business or a vacation” I stayed for almost a week at the Courtyard Marriott while in town on business and had a fairly spacious (for New York) room with two queen beds, looking out on Ninety-second Street. I needed to work while at the hotel and there was a reliable and fast Internet connection for my laptop. The bathroom was clean and pleasant, with a granite sink and mirrors galore. I had a moment of panic thinking there was no hair dryer, but it was hidden behind some towels. There were plenty of clean towels supplied daily, for once more than I needed. Beds were comfortable, and you are able to set your own temperature in the room, a definite plus. Really, the room was so up to date and functional you wouldn't believe you were in a New York hotel room. Free copies of the newspaper downstairs and a well-decorated lobby. The staff was fast, polite and efficient; I never had to wait at the front desk. Step out onto First Avenue and you'll find all kinds of restaurants. Down side? It is a hike to the subway, about 15 minutes on foot, and it can take awhile to hail a cab even on nearby First Avenue. There was no refrigerator in the room though it looked like there used to be, and for long stays you really, really want a refrigerator. The elevators tend to be slow and verrrrrrry crowded in the morning. Noise leaked through the windows from the street, and started early. All in all, though, I'd happily return, though I'd bring my comfortable shoes for walking to the subway.

“Great hotel, convenient, great staff!” Business travel can be unpleasant, especially when there's not much in the way of choice in close proximity to the meeting. I was not looking forward to staying at the Marriott in SanDiego, but it was one of only two hotels (both Marriott) offered for the trip. See, I am a smoker, and have not 'had to' stay in a Marriott since they went smoke-free; and was anticipating a long week! Well, the staff at SpringHill Suites wonderful, understanding, and gave me a room close to the outside door. I was very pleased with not having to beg for a room close to the exit, as my experience in California hotels in general have not been the best – and especially at Marriott (and I am a Starwood member – with a lot of points!) Comfy beds, quiet, great internet connection, clean and roomy bathroom and dressing area. The kitchen area was tiny – but you don’t need much room for a microwave and a mini-fridge! I have reevaluated my California Marriott experience and am looking forward to my next business trip in October!

“Loved the Alex!” My husband and I were there First weekend in March, great location, extremely friendly staff, delicious sushi!!!! The room we had was small but very well appointed. No traffic noise!!!! Overall terrific place and I would recommend staying at this lovely boutique hotel. Booked through ---.com which is a split off of expedia and got a great price!!!!
“I Wouldn't Recommend” This is a horrible hotel. The front desk clerk, Laine was very rude. I would not recommend. The only good thing about the hotel was the manager, Matt was very accomodating.

“Nice Hotel at the top of Nob Hill” This hotel styles itself as boutique. It's really not that. In fact, it's a fairly typical Renaissance in terms of room size, style and amenities. That's more than good enough for me, and the views are spectacular. The hotel restaurant was less to my liking: crowded, trendy and overrated. However, the hotel was across the street from the Fairmont Hotel and the Tonga Room, which is a blast. If you like streetcars, they run right in front of the hotel, and it's an easy walk to most of the city (unless you are lugging suitcases, in which case the last two blocks back to the hotel are a pretty steep hike from almost any direction).

“Excellent hotel, great location” I just returned home from a very pleasant experience at the Omni Hotel. Starting with our arrival which was smooth, politely received and right up to our rooms. I luckily drew a corner room with windows on two sides and a view directly down to Independence Hall. Huge room - L-shaped entry, big bathroom with terry robes, big soaps and all amenities.
