Nice closet with swing out doors (not the dreaded sliding doors), real hangers (not those miserable kind that hook into a clip), safe in the closet and the minibar. The room had a king bed, bedside table, big desk with chair and a 3-seater couch with a side table. The staff was uniformely polite and helpful for all of the 6 nights I was there. Cleanliness was tops, bar was very comfortable. (Drinks about $10 ++) Cons: dim 60W bulbs in all three lamps in room. I asked for stronger and within 5 minutes a guy was there replacing with 100 W bulbs. They could put a coffee table in front of the couch (plenty of room for one). Dining room service very amateurish (the only weak spot in hotel service). Had breakfast every day which was standard fare. Dinner once which was good. The location is great! In the picturesque historic district and many, many restaurants within a two or three block walk from the hotel. It will be my hotel of choice next time I am in Philadelphia.

“Comfy bed and decor...good TV and cold A/C....no better way to spend a hot, sultry summer night in Chicago.” Hotel is an easy walk to tourist area and just across the river from my business. Good restaurants and bars were close by. The neighborhood is not an A+ but it appeared to be rejuvenating. I wasn't out late due to the heat, so don't know if it got seedy in the after hours.

“New Years Eve Stay” My husband and I stayed in the hotel over the New Years Eve holiday. The hotel was VERY busy but every employee that we encountered was very helpful and friendly. We were a part of a large group of couples and everyone had a wonderful time. The location is great to walk to bars and restaurants. The package rate for the room included parking and breakfast for a great price. The only head ache we encountered was when it was time to leave and we had to wait for 45 minutes to have the valet bring us our car. Eventually we learned that we were not even in the queue because of a mistake on the attendant's part. It was quickly corrected and we were out of there shortly after that. Other people were not so lucky. Overall it was a great hotel in a GREAT location. We'd stay again.

“Great for Business Travelers” I stayed here on recent business trip to Austin and I must say that I was very impressed with this property as well as with the level of service that I received from the staff. As is stated in the hotel name this property is located in Central Austin about 20 minutes from the airport and 15 minutes from downtown Austin and the 6th street area. This hotel is an all-suite property with each room having a separate bedroom and seating areas as well as a small kitchenette with microwave and mini-fridge and a sink etc. It was nice to have the extra space! The décor of the hotel is very Tex Mex with tile on the floors and an arboretum in the middle of the hotel with koi pond, tiny bridges and vegetation. This area leads to a restaurant onsite as well as to the breakfast area, business center, and pool area. Breakfast is served daily with many hot and cold items and there is a reception every night with snacks and drinks. The staff here was amazing and really helped us make the most of our trip to Austin. With limited downtime we received excellent recommendations on what we must see as well as great places to eat and drink. The shuttle service from the hotel is great and is a gratuity only service and you can call and have them drop you off or pick you up anywhere. The staff also remembered our names and was very solicitous of our every need. Calls to the front desk were answered promptly and requests met quickly and kindly. Whether it will be another business trip to the area or one for pleasure I would stay at this property again! It is a great hotel for business travelers.

“Reasonable Budget Hotel” This is reasonable budget hotel for New York, where hotel rates are very high. If you are expecting the Ritz, you will be disappointed. If you come with reasonable expectations for a budget hotel, then you won't be disappointed. details at [--] PRO: Location, within reasonable walking distance of Union Square subway; provides robes & flip-flops which almost no other budget hotel provides; reasonably quiet location for New York; reasonably clean; stayed on 4th floor East; had small kitchen with sink & fridge but no dishes or utensils; seems safe with 3 locks before you get inside room. Provides toiletries: soap, lotion, shampoo, sewing kit. Small color TV in every room; some of about 15 channels may have audio/video problems but enough choice to watch TV for few hours. Enough shared bathrooms that never had to wait for one to be free CONS: singles are very small rooms; rickety bamboo furniture in room; old hotel in need of refurbishment; expect worn carpet, etc. Plenty of restaurants in all price ranges within a mile of hotel BUDGET TIPS: WHOLE FOODS GROCERY STORE right across from Union Square Subway; you can buy sandwiches, salads, etc. at reasonable prices & picnic on Union Square across street; pharmacies like Rite-Aid give reasonable price of things like fruit juice, etc. Remember New York is one of the most expensive cities in USA.

“Only so-so” I am normally a huge fan of Marriotts, but I found this property disappointing. On the plus side, the beds were very comfy; the TV was huge and had lots of channels; the staff were generally quite helpful. On the minus side: housekeeping got less fastidious every day (I was there for 4 nights); there was "gunk" of some kind on the vents of the bathroom fan; the bathroom floor doesn't appear to have been mopped each day; there is very little seating in the public areas of the hotel; my room had only a shower (which was nice and clean, but I prefer a bathtub); and the concierge desk was frequently unmanned. Because this was a business trip and I wasn't paying the bill personally, the overall experience was fine, but I probably wouldn't stay here on a pleasure trip. What I consider to be a great location doesn't make up for unimpressive accommodations.

“Nice Place - Good Cookie!” We had three families stay, each family included 2 adults & 2 kids and the place was nearly perfect. Price was good, rooms were excellent, front desk & concierge service impeccable. Only negatives: location made shuttle absolutely imperative, road noise for west and north facing rooms was surprising (even on 8th floor), morning heat on west side (best view) was intense & we had to call down everyday, save one, for enough towels & lack of ventilation fan in bathroom causes moisture buildup Remember to ask each evening for your cookie!

“Great location for sites; sketchy cleanliness; bring your earplugs” I booked this hotel using AAA rates on the hotel website. Great location. Hotel appears to be in a post-inauguration hangover mode. Pros * Location - 15 minute walk to Mall/Museums, White House; short walk to Verizon Center, Fords Theater * Room set up - Like other Embassy Suites, the separate sitting and dining space is always welcome, especially when traveling with small children. * Staff was pleasant. Cons * Room cleanliness. At first glance, the room looked fine. Random hairs in the bathroom. Popcorn under the master bed. Removed sofa cushions so we could pull out bed for my child. Peanuts found under cushions. Pulled sofa bed out; underneath sofa many, many snacks. * Thin walls. We could hear our neighbors quite clearly in the bedroom areas. * Zero view; our room looked directly into the office windows in the very nearby building. Neutral * Breakfast buffet was complimentary (a plus) but extremely crowded, so it didn't really meet our needs. * Social hour also complimentary, but again very crowded. As it is not the high time for tourist visits, I imagine the situation is worse during other times of year. * Pool - area bright and airy; standard city hotel size; 3' 3" depth throughout. Whirlpool out of function. I am a Hilton Honors member, so I generally look for Hilton properties first. Since there are many other hotels in the area I will check out other options on our next visit.

“Huge bathroom & free wifi” Those are the highlights. The bathroom was unusually spacious, even compared to other 4-star+ hotels and free wifi was a pleasant surprise. Otherwise, it's a standard business-class experience; no complaints but also nothing to rave about. Recommended for a quiet and uneventful stay.

“The Staff are brilliant... but the rooms are pretty small” I stayed here based a lot on the recent reviews and whilst I absolutely agree that the staff are fantastic, the room itself was a little disappointing. The bed at a push was a double and the room would be a tight fit if there was two of you there! Location is great, but next time I would stay somewhere perhaps not so close to Union Square in the hope of getting a little more room.

“Nice hotel, nice rooms, great location, great price” I would stay at this hotel again and definitely recommend this hotel to others. Nice renovated room. The room with a Queen bed is small so no more then 2 people should stay there - but we have stayed in smaller rooms. Nice flat screen tv on the wall. Staff at the desk was nice and helpful, gave us a room on a high floor. The lobby needs to be renovated but then maybe they wanted to finish the rooms first. There is an elevator to get to the lobby from the entrance but hard to find - there is an escalator to get up to the lobby and stairs to go down New bed, new furniture and new carpeting, night stand and small desk. Also looks like they renovated the bathroom although small and no counter space. Small bathroom but sufficient. The toilet paper holder doesn't work - it's a modern holder that falls over and the toilet paper falls off. For a newly renovated hotel they need to fix that. No place to hang the wash cloths or hand towels - the cleaning person had to put them on the window sill or the radiator. Cleaning crew needs to do a little better - missed some areas to vacuum and the light switch was dirty. Also dirty spots on the drawer in one of the night stands Light on the desk didn't work - but liked the fact there is a bright overhead light on the ceiling and one on each night stand. Only problem was construction work starting at 8am one day - ridiculous to start that early in the morning Great location a block from the chaos of Times Square - subway entrance across the street. Great price for the location I would definitely recommend this hotel

“Great Botique Hotel” I have stayed here several times for meetings. The second floor lounge and meeting rooms are great for small meetings. The staff is very friendly and helpful, the location of the hotel is great for downtown activites (when not in meetings). Room services was very prompt and they make a really great steak! The property is clean and well maintained. Hotel is nice and quiet and great for couples too.

“Busy location” I had a pleasant stay at the Muse Hotel. The hotel is very well located if you’re going to a Broadway theater or for shopping. It's about half a block for Seventh Avenue and Time Square. It’s a block and a half from Fifth Avenue’s high end shopping district and about a block from Radio City Music Hall. It is not a quiet neighborhood. Time Square and its wall-to-wall crowds 24/7 are right there. Generally, I prefer a quieter setting. The room was modern and very comfortable. It had recently been updated. Located on the 15th floor, it had a nice balcony, but there is not much to see. The bath was fine though the tub had a very slow drain.

“Good bargain and a a decent hotel” This hotel is now called the "Columbus Gatehouse Inn" For the money, it was a great deal! It's near the airport and we just needed a place for one night.. big room with kitchen, fold out couch and hot breakfast for $63 how can you beat that deal? Breakfast was good with eggs, pancakes, sausage, hot oatmeal, danishes, yogurt, waffle maker etc... Can't go wrong here.. yes, it's dated, but a true value!

“Enjoyed my stay” Stayed at the Westin, Columbus during the last week of March 2012. The hotel was very clean and in a nice location of Columbus. Many restaurants and entertainment options within walking distance. The King-room itself was a little small, and unfortunately was facing the building to the south, which didn't allow much natural light in the room. As a result, the room felt smaller and colder than it probably was, but I didn't travel to Columbus to spend time in the room so that was okay. For someone planning to stay in the room for a few hours or more during the day, make sure to get a room facing another direction. Service and the staff we very good and it was a very nice place to stay.

“Surprisingly quiet” Despite it's location in the heart of Times Square, the suite I occupied was one of the quietest I have ever had in Manhattan. The rooms are spacious by NYC standards, and the beds very comfortable. Highly recommended for a Times Square or mid-town visit.

“Perfect Location” This is in a perfect location within walking distance to the park, shopping, great resturants. A very easy location to stay at. The rooms are so so. Nothing fabulous, but big enough and everything you need. I would stay here again, especially for business

“Sadly, not up to snuff” The Renaissance Worthington has been a part of my life since I was 18 years old, so it pains me to say this, but the hotel is just not up to snuff anymore. I think because I'm so attached to the hotel (having attended countless weddings and official functions there, as well always staying there anytime I return for a visit) I've been unwilling to write this review. But I can't take it anymore...this hotel has lost its hold on me. My husband and I are loyal Marriott (Platinum) members and of all the Marriott brands, Renaissance is our favorite. But this hotel is in desperate need of an update. The past three times we stayed there all of the beds have been old and creaky. Its hit or miss whether or not we get bathrobes and the valet service is aggravatingly slow. So slow we don't even tip...and we ALWAYS tip...but it became a principal thing after the first fifteen minutes of waiting. I still love the apple pie for room service, but that's it. We finally caved and stayed somewhere else this past visit (the Omni Hotel) and I realized just what I'd been missing (hospitality, amenities and a great night's sleep). I'm sad for the Renaissance. They have the clout to compete with the Omni, but without more comfortable beds, more attentive staff and better amenities, I'm afraid they are on track to lose their place as Fort Worth's finest property. Fingers crossed they start trying to be better than average...soon.

“Very convenient location” I stayed at the NYMA (formerly Red Roof Inn) for a Friday to Monday weekend stay in July 2010 and it was perfect for what I needed... a place to lie my head after shopping. I was steps away from that very cool women's accessory store called Accessory Palace and another block form the Macy's compound. Also on the street of the hotel was a very cool yogurt/specialty cold tea drinks place called Red Mango (this location now moved down to 11 W. 32nd Street), which was also competing with Pinkberry Frozen yogurt. The hotel room was a good deal for the location plus it was very sizeable with plenty room to move around and a decent sized closet with a king size bed. The plus for me was the small microwave and fridge in my room. Also, the hotel lobby area had 2 computers with internet service and I had a couple packages delivered to the hotel, which were handed off to me without a charge. The NYMA was a good stay and I will definitely return.

“Great Hotel” Stayed here for 2 nights. Booked hotel via hotels.com and got an excellent rate at the last minute. Reception: Fast, Friendly very helpful and informative. Rooms: Clean, Spacious and silent for a city centre hotel. Parking: Used the Valet service which was efficient also. Location: 2 minutes walk to Newbury Street, 5 to Boston Common so ideal for tourists. Overall an excellent hotel and would recommend for business and tourists alike,

“LOVE LOVE LOVE THIS HOTEL” If you don't receive good service and a wonderful nights sleep at this hotel I'm sure there is something wrong with you. I love this hotel, stay there at least once a year and just love arriving every time. They are very professional, do their extreme best to give you anything and everything you wish and the beds are FANTASTIC. I just feel like royalty for a few days and as you can see, can't say enough good things about this hotel.

“Best location in Chicago” I wanted to try this new luxury property in Chicago. I've stayed at the Peninsula, the Four Seasons, and the Park Hyatt (and other lesser rated properties) and I was looking forward to comparing the Trump to these fine accommodations. First, the good. Location, location, location! By far the best feature of the hotel is its scenic perch on the river, close to the Michigan Avenue scene AND the loop stuff like Millenium Park and the Art Institute. Right now it is a bit tough to find and walk around because of ongoing construction, but this should be no problem when it is finished. Second, even the standard rooms are huge. I was on the 24th floor in a 'city view' deluxe room. The view was forgettable, but the quality of the interior was impressive. I especially liked the high end ktichenette with a microwave, SubZero fridge, Meile stove, etc. There are even cooking utensils, pans, and dishes! Now, the not so good. Even though the room is large and luxurious, I found it a bit sterile. The slate color scheme should be brightened up a bit with a dash of red roses or something else to break up the slate monotony. The duvet on the bed was very thick and the a/c didn't seem to work so well so it was a bit stuffy. I took a tour of the spa and fitness center, but didn't partake of any service or activity. I had no meals at the hotel either. The one downside of my stay was the construction noise that started early in the morning. I know that I paid a soft opening rate of $347 because of the construction, but I had hoped that there would be a minimal amount of noise. Not so -- they were pumping concrete up to the 90th floor and there was a 5 second interval pounding in the core of the hotel that did not stop. When I checked out, I told the front desk person about this, and she apologized. I actually checked out early because the pounding was so annoying. All in all, the Trump is a fine choice for Chicago, but if you are looking for lavish, extensive public areas and a bit of warmth in the guest rooms, I'd suggest the Four Seasons or Peninsula.

“So so....for the price” The room size was fine. Parking was close and easy, and the location of the hotel is great. But if you're into a "hotel experience" you will be underwhelmed. Older rooms, kind of a funny smell. If you stay here ask to NOT be placed on the side closest to the street. All night/early morning buses and large trucks rumbled by and stopped outside our window (it's at a stoplight). Other than that, for the price, it's a convenient and fair place compared to the pricier options in downtown.

“Would Stay Here Over Trump” I continue to enjoy the fine service at this hotel. You will feel like part of the family if you come regularly, which I do. The management, Mr. Brooks and Mr. Kirincic are of the best in the business. I've stayed everywhere in town from the Four Seasons/Le Parker Meridien/Essex House/Helmsely to the Benjamin, et.al. My needs require a downtown hotel and this is sensational. Even if you have business uptown, the subway is right there and it is easy to get a cab M-F. McDougal Street takes you directly through the village and is only a couple of short blocks from the hotel. This is a fine boutique style hotel with a luxury, but not pretentious feel.

“A nice stay” Hello, We just spent two nights at the Waldorf Towers. Our room was a one bedroom Luxury suite 800 sq. feet that we booked on-line for a great rate.The room was beautiful. Based on our room rate I do not think we could have done better. If you are picky about service this may not be the Hotel for you.Everytime we asked for something they said they were overwhelmed by diplomats who are staying at the Hoel and it would take one hour for our ice to arrive and when my husband was checking in there was nobody there to greet him and he had to take up his own bags. To me this Hotel is more like a Luxury Apartment building which I like and that is probably why many celebs stay here.As we were leaving Ted Turner was checking in. Overall we had a great time and if you like the old world feel this is a great place to stay.

“Great location, wifi, free breakfast” I just returned from a 5 day stay at Hotel Metro and here are my opinions: Positives - Free breakfast (includes 3-4 cereals, many kinds of muffins and bagels), not hot - Location, literally 50 paces from subway entrance. - Free wifi worked extremely well from my room and the cafe. Negatives - Room was small but knowing this going in, it wasn't a big deal. - Street noise was pretty bad. Get a room facing away from the street if possible. Otherwise you'll hear the trash trucks and horns all night. All in all I liked the place but I'd probably try another hotel next time anyhow. I just like to try different places. I paid $175/night and while that is good for NY, it felt like a lot for the small room. But the price was worth it with the free breakfast and wifi. Notes: There is no pool. Our room did not have a pillow top bed.

“very comfortable and excellent location” This hotel is just off the main shopping street of Chicago - the Maginificent Mile - and as such is in an ideal location for walking to shops, almost all tourist sites and restaurants. It calls itself 'The Avenue' and the 'Crowne Plaza' sign is difficult to see making it hard to find if you aren't aware. The reception area and public areas are rather cramped. However these are the only minor drawbacks as in all other aspects the hotel is excellent. The staff are all cheerful and helpful. The rooms are high in the building and have very good views. The bedrooms are roomy, clean and well equiped. The bed is extremely comfortable (among the most comfortable I have ever experienced in a hotel). There is a fresh coffee maker, excellent bathroom, ample storage and very good blackout curtains. My only minor complaints are the noisy air conditioning/heater unit (though this isn't a huge problem as you can turn this off at night) and the poor strength of the Wifi signal (maybe this was just where my room was). Overally I think this is a very good hotel at a reasonable rate for Chicago. Definitely recommended.
“Convenient to the action” Very nice hotel with excellent amenities. Staff is friendly, helpful and the facility is immaculately kept.

“OK but nothing to rave about” I chose this hotel based on the proximity to my client's office. A colleague stayed at the nearby Hyatt Regency. The Doubletree was fine, the room was fine and clean, but for the price I think I expected more. The hotel charges $9.95 per day for internet, and the hotel's Printeron service wasn't working and the front desk was apologetic, but the workaround they gave me - emailing my files to the manager - didn't work as when I went to collect the printing, they couldn't find it. I appreciated they tried to offer a solution, but was frustrated. I chose not to print in the business center as it was $1 per page and that's highway robbery. The hotel has a very small gym for a hotel of that size - only 2 treadmills. Valet parking was efficient and staff was always friendly, welcoming me when I passed. Good views from my room.

“Great Hotel in Downtown Chicago” The Amalfi Hotel is a very nice hotel in downtown Chicago, close to everything. As a frequent Chicago business traveler, who has stayed at many hotels in downtown Chicago, I would say that this is one of the best. Free internet (that works!), continental breakfast on each floor, gym, and restaurant on site. Would definitely come back. No complaints!

“Great Hotel!!” Everything was great here. They knew I used Priceline yet were so warm and welcoming at check in (doesn't always happen). I paid a $30 upgrade and had a perfect two room suite- kitchen, oversized furniture in living room, great work area, large bedroom with major built-ins, nice enough bathroom, and amazing view of the east river (I woke up to watch the amazing sunrise). The room was gorgous!! (for $130 total in NYC!!!!) They had a top reviewed spa and a nice restaurant that I didn't use. I don't know why they still have tube TVs- so outdated. SO OUTDATED! I would stay here again and recommend it to everyone. This hotel deserves to be #11 of over 400 in NYC. I really can't wait to come back!

“never ceases to amaze” i hate to share hotels that are really good - i fear i'll not get a room when i really need one! This hotel goes out of their way to please (the same can't be said about the restaurant). The rooms are great design, the lobby cozy and sales staff does what it needs to get it done. Odd, but the banquet staff timed it perfectly to NOT clear our dishes, etc while we were on break, but after we'd started our session. Doesn't sound like a problem, but our food was IN our meeting room. The only change from my last review is these oddly pulled back curtains in the "living room". They aren't pulled back in a cool/elegant ashion, but tied with a large rubber band. Split them at the top and have them hang naturally down the side. The light that streams in is amazing and adds to the great vibe there. Fine, piddly, I know. Just stay there.

“We liked it” We had a very short stay here, so I don't have much to say. We checked in late and checked out early. If you need a luggage cart, they don't keep them by the front door, so that can be difficult to find. I also did not like the "courtyard" design. I never thought about it before, but I guess that's where they get their name. It makes it difficult to get to your room. We had to find the elevator and then walk around the perimeter on our floor looking for our room. Those are just personal gripes, but they may help you. The room was very clean. The staff was very nice. We did not visit the dining area or the fitness areas. I would go back again.

“The price was right...free :-)” We had previously been aware of this property, having checked it out on several travel sites. Since we connect through IAH frequently on Continental/United, there had been times we made back-up hotel reservations in the event of weather problems or missed flights. The prices had always seemed good given the property's proximity to the airport, but we had never actually stayed there...before this instance. Furthermore, it was not our option to choose because the airline with our misconnect assigned us to the Hyatt Place. The hotel was apparently having a problem obtaining its permit to access IAH with its shuttles, so they were sharing a shuttle with another hotel or two. We were picked up where promised (although a bit delayed) but then circled the terminals looking for and picking up a number of other people. Since the shuttle was full, I decided to leap off quickly while my partner gathered up our bags. Good choice because there was already a long line at the hotel check-in counter...basically a table top. Confusion reigned throughout with ONE person handling the check-ins! When we finally got to our room, it was quite nice...modern, clean, bright and good-sized. Instead of trying to enjoy a drink and perhaps food in the chaotic lobby/bar area, the shuttle transported us to a local restaurant and picked us up again when called...much appreciated. I think we enjoyed the "free" breakfast instead of paying for eggs, etc. but really don't recall. Our flight was not scheduled to leave until the evening, and a real positive was they gave us a very late check-out without charge. This hotel voluntarily signs up to take "denied boarding" guests from the airlines. Hence, the long lines should probably be expected frequently, and since it is difficult to actually staff for guests such as we were, one should expect this hotel to be understaffed. In any case, even with all the issues at this property, the price was right...free :-)

“Very nice stay!” Recently stayed at the Westin Post Oak for a conference nearby. The hotel room was very large with 2 queen heavenly beds. Hallways were very well kept, room appeared recently updated, nice finishes, new carpets, very clean. Being in the room was a very pleasant experience. The hotel employees I encountered were all very friendly and helpful. I liked being connected to the Galleria Mall for convenience, however at times felt a bit uneasy entering from the mall to go directly to the elevator, as there was no security or hotel employee visible. The only other problem I would say is that the traffic noise on Westheimer is horrible. It does get quieter after midnight but if you need to fall asleep early, ask for a room on the other side of the hotel. It sounded at times like street racing on Wednesday night. Parking in the garage is free but kind of hard to navigate the Westin entrance. You can park outside the hotel for $12 a night but have to validate the ticket in the mall at an automated machine; pick your poison. Valet is available, I just choose to spend my $ elsewhere. I got the room through Priceline at what I think was a very fair offer for myself and the hotel. I would stay there again.

“The Best Service in all of Boston” After some mixed luck with some of the Boutique hotels in Boston I opted for something that was five star and had review which raved about service rather then a gitchy lobby or iPod docks in the rooms. The old expression goes that "you get what you pay for" and in the case of the Boston Harbor I paid a bit more then those Back Bay Boutiques and received service from the staff which was ten fold that of the price difference between the hotels. The greeting at the door was excellent and friendly; The doormen know the city and were a very valuable resource during my stay in Boston. The lobby itself has a typical five star hotel charm to it; an attempt to look old world which offers a traditional classic type of charm. The check in process was excellent; my room was already assigned my requests were filled and I had a wonderful dinner recommendation and directions within a few moments. Its rare that in today's day and age you actually get a concierge who truly knows the ins and outs of a city without having to go to some pre-bookmarked website in order to give the guests a recommendation. I was asked what sort of dinner fare I was seeking, I made three general comments and was given three different restaurant suggestions off the top of his head with recommendations at each. Now THAT is a concierge. Note: The hotel bar has one of the most extensive scotch selections I have ever tried, not to be missed. The rooms themselves were very nicely done; they felt like they belonged in a high end hotel, however I am rarely a sucker for decor. The bed was wonderful, the TV was large, and the water pressure in the shower was great. Nothing but positive things, if you want service and comfort this is the place.

“Gutes Hotel” Wir haben 2 Nächte während unserer Rundreise in diesem Hotel verbracht. Das Zimmer war sehr geräumig und sauber, das Bett war spitzenmäßig. Das Personal war überaus freundlich und hilfsbereit. Für all diejenigen, die eine Kreuzfahrt antreten, ist dieses Hotel auf jeden Fall zu empfehlen. Allerdings sind die Hauptsehenswürdigkeiten doch etliche Kilometer (40 - 50 km) vom Hotel entfernt.

“Get a room with a view” We originally booked an Urban Studio room, but after viewing it we immediately asked to change to a Waterfront room. The Urban Studio is a funky space, larger than normal, and with a soaking tub. But it looked out over a non-descript street. Being stuck with that view was so NOT why we came to San Francisco. In contrast, the Waterfront room looks out over the bay and has a wonderful view of the Bay Bridge. Much better! Even though the room only had a shower, and I thought wistfully of the soaking tub, it made for a more memorable stay. The hotel is well sited if you're a visitor. We're urban walkers, but even non-walkers should have little trouble getting to Fisherman's Wharf, Telegraph Hill, Nob Hill, Chinatown . . . all the bits you want in your holiday snaps. We had a very good dinner at a restaurant called Boulevard that's directly across the hotel on Mission Street. The hotel service was fine, but the only stand-out was the bell captain. She immediately saw that we were less than thrilled with our original room and suggested changing it. Then she contacted the front desk for us, and within two minutes it was done, with very little fuss. That's the kind of initiative you wish all hotel staff would take. When we needed a taxi, it sometimes took a while for the doorman to find one. So leave adequate time, or book one in advance, especially during busy periods. This is a chic, not-too-large hotel in a very good location. We would consider staying here again, but only in a room with a bay view.

“Not worth more than 175/nt” Because we were part of a conference, our rate was under 140/nt and while this hotel is beautiful - i wouldn't have paid more than 160 or 170 for it. The rooms are large, yes, but overall, they're pretty average. It's the lobby, grounds, restaurant & location that make this a great hotel. Service is good, but check-in was horrible - long lines all evening long at the front desk! . Couple of quirks with the room - nothing major - a lamp that stopped working, the pedestal sink was unstable and the hair dryer kept shorting out - but nothing too major. Not many kids networks on the tv but hotel was quiet, despite loud doors closing (i never noticed it from neighboring rooms). Book it if you can get it for under 150-ish.

“Pleasantly surprised by the Bahia” After reading some of the more negative reviews of the Bahia Resort we were nervous about what to expect. It was much better than I had hoped. The only negative comment is that the room had a mildew odor. Other then that it was clean, spacious and a bargain for the location and amenities available. My husband and 9 year old son enjoyed the area very much. We went for a long weekend to explore the zoo, wild animal park and see the main sights. We didn't have time to use the pool, but it looked beautiful and many families were enjoying it. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The location so close to the beach was excellent. We chose to stay in probably their cheapest accomadations near the tennis courts and it was very quiet and convenient. If you don't mind the mildew odor in the room the place was great. We travel often and felt it was a bargain and would definitely stay there again.

“Nice hotel near T stop and Faneuil Hall” This is a great hotel. I was there for business, but I checked out the pool. The T stop is one block away and Faneuil Hall is 1/2 a mile. The room was large, and there was a free internet room. (wifi was included free too)

“Nice Home Base for Sleeping” Had my parents stay here for two nights while they were visiting. I believe this is their third stay at the hotel, and I'd definitely have them stay at the Holiday Inn again. It's a great home base for resting and sleeping, as they don't need anything fancy beyond a comfortable bed and friendly staff and Chinatown restaurants less than two blocks away. The Mondrian is right around the corner, but the Holiday Inn feels more homey. Pros * Very friendly staff. The bellman Abhi (sp?) was especially helpful and super friendly. Liked the complimentary iced tea in lobby. * Great location, especially for walking tours of SoHo, Chinatown, Little Italy. * Comfortable, but small room. The bed was very comfortable and the furniture seemed pretty new. The bathroom was a little dated, but clean. * Free wifi, but service was spotty at times. * Tiny gym, new equipment. Cons * Tough to catch a taxi outside hotel. The bellman will help you, but it may take awhile. Use Uber or car service if you're on a tight schedule. * Small room. The sleeping room is dominated by the king bed, with just enough room to walk around the bed. * Window A/C unit a little loud. No central air. * A little bit noisy. Can hear conversations outside and occasionally ice being dispensed from ice maker.

“Smallest room ever offered to humans” I have stayed here before and had a good experience and decent rooms. The lobby bar is just redone making the lobby area much nicer over all. We stayed here because our water was out and we found a very good rate online. My wife checked in and not being a complainer took the room she was given. When I arrived was late that night and when I walked into the room I was shocked. It is a closet, the bed is barely larger than a twin and the bathroom is unusable unless you happen to be a child. In fact the only value I see to this room is as an adjascent room for a parent to let their kid have his/her own room, but even then it is barely acceptable. Apparently this hotel has 50 rooms like this so if you are not very careful about what room you get you'll end up here. the shower is barely big enough to turn around in and the shower curtain clings to you the whole time. It was a cold night in May but the heat is off in the whole hotel so don't bother asking, the space inthe bathroom was so small there is nowere to put your towel while showering other than in the sink. I have stayed in small rooms in hotels in NY that were better appointed than this so you could function. I realize I got a good rate ($99), but that does not mean I deserve to be put in the equivelent of a human pet crate. The will bring you up a small space heater that is from the 50's and sounds like a helicopter is landing in your room, which sucks but since the room is at most 125 square feet it takes moments to warm it. My wife checked in alone and was not feeling well and just needed a place to lie down, but what desk clerk would put a woman in a room like this? There is no way any woman who puts even the most basic effort could get ready in it. I would rather have had a euro hotel with a shared bathroom than this, and at least i'd be in europe. For Boston these rooms are an embarassment to the reputation of the hotel . Be warned before you get a good rate here, and if the room is one of these, assist on an upgrade, especially if you have 2 people

“Great location - cramped rooms.” Stayed here for a girls night out... the location is great. 1/2 a block away from Mich Ave. Lobby is huge - big bar & will always be packed on the wknds. Starbucks there... line can get very LONG. I found the rooms to be very small. The beds were extremely comfortable (pro) but the bathrooms were very tight, not a lot of move around room. The room was fine, served it's purpose but I have stayed at other hotels on Mag Mile and will def look elsewhere next time.

“Excellent value for money, one block from the White House” Booked in advance with a good rate, we've been upgraded thanks to our A-Club status. Suite had poor view but very cozy but we were here to walk around the city so the view was not an issue at all. As always, outstanding Sofitel bed which makes the difference with any other hotel. Overall, services prices lower than NYC Sofitel, which was a good news. Rather good service, even if there were some glitches on our bill but, these were solved very easily at checkout. Overall, one of the 5 best located hotels in DC!

“If you want elegance, excellent service and fantastic location...” If you are looking for elegance, excellent service and fantastic location...stay at The Pierre Hotel in New York! The hotel is beautiful with a staff trained to make every guest feel very special. Our "premier room" was very large and immaculate, but could have had better lighting for reading. The bathroom is adequate, but needs updating and we were told that the new owners plan a major renovation in the near future. Our dinner in the dining room was outstanding as was the excellent "substitute" pianist. The hotel's location is perfect for all 5th Avenue and Madison Avenue shopping and we would highly recommend a stay at The Pierre.

“Would have been great... if the airport shuttle had been on time!” I really liked this hotel when I first checked in. The front desk staff was friendly and welcoming and I thought the decor was quite nice for a Doubletree. The room we were assigned was spacious and the bed was comfortable. I did not have a chance to use it, but the pool looked like fun. Anyway... I stayed at this hotel because of its proximity to the airport, as I had a 7:00am flight out of San Antonio the next morning. I asked for information on the shuttle as I checked in. The front desk agent stated that we should be in the lobby just 15 minutes before we wanted to be at the airport, as it is just a few minutes away. In the morning, I went downstairs 15 minutes before I needed to be at the airport. The front desk agent called the shuttle driver multiple times and could not get in touch with him. The shuttle was parked in front of the hotel, so it was just a matter of the driver coming to the lobby. It took FOREVER. The front desk agent was so nice - even offered to pay for a cab! In the end, we had to wait in the lobby for 30 minutes to get the shuttle and were at the airport about 40 minutes from the time we arrived in the lobby. I was livid and almost missed my flight! Granted, one might suggest I pad some extra time to get to the airport, but my reason for staying at an airport hotel was so that I could sleep in a bit. It was just so frustrating! All in all, my experience with the airport shuttle was a real damper on my experience with this hotel. Otherwise, I would have rated the property much higher. Bottom line: If you are an airport hotel, make sure your shuttle is running on time.

“Fantastic Location” The Westin is very conveniently located to downtown attractions - we walked pretty much everywhere. The twin towers are interestingly shaped - round so all rooms seem to have a pretty decent view. Room was very clean, modern, and well appointed. We loved our stay there.

“Worst Experience with a hotel ever” We went to Dallas for Super Bowl. It was a bad experience all around, but especially for us. I am on the Super Bowl committee and we had almost 100 prepaid rooms in this hotel. We arrived at 11pm. They gave excuses about mix ups with the keys, lost keys, a stack of keys that were not coded. This went on for a couple of hours as we talked to friends in the lobby. There was a party in the resturant and bar, so we couldn't go into those areas, they wouldn't serve us in the lobby as we waited and we couldn't even go to the bathroom. Finally they gave us a key to a room...that had someone in it. When we went back to the desk they RUDELY told us they were sold out and we would have to go to another hotel. My husband found a Hampton Inn that was new so wasn't sold out in the Super Bowl block. We got in at 2am. It was a very nice accomodating hotel. Unfortunately we moved back over to our "prepaid" room at Crowne Plaza the next day - to mediocre rooms, horrible food and bad management. Do not stay there! I have never written a bad hotel review and I travel several times per month. This hotel was HORRIBLE!

“a low class motel” I stayed here for one night. Granted this was paid for by the hospital for me, I would highly recommend booking your stay at the La Quinta near Medical Dr. Both hotels have a shuttle and continental breakfast. So when I checked in, the customer service was very nice and friendly. our first room had an old stanky smell so I was glad to see that there was construction debrie so we checked into another room. the second room smelled less and the smell went away when you turned on the a/c. however, when i wanted to take a nap, I pulled back the sheets and there were blood stained pillowcase. I thought, ok I will just use the other pillow but then pulling the covers back further there is more blood on the sheets. I had to change rooms again. the third room was cleaner, and the room smelled less. This time, the sheets were clean and blood free. The bathroom however was very dirty. When I took a shower, the water that ran from the pipes was brown. The water cleared up after a few minutes. The place also lacks a fitness center and they will direct you to gold's gym if you ask. the food in the AM was fine, a waffle maker, coffee and some pastries. the best thing about this place was the shuttle service. Everything else was plain bad. take your money and go to La Quinta.

“love JDV hotels” great hotel, too bad about the location. If you don't mind your room being literally feet from one of the busiest freeways in CA you'll love it here for the price ... free parking & wi-fi is a standard for all hotels even with the A/C on full bore & ear plugs traffic roar is still noticeable

“Meh.” Hard to get excited about this hotel experience. I stayed for 2 nights with my wife and another couple who were new to NYC. I think they were disappointed with the feel of the rooms and the overall hotel mojo. As the veteran traveler to NYC, my view was a bit more charitable. Rooms are sizable enough, for NYC. The place was overall decent enough, for NYC. The location was actually good, for NYC. Detect the pattern? The location is so far west that getting across town is a royal pain, so if you have business or need to get to the East Side much while you are here, this place is not for you.

“Best staff you will ever find” This hotel was not our first choice when we started our Baltimore planning but I am so pleased that it is where we ended up. The location is wonderful. We were able to walk to every attraction or location that we wanted to go to. It is only 3 blocks away from the Inner Harbor and just a short walk to Camden Yards. There were Metro stations only 2 blocks away and bus stops across the street. The hotel itself was clean, updated and comfortable. Our room had 2 queen beds and a pull out sofa bed, since I was traveling with my two teenage sons it was perfect. I have never seen a room with that set up. The room also had a mini fridge, microwave, and small counter. They did offer a free breakfast in the lobby. This would be one of my only issues with our stay. The first day it was not that crowded and we were able to get our food with ease, including waffles and other hot options. The rest of our stay the breakfast area was over crowded and the hot food was always empty, the wait for the waffle maker was about 10 people and even the cold items like cereal or mufins were empty. Then there was not enough seating for all the people. I know this is probably a seasonal thing but it was frustrating. I would suggest that they have extra waffle makers that they could put out during peak times or make sure they have more staff working that area to make sure it is always stocked. The other issue was that the pool had very limited hours 3-9pm. Maryland requires a lifeguard be present and I imagine that is the reason the hours are so limited. The best reason to stay here is the staff. I do a lot of travel for work and family and this hotel has some of the best staff members I have ever come across. We arrived very early after a red eye flight and I knew we would not be able to check in yet but the staff welcomed us, held our bags, let us eat breakfast and made note that we were there so that our room would be ready as soon as possible. We did some site seeing and came back a short time later and they had our room ready. Any time we had any contact with staff members they called us by name and remembered our names later. The bell staff was great as well. Over all this was a great stay and we would definetly stay there again. If you are looking for a great place to stay that is close to all attracations and has the best staff, then look no further...

“I never thought I would love Trump” Thanks Donald, I stayed last weekend and had a wonderful time. This is an excellent hotel for both business and leisure. Comfortable, stylish wired and served by an attentive, well trained staff. The spa is the best I have ever experienced. The rooms are comfortable and well appointed with a kitchen in each. Unlike some high end hotels, you are not nickled and dimed to death with extra fees (eg. internet is free). Mr. Trump, I still don't like your show but, I love your hotel

“Classy, understated luxury in the heart of Seattle” What a lovely hotel. My room - 437 - was the size of an apartment. A hallway, dining/living area and separate bedroom - all with stunning views of the sea and Cascade mountains. On the walls, lots of original artwork. Decor muted and expensive. Furniture heavy and plush. This is how it should be. Competent, unobtrusive staff who know their way around the city as well. Best of all, quiet.

“Chic But Comfortable” This was my second stay at the Hotel Valencia in San Antonio. Each was a business trip to a downtown client. The location is terrific -- adjacent to the Riverwalk with beautiful views of the river, and within relatively easy walking distance of most of the downtown sites, including the Alamo. The interior is dark and quiet (almost somber), because they are trying for an upscale chic look. Rooms are comfortable, but a bit eclectic in decor because of the overall look the hotel is going for. The hotel restaurant (Citrus) is a great choice for breakfast. This is a nice alternative to the large convention hotels that tend to predominate on the Riverwalk.

“Beautiful rooms” The rooms were so modern and new. I really enjoyed staying here. The beds were extremely comfortable and it was roomy. The entire room screams stay in here and don't leave! But of course we weren't about to do that. The reception staff were rather cold when we first checked in. But the staff that checked us out were very friendly and bubbly. The location was good as it was close to Dupont Circle metro station. There were also several restaurants around the area, we ate at this pizza place that was recommended on Trip Advisor (sorry can't remember the name).

“Nice but not five stars” I visit San Francisco about twice a year and usually stay in a four star hotel like the Grand Hyatt or the Argonaut at Fisherman's Wharf. But decided this time that I'd try the Ritz that everyone seems to talk about. Checked in on a Friday for a stay till Monday. Upon driving up to the entrance of the hotel, the valet quickly opened the door and asked us whether we wanted to use the hotel's parking service or just park in the public parking lot which isn't very far from the hotel. What I liked is that they didn't automatically assume I wanted to pay $59/night for the hotel's parking service. But ultimately we decided to use the hotel's service because it's so convenient and given that in San Fran $59/night isn't too bad. We checked in at the front desk and everything went smoothly. Everyone greets you with a smile and a "hello". But what was interesting and a little bothersome is through my entire stay no one bothered to find out what my name was, only my friend that came with me that the room was booked under. Hmmm.... As stated earlier, the Club Level is great. Food is available nearly all day. You really don't have to go out for any meal if you don't want to. In fact, you'd probably pay $$$'s for similar food. Prosciutto and salmon for breakfast and caviar and foie gras for dinner! What more could you ask for?! The limo service is also great. Hop on for a ride to most anyplace in the city. I don't understand why the other reviewer was upset about tipping, that's the way these folks make their living. If you took a cab it'd cost you as much or more that the tip. So what's the big deal? The room was VERY large compared to other hotels I've stayed in. Bed were very comfortable. The amazing thing is how well the windows insulated noise from the outside. Not sure if this is due to the renovation. However, we could hear folks walking around the hallway if they were talking loudly, but it didn't happen often. Security seemed good. One time I left the door slightly open and security knocked and let me know the door was open. Not bad. All in all it was a pleasant stay. Was it worth the money? Not sure since you can get 90% of the service and amenities at other four star hotels. But it's nice to see how the wealthy live (or vacation).

“Amazing hotel, but kind of like staying at a Club! ha” We took our 16 yr old daughter to the W for one night as we were passing through NYC on an East Coast College Trip. We wanted to stay at our favorite (Doubletree Times Square) but they didn't have any discounted rates available. We read the great reviews on here and booked the W. It's simply an amazing hotel. GREAT location btw. Could not have asked for more when spending a night seeing a Broadway Show. However, be prepared. The hotel is VERY modern and between the water in the lower lobby, the unconventional seating areas in the main lobby, the hot pink neon lights everywhere, and the techno music being played in the elevators, it does give one the feeling that they are at an exclusive dance club rather than a luxury hotel. Bathroom is one of the weirdest things I have ever seen. Separated from the room by a sliding 'plastic' type door. Whole thing is like a giant plastic cube. Our daughter just LOVED it - great view, great ambiance (for a youngster like her,) but hubby and I agreed, we're happier at the Doubletree where it feels like home. Major kudos to all of the staff at the W. They made our stay completely painless and very enjoyable. Also - if you are concerned about security - elevators neat because they will only go to the room floor that your key is key-carded for. If you stay on the 52nd floor, you're going to the 52nd floor. Very good system to prevent 'just anyone' from getting in the elevator and roaming the various floors.

“A Special Place” I found this hotel had the little extras that marked he difference between an adequate hotel and a special one. It starts with the desk clerk who is especially friendly and says hello to you by name throughout the stay. Then there is the complementary champaign and chocolat pre-dinner snack in he lobby. Also our room was quite inexpensive ($230) and while not a suite it had a couple of nooks and crannies that made it interesting and a HDTV in the bathroom. My wife was upset with the comforter being thin and foam but when we asked for it to be replaced housekeeping brought a nice fluffy one in about five minutes. Also convenient is the fact that they have two great restaurants on premisis: Smith and Wolensky for steak and Lacroix for up to date continental. Unless you are expecting perfection you won't be disappointed with this place.

“Paper Thin Walls in Expansive Hotel” Stayed at the Westin Bonaventure for several nights to attend a conference at the LA convention center. The hotel is huge with 3-4 separate towers...I was in the Blue. The staff was OK. Didn't always seem too knowledgeable of the area. I asked which direction to head for shopping once and another time a specific address (on South Figueroa Street) to an Avis rent-a-car, both times they weren't sure which direction to send me. The room itself was fine and the amenities were good. The Heavenly bed just as comfortable as at other Westin's. Cons: Charging $12.95 per day for internet and paper thin walls. My first night I was awakend at 3am by the party next to me...2 guys and a loud woman. The next morning I could hear a entire business meeting carried on in the room on the opposite side of me. Also, could hear the guests in the room above me through the vents from time to time. Enjoyed using the fitness room, which was large and well appointed. Experienced the main bar/restaurant in the lobby, where the service and food were perfectly fine. Wouldn't refuse to stay here again, but hope to experience something else on my next LA visit.

“Average Hotel but good central location” We selected this hotel by the Sheraton name. The rooms were an average business-class, but with poor housekeeping. One morning I wasted powder on the carpet in the main room. Even though the bed was made up, the powder was still on the floor when we returned in the evening. The beds were nice, but too soft for me and my back hurt the entire 4-day stay. The hotel does not have any type of bed board for those who need a firmer bed. My husband did not have a problem with the bed. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful and always courteous. The rooms need renovation and a thorough cleaning, especially the bathrooms. Part of the countertop was only partially connected and there was slight mold around the tub edge (caulking). Curved shower curtains were nice. I just expected more from a Sheraton hotel. I guess this is why my husband usually stays at the Westin. One good feature of the hotel was it's cental location. It was easy to get to other areas of Denver area and sightseeing to other cities. It is located off I-25.There is construction around the area, but nothing that interfered with our navigation.

“Perfectly fine for the price” We got a great deal through Priceline over the Labor Day weekend, stayed 4 nights at CQ Downtown. The standard room we got was small, yes, but very well designed to fit in all the important things--bed, tv, desk, wardrobe. Bathroom had only a shower, but it was spacious and clean. Asked for extra pillows as we were going out for dinner, they were in our room when we returned. We knew when we booked that the Wall Street area clears out on long weekends, but we enjoyed walking around (with lots of other tourists) the old streets. Club Quarters is what it is--not a full service hotel, but fine if what you want is a reasonably priced room with FREE INTERNET. We figured with what we saved on the room, we covered some other more important city splurges.

“Great employees, great location, smaller rooms” First of all, I cannot say enough about how great the employees at this hotel were! They are friendly and helpful from the moment we checked in until the minute we left. Everyone was quick to share any suggestions or help with directions. They also had no problem extending our checkout time when asked. Second, the location really can't be beat. It's on a quieter end of the Riverwalk with direct access to it. Our rooms didn't overlook the Riverwalk, but there were plenty that did. It's a short walk to the lively restauarants, the Alamo, and Market Square. The location is really great and the hotel is extremely secure, requiring room keys to get in the doors in the evening and to use the elevator. While we felt the area was pretty safe, there were also a lot of people wandering around. The standard rooms are on the smaller side, especially with the amount of furniture in the rooms. That being said, they are comfortable and nicely appointed with a sitting area. We appreciated the rotating table for the TV, so we could watch it comfortably from bed or the couch. There was a mini-fridge in our room, which was a nice touch for our leftovers. We never saw or were bothered by housekeeping, but our room was always attended to by mid-afternoon, which was nice when we were ready for late afternoon naps. We didn't use the pool, but we did see people using it on a rather warm day (50s-60s) in January, so it must have been fairly warm. Valet parking is $27+ tax which was standard for all the hotels on the Riverwalk (we checked) and even the Market Square Fairfield, so we couldn't really complain. Internet was free and worked well in the room.

“A prototypical Hyatt Place” I'm a fan of Hyatt Place and Hyatt Summerfield Suites. (I like Homewood Suites alittle bit better because they tend to be a little bit newer and nicer.) I stayed in this place last week because I had a very early flight out of Jacksonville. At Hyatt Place, I can always count on quick check in, clean rooms with plenty of space to work in and sit back and watch TV. I have rarely been disappointed and this HP at Jax Airport was a consistent winner. And at $100/night, this is well priced for a hotel of this caliber.

“Great base for exploring NYC” My cousin and I stayed at the Cosmopolitan last month for her first and long-awaited visit to New York. We found it to be an excellent and affordable place to stay in a very convenient location. Both subway and bus lines stop very close to the hotel. There's a subway stop just steps from the door. Using NY's subway system we covered a huge amount of ground during our stay. Our room was small, but spotlessly clean and quite comfortable. As noted in other reviews, the staff isn't exactly effusively friendly, but they were civil enough. Midtown was mobbed during our visit with holiday crowds and returning to Tribeca was a wonderful respite from the hoards in Time Square. If you're used to quiet at night, the street noise may disturb you (it did me) so I recommend bringing ear plugs just in case. We parked around the corner at a garage that gives a discount for those staying at the hotel. We would definitely stay at this hotel again. We had a great time and the hotel was part of the reason why.

“Great Hotel for the price” We stayed here for three nights before a cruise. We were on the tenth floor with a beautiful view of the Space needle. Rooms were very comfortable. Plenty of room for our family of four. We loved the location, since the hotel is situated centrally to everything we wanted to see. Staff was pleasant and helpful with any questions we had. If you don't mind walking, you can get to just about anywhere from this hotel. We will definitely stay here again when we come back to Seattle!!

“Relaxing and friendly” Felt totally ripped off from taxi drivers. Charged $9 to get to hotel. Charged $10 to go back to Amtrak. My stay was quiet and peaceful. The harbor was beautiful. The Gallery had a huge sale on my fav Aerosoles shoes and boots. The staff was extremely friendly. Room service staff was terrific. The turkey burger was dry. I felt comfortable. Would return today if I could.

“Modern Conveniences in Historic Building in Downtown” Husband and I stayed for one night at the Hotel Indigo at the Alamo on a weekend getaway trip to San Antonio. The location of the hotel is excellent, literally right at the gate of The Alamo, and within 1/2 mile walk to all the restaurants on the Riverwalk, Market Square, etc. Since the hotel itself is not directly on the river, I believe it provides a much better value. The hotel is also in a historic building, which adds charm. However, because the hotel is retrofitted to a historic building, not all the rooms are the same size. We got one of the smaller rooms and it did feel pretty cramped, just a king bed with a TV and one nightstand. Also, the heater (older) made loud noises when it came on, which didn't provide for great sleep quality. The room was extremely clean, the bed was comfortable, and I loved the modern bathroom with the Aveda products! Valet parking is $25/night with unlimited in/out privileges, self parking is an option at the parking lot directly next to the hotel that charges $16/day. If you're a Priority Club member, you'll receive a free drink at the hotel's lounge! The staff was superbly courteous and all and all we had a great stay at the Hotel Indigo. Would definitely consider staying here again, but would request one of the bigger rooms.

“Beautiful Architectual Hotel” Very nice boutique hotel in the heart of The Loop. Easy walk to stores, theatres, parks and many restaurants. The room was newly redone and very stylish. The bed was comfortable and the staff very friendly. I really enjoyed my stay except for a loud fan in the bathroom which I couldn't turn off. I should have called the desk but was only staying one night. I would stay again but make sure that was not a regular" feature".

“Attention to detail, with few exceptions” Checked in Oct. 24 for a one-night, quick business trip stay. My daughter made the reservation, obtaining a very attractive rate available to her employer, a big-4 accounting firm. My travel budget wouldn't have afforded my staying here, otherwise. The young lady at reception, noting that it was my first stay there and after determining that I didn't need assistance with my small overnight bag, personally walked me to the elevator lobby -- a nice expression of hospitality. The room was impressively large and very well appointed, even having an Eames lounge chair and ottoman for relaxation in front of the expansive windows (which included small windows on either side of a large picture window that were openable, allowing fresh air if desired). There was also a long window seat with a comfortable cushion and ample throw pillows for relaxing and enjoying the view from my location on the 17th floor, looking west. The bed was very comfortable, with a duvet, using high quality linens. The bathroom was particularly impressive with a large soaking tub that was easily big enough for two. They even provided large candles for a romantic bathing experience and have large, sliding wooden doors adjacent to the tub that open the view to the bedroom area and the city lights view out the windows. The separate shower are, enclosed in floor-to-ceiling thick glass panels, had both a tall shower head and a separate, adjustable head that could be removed from its holder for hand operation. Much marble, attractive wood, mirrors, glass and excellent lighting. In fact, lighting throughout the room and bathroom was remarkable for the variety of options available for creating different kinds of lighting combinations. The TV/entertainment area included a DVD player. A nice touch was, in addition to the high-end glossy magazines typically found in hotels at this quality level, there were several books including one that had fascinating information and photographs on Chicago architecture. Another interesting detail was a large bowl of potpourrie on the chest of drawers. I found the fragrance pleasant but a bit strong. Of course, you can hide that in a drawer if it offends. A few details were missed, though. Some of the chrome fixtures in the bathroom could stand polishing more frequently to avoid dust or corrosion. Also, the sliding doors between the bathroom and bed area were apparently somewhat off track, not allowing them to come together properly to completely close off view between the two areas. All-in-all, I thought the Chicago Park Hyatt was a top-end hotel with its guests receiving a very good experience. At their regular rates, you get good value for the money. At the deeply discounted corporate rate I enjoyed, it was a tremendous value.

“Nice Hotel” I spent the weekend at this hotel for a get away weekend. The location was outstanding and we had a beautiful riverview suite that was huge! The tub in the suite was amazing. The beds and pillows were some of the most comfortable I have ever slept on. Emerald loop across the street is a great lunch place. Service at the hotel was outstanding. When we went to leave we had a flat tire and I ended up having to call AAA however, the valet at the garage tried to change it for me out of the kindness of his heart but he could not get it removed but I give him points for trying. I will stay here again.

“Potential to be a great hotel” My partner and I stayed one night at the recently re-opened Book Cadillac Hotel in the heart of downtown Detroit. First, it's in a great location. The hotel is located within walking distance of many of the major sites in downtown: the Fox Theatre, Ford Field, Comerica Park, the Greektown Casino, etc. The architecture of the building is stunning. It's nice to see that the building was saved. Yes, the decor of the Westin is very modern with clean lines, but it works very well in juxtapostion to the ornate style of the building. Now, it's important to keep in mind that the hotel has been open only about a week after having been closed for about 25 years, so some of the issues that came up will surely work themselves out as time progresses. First, upon our arrival, we, and several other guests were wandering around the first floor entrance trying to find the front desk, only to discover that we had to ascend the escalator to the second floor. (There was no indication anywhere that check-in was up there.) The room that we had on the 8th floor was on the back-side of the building, giving us a view of some of the tall buidlings of downtown. It wasn't the most spectacular view, but it was still pretty cool. The decor was great. We had the Delux room with a king bed. There was plenty of room and the bathroom had great counter space. One thing that we noticed was that the mini-bar had two half empty bottles of juice in them, which we promptly called to inform the front desk so that we weren't charged. The next day when the mini-bar attendant was doing the inventory of the bar, we informed him of the call. He looked at the bottles and told us that they didn't belong to the hotel, and then left them in the bar! After settling into our room, we had drinks and appetizers in the bar to the right of the reception area. It's a very nice area and the prices of the appetizers aren't too bad, however, be forewarned that a glass of club soda will cost you $4, with no free refills! The main restaurant on street level is not open yet, but the breakfast restaurant is currently open for lunch and dinner until the other opens. We had dinner there before the show we were going to see at the Fox. Our salad and soup were amazing. Our main courses, however, were not so good. My partner had a pasta dish that he had about two bites, it was so overcooked and bland. I had yellow-fin tuna that was cooked, instead of seared at stated in the menu. It was dry and overly salty. My partner sent his meal back and I could only get down about half of mine. The waitress was apologetic, but her solution was to offer us dessert or coffee so that we didn't go away hungry. We didn't have time to get a different meal or time to complain further. Would we go back again? Of course. I think, given time, the staff will become more familiar with the hotel and the various kinks will be worked out.

“Friendly Staff & Comfortable Stay” In the medical district for business and stayed 2 nights. I would like to comment on how friendly and helpful the staff were and the well appointed room that met my expectations. Although not a large hotel, the services, food and attention to detail were very good. From the front desk personnel, the van drivers to the wait staff: all were friendly, professional and genuinely caring. My experience here was positive and I would not hesitate to stay here again!

“A pleasant surprise” I have to say that I was quite pleasantly surprised by the Paramount Hotel. I had difficulty securing a reservation at the major chain hotels in downtown Seattle, so I made a reservation at the Paramount (which is part of a small chain, called Coast hotels, of mostly West coast properties). I made the reservation with hesitation, because the room rate was quite affordable in comparison with other things in the area, but the level of service and the quality of the accommodations matched those of more expensive properties nearby. The lobby of the hotel is quite small, but well-appointed. My guest room was great -- well-designed, nice furniture, good work space, etc. Best of all, the bed was incredibly comfortable! It was really one of the most comfortable beds I've encountered in my travels. I found the staff very polite as well. The only thing I didn't care for was the fitness center, which was sort of a dungeon in the basement. Considering the value and other positive aspects of my stay, however, I will stay here again when business takes me to Seattle.
“とても便利でお勧め” お値段もお手ごろ、場所もペンステーション・コリアンタウン・タイムズスクエア等に近く大変便利。駐車場も目の前にパブリックりがあり、1泊35ドルで使えます。Mega BusやBolt Busなどの発着地点からも近いですし、かなりお勧めです。スタッフも親切でした。他のホテルが隣接しており夜も部屋は静かです。

“Luxury Hotel With Great Location” This is a fine hotel. I stayed in the "Historic" tower. My room was nice sized, super clean and in good condition. What really makes this hotel great is the superior location. You can walk to everything. There is just good restaurant in the hotel. Don't let that bother you though. Just more reason to venture out for some authentic local cuisine. I was skeptical about anything "historic" as that is often code for old. Not in this case.

“Can't be beat for what it is...” I stayed at this Courtyard hotel the night before flying to China, and obviously needed a good night of sleep before the long journey. Everything about this place delivered for me, and I was able to sleep in comfort. It's a fairly newly refurbished property, and the beds are very comfortable. Also, I asked for a quiet room (no easy feat near an airport like LAX) and got it. The room was on the 7th floor, room 727, like the old commercial aircraft. But there is nothing old about this room in look or feel, and it was spotless. It looked out over an alley, not Century Boulevard, and I heard no traffic or airplane noise. The lobby facility is just fine, with a casual dining area that had a good selection of comfort food to order if you aren't inclined to go out to a real restaurant the evening before a flight. The seating area is large, modern, and includes private flat panel TVs with remotes so that you may watch the channel or your choice while eating. I thought this was a fairly unique and welcome setup. In sum, nobody likes staying at airport hotels, but if you must, this Courtyard fits the bill perfectly. Finally, I should mention the 24-hour free shuttle that picks up and drops off every 15 minutes. The hotel is very close to the airport proper, so you won't miss your flight.

“Not Good Enough” Spent a night at the Pierre during business trip. My company had negotiated a 'discounted' rate for my room of $370 versus the usual $550. I just don't think it was worth it. OK, the room was large with a king-sized bed. But the bathroom needed updating and the free toiletries were minimal and unexciting. Where were the reams of fluffy towels, extra pillows and luxurious toiletries that make a hotel stay special instead of ordinary? And at those prices, I really objected to the surcharge for broadband Internet access! I also hate the type of access where you have to sit at a desk to plug in, instead of broadband wireless. That said, front desk staff were extremely welcoming. Service in general not bad, but instead of paying people to hit the elevator buttons, upgrade the bathrooms and give guests free Internet! Compared to its 5-star peers, the Pierre is a hotel coasting on an past reputation. Glad I wasn't paying.

“Would stay again...” The hotel is in a great location and was a wondeful respite after a long day. Very close to excellent restaurants and of course the Polaris Mall. The gentleman who checked us in had the right balance of friendliness, helpfulness, and professionalism. We loved our room. Very clean, spacious and comfortable beds. If I had to make one suggestion, it would to be to put a curtain between the sink area and the bedroom. We saw this feature in Europe and in Disney and it really helped to block out the light if another person(s) remained sleeping while another was getting ready. Will stay here again when we go back.

“Just average” I spent two weeks here while i was waiting for the closing on my apartment and the movers to show up. The hotel is walking distance to my office and has big rooms. I pretty much had issues with everything. Stained towels in the room, i had housekeeping come to see what they are putting in the rooms, after that, not one stained towel. But why were there any?? I was there for two weeks, not one person recognized me or called me by my name. The decor is fine, nothing special, pretty plain if you ask me. There was an issue with the cable at one point as they were switching providers, got a weird answer, it eventually got fixed but why was there an issue? The first time i ordered room service there were no utensils or napkins, i had to ask for it, strange. Then to top it all off. The day before i was to check out i told them that the movers had not arrived yet and that i would need to extend. The woman at reception said not a problem and to let them know the day before i needed to check out. So the next day i got a bill under my door as if i'm checking out, when i went to reception, they said they had no information about my extending. I didn't make it up, i had a conversation. I was then informed that i had to move rooms, as my room was booked. I told them that if i'm going to pack i'm going somewhere else. And i did, to a much nicer, friendlier, welcoming beautiful hotel!!! Hotel Giraffe!! I spent $4000 here!! Not a very good welcome to NY!!

“Updated rooms nice amenities” This hotel looks like it has been recently updated. The rooms are swanky There are complimentary apples and bottled water everywhere. The rooms are quiet (though I stayed mid week and don't think the hotel is very full). The fitness center is spectacular. However they claim a "lap pool". It is about 25 feet by 5 feet - skinny and really small. Not great for laps but ok for hanging out. They don't have wireless in the rooms yet which is a drag if you have two people with two computers. You have to plug in. But wireless on the first and second floors.

“"I'll be at the Roosevelt"” I stayed at The Roosevelt at the end of October, during my birthday trip to New York and I absolutely loved it. I had a corner suite with a view on Madison and 46. I was curious to see how the hotel felt, especially after seeing it featured in "Mad Men", where the main character says, "I'll be at the Roosevelt". Indeed, when you enter in that beautiful lobby, you feel the class of a long-gone era. The position is great... steps away from the Grand Central, for those who like public transportation. For those like me, who prefer the "walking + taxi" combo, it was great. I walked everywhere - to Central Park for jogging, to Rockefeller Centre, to Broadway for my show and only took a cab to go see the 9/11 Memorial. To answer to the few negative comments below... Yes, the bathroom is small, but it's clean. It's not a modern room, but the beds are new and it is really spacious, not only by New York standards. The service was excellent and the front desk staff extremely nice and polite. I have been working in travel business for 10 years and I have no reserve to recommend this hotel.

“One of Philadelphia's Finest” Ritz-Carlton has once again exceeded our expectations, with their truly outstanding Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia property. Contrary to several reviews on this site, we were pleasantly surprised to see that Ritz-Carlton was holding true to their reputation as one of the world's finest hotel companies. The Philadelphia property is historic, and delivers service on the highest level. The property is housed in an historic banking building, consisting of two structures: the Rotunda and a connecting high rise. The Rotunda is where you will the hotel's lobby, check-in and restaurant facilities. The adjacent high-rise is also historic, and houses each of the 300 guest rooms. We reserved a standard room with two double beds with Club Level access. The hotel was nice enough to reserve an xx16 Room for us, which apparently is quite oversized compared to the standard rooms.
