These "sixteen" rooms are located on each floor next to the stairwells. Guest rooms were well appointed, with all of the standard Ritz-Carlton amenities. The beds were heavenly as always, featuring divine mattresses and featherbeds. Rooms feature 42' LCD flat panel televisions. Our bathroom was wonderful, and featured a glass enclosed shower, and separate soaking tub. Bvlgari toiletries were all included. Club Level access was well worth the additional charge, as it featured five daily food presentations on the 30th floor, overlooking all of Philadelphia. The lounge itself is housed in what was once the bank's boardroom. The room is wood paneled, and reflects the historic nature of the hotel. Breakfast, afternoon snacks, tea service, evening hourdurves and dessert were all included. Service was impressive throughout, and typical of Ritz-Carlton. We were consistently greeted by staff members, and felt at home during our stay. The hotel is located in the center of downtown, and is only a short walk from the city's major shopping areas, historic sites and major corporations. Walnut Street is Philadelphia’s “5th Avenue” and is just one block from the hotel. The hotel is also about a fifteen minute drive from the airport. I would highly the Ritz-Carlton Philadelphia, as it lives up to its name, and delivers a unique experience which reflects the local history. I hope that this hotel begins to earn the rating it deserves, five stars.

“Okay stay - but not great.” Having never stayed at a St. Regis hotel before, we really did not know what to expect. Hotel was nice, but not our cup of tea. Classy, quiet hotel located in a residential area. Rooms at the back of the hotel face train tracks - we heard the train a few times - but really was not a problem. I only mention this because we thought it was odd that a 5-star hotel was built so close to the tracks - a bit strange. The design of the hotel includes faux balconies - with floor to ceiling windows that are sealed shut - a disappointment as we both enjoy sleeping with the window open. Small outdoor pool that was not heated - another disappointment. Shower / tub combo (no separate shower) did not drain well - was standing in water up to my calves! No ice machines or in-room coffee. Odd how 5 star hotels exclude these necessities. I hate having to call room service for a bucket of ice! Hotel staff was extremely friendly and professional. Valet remembered my name each and every time. Was originally built as a Ritz Carlton - I wonder if any thing has changed since being rebranded as a St Regis a few years back.

“Wonderful Hotel-"It's all about the view"” Intercontinental Hotel, Century City. Formerly Park Hyatt. We took the scenic drive from Burbank Airport- through the streets, passing through Cahuenga, Highland, Sunset Boulevard, La Cienega, then Santa Monica Boulevard. We passed Trader Vics, Dan Tanas, The Troubador, The Roxy, The Beverly Hilton, and many other famous venues. Pricey $ 25.00 a day mandatory valet parking -no self parking here. Soaring modern indoor glass atrium with all marble lobby.Gracious reception personnel and bellmen. Our two-room "Deluxe" overlooked the backlots of Fox Studios. Living room contained plush couch, chairs, work desk, bureau, TV credenza, minibar, and safe. Bedroom contained a very comfortable bed, dresser, and side tables. Pink marbeled bathroom is accessed through living room or bedroom, and contained a separate tub, stall shower, and upgraded toiletries. Large closet contained two robes and slippers for guest use. The balcony is adorned with a live flower basket, two chairs and a small table. We watched the sun set over West LA. Some guest rooms contained lavish outdoor patios with cushioned chaise lounge chairs, palm trees, and spectacular views. A hospitable bartender served us a few cocktails in the off-lobby Park Grill Lounge. Nice snack menu available in the lounge, with full menu in the restaurant. About a 3/4 mile walk to the Westfield Century City Mall, and to Santa Monica Boulevard. Hotel is very nice- but is somewhat "location challenged," for the guest who likes to walk to attractions. A quick 20 minute ride west on Santa Monica brought us to the pier and beach. Lovely outdoor pool and jacuzzi- with ample and comfortable seating. Overall, a good upscale experience.

“A functional hotel near Seatac Airport” Faced with every hotel in downtown Seattle full I had little choice but to book the Doubletree at Seattle Tacoma Airport. It is a big hotel with several wings and if you get a room in the tower it saves a lot of walking. Packed with retired cruise ship passengers, it took time to be checked in. Reception staff though were polite but not that efficient. I was given the wrong vouchers for breakfast (included in the room rate I ourchased). This was quickly rectified by the waitress the next morning who obtained the right vouchers for me. One obvious deficiency is no bottles of drinking water in the room. You are supposed to go to the machine on your floor and pay USD1.75 for a bottle of water, and then the machine fails to deliver the bottle! Reception however retrieved the situation quickly and put two bottles of water in my room. Good service recovery. The restaurant is far too small and at dinner I had to try and get a table at the bar. Food was quite good but service rather slow because of so many guests. Room decor is drab and boring, but overall the hotel was functional and I did get a couple of nights decent sleep.

“Wonderful Gem in University City” My husband and I stayed here this past weekend for a quick trip to Philly for our anniversary and I must say I was pleasantly surprised. I'm a native of West Philadelphia and I would like to say that this hotel is just what University City needed. The other hotel options in the area, while nice, are a bit dated. This hotel is like a breath of fresh air. This hotel is new and contains all modern, updated decor. The room furnishings are updated and the bed is super comfortable. I would like to state the only downfall is parking. There is no garage available however there is a valet service for $29 nightly. However, there seemed to be ample street parking. My husband and I both agree that this hotel will now be our "Go-To" hotel when staying in the city. You cannot go wrong with this hotel.

“Not Outstanding, But Not Bad...” My general impressions of 'Fairmont' as a hotel chain is pretty favorable. I've only stayed at one other, and the Dallas Fairmont doesn't really live up to my perceived standards of the chain. Room was fair, not outstanding, service was okay, not great. Food is definitely overpriced, albeit pretty good. I travel A LOT, and expect to pay premiums for breakfast, but it was like $30 a person for breakfast...I hate to spend $20 for breakfast as I often have to do, but $30 for the cheapest meal of the day? C'mon!

“Can't beat the location” This was my 3rd stay at this hotel (one time before remodel and two times afterward). As I have stated in my previous review, this hotel is a great location for Penn Station, Broadway, Times Square, and Rockefeller Center. If you are fit, you can pretty much walk between all of these locations from the hotel with no problems. Hotel was clean and rooms very updated. Almost a little too modern for my taste...I really dislike the 1/2 glass shower wall. Not user friendly and difficult to keep water off the floor when showering. Free internet in the rooms however, it is a bit slow. The best part of the rooms are the super comfy beds! Especially after being out and about on your feet all day, the beds are heavenly. Would recommend a stay here...great price for the location and quality of the hotel. Will stay again.

“Great value and location.” My husband and I have stayed at several Towneplace Suite properties throughout texas. This one was newer and very clean. The kitchenette was updated with nice appliances and the flooring was much improved. The rate was reasonable and the front desk staff was very accommodating. If you are looking for trendy and modern, this is not the place for you. If you want clean, great price, location to the downtown area and main attractions and a kitchenette to help with your food budget this is the place to be!

“Best Location By Far” A fantastic hotel, excellent location and good value for money in Manhattan! The breakfasts were a great way to start our day, the beds were comfy, the rooms clean & best of all the location was nothing short of superb.

“3rd visit in 2012” This was my third visit in 2012. The location is key and one of the best in the CIty. If you are coming from JFK take the Air Train to Jamaica then the E subway to 7th and 53rd. The hotel is 2 mins walk from the exit. For just $7.50 door to virtually the hotel its better than a $60 cab ride if you include tolls and tips. I stayed in an Executive Floor room which allowed access to the Executive Lounge. What a transformation! It has been moved from the 44th Floor to a brand new location on the main floor, This to my mind is a great pity as the views before were amazing. However the refurbishment is really good and for breakfast the extra space using the part of the lobby bar area is great. In the evening when they are serving canapes its a bit of a zoo to be honest. Too small, too many people. I will continue to stay for the location and the staff who are always friendly.

“Good and not so good points” So yes this hotel is a block from semi sketchiness but it's also super convenient to the Harbor, Charles St., the light rail, etc. The common areas definitely need sprucing up but the room itself was nice, big bed, good bathroom and decent products. I asked for an upper floor and had a great view. I also asked for a late check out which the very nice night guy John said was no problem (he was the best front desk person; the bellhop and some other random people were nice too). This was all being a Priceline customer too so that was cool (had a rate of $63 so can't complain). There are places to eat within two blocks on Charles St. so that person was wrong. Nice restaurant in the Hotel Monaco, Irish Pub, a couple others right on Charles. I walked to E. Saratoga past the hospital by myself and didn't worry about it. Only went to the Lexington Mkt on the west side of Charles and even on a Mon. afternoon, it's an interesting sea of humanity but nothing that worried me. Would hope to Priceline the Sheraton Harbor again but this was fine.

“Great place for a convention” Attended a 4-day meeting here. The hotel is directly on the waterfront. Ask for a room with a view. Food at the meeting was remarkably good. I also ate at the hotel restaurant, which was good but a little pricey. Room was very nice and in good repair. Appreciated the magnifying mirror in the bathroom so that I could see how to put on makeup. Front desk staff was pleasant and helpful.

“Great Value” We recently stayed in a very large King Deluxe room at the Arena Hotel for 6 nights. We had a great internet rate. We have stayed there before and will stay definitely stay there again. In addition to the reasonable room rates, we like the location & the free, clean parking area. (A few of the parking spaces are covered.) It’s a short walk to HP Pavilion and a fairly long walk or short, easy drive to downtown. Coffee is available in the lobby of the Arena Hotel all day (& there are coffee pots in the rooms) but there is also a coffee shop across the street for those who want fancier coffee drinks. There were some problems with our room – a very slow draining tub, extremely low TV volume & a “temperamental” TV remote. We didn’t report the problems until we left so I don’t know how they would have handled these problems if we had reported them during our stay. The room seemed a little dark during the day & the lighting over the couch isn’t really good for reading but there is plenty of light for reading in bed. We like having a microwave oven & fairly large refrigerator in addition to the free breakfast. We have never tried the free dinner. We didn’t use the Jacuzzi tub but the shower head has a lot of pressure. We stayed there during extremely hot weather. The air conditioning unit kept the room cool but, because the room was so large, it was definitely cooler near the unit. The unit only had one fan speed which was quite high & fairly loud. That was fine during the day but it would have been nice to have a low fan speed during the night. Overall, I think the Arena Hotel is a great place to stay.

“Good stay at Millenium Hilton” I stayed at this hotel with my wife and 17 month old daughter from July 20-22. The hotel rooms have clearly been renovated recently and they've added some nice touches. The bed was very comfortable and the large flat screen t.v is built into the wall. The bathroom was nicely renovated and decorated as well. We had a room on the 20th floor over looking the World Trade Center site. Although, it is not the most pleasant of memories, I the view was a good reminder of all that happened that day. I booked the hotel through priceline and got a great rate and a great room. I even requested to be moved initially because the original room they gave me was too close to the elevators. I was moved without a problem. The front desk staff were courteous and helpful. The location of the hotel is perfect is you're looking to be in the SOHO/Financial district and close to the Hudson River. It's only about a 10 minute walk to the river. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Typical Embassy Suites” I got a little worried when we went to check in at the front desk. This area is in need of sprucing up. The rooms appear a little bigger than other Embassy Suites. The flat screen TVs were a definite plus. The morning breakfasts were good, although some of the other Embassy Suites have fresh fruit. The manager's reception, as usual, was a great way to unwind from a long business day. Then the short ride of thge Red Line on the Metro Line to downtown DC was convienient. I didn't get to check out the neighborhood, but it looked decent enough. I did frequent Whole Foods and the Cheese Cake Factory both located inside the Chevy Chase Pavillion with the Embassy Suites.

“Second visit to this hotel, still good, better for families than business however” This was my second visit to this hotel for business and while it is convenient, offers a nice breakfast buffet, is clean and generally up to date, it is better suited for families than a business trip. The room lighting is a bit dim and cell service is difficult at best. Rooms are spacious and clean, although the bathrooms are tiny. Service is good. I'd still recommend it.

“The rooms are just too small” I had a difficult time deciding on the number of stars. In many ways this is a five star property - especially in regards to service. Everyone we encountered was absolutely delightful, smiling and helpful. However, the room is just too darned small. I was traveling on business but with my 13 year old and we had a king room. There is just enough room for the bed and side tables and nowhere to sit besides the bed and the desk chair. Even if you sat on the bed to watch tv it was uncomfortable as the picture on the wall is hung low so your head will be pushed forward. Normally we enjoy room service but we didn't even try (besides some coffee) as there was just nowhere to eat. The bathroom, on the other hand was large and spacious and gorgeous. The pool area is tiny and not very attractive. We were on the 8th floor and the noise from the street was very loud even through the double paned windows. This was especially annoying when some group across the street was picketing and every car that drove by honked at them. Not relaxing. Bonus for my teenager - the American Idol contestants were staying at the hotel and we had several sightings.

“Wrong Room!” We are locals who booked two night stay and ended up checking out within 1 hour of checking in. We had a two night gift certificate (for king/queen room) that we won at a charity silent auction. I called the front desk to book the stay and asked if we could pay additional charge for upgrading to a one-bedroom suite. The girl taking the reservation said not a problem - for an additional $159 we could do that - so I agreed and booked. Two days before checking in I called the hotel to confirm our reservation of the one-bedroom suite and was told they had us in the system. When we checked in that afternoon, the girl at the front desk was very nice and upon giving her my 2 night certificate, i mentioned that we has booked a one-bedroom suite for the additional charge and she said the room was ready. We got to the room and opened the door and were shocked to find a small (and I mean small) room with a king bed and a small chair jammed in the corner - there was no living area, just the small room (this seemed to be a bedroom for one of the suites - not a complete one-bedroom suite or even a studio suite). I called the front desk and let them know there might have been a missunderstanding - she assured me this was a suite that we booked. We ended up going back down to the front desk and asked again if there was an actual suite she could move us to and she said she was extremely busy with other check-ins and we would have to wait - well we didn't - it was clear there was no way we were going to get any help and we asked to just check out and we'd use the certificate another time - she was not to busy to give the certificate back and send us on our way. I will try and set this up again later in the summer - but don't expect much better - however, as I said, we were willing and actually were going to pay for the upgraded suite from our free certificate - that's not the issue, the issue is, we were going to pay $159 (plus our cert. worth $100) - but not for a small king room. We went just down the street to the Hotel Indigo Riverwalk and easily booked a King Studio Suite (corner extra large room) for the same rate $159!! I know this review won't matter to most who are coming to San Antonio for business or vacation - just remember for those who are booking a suite or studio suite - be sure to have a back-up plan.

“Great hotel near the airport!” Only had to stay at the hotel for a night, but the staff at this hotel made my stay great! I checked in late and was provided a nice snack pack as a gold member, which is something that I have NEVER received from any of my other stays Doubletree stays. Kevin at the front desk was really helpful and very friendly as well, he greeted me and let me know if I needed anything to be sure to call. I was a little surprised that I had to walk outside to get to my room, and that all of the room entrances were outside, but when I walked into the room it was well worth the trip. The suite hotel affords you great space, a fridge, sitting area, 2 desks, 2 tvs and a microwave. I slept comfortably and thought that the breakfast which was included was great for the price paid for the hotel. When staying at the airport I will choose this hotel going forward.

“Extremely Disappointed” Unfortunately our guestroom was located above the outside exit of the hotel lounge. When the club let out early Monday morning, we were startled awake from the loud, obnoxious people outside. There was no soundproofing in the windows, so we heard everything. We heard the screaming, a fight that broke out, drunk people yelling, extremely loud bass from a car that rattled our room, and when the police arrived. The police presence did little to calm the crowd down, with drunk people yelling at the police. I would have liked the staff to be a bit more apologetic than they were. I also would have appreciated some sort of discount for the room, since I was kept up for about an hour and a half while these issues took place. My likelihood to stay at this hotel would be low. I would not recommend this hotel to my friends or colleagues based upon our experience. Soundproof windows are a must, especially in a hotel that sells itself as being upscale. Needless to say, I was disappointed.

“great location, little old school but nice” i feel the hotel had more cache as a ritz, right at the head of newbury but besides the name, the interior feels elegantly old school. the rooms aren't brand new but are a nice size except for the bathroom. i don't think i've ever been in a smaller bathroom, where the door bumps into the toilet without opening all the way. nice views of park, room service food is pretty good, staff in general are friendly and professional. one night our room was not made up yet at 6:30p so maybe they forgot our room on the rounds. glass doorknobs, turn-locks on the doors--things you don't see at the newer hotels anymore. walls are thin or our neighbors were esp loud people. wi-fi is paid per computer (not per room). easy to walk to newbury, copley, charles st, chinatown. gym is basic gym hotel, 24hr key access.

“Quite fine, but not top-notch” We had the pleasure of staying here in January 2004. Our Executive Suite -- 800 sq. feet -- was very attractively furnished with thoughtful touches (e.g., the bedside, dimming reading lights), an exceedingly comfortable bed, and a huge, sumptuous bathroom. There is, however, a major drawback to the layout of the Executive Suites: there is but a partial wall between the bedroom and the living room, i.e., the two rooms cannot be entirely closed off from each other so that one's sleep might very well be disturbed if another member of your party wants to work at the desk in the living room or watch television there. Also, we heard more noise in the wee hours of the morning from the next-door suite than I would have expected -- but our neighbors were apparently a bevy of bridesmaids who had partied long & hard, so your experience might be better :-) The housekeeping was excellent, but the level of service otherwise -- at the front desk, in the cocktail lounge, the dining room --was fairly indifferent. Not terrible by any means, but not as attentive as we've experienced at other high-end hotels.

“Great hotel!” I usually stay at the Full Service Marriott almost across the way from this hotel. Well for now on I will be staying at the Springhil. More room, more amenities, and less money. The room was a lot nicer than any of the other hotels I have stayed in while in Chicago. I highly recommend

“Fabulous stay!!!” Residence Inn, by Marriott, Denver City Center, was absolutely one of the best hotels (or Residence Inns) we've ever stayed in, and we have traveled frequently. The hotel is sparkling clean, and well located to downtown attractions, restaurants, and shopping. The Front Desk Staff, among them Mary, Laura, and John, each were very efficient, helpful and pleasant. Staffers were especially courteous to my husband, who had sprained his knee a week before our Denver trip. Sergio, was an excellent attendant at Breakfast and Evening Snack buffets. Food and variety were excellent, and included in our suite rate. For example, one night we had wonderful juicy big slider-burgers, with or w/o guacamole, plus accompanying sides. Hotel itself was sparkling clean, had comfortabl beds, and a great lobby for people watching. We travel to Denver periodically for pleasure, and plan to stay at this hotel from now on. In my opinion, this Residence Inn should be rated at 4+ stars.

“Very good location for L.A. trip” Came down for a two-night stay in November, and shared a double-double room with a friend. The staff was courteous and knowledgeable; even gave us two vouchers each for free drinks at either the bar or restaurant onsite. The room was clean, the toiletries were good, and the animal-print bathrooms were a funny little touch. I had work to do in the Westwood area, but also met up with friends in BH and downtown, and the location was easy enough to get where I needed. A lot of nearby areas for dining and shopping, although not right outside your hotel. Taxis are everywhere, though, so it was easy enough to catch a quick cab somewhere.

“Praise the motel - hate the location” This is a difficult review to write. The motel has been renovated and is clean, fresh and bright. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I have good things to say about the motel, but the location is horrible. It is right off the freeway and the highway noise was terrible I mean terrible. It had rained that night and may have amplified the sounds. The neighborhood is questionable. The police visited twice and over their loudspeaker told the "individual" creaping around the motel to leave the property immediately or be arrested. I feel bad for the owners of the motel. They have a nice facility, clean and well kept, but terrible location. Be sure and lock all the locks and bring your earplugs.

“Comfortable Business Stay” Stayed one short night at the Houstonian on a recent business trip, although I have stayed at the Houstonian at least one time in past for a couple nights, several years ago, also on a business trip. The Houstonian is neither downtown nor in Galleria area, but conveniently located for my business visit. The lobby is warm and inviting. Check-in was fast, friendly, and easy. The service is very good. The rooms clean and comfortable. The bed is firm and comfortable, and the room comes with good amenities. The hotel has nice property and amenities, but is reasonably priced for those of us accustomed to the northeast. I arrived very late, so simply went to bed, arose, checked out, had breakfast, and departed. Breakfast service was fast. The only potential complaint, and it is not really a complaint, is the bathroom is a bit small and crowded, but fine for a single room stay. I would stay again if on a quick business trip, but if staying longer in Houston, might consider Galleria area, for more variety of things to do outside the hotel close by.

“Informal but very nice” My wife and I spent two nights at the hotel and we both enjoyed the stay. I especially felt at home because the personnel did not wear costumes like some hotels have their bellman and valets wear; this is a fine hotel that does not make you feel that you do not belong there. It has a very nice fitness center, at no charge and open 24 hours. The location is terrific, close to museums and shopping as well as restaurants. If you want a stuffy hotel that is very formal don't come here. If you want a good time, this is the place.

“Nettes Hotel – tolle Lage!” Das Phoenix Park Hotel hat eine sehr gute Lage. Direkt an der Union Station (Bahnhof) gelegen, ist Mall ist in Laufdistanz. Bis zum Kongress sind es nur wenige Meter, das Weiße Haus ist mit der U-Bahn und zu Fuß gut zu erreichen. Das Gebäude ist schon etwas älter, die Lobby und der Aufzug eher klein. Der erste Eindruck war bei uns nur mittelmäßig. Das Zimmer ist im typischen US-Stil gehalten und relativ klein. Wir waren mit der Sauberkeit zufrieden. Das Personal war sehr nett und hilfsbereit.

“Very good hotel in Fisherman's Wharf” This hotel is 2 blocks walk from Fisherman's Wharf. It's in a very convenient location for restaurants and also for public transport and tours as most tours start in Fisherman's Wharf. The hotel itself has a restaurant. I ate lunch there and it was great food. price wise it's not too bad. A little on the expensive side for what the food is, but it's in the touristy area, so that's to be expected. The hotel itself was clean and seemed to be well looked after and the concierge was very helpful. I had asked for a quiet, non-smoking room, which is what I received. However my room was on the same level as the pool, and I think if it had been summer, my room would not have been so quiet. The room was clean and I saw no signs of damage. The bed was comfortable and there were plenty of pillows. The aircon/heating could be heard, but for me it was not a problem as I am used to "white noise" while sleeping. I had only a couple of "gripes". Firstly, I put the "privacy" tag on the door after my first night as I did not need new towels or anything done in the room, however when I got back from the tour I was doing, housekeeping had been in, removed all the towels, moved a lot of my stuff, left the curtains open (which I actually did not realise at first when I walked in the room and I had started to get changed when I realised - luckily no one was in the pool!) and this made me feel very uneasy. I did speak to reception about it, and it was fixed for the next day. Also, I paid cash when I checked in and also paid the $13 a day for internet, but when i tried to use the internet it wouldn;t work. I called reception and the man at reception was telling me I had not left a deposit. I had to explain three times that I had paid cash when I checked in because he kept saying I had to use my credit card. After telling him the third time, he put me on hold and checked it out. He then apologized and said he could see I had paid already and he patched me through to internet support to get me set up. I just don;t know why I had to explain 3 times that I had already paid before he went to check it out instead of him just saying they needed my credit card and that I had not paid. Otherwise, I did like the hotel. It was convenient and clean and that is what I want in a hotel.

“Ridiculously outstanding!” Was stuck in Chicago for a few days due to a huge storm in Denver - booked my room through Starwood Preferred Guest and from the moment I entered the lobby, I knew I was in for an experience. Exceptional customer service by all staff. The small touches are what I noticed at the W ... a real person instead of a recording for the wake up call ... staff noting their names and indicating that I could call them personally for any needs ... an attentive concierge with great suggestions ... turndown service on request .... Just wonderful. Hip, trendy lobby scene - rooftop bar is a little crowded and small, but the views from 33rd floor were likely stunning. Since I was traveling alone, I far preferred the "Living Room" lobby bar. Less clubby. Better people watching. My 23rd floor lakeview room featured a luxurious shower - a deluge from above! A perfect weekend that could have been spent at a regular, boring, chain turned into an adventure to remember. Absolutely, stay at the W Lakeshore.

“Modern, New, Buisiness oriented” Stayed here for two nights (Saturday and Sunday) attending meetings with banks in the area. Location is very good for business, but if you’re here in vacation I wouldn’t recommend it (go for midtown instead). The hotel is brand new, it used to be Embassy Suites, also from Hilton, so all the rooms are... suites, with separate sitting/work area with flat screen, sofa, desk, plugs, bar, Nespresso machine. Then the bathroom is not huge, but very sleek. Again, brand new. The room is really fine, with very comfortable bed, decent size closet and large flat screen. It is also very quiet, and if you’re too sensitive, a couple sliding doors can make it even more isolated from the central atrium. The roof-top bas was closed; the gym is average and breakfast as expensive as expected. Business center is very comfortable and equipped. Definitely recommend it for business in downtown.

“Hot tub time machine - this hotel is trapped in 1987. Horrible.” The positives: Decent location Staff was pretty friendly Restaurant downstairs had a good breakfast Reality: Complete dump. This decor....is from late 80's to early 90's. The sink counters in the bathrooms would hit Frodo Baggins at the knees. I am looking at a console 19" television that is AT LEAST 15 years old....and difficult to see from the bed. The bedside alarm clock has a CD PLAYER! The hotel website touts that the fitness center was "remodeled in 1997".....EXACTLY. It is 2010. Parking is $23 per day across the street in their lot. The bed is just as old as the rest of the hotel......with the firmness of a king size tortilla....which makes the guest a non sleeping, grumpy insomniac human burrito. Oh hey....let's allow dogs in our hotel. Seriously....the WORST facility I have ever stayed in for business. I can't recommend stearing clear of this place with your OWN money.....more strongly. Horrible hotel....for $120.....which was our convention discounted rate.....you can find, literally, 100 hotels nicer in the San Antonio area for that price or LESS!

“Enjoyed every minute of my stay” Stayed at the Hotel Angeleno April 17-19 for business. The hotel is located close to I-405. There is free valet parking and high speed internet which was a great savings as valet parking and cost $36/night and internet at $14.95/night at the other hotel where I stayed at less than 10 minutes away. (Hyatt Century City) The valet and front desk staff were courteous. The hotel had a complimentary 1 hr wine reception from 5:30PM inside the lobby. I was in room 1400 which was facing directly onto I405. The noise didn't bother me at all. I thought the shower stall was great. There were bathrobes and extra towels. The mini bar was stocked, (manual system so you can move the items around to make room for your own drinks) The restaurant on the top floor had great views. I had drinks and food at the bar on both nights, and had breakfast on both mornings. Price was reasonable. Around $12 for most breakfast selections. Please note that coffee and juices are $4 which is a bit steep. There is complimentary tea and coffee in the guestrooms. The free internet in the rooms was decent for emails and webrowsing. There is an option to pay for faster speeds but unless you wil be having video conferencing or downloading large files, the free interenet is sufficient. There is also a business center where each guests are allowed 15 minutes of internet time per 24 hours. The pool was nice and there was a small coffee shop where you can buy some food and drinks to consume by the pool. There is no fast food places within half a mile. There was a small commercial complex about a mile away where the hotel suggested a bakery where I bought some cupcakes and tiramisu for some clients. Location was great, along Sunset and I-405. Great service, and unbeatable value. (150s with free parking and internet) Great to use as a base, but please note that you will need your car if you want to go sightseeing or get something to eat as there are no stores or shops within half a mile.

“Grand hotel, great location, lots to do....” We enjoyed our stay at this grand hotel right in the middle of the city and very convenient to all the shopping and downtown attractions. We went for a conference and were very surprised by this grand property. The service and front desk staff were very professional and accommodating. You could not ask for a better location as mentioned. Sometimes you can get a good deal for your stay even here like we did. The rooms were older looking but comfortable. The parking was expensive so don't bring a car. Overall a very pleasant stay and one that I would recommend to any Chicago traveler.

“Would be a good value - if not for internet charges” You get a nice (if generic) little kitchenette in the room, a nice bed, and a decent TV. The staff was friendly. But, if you're going to market yourself to a business clientele, you better not charge for wireless. Period. And the fact that the phone didn't work for dial-up reeked.

“Decent room, terrible elevators” On Tuesday morning I waited 17 minutes for an elevator. That is not a typo. 17 minutes. I would have been late for a business meeting had I not known that the elevators were terrible and given myself some extra time. The rooms are decent, there are plenty of food options and the location is in the middle of downtown. Just be prepared that there are certain things - horrible elevators, shoddy wifi, bland furnishings - that make this a hotel I would not want to return to.

“Good experience” This hotel is right in the heart of downtown SF, between Market and Union Square. Nice hotel with a boutique atmosphere and excellent service. The rooms are perfect for a solo traveler. Only downside was not much counter space in the bathroom, but nothing else to complain about here. The bed was really comfortable, good technology in the room, comfortable furniture, and nice amenities.

“An unconventional, yet delightful stay!” I must admit - I'm a fan of the Biltmore....from the Wright-inspired architecture, to the beautiful grounds and relaxing pools. My recent stay in August was a particularly nice surprise, replete with small touches - an upgraded room with a private balcony in the Garden Wing, attentive staff, and a promotional rate that essentially zeroed out the resort fee. Honestly, my only complaint? The pool was warm. It's the desert. In August. If there was a way around it, I'm sure they'd have come up with it. I can't wait to go back.

“Great hotel. Very nice. Excellent Location” This hotel is remodeled. It is excellent. The doors are somewhat old, but the infrastructure--bathroom, beds, etc.---have been remodeled. The elevators can be slow during "rush" hours, but otherwise, they were very reasonable. The location is just across the street from the Art Instittue of Chicago. Overall, this is a very nice hotel, and I was very pleased with it.

“Great” I bid a room on Priceline and got the Hotel Monaco. The staff of the hotel was EXTREMELY helpful from directions, telling about hotel services, etc. Very friendly... The were a nice change of pace from the typical hotel these days. Nice to have free Wi-fi. I found the location to be great.

“Clean with OK breakfast” Two blocks down from the Union sq, also a couple of blocks away from China town. Safe and comfortable area for walks any time. Room size was great for one person, but two migh struggle a bit. Don't expect views as the rooms are facing sideways. Coming from England it definitely has some old fashioned british charm, the only real issue i had with the hotel was the smell in the main lobby. Otherwise as long as you don't expect miracles and are realistic about hotels in the area, a good and affordable place to stay in Frisco. If you want a transfer to the international airport the hotel will organise this for you for $14, bargain!!!

“"Everything you need on the inside"” I was unlucky enough to have picked up some kind of cold or flu over the Labor Day holiday and wound up spending more than a little time indoors. This hotel is a huge infrastructure, and I was glad the desk could muster me through quickly. I bought a couple of bottles of chilled spring water from the hotel gift shop. Then I headed to my 6th floor room with my rollerbag. I jumped on top of one of the double beds and dozed until 7pm. I had seen a Boston Market in the neighborhood and thought I'd just stick my head out into the fresh air for a minute. At the valet station, one of the guys took a look at me and actually ran to get my car. This turned out to be the case the rest of my visit -- the guys seemed to like me. The next morning at 4am, a relative called me and asked that I fly to Denver. By 4:45am I as back at the valet station asking for my rental car again (I've since been informed the Radisson has an airport shuttle). I was back at 9pm and stopped at an all-night drug store for bath salts and a bath brush and spent the next couple of hours in the bath tub. As a matter of fact, during the rest of my visit, I saw very little of the hotel but the inside of my room and the valet station at the front door. I can vouch for the valets -- they are the nicest people I have ever met. The front desk people were efficient and treated me well. The 6th floor had recently been renovated, and the rooms there were cozy and comfortable. I will return here when I have the chance.

“Beautiful Older Hotel” This hotel is a little on the older side and the rooms are on the small side but that is true for most of NYC. I stayed here for NYE and my first trip to the big apple. The location is perfect for sight seeing or a pleasure weekend. As for the staff I rate them 9/10 they did a really nice job and were attentive to any of my needs. I did have an issue with a toilet not flushing in my original room. I called the front desk and they sent someone to fix it and quickly moved us to an even nicer room. I really enjoyed the decor of the hotel, it was old but very classy and clean, some parts of the hotel definitely are showing wear, but I actually liked that about the place. Bathrooms are smaller than most modern hotels to if that is an issue. Overall it was a great stay and I would recommend it to anyone.

“Functional, but not spiffy!” A few months ago, I reviewed a hotel near Princeton that had this strange, sort of sterile (but not in a clean sort of way) institutional sense about it. I would have to say, this property had many of those same traits. It wasn't bad. Nor was it dirty. It just wasn't spiffy. In fact, it sort of felt like a ... University hotel! The best decision we made was to upgrade by $20 for the club level (or whatever they call it,) which meant we got a VERY nice continental breakfast for the cost of a tip. Eggs, cereal, fruit, Starbucks coffee. We left feeling very satiated, and the desk staff was certainly kind and helpful. Weird, but safe neighborhood. (Near University of Pennsylvania, with some trendy neighborhoods nearby, but you're not quite actually IN one.) Would stay again if the price were right.

“Nice LAX Airport Hotel” Stayed 1 night prior to next day flight, upgraded to suite on 8th floor, had a nice feel to it, kind of like a corner room with bed off to a secluded area and separate seating area. Bathroom was a bit old school and tight where you have to shut to door to use the bowl. It is a shame that these older properties doen't get updated bathrooms because this is all the craze these days! Gym was perfect! Pool looked very inviting as well, didn't need to eat in house as I had access to club lounge, overall this is a nice perperty and I would no doubt stay here again.

“Small and Lousy” I got this hotel on Priceline. Now I understand why they have to sell rooms at such a discount. Despite being a Kimpton (I've stayed at the Palomar and the Monaco before and loved them), this was one of the worst hotels I've ever visited. The rooms are impossibly small, so small that Stuart Little might find the room cramped. Dominating the rooms is an enormous armoire (apparently, the letters "L-C-D" have not reached the ears of the management). These rooms are not "cool-small" like a New York hotel, either. They're just small. If one is lucky, one might get a tiny window with 6 feet of clear view to another window. My room had a view of netting used to keep pidgeons away, although there were several pidgeons roosting there. I felt like The Birdman of Alcatraz. This hotel was disappointing in every way one measures a hotel.

“Typical full-service Marriott” This was a typical full-service Marriott. It's right by the convention center, so would be a good pick if you were attending a conference there. Downtown San Jose has lots of restaurants and entertainment within walking distance. I was visiting a customer, and needed a car. Parking is in the public convention center garage and was an outrageous $20 per night. Marriott should work on getting a discount, especially since the garage was practically empty all 5 nights of my stay. I guess they want the extra $6 they can charge for valet parking. That's a mess, too - the circular drive isn't large enough to accomodate the arriving cars and taxis. I'm a frequent Marriott guest, so had concierge lounge privileges. The lounge had a nice outdoor patio, but I wasn't impressed by the "amenities".

“Not bad for a short trip” I got a cheap deal on priceline & reading some of the other reviews I was a bit concerned but I had a pleasant stay here. I was given a room away from the busy road without having to ask & although the room furniture was looking a little dated it was comfortable. The hotel is handy for the ferry to Bainbridge Island as well as other tourist places in Seattle such as Pike's Place Market & Pioneer Square. Free coffee was available in the lobby in the morning & later free hot cider was gratefully received as it was snowing outside. The restaurant was fine - nothing fancy, but good attentive service. I stayed on a weekend which may mean it was cheaper & less busy (hence nice quiet room without request etc) than during the week. I would stay here again - especially at these bargain priceline rates.

“Will keep coming back” This was my 4th stay at HRC, and my first as a Gold Passport Diamond. I change my reservation to one that had the AAA and FREE VALET-probably the best deal i've seen here, and better than the AAA free breakfast if you have a car. Regency Club is average compared to others, an usually quite crowded. Room was good with a great view of Michigan Avenue on the 25th floor of the West tower. I must have had the same room as a previous poster, as I did not have a trash can in the room. I requested it 3x to no avail. I finally got one on my 4th request when a housekeeper came by thinking I had asked to clean my room. She brought me a trash can, albeit quite beat up, but it did the trick. I realize in a large hotel like HRC it's hard to be perfect. I'll be back next month.

“Another excellent Kimpton hotel” I have stayed at the Alexis and Kimpton's near-by Monaco and these are both really great hotels. The Alexis shines in the areas that Kimpton Hotels do so well: excellent staff service; rooms with stylish decor that distinguish them from average hotel rooms; and great on-site restaurants. The Alexis is located closer to Pike Street market and the water than the Monaco. The Monaco's restaurant is larger. The Monaco is slightly more expensive. Whether you choose the Alexis or the Monaco, its hard to go wrong with either hotel.

“Nice Hotel close to the airport” Stayed hear one night after arriving at the airport. Clean, up to date. room with a nice balcony. very close tot he airport, but does not feel that way. Staff very helpful and friendly. Restaurant / bar in the lobby had great staff and good food.

“wow - what a deal” we took a package here for room & couples massage -- price was exceptional when you consider all that got thrown in ... above & beyond .... massages were very good, spa okay, but personnel down there were excellent.....my only complaint and this is my biggest w/many hotels is the sound when the heat or a/c kicks on & off during the night....i'm a light sleeper and it would keep waking me, my wife is a heavy sleeper, she didn't even notice......so bring earplugs if you're a light sleeper...otherwise an exceptional beautiful place in the heart of historic area that treated us like royalty

“A great deal for SF lodging with excellent service” This Holiday Inn transcends its surroundings with great service. Getting off BART from SFO late one Saturday evening at Civic Center was not reassuring, but the hotel is only a block away and the walk was safe. Things looked better when I entered the dated but clean lobby. Benny at the front desk went to great lengths to get me a smoking room, even to going up and checking the room first: impressive service indeed! The room was clean with new carpet and dated, but not unpleasant decor. The bed was thankfully on the firm side (and there's a pillow menu...at a Holiday Inn? amazing). Bathroom was half-updated with old fixtures but all was working well and very clean. My tip to the housekeeper (you don't tip 'em? you should) was answered by an even more thorough cleaning and a lovely thank-you note. Breakfast here is free to Priority Club members, and mine was served hot, quickly and with a smile. My call to request an extended checkout at 2PM was handled pleasantly and with great courtesy. Absolutely everyone I dealt with at the hotel was pleasant and smiling, and best of all quite competent. Given the slightly dicey area of the hotel, the reason to stay here is the outstanding customer service (and the great rates compared to other properties in the city). Not only would I stay here again, I would recommend this place to other budget-conscious travelers looking for a clean comfortable room at a well-run downtown SF hotel.

“Could be so much better!” Just one night so could manage. But a great price! Halls are dark and weird. Rooms are a shoe box for real. Bathrooms are okay, new. BUT things are not clean! Just vacuum and dust. Housekeeping needs to step it up. Yes, some floors are rehabbing but our whole floor was due. Clean up well, and will put up with small rooms. TV nice but only on HD channels? No coffee in room....no place to put...All things could be better...
“Omni OK” Dated facility. Pleasant staff. Nothing to write home about. Barely worth writing a review.

“Great accomodations in an incredible location” This is the second year in a row I've stayed at this property, and while both experiences were good, this one stands out. The location is outstanding. The hotel is on Mission Bay and Mission Beach is a 5 minute walk away. Sea World is less than a 10 minute drive. We stayed in a one bedroom bay front patio suite. It was HUGE and recently redecorated. The living room had a great sectional couch, large (42" I think) LCD TV, desk, table with two chairs and even two real plants! The carpet was newer. There were large sliding glass doors leading out to a patio with two lounge chairs. Mission Bay was right outside the room and the beach was about 15' from our patio. The bedroom was large and had a separate LCD TV. The bed was comfortable and the linens were clean and fresh. The entry, kitchenette and bathroom had glazed porcelain tile floors. The kitchenette had a nice pass through to the living room and featured a large refrigerator, cooktop, sink and coffee maker. Although we didn't take advantage, they provide microwaves on request. We did not eat at the restaurant, but did get to enjoy the pool and hot tub on a few occasions. Both were clean and not too crowded. In fact, both the pool and hot tub seemed very large and there are plenty of lounge chairs to use in the area. The room and the grounds (beautiful landscaping) were well maintained and clean. I'd recommend the hotel to anyone and will definitely stay again next year!

“Really great hotel” I stayed here because of its proximity to a work conference. The room was well appointed, very comfortable, and spotlessly clean. The beds were very comfortable too. When it comes to service, I have no complaints. The desk staff and concierge were pleasant and helpful. Although I was not on the conference rate (the room was cheaper if I booked it myself), the desk clerk gave me free wireless access when she heard I was with the conference. This was very nice of her, but you know, I'm sick of hotels charging for this. The location was good. The convention center, decent restaurants and Pike Place Market were all within walking distance. I would definitely stay here again. I only have two complaints and they are minor ones. The first has to do with the lights. In order to keep them on, you have to put the key card in the wall by the door. It's awkward. The second has to do with the bathroom door. I don't know what interior designer started the trend for translucent doors, but it's not a very practical trend if you're sharing the room.

“Great Service, Lovely Room, Perfect Location” Stayed three nights in March 2012. Very pleasant stay at this hotel. Room was on the small side, but not unusual for NYC. The room was on the 14th floor, with a king size bed (very comfortable) and the room had all the amenities and it was very clean. Clean, well appointed bathroom (small too) water pressure in the shower could have been better. I was concerned about hearing traffic noise, but it turned out to be a very quiet. Slept very well. The staff was absolutely superb, courteous, helpful and knowledgeable. Elevators were great, fast and reliable. Location of the hotel was great, just a few minutes walk to Grand Central Station and then you could get anywhere in the City within minutes. I got this hotel with Priceline, the staff never made me feel less for having gotten the room through Priceline, like I have experienced at other properties in the City.

“Great hotel, perfect location, good rooms” Great located, around the corner of Times Square. Good size rooms, small bathroom however. Breakfast is good and not expensive. Very good price-quality ratio. Free Wifi!

“Great hotel in a great location.” A well maintained hotel in a convenient location. Near The Plant (a shopping center with Target, restaurants for every budget, etc). SJ Fairgrounds walking distance away. Off the main drag, so a bit more peaceful, and layout shades cars from San Jose hot sun. Spacious room. Room clean, nice. Standard Hampton breakfast. Oreos on arrival a nice touch.

“more than happy stay at the Hyatt Regency” 2 nights/3 days spent in Chicago on business, staying at the Hyatt Regency. The service throughout my stay was impeccable. The check in desk was very busy when we arrived (the hotel does seem to cater to large conferences) so the conceirge desk checked us in. The rooms are spacious, climate controlled, comfortable, and VERY quiet when you consider how busy the hotel was. I didn't dine in the hotel apart from breakfast (average) but both bars on the 1st and 2nd levels were fine - the Big Bar in particular was very busy/buzzy with spectacular views and a great atmosphere. I don't think this is a quiet-getaway kind of place but then why would you be going to a busy City if that's what you wanted. Also, the location is fabulous, steps from the Magnificent Mile. Thank you Hyatt Regency for a wonderful stay.

“Great Location” We were first time visitors to Washington DC and wanted a location central to the main attractions around the Mall, White House, museums, monuments etc, and found exactly what we were looking for in this hotel. You have to be crazy to drive in Washington with the constant traffic jams, not to mention rich with the very high parking charges. So the central location of this hotel in walking distance to all the attractions was first class. In addition they are opposite a metro station which we took the three stops to visit Arlington. The price was reasonable for a central location and the room more than adequate for our needs. It was fitted with king bed, fridge, micro wave and safe. The view was not great but as we planned to be out all day that was off secondary importance. The concierge staff are very knowledgable and willing to share with you where to go, where to dine etc, without being pushy. They will also make phone calls for you, as in our case to check up on the whereabouts of the shuttle we had ordered to take us back to the airport. Check in and out was speedy and they were good enough to give us a later check out to accommodate our time to go to the airport with no fuss or charge. Our package included breakfast which consists of the usual buffet and also omelette station. We ate at their restaurant one night, and it was very good. There is a happy hour each evening with cut priced drinks, and they also supplied hot apple juice ( they called this cider but it is nothing like the cider in the UK) and cookies free of charge. Coffee, apples and newspapers are also provided free. They also have a small gym and indoor swimming pool. Not massive but enough for a holiday workout. Could find no fault with it so recommend if you are looking for something similar as we have described then go for it.

“Buono” Posizione ottima per potersi muovere a piedi. La nostra stanza devo dire che era piccolina come vedrete dalle foto, ma confortevole. Erogatori d'acqua sul piano, gratis. Personale ok. Posso solo dire che lo consiglio vivamente. Buona Vacanza!

“Near Everything (Including the Train)” This is mid-sized well run hotel in the middle of the action in downtown San Diego. It's a short walk to the convention center in one direction and the Gaslamp District in the other direction. Also, I could see Petco Park outside my window--you guessed it, a few blocks away. All in all, the stay was very satisfying. I had an end room with a very nice view. The only downside (probably true of any hotel in the immediate area) was the passing train traffic making a commotion quite often throughout the day. Were I not a good sleeper, it would have been a more significant problem. Service was prompt, pleasant and very good. While there were some convention meetings going on at the hotel, it was much less busy than the larger Hilton and Marriott that also tend to serve the convention crowd. All in all, this was a good choice.

“Extremely nice, comfortable hotel - great value” I got the Hilton Garden Inn on a Priceline deal during a quick business trip to Houston. I've never stayed at a Hilton Garden-Inn, but had a great night at this Houston location. The HGI in general was extremely clean, very well decorated, and had a nice lobby and lounge and breakfast area. My room was huge, really huge, including the bathroom. Although it didn't have a couch, there was a nice desk area, along with a coffee maker, microwave and refrigerator. It was very functional and comfortable, and I would stay there again.

“Wellmaintained friendly hotel” We were on a conference in the hotel. Very nice and friendly staff. Very professional treatment. clean and cosy despite the vastness. it is connected to other hotels and the mall by a skywalk which make it easyto walkaround from one place to another in cold weather without suffering. good location and nice scenery. Clean, professional and friendly place

“Better than their Center City location” Crowne Plaza has two locations in the area. The other is the run down Center City location. This location is definitely better. Conveniently located and shares a parking lot with TGI Fridays. Another decent restaurant, Houlihans, is just across the street. Lobby bar and restaurant (inside the hotel) are suitable. Large lobby, pool and free internet access in the business center with free printing. Flat screen TVs in the rooms. I always ask for double beds...so my room was very large and clean. Bathroom could use renovating. It did have a marble countertop. Comfortable beds. Free parking. I used a coupon and got my room for $89 after tax ($102). The Crowne Plaze in Center City (Market Street) has a coupon for $79 but I just couldn't stand another night in that place...after the last stay. I really didn't have any complaints due to the coupon deal. The price was right. My only complaints might be that the bathroom was small and not up to par. The hallways were very wide and the hallway carpet was nice and seemed rather new. There was no ice machine on the 6th floor and I had to get nice on the 7th floor.

“Some room problems but otherwise great” If not for the few problems encountered with the room I would give this hotel top honors. The one constant was the great service provided by the hotel staff. The Valet was prompt and courteous at all times. The front desk staff efficent, friendly and always available. The housekeeping staff ready to help and always acknowledge you when moving about the hotel. The staff at the breakfast buffet always said good morning even though they were there to merely replenish the food and had no direct guest contact. And wow, how about the breakfast buffet? That was a very pleasant surprise; everything was fresh and the presentation was outstanding. The only problems were in the room. They are starting to show a little wear and tear, on arrival the bathroom could have been cleaner, the door to the room was really hard to open and close, and the first day there was no heat in the room. Once I reported the heating problem it was immediately fixed (and I was subsequently asked twice if the heat was working by the front desk). When traveling one has to expect some small problems, but all of mine were easily overlooked because the service was outstanding and all issues immediately addressed. I would have no hesitation of staying here again.
“Great stay” I stayed overnight after a conference. The room was clean and spacious. The members of the staff were friendly. I enjoyed my stay,

“Exceeded expectations” I read all the reviews and was fairly sure that I would be happy with this hotel. I am pleased to tell you that it was far superior than I expected. Our room was very clean and updated with marble walls and granite surfaces in the bathroom as well as granite surfaces in the room itself. The shower was roomy, the water pressure high and the bed was SO comfy! I chose this hotel because I wanted a suite with two televisions so that my daughter could watch cartoons while I watched more adult-oriented fare. The television in the bedroom was a crisp flat-screen, but the second one in the living area was an older conventional style with less that stellar reception. But my daughter didn;t mind -- she was able to see her cartoons just fine. I don't know if all of the bathrooms in the hotel have sinks as low as ours was, but my daughter loved being able to use the sink herself without standing on her tippee toes. She's in kindergarten. I found it to be to low for an average sized adult, however. I used the small exercise room every day. It was equipped with a weight station, a step climber, a stationary bike and a treadmill. Although the stationary bike and the stair climber were in okay condition, all of the items in the room were a bit dated and the elevation mechanism on the treadmill was broken. There is a large TV in the room, a water dispenser, and a sauna across from the bathroom. Down the hallway is a small room with a pool table in it. The breakfast was the best I've had at a Best Western. In addition to a variety of breads, fruit and cereals, there was also single-serve wrapped english muffin and sausage sandwhiches in a warming oven along with hot, soft granola bars. We ate very well every morning. A particularly nice touch was the warm cookies that were set out for guests in the afternoon. The hotel staff were exceptionally nice. My rental car broke down as we were leaving to go to lunch. As we waited in the lobby the receptionist brought my daughter water and heated-up english muffin egg and cheese sandwich. I visit Los Angeles every year and this is the fourth hotel I've stayed at in four years. From now on I will always stay here. For just over $100 you get free high speed internet, a swimming pool, a hot tub, an exercise room, a good breakfast, free parking and nicely updated rooms with very comfortable beds -- WOW! Such value and quality at this price point just can't be beaten.

“Leaves a bit to be desired” Reading others reviews, it is obvious there is an "A" and "B" team as far as service goes. The front staff while polite were distant, as English was not their first language and they all spoke the same Eastern European one, they seemed more interested in chatting with each other, than taking care of guests. They also ignored us and avoided eye contact when we attempted to ask questions. However the bell staff and the one woman at the front whose first language WAS English were very friendly and helpful and asked if we needed help. We were told this hotel was the "top of the line" for the Hilton chain. Then why were the towels so crappy??? What do they give to dry off at the moderate Hiltons now? Paper towels?? The robes were plush, thank goodness so that was a treat. They give a "pillow menu" , how about a "towel menu" for guests that actually use the shower or bath?? Our room looked at the side of a building, so no view. The room was very nicely appointed and the bed was comfortable, the location is fantastic for sure. Just think they need to improve a bit, to live up to their claims.

“Beautiful hotel; soon downtown will sprawl out to the hotel” This is a lovely hotel. I am here now finishing a multinight stay and have enjoyed the amenities and the amazing view. The view, while lovely, is potentially the short-term problem. It is of the harbor, downtown, and the North End, all places I would like to walk around and eat and visit but are not yet close. There is clearly a lot of building going on and it is just a matter of time before this area is fully incorporated into the downtown area. Until then, there is some isolation. Ther are many benefits to being here but do know that you are not going to stroll to Quincy Market. in a moment It is a hike, a ride, or a mass transit event. With that out of the way, I sing the praises of the hotel. My room is spacious, ultra-clean, has gorgeous city and water views, is a block or two from the Convention Center, and has accommodating public spaces. You will lack for nothing here. There are many busy restaurants of all kinds in the area, and the hotel Navigator (love that rather than the pretentious "concierge") will get you someplace good to eat. It is an area still under development, and soon enough will be just an extension of the familiar downtown hustle and bustle. And when that happens, watch out. It will be a super hot spot. The bedding is of nice quality and comfortable, the flat screen TV big and new. We had a problem with a movie freezing up on us and the hotel could not have been more accommodating, eventually fixing it after we had already decided to turn in, and then slipping some Starbuck's coupons under the door as a consolation prize. That was very professional and appreciated. It is a well-run hotel. The hotel is well-soundproofed. While we are very close to the busy airport we cannot hear it at all. I am parked in a pretty expensive public lot nearby, but it was less expensive than the hotel valet by just enough to make me do it. I did not move the car during the stay because... well... I used to live in Boston and know that it is a liability rather than an assett to have to try to park a car at night downtown. There is a bus every 8 minutes or so to South Station and from there you can get just about anywhere, so you certainly are not isolated. But it is cold to wait for the bus, and cabs can be an added and unexpected expense. If I came with my family I think that we would stay here and stuff into cabs if it were winter, or enjoy what is a nice walk in warmer weather. The location is beautiful and interesting and the hotel is reasonably priced. Give it a try. Thankfully, the hotel itself is so pleasurable that it was a wonderful stay and I will come again, bring a warmer coat in cold weather, and take advantage of all it offers. Nice hotel.

“Pleasant Facilities & Service Tainted by Ethical Questions – Pay to up $150” It is hard to fault The Westin Georgetown: it is located in a clean neighborhood, the lobby is cozy, and the room is well appointed and maintained. We had little interaction with the employees – these days you can find almost any information online – but whenever we did approach, they were friendly, helpful and polite. The Westin Georgetown would have been a perfect hotel, if it weren’t misleading about its environmental impact. We’re all for protecting the environment, but we don’t condone duplicity. And here’s where the dishonesty lies: From the moment you enter the hotel, you are reminded to be more environmentally friendly. For example, you receive not just the standard notice in the bathroom about towels, but also subject to automatic turnoff of lights and air conditioning, offered cash if you refuse maid service, and reminded to use less water in the shower. But the real test of sustainability is not whether the hotel constantly reminds you to care for the environment. It is whether the hotel cares itself. Do they care about the environment only when it benefits them or do they care about the environment when it costs them money? All of these constant reminders help not just the environment but also increase the hotel’s profits: reducing the electricity bills, saving on wages, cutting on water consumption. When it costs something, does The Westin Georgetown managers care about the environment? If they do, why do they offer bottled water of the worse kind – shipped from a remote pacific island at a great environmental harm? If they must offer bottled water in every room, why not local water? If they care about the environment, have they switched to buying electricity from sustainable sources, such as wind and water? If they truly want to protect the environment, do they wash and clean using environmentally safe detergents, or do they resort to the cheap but environmentally damaging stuff? How about letting each guest know the full environmental impact of the hotel policies, rather than focus just on the most lucrative ones? We don’t condone the hotel’s environmental policies, but we did enjoy the facilities and staff. At $150 per night, it was good value, even if not ethically satisfying.

“Worth looking in to....” Booked one night on a Travelzoo promotion. Was upgraded to an executive level room with large desk, 37" LCD TV, nice amenities. Room size was excellent for midtown Manhattan. Stayed at the Waldorf at same trip and preferred the Warwick. The only negatives I had were the elevators and lobby size, but those have been mentioned. Very good location, room size and rate for the money.

“Excellent Hotel” We were booked here because I like the Drury concept of giving you the "little extras" that other hotels don't provide. Although not in downtown Austin you are only a few minutes away. [Although Austin traffic is terrible. Also, we're not used to the highway system in Texas. Weird access roads that parallel the highway.] The hotel is older and not sleek and super modern. Our room was super clean and the bathroom had been updated. Breakfast was good and the waffles were just as tasty as if we had been in a waffle restaurant. Also, the popcorn in the afternoon was great as well as the 'happy hour' buffet. It seemed to change everyday with offerings. [Swedish meatballs, egg rolls, chicken wings, salad.] The only problem we encountered was that we asked for a handicapped accessible room with roll in shower. When I called to confirm in the morning I was told that they only had one room with a roll in shower and that it was occupied. However, they had a shower chair available. When I got there DJ offered to show me the room and the shower chair. We were also offered the opportunity to upgrade to a suite for the trouble. I didn't choose the suite as it was on the second floor and we wanted a first floor room. The staff at the hotel went out of their way to make sure we were happy and also offered to call another hotel for a room if we weren't satisfied with the shower chair. All in all our stay worked out and we will choose Drury again in the future. There are plenty of restaurants and shopping nearby but be careful exiting the highway to get into the hotel if you are not used to Texas roads Can't say enough about the friendly staff and clean rooms. Laundry room on site was nice. Don't be afraid that the hotel is a little older.

“Solid New York option” I have stayed here numerous times and there's a lot to like about this hotel. It's centrally located, very handy for meetings in midtown and for hitting the shops on 5th Avenue. I struggled a bit with service this trip though. Staff on the front desk weren't as fabulous as they have been on past visits - and in some cases were downright surly (I'm looking at you, Nancy!) My Superior King room was well appointed and a great size. I'd stay here again but it would be nice to have friendlier and more helpful staff on the front desk. Concierge had a couple of shockers with restaurant suggestions but seemed genuinely contrite and eventually redeemed themselves.

“A large midtown hotel with old New York charm, you can’t beat the Waldorf” I had a wonderful four night stay at the Waldorf Astoria in early November 2011. At check in we were told that it would be about 15-20 minutes until our room was ready. She gave us a coupon for 2 free drinks and directed us to the bar across the lobby. She told us to relax with a drink and she would come over and get us when our room was ready. At 8 pm in the evening after a long day of travel a free cocktail was a wonderful surprise. Just as promised, our room was ready in 20 minutes. This level of service was above and beyond what you normally experience at a large hotel property. We had a nice sized room with a king bed on the 16 floor. By NY standards, our room was very spacious with high ceilings, a work desk, sitting chair, large closet, and large bathroom with shower tub. The room also had two large windows that opened about 4 inches each - I love a room with operable windows that allow you to get some fresh air. The room was extremely quiet – I never once heard any sound from neighboring rooms which were all occupied during our entire stay. The bed was very comfortable with soft sheets and lots of pillows. Several of the posts here talk of warn fabrics and old furniture. Our room did not have any of these deficiencies - everything was in good condition. The Waldorf is an old historic hotel with loads of old world charm. If you want a modern, sleek décor this is not the hotel for you. The lobby, halls, elevators, and common area are magnificent. In addition, the location is fantastic and provides easy access to most of New York’s major attractions. There is a Starbucks inside the hotel and as a Hilton Honors Gold member; we received a coupon for coffee, juice and a pastry for both my wife and me each morning of our stay. We also received free Wi-Fi. We did not eat at any of the restaurants at the property so I can’t speak to that. If you are looking for a large midtown hotel with old world New York charm, you can’t beat the Waldorf.

“Nice downtown hotel” So nice to have a real breakfast and truly free parking included with our stay. We would definitely visit again. Right in the center of downtown.Walking distance to everything.Great location. We had a great time.

“Brilliant choice in San Diego, great rooms and an ideal location” This hotel was a last minute booking for us. Great price for its location, which is right in the heart of everything and close to the main areas of restaurants and nightlife. The rooms are excellent, brand new, clean and modern - brilliant, friendly check-in service when we arrived and a nice touch with the courtesy call to check everything was OK with the room. Overall, we had a great night here and would definitely recommend it to others.

“gute Lage, etwas veraltet” Die Lage ist super, 2 blocks zum Kongreßzentrum, direkt neben dem Alamo und inmitten der wenigen touristischen Attraktionen der Innenstadt, neben der Riverwalk Mall und mit Ausgang zum Riverwalk. Ich hatte Glück mit einem Zimmer zur Straßenseite, besser wäre noch Blick auf den Alamo gewesen, allerdings gibt es auch Zimmer zur Innenseite des Hotels ohne Tageslicht und mit freien Einblick, wenn man die Vorhänge nicht zuzieht. Der Standard der Zimmer ist etwas veraltet, die Möbel etwas abgewohnt, und ein sehr kleines Badezimmer, bei dem man hinter die Tür kriechen muß, um in die Badewanne zu gelangen und dabei dann schon halb über die Toilette steigt. Zudem liegt das Bad ungünstig an der Rückseite des Zimmers. Weiterhin lästig aber in den USA üblich sind die geschlossenen Fenster und die bei texanischen Außentemperturen ständig laufende Klimamanlage. Ansonsten sehr freundlicher und zuvorkommender Empfang und service, außer dem Zimmerservice, bei dem täglich eine Kleinigkeit fehlte wie Coffepads nicht entfernt, Badematte nicht ersetzt oder am ersten Tag das Timmer erst auf Nachfrage gemacht. Sauberkeit allerdings exzellent. Alles in allem keine schlechtes Hotel, welches man weiterempfehlen kann.

“Absolutely loved the Westin!” When I come back to Memphis, I guarantee I'll stay at the Westin again. I loved it! I was here for only 2 nights, and I wish I could've stayed a few more. It was so clean and the beds were fabulous. Loved the style of the hotel and the rooms -- clean and modern, yet so comfortable. The Westin isn't ON Beale St., but just a block (and a short walk) away. It's also right across from FedEx Forum and the Gibson factory. My room faced Beale St., so I could hear the crowd and music at night. This didn't bother me at all, but it might bother some guests. If you think it would, I'd request a room not facing Beale St. As some other reviewers mentioned, self-parking is a few dollars less than valet, and they're in the same parking deck (next to the hotel). I can't wait to come back to Memphis and to the Westin!

“think W on a student budget” Nothing bad happened but was underwhelmed by all. There is no room service, barely food service to speak of, no newspapers for digital dinosaur preferences, push button soap dispensers in the shower that barely deliver not unlike the Y. Fine property for budget traveler I suppose.

“Not the worst...not the best.” I stayed here April 25-28. I booked a government rate two months prior and the only room category available for a government rate was a handicap/accessible room. In my note to the hotel, I made it clear that I did not need such a room. This was two months prior! Upon arrival, I was checked into a handicap room. I was not comfortable with this as someone who may truely need such a room should have it. When I went to the front desk to change the room to another one, I was told that the hotel was full. This was fine, but it tells me that my request was never read when I told them that I didn't need such a room two months prior. The room itself was okay. I was concerned that the head of the bed backed up to the elevator shaft. However, the noise was surprisingly minimal (especially compared to the screaming teenagers running the halls at night). The room was standard Sheraton...business friendly, clean, etc. There was nothing elegant about the hotel, and nothing that would detract from it either. It was okay. I ate my breakfast's at Andre's (hotel restaurant). Those too were satisfactory. A step above Denny's, but not five-start either. Again...okay. If you are not familiar with Mission Valley, you should know that you will need a car. There is very little within walking distance. The San Diego Trolley, while serving Mission Valley, is about a one and a half, to two mile walk. If I could secure a room under $100 per night, I would return here. Otherwise, I might be game to try other hotels in the area for comparison.
“WoW!!!!” It is a great place! Book it! It is in an excellent location-Back Bay.

“Great Hotel” This is a very nice hotel. The lobby is open and spacious. The check-in was courteous and quick. My room was large, clean, updated, very quiet and comfortable. Loved the location and the restaurant. Parking was easy as well. I'd definately stay there again!

“One night only...” Very close to being a Holiday Inn Express. Beds were comfortable, towels need an upgrade. Neighborhood was relatively safe and plenty of places nearby to get a meal. Check in took forever, not sure if the guy was new but it took 15-20 minutes for one room for one night.

“I couldn't have asked for more...” My sister recently came to visit from England for a visit. I chose the Silversmith because of the great reviews on this site! A few days before our stay I called Peggy the concierge and made a few requests. As it was my sister's birthday I wanted the stay to be memorable. When we arrived at the hotel our suite was ready! Not only were all of my requests met, but there was a bottle of white wine chilling with a birthday card for my sister! I couldn't have asked for better service! All of the staff and ammenities were perfect. My only complaints: 1.
