I called the hotel before booking online because I wanted a two room suite (one bedroom with a sleeper sofa behind the french doors.) Upon checking in I found we only had a one room suite. This was a bit of an upset as we had three people sharing the room and wanted a little bit of privacy. However, it was nice anyway. 2. We had breakfast at Ada's next door. The coffee was weak, the hashbrowns were cold and they didn't care. My main portion on breakfast, the Beneditct Arnold was perfect, but I'll never visit again. There's a 'Corner Bakery' one block south next to the Palmer House Hilton. Go there for breakfast, save yourself $5.00 per person and be much happier!

“Durchschnittliche Qualität” Das Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills Hotel ist ein imposantes zehnstöckiges Gebäude in fußläufiger Nähe zum Rodeo Drive und Wilshire Boulevard. Aber das Haus ist schon etwas älter und die Gebrauchsspuren finden sich überall - in der Lobby, im Aufzug, in den Gängen und im Zimmer. Das Bad hat die Armaturen der achtziger Jahre, der Wasserverbrauch der Toilette ist enorm. Das alles ist aber noch hinnehmbar. Man sieht den Verbrauch und fühlt die Erneuerungsbedürftigkeit, aber weil alles sauber gehalten wird ist die Wohnqualität doch noch befriedigend. Das neben der Lobby gelegene Restaurant ist plüschig dunkel. Da habe ich wenig Neigung einzukehren. Da gehe ich lieber in eines der umliegenden Cafes zum Frühstück und spare Geld. Zu loben ist der grosse Flachbildschirm und das freie Internet. Kabel und W-LAN sind unbeschränkt verfügbar. Auch eine Kaffeemachine, Tassen, Zucker und das Kaffee aus Kolumbien sind kostenfrei zu nutzen. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich. Man hat uns Rat gegeben zu den Zielen, die wir zu Fuß erreichen können und hat auch unser Gepäck zur späteren Abholung aufbewahrt. Direkt hinter dem Hotel ist eine Bushaltestelle mit der Linie nach Santa Monica. Selbst wenn man einen Leihwagen hat, lohnt es sich diesen Bus zu benutzen.

“Loved this hotel” I just loved this hotel. The room was clean, had all the amenities that I like, and just felt great to be in. The hotel is fun to walk around in. I liked the modern atmosphere and thought the lobby was one of the most stylish I have seen in Chicago. I think this hotel can only add to your Chicago experience. I have stayed at several hotels in Chicago and feel this one is my favorite for style and cleanliness. Also it is in a great location for shopping and going out to eat. Have fun!

“Great place to stay, business or fun” Attended a conference and really enjoyed the hotel. Great king bed room on the 34th floor with an amazing view of downtown San Antonio. The bed was very comfortable with soft linens though the pillows were not for me. If you prefer a firmer pillow, bring your own. Location was great during the day and evenings. Extremely easy access to the riverwalk and Rivercenter Mall. Parking is expensive at $25 a day and I found it frustrating that the hotel charges $14 for 24 hours of internet access from your room. There is free internet access in the lobby. The staff at the front desk and Starbucks were very friendly and courteous. The hotel was showing the Spurs' playoff game in the lobby on a large projection screen during my stay. The walk to the convention center and behind it to Hemisphere Park is very nice, as is the whole riverwalk. I would definitely stay here again for business or fun.

“Exactly what you expect” The rooms are exactly link the ones in the previous Aloft that I stayed in. They are clean and comfortable. The real advantages of this property is that it is across from the airport and directly on the light rail line. We stayed here and attended an ASU football game. It was perfect. There is currently a bus system from the airport which drops people off across the street from the light rail station and this hotel. It appears that the airport has built some sort of tram that will take passengers in the future. I suggest checking the airport website about when that tram will be open. One thing to know that I think is VERY IMPORTANT you do not want an odd numbered room that ends in x21 or below, because they get A LOT of direct sunlight. This means the room will be baking when you get into it and you will need to keep the curtains down and the air conditioner cranked up if you want to stay comfortable (read: dark and wind from air conditioning unit). Numbers 23-31 are not quite as bad, but still get some afternoon sun. On the flip side, odd numbered rooms have views of the airport (and Washington Blvd) if you brought your heat retardant suit or your x-ray glasses so you can see through the drawn blinds and your ear plugs. I am sure odd numbered rooms on the lower floors also have issues with street noise. Tip: high floor, even numbered rooms = great stay

“Excellent hotel in a central location.” I got this hotel via a priceline bid and was a bit scared after getting the brushoff when I called to try and request 2 beds. But early check-in was no problem and the 2 bed request was granted. Room was standard 4 star business. Very clean, comfy beds, 32" flat screen TV, minibar, bathrobes and high end amenities. There was a nice single cup coffeemaker with Starbucks coffee but my room only had decaf. No free wifi and only 1 accessible computer in the lobby but there was a Starbucks in the mall right off the lobby. The location is great with BackBay station right across the street and the hotel itself is attached to a high end mall withe several nice restaurant choices and high end shops. I would highly recommend Giacomo's Italian restaurant around the corner on Columbus.

“Favorite Hilton outside of downtown San Antonio” I've stayed at most of the Hilton branded properties on the north side, and this is by far my favorite. The staff is very friendly, and even put me into one of the 2 bedroom suites on a couple of occasions (This is a little bit of a waste as I was by myself, but I still appreciate an upgrade for no reason!). The rooms are clean, cozy, and I can feel at home. The dinner isn't amazing, but does the job when I am working late at the hotel. The cookies are delicious! My only complaint is that if you are on a bottom floor room, you can hear people being loud at the pool.

“Couldn't Beat It For The Price” I got a very good price on hotels.com with a king bedded room and buffet breakfast. The room was very quiet and I got a great sleep every night. Nice down pillows, decent food. The down sides were an armchair in the room with a back that was all show......when I leaned back there was no support, I don't care that the tv was the old tube kind but the picture was not so great, it looks like they remodeled and stopped when they got to the shower.....old style tub and tile. My experience around the world is that the better chain hotels are still charging for internet and I'd rather pay for a great connection and be able to do business than have free slow internet. All in all very good for the price.

“Great location good breakfast” My partner and I stayed here for the 4th of July weekend. We had room 1303, a corner room facing the street with side water view (if you leaned into the window) that was nice if a little small. The heat in Chicago that weekend was awful but the AC worked great, the bathroom and room itself were very clean and all room electronics worked well. I found it peculiar that the towels all seemed rather small. Maybe it just seemed that way cause I'm a bigger guy but it was weird. The breakfast area was very busy most mornings and the staff were kept on their toes refilling everything. One thing I did notice was that the lobby and breakfast areas had fans on the floor providing air instead of running the AC. It made these areas very hot and stuffy, I pitied the front desk staff. Overall this location was great, very central and there were plenty of food options in the surrounding neighborhood. Would definetly recommend this property.

“Good But Not Great” The Parc 55 recently underwent a remodel and while it definitely looks better than it did I still would opt for some of the other 4 star hotels in the area over this one. The Pluses - great location, great views on the higher floors, comfortable beds, nice products in the restrooms. The Minuses - internet was definitely hit or miss (and not cheap at $14.95/day), no light in the closet, room key stopped working halfway through the visit. All in all I would recommend staying here if you get a good deal but I will probably look elsewhere unless the price is right.

“Good Location” I stayed here while attending a conference at the attached convention center. Great location obviously to the conv. center, as well as, the attached mall. Located really in the heart of the city so, easy to get anywhere. I thought that the public space was very nice and I used the free internet in the lobby (like a laptop lane). I thought the rooms looked a little dated.

“Vue exceptionnelle sur le port” Cet hôtel est très bien situé pour affaire ou tourisme et les chambres bénéficient d'une vue exceptionnelle sur le port. il est d'ailleurs dommage qu'on ne puisse pas sortir sur la terrasse de sa chambre ! La décoration de l'hôtel et des chambre est très classique voire vieillissante, une touche de modernité ne ferait pas de mal (décoration, salle de bain, ...). Le service est de bonne qualité mais presque trop "protocolaire" : cela manque un peu de chaleur, d'humanité, ... Toutefois, séjour qui fut globalement agréable et je recommande cet hôtel notamment pour déplacement d'affaire

“Tremendous value” What used to be a pretty crummy hotel has been transformed into one of the best bargains in the city. We reserved a one bedroom suite for $225/night and were quite pleased with what we actually found on arrival. The hotel room was impressively large by NY or EU standards, impeccably clean, not super luxurious, but better than Hilton/Marriott type hotel furniture and with great sound proofing. The Beacon Theatre is next door and there was a concert one night and we didn't hear a peep from the crowd outside or the band inside. Impressive. Limited hotel services, but adequate for the price. This would be a great hotel if you need a relatively inexpensive place to stay while you are in NY to work, as it is so spacious, close to public transport, has a small kitchenette and in a safe neighborhood. The only downside for many will be its distance from most business areas of the city. But well worth the cab or metro ride.

“camere con vista e posizione strategica” Visto da fuori l'edificio composto da due blocchi rosa e azzurri non è niente di speciale, dentro per fortuna le cose cambiano. Abbiamo soggiornato in una camera con vista e credo che ne valga la pena pur di avere un piano alto altrimenti si rischia di avere ormeggiata davanti una nave da crociera e non vedere la baia. Dalla camera potevo vedere una foca che ogni tanto spuntava dall'acqua, bellissimo! La camera era grande e pulita il letto molto comodo. La cosa migliore è sicuramente la posizione, si può andare in centro a piedi e avere l'albergo sul mare. La nostra tariffa includeva il wi-fi ma il segnale era un po' debole. Dispone di piscina che non abbiamo potuto provare perchè non era molto caldo. La zona era tranquilla, gli homeless a SanDiego sono un po' ovunque ma non danno problemi salvo chiedere l'elemosina. In generale direi che è un buon albergo ma non ho niente di speciale da segnalare. Di negativo il parcheggio non incluso nel prezzo che costa 22 dollari al giorno ma almeno non avrete lo stress se l'auto è a noleggio e la colazione che non vale la pena di prendere inclusa nella tariffa perchè non è altro che un voucher per il ristorante accanto dove viene riconosciuto esattamente un importo pari alla differenza tra la tariffa senza colazione e quella con colazione. Della serie nessun vantaggio quindi decidete all'ultimo se e dove la volete fare.

“rock star gorgeous” If you want a full-on luxey experience of New York, and can afford the price tag to go with it, the St Regis is the hotel for you. It is well deserving of its Hot Pink rating on the neilsonparc lust list. The lobby is a masterpiece and the rooms and bathrooms are classy. The wine bar, though very small, is beautiful. No pool, and no rooftop bar or view, but apart from that we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

“Great Hotel” The DC Palomar is in a great location 2 blocks from Dupont Circle. In addition to it's perfect location the hotel is beautiful with large rooms, soft bed linens and towels, Aveda bath products, beautiful outdoor pool, delicious restaurant/room service and amazing friendly helpful staff. I loved this place and will be back.

“Just gets better” Logistics hadn't allowed me to stay at the Kennsington Park for several years. After a four night stay at the end of September I can say that the quality of the hotel has just gotten better. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever had and the service is impeccable. The location, a block from Union Sq, gives you a great location but a little less crazy than outside the St Francis. The lobby is lovely and a good place to hangout and socialize. The concierge is great and the front desk staff is very helpful. The rates were very reasonable. I recommend paying a little extra for a room on the 11 or 12 floor.

“Great Getaway hotel” My wife and I stayed at the Monaco for a weekend in Chicago. The hotel has a great location in the Loop and within easy walking distance of the Magnificent Mile. There are also plenty of restaurants in the area to choose from. Like the other Kimpton hotels I've stayed in, this one was stylish and clean. My only complaint is that I didn't get a room with a view, unless you like looking at the brick walls of a building overlooking an alley. But, I didn't ask for a different room, and who knows, I might have received one. The staff was very courteous and accommodating. I asked for a 3:15 am wake up call in order to catch a very early flight out, but the wake up call came 15 minutes late. When the desk made the follow-up call I asked for, the woman at the desk apologized for the late call. Fortunately, I relied on my alarm and was already up, but I appreciated the apology. The guys at the front door were always pleasant and helpful. And the wine tastings at 5 pm are always a nice touch. One day I played on the Wii game while sipping wine. On Saturday, they even had a cellist playing. All in all, I thought this was a great place for a weekend getaway. There are plenty of other hotels in the area, but you probably can't go wrong at the Monaco.

“Good hotel, but wifi charges are a deal-breaker” I visited this hotel with my husband for a conference I attended. It was on the list of official conference hotels with a shuttle to McCormick Place, and the Tripadvisor reviews also helped with the decision. Check-in was easy, and we got the room requested, a king corner suite. The room was clean (initially smelled like some kind of spray, but that wore off) and it was nice having all that space (about 500 sq ft) but not really necessary. We did appreciate the mini-fridge and microwave, though. Bathroom was average. The room decor was a bit dated but the design of the hotel itself was lovely -- built around a large atrium, and with glass elevators facing out. The main problem was the wifi charges: $15/day/device! We had 2 iPhones and 2 laptops. That would have come to a total of $300 for the stay. Fortunately my husband got them to reduce it somewhat, and I also used wifi at McCormick Place. Had we known in advance, we likely would have stayed elsewhere. This may not be a problem for other people, though. As others have said, the included breakfast is good with lots to choose from. We avoided long lineups by going early, which I had to anyway. The lineups for the "manager's reception" drinks were often unbelievable. I could not imagine waiting 30 min for a "free" drink, in our case soft drinks. The location of this hotel is very good: right downtown, within easy walking of stores such as Ferragamo, Bloomingdales and NM, specialty music stores, lots of coffee shops, as well as a fun mall with Macy's and a good food court. As our flight was at 8 pm, we were luck to obtain a 5 pm checkout for only $50. Overall we were fairly impressed by the hotel and the price (considering the conference) wasn't too bad -- but the wifi charges might be a deal-breaker for any further trips.

“Loving Seattle, 2 years in a row” My husband and I came back to Seattle for the second year in a row following a wonderful visit last year. During last year's stay, we lodged at the Holiday Inn Express that sits next to Holiday Inn, so we are very familiar with the area. This year, the area felt different. I don't know if it was because I am comfortable with the area, but it didn't feel sketchy like it did last year. There were plenty of professionals and vacationers walking around. I felt completely safe. Mostly, we crossed Denny Way, passed the awesome Pink Elephant car wash, and walked down Bell to get to the Market and everything else. The room was very clean and comfortable. The front desk was super friendly and helpful holding our bags so we could go downtown while we waited for our room to become available. The cab fare seemed more expensive this year from the airport, so we may consider alternative transportation next time getting to the hotel. If you are looking for breakfast options, I recommend Top Pot Donuts, located on 5th street. Fresh donuts, good coffee, in a great cafe environment. We went almost every morning of the 4 days we spent in the city. I highly recommend the HI. It's 1 mile from Pike Place Market, 2 from the baseball and football stadiums. The walking will help you work off the donuts!

“Great Location, Great Room, Would stay again” I'm a Platinum level member so was upgraded to a nice two room suite which allowed me to work very comfortably. The concierge lounge was well stocked for both evening and breakfast. The location is central to much of DC.

“I was less impressed then I wanted to be!” I lived in DC for years, in fact lived not far fron this hotel but I had never stayed here. I was really looking forward to staying here one night on my DC Christmas prigramage. I probably will not stay here again. Nice lobby, great classic building. The place was all decked out in Christmas decorations and looked smashing but the hotel was pretty much empty and felt like it was barely open for business. They obviously are not marketing to local folks with overflow Chistmas or holiday company. The room was nice, nothing spectacular about it, but nice. Good stuff - Attentive staff, comfy bed, nice flat screen TV. Stuff I didn't like so much: Expensive third party valet service when the hotel has plenty of parking and should have a self park system. No coffee marker in room and very steep room service charges for a cup of java. The little lobbt shop closes early in the evening so no place to get a snack or a hot drink without leaving the hotel and walking in the rain (or paying the jacked up room service). They make you pay for internet except in the lobby and the lobby was not inviting to actually sit and hang out in. A suggestion: maybe have some music or simething to make the lobby feel less like an abandoned movie set. Overall the place felt cold and not very welcoming. I imagine that things are very different during the large conventions etc. However even with other humans around, the extra charges for parking, wifi, and coffee iwould still annoy me. Beware if you are booking on priceline. The hotel does not honor the free breakfast that priceline says is included as an amenity.

“Plenty of style at this Hyatt” I spent two nights at this Grand Hyatt. It makes a great impression as soon as you walk in the front door. The front desk people were professional and my check in/out processes was painless. The rooms were smaller than most. We had a room with two double beds and it was not as large as I would have expected for a newer hotel. I have had larger in a Hampton Inn room. My room ended in XX67 and it was about a 2 minute walk to get there from the elevators. The only personal experience I have with customer service was with breakfast delivery. My roommate and I had filled in the order menu and hung it on the door for delivery between 7:30 and 8. Our phone rings at 7:30 from room service and they confirm our order. While on the phone with them I asked for tap waters and specifically asked for either 4 glasses if the glass was small or larger glasses of water. The gentleman said he would gladly make sure the glasses were large. I also asked for a side order of strawberries, and he agreed. When the order appeared at our door, it did not have the fruit, and the glasses of water were no larger than 10 oz. I was puzzled since we had just spoken and how the order could be wrong? Valet parking is $33. The convention center is literally right next to this Hyatt. The River Walk is through the front door and down some stairs. The exercise facility is the best and the pool is 25 meters long, but about 20 feet wide.

“Welcome Home” Stayed in this hotel for four nights with my daughter and husband. The room was large with a king sized bed and pull out sofa bed. It also had a fully equipped kitchenette, with microwave, Keurig coffee maker and fridge. There was also a small dining area. The bathroom was a good size and there was an area outside the bathroom with plenty of room for two women to get ready in the morning!!! There was also a walk in dressing room, with lots of storage space for our clothes. There were mirrors everywhere and lots of power points for our chargers and electrical stuff. The room also had a safe, free Wi-Fi and flat screen TV. The whole hotel was immaculate, and the floors gleamed. It was slightly off the beaten track, but in a lovely location just north of Dupont Circle. The subway was only about a ten minute walk away. There are lots of lovely restaurants around the hotel – and I do recommend you try the breakfast buffet in the hotel – it was excellent. The customer service is A+ and I loved it when we returned back each evening after a long day of sight-seeing and were greeted with a warm “Welcome Home.” I have stayed in many hotels across America and Europe and can highly recommend this one to you. I have absolutely no complaints.
“Amazing hotel!” Beautiful rooms, lobby, and sparkling pool. The views are spectacular too! Loved it.

“Nice Big Rooms (1 Bedroom Suite)” The Marriott Custom House is situated centrally. It is steps away from Fenuil Hall, The Boston Acquarium, IMAX Theater, and other points of interests. The only thing is that the hotel doesn't have a restaurant but right outside the Custom House is Fenuil Hall and there are hundreds of restaurants to choose from. My overall experience at this hotel was pretty good. I would highly recommend this hotel to families.

“Nice hotel but ask for a room in the back” This hotel is nice. It's in a good location, clean, well decorated and modern, and a good price. I was there on business and my travel preparer booked me in a king suite. The bed was awesome and it was a good size room. I'd probably give it 4 stars if it weren't for the noise. I'll admit I should have asked to switch rooms so shame on me but I figured I'd get used to the noises and I already unpacked so I figured I'd be fine...however, my room was at the front of the hotel and there is construction going on right across the street and they started promptly at 7:00 a.m. I mean promptly... I am used to loud noises. When I travel to NYC I usually stay on Times Square so I understand NY noise but the construction was so loud. Even when I was awake it was near impossible to even just sit in the room and there's no way to sleep with it going on. I also wonder if the windows are the triple panel ones because even at night I could hear buses driving by. That wasn't a problem for me because I can sleep through that but it did make me wonder about the windows. I was on the 11th floor and I could still hear street noise. Like I said, I should have asked to switch rooms but I still feel like they should have said something to me when I checked in to give me a choice. If I still would have picked my original room then it really would've been my fault but I probably would have told them I'd take a smaller room in the back instead of dealing with the construction noise. I'll stay here again but I will make sure to ask for a room in the back. My co-worker stayed the same time as me and he didn't hear any of the noise but he said his room was smaller. I recommend the hotel but if you stay, ask for a room away from construction and you'll probably enjoy your stay.

“Great Customer Service” A few years back this was a Hampton Inn & Suites. We stayed here almost exclusively while our son was attending TCU. We returned for a business trip and found the name changed, but little else. Customer service is still excellent, rooms are still clean, breakfast is still complimentary and plentful (eggs, biscuits, gravey, sausage, bacon, cereals, mixed fruits, toast, bagles, muffins, milk, cofee, tea, cocoa, etc) and they have added a computer for hotel guest use and a complimentary evening beverage and snack time in the lobby area. Apart from some minor wear and tear (this isn't a new hotel) and firm beds (I'm not fond of firm beds but my husband loves them) it's still a convenient, comfortable, reasonably priced place to stay. We would recommend it and will return.

“Decent stay, great front desk staff, but what's with the housekeeping?” Had a very odd three-day stay here, beginning with a confirmed reservation for a particular kind of room that they did not honor once I arrived. Just to clarify, I was told they did have that kind of room but were saving it for somebody else. Given that I'm an Honors member, I gently pushed back. The fruit plate and the comped parking sent as apology were very nice gestures, but geepers, people, can't you just honor your reservations? I didn't ask for a fruit plate, I asked for a king bed. To add insult to injury, I found a filthy remote control and a dirty bathroom sink -- literally toothpaste and hair from last guest still in it. I was too weary of wrestling with the front desk to complain about this too, so I just scrubbed these items myself with my traveling stash of handi-wipes. But hotel people, please keep in mind that we have very basic needs for a room we're mostly going to inhabit with our eyes closed: and cleanliness, quiet, plus the bed we asked for are at the top of the list. I added an extra star to my review for the very quiet room.

“Comfortable, Modern, Chic and LOCATION” Kimpton does a great job at keeping their properties on brand- all unique but plush, chic and always inviting. The room we were in was very large, the furnishings were high quality, the bed extremely comfortable, and the views stunning (but still very quiet). I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a modern gem in the heart of the city - without the 5-star price tag or stuffiness of some other hotels in the area. Book it- you'll be very happy with your stay. Have some free wine! =)

“A sad decrepit hulk of disappointment” I have pretty low standards for budget motels. I want a clean non smelly room, to feel safe in the parking lot and a minimum amount of customer service. If I have those I'm good. The Days Inn Camelback failed all those tests. My non smoking room smelled of smoke, had a broken shower curtain rod, chipped moldy sink etc.. It is in a seedy neighborhood and rough looking people who appear to live there spent the late night and early morning yelling at each other under my window. The water was turned off and staff was rude at check in and check out. Skip this one trust me.

“Great Location, very simple” It would be extremely helpful if this hotel had a website. We stayed at this hotel on a business trip, because there weren't a lot of other hotels available in the company's price range. The hotel's location is great. This is my third trip to NY in the past year, and compared to the other hotel we stayed at, this hotel was very quiet with very little street noise. The area is good, it's a residential area, with an outstanding little Italian restaurant just across the street. The front desk staff was fairly nice. They were going through shift change as we got there, and we were never acknowledged by the female clerk, but the male clerk was very nice. When we got into our room, we noted it was very clean. The room desperately needed a decorating update.....looks like it was last done in the 1980s, and the TV is probably about 20 years old. Both beds were very comfortable, but the sheets were a bit tattered, and the bottom side of the comforter looked like it hadn't been washed for six months. On the second morning, we never received our wake-up call......the front desk claimed that the phone was off the hook/busy, but it was not. Bottom line is, if you're looking for anything with frills, this is not the hotel for you. If you're looking simply for a place to sleep at night in a nice quiet neighborhood, this will work for you.

“リッツらしい~快適なサービスでした。” ハネムーンで宿泊。 部屋はスイート(EXECTIVE HARBOR VIEW SITE) 73平方メートルほどの広さで2室あり。(リビングとBEDROOM) 角の部屋でリビングには望遠鏡があり、自由の女神が覗けました。 バスルームもシャワー、バスタブ、シンクは2つあり、広く快適でした。 ハネムーンということでストロベリーパフェとメッセージカード頂き素敵な記念になりました。。 1FのBARにも通いましたが年配のインド人のバーテンダーが結婚について語ってくれたり、シャンパンのサービスをしてくれたのもよい思い出です。 街について、コンシェルジュに聞くと色々教えてくれます。(英語になりますが。、) またぜひ泊まりたいホテルです。 (ちなみにプールはありませんでした。)

“Very Large Hotel with a Grand Lobby” I have stayed at this hotel on two occasions. It is a very large hotel with a grand lobby at a great location. The first time, we arrived early, so rooms were not ready. We were assured that we would get two separate beds in the room, but when we came back in the evening, they had forgotten of this request, and only rooms with king-size beds were available. They made amends by offering us complimentary breakfast vouchers, which was nice. The second time I stayed here with my daughter, and we were able to check in early, and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. By the way, they have a $2 per bag fee, if you want them to store the bags prior to departure. Also, the bar/restaurant lounge serves nice cocktails.

“Good location, liked the hotel.” Good location in downtown Dallas, with several restaurants within walking distance. Free drink in the evenings (rather basic quality wine, but you get what you pay for). Fairly good free breakfast. Free wifi in rooms. Quite a good room, comfortable and reasonably large. Main criticism is expensive valet parking. We found a car park within a block which was a bit cheaper.

“An Ok Substitute!!” After being told the government rate at the ritz was only for federal employees and not state, despite having called and made a specific my mom was a state employee and not a federal one, we frantically move to the stanford court. Having stayed at the St. Regis on our last stay to San Francisco this was a major step down. Although it was about half the price of the St. Regis. The hotel is very centrally located, close to lots of good restaurants and only a few blocks from Union Square. The lobby is very modern and looks like a technology geek design it. The room was perfectly fine it had some luxury features, such as personal reading lights and a large TV. The service was fine, not exceptional though. If I were to come to San Francisco again I would consider staying at the Fairmont which is across the street from the Stanford Court. We went for cocktails at the Fairmont and it seem far nicer.

“A nice business class hotel” I travel down to the Warner Center quite often and when I do, this is where I stay. It's moderate in price, walking distance to the office, easy access to decent food (Flemmings and Roy's are both just down the road and PF Changs in across the street). Brought my wife and daughter last time to see her mother and the rooms were fairly cramped with the three of us. I would not advise staying at this hotel, or in the area if you are looking for a Southern California vacation spot. Unless for some reason you are centered on SFV. Also, I was unimpressed with the bar and food at the buffet, though the price was right. Starbucks in the lobby if you just need a quick coffee fix. Loved the valet guys. Always had my car in 3 minutes or less. Front desk was fast and pleasant. I'm looking forward to my next stay.

“Second time around was an improvement.” I have previously posted a negative review about this hotel. We had booked the room thru Priceline. I think we got a Priceline room at that time and it was less than desirable. However we booked this hotel thru hotwire and gave it a second chance. We had a better experience this time. No real complaints. However parking is expensive at $18 a night. Granted we only paid $58 a night not including the parking fee. Would not stay here at normal prices, however there are good deals to be had if you look hard enough. Beds are very comfy. If you drink the bottle of water provided in your room, it will cost you over five bucks. So if you can get a good deal on this hotel, give it a try.

“Good Hotel, Decent Location” We booked this hotel as a Starwood reward night. One of the reasons we chose this hotel was because of the location which is convenient to restauarants and are galleries in Chelsea. The staff was very nice and helpful. We stayed on a Saturday, and there were not any protestors while we were there. Yes, the rooms are small, however this is common for Manhattan. The decor was modern, and the room and bathroom were clean. One complaint about the bathroom is that there is very little room for your personal belonings. Another or different shelf would probably help. The view wasn't great but not expected for that part of the city. The machines in the workout room need some maintenance as both treadmills were not working properly. It is very easy to walk to restaurants and Chelsea art galleries. To get a taxi just walk down to 7th Avenue, and there is a Whole Foods right on the corner. Although breakfast was free, it took an extremely long time to get service and get our food. The staff was very friendly, however, and did what they could to make the experience better. They were severly understaffed which may be attributed to the strike. Overall it is a good hotel in a good location.

“Expected more from this luxerious hotel” I am hilton diamond vip member, and we only get room upgrade and breakfast in starbucks. I was surprised that there is no executive lounge like the other Hilton hotels.
“Great Beds” As always the beds are great in the Westin. If its stormy the building does creek and groan a little. The rooms are clean and the check in staff where very helpful

“Overrated!” Although I asked for a quiet room ahead of time (and on arrival), I was given a room directly above the trolley stop & freight train. I asked for a change & was then given a room with a view of a parking lot, close to the Petco Ball Park, which was even worse, because I had to listen to the sounds of the ballgames. Then, at 5:30 AM, I was awoken by the surprisingly loud shower of a neighboring room. Also, the lobby was bedlam, the bedspread was soiled & the carpet worn. I checked out.

“Nice people, nice hotel” Reading the last review, I feel obligated to post my recent experience at the Hotel Palomar. Maybe I'm not quite as "picky" as other people, but I found the customer service at the hotel to be excellent, as compared to the 200+ other hotels I've stayed at in the last 12 months. Apparently the hotel was good enough to win the "Conde Nast" Traveler's 2005 Gold List of World's Best Places to stay, so I guess I'm not alone in thinking that it's a nice place to stay. Being a "road warrior", I'm also an "Inner Circle Elite Member", so it's possible I get treated a little better than the average customer, but compared with my treatment at other chains (Intercontinental, Marriott, Starwood), I found the customer service to be more than adequate. Checkin: I arrived early at the hotel (approx 1 PM), and didn't expect to be given a room, but the desk clerk found one for me without a problem. Based on my "Inner Circle" status, I asked if I could get upgraded. Again, based on past experiences with equal status at other chains, I was more than prepared to accept a negative response. The desk clerk upgraded me to a jacuzzi suite, no extra charge. She was very friendly, smiling, and welcoming, traits that I unfortunately see a paucity of in the hotel business. Room Service: I believe that room service at most Kimpton hotels is not quite at the same level as larger hotels, because they are boutique hotels, which are smaller in scale by definition than main chain hotels. That said, I think the quality of food I've ordered at Kimptons hotels exceeds their rivals. I did have breakfast at the hotel restaurant, and though expensive, it really was not any more than rival hotels (esp. for San Francisco). Service was fast and good, so no problems there. Room: Clean, with relatively new appearing furniture (again, maybe I'm just not as picky as others - but I do stay in enough hotels to be able to judge quality of room accomodations). The bathroom had a jacuzzi with separate walk-in shower with Aveda toiletries. Overall: Considering I booked the room with a Travelzoo discount of 150 (with $25 discount towards restaurant meal), I would most definitely stay there again. And the friendly, welcoming staff was the icing on the top which is the feature that would lead me to stay there again. I think that the same Travelzoo offer also has free parking for those driving, and may be running through March (on the weekend). They also have "Hot Date Hot Rate" specials (like all Kimptons)

“Great Choice - As long as the price is right!” We travel to San Antonio a few couple of times a year and always enjoy staying on the riverwalk to be near nightlife and dining. We have stayed at several hotels all around the river, but this was the first time for us to stay at this Hyatt Regency....though it is somewhere that has been on our “list” for quite some time. We feel that the Hyatt has the absolute best location smack in the middle of the riverwalk and across the street from the Alamo. Knowing San Antonio well, we knew that there were better options for parking. Knowing that the hotel does not have a self park option, and the fact that their valet is $33 per night, and self park across the street is $25 we choose to use the convenient city garage two blocks away (E Houston) for $9 per 24 hours. (No in and out though...but we rarely leave once on the river) The lobby is in great condition and the staff was very welcoming and appears to have been recently remodeled. We skipped the automated check in kiosks (Come On Hyatt....get rid of these stupid things....cool at Hyatt Place limited service, but of Place at Hyatt Regency and Grand) They assigned us a nicely remodeled King room on a high floor so we had no noise from city traffic, and kindly coordinated our friends being on nearby on the same floor. I heard that the rooms facing the interior of the atrium can be noisy so we requested city view. They also have nice river view rooms, but since they do not have balconies, we did not feel it was worth the extra money. We were here over New Years and never had any issues with noise, and appreciated them checking room keys New Years Eve night to ensure that only registered guests were permitted in. There is also a nice outdoor swimming pool and nice sized fitness center, though we did not use them as they under renovation while we were there, which we knew at the time we made our reservation. (there was an alternate fitness center set up, and you had access to the Grand Hyatt pool) The pictures of them look like they will be very nice. The ground level lobby is small but does have some comfortable seating. The elevators are speedy. The restaurant and bar is located on the main lobby floor and has a wonderful view of downtown the riverwalk from the bar. The main lobby level exits to the street. There is a lower lobby level with some shops, and a neat feature, that I remember as a kid....there is a (clorinated) river from the walkway to the Alamo,through the lower lobby, and out to the riverwalk. The lower lobby level exits directly to the river. As with most Hyatt’s, the breakfast was very well done and the staff was very friendly. Though there is usually a fee for the breakfast, our AAA rate included breakfast, and it was very enjoyable. I do not recall the exact price, but if was not included in the room rate, we might have checked out other options we know well on the riverwalk. Other than breakfast we did not eat at the hotel because we have so many favorite options in San Antonio, for both dining and cocktails. The room we had was a typical King room with a nice work desk, chair, and desk. The rooms have nice HDTV’s. The room also had a refrigerator in the cabinet. The AC blower can be left on for white noise. The rooms were spotless, smelled fresh and had nice pillows. (Both foam and feather). The curtains do an nice job of blocking out light, and the rooms have a nice view with the floor to ceiling windows. There is a fee for wifi (per device) so we did not connect in the room, but wifi downstairs is free. The bathroom was nice size, and well appointed with plenty of fluffy towels and nice bath products. New Years evening, a young person was laying in the hall outside a room banging on the door for about 10 minutes. (not the hotel’s fault) When we called the front desk they had someone up there in less than 5 minutes and took care of the situation right away. A+! We also enjoyed laughing at the young man who was dancing up a storm in his atrium view room....fully entertaining everyone waiting for (and inside) the glass elevators. All of the staff at the Hyatt was very welcoming and made for a pleasant stay! It was also a special part of the holidays for us, to get our annual dose of Christmas Lights on the riverwalk. The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if the room rate was comparable too to other nearby options. We have stayed at a full range of 3.5 – 4.5 star hotels in the area, and this one is one of the best, but can get pricy, compared, to many, thus the reason we have never had the opportunity to stay here before. All of these are very nice options and similar in their offerings and the prices seem to vary wildly from day to day.

“Nice renovation, still lacks in overall amenities” Loved the location if you are running in the Rock n Roll Marathon and 1/2 for 2013. I was across the street from my starting corral which meant I could use the amenities of the hotel room right up to the start time. I also was amazed that after finishing the 1/2 and walking a quick walk back to the Hotel, the streets were clear and there were no obstacles to leaving the Hotel. The new elevators are cool, the room renovations are nice: our room was clean and comfy. The downsides sound a little nit-picky: our toilet rocked, our shower leaked onto the floors, and the noise level from adjacent rooms and the hallway was a little loud. Also the bar downstairs was definately an afterthought. Access to the riverwalk can be made by elevator, but other than that is a lot of narrow stairs. Overall a nice stay for a mid-priced hotel.

“Nice conference hotel, rooms a little small, poor value” Stayed here for a 5-day conference. My room was very clean and well-maintained, although a bit small. The hotel is somewhat lacking in personality, but not as much as some others I've stayed in recently. The bed was comfortable, and I had no problems with my stay. However, all my colleagues staying in nearby hotels paid much less. They also charge $15 + tax per 24 hours of (wired) internet service in your room, which is the highest I've encountered. Sending e-mails was oddly slow, but otherwise the service was good. They have free internet in the lobby, but that was much slower and sometimes did not work. I tried adjusting the thermostat in the room, but I'm not convinced it had any effect on the temperature (which was comfortable enough). I did not try the food or the gym facilities; colleagues reported that the gym is cramped. There are lots of restaurants in the immediate area, some of them very good. The location is excellent, but be aware that the while the official address is on Michigan avenue, the real entrance with facilities for loading and unloading is on Rush, parallel to Michigan and one level lower (this is the weird two-layer part of Chicago).

“Great Location, Views, and Staff!” This hotel is in the heart of it all. Seconds from the monorail, Nordstrom, and other shopping. It is also a short walk (4 blocks) to the Market. We had no need for a car or taxis the entire stay. The staff was very nice and knowledgeable and offered great recommendations. We were on an upper floor and it was very quiet and protected from the city noise. Beds were great, linens were plush, and shower was amazing. Although we did not use them, the hotel also offers a trendy seeming bar and restaurant. They were always busy and had an upbeat vibe about them.

“very good” This place is always good and cheap. But I find booking the room through orbitz is usually cheaper than going through my employer's membership... The rooms are small but nice, and there is a nice lobby and bar/ restaurant. Very good walking location.

“Hotel OK; Downtown a disaster” When I read reviews in here that are all over the map, it makes me want to check out a hotel myself. I usually stay on the westside in LA and decided this was the time to try downtown. Well, the hotel is great for sleeping and such, but if you are looking for a grand experience, go somewhere else. The hotel has no lobby or public area as such, and the restaurant is only for high end dining. The $ 26 valet charge is too high for me, so i walked the block with my rollabout and paid $ 5 for the Friday night I stayed. You can actually use the same garage the hotel parks your car in a lot cheaper, but there is no in and out. The rooms, or the room i was in, was way above average. The A/C was cold, the water was hot and it was very quiet. The pool area was closed the night I was there but it looked pretty inviting if you like tall buildings all around you. If you are just looking for a good night's rest, then the hotel is very nice. Downtown LA is very disappointing. I like sightseeing, and have been to most of the attractions downtown. But I took my late afternoon walk and when you go 3 blocks away from the hotel, towards Broadway, it borders on scary. Definitely not for children. You are better off staying on the westside and driving to the downtown attractions. Sorry LA, I love you as a city, but downtown still has a way to go as a destination. But if I had to go back, I would pay the extra money and stay in the Biltmore across the street just for the lobby and common areas which are beautiful and very historic. Note to Hilton Honors members. No preferential treatment here, for you info. I was not even acknowledged as a member.

“OK, not excellent” We stayed here for 3 nights in August because of a special deal (1 night free); we would not choose this hotel at the regular rate. On the plus side: huge rooms (ours had separate living room), clean, free internet, excellent location, quiet night's sleep. On the minus side: huge charges for anything extra (if you touch the minibar it automatically registers so watch out--and one receptionist wanted $200 for a late check-out; asked again later and recieved free 2 p.m. check-out), uneven service (many staffers seemed completely indifferent), no lobby, nowhere to sit down in reception area, guests were sitting in the fire place! This is a big hotel with little charm. We also stayed 2 nights at Casablanca: small room but loads of charm and freebies. If space is your main criterion this is a good choice, but note that there is only one bed (comfy) and charge for extra.

“Mixed Reviews aren't a surprise” I understand why this hotel has mixed reviews. First of all, let me say, for the price, this is a pretty darn good choice for NY. And remember, you get what you pay for.... If you don't plan on spending a ton of time in your hotel room, this place is fine. The rooms are clean and the staff was helpful. Our double room was a nice size and had a nice plasma TV. Beds were hard and the bathroom tiny, but again, we didn't spend much time there. There are no elevators, but the bell man will be happy to get your bags up the stairs. And again, the price is fantastic. Don't expect the W, or even the Hyatt....but it's not too bad. Best part of hotel: LOCATION. Next door to Little Italy, few blocks from SoHo and near Broadway/Canal. We love to shop in SoHo, so this hotel was perfect. Came back to drop our bags and headed out again! I would stay here again.

“What happend to this place........” I have always stayed at the Whitehall and loved the Boutique status they held. But wow have things changed since my last stay a 1 1/2 years ago. Our expirence at the Whitehall will be our last. The service was aweful. 3 people standing around and not once did we have a door opened for us. We pulled up for valet and no one helped with the bags or even walked towards the car. We had to go talk to him and after he got done playing with his phone. We stayed in the junior suite with the parking package. It came out to $310 per night. 2 of the lights didn't work, The bed which is usually out of this world comfy was totally worn out and you could literally roll back into your place if your tried to cuddle. We called the front desk for ice at 10:40 pm and finally gave up on it ever coming at 11:30pm. Upon checkout I followed another guest that was dissappointed and upon speaking to the staff member checking us out she seemed like it was an ok and normal thing that guest were not happy. We left our car there all day and that afternoon we returned to pickup our car and were told there would be an extra $15.00 charge because we didn't pick it up by 4:00. I understand that but it would have been nice to know. Its time for the management to crack down and turn it around before its to late. The staff has become lazy and theres no excuse for that at a Boutique Hotel. This place no longer deserves its Boutique status and it certainly wasn't worth it.

“Good place for a meeting” I didn't spend the night at this hotel, but my company did have a meeting in one of their ballrooms. We were very please with the staff. They were very accommodating and attentive to our needs as well as those of our meeting's attendees'. There was both a breakfast and lunch buffett while we were there. We didn't eat at either, but the food smelled wonderful and there was a good sized crowd eating there. Parking was adequate as well. The neighborhood around the hotel looked a little rough...just an older, close to the airport type of area. We didn't experience any problems. Would definitely use this hotel again for a meeting, and I'd stay there if I needed to be close to the Houston Hobby airport.

“Excellent - was expecting nothing and got... excellence!” Fantastic helpful fabulous people at this property (I hope they are still there!). Travelled with a group and nothing was too much trouble for the Hyatt Lincoln Park. Excellent facilities in the apartments - nice to make your own dinner once in a while when you are on the road all the time! Great location walking distance to Northpark mall with supermarket and restaurants again walking distance. Was very sorry to leave the property and will definitely stay there if I ever need to be in Dallas again.

“Convenient to LAX” This hotel is very close to LAX with shuttle service. The usual ammenities you'd expect form a Hilton - executive lounge, fitness room, business center, etc.. Room was very clean & modern. Hotel has a nice restaurant and bar.

“Excellent stay at Level 9” We stayed at Level Nine of the Dupont Circle Hotel for New Year 2011. The hotel is well located on Dupont Circle, with easy access to the red metro line, or a fifteen minute walk to either historic Georgetown or the White House. Definitely give Level Nine a go - we were warmly welcomed by Cole, the Guest Relations Manager who showed us to our room, and really couldn't have been more helpful, indeed all the staff we met were friendly and professional. The room, located on the penthouse floor, had a comfortable bed - crisp white linens changed daily, flat screen TV, full complimentary mini bar, with large bottles of top brand alcohol, soft drinks, olives etc. The marble bathroom was fully equipped with aromatherapy toiletries, spa tub - with huge floor to ceiling window to bathe looking out on the DC cityscape or you could always watch the over bath flatscreen TV, walk in shower and a very welcome heated slate floor. The level of housekeeping was second to none - immaculately maintained and nightly turndown service. Other reviews commented on inadequate shutters - level nine has blackout curtains in the bedroom. Level Nine Lounge access, gives all thirteen suites on the penthouse floor, access to canapes, snacks, tea, coffee, and again complimentary wine, cocktails and champagne. A real find for Washington DC - couldn't fault the room or the standard of service and one of the best hotels we've ever stayed in, in the US. Thanks :-)

“Great Old style luxury hotel” Stayed her for almost a week for a conference. I was upgraded to a gigantic suite (The Diplomat Suite) on the 22 floor in the tower. The room was of course great with fantastic views. All other experiences were also great. Hitghly recomended. Only downside was a lot of hills to get down to union square

“Stay here!” What was not to like? We stayed for 4 nights in 2 different rooms. Our first (an "04") was next to a stairwell and the noise disturbed our dog. Yes, it is pet friendly. They moved us to an "05" across the hall and all was good. Each room had 2 queen beds and a desk with chair. The 2nd room also had a comfortable chair in the corner. It wasn't huge, but also not cramped. The beds were uber comfy and there were large soft pillows in addition to some arty ones (long round ones and oblong ones with artist flourishes. There's a nice comforter and an additional woven throw. There was a large flat screen and lovely modern artwork in both rooms. The bathroom was clean and had Occitaine toiletries. They served coffee in the lobby in the AM and had a 1 hour wine happy hour from 5-6. They also have big purple umbrellas (big enough for 2) available in the lobby. They also provide one in the room. There's a restaurant in the hotel which received a good review while we are there. We didn't eat there, but we got room service once. We enjoyed the meal thoroughly. It came quickly, was hot and was accompanied by all the condiments one could ever need. The staff are GREAT. ALL of them. The location is good too. It's at the corner of 17th and Sansom and is near some good shopping, great restaurants, and the very pretty (despite the dog poop) Rittenhouse Square. We got a pretty good rate ($150) on line and it was worth every penny.

“Central Park and All” My wife and I just returned from our stay at The St Regis Club at the Essex House. It is an old world comfort station. A spacious room, in the very best location. I lived at the Essex House for four months in 2000 and it bacame my second home. Always happy to return.

“Great place” Loved the Park Hyatt Chicago. The staff was amazing so friendly and helpful. Extremely comfortable rooms and delicious breakfasts. Also a lovely touch having complimentary bikes for a ride along the shorefront. Would love to go back - great city, great hotel,

“Great stay...and what a view of Boston” Booked via Otel.com for 170$ (ouch).Check in was top notch, very friendly, making you feel important. They gave me a room with a view of the Harbah'. Room was classy and comfie, first class accommodations, LCD TV, beautiful bathroom, free internet provided given I'm a Hyatt Gold member. Nice gym and pool available. Easy access to water taxi and public transit. Left early so didn't use restaurants (pricey).

“First 3 Star W Hotel I ever stayed in” Ok, so I read the reviews over & over but got a good deal w/ Delta so decided to stay here. I should have gone with TA and stayed at Coronado. First, when we arrived, there were employees standing around the valet area and none of them asked to help. We walked in and the lobby is pretty..."calm beachy theme" but not as elaborate as some other W's, check in was professional but very cold. The front desk rep declined to upgrade me even knowing we were on a b-day/anniversary trip. When we arrived to the room, it was very small but comfy. We decided to check out the beach bar & gym, both were nice and yes the pool is pretty small but still ok. When we came back to change for dinner, that was when things started to turn, the lobby turned into a LOUD nightclub (and there was really no one there). You can hear the techno music thru the entire hotel, it was blasting in my room and also the walls are so thin I could hear the other room's entire conversation as well so I asked for another one right away, kinda of annoying to change rooms. But I knew that the noise would get worse as the night progressed. We were sent to the 18th floor, still could hear the techno music echoing off the walls. If you are sensitive to noise, then you def. should NOT stay here! For dinner, we spoke to the concierge who really had no clue....actually anytime we spoke with him, he seemed to give us the "same suggestions"....most of the time, I researched on my BB and told him the spot and how to get there. I even had to mostly set up our trip to La Jolla, he had no clue about the area. I think he def. needs more training, he was a sweetie but really needed to delve more into his work. When we got back from dinner, we also realized we have not seen the housecleaner but figured it was the changing of the rooms, wrong, we had to actually call when the 2nd day she didn't show up. They wanted to send her up at 10:30pm but I just asked for more towels, in the 5 days we stayed here, we had housecleaning twice. The hotel is in the downtown area of a city, lots of city life so if you are looking for more of a beach experience, this is not for you, I def. will not.The area is ok & yes there are some "wishy washy" folks but they leave you alone and mostly we felt safe anywhere we walked and we walked everywhere. The location to the Gaslamp Quarter is great but better suited to visitors looking to party. We were looking more for the coast and beach areas, for that you should stay in La Jolla or Coronado and pay the extra, it would be well worth it just for the location. The area gets you where ever you need to go though, plenty of cabs, buses and ferrys to take you around but that adds costs so as I said, if you are not looking to party and are looking for a quiet trip, go elsewhere. On the last day, I had to give them feedback because I just was SO disappointed and we spoke with a few employees explaining all the above and how they should smile more, extend their help more. I even told one of them, they should speak to the W in Washington (service there is to die for) and ask how to improve things. I told them I felt like we were staying at a Holiday Inn rather than a W Hotel, the rooms, the service are not 5 STAR. BTW, there is a Holiday that faces the ocean and looked terrific, you may want to check it out. My friend stayed there, it was a few hundred dollars cheaper and she liked it, not love but liked it. If I could tell TA members anything, is do not stay here, listen to the reviews...they were all dead on.

“Much Improved... a nice stay” Booked this time through Hotwire so I knew I was getting a 4-star on the riverwalk at a good price. When I found out it was Del Rio Hilton, I cringed a bit based on the previous reviews about the staff. I have to say that I was pleasantly surprised... the staff were quite friendly, actually. Everyone from pulling in to leaving 2 days later were 100% accomodating and service oriented. I think they must have improved quite a bit since the last reviews were written. As far as the hotel itself, location is excellent, right on the river. My only issue with Hotwire is the fact that I always get booked a double bed... so unless I check in right at 3pm, I cannot get a King... so I ended up with 2 doubles, but the room was a nice size and everything worked properly... the room even had an empty mini-refrigerator in it. Things like phone calls and internet are not free... as is the standard for 'upscale' hotels. As much as I deplore the practice, it is the way it is across these chains. What I will say is unacceptable is the parking situation at the Del Rio Hilton. You basically HAVE to valet (or walk a couple blocks with luggage in tow). And they rape you on the charge: $35.50 for parking overnight. That's the most I have ever paid for valet... E-V-E-R. And the charge isn't the main problem... the service is. I could understand being charged extremely high rates if the service was spot-on good, but the valet service is horribly under-manned. It takes close to 30 minutes to get your vehicle at times. Just horrendous. It's as if they know they have you over a rope and you have no choice to park there, so they kill you on the rate. Just unethical in my opinion for a chain like Hilton to do something like that. The parking fee was as much as 1/3 of my room rate. How silly is that? So to summarize, I will not knowngly stay in this hotel just because of the parking rate. It frustrates me to be a victim in something, and that is just how I feel when I sign the bill at the end of my stay for $100 and all I did was internet and park... that was as much as a night's stay through hotwire. I could have stayed at the Contessa for that.

“Sophisticated and Quiet” Loved this hotel-the neighborhood is amazing, with the grand houses of Pacific Heights all around you, great for walking. We booked a suite and it was very spacious and comfortable with a great sofa bed for the kids and pocket doors to separate the bedroom. The hotel is quietly elegant with a nice small reception area off the lobby with wine and snacks. I would highly recommend this hotel. You do have to self park, no valet but we had no trouble finding street parking for our Chevy Tahoe so this was actually a plus because most SF hotels charge $40 or more for parking. Breakfast was included too and was quite good. We will be back!

“Overall a great stay, shame about the noise” This is my second review of Copley House - I stayed here in July last year and loved it. I had no reservations about booking to stay there when I was in Boston again this year. In fact we ended up staying there twice on our vacation, once at the beginning before we left for our tour of New England and then once when we headed back into Boston just before we flew home. The first time we stayed for a few nights at a studio on West Newton Street, in the same building where I'd stayed last year. It was great - clean, comfortable and all the things I said in my last review of course still apply - great value for money, great location. The second time, we were in another building a few streets away, St Botolph Street I think it was. The accomodation was fine on the face of it, clean, comfortable and very spacious. But it was very noisy - I think it must be next to or back onto student accomodation, as I barely slept all night courtesy of thedrunken shouting and singing of groups of what sounded like university aged people. The place seriously needs soundproofing to stop noise outside the building coming in. Noise inside the building was a bit of an issue too, as after having finally got to sleep I then got woken up by the noise of the amorous activity of the people in the apartment upstairs... I would stay at Copley again as its value and location are great and I have had no problems with the standard of accomodatio at any timen. However, I would make sure I got a place on West Newton Street at this was very quiet and there were no noise issues here.

“Royal palace-- For basic royalty only” Warning upfront: My rental car was broken into (window smashed) in the middle of the day while parked at the Royal Palace. Don't leave any valuables in the car while in LA-- they stole my GPS system. Police told me that that has been the #1 item stolen from cars. I think of Westwood as a safe city, but I was disappointed this time. This is a basic hotel within walking distance of UCLA. Ralphs grocery store and Best Buy electronics are a block away. Peet's Coffee is down the street. In addition, the room rate for this caliber of hotel can't be beat. Don't walk too fast through the hotel's front door. It is a sliding glass door and will not open all the way if you go too fast. The front desk staff are friendly, although a few odd personalities do exist. Everyone, however, was very professional. I stayed in a suite, which was very nice as I had to stay for 10 days. The suite included a small balcony, which was surprisingly peaceful for LA. The hotel provides weak in-room coffee and basic hotel soaps and shampoos. The kitchen had a microwave and large fridge, but don't expect any other amenities. Bring your own silverware and plates if needed. The maids also sometimes forgot cups for coffee, but you can pick some up from the breakfast room. The bed/pillows are not the most comfortable, but are very clean and shets are changed everyday. Despite being what I consider an extended stay hotel, the room smelled very clean. Breakfast is very basic: bagels, danishes, weak coffee, get there early for the muffins. The hotel leaves LA Times on the tables in the breakfast room. Overall-- this is a basic hotel—but a great value and location. If you will be out and about for most of the day, and don’t have a car in LA, this is the place to stay.

“Not quite as nice as Grand Hyatt, but plenty nice” Stayed in October 2011. For an extra $20/night we got an over-sized queen, which had a lot of extra space, but nothing useful in it (i.e., a huge entryway, but no furniture or a closet or anything else to do with it; a standard sized bathroom; a lot of empty space by the corner). Everything is nice and new. This is just two doors over from the Grand Hyatt (the Paramount Hotel is in between), two blocks from the Seattle Convention Center. Very nice 24h fitness center. A sort of mini-Starbucks for morning coffee & snacks. My only complaints: first, the LEED certification evidently left the hotel wanting to only include low-wattage lighting, and only desk or floor fixtures (no overhead lighting in the rooms). Overall, there was just not enough light in the room. Brighter (CFL) bulbs would help, so would some overhead lighting. My other complaint, which applies overall to Hyatt: please, get some better toiletries. In the world of business travel and TSA grope-fests, I try to travel without bringing my own shampoo etc. The Hyatt Portico brand is consistent with 2.5 star hotels, and they should do better. Enough whining for one review. This really is a very nice hotel, with some nice touches for their LEED certification. It's not as fancy as the Grand Hyatt, but a tad cheaper to make up for it.

“Geniale Location” Das Hotel befindet sich in einem Flatironbuliding. Es ist nicht ganz hoch wie sein berühmtes Vorbild in New York, aber trotzdem einzigartig. Entsprechend knapp ist das Zimmer geschnitten, was nicht weiter hinderlich war. Die Einrichtung war ansprechend und es war sehr sauber. Das Bulfinch liegt sehr zentral, man kann den Quincy Market zu Fuß erreichen. Parken im Hotel ist sehr teuer $ 30 am Tag! Das Hotel ist im Film "Departed" kurz im Hintergrund zu sehen.

“Great Value, Service and Location” This was my second visit to this property and I am sure it won't be my last. This is a great hotel. My first visit was during Cherry Blossom Season in Spring 2010 with my wife and kids, the most recent was solo, both for business meetings. On both occasions, the management and staff were excellent, always making sure that we were satisfied with our stay. This past visit, I drove down to the DC area and knew that I would be early for my meeting that day. I made a phone call when I was about an hour away and was told nothing was available for early check in. Once I arrived a little after noon,the did another check and lucky for me a room was available. The hotel is in a good location, easy to access from New York Ave for folks coming down from NYC, Philly or Baltimore. The hotel is a few blocks from the Chinatown Metro stop and a short walk to the arena where the Wizards and Capitals play. The National Mall, White House and Union Station are also reachable within a 15 minute walk. It is a city location so you will see, hear and smell all sorts of things, places and people, but at no time would I feel unsafe. Breakfast is the standard Hampton Inn fare, more than enough to get you going in the morning. Free coffee, tea and hot chocolate during the day, cookies out at night. Poets and Busboys around the corner is a wonderful restaurant, and I have yet to be disappointed with anything I've had there.

“Great hotel” This is a great hotel. Great service and VERY clean. Large room and nice views. Great if you want to see a ball game. Be careful of the taxi cost to hannover st...$40!!! Close to Newberry St and shopping. Part of the SLH chain. I alomst always book SLH when I can.

“Flawless stay, though this hotel isn't for everyone” I found a great deal for $119/night at this hotel and decided to try it out. Overall I was very pleased. The staff was kind and accommodating, the room was very clean and spacious, the fixtures were modern and the bed was decent. The assistant checking me in asked if I'd mind a room near the elevators. I said no, and sure enough the room was very quiet all night despite being next to the elevators. I also appreciated being given the chance to choose another room. Despite my very positive experience during my single-night stay, I will concede that this hotel isn't for everyone. It's an absolutely enormous convention hotel, so you won't find the personal level of service of a boutique hotel. The lobby is gigantic and always crowded, though it's quite fun at night since the lounges and dance club are integrated right into the lobby. For the price I paid, I thought this hotel was well worth it. And by the way, that deal is still available from travelzoo.com...

“Unplanned stay turned out well” Passing through Seattle on the way to the east coast, we usually stay at the Doubletree Suites at Southcenter. However, inexplicably, our reservation there was overtaken by events and we ended up being "walked" to the other Doubletree facility at Sea-Tac. The manager from the hotel that walked us came in the van with the driver and personally apologized for this oversight. He explained that arrangements had been made for us to stay overnight at the Doubletree by Hilton Seattle Airport at no cost to us, in an upgraded room, with a 30,000-point bonus in my HHonors account. We accepted the deal and were quickly transported to the alternate hotel. I had stayed here years before, when it was still a Red Lion. Our room, which did not appear to be an upgrade, was in the tower on the 12th floor. The porter who helped us with our bags explained that the tower had recently been renovated, and that statement seemed to be true. The furnishings and finishings were indeed different (and newer) than I remembered them. Other than that, it was a standard room. Clean, comfortable, and somewhat quiet (our room faced the airport and the associated noise was sometimes audible). We enjoyed dinner in the Seaport Lounge. Wife had the hummus and broccolini. I had a shrimp caesar salad and an order of buffalo wings. I ordered a glass of Alaskan Pale and got served a glass of IPA. Who knew? I like them both, so no problem. This hotel is inferior to the Suites in terms of HHonors Gold benefits in that you only get an $8 credit at the coffee stand in the lounge for breakfast (if you have your MyWay preferences so set). At the Suites, Golds get a full hot buffet. It was nice to revisit an "old friend" but next time we will go back to the Doubletree Suites. Indeed, the Suites manager told me to let him know when we'd be staying there next so we could be well taken care of. I advised him that we would be doing so in nine days. It remains to be seen how well that stay goes but he will get his chance to make good on his word.

“Pleasant, friendly hotel at a great price” Want to go to Seattle but don't want to spend a lot of money on a hotel? The Mediterranean Inn is a great deal. I didn't want to spend a fortune on a hotel, but I didn't want to stay in a dump, either. I found the Mediterranean on Expedia, where I got a GREAT deal. I've read that if you deal directly with the hotel, they will match anything you find online. I paid less than $100 a night. The staff is very friendly, the hotel is attractive, and the rooms are comfortable. Having a kitchenette is a great feature and there is a nice Safeway right around the corner, so you can stock up on groceries. The hotel is right on several bus routes, so you can get downtown in mere minutes. You can also walk about two blocks to the Space Needle and Monorail, which is another great, quick way to get downtown. The neighborhood is lower Queen Anne and very pleasant. As a solo traveler, I never felt uncomfortable walking after dark in the vicinity of the hotel. The Mediterranean is not fancy, but it is definitely comfortable and pleasant. I would certainly stay here again. It's a great base for seeing the various sights of Seattle.

“Great location and good breakfast, but bed comfort and service need improvements” The hotel is steps away from the Capitol, making it very convinient to it and surrounding places. However, their service from valet to front desk to restaurant was mixed. Valet was not courteous. Front desk was accommodating and helpful, but had some difficulties with recognizing my Hyatt Platinum. The restaurant service was sometime slow, while their food was very good to excellent. The rooms and amenities were good, but the bed was a bit too firm and not as comfortable as usually encountered at other Hyatts.

“Perfect place for a girl's weekend in Philadelphia” Several girlfriends picked Philadelphia for a meeting place in mid-May. Having stayed at this hotel many times, I recommended that we stay here. It was a tough weekend because it was Penn's graduation and reunion weekend so the hotel was packed. As a result, the service at check-in was not quite as helpful as usual. Certainly acceptable, but not perfect. I asked to be put on the same floor as the other friends and she said she was unable to move anyone. I was a bit annoyed that she didn't even look. That said, we were all on the same floor anyway! The rooms are nice, typical Marriott but well appointed and comfortable. Even though the room faced Market St the soundproofing is very good and the rooms are quiet and the bed comfortable so a good night's sleep. Typical ridiculous charges for internet so we didn't use it. I was a bit disappointed that the hot tub in the pool area has been cemented over. It was a nice feature and I am sorry not to have it anymore. The location is excellent - steps from the Reading Terminal Market and right on Market St where you can get public transport all over Philadelphia. It is my location of choice in Philadelphia - as a Penn grad and with much family in the area, I go often and always stay here.

“safe, reliable but isolated” I wanted to stay with hilton property and wanted to stay in the smu / northpark area so i tried this hotel and it was ok. nothing special but no problems. didn't get the requests I indicated but when i asked again at check in they made a change. the hotel was clean except for the stained bedspread, limited tv channels, it's an old hotel that was partially renovated a few years ago. parking was free and easy, getting in and out of the hotel is a bit tricky and you have to drive anywhere. business center computers were slow. front desk staff - nothing exceptional, just answered standard manner. recommended an hour anywhere i asked to drive to - even though it was only 15 minutes away.

“High price for disappointing stay” I was to stay at this hotel for four nites. The hotel is nearby Qualcomm facility so if anyone is visiting Qualcomm, it is ideal location. This is an older model of Courtyard hotel -- where all rooms are accessible from outside. The hotel has small courtyard in the middle of the facility and all rooms have sliding doors to go to the courtyard.. The sliding doors are masked by curtain. After entering the room and checking the overall security, noticed that the sliding doors were fully open -- one would not know that there is security issue. (Why would the sliding doors be left open once a room is cleaned for next guest?) Then I tried to lock the sliding doors -- however, the lock mechanism is not easy to engage and one can't be sure whether it worked properly. I raised the concern with the front desk and they did nothing of it (meaning - no response from them of my concern). No wireless internet in the room. Had to park my laptop on the desk all times. Tried to iron few clothes -- fill the iron (halfway with the water). After the iron got hot and as I was pressing my clothes, it started to leak and spilled water on my clothes. Left permanent marks on my clothes. The room is need of major renovation. Got old console TV. The business center facility -- tried to print few docs (few pages). The printer(s) were out of the ink and blank paper. After first night stay, I checked out and stayed in a different hotel nearby. Best decision I made during the trip.

“Parfait pour une étape proche de l'aéroport” Nous avons choisi cet hôtel pour sa proximité avec l'aéroport de Denver et son excellent rapport qualité/prix. Nous sommes arrivés à l'aéroport de Denver avec beaucoup de retard et lorsque nous avons appelé l'hôtel (téléphone gratuit dans l'aéroport), ils nous ont informé que la navette ne fonctionnait plus, mais qu'il s'arrangeait pour nous envoyer celle d'un hôtel voisin. Celle-ci est arrivée 15 minutes plus tard comme annoncé. Le check-in a été aimable et rapide. Notre suite n'était pas très grande, mais fonctionnelle et agréablement meublée. Le lit était très confortable. Le Wi-Fi (gratuit) fonctionnait correctement. Dans la kitchenette, nous avons trouvé le nécessaire pour se faire du café, du thé et du pop-corn ! La salle du petit-déjeuner (inclus) était suffisamment spacieuse et le choix des aliments très variés (toasts, yaourts, fruits, oeufs brouillés, bacon ... et possibilité de se faire des gaufres). Nous n'avons pas dîné sur place bien que le repas soit offert car nous avons préféré sortir. Il y a plusieurs restaurants à proximité immédiate, notamment le Chicago Grill qui nous a bien plu. Nous avons utilisé la navette de l'aéroport le matin pour récupérer notre voiture de location : très pratique et sans soucis, chauffeur très sympathique. Le check-out a été très rapide car il a suffi de valider la facture glissée sous la porte pendant la nuit.
