Cet hôtel a parfaitement répondu aux attentes que nous avions et nous en sommes donc totalement satisfaits.

“Overall Good” We got a great deal at this hotel so I feel I can complain too much. But if I had paid full price I would be unhappy with a few things. The bathroom was a bit dirty...hair in the tub, a ring on the side of tub from someone's drink before us, and was a just a bit beaten up. There was a dirty towel in the bathroom. It looked like someone had just wiped their hands on it while it was on the rack and in effort to "be green" they don't wash unless it's on the floor. I think it's unsanitary to not change all towels between guests whether the "look" like they've been used or not. That being said, I'm sure the Omni is not the hotel hotel doing that...it's probably quite typical but unacceptable. The worst thing about this room was the heat. This room was so hot we could not sleep. We turned off the heat and even cracked the window as much as possible and it was still 78.4 degrees when we woke the next day. The head of housekeeping was very nice and apologetic and sent someone to fix it, but he clearly didn't know the first thing about it and said there was nothing he could do. We asked to change rooms and the front desk allowed us to change but acted like we had inconvenienced them. The room we were moved to was significantly smaller and not as nice but at that point we just wanted to be able to breathe. At that point I was underwhelmed with the service, but they did redeem themselves later with a complimentary champagne and chocolate covered strawberries...which were wonderful. There are no coffee makers in the rooms but if you are a select member they will bring beverages to your room in the morning which is a very nice perk. The gym was ok but not impressive. The beds are comfy. The location is great and overall we had a good experience and for the right price would return again.

“Walk to everywhere in midtown!” Excellent location right at Rockefeller Center, bus and subway one block away. The rooms are small (think cruise cabin size) and kept very clean, bathroom with pocket door with decent amenities and walk-in shower, no tub. Free wired and wireless internet is a plus. The Terrace Club on the 7th floor is open to hotel guests and outside members serves a good Continental Breakfast for $11 ++ and American for $16++ which then includes scrambled eggs and hot meats; as well as lunch and dinner . The bar is open till 10:00PM and is well attended. Right next door are 2 coffee shops for casual meals and easy take-outs. The front desk staff is helpful despite working in a small area and many people asking for keys, help, directions etc. And the area can be noisy, the Radio City Music Hall loading dock is across the street so trucks can be loading or unloading at any hour of the night causing noise. The double paned windows block most of it though. Overall a good choice if one can get this at a discounted rate - if you have to pay full rack, try elsewhere especially if you prefer a larger room than this hotel can offer.

“I will try somewhere else next time...” We enjoyed our stay at the Drake. It seemed to be a great location for touring the city. Very small, somewhat noisy if you're on the street side, but the beds and pillows were the best! Extremely small bathroom. Concierge seemed a bit too busy to help us. Also, I awoke in the middle of the night to the sound of the fire alarm. (There had been a fire earlier that day at one of the piers, so it was a bit frightening.) As anyone would, we rushed out of our room and began the decent down twelve flights of stairs. When we finally came out of the stairwell, we were surprised to see that everything was as it should be. The staff looked at us like we were morons. They said that someone had pulled the alarm manually and only the Fire Department could turn it off. Was it too much trouble to try to alert your customers that this was a false alarm? Maybe place a staff member in the stairwell? Apparently so. I was very ill that night and we met older customers in the lobby that had complaints as to how the hotel handled the situation as well.

“So easy...NYC easy? 70 Park Ave made it a pleasure.” Loved this property, but I love Kimpton's in general...and this one did not disappoint. King guestroom/quiet room requested-not much of a view..interior courtyard), but it was QUIET and I that's what I requested. Room was compact, but that is typical the city. It was not missing anything and just my hubby and I, so no big deal. We had a great time; staff was outstanding, check-in super-fast. Staff was very knowledgeable and I LOVE a doorman in the city :-) Great hotel bar for a post-show cocktail. Valet parking was convenient and not overpriced compared to other NYC properties. While we did not travel with our puppy, we did see doggie water bowls here and there, nice for those who cannot leave their pets at home for the holiday. Be sure to visit the Chelsea Market, Sarabeth's and the Fat Witch Brownie stores!

“Great value and location.” If you're looking for a clean, safe, friendly hotel for a good price, this hotel is the place. Wish I had discovered the breakfast restaurant on the 12th floor a little earlier! There is also a great selection of restaurants within 10 minutes walking distance.

“Good Stay” I was here for a business meeting. Great Location. Good fitness center. Good Food. If you want to see historical sites--most are within walking distance. I stayed in the tower with was quiet and enjoyable.

“Very enjoyable” I really enjoy this hotel and it is my choice when in sfo. Convenient to all points in city, both cable car lines meet outside, very clean, friendly staff, rooms very comfortable. Modern interior, but bright and airy. If the bells of the cable cars are too noisy, request a room on the interior. You lose the view, which is often very nice, but gain some quiet. I enjoy the views and don't mind the mild sounds of the city. I'm a light sleeper, but never have trouble getting to bed. Concierge lounge is small, but comfortable and good choices of food. I look forward to returning.

“Tripadvisor comments were right-on.” I told my wife before we drove up to the hotel --- "This hotel is brand new. It is $100 cheaper per night than any decent hotel in the Times Square area. The room is going to be small, with very little storage, and the A/C will be loud. The breakfast is free but it will be the usual Fairfield Inn variety and the breakfast room will probably be crowded. My wife said - we are going to the US Open and will only be sleeping, then eating breakfast, in the hotel -- so, no problem". Well, the tripadvisor reviews were right-on. The employees are very nice. When I told them I thought the A/C was louder than normal, they offered to move us to a different room. We had already unpacked so we did not move. Since it was September, we just turned the A/C off at night. You could open the window, but even from 12 stories high, the street noise was too much. In the Times Square area, we have recently stayed at the Marquis, the Westin, the W, and the Fairfield near 8th Ave. The rooms in this Fairfield are the smallest. Two people could not pass each other as they walked around the bed. For us, the location was very good. We had about 3 blocks to the 7 subway to go to the US Open each day. We were within an easy walk to Times Square and the Broadway shows. 37th street is a nice street (for NYC), felt very safe, with generally a good flow of traffic. Close to Macy's too. If you have stayed at other Fairfield Inn's, the breakfast was the usual. One staff person was responsible for re-stocking and was available if you needed something. Based upon nyc prices, probably saved another $20-$25 there too. Both of the 2 new Fairfield Inns in NYC must have bought their A/C units from the same company. They sit by the window and are very loud. We had the same issue with the other Fairfield. Overall, next year, I will probably pay the extra $100 per night and stay at the Westin. Also, I use CarmelLimo for my car service when in NYC. They are the lowest cost I've found and have been very dependable for me.

“Great little hotel in the middle of Times Square” This is not a large property but it offered a pleasant stay for a business/pleasure trip. Location is about as central as you can get, 49th St. between B'way and 8th Ave. A,C,E trains are a half block west and the Times Square Station is around the corner and south. You can take MTA from JFK into Manhattan, around the city and back to JFK without ever having to take a cab, if you're up to it. The room aren't spacious and I would have like to have a chair to sit in but the bed was comfortable and the sheets were clean. Bathroom was adequate and the towels are in decent condition. The restaurant, Serafina, was excellent for both breakfasts and dinner. Bonus is that you get 20% off as a hotel guest. It get s very busy before the shows but at 8 it can be an easy seat. You won't leave hungry. The staff is friendly by NY standards but sometimes can be a bit rough around the edges. Housekeepers are wonderful! They are almost invisible until you need something and couldn't be more accommodating when you do need them. The desk staff could use some warmth and the maintenance staff needs a fine tuning. Word of advice: the televisions in some rooms have a small box attached to the desk that is the receiver for the remote control. We didn't know what the box was for and couldn't figure out why the remote wasn't working even with new batteries. The less than friendly maintenance guy came up and in a very brusk manner admonished us for placing something in front of the mystery box. In broken English he stated; You place bottle in front of THIS! Well, maybe a small note in the room identifying the receiver would help in the future! Hello? Management? Are you listening? Overall, it was a great stay and we would consider The Time again. Thanks to all for a great stay.

“Great Sleeping Experience” For some reason the air conditioner ran nonstop so I slept great! The bathrooms are a little tired but the rooms are current. I thought the location on the 16th street mall was great.

“A good stay” A three day stay on business . Got a good rate at $129 per night. Nice clean and spacious room, must have been upgraded recently - good standard of furnishings, LCD TV with HD channels. Hotel location is good, close to Union square etc. I would stay again, helpful staff .

“Excelente elección antes de visitar L.A.” Hotel bastante bueno, perfecto para relajarse del vuelo largo y recuperarse. O bien antes de emprender el viaje. Excelentes habitaciones, limpieza, desayuno, etc.Zonas comunes comfortables. Perfecto para hacer una pausa antes de visitar L.A.

“No-frills, but safe and economical choice in East Hollywood” When I need to hang by hat for a brief stop in LA on short notice, I'll often choose the Travel Lodge on Vermont. It offers a very basic motel room, but is one of the few places this far east that is a "normal" motel. It certainly has its flaws--arrive back past 11pm and you'll have to park wherever you can find on their undersized lot--usually including no parking zones. No elevator and few stairways mean that lugging bags upstairs is a necessary chore. They also cut off breakfast way too early on weekends. But the breakfast is free and relatively nutritious (i.e., not just a prepackaged sugary danish as in similar motels). Coffee is horrible--next time I'll bring my own. I'm from LA, so I don't find the neighborhood as sketchy as some others do. It is down the block from some large hospital complexes, so not particularly isolated. It is also within an easy walk of great LA restaurant/lounges like the Dresden (see the movie "Swingers" if you don't know it.) So you can stay out late without worrying about driving--a rare LA treat. Between Vermont Ave. and downtown LA is a no-man's land for clean, safe, economical lodging, so this place is great if you want to be near Hollywood, downtown, Silver Lake. Los Feliz or the other nearby areas but don't want to pay downtown or central Hollywood prices. There is a charm-free pool in the middle of the parking lot but I've never used it. It seems most guests are Europeans--I guess they recognize a bargain when they find one.

“Super Lage mit teurem Parkplatz” Das Hotel liegt in Laufnähe zu den Attraktionen und Restaurants des Hafenviertels Fishermans Wharf und ist ein idealer Startpunkt, um die Stadt zu erkunden. Das Zimmer war sehr geräumig mit gutem Bett und schönem Bad und die obligatorische Kaffeemaschine durfte auch nicht fehlen. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und professionell, obwohl das Hotel gerade ziemlich voll und hektisch war. Allerdings muss man ordentlich für den Parkplatz bezahlen (50 USD pro Nacht).

“Clean, useful features, but not luxurious” We stayed at the Residence Inn Sorrento Valley in mid-January '06. I used my Marriott Reward points to cover a 3 night stay in a Queen Bed Studio Room. The hotel is currently being renovated. Our room was supposed to have been renovated but I thought the cabinets, tv, and dressers, etc were just average. Dont expect posh interiors. This was my first ever stay at a Residence Inn. Maybe I was expecting a little more. The hotel has a free evening managers reception (Monday thru Thursday, 5-7 pm) where they serve beer, wine, and a small entree. During our stay they served Chicken with Scalloped Potatoes and Chicken Parmesan on separate evenings. The food was okay but its FREE! A free continental breakfast buffet is served every monrning with Eggs, Waffles, Country Potatoes, etc. Menu items vary daily. Breakfast was ok, but hey its free. Rooms were clean. There is a swimming pool, jacuzzi, sport court, bbq grill, aerobic machines, and a ping pong table. Room has all you need in the kitchen utensils department (knives, silverware, plates, etc). One complaint was the bed. We were placed in a room with the older Marriott foam bed. It was not comfortable at all. We did not get a good nights sleep at all. The hotel is currently in the process of updating the beds with the newer Marriott Revive beds which are wonderful. My other complaint was the a/c unit is very noisy. In the Queen Studio its located in a closet adjacent to the bed. Not the best way to get a good nights sleep. Overall, the rooms were clean and spacious. However, ask for a room with the new Revive beds for a better night sleep. Dont expect luxury either. I will stick to full service Marriotts and Marriott Vacation Club units.

“Standard Sofitel offering” I like Sofitels. They are usually very similar and you know what you are getting. A comfy bed, decent breakfast, clean rooms and in a good location. The Water Tower doesn't let you down on any of these, however having just come from the Intercontinental Time Square I miss a few of the touches they have. No easily reachable power sockets near the bed for example. The IC has lamps with sockets built in, spread out over the room, so never a problem finding somewhere convenient to charge up the many devices you now carry. No iPod dock so you can charge up your iPod or iPhone, though there was a Bose player with an aux port. Wifi should be free, it costs so little to the hotel to provide so it's good to see the Sofitel offering it free, however what they mean is they give you an extremely low throughput for free, but you have to pay if you want to do anything more than browsing. Wifi reception in my room was also extremely poor. It didn't work near the desk or sofa, and near the bed it kept cutting out. Maybe the strange building shape means they didn't put their APs in properly? I did get upgraded (due to their loyalty program) but from a high floor room to a low floor suite. They tell me it's their policy to only offer high floors on request. Bit odd, but they did sort out a new room after a bit of pushing them. Overall it's a nice hotel but they could do a with a bit of a refurb and think about what guests need nowadays.

“A very decent stay” My family with children stayed here for a school related event near downtown. Check in was very speedy. You could tell the place has been renovated- there were a few small signs in the hallways of an older hotel, but overall a good remodel job. We were able to park near the entrance to our upstairs room. We found the hotel convenient to the Stockyards and downtown area- a quick trip away down the highway. Our room was clean and tastefully updated with white linens and modern furniture. The view was to an open field toward downtown. The bathroom was nicely tiled. The curtain rod was not hanging correctly-a bit broken. The sleep number bed was bit awkward- kind of kept running out of air- felt a bit gimickly and didn't contribute that much to comfort, but I slept well enough. The kids enjoyed the small indoor pool- we had it to ourselves, so that helped. It was clean around the pool area and towels were available (even though I don't find indoor pools in general have the best atmosphere). Staff was helpful/friendly. Breakfast is not included and the $10 buffet was too expensive for my family of 5. There are several nice restaurants for dinner just north of the hotel ,near a golf course (chain type, which I usually don't prefer when traveling, but nice) The BBQ place we chose had live music going on their side lawn- nice. Overall, this was a good stay for our purposes- which was a clean place to sleep at night between touring the many sights of Ft. Worth.

“Excellent Accomodations!” Stayed for two nights while on business....My room overlooked indoor pool and was very relaxing. Hotel was very clean including the room. Flat Screen TV and a very comfortable bed. Excellent service at arrival and departure....Lounge was nice and Bartender very friendly! Hotel is located near I-17 and very convienent for travel

“Great location in downtown Seattle” I've stayed here a number of times in the past few years. The location is awesome if you want to shop, drink, eat, watch a movie or attend an event at the Convention Center or the Paramount Theater. The rooms are comfortable and the service from the front desk and the valet parking is great. Internet access is now free (it used to be $12.95 a day!), but the valet parking is $42 (tax included) a day.

“tiny rooms” The first junior suite room we were allocated on the "executive floor" was tiny. I left the family there and went back to reception. I looked at the next suggested upscale suite and rejected that too. Eventually I gave up and we took a standard room that was a long walk from the elevator.

“「感じがいい」ホテルでした” チェックインからレストラン、ルームサービス、ベルマン、お世話になったスタッフみなさんが感じよかったです。朝、誰もいないプールからの電話で朝食をお願いしても20分ほどで届けていただけました。1階奥のレストランも素敵で、赤白1杯ずつ含まれてのディナー(お料理は選べません。前菜とメイン、デザートで)はおいしくて量もちょうどよくて$60+TAXはお得です。ビバリーセンターの前というのは立地が良いという評価になるのかもしれませんが、ロバートソンブールバードからロデオドライブまで歩いて行くと、帰りはタクシーのなってしまいますね。もちろん個人差がありますが。ひとつ残念だったことは、隣の部屋からテレビの音や声が聞こえてきたことです。

“Luxury Hotel - Comfortable, Convenient” Everything one would expect from an upscale, somewhat pricey, luxury property. Attentive and charming staff; comfortable rooms; nice amenities; pleasant views from lakeside rooms. Meeting space was good as well. Bar area served not only drinks but light food, coffee and decadent desserts. Lovely all around -- what you would expect from a hotel in this category.

“Enjoyable stay, one of the best hotels in DC!” Thoroughly enjoyed my three night stay at the Fairfax on business. Not a single complaint, one the bets hotels in DC, on par with Sofitel. Location is close to Dupont Circle, my favourite DC area. Service was outstanding throughout. Painless check-in process, got upgraded to Suite as SPG Gold Member. Everyone was helpful, from front desk personnel to concierge and wait staff at breakfast. Rooms are tastefully decorated and have all the right amenities. I was glad that I could use Internet for free, as SPG Golod amenitiy, extremely critical of most of US hotels charging guests for Internet, not acceptable! Nice building too. Breakfast was quite expensive, ate there only once. Lounge is pretty good too for drinks. Finally, the value was also great, booked directly on SPG site, prepaid rate was quite good,

“Posizione fantastica” ho soggiornato una notte in questo hotel prima di lasciare gli stati uniti per il paradiso polinesiano. L'albergo è molto bello, camere pulite e molto spaziose. Purtroppo non ho provato il ristorante. il personale della Hall è gentile e disponibilissimo. Wifi gratuito e Starbucks presente nella hall Posizione perfetta per visitare Los Angeles. Universal Studios ed Hollywood a 20 minuti di macchina L'autonoleggio Hertz comodissimo, a 5 minuti a piedi e navetta gratuita per i vari terminal.

“Good hotel with good features” I like the Embassy Suites chain. It offers a consistent standard across all of the various Embassy Suites I've stayed at. This hotel was no different. Very good comfortable bed, good bathroom facilities with plenty of space. The room was very clean and very tidy. The hotel offers an excellent breakfast which includes a cooked-to-order area. The hotel also offers a "Manager's reception" which makes for a great start to the night! This hotel is well situated for various tourist areas in Chicago so makes it easy to get around. It is probably also well positioned for the business traveller as it is downtown. As always, a good, clean, comfortable place to stay. Recommended.

“Very good if you want to be near Carnegie Hall” I got this room at a steep discount at close to the last minute. The location was ideal for me, since I was meeting people for dinner at the Carnegie Deli and then attending a concert at Carnegie Hall and this hotel is within a half-block of both. The room was on the small side, but still decent for a midtown Manhattan hotel, and it was clean and comfortable, though the mattress was a little soft. There's a decent-looking exercise center on the third floor. A few things you should know: Check-in can be slow, especially at the designated 4PM (!) check-in time; the computers in the business center are $.35/minute ($5 minimum); and you have to turn the shower lever all the way counter-clockwise to get hot water. Another nice touch was the bath soap, which was better than I usually encounter in hotels.

“Step back in time” A liitle expensive at £115 per night but worth it for the experience. We had three rooms for our group of 6 adults so we opted for one room of each of the themes 'Mountain Man' 'Native American' 'The Cowboy'. They looked just like the website. Attention to detail was fabulous and the service from the front desk and valet parking were great, I'd forgotten some paperwork out of the car and the valet were very quick to help in fetching it for me. We stayed on a Saturday and one of the rooms was on the front overlooking street. The music from the bars could be heard until they close all the music down at midnight. We would definately recommend the Stockyards for anyone wanting something a little different.

“Making Improvements. Solid 3 star property.” I've stayed at the Sheraton, Hilton and Westin at LAX. The Westin is the cleanest and most comfortable of the three. That said, LAX doesn't have a luxury hotel so if you are looking to stay at a 4 star (or higher) property you will need to stay at the Ritz Carlton in Marina Del Rey or in other parts of Los Angeles. Check in was fast. The lobby is undergoing a remodel right now, but it didn't seem to be a big issue for any of the services. Parking is convenient and attached to the elevators. My room was dated but clean. The shower had good pressure and the towels were new. I wouldn't want to stay in the area for more than 1 or 2 nights. It lacks charm. But, if you need to be on an early departure or you arrive late, as I did, it's a solid 3 star bet. This is a hotel heavily used by airline crews and business people. It's not ideal for leisure travelers.

“Disappointing” The location is great and the staff friendly but this hotel doesn't do the little things that make a great stay. We booked a deluxe room because of the touted separate walk-in shower. None of the other plusses in the hotel's own literature are worth paying a nickel more for. However, our room did not offer the promised separate shower and when we called to inquire about the mixup were told that "not all deluxe rooms offer the walk-in shower feature." Then how can you advertise it as a deluxe room? The bathroom was designed so poorly that the very large door, when opened cut off a full third of the bathroom making it impossible to access when someone was standing at the sink! The drawers in the chest wouldn't stay closed so we had to wedge paper in the corners to keep them from hanging open. It appears that paper or shims of some kind were used underneath the furniture to try to level it but the attempt was unsuccessful. Local newspapers were generally unavailable on the weekend and we were directed to a 7-11 down the street to get a Sunday paper. We found one at a different hotel and will likely consider that place for our next visit. Excessive noise was another problem: traffic noise from the street even though we were on the 5th floor, hallway noise and slamming doors, even the A/C unit made a racket when it was running. Definitely not a place for quiet relaxation. We love Boston and the location is very convenient but we will not stay here again. There are better options for the money.

“Decent place, good shopping” The Orlando's staff is attentive and helpful but as others have mentioned, the rooms are a bit junky for the price, especially the bathrooms. If you are there for shopping, there's plenty of good places around there -- Plastica, Built By Wendy, Paul Frank et al but other than that, the neighborhood is rather boring.

“Great Hotel, nice location and big suites” I've stayed at the Homewood Suites by Hilton in the Galleria area for 8 days in September 2010. Overall is a great hotel! Very, and i mean VERY clean, and that is the most important thing to me. I stayed at a One Bedroom King suite, room 1302 and it is really Big! i had, a small kitchen, a big refrigerator, a living room with sofa bed and the beedrom of course with a bathroom. Very nice view from the 13th floor looking at the Galleria mall, which by the way is whithin walking distance, you just have to cross the street. With a very few minor details this could be my favorite hotel in Houston like: * No wireless internet conection ( i had free wired internet, but it is very annoying because you cant move anywhere in your suite other than the table at the kitchen )... come on Homewood suites! even super 8 has a wireless internet! and by the way, a little faster internet conection would be great too, because the maximum speed i got was like 120KBs ... thats too slow in my opinion. * 10 dlls per night, if you want to park at this hotel, you have to pay this fee (in my opinion, should be free and for guests only) * Big old CRT TVs... once again, even super 8s has LCD tvs now a days (anyway i didnt watch Tv) And thats it, only this 3 complians, everything else was superb! i really like the free hot breakfast every morning. Also i got the USA newspaper at my door everyday, the recepcionists at the front desk always gave me a smile everytime i walk by the lobby. And i want to make an special mention, to the nice lady at the breakfast area, she was very very nice and every time i asked for something she go inside the kitchen and bring me what i asked for, ...she was vey kind, and also, she speak spanish like me, that was a big plus for me :) I really recommend this hotel, whether you are a solo traveler, or with a family, THIS IS THE PLACE YOU WANT TO BE when in Houston, Tx, because is really located in the center of all the action, rigth just in front of the Galleria mall. Hope i will visit again this hotel by the end of this year.

“Nice, Mellow Stay” We recently spent part of the week between Christmas and New Year at Barton Creek. The room was relatively large (tower room). The bed was nice and comfortable. The bathroom, however, was nothing special (a lot of cut corners?) with a small tub, The fitness facility had regular classes which we really appreciated (including spinning and yoga!). There was an additional fee for them (though the fitness room, which was well equipped, was free and nice too). The only meal we got a the hotel was breakfast, which we thought was excellent. We had no trouble traveling to Austin (this is simply suburban Austin) or to Fredericksburg (sp?), Enchanted Rock, from this location. We did not golf, though this is an emphasis at this resort.

“Yin and yang” BRILLIANT: Blue Ribbon is the hotel restaurant. You will stay in a lot of hotels. Very few of them will have a hotel restaurant as good as Blue Ribbon. NOT SO BRILLIANT: A television that didn't work for my stay, with the wrong remote provided and no access to cable channels. APPRECIATED: The hotel offering me free wi-fi as a result. NOT APPRECIATED: That it took talking to two different managers on two days to get that discount taken care of. The first manager offered an upgrade to another room the following day, which isn't really all that much fun when you've already unpacked two suitcases. GREAT LITTLE THING: Heated bathroom tiles! No, really! There's a little knob in the bathroom to adjust the heat, although I couldn't figure out how to work mine. UNGREAT LITTLE THING: No public ice machine, so the doormen would be summoned to bring up ice (requiring a tip in the process) GREAT BIG THING: A nice variety of pillows, both firm and soft, even for a full-size bed. UNGREAT BIG THING: The stairs smelled like vomit. THE BEST THING: The hotel's location, facing the Time Warner building, means that you're about 20 yards away from some fantastic restaurants (including Per Se! Come on!). There's also a Starbucks next door and a 24-hour Duane Reade (and a NY food cart that's open till 3 AM!) on the corner, and multiple subway lines are within two blocks. So it's a great place to stay in the sense of having both things around and ways to easily get away.

“Loved this hotel~” Beautiful exterior, pool and hot tub and outside cabanas, shuffleboard, even an outdoor tv area. Elevators were a bit slow during busy time but rooms were very well appropriated and beds very comfortable. Matthew the Shuttle guy was very friendly and accomodating. He took me to the Torrey Pines beach and to the Coaster shuttle very promptly. Barb at the front desk very helpful as well. Delicious breakfast buffet in the morning and nice bar for a cocktail at night. I will definitely stay at the Doubletree Del Mar again.

“Great if you are visiting Aon” This is the perfect hotel for a visit to Aon Center, since it has direct access without having to go outside. The rooms are very nice, beds comfortable, and staff is friendly. It is not huge, so you don't get lost in the crowd like the Hyatt near by. Tip: Do not valet park your car, it cost $58!

“Hip but comfortable” Impressive, modern new hotel that is both stylish and comfortable. Staff was friendly and accomodating, not at all snotty as in some hip hotels. Loved the clean decor and the bed was so comfy! Housekeeping comes twice a day which is so nice. Yes, the rooms are small but the norm for NY and well arranged so they don't feel cramped. Just remember your curtains - the whole hotel is glass and I've heard the view from the street is interesting as people often forget to close the curtains! Great neighborhood too, I would definitely stay here again if I needed to be in the area.

“Mixed bag: Lovely Room but...” A long review but trying to be fair as I am normally a big fan of this chain. Went to Dallas for a special art exhibit & just to play tourist & the Fairmont was within 2 blocks of Fine Art museum & had a great rate offer for a suite. Perfect! Then I read the TA reviews and got nervous, but as first night was at another hotel, thought I'd keep the suite for major portion of stay & look it over day before checking in. Did & everything looked great. Upon check-in, suite I was shown was lovely but was advised that the new Gold floor was open and would I like to upgrade. Looked at that suite - wow, stunning! Took the beautiful new suite. Really outstanding decor and club floor was great for breakfast & nightly appetizers. OK, so for the negative: room A/C did not work very well entire stay; if it had been summer, oh boy, room would have been unbearable. Gold floors were still undergoing final "tweaking" so there were minor to major inconveniences: no elevator one day-hiked down 3 flights to lower floor; hot, scalding water in bathroom sink one morning (yikes!) and sadly, not very knowledge staff in Gold Lounge (although they did refer us to main concierge for help.) Response to all our daily issues/problems was polite, quick & fixed as much as possible, but some things, just weren't fixable. So, while room was great & hotel is lovely, not sure I'd stay again just because, heat, A/C, water are pretty basic requirements & having inconsistent basic necessities really cuts back on quality of stay. Too bad because the Gold floor is a real addition to hotel.

“Nice Stay, But Missing Some Essentials for Business Traveller” I spend much time on the road and also like to stay in nice hotels when I travel. I chose this hotel because for this business trip I was traveling with my family and wanted a suite with a door dividing the two rooms to accommodate my daughter. There are not many hotels in SF that have this set up at a remotely reasonable price, so Monaco it was. As mentioned by many others, the staff are attentive and very nice. I stayed in a deluxe suite, which was nice - size very large, though when pull out sofa was pulled out, it was impossible to cross the living room and actually exit the suite. Just as the "W look" has gotten a bit tired as it's been adopted by other hotels, the "Monaco-look" (hipped-up Renaissance Italy) seems even more tired. Many minor annoyances in the room - toilet clogged up twice and the electronic door would fail to recognize my key daily despite protecting it from demagnitization. The bigger issues were amenities - breakfast at the Grand Cafe really is not suited to business travelers - very limited menu, very expensive, notihing really remotely healthy. The location of the hotel is actually NOT great - borders on the popular union square area, but really more firmly rooted in the Tenderloin. Homeless beggars are incessant, and any walk to the MUNI/BART or convention center is either very indirectly routed around tenderloin or directly through it. And I used to live in SF, so I know t he city well...Other "frills" seemed tired - the animal print robes were actually very old and not soft at all, etc. So all in all, a pleasant stay, but given the myriad of choices in SF, I'm not sure I'd be back.

“Good place...good priceline value” I stay at the Airtel pretty frequently when I am in CA. Overall its a solid price (great value using priceline, $60) and has a nice restuarant and bar. The rooms are large, with a nice desk area and large bed. Its right near the Van Nuys airport and close to the 405. This it not some plush Marriott, but its on par with a Radisson and chains like that. I give it a a solid 4 stars for the priceline value I get and the nice bar on site.

“pratique!” situez relativement près de tout, du port, mais aussi du centre! chambre avec vue sur le golden gate, chambre confortable avec tea et cofee facilities. le plus, c'est le petit déjeuné, bagel, gaufres,oeufs, toast... l'hotel est vraiment bien, s'y je retourne a SF, c'est la ou je descendrai!

“Hot/Cold” The hotel is labeled a "boutique" hotel although it lacks character. The hotel hallways are exceptionally small and slightly crowded. BUT the hotel was very clean and the room service was excellent. The Inc. Bar in the lobby is EXTREMELY loud on the weekends - has a "club" feeling. (good nightlife!!) If you are looking for a unique boutique hotel, I wouold recommend the Night Hotel in Times Square over the Time Hotel.

“Great Boutique Hotel Experience with Doubletree Brand” Stayed 1 night here at end of a family wedding weekend. The staff was fun and inviting. The hotel decor was fun and interesting. Room size was excellent and featured a large TV. Their HHonors benefits were great. The breakfast buffet given to diamond members in their restaurant was a great benefit. Location in Denver was great. I would recommend to anyone going to the convention center or need to be in Downtown.

“What a Great Find!” The Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue has many features you'll seek when visiting Seattle. It's smack in the middle of the city's terrific shopping district, so Nordstrom, Macy's, and many other popular specialty shops and fine restaurants are within walking distance. Just down the hill is Pike Street Market. The hotel itself is comfortable and looks recently updated. My standard room was excellent, with coffee maker and refrigerator included. The lobby has free cookies and coffee (for December, hot cider is served). Downstairs is a pub with reasonably priced food. I wish the hotel had a gift shop, but Walgreens and Rite Aid are within a block of the hotel. Every Red Lion Hotel I've stayed in has offered great value and the Seattle location is no exception. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Simply amazing!!!” The Royal Palms Resort & Spa was amazing! Its styled as a Spanish Casita and used to be the vacation home of a married couple in the 1930's. The history of the property is uniquely detailed as wall art. The service was exceptional. Housekeeping was meticulous and precise. For turndown service, our robes were laid at the edge of the bed, lights were dimmed and soft, instrumental Spanish played as we enter the room. The resort charges a $25/day "resort fee", which covers valet and bellman fees/tips. The room was a nice size....king size bed, Jacuzzi, walk-in shower and separate toilet area. The pool area was tucked right in the center of the property with wait staff ready to take your order or provide you with nicely chilled water with lemon. The property also featured a fitness center with room key entry....three treadmills, two elliptical machines and dumbbells with a weight bench. We didn't get a chance to experience the spa treatments, as this wasn't the purpose of our trip. The price list indicated higher prices Fri-Sun. The resort also features a fabulous restaurant called T. Cooks (named after the original owners). T. Cooks' service was enchanting and the food soared above all expectations. The "cherry on top" was the chef's dessert special.....caramel cheesecake crème brulee with guava puree. It was fantastic! The resort was about 15 minutes away from Phoenix Int'l Airport and close to grocery stores and other restaurants. The Grand Canyon is about 3.5hrs away. The resort offers day trips for about $150/person...the trips leave the resort at about 6:30am, returns about 8:30pm and includes several stops at various sightseeing points along the way. We rented a car and decided to drive up ourselves...the views were amazing!

“Lots of charm” Lovely hotel with lots of character. Rooms were small but we expected that and didn't spend much time there other than to sleep. We asked for a quiet room and got a back location where it was peaceful. Unfortunately our neighbours were not quiet and the walls are VERY thin. Cookies and coffee in reception were very appreciated! Reception staff polite and helpful. Got a great deal on travel ticker - $99 a night with $25 credit for food and drinks. We didn't even spend it all before we left!

“Convenient Hotel, Quality Service” I recently stayed at the Grand Hyatt New York just before Hurricane Irene. The hotel was extremely busy with people both coming & going right before the storm. Even with the high volume of guests, every staff member I came in contact with at the hotel was very friendly. Also, the large number of elevators meant that I never had to wait very long for an elevator, even with how busy the hotel was. This was sort of a surprise, since I've experienced far worse wait times at other convention hotels. I received one of their newly renovated guest rooms. The furnishings were very contemporary and comfortable. The bed was, in fact, extremely comfortable. Everything was very clean as well. In addition, the room had very strong air conditioning. This came in handy since the weather was very humid at the time. The one thing I would complain about is that all Hyatt Hotels still charge $9.99 per night for wifi thru T-Mobile hotspot. I wish mainline Hyatts would follow their corporate brethren at Andaz and make wifi complementary. The Grand Hyatt is by no means a 5 star hotel. It's very large and seems to cater to large groups & conventions. What you will receive is a solid 4 star hotel that is located directly on top of Grand Central Terminal. The people working there are very nice & the rooms are new. I have no hesitation recommending the Grand Hyatt to anyone. The hotel will be even better when construction is completed in the lobby & the restaurants.

“Noisy and pokey rooms, but good customer service” The street on which the hotel stands, Canal Street, is not for the faint of heart. I lost count of how many fake Rolexes I was offered on my way to the subway. Yes it was grimey and noisy, but it's a fun area and a part of town where you really can say that it's the city that never sleeps. Fantastic shops and restaurants are within a very short walk, as is the subway. But it is noisy at night. I think the hotel tries to drown out the noise of the traffic by making the A/C even noisier; and gaps under the doors mean that you can hear hallway noise very clearly. The room was small, even by NY standards, and the bathroom was tiny. A little bit mean with bathroom products - only one soap and shampoo, no matter how many nights you were there - and the room was never cleaned particularly thoroughly. There were still coffee stains down the wall from a previous guest, which hadn't been wiped away. The communal areas are fine and very clean. The best thing about the hotel was the service of the staff. From the barman, to the doormen, to the reception staff, everyone was friendly, helpful, and really made you feel welcome. Oh and one piece of advice - if you want to get Starwood points (this is why I'd chosen this hotel), you can't get them if you book through Expedia, as I had done.

“A wonderful hotel with classy rooms and understated elegance.” I was really surprised with my visit here. After staying at other hotels near the convention center, I didnt really get my hopes up high. But the Omni really changed my mood. Prompt check in, speedy valet, clean crisp rooms, this place has got it all. The pool is gorgeous, and almost empty 99% of the time. This is more like a boutique hotel amid all the other mega chains nearby. Cons include being close to the ballpark and Hard Rock Hotel (this place has like 3 clubs and 3 bars), so expect to hear NOISE Friday and Saturday night. Also they need a better restaurant other than McCormick and Schmicks, really, who wants to eat breakfast at a seafood place?? Overall though, this place gets high marks.

“Absolutely Loved This Place!” We stayed here in a suite for 4 nights w/our two boys age 7 and 9. Everything about this hotel was fabulous! We upgraded to a suite for very little extra and it was huge, clean and luxurious. It completely made the trip feel like a getaway. Bed was super comfortable. We loved being on the 5th floor steps away from the nightly wine reception. The goldfish bowl was such a nice touch. It served as a nightlight for the kids and they even named him Goldie. The location could not have been better. Steps away from BART, Cable Car stop, bustop, Westfield Mall, Walgreens, restaurants, great stores for shopping. But since it was off a side street, we were far enough away from the chaos of the main Market Street area. The free coffee in AM, fruity water all day, yummy iced tea 2-4, then wine reception at night were such a nice bonus. This saved us so much money in buying coffee, water and drinks for the 4 of us. It was nice to be able to sign up for the Kimpton In Touch club. This gave us free wireless internet which we used daily and a mini bar credit which also came in handy. The service at Hotel Palomar could not have been better. We were there on our 12th anniversary trip w/our kids and we had actually come to San Francisco 12 years ago for our honeymoon. They treated us to Proseco (not sure how they knew this was my favorite!) & chocolate in our suite, then snacks and movies for the boys. Rachel at the front desk went above and beyond to be helpful and make us feel special here. She greeted us by name and got to know our boys. I must say though that I noticed many other guests being called by name which is a nice touch. The entire front desk staff was so nice, friendly and helpful. It's hard to say what I liked best since I liked so much about Hotel Palomar. But something I have not already mentioned is I liked not having to wait - for anything. Elevators were fast, was always someone at front desk ready to help us in seconds, asked for things from housekeeping and it came immediately. Bell service came immediately. This is very different from what we would have experienced at a larger chain type hotel. I think the kids favorite thing was the house dog Maverick. What a treat to have him hang out at the front desk and visit with him everyday. The only negative we experienced was in the hotel restaurant for breakfast. We decided to try it and take advantage of the Kids Eat Free promotion. It ended up being understaffed that day and the service was both slow and bad. After expressing concern we were treated much nicer but the main issue still came down to not enough people working and one person trying to do it all. I will say at night the French Fries were excellent.

“Excellent” This magnificent piece of property is located right outside of Central Park and steps away from all NY has to offer. The rooms are beautifully redesigned and modern. Lights come on as you walk into different bedrooms. Door people and staff are very helpful. Bed comfortable. Very modern and trendy bathroom. Highly reccomend. Stayed here for business and didn't foot the bill but I imagine it is a bit hefty, but worth it.

“A good option for downtown Dallas” First impressions were not good, valet parking full & the self parking crammed with people (many already celebrating) in town for the Texas vs Oklahoma football game. There was a long queue for check in but the Starwood preferred guest line was very short. Actually, the hotel coped well with the influx of people, and although it was very busy it didn't really affect our stay. The hotel is very well situated next to the tram station, so getting around is cheap & easy, it is also an easy walk to the museums area. The room (junior suite) was large, but badly laid out, the furnishings were ok, but not much more than that. The club lounge was pleasant, but breakfast finished at 9am seven days a week, which seems very early. I was double charged for valet & self parking, which was sorted out on check out, but the next day I received an amended bill & it had been put back on again - not impressed!

“Holiday weekend in NY” My friend and I stayed at the Intercontinental on June 30-July 2 2006. We had an excellent time. I have stayed in NY before and the rooms are usually small. This hotel had regular size rooms that you usually find elsewhere besides New York. You walk into the room. There is parquet wood flooring. The bathroom is marble. There is a large closet with a regular door so the closet is fairly large. The beds are pillowtop with light down comforters and pillows. There is a mini-bar, coffee service, and a small safe in the room. We used the parking service which was $45 a night. Everyone was very helpful. The bell captain held our luggage after check-out so we could spend 4 more hours in NY. The doorman was nice and held our car while we finished our lunch in the lobby of the hotel. I got a great price for under $150 on a discount website. The hotel is located a block or so from the Subway. There many little places to get coffee and breakfast ( as opposed to the hotel). We also had drinks one night at Whiskey Blue at the W which was extremely close to our hotel. My friend goes to NY every year and she said she will go back to the Inter-continental instead of the other hotel she usually visits. My friend and I would stay there again and might go back next year.

“Convenient and Comfortable” Stayed at the BWI Four Points by Sheraton in late-November 2008 for a business meeting held at the hotel. Hotel is located on the BWI airport property and is VERY close. Free airport shuttle on demand - you call from the airport - van arrived within 5 minutes. Be careful, there is another Sheraton in the neighborhood and the vans look alike. The hotel itself is old, but it has been refurbished. My room was clean and functional. Wide screen TV, WiFi...all the basics. The breakfast buffet was OK - nothing fancy. Banquet food and service was excellent. A great stay if business takes you to the BWI area.

“A solid 4-star” We stayed for the first time at the end of June for one night in a junior suite. The space was adequate for a family of three, with a separate seating area. Our normal Philadelphia hotel is The Rittenhouse, but we thought to try the Sofitel as a less expensive alternative. So even though I should not have compared every aspect against the Rittenhouse standard (which is tops in the U.S. as far as I'm concerned), nonetheless I did compare, and Sofitel just doesn't measure up. Service was good all around, the room was nice enough, the bed was not quite top notch. Maybe that's it - nothing was quite top notch, which in the $500+ per night category one would hope for. A solid choice in Philadelphia, just don't expect 5 star.

“Good service but pricey” Okay first good things: Spacious Room, Nice Restaurent, Hertz Car Rental at place, although not in middle of uptown but easily accesible to Trade and Tryon with Goldline Trolley, Starbucks in walking distance Downside: Internet and parking are expensive, my stay was paid, but normal room rate could go up

“Will be back...” We travel to NYC a lot for business and pleasure and have always stayed in the Crown Plaza, but this time tried the Staybridge and was so glad we did. It is a few blocks off Times Square, but that can be a good thing. It may be hard to catch a cab at times, but the doorman can help. We were walking there from the train station and actually walked past it - so be careful if walking, we missed the sign. We called the front desk, but they actually gave us incorrect directions – huh!!! The included breakfast was great with many choices and the little kitchen in the room was nice for keeping cold beverages and leftovers. We didn’t find the elevators that big a deal as previously mentioned. It is a very narrow and high building, so the elevators need to make lots of stops. The front desk folks were a little gruff, especially the tall blonde woman, but the manager on duty made up for her. With so many choices competing for your travel dollar, Customer Service should be on top of everyone's list... Had a great view of the Empire State Building - so ask for this if it's important to you. We will definitely go back - a great bang for the buck!

“Nice Budget Hotel” We stayed 2 nights with 3 kids, ages 6, 4, and 4. The room was large, attractively furnished, and had the kitchen and bath essentials, including fridge, microwave, and two burner cook top. The beds were comfortable, though queens instead of doubles would have been better. The pool was perfect with the kids, big enough to enjoy, but I could have reached them in 2 seconds from any spot around it. It had a hot tub and an area with some bubbly fountains that they liked. There was a gas powered grill there, though we chose not to use it. The store there was stocked with things for any meal or snack, so you did not absolutely have to go out for food if you are okay with micorwave. Prices were reasonable. There is also a Burger King a block away for a quick meal. This is close to the airport, but also on Beltway 8 for easy access for othr points in town. Staff were friendly.

“Excellent Stay, Location at Long Wharf” We (family of four, children 16 and 9) had an excellent stay at Long Wharf in March 2003 weekend. We wanted to stay in Boston so as to be able to walk to places and this hotel sure fit this bill. We were just steps away from the Aquarium and a few blocks away from Quincy Market. An unexpected bonus was being only a 10 minute walk away from North End (Little Italy) and we walked there one night and that was very enjoyable--a very bustling, energized neighborhood with restaurants galore. We didn't have a formal meal, but snacked on some pasta, pizza and gelato which were excellent. I am told that anyplace you go there is very good. Hotel is also a short walk to the T to get to other Boston destinations and is also in walking distance of the financial district which has many modestly priced eateries (wrap places) during the week (but which were closed on weekend). As for the hotel itself--we found it to be very lovely and classy (but not snooty) and the staff exceptionally helpful and pleasant, without exception. We had a weekend AAA rate at $155 which was very much worth it. Parking was steep ($32) but also worth it, it is valet parking, unlimited in and out (in case you do have to go somewhere) and secure. (There is a public garage a block away which is probably cheaper by a little). The beds were uncommionly comfortable and they provide a very decent rollaway for no charge. The food: the breakfast buffet was terrific. It was $15 for adults, $6 for kids (also available in packages) and was realy, really good. Highlights were malt waffles, cheese blintzes, a small tray of lox (but always refilled), real OJ, thick strawberry sauce for waffles and blintzes--don't laugh, it was that good!!-- full array of other breakfast items. (They also ahd a Sunday brunch which we didn't try). The buffet was well worth the price. The restaurant itself is very nice overlooking the harbor, and the club lounge (adjacent) is very nicely decorated in a ship motif. We had a light meal there one evening which wasn't bad (but not great), but if we had more energy we would have gone (back) to Quincy Market for dinner. (Yes, even though it is a short walk, our kids were THAT pooped!!) That's another advantage of the hotel--you are close enough to Quincy Market, etc. so that you can get reasonably priced food and are not stuck with high priced restaurant. (Regina Pizza at Quincy is excellent). Plus, there's a 7-11 a block away. They have a great health club--separate rooms for weights and aerobics, which is free. And a very nice pool. Not large for swimming, which is fine, but great for hanging out with the kids and the water happened to be quite warm (88) which is even finer. I reiterate that every satff member was polite, friendly and helpful--from when we drove in, bell staff, desk staff, restaurant staff, concierge--everyone! That makes a difference. A very excellent stay on all fronts. Being able to walk really made it an enjoyable experience and the hotel was excellent all around. Will definitely return and heartily recommend.

“Standards as igh as ever!” Have been coming here for 8 years and the standards are as good if not better than ever. The rooms have had a facelift with new carpets, showers and artwork. There was a longer than usual wait to valet park but the attendant was very apologetic and welcoming. Room service was fast and the food was better than expected. The location s fantastic as the hotel is part of the huge Copley / prudential indoor shopping complex so every store you could ever want is at your fingertips. Highly recommend

“The best room in New York I've had” I liked this location; away from Times Square a bit, right on 6th, but close to the Theatre District. In fact, I saw a musical at the Steven Sondheim steps away from the hotel. The room was the most luxurious in Manhattan I've had; really, an apartment. Full fridge, great for a large group. Warning; breakfast was jammed and it was better getting downstairs before peak time, but the service was great, though you may have to wait a bit for a table. I only stayed one night, on Black Friday of all days, but a great stay.

“Dingy hotel although located in a nice location” We stayed here for only a day but didn't like its dingy feeling although the location next to the ocean was nice. We booked for a room with a view for an extra $10...but this was not worth it because the view was basically a small glimpse of the ocean from a tiny sliding door. Other negatives include: smelly hallway, saggy beds, no newspaper on the checkout date, $10 for parking, so so continental breakfast and not so clean carpet. Positives include a nice location next to the ocean and being close to many restaurants, including a Starbuck across the street. It is unlikely that we will stay there again.

“Oops! I used to LOVE this place!” Stayed Fri,and Sat. after Thanksgiving. This was our third or fourth visit to the Magnolia. We have always been impressed by the fact that front desk remembered us from previous visits. The woman at the front desk this time was having trouble remembering what year it was. She asked us if it was our first visit and if we would like a higher or lower floor. We had already expressed our preferences when we made our reservations. Our room was small,on the 23rd floor. It was right by the elevators,which proved to be a major problem. It was so loud,I kept dreaming I was at a train station all night. So,the major problem happened at the breakfast buffet on Saturday morning. There was no food! All these people are standing around the steam tables holding their plates. The restaurant was filthy,not a clean table anywhere. I called the desk from my cell told the same front desk woman there was a major problem in the restaurant and I needed to speak to the manager. She said the manager was at the restaurant and would call me back. The staff kept saying food was coming,but it showed one thing at a time,eggs showed,then potatoes,etc. These small dishes were shared by the 50 or so people waiting. If the manger was there,why was she not apologizing for this horrible breakfast? I was contacted by the manager who told me they were undergoing renovations and had no kitchen. They had to make breakfast in a room. They should have just cancelled it. I had to be somewhere and it was really frustrating. The manager acted like I was an [--] or something for demanding something I had paid for,like THEY were the ones inconvinienced. She sent some drink tickets to the room for the FREE happy hour. I used to really like this hotel,I was very disappointed this visit and may not go back.

“Very Nice Staff and Location is Good” If you have to stay downtown this is a great and affordable option. The rooms are spacious and the staff is really nice and takes care of what ever you need. You do have to valet your car for $20 a day, so keep that in mind, but the valets are quick to get your car when you are ready to go. They also have a free shuttle that will take you anywhere you need to go in the downtown area - pretty cool! The only down side is that the breakfast area was a little small for the amount of people there and there is a restaurant next door on the ground floor that's usually overflowing with construction guys smoking out front. Other than that - great place.

“If you work in music - this is the place to stay!” OK, funny place, a little tired and dated, but full of charm and history. The place is a favourite for anyone that works in the music industry; never seen so many tour buses, managers, roadies, lighting guys and productions engineers in one place - it was awesome. Beds are too soft, but otherwise the rooms are fine and well cleaned. Hallway carpets are very 80's! Food is good and the poolside bar is very sociable. Staff friendly, especially the ladies in the breakfast area. This hotel is fun and full of very interesting people - you never know who you will meet in here.

“Pleasant stay” This is our third time staying at the San Carlos, and it was pleasant, as always. We had one room, with two nice beds (no view). The room was clean and comfortable, and the staff is just great. Everyone is friendly and helpful. The free breakfast is a nice touch, but the food is very mediocre--various breads that don't seem particularly fresh, yogurt, cottage cheese, coffee, and juice. We ate it two out of three mornings, but couldn't face it the third morning. The other times we have stayed there, they have had the exact same thing every morning. I wish they would throw in some cereal, oatmeal (packets), and waffles (they do have a toaster). These things would improve the breakfast fare tremendously. The "business center" is nice--quite a few free-use computers and couches. We hung out there for several hours after we checked out until it was time to leave for our plane. One more thing--we were never supplied with hair conditioner in our bathroom, and we had not brought any, so our hair was a mess on this trip. If you stay here, better bring at least a little, just in case.

“Great Hotel!” I just returned a week ago from a 4 night stay at the Novotel. For the price it was well worth it, the hotel's website always has deals it seems. I had a king room on the 22nd floor, no complaints. Room was good size, nice hard wood floor in the bathroom, though the shower pressure will blow you across the tub, it's powerful. Comfortable bed, small sitting area with a couch, chair and table, minibar, desk, TV, iron, safe, alarm clock, only thing missing was coffee pot. There's no high speed internet access, only wireless, which I don't have, so I had to plug in my laptop via dialup, which worked great. There is a business center that has high speed though if you really need it. Wireless has a daily fee. My view was of the theatres which are nearby, Hairspray, Jersey Boys and Wicked. I can't comment on the restaurant or room service, as I didn't use either, but there is some cheap restaurants nearby if your looking for them, like the cafe/diner that's on the corner right next to the hotel. If you want more expensive outside the hotel, Gallagher's steakhouse is right next door also. The location can't be beat, only a 5 minute walk to Times Square, and the subway is only a couple blocks away. There's a doorman always outside also, and cabs are readily available. I found the staff to be very friendly, especially Kevin the front desk clerk. One downside, and it's really minor, is the two elevators, one from the street to the lobby (7th floor), then from lobby to the rooms, but the elevators come quickly. Late at night, they won't even let you up to the lobby without everyone in your group showing a room key, my friends who weren't staying there were denied access upstairs with me when we came in at 1 AM. I only had one problem during my stay, and that is on the late night I came back, my room key must have de-magnetized, as I tried about 20 times and it didn't work. No problem though, just went down to the front desk and got a new key in about 2 minutes. All in all a great stay, and I'll definitely stay there again!

“Probably one of the worst places to stay in San Diego” Only stayed here because a conference I was at was here - otherwise if this is YOUR money and you are on vacation, please do yourself a favor and stay elsewhere. First off, this property is ooooold compared to other major hotels in the San Diego area, the rooms in the marina tower are tiny and the while the front desk tries their best to trick you into staying at the Bay Towers (about 1/2 mile away) where the rooms are supposed to be 30% bigger, those rooms are even OLDER (if you can believe it). It's like stepping into a run down 1980's movie set. And while the rooms are bigger, the furniture size didn't increase and the room is poorly laid out so that you have big blank spaces of wall and carpet where there really should have been something else. First floors in the Bay Towers where I got shunted too (after expressing obtaining a reservation for the Marina Towers) faced the parking lot so any crazy person could just cross from the parking lot into your room if you left the balconey door open. Surprisingly enough someone in the conference said that the hotel cleaning staff or room service had come in, unlocked the balconey door and not fully closed the front door - how scary is that??!!! Front desk was rude too - when I pointed out that I had PAID for a reservation for the Marina Towers she said - sorry they had given up my room and there was no choice. I wasn't late or anything for check in. I was shocked! Parking at the Marina Towers is a bit nuts if there is a conference in town, they are doing some sort of construction on the parking lot (what I'm not sure - since i never saw anyone actually doing anything) but it's basically a dusty dirt lot with very NARROW parking spaces. There is not enough parking in the self lot (again if conference in town which usually there is), so you see lots of cars just circling around stalking people. Also it's not a very close walk from the self parking lot to the Marina towers. The parking at Bay Towers is a lot better - but then you're away from all the action. There is no gift shop yet at the bay towers (they're building it) and I didn't remember seeing any business center either - remember everything is really headquartered at Marina Towers. The good news at both towers. 1) Noise - while you're pretty much right next to the airport the noise inside your room is pretty much not there 2) Parking - it's $20 but for in and out privileges so that's not too bad for hotel parking. Good luck for anyone risking a stay here on their own dime.

“Clean enough - good location” I needed a hotel at short notice and, because of lots of events in SF that weekend, the only affordable accommodation was the Park The location is great, just one block from Union Sq, 2 blocks from Cable Car and not far to BART train and Market Street. Lots of shopping and eateries around as well as theatre. I had a room with a shared bathroom on the 2nd floor. The room itself seemed clean enough though there were some bonus hairs on the worn bedspread but the sheets were clean. It was basic as expected. There only seemed to be 1 shower and 2 toilets on the floor but I don't know how many other rooms were sharing. Shower was clean. Staff were helpful and I could leave my bag there for the day of departure. There is a microwave, washing machine, vending machine and free wi-fi for use in the hotel. There is a bar or something next door because the music was loud. Even with the window shut I could hear every word which went on until 2am so take that into consideration though it was a Saturday night"

“Room with a view” Anchored on its south end by the Intercontinental (its latest reincarnation) and the Drake on its north end (it's always been The Drake!), Chicago's Magnificent Mile is a classy strip of high-end stores, hotels, boutiques and restaurants. Located at its mid-point is the Allerton, surely one of the best bargains on this pricey thoroughfare. The Allerton's neighboring hotels include the more luxurious and expensive Peninsula, the Affina, the Park Hyatt, and the Omni. I got a great deal here on Hotwire. As an older property, rooms tend to be on the small side. Mine was furnished with a queen-sized bed (a king would never have fit), a minimalist thin table/desk pushed against a heating unit under a window (but compensated for with an excellent ergonomic swivel chair), a small closet of little use because the floor-mounted safe took up most of its space, and a bathroom with a full window view and a commodious marble tiled walk-in shower with a rainshower head and an abundance of hot water. Towels, etc. were plentiful and of good quality. There was a small shelf above the sink and toilet which is probably adequate for a male guest, but a female guest might have trouble finding enough room on it to accommodate all her toiletries and what-not. The room was supplied with four GLASS glasses (how I hate plastic cups wrapped in plastic -- something one finds all too often even in "better" hotels) which were replaced daily. There was a wall-mounted flatscreen TV which you could really only watch from bed owing to its stationary positioning. The bed was very comfortable, the white linens sparkling. There were an abundance of electrical outlets in the room, but many of them already in use and the free ones inconveniently placed for my Bi-Pap breathing machine. So, I sacrificed the use of a bedside lamp to plug it in. The bedside table was miniscule - so small, in fact, that the alarm clock was on the table/desk on the opposite wall. But the view? WOW! I had two full windows in this corner room and another full window in the bathroom. From my 12th floor aerie, two of them looked north down Michigan Ave. overlooking the historic Water Tower and on to Lake Michigan and the Oak Street Beach. With the exception of the occasional fire engine or police siren, the room was amazingly and peacefully quiet. There's shopping galore (even if only gazing in windows) nearby. There's a Brooks Brothers on the ground level of the hotel, a multi-storey indoor mall across the street anchored by a Saks Fifth Ave, a Neiman-Marcus on the next block and a Bloomingdale's further down the street. There's also a Polo Ralph Lauren store and Tiffany's is right there too! For regular, last-minute needs, there's a Walgreen's just steps away. The neighborhood has an array of very easy-on-the-pocketbook eateries. M Burger (think In-and-Out or Five Guys) has only 7 stools, so plan on carry-out. It's across the street from the hotel. On the same block, head east to Elephant and Castle. Gino's East (originators of classic deep-dish pizza) has an outpost just a few blocks away. Even Walgreen's has a huge selection of good food items - sushi, even! I got a veggie tray, a fruit cup, pita chips and hummus, and a yogurt parfait there along with soft drinks. Given the area's eating options, the Allerton's restaurant is serviceable but uneven and expensive with sporadic hours at dinner. I got an excellent reuben sandwich and lobster bisque from room service one night. However, the yolks on the eggs benedict one morning in the restaurant were hard-boiled, not runny. Another day at lunch downstairs, I repeated the reuben sandwich (go with a winner) with their excellent shoestring potatoes and a top-notch generous bowl of cream of mushroom soup. The $9 apple tart for dessert (which had been obviously nuked) did not come with the advertised ice cream but only a sliced, fanned-out strawberry. The menu featured "a trio of gelato's (sic) and sorbetto's (sic)." So much for proof-reading and basic grammatical knowledge, a sad sign of the times, alas. My 12th floor hallway would have benefitted from a thorough vaccuuming, but overall the physical appearance of the Allerton is very good from its motor entrance to the lobby, restaurant, and other public areas including my room. Many of the meeting rooms are named after noteworthy architects associated with Chicago such as Burnham, Wright, Sullivan, van der Rohe et al which is a nice touch.

“nice, but no free parking or wifi” the rooms are updated and nice. the bed is super comfy. the room was large. i also got a great deal from priceline. There is no free parking here, which is pretty unbelievable for a hotel that's not downtown. It was also $10 a day for wifi. I also felt like it wasn't as clean as it could be, but nothing major. the location was good-right at the tech center at i-25 and i-225

“Just okay.” We stayed at the Sheraton earlier this week and found the hotel only average and below average for what one would expect from a Sheraton. Positives: Great location if you are visiting the UPenn. Nice that there was free internet and the room had a nice flat screen TV. We paid on Priceline and at 70 for the night this was a great value, but if we had paid rack rate (249 the night we were there), we would have been very disappointed in the quality provided for the price of the room. Negatives: The lobby and hallways were not vacuumed, cleaned. The bathroom was clean but had old wallpaper, fraying at the edges, cheap tub. The AC was loud. There was no luggage cart available when we arrived to bring our luggage up. We were there for a Sunday breakfast and you had to purchase a buffet breakfast or order "takeout" and then eat it at the table. Breakfast was overpriced for what was offered and restaurant, like the rest of the hotel, felt a little shabby.

“Perfect Hotel Near Mass General” If you find yourself looking for a hotel in Boston within walking distance of Mass General Hospital, the Liberty is your best bet. It is literally next to the hospital and within walking distance of several great restaurants on Charles Street. The best part of a stay at the Liberty is the check in process. The first thing the staff does is pour you a glass of champagne! I never thought I would want to wait on line to check into a room, but with a cold glass of bubbly...I would wait happily!! A few things to note, there is a very lively after work bar scene (young professionals) in the lobby. Great if you are looking for that, but not so great if you are traveling with kids. It is also a pet friendly hotel so be prepared to see some pooches in the lobby as well! Rooms are spacious and comfortable. Some great views of the Back Bay area and the Charles River.

“立地が良いが、部屋は狭かった” ユニオンスクエアには近く、その割に値段が安く、お得なホテルではないでしょうか。朝食も簡単(パン類とコーヒー類)ですが無料でついています。無料インターネットは部屋で使えると思ったのですが、駄目でしたね。フロント付近はOKでした。部屋はまあまあきれいですが、狭いです。観光であまりホテルにいないのであれば、お勧めです。ちなみに、このホテルからシビックセンター方面ですが、あまり行きすぎないように。雰囲気変わりますよ、治安があまり良くないようです。ホテルも、ユニオンスクエアやフィッシャーマンズワーフなど観光地近くのホテルに宿泊するのをお勧めします。

“Surprisingly good” Recently stayed here with my husband & two kids, ages 2 & 4. We did not have very high expectations for this hotel, but had read lots of reviews and thought it was probably one of the better kid friendly centrally located hotels. First impressions were good as the bellhop & valets were very helpful & welcoming. Check in was easy. We were given a corner suite on the 11th floor. The room was not extremely spacious but was adequate. There was a full size fridge/freezer, dishwasher, stovetop, microwave in kitchen. A very small table with two chairs, a pull out sofa & arm chair as well as tv in living room. The bedroom & bathroom were separated from the kitchen/living room by a door. The bedroom was pretty tiny (we had 1 king bed) but had a tv too. No vent fan in bathroom which is a pet peeve of mine but not a deal breaker. Breakfast was very nice although very crowded and hard to find a table. They had fruit, cereal, oatmeal, bagels, muffins, make-your-own waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage, potatoes, coffee, juice, etc. definitely something for everyone. Overall, an easy place to stay with a family. Our room was quiet but we were literally steps away from michigan ave, Nordstrom, lots of restaurants (in the same block or two was Pizzeria UNO, PF Changs, Joes Crab Shack, Cosi, Jimmy Johns, Rock Bottom Brewery, Weber Grill) and tons more just around the corner.

“Great stay over New Year's” Got a good deal here over Christmas and New Year period. Like the Westin Times Square, the location is absolutely perfect, but the entry way could be a little better/more obvious if you ask me. The security was really good with a guard on duty at the street level all day. The lobby is upstairs in the hotel's tower so it's very quiet and away from the hustle and bustle of the streets of Times Square. The location is right next to the AMC cinema and near the subway. The rooms were very large for our 3 person family staying there. In a way, it's not as nice as the Westin in terms of luxury feeling, but it is very upscale for the average Hilton hotel. The only weird thing was on check-in, I had gotten there before my parents and they wouldn't let me go up to the room because I didn't have the credit card used during the booking, but that wasn''t a major deal. Overall, I would recommend this hotel to families and tourists in New York.

“exceeded expectations” Location in Little Tokyo on SE side of downtown LA is convenient and accessible. Both valet and public parking adjacent. Lots of restaurants and shops, and an easy walk to cultural center, city hall, and Olvera Street historic area. Staff was great, from checkin to checkout. Good value. We arrived early and they accommodated us graciously. Breakfast buffet in the restaurant is a generous mix of tasty American and Japanese dishes. Coffee/snack shop in the lobby offers continental breakfast. as well. Room on top (executive) floor was spacious, comfortable, and neat with a large window that could be opened for fresh air - live plants. Recommend upper floors to avoid noise. One niggling complaint: the iron was tethered to the ironing board with a coiled security cable, making ironing a little difficult. Now, the stellar: we had a morning meeting so checked out early and left our luggage with the bellman and told the valet roughly when we'd be departing. When we returned to the hotel after lunch, our car was ready and waiting with our luggage already stowed away. Top tier service for a mid-range cost.

“A review from your extended stay business traveler.” Don't judge a book by its cover. This is another 90s era built Homewood and from the outside it may disappoint at first. The property is made up of several separate buildings, some with outdoor room entrances from outdoor stairways with three stories and some buildings with unified hallway entrances to the rooms. I stayed in the latter. The hallway condition also gave an impression of 1990 with what smelled and looked like old moldy carpet but once inside the room and its a complete paradigm shift. The rooms have new carpet, marble counters, flat screens, large comfortable beds and other appointments. The bathroom was of equal quality nice too. One note, the microwave looked like it came from the 90s too. Without an auto rotating inner cooking surface it's ancientness almost kills the rest of the room. Almost. The outdoor grounds are a mixed bag. The front "lodge", for meals and check-ins is nice. The outdoor pool is good too. Near the lodge is a nice gazebo to stop by and relax after a meal. But the property also has a fenced off large square pond smack between two major buildings with floating algae and a spurting fountain that looks like it's working only half way. This has to be an eye sore to the owner and management of this hotel. The breakfast and evening meals offer good variety and are hosted well. The property also has an outstanding cable TV line up. So to sum it up this hotel gets it right in what is to me are the most important features, the room, meals and most of the property. For extended stay type hotels Jacksonville doesn't offer a lot of ultra new choices. Especially in the suburbs away from the beach. For first time stays be advised the southern edge of this hotel and its lobby borders right along the major street it is against. if you are driving from the east you could drive right past it because of it's small sign.
