If you miss the almost hidden entrance from the east you have to drive the length of the hotel north for its second only entrance and then drive back south to it's front .

“The good and the not so good” The location of the hotel is good...it is just over the Charles River and a very short walk to The Constitution, the ferry to Boston (which docks next to the Aquarium) and Bunker Hill. If you are not infirmed, you can walk over the bridge to Boston and walk the Freedom Trail in one day, very easily. The room seemed a little small in comparison to other Residence Inn's we have stayed in. It was basically in the same configuration as the others; a kitchen and living area with a sofa bed, a separate bedroom and bathroom. The problem with the room was that we booked a Pure room which is to be allergin free and it cost quite a bit extra to book this type of room. The room seemed clean enough until I prepared for my shower the first evening. The shower curtain and the liner was covered in black mold. I decided I was not going to take a shower that evening and I'm glad that no one in my family is allergic to black mold. It was late and I didn't want to deal with housekeeping that evening so I decided to take my shower the next morning. I reported this to the front desk the next morning and they were apologetic and said that the curtain would be changed by the time we returned from our tour of The Constitution. Upon our return, the curtain appeared to have been washed, as it was wrinkled and still had black mold in the same location, but just not as much. I wonder - - for the amount we paid for that room for 4 nights, they easily could buy hundreds of new shower curtains. At least the liner had been changed out. The bedroom had two queen sized beds, which were very comfortable. They were not hard as some hotel beds can be. But, with two beds, there really wasn't much room to walk and at one point I tripped on the bedskirt which was hanging down on the floor and found out that it was safety pinned to the bed as it previously had ripped the length of the bed. It was also filthy with random stains. All-in-all, not what we paid for. The location was good, the breakfast was okay albiet crowded, the staff was friendly and prompt, but the Pure room was not up to standard.

“Above average” The Nyma is a good hotel ,exactly what you need for a family trip to manhattan.It is well located,the rooms are clean and the staff are friendly.Well,not all of them.The guy who works at the restaurant should adopt a new service providing attitude.

“Good location but overpriced” The Holiday Inn Boston Government Center has a great location near Beacon Hill and adjacent to the Boston Commons. Convenient to the "T" Red Line. Rooms are seviceable, with nice views. Somewhat overpriced.

“Above Average But Not Spectacular” We stayed for two nights over the long Thanksgiving holiday weekend and chose the hotel primarily because of the favorable reviews on Tripadvisor. Check-in was quick and efficient. Our corner room was on one of the higher floors with floor to ceiling windows and the view was great. The room itself was comfortable with a large flat screen TV and working area. The bathroom had one hook, which made hanging wet towels or more than one thing (robe, travel accessories, etc.) impossible. The low flow showerhead was pretty wimpy. I've experienced better quality low flow showerheads at other hotels. The $14.95 charge for 24 hours of Internet access was exorbitant as well as the $50.00 for overnight parking at the hotel. Like others have commented, we parked in the structure behind the hotel for $30.00. There's a lot of shopping and restaurants nearby behind the hotel. I would recommend it if you're attending a convention. We got a decent, but not great rate by booking at the hotel web site, but I wouldn't rebook if it were a single penny more. There are too many hotels of the same caliber in San Francisco that offer better rates and location.

“Pleasant Stay” Was booked there for a meeting. Generally was pleased, was greeted warmly and room was clean pleasant and in excellent condition. The staff was attentive, though housekeeping was slow in cleaning the room one day, but did get there in that later afternooon,. Bed was comfortable, nice selection of pillows. Convient to Capitol Hill and Mall. Art and Soul Restraunt was good.

“Disappointed” My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel and we had some issues. First, I'd like to say that we've stayed at other Affinia properties (Affinia Dumont, Beekman) and they were lovely. We went to the front desk to check in and were told they could not accommodate my request for a room with a view. I said ok but was disappointed. They gave us a key and we went to the room to find that it had not been cleaned. We went all the way back down and the desk person then called housekeeping and had an argument about why the system said it was clean. She gave me a key to another room and up we went again. Front desk staff should not argue with housekeeping in front of guests IMO. This room was clean, but the bathroom was a major issue. It stunk so badly of mildew. At this point we were sick of lugging our luggage and wanted to get on with the day, so we called and asked them to clean it. They did clean, which helped, but it still smelled a little. Plus, you could see black mildew between some of the tiles in the shower - Gross! This was the smallest bathroom I've ever had and I've stayed in plenty of NYC hotels as well as hotels in Europe. The shower stall (no tub) was literally 3 feet by 3 feet. You had to practically be a contortionist to wash your feet. Luckily my husband and I are not big people because large people would have even worse issues. It was so small I thought they must have converted a walk-in closet into the entire bathroom. The main room was very large and the bed was comfortable. I just couldn't get over the scary bathroom. The front desk person at check out said some of the rooms have tubs, so I'd advise requesting one of those. To top it off, we were charged $70 to park our car for 30 hours, which is a good bit more than most of the public lots in the area charge. I won't be staying here again.

“Great Hotel, Great Location” I stayed at the Homewood Suites while at a conference. The Homewood was $50 cheaper than the conference Hotel, and was just lovely. It's located right on Riverwalk, yet far enough away from the main part of Riverwalk that it wasn't loud at night. I walked back and forth to the Hyatt for 5 days at all times of the day, and it was the nicest commute I've ever had (no streets, etc.). I was given a random complimentary upgrade, so I stayed in a 2 bedroom suite. The rooms were immaculate, and include a full fridge, a dishwasher, stove and microwave (and free microwave popcorn). The kitchen was fully equipped with pots and silverware, but I didn't need it with all the food they provided for free. The free breakfast was perfect - eggs, juice, bagels, cereals, fruit, make-your-own waffles, coffee etc. It wasn't perfect, but it saved me a lot of time and money. The free happy hour was great too. Free beer and wine, some snacks, and then some bigger entre - like a baked potatoe bar or enchiladas. The breakfast room itself was quite nice - a huge area of lobby looking right over the River. I used the rooftop pool and hottub several times. It is TINY. I wouldn't have felt comfortable getting in the hot tub with strangers, but luckily I was always the only one there. Likewise, the workroom is very sparse, but had 2 bikes and a treadmill which is all I need (again, while the hotel was completely booked up, I was the only one in the pool or workout room). Lastly, the staff was very pleasant, including the front desk staff as well as all the rest. I think this hotel is a gem. I only wished I had my whole family with me, as I think it would have been perfect for a family stay as well. One last comment. I had never been to San Antonio before and I just loved it. The Riverwalk was very fun. Touristy, but somehow much less ticky-tacky than other tourist areas. From the Homewood, you could walk all over downtown to bars, restaurants, the Alamo, museums, etc. very easily. It also seemed very safe, and I walked by myself at night around town.

“Great location, very nice hotel” We ended up here when the original hotel we booked, The Brexton, messed up our reservation and we were forced to find alternate accommodations at the last minute. There was space at this hotel for a reasonable price and are we ever glad the Brexton messed up because otherwise we would never have stayed here. This is a nice size hotel right at the Inner Harbor area of Baltimore. It has a lovely lobby, a parking lot attached (pay parking) and the rooms are clean and comfortable, if not luxurious. But this is a Courtyard and it's actually better than I expected. And the staff are very helpful with directions and recommendations - always with a smile. Oh, and the free WiFi was a nice touch. Walk outside the hotel and you are a block away from beautiful high end stores and lovely restaurants of the Inner Harbor area as well as the usual standbys like Filene's Basement, etc. A block or two away is Little Italy filled with what I hear are great restaurants but we didn't get to try any because Hurricane Irene rushed us out of Baltimore earlier than we had planned. But if we return to the city, I would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Loved the Affinia Chicago” Affinia Chicago is the best of the best. The rooms are in mint condition and the beds are awsome. The best selection of pillows that we have ever had at a hotel. The LCD television was awsome as you could watch it from any place in the room. The rooms are very large in size. We thought we had been upgraded, but they said that was the standard room. The employees are the most caring and wonderful people that I have ever met at a hotel. You are truly more than just a guest. Victor (doorman) is your friend from the minute he greets you while he is opening the door for you. What an awsome person. He really cares about each and every person and always remembers your name after first meeting you. You are truly a blessing for the hotel. Way to go Victor !!! Daniel and Pedro are also doorman always friendly and ready to tell you great places to go eat. Great job guys. Next is Milton the night manager. He wants to do all he can to make sure your stay is the best. He goes up and above the call of duty. He makes sure you have had a great day and if you didn't well he will make it better for you. He truly cares about each and every guest that enters the Affinia. You are a friend and not just another person. You are so awsome Milton. Kathleen the concierge is equally as good. The last minute we asked her if she could get us tickets to see Jersey Boys and she got them at an excellent price. Thanks !!! Now for general manager Tom Brady. He actually took time to introduce his self to us. Gave us a mini tour of what the new front lobby looks like. He runs one awsome hotel and it shows in the hotel and the staff. Yes there is some construction going on for the new facelift, but we never heard any noise. If you stay here you will not regret. This is a five star hotel and they have it down to perfection. Love the Affinia Chicago

“Wonderful oasis” This is the third time I have stayed here... I love it. I have only stayed in the Harborside rooms..so cannot comment on the others..but they are spacious, comfortable and quiet with gorgeous views. The continental breakfast is fresh and plentiful... We love this place!

“WARNING to Hilton Diamonds-Don't plan on Lounge Access” The room was ok, but was VERY DISAPPOINTED as a Diamond member not getting lounge access. The Hilton Website states: If you are a Diamond HHonors Member, you’ll enjoy access to the Executive Floor lounge, even if you don’t receive a room upgrade to the Executive Floor, including daily complimentary Continental breakfast. I have never been denied access to an exec lounge as a Diamond until this stay. When I checked in I was told no exec level room upgrades were available. Not a big deal, since it's space available. What WAS a big deal was being told that I couldn't have lounge access due to the lounge being small. I was told that it was a small lounge and the only people that got access were people in exec. rooms. No where did it say that when I booked the3 room (I was signed into my hilton account as a diamond member), on the drakes webpage or on the HH page. I have stayed at the Hilton chicago a few times and the Palmer house many times, and if I wasn't upgraded to the exec floor, I was ALWAYS given lounge access, and in fact at the Palmer house I was granted access to the lounge if I arrived early and my room wasn't avilable or after checkout if I had a late flight or was taking amtrak on a 6 p.m. train. If they aren't going to give lounge access, then it needs to be pointed out on their webpage when making the reservation, I would have stayed at the Palmer House or Michigan Hilton if I would have known that. Or at least give a voucher for an appetizer every day in the bar like properties do on weekend stays if their lounge is closed on weekends. The room was ok though and the staff was good. I didn't care for the location, it wasn't very close to the L. If you want convenient L access, stay at the palmer house. If you are a diamond and want lounge access, then definitely stay at the Palmer house or Hilton Chicago on michigan.

“great hotel!!” loved this hotel!! we found a coupon for €70 which we found to be great value for money!! the hotel was spotless and very stylish too! the staff were all very friendly and helpful. the location wasn't near much but there is a free shuttle that takes u to downtown and the stockyards. the shuttle drivers were friendly too and gave us some great suggestions of what to see and do! breakfast was nice and included hot cinnamon rolls and pancakes!! yum! definately recommend this hotel!!

“Excellent stay in Denver” My son and I stayed at this hotel for one night while on vacation. We loved the location and it's convenience to the 16th street mall (one short block out the front door). We were greeted by the valet parking staff, front desk staff, and other hotel workers always with a friendly smile and welcome. You can tell they have done some great training of their staff here. The hotel is very modern and clean. Our room smelled wonderful upon arrival (not over the top or too much but, it just smelled fresh). Bathroom was clean and had everything we needed. The beds were fine. Furniture and bedding appeared to be new and in excellent condition. The only drawback as other's have mentioned is that the pool is a lap pool and not conducive for kid's swimming (although there were some that were). This was well advertised as such on the website so I knew this before arrival. The hot tub is outside which was very nice. The gym/workout room looked to be state of the art and very large. Our price was a bit high but, afterall it is downtown Denver. I would stay here again and recommend to others.

“Quite alright!” Checked in late after I had been rerouted to LAX for the night (United...) Staff was extremely friendly and understanding. The room was decent, but looked a bit older than the other Westins I had stayed at. I'd say late 90s looking. Bathroom was small, but sufficient, and shuttle service to airport was excellent, though shared with several other hotels. If you have a quick layover at LAX, this is your place!

“Luxury hotel nicely located for shopping and the lake” The Ritz Carlton is located above a shopping mall so you have to take an elevator to the twelfth floor to get to the reception desk. But once you make it up there, it's a million miles away from the hassle and bustle of the street below. There's a relaxed lounge bar under a conservatory roof to grab a drink whilst planning the day ahead. The reception staff where efficient and gave us a mini tour of the facilities available - the bar, restaurant and fitness centre/swimming pool. We got a room upgrade and ended up with a splendid mini-suite consisting of a bedroom and separate lounge. The bed was luxuriously comfortable and the bathroom very spacious. The turndown service was effectively a second daily cleaning of the room, with fresh towels and bottles of water provided. All in all a great hotel for any trip to Chiacgo.

“Adventures in Gansta-Land” My friend came to Dallas for work and I told her about this place which I had read about. She got a reservation and we decided to meet for dinner at the hotel on her second night. I was waiting out front of the hotel restaurant (overlooking a Dollar General Store) watching for my friend to walk down the hill from the hotel and there was this group of crazy looking gangster types walking down Ft Worth Ave (very bad area) they were just hanging around, drinking out of paper bags. They were scary and I just froze as they approached. I was not sure whether to run or scream but I just stepped backward towards the door. One of the guys rushed towards me and got about 10 feet from me so fast. He thought it was hilarious. Tattoos on the face and neck and visibly wasted. He walked away and threw down his paper bag/bottle. I managed to duck into the restaurant, which was really pretty. But I was still worried about my friend because these people were just walking around out there and hollering at the other ‘ganstas’ driving down the street. She made it safely. Dinner was ok but service was painfully slow and they were out of the entrée I ordered. I only found out they ran out after waiting for my meal. They were a little unorganized in general. Waitstaff was nice. So I went back up the hill with her to see her room. Cute bungalow that was correctly represented on the website. The only problem is that it backs up to some big construction site and they start working early each morning. Later I walked back down to the parking lot and hurried into my car. My heart was pounding. It is just a dangerous area. It did not help that on my way out I commented to an employee and they just chuckled and said that the area IS bad and they see a lot of crazy stuff. The parking lot is mostly dirt and concrete chunks. It all seems so out of place. I got out of the parking lot and headed towards the highway and what the... a freakin’ sheriff is behind me with his lights on. I was worried but I had done nothing. He ID’d me and was friendly enough. We chatted for a few minutes and he said that they check a lot of people in the area because of ‘problems’. He thought I was someone who possibly just stole a car. OK. Well I got the heck out there! Bottom line, I think the place is kind of cute but I just don’t know if it is worth risking my life to go there at this time. It looks like it will be gentrified in a year or two. Loads of construction and lots of space for sale. Maybe I will check it out again in 2010. Until then I will recommend that out of town friends stay in the uptown area.

“Overpriced - Dont believe the hype!” Stayed here for a few days for new years. Had to ask to move rooms as they put us in the room over the lobby drop off. Rooms were fairly clean but worn. Moved to another room - it was better than the first. Nothing special about the rooms or hotel. Hotel does not validate the price they are asking for rooms. Plenty of other hotels in the area for better value. I will not go back again.

“Great stay at the Intercontinental Hotel!!” Initially, I was disappointed that I wasn't able to get a hotel in Times Square, but this little gem in Midtown East was just as nice. It sits in a (relatively) quiet area and was a delight to stay in. I booked through priceline for $150/night...which was a steal once I heard guests checking in next to me who were paying $359/night for a smaller room. Due to the circumstance of them not having a double room available, they upgraded me to a suite that included a living room, complete with sofa, occasional chairs, refrigerator, etc. Thanks Luis!! The staff was always friendly and helpful. The only thing I could say about this hotel that was negative would be that this place does seem outdated for 2012. I saw lots of cracked paint and other visual eye-sores that makes you wonder where all the $$ goes. The bed was comfortable, the room was spacious (even for this Texan) which was a shock. There was WAY more space than I expected from my previous hotel experiences in NYC. The hotel was in close proximity to great dining, subways, and shopping.

“NO AIRCON” We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights prior to our cruise. We were told on arrival that we had been upgraded. When we got to our room it looked exactly the same as the photos and was the same as the description of the room so could not understand what we were upgraded to. We had booked the same hotel for our return from the cruise for 1 night prior to flying back home to Australia. When we checked in to our room we found that it was very hot and could not find the aircon switch. We phoned the front desk and were told that there was only 1 floor that had aircon (their deluxe rooms) and we were not on it (we now understood where the upgrade was for our first stay). The room was so hot that we asked to be put into an airconditioned room so that we could at least get a good nights sleep prior to our long flight home. They readily obliged....for an additional $40. We are on our last leg of a 6 week tour through the USA (covering 10 cities) and this is the first hotel we have been in that does not have aircon. It is also the only hotel where we have had to pay for wi fi. I would not consider this hotel to be cheap either. We stayed in New York Times Square and paid not much more for a room, but included in the price was air con, wi fi, full hot and continental breakfast buffett and wine with hot snacks every evening.

“Rooms perfect but breakfast horrible” I stayed 4 nights there (139$/night). The rooms are excellent, clean and you don't hear anything. When arriving on Fridays or Saturdays, they ask you to sign a paper stating that there is a "no-party" policy so that the rooms are quiet, this was perfect! The staff is really nice and polite, the area is quiet even if you are near the airport. There is a rail station just 10 minutes away from the hotel where the R1 takes you to the city in 15 minutes (see the photo). The hotel has a free shuttle to the airport. The breakfast is really not at a level of a Marriott! You eat in plastic plates with plastic knives and forks and plastic cups. It closes early during the week so make sure you awake in time! They have donuts, toast bread, Philadelphia cheese, some marmelade, strange sandwiches in a freezer that you need to put in the microwave (horrible taste!), be careful if you take yoghurt since some are frozen (it's normal apparently!). And Americans eat waffles in the morning with whipped cream! (We have this for dessert normally, no?!) If you are European and look for bread and croissants, this is not he place to go. Also, the breakfast room is very busy on weekends so go early to get a table. Accross the street, there is a Ruby Tuesday restaurant: cheap and really good good, go there in the evening. (anyway, there is nothing else in the area ...)

“Needs work to be 5-star, but a nice place” Hyatt really wants this place to be a fancy 5-star spa/resort. They are nice, but as I find with many of the more upscale places, they charge you for all the little things, and that's truly annoying. $20 for parking (tiny spaces, too) and fees for wi-fi and the business center (with my Hyatt membership, I get free wi-fi, but had no laptop, so I had to go to the business center to use their pay machines). I think they figure since people are 'splurging' to stay there, or are on expense accounts, they can pick up some extra cash that way. There are a lot of people griping on here about these expenses. Hope these chains start noticing, but probably not....it's ok, no one is entitled to this stuff. But I always find it funny that lower-end hotels wil gladly provide free wi-fi and business center access to all, but when you get to the 4- and 5-stars, it's "Whammo, sucker! Fork over some more cash!" Overall, the location is wonderful. I had a beautiful room overlooking the pool and marina. Very relaxing. It was a short walk the next morning to the beach. It was cold out on my stay, so I didn't use the pool. Very short drive to the airport, but far enough that we weren't under a flight path. Shower was pretty good. Good pressure and temp, but the head was short enough that I had to duck down to get my head wet. With the location, I will probably stay here again, unless I find something comparable that doesn't like to play 'gotcha' for all the extras that really shouldn't be.

“More than happy” Simple hotel, a lot complain about the location, but myself and my wife had no troubles with it, enjoyable 4 night stay there before jetting off to SF. Penn station just a 5-10 min walk away made this more than adequate location wise. Room was clean, staff helpful. Recommended.

“Location, location, location” This hotel is all about location. Belltown has few hotels. Two blocks from the water, 4 blocks to Pike Market, 4 blocks to downtown. Rooms are spacious and lots of extras, but not terribly clean and lots of dings. Service was mixed with only one person at the desk at a time. Biggest downside is the smell--the hotel is above legendary steakhouse El Gaucho. By 6:00 the entire hotel including your room smell like cooking food.

“Luxurious stay in DC!” We had a wonderful stay at Park Hyatt in DC. Absolutely wonderful people and accommodations. We used Hyatt points to upgrade to a Park Suite and wow was that a great idea (if you do, remember to bring your bath salts). The soaking tub was fabulous and so very necessary after all that DC walking in 100 degree heat. Oye. I took a long hot bath every day and it was heavenly. The rain shower bath was oh-so-wonderful too. Bed was so very comfortable-- lovely down comforter. There are a lot of sirens in DC so be sure to request a higher room (and possibly bring ear plugs if you are sensitive). I used the gym (small but effective) and room service (yummy food from Blueduck tavern). We thoroughly enjoyed the tea cellar (try the "performance teas"-- amazing). The bell men were so courteous and considerate. Every time we pulled up in a taxi, they were careful to check the back seat to see if we had forgotten anything-- and we were always received with a "Welcome back!" and a nice bottle of water. The only thing I didn't like about this hotel is the bath products.My daughter and I just didn't like the smell at all. (It's sort of a masculine smell but not in a good way.) But Hyatt was kind enough to sub out the products with a spa variety, which was much appreciated. Housekeeping was wonderful and thorough. All in all, very nicely done. Would love to stay at more Park Hyatts in the future!

“A nice place” A nice property with very nice lobby area. Bathroom door a bit weird but not a problem. It was not quite as close to airport terminal as I thought it would be. Lots of parking and they wre quick to clear the snow. The day staff was friendly and made sure everything was good. I will stay again.

“Cool hotel, Great location” Stayed at the Clift for a girlfriends weekend getaway... Very speedy and nice front check in experience. The doormen were also great at getting us car service quickly. We stayed on the 14th floor- it was quiet and our rooms had decent views. I thought the room decoration was simple and clean. The decor in the front lobby is very cool and funky. We also came back late one evening and hung out in the packed bar- Redwood Room. We had table service and the waitress was a bit snooty- I didn't care for her. Overall, the bar was quite trendy and fun but be prepared to drop a few bucks on drinks....try the lavendar lemondrop martini...it's good stuff. I would stay here again and recommend it to friends that wanted to stay in a busier trendy spot on a city getaway. It was just a few minutes walking to Union Square, good restaurants and a ton of shopping nearby.

“Refurbished Rooms in front building Ok, Smoking rooms are total dives” I've actually stayed here quite a few times. The refurbished rooms in the front building are decent. It's nothing fancy at all, but the staff are friendly and will usually work out a great rate if you ask them at the front desk. The pool area is actually pretty nice too. They usually have music going and it sets the tone for a good party. In my most recent stay, I had a smoker with me so we had a smoking room in the back building. It's pretty gross back there. The building itself looks like it has been abandoned and the room was just icky. Again, for the $50-$60 a night range, my expectations aren't too high, but this doesn't work for me. Will I stay here again? For that price range, yes, in the front building.

“Great Time at the St. Regis!” We stayed at the St. Regis Hotel over Memeorial Day Weekend. Everything was perfect. The room was gorgeous and the service was outstanding. The hotel is so convenient to everything. My husband got a great haircut and I had a terrific pedicure and manicure in the salon. The spa treatments were execellent too. We ate several eals in the hotel. The food was overpriced but very good. We will definitely be back.

“Very nice Hampton. Great Property” Stayed at this hotel for business in mid November. Booked through hotels.com and had no problems (I did call the hotel to reconfirm my reservation for the week which I recommend doing). The lobby is very clean, bright and modern. Free wifi in the lobby area with access code when you check in. They have coffee 24hrs by the gift shop. Free breakfast is great and starts at 6am during the week. It has juices, coffee, assorted toast/bagels/croissants, and sweet danish rolls etc. They also have cereal, milk, fresh fruit, and yogurt. You can watch the news on their flat screen tv during breakfast. They have 2 elevators that I had no problems with. The room is very roomy for NY standards and has free wireless and wired internet. It also has a tv with extended cable and a work desk. The bathroom was clean and came with your normal toiletries. The bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet considering my location on 2nd floor facing 8th ave. There is the blue line metro station 1 block at 50th and 8 ave next to Rite Aid store. Enjoy!

“If you have kids - stay here!” From the moment that we met Steve at the front door, it was a family-friendly experience. He had my son help him with the luggage, showed him where the toy chest was, told him of a spy shop around the corner, and made us feel very welcome. Then we met Ernie who was awesome as well - playing versions of rock paper scissors every time he saw my son. Rooms were clean and cute. Not a 5 star fancy property, but 5 star for service and location!

“Good” Excellent location. We had a one bedroom suite....which was huge. Unfortunately, it did have a must smell which didn't bother us too much but likely would have bothered others. Still, I would recommend it.

“super gut gelegenes Stadthotel” das Hotel liegt super zentral, man erreicht in wenigen Minuten zu Fuss die Einkaufsmeile aber auch die unterschiedlichen Metros. Mi 2 Dollar fährt man vom Flughafen aus mit der Blue Line in 30 Minuten. Die Zimmer sind im gewohnten sehr guten Hilton Status und für die Stadt sehr leise. Im Hotel befindet sich ein Grill Restaurant das man, wenn man Burger mag unbedingt besuchen sollte. Frühstück, esst auf jeden Fall ein Omlet, eines der Besten das ich bisher in den Staaten gegessen habe.

“An Average Overnight Stay” This Residence Inn has an apartment layout. Finding my room was quite challenging and can be compared to entering a maze. Once found, I brewed a fresh pot of coffee but could not find any stir sticks. The kitchenette had no dishwashing soap which I needed to clean up my coffee spill mess. The room was average. I saw no bugs. Breakfast was average. On a positive note... this hotel is only minutes to Rice University. Rice Univ. has an amazingly beautiful campus; hopefully my son gets accepted. I hear that it's hard to get into Rice Univ. but God has our backs.

“Nice room, location, and service” Great Westwood location. Stayed here for Valentines Day. They coordinated a flower delivery very well. Room was nice. Secured reservation at half off website price using Hotwire.

“Not bad for the price” Was scheduled to arrive in Columbus very late and was leaving early the next morning, so we were looking for a place to sleep for about 5 hours. We selected this property due to the price and location. The hotel has definitely been used and appears to be an older property. The room was decent and we did get a good nights sleep. For the price we payed, it was an average stay.

“working on it....but still needs some work” I have stayed here twice in the past six months. The first time they were working on the workout room and the pool area so it was unusable, then next time the lobby was refurbished. It has a very modern, ecclectic feel, very pleasant. Both times the housekeeping was fair to poor - the first time I found a brown sock underneath the bed (unvaccumed) and the second time the desk area had water rings and crud on it. I requested to change rooms both times.

“Decent Hotel” i stayed here at the beginning of August and found the hotel to be in a good location, but noisy. The rooms are a decent size for NY hotel rooms and the fact the internet was free and always worked was a plus. My problem with the hotel is that it's right across the street from Ground Zero and there is all kinds of construction going on. There is constant noise from generators and dozens of lights blazing at all hours.

“2nd Visit Out of Infinite Future Visits” I have been to Chicago about a dozen times, and I have stayed at many locations. This hotel has served me the best for all my Chicago trips. I say that because this was my second stay, but it sure won't be the last. Let's start with location as this little boutique hotel is situated on the edge of Boys Town in the heart of the Belmont area. It is conveniently located next to the Belmont El Train stop on the Red Line. It is within walking distance to lots of great restaurants for eating, tons of shopping in the Belmont area, Wrigley Field, and, of course, Boys Town where many events happen all year long. During this particular trip, Maket Days was the main event, and with the hotel being so closeby, we were able to party and drink up the festivities without worrying about having to catch a cab or bus back to the hotel. Being so close the Red Line that runs 24 hours a day made it very convenient to travel downtown or other parts of the city. I don't think you could ask for a better location. The hotel itself is excellent from its cute covered doorway to the large mirrors that line the hallways to the welcoming lobby and staff. The hotel clerks and bellhops were always friendly and jovial, and I can't remember a time when I didn't pass by without hearing a "Hello!" or some other greeting. The maids were also very friednly and helpful, and they always made sure I had coffee when I requested it, which is a plus in my book since I drink it all day long. Like the lobby, the elevator, staircase, and hallways were always kept clean. The room was small but had a very plush queen size bed with a window air conditioning unit, two night stands, a business desk, a tall armoire for clothes, and a decent sized flat screen tv. I have to say that I loved how comfy the bed was, but it really made for a sore back in the morning. The bathroom was very nice with shiny white tile and glass block in the shower, which contained fragrant set of shower gel, shampoo, and conditioner. It also had fragrant lotion for those who need a little moisturizer to start their day. As for downsides, the room was on the side facing the El Train. So, one would think that noise was an issue, but I did not find that to be the case. Sure, I could hear it, but the noise was not overbearing, and the air conditioner actually drowned out most of the noise. I would also point out that the room came with very thick curtains to block out light, but since they were so long, they also covered the air conditioner. I'll just try to post them up around the air conditioner next time. Overall, I give this hotel two thumbs up, and I would recommend it to anyone visiting Chicago!

“Goof recommendation” Just what we were looking for after an evening arrival at SFO following the long flight from Florida. We were leaving for wine country the next morning, so our needs were simple - a decent, reasonably-priced hotel for a good night's sleep. This was it! Our room was immaculate, quiet and comfortable. Self-parking in the covered garage was included with the very reasonable room rate. The hotel is in an excellent location to head north out of the city. We had breakfast at Pat's Cafe around the corner before our departure and it was fine.

“Hotel was full of rowdy rugby players, but still a good time” When I stayed there the hotel was packed with rugby teams competing in a tournament. It was highly entertaining. Not especially quiet, but a whole lot of fun. I was part of a work group that wasn't especially quiet either. Let's just say we had a very fun Friday and Saturday in the hotel and surrounding establishments and we were all far more subdued on Sunday. We got a good rate and was a pleasant place to spend the weekend.

“Good Hotel in Great Location” This hotel is in the BEST location ever. The hotel staff was very nice, friendly, and helpful. Check-in was quick and they even gave me a choice of 2 full beds or 1 King bed. The common areas are very art deco style and cool looking, especially the elevators. Marble galore and immense paintings grace the lobby, and make the place look super fancy, but the furnishings in the waiting area in the lobby are more than a bit worn. The room itself was very clean and in good shape. The dresser and nighstand were scuffed up, but not in a major way. The bathroom was very clean and the tile and marble was all in perfect shape. We had a pretty good view from our room on floor 21. I can't say enough about the location. It is right next to the Times Square ToysRUs, on 44th St. This hotel was a bargain on Hotwire for around $188. Loved it! To sum up: PROS: 1. GREAT LOCATION- 2.Friendly & efficient employees- 3. Clean, comfortable rooms- 4. Price Con: 1. A few areas in need of refurb.

“very affordable” We had a great 2 night stay at the Union Square Hilton. The rooms were average size with comfortable bed's. Good city and Bay views and very good service from the Concierge and front desk. We had a room on a high floor which was great as it would have been quite noisy on the lower floors at night. Good shopping, restaurants and bars nearby.

“Great place for a family to stay” My family stayed here mid-June. I cannot think of a better place to stay- location is ideal. Several blocks to the waterfront, several blocks to the monorail, Pikes, shopping. A short cab to Safeco. Very attentive to my entire family. Also looked like a good place to stay for the business traveler too.

“Good, But...” Hotel is architectural and the public spaces are very nice. I understand the public spaces were re-done about five to seven years ago. In fact, a movie was being filmed during my stay at the hotel. The room - at least my room - was marginal. It was clean. Everything was as it should have been, but it seemed empty. There was a large bookcase and a secretary desk with no books and no scratch paper, pens, etc. What astounded me was that I learned that the hotel management company changed about five to seven years ago. Yet, items in the room with logo's on them (that is, hotel name) were still of the old management company. The hotel is located downtown. I had not been to LA before. I learned that the downtown area essentially closes after about 6:00pm. I walked around within a block either direction to find a restaurant or deli to get something to eat on my arrival night. Nothing was open. Walking more than a block from the hotel, I found the areas rather seedy. I think this hotel is good if you attend a conference (which I did), but it would not be good to use as a base for a vacation.

“Lovely hotel, customer service takes it over the top!” Simply adored our stay at the Omni Hotel! I'm a firm believer in quality customer service and it's definitely one of the attributes that I do remember from a hotel. Sure, you could have the clean, simple modern architecture but w/o a friendly face to greet you at valet, the front desk, in the lobby, on your hotel floor you might as well stay across the street at pretentious Hard Rock! (did I type that out loud, oops!) The valet offers you bottled water for your excursion, the bell boy is friendly, and if you sign up for free Omni rewards you get complimentary wifi in your room! The bathrooms are clean and well kept. The bed could use a little advice from the Westin beds, but they're not too bad. They definitely need to upgrade their TVs to flat screens. But the location is perfect if your stay includes a Padre game, a trip on the trolley or just running around downtown. Just goes to show that hotels can be stylish and trendy w/o being cold and snobbish! Yay Omni!

“Spectacular Hotel!” We stayed at the Renaissance Boston Waterfront hotel during our stay in Boston while we did some looking around for our March wedding - we stayed in their Executive King Suite. The room was fabulous! It was huge - a large living room w/HD flat screen TV, large window with view, nice kind bedroom with another HD TV and a walk-in closet! The bathroom was oversized with two sinks seperated by pocket door! We ate at the restaurant downstairs, 606 Congress and enjoyed the food and atmosphere - the service from all staff was 5 star all around - a great stay, good location and the silverline stop is right outside the door of the hotel - jump on that and your on your way to the subway connections downtown and beyond! Thanks to Lindsay and Karen for setting up our stay - ya'll rock!

“Excellent In Every Way” Just completed our 4th or 5th stay at this hotel. I host a small group of 15-20 here every six months. Since staying here the first time our group won't even discuss going anywhere else. The convenience of flying in and connecting to the hotel is great but it is the quality of the property, the staff and the amenities that make it outstanding. The rooms are modern, clean and comfortable with huge well insulated windows that give you a great view of the runways without the noise. The food in the main dining restaurant The Met is outstanding. The meeting rooms are large, bright and comfortable. Finally, the staff is outstanding in every way from front desk, to bell staff to banquet and AV. Be sure and ask the concierge for a pass to use the first class screening line when it's time for your flight.

“I cannot wait to go back!” I adored this hotel; have stayed at the Palomar in Chicago as well and it has become my favorite hotel chain. My room was huge and extremely comfortable. Seemed very convenient to everywhere I had to go-- I was there for work and was able to take cabs, but even cab rates seemed reasonable. We will be taking the kids to DC this year and I will not even bother researching other hotels. In my opinion, this hotel is flawless. (Service, amenities, food, comfort, etc!) Top-notch.

“Comfortable Older Hotel” I enjoyed my weekend stay at Westgate. For the $139 per night I paid, it was a bargain. Yes, the rooms will remind you of your grandma's decor, but they're very large and comfortable. My room was very quiet on the 7th floor. I appreciated the free bottles of water and the turndown service with chocolates. The hotel is just a short 3-4 blocks to Gaslamp which I walked alone and felt perfectly safe. The people were helpful at the front desk when I had questions. The $28 per day valet parking charge was a ripoff, but I knew it before I booked. I would stay here again for this price.

“Great Service - Small Hotel” I agree with all of positive comments about this hotel in previous reviews. I love Ritz Carlton and do not intend to suggest that this location does not live up to Ritz standards. However, there are some important characteristics of this location that you must be aware of which may or may not be an issue for you. I kind of expect that the staff will bend over backwards for your every need at these prices, and they do. However, that doesn’t mean that they do so for free. They will get you whatever you want, whenever you want it, and charge you 4 times more than anywhere else. I have never appreciated the significance of extraordinary service at extraordinary prices. What impresses me is extraordinary service at moderate prices. I realize that complaining about cost when one is staying at a Ritz is silly, but this Ritz is more costly than any other Ritz I have stayed at. I just want to prepare anyone who is used to paying $15 for a cheeseburger at a typical Ritz for the sticker shock; they are $29 here. Also, I did NOT pay the premium for the Park View. I was in the Superior Room ($995/night) for 5 nights that was supposed to have a courtyard view. A courtyard view here means brick wall. I realize that this was my error, since I could have paid 50% more for a view. So if you don’t want to see a brick wall, pay for the view. Otherwise the rooms are beautiful, comfortable and the bathrooms are huge. I had no problems with noise on the 6th floor. But the prices and lack of view aren’t my real concerns. The reason I would not return to this hotel is that this hotel had virtually no common areas to speak of. The lobby and the adjacent lounge are small by any standards (about 40 chairs). Their is a small bar that is really a common corridor that leads to the hotel's only small restaurant. That's it. The grand tour will take you 3 minutes. It reminds me of a nicely appointed apartment building where there is a small lobby and elevators. So the only thing we used our room for was a home base. When we came in, we went straight to the elevator to our room. When we left, we walked straight outside. There is noting to see or do inside this hotel (they do have a spa and meeting rooms on other floors). The lack of common areas in the hotel may not be a factor for many of you. I realize that many travelers would say that they come to NYC to see the sights, not the hotel. But why can’t you have both? Particularly at these prices. I like my hotels to be destinations unto themselves. If it is raining (like it did one day during my stay) I want an oasis from the storm. Here, there was no place to sit because the chairs in the lounge were full of people escaping the rain. For example, The Plaza is right next door and is about 6 times the size of the Ritz and has large common areas and probably similar levels of service. I can make example after example of nearby hotels that are bigger, but I realize they are not Ritz Carltons. If I had it to do over, I would have stayed at the Marriott Marquis in Time Square, which I realize is a whole different experience in the middle of the hustle and bustle. The bottom line here is that the Ritz is not much of a destination as far as hotels go. The reason to stay here is the great service, Central Park across the street and its proximity to many great attractions.

“Large Rooms; Excellent Location” I stayed at the Doubletree Times Square over Thanksgiving (11/24/10-11/26/10) with my wife and 6-year-old son. I booked a Queen 1 bedroom suite using Hilton Hhonors points. This was the only category room available at the time for an award booking. We arrived at around noon and our room was not ready, but the front desk agent took my cell phone number and called around 1:40 to say the room was ready. As an Hhonors diamond member I was upgraded to a King 1 bedroom suite. As part of a promotion, the hotel was giving children a “minion” (from Despicable Me) knit hat. The room was large for NYC standards and had a living area, wet bar area and separate bedroom. The bathroom was accessible from both the bedroom and living room. There was a mini-bar (the kind that automatically charge you), a separate mini fridge, microwave and a safe. DINING: I had free breakfast for 2, so we ate the Breakfast buffet in Gingers restaurant. It was a good buffet with everything you would expect, plus an omelet station. Although the regular price is about $25 plus tax for adults and $13 plus tax for kids. There are plenty of less expensive options in the area, including a Mcdonalds a couple of doors away on 7th ave. The hotel offered a Thanksgiving buffet for dinner, but it was $60 per person for adults and $30 per child, so we skipped it. LOCATION: The location is great, right in the middle of the Times Square area. We were able to get a very good spot for the parade at 47th and 7 th ave at around 8:40. The parade doesn’t start coming by this location until about 9:25 and lasted until about 11:25. We only had a partial view of 7th avenue from the room and wouldn’t have been a good way to watch. TIP: The police will insist you stay on the one side of 47 th to watch the parade, but as the start of the parade gets closer they stopped preventing people from watching from behind the barricade in the street and on the other side. So keep trying to get the front row in those areas.
“typical great service Hyatt” As always, Hyatt did not let me down. Great customer service, nice bar experience, very nice and clean rooms. Good location.

“Could do better, but far from 'scary' "!” Having transferred from the excellent Santa Monica Doubletree, the San Pedro one had a lot to live up to. To a certain extent it failed. We arrived early but were told our room would not be ready until 3pm. Fair enough. And they took charge of our bags whilst we drove into Long Beach, as planned. All seemed efficient enough and a nice location by the Cabrilla Marina. We returned around 3 to find our room still not ready. There was not the professionalism behind the desk we'd found in Santa Monica and we had to keep going back to the desk to check on progress. Once the room was ready, check-in itself was disorderly and confused and they did not seem to know what we were entitled to as HHonors Gold members. We eventually got into our room at around 3.40pm. Not good enough for a 3pm checkin. We'd paid for a marina-facing room with balcony. We found the deep balcony was shared with the room next door and much of the view obscured by a wall and this deep balcony. We did not want to share our paid-for balcony with others, to be honest, so we did not use it. Eventually we got coupons for a full breakfast and they'd already given us free Internet access which was OK. The room was clean, comfortable and attractive but dated. We were told that a thorough upgrade is planned, which is about time. No safe, no fridge, and worst of all, NO WARM DOUBLETREE CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIE when we checked in. I'll never forgive them. For Dinner we drove down to "Port O' Calls" expecting some twee artificial set up but found a huge latino party going on. With a massive choice of eating options, most of them involving ordering from counter and then finding space on communal white-topped tables. We found a tranquil waiter-service area from where we could comfortably watch all the fun. Scary? Not at all. Had some great fish and a really great time. It was just like fiesta time at home, sort of! We went to bed early only to hear fireworks and a band striking up not far from our window. Luckily the racket died down and did not disturb us too much. Breakfast was fine and the staff very friendly but not outstandingly professional. We enjoyed our breakfast nevertheless. A pleasant stay but it could have been a lot better.

“Nice” The Warwick NY Hotel was fine. Clean, no bed bugs, friendly staff, and best of all, great location. Not their fault that the no honking ordinance is TOTALLY ignored in this city! We were up early every day due to street noise. Taxi drivers are generally insane. Our 7-night stay went smoothly. My very minor complaints are: the lack of a full-length mirror, (and mirrors in general), in our room, and that the lobby bar always closed relatively early. Isn't this the city that never sleeps? No big deal. Our mini-bar tab probably made them very happy! :)

“Nice hotel in a sketchy area close to the airport” Clean, nice, comfortable, spacious rooms. Good bathrooms as well. The area is close by to the airport, however, it does look sketchy nearby. I'd recommend for a good, decently priced hotel near the airport. Free wifi.

“Best Downtown Hotel in Indianapolis” We stayed at this hotel over Christmas for work and I almost forgot I was traveling over the holiday. The rooms are upscale and the main restaurant had a fabulous buffet. I'd definitely stay here again. I've stayed at the Marriott, Hyatt, Westin, and Hilton but none of these hotels can compare to the sophistication that the JW offers.

“Expected more, just okay” Stayed here for 2 nights, we had 2 adjoining rooms. Quick and friendly check-in, friendly valet, nice lobby. Rooms were nice, very spacious bathroom in both rooms. Ordered room service for 5, fries on 4 of the orders were stone cold, ordered bread & butter which we did not receive. Caesar salad was made with very unfresh lettuce. Called about the fries being cold, and request that replacement fries be sent up, which we did receive. Was not really pleased at all with the meal. Ordered room service again the next night, also requested bread for 6, was charged $12 for 6 pieces of bread!! No soda machines in the hotel, went to Whole Foods downstairs, no regular pop is sold there, only "organic" pop (nothing to do with the hotel, just a heads up if you are a pop drinker). After staying at a hotel, you should have the feeling that you can't wait to come back and that you want to tell everyone what a wonderful stay it is. This hotel in my opinion is just okay, I would not return here. We will continue to stay at the Hyatt at Olive 8 where we usually stay.

“O.K. Price, Good location, A bit underwhelming” I stayed here during the week for business (as the Four Seasons, W Austin, and a few other five stars were wanting in the $700s for a room) and paid around $310 all-in. I was able to priceline.com this hotel with the name my own price feature for around $212 (just an FYI). With the valet, paying for internet, breakfast, etc., the total was in the three hundreds. I am comfortable with that number, however, it seemed a bit much for the look and feel of hotel. The lobby is nice and the location is wonderful. I was actually able to walk to my meetings downtown. However, the room itself is very underwhelming. The in-room coffee maker is expected, but the tiny T.V. coupled with the bathroom with shockingly bright lights was not. I was not able to test all the hotel's amenities, but it looked to have everything you need (gym,conference rooms, grab and go snacks/meals, etc.). Would I stay there again? Considering the other prices of the hotel, maybe. But next time, I will compare this hotel to three star hotels nearby, not four, which will most likely mean that I will be headed elsewhere.

“Stay away!” We were there for 7 nights Apr 3 - 10 for convention. There are some positives such as the comfortable bed and friendly service. But we had to call every day to get our room cleaned because twice they forgot. The hotel is old and tired despite recent renovations. The bathrooms are tiny and remind one of Howard Johnson's. The bathrooms need to be gutted, bathtubs changed and new counters. They do not have a signature restaurant and offer a limited menu in the bar. And absolutely unforgiveable: THEY DO NOT HAVE INROOM SAFES. The only thing going for this place is the proximity to HInes Center. But you do have other options: Westin, Hilton and The Colonade. These places all have great restaurants and bars. I wouldn't go back under any circumstances.

“Getting Progressively More Horrid” This is my second stay at the Red Roof Inn. The property is conveniently located off of Michigan Ave and the staff is very friendly accommodating. That is about it. The following things don't work or are not right: a) Second door or hotel opens at turtle speed. b) The elevators are chipped, scuffed, paper all over and dirty c) The hallway carpets (12th floor as a benchmark) are smelly and filthy d) There is garbage and random ice buckets scattered on the floor next to 1215 for three days of my stay e) Rooms smell This property is going down hill and down hill fast. It will be horrid esthetically in no time if the management does not start providing upkeep to the property

“Wonderful location - easy walk to shopping and dining” All Kimpton properties are nice, but the Palomar presents itself as a quaint hotel in the middle of this shopping district. I chose the Palomar over the Marriott across the street based on the quality of the Kimpton brand and the service, and this hotel did not disappoint. The beds were top-notch!

“very good deal” got a broadway package deal with hotel and tickets for wicked. beautiful location on michigan ave opposite Grant Park, right on the lake. the room was nice and the pool area was very nice.

“Stay here, relax and enjoy Boston!” The Taj is wonderful in every aspect of Guest Services and Relaxation. Check in was a breeze (they do had a $200 credit during your stay so be aware of this up front). Room was a Premier Park View on the 4th floor, ask for higher (some street noise). The view was very nice (large bay type window). The layout was very nice, very clean room and the bed was perfect with superb linen. The room was very clean to include free of dust. Some age detected on the furniture but nothing major. We were provided a daily newspaper of our choice. Hallways and room was quiet. The old school charm with all the dark wood and gold/beige wallpaper and brass fittings enhanced the feeling and experience. The lobby was very cozy, the bar and restaurant looked very nice (there is a dress code). We ordered room serivce (VERY $$$$) and it was quick, less than 30 minutes. The food was perfect but the portions small with basic presentation. There is a very nice Chanel store adjacent to the lobby. The staff is very nice and helpful. Direct access to the park across the street on your way to the Freedom Trail and all the local Hobo's who occupy Boston. Local shopping is all high scale, had to walk several blocks north to find a nice breakfast shop or starbucks. Overall it was a nice experience, we would visit again.

“Beautiful hotel , very friendly staff” This hotel is an old bank building. Gorgeous structure. Staff is very helpful friendly and really responded beautifully in the blackout. This was also one of the only downtown hotels that had good emergency power. We still had an elevator, lights in lobby, stairs and corridors. It made surviving the outage much easier than it might have been otherwise. Lower level rooms have better sound proofing from street noise. Third floor was quiet. Room right above on 12th floor had more street noise. Negatives would be the $30 a day for valet and small standard rooms. Very small. And no wi-fi in the rooms, only in lobby. That was disappointing.

“Friendly staff...clean hotel” On our (bit early) arrival, we were greeted by Mike, very friendly, who asked us to hold for a minute while he checked a room for us. He wanted to upgrade us since we were platinum members. We received a one bedroom suite, which is great for an extended stay. One evening when we came in we were greeted by Chris, also quite friendly, who gave us some useful information on some restaurant specials while we were in town. We took advantage of complimentary DVDs during our stay as well as the comped washer/dryer faciltiies. Yes, we would stay there again.

“Ordentliches Hotel in prima Lage” Wir waren für zwei Tage im W Seattle und hatten ein Zimmer mit Aussicht auf die Stadt und das Wasser - das war natürlich toll. Grundsätzlich ist das W in Seattle nicht so durchgestylt wie die anderen W-Hotels, also eher normal. Sehr ordentlich. Die Zimmer erstaunlich geräumig für W. Der Eingangsbereich ist etwas merkwürdig - von der 4th Avenue aus muss man über fiese Treppen zur Lobby, und von der Nebenstraße durch einen kleinen Seiteneingang sein Gepäck in die Lobby zwängen - also die Gestaltung des Empfangsbereich ist wirklich sehr merkwürdig. Auf den Zimmern gibt es keine Kaffeemaschine - das war SEHR ungewöhnlich, gibt es die in den USA doch sonst in jedem Motel... Aber es gibt immer frischen Kaffee unten in der Lobby umsonst. Das Hotel liegt prima, um an der Waterfront abends Essen zu gehen oder sonst auch die Stadt zu erkunden. Wir fuhren mit der Straßenbahn (lightrail) direkt vom Flughafen zum Hotel (einen Block die Straße hochlaufen) - das war klasse. Und mit 2.75 USD unschlagbar preiswert. Würde dieses Hotel in Seattle wirklich weiterempfehlen und dort wieder übernachten, wenn der Preis ok ist. Klasse ist natürlich der Acura- Shuttle-Service, den auch dieses W-Hotel hat. Da braucht man dann für innerstädtische Fahrten kein Taxi oder so. Wunderbar.

“I've had better experiences” I have learned here to ask for one of the renovated rooms. After getting to my room I found a hair in the tub and it just didn't look clean to me. I asked housekeeping to reclean the tub which they did. When I climbed in to bed in the evening there was something grainy in the bed which looked like salt or sugar. I asked that my sheets be replaced and they were. Staff were friendly and helpful. There was pool noice until about 10:00 but then it quited down. Breakfast seemed a little overpriced.

“Great Hilton Garden Inn.” 1 night stay on day of Hurricane Sandy, got a really good rate at 7am on Hilton site $159.00, by 3pm rate was up to $399.00. Arrived 5pm, check in quick got nice clean room with comfortable king on 22nd floor with great view of Empire State building. Fridge and microwave are nice touch. Free WSJ in lobby next morning, I will stay here again.

“Perfect location just steps from the AMNH and Central Park” In Manhattan on business, we were booked at the Excelsior by someone else and were really happy with the location and atmosphere upon check-in. We were surprised to enter our room and see that it was a two room suite on the front corner of the building with windows on 3 sides. There are French doors to the large king bedroom from the adequate sized living/sitting area and it's large windows overlooking the museum's picturesque grounds. We stayed for several nights and really loved the neighborhood - typical upper west side - near the park with eateries, bakeries, shops, pharmacies and dry cleaners everywhere. There is a dog park on the museum grounds which we enjoyed watching from our giant window-seats. We extended our stay - thinking we'd be moving to a cheaper room - and discovered that this hotel was not outrageously priced AT ALL and we could actually stay put. Grrrreat place!

“Exquisite service trumps problems with gadgetry” The "new" Plaza is quite nice. The rooms are clean, the bathrooms are beautiful, the service is on par with a Four Seasons. Never knew about car service or would have used it. The butler phoned 5 minutes after we checked in to see if we needed anything. Location can't be beat. The electronic room panel never quite worked to our satisfaction, but if you can get around that, you're good to go. (controls lights, heat, and tv) Service in the Oak Room for a late night hot chocolate was quite attentive even though the room was full.The champagne bar service was a little slow on a busy Friday night, but the food we ordered there was good, and the view of the lobby was fun. Room service was good, other than on one day (of 5) when I had to wait 45 minutes for a pot of coffee. Can't say enough about concierge service - spot on about everything they recommended and it showed that they had visited the places they recommended unlike many others. Although there were no longer any park view rooms, our view of the inner courtyard was actually quite nice - and QUIET! Internet only worked once - apparently this is being worked on.

“Big rooms; not the best choice for kids” They try - really. It just doesn't quite work for kids; I'm not certain why. We've stayed here a few times. Rooms are huge. Two bathrooms is a nice touch, great tolietries and amenities. Cotton candy and a goody bag are given to the kids (sometimes, we've found it to be a little inconsistent when checking in). Check in can be a little pretentious - it takes a lot for me to say that given some of the places we've stayed in around the world with our children. Great room service and nice to have a big kitchen. Excellent views, comfortable beds. Why am I not impressed? Again, not sure. No hot tub bugged the girls a little. I like the area and I love the size of the room. Obviously, this is a pricey hotel comparable with the Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons. Let's just say that the girls would rather stay in a smaller room at the Four Seasons than a palatial rooms at the Trump.

“This isn't the Grand Hyatt” It's okay. Your basic Hyatt. But don't confuse this hotel with the other that is close to the Convention Center. The front desk personnel were extraordinarily helpful - including printing out a boarding pass for my flight home when I hadn't had time to do so and was running late at check out. The views from the rooms that face into the hotel can be a little unnerving! ;) Be sure you are dressed appropriately if you open the curtains.

“Great Stay” A very nice hotel, somewhat similar to an Embassy Suites (except that breakfast is not included unless you are Hilton Gold or Diamond). I found the room to be large (separate living room and bedroom, with a fairly large bathroom) and experienced no noise problem. Wireless internet costs $9.95/day unless you are Gold or Diamond. My room was close to the point of needing a facelift (wallpaper and carpet getting dated), but the room was clean and comfortable. The buffet breakfast was also good. I would stay here again.

“Excellent value in mid-town NYC” Nice, clean hotel located on a quiet side street (W 35th). It is located half a block from Macy's and 2 blocks from Madison Square Garden. You can walk to Times Square in about 10 minutes. There is a subway line right outside the hotel. Penn Station is about a 5 minute walk away. The hotel gets a 5 star rating because of the location, price (around $160 per night), pleasent staff and cleanliness.The free internet was a nice touch as well. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who isn't going to be spending much time in their hotel room but need a good value hotel in a great location.

“Well run Hampton Inn” I stayed here during Super Bowl weekend in Indy. The hotel was very clean, the staff was extremely friendly and helpful, and the location was easy to get in and out of. I will definitely stay here again when I am in the area on business.

“Great location, great service and nice spacious rooms” This hotel is in a great location. Close to Millenium Park, close to Michigan Avenue and everywhere else. I have read some reviews describing it as out of the way but I certainly did not find it to be the case. Beds were comfortable and there is a Nespresso machine for coffee. Bathroom is spacious. My only complaint is that there is very little in storage space in the room - I like using drawers to put things in and there was literally the night table and nothing else. There are plenty of places to put your luggage though. Breakfast buffet is a bit on the pricey side at $29 but the high quality of the food made it worth it. We came downstairs a bit too early (30 minutes) on the Monday to the restaurant for a quick breakfast, they weren't open yet but the manager came running over and said he would have the staff (they were setting up) make us a coffee and then he also told us to help ourselves to something in the buffet. We did not want to take advantage of them so we grabbed a couple bagels. I gave them my room number and told them to charge me and they said no no there's no charge. That's great service. Our rooms were cleaned efficiently. For those who get parcels delivered be warned - there is a $5 per package fee and ...this surprised me... they return parcels after 10 days.

“Amazing Hotel” I arrived in the pouring rain after a horrible day at work, feeling really sick, and the check-in was so quick and friendly. The woman asked how my trip was, if I needed a map of the area, a dinner recommendation, just was really really nice. The room was great- and the bed was so comfortable. I was very sick and I still slept amazingly. The room service was up in close to 15 minutes- and I had a great salad for dinner. The next morning, check-out again was very fast and friendly. They seemed genuinely happy that you were staying there. It was a great value. For those who are not familiar with Boston, it is a great location walking distance to the North Station Bars, the North End, and the Faneuil Hall.

“Best in Philly” No question this is the best hotel in Philly and it has been for a long time. I have stayed here many times since the 90's and have also stayed at other top hotels in the city, but this is the cream of the crop. The service is superbly delivered from an obviously well trained and motivated team of professionals, the rooms are extremely comfortable and well appointed (get a fountain view if available). Great everything. If you're not on a tight budget, this is it. Although for 500/night, I was surprised they still charge 10/night for WiFi access!

“Excellent Hotel” Stayed for 2 nights in December, 2007. Excellent, excellent hotel. Yes, it's pricey but fairly standard rate for this quality of hotel in DC. The rooms have a sitting area with flat screen tv. Separate bedroom with tv. Nice size bathroom. Comfortable beds with white bedding and lots of pillows. Fridge and microwave. Clean. Nice, decent size rooms. High speed internet available in the room (they have the cord ready for you). It did cost me $20 for the internet for the two days but good high speed connection. They do have computer kiosks in the lobby area for guests to use if you don't bring your laptop-not sure if there's a fee or not. Several elevators. Pay for view movies are available in the rooms if that appeals to you. Basement area is where the meeting rooms are located. Has an excellent free breakfast in the morning. Located within a couple blocks of metro which will get you to major sites. Starbucks located directly across the street. Also has a gift shop inside and a restaurant and bar but within easy walking distance of many, many restaurants and bars of various ethnicities and choices. Also within walking distance of Verizon Center and close to Convention Center. There is a building under construction next door which should only be a problem if you're looking to sleep in and get a room on that side. I had a room on that side but was there for business so was up by 7 am each morning. Construction usually started after 7 am and was done by 6 pm in the evening so I really didn't notice it. it's otherwise located in a quieter section of town. Very friendly staff. Probably one of my absolute faves that I've stayed at in DC.

“Great hotel in Superb Location” My wife and I stayed in the Lenox Hotel between Thursday May 15 and Sat May 17. We had a great experience. We would recommend this hotel to everyone visiting Boston. Room We had a double room on the 10th floor with two windows. The room is reasonable size in the Boston metro area. Not huge but big enough. It is nicely furnished. Room was super clean. The maid came to clean the room multiple times each day. They restock the bottle water, clean the bathroom and towels, and refresh the bed and bath robes. Free Wifi was available throughout the hotel. I believe that exercise facility was available also, but we did not use that. Service ALL the hotel works were very professional -- from bell boys to check-in counter to maid service. Always helpful and always smiling. The front desk was very efficient. We did not waited for long for anything. I am very happy that we were able to check in 7:30AM in the morning. That enable us to take a shower and have a full day to activities. Location The hotel is near the Back Bay Area in Boston. Near the Boston Public Library and the Green Line on the T (subway). The hotel is next to the Newbury Street shopping area, the Prudential Center shopping, Copley Place and the Duck Tour starting point. Boston Common, Faneuil Hall, Freedom Trail, Boston Harbor and Convention Center, and MIT can easily be reached via the T. Transportation We took the Silver Line, to the Red Line, to the Green Line on the T to the hotel. Easy, cheap and fast. No problem at all. We took the T everywhere and did not try taxi or bus.

“Gute Lage” Die Lage ist einfach super, das Motel 6 Los Angeles Hollywood liegt direkt am Hollywood Bvld. Man kann zu Fuss die meisten touristischen Ziele bequem erreichen. Die Zimmer sind für Kurzaufenthalte (1-2 Nächte) ausreichend groß. Insgesamt darf man nicht zu viel erwarten. Wer schon einige Aufenthalte in anderen Motel 6 hinter sich hat, kennt auch dieses, da es eine standartisierte Ausstattung hat. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und hat uns noch einige Restaurantempfehlungen mit auf den Weg gegeben. WLAN ist gratis.

“Great location, great service!” This hotel is in the best location! It is walking distance from just about everything you want to see. Service was very attentive and the food was excellent. We were upgraded when we arrived with the American Express Platinum program. We were also upgraded a second time to a lovely room when our neighbors were too noisy in the next room. Not their fault, but they were willing to help. Great view of the White House!

“Solid, reliable, convenient” I've stayed here several times, most recently last week. This is a large Hyatt that caters to meetings and conventions. It is not the most central place to stay for tourists, but the location is not too bad, and it is directly connected to the Metro. The rooms are standard Hyatt. I've not had trouble with noise, and I've found the staff generally friendly. Internet is not free, but works well. Fitness center costs $10/day, well equipped, pool. Room service and food service generally is expensive for what you get. Overall, this is a solid, reliable place to stay; I would stay here again (and probably will)
“割り切りができればお勧めします” 最寄りの地下鉄からは徒歩10分くらいです。朝食付きですが質素です。ワッフルは自分で焼きます。早めにいかないと食べるものがなくなってしまいます。部屋はただ寝るだけ。

“Just Ok...” It wasn't amazing, and it wasn't bad. "Just ok" is how I would characterize my feelings about the property. Check-in was easy and the staff was very helpful and friendly. I had a double room on the first floor of the Point Loma Building. The bed was comfortable but I could have done without the green bedspread. It looked very old and I wasn't 100% confident that it was cleaned on a daily basis or at minimum, in between guests. The ambiance is pretty plain and the bathroom very small. They currently have a "water-saving" feature on the shower so the water pressure wasn't that great. I was able to enjoy breakfast and dinner and it was very good. At the front desk, there is a card that encourages individuals to place a review on tripadvisor which is why there are several new reviews. I would stay here again, but only if I absolutely had to.

“Great weekend get away” My husband and I live in Austin and decided to drive the 90 miles to San Antonio for a long, relaxing weekend. The Westin turned out to be pefect. Positives: Lovely hotel with great grounds for walking. Adult only pool was not crowded and the waiters come right to you. I never wanted for anything. Francesca's at Sunset, although pricey, was excellent. The best corn bread we've ever had. And try the sea bass...very good. The spa is excellent as well. We had great massages. Staff was friendly, helpful and abundant. The room was clean and large. Negatives: We paid for the club level room, and although our view of the hill country was beautiful, I'm not sure the room was THAT much better than the regular priced rooms. We did have access to free cocktails from 5-7 pm, but the room was so crowded that we didn't have a place to sit down. The kid pool seemed a bit small. We didn't bring our 4 year old, and I'm not sure I would. Honestly, if you have kids and are going to San Antonio, the Hyatt Hill Country is probably better. However, if you're looking for a romantic, relaxing get away, the Westin is just great. The golf courses looked beautiful and we'll be bringing our clubs the next time we visit!

“Great location but needs renovations to really be top notch” The location of the TAJ is fantastic and the prices are good for views of the pretty Boston public garden. It doesn't compare though when looking at the Mandarin Oriental or Four Seasons (or even some of the smaller new hotels in town). The rooms are definitely showing their age - in our room there was something drawn on the wall (red marker) behind the door that someone had clearly tried to erase but could still be seen. Carpets are faded, furniture is really dinged up (look down at the tables in the restaurants). And although prices are good there are lots of extra charges.. they charge for using the internet for every device (phone, ipad, computer etc.) that is used. And it's not clearly spelled out anywhere in the room. There's no complimentary water like the Four Seasons .. so you use the mini bar etc.

“Wonderful staff and great location!” This is not the most up-to-date hotel in terms of furnishings, but it the rooms are spacious and the location is excellent for sightseeing and business. The staff is friendly and helpful which makes this a great value and a good location for travel to DC.

“The Pod Hotel, a mini version of the W Hotel” I recently stayed at the Pod Hotel for a weekend in NYC and the best description of the place is a miniature version of the W hotel. I have stayed in many hotels in NYC (from the Hyatt to the San Carlos) and the Pod Hotel has been my favourite by far. As soon as we stepped out of our shuttle there was a courteous staff that took our bags in the lobby. This area looked like a lounge with chillout music playing. Check-In was a breeze as well as checking out. We had the bunk bed pod that overlook 51st street and was well put together with the miniscule space available in the room. It was great to have the individual TV and I suggest to bring headphones to drown any outside noises while sleeping. The room was very clean and it was made every day. Beds were comfortable, an extra pillow would be nice to have, which you can request from the front desk. There were four shared bathrooms on the 5th floor where we stayed. We were lucky to have WC4 right across from us which was the biggest bathroom, WC 1 & 2 were small, and WC 3 had a hallway leading to the toilet and shower. As the other reviews stated there was always a bathroom available, very clean, and the shower was an experience to remember. On Friday and Saturday they had a social gathering serving free cuervo shots and maragritas. The terrace above the 14th floor is not completed, but worth seeing since it had amazing skyline view of the neighborhood.
