Overall, I highly reccomend the Pod Hotel for it's cleanliness, affordability, and courteous staff. Most of their patrons were not all teenagers, I saw guests ranging from age 19 to 70. Most of the guests were from Europe. My tip is to reserve your pod on the hotel website since it was less expensive than the other travel sites. Airlink is their official shuttle that drops and picks up guest to the hotel from all three major airports in the viscinity. I suggest booking your reservation on their website as you save $6 for roundtrip transportation. Places to eat around the neighborhood would be Tanaka for good sushi next door, on the corner of 51st and 3rd is PAX with good soup, salad, and desserts, and for breakfast Ess A Bagel serving a wide selection of cream cheese flavors. If you are looking for a memorable experience without hurting your wallet in NYC, the Pod Hotel is the #1 choice. Since its opening, the Pod Hotel has become popular and regarded as the next best boutique hotel in NYC. So hurry and reserve your pod before the price begins to increase due to its popularity. BON BOYAGE!!!

“Much better than my last stay...” I had a horrible experience the last time I stayed at this property so I was really skeptical, but this stay was positive. The rooms are a really nice size and redecoration appears to be occurring, but the hotel still looks somewhat outdated. The breakfast was amazing, the parking is free, the fitness facilities are nice and the staff was adequate. It is not as nice of many of the ES properties I have visited, but it is definitely still positive. I would stay here again during the week, but on weekends it is too family filled. If you are a family this property is perfect, but if you are a business traveler you will likely be frustrated by the noise, children running through the breakfast area and filling the pool.

“The best place to stay in NYC” After a stay of a week at the Affinia Shelburne, I can't say enough about this lovely hotel. Set is a very pleasant residential neighborhood in mid-town equidistant from the Chrysler Building and the Empire State building, the hotel is in the ideal location to get anywhere in Manhattan. It's walking distance from Grand Central Station, Bryant Park, even Times Square (if you have trouble finding a cab at rush hour and don't mind walking a mile or so). Any services or type of food you can imagine can be found within a few blocks of the hotel. The roof-top bar terrace has lovely views and the hotel staff will provide access for guests even when the bar isn't open. The staff at the desk and in house-keeping were polite, friendly, and unfailingly attentive to any requests, whether for more towels, to replace a broken coffee-maker, or to deal with a rude bouncer in the roof-top bar. The concierge had great information about area restaurants and services, too. The restaurant on the ground floor serves nice breakfasts before turning into an upscale burger place (with bar) for lunch and into the evening. The restaurant staff was just as helpful and efficient as the hotel folks were. The hotel decor is modern and interesting; the rooms are furnished very nicely. The substantial fold-out couch in our suite was as comfortable as a real bed. This is the kind of place that makes you want to leave your daily life and live here - if only one could afford it long-term!

“Good location, so-so accomodations” I must agree with all the comments mentioned by the previous poster. The location of the hotel is great and so is the fact that they offer free parking, and a car is very much needed in LA. I was not impressed at all with the hotel, it looks and feels like a motel and the free wi fi service was slow and went on and off. We drove by the Best Western Sunset Plaza and I believe next time this will be a better choice for me... a little bit more pricey, but I am sure it will be well worth it.

“Beautiful Hotel, Good Location” We enjoyed our stay at the Adolphus celebrating a special occasion. We booked a suite and were given a spacious suite with a huge balcony (the balcony was bigger than some hotel rooms) with a view of the Dallas CBD. Besides the balcony, the highlight of the suite had to be its size – it had a spacious bedroom, and a separate lounge. The king bed was extremely comfortable, and helped us get some rest after a long haul flight from Australia (the 15 hours flight and -15 hrs time difference did not help the jetlag)! The manager sent us up some cookies and chocolate strawberries to congratulate us on our special occasion. This was a nice personal touch which we greatly appreciated. We were initially concerned the hotel might be run down due to its age (100+ years old), but instead we found the hotel was reasonably well maintained. The lobby is quite grand and retains its old warm charm. The staff at the Adolphus were great. We encountered warm service with a smile at all times – and we experienced that Southern hospitality. Special mention of Phillip at Valet, that guy has one big personality – he was a funny guy and he was looked after us well. We noticed everyone in Dallas was extremely friendly (more so than other parts of the US we have visited, which we already thought were overly nice– we love the Southern hospitability!). Notwithstanding the above, a few of the following things could be improved: (a) The furniture appeared to have been there since the dawn of time – perhaps rooms should be refurnished with new items (but still retain that old world style); (b) The shower head looked like it had given up a decade or so ago – it was in need for a replacement – water pressure probably suffered because of this; and (c) We love hotel slippers, it's a small touch but guests notice little amenities such as this. The location of the hotel is great, situated in downtown Dallas. Within a short stroll of the hotel there's a Starbucks, 7-11, Wich Wich (great turkey and stuffing sandwiches), a grocery store and some fashion stores (the Marcus Neiman store was around a 5 mins walk – the wife and I were quite disappointed at the 'flagship' store, but I guess we are hardcore shoppers). Also, the sixth floor museum (JFK museum) is a short 10-15 minutes walk from the hotel and is a must see activity in Dally. I should note that JFK's memorial is also on the way to the museum. In summer (it was scorching hot that day), I would recommend using the hotel's town car (complementary) to get there – I should have used our hire car, but decided to burn off a few of those calories from fine dining at the French Room. Hire a car in Dallas it's a big city and a GPS system does come in handy. Speaking of which, the French Room is an amazing restaurant. My wife and I have fine dined around the world at 3 Michelin starred restaurants and highly rated Zaget restaurants and must say this restaurant is one of the best we've dined at. The food was spectacular to the eye and divine on the taste buds. The service was prompt and efficient (the head waiter knew his stuff – he had been there for a couple of decades!). In Australia we have world renowned premium beef, but I must say Texas beef could give us a run for our money. The fillet was slow cooked in a water bath and finished on the grill – the result, beautifully tasty and tender meat which could be eaten with a spoon. The soufflé was a stand out dish too – delicious. We must say the quality of food in Dallas is excellent based on the restaurants we dined at. Pappas Bros, and Fearings Restaurant all had top quality food and service. We highly recommend all of them – we consider French Room to be the no. 1 restaurant in Dallas. We had some daily food and beverage credit included in our special rate, and decided to use this for breakfast in our room. The food was quite nice, but quite expensive – not sure if we would have opted for breakfast at the hotel if we didn't have the F&B included. If you're into shopping you must visit the Premium Outlets in Allen. The shopping was great, up there with outlets in NY, Miami (Sawgrass) and Hawaii. I had a ball at DFW Shooting Range. The staff was friendly and the prices are reasonable. I shot a Glock and an AR 15. This did not satisfy the little warrior kid in me, so I also shot the fully automatic 'Grease' gun which was a hoot. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and we were very comfortable at the Adolphus. I would stay at this hotel again, especially if management decide to update the rooms.
“ハドソン、お洒落、広い部屋がとれればいうことなし” お洒落なブティックホテルのさきがけのホテル。 セントラルパーク、コロンバス・サークルに近い。 何度か泊まったが、同じ値段で極端に狭い部屋もあったが、ソファなどもある広い部屋の時は雰囲気もなかなかでよかった。

“Very pleasantly surprised” Sofitel New York is very convenient for 5th Avenue and Times Square in Midtown Manhattan. Got a good rate but the facilities were very high end. Got a nice upgrade with a King room, no view but this is Manhattan so many roos view dingy courtyards. Excellent bed, very nice bathroom indeed and very roomy all round. Used the bar/restaurant which was quite classy. Staff were attentive throughout, they have carried the French accent well. I'd recommend the Sofitel for a high quality stay in Midtown at a good price, especially for NYC

“Not your standard Hilton Garden” Rooms are dated and common areas a bit beaten up but both are very clean. Parking is off sight but a very short walk, shorter than one would walk at a large hotel or shopping mall. Service is friendly. The pool area is nice. As a guest you get access to City Gym in lieu of a workout room. This is connected to the hotel through an interior hallway. Gym has saunas, steam rooms, showers, whirlpool, classes, basketball courts, the whole bit. Bring your swim suit is you want to use all gym facilities. I was upgraded to a 2 room suite with my Hilton Honors status. My room was a great value at only $89.
“Try the Lexington Ave one 1st” All ok, nothing wrong, just that there is a better W a few blocks away. That said, I had a great weekend, but that was more to do with who I was with :)

“not as good as it once was” I have stayed here several times and it quite honestly missed the mark this time. I usually stay here on business during the week and this time stayed thurs. thru sun. I do not know if it is because it has gotten too popular but there was noise in the hallway all night saturday. It really is bad when the hotel and spa are so nice but that you can"t get a good nights sleep. I called downstairs to ask someone to come up an end the conversations going on in the hallway but it did not seem to do any good. Upon check out I mentioned it to Jerry and he said that "it is difficult to control other peoples actions". Maybe so but it is also difficult to pay for a premium hotel and have drunk 20 something roaming the hallways loud at all hours of the night. The other complaint has to be about the water pressure.....there is none. It really is a shame because we really did like the hotel in the past.

“Huge hotel, nice location” Upon arrival, I was quite overwhelmed with the size of this hotel! The check-in area has a large waiting section, much like I've seen at hotels in Las Vegas. This Hyatt Regency hotel has over 2,000 rooms! We had a special Travel Zoo rate, and as such suspected that we wouldn't have a great room or anything. We were happily surprised to learn that we had a "VIP" room on the 32 floor, which required us to use our key card in the elevator to get to the floor (though when we called down to the front desk later, we found that we didn't have access to the Regency Club, which was kind of annoying). Why only provide partial "VIP" access? The room was a standard size that you would expect in a large city. There was one king-size bed, behind it (along the window) a huge desk, and also a small couch to the side. The bathroom was very modern and spacious. However, a few things were not great. The lighting was odd. In the main room area, all of the lamps had to be turned on individually and there was no overhead light. I found this to be inconveniencing. Also, the hotel delivered the WSJ in the morning- I would have much rather had a Chicago newspaper or even just USA today. I am not interested in the WSJ. The location was good, just a block off Michigan Ave on Wacker. It is walkable to Magnificant Mile, Grant Park, the Loop and Streeterville dining.

“Exceptional Service” This is an unbelievable property. Best view of the city overlooking the harbor. I am a devoted client and will stay here every time I come in the spring, summer and fall (don't know about crossing the harbor in the winter). Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com Friendly, friendly, friendly. I am so happy here and I really feel special when I stay here. The rooms are great, beds are comfortable and did I say they were friendly? Total - 219 rate, $246.26 after taxes.

“Our Stay at Courtyard Rancho Bernardo” me and my husband stayed here for four nights in July 2006, as we were going to be attending Comic Con in San Diego and at the time we booked, we were not going to pay $500 a night for a room that is not worth that much. First of all, the drive to San Diego was not very convenient, especially with afternoon traffic. Secondly, although the room and the hotel were nice, air conditioning was awful! Even at full blast, the air conditioning in our room felt like it was on low, then on one morning we went down to have breakfast, and it was SO hot, no air conditioning, there was sweat running down the cook's face, and they ended up giving everyone their meals for free. It is a nice place, but I would only recommend it if they fix their air conditioning situation, and definitely not for people who are looking to spend time in Downtown San Diego.

“Great overnight getaway!” We really enjoyed our one night stay at InterContinental Dallas! The room was very nice and comfortable. The hotel is conveniently located near great night life in Addison. The Sunday Brunch at Q De Cheval Restaurant was fabulous, and we will definitely stay here again!

“Comfortable and Cozy Boutique Hotel” A very comfortable and impeccably clean boutique hotel. Spent a week there in early March. Close to Times Square, Macy's and public transport. The beds are very comfortable as many other reviewers have noted. If small rooms are a concern, I would opt for the Contemporary Queen - not the Petite. It was great having a Starbucks attached to the hotel - quick way to grab a coffee and muffin in the morning. Highly recommend. I should mention that room prices have already increased considerably since March - I would say by at least a hundred dollars (unless I just got lucky reserving through Expedia).

“Very Nice” I was here for only one night while in Phoenix on business. My flight arrived early and I was able to check in early. The room was very clean and comfortable. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful; they even offered to have the free shuttle bus take me to and from dinner so I didn't have to drive there in the dark. Breakfast wasn't the best I've ever had at a Hampton, but it wan't bad. All in all, I'd definitely stay here again.

“Good Value, Thin Walls” This a good value hotel in a pretty good location - midway between Union Square and the Pacific Heights neighborhood. We stayed at The Carlton for 2 nights in one of their "upgrade" rooms ($129) on the 7th floor. The hotel and the room were very comfortable and tastefully decorated, we also found the hotel staff to be very accomodating and pleasant to deal with. Other positives include the hotel lobby (a pleasant place to spend some time), and the short but very appreciated wine reception. Our only real complaint with the hotel were the thin walls - we're not sure whether that was just our room or all the rooms, but it was very noticeable on one of the nights we stayed there. Also, although this is technically the Union Square neighborhood, it is still a 10 minute walk up/down hills to Union Square itself.

“Another great night at the Park Plaza” A perfect night for me in the bride in Boston. Location is perfect, close to all the areas we want to be. Would recommend staying in the Towers, get a happy our snack at night and breakfast in the morning. Staff was excellent!

“Great location, great accomodation, fabulous staff” Initially found this on LHW, and then on reading TripAdvisor reviews found out about Jet Luxury and booked through them. As more reviews were posted , I too became a little suspicious at how good they all were and wasn't sure what to expect. Arrived mid afternoon Thursday for a 4 night stay , and had requested late checkout in advance via Jet Luxury. Staff in Setai are absolutely amazing, incredibly friendly and eager too please without being over the top or appearing false. The free WiFi is a big plus and is high speed. Room which was billed as Standard Deluxe Avenue Rooom on Jet Luxury website, was actually overlooking 36th Street , but you could see 5th Avenue from the window. Room was a reasonable size, and absolutely immaculate . Very comfortable bed, furnishings and bathroom. If I had any criticisim it would be that there is no mirror over the desk, and not enough room on the bathroom sink nor a shelf next to it, so it's difficult to do hair makeup etc without walking back and forth from shelf to mirror. The Nesspresso coffee maker, and fridge with soft drinks and water is complimentary and restocked daily. Very welcome. House Keeping is morning, a refresh afternoon and turndown in the evening (although we didn't get turndown on our last night) and the standard of housekeeping is excellent. The bar was nice, a good ambience, although didn't find it anything to rave about like some of the reviews, service was good but not particularly speedy . We ate in the bar one evening and the food was tasty and came to about $80 for two soups and sandwiches with beer. We had breakfast once in the restuarant which was excellent ,again about $80 for 2 people. Front desk and concierge are very friendly , although I was a little surprised the concierge was unable to recommend a casual pizzeria for beer and pizza and directed us to an upmarket grill. The door staff really make this hotel in terms of service, absolutely exceptional, greet you by name , welcome you back etc. The big question is do you get the same standard of room and service through Jet Luxury as you get direct. I don't know for sure, but I can't see that much could be improved. I guess the room types are limited through Jet, you can't book a suite or a premier room for instance, just a standard or an apartment. And I was slightly put out to be told on check out day that our 2pm checkout wasn't available and the latest we could have was 12 ( very polite and stored our luggage though, so not a huge deal) - which I guess wouldn't have happened if we'd booked direct as the hotel literature states there no set check in and out times. So overall, fabulous, we'll go there again and recommend it to friends, and I'd go via Jet Luxury again too, although if I wanted the option of a bigger room would book direct.

“Great value hotel in downtown Seattle” I booked this hotel at a discounted price through Priceline and it proved to be a great value (even if I paid full price). The room was very spacious and comfortable, they offer a very good complimentary breakfast, free Wi-Fi and free parking! The hotel location is also very good, you can walk 5 minutes and take a bus or enjoy their free shuttle service, it runs every 30 minutes and takes you to the Space Needle and Pike Place Market. There are also some good restaurants nearby, we ate at a seafood place called Duke's Chowder House and it was delicious (there's also a crab house and sushi place very close to the hotel). Overall, I highly recommend this hotel!

“Not bad, but there are better hotels for the money in Baltimore” I was here for a conference - so I don't think I would have stayed here otherwise. The property is dated and is due for a refresh. The room we had was rather small, even for a downtown property. The bathroom was almost cruise ship small. We had to call twice to get additional pillows to the room. Not the end of the world, they might have been busy. But when my wife called for a porter at checkout they never arrived. She carried the bags to the bell stand by herself after waiting 30 minutes. The breakfast room service did arrive right on time and wasn't super expensive - so that was good. The hotel bar staff was good, and they had a couple of local beers on tap. The crab soup was actually pretty good. Valet parking is crazy expensive - not unexpected - but there is a parking garage right across the street that is open 24 hours and is $14 a night - less than half of the hotel valet rates. Buy a couple of local beers at the bar with the money you will save. Location is pretty good. The First Mariner arena is across the street. The Inner Harbor and Camden Yards are a few blocks away. This is more of an office district, so head to the Inner Harbor or Fells Point for food, drink and shopping, especially after 6. This area pretty much shuts down after 6. There is local construction going on as of June 2012. The hotel provided ear plugs for rooms facing the construction. I was up early anyway, but it would have been loud enough to bother me had I not been up already - and it would be quite bad on a lower floor. If this concerns you, ask about it at check in and get a higher floor or a room on the other side of the hotel.

“Find something else” I requested a non-smoking room and we were given a smoking room with a view of dumpsters, A/C units, and brick walls. The hotel was booked and could not move us until the next day. When we asked about our new room, the front desk staff said there wasn't a notation that we requested to move. Apparently the night manager wrote the wrong room number down. So we had to stay in the smoking room another night. Finally, they changed our room on our third day. Thank goodness I brought travel candles. The breakfast isn't great, but it's complimentary so might as well take advantage of it. The deli next door has good paninis and the pizza joint across the street is also good. There is a bar directly across from the hotel so if you have kids, you may want to request a room away from the front because it gets pretty loud. The only staff that showed any kind of concern or interest in us were the housekeeping ladies, and the "bellboy", if you will. He stored our luggage and/or hailed a cab for us with a smile.

“All that you expect from a Hyatt” Stayed here for two nights while in town for a conference (at the hotel itself). The hotel offers what you would expect from a Hyatt- clean, comfortable, cosy but not an exceptionally friendly staff. It is a 10 minute walk to the downtown "sights" in Dallas like JFK Memorial, 6th Floor Museum, West End etc and a $ 45 cab ride from DFW airport. Get a room on a higher floor with the city view. Reunion Tower, a Dallas landmark that is connected to the hotel, is currently closed for renovation.

“The Marriott was great!” After much hand wringing of where to stay in San Francisco with a 16 yr old and a 14 yr old on a family vacation, I finally choose the Marriott Fisherman's Wharf (primarily because I'm a big Marriott Rewards member). I had read varying reviews of this hotel and also had several recommendations from San Francisco regulars to stay near Union Square or in the Financial District . . . not tacky Fisherman's Wharf. Well, I'm glad I didn't listen to them! In my opinion, if you are in SF for a short time with kids, the Fisherman's Wharf area is a perfect place to base your operations. The Marriott hotel was great! Nice lobby. Nice bar. Free internet (with 2 computers and a printer) in the Business Center. Very accommodating staff. Beds were terrific. Typical Marriott furniture and decor. Very close to the Cable Car lines. A full service Safeway grocery store a block away. Lots of restaurants (including fast food -- In and Out, Burger King, McDonalds) close-by. You can walk to Lombard Street, Coit Tower, Fisherman's Wharf (Pier 39) and easily catch the boats to Alcatraz. It's true that parking is expensive, but it is everywhere in this city. Take my recommendation and avoid the hassle. Don't rent a car... you don't need one. You can walk, take a taxi, or buy an all day muni & cable car pass for $9/person and get anywhere you want to go. We did that one day and explored downtown, visited the Cable Car Museum, went to China Town and even searched out the house in Mrs. Doubtfire and Lombard School from the Princess Diaries. It was great fun and our kids loved exploring and riding the cable cars.

“Good Show, Old Chap!” Stayed at The London over Memorial Day weekend, and found much to like at this renovation of the Righa Royale. The location is great, as within a 10-minute walk you can reach such top attractions as Central Park, the Time-Warner Center, 5th Avenue, Rockefeller Center, and "Wicked". Only had to take one cab, and that was because I was running late. There's not too much in the way of public areas, except for a sensational gym. The lobby is really just a long hallway with high ceilings and a check-in desk. No lounging, etc. The bar is located in the restaurant, so it's not a lobby bar proper. Had lunch at "Maze", which offered exceptional food at three courses for $35. The lobster risotto is utterly superb. The $35 is a great deal, until you splurge on a couple of cocktails, then with tax and tip you have an $86 lunch. Still memorable, with attentive service from reservations through the waitstaff and a pleasant room. Drinks are expensive, just like everywhere else in New York, which is firmly the land of the $20 drink [and $10 beer!] I had a fine check-in experience, with the agent communicating with housekeeping to find me a room that was ready at 10:30 am, which was fantastic. I did receive an escort to the room, with a room tour, ice service, and a personal fridge brought to the room--the minibar has no room for personal items, and it's one of those weight-sensitive set-ups, so if you so much as leave a fingerprint in there, it charges you. How do I describe the room decor? Try to stay with me here--they look like crash pads co-designed by Austin Powers and a French prostitute. Thus, you have a three-armed torch lamp and a round reflective metal wall piece side-by-side with a three-sided burgundy velvet sofa in the living area. Somehow, this all works and is distinctive rather than horrifying. The bedroom [through French doors] is more reserved and traditional, with very comfortable linens and mattress. The windows in both rooms open slightly, so that you can hear the cacophany of honking from all those drivers solving the city's traffic woes with their horns. There's no closet; clothes storage is on a large free-standing rack with drawer space below. There's an iPod dock, good lighting, and wall switches for the sheers and curtains. I found the Waterworks bathroom to be a little stark--all white, and sort of narrow, so it feels kind of like being inside an egg. The tub's a bit short and the shower door doesn't meet the back side, so there's an open gap. It's obviously deliberate, but I'm not sure what the point was. If you want style and luxury at a slightly more bearable price than some of the topmost properties around town, try here. I compared The London to other places I've been--St. Regis, Peninsula, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, and Ritz-Carlton--and it was from $130 to $270 less per night during my stay. It doesn't have quite the effortless grace and refined elegance of those hotels, but it does still have a lot to offer. Couple of other New York notes: --The Whole Foods at Time-Warner Center is a great stop for a tasty, quick sandwich or salad at lunch --The Peninsula's redesign of its rooftop bar, now called Salon de Ning, is terrific. [Though see note above about the land of the $20 cocktails.] --"South Pacific" at Lincoln Center is hypnotic and wonderful.

“Another Nice Stay” This is the third time I've received a great rate on this hotel through an online bidding site. Amazing Value!! It is always clean, the staff is always very nice and the location is great. Location: Close to so much! Around the corner from Boston Common, Theater District, Beacon Hill, Chinatown and great restaurants and shopping. Rooms: Your standard room size. Clean and attractive. Staff: Friendly Cons: There are two elevators, one from the street to the lobby and one from the lobby to the rooms. The elevators from the street to lobby are sometimes very crowded. The street of the hotel gets very busy during the weekends due to the nearby theaters. Otherwise it is a quiet street. I mentioned in other reviews that the one entrance of the hotel is on a dark and quiet street which you may find strange, but just turn the corner and there are ton of people walking to dinner, bars, etc. I like this hotel and hope to get it next time I bid. If the hotel's rate is in the high $100's and up, shop around because there are a ton of great hotels in Boston that have comparable rates.

“Good value at the Chancellor” I was in San Francisco for a conference and had a lovely stay at the Chancellor. I am female and was travelling alone but felt perfectly safe in this hotel. The rooms are not plush but are tastefully decorated with proper duvets, TVs, little bowls of sweets etc. The bathrooms are tiny but very nice with good, hot showers. The free tea and coffee - and free wifi in the rooms - are nice touches. The best thing about this hotel is the location - right on Union Square. I didn't eat at the restaurant (it's worth queuing at the famous Dottie's true blue cafe round the corner for brunch!), so can't comment on that.

“Ottimo per visitare washington” l'hilton garden inn di washington si trova a 5 minuti dalla casa bianca. senza dubbio una posizione davvero ottima per visitare la città. le stanze non sono grandissime ed a noi è capitata quella con vista impianto di condizionamento, anche abbastanza rumoroso. il personale è gentile e disponibile. Ottima colazione, vasta scelta tra dolce e salato. Hotel da consigliare, visto anche il buon rapporto qualità prezzo. gli alberghi a washington hanno costi elevati, soprattutto nella zona vicino ai monumenti.

“The position is the positive” We had stayed at the Hotel 4 years ago and it was the logical choice for us to spend the night near the airport. The position is first class - our sons love being able to see planes on their approaches. Also the airport shuttles that run every 15-20 mins are excellent. What we did notice this time was that the rooms seemed a little tired with wear and tear. We had two adjoining rooms that were adequate and I guess for just over $100 a night you get what you pay for. The prices in the breakfast and bar areas are expensive. Front desk staff were efficient without being over friendly.

“Old World Arizona Luxury” Overall, my partner and I had a positive experience. We loved the displayed pictures of the original Biltmore -- on the outskirts of Phoenix at the time. The Frank Lloyd Wright architecture is still relevant and the hotel is kept up very well and the layout is excellent. The grounds are spectacular. Frank and Albert's has a killer happy hour seven days a week. Due to my credit card plan, we had a very generous dining credit and very late checkout. Staff, start to finish, was excellent. We brought our dog with us for a deposit of $100 ($50 refundable upon checkout). However, the personalized "pet amenity" the property and its agents boasted about was never given to us. The room was spacious. The decor was mostly nice, but there were some outdated elements like the wetbar and refrigerator. The bathroom was large, but the tub and bathmat were dingy. The main pool has a loud and rowdy crowd. But, if you seek quiet, get a property map. The resort features a number of pools and most are empty and peaceful. The resort fee of $28 is waaaaay too high for what is offered. That included entry to the spa and fitness room. The spa was an incredible disappointment. The whole area is small and dated. The showers are also small and the doors are dingy. There is a hot tub and the decking area appears worn down. The steam room and sauna are small. We did not get a treatment, so I cannot answer about that aspect. DO NOT go here for a spa vacation. The spa is absolutely pathetic. Also, the resort fee was supposed to include a newspaper. We never got one. Parking is a rip off. Self parking is $12/day. Yet, if you just park your car in the structure or the spaces around the property, there is no verification you are a guest. There are plenty of spaces, too. Just tell the front desk you took a cab! Also, beware, the staff does landscaping very early on weekend mornings. Our neighbors smoke alarm also went off in the very early morning hours. As a result of the newspaper and noise, we were given a $30 credit which seemed fair. Overall, we had a great stay. Whether we stay here again will depend on price. We will also think twice about the overly high resort fee. I would rather pay a higher room rate for a property I feel is not ripping me off.

“Quirky and refreshing” This is a fun, eclectic hotel. Every floor has its own theme. I was on the sci fi floor with movie posters up in the hallway and pictures in the room. I stayed here on a business trip for 3 days. The room was spacious. I would definitely stay here again.

“Muy Agradable” El hotel está super bien ubicado. Centro ciudad. Al lado del barrio chino (superrecomendable) y de varios restaurantes muy agradables. Al entrar la atención es supercorrecta y encantadora. Desde el botones, un encanto, hasta en recepción, en este caso Rory, que se deshacen por ayudarte con cualquier gestión o preguntas que tengas que hacer. Las habitaciones son muy confortables y el wifi va estupendamente.

“Great location, helpful staff” My boyfriend and I booked a last minute trip to the Inner Harbor and got this hotel through Expedia. The location was great, literally right across the street from the inner harbor and connected to a mall. We walked to Little Italy for dinner. The walk was about ten minutes and it was very safe. Speaking of safe, the hotel had two police officers standing by the doors after 9pm. The room was spacious with newer furniture and flat screen tv. The king bed was comfortable although the pillows could have been better. Our room did not have any special view but we were ok with that. Unlike many other reviews, I did not have a problem with other guests’ noise (maybe we were lucky?). It is true there is only one location for elevators so you might need to walk a little if you are on the side opposite from them. We used the indoor pool and hot tub once. The pool was filled with screaming kids but we were not too bothered by them. There was a lifeguard, but she wasn’t really paying attention to the kids jumping and diving even though it clearly said not to. We also liked the patio area outside of the pool. Nice to sit outside and relax. Like others, I agree that parking was a little high but I guess that is the price you pay for being so close to the inner harbor. We did not eat at the hotel’s restaurant but did go look at it, it looked nice. The hotel staff was friendly and even brought my boyfriend Band-Aids when his shoes were causing blisters within a few minutes. Overall, I would stay here again but only if we got a good deal. I am someone who would walk an extra 5-10 minutes to save some money. On a sidenote- if you are planning to go to the inner harbor and are thinking about going out at nightime be aware that things close early. By midnight on a Saturday the restaurants and bars (even ESPN Zone) were closed. However, it is still nice to walk around.

“A little tired - but great staff!” An older Hampton Inn but not too bad and conveniently located to business and shops. The pros: The woman who checked me in was very pleasant, cheery, and helpful! The breakfast was the usual Hampton fare, but prepared well - and the woman setting it up was also quite cheerful at 6 AM ! The cons: It took forever to get the TV working with this new DISH set up - I had to go re-program the channels. The walls are paper thin and I had to listen to my neighbors loud TV and conversations next door well into the night (which is why I always carry ear plugs).

“Great views, fine stay” After my flight was delayed, delayed and finally cancelled I was able to get one of the last rooms available at this hotel for an unexpected stay. The airport shuttle was around to pick me up in around 10 minutes after calling. Walking into the lobby the first thing you notice is the fantastic view of the Boston skyline. The rooms were well appointed, but no mini bar. Room service was quick as was service at the lobby bar. Prices were high, but to be expected when the hotel has a captive audience. There is nothing else within walking distance to this place. Check out was quick and the shuttle left almost immediately. Overall its not my preferred BOS airport hotel but the views are great and its a fine place to spend the night.

“I wanted to stay.” My daughter and I spent two nights at the Trump in October. Like, Nita W., this is not the typical hotel we can afford, but we chose to splurge. What a treat. We had a beautiful view of the river, the weather was gorgeous, and there was a full moon...a photographer's paradise. We were delighted with the kitchen area. In fact, we were delighted with almost everything. There is just one thing I missed. I would like to have had a restaurant similar to the Pierrot Gourmet at the Peninsula on this property. Other than that, this was memorable. I'm glad we made this choice.

“Extremely quiet hotel in central NYC and room exactly like website pictures !!!” We stayed five nights from the 12th April at the Four Points Sheraton Chelsea and were extremely happy with our stay. I know the city very well after many visits but my other half had not been before so it was great to have such a good base to explore from. We arrived at Midday on the 12th to drop our bags off expecting that we may have to return later but they allowed us to check into the room straight away, much to the delight of the person checking us in. Honestly she seemed happier about the early check in than we did !!. We had requested in advance a higher floor away from Ice Machines (thanks to the good people writing here) and got a lovely big room (for New York) on the 14th floor. The decor is exactly as shown on the (--) website which we booked through at a rate of $205 a night plus tax which was great value for this modern room. We had a large television, very comfortable bed, very nice bathroom and everything seemed new, there was certainly enough space so we didn't feel cramped at all. I was very happy that there was a free digital in room safe that I have often been charged for elsewhere. The room was so QUIET right in the middle of Manhattan. We could not hear any noise at all from the street or from other rooms which I was particularly pleased about. Let me stress again, ask for a higher room so you have a view, away form the very noisy ice machines that are on alternating floors, book through starwood(--) to get the cheapest price and you are in for a very nice stay here indeed.

“Great place, excellent location, smashing cocktail...” Stayed for 5 nights and have nothing but positves to say about the Amalfi. Its location is perfect, Close to the river, so both sides of the city easily accessible. 2 blocks and you are on the 'Mag Mile'. Check-in was so smooth, we stayed on the 4th floor of 6. Bed was huge and for a hotel extremely comfortable and good pillows too. Complimentay drinks were a super touch and the 'Amalfitini's' went down well after a good days sightseeing. Also nibbles served here too. Breakfast was provided on each floor outside the lifts, juice, fruit and pastries as much as you want. Free paper delivered every morning too. Bedroom and bathroom both large and shower heads powerful. Only issue, new apts being built across the road, deliveries early in the a.m. will wake the deepest sleeper, once completed all will be well. Great hotel, friendly and great city.

“A Fine Spring Weekend!” The room was nicely laid out and clean; the bed was very comfortable. It was clearly not a luxury hotel but we got a good rate. There was something wrong with the sound on the TV and the furnishings were a season away from looking shabby. But the location was good, the people were nice and the price was right. I would stay there again.

“rather good hotel but needs improvement” rinStayed there 4 nights and wanted to combine business and pleasure. Asked the receptionist to put me in the room with better water view and she did the opposite - I had to drive 7 minutes to Bay Tower and got the room with view on PARKING and road (and the bay is somewhere far!) Next morning I had to move to Marina Tower. That's first time I see the hotel where You need to DRIVE between towers . Parking is open air but cost 22USD (self). Marina Tower (Main) was rather good, they have nice restaurant and free internet in the Lobby.

“Los detalles... hace a un hotel grande, y este no los tiene” Me alojé en este hotel por las buenas críticas que había en tripadvisor. El precio me pareció exagerado. La habitación que yo disfruté, estaba limpia, era grande, espaciosa, y el baño nuevo, a diferencia de otros hoteles de NY. Los únicos "peros" del hotel, son: Insonorización de las habitaciones, se oye todo lo que sucece en la calle, coches sirenas, motores, etc. ellos ya lo saben y por ello te dejan en la mesita el primer día tapones para los oídos. Es una solución, pero no para un 4 estrellas. El segundo "pero", ya lo había leído en algunas de las críticas de tripadvisor, y es lo desagradables que son las recepcinostas feminas. Los hombres de la recepción, son amables y complacientes, pero las mujeres, no sonríen nunca, te hablan y te contestan sin nisiquiera dejar de mirar al ordenador, lo dicho, muy desagradables. La ubicación es muy céntrica, algo alejado de Times Square, pero en pleno Madison Square Garden, cerca del Empire State Building, y con Penn Station al lado.

“good room service food; mediocre spa; limited gym hours” Stayed here for three nights on business. pros: - fitness center will give you sneakers if you forget yours (as I did); there is water and towels and a good selection of new machines - nice pool - could be bigger - fruit and drinks available in the sitting room near the pool - very nice looking locker rooms with steam room/sauna (did not get a chance to try) - tasty food - made 'special request' fruit platter for me with papaya and figs - l'occitane amenities in the bathroom (but no cotton swabs / cotton balls) cons: - fitness center not open 24 hours a day (why???) - spa was booked solid on a Friday and I had to have a massage at 8 am; the massage was unremarkable and when it was done (and I was still getting dressed) - the therapist came back in to see why I haven't come out yet - apparently I was not moving fast enough (though I did only take a couple of minutes) - one morning messed up the time of my room service breakfast and delivered it one hour early. When I did not open the door (I had earplugs in), they started calling me. Normally would not have been a big deal, but I had only gotten a couple of hours of sleep that night due to intense work schedule and was looking at another really long day (which I mentioned to them when I placed the order at 3am that same morning), and their early delivery deprived me of one hour of sleep. - the same thing happened on the last day I was there - I wanted to have a massage, but wasn't sure I could wake up early and come by at 8 am. I asked the front desk to leave the spa people a message that I might come by in the morning to see if they could accommodate me. They said they would send an email. Of course the following morning the spa people called me at 7 am to see if I wanted to come in at 8. I should have specifically asked the front desk to instruct them not to call me I guess. The stay was fine - just wish there was more consideration for people's schedule and fewer phone calls.

“Auch beim zweiten mal alles in Ordnung” Ich war zum wiederholten Mal in diesem Hotel. Es ist ein sehr großer Komplex mit mehreren Restaurants, Starbucks, Bar, Cafe und riesiger Lobby. Die Zimmer sind modern und großzügig. Super Betten und ein tolles Badezimmer (mit 2 Duschköpfen). Perfekt für eine Geschäftsreise zum Übernachten, einem Abendessen und ein paar Bier an der Bar

“Not what I expected from a Crowne Plaza” Pros and Cons to this hotel: Pros: 1) Staff is fantastic. I screwed up my reservation and they very graciously helped me out. Thanks staff!! 2) They offer a free shuttle to get you around the downtown. Our driver, Reginald, was just great and answered a lot of questions about the area and gave great advice. 3) Its about a 15 min walk to Beale Street but was a safe walk back. 4) The rooms are clean. Cons: 1) The building is very dated. I think we both described it as "dingy". 2) The vent in our bathroom (room 523) looked into our neighbor's bathroom. I could tell when they had their light on in the bathroom and could hear everything that went on. This was a bit off-putting. 3) Hallway could use more lighting and my wife felt the room was very dark.

“Very nice hotel in quiet area” Just spent three nights at the Carlyle Suites in DC. The rooms were very large, and included a desk, pull out sofa and large TV. The bathroom was also large, with granite countertops. My room only had a shower, no tub. The separate make up area was very nice. The rooms also had a small kitchen, with stove and fridge and K-cup coffee maker. Front desk staff were very welcoming and helpful and quickly answered any questions, gave directions, etc. The hotel is in a more residential area, which meant that it was quieter than the hotels on major streets and yet, it was not that far to walk to restaurants and stores. Overall, it was a great stay. Oh, and the price was right! One comment that I would have is that it would be nice for the hotel to have bathrobes in the rooms because I find it a pain to have to pack a robe (takes up too much space in the suitcase.)

“Not the best Hilton. Not the worst, either” Got a great rate on Priceline, so I couldn't be too picky. Everyone who we asked helped us, and did so cheerfully. Room was fine, fairly spacious, comfy bed, plenty of pillows. Was some stale smoke smells, not in our room, but in some of the hallways. Room was clean, bathroom and amenities were just fine. Could have used a little more in the way of a gift shop, personal items etc. Area around hotel a tad sketchy, not overwhelmingly so, but nonetheless, it seem a little eery later at night. Would I stay here again? Yes I would. I go on vacation to see the sights, hotel is for sleeping. I slept just fine.

“The place to stay in Seattle - location, friendly, comfy, highly recommend” This was a terrific place to stay for so many reasons. Location: easy walking distance (well, as easy as it can be in Seattle) to the Convention Center, Pike Market, the monorail & train... it's got a great location. Friendly: Everyone, all the time. An easy 5 out of 5! Comfy: Great room, VERY comfy bed, kitchenette (great for leftovers!) our room had a small but very cool balcony. Clean, well-furnished, free internet - Room: easy 5 out of 5. Food: Free breakfast which was really well done. Never too crowded, good selection of hot and cold food. Reception (dinner) in the evening - also well done! Extras: car rental in house (this was great since we were there on the weekend and decided to rent one day). Highly recommended! We would stay here again without looking anywhere else.

“Awesome location” Large rooms, great service. - Shampoo & conditioner provided - Soft, big towels - Flat screen TV with remote for games - Desk area - Decent view of city to the west - Convenience store & deli across the street - Restaurants & pubs galore - all within walking distance - Plentry of shopping near-by (Macy's, Borders, etc.) - Historical sites - many within walking distance - Old City and convention center close by - Bally's gym near-by - front desk provides passes The bed was a little hard for me and the walls are pretty thin. Turn on the room fan and some ear plugs seemed to take of the noise. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

“Traffic noise!” Moderately updated rooms. Adjacent to i35 and the noise that goes with it. As if the traffic noise wasn't enough the air conditioner made a terrible racquet all through the night. The gym equipment was mostly broken and no one ever answered the room service line. Shower tile is old and cracked. Was reasonably clean. Front desk staff were rude and oblivious. Stay at one of the several neighboring hotels.

“Not a typical Park Hyatt - and not in a good way” I have stayed at several Hyatt's an travel for business about 6 times a year. I have stayed at the Park Hyatt Chicago, which is one of the nicest business hotels I have stayed at, so I thought this would be similar (after all Park Hyatt is the top line of the chain). I was disappointed. The hotel is very old and the rooms have not been rennovated. The carpet has threadbare spots, peeling wallpapaer, a cabinet door falling off, a lot of door dings and pain nicks's and a tub/shower combo with holes in the tile and a cracking tub basin -- and this was in one of their Park Suites (which I was upgraded too when their was broken glass on the bathroom floor -- and a fair amount of hairs -- of the first room I checked into). The good things were the attnetiveness of the staff, great location, and the interior rooms are quiet (but no view and very dark). I had a AAA rate of $274 a night. Next time I will try a different, more modern (newer or remodelled) hotel, for the same or similar price. This was a disappointment.

“Trendy, simple and beautiful” Stayed in this place in May and loved it. Rooms are very clean, modern design. Great artwork and photography through out the place. Very comfortable bed and pillows, the ones you would want to purchase for your own house. Interesting black and white decor. Good location. Nice breakfast set up downstairs, friendly staff. The room service dinner wasn't that good but there are so many restaurant to pick from in NY that is not a problem.

“Great Location and Helpful Staff” We really enjoyed staying at the Hotel Rex, with a very clean cozy room. We arrived a little early and they were able to help us get into the room and on to the city to do our planned events. Staff, location, room and wine tasting in the evening were excellent. Only 1 small elevator, but never a wait to use it to get to the lobby or to your room. Could be a tight fit for a wheel chair, but still accessable.

“Happiness in the Big Apple” Our family of four (incl. two teenagers) was looking for 'economical' accomodations for a few days around Christmas in Manhatten. After looking at numerous websites and lots of reviews, I decided on the Ramada. We've never been to New York City before, so it was a bit of a shot in the dark, but overall I was very pleased. One note on price. After getting over the relative high price of all NYC hotels, after booking the Ramada the price quoted, despite listing 4 total people on the reservation, was the 'single' price. The actual price for four was about $30 more per night. Make sure you double check the rate based on the actual number of people in the room. The hotel location turned out to be nearly ideal. Transit to/from LaGuardia was fairly painless, even leaving on a Friday afternoon. The hotel sits at 30th and Lexington, about a 5 minute walk from the nearest subway, 10 minutes from the Empire State Building, 15 minutes from Macy's and 20-25 minutes from Times Square. The hotel neighborhood is relatively quiet, with a number of 'hole-in-the-wall' restaurants nearby. We actually had dinner on Christmas night, when we arrived, across the street in a Chinese noodel house (ala The Christmas Story) but our biggest surprise was the quaint Italian restaurant (Trattoria Belvedere) right next store (yellow awning in picture). Moderately priced with a cozy atmosphere, I'd definately recommend this place if you want something good and very close. Our dinner for four, including a bottle of wine, was just over $100...a real bargain for NYC. The hotel itself was about what I expected. The room was small, so with two queen size beds there wasn't much elbow room, but everything was clean and the bathroom looked to be recently renovated. Our room was on the 11th floor, facing opposite 30th street and we barely ever noticed street noise. Could even see the Empire State Building from our window. The free continental breakfast was above average. The dining room and food layout was very clean and well stocked, with an attendant available for any need. The food included donuts, bagels, yogurt, cereal, fruit, microwavable pancakes, and a full range of beverages. Definately a cost-conscious bonus not needing to purchase breakfast everyday. One comment on the coffee. I'm not a coffee drinker, but my wife was less than thrilled with the home brew, but there's a coffee house next door (see picture) so for a buck fifty, you're covered. All in all we were very pleased with the choice, and based on price, would certainly consider returning our next time in the Big Apple.

“Great location, not worth the money. So so rooms.” I stayed here for 4 days recently with my wife. We arrived at 830am and were told at check in that our room was not ready yet. I informed the lady that as a member of the IHG Ambassador program I should get 8am check in. Promptly another man behind the counter sent me to another desk to be assisted by a dedicated ambassador check in agent. This agent attempted to get us a room but could not, as they were fully booked. However, to compensate us, she provided us with free breakfast for the stay in the hotel, which was a VERY generous gesture. She offered us a temporary room which she would have cleaned asap by housekeeping and we could stay there until our regular room was ready. We returned later to this temporary room to rest a little while only to find housekeeping did a very shoddy job of cleaning it. The toilet had caked on urine on the seat with hair stuck to it. Now, I understand some things may be missed during a rapid cleaning, but this is unacceptable in any hotel, PARTICULARLY in a hotel of this stature. We were later moved to our regular room. This room was a 1 bedroom suite, which I received as a complimentary upgrade due to my Ambassador status. This was a decent room. It was large with a couch and chairs and desk, and a large, very comfortable bed. The decor was very stuffy and early 1900s in my opinion, and the TV was a 27" tube tv, which I found ridiculous. I would think in 2009 in a hotel of this class, flat screen tvs would be installed, and in a nice way than an obstructive wood cabinet smack in the middle of the room across from the bed. My major complaint was the bathroom. It is TINY. Now, I know that in older hotels of this type, that is often an issue and I know it is not easily changed, but I literally could not sit on the toilet and close the door without moving my legs. The counter space at the sink was almost non existant and the shower squealed while in use. Aside from the bathroom however, the room was nice enough and very comfortable. One thing was the traffic noise though. On the 6th floor, we were constantly bombarded by street noise. The minibar was restocked almost fully, with the exception of a minor oversight on the final day, but overall was efficiently monitored. Now, I was a bit irritated with the frequency that my room was entered. On one day, we had at least 3 entries into our room, presumably housekeeping once, then later by someone to fill the minibar while we were there, and finally again by some unknown person. The last we only know about because we returned to find the stereo playing, presumably left on by housekeeping while working? Also, the staff generally would knock and attempt to enter the room without even giving you time to barely get off the bed, let alone come to the door. I hate that kind of intrusive behavior. Housekeeping was friendly though, and did not give us any issues. Another minor issue was none of the clocks resetting themselves on Daylight Savings time by themselves, despite the letter left in our room assuring us that they would do it automatically. This could have been an issue for someone relying on that. The location is superb for Manhattan, as you are within easy walking distance of most of Manhattans sights. The hotel is a few blocks from the subway, which is not that bad if you are travelling light, but I would not do it with multiple bags per person. Overall, a nice hotel, with some ups and downs. Would I pay the rates of $300 + a night that I often see to stay there? No. Would I stay for $150-200 a night? Maybe. I just think there might be overall better and more consistent experiences in NY, but I will not say I would not recommend it. Rather, I would not tell people to avoid it, so I guess that is recommending it by default.

“Lots of personality and great location!” I always enjoy my stays here, and I find it perfect for the business traveler (though if I was looking for a location close to Times Square, Central Park, etc. I would stay here for leisure too). The hotel is very boutique-y and roomy for NYC standards. I've always found the staff to be ridiculously accommodating, and surprisingly I've been able to check in early every time I've stayed there (though I never assume it will happen!). While waiting in line to check in early, the doorman always offers to check my bag if it doesn't work out--super thoughtful. Located 1 minute away from Times Square, the location for sightseeing can't be beat! Though in a touristy area, you wouldn't know it at this hotel. It's just the perfect distance from all the sights and sounds of the city. I've had rooms low and higher up, front and back of the hotel and I've never been disturbed by the city that never sleeps. I don't think there's a room with a view at this hotel, but that doesn't matter to me since I'm rarely in my room during the day. I had recently signed up for Kimpton rewards since I seem to stay at their hotels a lot, and there was a note and $15 mini bar comp card. Fabulous! Not sure if this happens every time, or only the first time after sign up, but still...a nice touch--so sign up! They also have a free happy hour too--a nice way to start your evening. I also appreciate all the channel offerings--Bravo, MTV, HBO, etc...it may sound weird, but I hate staying in a hotel and being confined to 3 channels. All rooms also have the ipod alarm docking stations which always makes me happy too!

“great hotel, BAD location” I stayed here on a business trip-- this was the designated conference hotel with a special rate. Otherwise I would not have chosen somewhere so far from the subway, so far from EVERYTHING. Even though my conference was on the Upper East Side (at various locations), this place was always a hike, uphill to get back to town. It rained all weekend, making the extra distance even more of a pain. I suppose that's why the prices are lower. Other than the location, most everything about the hotel was great. Room was large, clean, very comfortable. Staff was courteous enough, but always very busy at the front desk-- I had to wait several times because things were slow, or maybe other customers were needy. I used the exercise room, which was clean and helpful. There is an indoor pool, but I didn't use it. No vending machines!!! It seems many Marriott locations now make you buy your (over-priced) snacks from the front desk. That's annoying-- I stocked up on snacks at the convenience mart around the corner, once I discovered this problem. Decent view across the city-- because you're so far from civilization, there are fewer buildings to block the view. Oh, I remember the elevators being slow, tiny, and always crowded-- always people with luggage and strollers, always cleaning staff with carts. I started using the stairs, rather than waiting. Overall, I was pleased with the room, but in the future, I'd happily pay $20-$50 more for somewhere in Midtown. You'll recover the extra in what you save on cab fares and in the time you save by walking less distance.

“friendly staff, would stay here again” This hotel is walking distance from graceland and if you are going to memphis to visit this famous site, this hotel would be a good choice. (to save on parking fees) There amenities are the same as any other days inn, but the staff were very friendly and helpful. We had the choice to stay downtown but since we were not doing any walking around at night (traveled with family and did not feel too safe in some areas), I was very satisfied with our stay here. Did not swim in the pool but it's interesting to note that it is guitar-shaped. And for Elvis fans, there are Elvis movies showing on 2 channels 24/7. It is also next to a souvenier outlet, but you still have to shop around for good bargains.

“Simply beautiful!” What a beautiful hotel! Everything from the lobby area to the hallways and the architecture was beautiful! I stayed in one of the Club Rooms (business travelers) on the 10th / 11th floor. One of the perks of these rooms is that you have access to the business lounge on the 10th floor which offers continental breakfast in the morning and refreshments in the evening (all inclusive of your room rate). Keep in mind, you are paying a higher room rate, so not sure if it's necessarily worth it for leisure travelers. The breakfast was average (coffee, juices, cereal, fruit & yogurt, and some pastries) and the evening refreshments consisted of sodas, crackers & cheese & meat, fruits, and cookies. It was a nice set-up in a lounge area with tables and couches and flat screen tv's. Internet access is also free should you have access to the lounge. Speaking of Internet access, it costs $9.95 for a 24 hr period from your room. Also, because the building is older, wireless reception is not that great and the signal quite weak. Make sure to bring an ethernet cable along to plug into. Cell phone reception is also quite weak -- mine kept fading in and out depending on where I was in the hotel/room, so beware of that. The room size was awesome. So much floor space and a sitting area with couch and table also. Not sure if this was just available for Club Rooms, or it's a standard feature. The only disappointment was the bathroom size. On one hand you have a HUGE room with TONS of floor space and even a walk-in closet, yet the bathroom was TINY with not much room to move in at all. Also, the tub was in bad shape -- cracks in the drainage area. I think the bathroom needed a renovation. All in all, great place to stay. Excellent location, if you want to be in downtown. Seems like there were quite a few restaurants in the area. I didn't have much time to get out, so I grabbed a bite at Smeraldi's one night and Sai Sai the next night. Both restaurants are within the hotel. Smeraldi's is Italian with a Meditteranean touch. Really great food and excellent creme brulee! Best I've had in LA so far! Sai Sai is a Japanese place. Beautiful setting and excellent service.

“the view was amazing” we were here on business, and booked this hotel because of the location of,our seminar, but were not dissapointed at all. the view fromthe terrace is spectacular, the service is good and friendly and the rooms are just fine. All in all a very nice experience. If I could name my dissapointments, Iwould say $30+ for breakfast is, to me, way to much and being on business I would have appreciated a free wifi. other than that, wonderful experience.

“Nice family hotel, not right in the middle of things but close enough” We got there early, about 11:00 am and early check in was no problem at all, even though they were fully booked. Our room was the standard size for a city hotel, (you're not gonna find too many huge hotel rooms in DC unless they are suites). The rooms are equipped with besides the standard, bed, desk, chair, dresser and wardrobe, there's a flat screen HD TV and mini frig also. I called down to request a microwave; they said they would see if there were anymore available. We left the hotel and when we got back, they had set up the microwave for us. This hotel is one block from a metro stop, which is very convenient. There's a couple of sandwich places nearby and a CVS. However, there isn't any nearby restaurants except the on site Marriott restaurant. There is on site parking. The parking deck does fill up at night, and they have to valet park your car so you have to leave your keys. I have to say they have the cheapest hotel parking I’ve seen in DC. The area this hotel is in is right near the new Nationals baseball stadium. There is a lot of new development coming up around the hotel, so I do see restaurants and more stores in the future. I'm not sure if this hotel is always as busy as it was when we were there because we were there during the Cherry Blossom festival, in the heat of tourist season and with the new baseball stadium there seem to be a game every day. Nevertheless, even with all this people traffic the service was still good.

“Time Warp Dance” If you are looking to harken back to the 70s, this hotel is for you. lots of old school brown and green, old carpets and drapes, outdated kitchenettes, and carol brady's bedspread. and her touch tone avocado colored phone. but those aesthetics aside, the Bedford offers a great location, large rooms, good HVAC, and a quiet place to sleep. for the business traveler who isn't hanging out that much in his or her room, but is looking for a good place to sleep, this isn't a bad spot, though the mattresses could certainly use an update. it is really saved by its convenient location.

“Best Family Rooms on the Planet!” Without question the best family rooms on the planet are at the Helix Hotel in Washington DC. This is a hotel with a sense of fun. The minute you walk through the front doors you know you are going to have a fun stay! We arrived late and the club on the ground floor was hopping. It was a scene for sure. The front desk was friendly and helpful. I had my two kids and had requested a family room. Once I opened the door to the room I was pleasantly surprised. The room was large, it had one area with a large king bed and a small alcove with a bunk bed. The perfect space for a family. We had a great stay here. The food was good, the room perfect and the staff friendly. Although we did not have our pet with us, I did see they were very welcoming to pets. I just love the attitude here. Customer service is high on their list. They work hard at keeping things lively and fun. The location is good and a metro station is walkable. There is no question that I would stay here again on my next visit to Washington DC.

“Cheaper in Chelsea” Preamble: We used Starwood Points to stay for our annual pre-Christmas holiday shopping trip; given the current prices of NYC hotels it was a great use of points: saved us well over $700!!!!! Check-in: Professional efficient and friendly. Lobby: Small with a friendly bar immediately adjacent to the front desk. Room: Small, nicely decorated. Nice color and furniture scheme although the furniture was suprisingly worn in places, despite our placement on a "Starwood Preferred Guest Floor". Bed: Very firm, nice linens and covers. TV: Excellent with HBO and lots of cable choices. Bathroom: Spacious with a great shower, excellent lighting, wonderful bath products, and nice towels. Check-out: Professional efficient and friendly. Location: Awesome if you want to roam around Chelsea and Greenwich Village; quiet location but close to lots of shopping and restaurants. BONUS: FREE HIGH SPEED INTERNET SERVICE!!! FREE BOTTLED WATER IN THE ROOMS. This answered two of my pet peeves about hotels these days: $10-15/day for high speed internet and $5 bottles of water that you can get elsewhere for 99 cents. Complaints: You can hear everyone talking in the hallways in your room, although not from the interior of the adjacent rooms. Scratched furniture contrasting with an otherwise creative decor.

“Fantastic Hotel and Great Customer Service” My stay here was a very last minute decision, as in I saw it from I35NB and took the exit right then! I wasn't sure where I would be staying until I saw this hotel. It is right off I 35 near the Texas Motor Speedway. I had spent the previous 7 hours on I35 from San Antonio -which is normally a 4 hour at most trip- with a slow and go bumper to bumper Thanksgiving traffic and by the time I reached Fort Worth, I was too tried and frustrated to go further. I was welcomed to this brand new property by a very nice front desk clerk. She had me checked into room 320 very quickly. I asked for a 6am wake up call and went to my room. I had chosen a king non smoking room. It was very nice. Very clean and the bed was comfortable. I saw allot of upgrades in this room that you only find in much pricier hotels, such as a ceiling fan, nice linens, and superior toiletries including some Axe Hair samples. There is a mini fridge and microwave in the room as well. The next morning I was up at 6 with my wake up call and after having a shower, I went down for breakfast. Breakfast was your typical breakfast breads, cereals, juices and coffee as well as Belgian Waffles, eggs, sausage, biscuits and gravy. The coffee was great! I was on the road by 7.15pm to my destination. I would highly recommend this hotel to whomever is traveling north on I35 and find that you are too tired to carry on or just want a nice stay in Fort Worth near some of the attractions.

“Great property, spotty service” This property is very attractive with service that leaves something to be desired. The spa is incredible, comparable to any of the others in this range. The staff provides excellent service. The pool is heated and very nice but service is better at the pool with only one wait person than the restaurant which is poolside (Rivertop). Most of its staff stand around checking their text messages. We were a party of six who could not get any service whatsoever and there were not menus on the tables. Strange as we wanted to make sure there were vegetarian options for one of party. We left the property to have drinks and some munchies in the late afternoon. Although there is a lot of staff standing around the pool and ample lifeguards, I wouldn't suggest this property until summer time. Then I am sure it is heavily staffed and your children will be delighted with the pool and the other amenities. The golf course, I would bypass on service alone. They do not carry the types of clubs other resorts do for rentals.

“Great Hotel - Just What We Needed” Had a very nice stay at The Benjamin. While we are local, (from NJ), we were just looking for a nice hotel to stay overnight and enjoy some family birthday celebrations and the city. The Benjamin did the trick. Walking distance to Central Park and all the 5th Avenue/Madison Avenue shops, very close to the subway and an extremely accommodating staff. They were doing some renovation in the lobby and things didn't look "perfect." I think that will all be taken care of very soon -- it didn't have any bad effect on my room. Bed was comfy, and bathroom was small but clean. Only disappointment was that once we were home, my husband realized he left his iPhone in the room. He kept trying numerous to retrieve it by calling the hotel and they claimed it wasn't there. Finally, he got go the right person and went back and got it. Why didn't they just call us and let us know we left it? Other than the phone incident, we had a great stay.

“Great time in spite of condition of hotel” Our 4 days in Boston were fun and the Parker House Hotel was a joy to see in the lobby and restaurants and bars. All the staff were very friendly and helpful. Room service was always prompt. I am always happy to stay somewhere with history or a hotel with character rather than just a chain hotel that could be in any city or any town. That said, however, the condition of the carpet in the hallway on the third floor and in our 1-bedroom suite was deplorable. The only way to describe the condition directly outside our room (306) is NASTY and in the room was not much better. It is inexcusable that the Parker House would let things get to this point. The furniture was also frayed (which I could live with) and stained and filthy (which I could not). We hated to sit on the sofa but had to sit someplace. I thought of asking to be moved but after walking the hallways on 2 other floors I decided it could not be much better in other rooms. After reading the other reviews on this site I have decided that decision was a mistake. Apparently not many others have had that problem and I'm happy for their luck. We must have been assigned the worst area of the hotel! I was in the room one day when the maid cleaned and she did an excellent job so none of my complaints are with her. When I did bring it up to the young lady at the front desk, she was very nice and told me the hotel is to be renovated soon. (When I don't know -- perhaps sometime between now and never?) At any rate she was very apologetic. Unfortunately, no apology could make up for that carpet. I have not seen anything that horrible in a hotel room in many, many years. Perhaps a token pass with a steam cleaner?? I was amused to hear the "haunted tour" near the hotel one night talking about the 3rd floor of the Parker House being the haunted floor. No wonder I never saw anything -- no self-respecting ghost would hang out on that floor very long! Mr. Parker must be twirling in his grave.

“I liked this more than the regular Hilton three blocks away” I really liked this property. I stayed at the regular Hilton a few times prior, and I actually liked this property better. Obviously it's not a full service hotel like the Hilton, but the staff is exceptionally helpful and everything feels more streamlined here. Great location as well.

“Nice place but but not near anything” I stayed here for one night before running the NYC half marathon. I had a discounted rate of 189.00 through NYRR. The hotel itself is on the small side, with a bar and restaurant that closed at 10 pm on a saturday night. The pool was only open until 6 pm! The hotel isnt near anything within walking distance. It was in a safe, residential area and clean.

“Very Disappointed With This Stay” I stayed at this location last year during the last weekend in October. You will see my previous review below. I enjoyed it so much that I returned again. I made the reservation for myself and a friend several weeks in advance for two beds, non-smoking. I arrived at the hotel around 3 pm on Friday, November 6. The front desk clerk asked me if I really needed two beds instead of a king. I said that I need two beds. The other desk clerk chimed in and kept asking me if I absolutely need two beds. I was rather annoyed and said that I needed two beds. End of discussion. When I checked in my room, I called my friend who was enroute to the hotel. I told him the room number. Minutes later, there was a knock at the door. I thought it was my friend. When I opened up the door, it was the security lady. She just stared at me and I finally asked "May I help you?" She was staring around my body looking through the room. She said rather curtly, "Oh, I'm just checking on the room!". I thought that was rather strange and rude! When I went to the business area, there was a noticed that the Internet was down. Bummer! The breakfast was very limited and an awful experience. Last year, there was an ample selections of pastries, etc. This time there were very little to choose from. The few selections that were being offered were not kept stocked and there was no coffee. There was some group that looked like a high school cheerleading team. They totally took over the breakfast area and were practicing in the lobby!. Trash cans were overflowing with trash and it looked like a war zone. I went out to the gazebo in the garden which I really enjoyed last year. The place was trashy all weekend. I mean all weekend! Saturday, we were in our room watching TV and there was a knock at the door. There was a couple with their luggage. The wife said, you're in our room! We told them that this was our room and that we checked in last night. We kept the deadbolt locked not knowing what to expect next. We skipped the breakfast before check out on Sunday. It was very sparse with boring minimal selections. I stayed at the La Quinta in Mt. Pleasant Texas on Friday, October 23 and the breakfast there was excellent. This breakfast was pathetic! Overall, I was very disappointed at this LaQuinta.

“Good value for the money” Stayed here for 2 nights..the night before we flew out to Hawaii and one night when we returned. We actually had 6 people and a toddler but since we were in the room for less than 12 hours each stay, we did not mind the cramped quarters. We did the snooze and cruise so the hotel allowed us to leave both our cars at the hotel for the snooze and cruise price which was about $20.00 more than the regular AAA rate of about $89.00 so it made it $109.00. That was a deal and it saved us a fortune on parking. Check in was fast and pleasant. Small lobby with a computer with internet for guests to use. Room was nice size...2 double beds, TV with cable, coffee maker. We had 2 people in each bed and a crib in between them and 2 people on the floor and still room to walk around and room for all of our luggage. They have a shuttle bus that takes you to and from the airport (about 7 or 8 miles away) and Seaworld (only a mile or 2 away). The shuttle bus stops running at 10pm which sucked for us on the return since we had 6 people with bags so we got totally ripped off by Sea-top Shuttle which charged us 10.00 per person for a 10 minute ride. It would have been cheaper for us to take 2 cabs, even 3 but my husband did not want to wait. When you have a group of people, a cab is cheaper since they are not per person. I argued with the driver that I thought his price was too high since we had 6 adults and he told me by the time I hire 2 or 3 cabs it would be the same. We should have just taken a cab anyways. Our return room had a nice kitchenette in it with small fridge and microwave. the next morning though was noisy and we kept hearing alot of loud people outside our door. I understand this hotel has inside corridor rooms like a hotel does but we did not see these, we didnt care since we were only in the hotel for a very short time. Check out was fast and easy. I have always like Days Inn hotels and this one does not disappoint. Highly recommended especially for families.

“Nice Location, Parking Sucks, been to better Homewoods” The location of this Homewood suites is very nice, right on the riverwalk. The thing that I really did not like was the parking, you are FORCED to use the valet parking. They tel you to call for you car 10min before you want it out. Everything I called over 4 times, the phone rang and rang, once someone answered it was ALWAYS over 10 min to get my car. For $20.00 plus tax per night, this should have worked better. The room was ok, not as big as some other Homewoods, but nice for a downtown location. The building is an old factory converted to a hotel. So the shape of the place is odd.
