There is a full kitchen in the room, and 2 TVs. I did find the lighting in the room not as good as it should be, the bathroom lighting was very bad. There is free wireless in the lobby and wired in the room, they called it high speed, not so much.. It was painfully slow. The Free breakfast was nice, and also the weeknight "dinner" was also very nice. This made it worth staying here over a full service hotel. I have been to much better Homewoods, but this place was not that bad. It was clean and the stuff was very nice. My room was not ready, ( I got there early) so the front desk lady made me some popcorn and gave me a drink. This was nice.. It is a good place to stay, but the parking was not fun.. you are going to pay any place you stay on the river, but the long waits..

“convenient but tacky” I stay here simply because I can walk to and from Union Station. The ladies locker room is disgusting and I am not sure if the pool had been cleaned recently. If you want to swim laps, don't pay the pool surcharge until you see how many kids are horsing around. The food is toxic and expensive.

“Great But Expensive” This is a well positioned hotel as it is central and provides easy access to most attractions and buildings. It is a large hotel with some 800 rooms so it can be very busy. It is also very expensive and there are better value hotels close by. The customer service was outstanding especially that of the General Manager. You can't beat the location but you can beat the price.

“Another nice stay.” This was our second stay at Sheraton West and we stayed 3 nights this time. The staff was friendly. The Memorial Day Weekend had several baseball teams there so they pretty much took up most of the hotel and took over the Club Lounge. The staff seemed to be working very hard as we would often meet them in the elevator on the way to the Club Lounge to deliver more food as we could sense the baseball teams were literally eating them out of the house. We would go by for water every now and then and the staff did a great job restocking it considering how many people were on that floor. Our pet really enjoyed the Sweet Doggie Sleeper that was freshly dry cleaned when it was delivered to us. The coffee was very good as usual. The only mild complaint was the sheets on the king sized bed didn't seem to fit the bed. We constantly had to remake the bed as the sheet was coming off during the night as well as day at times. This was a bit annoying. We did inform the manager on duty and the housekeeping manager came to our room so we showed her how the sheets did not totally fit the king sized bed very well. She was very nice and courteous and indicated she would inform her manager but that these were the only sheets available. The manager on duty was very nice as well and apologized for the inconvenience and offered us another room or breakfast credit but we declined. We got a nice little note from her on check out day which was very professional. We would definately stay here again and recommend this hotel.

“All new...definitely above average” Hotel is completely renovated. Everything is brand new. Beautiful carpets in the room and in the hall. Modern furnishings, plush bedding, new bathrooms with separate shower. Flat screen TV. Very comfortable and great location in downtown Memphis area near the water. Across from a seedy park where the homeless get their free daily meals. Otherwise, it was great with adequate parking (although not covered parking). If there was a parking garage, I don't remember seeing it. Plenty of vending machines and a nice breakfast area. Room was a bit small but bed was comfortable and room was freshly painted. Downtown trolley tracks run next to the hotel. Another very nice all-suite hotel is across the street. City bus stops in front of the hotel. Short walk to a Walgreens pharmacy. Not very far from the greyhound bus station. Many nice restaurants in the area. Quiet and secure...key card is needed to enter the side doors of the building. Nice art work in the halls. A bit pricey at $90/night including tax and after using a coupon.

“Awesome location w/Water Taxi landing” We stayed at the Waterfront Marriot as part of a conference, and we got the all important conference rate. We also got a harbor view, which is highly recommended. I recommend you park your car and use your feet or the water taxi to get around. There is a water taxi landing 50 feet from the hotel's entrance, and all of the inner harbor and Little Italy are just half a mile away (though in different directions). Harbor East (where the hotel is located) has also been growing fast. It seemed very happening. One criticism: the concerge didn't know anything about the surrounding area -- particularly Little Italy. So, come armed with your own information.

“Good new hotel on Gold Coast” Great new hotel. Service is first class. Room was very large with a full kitchen. We loved the espresso coffee machine. Enjoyed beverages at Rebar. Bathroom amenities were great and loved the in mirror HD TV. I do prefer totally separate shower and tub but this was a nice design. Comparing to Park Hyatt, we do prefer the Hyatt instead although not taking anything against Trump. It is a great new addition to the luxury hotels in Downtown Chicago.

“Excellent hotel, excellent location” Lenox is an excellent hotel in an excellent location. Our room was spot on clean and well appointed. The staff is incredible with interest in your needs being met. Just out the door Boylston street and around the corner from Newbury Street means plenty of dinner locations and lots of shopping. A short walk to Fenway Park. We highly recommend the Lenox.

“Great but overpriced” Stayed 3 nights in april 08. Hotel was booked for a business outing at 550$/night. Room was extremely well appointed and quite large, wonderful bathroom. Staff was nice and I really have no major complaints other than the price (which is probably not out of line for New York) but I don't feel it was really worth it. Pros: clean, luxuriously renovated rooms, competent staff. Cons: paying wifi (16$/day) and shampoo/soap... At 500$ + per night this W could offer a 2 ounce bottle of shampoo to their customers...

“Good hotel in a great location” Spent a night on points to explore the city with my wife and daughter. Used a rollaway as we don't like the 2xdouble bed option, which often puts us in non-marriotts to get 2x Queen beds. Was a little tight with the rollaway, but perfectly usable. Know the two towers; in one all rooms have balconys, in the another (which has the concierge lounge) there are just large glass windows. Great views, easy walk to gaslamp diistrict, marina for harbor tours, ferry to Coronado, Midway carrier museum. My 11YO enjoyed the pool as well, though it was a bit chilly for me! Would stay again.

“Awesome service! Great Location!” My wife and I stayed here for a quick weekend getaway and were extremely pleased with our stay from beginning to end. The parking valets were prompt and friendly. The bell staff was welcoming even though we were carrying our own small bag. Three hotel employees welcomed us on the way to the front desk! The check-in experience was fabulous. Linda was not only efficient and friendly, she came out from behind the counter and walked us towards the elevator, pointing out hotel highlights as we walked. We stayed in a corner room on the 22nd floor. Beautiful view! And the room was very large - I'd guess close to 500 square feet. The bed was a typical newer Hilton bed - very nice! While the furnishings appeared to be a few years old, everything was in great shape. And the fruit basket delivered to our room was nice touch. The concierge lounge is open weekends, which seems to be rare these days. Typical evening snacks and continental breakfast. But it's open all day for that cup of coffee or bottle of water. The location is perfect! Easy access to the freewway and all of L.A. And right next to Universal Studios and Citywalk. A short walk puts you in the middle of lots of shops, restaurants and movie theaters. This was one of the best hotel stays we've had lately. Every hotel employee we encountered greeted us and made us feel welcome. We highly recommend the Universal Hilton!

“great when I can get a good rate” have stayed several times on business, once through the weekend. keep coming back because (1) breakfast by the fireplace can't be beat, (2) friendly staff, (3) comfortable beds, (3) coffee/tea in room, (4) great location, (5) modern shower/etc. never can quite get the wifi to work, but it is free, I think it depends what floor you are on.
“日本人向けホテルです。” 卒業旅行で利用しました。すぐ近くに日系スーパーがあり、リトル東京も徒歩すぐです。またスタバが隣接していて朝早く出るときには便利です。 部屋も広く快適で、窓からは日本式庭園が見れて良かったです。 ただ、最寄り駅のcivic centerまでは少し離れていますが、人通りも多いので安心して利用できます。

“Solid choice” Just checked out after completing my planned 1 night stay --- coming to NYC weekly now for work and checking out different hotels in close proximity to my office. Hilton Fashion District will stay definitely be on my repeat list. Pros: -- location is halfway between Penn Station and my office so dropping off my suitcase on my walk to the office was a great convenience, a bonus was that my room was ready so I got to check in early as well. Room was decent size and very clean. The set up of the room was great and plenty of room to move around. Bathroom was good size and clean. Good water pressure and roomy shower. Bed was extremely comfortable and the reading lamps were nice to have. Elevators seemed efficient. Front desk folks were very nice but not overly gushing. Room service menu had many reasonable options and food arrived quickly and hot. Cons: -- location was convenient but my real preference is being slightly closer to Park Ave; room noise as my room was right across from the elevators on the 5th floor so I heard the elevators and the street noise (note to definitely request a higher floor next time); the entry of the room was definitely on the dark side and because of the safe location in the closet any long garments would pool on top of the safe; turning on the shower required getting wet; the front desk area seemed crowded and frenzied. Ultimately the convenience of the location and the Hilton Honors points keep this on my list.

“Fantastic location!” For us, this hotel was an excellent location. It was close to my husband's conference, next to shopping, walking distance to China town, and even a little further (but still walking distance) to North Beach & Fishermans' Wharf. The hotel was better than average but nothing spectacular. We were there for 8 nights, with a complimentary upgrade to the 28th floor in the Tower. Glass elevator was great! Views were fantastic. Cleaning was done daily, but not consistently (ie tea/toiletries sometimes replaced). Hotel is very large and very busy, it therefore lacked a more personal touch. Overall though, it was good.

“Great location. Decor very tired but does the job.” 3 nights standard room $80/night Pros - Location is great. Right in the heart of the union square region. 5min walk to BART Powell station and Market St. - Complementary continental breakfast Cons - Right on the main street Powell. Can be a little noisy with the cable cars at night. However our room 406 was surprisingly quiet. - Small room, the furnishings a little tired. Wifi was charged at $10/day. Lots of free wifi all around San Francisco. Overall the hotel does the job, but if you are looking for the extra little touches of flashiness and hospitality don't expect much.

“Nice Hotel and Great Location” We stayed here for 1 night to go to a Red Sox game. We then moved down closer and stayed at the Doubletree. This is a nice clean hotel and had no issues whatsoever. A little pricey and you get a convention charge (tax). I would recommend especially if going to a ball game.

“Hate the elavators!” Got a good rate from Travelzoo.com. The room was updated and clean. Heaters worked quietly and efficiently. The bathroom was clean and the water hot. The staff was friendly and courteous. The only complain and its a big one....it took forever for the elevators! Average wait was 5 minutes! And these are express elevators!

“Yuck” Not the best of hotels. I was in one of the wings. Hotel is old and visably unappealing. It says its on 35 acres, but they literally use all that area. Parking gates to get in and out of lot. Very big hotel, not very good hotel though. If I returned to Seattle, I would most likely skip this place.

“Another Outstanding Stay at the O!” Just had my annual stay at the Orchard, and as usual, it was an oasis of calm and comfort in the midst of a chaotic business trip. I would not stay at another hotel in San Francisco--the value at the Orchard cannot be beat. The rooms are a nice size compared to many boutique hotels in the area, with quite a large bathroom--plenty of counterspace for a lady to spread out her necessities! The down comforter, crisp linens, and fluffy pile of pillows make for a wonderful night's sleep, as does the individually-controlled air conditioning--another item missing from many SF hotels in this range of quality. Lovely robes, nice toiletries, and plenty of room to pack away your things all add up to an incredibly comfortable stay. Free internet adds to the allure, as does the excellent room service provided by the restaurant downstairs. Food is really good and always arrives promptly and at the right temperature--best of all, The O is thoughtful in providing the appropriate condiments and utensils--things you may not have thought about yourself! The daily maid service is unobtrusive and consistent--I have never failed to have exactly what I need or requested provided promptly. And best of all, the service and attitude of the staff are just amazing. They respond with friendly professionalism and never fail to offer a smile along with their excellent service! And all of this at an excellent value in a truly convenient location. What more could you ask for? I highly recommend this hotel to people who want to feel comfortable and welcomed and prefer a quiet, traditional-style hotel to the newer "hip" hotels full of sleek, minimalist decor. The Orchard is, admittedly, showing a wee bit of wear, but like the grand dame she is, her put-you-at-ease personality is like your favorite aging aunt--you love her all the more for her little cosmetic flaws. Everything is spotlessly clean and fresh, and all you will find are a few worn spots on the edges of furniture or carpet--certainly nothing that will spoil the experience. I won't stay anywhere else in San Francisco. The Orchard Hotel is my home away from home, and I wish there was one in every city!

“Decent stay with somecomplaints” The embassy suites at Logan was a decent place, the bedding and TVs are new and I never heard any noise when I was trying to sleep. The location is very, very good with the property being adjacent to the airport and next to the T. The price was stiff, but didn't seem out of line for the area. I do have some minor complaints : Took forever to pick us up from the airport (could have just taken a taxi). We called and they said "we'll send the driver right over" and I had to call back 30 minutes later to find out where the driver is. That's not enjoyable late at night. Breakfast was the worst I've ever had at an Embassy, there was an extremely long line for omelets, the coffee was awful, and the juice never seemed to taste right. All the pastries were stale and the bacon was flimsy. There was also no alcohol served at the "managers reception". I don't know if this is an Embassy issue or a state issue, but it was dissapointing.

“LOVE LOVE LOVE!!” We love a nice short weekend trip to get away from it all, and the Hyatt at Olive 8 is a great place if your destination is downtown Seattle. It is a very new hotel, and were fortunate enough to try it after winning it on a bidding website (the price was still above average, but this was a crazy weekend in Seattle where barely anything could be found for under $300/night, and this is an above average hotel). Worth the splurge, and we felt we got our money's worth. If only our stay was longer, but there's always next time. A true pleasant surprise. We were welcomed upon check in with a map of the area (nice gesture), and we arrived in our room to be wowed by such a nice room we wished our stay was longer. The location was next to none, right next to Pacific Place (a shopper's paradise), and only a short walk from everything else downtown Seattle has to offer. We had previously stayed at the Westin, and this is a much nicer hotel by a long stretch. The bathroom was so nice and modern, and we loved the shower (no tub--which we actually loved). They even had my favourite toothpaste!!! Love the space saving, modern sliding glass door (wish we could do that in our condo back home!) They have free wifi in the lobby, and we wished we had a chance to try Urbane, which was always bustling. We wished we had the time to try the steam room/pool, but there was so much to do (Seattle has so many nice restaurants--try the Ponti Seafood Grill--a drive away in the University district, or walk to the Hunt Club in the old Sorrento Hotel for the $30 prime rib special). Would be back in a heartbeat! TIP: If you are on a budget you can self-park overnight in Pacific Place (2 blocks away). It was very secure, and even though the overnight rate is $28/night we lucked out and only paid $11 and we entered before the 5pm!) The people in the parkade were a bit confusing, but I think it was a summer parking special. The rate is cheaper if you enter after 5pm I believe.

“Great Hotel Good Location Great Service” I stayed here on a last minute trip to Washington. I am in Washington very frequently and I normally stay at the Willard but have decided to move my travels over to SPG hotels. So far have had excellent service and this St Regis is no different. I am only SPG Gold yet have had nice upgrades, can't wait to see what I get once a Platinum! Check in was quick and efficient and was given a lovely room and told breakfast would be included. Next I was handed over to the bellman, I "think" his name was Jose or Juan, who was really great, what an asset to the hotel. Other staff I encountered were also very friendly and went out of their way to be helpful also. I didn't end up taking advantage of the breakfast but did order a very late night room service and the food was very good, came promptly and was reasonably priced for Washington. The location of the hotel is excellent and very close to the Metro, pretty much exactly between 2 stations. 5 minute walk either way. Although I didn't use it, I checked and they do offer valet parking. Daily rate of $25 or overnight at $45 either with in/out privileges. Yep, expensive but at least they offer daily rate which many hotels do not. I did use the butler service to handle some pressing and packing. I had just come from a quick overnight trip from Mexico and had nothing but a backpack, bet the butler doesn't get a lot of requests for packing up backpacks!! LOL I had to rush out in the morning for a meeting so I sent a quick email from my phone and when I returned my bags were packed and ready to go! Much appreciated seeing that I was in quite a rush leaving, made things so much easier on me. While I still love the Willard, I can see me staying her on my future visits to Washington.

“Friendly people and lovely grounds!” My daughter and I stayed here while doing a college tour of nearby Pt. Loma University. We picked it based on location and price. I must say that this hotel has one of the friendliest staffs (from phone reservationists to front desk people to restaurant workers, maid service, etc.) that I have ever dealt with. I was very impressed with everyone. The hotel sits on Shelter Island on a strand backing onto a boat marina and across the street from a fishing bay, so there is water on both sides. There are three sections, all styled differently. It looks like they were once three separate motels which have all been combined now. We stayed in the "Island Palms" section which had a Polynesian flair and decor. The lobby and restaurant are in this section, so it was convenient for us. The rooms were motel style with openings to the outside. We opted for a non-view room, since we knew we'd be arriving late at night and leaving early in the morning. The view rooms look out over the boat marina--some have little patios on the ground floor. Our room was very small and rather dark, but comfortable. The most impressive part was the bathroom--it was very nicely decorated with good amenities. The bedding was okay--not luxurious, but not scuzzy by any means! My main complaint would be the heating/cooling system. It was noisy and didn't seem to have an automatic thermostat. It was either ON full blast or off. The decor was rather blah at first glance, but grew on me as I noticed many of the themed little touches. With better lighting, it may have impressed me more immediately. We had free internet access, cable tv, coffeemaker, blowdryer and free parking. The area is nice for walking, looking at the boats, watching the fishermen and enjoying the lovely views. There was a lovely pool area with a Tiki bar and an onsite restaurant. I was disappointed that there was no free or discounted breakfast, but we ate there anyway. The food was fine, nothing extraordinary, but in a nice setting with views of the marina. There was outdoor seating, also, but it was too cool in the morning to sit out there this time of year. I would recommend this hotel for a nice relaxing visit to San Diego. The price was good, and the location was lovely. I would opt for a larger room next time, however.

“Hellish nights in Hell's Kitchen” I am staying here trying to recover (albeit unsuccessfully) from the flu and after being awakened in early morning with hammering right outside my window, and feeling even worse, I asked for a comp night because I was in no shape to fly home. The asst. general manager wasn't able to do that. I guess he's also not able to ALERT guests to the fact that construction is taking place throughout and outside the hotel like most 4 star hotels? It's a courtesy so you can change rooms or leave. This was the second room I moved to because of construction above me in another room! But the velvet ropes are up and the restaurant will be opening any day, I've been told 20 times. Where are the priorities here? The construction on this hotel was done quickly and is pretty shoddy. For example, my toilet seat won't open and stay up. I have never experienced this in my life. It closes down on you! Was there no quality checks done here? Garbage trucks also roam up and down all night long and the windows aren't nearly sound proof enough. Now I know why they call it Hell's Kitchen.

“Great location” The hotel staff was very friendly - parking was very convenient and rooms were nice and clean. Room layout a little small (beds are only doubles). Otherwise very nice. great location. Area recommendations I like Magnificent Mile and Streeterville but sometime choose Lincoln Park or River North It depends on what we plan to do.

“Great value and convenient” A great place to stay if you are in Chicago for a getaway weekend. Rooms are small but adequate, especially since you will probably be out exploring most of the time anyway. Well furnished and comfortable for their normal business clientele. Nice pub/restaurant downstairs. Very convenient to the El so you don't feel isolated despite the Loop location. The staff was excellent - my bag was mistakenly taken from the luggage room by another guest and the hotel staff went above and beyond to retrieve it and mail it to me overnight when it was returned. (I will now invest in something distinguishing to put on my bag to avoid the "all black roll-aways" problem!!) Hotel is very safe and secure - also set up so that noise does not seem to be a problem. Walking distance to the Berghoff and Sears Tower.

“Great Stay at W San Fran” I stayed at the W San Fran from July 21-27 for a conference at the Moscone Center. The hotel is directly across the street from the Moscone Center, and while most of the 8,000 attendees were shuttled around in buses, I simply hopped across the street! Check in was slow; there were only 2 people at check-in, and there were a lot of conference attendees in line. However, the service was very professional. The room was a standard W suite, with a fully-stocked bar, robes and Bliss toiletries. We requested a refrigerator (for medication) ahead of time, but it was not available. We were directed to use the fridge in the mini-bar. They had to unlock it remotely, and then we had to unload all the contents in order to use it. We weren't thrilled about that, but we didn't dwell on it. Well, when we realized the fridge really didn't get cold, we were told once again that there were none available. We had to use ice from the ice machine to keep the medicine cold, which worked. We had a 25% coupon for all restaurants in the hotel, and it came in handy a couple of times during the week-long stay. I used the gym every morning, and it was a typical, well-appointed gym, with apples and Bliss moistened face wipes for post-workout. They also have the standard spare earbuds in case you forget yours, cold water dispenser, and very clean restrooms. The gym overlooks the (small) pool area. Requests for extra towels and toiletries were handled quickly. The hotel lounge area (right next to the lobby/check-in) is quite lively (loud) during happy hour. The concierge and staff were very accommodating. I needed to print something out, and the fee was like, $7.00 to log on to the internet, and about $1.00 per page. REALLY? I had my personal wi-fi, so I didn't have to pay for the internet, but instead of spending almost $10 to print out a document, I had my administrative assistant fax it to the hotel. So, as usual, I had an overall very good stay at the W San Fran: PROS: proximity to the Moscone Center; proximity to premium shopping (short walk). Short cab ride to the wharf, but the traffic makes the fare a bit expensive. Gym facilities; toiletries (love BLISS!). Secure - you cannot access floors 5 and above without your room key. Bay view from our room. CONS: Inability to get a facial appointment at the Bliss Spa (so disappointed!); no fridge - despite the early request.

“If you do it right....” The hotel is good if you book a deluxe or above level room. If you book a standard room or win a bid on Priceline (which you get a standard room), like we did, then you will be really cramped. Two skinny people had trouble maneuvering around the room. Also, the shower is separated by a sheer curtain from the bedroom so there is no bathroom privacy if you are traveling with anyone other than your significant other. There are a lot of great things about this hotel. The location is perfect, the rooms are very clean, the staff is excellent, the crowd staying at this hotel seems very young and hip. Overall a good experience. What this hotel desperately needs is new windows. The windows are so old and not sealed well and you can hear everything outside, all night long. I can't say we got a good night sleep.

“The breakfast is a horror; an otherwise very good experience” Clean, quiet, characterful, convenient; pleasant staff; hot water and lots of it (I do like a good shower, and my suite's was excellent)... but oh, what a sad little droopy breakfast! Twelve tubs of vanilla yogurt and one of strawberry; a platter of shelled hard-boiled eggs; a bowl of bananas, a bowl of apples, several dispensers of dry cereal; juices; coffee; two toasters and various sliced second-rate baked goods (pseudo-bagels, Engiish muffins several notches down from Thomas'; nasty would-be waffles); dreary tublets of margarine, non-maple syrup, Smucker's preserves, and Kraft's library paste -- oh, all right, "Philadelphia cream cheese", but how DO you tell the stuff from spackling compound?). Clearly a breakfast selection put together principally to discourage people from carrying their lunch away with them... Are you reading this, hotel management? Then take $5 / person off your overnight rate, provide your guests with chits good for the Alexander Inn Selection at any of the many, many little eateries within a two minutes' walk from your door, and make coffee available off the lobby as a backstop. Don't skimp and botch: Outsource to someone who can do the job properly!

“Pleasantly surprised....” Courtyard is not my favorite Marriott brand, so was not looking forward to staying here - but glad that I did. A reasonably priced option 1 block off of the Miracle Mile, Starbucks in lobby, Dunkin Donuts across the street, and Capital Grill and Lux Cafe up the block. Of course shopping is just a few steps away - within one block is Forever 21, Nordstroms, and Home Goods - all price ranges for all pocketbooks. Oh, and don't forget Garretts next door! Check in staff was pleasant, also all front end personnel. Room was a normal size, somewhat surprising for the price and in the city - was expecting a cubicle! Marriott clean, nice marble bath, with sink outside of toilet area...so much easier than when it is all in one. AC was not working correctly when I arrived, and was corrected within 15 minutes. (and when is AC even needed in March in Chicago!) Internet speed was good, elevators were fast (I was on 18), and keys consistently worked. I would be surprised to find a better value in this area, and will definitely return. Why not a 5 star? - I hate paper cups and that horrible in room coffee service...along with cheapo toiletries. Other than that - this is a decent hotel, and when you factor in the price - well above average. And since I spend 100+ nights in a hotel...........

“Trendy” We had stayed here on business last summer and found it too trendy. The front desk check in doesn't look like any other hotel. The problem with these new trendy hotels is that they seem to be cold and lack character with all that glass. This is personal taste and doesn't reflect the service of the hotel. The location was great and walking distance to all attractions and restaurants. There is a famous restaurant that serves breakfast all day long and is the only restaurant open 365 days never close within a block of the hotel. Our rooms were clean and the lounge area offered free WIFI. You would have to pay for it in the room. The hotel has a large ballroom which held our dinner event.

“A Very Elegant and Classy Night” The moment the concierge opens the door to the Waldorf, we catch a breath of regal air and instantly our eyes scan the lobby to make sure we aren't violating a dress code. We were awestruck by the amount artwork put into every square inch of this place. We arrived HOURS early for check-in and wanted merely to drop off our bags. Instead, we were able to check into a room on the 12th floor immediately. Gorgeous room, nice view, quick and courteous service. It took us longer to check out than it did to check in. We walked around and window shopped; listened to a man play the lobby piano; and hiked around the corner to a nearby deli for a late night snack. This classic is the heart of the city, in the heart of the city. There can't be too many other ways to do New York City. $200 a night was well worth it. Next time at the Waldorf, we're gonna raise the bar a bit. Hopefully they'll welcome us again.

“Recently Updated, Thin Walls” Many of the reviews below mention that this property was old and worn down. Just wanted to update that they've renovated at least several rooms and I assume eventually all of them. The interior is as nice as I've experienced at a Residence Inn. Granite counter tops, stainless steel fridge, upgraded stove top, flat screens in two rooms. Upgraded and very satisfactory workout facilities. Based on my one night here, I don't know if they've fixed the sound issue though. I'm in a room that has an adjoining room, and even though the people next door are speaking at reasonable volumes I can pretty much hear them like they're in my living room. So, awesome rooms, just hope that you get a quiet neighbor.

“Great Hotel in a great location!!!” We drove down from northern NJ on Memorial Day Weekend and researched this hotel for about a month. This is a great hotel in a beautiful area of the inner harbor of Baltimore. The staff is well versed on working a hotel of the nature and from parking to check-in was a breeze. The price of this hotel isn’t cheep but it is well worth it. On previous recommendation we heard that the harbor view was the way to go and boy it was worth every penny of the extra money. The rooms are large enough for a family of four and very nice. It was true about the hall noise could be heard through the door but it stopped after 8 pm but the activity and noise from the street could be a problem if you are not accustomed to city life. The hotel is connected to a very nice mall and is in walking distance to everything to see in the inner harbor area. The restaurant and lounge in the hotel are first class and kids under eight eat free, with a child menu for kids under fifteen. This is great because the food isn’t cheep but the meals are worth it. The harbor restaurants in the area fill up fast so it is nice to have a nice place to eat with kids to avoid the wait near the water. Our family of four with young children found this hotel very kid friendly and accommodating to every adult need and more. We will be back for another two night in the near future as soon as our new addition arrives and try to fit five in a room ( if they let us ). Great place great location, give it a try!

“Not impressed” Stayed for one night during a meeting in Detroit. It has some things going for it but I wouldn't stay there again given other choices in the area. Pros: - Convenient to airport - Rooms have been refurbished and are comfortable though somewhat small. Flat screen TV (though no digital or HD channels). Good beds. - Free parking - Wifi is $9.95/day but free for elite members - Friendly and efficient reception service - Nice fitness room with modern equipment and good sized indoor pool/hot tub The cons: - The airport runway is across the road. It was quiet the night before but at 7:30 am jets started to take off and it was LOUD. For some reason they stopped about an hour later and I didn't hear it for the next few hours. But don't expect to sleep late. - The building shows its age despite efforts to refurbish - Guests and staff share two elevators so you are riding with housekeepers & their carts and room service. Odd in a large hotel. - The day I checked in I noticed that some travel websites had a lower rate and I asked if the receptionist would match it and they said no. Strange, given other chains have been willing to do this. - I did not eat in the hotel but noticed that their 24 hour pantry prices are high. $2.50 for a 20 oz. bottle of water--the same bottle was $1.50 in the vending machines on guest floors. They were asking $1.50 for some bananas which were old and black. - There is only one computer in the lobby. If someone else is using it you're out of luck. The cons are not deal killers--it just shows that this hotel has tried to modernize to compete with the newer hotels that are business traveler-friendly but doesn't quite get there. The hotel caters to conferences--there are many meeting rooms on the ground floor. Other than that it's a typical airport hotel.

“Lovely Botique Hotel” My wife and I stayed here for our anniversary last night. We live in Dallas. We arrived early and had drinks at the bar. The bar is very comfortable and a small but able selection of beers. My wife had an excellent Pinot Noir by the glass. We ate dinner at Bolla, which was excellent. The room was huge, and very nicely appointed, and new. There was a nice view of downtown. The bath and shower were again very large and well designed. The staff was helpful and very professional. The rate was quite reasonable, especially for the quality of the room.

“Flowers Waltz” Sofitel NY is really beautiful. A small island of French spirit in huge cosmopolitan city. “Bonjour!” is the first greeting you hear at the entrance or by phone. An ocean of fresh flowers. Thousands of flowers in big glass vases everywhere. Orchids, carnations, roses, peonies. A kind of a flourish summer garden in cold winter. Such a stylish place! I just couldn’t pass by that miracle and put my curious nose into a pack of white-and-pink peonies - Oh! What an adoring aroma! - And immediately got a condemning look of a lady from reception. Pardon madam, no more boyish behavior. Promise. The reception staff in general is friendly and effective. The check-in took some minutes. I got a room on the 7th floor just in front of an office’s window on the opposite wall at the distance of a few meters. Hope, the guys who daily were working there could hardly see me thanks to the dirtiness of my window. The room was quite spacious and very nicely designed. For instance, I liked the b/w photos on the wall picturing the construction of the Eiffel tower in Paris. Besides, the bouquets of fresh cut orchids in the bedroom and bathroom – nice touch also. The room was very clean and equipped very well – cable TV, air-conditioner, mini-bar, alarm-clock, CD-player, iron and ironing board, electronic safe-box. At daily turndown service, a bottle of Evian still water and a small set of Belgian chocolates are always complimentarily left in room. In marble bathroom, there are a small tug with shower and a separate shower cabin, a hair-dryer, a lot of high quality bathing cosmetics, bathrobes and slippers. Everything is perfect! Dry cleaning and laundry service is absolutely efficient. Every day I sent my shirts to laundry; and my trousers and jackets – for pressing. And I received all my items the same day evening perfectly done. The maid service is very good. In half an hour after my arrival, maids’ supervisor visited my room wondering if everything was all right. Moreover, I was immediately provided with bigger size slippers when I complained that ones already obtained were small for me. And usually, I got my room cleaned already in the morning coming back from breakfast. Breakfast is served at Gaby restaurant as well as lunch and dinner. American breakfast for $20 is great! It traditionally includes eggs, sausages/ham/bacon, pan-fried potato, tomatoes, freshly squeezed orange juice, coffee, croissant, and jam. Besides, fresh berries plate with soar cream is also highly recommended. The restaurant and bar designed like a French café-bistro and stylishly decorated with old French movies’ snapshots with famous actors - Jean Gabin, Gerard Philippe, Jean Marais, et al. It’s a nice place to have a dinner too. The French cuisine is very good. The personnel are extremely pleasant and well skilled. But most of all, I’m pleased by the concierge service. Daniel and Vlad, thank you guys for your great job! I’d like to especially appreciate Vlad’s personal assistance to find out my disappeared prepaid tickets to Metropolitan Opera which hadn’t been delivered by a local ticket agency on time neither to my place in Moscow nor to Sofitel in New York City. Many thanks again, Vlad! All in all, I really liked this hotel very much. It’s a wonderful place for staying there. It’s not cheap at all, but worths every buck spent! And location! Just in the heart of Manhattan! Take a few steps on your left – the 5th Avenue; a few steps on your right – ever shining Times Square, 42nd Street subway station and Broadway theatres; fifteen minutes slow walk straight ahead downtown – the Macy’s shopping kingdom. Where to go? That depends... No doubt, definitely would stay here again!

“Great if you need extra space.” We stayed in a 1 bdrm suite 8/17-18 ($149/night on Expedia). The room was certainly nothing fancy but it was very large and clean. The kitchen had a decent sized refrig and microwave so we were able to bring some meals and save money. The courtesy shuttle never seemed to be available when we needed it but the bellman got us a taxi within seconds and it was a $3-$5 cab ride wherever we wanted to go (Camden Yards, Inner Harbor). We also walked to the Aquarium; probably 15 minutes. The walk back is uphill but not too bad (even pushing strollers). The self-park lot next door wasn't too expensive ($13/day I think). The staff was courteous, the pool was small but adequate, the deli made great sandwiches.

“Was expecting more” There is nothing near this hotel and the restaurant/pub next door is a dive! This hotel seamed like they remodeled a run down old hotel. The breakfast was WEAK! i did enjoy the complimentary shuttle service to Mill Ave. and the bed was comfortable.

“Typical business hotel.” I stayed at the New York Marriott East Side for two nights while attending a business conference. My room was small but clean and comfortable. I did eat a late night dinner at the hotel the night I arrived and it was nothing special.

“Good Location and Value With a Clean Comfortable Suite” The property is easy to access from I-405 just east of I-5 south of Seattle; there is plenty of parking on the side and a short walk to the main door. Even though I checked in early, the friendly front desk representatives didn't make a fuss and I was in my way up to my suite within a minute or two of arrival. My suite was quiet, well-furnished and very clean. The property is not new and does show its age in some areas (the silicon grout used to seal the corners between walls and ceiling was sloppy). The lobby and other common areas are well maintained. The suite had all of the essentials - microwave, small fridge, two flat panel TV's, and a work desk and chair. Internet access is wireless, and unless you're a Diamond HHonrs member and elect to receive no-charge access, be prepared to pay a hefty fee as others have noted. Internet upload/download speeds were pretty good. The manager's evening reception and the included breakfast each morning are nice touches that represent value when taken in the context of the rates at this property. Overall, I believe I received a good value for what I paid and I recommend this property.

“Good on an expense account--otherwise not worth it” I stayed at the Clift for 1 night this past April. It is similar to other hotels owned by this hotel group, with basic but tasteful furnishings, and an overall calm, zen feeling in the rooms. Even though the bathrrom was minimal (including a shower that was way too basic for the price of the room), I found the bed very comfortable and the night very relaxing. As it was a weekend night, the lobby was overrun a by loud, drunk, 20something crowd, most of whom were not hotel guests, and made getting in/out of the hotel a nightmare. In summary, the hotel is great if you want to party and are not paying for your own room, otherwise it is overpriced.

“Best value out there! There are hotels in SF in worse shape for twice the price!” Got a good deal on a double room for $45.50 and was next to my favorite mexican restaurant colibri. 3 buildings away from 24 hour fast food at jack and 45 seconds away from my favorite night club Ruby Skye which I attended on friday and saturday for mardi gras, both complimentary due to friends in high places($30 savings each night!) The room was actually in pretty decent shape and was good sized. I was aware that shampoo/conditioner was not provided, so I brought along some i've collected along the road from some of my other SF hotel stays in 4 star hotels i've lucked out finding for under $100. You are in SF to have fun and explore not to be in the room all day, but I did take it easy and watch the NBA all star festivities in the room on my last night in SF. Brought ear plugs, but they were not needed. The manager at the hotel was very good at answering my questions prior to my stay, so I would like to give him praise as well. Unless you can find 4 star accomodations for under $80, i think this is the best value in San Francisco!

“Nice hotel in a good location” I stayed at Hilton Union Square over Labor day weekend, in a room on the 16th floor in Tower 3 facing the pool. The room was recently renovated and was very nice. There is a skybridge connecting towers 1 and 3 with a view of the city. There are lots of seating areas in the lobby and many people hang out their on their laptops to avoid the Internet charge. The hot tub is a great way to unwind after a day of seeing the city and there is also a heated pool. Seems strange there is very little light in the pool area at night. Hotel is one of those big, convention hotels and can be crowded. It is in the middle of the heart of downtown San Francisco. The hotel is close to some sketchy areas but as long as you go east when leaving the hotel you will avoid them.

“Good place to rest for a night” I was on a cross country trip for rest and relaxation with various friends and stayed at hotels between stays at friends homes. I was only staying for a night as I rested on long drive days so I did not need anything fancy. Microtel offered a friendly staff and a safe comfortable room. That was all I needed.

“Great Hotel, Bad Business Practices!” Recieved an email from Omni on May 17 for a special stay one night, get the second night complimentary promotion. The promotion was booked through the Omni website, and I got a confirmation from the Omni Hotel for one night, and the second night complimentary. Called the hotel that night to verify the rate, and was told the rate was good-one night at $287.10 and the second night was complimentary. Called back again on May 21 and spoke with Marisol who again verified the confirmed rate and reservation. Called again on May 25 and spoke with Tony who also verified the confirmed rate and reservation. When I checked in with my family on May 26th, I AGAIN verified the confirmed rate with the clerk who checked us in. He verified the rate of 287.10 for one night with the second night complimentary. We checked in and had a wonderful time in NYC. The morning we checked out, we recieved a bill that charged us 287.10 for EACH night we stayed (we stayed 2 nights). I immediately questioned this with the front desk, who said someone would call me back. No one did, so I went to the front desk, only to be handed off to Chat, the Assistant Front Office Manager. Chat showed me her paperwork which verified the confiirmed rate and complimentary night, but said she needed to check it in the system, which was down. SHe promised to call me on May 31, but didn't. I called her, and she told me she hadn't had a chance to research it yet. I called again June 1 (since the 2 nights has already showed up on my statement), and she referred me to Catherine, the Omni Revenue Officer. Catherine tried to insist I didn't make the reservation through their website, and then tried in say that the front desk clerk told me the 287.10 was for each night. I told her the clerk said no such thing, and that my husband was standing right there and heard it. I also pointed out the 4 times that the confirmed rate and reservations were checked and verified. She said she would get back to me. In short, I feel a bait and switch has occurred here, and I will be taking this up with their coprorate offices. BE AWARE to keep all your copies and makes notes of who you spoke to and when. It may come in handy.

“Great hotel in convenient location” The Kimpton chain seems to be getting better and better. Very comfortable room, close to elevator, but did not hear at all. Curtains really block out the light in the daytime. Free internet with Kimpton membership + $10 free from the minibar. Front desk very helpful in getting my Boarding Pass printed. Add to that the great restaurant on the premises, which helped in the heavy rain when I arrived, and you cannot get much better. I should not forget the wine at 5 pm, which came with a very nice light pizza.

“Beautiful Great Hotel” My travel agent got me a deal, so I stayed here on a business trip in November. The room was very comfortable, quite, spacious (small suite), great bed, and nice amenities. The service was also outstanding! The only drawback is that the room appeared a little aged and tired . . . but this same drawback can also be viewed as a positive and part of the "yesteryear charm" this hotel exudes. If my travel agent got me a good deal on this hotel again, I would be more than happy to make this my next stay in NYC! Oh yes, the hotel has a great bar!

“Not too bad, but WiFi was terrible.” The Adante Hotel was average. Customer service was good and staff were always friendly. Rooms were quite clean (although decor was very tacky). Carpet was covered in stains. They also provided extra amenities such as a razor and toothpaste. The main issue we had was with the hotel's free WiFi, which basically was non-existent. As we were staying for six nights, this became a major issue for us. (We assumed that the problem was a result of us staying on the top floor, however even going down to the lobby did not improve the connection quality whatsoever. We eventually resorted to using free WiFi at nearby Starbucks.) Location is average. There are many pubs and bars nearby on Geary St, and a great Thai restaurant on the same block. Short walk to cable car stop and Westfield shopping mall. Be prepared for many beggars in this area.

“Good stay but could have been better” My daughter and i visited Chicago to see the city and go to a couple of cubs games from 8 May -13 May and were using reward points. i will do a pros and cons for this stay: PROS- 1. early checkin- big thumbs up to be able to drop bags off and not worry about coming back later to checkin. 2. nice breakfast-had just about anything you would have wanted. 3. location-i will put this in the pros and also the cons. really like how close the "L" was to the hotel. 4. really close to some good resteraunts like the Weber Grill and Rosebud Trattoria. Cons: 1. using points i was hoping for a bigger room with a somewhat decent view...room 1021 had a great view of the huge crane next door and the construction of the building or some structure going up. not the hotels fault but... 2. the extremely loud club next door which was banging techno music until at least 3am. again not the hotels fault but be warned if you are a light sleeper. i would suggest to get on the front side of the hotel on the street with Ruth Chris to help drown out the noise 3. Parking-we took the "L" everywhere but if you have a car it is $54 a day for parking. ouch! 4. elevators-had some minor issues. i am all for security but i had trouble with my room key using the key pad to get the elevator. i kept getting a yellow light and had to have the card changed out twice to get it to work. one day the key pad was not working and the elevator was done and some people were walking up 10-20 stories to get to their room. finally you may want to allow time on Sundays for getting to the lobby for checkout. took about 15 minutes to get an elevator with what seemed like everyone coming down at the same time (again this is not the hotels fault, just a friendly warning. normally i stay at the Residence Inn on East Walton Street but chose this hotel from the reviews. i would stay here again but i would make sure that the room is on the other side of the hotel. if i couldn't then i would go back up 1 stop on the "L" to the CHicago stop and stay in a quieter area of town at the Residence Inn.

“Wonderful!” This one is not to be missed! Everything about this hotel is wonderful. The decor, the bedding, the staff, all amazing. It's in one of the nicest neighborhoods in SFO, and is just a ten minute bus ride from everything. I know, I don't usually ride buses either, but in SFO they're great. The restaurant recommendations were perfect, and within walking distance of the hotel. If you're going to be in SFO, you owe it to yourself to try the Drisco.

“Good location, good facilities,” I stayed here overnight prior to early morning departure from LAX. Comments: 1. Overall a good property, albeit one that is aging just a bit, that delivers what you would expect from Marriott . . . clean, comfortable, efficient. 2. The room had soap bars, but no shampoo, conditioner, or any other customary bathroom amenities. Obviously a mistake. Yeah, I could have called to send some up, but I was willing to settle for washing my hair with soap rather than deal with it. 3. The fitness center is excellent . . . lots of equipment (probably about 10 treadmills, a half dozen elliptical machines, wide assortment of weights). Towels and cold water were available; equipment was equipped with individual TVs. A complaint about the fitness center is that it was kind of warm. 4. The outdoor pool is impressive, and water was bathwater warm despite it being a rather cool day. 5. The television set was an old-fashioned tube, with limited channel selection. 6. Good in-room climate control with quiet operation. 7. A large airport hotel like this should make it very easy to find out about its complimentary shuttle service to the airport -- for example, lobby signage, a prominent notice in the room, etc. -- turns out I had to call to ask, and the word was the shuttle ran about once every 25 minutes and not on a schedule. That tends to work against a primary objective of staying at an airport hotel: minimizing time spent getting to the airport. My recommendation -- if you can get past the ethics of it and your luggage is not too cumbersome -- is walk across the street to the nearby Budget Rent-a-Car and ride their shuttle (which is nearly continuous) to the LAX terminals. 8. The room was very quiet . . . no problems with airplane noise.

“Nice Hotel” The hotel is nice, but the people who work there are not friendly.....well, except for the waitress in the bar! We did not receive a warm reception. The girl that checked us in acted like we were bothering her. Valet is never on the ball. They would hang around and chat with the front desk and you would have to go in and get them. They really should not charge for parking here as the lot is right behind the hotel and it's not inconvenient to get to like downtown. Rooms are a bit on the small side and have no refrigerator like the one downtown. There is a place for one. The bathrooms are tiny. But like all Hilton's, the beds are heavenly. The hotel was clean and they have a great breakfast. Also have a wonderful sports bar and work out room.

“Beyond Bad” Terrible customer service and the room was absolutely disgusting. I checked in and out in 10 minutes and moved to a nearby hotel. Personnel was extremely rude I have never been treated so rudely anywhere else. I rather sleep in the street than at this establishment.

“Great location, nice hotel.” I've made several week-long stays at this hotel. It has a great location, close to Times Square but out of the general hubbub. It's also within easy walking distance to a lot of ethnic restaurants, plus it's across the street from a Food Emporium, a grocery store that also stocks prepared foods. There's also a very nice French bistro attached to the hotel. I only tried it for breakfast, but it was very good, and the atmosphere was relaxing, early in the morning at any rate. My rooms have been fairly large large by NYC standards and clean, although some of the upholstered furniture (and sometimes the curtains) have been stained and in need of professional cleaning or replacement. The beds are comfortable, and the microwave and refrigerator in good working order. There is also coffee/tea available in the lobby in the morning. The staff is polite, especially the maintenance people. A small pet peeve of mine: a man at the front desk told me we were bing "upgraded" when I knew the rates were identical between the room I booked and the one they gave me. Guest services staff is helpful though. All in all, this hotel is in my top 2 for stays in NYC.

“Nice ... but pricey.” I got a really good rate for this hotel on Hotwire which was about the only good deal really. The hotel is lovely and well located (has an exit right onto the Riverwalk) and has rooms that look out over the Alamo. However, parking is $23.00 a night, internet is $10 a night, the restaurant is expensive and so is the room service, Rooms are nice and big, very comfy with big flat screen TVs. The lifts are neat and the skypool is excellent on the roof!! If you got a hotwire/priceline rate for this hotel, just use it for sleeping as you wont be too happy with the prices of food etc.

“Good Airport Hotel” I've stayed at many of the properties near LAX. I'm not in love with any of them, so when a corporate rate appeared at the Sheraton that was $100 cheaper than hotels of comparable service levels nearby, I decided to give the Sheraton a try. It ended up being an acceptable experience -- I wish TripAdvisor had 3.5, as I couldn't quite give this hotel a "very good" but think it was slightly better than "average." It's still got that feeling of an airport hotel and, overall, wasn't a fabulous or amazing place. However, it delivered a solid, airport hotel experience, and I had no major or deal-breaker complaints about my stay. My room was relatively spacious and pretty well-appointed. Decor was bland, but pleasant enough. The room's plugs needed some work -- a couple of the wall outlets looked pretty old and were so loose stuff just fell out of them when I tried to plug it in! Lighting was fine. The bathroom was OK -- it was in good condition, but the tub was very elevated, so even I (of average height) had my head above the shower head. My television didn't really work so well -- the remote's batteries were dead and the buttons on the TV were stubborn. That was kind of frustrating. It was a flat-screen TV, but in a large armoire; I wish it had just been on a dresser. Most importantly, however, the bed was super-comfortable -- nice linens, great mattress, etc. Public areas of the hotel were fine. Decor is a bit dark, but the place was clean. The fitness center was excellent -- lots of windows, well lit, good equipment, a nice variety of cardio and weights. I didn't go to any of the restaurants, but I did order room service. It came at the expected time and was actually very good; my chicken sandwich was above-average for room service food, with tender chicken and a tasty avocado topping. Service was OK. My check-in was a bit disorganized -- I got asked for my ID a few times, because the clerk couldn't remember where he was in the transaction -- but it was more just him being near the end of a long day than incompetence. He was welcoming. Check-out was a bit slow but also competent and the clerk seemed appreciative of my business. The airport shuttle ran in a timely fashion and had a helpful driver. Overall, it was an acceptable experience, and for the price in comparison to its competitors it was an easy win. I wouldn't come for vacation or expecting much luxury, but for a quick overnight near LAX it did quite well.

“If you love southwest airlines you will like this hotel” And if you don't, I would suggest avoid this metropolis of a hotel. I'm not talking about the sense of humor of the SWA flight attendants, but rather the cattle car nature of the flights. You are not a guest here, but rather, a commodity (hence the southwest airline metaphor). If you have to stay here due to conference or meeting then go ahead, but if you are just looking for a nice hotel in a downtown chicago, may I suggest the Palmer House or the Swissotel? The thing I most dislike about this hotel is the lighting in the room. Super dim. There is a nice magnifying light in the bathroom, but even the bulb in that is not bright. the hallway to my room was dingy and the carpet needed to be replaced. At $250+ a night, I think the hotel could afford it. If you are here for a conference... bring your walking shoes. Although capable of accommodating large conferences, the conference area is the most inconvenient imaginable. Three floors below street level, no cell phone service, and miles from the main lobby. If you are a conference planner.... please keep looking. There are much better options in Chicago.

“Nothing special” Recently had a long weekend at this hotel. We were disappointed. When we booked a downtown hotel at the convention rate we got, we expected a lot more. This property seems a little blah even for a Hilton property. It is clean. The valet attendants were friendly and helpful. The location was pretty good. That's all the good I can say. It will make me rethink even booking a Hilton Garden in the future. The Hilton Garden Inns I have stayed at before were nicer all around. I prefer a couple of Hampton Inns in other cities I would gladly stay in again over this tier hotel. I would call it a lower 3 star property. The room was clean, but the sleep number beds and linen quality were lacking. The decor was boring. The furnishings were average. I really tried to put my finger on what was missing and never really could. I think it was all the little things that didn't add up. Even the information cards with requests for linen changes, television channels, etc. were poor quality and very used. There was new carpet in our room. The bathroom had new wallpaper. But there was no artwork on the walls and our room still had popcorn ceilings. Friends we were with had the same impressions. It was very standard and nothing special. The common areas were just that too, pretty common. The bar on the 18th floor had a nice view of downtown but not one beer on tap. ??? They seemed short staffed. It was not crowded either night we went up before leaving for dinner. We had to ask for bar snacks and were obliged. There were no vending machines on the floors, you have to go to the poorly stocked snack area near the desk. This is not my experience at other hotels of this brand. Another thing that was really odd was the number of times I was on the elevator with either a housekeeping attendant and cart (3 times), maintenance (2 times), valet and kitchen staff (2 times). I guess I have never before considered the utility for a service elevator. I might choose this property for an overnight because it fits my standard for cleanliness. But that's it. It was so lackluster that I notice my face is grimaced as I try to explain it. It is certainly not a place I am accustomed to for a couples weekend or a base for exploration with older kids. If you get a good rate it may be worth it for a night. But don't pay a downtown rate or you will be sorely disappointed.

“Fabulous Location & good service” The Hilton times square is a great location, it's located right next next to the New Amersterdam Theater. The location worked out wonderful and we were able to walk to 5th avenue, central park and many other touristy destinations. The staff was very helpful, they gave us the exact trains we needed to take to get to the Yankee's game. The hotel bar was charming, a bit pricey but something I would picture in NYC. Our room was spacious for NY standards and the room was very clean. I would definately stay here again!

“Better than the reviews” I rely on Tripadvisor to give me solid choices, but his trip I had almost no option. I was very leary to stay here based on the reviews below. All I can say is the Four Points did not let me down at all. It was clean and quiet, with a VERY comfortable bed. The staff was not only nice, but they also remembered my name hours after I checked in when I returned to the lobby. No, it's nothing extraordinary - there's updates to be made and it's off the highway. That said, it was close to where I was working, so I chose it for ease. It was a pleasure to get such a nice surprise.

“Una buona struttura” Situato a 20m minuti a piedi dal Mall nei pressi della stazione Foggy Bottom della metro, e' un hotel comodo per visitare Washington. L'aspetto esterno non è dei più gradevoli a differenza della hall e delle camere grandi e accoglienti.Viene servita una buona colazione compresa nel prezzo. Unica pecca la freddezza e la poca disponibilità del personale della reception.

“Location Location Location” Great lobby and great location. I always enjoy staying here. The hotel has great energy in the lobby. The rooms are small like all hotel rooms in New York, but they are very plush. The beds are high and comfy. The view is great if you get an upper floor room. My company paid for this hotel, but I think it can be kind of spendy.

“Wonderful boutique hotel” I looked at some of the sterile looking rooms of other hotels in the area and chose to avoid those and stay at the Lombardy. I'm glad I did! The room was large, and best of all, the luggage area was separate from the bedroom area which I always love. It means that you can keep your room "hotel" pristine without seeing your suitcase open and clothes hanging over a chair etc. There was also a separate kitchenette. Rooms were super quiet, wonderfully decorated and clean. I loved the quirky elevator and some of the staff were super friendly. (one woman who answered the front desk phone was less so ). Perhaps I've lived in Boston for too long, but I found the concierge who helped me in the elevator a little uber friendly, touching my arms a few times too many. Tip: You can't order breakfast before 7AM, and they won't accept orders the evening prior. If you have an early meeting or have to catch a morning flight, the earliest you'll receive room service is 7:20.

“Clean place, friendly staff” Stayed here for one night, and found it to be a pretty good place. It is relatively new, and consequently was in pretty good condition. The lobby, room, and common areas were all clean. Everything was typical Hampton - although I guess the "pantry" with items for purchase is more for teh Hampton Inn and Suites. Normal selection of sundries, but expensive! An ice cream bar was $5. The staff were all very friendly and helpful - there always seemed to be someone walking around keeping things clean and in order, and the front desk staff were eager to help with whatever questions I had. The fitness "center" was the standard small room with cycle, elliptical, and running...but used it and it worked well for my needs. I got a mid-week rate of $98 - so not too bad. The breakfast area was well stocked, with the standard Hampton breakfast, but again the staff were asking if there was anything they could do to help or if I needed anything. Finally - the location is the location - in other words, if you are doing something on the far west side of town, then it's a good place to stay. It's right off the Beltway at the Bellaire exit, and if you have to get back to downtown, you can get right on the Westpark tollway and head east. There aren't any restaurants or shopping within walking distance, so be sure to have a car or ride.

“As always, HGI is just a very nice place to stay” For the non-business traveler (assuming money is not unlimited) Hilton Garden Inn is almost always a great choice. It is a bit pricier than the Hampton Hotels but the extra money buys you full hotel service and it is usuallly very good. This hotel was no exception- from the valet parkers to the bell staff and front desk everyone was always eager to help in any way possible. The rooms are not huge but they are spacious enough. With a few pieces of furniture moved we had a king bed and roll-away bed and still could walk about. The rooms also feature microwave and fridge and that is great when traveling with kids. What's one downside? It has the standard hotel air conditioning that is a bit loud when it runs, especially when you can't get very far away from it. But it was not a big enough deal to stop me from staying there again- just not idea. And then there's the location: perfect. We never really had to take a cab once we were in town. If you can walk 10-15 minutes you can reach almost everything downtown Chicago has to offer: Navy Pier, Mag Mile, Hancock Center, etc. We have a 3 year old so fine dining was not in the cards but okay-dining was always within reach. The Weber Grill is in the hotel (we didn't eat there but it was always packed). And stocking up on supplies is also easy: nearby are Trader Joe's, Jewel (supermarket), Walgreen's and more - so you could get supplies at reasonable prices. Willl the Rizt Carlton be threatened by this hotel? No. But we would be hard-pressed to come up with a better option in the affordable hotel class. You get you money's worth in every way.

“New Building in Convenient Location.” I have stayed at this hotel several times in different kinds of rooms, along with other hotels in their brand in New York. For quiet, outstanding restuarant food (thank Chef Todd English) a lovely bar and lobby experience I like this hotel and lately tend to choose it over the others in their brand. Service is correct, fast and unobtrusive. Concierge service is top notch. The rooms are very new and modern but only a few lower floor rooms have a bathtub, and those tubs are nothing to rave about. The lack of bathtubs is perhaps my greatest disappointment about this hotel and that the gym is lame and also has no sauna or steam room which might help offset the lack of bathtubs. Though I greatly prefer a bathtub and good gym and spa, I tend to choose this hotel because it is quieter, newer and has a lovely lounge and some the best hotel food I have experienced should you need to eat in the hotel. If you want a massive gym, bathtubs and a louder lobby experience the Crowne Plaza Times Square also in their brand is a good choice. Both properties are very good, but this hotel I think is a touch better in doing what hotels should do well.

“Update on Hilton's amenities” Stayed at the Boston Hilton in late December and was very pleased. The location (nr to Prudential Center and easy access to Green Line and Orange Line T) is excellent. The hotel is modest in size (about 25 floors but limited rooms on each floor), but they now have a Diamond Lounge for breakfast on the ground level - too bad it is not also open all day for use. The rooms are pleasant, particularly if you snag a 'corner room' which is sized up. FYI - free internet is available in lobby, but very costly ($14.95) if used in one's room. Rooms have flat screen TVs with a good selection of cable channels. Management has made the main lobby more hospitable and it is easy to use if working or visiting. Will be nice when they finally drop the Internet fee for in-room use. Recommend for stay when interesting in having access to shopping parts of downtown Boston.

“Good hotel for tourists but not a business hotel” Booked this hotel online while on the last train of the night from Boston to the city. Since I'd be arriving later and leaving early I felt like I should stick to a low rate and this came up for quite a bargain. Anyway, this is a basic hotel, drab room, great location and packed with tourists. The lobby was mobbed in the morning for the breakfast buffet so I skipped that. This hotel doesn't really doesn't cater to the business traveler but that said it is a fine pick if I was coming to the city as a tourist on a budget and in need of basic accomodations.

“清潔感のあるホテル” 1泊のみ宿泊しました。宿泊したのは2ベッドルーム。部屋には1人がけのソファーと小さめのテーブル1つがありました。そんなに広くないので荷物を置くと狭く感じます。 シャワーは固定式で、必要最低限のアメニティーは揃っていました。 部屋もホテル内も清潔感があり、スタッフの方も親切なので安心して宿泊できます。 またホテルを出て、道を渡ったすぐ目の前にバーガーキングがあります。ホテル内にも1階にレストラン、売店がありました。

“Clean, quiet and convenient. What more can ya ask for?” I had stayed here before in 1983 & just for kicks inquired to see if was still around. Lo & behold, it was and was still a Holiday Inn. Checked around & was recommended in safe neighborhood, etc so I booked into it for 6 nights. Lots of plusses! Safe clean neighborhood with lots of eating establishments within easy walk and shopping 1 mile walk. With the hotel shuttle (2 mile radius) and the Georgetown bus ($1 fare) a person can get anywhere from this hotel easily. Easy shuttle ride to Foggy Bottom metrorail station and off ya go anywhere in DC. Furthermore, Grayline does a courteousy pickup from this hotel at 7:10 am for their tours. Staff is very friendly & answered every request with "not a problem" & delivered what was asked for promptly & politely. Room is clean, bright & quiet. Restaurant offers good food, great portion sizes & reasonable prices. Lunch & dinner cheaper than in Georgetown & about DC price. Breakfast buffet priced comparable to other Holiday Inns I've stayed at ($15, too much, but what can ya do?) And the gift shop is well stocked, open late & reasonably priced too. Very few negatives. They really should replace the main floor carpeting as it looks pretty soiled & worn in several spots. Also, Priority Club points for free nights here were pretty costly, but it is the height of tourist season in a touristy town. Lastly, 1 of the 2 computers in the biz center was out of order since 2nd night of 7 creating quite a backup. But all in all, was good value for the money. I mean, I was here to spend a lot of time sightseeing, not a lot of time lounging around the hotel, so it suited my budget fine.

“Great location and very nice hotel” We stayed one night using points. The locations is fantastic, blocks from Times Square and within walking distance of so much more. The room was small (as expected for NYC) but clean and comfortable. We did not visit the bar or use the pool but both looked nice. The hotel staff was fantastic, special mention to the concierge who let us borrow his iPhone charger. For the location, this is a perfect hotel.

“Déco lourde, chambres minuscules mais emplacement parfait” Franchement, ayant vécu à New York quelques années, je sais comme les chambres peuvent être minuscules dans les hotels new yorkais, mais bon, là, quand on n'a même pas la place par terre de poser et d'ouvrir sa valise... Quant au 'tout bleu', niveau déco, bof. On est dans un entre deux, on ne sait pas trop si ça se veux moderne, baroque, ultra contemporain, ou autre, ça se cherche, ça manque de personnalité, tout a l'air déjà vu avant. Le petit déjeuner qui revient à presque 40 dollars par person tip included : non, ce n'est pas possible. Remarquez, tant qu'à être dans un quartier sympa, on se dit du coup qu'on va petit dejeuner dehors.

“As Expected - Good Quality Hampton Inn.” I stay at this hotel two - three times per month for about two nights per stay, and keep coming back. Overall this Hampton Inn is at the top of its game. Breakfast and lobby area is nice, staff is always attentive, breakfast is typical Hampton (egg pucks, biscuts, sasuage, breads, pasteries, juice, coffee.) The rooms are always nice, crisp, and clean. The workout room is acceptable, though nothing special. Hector the manager is always willing to go above and beyond. The location is a centeral easy drive to most business activities in Austin and is located in a small business park area across from the Omni Hotel and next to a Homewood Suites. If you have a car, there is dining nearby, though without a car there is not much in walking distance other than the Omni. The outdoor pool is average, and they do not have a real business center, but do have a PC and printer in the lobby you can use as a business center. The only negative I have about the hotel - they tend to change my reservation from a King Non Smoking to a Double Bed Non Smoking at their will without notice. They always fix it as I am a Diamond Member, but at any rate, it seems to happen pretty frequently which leads me to think it is common practice. For its location in Austin, the price is reasonable compared to many other choices.

“Great Value and location, a little weary, in San Francisco” My husband and I have journeyed to San Francisco many many times over the years both for business (a yearly food show) and pleasure (family in the Bay Area) staying in a wide array of hotels up there. We were pleasantly surprised by the Donatello. I would stay here again. The only real con is that the furniture was older and could use a freshen up. Examples: The handle to a drawer came off as I tried to open it, the table was clearly worn down, there was a burn hole in the couch, overall the style of the furniture was dated, lots and lots of mirrors in the entry (good and bad, depending on from how many angles you want to view yourself). Pros: Friendly staff, some of the nicest I've encountered. Great location -close to all with plenty of good restaurants around and we could walk to the convention center (we like to walk but it is pretty close). The room is Large, especially by San Francisco standards which is more European in style. I think ours was about 400 sf. It had a couch, a nice desk, a good entry way, and a decent view (not a lot to look at, but nice space outside). We were on the 12th floor and faced South. If we were on the other side we would have been looking into the Marriott. There was a small workout room on the top floor with a sauna and whirlpool in the women's bathroom (assume the same for the men). There is also a lounge on that floor with an outside patio, nice chairs and tables, coffee and tea and such. This was a nice place to sit and get some light. A concierge was also up there and very pleasant. Note: I booked through Club Donatello (just by happenstance) so I am not positive if everyone gets use of this room, although I would think so. When I checked in and asked for a higher floor the man said that I booked through Club Donatello which starts on the 8th floor. They have a timeshare there, so that may be part of the timeshare. We had a very good time here and would consider staying here again. There are a lot of homeless in this area so you will be hit up when you go out. Just part of the scene there. We have been staying away from Union Square partially for that reason and there are hotels we like in other parts of the city. Despite the slightly funky furniture, we had a great time at the Donatello. The people there are proud of their hotel and you can feel it. It had an upbeat feel, I loved the larger room and the location proved very good for us this trip.

“Loved it -great Hotel.” My family and I stayed here for 4 nights at the end of July and beginning of August. Hotel was booked purely on comments on Trip Advisor. The hotel had done well even before we got there as I had been in constant email contact with them - we had 3 small children (one of whom needed a crib) and they managed to fit us all in the room - shows how big the rooms are. Arrived early afternoon and room wasnt ready - we were told to come back at 4 pm and they held our luggage. Turned up at 3pm and checked straight in. We used the elevators all the time as we had a pushchair but never had a problem - instead of using main elevators, use the ones at end of corridor - never had to wait. Room was great - loved having a fridge. Air con was fine. We overlooked the road and didnt have any problem with noise. Loads of places to eat nearby - Empire and Galaxy Diners good for breakfast - fantastic Hard Rock Cafe on Times Square for dinner that was walkable. Paid $160 per night for room through hotel web site. Good value. Loved everything about this hotel.

“Wonderful Location for New York City!” We stayed here for 2 nights on one of the Hilton Honors promotions. We got a fantastic rate for 2 nights but had to agree to participate in their sales presentation for an hour. The hotel itself was very well done and our room was comfortable and well detailed. Everything is sleek and modern there and it offers what today's travelers are looking for. The staff were all friendly and customer service oriented.
