The gym was small but had all the equipment you need to get a good work out in. The location of the hotel is the best. You are next to Carnegie Hall and Central Park and all the wonderful shopping and restaurants that New York is famous for. As far as the sales presentation, it is "not your Daddy's timeshare" and the timeshare world has changed a lot since we last sat in on one of these presentations. We didn't buy, but it does appear to be a good value.

“Disappointed in this Westin” I love Westin properties so I was really disappointed after staying at this one. Let's start with the advantages - the location couldn't be beat. It was within short walking distance of fabulous shopping and restaurants. The restaurant downstairs was very good and had a great bar. The lobby was nice and customer service was prompt. The beds were the typical comfortable heavenly beds. The rooms were run down and in need of updating. I was in a room on the 6th floor and the caulking in the bathroom was moldy and the first time I used the shower it was clogged so bad that the water was up to my ankles by the time I got out of the shower. I called the front desk and they had maintenance fix the drain that day and gave me 500 rewards points for the hassle. I used the tea each day I stayed there and the tea and the mini-bar water was not replenished when my room was cleaned each day. There was also a hair on my pillow and one on my towel - housecleaning needs to be improved. I stayed at this hotel for three nights and the first two nights I went to bed around 11:30 and it sounded like there was a party going on in the hallway. The walls seemed very thin or something because every time a door slammed you could hear it. The second morning I got up and there was a package of crackers strewn across the hallway right outside my door. I think because of how inexpensive this hotel is compared to others in the area, they get a shady crowd of people staying here. It wasn't your typical business group, even though I stayed during the week. The last night my friend, who was in a room next to mine, saw a group of four men and one woman check into the room next to her with a few ice buckets and beer. When I came up to go to bed around 11 pm, the floor reeked of marijuana and there was loud music. I asked to be moved because between that and the party still going on across the hallway, I didn't feel safe in my room. They were apologetic and promptly moved me to the 15th floor, but it was an inconvenience and the room on the 15th floor was much smaller. I will add that my view in both rooms was non-existant as I looked into another building from both rooms. Bottom line - if you're looking for a good deal, try this Westin, otherwise I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

“They have got it Right” We moved from another hotel that really got it wrong. This was a terrific experience. Firstly, the smallest room in the hotel is 450 sq ft. which is amazing for NYC. The service is first class. The restaurant excellent. They are doing everything right! (Except this ridiculous daily charge for the internet which all hotels are doing for some stupid reason - if you ask they will remove it) The rooms are beautiful. The suites on the top floors are panoramic and in SoHo you can still get amazing views without being blocked by tall buildings. I would happily stay here again. I understand it is an Ivanka project, doesn't surprise me. She is a pretty impressive lady.

“A HUGE HOTEL” I recently stayed at this hotel for a week on business. This hotel is very huge and can be confusing with all the elevators and the business center being connected to it. If you are ederly and DO NOT like to do a lot of walking this is not the hotel for you. Front desk staff gave me a room with a wonderful view of Windsor, Ontario and the Detroit River. I was in awe my entire stay that I could see another country from my hotel room. The room was very spacious and clean. All of the front desk, concierge and bar staff were very helpful with my request. Nice fitness center too with lots of equitment. I also liked the fact that the hotel was right next to the Detroit/Windsor tunnel. This made it easy for me to hop on the bus to go to Canada. Remember to have your passport folks!! Also, note this hotel is in a great location of downtown Detroit everything close by. My only complaint is/was the hotel can feel like a maze.

“Fabulous stay!” We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Kyoto Grand. Thanks to the Trip Advisor community, we checked in with a list of our preferences: updated room, highest possible floor, city view. The Kyoto Grand was able to meet these requests cheerfully, and our room looked exactly like the photos on the website. The room was stocked with quality bathroom products (soaps, shampoos, conditioners, lotions). Housekeeping efficiently brought up toothpaste when requested (we ran out!). Found out (too late!) that there was a fridge in the room (check out the area under the TV!) Used the treadmill in the fitness room both nights of our stay. Basic machine, but entirely functional and well-maintained. We didn't utilitze hotel parking; parked at Joe's directly across the street for significant savings. Used the guest shuttle once; the driver couldn't have been nicer and more gracious ~ excellent! Loved the expansive dining options in Little Tokyo ~ literally a block or so away. Sushi choices abound! Really, truly loved our stay at the Kyoto Grand ~ a solid choice when travelling to downtown Los Angeles.

“Independent Buildings” This was my first stay at a Residence Inn and I was unfamiliar with the properties layout. There are multiple buildings on the grounds containing the rooms. Therefore your hotel room is not connected to the lobby/front desk. You have to go outside to reach the lobby and continental breakfast area. Overall the property was very nice. Nice pool area and very good cont. breakfast. There is no wireless internet in the rooms you have to plug in. We had one laptop that was not compatible and one that was. There are no vending machines on each floor only on the 2nd floor. We ordered more towels and they were delivered immediately. We had a two bedroom suite and it was very nice. There are fast food restaurants north of the hotel a couple exits but the good Mexican food is in Old Town San Diego.

“Just another Holiday Inn......” Well, this is really just another Holiday Inn. Public areas were not fancy but acceptable for a hotel this class, service was just OK, the rooms were kinda dated but comfortable and clean enough. The restaurant did serve a pretty decent breakfast with some really good pastries. Location wise, it's a few blocks away from the nearest "T" Station so there's quite a bit of walking involved.

“Clean, Comfortable, Good Location and Outdated” I booked here on a last minute business trip and landed a rate at just over $220 a night which is a great rate during the holiday season here in NYC. For comparison purposes other Times Square area hotels are in the $350-400/night range (Marriott, Sheraton, Hilton, etc.). There is construction next door where a new building is going up. My 1st room was 427 and on the side of the building where the construction is. Construction was on-going when I checked in and the jack-hammering was intense. I went downstairs and talked to Natalie about another room. She promptly moved me from a standard to a deluxe King bedroom without hesitation. The standard room was tight, but adequate. The deluxe King was more spacious relatively speaking. If you're used to Court Yard, Marriott, Hilton, etc. sized rooms you'll be disappointed, but remember they are 2 times the $$. The rooms, halls, stairs, windows, and air conditioners are all outdated. The wallpaper is dark, the carpet is worn in the halls, the lighting is dim, and the furniture is worn. The windows don't seal tight to keep noise out. It wouldn't matter anyways because the air-conditioning is an in-window type which means one of the windows is halfway open to accommodate the unit and the noise comes right in. (Hint: turn on the AC to Fan only and create some white-noise to block out the city if you need to) Just because it is a bit dark and worn doesn't mean that it is dirty. The place is clean, the rooms are comfortable, the bathroom is clean, has good water pressure and plenty of hot water. The iron works, the hair dryer works, the TV is fine and the bed is comfortable. Net-Net: Its a great little place for the price and location as long as you're not planning to spend a lot of time in your room.

“Superb staff & service; room, not so much” Hubby and I stayed at this property in 2007, when everything felt just right about it. This time around, it's still go a lot going for it (the woman at the front desk... Marilyn?... is terrific and the hotel staff were helpful), the room itself is in need of attention. The rooms are among the largest I've found in this chain, which is always nice. But the woodwork shows the worse for wear, there was a large smudge of some kind on the bathroom wall that felt kind of creepy, the bed was quite hard, there were burned out light bulbs, and the A/C sounds like small aircraft when it kicks into gear. The manager's reception is minimal but no limits on drinks. The breakfast omelette landed badly in hubby's stomach (the same happened to me and my sister at other properties so I've taken to skipping them). The atrium is a gem: as far as we could tell, all the plants are real and there are a lot of them, along with running water from a fountain. So it's a mix of great, good, and needs improvement.

“Very good hotel, great beds but watch out for the extra cost of parking” Very good hotel. The other reviews prior to this review are accurate both the good and the bad comments. I paid $78 for a standard double bed. The bedding was wonderfully fluffy with just the right amount of back support. The decor was also nice for the price. The room was very large. Everything from the shampoo to the coffee was upscale. There is a Starbucks in the hotel plus several nice restaurants. If you can get a room facing the pond, then you will get a nice nightime view of the business parks in the area. This hotel looks like its website photos. My room was a very clean, but a bit ragged. The chair had tears, the lamp had large splattered stains, and the corner lap did not work. The bathroom was a plain bathroom. The beds were full size, not queen size so 2 people per bed would be a tight fit. This is what I wish I had known before I booked this hotel to improve my stay: First, the parking to this hotel is far from the entrance. Across a small street is garage parking. The cost is $10 flat fee for unlimited parking. Save all your tickets so that you can turn them in at the end of your stay. For a one night stay, it would have been better for me to park in the free parking lot on the side and back of the building and haul my luggage inside. The valets were young and enthusiastic. If I were less able or not been on a tight budget, I certainly would have used their help. Second, the room was rather worn, like at a much lower quality hotel. I would not have expected more. Third, I would have tried to negotiate a lower price from the hotel before booking it on line. They had lots of avalable space during my stay. The previous 3 nights I had stayed at the Fairfield in across the highway which to me had equally good beds, free breakfast, indoor pool, a workout room and nice staff. On this night the Fairfield Inn was charging $99 per night so I thought "$78 at the Hilton has got to be better". It was not. I did not have a bad stay, but it was not all that I expected. Maybe staying on the higher floors (we were on the 6th floor) would have given us better quality and having a higher budget for tips would have given us better service. As someone passing through, I did not want to pay for Internet service, so I used my phone as a modem which was slow. There is a Business Center in the hotel but it was so far away, I was too tired to make the trip. Finally, I wish that I had known that this hotel is part of a complex of buildings that are linked together making this hotel a city all its own. The entrance is breathtaking. Travel in jeans and a t-shirt, I felt completely out of place-- until nighttime when I saw other people in jeans and regular shirts practicing their music in the lobby and kids playing in the outdoor pool. Many people wore business attire because they were coming and going from work whereas my work had ended. While I would definately stay in this hotel again only if I had a great rate. This hotel was like a taste of Texas for visitors to the state and I recommend it for visitors to the state, to Dallas, or for anyone wanting a good bed only if they get a great rate or they pay more for a better room and have a good budget. Trip Advisor customer reviews has been great in helping me pick good hotels for several years, and I hope this review helps others in their decision making process.

“A so-so, worn-out Ritz” I stayed at the Ritz for a business trip and left quite underwhelmed. The lobby is beautiful, the service was great, but the room itself was disappointing and in need of a makeover. The furniture was worn and starting to look a bit beaten up, the towels were thin and worn, the bathroom showed signs of rust in various places, the bathtub's coating was peeling in several spots, the TV was old and didn't work very well, and the room service food was nothing special. I expected much, much more from a Ritz property.

“Believe the Reviews!” We always stay here at the Alexander Inn when visiting Philadelphia several times a year , but it's been several years since my last review of the property. As we just got back from a weekend visit to catch the Van Gogh Exhibit at the Philadelphia Museum of Art (Go see it!), I am pleased to report that the Alexander Inn CONTINUES to impress. As other posters say, location, location, location. But that would mean nothing if the rooms weren't in terrific shape, and they are! This boutique hotel is the BEST. We believe the rooms are a good value! But truly, the Alexander Inn has the BEST STAFF around. Can't wait for our next visit.

“"So Sold Out" they don't need to care about guests' requests (or reviews!)” It's a shame the management staff at this property and at Hilton Corporate failed, because the hotel would rank average or above average were it not for service deficiencies from managment. Larger-than-average rooms, a standard continental breakfast, ample parking, and gracious front-line staff made my stay here worthwhile. Some aircraft noise from the nearby military base, but it's San Diego - good luck NOT hearing military aircraft! My issue arose when I discovered my work colleague had booked a double-double and I, a king-bedded room ... with our rate varying by $10. When I asked for a minor variance on rate, so we could bill identical hotel charges to our client, the kind desk staff referred me to the GM. I know she was the General Manager not just by her namebadge, but by her clear need to announce her title to me. She promptly corrected my adjective, ensuring I now know that a $10 variance in rate is not "minor." She then declined my request. I felt this was unacceptable, to which her fallback position was to raise my colleague's rate by $5 and lower mine by $5. I was then lectured on how "incredibly busy and sold out" the hotel was. My response was (an admittedly toothless) threat to check out, given that her hotel is "so busy" she could re-sell my room to another guest at a higher rate. She seemed perfectly content if I were to have elected that option. The feedback I left with Hilton Worldwide was met with an auto-response e-mail about how important my business is and a promise to get back in touch ... but I haven't heard anything. I average about 100 room nights a year. Through the actions of their GM at Hampton Kearney Mesa, and lax response from Guest Relations at Corporate, Hilton's given me nice cause to cut up my HHonors Elite-level card and shift my business to another, more gracious operator.

“Acceptable, but nothing to rave about” Convenient to IH-35 northbound, but if southbound, or coming from Mockinbird, you have to go IH-35 southbound to Commonwealth and U-turn under IH-35 on the service road to get to the hotel. I was on 6th floor and wanted something to drink from the vending machine, but the dollar bill accepter wasn't working - nor were the vending machines on 5th floor, 4th floor, or 3rd floor. I finally went to the desk after the 3rd floor vending machine took my first dollar, but not my second dollar, and then wouldn't return my first dollar. I asked the desk for change for a $20 and told them of the machine problems. I got $19 and 4 quarters. Uhh... cokes are $1.50 - four quarters won't cut it. I cut my losses and went to a grocery store and got some stuff to drink during my two-day stay. The hotel needs updating/renovation in the worst way. The look is very dark and drab. The elevators definitely have a moldy odor to them, which is occasionally mitigated by a good spray of Febreeze during the daily cleaning rounds. The rooms are very poorly lit. My room has two full-sized beds and is illuminted by one desk lamp, and two tablelamps, for a total of four of those new flouroescent bulbs. One end of the room remains depressingly dark, even with all lights on. The room is full enough with a TV/dresser, work desk, nightstand, and two beds, but then they add two sitting chairs and a table between them - and the room is just claustrophobically cramped. Housekeeping service can use some emphasis on attention to detail - when restocking my in-room coffee, I was left with one coffee amenity pack, instead of the usual two. Not a major, until I went for my 2nd cup of coffee this morning. The neighborhood around Mockingbird/IH-35 isn't the nicest part of town to be sure, so the parking lot security is a nice touch. You know it's a bad neighborhood when the hotel has blocked all but once of the vehicle entry points to the property. I'd definitely not leave anything worth over $10 in view in my vehicle here. All in all, not a bad place to stay if you got a good deal from Priceline or Hotwire (as I did), but if I'd paid the hotel's full rate, I'd be very, very dissatisfied.

“Much nicer than the usual Doubletree!” Stayed for a long weekend with teenage daughter and her friends. Used Hilton points, but haven't stayed in a Doubletree for a long time, so I was very surprised to enter a trendy-feeling contemporary lobby, with very friendly staff, and the girls loved the warm cookies. We had booked a double bedded suite, with two double beds plus a sofabed, and as a Hilton elite member we were upgraded a city view suite. The suite wasn't huge (maybe 450 sq ft) but very efficiently laid out, with very nice furnishings and a great view. The suite could easily sleep 6, so it was very comfortable for the 4 of us. We arrived late, so we decided on getting chinese food delivered, and the reception staff provided us with take-out menus from several places as well as recommendations. The food was excellent and very inexpensive, so having the fridge and microwave was very nice for leftovers. The bellman arranged a car service for our return trip to the airport; a very nice black SUV at the same price as a standard taxi. Would have like to stay there again on return trips in January and April, but prices were astronomical compared to other comparable properties. Would definitely stay again on points or if prices were more in line with Starwood and Kimpton properties.

“Inconsistent Quality” I travel to DC for professional meetings and the company frequently has us stay at the Mandarin Oriental. It is conveniently located near the Smithsonian, Metro stops, and a quick taxi ride form Reagan Airport. In general, this is a luxurious hotel with superb service, including very above average banquet food service. This last stay, however, I experienced a couple of problems worth noting. It was extremely difficult getting the water temperature regulated in the shower/bath, alternating between freezing cold and scalding hot (no in between) unpredictably but frequently. Difficult enough that it made all but the most rapid of showers impossible. No explanation. Usually this hotel attracts a pretty good clientele, but this trip we had excessive noise in the halls at 1-3 AM from adult guests (evidently drunk) shouting and carrying on like a high school prom night. Multiple calls to the front desk from several of my colleagues in rooms on the same floor failed to get the problem resolved. Uncharacteristic of what I have come to expect from several stays at this hotel, and totally unacceptable.

“Switched our room at check-in, safety concerns” I travel to New York at least once a month for business and pleasure. I have a lot of friends in the city, I attend charity events, and I go for work on occasion. Most of the time I stay at the W or Westin in Times Square. Due to the proximity of a dinner I had to attend with my husband on this occasion I chose the W New York instead. This property is much older than the ones in Times Square so the rooms are smaller. The decor was nice, having just finished extensive renovations. However, this is the first time I was downgraded from the room I paid for. I have been upgraded many times at Starwood properties but this was a first. When we checked in the desk clerk called someone about our room but didn't say anything to us. She handed us our room keys and I asked if this was the Mega room that I booked. She told us that yes it was the Mega room. I guess she didn't know that we stay at W's a lot and would notice if she gave us a smaller room. As soon as I walked in I knew it was the wrong room. We were late for our dinner (people were waiting in the lobby for us) so we decided to deal with it at check out. We were leaving the room when the phone rang, it was the desk clerk downstairs telling us she made a mistake and gave us the wrong room so she had upgraded us to a suite for our inconvenience. We were happy she had decided to own up to her mistake but we were really late at this point. I went alone to switch the room so my husband could meet up with our friends. The suite was a very small, handicap accessible room, with a terrible view and a tiny bed. Not at all what I wanted, when you sleep in a big bed, downsizing is not fun. The view in the smaller room was better, it had a king sized bed, and a bigger bathroom. At this point I could not take the time to argue and just accepted it but I didn't need the miniature living room since we only wanted to sleep in the room. The bigger bedroom is what I wanted and I am still upset with the tiny bedroom we got stuck with. After dinner we went to The Whiskey Bar with our friends. From dinner until the end of the evening I had a glass of wine and two drinks over an eight hour period. In addition to four glasses of water and an espresso. I had just ordered a water and taken a couple drinks from it when I went to the bathroom. I was feeling fine, not at all tipsy until I reached the bathroom. I collapsed in the stall, I could not see or hear correctly and my legs would not hold my weight. After about an hour I was able to make it back downstairs, meet up with my husband (who, along with my friends had been frantically searching for me) and made it to my room where I passed out. I had a terrible headache the entire next day. The only conclusion we could come to was that someone slipped something in my water, probably at the bar where the wait staff picks up the drinks. I have never had anything like this happen to me before although I've heard of travelers being robbed and assaulted this way. Just be aware, the crowd in this bar is not the type of people I socialize with, it is very small and crowded; I think this may make it less safe than the ones at the other W's and Westins downtown.

“Great location, charming hotel, comfortable rooms!” Stayed here in the 2nd part of trip to always fabulous NYC. This property was a priceline bid winning, and I wish I could win it again everytime I bid for NY hotels! We had already stayed at 44th st and loved the location. The hotel common areas are charming, classic, with great memorabilia from the Dorothy Parker times... and free wi-fi, what unfortunately they do not offer in the rooms. Our room was very nice, clean and comfortable, with fine decor, regular size and good bathroom and shower. A convenient plus for us was the two daily complimentary water bottles. We had no view, though, and that was a minus. The staff was professional and since we only needed them to check in and out, I could not evaluate that very well. Loved Matilda at the lobby!

“Cold room, old TV” The room thermostat only went up to 75, which kept the room at 74, which sounds fine but it was a cold week in Houston and the large windows cooled the room down. I was always cold. The front desk could not send up a portable heater but offered to send maintenance up to the room (why?). There were hairs in the bathtub, sink and on the floor for all four days of my stay. The TV was old, with poor reception. Expensive valet parking.

“Great location, excellent, friendly staff” We stayed here for 2 nights for a wedding. We had a great room and it was clean and comfortable. We were welcomed at the front desk by a very friendly guest representative. We had another room reserved for the 2nd night and she made sure it was close to us. The wedding was at the Four Seasons which was a block away. It was convenient for us to walk over there. We had plenty of places to eat nearby. There is a Whole Foods very close which was convenient. This is a very well maintained and well staffed hotel. I would not hesitate to stay here in the future.

“Not my favorite Kimpton, but not bad either” This has been my least favorite Kimpton hotel. The service was great and very friendly. The location was good. The noise level was very good in that we did not hear a lot of the door slamming and talking in most hotels. I just did not care for the overall style of the hotel. Just appeared dated and bordered on tacky. Fixtures looked weathered as if they have been untouched for years. I like their other more modern hotels like Ink 48 and Eventi in New York. There is such a thing as too much for room decor. I am sure others will find it charming, just not our cup of tea.

“a due passi da Times Square” consiglio per la sua ottima posizione : a 5 minuti da Times Square senza stare in mezzo alla confusione di Times Square. Si puo girare tutta la parte alta di Manhattan a piedi (dalla 30° fino a Central Park). Per essere nel cuore di Manhattan rapporto qualità / prezzo più che onesto (camera spaziose per NY) : ho avuto la fortuna di avere una camera in un piano alto con vista stupenda sulla Hudson river. C'è anche unbel fitness center (visitato ma non utlizzato). punto d'attenzione : pulizia delle camere approssimative.

“beautiful hotel close to everything” I spent 8 nights here recently, this hotel is very very nice, very spacious, the staff is very courteous and friendly. The Hotel itself is very nice, not overly modern, not overly classic, just a very straight forward hotel. The room was very spacious and comfortable with a huge bathroom and awesome shower. Very close to tons of restaurants on 8th and obviously, times square is right around the corner. Overall I was very pleased with this hotel and would stay there gladly for a trip to NYC.

“The Worst Snobbery” We are Omni Select members and usually prefer this chain in other cities over others for attention to details and welcome kids program. This time in Boston they ran out of suites and we decided not to stay there (although less expensive but smaller rooms were widely available at the hotel). Accustom to typical good service standards at other Omni hotels, I stopped by a concierge desk to ask about a nearest ice cream place. At other cities, the staff of this hotel group is extremely professional and helpful but not in Boston. The concierge gave us an address of a closest place - 131 Tremont Street. The sign on this building says - Boston Visitors Center... Never expected this from an Omni employee. Despite our Planitum level, we'll have to leave the program. Totally unacceptable!

“Kudos All Around” My wife and I missed our connecting flight in Memphis. We had been on an airplane for 19 hours straight and were dead on our feet. The airline wanted to put us and the other 200-300 people on our plane up at the same hotel. There had been lines to see our passports, lines to get our luggage, lines to get through the customs, lines to have bags checked, lines to have luggage rechecked. No there were lines for hotel and food vouchers, lines to get the hotel shuttle, and (I am certain) lines for the restaurant. We decided to skip the lines we could and to stay at the Peabody. We caught a cab (no line) and went straight to the hotel without any reservation. It was late. The bellman greeted us and took our bags and inquired about our stay. We told him why we were there. He took us to the front desk (no line) and told the clerk our situation. She upgraded us to a Club Level room without charge. We were given a free breakfast and drinks. We even got two free shoe shines. The restaurant stayed open late for us. We had extra towels and wash cloths in the room (without having to ask). They called to get us up in time for our flight out the next day. The bellman loaded our luggage in the taxi while we checked out. When I got home there was a thank you note in my email and a survey. I responded to the survey and my comments were acknoledged in another email. Now that is what I call service. Yes, we paid for it, $240 for overnight, but they really seemed to have gone out of their way for us and it was worth every penny.

“Lovely Well Run Hotel” My mom and I stayed here for two nights for a girl's weekend in the city. The hotel is spotlessly clean and the service was very professional and friendly. The location of the Monaco is perfect for just about anything you could want or need to do in the downtown area and the Valets are very helpful with assisting you in getting around. The room was very spacious with super high ceilings that gave you an airy feeling. Our room was located next to the elevator which we did hear "dinging" late at night and in the morning. We didn't care enough to ask to be moved but if you need quiet I would recommend not accepting a room close to the elevators. The sheets on the beds were absolute heaven! As nice as mine at home, which I miss at hotels. Although the mattresses were comfortable they were slightly worn. We ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant and it was delicious. All in all it was a lovely stay and perfect for a relaxing weekend.

“HIGH LEVEL & RELAX !!!” Je voyage souvent à New-York, et parfois j'aime découvrir un nouvel hotel. J'ai choisi le Gansevoort pour son design et sa piscine sur le toit. Prestations de tres haute qualité, les chambres standard sont superbes et parfaitement équipées, trés calmes. Le petit dej est un buffet à volonté trés frais que l'on prend en haut au lounge ou en terrasse (c'est juste un rêve juste avant de démarrer ses RDV !!). La piscine est une pure merveille. Le personnel est remarquable: accueil, étage, housekeeping, bar... on s'y sent chez soi. L'emplacement n'est pas super glamour (je préfère de loin Soho), mais vous êtes à proximité de tout à pied ou en metro ou en taxi. (Soho 10 mn à pied).

“Perfect choice for downtown LA.” We staid at this JW for 4 nights in March of 2012. It a newer property that is part of the LA live complex. Our check in was easy and the staff was very nice. Our room was on the 21st floor facing the city. The other people were with with were also on the 21st floor but facing the Nokia Theater. We had a king size room that was very spacious. One of the things we really appreciated was in addition to all the space there were plenty of places to unpack. The bathroom was also very large. The room had a modern feel as did the rest of the hotel. This hotel is great if you are going to LA live or the downtown area. It was also pretty easy to get to Universal and Warner Brothers studios. But getting to parts of Hollywood, Beverly Hills and Santa Monica was a mission. Especially with LA traffic. The hotel lobby is big, modern and great. They have an Illy espresso bar, a wine bar and a place for breakfast. If you prefer Starbucks there's one right next to the hotel in the LA live complex. I will say that the complex was very busy the entire time were there with an NCAA basketball tournament, a Lakers Game, a Clippers Game and the premier of the Hunger Games. It was exciting but there were a lot of people in and around the hotel lobby at all times. We did have dinner at WP 24 which is at the Ritz Carlton next door. You can actually get to the Ritz through the JW lobby which is nice when it's very busy outside. WP 24 is fantastic and worth the money.

“Good Stay at This Hotel” This hotel is located downtown on Sherman Road. It is only three blocks to the 16th Street Mall, this mall has a free shuttle that stops at each block along the mall route. The room was nice and clean. The closet was nice and you had plenty of room to store your clothes. The front desk was efficient and helpful with directions and recommendations. If you are coming for Sports Games, Coors Field/Pepsi Center are virtually next to each other, walk down to the 16th Street Mall and take the free shuttle to the end of the line, then you walk two blocks over and your at the arena/stadium.

“Better than average convention hotel.” My wife and I stayed at this huge convention hotel for two nights at the beginning of a wonderful trip to New England and Upstate New York. The front desk staff was very helpful and the late check-in (23 pm.) was really fast, what we really thanked, as we were tired from the flight. Our room was big, silent and had a very comfortable bed. Even that it is a very big hotel, the service is perfect and it has a perfect location with a lot of restaurants nearby. It also has a sports bar called Champions that is real fun. All in all, as we had a very good internet offer, staying at this hotel was a anice start for a great vacation.

“dated average stay” NIcely furnished dated hotel. Could hear people in next room on phone, noise from events was loud. Food was average. Bed was comfortable, bathroom really tiny. The hot water took about 5 minutes to come to the room and there was no counter space around the sink. Lack of power outlets meant I had to switch between charging my phone and computer.

“What a dump” I stayed at the WP for a conference. Based on my experience, avoid this hotel if you can. I was placed in a room next to the elevator, and like past reviewers, I heard a clanging noise at all hours. The room features shabby decor and sparse ammenities. I had to wait in line to check in for over 20 minutes, leaving my belongings with a bellhop (scary). Don't stay here.

“renovation time” A huge marble lobby which only makes the hotel appear empty. Decent check in staff. Room was a decent size but SOOOO run down. chipped bathroom tiles, dodgy shower arrangement, and a ac unit that gave the option of sweat or not sleep. It is convenient for the airport but dont believe the concierge staff over times to get around LA. The resturant needs to get jumping. expensive and overly laid back

“Clean, comfortable and outdated” I had to book a last minute trip to NYC and found the Wellington available for $199 a night (about $220 after taxes, etc.) on Bookit.com. Given the location and mid-week timing for a stay in NYC last minute that's a good deal. The staff at check-in was accommodating and gave me a quiet room on a high floor away from the noise of the Avenue and elevators. The room was in the back of the hotel which required going to an elevator which is up/down several stairs and corridors and could be a problem if you had several bags. The main elevator for the front set of rooms is not as difficult to get to. The room itself was reasonable in size particularly for anyone with European standards and had 2 closets. It was a bit out dated, but clean and comfortable. All in all not a bad experience for the price and location.

“Very Comfortable, Solid Hotel” This is the second time I've stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Downtown DC. It is hard to fault the place. The staff is very prompt, friendly, and attentive. My room was large and had a king bed and a chair-and-a-half and and ottoman. The bathroom was spotless, and I am pretty picky. The lighting was good, too. The only downer was the water pressure -- not great. My view was of absolutely nothing -- other hotel room windows on three sides. What that meant was there was no street noise so I had a quiet night. The last time I was there I had a street-facing room and heard lots of pre-dawn noise. The breakfast was good with a made to order egg station. It was pricey, but convenient. If I had more time I would have found a local breakfast joint instead of paying $16 for a buffet I didn't need. All and all this is a very clean, comfortable, convenient choice near K street in DC.

“The Drake reminds us that a great hotel is much more than a building with great rooms” After experiencing many Chicago hotels, almost all rated more highly on tripadvisor than the Drake (Sofitel, all the Westins, Sheratons, Ws, Hampton, Sax and many more). Starting with the minimum criterion of a good room which matters when I travel with some or all of my kids: the family room (one king bed/one sofa bed) is absolutely lovely: spacious, great bedding, great sofa -with all the needed sheets/blankets/pillows-, five large windows on the street spectacle and even a sliver of lake Michigan, wonderful curtains to actually block off the light of early morning, great bathroom. Now, here is the special part: first it has taken me years to make my way to the Drake (because of relatively poor tripadvisor ratings!!) eventhough I've wanted to try the high tea at the Palm court , to experience proximity to the beach and to stay in this landmark hotel with a wealth of history) and....we are here not a moment too soon. It is the anticipation of needs which sets the Drake way above the other hotels I have mentioned: at check in, all around the room, when changing any aspects of reservation, enquiring about anything: the employees appear to have a level of skill that is noticeably better than the employees (even well meaning ones) at other hotels. This will be where we try to stay when in Chicago from now on.
“great hotel, awesome location!!!” this is a beautiful hotel. it is centrally located and the service is great and the room is clean.
“Decent Stay” The hotel was convenient and comfortable. Rooms were a bit dated, but not an issue. Staff was really friendly and helpful.

“Mixed Review” We have stayed in a number of Residence Inns. This one is older and has separate entries from outside, with many exterior stairways. The Good: 1. As with all Residence Inns, staff was exceptional and breakfast selection very good. 2. Shuttle to downtown and area attractions is excellent. 3. We had townhouse style room with queen loft up, murphy bed downstairs and 2 baths -- more room than most Residence Inns, plenty of closets and bureaus for long stay, dining area, living area, kitchen with counter seating. 4. Room was clean, furniture and carpet looked fairly new, bed was comfortable. 5. Free internet access. 6. Good value for the money (we had special deal, $119 for townhouse). The Bad: 1. Bldgs are old, and outside is in great need of upgrade -- there is peeling paint, wooden stairways are worn and have nails popping up, wood trim is clearly rotten in many places. Outside appearance is so dilapidated that when we first drove up our daughter wanted to us to look for another hotel. More barren than newer Residence Inns, with little by way of landscaping or open space, even pool area did not was just surrounded by concrete. 2. We had room with outside wall. Right above bedrm window (on outside) was floodlight that bathed room in light even when blackout curtain was closed (which at least should have been larger to help block light). 3. Only bath items provided were soap and shampoo (and not enough shampoo for 3 of us). Considering price, this is no big deal if you know to pack these items. 4.Was very hot went we stayed (90+), and was difficult to keep upstairs and downstairs at reasonable temps. Upstairs was always much warmer, in order for the upstairs to be comfortable, the downstairs had to be freezing. In more moderate weather, this may not be such a problem. 5. Nothing in neighborhood. Really need to drive or take shuttle to dine, shop, sightsee, etc. 6. As mentioned in another review, there is no elevator. We stayed in townhouse style room, which started on 2nd floor, and loft bedroom was on 3rd floor. We had to lug very heavy luggage up 2 flights of stairs. Unlike other reviewer we did not find the supper selection any better than the other Residence Inns we've stayed at. It is a great option though if you have had busy day and do not want to get into your car to drive to restaurant. All in all, altho we enjoyed our stay, we'd probably stay somewhere else if we came to Denver again (new high rise Residence Inn is under construction in downtown).

“Great Place!” My sister came into the city and stayed here while visiting. Very impressive! And very stylish! The room was fairly large and had a wonderful plush bed. Accents in the room were beautiful and clean. It was a bit scant of light, but if you go all day, you want to just come back and relax. If you want to work on business papers, well, you may need a couple of extra bulbs. Nice roomy bath area and excellent bath products. The TV seemed to have quite an array of channels and movie offerings. I would have given this a higher rating had they not had the Skyview Lounge on the 26th floor closed. I wonder if this was disclosed when booking a room. That was one of the reasons she had selected this place to stay.

“Standard Hilton hotel” We stayed her on personal travel in November. It was unseasonably cold for that time of year so any walk seemed farther than it really was. Convenient to Newbury, the Common, Back Bay and the shopping centers. Hotel was clean, pool was on the small side and as with most Hiltons, slightly over chlorinated. We kept running in to the housekeeper no matter where in the hotel we were, and she was always polite and asking if we needed any amenities. The only drawbacks to the property are the wait times at the elevator and lack of a close T stop if you have more than a wheeled suitcase it will be a haul. I would recommend this hotel as clean and comfortable.

“SUper location, walking distance to shopping and restaurants” Room was comfy, two double beds, but no slippers. Great bar/restaurant inside hotel for late lunch. They triple charged internet because of three devices, but then took two off when we checked the bill. All ok.

“Excellent Location and Nice Hotel in Downtown Chicago” Recently stayed at this hotel for business travel. They had my room ready upon arrival in mid-afternoon, the room was very spacious, bed was very comfortable and the entire hotel was very clean. The staff was very friendly and attentive to all of my requests. If you are looking for a clean, reasonably priced, good hotel that has an indoor pool and hot tub I would highly recommend this hotel on your next visit to Chicago.

“Nice Hotel/Good Location/Walk to Sites” Solid Sheraton Hotel in very good location downtown. Took just about 10 minutes to walk to teh white house... about the same if walked right down to the national mall... enough places to eat on K street close to hotel... some more high end nightlife a few blocks down on K but fore more serious bar hopping take a quick cab to Adams Morgan or Dupont... Parking $35 stinks, but downtown DC price is high pretty much everywhere... there is a public garage about a block down 12th which is another option, probably a bit less, but not sure.

“Really Nice Place to Stay” Stayed here for a week while in Dallas area. Hotel was very clean and staff was very professional. The housekeeping service was very good and kept my room clean and very comfortable. The club lounge was very comfortable and breaksfast / evening snacks were well presented and tasty. Parking at times can be a bit of a strain but it was free and not really enough to complain about. My wireless internet seemed to slow down in the evenings. I had a room facing the highway and even with that, the highway noise wasnt as loud as I thought it would have been. Overall, i would stay here again in a flash without hesitation.

“Quiet hotel in Embarcadero” An actually quiet hotel in Embarcadero at the edge of Financial District. I saw a lot of reviews about the small room size but I've seen smaller rooms on other boutique hotels. Great service, nice complimentary car to downtown. Just across from Rincon center sogood dim sum (Yank Sing) is within walking distance. Just 1 block from Ferry Building so gourmet food is just 5 minutes walk away. Close to BART and F-line streetcar - no problem with public transit whatsoever. I did not book the bayview room but seriously - all you have to do is step through the lounge backdoor and you'll get the same view. Also I spent most of my time out of the hotel - so paying extra $30 per night did not really work for me. Overall - great stay experience.

“nice hotel but DONT EAT THERE” I arrived late about 10pm and had a cheeseburger at the bar. By 8am I was sick and vomiting. After vomiting all morning I began to feel better but wasted a whole day recovering from food poisoning. By the way I am an infectious diseases doc and I didnt appreciate the manager doubting my diagnosis, I probably can manage a hotel better that they can play doctor. Defensive posturing was not the best way to make it up to me.

“Espaçoso para famílias grandes” Um hotel sem serviço, apenas limpeza de quarto - como um flat / apart-hotel no Brasil. Não considero um 4*, e sim um bom 3*. Localização boa, e quarto bem espaçoso. Serviço foi desatencioso, quarto não estava pronto quando chegamos para check-in.

“History served up with great service” This was my first stay at the Willard Hotel in Washington DC. It is said that this is where the term "lobbyist" began when people seeking to influence government would hang out in the "lobby". A plaque outside commemorates the hotel as the site of a pre-Civil War meeting hoping to resolve North and South differences before shots were fired. A. (I won't use real names) at the front desk was exceptionally helpful not only during my check-in but during my entire brief stay. K. was another exceptional employee I encountered several times and who was always helpful and courteous. The room had sufficient space, actually larger than I expected by Washington DC standards. (I believe it was called a "King Deluxe".) It was very clean and functional in every way. The restaurant was outstanding! Pricey, but very good, with excellent service. We also had one dinner at Occidental Grill which is adjoining and somehow related to the Willard Group--outstanding with great service. Pricey too. Maybe it is better for couples than tourist families. The White House is a very short stroll from the Willard. However, this neighorhood is not vibrant at night. You might want to consider Dupont Circle or Penn Quarter areas, as examples, even though both are a short taxi ride from the Willard. The Willard - a great property with historical significance.

“Great Location” I travel to New York several times a year and for the past several trips have stayed at the Grand Hyatt on 42nd Street. The overall location is incredible. Adjacent to Grand Central Station, most desitnations are typically only minutes away. Within walking distance of Times Square, 5th Avenue Shopping and the NYC Library. Most rooms are nice, but don't expect big spacious rooms unless you book a suite. Some rooms are nicer than others, but all in all the hotel is really nice and very elegant. Security is tight so don't be surprised if you are approached by a "jacket" if you don't appear to have a purpose in the hotel.

“Different Kind of Courtyard...good option for Jacksonville.” Spent two nights here last week while in the Jacksonville area. Location: As the name indicates, this hotel is located on the Northeast side of Jacksonville. The surrounding area, while safe, seems a little on the bland side. There is a mall/shopping area nearby, but not much else. Oh yeah, the hotel shares a parking lot with a Walmart Supercenter...lots of interesting characters hanging out at all times. The majority of the parking for the hotel is located in the back. This would be fine, except they lock the rear entrance at certain times. So if you arrive to check in the evening, you have to park in the back, and drag your luggage all the way to the front door to check in. Since the back door is the main entrance for anyone arriving by car, they really should leave it unlocked for people checking in. Hotel/Rooms: Once you get past the awkward location/parking/door situation, it's actually a very nice place. Very modern lobby area and rooms. Outdoor pool in back of hotel always seemed to be busy. Nice fitness center. Room was clean, bed comfortable, everything worked as it should. Nice large flat screen TV. Lots of nice options in Jacksonville, but if you need to be on this side of town, this is a good choice.

“Great hotel and great location” Spent a few nights at the Affinia Shelburne during a recent visit to NYC. We had a nice one bedroom suite with a nice living area and good size bedroom. View out the window was of the Empire State Building. Everything was top notch and the room was very quiet. Neighborhood had a wide variety of great restaurants and was a short walk to the Theatre District or subway. We have had great luck with all of the Affinia hotels we have stayed in.

“Good quality for the price we paid” We stayed here for a couple of nights in late July, visiting San Antonio on business downtown. The family went to Fiesta Texas. This is a nice property, friendly helpful management. The pool and pool area are clean and well maintained. The breakfast is hot and plentiful. Good coffee too! Rooms were clean and beds were comfortable. AC worked well, but stayed on one speed all night long. My biggest complaint about this property is that it looks a bit worn. Wallpaper in the hallways is peeling, and the border at the bottom of the wall near the floor was missing all along the first floor. It also looks like room number markers were removed from the walls near the doors, and so it has that "scarred" look. It's the details that made up my mind on the ratings. Although we were very comfortable there, this hotel lacks the attention to details for the highest rating. The rates we paid were very good, and I would come back here again. This is a nice part of town, where you don't necessarily have to worry about the urban landscape.

“Excellent hotel, great staff, in the Times Square area” I stayed here for 2 nights on a business trip. Everything was excellent. The room was comfortable, clean and quiet. The bed was very soft and comfortable. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The in-room coffee was very good, although the coffee machine was hidden under the desk and it took a few minutes to learn how to work the machine. They should put a little instruction sheet or card on the coffee/tea machine so that people know how to use it. I travel a lot and this is the first time I have seen such a contraption. But it did produce a great cup of coffee once I figured it out. They gave me a late check-out without a problem and helped me with other issues as well. If you like to run daily as I do, this hotel is not that far from Central Park, which is the best place to run in NYC. Just turn right when coming out of the hotel and go for less than one-half block to 8th Avenue. Then turn left onto 8th Avenue and take it up to just a little past 54 Street where you will find Columbus Circle and quick entry into Central Park. Take $5 or $10 with you so you can buy a gatorade or other drink in Central Park as many of the water fountains there do not work. Also, the exercise room on the 3rd floor is very nice and convenient if you want to stay inside. I would stay at this hotel again.

“Not what I expected at all - and then there's more...” The Comfort Suites in the Westchase area is at the end of a strip mall in a very business-focused area (lots of mirrored, repetitively-built office parks in Westchase, which I see as being a lower cost part of Houston and far from everything else in Houston). I begin by writing I have stayed in every type of hotel or motel imaginable and am not a "hotel snob"....my work takes me various places around the country and to Europe and in some places I have no real choices. In Houston, I did. I also believe that if one must travel often, one should have a pleasant sleep with pleasant surroundings. This was not the case for me at the Comfort Suites. To be frank, I am unclear how this hotel is ranked in the Top #40 (#30 as of this date) of all hotels in Houston. I chose this hotel due to its reviews and ranking as I was unfamiliar with this part of Houston (Westchase). The hotel lobby is spacious with the usual sitting area, etc. The staff are very kind and helpful and the breakfasts are the usual "waffles in a cup, boiled eggs, juice and coffee." The business center was an added plus as I did not bring my laptop for this short trip. The bathrooms were stocked with plenty of towels. That said, the room I had was spacious but extremely plain and rather "mish-mosh" in design, as if the furniture was bought at a liquidation sale and thrown together. I would not have even considered sitting in the area with the little mini-sofa (scratchy upholstery) and table that makes these room "Suites" instead of a regular "Comfort Inn". This area was a non-entity. Besides, of the five lamps in my room, only three worked, and not the one in the <ahem> sitting area. The room also had the oddest odor, which was noticeable as soon as I opened the door. I don't know if it had anything to do with all the rain that Houston had been getting in the prior weeks, but being on the 2nd floor I doubt it and it was not a musty smell. Also, along with many other "budget" hotels, this Comfort Suites has sadly replaced good lighting with the cheapest possible blue-tinted irridescent "stick" bulbs. They give off the most horrific light. The bed was firm but the sheets, blanket and pillows were of poor quality. The weather outside was around 50 degrees and rainy....but the room seemed to have no "air quality" so I turned on the A/C to "clear the air". I also like to sleep with the room temp. quite cool. The A/C gave out and blew only warmish air and rattled, so I turned it off and endured the odor and the stuffiness. Needless to say, I moved to another hotel (a Doubletree) the next night. (I was to have stayed at this Comfort Suites for two nights total.) In Westchase, there are many other hotels to choose from and I have to say I would look elsewhere, like the Holiday Inn Express or other chain hotel around the corner if you are on a budget. Truly, this is an odd area in Houston, and I would go further to say it is off the "beaten path" of Westchase. On a complete side note, don't stay in Westchase unless you have to due to business....stay by the Galleria or downtown. Westchase has some great restaurants and hotels, but the area is a bit seedy and it is like you died and went to strip mall purgatory with the ugly facades and the oddest conglomeration of rental planning. It is as if the realtors/owners have given up on Westchase and are taking whatever they can get to occupy the empty spaces. In the strip mall next to the Comfort Suites, you have a great Whole Foods Market and a great but tiny Thai restaurant and then a deeply discounted bookstore where shady characters hung around, and then two types of "spas", one of which is not at all where a lady would go to have a facial or massage if you get my meaning. You get this info from a quick internet search. There were more than a few shady characters at night hanging around checking out cars in parking lots near this Comfort Suites as the area is not heavily traveled at night. I am from a large city myself and have seen it all, but this was too much for a woman traveling alone on business.

“Very nice and quite reasonable !” I thought this hotel was quite nice for a weekend business trip. It certainly isn't the Ritz, but for $79/night I think you would have a hard time finding a nicer hotel. I liked the heated indoor pool and jacuzzi. Also, the free breakfast was a cut above average. Nice people and very clean.

“Our stay was nice...” After reading some of the posts I was getting nervous but to my relief we had a very nice stay. We only stayed one night due to being there for a concert. The room was nicely sized, clean and had a river view. Hotel staff were very nice and helpful. I also booked on line but had no problems. Either I got lucky or someone is taking notice to the complaints. All in all it was a more than an OK stay and we will return if need be.

“Great Stay” We booked this location because we used to live in the neighborhood, and were we ever impressed with the changes! First off, we were met at the airport by the house driver, who was nice as could be while we wrestled with the paperwork of lost luggage! We arrived at a very discreet entrance and were whisked into a world of pampering. We were greeted by Jeremy, who informed us that he had upgraded us to a 2-bedroom suite (did our driver inform him of our frustrating little luggage experience?). Whatever, we were happy to be treated so nicely! Our view wasn't much (the high-rise next door), but we took full advantage of the lovely terraces (shielded from the wind and heated, one with a fantastic view, the other just off the member lounge). The included breakfast (fresh-squeezed orange juice, Illy Coffees, fresh fruit, assorted breads and pastries, cereals and oatmeal, and a hot entree) certainly did the trick for us, and we kept meaning to join the complimentary wine reception, but ended up with so much wine from our excursion to the wine shop in Ghirardelli Square, that we just took it up to the terrace and enjoyed the view and the fire pit. Our apartment was very nice, with a nicely equipped kitchen with a very clever dining arrangement, living room with fireplace, and two bedrooms and bathrooms. There was also a washer and dryer in the unit, as well as a laptop safe in the master bedroom closet. Bicycles were available for guests to use, as was the wonderful house car. We used the house car several times to ferry us to one restaurant or another. The staff was impeccable. The housekeeping staff was everywhere, from polishing the rails outside to the twice-daily service. I'd single someone out, but it wouldn't be fair to do so because everyone was spot on. This is a great place for couples, families, and groups of friends. The location is surprisingly quiet, and there is so much to do right outside your door. My only suggestion would be for management to make the coffee/tea service available all the time. We noticed quite a few international guests and they can be on totally different timetables. The Fairmont Tea, by the way, was delicious!

“Nice room for the price” I got a good rate for this spacious suite. I enjoy being able to have space to entertain friends/collegues for a drink in my room and this suite was a perfect set up for that. The front desk staff was friendlly and helpful. The hallway on my floor had a rather funky smell but everything else was nice.

“Good Convention hotel and Convenince” The hotel is adjacent to the famous "Bat Bridge." SoCo is within walking distance. If you have time, you can take a bike ride around the Town Lake Trail or paddling a canoe. I always enjoyed the 24-hour gym with the ice-cold towels. If you don't have a car, I would recommend staying across the bridge, closer to the Convention Center, the bars and the restaurants.

“They take the word "accommodate" and "green" seriously!” As far as hotels go, the Hampton Inn is always a good stand by when you need one in a hurry and don't have lots of options. In this particular situation, for the holiday, the family home was packed so we were put up at the ONLY hotel in the Anthem area. So, if you are staying in Anthem, just know this is the only option in a 10 mile radius. The hotel is updating and remodeling it's breakfast service area and gym but have made arrangements for a local gym to accommodate hotel guests, which showed they cared about their guests. Every day in the lobby is a tray of warm cookies, for guests as they come and go. A nice touch for a middle of the line hotel chain. What we particularly appreciated though, was the "to go" breakfast in a bag at the desk for those who check out or leave before the "included" breakfast is served. LOVED that extra touch to accommodate all guests at the hotel. What I particularly liked was something I wish more hotels/resorts did purposefully. Each morning we were asked if our room needed service. In a city where water is a premium, I was happy to help conserve by not asking for new sheets & towels. I made my own bed, by choice, but was very appreciative of their sensibility. This would be a great way to save money on room rates as well, as you don't have to pay for so much unnecessary services unless you want them. Across the street is an outlet mall, a Wal Mart, Dennys and Del Taco. 1/2 mile over I-17 is a Starbucks, banks, grocery stores, etc. Beautiful area. Would I stay here again? If my entire family gets together again and someone needs to go to a hotel, YES!

“Historic feel” We stayed here for 1 night after our cruise. Of course, our room was not ready so early in the morning. They kindly stored our luggage. We were given a time of 4 pm for our room to be ready which was fine with us since we were going off sightseeing for the day. Our room was ready early & they called my husband to let us know. The bed was the most comfortable hotel bed that I have ever slept in. The bathtub was huge! The showerhead was amazing. I liked that the bathroom was in a hall between the bedroom & the livingroom. Too often in a suite the bathroom in located in the bedroom. If you have people sleeping in the livingroom, they have to disturb the people sleeping in the bedroom in order to use the bathroom My only complaints were very minor & maybe a little silly. The common areas were dimly lit & very warm. I also thought the pictures over the bed were very creepy.

“We didn't know!” I reserved a 2 bedroom suite in December for a June weekend. The website states it has one room with 2 doubles, and one room with a king, also includes a parlor. When I checked in, the clerk told me we had 1904 and 1905. When you get to the room, 1904/5 are listed on a plaque together, and have a seperate enterance at the end of the hall. You go in the double doors to a little foyer, the room enterance to 1904 is off to the right, and 1905 is straight ahead. 1904 was the 2 double bedded room, with 2 bathrooms. 1905 was a huge room with a wet bar, lovely views, a king size murphy bed, a sofa with a fold out bed, a loveseat, and assorted chairs. This room had one bathroom. We believed that this was the two doubles/one king/parlor, and this was sufficient for us, but we had another relative that decided to come in at the last minute, and I couldn't get another room unless i paid almost double for a single room than what I paid for the suite. So we reserved a room at the Swissotel, and she cabbed back and forth over the weekend. Upon checkout we examined the bill and there was a charge for food and beverage. Called down to see what it was, and was told it was for a bottle of water from room 1903. I said we don't have 1903, we have 1904/5. The person said you have the two bedroom suite, that encompasses 1903/1904/1905. The check in clerk never told us that, and we wouldn't have known, because the entrance to 1903 is outside the double door entrance to the suite. I had someone check, and sure enough, our card opened the door to 1903. We had shelled out over $250 and countless cab fares for another hotel room, and had an empty room with a king size bed sitting there all the time. I felt sick. They did check with housekeeping and verified that the room had not been touched. They took off the beverage charge and gave me a slight credit. I think they were unwilling to do more because I had such a good price on the room. The guy asked when I had made the reservation because he had never seen a price that low. Other than our unpleasant surprise at the end of our stay, we were very happy with the accomodations. There were a few gnats in one of the bathrooms, but not a big deal. My mom could sit at the window, and watch the boats on the lake. We are all women, so it was nice to have 3 bathrooms. The staff was all very nice, especially the waitress at breakfast at the Pavilion, and the Valet guy. I'd like to reserve that suite again, not hopeful about getting it at the same price though, because I have been checking for different dates, and have never seen it for less than twice what we paid. If we are lucky enough to stay there again, we will know what to expect!

“Nice and within walking distance of the Riverwalk” I have stayed at this Best Western numerous times for business and and I have always enjoyed my stay. The rooms are spacious and always clean. The bathroom is always spotless and the shower head actually has a good amount of water pressure as well (this is always a pet peeve of mine). The hotel employees always treat you like a guest and are willing to help you when requested. The hotel is a short walk to the Riverwalk ( 5-6 blocks) or you can easily get the bus or a cab to the Riverwalk. Parking is a bit limited and you must cross a feeder road to get from their main parking lot to the hotel if you dont get there early enough to grab a front space. For the money, this is one of the best values in San Antonio.

“One of my best Westin stays ever!” I was pleasantly surprised to have such a warm and welcoming staff. I'm a frequent business traveler and am a member of several hotel reward programs, but the staff at the Westin Georgetown was the best I've experienced in a while. I arrived early and had to wait for a room but I was sent a complimentary tea service that evening for my inconvenience. The room was warm and comforting and I took the time to enjoy the spa tub. Even on my way to the airport, one of the bellmen, Deenny, made sure my cab experience was the best it could be. I'll definitely return to the Westin Georgetown on my next trip to DC.

“Functional business hotel” I stayed there a week as part of a conference that occurred in mid-March 2006. I had no problems with it except that I agree with the earlier review that there was inadequate drawer space. The only drawers in my large room were in the desk--it was kind of strange. You need your room key to access the elevators after 10pm so don't forget it if you're arriving to the hotel late at night!!

“Genteel charm uptown” If your NYC visit centers on Museum Mile and environs, this hotel is a great choice. It's walking distance to all the big-name art museums. If you are a first-time NYC visitor, I would not recommend this location because you will have to navigate multiple mass transit options to reach the major tourist attractions. The hotel is small and has Old World charm, such as a nice, small breakfast room with complimentary continental breakfast. The rooms are small. If room size is a concern, this is not a good choice for you. We have stayed in a few other NYC hotels in the past and understand that rooms in this city are small, but The Franklin was the smallest room we have yet encountered. Although clean, the hotel is threadbare in spots. The desk in our room was scuffed and scratched, although it had a lovely ceramic chandelier. The window air conditioner, while welcome because of the outdoor temperature was as noisy as a jet plane. The neighborhood is residential, but lively. You are not "in the heart" of Manhattan, but you are in a nice place. So choose this hotel if it meets your itinerary and inclination.

“Tastefully decorated and plenty of space” The desk was large and easy to work at. There was plenty of space in the room and it was well appointed. The bathrooms were small and had limited counter space. They should drop the extra vanity area and basin to make larger bathrooms.

“What a quaint hotel - good price too” My husband and I stayed here for a wedding held at the same location. The rooms are small, but quaint and nicely decorated. It was more boutique hotel - great location to UT Austin, and overall, I wished we could have stayed her all the nites as it was cheaper than the Omni (too corporate). Highly recommended if you'd like to be within walking distance of the college campus, but not feel like you're on a college campus. Also - the bride and groom stayed in the honeymoon suite and I got a peek at that, much bigger room with a great balcony (connected to other rooms since this is an old home).

“Fantastic Location/Service with Modern Style” There's really no other way to say it: you just really need to stay here when you're in Boys Town. I highly recommend it based on these redeeming factors: 1) The hotel is on a very fun, interesting street with lots of unique shops and restaurants. We could view the L Train from our windows, but rarely heard the train itself; the A/C maintained some nice (but not abrasive) white noise. The station was right next to the hotel. 2) The room's design and amenities were fantastic; containing a lot of modern features, from the flat-screen TV and mounted DVD to the glass block windows in the bathroom. The awesome-smelling eucalyptus shower gel/shampoo were provided via dispensers and the shower head and pressure were great. 3) The service at City Suites was much-appreciated. The front desk clerks were friendly and welcoming; we rarely got past the front desk without a greeting from either the bellhop or the clerks. They were informative and very helpful. A light continental breakfast with assorted cereals, pastry and juices was provided. The only disappointing aspect of my stay at City Suites unfortunately had to do with the quality of sleep there. Don't get me wrong; the bedding was comfortable with its down comforter and several pillows. However, the reader should note that the mattress is an EXTREMELY plush pillow-top. I woke up each morning with a slight backache; if you have back problems like I do, it may pose a problem for a long-term stay. Still, for our three nights at the hotel, I was extremely pleased and would stay there again, if given the opportunity. This hotel has it all: location, cleanliness, service and quality.

“Great experience” Stayed 1 night at the Sofitel on business. This was a great experience overall - good sized, clean room, nice bathroom, quiet, etc. The lobby is a bit disorienting on arrival, but there's a good restaurant downstairs. Service can be hard to attract, but the food was good when it arrived. (Apparently the lounge/bar attracts a fabulous crowd on the weekends, but I was there on a Monday so my colleagues and I had plenty of room to lounge and relax.) The view from my room included the Hollywood sign - fun! - as well as a number of nudie bars - but some people might consider that a bonus. My colleague had a balcony as well - I think you have to ask for an upper floor for that. I'm always a little skeeved by hotel bathrooms, but this one seemed scrupulously clean. It has one of those "rain forest" showers, which was a nice touch, although if you're really tall or don't want to wash your hair I'm not sure how you'd manage. Lovely thick robes (2) and slippers were provided. Turndown service with a free bottle of Evian, another nice touch. Best of all, I couldn't hear the comings-and-goings of my neighbors, which is great when you're trying to get a good night sleep before a meeting. I will probably stay at the Sofitel again when I return to LA.

“amazing value, great service and location” we needed to spend one night in DC, and at my $95 AAA rate i guess i expected a bland convention hotel experience - not so! all service staff greeted us warmly. the room had updated decor and was very comfy. buffet breakfast was outstanding and included in my AAA rate. the DC metro stop is in the building, as is starbucks. we will definitely stay here again.

“Great rooms, great service and great location; but a few flaws” Stayed here with my wife for a night on the way to Maine. This is a boutique hotel in a beautiful building, perfectly located for shopping and with a number of great restaurants nearby. The public areas are small but very welcoming and the staff were uniformly excellent. They recommended places to go, remembered our names and room numbers and were generally exceptionally helpful and friendly. The room was also great. The decoration was a little fussy but if offered two particularly comfortable beds and a small separate sitting area with its own television - no bad thing if one of you is ready for bed and the other wants to stay up. The set breakfast was also good value (on special promotion). Downsides were: a kitchenette area but no tea/coffee making facilities, a shortage of sockets for charging devices (and at least one of them connected to the light switch - as I realised when my laptop was flat in the morning after a night plugged in) and a bathroom with no bath, just a shower. Overall, though, it was a great hotel and very good value for money

“Great location” I enjoyed everything about my stay at the Crowne Plaza. The location was great; near Union square shops, handy to the cable car (if you like that form of transport - I prefer foot). The food at the conference I attended was excellent. The internet connection could have been cheaper though - like free. I've stayed in cheaper hotels where it's free. The relaxation pack provided was a bit of a gimmick, but nice that they tried. The staff were all very friendly and courteous. Overall very enjoyable, and would stay again.

“Great Resort, Friendly service, but isolated” I was at the JW Marriott for a conference. It is a great resort, great waterpark-like pool area, and plenty to do if you play golf, tennis, or hike. The rooms are beautiful, well appointed, great bath with separate shower. The beds are very comfortable, but somehow, no-one seems to have as good a bed as a Sheraton or Weston. The desk was very good with a great panel of connections for my laptop - great for preparing my conference presentation. Unfortunately, the desk chair didn't raise high enough for me. The staff is extremely friendly - not one staff member passed me without a greeting and a smile, and if I stopped or looked like I needed anything, they always offered to help or find someone who could. There even was one young lady who was working the cash register in the pool area where I bought pizza for lunch on Saturday. On Tuesday night, she happened to pass me again in the pool area, and greeted me by name. That to me is amazing. The big problem with this resort is that it is very self-contained. You'll find good (not great, but very good) restaurants, and plenty of activities, but if these don't satisfy, the resort is quite a distance from anything else, and more than 20 miles from the heart of San Antonio. So I've visited a nice resort, but not San Antonio. You may want to rent a car.

“Loved this one!” My husband and I stayed here for his birthday. We had a large group that went and everyone loved it! From the full breakfast, free popcorn and soft drinks to the evening snacks and adult beverages, it was a real bargain. The only thing we didn't really care for was the pool and oberservation deck hours. They close around 10, but I would stay again!
“素晴らしいホテル” モスコーニセンター、近代美術館の隣に位置しているので、観光、ビジネスに大変便利です。ユニオンスクエアまでも歩けます。 このホテルのお勧めはコーナールームです。高層階からは美しいサンフランシスコの景色を見ることができます。 1階のバーも使い勝手がよいです。

“Rough around the edges” This hotel is badly in need of a renovation, the public areas in particular are run down and tired looking. That being said, the rooms are quite large for the price and having a bath tub is a real plus when you’ve spent the day walking - to help soak the tiredness from your legs. I booked a single queen and understand why they urge folks that this is a room best used by a single person. The space between the dresser and bed was so tight I had to lift my suitcase up and over the bed to get it out of the way. The location is ideal for exploring the Mall and downtown area. It is convienent to the metro and bus lines. I did not try either of the hotel dining rooms, did take a look at the breakfast buffet offered at Harriet’s but was not enticed so I got coffee to go. Harry’s looked to be a fairly popular but I’ve learned to be wary of hotel food. The most pleasant surprise to me was the friendliness of the staff. Every one of them went out of their way to help and to make me feel welcome. The one criticism I do have was the one young woman who was at the desk on the night of November 4th had a rather loud voice and talked nonstop to her coworker about some personal experiences for the entire 45 minutes I was in the lobby. I’d return as this is a servicable hotel at a good price.

“Ambivalent” Die Lage ist sehr gut, um alles in Manhattan zu Fuß zu erreichen. Mein Zimmer war sehr groß, mit Badewanne und gutem Bett. Der Fernseher hatte, ebenso wie der Teppich seine besten Tage hinter sich. Kann mich nicht erinnern, wann ich das letzte Mal einen Röhrenfernseher hatte. Hatte einen Wasserschaden beim Baden in der Badewanne morgens um 6 und wurde dann rausgeklingelt. Reaktion war, dass große Lüfter aufgestellt wurden (war also wohl nicht das erste Mal), aber kein Zimmerwechsel angeboten wurde. Da ich nur zwei Nächte da war, war es mir dann auch egal und ich habe einfach den Stecker gezogen, wenn ich im Raum war. Aber für Kurztrips eine ordentliche, günstige Alternative

“Great location, needs updating” Stayed here on a recent business trip to Baltimore. While the office I was visiting was far from central Baltimore, wanted to stay in the Inner Harbour area as I'd never been to the City. The hotel is extremely well located, within walking distance of just about anything you'd want to see in the Inner Harbour area. While everything was clean and staff was extremely courteous and helpful, the hotel had a worn out, tired look to it. I just recently visited a friend who was staying at a Hyatt in my home city and got the same impression. Don't know if there's a pattern there, but at least with the two I've visited recently, seems like Hyatts need some serious updating. Room was large, clean with a nice bathroom although I found the amenities a little thin. Walls were on the thin side---could hear conversation of family with kids next door. I hate adjoining room doors in any hotel room and my room had one but it was well secured. Given proximity to the National Aquarium, there seemed to be lots of families with lots of kids and the hallways were somewhat loud at times.
