Not the hotels fault, but perhaps they could have a quiet floor for those who are on work, rather than a pleasure trip. Also on the negative side----the coffee maker had missing parts. I didn't bother calling the front desk but this shouldn't happen at any hotel. The tv, while nice, big flat screen, was thin on channels, except for all types of ESPN channels you would ever want. Room service was excellent in both delivery time, service and quality of food. I booked through Priceline and paid $75 per night so absolutely no complaints as to price and overall, happy with the hotel. However, if I wasn't booking through Priceline, not sure I'd choose the Hyatt. There are many other hotels in the area which look a lot fresher.

“Lovely hotel, excellent staff” After a long journey from the UK we drove from DFW airport, the hotel was on the LHS of the road, plenty of room to park outside to wait - a few seconds only before we were attended to. From first contact at valet parking (some reviewers thought it was expensive - they should go to Chicago!) all staff were helpful, friendly and efficient. We had a lovely room on the 22nd floor. Too tired to eat out and so had a meal in the hotel bar area, well my husband did - I just managed a glass or two of wine. As it turned out it was a good choice, tasty food, freshly prepared and suprisingly good value for money - so much so that we ate here again on the second night (did go to eat in the bar underneath the Adolphus hotel next door, but I just don't get the throwing peanut husks on the floor thing and the menu and table were sticky so we had a drink and came back to the Magnolia). The complimentary wine and beer were also enjoyable, the bar area is nicely decorated and service was good. Easy walking to Dealey Plaza, Nieman Marcus and a CVS pharmacy (for water). A nice touch was that the room keys were placed in a pocket attached to a fold up map of Dallas. A good start to our holiday.

“Top quality rooms, great location, really truly nice staff.” This was our first trip to Chicago so we selected this hotel based on Tripadvisor reviews and we were not disappointed. When we checked in we mentioned that it was our anniversary and when we returned from our walk we found iced champagne in our room with a card from the concierge. We enjoyed it on the rooftop deck. The hotel location is perfect for walking and for taking the Red Line subway. The wine tasting from 5-6 pm every day is so nice. It is served in the 'living room', is free, and serves as a nice place to meet other visitors to Chicago. The staff members here are a happy group. This place is well-run. We can't wait to come back.

“Okay, Not Amazing” We booked this hotel after reading all the super positive reviews here on TripAdvisor, and after viewing the hotel's own website... We were disappointed. The pros: Great location in the Marina District with great restaurants and the waterfront within short walking distance. We loved the Marina neighborhood and loved being away from the more touristed areas of the city. The hotel is perky, pretty and fun--on the outside. Good quality bagels and pastries and fresh bananas for breakfast. We did enjoy this morning meal. The cons: We had a room with 2 full beds (not 2 queens). Bedding was average, not the best comfort. Really, this hotel was only comfortable for the 2 nights we stayed there. The room was fairly small, the bathroom: very small. Also, the bathroom was in sorry shape, with rust evident and a worn, small shelf. No hand-held shower. Really, the bathroom reminded me of college apartment digs. Quirky and funky can be okay, but when I travel, I want to feel comfortable and clean in the bathroom. The front desk guys were young, and a bit cavalier to my taste. I mean, they were nice enough... There was just not a level of professionalism that let me feel I was in competent hands. Overall, this is a good choice for a quick visit...nothing to get too excited about. I traveled with my husband and young daughter. I don't know what all the fuss is regarding this being the best family choice in SanFran. I don't mean to be a nay-sayer...We simply didn't find this to be the outstanding place it is hyped as. Happy Travels!

“good for overnight” We needed to be in the area for an appointment close to the Mall the next morning and the location was great! Hotel is fairly quiet and clean. If you arrive late, try to eat on your way since the room service is only open until 11pm and you can't walk to any restaurant close by. Parking costs extra.

“terrific location/beautiful large rooms” I stayed one night here recently during a business trip and will definetley return. Main perks: self-parking garage is very convenient; great location to get on highway quickly/with ease; huge rooms; many dining/lounge options in hotel; comfortable bed; nicely appointed rooms. I found a great deal on priceline. I would return on a future trip.

“A Suite For $139!” Great Location overlooking River and Bridge. But what a surprise to enter a downtown capitol city hotel to find two complete rooms - 2 TVS - huge king sized bed with fluffy pillows and comforter. TGIF and Starbucks in Lobby. Yes as another reviewer said - dated decor but huge. Checkin smooth and prepared for me - check out their on line checkin service. For $139. Parking costs but not outrageous for capitol city - $14-$20. Negative Big Time - Business Center was created back in the stone age. Printer cable was incompatible with today's lap tops, printer ink was running so low that white lines appeared, fax didn;t connect for outgoing calls, actually had Word '98 and Fees were outrageous even by capitol city standards. $60 minimum to use the fax. Other Negative - Operator. Couldn;t find messages even though message light on - then couldn;t turn off light. Next day found 2 faxes waiting at front desk even though operator said light must be a mistake. Twice called my room and then said she had the wrong number. Convention rooms freezing but bedroom very comfortable (in line with another traveler's comments). Definitely worth the price for Austin.

“Hotel with a great location” My review will be short compared to previous hotel reviews. I would say that it's mainly because I don't have much more to say beyond what others have already said. Five of us shared a room on the 24th floor, facing the river, and really enjoyed the hotel. I do agree that the lobby was a bit chaotic. My other gripe would be that the elevator situation just was not great. There was an AAS (I believe) conference at the hotel the same weekend we were there and at one point we had to wait about 20mins for an elevator. It seemed like only 4 of the 6 elevators to the 1st 26 floors were working and it was really a pain to get up to our room. Also with 5 people in the room we showed up in our room that had 2 double beds to find 2 towels. That's just a silly number of towels for a room with 2 beds. My other complaint would be the collection of beer caps under the beds and the two 40oz Corona bottles behind the curtains. That to me either says they didn't clean very well, or the maids were getting drunk in our room?? (2nd part is more of a *wink**wink*). Other than those issues, the hotel was really nice. The ability to walk via Skywalks to places in the area was really convenient since we were there in February & it was quite cold. Also, the Shaw's grocery store across the street from the hotel was really convenient for picking up snacks, bottled water, etc. I'd definitely choose the same location again, probably even the same hotel. The T line stops were very close. We actually avoided the sky-high parking at the hotel by parking off of the Orange line on our way in from Manchester Airport. Everything went well, definitely a good deal for Boston. The rate was even good for a hotel in a big city.

“Very good - not amazing - but very good!” Here at the Seaport on business. Had a very late check in and my sense was that they were oversold. They found a room for me, but had to move me at 9:00 am the next morning. But they DID send a porter to move my luggage, and as noted elsewhere, all employees were quite consistent about their "service included" policy! Very nice, indeed! As is the free internet - something you rarely find in an upscale, city hotel. My room was very nicely appointed. I somehow missed the pillow menu, though there was a nice selection on the bed, which also was very comfortable. My second room had a view of the World Trade Center and the harbor - a bit industrial at best, but worth requesting, I think. My business was at the World Trade Center, and the hotel is essentially connected (just across the street). Very convenient. It is also very close to the Silver Line which means you can get to South Station or Logan Airport very easily. Would be ridiculous to take a taxi to the airport when the Silver Line is right there. Why not five stars? Just not quite the five star ambiance. Would somehow expect something a bit more grandiose when you walk in the door. (Stopped by the nearby Renaissance to visit the Starbucks - VERY sleek lobby with a real artistic flair - Seaport doesn't have that.) And I'm simply not a fan of the Keurig coffee systems. Seems like a bad deal in terms of plastic waste, and I never quite get enough coffee! But... that all said, I would stay there again in a heartbeat. Would much prefer it, in fact, over a typical Westin or Marriott! Hope to go back to Boston with my wife to play. Would look at the Seaport first for a good rate.

“Great Hotel in a great city.” The Westin San Francisco Market is just perfect located just between Market Street and Moscone Center. Everything is perfect like the internet speed connection, rooms, service, TV and breakfast. The front desk service must be improved and faster.

“not bad at all!” We stayed one nite for an early Valentine's Day trip. Check in and out was quick and painless, the property is clean and maintained. We missed the happy hour (which is 2 drinks per person, either wine or beer) but we made it to the breakfast, which was fine. Cereal, juices, fruit, yogurt, waffles, sausage,eggs, etc. The pool looked nice, but small and the weather kept us from it. The room(king suite) was very large and looks just like the pictures online. Didnt have much personality, but good nonetheless. Had an elevator and many different vending machines, ice machines, and laundry area. Right on the edge of downtown, close to aquarium, restaurants, etc. Paid close to $200 which was a bit much, but it was clean and everything worked! And parking was free.

“Loved the Hilton Times Square” We had a wonderful stay at this hotel over the July 4th weekend. The hotel is amazing, very cozy. The staff was very friendly and helpful, always attentive. Our room had a fantastic view over the lower city. And we were able to watch fireworks played from 5 different locations through our large room window on July 4th evening. What a treat! And it also has a great location, convenient to everywhere in the city. After came back from sightseeing, we were able to refresh ourselves and change dress before went to the Broadway show. I'm so glad that I came across those hotel reviews at tripadvisor which helped me make the right choice. We will definitely come back to this place on our next trip to New York.

“Another home run by Embassy Suites” We came to San Antonio by car, and really didn't know where we wanted to stay. I stay at Embassy Suites a lot on business, and it seemed like a logical choice for us here when we learned they had a Riverwalk location. Their placement is excellent in our tastes, in that it is on the Riverwalk, but about 5 minutes removed from the heavy traffic/noise of the primary zone. We found the walk to and from the 'hotspots' both refreshing and a bit of a relief. We were there Saturday before Mothers Day, and the sidewalks were packed. The hotel is not a "standard" ES, in that the typical atrium area is absent. The lobby is expansive with the reception breakfast area to the left, and the front desk and Luke restaurant to the right. The front desk is a little "too cool" with small granite podiums for the staff, and was actually a little difficult to identify as the check-in area. Arriving at the desk was when our concern over finding a place to stay began to shed away in a hurry. We were greeted in a warm and sincere manner by Caitlin, who simply pulled us right in. A short discussion later we were headed for our beautiful suite overlooking the riverwalk with big smiles. I'm not sure I've ever felt so welcome at a hotel. Caitlin was training a new employee, and hearing her guidance to the recruit told us that everyone at the ES Riverwalk will know how to make customers feel welcome. Our room was a little smaller than typical ES. We took a two-queens suite to get a balcony that we considered important. The space around the beds is very tight, and one side of the bed will be without a table to set sundries on. The living area was tight, but well designed and flowed well. We found the furniture among the most comfortable we've had at an ES. We had a fridge and microwave as expected. We didn't use the pool, as it was perpetually invaded by screaming kids. We tried to go down at closing time (10 pm) to see if we could sneak in a soak in the hot tub, but alas, parents still don't know how to reserve a moments peace for us old folks. The pool area was clean and secure. One tip, if you go through the "Luke" restaurant, there is an elevator there that will take you straight down to the riverwalk, saving you a couple sets of stairs. We always enjoy the managers reception at ES locations, and this one had a decent selection of fresh fruit and snacks. They had a candy dispenser with M&M's, Reese Pieces, and Gummi Bears which looked like inviting trouble. When you see the candy scattered everywhere, you can imagine that it is a hassle to clean up. In addition to 40 or so tables inside, there are a few outside to get away from the masses to enjoy your drinks and snacks. The bird population clearly knows it's snack time and hover near, but never were an issue. Cleanup of the reception area was an issue, as stated in other reviews. When we arrived (about 6 pm, or 30 mins after the reception started) we saw at least 10-15 tables that were vacant, but pilled high with dishes and glasses. There was food on the floor everywhere as well. We went outside, primarily to escape the mess, but also because there were zero tables cleaned inside. I know that some managers find that encouraging quality at the reception only invites more people to take advantage of the free stuff. These managers need to realize that a strong staff for the reception is what can make a difference on a return trip or not. It was a disappointing edge to an otherwise perfect stay. I also noted that there was zero security for the reception. No one asking to see our key cards, or anything else. Since the hotel seemed to be fairly empty, I suspect that a lot of the people at the reception really didn't belong there. We did find one other housekeeping isssue:). My wife found a note hidden in a hanging lamp over the dining area that said "Whoever finds this is awesome! Sabrina and Maddie". We got a huge kick out of finding this, and were pleased that housekeeping had missed it so it could make our day!
“Great View” We had a very nice stay. Will stay again!

“One of Seattle's Most Comfortable Hotels” I've been traveling to Seattle on business regularly for over 25 years now and I've stayed in probably a dozen different hotels, maybe even more and my choice is almost always a Kimpton Hotel and of the Kimptons, the Vintage Park is my first choice. The hotel is incredibly comfortable and has an understated elegance that appeals to me and the staff is amazing. Yes, they recognize me and greet me by name, but friends who I have sent here have experienced the same level of friendliness and warmth that I get. I always look for a Kimpton first when I travel and I am thrilled that they have expanded beyond their San Francisco/Pacific Northwest base. As with every Kimpton Hotel I've ever stayed in, and that is a lot of hotels, they have an evening wine reception and I've made some good friends through them and some good business relationships through them as well. They also have a coffee reception in the morning that is also a nice touch. The rooms at the Vintage Park are good sized for an older hotel and every every amenity a traveling business person expects in a hotel these days including WiFi in your room and 24 hour room service. Another big plus, again a feature in most Kimpton Hotels, is to bring in a top notch chef to operate a restaurant on the hotel property and in the case of the Vintage Park it is the excellent Tulio Ristorante, that I will review separately.

“A real mixed bag” Sir Francis Drake hotel is a difficult one to review for me, as it did some things brilliantly, and some things rather badly. Let's start with the positives. The location is great. The rooms are lovely - very modern and stunningly themed, as you'd expect from a Kimpton hotel. The room service food (served from the Bistro downstairs) was possibly the best ever food I have had delivered to my room - I had a stunning pan-seared salmon fillet one night and a house pasta the next, both amazing. It's rare for me to get excited about room service food, but this was really, really good. Onto the negatives, and this mainly relate to the service: the staff just weren't as accomodating / helpful as they could have been - perhaps they're taking the olde English aristocratic thing a bit too seriously? Upon checking in, we first had an issue where our booking reference wasn't being accepted - and the receptionist rather patronisingly suggested we had the wrong hotel and attempted to direct us to another hotel of a similar name nearby. After insisting that we were in the right place, he checked with a more knowledable colleague who explained to him that the number I was giving him was from some sort of central reservations system, and hooray, our booking was found. Not a great start. Then, despite the fact that our rooms had already been paid for, the receptionist attempted to put a hold on $900 on my credit card, the cost of the rooms (despite the fact a third party had already covered their cost), plus $100 per night incidentals. I explained that I didn't understand why this had to be done, as our the cost of our stay had already been paid for, but his system insisted on doing it that way. Unhappy with him putting $900 on hold on my credit card I eventually just gave a cash deposit of $100 for each night, and we evenutally checked in, after about half an hour. That was the biggest issue, hence my still fairly high rating. We just felt on occasion the hotel staff didn't really make things as easy for us as we'd expect in a hotel of this calibre. That said, the rooms are gorgeous inside, and I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Value” We just returned after a long weekend in Chicago. The Hampton Inn Majestic is a great property in a good location-great for walking to many places-shopping, Millennium Park, The Art Institute, etc. We had a triple room with 2 queen beds-very large room with nice amenities, flat screen, free wi-fi, coffee maker-loads of space in the bathroom to put things-very comfortable. We also booked a room for our newlywed son and his wife-they had a large room with a king. Very comfortable beds and pillows too. Besides the great location, the entire staff was so friendly and helpful-always smiled and said hello and made you feel welcome. When we arrived on Friday, we asked for a recommendation for a restaurant nearby--Pizanos-excellent-we even went back. The great value for us-since there were 5 of us-was the free breakfast! I was expecting just toast and coffee-but NO! They had something hot each morning plus make your own waffles-fresh fruit-very delicious-and bagels, cereal, muffins, different juices too. The area to eat breakfast did get crowded, but we managed to find space for all of us. We also found out that the Blue Line metro was just around the corner-we were able to use it to return directly to O'Hare airport for $2.25 each!! It took less time than the shuttle van!! We saved a lot of money on the return. There are stairs-but we had small suitcases. All in all-they are doing a great job at this hotel-Excellent value!

“Good postion” Stayed one night good postion close to Cheesecake factory . Walking distance to Market and waterfront. Room very pleasent beds so comfortable floor to celing windows with great view form 11th floor. Bathroon modern plenty of towels . Flat screen TV coffee machine. Bar very expensive as you would expect for city hotel Dont attempt to carry an 18 pack of beer from suppermarket through the lobby to the room to bring home to UK as you are not allowed to carry beer without it being covered with carrier bags!!!!!!! Had to take it back outside and wrap it up - How mad !!!!

“Great Location” This hotel was a nice surprise. Very clean and roomy. Staff was very nice and helpful. Close to many attractions in the LA area. Free parking and Internet as well. Very nice breakfast in the morning. Affordable, clean and great location!

“Great location!” Hotel was directly across from Fanuil Hall Market place so it was very convenient. Rooms were nice even if on the small side. Bathroom was spacious, but no bathtub. Lobby area, public restrooms, and bar (North 26) were all nice. The hotel was a little pricey, but may have been due to the timing of my trip (college graduations and cubs vs. red sox game). I would stay here again.

“Underrated hotel of downtown Indy” Have stayed here twice in the last year. Very clean hotel with some of the nicest Hyatt rooms I have seen. Outstanding location in the city as it is connected via SkyWalk to anywhere you want to see! Great service at front desk. Only downfall is parking is expensive as the garage is not owned by the hotel. I would definitely park in a garage down the street for much less (government building garage or even the Mall Parking garages).

“Nice Hotel, Not a Convenient Location” Nice hotel, nice rooms, beds comfortable, location is right next to Mission Bay, but in my opinion not within walking distance to the ocean beach. If your with a family and don't want to venture out, this is a great location. Park nearby, walking trail behind the hotel. I prefer to be near restaurants and the ocean, this is bay front. I booked through hotwire. Tennis courts on site and very large pool with a childrens pool too. Game area for the kids and during the tourist season a childrens program. They rent boats, ski doos, bikes, and other play items right at the hotel. There is a restaurant on site, but a bit pricey. Didn't eat there. Had to drive to another location, since no other eateries within walking distance. Paid $14 to park my car outside of my room. No parking garage. Just another way to get another buck from the consumer.

“Very Good, but Could Be Great w/Minor Improvements” Stayed here over a week in September, first with a Road Scholar (Elderhostel) group and then on my own! The great items included: 1. Ideal location, close to everything - excellent restaurant (Prime Rib) at hotel, plus a more causual sports bar / restaurant (Tavern 17) -- see separate reviews of Tavern 17 2. Historic hotel, exceptional grand lobby -- make certain to look at the ceiling 3. Room size and layout great (both for working at desk and watching TV), quiet, comfortable, good A/C, relatively recently re-done room 4. Sleep number bed (YAY!) 5. Free bottled water in the room, along with a good working coffee maker 5. Excellent front desk services - friendly and competent 6. Very well-lighted hallways 7. Fruit infused water in the lobby - very tasty The not-so-great items: 1. Business center PCs (two) -- although free, PCs did not seem to work very well - old and a couple of times could not get on-line or could not print. Definitely need to upgrade the business center. 2. Housekeeping was erratic - some days very good, other days not so much, e.g., some days the bottle of free water was replaced and other days not; one day the trash was not emptied, etc. 3. Airconditioning in the lobby and hallways was extremely cold. Nice when you first walk in from being outside in the heat, but too cold to linger in the beautiful lobby. 4. Hotel parking at $34 / day. Yes, it is a big city, but all of the parking lots around there were charging between $20 and $25 / day. However, valet was very nice and provided good directions to exit the city. All in all, I would definitely stay there again and would recommend this place. With just a few, relatively minor improvements, this place could be exceptional -- mostly a better business center and a little more effort on housekeeping.

“Very nice hotel” The room had a separate sitting area with a work desk. There is a fridge in the room, but you can buy cold water (and some snacks as well) at the reception. The room was perfectly clean and nicely decorated. The breakfast included healthy food as well, like grapefruit, I loved it! The hotel is close to the airport, right on I-10, but not noisy. They have a pool but we did not have a chance to try it.

“Great location, no issues” The location is great if you plan on doing a lot of running around Chicago. It's walking distance to both Lake El stations which means you have every El line close by and a straight ride from O'hare for $2.25. The lobby is large and a nice place to meet and hang out. They have 3 pay computers to use. I have some status and got probably the best room location, a river view at the end of the hall. The room looked like housekeeping had cleaned it in a hurry, the drawers were all open and a couple of spots needed a sweeping though. The room was a bit larger than normal and the bathroom was large. Between the wide bathtub and curved shower curtain rod I felt like I was showering in a wet room. Sheets and towels were of good quality as was everything else. Everything else was Westin nominal. Definately recommend!

“OK Hotel” The hotel is very large with a nice lobby and efficient check-in. But once you get to the hallways and rooms on the guest levels, it feels much more institutional. My room was large but kind of drab. Not all the lights worked; it was impossible to turn them all off without unplugging them. I had an issue with the TV I asked guest services to fix but they never followed up. While not a huge deal, it was just one small thing that could have been better. Not a bad stay but not memorable either.

“Terrific Location for Mall visitors” The Marriott Residence Inn Capitol Hill is a remarkable location for visitors to the national mall in DC. A mere three blocks away from the mall, visitors will enjoy the convenience of major attractions just a short distance away. The hotel rooms are clean and spacious, and including kitchenettes--virtually unheard of among DC hotels. The hotel offers hot breakfast (included in our rates) and hot dinners (for an additional cost) on weekdays. Being so close to the mall does have some downsides however; things quiet down considerably in the evenings, and one will have to take a cab to get to a wider selection of restaurants. The hotel is comfortingly secure, in that guests must have an electronic key to have access beyond the lobby floor.

“Scans drivers license and credit card into their computer” This hotel scans your drivers license and credit card into their computer. They say it for my benefit so another person can't walk in and pretend they are me. I don't believe that and I don't want to be in their system. It is more dangerous for me because their computers can be used by dishonest employees or hacked and I don't know the safeguards. I asked for the cards to be deleted from the computer after I left but the clerk said they can't be deleted. I'll call my credit card company tomorrow and the North Carolina Chamber of Commerce. The hotel clerk said all Best Westerns scan drivers licenses and credit cards. My room was paid ahead and was nonrefundable. I guess I will cancel my credit card after I get home. I want to inquire at the NC Chamber of Commerce and the NC Board of Corporations to see if this policy is legal.

“Very stylish” Stayed here for 2 nights in October 2012. Very friendly staff. Our room was pretty big and comfy, worthy of a 5-star hotel IMO. The hotel is within walking distance of several Gaslamp quarter restaurants and bars, which is nice. Valet parking is quite expensive, but there are some alternatives in the near surroundings (street parking is free on weekends, and there are several garages around that are more affordable than their valet). Very stylish rooftop pool and bar.

“Beautiful hotel, killer restaurant, dazed service” IF you can get a good rate here, 60 is your best boutique bet in NYC. Even the tiny rooms are on the stylish relatively comfy side, but I've been upgraded a few times, and the suites are great. Lobby is cool and fun- bar's a good scene (rooftop especially) - restaurant Kittichai is one of my favorite rooms anywhere and totally delicious. You cannot beat the location- just off of bustling West Broadway, so you don't step out into the madding SoHo crowds, but close to everything. I can't say that service really exists here, but they're not nasty or snotty, just kind of dizzy and uninterested.

“Great Business Class or Family Hotel in Downtown” On our most recent stay in Indianapolis, my partner and I brought my mother-in-law along for Mother's Day weekend. We booked her a room at Springhill Suites for the weekend since it would be close to our hotel(attached actually to the JW Marriott). Check-in was swift and the young lady who checked us in was very congenial and had a great attitude. We chit chatted with her for a few moments as no one else was checking in and then took the MIL to her room. The rooms are nicely appointed with comfy beds, a sitting area, flat panel tv, and even two bathrooms. A 1/2 bath sits adjacent to the full bathroom. I dare say it, but the bathroom was actually much bigger than our room at the JW Marriott. The view was spectacular and looked out over the river. Amenities were adequate and included a pool and fitness center. Hot breakfast was also complimentary the next morning. There were only two snafus the entire stay ; one being noisy plumbing and the water had shut off during the MIL's shower. She turned the valve off and turned it back on and the water came back although the plumbing continued to rattle the rest of her stay. Somewhat strange for a brand new hotel. The other thing I observed as we went to check the MIL out the morning we were leaving was one of the breakfast attendants standing in the hall near the check in desk stirring what appeared to be oatmeal in her arms?? and asking guests if they were staying at the Springhill as they approached the breakfast line. I understand trying to keep the correct guests in line for the morning breakfast, but have some respect about it. Minor annoyances to an otherwise great stay. Highly recommended.

“An overall pleasant experience.” My partner and I have stayed at this hotel on several occasions and have had pleasant experiences every time. There is quite a difference in some of the room sizes, but they are all nicely decorated in a very contempory style. We love that they have a pool, a nice exercise room and are pet friendly. There usually is a manager's reception for guests in the afternoon and a complimentary "snack" in the room on arrival date. The staff is friendly and professional. Room rates are often a bit high, but we find that they sometimes offer good deals on weekends. Overall, this is a good choice if you're looking to stay in the Dupont Circle area of DC.

“Great but try not to get a connecting room!” The Palomar is a fantastic hotel, great atmosphere whenever you come into the reception, fabulous free drinks hour as at all other Kimpton hotels, lovely robes, socks and free umbrella (handy when we were there as it was horrible weather!). Location is good for the metro and for Dupont Circle/Georgetown but the main part of Washington is a metro trip or a 20-30 minute walk away so if you like being on top of things it's not that good for that. Rooms are fabulously large but unfortunately we were in a connecting room and our neighbour decided to get up at 6am and talk very very loudly with no concept of the time or that other people may want to sleep. We were also in a room at the front of the hotel so got noise from the road. If you are a particularly light sleeper I would recommend asking for a room at the back of the hotel and not a connecting room! I'd go back.

“Cool Hotel” The location of the hotel is good. It is only a few minutes walk to 125th Street which is on lines A/B/C/D which you can take to get downtown. The area is safe to walk around and perfectly fine. The style of the hotel is a vision of a W hotel so very modern and clean cut without the price of a W. The staff at the hotel are so friendly. Nothing is a problem and they are very upbeat. From check-in to check-out they were cheery and efficient. The Aloft room I had contained a king bed and was comfortable. Room size was good for New York and bathroom had a shower only but it was a double shower. Good sized. There was free wifi. The only quibble I had with room was the noise from the air conditioner as it was not ducted but a stand alone one. There was also a bit of street noise coming into the room too. They were minor issues though. The hotel is good value considering how expensive NYC hotel prices can be. I would stay here again

“Great location” The room was very comfortable and the staff went out of their way to make me welcome and allow an early check in. This hotel is in a great location for walking to sights and shopping in downtown Seattle. I stayed overnight for business, so did not have much time to partake of the hotel amenities.

“Well located and good for business traveler” This is my second trip to the hotel, I was here in August of 2011 and now again in June 2012. The remodeling is now fully complete, and there has been time for dust to settle around the edges of the carpet in the room and mold to form on the shower curtain. When I was here a year ago, I had a nice size room with a large bath and double sinks. This time when traveling with my wife and 2 adult sons, I got a small room with a really small bathroom. One thing that puzzled me is why housekeeping left towels for 3 in the room each day when there were four of us in the room. They were quick though to cheerfully deliver more towels when requested.Front desk staff was friendly and accomodating, as well as the bell hops. Location is adjacent to Grand Central Station, so subway acccess is easy. Many attractions are a less than a 20 minute walk from hotel. I would definately return for a third time, but just request a larger room.

“Second time as good as the first” We stayed at the HI Express in September last year for 5 nights and were as pleased with it this time as last. Excellent free breakfast which is served just off reception and it can get very busy here , but the place is quickly tidied and you wouldn't know that there had been hundreds of people eating there. We had a large disabled access room which was immaculate and very roomy. Large bathroom well stocked with towels and toiletries. Front desk staff were the same as 2 years ago, which I liked. I'd definitely stay here again as I actually like being near the Wharf but close to transport. Great value.

“The WORST service I ever had - this can not be Radisson!” On the way from Red Woods to Los Angeles I just wanted to overnight at secure and clean place, to relax a little bit etc. As Gold Elit member of Radisson it was a fast decision to check first the Carlos hotels. Well I was really surprised when I found a great rate on Hotels.com and booked a room at this hotel. I arrived at the evening and did not really see a lot of the neighborhood. The first impression of the lobby was OK. Two persons at the reception desk - no line - great. The young lady at the reception looked not really friendly but OK at the evening is somehow understandable. I asked her to put my member number on the reservation in case I can get some award points for my stay. She said immediately "We can not do this because you booked over Expedia". Here I started a short discussin with her because this was not the first Radisson hotel which I book over Hotels. com (she affirmed all the time expedia and hotels.com are the same). She asked me then to sign a registration form ... with very different rate. So I asked her why it is written something else and not my rate and she told me again "You booked over expedia and this is your rate". She was more and more rude but I was tired and no fancy to discuss so I just went to my room. The first impression was not so bad - big room but with old furnishing. The first thing I checked was the window - you know how the room smells if not aired the last 2-3 days . It was a sash window but not possible to open more then 1/2 inch... well the first problem - I do not like to use the aircondition in the night when I can open the window but here not possible. It was about 22-23C (71-73F) and really a nice weather but OK. I turned on the aircondition and it was very loud - so I switched it off again. Next I wanted to call a freind who is leaving in San Jose and ... something was wrong. Yes, I was in 5th floor (room 527) and on the telephone was written 306???? Strange but good I saw it and checked in which room I stay before tell this to my friend. My first shock was the bathroom. It looked not really clean and VERY neglected. The tube was in terrible condition - may be cleaned but looked not clean with the scraped parts. My decision was fast and I took just a shower... Even loud I turned on the AC because it was very hot inside and tried to sleep. It was not possible and I turned it off again. I was arouse from a VERY loud noise... checked the time - it was 7 a.m. Looked trough the window - and... yes this was a big building lot across the street and they already started to work. Tried to close the windows was not possible and the 1/2 inch was enought to hear even the cars on the highyway behind the building lot. Well sleep was not possible. My next surprise was as somebody knocked on the door at 8.30 a.m. This was the maid who wanted already to clen the room! I told her she should come in 2 hours when I leave and close the dore. Well I just packed and went to the reception to complain and to check out. After the usual "good morning. checking out" ... I just heard from the guy at the desk - "Done. Have a nice day"???? Well if he do not ask me how was my stay so I should tell him. I complained that it was loud, bath was not clean, room service at 8.30 a.m. in the morning etc. it was not a pleasent stay.... and what was his reaction "Sorry, Sir, but you booked over expedia and your room is prepaid so no refound possible even you are not satisfied." So this was the best I heared - if you do not book over Radisson - you do not have 100% satisfaction guarantee. So I left this hotel with the feeling - you booked over expedia (even it was hotels.com) - so it is your porblem and do not boder us with your complains. I NEVER heared my name on the reception desk which is never happened even in a 2-star hotels. So if you want to be treated like an intruder and not like a guest - this is the best place for this.

“very nice” We were in Indy for a cheerleading competition. The hotel is convenient to the convention center, it will be better when the JW Marriott opens and the skywalk is opened. I had reserved 2 double beds, when I got to my room it was a king. I called the front desk and they put us in a handicap room since we already had our luggage on that floor. The room was huge. It was clean and I appreciated the mini fridge. My only complaint with the room was the bathroom and shower doors being opaque glass and sliding open and close, it was hard to be quiet in the middle of the night. I liked the breakfast, that was a money saver for us. We were in town for a cheerleading competition and although the hotel was full of cheerleaders, it was still quiet. The valet were wonderful, my car was nice and warm when it was time to go. This was a stylish and clean hotel, I plan on staying again in the future.

“Our New Favorite in Indy!” All I can say is WOW! What an incredible experience...and that’s what this hotel is – an experience! From the moment we pulled into the very modern entrance drive to the time we checked out, we were astonished by the level of service we received from every staff member we encountered. We have had the opportunity to stay at most of the downtown hotels including the Conrad, the Westin, the Marriott, and the Hyatt, and I can truly say that in our short stay at the JW Marriott, they have made us customers for life! First of all, the building itself is a knock-out – contemporary and sleek...a beautiful addition to the Indianapolis skyline. The lobby was bustling with activity at all hours, and although we didn’t have the chance to visit any of the restaurants, they looked very inviting - especially the lobby bar which had plenty of cozy areas for drinks and conversation. The design is one in which there is no congestion. Even though there were many people passing through, the flow of traffic was smooth...just one more indication of the many details that have gone into designing this hotel. Although it was quite busy when we checked in around 8:00 pm, we had no wait. All the check-in desks were busy, but as soon as we stepped into the waiting area, a gentleman who had been observing the lobby area came to greet us and take us to another check-in station. We appreciated his attentiveness, but were even more impressed with his personalized service. We were informed that as Marriott Reward members, we had been upgraded to one of the higher floor rooms, and believe me, the view is incredible! When he asked the purpose of our visit, we explained that we were celebrating our daughter’s 21st birthday. He immediately focused on her, wishing her a happy birthday and giving her the “royal treatment.” He then proceeded to ask her if she had a favorite wine, as he wished to send up a complimentary bottle in honor of her special day. What a thoughtful touch! Then, instead of just issuing our keys and pointing us in the direction of the elevators, he escorted us to the bank of elevators that we would be using to reach our floor...just one more little detail to make you feel truly welcome. We liked the added security of having to use your room key to activate the ability to press the floor button, a feature you don’t see very often. The room itself was comfortable, well-appointed, and visually appealing. A variety of colors and textures were used to create a space that was just different enough from most upscale hotel chains to make it really stand out. Although we were not in the room much on this little get-away, I am looking forward to going back and spending time at the hotel to take in all they have to offer. If you are heading to Indianapolis, whether it be for business or pleasure, I would highly recommend staying at the JW Marriott. By the way, even though we were in town during the time that the Brickyard 400 was being run, the rates we secured (via the hotel Website) were better than those offered by most of the other downtown hotels.

“All you need and comfortable” Stayed here for one night for a concert at the auditorium downtown. Really not sure about the location since we don't know the area - it did seem a little far from the nicer areas but only 5 or 10 minutes from downtown. The hotel itself is just enough - good value for money, clean, and comfortable. Front desk staff were very friendly. Got a nice room that had a separate living area with small kitchen. Beds were very comfortable, new flat screen TVs, and very clean. No complaints about this place if you're looking for a decent hotel at a good rate.
“交通の便が良い” 立地が良く、どこに行くのにも、便利なロケーションでした。 大きいホテルなので、人が多く、特に団体客と、一緒になるのが嫌な方には、向かないかも知れません。

“funky charm” We often use the TraveLodge LAX as a stop-over before early morning flights or after a long journey. It's a "mature" property, so anyone looking for a spiffy cookie-cutter hotel feel ought to look elsewhere - all the chain biggies are within walking distance (as is rent car return). This place has character. For those who enjoy live plants (poolside garden and ivy in the rooms) and a retro feel of LA like it used to be, this is a good choice. You'd not be surprised to find this hotel as the upscale choice in a small California town. Free Wi-Fi, and a conti breakfast of bagels, cereal, oatmeal, etc. (Used to have hard boiled eggs, but no more.) Housekeeping tries hard, and linens are good enough - how many hotels provide a soap dish, or a really good iron? Staff is helpful. There's a small convenience store/souvenir shop inside. Computer in the cozy lobby. A Denny's adjoins the property, and a Shell station with a larger convenience store is only yards away. Bargain online rates are common, and it's convenient to LAX. Shuttles run outbound on the half-hour; just call the hotel (phone at bag claim) to get a pickup. The area is a little noisy, so be prepared for that since many rooms have patios/balconies and large sliding glass doors. Upstairs is best, and avoid middle rooms or stairs since the hotel bustles throughout the day. Air handling by classic Friedrich heat/cool units, or windows. The TraveLodge doesn't pretend to be more than it is, and what it is serves very well.

“The name says it all . Top of the Mark” I know the hotel is not named Top of the Mark but the name of their signature bar / restaurant is on point. The staff is nice. The rooms are comfortable. The views are amazing. The location is great. SF has so much to offer and when you have a relaxing hotel to unwind in to rest your feet it sure makes the whole SF trip even better. I have stayed here before and will most certainly return.

“Cheap, easy.” The Adante is a good place. The rooms are as expected, small & dated but clean & tidy none the less. The view of the lovely old Victorian apartments on our street was lovely, however the road noise was a bit too much at some points. Recommend requesting a non- road side room. Staff kept to themselves unless needed, they were friendly & prompt. Location was good enough. Happy.

“Great Value & Service...loved it.” Booked for $99/night including breakfast coupon ($10/pp for 2 adults) on Travelzoo. Includes free Wi-Fi in room. Parking was $10/day but that was reasonable compared to all the hotels in the area. hotel was near the Marina so great views and surroundings (no beach access though). The pool was very nice and they also have parrots/fish ponds/turtles in the garden....little things that kept our toddler entertained! We were staying on the 2nd floor and they don't have any elevators so you'll have to move luggage up the stairs...not a big deal for us as you can park right at the bottom of the stairs but some people might not like that. Great staff! very friendly and helpful. All in all a great stay!!

“Best location in town” Great views with this hotel located by the water. The rooms and bathrooms are spacious and the beds are very comfortable. The hotel has a burger restaurant on the waterfront which is very pleasant. There is also a Starbucks on site which is very welcoming.

“Great location, nice rooms, a hitch here and there” The Westin Copley Place, attached to the Prudential Mall, is a very good hotel with the usual Westin amenities. We found the bathrooms a little cramped and had one glitch with getting a coffee bar re-stocked that was just comical - someone, please get them those neat Nextel two-way radios. On the whole it was convenient and up to snuff. BEWARE, however, the valet parking/luggage morass if it's at all busy - they had no idea how to handle it and didn't seem to care.

“Employees Loved this Place” I booked some employees here for a week and they were very happy with the rooms the hotel and the service. I am looking forward to visiting while I travel down to LA on business.

“Still A Favorite” Always clean. Always pleasant. More than a place to crash for the night. On this trip, front desk staff took the time to: 1) ensure a place for us to easily park our trailer and a room from which to see it and 2) replace the ink cartridge on the printer so we would have clean printouts.

“Nice hotel near convention center.” Very nice hotel directly across from the convention center. Rooms are clean and functional. As a HHonor Gold member, I was upgraded to a corner, larger room. Although nice, the space and "mountain view" would not be worth the cost if not upgraded. Staff at breakfast were great. Lots of seating, which is always appreciated. All other staff confident and friendly. Food was good and reasonably priced. Quick bus ride or walk to other downtown attractions. I walked to Coor's Field in 20 minutes. Of note, Walgreen's was two blocks from the hotel along with a few fast food restaurants.

“What a beautiful property!” I stayed here September 27 - 30, 2009. Conference hotel was the nearby Hyatt, but I got a better rate and stayed at this beautiful, new property. Refurbished beaux arts building originally built as B & O Railroad HQ's in 1906. It seemed like I was the only guest on my floor. Totally quiet and from the 9th floor, even street noise was minimal. Also enjoyed dinner at the adjacent restaurant and the manager on duty was a fellow Michigan State grad. Try the gnocci made of ricotta cheese. Much lighter than potato based pasta and tasty! Treat yourself and stay at the Hotel Monaco.

“Excellent Service, Beautiful Hotel” Let me start by saying, I will certainly stay here again!! The hotel is beautiful, and the rooms are even better. I had a Corner King room on the 15th floor with great views south and west. The bathroom was beautiful, with a large shower and an oversized rainfall shower and outfitted with high end fixtures. It featured a glass wall looking into the bedroom with an electronic art shade. The bed was soft and luxurious with natural, organic fabrics. The location is also a few blocks away from several subway stations as well as the happening area of Soho. The service I received was as good, if not better than many other 5 star hotels I have stayed. Dan, from the front desk, was awesome! He arranged dinner reservations, shared his knowledge of theatre options, and always called me by name. The continental breakfast is limited, but nice and convenient. The wine and cheese service in the early evenings is also a nice amenity for the hotel. The rooftop Pool and bar is quite popular with awesome views of the city. Also, the David Burke Kitchen in the cellar of the hotel is incredible. It makes for a convenient and excellent meal while in NYC.

“Gutes Stadthotel” Wir haben 6 Nächte in diesem Kimpton-Hotel verbracht. Die Lage dieses Hotels ist ideal um die Stadt zu erkundigen. Sämtliche Sehenswürdigkeiten dieser Stadt sind bequem zu Fuss oder mit ÖV zu erreichen. Eine Subway-Station befindet sich in unmittelbarer Nähe. Die Kimpton-Kette werde ich in Zukunft mehr berücksichtigen. Fazit: Sehr empfehlenswert.

“Nice hotel, but can't quite compete with the Four Seasons” My family and I stayed here on New Years Eve, as we were attending a private party at the residence of a tenant in the Tower portion of the building. This is a luxury hotel, yet I don't feel that it can compete with the like of a Four Seasons or Ritz Carlton. Pros: Beautifully decorated room, great views, and my husband and I had an EXCELLENT couples massage. Cons: spotty service (for example, after waiting in line for 15 minutes to check out, the clerk decided to take a break just as I got to the head of the line...!), the spa waiting room was littered with dirty glasses, and I really didn't need to see Donald Trump's face plastered over half the items in my room. Overall, when spending the kind of money you spend to stay here, you expect a much more polished experience, such as the one you get when you stay at a Four Seasons (which actually, was cheaper than the Trump).

“Excellent value for the price” I stayed here for three nights with my family during their trip to Jax. We had the master king suite, which consisted of two rooms - a living area with comfortable sofa bed, and a separate bedroom. There was also a sink, microwave, and refrigerator. The spacious bathroom had two sinks, a whirlpool tub (did not use), and a shower stall. The entire suite was decorated in bright colors, which were very modern. The whole suite was extremely comfortable, clean, and an amazing value for the price we paid. We had considered reserving two separate rooms, but the suite ended up being a better value. It also was good for nights when my sister and I wanted to stay up and watch TV. My father could go to bed in the separate room and not hear the TV. You would never know this property was a Hampton Inn by the decor and overall atmosphere. It looks brand new. The free continental breakfast was above average and was located in the large lobby area with a fireplace and flat-screen LCD TV. The pool is located adjacent to the lobby. It is small, but adequate. Other items of note... the hotel is located in the Tinseltown area, which has a huge selection of restaurants, shops, and a movie theater all within walking distance.

“Nice, warm and well appointed” I liked this hotel. It doesn't have that corporate feel at all. The rooms are small but very comfortable and well appointed. The lobby is the same - small but warm. The location is odd but good. It is only a few blocks from the public library and 2 blocks from Grand Central. Times Square was a 10 minute walk. But you are on the "other side" of Park Avenue so it feels more residential and quieter. I was really pleased with my stay. It's not grand, or impressive. But it's warm, nice touches (like cocoa and hot toddies, water all day infused with citrus, and the "raid the mini bar" coupon) and a good-enough local.

“Consistently beautiful and comfortable with top service” I had yet another wonderful stay at The Greenwich this weekend utilizing the restaurant, library room and spa and all did not disappoint. A wonderful enjoyable visit. One minor note is my very large room had one of the smallest bathrooms I have experienced there...too small for women so be sure to ask for a bigger bathroom as the rooms are all different. Also if you have a platinum amex, definitely book through them as the benefits are great.

“"Hot" place to stay!” We got a good rate over Thanksgiving weekend, and were pleasantly surprised by the size of the room. However, the weather was unseasonably warm, and our room was quite hot when we checked in. We tried lowering the temperature using the thermostat, but while we set it to cool the room down to 68 degrees, there was only a tepid amount of cool air coming out of the vent. When we went out for the evening, we left the window open a crack (this is one of the few hotels where you can still actually open your windows!). We didn't leave the window open enough, and when we returned late that night, it was once again quite hot. We again tried to cool the room off, but the temperature actually kept rising instead of falling. By morning, it was a balmy 81 degrees in our room. I actually slept on top of the cover and sheets for most of the night. The other problem we had was that our special weekend rate include a coupon for two drinks at the Polar Lounge, located underneath the hotel, or at Inoteca, the hotel bar (which you actually have to walk outside from the hotel lobby to get to!). When we got back to our room late that night we noticed a line of much younger people on the sidewalk, apparently waiting to get into the Polar Lounge. We called the front desk to ask if we had to wait to get into the place, and were told there was no wait, but there was a dress code, and no jeans or sneakers were allowed. We were also told we couldn't use our drink coupon at the hotel bar. Since we had only brought jeans to wear, we were out of luck. To the hotel's credit, when we asked about this at the front desk in the morning, we were told we had been given incorrect information, and we could have used our drink coupon at the hotel bar. We were able to do so that afternoon before we left town, and had a nice, generous glass of wine there and ordered some delicious bruchetta to snack on. The hotel doesn't give you a lot of towels (there's not much room for them in the bathroom), but gave us some extras when we asked, and when we broke a glass in our bathroom, someone came up promptly to clean the mess up. There were two computers with free internet access in the guest lounge on the 10th floor. Except for the Saturday night front desk clerk who gave us bad information about our drink coupons, the service was friendly and efficient. But I wouldn't want to stay here in the summer unless I knew you could actually cool your room off!

“Chic, Trendy, Comfy and FUN!!!” I don't have much to say about this place other than to say I really enjoyed staying here. Its visually appealing inside and certain was equally as impressive in the room. I got this beautiful hotel for $55 on Priceline!!! The Galleria Mall is right across the street...shopping and dining were real close! Things to be conscious of: PARKING FEES (however, during my stay the kind young lady at the desk waived the fee). THEFT (during my stay someones car was broken into on the paid parking lot). I loved the trendy decor and the spacious room environment, which included a sofa, ottoman, high desk which doubled as a dining table, huge tv's, spacious bathroom, etc. This place is somewhere I'd definitely stay again!

“Met all my expectations” This hotel was in a great location - easy walk to 16th Street shopping, restaurants, and other activities. The hotel's conference facilities worked out just fine, front desk and bell staff were friendly, room was spacious - no complaints at all. There is an espresso shop right on the property, although there is at least one Starbucks within easy walking distance (I have my priorities).

“Wonderful for park n flying families!” What a value! For $99 got over a weeks worth of covered parking, free shuttles and a spacious suite! Just parking at O'Hare for 10 days was going to cost us more! This hotel really is the absolute best parknfly option at O'Hare. The room and bathrooms were very large. For a family with teenage daughters, all trying to get ready before our early flight, we could not have asked for more. We have stayed at other ParknFly hotels near O'Hare, so we know what we are talking about here. The pool was awesome, and the workout room has a window into the pool. So I could keep an eye on both of my girls, one swam and the other worked out. The "L" is right across the street for easy access to Chicago. We will definetly use this hotel again!

“More like individual apartments than a hotel” The arrangement of the building makes this complex more like an apartment complex than a hotel. All of the rooms are suites, so there is a separate bedroom. Even though the bedroom was kind of small, the layout worked well. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The only downside, if one can call it that, is the entrance is somewhat hidden. There is no large, obvious sign for the hotel, it looks more like you are entered a private community. Kepp this in mind as you have to be observant or you'll miss the entrance
“Would stay here again” The room was clean and sufficiently comfortable. The in-room safe never worked. I was moved from the 1st room I was allocated and the safe in the 2nd room never worked!!!

“Great location, nice hotel.” We spent a weekend at this hotel with another couple (seperate rooms) for their aniversary. This hotel is within 2 blocks of the water, next to Little Italy, and within walking distance of the Aquarium. Breakfast was included with the stay. The hotel was affordable, clean, and convenient. We will stay there again.

“Silver Elite Treated Very Well at Check-In” Rooms and Check-in: We asked for an upgrade (we are silver elite) from a cozy room to a larger room at check in (they had a separate line for elite so there was no wait at all) and were given a superior room right away. Our room was a king corner room on a high floor. The superior room was not very large (can't imagine what a cozy looks like) but was perfect for the two of us. Security: The security is fantastic at this hotel. There were several security guards at all hours of the day and night in the lobby and right outside. We felt very safe. Concierge: We didn't use the concierge much but did a map from them and that was all we needed. Other: We did not use any amenities in the hotel. The location is fantastic, very close to the subway (several lines). It is a quiet area and very nice. We would stay here again. Pictures will be posted shortly.

“No Customer Focus” Our family of four stayed here for two nights in July 2008. Based on other TripAdvisor reviews, we made sure we were on the newer side of the hotel. The room was huge and had an upscale feel, and the view of the bay was very nice. There is a nice walking/jogging path right along the edge of the water. The bathroom was roomy, but it could have used an exhaust fan to clear out the humidity after showers. One selling point we were excited about was the hotel's free shuttle to Sea World. However, it turns out there are three fixed departure times in the morning and three fixed pickup times in the evening. This does not allow flexible coming and going from the park as we had hoped. We tried taking the shuttle the first day, but the shuttle back to the hotel was over an hour late. The next day we drove ourselves to Sea World and paid the $12 parking fee. That night when we arrived back at the hotel, the "reserved" parking area near our room was full! Oh, did I mention this hotel charges guests $12 a day for parking? Another irritation: when we needed someone to reset the room safe so we could lock up our valuables while at Sea World, it took three phone calls and almost an hour of our valuable vacation time for someone to finally show up. Overall, I think this is a nice property and location, but the staff needs to refocus their efforts on customer service if they want to become a great facility. For this price, I expect to be "wowed", and that didn't happen at the Dana.

“Downtown Chic” Just enjoyed four fantastic nights here with my 16 year old daughter and we can't wait to stay here again on our next visit. I don't understand some of the recent negative reviews as we had a great experience on all levels - the entire staff couldn't have been nicer or more friendly, the hotel itself is beautifully outfitted with a very cool, retro, downtown chic decor and the room was spacious, comfortable and very nicely appointed. The concierge members here were some of the best in the business, so helpful with restaurant reservations and assisting with all of our inquiries. The doormen and especially everyone at the front desk were super friendly and welcoming. Special thanks go to Rina with reservations who helped make our stay a most memorable and fantastic experience. She couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. Our corner room on the 15th floor was super quiet with stunning views of the city and more than enough room and closet space for two. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the bathroom nicely appointed and tiled. We loved the decor of the lobby lounge areas - so comfortable and a nice way to start our days with the continental breakfast that serves probably the best croissants we've ever tasted. The only negative I can say was that the breakfast service was too slow. But other than that, we had a top notch experience. Also, I normally stay in midtown but i wanted my daughter to experience the fun and excitement of staying in the heart Soho with all its great restaurants and shops, plus we wanted to be walking distance to the Village. We couldn't have been happier with our choice of hotels as it offered us that great downtown experience with all the luxuries of a top NYC hotel. I will most definitely stay here again.

“They Know How To Treat You...!” A couple of high school teachers sneaking away to our favorite vacation city, my wife and I darted off to the Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf in mid-November for our second visit (having stayed there at Christmas last year). The place was its usual wonderful self, although we did have one small complaint. While we were told this was temporarily specific to our room only, we still decided to write a letter when we got home. Within a week, we had a very gracious reply from Assistant General Manager Sean Haughey. He informed us the hotel engineers were investigating the issue with our room, but in the meantime, he wanted us to know a one-night complimentary stay certificate was in the mail to us. Guess who can hardly wait to get back to those wonderful folks who certainly know how to pamper you... at the Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf?

“Great staff but the hotel needs updating.” The staff was amazingly friendly and helpful from check in until check out. However, I felt the hotel facility itself disappointed me a bit and I was expecting more from a Doubletree. The entry was a small issue for me, being you walk into the main level but you had to take two separate elevators to get to your room (no direct elevator access from the main level to the room level). The hotel was actually two separate buildings molded into one, a newer building which is the front and an older building on the back. My room was located in the older portion and you could hear the creaking floor as soon as you crossed from newer to the older portion, and the noise from the floor wasn't any better in my room. The room was a good size and very clean but it was lacking on style and in need of renovations to replace old fixtures, carpet, fridge, and furniture. The internet worked great in the room for a charge of $12.95 a day per device, so that is $25.90 for the internet on your phone and computer. The location was very close to the Tufts Medical Train stop on the Orange line. Directly outside of the hotel was the Tufts Medical campus which surrounded the Doubletree hotel. It didn't provide for the cosmopolitan city scene some people might me looking for but you can definitely walk to a posh area within 5-10 minutes. The hotel was secure at night and you have to use your room key card to gain access to the lobby. Lucky for me I only paid $70 a night by bidding on Priceline.com. I would stay here again if I got a great bargain but I would not pay the published rates due to the lack of value I saw during my stay.

“Need a hotel? Don't be silly, stay here when you go to Philly!” We had the opportunity to stay here for 4th of July weekend when we were in town to see the Mets play the Phillies. Staff: Valet and front door staff was very friendly when I parked my car and every time I left the building. Additionally, they always said “welcome back” when we came back to the hotel. Concierge staff greeted my every time I got off the elevator from the entry. The lady who checked me in was wonderful...very warm, friendly and sincere. Facilities: The hotel has an odd setup, where there is a motor lobby where you enter, then you take an elevator up to the lobby. The lobby area is somewhat small but it’s functional. The common areas are decorated nicely in muted grays and earth tones. The gym on the 4th floor is nice, with good machines, free weights and stretching equipment. The room was a nice size with a king bed, desk, arm chair and flat screen television. Some people rave about the “Heavenly Bed” but I thought it was just okay. Didn’t sleep real well on it. Plus, on a king size bed there were only 4 pillows and in a lot of other hotels, they give you more pillows on a king bed. The bathroom was great and I think their products such as soap and shampoo are really nice. My hair felt great after the shampoo and the soap smelled good. Highlights: The Mets were staying in the same hotel and I saw radio announcer Howie Rose in the lobby and ran into David Wright as he was getting out of an elevator and I was getting onto it. Nothing could top seeing David Wright in person, even though this was just after a game where he missed a pretty simple pop up (apparently he thought Alex Cora had called for it, so he’s forgiven!) Also, the location for this hotel is perfect...very close to both subway lines, within walking distance of parkway museums and terrific dining options near Rittenhouse Square. Areas for improvement: Other than providing more pillows for the bed, I can’t think of anything. I could have called for more pillows, but didn’t bother to do so. Overall impression: I’m a Hilton Honors member so I usually stay in Hilton branded hotels, but couldn’t get a room on short notice for the 4th of July weekend, so decided to try the Westin. I have to say, it makes me reconsider being so loyal to the Hilton brand, especially after my displeasure with the Hilton Palmer House in Chicago (see my review of that). I had a great stay here and thought the staff really delivered a consistently high level of service. Maybe I should join the Starwood points program. Nearby transportation: Two blocks from the subway/trolley lines. One stop on the subway to the 30th Street train station if you’re taking the Amtrak into town. Philly is very walkable and this location, only two blocks from City Hall is very centrally located.

“Large rooms and great service” I recently stayed at the Affinia Dumont for 3 nights. I selected this hotel based on the recommendation of a colleague who hosted a meeting there and based on the incredibly affordable rate we were able to get. The hotel itself is located in Murray Hill area of midtown east. Though it is not necessarily the most touristy area with loads of fantastic restaurants, the hotel's location is within walking distance of more populous areas. We walked up to Times Square which was about 7 blocks or so. The staff at the hotel was attentive and polite. Room service is served from the on-site restaurant, the Barking Dog, and while it certainly isn't 4 star quality, it was ok and really inexpensive in comparison with most NYC hotels. The rooms are exceptionally large with a small kitchen. I was in a King Studio Suite and could have easily fit a pack and play in this room without compromising walking space. MOst importantly, my room was impeccably clean. I will certainly consider this hotel again in the future.

“Not a great hotel” I am working in Memphis four days a week for the last six months. My company forces me to stay at this property. It is not great. It really depends week to week what kind of stay I will have. Now I am Gold with Hilton Honors so sometimes I get a great room. However, when I was just Silver the rooms were really bad. Below floor three. The floors were really dirty. I always bring slippers. The staff turns over weekly. I have yet to see the same front desks staff. They do not know the area well. I do know alot of airline personnel stay at the place. It is less than a block from my client so that is nice. Workout rooms is ok. Standard for a Hampton Inn or that line of hotel not a Doubletree. Has the window units. Which can be loud. I am sure there are better places to stay in Memphis. I just am not allowed to look.

“Good value if your timing is right” I recently spent a long weekend at the Hard Rock with family. We managed to get pretty reasonable pricing on a pair of Platinium Double Queen rooms at 150 per night. For the area and the size of the room it just couldnt be beat. We were a block away from the bean and the nicer parts of Chicago. The beds were quite comfortable, the bathroom was huge, and the view wasnt spectacular but looking down on busy Michigan Ave wasnt too bad. We ordered room service one day, it was kind of expensive as most room service tends to be. With a jug of coffee, a one person breakfast crept up to 50.00. Check-in was pretty effortless, and prompt. One of our rooms was on the lower floors (4) with the China Grill private party area nearby. This would normally be a bad idea as you'd get alot of the ambient noise, but the Hard Rock did its homework and has an extra set of glass doors on that floor before entering the rooms area so the noise was non-existent even with a function going on. Michigan Ave is a fairly busy road, so if ambient noise from outside bothers you, I'd say pick a different hotel. We didnt mind it because we liked the energy of busy Chicago below, but if youre a light sleeper it might be an issue. On checkout, we had a slight issue with a can of redbull that we took out of the minifridge to make room for some milk we had left over from the convenience store. They had originally charged us for the redbull (8 dollars). But they quickly removed it when i brought it up that we didnt drink it. The people behind me had a similar complaint so I assume its pretty common. It might be one of those pressure sensitive minibars that senses when somethings been moved. Definately skip the minibar, its way expensive and theres limitless convenience stores and establishments all around there. The sale rate we got was kind of hidden online. If you goto their site the default rate is labeled as The best rate, but there are specials underneath that drop down that are actually better rates. So the term 'best rate' is kind of decieving. All in all, it was a pleasureable experience and I was pleased with the value of this hotel.

“A nice respite in the rain” I had wanted to stay in the property closest to the White House and was upset when I got there to realize my reservation was at this property. I was tired. Driving all night in the rain. Had an early morning meeting and I just wanted to get off the road. After having trouble finding it due to awful direction from the bellman at the first property, I called and they talked me in. All that said. Yes, it was pricey given the distance away from where I thought I'd be starting from in the morning. ($476 with parking). However, the staff knew I was having a hard time and greeted me warmly. Promised me a nice stay and delivered. I was put in a very nice room. (the hotel just opened 6 months ago I was told). It is a very nice space. Nice bedding and bed. Nice amenities. Very nice space. Lots of window. Only problem was trying to get my car in the morning. I was on a tight timeline and they missed the time I requested by 20 minutes. Created more stress than I needed that morning but otherwise, a very nice property.

“Great Stay in San Antonio” Just getting around to writing my reviews... Stayed at this hotel in July and it was quite and enjoyable experience. The service level of this property is exceptional. Our room was on the club level and had an excellent view of the city. Room was spacious and modern. Great location right off the river walk. Just a short walk to the heart of all the action. Would definately stay here again. Parking was pricey, but that seems to be the norm in downtown San Antonio.

“Nice property right on the mile.” Stayed here after getting stranded in Chicago last month. The rooms are nice...clean and current. The restaurant had a nice beer selection and a great burger! Will definately look here next time I'm headed to Chicago

“A great stopover” An unexpectedly high quality hotel, directly attached to the Delta terminal so you don't have to take a shuttle. There's a security checkpoint from the hotel back into the terminal, making getting to your gate quick. Delta has a check-in kiosk in the hotel lobby, along with a monitor with flight information. The hotel is quite new and with a dramatic, multi-story atrium lobby that has a large water feature -- very attractive. The room was very well appointed, including the ubiquitous 50" flat screen LCD TV. The bathroom had 14" marble squares on the floor and lining all four walls up to the ceiling. The workman who installed the marble was a true craftsman. Every seam was perfect. The restaurant is rather pricey but the food quality is good. If you're on a budget, much better to eat in the terminal before you enter the hotel. This is a great spot for an overnight on your way from one place to another, particularly if you're from the west coast and want to connect to a flight to Europe. Much better to sleep in a bed and have shorter flights rather than taking an 11-12 hour direct flight from LAX to LHR.

“Old and Tired Looking” During a recent business trip the Westin was fully booked and we tried the Marriott in the alternative. It is seriously in need of a makeover and the hotel services could be much improved. Everything was clean and the bed comfortable but the decor is tired and old. I had a problem with my two hotel phones not working and in the 4 days I was there they were unable to fix it with repeated calls to the front desk. I was charged for internet usage even though I had no computer (they promptly removed the charge when brought to their attention). My colleague used the internet in her room ($9.95 a day) and said it was painfully slow. No wireless in the hotel rooms only in the conference rooms. Housekeeping did not remove room service trays promptly (7:30am breakfast was still sitting outside my room at 4pm). And breakfast trash was not removed from my room at all. Savannah red, the hotel restaurant was a disappointment. Delicious fresh salads but really boring and bland entrees (we tried the Shrimp and Grits, Chicken, and pork chops). Also the "Starbucks" in the hotel lobby does not taste like Starbucks. The hotel was very helpful with shipping out boxes but they have no fed-ex account so remember to bring your own with you. A perfectly convenient location and if you don't care about looks a fine place to stay. But the service could use with an upgrade too.

“Wonderful Oasis” My traveling companion had stayed at The Edison a few times. So for this trip I took her at her word that this was the place to stay. She was so right. The price was right. The room, though a bit worn, was large and clean. The hotel is used mostly by Europeans, but we felt right at home. It the heart of the theater district we were a very short walk from most shows, which was are main reason for being there. There are places to eat right on the premises.The Edison Cafe, great for breakfast and lunch. And the Sophia. As for The Sophia, the food was fine, but there are many other more friendly places to eat. Also The Rum bar was a wonderful place to relax and listen to the lounge singer. We had two double beds and were quite comfortable. Don't expect fancy furnishings or a large bathroom. And things look a bit worn. But for the money.... and location,this a clean wonderful place.

“loved the Plaza” Had a great time at the Plaza. Recently renovated, the building is gorgeous. The lobby is spectacular. Its an old bank skyscraper. Checkin was easy. Staff was better than average. Elevators are very fast. Had a room on the 9th floor. View was ok. THe room was great!!! On the small side, but the bed was very comfortable (except the sheets- they seemed worn already, and pilled).
