Room had an LCD TV, fridge, and microwave. Small desk. Great bathroom! Hotel is on the riverwalk. Had no problems with safety.

“Wonderful Location and Room” I just returned from a 3 night stay at the Monticello Inn for a long weekend in San Francisco. Having stayed within the Kimpton chain in San Francisco previously, I had a high expectation for service that was met by all staff members I came in contact with. When I arrived, I was immediately greeted at the door and they made quick arrangements for my car to be parked (note that parking is $33 per day plus tax, which I knew about before hand and chose to pay on this trip). Since I arrived around 1 pm, I did not expect my room to be ready, but it was! This was an added bonus. I had reseved a king room with a AAA rate, but was upgraded to a suite. The suite was on the 4th floor facing the courtyard and was great. It was two rooms, with an incredibly comfortable bed and a nice sitting area in the "living room". The hotel also has free wireless internet access throughout as well as complimentary coffee service in the morning and a wine reception in the afternoon. The Monticello's location cannot be beat. My wife and I love walking around San Francisco, and from its location a block from the cable car terminus at Powell and Market, it cannot be beat. We did not try the restaurant at the hotel, but the menu and decor looked very nice.

“Doesn't live up to "Resort" status.” First impressions are pretty good... hotel looks nice from the outside and the common areas are attractive. The room itself is dissapointing. The good: attractive lobby, proximity to Seaworld, proximity to food and shopping (as long as you have a car... there's a new complex about 2 miles S/E of the hotel off of the 151 fwy). Nightly free (albeit old) movies were shown on a wall near the pool area, and the open fire pits were nice. The bad: The room was extremely plain (a standard Holiday Inn is fancier). The bedding was uncomfortable, and everything was old and worn out. We paid a $25 "upgrade" fee for a room with 2 beds... this was the only difference from our "standard" room... 99% of hotels do not distinguish between rooms with one or two beds on pricing (to the contrary I mostly hear about folks who are on a romantic get-away who are dissapointed to be assigned a room with 2 beds instead of one King size bed). Worst part was each day we noticed black spotted stains on the bathroom sink, which I would clean with wet towels... the morning of our last night there I saw about 2 dozen tiny black bugs crawl out of the sink (which I killed)... then a couple of hours latter "yellow" mystery water with black solids in it backed into the sink, when the water fianlly drained the black residue was left behind (GROSS!!!!!!!). This was on the morning of our check-out... I showed pictures of this to the front desk and was able to get our "upgrade" fee removed (had to ask for it though, nothing was offered)... this was the only reason I didn't give it a 1 out of 5 rating. Also, decent parking was often hard to come by. Other: The pool area was attractive... but only marginally better than a standard mid-grade hotel... by no means anything extraordinary, and was by-far the lamest "resort" pool we've ever seen. A normal "resort" pool area would be no less than double the size of this one. Free shuttle to Seaworld was offered and I was told it ran every 30 minutes... we didn't use this service though (only being a mile or two away we prefer to be able to come and go as we please). If the rooms could match the common areas this could be a pretty nice place... as it stands I was dissapointed.

“Wonderful Stay” Stayed two nights at this hotel during a recent business trip. Hotel is located close to the airport, and the room was very nice. Fruit platter/yogurt was excellent and room service was delivered within 15 minutes. Breakfast bar the following morning was also fantastic. My only complaint dealt with a housekeeping issue when I discovered a pubic hair in the tub, and that my car rental program was not credited on my folio. After an e-mail to the GM this was credited, and on my next stay the housekeeping issue was corrected. The walls are a bit paper thin, because I can hear the businessman next door speaking loud with his crew, but overall right place, location and the staff do care about their guests. I would return in the future.

“Right in the heart of it all!” This hotel was a pleasant surprise. Bring in the heart of Times Square, I had doubts... I thought it might be noisy or trashed or crowded. It was none of those things. And the things that were there impressed me. Between 41st and 42nd Streets (between Seventh and Eight), the location couldn’t be better. Restaurants galore within a blocks walk. Theaters, nightlife, bars, etc. all around. My room was very pleasant. Clean and modern and ultra comfy. I had a desk with two chairs plus a club chair with an ottoman. I would stay here again for sure!

“Sometimes being cool isn't cool enough!” The relaxed and informal easy-going attitude of the reception staff has gone a bit further. Firstly, they chat with each other in a loud voice behind the reception curtain and leave guests stranded and eagerly waiting for their conversation to end to get assistance. Then, they show up, preauthorize an extra USD 500 on the credit card without notifying the guest; who given an aggressive answer "every hotel has its own policy" . The over-doing act of having to present a photo ID for every transaction or even when accessing the room is very annoying.

“Pretty Good” This is clearly an older hotel - not one of the newer Garden Inns that you seen by airports and interstate exits. So the rooms are small and the carpet pretty worn. There was mildew on the grout in the shower. But the beds and pillows were comfortable and staff was friendly. There's no free breakfast, but the breakfast in the hotel restaurant was reasonably priced and good quality. There is free parking at a lot across the street. The pool area is gorgeous. Overall, a good option if you need to stay in downtown Phoenix.

“Great Hospitality from the Start” As my usual, I was here on business and the hotel was located conveniently located to where I was working. When I first arrived, I was greeted with a smiling front desk person and warm cookies with lemonade. They also had some appetizers in the reception area. My entire stay was delightful. The rooms were great. You should get a good night's sleep as I did. Decent gym. You will need a car as not much is in walking distance. The downtown area is only about a 15 minute drive. I experienced wonderful customer service and will stay again.

“Good location near the convention center-kind of run down though” This is a PRIME location if you are in town for an event at the convention center. However, if you are just visiting....I can't imagine that there aren't better choices. No mini bar, run-down rooms, no view, bar/restaurant that is connected doesn't offer any wine other than dime store sugar water. Bad lighting! However, it is very clean.

“Boston Westin” Stayed at this hotel because it was connected to the Convention Center. Nice modern hotel, but a bit away from the core of Boston. So you will need either to hoof it about 1 mile plus or take a cab. Great, new, modern and clean hotel. So if you are going to a conference, I'd plan on staying at this place since its so convenient, but be forewarned that it books up pretty fast for conferences.

“Great value and location” We love the location, away from the 6th street crowd and yet just a short drive downtown and to Walmart and many restaurants nearby. Hotel and rooms are clean. Even though we were there during the Labour day weekend and the hotel was packed, it was still very quiet and breakfast was well stocked. Could see a lady working very hard to ensure breakfast items were duly replenished and place kept clean. All day coffee and hot chocolate in the lobby was a hit. Bonus: Complimentary breakfast and free internet. Free parking too. Good value for money.

“Very Nice” This is a very nice Hilton property in the University district of Philadelphia...but only a 10 minute drive to the historic areas near downtown. The hotel has a charming art deco feel, and the room was large, clean, and nicely decorated. I love the white down comforters I've seen at the last few Hiltons I've stayed in. It's very easy to see how clean they are (which is always nice in light of the occasional television news reports that remind us what DNA-encrusted nightmares most hotel bedspreads are), and (lest you think they are stark) they are dressed up with a rich looking coverlet that you can remove at bedtime. We had a very comfortable king-sized bed, a large armoire with television, minibar, a very roomy desk w/ office chair, and a sitting chair w/ ottoman. The bathroom was also roomy, and had plenty of counterspace surrounding the single sink, a standard tub, and shower. Plush bathrobes were also provided, which were very cozy and must've weighed 20 lbs. apiece. Coffee in the room was a better-than average brand, and real creamers were provided...a nice touch. Godiva chocolates, bottled water, and a fresh bag of ice were delivered at turndown time. There was not mini-fridge in the room, but they are available at no charge upon request...one was delivered to us within 10 minutes after a quick call to the front desk. One of the nicest things about the hotel was the service. All staff members we encountered, from concierge to valet parking attendants, were highly professional, very courteous, friendly, and helpful. Another thing I loved was the quiet. The sound-dampening must be very good in the hotel, because I never heard a sound at night...either from the adjacent rooms and hallway or the streets below. There's a small, cozy lounge in the hotel, which is where breakfast is also served every morning. We did not try either, but did go to the hotel's attached wine bar and restaurant (Penne Restaurant and Wine Bar) one night. We found the wine-by-the-glass selection there to be limited and overpriced, and the menu selections uninspiring, so we moved on. The only negative experience occurred when the housekeeping staff failed to close our door completely after servicing the room. one day. Nothing was taken, but it was a bit unnerving to return to the hotel in the early evening to find our door slightly ajar. I recommend this hotel for its service, comfort, and attractive decor...but at rates of approximately $200+ per night along with valet parking charges of $27/day (there is no self-parking on the property, or anywhere nearby that I could see), you will pay for that.

“3 Star Hotel? Are you kidding me?” I'm speechless. I cannot even begin to express how shocked I am that TripAdvisor gave this hotel a 3 star class. From a straphanger who has stayed at some of the BEST hotels in the WORLD, the Hotel Giraffe is FOUR STARS. In New York, I have stayed at Le Parker Meridien and the New York Palace, two five star hotels that are without argument two of the best hotels in the city. Other hotels I've stayed at include the Westin Rio Mar in Puerto Rico, the Broadmoor in Colorado Springs, and the Atlantis in the Bahamas. I am ashamed that TripAdvisor gave this hotel 3 stars just because it is a very small, boutique style hotel and does not have all these bling features that are overhyped and overrated anyway. I'll start with the location. Some might criticize the location because it is not close to anything. WRONG! Union Square is less than a mile south. Amazing shopping on Madison is one block east, 5th Av is two blocks. And best of all, the Subway is two blocks north! TWO BLOCKS! And these are two short blocks, too, the ones that go north/south. It's also a very convenient and frequent subway. The (6) local train is very reliable, and it serves many important places. Want to go to Union Square? Two stops downtown. Want to walk across the Brooklyn Bridge? Seven stops downtown. Have some relatives in Brooklyn? Two stops to Union Square, then walk across the platform to the (4) express train to Brooklyn. Have Yankees tickets? Two stops uptown to Grand Central, then walk across the platform to the (4) express train to Yankee Stadium. Oh wait, am I forgetting something? Ah, yes, Times Square/Broadway: Two stops uptown to Grand Central, then transfer to the (7) or (S) to Times Square! How easy is that? But the location is just the start. I'll move on to the lobby. The Grande Lobby is nothing short of just that...grand. It is a wonderful lobby. Check in is easy and once your done just walk two steps and you're on your elevator to your room. So what if its not bustling? Is that a bad thing? Does this hotel get 3 stars just because it has a small, quiet, charming lobby? Plus, there's often a piano player, and there's free breakfast every morning with muffins and fresh fruit and refreshing coffee. If you think a lobby has to be packed and bustling, stay at one of those overpriced, small room Midtown tourist trap hotels where all the tourists ram into each other's rear ends, where all the true New Yorkers avoid, where you spend your entire trip waiting for an ELEVATOR. The Hotel Giraffe is so pleasant, elegant, and charming and even if you don't stay there, it is a wonderful place to relax and hang out after a long, exciting day in the city. Finally, the ROOMS. I can't say enough about the beds. These beds are SO COMFORTABLE. You tuck yourself under the sheets and an angel is waiting to greet you. And the rooms, while not big, are not so small that one can't easily make his way around the room and move from one side of the room to the other without touching the bed, regardless of how much he/she weighs. And if you pay a wee bit extra for a deluxe room, you get your own private balcony, which, if it is a nice, sunny day, is quite a privilege. And you get ALL THIS for LESS THAN $300! No, you're not seeing things. Less than $300. Talk about a bargain. This hotel should be charging in the mid $300 range, but hey, I'm not complaining. So if you're looking for a peaceful, charming boutique FOUR STAR hotel with a relatively large room with a bed from Heaven and possibly a private balcony and a lobby with free breakfast and music on any given day at any given time, all located two short blocks from a Subway station in a quiet, safe neighborhood at a bargain price, the Hotel Giraffe is for YOU! TripAdvisor, I request that you change the hotel class for the Hotel Giraffe from 3 stars to what it deserves i.e. 4 stars.

“Hotel is Great, Memphis is Desolate” The hotel itself is very modern and clean and has every expected amenity (but really, charging for WiFi is so ridiculous when Motel 6 gives it for free), and I guess you could say it is located perfectly. The problem is that there is nothing going on in Memphis. Beale St. is 1 or 2 blocks long -- step away from there and you're surrounded by huge swaths of vacant land/decrepit parking lots, or urban renewal-type shopping/parking complexes that are all vacant. Really depressing. So stay at the Westin, go to Graceland, Sun Studios, the Civil Rights Museum. Go see the duck march at the Peabody, then get out of town. It's a shame, because the buildings that remain on Main St. are very attractive and would make a great entertainment district if there were only people around. We had a problem with the electical outlets in our room (None of our white Apple plugs would stay plugged in, as if the outlets were too loose). We told the front desk, and in minutes engineering came and fixed them. The fitness center was nice, but the elliptical machine was completely unbalanced and was close to tipping over into the window. I told the front desk, so I hope they took it out, or had it repaired. Joan the concierge was very enthusiastic and helped us with directions several times!

“Meh--You can do better” The only real reason we stayed here was it was properly positioned (Columbus, OH; breaking our trip up in half) right off the interstate and had a larger room than most hotels allow (7 people). For the price of the room, we could have done better, I believe. It was an OK stay, but *not* one that I would repeat again. The room was more cramped than I expected and not as clean as one could have hoped for. There was a plastic fork on the floor when we arrived and the carpet was definitely older and needed replacing. The heating units worked but were difficult to get the temperatures right, long term. The breakfast was definitely of the run-of-the-mill ilk (waffles, cold items, along with something that was passed off as eggs and sausage---not edible by my standards, which are pretty accomodating). I went for the cold cereal. On the positive side, staff at the desk were very friendly and responsive to our request for additional towels. The beds also provided an excellent rest, which is the main reason we were there anyways.

“Interesting- Mixed Feelings about this one” This is a boutique type hotel but it still carries the Renaissance brand. Room was small and had some clear cigarette burn marks on the wood surface next to the window and on bedside table.... not what I would have expected in a hotel of this caliber. Overall room needs a good do-over (paint, varnish and some scrubbing). Location cannot be beat and even with issues is still better than many other NYC properties. Price was right compared to other hotels in vicinity but still feel this place needs a good clean and renovation.

“Service Outstanding, Facilities at a 4-star level.” I just want to highlight the excellent service from everyone here, which was above and beyond a normal 4-star hotel. The staff at breakfast was really pro, and I even saw the chef coming out to inspect the buffet and make the slightest changes. There is also a nice bar with good service, but it can't shake the business hotel bar vibe. The bellmen were happy to hail cabs, take luggage and provide directions with a smile. When I missed a bus to the convention center they rolled up the hotel car and drove me there. Outside of the great service, it is a stock 4-star hotel infrastructure. Rooms were very pleasant and clean though not remarkable. But it is distinguished by the people there. I enjoyed my stay.

“Not a great value- poor service” Hotel is attached to the convention center- the primary reason I stayed here. I would probably choose somewhere else next time. The hotel was fine. Beds were reasonably comfortable. Room was not especially clean and showed some wear. Needed to re-caulk tub, ceiling in bathroom was peeling, and some floor tiles were cracked. Internet was not free ($13/day) and room service ended at 10 PM- which made it difficult to get a late dinner. Unfortunately, some service issues made this stay unpleasant, and a poor value at $185/night (conference rate) The primary reason I would not recommend this hotel was the staff and customer service I received. In general, I did not feel welcomed- primarily felt like the staff was kind of annoyed to help you. Two issues: First, the morning of my departure, I discovered that someone (not me) had charged a dinner from the bar/restaurant to my room. At check-out at 6 AM (leaving for a flight) I asked that the bill be fixed, and was told that I had to wait while they searched for the receipt that someone had signed to my room. "Someone charged that to your room, so we have to find out who", with the implication that I was lying, and had forgotten or charged something to my room and was trying to get out of paying. Why I had to wait was unclear- if a customer says they didn't charge something to the room- the staff should just fix it, and apologize for the mistake. There should be no need for the aggrieved customer to wait around for 20 minutes while you go through every receipt from 3 days worth of restaurant charges. Secondly, when I was leaving (around 6:30 AM), I asked the bellman to call a taxi. He pointed us toward a fancy Cadillac Escalade, so I asked whether this was the standard $30 cab ride to the airport from both the bellman and driver. I was splitting the cab with 3 other travelers. Both the bellman and driver assured me it was. When we arrived at the airport the driver charged us $35 EACH- it should have been around $30 total for a regular cab. Clearly the bellman and this driver are scamming travelers together. Bottom Line- Not a good value, with unpleasant staff.

“Lovely hotel.” I haven't stayed at The Plaza since the early-mid 90's, but of course I know about all of the renovations, etc. It's not the same, but still very nice. You simply can't beat the location, in my opinion. It's walking distance to absolutely everything. My only complaint here is the staff. I can't say that they were all like this, but the people who I dealt with were very snooty. I felt like they were waiting for a tip just for saying "hello" to me. I didn't enjoy that part of my stay at all. I've stayed at the Waldorf, Four Seasons, and Inter-Continental... and The Plaza would honestly be at the bottom of that list. Although the location is wonderful, I'd give it up for a better atmosphere.

“Best overall deal in Dallas” This is my third stay here since the first of this year, so I'm comfortable with writing a strong positive review. This hotel is the old Sheraton (which I also stayed at some years ago) and MCM has done a great job remodeling it. There are a few very minor signs of age but the hotel more than makes up for it. Staff is great and well trained. Rooms are clean, beds are first-class as are the other furnishings (flat-screen TV, microwave, large frig, granite counters, bath fixtures). They do all the small things well also - good coffee mugs, real glasses, Starbucks coffee in the room. Pool area is clean and very well landscaped. Hot breakfast is one of the best I've had in the US - bacon, sausage, great scrambled eggs, pastries, fresh fruit, berries, cereals, pancakes, yogurt, etc., and it's included. Great prices as well, as they'll match online prices. For those who want more space, the rooms around the pool are small suites (they call them cabanas). I've seen them and they're very nice and not much more ($20 more a night ?). I think they sleep 4+. Tonight I checked in and noticed the microwave was missing. I called the front desk to let them know (didn't want them to think I'd stolen it !) and they had a new one up here in five minutes, and replaced the TV remote when I mentioned it was weak. The two guys that came up were super friendly and wouldn't accept the offered tip. Excellent location right off I-35 and NW highway, good restaurants just a few blocks west. I'd give it five stars but I save that ranking for the Dorchester in London. I've stayed at a ton of hotels in Dallas and won't stay anywhere but here in the future.

“great location” A very nice hotel with very friendly and helpful staff. Prices are much higher during Fashion week, like all hotels in the area. I would definitely stay here again, even if I don't care that Macy's is across the street.

“Wonderful hotel” The Hotel Vintage Park is a boutique hotel and is part of the Kimpton Hotels group, which are known for being lovely and eco-friendly too. I have stayed at a few other hotels in town, but this was by far one of the nicest for serveral reasons. I'm not a big fan of big chain hotels, but I do stay in them on occasions too. However, I prefer personable places that remember you when you come back. I had joined their club before we arrived, and though I had never been to a Kimpton hotel before, I was treated as though I was a regular. Special gifts in the room were just as I had ordered. Orgainc fruits, sparkling water, and chocolates, for my daughters as well as myself. When we showed up at the hotel, I was sick. I wasn't sleeping well and was keeping my family up at night with my coughing. When I spoke to the front desk about maybe getting another room on the same floor, I was easily accommodated, despite the fact the hotel was pretty full. They moved us to a higher floor so we could have rooms across the hall from each other. And even though the elevator was right next to my room, I never once heard any noise coming from the hall, the elevators, or the rooms next to me. I found out later from my sister that Paul Newman had stayed at this same hotel the week before I arrived. Now, we don't normally rub shoulders with the rich and famous, but it seems his taste for eco-friendly places are on a par with mine. And it wasn't too expensive either. Everything was great, though I agree their parking garage is expensive, but it is very protected too. There is free overnight parking on the streets after 6pm, but you have to out there by 7 or 8 am to get a parking permit if you plan to stay longer. Personally, after doing this one morning, I found I prefered spending a couple extra dollars was worth my extra hour of sleep. Wonderful morning coffee and teas. I never saw any food though in the mornings. We missed the wine hour and didn't get a chance to eat in the restaurant, as we were eating with family most of the time, or being tourists. I'll certainly stay here again, or one of the other Kimpton hotels in town, from now on.

“Love It, Very Convenient” Stayed for a month this past July for work and loved it. It is so close to the T and water taxi. The staff are professional, especially Dulce in the Executive Lounge she was very helpful. I recommend a corner room, you get more space and the views are great. The gym is great also, they have a sauna, steam room, Jacuzzi, and a nice pool. The bellman will tell you the right places to go and with a smile.

“Great hotel. Friendly staff.” We loved this hotel. The location was great ..... although my credit card did not like how close it was to Macy's (hehe). The staff were very friendly and always helpful. The free breakfast was really good. The room we had was great - two double beds and plenty of room. The only downside we can think of is that the bathroom was a bit on the small side ..... but it was more than adequate..

“If you have to stay in Lincoln Park - I guess The Willows will do” My husband and I stayed at The Willows for 5 nights this Dec. 04 b/c it was a few blocks from our daughter's apt. Be forwearned - their internet ad is MUCH nicer than the reality. It's centrally located if you want to stay in Lincoln Park - but it isn't a cute, boutique hotel, even though it advertises itself as one. The lobby was a bit shabby - and the free continental breakfast was fast-foodish, carb-laden, and recycled. We didn't eat it once. The hallways were long and narrow - not very inviting. I felt as if I were walking down an old-fashioned rooming house kind of place - not an inviting little hotel. The elevator was a small, old cage affair (cute in movies, not in real life). Our room was very 1950's - beige, dingy, and dark. We had twin beds, I think - not two queens. Our windows overlooked a parking lot which had an all-night light that shined and made loud noises (so I wore ear plugs and kept the shades down). The bathroom was large - clean - and the products were replenished daily. We could hear someone practicing her flute down the hall - and people having sex in a room above us. The people next door had small kids - which we could hear clearly through the walls. Our TV was small - but hooked up to cable. There wasn't a closet - just an old armoire. I checked out the Days Inn a few blocks away - and The Willows was definitely better - but it wasn't a great, charming, adorable place by any stretch of the imagination.

“Wonderfully Surprised” I had to travel to Denver on business and this hotel fit within the budget. I was a bit disappointed that it wasn't downtown, but I had a car and the distance to downtown and other areas of interest wasn't an issue. In fact, there seemed to be a lot of families who also chose to stay here. The room was big and clean and nicely furnished, although the tv's could stand to be updated to flat screens. My only complaint was that the mattress was too soft for my taste. The breakfast with the made to order omelets was great, and the happy hour in the evenings for guests was a great touch. My co-workers and I enjoyed sharing a few free drinks at the end of the work day. Overall the staff was very helpful and friendly. But there was one gentlemen at the desk who seemed like he didn't want to be bothered (because he didn't want to look up from his computer screen) when I asked him the hotel address so I could give it to a friend who was coming to visit. Despite this, the hotel stay was very nice.

“Great place for an extended stay!” Stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown by the Canal for three weeks. I would not hesistate to stay at this hotel if you're in Indianapolis for extended period of time. The staff really goes out of their way to make you feel at home. The hotel is located conveniently downtown (you are within walking distance from many restaurants and the Circle Center shopping Center), near the free bus routes and cabs are easy to get from the location as well. I was really impressed by the amenities offered: a more than adequate free full breakfast (that included hot items like eggs and sausage) the free wifi throughout the hotel, as well access to a color printer and computer in the lobby. While I didn't use the service, there is a free grocery delivery service available (they just charge the actual price of the groceries on your list to your room bill). My room, located on the second floor by the elevator, was clean and pretty spacious. The only problem I had with the hotel would be the elevator--while there are only 4 floors...it is super slow. Take the stairs instead! All in all it was a great stay.

“Great New OSU Area Hotel” Company booked me downtown, but I opted for this brand new university area hotel. I've always been a huge fan of the HGI brand for business travel and this new location does not disappoint. I found all of the standard HGI amenities to be in place. Two free bottles of water at check-in and free internet access. Additionally I liked that they had new HDTV's with HD signals. The room rates were fair, and I would definitely stay again. AC POWER: Plentiful, next to bed and at desk BATHROOM: Very clean, very comfortable BEDDING: Comfortable bedding, plenty of sheets, blankets CLEANLINESS: Very clean, brand new INTERNET: Free wifi and cat 5 connections, decent speeds, and web based printing to business center LOBBY: Large, wecloming, includes restaurant, fireplace and plenty of seating for one-on-one impromptu meetings PARKING: Large, well lit, free parking STAFF: Extremely friendly and accomodating TELEVISION: Widescreen LCD panel with Digital HDTV signals, all the local affiliates as well as ESPN HD. WATER PRESSURE: Sufficient

“Decent” I stayed at the Shelburne mid-February and found it to be a very decent value. I was impressed by the size of room itself (booked a one-bedroom suite), location, and price. I do agree that the hotel needs a major upgrade. If you happen to care about service (doorperson, etc.), this is not the place for you. I care mostly about noise level (hearing people in the next room or in the halls) and was happy that I could not hear anything. Of course I could hear the honking cars and street noise (up on the eleventh floor) but as a former New Yorker, it felt like home to me - you screen it out. Yes, the carpets and bedspread were a bit nasty, but aren't they all? The bathrooms were tiny but I've seen worse. An upgrade will do well for the hotel but of course it won't be as affordable. The hotel is in an excellent location - very central (not for food choices - restuarants in area geared towards frat boys and tourists, but for transportation). If you can get a decent price (under $200.00 for one-bedroom suite), I highly recommend the Shelburne. If you pay much over that ($300 and up) I wouldn't do it.

“Swanky Digs in Westwood” Located on a small residential street in upscale Westwood, the W's exterior is low key....but that is certainly where the low key ends. The lobby is quite swank, and you can tell immediately who the hotel chain caters to....the affluent hipsters of the universe. We stayed in a mini-suite, which felt like a small 1 bedroom apartment with no kitchen. We had requested a non-smoking room and were unfortunate enough to receive a room that reeked of smoke (and had an ashtray in the armoire), so when you stay here, remember that lots of "hip" persons still smoke and will do so in non-smoking rooms. Amenities were upscale (Bliss toiletries, magnified make-up mirror, cd player clock radio) and the rooms were quiet, but if you're there on a weekend, be forewarned that the bar downstairs is PACKED, smells like incense and is nearly impossible to get service in.... it's very popular with patrons and locals alike. I LOVED the "beetle juice" hallways, and running into familiar faces (like Thom Filicia from Queer Eye). This is a great hotel for people who thrive on hip, stylish surroundings and hanging with similar people....a beautiful place for beautiful people. ,

“Third Time Not a Charm” We had stayed at this Courtyard twice before and had been pleased. This time not so much. As others have said the location is excellent as is the free parking. It is close to Rice University, the medical complex, the museum district and the Rice Village entertainment and shopping district. The access to Highway 59 is also easy. Our room was quite and the flat-screen TV had a good channel lineup. However, The room felt damp and clammy. The air conditioner's fan ran all the time and was difficult to adjust. Housekeeping was disappointing in that we were not furnished fresh towels nor was coffee replaced. The high-speed wired internet was not so speedy. Don't expect a free breakfast as this is a profit center. We visit Houston at least once a year but next time we'll find other lodging.

“Great location but needs more pool!” We stayed at this zhilton property because it was close to the light rail so we could get to Chase Field without having to drive. We enjoyed the room with the separate living and bed rooms, but the parking garage got us all mixed up one morning! The breakfast buffet was standard but the staff was very friendly and accommodating. We would have like to use the pool, but it was always overrun with kids and large groups. Oh well. Overall, we would return to this hotel if we stay in Phoenix again.

“good solid hotel” bid Priceline $39 per night plus fees. Read that there is a $16 charge for parking, parked about six blocks away near a ASU offsite building. Meters work 9am to 5pm, other times appear free. Checkin was easy, up to the room, seem to be remodeled in the last ten years. Nothing special, but nothing bad either. The pool and fitness center were next to each other. Fitness center had newer machines with video, free weights are nil except for some dumb bells. Water cooler, towels and headsets are provided, 24 hour access. I asked the desk person if there was a drugstore within walking distance, he replied no, but a Circle K was within a 10 minute walk. I would not walk in the dark for 10 minutes near downtown, I would suggest the same to you. The bagel store in the lobby was open and overpriced, but convenient. I scored another parking space on the street the next evening, three block walk. The hotel was busy with a convention going on. Bar and restaurant in the lobby and also across the street. There was a breakfast place, First Watch, about one block away towards First Street. I had a good stay.

“Good Hotel for staying and for those who love planes” It is a convenient hotel for those who need to transit in LAX. Front desk agents, house keepers were nice and willing to help. The room was really good to stay, roomy and sleep number bed was awesome. In room TV was fancy, showing my name on screen. For those love planes, it is a good place, since you can watch planes landing one by one to LAX, from regional jet to big jumbo... Now comes to the bad part: too many charge items... Only valet parking is available...$25 per night and actually you need to pay more...such as tips.. right? Breakfast was $19 per person. The room didn't equipped with water and no electric kettle but irony it has coffee maker... I don't know how I can make coffee without hot water.. The front desk agent confirmed no drinking water was provided in room. There were a 4sq promotion saying if you submit a tip or take a photo for this hotel and you will get 1000 club carlson points after showing to front desk agent.. I did this after my check out.. But till now I am still waiting for my points showing up in my account....

“Business Travel” I had fairly low expectations of this hotel based on some of the previous reviews. I was pleasantly surprised by the friendly staff and the good service I received throughout my stay. My check-in was a breeze and I was given a corner room with a nice view of the harbor. While the room itself was fairly bland, it was comfortable, clean and overall pleasing to my very particular taste. I agree that the location is not ideal for a tourist, but for a business traveler, the location is quite good. Overall, I had a good experience.

“Characterful and quirky” No one could accuse the Tabard Inn of being a monolithic chain hotel. Instead it is a collection of quirky rooms, narrow staircases up and down, and a lovely restaurant. Not a bad place to stay at all - and very reasonable rates for D.C. I paid USD210 per night in a room with a private bathroom (they also offer cheaper deals with shared facilities). The room itself was huge with lots of antique-looking and rather lovely furniture. The free wifi and breakfast were nice touches - the noise from the bar one floor below and the lack of good lighting and a shower screen less so.

“Excellent hotel” Had a wonderful 6-night stay at the Sofitel Washington DC and this is certainly one of DC's best hotels: The location is central, the hotel staff is attentive and helpful, food excellent, rooms well equipped, and lots of nice, attentive touches during my stay such as a welcome gift awaiting me in my room upon arrival. Also, the atmosphere in the lobby, restaurant, and bar area is cool and chic while being welcoming and relaxed at the same time. My only qualm was that the hotel automatically adds a tip to restaurant bills and I ended up double tipping on my bills during the first days of my stay until I asked a waiter what the "sc" charge on my bill stood for. In any case, given that many guests are not from the US, this all seems reasonable but it would be great if this all could be communicated a bit more clearly... As said however, this was a minor issue and I will not hesitate to choose this hotel again for my next visit to DC.

“Will stay here again” I usually find the Hyatt Regency hotels to be a bit cold (Think Mel Brooks "High Anxiety" - this is the hotel where it was filmed). However, the friendly staff made this a hotel I will return to. It helped that I could enter the hotel at the stree level and avoid the vertigo inducing lobby. It was convenient to my office (I was on a business trip) and it would be very convenient for tourists, as well.

“Well located hotel with large rooms, but Breakfast can loose you precious time...” This is a very comfortable hotel, well located for tourists, being close to shopping like Saks 5th Ave and more. Also for business executives, I like the large luxurious sized rooms, especially in the heart of Manhattan - NY. One real painful experience is having breakfast at the hotel. The queue's are painfully very long and if you are in NY for business, you will lose valuable time, and may end walking away from breakfast. If you are on a vacation, you will spend valuable time of your morning waiting for a table. The funny fact is that there re many tables vacant, just the cleaning, and seating seems a painfully slow process. I had to skip my breakfast as the queue's were too long. Otherwise, friendly staff and comfortable rooms.

“Short Weekend with Siblings” First off, the hotel rooms are pretty big for NYC. They come with a cute little kitchen that we did not end up using. There is a great little spot for brunch, "The Barking Dog", that is part of or adjacent to the hotel. The service staff (housekeeping and bell hops) was fantastic. We stayed in two different rooms over our 2 night stay. Our first room was absolutely amazing! It was the biggest room that I have stayed in NYC. It was a junior deluxe corner suite and had the best view of the NYC skyline. The space included a nice sitting area and desk. One drawback was the TV. It was an old fashioned tube TV that was difficult to swivel. In a room like that I was expecting a nicer TV. Most nicer hotels have flat screens now, but who goes to NYC to watch TV. The bed was very comfortable. Our second room, unsurprisingly, was a bit of a let down. We made last minute reservations and weren't able to book 2 consecutive nights in the same room. The second room was much smaller and didn't have much of a view. It also wasn't as clean as the other room. In terms of location, the hotel is great and within walking distance of many attractions.

“Not Bad, Not Bad At All!” A quirk in air reservations caused me to schedule a layover in Chicago. I'm really glad I chose this place - first it's about a two minute walk from baggage claim to their front door. At check-in I found the staff extremely friendly and anxious to help. The rooms, typical for a Hilton, were clean and comfortable. The only negative I can say about this place is that one must be tolerant of the occasional take-off -- but it's not like you didn't know it was going to occur! A very nice place - and definitely one I am keeping on my A-list.

“GAVE AWAY MY ROOM AND NEARLY RUINED MY TRIP” My mother just turned 55 and for her birthday my father and I purchased tickets for our family to attend the Texas - Oklahoma football game in Dallas. She is one of the biggest University of Texas fans and on her list of things to do before she dies, this was number 8. Hotels generally sell out early and cost was a huge concern given the high price of tickets so I had booked us reservations for two rooms at the Aloft Dallas on August 18th. Then I noticed that they disappeared out of my account and so I decided to call and see what the deal was. No one could explain how my reservations were lost and since they had no record of them, they refused to honor them. I was only offered to book at the current rate, which was higher at that point and there were no longer any suites available. All I was able to book was a King room for two nights using points, but I had to book another room at another hotel because the Aloft didn't have any suites or two double bed rooms available. I then called a week before my stay to make sure they had my new reservation. The woman at the front desk and the manager both basically called me a liar, saying that if I had made a reservation online they would have it. I had to call the national reservations number and have them e-mail the hotel a copy of my reservation before they believed me. The manager said he'd call me back after he received the e-mail, but never did. He was then unavailable when I called again, but this time they had my reservation on file, so I didn't press it. So now the day arrives. After a full day of flying, I arrived at the Aloft hotel a little before midnight. I walked up to the desk, and was immediately told that they have no more rooms available, and they'll try to get me into another hotel. So after calling numerous times to confirm, they still screwed it up. I was extremely upset, as was my entire family. I am a platinum preferred guest and should not have my room given away, EVER. After I sat at the desk for 45 minutes while they called hotels in the area, I told them I hadn't eaten and was going to walk to get some food and if they could call me immediately when they have it figured out. After about 25 minutes, the manager called and said that he has a room at a Hyatt Place and for me to come by the hotel for the paperwork. I inquire as to the location of the hotel and he tells me it is in FORT WORTH, which is 30 miles away!!!! The game was at 11am in the morning and traffic is horrible so this was unacceptable, not to mention I didn't even have a car. He then said he could put me Irving which was a less atrocious 17 miles away. Hardly comparable as the entire reason to stay downtown is to be able to take the DART to the game and to avoid gameday traffic. Since I didn't have a car I couldn't have even gotten to Fort Worth or the game so I told him that I didn't want to stay in Fort Worth or Irving and that I would have to make alternate accomodations on my own. He said they would try to fit me in the next day, but after making alternate plans I called the next day to let them know not to even bother. Three things really upset me about this situation. When I arrived, the woman at the desk mentioned that a woman earlier had nearly threatened to kill her because they gave away her room and she appreciated me being cordial to her because she of course had nothing to do with reservations. This upset me because it shows that they KNEW about this problem much earlier and did NOTHING to try to make alternate plans for me until I got there. It's clear they were basically hoping people didn't show up so they could avoid the problem. How hard would it have been to call me when they realized the problem to give me a heads up and to let me know they were working on it? Secondly, I was never offerred any sort of compensation nor have I received an apology call or e-mail since the incident. This upsets me even more because not only should they have been working on this problem from the second they realized it (I'm positive they could have fixed it because the person right in front of me was booked into a hotel right down the road) they didn't even care enough to try to appease me after I showed up. I expected, at the least, two complimentary nights at the hotel to be used whenever I returned to town in addition to having my points refunded for the stay. Neither of which has happened yet. Thirdly, throughout the entire situation, I was treated like I was an enormous hassle for them and that I was being ridiculous and difficult for being upset about being offered a hotel in Fort Worth. This was the best they could they said. This is a lie because they should have been trying to fix this problem hours before. The lobby was clean from what I could tell, but I was never able to see a room, because someone else was sleeping in it. TERRIBLE HOTEL AND HORRIBLE MANAGER.

“Worth every penny!” This is our second stay at the Inn at the Market. Perfect in every way! Pros: Location, location, location! Roof top deck is amazing with amazing views! Clean. Amazingly comfortable beds! Close to many bus lines and the LINK to SeaTac. Cons: None that I can think of!

“Stayed Here Because of Location & Breakfast is Included” Stayed in the Best Western recently for 7 nights & the main reasons for choosing this hotel was its location and even though the rate was similar to some 4* hotels close by this hotel supplied breakfast.It always seems much more convenient to have breakfast included when staying more than a couple of days. The self serve breakfast was well stocked with choice of cereals ,breads,fruit ,juices,scrambled egg ,sausage, tea/coffee & waffle makers.Just to be fussy I would have loved some bagels & cheese. Location is bang in the centre of the historical district ,only 5 minutes from the visitors centre and No1 stop for hop on hop off tour buses. There is an huge number of restaurants & bars within walking distance & even though it is not the classiest area of the city many of the top expensive restaurants are situated close to the hotel. We booked a King room room and was glad I did because the Queen rooms are quite compact. The decor in the room was fine but nothing special ,slightly dated but the hotel is obviously trying to match its historic status.Our room was on the second floor and you could definetly hear all movement in the room above which may annoy some guests.Also my biggest gripe was the inefficent heating in our room ,it is an in wall blow heater with a loud fan which we needed to keep on through the night as it was quite cold for December and it was difficult to achieve comfortable temperatures. The hotel is within walking distance of the city centre stores such as Maceys but there is an excellent bus system with a drop off point just beside the hotel ,single journey each way is just $2.00. All in all this is a quite good 3 star hotel but dont expect any luxuries.

“very nice modern rooms.” the hotel is very nice. it is a short walk away from a covered pedestrian bridge/overpass that takes you right to the airport! the room decor is pretty new - new furniture, curtains, lamps, bedding, tv, etc. i loved the bright CFL lights in the bathroom - good for putting on makeup. the only negative is that they charge for parking! so we just took our rental car back to the airport early, and then walked back to the room via that pedestrian overpass.

“Tolles Boutiquehotel” Ich kannte das Hotel vorher nicht, es hat sich jedoch eine günstige Gelegenheit ergeben, welche ich nicht bereute. Das Hotel liegt direkt an der Wall Street, U Bahn 5 Minuten entfernt. Hotel ganz stylish, keine herkömmliche Rezeption vorhanden. Personal extrem freundlich. Zimmer für New Yorker Verhältnisse riesengroß, einige nette Kleinigkeiten vom Architekten eingebaut. Minibar (antialkoholisch und Snacks) sind kostenfrei und werden nachgefüllt (über Nachfrage). Ausgezeichneter Schlafkomfort, auch sehr ruhig. Einige Lokale in der Umgebung, manche aber nur wochentags geöffnet. Hotel für New York sehr zu empfehlen.

“Great location” We wanted a little luxury with a great location and that's exactly whet we got. Self-parking right accross the street was not cheap but convenient (cheaper than the valet parking offered by the hotel at least). Check in was personable and extremely quick and we were straight up stairs within minutes of arriving; we had paid a slight premium for a city view and were not disappointed with a great view accross to Union Square. The room itself was triangular, which was unusual, but which meant that the amount of window space (therfore the view) was maximised - great by day and night. The decor was modern and attractive, the room was quite spacious and the beds very comfortable with crisp linens; so comfortable in fact that I kept on falling asleep when we were supposed to be heading out! The bathroom was small but okay with nice toiletries and complementary bathrobes. The location of the hotel is excellent; the upscale Westfield Mall is a block away and Union Square three blocks at most with cable cars and the muni right around the corner. SFMOMA is right down the street and convenient for a early start. Some reviewers mentioned being uncomfortable with the area and homeless people being around... This is really not a problem and typical of any modern city (or indeed town) - we came back to the hotel well after midnight and felt perfectly safe as we did throughout the city. Other reviewers have been critical of the Westin's business facilities (internet etc.) but I felt that the hotel offers a great deal for leisure travellers and tourists; much better to be at the heart of the city instead of being stranded at the end of a cable car line in tacky Fisherman's Wharf. We were going to stay at the Argonaut but I'm glad we chose the Westin instead.

“Cramped room and flat pillows” I stayed at the Marriott Wardman for a conference and the room was incredibly small compared to other Marriott hotels in the area. When I sat at the desk the chair bumped up against the bed. Conference services also left much to be desired as well.

“Completely average” I stayed here for two nights on a business trip. I would not stay again. Nothing bad but the rooms seemed dated and not well kept, even in what I was told was the refurbished part of the hotel. The rates are good and if it was just for one night and you didn't have to spend much time in the hotel, it would be okay, but the next time I need to stay near LAX, I will look elsewhere.

“Great Location” Stayed at this hotel on a Saturday night. We had a superior size room, which I would recommend spending the extra for it. It was still on the small side, but adequate. Room was clean and refridgerator was a nice extra. Staff was very friendly and made us feel welcomed. Value and location cannot be beat. Right near subway and Times Square!

“Great place to stay” I made a four-night reservation for this hotel on Priceline, so I got a great rate. This was the first time that we went for a 3.5-star (boutique) instead of a 4-star hotel in NYC on Priceline and we were just delighted. The location is phenomenal--Tudor City Is like another universe--hard to believe you're just a couple blocks from Grand Central Station. There are quiet parks (with fireflies this time of year), beautiful views down to the East River and the UN, and elegant restaurants nestled in the bottoms of beautiful old apartment houses. The historic building the hotel is in is really charming, and our room was clean, pleasant, comfortable, and had a great view. A couple minor flaws: housekeeping is strangely chintzy with the toiletries--one bar of soap was provided at the start of our stay and was not replenished (however, we asked at the front desk and were cheerfully provided with a couple more), and shampoo was not provided on the first night. Also, the towels aren't great quality and smell strongly of detergent. Finally, the high-speed internet provided by the hotel is rather expensive ($14.95/day)--so much so that I decided to forgo using my laptop during my stay. On the whole, though, we found this to be a great choice, loved that the place had more character than the big chain 4-stars we usually stay in, and loved the proximity to a unique NYC neighborhood.
“They have got it right!” Another stay at this modern friendly embassy suites in a great location for walking out to downtown restaurants. Really liked the beds and linen too!

“Don't get stuck with a small bed” Wife and I stayed here for one night after getting the room via Priceline. The room amenities were nice and included a flat screen tv. However, there was only one bed for two adults and the mattress was the smallest we've ever had to sleep on. It was a full size (also known as a double). Although the headboard was for a queen size bed, the bed in our room was tiny. Right after we checked in I went to the front desk and requested either a room with a larger mattress or a room with 2 beds. The clerk dismissed my request without even looking at the computer. He said that there were no other rooms available. Once I got back to the room I checked the hotel's room availability online and they had "standard", "king bed standard" and "king bed executive" rooms available. So much for customer service.

“Amazing value” My parents live in Dallas and celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary this past weekend. A block of rooms was reserved for us at an outstanding rate of $49.00 per night. I've stayed here before, but I thought I'd update my reveiw. The hotel is immaculately maintained. If you've been in one Courtyard, you've been to this one, so no surprises here. I must say that the bed was too soft. I had a back-ache from our 15 hour drive and frankly the mushy matress did nothing for it. Everyone else liked the beds though. I'm a weirdo who likes a hard bed. Nice big bathroom, great water pressure, plenty of room to spread out and enjoy life. Kids went in the pool, and I enjoyed a nightly soak in the hot tub. There's one washer and one dryer on the property at $1.00 per load. Went to the laundromat down the street and did my wash there in very short order. Starbucks is to the right at Webb Chapel. Movie theater is there too. Quick Trip next door is an awesome convenience store with hot and cold food items (that are very tasty) and probably the best donuts anywhere. Very reasonably priced (as opposed to The Market) Our maid was awesome never disturbing us, the front desk did everything possible to help us out and even gave us some pennies for a game we could play on our trip back to Atlanta. There's a Motel 6 one exit before this, but at the same price, is there any contest?

“Can be a good choice” Magnolia rates vary widely. If you can book it for $150 or so it is a bargain. Over $200 and there are better places to stay (Icon). It is a neat old building (former newspaper delivery station). The desk is professional and the rooms are nice. The roof-top pool is nice. Food is good enough.

“Don't go for the pool or fitness room” We booked this hotel near the airport because it had a pool and fitness room. The rate is good and the room was comfortable and clean, no problems there. The free breakfast is nice and there was a wide selection of different foods available. However, the fitness room and pool leave something to be desired. The fitness room is the walk thru area before you reach the pool or exit the pool, so the floor was wet, the kids played on the machines (that is an issue with the parents and not the hotel), the room was a balmy 80 degrees and there was no fan. The TV has no remote and the channel can't be changed and there are no anti-spetic wipes for the machines. Most people would not be bothered by any of these issues, but for the die-hard exerciser (like me), it was a touch disappointing. If you don't exercise, then this is a great hotel and I really recommend it for the close proximity to SEATAC.

“Convention hotel on the wrong side of the river” Big convention hotel. Clean and well maintained, but isolated. Few restaurant choices nearby or in the hotel. The casual restaurant was only opened for breakfast and lunch. I had a upgraded corner room with a great few, but a in-room safe was barely big enough to get my iPad in it. Honor bar was the "lift it and you bought it" model. Room service was quick, efficient and good. Navy Pier is six blocks as are restaurants and other activities, but mostly on the other side of the river. Just remember, six walking blocks in Chicago in April is six Taxi blocks in Chicago in January.

“great location for exploring” This is the 4th Courtyard visited on this 9 day trip and it has lived up to all expectations. Ask for an E-King room - there are only 3-4 in the hotel and they an extra seating area with couch, making for a much more spacious experience. Great location for all the tourist spots along the piers. Tons of restaurant options within easy walking distance.

“Average Hotel” This Marriott is in a great location. The hotel is in need of a face lift....while not in terrible shape, the hotel has suffered from some deferred maintainence. Average hotel....nothing special.

“I liked this hotel” This hotel was in a great location. Very close to the Galleria and Memorial areas. The rooms were very well kept and maintained the bathroom was spotless, and all of the necessary amenities were provided. The bed was EXTREMELY comfortable. The internet access was a little odd, as the login screen kept interupting my session, however. I never had that happen ANYWHERE before. The service was very good, especially, in the restaurant and the bell service. The grounds were very nice, and the pool looked nice (though I did not use it) and clean. I would recommend this hotel.

“First Hilton Experience....” Unlike most reviews for this hotel on here, this is real not fake. The property is older, but it is clean. The Good... 1. The Lobby was pretty open and wide. 2. It has an internal restaurant 3. Pool and Exercise Room were clean. 4. Starbucks Coffee is brewed here. 5. Saved a ton of cash by using Priceline.com, I named my own price. Hell yes. I would be ticked if I paid full price. The Say Whaaat? 1. The hotel has breakfast services in the morning...Omelettes cost over 16 bucks. Holy crap batman! 2. The Bathrooms DO NOT have Fan Ventilation! Hot damnnation, I have to towel off in the bedroom, because the bathroom is like the amazon?!? 3. You cannot see the hotel from I-69, there is a large competitor hotel between the hilton and freeway. The Bad... 1. The hotel has both rooms, Smoking and Non-Smoking 2. The parking lot is not well lit, pretty scary if you were parked far away. (many lights were not working). 3. The trees have sap warning signs, damage could occur if you arrive at the wrong time of year. 4. The cost, a normal night ranges from 130 to 160. Pretty high, the Hilton Garden is a ramp north of this hotel. It may cost the same, the rooms may have Ventilation Fans! 5. There is a Starbucks coffee pot when you check out in the morning, it was empty when I left. So no coffee for me!! If you are not paying for this hotel, then I can recommend it. But if you are paying this, then this place is 50 to 60 bucks too much.

“Great Overnighter in The City” We stayed here because my wife's company Christmas party was nearby, and we didn't want to deal with transportation home afterwards. It was great. The front desk staff was super-friendly (without appearing insincere), the room was great, and we had a nice view out the window. It was a short stay, but everything was perfect.

“I love this hotel!” This place is great. Good location. Not too expenisve. Excellent staff, especially Sharon in the breakfast room. Not too far from City Hall and downtown or the art museums. An excellent value. And, the cabs are not expensive.

“Problems with Internet Connectivity” Although the service at the Homewood Suites Chicago Downtown is generally quite good, we had two major problems during my stay that contributed to my giving this hotel an average rating. I had significant problems with Internet connectivity. The hotel staff moved us to another room, which helped a bit, but which did not resolve our Internet problems. I stay in many hotels and would rank our experience with the Internet here in the bottom 10% of all hotels. I also did not particularly like the room configuration of either room. The Homewood Suites has two room suites. In both rooms that we were given, the bathroom was located off the bedroom with the sink area in the bedroom itself separated from the toilet and bath by a door. This meant that I woke up from the sound of running water every time my traveling companion used the bathroom at night. The Homewood Suites offers free breakfast and an evening meal, which my traveling companion enjoyed. I did not like either very much and did not believe that the meals were very healthy.

“Great location” I've stayed at this hotel a few times and have been overall pleased. The rooms are comfortable and clean, the hotel staff is terrific, and if I don't want to go out, the hotel has restaurants that are OK. Cabs are always outside and the Metro station is very close. One of my favorite places to eat is across the street on the way to the Metro station (L'enfant Plaza). It is Vie de France and has wonderful pastries and reasonably priced breakfasts, sandwiches, and salads. A couple blocks away from the hotel is the National Mall. Check in and check out are quick, even during a computer upgrade this last time. I enjoy staying here.

“Good hotel, great location!” Stayed at the Grand Hyatt for two night at the end of my Easter Vacation in the US. The location of the hotel is great, and it is a short walk to the different attractions in DC. We had a standard room with a king bed. Both the room and bathroom was nice and clean. The people at the front desk was kind and helpfull. Do mind that parking is a bit expensive here, that also applies for the wireless internet. My only negative experience this stay was that some of the people working in the resturant where breakfast was served was rude!

“Setting the gold standard for hotels” This was my first stay at a Four Seasons when I was on a business trip. I had high expectations which were surpassed in every way. I was in a standard room which was huge. Amazingly comfortable beds, huge bathroom with a huge deep bath and a TV in the mirror, Customr service was exceptional in every way especially in the bar where the bar staff made exceptional cocktails. The Spa and Gym were top quality and well worth the money. Highly recommended if you can get to stay here.

“Slept well, nothing special” I stayed here while having my household goods packed and picked up for a move to Hawaii. My usual place was not offering discounts and the rate at this hotel was about $35/night less. The room was okay, although the air conditioner was not turned on until I arrived and given the heat wave with 100 degree-plus temperatures, it was unbearable for the first few hours. I had to leave and return later in order to let the AC cool the room sufficiently to get some sleep. I liked the location, close to the freeway, yet far enough that there was no highway noise. There are several restaurants within walking distance and several more just across the freeway. There is shopping a short distance north on I-35. Downtown Fort Worth is only about ten miles. There are several very nice golf courses near this hotel. The Texas Motor Speedway is about seventeen miles north. Burlington Northern Sante Fe railroad corporate HQ is about one mile west of this location. I did not try the free breakfast because there were several nice restaurants close to the hotel. I would stay here again, but people not familiar with the local area might struggle a bit with the traffic along Interstate 35. Knowing your way around the surface streets to avoid the freeway traffic makes this location a lot more tolerable.

“So-so hotel, but very high marks for location and value.” I snagged a huge, immaculate king room overlooking the Alamo on a busy weekend for only $108, so I feel a bit sheepish about complaining about the Crockett's flaws, but here are my two biggies: --Although the room was vast, it was barely furnished! It included two large clunky chairs, but no table. --Bathroom was very clean, but in serious need of repair. The bathtub had peeling paint and a plug that wouldn't hold, fixtures that need replacing and walls that need replastering. If you're not fussy about this sort of stuff, and just need a clean, safe, reliable place to stay while you see the sights, by all means stay here.

“Excellent” My son (20s) and I just returned from 4 day "mother and son" trip to NY, and had a simply great stay at the Warwick. We live in Northwest Arkansas now but I worked in NY for years and know midtown well, so I knew I wanted a midtown west location, an authentic NY atmosphere, and a decent sized room, room service, an onsite bar/restaurant...the Warwick seemed to have it all, so when I was able to get a $144 (plus taxes) winter rate for February, we booked. It turns out that the majority of the Tripadvisor reviews were right. We were greeted with a smile, registered in 5 minutes. As for the rooms, my son's was on the 20th floor, had 2 beds, a lovely granite bath that was fairly large (just like the nicest one in the photos), clean as a whistle, nicely outfitted, bed crisp and white. Perfect. I think this was one of the renovated rooms. My room on the 24th floor was also very clean and fresh, big sunny windows, lots of space (these rooms are twice the size of most NY rooms), had a king bed and a sitting area. Yes, as some reviews say, there were a few scuffs on the older furnishings, and a few carpet stains, and the sofa in that room should be recovered or replaced...but I loved this room anyway. It had some elegant touches, high ceilings, felt safe and cozy, great bed....the only real complaint is that my room had the tiniest bath I think I have ever encountered. It was hard to get in and out of the shower with the door closed. I am a fairly petite person, and I was the only one using the bath, so it was manageable - however if my husband had been with me, I would have had to ask for a different room. Now, having said that, don't for minue let that keep you from booking this hotel. The tiny bath was nicely appointed, and the rest of the room made up for it. As for the staff, everyone was professional, nice, efficient - without exception. When I accidentally left my glasses at Randolf's they kept it and made sure it was returned to me. Lovely. The two times I ordered room service it arrived in 15 minutes, nicely presented and delicious. Randolf's bar is very nice - I had a very good crab cake with my martini. Murals breakfast bar was too expensive, so we only ate there one day. I have stayed in about 10 hotels in midtown west area. The Warwick may have just become my NY hotel "home." My sincere thanks to the Warwick staff for making our trip so pleasant, and for helping make it a week of great family memories in a magnificent city.

“Excellent for the price” The hotel is in a prime location, only a minute from Macy’s, right next to the subway and just round the corner from the Empire State Building and a short walk to Times Square. It obviously wasn’t going to be a high class hotel but the staff were super friendly, the room was spacious enough with an OK bed, couch and TV. Bathroom was also fine. One small problem was the very loud heating system. The radiator hissed very loudly for about 20 minutes then would stop for an hour then start again. May not be great for light sleepers! Some of the décor needs a bit of updating, just drab and looking worn in places. The complimentary breakfast was good, cereals, bagels, waffles and donuts! There is also a free coffee machine in the lobby – great for when coming in out of the cold! For budget travellers a great choice in the heart of the city.

“Very nice experience” Got a great rate on this stay via an opaque booking service. Given choice of smoking/non, placed on a high floor. Convenient parking is $17/day, but with in/out. Room was perfectly furnished, with excellent amenities in the bath. Bed was wonderfully comfortable. A/C was adequate, overall the stay was terrific. Dinner in the hotel restaurant was reasonable and delicious. Two night stay, and the housekeeping was polite and helpful as well. I would definitely stay here again!

“Great Place for a Meeting” We held a regional meeting at the facility. It was very well run, with a staff that centers its attention to the "details". Food quality was very good and the overall funtionality was excellent. The only down side is dealing with finding the hotel and traffic. If you miss the turn on East Wacker, you are going to work a little to locate the entrance. Without question, great town, great hotel, great attractions equals very strong meetings and or vacations.

“Beautiful Hotel” The hotel is beautiful and the staff is great. Everyone who worked there was very friendly. The only downside is the location, its far from downtown and doesn't seem to be in walking distance to much. There are some restaurants onsite but as typical with hotel restaurants they are pricey. But the hotel itself is one of the nicest I've stayed in.

“Excellent hotel” Stayed for 4 nights while sightseeing in Charlotte area. Good location, hotel itself is down a quiet street but close to main roads. Lots of restaurants close by, also a Super Walmart. Easy access to I85. Only about a 10 minute drive up to speedway area and concord mills mall. Room was above average, microwave, frig, large flat screen tv, free wifi. Very clean and fresh. Nice to be able to open the windows. Friendly staff. Better than average breakfast. Would defintely stay here again.

“Calm Competent Convenient Courtyard” This property is perched on the Inner Harbor between the Fells Point area and downtown. It's a pleasant 15 minute walk across harbor footbridges to the Convention Center and no more than a ten minute walk to Broadway in Fells Point with its clubs, restaurants and cafes. It's a relatively new residential neighborhood and there's a Whole Foods around the corner and a trendy coffee shop across the street and just about anything else you could want for an extended stay. The hotel boasts large rooms, opening windows, nice views and a quiet street for pleasant sleeping. The staff is exceptionally friendly, the restaurant serves a fine breakfast (buffet if you want), and the cozy bar area includes a smiling, competent bartender. I could not find anything wrong with this place and would choose it anytime over more expensive hotels in the area,

“A restful LAX oasis with great service” I've stayed here twice...first before a long flight to Australia and the second when I came back. Living on the East Coast, I thought it would be a better plan to go a day early before my long, long, flight to Sydney and what better place than an Embassy Suites!? Planning my trip early, I followed & chatted them upon the Twitters & they were nicely responsive. Good sign! The complimentary shuttle picked me up both times in under 20 min TIP: Find the RED hotel shuttle island outside & wait for the BLUE shuttle van. After tipping the nice driver who lugged my heavy suitcase, I was whisked away EARLY to the hotel. Both times they accommodated my early arrival and I got a room before the official check in. The first time I had to wait a little bit, so I grabbed a burger at the hotel restaurant. It was delish & definitely helped with the jet lag. Mmm meat. On the return trip from Australia I arrived around 7am LA time (weird, 'cause I had left Sydney at 10am the SAME DAY - time zones freak me out!) They had only one room avail & I had to pay $20 extra because it was the hepa ultra clean room which all I could figure out meant that it had an air purifier in it. Either way, it was a great room to take a quick shower & much needed nap. Flat screen TV's with many channels to choose from was a plus..If only there was FREE Internet. Of course both times I woke up in time to catch the Manager's Reception! (Australians were AGOG hearing about all the FREE perks an Embassy Suites offer!) Manager's Reception: The happy hour was awesome! I tipped the hard-working but cheerful bar tender $5 straight away & got great pours whilst there. Nibbling munchies, sipping a cool chard, & reading from my iPad relaxed me greatly after so much packing, trudging, & flying, etc. On the second stay, I did order a room service small pizza & Caesar salad which was delivered fast, priced well, & yummy. (On that flight back from Australia I hadn't eaten since 4am, then took that much needed nap, had a couple free glasses of chard...so yeah...dinner was required!) Slept like a baby! Breakfast: This is definitely where Embassy Suites shines! I grabbed a couple pancakes & asked the kind omelette chef for a few crispy slices of bacon - added a bowl of fruit, a big orange juice & coffee and I was ready to take the shuttle back to the airport & fly back east. If you have a LONG flight to catch going out of LAX you couldn't find a better place to break your travel than the Embassy Suites North. If only they had a spa like the one in St. Charles, Mo it would be PERFECT! Every person I came into contact with on the property were friendly, accommodating, & helpful.

“Centrally located timeless charm!” Fourth time staying at this hotel has timeless charm.Center city location within 5 blocks of Rittenhouse square. Gourmet shops within hotel including tiffany, williams and sonoma, ralph lauren,Palms restaurant.roof top cocktails lounge.circular breakfast room.service very helpful and friendly.room comfortable bed and linens at $125 weekend rate it was a great deal in the center of it all!
“Great hotel” Tge friendliness of the staff is great. They have a customer first Ttitude. The room was well kept and comfortable!

“Bugged” This seemed like a nice Marriott and the staff was courteous throughout my stay and the location is outstanding! Unfortunately, after the second of my two nights there, I woke up with bites on my torso that were much worse than what one might expect from a mosquito or a spider and may have possibly been from bedbugs. There was a line of three bites along my side and they took about three weeks to heal. I hope that this is not a regular occurrence.

“Nice hotel” Had a nice stay at a great Priceline rate last weekend. Good view from my room even tho I wasn't as high up as I could have been. Great bathroom products, clean room, sparkling lobby, and helpful staff.

“Fantastic hotel, perfect !” We booked the Distrikt because of the wonderful Tripadvisor reviews we had read, and the price could not be beat. Great value for a NYC hotel, especially due to it's great location. We were coming to NYC for my 29th Birthday. My husband mentioned on the online reservation that it was going to be my Birthday. After be greeted outside by the lovely and friendly staff, they took our luggage so we could check in. At check in I was told Happy Birthday right away from the front desk lady, that was so nice. Check in was fast. We are choice privileges members, so we were given a coupon for $10 off at the bar in the hotel. Also We were explained to about the room key, which I think is great. You can only get the elevator to work after you scan your card over this black disc, it will also only allow you to go to your floor. There are only about 5 rooms per floor, this card is great for security of your room and your stuff. When we arrived in the room, there was a card wishing me a Happy Birthday, and it was thanking us for choosing the Distrikt. It came with a cupcake as well :) This was a really nice touch and a great way to start our trip and our 5 night stay at the Distrikt. The room was so nice and clean. The bed was gorgeous, Loved the big padded headboard and it was super comfortable, no problem sleeping. It was so nice and quiet. The TV was a flat screen and a nice size. There is a lot of space for clothing, 4 drawers and a closet. There is a desk area and free wireless internet. we had a wonderful view of the Empire state building as requested. The bathroom was the best we've ever had in NYC. So clean and spacious, we loved the shower, it was wonderful, great water pressure. The AC worked great, we were there during a very hot week, and the room always stayed so nice and cool. Every evening we had turn down service, although most nights we happened to be in the room getting ready for the evening when they would come. I just told them not to worry , but I'd take some of the delicious chocolates they left, very good. We had a lovely housekeeper, on our 2nd day she left us a note thanking us for the tips, it was nice of her to do that. We did go down and check the bar out one night, and use our coupon, drinks are a little pricey, but they are made very well with good liquor. The bar tender said they are all his own recipes and he made me a grape mojito. Hands down best mojito I have ever had, and I enjoy mojitos and have had many, it was delicious. My husband got a manhattan, and he also said it was the best manhattan he had ever had, a lot of work went into our drinks, so we felt they were worth the price. As far as location , some people had said at night it was a little sketchy, we did not think so at all. We Never felt worried , and we went back to the hotel after midnight most nights. The area is fine, and it is close to Hells kitchen you have a lot of great restaurant options and some great bars.
