It is right next to Port authority, so you have lots of transportation options, subway is right there too. You are minutes away from Times square and all the theaters. I just want to say the location is nothing to worry about. We had an absolutely perfect stay at The Distrikt. Every single member of staff was so warm and friendly,they were always happy and smiling and saying hello. This trip was a trip of a lifetime, and it was made perfect thanks to the Distrikt. I would recommend this hotel to everyone making a trip to NYC. I just want to say Thank you so much to all of the wonderful and amazing staff, this was the best Birthday of my life. We love NYC and now we love the Distrikt , we miss you both, and we will definitely return.

“Nice Large Suites, but...” i was initially very pleased with the hotel when we arrived @ The London NYC. However, the street isn't the prettiest, nor is the surrounding area. On the flip side, it's centrally located to everything I needed: The Met, Ed Sullivan Theater, MoMa, shopping, etc. Also the rooms are large (all suites), clean and tastefully decorated with a contemporary and traditional flair. Our room was at least 725 square feet, had beautiful hardwood flooring installed in a haring bone pattern, Waterworks bathroom fixtures, glass mosaic tile walls in the bath, a 7' two person shower (with a rainhead shower, hand held and a standard shower head) white carrara marble bath vanity, mosaic tile bath floor and thirsty robes. Complimentary one day internet -- after that they charge 12.95/day, a well stocked mini-bar, two flat screed televisions with a nice lineup of free cable channels (HBO, etc), ipod hook-up for the alarm clock, plenty of storage for luggage, a decent view from our room on the 46th floor, drapes and sheers were controlled electronically, very comfy bedding (down comforter and pillows - synthetic pillows available on request if you're allergic as my wife and I are), desk with ample work space and speaker phones, a comfortable couch and leather rocking chair in the livingroom all of which made me quite happy. My only real complaints about the hotel itself was the noise. In my opinion, they didn't insulate for sound very well during the renovation of the hotel. I could hear water rushing through the pipes when my neighbors were showering and every single time someone entered or left their room I could hear their front door slam shut. If the hotel can adjust the mechanism on doors it would keep down some of the noise. At this point, there's not a whole lot that can be done about the plumbing noise. I live in downtown Chicago so I am accustomed to quite a bit of noise. Perhaps it was the newness of the noise that bothered me. Nevertheless, if you are sensitive to these things keep it in mind and ask for a room where you will be farthest from neighboring rooms. Also, I think our room was close to an area where housekeeping may keep supplies. Each morning during our four day stay, I heard a door slamming shut, with regularity, between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM. One more note of caution, I believe they are still renovating the hotel so you may hear some construction noise after 8:00 AM or 9:00 AM. As for the staff, everyone was friendly and helpful. I didn't have a chance to have dinner at the restaurant, but I did have a drink and an appetizer. The BLT was tasty and the bar was quite busy for a Thursday around 11:00 PM. I don't know if I would repeat that meal as it cost me just under $50 (with tip) for a sandwich, drink and french fries, but I was too tired to seek out anything else. I'd consider staying here again, but for the money I would look at my options as well. The main reason being the noise issue. If that could be fixed, and the hotel maintains its current level of cleanliness, I wouldn't think twice about giving it another try.

“Don't bother with the food” I had a stylishly pretty room, with a bed that was more comfortable after I straightened out the bottom sheet. Noise was not a problem at all. But breakfast was -- very expensive, and scrambled eggs so salty I had a hard time eating any. Other items edible but nothing special. No time to ask that the eggs be redone. I left a note on the half-eaten eggs, and mentioned it to the desk when I checked out -- his reaction was a shrug. Don't use the valet parking unless you're okay with $60/night, with tax and tip. I used the Fifth and Mission garage, two short blocks away, for a total of $41 for a day and a half. The hotel would have charged me for two full days, or $120.

“Convenient location, gorgeous rooms, great service” The Grand Hyatt Seattle always provide a excellent experience. We were here for four nights and found housekeeping meticulous and other services well above par. Walkable to hip restaurants and entertainment in Belltown and Capitol Hill.

“Alright not great” I have stayed here twice, the hotel is good for the price for the rate I get from work, but I would never stay here under the regular rate. Hotel is quite old, and is very average. The parking garage is tiny and if you have a larger SUV you may have problems. I would avoid the TGI Fridays, its not very good at all. The one plus is that there is a Starbucks in the Lobby. The location is the one good thing about it.

“Great place to stay” My partner and I stayed at DoubleTree Arctic Club Hotel in Seattle before and after our Alaska cruise. This was our first time visiting Seattle. The location was perfect. The hotel staff were very professional and helpful. The rooms are very well decorated (very masculine). I would recommend this hotel highly.

“Nice option if you are at the Mascone Center” I liked this hotel because of the location, the gym, and the amenities. The spa is great. The key to really enjoying the Intercontinental is to be an Ambassador. You pay for this, but if you travel a lot like me, the free internet, fruit and water in the room, free upgrades, and free movie are a definitely perk. And, you get a free night a year at any Intercontinental. My room was great, with a beautiful view and a roomy bathroom. I had a nice fluffy robe, a corner room that was very quiet, and everything was clean and very tidy. I would definitely stay in again (it is close to the BART too, makes for easy transport to and from the airport at a reasonable price).

“Best surprise of the trip!” Stayed at the Hilton Bayfront at the urging of one of my colleagues. Was not disappointed. Pricey ($269/night). But everything was very high quality. My king standard was ready prior to 3pm check in time (very nice), had a great view of the bay, and everything was practically brand new. I would stay here again for sure.

“very disappointing” I lived and traveled world-wide and stayed in 1-5 star properties. This was the worst night's sleep I have had in 35 years. I was told the day before arrival for a one-night "staycation" that an early check-in would not be a problem as there were plenty of rooms available. When we arrived, an upgrade to a suite was not available. I requested a rollaway which took two calls and two hours to arrive and a coffeemaker which also took an hour and a half. Micah at the front desk apologetically gave us a $25 credit. The afternoon at the pools, water-slide and swim-up bar was wonderful. Food at the poolside restaurant was good, service was fair at best. The drama started around 11 p.m. From 11-12:30 a.m. I was awakened four times by young parentless children running down the halls laughing and talking loudly. After reprimanding them myself, I finally had to call a security guard who promptly helped. At this point it was too late. In the morning I staggered to one of the restaurants with my young son, looking forward at least to the $40 breakfast coupon that came with our package. One clueless and apathetically slow hostess tried to field a line of hungry guests. When we finally got to the front she told us there would be another half hour wait. I returned to the front desk and told them of my disappointments (the coupon was not valid for room service). I was told that they could only offer a monetary reimbursement but that they were terribly sorry. That monetary reimbursement has yet to arrive.

“Grosszuegige Räume” Das Hotel bietet sehr grosszuegige Suiten, die jeweils aus einem Schlafraum, einem Wohnraum und einem Bad bestehen. Das Zimmer war gepflegt und sauber und die Betten boten einen guten Schlafkomfort. Das Hotel selber bietet einen großen überdachten Innenhof mit restaurant und Bar und eignet sich gut Konferenzen. Es bietet Schwimmbad und Fitnessräume. Es liegt zentral.

“a great place in DC” We were here for five nights in October. We were staying on points so we were on the 15th floor, the concierge floor. The lounge is on the 2nd floor. It is not open at all on Saturday. Sunday it open for night but not breakfast. M-F it is open for breakfast with a night reception. The ladies that run the lounge are extremely kind and hard working. We enjoyed the service and lounge. If you are light sleeper you may need ear plugs as even on 15th floor could hear traffic noise. The rooms are standard Marriott. Desk, TV, hair dryer, two nightstands, Wifi and cable network. Our bed was comfortable, shower had good pressure and hot water, room was clean. My only complaint was that we had a refrigerator in our room. These are not standard as my other family members did not have one in their rooms. The refrigerator was very dirty. The rest of the room was spotless but the refrigerator had sticky stuff all over the top of it and the inside could use a good scrub. Not a huge issue for us as we didn't use it but did make an impression. The restaurant has a nice happy hour at normal hours and then later again at late night. Metro station is at the end of the block. However, it is just as easy to walk to the Mall or other sites. Macy's across the street if you forget anything or the weather changes on you. Nice workout room and sauna. Indoor pool but didn't put a foot into it but appeared the kids enjoyed it. The door men are extremely professional as well. Overall a nice experience. When we are back in town we would stay again.

“Beautifully Restored Hotel with Great Amenities” We have just returned from a 4-night stay at the Drury Plaza Hotel, and were very glad we chose this hotel. The restoration of the old Alamo Bank building is quite impressive and provides a unique experience. Being "Yankees" we had never stayed at a Drury property, and we found we got a lot for our money. Check-in was very smooth, and our room choice was honored, even though we arrived very late due to flight delays. We had a room on the 18th floor with a fantastic view of the city, including the Hemisfair Tower. Although our king room was a bit on the small side, everything was provided for us and all was very clean. We especially appreciated the fridge, microwave, and very speedy free wireless connection. Linens and towels were very clean-smelling, and the bed was comfortable. We would definitely advise you to get to breakfast early, especially on the weekend. However, regardless of the time, the food was always fresh and hot. The pancakes and sausage are especially good, but there are a lot of other things to choose from, as well. We also took advantage of the evening reception, where they were serving complimentary beer, wine, soda, and snacks. The staff is extremely friendly, and we always felt welcome. This is not the case in many other hotels. We can suggest a few slight improvements: 1) A hotel of this size needs a concierge. The front desk was not always completely informed about various activities/restaurants. 2) This is a picky thing, but such good pancakes deserve real butter, not Country Crock spread! Some general SanAntonio suggestions: Boudros on the Riverwalk is a fantastic restaurant. Plan where you want to eat during the day and make a reservation- otherwise, you'll have to wait. The BlueStar Brewing Company served great beer and food. It's about a mile south of the hotel, but there's plenty of parking. Walk down Market St. about 3 blocks to the Riverwalk entrance and get your riverboat tour tickets there. Boats leave every 15 minutes and the guides are very interesting. When it's hot, try to walk via the Riverwalk rather than up on the street. I was able to figure out how to walk from the convention center to the hotel via the Riverwalk, and it was very pleasant.
“Good for what it is.” Well located comfy airport hotel. Well managed and exceeds expecations. Repeat stayer would do again in the future. Great priced for value.

“Decent place to stay on the edge of downtown” My mom and I stayed here one night and were happy with the value. The hotel was affordable, on the edge of downtown, close to the Port and it was clean. The lobby is pretty small and the restaurant is a little dated. Parking was $10 a night which I felt was good and we received a complimentary breakfast which was just okay. I'd stay again if we need a one nighter or just a clean place to lay my head at night and didn't plan to spend a lot of time in the hotel. Oh plus there was free wi-fi.

“Treated like VIP's” We were a little concerned we might not be hip enough for the Gansevoort, we needn't have worried. During our stay we were treated like celebrities, I have never had such attentive service or knowledgable help from any hotel. Our room was lovely, not over the top, but thoughtfully laid out and furnished, we had a view of the Hudson river and of the street below, great for people watching, in our Grand deluxe room. There was plenty of space and storage in the bathroom, which was well lit. Bed was comfy, with a feather top, mini bar very well stocked. The roof top bar has different sections depending on mood, the staff are superb, once they realise you are a hotel guest they will ensure you get a table, however busy they are. As guests you can ignore the queues outside and staff usher you into the next elevator ahead of everyone, it's great. The buzz in the bar is superb, so much to see, it feels like the centre of the New York universe. Staff remember your name, your tastes and your drinks, the room was very clean and fresh, we left a wad of money in ours by mistake, it was neatly tidied and hidden when we returned! All the food we had was very good, breakfasts especially. We were on floor 8, far enough from the noise below and above, but you wouldn't come here for peace and quiet! The area is fantastic around here, some of the best food in manhattan is available, there are many, many bars. In this respect it is more like Europe, there is a distinct French feel. Shops are mainly high end, such as Marc Jacobs and Stella Macartney. We usually stay in midtown, but not anymore, we only ventured in once for shopping and couldn't wait to get back to our 'village' and our Gansevoort oasis.

“Great service, great location for tourist, hotel needs renovation” The only reason I booked this hotel was becuase of the rate of $143 over labor day weekend. The hotel is located in the heart of the city, and has some real nice city views. The lobby, and the rooms need some renovation, the furniture is kinda worn and outdated, but it is clean. The hotel has the new Hyatt Grand Beds, has to be one of the best beds I've slept in. The fitness center is a decent size with new equipment. I thought the service was warm, and professional which I find rare at these large touristy hotels. In the end this is a large outdated tourist hotel in the heart of Union Square.

“just OK” I don't have anything specifically negative to say about the Langham, only that it failed to knock my socks off. I stayed here for 2 nights en route from California to London, so I was in transit somewhat and the hotel did provide me with what I needed - a quiet room, comfy bed. Good points: the staff were friendly, the swimming pool and whirlpool were very nice and Julien's the cocktail bar was beautiful. Also I asked for a DVD player and one was provided promptly, which impressed me. Not so good points: there's nothing really close by in terms of places to grab a snack or a soft drink - there's a 7 eleven the other side of the park but that's it really. The room service was extortionate - all of the wines were expensive but so was the food - way overpriced I thought, and I begrudge this. Its a nice hotel and a grand building but like I said, it didn't knock my socks off.
“Ageless beauty” Great location, beautiful hotel, fabulous furnishings. Will be back. Note-stairs only but staff will help with luggage.

“It Would be Hard to Stay Anywhere Else” I travel to New York quite frequently for business and pleasure. Usually, I use points from another hotel point program and stay free. In February, W did a promotion where if you booked with AMEX, you'd get one night free at a W hotel, so I decided to try at W Union Square. I'd heard it was a hip and trendy place, which has it's pros and cons. The pro is, it's fun and people watching is great. The con is, as a 36 year old woman I might feel a little "old" and out of place. This was not the case. When I arrived, I was welcomed by the staff and taken to my room. A few weeks prior, I'd requested a sunny room and they complied with a giant, corner room with a view of the park. Because they knew I like "sunniness", they brought me a giant sunflower and some fruit and champagne about 5 minutes after check in. That right there would have won me over in terms of personal touches and friendliness, but throughout my stay, the entire staff did little things to show they were anticipating my needs -- they even went so far as to bring me a tray of comforting things on a day I was sick. As for the room itself, it was a good size for New York and had a great view of Union Square. Unlike many hotel rooms in the city, this room had a full bath (soaking tub) with Bliss Spa products -- definitely worth talking about. I don't think I've ever been as impressed with bath products. The water pressure was very good and the hot water never ended. There were no coffee pots, however, the hotel sent up a coffee maker for me to keep in my room, so if you are a coffee addict, keep this in mind! Just ask and you shall receive. At night, the lobby does become somewhat club-like. It's a stylish, loud, see and be scene place. That being said, it's kind of small and there's so much going on that if you do happen to be schlepping through in your sweats, no one really cares. It's smaller than it looks in the picture. The "living room", a place to congregate and have drinks, is very small and I felt a little uncomfortable going there alone....so I didn't. Underbar is a different story. I went with girlfriends and we had a fabulous time. The waitress was super nice (which was surprising, since others have said the opposite about Underbar staff) and the music was a good mix. It was dark, so I think I wouldn't have minded going in by myself for a drink, though I never got around to it! Olives, the restaurant in the hotel, is incredible. My friends and I were seated in a big, comfy booth and treated like royalty. The chef (Todd English), who owns about 20 restaurants, just happened to be there that night and sent us loads of free samples because he'd heard we were all cooks. You can't go wrong with the hotel restaurant, that's for sure. Still, you'll want to get around. The W is a minute or two walk from the Union Square station, so in minutes, you can get anywhere in NYC. There's plenty to do right in the area. Sephora and Barnes and Noble are right smack across the street and Filenes, DSW Shoe Warehouse and a Children's Place are also very, very close. You'll want to take a subway or cab ride for finer shopping, though. The concierge knows what stores have what and will help you out. Restaurants in the area include Veritas, Candela, Union Square Cafe, Tabla and many more I can't think of right now. There are plenty of nice hotels in NYC, but when you find one that's perfect, it's hard to stay anywhere else.

“Very nice hotel but no wow factor” This hotel was booked for me for business. The location is GREAT - you have a metro stop in the building, so you can't get any more convenient than that. Some excellent restaurants within a few blocks. The hotel is very nice but doesn't seem "5 star." I would definitely recommend it if you get a good price, but it doesn't seem to be worth $400/night that it sometimes runs. The common areas were very nice but not spectacular. The rooms were very nice and updated but no nicer than many new or renovated Hiltons or JW Marriotts that I have stayed in, and not as nice as some I've been in. The workspace was great - an extremely comfortable, ergonomic chair. I hate paying $10/night for internet, though, but I had no choice. (That's why they do it.) Would I stay here again? Absolutely. Would I rush back here? Not really - it was a very nice hotel and I'd be happy to stay here again but there was no "wow" factor to make this a really memorable stay. Considering it's a business hotel in downtown DC, I don't know if it's really fair to expect it to!

“Fantastic hotel in downtown Fort Worth” We loved our stay at the Omni in Fort Worth! Our room on the 15th floor was amazing, large, great views over Fort Worth towards Dallas. Great for a sunrise when the weather is clear! The staff were helpful & friendly. We ate at Whiskey & Rye (nachos & wine) and at Cast Iron (dinner) Both were great. The valet staff were quick & efficient & always smiling! It was busy with teenage girls (dance nationals) & a conference but aside from more people in the lobby & slightly fuller lifts we didn't notice until they'd gone (it felt very empty on the Sunday night!) we felt this meant the hotel was working very efficiently! All in all, a lovely stay!!

“I'll sleep on a street corner, thanks” I have done a lot of traveling this year - from Paris to San Diego to Honolulu - so I have something to which to compare this hotel. The bottom line is if you want a relatively clean hotel room at a moderate price and don't mind dealing with staff that have not yet understood that the hospitality industry is a people business, then this hotel is for you. Dealing with staff, however, that won't make eye contact, let alone do something you request, ruins my stay and my stay was ruined here. There must be a sign somewhere in their backroom that says it is forbidden to smile. I'll sleep on the street corner before I stay here again. Unfortunately, I was in a rush and didn't check tripadvisor before booking. Others have commented on the miserable service. They are right.

“Nicely done, Indigo!” I thoroughly enjoyed my three-night stay at Hotel Indigo. The king room was ideally appointed and I actually really liked the hardwood flooring used in place of carpeting. Free Internet is always key for me and the connection speed was decent. There's a rooftop bar that seems popular with guests and locals. Convenient location just three blocks from Penn Station and literally down the street from the 28th St MTA subway station. The only downside was a constant pet peeve of mine: an inaccurate bill slipped under my door prior to checkout showing a $14 minibar charge. I hadn't touched the minibar. I can never understand how hotels cannot get the minibar piece right. Shouldn't it be checked prior to allowing another check-in to the room? The hotel did take the charge off my bill and apologized, but I am always uptight when this happens as it gives the impression to me that the hotel is trying to add a few bucks to the till. Overall, a five star visit, busted down one rating point by the minibar episode. I do highly recommend this property overall and want to note that I got a very nice rate on Hotwire for my stay.

“Horrific Soundproofing” I stayed here for 3 nights with my colleagues. I took the "Go Airport Express" from O'Hare which cost me $50 for a roundtrip ticket and arrived in about 30 minutes to the hotel. There is a main reservation desk in the main lobby, but the van dropped me off at the West tower and I just checked in at the small desk there. The West tower is in the middle of being renovated, so there is construction going on if that is a concern before you stay here. When I saw my room, I couldn't have been more pleased. I had a great view of the river and it was just renovated so everything looked brand new. It is right near Michigan Avenue and awesome restaurants. I'm not sure why another reviewer said not to walk around the neighborhood at night. It seemed perfectly safe to me with lots of people walking around. Anyway, the bathroom was clean with a mirror which was backlit, so putting on my makeup was like being at the makeup counter at a department store. However, my pleasure soon turned to displeasure at about midnight when I was awoken by my neighbor's TV. My room had two adjoining doors to the neighboring rooms. By the way, why do hotels do this? Most people don't need to share rooms. Anyway, I could hear every word of his program he was watching. The TV wasn't loud, it was because of those adjoining doors which offer no soundproofing! This was proven again the next morning when I heard my other neighbor on the phone. I could hear every word she was saying, including her full phone number when she left someone a message! I asked the front desk to move me, but they didn't have any rooms available. So it continued for 3 days. I heard my neighbor's TV at night, blowing his nose, the other neighbor on her phone...it was a complete nightmare. This next example will show you how poor the soundproofing is: I was awoken at 5am by my phone vibrating on the nightstand (or so I thought was my phone). I went to go turn it off, and it wasn't my phone vibrating- it was my neighbor's!! Then I heard him walk to the bathroom...urinate...then let out a big fart. It sounded like he was in my bathroom, not in another room! Now.....If I can hear all this, it tells you how BAD the soundproofing is between the rooms. If other people who have stayed here have adjoining rooms like this and don't hear anything...its either because they had no neighbors, or they were very quiet. If you do choose to stay here, make sure to ask for a room without the connecting doors. I couldn't sleep well, because I was kept up late by one neighbor...then awoken early by another. Oh, and my sink started backing up also, but I asked them to come fix it after I checked out since I didn't want to deal with it. The whole experience was just terrible. Adding to the nightmare, the last morning I decided to splurge for room service for breakfast because I was in a rush. I ordered a bagel with smoked salmon and cream cheese. Imagine my surprise when my bagel turned out to be blueberry. Since when is a blueberry bagel eaten with smoked salmon?!? Glad that set me back $25. Although the room was clean and the hotel was in a convenient location, hearing every movement by my neighbors at all hours completely negates anything positve about this hotel. I asked my colleague how her stay was. Her shower knob broke off the first time she tried to use it, and she couldn't access her coffee maker because it was built into an alcove. The cord was too short so she couldn't pull it out of the alcove to open the top to put water in it. She also said she didn't even have any counter space in the bathroom to put her things. I showed her the pictures of my bathroom, and she said hers didn't look like that at all. She was in the West tower also. Parking here is about $53 a day, so if you have a rental car, just beware of that. The breakfast buffet was $22, so its not a cheap either. I was very disappointed in my stay, but again, if you do stay here, ask for a room that doesn't have adjoining doors, and maybe in the main tower you'll have better luck not the West tower.
“Opplevelse!” Bortsett fra relativt små rom er det lite å utsette på W NY. Luksusfølelse gjennom hele oppholdet!

“Below Westin Expectations” Usually Westin hotels are very nice, but this one did not live up to the others' standards. The hotel itself was very nice and the elevators were very fast. The room was nice with decent space to move around. The bed, like all Westin hotels, was very comfortable. The TV and internet were great, although charging $13.95 for internet is a joke these days, especially when other hotels are offering free internet with much better speeds. The room had a mini bar and a small personal refrigerator. The air conditioner worked well and kept the room cool. The downfall of this room was the bathroom. The bathroom was extremely small. There was no space on the counter or anywhere else in the bathroom to place any bath supplies. The bathroom was also extremely dark. Maybe one of the fluorescent tubes was burned out, but housekeeping should have seen this and reported it to have it fixed. The shower was nice with the dual shower heads, but it was also very slow to drain.

“Nothing extraordinary” My husband and I stayed at this hotel for the Chicago Half Marathon & 5K race in September. The hotel is in a nice location and the mini bar was great, but the hotel room was a little outdated. The bellmen were extremely helpful. My husband and I prefer The Conrad across the street.

“Nice NY's Eve” We stayed here on 12/31; booked their full New Year's Eve package, which was a great deal! I asked for a room on an upper floor, no smoking (be sure to specify, they do have a smoking floor, but we never smelled a hint of smoke on the 10th floor). The Sam Bar that is attached to the hotel was a great way to begin our night; very comfortable seating and great bartender; the drinks were well made and the entire staff was very friendly. Our room was large, clean, and comfortable. The bathroom is very nice; loved the beautiful chocolate marble tile with the teal accents. We had a nice view of the old courthouse, and plenty of room moving around, in a regular King room. Unfortunately, our air conditioner was not functioning well. Luckily, it was not a hot day or night, and it was bearable. I called the front desk, and the young lady was helpful and caring, though they did not have maintinence onsite after 11pm on a Sunday. Understandable. Our package included a great dinner at "17", located in the hotel. Our waitress was wonderful, and we enjoyed a 4 course meal, wine and were pleased with every aspect of the food;it was fresh and beautifully presented. Eclectic mix of flavors we really liked. The location of this hotel was perfect, as we walked to Discovery Green for the amazing fireworks, about 5 blocks away. You can easily get to so many places in Downtown from the Alden, or take a quick cab ride, as well. The hotel shuttle van seemed to be giving people rides, but we needed a walk, after our full dinner. We got a continental breakfast included the next morning, as well. They were a little slow getting the breakfast out,but we saw even the manager working hard to make things happen; our guess was that some of the staff took a "sick day", after a big NY's Eve! We did enjoy the pastries, fresh fruit, good coffee and fresh oj,when they did get things going. When we checked out, we mentioned the a/c problem we had. The front desk clerk was equally apologetic (they did mention changing our room the night before, but found the hotel sold out for the event, which we didn't doubt), and they gave us a generous discount on the room, as compensation. We foundthe entire staff; from valet to all staff members in the hotel, bar and restaurant, to be friendly, helpful and very customer oriented! Will definitely recommend the Alden to visitors and also keep it in mind as a good place to stay when we have an event downtown.

“Nice Hotel, room service...ruined it though” Old building, well kept though. Nice staff. The rooms are large kind of like an apartment, at least the kind room we got. The living room and bathroom are very nice. The kitchen is off to the side of the living room, not noticeable, lovely dark granite counter sink, small mini fridge. The bedroom was ok, the bed wasn't really comfortable, and it think it was a queen not a king...or just not that comfortable, but ok. This hotel is a short block from the 16th Street shopping area. Yes, there are a lot of homeless people walking around, some hippies, maybe an occasional protest (Denver style), but you will see the presence of many officers, security guards and police. It is safe enough. It is only about 3 nice safe blocks to the Colorado Convention Center. However, downtown Denver seems super far from Denver International Airport. One severe bad thing is I found a short hair in my reuben I ordered from room service. So I will never stay there again, sorry that is UNACCEPTABLE, hairnets people!!! Even men should wear hairnets! Didn't tell the hotel, what could they do? I needed it erased from my memory. Actually, none of the fine restaurants were that good, pretty mediocre. Never thought I would be hungry on that trip with so many restaurants nearby.

“Decent, not 4 star, good if gotten at a value!” I will start this with the basics, but please read the whole review! This is the FIRST time I have written negatively about service (I honestly am not picky and will stay at a motel 6, etc.). First, the room. Very clean, warm hallways, cool in the room. Bathroom was a mid-range space, not four star. Basic, some outdated fixtures, good size. Room itself good size for NYC. Bed very comfortable, chair and ottoman clean but starting to show wear. Coffee maker and desk area good. TV console great size, minibar fridge stocked (and of course, expensive). View gorgeous over into New Jersey and over the WTC work site. About the noise - we were on the 24th floor and could hear some rumbles, but it did not upset any sleep. Hotel public spaces not impressive, again, basic. Quick check in, elevators, front desk and front doors all within 40 steps. No grand lobby here. ON TO SERVICE. I promise that I am not picky, yet when I stay at (and pay for) a 4-star hotel, I expect service that makes me feel somewhat special (anything - a welcome note, door help, anything). First, I walked in carrying two large shopping bags and a purse. Went through the revolving door with a door/bell man outside and one inside, no help offered (eve though it isn't that large of a lobby, there should be some help offered to guests). After checking in, still no help offered for carrying bags after passing a different bellman. This is not 4 star service - I wasn't even asked by reception if I needed help, had a preference for floor or beds, etc. Went in and out of the hotel at least 4 times first day, and never a door held open when I did not use the revolving door. HERE IS THE REAL COMPLAINT! The next morning, and this is the kicker, housekeeping knocked and came in the room THREE TIMES while we were sleeping!!! at 8:30am, I did not hear a knock (sleeping), but heard my door open and housekeeping talking to each other and walk in. They then saw us in bed and closed the door. At 9:45, I heard knocking, then the door open AGAIN! I shouted out that we were in the room, and they left. At 11 or so, they knocked once again, but this time I put the security lock on (I must have forgot) so they couldn't get all the way in. FYI - checkout is not until NOON!!!!! At 11:40 a gentleman knocked on our door (we were packing up) and asked if we were leaving!!!!! Of course we are - after we CHECKOUT! I have worked hotels - a simple report shows what guests have checked out. I was appalled that at a 4 star hotel I would be awoken twice by housekeeping HOURS before checkout, then twice more been bullied out. Absolutely unacceptable. Overall, would NOT stay here again unless desperate or paid almost nothing. Felt overpriced for the room - even in NYC. To deal with poor service, less than stellar accommodations, etc, but have to pay for 4-stars is not okay. Look around for other deals.

“Mein absoluter Favorit für San Francisco” Das Hilton San Francisco am Union Square ist an allerbester Lage ca. 3min vom Union Square entfernt. Es bietet alle Extras und Service wie man es von Hilton erwarten kann. Die besten Zimmer sind im Tower, ab 20igsten Stockwerk mit City-View. Diese Aussicht alleine ist es Wert dort ein Zimmer zu nehmen, richtig genial wirds dann ab dem 40igsten Stock. Leider wurde letztes Jahr die Executive Lounge im 45sten Stock und die Bar im 46sten Stock geschlossen, der Grund hierfür ist mir immernoch nicht klar. Trotzdem kann ich das Hotel nur empfehlen.

“Classy Place” It may not be downtown, but this hotel is worth the drive. First, the staff is very friendly, helpful, and courteous. I'm a Platinum level so I was able to take advantage of the Concierge Lounge. Here again, it couldn't have been a better experience. If you go to Houston, strongly consider staying here.

“Sshhh, Keep This Place a Secret!” This is the best kept secret in all of San Diego's Pacific Beach! Guest Service Manager Karla Jauregui and her assistant Frank make you feel like you're somewhere that should cost twice the price. The pool is sparkling clean, linens are plentiful (even poolside), the morning coffee and pastries are a delight and even though all 56 units were filled, it's as quiet as a walk in the woods. Other reviewers talk about trying to get one of the renovated units, but my wife and I found the older rooms more desirable -- because you had a patio table and chairs right outside your door in a shaded area. The bus stop is in front of the hotel and just ask Karla or Frank for directions, they'll get you right to wherever you want to go. There was only one downside to the whole Pacific Shores Inn experience: Ultimately, you have to pack up and go home. -- MP, Santa Monica CA

“Outstanding Service” We have stayed stayed a few times at the Omni Parker House in the past. We continue to return due to the central location, quality of bedding/furniture, amenities (particularly if you are an Omni Select Guest), cleanliness and value of the hotel. However, during this stay, one employee in particular stands out - Neal at the front desk. We appreciated his outstanding, personalized customer service from check-in to check out!

“Nice "Business" Marriott in a Business Park setting” We decided to priceline a hotel in San Diego Coastal and we got the Marriott in Del Mar in a Business Center area. Sure, it's only a short drive to the beach but still....but when you Priceline you get what you get and they will not re-nigg on it and let you cancel. We got our room for $75 per night. Safe area, clean area, nice hotel, very clean, rooms nice. Did not eat at the restaurant in the hotel. Hotel seemed very dead. Weekends the business park area was DEAD, kind of a strange feeling but nice at the same time, NO PEOPLE! We used the pool twice, heated but very windy always at the pool area as it's up on top on the side of the building. Hot tub very nice, POWERFUL jets felt great on my back. We were traveling with our 2 1/2 year old daughter, I think we were the only ones there with a kid. Lounge area outside is nice, lots of cushy seating, gas pit fireplaces for at night. Pool area nice. Gym looked really nice, did not use it. Free bottled water in the gym, FYI. I had read several reviews that said there were no mini refrigerators in the rooms so we did not expect one at all. The dresser the TV sat on was odd, one side had 3 drawers and one side looked like faux 3 drawers but only one handle, we thought that side was broken. So we left it. Then on the 2nd day I was observing it again and saw hinges on it, it was a door! There was a fridge behind it, tricky. (see pics). So YES there are refrigerators in room. Maid service very good. Free newspapers during the weekday. Free in room coffee and tea. Hair dryer, shampoo, conditioner and lotion (all Bath & Body Works "Energyze"). The theme of this hotel is "Energize". Oranges, reds and yellows and golds are the dominant colors in the decorating scheme, I'm not sure I liked it..... Biggest pet peeve: parking is $18-24 a day or something like that. We parked on the side of the hotel (the cul-d-sac road). We never had an issue finding a spot but you could if the hotel gets busy. I noticed the maids park there during the day. My other issue is that they charge $14 per day for wi-fi, get out! There is free internet in the lobby and you can print stuff for free. We printed out our Legoland coupons and our boarding passes from the business center downstairs. Overall, this Marriott stood up to Marriott's exceptional quality standards in my eyes, I just didn't care for the location. Not very many restaurants nearby. About a mile down the road is a Von's grocery store anchored shopping center with a bagel place, an italian restaurant, an indian restaurant, a mexican restaurant, an ace hardware, starbucks and other small businesses you would find in a shopping center. We ate at the bagel place, but not the others. There is also a Pat and Oscar's restaurant. We do not have these where we live so we went in & checked the menu, didn't care for pizza and pasta so we did not eat there. Right next to the hotel is a Howard Johnson's hotel and a gas station. Next to the Howard Johnson's is a Taco Bell and also right next to the hotel is a Mexican restaurant. It did not get the best reviews so we chose not to eat there. We actually took a drive to Encinitas to eat at Chili's. :) Yes, it was 10 miles to find specific restaurants! Oh well. You get to get out and drive around and see the different areas right? The hotel is a short drive to Torrey Pines State Reserve. Get there early to get a free parking spot. BUSY on the weekends however.

“Belle situation” Hotel trés bien situé a à peine 5 minutes à pied du capitol Chambre plus que correcte, personnel d'acceuil trés bon Parking gardé dans l'enceinte de l'hotel a 13$ par jour Petit déjeuner assez copieux et varié gratuit

“Civic Center駅のすぐそばですが高級志向の方はやめた方が” BARTのCivic Center駅のほぼ真上なので空港からのアクセスはよいです。 私の泊まった部屋はプライベートバス付ということでしたが実際はシャワーだけでした。 部屋はまあ我慢できる程度の広さと清潔さです。 フロントのそばに無料のインターネット設備(MAC)があります。 無料の朝食は典型的なアメリカンプレックファースト(ドーナツとコーヒー)付です。 ホテル代は安いことは安いので割り切って泊まれる方にはおすすめかもしれません。

“Excellent stay” I've stayed at many, many Hampton Inns across Texas -- and this is one of the nicest. Also easily the most expensive: my very small room was $139/night. But for that price, you get an awesome bed in a very clean, well-maintained room. Much more than I can say for the El Paso Embassy Suites. As others have said, don't be scared off by the fact that this is an "airport" hotel. I never heard a single plane during my 4-night stay. I was on the side closest to the freeway, and had a little freeway noise at night. Not enough to keep me awake. Breakfast was average for Hampton. I was very surprised by the manager's reception, which had enough food to make a light dinner of, including wine and soft drinks. The Embassy is the only other El Paso hotel I've stayed at. The Hampton is far superior, well worth the high price, and will certainly get my business in the future. Highly recommended.

“Some check-in problems - but still a great value and location!” We spent a week here during our stay in NYC. It's the third time we stayed at the Edison Hotel. We pre-booked the room long ahead through our travel agent and we got a really good price. The staff was very helpful when we arrived with our car (and loads of luggage). But then the Check-In: We did book a room for two with a queen bed. The quite unfriendly desk staff told us there's only a double-bed left (smaller than a queen). We argued a while but then decided to take it anyway. But then we went to our room....what a shock! It was so small, the bed did barely fit in there and was tiny. The furniture and bed looked so old and tired. And we almost couldn't fit our luggage in the room. We couldn't accept that. The other two times we were here we got much bigger rooms with a much newer interiour. So my wife went back down to the front desk and told the we will not accept this. We booked long ahead, we stayed here before, we will stay for 7 nights and will not accept this room. If not, we want our money back and stay somewhere else. After a few minutes the manager stepped in and....surprisingly there WAS another room available. A lot bigger room with a King-Bed ... the room was more than twice the size of the other one. After that our day was saved and we could enjoy our 7 nights in NYC. The Hotel itself is dated, but the location is, for this price, unbeatable! The room was clean and actually really big (by NYC standard). The bathroom was also a quite dated, but clean enough. And even though the Hotel is so close to Times Square, we had quiet nights here and a really good sleep. We had a good week, after a pretty bad start. It's comfy, it's safe and you just really get great value here. Staff is helpful and nice (not counting the Check-In). We sure would stay again. But just be aware that room sizes and qualities do very much vary obviously. Check your room and, if you're unhappy, insist on getting a better one. Wanna know more about my trips? Click on my profile or visit: route66traveler.jimdo.com

“It wasn't that bad, honest!” I'd read the reviews, but also seen the cheap price they were asking for our stay so took a gamble on the Pennsylvania. To be honest it wasn't that bad! Location : As most of the reviews have indicated the location is ideal. a tube station right outside the hotel giving access to virtually the whole city, and getting to some of the major sites on foot doesn't take too long (15 mins to Times Square, 5 mins to Empire State Building, etc.). Rooms : Our room was on the 16th floor and we had a pretty good view of both Madison Square Garden and 33rd street. The room was basic but clean, with 2 double beds which were comfortable. The bathroom wasn't great, the shower wouldn't turn off completely, but at least we couldn't hear it in bed and I'm sure they would have come and had a look at it if we'd bothered to call reception about it. The TV although old had a good few channels and room came equipped with both Iron/Ironing board and hair-dryer. Staff: The maids were all friendly and said hello when we passed outside the room and they kept our room clean. Reception staff were fast to check us in (we did arrive approx 15:00 which may have made the difference from the huge queues mentioned in other reviews) and also happy to chat about the hotel and the area. Additional : The cost of Taxi from Newark Airport to the hotel was $80 (that includes a tip) and $87 on our return journey back to the airport. I would recommend staying in this hotel if your looking for a cheap place to stay in a good location. The quality isn't great but the room we had was clean and the hotel made a great base for exploring the city, I'd stay here again (if it hasn't been knocked down by then as other reviews have mentioned)

“Bon emplacement, prestations moyennes” 1 nuit en chambre superieure. L'hotel est situé à 10 min a pied de la Galeria mais n'a pas d'acces direct. La Galeria est le seul centre d'interet accessible à pied.Le personnel, bien que trop peu nombruex est efficace et soucieux du confort des clients. Les suites sont de bonne taille. La finition de la chambre, comme souvent aux US n'est pas extraordinaire.
“not so great for cost” Very expensive...costly, so-so front desk, so-so breakfast, costly parking

“VERY average” I did not pick this hotel by my own choice but rather because of a work conference. I usually avoid the Holiday Inn chain, but I had high hopes for this one because tripadvisor users gave it several good reviews. I will admit this hotel had a few good things going for it . Unfortunately it also had several things that made me decide I would most likely never stay there again, and I will continue to avoid the Holiday Inn chain. As many other people mentioned it has a great location and you can walk to everything including the trolly/metro which is great if you want to avoid the pricey cabs. We had an easy walk to seaport village and a nice mall downtown, as well as many different places to eat. I thought they did a good job with the conference as far as stocking the room with food, regulating the temp, etc. I liked the lobby area and they have a great little pub. We had no problems with the shuttle service and the drivers were nice. They came and went as promised and on schedule. The room was located in the south tower and it was clean. The beds were pretty comfortable. The free wireless was great. Other than that it is very very no frills. My biggest complaints are the customer service and the noise. At about 9:00 every night we could hear a lot of banging and dragging of furniture from somewhere near us. It was definately not guest noise...it sounded like renovations or something the hotel was doing. It started promply at 9 every night and ended around 10:30 or 11. It was very loud and annoying, so I called one night. They played dumb and said they had no knowledge of anything going on that would cause such loud noises. Basically they had a very we-don't-care attitude. Also you will hear lots of beeping and honking and car alarms, as well as typical port noises, so just be aware that this hotel is in NOT in a quiet area. I know many of these noises cannot be helped, but slamming furniture around? I asked other people at my conference and they heard it too. Very strange. Another thing that sealed the deal for me and made me decide I would not come back is when I came down to the front desk to ask a quick question. I noticed one of the concierge workers was being very short and rude to the people in front of me. I waited patiently in line, and when it came my turn, they guy stared down at his computer and ignored me for at least 10 minutes. Finally someone else came over to ask if I had been helped. He never once looked up from the computer. Bottom line...if you tolerate noise well and you just need a clean bed to sleep in...and don't much care for nice pools and luxury...this is your place. But if customer service is matters to you, I would not recommend this hotel.

“Not Marquis” We stayed at this Marriott on San Diego's bay from 12/29-01/01. We booked it for 3 reasons. 1st we are Marriott Elite members. 2nd the hotel is pet friendly. 3rd location. We were very excited to check into this hotel to get away from the cold weather and ring in the New Year. We were royally disappointed. The hotel is undergoing an extensive renovation. The hotel lobby and common areas were recently redone and are beautiful. The rooms in the north tower were also redone and are nice and comfortable, but I would not say they are anything special. The south tower is currently closed for renovation. The hotel had a wide mix of people from families to people in town for the bowl game and New Years eve to people doing business next door at the convention center. While I felt the hotel was extremely busy, it was not out of control or very loud. After a short $14 cab ride with the most unfriendly cab driver in all of San Diego we arrived at the Marriott Marquis. Our check in was swift and we were in our hotel room with in 10 minutes. We were assigned room 419. a corner room on the 4th floor. Sounded nice, but upon arrival what we found was a very small room, with a tiny bathroom. We made the decision to stay and unpack and go about our day exploring the city. But we ran into problems when we got back. The room was so small we kept bumping into each other. The bathroom was so small that only one person could be in it at a time, which made getting ready extremely time consuming. At the end of the night we noticed the toilet would not stop running which kept waking us up. When we got up the next morning we decided we had to say something, Our rate included breakfast. So we went down to the first floor restaurant and waited to be served. The restaurant can only be described as a mad house. It was over run with families who let their children run wild. The staff was overwhelmed and slow. The hostess forgot to call our name and crossed us off the wait list. After waiting a half hour and noticing people who got their after us were now being seated we said something to the hostess. After saying that she called our name, which she didn’t because I was standing next to her the entire time, she sat us down. We immediately got on line for the omelet bar which was average, but extremely slow. Following our breakfast which took entirely too long, we went to the front desk to complain about the room and service thus far. The woman at reception was nice and apologetic and moved us from our 4th floor room to the 19th floor. Our new room was 1925. What you need to know about the hotel is the north tower is shaped like a football or oval. The largest rooms are towards the center. When you get to either end of the building the rooms get considerably smaller. This was evident from the second we walked into our new room and reinforced by the bellman who helped us move. Room 1925 was right off the elevator and was probably twice the size our original room. It faced the pool and had amazing views of the bay. The bathroom was much larger and had a separate toilet and shower area. It also had a much bigger closet and more drawers for storage. The great part about this room was it faced the bay and had fantastic views of the water and Coronado. We also we had a birds eye view of the Red Bull No Limits jump across the Embarcadero Marina. The service at the Marriott Marquis Marina was lack luster and the employees did not make us feel special being that we are elite members. For the most part we found ourselves frustrated with the service more than usual. There were several small instances, starting with our original room that all added up. One of the biggest was the lack of communication. After spending an entire day out we came back at 4:15pm to find our room was not made up. When I called down to “At Your Service” they said it was because we left our small dog in the room and not in a cage. I understand why they would not enter the room, but we really wished they would had told us that was their policy upfront. They tell you there’s a $75 pet fee up front. How come no one mentioned anything like “The maids will not enter your room for service if your pet is not caged or you are not there”? So that lead to me calling down 3 times for maid service. Each time I was told they were on the way. A maid finally showed up an hour and a half after my first phone call. Another frustration we had was paying for wine glasses. We picked up a bottle of wine along the way and called down for some glasses to enjoy it. The woman who took our request told me there would be a $3 per glass charge since it was a room service request. I find that ridiculous. And I have stayed in many other Marriott’s where there were wine glasses already in the room. Some good parts of the hotel, it’s location is great. It’s on the water. It’s a 5 minute walk to the Gaslamp Quarter. It’s a 2 minute walk to the convention center. The pools are very nice. The gym has been renovated and has all new equipment. One cool thing is you can take a water taxi from the hotel across the bay to Coronado, it’s $6 per person each way. It’s a 15 minute ride across the bay to the Coronado Marriott Resort and Spa. It was a relaxing ride and one of the best days we had in San Diego. I will say the walk from the Marriott in Coronado down to Orange Avenue and then to the beach was 2 miles. So there’s a lot of walking. But if you can do it, walk down to the Hotel del Coronado and have a drink and some food on the deck. You won’t be sorry. Other things about San Diego: Most of the cab drivers were not very friendly. Balbo park is beautiful and worth a trip to see. We had amazing dinners at two restaurants: Bencotto Italian Kitchen in San Diego’s Little Italy. Our second recommendation is Searsucker in the Gaslamp Quarter. Make reservations at both, you won’t be sorry and it will make up for the lack of service at the Marriott.

“Across the street from the airport ... location is everything” This is a very large hotel, a bit dated ... but, it's very close to the airport, clean and not too expensive. They charge you a bit more for a room in the tower, but go for it since the tower is closer and the higher floors have a better view (even if it's only of the airport). Chocolate chip cookies make Doubletree a favorite chain, but why do they (and other mid and high end hotels) feel the need to charge for internet service?? That's getting very annoying ... it's not worth $15 to $20 per night!! Stop it! Charging for parking is bad enough (but so close to the airport, that's understandable), but there's no excuse anymore to charge for internet.

“ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC - AGAIN!!!” I love this hotel! Everyone from the front desk staff to housekeeping, to bellmen, to valet staff, to wait staff etc., etc., are cheeful, friendly, kind and professional! The rooms are incredibly large and comfortable and the location in Greektown can't be beat. This is my fifth or sixth stay at the Atheneum and I honestly can't imagine staying anywhere else!

“Could be better” We typically...almost always stay in Marriott hotels. Residence Inns are good options for us as they have true suites which make it easier when traveling with small children. Although a little deceiving having "Sea World" in the name of the property. It's not actually near the park but the hotel is in a decent location if traveling to Sea World (15 minute drive). Overall the stay was average, but not near as good as other Marriotts in San Antonio. We stayed 3 nights and I had interactions with different shifts at the front desk. Each time the staff acted as if they did not have time for my questions. I am really a low maintenance traveler. The only request I had was for an extra blanket. I asked the lady at the front desk at 9:30...waited until 11:30...no blanket ever came. Breakfast options were OK, but have had better at the Towne Place Suites in San Antonio. The breakfast area is so small and gets so busy that it is very difficult to get any item that you want. This happened all three mornings. For a newer hotel, the carpet in our room had lots of stains and carpeting in the elevators were filthy. Fabric on couch looked dirty and roll away bed was VERY uncomfortable. With all the complaining I would actually stay here again, if nothing else for the location and the guarantee of getting a true suite.

“Nice Hotel, Good location” I stayed at the Omni with a few of my friends for 3 nights for a wedding in Austin. I was very pleased with the service and quality of the hotel. Pros: - Very friendly staff - Consierge was very attentive and welcoming - Front desk was helpful and knowledgable - When you called for towels, they were at your door in minutes - Great patio on the roof with a pool and hottub. Very fun and relaxing. - Fast elevators - Great food in the lobby, nice restaurants and bar area - Close to 6th street and many other downtown locations Cons: - The room felt like a motel 6

“I didn't know JW Marriott was in the Prison Business” Ok, I admit I'm going to be a little harsh here but hey... they put the JW on the name here so I figured this would be Marriott's top of the line hotel... well, such is not the case. Let's start at the beginning. The valet parking here is a whopping $28 dollars a day (well beyond the going DC rate which is about $20 a night). That wouldn't be all that bad if they had an efficient valet system but their tiny driveway frequently has cars backed up all the way into the street which is quite an adventure in DC's traffic. It takes a crew of about 6 to manage this mess. The lobby looks like a bad episode of Dynasty from 1985 and certainly pales in comparison with the nearby Willard (a true premium hotel) or the Omni Shoreham. I arrived at 2:45 and my room wasn't ready... yeah I know check in is at 4:00 PM but come on. They were kind enough to offer me a coupon for a free coffee while I waited an hour for my room... thanks guys. On to the rooms... standard Marriott fare with a touch of "West Wing Chippendale" to give the illusion of grandeur. This illusion fades fast when you pull back the curtains to see the bleak view of the interior courtyard. Yikes! I expected guys in orange jump suits to be getting their afternoon exercise in the middle of this thing. The prison metaphor continues with roped off entrances, an army of security guards, and obnoxious "show your room key for entrance" to the lobby signs everywhere. I don't think they would seriously turn away a patron to the hotel bar for not being a guest in the hotel but it sure gives the illusion that outsiders are unwelcome and makes you wonder who actually is staying in one of these average rooms... CIA, KGB? The healthclub was nice but I didn't know you could fit that many screaming children in a pool that small! (Yes I was there on the weekend... on the twelfth floor... with a stop on each floor each time I got on the elevator). Again, I apologize for being so harsh as there was nothing really THAT bad about the place except that I expected MUCH more from the Flagship brand of Marriott. Don't pay full price!

“Love this hotel” Every time i come to San Fran i stay at this hotel. It is such a great property - I travel a lot on business and will always stay at this hotel when i am in San Fran. The staff is incrediable and the rooms are great- Very quiet...! Love the view of the water ! Thank you for the stay.

“Charged for the safe again!” Having stayed and reviewed the motel two years ago I was ready to register with with coupon from the highway magazine and avoid the extra charge for the optional safe. Informed the front desk at check in I wouldn't be using safe and didn't want to pay the extra $1.73. The final bill reflects an extra $1.73 for "Safe with limited Warranty". In the summary the $1.73 is included under taxes. The coupon says $49 per night plus taxes. Apparently the motel believes they are justified in classifying the safe charge as a tax for advertising purposes. It's only $1.73 but just really irritating. Overall a good stay at a good value business. Clean rooms, better than average breakfast.

“Nice hotel - great location” Da es sich um meine erste Reise nach Washington DC handelte, bin ich schon einen Tag früher angereist und wollte mir unbedingt noch ein paar Sehenswürdigkeiten ansehen. Gerade für einen Wochenend-Sightseeing Trip könnte das JW Marriott nicht besser liegen. Alle Top-Sehenswürdigkeiten (White House, Lincoln Memorial, Capitol, etc.) liegen in kurzer Gehdistanz. Ansonsten verfügt das Hotel auch über alle Annehmlichkeiten, die man sich von einem Flagship-Hotel einer großen Kette in der US-Hauptstadt wünscht. Einrichtung und Ausstattung ist im gehobenen Marriott-Stil, nichts besonderes, aber durchaus angenehm. Bei meinem Aufenthalt sind mehrere Fauxpas passiert, die in dieser Preislage allerdings nicht vorkommen sollten: Kein Kofferträger-Service (Bellboys zu sehr mit ihren Zigaretten beschäftigt), um 8:30 Uhr sind bereits alle Regenschirme vergriffen, etc. Aber alles in Allem, war es ein sehr netter Aufenthalt in einem guten Hotel.

“Nice Stay for $200” I arranged my one night stay through Quikbook, at a rate of 199.00. With this rate in mind, I found the hotel very nice. It was clean, modern, safe and nicely located in Columbus Circle. The staff were friendly and fairly helpful for my few questions. The only drawbacks I found during my stay were the loud doors and cleaning staff that seemed to be yelling "housekeeping" all morning long. Minor issues...As has been mentioned, the rooms are small, there are no views nor real amenities. I would not pay the rates they list on their website (425 for the queen room etc.); even in Manhattan you can find a better room for that price. I only needed a place to sleep near Central Park for one night, and did little more than sleep in the room, so it was perfect for my needs at the reduced rate. Nice new option in the city.

“Housekeeping Ninjas” not sure how these Housekeeping ladies do it, but it is amazing. I took out my dont disturb sign, went out for a run at central park and back in 1hr. my room was clean spotless. everyday!!!! amazing service. big hotel but they treat you as a person. I didnt feel anyone was rude or anything as some reviews say. I was wearing casuals and am not the elite types but the reception staff was very pleasant.

“Great location and staff” We like staying at the Homewood Suites and the Hitlon Garden Inn at this location (they are each one half of the same building). The location is close to the Inner Harbor, Little Italy, and Fell's Point, so we never have to drive. The staff is also very friendly and helpful. The rooms on the Homewood size are larger and have a small kicthen (which we didn't need), but the extra space is nice. A great benefit for both hotels is the MAC gym that is connected to the building. It is a priviate gym with TONS of equipment, pools, and classes that are all free to use to hotel guests. Also, on the Homewood side, there is a free buffet breakfast each morning. Great restaurants close by include Pazo (Spanish tapas), Ciao Bella (Little Italy), Fleming's (Harbor East - wine and steak), and James Joyce across the street (Irish). Our only complaint, is that the valet parking is a bit high at $32 a day. There are some less expensive options around if you self-park.

“Mediocre & under renovation” I've stayed here twice, first in June '06, and again in Jan '07. While this review is specifically for the Jan '07 stay, both stays were comparable, Fri+Sat nights, and both were at a nightly rate of $55 via an opaque, prepaid, online booking service (I named my own price). The hotel's own website states: " Please note the hotel will be undergoing renovations from Nov. 1, 2006 until Mar. 30, 2007." My advice is: Do not pay rack rate here until after renovations are complete! On the upside, the room was well-furnished, with two double beds, attractive wall coverings, TV, ironing board and steam iron, free wireless & wired internet (more important than TV!), a small desk, and adequate lighting. There were nice soaps and shampoo/conditioner/lotion in the bathroom, along with clean towels, washcloths, and a coffee maker. As noted by others, the elevators were functional and fast. Climate control in the room was adequate. I also appreciated ceramic coffee mugs and glass tumblers (rather than plastic). And there was a sliding-door closet, with hangars and plenty of storage for luggage, etc. I was annoyed that there was not a luggage rack, however. On the downside... the bathroom ceiling was absolutely filthy with mould and peeling plaster, the grout was mouldy, and the floors stained. I'll stop there, because as noted by the many flyers, the hotel is undergoing renovations to replace all guest bathrooms "from the studs out". The worn carpeting and shabby draperies are also set to be replaced. I can only hope that the hard and uncomfortable mattresses will be replaced too. As noted by others, the rooms facing the hospital do experience sirens and road noise all night long, and I don't think the renovations will fix that. And renovating the tiny bathrooms won't make them any larger. I had little interaction with the desk clerk; however, I was pleased that my advance phone call at 10 PM the day of check in was sufficient for them to hold my room until my very late arrival of 12:30 AM. (Prepaid bookings are sometimes cancelled with no refund if you don't check in before midnight of the arrival date. Fortunately that did not happen to me.) Aside from the items noted above which will be rectified by renovations, my stay was satsifactory, and the price was terrific. The outdoor pool was closed. Others seemed to be enjoying the restaurant, though I ate elsewhere. There isn't a lot of late-night dining in the immediate vicinity of the hotel, other than a pizzeria. There seemed to be a security guard out-and-about, so I always felt safe. Yes, there is a Red Line "T" subway station about two blocks away; the hotel has no self-parking and the adjacent garage charges $36/day with no in/out. (So if you're going to park, use the hotel's valet parking, which is the same price but allows in/out). There is no on-street parking available. I would stay at this hotel again, though I'd really want to find a cheaper parking option. I'm sure that after the renovations, this will be a much more attractive property.

“great location, terrible business center” Ok. Some great stuff first 1) great location "uptown" 2) very comfy bed, linens and awesome black out shades for those that like it very dark 3) valet is a cheap 8.00 per day 4) room rates were acceptable for being in prime location 5) great room service from food to extra towels-great job Corey! 6) Food is above average for hotel food and is not overly priced, there is room service 24 hours. If you want to be within walking distance to uptown/downtown/sports arena, etc this is great place. Plenty of stuff withing walking distance. Minor issues: Hotel room key stopped working twice and the elevators take keys to work (inconvienent). This was a hassle when i had to schlepp back to front desk twice to get me new keys. Bathrooms are way too small for a hotel this nice. 4 star room with a 1 star bathroom. Staff is a mixed bag. Some were GREAT. Kudos to Patrick and Corey and Charles. Others were snippy. I guess this is anywhere you stay though. Big problem: They have an awful business center. Their internet access is very expensive and does not work 1/2 the time. They require a credit card and they charge it 6.95 for 15 minutes of use. Yikes!!!! Then the computers kept logging off but kept charging me and i spent over 30.00 trying to send an email. Why would a 4 star hotel have such crappy service?? I complained to the front desk and all they did was take my credit card info and said they would reimburse later?? I asked if it could be taken off my room bill and they said no. I never did get Internet access but they let me quickly use the one behind the front desk. If you need to do business and need a printer, fax, Internet, etc do not stay here. Also, there is a great attached shopping mall and Starbucks to this hotel but they are closed on weekends. Again, weird. I am from Los Angeles and nothing closes. Staff said in NC stores are closed on Sat and Sun. I would have really loved this hotel had i not had these Internet issues. This is very important to me. I need technology when i travel. I still do not know a final total of my Internet fees as they could not tell them. Omni staff claims they are not responsible for thier onsite business center. BS.

“Enttäuschendes Hotel im Financial District.” Das Hotel ist im Financial district gelegen, also in einer sich nicht durch ausuferndes Nachtleben auszeichnenden Gegend. In Gehweite ist die Faneuil Market Hall mit ihren Restaurants, dort ist auch abends etwas mehr los. Zum Aquarium und zur Central Wharf ist es ein paar Schritte mehr, aber alles ist gut zu Fuß zu erkunden. Im Hotel selbst waren zum Zeitpunkt meines Besuchs gerade Umbauarbeiten, was aber nicht zuvor kommuniziert worden war, daher die deutliche Abwertung im Gesamturteil. Mein Zimmer war zum Hof hinaus, es war recht klein und abgewohnt. Trotz meines HHonors Gold Status sah man sich außerstande, mir ein besseres Zimmer zuzuweisen. Es sei nichts anderes frei... Das Personal an der Rezeption war nett, aber das housekeeping war unmotiviert und nicht wirklich um die Sauberkeit der Zimmers bemüht. Es gibt in Boston wirllich bessere Hotels in gleicher Preislage.

“A good experience” I stayed at the Embassy Suites La Jolla during a workweek in August 2005. Overall I was pleased with my stay, and if I ever get back down this way again, I will stay here. Check-in was during the evening rush, not too fast and not too slow. My Hilton HHonors Gold status finally paid off as I was assigned to a huge corner suite on the 10th floor (which is their HHonors floor). I have no complaints about the room. It was clean and quiet in there. It was big enough that I could host a workgroup of six for a breakout session during one of the days we met. There was wireless internet access in the room for $9.95/day. It tended to bog down during peak periods, but was still much better than dialup. The exercise room is on the lobby level, off to the side of the pool. It was well equipped with three treadmills and three bikes, plus a stairclimber or two. Adjacent to the University Town Center across La Jolla Village Drive, there is a 24-Hour Fitness facility for those who want more of a weight workout. I did not check to see if the hotel gives out passes to this gym, but it would be nice if they did. Speaking of the University Town Center, it was quite convenient to walk over there for lunch and grab a quick bite at one of the many fast food vendors. We had dinner at a Mexican restaurant adjacent to the mall, Cozymel's, and for a chain it was quite good - and fast, too. Laundry facilities are in the ice-and-vending area on floors 2 through 5. There is no charge to use the washers and dryers; bring your own soap and fabric softener for a completely free experience! Parking is $12 a day, as previously reported. Make sure you get a parking card when you check in, I didn't and had to pay the fee when I left the lot. Not a big hassle but just something to remember.

“etwas älteres Hotel mit sehr schöner Lobby” Das Hotel liegt sehr Zentral in Chicago. Das Zimmer war ruhig, komfortabel und ausreichend groß auch wenn man das Alter nicht mehr ganz verleugnen kann. Die Lobby ist traumhaft schön und lädt zum Verweilen ein. Weiteren Service habe ich nicht in Anspruch genommen und kann daher dazu wenig sagen. Aufenthalt war auch nur eine Nacht.

“Four Stars For Sure” My mother and I spent the Mothers Day weekend at this recently renovated property. Our room was on the 22nd floor with a wonderful view of Broadway. The window tilted out to open for ventilation - something I really enjoy as an alternative to a steady diet of stale, manufactured air. The room was clean, well appointed and large by New York standards. The carpet was clean and appeared to be fairly new with no worn or stained areas. The beds were as marvelous as you'd expect in a high end Marriott property. The bathroom was large, very attractive and supplied with Lather brand soaps, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. A magnified shaving / make-up mirror was a nice addition. The shower was a real treat - glass doors, a huge shower head that produced a soft rain-like flow and a generous supply of soft, white fluffy towels. The only negative here was that the bathroom was not vented - a common fault even in the finest hotels. The recently renovated and ballyhooed lobby was a bust with me. The furniture was trendy but not overly comfortable. The music was loud and poorly chosen. We attempted to have a conversation with a friend in the lobby and ended up shouting over the obnoxious music like we had blundered into a Techno club. I'd recommend Maxie's deli on the corner of 7th avenue and 48th street. Grat sandwiches and the chocolate cappucino cheesecake is mandatory. A good stay in a wonderful hotel. As for price - let's just say that I was fortunate to be able to use my Marriott Rewards points.

“Excellent Customer Service around issues” I helped my son book an overnight stay at Crowne Plaza hotel. We booked through orbitz.com which I will warn you, does not always give accurate information regarding "rules" around a hotel stay, even when speaking with a person live. Our challenge was to find a nice hotel near United Center as my son who is 20 and his girlfriend had tickets for the Bulls and Hawks games back to back. My son is on a budget and so it was important that there was no high fees for parking. Also since he is 20 we wanted to make sure there were no issues with him checking in. Again, booked through Orbitz who confirmed there were no restrictions on age and also that parking was free. My son arrives at the hotel, calls me very freaked out to find out that first, he has to be 21 to get the room and second, there is only valet parking at a cost of $30 per 24 hours. He handed the phone to the manager, Michael, whom I spoke to and explained the due diligence I did in booking the room, the information received from Orbitz and also that the write up on Orbitz.com listed parking and valet parking indicating there were two options for parking. This situation could have turned out to be a nightmare but Michael exhibited excellent customer service in handling the situation. He asked that I send him an email confirming I would take responsibility for my son and second asked I email the description listed on Orbitz and our reservation regarding no mention of fees with parking. I did both and he not only let my son and his girlfriend get the room, he waived the parking fee for the night. He handled the situation well! My son said the room was great, they ordered room service and learned the hard way how much that cost and had a great night watching the Bulls down the street! Thank you Michael and Crowne Plaza Chicago for making my son's weekend trip wonderful. I would highly recommend this hotel!

“Upgraded rooms are nice; older rooms are very dated” I recently stayed at the Omni for a weekend trip to Austin. It's in a good location downtown with some things within walking distance. However, in Texas style, you'll need to drive most places. Valet parking is available for $25/night. Friday night we were given an old, unrenovated room. While it was spacious enough, the decor and finishes were extremely dated and not of very high quality. I thought to myself, "This does not look like the pictures I saw before booking." Regardless, it seemed alright, until 8 or 9am on the dot Saturday morning (I can't remember exactly, as I've tried to block this from memory) when the renovation construction in the room DIRECTLY next to ours started. That would be sawing, drilling, and hammering into the other side of our wall. We'd had a late night out on the town the night before, and these were VERY unpleasant sounds to wake up to. The loud music played by the construction workers over the noise did not help. We talked to the front desk and told them about the unacceptable noise and that we would need to move, which they said they could *try* to accommodate (note: they did not guarantee the move, which I think is the wrong thing to say here). Luckily, late that afternoon they said they could move us. We got switched to a newly renovated room which was a bit smaller but had high end finishes and no construction noise. They also offered to comp us with free breakfast (we already had plans) or wine (we were about to leave for the evening), so they instead removed a night's charge for valet, which was a nice gesture. While the 2nd room ultimately ended up being nice and they made up for the inconvenience, the stay was overall a wash, based on the not-so-nice room the first night and the ridiculously loud (and early!) construction noise. I also felt a little misled based on photos of the property I'd seen before arriving. I likely won't stay at the Omni in Austin again but do give them credit for making my stay a lot better for the 2nd night.

“A cut above” Ok, so I was skeptical of this hotel being as charming and elegant as so many say it is, but after finding a great deal on booking.com, I had to give it a try. It really is a beautiful boutique hotel, full of old world charm and modern sophistication. I actually wasn't all that impressed by the lobby, but it grew on me.
