Especially after I saw the beautiful room I was staying in, which was supposedly an "upgrade" and certainly felt like one. This was a fine guest room with a hallway at the entryway leading to the bathroom that added to the overall size of the room. I was on the 12th floor and the views were quite a sight. My only complaints would be the shower, which was kind of a pain or manipulate and get the right temperature and pressure, but that could just be me, and some rather tepid and conniving desk attendants. Luckily, though the receptionist had changed the following morning and I was assisted by a very friendly woman who gave me an extra 30 minutes of check-out time.

“Average hotel in good location” Got via Hotwire for around $100 so not too bad value. Once upon a time it would have been a fancy place, now it is somewhat faded and in need of a revamp. But the location is good and the rooms a good size. Shame about the internet charge, but you can sometimes find it free in the Lobby. Do not confuse it with the much fancier Hyatt Regency down the road.

“Awesome Hotel!” We stayed at this hotel for 1 week for business and leisure purposes, and were glad we did. Check in was very smooth and the front desk clerk, Jason, was very friendly and helpful as well as all the staff. We went up to our 2 double bed suite, on the 11 floor. Our room was very clean and since we had a suite one part of the room was a living area and in another room there was the sleeping area. We are glad we paid the extra 15$ extra a night to have a very nice suite, it was well worth it. The bed was extremely comfortable and the pullout bed in the living area was surprisingly comfortable too. I would ask for a high floor because we could hear all the street traffic and the fire house must have been near the hotel. Once you were asleep it was not that loud that it was wake you up but it didn’t rely matter to us because by the time we got to the hotel room we were all extremely tired anyway. The pool and hot tub were awesome. The hot tub was the rite temp, and it was extremely big and the pool was a nice size too. They had a sauna that I never went it and the workout room was massive with all the workout equipment in the world. We did the Dinning special, you got 25$ a day to spend at the hotel restaurant (which was not very good) and star bucks. We paid an extra 10 dollars a day for this but we never used all of our credits and they did not roll over. They did not take the 25$ off per day, there for they charged our credit card. After 4 calls to the hotel this problem has finally been fixed The location of this hotel is awesome, rite in the middle of everything; it was a block from the red line 2 blocks from the Magnificent Mile, and very close to navy pier! For the price we paid we would return without a doubt. Thanks courtyard Marriot for such an awesome stay!

“Centrale ma non eccelso” Un buon punto di riferimento per chi si trova a Boston per una visita di qualche giorno e non vuole spendere troppo. L'hotel dimostra tutti gli anni che ha, ma è abbastanza centrale, vicino alla metropolita, ed ha un buon rapporto qualità/prezzo, considerando che Boston è una città alquanto cara. Le stanze sono spaziose (nella mia doppia c'erano due letti matrimoniali) e mediamente pulite.

“Away form anything else.” This is a fine and comfortable hotel. But it is a $10 cab ride away from anything and everything you want to see, do or eat in Philly. The rate was good and it sure beat staying at the airport when everything else was sold out, but I'd rather stay closer to the action next time.

“Best of Both Worlds - Superb Location and Superior Accommodation” Compromise is inevitable in selecting hotels. Superb location often means sub-par service and amenities. Well, this hotel did not get that memo. The prime location – adjacent to Petco Park, heart of the Gaslamp district – is accompanied by superior service and accommodation. I arrived at 12pm and was immediately greeted by the valet attendant. After a brief exchange, I proceeded inside to the front desk. A room was available, and the front desk associate gave me an efficient yet comprehensive synopsis of the hotel’s amenities. The room was faithful to the Marriott brand- clean, comfortable, and a bit of style. The view included Petco Park, and my only wish would have been a balcony to enjoy the gorgeous evenings. Another in-room plus is the litany of television channels. While I have found many Marriotts include the minimum, this one offered more than enough cable channels to pass the time here. Finally, if you are more of an internet person, note that in-room internet is not included in the rate. Once you step outside the room, the hotel’s selling point is the 22nd floor. The outdoor bar is a local favorite on the weekend. And the exercise room boasts the best view of any exercise room I have encountered to date. The equipment was standard – treadmill, stair climber, weights – but the one downside is that the treadmills do not have personal television screens. However, the aforementioned view is an acceptable trade-off. In terms of food and beverage, I indulged in room service one evening. While the menu is not generous on variety – not one pasta dish - there are unique options including flatbreads, jumbo shrimp, and jadori chicken. Perhaps they make up for variety with speed - my order arrived hot in less than 20 minutes. If you have access to the lounge, there are no surprises here– breakfast, snacks, and evening desserts. As with most Marriott properties, the lounge is closed on the weekends and re-opens Sunday night. Finally, the valet attendants were amiable and responsive. At most, I waited 10 minutes for my vehicle. Valet parking was included in my rate; otherwise this is a $36 fee per night. There appeared to be more economical self-parking options in the area, but I did not utilize them. In summary, this hotel is an exceptional choice for the Gaslamp District. Valet parking and internet will add $46 per night, so take this into account. Pros: No trade-off here between location and amenities/service Cons: Very expensive valet parking, internet fees

“Solid, good value” Stayed 1 night passing through in September 2003...if you are passing through and need a place to rest this is as good a place as any and cheap (40-45 w/ advance booking).... comfortable and clean but the pool is indoors and tiny....

“Amazing hotel in a wonderful location in a great city” My wife and I recently had the pleasure of spending seven days at the Park Hyatt Chicago. Located adjacent to Water Tower Place, the Park Hyatt is perfectly situated on Michigan Avenue and convenient to many of the city's hot spots. My hotel reservation was made through American Express, so we received several great bonuses, including: continental breakfast; 4pm checkout; $100 dining credit; and every third night free. This is an outstanding deal for the hotel and I highly recommend anyone considering this hotel to take advantage of this offer. The room we were given was on the 13th floor and had a great view of the city. The room itself was lovely and well outfitted. The bed was incredibly comfortable with a feather duvet, pillows, and mattress cover. Although the becoming-standard flat-screen television was missing, the inclusion of a DVD player more than made up for it. Sliding panels between the bedroom and luxurious bath allowed the opening of the two rooms for extra ambiance, especially if using the beautiful soaking tub. The true jewel may be the supremely powerful and hot walk-in shower, along with the incredible bath products. The doors are also very heavy and make for excellent noise blockers; despite being close to the elevator I was never aware of any noise from the hallway. The staff of the hotel was wonderful from the very first moment. As a sidebar, member of the group U2 were staying at the hotel during the same time and the staff did an outstanding job managing the crowds and the extra level of excitement around the hotel. They never let the other activities interfere with them serving other guests. We had the opportunity to use the excellent gym, steam sauna and pool facilities, all of which were spotless and well maintained. The staff was always attentive and helpful while we were in the facilities. We also took advantage of the hotels dining options. Each morning we enjoyed the Park breakfast (basically a continental breakfast option) in the lovely NoMI Restaurant. During the evening there are two basic options/menus: "indoor NoMI" features several ultra-fancy selections including superior sushi; "outdoor NoMI" features a delicious menu of sandwiches (Kobi burger, anyone?) and sushi to enjoy while looking over the city.

“Eventually a great room! Dreamy location, but SLLOOOOWWW elevators.” Our first room at this hotel was oppressively small. You expect a small room in a NYC hotel, but you also expect a) to be able to walk around the furniture without tipping over, and b) maybe -- MAYBE -- having a glimpse of sunlight while you are there. Not so with our first room -- tiny, and overlooking a long brick-lined alley, which prohibited any sunlight from entering the room. We asked for a better room and were immediately provided with a generous suite. From there on, we had no complaints. Fantastic location for NYC exploring! Two blocks from a train, about 4 stops to midtown, 3 blocks from Central Park. It was really fantastic and easy! The elevators are ridiculously slow. Add an extra 5 minutes to any plans you may have because of this. Tip: the hotel does not have a restaurant, which means several things, including no room service. Tip - go to the Westside Market, which is pretty much across the street, and stock up on sliced fruit, cheese, whatever you want! All very reasonably priced, and very fresh. Tip: the hotel is NOT actually on Broadway, so it may be confusing if you are taking a cab and you give the address listed for the hotel. This address actually takes you to a storefront with giant "FOR LEASE" signs in the window, which is a bit stomach-dropping upon arrival when you mistakenly think that you are looking at your hotel. Incident: We happened to be staying there during the heat wave of 2011. Our last 2 days included temperatures in the 90s, with heat indices in the 100s. Our AC gave out that last evening and while we were just fine, knowing that we would be leaving in the morning, we tried to tell the front desk multiple times that they should not check someone else into the room, and they didn't seem to be particularly concerned.

“overfurnished undersized rooms, $15 for Internet, annoying music in lobby” It would have been one star, given the price of this place and the value delivered, but they are pet-friendly so I made it two. I come here on business and the folks I work for have some sort of deal with the W, but the rate is still over $200/night for a ridiculously small room stuffed with furniture. The experience starts with walking into the lobby at 11 pm and hearing dance club music turned up fairly loud. The hip young crowd consists of exactly two people working the front desk and no guests. So the lobby is totally empty, but the music is cranked up as though it were a happening scene. I grope my way through the dim lobby to the elevators where I have to use my room key to activate the machine. Then, like the boring business traveler that I am, I want to set up my computer. There is nowhere to plug in a laptop charger on the desk. Internet costs $15/day. The average Hilton Garden Inn or Hampton Inn is way more user-friendly. You get a room that is twice as big, for half as much money, and enjoy free Internet.

“Beats my high expectations!” We have visited NYC for many years, always for a week after Thanksgiving. The city is at its best and the buzz is tangible. Our experience of many of the grand hotels on Upper East Side has been varied. The Carlyle is a grande-dame, the Plaza Athenee too precious. The Pierre is the in a splendid position, but I can't justify the cost of the rooms. Walking along Madison Avenue at Xmas time, the New York Palace Hotel is awash with decorative festive lights and the most beautiful Xmas tree. Step inside and the theme continues, it is gorgeous! This year we spent a week at this magnificent hotel, rooms and service are top notch, but the position of the hotel is within five minutes walk of all attractions in mid town. It deserves the accolade of #1 hotel in NYC, and that includes the Four Seasons Hotel.

“Don't stay here if you don't light compact fluorescent lights!” I arrived late that evening and was upgraded to the presidential suite because there were no other rooms. I was particularly excited because the hotel had recently been renovated and the lobby was gorgeous. It was a very nice blend of traditional and contemporary decor in light cream/beige tones. The presidential suite had also been renovated, but was done so in very dark, masculine colors (burgundy, black, and greys). It was definitely a guy's hangout, not a place that most women would want to be. To be fair, it was well appointed, with a sitting area, powder room, a lounge area (all ready for a poker game) with a very large screen TV, separate bedroom with another Samsung flatscreen, a dressing area, and bathroom with whirlpool. The hair products were excellent. Room service breakfast came quickly and was very good, although the allegedly "fresh-squeezed" juice was not. Excellent service all around. My chief complaint? Every light had compact fluorescent bulbs in them. I know they are environmentally friendly, but the light they give off is absolutely depressing, particularly with a cold and stark modern decor. It just did not make for a very warm, pleasant environment. . I may start bringing my own lighbulbs (just a few) on trips from now on. . . .

“Nice hotel but bring own pack and play” I had a business conference here and extended the stay to visit nearby family. Like many hotels, wireless was extra. We had our baby with us and asked for a crib and fridge. Despite being requested at the time of reservation, we had to call down once we arrived. Both were brought to the room...the fridge worked fine. The crib was an old wobbly pack and play. On the positive side, they provided baby shampoo and lotion.

“Funky, fun and I was lucky and got it cheap” An old hotel revamped into a trendy nightspot. Take a torch to find your way to the lift! Upstairs the rooms are large and light. Great location next door to the ACT. I was lucky and got it through Hotwire for $90 a night. At that price it was a bargain, the rack rate less so. Pity as always about the internet charge

“Good service, bad room.” My wife and I took advantage of a low weekend rate and stayed at the Hotel Madera for a couple of nights while visiting friends. We've stayed at other Kimpton properties and like the brand. The room we got was not so good but the service we received was exceptional. We checked in relatviely late on a Friday and were assigned the one available room in the class we reserved in. It was Room 101, the only room on the first floor and is located in the back corner of the floor past the hotel and restaruant offices. The person working at the desk was overly apologetic when we were checking in about us getting room 101. She said that we could switch rooms the following night if we wanted but that they were booked. She was almost too apologetic. I told her we'd be fine and I would let her know if we wanted to change rooms. The room itself was fine. It wasn't amazing, but it was good enough. It was large and the bed was comfortable. There seemed to be a missing wardrobe or somethign as there was an empty alcove. Some of the light fixtures seemed to be broken, but the lights themselves worked fine. My biggest complaint was with the shower/bathtub. The drain did not adequately do its job and it seemed that the shower/bathtub was incorrectly installed as the floor was loose and rose and fell with each foot fall. Also, one corner of the room bordered the kitchen for the next door restaurant and you could hear people chopping vegatables through the wall. It was not enough noise to keep us from sleeping, but it was noticeable. With all this being said, my wife and I didn't care enough to switch rooms. I am confident that we could have switched the second night if we wanted to, but we didn't want to pack our stuff up to move. When we checked out we mentioned the bathtub to the person working at the desk and it seemed that he genuinely cared. Although the room was not amazing, I was impressed by the service we received. One morning we were heading out and the free coffee and tea had been just removed. We asked the desk clerk about it and she gladly went into the nearby kitchen and got us a couple of cups of coffee. I will recommend this hotel to others and come back myself. I will ask not to get Room 101 though.

“Great Value; 10 Minutes to Downtown” Selected this hotel due to price and amenities as the downtown hotels were premium priced due to a convention in town. This is right off the Highway and from my top floor room, I had an amazing view of the downtown skyline and endless suburbs. While I did have a car, I found that I was able to get downtown in 10 minutes and over to the vibrant restaurant scene on McKinley in about the same time. PS, there are very few dining options walking distance from the hotel but the same is true of downtown. The rooms are clean and updated with the latest Renaissance scheme. My room came with a buffet breakfast which was extraordinary...the restaurant is beautiful and anything from waffles to egg creations and fresh fruit. This is a big hotel but updated nicely from it's 80's roots. An overall great value.

“Nice location, good price” I am glad i stayed here. The staff was very nice. Got a decent price on the room, i think it was like $70 or so. Keep in mind they get you for $25-30 a night to park. They also lost my car for an hour when i was checking out. The location is nice, next to public transportation and within walking distance to the Giant's ballpark. The room was small and the bed was smaller, but all in all it was a fun place to stay, different than the standard motels, so fun. Would look into staying here again if i returned to SF because it was good deal and nothing negative can be said about this place. G Man

“nice hotel, friendly staff, def better options for parking, location” I liked the hotel. It wasnt anything special but the staff was extremely friendly and was clean. The parking is a complete rip off at $30 a night. I actually found parking on the street near by the hotel for free. All street/metered parking is free in the city of San Diego on weekends. The hotel was in downtown but still isnt the closest walk to all the main tourist attractions. I got a great rate through priceline name your price, so I thought it was an excellent deal. Also has free wifi and depending on the room you may receive a great view of the city of SD. If I go back to San Diego I probably would stay elsewhere but if I got another great deal like I did I would stay here again!!

“Location, location, location” Lets face it. The best attrribute of this hotel is the location. Literally steps away from the heart of Times Square and all the Broadway theatres, The room was comfortable and clean. TV was flaky (could not mute it) and the staff was NYC gruff. But overall, a nice stay at a great location.

“Clean, nice but little bit tricky to find restaurants.” Stayed for 3 days with my mom and my 1 yo, clean and very nice room! We visited relatives and visited Dallas Arboretum and botanical garden. We didn't have a clue to find restaurants until the relatives brought us to a short cut road to get to it (a lot of restaurants). No charge to parking (that's a plus!). I wasn't familiar with Dallas's road (with a rental car from the airport) got a charge for a 'toll' way. ** The date that we traveled is not 'correct' We traveled to Dallas May 2010

“great for families” We stayed here for 5 nights in the middle of November and absolutely loved it. We stayed in a 2 bedroom condo. We arrived very late at night and were had to phone the security to obtain keys but this was very easy and the chap was helpful. The condo was brilliant for us, 2 bathrooms and 2 bedrooms large kitchen and living room. We also loved the washing machine and dryer which came in handy with two young kids. The place was also spotless which is always nice to see. The only down side was that the resort was quiet and the lazy river was cold but thats not the fault of the resort. Its a stones throw from seaworld 5 to 10 min by car. The shop was expensive for food so be sure to bring all the essentials with you. The best bit was definately the heated pool and slides. We went there every day. Shops and restaurants are a short drive away, we didn't eat at the resort it was a bit expensive.

“Would go back” Check in easy and fast. Hotel clean, but room small. Great breakfast--waffles, fruit, eggs, sausage, juice--really good. Room a bit small, but clean and large TV to enjoy. Nice pool area. Hallways, lobby all clean. Front of hotel well lighted. Tip: parking is $12 a day, but behind hotel is a 24 hour lot that is only $5 a day--you only have to put money in slot. Short walk to River Walk/River Center Mall. I would stay there again.

“Looks high end...but not” Big hotel, smallish rooms. Air conditioner barely adequate and noisy. Overall found staff to be inadequately trained. Restaurant waiter disappeared. Waited ten minutes for a bellman to appear. Meeting rooms poorly ventilated. Pointed out two minor maintenance issues in fitness room; still wasn't addressed two days later. Front desk staff was friendly.

“Nice hotel, good service.” Stayed one night while passing through Baltimore. Very nice hotel - quiet, elegant. Excellent service. Room was comfortable with upscale amenities. Bed was probably the most comfortable I've ever experienced in a hotel. All phones in the hotel were out the night we were there. A little frustrating, since we'd planned on ordering dinner from room service. Instead, we skipped the hotel restaurant and walked to a steakhouse on the harbor, then walked along the water and back to the hotel. The location was great - very close to the National Aquarium and Inner Harbor attractions. Would stay there again.

“Great Experience in DC” We stayed at the Grand Hyatt during a fun-filled trip to DC. The location was excellent - an easy walk to the Mall and the Smithsonian museums. We had a tour of the White House, and it was just a ten minute walk there, too. The room was clean and adequately appointed. We were particularly pleased that there was a refrigerator at no extra charge. The staff were very friendly and accommodating. We took the subway system from the stop in the basement of the hotel - talk about convenience! While this is primarily a business hotel, we had no problem feeling comfortable there on a family trip. The meeting space is located on the lower levels (out of the way of the vacationing families and vice versa) and the openness of the Lobby area makes it feel like a sanctuary within an urban setting. We would stay here again, and I would consider using this property for a business conference as well.

“Nice Visit” We stayed at the Hilton Polaris after going to the OSU - Minnesota BB game. We were able to check in early then head out to visit Columbus before the night game. The hotel is new and the employees were very nice. and helpful We stopped at the bar after game and it was a nice relaxing time. The rates were very afforable compared to the downtown area. We will stay at the Hilton Polaris again for our next OSU visit.

“A couple of stays later... nice place” I stayed here twice; once for a conference, and once for a quick overnight on a roadtrip. Both times I was impressed. It is a really large conference hotel, so the entrance is rather grand. There are multiple food/beverage options on-sight, and it is located right downtown. It is really easy to walk to the mall (where there is a movie theatre) or to multiple restaurants, or the canal walk (with museums). The front desk staff are really nice. It is also easy access to the expressway. My secret for downtown Indy is we usually priceline something for under $75, but with the nationwide boycott of Hyatt Hotels, we had to priceline a four-star instead of a three-star. We ended up with a room at the Marriott. The room was large-ish, comfortable, and quiet. A really nice stay. My other secret for downtown Indy is that if you're in town for a quick overnight, it is possible to find street parking for free. You just have to keep an eye on the signs and make sure you go put money in the meter in the morning before they start ticketing.

“Superb hotel but a bit noisy” Everything about this hotel was brilliant except we had a problem with the traffic noise. I must admit we live in the quiet country in the UK so maybe we are not used to it, but we have been to NY many times and have never had this problem before. Our first room was on the 7th floor and we could even hear people laughing down on the pavement at night. The hotel was excellent and moved us to the 17th floor for our last two nights. This was certainly quieter but we could still hear the traffic. We think it was coming in via the air conditioning units which are under the window. However, both of the rooms we had were very big, clean and modern. We had a studio room with a little kitchen area which was very handy. We had a small maintenance problem in the second room and this was sorted out immediately. It has been said before in reviews, but the staff at this hotel are wonderful. You very rarely have to open the front door as there is always someone there. The bar area is nice and all of the reception staff are very helpful. We have stayed at the Waldorf before which is opposite this hotel and loved the location, which is why we tried The Benjamin. We could not fault the hotel, but may not stay there again purely because of the noise which stopped us from getting a good nights sleep.

“Management Failure” We booked throught Agoda and there was a booking glitch on the duration of stay between agoda and the hotel. The management were extremely rude and actually accused us of lying at one point. Made me make international calls to agoda to clarify and insisted they had no role to play with agoda. To long a story but if the management is reading this pls lets do it online and say what you had told us. U have to pay for everything from internet (very very slow dont bother paying) go to the nearby starbucks or pubs. U even have to pay if u need a mini fridge (they have one but its filled to the brim with their minibar so u cant chill your own beer/wine). No coffee maker either.

“potential is there, less than ideal stay for me” Rooms are quite large especially for NY and well-designed and laid out. The hotel is pretty new so they are very fresh. The bathroom and closet in my studio suite was quite large. Large windows with great light. Great sheets/ comfortable but quite low bed. Bathroom products were nice and unique but lacked basics like a shower cap or Q-tips. I had to call for those. The location is okay. Neither uptown nor downtown, but accessible to both. Lobby is small but chic and nicely fragranced. There is one hotel car available for the guests, so if you are really lucky you might get it. Not great or exciting when you walk out the door. There were a few problems though. They did not make up the room two of the three days I was there. The first day they missed both cleaning and turn down. The second day I had to call for them to fill the mini-bar which was only done only once b/c I called and asked on a three night stay. They give you free soft drinks but don't refill much. The third day I did accidentally leave the do not disturb sign but called the " personal assistant" ( their name for concierge) and asked at 2 00 that they override that, take the sign off and clean the room. They did not do the day cleaning or turn-down even though the assistant said she could help with that and make sure that it would be done. Asking for cleaning and minibar refill is far too basic to have to deal with in a property that is built to be a five star. Stay here if you primarily need a large NYC room and don't care too much about the rest. Hopefully they will iron out the rest of the kinks.

“You come to the Four Seasons for the service....” We (my family) chose to stay at the Four Seasons as we had a corporate rate and were interested in doing some sightseeing in Philadelphia. As expected, the service at the Four Seasons was wonderful. Everyone was courteous and solicitous. Here is a quick summary of my stay: +We stayed in an executive suite - which had ample room for 2 children under the age of 7, as well as my spouse and me. The kids slept on cloud-like double beds in the bedroom area and the adults made do on the pull out sofa in the living area (which was hard and uncomfortable). The room was clean and tidy; the carpet looked newer and the draperies were clean and pristine. It was a nice looking room; not spectacular. +Unlike other Four Seasons I have stayed in, the bathroom was not on par with the usual standards of that hotel chain. There was only one sink in a very large vanity area and the bath/shower was a combination unit. Upon checking out the bathroom, my spouse wondered aloud if the hotel had been built for another chain. +The service was solicitous - at one point there were three hotel employees in the room to make the pull out sofa, as well as put in a bed rail for my son, and attend to general house-keeping. +Critique - it was a busy weekend. At times, the bathrooms in the main lobby were unkempt and out of toilet paper and tissues. In addition, the Four Seasons typically prides itself on its child friendly trappings - but there was no toy trolley for the kids, etc. I think the staff may have been overwhelmed with the high volume of people.

“One of the Best Hotels we've stayed” We travel enough to know a great hotel and this is it! The staff was A+. The atmosphere was A+. The rooms had such charm. This hotel was a former police headquarters and when they did renovations, they did so properly. The rooms were a bit small though. However, they take care of every detail in making you feel that you are their number one priority. We'll be back for sure!

“Great hotel! Walking distance from the airport.” I had a last minute business trip to Boston. A majority of the airport hotels were sold out. This hotel is very expensive. (I paid over $275 for my stay.) The signage from the arrival terminal to the hotel is nonexistent, I had to call the hotel and ask for directions. The room was clean and cozy. I had room service. The service and food were excellent. There is a bar, restaurant and coffee bar onsite. Service was nice and everyone was friendly. It was a great stay!

“Smallest Room I have Ever Had in a Hotel” My wife and I stayed here the night before returning home from a business conference. This was without a doubt the smallest, most cramped room I have ever had in any hotel. We picked up a couple of foot long subs on the way here and ended up having to eat them on the edge of the bed because there was no room for two people to sit comfortably anywhere else. That is unless you wanted to sit on the floor by the front door. On a positive note, the staff member who checked us in was very friendly and professional. The entire hotel was very clean and well maintained. There was complimentary wireless internet that worked well. The one feature I liked very much was the multimedia interface box that allowed me to connect my laptop to the 32 inch flat panel television. I wish all premium hotels offered this device. We left too early to try the free breakfast so I cannot comment its quality, but the eating area appeared clean. My wife, who made this reservation, is a Gold member of the Marriot Rewards program. If we were given a room this ridiculously small with Gold status, I can only guess how bad it is for regular guests. We stayed in the Marriot Residence Inn on 44th street the night we arrived and for only $10 more we had a full kitchen, living area and separate bed/bath area. I will definitely not recommend this hotel to anyone. I have had larger rooms in hotels in Cambodia, Nepal and Thailand.

“Views!” Just spent a few nights here with my husband. Had a beautiful, large corner room complete with stunning views of the lake! Used the fitness center every morning & jogged while looking straight at the John Hancock building. Fantastic! Ate lunch at the hotel restaurant & had a phenomenal beet salad! SO delicious! Front desk upon arrival was very personable & friendly. Concierge recommended Michael Jordan's Steakhouse for us 1 evening being that we were interested in steak. Best filet I've ever had! Close to shopping & Magnificent Mile!

“Lousy service” I stayed for 3 nights and had to change the room 3 times, first it was noise coming from the room above me, second it was clogged toilet which they could not fix in 2 hrs, that too in morning hrs.. you could understand, third time it was the shower not working...The hotel itself is great, its a boutique hotel, curtains, linens are different in a better way. All the three rooms were designed with Orange theme...location is good, although it says right in middle of Gaslamp quarter but I would say its good 10 minutes walk...and given San Diego Downtown is not the safest one, I wouldnot recommend walking. There are few restaurent near hotel but they are not the best. Parking is valet only and $32 per night. I dont agree that the hotel matches 4 star quality, service is horrible for the price you pay.. Indigo hotels are nice but this one certainly doesnt live upto all the hypes

“Disappointing, Poor Service” I was on a business trip in Manhattan and had stayed previously at two other properties, Residence Inn Times Square and Affinia Dumont, both I can highly recommend and have written previous Trip Advisor Reviews on. Check in was average. Welcome was not welcoming. Small and busy lobby. This building is a bit old and the rooms reflect that. I was issued a small but quiet room. The bed was comfortable. There was a desk and a chair. The chair was a bit hard to position since the room was so small. I could hear a little noise from adjoining room. The bathroom was small too. The room was moderately clean but not thoroughly clean. Water pressure and temperature were okay. The plus in the room was there was a mini fridge. The plus with this property was the conciere lounge which had well stocked refreshments and snacks. Also the exercise room was well equipped too. The property was nearby to my workshop at PWC headquarters on Madision. I was attending USC CEO Stratgegy workshop and earlier in the week, attended a workshop at Cornell ILR's conference center on 34th and 5th. Prior to my last day I looked at bill to date and notice that I was charged for a local call. I went downstairs and told the front desk person because of my Hotel membership level, I get free local calls. She told me they do not honor that at this property. This was typical of the service at this property. I don't know if the property mgmt. treats that staff poorly but I do not know that their staff does not treat their clients well. This is one of the worst Marriott properties that I have stayed at and I will do my best not to stay here again! There are several other properties nearby, Double Tree Metropolitian, Waldorf Astoria, Omni and several others. I do not recommend this property if this location is not critical, I recommend the Affinia Dumont or the Residence Inn, Times Square.

“Good location” My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary. The location is great. We were able to walk everywhere. Including the Buckhorn Saloon, the Marketplace, and the Alamo. The parking cost 10 dollars. I thought that the room we stayed in needed more light. It seemed very dark. Also, it was not the cleanest room. I found a number of items (chapstick, etc.) left by the previous guests. We were not happy with the bed and the pillows seemed hard. There was no shampoo, so the maid left us two conditioners instead. When we asked for some, she had a difficult time tracking some down. The free breakfast was nice. They also had a waffle machine. I think the best thing about this hotel is the location. I'm still not exactly sure why it is called "historic." The hotel opened in 2003, and from what I read it was previously a Mexican food restaurant. It was decent, but nothing to "wow" over.

“Location makes it "no brainer" for me” My room was $209 a night and as earlier reviewed, there are some better rates to be found a little further out. For me however, the location is worth it when I'm in DC. I'm within walking distance to the Convention Ctr I can get to the White House in 10 minutes and stroll the Mall after a hectic workday. The neighborhood is SAFE, the ESPNZone is a block away and a quick escape before bedtime. The attached photo was my room #1152 and it is a corner and quite nice although no monument viewing from the 2 windows. I must commend the service. There was an accident on 12th St corner as I was preparing to leave to the Airport. The young porter walked in the other direction to hail a cab for me while I waited with my luggage. I received excellent restaurant advice and can recommend Beck's Brasserie - great Chimay beer. Hope this helps.

“Excellent Stay” Stayed here two nights while moving my son into college in DC. Received an excellent rate from an Omni promotion (stay 1 weekend night, get 1 night free) and was upgraded to a suite with a sitting area separate from the two queen bedroom. The hotel is beautiful and our room was very nice and spacious. Bathroom was modern and clean (a bit small, but understandable as it's an old hotel) with nice toiletries. As members of the Omni Select Guest program, we received free wireless internet, nightly turndown and morning beverage delivery (although I did not receive the cards for the beverage service at check-in as I was supposed to - I had to call and ask for them). The hotel is beautiful and historic and we enjoyed checking out the different wings and gardens. It's true the hallways were sometimes loud at night. It's in a nice neighborhood with plenty of restaurants in the surrounding blocks. I would absolutely stay here again.

“Very nice hotel” I stayed at the Rivercenter Marriott for two nights on a business trip. The room was large, clean, and well appointed. It included a large, HD TV and input panel (to hook up your computer, DVD player, or other electronics, but you need your own cables). Service was excellent, from check-in to check-out. I ate at the lobby bar and at the meeting functions. The food was tasty. They room included a card that you could use to specify what time you wanted maid service--a nice touch if you're staying more than two nights. The A/C unit was reasonably quiet. I didn't notice it if I wasn't actually listening for it. Hallway noise was better than average. I didn't notice a lot of doors slamming. I don't know how full they were, but there was an 800-person meeting at the hotel. The only negative point (and it's hard to blame the hotel) was the freight trains. I was on a high floor but could hear the train horns clearly--at almost all hours. It's hard to blame the hotel. I'm sure all the downtown hotels have this problem and it may not be possible to avoid. Although I didn't take advantage of the location, this hotel is attached to the Rivercenter Mall and gives access to the Riverfront district. I wish I had had more time to explore. I would definitely return to the Rivercenter Marriott if I return to San Antonio.

“Great location-very small rooms” I like staying at Hamptons andHilton Garden Inns so I knew what to expect here. I thought the rooms were smaller than the other NYC Hilton properties I have stayed at but I've stayed in smaller. Great location.

“Still Amazing” This is my wife and I's second visit to the MGM Grand Detroit. The check in process was very smooth. There is a coffee/espresso machine in the hotel lobby for guests, a nice touch. The room was spacious and clean. We requested late check out and it was no problem. Nice and easy. The staff at the hotel is top notch. This is our go to hotel in Detroit when we want a couples getaway.

“Great SF Location, but "Small breakfast"” It's a great San Francisco location closed to everything (the cable car, SF, Golden Gate .....) Small room with two small queen bed. Free parking. They should change the blanket ! Very noisy if you leave the windows open (lombard street). The breakfast : coffee or juice, some fruit (mostly bananas) and a cake. The staff was not very friendly.

“Pessimo hotel, stanze terribili, arredamento terribile... niente di positivo” Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel purtroppo per due notti durante una tappa del nostro viaggio di nozze.. la camera che ci hanno riservato era al secondo piano, e dava proprio sulla piscinetta dell'albergo presa costantemente d'assaldo da ragazzini urlanti... Era praticamente impossibile riposarsi. La camera era decisamente brutta, nememno troppo pulita. Da dimenticare.

“Would stay here again” We stayed at this hotel on a business trip in Feb. 2012. The hotel is clean, in a great location, and has great water pressure. Room layout is convenient. Beds are reasonably comfortable. Best thing about staying here is the hot cookie you receive upon check-in. (They're really good cookies!) We'd definitely stay here again.

“Divine beds!” We were only here for one night, as part of our cross-country trip - but we wished we had been able to stay longer. Without doubt, the beds were the softest, most comfortable of our trip! The location was convenient, the staff friendly and helpful, our room was very spacious, room-service was excellent and the atrium was very attractive. Would happily stay again!

“We'll Be Back” This was our first official stay at a Quality Inn and I must say that we'll be back. For starters we arrived very early but to our surprised our room was ready. No we did not have to wait to 3PM. We just checked on in and was well on our way for the perfect stay-cation. Upon entering the room we discovered that we did not have a remote. Called the front desk and within minutes they immediately brought one to us. The room was spacious and clean. Wireless connection was excellent and the location was perfect. Shops, restaurants and Orange Park Mall is literally just a minute or two away. Breakfast was delicious. Consist of waffles, eggs, sausage,biscuits, toast, bagels, muffins, pastries, fruit, assortment of cereals, juice, coffee, tea and milk. Overall we were very please with our stay and will diffidently be back again. Thanks Quality Inn of Orange Park for a very pleasant getaway!

“Comfortable hotel on east side.” If you are looking for an hotel on the east side, this could be a good option. It is far east at York, so if you have business on the west side, it is far. ($13-14 to Javits Center. I had an upgraded suite room (thank you) with fantastic views of 59 St Bridge and up/down York ave. Lots of amenities in room typical of 4 star hotel. Robes, sewing kit, shaver, toothbrush, nice soap & shampoo. NO coffee makers in room. Coffee bar downstairs in morning, not included w/room. Walls a bit thin if you have noisy room neighbors. I liked the room decor w/ zebra stripe carpet and hounds tooth pattern pillows. Small bathroom - but this is typical in New York. Pleasant staff. I'd consider this a 3 1/2 star hotel with some 4 star amenities.

“Great Location” I went to Los Angeles for a work-related conference, which was held at the convention center. I am not a big fan of the neighborhood around the LA convention center because there's really a lack of a neighborhood feel around it. Also, there is a lack of reasonable food options around the convention center. Instead of staying too far from the convention center, we decided to stay in Little Tokyo, which is relatively close to the convention center. Being a big fan of Japanese food and culture, it was a perfect solution to our problem. The hotel itself, however, was not as nice as I hoped. Basically, we got what we paid for. Our room was clean and relatively functional, but was very small. No special amenities. The doornob, I think, was in need of repair. However, free internet access was great. We had a great government rate deal (I workk for a public benefit corporation for the state of New York) which included a room, free internet, free "continental" breakfast, and a visit to their spa. However, by no means we felt "unsafe." In terms of safety, I would feel much less safe around the convention center. If this hotel was located in a boring neighborhood, I would never recommend this hotel to anyone. However, for those who will be going to LA for a convention, I highly recommend staying at Miyako instead of any of the typical "convention hotels." The hotel is centrally located in Little Tokyo, more centrally so than other hotels. We found too many wonderful places to shop and eat around the hotel than any other hotel we have ever stayed in our travels. We had breakfast mainly in their "Take 5" lobby cafe, but we tried the Japanese style buffet breakfast in their 2nd floor "Tamon" restaurant twice. The breakfast was pretty good, since it was either part of the package at "Take 5" or discounted at "Tamon." However, I think it is sort of silly to stay in the hotel for your food, since there are a lot of options just outside the hotel. Also, the hotel is very close to a couple of museums (Japanese American National Museum and MOCA Geffen), both of them are worth visiting. The spa area on the third floor is clean and nice, probably not the nicest spa I have been to. I may not recommend it unless it is "free." There is a coin operated laundry area, also on the third floor. In summary, I highly recommend this hotel to anyone who needs to stay in downtown LA, especially for conventions. What Little Tokyo offers more than makes up for a old and tired look of the hotel, as well as their quirky customer service. However, if you have no interest in Japanse food and culture, this location is probably not recommended.

“With character but without class” Found the Diva not very comfy and convenient but it does have a style of it's own and gives decent service. Smallish rooms and cramped reception and a bit noisy. Got good advice on eating and getting around town by the concierge.

“My favorite hotel” I should qualify my review by saying that I have a hard time being critical of the Peabody. I think I have been too charmed by the romanticism of the place to critique anything. I travel weekly and must admit that the beds at the Peabody are THE MOST COMFORTABLE beds I have ever slept in. Even the smallest rooms (and I have stayed in the smallest) are comfortable and beautifully decorated. The bathrooms are stately and the toiletries are above-average. If you are bothered by small rooms, reserve an executive room (for approx. $50 more a night) for a beautiful room with lots of space. The hotel itself is beautiful and welcoming. The staff is, for the most part, very friendly and willing to help. I have encountered a few employees over my numerous stays who seemed a bit lackluster, but they are outnumbered by the good. The only real critique I have is of their room service. Breakfast is decent (about average), but I have tried several of their dinner items and have rarely been pleased. I'm not sure which restaurant the food is coming from, but it needs help. I have dined in the Grill restaurant and found the food to be acceptable.

“Great Location, Good rooms, bad rooms just depends” Stayed at this property for three nights for a conference. Based off its Tripadvisor rating would not have stayed here, unless designated as the Conference location. Booked a Tower room in advance as based on previous reviews those rooms had been recently updated and reviewed well. Upon check in was told they were "over booked" and they placed me in a 9th floor King room with an attached suite. Really, as a solo traveler i didn't need a big suite, and truly all I did was walk through the suite when I came and left. My King room was small, with a poor functioning AC. Bathroom was even smaller. I was let down to have a room as was described in other poor reviews. It was fine, but not what i had paid for. This room had standard tube tv, (not the plasma that the tower rooms have) and was just old and tired. The rooms don't have wireless internet and cost 12 dollars a day. I believe you can get wireless access in the lobby for free. The plus is the location of the hotel..great for everything in Boston and the people that work are very nice. I would not pay full fare to stay here, but if you win on Priceline or get a good rate through AAA, or some other consolidator it may not be too bad. If I return to Boston for any kind of travel I will not be staying here. It needs to get catch up to the year 2010 and get up to speed.

“Bay View Premium Room Was Good” We stayed at the Bahia for 2 nights prior to a cruise from San Diego. In spite of horrible weather, we enjoyed outselves. The location in Mission Bay is convenient, across the street from the bus stop. We took the bus to Old Town where we could get the trolley to downtown, including the cruise ship terminal. (You could go all the way to TIjuana on the trolley if you wished.) Other than our initial taxi from the airport, we did not need a rental car. Despite some of the previous reviews, we had a very nice room which was clean, comfortable, and quiet. We were upgraded to a premium room (no. 364, on the ground floor of the Marina building) with a kitchenette (which we did not use). I took a walk around the property, and it was evident that the building we were in was one of the newer ones.

“Attractive, clean and convenient” My husband and I attended a convention here and stayed for three nights. We like having an extra bed to put things on so we got a double queen. It was clean and comfortable, with good-quality comforter and thick towels. Service throughout the hotel was friendly. There are free computers in the hotel lobby, but you pay $12.95 if you want Wifi in your room. There's a business center that also charges for Internet access, so use the lobby computers--they are in a separate section so there is some privacy. The lobby is large and has an attractive seating area that's located away from the front desk area, so you have some space to lounge, and there are free copies of USA Today. We ate dinner in the hotel restaurant on the last night of our stay. I don't generally expect much from chain-hotel restaurants, but the food was surprisingly good. There's a Peets Coffee in the hotel, which is a bit overpriced compared to a freestanding Peets or Starbucks, but it was very convenient for breakfast. (There is a Starbucks several blocks away.) It closes at 2, which is a bit strange for a hotel location. There is also a frozen yogurt shop, but it closes at 4, so if want a snack or a coffee after dinner, you're out of luck. We peeked into the sports bar, which is modern and nicer than the typical, cheesy hotel sports lounge. We didn't have a chance to use the pool or spa. The convention center is attached to the hotel and is pretty nice as far as convention centers go...I've seen a lot worse. The downtown location is walking distance to the arts district so I was able to get away for two hours and see the Gaultier exhibit at the art museum - highly recommended. There were a few restaurants within walking distance, but keep in mind that downtown Dallas is very spread out and very few people walk, so at night it may not be the best option. There is a trolley down the street, although I didn't find out where it goes. Overall, this was a good value - we paid $135 for our room.

“If you're in Washington, stay here...” The Washington Sofitel is my favorite hotel in my favorite city. The staff is very helpful. The rooms are on the small side but definitely comfortable and romantic. The bathrooms are spa-like. It is located near the White House, metro station, and museums. What more can you ask for? Although it can be expensive, watch for deals on Hotwire.

“Très pratique” Hôtel sans surprise qui correspond aux standards Embassy Suites. Parking gratuit. Grande chambre un peu sombre mais très confortable Bonne insonorisation Permet après un long vol de bien se reposer pour affronter les longues routes américaines. Petit déjeuner compris : Copieux et correct dans le traditionnel patio. On vient dans ce type d'hôtel pour trouver de l'efficacité et non du charme. Typiquement l'hôtel pour une étape et non un séjour prolongé Bon rapport qualité / prix

“Standard Marriott, aber beste Lage am Riverwalk” Das Marriott Rivercenter liegt direkt gegenueber des Marriott Riverwalk. Es hat aber leider keine Balkone im Gegensatz zum Riverwalk. Dafuer sind die Zimmer neuer. Das Hotel ist ansonsten ziemlicher Marriott Standard, nichts aufregendes aber man wird auch nicht enttaeuscht. Die Lage ist perfekt fuer San Antonio, man ist in wenigen Minuten direkt am Riverwalk oder in der Rivermall. Wuerde das Hotel wieder nehmen, aber das Marriott Riverwalk mit den Balkonen bevorzugen.

“Construction going on all around this hotel” Stayed here for 2 nights. The hotel is being upgraded so construction is going on at present. Also, there is so much construction going on around the site that it's not pleasant sitting around the tiny little pool. The pool deck is so small that one subed almost reaches into the water. The room was spacious and clean. It had a microwave and fridge. There are numerous TV channels and it seems to be used a lot by business travellers rather than tourists like us. We visited the Frank Lloyd-Wright house which was indeed worth the trip. We also shopped at Arizona Mills Mall. There is another HIE right beside the Mall and that location would suit toursits better. We also visited the cinema there and ate at Carrabas nearby. The breakfast was pleasant and regularly filled up by staff. We found the location difficult to find as 6th Street is not on a major junction with traffic lights. If you don't know the area you need to look for a right turn from the Interstate. Once we saw the sign we were OK. As a tourist, I wouldn't stay here again as there are better locations.

“Wow!” We were so pleased with this hotel. We have done quite a bit of traveling this summer, from a cabin in the woods to cheap motels to high priced hotels and all have had issues that made the stay unpleasant in some way, not this place. Everything was in great shape, comfortable bed, quiet, good shower, friendly staff and for our needs a perfect location.

“Cheap but not a pleasant stay” The front desk staff was rude and made a favor to make a reservation for us. He didn't gave us any kindness. Even didn't felt secure while gave him my credit card altough it a branded motel. The room wasn't that clean and the area wasn't look that safe to me. At least they had a small breakfast in the morning.

“Highly recommended hotel close to sights, shopping, restaurants and transportation” I stayed here over Thanksgiving for 2 nights. The rate was $89, which was low compared to other comparable hotels I saw when booking online. I was highly satisfied with the amenities and convenience of this hotel. I previously lived in Chicago for a long time, so I knew what to look for in a hotel location. It is only a couple blocks from the el, and even closer to the bus stop. There are so many good restaurants and shops nearby. The lobby are rooms are pleasantly decorated. The staff was very helpful and had handouts available at the front desk with information on attractions and recommended restaurants. The included breakfast was abundant and convenient. It was so nice to have a refrigerator and microwave in the room. I would definitely stay here again.

“Won't be back to this one” Stayed here 12/01 - 12/03. This was my second stay. Had a confirmed reservation for a king room - ended up with a queen even though the hotel was half full. The deadbolt lock did not work on the door, and after I requested that it be fixed and gave them all day, it was not fixed. There was hair in the shower. Worst of all, the one glass that was in the room had been wiped clean, was not washed or replaced while I was there. Makes one wonder about cleanliness of other items. Had to wait 15 minutes at 7:15 in the AM to check out as no one was staffing the front desk. I will not return to this hotel. This is a very nice facility, reasonably priced, with very poor management.

“Right outside the center of downtown, nice location on the bay” Great place to stay in downtown SD especially if you can catch a good rate. My friend works for Hyatt and got us a room on a Saturday night for $85. We were throwing a going away party for a friend. The pool area is very nice and staying here allows you access to all the greatness that downtown SD has to offer. There are some good restaurants and lounges at the hotel as well.

“Nice and Trendy - Awesome” My wife and I celebrated Valentines Day with a stay and dinner at this hotel. This was our first time ever staying at one of the W properties. In a word “sweet”, this place is very trendy and located in the heart of DC. When we arrived the staff treated us very well in so much they gave us a an upgraded room without any prompting from either of us. When we arrived at our room, more of the wow factor, the room was a display of art and functionality Everything was unique as though an artist came to the room and arranged the furniture and place the pictures and displays. I highly recommend this hotel as a place of choice. In addition, the J&G restaurant food was pricey but excellent and well worth the cost.

“A solid business hotel with great service” If you don't like 'business' hotels the kindness of the Renaissance O'Hare staff will win you over. If you do like cookie-cutter business-focused hotels you'll be surprised by larger than usual hotel rooms and nicer than usual decor. That said because it targets a corporate crowd I despise the fact that it still charges for in-room wifi. All and all a solid hotel.

“Good business hotel” I was at the Marriott for a meeting of my professional society. Overall, I liked it. The room was clean and well-equipped but a bit small. There are plenty of grocery stores and restaurants within easy walkting distance so you're not stuck with paying hotel food and restaurant prices. Business services were decent with one “miss”. I was moderating 2 panels, so I really appreciated the fact that they had A/V people walking in before sessions and asking if everything was OK- technical issues with the equipment could be resolved quickly and easily. They also had a single in-house number to call for support if you needed them at other times. The “miss”- one of my panelists was stuck in traffic and called the hotel trying to reach me. They told him I wasn’t registered there. I’d been there for 4 days at that point. We also found the elevators very slow when sessions finished up; sometimes we waited forever and then 3 showed up on the same floor at once. The high-speed Internet was consistently reliable, which I can’t always say for many hotels I’ve used. You have to sign on daily unless you get the “wired for business” package ($9.95/day) when you check in. Oddly, every time I signed in it gave me a choice of a $14.95 rate or a $9.95 rate and I always chose the $9.95 one even though I hadn’t bought “wired for business” and $9.95 is what I was charged. Note there’s a 15% “Internet tax” on top of that. Nasty. The hotel offers shuttle services to and from Midway and O’Hare every 15 minutes. It’s cheaper than a cab- for the 2 of us it was $38 one way. An alternative is the subway/train system (Grand is the nearest stop) from the airport for $2 but it involves a change of train, which is even worse if you have bags. Two warnings about the shuttle bus: first, we were waiting in the lobby and one came and went without anyone announcing it. So keep an eye out the door. Fortunately, we weren’t in a hurry and got the next one. It’s also “first-come, first-serve” and they don’t take reservations. Ours stopped at a second hotel and couldn’t pick up all the people who were waiting for it due to lack of space. We were skeptical about the one-hour estimate for transit time to the airport when we got into a traffic jam (this was a noon departure from the hotel) but it was almost exactly an hour door to door. You can get tickets for the shuttle at the Concierge desk and they can add it to your room charges. The pool was decent- a nice length but narrow enough that when there were 3 of us swimming laps we had to duck out of each others’ ways as we passed. The Fitness Center had enough equipment that I noted treadmills available at 7 AM. Overall, I liked this hotel and would return if the price is right.

“a step above a hostel -- but only a step” We had the 2 beds only room -- it was about 8 X 8, with 12 inches between the beds and double that at the foot of the beds. Two people could stand in the room, but just barely. The window air conditioner was ancient, with a broken grill, missing knobs, etc. It was not a pleasant place. The kitchen was the lowest grade, junkiest stuff you could imagine. No coffee maker, no clock in the room Bathroom was reasonable, a decent size, and the lobby was OK too. The closest of the two subway stops was on a line that pretty much went only to Brooklyn and the financial district and the other (Grand Street. ) was more useful, but several blocks away. The neighborhood is fascinating: chic galleries next to bombed out bodegas. Its a walk to anywhere, but if you like walking (I don't) great neighborhood to be in.

“very nice” I thought it was very nice. It's in Japan town with lots of places to eat. Fillmore is less than 5 mins walk and they have nice restaurant too. I always stayed close to union, but I like this location better now because you can find street parking easier and you can park for $16 per day at Japan center which is cheap in San francisco. Room was nice, especially their bathroom. They have 2 showers and seperate toilet. I wish they had an actually coffee maker because I always bring my own to make. I realized it doesn't matter what part of time you stay, San Francisco is a loud city. I heard silent all night long, and I'm glad I took my year plugs. It didn't help it was 4th of July weekend plus fillmore jazz festival going on. | would recommend this hotel to anybody. You have to remember it's not a walking distance to union or fisherman's warf, but bus stop is very close and easy to take.

“Bang For Your Buck take Two” I could not agree more with the recent review by Queenbee19. I too have stayed here several times thanks to Priceline and it has been a great deal in a perfectly fine hotel. Yes...the area is very mildly sketchy thanks in part to the nearby bus station and Chinatown. However, walk a block the other way and you are in the heart of Center City. Easy to get to the Kimmel Center, the historic district, the subway etc. As for the hotel, it is very clean and comfortable. Check in was nothing special but fairly friendly and quick. The room was very clean and comfortable - especially the bed. The room however was showing slight signs of age. Some scuffs here and there as well a Philadelphia guide book from 2005-2006! (Perhaps an oversight). Parking is no baragin ($26 per day) but never is in a city. A very slight annoyance can be the elevators. All the rooms are on high floors above a parking deck so at peak times, waits can be a little annoying. There is a nice bar with a decent view on the 10th floor but it closes pretty early so plan accordingly if you want a nightcap. Literally 20 feet across the street is a Wa-Wa - that was super handy for a late night snack or morning coffee. All and all a very good stay...I would surely stay again.

“Great for an overnight stay” I did not spend much time in this hotel as it was just an overnight after a flight cancellation. The shuttle was quick and efficient. I was given a suite as a Starwood Platinum, although I literally just walked in the room and went to bed. Rooms were clean, quiet, and comfortable. Beds were comfortable. Bathrooms were clean and functional. I wouldn't hesitate staying here again.

“Perfect location / Average Room quality / Overpriced” This hotel is in a perfect location, right near all the action or at least walking distance to it. The price however, $350+ for a petite room was awfully high. The quality could be greatly enhanced by simply adding comfortable bedding. Yes it was small but thats NYC. The lobby is very impressive and the staff was very nice. Doubtful I would stay there again as the next day I stayed in another hotel around the corner for the same price and it was of much better quality.

“Good, but not quite up to the usual Doubletree standard” This hotel isn't as nice as other Doubletrees-- for one, the architecture reminds you of a government office building from the 60s, but it's perfectly fine inside. The showerhead wasn't well stuck to the wall so it would slide down, but hey, we still got a comfortable shower. The plumbing in the bathroom seemed to need some updating, too. The pool looked well-kept and inviting, though. The staff were perfectly nice and I saw them cleaning up an unfortunate set of dog-pooped shoeprints in the foyer that someone tracked in. Parking: Free and well-lit. Food: The restaurant breakfast looked perfectly nice, but the Denny's across the way is less expensive, though, of course, not as nice. Location: I have to agree with the earlier poster about the location: it's a little strangely placed in a big cluster of hotels. Surprisingly, then, there's not much in the way of restaurants or places to go for a walk around there. There's a divey-looking "massage parlour" across the street from this hotel that doesn't really invite you to go for a walk or hang out around the hotel's neighborhood. So I'd say this: it's a good location because you're a quick drive in to downtown Dallas and some of the cuter neighborhoods around Lemon Ave and Uptown. But forget it, if you just want to do much around this hotel, because all that's there is antique restoration studios (some quite nice, acutually, but it's all mixed up and kind of too far to walk around between) and more big hotels.

“Large and beautiful room” My room was large because I paid 10% more to get an Executive King room, which is 40% larger than the normal (Deluxe) room. It is well worth it. I stayed in a Deluxe room on a previous visit and the modern decor was elegant both times. The hotel lobby is large and beautiful. The gym is excellent, although for some reason they seem to have two of one type of weight machine and none of another (i.e., two lat pulldown machines, but no low row.) My room was right next to the elevators and I could occasionally hear the machinery, but it was not bad, and I am very sensitive to noise. Many hotels have heating and/or A/C systems that are noisy, but this one was quiet, so it was easy to get a good night's sleep. I was on the north side of the building, away from LA Live, so there was no noise from their music etc. But on the previous visit I was facing LA Live and noise was not a problem. There is, however, one problem, and that is not with the hotel itself, but with its location. If you are going to an event at the Staples Center or the Convention Center, they are just a few steps away. But if you are not driving and want to visit the main part of downtown L.A. or go someplace else in L.A., you either have to walk four blocks to the Red Line subway stop or DASH (Downtown Area Shuttle) bus stop at 7th Street, or take the F DASH bus on Figueroa Street, right by LA Live. The F DASH runs every 10 minutes on weekdays and every 20 minutes on weekends.

“They never claimed to be an Aman resort” On the Ave is a nice little hotel in an overall residential section of Manhattan. They do not claim to provide the ultimate in luxury and like too many hotels, they overuse that term. This is a reasonably priced hotel in the middle of a large city - expectations must be appropriately adjusted. The standard rooms are small, but have excellent sound proofing and extremely comfortable beds. They look just like the website photos. The service was friendly, but not effusive. Unfortunately, in todays world, excellent customer service is a luxury. The surrounding blocks on the upper west side are not tourist areas, with minimal nightllife and few restaurants beyond coffee shops. A little research by reviewers would likely cull many of the negative opinions. If I needed to be in this area again, I would return to OTA.
“We love this place!” We stay here every time were in Austin, you can't go wrong, great service, super beds

“great location, nice hotel” The location of this hotel is ideal, right in the heart of the Gaslamp District, directly across the street from the convention center, and right by one of the trolley stops. It was really wonderful to stroll out every night to enjoy the Gaslamp's night life and to feel very safe doing so. I would be a bit leery staying at some of the hotels in the outlying areas of the Gaslamp, as many areas of downtown clear out at night. I walked to an evening reception at one of these hotels and was harassed and followed for several blocks. Any of the hotels within a block of the conference center, such as the Hyatt & Marriott, would be safe, though the Hilton is the closest to both the restaurants and the conference center. The Hilton was nice -- everything in good condition, nice decor, clean and with a courteous staff. That said, I had expected that at the price I was paying it would a little more spectacular; I guess you are paying for the prime location. I had just stayed at the Holiday Inn - Old Town at slightly more than a third of the price of the Hilton, and the rooms were the same size with the furnishings at the Hilton just slightly nicer, the one exception being the beds. The beds at the Hilton were the plushest I've slept in at a hotel, very comfortable mattresses with two down comforters. I was a little thrown by the wet bar. There was a note on it said the fridge was equipped with an electronic sensor and if you moved anything in it and didnâ t put it back in 20 seconds or put anything into it you would be charged $20. I got the feeling they suspected their guests would be sneaking out to buy cheap items to replace what they used.

“Great location but starting to fade” When I stayed here A few years ago it was modern and everything was perfect. Now the rooms are looking tired, towels are thinner, carpet is the same they have been using for years, dull. I think the Westin brand needs updating . Starwood have invested a lot of money into the W brand and have updated Sheraton but Westin has got left behind . The location of this hotel is what sells and the service is very good. Please can you open the main restaurant at 6am, a lot of East coasters are up early!

“The only downside is the location, which actually isn't so bad.” Lived in NYC for many years and after coming back for a visit, this hotel was what we got for a decent price on Priceline. The hotel itself is great. The rooms were surprisingly decent and good-sized. The staff were helpful and there was always a cab available when we needed one. The only major downside is the location. Which in the end, wasn't so bad and since this visit, I have stayed Downtown again. At night, the area is relatively empty but feels safe. It's a 23 dollar cab ride on non-peak hours from the UWS. There are many trains nearby so it's all very easy and quick. Tribeca is really close and staying here finally let us explore that area (previously lived in Midtown and W Village). I would stay here again now that I am familiar with the area. There are great eats nearby and Sarabeth's is not too far!!!! Save your money.. spend it at Century 21 down the street instead!!

“We keep going back” With our daughter living in D.C., we have made many visits there in the last few years and stayed at many different hotels. The last 3 visits were spent at the Fairmont, because we kept having such delightful experiences. The location is wonderful, as it gets you out of the frenzy of D.C. itself and very close to Georgetown. The staff is great, as are the rooms. The beds, pillows and showers are heavenly. We have stayed on the regular floors and also the Gold level. The service on this floor is amazing, as are all of the amentities, but you do pay quite a bit more. My husband is a Fairmont Club member and we were able to use one of his upgrade certificates to get on this floor. This is our hotel of choice for all future stays!!!

“Excellent Stay” I just returned from the JW Marriott after staying two nights for a conference. I was very impressed straight from check-in. The lobby is large, airy and beautiful. Check-in was quick (and I checked in a little early). My room was really fabulous - and much more than I expected. It was a large room with a king size bed. My bathroom had a separate deep-plunge tub (that I was too busy to use!), shower and toilet closet. The bathroom counter had tons of space and there was a magnifying mirror. The bathroom was well lit, spacious and very clean. The bed in the room was also terrific. It was a good firmness and so very comfortable for me. The desk area was well-lit with good plug points and space. There was complimentary bottled water. Lastly, my room was so very quiet which as great. I wish I could have spent more time relaxing in it!

“Perfect Place to Chill” What a find, and a price to match! Everything about this hotel was perfect from the friendly clerks to the soft sheets and comfy bed. The service was impeccable, treated me like family immediately, and even gave me the location of the closest inexpensive garage. The room was large, particularly by San Francisco standards and I was treated like royalty. The only place I will stay in SF from now on....

“Convenient to LAX, Good Value” Before early-morning flights out of LAX, I've stayed in several LAX airport hotels like the Courtyard, Crowne Plaza, the Courtyard at Marina Del Rey, and the Renaissance (on many occasions), but I now prefer this Hilton. It's close to everything, so I usually grab dinner somewhere in MDR, Santa Monica, or Malibu and drop the rental car off and get a free ride from Hertz to this hotel for the night. I’ve found $99 rooms here many times, which is great, considering it’s a full-service Hilton property and the aforementioned hotels go for between $120-150. I guess Hilton is very proactive about keeping the rooms full every night, because it seems very crowded whenever I check in here. Rooms are all nice, clean, and up to Hilton standards, though the bathrooms are usually a bit old-fashioned (always clean though). There is a fitness center on site, a full service restaurant and bar area, as well as an executive lounge for HHonors elites. Both are nice but not exceptionally good. Overall, I will choose this property as my go-to LAX Airport hotel due to its location – you’re at the terminal in 2-3 minutes’ time, thanks to the free shuttles.

“Toilet paper and hot shower and ear plugs...” ...I knew that would lure you into this review. I recently spent 2 nights visiting old pals from grade/high school. Love Chicago. There was a convention downtown so the next best thing was to move North. We were all on a budget and The Days Inn helped us out with some volume pricing. It was set as a 2 night minimum but I think the value was great. First off it's a very clean, secure hotel. Staff is very friendly and get the job done. I never had to wait checking in or out. They serve a continental breakfast which I never cashed in on but it looked adequate. My room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Truthfully I didn't spend a lot of time in the room except for sleeping. The only criticism I have is that the hot water in the shower never really got very hot. My shower was right next to a window and I can only imagine in the dead of winter how chilly it might get. As or the toilet paper...well, kind of personal but if you're at all familiar with printmaking...I would say...I wouldn't wipe an etching plate with the particular roll that was in my bathroom. One last bit of business. It's a bit noisy in terms of people coming and going. The good thing is, earplugs are provided. Truth be told, every hotel should have this amenity. Oh yeah, one more note. I was told this is where the rock bands stay when their gig is on the North Side. All in all it was the right hotel for the money. These are trivial things for a two-night stay but could be a nuisance if you're there any longer.

“Enjoyable & Affordable Stay” We were in New York for only two nights and had struggled to find an affordable place to stay that would also be well situated and comfortable. Fortunately, we came across the Warwick. We were very pleased and the experience exeeded our expectations. The price was very competative, our room was large and well appointed, and we had a decent view of 6th Avenue. The Premium room had a large closet, a very nice although somewhat small bathroom, and was very spacious overall. We did not hear noise from any other guests, nor were we disturbed by anyone in the hallways. The bed was comfortable, the hotel was very clean, and the room was sufficeintly quite (11th floor) (. . . .there was some street noise, but this is mid-town Manhattan after all). The staff was exceptionally friendly, but not obtrusive. The hotel has a very classic grand old hotel feel. For example, our rooms had very nicely finished mouldings and a classic boutique hotel feel. The lobby was very nice, although always quite busy. There were two restraurants off the lobby. We didn't have a chance to try either, but they looked inviting. My only complaint, and it is minor, is that the elevators are small and when the hotel was busy, it could take a few minutes. That being said, this is an older hotel, and 9 times out of 10, we got an elevator within a minute or so. The elevators, as well as the rest of the hotel, have beautifully finished woodwork. The room stayed nice and warm, and the windows opened so you could enjoy the night air. The rooms were very clean and well maintained. The room had switches in 2-3 locations which could control lights all over the room, allowing you to turn lights on/off from bedside or as you entered the room. A very thoughtful touch. The location was fantastic. Just 2-3 blocks to Central Park. About a 10 minute walk to Times Square. Just a few blocks from Rockefeller Center. We took the E Subway train from Penn Station and only walked two blocks to the hotel. MOMA is accross the street. We arrived on the subway about 6:30, walked down to Times Square, bought some last minute show tickets from the box office (Nice Work w/Matthew Brodrick - Great Show), and still had time to eat dinner before the 8:00pm show time. Our price with an AARP discount was $285, which I thought was quite fair given the quality of the hotel, size of room, and location. I would not hesitate to return here and highly recommend it.
