“Big Hotel In An Arty Area” The Fairmont Dallas is Texas big with two tall towers and a lengthy lobby. Originally built as residential development, the property was converted to a hotel. Architecture and interior decor buff will larger concrete overhangs in place of balconies. Right in the midst of Dallas’ mod Arts District, you can walk to any the AT&T Performing Arts Center theaters or museums. If you have time, do this. The buildings are architecturally impressive. In the opposite direction find casual restaurants in the Old Town, or a more NYC- feel near Neiman Marcus. Like most hotels, some rooms are renovated, some are not. All rooms are spacious. Renovated rooms have granite surfaces, sliding glass doors, fresh wallpaper and paint. The bath products are in the midst of being converted from Miller Harris to Le Labo, Fairmont’s new bath amenities provider. Le Labo products have a nice consistency with a faint---almost unisex---rose smell. Based on interactions with the front desk, housekeeping and maintenance, the service was mostly excellent aside from an off night we had in the Pyramid Lobby Bar {where we had to ask to be served etc...}, and a concierge who was earnest and helpful, but a little glass half-empty. Perhaps isolated experiences? All in all, I would stay at the Fairmont Dallas again if I return to Dallas because of my Fairmont loyalty and points accrual. The hotel is EXCELLENT value {in comparison to other fairmonts and upscale hotels} for the price point paid. WHAT TO KNOW - free wifi if you join the Fairmont President’s Club {the hotel group’s free loyalty program] - there is no shopping mall within walking distance, the closest is NorthPark Center, located a $25 cab ride from the hotel - There’s a Starbucks in the lobby - Highly recommend: The Nasher Sculpture Center and Dallas Museum of Arts - Also recommend Private Social Restaurant, a 7-min drive away - If the gold floor upgrade is available at the time you purchase the room, I felt it was good value---the best value I’ve seen at any Fairmont, and I’ve stayed at close to 25 worldwide. - The Fairmont gold staff are incredibly helpful and having what feels like your ‘living room’ at a hotel makes for a more pleasant travel experience. - The city, mostly office buildings and not much residential, is pretty quiet on the weekend.

“Always Nice” This was our third visit to the Doubletree Times Square. We are always very happy and plan to stay here many more times. The rooms are clean and the staff is friendly. The location can't be beat. This is one of our favorite hotels.

“Great Value...Great Location” My girlfriend and I recently stayed at the Belvedere in NYC. We absolutely loved the Belvedere. We stayed on a high floor and did not hear all the noise that other reviewers were talking about. There is a fire hall nearby, but it is 2 blocks away, and we didn't hear it once. The main elevators are slow, but on our way out we noticed elevators at the end of the hallway for public use that are much faster. If staying in New York, stay at the Belvedere.

“Stale for Doubletree” They have recently refurbed the Fourth floor, however, the carpet and new paint cannot cover years of stale odor and bad upkeep. The service has always been ok here, but the quality of Hilton property is not here. The rooms are slightly small the beds are small and hard, the furniture is still old and worn inspire of the refurb. The TV's are old and huge. They just really haven't put effort into updating the hotel. The refurb was merrily a coverup. The history of this property has had problems with bedbugs but I haven't heard of any cases here in quite sometime now so they have this cured. On the plus side, this hotel is close, walking distance, to plenty of restaurants and sports bars with good food and also a movie theater. You are about 20 to 30 mins drive to downtown and about 10 mins from the Polaris Mall.

“Best Fairfield I've stayed at” I don't know why this is the only hotel shown in "White Marsh., MD" reviews. There is a Residence Inn on the same street and a Hilton Garden Inn and Hampton a block away...but in any case this is the nicest Fairfield Inn I've ever stayed at. I'd put it up against any Marriott Courtyard or SpringHill Suites and it's every bit as nice as the HGI and Hampton up the street. Very friendly, quality construction and here's a rarity: Flat Screen HD TV's AND the HD channels to go with it! Lot's of restaurants and shopping nearby. Highly recommended.

“Great Staff, Great hotel...” We couldn't believe it when the Courtyard popped up on Priceline for the price we bid. The staff was exceptional, the hotel was great, the location was fairly central (if you have a car.) The only issue was that the place appeared to be selling itself short. We put in a very low bid for our room, and apparently so did many of the other guests at the hotel. From the drunken college kids partying next to us and across the hall (screaming about coke at 4 in the morning) to the sketchy trashy looking guys in the elevator, we felt like we should have been at one of those chains with a number in the name. i felt bad for the people who were paying full price. The rooms were huge and comfy, the amenities were great. Loved it, all the way down to the extended pool hours.

“Flawless!!!” I have stayed at the Four Seasons in Boston 9 times over the past few years.....it's such a fantastic city hotel, surely the best hotel in Boston, & one of my favorite hotels in the US. :) The staff, from the Front Desk, the the Bristol, to Room service are all so amazing, kind, warm & utterly professional & polite. I recently stayed a few days ago & all was perfect, as always! I was in room 522 & this particular room felt quite spacious, but all of the rooms I've had are a nice size. I don't think I've ever had to wait for a room either, which is so nice when traveling! The rooms are quiet & have so many nice touches, including a Sachet in the closet, a jogging map of the area, a selection of current magazines, a small flower in the bathroom & plant in the room, etc. The beds are amazing, with great pillows!! The food at the hotel is really good!!! The Bristol Lounge is the main dining area & the service is incredible! Their Lobster roll, Crab Chowder, Steak, desserts, are all amazing & so tasty!!! The fitness center has a lovely set-up with chilled mint-scented towels, fruit flavored water, fresh fruit.....nice touch!! This is the only hotel I will stay at when visiting Boston & I truly look forward to my stays here! they are always very memorable, flawless & relaxing:) looking forward to returning in November for a long weekend! Thanks for everything FS Boston! Best, Patrick Winkler NYC --

“Not a 4-Star Hotel” We stayed at the Magnolia (Dallas) for one night while in town for The Cotton Bowl. The building is historic and the location is good (downtown), however, the room lacked. We were in a standard room (#2313) and paid $179 (before tax). Unfortunately, our free-wireless internet did not work in our room, likely because our room is in the corner. We called and the front desk promised to switch our room, but it never happened. I guess they were busy with all the Cotton Bowl attendees. I read that the rooms were renovated but they didn't look and feel that way. The bathroom was average and the pillows horrible. Also, the bed is a queen, not king. The staff is nice and we really wanted to like this hotel. They offer free breakfast, cocktail hour before dinner, and milk and cookies at night. Nice touches, but if you are looking for a 4 or 5 star property, this is not it.

“'I left my heart ...' - thanks in part to Hyatt Regency” This hotel is a gem! Stayed here for a Fri, Sat & Sun night in Aug 2006. Got it from Priceline at an extraordinarily good price (90). My room was on the 3rd floor and I had a partial view of the bay, which was great. Especially when there were fireworks on Friday night! The room itself was very large with a king bed, dresser with TV on a swivel (so you could watch it from anywhere in the room) a desk w/chair, an upholstered chair by the window and another nice comfy upholstered chair with ottoman and convenient reading light/table right next to it. There was a coffee maker and coffee/supplies in the room. Bathroom products were fab with a nice fresh scent - and replenished daily. King size bed was a dream - pillowtop mattress, loads of pillows and a feather comforter. Felt like I was falling into marshamallow fluff each night! You absolutely could not ask for a better located hotel. Right across from the newly renovated ferry building, with all the convenient public transportation right outside the door, including subway to airport and trolley car to Chinatown. Quite a few coffee shops and some fast food type places within steps of the hotel. Embarcadero center shopping (with all the standard chains) right up the street. Definitely go over to the farmers market at the Ferry building on Saturday if you are there. They also have Arts & Crafts booths each weekend right outside the hotel. It is such a breeze to have the ferry right across the street from the Hyatt, too. Just walk over and hop on to spend a day in Sausalito. There are a few nice restaurants within walking distance (reccomend Schroders on Front Street - for great beer and German food.) My stay at the fabulously located, highly appointed Hyatt was a good contributor to "leaving my heart in San Francisco..."

“Nice Hotel in a Good location” This hotel is highly recommended as a great place to stay. My only caveat is that I would have liked to have been able to make my own morning tea, rather than spent $13 on a thermos of hot water, 2 teacups, 2 teabags and some milk; but I guess that's the deal in up-market hotels these days.

“Disappointing” Pro: Location Parking LG Plasma TV (45" or 46") and cable Starbucks coffee Con: Small rooms Room had a very distinct chemical odor. Toilet paper was incredibly cheap single ply - worse than the cheapest airport I have ever traveled though. Complimentary breakfast is well below average.

“Ridiculously large and opulent” Simply huge is the only way to describe the corner room (suite? flat?). If i had 20 friends over at the same time, we wouldn't have even bumped into one another. The Bose sound system in the living room was a nice touch, but i only used it for about 15 minutes. Con - i couldn't get the water to heat up in the shower and didn't have the time to call anyone about it. After the fact, the management sent me a letter offering a discount on my next stay. Hard to say on the relative "value" when $750/night isn't too far off from many other hotels in the area...

“Perfect in Almost all Ways” I am actually checked into this hotel now and have been here for three days while attending a function at the Convention Center. The location is great in that respect. They are building the new City Center across the street in which used to be a huge parking lot. I asked for a room on the quiet side and am not bothered by any outside noise (9th floor). My room wasn't ready when I arrived, but my train was early. It's a short cab ride from Union Station. I was called by the front desk less than a hour later and was able to check in. The nightly Manager Reception and the included fully cooked breakfast are great! I went early in the morning and never encountered a line or wait. Very short wait for cocktails in the evening as well and I beleive the hotel is full due to the convention. I don't like paying for internet though, and since I booked through the convention, thought my rate of $250/night (w/o tax) was a bit steep especially since I booked backed in November. Most staff is helpful, but some are a bit reserved. I just returned from a business trip to NOLA where staff at the hotel I was staying in were full of southern hospitality - Windsor Court, so a bad comparison. Many resturants are within easy walking distance. Great take out sushi at Sushi AOI. The only real negative for some people may be the very thin walls and lack of sound proofing. Certaininly, the staff can't do anything about that, but I wanted to list it here. The toilets have a super-sonic flush - and you can hear the ones flush from the rooms next door and even when walking in the halls. The doors close very loudly and some folks just don't think about their neigbors when closing them. The good thing is you can close the door to the bedroom and if offers some sound protection until your neighbors start having a conversation in their bedroom. It didn't bother me, but it was noticable. To get optium cooling in the bedroom at night (record highs here now) you need to leave the bedroom door open and the A/C definately keeps the front room cooler. All and all a wonderful stay and I will return next year.

“Nice, comfortable room, but.....” First I will comment on the pros - The hotel is in a very convenient location to the airport. We stayed at a different hotel for the start of our mini vacation, but booked this hotel for the night before our flight out of Denver International, as the traffic in Denver can be a nightmare. The room was very nice and met all of our needs. The bed was very comfortable and that is a big plus to us! Our teenage daughter used the sofabed and as sofabeds go, it was okay. We used the fitness center and the hot tub and both were very nice. The check-in process was fast and easy as well as check-out. The front desk staff were pleasant and helpful. The look of the interior of the hotel is what you would expect from an Embassy Suites. Now, for the cons. The evening reception was not up to what I am used to at Embassy Suites. Yes, I did have a nice glass of wine and my husband had a beer, but the finger food consisted of celery, carrots and some stale chips and a few dips. Most of the tables had not been cleaned from previous guests and the floor was a mess with chips and popcorn. It was very unattractive. I guess it just gets cleaned up during the night. We heard that breakfast was until 9 a.m. so we slept in and went downstairs at 8:30. There were employees already removing the breakfast condiments from the tables and I was afraid we had missed breakfast! I ordered my cooked to order egg dish, which was very nice and grabbed some bacon. My husband looked for coffee and there was none---except decaf so he poured us some. It was stone cold. We asked an employee if more would be available and she said she would bring more....it never materialized. As I was eating my eggs, I noticed that the other items were being cleaned up and it was only 8:45. I rushed over to get my fruit just in time. A family arrived about 8:55 and managed to get some cereal and left over bacon. So, as you can tell, my complaint is that if you offer a breakfast until 9:00, please do so. We felt rushed and didn't get to enjoy a good breakfast and a nice cup of coffee.

“Lovely!” The Omni Houston Westside is a lovely hotel. I stayed for three nights (in May, 2004 - over Memorial Day) while visting an old friend who lived near by in Katy, TX. The staff was very helpfull and gracious, the lobby was spacious and inviting, room service and wake up calls were always on time. The ONLY problem was mositure. My room, and the entire hotel for that matter, seemed damp. However, that could have been due to the weather outside(extremly humid). Overall, it is a lovely hotel and I plan to stay there again.

“Nice hotel” I came to San Diego for a conference and was pleased overall with this hotel. The rooms are very nice and beds are comfortable (big plus). The location is okay, there are definitely hotels closer to the gaslamp district. But that is not always a good thing as I stayed at another hotel in the gaslamp and it was very very noisy with drunken people coming in at all hours. This was quite and nice

“Courtyard was nice - skip the valet” My husband and I stayed at the Courtyard recently. Overall, it was pleasant. The front desk manager, Lisa, was very helpful and on-the-ball. She allowed us to check in earlier than the standard time, and this enabled us to drop off our luggage and go tour. The rooms were clean and the bed was soft. One aspect cast a negative light on the trip - the valet service. I took the warnings from previous postings and ensured we called ahead for the valet to get our car. We had to use our car twice during the one-night stay and on the first night, we called ahead to get the car and when we came downstairs 20 minutes later, the valets informed us that they forgot to put a ticket in our window and they couldn't find our car. We waited an additional 20 minutes for the crew to find and retrieve our vehicle - so that was 40 minutes total. The next day, there was a parade in town and the city shut down most of Market Street - no one informed us of this and no one warned us that it may take longer to get our car. We again called ahead and then proceeded to wait for an hour and fifteen minutes for our car. We can't fault the parade, the city warned the businesses - but had we known that we would have to wait that long to get out, we would have parked it ourselves at a commercial lot or ensured that we got our car very early in order to avoid a delay. Additionally, this cost us $40 - so it wasn't cheap. Lisa, the front desk manager, was helpful and there was no way she could control the valet. Once she became aware of how long we were waiting, she prioritized our vehicle. I've been to Philadelphia many times and I probably won't stay at this property again. The Downtown Marriott next door was preferable.

“Can't Beat The Location” The Westin Michigan Avenue sits near the northern end of the Magnificent Mile, steps away from all of the great Chicago attractions. You can walk to the shore of Lake Michigan in about 2 minutes. A multitude of shopping and restaurant options are all around you. And nearby subway stations can get you to museums, parks and stadiums very conveniently (Red line Chicago Ave station is about 4 blocks away). This hotel is classic Westin. Rooms have dark wood and earth tones. Mine had a comfortable chaise lounge chair that sat by the window. Beds are the ever-comfortable Heavenly Bed. The bathroom was standard - tub and shower, nice big marble countertop with a big mirror. There are two towers that make up this hotel. The taller one has lake view rooms on one side, which are pretty stunning. This isn't the newest or fanciest hotel in town. In fact, while this property is nice, it's showing a few tatters here and there. But the location is so good and the service tends to be better than average. So I keep coming back.

“A Priceline Win That Can't Be Beat.” I won this hotel on Priceline for $130/night x 3 nights for two rooms. With Priceline I always expect to get the absolute worst room in the building but I was pleasantly surprised here. We ended up with 2 double beds in each room with a pretty decent view from the 17th floor. I was also a bit concerned about staying downtown as I usually stay in Midtown. I needn't have worried. This was a fantastic location for taking the subway. There were at least 4 lines to choose from within 3 blocks of the hotel. The WTC memorial was steps from the front door. I loved the fact that the fridge they supplied was empty, rather than filled with items that are too expensive to purchase. The beds were comfy, the room was clean and quiet and the front desk, bellman and maid service were fast and efficient. I loved the Marriott and would definitely stay there again.

“Great hotel” Have enjoyed many stays at this good hotel. The location is great, the rooms are spacious, up to date and very clean. The bathrooms are well equipped. The views are lovely and the beds very comfortable. Reception staff efficient and friendly. My only negative comments would be that there is not a mini bar in the room and the wifi is expensive at £14.95 + tax for 24 hours.

“Strictly business” I stayed here for a few nights in mid-August on a business trip. This hotel basically gears itself for the business crowd and does a perfectly adequate job at meeting their needs. The rooms are your standard Sheraton rooms with somewhat dated and worn furniture, but still perfectly serviceable (though the air conditioning doesn't get very cold, which some people may dislike). They have free parking in an underground garage, so that was a nice touch. Though I am a Starwood Platinum member, they did not upgrade me to a suite even though the hotel did not seem particularly booked to me, so that's a minus in my book. They did give me access to the club, however. The club is a little small, but they have a decent continental breakfast spread every morning and the light appetizers they put out during dinner time were quite tasty and filling. All in all, I wouldn't mind staying here again but I might be inclined to try a different hotel in the area to see what they have to offer.

“Perfect! Great views, rooms and service.” Stayed here for three nights to visit NYC in a King corner suite. The hotel is located just in front of Ground Zero and construction site of the Freedom Tower, in Lower Manhattan. The king corner suite is not very spacious, but generous enough to give a sense of luxury in NYC. Very comfortable king bed facing plasma tv, nice bathroom, small lounge with sofa-bed, workdesk, coffee table and second TV. My favorite feature is the large floor to ceiling windows. Our suite had breathtaking views of midtown and the ESB, the Woolworth building, the Hudson River and New Jersey, and Ground Zero. Service was professional and pleasant, and we felt welcome in this property. The buffet breakfast was a little limited but reasonably priced for NYC. Second and third day ordered the midwesterner (steak) breakfast instead. Room service is average, but prices reasonable. The location of the hotel didn't prove to be much of an inconvenience to us. We could walk to pay respects at Ground Zero, tour Lower Manhattan and get to the Statue of Liberty ferry. Access via subway to the attractions in Midtown is very fast (take the express trains) and easy (there are at least four different subway lines that stop within walking distance of the hotel). Taxis aren't expensive either. The construction of the Freedom tower was just starting during our stay, and there is also a condo building under construction on the north side of the hotel so there is some construction noise during the day which may bother some. This hotel played a key role in our having a great stay in NYC. This is my second stay here. I can't recommend this hotel enough.

“Just okay” We stay at this hotel for work, which is the only reason I have to return there. It is way overpriced for what you get, and the rooms rae becoming more worn and outdated all the time. The lobby is non-existent, and the restaurant is overpriced and average. The staff are typically not helpful. There can also be very long check-in lines, as the check-in desk only has one or two people working at a time. If you arrive late, they try to stick you in a room with two single beds - very lame. The only redeeming thing is it is centrally located. But there are lots of other hotels in the area that are both less expensive, more modern, and much nicer. Go somewhere else.

“Disappointed” Having not been to the USA for 30 years it was a bit of a shock to find US Airways to be worse than the Budget Airlines in Asia. The Hotel room did not have a refrigerator, plastic cups instead of glasses. The buffet breakfast was OK , but paper plates,plastic knives and forks, plastic cup spoilt it. The price we paid was US$ 370 for two nights, I would of expected to be able to get a beer in the Hotel or at least have a glass for one at that price. The only good thing was the internet in the reception area.

“Okay Westin, but would probably chose a different place next time” Very small room, needed some patch work done in the construction. The internet was very slow. Room was clean, and bed was okay. But the room was just too small.

“Clean and comfortable” A pleasant surprise! The room was modern and clean. The location is great as it's near many restaurants (walking or driving distance) and shopping. The roolm view was peaceful (my room overlooked a man-made pond in a business park district). The bed was average in comfort. Unique large shower stall and laminate floors added a nice "urban studio" feel.

“ideal location” Stayed at this hotel for one night before early morning flight.. Perfectly comfortable and clean...excellent location just a few minutes walk from airport main terminal. Most of the other guests were also staying for just the one night too. Hotel has a restaurant , but there are a few alternatives within easy reach . No noise heard from aircraft landing or taking off. General decor a bit bland but for one night ,who's complaining.
“Good value” I stayed here after attending a concert at the Schottenstein Arena. It was the perfect location! It's not fancy, but it has everything you need.

“Good Hotel, Clean and Quiet” This is a good hotel in a good location. Plenty of eating options nearby. Hotel check in was smooth. Parking was $14 per day. Rooms are a little larger than normal, and decor was above average. Nothing really great or terrible.

“Older Boutique Hotel: Small, dated rooms” The room was very, very small and dreary. Very little lighting, and very depressing. After a couple of hours in this room, I couldn't take it anymore and request a different room for an additional $20 charge. This was well worth it. The room I was moved to was still old, dated and smelled musty but was at least something that I could tolerate for 1 night. I was booked for 2, but when I advised the front desk that I simply could not stay there the 2nd night, they were accomodating and did not charge me the additional night's penalty. They were also very polite about it. Also note: this hotel is not for the claustrophobic! There's 1 EXTREMELY tiny elevator that has no air circulation. You can really tell that this is an older hotel. If you must stay here, without a doubt pay the extra $20 for a room upgrade.

“We had a blast” On a very hot July 3rd we decided on a staycation to a hotel with air conditioning and a pool. Right choice! We were a bit surprised to find great rates available for same night the day before the 4 th so we grabbed it! We upgraded to a bay villa non tower. Again - right choice. We had ground floor patio and watched the fireworks from Seaworld. Very fun. The pool was great and we enjoyed the water. Not enough lounge chairs whe it was busy so second day pool was harder. We went sailing instead. Very reasonable and very fun. Yes - we will be back. The whole staff turned out for the 4 th of July pool party. Everyone from a management to accounting to catering! All hands on deck with huge smiles. Thank you!

“great hotel choice for NYC” So I have stayed at lots of hotels in NYC - and I love this hotel. I booked the day before I needed to check in, and got a great rate. Some hotels will screw you when you book cheaper rates - but I got a great corner room with a view. They even let me check in early, which a lot of hotels in NYC don't let you do... Some pros of this hotel - Location is excellent for times square, and very walkable to central park, empire state building, etc. - Beds are outrageously comfortable. Outrageous. You will want to buy one when you leave. I did! - Great shower - Very good toiletries - Twice the size of many similar-priced NYC hotel rooms. Sitting area near the window, large desk, etc. - Great view from the upper floors - Staff is polite and super helpful - rare for NYC as well - Bathroom is clean and spacious - Nice flat panel TVs in the rooms - Near tons of restaurants and bars, as well as small grocery stores to get water, etc - ipod docking station I have to come up with a couple cons - Not a ton of counter space in the bathroom - makes it hard to maneuver - This is a giant hotel that seems to get lots of groups - so the lobby can be sort of a zoo sometimes Love this hotel! I find myself trying to find ways to come back!

“Great experience and value...friendly staff...nice room” Have stayed in a couple of other places near Times Square and they have tended to be a little worn-down. Not so at the Muse. NYC chic entryway leading you to polite, helpful receptionists. Was impressed with the clean and well-appointed the room. Great value for the money as well as I've stayed at Club Quarters before and paid as much or more.

“Terrific Customer Service” My husband and I stayed at the Alexander Inn for three days in June during the second leg of our vacation which began in the Poconos and attending a NASCAR race. We hadn’t been to Philadelphia before and wanted to be near all the typical tourist sites we planned to visit and the location was perfect walking distance. Upon arrival the streets are a bit confusing and parking is off-site however the hotel offers a discounted parking rate and provides you a map to the garage at check-in. The gentleman at the front desk was most pleasant and helpful. The neighboring area was clean and has a variety of restaurants. We never felt concern when walking around, however we were never out that late in the evening. The room was lovely, yet small. I was able to unpack the luggage and used the minimal counter space in the bathroom along with the window sill and made it work. My husband is a bigger guy and his only negative comment was the size of the bathroom/shower and overall room but it was extremely clean and very well maintained even compared to four star hotels we have stayed previously. Bonus was the exceptional complimentary continental breakfast they provide with fresh bagels, fruit, eggs, juice and coffee. Lovely sitting area downstairs was a nice way to start each morning and plan our day in the city. The hotel staff and one gentleman in particular, wish I could recall his name, was extremely helpful. He took it upon himself to map out our desired destinations for the day and even provided us with an umbrella to use one day as rain was in the forecast. Being from Arizona we forget about those things occasionally when packing! His recommendations were terrific and added to our overall experience. I would not hesitate to recommend The Alexander for the location, service and pricing they offer their guests.

“Impressive Treatment Despite Size” I was very impressed with this hotel. The tremendous size of the facility didn't stop the staff members from giving me special treatment. I was there for a conference and was impressed at how well the hotel managed to take care of the 700 people in my group. It's a beautiful hotel, situated right near Millennium Park and downtown. If you run, it's a block from the shore.

“Nice airport stay” Only stayed here on a quick overnight stay arriving late one night at the airport. The lobby is quite nice and modern but the rooms are quite a bit outdated. Again...was fine for a one night stay but not sure I would like 'hanging out' in this room for long if I was here on business, etc.

“Great location, overall good stay” Stayed for several nights recently and enjoyed this hotel overall. Our room was very small, but clean and functional - comfortable bed, big closet, nice big windows, modern TV. The unique artwork in the rooms and elsewhere in the hotel is interesting and enjoyable. We liked looking at the walls of our room and discovering new details in the artwork over the course of our stay. Our room faced toward the centre of the building, which meant there was almost no noise from the surrounding neighbourhood. However, the building is old and creaky, and with windows open in the summertime, noise from other floors can be an issue (even when fellow guests are being quite quiet). Our bathroom was small, but had a lovely clawfoot tub. The shower, however, was underwhelming - very little water pressure and no fan to help with humidity. The hotel is well situated - right near the entrance to Chinatown, and within easy walking distance of transit, restaurants, laundry, decent little grocery stores, etc. Overall, a solid choice.

“Very safe, friendly, large hotel” We just left the Embassy Suites Washington DC after a 3 night stay. It was a great hotel. It was myself and my teenage son. We had a nice, large room. The hotel is in a very good location. It is pretty, has lots of amenities & is in a safe area. Our room was on the 8th floor. We had a nice view of the city west of the hotel. The room itself was large. There is a living room area with a couch, chair, armoir with LCD HD tv, and a table with chairs. It is a large table, like a kitchen table. There is also a wetbar sink, and across from that a frig & microwave, coffee maker in a closet. The bathroom is large and very pretty. There is a separate bedroom area. We had two queen size beds, a dresser with tv on top, and another sink (came in very handy). The beds were very comfortable, they give you lots of pillows. The towels are also plentiful & fluffy. We had no problems with our room at all. Housekeeping did a great job of emptying our trash, making the beds and supplying new towels. There are some fun elevators, they are glass and you can see the entire atrium area as you go up and down. They sometimes take a long time to come, because of the crowds. During peak breakfast time, you may have to wait a lot longer. The atrium area is really pretty. There is a koi pond and other water features. They have lots of tables and chairs to relax and meet people. There are computer stations spread around for everyone to use. The kids pretty much monopolize them, but there is also a business center for adults to use. I had a laptop so I didnt use the business center. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Every single one we encountered had a great attitude and really wanted to help. The concierge desk lady was so nice, she gave us advice and ideas on a few ocassions. The bellman gave us some ideas of where to eat, they also gave us some directions we asked for. They told us what areas to avoid after dark, and which areas are safer. They have a full hot breakfast every day that is included. Its not a typical hotel breakfast, they have a LOT of choices. It is crowded, though, so its not a 'quick' meal. You may not find a table, but you can take your food up to your room. The food is fresh and there is quite a bit to choose from: eggs, omelets, bacon, sausage, french toast, pancakes, bagels, pastries, toast, fruits (cut up and whole), yogurt, potatoes, grits, oatmeal, cold cereal, many different juices, coffee, milk, oh and make your own waffles! We never left hungry. Afternoon snacks are a hit, too. They have cocktails for adults, sodas and juice for others. They offer popcorn, pretzels, chips, and chex mix type stuff. It is really nice! Like someone else said, its a family-friendly hotel, so be prepapred for TONS of kids everywhere you go. Many, unfortunately, are unsupervised and run wild throughout the hotel. The pool is wild during the day and early eve - we just avoided it. It wasnt the hotel's fault, there were just too many kids. There is a gift shop with shirts, hats, small gifts, medicines, drinks, snacks, etc. Prices are elevated, but what you'd expect in a hotel gift shop. The people working in there are very nice. The only negative thing I can think of is that they charge you $9.95 per night for internet and it is very slow internet. Everyone else includes it now, but not them. I had to upload things for work, and it was painfully slow. In fact, many times it errored out before completing my upload. They also charge for parking, but everyone in the area does, too. It was $23.95 per night plus tax. We just left our car in the lot and never used it, but you can have in and out privileges (many dont offer that). The metrorail is about a 5-10min walk, depending on how fast you walk. Its the Foggy Bottom station, which will give you easy access to just about everything. Keep in mind, if you take a taxi, this hotel is on the border of two zones & since they charge by zone (I think it was $6.60 for one zone, then $8.80 if you went the second zone, then $10.oo for the third, or something like that). So if you stay within a certain zone you only pay the $6.60, but if you go even one block into the next zone, you pay the two zone price. It is confusing at first. We took the taxi from Union Station to the hotel and it cost us $11.00 (2 people). It was worth every penny to us because we were exhausted & it was super hot out. The taxi driver told us to go to 21st street next time and we would have saved a zone 'change'. Safety: I never felt in any danger anywhere near the hotel. We walked all over the place (during the daylight hours). At night we were told not to venture more than a couple blocks, but we ended up not even going out at night. I would definitely stay here again!

“Still needs a lot of work” My husband and I were looking for a hotel close to the El Paso Airport. After reading the reviews of recent renovations, we booked a "Concierage Suite" for one night. We will not be staying there again. We nearly left after checking in when we saw the carpet on the stairs and hallway to our room; it was filthy with debris, the kind of debris that vacuuming would take care of and obviously had not been done in some time. No elevator to our second floor room, so we towed our rollaboards up 1 flight of stairs, then a half flight. The "concierage suite" was not a suite by our definition. It was one big room with a reasonably comfortable chair and ottoman, not a separate seating area. The "refrigerator" was a very small dorm-style unit, sitting on the floor. There was no microwave as promised in the booking information. This hotel is obviously an older one, but the touted recent renovations don't make up for dirt and rooms not as advertised.

“Adequate Hotel for Business Travelers but not for Vacationers” I’m a Starwood card member and anytime I travel for business I prefer to stay at one of the properties. The W Hotel is my favorite Starwood brand, so when I traveled to Chicago for Lollapalooza, I booked five nights at the W Hotel City Center ( got a decent rate using my AAA card). The hotel lobby is beautiful on the inside. It reminded me of being in an exclusive hotel in NYC. The aesthetic of the outside of the building blends in perfectly with downtown. I booked this hotel because it’s walking distance to Grant Park where Lollapalooza was being held. Very convenient location but the area is dead on the weekends. I ordered room service alot due to the lack of restaurants being open. The gym (SWEAT) was okay but not fancy. Unfortunately the property has no pool so if you want to beat the Chicago heat during the summer and you are brand loyal, book the W Hotel Lakeshore. Room service was quick and the staff was helpful. I asked an attendant at the front door where I could find the nearest Harold’s restaurant and he directed me to nearest location promptly. My room was on the 11th floor. Make sure to request a room that faces the front of the building or you’ll be facing the back, which faces another building (no sunlight). I had a wonderful room, which was nice. There are a lot of light switches for the minimal amount of light they produce – the light under the bed was kinda cool! My only major complaint was the noise from the room next to mine ( thin walls) and the activities in the hallway (cleaning staff seemed to slam doors non-stop).

“A lot to like, a little to put up with” Here's what I like about the Holiday Inn Express Times Square. It's clean and modern. Plenty of heavy-duty towels. A huge flat screen TV and real HD channels. Big, comfortable beds. A generous supply of electric outlets. Quiet rooms, only 6 to a floor. Best of all, my two favorite amenities: a free, well stocked breakfast, and free high speed wifi. Here's what is less than perfect: small rooms, hardly any shelf space in the bathroom, and it's not really at Times Square but a half mile walk past the bus terminal and down a rather grungy street. But I'd walk that walk any day for the user-friendly amenities at this hotel. I notice comments about the elevators. I stayed on the 34th floor and never had to wait more than 30 seconds for an elevator. The building is interesting - apparently it contains 3 tall and thin hotels side by side, which is why there are only 6 rooms to a floor, and why - at least for my stay - 2 elevators can do the job in a 36 floor hotel. As for value, I had a great rate from a discount website, and if the Holiday Inn's rack rates were twice that price, it would get 5 stars for value. Unfortunately, they are considerably more. At $300+ per night, the small rooms and somewhat gritty neighborhood would be harder to overlook, but for a reasonable discount the HI-Express is a hidden gem.

“Great room and location” Just got back from a 3 night stay at the Beacon. We wanted to stay in an area that had a more local neighbourhood feeling so we thought the Upper West Side would do the trick. I was really impressed by the value of this hotel. With the tax we paid $344 a night for a King room. Other hotels I researched were even more then that and the pictures didn’t seem as nice. We got there late at night and there was a big crowd in the lobby and low and behold Robin Williams was there visiting with fans. I assumed he was performing at the theatre next door but not sure. Seemed like a sign of a good visit. The room was very large. Much bigger then other New York hotels I’ve stayed in. As well the décor was really nice and bed very comfortable. It definitely seemed like they had renovated recently. Before our arrival I emailed to request a quiet room on a higher floor. They gave us a room on the top floor which is 25th. Our room was across from the elevators which I thought might be a problem for noise but we barely heard anything from the hallway. As well I had read reviews about the elevators being slow but we never had an issues with them. We had chatted with some local residences of the hotel that had been living there for 25 years. It was interesting to stay in a place with such history. When we woke up our first morning we were stunned at the view. A great way to start everyday. The subway is right around the corner which is really convenient. At the last minute I considered switching hotels to somewhere around Greenwich Village because I thought that we might be spending hours on the subway but the express train to Time Square is super fast. We would be downtown in around 15 minutes so getting around wasn’t a problem at all. Having the Viand Café downstairs is really convenient as well. We arrived late at night and it was so nice to pop down for a snack and drink. On our last day we had to leave for our flight early so again it was nice to have a reasonably priced meal downstairs. We also had breakfast at Le Pain Quotiden on 72nd which we really enjoyed as well we went to Sarabeth’s West which was good but nothing really special and pricey. We also partook in the famous Gray’s Papaya for a snack too. A really nice wine store is just downstairs too and a Duane Reade closeby if you forgot any toiletries. There’s lots of shopping around the area too which we didn’t expect which was great. A big DSW was just down the street. We rented bikes at Master Bike Shop on 72nd and did a nice ride around Central Park. For the beautiful room, view, location, and value I’d definitely recommend the Beacon.

“Sehr empfehlenswert” Super Tipp für Städtereisende, kann ich ruhigen Gewissens weiterempfehlen! Modernes 4-Sterne Hotel in Top-Lage mitten in Manhattan. Zwar nicht das Günstigste - aber das Geld war es wert. Wir hatten ein schönes, sauberes und für amerikanische Verhältnisse grosses Zimmer im 34. Stock mit Blick zur Strassenseite. Nach links gedreht konnten wir das Chrysler Building in unmittelbarer Nähe sehen, geradeaus über die Dächer der Nachbarhäuser. Das Zimmer war modern in dunklem Holz eingerichtet, ein grosses Doppelbett mit weicher Matratze und vielen Kissen, Schreibtisch mit Stuhl, Wandschrank mit Kleiderbügeln und Bügeleisen, eine leere TV-Kommode mit Schubfächern sowie ein kleiner Beistelltisch und ein Sessel, neuer Flat-Screen-Ferneher an der Wand (deshalb leerer TV-Schrank).

“Small, but lovely and in a great location” We have stayed at this property before and liked it. The rooms are very compact, but well appointed and extremely clean. You check yourself in and out which is a huge time saver. The amenities are nice - bottled water and all! They have a deal with a near by garage that offers $28 parking - can't beat it! Quiet location on the weekends. Very near to subways and a short walk to Century 21 - the best store in NYC!

“A great place to stay if you want to be near Fishermans Wharf” This was my first time in San Francisco. As a lot of first time tourists do, I stayed very near to Fishermans Wharf. As hotels in the Fishermans Wharf area go, this one is a beaut. It's less than five minutes walk to the famous sign. You can be at Pier 39 in under 10 minutes walk and take in all the shops or the famous sea lions. There are two lines of the cable car within 10 minutes walk as well. The bed was quite comfortable. The rooms are clean and very acceptable, though I really do HATE low flow showerheads, and the bathroom here was guilty of having one installed. I would have appreciated some curtains on the windows (not just shutters) because too much light got through when I was trying to recover from some jet lag. Do be aware that there are charges for using the in-room safe. There are complimentary wine tastings in the lobby early the evening, which are a great way to sample some local products and say hello to a few other guests. Staff are courteous and very friendly. The concierge service was especially helpful. The restaurant in the building serves a very nice breakfast and has a simple bar if you're after a late night drink, although prices are a tad on the expensive side. There is a supermarket and drug store over the road and can be reached in three or four minutes from the hotel's front door. McDonalds, Subway and Burger King are all nearby. During my stay, there was only one elevator operating. It was very frustrating! I would imagine when they have them both working again it wouldn't be so bad. My experience was that it was quite an ordeal just to get upstairs! By biggest tip for anyone staying in Fishermans Wharf is to get away and see more of the city beyond Fishermans Wharf! Take a cable car and see the city on the move. Go and explore Union Square or Haight-Ashbury. It's a great city and it would be shame to spend too much of it in (what I found out to be) the kitsch, overly touristy part of town!

“Average Historical Hotel in a nice location in” Crockett Hotel has got some historical cache to it being right next to The Alamo. However, it's not a "grand" historical hotel but rather a "ordinary" historical hotel experience. The rooms are kinda dated from the 1980s - quite small and the walls are painted in an unappealing green tone. We also got a room facing the street and the outside noise was loud, had a hard time sleeping. I guess for less than $100 dollars this hotel would be an okay choice. However, I think next time I would just stay at the nicer Menger Hotel next door which is a grand historical hotel experience.

“Second rate Sheraton- avoid!” Pros: - Close to airport Cons: - Terrible staff - Understaffed - Over-crowded shuttle - Lousy food - Old gym equipment In my opinion, this is absolutely a second-rate Sheraton property. It was a mistake on my part booking this hotel when there is a real Sheraton about 2 blocks away, but I've stayed at other Four Points and they have been fine. The afternoon front desk clerk was pleasant when checking in, but a heavy-set female clerk checking guests out in the morning had an attitude like guests are an inconvenience. There was one bartender and one waiter working their butts off in the bar/restaurant, trying to take care of about 10 tables plus the bar. After about 10-15 minutes without being able to order, I got up and left. It was not the fault of the employees, they were just overwhelmed. I ended up getting room service, which was only luke warm and over-salted. The gym has a decent amount of equipment, but most of it is dated and in need of repair (rust, missing parts, noise, broken tv monitors). The morning airport shuttle looks like a clown car. I had to stand on the bus and was lucky to have that. I saw at least a half dozen guests who were unable to get on and had to wait or take a cab. I contacted a manager when I got home (which may have been a desk clerk who was pretending to be one) who just gave a bunch of "uh huh, sorry for the inconvenience" ramble and seemed like he couldn't care less. The regular Sheraton down the street is light years better, so don't make the same mistake I did. The price difference is small, but the quality is night and day better. I will stay at Four Points again, but never at this one!

“I would never spend my own money to stay here...” I would never spend my own money to stay at the Hudson Hotel, and was pleased that on this trip I did not find out the hard way like so many of the people I heard complaining about the rooms at the reception desk. The hotel has a great location on 58th Street and was designed by the famous designer Philippe Stark. From the moment that you arrive you know that you are going to a hotel like no other, as there is no name to identify the place. You then travel up some very long and striking yellow light escalators and emerge into a gloomy lobby. Music is pumping away and you really cannot see very much as it is very dark. You can make out a huge long check-in desk with a massive trendy chandelier hanging above it. As you check in you will usually hear people complaining about the size of their rooms and the staff explaining that the rooms are that size and it is not just that they have been allocated a tiny room. I did think that people were probably being a bit fussy and over dramatic, until I went to my own room. Getting to the room was another surprise as the hallways are incredibly dark as well. The rooms are very small, around 125 square feet. If they were very cheap then this would be less of an issue. But they are not. On the positive side they are a masterpiece of clever design by squeezing so much in to such a small space. But no matter what your view on design is, the fact is the rooms feel cramped and unpleasant to stay in. The dark wood panels making it feel oppressive. There is around 1.5 feet on either side of the low bed. The bathroom is hard to move around in as you squeeze past the toilet to get into the shower that has a glass panel into the bedroom. There is a small TV and a CD player in the room – but no real space to put luggage and much clothes. If there were 2 of you in the rooms it would be really cramped. The restaurant in the hotel is also dark, but here the design is very stunning with the kitchen in the centre and long tables. The food is excellent. The buffet breakfast ($27) was excellent as well. The main bar on the lobby level has glass floors with light underneath. They are very fussy about keeping the look and would not let us put our coats over the back of the chairs. There is also a “library” that is also great design and more comfortable. The fitness room is pretty good with a fair selection of cardio machines and weight machines. The meeting rooms are very ordinary considering the rest of the hotel. As you can imagine, I will avoid staying here. I had to stay in the hotel for 4 nights and that was too long! You cab see from the pictures I posted on here just how small the rooma are. You could also look at a video I took of the room by copying and pasting this link to a new browser: [--]

“rien d'extraordinaire” San francisco était la 2ème étape de notre séjour aux usa, nous avions choisi cette hôtel car il est situé dans le centre donc proche des commerces; Cette hôtel a une clientèle de prestige, très sophistiqué, la décoration du hall était magnifiques. La chambre avait une vue exceptionnelle, par contre ne pas s'appuyer sur la vitre simple vitrage, pas très costaud. Ne pas enlever les choses du mini bar car la facturation se fait automatiquement. Nous avons eu une chambre avec lit queen size, et donc pas beaucoup de place pour dormir. Il propose le lit heavenly et le heavenly bath, mais pas de quoi foueter un chat. Pas de piscine, belle salle de sports.

“Great Stay for this Airport Hotel” We stayed at this hotel for one night. We were upgraded to a room with a pool view on the 3rd floor since i'm a Honors Member. The room was nice in the corner and had a nice balcony on which to sit out there and enjoy the evening and so forth. The concierge lounge located on the 4th floor was nice, and had great staff in there to help you with any questions or concerns that you had. The hotel has a restaurant/bar connected to it and the airport shuttle works great on the hour and half hour. Very efficient staff and the shuttle drivers were very courteous and helpful as well. Definitely would stay here again.

“Great All-Purpose Hotel” This Omni is right across the street from the Convention Center, so it is great for meetings. It is also just a few block from great restaurants and activities in downtown Ft. Worth which has a very charming city center. Right across the street is the Water Garden, which allows you to feel like you have totally escaped the city. Staff are very helpful even when stressed out with what seemed like 1000 older, confused convention attendees. Valet parking is $25 but you can choose the city garage a few blocks away for $15 instead. The AC/Heating system at this hotel was the best I've encountered in a long time. The fan was almost inaudible so it didn't disturb your sleep.

“Upscale business hotel; great location” The Grand Hyatt San Antonio is very nice - it really has the feeling of an upscale urban business hotel. Check-in is made easier by express check-in kiosks similar to what you'd see at an airport. The lobby is modern and inviting. The restaurant and bar looked very pleasant, though we didn't visit. Taxis are available out front around the clock. Rooms very clean and comfortable - our king bed room had a day-bed type lounge to the side of the bed, a nice alternative to the standard chair. The location is really perfect though, especially if you are in tour for a quick tourist trip as we were. The hotel itself is on the Riverwalk, and a quick walk takes you right to the heart of things (the main Riverwalk area and of course, the Alamo). There are other hotels that share this location (Marriott across the street, somewhat dated looking Hilton a few blocks away), but the Hyatt definitely looked to be the newest and best in the area. If my travels take me to San Antonio again, I'll choose to stay here.

“Wonderful surprise” We have stayed all over New York and must have walked past this hotel a million times. Because we were coming on a busy weekend, most of our regular hotels weren't available, so we came here based on trip advisor reviews and one friend's recommendation. We were pleasantly surprised by the well-appointed room. The Michelangelo was hospitable and our room was beautiful. We were upgraded to a mini-suite -- don't know why -- but, thank you very much! While the view was nothing to write home about, the room was quiet, comfortable and large! I could do without sliding doors in a bathroom, but, that might be my only complaint. While it is a long walk from Penn Station -- it is doable and we did it -- stay on Seventh Avenue though -- less crowded and bigger sidewalks. We wish it was part of one of the "points programs", but, we'll probably be back. This was a great choice for a reasonable rate.
“Loved Hotel Monaco” I purchased rooms for $80 per night on Priceline.com. What a wonderful surprise. Hoel Monaco was absolutely beautiful.

“More of a business type hotel” My husband and I recently stayed overnight as we were visiting the medical center. I chose this hotel because of its proximity to the medical center and the fact that they have a shuttle service. We did have trouble with the shuttle when we called for pick up and they failed to tell us the van was not going to be marked with the hotel's name. We stood for 45 minutes and after our third call to the hotel were given the correct information, the shuttle unfortunately is not solely for the Courtyard and we drove around several other hotels before getting to our own. We decided to take a taxi the next day back as the shuttle was inconvenient. The check in process was easy, we had a king room on the second floor. The decor was nice, the bathroom was clean and up to date but the only mirror is located in the bathroom and getting ready in the morning was cramped. The bed was comfortable, free wifi in the room is great. They do offer breakfast/lunch and dinner with several options, we did stay for breakfast and it was well done. There were mainly business travelers in the lobby area and having meetings in the breakfast area as well. If you are staying for a length of time you might prefer a different type of hotel but for one night this was fine. Of note, the Residence Inn is directly across the parking lot and shares the same shuttle.

“Needs updating” We stayed here years ago and nothing has changed. It needs a serious update and repaint. The whole place looks faded and rather shabby. The staff are great, helpful and cheerful, but this hotel is stuck in 1975.

“Excellent Historic Property” During my four and a half week North American motorcycle tour (July 31 to September 1, 2012), I stayed at a number of hotels, motels and inns across the USA and Canada. My wife had made arrangements to fly and meet me in Austin for three nights, so I wanted a positive, upscale experience for us, as this was our first trip to Austin. Upon reaching Austin, Texas I checked into the Driskill Hotel, room 544, in the 1886 wing of the hotel for a three-night stay. I then went to the airport and picked up my wife. We then returned to the Driskill. What a hotel! Now managed by and part of the Destination Hotels and Resorts collection, and a registered "Historic Hotels of America", the Driskill Hotel is a wonderful example of late 1880s Texas, combined with 1930's flair. In excellent condition, this is the place to stay in Austin. Ideal downtown location on 6th Street, great ambience, and lots of history. And did I mention they make a killer grilled vegetable sandwich, on sour dough bread, in the 1886 Cafe & Bakery?! The Driskill. Pros: 1. Ideal location for exploring Austin. 2. Historic property that is well maintained, with friendly staff. Eleni, at the conceirge desk, was especially helpful. 3. Room amenities were excellent. Room 544 in the original 1886 part of the hotel was not large, but it was well furnished. Comfortable king size bed with luxurious linens and many pillows, historic desk, flat screen LED television, nicely tiled bathroom (with a classic look, including tub and tall showerhead), large fluffy bath towels, comfy bath robes, and an excellent selection of shampoo, hair conditioner, body lotion and soaps. 4. The hotel property itself, a combination of the original 1886 building and a newer 1930 addition, is well maintained and gives a real taste of the grandeur of old Texas. 5. Two good restaurants and a bar in the hotel (the upscale "Driskill Grill", the more laid back "1886 Cafe & Bakery" and the large "Driskill Bar" with its cool, historic tin ceiling), and you're within walking distance to literally hundreds of other restaurants, cafes, bars and grills in the downtown area of Austin. 6. Pet friendly hotel, including neat little specially designed pet beds, pet treats, chew toy and water bowl. 7. A good hotel for romance. Cons: 1. No on-site parking and no street parking. Valet is $28 per day (the park your vehicle off-site). 2. If you have allergies or don't want to see other people's pets, then the fact this is a pet friendly hotel will be a downer. 3. I had booked my stay at the Driskill Hotel using my American Express card and was suppose to receive 20% off their "Best Available Rate", a free upgrade (based upon availability at check-in), and early check-in or late check-out (based upon availability). I did receive the promised 20% off rate, but I was not given a room upgrade. At check-in, I was assisted by the wonderful concierge Eleni. She was uncertain as to how to process my room upgrade, so she went to ask a manager. As she approached the manager, she began to explain that I was to get a room upgrade as I was using my American Express card. However, the male manager summarily dismissed her with a "we don't have any" without so much as checking the hotel computer system. Several hours later, as I was standing by the hotel check-in counter waiting for an elevator, a saw and overhead another guest getting a complimentary room upgrade. Needless to say, I was not impressed. I had to wonder if I was discriminated against by the front desk manager because I was wearing my motorcycle gear during the check-in process... Overall, I was very pleased with the Driskill Hotel (but for the one negative at check-in) and I have no hesitation recommending the Driskill Hotel. On a scale of 1 to 10, where 1 is terrible and 10 is excellent, I rank the Driskill Hotel as an 8. High praise indeed!

“The best hotel lobby in Chicago” I have been to the Palmer House many times over the years, and I still love looking around the lobby with great art work on the ceiling. The renovations they made a couple of years ago have really updated the restaurants and bars in the lobby area, but it can get a bit crowded in the evening if a big convention is there. Although a lot of the hotels downtown are either by the river or just north of the river, the Palmer House still has a great location near the art institute and Grant Park. Plus, you can take a short trolley ride to the aquarium, planetarium, Field Museum, and Soldier Field. On the negative side, the Palmer House has expensive parking in a nearby building, and web access is very expensive. Also, the rooms vary a lot in size so some of the standard rooms are very small. The concierge level can be worth the extra cost as the rooms are much bigger, often with two bathrooms, and you get free snacks, free soft drinks, and breakfast on that level (so it can be worth it if you have more than one person in a room).

“Characterless!” This convention hotel is a big steel and concrete box with absolutely zero character or personality. It is located one block from the convention center which is its raison d’être. The lobby was often packed with conventioneers eating food procured at the hotel’s various take out venues, for example, Starbucks or taking advantage of the lobby’s Wi-Fi capability. The hotel charges $12.95 per day for in-room internet access. The corner room was comfortable although both it and the bathroom were very tight. Attention to detail is not the venue’s hallmark, for example, there was no trash receptacle in the bathroom. Service was inconsistent and ran the gamut. Washington offers a number of alternatives at comparable price points. Given a choice, I would recommend an alternative!

“Love Hamptons” We stay at Hampton Inns almost exclusively when we are traveling for pleasure and this one did not let us down! The staff was very helpful and accommodating, the hotel itself was immaculate and the room/suite was very spacious and comfortable. In addition to the standard amenities, the room included a cozy seating area with a sofa, coffee table and chair. The "kitchenette" included a sink, fridge and microwave. The bathroom was roomy and super clean. The only little negative was the TV did not pivot fully so it was a bit difficult to see from the bed. Free Wi-fi in the rooms is a big plus. It was a bit chilly when we were there and the staff lit the fireplace in the lobby area for our comfort. The seating areas in the lobby are conducive to family and friend gatherings. The breakfast was ample and very good, as is usually the case with Hamptons. We enjoyed our 2 night stay and would definitely stay here again.

“Great Hotel - friendly staff” I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights over Valentines Weekend. I got a great rate on Travelzoo and managed to get a studio suite. On check-in I was told that I had been given a room with a great view - boy was he right. I could see the Bay bridge, Coit Tower and many other sights - a truely wonderful view. The hotel is in the financial district - which shuts down at the weekend. It was a short walk away from the ferry building which had a great vibe in the evening. The hotel staff were very nice and the hotel itself is top class - my only comment would be that it is quiet at nights and the weekend. I thought the hotel would have a good restaurant to copensate but the only food available was a limited choice at the lobby bar. All very nice but I think I possibly expected more - I did not realise that the Park Grill was shut in the evenings. Other than that I loved the hotel - and room service was quite and delicious!

“Clean, safe, convenient” Centrally located within walking distances to Chinatown, Union Square, and SF MOMA. The small hotel is clean, safe and comfortable. Reception is friendly. Good selection of complimentary pastries and basic coffee. Juices and espresso are extra $1.50. Paid $120 through deal via Travelocity for the evening of the Chinese New Year Parade which was a couple of blocks away for the bleacher seating. Would definitely return when visiting the vicinity.

“ホームレスが徘徊” サンノゼは比較的治安がいいですが、はやり大都市のダウンタウンにはホームレスがつきものです。しかも、モーテルのため、深夜自室までたどり着けるので、私や同僚の部屋をノックし施しをうけようと徘徊しておりました。 アメリカのスタッフに言わせれば、そんなの平気ということでしたが、旅の疲れでこれをやられ、結構参りました。 部屋は清潔で、悪くはありませんが、ダウンタウンのモーテルとはこんなもんだということでしょうか。 朝食は毎日一緒で、パンとコーヒー、ヨーグルトというコンチネンタル形式です。

“above average airport hotel experience” I normally stay at this hotel as I have to do some business near by. I was a little bit hesitant the first time i stayed there and planned to have 3 overnights as you "normally" only want to stay max one night at any kind of Airport Hotel. But the Hilton is really a good choice, not the kind of Airport Hotel Experience that you normally have. The bar is good, the staff very friendly, the rooms are nice and the location is pretty calm. Only negative comment: the F&B Manager should look at the Menue of the restaurant. Not really a good idea to have dinner there.... Additonally, you should have a car if you plan to stay there as the taxi services in Phoenix are pretty poor (long waiting time). The shuttle service to the Airport is free with a frequency of 30 minutes. Fair rates.

“Party Hearty All Night Long” I paid $100 a night which was a good deal. The location is great- a block from the Magnificent Mile. However, the prior Trip Advisor reviewers were right. This is a noisy place. The room was relatively clean and the staff was very accommodating. I don't mind a small room either. However, I went to Chicago on business and it was like trying to work in a bar on Bourbon Street in New Orleans during Mardi Gras. This a party hotel for "20- somethings." Party Central. The parties spilled out into the hallways too. Different 20 year olds each night. I can't blame the staff. Some hotels are just party places. This might be a great pick up place for all I know. There is always laughter and partying until the wee hours of the morning. If you have kids it would work too, I guess. No one would notice their crying, even if they screamed at the top of their lungs -- and the young adults don't make out in the hallways at least. Sadly, I am a light sleeper and I needed to rest up before a work conference. I was old and tired enough to be everyone's mom. It was just a mismatch. So, while this place is OK and the location is great, just know that the rooms are tiny and the hotel is PARTY CENTRAL for "20 somethings." And, after all, the "young-uns" need their kinds of hotels too. So, if you are a "20-something," this is a place where you might have a good time. Have fun! Love, "Mom"

“dirty and "used"” stayed here as part of a bachelorette weekend. while the 2bd suite was quite large and had excellent views, the furniture was spotted, soiled, and damaged, and there was virtually no decoration except for a yard sale picture of flowers. they have a good space to work with, but sadly have treated it like a cheap motel. the room didn't feel welcoming in any sense of the word, and the extra cots we ordered were stained, lacked appropriate linens, and had linens with obvious repairs -- not quality at all. one bedroom was too hot, and i ended up sleeping in my jacket since i couldn't turn off the A/C. the internet router was sloppily attached to the wall, and served as the decor for one feature wall. the ironing board wouldn't stay open.

“Very close but not up to expectations.” Hotel is five minutes walk from baggage claim which is great! However room was very dated and poorly maintained. Bed was very uncomfortable and wouldn't inflate or deflate properly. I'd probably look else where next time to compare rates but wouldn't rule this place out if it was a good deal again.

“Pretty much top notch” I stayed at the Omni while attending a conference. At times the lobby can become overridden with meeting participants, but the hotel staff handles the crowds very well. The lobby is spacious and beautiful and has many plush couches to sit on. My room, in the West wing, was much larger than the average hotel room, and was extremely quiet. I never heard a noise from the hallway or the adjoining rooms. The bed was very comfortable. I never had to wait long for an elevator. If you are a member of Omni's frequent guest program you can get free Wi-Fi. A number of restaurants are within a block or two of the hotel. I ate at Open City, which is good and affordable.

“Excellent every time!” I have been staying at the Omni every May for a business conference for the past 3 years. I always have to send a bunch of boxes over and then back to the office. The staff has always been very accomodating both before and during our stay. They have actually helped us carry the boxes out to the convention across the street! The hotel has a nice ambiance, the rooms are clean, and the employee's are great. Have had room service on many occasions and the food is excellent. I look forward to going back in May!

“Really can't fault.” Have just stayed three nights at this hotel and really can't fault it in anyway. It's all about location, location, location and when you are located on 45th and 7th it just doesn't get any better than that. The only slight negative is that there is a lot of building work currently going on going on so during the week the hotel suggest the curtains are permanently closed to avoid embarrassing moments. Will stay here again for sure.

“A fun retreat” The JW Marriott is a beautiful facility full of fun diversions. It is a great, family-friendly place, with massive pools, a lazy river, and water slides. The golf course is one of the best in the area and will make you re-think your handicap. There are also tennis courts that double as basketball courts. The staff were friendly and helpful.The lobby was often a crazy mess full of people, but the staff seemed to do a good job of managing the chaos. The suites are modern, spacious, and luxurious. Our suite had a nice balcony view of the pool and golf course and was in pristine condition. The downstairs restaurant/bar is quality, if you are going for a relaxed atmosphere, lots of sports, and American-cuisine. We had a pretty big group, so the wait was a little long (an hour), but they let us take a buzzer to our room to wait, which helped pass the time. All in all, this is a great place if you are looking for a retreat, family-friendly spot, or a golf destination. Couples and urbanites who like to explore will likely be disappointed by its ambience and location 20 minutes north of the city center.

“Great location, well kept property.” The location of this hotel is terrific for a young couple. Plenty of bars and places to eat nearby, so you can leave the car and have plenty of options to walk. The room itself was disappointing, as we were near the elevator, lobby, and breakfast room so it was incredibly noisy in the mornings. We could mostly only see the pool even though we booked the partial ocean view room. We did not get turn down service the first two nights, even though we took our sign off of our door. They did leave us a bottle of wine as a gift for our anniversary, which was very nice. The housekeeping staff did a good job and everyone was very polite when we entered the lobby. The $22 parking (which I knew about from this website) was fine since it was very crowded around. Unfortunately it was very cloudy by the beach the week we were there, but that's not the hotel's fault.

“Excellent Choice in Midtown” This was my first stay at the Times Square Intercontinental. I visit New York regularly, but have stayed at a number of other properties on those visits. I will now focus upcoming stays on the Intercontinental. It was a thoroughly enjoyable stay in all ways. The location is excellent. Times Square, but a block or two off the heaviest pedestrian area. You are right in the middle of everything, but not directly in the congestion like some of the other Times Square hotels. The staff was excellent. They were helpful and courteous. While my room was not ready when I arrived, they called me as soon as it was ready so I could return to the hotel and go up to my room. The room was one of the nicest I have enjoyed in Manhattan. Spacious, spa-like bathroom, quiet, and nice views of the city. I slept very well and found myself happy to be in the room when I usually cannot wait to leave for my meetings and activities. The hotel is a bit more expensive, but not consistently. This stay was during the Big East basketball tournament and I found the rate competitive with most of the other properties I considered. The value was definitely there and (as I said) I am looking forward to returning on my next visit.

“Nice hotel if you aren't looking to relax in the bar in the late afternoon.” We arrived at the Embassy Suites hotel after a pretty long, white knuckle drive (heavy rain for three hours!) @ 3:30pm on a Saturday, check in went smooth, front desk folks were pleasant. We went to our room (highest floor-just like we asked for), unpacked & headed down to the bar to get a drink to relax our nerves after the rainy drive. The bar was not open. The guy in the restaurant side said the bar would open at 4:00. Really? On a Saturday afternoon with a full hotel??? So, we sat in the lobby & enjoyed Butch & Sundance (the hotel's two beautiful swans) swimming in their pool. We wandered around the grounds, checking out the pool & spa, which is nice. We came back to the bar area at 3:55, only to be told again that the bar would open at 4:00. The bartender was there setting up. 4:00 came & went & by this time our friends had called & we were off to meet them for dinner.... So that is my only complaint about this hotel. Would I stay here again, probably not, as it wasn't close to anything we were in town for. We only chose this hotel because it was the start of SXSW & there were NO rooms available close to the area we would be at. Nice hotel if you aren't looking to have a drink while you unwind.

“Great location - modern hotel” The hotel is located in Time Square - enough said. Definitely encountered several foreign tourists. The rooms were modern and surprisingly spacious for a NYC hotel. Overall, the rooms could have been kept up a little more. Service was OK but not amazing and it was a bit noisy (surprising being on the 22 floor). The price was great for the location. I had a great view of the time square. Keep in mind this hotel is not 5 stars but closer to 3.5 to 4 stars. Would likely return depending on price.

“This property runs the gamut” Overall, this is a respectable property with all the amenities that one might expect from the Embassy Suites brand. I would have no reservations about returning over and over again - however, there are a few items to consider for the occasional traveler: Rates EXCELLENT: On corporate policies (finding the appropriate room, allowing early check-in if possible, shuttle service to/from airport and T station). Rates VERY GOOD: On housekeeping, effieiciency of service, and a professional presentation. Rates FAIR: On staff demeanor, the hospitality hour and breakfast. Although they are provided, they are not as extensive as at other Embassy Suites properties. During the manager's reception, we had our sodas in styrofoam cups and no one offered us any other beverages. (3 days in a row). The breakfast is plentiful, but not prepared with any great care - the food is allowed to get cold in the trays, and the bacon was so soggy as to be inedible on two mornings. The front desk staff, as I mentioned earlier, is efficient and capable, but certainly not overly warm and friendly. This, in stark contrast to the desk staff at the Embassy Suites Manhattan. NEEDS IMPROVEMENT: The only real issue we had with this property was the lack of self-service laundry facilities (or if they existed, they were not mentioned in the Service Guide), and the little store in the lobby. Horrendously overpriced, and poorly stocked. Sodas are only sold in a vending machine down there, and the desk had no change. Many reviewers have mentioned the neighborhood - and, while we can see their point of view, we certainly did NOT feel unsafe. We found a spectacular pizza parlor three blocks from the hotel (as directed by one of the shuttle drivers), that we would never have encountered if we had stayed within the confines of the building. We walked from the T in the daylight hours, and called for a shuttle when dark. (That, only because one must traverse a construction site with very little light). Good value!!

“I wish there was...” I wish there was a "Good" rating, instead of Average or Very Good, as that might describe my evaluation better. I stayed a couple of nights in December 2012. I did not have a car to park and understand that parking is not free. The location was chosen to be close to family and events, and I think you would have a specific reason to stay in this area before choosing this hotel. It is on Santa Monica Blvd, right next to the San Diego Freeway. That could be be good or bad, depending on your needs. My room faced west, away from the freeway, and was very quiet. The hotel is not far from LAX, but I felt my cab ride was WAY overpriced at $40. Perhaps that is a "Welcome to LA" moment. The room was plain, but very clean and comfortable. I had free WiFi (NEVER get that at the high priced hotels!) and I don't know if that was becuase I am a Priority Club member. Membership is free and recommended... it may have resulted in my goodie bag offered at check in (bottle of water and a few snacks.) Hotel is not in a pedestrian friendly area, with few restaurants or other shopping available, although there was a neat little movie theater located next door I was not able to check out any further. The physical hotel is in fair shape... this is not a Hilton or Omni... yet I repeat my room was clean, quiet and comfortable. Breakfast buffet was fine.
