Hot choices included a pancake machine I did not try, sausage patties and okay egg omelots. They also had biscuits and gravy, plenty of fruit, cereal, and muffins. I would like to brag on the staff. Customer service was friendly and helpful at the front desk. Nothing "bargain hotel" about the way I was treated! I would recommend this hotel for a solo traveler, perhaps an adult couple, but not for family with children.

“location location location!” basic budget hotel in a fantastic location for access to bars, cafes, shops, etc. large rooms and friendly staff and a bargain if you don't mind not having the lil extras like coffee makers, shampoo etc.

“Nice stay!” We stayed at the Colonnade while my husband was in town on business. We'd been here before and looked forward to coming back. Our room this time was not quite as nice as what we had before but still a very nice room. The bathroom for this stay was pretty small but we'd had a nice big bath the last visit so I don't know if this was just luck of the draw or what. You'll get a cute little rubber duckie to take home to remember your stay! The only thing I disliked was that the iHome clock was very, very bright. It was not until the day we left that I realized it had a dimmer button (same button as the snooze) that would have made sleeping much easier. We got room service for breakfast two days and it was very prompt and courteous. I had a bit of a disappointing lunch at Brasserie Jo with really slow service but this may have just been a bad waiter as we'd had good luck there on our prior visit. Great location across from the Prudential Center and an easy walk to Newbury Street.

“Buy Low and Expect to Get What You Paid For” Just stayed at the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown for 2 nights this past weekend. If you get a low rate and go without a lot of high expectations, you should be ok. The location is good, central. Like the convenience of being across the street from Reading Terminal Market. Nice having Starbucks (a real store) in the lobby. As a platinum, was "upgraded" to a concierge level room. The room was one of the cookie cutter Marriott layouts, not very roomy, but ok... no robes, amenities, etc. you'd expect on the concierge level. Of course, lounge was closed on Saturday, but went on Monday morning for breakfast at 915am... and found out breakfast stopped at 9am (didn't receive anything with the hours of the lounge on checkin or in the room... they are posted on the wall outside of the lounge (the floor above mine). Seems a little early for me, but the attendant gave us a yogurt and some juice from the back. This hotel is a large, older hotel that caters to conventions and large groups. The staff was nice enough but doesn't seem to go the extra mile. Staffing seemed bare bones, so experienced waits at the front desk. First night didn't ask for turndown... 2nd night asked and upon entering the room it didn't seem that they came as the towels in the bathroom were still on the floor... curtains still open. Then, I noticed 3 mints on the pillow and the corner of the blanket pulled back. Wow, nice. The main reason I like turndown is to get fresh towels... pickup trash, close drapes, etc. So, what do they consider turndown here... mint delivery? Very poor. FIRE ALARMS... Both days the fire alarm went off in the hotel. The first night at 11pm... after a while when they made the announcement that all was ok... they kept repeating it every few minutes... so annoying, esp. when you're trying to get to sleep. They must have made this announcement at least 5 separate times over a half hour period, each time repeating about 5 times... seemed unnecessary. The next day the fire alarm went off again mid morning. Again, after the leave the building announcements.. and a wait, the announcements started saying that there was no fire. So, do they have false alarms every day? So, even with the very low rate I got for the weekend, I doubt I'd return to this hotel. Too many inconveniences and lack of service. My stay at the Westin (the old Ritz Carlton) was on a much higher level.

“Good option downtown” Just stayed here on business - rooms have a "beach" feel, color scheme etc so that's a little different but overall I enjoyed my stay. Very friendly service at the desk, bell stand, and breakfast. Free shuttle within 3 miles - very convenient. Great feature - the bellman has a contact with a car service. Driver waited 20 minutes for me running late from a meeting.

“Fair Enough Fairmont” We stayed here for 2 nights and had booked a smoking room yeah i know how bad it is but well we were on holidays and the option was there. I found the check in staff quiet abrupt, she growled that firstly she did'nt think they took travellers cheques and that she did'nt have a smoking room because they were busy, fair enough but i had gone to the trouble of phoning to enquire about both issuses and was told neither was a problem. The receptionist stomped around because i had a few traveller cheques to sign and then gave me a key and i had to ask her what floor, i found her attitude a bit crap and i was after an 11 hour flight with stopover and delays. The room was nice but small and the bed was small for a kingsize but squash in and it was comfy. We had a corner room so maybe avoid this type. The bathroom was small but spotless with nice selection of toilitries and towels. Concierge desk was a breath of fresh air very polite and helpful. The hotel itself is lovely a bit of old fashioned glamour in a handy location quiet close to Dealey Plaza and there is tourist office also near Dealey Plaza which was convient . Breakfast outside the hotel is mission impossible,however if you walk towards Dealey Plaza there is a carpark on open ground and on it in a corner is a strange almost invisible little blue and white hut which was fab...looks aren't everything as you stand outside,my husband has a serious food allergy so we can't just eat anywhere. For restaurants there are a few nice ones just 4/5 minutes stroll from the hotel and they are lovely.Not a lot to do downtown at the weekends its a bit deserted. Overall we had a good time ,hotel is nice and well kept

“Always a great stay!” I love staying at the Four Seasons Hotel when I come to Austin. The staff is wonderful and always accommodating. The rooms are always clean and I absolutely love how comfortable the beds are! Great location and beautiful lobby. The Four Seasons Austin really does go above and beyond to make their guests comfortable and happy! If you are planning a trip to Austin this is the place to stay!

“Surprisingly Awesome!” We stayed here for two nights with our five year old while attending a wedding at the Tremont Grand (the buildings are connected). I used to live in Baltimore so I am familiar with the city and hadn't heard much about this hotel. I wasn't expecting much, judging from the chaos we experienced at check-in. There was a wait to even pull into the line to wait in line for valet parking, and inside things weren't much better. However, once we cleared the first floor, things were much much better (and stayed that way). We could see the entire harbor and more from our 31st floor room. Room was spacious, clean, and came with free wifi and bottled water. No strange smells, which as a frequent traveler I always brace myself for. Everything in the room worked. There were several weddings going on so we heard people coming back to their rooms at midnight or so but nothing too awful. The next day, we found that all the wedding guests were abuzz about the comfie sheets and beds! We loved the deli downstairs. Valet guys were great, as we were in and out. Front desk staff were very helpful. Full grocery store around the corner. At check out, staff gave me a print out with custom directions. Location is very convenient - you can walk south to the harbor (we walked to the National Aquarium) or north to the hip shops/cafes in Mt. Vernon. If you're not a walker, they offer a free shuttle service pretty much anywhere you'd want to go within the city (Fell's Point, Inner Harbor, etc.). Minor complaint - at one point two out of four elevators were down, but it was repaired quickly. And as I mentioned, check in area is small and can get crowded. Bottom line - we'd stay again. Great value (Tremont web site rate), great room, great location.

“Unkempt, Unclean, Unfriendly” In the last 4 months, I have traveled to NYC weekly on business, staying in hotels all over Manhattan. This is my FIRST NEGATIVE review. The front desk staff was lazy, lifeless, and unhelpful. The manager was rude, disagreeable, and even less helpful. And the room - the room was unkempt, unclean, and well-worn. Would NEVER recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Cheap for downtown, but BRING EARPLUGS!” Right next to railroad tracks with freight trains going by and blasting their horn at least once per hour. This definitely kept me awake despite wearing earplugs. On the bright side, the breakfast was good and this is walking distance to some good bars and restaurants in the gaslamp as well as the SS Midway and other ships in the harbor.

“Good for business stay” I stayed at the Aloft Dallas Downtown for a business trip and it was conveniently located just a walk away from the convention center. The hotel rooms look like they are from a converted warehouse (brick walls, exposed pipes, etc.), so it is good if you are looking for a modern. For food, there is a wide variety of breakfast and lunch food options (I saw a chef cooking breakfast in the morning). There are several places to sit and eat, but not a restaurant. The bar does serve food (think appetizers, small plates) so it is good if you are looking for a quick bite, but I would not recommend for a sit-down meal. The staff was extremely helpful and answered any requests quickly and courteously.

“Great location, but smelly and overpriced.” On the last night of a family trip centered around seeing Mount Rushmore, we wanted to be in the heart of Denver. On the positive side, the Oxford is ideally situated one block from the 16th street Mall (a very nice fifteen-block promenade). It has some wonderful restaurants nearby (Gumbos was a treasure) and is perfectly located for access to the river trail, the performing arts center, and the various sports complexes. On the negative side, there is the snootiness of select members of the staff, a wretched cover-up smell of the room (aimed at hiding tobacco remnants), and a general lack of customer service. When we first arrived, the curbside parking for the hotel valet had five cars occupying the entire section. After circling for roughly twenty minutes, the same five cars were there, including a van for a vendor in their lobby promoting their service. We eventually found metered parking. Upon entering the double doors to the lobby with our bags, we literally bumped into two employees on their way out the doors who rather than offer to assist, instead barreled right past us, not even noticing we were there. Perhaps they were on their lunch break, but the basic courtesy of yielding right of way to people schlepping bags or at least holding a door open as a nice gesture would have been appropriate, not as an employee, but a basic rule of etiquette. While waiting for our turn to check in, two people popped behind the counter to collect documents from a printer. Neither took even a second to look up and at least acknowledge that they were not a desk clerk and that the one desk employee would be with us soon. This set the tone for nearly the entire stay (sans the valet at checkout, who was wonderful). What perhaps is most vexing is that while we waited to check in, we were asked if we needed a house pet by a vendor in the lobby. While we are animal lovers, it felt a bit pressured to be hustled a dog or a cat while on vacation and checking into a hotel. Once in our room, we got a telemarketing call from their spa pushing us to make an appointment. This was after we already mentioned to the clerk at check in that we weren’t interested in the spa service. If they would put half the effort they put into selling you more services while on site into making the stained plastic bathtub and ugly caulking a bit nicer, the rooms would be magnificent. The room itself is very well appointed, except for the bathroom. The psychotic temperature of the shower water is to be expected in an old building, but be prepared for a hot-to-icy-back-to-hot ride in the shower. The only issue we have with the hotel itself is that we reserved a non-smoking room that they deemed to be tobacco-free after unloading enough “air-freshener” to kill any and all insects that may have been living in the room. The fact that only one of three windows opened (the other two were painted shut) didn't allow the fragrance to vent as it should have. All-in-all, it was a very below-average experience. We did have a great experience at the other two Denver area hotels we selected during this trip, but they aren't as ideally situated as the Oxford. Be advised, this is NOT a place to stay with kids. They don’t promise to be, so it’s no fault on their part. If you wish to stay here with kids, plan many off-site activities (which there are several within walking distance).

“Loved the Grand Hyatt” I live in DC but stayed here for one night to escape my housemates when my boyfriend was in town, and everything was impeccable. Both the service and room were excellent. We stayed at the club level which was definitely worth it, there's a cozy little lounge with refreshments, and our floor was very quiet. The room was on the small size but was comfortable for two people and was wonderfully decorated, the desk had an aeron chair and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was also very tastefully done and everything was clean and bright. Definitely recommended!

“Very nice - recommended” We lucked into a great rate of $139 for this hotel, and were very pleased with the property and its location. The hotel is at Herald Square with a subway station on the next corner. Times Square is easily within walking distance; just follow Broadway diagonally and you are there in minutes. Rooms were clean and furnishings very nice. High speed internet worked great, and there was also a free business center downstairs if you wanted to print anything. Breakfast was way more than I expected in an NYC hotel. Friendly staff. A/C was great and very welcome as Manhattan was having a series of its typical steamy summer days.

“Nicely upgraded Holiday Inn Express” This hotel is located right next to Lucas Oil Stadium and has been significantly upgraded. It's one of the better Holiday Inn Expresses we've stayed at--rooms are comfortable and modern. It's a little noisy because of location and it's not convenient to downtown. Breakfasts are typical for Holiday Inn Express. Front desk staff are friendly. Exercise room has a few cardio machines and there is a pool.

“Guess I was Lucky” I travel to Charlotte all the time for work and usually stay at the OMNI downtown. This time, ALL the downtown hotels were sold out and my company travel department booked me here. I was worried because it was not downtown and I wondered what there would be available to do at nighttime. I have to say I disagree with the more recent reviews. Maybe they've improved but I had a very good stay. My room was really big and looked exactly like the pictures. The bed was comfortable and there were 4 pillows per bed. Bathroom was clean and there were lots of towels. My room had a small sink and mini fridge for storing your own food. TV was huge. And they had internet service in the room which worked - something that never happens at the OMNI. The downsides to the room were that they don't give you any lotion (just shampoo and conditioner), there are no books on Charlotte in the room (only a bible) and they don't turn the air conditioner on prior to your arrival so the room is hot when you arrive. The hotel fitness center was impressive - I thought the machines were a better quality than the downtown hotels and it was empty. They also have a big pool which was empty the whole time i was there. I took advantage of the free breakfast and starbucks coffee in the morning before heading to work. The front desk staff were all very helpful and nice. I honestly didn't experience any attitudes or anything negative. The downside to the hotel - no waiting taxi's outside. We reserves a taxi the night before to pick us up and take us downtown and it never showed. We ended up sharing a taxi with another guest who graciously offered. Overall, I liked this hotel better than the downtown hotel for everything except the location! I would stay here again and just call for a taxi when I needed it instead of reserving ahead of time.

“Great accomodations - easy acess to airport” Spouse and I stayed here one night before catching a plane home. The room we had (1st floor) was immaculate, large, well apportioned and with a fully furnished very functional kitchen. It was a good as any hotel room I have had in last year – other being at another RESIDENCE Inn in Montana! So the room accommodation = A+. The other treats were the very helpful desk staff, the evening hors d’oeuvres (actually a meal of sandwiches/salad, etc) and drinks (no charge) and the very adequate better than average) hotel lobby breakfast. Other Trip Advisor reviewers comments on not being close to the airport – are, I believe spurious or reflect incompetence in following directions!. We were through airport security 25 minutes after we left the hotel and it took us a total of 7 minutes to return our rental car to the airport. What’s the big deal anyway - the hotel provides a shuttle! This is a good airport hotel – go for it!

“Great location” In terms of location, the Copley Plaza is in the perfect spot. This is especially true in the summer when there are summer markets in the square. The hotel has nice rooms and is reminiscent of a time that has past (although the rooms have all been updated and are complete with modern amenities). This is particularly true in the lobby as well as the Oak Room. While the hotel is very nice, I would not go so far to say it is anything out of this world (hence the 4/5 stars). However, if friends were going to Boston, I'd definitely recommend the hotel.

“Disappointed with a favourite hotel” This is the third time I've stayed at The Churchill. Each time I have booked my room with Hotels.com and had a beautiful room overlooking the Marriott. The last 2 trips we were very satisfied with everything and enjoyed our stay and recommended to friends. The staff at the front door is fast and helpful, the restaurant staff is friendly and prompt, the hotel is clean and frankly the location is perfect for our needs. This trip we were in a room that looked directly across at another wing of the hotel and while the light wasn't as bright from the windows that was ok. The bird droppings outside on the window ledge were disgusting, but we understood. The configuration of the room was such that the bathroom was so small we were literally sitting ON the toilet paper roll and we're not large people. The access to the closet was inconvenient at times. All the above was tolerable, BUT, the first day (the evening before Thanksgiving) I requested a comfortable chair in addition to the desk chair. We were staying 5 days and with 2 people in the room we wanted something to sit on instead of just the bed. The gentleman at the front desk (has been there in former trips) sent up 2 hard banquet chairs while we were out. We requested again later in the evening from the woman working the front desk for a "comfortable" chair. We returned downstairs 10 minutes later and found that she'd not done anything about it and in fact wasn't sure of the room number I'd given her. We stood waiting and holding her attention until she - under protest it seemed - called engineering and requested that they take a chair from a vacant room for our room. The 2nd desk chair was delivered after 20 minutes. If we had not insisted I feel we would never have received the chair. This was the evening before Thanksgiving. The hotel was not full. We felt totally abandoned by this staff member and her attitude. Our valet parking was $35 a night. I went to the Marriott next door and checked and theirs was considerably less. 1. I felt that Hotels.com did not represent the room to me properly as from the description I felt I was getting the same room I'd had 2 times previously 2. The configuration of the room was incredibly inconvenient 3. The above points were not as big a deal as the attitude of the front desk.

“Chic but LOUD, comfortable but LOUD” I didn't have a problem with the small rooms, they were very well designed and I appreciate that space is at a premium in Manhattan. My bed was comfortable, the shower was lovely, the lobby and bar and service were all great. But my neighbors were all either partying or fighting. One consequence of the design of the hotel with all of those efficient little rooms is more neighbors! Please soundproof those doors, LOLA, so we all can rest a little easier!

“Location is perfect” Stayed for 3 nights with my family and found this hotel to be a typical Courtyard in a very nice location. Checkin was fast, self parking easy ($23/n), room was clean. We spent a lot of time at the convention center and it was a sceanic 15 minute walk to get there or you could take a cab for around $7. Also it was very easy to walk to Fells Point for meals that didnt feel as touristy as the Inner Harbour. Whole Foods, CVS and a movie theater are within 1 block of the Marriott. Also had diner at the Mexican place attached to the hotel, really good food at decent prices.

“perfectly decent hotel, good location, good value” The hotel is in the heart of the downtown, a stones throw from the Tech Museum. It was a great value, under $100. The room was rather basic, but very clean. Very comfortable bed/bedding, small desk as a workstation, bathroom was fine, good water pressure in the shower. We were a little worried when we returned to the hotel around 11 on a Saturday night, as there were tons of people in the area going nightclubbing. We thought the hotel would be loud, but our room was pleasantly quiet. We made a bad choice on a place to eat breakfast, but there is a French bakery right around the corner (next to McCormick & Schmick restaurant) that looked great that we found later. I would stay here again if in the area for a Sharks game or concert at HP Pavillion, it is perfectly decent.

“Great hotel at resonable price” We stayed here to go to a fundraiser at McCormick Place. The rates were very reasonable and the location was perfect. the hotel room was large, and had a fantastic view of the lake. The front desk was very helpful and accomodating upon arrival and let us check in way early. The restaurant and bar of the hotel was the only downfall. Neither were very classy. Overall, loved the stay.

“Stellar location and indie friendliness” We wanted a stay with a little history and character and considered here and the Driskill, character of two very different kinds. We know now that spending more money and staying at the Driskill would have been a huge mistake. Nothing against the Driskill - it was an issue of location. The Driskill is off 6th street, a long strip of cheesy shot bars landmined with tourist puke and scored by godawful cover bands. Austin Motel is on South Congress, which has great food, cool shops and a totally different vibe. It was no contest where we wanted to spend most of our time. It's a small, quirky, independent motel. So that means none of the nasty upcharges chain motels pile on. Want wifi, parking, coffee? All free. The other side of that coin is that you can't reserve rooms online and the hotel is somewhat thinly staffed. Depending on when you call to book, the phone might ring many times or even be busy. (They admit as much on their FAQ page.) But the staff there are very nice and have impressive knowledge about the area attractions. Rooms are simple and clean, with powerful air conditioning that's vital in the summer. Nice beds, but those looking for high thread counts or top-shelf products will be disappointed. Friends stayed the same night and it appears each room is a little different. Pool is nice. They sell t-shirts that prominently display their blatantly phallic logo. We liked the place enough to consider buying one. If you read past the part about not being able to book online and you're unafraid of quirk, you'll have a nice stay here.

“Pleasant stay” I just came back from a stay at this hotel (3/26-3/28) and had a very pleasant stay. We were in town specifically for a cervical cancer retreat but we also planned on sightseeing as well. There is no shuttle to/from the airport so be prepared to pay approximately $45 for a cab ride. They do not have flat fares so traffic and the speed of the driver will affect this price. We did not have a car so we did not have to worry about the parking fee. Our room faced Lake Union and the view was FABULOUS! I did not experience any room noise as others noted except when I opened the window and of course that is expected. Watching the sunrise and people rowing on the lake, the boats sailing and the seaplanes taking off/landing was fantastic. The location is close to the space needle ($5 cab ride) and there are plenty of restaurants in walking distance. Jillians (sports bar) is across the street and Outback Steakhouse is in the next block. There are three great restaurants to the left of the hotel that have early and late happy hour. We went to all three! The bar/lounge is really nice and the bartenders are really friendly. The front desk staff was GREAT. They were very accomodating with suggestions, letting us borrow items (tape, scissors) from the front desk, and helping us with meeting room set up. There is no 24 hour room service so that was disappointing. We did eat the breakfast buffet one morning and that was $13.95. Overall, I had a great stay. If I visited Seattle again, I would probably stay at the Marriott Residence Inn only because they had balconies, but they lacked many amenities that the Courtyard had so it would be a toss up!

“Problem happens but good recovery” I stayed at the Iroquois in New York for two nights in October 2011. The stay started badly as I arrived on a parade day, had some trouble walking to the hotel from the bus drop off at Grand Central due to road closures but finally made it there a little after 2 pm. I was told the room was not ready yet, that check-in was at 3 pm and that I could upgrade and have a room immediately if I wanted. I declined the option to upgrade and opted to wait out the hour till check-in by leaving my luggage with the hotel and going shopping. I returned at 3:30 pm or so, checked into my room, went up to my room and waited for my luggage. It took a while and finally my suitcase was delivered but not my carry-on. It turns out that another departing guest had taken my luggage by mistake through a series of bad luck occurrences - she sent her friend to retrieve her carry-on, her friend did not know what it looked like and did not have a claim slip, chose my carry-on by mistake eventhough it was nothing like her friend's and rushed out with it. I spent an anxious hour or so waiting for the other guest to return from the airport with my carry-on as I was worried about the personal information and contents of my carry-on. In the end everything worked out, the lady returned from JFK having missed her flight but with my carry-on to exchange for her correct one, and nothing was missing from my carry-on. The hotel staff were most apologetic. Front-desk offered a couple of free drinks coupon, the manager responded to an e-mail I sent about the incident and assured me their procedures were being reviewed to prevent another such incident and offered a stay in a suite at their best available price next time. The most touching though was the effort from the bellman who came up to my room subsequently with a plate of chocolates and nuts and a bottle of wine in apology. I declined the wine as I don't drink but accepted the chocolates and nuts as he was insistent that I do so. In summary, I had a problem at the hotel but they managed to respond well to the incident and, lucky for all it happened on check-in rather than check-out when a delay with the carry-on might have had much more serious consequences. On a side note, I discovered that one of the concierge was someone I knew from my stays at the Casablanca Hotel who previously impressed me with her thoughtful and efficient service, and bright smile and warm greeting each time. It is a credit to the Iroquois that such a wonderful employee moved over from the Casablanca given how fine a hotel the Casablanca is as well. Aside from the incident, the hotel was fine. The room was large and comfortable, free wi-fi was included, location is excellent just off Times Square and with lots of subway stations near by and many restaurants within close walking distance. DB Bistro Moderne almost next door was surprisingly good and not stuffy notwithstanding its celebrity chef background, and the diner down the street from the Iroquois was excellent value, efficient and convenient for an early 6 am breakfast or a late bite. My favourite in New York is usually the Casablanca for its unbeatable location, service and value-enhancing inclusions, but the Iroquois also compares well, especially because I managed to book at a fixed prepaid discount rate that was about $100 cheaper per night than comparable hotels at the same time.

“Great Staff nice rooms” We were traveling with 2 teens and stayed here for 2 nights The rooms were spacious and very clean flat screen TV great bathrooms Front staff were very helpful My only complaint was that while we were there their internet was not available. Breakfast was served till 10am it was the usual coffee,Tea,Juice, Toast,Bagels.......not anything to get excited about but its there if you want it-----our rate for 2 nights was $180inc

“Stay in the Newer Tower” We've stayed in the St. Francis several times on visits to San Francisco, but this was our first stay in the newer tower. From now on, that's the tower we will stay in as it is much fresher and less "old style hotel" than the older part of this famous hotel (but the rooms are more expensive). We sprung for a corner room (also more expensive) but we had wonderful views of the city and a very spacious room. The bed was comfortable, closet space was more than adequate, and the bathroom was large enough for two people (through only one sink) and nicely appointed. Not as many electric plugs for devices as some might need but adequate. We like the location very much--right on Union Square and a long but easy walk to the waterfront. The lobby is busy and bustling (there are usually large meetings at the hotel and the lobby is the place to meet), and the Michael Mina restaurant is a wonderful (but pricy) place for dinner. There is also a less expensive option for breakfast, lunch and dinner (The Oak Room), but many very fine restaurants are only a few blocks away if you want to go out. This hotel is our "go to" place to stay while in San Francisco.

“completely satisfied” I was completely satisfied with this hotel for what it is. It's a tourist hotel, not a luxury hotel, so it's functional but not amazing. I stayed in a room with a queen-size bed which also had a desk, decent bathroom and good closet space. The only minor feature of the room I did not like was the cheap tissues, which were rough and uncomfortable, but of course it's not hard to buy your own. The room was clean and comfortable, decent size by NYC standards, and the hotel is well located. They offer breakfast but I prefer the Bread & Butter at the corner of 29th and Park. All in all, a fully satisfactory experience. I'll be back.

“OK, but lacks a few things you would expect” The Doral Tesoro has a somewhat secluded location, near Texas Motor Speedway north of Fort Worth. If you are using it as a base to explore the attractions of Fort Worth, be prepared to drive. The hotel itself is rather bland on the outside, and the interior is finished in a combination of art deco and Texana. A bit of an odd combo. Staff is friendly, but not always knowledgable. A few things that are missing: 1. Valet parking (they have it sporadically, but there are long stretches where the bell stand is not staffed). 2. Gift/Sundry shop. There is a small "closet" beside the bell desk with a few items, but selection is very limited. 3. Minibars and vending machines 4. There is no spa, is a smallish workout room. Rooms are comfy and fairly large. Ate dinner at the restaurant, faire is primarily fish and steak, with a few other selections thrown in. Again, the selections seem to lack a common theme. But the food I had was tasty and service was OK. All in all, this is one of those hotels I would not go out of my way to return to, but if I needed to go there on business or otherwise, would not be upset about it.

“Excellent Marriott property. Would stay here again” Stayed here one night on my way into San Diego. Could not have asked for a better hotel; had a room with two queens and a sofabed. Enormous room with a great balcony. Comfortable beds, clean as a whistle. Quiet location and a great price. Front desk staff when I checked in left a lot to be desired, but maybe working on a Friday night in a tremendous city like San Diego would make the best of us cranky! Overall, this is a top notch Marriott property, and I would stay here again in a heartbeat...

“Very nice with an exception” Now, as far as being one of the finest hotels in San Francisco, no it isn't. But I've seen this with Trip Advisor before. The rooms were tastefully decorated, almost elegant. The staff very accommodating. We were there on a weekend so prices were reasonable for a San Francisco hotel near Union Square. In fact, a bargain. Parking was pretty expensive though, about a third of the cost of the room. The room we had was a little loud even though it was on the seventh floor. Street noise and the cable cars but after all it is in the middle of San Francisco. The fitness room was just basic. The room had an older tube TV, minibar prices were reasonable, robes nice. The bathroom was a nice combination of original and updated. Now for the two irritants. one small, one not so small. The in room coffee maker was set up for one person. A single cup. So you got one cup of decaf, one of regular. The big irritant was the WiFi. Just awful. Slow, dropped connections, rude customer service. It was a third party vendor called "The WiFi Guys" and their business was to sell you an upgrade to their "free" service by making the "free" service as unusable as possible. In my opinion, WiFi is either free or it isn't. No sort of free. This was free, but terrible service and presumably better service, if you paid to "upgrade". Now, they did tell me at the front desk that "The WiFi Guys" were going to be gone next month. I wasn't the first to complain. So over all a nice experience but again, not one of the finest hotels in SF, but a very good choice.

“Fantastic Stay!” One of the best hotels I have stayed at in my years of traveling. I stayed the second weekend in July, and could not have been any more happy with this hotel. Upon arrival we were offered multiple times if we needed help with our luggage and we politely declined because we did not have that much to carry. The person checking us in (Kelsey I believe her name was) was very friendly explained everything we needed to know about the hotel, including the restaurants, fitness center and pool.After we checked in we went up to our room on the 11th floor, our room had 2 double beds, it was very clean, nice size for a hotel, and very well appointed. The hotel room was very business traveler friendly with plenty of outlets, a nice size desk and hook ups for your computer, on the bad side the wifi was slow. We chose to park our selfs at the paring garage right next door, the parking garage elevators were extremely cool and it was in out privileges for 13$ a day, not a bad deal! After settling in our room we decided to do he lunch buffet at one of the hotels restaurants, it was very average; the burger was very dry and luke warm, though the service was good.After that we decided to go and tour the stock yards, very cool considering this was our first time in Texas. After a long day at the stock yards and a nice dinner we decided to return to our hotel and to our surprise there was turn down service and milk and cookies, what a nice treat after a long day! . As previous reviewers said the pool was a little on the small side and the pool was a little to warm for my liking but it was a nice little refresher. Check out was extremely smooth and we did not have any problems. Over all a fantastic stay, if we are in the Fort Worth area again we would return in a heart beat!

“Not so boutique” This hotel was disappointing and as a frequent traveler to DC I know that for the price and the area one can do much better. This is one of the Kimpton chain that advertises their properties as "life style" hotels. I have stayed in many of these around the country, and have liked most except this one. This property received more of a make-up job than a re-do and feels more like a fancied-up motel than a "life style." For example, the old gouged door mouldings have simply been painted over. The rooms are on the small side; mine was configured in a very strange way and was noisy. And, it was not cheap. The contracted restaurant on the first floor served me inedible food for dinner and the "free" buffet breakfast turned out to be neither. When I complained by email after the fact, management was unsupportive. If you like Kimptons, try the Monaco (and get a goldfish). Otherwise, check Tripadvisor for one of the many other very nice hotels near Dupont Circle.

“Scary Place” It's sad that the management has let this hotel become so decrepit. For starters, the odor from the mold in the lobby is overwhelming (if you have any sort of dust or mold allergies, you really need to avoid this place). The internet service was not working at all when I was there. The beds are ancient. I stayed 30 minutes, and then bit the bullet and found another hotel because the odor was making me ill and the room was so dirty. There are so many excellent hotel options in San Antonio. If you love historic places, take a walk through the public spaces in the Menger. Just don't stay here if you are an aversion to mold and bugs.

“Pretty good, but not a 5-star” I visit Chicago every other month and hadn't gotten a chance to stay here (it's a little far from my business, but this time I got a good deal because of renovations to the 7th floor, so decided to try it out.) Had to say, I was a bit underwhelmed. Generally I stay at the Conrad, which is also not exactly 5-star, but is still good. But this might be on par with that, but definitely not in competition with say, the Trump. The service is pretty good. Everyone's very helpful. Like the coffee/tea in the lobby in the mornings, hot chocolate in teh afternoons and sparkling waters at night. Room was big with a nice view of the old water tour. Free internet with good signal. Big plasma TV, though no HD options on the in-demand, so kind of a waste if you need a movie to keep you up while you're trying to get some work done. Bed was not really comfortable. It's a shame, considering, but I was very surprised at the fact that it wasn't. Amenities were okay, nothing special. Ordered dessert form room service and was underwhelmed. Took awhile for a pre-made tarte. Pot of tea included one bag insufficient for the water provided and got cold almost immediately. The Conrad has far superior room service to make up for the smaller room size. Anyway, I tried it. I definitely wouldn't pay regular rates for it without some sort of refurb. If you want to pay that much the Trump seems far superior.

“Nice location but small rooms” This hotel was ideally located for a group of us attending an event just across the Park & handy for local restaurants on Columbus & Amsterdam Avenues. Staff were OK & the outside of the building appeared to be undergoing rennovation, but that wasn't causing any disturbance. the cost was about $275 a night. I've stayed nearer the centre of Manhattan in the past, but this place was far enough out to be relatively peaceful, eat in restaurants full of locals at night, but still be close enough to the action. The rooms were small & there were no tea or coffee making facilities & no free internet. But as all rooms I've stayed in in NY have been tiny & there's a Starbucks or equivalent on every corner these aren't major hassles.

“Nice suite type property, good location in DC” Spent about four nights here as part of an Adoption group reunion. This was a wise choice for families...and overall a good value with afternoon snacks, breakfast, good sixed suites, and a fine pool. Our group used it as a base to tour Washington DC. It was fairly close to the Metro Station at George Washington University. Recommend for family or group stays in the District. Standart Embassy Suites accomodations, nice staff.

“Marriott - Can Never Go Wrong” I absolutely love this hotel and recommend it to all my friends. Its in a great location downtown...perfect walking distance to entertainment and shopping. The beds were so difficult to get out of in the morning...just a little slice of heaven in my room. Now the rooms are a bit smaller but I don't spend that much time in my hotel room to justify having it any larger. As i said before, I love this hotel and recommend it to anyone that visits Downtown Denver.

“Wonderful convenient hotel with great service” Stayed for 3 nights in June 2009. Hotel is literally steps from Times Square, service throughout was wonderful and extremely accommodating. All the front desk people seemed to learn my name notwithstanding my brief stay. Rick's Cafe is a nice touch offering breakfast and through out the day refreshments. My room was not fancy, but it was not too small and it was well equipped with an air conditioner, a DVD player, and a ceiling fan. Free wireless internet in room and in Rick's Cafe is a nice touch. The Italian restaurant recommended by the hotel had wonderful food and service, I can strongly recommend that as well. I have already booked to return to the Casablanca and think it will be my home base in New York as long as it does not become too pricey.
“great location” This hotel is right in the center of San Fran. Watch out though, there are several other westins around. A bit confusing. Easy access to the city. Nice rooms and service.

“Great, convienent location” Used this Motel 6 for 2 nights based on location, reviews and price. Our room was clean, with few amenities, as expected from a budget chain. Not the quietest place to stay but some of that was inconsiderate guests. TV listings didn't match what was available on the TV and the reception wasn't very good, but not there to watch tv. Beds and pillows average at best. Internet slow but stayed connected. Additional $10 per day parking charge that you have to go to the desk every day to take care of, kind of a pain. The big positive is being 1 block from Hollywood Blvd and all the craziness that can entail. Around .5 mile walk to Metro (red line) in both directions. Priced considerably lower than most anywhere else in the area. A good choice if price & location out weigh amenities and real quiet.

“Ok” Stayed with Amex fhr rate - door staff good, desk staff unwelcoming and explained fhr benefits incorrectly - room upgrade good, but rooms still odd but interesting, bed very comfortable but the noise from the terrace for my 17th floor room ridiculous, and sounded like they were auditioning for Stomp. Breakfast good, but be careful as the fhr $100 credit is only good at the terrace and does not cover the other restaurant or minibar-very poor!!! Will try Crosby Hotel next time.

“Newer, spacious, clean and well located, this Residence Inn offers all necessities in a comfortable package” Spotlessly clean, this Residence Inn feels like a comfortable pied a terre in a great location in downtown Chicago. The well appointed suite lives like a studio apartment, with the added bonus that someone else cleans up after you and that a varied breakfast, with healthy options, is prepared for you. The staff were harried, as the hotel was full, and I did not receive a warm feeling from some of them. Others were managing the volume of work with a smile. I will stay here again.

“Everything. Right where you need it” Welcoming entrance. Lots of open areas for small meetings with colleagues or just lounging. Quiet hotel. Check in was early. Pleasant staff ... accommodated early check in and attempted to provide a room based on my specific requests. Nice fitness room, small pool, and spa. Wireless all over, including rooms. Complimentary business center. Airport shuttle. Beautiful rooms included refrigerator, microwave, and coffee pot (does anyone ever use those?). Flat screen TV (32 inch). Lots of channels., including HBO. Hotel room was clean. Well maintained. Very comfortable bed. Hotel was located in a new retail village with a few restaurants in walking distance and some shops. Didn't try hotel breakfast. Wasn't really hungry enough to justify the $10 breakfast tab. Chose instead to walk to area restaurant and a group of us had breakfast sandwiches there. Complimentary coffee in lobby. Didn't suit our taste, however. Found a coffee shop nearby to suit our taste (about four blocks away). Starbucks also in walking distance. Little pricey at $169/night. Made reservations from hotel website.

“Beautiful views” The room had a beautiful view. As stated in previous reviews there is a faint air freshener scent when you first walk into the room. The beds are very comfortable. Everything was neat and clean. The sink in the bathroom was actully set very high. I found this uncomfortable. It is unbelieveable to me that the do not have wireless access in the room. You would have to go to a desiganted area downstairs to use your laptop. The deli on the first floor next to the Lobby desk was large and has limited seating. For a deli that large the amount of food available was very limited. The sandwiches were pre-made and looked like they were there all day so I did not purchase. During the middle of the night around 2am the alarms in the hotel sounded. The loud speaker came on in the hotel room telling everyone that everything was under control. It was very frightening. This has happened previously at another Marriott I stayed in. I don't know what that is all about. The area has many restaurants however it was so cold out that it was impossible to walk to them. We took a cab to the mall which is really a dump. It cost over $5.00 which can be expected but we could not find one on the way back. It took about ten minutes and it was freezing. Ordered room service which was very good and came in less then 30 minutes. Everyone at the hotel was very helpful and pleasant. I would try the Hyatt next time.

“It's all relative in NYC.....” About me. Starwood Gold member and used points for two nights at this hotel. Rate I found on line was $315 per night which I felt was high for a Four Points property. Arrived just after 6 a.m. after a redeye from the west coast. Room availability at that hour is always a coin toss but they typically willl check you in when you are part of their "program." In this case hotel was completely sold out the night before. Seeing I was in a jam, the front desk clerk offered me a key to a room that had been vacated but not yet cleaned so I could change into a suit for me meeting. The clerk that came on shortly after, asked for my cell # and called me by 9:20 a.m. with a clean room ready for my use. I've been to 5 star hotels that do not offer that kind of service. Bellman and conierge were also helpful, friendly and cordial each time I encountered them. I cannot say enough about the staff at this hotel. Location - I had 25th floor at the back of the hotel facing the Westin at 51st and 8th. Noise was absolutely zero. I'm a little confused about the noise complaints from buses in and out of the port authority. There is some traffic in front of the hotel but I saw few buses and anything was rarely moving fast enough to make any noise due to proximity to traffic light and traffic. Perhaps it is louder on lower floors and/or facing another direction. I'm not sure what people expect in NY but there is nothing unsafe about this location. There is one or two adult bookstores on the block but never did I encounter anyone loitering and feel uncomfortable at any of the day or late night. Well located to attractions, dining, subway and Times Square. Best to walk 1/2 block to 8th or 9th to get a cab. They were not easy to find in front of the hotel. FInally, this place is great if you are traveling in or out of Newark airport. Very close to the tunnel and you can get a one way charter bus on Coach USA for $15. Door to door in under 40 minutes. Rooms - nice decor with minimalist approach to decorating. Beds were very comfortable and clean. Flat screen tv, clock radio with mp3 connection, plenty of outlets to plug things in. Bathroom lacks counter space as do most in Manhattan. Strangest thing to me was having the turn water pressure all of the way on to get hot water. The flat bottom sink would splash everywhere so use caution if you are fully dressed. Great glass shower with good pressure and lots of space. In room safe, iron and ironing board all in good working order. Two free bottles of water per day and wired/wireless internet included throughout the hotel. Yes - the room is small as most are in NYC. If you sit at the desk across from the bed, another person cannot pass behind you. You just dont get square footage in the city so I dont factor this as a negative. Hotel - did not use the gym. Lounge is small counter up front for breakfast and drinks in the evening with a tv for sports or news. Did not order room service or use small restaurant on premise so I cannot speak to food. All common areas were were cared for and clean. Not much negative to say about this hotel. If you can get a fair rate for this brand, it certainly is a little gem for business or pleasure.

“Can't top this hotel in Detroit” My wife and I stayed at the Westin Book over Thanksgiving while in Detroit for the Packers-Lions game and found the hotel to be beautiful, well-located and with excellent amenities. We had a very nice room with a comfortable bed, plenty of stoage in both the closet and dresser and a large, well-appointed bathroom. The shower was quite powerful, even in water-saving mode. We enjoyed drinks in the second floor lounge twice and had an excellent dinner at Michael Symon's Roast despite a slightly undercooked steak for my entree. We did not get a chance to take advantage of the pool or fitness facilities, though given the overall high quality of the hotel, I am confident they are fine. Finally, the staff at the Book is very good and exceedingly friendly, from the maids, to the front desk staff to the staff in the coffeehouse. If there is one small complaint about the hotel, the adjacent parking is separate from the hotel and is cash-only, which led to a little confusion when we were checking out. Overall, we would highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Detroit. We do not think there is another hotel of the Book's caliber in downtown Detroit.

“Fabulous Experience - Excellent Customer Service” I just returned from a 6 night stay at the Nikko for a convention. After initially reading reviews on TripAdvisor, I was concerned about staying here and booked a room at the Hotel Prescott instead. BAD IDEA. That hotel was so bad that I checked out before I checked in and fled to the Nikko. Everyone at the Nikko was incredible from the front desk staff to the business center to housekeeping. Everyone did whatever they could to accommodate us and make sure that we had a pleasant stay. We upgraded to the 23rd floor where we had a fabulous view and a wonderful room. It was very comfortable, clean and functional. The hotel was packed with convention attendees the entire time we were there, but the staff didn't skip a beat and we got first class service the entire time we were there. We attended several receptions there and the food was always good. Be sure to try the Asian restaurant on the second floor. The food was incredible. We sat at the bar and visited with the bartender who made great drinks and excellent recommendations for food. If we go back to San Francisco, regardless of whether it was for business or pleasure, we'd definitely stay at the Nikko again.

“Value and Charm” This is without question an extremely charming hotel with exceptional service. It is also a very good value depending on the deal but if you stay within $400 or so it's on the short list. Great location for shopping,restaurants and the park. The complimentary wine reception at 5 is a wonderful touch as is the breakfast. The service at all levels is polished and professional. The rooms are definitely showing their age but are still nice. However if you are staying here from April on be forewarned of construction taking place across from hotel on 54th street. The noise is ridiculous!!! I never get too upset because I visit the city frequently but this was exceptional noise. I dont know if the other side of hotel was more serene but do NOT stay in room facing 54th. Didnt bother staff with it so I do not hold them responsible for room but I thought it relevant to future guests for me to post it. Overall a very nice hotel with a French flair in a great "usually serene" location between Park and Lex.

“Great hotel!” From the moment you arrive, you know you are in for treat. The hotel staff was friendly, attentive, and helpful. The rooms were very clean and nice; I did not see one with a bad view. We were at the hotel with a large group for a wedding. The hotel was booked to about a 75% occupancy the night before we arrived due to accommodating a large group (Washington Redskins). Despite it, the staff was still able to accommodate us with an early check in. The staff offered water (bottles) at check-in and check-out. We did have spotty wi-fi in our room, but the hotel removed the charge without hesitation. There's a Capital Grille connected to the hotel that was out of this world. This hotel comes HIGHLY recommended.

“Comfortable and convenient” I often stay at Marriott Courtyard when I travel, and that's the main reason that I chose this hotel. I consider this hotel to be above average when compared to other Courtyard properties. The room I had was quite a bit larger than I expected and the bed was exceptionally comfortable. I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. The hotel is centrally located in downtown Columbus, walking distance to the Statehouse, the Convention Center, etc. As far as I can tell, the only option for parking is valet service, which was $18 per day when I was there. You park your car at the curb of the street and someone will take it away. The car was always there promptly when I called and asked it to be brought around. The only surprise for me was that you need to negotiate stairs (5 or 6 of them) to get to the elevator. As far as I know, that's the only way to get to the rooms. So you need to carry your bags up and down these stairs when you arrive and depart or you need to ask for bell service.

“Historic site in a superb location” I enjoyed very much staying at the Westin St Francis. The lobby is beautiful and remind us of all its history. It is located just in Union Square, with all the shops there, blocks away from Market Street, near the Cable Car stop... Everything worked fine in the room but watching paid movies. Nice room.

“Good Hotel, Staff Glitching in Overload” Good solid facilities with lots to offer, proximity to the convention center, easy walk to 6th SAt or even to the Capitol. Staff seemed to be on overload this convention unlike other times i have stayed, no acknowledgement of elite status, no checkout paperwork - which i was informed i would have an option at check in but was never offered, bar seemed to be slow and pouring into dirty glasses, the elite lounge was very pooor, no hot foods, comeon Hilton even the Hampton Inn offers hot breakfast, and difficulty with staff keeping the counters stocked. overall you wont go wrong for location and proximity, good facilities but staff needs work.

“Renovated Rooms Are Great...Service So-so” Our family (two adults, two kids) stayed here Dec. 18-21. We had read the reviews on TripAdvisor so we knew that some of the rooms were not that great. We deliberately looked for and booked a 'New Room' on the Hilton web site. Got a $279 rate that included full breakfast; high, but quite decent for New York. Overall, we were happy. The room was great; the front desk, concierge and bell captain service was so-so; the restaurant 'NY Marketplace' was decent for breakfast, terrible for dinner. More detailed descriptions below for those who are interested. Pictures of the renovated room are also posted. The Room: We were very impressed with the renovated room. Of course, since it was recently renovated, it was very clean and things looked new. It was also very spacious (except for the bathroom). The renovation included nice touches which you normally find in smaller boutique style hotels, such as stylish/funky lamps and a large LCD tv. The beds were extremely comfortable. Fixtures in the bathroom were very stylish and attractive. I normally stay in Sheraton NY Hotel and Towers, and I've never had a room this nice, even when I've gotten a renovated one. The Sheraton rooms are smaller, darker and generally less well decorated. And the Hilton 'Comfortable Bed' was much more so than the Sheraton 'Heavenly Bed'. Our room in the Hilton was on the 22nd floor. Some other floors appeared to have been renovated, but several did not appear to be; those older floors looked quite depressing. Book a renovated room and you're much more likely to have a good stay here! The Service: if you've read the reviews here, you'll know not to expect too much in the way of service. The front desk staff was efficient but fairly disinterested at check in. The concierge seemed annoyed that they had to give out directions to the subway to yet another customer. On the last day of our stay, the room was not made up at all. Sometime between 6pm and 9pm, someone dropped a new set of towels on the unmade beds but did not clean up at all; we called the front desk but they said housekeeping was behind (no kidding) and they would get to our room as soon as they caught up. Needless to say, they never did! Finally, the Hilton airport shuttle service charged us twice for our ticket to the airport so now we have to get that cleared up with the credit card company. Oh well. We liked our room anyway. NY Marketplace Restaurant: Breakfast buffet (included in our rate) was extensive and most things tasted good. Dinner was horrible (calamari, pizza, burger) and extremely overpriced; don't waste your money there, especially with so many restaurants nearby. Overall: if we can get a renovated room at a decent rate, we will stay at the Hilton again. If not, we'll keep looking...

“Would have been perfect had we NOT had the WORST view in Chicago” I have stayed at this hotel three other times and each time we had a view that was absolutely unbelievable! On these other trips, we were never told that there was an additional charge for a room that faced OUTSIDE. But, this time, that was the case. So, we were in room 1855, which looked out at a WALL. It didn't seem like the hotel was very full so I don't understand putting guests in rooms with awful views - the staff should be showcasing the marvelous views, which are an important feature of the hotel. The room was ample and the bedding was nice. Housekeeping did a fantastic job and when we returned in the evening, the room looked as good as the first day we moved in. But - one day housekeeping didn't come at all. When I mentioned this to the manager, he was indifferent. The front desk staff is a little unfriendly and robotic as compared to other hotels in which I have stayed. All in all, had we not had to look at a wall, I would have been much happier about our stay.

“It is what it is” This place has a certain '50s charm, and the room rate was reasonable. However, while there, the elevator was out 90% of the time, the pool was closed one day, and parking spaces were scarce. I heard there are some rooms that have been updated nicely, but we didn't have one of them. On the plus side, the shower was fabulous and the downstairs diner, Swingers, had great food and very nice staff. Location was very good for us on this particular trip. Very close to The Grove/Farmer's Market, CBS Studios and Hollywood.

“Brand New Grand Old Hotel” This hotel is located at the heart of a thriving and modern shopping, dining and entertainment zone. I could not find any downsides. It has a classical feel because of the furnishings and decoration, yet everything is brand new. The carpets are impeccable, the hotel is clean and smells fresh. It looks like an old building outside but inside it is all new. I got access to the Executive Lounge and it has a good continental breakfast offering. Everything is top quality. It has a very complete gym, spa and indoor swimming pool, a restaurant, a café, lobby bar. Quality is their trademark. Congratulations!

“Sauberes und freundliches Motel” Mein Zimmer war geräumig, gut ausgestattet und sauber. Der Verkehrlärm der vorbeiführenden Interstate ist zwar zu hören, aber ich konnte dennoch gut schlafen. Das Personal an der Rezeption war sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. In einem kleinen Raum hinter der Rezeption gibt es auch einen PC mit Internet-Anschluss. Das Frühstück war besser als bei vielen anderen Kettenmotels. Es gab Rührei und Hackfleischröllchen. Zur nächsten DART Metro Station sind es 15 Minuten zu Fuß.

“Good hotel for a business conference” Well managed property as you would expect for this brand and price point. Front desk very helpful with dinner and transportation arrangements. Rooms comfortable but AC is lacking. Good location within a couple blocks of several good dining spots.

“Not the Ritz, but a pleasant stay” I stayed at the Sportsmen's Lodge bacause I was speaking at a meeting there. I agree with the earlier review that if you're OK with Hampton Inn types, this will be fine. It's also got a lot more character than a Hampton Inn or a Courtyard. Definitely an older property but my room was clean and everything worked. The pool was huge and I pretty much had it all to myself although they were setting up for a reception for a vetrinarian's convention later in the evening. With Ralph's across the street, I didn't try the restaurants. Ralph's had everything- lots of good freshly-prepared foods, half-bottles of wine (some with screw tops if you didn't have a corkscrew!), even bagels and little containers of cream cheese so I had something for breakfast on my 7 AM flight home the next morning. The only hotel food I had was the catered lunch at the meeting. The chicken had some sort of clear lemon sauce that tasted good but was totally unappetizing because it had congealed. The catering service should do a better job of selecting dishes that will still be OK when you're trying to serve 30 people at once. Computers are available in the lobby but there's a charge to go on-line and printing is $2.50 a page. My room rate was $149 but taxes and $10 for high-speed Internet brought it up to $177. Still a good value for this area, I think.

“LOVELY.” We just stayed here in July for business. Very nice hotel. Lovely. Spacious modern rooms. Beds are very comfy. The shower is awesome. Very clean room. TV is awesome. Starbucks in the Lobby. The Front Desk staff were all very accommodating. For some reason one day when we returned to our room, it was never made up. We were heading out to dinner and mentioned our room and the front desk staff immediately apologized and jumped right into action. We came back and the room was beautiful. All extra towels. Bed turned down. Just very welcoming.

“Older Hotel Just Not Worth It” I spent a couple nights at the Marriott Plaza San Antonio after booking what seemed like a good deal for a 4-star hotel, but unfortunately this old hotel was unable to deliver. I would have rather stayed at a nicer hotel on the River Walk, where 3.5-star hotels can be had for nearly the same price. It was clear from the start that this is not a modern hotel. The lobby was in a good state of repair, but everything was dated. The hotel had been decorated in a more traditional and less contemporary manner, luckily, so it had not aged into a wholly unappealing mess. However, the age really showed through in the fitness center and pool, and the Jacuzzi didn't even work. This overshadowed the otherwise pleasant courtyard area. I stayed in a sixth-floor room with a view to the northeast, and there was a small balcony attached to it. The view was nice considering the hotel isn't on the River Walk; Hemisfair Park is across the street. The room appointments were sufficient, and Marriott seemed to do a good job maintaining the clearly older furnishings. Service was fine, although not particularly friendly, and oddly my room was not serviced during my stay. Luckily I don't make a complete mess of hotel rooms. Parking was an expensive joke at $23; I recommend parking at one of the cheaper ($5-8) surrounding lots or on the street. There were no special events during my stay, so I was able to park for free a block away. This hotel would have been an even bigger disappointment if I had been forced to pay for parking.

“Horrible stay, but it ended up free!” I had an awful stay at this hotel filled with many problems, but the management was helpful on check-out and gave me the nightly stays (2) free. My first room was musty, the a/c did not work, no windows - AWFUL!!! The second room was much better but overlooked a concert stage for a Microsoft event that went very late into the night with a country band blaring. I thought no windows was bad, but with this band that might have been a blessing. My room key on the second room never worked and I had to call security to let me into the room each time I returned - awful! The hotel was huge and full - I had to wait for everything longer than is acceptable (15 people in line at most services). There were 3 special events in the lobby, bar and restaurant areas on Saturday night - crazy! The parking was ~$14 and was too far and unavailable the second night. I WOULD DEFINITELY PAY LESS NEXT TIME AND STAY AT THE NEW HILTON GARDEN INN NEXT DOOR!!! My coworker stayed there and I saw her room - it was very nice and included free parking, high-speed internet, a complimentary business center, hot cookies and free parking. A much nicer and newer hotel.

“Great hotel; good value; nice area!” I got this on Priceline and didn't know what to expect but was very pleased. The front desk staff wasn't the most friendly but that's a minor complaint; overall it was a great place to stay that I'd be happy to stay at again. We stayed in a studio which had a king size bed, a pullout sofa around the corner, and a nice-sized kitchen. It was very spacious and clean. The bed was very comfortable as well. The breakfast was adequate but nothing special, but had plenty of hot items on it. This was right across from City Hall and Macy's and about a half-mile (nice) walk to Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. I would jump at the chance to stay here again.

“Great hotel with a great location!” My boyfriend and I stayed here for 2 nights and it was our first trip to Dallas. The location was great, really central and close to Dealy Plaza and Neiman Marcus is just around the corner! Our room was really big which we were really happy about as we had got a really good deal for a basic room on hotels.com - if the room we got is the 'basic' one it was fantastic! There was a large living area with TV, fridge, tea/coffee facilities etc. We would have liked however if there had been an in room safe, just to keep our passports etc safe. The staff were all very nice and friendly and we would definately stay here again if we return to Dallas!

“Excellent choice” This is an excellent hotel. The service is first-rate with all staff having a "can-do" attitude: from the bellhops to the front desk staff. The location is convenient for many touring activities (although some parts of Fisherman's Wharf are a bit tacky). The room was very comfortable. I highly recommend.

“location. location. location” This is my 2nd stay at the millennium. Didn't get off to a good start, our room was dingy and smelt of stale smoke. We got relocated to the 50th floor which was a corner suite, this included complimentary bottle of wine and fruit basket. The view was just awesome. Used the concerige to book a broadway show and felt that their commission was extremely high. Fantastic little restaurant across the street. Really convenient to Times Square, Port Authortiy.

“Unique building and great staff” We stayed one night and we were satisfied with our room, found the staff very accommodating, and the location to be ideal for what we wanted to see and do. It's across the street from the Alamo and within walking distance of the Riverwalk. It has a small bistro and bar, with one great bartender......very friendly! We liked how they had refurblished the old building into a hotel. Very quaint and unique.

“Fantastic Location” This hotel makes up in location what it lacks in amenities. Set on 76th Street between 5th and Madison, this small hotel is in the heart of the Upper East Side. For folks who don't want to be in midtown, but still want access to the museums, this location can't be beat. This is as upscale an area in New York as you can find. We had an Ultra Deluxe Salon, which was spacious, with a King Bed and large seating area, clean and nicely decorated. Our room looked out onto 76th street, and street noise was manageable. The marble bathroom had a large stand-up shower and double sinks, but no tub. Overall, the aesthetics of the room were pleasing and everything was in good shape. We ordered room service, which is provided by Cafe Boulud, and while tasty, it took a while for our food to arrive and they did not include any ice water. In addition, the video on demand function on our TV did not work and it took 20 minutes or so to get the problem fixed. Small quibbles, but at this price point, mistakes are not as easily forgiven. This hotel does not have a pool and gym complex like the Peninsula or the Mandarin, but what it lacks in that department, it has in charm. The hotel also has a beautiful roof deck that is open in warmer months. I recommend this hotel to anyone visiting New York looking to avoid Midtown and the Downtown scene.

“Enjoyable trip to historical city” We stayed for 3 nights at the Sofitel in Philadelphia at the end of April 2010. The hotel is located in the Rittenhouse Square area of the city. We caught the train from New York to 30th Street station and walked from there. It's also easy to take a taxi as we did on the way back for less than $10. We prepaid the accommodation and got a good deal on a luxury room on the 11th floor with 2 double beds. The room was a really good size and the bathroom was excellent. There was a separate shower and bath and all the usual top quality toiletries. The beds were very comfortable and we had no trouble enjoying our nights sleep. The room had all the amenties you would expect such as air conditioning, safe, flat screen tv, iron etc. The breakfast was good, it was made freshly to order. But it was slow, if you are in a hurry then I would look elsewhere. The location of the hotel is good, it is in an area where there are plenty of shops and restaurants close by. We walked everywhere from the Old City to the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Philadelphia is well worth a visit with all the historical sights in the Old City. I would make sure you visit the Philadelphia Museum of Art, this was a quality museum with something for everyones taste. Also the steps made famous from Rocky's training.

“Very Good Westin with great attractions near by” I have stayed at this property in Jun of '08 and July of '09 both times I have a good stay at the Westin Tabor Center. I have always gotten a good room with a balcony which was great for the summer month because you can lay out on the chairs and catch that nice warm Denver dry heat. Both stays I used Cash and SPG points and it was a great deal for the spacious modern room. The only complaint is that the bathrooms are a bit small but hey lets not get too picky for $60 a night and 4,000 points its a good deal. The staff is what I think makes this hotel excellent. They always smile and say hello no matter if it is the night maid in the hall way or the security guard roaming the hall ways at 3am. I would recommend this property to anyone visiting Denver that wants to stay close to the 16th street mall and larimer square. Great shopping and night life are within a stone's throw but really toward the end of the great outdoor mall. On a nice night during the summer there are several fun events near the hotel that take place. For instance I believe when I stayed there they had an outdoor movie night which was great for families which was right outside the hotel. Two excellent stays at this hotel!

“Underwhelming Hotel” Whenever I go to NYC I try to stay at a different hotel. And there is something I like about Morgan's Hotel Group hotels. My impressions usually run from OK to great. But I found the Hudson underwhelming. As with many Morgan's the lobby is a kick. It has the feel of a brick warehouse, with ivy growing all over the ceiling. It's dark, but that's typical. There is loud music playing all day and night. Having a greeter was a nice touch, though she didn't do much but say hello and welcome. Front desk staff was really pleasant and helpful. My room was about the size of a decent walk-in closet. I could barely move around the bed, the workspace just held my laptop. And the dark paneling made it feel even smaller. The bathroom was proportionately small. I could barely move around in it. The water never really got hot, the sink never really shut off. The only nice feature was a big window between the shower and the room so I could watch ESPN while getting clean. The dining space is intersting - same brick as the lobby with long community tables. The food was so-so, and definitely not worth the $30 I paid for the buffet. I was impressed with their gym, which had 3 treadmills and other cardio equipment each with their own TV, and plenty of weight equipment. And it was a big space so it never felt crowded. Location is fine, about 2 blocks from Columbus Circle. And you can't really beat the low room price. But there are much better hotels in NYC, and certainly better Morgan's hotels.

“Nice basic hotel, with updated bathroom!” After a full day in LA, we found ourselves too exhausted to drive home, with nowhere to stay. The Ramada Wilshire Center had no vacancies, but we drove a little bit and stumbled upon Dunes Inn. The location was great for us, relatively close to the Wiltern Theater (not walking distance though), and the mostly residential neighborhood--Hancock Park--was quiet and safe. (By safe, I mean, the only entrance is manned by a watchful clerk; there are no vagrants around; nearby are expensive condos, houses, and a few churches; and I would feel comfortable walking around the block, though the streets are quite dark.) The bed was comfortable, but not luxurious. The tv worked fine. Best of all, the bathroom must have been recently renovated, because it was impeccably clean with a nice granite countertop and new tilework. There was a refrigerator, a pool in the atrium, wifi, and a few rooms with a small kitchen, but we didn't use these and can't comment. Since we didn't pay full price, the room was a really great deal. Parking was free and greatly appreciated; since the neighborhood is not within walking distance of restaurants, night life, etc., you'd want to visit with a car. As a side note, some nearby places to visit by car: charming Larchmont Village, Koreatown, Griffith Park & Observatory, Downtown/Japantown, and LACMA. To summarize, Dunes Inn Wilshire is like a Travelodge but with a fancier, cleaner bathroom, and we'd definitely stay here again.

“One great night of rest and another night of billing nightmare” First of all, I do rate this Embassy Suites very highly. The location was perfect for a recent business project and it was a either an easy drive downtown or a team get-together at the Alamo Drafthouses (several nearby). I'm a HHonors member and like to visit as many Hilton venues as possible because of their consistent value and hospitality across their brands (and across multiple states). The swans did attract me to this place and they did not disappoint. I was felt sorry for the two, since the hotel was like a mini-zoo during my one-night stay. There was a conference event going on. The hotel is very kid friendly, so the combination of busy parents and hype kids were not the best environment for me or the swans. All aside, this Embassy Suites is a great place for families. The desk staff and restaurant are very welcoming (I didn't see any maintenance or other staffers strolling around like most hotels). I like the fruit-infused water by the elevators. The rooms are quite big, with separate rooms for living and sleeping. The King bed was very comfy, better than the HGI in my opinion. There's free parking and happy hour treats. My one gripe was with the billing. For some reason, additional charges popped up and they never all came off. Both in person, via email, and voice message. It did peeve me that there was one tiny amount left, but I reasoned it to bad luck I guess. I will return again to this hotel. I will give them another shot. I don't want to prevent families from considering this place because of my one slight mishap.

“The nicest LaQuinta I've ever stayed at (and I've stayed at quite a few)” The hotel is conveniently located just a few minutes from Denver airport. My room was huge and well laid out with a comfortable recliner and an entry foyer set at an angle, which minimized noise from the rest of the hotel. In fact, I had the best night's sleep that I have had on the road in years. The location is NOT convenient to downtown Denver so guests should not expect a quick drive there. The front desk staff was very friendly and, uniquely in my experience, called me in my room about 20 minutes after my arrival to make sure everything was as it should be and that I was comfy. While this hotel does not have a restuarant, there are several eating options in the area. The breakfast starts at 4am to accomodate guests who have early flights, and is standard LaQuinta. There is a pool and a fitness center as well as a nice interior courtyard. It is not cheap but, considering the area, is reasonably priced. The shuttle is shared with the Quality Inn across the street. If you need a place to stay between flights, one that is convenient to the airport for an early flight or a place to stay after a long evening arriving flight, you couldn't do better.
