“Great Location But Getting A Bit Worn” The Marriott Riverwalk, San Antonio, TX, is a good lodging choice when visiting the San Antonio River Walk area. The location of the property is directly on the riverwalk with most riverwalk restaurants, bars, and places of interest within close proximity. The gem of the Marriott Riverwalk is the fitness, pool, and recreation facilities. The fitness center is well appointed with equipment that will meet most people’s needs. The indoor-outdoor pool and indoor hot tub is a welcome pleasure after a hard workout. The facilities also offer a nice indoor and outdoor lounging space with plenty of chairs as well as a pool table and ping pong table. The rooms are comfortable and relatively spacious. Although the furniture, carpet, and interior walls are beginning to show wear and tear from heavy tourist and business use. That said, the rooms are clean and the bedding is comfortable. The staff of the Marriott Riverwalk is also quite accommodating and friendly. Each request or inquiry was answered with prompt service and immediate attention. Quite frankly, this in itself is a reason to patronize the Marriott Riverwalk San Antonio in the future.

“Great hotel. Will stay again next time...definitely!” I travel to San Francisco a lot and have had more than my share of less-than-desirable hotel stays there. But the Phoenix - I was very impressed. The courtyard/swimming pool area is beautiful and very relaxing. The room was spacious, clean and nicely designed. The shower was awesome. All the staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The bed was comfy. I like the location - central to everything - on the edge of the Tenderloin but not in the worst part of it. There are many decent restaurants, bars and clubs within walking distance. The guests were, as a whole, quite young and hip. Because of the courtyard you don't get the street noise that you do in many other hotels in San Francisco. They let me check in quite early, which was very nice after a long, cramped, early morning flight from Chicago. My only minor complaints were that the room had only a small heater which didn't seem to work 100%, so I was a bit chilly for a while, and my room didn't come equipped with a frig, which would have come in handy. Also the only chairs in the room were made of bamboo and weren't very comfortable. But, I can't say enough good things about how awesome the courtyard area is. I'd like to go back when it's warm enough to swim. I absolutely loved The Phoenix, and will definitely stay there when I visit next time.

“Rooms screaming for a facelift” I LOVE the overall setting of this timeless property and have been many times for extended family holiday vacations. However, when I was there this Fall for a conference, much as I still appreciated and enjoyed the beauty and elegance of the property setting, the rooms themselves (and how they are serviced) were a shocker. Newspapers and coffee service that failed to arrive, inadequate and inferior furnishings --especailly in bathrooms and window dressings, amenities that were not replensihed---were some of the common complaints at my conference. Too many excellent choices abound in this gorgeous part of the country for the Biltmore to take its eye off the ball. Planning a girls weekend now and won't even consider the Biltmore. A facelist is in order.

“Nice hotel with great service.” I booked this hotel on Priceline for a steal (over 50% off of regular room rates) for a few friends and myself. The hotel was in a great location near the 16th Street Mall, Union Station (Amtrak), and a short cab rides away from Coors Field (Colorado Rockies Baseball). In addition to the great location I was also very impressed with the entire staff at the hotel. They seemed very friendly and ready to go out of their way to help us. For starters my friend has a fear of small places and will not ride in elevators, so we very much needed a low floor room, so that she would not need to hike up too many flights of stairs. They were able to get us a room on the second floor of the main building. They were also very quick to bring us up extras towels and to help with our luggage. The rooms were a fairly nice size and had a nice desk with a comfy office chair. In addition the bed were great and I had a great nights sleep. Only things that I really did not care for was the overpriced items listed on their room service menu, so needless to say I did not order anything from it. Also our view of the 1st floor roof was nothing to write home about. I would differently stay at this hotel in future given that I am able to a great rate through Hotwire or Priceline, but would not pay the properties published room rates.

“Far Exceeded expectations !!!” What a pleasant suprise it was in the Staybridge Suites. I have never stayed at any Staybridge Suites befor and decided to give it a try as my partner and I were looking for a room with more space and a kitchen. From check in to Check out the ENTIRE staff was fantastic, they bent over backwards to see to our every need. I have traveld the world and never have i seen such great customer service. The maids did a GREAT job with cleaning, I have never seen any maid anywhere clean so well and so through, spotless rooms nicely appointed, roomy kitchen with stove refrig and ample cabnet space, bath room was larger than most hotels and the beds were super comfy !! TV was flat screen with a huge array of channel selection !! Sparkeling clean pool and jacuzzie to use ! Fantastic breakfeast buffet in the mornings with MANY selections and great dinner items as well, free parking, FREE laundrey rooms, this place has everything you need while on a trip of ANY LENGTH. I give this place a 100% YOU CAN NOT GO WRONG HERE !!! Cudos to the Holiday Inn brand !!! the only thing negitive i have to say is that the area around the hotel is being paved with new road surfaces and is sorta hard to get in to the property but this is no fault of the hotels and soon it will be all done so its an easy fix !!

“Clean, Nice and Convenient” My wife and I stayed two nights (1/1 to 1/3) for a short mini-vacation. We came to Chicago to see theater, eat at some good restaurants, and check out the Art Institute, and we chose this hotel after seeing an amazing $95/night (including parking!) listing on Travelzoo. We were happy with our choice and would stay there again. To be clear, if you are looking for luxury or a trendy spot, this is not the place for you. The Four Points is a simple, functional kind of place. The room was clean and crisp, with a mini refrigerator (no mini bar), a microwave and a coffee maker, which was really great to have. The TV was old-fashioned (not flat screen), but worked fine, and the hotel offered about 30 stations (including two HBOs). The bed was comfortable, and the furnishings (easy chair, desk, desk chair) were functional and in pretty good shape. The bathroom was clean. The heat came from a heat/AC unit by the window, but it worked great. Another great feature was free wired and wireless Internet. (Although, to be honest, I couldn't get the wireless to work on my old iPod Touch, but I didn't try that hard, nor did I seek technical support.) The hotel has an indoor pool/hot tub and an exercise room, but we didn't use either, so I can't comment on them. We also didn't eat at the hotel (breakfast was served from 7-10, and it was not included in our rate), nor did we order from room service. When we checked in, we requested non-feather pillows, and someone from housekeeping was in our room with the new pillows in less than five minutes. Probably the fastest service we've ever gotten from a hotel. The location is very good (if you are seeking a Miracle Mile stay). The hotel is a block from N. Michigan Avenue, and it was only a four-block walk to the subway (red line). Even in the harsh cold, we were able to walk to the Art Institute and the Oriental Theater, both south of the river. There are several restaurants in the immediate neighborhood, ranging from touristy spots like the Hard Rock Cafe and ESPN Zone to more low-key spots. If you are looking for a clean, nice base of operations for a Chicago stay, the Four Points fits the bill.

“Strange City” This hotel is so big they have banks of elevators for different towers and floors. Rooms are nicely appointed and the staff is very pleasant and helpful. The food is very Texas -- uneventful and generally unhealthy. The Kitchen Table has a breakfast buffet that is minimal in choices yet high in price. The location is central for Dallas, but there is no central shopping or entertainment are in the city. The main streets are dead compared to other large cities. Dallas is very low on my preferred city list. The food and nightlife compares low with other parts of the country. With that said, the hotel staff was very good especially a young man in concierge.

“a meeting with an out of town friend” Easy access to the freeway and several restaurants in the area, room was clean and so was the hotel, the parking was free, Friendly staff, good breakfast. even though this hotel supposedly smoke free i still smelled cigarette smoke in the hallways, and the Ice machine is missing on the 5th floor.

“Exceptional Property” I forgot what a SPECTACULAR property this is.......and what excellent service everyone provides. This is truly an excellent property!! Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com/ It began when I valet parked the car, the guy were all friendly and helpful. Next I moved to the registration desk and was helped by Katie. She was AWESOME, friendly, efficient and offered up some good local spots for dinner. Just what you want when you check in. Next, I headed up to the Regency Club to get some water and I met Alex. Great young kid who went out of his way to make me feel comfortable and help with directions and traffic to the airport. I had a note from Mark Stiebeling, the GM, and I called him to let him know how great the staff was and to thank him for the room I am in. He was friendly and I enjoyed our chat. I then headed to the 4th floor gym. It is excellent, clean/modern look, enough space with cardio, weight machines, and free weights. I always like a bench press, but that was the only thing missing. I also used Louise the concierge to book a reservation for dinner and she was very friendly and efficient. Excellent service!! Only thing that was below expectation was the maid service on Friday....I left early in the morning and when I returned at 3 pm the room was just as I left it....no maid service. I called down and they came in and emptied the trash and delivered fresh towels. The property was surprisingly busy on the weekend....the club level for breakfast had a busy crowd for breakfast and the gym was crowded every morning (someone said it was people on the cruises). Overall an exceptional experience and a wonderful place to stay. The staff is exceptional and the location is awesome -- right next to the shopping and a 15 minute walk to the fish market. In fact, I don't even think you need a car if you are staying downtown -- everything is a short walk or cab away. $169.15 a night, valet is $33 + 3.14 + 3.30 = $39.44 a night

“Tristounet” Hotel sans caractère, il est fort dommage d'avoir refait la déco sanss chercher à donner un peu de caractère à cet hôtel, c'est austère, dans un quartier assez triste. parking assez cher (30 USD/Nuit). Plutôt bruyant. Beaucoup de groupes (tours operators) Par contre, propre et personnel sympathique et compétent. On peut trouver bien mieux pour le même prix à San Francisco

“Good value Hotel” Nice hotel for the business traveler. The breakfast is somewhat pricey for the selection, but was quite good. Rooms are spacious and have the usual amenities. Staff was friendly and helpful. Rooms are around $100/night

“Excellent value and comfort in NYC” This was our first trip to NYC and we stayed four nights at the Tuscany. It was excellent value for money based on NYC prices. Everything was well done, staff were very friendly, restaurants within walking distance, and easy to get a cab to Times Square etc. We will certainly stay there again.

“Good value for money but definitely nothing special” Generally, I was rather satisfied with my stay. The property is located between Chinatown and Financial District, within a walking distance from the Ferry Building, Union Square and most other downtown attractions. The building and its immediate vicinity are rather shabby. The room was rather large and definitely very clean. "The Bay view" translates into a panorama of dirty rooftops of Chinatown and a massive construction site,but Coit tower and a glimpse of water on the far right offered a slight improvement. There was a room safe and a coffee maker in the room, but no fridge or minibar which I found rather peculiar for a four star property. One big issue was the capacity of elevators. Every single morning I had to wait for 10-15 minutes to use an elevator. I also found a bit insulting that they charge the full public parking fee to hotel guests (although they do grant guests in-and-out privileges). Soundproofing was inadequate by big city standards. Street noise was definitely an issue despite the 14th floor. Overall, a very good value at $98/night (Hotwire special rate, I did not know the name of the property before I paid), but definitely nothing special. Would stay again for $98, but not for their usual $168.

“What a fantastic hotel!” Just returned from a week's stay with my son. Was so delighted with everything in the hotel, especially our room. Most times the photos of rooms end up to be the very most expensive room in the hotel and your standard room looks nothing like it. This is the only hotel we have stayed in where the pictures on the web were exactly what the room looked like. The room, a standard, was incredibly beautiful! The hotel was like a small palace. What gracious service and surroundings! What a great location! Highly recommend this hotel.
“プールがよかったです。あと一階のバーガーもおいしいです。” 部屋はまあ、普通ってかんじです。ロービーや、プールの感じは中々いいです。あと、バーガーショップはおすすめです!セントラルパークが近いので、バーガー買って、公園にいきました。

“Great Location, spacious rooms, terrible service” I stayed here for work with 2 colleagues in June and chose this hotel based on it's great revues. It certainly had a lot to recommend it, a really fabulous location, close to great restaurants and the best area for going out in Philly. The rooms are very spacious and the bathrooms massive. The rooms had some quirks, but all in all pretty good. The biggest (and only) drawback is the staff. None of us recieved breakfaston time. One morning after waiting I went downstairs to get my breakfast basket and the server was talking on the phone with a friend! And the guy at the front of desk during the week was passive aggressive and in no way service oriented. All in all I would not stay here again unless I was guaranteed the staff had changed.

“Okay hotel in a good location” Made my first ever visit to Memphis for a football game and to see some friends. Chose this place in large part due to its location. Physical condition is okay. Not new but not falling apart either. Pros: Friendly staff, good location, plenty of restaurants nearby Cons: None, except for a slow cleaning crew (didn't arrive to room on Saturday until after 3:30)

“From a local's perspective...” I've stayed here several times (when my own house has been unavailable for various reasons) because it's a deal...and, it's not a chain (at least not a major one). First of all...the location is great. You can walk to many good coffeehouses, restaurants and shops in Hillcrest...and, Landmark Theaters are only a 1/2 block away. If you don't mind a long walk, you can make it to Balboa Park. The rooms are more like small very basic apartments with a compact kitchen, living room, bedroom, and bathroom. All the little extras - like a blowdryer and iron - are included in the rooms. Service here is great...they even give you free BBQ'd food on Fridays. Their free breakfast is better than the typical continental (waffle maker!) and is self-served up in a cute room by the pool. Pool area is small, but well kept.

“Brandnew feeling with easy access to downtown SanFran” Stayed here for two nights before we flied back to LA. The room is so clean like brandnew. The location is super since not only that it's right next to the San Fran's famous cable car, it also has extensive access to all the convenience that downtown San Fran has. We had a dinner right next door called Louis Dinner whose food was very yummy with a funky feel. My son played with the old coin record player right next to each dining table. They love Michael Jackson's songs!!! The front desk people are very efficient. We enjoyed this hotel very much.

“Great location for Hollywood, easy trip into Downtown” This is a classic old hotel that has clearl had constant and loving maintenance work done on it to keep it in top shape. Great staff, large confortable rooms and good on-site dining options make it a very pleasant stay overall. Not too far away from the relatively unused metro station means that getting to Downtown LA is a simple (and cheap) trip too.

“Above Average But a Few Problems” I was tough to decide between rating this a 3 or 4. I ultimately decided to go with a 4 due to the great service and staff, but some of the problems we ran into do cause concern. First, I reserved the room online and the online description for an executive suite clearly states that executive suites include jetted tubs. When we arrived at the room it was large and had a very nice balcony, but there was no jetted tub. In fact the bathroom was very small. It just had a shower/tub combo and no double sinks. To the hotel's credit, when I called down to complain they were very polite and quickly sent up a bellhop to move us to another room with an "upgraded bathroom." The new room was a bit smaller, but still comfortable. The second problem was hot water. We spent 3 days at the hotel and could never get the water temperture to work in the shower. It either came out scalding hot or cold. We were staying in the original historic part of the hotel so I guess that may be part of it. I have stayed here in the past in the newer wing and did not have a problem with hot water. Other than these two issues, the rest of the stay was very nice, and the staff did an incredible job. I was very pleased with how they handled the room change, although I do think someone should change the online description for an executive suite. We enjoyed breakfast in the room once and it came on time and was very good. The hotel's complimentary car service was also very nice, and was available every time we needed to use it. The concierge staff also did a great job recommending some local places to try out. If you're planning to walk around and visit downtown, then you cannot beat the hotel's location. One tip, the restaurant is every popular for breakfast on weekends. I think you're better off ordering in-room breakfast rather than waiting in line for a table at the restaurant.

“...una posizione ideale...” ...hotel ideale per la posizione strategica:si trova tra la 56° e broadway, a meno di un minuto dal Columbus circle, dove c'è uno degli ingressi di central park, e a meno di dieci minuti a piedi da Times square; verrebbe da dire"non ha prezzo", e invece è veramente vantaggioso e concorrenziale. Le stanze non sono campi da calcio, ma considerato che ci si trova nella grande mela, dove c'è qualcosa da vedere, si accetta il compromesso di stare un pò "vicini vicini"; in compenso la wi fi è compresa così come la colazione che ti consente di arrivare agevolmente a pranzo senza prendersi a morsi. Nel piano interrato buon ristorante.

“Classy and friendly luxury” In June we stayed twice at the Fairmont DC over a three-week period. Both times we booked their large 500 sq ft double double. These are huge rooms that are nicely furnished. Shortcoming: very small TVs. Otherwise, great. The second time we stayed, the doorman actually recognized me and greeted me like a long-lost friend. No kidding. At check-in, when I asked if the TVs were still so small, the front desk person apologized and offered to find me a bigger TV (the 9th and 10th floors have bigger TVs but alas they were out the large rooms there). I declined. Not a big deal. I was not in DC to watch TV. Service level is very high at this Fairmont (I'd say service level here is higher than at Fairmont Montreal, and perhaps similar to Quebec City). But not aloof. It's a friendly kind of highend service. Both times we had breakfast at Junipers, the hotel restaurant. The bfast buffet is great -- $25 and you get all kinds of fresh fruit, even Swiss yogurt, smoked salmon, and all the nice hot foods. The server remembered us too! Three weeks after our first visit. How's that for service? Location may be an issue if you looking to walk around to museums etc (I mean those at the Mall). But if the Dupont Circle area and around there is what you want, this is a wonderful hotel location. By the way, Blue Duck Tavern across the street at the Park Hyatt is a wonderful dining experience.

“Well Worth It!” Beautiful, smaller hotel in a great location, caddy corner to Marshall Field's and two blocks from Millenium park. Had a beautiful corner suite ($289 plus tax etc.) with huge windows looking up State Street. Room decor and amenities both excellent. Art deco design, but not South Beach psuedo art deco. Lobby areas beautifully designed - walk through it even if you don't stay there. Wine tasting from 5-6pm is a very nice feature and a nice way to end a day or begin an evening. Hotel will match any internet rate and you always benefit booking direct. If you need to stay in the Loop versus on the Magnificent Mile, this is a great choice. Only disappointment was the continental breakfast - should have just walked down to Starbucks for the same muffin and coffee.

“The biggest advantage is the location” Located close to downtown, walking distance to Liberty Bell and Independence Hall (a cab ride was only $7 plus a tip). Checkin was quick and easy (at 11 pm). Clean rooms with standard equipment, but small and dark, in need of renovation. The A/C was noisy. The fitness center and pool need work. Breakfast buffet was nothing special. The parking is expensive 28 USD/day. I would recommend this hotel for people looking for an hotel for a short stay. Bur for long stay I will go to another hotel.

“California the way it should be, a perfect hotel for San Diego Sightseeing.” I just returned for a 3 night weekend stay here with a 45 person family wedding party from Midwest and Eastcoast, and it was really nice, relaxing, hip, trendy and well managed. The rooms are really cool, very Cali in feel, and the bars, pool, and beach lounge great to hangout. Its 3 blocks to the train, and easy walk or taxi to everywhere, or walk, or rent a bike. You can stay in the convention hotels, or the typical sterile ones by the Gaslamp district, which they all looked nice, even the Courtyard and Embassy Suites, but those are cookie cutter hotels that you may as well be in Minneapolis or Atlanta. The W nails it again, with a nice value property thats unique in decor, feel, mood and ambiance, and everyone in the wedding party loved it, from age 65 to 18. Rent a car, and take in the sights of Del Mar, La Jolla, and even LA is 2.5 hours north for a day trip. I stay 4-5 star everywhere, travel 120 days a year, domestic and international, and this hotel at $150 is a delight.
“Going downhill every year.” We have bee staying at the Sixth Avenue Inn for over twenty years. It is clean and the staff is great but it needs updating. Time to spend some $$$ and re-model.

“Overpriced and charmless” We often stay at Affinia hotels, because they are suite hotels, which have studios with kitchens. We hadn't stayed at the Affinia Garden, which was probably a converted apartment building. The room was large, clean, with huge bathroom; the bed was good. The style was stark, minimalist, mono-tonal - an unfriendly look. There is no restaurant, but guests can order from a menu, and the breakfast is delivered from a local shop - better than I expected. The neighborhood is mostly residential, with a hospital across the street - nothing interesting to walk to. One computer, for which extra was charged, on the main floor.

“Pool is constantly green, fitness equipment and sauna, etc never work, rooms dirty.” Rooms are dirty, damaged, badly maintained and amenities rarely use-able. Stayed here numerous times before and this was the first time their green pool was swimmable. Not worth the extra cash and likely to suffer once the Ritz Carlton opens. All of this is rather a pity since it has such great architecture, is rather recent and has great potential. Just not clean.

“Nice hotel, beautiful views” Checked in at 11pm after a very long flight. As an SPG Platinum I was upgraded to a Grand Deluxe room in the north tower. The room had beautiful views of the Space Needle and Puget Sound. The room was spacious and clean. I took a quick shower and sank into a deep sleep in the comfortable bed. The room was quiet though there was noise from the housekeeper the next morning as she knocked on doors to clean. This property was clean and well located. The staff at the check in desk, concierge, and coffee bar were very nice. I was sad I checked out the next day at other recommendations to continue my Seattle stay at the Sheraton. Yes, it does have the club lounge, but the food there was actually quite poor and I found the staff at the Sheraton very unpleasant. The next time I'm in Seattle my Starwood business will go to the Westin.

“"Blah" and "wtf" about sum it up” Like everyone says - great location - had a great view of the park. But really - in such a large city - you can find others with a great location. The elevator situation was terrible. I couldn't catch an elevator in the morning. After 20 minutes - I had to ride up to ride back down. One of the three elevators servicing my floors didn't work the four nights I was there - and the other was hardly in use. Bathrooms were tiny. I had to pay for internet access - which annoys me to no end. The decor was nothing to write home about. The bed, however, was wonderful. I had mixed feelings about the staff - the guy at the front desk was ok but another two were RUDE. I would stay elsewhere. The W hotels are nicer at least.

“Average, clean, expensive and don't use the valet” This hotel is very clean.. It has a very expensive bar (domestic beer longnecks are $7) and expensive Valet. It is very close to many places downtown. My husband and I were there on business and walked to many places. As we were walking we noticed these crazy drivers coming in and out of this parking lot adjacent to the hotel. One of the cars nearly hit us and they were driving over the curb and what I call "thrashing" the cars. We were thinking -- who are these crazy drivers?? Until we saw that they were the VALET!!! So you pay $25 per day plus tips and they really treat your car like crap. Seriously??! Instead of paying for the valet - and after seeing how they treated everyone's cars, we parked at a city lot two blocks away and paid $8 per day. It was much cheaper and I felt our car was actually safer. :( This is coming from someone who usually does use the valet... that is how bad it was. Also take note that we saw lots of homeless people in the area, so if you're concerned about that, you may want to utilize the self-parking in the garage. As far as the room goes I don't have any complaints, I got a good night's sleep, was able to get the temperature where I wanted it. The bathroom was exceptionally clean. It really wasn't anything to write home about. I should mention that although I slept great, my husband did not. There was a lot of noise coming in from the hall and our room was right outside the elevator. I don't care for the scent of the toiletries, they smell too flowery to me, so you might want to bring your own.

“Great little hotel, will return” My friends and I had a mini-college reunion in Aug in NYC. We were alerted to good deals at 70 Park Avenue via the Jet Setter website and were so pleased that we selected this hotel. It is an excellent location at 38th St. Good for walking and subway. I had a king room with an interesting dark brown/purple decor on the 15th floor, it was great. Comfortable bed, min street noise. We liked the 5 pm wine reception and the all-day lemon and orange water. We had help with advice, maps and directions from their staff which was appreciated.

“Great experience and I recommend the hotel to all Houston visitors!” Blake Thorvaldsen was AMAZING! He made sure that we had everything we needed, and he was very friendly. The shuttle service was great. Osvaldo took us to restaurants and shopping centers in a timely fashion. He was also very courteous. Also, if you are a drinker, be sure to attend the manager's special; Ron makes the BEST drinks. Thank you Ebassy staff for making my stay so enjoyable.

“This is what I'm talking about!” After several less-than-satisfactory hotel stays in the last while, it was such a breath of fresh air to stay here. Where to begin? The staff is fantastic... every single member is friendly, accommodating and helpful; be it the valet, the check-in, the food counter, etc. Kudos to them. The hotel itself is clean, pleasant-looking and functional. The internet was very good throughout the property (note, I paid extra for better internet service). The food counter was very handy for a coffee, or a pizza at night, and the small marketplace (shelves of water, chocolate, chips, etc.) is also great for a quick snack. My king room was clean and, again, functional. Everything that is needed was there. The thermostat was easy to operate. And here's something I absolutely love: More often than not, after spending time removing all the pillows and bedding I don't want, housekeepers usually put everything back on to make everything "pretty", which annoys me, because every night I have to go through the same workout removing everything all over again. Not here! Housekeeping blessedly left aside everything I had removed from the bed, so when I was ready to go to bed, I could GO TO BED. Thanks so much for this small, yet very significant practice. And while the hike to the convention center can be a little onerous from this location, it is possible to do it entirely indoors. A few suggestions for improvement: One reviewer is correct in suggesting better shampoo bottles. Also, my king mattress has started sloping to one side, so I couldn't sleep in the middle of the bed. Another reviewer points out the pool is quite small. I did not use it, but could easily see that it is rather tiny. Might be best to replace it with one large hot tub. That would be great! I will stay here again.
“Best hotel I ever stayed at!!!!!” I will NEVER forget this hotel. I could basically live here!!! I will DEFINITLY be back!!!!

“Holiday Inn in Westin clothing” As a one-time resident of Baltimore's Roland Park-Homewood area -- it's my favorite part of the city -- we chose the Doubletree Inn at the Colonnade purely for its location, which is lovely. It's lovely by the way if you're not married to being in the Inner Harbor or in other truly urban Baltimore neighborhoods (like Fell's Point and Inner Harbor East). This hotel is prime for people with connections to Johns Hopkins University (mind you, I'm talking about the university, not the medical campus whose proximity is more toward Fell's Point, a whole other part of the city). The weekend we were there we saw numerous families (with boisterous kids who overpowered the tiny indoor pool) and wedding events. Still, very pleasant if unremarkable. We booked a suite and from what I could tell when wandering through halls when housekeepers were working, it was the same space as regular rooms (with slightly fustier furnishings, certainly no flat screen televisions while standard rooms had been upgraded) though suspect our bathroom -- with jacuzzi tub -- was an upgrade. Hate the kind of "suite" that basically puts the living room at the entrance (with no windows). Didn't really care for the room, frankly (though did appreciate the empty mini-fridge and liked the bathtub). The other thing I didn't love about the hotel was that despite all these great outdoor spaces -- two patios off the pool, an area off the entrance that clearly has been marked as a gathering spot because chairs and tables, as yet unwrapped in mid-June and so useless -- was that the urban/suburban nature wasn't properly addressed. The restaurant (Alize something or other) seemed rather sad sack (though we enjoyed the bar), definitely not possessing any kind of buzz. In fact the hotel itself had a sort of sad sack air about it. Hallways reminded me of the kind of airport hotel that tracks in one night stays. The smoke scent in our room, ugh. Will we stay there again? The Doubletree Inn at the Colonnade was certainly inoffensive but memorable? I love the neighborhood but next trip to Baltimore we'll give a try to the Radisson at Cross Keys and explore our urban/suburban options.

“Great Stay for Quick Houston Layovers” Stayed here for one night on a quick layover at the Houston airport and it was perfect! Very affordable, but the property is new, modern, clean and spacious. Would definitely stay here again on a layover: Positives -Clean, modern property -Spacious rooms -Free shuttle pick-up/drop-off (just call the hotel when you land) Negatives: -The shuttle pick-up at 11 p.m. was a long wait, and then the driver kept doing repeat rounds around the airport to pick-up more people. I know he wanted to get everyone, but total the wait and then time in the shuttle was almost an hour. Had we known that, we would have taken a cheap cab the the hotel - we needed sleep!

“Lovely Hotel” Had a nice stay here but the front desk wouldn't give me a king room, though she gave my client an upgrade. The room was lovely and staffs were friendly but there's no free internet unless you get a drink from the bar. The bartender was kind enough by giving me a password right away but I sat at the bar anyway because it won't work upstairs. Bed was very comfortable Location was excellent. It's only around the corner from Mel's, Denny's and Westfield. Overalll I had a lovely stay and would stay here again if the rate is right.

“Good value for the $” Pros: outstanding location, well-trained and personable front desk staff, polite maintenance staff, well thoughtout lobby with tons of workspaces for those of us traveling with laptops, $149 rate plus Marriott points and a flat screen HD TV in the room. Cons: small rooms and bathrooms, noisy heating system and street noise even on the 32nd level. The building is what it is; a 1970s hotel. Bathrooms have been updated with granite countertop, but the space is tight. For us the tight space was a worthwhile trade-off for the price.

“Just ok - Like Staying at an Office Building” Decent hotel, but they really need to renovate the hallways. Feels like an (old) office building. The elevators are confusing and a bit scary - they seem quite old. I was recently there for my grad school reunion and friends told me that my hotel room was the best out of the others in the surrounding area. So that made me feel a bit better since I had to pay more. The rooms are nice. Nice bathrooms. Just needs some work to the hallways and perhaps a bit to the lobby. But it's a great location downtown, staff is very nice, I slept well, and appreciated the complimentary lemonade and coffee in the morning. Nice touch. Our party that night was at Lowe's and the food was quite good. I'd stay there again, but may explore other options first until they give the place a little face lift.

“Great Stay @ Homewood Suites” Stayed one night, Aug. 16, at property with wife, and 3 year old. Very comfortable and large suite. Nice view of downtown Dallas skyline. Looks like hotel is undergoing refurbishment, repairing sidewalk, replacing a/c units, etc. Greeted warmly at registration. Nice manager's reception, and good breakfast buffet (included w/ stay). Not much to do around this part of town, a little dearth on restaurants, though a Whataburger is next door. Sonny Bryan's BBQ is right up Inwood Rd. about 1 mi. from hotel - excellent brisket / hoagie sandwiches in unassuming location. Typical Homewood suite features you would expect - large king bed, seperate living room, large bathroom/vanity area, refrigerator, two-burner stove, dishwasher, all plates, utensils, etc., reclining chair in living area, leather sofa. For the price - excellent value ($ 90 NetDirect rate). Downtown Dallas about 2 miles S.E., and right off IH-35E. Southwester Medical Center across freeway. Would stay here again in the future. A very quiet and uneventful stay for one night.

“So impressed with the service!” Me and my two young children were recently in Boston for 4 days and travel there often. This was our first time at this hotel and I was very impressed with the level of service they offer to make your stay comfortable. We had a redeye flight and arrived at the hotel at 8:30 am (they offer an airport shuttle, which is not offered at many of the hotels in the city, so very nice) and was surprised that they had a room clean and ready for our arrival. We were exhausted, so I couldn't have been happier about this. The hot breakfast buffet is nice with alot of options and the waffles are very good. My children loved having the access to make hot chocolate all day, every day and usually there are cookies in the lobby as well. We had a little maintenance issue one night and they sent up a tray with bags of popcorn, cookies, candies and drinks. My kids were thrilled. The location is very close to a hospital, so a bit noisy outside, but it didn't bother us. The only drawback is that the closest "T" (subway) stop is quite a walk. Maybe not for adults, but with kids, long. There is a bus line that runs right down Massachusets Avenue though that can get you to the hotel fast & for only a few bucks. I would not walk down there at night either. But, the best thing is that their shuttle service is wonderful! Not only does it take you to the neighboring medical area hospitals, which we visit, but they are very gracious to drop you off at local attractions, like Quincy Market or a "T" stop. We really appreciated this very much and are grateful to the staff for making our stay so enjoyable.

“Great Mid-town Hotel with Lots of Room” This is a great hotel in Mid-town. There is lots of space in the rooms as they have a seperate living area and bedroom. The front desk staff are friendly and helpful. The bed is very comfortable and the room is everything you would expect in an luxury hotel. The location is great, within easy walking distance of Broadway and Times Square. I would return to this hotel on any trip to NYC.

“Fantastic Stay” From the moment we checked in, we felt warm and welcome at this small boutique gem in NYC. Justin and Shane were outstanding behind the desk - they really made us feel welcome. Carlos and the other bellmen staff were also very helpful and greeted us with smiles and farewells as we went in and out during our stay. The lobby is chic and nicely decorated and they often have nibbles out, such as iced tea, flavored water, cookies and fruit. The rooms are very large by NYC standards. It appears that the hotel was converted from a traditional NYC apartment building, so the rooms still had a lot of character that I like in the old style NYC architecture. There was a nice hallway leading to the bedroom area, a nice sized bathroom and a small lit bar area. The sleeping area was very large with 2 nice sized and comfy beds plus a sitting area. The closet was huge - big enough that we could use it as a changing room. The decor was very nice - good bedding and nice draperies. The one comment about seeing some wear and tear is true, but nothing very glaring (the carpeting seems fine; they could touch up a little bit of paint in the bathrooms, but it was not bad at all). The fitness center was a nice plus - it was large by NYC standards, had great equipment, was clean and well maintained and had great machines. The location is great - a couple of blocks from Grand Central, which gives you access to a variety of train lines. Plus you are right off the Lexington Avenue bus lines, as well. As it is in central Manhattan, you are never too far from anything. We travel a lot here in NYC and the rest of the states/Europe and I think this is one of the best values we have found - especially in NYC. The service is top notch (welcoming and fun) and the accommodations are large and nicely maintained. We look forward to staying at the St. Giles Tuscany again.
“Great Hotel, Great Value, Great Location” Hotel is located 1 block from the Metro stop-, or a 15 minute walk to the White House. very good lcoation. Clean and quiet. Would stay here again.

“Nice Views, Nice People, Absurd Fees, Poor Value” If you're looking for a value, don't come here. I booked a room at about $165.00 a night, thinking that was a decent rate for the area. However, once I got here, I was getting soaked left and right in absurd fees. Some good examples are $22/day for parking, and for breakfast, your only option is one downstairs restaurant with a lovely $17 egg dish!! On top of all that, I had to pay $18/day for high speed internet! In this economy and competitive market, I find it ridiculous to go to a hotel and have to pay this for web access. The views are very nice, but the location is basically right on top of the airport, so be prepared to listen to take offs and landings on a regular basis. And if you don't have a car, there is really no way to walk to an affordable local restaurant or store. On the plus side, all of the staff here were very very nice and friendly. My views of the harbor were great, and there are some good walking/running paths around the hotel and harbor. The room seemed to be renovated and updated, and was clean and comfortable. If this location can get with the year 2009+ and offer a nice breakfast buffet, free internet, and free parking, I would probably stay here again. Right now, no way.

“Good 3* airport hotel with free shuttle every 30min/24h” The hotel is a typical Holiday Inn Express, neighborhood is not the poshest, but reasonably safe for LA standards. If you reserve a Holiday Inn near LAX make a note of the address: there are at least three different locations, so don't just board the first Holiday Inn shuttle you see, make sure with the driver it is the correct one. While the shuttle leaves every 30 minutes from the hotel, it may still be a good idea to alert them after you arrive, which terminal, especially at very late hours. Room was spacious, relatively quiet, even though planes were definitely noticed. Windows in rooms do not open. Stayed two nights and would probably come back here, even though it seemed somewhat pricey. Plus: Air conditioning was not blasting upon entering the room for the first time. Minus: while at breakfast house keeping replaced towel and soap (should have put sign on the door. Note to management: get a little more environmentally conscious, hanging towels do not need to be replaced, soap also should stay if the guest is there for another night.) Breakfast itself was OK with sausages, scrambled eggs, peeled hardboiled eggs, cereal, muffins, bagels, pancakes. No bananas or any other fruit. There is a Trader Joe's grocery store less than a mile away, and both Hertz (0.5miles) and Dollar rental car returns are within walking distance (less than 0.8miles)

“possible spiritual experience had here” The Standard hotel NYC would have been cutting edge a few years ago and even today was a good example of how good a hotel room can be despite being tiny. I loved how much light flooded into my room, it made me feel expansive - a feeling of lightness that I have never felt in a hotel room before. The room was small but very well laid out. Loved all the low key wood finishes - very understated and appreciated it. The bed was the most comfortable hotel bed I have slept in. It invited you to fall asleep as soon as you lay upon it. The bathroom fixtures were soft rounded rectangular shapes - once again understated yet modern. I loved that the sink was shallow and flat. At the same time the bath tub was unexpectedly deep. The toiletries were organic and very subtly scented. Bravo. Finally, I have to say I have stayed at other Thompson Hotels but this one had great, efficient service. The right level of friendliness. I stayed at the Thomspon LES earlier and the staff their were sassy, dumb and basically incompetent. The view from the cocktail lounge on the top floor was simply amazing. Check it out if you get the chance. Room Tip: facing brooklyn, as high as you can get

“Very good customer service” Stayed at this location for one night. There is an Applebee's restaurant across the street and a Wal Mart within five or six blocks. We stayed during the World Series and they provided extra snacks, etc. for guests who wanted to watch the game in the lobby. The breakfast food was all "instant" and was not fit to eat. I had a box of Cherrios.

“Muy bueno, pero un poco caro” El hotel es un 5 estrellas en todos los sentidos. Las habitaciones son muy grandes y espaciosas, limpias, cómodas, etc... Quizas la única pega sea el precio, un poco elevado.

“Very good location” we stayed here 3 nights on a high floor at the back,whilst the view was not much it was quiet. Staff were helpfull especially the concierge who found us a van ride to the airport and took care of our luggage. The hotel is in the theatre district and near enough to all main locations so you can walk. having read the reviews of this hotel before iwe went we wonder if we were at the same hotel.

“Perfect location with a great view of the city.” Rooms are a decent size, considering this is NYC, with floor to ceiling windows. Very clean hotel with a nice bathroom. The bed is very comfortable and the glass shower is very modern. I recommend this hotel if you are looking for convenience. It is very close to the subway and walking distance to Tribeca and Soho. FYI-There is only complimentary wifi in the lobby. If you are a SPG, good for you as this hotel has high floors with great views and complimentary breakfast. Of course the breakfast is for gold members and above, but the view is amazing. You can sit inside and watch TV or sit outside on the rooftop and enjoy the city views.

“enjoyed our stay” I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in mid Oct. I got $209 per night weekend rate which I think it was a pretty good deal by its location. The hotel seems got remodeled recently. I like the new room décor, much better than the one I saw two years ago. I gave it 8 out of 10 score.

“Pros & Cons” As noted in other members' reviews, this hotel has negatives and attributes. The location is not as close to the popular Sundance Square area as are other popular chains. It is on the south end of the downtown area where there are no nearby restaurants. However, it is close to the Amtrak station and the TRE commuter rail service to Dallas. With that of course come the views of the rail yard/freeways. Comment was made about the expensive parking - skip the valet and self-park across the street for $15.00/day Our room was clean and modern but not exceptional. The ice machines are not located on every floor and during our stay, only one machine was working in the wing we were staying. The staff members were very helpful and courteous but at times the front desk was overwhelmed with people checking in and only one staff member to assist.

“It's all about the view!!!” My wife and I recently stayed at the Swissotel Chicago with our infant son. This is my favorite hotel in Chicago for two reasons: 1. View and 2. Location. This hotel is only a 5 minute walk from Michigan Avenue, and the Chicago River boat tours. You can also walk to Navy Pier in about 10 minutes from this hotel. By far the Swissotel Chicago offers a superior location. But my favorite thing about this hotel is the view. If you stay here, opt for a corner room since it has a very unique triangular shape and will afford you a truly panoramic view. Our oversized room had a suberb view of the Chicago River, Lake Michigan, and Grant Park. We could see the fireworks at Navy Pier. You can't beat this kinda of a view. Despite the fact that this hotel is ideally designed for the business traveller, they had plenty of amenities to accomodate our infant son. We were able to get a crib, a play pen, and a small room refrigerator for storing baby food at NO additional cost. Many other hotels charge up to $50 for baby amenities like a crib or a room refrigerator. These rooms are very speceous and the beds are very comfortable. The hotel has the Palm restaurant which is ok but a bt overrated. This restaurant is within the hotel but seems to operate independantly so you cannot order room service from the Palm but you can get take out and then have plates/utensils delivered from room srevice. The food at the Swissotel is better than the average hotel but nothing special. This is why I opt for 4 stars and not 5. One other downside is that there is no self-parking at this hotel and valet parking costs a whopping $37 dollars which seems to be the going rate at all downtown Chicago hotels. If you want to self-park, you will have to find a nearby garage and walk to the hotel from there. There is a garage at the Hyatt Regency which is one block away. By the way, all housekeeping and room service requests are handled promptly. All in all, the Swissotel is an excellent hotel in Chicago and we will continue to stay there during our future visits to Chicago. This is an excellent hotel for families and is very baby-friendly. When you go, be sure to opt for a corner room or a room with a view of Lake Michigan. Otherwise, you might get a room that directly overlooks another office building. One additional tip I would offer is to call the hotel's in-house reservations department to make the booking. They have access to specials and packages that might not be on the Swissotel website. We got a $209 rate for a corner king room which included breakfast (room service or at the Geneva Restaurant), discounted parking at $16/day and 2 tickets to the Field Museum. As I said before, it's all about the view. The best views in Chicago!!! P.S. Please note that during our stay, we noticed some construction taking place in the lot next to the Swissotel. It seems like there is another building going up. I am unsure that impact this will have on the view from the Swissotel. I would call the hotel directly to inquire.

“club room benefits” Stayed in queen club room. Room and bathroom was very clean. Bed was comfotable. Access to the lounge for breakfast, afternoon tea, etc. is a great benefit. The check-in agent was very helpful and pleasant. I couldn't help overhearing a couple checking out complaining about the original room and second room they were moved too. I must admit I started to feel some concern, in case my experience matched theirs. My experience was totally different. The only concern was the room opposite to mine going in and out of their room banging the door each time. Staff were very pleasant. The guest relation manager was very helpful and extended my request for late check out with no extra charge.

“Perfekte Lage, toller Service, guter Preis. Gerne wieder!!!” Wir waren 2 Nächte im Hotel Fusion, nachdem ich lange nach dem perfekten Hotel gesucht habe. Ich war mehr als überrascht von diesem Hotel! In einigen Bewertungen hieß es, die Zimmer wären so klein und man bekäme Platzangst. Das kann ich nicht bestätigen. Das Zimmer war geräumig mit Schreibtisch, Schrank, großem Bett und eigenem Bad & WC. Unser Zimmer war im 4. Stock, Blick auf den Innenhof. War kein schöner Blick, aber es war dadurch natürlich ruhig, da man keine Straßenseite hatte. Und wer braucht schon einen Ausblick in SFC?! Die Lage ist sensationell!! Ums Eck der Powell St und dem Union Square, gleich bei der Endhaltestelle von dem Cable Car. Super für Ausflugsziele. Man braucht kein Auto! Der Service war übrigens von der Buchung an schon toll. Sehr nett. Dort angekommen haben wir das Auto vor dem Hotel geparkt und eingecheckt. Den Schlüssel hat das Hotel behalten, es war Valet Parking, wenn man es wieder brauchte, so sollte man 20 min vorher anrufen. Das hat auch geklappt, als wir es ausprobiert haben. Das Hotel hat sogar einen Concierge, der Nachts auch den Zimmerschlüssel sehen will. Ich habe mich hier sehr sicher gefühlt. Das Frühstück war völlig ok für US Verhältnisse. Es gab Säfte, Kaffee, Bagels, Toast, Marmelade, Muffins.. Frühstücksraum soll es ab 2010 geben. Wir haben auf dem Zimmer gegessen, fand ich nicht weiter schlimm. Das Einzige Manko, welches ich aber nicht ganz sicher dem Hotel zuschreiben kann, war das Parken. 2 Tage nach Abreise haben wir einen großen Kratzer am Auto bemerkt. Es könnte durch das Valet Parking bei Tuca Park gewesen sein. Ich weiß es nicht, es gab zum Glück auch keine Probleme mit unserem Vermieter Alamo. Welch Glück! Ich würde künftig das Auto selber in einem öffentlichen Parkhaus parken, das kostet weniger als die 25$.

“Excellent for work” Our annual meeting was at this location since we had recently outgrown our previous location. The staff are very accomodating, the meeting space is comfortable and easy to work in. I stayed in the central tower and although the view from the room wasn't much, the beds were comfortable. I love the fact that it is straight up the hill from the metro stop which makes it extremely accessible from the airport if you don't rent a car.

“What you'd expect from a Best Western” Clean room, comfortable beds, free parking, free wifi in rooms and lobby, and a free hot breakfast but not great. You get scrambled eggs, juices and other continental breakfast stuff. Location is good, across the street is liquor store, and other fast food places, only about 15 mins drive from downtown, and Aurora. I'd stay here again.

“Fun family holiday” This hotel worked well for Grandparents, Aunts, Uncles, Nieces, Nephews, Cousins and family friends ranging in age from 2-77 (a group of about 40 people) who wanted to save seats for each other by the entertaining Lazy River during one of the busiest weekend of the year. Among our large group -- no complaints except about how big this place is and how far it was to get from one place to another and to the self-parking. Rooms clean and convenient, bathrooms big and functional, enough closet space for a weekend of varied activities. Starbucks in the lobby, great lounge with inside and outside seating. Poolside dining. A good place for all ages if you are looking for a common denominator that will work for a couple or a bunch of kids.

“Strange Smell???” The one thing that really killed this hotel for me was a strange smell in my room and my colleagues rooms also. I was told it was disinfectant I couldn't get used to it at all. Check in Easy and quick. The gentlemen at the front desk was very nice and we had a good laugh. We arrived in the early evening so that had cookies, popcorn and pretzels which was nice. Rooms Nice size single king room. The AC was a big loud but I have heard much worse. I ended up turning up the temp. so it didn't go one every 10 minutes. THE SMELL it really killed me. It stunk so bad and I could never get used to it. It was so bad I wrote my 1st complaint to Hampton ever. I know I'm ranting but it was bad. I did have a few problems with the TV on some channels. It fuzzed out. ((Update. The manager called me from the hotel and apologized. I was satisfied with how they handled the situation)) Bed Nice bed but the heavy comforter was a bit much in the summer. Bathrooms I really liked the setup of the bathroom. It was very open and easy to move around. Nice shower pressure and hot water right away. Internet Free and good speed Parking Free but that had some outside meeting at the hotel 1 night so there was no parking when we got back from dinner because of a seminar at the hotel. Free shuttle to the airport. Free breakfast is always nice at the Hamptons. Overall it was a good hotel except for the cleaning product smell. I really wish I didn't have to sleep in it all night. If it wasn't for the smell it would get a higher rating.

“Great place! Love the location and the pools!” We had visited Hill Country over spring break, so we headed to Wild Oak Ranch on a recent trip through San Antonio. The property is gorgeous with nice and spacious rooms. There is a great little market, restaurant, fire pits, game area and the pools? AMAZING! The kids loved the lazy river and we had a hard time getting them to leave! The beds are very comfy and the bathrooms are gorgeous and spacious. The service and cleanliness are the exceptional quality you would expect from a Hyatt property. I would recommend this for couples or families looking for a fabulous experience!
“First Rate Service” I have stayed at the Waldorf a couple of times now, very consistent with their service and a good location for your New York experience.

“Better than other Mission Valley hotels” I stayed at the DoubleTree by Hilton San Diego in Mission Valley for only one night, but I would have been happy to extend my stay. The hotels in Mission Valley are, in general, a bit dated. However, the Doubletree stands out as a clean, modern hotel amongst the dinosaurs. Mission Valley is a very central location for getting around San Diego. However, Mission Valley itself is not the nicest area. A short hop on the freeway and you can be in downtown or at the beach, both nicer areas than Mission Valley. My room was very clean and comfortable, with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Mission Valley. "Modern" decor often means cold, but not in this case. Look at the included room picture and you'll understand. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was immaculate. The hotel lounge has a nice Happy Hour daily, and the lounge overlooks the outdoor pool area. The weather was not warm enough for me to take a dip, but the pool still looked clean and inviting. The San Diego light rail stops right across the street from the hotel, which is convenient for getting around if you don't want to drive and fight for a parking space. Speaking of parking... The only reason I am giving four stars instead of five is the $16/day parking fee. I found this charge to be excessive for the Mission Valley location. This is not in the heart of a crowded downtown San Diego, where high parking fees are the norm. Still, I would recommend this hotel for its location, its comfort and the professionalism of its staff.

“good location - some issues” liked this hotel as it is close to my office, and not so close to the mag mile tourist traffic area. the staff in the hotel is very friendly - when i checked in they were going thru an upgrade on their system, and doing things the manual way took a bit longer than normal, but not too bad. upon entering the hotel there was a man that "appeared vagrant" sleeping on the couch in the lobby - he didnt bother me per se, but he was bothersome looking... the room itself was nice - this is an older hotel and the tv, carpet, etc were actually quite fresh looking so that was a treat. the only other room issue was the bathroom - the tub had some black crust that washed away upon turning the water on so not sure where that came from... the shower did not work very well and there was a lot of water that came from the spout and shower, so you had to take a shower/ankle bath at the same time, not enjoyable. but again, overall with these minor hiccups a moderately priced hotel and pretty decent deal for me.
“狭い部屋は狭い” 2人で泊まろうとチェックインをしたら、部屋がビジネスホテルのダブル並みの狭さで驚きました。すぐに、追加料金を承知で広い部屋に移動しました。聞くところによると、一人で泊まるのにちょうどいい狭い部屋とデラックスという名の普通のツインサイズの部屋があるそうです。広さ以外は、清潔さ、スタッフの対応など、とても繊細でしっかりとした日本資本らしいホテルで満足しました。

“Great hotel, great staff” Beautiful, unique, hip, CLEAN hotel! Fantastic helpful staff. To get here from the airport, took the light rail to the end of the line (Westlake Center) for $2.50....then the monorail and walked a few blocks after that. The walk with heavy bags would not have been fun....need a cab for that....but all during our stay there, we used the monorail to get to the city center area. Rooms were great, clean, high quality bedding. Bathroom was nice and large (stand-in shower only, though). Had a fridge and a microwave. Free parking in the garage downstairs!! Keurig coffee maker in the room....and coffee and cupcakes available in the lobby. Free water in the room, too. What really makes this place is the staff. The morning we left, we needed to get to the Amtrak station...I asked if a cab would be easiest....the young man at the desk suggested a towncar service for a flat $15 fee and arranged for it for us....it was painless. Really appreciated that. Space needle, Experience Music Museum very close (walking distance) and the monorail could take you to the city center from where you could walk anywhere. Felt safe walking at night. Would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Great hotel, Great Rooms, Great Hotel Gym” Stayed here on business in January 2012 for 6 nights for a conference. I travel a lot for business and this hotel definitely exceeded my expectations. Rooms are large for NYC-- clean, spacious, and comfortable. Elevators are quick and fast, even though there is a lot of traffic and many floors. In-room internet worked great and the fitness center (although it cost $14.95 to use) was large, well-equipped, and open 24 hours. Definitely reccomend for business.

“Beautiful Remodel” Beautiful, newly remodeled rooms. Comfortable beds with clean, fresh linens. Lobby is being renovated so you check in to a conference room. Called housekeeping for towels and they were there in minutes!! The hotel had several events happening but was extremely quiet.The internet was $15.00 but that seems to be the standard, I would definately stay here any time.

“Beautiful, spacious, comfy!” Two old hotels renovated make one great hotel! The rooms are spacious, and beautifully furnished. In the heart of the bar area, it's a bit wild in the streets on weekend, but the rooms are quiet and the front door is secured. Valet parking only is pricey at $24.00 a day, but overall they attendants were very responsive and took good care of the car. 5 minute walk to the Colts Stadium. Only one elevator can be slow, so we often took the nicely carpeted stairs to get down to the first floor from our room on the top - 5th floor. Nice furnished living room/kitchen/dining room area with a large sofa bed/chaise lounge. Two comfy Queen beds and another TV. We like it cold and the AC worked well. Breakfast was decent and they even include a decent diner Monday-Thursday. No evidence of smokers here! Room 503 has a decent view out the front of the building toward the west.

“Very friendly staff” Just back from NYC, where it was very cold, but coming back to this lovely cosy hotel was wonderful. The hotel was luxurious, and the beds were so comfy (had to climb on them, they were so high). Staff were very friendly, mini bar and food expensive in the hotel, as with any top hotel, but you have the option. Or you can go over to Raffles cafe/restaurant on the corner of Lexington Avenue (2minutes) for a wonderful breakfast (pancakes were terrific). Relaxing bar, only 6$ for a lovely glass of wine. If you have to phone home buy a phonecard from any street vendor or deli for 5$,10$20$, they last ages. You can phone from phones in the hotel. Also try Marriott Marquis Hotel on Times Square, The View restaurant,(Revolving while you eat) All you can eat buffet for 20.95$ or cheese and sweets 11.95$. Great views. Jan 10th - Jan 13th.

“Gutes Flughafenhotel” Das Westin ist zentral gelegen. Mit dem Wagen erreicht man innerhalb nützlicher Frist die meisten Sehenswürdigkeiten der Stadt und ist erst noch nahe dem Flughafen (gratis Shuttledienst). Sicher das Hotel bietet keinen Strand und keine schöne Umgebung, aber es ist vom Preis her okay und sauber. Auf Anfrage gibt es Late Checkout (für Starwood Goldmember gratis), was von Vorteil sein kann, da die Flieger nach Europa gegen abend abheben. Den letzten Tag in der Stadt geniessen, ins Hotel duschen und ab auf den Flieger. Frühstück auf dem Zimmer können wir empfehlen...

“Probably the best for Universal Studios” The closest hotel to Universal Studios, Hollywood, lives up to the hype. The Hilton is only steps away from the main gate, and we got our tickets to U.S.H. thru a package we bought on the Hilton website, Check-in was quick, and we had a room ready although we arrived at 10:30AM. Went directly to the park. When we came back, we were greeted by a basketful of goodies, including two bottles of water, fruit, cookies and the likes. Did not use the restaurant on-site as we walked to CityWalk for dinner. The hotel was experimenting elevator issues on our way back but they were fixed by the morning. Overnight, the air conditionning made the exact same sound as if someone on the upper floor was flushing a toilet, everytime the motor kicked it. Were awoken by that a few times. The wired Internet connection never worked. Had to go to the lobby for the wireless to be within range. Might be because we had a corner room. Parking is affordable (17.00$ self with in and out privileges)

“Reasonable for 1 night” We had a one night stopover here between flights and the price wasn't bad for LAX. The shuttle runs every half hour from the hotel to the airport but you need to ring the hotel to be picked up at the airport. The breakfast buffet had hot and cold choices and the room as fine.

“Pleasantly welcoming” We wondered about the Royalton because it's now been around for awhile. Once the bar and restaurant scene was uber-hip, not sure about that anymore. However, hip can mean unfriendly to ordinary folk and this was somewhat of a concern. However, fear not, the front desk welcome was warm, speedy and smiley. We felt 'invited-in' and then wondered about the room. We were pleasantly surprised because the room was a comfortable size and very attractively furnished with usable desk space, a sitting area and a sumptuous bed with lots of sleeping pillows and a super cozy duvet. The bathroom, too, was spacious, clean and included a real hairdryer. We will happily go back. Maybe next time we'll have a chance to try the bar/lobby scene that has been completely refurbished, looks more comfortable than the original lobby and still appears very popular.

“Good and Bad. Mostly Expensive.” There is good and bad with the Hyatt Regency Convention Center. First the good. It was centrally located to the 16th and the Convention Center. Great food and bars within stumbling, er, walking distance. The BEST part of the Hyatt was Chris at the lobby bar. He was awesome. And the rest of the staff were friendly and personable. Now, the bad (and there is so much!) As others have said, the parking is HORRIBLY expensive. To give you an idea, there are lots next door that charge 1/2 of what the Hyatt charges. HALF! $12 compared to $28 for valet. I paid $75 a night for a room but the parking was increased our room rate to over $100 a night. Internet access cost $10 a day and there was no free WiFi. Both wired and wireless were $10 for 24 hours. The wired was fast but still, $10 a day?!? I was surprised the pool didn't cost money. it did cost though. I was in the hot-tub and sliced my toe on a grate at the bottom of the hot-tub. Took a patch of skin right off. :( Completely preventable had they installed the proper grating. The rooms were average size. Yes, the bed was comfortable but the rooms were small. The shower put out so much water, I started to believe Denver didn't have a water problem. Would I stay here again? Nope, not at all. The additional costs were my breaking point. Just not worth it. Felt like I was getting "nickle and dimed" for a Hyatt.

“My favorite hotel in the world” I travel quite a lot for business and pleasure, and this is the best hotel I've ever stayed at. No matter where my meeting is in Seattle, I stay here because I love it so much. It's not right downtown, but close enough that a short stroll into town is not a problem. The rooms are amazing, usually with great views, super comfortable beds, aeron desk chairs and very nice bathrooms. Considering the cost of the hotel, you'll think you may be staying at the Ritz. The hotel bar is also great with a friendly staff. Unlike other premium hotels, the Pan Pacific does not nickle and dime you, and Internet is free. Right above a Whole Foods is convenient for grabbing a quick meal in your room.

“Fantastic” My husband and I stayed at the Eastgate Suites from 3/16-3/22/04. We were very pleasantly surprised. The rooms themselves are modest but large and the windows actually open! The hotel is in a great location and we found it to be very quiet, both inside and out. We loved having the kitchenette where we could make bkfst and coffee or have light snack and keep a bottle of wine. The bathroom is small-ish but has great storage and the shower was great with plenty of pressure. I would definitely stay there again. We found the staff to be friendly and attentive as well. As for the maid service, it was excellent. We are late risers and it only took her one day to figure that out. Thanks again Eastgate Suites!

“Hyatt Great Experience Once Again.” We completed our stay yesterday and were very happy once again. We stayed at this hotel two times prior to this trip. The staff from the manager Kristy Cotton to the housekeeping staff and everyone in between were courteous and helpful. The hotel is located in a good spot with the t stops, shopping, and the Market close to the hotel. The hotel has beautiful old oil paintings in antique frames, waterford lighting fixtures that lend an elegeant flair to the hotel. Room service was prompt, very courteous and the food was good and hot. The restaurant Avenue One was great quality food at a fair price with excellent, excellent attentive service(Jason I had to mention you.) The pool area is a big hit with our kids, unfortunately this time we hit a snafu with the pool being closed for part of our stay due to the inconsideration of a parent of a child using it. The beds are heavenly, the rooms are very clean and spacious. Parking is expensive, but isn't it expensive EVERYWHERE in Boston? The hotel concierge is excellent and patient. Everyone of their staff took the time to explain different attractions and directions to me. The front desk staff bent over backwards for us(Natalie and Lisa we must mention you too,). I would stay at this hotel in the future once again without hesitation.

“Fantastic Hotel” I was in Indianapolis, IN for a weekend getaway and stayed here at the Conrad. The hotel is wonderful! The room is very comfortable and the bedding is quite nice. My only problem was the concierge. She did not follow up on a couple of things we had asked her to do. She was given plenty of time to work on our requests and it was not done. She also gave us incorrect information on an event we attended.... her "research", proved incorrect. Beyond that, the hotel was great. The hotel has a great gym... free to guests. The spa is still not open, but from what we saw it looks like it will be quite nice. Again, great hotel!

“buono ma camere troppo piccole” Abbiamo pernottato per 3 notti nel mese di agosto 2008. L'hotel internamente è bello, ristrutturato e ben tenuto e le camere sono silenziose e pulite. Un problema non indifferente soprattutto se si viaggia con bagagli al seguito è che le camere sono molto molto piccole. Non c'è assolutamente posto per mettere le valige. Noi avevamo 2 trolley e dei sacchetti con dei regali che abbiamo dovuto lasciare in auto (il parcheggio dell'hotel costa 28 $ a notte). E' comunque vicinissimo al Galsamp Quarter, all'Horton Plaza e ben servito dai mezzi.

“Ottimo in perfetto stile sofitel....” Situato nel centro di Philadelphia ottimo per visitare la citta' senza utilizzare il taxi. Hotel pulitissimo e le stanze sono arredate in stile sofitel. Noi abbiamo Soggiornato in una spelndida junior suite con un'offerta via internet. La stanza molto grande e pulitissima con doppio accesso ad un bagno di grande stile pulitissimo con una doccia doppia ed un letto king size molto comodo. Che dire tutto perfetto.

“Comfortable stay, but with some shortcomings” We enjoyed staying here -- on the whole, the staff were very friendly, and they had coffee, newspaper, and games in the lobby. The room was small but clean and comfortable, with a remote controlled a/c that worked well, microwave, fridge, two luggage stands in the closet, etc. It was clear that the housekeeping staff had taken good care of the room. Some shortcomings: Although the hotel is non-smoking, the hotel does reek of smoke. Usually, that doesn't bother me, but on some nights I woke up feeling suffocated by the smoke stench in the sheets, and our belongings ended up smelling like smoke by the end of the stay. Also -- the wifi network was not set up properly, such that there were routers conflicting/competing with each other on the same channel and causing the Internet to be unusable for long periods of time. The front desk person was unhelpful and defensive ("wi-fi works just fine in the lobby"; insisted that we came down to the lobby with our computers to show that it was not working, though we explained it very clearly that the problems were not with our computers), and the IT support number they had posted in the room was outdated and had been disconnected. Not helpful. Tip: The hotel can be a little tricky to access. Take New Brunswick going South off of Hwy 64, then take the first left onto Ricky Bell Cove. Watch out for potholes; the hotel is at the end.

“Great amenities, OK location” My spouse and I stayed at this property for a weekend getaway in Charlotte. The location is fairly easy to find and convenient to I-85, Billy Graham Pkwy, and the airport (we didn't hear any airport noise though). However, guests will need a car while staying here because there are no restaurants, convenience stores, etc. within walking distance. Our early check-in was quick and very easy. The lobby is spacious and has a great restaurant, sundries shop, meeting space, etc. The glass-paneled elevators make for a scenic ride to the upper floors. Our room was very spacious with seperate living and bedroom areas. The couch pulls out into a sofa bed for those that need it. The room had 2 televisions, microwave, dorm-sized refrigerator, and coffee pot. The bathroom was very clean and bright. The bed had plenty of extra pillows and the linen were soft and comfortable. The concierge and front desk staff were knowledgable about the area and gave great directions. We would definitely stay here again!

“if you like barren & outdated walmart style hotel” I've stayed in hotels in 12 countries and in 30 states in this country. Only one has disappointed as much as did the Mansfield. At a price tag of $400 you do not expect (i)metal TV stand from the Goodwill store (ii)plastic peeling from the bathtub, (iii)marble floors that have not been polished in 20 years and (iv)floors where you debated over whether or not to walk without slippers - there was no carpet, just a very thin strraw "pad". The rooms are small and I can live with that & fully expect it in a city. The hallways on the 10th floor are so narrow that it is difficult to pass by the service cart that the chambermaids use. The hotel has location & a clean & comfortable bar & lobby. The staff was friendly and helpful. Beyond that, you would be better to stay in the suburbs @ a Days Inn & commute in each morning in a limo - and likely save $. With a facelift this could be a relatively nice hotel. At $400 a night the owners should clearly be able to afford renovations unless their occupancy rate is so low that they are struggling.

“Great hotel in great location.” If you don't want to stay downtown, then this is a good option. Very friendly service, and walk to the Space Needle, EMP, Children's Museum (not great) and ride the Duck. Also walked to the monorail station, which goes to Westlake Center (mall) and a good food court. Got a great Expedia deal on this one, cheaper than going direct.

“Pretty old place” It's a nice place, but it does have its glitches. I laughed when I saw the other reviews talking about towels - how difficult can it be to get enough towels to go around? Our room also had just one bath towel and one washcloth, and when I called for more towels, housekeeping asked what we had in the room, then brought precisely one more bath towel and one hand towel. Other minor quibbles: the rooms are desperately in need of an updating, and I don't mean that what is there is a bit old-fashioned in style. I mean that the furniture that was there was pretty beat up, with chipped finishes and crooked doors. The valet desk also took a long time - but while you wait for your cars, be sure to check out the insane elevator system that the valets use - it is amazing!! Now, quibbles aside, it is a very pretty landmark building in a nice location, the room was a decent size with a very comfortable bed for a good price, check-in and out was fine, and all of the staff was very friendly. I'd stay here again, but I do hope they invest in a few more towels.

“Two Beds would have been nice” When I showed up to check in at this hotel the front desk woman never smiled once. I was traveling with 2 teenage boys and I asked for a room with 2 beds. The front desk woman told me that it would be $25.00 more for 2 beds. I figured for $25.00 I would just sleep with my boys. The room was clean and nice. The prices at the hotel bar were outrageous. I went around the block for a great meal at Dubliners (an Irish Pub). We just slept in this hotel one night and were really not impressed at all.

“very nice boutique hotel” My husband and I had a wonderful stay at this hotel. I will categorize key points in this review, which will explain why I gave it a 4 instead of a 5 star rating. Checkin: Upon arrival we were met outside the main entrance by the doorman. He took our bags and took care of valet parking our car. We were escorted to the front desk where we were warmly greeted and provided with an upgrade (without our asking) at no extra charge. Our Room: we stayed in a king room with a small refrigerator, coffeemaker, and microwave and was very spacious and quiet, especially considering New York standards. The room was very clean and in a quiet part of the building. The bathroom has a large shower and nice tile work. Concierge: at front desk, who was very helpful with theatre tix, restaurants, and directions. Location: in the heart of the theatre district, within convenient walking distance to theaters and times square ** here's why we rated it out 4 out of 5 Breakfast - continental - included in rate: had all food items one would think would be included in continental breakfast except fresh fruits (apples were not ripe) Wine reception: daily from 4-5 PM - included WINE ONLY. no munchies, no cheese. hmmm. TV - in room - hard to work and hard to access movie channels. we felt that the service and cleanliness of hotel outweighed any of the minor problems and will definitely return to this hotel in the future.

“Good location, poor renovation.” Just got back from our trip to DC and was disappointed in the Liaison Capitol Hill Hotel.
