I supposed I should not have been surprised after how much difficulty we had before we even arrived. After I made the reservations online with no problems (thank you, Hotels.com), my wife called the hotel to ask some questions (was the pool open, what’s the height of the ceiling in the parking garage, could we request a renovated room, etc.). When she asked if their renovation was complete, the woman rudely asked, "Who am I talking to?" It went downhill from there. Since my wife had no luck, I called back a few days later to ask the questions and was put on hold. After 10 minutes, I hung up and called back. I was put on hold again. After 10 more minutes, I called back and asked if there was a better time for me to call. They promised to call me back. They didn't. After 90 minutes, I called them yet again and finally got my questions answered. The hotel supposedly just went through a multi-million dollar renovation. I would hate to have stayed there BEFORE the renovation. When I made the reservation, I hoped that it wasn’t just a dump that had lost its flag (used to the Holiday Inn on the Hill). Not sure why it changed names/ownership, but in the end I guess it’s somewhere in between. The lobby had a stale odor to it and the rooms smelled musty. Very low ceilings in the rooms (I know a renovation can't help that). Overall, the rooms were cramped. The tiny bathrooms did not have fans, so even a quick shower rendered the bathroom an unusable sauna for quite a while (hot and steamy). The water was very hard and was unkind to everyone’s hair. We were told that all rooms had been renovated. Again, I’d hate to have stayed in them before the renovation. The door to the bathroom was difficult to open and close and flakes of paint drifted to the floor each time you opened it. The “wood” on the side of the sink next to the toilet was peeling. The A/C had to be set at 67 just to keep the room at 72. No big deal, once you figured it out. The swimming pool on the roof was in decent shape, though there’s really no view. You know you’re up in the air (10th floor), but you pretty much just see the top few floors of surrounding buildings. You have to be a fairly tall adult standing right up against the fence at the edge of the building to see anything. And even then, you can’t see much. There was hair on the bathroom floor when we checked in. Doesn’t exactly make you feel great about the cleanliness of the towels and linens. I would not recommend walking west of the hotel at night. You’ll be passing a very large homeless shelter on E Street. And even during the daylight, I didn’t necessarily feel all that safe walking by there, what with a number of people milling about in front of the shelter. But in a big city, you’re going to have to deal with some of that, unless you take cabs door-to-door all the time. I will say that the only times we were ever approached or otherwise bothered was on busy downtown streets in front of restaurants, etc., or at Union Station - not on the walk to and from the hotel. I’d say the hotel was worth the $90 per night we paid for Friday and Saturday nights for the location alone. It’s an easy walk to Union Station and the Capitol and a reasonable walk (if it’s not too hot) to most other sites. But it certainly was not worth the $300 per night we had to pay for Tuesday or the $279 for Wednesday or even the $195 per night for Thursday. Our average cost per night (with taxes) was $225. I guess I shouldn't be surprised in the quality of room I got for that price, but I have to wonder if another $50 or $75 per night could have put us in a much nicer hotel. I would recommend this hotel for a short weekend in DC if you can get the $90 per night rate on Friday and Saturday (and you take cabs in the evenings). But if you’re staying for 5 nights, or longer, as we did, I would look elsewhere.

“Good customer service” Aesthetics of hotel had no flaws whatsoever. Room/bathroom very clean. We were fortunate enough to have a nice view from 16th floor. Good location close to shopping and restaurants. Gym is spectacular. Outstanding customer service wowed me. Finding the parking was confusing, even with the outside bellhop's directions; once we phoned the hotel, the receptionist was able to give us better directions. Do not expect any freebies at this hotel. I give this hotel four stars, as I really do not know if the $500+ room rates are justified; I would have preferred to stay elsewhere and save $200.

“Excellent place - I almost feel we should keep it a secret” I booked this hotel directly with their website since this gave me the best rate; about $130 per night which for New York in May is pretty good. I stayed here for four nights at the beginning of May in a single room , and using the shared bathroom. The room is compact but had everything I needed and I wasn't in the room much anyway. The shared bathrooms were good and clean. I looked in a room that was being changed which had a private bathroom and to be honest the shared bathrooms are significantly bigger! No bathrobes are provided - perhaps an oversight here - so you either have to dress in the bathroom or be comfortable with walking along the hallway wrapped in a towel. The location of the hotel is fine with a couple of subway stations about 1 block away, plus a smattering of Irish bars just around the corner and plenty of close by options for breakfast. I would happily stay here again and recommend it to others.

“Overrated, but great location and GREAT staff!!” Expected much more. The river view room was amazing in regards to the view. It was beautiful. the rooms are big however, old decor which could needs to be updated. Its clean however. The windows feel awkward because they make the room look small (!) if you know what i mean, The location is GREAT!! Walking distance to Michigan Avenue. The staff is WONDERFUL. Nice, caring, polite.Really good people. It can been noisy in the morning and i guess the walls are thin. you can hear the cleaners etc. Otherwise no noise from the traffic or so. with train from O'hare it takes about 35-40 minutes.Really easy to catch and it cost about $2,70 or so for a one way ticket. Also free internet!! The food was ok at the hotel but since the bar staff are nice its pleasent to sit there....

“Keine MR Gold Benefits / Unfreundliches Personal / kleine Zimmer” Die Lage des Courtyard ist sehr gut, es sind nur wenige Gehminuten zum weissen Haus un der Washington Mall. Ausserdem ist im Erdgeschoss ein sehr gutes Restaurant, die Brauerei Gordon Biersch in der es auch eine grosse Auswahl deutsches Bier gibt. Das wars leider mit den positiven Punkten. Zum negativen: Genaue gegenueber ist ein Nachtclub, man hat die ganze Nacht besoffene vorm Eingang und laute Musik ueber die Strasse wummern. Das Personal ist unfreundlich und hat keine Ahnung. Bei Courtyard ist normalerweise fuer Marriott Gold Members das Fruehstueck inbegriffen. Beim Cehckin fragte ich danach. Die Dame lachte und meinte, bei meiner billigen Rate waere ganz sicher kein Fruehstueck dabei. Ich verwies sie darauf, dass es nichts mit der Rate zu tun hat sondern mit meinem MR Gold Status. Sie wusste leider nicht genau was ich meine... so viel zur Ausbildung des Personals. Mit unserem Zimmer waren wir dann auch nicht gluecklick. Es ging zum Innenhof, komplett verbaute Sicht, dunkel und klein. Wuerde das Hotel nicht empfehlen, da einzig wirklich positiver Punkt die Lage ist.

“Great Stay & Value” We went to Austin last minute and booked a 4 Star property on Priceline. We were pleasantly surprised to get the Hyatt Austin. The property is on the south side of Lady Bird Lake with direct access to a jogging trail on the lake, nice touch! Fitness room was nice but why stay inside when you have a beautiful path with great views. The hotel staff were young yet attentive and the hotel looked to be recently remodeled. The room was clean and modern with a boutique feel. Bathroom was standard fare, nothing remarkabe. You can walk across the bridge to downtown, everything was at your door step. One complaint was the back-up in the parking lot. A meeting let out the same time as we checked out and there were 20-25 cars in line to get out and only one pay-booth open. Luckily we were not in a hurry!

“All Great Except Elevators” The rooms are small but very modern, clean, and well appointed. They did a great job with the space they have. The issue is the elevators. There are only 3 and you have to wait a long time for one. And by "long time" I don't just mean a few minutes. There is no air conditioning in the hallways on the guest room floors, so waiting for a long time for an elevator with no air conditioning in July is a challenge. Make sure you aren't in a rush when you head out, and give yourself plenty of time to get downstairs. Other than that, this is a great hotel in a great location. Recommended!

“Nice Place to Stay” This was my first stay at a Four Points by Sheraton. I doubt it will be my last. This brand appears to be Sheraton's version of a Courtyard by Marriott. The room was a little smaller and featured a side chair rather than the sofa normally found in Courtyards. I found the desk chair to be uncomfortable, but two ottomans, tucked cleverly into the bedside tables proved to be much better for use at the desk. The bed was awesomely comfortable. In fact, it might have been too comfy. We spent four nights at this location, and sometimes I just didn't want to leave that wonderful bed. The bath might have been a little smaller than the Courtyard, but it was still sufficiently comfortable. The bath decor was a little sparse, no towel bars, just hooks behind the door and a shelf under the vanity--and they were a little stingy with the towels: 2 towels, 2 wash cloths, 2 hand towels. Weekday evenings there are drink specials and appetizer specials at the lobby bar. You can order them and take them back to enjoy in your room. The wings are a great deal, and they taste fabulous. A nice stay!

“Hard to be objective” After a rather chaotic flight from New Orleans, arriving at the Mercer was pure redemption. "Did you have a nice flight?" the concierge asked us. "No!" we answered. "Don't worry, now you are here". True and wise words. The Mercer is the very epitomée of Boutique Hotel. A splendid building, tastefully hip decor, excellent and very friendly service, sophisticated laid-back clientele. The Lobby is basically a very comfortable, smartly designed, large living room. You have your breakfast there, an afternoon snack, or a late night cocktail. It's cosy, sophisticated and happening. The Kitchen is the very lively restaurant in the basement. Excellent drinks, excellent food, excellent service, in a cool environment very popular with locals. The rooms are a decadent experience: smart time-standing design, huge tub and walk-in shower, and a mini-bar loaded with delicious snacks, spirits, champagne, cigarettes, city maps and shopping guides. I admit it is hard to be objective when writing about The Mercer. Hotel wise it may not be the perfect top-notch experience you could get for that kind of rack rate. But as an experience of what New York is all about, it can't be beaten. And if you're the urban kind, you'll leave with the tranquil sense of having found your home in New York City.

“One of the best hotels I've ever been to” I had originally booked another hotel for this trip, but had to change the dates and couldn't extend my stay at the other place. To my surprise, I was able to book the Conrad within the rate I can afford, and I am glad the other place couldn't help me this time. I had never stayed at a Conrad before, but all the reviews were right - this is a great place to stay. I was in Indianapolis for a conference three blocks west at one of the state government buildings, and the short walk was very pleasant. I can't add much to what has already been said, except I will definitely try to book the Conrad next time I go to Indy. I really didn't take advantage of all the Conrad has to offer, but I greatly appreciated the wonderful bedding, very large flat panel TV and the really nice bathroom that was perhaps the cleanest hotel bathroom I've ever seen. I did use the fitness center, and had the exercise room to myself each time. I wish I had remembered to take my ear buds so I could listen to the TV while using the exercise equipment. The indoor pool and hot tub were very nice and very clean. I can't comment on the restaurant or room service because I ate elsewhere, but I understand teh Capitol Grille is first rate. Thanks to all the staff, from the front desk to the housekeeping and maintenance, that have maintained such a nice place. I look forward to seeing you again in the future.

“CLASSIC AND CHARMING” The high ceiling lobby alone is worth the experience. Yes, the Palmer House is an old hotel and at times appears "tired". But the experience is so different from almost every other hotel business travelers experience that its worth it. Nice executive loungue, standard Hilton rooms with great bedding. TV reception so-so. Location Excellent. Seems like it hasnt changed in 20 years. That's what made my stay great. Classic Hotel!

“Yes Small Rooms, But Nice Hotel” I had read the reviews and looked at the pictures on the internet so I had a good idea what we were getting into. We had also been to the bar on a previous visit so we knew how to find the hotel. (Hint - Look for the flame and the bushes) The room is small and about the smallest I have stayed in NYC. But we only paid $179 and we were staying for only one night. With those parameters, it was just fine. I would also say that based on some of the reviews I would have thought the property was run down, but not at all. The room was well appointed and the amenities were fine. I would check out the hotel's website and look at one of the rooms, before you book. It gives you a great idea of what they have. My only real complaint was that the beds were low to the floor and to get in and out over the course of the night was a pain (I'm getting old).

“Very strange practices” Let me start by saying the property is decent, it was the staff that made it awful. Very strange goings on. I was moving across country and this hotel seemed like the best option. When calling them from the road, they quoted me a rate of $79.00 plus taxes. I was about 1 hour away from El Paso. I held it tentatively and wanted to explore other options so I contacted a friend on the phone and he found the same hotel for the rate of $59.00 on line through their website. Now, I called back the hotel and they stated that we should book it online since it was less expensive. We did that. I use Wyndham a lot and sometimes get upgraded. When we checked in, the woman at the front desk told me that she would give us the room we booked with two double beds. I just asked very politely if there were any upgrades available. She seemed perplexed by my question. She actually stated that "We were the last ones to get a double bedded room and would not be upgraded." When we saw the people after us check in, they were upgraded to a suite since they needed two double beds. I asked the front desk person (who was clueless) why they got upgraded and she responded that they had no more rooms with two double beds. Come on, it would have been common sense to give a frequent guest the upgrade instead of a non-frequent guest. I asked if I could speak with the MOD (even though I was very tired). There was no MOD and then she stated that she had no authority. She then actually contacted the hotel manager! She then stated that the hotel manager had an emergency and would not be able to call back. This was all very bizarre. The room was OK (average) but the situation and the lack of communication and bad staff manners was inexcusable. I would opt to stay at the Hilton Garden Inn or another comparable hotel.

“Hidden Gem that Won't be Hidden Much Longer” My greatest fear is that everyone writing great reviews for this hotel are going to just lock it out for those of us who want to return. When word fully gets out about this quaint, kitschy, neuvo, funky little place - it will be booked months in advance. The keys here are location and price. You can't beat either. It's not a luxury hotel by any means, but it's comfortable friendly and one of the best situated places I've ever stayed. You just can't be in a better location for the price, which for us was only $149. My wife and I were there the weekend of December 17, 18 and 19 and we shopped til we dropped - literally. This place is in the heart of Copley Square, and close to the T so you don't need a car. We had a blast and the desk support was extremely helpful and friendly. The rooms were cute and dark and fairly small - but frankly - we didn't spend much time there anyway. The room we had faced Boylston Street and was noisy, but we found that if we ran the heat fan in the room, it cut off a lot of the road noise. There's a new lounge going up on the first floor (much needed) but won't be open until spring, I'm told. Just a couple of nitpicky items: - We asked for extra pillows (they are pretty small and flat) and we got two sent to the room without pillowcases - The coffee in the lobby was cold to lukewarm most of the time and not refreshed enough and the doughnuts and bagels from the morning sat there all day and evening. Overall we loved the place and would go back in a second. And will. I just hope the prices don't go up with the demand (hint to ownership).

“Great Hyatt Experience” Just returned from a vacation with my spouse. Was very pleased with the Hyatt. The front desk associate was very friendly and upgraded us to a room with a balcony and a harbor view. He said it was because we were staying for a week and we were nice. (I got the impression that most of the business travelers are in a rush and rather rude). The lobby and atrium are beautiful with a large sculpture and running stream. The room was a good size and clean. Bed was comfortable with decent linens and lots of pillows. Bathroom was smallish but adequate. Sink and counter were outside the toilet/shower area. The hotel was full, several conferences, but we didn't hear much noise and slept well. We stayed with a AAA special and had breakfast included. Most mornings we had the buffet which had many good selections. On the weekend they had made to order omelets. A couple of mornings we ordered from the menu. This area of San Francisco is very nice as it borders the financial district. The Ferry Building is a short walk down the street. The cable car stops just outside the hotel and the trolley and subway were also very close. There are a few restaurants and stores within walking distance and many more a little further walk away. Chinatown is a short cable car ride up the hill (we walked back as it was all down hill). We took a couple of bus tours; one to Muir Woods/Sausalito that picked us up at the hotel. Another tour to Napa Wine country picked us up at the Ferry Building. Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf is a short trolley ride that can be picked up in front of the Ferry Building. This was a great location for seeing the city. (Be warned however, there are homeless people everywhere even in the best locations)

“Amazing location, great hotel” I stayed at the Millenium for 2 nights and it was great. The room was somewhat small, but for a city hotel, that is to be expected. The staff was amazing, the bed was extremely comfortable, and the location can't be beat. I would recommend this to anyone looking to spend a few days in Boston sightseeing.

“First, the good...” Stayed at this hotel for a large conference... Good: easy access to the Dupont metro station. Plenty of restaurants in the area (recommend Obelisk, Bistrot du Coin, Teaism - but not Odean Italian). Locale seemed very safe. Close to the Adams-Morgan neighborhood with additional restaurants. Coffee in the rooms. Bedding and bath linens were nice. Beds were comfortable. Security safe in the room. Affordable to the masses. Bad: hotel, although non-smoking, smells like smoke. Walls are thin - you know exactly what your neighbors are doing. Bathroom is on the small side. The housekeeping is shoddy - the room is given a "lick and a promise" and, by past reviews, the promise is never kept. Extra charge for Wi-Fi. Overall, a good choice for a conference hotel, but I would never choose this site for a getaway with a significant other or a girlfriend getaway.

“Best Hotel Experience” This was, simply the best hotel experience we have ever had. My wife and I stayed at this hotel to celebrate our anniversary. Upon check in, they knew (and remembered!) our names, what we liked, everyone congratulated us on our anniversary! Upon check in our room was not ready, but they offered to hold our luggage and let us swim in their pool. The pool! It was a salt water pool on the 12th floor that juts out over Main Street in Dallas. The service there was exceptional, the area was very clean and very well maintained. The concierge came and gave us our room key when our room was ready. The room was immaculate - superbly decorated, super clean, and there was a complimentary bottle of champagne for us, with truffles and a lovely note from the manager. The room was superb! Large, quiet, excellent! The room service was wonderful - the food was great, and the service was, again, exceptional. Stay here - it's expensive, but absolutely worth it - we plan on returning next anniversary!

“Modern, classy, great views” The hotel is on Wilshire Boulevard, three blocks east of Westwood Boulevard. The modern decor is pleasant and not overdone or far out. You can easily walk to Westwood Village, the area south of UCLA, with many stores and restaurants. If you are a fan of modern art, the Hammer Museum is two blocks from the hotel. You can drive or take the bus to the Century City mega-mall, with its upscale stores and restaurants, or go west to the beaches of Santa Monica or the new Santa Monica Place (another upscale mall) and the Third Street Promenade. The hotel has coffee and tea in the lobby in the mornings and wine in the evenings. There is live music during the Thursday wine period.

“Good Hotel for Families” Our group of 7 (two families) stayed here at the beginning of August. We had two ground floor rooms which were really spacious with a lounge/dining/kitchen room, a good sized bedroom and bathroom. We had a bay view, which had great views of the Seaworld fireworks in the evening. The hotel is a bit dated, but the size of the rooms is a huge benefit for families, we stayed in 9 hotels during our tour, and this had the largest rooms of any. The pool area is a bit smaller than it appears in the photos, but the beach is nice, we hired kayaks which the children enjoyed. We ate in the hotel for breakfast, which was a good buffet, and also for dinner. There is a good choice, although on both occasions we opted for the buffet, which was fine. The hotel is well located for Sea World, and in the evening we walked to Belmont Park for a ride on the roller coaster. The only problem we encountered was that when we arrived our rooms weren't ready, which seemed to be a common problem. If we visit San Diego again, we will probably stay here, but arrive a bit later to guarantee getting our rooms on time.

“Excellent stay at The Mark Hopkins” We returned to The Mark Hopkins this summer after more than a decade and had an outstanding long weekend. We arrived at San Francisco Airport and were brought to The Mark Hopkins by a most friendly driver of Virgin Limousine, arranged by the hotel. Location atop Nob Hill is great, architecturally stunning building. Rooms are decorated with beautiful fabrics, great beds and all marble bathrooms. We took advantage of the rate including breakfast, which I would recommend to everyone. The breakfast at Top of the Mark was one of the best we have experienced in a hotel in a long time; delicious food, excellent staff who cared for every detail. Most importantly, the view is fantastic!!!! On weekend nights, it is possible to have dinner and drinks in Top of the Mark as well, with great live jazz, dancing, cocktails and the city lights all around you. Top of the Mark is reason enough to stay at The InterContinental alone! All in all, our stay at The Mark Hopkins added a lot to our weekend in San Francisco. Although we stopped by the new Four Seasons, which looked gorgeous inside, we would choose The Mark Hopkins again for ambiance, location, and breakfast at Top of the Mark.

“Boutique hôtel agréable mais...” Idéalement placé à deux blocs de Columbus Circle, mon expérience au Empire Hôtel a été positive dans l'ensemble. M'attendant à un hôtel 4 étoiles, je n'ai pas été déçu par le cadre, plutôt moderne et luxueux. L'accueil était un peu froid et le check-in est à 3 PM pas avant... Le lobby est accueillant et permet de patienter à l'heure d'affluence du check-in. La chambre était petite mais agréable, propre et fonctionnelle. La salle de bain était minuscule. En y regardant de plus près, le souci du détail dans l'hôtel n'est plus le même dans les chambres (en tout cas la mienne) Chambres : ++ : les produits L'occitane, un must! les peignoirs. -- : Pas de wifi gratuit dans les chambres (uniquement dans le lobby qui bénéficie également de celui du Starbucks adjacent), 12$ pour 24h... définitivement un non-sens! Prenez le temps de faire un tour sur la terrasse du toit, belle et offrant une excellente vue sur Lincoln Center notamment. (couverte en hiver) Je recommande la découverte de cet hôtel mais je ne suis pas certain d'y retourner à l'avenir même si c'est une belle prestation dans l'Upper West Side.

“Amazing place!” Absolute gem of a place! Friendly staff, clean facilities, groovy rooms, fab kidney shaped pool and a fantastic location in the heart of all South Congress' many cool bars and boutiques. And, on top of all of this, incredibly good value! Amazing!

“Unusual hotel, good value for Manhattan” Stay is a totally renovated older 10 story building on 47th Street near 7th Avenue. The location is excellent for Broadway shows; the half price ticket kiosk is right down the street and the major theaters, as well as many other attractions, are easy walking distance. Many subway lines are nearby, and 47th is a busy commercial stretch with useful inexpensive restaurants for breakfast and quick meals. • The main disadvantage of Stay is that the rooms are extremely small. My queen standard room was 12' X 12' and most of that taken up by the bed, leaving a narrow strip of carpet to navigate around the room. I was travelling alone so I could manage but even two people would find it close quarters. • However, the lobby and the rooms are stylish and chic, and my room was very clean. The decor is gray/black/white with touches of burnt orange in silk drapes (covering the narrow window looking onto an air shaft). Very attractive overall. The bed is excellent with nice linens. All the fittings are upscale, big wall-mounted TV. Bathroom, also very small, was perfectly clean, well lit, with step-in shower stall. • An important plus: the climate control system worked very well, so I could make the room cold to sleep as I prefer, and warm it up quickly in the morning. • The lobby + bar turns into a noisy, but well-behaved, club in the evenings. Getting a room Not directly above it was good advice from tripadvisor. My 5th floor room was quiet. • At a good price, as I got from expedia, Style is good value. * This hotel is good if you are on a brief trip, out all day and only in to change clothes and sleep. A longer visit when you may want to use your hotel room more would become uncomfortable in the cramped room. The staff were pleasant and helpful with my questions about subway directions.

“Our Favorite NYC Hotel” We stay at the Lucerne about four times a year and have done so for the past five years; the one constant is the excellent level of service from every member of the staff. The location on the Upper Westside is perfect, the rooms are immaculate, the adjoining restaurant, the Nice Matin, is wonderful; the neighborhood has numerous small cafes, restaurants, stores; but what makes the Lucerne so special is the caring, friendly staff from the bellmen who greet you when you arrive to the folks at the reservation desk and the housekeepers. They make guests feel welcome and that's an intangible that many NYC hotels still haven't figured out.

“Fine for the price” As a pet owner whose dog travels everywhere, I am a big fan of Kimpton hotels. While Kimpton has several hotels in San Francisco, I chose this location as I thought it was right across from a park area, and a little less crowded. However knowing what I know now for going out, or getting a cab, or eating anywhere nearby, I would definitely choose one of their Union Square locations over this one. Pros/Cons from my stay.. PROS - Great view of the bay bridge (if you book a bay view room) - Friendly staff - Near a BART stop if you're coming from SFO CONS - No restaurants nearby - Teeny, tiny rooms - Occupy Wall Street is about two blocks from here - Area is completely shut down in evenings Overall, this doesn't change my perception of Kimpton, just would choose a different hotel in another neighborhood for the future. If you're a business traveler attending meetings in the financial district and taking the BART from SFO, then this might be more ideal.
“リーズナブル” ユニオンスクエアから徒歩圏内、日航ホテルやヒルトンホテルにも近いという好立地にあります。無料インターネットあり、朝食の無料サービスありと2つ星ホテルとしてはサービスが充実しています。部屋の雰囲気も悪くないです。サンフランシスコ空港発のフライトが朝なら、フロントでシャトルバンを頼みましょう。15ドルで30分以内に到着しました。

“Relaxing Hotel Still Near the Fun in San Diego” Stayed at this hotel on a short business trip. Hotel is not new but is well-maintained. Reception staff were courteous and efficient. Hotel was busy when I was there. The hotel is tucked behind a shopping plaza with many stores and a wide variety of restaurants, and within a few minutes walking distance. The location is quieter than a downtown hotel, and relaxing. This Courtyard was very close to the San Diego Airport. Hotel offers a free 24 hour airport van. Call for a free pickup when arriving at the airport. Parking is free, My room was of standard size and had two queen-size beds. Public spaces in the hotel were pleasant. A bar adjacent to the lobby is open evenings. Hot food can be ordered from the hotel kitchen. A sit-down restaurant is across the aisle from the bar for a traditional dining experience. Prices are fair. Work out room had the standard aerobic equipment and some free weights, although the exercise room was larger than one normally sees in a hotel this size. Everything worked in my room. I was pleased with this hotel. I will look to return on future trips.

“A solid choice” My husband and I stayed here for two nights in December. The location near the Port Authority is not the greatest, but it is acceptable and reasonably convenient to the Times Square area. We had a few minor glitches. The first room they gave us wasn't finished being cleaned, but in their defense, they were trying to accomodate us on an early arrival. The second room was clean, and in a quiet part of the hotel away from the street. We did have a large crack in one of our windows, which we thought was odd for a newer hotel. We've stayed in five hotels in NYC in the past two months due to a work assignment, and this room had the second tightest space, but they did make good use of what they had. Staff was helpful, room was in good condition except for the window, and bottom line, I would stay here again but it might not be my top choice. I'd probably give it 3.5 stars if the system allowed, so I'll give them 4 because of the staff.

“Ask for a Junior Suite” After staying at several SF Marriott properties in recent years, landed at this place for the first time after scoring a $100 room rate. Used my platinum status got me a Junior Suite, which was huge. The place was nice, bathroom looked a little dated. When I travel to SF I NEVER rent a car. It doesn't make sense as between trolley, BART and cabs, you can get around easier. If you don't like the spendy parking charge, well, DON'T DRIVE. Love the free breakfast buffett (another platinum perk) and the walking distance to all things on the Wharf and North Beach (an easier walk home than going up the hill). Anyway, I would stay here again in a heartbeat if the rate was right.

“Quite a hotel” The newest and biggest addition to the Riverwalk-area hotels in San Antonio is the Grand Hyatt and the name fits. Grand, indeed. I came here for a conference and was not disappointed. Service was excellent in every sense of the word from check in to check out. Staff stumbled over themselves asking how they could help and make my stay better. While pricey, one should expect as much from a place named the Grand Hyatt on the Riverwalk. If you want value, go over to La Quinta. The Internet connection was great and fast and the rooms featured modern decoration with a nice, large flat screen television. Stayed in a double-double which had a nice coach and ottoman by the window. Bathrooms were large and had a very nice, large sink with good amenities (shampoos, creams, toothpaste). The bed mattresses were comfortable. The only negative I can think of is that the rooms were on the smallish side ... but it is a little blip on the radar. Otherwise, this is an impressive hotel and one dedicated to making your stay a very good one.

“My favorite Austin hotel!” I miss the hotel reward points but it would be hard to find a hotel in Austin that beats the AT&T Executive Education and Conference Center. I have held multiple events there and the staff and service is the best in Texas. The rooms are fantastic with amazing views from the UT campus. The on-site restaurants can not be beat and the service encountered everywhere at the conference center is of the highest standard.

“Great staff, tired decor” Good location, right in the heart of downtown Columbus, I could walk everywhere I needed to go. The staff were helpful and very nice. The only problem was that the rooms and the decor definitely needed a refresh, I got a tired feeling from the furnishings.

“Great service, rooom needs attention” My company put on an event at the Sheraton Austin, and can say that the desk, catering and other staff were great, no issues here. The public areas and conference rooms were fine, and had not been in the hotel since it's remodel many years ago, it's nicer than I remember from my last stay. My room, while nice sized and clean was a bit tired, wallpaper peeling from the wall in my room and there were huge cracked tiles in the shower, they'd been attempting some repair, but really the tiles need to be replaced. Can't speak to the state of the other rooms, this makes me wonder if I shouldn't go back to the Westin. I'm afraid that I would not go out of my way to return to the Sheraton based on the maintenance level of the room. I travel a lot, and this was not up to standard.

“A good property that misses on the finer points, with poor work area” PROPERTY: This is an older property which has been well cared for and still looks fairly current. It has fresh bright colors which help it look newer than it is. I stayed in room 602 which was a double/double. ROOM: The room was clean and the décor looked fresh and bright. The room had its own, window mounted A/C unit which worked fine. The furniture was in good condition and had a 32” flat screen. The bathroom was large and clean. The ironing board cover was heavily soiled and embarrassing. I actually put a towel over the ironing board to prevent staining my shirt when I ironed it. BEDDING: The bed was fair and had good pillows. The second bed nearest the window had a visible “bow” in the center which I did not use. The bedding was good, but not of the same quality as a other mid range hotels like Hampton. WORK AREA: LaQuinta is obviously not trying to cater to the business traveler, which is OK if you can get enough recreational business. The work table is small, the mismatched chairs are useless for laptop work. There was only ONE HALF of an outlet for laptops and electronics which was troublesome for working. The staff was friendly, especially the shuttle driver who had only been on the job 3 days! Great job. RATING: Overall I would give the property an 78/100 and 85/100 for value. I would consider staying here again, but would also look at other properties nearby. PROS: price, location to airport, good overall condition CONS: HORRIBLE work area.

“Worth it if you get a spectacular rate” There is nothing that I could find to criticize about the service or the location of this hotel. It was very HGI-like in its amenities and decor. However, if you need space, this is not your hotel. The room was small ... even by NYC standards. Spotless clean, but scarcely enough room for the king bed, a chair and the desk. The view from the 27th floor was spectacular. I could see Macy*s and the Empire State Building. I was able to walk to a show on 46th St. in about 10 minutes - and the walk from Penn Station about 3 minutes. I would return, but only if properties with more space were substantially more expensive.

“An Average Hotel with Friendly Staff in a Good location” We stayed at this hotel while visiting Houston for 2 nights with our two young children. It was conveniently located near the museums that we were going to be visiting so we decided to give it a whirl. The hotel is a bit older and the rooms could use a little sprucing up, but it was clean and the staff was very friendly. We were put into a 2 room suite which was great. We assumed that they had just upgraded us. UHM that wasn't the case. They did remove the extra charges without any argument so I am glad we asked about that. This Hilton doesn't give children under 5 breakfast for free. Just FYI. Most do, but you will have to pay for your kids even if you have Hilton honors coupons. It really wasn't a big deal on the day of the buffet, but they charged us for adult meals on Sunday when they don't have the buffet. The hotel was quiet. There really weren't too many people staying there and you could really just relax there if you wanted. We spent most of our time seeing the sites so we were just happy to have a nearby hotel to rest and sleep.

“This hotel was a star among local hotels but not anymore” I have been staying at the Universal Sheraton for the past 12 years. I have experienced a wide range of service and issues during all 4 ownership changes and management at the hotel. Prior to the renovation was probably the best time period for this hotel. Management was great at that time. Presently over the past 12 month period I have stayed at the hotel about 6-8 different times. Current management is not what I would consider to be responsive or care about their customers. They offer comment cards but NEVER respond to issues. This is not a hotel for business travelers as the hotel does not cater to them. If you are on vacation then you are the perfect victim to the hotel as there is no timliness in their vocabulary. I met with the operations manager On one of my past trips and he assured me everything would be corrected. That was a lie. The hotel has no quality control - some examples arriving in the room and TV doesn't work or no shower curtain in bathroom or telephone never charged and not operating or light bulbs burned out and non operating. This is hotel management 101 and this hotel doesn't care. Other negatives include untimely delivery of room service breakfast when ordered the night before, not reading breakfast card to not include certain items because they cause extreme allergy and could cause medical emergency, high speed wireless is a joke, some rooms have air conditioning while others don't, gift shop hours vary depending on when they decide they want to close despite hours posted in hotel guide. Forget about enjoying the view frOm your room as it would appear windows have never been washed on the outside - only when it rains. The value charged for nightly accommodations increases during summer months when there are more tourists. The prices do not meet the value at this hotel. It is sad that a hotel within the SPG family lacks proper management, upkeep of technology, quality control and time management so that all guests are treated fairly and their needs are met. I guess long time loyalty to a hotel doesn't matter anymore.
“Perfect for business stay” This hotel is great. Room was clean. Staff was polite. Quiet. Free Wifi. Great location.

“Great Pool, Gardens, and Excellent Staff” Superb from start to finish. The pool was a resort style pool complete with full service bar, food and great service. Grounds were drop dead gorgeous and though it seemed like thousands of people in the halls and lobby, the grounds including hammocks and pool area never felt crowded. Room itself was plenty big with 2 full size Queens and a walk in closet. Staff were all excellent from the Valet, front desk, pool area, and service staff. Am a HHonors Diamond Member but thinking I'll be at the Omni much more often from here on out.

“Average Marriott” I stayed at this hotel for one night, it has the typical Marriott amenities but it seemed to be missing something. First the location is great, and its near many other more expensive high end hotels. The lobby is updated and rooms have the standard good bedding and furnishings. However the hotel was crowded, elevators slow, the gym full, and the concierge lounge closed on the weekend (no free breakfast for Platinums and gold) There was no weekend newspaper either and I got frustrated with longer waits for the elevator and trying to get a gym machine I wanted to use. The place is absolutely fine, but just average for a full service Marriott having been to many over the years. Otherwise service friendly and Id stay again if I got a similarly low rate as compared to other full service hotels in the immediate area.

“GREAT location, service, and hotel.” I was apprehensive after reading the reviews. I was pleasantly surprised by how awesome this Hyatt really is. To start, you cannot find a better located midtown hotel for the quality. It is next door to Grand Central, literally just steps!!! You can easily walk to Times Square and 5th Ave. Madison Ave is also manageable walking distance. If not, you can take the subway to wherever you go. Subway station is outside the hotel door!!! This hotel is always crowded. HOWEVER the staff is amazing for the amount of people they have to deal with on a daily basis. The staff at the bell desk is so helpful. The lobby is breathtaking, MUCH better than the Waldorf! I went by myself and stayed in a room with a queen bed. I found the room to be spacious for NYC standards. If you want to talk "small", try the W on Lexington. Bathroom is small but totally adequate. If you want a huge bathroom, go to Vegas and stay at the Venetian. The bed, sheets, pillows, and furniture in the room are very comfortable. For a hotel to be in Grand Central, I find it to be very quiet. I have had my best nights sleep in NYC EVER here!!!!! Now the BEST part of this hotel (besides the FREE coffee in the morning which was great!) is that you can actually PRINT your boarding pass in the lobby. Saves plenty of time for me at JFK. Hyatt really tries to cater to its customers. So if you want to get a great place when you go visit this great city, stay here and make Hyatt your hotel of choice. I did!

“Great Staff!” There are a lot of options in downtown San Antonio however this hotel really makes your feel special. from the warm greetings at the front desk, the smiles and hellos for the housekeepers and all the smiles on the restaurant staff. You can really tell that everyone at this hotel is happy to be there. Love the peeacocks in the courtyard.

“Great location - service not-so great” My husband and I chose to stay at the Town Place Marriott based on two factors: 1/ location and 2/ we are extremely loyal to the Marriott family of hotels - based on our being Silver/Gold members respectively. The location for this hotel is extremely convenient for all of the cities major attractions - the Alamo is just a couple of blocks away - as is the Riverwalk and all of the other highlights of the downtown San Antonio area. The downfall of this location is that towards the evening hours it tends to get a little "seedier" - as there were definitely a few times in which (even before 9 pm and in broad daylight) my husband and I were approached by street people asking for $ while waiting for our car to be brought around by the valet staff. The hotel itself is situated across from a fairly loud sports bar called The Ticket. From our room on the 3rd floor we could definitely here the bass thumping music until about 2 am every morning of our stay - - so this was definitely something we were disappointed with - though we never asked to be moved - based on having settled in and then realizing the first night that the noise-level was fairly constant and made it difficult to sleep. Having stayed over 200 nights at Marriot properties around the world - I was a bit dismayed at the lack of "Marriott" service that I have grown accustomed to during our travels for both work and pleasure. The check-in experience was OK - as there were no rooms available due to their being sold out the evening before so they had just indicated that but did not suggest other points of interst or things that we could do with our time - having just dropped off our car at the valet and mentioning that we were first-timers in the city. The valet service is probably some of the worst if not the worst I have seen - - as they took our tickets and then asked us to show ID every time we wanted to get our car back - the system is slow and ineffective and they could definitely improve in that area. The housekeeping is also something that I did not understand - as we left our room at about 11 am the first morning we were there and returned around 3 pm and the room was not cleaned. I called down to the front desk and they had someone from housekeeping call me back who did not apologize nor provide explanation - rather they asked if they could bring us some towels - which we made the exchange and that was it. Overall, pretty ineffective and not typical of the Marriott experience. The room itself was new and modern - with everything you need and nothing you don't. It would have been nice to have a pen and paper in the room - - which was odd that for an extended stay place like TownPlace they did not provide. Overall - I would be hesitant to recommend this based on service - but if you can look past the bumps and need a place to stay that is reasonable in cost and near all of the city attractions - this is a reasonable value - just ask for a high floor room away from the sportsbar noise across the street. Good luck!

“Much worse than expected” Ugh. The hotel is in serious need of updating, it's celebrating 30 years and cracks are showing all over the place from the dated lobby and elevators to old carpets, furniture, bathrooms. Expected a modern hotel, this definately was not it - although it came with a hefty rate. Probably most dissappointing was the level of customer service. We had requested high floor room prior to check in, requested this again at check in and very nicely explained we were on a special weekend celebrating anniversary. The guy at front desk must have had a bad week because we got a room next to the elevators and across from the service room on a lower floor. Thanks for your help buddy. We could have complained but chose not to -we didn't spend a lot of time in the room. The concierges need to attend mood modification classes they were all grumpy and seemed annoyed to be answering any questions, why is this not apparent to management? Spend 5 minutes observing their interaction with guests and you know you have problems. Not impressed, no way coming back here, would look for W, Hard Rock or Monacco at this price range and for a more modern vibe.

“Nice location” The location was perfect for Beale street and restaurant availability. Checkin was slow. My room was promised in about an hour (approx 3:00pm), with a call to my cellphone which never happened. This made is difficult to juggle our schedules. We didn't eat at the restaurant (was closed later afternoon), however did enjoy the music in the lobby lounge area as a break between meeting clients for dinner and the work day. Parking and internet overpriced.

“Surprisingly Impressed.” This is a business class Hilton in a less than desirable part of Houston. It located immediately in the energy center, so the immediate area is okay. Drive a block away and things change quickly... With that said, my check in was efficient. I was upgrded to a suite on the 9th floor. The suite was spacious and exceeded expectations. The executive lounge had a nice breakfast as well. All in all a good stay...

“Spent four nights here and loved it” Spent four nights here with my teenage daughter and found it to be a very good experience. The location is fabulous. A couple of blocks from the Metro, which is easy to use and much cheaper and even quicker than taking a taxi - especially during rush hour. We were five blocks away from the White House and strolled down there as soon as we checked in since our room wasn't ready. Since we traveled during April vacation the place was packed over the weekend (we were there Saturday thru Wednesday). The lines for the Manager's Reception looked worse than they actually were. The easiest method was to split up. I got the drinks and my daughter got the munchies. They offer mixed drinks, wine and beer. The beer was fine but the Cosmo I got the second night was undrinkable. My fault expecting that to taste good when being made with 'cheap' vodka. The staff manning the bar were very pleasant. There are signs up warning you about the wait times for breakfast. The first morning we ate there (Sunday) they opened up a second room for breakfast and we breezed right in - right around 8:30. Monday morning I let me daughter sleep in and we didn't get downstairs until after 9 and the lines were huge and we waited a good 15 minutes to get our food. The main dining room consisted of two lines. One for cook-to-order eggs/omelets and the other for the buffet line consisting of scrambled eggs, hash browns (salty but very good), bacon, sausage, either pancakes (quite good) or waffles (cold and undercooked), melon and yogurt. There were also muffins, toast, bagels, bananas, apples, oranges, several types of cold cereal, juice, milk, coffee and tea. A pretty good assortment considering it is included in the price of the room. My daughter opted for an omelet every day and enjoyed them very much. Our room was on the second floor and very comfortable. The living room had a sleeper sofa, dresser, desk/table, flat-screen tv, coffee table and was very spacious. The kitchenette was in the 'hallway' between the living room and bedroom and had a microwave, fridge and sink. You could hear the noise from the hallway but once you closed the door between the living room and the bedroom, you couldn't hear it at all (in the bedroom). There was a closet in the 'hallway' too. Our bedroom had two very comfortable beds and an entertainment center/dresser/closet combo (which held the tv and three drawers). My only complaint about the bedroom was that it was very dark due to the fact that the neighboring building was extremely close. You had to crane your neck to even see the sky, let alone figure out whether the sun was out or not. I like lots of sunlight so I was disappointed with the lack of view/light but we spent so little time in our room it hardly mattered. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We booked the moonlight tour of the monuments through them - great tour and the best part was that they picked us up at the hotel. We ate one meal in the hotel restaurant. The food was very good but very pricey for what we got. Two cocktails, a soda and two entrees cost over $100. We were much happier with the Belgium restaurant around the corner. Very happy with our experience here and would stay here again anytime.

“Ok, but would not stay here again” Hotel is ok. Just not really my style. I am sure I got the smallest room in the house, must be a specialty of quikbook. Staff was very nice though.I happened to walk into the Mansfield Hotel across the street on this visit and found my next hotel! It had an aura that Iroquois was missing.Fitness room was adequate.

“Hipster Heaven - But Delightfully Friendly & Spacious for this Midwest Gal!” I stayed at the Ace Hotel in early December for a girl's trip. Hotels are always so crazy expensive during the holidays in NYC, so I was trying to find something 'reasonable' but still fun. I have visited the Ace Hotel in Palm Springs, so I was familiar with the whole "vibe" of their hotels (young, hip, modern, nontraditional). I always check TripAdvisor before booking, and I read a few horror stories about tiny rooms, rude staff etc - So I was sure to call the hotel ahead of time to make sure my room was not a coat closet! (***BOOKING TIP: I found a much better deal on Tablet, so I called the hotel and they were willing to match the price! Amazing***) When I arrived my room was not ready for check in, but the gentleman helping me at the front desk (I can't remember his name...) was SOO helpful and friendly. He told me it would be best to wait for my room since anything they had available would be tiny in comparison. I am happy to say that everyone I encountered at the front desk was delightful. I was expecting a "too cool for school" attitude based on what I had read, but everyone was very kind and helpful (even in my preppy clothes & fur coat... very un-hip to say the least!) The lobby itself was sort of a nightmare. There was NO WHERE to sit at 3pm on a Thursday because it is full of hipsters and MacBooks as far as the eye can see. I was told there was a "reserved area" for hotel guests, but no one actually abides by this rule. Anyway, I strolled around the neighborhood for a while (lots of junk jewelry stores and wig shops), then went back to the lobby and finally found a spot in the "reserved section". I ordered a late lunch, and after a while my room was finally ready. I stayed in a "Large Double Double" (Room 915) and it was huge! The layout of the room was really bizarre and looked like a dorm room (again, I knew to expect this - but it was a fun change up from my usual hotel routine). There was a full size fridge, two large queen beds (they looked a little creepy with wool blankets - but had AMAZING sheets and pillows - so sleep quality was terrific!) The TV was not well positioned, but I wasn't watching it all that much, so it was not a problem. The bathroom was super tiny, and did not offer much storage space or any counterspace for that matter. I did love the products that were available to use, and the cute little black soap on a rope! Free wifi, and it actually worked! The view - AMAZING. I'm not sure what the building across the street is called, but it looks like an old fashioned French chateau - beautiful! We also had a full view of the Empire State building, which was SO fun since it was all lit up for Christmas! A few other things to note: -Don't forget your MacBook if you want to fit in while hanging out in the lobby during the day. -The lobby is totally not my scene, but if you are looking for a loud, fun environment - this is the place for you! On Fri & Sat they had live music. -There is a cute little coffee shop in the lobby, but it gets crazy busy - so be prepared to wait for 20 minutes to get your drink. -The gift shop is actually an Opening Ceremony store - so don't be surprised to see $700 t-shirts for sale. -The front desk has umbrellas to borrow if it rains ($20 deposit, and make SURE you get one that isn't broken!)

“Great Airport Hotel Option” I stopped over in LA on my way to and from New Zealand last month and stayed at the Sheraton LAX in both directions. I have stayed at the hotel before and think it is one of the best in the airport area. If you are an aviation buff like myself, some of the airport view rooms have a great view of arriving and departing aircraft. The rooms are clean and very well appointed . The Club Floor is worth the extra money if you are arriving after a long haul flight as you can enjoy access to the lounge for snacks in the evening or continental breakfast in the morning. Free wifi is also available on the Club level. I have never had anything bad to say about this property however I did have a small issue with the bathroom this visit. Oddly enough I was in room 1565 both on my way to New Zealand and on the way back. During both stays (about 3 weeks apart) there was such a loud noise of air blowing quite forcefully through the air vent in the bathroom that the door to the bathroom had to be closed at all times. And when in the bathroom it was not only irritating but this constant flow of cold air that could not be controlled was very unpleasant. Especially when getting out of the shower. The bathrooms are definitely in need of some updating and this air vent issue needs to be addressed. My only other issue was with respect to the shuttle service from the airport terminals. For whatever reason (possibly just luck) it always seems as though the shuttle for the Sheraton LAX arrives at the airport shuttle stops much less frequently than the shuttles bound for the other airport hotel properties. Just an observation. I would still highly recommend this hotel to travelers stopping over and looking for a nice place to stay in the airport area.

“Top Notch in making you feel welcomed, very impressive!” We were not registered guests at this location, but have stayed at Hamptons in other states. We dropped in to use the restrooms and were warmly greeted each time and noticed how outstanding the staff was in meeting guests needs and making them feel at home. There was always lemon water available to quench the thirst and the warm cookie we tried was better than Homewood's. We asked questions and were astounded that their parking was free as all other hotels, even ones 3 blocks more away from town center really soaked the patronage for parking fees. We observed patrol in the parking area and at night it was well lit so we felt relatively safe as that whole area is plucked with delapidation and new construction intermixed. I just wanted to say that based on the courtesy and kindness of this property, we would definitely make it a base point for exploring the attractions within walking distance should we return to San Antonio.

“Well appointed and excellent service” Usually stay at RC on Nob Hill but went to 4Seasons for change. Very impressed with quality of room, extremely comfortable bed (very key), and spacious/well laid out bathroom. had casual dining in lounge and food/service/atmosphere was excellent. The staff directed us to the farmers market a few blocks away that was simply wonderful. Very peaceful and quiet. Would stay here again.

“Tired hotel, mediocre rooms, nice reception but rude restaurant personnel” Rooms are old and mediocre. The hotel is not too clean including in the rooms. Very worn out. The lobby area is tiny and not convenient. Food: food is average quality. Restaurant staff is not friendly (they said that they were not part of the hotel, which may explain their rudeness). Reception was friendly and helpful, apologizing for the rude service in the restaurant. Not sure why it’s called 4-points, when the hotel is actually 3 points at best. It is a shame for Starwood group to have both this and Westin hotels in the same portfolio. Unless you are on a small budget (although it’s also not too cheap), don’t stay there.

“Overall very good, a few issues” Just spent a night at the relatively new Four Points Sheraton Columbus Airport. Got a good rate via Hotwire and that does have some bearing on my feeling. Overall it was a very good experience, would certainly consider staying here again and would recommend it to others (especially at the rate we got via Hotwire). I do have one *MAJOR* issue/complaint, however, the pool photo shown on their website? I'd like to know where the heck that pool is at the hotel. The hotel pool is a *postage stamp* size *indoor* pool - not a luxurious outdoor pool as "shown" on the website. As I look closer, it even appears that the pool on the website is a rendering. Maybe it was planned that way and/or will eventually be constructed, but it sure doesn't exist that way now. Had two other *minor* issues, neither of which were really problems. First is that I had booked the room for 2 adults and 1 child, and they "gave" us a room with a single bed. I confess, I didn't call in advance to confirm a room with 2 beds, but that's because I never considered the possibility that they would give a booking for 3 people a single bed. There was absolutely no problem and the front desk quickly gave us a room with 2 beds, but if they hadn't had one available . . . (and I will always try to confirm a room with 2 beds when using Hotwire in the future). The second was that the in-room coffee had 2 "decafs" and no regular coffees, hello? Again, not a problem and the front desk supplied "leaded" coffee without any questions upon request. To recap my other observations: Pro: Nice, new, hotel with nice lobby, etc; Staff was pleasant & professional, taking care of the minor glitches we encountered; Lobby bar had a good beer selection and prices weren't outrageous; Room was clean, and nicely decorated; Beds, linens, etc were nice; Nice shower (but see below). Cons: Pool not as "advertised" on the website photos; Minor glitches encountered (see text of review); Bathroom was shower only, not a problem for me, and they might have rooms with tubs, but it's worth noting and might be a con for some travelers; Not much in walking distance (which I like in a hotel, but certainly don't expect with an "airport" hotel). As much of what I talked about above issues/complaints, I don't want to give the impression I didn't like the hotel, I did like it. That said, but had I booked it expecting a nice outdoor pool, I would have suffered a *major* disappointment.

“Awesome hotel!” I booked this hotel after reading the reviews. I booked a courtyard view due to some of the comments about the noise from the busy streets nearby. We were upgraded to a view of 77th, which turned out to be awesome! I did not hear any noise from the streets below. (We were on the 4th floor.) The room was spacious & clean. The bathroom had every ammenity, including a large bathtub and towel warmer. The hair dryer in the room didn't work, so when we called to request a replacement, they brought one up within 5 minutes. We received a turn-down service every night, which was nice. The service all around was exceptional. The hotel was located very close to Central Park.

“Great stay at the Hyatt Regency Austin” My wife and I had a Monday morning business meeting, so we booked the Hyatt Regency Austin for Sunday night.. We got a room for $92 on priceline. The front desk was very friendly and we were checked in quickly. I was told parking would be $11/day, but was never charged. The hotel is in tip top shape. It had recently been remodeled. The room had a view of townlake and the Congress Ave bridge. It was one of the nicest rooms I have ever stayed in. The bed was great. I have a select comfort sleep number bed and find when I travel I usually wake up in pain the next morning. I got a great night's sleep without pain. There is a flat-panel HDTV in the room, but all the channels were only SD. The room did not have a refrigerator / mini-bar. The alarm clock has an iPod dock . There is a safe. The service in the bar was a little slow. There were two bartenders working, but they never checked on us. We had to flag them down to order. We had breakfast in the restaurant. It was very expensive. They have a buffet for $16. It did not have a lot on it. We ordered off the menu for $13 each. The food was very good. The waiter was excellent. The Congress Ave bridge next door is famous for the world's largest urban bat colony. There are up to 1.5 million bats there. The bats stay in crevasses under the bridge during the day. Every night at dusk from mid-March to early November they leave the bridge in a solid stream. There is a jogging trail between the lake and the hotel that you can use to walk to the bridge.

“Nice place, on the pricy side” Very nice luxury hotel. This is a huge, very nice, expensive place to stay. I only recommended if you have a car (even though you have to pay over $30 for parking), cause it is a little far for walking. Rooms were big, nice and comfy. And service was very good. The pool is nice but if they have an event you wont be allowed to use it (or even walk by for that matter) The place stills holds plenty of parties and important events so you might spots celebrities and important people. I have no complains of this place cause I got it for 100 on priceline, but I would never pay their >$300 rate to stay here again. I just don’t get why you stay at a comfort or holyday in for $80 bucks and get breakfast, wifi, free parking and movies, and on a $300 one you have to pay $14 for room internet access, $50 for breakfast, $35 for valet and $15 to catch a movie. Lol. They had no vending machines in the floors and the minibar has that electronic system that if you touch something it is billed to you, so forget about bringing a bottle of water to cool in the fridge. Again, don’t get me wrong, this place is super nice and service was great, but for that kind of money and such little extras, I would go elsewhere (if i had to pay full rate).

“The day the earth stood still” I frequently stay at this hotel because my company puts me up here. The front desk is either outstanding or terrible. There is no between. You will know it the minute you walk up to them. In addition, the location is odd. When you look out it is as if the earth stood still. There are empty parking lots and empty parking stuctures from where the old airport was located. You feel like the last man on earth. Also, some of the rooms do not have a window that looks outside but rather a window that looks into the atrium. This can be very noisy if there is a function going on. Please ask when you check in whether your room is an inside atrium room or an exterior room. It makes a big difference if you want to sleep

“Great value: A 3-star hotel with 4-star service” I stayed here for 4 nights. Service was great -- the hotel's staff was always very helpful. Free wireless internet with computers to use and a 24 hr gym were also pluses. A simple continental breakfast of pastries, toast, and cereal was also provided free of charge. It's a 3-star room with the basic amenities --honestly, it's not the Westin. But it's a very good deal for Phillie, which has a hotel tax of almost 15%. (My $150 room had an added $20 tax, I shudder what the final bill of the 4-star and 5-star hotels would be.) So the tax can really add up, and if you're on a budget or not on an expense account, then stay here, because it's very good value, and pretty darn good.

“nice hotel” this is a very nice hotel, with great bay views. It is very spread out, 2 towers so you may walk a ways for parking. Rooms are average size, but the views are nice. The bar at the top of the hotel is always packed and have bay views also. This place is close to convention center and gas lamp/downtown area. good location.

“Great New Hilton Rooms, but needs work on the service” I like the Hilton brand hotels and stay frequently. Booked the brand new HGI Inner Harbor for a weekend family getaway. I was delighted but disappointed all in the same trip. The pros - the hotel is brand new and the location is fabulous - close to all inner harbor attractions. Since the hotel is new, it is very very clean (spotless actually) and the rooms are modern and cozy. They are a little small, but I find that common with any big city hotel. But overall, I was satisified w/ the accomodations. We had a room on the 12th floor (top floor) with a nice view of the inner harbor. The odd # rooms face towards the harbor/city. The cons are that because the hotel was new, I think the staff was too. Service can use a Hilton make over. Check in was very slow. The clerk seemed genuinely unwelcoming and uninterested that I chose his hotel to stay in. He provided no information and barely made eye contact. The hotel is co-located w/ the Homewood Suites by Hilton so be careful to go to the correct desk & elevators. Homewood clerks had no action but stood at their stations staring at 6 of us in line to check in to the HGI without offering any of us assistance. When I got to my room the card keys didn't work and my wife had to keep my three small children out in the hall while I went back down to rectify the problem. I barely got an apology and was told I probably put them next to my cell phone (meanwhile my cell was in my bag on the baggage cart so it was impossible for that to have happened). I told the guy that wasn't the case and he just handed me my keys and said "here you go." Not Hilton-esque service! After we got settled, we attempted to order room service but the book in the room didn't have a menu. We called to ask for one and I actually had to go down to the restaurant to go get one (that's what the staff suggested when I called). They said they hadn't gotten the in-room menus yet. No offer to bring one up to us. To access the pool, you need a separate pass to the health club (non Hilton facility in the same building, but guests can get in with a pass and photo ID ). Ask at check in b/c they don't tell you about it when you do check in. Also, you should inquire about parking so you can get an in/out access card - again you aren't told by the staff, you have to ask for everyting. It's $25 but that is actually a bargain for the area especially with in/out priveleges. Main attractions are in walking distance anyway. Ate breakfast at the Great American grill. Food was good but very slow at the counter - they cook to order eggs, pancakes, etc.. There was a wedding party so that may have contributed. Restaturant staff was friendly and helpful, but again, you could tell the hotel was new in operation and all parts weren't moving in the same directions quite yet. We walked by the General Manager's office on the way out and he looked up with a mean grimmace. Not even a good morning or anything. Not so friendly like I'm used to at other Hiltons. Overall, I was pleased with the room, the cleanliness, and the location. The level of service needs to be improved for me to consider it of Hilton quality. I would call my stay an "Ok" experience and I would consider it again after the staff was properly trained and had some experience under there belt.

“Best Choice and Value in Houston for a weekend getaway” My wife and I stay here often as a getaway from San Antonio. While it is an older hotel, you will find the rooms decor to be up to date. Service is impeccable. The food can be pricy, but it is always good. The great thing is that you are close to the Galleria and numerous restaurants. The best part is the pool area. They have one pool for kids and another for adults. Recommend going down early and securing one the lounges with umbrellas...limited number. It very relaxing and quite. They have a grill and bar and the far end for your convienence. Valet parking is $26 a night. If you do not mind walking 5 minutes, you can park for free around the corner in the garage. If you need a car, try budget, Avis or dollar...one of the three usually has some deal in Houston. This hotel is highly recommended.

“Perfect stay in Seattle at Pioneer Square” I stayed in the Pioneer Square Hotel for 5 nights last week. When i arrived, i was warmly greeted by "Randy" who could not do enough to welcome me. He was so pleasant, it was a great first impression. I stayed on the 2nd Floor towards the back of the hotel. The room was very spacious and had all the amenities you would expect from a really good hotel, flat screen tv, iron, free wi-fi, coffee maker, desk and a very comfortable king bed. Maid service was good, and although i can be messy, the room was as good as new every time i came back after a day out around Seattle. The free continental breakfast was great also, and filled me up for the rest of the day. Particularly, the waffle making machine meant i could have a tasty hot waffle and maple syrup every morning, FAB. Location wise, you cannot get much better. It is close to funky jazz clubs, bars and restaurants. It is also really close to the waterfront and harbour cruises. There is also a bar next door and an Italian restaurant on the corner. It is also close to the baseball and football fields. I went to see the Seattle Mariners and had a great night with only a short walk back. Great hotel for the price. So glad i booked this hotel instead of splashing out double the price on something which could not deliver any more. Great place to see Seattle from.

“Great for business” The Intercontinental provides modern rooms in a great location. If you can stay here at a corporate/reduced rate, I highly recommend you try it. The rooms are very large with huge bathrooms. My suite had a large whirlpool tub, flat screen TV, and a great view of the water. I also recommend the restaurant - it's a bit pricey but the fresh seafood dishes are worth every dollar on your corporate card. It is also easy to get to from the train station.

“Excellent, Friendly Service” Had family fly in for a weekend recently and I reserved two rooms at the Hilton New York for them. When they checked in the front desk staff was extremely professional and friendly. I am an Hilton honors Diamond member and I chose the option to have an upgrade to a suite if available. To my surprise the one room I needed upgraded was. The entire staff is professional and friendly, the rooms are much larger than your average New York hotel room. The amenities are modern, as are the rooms. The executive lounge is on the 44th floor, for you to see Central Park and enjoy a snack or drink. The location is excellent, it is only a couple blocks from Central Park and half a block from the 7th & 53rd subway stop, you can get the E train there. It is several blocks from the theater district, it is only a 10 minute walk. If you plan to visit New York, this is one of the few hotels I would recommend. If you are a fan of Halal food, right on 53rd is the Halal guys carts, just right outside the hotel. The Hilton is located on the avenue of Americas, far enough away from Times Square yet you know you are in New York. My family enjoyed it, my Nephew ate duck for the very first time, at the executive lounge. They will be staying here again when they return to visit.

“Convenient but not ideal location” The Hilton is definitely convenient to Times Square and the BART, but first-time visitors need to be aware it's very close to the Tenderloin. Once you're oriented, you'll find it's a short stroll to the Square or to Moscone or even down Market to the Ferry Building. The hotel itself is a pretty standard convention hotel. Some of the rooms with the nicest views are very tiny, but it is wonderful to wake up to a view of the Golden Gate or the Bay Bridge. Because of its size and the number of conventions at either the hotel or at Moscone, the hotel undergoes frequent renovations. It appears the hotel is finally redoing the section that used to hold a variety of shops and restaurants. Be sure to ask where the noise of renovations will be lowest when you select a room.

“We liked our stay at the Blakley.” THe Blakley was nice. Good midtown location. Room was adequate size. not big..but that is NY. Great location to take a walk in Central Park each morning. Breakfast that came with the room was good. Great location to walk all over. Room was clean. Bathroom was nice but small...but once again that is NY. They have a small gym that is open 24 hours a day and that was nice. The restaurant that is attached to the hotel is quite good. Expensive but worth it.

“Comfortable Hotel with Great Service” The MGM Grand Hotel is a relatively new property and replaces the old MGM casino that was in downtown Detroit for many years. Its style is more modern/fashionable than traditional. My room was large, comfortable, and had huge windows with a great view of the Ambassador Bridge and the Canadian side of the river. The room was clean, but one of the towels in the bathroom still had a large amount of makeup (I assume) from a prior guest. The concierge club on my floor had the best selection of evening snacks I've seen in a club, but the breakfast was largely a continental breakfast without the hot selections found in some other chains. Because it is connected to a large casino, there is ample free parking, but you either need to walk along the outside of the building or through the smoke filled casino to go from the self-parking garage to the hotel. Valet parking is also an option but I don't know if it is free. There are a number of great restaurants on the property as well as the standard buffet, but because they are all inside the casino rather than the hotel, you have to deal with a lot of cigarette smoke to reach any of them. Unlike the Las Vegas hotels, the ventilation system here does not do a very good job of letting you breath while inside the casino. I have noticed that each time I have visited this casino. The hotel is in downtown Detroit, but is a few blocks away from Ford Field, Comerica Park, Cobo Center, and the office buildings in the central business district.

“Perfect location. Service could use improvements.” Unfortunately I feel the best Affinia Chicago has going is its location. Steps away from Magnificent Mile. Hancock Observatory and Millennium Park are within walking distance. Lincoln Park Zoo and Navy Pier are a short bus ride away. Everything is at your doorstep whether it's ATM's, convenient stores, restaurants and shops. Gino's East, famous for their deep dish pizza is right next door. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Housekeepers were friendly and always says hello. Front Desk staffs were inconsistent with service as I encountered. Sometimes helpful, uninterested and unaccommodating. Had a little incident where they made me feel like they wont let me check in unless I fix this problem myself when they could have been a little more accommodating. I was in shock and disbelief. This is my second stay at two different Affinia Hotels and had a similar problem with Front Desk staffs. So that led me to believe it's not my problem, but perhaps their policies? Would I stay here again? I probably would just because of its location. But if you're the manager is that the sale pitch you want to give to your customer, "we offer bad service, but perfectly located?"

“Downtown Denver” Spent two nights at the Grand Hyatt when I was in Denver for work. Likes: - Corporate rate was $149 - which is a good value for downtown Denver. - Room on the 24th floor. - Location - 1-1/2 blocks from 16th Street Mall - Hotel restaurant - Pub 17 Dislikes: - $10 day for internet - Room keys were a bit finicky - Expected a little more from GRAND Hyatt ... this was more like a GOOD Hyatt

“Mostly happy with the LES” I've stayed at the Thompson LES a few times in the past three months.
