My colleague and I get a double deluxe room which is not that large or deluxe, but for NYC, it is fine. The rooms are very spartan, but comfortable. The last time we were there, a few items in our room didn't work great- the faucets and shower were quirky (Like having a really hard time getting full water flow in the shower, only hot water coming out of the bathroom faucet) and some signs of wear were evident in the bathroom/grout and ceiling. I always choke when paying over $300 a night for a hotel with rooms this small and spare, but comparatively to other hotels in Manhattan, this is a good value. I love the location, right across from the LES subway stop and in the heart of a great neighborhood. The staff is generally helpful and friendly. The restaurants are definitely overpriced but the food is good.

“Poor housekeeping...and watch the mini bar” This hotel is OK if you can get a good discount but not if you pay the rack rate. The location is excellent if you like the seedy fringe of Soho next to China Town (which I do), but not if you need to be in mid town for an early meeting or are nervous about the dingier parts of Manhattan. The rooms are small and comfortable but the housekeeping is consistently poor. The lobby and hallways are grimy and in need of refurbishment. On a recent stay the cleaner removed the soap and the toilet paper and two light bulbs, and did not replace them. On another occasion, the television remote control was missing and a replacement never arrived. After my last stay there mini bar charges were incorrecttly added to my credit card one week after I had left. I never use hotel mini bars but when I contacted the hotel they refused to reverse the charges and I eventually gave up trying to do anything about them.

“Top Notch all around” I was assigned the St. Francis by the conference that I attended. Back, when we lived in the Bay Area, my Mom and I used to shop, and then lunch at the Oak Room. Those were the days. We arrived a bit after noon, and were checked in quickly and given our room early. Painless considering there were 90,000 other conference attendees. There are two parts to the hotel. The older, character filled part, and the tower. I stayed in the tower. The room was very large, with two queen beds, a desk, an enormous bathroom and a two door closet, complete with iron, ironing board and safe. Also, a decent number of hangers. The bed was comfortable. A feather mattress top, then sheets, then a light coverlet wrapped in sheets and a HEAVY comforter on top of that. No reason to be too hot or too cold with those options. I like a firm bed, the mattress was firm enough not to cause back pain, and those who like cushion will appreciate the fluffy aspects. The Internet connection was included in my rate; it was lightening fast and I could use up to 3 different devices per day on it. The television had plenty of cable chanels, so when jet lag kicked in, I had a good choice of what to watch. Our room was quiet. I never heard doors in the hall slam or city traffic. There were a couple of sirens, but honestly, dead quiet. The shower had that freeze or fry thing going where the water temperature is inconsistent, but the pressure was nice and strong! There are two shower-heads. I'm not sure what the benefit of that is, but it was a great shower. The toilet was the loudest in North America. The soaps were yummy smelling. The towels fluffy and absorbent. The in-room coffee is a single cup drip maker, with Starbucks. A few extra $$ to the chambermaid kept us loaded up on coffee and mini-moos. There's a mini-bar fridge in the room. We were able to balance small leftovers in it, although they'll send an empty fridge up if you want one. Lots of space to spread out in the bathrom with an enormous countertop, as well as shelves to store your trial-sized whatnots. The elevator system is fast and modern (in this part of the hotel.) Some places nearby to eat include: Burger Bar, Hubert Keller's burger restaurant in Macy's. Tian Sing on Cyril Magnin St has Shanghai (soup) dumplings and Peking duck. Colibri Mexican Bistro is a block and a half away on Geary and I had an excellent Mexican meal there. More mole than frijoles, so upscale. Caruso's in the lobby was a great place to get a little breakfast before starting my day. I was pleasantly surprised by the St. Francis. It's nice to see that my old friend is aging well. We had room 996 with two queen beds in it.

“Very Nice Room” I stayed at the Carlton from December 27-29, 2004. As mentioned in other reviews, the hotel is currently undergoing renovation. There really is not much of a lobby at this point in the renovation and what little space the hotel has for a lobby is very crowded. That should change when the renovations are completed in 2005. I stayed in room 715, which was fantastic. The room was exactly as pictured on the hotel web site and very clean. I was especially impressed by the large size of the room---huge by NYC standards. The bathroom was small, but more than adequate for one person at a time. The high end bed linens and toiletries were a great touch and the bed was very comfortable. The room had a view of the Empire State Building and was ideally situated in midtown. I will seriously consider staying at the Carlton again during future trips to NYC.

“Sehr gute Ausstattung, schöner Blick auf die Stadt” Das Hotel ist ziemlich neu, die technischen Einrichtungen sind auf dem neuesten Stand. Das Schwimmbad in der 5.Etage ist ziemlich schmal. Mein Zimmer lag im 16. Stock und hatte einen wunderbaren Blick auf die Skyline von Boston. Das Zimmer war komplett eingerichtet mit Kühlschrank, Kaffeemaschine, Fernseher, Bügeleisen und Bügelbrett. Beim Frühstück kann man wählen zwischen kaltem und warmem Buffet zu unterschiedlichen Preisen oder auch à la carte essen. Im Erdegeschoss stehen zwei PC's mit Internet Zugang. Das Hotelpersonal ist sehr hilfsbereit.

“Good hotel for a very good price” Stayed at the Comfort Inn in January for three nights. We had 2 rooms with a connecting door. -Check-In: Very friendly and efficient. -rooms: Clean and comfortable with free highspeed internet (wifi) and flatscreen tv. Rooms had coffee maker, hairdryer, telephone, alarm clock and big enough safe for a laptop. Beds were very comfortable. -bathroom: good shower but no storage possibility for shower gel in the shower. One room had a window wich was nice. -Service: Free internet and computers with printer in the lobby, free luggage storage after check out, vending machines in lobby. -breakfast: Standard (but free) american breakfast (pastries, bagels, toast, waffles and fruit, coffee, tea and juice). breakfast area quite small, but there is an extra room with tables. location: chinatown begins right at the doorstep, walking distance to the LES and Soho. Next Subway 3 minutes walk, very convenient for JFK by Taxi. Area is quite secluded after dark, but never felt unsafe. All in all, nice hotel for a very good price. Would stay there again.

“Decent...Remote Area” It's my first day here and so far so good. I basically just needed a place to lay my head. It was easy to get downtown on the bus (#56) but it took awhile for it to come (something I'm finding common with southern bus systems). The lobby is cute, the room is boring looking and there were a few things I photographed that weren't on point (i.e. tile missing on bathroom floor, only one washcloth etc.). It was 'hella cold' in the hallway but I blasted the heat as soon as I hit my room. I would rather have stayed at a hotel on Main as I did before but this is ok at the last minute.

“Great Location - OK Hotel” I got a terrific Hotwire price for this property. for the price I paid, it was worth it. Had I paid the published rate on the E.S. website I may have been dissapointed. The location is perfect. You can walk to most anything in Center City. Parking fees are expected, it's a downtown city hotel. The furnishing in the rooms are kind of tired. My bed was OK. There were plenty of pillows on my King but none of them were good. Evening reception was fine. We ate dinner at Con Murphy's Pub on the corner of 17th, it was very good (we can eat at TGIFriday's anywhere). Breakfast was included. Typical E.S. buffet. Lots of choices. We were there when they opened at 6:30 so seating was not an issue. Overall it's a decent property, it was clean. It would also be great for families because the rooms are large. Free high speed internet in rooms would be a huge plus.

“Dream Hotel - needs a couple of things to rate higher” Nice looking building from the outside with a good location at 55th Street West and 7th Avenue - close to Times Square, Central Park and a number of subway lines. The lobby is quite attractive with a fish aquarium from floor to ceiling, statues with a sitting area and a small stylish check-in desk - staff were friendly and efficient. There are a number of elevators - all on the small side but typical for older NYC buildings. I had booked a larger room - appx 285 square feet - the standard rooms are 185 sqaure feet and come with a smaller bed. There was decent closet space and a sizeable bathroom that was well designed with many mirrors, bathtub/shower combination with good water pressure and temperature, great lighting and good storage space. The room was clean and had a neat blue neon type underlighting that gave the room a nice ambient feeling and had great lighting with lamps over the bed, halogens with dimmer in the ceiling and accent lights. For improvements and to rank higher in my opinion, the rooms need some upgrade treatments: * The chairs in the room were not comfortable to sit in and read - a nice reading chair would be good for a room in a hotel of this calibre * The bed was a mattress sitting on a wood frame - it was reasonably comfortable but would have been better with a boxspring/foundation underneath * The windows could use more upgraded sound proofing - I have stayed in NYC before so I do have an idea of amount of noise to expect, however I was on a bit of a loud street and close to it (was on 2nd floor facing onto 55th) and believe that the windows would benefit from more soundproofing * The clothes dresser was or functioned as if it was a cheaper design - the drawers stuck and the piece screamed lower quality (again for a hotel this calibre, I expected better) All in all the stay was decent and it is a good hotel - if the above areas were improved, my rating would be above average.

“Just okay- rooms could use a fresh coat of paint” It was fine. Glossy lobby and pool deck areas. Rooms probably were great when they were built, but they have definitely seen better days. Bathroom door swipes the toilet...the bathroom is that small.

“New Hotel, Great for a pre-marathon sleep” Four of us stayed at this very nice brand new hotel for two nights while we were in Jacksonville for the marathon. The location had easy access to buses for the race. The rooms were very nice with brand new everything. The beds were very comfortable with hard and soft pillows to choose from. The free wireless internet was easy to use and I used the business center to print out my boarding pass for our flight the next day. The bathroom was very nice with a shower that had excellent water pressure. The room also had a nice large LCD TV and good temperature control. The only 2 negatives were that the hot tub was not working or heated while we were there and they did not have free breakfast. Instead they had a new contemporary bar and restaurant which we never saw anyone in. Then again there were very few people staying at the brand new location yet.

“A wonderfully comfortable hotel” I recently stayed at the Hotel Nine Zero as a part of my company holiday party. My firm usually puts its employees up in a hotel nearby so that we can all enjoy ourselves to the fullest extent without worrying about getting home after a long night of partying. I chose Hotel Nine Zero and I must say that I was definitely not disappointed. All of the staff that I encountered, whether at check-in, valet, or even passing house-keeping in the hallways, were beyond pleasant and unbelievably helpful. Accomodating the guests needs is at the top of the priority list and it shows. My room was gorgeous, comfortable and chic. I had a corner room with a beautiful night time view of the Park Street Church and the Boston Commons. I have to tell you as a Bostonian, born and raised in the city, waking up in the middle of downtown Boston was great. Being as a I know where everything is located, I must tell you that as an out-of-town visitor the location cannot be beat. I thought to myself upon checking out that it must be wonderful for tourists to wake up and be right in the center of everything and have access to so many Boston local attractions. I had a more than wonderful stay and even though I live in Boston, I am already planning a night out back at Hotel Nine Zero.

“My first pick when going to SF” I have stayed here twice in the past year and love this hotel. The central location is fantastic and you can always find good rates here. My first stay was December 2006 for my birthday celebration and it was wonderful to see it all decorated up. My most recent stay was June 2007 for the Builders Convention and it was just as comfortable. The beds are so comfy and cozy. The bathrooms are nice and remodeled. In the double/double room it was much larger than in the one double bed room. But everything in the bathroom worked well and the shower water pressure and heat was great. The amenities were nice, too. The bedroom was a tad small, but adequate for one person. The front desk staff aren't overly friendly but they are also very busy. Room service was good and the speed was ok, not fast but not as slow as I've had before. One night during the convention we had drinks in the hotel lobby sports bar and that was ok, drinks weren't super strong and they were a bit pricey but you did get some tasty snack mix. I will stay here again, just for the comfort of the beds, the ideal location to Union Square, and the fact that if you search you can find excellent rates.

“Get it at a cheap rate” 3 night stay with a King suite for $115 a night through their website, of course the wretched taxes are never included in the bargain prepaid rate. Needed the sofabed for one of our children for one night. Just like the last time we were there, two bath towels, two hand towels. Had to request extra towels twice - once before we left for the evening and again when we returned three hours later. Next day after housekeeping came we were back to two towels. Every other hotel I've stayed at always provides more than 2 sets. It's a minor irritation. Room was clean, quiet, comfortable bed, no problems with water pressure in the shower. Wet bar with fridge and coffee maker. Small FREE bottles of water instead of the usual $5.00 rip off. Parking is $7/day with in/out privileges. Used the fitness centre, again two of everything - 2 ellipticals, 2 treadmills, 2 bikes. The indoor heated pool is small so go early when not many people are in there. The hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful. Didn't eat in the hotel as we were not impressed by the quality, price or service last time we stayed there. Hook up for Internet access $10.00/day and it was fast, free wireless in the lobby. My previous stay in Philly in March was in a downtown hotel and it was less than ideal - noisy and expensive. At least if you get a good rate, the Sheraton is a much better deal.

“Often a two, sometimes a four, thus the three” Blah. We stayed at the Clift a few years ago and really liked it, overlooking some problems (terrible bathrooms). But this time around -- boy oh boy, do things look dated. We were in town for a big conference and were staying four nights. Our first room was a bust. You could smell cigarette smoke in the lobby (on the ninth floor). Our room was tiny. The bathroom was TERRIBLE. You could barely turn around in it. The worst thing? You could hear the person flossing her teeth in the next room. While that is a slight exaggeration, the walls were paper thin and we could hear her phone conversations, her TV, her sighs. Not good and not great for four nights when we needed to be bright and chipper in the morning. Rating so far? One star. We politely complained and the assistant front desk manager was great. He promptly said we could change rooms and generously gave us a suite. Rating for service? Five stars. Good stuff: The king bed was very comfortable; good linens; great pillows; very quiet. YAY! The concierge staff was very helpful and kind. Oscar and Erica (?) were lovely and helped us find some nice restaurants. Front desk staff and door staff were pleasant but distant. They warmed up once you engaged them though. Bad stuff: The bathrooms are terrible. Tiny, depressing, this side of dirty (despite being cleaned -- they just look grungy). Liked the toiletries a lot and the shower pressure was great. Lovely thick towels. Only one robe. Grrrr. No fan so it got pretty foggy in there. The decor is starting to look dated as well -- lilac walls, Ikea-like desk, orange plastic cubes for tables. That's the problem with trendy hotels -- after awhile, their cutting edge decor looks very dull indeed. Other issues: I HATE paying for Wi-Fi, especially in tech cities like SF. Want some ice? Perhaps some wine glasses? Not provided. You have to call room service. Be prepared to wait. And they hover at the door for a tip for something that should've been provided either nearby or in the room in the first place. The bar is nice. But it's expensive and boy, are there a lot of hookers hanging around. Makes for some very interesting people-watching. Liked the security that made sure you were a guest if you wanted to access the hotel rooms. On our last night there was a fire alarm at 2 a.m. Not fun when you have a 4 a.m. wake-up call to catch a plane. Some drunken bozo (not a guest of the hotel) threw his jacket on the gas fire. The alarm went off and at first they told us to stay in our rooms. We opened the door and smelled smoke -- very acrid and strong up on the 10th floor. We evacuated. Can't say the staff was very helpful. Nobody to guide us out and there was confusion near the second floor (which was the right door). Nobody really gave us an all-clear when it was safe to return either. Not very impressive. I think this hotel should really conduct a thorough review of emergency procedures.
“BARTに直結” 良い点: BARTのCivic Center Stationの真上です。空港からはBART直行で29分。大変アクセスがよいです。 悪い点: フロントの能率が悪くがいつも混んでいます。 チェックインも午後3時前だとまず不可能です。

“This hotel makes a bad name for Hilton :(” Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights for an event and I was less than impressed to say the least. The hotel is located by the airport and with little things to do near by with the exception of a few fast food places. The hotel staff are not very acccomidating. I had booked my room 2 months in advance and had requested a fridge but was declined one at check in. There were no working ice machines anywhere on the 2nd floor and due to the strange shape of this hotel it would take 10 minutes just to get sw ice. Internet will cost you $15/day and I find this unacceptable in 2011. When you're paying $120+ nigt the Internet should be free. There was no WiFi in the conference area either:( The hotel restaurant is overpriced and the food is just ok. I'd eat elsewhere. If you need assistance the front desk staff lack any type of hospitality skills. I asked on arrival and my day of departure for a late check out (1.5 hours). I was given an extra 15 minutes or "additional chargers would take place". In conclusion, I would rate this hotel at a 3 star at the best and give it a 2/10 for value. Will not say here again.

“Plain, uninspired business hotel.” A lengthy line of people were checking in. Dirty carpet in the elevator lobby. Plain room in a contemporary design. Small Aveda toiletries. $14.95/day internet or free in the lobby. I had to whine to get a king bedded room rather than queen beds. Flat screen tv's but only analog service. Is it not 2011? Most of the pamphlets and the room service breakfast menu in the room are wrinkled and showing a lot of signs of wear. To prevent the next guest from having that experience I threw the worst offenders away so that the maid will know to put in fresh ones. I have seen much nicer Marriott's. All in all, to me it is a fairly pricey but very blah business hotel that caters to convention traffic. The restaurant and bar staff are ho hum, nice but again not very inspired. I stay in hotels way to often and this is one of the most boring I've been in this year. There's nothing really bad about it, but it certainly doesn't sparkle or shine like any other 4 star property. It's just overwhelmingly average. Last time I was here I stayed a block away at the Trump and for the money I'll gladly stay there again.

“Cosmopolitan Hotel - NYC” Hello fellow business travelers, If you're looking for a relatively inexpensive place to stay in the Financial District of NYC, this hotel is certainly great as far as price is concerned. Be forewarned, though, that the hotel is one of the oldest in NYC. It's obvious when you find out that all rooms are centrally controlled with no temperature gauges and the majority of the rooms DO NOT have AC controls. If you don't mind being in a hot, tiny, stuffy room, where the carpets on each floor smell like mildew, then this is the place to stay. The Reception desk on the main floor is also tiny, usually congested with line-ups of people (especially on Friday checkouts) and the ONE elevator (that holds a maximum of six people at a time) is completely unreliable. I ended up having to climb six very old flights of stairs on three out of my five days of stay. Although my room was comfortable and clean (after I ended up switching to a room with working AC), and the staff was as helpful as they could be, this is still a very OLD hotel - and that becomes quite obvious when you first see the hotel's front door entrance (you'd miss it if you really weren't paying attention). The lobby is also very drab (pale yellow) and could seriously use some artwork or color. If you're used to staying at the Marriott (like me) or other comparable hotels, spend the extra $100 and stay at a fully functional hotel. This one's great budget wise, but I'll probably never stay there again. On a positive note, there were no bed bugs! :-)

“Return was Good” I last stayed here before I started writing reviews for Tripadviser. I am happy to see it is still a good hotel. Check-in was welcoming, and I didn't even have to ask for a high floor, they gave me a room on the 15th, which was really comfortable, I relaxed in there for 3 hours before I went out again. The rate of $129 a night was a bargain for such a big-size room with a view, and free Internet. It was relatively quiet in my room and on my floor. Very relaxing. The bed was comfortable, especially the back rest. Only inconveniences and they were slight, was that the thermostat in the room was hard to control. Also, the location of the hotel was further from the Bart than I remembered, but once you get to the subway, it is a quick ride to the airport.

“Lucked out getting this hotel for a San Francisco conference” Was assigned to this hotel as the other conference hotels were full. While my room was clearly not the premium suite (a tiny bit worn, no view, low floor), this is very clearly a fantastic hotel. Not only did every member of the front desk who met me remember my name, but they really went out of their way to anticipate my needs (cabs, directions, refreshments, etc.). Room itself was spacious for SF - though my reading chair did not have an ottoman. King bed with Frette sheets (oh my goodness!) and a bathroom with jetted tub, separate shower, and enough travertine tile to satisfy anyone. And did I mention Molton Brown soap, shampoos, etc.? Room was cleaned TWICE a day, with full turndown service each evening. Quiet, excellent for business travelers. I will absolutely return to this spot when I am back in SF. Note this is also smack in the middle of the shopping district, so easy walk to everything retail.

“Stylish, great staff, great location but one or two small flaws” New York was the first stop on a trip through 4 US cities. We've visited New York many times before and following positive reviews and plenty of searching we decided to stay at the Muse. The Muse is located just off Times Square. It's subjective but having stayed at other hotels around New York I prefer to stay close to the hustle and bustle of mid town Manhattan. This was perfect for the bars, restaurants and shopping of mid town and close to the metro to get to other New York attractions. Check in was easy and the small but attracive lobby was served by excellent and friendly staff (and at times an overpampered dog). In fact the staff were one fo the highlights of the hotel. Always friendly and helpful, at times they went out of their way for us. Our room was as we expected for a New York boutique, small but well fitted. A large flatscreen TV was equipped with a fantastic cable package which gave us access to more channels than we have at home and the bathroom was attractive and immaculate. The room was very well insulated, despite being so close to Times Square we heard no noise at all from there (well not strictly true we heard the controlled explosion from the failed bomb but that was an exceptional event). There was no view but then again this is New York. Unfortunately the room did have 2 flaws. Firstly the air conditioning although efficient when on was as noisy as a jet engine. It was impossible to sleep with it on. We stayed at 4 hotels on this trip all with airconditioning and this was the noisiest by far. In a city where it gets hot better air conditioning should be expected. Secondly the bed. It was large but clearly the mattress was old. A groove (more of a valley in fact) had been worn in one side of the bed whcih meant I felt quite separated from my wife. This made for a poor sleep experience at the hotel. Overall the staff and location made this a positive experience (and I'm sure it's helped by the fact that, as always, I enjoyed New York) so I gave the hotel a generous mark. I could easily have downgraded it to 3 stars because of the bed but who wants to sleep in New York anyway.

“Met or exceeded our expectations” We stayed at this hotel the first weekend of November 2004. Ditto all the positives from previous reviews. This is a very nice facility. I was impressed with the exercise room, decked out with new equipment and a plasma TV on the wall to watch while on the treadmill. Complimentary high-speed internet is in the room and they even provide a Cat 5 patch cord (don't take it with you unless you wish to part with $15). The LA Times was delivered to our room both days over the weekend (may be just for Marriott Rewards members, though, so join this free program and reap the benefits). I can't remember the last time I stayed in a hotel and recevied a complimentary newspaper on the weekend. There is a small convenience store across the side street to the west. It's a good place to pick up bottled water, snacks, and/or a six pack. Clean, quiet, comfortable - we would stay here again.

“Loved the Dumont” Great hotel - the front desk staff were great. Housekeeping brought the specialty pillows and extra towels within 5 minutes of request. Doorman opened doors (which isn't all that common in some hotels in the city!) and ran up to the corner to hail cabs for us! We loved this hotel - we arrived early and they just happened to have a room available. They let us check in early, with no extra charge and we luckily had a room on the top floor. The room was very big. I didn't even know that the room was going to have a kitchen! THe room and bathroom were clean and the soaps/shampoos were very nice. The temp of the room was fine and we found that we could easily control it. We didn't order room service although the menu had a good selection and very reasonable charges. It might have been cheaper to order room service than go out to eat - but then again we wanted to experience some of NYC's great restaurants. We never had to wait a long time for an elevator. They had a 24-hour fitness room and these free spa-kits you could use during your stay. In all, we loved this hotel and would definitely recommend it to anyone who can afford it. I wish I could stay here everytime we come to NYC.

“Nice Hotel” The Westin Market Street is a very nice 'upmarket' hotel in an excellent location in San Francisco - a quick walk to Union Square and public transport on Mraket Street to just about anywhere We ( family of 2 adults + 2 kids, 5 and 13) had a large, bright and very clean room - on the 7th floor I think - and the beds were wonderfully comfortable. Bathroom was a little dark, but spotless and we had a bath , which was nice for the little one. Check-in was smooth and the girl at the desk who dealt with us was extremely pleasant, as were all of the staff we met there, including in the restaurant. This was a pleasant surprise given some of the remarks made on this site. We didn't have breakfast at the hotel - Starbucks is just up the street if all you want is a coffee and pastry- but we did have a very good , if rather expensive, meal at "Ducca". My only complaint would be that our room was right next to the service elevators that rumbled noisily up and down late at night and early in the morning. I presume that our room allocation was due to the fact that we had got an absolutely fantastic rate on Expedia, which I imagine gives the hotel some scope to allocate better -placed rooms to those paying the full whack. All in all our stay was very pleasant, and if we're ever back in SF ( it's a long way from France!) and get a similar deal, then I'd stay there again.

“Excellent location, value, experience in unique neighborhood” If you are looking to experience New York City without the bustle and chaos of Times Square (and the more expensive hotels), you should consider the Sohotel. The location is great! It is a one-minute walk to all the great restaurants in Little Italy (and Lombardi's Pizza!), and just around the corner from Canal Street. You feel like you are in a neighborhood rather than a crowded major city. The decor of the hotel is trendy, warm, and inviting (think exposed brick and zebra-striped couches in the lobby). While the rooms and bathrooms are not very big, the beds are extremely comfortable and there are nice TVs on the walls. Internet is available in some rooms and in the lobby, where you can also watch TV on a on a huge screen while you check your email. Even though there are no elevators, the staff is extremely helpful and carries your bags up to your room. I have stayed at many hotels in Times Square before, and staying at the Sohotel was one of the most relaxing experiences I have had in the city.

“THIS HOTEL REALLY NEEDS AN UPDATE AS THE FURNITURE AND CARPET IS OLD AND REALLY NEEDS TO BE REPLACED” ARRIVAL: Taxi from the airport to hotel approximately US$47. SECURITY: Good security as you have to use your key card to go to your floor level. There were large in room safes - big enough to accommodate a laptop. ROOMS: Rooms really needed an update as the furniture was at least 40 years old and the carpet was very old and not up to the Crown Plaza standard. We had a balcony suite but the door had no latch so you could not lock it. There was no outdoor furniture on the balcony and the balcony area was grubby with a bare concrete floor (untiled) which needed a really good clean up and you could not sit out there because there was nowhere to sit. The fridge did not work properly as any milk or water you placed in there became frozen solid. The coffee machine in the room did not work - we reported it to housekeeping but nothing was done to fix anything. At $320 per night including taxes and breakfast we expected better as the suite was very dated and needed new carpet and furniture. BREAKFAST: Approximately US$11 per person for the buffett breakfast which consisted of cereal, fruit, scrambled eggs, sausages, bacon, bread/buns and tea/coffee. Probably the same as you would expect at a Holiday Inn Express so not that exciting but the price was right if you do not have breakfast included. INTERNET: Good in room WiFi connection and no problems connecting. CLUB ROOM/FLOOR: There is no Club Room at this hotel but every Wednesday night they have alcoholic welcome drinks and snacks for Priority Club members from 5pm to 7pm. POSITION: Good position and about a 15 minute walk to the 6th Floor Book Depository JFK tour. Good selection of restaurants are within walking distance to the hotel. There is a CVS supermarket just behind the hotel that has a good selection of food products including wine by the bottle at good prices. They do not sell any fresh fruit. A free hotel shuttle van is available for guests to go to shopping or restaurants within a 3 mile radius. TOURS: There are really no tour operators and you really have to arrange your own sightseeing which is a little difficult if you do not have a vehicle. Forth Worth is definitely worth the trip - you can walk to Union Station (about 20 minutes from the hotel) or take the hotel free shuttle and catch the train to Fort Worth Stockyards (about $10 for a day pass that will include most bus trips). Train trip is about 1 hour. When you arrive at Fort Worth you can take a free loop trip around town and include Sundance Square on Molly the Trolly - many choices to have lunch. The trolly will take you back to the rail station where you can catch a bus to The Stockyards which is a very quaint and unique area to spend a few hours wandering around the many shops/restaurants and visiting some of the museums unique to the area. Really enjoyed Fort Worth and the Stockyards except for the heat as the temperature was about 110F.

“Very nice hotel...” My husband had to stay at this hotel for business reasons so he brought us with him. The hotel was extremely clean. EXTREMELY huge! We had two queen beds and there was a couch with desk in a sorta mini room. The negative was that they didn't have internet service when we stayed there. They have a pool that is partly inside and partly outside. It was great. If rained we had a pool, if it was hot, we had a pool. The staff was very friendly and helpful. One negative was that the options on tv were plain old cable. With three children to entertain until my husband got back it would have been helpful if they had Animal Planet! A good hotel in all though!

“The best,Amazing” The best,amazing and very beautiful.Great family motel you'll love it.So much to do and so warming and comfortable.Room Service is amazing great attitudes try this place out you'll enjoy it,I promise.

“Nice, small hotel in great location” Were in Boston with hubby and son for son's orientation at Boston University. The Courtyard Copley Square is a bit cheaper and on a much quieter street than the Marriott which is a block away . Check in was a breeze, everyone working at the desk were great. We were in room 909 which had a living area with sleep sofa (we opted for a large cot as opposed to small, which is available on a first come first serve basis but decidedly more comfortable than sofa), coffee table, fridge and a couple of chairs and a TV that could be closed off with a door from the bedroom which contained two queen beds, large desk area and a comfortable chair. Bathroom was adequate and clean. the view was across some rooftop gardens which was pleasant and the street was quiet. Our stay was 2 nights and on the first there was a free Sam Adams beer tasting with cheese and crackers in the lobby. Nice touch. Our breakfast was not included. If you choose the Courtyard and need a cot, request it when you reserve and mention it again when you check in. We will be staying here again for family weekend in October.

“Attentive staff, but hotel needs renovation” Very responsive staff, but this hotel needs maintenance and renovation to remain competitive. Our room was spacious and clearly had once been beautiful but now shows wear. Maintenance responded quickly to a toilet that wouldn't flush, but the problem recurred (fortunately our stay was short). Location is no longer central as Harbor East has developed - the Renaissance, the Marriott Waterfront and future Four Seasons are all probably better situated now.

“Location, location, and well, it's a Hampton Inn” My wife and I stayed for nine nights at this Hampton Inn for a combination of meetings. We made reservations and had several conversations with a very pleasant employee regarding our desire to get either connecting rooms or at least rooms next to each other for a portion of the stay in which friends would also be there. We arrived at 3:00 for check in and were told that check-in was at 4:00. No problem with that, but the clerk claimed no knowledge of our previous arrangements and promised only to try to get both rooms on the same floor. We finally got into our room at 5:00 and did succeed in gettting a room close to our friends. My wife and I are both Hilton Honors Gold members, so we had hoped for more than the room next to the ice machine that we received. Well, off to a bad start, but the week generally went fine. The hotel's location near the Convention Center and Metro was a plus. The breakfast was standard fare, although they did vary the offerings a bit from day to day. The room had the standard Hampton Inn amenities, which are pretty good (small refrigerator, microwave oven). The business center has four computers, although we found that several of them stayed busy with children playing games. In general, the hotel lived up to expectations despite our somewhat strained arrival.

“Mostly Excellent” I was concerned when I read many of the reviews. However, we had stayed in this hotel a few years ago and liked it very much. Also, at $199 for a high floor with a water view, the price was better than most other quality Seattle hotels I had looked at. I heeded the advice in other reviews and asked for a high room facing the water and away from the elevators. Overall, we were very pleased. The check-in staff was extremely helpful. So was the concierge. The housekeeping staff was also very helpful but not too intrusive. Our room on the 41st floor had an amazing view of downtown Seattle, the Space Needle, and the Puget Sound. It was especially beautiful at sunset. The windows are panoramic. The decor is contemporary and did not seem worn. The rooms were a little worn, but nothing to complain about. The bed was very comfortable with nice pillows and the two-headed shower was fantastic. The location of the hotel is excellent. It is right across the street from Westlake Center. The monorail to Seattle Center runs from there. There is a lot of other shopping and restaurants in the area. I recommend Assagio, which is 1.5 blocks away. We went to the Seattle Opera and took a cab rather than the monorail. The fair was only about $7 and that included fighting the theater traffic. The hotel is very lively. The gift shop was well stocked, there was a nice display of glass & 2-d art in the lobby, and we never waited more than 30 seconds for an elevator. The only negatives: 1) The walls are extremely thin. The door that could potentially adjoin our room with the next room had a one inch gap at the bottom. Due to the gap & the thin walls, we could hear just about everything our neighbors said. The lack of privacy caused us to whisper at all times. 2) At 4:30am on Sunday morning, the fire alarm went off. Being on the 41st floor, and with visions of 9/11, we didn't take any chances and ran for it. At the 15th floor, we ran into a lot of other guests and a hotel staff person who told us it was a false alarm. Since the elevators were not working yet, we walked down to the lobby and then caught the elevator back up. Apparantly, it was a practical joke, probably pulled on the hotel as part of the football playoff festivities (Seahawks v. Panthers) that weekend. I can't blame the hotel, as this was out of their control. However, I was disappointed that there was no memo to the guests or other appologies given how disruptive the event was. If you can handle the thin walls, the location and incredible view make this a worthy place to stay.

“Great Hotel” My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco for a week-end get away to enjoy the museums in DC. The hotel is in an excellent location, being very close anything and everything there is to do in Washington. After reading recommendations from fellow travelers, we requested a room on the upper floors. We were give a room on the second floor, unfortunately at the beginning of the hallway and very close to the elevator. The only negative about our room and/or stay was the noise in the nighttime when people were returning to their rooms. There must not be much insulation within the doors. Otherwise, the hotel was quite wonderful and would definately recommend to to fellow travelers. A nice italian restaurant in Dupont Circle is Othello's, where the food is excellent with a good wine selection.

“Great location with Free Shuttle to get you around!” I was attending a conference for 5 days at the Fairmont Hotel which is 4 blocks away, and with such a long stay I wanted a fridge and more space, so the SpringHill Suites was a perfect choice at a more reasonable rate. Check In: I arrived at 1:00 AM from my flight and all I really wanted to do was get to bed. The front desk clerk was chatting with guests and I didn't even really pay attention. After getting her attention, she definitely took the time to explain the hotel and all of its amenities. Very friendly and helpful. Room: It was just like the picture - great king bed, spacious living room, mini kitchen, new shower head with great pressure, a spacious open closet are with suitcase holder, and I particularily love the couch set up to the computer desk - could put my feet up on the ottoman while working away at the desk. Wireless: Great and fast and I also used the hard wired too. Pool: Small and shaded with the way the building is set up and sun would shine in after 2:30pm Gym: For a SHS, it was impressive with a good selection of machines. Parking; I didn't drive, but the valet guys seemed friendly Shuttle: Awesome service!! They will take you within a 3 mile radius and you don't really even need a pre-booked appointment for short distances. Posted as Runs 7am - 7pm every 30 minutes, but really only runs until 6:15pm. Breakfast: I also booked this location vs. the Fairmont for the hot breakfast included, so the eggs were good, and you could make your waffles. Yummy. Nearby: CVS Pharmacy was a block away so great for picking up snacks and drinks to put in the fridge. The main bus transportation hub is 3 blocks away to get you anywhere you want to be. There was a small cluster of homeless people, but they were very friendly. One afternoon, I actually was approached by a really nice guy cause I obviously looked like i was searching for something and after realizing he lived on the street, I asked him for directions to the liquor store - Come on - who better to ask, right?! Anyways I also needed to get to a few places, so he showed me around the downtown and after 30 minutes I paid him $10 for the tour. So not that this has anything to do with SpringHill Suites, but the general area is pretty safe in my mind and all types of people of Dallas were friendly. I would recommend staying there again for the large rooms, great location and free shuttle on weekdays.

“all the comforts of home” Spent five nights in mid-November. A short drive from the car-rental agencies at the airport heading South. In a rural area - largely uninhabited, this resort is a surprise when first viewed. Well manicured grounds and an unoccupied guard station at the entry opens up to very pleasant condomium-like structures on your right as you proceed to the hotel office. There are two (timeshare/living) areas on your left, but they are away from the facilities used by the holiday visitor. Finding the hotel office was somewhat delayed when the main building encountered as you drive in turned out to be the golf-pro-shop and restaurant complex. The accomodations building is the structure on your right as the road dead-ends. The staff was pleasant and I was allowed to pickup my room key hours before the normal 4pm check-in time. There is a concierge in this building also. Given a non-smoking Suite with king-size bed. All utilities of a home to include a washer/dryer (stacked) were in the unit. Suggest getting a lower unit to avoid climbing the stairs to the 2nd floor rooms. All rooms have a patio or balcony. The swimming pool is heated year-around and, being divided into two sections, permits one to lap-swim - although in somewhat shallow water. The golf course has varying prices for 18-holes depending on the season and the time of day one tees off. There is a nice driving range ($15) where you can hit as many balls as you wish all day long. Freeways with access to all of Phoenix are close by: if you want to gamble, the Casino Arizona is about 15 minutes away by car. Downside - on my last night had a loud party next door that lasted way past midnight but I think the Security staff (ever vigilant) finally shut it down. There is a shopping center at Baseline/24th street a short drive away.

“One of my favorites” I hesitate to write this review as I prefer to keep some of my favorites to myself. However this is my senior contributor contribution... so here goes. I am in Chicago a lot, 12-14 times a year. The Monaco is a few short blocks to the loop and Miracle Mile/Michigan Ave so the location is superb. This is a boutique hotel and the front desk staff has always been friendly to me, no attitude here at all. Rooms are big by Chicago standards and the rooms are clean. Note the carpets in the room are clean. Housekeeping is "on the ball here" The decor is bizarre. Lots of conflicting colors in the room. Just don't wake up with a hangover and you'll be fine. Speaking of hangovers, you are next door (it connects) to the Southwater Kitchen. Do yourself a favor and get a seat at the bar and order the Cuban sandwich. It is made in front of you in their gas fired over behind the bar and it is made with pork belly. Wow, what great smells and you'll not go wrong with any other food items here, great restaurant for breakfast, lunch or dinner. Overall this is a great hotel for couples and for business travel. No complaints and I will be back
“nice new hotel” The Garden Inn brand has expanded a lot in NYC and this one is a good addition.

“Good Choice when flying into Charlotte Int'l Airport” This hotel is conveniently located near the Charlotte/Douglas International Airport. Van service is available from 4:30am to 2:00am. Nice rooms. Friendly Staff. Elevator. Breakfast is OK, but nothing special, and ends at 9:30am.

“ask if renovated yet” When we ended up unexpectedly in Memphis for one night, I checked my family into the Peabody, hoping for a safe, clean, attractive and enjoyable place for my family. The rate was high, with high parking fee on top of it, (and I discovered they added a small but annoying service fee which they failed to mention at check-in.) The room was pretty bad. Carpet was old, dirty and worn, bath room caulk was moldy, and a big chunk of plaster was sitting in the bathtub. The front desk explained they were under renovation on the upper floors and kind of laughed that the plaster was making its way through the duct system. The Peobody might be the grand old lady of the South, but not in the summer of 04. I'd stay somewhere else until the place gets renovated.

“Lobby is much more exciting than the rooms” I was excited to stay at the Liberty because the concept is really fun, and indeed it is. The lobby space is very unique, the bar and restaurants are good, and the free coffee service in the morning is great. The rooms are pretty forgettable- basic design, small bathroom, but certainly has everything you need. We stayed in the modern tower section. Also had a bad bad view of the side of a building- in fact we overlooked a big sign of the Mass Eye and Ear Hospital! Not too exciting! The front door service was excellent (yay for the valets).

“LOVELY HOTEL” This hotel was excellent. Nice room; very clean; nice furnishings; comfortable bed. We had the "bed and breakfast" package and the buffet breakfast was excellent. Service staff very accommodating. Nice pool area. Location is about 15 minutes from Riverwalk; an easy drive. Nothing much around otherwise, but two nice restaurants on the same property as the hotel. Only complaint would be the size of the bathroom. Really, really SMALL. When you stepped out of the shower/bath, you literally were on top of the toilet.

“Didn't get to stay here but I'll still leave a review! :)” My review will be a short as my stay. I had booked this hotel for a 1 night NYC stay in mid June 2012 waiting for my friends to come in the next day. Once I got there, the manager, Mr. Khan I believe it was, immediately met with me at the front desk. He informed me that there was some plumbing issues with some of the rooms and he gave me the option of continuing my stay there or at a sister property. I chose the sister property. Mr. Khan was very nice and helpful. He also helped pay for my cab ride to the sister hotel. I'm greatly appreciative of this nice gesture. So I pretty much only stayed in the lobby of the hotel for a few minutes and from what I saw, it was clean! ;) There was a small store next door and a police station(from what I heard read from prior reviews). I hope that next time I WILL get a chance to stay at this property to experience it throughly. Thanks again for letting me know of the issues.

“A surprisingly good experience” I see that the 'hotel class' is given as a 3* on Trip Advisor - not sure why because its much better than that. Was at a conference in the adjacent World Trade Center and spent 2 nights here in late April at the conference rate of $249 + all the wonderful taxes which get added to the bill in Boston - they seem to have one for every eventuality! It certainly was better than 3*. I'd have it down as a 4*+. Room was fine, shower good and facilities above average. Room was slightly small perhaps but everything worked and free wired internet (even though they told me it was wireless). The gym had lots of kit - probably too much as it was 'friendly' but, even though it was busy, there was always something available. Didn't use the pool but it was basically 3 swimming lanes - no nonsense. The in-room folder explained that they have a 'no tipping' rule and I can honestly say that the service was as good as anything I ever had in this class of hotel and there was no expectation of a tip - wonderful. The hotel has a coffee bar type place where you can get a basic breakfast without having to have all the sit down stuff. There is a 7-11 and a dunkin donuts across the road. I didn't use the hotel restaurants as there are a couple of bars just down the street. Yes its a bit of a walk (~15 mins) from the 'main' part of Boston but its well provisioned and I'd happily stay there again - especially if the conference was in that area.

“Hotel on the Skids” Sadly, this hotel has hit the skids. We had our wedding reception here 10 years ago so I hate to see this happening. For our wedding night, they gave us the Kabuki Suite, a two-story suite with a large living room upstairs. So for our 10th Anniversary in July, I called to ask for the Kabuki Suite again. She didn't see one with that name so she suggested I call the hotel directly to make sure we got exactly what we wanted on our special day. Unfortunately, the local person acted like they didn't know what I was talking about so I described it in detail. She gave some vague reassurance that we'd get what we wanted. When we got to the suite, it was tiny and absolutely not right. There were several stories at the front desk - that suite was being renovated, that suite was available for $1K per night (it cost $500 10 years ago and we've rented it since for $450) - none of which rang true. We cancelled our reservation immediately. They nearly ruined a very important day for us but we re-grouped and went to the Ritz Carlton, a much better hotel with exceptional service. Save yourself the disappointment with the Intercontinental.

“Excellent location for shopping & dining at the 'Summer Shack' across the street.” Check-in was very quick at the SPG counter. My room was missing a coffee maker (had all of the fixens) and it took 4 phone calls to get one (an hour and half later). Plus there were two used contacts on the floor when I arrived - - I do not wear contacts. This means that the floor was not vacuumed after the last tenant. But I do like this hotel and do recommend it and will stay there again (if the rate is good !). I don't know which tower I was in - - but those bathrooms were extremely small - two people cannot stand in it at the same time (unless one is in the tub/shower and the other is standing on the toilet !!! It is so small that when I would shave - - the doorknob kept hitting me in the back-side !!! But still - - it is a great hotel with a great location and I would not hesitate staying there again.

“Spectacular hotel, amazing experience” from the moment you are greeted by name at the lobby to the last second you drive out the grand drive, you will be pampered in a veritable lap of luxury. This hotel has few peers (the Ritz Carlton Naples may be one). This is a hotel that spared no expense in any public spaces, whose guest rooms are simply gorgeous, and whose staff are as attentive and friendly as any I have ever seen. My wife and I spent four days there, and were sad to depart from the exquisite pools, the stunning grounds and golf course, and fine food and friends we made there. Simply amazing.

“Not so Thrilled-With Carrying My Own Luggage in From Street” I was in town for BIO 2008 and booked the Bristol When I got in at app. 8PM the cab left me at the curb and the employes in the lobby stared at me. I walked up to the door and stuck my head in and the girl at counter said hi- but the two guys just stared. I could not believe it. Then I fumbled in with my luggage (no small feat) and went to check in. I clarified that I needed a room with a desk and was told all have rooms have them. Then I asked if it was safe to walk around and where could I find a convenience store. I was told how to go to Ralph's and then told it was safe as long as I didn't go right when I left the lobby. Hmmmm. I got to room and there was a small round top table with no chair by window and two beds. Called down and they said ok we will move you to the king you requested. Went to that room and it was again a table with no chair. I was exhausted-went to Ralph's and fell asleep. When I woke up I saw I was across the street from GREYHOUND bus station. Aha- perhaps that is why I was told not to go right when exiting. The room was almost cool to look at it until you looked close and noticed where things were not painted or finished. I was not happy overall and did not want a hassle. I had already moved a heavy arm chair and floor lamp (both were in an odd little alcove by themselves) to table to make it almost a workspace -not to mention 50+ lbs of luggage (still cannot figure out why those two young men were sitting around looking so bored and not helping anyone) and decided it was just time to leave. I made some quick calls and found a room at Hampton Inn by the harbor. Checked out and zipped over there. Glad I did. I love botique hotels but they have to be well run and service has to be great to make it work-the Bristol is neither of those things (I will say the young man who checked me out was pleasant)Too bad.

“Top Hotel” Sehr schönes Hotel, super Lage (Apple Store 1 Block entfernt). Große Zimmer - typisch für Courtyard. Großes Bad und sehr sauber. (Zimmer 01 sind ein bisschen kleiner, aber auch sehr ordentlich). bis zur Waterfront sind es ca. 20 Minuten zu Fuß. Hotel ist umgeben von verschiedenen Shopping Möglichkeite. Frühstück sehr Gut und mit $12 sehr fair für ein Hotel. Hotel liegt 2 Blocks von der SUbway entfernt (Grüne Linie). Common Park ca. 10 Minuten entfernt (einen Kaffee mit nehmen und dei Herbstfärbung auf einer Bank genießen)

“Very nice alternative to downtown” My best friend and I stayed at the Hilton University Place for 3 nights for the ACC Tournament. The hotel is located in an office park/shopping area near UNC-Charlotte and about a 10 to 15 minute drive from "Uptown" Charlotte. The hotel has been recently renovated (with some finishing touches still going on in the lobby). The rooms had new, modern furntiure, new mattresses, quality linens, flat panel TV's, and a work desk with lots of outlets. The modern appearance continued in the bathroom with the ____ sink. Our room was on the back side of the hotel with a view of the side of the shopping center and the lake next to another shopping center. The check-in process was efficient and we were able to obtain our room at 11AM on a Thursday. Check out was similarly easy with the express check-out available. We did not try out the restaurants or room service and did not get a chance to use the fitness center or meeting rooms. However, they appeared to be what you would expect for a mid to upper level hotel. The convenience store just off the lobby had the usual gifts/snacks and, after paying ridiculous prices at the Bobcats Arena for 4 days, the gift shop's prices were reasonable ($2 for bottled water/20 oz. soda vs. $4 at the games). I'm a neat freak when it comes to cleanliness and I must commend this hotel. There were no signs of disrepair or dirt anywhere. The linens were new, the towels were new, and the cleaning crew appeared to do an excellent job. I will likely use this hotel whenever I'm in Charlotte for business or pleasure as you do not have to deal with many of the downtown issues (especially parking) and the cost was much less than the downtown counterparts.

“It's a gem” Lovely hotel in a lovely neighborhood with good restaurants and conveniences close by. Rooms are a good size and the staff is pleasant. The free parking (ample covered garage) was definitely a plus since we needed a car to move my daughter into college. It's proximity to American University and Georgetown made it the perfect place for us to stay. Since my daughter is here for 4 years, we will definitely be back again! We may not have a car next time but we noticed the DC Circulator bus stop is a couple of blocks away and is a good option for public transportation.

“Great location and service” This hotel is situated on the Georgetown Campus, near the medical center and a few steps from the Admissions Office. I agree with other reviewers that the rooms are a tad shabby. For example, there was a worn patch in the carper in my room. None the less, the location is terrific and the staff is very friendly. I would stay here again on Georgetown U business due to its convenience. I am in DC on other matters I would probably stay elsewhere. The staff pointed me to the free Georgetown University shuttle bus that leaves every 5 minutes for the Dupont Circle metro station. This makes all of Washington, DC very accesable.

“Wow! Best Value in DC AND the Best Night of Sleep I've Had on the Road in Years!” This is such a nice hotel! Evidently Hilton is reinventing this brand because this new hotel is gorgeous and has a destination chef-driven restaurant inside. My room is huge and quiet as a tomb. The bed has a sleep number dial for firmness, and the work area is better than my office. And the staff is super nice! I travel almost every week and this place is the best surprise I've had in years.
“lovely place to stay but disappointed with the staff” very well made new interiors, perfect location but disappointed with the staff, very rigid and unwilling to accomodate clients..

“Cannot go wrong...” Great location, beautiful building, wonderful service, best nights sleep ever! I had been ahving trouble sleeping for two weeks, then I checked into the Le Meridien. The hotel is situated such that the drapes can be drawn and the room is totally dark and totally quiet. No housekeeping staff slamming doors in the a.m., no elevator noises, just a perfect night's sleep in a wonderful bed and a well appointed room. From the robe to the nice bathroom amenities to the fresh linens and handy minibar. Everything at this property was fabulous. We also saw a wonderful show at the Walnut St. Theater and a delicious dinner on Rittenhouse Square. Valet parked the car and never had to move it. Perfect in so many ways.

“Large City Hotel” Stayed for 6 nights as part of a meeting. The hotel caters both to large groups and individual travelers. Check-in lines can be long, but are staffed and effecient. Check-out is the same. Rooms are small - very small. If you stay in a tower room, you reeive Starbuck's coupons for coffee, muffin and fruit or $10 for the restaurant buffet. My room was on the 32nd floor bay facing. Generally quiet. The room is as expected - comfortable bed, flat screen, bathroom. Lots and lots of electric plugs which is a help for phones, ipads, laptops, etc. Fitness center. Lobby is always crowded. Location is 3 blocks from bart. Restaurants abound in a 5 block area. Doormen are excellent for service and recommendations. Cleaning staff are effecient and friendly. Parking is $47 for park-yourself or $52 for valet. If this were not business travel, I'd pick another location.

“Good, but not worth the hype” Don't get me wrong, Trump Soho is a good hotel. But, it's not worth all the hype. I don't have a lot of experience in New York's "five star" hotels, but this doesn't exactly feel like five stars to me. While the hotel is within walking distance of SoHo, it seems misleading to suggest that it's in SoHo (rather, it's on Varick St, a block away from the entrance to the Holland Tunnel). The lobby is interesting and tasteful, though small. Elevator lobby feels very small. The rooms are nice, though nothing special. the bathroom is dramatic, though the shower is small, the lighting around the sink is bad, and the toilet has a cheap plastic toilet set. The window shades are electric - it literally took me about 10 min to figure out how to open them. Besides a good bed and a good shower, there is one additional basic thing that I want in a hotel room - a decent coffee maker. This hotel has Nespresso machines - not sure what's wrong with me, but I can't figure out how to work these machines (and there's no directions in the room). The TV is off to the side of the room - not well positioned for watching TV while in bed. Prior to arriving in NY, I had been at the Redbury in LA. I couldn't help but keep asking, why aren't more hotels like the Redbury? Will I stay here again? Maybe. There's a lot of great hotels in NY, this won't be my first choice for the next trip.

“Very convenient for airport travel” Great location at the airport if you want an in and out experience with no hassel. The shuttle comes every 10 minutes or so, and the driver was very friendly. Room service menu was pretty limiting, and VERY pricey. However, if you do room service, you must try the ice cream sundae - very delicious!! The rooms are pretty basic, and could use a reburbishment, but nice overall. They also have tiny little balconies which is good for us smokers.

“Truly the best experience always!” Because of work, I travel to Boston twice a month and stay at this amazing place. This is not just comfortable but everything about this place is unmatched. The service, the luxury, the rooms and the amenities: a class apart! If i were to pick up on something, it would be the internet connectivity which becomes overloaded and unreachable with the number of guests lodged.

“Great Spot in NYC” I have stayed at this hotel dozens of times--it's my "go to" hotel in Manhattan. I even prefer it to the more "upscale" Marriott a few blocks away on Lex. Here's what this place has going for it. > Great staff. The front desk team is friendly, courteous, and professional. They also have security 24/7. > Good location for business or pleasure. From a tourist perspective, maybe 2 or 3 blocks too far east but still good access to Rockefeller Plaza, Times Square, Central Park. > Big, clean rooms. Especially for a NYC hotel. > A gym. Nothing fancy - 3 treadmills, 2 elliptical trainers and some weights. Enough to keep me on track and it's never packed. My only beef with this hotel was its wifi which could be weak & flaky depending on your room but the old system has been updated within the last 6 months and it's much improved.

“'Green' hotel in great location...” Our stay at the Orchard Garden was very pleasant. We had stayed there before (see Nov 6, 2007 review) and the management messed up our reservation by not giving us the free breakfast that was included in our package. We wrote the manager and never received a reply. We mentioned this to the front desk when we checked in this March and they immediately gave us a room upgrade and two free glasses of wine with an apology. I said before that the hotel was very clean and in a great location and that we would stay again. We did and were very satisfied with the staff. We will definitely stay again. The location is great - close to Union Square. Cafe de la Presse is across the street, good for breakfast or dinner. Chinatown is around the corner. Ask for an inside room, no view but quiet. The roof top garden is a nice spot for a late afternoon drink.

“Typical Marriott” This is your standard Marriott hotel. It is starting to show its age but the location is excellent. We chose this hotel to host a business meeting of 35 so we had 20 plus rooms and used the meeting space. All was as expected but nothing special.

“Utter disappointment” My family and I were very excited for our New Years Eve trip to NYC. I love Exhale and sushi both which are located here. The kids were thrilled; they love the city and when I told them I reserved Wii for the room they couldn't wait. These things mean a lot to a kid. It finally did arrived at 6:30 on our last night of our 4 night stay with dead batteries and with only one controller despite telling the front desk we had 2 kids. It took about 40 minutes and 2 maintenance visits to get up and running. The fact that the room had peeling wallpaper, frayed carpets, and no towels in the bathroom was just icing on the cake. Each morning we awoke to the smell of cigarette smoke (on a nonsmoking floor) and no promised daily newspaper. On 2 of the 4 nights the room wasn't cleaned until 5 PM. Honestly I hate complaining but it actually became comical. On January 2nd the room next door had a loud party until 4 AM! The hotel is very unlike other the sister Park Ave location which seems much nicer. So much for luxury.

“Surprise Airport Hotel Find” Foolishly, I left my keys in my checked bag. Shouldn't have been a problem, except I arrived on the last flight into Austin that night, and my bag didn't. What could I do? I went to the hotel phone kiosk, and decided to call the Super 8. I've had a negative impression of Super 8, but at the late hour, they were affordable, and still offered a shuttle. I'm so glad I called this hotel. A very nice, modern, well kept property, everyone working there was so friendly and welcoming. The large, clean rooms even included a free bottle of water and some snacks. Their continental breakfast included eggs, sausage biscuits, and bacon. I woke up later than I planned, so I asked if I could delay my shuttle back to the airport for breakfast, and they accommodated me with a smile. I couldn't have been happier with my stay.

“worth 60 bucks...not a penny more...” another hotel group that pads the bottom line with ridiculous internet fees...12.95 a day...when will they ever get it?...dated property in need of renovation...for the full check-in price one can find accomodations with flatscreens, free wifi, dvd players and free breakfast...old tvs...tired looking rooms...very overrated...very.

“A bit out of the way.” We stayed only one night at this motel and it was quite ok. The room was small, but clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. We chose this motel mainly because we needed a place with a parking space. The location is not ideal and we ended up having to take a taxi when going out at night. In retrospect it would probably have been just as easy to find a hotel with a parking space more centrally located and the next time I am in SF I will choose a hotel closer to union square. Like most motel chains the breakfast was poor, but there is an Ihop just across the street so we ate there instead.

“What history!” Oxford Hotel is a gem. Very old and ornate. We did not stay there but stopped and enjoyed the Cruise Room, a bar opened the day after the end of Prohibition we were told. It is a dark, red-lit intimate bar with memories of the 1920’s. They are known for their martinis, but their wine list was excellent as well.

“Had a great experience” This was my second stay at this property. Everything was perfect. The executive suite that I was fortunate enough to have was beautiful. The staff handled ever request promptly and with a smile. The workout facilities were great as were the staff. Room service was prompt and the food excellent. When I called the hotel from the airport to see if I could get a room due to my flight being cancelled they accommodated me without issue. As my checked bags were not returned to me, they provided me with every toiletry necessary. They also provided shorts and a t-shirt to use so that I could work out. The concierge had a charger available for my blackberry and checked the next morning if my flight was on time. This time the Four Seasons got everything right. Being at the hotel was like a home away from home. No matter what the price, it would have been worth it. It was that good.

“Adequate” As with most airport hotels, it's really just a place to sleep. Basic room, comfortable bed and shower - not much more or less. It's fine for a night's stay if you have a layover at IAH.The hotel has a sleek, modern look to the lobby - including self-check-in kiosks, which I think are great. Staff was friendly. However, there is room for improvements. Bathroom toiletries were not great. Worst of all, the water glasses in the bathroom were visibly dirty (I was to tired to complain and ended up taking the $4 bottled water instead). And, as others have mentioned, shuttle service from the airport is not great. When I called from the airport at around 11:45pm, I was told that a shuttle had just left and it would be "at least" half an hour until the next one. I again took the pricier route as I only had about 8 hours in between flights -- but it ended up being a $25 taxi ride. I had gotten a pretty good deal on this room, but spending this much on a taxi pretty much negated my good rate. For future stays, I will likely opt to book a hotel with more regular shuttle service. Shuttle service in the morning was prompt however, and only a 15-20 minute ride to the airport. Overall, just a standard airport hotel that could become much better with a few improvements.

“Great service!” This place is on the other side of downtown Houston but the service and look of the place were just great! We went to a Astros game and the hotel gave us a free ride to and from the game. The staff was very friendly and nice and the area had some good reaturants near during the day. I would stay here again.

“Just average but wonderful service” I love Le Meridien and choose to stay here while passing through as the Westin I usually stay at had a very high rate for the evening. I paid a rate of 179 and was rather disappointed when I looked into Starwoods in the area two days later and found the same room for 79. At 179 this property was a poor value. Likes: Everyone at the property was very, very nice. Mir at checkin was quick, pleasant and professional. The valets and the guy who brought up room service were very nice. Being upgraded with my SPG Preferred status. The room was very quiet. Good location with easy access to 635 and North Dallas Tollway. The valet did get me bottled water for my drive when I asked. Dislikes This property is old and lacks the charm (local art, funky decor) of other Le Meridiens I've visited. Room service meal was not very good. I know not to expect 5 star, but I did not even eat my salad as the dressing was very mayo-y....like mostly mayo, gross. Also, they delivered the wrong dessert. But I was too tired to call down and ask them to exchange it. Also, they only brought one set of silverware, napkin for the two of us. I LOVE Le Meridiens bath products, but my bottle marked lotion actually contained shampoo. The towels were very scratchy. Paying to park (20). I could easily have parked my own car in the lot right by the front door. I rate this property as average because it is nothing special. I would stay again if I was able to find a good rate but now I know it is not worth paying in the high 100's range.

“Great little hotel if you want to be near times square” This is a very nice boutique hotel if your desire is to be near time square. it's just a block away but very nice. Room are spacious, newly remodeled and very clean. Staff is very friendly and helpful. There is wine social each evening. room service was fast and efficient. it does not have a business center however, so if you need that, plan accordingly. I would recommend this hotel for most travelers.

“Stayed here many times over the past 7 years...” Going back to 2004, when a colleague put me onto this hotel as a great location for accessing DC metro at Foggy Bottom station for trips into core of DC and easy access to airport (DCA), I have been returning regularly. Location, layout, and other features haven't changed. Nor has the superb food served at Dish in lobby area. Unfortunately, as time has passed so has the wear-and-tear on the rooms and hallways in some areas of the hotel. This latest trip showed this. Even though the rooms remain well-appointed it might be time soon for a redo. I love the 'rowing theme' in the lobby and elsewhere in the hotel logo, etc. I will keep coming back when I can.

“Overstimulating” Staff was nice, the bed was comfortable, the room was fine. The room was cozy. Great bathroom. The problem for me is that the hotel seems to be trying just a bit too hard to evoke a high-energy and cool vibe, which to me was simply irritating. If you like continuous loud music, garish lobby decor, dizzying 3D imagery (and loud music) in the elevators, then this place is for you. Also, internet in the room is not free, though it is free in the lobby.

“Very nice” This is a very nice place to stay. Rooms were clean and the hotel is closely (walking distance) located next to a shopping district. Lots of places to eat adjacent to the hotel. Hotel food was good but not outstanding. The gym had outdated equipment. They appeared to offer a pass to Bally's across the street. Take them up on that if you have the time.

“Great Experience” I just returned from a five-night stay in this hotel and would highly recommend it. I read all the reviews on this site before making this my destination for a recent trip. The room was much bigger than I expected it to be (28th floor--king non-smoking). In addition to the bed and two nightstands inthe room, there was a desk with chair, an additional fabric covered chair and ottoman, a television atop a wooden bureau containing drawers, shelves, and a safe. The closet was long and narrow and the bathroom contained a tubwith shower, a single sink and wall shelving to hold makeup, lotions, etc. There was also a wall-mounted hair dryer in the bathroom. There were three or four elevators serving the floor and I rarely had to wait to go up or down. There was a single window in the room and it opened and had some sort of shading so that you could not see into the room from the other rooms making it possible to keep the shades up and the window open but still maintain privacy. The window ledge held an ice bucket and a large red vase. There were two phones--one by the bed and another on the desk--and a clock-radio CD player. The decor was khaki and white with black--very smoothing and certainly pleasant. I had room service on several occasions and found it very overly priced even for New York standards--$23 for pancakes that I could buy for less than $4 at the Grand Central Station food court. The room service menu lists a three-egg omelette for $23 and I ordered it for breakfast one day. I knew when I signed the bill that the total was much higher than I expected and I assumed I had mis-read the menu and there was a per charge fee for ingredients. I decided to check the menu and saw that there was no such fee so I decided to eat and then call to complain. That was when i realized they had sent up three omelettes and charged me for three!!! I called room service and told them that when i read "three egg omelette" off of the menu I was placing an order for a single omelette with three eggs not THREE OMELETTEs. They removed the charge and were very gracious about it. Another time they left the toast off of my order but they quicky sent it up when I complained. All in all while the price was very high, the food was good and it was worth the splurge on those days when i wanted to get ready to go out and yet do so in a leisurely fashion. I ordered a B and B one night and the person did not know what that was and asked me if I wanted a bread and butter plate. The girl who delivered the drink later told me that the guy who took my call did not drink and had never heard of a B and B, but that even the bartender said he had only had requests for two or three ever-- I did not expect the request to merit such discussion! When I returned each day the housekeeping staff did a great job of cleaning the room. In other visits when I have used the blanket kept in the closet or shelf of most hotel rooms the staff has returned it to the closet or shelf each evening requiring that I pull it out and re-do the bed, but at this hotel they made up the bed each day with the blanket--something I greatly appreciated and I had also removed the heavier bed covering which they left off of the bed as well. I appreciated this attention to detail. The hotel was quiet except for the last night when a large group of college students stayed on the floor and were up and down the halls. I could hear them each time they talked as they walked by my door, but never heard any noises from the adjoining rooms and very little street noise when i closed the window. There are vending machines on every floor--two dollar sodas. The great thing about this hotel is that you can get to the subway without going outside so it is very convenient to getting where you need to go. There is a great market in Grand Central station with lots of pre-made food so if you want to take it easy and eat in the room you can find every sort of take-out food from the market that is ready to eat. Likewise, there are great choices in the food court of the station. I found that most of the places there would prepare food for take-out as well. The concierge was great about locating movies and tickets and providing advice on the fastest most economical way to maneuver the city. The bell staff is less helpful.
