When I needed a taxi to leave they were so busy talkig to each other that I ended up hailing thre cab myself. When i arrived at the hotel no one moved to assist me with my bags. I would have gladly paid a tip to have assistance especially since upon entering the lobby one must go up an escalator or stairs to reach the registration desk. All in all, I would choose this hotel again. The location is great.

“Disappointingly Pedestrian” Pros Updated hotel - modern design Nice bath products Cons Location Noise Level from street Price I had expected a fantastic experience at this W hotel, it's in a fantastic city, but the W San Francisco proved to be a disappointment. While I recognize that this is San Francisco and that space is at a premium, from a location standpoint this is a hotel on the far edges of the Union Square area. Seriously if you're planning to be closer to the shopping and excitement, be prepared to walk. This hotel is on the way into town, so also be prepared for some traffic noise. While not an airport hotel, at 20 floors up I heard constant car traffic in my corner room. Paying the premium for a corner room, nearly $100 more than a standard room, was a waste. You do get to benefits of W standard which include modern room features and amenities which is nice. You also get Bliss Spa products which do add a nice touch. All in all, this is an okay hotel. Maybe I expected too much from the brand and the price. The W San Francisco is not a spectacular place in a city filled with great hotels that are truly in the heart of it all.

“Good location, ok rates - room good size - could be in better shape” Stayed at the Shelburne Murray Hill for 2 nights recently - the hotel has a nice location very central and yet still residential in flavour which is a nice combination. The rooms are a good size for Manhanttan, and mine had a kitchenette as well as a decent sized work area. The bed was very comfortable, the towels were plush yet the bathroom was relatively cramped. The sink was quite small and close to the mirror so shaving was a bit of a challenge. The staff were friendly and informative and I would stay there again if in the area. The room could stand a little fix up on the ceiling and the paint job - nothing horrible, just needed a little TLC

“Had a Great stay at the Hampton Inn” We stayed at the Hampton Inn March 29-April 2 with a school fieldtrip of 16 people and 5 rooms - and were very pleased with the accomodations. The hotel had been open 3 weeks and was very clean. Having a refrigerator and microwave in the rooms was a plus. The locations was very central to the Gallery-Place/China Town Metro stop. However be aware that there are some homeless to contend with as you exit the stop. They were not troublesome...but simply a facet of city life. The pool heater was under repair so the water was a little chilly in the indoor pool. Also the pool-maintenance guy was TOOOO FRIENDLY with the female students, and I would not be comfortable leaving my kids in the pool area alone to swim. The front desk was very helpful and the breakfast was above average for a Hampton Inn. Although located close to a Fire Department, the noise was easily ignored. They also messed up our bill, but quickly fixed it when I pointed it out. There were LOTS of restaurants close by - mostly Asian but also some seafood and fastfood. There was a CVS pharmacy close by, too.

“I Wish All Hotels Were Like This Place” The staff are amazing, very personable. The elevator requires a keycard to operate. The room is reasonably spacious for the location which is perfectly close to everything. It’s half a block from The Cheesecake Factory, across the street from Barnes & Noble, and just a few blocks from The Hard Rock Cafe, the market, and Westlake. It's an older property which means it has character and charm but also slight issues like old tiling in the bathroom and a loud air conditioning system. The shower stall is very small, it worked fine for me but anyone with curves might have issues. Overall this is a great hotel; I would stay again but only when traveling alone.

“Nice hotel choice in Detroit” There aren't too many good hotels in downtown Detroit. This is the best choice we've found so far. The rooms are reasonably large, well appointed and modern in style. The upper floor rooms have nice views either towards the high rises or towards the rest of the city. Note that the hotel is in a separate building from the casino, connected by a skybridge. Other than a little signage, you would never know this was a casino hotel. Free parking and free internet. The buffet breakfast is not expensive but I found much of it not very flavorful. An unfortunate note on Detroit. From this location you will often take cabs, depending on where you are going. This last trip, we took cabs twice and neither time did the driver use the meter so one is at their mercy for what the charges are. You have to either insist on a price or on the meter being used. But on a positive note the Detroit Institute of Arts is wonderful, the Fox Theater amazing and the Detroit Zoo one of the best in the US, noted for its humane approach.

“In the midst of all the action!” A friend and I recently spent the last night of a week long trip to the US at the Hilton Back Bay and to be honest we wished we'd stayed at this hotel for longer. Located in the Back Bay area the hotel is great for getting to the many bars and restaurants in the Back Bay. It's also not bad for getting to other parts of Boston owing to the proximity of the T (metro) lines. We were put into a Twin Delux Corner Room which had excellent views of the city and a balcony. The room was large, well appointed and very clean. Overall the hotel gave a very good impression - it wasn't overly ornate, more like a business hotel and functional. It was also very well maintained and very clean throughout. To relax before our flights back home we made use of the pool and fitness suite. The pool area was excellent, with a reasonably sized pool and hot tub. The fitness centre was practically empty, with only us in the pool area. Throughout the stay the staff at the hotel were great and very accommodating. They seemed very friendly at checkin and checkout and the valet and doorman couldn't do enough to help. If I return to Boston, the Hilton Back Bay would certainly be on my hit list of hotels to consider.

“Attacked by bugs while I slept” I am a frequent business traveler and have spent about 80 nights in hotels this year thus far and this was one of my most disappointing experiences. The lobby and entrance of the hotel are clean and in order but the rooms leave a lot to be desired. I stayed in Room 521 and awoke with more than a dozen bug bites on my calves, ankles and feet. I had inspected the bed the night I arrived and while the mattress looked very worn I didn't see much to be concerned about at the time. The next morning under closer inspection (with more daylight) I found the bed to be quite dirty with stains on the sides and corners...there was a mattress pad and cover but they were littered with pubic hair and I found several small, dead bugs on the mattress under the mattress pad. They did not appear to be bed bugs but I could not identify them, even upon closer inspection with a camera. There was a chaise lounge in the room that had stains all over it as well. I awoke in the middle of the night running a fever and feeling very sick, which is probably when I was being bitten, but didn't know it at the time. I also used the exercise room in the morning which I found to be quite dirty as well. I've stayed at many Renaissance hotels and generally find them to be very clean and nice places to stay but this hotel does not match up to the Renaissance standard. I did report the bug problem to the front desk so they are aware of it and did some online research when I got home and the bugs resemble snow fleas.

“Perfect Airport hotel” I was scheduled to leave LAX very early in the morning for a business trip to the East Coast. Rather than trying to get to the airport from home, I decided to spend the night at La Quinta Inn and Suites. When I mentioned at check-in that I was on an early morning flight, the person at the reception desk immediately offered a wake-up call at 4:00 AM (yes, that's how early I had to get up!). I've traveled extensively and have never been offered a wake up call unless i asked for it. My room was adequate, clean, though a bit small. A 24/7 shuttle to LAX is available for free. The only complaint, and it had nothing to do with the hotel, was with the shuttle. I was down in the lobby by 4:25 AM to catch the 4:30 shuttle. By the way, the hotel offers coffee and muffins in the lobby for folks leaving early in the morning. Thank you, La Quinta! The shuttle never arrived at 4:30. It was closer to 5:00 before it pulled in. However, the front desk was very attentive and gave updates on the shuttle's status. Luckily, LAX is just a five minute drive from La Quinta or I really would have been upset. Overall, I highly recommend La Quinta Inn and Suites, especially if you need to get to the airport very early in the morning.

“Location/price in NYC” This hotel is basic, but it is clean and safe. At the price, for NYC, anyway, it's a good option. There is no real lobby, but the reception is nice enough. The room was small, the sheets clean, but the blankets allergenic. The bathroom was ok, at least it was inside the room. NYC is another universe for hotels, this is a reasonable, clean, safe option, but it is quite basic.

“Shame on Chuck Bass” I stayed there for one reason and one reason only - Chuck Bass "bought" it. What a let down!! small room, tiny bathroom, narrow hallways, super slow elevators, lousy AC. Though the bed is nice. DO NOT GO UNLESS U REALLY LIKE CHUCK BASS

“We love Hyatt” We stayed here just for a quick 1 day trip on 9/22. We choose this hotel because its location, just across from Union square. We got there at noon, almost able to checked in right away but another front desk checked in another guest while we were thinking about whether to take the room or not. So, we checked in our luggage and went out for shopping. In 1 hour the hotel called and informed me that the room is ready. The room was clean, new and also have contemporary design to it. This hotel is also undergoing renovation to all rooms and also the lobby. So, the lobby is a bit messy and seemed smaller. The bathroom has a big mirror with back lighting, very big and long sink. Tub and shower combination with Hyatt portico amenities. The bed was comfortable and new. The view from the room was ok. The fitness center was small and probably they will refurbish it later. I love that they provide cold towel and Ice water dispenser by the entrance to fitness center. No swimming pool is the only draw back. All the staff were great and very professional. I recommend this hotel and would love to go back again.

“Nice Surprise” This place is not luxurious, but it certainly fits the bill if you are looking for an affordable, clean and safe place to stay in NYC. Convenient to subways and other midtown attractions. Great price! Only drawback: a little noisy. Outside sounds come into the room, but that is NYC!

“Great Hotel, Great Location, Very Clean” stayed at this hotel for a weekend in July 2011. The hotel staff were very friendly and the check in was quick and easy. The hotel offers offsite parking which was very well priced considering you are in Manhattan. The parking lot is 1.5 blocks away from the hotel and less than 3 minute walk. The room that I got was like a bachelor apartment, with a separate dining area. It offered a small kitchen. There was an LCD TV in the room with lots of channels (not like your going to watch TV while in NYC) The hotel was very clean and located in a great location. I would certainly return back to this hotel and recommend this to my friends as well.

“Nice Average Hotel” Nice average hotel at most. Close to all attractions, well shopping in union square really. Nice buffet breakfast served at $25.00pp. Rooms are nice,clean, very small though. Very big hotel make sure you watch elevators you take up to right floor, this is really a convention hotel at best. Check out grand lux or theres a diner around corner not so bad either. Front desk checkin was breeze,and checkout as well,expect large crowds!

“Great stopping off point” Homewood Suites, Columbus/Worthington was the perfect stopping point for the night. We had been on the road for eight hours, with another ten to go the next day, so we were delighted to find our room to be off the interstate on a quiet side street. Our room was very clean and quite cozy & comfortable. The desk clerk was very friendly, and it was quite obvious a lot of the guests were thorougly enjoying the Managers Reception in the foyer/dining area. As was the case the next morning for their continental breakfast, which was well stocked. The Hilton Family of hotels is more than kind enough to offer a government/military rate which made it possible for us to even stay in this fine hotel. We thank them for that. We needed an early start the next day to get on I71 so going around Columbus on 270 to the Worthington exit was perfect. We did not have one single problem finding out way back to I71 or getting back on the highway the next morning, although I admit we tried to be on the road before the main rush hour started. We plan to stay at this hotel again in March.

“Maybe my favourite NYC hotel” I love this place. I've stayed here on three separate occasions. As far as I know, it was the first hotel with floor to ceiling windows, and hardly any solid walls. The design is very minimal and striped back. Reception is on the first floor, so take the lift. The staff are very 'New York' - low on smiles, and with the air of high end fashion boutique sales assistants. Very good looking though. The beds are the best I have ever slept in (Tempur-Pedic King size). You literally fall asleep the second your head hits the pillow. The breakfast buffet used to be free, but the last time I stayed, they had introduced a nominal fee. But it's plentiful and the coffee is strong. Also, the turndown service used to leave warm brownies by your bedside, but that didn't happen the last time I was there. The gym is very small, in a windowless room, but I found that often I had it to myself. The lobby bar scene is noisy and young. There used to be a nightclub on the roof which felt like something out of American Pie - hot tubs and all. The hotel guest bar is situated just above the lobby, so you can still feel part of it, while keeping a slight distance. The last time I stayed, there was a mix up with the number of days I'd booked. I usually ask for a room with a balcony and uptown view. The compromise was being offered, at the same rate, one of their signature suites. The room was bigger than my entire flat in London. The sweeping panoramic view made me gasp out loud. Oh, and in the bathroom was a 4 person sauna, done out in black tiles. I never did find out what the actual rate should have been, but I can't wait for them to make another mix up. The whole Lower East Side has been gentrified, and there is now a wide choice of places to stay. But for me, this place is special.

“An old Sheraton” Ok this is a Sheraton hotel, so expect an extremely comfortable bed, nice bathroom and quality details... all these things once you are inside your bedroom... Unfortunately the corridors where dark and with a strange smell. We stayed there for one night only as we had a very early morning flight the next day. As usual the breakfast is not included. The shuttle from and to the airport works every 15 minutes. I would recommend this hotel, especially for travelers.

“Excellent location right near Interstate but without all the noise.” I have read some negative reviews of this hotel and I am not certain that the reviewers stayed in the same hotel. This hotel was clean, neat, and smelled just fine. The breakfast area takes up half of the open lobby area and has at least 10 tables. One morning I came down to eat and all the tables were full as there was some kind of college sports team filling all of the tables. I grabbed my food and went outside and ate by the pool. My single biggest complaint is that the tub enclosure is absolutely the smallest one I have ever had to stand in. I did not take baths mind you but it was impossible to stand with both feet side by side and take a shower without feeling cramped. I have stayed around the corner at the Candlewood Suites a lower cost option in the Holliday Inn chain and their tubs are normal sized so why does the Holliday Inn the higher dollar hotel have such tinny tubs? If you want comfortable beds, clean rooms, reasonable price (for the area), and friendly staff then this place is worth a look.

“New Hotel... Many kinks to work out.” It was your typical Hampton Inn. We did have some problems, though. First, one of the elevators was broken the entire time we were there. The hotel only has two, and in a 30+ story hotel, one elevator is not nearly enough. The shower would completely lose water for about 1-2 seconds every 45 seconds or so. Our room did not have an ice bucket. I called the front desk for one, and after it had not come 45 minutes later, I went to get it myself. They did not give me a plastic liner even after I asked for one. The fellow just said the ice bucket is new and I don't need one. By the way, it is also located in a pretty rough looking neighborhood.

“Plesant Stay” Stayed at the Hilton O'Hare because I had an early A. M. flight the next morning. Check in was smooth, the front desk staff was helpful with information about the hotel. The room was clean and up to the above average standards of the Hilton chain. The bed is wonderful, and comfortable. There is a refrig.with items in there to be paid for if they are comsumed. No microwave, there is a small coffee pot for two cups of coffee. The hotel has a business center, and on the lower level there is a computer room with 3 computers and I think 2 or 3 printers. The cost is a miminum of $3.00 to sign on to the internet. Credit card required. The gym is on the lower level as well the gift shop and another small retail shop. There is a resturant on the check in level of the hotel. This hotel is clearly a hotel for Business Travelers although tourist will find it attractive. The convenience to get into the city is a plus for this hotel right in the airport. You can take the Blue Line right in to the city. I purchased a day pass for $5.00 for use on the CTA bus and train. BE AWARE, there is a lot of construction going on in the downtown area of Chicago. Also the blue line train route is under contstruction. From the hotel you will ride the line to the Western station and then take Shuttle bus to the downtown area. Allow more time to get to and from the downtown area from the hotel. I would stay at this hotel again.

“An excellent experience” Just back from a week's stay at the Central Loop and found it very much to my liking. Great location, somewhat away from the tourist traps of Michigan Avenue but nice and quiet. Cheap taxis plentiful around the area. The room was lovely - plenty of space and good sized closets. COmfy bed with good linens. Bathroom good - clean, nice big shower and good hairdryer. Excellent to have free bottled water available and good free high speed wifi. Staff was pleasant and not intrusive - bellboys/ valets very helpful. Great to be able to guarantee a late check-out for $35 - well worth it and saved us a lot of hassle! I recommend this place.

“Location..location” We booked junior suite in this hotel, and was given room overlooking Times square. The view was amazing. The size of the room is quite decent for Manhattan standard, the breakfast was very good with many selections. The interior of the hotel is quite old, but other than that, this property is quite ok.

“Awesome bed, pillows and newly redecorated!” I have stayed here at least 15 to 20 times now and have always been satisfied with the hotel, the parking is a little hard but the stay is worth it. They did a fantastic job with remodeling the rooms. The flat screen T.V.s, modern furniture, awesome bed and pillows that I promise you will have no trouble resting your head on. The breakfast is fast, hot and made to order. I have had dinner inside the hotel many nights and it was excellant each time. The rooms are quite, spacious and the newly redecorated bathrooms are equally beautiful. Great buy for the money and you can't beat the short walk to PF Changs!

“Central Hotel” This hotel is really central with easy access to the Prudential Center, Newbury Street and the shops in the Copley Center. The nearest T station is in the Prudential Center and is a 5 minute walk from the hotel. It is a large and busy hotel so you may wait some time for a lift or service at the front desk. The "lounge" area is essentially part of the thoroughfare for the shopping center so van be exceptionally busy. The queues at Starbucks are long at peak times. This is a hotel to use for either business purposes or shopping - you would not stay here for a quiet break!

“OK, I guess...” We stayed on May 2, 2008 for a meeting and checked in early after BEGGING to have a room ASAP. The front desk clerk was nice and felt sorry for us and did give us the first available room. The bathroom does have a slight urine odor and there was a fresh wet stain on the rug in the room. I think the staff here is nice and they do welcome pets. There is a lot of good grass out back to walk your dogs. I guess, i would stay here again.

“Confused by bad reviews!!” I am really not sure what the bad reviews of this hotel are about... maybe something has recently changed dramatically, but I found this place fantastic! My room was great - amazing bed, great shower, beautiful furnishings, and free wireless! Great location right off the interstate with reasonable self-parking, really convenient. Everyone I dealt with was super-friendly, I find this is usually the case in Memphis. I will definitely stay here again and would recommend this hotel to anyone, One elevator was under repair still, but I did not experience any delay getting to my room, people need to get a grip!

“Fun location, very pleasant stay” This Westin is located very conveniently to the Riverwalk. The staff and hotel rooms are very clean/modern/up to par with Westin standards. Our suite was large... and had the most lovely giant bathroom. We were very pleased. Sleep quality was great... even though there was a huge Spurs game/celebration (1st of the Playoffs), the room was quiet and had a nice view of the downtown area.

“Overall good hotel, convenient location - huge hotel” We stayed here for 2 nights - I had read about the long queues for the check in and about the homeless people in the area. But if you have been to SF, you have to expect some homeless ppl esp in the Union Square area. Location is convenient for the touristy (Cable Cars) to the practical (MUNI buses, BART). As mentioned by other reviewers, best not to park your car in the hotel parking which is over $40 (plus taxes)/night and you can easily get a "in-out privelege parking" in other garages within the block for $15-20 less. Regarding check -in, if you have a Hilton Honor membership (which is easy to get and is free) it's worthwhile since you have an express line. So we didn't end up waiting at all. The check-in service person was very attentive and thorough which we appreciated. The hotel is big - and we were up on the 3rd Tower above the pool area - and our room was not huge (as is expected in SF) but nicely furnished and clean. SF can be windy and cold so was not sure how the pool area was like but the fact that the pool area was surrounded by the hotel room in a courtyard style, the area was shielded from the wind so we could enjoy the sun and the heated pool and jacuzzi. This was prob the best part of the hotel. We would have used the gym but I understood that you have to pay a fee so we didn't go. We did have one incident on Sunday after noon when we came back from lunch - we were just dropping in to grab a few things - the room hadn't been cleaned yet but we didn't put the Do not Disturb sign since we were only going to be a few min. I was also using the bathroom. The cleaning service person came in - didn't speak a word of English and my partner had to tell her several times to "please come back in 10 min." She didn't leave and she proceeded to open the bathroom door without knocking (and these bathroom doors do NOT lock!) when I was using it. I complained about this incident and the hotel service person promised to let the cleaning service ppl know but we didn't hear much after. That experience certainly did not feel like we were paying for 4 star service... I mentioned it again before check out and this time the person said, "well, I recommend you put the do not disturb sign next time" - the point, however is that he had asked her to leave and come back in 10 min, but she proceeded to open the bathroom door without knocking. If it's recommended to put a sign on the bathroom door, they should have extra ones in the room. it was pretty unpleasant to say the least. Aside from that incident, it was overall a good experience and a reliable Hilton quality property. Just don't expect much from the general staff - the cleaning staff do not speak much English (and we saw more than the one that dropped in on us).

“great value unbeatable location” Booked through quikbook at a rate of 199/249 sept 2-4 labor day... It was a last minute bday getaway for my husband. This location is phenomenal.(two blocks from rockefeller center, 3 block from saks fifth ave, two blocks from times square, 8 blocks from central park) If you don't have a lot of time on your visit, stay here. The rooms are clean and have a contemporary feel. Room service was quick and pretty reasonable in price(10 dollars for a pizza). Concierge was very helpful. The front desk could use a little more improvement. At check in, the young woman seemed a bit annoyed since we arrived at 900am even though we told here we would come back at three or four. Another person was more helpful and preregistered us and gave us our key so we could go straight to our room after 300pm. I would not hesitate to stay here again on our next trip to NYC. Make sure you are booking a new and remodeled room...

“Excellent service, comfortable stay” My husband and I stayed for a couple of days over thanksgiving. We arrived earlier than check-in but were given a room immediately. The front desk staff was prompt and courteous as always and was more concerned that our attache services had not been completed. We freshened up and took to NYC for the remainder of the day, stopping by briefly in the evening to change into warmer attire. The room was tidied and our guests were very impressed with the room and the service. The only complaints that I have of this hotel are that it was a little out of the way for where we wanted to be but the Trump International was booked up, which really wasn't a big deal, and the bed was so comfortable that I had a hard time wanting to leave it in the morning. The room met our needs as did the staff. They have an excellent team and when in New York, TheTrump hotels are definitely at the top of our accommodations list. Thanks to everyone that made our stay enjoyable .

“Decent place” Stayed one night for a business trip. The hotel provides a free shuttle to/from the airport. The shuttle is shared with the Doubletree. The hotel also runs a free shuttle to the nearby shopping centers. The staff was polite but not overly friendly or helpful. The lobby is very nice. There's a fireplace and lots of cozy chairs and sofas. Parts of the room were worn and dated but overall it was nicely decorated. However, there was not enough lighting in the room. Even with all the lights on it was still dark. Overall a decent place to stay.

“Ideal for business travel” I have stayed at the Stoneleigh four times in the last three months. The first time I stayed here, I assumed that the rooms, and especially the bathrooms, would be small since the hotel is in an old historic building. However, the bathrooms are quite large, with giant bathtubs, and each room I have had has included a giant walk-in closet. The hotel is very comfortable and stylish. I have not eaten dinner at the restaurant, but several times I have ordered a salad at the bar (delicious) and the breakfast is also very good. The fitness center has all the basic equipment (it's been empty every time I have used it). The Katy Trail is a short walk from the hotel, so that is a nice option for walking / running nearby. I have no complaints about the hotel at all, so I am surprised at some of the negative reviews. I will continue to stay at the Stoneleigh when I am in Dallas on business.

“Just Okay” After reading the reviews of the New York Palace Hotel, I was convinced it was the place to stay. However, I won't be staying there again. Upon arrival, I had to battle with 2 wedding parties and their guests and a visiting professional baseball team. The hotel was completely unprepared so the regular guests had to suffer. It took forever to check-in and when I did, it was so loud I could barely hear what the person helping me was saying. He was very efficient, but I felt like I was being rushed. Everyday, but my last day (I stayed 4 nights) I was missing something from the bathroom. The staff, with the exception of housekeeping tried so hard to be snobby (not to mention grumpy). I don't know, maybe it's the word "Palace" in the name of the hotel? I never felt at ease and considering the price, it's just an average hotel. The bathrooms are small, but the rooms are a pretty good size, yet they don't really offer anything unique. Although, I did like the box next to the bed that controlled the lights & heat/AC and the bed was extremely comfortable. Maybe it's me, but I've stayed at many a 4 to 5 star hotels and this was... just okay.

“Quality room and nice staffs for the price, but noisy...” I stayed alone in this hotel for 2 nights. This is a design hotel, but the price is just like a business hotel. The lobby, the room, the bar... everything in there is nicely designed. I liked the amenity, too. Staffs are very nice and helpful. The only thing I did not like is that the wall must be very thin... If you don't mind it, I can recommend this hotel.

“Great little hotel in my favorite part of the city” I love Nolita. We've spent a lot of time in midtown and it's really nice to move south, away from the Fifth Avenue and Broadway areas. There are small shops and parks and neighborhood restaurants - it's like a refreshing world apart. When I read that a new hotel had opened in Nolita I made a mental note to look it up the next time we visited NY. And so we did mid-November and had a wonderful stay. The staff is friendly and accommodating - not a hint of attitude. Although we had booked two nights non-refundable, they graciously allowed us to stay just one night when something came up and we had to leave early. The coffee I ordered for the room came right on time. The hotel is stylish, the rooms almost minimalist (with the exception of the views, which are breathtaking). The rooms, granted, are small, but so are most hotel rooms in NY. I loved the way you could look right through the shower into the bathroom. And I loved the high-floor balcony room with views straight up to the Empire State building and over to the Williamsburg Bridge. I suppose you could complain about the price, but why bother? Every now and again it's worth a little extra to try something different. And besides, it's NY!

“Have a meeting here! Wonderful staff, great location for a small business meeting” An impressive staff that truly went the extra mile - very friendly, knowledgeable, and professional. They blew away the attention and quality of service that I've received at much higher dollar properties (Renaissance Times Square, Omni in Washington, etc...). The property is finishing out renovations/upgrades that should push it over the top in terms of value. I had a suite with the biggest HD TV that I've ever seen in a hotel room, a huge sectional couch that could seat a 8 if needed, and a nice work area and small sink/refrigerator/counter space. Minor complaint - the soundproofing on the rooms wasn't the best - hallway noise and outside noise could bother light sleepers. Breakfast was good and the availability of on-site and walking distance restaurants was decent and the shuttle van will provide a ride to Jakes and Jills, a pretty cool sports bar nearby. Our non-profit was here for a Board of Directors meeting and the rack rate with food and space for the meeting was a great deal.

“Odd and of marginal value” Austin prides itself in being weird. They even have a slogan that states "keep Austin weird". This Hilton certainly does not damage that image and in fact, takes it a step or two further. I stayed for all the wrong reasons ... mainly to be near the airport with a morning departure. In the future, I think I will stay closer to town and at a hotel offering better value. There is absolutely nothing around this place. That is, nothing but a a very good airport. They have a huge parking lot but will still charge you a parking fee per day. Valet parking is expensive the cars are parked smack in front and about 100 feet away from the front of the hotel. There is no covered parking and its expensive. They have only two computers in the business center and will charge you 49 cents a minute for internet use -- except it is free to print your boarding passes. A previous stay at a Hilton Homewood Suites in San Antonio proved cheaper with as good a room with free parking, free business center internet and free wifi. What gives? I'm not sure what Hilton thinks the lure of this place is/ I bet there were not but about 20 people staying there when I did. Furthermore, the staff at the Homewood Suites were much nicer and professional. At this place, I asked the waitress for some pancakes, as it was supposed to be free with my buffet breakfast. I departed 20 minutes later with no pancakes and no visit by the waitress other than the initial greeting, order and coffee delivery. She got no tip. The other waitresses, with one exception, were about the same quality. I asked a van driver for the phone number to the hotel so I could call for the shuttle after I dropped my rental car off -- and he gave me the number to an office at the hotel that went to an answering machine. He shrugs and apologizes when I return and explained the results of his guidance. The place is round, like the pantheon in Rome. The rooms are in the round walls. The hallways make a big circle. You are either facing the big round, open inside of the building or the outside. Thank goodness there were not a lot of air traffic or revelers in the hotel. I kept the air conditioner on to drown out any noises and the dark curtains did ok with the light. I recommend you stay elsewhere until Hilton offers some real value for staying out in such an isolated location. And with the room charges, the other service charges and lack of professional attitudes of the staff, I saw no reason to return.

“It was the place for us” Wonderful stay! We spend 4 wonderful days the end of August. I was with my 81 year old Mother and 14 year old son and we found something fun to do for everyone! Check-in wasn't the best. First gave us the wrong room. We then walked all the way back to the office dragging our luggage. Our room then wasn't ready. We went to sea world and when we returned many hours later room still wasn't ready. I need to say the room was worth the wait. Very comfortable beds, bath products to die for and a view of a duck pond that was breath taking. Food was good, including room service. Pool service and the pool its self was great. A little costly drinks and food at the pool. We loved the grill for any meal. I will always remember watching my Mother and son play putt-putt golf and all the laughs. I was expecting a little warmer bay water but we still managed to go wading. The grounds were wonderful for anytime of the day walks or even resting at a bench. So tropicial. We had a wonderful evening one night watching a dive in movie at the pool. (first my Mother had ever seen) All of the staff in general bent over backwards to make sure we had a great stay. All in all we will be back!!!!!

“Never again” Arriving at the Swissotel I was excited. It's location is prime and beautiful (other than the major construction taking place next door - but I could see past that). You drive up and ask for valet, to which you are pointed in the direction of the TIGHTEST drive WAY underground to the garage. There are no signs directing you and nobody there to tell you where to park or drop your keys. We had to walk up to a window where a woman was busy paying more attention to her computer than any guests arriving in this confined sub-basement garage. She tells us to park right where we were and we left our luggage with the bellman who came out. We arrived at 11 and check-in is at 3. We knew that but were told our rooms (2 of them) would probably be ready when we arrived. Not the case, but that was ok. Once you get up to the lobby you quickly enter a construction zone within the Swissotel. A strange registration area where there is no real line, just people standing all over the place trying to figure out if they are in line or not was difficult to navigate. We were assured that our luggage would be safe and that when we returned at 3 it would meet us in our rooms. (Valet - $55 per night) We returned at 3 and were given our rooms. Lakeview rooms were actually complete views of the wall of construction next door. They are going to need to re-name those rooms because there will not be a lake view until you are well above the 20th floor. Our luggage was lost and they called our rooms asking us to describe our bags because they never tagged them, only "threw them in a room with hundreds of others". After 2 deliveries and about 45 minutes, we finally had our bags. The TV's were flatscreen and about half the channels wouldn't come in and the other 40% were snowy. The only channels that came through clear were the ABC, NBC, CBS and about 2 others. Beds were great (although our friends room did not have sheets on their bed). Very comfortable rooms. We set our room temp at 70 (about 80 outside during the day) and the room was still humid and hot through the night. The hotel was very loud. We could hear people using showers, toilets and talking in the hallways. You could also hear people outside and we were on the 19th and 20th floors. Wi-fi is available for $10 for 24 hours. Although when our friends tried to get it, they sent up an IT person who after about 30 minutes of trying to figure it out, told them that our whole side of the hotel would be unable to get wi-fi. It's hard to believe that a hotel that big and these days still charges for wi-fi... considering how much you have to pay to stay there! Woke up the next morning to a shower that was between cooler than luke-warm and cold. An hour later it was still the same way and never warmed up. Was the same for our friends on a different floor. The breakfast was the shining star of this terrible hotel. An amazing breakfast buffet ($26) was the best part of the stay. Very European and freash! I would walk to this hotel, from a different one, just to have the breakfast again. We were told that to get our car from valet would be about a 30 minute wait. We were then sent to the garage to pick up the car again and squeeze our way through the twisty turny skinny tunnel to get out. We have a normal size SUV and it was TIGHT! I would not stay here again. It's too bad because it is in a great location.

“Good hotel” This is an older hotel which has been modernized several times and is well maintained. It is an excellent location for business near the airport or an overnight layover at the airport for connections to flight, cruise, etc. It occasionally offers excellent value internet rates. It is about a block down from the main SEATAC terminal and can be walked in about 10 minutes, however, there is a shuttle service to the terminal. There are several decent restaurants within easy walking distance (remember it rains a lot here). One may also walk/shuttle over to the airport parking garage and catch the light rail directly into downtown Seattle, travel time about 25-30 minutes. Hotel motif is NW Pacific rustic but it wears it well. As it is an older hotel the rooms are quite large and fully equipped. The rest of the hotel amenities are as advertised, think four star here. There are a number of other hotels in the immediate airport area but this one presents an excellent compromise between price and hotel condition.

“great value for airport access” Stayb here a lot when needing to travel from the airport. No frills with excellent service to airport and free parking while away. They'll even pick you up. can't beat the service for the price.

“Overpriced: Needing Renovation” This hotel has rooms that are seriously in need of repair--wallpaper coming off the walls, ventilation system that doesn't work, etc. No minibar or many other features one would expect of even a "three star" hotel, which this certainly is not.

“Nice Stay” Purchased on Priceline for $80.00 (Thurs-Sat) This hotel was previously a Holiday inn. They have done a nice remodel. Watch out for room 25 on each floor. Very small window. This hotel is directly across the street from Chinatown which was fun.

“Great Location, responsive staff” The location can't be beat: close to everything and near beautiful central park. The staff was very responsive to any request we made. As an SPG gold member they upgraded me to the 49th floor and we had an excellent view of Broadway. A bit dark (they need backlighting on the elevator numbers: we old guys can’t read the numbers) and a good tourist hotel though not great for business: The cramped business center almost seems to be an afterthought and the room desk was not particularly useful for actual work. Very nice workout center: each workout machine has it’s own TV, ear phones, weights, water. They play this ‘modern” background music constantly and it eventually gets quite old: change up a bit. On balance, we enjoyed our stay though I think equally nice and well located hotels can be had for about 50-75 less per night.

“Noticeable improvements...keep up the good work!” During this stay at the Hilton Post Oak, I had the good fortune of staying on the 12th floor. The room was nicely remodeled and had a brand new flat screen TV. This is the first time I had a nice television at the Hilton. Previously I was always disappointed to find the huge CRT televisions being used in the rooms. Seeing these things make me think of cutting edge Amish technology, disco balls, and polyester. I felt stuck in an unwanted time warp. Not good! Kudos to Hilton for upgrading this property!!!!

“"Less than Stellar"” I really expected more as we had stayed in the property 4 years ago and found it to be delightful. What were the problems: 1) I booked the room and made note of the fact that we were getting married while staying there. Hotel did not acknowledge this in any way. I didn't expect a lot but at least some recognition of the event. 2) In fact the room we received was on the top floor and the furthest possible from the elevators (literally as I checked the layout of the hotel). 3) Lobby and other common areas closed during our stay. Not much they could do about this but I would have liked to have known before booking room. 4) No ice machines on floors. If you want ice you have to ring the front desk (which was an experience in itself as there was nothing on the phones telling you who to call other than the valet or concierge. When you called these numbers you would more often than not get voice mail. So you leave a voice mail to get ice? Not a good set up. 5) Room was really small. I am used to that in large cities (Chicago, New York etc.) but you had to move the ottoman at night and block the door so that you could get to the bathroom. 6) Coffee in lobby not out until 6:30 or 7:00 in the mornings (coming from the central time zone this was way too late). 7) Rooms are recently refurbished in the style of a "W" hotel and very hip but not to my liking (ok this is a personal taste matter. But the rooms previously seemd much more elegant.) Overall the location is nice at the top of Nob Hill but I don't think I would stay here again. And ignoring our wedding date is really inexcusable.

“Beautiful hotel but awkward service” Stayed at the Intercontinental for 3 nights on business. The hotel is beautiful. Very modern looking. Rooms have huge windows and great views.I actually stayed on 2 separate occasions within a week. The first time I stayed my room didn’t have a bathtub, the next time I stayed I asked for one and was upgraded to a nicer room. There were nicer toiletries in the better room too. The location of the hotel is very good. It’s close to Union square and shopping. I went to a place by Union Square called Mocca for lunch. Excellent sandwiches. The service was good at the hotel but sometimes I felt that the workers were sniffing out tips. Such as when I dealt with the doorman, bell hops and room service people. So sometimes I felt the service was a fake friendly and awkward. The hotel has a courtesy car that can take you to areas close by. They drove me and a colleague to my office. The doorman told us we should tip the driver even though it was a courtesy car. I don’t think people should ever be told that you have to tip someone. They also had a limo that took me to the airport. I thought it was a courtesy car as well but when I got out they told me it was $45. Which is reasonable but they never told me that before I got in the car. So a bit awkward. The room service food was not that great for such a nice hotel. When the room service person brought my food to my room I notice on the bill a line for the tip but they already include 18% gratuity and a $3 service charge on my bill. When I asked the person if the gratuity was included he just said there is a service charge, even though on the bill the gratuity is stated. Again I felt he was sniffing out a bigger tip. All in all it was a very nice hotel but sometimes the service came out a bit awkward by certain staff.

“A wonderful stay” After a bad experince at the hotel next door (read other review), I came here to see if they had a room available. as it was spring break, they were pretty full, but the kind concierge assisted in freeing up 2 rooms for us..and making good the bad taste the hotel next door had made!!! Well done westin!!! The rooms were wonderful, with a balcony overlooking the riverwalk, clean and well presented.

“Billig aber nicht zu empfehlen” Das Hotel hat eine sehr gute Lage - 5 Minuten vom Zentrum entfernt. Im September 2009 habe ich auch ein tolles Angebot gefunden (super billig - unter 70 USD/night ohne Steuer) was eigentlich ein super Preis für SF downtown ist. Es hat alles super angefangen - der june Mann beim Empfang gab mir bei der Einreise super Tip - das Hotel hat eine Vereinbarung mit einem Parkplaz 2 Blocks weiter und man kann dort gratis parken. Das hat mir sicher mind 100 Dollar erspart. Ich lese aber jetzt auf mehrere Seiten, dass dieser Service nicht mehr angeboten wird sonder Valet parking um 18 USD pro Tag.... aber gut - viele reisen ohne Auto nach SF und diese Info ist wahrscheinlich uninteresant. Der ersten Eindruck war OK - für ein 2* Hotel war der Lobby nicht so schlimm. Ich bin dann zum Zimmer gegangen - na ja - erster Eindruck war... die Tür ist nicht geschlossen. Sie war aber zu - nur die Lücke zwischen Tür & Rahmen war sehr gross (!) und hat den Eindruck gemahct als diese offen ist! Im Zimmer war eigentlich alles vorhanden (keine grosse erwartungen beim Preis und 2*) - Kühlschrank, TV, Telefon. das Badezimmer war aber in einem sehr schlechen Zustand - teilweise auch Schimmel! Ich habe mich aber gewundert, das dieses (soweit möglich war in diesem Zustand) anscheinend gründlich geputzt war. Die Bediesnerin hat sich anscheinend die Mühe gegeben das beste zu tun (auch die nächste Tage merkte man, dass es so ist) aber bei diesem Zustand der Einrichtung war sinnlos. Z.B. der Teppich im Zimmer war schon SEHR dreckig - anscheinend ausser Staubsauger hat er jahrelang nichts anderes gesehen. Das Frühstück ist gleich nichts - Muffins und American Coffee. Also eher kein Frühstück. Wie gesagt die Lage des Hotels ist sehr gut obwohl SOMA wirkt ein bischen gefährlich in der Nacht (Bettler, Obdachlose...) - es ist aber NICHT gefährlich - ich habe auch im anderen Hotels in der nähe übernachtet und es wirkt mehr gefährlich als es ist. Ich kann das Hotel nicht empfehlen weil dieses eher 1* bekommen kann aber nicht 2* und für das Geld.... nur die Lage ist sicher das Geld wert aber sonst würde eher abraten.

“Great, but expected” It's a JW, so my expectations were high, and they were met on every level. Room great, staff super friendly and helpful. Special thanks to their Security team, I needed FedEx packages from the closed and locked FedEx office, and they made it happen, retrieving the packages on an early Sunday morning. Great security staff there. Special thanks to Aaron in the High Velocity restaurant, I ordered a diet coke, but all they have is Pepsi products. I joked and said I hate Pepsi, so Aaron volunteered to see if he could find a diet Coke for me and he DID! I was pleasantly surprised and didn't even ask for it. THAT is service you just can't get anywhere anymore...sounds silly, but is proof that "service" still does exist out there, although rare.

“Great Room and Views!” This was our first stay at the Hyatt Regency in San Francisco. We have stayed many times at the Grand Hyatt, but I am thinking I like the location of the Hyatt Regency for a nice change. Rooms are nice, and we had a great view. I liked being able to open the sliding doors to the outside. It is just steps from the Ferry Building and the Cable Car is right outside the front door, as well as the BART. Would be nice if there was free WIFI, but guess Hyatt figures if you can afford the price of the room, you can pay for WIFI! All in all very nice, and I would definitely stay here again.

“Better than last year, excellent food service” Returned here this year for a large event. Nice rooms, concierge helpful. Food is excellent, esp. BBQ salmon with blueberry chipotle, pork shoulder sandwich with slaw, collard greens, etc. Good southwestern cuisine. Cons: difficult to walk anyplace due to hills. Outdoor pool only, not open in winter.

“Best part was near Union Sq. and in Chinatown...” I was there for about 4 days approximately a month ago. The positives are the location and the price (approx. $115 per night with taxes) considering what SF charges for rooms. Unfortunately the negatives outweigh the positives-- extremely small room and bathroom, and a double bed with a big sag in the middle. Broken tile/dirty grout/basically a very run down room. No a/c so very warm during some warm weather there, then when it turned colder, no heat. Smelled musty and just "3rd world". Wasn't really up to American standards, despite the "you get what you pay for" was understood. The bottome line was would I stay there again? No. I would have researched a little more and found another basic, but more inviting space.

“Great stay!” Single night, king room on floor 6. Hotel in a great location, plenty of food, shopping and things to do in area if that is what you are looking for. Lobby is clean, modern and gives very good first impression. Greeted by hotel staff at concierge and front desk and all are extremely helpful, friendly and just aswesome! Room is standard nothing over the top king bed, decent bathroom with a slow draining tub. Called front desk, they sent someone up but whatever they did, didn't really help still slow drainning. Carpets look new, flat panel TV with pretty poor quality picture, granite in bathroom and on all vanities throughout. Nice view of shopping close by. Gym was very nice, good amount of space and equipment is all good working order. Executive lounge was great, nice view, super sweet conceirge, Marietta Bryan, was always there in the eve greeting me with smile and more than willing to help with anything I needed. Kudos to Marietta! Parking situaiton here is pretty rough, busy location so have been unable to find a spot close by but not a huge deal. They have valet which I can't understand as this is really a business hotel, who is going to valet a car here! Get rid of that and open up the balance of the parking for self park, wake up!!!!!! All in all good hotel, would stay again.

“Not that great...” Well, I needed a place to stay in Los Angeles for a night. (I live in LA but needed a place to sleep near my office for a night). This place was REALLY close to my office. They have another location on Sunset that I drive by all the time. So I gave it a show. $80 something for the night. I have to say, the man behind the desk was HORRIBLE! He was behind a 3 inch thick bullet proof glass. Half the time, you couldnt hear a word he said. And he really wasnt happy working there (And I think he must be the owner) He has NO CLUE as to what he was doing. He made numerous errors and even tried to charge me for 2 nights when I was only staying one (He said I told him2 ) It was rough . A process that should have taken 10 minutes, ended up taking 35 minutes. The rooms were ok. Clean enough for the money. My advise, spend alittle more money and stay somewhere else... The are isnt great. Not very safe at night.

“Clean, Updated, Convenient, Cheap...” Overall, this hotel was clean and in a very convenient location. Hotel is nothing luxurious, just clean and basic. (Then again for $115 a night, I cannot argue) Every restaurant we ate at, we were able to walk to, no problem. Workout facilities were great, treadmills are brand new, with personal TVs. Pool area looked clean and up to date. Wireless internet in the rooms was speedy and easy to setup. The only con, is that a lot of reviewers had talked about free breakfast. This is long gone, there is now a charge of $11 (I think) for a continental breakfast or $14 for the full American. With so many good brunch/breakfast places around, it is worth your time to venture outside. Traders joe’s is right around the corner, great for a quick bottle of wine, or snacks. Overall for the cost, it was great.

“Crushing disappointment” I wanted to celebrate my seven year old namesake's birthday with a special tea. I selected the Willard even though I knew the cost was relatively high. For $150 plus $30 tip we got a glass of champagne for the two adults, a pot of tea each, six small scones (with lemon curd, clotted cream, jams), 12 little cut sandwhiches (peanut butter and jelly, egg salad, chicken salad, ham, and smoked salmon), and 12 small dessert samplers. The food was fine, the service polite, but the price is simply unwarranted. We were given "suggestions" to be sure we were appropriately dressed. The tea was served in a hallway through which passed every sort of costume ranging from shorts/crocs to jeans. It was noisy, at times drowning out the Japanes music which was offered as a Cherry Blossom special. It was neither relaxing nor elegant as it is described. The cost of the tea was disclosed, but I was completely taken aback by the extremely small amounts of food served and the atmosphere. I would never consider returning.

“Absolutely Amazing Hotel” Wow...what a fabulous hotel. Everything was absolutely "HEAVENLY". Check-In was fast and efficient. The location is absolutely the best. Elevators are super-fast. No waiting at this hotel. I had a 41st Floor room overlooking the Hudson River. It was magnificent. Rooms are very plush and the beds and the shower are really of super high quality. If you frequently stay in hotels you will be quite delighted at your decision. Rooms are even of a very nice size (considering most rooms in NYC are extremely small.)

“Good location and views” After reading so many negative review here and yelp, I was starting to worry. However, the hotel was great. Easy check-in, only about a 10 min wait. The room was a decent size, actually big by NYC standards. We stayed on the 39th floor and had a great view. Easy check out too, just drop the key in the express check-out box and your are done. The E train (53rd & 7th) stop but about 30 ft from the door. The A&C were only a few blocks away on 50th & 8th, so you can pretty much get anywhere quickly. It seems like a lot of complaints were from people who wanted some service beyond just a place to sleep (like concierge etc.), but we didn't do anything but sleep there so that's all i can comment on.

“Ok, not bad, but a bit disappointing” I stayed 5 nights at the Crown Plaza, and overall the experience was fine. The room was clean, comfortable, and quiet, and the hotel is situated in a great area. Check in and check out were easy and quick. But overall there is a sense that the hotel has seen better days. It certainly didn't look as new and modern as the pictures on the website would lead you to believe. The carpet in my room was worn; the bathroom needed a re-paint; and the overall decor was quite dated. There was no mini-bar in the room. The lifts were quite slow, and although they worked, they'd sometimes take you to the wrong floor. There was a swimming pool, but for some reason it's an outdoor one, and it was closed for the season. The front desk staff were pleasant, though when I checked out I was surprised I wasn't asked if I'd enjoyed my stay. If I'd been asked, I would have said all of this to them. So, in a nutshell, it was ok, not bad, but not a quality addition to the chain.

“Apprehensions Eased” I was somewhat apprehensive about staying here after reading negative reviews on TripAdvisor. However, we ended up holding a three day conference for about 65 people here in July, 2008. The conference set-up, service, and facilities were fine. I found the hotel staff in general to be very pleasant, competent, and service oriented. According to a letter left in the rooms by the manager, the hotel is "currently in the process of upgrading our accommodations". The letter goes on to talk about "completion of this phase of the renovation later this year that will eventually include the lobby and conference areas". The common areas are in need of renovation, especially the carpet stains. It's not terrible - just needs work. By the way, I never noticed any construction noise, and was never inconvenienced by any renovations. None were apparent on the floors I was using. My sleeping room was generally fine. It was VERY large (could have fit three king-size beds in it), as were the bathroom and a walk-in closet. However, the size of the room and lack of overhead lighting contributed to not having enough light in the room at night - especially at the desk, but also beside the bathroom mirror. The room decor is so-so... with older looking furnishings. One plus is a nice, large flat screen TV. I followed the good advice of another TripAdvisor contributor and requested a room not overlooking the parking lot, or, as the hotel staff calls it, a room on the west side. Each room has a nice sized balcony with two chairs and a table. Nice. Bathroom amenities were Gilchrist and Soames. Not sure if that's good or bad - it was fine for me. Room service for dinner was OK. It was delivered by pleasant staff members with a flower, ice water, and condiments. The food (club sandwich one night, steak the second) was acceptable. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by the hotel given what I had read. I wouldn't hesitate to use the Warwick for another conference. Not fancy, but perfectly satisfactory.

“All About Service” There’s nothing like experiencing holiday time in the City--so invigorating and yet also relaxing! This Dec. we stayed at the Ritz-Carlton on Nob Hill. The building is a gorgeous Neo-Classical style, circa 1909. Upon entering the building one expects to see a grand, expansive Lobby, but this isn’t the case. The Front Desk is off to one side and more perfunctory than impressive. We heard that a multi-phase redesign is planned for the near future. With 8 stories and located lower down the hill, it doesn’t offer quite the panorama that the Fairmont or Mark Hopkins does, but we were thrilled with the impressive night time views (over Chinatown, St. Mary’s Cathedral and up towards Calif. St.) from the large windows in our corner room (#628), located at the end of the hall on the 6th floor. I’d requested a quiet room and it was a wonderfully peaceful environment both day and night with absolutely no intruding sounds. I noticed that the large windows were also openable, something I would have taken advantage of had the season been warmer. Our room had a small foyer containing the honor bar and complimentary coffee station which was hidden away in an attractive wooden chest. We immediately made use of the wine glasses that were provided. The closet with automatic lighting had ample space and plenty of hangers. There were 2 luggage racks, an iron, and in-wall safe. The King bed with Sealy mattress was extremely comfortable--and you can actually arrange to purchase one of these mattresses per the guest info. booklet. In fact, it did seem that most everything in the hotel was buyable. It was a bit disconcerting to find that even a delivered morning newspaper was “for purchase”. Our room was nicely sized, spacious but still exuding a warm feeling, There was a large desk, lounge chair with ottoman, large flat panel TV, (3) phones inc. one in the bathroom, and iPod/MP3 dock. What seems like a small matter, a clock on each bedstand, represented attention to detail that I’ve found in few hotels. Decor was classic with dark woods and warm beige and gold hues. Full-length heavy drapes allowed you to darken the room completely--or (in our case) leave them open to enjoy the gorgeous City lights at night. The lamps were rheostat controlled and provided enough light to comfortably read by. The thermostat controlled forced air heating/cooling system worked efficiently and our room was kept at a comfortable temperature. The bath had marble flooring, counters and tub surround; dual sinks and a separate toilet compartment. The standard size tub/shower had a dual control water saving showerhead. Pressure and temperature were both fine, but unfortunately, the tub drain plugged up (we did report it when we checked out). Plenty of towels plus bathrobes were provided. The hotel offers a spa and fitness center but we didn't get a chance to check out those areas. For business and events guests, there is a separate lounge area and access to special concierge services and around the clock refreshments. When I originally made our reservations I dealt with Fideles, the Executive Reservations Service Coordinator and I was extremely pleased with his prompt and very helpful communications. Once we arrived at the hotel, the flawless service continued. Each time we entered or left the hotel we were greeted by staff members. The valets, front desk personnel, restaurant and lounge wait staff, and housekeepers were all genuinely friendly and attentive. In the evening, 6 large chocolate-covered strawberries on a platter were delivered to our room along with a handwritten “thank you” note from Fideles (once again)--a delightful surprise! And the chocolate-covered strawberries were supremely delicious. We enjoyed appetizers and drinks in the late afternoon and breakfast the next morning in the hotel’s newly reopened, redesigned restaurant/lounge “Parallel 37”. Good quality food and good service, but pricey. When we first checked in we opted for turning over our car to valet parking for the duration of our stay, choosing to take the taxi to dinner (the fabulous Waterbar on the Embarcadero South) and walking up to Grace Cathedral the next morning. Being “car free” for a day is a rare treat for us and we bit the bullet, paying $70 for the valet parking. “Superb service; pricey” sums up our Ritz-Carlton experience, but it was, indeed, a fabulous one and hey, for a special holiday stay--exactly right.
“Very average in any sense” Simply a hotel you won't remembe for anything great but on the other side also for anything too bad. OK for a night stay at the airport but not for more.

“Quaint but definitely not ready for business” Like most who stay at the Driskill, I was anxious to experience the Texas authenticity and charm for which the place is famous. In this I wasn't disappointed. If I had been there on a different sort of trip, say, a family vacation or special weekend, it would have been fine but alas, this was a business trip. For business travellers, the Driskill has big shortfalls. First problem: Internet access. I needed to get online to review some figures for my presentation. The front desk assured me that all I had to do was select the Driskill network. Not so. On calling back, I was transferred to external tech support and put on hold for about 10 minutes. A technician finally answered and helped me tinker around with the connection. The service worked temporarily but quit working after I hung up. Disappointing! I called the front desk (again) and asked to be transferred to tech support (again), complaining that really, they should have basic working internet service. This is Austin, after all! The curt and infuriating reply was that other rooms weren't having a problem - as if it was my fault! So it was back to tech support, back to more hold time . . . are you getting bored? So was I! This went on until late into the evening to no avail which was unfortunate because I was presenting early the next day. Second problem: Fire alarm. During my presentation, which was going well initially, the fire alarm went off complete with flashing lights. No big deal. I kept going and everything seemed fine until . . . "Ladies and gentlemen, please may I have your attention, we can verify that the preceding fire alarm was false. Please disregard, &c". OK, we all stopped and had a good laugh. After the explanation was over, I began to present again, until . . . "Ladies and gentlemen, please may I have your attention, we can verify that the preceding . . ." Again I had to stop! Fewer laughs. I proceeded until again, a third time: "Ladies and gentlemen, please may I have your attention . . ." Oh for heaven's sake! It was like the hotel was trying to sabotage my presentation. Third problem: Transportation to the airport. I won't belabour this but suffice it to say, the hotel did not communicate with the company giving the conference and I ended up standing around on the curb in Austin unnecessarily wasting more time when I should have been en route to my flight. These three separate occurrences convinced me that the hotel is not fit for purpose for business conferences or maybe even business travellers. If you are a casual tourist with time to spare, it's probably a quaint, authentic, charming experience. If you need businesslike dependability and zero drama, there are better options in Austin.

“Great location” The Boston Marriott at Copley Place was a perfect location for a weekend getaway. It is connected to the Prudential Center, so even though it was raining when I was there, I could still shop without getting soaked. The hotel itself has most everything you would expect from a Marriott. The rooms were nice - the beds were very comfortable. We ordered room service, which was prompt and delicious. We did not have any other meals at the hotel. We stayed on the concierge level, but this didn't matter because the services are not available on the weekends. My friend booked a morning massage, while the rest of us enjoyed the pool. The pool area is lovely with a huge skylight to let in natural light. There is a hot tub and a sauna, with the workout area in a room just off the pool. I did try to upgrade to a suite with Marriott points, but was told there was no suite available, which was a little hard to believe - the hotel is massive. Overall, a very pleasant stay with a perfect location for shopping and sightseeing.

“Location and comfort in Chelsea” What a great little place in Chlesea. Absolutely no complaints about anything- room was fine, staff great and even a complimentary breakfast. Since I was by myself, the rather smallish room did not bother me although if there were two people-it could be cramped. But on the whole, it is a great little property. The location was outstanding in that I could return from my conference and after changing, set off exploring. There is nothing *fancy* about the hotel, but it is clean and the staff exceptionally nice. Go to Hilton website for best rates.

“I didn't stay there, but the Boston Creme Pie is worth the visit” I didn't stay at this hotel, but knowing that it is the home of the first Boston Creme Pie was reason enough for me to visit. I walked in and the staff was very polite and helpful when I needed to find the restaurant, and the wait staff in the restaurant was great. The Boston Creme Pie and glass of port were the last things I experienced before heading back to the airport and it was the perfect way to end my vacation.

“Okay hotel. 4th stay” Stayed here again for 2 nights in a king on the first floor facing the pool. Check in was fine. Room had kind of a smoky smell even though it was non-smoking. The 2nd day it was more pronounced after the deodorizer or what ever they used wore off. Bed was comfortable. I could not get the aircon/fan to work even though I used their instructions on the bedside table. Temperature was not bad so I did not complain. Toilet would run occasionally. Fridges are turned off at check in so plan accordingly if you bring perishables at check in. I could not get the wired internet to work but I could get in with the wireless but you would have to log back in every so often. There is noise and light that comes in under the door. They are not very generous with the towels. 2 bath, 2 hand, and 2 wash cloths. If I had an extra towel I would have put it at the base of the door. The breakfast is still the same and there is plenty of it. If they are having a meeting on site the breakfast room gets halved so seats can be scarce. All in all this hotel is a great value so we will return.

“Nice beds, pillows and service” This is the best place to stay when visiting Ohio State if you can get a room. The beds and pillows are comfortable and the people are very friendly. There is always Ohio State merchandise on sale as well. Price was decent

“Great location for Times Square, a bit inconvenient for anything else” We stayed here two nights right after the NYC snowstorm. We left before New Years Eve, thank goodness. The hotel was wonderful; right on Times Square, close to the ticketing counter for Broadway shows, in the middle of all the bustle of NYC. The rooms were comfortably sized (much bigger than I expected in Times Square), and the staff was very friendly and accomodating. Beds were standard Marriott heaven. The only inconvenience of the hotel itself was the dual elevator set-up, which I guess was necessary for the real estate. You basically had to get into a small elevator to get to the real main floor of the hotel, then walk across the lobby to the real elevators. Not a big deal though. The biggest issue I had was how impossible it is to get in and out of Times Square/get to and from the hotel. We weren't even driving but the crowds were insane. I expected mobs of people, but with the snow and puddles and it being almost New Years Eve, it was basically a mosh pit getting to and from the hotel. I guess that's par for the course for Times Square though.
“Perfect Location - Great Hotel” The hotel is in a great location for sight seeing - close to the T and walking distance to the Boston Common and Newbury Street"

“Great, friendly staff” My mother-in-law stayed here for two nights; we live about 6 minutes away. We brought our small children over to hang out in the lobby and decided to go ahead and have dinner there since the kids were having fun and the bar was loud (no worries about the kids disturbing other people). We went back today to swim in the pool, and overall we just had a blast. The staff was beyond accommodating with our kids and even allowed my mother-in-law to check out at 2 p.m. on the day she left. I love the location near the Domain--you can walk to great restaurants and even catch a movie.

“Fabulous hotel right in the centre of Austin” We stayed here for 2 nights and we were very impressed with this hotel. On check in, we were delighted to get a free upgrade to a bigger room and it was beautiful. The staff were very friendly and helpful and they gave us loads of ideas about things to do in Austin. We had lunch in the hotel bakery/cafe both days and it was delicious. The hotel is located on 6th St, right beside all of the entertainment and only a short walk from the Bat Bridge. We had a great stay here and would definately return in the future.

“Central, clean and comfy” Booked the doubletree chelsea on expedia and the main reason for booking was a) central location and b) two beds!!! With flighs from London and for 3 nights it was £525 each The hotel is located within very easy distance of two tube stops which between them serve most of manhattan and Brooklyn including Times Square, Macy's area and bus terminal as well as battery park and ferry port. We used the subway as it was easy and cheap. Taxis were plntiful down the road. You would need to ask for 29th Street between 6th and 7th (From Newark cost about $65 including tolls). Its barely in Chelsea and actually aonly 10 minutes walk from Macys so almost a midtown hotel! The lobby area is small but well decoratedand suitable shoudl you need to wait around. Small bar and breakfast area which alwasy seemed to have a few people in. We didnt eat at the hotel so couldnt comment on the breakfast. in-room dining menu loked good with plenty of choice. Reception were helpful and extreemly polite upon checkin (and later when our key didnt work!!) and you get a warm cookie upon checkin - always a bonus!! there are only two lifts and yes you do have to wait around a bit, but not sooo long. the lists are also quite big so plenty of room for passengers and luggage! We had a non smoking room on 5th floor (508 if you're interested!!) looked out over 29th street (not so exciting). Was quiet at night apart from the snow ploughs at 7am. The rooms are small, but quite normal for NYC. We had two big doubles and somehow they managed to squish a wardrobe and desk and bedside cabinet in too. The beds were soft and very comfy, 4 big fluffy pillows per bed - perfect after a days shopping!! Bathroom with bath and overhead shower. Plenty of towels and nice complimentary toiletries (and a note if you have forgotten anything reception will provide). It was a nice hotel, nothing spectacular but certainly worth staying in. Will stay again due to price, location, TWO BEDS which were lovely;-)

“Nice hotel” I do not agree with some of the negative reviews on this hotel and I am very picky. My room was large and comfortable and clean. I had all of the things I require for a good stay: clean, clean, clean, comfortable bed, thermostat, refrigerator, Internet access (at $9.95 a day, I did NOT like that, I think it should be free), quiet, newspaper each morning, good location, and good service. I was paying meeting rates and it felt fine for the price. I believe I may have been upgraded as I had a spacious suite with a balcony. The concierge could not have been more helpful and polite as was the front desk staff. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great value and great electronics” Okay, so the rooms are very modern. What was important to me was that the mattress is outstanding and so is the TV and stereo system. This is the place for audiophiles! It is probably a little too sleek and trendy for some -- it is the "Hard Rock" afterall. Service is outstanding. Room service would bring me anything reasonable that I wanted cooked. They have a steak salad that is delicious. I've stayed in a number of different rooms and one week that I stayed here, I ended up being stuck in the room sick -- the hotel staff brought me stuff from the drug store and called to check how I was doing. How can anyone say that it isn't a warm place? It's the people who make a place warm and welcoming. Moreover, I travel to Chicago a lot and this is one of the best hotels around for comfort, service and value. The rooms may not be to some people's taste in terms of decor, but it isn't suppose to be your home -- only a place to sleep at night. I like the fans in the rooms because they can be used to drown out outside noise or you can turn them off, if you find them annoying. I think this is a wonderful hotel and if you don't like the grey, order some nice colorful flowers to compensate!

“Enjoyed the Biltmore” My husband and I just spent a week at the Biltmore, staying in room 3313 in the Valley Wing, a nice large, well kept room,overlooking a smaller pool, for a $265 convention rate.( The third floor rooms have no balconies.) We were prepared for the extra charges and all billing was correct. The hotel is an architectural delight - the grounds lovely - most of the staff are more than pleasant. I took the gratis architectural tour of the hotel and grounds and it was extremely well done, done by Nathan, the lead concierge and 13 year employee . ( I tipped him $10, but he did not have his hand out...) The front desk clerk felt a bit defensive when we registered, but calmed down when I was reasonable about room questions. Apparently many of the rooms are so different in size, ammendities, that it is probably a real set up for confusion/disappointment. It is also a very large hotel,( like sister property, Grand Waliea) so must need to have conventions to be profitable. We really loved the Wright's restaurant; grill and pool cafes were also good. Our maid did a great job, so I hope she got the extra we were charged each day.( I left more...) Attention to detail: our heat wasn't functioning and it was dealt with very quickly by two pleasant fellows. We were given a late check out at 2pm with no extra charges. They let us park our rented motorcycle in the valet lot. ( self parking is a a pain, as mentioned earlier by others) The carpeting in the room had a few spots, but it took me two days to notice...sheets, towels, robes were excellent and i loved the desert flower shampoo etc. Occasionally there was uncaring, lackluster service, but it was the exception, not the rule. (Phoenix has really low unemployment.)The pool outside our windown was pretty noisy one day with high energy team building stuff....so was glad I was not napping! Concierge staff were great - helping us get to the wonderous Barrio Cafe, Le Grande Orange Grocery, and Desert Botanical Garden. Also loved the area of the Biltmore - there were actually mature neighborhood trees being nurtured! All in all, the Biltmore made giant, overbuilding Phoenix a good place to visit. It's expensive, but then it is an iconic property with its Frank Lloyd Wright influences and interesting history.

“Definitely not a 4 star hotel” Won this via Hotwire at a decent price for the location.
