But there was hair in the bathroom behind the door, the room felt kind of gross (carpeting mainly) and the beds were TINY. How they were considered doubles was beyond me. At check-in, only one room of our booked 2 room stay was available. The clerk, when asked about bypassing the LONG line to check back for Room 2 later, replied "you'll have to wait, everything in life requires a wait". THIS was our check-in/first impression. Ummm, NOT customer-service friendly. Our TV went out and a lightbulb was burned out. This took 3 separate trips to have both fixed and when the TV was pulled out from the wall, the NASTY debris under the dresser was sickening. The room was VERY hot although we had the A/C at 60 for 4 days straight and kept the blinds closed. The hotel was overrun w/a tourist group and the last 2 days were horrible in getting elevators. Just be warned if you see a huge group milling in the non-existant lobby that you're in for a wait. There were 1,000 in town, we probably had 200+ of them at the hotel. All trying to visit each other in their rooms and meet in the Lobby at the same time. Although the location to Times Square is excellent, I really didn't feel this hotel had anything else going for it. In fact, if I would use Hotwire again, I would purposely NOT choose Times Square area just to avoid this place.

“Get it cheap and its worth the stay...” Get your room cheap and the hotel is worth the stay. Pay over $100 and you will be disappointed. Read the other reviews...they are ALL correct...the good, the bad, and the ugly. You can get rates for less than $60 here on the weekend. Rates go up during the week. Price shop at TripAdvisor.com. Always check the hotel's website first before accepting a 3rd party rate. At that price, you will have difficulty finding a place this good in Houston. The other places nickel and dime you. This place is what it is, an older hotel trying to improve itself without completely shutting down. Now for my review... I rarely stay at a Sheraton because they are inconsistent compared to Hampton Inn and Marriott Garden Inns which is what I compared this Sheraton brand. While this appears to be a "full service" hotel, it is not full service quality which is why there are mixed reviews. This disappoints people so focus on the negative...which are all true but this place is really acceptable if you want a clean room with a comfortable bed. Here is the good... During this visit, I spent 2 nights at Sheraton and one night at the Hilton Post Oak. Truthfully, the standard rooms were very much the same. This Sheraton has a plus in that the parking is free. The parking is fenced. A security guard comes out late at night which is why it appears unsecure. The letter given to guests is apparently because a car was broken into which is why the extra security. Most big city hotels have extra security at night...this one was just more straight forward about it. The atmosphere at this hotel was straightforward. The staff are just staff and were better than at the Hilton Post Oak...except the Sheraton had southern accents. Some staff had better customer service skills than others. Something to consider...next door there is a well-maintained doggy park. The dog park next door to the hotel was well-groomed, the pets well-behaved, and also had a walking park for runners and walkers. For those planning a family event, there is covered seating at the doggy park and a playground for the kids. Access to the park for guests is from the Sheraton's back parking lot. Next door to the dog park was a free lovely walking garden for the plant lovers out there. The garden is maintained by a private group and a hidden jewel...but no dogs allowed. After taking a walk, cool off in the clean Sheraton swimming pool. A night some guests brought in their own pizza and had a pool party so for teens and young adult groups, this is a plus. Our room overlooked the pool and faced the highway, but we heard no noise. Breakfast was too expensive for a small buffet at $10 each. The breakfast tasted good but choices were very limited which is why I say "too expensive." They would get a lot more if they would reduce the breakfast to $5. For now the breakfast is served in a lounge area while remodeling is taking place so it seems they are actually discouraging people from eating at the hotel. They do seem to have room service, but they don't pick up the dinner trays from the halls for a very, very long time which gives the halls a cluttered look. The rooms themselves are actually large. The bathrooms are small...but after the remodel, I believe this will change. The remodel is quiet. They are renovating one floor at a time starting at the 9th floor. They are ripping out walls so I am sure this place will look much better in the future. For now, don't expect 4 star quality or 4 star service. If like free parking, this is an acceptable place for businesses. If you have to feed a family, go down the street to the (east) to Taco Cabana to eat affordably or across the highway to Chick-fil-a. There is a Starbucks and lots more food places on both sides of the highway about .25 to .5 miles down the road which stay open late. Walk during the day...you are in a big city.

“When you need an LAX hotel, stay here” Seems to me that the LAX hotel market is rather dismal, inexcusably so for such a major hub. For one thing, it’s mature... most of the properties have been around for 20 years or more. I don’t find it to be particularly user friendly; Century Blvd. is kind of a nightmare for a driver to navigate, and even worse for a pedestrian. Aircraft noise can be an issue. Venture much beyond and you can wind up in some pretty unwelcoming areas. And one really has to shop around for a good value. The Custom is a terrific alternative. Not sure what this hotel used to be, but the Joie de Vivre chain came in and really jazzed it up. I liked the aesthetics of my room a lot, particularly the bathroom, and when I looked out the window, I saw what appeared to be a surprisingly trendy pool deck. Granted, the common areas are a bit scuffed up in parts, but this is a busy hotel. I had a rental car the entire time, but I stayed here on the last night on my trip and was sick of driving. I was pleasantly surprised to see a few restaurant options within walking distance, including a couple that are located in a shopping/condo complex right next door. The immediate area had a bit more of a neighborhood feel than one would find anywhere else around here, and it was quiet – no jets flying past your window – seemingly safe and less congested. And they had free wi-fi! With parking and tax, I paid under $150, so I have no complaints on that score. Some people probably stay here for the duration of their Los Angeles stay. I wouldn’t, just because the Westchester/LAX area isn’t one that I regard as particularly convenient to the rest of LA. But because this place really hit so many of the high points for me, I would definitely stay here again for a late arrival or early departure.

“A few glitches but fine” Don't plan on an early check-in on a Sunday. They attempted to put us and our two therapy yorkies on the first floor over looking a rather ugly parking lot. Children were runnning amuk and being very boisterous. We knew that would not work with our pets, as they are used to dealing with Alztheimers and nursing homes. Not loud invasive activities. So, we waited until an appropriate room came up, and staff did the best to accomodate us and put us on 4th floor over looking the beautilful grounds. The hotel itself has been beautifully renovated. large rooms--very spacious. Disappointed--no mini fridges in rooms. We were tired after a day trip to Fredricksburg, and opted to have dinner on the veranda at the hotel. Service Very very slow. We had to go inside to grab our utensils, s and p shakers etc. Simply understaffed and not prepared for the glut of conventions that were taking place. Still there was something rather charming about this hotel with the open pits and three pools. Rooms were adequte and bedding very comfortable. Unless, you are into chain restaurants, plan on making a twenty minute drive to --a real restaurant. We would stay here again , now knowing the ups and downs. Nice business center.

“Disappointing” I love Kimptons and had great experiences until staying here. The coupe de gras was they neglected to provide neither my wake up call nor the back up wake up call. Kimpton has only had this property for about a month. They have a ton of work to do. Other issues - no drinking glasses in the room, we called to ask for some and instead they brought ice. They didn't have a selection of towels in the bathroom, and didn't deliver the proper paper the first day, delivered papers late the 2nd day. Overall, they just don't have it all together yet. I could have spent less, had a wakeup call, etc. etc. When I told the mgr about my lack of wakeup call, she apologized, but didn't seem to think it was such a big deal. Also, would recommend staying on a high floor and not near the elevator. They put us on the 3rd floor - street noise all night long and the dinging of the elevator outside our door.

“Pretty good for the location” Cleanliness can be better but acceptable. Rooms are small but the price and location cannot be better. (booked with expedia with flight package) It is right on magnificent mile.

“convient for ongoing flights” Rooms a good size, clean, room service not very good could not understand I wanted slippers they bought sugar. good size gym, internet expensive being $5.95 for 30minutes. courtesy shuttle to airport, we usually stay at Embassy suites North which I think would still stay there again as alot more room and breakfast and managers drinks but have to shop around. Starbucks in the hotel made the best coffee I had in the time I was in america. We told the girl as well.

“correcto” solo estuve una noche y no supe situarlo bien pero en otra ocasion que volví a Washington me fijé en él y la verdad es que estaba a un paso del Capitolio y proximo a todos los Museos y Monumentos mas importantes. Hotel correcto, serio y no puedo opinar nada mas porque lo vi de noche unicamente.

“Roaches” Came in from a long flight.The heat was not working. Check in and tried to get some sleep. Well, i was awaken with roaches in my bed. Called front desk around one or two am. Person did not offer anything at all.Took my clothes at first light to have dry clean and went to front desk and asked for a refund. Person did not give and stated i would have to call back on monday, this was saturday on a two day stay. Check out and went to another hotel. Overall bad, hotel, bad service, bad employees, just bad all the trip with this hotel. Not worth the headace.

“Fantastic place to stay in NYC!!” I loved staying here!! Bed was so comfortable, spotless room, marble bathroom and very reasonable price. Staff were very helpful. I liked overlooking the bridge, seeing trains and people going past and even had a view of Lower Manhattan buildings. Yes the area (Chinatown) does have a bit of a smell out on the street, but you can walk to the Brooklyn Bridge, Heliport, Battery Park and trains to take you to midtown Manhattan in 10 minutes. Thank you Hotel 91 for a great stay in NYC.

“Excellent Staff - Excellent Stay!!” Conducted training at SCH and my 2nd stay was even more enjoyable than the first!! You're about 20 minutes from the Airport. You get a resort type experience and atmosphere without the resort nickel-n-diming. Customer service is OUTSTANDING and I must thank Ms. Angela Willette and her amazing staff. Everyone is very attentive and eager to please!! Rooms are clean and comfortable. Club Level Room offered great food and atmosphere (only con is charge for drinks). Fitness Center is among the best I've used. Room Service food and quality were great (the Salmon Burger is a must!!). SCH is close to host of restaurants and shopping. I'd stay here again on my next PHX trip - whether on business or pleasure.

“Classic, elegant hotel” It's an oldy but goody. Great location in Philly, easy walk to most sites. The interior of rooms were nice, and everything worked well. I was on an inside interior courtyard, so no natural light. Fairly quiet overall, but easy to hear people in the hallway. Decor is dated. Poor wayfinding. Best feature: complimentary access to one of the best health clubs in the country. I would only stay here if someone else was footing the bill.

“Location Trumps All” The lobby of this hotel is like a woman who aged and didn't try to keep herself nice. You can still see her good bones, but little has been done to update it or make it beautiful. The room we had was quite small, and despite the fact that we had cool fall weather it was somehow humid in the room. The bed was comfortable, and the lamps had extra sockets on them so we could plug in all of our many chargables. Surprisingly, the bathroom is great: euro-modern, with good lighting, a marble double shower with room enough for two. It had a hand-held shower as well as a rain shower from above. Very nice. There is a full-length mirror in the room, and a good sized closet. Most of all, the location of the hotel stands out. It is half a block from Michigan Avenue, with it's many restaurants and magnificent shops. The hotel is convenient and had some nice ameneties.
“Average stay...” Pretty average stay, it was ok, we got it on priceline, but it was just ok. Nothing spectacular.

“Nice place” Stayed here for a famiy wedding. After reading other reviews (and asking the concierge) decided not to pay for the internet service. Location was perfect. Close to Pike St Market, Belltown, the pier, and Pioneer Square. The staff was exceedingly helpful and pleasant. Rooms were clean and well appointed. A nice feature was the "curtain clip" that held the curtains together so we could avoid the morning sun and get some sleep. Restaurant/Bar had good food and was reasonably priced

“Updated Property. Clean and Comfortabel” This Fairfield Inn is very close to my client's office and is on the outskirts of Indy. Many restaurants and a supermarket located just across the street. This property has been updated with new amenities--a nice workout room and a pool that doesn't have windows looking right into it. Rooms are clean and comfortable. Front desk staff have always been very helpful and kind.

“Basic hotel” Staff kind of rude, some where ok, but overall there is an attitude problem with some of the staff. The hotel itself is in a good location with the acception of the back of the hotel. Beware, there is a construction site. I asked 3 different employees if there would be work and noise on the weekend and they all responded with a "no." Well, at 7:30 am the draglines were loud and noise was really loud. The rooms are basic and small, but clean. I stayed at the Omni, Marriot on water, the Hilton near sea world ( terrible.) The Omni rooms were newer with a sliding bathroom door, I hated it. The Hyatt on the dock had horrible beds. If you can get a room facing the front of the Marriott I believe you will be happy.

“Good location, nice views” The location of the Grand Hyatt is very convenient, and the views from the bar & restaurant on top are great. Our bay-view room was smaller than the one we'd had at the St. Francis last summer, and our view was not quite as good (although some bay-view rooms would have truly fantastic views). Our room faced toward the financial district (which was actually rather attractive at night), with some views of the bay at the sides. The few things that brought the hotel down a notch for me may not matter to others. The lobby was virtually non-existent, with nothing there but the check-in desk & concierge. No sundry shop, no gathering place, etc. I missed the feel and amenities of the St. Francis's lobby. The buffet breakfast, while in a room with a great view, was disappointing and sub-par (particularly the muffins and croissants). It's been a while since I've had croissants that bad. Aside from these things, I would have given the hotel 4 stars.

“Beautiful lobby and property, average rooms” I stayed in the Manchester Grand Hyatt for a weekend in September. The hotel is incredible. Enormous lobby, beautiful pools, great facilities. However, the rooms are very blah, although the harbor tower has goregous views from the top floors.

“Good Location” Went on a girly weekend to NYC and booked this hotel as part of a cheap internet deal. We were a bit disappointed on arrival that the rest of the hotel wasn't as nice as the lobby. 2 of us had to change our room immediately as the lights didn't work and the window was stuck open. We ended up a 5 minute walk (on the same floor) from our friends. Our rooms did look like they had been decorated in the seventies but they were fairly clean and one had a fridge, the other had a fantastic view of the Empire State building. Anyway as we didn't plan to spend too much time here we got over our disappointment and relished in the fantastic location. Close to loads of top attractions and near the subway.

“Very Good, but not Great” I recently stayed here while in San Jose on business. The hotel is nothing special to look at from the outside, but the interior is much better. Service was very friendly. Room and hotel public areas are nice, but nothing to rave about. Overall, this is a good hotel and a reasonable value for the money, but after reading some of the other reviews, one might think this was a Ritz or Four Seasons property. It isn't. If you book here with reasonable expectations you will be pleased. If you expect a five star hotel, you may be disappointed.

“It was....fine (sigh...)” Don't want to be unfair. Great bed. Fine room. But the lobby has a vaguely tired air, and not in a Tom Waits hipster kind of way. A stain on a chair. A dated carpet. Ancient feeling elevators, but not classy. For just a bit more, I could have stayed in a 4-star hotel nearby that would have left me invigorated, not worn out. And charging for internet access is so...Stone Age. Jeez, guys, this is Chicago! This is the 21st Century!

“Worth a Visit, Not a Stay” The hotel itself is worth a visit inside, visit to the pool and bar, but I can't recommend staying over night. The staff is very helpful but overwhelmed with helping people just visiting the hotel, so why bother staying to wait in line for valet after 20 pool revelers. Adding to this the hotel rooms are very tiny (smallest I have ever seen, even smaller than NY) and terribly outdated with mismatched thrift store furniture. The doors & windows aren't sealed properly allowing in noise from the parties. I have no idea how this hotel is holding on to its 4* rating with their room quality, it is no more than a 3*. We also found no need to stay in this Hollywood area, once you do a quick walk up the street, maybe spend 1/2 hour, it's done. This area is central to drive everywhere else, but there's no need to stay in this area and certainly not at this hotel, so stay somewhere nicer for your money.
“アッパーウエストのホテル” 部屋はせまかったですが清潔でした。二つのビルを後からつなげたような構造でした。周辺の環境は落ちついていました。夜でも危険とはおもいませんでした。地下鉄の駅から歩く途中にスーパー、ドラッグストア、飲食店などがあるので、困りませんでした。

“Loved my stay, incredible staff” Close to convention center in gas lamp area. I had a wonderful king suite, loved modern yet sea inspired decor. Huge tub in bathroom. Comfy bed. Enjoyed free wine in evening and coffee in the morning. Weather was bad so could not check out terrace. The valets were helpful and great at getting taxi cabs. Loved front desk staff. Only negatives were the workout facility was tiny tiny, outside street noise loud on Fri & Sat nights, and JSix restaurant was not good.

“Location, Location, Location!!!!!” This hotel is perfect for a weekend getaway with your spouse. The location is the best. The rooms are very nice, even had a view of the Empire State Building. Applebee's is adjoining in the lobby, but there is much better choices right out the door. I would not hesitate to stay again. The lobby bar is a nice place for a nightcap and the staff was friendly and helpful!

“it's ok” I stayed at the Palomar two weeks ago and it was OK. If you get a good deal from something like Priceline for about $125, then it's worth it. But full rate? ($200 or so) Forget it - there are better choices like the hotel right across the street. I guess my view is colored by the fact that I had a dark room - no light at all due to the adjoining building. So depressing since I tend to work in the morning before going out. I guess they would have moved me if I had asked, but I unpacked the night before and packing again was too much trouble. My view is also affected by the great stay I had the other month at the San Diego Residence Inn: full breakfast in the morning, great room, and staff who would greet you with a "Good morning" as soon as you stepped off the elevator. Now that's hospitality. Oh, and that fire alarm at about 3am? Talk about a hear attack! I was told by staff that it happens "occasionally". Occasionally?!? Fix it, is my advice.

“A Beautiful Facility” This is a very lovely facility that sits in the heart of beautiful San Diego. The views from all the rooms are spectacular and breathtaking. Centrally located to wonderful restaurants, shopping and sporting events. We stayed the weekend of January 28-29, 2012. This is actually our third visit to the Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego. We enjoy the amenities offered and excellent service from staff members. This place is spotless and the grounds are clean and well kept. I must admit that I am not thrilled about the price to pay to park your vehicle overnight at the facility. I congratulate the management of the Grand Hyatt for maintaining such a beautiful facility.

“Reasonable motel for budget travelers” I paid $130 including tax for two nights for a nonrefundable, non-changeable reservation with full payment made about two months in advance. Since I charged it to Discover card when they were offering 5% cashback for travel and made the reservation from hotels.com [preferred online partner] through the discover card website, I got an additional about 4% cashback from Discover card. So I ended up paying net about $118 including tax, which is a decent deal for LA where hotels tend to be expensive and this rate included a free, basic breakfast. As others have pointed out, parking space is tight and entry is narrow so drive carefully. Hotel was only about half full so I did not have parking problem This is an older property so come with realistic expectations. The mattress was somewhat saggy, and as several others have pointed out, the carpet is old and dingy. The rooms and bathrooms are small but sink is outside bathroom so if there are two of you, that may be convenient. The bathroom tile and bathtub seem to be redone recently but the water control for shower head is finicky going from hot to cold very quickly. Hotel only provides soap, shampoo and towels so bring other toiletries. Old CRT TV but reasonably large size squeezed in corner; good part is about 66 cable channels including HBO As Super8 website says, every room has old fridge and old microwave but they worked fine. The furniture [table, chairs, dresser] are old and rather dingy but worked OK. Window AC unit seems new and worked fine without excessive noise. Sink had one blown light bulb but I got a new one from reception. One lamp above dresser did not work. Manager lives onsite and was friendly, cooperative and helpful with directions as was the receptionist. I asked for room not on Huntington Dr or Poplar so would not be disturbed by traffic noise and manager cheerfully and readily accommodated me. Basic breakfast with bread, two types of cereal, muffins, danish, coffee, orange juice, milk. Frozen waffles on Saturday but not on Friday. Area around motel did not seem very safe so be careful after dark Gas station opposite motel Has WIFI but I did not use; has computer with internet connection in lobby [$5/hour] All in all, this is a reasonable choice for those on a limited budget. I stayed here mainly for the location, which is not too far from Pasadena.

“Great hotel next to Chinatown!” This is the 4th time I have stayed at this hotel, Sept 14-19, and I am always impressed by the view (Coit tower and SF Bay & Sausalito), the size of the rooms, and the friendliness of the staff. Plus free WiFi! The only drawback is the expense of valet parking, which you can solve by parking in the lot across the street. I brought my bike and kept it in the room with no hassle. You can bike all over town via the Embacadero a few blocks to the east. Highly recommend!

“GREAT rooms, poor service” Beautiful, large, pseudo-suite rooms. If you're into nice tvs, you'll love the ones in the rooms here. Beds are fantastic, with a huge sofa sectional on the other side of the room. The tv is well-placed in the room to be seen whether lying in the bed or sitting on the sofa. We also agree with recent posts about dim lighting in the bathroom. The biggest problem here though is with the front desk staff, as most all of them need more training. Both times I called down to ask to be connected to a friend's room, Keisha put me on hold three times, each time coming back to re-ask for the spelling of the name "Weiss". When we stopped by to ask for directions for the nearest fitness center, she set us out on foot in the opposite direction. We are staying as part of a large group, and when we went downstairs to pay the bill to check out, another clerk said she didn't know how to do the check-out for a group - that person would not be in until the next day. And yesterday we came back in from being out all day and our room had not been made up. A manager came up with replacement towels, asked if we could make the beds up ourselves, and offered us free breakfast in the morning. Sure enough the next morning, getting the desk staff to understand that our breakfast to be covered took 15 minutes and another visit from a different manager. Then there was confusion because the hot breakfast items are billed from the kitchen window in the breakfast room, but the cinnamon rolls are billed from the counter in the lobby. It created two different bills, which confused the girl at the desk even more. This is a beautiful hotel, and very comfortable. I would think that with a couple of weeks of "stand-down" training for each employee, they would have a great product to sell here.

“Very nice hotel, great location in NYC, highly recommend!” We just returned from a 3 night stay at the Hilton Times Square over the 4th of July (we used Hilton points for this stay). This is a VERY nice hotel. Beautiful lobby with floor to ceiling windows (not dark at all, per the previous reviewer!), excellent location off 42nd St. Very LARGE rooms (the largest in midtown), very clean, new and tastefully decorated with good closet/dresser space. We had a great view of midtown and the river, and could not hear any street noise in the room. A/C worked just fine and kept the room cool during the 90+ degree weather. We did not hear ANY noise from doors slamming or from people in the other rooms. Only one small complaint - the bed was OK but a bit soft (just a mattress with a thin feather bed that was too small for the king mattress)...the newer Doubletree and Hampton beds are more comfortable than the beds at this Hilton. The bathroom was bigger than average with plenty of counter space and nice Crabtree & Evelyn products. Water pressure was fine and we never had a cold shower. All staff we encountered were very pleasant and helpful, from the bell staff to the front desk and housekeeping. We did not eat in the hotel, but the bar in the lobby looked nice and there were always people there. Overall, we really enjoyed this hotel. It is so nice, new, and clean, and the location was perfect for us. It is a wonderful retreat in midtown and we highly recommend it!

“Best Hotel Stay in Chicago Yet!” I stayed for a week at the Amalfi hotel and had an amazing experience. I've stayed for the same amount of time for business in Chicago before, and have never had this great of an experience. Upon check in, I was happy to see the intimacy of the lobby and professionalism of the staff. When I told the front desk staff I would be unable to make breakfast the next morning due to leaving early, they sent up a breakfast to me that evening for the next morning. They were VERY knowledgable about the local area, public transit, and recommended the perfect restaurants for me based on my food likes. The rooms are spacious, the bathrooms are huge. The showers have dual shower heads and the water pressure was great. The work out room is open 24/7 and has TV's on the machines which I love. They also had medicine balls, matts and free weights. The breakfasts are good, if not a bit limited. But all I really require is cereal and they had many options for that. They have breakfast right outside your room, on your floor, so no need to be awake to grab a bite! Very convenient. Also you can lounge around in the provided bathrobe and slippers which are simply heavenly. I also slept the best I've ever slept in a hotel in their beds. The room was quiet and I didn't hear the busy city outside at all! I'm not much for cocktails but the reception was decent. They had open bar and some cold cuts with bread/spread as appetizers. Didn't appeal to me very much, but it was a nice perk. The location was fantastic for public transit on every El line, and most bus lines. If not directly outside the hotel, they are only a few blocks away. You're also right by a CVS to purchase metro cards. My only complaint would be that the valet parking is quite expensive, but it's Chicago and I knew what I was in for anyhow. Next time, I will be staying at the Amalfi again for sure, but will most likely rely on the public transit since it's so convenient to the hotel and much less expensive. The staff at the hotel went above and beyond the call of duty to make my experience exceptional. I stay at a lot of hotels, and I've never been given this much personal attention. It was truly extraordinary and they will get my business again. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the Chicago area and it's within their budget. The amount of service and amenities you get for the cost and location is superb.

“Very Good Choice” Stayed here during the early part of September and it was a very good choice overall. The hotel appears to be quite new, maybe a couple of years old as it still appears very fresh. We are always impressed by the rooms Hampton have to offer and this was highlighted here, it had everything we required, nice comfy bed, fridge (not a mini bar), microwave, safe and a television which was obviously new as it was the most up to date television I have found in a hotel room. The staff were very friendly and the breakfast was good, nothing fancy but good all the same. It is quite a walk into downtown Denver and as we had no car this was our way of getting there. The area to the north east of the hotel appears to be quite chic and there are a few restaurants/wine bars/bars within a ten minute walk. We loved The Alehouse which is within that ten minute walk and has fantastic views of the downtown area at night. The food here was excellent and was always busy which is a very good sign. Nice place to stop for a drink on the way to and from downtown. About 100 yards from here is the Ice Cream Man which is a shop which sells ice cream, surprise surprise, however this is no ordinary ice cream shop. It is in the shape of an giant milk urn and on our Friday night there we found a line of people about 40 yards long waiting to be served at 10 pm !!! How cool is that. We also found it very safe to walk in the area and had no qualms about doing so. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in a nice area but with a 20 - 25 min walk into the downtown area. It is a nice walk though.

“Horrible costumer service” Just to be clear - I did not stay at this hotel. I tried to stay at this hotel and while booking with Travelocity, I was assured rooms were available for my dates. I went through the multiple steps (including giving my credit card # twice) to book the room. The last step said "ERROR - no rooms avialble". OK, fair enough, Travelocity isn't the hotel. Let's call the hotel directly. Two phone calls - no one picks up either time and a machine answers saying they will call the customer back - no return phone call. Forget it. Plenty of other places to stay in SF!

“fancy but very small rooms” Was looking to stay at this hotel for a few nights as my cousin was getting married and having his functions at this same hotel. The room itself is fancy if not very tiny even for NYC, i suppose i would recommend this property for anyone that was looking for someplace hip and convenient to central park. It is relatively pricey even when using priceline, though perhaps not since this is NYC during a busy month. The atmosphere is chic and the place was clean and adequately furnished.

“So far, my favorite perch in San Francisco” So far, my favorite perch in SF. We had a small but lovely room (extraordinarily comfortable bed) with bay windows overlooking the city. Yes, you pay for some extra$ (martinis and valet parking), but the concierge couldn't have been more helpful. No attitude toward our (well-behaved) kids which is unusual in SF. We parked up the street to help meet our budget. Take your kids to the hilltop park a few steps up Nob Hill and across from Grace Cathedral.

“Very Nice Hotel, good value, great location” I stayed here for a 3 day conference. I read some of the reviews and was a bit concerned. I needn't have been. This is a very nice hotel. The common areas were stylish, with lots of places to sit. My room was large, clean and comfortable. It was on the 6th floor and had been renovated recently. There was a nice desk. the bathroom was large and clean. The area is close to many restaurants. I chose not to drive, took a cab from the airport. I walked to the Stags Head Pub, which was an excellent pub, with great beer selection. There are lots of restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. Very good experience.

“Very nice choice south of Market” Beautiful older hotel, reasonable priced. Rooms have very high ceilings. TV didn't work at first but front desk was very responsive in getting a technician up to fix it.

“Nice..” I am a diamond member so stay in a lot of Hilton owned hotels and also very very picky about where I lay my head down at night... And I am comfortable in this hotel- I come back every time I need to be in jax for work. It's clean and updated. Only negatives are that they do not offer room service for breakfast, staff never seems very friendly and they charge to park in the garage and tell you the lot next to the hotel is city owned and that you will be towed- even though right now there are about 30 rental cars sitting in the lot now... I have the feeling they just tell people that to make more money with the garage. Overall it's a good place though..

“Great location...Times Square” Great stay! Rooms were large. I had already been in the city for 5 days on business staying at the Hilton @ 53rd & 6th. My husband was joining me for a few days of personal stay & the Hilton would not give us a reasonable rate, so I found this hotel thru Priceline...and moved...rolling my suitcase 4 blocks. Comfortable beds, quite, easy to sleep. Very convenient...anytime of day! When leaving for the airport, a cab driver gave me a price that he made sound like he was giving me a bargain. When I told one of the bellmen he told me the driver was ripping me off. He flagged us another cab.

“Nice boutique hotel” Hotel Monaco is a smaller property in downtown Denver. Staff was friendly and welcoming. Room was spacious. This particular hotel is in an old building so you have high ceilings in the room. View was not so great as room overlooked center of building so you only see windows of other rooms. Like that there were Aveda products in the bathroom. Only complaints were a very loud mini-bar fridge that made it hard to sleep and tissues/toilet paper that were one step above paper - very rough!

“Standard hampton inn quality” I stay in lots of hampton inns for work. This hotel was great, nothing fancy but clean and comfortable rooms. My room had a sofa and king bed. I really like that hampton inns always change the duvet cover, it makes for a clean bed. No room service but it has a nice indoor pool and really good but small fitness center. I would stay here again. Easy to get food with a mall down the street. Easy for business traveler.

“Great location” This hotel has a good price and the parking is free. The staff is very helpfull. There is no breakfast but 3 blocks further is Mell's where you can eat a original breakfast, good hamburgers and great steaks. Easy to find, when you come from the north ( 101 ) take exit Lombardstreet, Downtown and you are entering Lombardstreet. The flatscreen tv was the biggest we had in our 3 week trip

“Great experience in NYC landmark” We have stayed at the Excelsior several times and love coming back. The upper West side location is great: 3 minutes walk from Central Park and subway stations close by for downtown excursions. The beds and linens are top notch. The bathrooms are stocked with fine soaps and shampoos. The think we liked about this hotel is that there are 1- and 2-bedroom suites which are perfect for large families like mine. I found the prices to be very reasonable for the value received.

“A very pleasant hotel with a very decent buffet breakfast” I had the pleasure of staying at this hotel twice within a matter of weeks. On the first stay we were updated for a little extra to their executive floor which also included some extra food vouchers to use for dinner. The food in the restaurant was very tasty and fresh. We were very pleased. The lobby was very neat and spacious and stylish. The staff was also polite. The hotel has a regular free shuttle to the airport. The rooms were just a little on the old side but they were still well maintained and very well sound proofed. We had breakfast on the executive floor and the food was great, however we enjoyed even more the full breakfast downstairs. We had a pleasant stay and everything was great. The only negative I can think of was the fact that if you want to self park the car you need to park the car behind the hotel and walking back from the parking lot behind the hotel (fully separated from the hotel) feels like a bit unsafe. However, it is a very short walk. We would not hesitate to stay at this hotel again.

“Sehr gute Lage, aber etwas zu teuer” Wer sich die Lage des Hotels auf einer Karte ansieht, wird schnell erkennen, dass es hier nichts auszusetzen gibt. Ein idealer Ausgangspunkt für einen Manhattan-Besuch. Das Hotel ist insgesamt sehr sauber und gepflegt, aber ich muss leider sagen, für knapp 500$ im Doppelzimmer hätte ich mehr erwartet. Es ist Meckern auf hohem Niveau, aber dennoch das Zimmer empfand ich als zu klein und die Einrichtung etwas unmodern.

“4.5 stars. Great views. Nice Hotel” I can't quite give five stars as I just used the hotel for a place to sleep and get ready for work. I didn't use the concierge or eat at the restaurant. I did however, have a room more spacious than my current apartment. The bedding was amazing. Never wanted to get up. Everything was clean. Check-in was easy and the people were friendly. The lobby is on the second floor and spacious. I preferred this to the W hotel lobby which feels crowded to me. Location is wonderful too. Would stay here again.

“Needs renovation, there are better Kimptons for similar price in the area” My husband and I stayed at the Prescott while in town for business in September. All of the staff we encountered, at the desk, on the phone, and the valet out front, were helpful, responsive to issues, friendly, and welcoming. Our room (a classic queen, in the older part of the hotel) was well-laid out. I liked the desk area being to the side, out of the way--something that's important to me as a business traveler. The bathroom was quite spacious as well, especially compared to other hotels of similar age. It's a Kimpton, so free wifi and a $10 "raid the mini bar" coupon for members of their loyalty club. I did not order room service, but the menu is exhaustive, and they do serve food until 10:30, half an hour longer than most area hotels. While the hotel has good "bones", it is definitely in need of renovation. The bed was sloped toward the middle, and the mattress was very uncomfortable. Both of us woke up with backaches, and we're both in our 30's and in good health. The linens were fine, but if you looked at the comforter the sheets were covering (and they do come apart once you get in bed, so you always see this), it was a little dingy. I hear the "club rooms" in the other half of the hotel are nicer, but they are also more expensive--significantly so when I looked. The location is, as other reviewers have mentioned, two blocks away from Union Square, but I would add that it's not the best side of Union Square. The neighborhood is fine, but most of what you're going to want to see is to the right as you leave the front door. If you go left, it gets dicey pretty quickly. Overall, what I experienced at this hotel reminded me of the Sir Francis Drake pre-renovation. It was fine, but given the choice, I would probably still recommend the Drake. The price point is usually about the same, and the amenities, location, and freshened up rooms there give you a little more bang for your buck.

“great location very nice staff, restaurants a bit overpriced” I wrote an email to the hotel long before arrival with the request of a non smoking room in one of the upper floors. I never got a response. However they were able to fill in my request at the time of check in. We had a nice room in the 27th floor. The room was big, the bathroom pretty tiny with no space to put your own staff. There were some stains at the bathroom floor and in the tub. They could have vacuumed the room a bit better but other than that it was clean. There was also a walk in closet. The bed was very comfortable and we had a good sleep, the room was very quiet. The view from room 2736 is a bit blocked from the building across the other side which is pretty close but since there was no street between the buidlings it was also very quiet. Internet was wireless for 9,99 extra a day. We had breakfast every morning in the restaurant Commodore Grill. It is a bit overpriced but good quality. The staff was always very nice, reponsive and helpful. The location is excellent. Next to Grand Central Station and withing walking distance to Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center, The United Nation Headquarter, Time Square and other interesting points. I would stay here again!

“Great location!!” The hotel is very contemporary. It's recently been renovated. Very clean, comfortable. The lobby area is a bit small and plays techno 'runway' style music. We arrived early, before check-in and they stored our luggage. I was traveling with my daughter and we wanted 2 double/queen beds, but only Kings were available. They gave us a complimentary roll away bed. The rooms were clean and comfortable but very small. There was only a small chair, no desk & a tiny closet. The bathroom was small as well. There wasn't even an ice bucket in the room and I never saw ice machines. (Dean & Deluca by the lobby gave us a free cup of ice.) There were 4 elevators so there was very little waiting. Our room was near the elevator so we heard a lot of noise from that. We had to set the room temp so the heat would not come on at night because the heater made a loud clanging noise that woke us up one night. The best part was the location. Very close to Times Square, but not right in the middle of the chaos. Very convenient to all the little deli's right around the corner, too. Easy to pick up a snack or a continental-style breakfast to bring back to the hotel. I would stay there again, but make sure there are only 2 of us.

“Very Comfortable Boutique Hotel in Excellent Location” We completed a two week business/vacation in Washington DC and New York by staying in the Benjamin. Of the four hotels we stayed in on our trip, this was by far our favorite. We were traveling with two children (ages 8 & 10) and elected for the one bedroom suite. It was very spacious and nicely furnished. The suite has a kitchenette, which consists of a sink, microwave, dishes and utensils, and a small refrigerator/freezer. We enjoyed the city for all of our meals, but it was nice one morning to warm up rolls that we had bought the night before in Little Italy. The beds are very comfortable. I always have problems with hotel pillows. The Benjamin has a pillow menu, which allows you to choose from about 9 different pillow types. Many of these are relatively exotic, such as a magnetic theraby pillow, buckwheat etc. My kids chose the memory foam and water pillows, and switched off each night of our stay. The location of the hotel is outstanding. It is located at the corner of Lexington and 50th in midtown manhattan. There are many choices for breakfast, lunch and dinner in the blocks around the hotel. To help place this hotel in relation to others, the back of the Waldorf Astoria is across the street. The hotel is only a few blocks from Rockefeller Center and about 8 blocks from Central Park. The hotel is on the side of the park that is nearest to the Wollman Ice Skating arena, which we enjoyed on one of the few sunny days of our trip. There is a subway station one block away, although we found that taxis were a cheaper alternative than paying for four subway fares anytime we went any distance in the city. The hotel staff is extremely friendly. Whenever we left the hotel, the staff would wish us a good day, and upon our return, welcome us back to the hotel. The hotel was very dilligent about the turndown service, and whenever we asked for anything, it was promptly provided, along with a call confirming that we were satisfied. Because we have kids, I am very aware of noise from adjoining rooms, and we constantly police our kids whenever the walls appear to be thin. In the Benjamin, I never noticed any noise from adjoining rooms, and just a little noise from the hallway. We didn't try the spa on the 3rd floor, but we would frequently see others in the hotel who were heading to or from it. We also didn't sample any of the cuisine. I will say that the room service breakfast, at about $30 per person, seemed high, even by New York standards. There is a lounge that is very comfortable and has a beautiful view of Lexington on the second floor. The bathrooms have some nice fixtures, such as lighted vanity mirrors. The sound for the TV in the bedroom was also wired into the bathroom. Another very nice feature was the Bose Wave Radio next to the bed, which was always tuned to a classical station when we returned from our travels each day. All in all, we were extremely pleased. I cannot recommend it highly enough. As with every hotel, there were a couple very small negatives. These are extremely minor items though: - The windows use very nice Roman shades. However, they are an all or nothing affair. As our room (4th Floor) looked right into an adjoining building, we never felt comfortable having them up, especially at night and in the a.m. - There were only 2 elevators servicing about 20-some floors. The wait for an elevator was longer than usual as a result. - The housekeeping staff was very attentive, but almost too attentive. Unless we had a do-not-disturb sign on the door, we would frequently get a knock to see if we needed anything. The bathroom was large, but lacked shelf space. We sometimes kept towels on the marble floor and used the towel shelf for our toiletries. Next time we come back to New York, we will not hesitate to stay at The Benjamin.

“Good location and functional rooms” I stayed at Club Quarters for about 2 nights in July 2011. The location was great - close to major subway, tourist sites, shops and restaurants. Rooms were pleasant and spacious - clean and comfortable. I like the fact that there is a water dispenser for guests to help themselves with water but there is no fridge in the room. Price of stay was reasonable.

“Nice Hotel” The hotel was nice with a friendly and helpful staff. Our room had a view of the Bay Bridge. The room was a little small but had enough room for two of us to move around. They have a nice wine and beer happy hour in the evenings. It was close to the Ferry Building. Which has a fun Saturday and Tuesday Farmers Market. Would stay there again when in SF.

“Good Hotel; Few Complaints” This place was recently updated. Good location (make sure you map the nearby highway interchange and streets or you may get lost!) and the rooms have a nice kitchen, bathroom, sitting area and flat screen TV. Nice closet too. Breakfast is included and is pretty good. It's all neat and clean, if a tiny bit dark and dingy at times. Good value and nice staff. Near a nice mall and Blue Mesa Grill; you should eat there if you can.

“Another wonderful review” I'll just add my kudos as other before me have done. The Talbott is a small, european feeling hotel just off the hustle of Michagan Avenue. The charming street is a beautiful backdrop to the outdoor restaurant where food is very good. The hotel staff is exceptionally helpful and friendly (Gene the conceirge is fantastic!) Our room was huge, clean and comfortable -- extra nice Aveda toiletries! A wonderful property in a wonderful location and a good value for $179/night.

“Best Holiday Inn ever!!!!!!!” I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in may 2010. We hotel staff were more than helpfull, they let us choose what floor we wanted to stay on and what type of bed!! There us is a resturant at the hotel called Dennys...... the food is great... good value and excellent service... The hotel is in a great location you can walk to practically everything. However just round the corner from the hotel next to the italian resturant there is a hop on hop off bus!! You can do this for the day or get a 2 day pass.. we got a 2 days pass so we could do all 3 loops. It cost $50 each. It was great an open top bus, took you to all the main site, union square, golden gate bridge, china town etc.... There are so many souvenier shops and places to eat you are spoilt for choice..... Make sure you book the Alcatraz before you go as you won't be able to buy tickets when your there, they get booked up really quick!! The are so many restuarnts to choose from the best ones are on pier 39. Great sea food. Also check out the sea lions while you are there. When you are leaving get the hotel to book your taxi for you back to the airport.... it costs $50 but you get to go in a Lincon...... If anyone has any questions please don't hesitate to contact me.

“Great location, great service. Rooms need upgrades for the price you pay here.” I would say that overall we were satisfied with our stay. The service was incredible. You can't beat the location. There is great shopping and tons of excellent restaurants within walking distance. As a matter of fact, the Crescent is in the same complex as the Capital Grille, Nobu and Stanley Korshak. The building is a beautiful one. Probably my favorite building in Dallas. The only drawback to this place, and it is kind of a big one, is that the rooms need updating and upgrading. The bed was pretty uncomfortable. There were several items that needed repair. The bathrooms needed an update badly. Everything else is great. But for the price, I'd stay somewhere else and then visit the beautiful Crescent complex. You can make a day out of it easily.
“Awesome view from the top floor” My only disappointment with staying here was that it was for only one night.

“Your opinion is going to depend on how much you pay...” I booked this hotel through priceline.com for $72 a night. I feel I got a pretty good deal. This hotel is not dirty. It is not unsafe. It is however in need of a renovation, and does not carry same quality that most upper level Marriott hotels carry. Bottom line: if you get a good deal on this place, you'll be pleased. If you pay full price, I guarantee you'll be disappointed.

“Then suites were new spacious any very clean. Staff was great and so was the location. The food was o.k.” It's a perfect place to stay if you are bringing the kids to Fiesta Texas or Seaworld. There is an excellent shopping mall 5 minutes away. Great indoor swimming pool We were very happy with the hotel. Next time we will request a room with a balcony. We will be back.

“lovely & modern” Used priceline to save a few bucks on the room and booked it sight unseen. The Westin is located within walking distance of an outdoor mall called the Domain and there is plenty of things to do - even late at night all within a few minutes of the hotel. The only downside is that you have to brave mall traffic during the day, which wasn't too bad in July but might get worse closer to the holiday season, I can imagine. The room was incredibly spacious, with a great view from the 6th floor. The windows boost a sun shade so you can still get plenty of light without burning sunlight entering the room during the day. The bathroom had a great lit vanity and a makeup mirror, which we found very nice. You get free wi-fi being a Starwood Preferred member as well as two bottles of free water, which we really liked as well. We did try to use the pool during our stay but found it very crowded with not enough seating, it was also fairly small -somehow the hotel was so large and spacious that we expected the same of the pool. We were told that we could have enjoyed drinks at the pool from the restaurant had we found space there, which would have been exciting. I definitely enjoyed my stay and would return to this hotel in heartbeat.

“Better than Expected” After reading the reviews here, I almost cancelled our reservation. However, it was difficult to find reasonably priced rooms elsewhere at the last minute. We stayed here from Jan. 25-30 2004 and were pleasantly surprised by the very nicely renovated rooms, the beautiful lobby with fireplace and plenty of comfortable seats, and the very good (small chain) restaurant, Il Fornaio. With the exception of the morning restaurant mangement, we found all of the staff to be very friendly and helpful. Our room on the 5th floor was nicely renovated with all brand new inlaid-look wood furniture, a large armoire, small table with leather chair, a very large (ca. 6-ft. x 3 ft) desk with a funky (& uncomfortable) leather desk chair, new carpeting, and very comfortable bed with Matlasse bed linens. The bathroom, while small, was white tiled and had an interesting, well-lit, trayed ceiling painted with clouds & butterflies. One of our colleagues even had a jacuzzi in her room. The very small countertop around the sink was wooden (right now in good condition, but years of moisture will surely cause deterioration). There were a few downsides, although these were in no way irritating. There was no comfortable chair for reading or relaxing, but I enjoyed sitting instead in the large sitting room with fireplace downstairs. While we did not have a problem with sudden temperature swings in the shower, the flow was not a very forceful one. In fact, it almost seemed like a trickle, and I was grateful that I didn't have long hair to wash! The TV reception in our room was very poor. There were not many channels to watch; no CNN. (The CNN logo appears on the screen, but the Food Channel was playing instead). The walls may be paper-thin, but this was not a problem in our room since the heating fan was so loud that we could not possibly hear noise from surrounding rooms. It is true that our room was very cold upon arrival, but after we turned on the heat, it was quite comfortable. Finally, there was a 2-3-inch diameter paint splotch in the bathtub which had never been cleaned up & was left to dry. Not a very professional look. We were already familiar with the Il Fornaio chain from other cities and find it to be a good quality restaurant with food selections for every type of diet. During our week there we encountered very, very nice waitstaff. However, we voiced complaints with management about never being able to get seated for breakfast. As the restaurant was very short-staffed in the morning, only two rows of tables were opened for breakfast service -- this despite the fact that there is a buffet breakfast. The morning management was fairly surly about this and claimed that he could not fix the problem until next year since they are not able to hire anyone to work. As we would be on our feet all day at a tradeshow, it was a big problem for us not to have a decent breakfast in the morning. This could be a big problem for convention travelers. Instead, we were relegated to the little coffee bar next to the restaurant (excellent coffee & breads, but too drafty for sitting there). All in all, we enjoyed staying at this hotel for the $89/night price we booked through the hotel's website. If I were paying $150 or more, I would stay across the street at the brand new Marriott -- which is what we had to do for the last night when the Hyatt could not accommodate us because of a large wedding. The new Marriott hotel was exquisite!

“Nice spot” I stay when in Seattle here because of the location - immediately adjacent to Pike's Market and lots of interesting food options. The hotel itself is pleasant, small boutique. The service is very strong from the bellman to the front desk. Also, the Hotel's french cafe has a terrific food and wine selection.

“Very Impressed” I attended a recent business meeting held at the Avenue Hotel. I was very impressed the the attentiveness of the staff on check-in and the very spacious room. The bed was comfy and I didn't hear a peep from neighbors on any side. The location was terrific as well - one block or so off Michigan Avenue. Parking was alot but that's what parking is in Chicago. The meeting room was spacious and the staff was as attentive as at check-in with excellent service and refreshments. All in all, I was very pleasantly surprised as we normally use more "name" chains for our meetings. I would gladly consider this hotel for personal stays as well.

“Nice on the surface-beware” Upon arrival in San Diego, we couldn't wait to get into our room. The first room smelled on smoke and had cigarette ashes in the sink, so we were moved to a "better" room with a great view. We unpacked and headed out. When we climbed into bed, the sheets were wet with urine! I called housekeeping, which is closed at 10:30, and then the front desk. All they could offer was clean sheets. I told them we'd both sleep in the other bed, since it was just my daughter and me. I stripped the sheets off the bed for them to be changed. The next night, around the same time, climbed into bed to find them smelly and slightly wet. The sheets had been changed but the mattress pad was still really wet. So I called down again. They offered to let us change rooms, but at 11:00 pm it was too late. So I stripped it again, and laid a blanket from the closet on top and some fresh sheets. The next day, mattress pad that I removed was gone, but the blanket was still on the bed in its place. Called down again, and they offered free breakfast for the following morning in which we were leaving. ONce we arrived home, I emailed the hotel and the customer service of the Hyatt. Their offer was if we traveled and stayed at a Hyatt, to call a number and they would upgrade us, if it was available. So beware!

“Good property, ideally located” Stayed in this property twice in a week during end of March12. Hotel is comfortable, rooms are done well with a functional kitchen, small but well maintained bathroom (no shower cubicle but bathtubs with glass partition) and a nice exercise room. The most disappointing factor was the baggage storage rule that was not conveyed clearly. due to security reasons they outsource storage and that location is inconveniently poised if one were to leave in haste (I experienced this process and quite shaken due to last minute rush). if they administer an informed consent ahead (may be their storage policy is hidden somewhere in the Hotel guests' manual or rather I did not notice!) guests are better prepared to deal with this situation or examine alternatives ahead. I may not return back to this hotel as that experience certainly was very disappointing....

“4th of July at the Omni” We booked our room on Priceline, and were pleased to win the Omni at $112.00 per night for two nights. Our room and experience was very much like other reviews written here on the same weekend.We watched the fireworks right from our balcony on 4th of July! Our room, standard King, over looked the pool on the 7th floor. We enjoyed people watching of the beautiful people and the babies and kids in the pool itself. We rarely interacted with the staff except a snack & cocktails from room service which was prompt. The room service food was good however the cocktails (Mai Tai's) were horrible and non edible($18.00 for both). We didn't complain and just left them on the desk to be cleaned with the room. We had a semi stocked mini bar, as there were two empty bottles of Grey Goose bottles, that had the caps replaced and put back in their perspective places. I called down to the front desk to advise them and they said it happens all the time, and they will not charge our room which they didn't. There were other empty spots leading one to believe other items had not been replaced as well. The Valet was prompt all weekend except the day we checked out, we stood their with our bags in hand for a good 6-7 minutes and no Valet staff every asked us if we needed help. Finally my husband muscled the bags over to the Valet desk where two young gentleman were chatting close by and asked for someone to get our car. Not the best for $30.00 a day I thought. Nothing special about the Valet either for the price, unlike the Four Seasons or The Ritz where you get bottled water, direction basically anything & everything you can think of and things you don't think of. The reasons we continue to visit those chains over and over again. This was a very pretty hotel and had lots of nice amentities. Had we paid the hotel website rates, I would have been a little miffed on the size of the room and the lack of privacy the bathroom does not offer. It truly does bring a couple closer than you may want to be!!!! My husband was nice enough to fetch coffee when it was my turn to shower (: so I could have some privacy. We would stay here again but only via Priceline, if I was going to pay top price I would look elsewhere. There are sooo many choices in this beautiful city. We spent the final two nights of our trip at the Hyatt Regency Mission Bay, see review.

“La Boheme......................at a price!” This hotel, is on the whole pretty tatty looking. Its for lovers of Art or those who grieve the historical pasing of an age that their birthdate means they can never be part of. First impressions are of quirky characters in the lobby area juxtaposed by chelsea go getters with lap tops and art pieces on every available wall or surface, and just the promise of a ghost of a departed, tortured artist. Its about mis matched furniture from antique shops and high sheen and boutique finish is a million miles away. All that said and done, elements of the bohemian past, art pieces and tortured artistic souls could still be kept following an extensive refurbishment. Our room (321) had a balcony on the same level as the famous sign and the room was large but cosy with a small tatty kitchenette (complete with mouse trap), walk in closet and very tired looking bathroom in pink and black tiles complete with a sink that had been repainted at some point and was now looking worse than ever. However, I liked the room immensley. The famous wrought iron stairs are beautiful and the paintings (good, bad and indifferent) on the walls brighten the hallway up and lend to the artistic feel of the place. The hotel is in a prime location in Chelsea and for those who want to soak up something other than an impersonal hotel then I'm sure you'd love it. For no reason other than the fact I've now stayed there - and paid well for the privelege - I probably wouldn't stay there again when there are millions of other hotels and areas in New York but I urge others who haven't to give it a try with an open mind as I'm sure that in years to come you'll remember your stay.

“Top notch - though, be warned, still only 95% operational” Pros: Good shopping location, nice rooms, huge bath tub, attentive service Cons: Outdoor pool isn't open yet (failed to inform us of this anywhere prior to visit), rather thick & hot bedding made for some tricky sleepover-complex lighting and curtain system, (current) limited bar opening times, $15/day internet access (business centre is free however) Trump Soho is ideally located in downtown Manhattan if you're a shopping fiend. Failing that it makes walking to the downtown area for great food, sights and culture a breeze. Although well located and with an apparently top-end spec of features that includes a pool on the 7th floor, not all is open yet. With a current pool permit lacking it's not possible for patrons to swim despite, in my instance, neither the hotel nor booking agent making this clear until the moment I checked in. Needless to say I wasn't impressed with this. Furthermore the bar has a fairly limited opening hours of 6-11pm at present, adding to the not-to-full-capacity operation of the hotel. Saying that, however, the (admittedly expensive $16) Raspberry Press cocktail was absolutely sublime and, once sat by the pool barefoot with feet gently splashing, a member of the service team promptly bought over cushions to seat us on. Attentive service is a certainty here. However, given the location of the outdoor sun loungers and Manhattan's often brisk winds down the avenues there is an accident waiting to happen: I saw sun loungers whipped up a few feet into the air land into the pool which could be potentially serious; I do believe that Trump ought to purchase more weighted outdoor furniture to ensure they stick to the spot! The room itself was of a good enough size, though I found the king size bed's bedding overtly plush to the point that sleep was met with some mid-night sweats due to the heat (even after removing the second duvet that's sneakily tucked underneath the sheet!). Plus, even up on the 14th floor with windows sealed shut, passing trucks were audible during the early hours too - perhaps the triple glazing isn't quite thick enough. Room lighting controls are 'state of the art' as in they're controlled via the TV remote. However, this doesn't speed things up whatsoever. I spent many a moment faffing around with the control just to open the curtains when I'd rather have the second option of a simple 'open/close' switch. A nice idea, but it's not been fully thought through. The bathroom has a huge bath that's an absolute treat to fill right up. The shower provides reasonable pressure at best, though it's not exceptional. Towels are around the room in abundance, so you'll never run short and, if you were to, then housekeeping would sort you out at the drop of a hat. Oh, and it's not a cheap stay either, but then you already knew that based on the 5 Star status. This isn't an 'old skool' five star fare though, it's very much the new wave of polished exterior and a number of front desk staff are clearly at the opening stages of their hospitality careers. Overall though a lovely stay with plenty of access to lower Manhattan. Just don't expect the world just yet - when the pool's finished and the bar open more extensively it'll be that bit extra of a treat.

“Location, Location, Location” I was disappointed when I was unable to secure a last-minute reservation at the Riverwalk; I booked a room at this Hyatt, because of its location to the airport, but also because of the Hyatt reputation. What I was surprised with, was the awesome location in Alamo Heights. Lots of great new shopping and restaurants nearby. It is NOT the Riverwalk, but a welcome addition to the options in San Antonio. The hotel was as expected with this Hyatt brand. Staff was very helpful and attentive, hotel was clean and in working order. Pool was nice and parking sufficient. Great hotel option that I will return to when back working in San Antonio

“Great Hotel and Staff!” Based on the comments on Trip Advisor, we booked a one bedroom suite for the weekend. Although it was a little pricier than we normally spend in NYC, it was worth it, due to the additional size and parking included with the package. It had a small kitchen area with a refrigerator and microwave, as well as a pull-out sofa in the living room. Their turn down service was a nice touch with soft music playing upon our return. The staff was very helpful from the bellmen to the registration staff, plus the hotel was centrally located for plays, shopping and Central Park. We've stayed at numerous hotels in NYC over the years, but the Benjamin will definitely be our favorite and first pick from now on!

“Another Excellent Experience at the Philly Ritz Carlton” I have stayed at the Ritz three times for business in 2011. Each time the hotel was top notch. My room has alway been very nicely appointed. My most recent trip was the week before Christmas. I was upgraded to a junior suite which was very nice. The beds and bathrooms in the hotel are very nice. The service at the front desk and restaurant could not have been better. The hotel itself is very beautiful and is ideal for a a business traveler. I recommend it strongly.

“Free rooms with points -- not unless you argue” This is a great resort, especially for families. So it is unfortunate they are trying to add a "resort fee" to rooms billed as free nights, a cost of $20 oer night per room. Since it is added without regard to use of additional services, it is really just additional room rate, stated as an add on. They did remove it after an argument, but it leaves a bad taste, especially after the cowardly way of informing you about it - a little card tucked in with your room key, explaining it covers internet and other resort amenities, never mind that you did not bring a computer. That said, to the resort itself. It is what you would expect in a Westin, nice room, big pretty public areas, several dining venues casual to upscale priced accordingly. However, this is really set up for kids to enjoy. There are daily activities such as Dinosauer George who came with a huge array of fossils and a very entertaining program. Smores on the patio at night, etc., all at no charge. The pool is great, one has a slide. We spent a whole day there. There is an adults only pool if you are single or a couple with no kids. KIDS EAT FREE if they are 5 and under, even at the pool. The pool service was good, and so wax tne food. We brought some drinks and snacks of our own poolside with no problem. Breakfast on Sunday we went to the cafe for the buffet, $22 adults, $12 kids over 5. Menu selections at lower prices were also available. The food was really good and service was friendly and prompt. The kids loved the loony tunes characters who went table to table and posed for pictures. We really liked this resort and hope to return. One family told us they come every year because of the programs for kids. Have kids and want free time or a quiet meal? Use kids club. It is not cheap, but they charge you half with a hotel restaurant receipt. We did not use this, so I cannot comment on quality.

“Disappointing Room” Sometimes first impressions are accurate. A NYC size room (about 12 x 15) with a tiny closet (had to request more hangars) and no dresser. Expensive parking. No room to put our two suitcases on suitcase stands (there's only one stand anyway). No iPod dock. Dim fluorescent bedside lights. Window open upon arrival (in the 40s outside) and heat doesn't seem to be working properly. Oh yeah - free wine at 5 pm, a flat screen TV and nice bathrobes. I think we got what a friend calls the "Ha Ha Room" - let's give them this room and see if they complain. Last week we were in a luxury hotel in Portugal at lower cost, so the comparison is stark. This doesn't feel like a fine hotel...at least not to us...at least not on this visit.

“Nice Surprise! 5 Star service” Stayed here for one night with my husband after finding a great deal on Travelzoo. We were greeted very warmly by staff, and we were offered hot cider on a freeeezing NYC day. The room was not large, but every inch of space was decorated very lovely and efficiently. There were many touches that you only find in the finest of hotels. The bed was comfortable, they left treats at turn down, filled the ice bucket and turned on soft music for our arrival. We had a complimentary buffet breakfast at the hotel restaurant, which was nice. The only complaint would be the shower pressure was very low. All in all, a wonderful experience. Would stay again for sure.

“As far as airport hotels go...” ...this one's pretty good. I've stayed at the Seatac Radisson a couple of times now, for either a quick business trip or a close-to-the-airport stopover, and both stays were better than adequate. You don't usually expect much at aiport hotels, but this place is pretty decent. LOCATION The hotel is on International Blvd, literally right across the street from the airport. You can walk to the airport if you want to. Both times I've taken the shuttle, but would certainly walk if it seemed like the shuttle was running behind. The area is primarly hotels, restaurants, gas stations, and parking facilities (and, um, the occasional "gentlemen's club"). If you're driving, there's a Safeway with a pharmacy not too far away. Anyway, it's ideally located for a preflight hotel stay. ROOMS The rooms are pretty nice. (Many Radissons I've stayed at previously have inspired me to rename the chain "Ratisson" due to their general griminess; this one is much better.) I stayed in a king-bed room; the workstation was large (great since I was working), the WiFi was free, and the furniture and decor were tasteful. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean, and the room was quiet. In short, it's pefect for catching up on business before you have to fly out the next day. FACILITIES/LOBBY The lobby is functional; not huge, but not tiny. There's a restaurant that wasn't too bad (for lunch, anyway), and there's a comfortable bar/lounge where you can grab a drink and watch the Mariners lose horribly to whoever they happen to be playing that day. It's not fancy, and don't look for a party scene there, but it's perfectly adequate. Aside from WiFi, I didn't use the business facilities, so I can't comment. There's a pool, but I didn't use it, so I'm not sure what it's like. STAFF The staff was very helpful and cheerful. On one of my stays, I arrived *way* before check-in time, and they were happy to find me a room that was ready early... which allowed me to get a lot more work done than I would have otherwise. That was great. They answered all of my questions about local services, and did so with a smile. In short, the staff greatly enhanced my stay, which is always a nice surprise. SUMMARY If you're a business traveler and you need a good place to stay near the airport, this is top-notch. It's a particurlay good deal if you get it through hotwire or priceline. The staff is helpful and friendly, the rooms are nice, and you can't get closer to the airport without sleeping at the terminal.

“I was scared for my life all night long....” I stayed at this hotel because I was attending a trade show at the Mount Vernon the next day. What a dump! I travel pretty frequently for work and I have never been so scared throughout the night as I was at this hotel, I barely slept. Although it was surrounded by several churchs It still felt like it was a bad part of town. My room was gross, feet stuck to the floor in the bathroom, sheets did not fit the bed, the smoke detector was hanging from some wires off the wall and did not appear to be connected to anything but when I turned the A/C on I found out it was in fact connected as it went off loudly until I turned the air off! Stay away from here!

“Point de chute luxueux pour rayonner sur Frisco.” Usine à gaz de luxe, idéalement située, près de Union Square, pour le shopping. Le lobby est un véritable poulailler ou vous croiserez des espèces de tous pays. Bar au top floor à la verrière originale. Chambre Marriott des plus classiques et confortables. Tuyauterie de la douche bruyante.Personnel accueillant et compétent. Etablissement gayfriendly. Lumière blafarde à la piscine. Petit déjeuner cher mais complet. Internet payant et de midi à minuit!

“Weekend escape” This hotel is a true weekend escape. I have stayed tree weekends in two years and love this place. The rooms are big, clean and beautifully decorated. The bathrooms are so big you could live in one. The housekeeping, room service and food are perfection. They do need to retrain the restaurant wait staff as they are a bit unorganized and unfriendly (but the food is great). Front desk and concierge are friendly and efficient. Can't wait to come back. The beds are clouds of dreams.

“5 <>'s for a reason - service was flawless!” At first, I was a bit uncomfortable having to stay at such a nice/expensive hotel for a conference -- after a day or so, I realized why this hotel was so wonderful. Perfect location, excellent appointments and details, and mostly great staff -- with lots of energy, who really care. . As I said when I checked in, using my Marriott Credit Card, "I'm usually a Courtyard kind of guy." The front desk folks simply smiled and asked me if I needed help with my bags - "No way! Not another waste of a tip," I thought. Later, I realized that the staff continued to go out of their way to help guests in almost every way - they were really great. . Rooms (I think I got a nice one) were generously laid out with a great working surface (lots of extra stationery items), fantastic media center (21" LCD with DVD player and "hub" for plugging in one's own electronics) and possibly the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. . As above, service (room, housekeeping, front desk) was impeccable with many VALID reasons for comforts provided and tips. Shaving kit and many toiletries were provided in the bathroom "mini-bar" which was a great convenience. Not free, but good to have since I forgot my razor. I am mixed on the lack of ice machines on each floor - since to keep my Diet Dr. Peppers really cold (mini-bar fridge was more of a "chiller"), I needed ice twice a day. Each time necessitated a special cal/request from housekeeping (and a $1 or $2 to "thank them" sigh). The upside is that no room is burdened with the noise of folks listening to folks getting ice or filling up their coolers. Later, I realized that nightime ice (and some dark chocolates, and the upcoming weather) was provided automatically with their turndown service. Nice, huhh? . I was also chagrined that the only parking available was valet for $27+ each nite (+ tips when dropping off/picking up one's car). I supposed I could have left my rental in one of the lots nearby, but this is River Oaks and very upscale part of Houston.
