I suppose they don't want guest and strangers randomly mixing and interacting in a parking deck, but I found the lack of self-parking for a more reasonable fee burdensome (although one might argue that the land necessary for parking is a big cost in this area of town). . Swimming pool was also a notch or so above average -- beautifully laid out. Not too small and a great treat on a medium-cool fall morning in Texas. Typical of the hotel, the guy who was cleaning the pool went out of his way to get me a towel. . Should I mention that the internet was priced a bit more than the "standard" $9.99/nite? Maybe a bit less, if one locked in a package for 3 days at a time. Just seems chintzy when such a great TV and DVD player is offered for free. . Room service and the hotel restaurant (Remington's) were both excellent. Not inexpensive but great quality, wonderful service, delicous food. Nice to have and worth the price. . Overall, I did feel that the value of the hotel (room, tips, parking, internet) was excellent given the wonderful quality and service that were present. Not a Marriott but compares very favorably with the best Ritz-Carleton's. This was a fantastic place with terrific service.

“She said yes” Stayed here even though i live 2 hours away. I asked my girlfriend to marry me at the Bel air restaurant. This is a great hotel. The front desk employee's were very attentive to us when we checked in. We stayed in a very nice and big room. although it was a suite. The beds at Westins are amazing!! Very cool atrium.

“Pricey for an average property” Stayed for three nights here while on business. The location is great but the rooms are loud. You hear everything from the halls. Even while walking through the halls to your room you can hear the tvs from within all of the rooms blaring. Check-in was easy and quick as I'm a Gold Hilton Honors member and checked in at the Platinum and Gold Member desk. Did not receive upgrade to Executive lounge however did receive free bfast every morning. Bfast was the usual - muffins, yogurt, fruit, etc. Concierge desk is busy and there was always a short wait but the staff was friendly and helpful. I'd stay here again, but wouldn't pay the $$$ on my own dime.

“Clean, Modern, Great!” One of the nicest Marriotts I've ever stayed at, and I've been to a few dozen. Everything seemed pretty new. The room was clean, fresh, and very pleasant. The bed was standard Marriott plushness. The TV worked fine (although it was a standard flat-screen CRT, not an LCD). The bathroom was well-stocked and water pressure was pretty good on the 16th floor. Two caveats: One, there's no mini-fridge in the room. This was kind of annoying since we had a few of our own bottles of water and it was like 95 degrees out that weekend. And two, hallway noise seemed a little louder than usual for a Marriott. We could hear quite a bit of activity whenever people would walk back and forth. The front desk staff were very nice (Kirby was pretty cool). The only issue was that when we arrived at 5pm, there was only one front desk clerk and like 4 or 5 people backed up in line. We waited for about five minutes but then 2 additional front desk staff showed up and we got checked in quickly. But where were those 2 staffers for the first five minutes? The location, also, is excellent. You can actually SEE the infield at Petco from the rooftop bar. But be aware that the streets will get a little crowded if you visit during a home game. And the Gaslamp Quarter is right around the corner with a TON of bars and restaurants. If we ever returned to the area, I'd probably stay at the Marriott again.

“An Update on this property” An update on this property. Management vigilance at the Embassy Suites-Convention Center may be slipping some. The personnel at the front desk are not as well trained as previously. Some appear new and are more curt, less friendly, more unsure of themselves. The rooms are still ok, but in need of capital investment to upgrade carpets (getting worn) and TVs. Management did invest in a newly renovated Fitness Center, which is an improvement. Perhaps due to budget cutbacks, the last few times I have used it there have been no newspapers or magazines put out in the fitness center. The pool next door to the Fitness Center is very popular with families. The “Manager’s Reception”, as is generally the case these days in Embassy Suites, is pretty bare bones in terms of food – bowls of chips, party mix, pretzels and occasionally crackers. (The Managers’ Reception at the ES in San Diego last month was even skimpier, however). As has been noted, breakfast can be way overcrowded. Come between 600 and 700 and it’s not too bad. A clue: Skip the made to order hot breakfast line. One can do pretty well with the other food stations, which include eggs and bacon, cereal, yogurt, fruit, and so forth. There are only a finite number of tables. The location remains a positive if your business is in the Convention Center part of town; the walk down to the Mall is about 15-20 minutes. Metro will take about 10 minutes to walk to. If one is not an HHonors member, one pays for Internet, which is not uncommon at many hotels, but still a negative. There are kiosks downstairs off the elevators, however, that allow one standing up access to the Internet if your needs do not involve a great deal of time. As is true of many DC hotel properties, the nightly rates for this hotel go up and down just like airline fares, depending on convention activity and overall booking. Sometimes it can be a great bargain, other times very high.

“Historic Hotel” I stayed one night at this historic hotel in downtown San Antonio. The hotel was built in 1910 and the lobby shows the beautiful period details. The hotel has a restaurant with outside seating on the sidewalk out front. There is a pub-style bar that was very nice. The hotel is in a great location, just blocks from the Alamo and the Riverwalk. This hotel is over 100 years old and I found my room to be very small. It was well appointed with nice furniture and comfortable bed. There may have been a little too much furniture for the size of the room. If you were sitting at the desk it was impossible for anyone to walk by between the chair and the bed. The batroom was also tiny. They did their best by installing a shelf above the sink and a wall rack to hold towels but I found the bathroom to be very cramped. I would not have wanted to stay more than a night of two in this tiny room. Hopefully there are more spacious rooms in the hotel. The staff is very nice and helpful.

“Beautiful boutique style hotel” Stayed in a Lux king suite sept. 4th to the 8th. Chose the hotel based on reviews and location. We were not disappointed, the hotel was a very easy walk from the Westlake light rail station. The lobby made a great first impression, beautifully finished, very comfortable and set up for meeting and visiting friends, lots of cozy seating areas. We were greeted by a very friendly, professional front desk staff, they were quick, had us checked in and up to our room in no time. Our room was very clean, well appointed with everything you could need, two closets, lots of room and very bright from 4 windows which open if you desire. The bed in our room was very comfortable, I don't know if it was because we were on the 9th floor but the nights were very quiet, no street noise and no noise from the hall or other rooms. Although the bathroom wasn't huge, it had all you need, lots of shelf space, roomy shower with excellent water pressure and good lighting. The Hotel Andra is in an excellent location, many restaurants nearby, the two in the same building as the hotel are the Lola which was excellent, Meditterean style...and an Italian restaurant called Assaggio (hope I got that name right) which we returned to 3 times for the happy hour, great host Mauro and bartender Marcin, food and drink was top notch. Pikes Market is a short walk from this hotel, as well as many other shopping choices, we would stay in this hotel again in a heartbeat and strongly recommend it.

“Top Lage” Top Lage, Waterfront. Sehr schönes Hotel, mit sehr schönen Zimmern (wenn man es mag, Blick auf den Flughafen - hört man aber kaum). 1x über die Str. und man ist im Herzen von Boston. Nette Hotelbar und natürlich auch ein Starbucks im Haus - Frühstück (falls nicht inkl.) sehr teuer und ungemütlich - man kann von den Zimmerngänge auf den Tisch schauen!.

“Great Hotel - wouldn't know it had over 500 rooms!!” Had a wonderful experience here recently. Stayed for only 2 nights, but all my "urgent" needs during this trip were handled by the staff perfectly! The lobby bar/restaurant is a great meet up place and the bartenders were very friendly. Got a few great drink recommendations and will definitely stay here again in the future.

“Good value hotel for staying in NY” My wife and 2 children stayed at this hotel for 3 days at the end of July. The hotel is located just off Times Square and is therefore a great base for sightseeing. It's not in the best of neighborhoods (there is a parole office close by and the bus station is across the street) but we never felt threatened and it was a very short walk to the crowds of Broadway and Times Square. All the staff were very helpful and eager to help. The room itself was clean and spacious (for New York). In other words it was pretty small for 4 people but we didn't spend much time in it so it wasn't a problem. It was also probably the quietest hotel room we've ever stayed in in NY. OK, we were on 30th floor but there was absolutely no street noise - quite an achievement in the city that never sleeps! The lack of elevators and the wait time have been commented on by others and we can concur. 3 elevators serving 32 floors (each floor with 10 rooms I think) just isn't enough. We waited a good 15 minutes on more than one occasion. We weren't in a rush but it got pretty frustrating. There is a free breakfast in the morning every day. Nothing special - fruit, bagels, an egg and meat dish and a reception with wine/beer and nibbles on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. This is nice but there isn't enough seating and it got very crowded when we were there. If you're going to NY for a few days, I can recommend this hotel. It's not 5* luxury but it represents good value for money.

“Good location, value, and comfortable stay” My 2 night stay was very comfortable here. It is a good location. I've stayed in the area before at a Courtyard Marriot and also practically next door at a Best Western. This was right in the middle both price wise and value wise. I do believe this will now be the hotel I choose for my San Diego business trips. I felt like the area was safe and was close to whatever I needed. The room was very comfortable as was the bed. All the staff I encountered was friendly. I ordered room service and it was shocking how quick my food came. This seems like a good hotel for both business and vacation travelers. I was very happy with my stay.

“Adequate for a stopover” Had a short overnight transit at this hotel. First impressions were good but the rooms are quite tired looking but adequate. One does not stay at airport hotels and expect wonders - even if it was a Westin. However, my greatest peeve is the service at the hotel. Check-in and Check-out was rather slow and this can be annoying after a long flight (for the former) and when you are rushing to catch the shuttle bus (for the latter). One thing I would note that needs a large improvement is the attitude and service level of the front door staff. I was carrying three big pieces of luggage and they did not even try to assist me as I was making my way across the expansive lobby to the front doors (ditto upon arrival). They made a show to help me load into the shuttle bus but it was the driver that exerted himself to help while two of the front door staff were having a protracted conversation while pushing the bags to the driver to upload. Thereafter, they looked expectantly for a tip from myself even though I do not think they are worthy of it. So in the end, adequate but some training is required of the front door staff for this to be an 'inspiring experience...'

“Wish there had been a tub” Staff is very accomodating and helpful. Our room was small but modern. Had to use the lap top at the desk which I hate. Our room did not have a tub but I did not check if some rooms do have tubs. The bathroom was not clean. Do not book a room here if you are doing so for the Galeria mall since it is pretty average shopping. There are restaurants worth going to in walking distance which is nice since cabs are a problem in this area.

“Excellent Off-Riverwalk Option” This is an excellent off-riverwalk option which offers value for quality, service and location. There is a complimentary hotel shuttle to take you to the Riverwalk and downtown tourist attractions though walking from the hotel to the Riverwalk is only a 15 minute walk. Very uptodate hotel with responsive, courteous staff. I will stay here again.

“Beautiful views, holes in the sheets.” I enjoyed my stay at the Standard but would never pay full price. They had a deal on Jetsetter so I decided to buy it as a birthday treat. Beautiful view, stylish room, friendly service, great bath tub, and robes. However, I was surprised to find multiple holes in the sheets. Also, room keys dont appear to work to go to the roof bar. There was a line outside to get in so we didn't even get to check it out. There are better options in New York, at much lower prices. (the next night we stayed in the Yotel which was fantastic!)

“Decent hotel near downtown” Dwcent all suites hotel near downtown. Pretty much on the edge of the ghetto section of town. I stayed here since they have a free shuttle to the medical center and will take you anywhere within in 5 miles of the hotel. The place was safe, clean and would def stay there again.

“Yummy but with annoying expense or two” I loved my stay at the Doubletree but it had two expensive irritations. I took an upgrade to the top floor which has a nice little cracker, snack, soft drink, etc. area in the common room. This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel and again enjoyed my stay. The exercise facilities, sushi bar, bar, breakfast area, coffee stand, etc. are all very nice and offset the fact that I didn't want to deal with rush hour or being away from home. I stayed over the weekend so I got to enjoy the pool and the lovely weather while I did some shopping and exploring in the San Francisco area. During my stay I had to get some work done in the evening so I enjoyed room service. I have no complaints about the menu or the service. There was a nasty storm in the middle of my stay flooding many places including the hotel. The staff responded well to it. The one annoying thing is they charge for parking now and it is a high price. Most of the area hotels have free parking. Not sure why but it does push the daily price too high for me. The other nit I have is that twice now, I have eaten at this hotel's high end restaurant, Spencer's. A long time ago, the meal service and so on left me frustrated with the price. It wasn't worth it especially with a poor margarita and unimpressive steak (prepared very well I should say). This time around, I ordered a salad of some sort, several wonderful glasses of red wine and a chocolate desert. I didn't mind paying well for the red wine. The service was good not great. The salad okay. I was annoyed when I ordered desert without any ice cream, it came with ice cream. I looked at the final price and just didn't think it compared to other meals I have had.

“Decent typical New York hotel” My wife and I just stayed at the Paramount for one night, October 10. I had booked through Hotwire and when I got to the hotel they said it was for a double bed room. I asked if they had a larger bed and they upgraded to a queen bed at no extra charge. A little noisy in the morning due to new construction next door.

“Cheap and Easy” We stayed at Microtel for our very early morning flight out of Denver. Cheap, small yet clean and easy. Long term parking and shuttle is the reason we stay there (this is our 2nd stay). We realized during our layover that my husband and left behind his "tempurpedic" special pillow. We placed a call and when we returned 5 days later, they had it waiting for us. Great service for such a cheap hotel. Don't expect much then a good night's sleep!

“An overnight with the kids that did not disappoint at all” Last week (the week after Christmas), I took my sons for a two day trip to Philadelphia to see the sights. I was looking for a hotel that was conveniently located, nice and reasonably upscale but not breaking the bank. I booked through the hotel's website which has lower rates for non-refundable reservations and got a great rate ($180). I was very pleased with the hotel. The highlights: excellent room service including children's menu items, prompt service, and wine by the carafe; very comfortable beds; and a TV that was so clear it was like being in a movie theater. The only downsides were minor: the building across from the hotel is being rebuilt (there was no noise but it was a little bit unsightly), and the tub was not big enough for one of those long soaks I like to do at a hotel. But, the hotel was so quiet you could hear a pin drop. I slept like a baby. I heard no noises in the halls or outside. And the room was (as advertised) very sunny. Best of all, it's 2 blocks away from Rittenhouse Square. I was very pleased with our choice.

“They charged us extra for almost everything.” I'm going to be very punctual with this review. -The hotel charged us 25% because we needed a 2 bed room (which was requested when booked) -Extra internet cost (ridiculously high) -Extra cost for parking. -uncomfortable beds -Big bathroom with a small shower. This isn't a crowne plaza, it looks more alike a days inn or something similar.

“Exceptional Service” The Hotel Valencia is not only very hip the way that a W might typically be, but the service is exceptional. When I arrived late one afternoon and needed a full suit, shirt and other clothes washed and presed in 4 hours, the bellman made it happen for me even though laundry had already been sent out for the day. Indeed, everything was hanging in my closet when I returned from dinner. BTW, the rooms are modern, elegant and fun. The bar downstairs is also very nice.

“Sreet Noise Is A Problem” I agree with many of the other posters. The hotel is very nice, and the staff tries to be very accommodating, but one feature over which they have no control is the noise--not only from the fire station right across the street, but the general street noise. The latter may be a problem in many Chicago hotels that are adjacent to a major street, but it is certainly a problem here, accentuated by the fire station. We had to leave the hotel, and they were very pleasant and understanding of that. If this is ok for you, then a good point of their location is their proximity to Lou Malnoti, a Chicago icon for deep dish pizza--not just for tourists, but for locals. It is delicious, famous for their corn meal crust; located a short walk away from the hotel.

“Would Only Stay Here If I Had To.....” I would only recommend the Palmer House if you had to stay here. The only reason we stayed here is because it was the hotel for our meeting. Here are the disadvantages: Service - Service is uneven. I think this has to do with the size of the hotel (because it's BIG). If the hotel is near full, everyone seems overwhelmed. Every call we made to the front desk resulted in being put on hold. There were lines of people everywhere. Maybe things are better when the hotel is not so full. Rooms - I don't really understand the rooms. Our room was on executive level. The positive side to this is the top two floors had private elevator (instead of the big bank of about 12 elevators). Our room was modest in size (but OK). Bath was tiny. Decor was kind of over-the-top fussy style (sort of mid-80's maybe). I visited friend in regular type room, which was spacious with big bath. Regular room had flat screen TV. Executive rooms had older type TVs. Other reviewers have mentioned varying sizes of rooms. I don't think you'll know what you're getting until you are there. Cost - Others have mentioned the extra costs for about everything. Internet was extra $20/day. Just go to the Corner Bakery (on outside 1st floor of hotel) and it's free. Other little things - I called in advance to see if rooms had coffee pots and was told yes. Written information in rooms said rooms had coffee pots. There were none - staff said they'd all been removed. All-in-all, I'd chose a smaller type hotel if visiting Chicago for fun. I think there are much more comfortable, modern, and economical places in town. We stayed at the Renaissance (Wacker Drive) and Burnham before and loved both of them!

“Ok location but.....” We stayed two nights in this Murray Hill hotel. The location is not bad but too far from subway stops for me. It is only a few blocks from the greenline stop at 33rd but I generally use the red and blue lines. The hotel was clean and staff were friendly. We requested an extra blanket and it was delivered as promised. The concierge seemed aloof but the bellman was very helpful as were the front desk staff. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant which was average as was the service. Concerns were that the room temperature could not be adjusted unless the outside temperature reacted below 55 or above 65. You also could not choose to turn on the fan to circulate air or dull exterior noises which I often do in the city. We had an end room that should have been very quiet but we heard all the hall noise clearly. I think this was due to the jam which had so many gaps it let light stream in around the entire door at night. This also let in all the noise. We were also woken in the night by loud rumbling and shaking. Not sure what from. The room itself looked great and was well decorated and the TV worked as did all lights, etc...but the sheets were so scratchy and of such poor quality that they actually made noise, like cellophane, when we move in them. The last concern occurred on our date of check out which was supposed to be by noon. We received a note that advised we would have no water after 10 am so please plan your bathrooming accordingly. They were cleaning their system and it would not be back in service until 4 pm. As a result, the restaurant was also closed. We had been out late and planned on a late breakfast down stairs as well as hanging out until checkout time. This was very inconvenient and I believe the hotel should have advised us that this would occur upon booking as well as offered a discount. New York is not known for it's many public restrooms and I really felt sorry for those who were staying over that day. Although there were many positives, we would not choose to stay here again. There are many great alternatives!

“Great Location, Dirty Room” I travel regularly on business and was not shocked at the small size of the room, this was expected and not a problem but this was the first hotel in NYC where I was not comfortable putting my toothbrush down in the bathroom. There were many mystery splatters throughout the room and the blinds were downright filthy with drips and stains. Most of the mess, including dust and dirty fingerprints on the light switches looked like something that could easily be solved with a damp cloth, but apparently this effort has not been made in quite some time. The shower tile was very stained looking. I had a look at the mattress under the sheets and it was very worn. There was a ring around the toilet bowl and the rust/ grunge under the glass shelves in the bathroom was super gross. Carpet was clean & the bed was comfortable, I'll give them that! The lobby has some interesting decor items and the elevators are relatively quick. There is a good concept here but the filth is a total deal breaker. The staff were friendly and helpful with me, but I definitely heard some attitude being handed out to other guests. I didn't even know that there was a pool or rooftop patio (read other reviews), they didn't mention any of this at check in. The location is great and I suppose that they sell rooms easily based on this fact alone, but there are better choices, see my other reviews if you want to know some of them.

“Like Everyone Else - We Love the Hotel Burnham” There's not much more to say about the Hotel Burnham, but we love it just like the rest of the reviewers here. I think it's a great value for the location and everything else about the hotel. Service was great. The only downside was rooms don't have coffeemakers....however, when I asked one was sent to our room immediately. Restaurant was great for dinner and breakfast. This has become "our" hotel in Chicago. Oh, you can't beat location on blue line of subway, which takes you right to OHare.

“Great Stay at Affinia!” Just returned from a five night stay at the Affinia Shelburne -- and all I can say is WOW! I had previously stayed at the Affinia Dumont (a couple of blocks down) and really liked their rooms and service. However, this time as I was traveling with two teenagers -- the idea of two bathrooms was quite enticing -- not to mention the great Travelzoo rate ($199 for a 1 bedroom suite). The room was huge -- I had also previously stayed at the Sheratown Towers in Times Square (executive level) and the room was so tiny we had to walk out of the room to change our minds. Anyway, this time I wanted to stay away from Times Square, in a more residential, quiet neighborhood and chose the Shelburne. The hotel is very, very nice. The staff were very friendly and the rooms were quite roomy and clean. As I said before, we stayed in a 1 bedroom suite with two queen size beds in one room and a pull-out sofa sleeper in the other room, and with a bathroom in each room, plus two mini-fridges. (It would have been nice to have a microwave for reheating leftovers -- a necessity with teenagers.) While we did not dine in the local restaurant -- Rare -- we did notice that it was quite crowded most nights. Found some great restaurants nearby and it was really easy to walk to just about anywhere -- we even walked down to Greenwich Village one evening -- a nice 30 minute walk. All in all, the hotel and location were great and we will definitely stay here again -- in fact, I am planning an "all girls" (with sisters and nieces) trip for next summer and will definitely look into staying here again. NOTE: My only small complaint is that prior to arriving I had gone onto "myaffinia" and requested certain items be placed in our room (i.e., certain pillows, nail polish kit, etc.) -- and, while checking in, the front desk even commented on it -- but we never received any of the items I had requested. My son, however, finally called down and requested a sound pillow -- which he got and loved. But all of the other items I had previously requested and confirmed on arrival -- were never brought to our room.

“You couldn't do better if you tried.” I knew this would be a great experience when a good friend that I have a great amount of respect for, recommended this location. I had a terribly long and busy week, but this hotel was so great, it made me relax and put a smile on my face. Every aspect about it was amazing. The bed was perfect, the Television was clear and worked quickly, which I can't say about many hotels. The decorations were great, I loved the art on the walls. Design couldn't be better, neither could the soaps and toiletries. I can't rave enough about how much I loved this location. Even the hotel restaurant was amazing. I ordered the chicken and waffles, Mac and Cheese, three cocktails, and paid less than I did at my last hotel for a Philly Cheese steak and a coke! The prices were amazing, almost as amazing as the food and drinks. But I will say that the drinks are either on the Tart or Sweet side. Every time I was told a drink was not too sweet or too sour, I felt that it was. My only other qualm, was that my room key was deactivated before I had departed and the woman I called on the phone at the concierge desk (not front desk), was not very friendly, so I went to the front desk and they were happy to help me. If you love your technology, fine art, great sleep, and the ability to impress your guests, this would be the place. Any husbands out there who are looking for something romantic to do for Valentines day, take your wife here for food and drinks, then head up to your room. Guarantee she will fall deeper in love with you. Anytime I find myself back in Seattle, I will be staying here. It's a short walk away from Pike Market, has a great staff, and the fact that there is a technology hub in the rooms with USB chargers, A/V , HDMI, and component ports is incredible. Now stop reading this post and go book your room before they are fully booked if the aren't already for the next 50 years.

“perfectly fine, but nothing special” The property is convenient to the airport and nearby major roads. Planes take off and land away from the property, and the rooms facing the airport actually seem a bit more quiet than the ones facing the roads on the other side of the property. Service was fine with check-in and check-out. My room was a decent size with a nice very small balcony, the bed was comfortable, and the shower had enough water pressure. The room was broom-clean, but could have used a bit of deep-cleaning, and it had some deferred maintenance issues (e.g., a leaky faucet that was reported but never fixed). There was a charge for parking (valet approx $22/day and self-park approx $18/day) that seemed unnecessary and excessive, given that the parking in surrounding office parks appeared to be free. Food in restaurants was overpriced for what it was, but served in large quantities - some room-service dishes were pretty bad. There were some restaurants within a reasonable walk, and plenty within a short driving distance. All in all, it's a perfectly serviceable, comfortable property with pretty good service. It's not extraordinary in any way, but it's a solid choice, and I'd likely stay there again.

“Good hotel, GREAT location” We stayed here two nights at the end of Nov. 2006 as tourists NYC. Got a good deal through Priceline. The hotel is older, but it has great character. Service from the front desk and the concierge were impeccable. However, the lobby area can get very busy during the early evening. Our room was nice; pretty much what you would expect from Marriott - complete with essential amenities. The only complaint about the room was that it quite noisy at all hours, with the traffic on Lexington. The highlight is that the hotel is in a GREAT location with a lot of GREAT shopping nearby and easy access to cabs and the subway.

“No me deslumbro” Nos recibieron muy bien convidandonos con unas cookies calentitas que no se si le dan a todos los huespedes o solo a los que somos hilton honnors. Nuestra habitacion daba al fondo del hotel y no era una linda vista. Lo positivo, tenia wifi pero solo en la zona de recepcion. Teniamos desayuno incluido, normal, podria ser mas variado. En el check out quisimos abonar con 2 tarjetas distintas para compartir la cuenta y la recepcionista no sabia hacerlo, tuvimos que llamar al gerente para que lo resuelva. La ubicacion es bastante buena, muy linda zona. Tienen maquinas expendedoras de bebidas y snacks en algunos pisos.

“Great budget hotel” I stayed at the Belleclaire Hotel after finding it on the internet, on my 6th visit to NYC in November 2005. I was careful to book a twin share room with a private bathroom, but upon arrival found the room was a double. Within minutes, my cousin and I were checked into a great little twin room that had been recently refurbished. The beds were comfy, the linen was crisp and fresh, the quilts new and the pillows soft and fluffy! The bathroom was clean and had been renovated with a regular size bath and shower over. Typical of New York hotels, my view was of a brick wall, but I wasn't in New York City to sit in my room to look at the view so that didn't bother me at all. The staff were really friendly and more than helpful with tourist info. The location is perfect for those not so keen on staying in the hustle and bustle of midtown and I found it to be really quiet. It's a good half hour walk down Broadway to Times Square (maybe longer), but a pleasant stroll after a meal or a show. It's also a great location to stay if you're interested in museums and exploring Central Park. The subway is a mere hop skip and jump away so easy to get anywhere in Manhattan. Big bonus having a 24 hour supermarket next door and the 24 hour Manhattan Diner diagonally across the road that did a great brunch! At least I think it was open 24 hours! Oh, and the pizza place next door looked like a dive, but did awesome slices of pizza. All in all, a great little budget hotel for people who have maybe been to New York before and are looking for something a little quieter. Would I stay there again? Yes. Enjoy New York! And for those of you who thought the lift was too small ... get out of the hotel and enjoy the fabulous energy of New York City instead of spending time in the lift!!!

“really a DREAM hotel” in the heart of meatpacking district, close to the most beautiful places and amenities of south Manhattan. Crowdy, trendy, nice views, spacious rooms, a great experience in the city that never sleeps.

“Very Nice.....” I just needed a safe clean room at a good price. I found this here! My room was huge. Bathroom and shower huge. Nice kitchenette and mini bar. It is nit the Four Seasons, but I felt it was an excelent value. Good location, also. I checked in early and they were very accomodating. The only bad part was I had black hairs all over the bathroom. I guess the housekeeper was having a problem. Other than that, it was very nice. I would stay here again.

“Amazing Pool Area” We stayed in one of the property's casitas twice in the last month, so this is a review of that particular type of room. The casitas are large and have a private carport and private entry. They have lots of room and would be great for families. The downstairs had a dining table, 2 sofas, t.v., wet bar and small refrigerator with 1/2 bath. Upstairs is the main bedroom with full bath and bed. The decor in the casitas was a bit run down, with really old burgundy carpet, very outdated bathroom fixtures, and furniture in desperate need of reupholstering. I think with some simple remodeling updates, this could be a first-rate property. One of our casitas had a nice large balcony off the main bedroom, while the other had a huge sundeck right off the second floor. The sundeck had a full sized table with 4 chairs and an umbrella and 2 lounge chairs! Awesome for soaking in the Arizona sun. One casita overlooked a "private" pool, which was so much fun to step right outside and hit the water. This is a super resort for kids! The main swimming pool area is amazing! The Hole-in-the-Wall River Ranch has a huge lazy river, waterfalls, mini golf, a Western themed town and a gorgeous outdoor patio with a firepit and smores at night. If you have kids, this is a super place to stay!

“Overworked Housekeeping Staff” Stayed for a quick overnight in-town getaway. The cleanliness of the rooms for the price is not worth it. Sheets are not changed everyday anymore. You have to request it. Towels not changed everyday either unless you request it. Hotel was over run by convention visitors. The Housekeeping Staff do the best they can, but they now have to clean 30 rooms a day (according to housekeeper that I talked to). Thats only 16 minutes a day. They used to clean 16 rooms a day. Which is the typical amount most hotels require their housekeepers. I worked for several years at a Marriott and that was they required from the housekeepers. 16 rooms equates to 30 minutes per room. This was confirmed recently by the local news. So, dont expect a very clean room if you stay here. For health reasons, I hope the Manchester Hyatt management staff realize that a room cannot be sufficiently cleaned and sanitized between guests. Do you want to stay in a hotel that only allows their cleaning staff 16 minutes to clean the mess of a previous guest? Otherwise, the views are outstanding. Convenient to the Gaslamp and Seaport Village Shopping/Dining area.

“pretty good for NYC” We cashed in some SPG points for a free night here and were very happy with the hotel. A couple of hiccups, but nothing serious. We were first assigned a room that the desk clerk said, with a smile (as if it were a good thing), was on a floor with an ice machine. Only when we saw that the ice machine was jammed into a space between the stairs and our room did we see why he was smiling. My loved one said it wasn't a big deal until I asked her to go into the room, close the door, and I then pushed the button for ice. After the avalanche of ice and noise she opened the door and said, "Let's move.". It was literally next to the wall that was 2 feet from the bed. We got a nice room on the SPG floor (no ice machines). The size was typical for NYC budget hotels, enough room to move around, but not a whole lot of room. We were on a very quiet side facing the back of buildings on 24th street, so minimal street noise. We could hear the conversation of the maids quite clearly, so pray you get quiet neighbors. The room was done nicely with the famous sweet sleeper and decent ammenities in the toilet. The location is great if you like Chelsea, but it's close to walk to mid-town, Union Square, or even the village if it's nice out. The major downside to this place is the breakfast. They wanted $3 for a simple coffee. I told the guy I was only going to have half a cup anyway, so he let it go, "Just this one time" he scolded. Seriously, for rooms starting at $225 a night, they can't have complementary coffee in the lobby or restaurant? Summary, go there, it's nice, clean, relatively cheap for NYC, no pool, gym, good service and nice staff. Bring your own ice!

“Detail Oriented, Great Sleeping” I slept great at this hotel. Didn't hear a thing all night which is amazing considering its central location. My room was small but just right for one person. I was amazed by the excellent service at this hotel. It was the kind of service that you expect from a 5 star hotel. Every little request I made was attended to immediately. Also, the room had many amenities that are usually found only in more expensive places. I would definitely return here.

“Great location; poor hotel” The good: Hotel is in a great location, close to a lot of good NY spots The bad: Basic rooms are miniscule (imagine jumping across the bed to get to the other side of the room), A/C units are very loud, lighting in rooms is not great, very expensive relative to other places you could be staying

“Embassy Sweet!” The room was a king size with a pull out sofa that accommodated our family of four. The stay included the usual manager's free drinks and appetizers. The free full breakfast was outstanding and the walk to the convention center was less than 2 blocks. The parking on the street on the weekend was plentiful and cheap and our view was great. Additionally, we were only a few blocks from Chinatown and several attractions. From the excellent service to great rooms, I will definetly go there again. Kudo Sweet Embassy!

“A cat or two would scare away the mice.” I stayed at the Hotel 31 when the sister hotel, Hotel 17 was booked. It came highly recommended from the staff. Well, never again! While the room was large, I had the misfortune of being awaken by a mouse at 2:30am! I called the front desk and they explained that because of the construction next door that mice had come into the hotel! Not even a "I can move you" gesture, nothing, nada, zero. Just a chuckle and a "yea we have a mice problem" attitude. Disgusting! Never Never again> Stay away from this mouse infested hotel.

“Oversized shower -- plenty of room for two” Yes, the shower might have been the best thing about the room. Lots of room for extracurricular activities. The room layout was great too: two queen beds facing a swivel TV and then a living area with chairs and a couch (see photos). The hotel scored some points from me for having my favorite toiletries (Aveda rosemary mint shampoo). The shuttle to the airport was on-time; it runs to the airport on the half hour. The only problem was that the door handle didn't work properly -- as you closed the door, the locking mechanism extended so you couldn't close the door (see photo). I told the front desk, so I'm sure it's fixed by now.

“Fine stay” This is a newer property and it shows. Everything is quite clean and well serviced. We stayed as a visiting business guest. Our itinerary was 'club level', but this was not in the booking system. Upon discussing this with the front desk, we were given full access to the club level amenities, but not physically roomed on the club level. That was fine with us. Bed was comfortable. Pillows too soft for me (i realize i am finicky in this department). There was a reasonable amount of room noise from our neighbor (sounded like a late night drinking group), and I did call the front desk who had security put out the flames. Much appreciated. Check in and out was fast and stress free. You are right on the Easton shopping complex. My wife loved this as she could walk to any store she wanted and the movie theater while I was out on business. I would stay here again and would recommend this to everyone from families to business travelers.

“The Most Inattentive I-Don't-Care Staff Ever Seen” We selected this hotel because of its proximity to the Amtrak Station. We were just using it as a quick way-station between the train one day and a flight the next. I cannot understand why Crowne Plaza is considered upscale. The accommodations are certainly acceptable, but not much more – and the service at this location was appalling. I called a couple weeks before my stay and there was no answer for five + minutes. My next phone experience was after check-in. The ventilation system didn’t work, so I telephoned for assistance. The operator put me through to front desk and it went straight to voice mail!! I tried again and no operator picked up at all. My husband finally went down to the front desk which was unattended; he had to search for someone to help him. With 398 guest rooms, you would think someone would be minding the place. When my husband finally located someone, they told him that they’d send someone up to take care of the problem. I called down to ask when he’d get there and I was told (verbatim): “When he knocks on your door.” When the man arrived, we showed him the wall unit and demonstrated that turning the dial did nothing. He says, no, you have to use the thermostat – which was way on the other side of the room. We didn’t even see it and apparently the front desk personnel didn’t know anything about it, as I learned when I later explained what happened to the in case another guest had a similar experience. And the system didn’t work anyhow. There is no setting for “fan.” It is either AC or heat with an automatic turn-off when the room reaches the desired temperature; we had to keep adjusting the temperature all night. Although there was a balcony, we couldn’t leave it open it for fresh air because of the roar of traffic from the adjacent expressway.

“Holiday Inn Plus” The bottom line is that this is a Holiday Inn. A little nicer furnishings but basically a Holiday Inn. The biggest issue I have with the hotel is the location. It's right on Wabash and the "L" runs 20 feet away every 3-5 minutes. We had a room in the back which I requested and the "whooshing" sound went on forever. The noise is an annoyance, but not a prohibitive issue. Staff tries hard. All but one young man who works on Sundays and has an attitude. Management probably knows who he is. I won't give his name, but he's slight of build. Couple we were travelling with had a problem with a distinctly moldy smell in the room. They were finally moved, but it took a lot more arguing than it should have. And this was dealing with the manager, not my arrogant friend. Room rates seem to be all over the board on this place. Weekend rates can be reasonable or outrageous. We stayed for three nights. We had three rates and the highest rate was twice the lowest. And you don't get a lot of warm fuzzies walking on Wabash after dark. The hotel insists there's no problems, but they sure have plenty of security in the ground floor entry. In terms of hotel preference, the Silversmith ranks in about the middle of the pack of Chicago hotels.

“good location if you like to golf or shop” This is a medicore westin property- mainly due to service issues. The setting is pretty- 20 minutes form the riverwalk- surrounded by golf courses, six flags and an upscale mall. There is not much around other than that- so if you like to be able to walk to fun restaurants or bars- this is not the place for you. This would be a fun place to bring children- given the proximty to Six flags, also, they have nice pools. The westin work out and spa are ok as well. If would reccomend having a room that faces the pool and countryside over the city view- all I saw from my room was the valets talking. It is a nice property- but if you want to see the san antonio sighs I would stay at the westin at the Riverwalk.

“Second time even better than the first!” We were fortunate enough to visit this gem one more time. We paid in Starwood points and regular good old fashioned do re mi! Our two rooms were adjoining with a private hallway that we shared. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. Everything was "clean a whistle"...whatever that means! The showers were both so strong that we were almost knocked over! We never encountered another guest on our floor and only saw one or two other guests on the elevator just once or twice during our whole stay there...this hotel is PRIVATE!!!! We used the complimentary limo service three times and the driver was courteous. It was really fun traveling in high style! They say the driver will only drive you 10 blocks, but that number was very loose... Also, be sure to stop at the Illy coffee shop across the street in the indoor public park area...yummy!

“The Stoneleigh For Business is Comfortable” In this part of town for business travel The Stoneleigh is a good bet (as compared to the Warwick, Palomar or even the Mansions – have not stayed at The Ritz yet). The rooms are comfortable, quite and clean and the bathrooms have been completely redone (unlike the Warwick). I stay in the studio suite for some extra room. While I have not tried the spa, this is not a hotel of elevated personal service like The Four Seasons – they have trouble calling you by name and there is a small front desk area with typically one person working, so you have to wait. The hotel bar could use a little more customer focus also, and dining was typical, but there is a great steak place across the street. If you are on business, go to the bar at the Warwick and stay in a comfortable room at The Stoneleigh. If you want a higher level of personal attention, go to the Crescent, Four Seasons, etc. as this is a notch down.

“Great rates, average hotel” Stayed a couple of nights with an amazing rate of $109 that included valet parking. Valet service was nothing special and I had to take care of the luggage myself while the guy stood there still expecting a tip. Front desk service was very good and quick. I had requested early check-in and my room was available 4 hours early, which was very nice. I was in the "Club Tower", though I found this to be nothing special, so I do not recommend paying extra for it. The Club lounge was closed on weekends and had only modest food when it was open, though the lounge itself is very large and nice. The rooms were only average, though quiet and comfortable. The hotel is still within walking distance to most DC sights at a fraction of the cost of hotels a few blocks closer. I also felt safe walking around outside the hotel, since it is a fairly active area with several popular restaurants nearby.

“River Inn is fantastic!” I had a quick one night stay in DC, and the company paying for my visit put me in the River Inn. I'd hear good things about it, but I've never stayed there. The last time I stayed in DC, I was at Hotel Madera in Dupont Circle. I have to say, I LOVED the River Inn. The decor was very similar to Hotel Madera - very fashionable and sleek. The hair products are Aveeno and simply wonderful. The rooms are extremely large - I was upgraded to a one-bedroom suite overlooking the street but I understand all the rooms have their own kitchens. What a great bonus if you are staying in DC for a vacation! The furnishings were beautiful, and the bathroom was gorgeous - Kohler sink that I would love to have in my house, and the bath/shower was stunning as well. I loved the bedding - the pillows were wonderful, firm but still very comfy, and they had these gorgeous soft throws to snuggle up with. My only complaint is the TVs are small and old - they are perhaps 19", which is definitely not what I'm used to in nice hotels. Plus, in the bedroom, the remote for the TV only worked for channels - the volume and power buttons didn't work. That meant I had to drag myself out of the cozy bed to shut the TV off. I love the neighborhood - very close to a metro, the Watergate complex with a grocery store just a few minutes walk away, and right near George Washington University, which means you've got the energy and excitement of all those students. Despite this, the River Inn is extremely quiet and the residential street that it's on has almost no traffic. I would definitely stay here again, and if I was bringing family for a vacation to DC, I am 100% sure that I would book the River Inn. PS I had excellent service as well.

“Good modern compact hotel...” First time at a Yotel.... At first it's interesting intriguing and a tad confusing. But once oriented it's a great concept. The cabins are an efficient and thoroughly cool design but they are compact. For one person it's perfect but for two you better really like each other! The best surprise was dinner one night at Doh Yo the restaurant..... Alll small plates and wonderful! Still dreaming of the dessert..... Churrahs! Oh my!:-)

“Welcome Back Four Seasons!” I for one, am very happy to see the Four Seasons back in Seattle. I used to be a semi-regular at what was the Four Seasons Olympic before they sold it to Fairmont and was so pleased to have a nice high-end property back in Seattle. I have to say, the old Four Seasons reminded me a bit of what you expect a Ritz Carlton to be like (traditional, etc.) and this one is much more in Four Seasons style (modern, sleek, etc.). Location is great, you can walk to everything and close to the city attractions, water, great dining, shopping and park activities. Be warned (as others have mentioned) it is in a mixed-bag part of the city, on one side you have the arts district but you also have an element of homeless and "X" rated places. This is a bit what every city has and as long as you are smart about your surroundings when going out, you will be fine. The number one thing I like about Four Seasons is the service. They make you feel special and all the little touches are especially nice (i.e. fresh ice being brought to your room each night, the turndown service, the staff being friendly and helpful). I certainly can’t complain on the rooms, they are brand new so clean, comfortable, etc. etc. The views are “urban” (even the water ones to some degree, we did opt to pay for a premium room). I have to say, however, this location compared to the old one, is better. I am not sure if the extra cost we paid for the premium room was worth it (I did not go into the city rooms) but we enjoyed our room a lot (who does not like a new room)? The restaurant was excellent, especially for a hotel. It has personality and a unique style onto it’s own. The gym, pool and spa are also nice (I utilized them all). I did use the spa for a couple of highly overpriced treatments but loved every minute of it! I used to also frequent the spa at the former Seattle Four Seasons and this one is much more ZEN and relaxing! Welcome back to town Four Seasons, hope you will be here to stay for a while!

“Pretty good overall” I don't have a good track record of picking hotels in New York and so when this one was recommended to me by a colleague I thought I might as well give it a shot. Overall, I was not disappointed. Arrival impression was not great because at street level is the restaurant; reception is upstairs and I was not offered assistance with my luggage. Furthermore, both receptionists were on the phone when I arrived and so I waited longer than I would like to check in - which after 8 hours travelling is not welcome. Room itself was clean and looked fairly recently updated, bed comfortable, decent bathroom. As with most NYC hotels, pretty small though. I didn't have any noise issues (another common problem in NY). Breakfast quite nice. Wall Street is about a 25min walk away. Certainly worth considering.

“Older hotel, great location for travel and conference goers” Stayed here for 4 nights due to business travel- this hotel directly connect to Conference Center- big plus. The hotel is older- there is some wear and tear in places, but it is in a great location. Next to Reading Terminal Market- not just a farmer's market, but have booths that sell cheese steak sandwiches, ice cream, great Amish breakfast, etc. The Market does have free wifi as well. The Italian place (Mangione's- spelling?) behind the hotel on Filbert Street has great Italian food. About 8 blocks walk to Independence Square and Liberty Bell. Close to metro and train stations. Only ate conference food, so I do not know price/quality of food at hotel- went elsewhere to eat at night. Does have a laundry room on 8th floor, but it was difficult to get quarters from the hotel for them. Did not drive, so could not say anything about parking or valet parking.

“Lackluster Luxury-ish” I am accustomed to staying in NYC hotels of this category, and at first sight, the Palace stands tall. The building, the lobby and all public areas are outstanding. I stayed in a room which was $545, probably among their lower priced rooms---but still, it represented a severe drop in quality from my first impressions. It was basically a completely ordinary room, ordinary furnishings, cheap old fashioned tv, nothing whatsoever which would give you the impression of any level of luxury. The bedding was well below the standards of the chain hotels which seem to pride themselves on bedding these days. The Palace bed had thin, cheap feeling linens, a completely average blanket, all what you might expect at the most ordinary Sheraton. Even the bathroom "lotions and potions" were ordinary, private labelled, just like you'd find in a Hilton or Marriot. There wasn't even a thermostat in the room! I should add that the lobby staff is abundant with bellhops, but every time I needed them, I had to interrupt their constant chatter among themselves. And finally, at checkout, there was $60 of food charged to my account which I had never purchased. They fixed it, but still, this is not how fine hotels operate. Take a look at the St. Regis if you'd like to enjoy luxury done right at a similiar price.

“Go for the Gold Floor” As with many of the US Fairmont hotels, this is a large ornate hotel built in 1912. The regular reception desk is almost a block long with the regular Concierge desk about half that size. We booked into the Gold Floor with its own check-in, Concierge and lounge and didn't regret it. The rooms are spacious and luxurious, and all the members of the Concierge team were very knowledgeable about restaurants and sites to see in Boston. A large buffet breakfast (with Boston Baked Beans among about 30 other things!) is laid out as is a large pre-dinner spread (including Vodka from Maine). The Concierge Manager, John, is from Ireland which seemed perfect for Boston and he knew all there was to know about what we should see. We've stayed at several other Boston hotels before, but would definitely return to this one...but only at the Gold Floor level. One warning: there is a $39/night parking fee. When we do it again, we'll let the Concierge get us a car once we're at the hotel, not arrive with one and pay for it to be parked.

“Wonderful” We booked this hotel via priceline for a same day visit. I will most certainly go back. I loved it! Our room was not large but plenty big enough for two. The tray ceiling makes it seem "roomier". I loved that they use Aveda products in the bathroom. The room itself was very clean and quiet. We enjoyed the flat screen tv as well. The only downside was that the bed itself was a bit hard but not enough to keep me awake...but enough for me to know I wasn't in a heavenly bed:) I will also advise anyone staying there that the valet parking was a bit pricey ($35). We enjoyed a nice breakfast at the espresso bar in the lobby. They offered coffee, tea, latte's, sweet rolls, yogurt, fruit, homemade oatmeal (with brown sugar, craisins, golden raisons, etc)..the prices were comparable to a Starbucks. All in all quite a nice surprise for us as I had never noticed this hotel on recent visits.

“Decent Enough” This was an adequate stay for a reasonable price. The hotel is well situated on E 50th; across the street are both the Benjamin and Affinia 50, so others might want to try them for comparison. There's nothing special about the property. The reception lounge is relatively small yet efficient. The executive room I took was ok, decent space, comfortable sofa and chairs, workable kitchen facilities - but not of a quality of a place like the Alex. Bathroom was small yet functional - ok water pressure and Aveda giveaways. Bed quality was fine. Two gripes were the towels and the continental breakfast. The towels were so worn and thin that I thought their sandpaper-like quality might exfoliate my entire body without ever really drying it. Really, it was like a bad summer camp experience. And the continental breakfast was bland, cheap in quality and tasteless. The hotel management must have someone specifically picking up months supplies of huge quantities of nourishment at BJs or Walmart. So, if you want that location (50th and 3rd) for a decent night's sleep, grab a discounted rate and avoid the breakfast. It's a decent enough place for a night or two (p.s. go get a breakfast bagel at Ess-A-Bagel and coffee across the street and don't even try to justify the embedded continental breakfast cost).

“nice rooms/not as nice lobby and location” I was in town for business recently and stayed two nights. The location, near the Convention Center/Chinatown area, was a couple blocks too far for a female traveling alone. I didnt feel very comfortable walking home once it was dark outside. The cab fare I spent each day to feel a little safer going to and fro could have been spent on an upgraded hotel. The rooms were very comfortable. Smaller than I expected, but sufficient. Bathrooms were clean and shower was nice. First night woken at 1am-ish for garbage collection on side of building, right outside of window. That was disruptive. All in all, a good value but I would probably not return in the future.

“First time at Rouge and I was not disappointed” Im a big Kimpton fan and frequent traveller to DC but this was first visit to the Rouge. I will definately come back. Typically I got complementary upgrade to King deluxe room. Lots of room, light and very clean. My only request was for "quiet" room and my upper floor room on back side of hotel was very quiet. Good location. Few blocks to shops and restaurants on Connecticut Ave and 17th Street. About 4 easy blocks to Metro. Staff were super. Good value and I highly recommend to business travelers and anyone else for that matter.

“Buyer Beware!” This was a one night stay so my contact with the hotel was limited. I thought the front desk and it's President's Club Check in was a model of efficiency. My room was a rather strange one. I assume that when the hotel opened in 1913, this was two tiny rooms with a shared bath. As it is now configured, one of the rooms is a tiny two armchair and a desk sitting room, the other a bedroom with an armoire holding a TV and the minibar. The bathroom is between these rooms. A little odd and were I staying longer I would have requested something else. The bathroom is fine, the cleanliness unquestionable and the bed comfortable. I was pleased to see that one of the benefits of memembership in the President's Club is free internet access. Unfortunately, I use WiFi so much that I'd left my ethernet card at home and could not be connected through the hotel system. This led to an unfortunate use of the lobby work stations which are pay per use and I ended with a staggering $30.50 bill for 13 minutes of service and the printing a boarding pass. Buyer beware. There is no business center here and that I think is a major debit for this property.

“Great choice for our needs” As per a lot of other reviewers, we chose this hotel for an overnight stay between flights to/from LAX. This hotel was a great choice for our needs. Yes, we agree it is not 5-star, but it is comfortable and quiet. Easy pick-up from LAX using the wall phone at the terminal exit. Courteous drivers and easy check-in. Only mild problem was lugging bags up to the second floor. We also used the Denny's on site for a light lunch upon arrival and later, for dinner. Once again, not a winner but more than adequate. Our morning flight was too early to take advantage of the included breakfast, but no problem, the shuttle driver grabbed an assortment of pastries and fruit for all of his passengers. We not only recommend this hotel for an overnight stay, but will have no hesitation of staying there again.

“Never saw the inside” As a Diamond frequent stay member of the Hilton Honors program I had read reasonably positive reviews here on Trip Advisor and booked a three night reservation at this property. In July I called the HH Diamond desk reservation line and asked that the reservation be amended to one night from three as my family member had returned to the hospital with their battle against cancer and I would be returning home earlier. Before allowing the changes to be made to my reservation I asked the agent to make sure that the rate would not change and they assured me it would not. After hanging up the rate had tripled when I looked back at the reservation online. Though the weekend rate for Friday I was requesting could have originally been booked at the same rate for one night or each of the three nights as originally booked. In calling back to the 800 Hilton/Doubletree reservations line I was to told to call the hotel myself as Hilton Reservations couldn’t get anyone to fix their error........ I spoke first with the hotels front office manger first for assistance who said you will have to pay the new rate in our system as we don’t honor our companies booking errors. The General Manager of the hotel also said we will not honor the rate you originally booked with us at our website. Reason given. The hotel is doing better business now since you originally booked the reservation. We are here to make as much as we can on our rooms. However we could rebook the room for 50 dollars off the rack rate for the Friday night. you intend to stay......... Never in decades of travel have I come across such silly behavior with a brand I support all over the domestic US. And booking mistakes have certainly happend before over the years. Needled to say I cancelled and had a fine stay elsewhere. This post is just to make others aware of the less then cooperative business behavior of the hotel and in no way represents the experience inside the hotel itself during a stay. My experience tells me when a hotels management and business culture is this inflexible before the stay I would not want to be a guest inside the hotel and need their cooperation during my stay.It is interesting to note that this same hotel who refused to honor my previously booked and confirmed reservation through the Hilton website had been dumping rooms on Priceline for 50 dollars a night on those same nights.My suggestion is management get a refresher course in a good hotel business school...........

“Good location,” Good location, but room and amenities are somewhat dated. In their defense they are remodeling through 2013. The staff was very nice. The location is within easy walking distance of Central Park, Times Square, or Rockerfeller plaza.

“立地が良い” シカゴ滞在は一泊で、しかも観光&ショッピングの時間は6時間ほどでしたが、立地の良いこのホテルのおかげで、シカゴ滞在を楽しむことができました。小さめのスーツケースだったので、空港からは地下鉄を利用し、最寄の駅から荷物を引いてホテルに到着しました。フロントが何というかとってもカジュアルでホテルっぽくなく、驚きました。 部屋は値段に比例してか、狭く感じました。朝食は、フルーツ、シリアル、パン、ジュースなど、ゴージャスではないですが、充分だと思います。家族連れの滞在客が多かったです。すぐ近くがミシガン通りで、ショッピングも美味しいレストランもあり、とっても楽しかったです。

“Great public spaces, Corner Suite = depressing and, just...icky...” I am a SPG Gold Member (I travel a lot for work and love it!). For this trip, I booked an Executive Suite (online deal via SPG web site) for business. They gave me a standard room instead. After a short wait they were able to find a Corner Suite. However, even though this sounds great (and most other Sheraton's Corner Suites ARE great), this one smelled musty, dank and the best word I can think of is...icky... (when the manager met me with the key to this 2nd room - he even commented that it was "musty" and did I want housekeeping to "spray it." I opted out of that masking solution. Anyway, it is not a very comfortable room overall.The worst part was the air conditioning, which not only sounds like a loud, rattling lawn mower in your room, but it also leaks (the carpet was wet - was nice stepping in that with stocking feet-yuck). When you turn it off it sounds like water torture (drip, drip, drip, drip...) dripping into the space/wall (I looked inside the wall vent and sure enough there was a puddle in there). I called and they were going to send engineering to fix the AC when I was away from the room working, but it was not fixed. Also, the room had an odd, very strong odor of cigarette smoke & BO upon my return. Again, ick. The bed was somewhat 'thin' and hard and there were no extra blankets. The tub water backs up to your calves when you take a shower (triple ick). I usually order room service, but the room was so dank and depressing and smelly and... icky :), I left to sit alone in the lobby restaurant. Positives: The Corner Suite is MASSIVE - and if you want space - that is what you get (albeit, not very comfy space). I have stayed at this hotel 4-5 times and the staff is always very pleasant and accommodating (when you have an issue they throw lots of points at you to 'fix' it - which is OK with me because I am a points hound, but I wish I didn't have to complain in the first place). Watching the planes land at LAX is fun from the room. The lobby is modern and bustling and the bar area is well laid out, which is a great place to people-watch, and although the service was sloooow, the food is decent 'bar' food. Starbucks in the lobby (but very long lines - out into the lobby - in the AM). Very easy to catch a cab at any time of day...

“Beware: bed bugs found here!!!” This was the second time I've stayed at this location, but never again. The property is old and worn, and on my most recent trip I made an unsettling discovery that my room had bed bugs. While the mattress seemed fine, after sleeping in the bed for an hour and waking from itching of being bitten, later inspection showed evidence of bed bug feces on the cover to the box spring (among other things like hair, gross!) I alerted the front desk, who simply asked if I wanted another room--clearly they don't understand that if it's in one room, its likely in others. They offered me points and to not charge me for the room, but did not seem to take the matter seriously, even after I showed them pictures. I immediately left and went to the hampton inn down the street that helped me treat my clothing in their dryer and set me up with a nice room. Not only is the Sheraton below standard for a Starwood property, I was saddened by their non-chalante attitude and made sure to report the incident to corporate.

“Great Service, Great Location, Perfect for Meetings” Normally, I dread a trip to an airport hotel, however I have found the exception to that rule! I found this Hyatt to be a real gem - clean, quiet, great service -even good food (when do you see THAT at a business hotel?) and great Wi-Fi service! There are two Hyatt hotels at DFW - the Gand Hyatt is closer to the runways, and the Hyatt Regency, where I stayed, is across the street and further from the runways (which I would assume makes it quieter). Free shuttle service makes the trip from any one of the numerous terminal buildings a snap. My room was on the 9th floor facing the airport. It was clean and spacious. I was able to keep the room very cool, and found it to have a large work space that allowed me to be productive. While Wi-Fi service is often slow at hotels, I chose an option that allowed up to three devices to connect and all at a higher speed. Certainly the best Wi-Fi service I've had while traveling. DFW is a large and isloated airport (thanks to crazy road construction surrounding the airport),and I was very happy to find great service and good food in the hotel restaurant for both lunch and breakfast. Finally, as other reviewers have mentioned, every staff member I encountered was pleasant, personable and helpful. All had a smile and a genuine approach that made me feel welcome. I'd stay here again without hesitation.

“Yummy” Stayed for two nights on a business trip - on the meeting convener's dime. Truly lovely hotel, spacious room, extensive workout area that included private women and men's whirlpool and steam rooms. Staff members were helpful and good natured - the turn down service warmed the room each evening in ways I'd not experienced before. This was the most resort-like hotel I've had the pleasure to stay in. Two things to note: there is no commerical district nearby, so dining option are very limited. If you're willing to walk a mile or two, you can get to areas with more choice. While menus from the hotel's restaurants / room service offered a broad array of choices, the prices were very high - I paid $46 for a house salad and appetizer. Would gladly stay again if seeking a respite from the mad rush of D.C.

“Totally charming!” What a lovely and comfortable visit! The lobby alone wafts you back into Round Table days, all dark wood and elegance. My room was truly large enough for two, a rarity in these days of boutique "closets" masquerading as hotel rooms. The staff was so pleasant. The location is not too close to Times Square, across from a great coffee shop, easily reachable by subway. I got a reasonable (for NYC in May) price from Getaroom.com, $267 including all fees, for a Thursday night. The Algonquin is now tied with my other favorite, the Roger Williams, and I like the location even more.

“First stay in DC” Next time would stay more central as this place is on the outskirts however you still have to pay $24 night for parking which is crazy this far out of the city. Check in process was lengthy, took around 15 mins cause checkin lady was continually answering the phone and could not multi task. Room had a king bed, fairly spacious, clean, free wi fi. Bed was comfortable but pillows were tiny.

“Good Value on the Edge of Koreatown” Check-in and check-out were extremely expedient; easy access to Koreatown and Herald Square; hard to beat low triple-digit rates, especially in Midtown Manhattan; not much of a lobby or bar; rooms are small; slim and tall building with a narrow entrance; views are poor on the lower floors.

“amendment” I posted an earlier review about a disappointing stay for a small group at Royal Palms .. I also wrote to the GM, Greg Miller. He has gone over board trying to 'make it right'. I do believe their interest is to be 'guest-centric'. He even refered to my posting here. So if you do book into the property you can rest assured that they will do their all to correct any errors. It IS a romantic setting and while expensive when they do get it right it can be worth it. Certainly better than the hundreds of rooms behemouths they compete with in Scottsdale. don.brown@brownchild.com

“good value on Priceline” my third stay here and all via Priceline. The most recent winning bid was $58 per night two nights. Valet parked because it was most convient. No mention of Priceline during checkin and it was rather fast. Assigned a double non smoking, asked for a king non smoking and that's what I got, away from the elevators. No use of the facilities, except valet and they were rather prompted. Still a small problem was the bathroom toilet, the seat did not fit under the counter, making putting up the seat impossible. Last time, it fit under the counter and I felt the counter every time, like a stick up man robbing me. I think I robbed them with the price.

“Good Gaslamp Hotel, Great Padres Game Hotel” Stayed at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront with a group of 11 for the Padres/Phllies game. I am just going to move straight into the pros/cons for this hotel: Pros: Location for a Ballgame: It is a great location for attending a Padres game. This will increase once the pedestrian bridge is complete. Décor/Style: Personally, I loved the look of the place. The outside is very cool, the décor and style of the lobby and sitting areas works really well situated on the water. The entrance as you drive up the car ramp to the valet is something that you would expect in other large cities, not San Diego, very cool. Same goes for the in room décor, it works. Room Service: Very quick service, good food. Drink Prices: Drinks at both Vela and Odysea were competitive with or less than most places in the Gaslamp. Price: We all got a very good room rate right from the hotel website that was well below what the other hotels in the area were asking. Cons: Noise: The doors in this hotel might be the loudest that I have heard when they are shut. They seem to be super heavy which probably does not help the situation. Tub: The tub would not drain properly so showers were taken with 4 inches of water around the ankles. Check In: We were told our room was not ready yet the other people in our group all got their rooms. Thought that maybe it was b/c we asked for a King Room. When finally got our room after the game it was a double queen room, same as the others in our group. Was not very happy about that. Room Size: The standard two queens room is on the smaller side of rooms that I have stayed at in the gaslamp. Also, no fridge in the room. Location for Dinner: Not sure if I would stay at the Hilton if I was not attending a Padres game or an event at the Convention Center. It is a bit of a walk to get into the heart of the Gaslamp if you do not want to get a taxi. I would stay at the Hilton again if I was going to be attending a Padres game. The Pros do outweigh the Cons of this good hotel in the gaslamp.

“Would not recommend this as a secure location” We arrived on an early flight and had to wait in the lobby until 3.30pm to gain access to a room. The room was clean but very small The staff were less than friendly. Free wifi was available in the lobby and the free breakfast was good including fresh waffles. It is not a very safe location at night. I tried to walk out the front door and even though there were security out there I was approached by someone within 2 secs. It is in downtown LA but has public bus at the door. The hotel entrance is done in grand style.

“My experience was otherwise” I don't doubt my experience is the exception, based on the reliable reviewers' posts, but it should be noted for those Tripadvisorists who live by reviews... that this isn't a perfect hotel. First of all don't get all excited, thinking you're checking into a fancy Hyatt. It's a roadside property at the bottom end of the brand. The rooms are spacious and funky, which is always a welcome addition to the cookie cutters out there. For that I am deeply thankful. That said, it's still a cheap hotel. And in my case, a smelly one. Perhaps it was just this room, though I doubt it. The elevator area had a chokingly bad smell as well. The smell that permeated the entire studio suite was foul. Foul to the point of keeping me up most of the night. Foul to the point of burying my head in the (comfy) pillows to suffocate myself. Foul to the point of leaving my clothes with a stench of, I don't know, a combination of paint, cleaning fluid and old war bandage that needs to be changed. I opened the window to the 18 degree winter, but even that didn't clear the air. Really really unfortunate. They did put my able self in a handicap room when I checked in after midnight, so maybe I just got the leftover room that nobody actually wanted. I don't know. Yes, it's inexpensive for the amenities and space you get, but if you can't sleep for the stench, than it still costs too much.

“Solidly reliable 4-star quality, and affordable!” Return visit to the Intercontinental Chicago after about 3 years. I've been staying at the Four Seasons in the interim, but needed to be down by the river this trip. The IC Chicago is perfectly located on Michigan Ave's "Miracle Mile", in easy walking distance of just about everything - stores, restaurants, clubs, and the river. I've become a fan of IC hotels in recent years in other cities; the last time in Chicago, this one was a bit quirky, but it's now up to snuff. Easy check-in and excellent room facing the lake on the 34th floor (thanks, Trent at the front desk!). Bed check all clear with no critters, but that formerly pillow-top mattress is going to need replacing soon. Huge bathroom with separate glass-enclosed shower stall, excellent shower head, plenty of hot water. Big closet, plenty of hangers. Good-sized desk with good lighting. The room itself was of reasonable size, too, and had windows on two sides. This is a solid 4-star hotel. I could have easily been comfortable there for a week. And, it was affordable ($180/night). The only ongoing peculiarity, not limited to IC hotels, is the ridiculous daily charge for wifi. One can get around that by prepaying to join the "Ambassador" program ($200/yr) if one is going to stay at least 12 nights annually in a hotel. But why do hotel chains annoy their good customers? IC could set itself yet one more level above the rest by raising the rate $5 and offering "free" wifi. But I will be back. The Four Seasons is nice, but the value for money makes the IC a better alternative.

“Clean new hotel, friendly staff” We stayed here from 3/14 - 3/17. The hotel is easy to get to off highway 101. Highland Blvd. is a very busy street so turning left out of the hotel parking lot is almost impossible, you have to go another way if you need to go north on Highland, like if you are going to Universal Studios which is not far up 101. The hotel is very new and is therefore very clean. The staff was always friendly and always greeted us warmly with a smile - the front desk staff, the parking attendant, the maids and the breakfast buffet custodian, everybody.
