The lobby is tiny and only consists of the front desk. Everything else is on the 4th floor, which is good for security purposes. There is a convenience store and a few food places across HIghland, but I felt a bit uncomfortable going there because there are bums that hang out in the parking lot. However they did not bother us for handouts or harass us in any way, it's just a little disconcerting that they are around. The location of the hotel is very convenient to Hollywood Blvd, practically around the corner from the famous Graumann's Theater. Be aware that it is an uphill walk back to the hotel from there, but it is only about 2 - 3 blocks. You can find lots of places to eat there too - we went to the Disney Soda Fountain for an ice cream treat right at the corner of Highland and Hollywood, yum! Our room was an executive queen suite, which was a very large room for a family of four and probably fit 6 comfortably. It was offered to us at the same price as the standard two queen room so it was a good deal at the time. There is no separate living room, just an arched wall separating the beds from the sofabed. The sofabed, being new, was in good shape and not lumpy or uneven. When opened there was still plenty enough space to maneuver around. The queen beds were wonderful and I liked that they provided lots of pillows on the beds. I added photos of the room so you can see how it looks. We were on the 4th floor which was THE BEST, get a room there if you can because all the amenities are there - business center, pool and FREE breakfast buffet. Our room was in a corner of the building and was a few steps from all the amenities and I felt safe letting my 12 and 9 year old daughters run out to breakfast alone to grab a bite in the morning while I finished getting ready. Even though our room was right along Highland Blvd, we never heard traffic noises, and like I said it's a very busy street. I wasn't expecting much from the breakfast buffet because it was free but I was pleasantly surprised. Every morning, there were eggs, bacon or sausage, an array of bready items (bagels, bread, muffins, pastries, cereal), juices, milk and coffee/tea. A very decent start to our day. We really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely recommend this hotel. I would stay here again if I'm ever in Los Angeles.

“ニューイヤーカウントダウンに予約が取れれば楽しいかも。” ニューイヤーのカウントダウン会場の中心付近に位置しているので、お部屋によっては世界一有名なカウントダウンがみれるということで、予約が殺到します。 そのかわり、31日は宿泊者チェックが非常に厳しくなるし、ホテル付近が入場規制内に入ってしまうと身動きとれなくなるのでお気をつけて。 1Fに併設してあるカフェのクッキーが、チェックイン時に宿泊者全員にプレゼントされます。 タイムズスクエアのど真ん中なのにキッチン付きで広々としていて、都市型ホテルとアパートメントタイプのイイトコ取りという感じも、家族ずれにはいいかもです。

“Beautiful hotel, but......” This is a beautiful property and the rooms and spacious and nice. However, the hotel is having some major water pressure problems that makes taking a shower a chore. The water will actually shut off for 10-15 seconds (several times during a shower) and the temperature will vary greatly. The hotel themselves say this problem will only get WORSE over the next year due to construction in the area. The hotel's handling of the issue both while I was there....and in my correspondence afterwards was unprofessional and unsatisfactory. Again, nice place. But if enjoy a nice shower, be warned.....

“Nice hotel, helpful staff....” Having been to a few Ritz Carlton hotels before, I can say that this may not be the best one of the chain but it was certainly very nice. The rooms were good but not exceptional. The bathroom looked as though it was time for a renovation. This is a city hotel and a good choice if you don't need a resort. I would compare this hotel to some of the best in the Marriott chain such as the JW Marriott locations or even the Park Hyatt locations. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Their executive floor lounge was better than average in that they served a very nice buffet for both breakfast and dinner. The public spaces are quite nice.

“Better than the reveiws would lead you to believe” I have stayed at the nearby Courtyard and wasn't overly impressed so the next time I was in the area I decided to stay at this property. Rooms are fine, decor trendy and hip, HVAC worked fine. Flat screen TV. Very good internet connection. Room and linens clean. Housekeeping seemed good. Rooms have a clothes rack vs. an actual closet and there is a single drawer bureau that doubles as a TV stand. Rooms have a strange shape, which breaks up the room nicely, but also makes it difficult where to put suitcases etc. if you have multiply travelers in your room. The lobby area is going through a remodel which has relocated the breakfast area and business center. No big deal but I believe that hotels should be required to disclose this information to anyone making a reservation. The breakfast looked weak and unappetizing and due to the remodel you get the pleasure of eating it in two emptied guest rooms filled with tables. Other than the remodel issues I would stay at this property and it's conditions are much improved than previous reviews would indicate.

“Very Nice Suite for a Wonderful Stay” The king suite was very comfortable for our weekend stay in Jacksonville. The bedroom and bath were separate from the living and kitchen area -- a true suite. The suite had plenty of space and convenience; it was also neat and attractive. We enjoyed having 2 TVs -- one in the living room and one in the bedroom. Everything looked clean. The one thing that I did not like about the Staybridge Suites is that they accept pets. That would certainly be a plus for those who travel with their pets. Those with animal allergies would want to consider this. I wish I had noticed this before staying -- I would have inquired if they have any pet-free rooms. The breakfast every morning was very good. Hot items are offered every morning as well as cold cereals, fruits, and beverages. Even with all the tables available, there were times that seating space was at a premium. Other amenities include a business center, laundry room, and fitness room. The business center has 2 PCs in a quiet room. The laundry is free to use; just bring your own soap and rinse, or buy them at the hotel. We certainly received good value for our money, and the front desk staff were very friendly. With our Priority Club membership, we were able to get late checkout on the day that we were leaving town -- that made our morning much easier.

“Perfect Business Hotel” Stayed at the Westin for four nights while attending the American Academy of Pediatrics National Conference at the adjoining Boston Convention and Exhibition Center. As many have said already, the Westin is perfect for one attending a conference at the BCEC. The hotel is spacious, airy, cool and contemporary in design. It's not warm or intimate. The Westin might be OK for a casual tourist since the World Trade Center T-stop is literally a 5 minute walk from the hotel; however, given convention business, it's unlikely that a "special" rate will be available to make the Westin Waterfront a better deal than other establishments closer to central Boston. I stayed in room 1308. Pluses: 1) The staff seems very prepared for large numbers of people passing through the lobby and/or checking in to the hotel. 2) Nice view of the Boston skyline from 1308. 3) Free internet in the public spaces. Wireless/wired access for a fee in the rooms (two speeds). 4) Very nice and spacious workout room with several Lifefitness treadmills, ellipticals, recumbent and upright bicycles. The indoor pool is just long enough to make laps possible. 5) The Westin is very close to restaurants in the Seaport area. The Seaport and Renaissance Hotels are the two other large establishments in this part of town, and both are only steps away from the Westin though they are technically closer to the waterfront. (The waterfront, incidentally, isn't a particular draw for any of these hotels including the Westin. None are actually on the waterfront). 6) Direct access to the BCEC (in a way both a plus and a minus depending on your point of view). 2) Rooms are typical Westin: contemporary, reasonably spacious, nice bath and amenities, and, of course, the Heavenly Bed. A little wear and tear is evident in some of the furnishings. Minuses: 1) Selection of dining establishments in the hotel is limited, especially for dinner. MJ O'Connors is an "Irish pub" that serves perfectly good food in a very casual environment. Prices are relatively modest. Sauciety is a breakfast and lunch venue that is actually more aligned with the open and contemporary design of the hotel. I had a very enjoyable lunch here. Too bad Sauciety isn't open for dinner! Other restaurants in Seaport are not far away even on foot, but good luck in getting in if convention activity is strong and the Seaport and Renaissance Hotels are full (which is highly likely). 2) While the Westin is theoretically within walking distance of central Boston, the environment isn't exactly "walking friendly." Overall, the Westin Boston Waterfront is a very nice business hotel. The Westin Copley Place would be a better Starwood alternative closer to central Boston.

“awesome beds” I wanted to stay at the westin gas lamp. This hotel was open and I have to say that even though it wasn't on the gas lamp it's a great hotel. The staff is awesome and the rooms were great

“Great location, rooms average” Stayed here for a week for a business meeting. The event staff is exceptional. The rooms are average and halls dark. Very busy property--lobby is always bustling. Concierge lounge just OK. Breakfast consisted of eggs or oatmeal--typically they have bacon or sausage and switch it up--here it was the same everyday. Also, they didn't have sodas as they normally do--just fountain sodas that the staff had to get for you. It's a great location though--right on Michigan Avenue--walk out and you're in the middle of everything. I would stay here again.

“Above and beyond. Great rooms and service.” Just stayed one night for business and found a good rate online and decided to book Hotel 1000. The new construction (2006) was attractive and its downtown location near meetings and shopping. Upon check-in the staff was great, offered us a complimentary drink and upgraded our room. Rooms are spacious (saw two) and contemporary in style (more Four Seasons than Ritz). Complimentary newspaper, coffee and donuts in the morning were a great surprise along with free wifi. As we left, we could not be happier with our stay at Hotel 1000 and found two new water bottles in the cup holders from the valet. Many hotels aspire to exceed expectations but Hotel 1000 deliver with professional and friendly service. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Great service. very contemporary hotel.” Great location, very very contemporary, even the entry door is weird and tricky the whole wall moves and rotates. The bar is nice, prompt service all fresh ingredients drinks. Thats good and bad for some since they can't make like a standard tom collins or long island. Service was great from top to bottom. Seems like everyone gets paid well, from the way they treat you. Great location

“Overpriced below average hotel” I booked a room at the Embassy Suites San Diego for Memorial Day Weekend at the Hilton Honors website. After I was done with the reservation, they offered me an "upgrade" to a suite with a veranda for 9.000 Hilton Honors points and I accepted. Big mistake! Upon arrival, at 2:45PM, I was sent back since there is a big sign letting all guests know that checking time is 4PM and they will enforce this with pleasure. o exceptions! I went back at 4PM and a sleep walking front desk attendant called Franscisco mumbled something inaudible before send me to the special suite with a veranda - room 805. When I got to the room, I realized that I had given away 9000 points for a practical joke that they call "veranda". Please see pic attached and you will understand. The room is dated (see pics) and the hotel has a Motel 8 feeling to it. The downtown area has several nice hotels - Marriott, Hyatt and W - just to name a few, on the same price range, but with a much more upscale feeling. The Embassy Suites is out of place there but still charges premium for a below average property. Breakfast is also average and complementary and the long lines and the mob scene make it frustrating to enjoy a nice meal. But the worse of all is the valet service. I have to say that the crew is very polite and helpful but they can't help the lack of space and organization. To get in the hotel or to get out of it, was always a 30 minutes ordeal. Take a look at the picture where the valet guy is trying to find my key in a pile of keys on the floor... and you pay $30 a night for this mess. I had booked the Embassy Suites Waikiki for an upcoming trip and as soon as I got home I cancelled that reservation. Once was enough. Never more!

“A Nice Place” The Hollywood Celebrity Hotel is well located for seeing the usual Hollywood sights. The rooms with the even numbers face a busy street and the odd numbered rooms face an apartment building's pool. The hotel is very clean with a friendly staff. My room had a nice kitchen and the desk person offered a coffee maker but no coffee. Not really a problem since there's free coffee 24/7 in the lobby. The A/C worked well and I used it to block the noise from the late night party at the adjacent apartment building. I encourage visitors to use the excellent, though limited subway system. It sure beats driving in LA traffic. The Hollywood and Highland, Kodak Theatre complex is lots of fun and just a block from the hotel. Overall, a decent place, at a good price. .. Two thumbs up!

“good hotel, but” We chose this hotel for one night before our flight early the next morning. We always stay in an airport hotel prior to flying. There were a few reasons we chose this particular hotel. First, we found a good rate because it was a Saturday night. It made the hotel comparative even with the $17. per day parking fee. (We were only gone 4 nights.) Second, we knew we would arrive late on Saturday and needed to be at the airport very early on Sunday. Because of its location, we thought we could simply walk to the airport and avoid the shuttle. This is the case if flying US Air; flying the other airlines still requires a shuttle. It was not a great inconvenience, but not what we expected. Returning was easy since the baggage claim does have arrows connecting with this hotel and parking garage and we did walk directly to our car, avoiding the shuttle hassle. The hotel lobby and rooms were probably the nicest accomodations we have ever had at the Philadelphia Airport. We often stay at the Renaissance, and this was a nice upgrade. We will probably stay here again, expecially if flying US Air, if we can find a good rate and are not gone longer than a few days. The parking fees definitely add to the total cost! However, most of the airport hotels are really restricting free parking to Park n Fly packages that are more expensive than their base rate as well.

“Old glory” A few days ago we stayed at the Biltmore. The hotel has a good location (Pershing Square) and is very close to metro. The hotel's lobby is absolutely beautiful, the cocktailbar is great as well. Overall, the service is good. The rooms have good furniture, but the hotel is quite old. Meaning, the mattress is old and squeaky, there are single pane windows and the bathroom is old. The most frustrating thing is the amount of noice coming from LAPD copters at night (single pane windows) and the staff can be quite loud in the morning. As usually with big name hotels, the internet is $10, the parking is $40, there is no fridge or microwave in the room etc. Overall, a wonderful building and good service, but definitely not the right value for money spent.

“Excellent value at a great location” Stayed 3 night in Sept-Oct 2011 at this hotel and were very pleased with it. No, it is not a 4 star hotel, it is a Comfort Inn, so it is not fancy or luxurious, etc. We found it clean, efficient, modern and entirely adequate for our stay. We reserved a mini-suite which was fine, space-wise. Although we were on the 19th floor, the 2 elevators seemed surprisingly sufficient. The bed was very comfortable. We inspected thoroughly for bed bugs before settling in, and found no evidence anywhere. TV was limited; just a few stations and the reception sub-standard (non HD on flat screen TVs?). Free wireless, which worked well. As stated in other reviews, the breakfast area was quite cramped and the lobby small. The good news is that there is indeed a breakfast provided! 39th St is a bit "gritty" but not too much so; really felt like it was part of NYC. Finally --- the location was fantastic. Just a minute or three walk to just about anywhere - Times Square, Penn Station, whatever. Also, our windows were openable; it was nice to get some fresh air. All in all, we had excellent value for money. There were NO substantial weaknesses with this hotel. I was a bit anxious about a midtown Comfort Inn but this was without foundation --- it more than met our expectations at a reasonable price (for Manhattan).

“Spa weekend in Detroit? Don't laugh” The Tony Chi-designed spa is like a whole universe of happy, complete with amazing pools and a jewel box of a fitness center overlooking the whole affair. It's monster, and unbelievably secluded from the rest of the property. You won't want to leave. I have been through a bajillion spas in my time - never did I expect to see something like this in Detroit, which is fabulous in all kinds of ways but not necessarily known for its luxury spas. Everything else is just gravy. I want the front-of-house and executive lounge staff to be better, particularly when paying $300 a night (for admittedly beautiful rooms), but the spa staff were great. So was our waitress at Bourbon Steak - another "are we really still in Detroit?" surprise. Not as good as Roast over at the Westin - that's my opinion, you may want to eat at both and make up your own mind - but amazing all the same. Hope this place survives the local downturn, even though it feels weird to be rooting for a casino.

“Beautiful hotel, great service” I booked two rooms via Priceline at a great rate.It was a beautiful, classice hotel with great service. One of the rooms was very small (bed was way too small for two adults that weren't married) but they changed it to a king, no question. Took the courtesy car to the American Airlines arena, which was a great service. Excellent bathroom/shower and ammenities. Loved the free wi-fi too. Only negatives were the $24 valet parking (no self park) and the small blood stain on our bed's comfortor (eek).

“Perfect For One Night...” It's hard to write a review on a place you only stayed in for one night but here's what we noticed while we were there: The staff at the front desk were friendly for the most part but not above and beyond in any way. For dinner, they of course recommended the hotel restaurant which looked very nice but we were in Chinatown and wanted to enjoy a restaurant that reflected that. We went with Tazia's, a recommendation from the nicer of the front desk clerks, and loved it! Parking was good, it was a bit pricey but you are staying in a large city so that's to be expected. I did like that the parking was in the same building as the hotel. Rooms were basic, nothing wowed us, but nothing greatly disappointed us either. We could hear everyone that passed by outside our door, but this didn't seem to be something that was so bad it awoke us, so overall we were pleased. We would definitely do another overnight here, but would probably look to somewhere with a bit more of a "wow factor" if we were staying in Philly longer.

“Nothing special, good value” LAX hotels can be HIGH! This hotel is very reasonable and offers on-site dining with a couple of restaurants and a lounge that all are adequate. Parking is extra but that is the norm for this area. Room was a little worn but functional. A/C was a little noisy. Sleep number beds in rooms if you get excited by that. Convenience to the airport can't be beat. Set up for the business traveler. Staff was nice. This might not be the quality of property I would normally want to stay, but for LAX, it fits the bill, or lack of bill nicely.
“Business stay” The hotel was average. Nothing was bad and nothing was great. Stay here if the location is convenient. The cost to park is crazy but that is par for the course in DC.

“Great location” This hotel is one block off the National Mall by the Native American Museum. (Others have said best food on the mall!!). It is a clean bed, clean room, very quiet. Location cannot be beat. Very close to L'Enfant Metro - walked easily in the heat with luggage. Room has has a fair sized fridge in the room and plenty of outlets. The staff was great. very friendly. Nice bar/ eatery in lobby. The decor is tired. Old wall paper, plastic trash cans, 60's tile in bath, you get the picture. It needs an update. But would I stay here again? yes. However, if one of the other more updated hotels in the same area was available for even $20 more, I would stay there instead.

“If you get a good rate then it might be ok” I booked a basic room and got a free upgrade but the room was still very small and very dark (hence Night Hotel) particularly as it looked into quite a dingy light well. All in all the hotel was fine. Great location off Times Square. The only gripes, one lift for the entire place which took forever when it was working and a $30 fee if you wanted to store your own drinks in a fridge!

“Un hôtel idéalement situé pour découvrir New York” L'hôtel est situé dans le quartier de Chelsea (à 15mn à pieds de l'Empire State Building et très proche d'une station de métro). Les chambres sont d'une taille correcte, sont confortables et la literie est très bonne. Seul bémol, l'accueil qui pourrait être amélioré.

“Wonderful historic hotel in downtown Denver” I had a great stay at the Brown Palace - staff was friendly and attentive. Loved seeing people having tea and the style of the place. My room was huge, nice towels, bathrobe, etc. Had breakfast there, which was a little pricey but what I expected in a hotel like that. Very handy business center.

“Roomy Comfortable Clean Rooms” My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Philadelphia Embassy Suites. The hotel is very comfortable and welcoming. It is in a great location to visit the museum section of Philly, the Art museum and Franklin Institute. If you want to be in the heart of the historic section with independence hall, you might want to stay closer to that area. We were friendly greeted promptly by the valet and bellman who offered their assistance. Check in was an ease with the reservation in order. The lobby is pleasant and comfortable. We were given a large suite that had a view of the Franklin Institute and Ben Franklin Parkway which was very pleasant. There is a large living room area that was clean and well furnished as well as a large bedroom. The room was updated, clean with nice linens and towels. The bathroom was very nice with marble on the walls in the shower. This is a great place to stay if you have children since there is so much room. The evening reception was a nice way to start the evening with the bartenders being very generous with the free drinks. The only complaint was the complimentary breakfast which was cold and the tables were not being cleaned promptly. There was a lack of care in serving the breakfast. Overall, I would return without a doubt.

“Un lugar especial” El edificio Acqua es ya de por sí espectacular. Las habitaciones tienen aún ese olor a nuevo lo que es muy reconfortante. Si tienes la suerte de tener balcón puedes atreverte con fotos más espectaculares, aunque el viento de Chicago dificulta un poco la labor. El baño es espectacularmente limpio, amplio y bonito. Es un sitio precioso, cómodo, y muy amplio. El staff del hotel encantador, desde los chicos de la puerta hasta el restaurante.

“5 nights of comfort” Just returned from this hotel and i was happy with my stay. Stayed in a room with 2 queen beds. The room was clean and spacious. The decor is slightly dated, with an old TV. However, room had good basic facilities required for a tourist stay. Room included a big desk, coffee machine, iron and board, large wardrobe and comfortable sprung mattress beds. The bathroom was small and the wash basin was outside the main bathroom, but this caused no problem. The hotel is centrally located and close to all the nightlife, business district and tourist attractions. All within easy walking distance. During one evening, a heavy winter storm hit. However, we used the pub, "Elephant and Castle" downstairs on the ground floor which had good pub food and drink offers. Staff were always courteous and efficient. There is also a small coffee shop downstairs if you fancy a pastry and coffee anytime. There are 4 elevators which are quick and readily available. The hotel recently been bought by the sonesta chain and is slowly being modernized. However, for £80 a night, i was happy with this hotel and would stay there again.

“Had high hopes from Trip Advisor Reviews” Arrived at 1pm on Sunday for a 2 night stay. Booked a deluxe king room. Received keys to the room on the 6th floor. Arrived at the room and the keys didn't work. Went back down to the front desk and got new keys. Went back to the room and went in to find we had a room with 2 doubles/fulls as opposed to a king. Also, was a handicap accessible room, so shower wasn't enclosed, closet was very low etc. Called the front desk and they said a king wouldn't be available until 3pm, and we said no problem, as we wanted to go eat lunch anyways. Went back to the front desk and turned in our keys. A different desk agent then said that they had king rooms ready and we could get keys right now. Got the keys and had a king room. Room size was good. A/C worked fine. Decided to shower before heading off to lunch. Heard a knock on the door and not even 5 seconds later a staff member was in our room having used his own key. He was there to restock the mini bar. However, he did not give us a chance to open the door and just came in and we were not fully dressed. When he saw that the previous customer had used the mini bar, he commented that we are lucky that he came by or else it would have been charged to us. Our room, now on the 3rd floor, faced Ontario Street and was very loud at night time as you could hear cars (mostly motorcycles) zipping by. Would request a higher floor room for sure. In room safe, robes, coffee maker, iron etc all good. Made an appointment at the spa (which is not actually affiliated with the hotel, but is on the property). Asked for a treatment that was listed as $155 on the hotel website spa menu. After the treatment, they charged $200 instead of the listed $155. Just felt like they were trying to get over on me. Seemed out of place for a nice hotel/spa. Would not return to The James unless I was assured a high floor room that was ready upon arrival, fully cleaned, mini bar stocked etc. And would not use the spa.

“Needs some updating” I've stayed at the Palmer House Hilton many times. It always seemed like a nice, grand hotel but this grand dame is showing her age. The room I was in was very small and a bit shabby. I understand a lot of rooms at these old, traditional hotels can be small but the room seemed very tired and in need of an update. For exploring the loop, Millinium Park, and the Art Institute, the location is great. The lobby is lovely but I believe I will stay elsewhere next time.
“A true gem !” Very trendy, boutique hotel. Reasonable price. Staff provide great service. The rooms are very chic. Nice location.

“Great value hotel in downtown Denver” Great service at this hotel - staff has gone out of their way to make this stay (and the previous stays) amazing. The hotel is starting to show small signs of wear from a late 90's renovation, including wear on the bed linens. However, value for money at this hotel is high based on the rates I've been able to get by booking directly with the hotel.

“Hotel Fine, Not close to Riverwalk!” Stayed at Crowne Plaza San Antonio Riverwalk for three days, early October, for conference. Check in fast and friendly - bellman/valet took luggage to desk quickly and everyone very friendly. I am a Priority Club member and was "upgraded" to the Executive Level. Had colleague on lower floor who's room was identical, so the only difference in Executive level was waiting on elevator longer. The elevators were horrible for the entire week - this is a fixable issue that seems to have been a topic on previous reviews of property and should be addressed! Room was clean and had usual amenities - tv, couch, desk, chair. No refrigerator or microwave although a refrigerator is available for a one-time $25 charge. Toiletries were Renu - Crowne Plaza branded and pleasant, non-floral scent. Shampoo, conditioner, lotion and bar soap - no shower gel but ok. Towels were soft and fluffy. Not huge but not skimpy. Coffee pot was small, 4 cup and only one pack of caffenated and one pack of de-caf furnished. Easy to bring own coffee and filter and use. Ceramic coffee cups nice touch - no paper coffee cups is good. Bedding was great - total of 6 pillows, counting ones in closet. Mattress a bit too soft for me but ok. Plenty of plugs in room, including plugs in lamps so you don't have to crawl on floor for plug-ins by desk. Our group rate included free internet, which was very slow. I brought my own mi-fi hot spot and it worked fine. Restaturant was good - group 25% discount made prices reasonable. Only one beer - a domestic - on tap - and a bit disappointed that no Mexican beers available, considering location. Perfect segue - location. Cab rides were cheap, thank goodness - this hotel is not close to the "good" part of riverwalk - at least not for someone with mobility issues. Walgreen's about 4 blocks away - don't advise going there alone or after dark. Homeless/jobless hanging out on corners, muttering observations in both Spanish and English. (Have to say they were creative - I'd never thought about doing something like "that"!) Conference rooms were good but long walk to Fiesta Pavilion where we met for most sessions. Housekeeping did a great job in both rooms and conference area restrooms. Check out was fast and accurate. Bill was correct. Bellman held luggage until mid-day departure and had cap to airport waiting for us early. I'd stay here again, if visiting San Antonio. The main complaint I have that is fixable is the elevator.

“Very busy area, buzzy hotel” We didn't have a great start here - they had got the reservation wrong so we had to sort this out via the UK before we arrived, and when we arrived one of our rooms wasn't ready for an hour and a half. They did however credit us $50 for this and I appreciated that. The valet guys are fantastic. The reception staff are charming but stretched (this was the weekend tho so that might explain it). Rooms are comfy if not massive, beds are exceptional. The hotel has a hip, buzzy vibe and the Gaslamp quarter is very busy which was a bit of a shock to us - with two kids and after a long drive, Saturday night in the quarter is a bit of a culture shock. But we found a great sports-bar type place attached to Nicky Rotten's (?) which did us a great family meal. If you're into partying (and probably don't have kids although ours seemed to get used to it pretty quickly!) this hotel would be a blast to stay at.

“Nice Hotel” We were in town for club soccer at Meyers Park. We were about 10min from the field. Easy to get to and from the fields. Grocery store across the highway (HEB) but easy to get to. Along with HEB is a strip center that included a couple of sandwich shops. Right next to the hotel is a McDonalds, pizza place and a Taco Cabana. There is also a Shipley's doughnuts. Breakfast is not free so we ate breakfast tacos at Taco Cabana. The rooms were VERY clean. The front desk was very friendly and helpful. There is wired and and wifi in the room. Son was able to play online game with his ITouch. Would not have any problems staying here again or recommending this hotel. The fitness center had elipticals with TV's attached, treadmills with TV attached, weights and stationary bikes. They were up to date and user friendly. I enjoyed them. One negative, I asked and 800 operator if this hotel had a fridge and microwave and she said yes. That is not the case.

“faultless service with a smile” my wife and I stayed at the SF Omni for 4 nights early august. on arrival, we were a little deflated because we had travelled from one of the uber-casino-hotels in vegas, but (back on planet earth after vegas!) the omni quickly won us over with its always pleasant staff, its cleanliness and (in our opinion and not withstanding other comments) its location. our room was on the 17th floor, with OK views. the room itself was fairly standard, of average size with an acceptable ensuite. the main factor in any room is its cleanliness, and here the omni was perfect: clean bedding, towels and surfaces made us warm to the hotel immediately. check in staff were pleasant and efficient, and full of tips about where to go and how to get there. its only a 7 buck taxi down to the piers, and a quick cable car ride to union square. its also possible to walk back to the hotel from union square because much of the walk is downhill; its an arduous journey the other way! china town is literally on the hotel doorstep; step out, turn right, walk one block and you're there. san francisco is great and a visit to alcatraz a must - although you have to pre-book - don't wait 'til you arrive. we got a town car from the hotel back to the airport - the same price as the taxi on the inward leg but much comfier and a nicer drive. maybe the hotel could send a car to the airport to pick you up - its certainly worth enquiring 'cos some of the SF cab drivers are not the best we've ever met! 10/10 for the omni - it deserves its high standing on trip advisor.

“Si quieres dormir con bichos...” Ibamos a alojarnos 2 noches en este hotel. Las criticas que leimos de él, eran todas practicamente buenas, por eso nos decidimos a reservar en él para nuestra visita a Dallas. Al llegar nos atendieron bien, tuvimos que esperar un poco porque llegamos a las 13:15h y en teoria el check in no se puede hacer hasta las 15h en teoria. La habitacion era una smoking room y nos la peparararon en apenas 15min. Asi que con las mismas, fuimos a la habitacion, dejamos las maletas y nos fuimos a comer al Downtown de Dallas, ya que era el motivo de nuestra estancia alli. Asi que despues de casi 4 horas, y sofocados por el intenso calor de Dallas (casi 50o C) volvimos para darnos un baño en la piscina del hotel. Total que a lo que subimos a la habitacion para darnos una ducha, cambiarnos de ropa y salir a cenar. Pues nada, como apenas habiamos estado en la habitacion, no nos habiamos percatado de que la habitacion estaba llena de bichos (grillos o cucarachas, no se) por toda la habitacion, algunos vivos y otros muertos. Hasta una colilla de un cigarrillo nos encontramos en el suelo. ASQUEROSO!!! Con las mismas, bajamos a la recepcion y les dije que me devolvieran el dinero que yo en ese hotel no me quedaba. Los de recepcion, que eran hindues, se les entendia fatal y me pusieron muchas pegas para devolverme el dinero. Me decian que habia pasado mucho tiempo desde que habiamos hecho el check in, que habiamos tenido suficiente tiempo para checkear la habitacion. Por eso y por todo lo acontecido, no aconsejo el Hotel a nadie, de verdad, ES REPUGNANTE, por los bichos y por el trato recibido. Esperaba mas de un Best Western la verdad.

“Sehr komfortables Hotel” Tolles Hotel, sehr hübsch eingerichtete Zimmer, modern, elegant und sauber, wenn auch nicht sehr geräumig. Guter Schlafkomfort. Die Lage in East Hollywood ist ohne Auto sehr undankbar. Aber mit Gefährt ist man schnell an Orten wie Silver Lake oder Hollywood. Hauseigener Parkplatz gegen Gebühr. Frühstücksbuffet ist toll. Grosse Auswahl, frische und Leckere Sachen. Würde das Hotel weiterempfehlen.
“Close to Little Italy.” Very nice hotel with convenient parking. With in walking distance of Little Italy, the Inner Harbor, and Fells Point. Can not wait to go back with the whole family.

“OMG” When you are visiting, this is the hotel to stay in! It is relatively close to everything, great service in our stay, good food service, and a very comfortable sleep. It has very comfortable rooms, an almost asian type of theme, and I almost didn't leave the hotel at all. Make sure you go to the lobby at night to have fun. Heck, it even has an old PacMan game! This place is awesome!

“Tiny tiny tiny6317453979” Booked it for $USD 415/night on the hotel website with an AAA discount. 2 interior hallways down from the Hynes Convention Centre. Free wifi on 1st and 2nd floors. Free access to onsite huge gym with lots of weight machines and treadmills, and massive pool and cozy hot tub. 7 minute run to Charles River. Lots of eateries in adjacent area (Newbury Street, Prudential Mall, etc.). Grocery store (Shaw's) directly across. Closest T stop (Prudential, Green Line) is within connected mall. Great view from 25th floor. Old, dusty and a bit dingy in decor. Small rooms, especially once crib and fridge placed for our baby. Ridiculously tiny bathrooms. Quick elevators. Uninterested frontdesk staff in response to complaints re: significant delay in arrival of requested crib to room.

“Tolles, Nagelneues Modernes Hotel” Das beste an diesem nagelneuen Hotel ist die Lage. Es befindet sich direkt an der Ecke Canal Street und West Broadway, direkt an der Grenze zu SoHo. Im Umkreis von 5 Minuten kann man zu Fuss zahlreiche super Restaurants erreichen. In weniger als 5 Minuten ist man auf der Shoppingmeile auf dem Broadway. Wir haben ein schoenes Corner Room auf dem SPG Floor im 20. Stock (von 22) mit Blick auf Uptown und das Empire State Building bekommen. Das Hotel ist sehr schoen und modern gestaltet. Die Zimmer sind auch sehr nett und modern. Fuer New York sogar relativ gross. Downside ist, dass bei ein paar Details wirklich geschlampt wurde was das Bild ein bisschen truebt. So haben die Zimmer keine besonders schalldichten Fenster. Andere Hotels in New York sind da schon deutlich weiter. Selbst im 20. Stock hoert man noch das Gehupe sehr deutlich. Ausserdem gibt es im Bad keine einzige Ablageflaeche und die Lueftung (die automatisch mit dem Licht angeht) hoert sich an wie eine Flugzeugturbine. Wirklich schrecklich, da hat man nach 2 Minuten Kopfschmerzen. Das Hotel hat auch ein Restaurant das ich allerdings nicht empfehlen kann. Voellig ueberteuert, die Qualitaet des Essens hat nicht ueberzeugt. Da gibt es im umkreis von wenigen Minuten viel besseres.

“Location, location, location...” This hotel is situated perfectly for anyone, but particularly first time visitors. A short walk to Fanueil Hall/Quincy Market and the North End but also close to T stops to get around the city. The staff is quite helpful and the rooms are kept up.

“Mediocre, won't stay again...” positives first.... location is awesome! right in the heart of times square. nice views, rooms are of a good size considering the location. appealing lobby and friendly front desk. negatives... the bathroom had a displeasing odor as if it had not been cleaned well (smelled of urine)--the bathroom was pretty large but everything but the shower looked outdated, as in there were rusting around the metal pieces. the tv cable connection was not consistent considering its a supposed 4 star hotel, i was disappointed and not impressed. it didn't impress me more than just an average 3.5 hotel such as ramada, holiday inn.etc... also loud noises in the morning (sounded like construction, but there was no construction in sight mind you our room was on the 40th floor) last negative, there is a random charge on my bank account, no idea what its for--since checkout went smooth can't complain too much bc we paid a lower rate from hotwire, so i wouldn't be surprised if we were given one of the not so great rooms. if i had to pay the regular full rate that's stated on the website i would of given it 2 stars. i'd recommend hudson hotel or on the avenue hotel instead for those looking to book in manhattan =)

“Quite happy with this hotel” We were quite happy with this hotel. It has a great location and we did get a really good price using Hotwire. Decent room with a comfortable king size bed. Also, even though we were right on the corner of North Point St and Jones St in the Beach St building, we were not at all troubled by any outside noise. Our only gripes were the TV was a little old and needed replacing, albeit there are dozens of channels to choose from. Also, the management are a bit stingy getting you to pay extra for a fridge. Oh, one tip: we suggest you call before you arrive to find out which building you will be staying in. Believe us, it will make it a lot easier than doing what we did, and get the airport shuttle to drop you at the wrong building. Both buildings have a lobby and reception desk. We read elsewhere that the Dennys Restaurant off the Beach St building lobby was not real good. We had one dinner there and found it quite OK, together with friendly staff. Other than the couple of minor gripse, everything else was just fine.
“Nice place to stay” Pretty nice, paid $80 on priceline. Food was not very good in the restaurant or the bar. Rooms clean and nice place to stay.

“Preferred Choice near IAH” Stayed here for one night recently - first time at a Hyatt Place. Conveniently located near Houston Intercontinental and also I-45. Nice rooms with a unique ambience. Excellent service and nice breakfast. Could not find the closet at first -- it is behind the full length mirror near the sink! Well designed with a wide screen TV. Did not use the shuttle service. Will return.

“hôtel magnifique ! A ne pas manquer !” Pour une première visite à San Francisco, j'ai décidé de réserver cet hôtel car il est dans le centre, tout neuf et possède un beau centre de remise en forme. Ma chambre se trouvait au 30ème étage avec vue sur la baie de San Francisco. La chambre était en parfait état, bien entretenue, confortable. La salle de bain sans baignoire mais avec une grand douche vitrée idéale si vous êtes deux. L'hôtel est magnifiquement décoré et le personnel est très disponible. La piscine et le centre de remise en forme est très utile après une bonne journée de visite dans San Francisco. Si vous aimez le moderne et le confort n'hésitez pas !

“Fantastic Resort - You Won't Be Disappointed” Fantastic Resort - everything you need is right there. They offer five different restaurants, pool and spa. My friend and I had a girls' weekend and enjoyed every bit of it. We got an awesome deal for SPA treatments (facials) and spent part of the day at the SPA's pool, which was very relaxing and a great way to cool off in 103 degree heat. I would recommend eating at Roy's and getting the price fixe dinner - it was awesome! Also, I would recommend upgrading to the Cloud Club. The concierges' are wonderful and you get a cooked to order breakfast. It was well worth it especially if you're a Marriot Rewards Member. Although the valet parking is a bit expensive, it's worth it in the summertime! Enjoy!

“Central Downtown location” This is an older property but the location in central LA is perfect for activities in the area. Overall neighborhood is on the edge of the rough sections, but the access to metro, downtown businesses and the mall located in the complex make this an acceptable location to stay. The staff is extremely nice and helpful, and the rooms are clean and beds comfy. Would stay there again.

“Lobby was loud/noisy, but our corner room on 25th floor was great” We spent three nights at the Marriott Marquis over the weekend. We arrived at 11:30 pm to a busy lobby, still loud from the bar action adjacent to the check-in area. The folks in front of us seemed to have to wait a long time and did not seem happy, but our check-in was quick and efficient. We had asked for a rollaway and it was in our corner room. There was tons of space, great views and even though we were literally around the corner from the elevator, it was relatively quiet (unless some folks got off the elevator and were loud--which happened a few times. Location was great. Near the Apple Store and lots of shops. We walked all over Union Square, up to Nob Hill, Chinatown and the Ferry Bldg. If you want a quick, informal meal, grab something from Bristol Farms in the basement of the nearby Westfield Center. I found that the lobby was always a hotbed of sometimes chaotic, loud activity--and the decor was a bit dated, but the staff were very gracious and we loved our room. We'll be back.

“Really Nice Stay” I stayed at this hotel for a week 2/19-2/26 and really loved the place. Staff was wonderful and could not have done enough for our family. Everyone always asked if they could do anything for us and if we were enjoying our stay. Hotel was clean and very appealing and the hotel was obviously remodeled very recently. No funky odors or rude staff to report here. Parking will set you back 22 for valet, and 16 for self park. I would definitely stay at this hotel in the future with out any hesitation. Nice area and hotel is very close to I-5.

“Very good hotel with some staff problems” Although the hotel opened after renovation in 2004, I was still able to get a pre-opening rate (186 USD) for a king executive room for May 2005 on Doubletree's website including lounge access - at least so it said on my reservation confirmation. Upon arrival, I was asked by an rather arrogant front desk staff member if would like the twin bed room I reserved (?). Furthermore, she denied lounge access stating, that the lounge is for Hilton HHonors status members only. She got the manager for me, who said the same thing. Showing him my confirmation print-out which clearly stated "lounge access", he oh so generously gave me continental breakfast coupons for the Met Grill, but only for five out of seven days, stating that the lounge is closed on weekends (in fact, for those weekend days guests with lounge access get breakfast coupons, too), repeatedly saying "I don't have to do this". THANK YOU VERY MUCH! After that unpleasent incident, a bellman showed me my king room on 14th floor (I wonder if that really was an executive room as the exec floors are according to my confirmation floors 16-19, but front desk said so at check-in) facing 51st Street with its police and fire station which was NYC standard size and well appointed with flat screen TV (although NY1 and Weather channels missing) and the best bed I ever slept in at an U. S. hotel, Doubletree's new Sweet Dreams bed, with lots of cushions and downs. Bathroom featured Neutrogena toiletries and lots of hot water. Room attendants did a great job: room was very, very clean, they replaced the many towels every day. Bed linens were changed on a daily basis, too. Don't believe that the new windows are sound proof (as mentioned on some websites) - they are merely sound-resistant, but nevertheless keep enough noise out to have a good night's sleep. The biggest noise problem (as many reviewers mentioned before) comes from the inside: the very thin doors with a huge gap between door and frame which let a lot of sound and light through and which you can't close without a major "bang". IMHO, it should not be a problem giving those doors some rubber isolation. The in-room safe deposit box was a nice touch. Two features I at first wondered what all the fuzz was about were very good: the really delicious warm signature cookie you get upon arrival and the arched shower bar, which prevents the shower curtain from sticking to your wet body. I was not so impressed with the hairdryer, whichs cord was only about 6 inches long (prepare for unusual hairdos using the hairdryer head-down). Breakfast buffet in the bunker-like Met Grill with its stained chairs was a laugh riot considering - not holding coupons - you have to pay 20 USD for continental and 26 USD for an pathetic American breakfast. Luckily, there are enough diners and other hotels you can have breakfast at in the proximity of the hotel. Unlike guests rooms around me, mine never got a morning newspaper, although I am Hilton HHonors member (apparently they think foreigners can't read English, anyway). Check-out was a breeze, but only because I had some phone fees for 1-800 calls removed from my account beforehand (front desk said, they were still having problems with the phone system - Hello? The hotel is open more than half a year and is surely not the first to run this system!) Location of the hotel is great: several subway lines and downtown buslines right outside the door, crosstown und uptown bus lines only one or two blocks away. To sum this stay up: if you get a good rate, absolutely stay there! If only they improved the doors and management/front desk attitude, the hotel would be perfect.

“Convenient airport hotel, great rooms, clean and quiet” We had a horrendous journey, getting to the hotel at close to 7pm because of all of the traffic disruption in Boston. Check in was fine and the hotel is very well placed for car rental returns (Avis is the closest) and the shuttle picked me up from Alamo. Room was really comfortable, shame we were only there until 6.30 am the next morning for our flight out to the UK. Comfy doubles in one room and a sitting area with a sofa bed. Kitchenette (no cutlery though) and walk through bathroom. If downtown is accessible, then I guess this is an option for a Boston city stay, but it struck me that this is reallly meant to be an airport hotel. There's not much else in the immediate vicinity.

“A Very Nice Hotel and Staff” My husband and I recently stayed at this hotel while he was having an outpatient operation at the Texas Medical Center. The hotel is very clean and the staff seems very anxious for their guests to be happy. Our room was a king suite. The room was spacious, clean and very comfortable. The hotel is also very quiet and has free parking. The hotel is immediately adjacent to a Luby's cafeteria. There is also a Krogers about a half mile from the facility. It takes about 5 minutes or less to drive to the Medical Center. The hotel also has a shuttle that will take you to the center. The breakfast was the typical Hampton Inn breakfast. It was very well stocked and replenished immediately. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“A wonderful stay!” I loved the Hotel Allegro! This has been my favorite place to stay so far in Chicago. The somewhat retro decor is fun, the employees are very friendly and helpful, and the location is also great. I checked in early and as a result took a handicapped room, which did not have a standard armoir and had a HUGE bathroom, but otherwise the room was very comfortable. Soft bed, plasma TV (!), FREE wi-fi (!!), and FREE wine bar in the evenings (!!!). You may want to try to get a room on a high floor (maybe 10+?) because the El train runs right past the back side of the hotel. I was on the 16th floor and barely heard anything. Also of note: unlike many hotels housed in older buildings that I've stayed in, the elevators at the Allegro are modern and FAST. Very nice when you're high up in the building! I am a big fan of Kimpton's "green" practices, and this is the first chance I've had to experience them. I liked being able to continue my habits of recycling and such while traveling. Also, unlike other hotels I've stayed in, Kimpton actually DOES let you reuse your towel instead of just saying they have a program and still replacing your towels anyway.

“おかゆ 飲茶 中華料理三昧” ニューヨークのソーホーに程近い、このホテルはミッドタウンのホテルとは別と考えて、 中華を食べまくる、という決意のもと、早起きして、出来立てのおかゆを2ドルくらいで食べ、 昼には飲茶を堪能し、夕食はたくさんのお惣菜屋やレストランからテイクアウトしたものを 部屋いっぱいに広げて、幸せな気分を味わった。 毎日住んでいたらどんなにいいだろう。 野菜は新鮮、パンは日本の味に近くて安い、 中華料理は文句なしで、高いチップを払ってレストランに行く気がしなくなった。 ホテルは中流、サービスは良し、ディープな中華街を味わうのにお勧めのホテルです。

“We shall return” We spent three nights here, largely on Tripadvisor's recommendation, and we were quite impressed. Our room was the least expensive--no suite, no kitchen--but it was a fine size for us. Bathroom small but comfortable enough; loved the shower. Also loved the buckwheat pillows on the pillow menu. Even though we were only on the 4th floor, the street noise was minimal. And the staff--everyone was so helpful and welcoming! The doormen were great, the maids smiled, and the desk staff were efficient and pleasant. All in all, we'll be back...soon!

“Only for lone travellers intending to spend minimal time in hotel” My husband and I stayed 3 nights in this hotel in August. Overall, I was satisfied, but my husband not. Here are a few points: - Great location: 1 minute walk from Columbus Circle metro station, serving a few metro train lines, including Line A which will take you directly to JFK airport. Also, it is very close to Central Park, and about 20 minutes walk to Broadway theatre district. It is close to restaurants and cafes, and a shopping mall (where you can find the Whole Foods grocery shop). - Peculiar decor. The lobby and the rooms are decorated stylishly, that is, if you like this kind of modern decoration. The main complaint we had was that it was too dark everywhere: in the lobby, in the restaurants, and in the rooms. - Hardwood floor and nice wood paneling in our room, which I really liked. - Room is very small -- many other reviewers have already commented on this. - Bathroom is very small -- I don't particularly mind a small bathroom without a tub (shower only), but there does not seem to be enough room in front of the toilet, making it very cramped. (I am a small person, so I could still fit into the space, but I imagine it would be really difficult for a big or even an average person.) Also, not enough room around the sink to place the basic things (like cups and toothpaste). - No free Internet. One has to pay US$10 per day for wireless Internet access. No wired Internet. - The restaurant in the hotel is expensive, and the food is not good. Avoid the crab cakes. They are so salty I had to drink a lot of water to wash them down! (As I was hungry, otherwise I would not have touched them). I would say try restaurant outside the hotel. It is very close to the Hell's Kitchen district with lots of restaurants to fit every taste. - The AC in the room is very noisy, so we had to turn it off to go to sleep. - Lots of noise from the busy streets below (we were on the sixth floor). - Our room was very far away from the elevator. I never thought this could be a problem until we actually walked for probably 2 minutes (3 long corridors and two turns) to get from the elevator to our room. If you have lots of luggage or small children, this could be a problem. In short, if you are a lone traveler intending to spend minimal time in the hotel, this could be ideal. Otherwise, you need to consider the pros and cons.

“Great place to stay” I know that I have previously had written bad reviews in this site about other Sheraton Hotels, especially the one in Denver-Colorado but I think it is important for us, travellers, to write true views of the places that we stay or dine, so I have to tell you about this hotel. what a difference, this is a modern, clean, well presented hotel with excellent facilities, good bar and restaurant but overall good size rooms in a very well presented conditions. Great place to stay in Phoenix, yes, a bit expensive but a real 5 start hotel.

“Rooms have an odd layout” The hotel is nicely appointed but I did not find the rooms to be functional at all. The room was small, the closet so small I couldn't fit my carry-on suitcase in it and pants could not hang straight down without hitting the safe. Besides the desk, there are really no places to put anything since the nightstands are so small and with the lamp on each one leaves no room for anything else. No dresser - the only drawers were in the tiny nightstand. There was no space in the bathroom for toiletries. Somehow I got a handicapped bathroom, so it was huge but had no space at the same time. I do have to say that the water in the shower/tub was really hot. The menu in the restaurant didn't look all that great to me and was slightly overpriced. There is a wine reception from 4:30-5:30 each day and the bar/lounge area was nice for a drink. The location is great - right in the middle of Michigan Avenue. This is my new corporate hotel, so we'll see if I got a flukey random room this time and will get a better room next time. I'll be visiting the Allerton often in the future.

“Best Hotel in El Paso” While I stay at all types of hotels, I am typically a fan of Marriotts because they tend to have a strong service and good food. The El Paso Marriott has all of these things and more. The hotel is a a short cab ride or free shuttle bus away from the airport hotel and well worth the trip. The lobby is pleasant and a good place to meet colleagues before going out to dinner, etc. They also have a small business center with a fax, a computer with internet and such right behind the lobby and all of these things are COMPLEMENTARY. The restaurant and bar are very pleasant as is the gym and pool area. The concierge lounge is also nice for a quick snack or drink if you have a bit of time or just want to relax. Best in El Paso, highly recommend.

“Double Tree Austin Hotel” The rates at this hotel are somehow high for its location and quality. There is no free Internet in the rooms and guests must pay for parking when there is plenty of space around. The hotel is also far from downtown in an unremarkable neighborhood.

“Assets and liabilities” My husband and I purchased an auction package that included the Driscoll hotel so we came taking our chances. This is a boutique hotel with some limitations. The building itself is older so no air conditioning, no on-sight resturant or bar, and no outdoor seating or patio. The most difficult was finding on-street parking and when located it was on a steep hill! But the assets Far outweigh any difficulty. This is a place where the service is consistent and sure to spoil you for anywhere else. In advance of our visit we asked for resturant recommendations and Marty arranged for some of the best dining experiences ever. We highly recommend this if you don't already have your favorites. The continental breakfast is superb. For a cold breakfast the offerings are so bountiful you don't miss anything hot. You eat in elegant room with fresh flowers throughout the room and several choices of national and international newspapers to choose from. Added fun were bottles of water in the room personalized for the hotel with picture of the Driscoll on the inside. Our grandchildren loved them! If you want to be pampered, this is the place to go.

“Good for Europeans, not good for Americans LOUSY BREAKFAST” It is on a street with all the sexy smut shops. Lingerie stores, peep shows, Adult videos, etc... If you have children or family members you want to shelter, this is not the street. It is close to the Empire State Building, 5th Avenue shopping, and Times Square. We stayed in a nice QUIET room #2009 The view was lousy, but the quietness made up for it. The rooms are small, as with most New York Properties. The breakfast was HORRID and cheap. They claim it is till 10 or 10:30 on the weekends, however when stuff runs out its gone. So if you come around 9:30 your left with some white toast, cereal and cold cuts. Americans don't eat Ham sandwiches for breakfast! There is no cut fruit. Just some bananas and orange slices. We did a name your own price for $295 a night and got assigned here. Elevators fast. Beds clean, large, and comfortable. Computer room was wonderful. Hard to get a taxi on the street, but not impossible. When coming to New York City remember to book everything in advance. If you are a night owl forget it... The Statue of Liberty closes early, the Empire closes early even if their website mentions otherwise. The 911 Memorial, the museums, everything... Plan your schedule and have your event tickets and everything planned. We missed out on stuff because we rolled into town for a marathon and showed up later in the day. The restaurant food was good. The water is very expensive and the tap water is horrid. Stop by the market and get your water stashes. There is some 24 hour delivery restaurant and their food is crummy. It has the orange menu. Make sure to take in a Broadway show, they are fabulous.

“Good hotel, some problems” Stayed here for 3 nights in November 2007. Location is excellent, downtown with a short walk to Horton Plaza and the Gaslamp Quarter. Because it is right next to the Greyhound station it does attract some homeless people, but we were never bothered once. San Diego is certainly not alone in having homeless people, and this is hardly the fault of the hotel. The room was very nice, albeit very small as other people have commented, though it's certainly not the smallest room i've ever stayed in. The room is tastefully decorated, the bed is very comfortable (didn't like the small pillows however), good selection of cable channels. The bathroom is very small, the sink is directly to the left as you walk in, and the shower has no screen so water tends to go all over the place, but that's what housekeeping is for. While the room itself was very nice, the hotel suffers from paper thin walls. We had loud drunken people in the next room to us who laughed and talked very loudly until very late (they finally quietened down by 2-3am). We could even hear when our neighbours turned their lights on and off. The other 2 nights we were fortunate to not have noisy people next door, but it really is just pot luck who you get. We are returning to San Diego in May and will be choosing another hotel to stay in due to the noise issue. The room was great, location great, very good value for money, but we value our sleep too much. There's nothing worse than being tired all day on vacation because of your noisy neighbours.

“Perfect Location - Perfect Stay” My wife and I stayed here from August 15th-18th, 2012 in connection with a convention at McCormick Place. We had our car and parking was a bit confusing as we pulled down into the parking garage and began looking for a spot - only to be told that due to renovations, only valet-parking was available at $55 a night. However, the attendant pointed us out of the garage and into an adjacent parking facility that was only $30 a night. However, other than that little glitch, our stay was perfect. I usually stay at Embassy Suites and Marriott properties but I did join Starwood's frequent guest program so I could earn points on this stay. We were upgraded to the next level room at no-charge as a result of the membership so I highly recommend it. In addition, the card also got us 20% off the on-premises Shula's restaurant. Speaking of the latter, it's as pricey as many Chicago steakhouses - my 12 ounce filet was $48 and my wife's salmon was around $34. As is typical, salads and starches were not included. If you feel like splurging a bit and staying in the hotel - this is a very good dining option - our meals were outstanding. We had breakfast each morning at a restaurant on the lower floor. Individual meal options were $14-$16 and they have a daily breakfast buffet for $24.95. The buffet was good but I'd like to see more a la carte individual options - I'm not an egg eater and pancakes or french toast were not options on the menu. We had a few cocktails one evening in the lobby bar - a relatively quiet but large space. The other cocktailing option at the hotel is a nice-size bar inside the aforementioned Shulas. Those looking for more hip-happening places or sports bars will need to walk a block or two - PJ Clarks has an outpost a block away just inside the Embassy Suites hotel lower level. The health club features state-of-the-art cardio and strength-training equipment as well as separate saunas in the bathrooms. A nice size indoor pool adjoins the health club as does an outdoor sun deck with lounge chairs that is great for afternoon tanning... until the Trump Tower blocks the sun to the west - about two hours before sunset during our stay. The location is perfect - a short walk to Navy Pier and a reasonable walk to just about everything business travelers and vacationers alike could desire.

“Sweetest little Hotel! Very unique experience!” We stayed here as a group attending a friend's wedding. I fell in love with this cute little hotel. It is a truly unique experience. It helped that everyone at the hotel was there for the wedding, but I certainly fell in loooove with this facility. Very cute old fashioned hotel. We had a nice little balcony that we could use. The common area was fantastic. The customer service was awesome too. Over all a great experience.

“This Place Rocks” I've stayed at the Hotel Montgomery twice and both experiences were excellent. The second time I had a suite - I highly recommend the suite if you are there for business. Very spacious, lots of room to spread out and work and also quite appropriate for meeting with business contacts. The Paragon Restaurant is excellent - good food and excellent wine. I was surprised to find such good food in San Jose (okay, I'm a big city snob). This is the only place I would stay in San Jose.

“Great for Business Travel” Perfect for Business Travel. I am in this area for work often, and I've tried the Four Points down the street - the DoubleTree is WAY BETTER. It is NYC, so the room isn't huge. But, they have a breakfast buffet (THIS IS KEY), a decent gym (no view), and they give you warm cookies upon check in (yummy). The staff is very friendly. They do have good room service too. Even in a two double bed room, it woud be a tight squeeze for any more than two people.

“Good service, great location, good prices, but a lot of negatives..” Along with the Chicago Sofitel, the Los Angeles location is a good enough, reliable property. The service is consistently professional, the rooms were adequate, and the gym is phenomenal (one of the best I've seen at any hotel). But the hotel is letting down it's guard, and there were several notable problems: 1. The restaurant was painfully slow, and the product which I remember being exceptional, has fallen dramatically (think dried out sausage, and practically cold has browns.. and 20 minute waits for coffee in rush periods). Our server was delightfully and painfully apologetic, but even with a huge staff, this restaurant does not seem to be well managed. (And what's with the broken sign on the front of the building? A 5 star hotel usually fixes such visible items quickly!) 2. Crappy internet. Like all Sofitels, you need to pay for the fast internet, and expect slowwww internet if you want it "free". However, even when I paid for the fast internet, it was intermittent, unreliable, and problematic. 3. Priceline. Since Sofitel is one of the few higher end hotels in the area that accepts Priceline, you can see it in the caliber of guests as well as the front desk's service of said guests. You will always diminish your brand when you give it away to some people inexpensively. 4. The swimming pool is *awful*. Tiny, weirdly shaped, and constantly packed - you practically can't assume that you'll be able to use the pool to any level of satisfaction. Especially compared to other properties such as the Roosevelt, the pool here is very disappointing. Admittedly, as a Priceline guest (I know, I know), I got what I paid for here, as the rate was cheaper than comparable properties. But paying the price I would have to pay on the Internet, I wouldn't choose to stay here again. There are a lot better options nearby.

“Overall - excellent.” The hotel is well located in midtown Manhattan and easy to find from Grand Central Station or the airport bus drop off point. It was our honeymoon and the hotel offered us an upgrade and a bottle of sparkling wine; a congratulations note was also left in our room. The room was nicely furnished, though on the small side. I suspect though this is the norm for New York. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. Cheese and wine is included from 1700-2000 each evening. The only bad points are that the wireless internet connection is poor (I appreciate that our room was on the 11th floor but that shouldn't be a problem). Also, although breakfast is included, the self service area is very small and we often had to wait before we were able choose what we wanted. The room they use for breakfast only has around 10 tables and it is sometimes necessary to sit with others. I would question that for a hotel with 60 rooms, 10 tables is not sufficient. Overall though, we enjoyed our stay and would recommend.

“In the heart of the financial district” Everytime we come to NYC we like to stay in a different area...this time Wall Street. Club Quarters is good value for money. Our room is spacious and generally it's pretty quiet. Bathroom is on the small side, however it's a good base to sightsee from. Staff are friendly and helpful.

“Memorial Day Weekend - FUN” I love the Marriott Autograph Collection ~ Boutique Hotels and this one did not disappointment. This was my first trip to Houston and I could not wait enjoy all the city has to offer, Initially, I checked in and was offered a beautiful room that face an abandon building. I called downstairs and asked for another room and was told that there was another room available but on the same side and the view should be the same. I was never give the option to check it out. I went downstairs and requested information to another Marriott in the area. Well, that request got the General Managers attention who was standing within an earshot of the conversation and I was moved to larger corner gorgeous suite and offered champaign. At that point my stay flawless... The fitness center had everything you would need for a great workout. The Standing O restaurant and bar in the lobby was fun and cheerful. The valet and waitstaff were attentive and always smiling. Nice robes and bath amenities. The drapes and furniture were regal and the location gave you great access to the historical, municipal, theater districts. I had a car but did not drive around the city. I walked to shopping area and took the hotel shuttle when I was dressed for dinner and it picked me up. I did drive to other areas such as the Galleria and Stadium. It was the valet that informed me this hotel was frachised to Micheal "MAGIC" Johnson. I would definitely return. At the end of my stay the GM sent a letter thanking me for choosing the ICON while in Houston. I will definitely be back!

“Beware of the Bed Size” The Marcel Gramercy is pretty much everything you would expect a contemporary "funky boutique" hotel in New York City to be. The rooms are small, the furnishing are more sleek than practical, and the staff is more interested in being interesting than helpful. These things aside, the hotel is clean, the rooms are priced well, and there is a spectacular open-air terrace with free internet access and an amazing view of the Empire State Building. The only real issue with this property are the bed sizes. It is worth noting that the "Standard" bed-size for the Marcel (their cheapest room/size) is actually about the size of a double bed. In fact, by length it's actually shorter than a double bed. The bed is quite comfortable, but sleeping 2 people is a real challenge. It is also worth noting that I got this room through Priceline, so be aware of that if booking a room for two people in the Gramercy Park area. Other than that, it was an average stay.

“Pretty good hotel” Pretty amazing place with amazing staff here and nice rooms but the only thing is that whenever i stay with my family at least one person gets sick in my family for the last 4 years weve been coming and staying here either every summer or christmas and someones always gotten sick i do not know why but maybe its something thats in this hotel or something i dont know but heads up to people watch out just in case u get sick!!!!!

“Pretty good Crowne Plaza” Stayed here this month and a few times in the past. Overall it's a pretty good crowne plaza especially for the price. The hotel furnishings are a bit dated but the room is always very clean. Seems to be a very limited staff but great service. Very timely and always polite. I do love the free parking and the free internet. Will stay here again in the near future.

“Great Hotel” I stayed at the Sheraton Mission Valley Hotel in San Diego for a recreational getaway. I checked in a few hours early with no problem. The front desk was very courteous and even gave me an upgrade to a suite (elite level with Starwood program) which was just a room on the top floor with high ceilings and a balcony as well as access to the club lounge. The only thing that wasn't perfect with the hotel was that there was a suitcase in my room when I got to the room. Called the front desk and they apologized and picked it up. I looked around and everything else was perfect. It's amazing that the maid just missed it though. Other than that, the entire room, bathroom and everything was clean. Breakfast in the club lounge was just ok. I've had a lot better at other Sheraton lounges. It was just very basic continental food. I didn't use the pool or the gym but I went outside to look at the pool and it looked clean. I checked out at 1:30. Check out was fast and the front desk was very nice again. I recommend this hotel and I will definitely stay here next time I am in San Diego.

“Delectable” Recently stayed at the Ritz for two nights on a business trip. From the moment you check in to the moment you leave, you can feel the power of the aura created by staying here. The service is excellent, the staff obliging, and the furnishings and appointments are comfortable and elegant. You are well cared for here, and if you have the money, it's a worthwhile experience.
“Prime Location” This is a newer hotel and was very nice. It is in the heart of most shopping for Austin Domain area. We will be back.

“Conference Hotel... Big!” Was there on business for a few nights and needed a centrally located place. I usually stay at the Intercontinental but decided to give this a try (as it was more central). It is a big hotel... rooms are neat and clean but the food is very very poor - I could not believe it when they messed up porridge!! Probably going to head back to the Intercon the next time around.

“Perfect place to stay for families!!!!!” We love staying at Embassy Suites whenever we travel for multiple reasons, namely the seperate room and living room. Kids in one, adults in the other! Two TVs so there is no fighting! Comes with a mini fridge and a microwave which is also perfect to bring snacks to the room and save cash as opposed to eating out all the time. The breakfast is good, not as great as others we have been to, mostly because during the week they do not place all of the warm food out for self service and you have to wait in the omelet line to get it. Not too much of a hassle, unless you show up late when everyone else is trying to eat. The managers drink reception is awesome too, 530PM-730Pm and some days it really saves the day when the kids are on you rlast nerve. Pool is a tad small but still enjoyable, not a chlorine pool and the water burns the eyes quite a bit. Service was great, always greeted with smile even the GMs wife was on hand to help out and say hello one evening. Worst part is trying to check out and get your luggage down the elevator. Only 3 elevators and usually crowded around 10AM-11AM for checkout. Might be a good idea to take some things downstairs earlier, or even the evening before to save yourself the hassle. If you have kids, stay here!!!!

“hip, comfy hotel” This hotel has a lot of funky style, our room was huge and had tons of little extras (magazines, free bottled water, great shampoo, two floor to ceiling windows.) It was a very comfortable, clean, friendly stay. The only downside is there's nothing to walk to, it's far from everything, and parking is expensive. If you're looking for someplace near the airport, this place is great, if you're a tourist going downtown, it's too far.

“Disappointing with some upside” Quick background - I stay in about 6-10 hotels a year and I try to be completely fair with all of them. I also in pretty patient compared to most. When we arrived the check in was fine, handed a couple of waters nice touch so we head up to a room that wasn't made up. No big deal, we called and told them and after we came back it was fine. The beds are pretty old and lumpy for such a nice looking hotel on the outside. So two negatives so far, one positive is that even though the place was completely full we found the hotel to be quiet, no thin walls. So next morning my wife said the hair dryer didn't work, she didn't even want me to call but I politely told them and then came right up to fix it as we were heading out. Another positive. A big negative was that we left around 10am and pulled the "do not disturb" sign off at that time, when we came back that evening the room had not been made up and the note said at 5pm the sign was still on the door even though it hadn't been on there all day. When I called down they said that they were really busy and that they couldn't get to every room that day. I asked for a couple of towels and was able to get those. Check out was fine and I can't speak for the breakfast as it didn't work into our plans. The other incident that wasn't an incident for us is that three cop cars were outside one evening when we got back but I don't know what they were doing there so I call that neither a positive nor a negative but it's usually a negative. It's in an odd place on a one way part of the highway so it is a little tough to get to but not a huge deal. Overall, I would have to rate it lower than I normally do and again I'm pretty tolerant of things. The last item is that it is overpriced for an HI Express.

“Great Location - nice room” Very satisfied with our room and with this hotel -once we got settled. Would have given them the highest score except for the fact that the front desk staff on duty was not very helpful. One front desk staff member was unfamiliar with local attractions and gave us misinformation (and didn't bother to confirm with his colleagues. Fortunately, we did get the correct information from the bellman before we set out.) The location was perfect - you can walk through the "habitrail tunnels" to get to shopping and movies without having to go outside in the cold. The fitness center was terrific. No waiting for treadmills! We will definitely stay here again.

“Nice but overpriced” Boston is a pricy town, but $1382.06 for Thur, Fri & Sat seems a bit steep for two double beds including $46 per night valet parking. The Hotel is in a great location, staff is friendly and cordial, atmosphere relaxed, housekeeping superb. For the price, the rooms should have been much better. Beds were too small if you are accustomed to a King or Queen. Room décor was comparable to a hotel at half the price. The central air worked great and was not to loud. The walls are thin, and neighbors can be annoying if music or TV is played above low volume. At least you get a small refrigerator with a large Shaw’s grocery store across the street where you can purchase organic fruit for the room.
