“Best bargain room in The City” The rate is almost always less than $100 for a spacious room and good bed ($75 the other night). You can park for free. Everything works. The hosts (who, sadly, are planning to move to Utah) are friendly, helpful, and efficient. What's not to like? I've stayed there twice and it is going to be my regular hotel when I need a room overnight in San Francisco. You will get a good, quite night's sleep and a good bath or shower in the morning. That said, if I was going to San Francisco on a once- or twice-in-a-lifetime vacation, I'd spend the money to stay somewhere nicer, probably near Union Square, with a room big enough to enjoy hanging out in. Yes, you can walk up to the Hyde St. car, but that's not the same as being able to walk to all the stores and to the main Muni (local bus/streetcar) and BART (regional subway) routes. Fact is, the Nob Hill is near a useful, workaday section of Polk St. that is likely to have little charm for a visitor. A perfectly respectable neighborhood, and you can walk over the hill to Chinatown and North Beach, or down to the Wharf, but not what people think of when they think of San Francisco. P.S. The motel is *not* actually on Nob Hill, which is just as well, as there is no way they could offer free parking if it was.
“Love the fairmount chain” Refreshing. Excellent executive lounge and again a superb gym. Love their presidents club where they provide sporting kit. Wonderful touch.

“Hate the bedspread!” First time in a Homewood Suites and this is a personal thing, but I travel a lot and am a little spoiled. The deal breaker for me in any hotel is a bedspread instead of a duvet. We all know that those bedspreads get cleaned twice a year and probably harbor more bacteria than a public toilet. So if I am stuck with one far away from any alternative lodging, I'll shove it in a corner and ask for a clean blanket and extra sheet to 3-sheet the bed. In this case, there was lots of alternative lodging nearby. The hotel appeared clean and pretty well maintained. It wasn't until after we left the next morning that my husband gave me the bad news: a big cockroach on the bathroom floor....and the good news: it was already dead. But really, it did look clean and it might have been a one time occurance. I'd give them the benefit of the doubt, but would suggest that management get in touch with their pest control contractor. The decor was bland, non-descript and very thrifty looking. The sofa in the room was not the least bit soft, comfortable or inviting. The guilty bedspread was actually a big comforter that would not have shown soil if someone dropped an entire dinner on it. The rooms were very small but separated by a pocket door. The kitchen/living/dining area was all one. The tub and toilet were enclosed in the bathroom, with the sink outside of it. One very nice feature was the curved bar for the shower curtain, something so inexpensive that all hotels should have them by now. The breakfast was very good - a generous buffet that included waffles in the shape of Texas - and served by the nicest ladies! The reception staff was terrific as well. They could not have been kinder. The location is in a green area near a highway, about a half mile walk to any restaurants, etc. They serve a free dinner at the hotel Monday thru Thursday, but we weren't there on one of those nights. Satisfaction with anything, including hotels, is based upon one's expectations. And since everyone's expectations are different, you can (and often do) have some people ranting and some raving about the very same hotel. My heaven might be your hell or vice versa. This place came up short for me. But unless a kitchen is mandatory, in this price range I think a Hilton Garden Inn or Marriott Courtyard is a much better choice.

“Nice Location, Clean Rooms, Residence Inn Standard Offering” The location was easy to find and the hotel is in a commercial area between 6th street entertainment and the convention center and a 5 minute walk to all the action in the warehouse district as well. You have the choice of valet or self-parking. Self-parking is in a connected garage with easy elevator access. ($21 self with in and out) There is a nicely decorated inviting lobby with front desk and nicely appointed common area. Across the elevator bank is the Courtyard by Marriott which shares a common building. There is free Wi-Fi available in the lobby area and rooms. The hotel has a large, nicely appointed gym. There is small indoor pool, but unfortunately no significant outside deck space. They have an acceptable business center with two computers near the front desk. Check in was quick and efficient, and they accommodated our request for a quiet room (away from the 6th street noise) and put us in a room facing 4th street on a high floor. Though we were there for the nightlife of Austin, it was nice to be away from the hectic side of "dirty 6th" and we were really appreciative of the hotels strong stance on no noise. They have prominent signs stating no parties are allowed, and that only registered guests are allowed at the hotel. When we came back to the hotel Friday evening, they had security at the door to ensure that only guests were allowed in. This is a nice touch. There was some kind of ruckus in the room across from us with someone apparently smoking pot. Police were called and things quieted down. I don’t know the outcome. (They kept telling the security staff "dude I have a medical marijuana license" ---> that does not work in Texas, and why the heck would they stay at a non smoking hotel! Goofballs.) The rooms are nicely decorated, but seem smaller than the rooms at the adjoining Courtyard, most likely because of the full kitchen. The rooms still seem new, and we understand they are getting ready to remodel. The beds are comfortable and they have nice HD TV's and plenty of channels. The climate control works well and the blower motor stays on for white noise while the climate control is still functioning. We had no noise from adjoining rooms (other than the ruckus with security) nor outside city noise. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space. There is a tub with shower We could hear doors slamming in the morning from time to time. The Residence Inn includes a very nice full breakfast buffet in the restaurant at Courtyard by Marriott. (It is not included at the Courtyard, but was reasonable if you needed to purchase it and the food was good) The area has every type of dining and entertainment option you could ask for all within easy walking distance. We did not partake of any of the hotels dining venues other than the free breakfast.....too many good choices nearby to eat in a hotel. We would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if we wanted to stay in the area for a personal trip. Room rate seemed appropriate for the area, especially with the AAA discount. (We checked the rates, though we were on a reward stay....since it was the same number of points as the Courtyard and had free breakfast, we stayed at the Residence Inn) Having also stayed at the nearby Hilton and Intercontinental hotels in the past, I would feel comfortable choosing any of these hotels based on who has the best price at the time. All of these are very nice options and similar in their offerings and the prices seem to vary wildly from day to day. They were agreeable to late check-out when we asked which was nice. The entire hotel is non-smoking which is always a plus.

“Exceptional” We stayed over Columbus Day weekend and therefore NY was really expensive, but the Andaz came in at $360. This isn't cheap, but from the moment we arrived at check in and were offered a glass of wine, we knew this was an out of the ordinary hotel. The check in process was very neatly handled - efficent but warm and casual, with a hand held i-pad and a charming host. Our room was big - high ceilings, a massive wet room and very stylish - much nicer than the pictures imply. Nice touches; the excellent ipod dock and alarm; the free soft drinks and snacks; the exceptionally comfortable bed, free wifi; very effiecient aircon and most spectacular, the air refiltering system for smokers! Smoking rooms are hard to come by and when a hotel makes your stay really comfortable because they have invested in superior air technology - then I am sold... this is really thinking through what your customers want. At no time did our room smell of smoke. Housekeeping is superb - the whole hotel is perfect. Location - superb. Loads of great restaurants at South St Seaport, a 5 minute walk to the subway, 10 minutes to Battery Park. Cannot be beaten. OK uptown is a 15 minute subway ride, but the city was incredibly busy and coming back to the Andaz was like walking into an oasis of calm. The best thing? Every member of staff we encountered was exceptional. Welcoming, open, kind, helpful - I cannot say how much we appreciated every staff interaction we had. This is as good and maybe beyond Four Seasons, which is my benchmark in exceptional service. Thank you for making our NY stay truly memorable because of this wonderful hotel.

“Convenient location for LA convention, LA Live!” Very nice stay at downtown Sheraton for a conference in LA convention. Although the hotel lobby is not the most up to date, the room was very comfortable, well appointed and quiet, and the bed was extremely comfortable. Staff were friendly and accommodating. The club on the concierge floor had a basic but tasty hors d'oeuvres selection, with wine and beer for a fee. The hotel is directly connected to a mini-mall with Macy's, health club and other shops. It was a 15 min walk to the convention. Lots of restaurants a short cab ride or walk away. To save on the $50 cab ride from the airport, I took the flyaway bus to union station for $7 just outside baggage claim, walked through the station and got a $12 cab to the hotel. Turned out to be pretty quick.

“Wow!” This hotel was amazing. The rooms were tastefully decorated with heavenly carpet. The bed was the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever stayed in - not too firm, not too mushy - with hypoallergenic bedding. The bathroom suite (in a standard room) had a tub and stand alone shower, and was of high quality. Both the room and the bathroom were very large for a DC hotel. The service staff was also more than excellent. Room service was more delicious than many of the restaurants I ate at in the area, but the hotel restaurant was also excellent. Room service was also very fast, regardless of time of day. The hotel is pet friendly, with a pet room service menu too! There were no noise problems either, from the street or other guests. The hotel is around the corner from the White House, and an easy walk to the Smithsonian. Although I was directed to the hotel through a discount hotel booking service, I would have gladly paid full price.

“Mittelmäßiges Hotel in guter Lage” Das Holiday Inn liegt recht zentral im Historic District von Philadelphia. Man kann zu Fuß die Hauptsehnswürdigkeiten, wie das Betty Ross-Haus oder die Unabhängigkeitshalle, gut erreichen. Die Zimmer sind sehr einfach und ohne etwas Besonderes eingerichtet. Alles wirkt etwas renovierungsbedürfitg. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und zuvorkommend.

“Great location, average rooms, very noisy” Stayed here for two days, got a great deal, 170 dollar for an executive floor suite. Typical Intercontinental hotel, in old fashion style. The room (14th floor) was just average, not the typical suite size, but not small either. Couldn't really see what that kitchen corner was about. no refrigerators or chair attached to it. The biggest problem was the noise at evening/night, both traffic and music. In Austin you must of course expect some noise, especially when you live at a hotel so close to sixth street. But a four star hotel like Intercontinental should have double windows or other type of noise isolation. My room had only some old windows, and the noise kept me up all night. And this was not even on the weekend, when Austin really turns up its heat. I wouldn't stay here again, unless I get a really good deal.

“Nice, but somewhat overrated” I stayed at the Lenox from Sep. 18 - 20th. The first room they put me in was not very nice. The carpet was worn, the bathtub leaked, there was no comfortable chair in the room, and the view was of the roof of the back of the building. For $199/night I didn't really think this was adequate. When I complained to the Front Desk, and mentioned that I was supposed to have a corporate rate, I was moved to a much larger room with a loveseat and a better view. I was very satisfied with that room, but I did wonder if I hadn't been a corporate guest if I would have been left in the small, dingy room. In my opinion the amount I was paying was way too much for that room. The amenities are very nice at the Lenox (soaps by Aveda, bathrobes, even umbrellas to use while you're there), and the location is wonderful.

“Stayed for a week - ok hotel, but service needs improvement fast” I stayed at the W-Hotel for a week in a 'spectacular room' - (third category up). It was very small, but I did not mind it too much. The bed was super comfortable. The bathroom was small, but relatively clean (some corners need better cleaning). The toiletries from the bliss Spa were extremely good. As a frequent traveller, I find it absolutely ridiculous of Starwood (and Hyatt for that matter) to charge for internet usage - just got back from a stay at the Grand Hotel in Stockholm where it is free... The gym is fine, some machines are quite shabby (bikes), but the spa is nice and clean. The bar has a good vibe (Blue Whiskey, not the lobby one). The hotel tries very, very hard to be hip, which is sometimes a little painful. Now, the service really needs improvement. Two examples. First, I asked for a restaurant recommendation and I felt that the lady concierge was very arrogant and could not care less - the same one showed the same attitude when I asked her how to get to the Plaza Hotel for a meeting. Second, I left my ipod in my bathrobe, which was unfortunately taken away by the cleaning staff along with the towels. No problems here or accusations, as I should not have left it in there. However, when I noticed it just an hour later, no one made an effort to find it. In fact, I called WhateverWhenever and they did not even bother to get back to me that day to tell me what was going on. The same happened with security the next day. I stayed in many good hotels and never had an item stolen or disappear besides this one and to be quite honest, it could have been found if someone went through all the bathrobes in the cleaning department. I was very displeased about security/concierge not bothering to follow up and letting me know - after all, every room phone has a voicemail.. So overall, the location is very good. The beds are very comfortable - my room was opposite the cleaners' cupboard though, which meant that it was noisy from 8am onwards.... The concierge is less than average. The atmosphere is like a Preppie Kid in hip clothes trying to show to everyone that he/she is REALLY cool and trendy - just simply trying too hard... well, hello there... as they keep saying in their emails/notifications...

“great location for baseball” we stayed here for three nights in july - saturday to tuesday - and enjoyed the great location we had two adjoining rooms - which were a good size, although the bathrooms were small the corridors were dark and dingy and the overall impression was quite depressing - little light we were able to walk to the ball park from the hotel in just a few minutes so that was a real bonus the parking is $7 in the nearby multistorey and $14 with in/out access if you are a hotel resident - reasonable for a city centre one negative point - they wanted to charge us $25 for a fridge to store my son's medication - they didn't add it to the account in the end though - also no room safe the pool area is small and not very welcoming but for a city centre hotel an outdoor pool is a bonus anyway we got a great rate through priceline so at $35 a night the hotel is fantastic value - i would probably try for it again on priceline the rooftop hotel does a very grown up champagne brunch on sunday but we were unable to get a buffet in the other restaurants as the hotel was nearly empty (20% full we were told on the sunday) if you want to go to a game, baseball, basketball or whatever, then this hotel is a good bet - easy walking distance
“great hotel and great staff” We had a great time in this hotel. The staff was fabulous, our room was spacious, our bed was comfortable. The breakfast was average but decent.

“Nice Business Hotel” My company had a business conference at the Manchester and I stayed for two nights. About 250 people attended the conference, and the meeting rooms were nicely prepared, and the staff was helpfull. The room were nice, and my room had a nice view of the bay. I would stay here again. The food prices were high, but there are a lot of dining options in seaport village which is right next to the hotel.

“Great Hotel in Washington D.C.” Had a wonderful 5 days in at the Mandarin Oriental in D.C. with my parents. The rooms are wonderful and the restaurants are great. It is a quiet location, but if you like to walk, most things are within walking distance. The hotel is located only two blocks off the Mall and to the closed Metro Station. You can walsk to the Capital, Whitehouse and Chinatown in 30 minutes. The food at the hotel is wonderful and the staff could not be any nicer. I had a small issue andit was resolved without a problem. I can not wait to return with my wife and family. The hotel only hav valet parking that is expensive, but you are ind.c. and parking everywhere is expensive. Also, a new CVS, Strabucks & Pottbelly just opened and it just outside the front door. However, we did walk to several other restaurant that the hotel recommened to us. Try Tony's in Chinatown if you like Dim Sum. They also had Jazz in the loby most evening and thay have what looks like a wonderful dessert/wine/tea tasing on several afternnons during the week. I was not able to try it, but would have if I would have had the time to enjoy. Also, the Taxi to the hotel was only about 10 minutes and $12.00 from Reagan.

“Great stay!” Wife and I spent two nights at the Intercontinental Hotel in San Francisco. Got a great rate on Hotwire. We had arrived early (about 11:30am) and the rception desk still checked us in early and gave us a nice room on the 21st floor with a great city view. Beds were very comfortable and room was nicely equipped. Location is excellent right in the middle of the SOMA area and very close walking distance to Union Square, Civic Center, and AT&T Park. Lots of great restaurants near by as well. We did not try the bar or restaurant - both were very busy when we dropped by, so we headed next door to the Chieftan, a very nice Irish pub.

“Wonderful surprise near Times Square” What a wonderful surprise - a quiet hotel room right in the the middle of Times Square and the theatre district. The room is small - but not as small as others we have had in the area. We had a computer area with office chair, a second chair, a small dresser, & full size bed with two nightstands. We also had a regular size closet with iron and ironing board. Bathroom was small, with very limited counter space, but again not as small as other hotels in this area. Towels were small and thin. Biggest surprise was the quiet - we were on the ninth floor and even with two windows the room was quiet. The window unit A/C did provide some "white noise", but there was no noise coming from other rooms either. Staff was very nice and polite throughout our stay. Breakfast was minimal - mostly donuts, cereal and fruit. Compared to other Comfort Inns I would only rate the breakfast as fair. I was a little surprised at the tip "bowl", but the attendant was very good about keeping things stocked.

“Great location, friendly staff and clean modern room!!!” This hotel from the moment we checked in we had friendly staff that were very accomodating and gave us tips about the city. When we got to the room we were impressed a very modern room with a good view. The hotel is so unique!!! You feel as if you are totally in a fun space. The breakfast is good way to start the day. Can't complian complimentary breakfast. Tip arrive early to get a table. Later in the morning it can get a bit packed. The location is so great steps away from Michigan Avenue, tons of great shopping, restaurants, Uno's for the deep dish pizza (every time we walked by there was a long line). We walked everywhere from this hotel. Chicago is such a great city to explore via foot. I would definitely recommend this hotel. One night we even had loud neighbours that woke us up at the middle of the night. We called the front desk once and they came up a spoke to the loud guests. They continued to be loud and the first desk came up again and finally the noise went away. Overall a great stay!!

“Nice inexpensive place to stay with easy access to Seattle sights” We stayed one night at the Executive Hotel Pacific after flying from the East Coast for a Norwegian Cruise Lines cruise which departed the next day. The hotel is centrally located for anyone that wants to enjoy the Seattle sights. A quick walk to anything a tourist would want to do! Courteous staff. Clean room. Older style bathroom, like something out of the twenties, but nicely maintained. Would stay here again. One odd thing -- the hotel is located on a corner with a steep street on one side. So, the lobby has two levels, with the elevators not being on the same level as the entrance. You have to carry your bags up and down a short set of stairs, four or five. We did this ourselves, but I imagine the front desk could call someone to provide assistance if you needed it.

“Great for meetings” I have to start my review by saying that I did not stay here overnight but was here for 3 days for a meeting ( I live nearby). From a meeting standpoint this is a great hotel. The staff was always friendly and curtious and all the meals were great. One concern was with their valet parking. One of the attendants didn't seem like he was awake enough to be driving cars and every morning I had to go inside the hotel to find the valet person. Just doesn't seem to be run with the same standards as the rest of the hotel. Otherwise great location and great overall meeting experience.

“Excellent location and large rooms” This Motel 6 is more hotel style, it was the priciest Motel 6 we have stayed in, but its location just behind the Hollywood Boulevard is brilliant (always ask for a discount, especially if you're staying for a few nights). You have to pay for the parking but it has 24 hour security. The rooms were huge and clean with a fridge and large bathroom. The staff were helpful. The only negatives about this motel were noisy neighbours being unable to park in the car park two nights in a row as it was full.

“Small rooms, great service, convinient if you get a good price..” Before we even stayed there, I had a good idea of what the property was going to be like. It is located right next door to the Four Points (basically, attached to each other) and so I figured it would be similar. It is. Lobby is functional, if just a bit small. Room off to the side with computers is very helpful if you don't have your own though there are always people on them. Rooms are small - smallest I've seen in New York I believe. There were 3 of us, and with all our suitcases I found it a bit cramped. While we never really 'fell over' each other, it was hard to get organized in the morning with all 3 of us in the room. Therefore, we went down for breakfast in turns so there was more room to get ready in. Our room contained 2 double beds, the bathroom, a TV cabinet/closet and a desk. Well laid out for the size, just very tiny. Breakfast was a great addition with many items to enjoy. Cereal, baked goods, heated sandwiches, coffee/tea/juice, fruit and yogurt. Breakfast room could be busy at times, though we never had a problem finding a table. One thing to note, however, was the wait for the elevators during breakfast hours. Sometimes it took up to 10 minutes for one to arrive either on your floor, or in the lobby. One huge mention goes out to the staff - all front office staff were very friendly. Always said hello to us, and remembered who we were throughout our stay. Very helpful, and that is a good find in New York. Another positive mention goes out to the free internet in the rooms. The hotel is located on 40th street, bordering the south side of the Port Authority Bus Station. It is a fairly desolate street with adult video stores, a liquor store and a corrections office located on it. I never felt unsafe on it, though my mother remarked she would probably never walk down the street alone at night. Subway entrance, when open, is located at the corner of 40th and 8th Avenue. Overall, a nice hotel in a bit of a down area. Good value for the money, though not incredibly cheap. To be honest, some of Marriott's other properties in Times Square were available for only a fraction more, though if you want free breakfast/internet..you will only find it here.

“So-So” The Union Square Plaza is a cheap hotel with a central location. It's definitely a place for the budget traveler-------divas, asthmatic grandmothers and neat freaks won't be happy there. (But those people shouldn't even be looking in the budget hotel category anyway.) The hallways at the USP were the worst thing about the hotel--------hot, stuffy and musty. And the carpeting was the dictionary definition of "threadbare". My room, however, smelled nice and fresh when I opened the door for the first time. (It wasn't so fresh after I had left the "Do Not Disturb" sign on the doorknob for a couple of days, but that's not the hotel's fault.)The building is old and the rooms are heated by steam radiators.There was a patch black mold or something on the baseboard down by the radiator. Even a hardy budget traveler is grossed out by stuff like that. Otherwise, however, the room was fine. I asked for a room at the back of the hotel, to be away from the Geary St. din, and was very pleased with what I got. There's a small alley behind the hotel, but it's gated, so the only people back there are kitchen workers. (There are four hole-in-the-wall restaurants located right in the USP building. When you walk out the front door of the hotel you're literally three feet from the entrance to the first of them, Katana-Ya.) Union Square is a crowded,densely built neighborhood that reminds me a lot of Manhattan. Which means that you can walk out of the hotel at four a.m. and find four restaurants open for business within a block. Of course, each of them will have at least one homeless panhandler out in front, but that's San Francisco.

“Great location, but too expensive to eat here” Have learned my lesson at the Palace Hotel: come for the central location, but don't eat in any of the restaurants, given the proximity of better and more affordable options nearby. Gym is nice, plenty of machines and not crowded in any way; only gripe is that it would be nice if it were open 24-7. Rooms are fine, nothing to write home about but mine was reasonably clean and quiet (since I had asked to be far away from the center elevators), with a view over the cathedral. Wifi access in room was extremely spotty and the wireline ethernet cable would duck out intermittently. Molton Brown bathroom amenities are a nice touch. And the location relative to anywhere you need to go in the city is great. But the restaurants are absurdly over-priced, even by New York standards. The breakfast is much more expensive and less exciting than the Le Parker Meridien's. And Gilt for a round of after-dinner drinks will cost you a kidney. Stay out of the restaurants, however, and you could have a pretty good stay.

“Lovely Courtyards” This is a great hotel complex on a hillside with lovely courtyards and fountains. With multiple buildings stepping up the hillside, it is easy to get lost in the quaint planted courtyards if you don't pay attention. The rooms are basic with a comfy bed and a character befitting the California Mission style of the complex. And the walking distance proximity to Old Town is ideal. The hotel restaurant lacks prompt service. But, luckily there are plenty of higher quality restaurants nearby in Old Town. I was pleased to see recycling bins in the rooms. However, their shower product bottles were not recyclable, indicating a serious lack of basic corporate environmental responsibility. Additionally, I was not able to connect to the high speed internet either in the room or by Wi-Fi in the courtyard. But I didn't feel like calling the front desk to resolve the problem. So, I suppose I shouldn't hold it against them.

“Unique for a chain hotel” Our family of four really enjoyed this hotel. The property was not much to look at from the outside, but inside it wasquite attractive. Brick walls in the lobby were a bit dark but whimsical furnishings, flooring and art made the atmosphere fun and unique. As an eco-hotel, there's an emphasis on recycling, "green" products, etc, though I can't say that it was really evident during breakfast.The courtyard was very comfortable to use with an interesting water feature. There is no pool, and there's a tavern attached to the lobby, so it's a bit more "grown up" perhaps than some Fairfield Inns, but the location is perfect for families visiting the Inner Harbor, National Aquarium, Little Italy, etc... Valet parking was about $28/day but we parked on the street one block behind the hotel in an area where the residents had no garages and parked on the street. It seemed fairly safe and the car was fine. The desk staff was not super knowledgable but always tried to be helpful. I found it easier to use the internet to find direction, but the computers were conveniently only a few feet away from the front desk. There was also free wifi in the rooms. At check in, I was informed that due to fire code, no rollaway was possible with the 2Q room, despite having reserved this hotel on the Marriott website months earlier and indicating a desire for a rollaway. Since I have teens of different genders, we really have to have a 3rd bed. The clerk worked with me to find a solution, first offering me a different type of room at a much higher price and then, when I expressed my disappointment in the additional costs, looked to find a handicapped room with 2 Qs and asked if we would be okay with it. Turns out this room was huge and had plenty of room for a rollaway. We were very comfortable. There was some noise in the hall which we could hear in the room and at one point, someone was running around up a floor from us and it was fairly loud, but we didn't hear the folks next door. The breakfast was definitely a step below the Residence Inns we'd been staying at. There was cereal, yogurt, instant oatmeal, some refrigerated prepared fruit, small (but tasty) muffins, the ubiquitous make-your-own waffle maker, and pre=packaged, refrigerated breakfast items (one was allegedly a pig in a blanket on a stick, but looked like a corn dog and the other was an awful "quiche"). Also toast, juice, bananas, etc.. But the coffee was the best we had on our trip and made up for alot with us! Disposable everything--plates, cups, glasses, etc,. However, the room was clean and had lots of different seating options; again we found it very comfortable. The only facilities issue I had was that there was only one elevator and no staircase we could find to the lobby (it went outside). The hotel did feel really secure because of that but the waits at the elevator could get a little long. I would stay here again without hesitation. The price was right and it was super comfortable and convenient. While not upscale, it was modern and well furnished and just unique enough to really fit into to the renovated Inner Harbor/Little Italy neighborhood.

“Absolutely Lovely Hotel in New York City” The Lowell is a truly rare find in New York City - a wonderful location with gracious staff and distinctive rooms! I literally booked the room minutes before arriving and yet was met on my arrival like a returning family member. No-one even batted an eye when I checked-in sans luggage as I had not planned for an overnight stay in the city. Within minutes of being shown to my room a small assortment of toiletries was delivered -- a hair brush, tooth brush/paste, etc. Coupled with the yummy Bulgari toiletries I was set for a night of pampering! The room itself was a dream. It was beautifully decorated in a personal home way, large, well-lit and had french doors leading to a terrace which ran the length of my room. And the bathroom was huge complete with double sinks and lovely window (more light) and heated marble floors. I could move right in! A small kitchen is cleverly hidden behind what appears to be a closet door. It comes complete with a refrigerator, microwave, small cooktop and dinnerware. Did I mention I could move right in? The staff was gracious and kind. I ordered a tea service for dinner and it arrived within 15 minutes. About 9pm I ordered a snack and it to was at my door in minutes -- but the biggest surprise was the excellent quality of the room service food. When leaving the next morning the doorman ran between Madison and the hotel to locate a taxi for me if the rain. Now how often does that occur? Beg, borrow and plead but do stay here your next visit to NYC. They absolutely have me as a client for life!
“Adequate” Decent hotel. Comfortable rooms, if a bit small. Neighborhood isn't the greatest; not much character. Bar and restaurant were okay. Parking costs, like most of SF, are outrageous.

“Just okay” Located centrally in the heart of Boston's shopping district, I have stayed at this property several times. The guest services are not bad and they are quite attentive to the needs of the guests. However, I am disappointed with the hardware goods of the hotel. The rooms are comfortable but the decor is not up to the usual 'MO Standards.' In comparison the MO New York spent much more on the final finishing. For the amount I am playing I would like a better television. The hotel uses a very ordinary Philips TV with no Interactive system. The bed is also very soft !

“One of the best Courtyards” In terms for value for money, I think the Courtyard brand takes some beating. This is one of the best courtyards. While I really like the new receptions they have been standardizing on in other Courtyards, this one is different, in that it has a more traditional reception area, with a nice fireplace and seats in the reception area, which makes the place feel welcoming, and the reception staff were excellent. The room was good, comfortable bed, though still with the relatively low quality sheets that you get at Courtyard (not really a criticism - when you're not paying top dollar, you shouldn't expect the high end luxuries). The bathroom was a little small and not well lit, but it wasn't too bad. This hotel has one of the better hotel bars. Nice welcoming staff and a decent menu. The gym and swimming pool are excellent. I actually couldn't get into the pool due to some sort of problem with the door card system, but the receptionists couldn't have been more helpful in getting it resolved so I could get my daily swim in. All told, this is an excellent hotel.

“nice setting” My husband found this hotel on bookingbuddy.com for a pretty good price, so we booked despite being 10 miles north of the airport. We arrived after 11 pm to a warm welcome. Finding the hotel was a challenge but I'll blame the gps. The hotel is in the middle of a business park, but is very pretty. Lots of greenery. The one bedroom suite had a furnished kitchen and a fireplace. The hotel's selling point to those who care is the "green" choices they made in water and energy. See their web site for details. Bed was not top quality but not uncomfortable. TVs not high quality (old box style in both rooms) and only one remote. In the morning we discovered our shower didn't work. We went to the on site breakfast, and reported the problem. They gave us keys to another suite to shower while they repaired ours. The breakfast was great. Lots of organic and healthy choices. Didn't use pool but it is smallish. Would stay again, especially for multiple nights.

“Originale e con Notevole Vista” Avevo scelto per la nostra (purtoppo) unica notte a Chicago questo hotel per via di una buona offerta su internet. L'Hotel è in centrissimo e si presenta veramnte molto bene. Si entra in una hall molto invitante che alla sua destra ospita un bel bar (con costi molto accessibili) a sinistra l'ascensore (rivestita in plastica!!) ti porta al primo piano dove c'è la lobby. Gentili (anche se un tantino altezzosi... questo lo devo dire...) di assegnano la camera. La camera piccina per la media americana ma una chicca! Bagno con uno specchio incredibile (quando ti gradi si riflette la cornice negli occhi... una roba stranissima!!!) La doccia è separata dalla camera da una vetrata! IL letto comodo! Frigo bar con buona ed elegante fornitura, casse con carica per Ipod, ADSL inclusa discreto caffè! La camera ha un bel terrazzino e una vetrata con una vista notevole! Il parcheggio non è incluso $ 36 ( un pochino caro!) Ah dimenticavo legno per terra fantastico!!!! No orrida moquette!!!

“Nice Change from the Norm” Modern design and furnishings in a great change from the standard franchise hotels in the area. Comfy bed and pillows. Fun shower and tub. Breakfast was okay but would have been nice to have fruit or yogurt available too. Difficult access from I-35 North. I will stay here again.

“Pleased with my stay. Met my needs.” As always, before booking a hotel stay I consult TripAdvisor to read the various reviews on a property. Previous reviews were all over the map. Upon check in I was pleased with the lobby area and it's welcoming feel. My room was a standard double and yes while somewhat dated (wall paper); it was clean and met my needs just fine. The bathroom is well appointed with amenities and well lit. I would've liked more lighting in the room. Also, the prices in the restaurant are pricey, which surprised me for a Holiday Inn. The breakfast buffet was $12.95. There are many other less expensive places to eat very near the hotel. Overall I enjiyed my stay. Even though I used reward points for this room, I don't I was short-changed. I belong to a lot hotel reward programs and feel IHG's ranks among the at the top for what you are able to get for your points.

“A Very solid six night stay” Wow! This place was really cool. I stayed here with a group on a teen-tour to So. California and Hawaii. I stayed here for six nights. We checked in very quickly in the nice lobby. My room on the 12th floor was spacious. The beds were so comfortable, even the rollaway was quite comfortable. The shower was nice and powerful. The pool area is beautiful and it has a hot tub. The location is great too...right next to a trolley station! The hotel restaurant has good pizza, but the best food nearby is at Seau's, owned by former Chargers linebacker Junior Seau. I never had to wait for an elevator, which was good. My only complaint was the staff. We were a large group, so naturally we were going to make a lot of noise. The staff would not stop complaining about our noise! They said that the doors kept slamming shut. Well, then get doors that don't make so much noise! It's not our fault. Besides, we barely made any noise...it was the people with babies on our floor that made the noise. The staff assumed that it was us just because we were a large group and easy to pick on. And they didn't tell us nicely. They used nasty tones of voice and were very rude. But the hotel itself was excellent, so I would definitely stay there again and recommend it to others.

“clean modern design at a great price” Stayed in February for a weekend dedicated to play-going with spouse. Reserved room at a super rate $139 per night for a standard room. Room was well designed - not large, but fine by Manhattan standards. Bed was firm and comfortable. Husband loved the Ihome alarm clock. Lobby is minimal - not even a desk. Several check-in computers attended by helpful staff. Room service is possible from several restaurants, though be careful - some listed in room guide have closed. Hotel is quite convenient for mid-town attractions. This is a case where I debate star level. It was perfect for what we needed - a clean, modern, comfortable base to explore for 2. But it lack things like a refrig in room. The bottled water advertised is in the hallway with reusable plastic bottles provided - eco conscious but not necessarily 5*. Fitness room is limited - no treadmill for example. So I compromised on a 4 star rating. Still highly recommended for the right stay. Note: we drove into the city - hotel has a $35 24 hour parking rate with a nearby garage.

“Nice Stay, but wont go there again” I have stayed at The Wit before and had a pleasant experience, so we decided to give it another run and stayed for 2 nights to celebrate my birthday and take in the city. Let me start by saying I have Diamond status with the HIlton brand and stay at alot Hilton properties. The hotel has a nice vibe when you walk in, a great location and very nice rooms. Since we were having a few people down to celebrate my birthday, we went with a suite that had a kitchen/dining area, famliy room and a very large soaker bathroom. I must say, the electric push button blinds/curtains were pretty fun (they only have those in the suites). Overall, the hotel is very nice. Now, the bad part and the reason i wont go back. My wife and I have a bit of a tradition, when we go out for our birthday, anniversary, etc, we always surprise each other with a nice bottle of Champagne/Wine and some type of chocalates/fruits delivered to our room-its fun and romantic. My wife called in the day before to have the champagne and chocalate delivered at 5pm (HIlton is normally perfect at delivering right on time!). So as I was anxious to get ready for the night and wanted to leave the room, she patiently asked me to wait. Long story short, 5pm passes and at 5:45, she breaks down and tells me the items were supposed to be delivered at 5. We called the front desk 2 times over the next 45 minutes, two times they said they would call us back with an update, but didnt, so we start to get ready for our night and at about 6:30, our items finally show up. I nicely told them we no longer wanted the items as they were 90 min late and we were now leaving for dinner. I called the front desk one last time and mentioned I turned down the room service and they said a manager would be contacting me, but he never did. They did offer up a free bottle of wine for our room, which I turned down. I am not super picky with service and Hilton Hotels have always been great! I get that mistakes happen, but this had that "so what" feel to it which was a disappointment. I will add that outside of this, the service was good.

“Excellent quality, everything you expect of a JW” Stayed here in September on a weekend away. Weekends in downtown San Francisco are curious - hordes of tourists from all over the world give downtown give a somewhat theme park feel to the city. The absence of locals detracts from the experience, but that being said, the JW Marriott is exceptionally well located right near Union Square, and not too far from the BART/MUNI on Market. I arrived to SFO, and walked to the JW from Powell Station. Don't let anyone tell you that you have to take a cab to/from SFO or Oakland airport. Unless you have industrial sized luggage, take BART from the airport. Arriving early in the morning, I tried for an early check-in, but the room wasn't ready. This isn't a huge gripe except Marriott has an option for early check in - subject to availability. I wish they would simply remove this option since there's really only downside for the hotel. It creates an expectation for the traveller and makes the hotel say 'no' to something on first impression. Notwithstanding, they were very gracious to take our bags and we went sightseeing in the meantime. The room was exceptional. Sometimes the Marriott interiors are so generic it's impossible to tell whether you are in Bangkok, Boston, or Bangalore. This is different - great pictures with SF themes and a true luxury edge to the room made this very special. Service was very good - I ordered a wine and cheese platter which came promptly as promised. The cheeses were excellent quality, Stilton, Camembert and Jarlsberg and beautifully presented. I travel a lot and it's clear they pride themselves on going the extra mile here. Downsides: I don't blame the specific hotel for the early check-in disappointment, but Marriott really does need to give better guidance as to how likely it is. The only other problem was all elevators were not fully functional which led to some delays lining up for the elevator, but this was minor. Upshot is: An excellent quality five star hotel which meets all expectations. I do recommend travelers to SF venture farther afield than downtown and explore places like the Mission, Haight, and Castro to get more of a real SF flavor.

“Very good Westin in the heart of Denver” Had a short trip for business to Denver and stayed at this property. I'm a SPG platinum for almost 5 years straight now and I tend to have a discreet standard for Starwood properties. This particular Westin met all and exceeded most of those expectations for the short trip. The Good: - Valet service was friendly and prompt. Had my car ready within 5-10 minutes of calling down. - Check in staff was friendly and knowledgeable. Greeted me by name. - Rooms were what you would expect for a Westin. Clean and spacious. Lots of convenient plugs to charge your laptop and phones. - Location was probably the best thing about this hotel. Right in the middle of the business district and walking distance to everything you need and food options. The Bad: - Close to a park frequented by a lot of hipsters. I heard street drumming up until 10PM one night. - I just remember the bathroom as not being as new. But I think I'm just being picky now.

“Close to perfect location, without frills despite its reputation” I bid on this room through Priceline and got an incredible mid-week deal. Since this was a surprise birthday present to my husband, I phoned ahead requesting a room with a view of the lakefront. Upon arrival, I was told that due to its location there was no such thing. The first room we were given had a view -- of a courtyard-like area showcasing outside emergency exits. When I asked to be moved, the front desk moved us into another area where we actually were able to see a tiny bit of the lake. The lake is the object my late night gazing and meditation tradition, so this small view made a great difference. The room decor was austere but classy, with the exception of an ulgy headboard that took up half of the wall. The bathroom had beautiful marble tiling, and the shower was immaculate. There was no exhaust fan in the bathroom, which made no sense given the scant privacy afforded by the wood and glass pocket door. Just down the street from the Mag Mile, we did some shopping and celebrity peeping. A famous actor who calls Chicago home was enjoying the abnormally warm weather with his wife and baby. No one bothered him because the area is accustomed to spotting beautiful people. I would stay there again, as it is a short walk to the jazz clubs and foodie options just to the north and west across Michigan Avenue. We stumbled upon the Original Pancake House and learned how justified the long lines are: the wait was only 20 minutes and the pancakes are TO-DIE for.

“Great Fitness Facilities” Some colleagues and I booked the Marriott for a quick overnight because of its proximity to our Denver office. The hotel is in an area loaded with major restaurant franchises to serve all of the office buildings in the complex, but they're far-flung enough that a car is a good idea, anyway. The hotel itself is very well-equipped: a large business center that doesn't charge by the page to print things, a Starbucks that's got a large seating area, a gym worthy of a freestanding Fitness Center, and a generous indoor pool. There's an outdoor pool as well, but not very inviting in December. I was given a room with a balcony- it had a nice view of the mountains but a busy highway was in between my room and the view! I did notice the traffic noise some, since it's only a 5-floor hotel. My room had a microwave and a small refrigerator. The coffee maker contained a used filter pack, but had been fully stocked with replacement packs- minor housekeeping omission. Everything else was fine. No meals there, so I can't comment on the restaurant. I hope to use the Marriott again if I return.

“A reaonable, if unremarkable, hotel” There's little that's memorable or out of the ordinary about this hotel. The location, close to the restaurants, bars and shops or Newbury and Boyleston streets, and adjoining the Prudential Center, is great. The rooms appear for the most part to be on the small side. While clean and habitable, they're not luxurious and don't appear to have been modernised in the recent past. The whole place feels very much 3 rather than 4*. If you can get a room at a reasonable rate (I paid $110 via Priceline), then this is reasonable enough choice. While I wouldn't discourage anyone from staying, nor would I go out of my way to choose it over other alternatives.

“We'll be back bur would like some changes in the Happy Hour.” the hotel and the room was very nice. the bed was comfortable, the pool and hot tub area were clean and not over crowded and the food options the hotel offers are great. My biggest problem was at Happy Hour the hotel so graciously offers guests was disrupted by one child screaming the whole time and another handling all the fruit at the buffet table, even sucking and biting on some and putting it back for unsuspecting guests take. I did tell a buffet worker and she just shrugged ( maybe didn't understand English) it was rather disgusting and certainly unhealthy. Maybe if there were rules on how old a child is to be able to go to Happy Hour that would help( because some guests are just poor parents is not the fault of the hotel) But rules are

“Excellent Historic Hotel” I recently stayed at this very historic hotel. The entire hotel is in outstanding condition. The lobby when you enter is very well maintained, the shops are all very clean and update to date as well. The rooms have the old school charm that brings back a lot of memories. The beds are very comfortable and the linens are very soft. The in-room high speed wireless internet worked very well. My colleagues and I had dinner in the hotel at the bar. The food and service was both top notch. If you are looking for a nice hotel, reasonable price and historic charm I would highly recommend this hotel. The only gotcha is parking is $40 per day.

“Convention center hotel in Seattle” The Sheraton is a big, bustling hotel immediately across from the convention center. The rooms are nice, but vary a lot by the price you paid. Based upon fellow travelers, opaque site guests will get the rooms next to vending machines, elevators etc. I liked the hotel, but fellow travelers (girls) complained about the beds not being comfortable. Internet charges are high, and overnight parking is $40. The hotel is 3 blocks from the light rail station (to the airport) which is $2.50 and 30 minutes. Taxi fare to the airport is $35 and 30 minutes as well. Busses in the downtown are free, but this is a good walking city (bring an umbrella). About 5 blocks to Pike’s Market. Nothing special about the hotel (except convince to the convention center), but you will like it

“Stayed 2 nights while shopping” We often stay at Residence Inns because we enjoy the breakfasts, spacious rooms and Jameson mattresses (we even went to North Carolina to buy one after sleeping on one several times at other Residence Inns). Planning to spend the weekend shopping between Jeffersonville one day and Easton the next, I looked for a hotel on the south side of town or at Easton. Easton hotels were very pricey this time of year so I booked The Southeast Residence Inn through Expedia for about $70 a night with a coupon. Our room was spacious and clean with a full kitchen and pull out couch but not the suite we were used to at other RIs. It did have a fireplace and the front desk provided a firelog on request. The mattress was comfortable but not Jameson. Breakfast was great and the staff friendly at the front desk and at breakfast. While not in the best part of town, I felt the hotel was safe, secure and well lit. Other Residence Inns are nicer but this did suit our needs and was very reasonable.

“Not awful, but needs work on a few fronts” I recently stayed 3 nights at the Marriott Tech Center for a business meeting in Denver (which was not conducted at the hotel). It wasn't terrible, but I wouldn't pick it for a return visit to the area. Although front desk staff was friendly and the shuttle staff were super helpful, I had a few discouraging interactions with staff answering the guest services line regarding the difficulty I had getting wireless internet. The information I got was contradictory, they sounded put-out with my questions, and it took 20 minutes to find out that I was supposed to ask the front desk to "connect" me to wireless (why anyone should have to do this, I can't imagine; and there was zero information in the room about this). Overall, the hotel seemed kind of shabby to me. Some of the towels in my room had bare spots worn through and the furnishings were sort of run-down. A colleague who stayed at the same time as I did broke out in a rash and thought she had bed-bugs. But she had been to the hot tub the night before, and I just saw in a previous review that another guest got a rash from the hot tub. It seems that this hotel has some issues it needs to address before it will attract repeat customers.

“Good Location, Cramped Space” Execellent location, easy access to all major business offices in downtown, negative things are very cramped parking, and noise in room. Has a restaurent/Bar which is good

“Best location in city!” Great location rooms are really nice. Everything within walking distance makes this hotel the perfect location. Don't miss little Italy it's some of the best food we've had. Bellman Eddie was great and really went out of way to help us. Thanks for a great stay

“”アッパーウエストサイドの住民”を体験できるような素敵なホテル” Deluxe QueenBedに宿泊しました。 高級エリアのアッパーウエストサイドにあり、近くには地元で有名なベーグルショップやスーパーマーケット、かわいいレストランがあり、地下鉄の駅からの近かったです。ミッドタウンのような観光客向けでなく、NYの生活を体験したい方におすすめ。部屋も値段の割りには広く綺麗で、スタッフも親切でした。

“WOW” here is why the price - a little bit pricy, but here is ehat u get... 1. close to every thing ( almost ) :) ): 10 min from the center. china town, Reading terminal market, JFK plaze park... and so much more 2. good service with a smile :) 3. big, no wait, HUGE rooms, king king size bed ( double king :) )... cool bathroom, two huge closets, the size of the sleeping area was bigger that my room :) 4. a kitchen wityh all the appliances, including a dishwasher, come on how cool... 5. we staied at 7th foolr, and at the 8th floor u have washer/dryer.... very handy... and get the job done VALUE MONEY :) :) definitely

“Comfort and elegance in a great location” My room was on the small side, but perfectly comfortable for one person. The bed was heavenly--down blanket, fluffy pillows, luxurious sheets. The bathroom was small but beautifully appointed. My window had a very nice city view, and my room was deliciously quiet. The only downside was room-service breakfast, which is something I really look forward to on a trip. The Oj and coffee were excellent, the bacon very good, the French toast mediocre, and the potatoes inedible. The desk clerk removed the charge very graciously, and apologized. I would certainly stay here again.

“Best hotel ever stayed in” We got a special on stay 2 nights get 1 free on the Club Lounge floor. We stayed 4 nights. The service in the lounge was excellent. Could have eaten all 3 meals there, but had booked 4 of the top 6 Trip Advisor restaurants for dinner each evening. Breakfast included smoked salmon. Coffee machine that's like making your own Starbucks. Lunch of sandwiches, soup & mini salads. Evening cocktails were included along with heavy snacks & 1 hot item and light desserts. I'll never stay in a regular room again. Staff was knowledgable in recommendations. Spa treatment was an additional highlight. Con~wish they had an outdoor pool. The pool was in the fitness area & roped off for swimming laps.

“Close to everything without the high prices!” My husband & I celebrated our two month wedding anniversary with a weekend trip to Philly. The Hilton Garden Inn was great! We checked in and spent the evening in our hotel room. The beds were comfy (we ended up with two doubles) and the bathroom was fairly spacious. There's a Wawa convenience store across the street with normal prices, so it's a great place to get a snack or a drink without paying a fortune. We walked to all the sights on Saturday morning. I doubt it was more than a fifteen minute walk to the area, making it easy to get around without taking a car out of the garage. The hotel is right between Chinatown & Center City, so if you're looking for Chinese food, you're in luck. The Reading Terminal Market is also nearby, so be sure to get a yummy and great value breakfast from one of the many Pennsylvania Dutch stands inside. Only hitch was parking; the hotel lets you pay the same price to them (instead of the garage) and you'll get in-and-out privileges. For some reason, they never charged us but had already given us the voucher to give the garage at check-in. Worried that something funny would happen with billing later, I pointed out the problem and they went ahead and charged us the $20/day parking. Probably could have said nothing and gotten it for free! If you don't mind a little walk, this is a nice place to stay for exploring Philly.

“Great Business Hotel” I was in town for 5 days/4 nights. Great rooms, very clean, love the separate living room and bedroom. The warm breakfast in the AM was good with eggs made fresh to order. And the happy hour in the evening was perfect. I did use the gym and the business center, both were adequate. The Omaha Steakhouse on site was very good and convenient. Would highly recommend this place to business travelers. Close to the Interstate and only a few miles from Uptown.

“Nice stay” I made the reservation for this hotel through calling Sheraton's reservation hotline. This was my first time staying at a Four Points, and I thought the rate was decent. Driving to the hotel from the highway was not simple. I arrived after a 4hr drive frazzled, not to mention it was one of the hottest days in the South (102 degrees). However, upon arrival, the clerk at the counter was very nice. She was a trooper seeing that it was a large number of kids in the hotel for some event and the lobby felt like it was 98 degrees in itself. Check in took only a few minutes. My room overlooked the pool, which many people took advantage of into the night. The walls and windows are thin, but the noise wasn't a big deal to me. The kids had a blast in the pool that night. I was glad to see the fridge, but disappointed to see there was no microwave. The bed is super, super comfortable. Matter of fact, a friend who had been staying at a Ramada since Thursday, decided to spend the night at my hotel that night because of the bed. One issue i had: I forgot to ask the customer service rep on the phone was this a pet friendly hotel, because i'm almost sure the little black hairs i saw sporadically in the bathroom belonged to a dog or cat. Also, the hot water handle on the sink became loose while i was there. Other than that, I had no problems. Overall, this was a very nice hotel for the price. As others mentioned, there was free parking and wi-fi. I don't know if it was because I used the wi-fi on my phone, but every time i clicked on my browser, I had to get past the screen that have you accepting the terms and conditions--each and every time i opened my browser.

“Really, This is Just an OK Hotel” Just left a big conference there. Major construction going on, be advised. I mean all around. Location is crazy. Forget about a morning or evening run. Too much construction. Hotel has two lobbys. Confusing, and must take two elevators to get to the main lobby, I mean the lobby that will take you to the street, not to the restaurant and bar area- confused yet? Rooms are decent, gym just ok. Pool is nice. I will say the food is pretty good, very good in fact. Service is good. Nice people. WiFi charge was taken off my bill because I hate getting nickled and dimed. Just give us free WiFi in the room! Show folks you care abut their business. They need to get this place together. It just feels disjointed. It's ok if you get a great deal on price. If not, I'd try the Intercontinental instead.

“I expected more.” As far as room quality, I really expected more for downtown Boston. The rooms needs a serious face lift. Service was fair and every time we walked through the lobby there was an extremely long line at the front desk. Everyone was friendly and polite but didn't have a sense of urgency about them. The location of the hotel truly saved the stay from turning more negative. The grocery store right across the skywalk/ street was wonderful and a great convenience. We walked over every morning for breakfast rather than eating the same old Marriott eggs. Also, note that valet parking is $44 a night. Not exactly cheap, but unavoidable for this part of the city.

“Great location, interior grandeur, though small rooms may limit appeal” Pros: Central Park location, spa, cozy and romantic ambiance Cons: Had a poor view facing a brick wall, small room, lighting system frustrating at times, current scaffolding out front (necessary though it is) downplays the luxurious interior Having walked on by the chandeliers and sunflower-laden vases, things were already looking good in the spacious lobby area. When the receptionist then passes you a hot towel upon arrival you know this hotel means business. And Essex House, in general, delivered. This is all about location: across Central Park South, you have the park at your doorstep, but it's also easy to get into midtown too or to either the east or west side for whatever you may choose to do on your stay. The room I stayed in was small, cozy and (on the downside) had an awful view looking onto a brick wall. The bed was big, though uses up most of the space in the room - as to be expected in most downtown hotels one imagines, yet it's the smallest of the six other Manhattan hotels that I've stayed in. So don't expect to bring the whole family and have room; not that this was a problem for myself cozied up with the girlfriend with soft lighting adding to the ambiance (with auto-sensing lights excellent to locate the bathroom in the middle of the night, the abundance of actual lights and switches elsewhere did make turning all the lights off for sleep a bit of a light switch hunt). Any of these pernickety issues brushed to one side however and Essex House staff were seriously helpful with a number of issues: rather than spending $30pp/each way to stow bags on an internal American Airlines flight, the Bell Hop happily held two pieces of luggage from Thursday through to Saturday prior to check in. Of course we tipped for this service, but this in the long run saved me about $110. And it didn't stop there: even after checking out on the final day of my holiday and trekking around Manhattan for several hours, the hotel spa still accepted us post-check out (and I'm talking about 8 hours after check out) for a free steam, sauna and shower before nipping off to our flight home (felt so clean approaching the airport it shaved a chunk of the stress of flying off). If it wasn't for this attentiveness then I'd actually only award Essex House 4/5 rather than 5/5 (due to the small rooms and poor view) - but such service really added massive Brownie points to my experience. Restaurant and bar also looked very cool. Expensive, sure, but were only really let down by the current scaffolding that's erected outside. The sheer volume of staff to ensure everything was right (and the down-right awesome complimentary nut selection) held a firm smile on my face.

“No worries. Great relaxing stay!” Travel was for a business trip. BLUF: As a business traveler, this hotel offers all the amenities you are looking for. I would stay here again. Check out time - 12 Noon. Cheers: ------- Kitchen – just like home only smaller. D/W, frig (w/ ice maker), microwave. My room had two separate living areas. Bedroom and a kitchen/living room. I had 2 TVs – one in the BR and one in the Living room. The room was nicely decorated with 9 foot high ceilings with modern furnishings and a nice neutral paint color. Nice bed and sofa. Free breakfast. Free dinner on Mon – Th. Nice quite AC unit. The room was nice and cool when I arrived. Internet service w/o logging on. 2 phones – 1 by the bed and 1 on the desk. A nice work area with power outlets above the desk. Pool. There is also a small on-site convenience store to get soda, chips, water, snacks, etc... The room darkening shades did a good job on keeping out the light if you need to rest during the day. Free paper. Jeers: ------ OK water pressure. Slow Internet Local area info: ------------- There is a BP right next door so you can gas up the rental car before you return it to the airport. There is also a Subway within the BP. There is also a FedEx Kinko’s and Jersey Mike’s subs close by.

“Very impressed” Stayed here for a few days and was very impressed. While the building is older, the rooms have been recently renovated in the modern style. Staff was very nice at check in and throughout my stay. My only complaint is that the room could have been cleaner, especially in the bathroom, where there were a few handprints and smudges. However, overall I was very satisfied and I look forward to staying here again.

“Excellent choice” This hotel was great. The staff friendly and helpful. The room was small, but comfortable. Bathroom was roomy. Great location in NYC, close to everything. Fantastic Italian restaurant directly across the street. I will make this hotel my first choice on any future visit to NYC.

“Great views” Get a room on the 40+ floor facing the lake..very nice view. I like this hotel. Its got a great lobby with a good bar in an open floor style. Restaurant is good for breakfast and lunch. The exec lounge is excellent, large and airy, compared to many other marriots which are small and dark. Rooms are pretty good size and works without a problem. Location is fab just around the corner and walking distance to most of the down town stuff. Service is professional and good.

“A Great Choice” This is a wonderful hotel. Relatively new, in an area that is seeing considerable redevelopment off the main drag of downtown Seattle. The hotel itself is an oasis – the architectural and styling lines ooze creature comfort. Check in is flawless, with no limit on the amount of information conveyed in a helpful, welcoming way. Even booking through Expedia, at a reduced advance rate, we were given a 10th floor Lake view room. The room boasts almost floor to ceiling windows from post to post. The amount of natural light is stunning, even on two gloomy days in Seattle. The bathroom is set off by sliding doors, which when opened convey and reinforce a sense of roominess. The natural wood and compatible fixtures are handsomely elegant, again, just right for the space. The bed and working areas are top notch. As others have noted, the only glitch in the offering, if you have to fall for it, is the parking rate, now up to $39/day. There are many other self-parking options in the neighborhood, all apparently safe. I managed to leave our rental car on the street each night for a grand total of $0. If you need to be caressed by valet service, and don’t mind that cost, go for it. The service level undoubtedly is on par with all of the other interactions. But if you’re failingly cost-conscious, don’t fret; on-street parking and takeaway from the fab WholeFoods in the complex should make you consider moving into the PanPacific for an extended vacation....

“Wonderful hotel for not only quality and location, but price” I stayed here, under name alone two years ago, since then they moved next door and are just as good. I came here for an automotive event I worked on Hollywood Blvd which was hdqrtd at the nearby Rossevelt. This is the best hotel I have found which is equally within easy walking distance of the Hollywood Bowl, and the Hlooywood Blvd Strip (Grauman's Chinese Theatre, Hollywood/Highland complex including the Kodak Theatre, Jimmy Kimmel, etc...) After arriving I had a room with two queen beds, cheaper than a single king, and after asking if I was there alone, they instantly upgraded me to a king room on an upper floor. While they don't have a restaurant, they do offer a complimentary full breakfast each morning. For other meals there is every type of eatery either across the street or down the block. They also offer a refrigerator for anything you bring with you or bring back. There are all of the ammenities you would expect from this level. They offer free internet, printing, a pool, and exercise room. While some of these have a listed closing time they seemed to go much later. It is not a 'party' hotel, mainly tourists so even later in the night it does not get wild and noisy. Very friendly front desk guy who worked afternoons when I was there, we talked a bit and I even ran into him on the street a couple times as we both were coming or going. There is a small 'convienence' store for items you might want.

“Angenehmes Hotel - und günstig” Das Hampton Inn konnte ich für 72 $ (plus Steuern) mit AAA-Rabatt buchen, was ein sehr günstiger Preis für das Gebotene ist. Das Zimmer ist großzügig und neuwertig, mit Kühlschrank. Die Lage ist am Rande des "Krankenhaus-Viertels", was ich Abend bei der Fahrt mit der Straßenbahn in die Innenstadt merkte. Die Station ist direkt am Hotel, so dass man abends in die Stadt fahren kann, ohne das Auto zu brauchen.

“Friendly staff, W standard” This is your W experience through and through with uptempo common areas and stylish room decor. The staff here was very friendly. I will note however that as a platinum member the experience was not quite as nice compared to that of other SPG hotels. Overall however this is a staple W experience which is by far above and beyond most. With only one note being that room size is smaller than those in other cities. The rooftop view is superb and location cannot be beat.

“Best of the Best!” From the moment I arrived at the Vintage Park Hotel in Seattle, I was a welcomed guest. The staff greeted me with smiles as I arrived in the garage. In the lobby I was quickly checked in and my three dogs were each offered a treat. The room was spectacularly decorated with the wine theme as advertised. I, and my three dogs, enjoyed the ability to open the windows to allow fresh air in. The windows are appropriately nose height for my k9's, offering them a view and smell of the city. On our first walk outside of the hotel, the staff offered locations to doggy bathrooms guiding us right to them. As with other Kimpton properties the service and amenities were top notch. I dined at Tulio, the restaurant adjacent to the hotel. Like a fine wine pairing at a great meal, the dining experience only added to the value that Vintage Park offered. I enjoyed the meal and the stay very much. When I return to Seattle I will return to Vintage Park. Pro's Windows that open Large Spacious King Room Views Wonderfully Welcoming staff Great food at Tulio Close to all that downtown Seattle has to offer Con's As with many older hotels that have been remodeled the bathroom was a little cramped, (but I don't get a room for the bathroom). Internet was intermittent and slow (it was a vacation so I didn't mind)

“Cool Hotel, Great Views, Great Service” Stayed here for business for a few days. I was on the 48th floor. Room was clean, roomy, had what I needed, but just a bit dated and rough. Not what you would expect from a Marriott for the price. However, the service folks -- valet, front desk, room service, operator -- were A Plus -- attentive, friendly, concerned, and just great innkeepers. Did room service twice for dinner and service was great, food was terrific, and priced reasonably. I'd stay here again. The whole complex is a bit confusing at first, but not hard to figure out. Work out room on the 40th floor was one of the best hotel work out rooms I've used.

“Location=awful. Lobby=beautiful. Rooms=apparently getting updated soon.” The intial impressions of this hotel are equivalent to "WOWWWW this is amazing!" and then you get to your room... The lobby is very typical of the updated large Hiltons...very modern, very calm, tons of seating/meeting area, trendy/courteous staff. The rooms leave a lot to be desired...in fact, many of the staff have seemed to automatically resort to telling guests that rooms will be updated "soon" so guests do not complain. Well, that's great you're up soon for a remodel, but it didn't help me at the time. At this point, the rooms are basically what you would have found in the mid-1990's. Aside from the bed, typical Hilton pillowtop (always nice). I think for the time being, the hotel management could have the engineering staff in those rooms after every guest to polish things up and at least give the appearance that the old hardware is well-maintained. The rooms really were lackluster. The location is also god-awful. Basically just a hotel in a business park. There is NOTHING within walking distance. Not even something as simple as a Walgreens or CVS. My coworker and I were warned by staff that it's not safe to walk anywhere in this particular area. We didn't ask if it was due to no sidewalks (near a major freeway) or due to other reasons. Therefore, if you do not have a car, you are at the mercy of the spotty service of the hotel shuttle (which really only takes people to the Galleria mall & back) or a taxi (super expensive.) I wouldn't stay here again until after the rooms are updated. Also, there would be no point to staying here without a car.

“Small room but excellent location” My wife and I spent a Friday and Saturday here to escape from Hurricane's Sandy's havoc in New York. It is a small hotel with smallish rooms and a tiny bathroom better designed for one person on a business trip than a couple but the very favorable weekend rate made up for the tightness. The hotel is perfectly located for business in the middle of Boston's financial district which is a warren of narrow and dark streets with little of appeal. Do not be put off tough because all Boston's charms surriound this area so the hotel is very centrally located and you can easily walk to all Boston's many pleasures. Although no car is ever needed in Boston, and the hotel is easily walkable from Amtrak's South Station and the State Street T from Logan Airport, if you have one you can park on the streets during the weekends. Just be sure to read the all the parking restriction signs very carefully.

“ottimo hotel” albergo comodissimo, dietro il quincy market e vicino al porto. Camere grandi, molto pulito, noi avevamo una doccia larga ben 2 metri in marmo nero...uno spettacolo!! Personale cordiale e disponibile.

“Gutes verkehrsgünstig gelegenes Hotel in San Diego” Das Hotel liegt sehr günstig in der Nähe der großen Highways. Man ist innerhalb von 30 Minuten in Downtown San Diego oder auch bei nahegelegenen Sehenswürdigkeiten. Die Zimmer sind sauber, wenn auch schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen. Ich hatte ein Zimmer nach hinten am Berghang dort war es sehr ruhig. Der Personal war freundlich. Frühstück war nicht inklusive, kostet extra. Parkplätze sind frei und genügend vorhanden. Was positiv ist man dann das direkt am Hotel anschließende Fitnesscenter als Hotelgast umsonst benutzen. Das Hotel hat eine outside pool. Internet ist frei für Hotelgäste über Wi-Lan oder eine Feststation.

“Good airport area hotel” Decided to stay one night by the airport and used priceline to get a room and ended up with the doubletree at a good rate! The hotel is pretty big but the location next to the airport is great. I asked for a room in the tower and the room was spacious with a nice king bed and a balcony that overlooked the airport. The views of the airplanes taking off was great! There are a few restaurants around the hotel area and you can also easily walk to the airport should you want to.

“Sheraton 4 Points Mag Mile--a Keeper” We go to Chi-Town every Thanksgiving so we have stayed at several downtown hotels. The Sheraton Mag Mile 4 Points was a nice hotel and I would recommend. Great location, a block off Mag Mile and close to bunches of restaurants. Room was well appointed and had microwave and frig which always comes in handy. Beds were fine, but I didn't notice anything "special" about them. Staff was courteous and always looked up and said hello. I had prepaid reservations well in advance and had asked for a room w/ a street view ... but didn't get one. That would be my only complaint w/ the hotel -- it is only 8 floors and where it is located there would be few rooms w/ a view.
“Pretty good but rooms were tiny” Nice staff, very good restaurant in lobby, nice gym, but very very small rooms by a noisy street

“One Of The Best In The City” Have stayed in over a dozen hotels in San Francisco. Must say that this is one of the best properties! Read some other reviews about noise, well it is a city and with any good economy you get a bit of noise. This property certainly isnt any noisier than the others in town. As for cleanliness, location, and staff it is 5 star all the way! I will be back. Be sure to grab breakfast at the Grove cafe 3rd & Mission! It is 1/2 a block from the hotel.

“The Monaco is First Rate” We stayed at the Monaco for four days the middle of May. We had never stayed in a Klimpton hotel but booked the Monaco based on customer reviews. We were pleased with our decision. From the doorman to the desk clerk to the bellman all were friendly and helpful. There was a real effort to make guests feel welcome. Our room was first class. The bed was very comfortable as were the the linens. The closet was bigger than most hotels. The bathroom was clean and the towels thick. We both liked the shower and never had a problem with hot water running out. The television had an adequate number of channels and had good reception. We were on the fifth floor above Wabash but had no problem with street noise. I would have preferred an in-room coffee maker but there was Starbucks coffee in the lobby every morning. A selection of newspapers in the lobby included the Chicago Tribune, the Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times. USA Today was at your door in the morning. The location of the Monaco is a plus, It's one block off Michigan and a short walk across the river to the Magnificent Mile.
