We will look for a Klimpton property on future trips and the Monaco when we make it back to Chicago

“Nice Hotel” I stayed at this hotel for a conference, and I was completely satisfied. It had the nice bonuses of most Marriott's these days: really comfortable beds, good front desk service, nice hotel bar. The room I was in was a little bit small for my liking (as was the bathroom), but nothing was wrong with it. Very clean hotel. I second the comment made about needing more elevators-- I, too, had to wait quite a long time to get down from the 36th floor in the morning. Also, they shouldn't have charged for wireless internet, but I paid for it anyways. Nice lobby to "people watch"-- very bustling. Overall really nice hotel, would definately stay here again!

“Beautiful property in Downtown Dallas” My family traveled to Dallas to attend the State Fair and wanted to stay in the downtown area. We do subscribe to the Omni loyalty program and have stayed at a number of Omni hotels in the past. This was a beautiful hotel inside and out. The lobby is very contemporary and had a fireplace wall that was very pretty and useful since there was a cold snap during our visit. We had a king room which was not huge, but the perfect size for us. We loved the artwork in the room highlighting Dallas landmarks. The TV in the bathroom mirror was a surprise and allowed us to keep up with football games even while getting ready. The staff were extremely nice, especially the concierge that helped us with Dart Rail maps and directions on how to take the rail to the fair. We were not there for a convention, but the hotel is attached to the convention center which seems like it would be great if you were there for that purpose. It is only 3 blocks to the red line Dart Rail at Union Station and only a little further to get on the green line and others at the West End Station. We were walking distance to the JFK landmarks and West End. We will definitely stay here again.

“Love the hotel, love the rooms....” This hotel is absolutely lovely. The history and beauty of this hotel are evident when you walk thru the doors. The rooms aren't large but they are clean, comfortable and super nice. The Old City Hall is across the street and everything is right there in walking distance. The only negative, if you really consider it a negative, is that the music in the lounge was not appropriate for the locale. A nice jazz, classical or soft rock would've worked but Tool and Linkin Park (rock)?? Otherwise...the staff is fabulous and the hotel is simply beautiful.

“Good Business Hotel” This hotel is an atrium-style Embassy Suites property typical of those built in the 1980s. You have the rooms opening onto interior walkways that surround a large three-sided atrium tower with waterfalls, dining area, and glass elevators. The rooms have been renovated at some point and were fine, if nothing fancy (but hey, you are staying beside an airport!). This hotel seems to be executing everything well. The shuttle to and from the airport was great and convenient. Staff was very helpful. Although I was not paying top dollar for my room, they gave me an upgrade without my asking, and they took care of a couple of business and shipping needs. Everyone was cheerful and helpful. There is a business center. The internet worked fine. Although I did not use it, parking is free. They have a decent exercise facility. I did not really use the evening reception or the morning breakfast, but several people did. All in all, I thought it was a very good value--better than many limited service hotels you can find. I would not hesitate to stay here again or to recommend this hotel.

“gentilezza e cortesia” Sono appena rientrata dal mio soggiorno in USA e devo dire che pur andando a NY almeno 2 volte l'anno questa è la prima volta che sono contenta al 100% della sistemazione. Personale gentilissimo, camere spaziose, bagno perfetto, tutto NUOVO ( cosa non da poco a NY). Lo consiglio vivamente!

“Small hotel in a nice location” This was our second stay at the Elan, and it was just as pleasant as the first visit. The hotel is within walking distance of nice restaurants and shopping. The surrounding residential areas appear upscale and safe. A nice touch in the Elan is that the room doors have slow closings, such that doors do not slam on their own. Thus the hotel is relatively quiet, unless there is loud talking outside your door. Worth mentioning is that internet access is free, but parking is not. And there are few safe alternatives for parking that would cost less. With free parking I would give this hotel 5 stars.

“Nice Staff, But Some Problems” We stayed at the Mission Valley Sheraton for two nights after booking it for $105/night on Priceline. Although the staff was uniformly helpful and friendly, and none of what happened was their fault, we had a very troubled stay and probably would not stay there again. First of all, I don't care for the Mission Valley location. It is conveniently located to a lot of attractions, but I find it very sterile and prefer to stay in the Del Mar area, or even downtown. The worst thing that happened was when we exited a side door to go get dinner one night, a huge snake was coiled right next to the door. It seemed to be almost 5 feet long. This of course was not the hotel's fault, but I have no idea whether this is a common occurrence or not (probably not). There are hills around the property and I guess there are snakes in the hills. Anyway, suffice it to say I almost had a heart attack! Also, we had to call housekeeping three times - once the toilet wasn't working, once there was no hairdryer in the room, and once to have the batteries in the remote control replaced. That's a lot of calls to housekeeping for a two-night stay. I don't want to put anyone off from this hotel, because the odds are you would have a nice stay. The hotel itself and the room was nice and everything that happened to us probably would not happen to you.

“Great hotel - boutique feel in a fun location” I typically enjoy Kimpton hotels. In boston, I like the nine zero (beacon hill) and the Hotel Marlowe in Cambridge (both Kimpton properties). Eventi is much larger than I expected - 23 floors about 10 blocks south of Bryant Park. The location is interesting - with lots of hand bag shops, just block from fun Korean restaurants, and a short cab ride to Chelsea Market or High Line Park. The one bedroom suite was modern, beautiful, with floor to ceiling windows and a huge bathroom (rain shower and separate soaking tub). Wine reception is always nice and the folks at Eventi were all extremely helpful. I travelled with my wife and daughter. It's OK for a family, but better suited for a couple. The area is pretty mixed -but that is what I was looking for. It's 10 miinutes to Bryant Park and there is a lot of action, import/export stores, hand bag stores, and other fun things directly outside of the hotel. Great views of the Empire State Building, great service, and a fun location. The pull out sofa was not very comfortable and they didn't have any cots...so my daughter didn't sleep great.

“Love The Surrey” The hotel has the perfect location on the Upper East Side for museum lovers like me. Within blocks of The Met and The Frick, the hotel is also just a block away from one of the entrances to Central Park, and walking distance to the Guggenheim and the Whitney. Service is impeccable, with the concierge, front desk and bell staff always polite and responsive. I never had to follow-up or try to chase down a response to my request. Housekeeping came twice a day and did a wonderful job. Turn-down service was greatly appreciated with bottles of water and choclate-dipped madelines. Stayed in a Grand Deluxe Room and loved it. It was a nice-sized corner room with beautiful furnishings, marble bathroom, and plenty of closet space. The very comfortable bed and awesome shower pressure are enough to make me return. Please make sure you stay at The Surrey when visiting New York City.

“Excellent location, first rate service!” I ́m travelling to San Francisco on a monthly base and decided to try the Campton Place (usually stay at the Omni) for a five night stay. What a great experience! I got exactly the room I requested with a great view and a windowseat. The location of the hotel is unbeatable - and quiet! Room was elegant and spacy, the bed extremly comfortable. Tried the hotel restaurant and can only praise food and service. The concierge (Maria) also deserves highest praise. My only suggestion: Provide a tea- and coffeemaker in the rooms. Otherwise, a perfect stay with very polite and extremly personal service. M. Morawietz

“A little less than expected” We stayed at this hotel in Boston because we had enough Gold Passport points to get a free night, otherwise, we wouldn't have because the going rate of $259 per night was way beyond our budget. When we arrived, we were presented with the opportunity to either valet park with in-and-out privileges for $46 per day or just use the public parking for $36 per 24 hour period. We elected to save some money by using the public parking because we did not plan to drive around the city. Otherwise, if you do plan to, the valet parking is definitely a better deal. We had no problem finding parking, but were confused when we got off of the elevator to the hotel. There were several options of where to go but no clear directions to the hotel. Eventually we figured it out, but were a little discouraged that we had to take another set of elevators to get to your room...just a little inconvenient if your just trying to get out of the hotel. Otherwise, the entrance, lobby and hallways of the hotel were very nice. The staff was almost overly perky and actually asked the same questions more than once. Overall, good though. We ended up on the 21st floor was provided some pretty decent views. The room was nice enough but nothing spectacular. If I was actually paying the regular rate, I would have been disappointed. The most disappointing part was the bathroom. Although at first glance it looked nice, once I sat down on the toilet, I noticed that there was white paint splattered all over the dark wood portions of the sink/vanity. Then when I jumped in the shower, the grout was clearly discolored. From the ceiling to about half way down the wall, it was white grout, then all of a sudden turned dark gray. It almost appears that they started re-grouting with a different color and never finished but I'm not sure if that's the case. They have a decent bar area but the drinks (of course) are pretty over priced. In the middle of the night, it got hot in our room for some reason so I called the front desk. The offered to have engineering take a look at the unit and also provide a fan. They brought the fan up within minutes and also reset our AC which seemed to have fixed the problem. Overall, I would say that we had a good experience considering we paid nothing, but I must say the bathrooms at the Holiday Inn that we stayed at the night before were cleaner than there's. I would definitely not have paid the full price to stay there.

“Dated, dirty and overpriced” Stayed two nights. Picked this since it was close to my business meeting. Carpet in room was filthy and stained. Room was large but had whirlpool tub in the room, not the bathroom. At least it had Starbucks. Not worth 449 per night.

“A good value adjacent to a ritzy area.” The Galleria section of Houston is a busy hub of corporate and high-end retail activity, and many of the local hotel options can be pretty pricey. This property is located just outside the Galleria district, which is reflected in the more reasonable rates. It’s still a very convenient location; it was less than a 15 minute drive from the hotel to my company’s Galleria office. It’s not in the best neighborhood I’ve ever seen, but it’s not all that bad, either. They do offer gated parking for guests for that extra piece of mind. Check-in and check-out were efficient and cordial. The complimentary breakfast area was well-maintained and featured a different hot egg and meat item each day. My room was certainly large enough, the plumbing, air conditioning and appliances were all in good working order, and the bed was very comfortable. The only downside was that my room’s entry door was not flush to the door frame, so I could hear whatever was going on in the corridor quite clearly. The hotel was undergoing renovations during my latest stay, so perhaps that will be corrected in the future. One nice touch (especially in hot, humid Houston) is that they offer ice water in the lobby throughout the day. In the afternoon they put out fresh-baked cookies. This is the second time I’ve stayed at this property, and both times I found it very suitable for my needs (and my company’s budget).

“Grand Hyatt Seattle has it all...” ... We were greatly impressed during our stay at the Grand Hyatt in Seattle, WA. Design, technology, and service converge to create an entirely enjoyable experience for guests. When one enters the guestroom, it is as if one is entering into a luxurious apartment, complete with a doorbell and foyer. The bathroom is bigger than some hotel rooms, with a glass-enclosed shower and a separate, deep bath perfect for soaking after a long day's worth of attending conference sessions or sight seeing. The rooms are also fully automated, yet the wood and stone furniture and accents in an almost Frank Lloyd Wright style sustain a discreet warmth. Service was personal and excellent, as well. Our only complaint was that the Hyatt in its literature and web page had advertised free high speed internet; they were charging 9.95/day when we checked in. This seemed slightly like bait and switch, especially when the binder listing the amenities stated that internet access was free. The least they could have done was waive the charge for those who booked before the fee was instituted. However, being able to print documents from one's laptop in the room directly to a printer, and being able to pick up the documents at the front desk easily (at 50 cents a page), was quite convenient for those who do not have a mobile printer. This is a terrific place to stay for business and pleasure.

“Très pratique” Situé sur un axe routier, proche de l'aéroport, grand complexe calme, chambre spacieuse, très copieu petit déjeuner et parking donc parfait pour y résider avant de partir de LAX ou en arrivant sur LA.

“A Unique "Nautical" type Hotel” The Maritime Hotel is located in the Chelsea/Meatpacking area of Lower Manhattan. It was once the headquarters of the Maritime Institute, where sailors could stay while in port in NY. After falling on harder times, it was purchased by a Japanese firm several years ago, and they renovated it and took back the original Maritime name. It’s well located near a subway station and across from the Chelsea Market, where you can grab some breakfast or lunch, and have some great people-watching time. We stopped in for a drink in the Maritime’s lobby last summer, and loved the cozy, welcoming atmosphere of the place. It’s a great lobby. So when we were coming back for Christmas, we decided to stay here. This is not your standard Hilton. The rooms are small, and fitted out in a nautical style, with compact and well organized nooks and crannies. Each room has one queen sized bed, and a 5 foot, round porthole style window. We had a “View” room, which had a sliver of a view of the Hudson between buildings. It was extremely clean and well maintained. Service was excellent and friendly. We also had control of the temperature in the room. Our room had a mini-bar/fridge, DVD player, and a flat screen TV. It did not have a coffee maker, but they will bring one up at no cost if you request it. With the limited space, if you didn’t need one, it’s better to not have it taking up space on the desk area. Ice is available from Room Service. They also supplied ear plugs, which was very thoughtful, because a) you’re in the city that doesn’t sleep, and b) the original round windows don’t offer a lot of sound proofing. With the ear plugs, we had no problem with street noise, and we were on the 9th floor. The entire hotel seems to be on a low-light regime. There was plenty of light to read in the room, but the hallways were very dim, as you might expect on a ship. The lobby and restaurants were also dim. Our only complaint was that the bed was very soft and saggy. We like a firm bed, and this was difficult. If you enjoy a non-traditional, yet comfortable and well-designed hotel, this might be right for you.

“Nice hotel, boring location” The hotel in itself if very nice, but the location in downtown Dallas must be the most boring one can imagine. There is no life, no people on the streets, it is just a deserted desert! Sure, there are some nice restaurants around, and walking distance to the arts centre as well as the JFK sites, but we still left Dallas with a very depressed feeling. It is the nightmare of all cities! Further, in a place like Dallas in the summer, one really needs a pool, and therefore I would easily pick another hotel, in another location.

“Must of been adopted” I'm surprised this hotel is part of the Conrad chain. I stayed at the Conrad Tokyo, which was outstanding, and Conrad Hong Kong, dated, but a classic. The Conrad Chicago definitely has some pros; PROS Nice location, with easy access to Michigan Ave. A beautiful lobby. Refurbished rooms have 42'' screen TV's Bath tub, although mine was visibly dirty Bed, pillows, linens are great CONS Room I had 1205 was small. I was told it was an upgrade since I'm a Diamond Member. When I asked about breakfast, I was told I could have either a room upgrade or a credit of $14 for breakfast. I took the room upgrade. They did send a $14 certificate up to my room, which was a very nice gesture. Heating/Cooling system is antiquated/terrible. Final words; If you are used to Four Seasons or Park Hyatt then you may be disappointed. Otherwise, it is a nice option, but not of same caliber as overseas Conrads I've stayed at.

“Hotel OK, Location terrible” I stayed at the Seaport Hotel because I ran in the Boston Half Marathon (Memorial Day weekend), and the starting line was just outside. It's a typical large convention hotel. If you've got a function to attend at the Boston World Trade Center, or at the hotel (they seem to do a lot of weddings), then ok, you've got to stay there. But for touring Boston, this place is not where you want to be. Too far off on the periphery. The check-in is ok but impersonal. Room is satisfactory. Room service breakfast was ok but not worth the $35 (I had no choice that day, because I had to leave early to line up for the race). Bar was good, and they made an excellent gimlet. Overall, don't come here if you are looking for a great Boston vacation/touring experience. Only stay here if you need to attend a function at the Trade Center.

“W consistency - a good thing” The W hotels are very consistent from city to city. When you're traveling for work, as I was on this trip, that's a good thing. It means I know the front desk will always make me feel special, there will be good Internet access (although I'll always curse when they make me pay for it at these hotel prices!), the room service will be tasty, and I'll get a great night's sleep. This W in particular was extra spacious, with a couch/coffee table sitting area. It's my second time staying there and I'd gladly do it again next time work sends me to Seattle.

“Enjoyable!” Got a great deal on this hotel on Hotwire. Boy, was I lucky! As soon as we pulled up, two valet attendants came to the car to welcome us. We explained that we were just checking in and not staying as we were heading out to dinner. Upon walking into the lobby, the area was clean and nice. The reservation desk had 3 large bowls of candy waiting. What a nice touch! Desk clerk was very nice. The room was nice too. Great linens and nice toiletries. Tv was cool, although it needed to be higher because you couldn't see the bottom of the screen if you were laying in bed, but we didn't go there to watch tv anyway! Our room overlooked the ballpark which was awesome. We went up to Altitude Bar on the 22nd floor. What a nice view! They were having a Pajama Party that night but unfortunately we already had plans or we would have loved to attend. Slept like a baby in the beds. Next morning it was Starbucks in the coffee pot! Shower has the nice rounded shower curtain and the bathroom was nice with a sliding door. When I went to check out the next morning, the clerk said I was charged for valet service, which I didn't use. He promptly reversed the charges and apologized. What a cool place this is. I cannot wait to go back!

“Beautiful views of the City” We requested a room on a high-numbered floor, and pretty cool - our king bed faced the window to view the city lights (even when it was raining) and to wake up to clear skies the next day. One side of the building will let you see the Bay Bridge. Standard Courtyard setup: large room with extra-wide sofa chair/ottoman, well-lit desk, mini-fridge, and large flat-screen TV; tall showerhead with good water pressure; comfortable bed with extra pillows. Marriott restaurant/bar was on the main floor, and a Starbucks was also in the lobby (we did not use any and went instead to a recommended place by the staff that was close by). Valet parking was $45/day with in/out privileges, and attendants retrieved car quickly.

“Great lobby & front desk staff, dated room” My family with young children stayed for one night. We arrived early after a long road trip. Tim at the front desk made sure that we could check in as soon as a room was cleaned and ready. He gave us excellent customer service and seemed very happy and accommodating. Upgraded lobby area is functional and lobby restrooms were immaculate. Rear patio is well appointed. Sleeping rooms are in need of updating but were clean. Cracker barrel next door is convenient for meals. McDonald's, Wendys , etc. Are across the main Hwy (Butler Blvd). We booked through priceline and got excellent rate.

“Nice Manhattan Hotel if you can get a deal” My wife and I spent 5 days between Christmas and New Year's at the Intercontinental Barclay. The hotel itself is a little older, but still nice. Definitely a different feel from boutique hotels in New York and large chains. The real bright spot at the Barclay is the staff. We received excellent service from the bellman to the front desk and on. We had the deluxe King, so the room was very large and appointed in an older style, but still very nice. The bathroom is small, but is also more than enough to fit your needs and has excellent toilettries. This hotel has an excellent Midtown East location, just a few short blocks to Grand Central and many nice restaurants close by. I highly recommend using the hotel's concierge as they can steer you anywhere you want to go. This is grand hotel, but don't pay the full rack price, do your research and get a deal.

“location, location, location only the beginning, beginning, beginning” General Manager Wes Tyler recently referred to the Chancellor as a “simple hotel in a great location.” Me thinks Wes is too modest. Certainly the Chancellor enjoys an unbeatable “Five Star” location on Union Square and the property itself is more of a three star hotel, longer on historic charm (the wide moldings, original bathtubs, wrought iron banisters) than luxury. But simple? There is nothing simple about assembling a staff who take such obvious pride in their work as evidenced by keeping the place spotless and extending themselves beyond the call of duty to provide helpful suggestions about nightlife, restaurants, and transportation. There is nothing simple about the extra touches that make a stay here enjoyable—fresh coffee and cookies 24/7, “four star” sized towels, pillows and linens in a three star hotel, free wifi in the rooms, and in-room umbrellas in case of rain, or the option of a free newspaper In the morning from a menu including the SF Chronicle, USA Today, the Wall Street Journal or the NY Times. There is nothing simple about the manager asking guests their preferences and selecting a room suited to individual tastes. Or about the bowl of hard candy, the welcome bottle of local wine, or the rubber ducky in the bath. These touches require a certain obsession with being the best hotel possible, within the limits of the hotels architecture and age. This commitment to excellence, perhaps commonplace when the Chancellor was built, has become a rarity in our time. The hotel is old but is by no means rundown. The paint our room was fresh and the carpet was new. Furniture has been updated. But it is not the Marriott or Ritz Carlton. As Wes frequently writes...do not stay here if you are looking for a luxury hotel. Rooms here are adequately sized but not spacious. Our room featured a queen bed, writing desk, small end table flank. The walk-in closet was huge. Since we were able to place all of our bags in the closet, we had more useable space in the room itself. Bathrooms are charming but not very large. There is no air conditioning. Do stay here if you are looking for lots of value for not much money...an immaculate room....and welcoming staff....and lots of little touches..... The Chancellor is rated by TA readers as one of the best value hotels around. Given the prices for other hotels in the heart of SF, we wholeheartedly agree. We spent more for dinner for two than for our room! Wes, thanks to you and your staff for helping to make our trip special and for a reminder of the real difference a commitment to excellence can make.

“Happy with the Grand” I've stayed at this property several times in the past year and have had very good experiences. First off, request a room facing the courtyard. It's much quieter on the inside of the building - especially with the large apartment complex that's under construction across the street. Can definitely be a nuisance if you're on the side of the building facing 24th Street NW. The workers get going at about 7 am. Unlike some below, I can't hold it against the hotel (it's not the Grand's fault that they're building across the street); that said, make sure you ask to be away from that side of the building when you reserve. The new construction should be wrapping up later in 2005 and should not be a problem after that point. The rooms themselves are modern and clean - and the Heavenly Bed is all it's cracked up to be. Quite comfortable. You just sink right in. Certainly makes it harder to get up in the morning!! Unlike several travelers in previous reviews, I've always had good service from the staff at the Grand. Very friendly and responsive. I expect to be back at the Westin Grand often - in fact, have a reservation for next week!

“Only Fair” My husband booked the room through Amex Fine Hotels for two nights for my birthday. While the service was excellent (champange and fresh baked cookies upon check-in) the room was less than stunning. We found the decor a bit "dated". The wallpaper in the bathroom was a very 80's orange/gold stripe. Nothing about the room said "luxury". Overall, I felt the hotel was on par with nicer properties in the Westin/W chain but nothing to write home about. I would not stay here again.

“Horrible Stay and Horrible Meeting” Booked a meeting with 50+ sleeping rooms and an all day meeting at the hotel. They screwed up the rooming list (and blamed us until they found they updated list that they never entered). Told participants they didn't have reservations, hotel was full, they would have to find somewhere else to stay. Some were checked in and then found that their rooms were dirty and never cleaned after the last guest checked out. The sleeping rooms were musty and old. Bathroom fixtures all chipped and stained. As previous posters have said, the air conditioning leaves alot to be desired. I had it set to 60 and it never, ever got close to that. The AT&T wifi in the rooms was down more than it was up. (They blamed AT&T). The toilet in my room had a dripping noise that didn't stop for 2 days. For the meeting in the ballroom, the food was the only positive. Breakfast and lunch were good. That being said, the room was a mess when they set it up. Several of the linens on the tables were stained and dirty. Overall, can't believe how bad this hotel was. Not only was the facility disgraceful, the level of service was unbelievably bad. At every corner the hotel staff didn't care. They said it was our fault or just simply moved on. Only after speaking with the hotel manager did I see any results. (That being said, I saw her in the hallway the next day and she averted eye contact and didn't even acknowledge me or ask how our meeting was going.) They did mention they are about to renovate. That might help the facility - but they need to renovate the staff a bit as they were rude beyond belief. They promised a bunch of Starwood points for the meeting and all the problems. We'll see. I'm not holding my breath.

“Perfect New York Holiday Experience” My husband and I stayed at the Waldorf = Astoria for a long weekend in mid-December. It was wonderful! The hotel is beautiful and the service is world class. Although our room was one of the "small" ones, it was still a decent size for a city hotel. Big windows, comfy bed, and very quiet. It did not have a room safe, which is something I now expect everywhere. The temperature control for the shower was either hot or cold, no in between. The hotel bars were very nice and, for NYC, the drinks were moderately priced. Room service is expensive, but there is a Starbucks on property and plenty of restaurants nearby. If you are looking for an elegant experience, this is the place!

“lovely location, but.....” Spent three nights here at beginning of October. The suite was lovely and the location perfect. However, I was trying to sleep on the lounge sofabed one night and the ice machine along the corridor developed a fault which caused it to bleep loudly - just like an alarm clock. I informed reception and they sent someone to sort it out the next day. As always in this design of hotel (Embassy suites are the same) the sound proofing in the lounge area is non existent. Fortunately the live music from the bar area finished at 10.30pm so the staff seem aware of this problem. As the hotel is next to the wedding island, I would avoid this place on Saturdays, when the place gets taken over by the inevitable wedding, and you won`t be able to sit on the terrace overlooking the riverwalk. If we get back to San Antonio, I`d probably opt for the Homewood suites again next time. They are almost next door and slightly cheaper. (and you get free brekkie and manager`s cocktail hour!) I chose the Contessa this time because I wanted a swim in the evenings, but never managed this as the pool was always full of kids.
“まあまあです♪” 普通のチェーンモーテルです。値段が安かったので宿泊しましたが、特に可もなく不可もなくって感じです。ネルだけであればも音大ないと思います。部屋にドライヤーがなく、フロントで借りました。 サンディエゴの有名行列レストランのphills bbqや、スポーツアリーナ、オールドタウンが近くにあります。

“Good Courtyard, A Few Quirks” Overall this is a good property in the Boston Area - reasonably priced by Boston terms yet close to downtown and Logan. There is a big shopping area close by with restaurant choices (mostly chains). The room was comfortable and well appointed with a flat screen TV, in room coffee, couch, work desk - the things you would expect at any Courtyard. In terms of the quirks - the room was not as clean as I would expect. There was a hair band from a former guest on the floor and dust on the desk. As a Marriott Rewards member, my profile ensures I never get a room by the elevator - except this time - I was right next to the elevator...and the ice machine. This particular elevator makes an unusally loud ring when it arrives at the floor, so I recommend if you stay here that you get a room away from the elevators. Overall, I'd stay here again, but would insist on a better room location.

“Fine for one night airport stay!” I got this hotel through a discount hotel service. Parking was ample and worked for us. We wanted a king room, but they only had doubles left however that was not a big deal. Room was nice, very clean and had a great view. The room smelled nice, furnishings were clean and the bed had nice sheets and was comfy. The wallpaper needs to be replaced, however...the location, comfort and cleanliness makes it perfect for a one night stop over. Soooo close to Love Field too!

“Nicest budget motel ive ever stayed at. GREAT stay. Brand New Property!” First off, this property is only about a year old so its one of the nicest budget motels you'll find in Houston. Ive stayed at 4 different Super 8's on business trips in the past month and this one is the BEST ive ever been to. (Including other motels ive stayed at.) The price is great (I paid $50 per night) and the location is extremely convenient (right off the highway). Nice new property, clean comfortable rooms, free continental breakfast, very nice pool/hot tub and patio area. and great staff. (NOTE: I saw that people had complained about highway noise. There IS highway noise but its not all that bad. Its not like people are honking and making a ruckus while flying down the highway. Its I-45 thats right outside so all you hear is cars passing by. The a/c and tv drowns it out for the most part and didnt bother me at all. and im a light sleeper.) The rooms were equipped with upgraded everything and had a nice design factor with the choice of patterns and colors. I got a King room for a few nights and it had everything I needed and then some. The room itself is somewhat small but when your just relaxing and sleeping in your room, what more space do you need?The size and everything that was in it, made it feel like a little studio apartment. Well, minus a full kitchen. There was a huge and comfortable king size bed with clean linens and 4 pillows. The matteress was firm, as i like them, and didnt have that slept in feel. (The bed in the last Super 8 I stayed in before this one had an indention on one side where other guests had slept over the years.) Above the bed, is a huge picture of Houston, which also acts as a sort of headboard and gave the room a really modern feel. The furniture was all modern designed, like Ikea, and was in really good shape. 2 side tables with nice modern table lamps,alarm clock, phone, a big entertainment center with a microwave and mini fridge built into it, with clothes drawers on the sides and underneath. The entry way had a small desk with a rolling desk chair and lamp, and near that was a small coffee table and a loveseat for lounging. The bathroom was spotless clean and equipped with a nice stone tile floor, stone design shower stall, clean white bathtub, nice soft bathroom towels and cloths, a wall mounted iron, and coffee maker in the dressing area counter. All rooms have wall mounted 40" flatscreen TV's which almost blew my mind when I walked in. almost every other Super 8 that I have ever been too has had an old school 27" or 32" tube tv with about 7 channels of nothing. This one was a full on high definition Dynex 40" lcd and it rocked. mounted above the entertainment center, I was able to connect my laptop via HDMI cable (that i keep in my work bag) to stream movies and games while I stayed. Speaking of streaming, they have free WiFi as well. and its FAST! Great download speed and upload speeds for smooth internet cruising for work or play. I got a great signal in my room and had no issues connecting from the password I was given when I checked in. All Super 8's offer free continental breakfast now and this was one of the better ones that I have tried. They are all basically the same but depending on the franchise owners some of the better items can be left off the menu. while all offer cereal, milk, juice, coffee, toast, and muffins. this one also had fresh fruit (apples, oranges, bananas), donuts and large bagels, and a texas shaped waffle iron for fresh waffles from a pre-made batter mix dispenser. the waffles turn out huge and they were pretty good. The staff was great and contributed to my great stay by getting me checked in quick, providing me with information on the area, and cleaning up my room in between nights. The property as a whole was very nice and I will DEFINITELY be staying there again. this super 8 blows all the other motels in the area away! the price is insane for the quality you get. usually, if you pay cheap prices, you get a cheap quality place. this was quite the exception. Great stay.

“Great hotel in the heart of Chicago” I have stayed here several times and it is my hotel of choice in Chicago. The staff goes out of their way to be helpful and friendly. Internet and breakfast are included, making this a great value compared to other Chicago hotels. The rooms are spacious and clean, and the beds are comfortable.

“Fantastic renovation! Highly recommended” I stayed recently and loved it. The recent renovation makes this feel like a W rather than a Westin, which is a good thing! Very contemporary, comfortable rooms and public spaces. The lobby is beautiful and inviting. There was nothing in the room, including the carpet, that I would not put in my own apartment. How many hotels can you say that about? The bathroom has a terrific fogless wall mirror, great for shaving right after you shower, and a nice wood and granite counter. The Westin shower curtain rod, which arcs out away from the tub, is a welcome relief from brushing up against the curtain. I was upgraded to a high-floor room with two views, very nice. The sushi restaurant downstairs, Osushi, was hip and delicious. Room service is very good, too, and quick. Having a full Starbucks downstairs is great, too, as is access to the upscale mall across the street via skybridge.

“Large Modern Rooms, Great Service, Perfect Location” When you arrive at the Bryant Park, it doesn't look like much. I have to say I was initially disappointing by the lack of a real lobby. But seeing the size of the rooms and realizing how incredibly convenient the location, it ultimately did not really matter. The building is grand. It's the former American Standard Building/ AMERICAN RADIATOR BLDG. Located 1 block from 5th ave shopping, a few blocks from Times Square and the Theater District, across the street from the NY Public Library and right near the subway line. There's an ice skating rink in the adjacent park in the winter (with the Xmas fair huts) and outdoor eateries in the summer. Our 1 bedroom Bryant Park suite overlooked the park and winter skating rink. Rooms were modern...one could really say sparse. Not a photo or piece of artwork anywhere. Large kind bed in the bedroom while the sitting room had a couch, day bed and room for an additional roll-away. There was also a 6 person dining table which went unused on our stay. With all the space, the room design could have allowed for more drawers and shelves for staying organized. The only noise we heard of other guests the entire week was the rolling up or down of someone's window shade a couple of mornings. Weird. Other than that, silence from the other rooms. A huge plus on our scale. The bathroom was clean and contemporary with good quality towels (some were so new that the fuzz came off while toweling off after a shower). I wasn't thrilled with the products offered but that was a personal preference and shouldn't make or break a stay. For a room this size, double sinks would have been appreciated. Free drinks and apps M-F 5-6 in the Cellar bar was a very nice touch. We did try Koi which was neither here nor there for the price. Not a disaster but nothing to write home about. The best spot for breakfast was an organic bakery cafe about 4 doors west on 40th. Great granola and hot chocolate. Entire staff was friendly, helpful and personable. Our only hitch was as we checked in, we were asked to sign a no-smoking commitment. We were thrilled as we are not smokers, hate the smell and would be thrilled to be in a no smoking hotel. When we arrived at our original room, there was a lingering cigarette aroma. "A smoker has been here", we thought..."it will dissipate." We unpacked and settled in. As the hour passed, the smell got stronger and stronger...even in the shower. On our way out we mentioned it to the front desk fearing that we would be accused. The staff was "on it" and immediately offered to move while they investigated. Although it really was an inconvenience on our part, we agreed. We did not experience any smoke during they rest of our stay so it was obviously a fluke and beyond their control. However, I do feel that we should have been offered something for compensation/acknowledgment of our inconvenience (a bottle of wine, a breakfast, etc.) but none was offered. We did have a wonderful stay and we would highly recommend the Bryant Park

“You should avoid this hotel if at all possible -- even with $99 rate” This hotel had service on par with what you would see in a bad hotel in a third world country. I would have rather have slept on a park bench and came very close to leaving for home, but did not due to family member intervation. This hotel had a horrible front desk staff and made errors on our bill to the extent that we had to go to the desk three times before we checked out. Our parking ticket was never vailidated and we waited 15 minutes for the parking attendents to open the gate. The parking attendents were very rude.

“Labor Day Oasis” Stayed at this stylish hotel in downtown over Labor Day weekend with friends. Despite the busy area and influx of tourists, our room was quiet and comfortable. The hotel staff was very kind, especially when I needed some assistance after my wallet had been stolen at a nearby bar :( They were more than willing to let me use their computer at the front desk to file a police report and print out a needed document. Unfortunately there are all kinds of tourist-trap restaurants nearby, but that's no fault of the hotel's. Also, the bathroom doesn't feel completely private when sharing a room with 3 other people, but the sliding door sure looks nice! Extra points for the lobby happy hour where we got to sample a drink before heading out for the evening.

“Great staff make a difference” I have been staying at Hyatts a lot lately, and one reason is the staff. The Hyatt downtown Houston was a good example. Kurt at the front desk was great - he went beyond my expectations, really wanting to make the stay pleasant and restful. Finding a nice room, and even sending up a welcome amenity because of my frequent status. Thanks Kurt! The building is older, but has been kept up well. Room was large and beautiful. My recommended hotel in downtown Houston.

“Nice but some frustrations” I wanted to love the Hilton, and in some ways, I did, but in others, we were disappointed. My husband and I just came back from enjoying two days there relaxing over New Year's, and there were positives. Our room was clean and large by city standards, but I agree with earlier posts that size of room is completely luck of the draw based on what I saw on the floor diagram. The bed was very comfortable, and the location of the hotel was great for being out and about in the city for First Night -- close enough to get there fast but far enough away to avoid the worst of the noise. The staff was great -- helpful and courteous, though we were disappointed that our request for an upper-floor room was not duly noted until we pointed it out, and then we were only put on floor 9 (of a 15 floor hotel). Our room maid was wonderful, however. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was fabulous -- a really good buffet though it was part of a package for us. Not cheap if you have to pay separately, but worth it. And that brings me to the negatives. The hotel nickels and dimes you with charges for things that in other hotels might be part of the high rate charged. Wireless internet is on a per-day charge, and if you instead decide that you'll just use the hotel's "Business Center," be prepared to pay a minimum of a $10 charge then $1 per minute after 10 minutes. This seemed ludicrous to us who just wanted to check our e-mail. The bottles of water in the room were available for a mere $4.50 each (we bought some of our own nearby for a lot less), and a $80 charge for dinner in the hotel bar when we only had a few drinks and two light entrees seemed really high, even by hotel restaurant standards. In general, it seemed that the four-star rating was not really warranted given how many of the little extras one expects at four-star locales involved extra charges here. In addition, there were some aging issues -- the sheet that had a hole along the edge where it was folded over on our bed; the scratchy towels that were too old to still be soft and fluffy; the slightly worn wood on the furniture like the arm chair and entertainment center. The room was also quite noisy, in part due to the expected city sounds, but also due to how easily we could here our loud neighbors across the hall as they came and went. It was not a bad experience -- in fact, we were quite happy when all was said and done. But with a little more inclusiveness in their rates and some upgrading of slightly aging fixtures, this hotel could more fully embody a four-star experience.
“Rooms were ok” Not bad, but not as good as Country Inn and Suites airport, Stayed at both, but Country Inn was nicer. La Quinta did not have a mini fridge.

“Hotel vecchio e da ristrutturare” L'hotel ha una buona posizione perché si trova a pochi passi dalla 5 strada. Tuttavia le camere sono davvero vecchie e sporche. Anche gli spazi comuni lasciano a desiderare. Considerando però che siamo a nyc può anche andare!!!

“Great place, great staff, great location!” I'll start by saying there is nothing bad I can say about this place. From the moment we arrived the entire staff was friendly and helpful. The room was great - super clean, well decorated, etc. We had our two children with us (3 1/2 yrs and 10 mos) and never felt like they weren't welcome even when my 3 year old was running around the lobby looking at all the decorations and touching everything! He thought it was great to have a bunk bed to sleep in (we had a 1 bedroom suite) and everything was so clean I had no problem letting our 10 month old crawl around on the floor. The hotel is right across from where the green city market sets up (weds and saturday), and a very short walk from the zoo. It's also only about a 20 min walk through nice neighborhoods to the Clybourn area (restaurants and shops). Highly recommended and will definitely stay here again!

“Adequate - good location, nice staff” My experience was consistent with many of the other reviews. I stayed recently for a few nights, and while I normally stay in the popular hotel chains, none were available then so went with this property. Pros - good location, some rooms have great view of the bridge, comfortable beds, front desk personnel/service Cons - NO air conditioning. This wouldn't normally matter in SFO, however, the week I was there was unseasonably hot and the room was stifling. The only alternative is to have the windows open through the night, however Van Ness is incredibly noisy so you have to put up with that. With the windows closed though, it does block a lot of street noise. Also, while the bathroom was clean, it is incredibly small and no room for Dopp kit etc.

“Hotel Metro... Great location!” We stayed at Hotel Metro November 20-23, 2006 while in NYC for the 80th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The hotel location is excellent, Macy’s is 1 block away (so close that you can see part of it from the hotel’s door)& 5th Ave. is in the opposite direction, full of shops, restaurants & of course Starbucks. Times Square is also with in walking distance, it’s about 7 blocks from the hotel but in NYC that’s nothing. There is also a subway stop less then 1 block away from the hotel. There are several restaurants next to the hotel, 2 Korean, an Irish Pub & a Subway (sandwich shop). For a good fast food lunch or dinner I’d suggest Chipotle (great Mexican/burritos) located around the corner from the hotel @ 5th Ave. & 34th St. Our hotel room was quite small even for NYC but it was comfortable & clean with a queen size bed, desk, chair, small table, TV & mini bar; the high ceilings in the room did give it a roomier feel. The main overhead lighting was florescent which I didn’t care for but turning on the 2 lights next to the bed fixed that. The bathroom was also small but clean, it was modern with a standing tile shower. One of the best room features was the free in room internet access, which is rare among most hotels. A business center with a computer & printer was also available, free to guests, though we didn’t use it as we had our laptop with us. The front desk staff were professional & friendly, they offered us a map of the area upon check-in & offered to hold our luggage when we checked out. A nice complementary breakfast was available between 6-11am, it consisted of cereals, fruit, yogurt, bagels, toast, pastries, oatmeal, tea & coffee; complimentary New York Times are available each morning at the front desk. There is a nice sitting room off of the lobby where guests can enjoy 24 hour tea & coffee (this is also the same room where breakfast is served in the morning). The roof top terrace was closed during our stay but from what I understand it’s a great bonus & provides an amazing view of the Empire State building which is within walking distance of the hotel. Hotel Metro is in a great location & met our needs, I would stay there again & recommend it to others. While in NYC I would also recommend the Vegetarian Soul food café Red Bamboo (140 W. 4th St.) & shopping in NOLITA/SOHO, esp at Yellow Rat Bastard (478 Broadway) it’s a great shop for fun, funky finds. Enjoy your stay in NYC!

“Close to subway lines, all the basics, great price” Hardly a five-minute walk to Herald Square's multiline (BDFNQRVW) subway & PATH station at Sixth Avenue and just a bit farther away from Penn Station's additional lines, the location was convenient for my tourism. It was just a couple short blocks to the Empire State Building and an easy walk to Times Square. Just like a La Quinta adjacent to an interstate highway, this hotel has all the basics, including a free breakfast buffet and a free wireless internet connection that was very, very easy to set up. I paid $125/night plus tax, which was very reasonable, compared with other Manhattan hotels I checked online. Check-in and check-out were quick and accurate. It was easy to store my bags on departure day since I checked out just before noon but didn't have a departing flight until that evening. Heat and water worked well in my room. Even though it faced the street, I didn't notice any noise. The room safe easily accommodated my laptop computer. Only one minor complaint: Electric outlets were a bit loose--my plugs tended to fall out of them rather than being gripped securely when I plugged them in. This was a repeat visit (my second time this year), and it would be tough for me to find a better hotel option in Manhattan for my next stay.

“Disappointing” I have stayed at Kimptons before and I like unique hotels. So, we thought we would move over here after our room block was up at a generic hotel we were staying at for a wedding. Bad idea. The first person that greeted us seemed really friendly and nice. Even though everyone around us was allowed to check-in, they told us we had to wait for a pet-free room. No big deal, we just checked our luggage and went on our way. When we came back around 6pm, we had a different person who was much less friendly and less on-the-ball. We had to make sure our room, this time, was the pet-free one we were waiting for. When we got to it, we realize it was very small, which we had expected. What we didn't expect was how run-down it was. The pain job was crappy - peeling and parts, painted on the tile in others. Our toilet paper holder had graffiti written on it, which, didn't go with the aesthetic so I don't think it was intentional, but you never know. Our pet and allergy free room had a not-so-allergy-friendly moldy bathroom (and not just little bits of mold in the shower, a giant splotch of mold on the wall - see photo). There were also lots of super annoying things - like the windows don't have screens. So, if you want to get air, you need to also let in 100 flying insects. Our bathroom door handle was falling off, so I kept getting nervous I was going to get locked in there forever. And, finally, the most annoying, we had a "Raid the Mini-Bar" certificate for being In Touch members. However, they locked our mini-bar. I think it's far more annoying to have a perk that doesn't work than than to not have a perk at all. Especially combined with everything else. We didn't book discount, we booked on the Kimpton website because we wanted a quality experience - this was certainly not it.

“Hotel ben servito a nord di Chicago” La struttura si trova a nord del centro, a circa un'ora dall'aeroporto di O'Hare. Pur non essendo in centro, è ben servito da autobus e metro. Si tratta di una vecchia casa signorile, ora adibita ad hotel. La nostra stanza non era grandissima, ma ben curata e ben arredata. La pulizia era ok, l'unica cosa che proprio non mi piace è la moquette, ma purtroppo quella si trova un po' in tutti gli hotel negli USA. L'hotel offre la colazione continentale, anche se non hanno una vera e propria sala (la colazione si fa nella hall), e dispone di un parcheggio a 22 usd a notte. Purtroppo noi non abbiamo trovato posto nel parcheggio, ma lì vicino ne abbiamo trovato uno pubblico ala stessa tariffa. Il wifi ha sempre funzionato bene, e il personale è sempre stato molto gentile.

“Alright, but not spectacular.” Having stayed - in the last year - at the Sanctuary and the Montage, I expected the Biltmore to be of the same caliber, given that it was in the same price range. Don't get me wrong - it was good, but not that good. Sure, the unique architecture of the "old building," both inside and out, is remarkable. The service is impeccable. However, the inside of the "new" buildings was not up to my expectations. I stayed in the Arizona building, built long after the original building, but a long time ago. The hallways reminded me of a run-of-the-mill Marriott. The "half-moon" lights down the hallway doubled as dead bug receptacles. The room was spacious and the furniture and appointments okay, but not plush. It really reminded me of an apartment I lived in 20 years ago: hard plastic sink and bathtub, '80's style light switches, and double-mirrored closet doors that won't stay on their tracks. The carpet had stains as did some of the chairs. And the sliding glass door to the outside (no balcony, just iron bars), had a shabby "afterthought" night lock that looked like "Uncle Bob" slapped up. In this era of "Spa Resorts," it seems like the emphasis is more on the spas and not so much on the facilities. (I had a similar impression of the Phoenician also.) Next time I go to Phoenix, I'll try the Ritz or Four Seasons (if they have locations in Phoenix).

“Only one drawback” The Peninsula is almost perfect. Simply beautiful hotel. We generally stay at the Four Seasons in Chicago and decided to try the Peninsula for a change. Staff is superb, rooms relatively spacious and location can't be beat. Only one negative. If you are seeking a quiet enviroment, the Peninsula may fall short. Our first room faced Michigan Aveneue and even on the 18th floor, the street noise was significant. Also, our room had a connecting door and the sounds from the room next us were annoying enough that I requested a room change. Staff handled the request quickly and professionally. Our new room faced Chicago Ave and was much better. I do understand that if you want to stay in the heart of a major metro area you will have noise. Although I will say that we've not had noise problems at the Four Seasons. And it borders Michigan Ave also. But overall the Peninsula is a real treat. Just as a sidebar, I didn't think the Shanghai Terrace was that good. It's ok but the food had too much msg.

“very pleasant surprise for a ramada” hotel is very well maintained and very clean. the room and bed are comfortable, and even slightly more modern-feeling than a usual ramada, i'd say. free parking, free wifi (which worked fine), and location is very near downtown (austin is small, it's just a short drive on the highway). staff was friendly and helpful, and price was amazing. i'd say this is a very good deal and i would stay again for sure. the main thing to stress is how clean & well-maintained it is. that's really the most important thing in the end. at the risk of providing too much information, i got some sort of food poisoning the night before my departure and was awake all night & slow getting out of the room the next day. the staff allowed me to check out a couple hours late without any charge, after i explained i was having a hard time getting going because of my nausea. that kind of sensitivity is appreciated and not forgotten. this hotel is doing a great job.

“Noisy poolside rooms” This was our second stay here, very convenient for all attractions on Hollywood Blvd. and right opposite the Grauman theatre and the new Hard Rock Cafe. Decorated in dark woods and lots of old hollywood style and history. On arrival we were checked in promptly and given a refurbished room in the poolside block which was very nicely decorated and clean. The room had a Lanai (terrace) but this was quite dark and the greenery was overgrown so it was not used. After going for a walk, we returned to the hotel and decided to have a drink and snacks at the poolside bar (bottle of wine, chicken tenders and some fries)where they were setting up for the Friday night pool party. Be prepared it's loud and if you are in the poolside rooms the music goes on until the small hours (3am). Fortunately we were so tired from our flight that we crashed at 11:30pm and only heard a couple of doors banging and girls shouting at around 2am. The following day we decided to lay by the pool ... NOTE this has to be booked the day before or early in the morning with the pool guy! There were "no free beds" available at 10 am!! We booked for the following morning and went out for the day. On our return they were setting up for another pool party which seemed to be for some college students, aparently the party people of Hollywood come here for the weekend pool parties. Any way another noisy night ensued but we stayed up till midnight and partied with them. Breakfast can be taken at the restaurant or cafe, bu the service is slow. My advice is to go across the road to the Tea Leaf and Coffee Beean Co or to the Starbucks at Hollywood and Highland. Good overall stay, right in the middle of Hollywood Blvd.

“Parc 55, excellent location, superb breakfast!” Me and my boyfriend stayed in Parc 55 for 5 nights and were very impressed with the accomodation and service. Our room was a corner room on the 12th floor with a maginificant view, the room was spacious and well furnished with the only downside being the bathroom which could do with some updating and also lacked adquate ventilation so got quite steamy. We had breakfast a couple of times at the hotel and must say the all amercian buffett breakfast was excellent value at $18. I was in San Francisco on business and working at the Hilton, which is only 1 block away, my boyfriend visited numerous tourist spots throughout our stay and found Parc 55 was in the perfect location to visit the Information bureau and catch the cable car and buses. I would recommend Parc 55 and Union Square to both tourists and business travellers. If travelling a lot whilst in San Francisco I would defintly recommend getting a Muni pass.

“A Jewel With A Terrific View” What a great find! We had a "getaway weekend" in San Francisco over the Memorial Day weekend and as we particularly like Kimpton Hotels we didn't think we could go too far wrong by booking a stay at the Harbor Court. We were not disappointed. We booked a standard room with a queen bed and discovered that we were upgraded to a queen view room overlooking the Embarcadero and the bay and the San Francisco/Oakland Bay Bridge. As soon as we entered our room we were spellbound by the view. After spending an evening out attending a jazz concert we returned to our room and were met with the scene of the waters of the bay glistening by the twinkling lights of the Bay Bridge. We stood in our room and gazed at this portrait with the room lights turned off. This experience alone was priceless - as they say in the credit card ad. Our service from the staff was exceptional as we have come to expect from this hotel group. The room was adequately but not overly furnished with hardwood flooring rather than carpeting. Our bed was positioned so that we could look out of the windows to see the view. There was only one desk chair in the room and a couple of more comfortable chairs would have added to the enjoyment as an added comfortable place to scenery gaze or to watch T.V. rather than standing at the window or sitting on the bed. But that criticism is but trivial to the total experience we enjoyed at this property. Oh yes, there is free wine hour near the lobby in the late afternoon and don't forget the milk and cookies waiting in the lobby when returning from a late night's entertainment. The hotel is only about a block away from the downtown financial district and the Ferry Building. For baseball fans the Harbor Court is only a fifteen minute walk down the waterfront to the Giant's ballpark. We will certainly stay here again and we will be more than willing to reserve a room with a view.

“Fun as usual” We go to an annual meeting here and have always enjoyed it. The lazy rivers is fun for kids and adults and lots of activities for kids. There is an adult pool when you get tired of the kids. We have been coming here since our kids were young. They always looked forward to the lazy river, s'mores by the fire at night, the movie on the lawn. It is expensive, even at the corporate rate. Food is good but also pricey. The pool is usually crowded and it was hard to find an empty chair, even at 5pm. People don't take their towels with them, and there isn't pick up of towels that are left unused, so you don't know whether a seat is taken or not. Service is usually good and very friendly. I had an unfortunate experience with check in this time, which is unusual. Had to wait 3 hours for my room; it wasn't ready even at 4pm. But, we had a good time as always. One downside--if you haven't been to San Antonio before, this is WAY off the beaten path from the Riverwalk. Do that another trip.

“Great Room, Different” New place. We had a petite suite - nice to have a tv in a separate area. Bed was great, bathroom wonderful (big tub, sep shower- a bit small), very clean, desk, nice couch, quiet (ask for room away from hiway), beautiful tiled area behind bed, empty small fridge to use (nice -not packed with overpriced junk). The window from the bathroom to the bedroom is a bit odd- I assume to improve 'visual flow/open-ness', but akward when sitting on the toilet, etc. There is a blind we had pulled down. I got the sense that the whole place suffered from iffy contractor(s) as there is obvious spackle messiness and paint mismatches around and there needs to be another piece of furniture or two in the lvg area and something else up on the walls there. Pool and hot tub and area very pleasant. Breakfast was basic. Near the South Congress neighborhood (not close to dwntwn) but fine w/car. A bit clumsy getting there using the 1-way service roads alongside I-35 but easy once you figure it out.

“Excellent Historic hotel in the heart of Boston” I stayed here for three nights in a king suite. The rooms were average in size (the suite consists of a living room and a bedroom), but well appointed and very comfortable. Room service was fast and very good. The hotel oozes history and is centrally located near all of the historic sites. I ate at all of the hotel's bars and restaurants. Parker's Restaurant was excellent and the staff were superb. The Last Hurrah had good food and drinks, but the staff were very slow and not particularly friendly. Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a luxury experience in the heart of Boston.

“Best Times Square view you can get, comfy spacious suite” This was my 10th visit to New York. I stayed here 30th May for 2 nights, and paid $250 per night (including tax) in advance to get the cheapest rate. I chose a King suite with a Times Square view. I really liked the room. The bedroom is separate so you can enjoy a quiet night without being disturbed by any noise from guests walking past the room. The sofa-bed was fairly comfortable, and the fridge was useful. The giant flat screen TV in the living room did not work properly. I am sure if I had reported it I could have got it fixed, but we did not spend much time in the room. Check in and out was very quick and easy, and the hotel stored our luggage on our last day. The bar in the lobby was small and always very quiet; but there are many bars around the hotel for a more lively experience. The best thing about the room was the view. We could see all of Times Square. I don’t think any other hotel in the area could give you as great a view – one that is now even more interesting since Broadway has been shut off to traffic and you can sit on chairs right in the middle of Times Square! I have stayed at the Marriott Marquis in a Times Square view room, and it was not as spectacular and cost a lot more. The area is obviously very busy all the time from the moment you step out of the hotel, but you only had to go round the side of the hotel and there was space to stand without being disturbed, or on the new light up red stairs above the TKTS booth outside the hotel . From my experience the rates at this hotel are usually pretty high; but if you can get a great rate like I did I really recommend the Doubletree Times Square. The following weekend I stayed at The Hilton on 6th Avenue, which was also very nice and I have reviewed this hotel too.

“Great new addition to the Chicago hotel scene” Beautiful new hotel with, what as a frequent traveler to Chicago, I believe are the best rooms in town: 90% large suites, fireplaces, balconies, huge bathrooms with very large walk in showers, dual bathroom sinks. Every suite also has a little kitchen area actually very well done with a concealed freezer and even a microwave. Location is wonderful and close to everything downtown. Service was also great - everyone was friendly and helpful. Style/atmosphere is modern neo-art deco with lots of grays and blacks which may not be for everyone. Not my personal favorite and I think it would get old to be exposed to it all the time, but considering all the great things this hotel offers, I didn't mind it.

“Great location, and comfortable experience” I have been visiting NYC for business for over 15 years, and I have recently been on the lookout for a new place to stay on my 10+ visits to the City each year. I particularly love the Village, and I was delighted to hear of this property. I just returned from a comfortable 2 night stay at this property, during which I stayed in a Village Suite. The bed was very comfortable, and the floor to ceiling windows were fun. I slept with the curtains open so as to really enjoy the view of the East Village. A few minor issues: my wake up call was 25 minutes late on day one, and I never did figure out how to turn on the TV! I recommend you consider staying here. I will return.

“Loved this hotel. Would want to return to it, definitely” Great hotel, right on the Riverwalk. Super nice room. I had a huge king sized bed, couch, desk, nice TV, big enough bathroom. The staff was great. The conceirge gave out vouchers for freebies at area restaurants. Everyone on staff I talked with from the front desk to cleaners to random people setting up the convention space was so helpful. The hotel is centrally located, right by the Alamo, the Riverwalk and the Convention Center. Guests are welcome to sit in the open bar seating in the lobby overlooking the riverwalk during the daytime. There are nice seats overlookign the river if you need to do work there. They have a riverfront restaurant too. The bus to Market Square runs right by the hotel. I don't write a lot of reviews but wanted to give this hotel a good review.

“Boffo!!” Our new favorite hotel in Chicago. Had a great recent 3 night stay. Absolutely gorgeous river view room. Never much cared before about a room with a view---I do now! What a knockout, wall to wall windows overlooking the river and bridges, the Trump Tower, and those twin tower round condo buildings that they drove the car off of into the river in that old movie. Wow. Room was quiet and comfortable with clean sumptuous furnishings and linens. Large marble bathroom with huge walk-in glass walled shower with bench seat and large overhead "rain" shower head. Free adequate wireless.>Staff was over the top friendly and eager to please. A special request was met quickly and eagerly. Only two slight negatives: elevators are a tad slow. And Sunday breakfast service at the restaurant was non-existent-so we left. Not nearly enough to even think about subtracting a star for though. From reading other reviews--apparently some of the rooms here are not yet updated (as ours must surely was), so until all rooms are experiences may vary. We had a delightful time.

“What a perfect way to end the weekend” I stayed at this hotel on a weekend when I was attending a concert in Boston. The staff was amazing. I had enrolled in the Omni Select Guest Program but wasn't sure I would be able to take advantage of the program since I had booked through Priceline; however, I was offered the opportunity to upgrade to a large deluxe room if I was willing to wait a few hours, which I gladly did. I did get a chance to see the smaller rooms and I would not recommend them as there is barely room for a bed and desk. The large deluxe rooms are wonderful and I had a great view. No interest access in rooms, only in the lobby. I personally don't like to use my computer where people can see my business. Also thought it was strange that hotel staff recommended a bar down the street for a drink when the hotel bar was open. Only other issue: as a Select Guest member you are entitled to two complimentary beverages and newspaper in the morning - I originally chose one time and then decided I wanted to check out earlier so called room service and asked if I could have an earlier delivery and they never showed up; however, Nicole at the front desk (thank you, Nicole!) went and got me a cup of coffee to go as I checked out. Would definitely stay here again.

“Best place in Austin” This place is a new hotel and conference center right next to the University of Texas in Austin. It is by far the best place I've stayed in Austin. The place is well decorated, the place is well staffed and the rooms are quiet and good sized. The food is excellent and the convenience either to the University, or the State Capital is much appreciated. It's only a short cab ride to the bars on 6th street (the best reason to visit Austin). The cost is OK given the quality of the place.

“Nice Business Hotel” This was our second stay at Hilton Back Bay. We were on the Hilton Honors floor. Our room had an unreal view, you could see all of Boston. It was amazing. The hotel is nice, its in close proximity to alot of attractions in Boston. The price of the rooms are very high though. We only stay there when we use spouses Hiltons Honors points. As was the case this past weekend, as it was son's college parents weekend, and the prices in Boston were through the roof. Nice hotel, would definitely stay there again!

“A New York Bargain "On the Ave"” Now that I don't live in NY and must travel there for business, I try different hotels around the city hoping to find something I can count on. A good rate (under $300 if possible since I have to bill multiple nights), clean, modern, relatively quiet rooms, with enough room so you don't feel like you're trapped in a closet. and in an area that doesn't make you wonder why you're staying there. Clearly not an easy feat given its NY, but it can happen every once in a while. After staying a few times at the Paramount, (which is tired, loud and I don't care what reviewers have said, does NOT offer decent service at check in or out.), the Royalton (which is actually a pretty great spot, if you're not paying over $300), and a number of others at a much higher pricepoint. So staying at On the Ave, was a last minute choice, when I got stuck one evening having to stay for a last minute meeting the next morning. It may not be the big happening space some travellers may expect, but this isnt that kind of hotel to begin with. The UWS area is not a place to see or be seen. It's an area you go when you want to hang out with your NY friends, visit some nice restaurants, walk around without worrying about getting a cab at 2 in the morning, check in at landmark NY stores, like Zabar's, etc. - pretty much get away from the hubub. First off, the hotel is located on 72nd, about 3 doors up from Broadway, which helps make it a bit quieter than you think. Service people are friendly, personable and efficient. And while some have remarked that some of the furnishings are shabby, I didn't see that. (and believe me, I do!). Besides the elevator needing a decent cleanup, I found my room to be pretty plush. It may not have the cheap hip chic of a "W" but it is rather cozy and modern. My room was on a corner at the end of a long hall which helped provide some peace and quiet at the end of a long day. And while it didn't have the sweeping views some of their other rooms may offer, I didn't care, It did have floor to ceiling windows, attractive wood blinds, big plush king bed with a great large plasma, and a bathroom with marble trim that was a nice surprise at the price I paid. (Below $200). I found it to be very quiet (a nice thing in NY), and when I called to ask for more pillows (alas hotel pillows still aren't enough), they brought them very quickly even late at night. No fridge in the room was a bummer as was no safe for my laptop, but I did like how everything was stylish and comfortable. Checking out the next day was a breeze and the doorman grabbed me a cab within 30 seconds. Something else that was nice...I filled out one of those time sucking surveys online and was honest about one of my windows not shutting. I quickly received an email from management apologizing for the issue and offering to provide an upgrade and guarantee of a better experience next time. As a result, I will be going back for a number of days for business, because of this extra touch. I may have a different experience next time, who knows. But I would still recommend On the Ave, if you could achieve as good a rate as I did. Its quiet, intimate and just what the doctor ordered.

“the good, the bad, and the ugly” let's start with the ugly: the first room they gave me was dingy, dirty and had paint peeling in the bathtub (who paints a bathtub in any case?)! in contrast, the room they gave me after i complained was more than good: a beautiful, large cushy king size bed, new flat screen tv, marble bathroom with amazing shower. and all i had to do was say: "are you kidding? give me a better room." and they did. the front desk staff were more than accommodating. here's the scoop: apparently 10 floors (the lower ones) have been renovated and the rest apparently are being saved for a second shooting of 'the shining.' advice: only book if you can be assured of a renovated room. next the bad: parking; the hotel didn't inform me that two doors down from their $45/nt parking was a lot for $28...bad. advice: don't drive to chicago if you can avoid it; i couldn't.... and now for a very, very good is location, location, location. hotel 71 is on wacker just above michigan avenue at the intersection of south michigan and north - there is easy walking down to the art institute or up along the miracle mile. it couldn't be more convenient.

“Great Value” Nice large room (1 bedroom suite). Just outside of Austin. If you are looking to for something close to downtown, this is not the place for you. Didn't try the breakfast. No real complaints. I don't think the bed was a true King but it was OK. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

“Riverwalk Plaza” Abbiamo scelto questo hotel per un capriccio dell'ultimo minuto e non poteva essere più soddisfatti. All'arrivo, ero un po scettico riguardo è stelle. La reception non sembrava molto professionale. Tuttavia, abbiamo notato che un sacco di aggiornamento e manutenzione è stato fatto. La nostra camera era davvero bello! Era pulito, aveva una buona vista e sembrava rinnovato di recente. Le persone ci sono stati davvero utili. Avevamo bisogno di una culla e si è portato subito e riparazioni minori aa fatto alla porta. Sarebbe sicuramente ci tornerei. La posizione è perfetta come siamo riusciti a piedi ovunque necessario. Abbiamo alloggiato all'Hilton (Riverwalk) in passato e ora sento come questo posto è tranquillo ma la posizione è ancora primo.

“Warm , welcoming and greatly connected” A little jewel in the Old Town of San Diego. Receptionists were excellent and went out of their way. Maintenance was instantly available - even on a Saturday night. The hotel is located in a side street, almost without traffic, and guarantees a quiet rest at night despite Old Town's busy Saturday nightlife in San Diego Street. Old Town itself is charming with lots of good restaurants, and it boasts fantastic connections to all interstates and other thoroughfares.

“Pretty good” I booked my stay here for 1 night for Hotwire, and given all the bad reviews was pretty apprehensive about staying at this place. However, when I checked in I asked for a renovated room, and they did give me one. The room was excellent, and we had a side view of the river. Everything was clean. The mattress and pillows were not of the quality you would expect in a 4 star, but its fine. There is not much around this place, but that might be a good thing since the next couple of days I stayed in Times Square and the streets were so loud, you could hear it on the 34th floor.

“Great as a club and a bar scene. Not so great for their hotel guests though.” What a great looking staff. All well dressed, eager, and oh so young and hip. Too bad several of them have no clue as to how to treat their hotel guests. On more than one occassion I had to finally push my way through the line of people waiting to get into their rooftop bar and lounge. One would think the hotel would make sure their paying guests could easily get to the elevator from the 15th Street entrance without having to force their way through the 20-something hip crowd. (My six year old even asked "why won't these people move?") They are concerned about getting those bar patrons upstairs. Would it be so hard to make sure they leave some space between the entrance and the guest elevators? One would think the hotel would stop bar patrons from using the two elevators designated for hotel guests as they are leaving the rooftop bars. No such luck.
