On more than one occassion we had to wait several minutes for an empty elevator to get from our floor to the ground floor because the bar crowd had it filled on their way down. One night we had drunks screaming on our floor around 1 in the morning. Security did come up when called. But, where were they to stop them from getting off on a guest floor in the first place? We had a concierge willing accept the $80 fee we paid for tickets to the Washington Monument with the specific instructions to NOT get the tickets for 1 p.m. as we had plans and we told him so. So of course, he gets them for them for 1 on the dot. He then makes up for it by getting us a table at 7:00 p.m. in their roof-top lounge. Completely ignoring the fact that the bar is off limits to those under 21 after 5 and he knew we had two young kids with us. At one point we waited for an elevator for about 8 minutes. The bar was crowded that night so I guess they needed two of the three elevators for their bar patrons. My daughter and I finally get on the elevator along with two other guests. To our surprise a hotel employee gets on with two people destined for their bar and proceeds to overide our floors and express the bar patrons to the top floor. (He picks up a few more for the ride down.) He was polite though when I asked why are they giving priority to those visiting a bar instead of those who paid over $400 a night (plus tax) to stay at the hotel who just waited several minutes for an elevator. The room we had was a nice size and was comfortable for the four of us. Though the lack of closet and drawer space is a problem which will require any family to live out of their suitcase if staying for more than a few days. Four small drawers and two medilum sized ones simply won't cut it if more than two are in a a room. (The closet is actually a half closet that might hold at most 3 dresses. This was a problem for my wife.) You can't complain about the location which is just across from the White House. We did eat lunch twice at their rooftop lounge POV. The food was very good and the view is one of the best in town. I can understand the appeal of those looking to hang out and drink in a nice setting. To be fair, we could not hear the music from either upstairs or downstairs in our room. But, if considering a stay here, I would ask about the noise level at a 15th street facing room on either the first or last floor of guest rooms. If you are young and want to be in "the scene" you will probably love staying here. 10 years ago sans kids, I might have enjoyed it. But, now that I'm out of the under 30 demographic and with two young kids in tow, not a place I'd pick again. For economic reasons, they seemingly have decided the bar is where the profits will come from and they act accordingly.

“Clean and renovated...across the street from the Convention ctr” I enjoyed the Westin Charlotte. My room was spotless. It has a great location. Food was average and restaurant was over run and couldnt keep up...food both in the restaurant and at room service was typical hotel fare....some challenges there...but all in all a very nice Hotel!

“Very comfortable stay at a very comfortable hotel” We stayed at the this hotel for four nights in mid September. First of all, this is not your typical Residence Inn. It most apparently was not built as a Residence Inn and is somewhat larger than your typical Residence Inn. There is a large atrium lobby, and the staff / facility could handle the larger crowds at mealtime (breakfasts / evening "receptions" several nights per week). The only less than exceptional aspect of the hotel was the room servicing, where as a result of what both the front desk and we considered to be a "language" issue, our room was not serviced one day. We also found stick pins on the floor from a previous guest, and we did not have toiletries restocked one day. Other than that, the experience was very good. Front desk staff were helpful, and polite, but efficient. Of note, I was not acknowledged as an elite member of Marriott Rewards. We were in room 510, overlooking Fairview Avenue. With the balcony door open, the street noise was noticeable, but otherwise, street noise was not a problem, although during daytime hours, the street is fairly heavily traveled. The location is exceptional - although one big warning on that - see below. The location is about one mile north of downtown Seattle. In the immediate vicinity is South Lake Union Park and a number of reasonably upscale restaurants. To get a cheaper meal, one would have to walk a bit. There is excellent public transport immediately in front of the hotel - both the streetcar and the 70-73 bus lines (at least one line is running at all times, with frequent service to both downtown and the University of Washington). It is also possible and apparently safe to walk from the hotel to the center of Seattle (we did it multiple times in daylight without any worries - note that two blocks of Terry north of Denny do not have sidewalks - use Westlake instead). It is also a reasonably flat route - particularly on Westlake. Note also that the streetcar does not run very late into the evening many nights, if you plan an evening in downtown Seattle. The hotel would make an exceptionally good choice for a long term stay for a family of a cancer patient at the neighboring Fred Hutchinson Cancer Care Center or someone relocating to one of the nearby large employers. As much as we enjoyed our stay, I must warn of upcoming construction closures for the Mercer Corridor Project. Check progress on www.seattle.gov and then search for Mercer Corridor Project. For those planning on using an automobile to venture out from the Residence Inn, check the site for planned closures. The detour routes make staying in downtown Seattle or an outlying area a more viable choice, in my view. Also, check for bus detours / route changes / stop changes. In my limited experience with some bus stop changes at the University of Washington, King County Metro does a reasonable job of placing signs at the affected stops, but does not update their web site (that I could tell). This construction will continue into 2013. Again, this is most likely to impact someone planning to use an auto to get around from the Residence Inn.

“Location, Location, Location” We have stayed here before and it's as good and consistent as ever, probably our favourite Hampton Inn. Yes there is noise, you are practically on Beale Street so bands playing into the early hours so if it's a quiet retreat you seek please look elsewhere. This is a fun hotel in an absolutely perfect location. Beale is all about the vibe so why not immerse yourself. Yet another flawless stay, we will return again some day soon.

“Ok for Single Business Traveler-Check alternatives for Couples/Families” We stayed at the Marriott for a business convention for 3 nights. The location was great (right next to Nordstrom's on Michigan Ave) for the meeting and for after hours events. The room was relatively clean and well maintained, and staff was responsive to special requests. Why would I probably not stay here again? There are so many options within the area of Michigan Ave, and most are probably more up to date. While the hotel has been cosmetically upgraded with great sheets/flat screen tv/etc, it simply isn't up to current hotel standards when you're talking about a room over $200 per night. An older hotel, our room was small, the doors were very narrow, the bathroom was extremely small (5x6) with hardly enough room to close the 24" door (and we're just average size folks), the light switch upon entering the room was located inside the closet, the beds are extremely soft (although staff quickly added a bedboard upon request). Because our room and bathroom were so small, we would probably opt for a different hotel in the area with more up to date comforts next time we visit. Not a problem if you're traveling alone or at a pure business meeting, but most families or couples out for a romantic setting would want just a little more room.

“Wunderbares "Durchgangshotel"” Das Westin Galleria Houston ist das Perfekte "Zwischnestopp" Hotel. Sollte man nur für ein paar Tage in Houston sein eignet sich dieses Hotel Perfekt. Das Personal ist sehr freundliche und zuvorkommend. Die Zimmer sind "Neu" renoviert und sauber. Wifi gibt es in der Lobby kostenlos. An das Hotel grenzt die große Galleria Mall, diese ist über den Hotellift direkt zu erreichen. Die Mall ist groß und beherbergt alle Geschäfte die man zum shoppen braucht :-) In der Mall gibt es verschiedene Essmöglichkeiten u.a. die Cheescake Factory. Um das Hotel ist nicht wirklich viel, jedoch wenn man nur kurz bleibt....

“Need some updating” The outside of the property looked not bad, but inside you would see that this hotel was old and needed some work. It didn't look like the photos on the website so I was a little disappointed. The view from the hotel room was not bad if you enjoy the mountains and sunset-on-the-desert feeling. Shuttle would take you to PHX and also, the botanical garden, which I strongly recommend for a walk in the morning. I ate breakfast at the hotel as well. It was not bad as well. The location is near the airport, but I guess if I go to Phoenix again, I might want to live near Scottsdale or Downtown Phoenix. The neighborhood does not feel 100% safe. Just my guess.

“A bit wierd” Bouyed up by my previous Kimpton experience (in Philadelphia) I booked into the Helix for a one night stay on business. Firstly, I don't know DC's geography very well, but it feels a bit remote. Maybe everything in DC is remote. Secondly, there was only one guy doing check-in and he was on the phone - and when he got off the phone, despite having acknowledged my presence, he wandered off. I was less than impressed. I found the room a bit wierd. They have tried to be funky in a 1970s way - a lot of lime green, orange etc. The bed is curtained off in a little alcove and there are no doors on the wardrobe, just a psychedelic curtain. Overall the room size was fine and it had all the things I needed - internet, TV, bathroom, bed etc. But it was definitely at the wierd end of the spectrum for me. I didn't eat in the restaurant but the bar looked lively and as usual they had the 5pm happy hour where they offer wine & sangria gratis for an hour which is a nice touch. I doubt I will be back.

“Great place to stay in Lower Manhattan” The Bowery Hotel is very nicely furnished in a faux antique old English kind of style. Since the building is a brand new construction and the furnishings are aging well, things are functioning and are not overly worn, noisy, or otherwise difficult to deal with, such as so many other New York hotels. The rooms have a decent size and nice powerful showers. Downstairs the scene is happening and chilled at once, with some celebrity spotting. My only suggestion would be to spend more time training the staff, especially the receptionists. They seem somewhat unprofessional and uninterested.

“No problems here” I wasn't sure what to expect after reading some of the reviews. I can't complain, especially considering I got the room for $44 on Priceline. It was also convenient to leave the car right on sight for $7 a night with no tax. It's a gated lot used by 3 hotels so I knew the car would be safe. In the morning we only had a 5-minute wait for the shuttle. Coming back we had a 15-minute wait for the shuttle to pick us up at the terminal. Staff was friendly checking in and our room was just fine for one night before an early flight. It was comfortable and I found it to be clean. The only thing the room didn't have was a refrigerator if that matters. The internet was complimentary. Our floor was quiet on this evening so sleeping wasn't a problem. The gym looked better than expected, but we didn't have time to use it. We walked over to the Sheraton Suites to grab a bite to eat. The restaurant at Four Points was empty which made me somewhat cautious, so went for the short walk. The only problem was the place was a burger joint (Burger Bistro). Food was good but it is a limited menu that obviously features mostly burgers. Not sure if I would pay rack rate to stay here, but the $44 room and airport parking is a big reason why this hotel gets 4 out of 5. I think the purpose of an airport hotel is giving you a decent night sleep with efficient shuttle service in the morning. Mission accomplished.

“Improved since remodel” I stayed here some years ago and thought it was below average because of age. Now the whole hotel has been remodeled and improved. I was surprised to see a few reviews saying the room was small. It's only the bathroom that is small - the rest is standard hotel size - certainly not spacious like a suite but perfectly adequate. My room had a balcony overlooking the pool. The best part of the room was the comfortable mattress and 6 fluffy pillows. I slept surprisingly well. There were some problems with noise in some parts of the hotel because of a convention and a wedding party but fortunately my floor was quiet. Cleanliness was a problem. When I first entered the room, I found the bathroom had quite a few stray hairs on the counter, in the sink, and on the floor. I called the front desk, and the housekeeping manager came to the room. She asked me to show her the problem so I started pointing "one there, another there, there's one..." and her eyes got big. A short time later a maid came to reclean the bathroom. I could hear her scrubbing and smelled the strong chemicals. She left, so I went in to inspect the bathroom. This time I found 3 hairs on the counter but none on the floor or in the sink. I could have called again but decided I didn't want to get the maid in trouble. So I wiped it down and from there everything was fine. We ate lunch one day and the food was good but not great. For a low-cost option, walk down the block to Dominick's grocery. They have a deli where they make sandwiches (breakfast and lunch) and there's a good salad bar. Across the street is Al's where you can get Italian beef sandwiches or all sorts of burgers, hot dogs, salads, etc. Internet isn't free but you can get wired or wireless in your room and in the lobby. If you like really loud music while you're working, go ahead and sit in the lobby. The furniture is comfortable. You can trade off partial deafness for a good atmosphere. The fitness room is great - clean, new machines, free weights, large-screen TVs at either end plus individual TVs on the cardio equipment. The pool looked good as well but I didn't swim. Newspapers (USA Today and WSJ) are free at the concierge stand but weren't delivered to rooms. The other nice amenity is the free airport shuttle. The weekend rate is pretty good but I would shop around if the regular rates are high - there are many others to choose from in area. One friend stayed at Embassy Suites where you get free food and probably a bigger room.

“Philly Airport Hilton is Fine - It is a basic Airport Hotel” I stayed at this Hilton on a Saturday night because I had a very early Sunday flight. The hotel is a five minute drive to the airport. Very simply. I did not use the hotel shuttle service, but it seemed that many folks were using it with ease. My room was fine. The room was not sound proof and noise from other rooms and the hallway were easily heard. The sports bar was average, but pleasant and an easy place to hang out when trying to kill some time or get a quick bite to eat. The restaurant was also fine. The servers and host were extremely pleasant. As an HHonors Member I did get a certificate for a free continental breakfast. I could have used this to get the hot buffet for a reduced cost, but I did not. THe staff...they are Philly folk and should be accepted as such. They were somewhat abrasive, but not mean or evil, just typical Philly Eagles Fans-type people. I thought they were charming. Worth the stay if you get a good rate. Lots of choices though, so this is not a must stay.

“good location & good stay” I recently stayed at this hotel for 1 night on business. Great location near many good restaurants, and walking distance to my client which was ideal. Not far from the airport, but the cab ride is still $20-25 with tip. Very polite and courteous greeting at checkin. I was looking to check in very early: 10am. They had no problem accommodating my request. That is always appreciated . . . when they don't hassle you about an early checkin . . . just check availability and let you know. Good stay. No problems with comfort or internet access. Breakfast in the lounge was good, but the lounge area is a little cramped and small. However, they do have a nice outside eating area that is terrific, with great views. One note of caution is that the walls are a little thin at this hotel. Sounds in other rooms and in the hall were pretty easy to hear with the TV off, etc. If you are a very light sleeper, this could be an issue. I would definitely stay at this hotel again for business in San Jose.

“IT WAS LIKE A GERMAN SAUSAGE (ONE OF THE WURST)” We booked 4 nights on line, stayed 3. We had 2 dogs and paid $20 per night extra ($10 per dog) The dogs were better guests than the others staying at the hotel. I could write a full page but will try to keep it somewhat brief. The room was okay, they try to do a good job but can't. Its in a horrible neighborhood especially during the night. Its a crack prostituteneighborhood. How do I know. while parking in a very tight back lot, we bumped a guest's car. No damage, however, he was a mental case, having seen him every evening shadow boxing in the back along side his car. His car was a junker, full of crap. i don't know what he wanted since he had no damage, but before it was over, the police were there at my request. They were on drug patrol in the area. They made a report and that was the end of it, we checked out the following morning with apologies from management. The other guest was a regular long stay. I have patronized Motel 6 properties for many years. Some are good, some are horrible. Its not the company, its the people who stay there. Losers, boozers, drug addicts, prostitutes. You name it and they are there. Unless you are tough, try to find another place. This place allows dogs which makes it easy to stay but there is a price you pay and I don't mean in dollars. Walk around the neighborhood in the morning. You'll see more bars than in San Quentin Prison. Res Ipso Loquitor. the thing speaks for itself. I have to laugh when I see foreign visitors write complimentary reports. If this is what they think about it, then their standards in Europe must be pretty junky and low.

“Just Not Worth It” As evidenced by the less than flattering title of my review, Paradise Point is a pretty mediocre hotel with less than great service. We chose Paradise because a friend was having a wedding here. After driving from LA and arriving at about quarter after four, we were told that our room wasn't ready yet and they had no clear idea of when it would be ready--- this happened notwithstanding that the hotel knew we were there for a five thirty wedding on their premises!!! After forty-five minutes were unapologetically given access to our room and therefore ended up being the absolute last guests to show up at the wedding. Overall, the rooms were ok-- but in the morning we discovered both that the hotel had forgotten to put shampoo in our room and that after about fifteen minutes the hot water in the bathroom runs out. Definitely not worth the price.

“excellent facilities and location” I stayed at the Fairmont for several nights last week. The rooms are large and well appointed. The hotel has an excellent gym with facilities above and beyond what I have seen in virtually all other hotels. Free high speed internet was provided for club members (you can sign up for free online ahead of time). The breakfast buffet is very nice, and reasonably priced for local prices. Overall, an excellent hotel for business or pleasure.

“My best and favorite hotel in the world” とにもかくにもハードもソフトも完ぺき。ここ数年で建物ごと新しく建ったホテルは少ないが、バワリーホテルはまるで19世紀からここに存在していたかのようなシャビーシックな雰囲気と、本当に心あるスタッフの温かいサービスでいつも最高のステイを約束してくれます。 フロントスタッフはもちろんのこと、ロビーフロアに続くバーのスタッフたちも最高にフレンドリーで、NYの高級ホテル特有のどこかスノビッシュでマニュアルライクなホスピタリティとは一線を隔しています。 部屋のハウスキーピングもパーフェクトです。 あまりに囲碁心地が良く、私はここを知ってから、ほかのホテルは考えられません。 一泊$500支払う価値がこのホテルにはあります。

“Mixed stay” We stayed at the Iroquois in a one bedroom suite for five nights over easter. The suite was spacious & nicely decorated & very clean. The location is excellent. The staff were for the most part very pleasant - especially the cleaning staff. We had a number of irritating problems though. First on the day we arrived I had to call 3 times over a 5 hour period & speak in person to the front desk before someone brought up an extension cord for a machine that assists me breathe at night while I sleep. The cord should have come promptly after the first call. This is the only hotel in the world where I've had such a problem. Second, & maybe because it was Easter, the hotel seemed under staffed - 70% of the time there were no doormen. The concierge was absent for a lot of our stay & made silly mistakes like booking 2 restaurants for the same night for us. We were called every evening to check if we wanted the sofa bed made up in the lounge room ? It seemed v odd. Breakfast in the room was very limited - essentially a continental breakfast. Room service after hours was not from an on site kitchen & was limited. The advised it would take an hour & they couldn't guarantee it would be warm ? All room service including breakfast came with a $4 delivery charge plus 18% service. An incredible mark up. Also we could hear everything said & done in the room next to ours - there was a connecting door - luckily this was only in the lounge room of our suite but it is still strange when you're paying a lot of money for a suite to not get privacy. None of the problems were terrible but they were aggravating when added together.

“Good value” This is not the Ritz so the 5 star review is based on this hotel category. It’s a nice updated hotel near the highway, very close to the stadium. It’s 15 minutes away from the zoo and downtown. Parking lot is sufficient and there is also a garage parking. The hotel was full during our stay, so the garage was full but there are parking spaces in the lot. Not issue with parking when we arrived around mid night. Next to the hotel is a small plaza with restaurants and Jack In the Box. The Thai restaurant in the plaza was very good. Across the road is another shopping plaza with more fast food, a super market, and gas stations. We are priority club members and the front desk staffs knowledge that. They gave us cookies and a cold bottle water upon check in. Front desk staffs were very friendly and professional. The best staffs we’ve seen amount hotels. A+ for them. We have a double room facing the front on the first floor. We could hear the road noise even thought it wasn’t too loud. The beds are not queen size as advertised. They’re double size beds so it’s tight for 2 adults. The linens are nice, the towels are thick. The pillows and beds are comfortable. The sink is outside the bathroom and it works well if you have more than one person in the room. The bathroom is big with a shower over tub and toilet. It’s a nice touch to have plenty of shelves around the shower/ tub to put the toiletries. We had breakfast at the hotel and they were very good, and good value. The omelets were delicious, the home fries were very tasty, and the toasts were very good, too. The service was a bit slow, so don’t expect a quick breakfast. The staffs were very friendly and they worked hard to meet the customers’ needs.

“Great location in Austin close to 6th Street” We left Dallas around 8 am and arrived in Austin right on time around 11:30. Being starved for lunch at that point, we were excited that there was a full size TGI Friday's restaurant right inside the lobby of the hotel (and a Starbucks too!). Do know that there is an onsite parking garage that costs $16 a day for hotel guests. Upon arrival, we were impressed with the decor and comfort of the lobby. There are plenty of sitting areas, mesmerizing aquariums, and a warm fireplace to relax by. Megan at the front desk told us that our standard room was not ready yet (we arrived early), and I casually told her that I had elite status and asked for an upgrade if it was available. She told us that a lakeside view suite with one king bed would be ready in about 30 minutes, which was fine because we were going to have lunch at Friday's before going to the room anyway. During lunch, Megan called my cell phone and told us that the room was ready when we were. We headed up to our suite (room 1039), and within minutes Megan called us and asked us if everything was OK with the room, which was a nice touch of good customer service. As far as location, the hotel was nested right in the center of town, walking distance to Austin's famous 6th Street and many restaurants (too bad it wasn't bat season in Austin, it would be been cool to see the famous bat colonies). Take a look at some of the pictures we took of our suite and the hotel below. We were excited that there was a full size (bar included) TGI Friday's in the hotel. It was nice to grab lunch before checking into the room. The lobby was spacious and inviting with plenty of couches, a warm fire place, and the elk chandeliers were a cool touch. The living room area of our suite - a bit dated, but clean and spacious. The desk was situated in the living room of the suite, and was big enough to work comfortably. The coffee machine was located on a separate nook between the bedroom and living room area. We were given two complimentary bottles of Dasani water. The shower was pretty basic, but clean, and had good water pressure and plenty of hot water. The bathroom sink area was stocked with Radisson's signature Asira product line (Shampoo, Conditioner, Body Lotion & Body Soap Bar). We shared a very large king size bed, and the bedroom had a door to separate it from the rest of the suite for added privacy. All Radisson rooms are equip with Sleep Number beds (not my favorite, but my sleep number is 30 if anyone cares). After a short nap for us in the room, we decided to hit the town and walk to check out 6th Street; believe it or not, Austin seemed to be dead all around (I'm blaming it being Sunday and the Super Bowl playoffs), so we had some dinner and drinks at Manuel's (Upscale Tex-Mex, which ended up being excellent) ultimately because we got a coupon for a free loaded nachos appetizer from the front desk. After dinner, we decided to head back to the room and watch the game (not that we are football fans or anything, but we did feel a sense of obligation to support our Giants...). Please visit my blog post at http://www.justanotherpointstraveler.com/2012/01/hotel-review-radisson-hotel-suites.html for my complete review including pictures
“Nice place to stay in NYC Times Square district” Contemporary and nice. For NYC - big rooms - easy access to Times Square and excellent "cheaper" places to eat nearby. I would recommend.

“A Great Bargain for San Francisco” I have stayed at the Marina Motel many times. For one thing, parking is free in individual covered spaces. That's no small deal because a typical hotel will charge $20 - $30 per night for parking in San Francisco. If you are looking for a Holiday-Inn-style place this is probably not your motel. This is a 1930's vintage motel and that's part of its charm. All the bathrooms have been modernized, and the staff keeps the place very clean. If you can get one of the rooms with a kitchen, it will really help you keep your expenses down by eating a few meals in your room. There are a bunch of great restaurants at various price levels within walking distance of the motel. The staff at the motel are really friendly and extremely helpful. One caveat, I always request a room that is away from Lombard street because it is a heavily travelled street with a lot of noise.

“Awesome experience at a historic Seattle hotel.” The Artic Club is a Seattle landmark. The Doubletree has incorporated this history with its usual high quality service and hospitality. The setting is great in downtown, yet the intimacy of this property makes it a great place to stay.

“Good Location, Nice Room” We selected the Marriott because of it's location and because of the Marriott Rewards program. The lobby was nice, the rooms were comfortable and modern. The King bed was fantastic. The bath was nice but with the sliding door and no fan their was no privacy. The location was close to Union Square and a short walk to China Town. Public transporation to the wharf and other attractions.We enjoyed a downhill walk through China Town to Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf. The cable car back is just $5.00 each. The staff was friendly and very helpful. THe only fault I could site is the outrageous parking fees of $47 per night (but every hotel in downtown SF has the same problem). There is a parking gargae next door that is just $35.00 per night, so ask about it.

“It was eh...” The W New York was an okay hotel. The Restaurant and Bar downstairs were ultra yuppy... good food, overpriced nonetheless. The location isnt bad - the middle of Midtown East/Murray Hill... I had a suite, and the room was ginormous, but the decor was blah. The beds, carpets, and decor was standard. They tried to be modern, but kind of fell short. Anyways, the place was clean, but the bathrooms kind of gross. I had to wear shower shoes because of the midlew caked on the bottom... but then again, I didnt have to spend too much time in the hotel. If you just need a nice place to stay while you are visiting NY, I recommend it. If you are looking to be pampered and relaxed whilst meandering around the city, I would suggest somewhere else. Not bad though. I would be indifferent if I had to stay here again.

“Standard Courtyard (which is good by the way) very close to the airport” I had an early morning flight out so stayed here for one night. I found it to be exactly what I've come to expect from Courtyards - it didn't disappoint. Clean, quiet, well thought out space, polite staff. And it was an easy 5 minute drive to the airport. I would not hesitate to stay here again if the circumstances were the same.

“Great Hotel, Great Location and Great Service” I stayed here for business and a get away for 9 days in May and this is one of those hotels that has about everything you could ask for. It's in a Great Location: Adams Morgan/Woodley Park with lots of convenient restaurants, services (dry cleaning etc) a block away. The Metro station is a block away giving you access to the whole greater DC area. Although it is an older hotel it feels very nice and the rooms are outstanding. The staff is very helpful and the pool area is just fantastic. I've stayed at a lot of hotels in DC on business and this by far is in my top 5. The only thing I didn't like much about the place were the elevators. There's only two of them per wing so sometimes you had to wait a bit longer for one than I'd like. You may also get the occasional flight noise from a plane taking off at Regan National but it's subdued.

“overall comfortable stay” was here for two nights. we had a jr suite connecting with a double. the connecting doors were awkward to use. beds were very comfortable. we noticed there wasn't a coffee maker in the room. the sitting area was very nice, pleasant furnishings. some wear and tear here and there, but not too bad. the bath products were quite cheap. the body wash smelled just like the tamarind sauce i eat with indian samosas! really! the bath was very large, though. our toilet clogged the last day. would definately stay again if i could get a decent rate. $500/nt was too much.

“Upscale, quiet, and clean hotel in lower Manhatten” High quality hotel with great service and first class accomodations. Stayed 4 nights in April 2012. Rooms are large with plenty of drawers and closet space. My bed was perfect, but since the hotel just opened that's probably expected. Separate living room with couch and love seat. 2 large tvs with plenty of local and national channels. Separate room for the shower. Shower was awesome. No bath tubs - if that matters to you. Ate dessert at the restaurant. It was ok, nothing specail. Several new restuarants around the area. Including Blue Smoke a fantastic bar-b-que spot and Shake Shack. It's a bit of a walk to the subway, about 10 minutes. But it's not bad. Better than catching a cab. It's a very business traveler environment - at night the bar is full. I stayed at the old Embassy Suites several times a year for several years. This is a significant upgrade in quality. Pricey, but this is NY. NOTE - all rooms have a couch but not all of the couches are fold out beds. If you need a fold out bed, you have to request it.

“Nice overnight at the Courtyard” I spent one night at the Courtyard in May, 2004, and was pleased with the hotel. The room was clean and spacious, quiet, and efficient. The breakfast in the morning was very nice, and everyone in the hotel was friendly. The first room I was given had no phone service or internet service. The front desk handled the problem appropriately and quickly, with a smile. Overall a good job and a good value.

“Good for the Location and the Price - Go Red Sox!” Wanted to stay in a clean budget priced hotel near Camden Yards. This hotel was perfectly fine! We were lucky to get a corner room. The walk to Inner Harbor and Camden Yards was 7-8 blocks. Parking in the hotel was $13/day and across the street (no in/out privledges) was $9/day during the week and $4/day on the weekend. Our family of four, 2 adults and 2 kids, enjoyed our visit. The continental breakfast was good-very simple. Other guests had problems with their rooms but we didn't. For the price,$99 per night,we were very pleased!The other hotels in the Inner Harbor cost over $350 plus parking.We would definately stay here again!

“Thanks From The Big Blue” The Millikin University (Big Blue) Volleyball team stayed at the Novotel during their visit to play at the NYU Labor Day tournament. We had 10 rooms and had no complaints other than one couple who's room must not have been sound-proofed - and they were promptly moved on request. The location was terrific, the rooms were nice and we were well-treated by the staff. They even allowed us to bring bagels/juice/cereal into the lounge for breakfast even tho the hotel had a restaraunt (albeit $20/pp for breakfast - too rich for us). The porters cheered the team when they returned from winning a co-championship - which the girls really enjoyed. The dual-elevator system is a bit inconvenent as is the automatic thermostats that turn down the AC when you are out of the room. But, all in all, a great choice for us - I would certainly put the Novotel at the top of our list should we return to NYC and would have no trouble recommending to others.

“Beautiful, elegant hotel” Hotel was lovely, room was quiet. Checked in after 11 and desk person changed reservation so ended up in a smaller room as I was a single traveler. Otherwise, stay was wonderful.

“Comfortable stay in Times Square - no frills, no issues” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Sofitel in New York for two nights during our weekend trip to hang out with friends, watch Broadway & ABT shows, and enjoy some great restaurants. All in all, the trip was enjoyable and relaxing, and our stay at the Sofitel - while not a standout - does not detract from the trip either. We were given a room right by the elevator bank on the 10th floor of the hotel, but we didn't experience any noise issues. The vibe in the hotel is definitely luxury, though not quite like the Pierre or Peninsula hotels. All the hotel attendants and front desk reps we interacted with were helpful, perhaps even eager to help. While I have no specific anecdotes to relay, in my mind and experience, that can be a positive! There are certainly no aspects to our stay that were sub-optimal - I would stay at the Sofitel again, particularly if our plans included more Broadway shows and gallivanting around the city. (The Sofitel is located right off Fifth Avenue, equidistant to the B/D/F/V and 4/5/6, making it easy to traipse around Manhattan.) If you know, however, that your plans don't require you to be near Times Square or Lincoln Center (or the general Midtown area), the Sofitel isn't necessarily the best option. The Bowery and Crosby Hotels downtown are better options for visitors who will be frequenting that area. Sofitel, however, I think is a reliable option for Midtown.

“ブロードウェイのショーの後に徒歩で帰れます” サンフランシスコでブロードウェイのショーを観るのであればその日はここに泊まるととても便利です。市街地からは数ブロックはなれていますが、徒歩圏内です。メイン通りからも1ブロックなので電車もバスもたくさん走っています。サンフランシスコの市街地よりも安いので節約したいひとにもおすすめです。安全の面でも問題ありません。改装中だったので今頃はきれいになっていると思います。部屋は一般的なホリデイインタイプで、広くもなく、せまくもなくといった感じです。他のホテルもそうですが歯ブラシはついていないのでお忘れなく。ディナーと朝食は別のところで食べることをおすすめします。周りにはファストフードはありますが、他にはあまりありません。

“Don't have much to say” My husband and I stayed here to catch an early flight the next morning. We had a suite and the room was a nice, but average. There were two tvs in one room, a little strange since they had to be on the same channel to work. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom was very small. The staff was nice enough to hold some things for us at the front desk that our family needed to pick up after we left for our trip.

“Clean, Efficient, Lots of Room, Friendly Staff...Perfect for Business Travel” As a grizzled road warrior used to other chains, I was a bit surprised when this was booked for me. What a pleasant surprise - friendly, efficient staff (obviously proud to represent the hotel), LARGE clean suites, nice simple breakfast, and daytime shuttle to area businesses. One touch that puts a smile on my face are the thick natural wood floors in the elevators...reminds me of the Best Westerns in the National Park areas. This hotel is in a suburban strip area with restaurants a few steps from the hotel. I will not hesitate to stay here yet again on a return visit.

“The Omni: Perfect location, beautiful accommodations” My daughter and I stayed at the Omni for the Holidays Lights Festival. I have stayed at four different hotels each time I have visited Chicago, and the Omni has been the best so far. It's right in the middle of the action - it was great to walk out the lobby and be within steps of Michigan Ave. (the hotel sits on MIchigan, but lobby entrance is on Huron). Every staff member I met was friendly and professional. I requested a room with a view and received a room on the 24th floor with a fantastic view of the John Hancock Building. The double room suite was spacious and very clean. Housekeeping was excellent and the room smelled fresh each time we came back from an outing. I had read through another review on Trip Advisor to sign up for the Select Guest program and I'm glad I did. Check-in was a breeze and it included complimentary beverages in the morning with the option of purchasing individual items such as bagels and muffins for a reasonable price. The hotel's special touches during the Holiday Lights Weekend were a real treat. On Sat. morning as we headed out to shop, coffee, a rich, delicious hot chocolate drink and mini pastries were available in the lobby. The night of the parade, they opened up their third floor board room (with floor to ceiling windows) for guests and offered complimentary hot beverages and sugar cookies during the parade. It was all very festive. The hotel offers express check-out through voice mail which was convenient, and the night before we left, the front desk called to see if we needed boarding passes printed or any help with our departure. I thought that was a very nice touch. The only problem we encountered was with the hotel's restaurant, 676, In regard to what we were charged for the buffet. I made note of this on the comment card at departure, and within a day, received an e-mail from the director of food and beverage who quickly resolved the situation. I am impressed with the Omni Hotel -- perfect location; beautiful, clean accommodations; friendly staff; and quick to respond to, and resolve, a guest's concern.

“Four stars for the property, minus a star for the service” The Back Bay Hotel offers significant aesthetic pleasures: - fancy Frette linens - plush bathrobes - no slippers, but who's that picky? - small rooms, but it IS Boston - across the street from one of my favorite restaurants in Boston - walking distance from the Financial District, commuter rail, insurance alley and a multi-city fitness club The only area where it is lacking is its policies. I can't even knock the service because it seemed to me that the staff genuinely wanted to help and were not permitted to do so. At issue: I had dinner at a wonderful (if pricey) restaurant and the food was so good I accepted the leftoveres they packed up for me. The Back Bay Hotel has refrigerators in the room that were more than large enough to accomodate the leftover food. Having stayed at many other hotels, including most that didn't have microwaves in the room, I expected to be able to heat up anything I put in the microwave. Many hotels accomplish this by bringing (yeah, I know) microwaves to the room any time a guest requests one. Other hotels have food heated up by room service. The Back Bay Hotel allows no provision for this possibility whatsoever. Believe me, I tried. I even asked if I could heat my food in the employee break room and to his credit, the poor associate who answered the phone wanted to do it but was told that it was against company policy. In the end, I had to go back to the restaurant where I purchased the food (which fortunately was across the street) to reheat the food but it was a fool's errand and a colossal waste of my time. When I returned to the hotel and requested utensils and a napkin so I could enjoy my inventively reheated meal, I was assured that someone would bring silverware to my room. Fifteen minutes later someone did show up with silverware but you can imagine my food wasn't as hot as when I made the request. I even offered to get the utensils myself but was assured that utensils were en route ASAP. It was a miserable experience for something that seemed so simple.

“Never again” Have stayed at Super 8s before and they were OK but nothing super. But looking for a short night stay was not even great. Cheap yes but did not sleep well. The air did not work and the fan really did not do the job. Would have just use the out side air but it was a first floor room. Told them about the air and they said they would have someone check it out. Used my shower sandals to walk around the room. The beds were made but not sure if the other bed had clean sheets. The bathtub had hair in it and the floor may have been sweep but not mopped.

“Good price, good location, slooow elevators, variable staff.” This is a boutique hotel a half block off of Times Square, very close to a lot of theatres. We were in an upper room on an airshaft, so the room was relatively quiet for being so close to Times Square. There are many dining choices within an easy walk. A block from the Hershey and M&:M stores. It is a converted older building. Once you get past the glitzy lobby (the large saltwater fish tank is fascinating!) the actual product is so-so. We had a room with a double bed that was tiny. Barely enough room for a suitcase in the space around the bed. Room was clean and had a Bose radio and a big screen flat screen TV. Air conditioner is noisy but effective. Window in bedroom did not open. No microwave. Minibar. Shower, no tub. Shower was very good and amenities are interesting. I did see some other rooms that are bigger. The elevators are small and slow. Some of the staff are friendly and helpful, others less so. The doorman, for example, watches while people struggle to get their bags thru the doors. The concierge was helpful but the desk staff was somewhat surly. Used room service trays stayed in the stairwells for days, untouched. On the whole, my impression is that this was an unhappy team that needs a new leader. However the room was acceptable and the price reasonable for New York and the area. One concern is that the stairwells are open so that in case of a fire on a lower floor smoke would fill the upper floors. There are enclosed stairwells as well, but this strikes me as a hazard. Internet access is not free. No gym or pool in hotel; they give you a pass to a club in the Crowne Plaza that is large and very complete, two blocks away. This club has a pool, free weights, and lots of cardio and weight machines. Bring your own earphones. Towels provided.

“Convenient location with wonderful service” What a excellent choice! I recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency Baltimore and was thrilled with my experience. The hotel is super convenient to the inner harbor (from the second floor of the hotel, you can cross over a pedestrian bridge and are just a minute walk from the water taxi) and the hotel has an outdoor pool to cool off in after a day of seeing the sites of Baltimore. The hotel staff was friendly, efficient and always ready to help. In addition, my nephews loved the glass elevators and the beautiful views of the harbor. I will definitely stay at this hotel in the future!

“Very Good with a few recommendations” We got this hotel through Priceline for $100, high but it was very last minute. We were upgraded as Hilton Honors members at no additional charge. We had a comfortable corner room with a great view of Boston and the airport, no noise! The hotel needs to be mindful of all the garbage and room service trays left along the hallway from afternoon to next day, it was smelly and an eyesore. There was also a wedding at the hotel and the ceremony set up was in the middle of the lobby which was annoying the rest of the guests who were not part of the wedding. There has to be a better place for a ceremony. There was a time that guests were asked to go back up the elevator to their floors while the ceremony got underway. In our case, it made us be late for our dinner in Boston.

“Great location and Price plus friendly staff” We've stayed at this particular Omni in Austin for a few visits. They staff has ALWAYS been friendly. It's convenient to South Congress, St. Edward's University and the downtown area. The pool is awesome. And the room is always clean and cozy. We took our little dog on two of our visits. The staff was accomodating and very pleasant about our pet. We sometimes come across scowls and annoying comments regarding our dog...but never at this Omni. Our most recent stay was during the New Year weekend. The guests next door seemed to continue their party through the work week. I spoke to the front desk and they promptly moved us over to another floor. The only downside is that the lobby is a bit outdated. My husband says it looks very 70's. But I wasn't bothered by it.
“Cheap with good location” No frills but good for exploring the city- far from top of the line but affordable and clean.

“Highly recommended” We were most impressed. This hotel is easy walking distance to Times Square / Broadway / Madison Sq Gdns etc; and only a block away from the nearest underground station. While the room was exceptionally TINY one must remember that you only sleep there (you dont spend many waking hours in it!). We were even pleasantly surprised that the price included breakfast (eggs, bacon, hash, pancakes etc - we thought we'd get a bowl of cereal at best). Filter coffee; hot chocolate; and fruit juice is available free of charge, 24/7 in the lobby. Everything was clean and in good condition. We'd come again!

“Clean, inexpensive hotel at great location - perfect for any stay” I stayed at this hotel one night while on my way home from a late night flight into Hobby. Long story short, I was driving on Southwest Freeway and remembered the hotel was here (I'm a member of their points program) and I was too tired to barely keep my eyes open and needed a place to stay just for the night. Even though it was late and most people were in for the night, there was plenty of free self parking. The parking lot could use a little more lighting but I knew my car would be safe. The front desk clerk was very friendly and efficient. The elevators can be a bit noisy and slow but they were repairing one while I was there so perhaps they are all fixed by now. The bedrooms was a pretty good size (I had a King bed) with just enough furniture to seem neither empty nor cluttered. The TV isnt flat panel but there were a lot of channels. There isn't wireless internet but wired internet is provided free in each room (and the wire is long enough to sit in bed while using your laptop!) My room faced the Southwest FWY and I don't remember there being an issue with traffic noise, but it could have been because I was so tired. The blackout curtains really do black out the lights, I wish every hotel had these. The bathroom is a great size for one person but the vanity/coffee&tea area just outside the bathroom provides more than enough room. There are some interesting tea choices to balance out the boring "earl grey" flavour. I love the smell of the toiletries too! Overall Four Points Southwest met and exceeded my expectations for needing a place to sleep one night, but the location is great too - near the Galleria and West U!

“I didn't want to go home!” I stayed here for 5 nights on business in January 2007. You just can't say enough for this hotel. The rooms are well-equiped and very tastefully designed & decorated and the bed & bedding are heavenly. The livingroom furniture is new and extremely comfortable. The staff and manager are at your beck and call, and they sincerely want to make your every moment there a happy one. I befriended the bellman "George" who greeted me warmly every evening as I returned to the hotel and always had a kind word. The evening manager's reception offered a nice variety of generous and quality drinks and the atmosphere was cozy. The breakfast offered a nice variety of quality foods ranging from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets. There was plenty of fruit, some prepared and some whole, and there was a nice assortment of breads and juices. And of course there were the usual choices of cereals, along with french toast, scrambled eggs and bacon. I need not rave about the flatscreen TV in the livingroom as others already have. Though I will mention the well-stocked bathroom with Neutrogenia products including a shoe shine mit and a handy sewing kit, and the coffee cups and glasses that were a pleasant change from the paper ones usually offered. Shortly after I checked in, a sweet lady knocked on my door, asked if there was anything I needed and handed me 2 bottles of water. I love this place. I've stayed at 4 other hotels downtown and they aren't even in the same league as the the Embassy Suites, though I've paid more for my room at 3 of those hotels. I plan to be a loyal customer for years to come.

“Definitely worth it for the price” Rates were very reasonable. Facility was clean. Staff was polite. Room was quite small, but big enough for two people to stay in. You might not want to stay here if you were going to be in the room all the time, but you should be able to find enough going on in New York city to occupy your waking hours.... Bathrooms were shared, but there were four on the floor we were staying and we never had problems getting into one. Be advised the hotel does not have an elevator.

“Great location” Great location only one block walk from Union Station and Metro stop. We got a great rate here, but primarily wanted to be near the train station to avoid running around town to pick up luggage before getting a train home, so this was perfect. We walked to the Mall museums and Chinatown area, but took the Metro home at night, because there is nothing open in the vicinity and it was not recommended to walk on E Street from 7th over the Expressway. But the Metro is convenient and the train station is busy even at night, so there were no problems. The room is furnished elegantly with plenty of space for luggage (one king bed). The bathroom is cramped, but has plenty of counterspace for toiletries and towels. The bathsheets are huge and thick! There is a mini-bar with just enough room to store my water bottle overnight. They asked if we wanted a view or quiet, and we selected the room facing the street, with the usual city street noise, but it didn't bother us at night. We had both brunch and lunch at The Dubliner pub, and both were plentiful, but a little pricey. We went all the way to Dupont Circle for our Saturday morning breakfast at our favorite restaurant. Would definitely recommend this hotel if you can get a good rate, and would stay here again for convenience.

“Nice rooms, but nOsey street” Very nice style rooms with separate shower room and toilet room. My only real pet peeve is on the corner of the street called north Community house,,, the pedestrian walk to cross the street seems to made of special break that makes an annoying noise when cars whiz over them, of course I ask to be moved away from that and they claimed all only rooms are booked,, so if your a light sleeper like me I strongly suggest you avoid rooms facing community house rd and Johnston rd or in my case room 329

“Lovely hotel, great location.” Stayed here for a few nights with breakfast included, the rooms were great with one being larger than the other. The breakfast was great. It is worthwhile to join their select guest program for free internet and complimentry beverages delivered to your room each morning. The train is a short walk, this was a great way to get around DC, we used it to get to Union Station so we could get to New York. We ate at a few restaurants in the area they were all fantastic.

“Great Location, Super Views!” This is the 2nd year my family and I spent the 4th of July weekend in SF. We chose this hotel because we wanted to try another location away from the very busy Fisherman's Wharf area. We got a pretty sweet deal from the Hilton website which included free internet, parking and full buffet breakfast for our family of 4 which was really great considering we paid twice as much the year before for a standard room (no parking, no breakfast) at the Fairmount Ghirardelli Square. Upon check-in on Thursday (7/1), we were told that we would be upgraded to an executive level deluxe room (we originally booked a standard room, city view). Not sure why they upgraded us (maybe because I'm a Hilton Honors member?) but we didn't complain. We ended up with a great room with an amazing view of the Coit Tower and bay. The good stuff... A Great Location - Chinatown is across the street (I highly recommend Hunan Home which is just around the corner...the owner at mee mee bakery - the original fortune cookie factory or so they say they are, recommended this place and they were right on). North Beach (Little Italy) is just 2 blocks away (you can't go wrong with any restaurant there). We had a great meal every night! The streets (other than Chinatown and North Beach) were empty making it very easy for us to access major roadways, bridges and highways. Awesome Views from Bay View Rooms - Ask for high floors when booking and always book a bay view room. The views are picture postcard perfect! My kids loved watching the 4th of July fireworks from our room. The Staff - Really nice and friendly desk, restaurant and cleaning staff. It was a very busy hotel the weekend we stayed yet they were very courteous, prompt and friendly. One night, my daughter changed the safe code and we couldn't figure it out. Within 5 minutes of calling, maintenance came up and opened it for us, no problems. Room service on the evening of July 4th was quick (about 20 minutes) and pretty good. Tour Bus stops in Front of the Hotel - We didn't use it this time but the hop on/hop off tour bus stops right in front of the hotel which is very convenient. The bad stuff (just one)... It is Noisy Inside and Outside the Hotel - As high as we were on the 24th fl, we could hear every street noise (people, cars, sirens- everything!). It didn't help that there was a shooting two blocks away that weekend so we woke up to sirens blaring at 1am. Actually, there were sirens blaring everynight but my kids got used to it pretty quickly (I never did). And of course, the fireworks were going off till late in the evening in chinatown. It was noisy in our hallway too but I don't know if this is the case all the time at the hotel. We had a very large group of chinese tourist staying on our floor and they were pretty loud talkers walking down the hall. Overall, we would stay at this hotel again. Maybe not on a very busy weekend though.

“Comfortable, clean, convenient, congenial!” Two of our friends got married, and arranged for out-of-towners to stay at the Comfort Suites-Indianapolis on Kildeer Drive (Southport Rd. exit on I-65). What a great place! The suite was fine, the bed was comfy, the place was very clean and the staff was terrific! And you couldn't beat the rate they offered for the wedding guests! Downtown is just a short drive away, and the hotel is surrounded by good places to eat, including one of Jimmy Buffet's "Cheeseburger in Paradise" outlets. If you are some big-time celebrity, you won't be interested in this hotel. But if you are an average middle-class couple who is looking for a clean, comfortable place to stay in Indy, offering free breakfast, check out the Comfort-Suites on Kildeer Dr. on the south side of Indy!

“Perfect tourist location” My wife and I stayed for 5 nights from 19 May to 23 May. This was our second time stayijng at this hotel, the first being about 5 years ago. We will probably use the hotel on our next trip to New York - assuming the TripAdvisor reports comtinue to be favorable!. The location is perfect for tourists, theatre-goers, and shoppers. Rooms are quite spacious and bright with large windows. Housekeeping and overall customer service are very good. We paid $100 extra [ 4 hours x $25/hour] for a 6:00PM checkout which was worth the money given our late departure from JFK. Opted for the "bed & breakfast" special and glad we did. For breakfast, you can go out to local eateries or bring someting in from a deli, but the hotel's buffet selection, quality and convenience was wortth the sligt added cost. This time we had a "15" room overlooking Broadway. Prevouslsy, we had a "12" room facing west to the Hudson. The former will give you the excitemet of Brodway, the latter will give you some respite from the noise - particularly on weekends.

“Lovely, except for the noisy children” I had been in town on business on Chicago and was looking forward to a relaxing afternoon at the Four Seasons Spa, which came highly recommended by a friend from Chicago. I purchased a day pass and had an hour Swedish massage, and also ordered lunch to be brought in to me. The Positives: the dry sauna, the steamroom, the large towels, the accessible lockers and huge showers with all the amenities, the prompt luncheon service, the staff (very, very kind...too much so...see below), the eucalyptus-scented cool hand towels for after sauna/steamroom, the pool, the food, the variety of beverages in the pool area, the massage (EXCELLENT) and the fact that the Spa area is located on its own floor in relation to this large hotel so you are not bumping into hotel guests. The Negatives: This is my big peeve. And please don't get me wrong....I love children. However, there is a time and place for them, particularly in an upscale spa. I did not at all mind the children who were guests of the hotel having access to the pool, which is seperate from the Spa, Sauna, Steamroom and Showers/Locker Area. They were loud, as small (ranging in age from 2 to 10) children will be at swimming pools and did not mind this so much due to the fact that the lounge area for the pool where the juices and teas were located were seperated by a glass wall. I was however, VERY perturbed at the mommies who were seemingly oblivious to their noisy, loud, spoiled children running around the Spa area grabbing magazines and spilling juices unsupervised in areas they were not to be permitted. One child, about 8 years old, was dumping tea bags on the floor for fun. Mommy could see this child through the window and did nothing. I understood the Four Seasons Spa to be "child-free" except in the pool area. The staff knew the children were running around the Spa area and did nothing about it, perhaps out of fear of the mommies. They definitely turned a blind eye, and I can state definitively that these mommies and their children were not of any relation to anyone who owns the Ritz-Carlton group. At any rate, the relaxation of my massage quickly disappeared due to the children allowed in the spa area. If you luck out, you will visit on a day when children are truly not allowed in an area meant for adults who mean to relax. But do not count on the staff to handle it. I will try the Penisula Spa next trip.

“a fine small hotel” Very good "boutique" hotel near Dupont circle, rooms recently renovated and are spacious and very nice. My KIng bed room contained sofa and desk as well . Very nice staff, address you by name, eager to help. Perfectly adequate continental bkft in the small restaurant. We did not try it for dinner. Many restaurants in the Dupont circle area. Hotel about 2 blocks from Dupont circle metro, not a bad walk, perhaps a mile, to Georgetown or downtown to the mall. Had a very good rate on the room ($150) but valet parking is $40. Go a couple of blocks to M street where garage parking is $21 for 24 hrs or use the street itself Sat after 6PM and Sunday. No hotel gym but passes to the Y 1 block away. Join Kimpton club if not already a member for free wi-fi and free passes to the Y and joining is free.

“Functional but not special hotel in an area that is lacking” I'm going to divide my thoughts into function, style, service and location. In terms of function, the hotel was good. The water was hot, my room was clean and the bed was reasonably comfortable. The hair dryer didn't work, but if I cared I'm sure I could have gotten a replacement. The shower head was broken (stuck on the massage setting), but it was not a big deal. The drain didn't keep up with the water flow, and that bothered me a little. I would have asked for that to be addressed, but my colleague had the same problem in her room, so I figured it was just the way it was. All in all, it served the purpose. The lobby was less clean, and I attached a picture of a stairway in the lobby where there was loose dirt that I noticed on both days (in other words, it wasn't cleaned). In terms of style, with a few exceptions, it's mostly old looking. The art on the walls had been updated, there is an Aeron chair and the TV is modern, but other than that, it's really outdated. The wallpaper was buckling, there were chips in the door, and the furniture looked cheap and old. The hallways had big electrical panels exposed (like circuit breaker boxes). None of that really matters much except that it contributes to a feeling that the place is not special. The service was good. I asked for a late check-out and it was no problem. The people were friendly and responsive. They seemed to care. The concierge was not great in terms of recommending places, but that might be because there was nothing nearby to recommend. Which leads to the discussion of the neighborhood... The neighborhood has NOTHING. It was a 10 minute walk to anything reasonable. Also, the doors had those metal panels on the outside (see pictures) to prevent someone from breaking in, which I found troubling. The metal panels might be a holdover from a more dangerous time. Notwithstanding, I did not feel unsafe, but the metal panels combined with a complete lack of activity in the area made me wonder. I think if you have business in the area, it's not a bad place to stay; it's just not special place (except the service, which was good).

“So snobby people stay here?” Those of you who take the time to read my reviews of the various hotels I stay at while traveling should know by now that I like to stay at places that offer the best value for the dollar. Generally, my favorite hotel brands are Marriott and Omni. The Mark Hopkins is about the same price as the San Francisco Omni about 3 minutes east of it. Difference is, you get so much less for your money and there just seems to be a very different "air" about the place. Don't get me wrong -- Mark Hopkins is a beautiful hotel that sits atop Nob Hill. It really is a gorgeous hotel, with a very vintage 20s feel to it. The rooms and bathrooms are a bit on the small side. Unlike the Omni, you get charged for all the little anemeties including Internet at a whopping $15-$18 per night (pending on speed) plus taxes. I went with the $18 faster Internet package and my bill came to nearly $21 on Internet alone per night. At the Omni, you simply sign up for their reward program and your Internet is free. You also get complimentary hot or cold beverages delivered to your room with a paper at the door every morning. Don't expect that with the Mark Hopkins. Their standard rooms are on the bottom floors. This poses a problem is you are facing the street. The cable car had me up all night. It drags itself up the hill with a loud scraping sound that is bound to keep anyone awake. I had to be moved to another room at the opposite side of the hotel which worked out better. It was difficult to block light from the room as the shades do not overlap each other causing there to be a slit that allows an abundant amount of light to enter the room. So, if you don't want to be awakened at sunrise, you may be out of luck. For tech-heads like myself, there is a total lack of extra plugs available in the room to plug in your computer, phone charger, etc. I had unplug lamps just to iron my clothes. Still, the hallways and rooms have a very "classy" feel to them and the bedding is to die for. Got a great night's sleep once I was moved away from the cable car side of the street. The biggest problem with this hotel is the people it seems to attract. The last thing I want to do is insult anyone and I want to avoid saying everyone who stays at this hotel falls into a particular "class." However, I found most everyone I bumped into to be very snobbish. I was wearing jeans and a t-shirt during the California Indian Summer. I looked clean and neat. I can't tell you how many people dressed in business attire or better gave a look every time I got into the elevator. It was if there was a particular dress code at the hotel that need to be adhered to, or, if you didn't look the part you were looked down upon. The staff here was first-rate. Everyone from the bellhop to doorman to front desk personnel treated me exceptional. However, I dunno, I have just never stayed at a hotel where I felt as if I didn't belong with the majority of "class" that stayed here. I am used to staying at hotels where vacationers smile at one another or say hello in the elevators. Since the hotel sits at the very top of Nob Hill, there is nowhere to eat in walking distance without making the climb back to the hotel. I didn't want pay for a $30 per person breakfast at the Top of the Mark, so I opted to go across the street to the Fairmont where they have a little coffee shop around back. Would have been much happier to stay at a hotel that wasn't atop a steep hill where I could easily walk to other restaurants. Valet Parking is ridiculously priced, but probably no more than what any other hotel is charging which seems to average at $50 per night. Listen, I have nothing against anyone who wants to pay the price to stay at a luxury hotel like this that charges much and gives you little. Frankly, I think the Omni offers a little less elegance but gives you free Internet and morning beverages. Given a choice where to stay in San Francisco city, I would not return to the Mark Hopkins.

“Exceptional!!” I have read a few of these reviews and I am stunned by the negativity...My stay at The Driskill was exceptional from start to finish. The valets are very friendly and professional. The front desk personnel were very warm and helpful. In fact the person who helped us, took the time to come around the counter and show us a map of the highlights in the downtown area. The first thing you will notice about The Driskill is how good it smells...from the moment you walk into the lobby, it smells wonderful. The whole hotel is immaculate. Our Bellman was a very sweet and friendly young man, who was very careful unloading our bags. We went downstairs later, he greeted us by name. We stayed in a standard room...and it was small...but it is beautiful and cozy. In my travels, I have found this is normal though with a historic/boutique type hotel...so I was not dissapointed at all. The bed was very comfortable, and the linens were high quality. The bathroom was very small....but nicely appointed...even the tolietries that they provide are top notch. We ate at the 1886 cafe onsite and it was a wonderful surprise. I was expecting typical "cafe" food and was quickly impressed by the quality and impressive presentation...even the breadsticks they give you for an appetizer are quirky and delicious. We had a great night sleep and the check out process was easy and the desk personnel were equally wonderful on check out. I would stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat...and would recommend it to anyone.

“This hotel is awesome...good value if you use your AAA card!” We got a great deal by booking this hotel directly through the Hilton website and using our AAA card. We paid $180 per night and got an upgraded King Tower room that had an outstanding view. Our room even had a balcony with small bistro table and 2 chairs. The rate came with free wi-fi internet, valet parking, and a daily continental breakfast from Starbuck's. The breakfast was nice because you could get any grande drink, 1 pastry, 1 piece of fruit, and a bottle of water or juice. Yes the rooms are small, but so are all the rooms in San Francisco. Yes the parking is pricey, but this is the same everywhere, so search around and get an outstanding deal like we did. Our stay was nice, people were nice, good location, we loved it!

“Nice Hotel - Not convenient to nearby attractions, dining or shopping though” This is a very nice Homewood Suites. The front desk and all staff were very polite and helpful. The room was spotless and very comfortable. The breakfast options were typical, but my husband and I were VERY impressed that each morning, in addition to the regular breakfast attendant, there was a manager present who would direct guests to whatever they were looking for. It was a bit cold while we were there so I didn't get to see much of the pool or other areas. My only problem with this hotel is that it was difficult to find - every day and there is nothing near by. I generally try to find hotels within a short easy drive to restaurants, shopping, etc and there is NOTHING near this hotel. We also found the directions compared to the area street signs to be VERY confusing. Anway, the hotels is nice, but if you like to be closer to dining and groceries.. I'd suggest someplace else.

“Absolutely loved it” I had read several reviews about the Se and only booked because I got a very good deal. So its fair to say I had some apprehension given the mixed feelings of other reviewers, but any concerns very quickly disappeared upon arrival. It is very difficult to recognise from the street and I only found it because I knew it was next to the House of Blues. The valet & bell staff upon arrival were extremely friendly, and this continued inside with the reception staff & concierge friendly, attentive and very welcoming. The lobby area is very funky with a Zen inspired chic, and the enormous door from the street is a fun novelty. We were given a complimentary upgrade to a room overlooking the pool, our 10th floor vantage point gave us additional views of the city to the north. As some reviews have suggested, the room was quite small, but very comfortable and modern. The dark timber floors and stone bathroom were a nice touch but the pillow top mattress was certainly the highlight. It was so comfortable and easily one of the best hotel beds I've slept in. It is comparable, if not better, than Starwood's Heavenly beds. I really loved the room, but light sleepers beware. We weren't disturbed by the House of Blues - it was the pool area at night that turns into an outdoor nightclub/bar with loud music pumped out on the weekends. We were advised on check in of this, so it was no surprise to hear it from our room, but it didn't cause us any real disturbance. Suite & Tender, the onsite bar & restaurant is easily accessed, and whilst we didn't experience the bar, the restaurant was outstanding. The spectacular food was perfectly matched with exceptional service, and it was easily the best dining experience I've had in San Diego by a long way. I cannot speak highly enough of it. Valet parking is available at around $36 per night, but with in-out privileges, it is worth it compared to local garages. I overheard some staff chatting about possible new ownership, so whatever happens with the Se, I hope they don't change the format or service levels too much. This is an excellent San Diego hotel in a prime location with the delights of the Gaslamp Quarter at your doorstep. The outstanding service & friendliness enhanching what is a fantastic and extremely comfortable property made for a truly memorable and positive stay.

“Great Resort!” Stayed at Westin La Cantera during my visit to San Antonio. The resort is just beautiful and in the perfect location just outside of the city center near Six Flags and great shopping. The hotel facilities are well taken care of and very manicured. Rooms are beautifully appointed and housekeeping service is very attentive. There's a gentleman that plays the guitar and sings in the lobby every early evening which was very enjoyable over a nice drink from the lobby bar. There is a Starbucks in the resort for those in needing the Sbux fix. The resort also has several other bars and restaurants worth visiting which I will review separately. One thing that I really loved about this place is the friendliness of the staff. Everywhere you go, you encounter someone with a big smile and a genuine desire of help. Absolutely loved Ruby at the front desk, she is just fantastic and do not be surprised if you find her recognizing you by name every time you see her. With such large resort, I don't know how she does it but the point is she does! Views from the resort are also beautiful from the city to one of the two beautiful golf courses. I can't wait to return!

“Great Place and Location” We selected this hotel as part of a package for an extended weekend in Seattle. To start with, the location is great, right on Lake Union near several restaurants, downtown, the Space Needle, etc. We had a car but you could probably do without if needed. The light rail and busses run right by the hotel and take you all over the city with frequent and easy access. If you do have a car, the hotel charges $19 to park in their secured garage or you can find metered street parking for less than half (which we did with no problems). The hotel has recently been remodeled and the rooms are some of the best I have seen for this brand. Very roomy, nice décor, nicely equipped modern kitchens, great comfortable bed, plenty of drawer and closet space, large flat screen tvs in both the bedroom and living areas. It is easy to spread out and even have a little privacy if you have more than a couple of you. For the working types, there is a nice work area with free high speed internet and comfortable desk and chair. The staff was very helpful and knowledgeable about the area. The hotel does appear to cater to families (and allows the family pet too which you see many of so that may or may not be OK with you). The hotel is busy and sometimes elevators and such are slow due to this but while the hotel was quite full, we never heard our neighbors (the lobby was a buzz but the rooms were quiet). We had a room that faced the back (not the lake) but this was fine and quiet. The lake side actually is along a fairly busy street so it has a little more noise but you get the views of the marinas, seaplanes, etc. I ran one morning along the lake which was great and I felt safe (and saw other runners out). Of course exercise caution since it’s a mix of nice residential, commercial, industrial and some transient all in the area but overall you should be fine to walk to local places, etc. They gym has decent equipment (but not a lot of it). A couple treadmills, a couple elliptical’s, one bike and some weights (barbells and a universal weight machine). The gym area is small and gets crowded and a little stuffy (indoor right by the pool) but if you go off –hours you should have no problem. They have an indoor pool and spa which is great for the kids and have adult only swimming hours also (later in the evening). The breakfast is extensive but busy. There are also some great restaurants within walking distance offering all kinds of cuisine and many with outdoor patios onto the lake. Nothing beats having a drink or bite on the lake front on a sunny day in Seattle. I would definitely stay here again, loved the location, the room and the staff.

“most amazing staff and lovely boutique hotel” the staff here were the most accommodating people I have ever met. Our group (my boyfriend and I and three of his friends) caused quite a scene in their lobby and fought over where we were sleeping. They attempted to give us various room options and patiently waited for us to sort things out, offering us apple cider, soft drinks and snacks all the while. They have free dvds to borrow during your stay for use in the room. The bed is quite high off the ground but comfortable. The shower is large enough for two to fit and good pressure. Definitely reccommend this. continental breakfast was included as well.

“Not bad, but not great” A co-worker and I shared a 2 double bed room here Sunday, June 11 - Wed, June 14. The NeoCon conference was nearby and the rate (via our company travel site) was $439/night. OMG. Given that most of Chicago is booked, we knew it would be pricey. The hotel was fine. We checked in about 2 and there were no double rooms, they asked us to check back around 4. We did some shopping and eating and came back later. Were sent to a high floor (14?) to check in and our room faced East. Never got as far as the window as the room was unmade, looked as someone had literally just crawled out of the bed. My co-worker hadn't even shut the door and we hauled out of there, back downstairs where we were met with an "Oh, we figured that out as you went up" and a minor apology but they acted like it was no big deal. Not a huge deal, but more than a small apology might have served better. We then ended up in 612 RIGHT across from the elevator. The view (ha) was of the roof one floor below us. Luckily we had no hallway noise. Given the rate, would you expect to pay for coffee in the room? $4.00 to make a pot of Starbucks coffee? I think not. Other than that, the room was fine, although the shower drained slowly. The location is excellent and for a far lower rate (maybe via Priceline?) this would be a great hotel.
