Given the rate and the lackluster service, I'd say it was only average

“Good location, good quality” We got a room in the executive floor with a city view : - room are very clean and comfortale - marvellous view Breakfast at the executuve lounge was OK, but not exceptionnal and crowded. Fitness center is very good with a lot appliances. Business center is not OK : printer doesn't work during our stat, low speed internet connection. It is not acceptable for a such standing hotel. Internet connection in the rrom is not free and was very expensive. This was a problem.

“All Style and no Substance!” On arrival here, we found Front Desk Staff to be pleasant, Bell Boy also very helpful. We had a LOndon Suite. when you first see the room, it looks very stylish, but on closer inspection, it then dawns on you, that you are in for a very uncomfortable stay. Lounge has a sofa, thats too uncomfortable to sit on, it also has stains all over it. slippy floor area, large desk, with the most stupid mirror above it, when you look in it you feel sick, it distorts everything - pointless. Positive - free Internet. Room also freezing, even with heating turned right up. Bedroom area - Comfortable Bed, again very cold, even with heating on. Nice ipod Dock. Dressing area- What a waste of space, all thats in here is an Ikea style hanging rack! very cheap looking. Beathroom - This is AWFUL, so tiny, all done in a strerile, swimming bath style. freezing cold, no bath, shower,that lacks any decent water pressure, so all the hype about the double rain head shower, is total rubbish, its very hard to wash your hair and get it rinsed, if you are a lady with long hair like me! I hated this bathroom. It could have been so much better, for instance ditch the stupid closet space and get decent bathrooms! After a long day shopping in New York, you want to come back to your hotel and chilax for a while before dinner - maybe have a soak in the bath etc. You cant do this here!!!! We ate in Maze - this was very good. Service was excellent. Staff were discreet, a very british type service, which I like. I dont like the in your face type service that you get quite a lot over here! Overall, would never stay here again. We cut our stay short here, and went home early, as this spoilt our trip. We Love modern hotels, and reguarly stay at The Soho in London, which is very trendy, but also uber comfortable, with superb bathrooms and sofas etc. If you want Just syle but no substance then this is the Hotel for you!!!!!!!!

“Would like to give it 4 stars.. But” The hotel lobby makes a great first impression as does the super friendly front desk service who upgraded me to a suite at no extra charge. The room was phenomenal, spacious and the city view was great. The etro toiletries and cloudlike king bed are amazing. I really enjoyed my stay here, until I woke up at 3am to dying smoke detector batteries in my room. Maintenance aka "engineering" came and fixed them right away, but it was not fun to wake up to a high pitched beeping noise in the middle of the night. I was also excited to use my kimpton rewards $15 minibar credit. I took a 2 small snacks that were clearly under the $15 credit. However, I was billed for two charges of $16 and $17 on two separate days after my stay. These charges were refunded within 48 hours after contacting kimpton. I wish I could rate this hotel higher, but I can't.

“Rooms and lobby are nice” I have been lucky to get the nicer rooms when I have stayed here. There are probably 70 or 80 rooms that are outside facing the pool and these would be very noisy. The rooms are large and comfortable and have nice updated furniture. The only issue I have is that when I put the do not disturb sign up so I could sleep in, the maids would call me to inform me that my do not disturb sign was on. Isn't the whole point of having a do not disturb sign is so that you are NOT disturbed?? That part didn't really make sense but overall I had no complaints about the room. The only real turnoff is that the hotel doesn't appear to participate in Sheraton's Best Rate guaranteed program. I called the hotel hotline and told them I found a better rate on the internet and they asked what the rate was. When I told them, they said that would be no problem, just inform the front desk and they could honor that rate. When I called the hotel directly, they stated that the rate I found did not qualify for the best rate guaranteed offer because the hotels.com reservation would not guarantee bed-type. I stated that I would be willing to pay the same price without a guaranteed bed type through the hotel directly and they refused and directed me back to the hotel hotline. After being transferred, I was then quoted a rate even higher than what was on sheraton.com. I called the hotel back and asked if I could speak with a manager about negotiating a long-term rate and they took my information and never called me back. Basically, the hotel policy is take the rate on the internet or we don't want your business.

“Fantastic property” I see mixed reviews of this hotel. I think this is my 3rd or 4th visit here. This time I give it a top rating. First of all, I was upgraded to a junior suite without asking. That is very much appreciated and the room is spacious with a separate living area. The staff have been friendly and helpful. As an HH member, I was given free wi-fi access and also a complimentary continental breakfast. A hot buffet upgrade only costs $10.00. The cold buffet is absolutely wonderful and one of the best I have seen. You will find every imagineable delight including delicious pastries, fruits, vegies, and much more. I have a corner room and it has been very quiet - I have no noise complaints whatsoever. The location is perfect for me so I give this a thumbs up!

“normal hotel, but great for NYC” We chose this hotel over others basically because of the price and the good reviews on tripadvisor. We were not disappointed. The hotel is located in Chinatown and near little Italy, just a couple of steps from the metro station Grand Street, which is a plus. The accomodation is just standard, with normal-sized rooms, shower only in the bathroom, and queen bed. You have coffee maker, tv and wi-fi in the room. GThey do offer breakfast, which consists mainly of sweet things like muffins, cereals and waffles. The rooms are clean and there' s no carpet on the floors. The price, slightly more than 100€ a night, would be inapproprate for the structure, was it not in NYC. As a matter of fact, I do suggest you stay at this hotel while in NYC because it is practically the best you can get from the city, if you do not want to pay 200-300€ a night.

“インターネット料金込みだったら良いのに。。” 立地がどの地下鉄の駅からも10分弱位歩くので、少し不便かなと思いますが、 部屋も広く、キッチンが付いているのでとても便利です。 ベッドの高さが日本人には少し高すぎますが、寝心地はとてもよかったです。 1aveに隣接していますが、騒音も気にならず、とても快適でした。 スタッフやベルの方は、皆さんとてもフレンドリーで良かったです。 ただ最近どんなに安いホテルでもWifiは無料なのに、 こちらはしっかり1日$12も取られます。 それがなければ、もっと点数は高かったかな?と思います。

“Perfect Stay Except for One Thing That's Easy To Fix” We travel to Chicago once a quarter and plan to stay at the Trump Tower from now on. the location is perfect and the view from my room, which I am looking out of now is sublime. The service has been super friendly and my room is decked out with well-thought out amenities. My bathtub is the nicest ever. It is modern with very luxurious spa products but has a homey touch with the shelf you can rest your juicy novel one while you soak. The pillow menu is fun and the choices of snacks and drinks in the mini-bar is eclectic in a good way. in short, the room is as nice as it gets. I love to exercise and was very impressed to see the Technogym weights and the yoga DVD included in the room. We have a spa room and there actually is room if you were inclined to workout in the room. I decided to take advantage of the excellent workout facilities and attend the spin classes that were offered. Sonya, the spin instructor, is as good as any instructor I have ever had. She is very motivating and her winning personality along with the super friendly people who regularly attend made me come back the next day. So here's my complaint: the temperature in the spin studio is almost unbearably hot to work out in. There is an extra charge of $30 to take the class so I am hoping that the management will use my $60 to buy some ceiling fans or even standing fans to help circulate the air in that stuffy space. I am hoping to see them when I come back in the fall!

“Great for business, fun location” Loved it! I have stayed all over Chicago for work trips, and would definitely return to Cass for the neighborhood, the value, and the basic conveniences of the rooms. Great price, great location with lots of restaurants and shops nearby, clean rooms, good free breakfast and free wi-fi. It's all you need for a simple stay in the city! Nice recent renovation of lobby and breakfast area. Contemporary design in new room decor. Windows opened in each of the rooms to let in fresh air (a big perk for me); small but clean, with very friendly staff who offered good recommendations in walking distance.

“Fairly good” Booked on the strength of reviews I found this Holiday Inn to be ok only. Staff were a bit distant, as is the location - although they provide a free shuttle to Andrew metro station, which is actually only 8mins walk away anyway. Town isn't too far, but it does take up time so bear it in mind. Rooms a little tired, lifts old and slow, but free breakfast, wifi, coffee all make it value for money.

“Pleasently Surprised” I stayed at the hotel last night on business because we were taking clients to the theater downtown. I usually try and stay at full service hotels although this downtown Courtyard was very nice. The historic building was quaint and my room was one of the largest I've ever had in a Courtyard. It was clean, the linens were nice and the staff very friendly and accommodating. I had breakfast in the restaurant and it was excellent as well.

“middle of the road” I recently stayed 4 nights at the Novotel Times Square as my normal haunt the Sofitel was just too expensive. The hotel is centrally located at 52nd St/Broadway and ideally located for any tourist activities (if one must). The entrance at street level is rather glum and down heel, up an elevator to the 7th floor lands you on the lobby and restaurant floor. The lobby is bright and airy. Unfortunately at 1 pm my booked room was not ready and I was told by the altogether not too friendly receptionist at the separate A-Club check in counter that I would have to wait til 3 pm which is official check in time. I wasn't too happy about the lack of welcome or the wait time after a transatlantic flight but at least one of the other staff got on the case and after an hour I got my room. Despite the reservation stating "KING BED WONDERFUL TIMES SQUARE VIEW" the view was of the back of buildings onto 8th Av. so technically not what I had booked but I was happy to get to my room. A voucher for an A-Club Platinum drink was handed over at check in. The corridors are bland and slightly worn out as was the room. Wear and tare has not been kind to the hotel and while there was nothing seriously wrong with the room it certainly showed its age and lack of upkeep. The bathroom was standard tourist size and not exactly spotlessly clean. Toiletries were unbranded Novotel and nothing special. The bed was large with a thin duvet and a good choice of pillows. Sleep quality was ok though unfortunately the air condition (despite what the display said) had only two settings: off and arctic rendering the duvet too flimsy to be warm (outside temperature was 39c so aircon was a must). Internet access was only available via paid wifi and if like me you travel with more than one laptop and iphone you must pay for each gadget's access separately which was very expensive and not acceptable. Very positive (and better than the Sofitel) was the fact that all TV channels were available in HD. The restaurant served a decent buffet breakfast ($25) which was good and offered great views over Times Square. The best part of the hotel was the outside terrace which had plenty of seating (limited service during the day) and is available to smokers. Room service was good and well priced. I had a fantastic steak and frites one night which was better than the equivalent in the Sofitel. I had arranged for a late check out which was confirmed on the day of departure for which I was very grateful. The rates were very high and 4 nights came to $1840. However it should be noted that all hotels during this week were expensive or sold out. Verdict: The Novotel is a standard tourist hotel and while basic in many respects offers a decent service. It is not luxury or even upmarket but if you get a good rate it should be fine. Some more loving attention to maintenance, customer service (though some receptionists were great, the initial welcome was not) and cleaning would make it better. While A-Club Platinum members per rules get nothing other than points at Novotel I was offered a drinks voucher and late check out. Points were credited correctly within 24 hours.

“Great location” Well you can't beat the location, right at Market and Powell St. So if your looking for downtown shopping you can't beat this hotel. It is a little dated and could us an update. But the rooms are a good size, very clean and comfortable.

“Excellent stay!” This new hotel is well maintained and clean throughout! The housekeeping was excellent and the staff were very helpful! My daughter and I spent a lot of time in the indoor pool area and had a great time! We were glad the pool was inside because we Seattleites are not used to the heat! The pool area was clean and had four colored streams of water flowing into the pool. No complaints! Good price and great service! Blaine at the front desk made us feel welcomed and went out of his way to help out (when we burnt our popcorn).

“Almost a home run - so close that I would have given it 4.5 score” I arrived early and they were kind enough to get me a room right away. May have been the luck of the draw - but kind. I had asked for a room with two double beds - as I had 3 days of business and then a friend was joining me. I was on the 7th floor - 2 floors above the lobby. At first I was disappointed being on a lower floor - but it worked. I would avoid the 6th floor only because the gym is on that floor and it is open extended hours - which may lead to more noise in the hallway. Speaking of the gym...the workout is getting there - LOL but really it is a great gym with a pool, state of the art gym equipment, steam rooms and really clean. The only misses were the housekeeping staff - they clearly do not read english - which I have no problem with - but they need to speak with their supervisor if they cannot read the note (and tip) I left. I wanted my window left cracked (it was closed) and I had asked for extra Decaf coffee. Also, I had requested turn down service each night - and it was only done 1 night. When I called - they were prompt to send someone quickly - and the turndown staff does a great job of refreshing the room and bathroom. Overall the hotel is in a GREAT location - centrally located - a quick walk from the T (several different T stations - Downtown Crossing, South Station, Chinatown and several others). Very close to Chinatown - attached to a Macys, near many theaters and near the Boston Commons. A couple of quick tips - great and inexpensive lobster at Peach Farm - Chinatown - close to a CVS and the concierge had great restaurant suggestions. I did eat at the Avenue one - the restaurant - the food was very good (lunch) and reasonably priced. I did drink in the bar and wish the red wine choices were more varied. Oh, and one more note: the weekdays the clientele was strickly business - the weekend is a WHOLE different (and louder) crowd - be forewarned

“Good value for what you get” I'm one of those people looking for hotels that are "clean and safe" at a reasonable price. HIE fit the bill. It is located on a busy street (traffic noise except 2-5am) about 15-20 minute walk from the Space Needle, waterfront, and Westlake along streets with other hotels, apartments, parking lots. So not in the heart of tourist sites. Few pedestrians at night. Bus stops about 2 blocks away. Taxis cost $6-12 to downtown destinations. Parking as mentioned before. We had the 2Q bed, 2 bath suite. The bedroom was large enough with vanity in room. Second full bath at entrance to living room. Living room had door to separate from bedroom and contained couch, coffee table, small table with chair, TV. Microwave, frig, and sink near door. Stain on living room carpeting. Rest of rooms seemed clean. We had one mechanical problem that was repaired the day we reported it. Maid replaced towels despite our hanging them up each day. She missed our room one day, but I think it may be because part of our party checked out. Room did have an odor, so we opened the windows each day while we were out. Traffic noise was loud to me so I ran the fan and wore ear plugs. Staff was extremely helpful with the reservation, check in/out, area questions, etc. One person seemed to be in training and needed some work to understand urgency of guest requests, but I think she'll get there under the guidance of the rest of the staff. Pool was tiny (did not use). Exercise room basic (did not use). Breakfast room seated 60 with some variation in the hot food each day. I thought it was generous. Free wifi and two computers/printers in a small room. A friend got a snack/drink at the adjacent HI and said it was fine.

“Another great Stay” Have stayed here several times..usually for Sounders Matches......I always book a suite when possible and did again this time. I booked through hotels.com because it always seems to be cheaper than the hotel website. The only mix up was they initially gave me a king bed room instead of a suite. They corrected the error fairly quickly. this suite had a little different layout than the others I have had and seemed a little smaller but it met our needs. Staff is always friendly and helpful..rooms are clean...and location is prime...just remember the trains in the morning can wake you up, but just bring ear plugs. With this location you are always paying for location, location, location. Not gonna get free breakfast or parking..but the location makes the expierience. As far as the restaurant and bar(Jimmy's on first) never been a huge fan..always so so....but there are some options near the hotel like Elysian for good beer and food or Pyramid accross the street. Overall, another great stay at Silver Cloud.

“Beautiful Hotel, If You Can Get A Good Price” I usually stay at a much cheaper hotel in San Diego, but when I saw the Days Inn at $59, I jumped. The place was fabulous, really only a few small steps (bad breakfast, lukewarm customer service) away from a 4 star hotel. (Yeah, I know it's a Days Inn!) The furnishings were beautiful, the lighting was great, the view was fabulous, the bed and pillows comfy, and there's plenty of room. So I swore my loyalty to this new hotel, then went back to book it for my next trip two weeks later, and discovered it was now $119, double the old price. Is it worth that price? Probably, if that's your budget. But I would guess that you wouldn't choose Days Inn first at that price. Bear in mind that the San Diego hotel market is terribly tight, and even bad rooms command a high price here... But if you see it again at $59, book it, you'll be thrilled.

“Gorgeous View!” We stayed at the Fairmont to celebrate our 23rd wedding anniversary. I booked a tower suite after reading the room/rate differences thinking that would be best for us. I opted for $25 extra for a higher floor if available at checkin and $20 more for early checkin seeing that we arrived at around 11am. The front desk gentleman and the bell service were very polite and helpful with our needs and questions. We were booked in the Tiburon Suite which was amazing! The room was huge with a corner view of the city, we could see the bay bridge as well as the Golden Gate from the 20th floor. The room came equipped with a telescope so you could read even the street signs far below and plan our route to Chinatown. This view was so wonderful that I never turned on the 2 flat screen TV's, opting to only enjoy the beautiful city instead. The bathroom was nicely appointed in marble and granite. The towels were great, the robes were great, the bed was comfy. Their were 2 air temp control buttons in the room, 1 for the living room and 1 for the bedroom. There was a mini bar which we did not use but no fridge to add our own items. If needed, I'm sure the hotel would have brought us one. We dined in the Laurel Court Restaurant and Bar twice, once for dinner and once for breakfast. The staff was engaging and very polite. The food was very good on both occasions. For breakfast one day I sent my husband to the El Centro cafe for pastries and coffee and it was good also. We used the Hertz service to get a rental car for a day to head out to wine country. I thought the gas rates were crazy, gas costs $1 higher in San Francisco than home but that was not Hertz or the Fairmont's fault of course. They brought the car straight to the hotel garage and we had to return it to a place 6 blocks up the street and catch a taxi back,(don't poke fun of me for not walking 6 streets, it's all up a steep hill!) it's a shame they didn't offer a ride back to the hotel considering what we paid for the rental car ($127 including gas.) Don't park at the hotel because they want $62.50 per night for parking! The lobby and the walls of photos and history were beautiful and interesting. This is one of the nicer places I've stayed (not counting the S. Pacific for obvious reasons). I would definitely recommend it to anyone coming to San Francisco. If you come here, join the club ahead of time, we were granted free wifi and access to the work out facilities though we never used that work out room. Membership is free. We did experience a 4.0 quake while sleeping on the 20th floor at 5:33am. It didn't even wake us. We found out about it by text 30 minutes later from my mother in law.

“What a dump” This place is a dump with the laziest most unhelpful staff. The room was dirty, smelled funky and the bathroom grout was full of mold. The staff is painfully slow and any question or request was met with an attitude of why are you bothering me. This place is terrible and at $150 ridiculously overpriced. Will never stay there again. Unfortunately I didn't check the Tripadvisor reviews before booking so I have no one to blame but myself.

“Disappointed” I stayed here the weekend of July 8-10 with my mom. The hotel has a great location; it is only a few blocks away from major attractions, which is essentially why I decided to stay here. (Also I booked the room through the company's website in February, and received a 20% discount through the pre-pay and save). We arrived early at the hotel, and the very pleasant worker at the front desk stored our bags. He assured us that he would rush our rooms and call us when it was ready. (I expected this since check-in is at 3, and we arrived at 11:30). When I did not receive a call, I became skeptical. We got back to the hotel at 3:45, our room was STILL not ready. We waited an additional 30 minutes before I asked to speak with a manager. The manager offered an apology and a complimentary breakfast or a late check-out. When I declined both, she stated that was all she could do since I booked through a third party (inferring that I did so through a travel website). When I told her that I booked through the company directly, she apologized and stated that she was looking at the wrong guest information. She then offered to take my room down to $199 for the night. Overall, the staff workers were very friendly and apologetic. However, no explanation as to why the room was not ready was given. (We were also not the only people waiting on our room). The beginning of our stay here was just extremely disappointing. With dinner reservations set for 6 PM, we did not make it up to our room until 4:45 and felt rushed. This is unacceptable-especially since we arrived at 11:30 AM! Due to this inconvenience, I will not be returning to this hotel on my annual NYC trip. I am positive there are numerous other hotels in NYC that can check-in guests on time. Cons: Too dark (in lobby and in bathroom), elevators are extremely small, no fan in the bathroom, hardly any outlets in the double room, potent smell upon entering hotel, front desk is not noticeable upon first entry. Pros: Friendly staff, great location

“Loved the hotel - pub disappointing” We found ourselves on the top floor (25) of this hotel - gulp!! But, it was a decent "Sleep Advantage" room, nice and clean and in an excellent location. Bathroom very compact. The reception staff were extremely friendly, which is more than I can say for the Business Centre Receptionist!!! We stayed in the hotel for 3 nights and visited the Elephant & Castle pub on our first evening and had a superb meal. We decided to visit the pub again on our second evening and were extremely disappointed - 3 out of 4 meals were returned as cold (yes, should have been hot). We did notice that there was a complete change of staff from the first night. In fact 2 of the meals (steaks) were returned no less than 3 times and were still inedible. They were very apologetic and they only charged us for 2 meals and our drinks but we were so looking forward to our evening. Needless to say, the tip got smaller and smaller! Having asked for the steaks to be "well done" they were, but on the outside only, and raw inside with blood oozing. On our third night we gave it a miss. What a shame! The hotel had a decent sized pool on the 8th floor with a good sitting area.

“A nice experience” We had 2 nights at theRennaisance and were totally happy.The jail comment in a previous review is very strange and totally unwarrented. What jail? A very nice and safe area. The room was very nice with the bed being one of the best ever. I was a little nervous about the hotel being at the top of the hill but it wasn't as bad as expected. It is so near great restaurants and shopping. The walk down to water is easy. The walk back up is tough but we took cabs if we were down by the water. The hotel staff were very friendly and always said hello in elevators and around the hotel. The concierge staff helped us greatly and were very nice. Of course it is not a 4/5 star hotel but we had a 5 star experience overall and would return anytime.

“Modern and Minimal” Lobby was very hip, staff was very nice but nobody took our bags up to our room for us. We had a small room but it was all that we really needed since we only slept in the hotel room. Sheets and mattress were fantastic, as were the towels and closet space. Only complaint is that they must have done some repair work in our room over a panel and didn't blend the drywall in with it. Splotchy work.

“Great business hotel, service is over the top” I have stayed at several St Regis properties. This is a business hotel!! If your looking for a first class property to conduct business this is a great choice. Dinning options are first class, rooms are well appointed. Fitness center is very good, pool is subpar for a property of this caliber. Hotel staff is excellent and greet you by name from the valet to the front desk. Great stay for business if your looking to vacation and need a pool make this a 4 star property.

“NOT ALL IT SHOULD BE” Triangular-shaped, Harry Weese designed, and still visually striking after 30 years, river or lake views from almost all rooms are spectacular and among the best in this magnificently beautiful city. But not all was as expected, leading one to conclude that management has unnecessarily and surprisingly become miserly on some aspects of hotel appointments and appearance. An unready room, which had been changed from king to double and previously confirmed with Swissotel central reservations and the hotel itself, had been overlooked, resulting in an unready room at a 345pm check-in. To the hotel's credit, but only at my request, Alex, an assistant manager, corrected the oversight, furnishing a full breakfast voucher as an apology. (Breakfast is excellent with made-to-order eggs, but otherwise rather expensive.) Because of the building's architectural footprint, the mostly low-ceilinged lobby wanders hither and yon without adequate sineage, and is surprisingly dark and colorless. Yet, the 6 new elevators are among the fastest in town, and computer controlled from the elevator lobby and not in the elevator itself. The Front Desk, while official and courteous, yet seemed stressed (confirmed by later visits), and lacked the welcoming attitudes characteristic of deluxe hotels. The same could be said for the concierge desk - stressed - and also furnished incorrect information about a church mass. Yes, the hotel was fully booked, but aren't staff trained for such situations? Guest rooms are certainy bright and well-appointed, quiet, excellent quality mattress, 42 inch flat screen television that actually was HD (and not a big screen analogue TV as common in many hotels.) But no CD player as shown on web-site. The bath appointments, such as the silver dollar sized soap and downscale motel - sized no-name shampoo and bath accessories, were a major surprise for a quality hotel chain. The aroma, or was it an odor, in the bath, could have been from the cleaning solution or from the soap, or perhaps both or none. Whatever it was, change the bath accessopries to match the hotel quality. Other indications of a lack of guest consideration included only a few free newspapers at the front desk and restaurant - and they had to be snatched early - and a fee-based internet. Contrast all of this with the James Hotel, where I stayed 5 nights in July. At the James, local, national, Wall Street Journal, are available in sufficient quantity seven days a week. Internet is free in business center. Deluxe bath accessories are far superior to Swissotel, CD players with excellent mini-speakers are part of room appointments, and the smiling staff is much more accommodating and knowledgeable than at Swissotel. The Palm Restaurant at Swissotel can be highly recommended, especially the happy hour menu with generously-sized mini portions at reasonable prices. Swissotel Chicago management was made aware of these issues in reply to computer - generated query, but to date has not replied. These complaints seem petty and overall the hotel merits patronage, but little things still mean a lot. A deluxe hotel is expected to be deluxe in every category from front desk welcome to concierge awareness, to bath accessories. Thus, in these areas of inn-keeping, the Swissotel Chicago has not succeeded.

“Good hotel, decent decor, thin walls” The hotel is in a decent location downtown with a nice bar in the lobby as well as a Shula's restaurant. The rooms are nicely decorated, bathrooms are large enough, the walls are a bit thin though so you will hear your neighbors. The beds are really comfy. The workout facility is in the basement and is not huge so it fills up very quickly.

“Once again, my home away from home!” I visit LA about three times a year and, once again I was at BGHI in December. I've ALWAYS had terrific service from the staff; it's one of the reasons I continue to stay there. Over the years, the ownership has upgraded the grounds, pool area, bar and lobbies. I've heard they're upgrading the restaurant -- a LONG LOOOONNNGGG overdue chore (as my previous reviews have noted) -- and I hope it includes an upgrade to the menu as well. I'm surprised by the recent complaints about the staff. Yea, the front desk staff aren't always at attentive as they could be, but everyone else at the hotel has ALWAYS been extremely service-oriented. The wait staff in the restaurant are the best, especially the breakfast team. I've been tempted to try other hotels in the valley -- and I've done it several times -- but the others cannot compare. Yes, the rooms are dated, but what can do with the old cinder block walls? My experience? If you smile at the staff and treat them with respect, you'll be rewarded in spades. I agree that the wireless is VERY slow. I hope the hotel works on this!

“Loved Staying at the Silver Cloud” This hotel is fantastic if you are attending a Mariners or Seahawks game. You can't get any closer to the parks. From my hotel room, I could see directly into Safeco field where the players were stretching on the grass. The beds are incredible. I wish my bed at home was this nice. The TV's are ~48" flat panel LGs. The bathrooms are large and spotless. There is a wetbar with fridge & sink in the room. And there is a very nice 1850 watt hairdryer in every bathroom (unlike the 1200 watt dryers that you see in most hotels). The staff was helpful. Check in was fast and painless

“Comfortable, elegant Hotel” I stayed one night at the Kitano and it was a very pleasant experience. Small room but very comfortable bed- nice amenities- flat screen TV, luxury bath products. There was a nice buffet breakfast that was a bit pricey- $29 - for what they offered- no omelettes for example, but very comfortable and great coffee. As far as the location, I liked that it was in a quiet neighborhood that was very accessible to midtown. It was nice to be away from all the hubbub at night and in the early AM. Recommended.

“Super extras with Select Guest membership” Stayed here overnight in Jan '10. I had registered online (for free) with select guest after confirming my reservation. My room key was waiting, and the benefits I received included free pressing of one item, free shoeshine, complimentary bottled water in the room, complimentary morning hot and cold beverage delivery to the room, and complimentary wifi. I asked about breakfast and the checkin clerk gave me a free breakfast voucher too! Room was good, well appointed - Bose music player. Excellent wifi (requires password from front desk). Pleasant breakfast with staff who were a delight. Overall a surprise world of benefits for a free online membership and an array of excellent features for just $105 a night - it's hard to beat.

“Typical Westin” The hotel can be a little tricky to reach by car as you try to exit from Thomas Circle on a one way street. Room were normally sized and fully acceptable. Has a good meal in the restaurant that has some imaginative dishes. The only problem was the front desk which couldn't cash a $20 bill. Unbelievable that a hotel of this size could cash a 20. They sent me to the gift shop which wouldn't give me change unless I bought sometime. I finally got change from the doorman. Imagine, the doorman has more cash in his pocket the the front desk. But, on balance, it was a good room and I got a good nights sleep.

“Ideal location” This hotel was in the best location for our trip to Graceland. Staying near Graceland you only have two choices and we chose this as it had better reviews. It was fine for what we wanted, a comfortable bed and a hot shower. We are so Elvis-mad that we didn't notice any problems, so it suited us and our needs. Free parking and free breakfast was a good addition, although I think they need more tables for breakfast, but where would they put them? We wouldn't think twice about staying here again.

“A few issues, but great stay” My daughter and I stayed at theWit for 3 nights while in Chicago for her college orientation. I originally booked a 2 Q bedded room for 2 nights at $299 each night, then decided to add 1 more night a couple of weeks before our trip. Unfortunately, the 2 Queen bedded room wasn't available, so I had to book a 1 bedroom suite for quite a bit more money-$409. I was told by central reservations to keep checking to see if there was a cancellation and I could change the reservation and stay in our original room for the same price-$299. After 2 wonderful nights in a really nice 2 Queen bedded room on the 9th floor (916) with a gorgeous view of the Chicago River, we were told that our room, indeed was available. BUT....they had a fabulous suite for us on the 25th floor with fabulous views-really nice. I asked if I could keep my original room and pay the $299 and was told I could keep that room, but would have to pay $409. Well, if I was paying more $, I might as well move to the suite. The suite was everything I was told it would be-huge living room with a wall of windows looking down onto the Chicago River, dining area and kitchenette, and a huge bedroom with a huge bathroom with spa tub and separate shower. We also had the breakfast included in our rate. The last morning we ordered room service which cost $50. Upon check-out, and after stewing about moving rooms and paying more $, I asked to speak to the manager. I was charged $50 for the room service breakfast and I was annoyed that I was told I could stay in my original room and pay the $299 if it was available, then was told I couldn't do that. Ryan, the manager, was great! He apologized for the mis-communication and said he would speak to the staff and central reservations regarding my issues. He immediately removed the $50 breakfast charge from our bill and was so nice about everything. I was really grateful for his kindness. Another issue I had was the charge of $11.95 for wifi. My 19 year old daughter was with me and we didn't realize that we were being charged $11.95 for each device for wifi. I think we were charged around $70. One of the charges was removed from our bill. TheWit has a lot of positives going for it-the location couldn't be better! We walked everywhere we needed to go. The hotel is modern and beautiful with good sized rooms that are furnished really nicely. We ate breakfast and a late night snack in the restaurant, State and Lake. The German pretzels with beer cheese were delicious! I wish we had visited the rooftop bar and spa, as they looked awesome! The staff were so attentive-always acknowledging us and asking how our day was going, holding/opening doors for us, hailing a taxi for us. A fun aspect of theWit that I'd never seen or heard of before was that in the hallways there is a speaker system and it doesn't play music-during the daytime you hear birds chirping and singing, and at night the crickets are chirping. We thought that was fun. We will be coming back to theWit the end of August when we move our daughter into her dorm to start college. Thanks to Ryan and his staff for addressing our issues and we look forward to our visit in a few weeks.

“Very nice” We booked a 2-bedroom suite. It appeared the room had had a fairly recent renovation. A nice large living area with a working fireplace. Complete kitchen with everything you need. The beds were extremely comfortable and the room was quiet despite its proximity to the airport. It featured 3 TVs, one in each bedroom and the living room and 2 complete baths. Although not exactly a garden spot, it was a very convenient place to stay to catch an early morning flight.

“Zimmer klein, viel los beim Frühstück” Wir haben ja im Sommer eine große USA-Reise gemacht. Da wurden wir von Meiers für 2 Nächte im Holiday Inn Express Fishermans Wharf einquartiert. Das Hotel war keine üble Wahl. Es hat angeblich nur zwei Sterne. Das wäre ja zu wenig für dieses Angebot. Gut, wir kamen zu Mittag an. Die Zimmer waren vorreserviert und die ganze Gruppe bekam Zimmer im Erdgeschoß. Wir fassten Nummer 156 aus. Kein großes Zimmer. Ich tippe mal so auf 18m. So ungefähr wie eine Schiffskabine. Das Doppelbett reichte bald bis zum braunen Schreibtisch nach vorne. Für meinen Rücken waren die angenehmen Matratzen gut. Ich kann nicht klagen. Wie ich im Bett lag, sah ich noch ein Bild mit Beausoleil drauf neben mir an der leicht grauen Zimmertapete hängen. Abends las ich noch paar Zeilen im Buch über die Roten Khmer und da kam die helle Nachttischleuchte gerade recht. Das schwarze Telefon fand ich bei der kleinen Benutzungsfläche mehr als störend. Nochdazu am Schreibtisch das zweite Telefon. Arghhh! Der hatte eine schöne, schwarze Tischplatte und links so ne olle Stehlampe mit langem, rundem Schirm fix montiert. Hell war er ja. Wieso? Direkt am Ende des rechten Fensters mit optimalem Lichteinfall. Der Fernseher stand in einer hellbraunen Einbaukommode. Die Tv Programme verstehe ich eh nicht. Aber es war halt der üblich US-Kram, Weather Channel, FOX, CNN Für mich interessanter waren die Schubladen, denn irgendwo mussten unsere T-shirts und Pullis ja hin. In der Ecke stand ein wuchtiges, rotes Fauteuil mit einem runden Steintisch. Eine Stehlampe fand dort ebenso noch ihren Platz. Was soll ich jetzte noch viel sagen? Der Boden war ein Spannteppich. Grau und mit schwarzem Karo. Das Zimmer war sauber aber für mich eine Spur zu klein. Das Badezimmer war eher gedrängt. Wanne mit fixem Duschkopf und Vorhang gab es weißes Waschbecken im schwarzen Waschtisch ebenso. Duschzubehör, Coditiner und 3 Stofflappen lagen ebenso darauf. Der Fön war rechts an die Wand mit quergestreifter Tapete montiert. Das größte war der Spiegel über dem Waschtisch. Zwei Dinge, die mich sehr gestört haben: Gegenüber von unserer Türe waren draußen so eine Sitzecke am Gang. Dort saßen Gäste und diskutierten und telefonierten laut bis in die Nacht. In der Früh quatschten dort die Zimmermädchen. Weg damit. Mit einer Gruppe von 48 frühstücken zu gehen war der Horror pur. Der Eingang in das Frühstückzimmer war eng. Man sah nichts außer vielen Leuten, die auf etwas warteten. Mit etwas Glück und Faustrecht haben wir ein Müsli ergattert, 2 Bananen, 2 Muffins und 2 Bagel. Die Waffeln und die Danish wollten wir nicht. Für die Gruppe wurde dann der Seminarraum aufgesperrt, damit wir echte Teller bekamen statt dem Plastikzeug. Einen sehr positiven Punkt sage ich noch: Die Lobby war riesig mit viel Platz zum Sitzen. Und, ganz super. Internet gratis bei der Eingangstür. 2 Stellplätze und 2 Terminals extra für den Ausdruck der Boardingpässe. Negativ war nur die Luft, die durch das Öffnen und Schließen der Türen daherkam. Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fishermans Wharf7

“A Great Choice for Business” I recently stayed here on two separate occasions. There is a walkway to the Convention Center; very convenient if you are attending a convention. Rooms are well above average with excellent beds and ample electrical outlets. All staff members I encountered were both professional and helpful.

“Surprisingly Good Value” My husband and I enjoyed a two room king suite. The breakfast was quite good with scrambled eggs, patty sausage, gravy, biscuits, and easy-to-make-yourself hot waffles. Also, from 5:30pm to 7:00pm there were hot snacks with with a complimentary glass of wine or beer, as well as soft drinks and popcorn available until 10:00pm. If that's not enough, while we were there, the Marie Calendar's next door offered a discount, as well. The bed was very comfortable, there was a TV in each of the rooms, and a wet bar in between. Overall, we had a very comfortable three night stay that was a surprisingly good value.

“Altes Hotel mit Charme” Mein Zimmer war zwar groß, wirkte aber dennoch duster und überladen. Die Tapeten sind dunkel und die Möblierung ist sehr alt und abgenutzt. Die Fugen im Bad und an der Toilette machen keinen guten Eindruck. In der Kaffeemaschine lag noch das Kaffee-Pad meines Zimmervorgängers. Die Flure und Treppen im Haus sind schief und krumm. Morgens gibt es im Aufenthaltsraum Kaffee und ein Kuchenteilchen. Das Hotelpersonal ist freundlich und hilfsbereit. In der Nähe des Hotels fährt der kostenlose Charm City Circulator Bus der Stadt Baltimore zum Hafen oder zur Penn Station.

“The third best hotel in the neighborhood” I spent four nights at the Westin Grand from May 4 through 8, 2005. On the last two nights, my wife and son joined me, so we added a connecting room. I'd previously stayed at the neighboring Ritz Carlton, Fairmont and Park Hyatt, and wanted to give the Westin a try. I'd rank it 3rd out the 4. The bed and shower ("heavenly") were in fact quite good. Both of our rooms did face the courtyard, and so the construction noise next door was minimized. The carpets in both rooms needed to be cleaned. Otherwise, the rooms were in good repair (albeit the furnishings were a touch worn). The lighting (my reason for ranking the Park Hyatt last -- but that's another review) was better than average (although they use flourescent bulbs in most of the fixtures, these bulbs were bright -- equivalent to a 100w incandescent). The service was below average. We ate breakfast in the restaurant only once, and due to very slow, inattentive service (principally from the server, not the waiter or host) and walked over to the Fairmont after that. The buffet offered was mediocre for the price. The desk staff was attentive at check-in, but the supervisor at checkout quibbled over my request to extend the 12 noon check-out by 45 minutes. He finally relented, but only for one room. Housekeeping never replenished the coffee/hot chocolate supplies for our coffee maker, diminishing what was a pleasant in-room amenity. I'd stay here again, but only if I couldn't get a room at the Ritz Carlton or Fairmont.

“Excellent location for business and easy escape” Attended a multi-day conference and was fortunate to come a little early and leave a little late. The proximety of this hotel to the beautiful San Antonio riverfront is virtually hidden, but a treasure once discovered. Room was cozy but perfectly adequate with all amenities needed. Staff were very helpful, including recommendation for local restaurants to take a large dinner party. Meeting and conference space is nicely available and intertwined while also being set apart from public areas of hotel and accessible from rooms. Business services provided via in-lobby business center store. Could miss the access to the river walk, so be sure and explore below street entry level lobby for a treat to the riverside, riverside dining almost on site (interior hotel restaurant and lobby coffee shop also available, but not as fun!), river boat tours leaving from under the hotel, and pick up anything you need at the adjoining mall on the river as well. Short walk to the Alamo, Tower of the Americas, and other downtown San Antonio sights. An evening stroll along the river should be checked with the front desk to suggest which side of the river is best to walk on based on the late hour- but a must see and nice relaxing end to a busy day of meetings.

“** CHECK THIS OUT ** “Real Business Review, real and independent business reviews only ! “” “Huntington Nob Hill has seen better days but still have personality ” OVERALL: Time of stay: April 2012 Location: You couldn’t be more Nob Hill that this! Convenient parking spot to valet the car, I was there for multiple appointments and did valet the car up to 5 times per day, alerted staff. Walkable to Union Square and in front of the Grace Cathedral. Pro: Historic Building for who likes historic hotel (like Portland Regency in Maine) Wireless available and large working desk in any type of room. Pro-active staff, really great valet service. Great cooperation for handling my business stuff shipped from Italy. Valet parking is pricey but considered San Francisco average is a Pro. Con: Did not try the famous Nob Hill Spa as I though it was overpriced and still proposing the same packages and treatment of the end of the century. Nothing compared to the Spa of Loews or Shutters on the Beach in Santa Monica. Somewhat a sense of “old” rather than historic, small and dark lobby, dark aisle, dark restaurant. No traces of a coffee machine in the rooms. Amenities (bathroom, wardrobe) very poor. ROOMS: I stayed in the king size room, spacious and overall clean. A small galley available if you cook. QUALITY\PRICE: Overall fair, at least wi-fi is complimentary. BUSINESS NOTES: Convenient food shop next door if you don’t like “old fashioned” restaurant like the in-house Big 4 Restaurant. Concierge available 24hrs, you better don’t need her as she does not respond to emails (sent her twice before my trip never responded so I just ship what I had to ship)

“Ask for Harbour view” Recently had a very nice stay at this hotel. We got a fabulous room on the 11th floor facing the bay, it was gorgeous! Beds were very nice and comfy. Most staff were very nice and helpful. Pool was fantastic... really big, lots of space, not too crowded, had seperate kids pool and two hot tubs. I saw a few areas that could use improving... I think it would be nice if they gave us more than two bath towels a day (really, most business class hotels provide 4). The internet was slow and it was annoying to pay $12/ day for this. If Best Western can offer free internet, why can't the Marriot? You could also hear the tooting of trains at all hours, even on the 11th floor on the quiet side. I imagine it would only be worse on the other side. Overall though, many more positives than negatives. The location is fantastic; right on the embarcado/ sea walk area, very close to quaint and beautiful shops of Seaport Village (i didn't find this hokey or touristy at all! thought it was great!) and Gaslamp quarter. Could walk to the USS Midway as well.

“Nice,Clean Budget Hotel” I was pleasantly surprised when my girlfriends and I booked this hotel for a weekend in Chicago. It is south of the Chicago Institute of Art, across the street from Grant Park. The area has become nicer (more restaurants and activity) since Millenium Park opened. You still are a long way from shopping at Michigan Ave, but they have a shuttle that takes you uptown to the Hancock building every hour and returns on the half hour. You can always catch the bus ($2.00) or take a cab. My friend said they also have a shuttle that goes to the different museums,aquarium, planetarium area and it's really close to Soldier Field for the football games. The room was adequate with nice beds and linens, decor is nothing special ,but it is clean and the staff is very nice. Parking in their garage is $30.00/per day. For the price you can't beat it if you are not looking for a lot of ambiance. It has a large pool with a lifeguard on duty and fitness center,which we didn't use but took a look at. They were also offering free gift wrapping for Christmas. They have a good and inexpensive restaurant,by Chicago prices, where we ate breakfast one morning.

“Excellent Hotel - Great Breakfast” Our family of 4 stayed for 3 nights in a one bedroon suite. The suite was very comfortable and a good size with a well equipped kitchen (including dishwaser - fantastic!). Our only minor issue is that only 2 dining chairs are supplied as standard. The hotel is very clean and the pool is nice. As previous reviewers are commented, the staff are very helpful. The highlight for us was the fantasic breakfast - a very good selection, including hot dishes, served on real plates with real cutlery. There is a supermarket a few minutes drive away, and it is an easy half-hour drive into San Diego. If you are visiting San Diego and don't want to stay in the city, this hotel is ideal. Very highly recommended.

“Great Location” Stayed in this hotel as the second part of a twin centre holiday with LA first. We stayed at a 4 star hotel in LA so it was a bit different coming to the Edison but it was fine! Rooms like all NY rooms are small but there was still plenty of room for 4. the bathroom was very small but clean. The room was cleaned daily with fresh bedding and towels. The corridors though did stink! however once you got into the room there was no smell so im not quite sure what the smell was! Hotel staff were nice and friendly and the cafe edison was great for breakfast and very reasonable. The main problem is that this is an old hotel with old furnishings which really need updating however non of our stay was bad but a re furb would do it the world of good. Would I stay here again? Yes because the location is amazing and there was nothing wrong with the hotel just a bit worn.

“Not bad for the price!” You will love BWRN if you're used to budget hotels, but you may feel like you're slumming if you're used to upscale properties. Pros: free parking, large room, good housekeeping, lots of table lamps, a fridge in our room, and two flat-screen TVs in our room. Cons: our A/C didn't work very well, the toilet/shower area is very small, the water pressure in the shower isn't great, the elevator is tiny, and the 3rd-floor hallway is unattractive. The blackout curtains didn't fully close, but I always travel with a clip. We didn't hear a sound from other rooms or the hallway. Breakfast isn't normally included but sometimes there's a special on Facebook. Location is convenient to everything except the museum campus, which would be a longer walk, and there are oodles of restaurants nearby.

“No” No. Just no. Let's start with the fact that the room was freezing. The heating unit is so blasted loud that you have to turn it off at night in order to sleep. It's seriously like a freaking rocket ship or something. Not to mention it does not heat the bathroom at all. Also, sometimes the hot water in the bathroom sink worked, sometimes it didn't. In addition, there is NO SOAP in the hotel room. I can understand offering body gel as an alternative, but there are some things you just need bar soap for. This is supposed to be a hotel, not a hostel. The hotel is exceptionally loud. In addition to the heating unit sounds, I could hear the people in the stairwell beside me and the room above me, as well as the jackhammering construction workers outside and the monorail passing by. In addition, there's a lot of light in the room. There are no curtains--only a shade--and the heating unit has a lot of lights on it. Makes it difficult to sleep when things aren't dark OR quiet. Also, the service was fairly lackluster. I got the impression they didn't really care if I was there or not. I don't think a single person told me thank you even once. On my second day, I had to return to my room around 3 pm or so. Evidently my room was the last one to be cleaned in the hotel and housekeeping is supposed to get off at 3. I was pretty much ordered by the front desk to leave my room if I wanted it cleaned and was rudely told they weren't going to pay their housekeeper overtime just for me. No. No, no, no, no.

“Stay away!!” Ok, I have stayed here twice and both times it was dirty, dirty, dirty. Ugh. Yes, the lobby and the restaurants are very GOOD. Even the front desk and management are tops. One of the best concierge floors anywhere with great service and food. Nice fitness center. Great location but the rooms were just old and I dreaded returning to sleep. There are such mixed reviews on here that I wonder if there are some areas of the hotel that are renovated and some that are not? Unfortunately I got the worst both stays.

“Convenient location to Camden Yards, Convention Center, and Waterfront.” The Hampton Inn provided a good room with very good breakfasts. We walked everywhere from there, and were surprised especially by the Baltimore waterfront and seafood. The hotel staff were very friendly, and anxious to please us and answer any questions that we had about Baltimore.

“Just an Average Marriott” High price for an average Marriott. Stuck in PHX had to overnight at the hotel. Real plain Marriott, smelled find of funny. The Concierge lounge was old an needed to be remodeled. Turned off the AC unit and it was still loud. Nothing fancy at this hotel.

“Decent if not paying full price” I've stayed here three times over the last few months. Twice for business and once for pleasure. Every time, I booked it through priceline. The location is good and the rooms are pretty nice for NYC. The only issue I had when staying twice for business was that the walls were so thin. I was woken up at 5am by someone else's alarm the first time. The second time, I was woken up at about 6am with someone else's tv blaring. Finally, I stayed there with my husband for a couple of nights over the weekend. This time, the room was not very clean. There was actually feces on the shower curtain next to the toilet. There was also part of a wrapper under the pillow. Since we had just moved rooms since they mistakenly gave us a smoking room at first (very quick to switch us though), didn't have the energy to do it again. Given this, I may decide to try a different area using priceline for next time. I'm really not thrilled with this hotel and would not rate it 4 stars.

“Perfect For Arrival Or Departure at SeaTac” We found this hotel with use of Trip Advisor and were very pleased by how it worked out for us. We had a late arrival and before I could call for the Marriott courtesy van it was pulling up at my stop just outside the airport parking garage. The room was ready, clean, comfortable and everything in it worked great. We had a fast check in around one o'clock AM. The room was close to the lobby and its window looked out on the spacious and very well appointed indoor atrium. The next morning, check out was also smooth and we picked up our Hertz rental car right at the hotel where Hertz has a desk and a parking area and you save by renting off airport property. We enjoyed a fine breakfast in the hotel restaurant before starting our drive. When we returned to the airport a few weeks later, we turned in the rental car at the Marriott. This was painless with the parking lot adjacent. We ate a fine lunch of salmon burgers and salad then took the courtesy van back to the airport. It doesn't get any better. The price was fair and we were treated very well. The front desk even held our bags while we ate lunch. We'll stay here again.

“Lovely long weekend at the Orchard” Had a lovely stay at the Orchard Nov 13-17. The room was spacious and quiet, the bathroom spotless, and the location fabulous. We made use of a lot of the 'extras'--complimentary dvds (great), car service (great), complimentary breakfast (eh. .. .). Our flight schedule meant we needed to check in early and check out late, both of which were graciously accommodated. A couple things to note--bring a laptop, as in-room dsl is free; beds are hard but not uncomfortable (ask for extra pillows). Linens are mostly very good, but not consistently so there was invariably one scratchy pillowcase or a rough sheet in with the lovely Frette bedding. Staff was competent. This is a bit petty, but I had mentioned when I made the reservation that we would be celebrating our 10th anniversary, so I was a little disappointed that there wasn't so much as a 'congratulations, thanks for staying with us' card in our room. But, for this price, I'm not complaining about the details. All in all the Orchard is a great hotel. We got a $119 rate as quoted on quikbook (we booked it through the hotel itself, not the website). Not as luxe as some, not as trendy as some, but for that price, the location and ameneties can't be beat.

“We REALLY didn't like this place” The price was fine. End of complements. Hotel seemed fairly new but cheaply built and falling apart. The immediate area seemed edgy, much worse than most areas which others express a fear of but which don't really bother me. I could be very wrong about this but I don't think so. Spreading out a little revealed the main attraction of the area-the Galleria on a street which had so much traffic it was almost impassable, as is much of Houston-and a car is really the only way to get around, and I have no interest in another mall.

“Good value, good area” Ive stayed in a variety of hotels in Boston, and this is a good one I would return to. Its fairly generic, could use some updating in the common areas but its very comfortable and standard comfortable Hilton quality. Its very near the convention center, backbay, the malls (prudential) and good and $$ dining on Newbury st. The windows open a little as well, which is nice if you want some good fresh Beantown air. I had a high room so noise was no issue. Not sure what the lower floors would be like. Good view! If you dont want to hit the ample fitness room, go for a run to Cambridge and backbay. You'll be happy. Enjoy Boston

“Nice” This seems to be newer property. It is kept up very well, the rooms have refreshing colors and a great set-up. The Free wi-fi worked great in the room. Breakfast was good and actually warm items along with the waffle machine. I enjoyed the choices of places to eat within walking distance. After a long work day it was nice not having to get back in the car and drive to eat. There is a Longhorns, Zaxby's and Ruby Tuesday's. I was traveling alone and enjoyed the bar at Longhorns for my dinners. Two cons: 1. I was in a room on the second floor and the person above me was very heavy footed. I think I would try for the top 4th floor next time. I did have a room at the far end of the corridor away from the elevator which was quiet and nice. 2. The a/c unit in the room is a window type. Very loud and noisy and it's right next to the bed. I finally figured out if I left the fan on it wasn't so loud when the a/c compressor kicked on. 3. I left for work at 0700 for work and came back at 3:30 and the maid still hadn't reached my room. When I called the front desk I found she hadn't even reached my floor. So I gave up and just asked for some fresh towels and received those promptly from what appeared to be the maintenance man.

“Second stay here...love this little place!” This was my second stay at Comfort Inn Lower East Side, and it was even better than my first stay. I had a room on the sixth floor facing the front, which I preferred to last time when I had a back room on a low floor with no view. Ludlow Street is very "lively" with partiers on weekend nights, but I stayed out late myself and was not bothered by it. I actually found it entertaining. The neighborhood is perhaps my favorite place to stay in NYC. So many restaurants and bars nearby, and walking distance to many things (including the East Village and SoHo). There is a Whole Foods just around the corner and down the street, so having a fridge in the room is a great perk for an NYC hotel. There was a very friendly and helpful woman at the front desk often - I wish I remembered her name but I don't. Housekeeping was also friendly, and very unobtrusive. It's always nice when you can sleep in on vacation without housekeeping making tons of noise in the hallway or neighboring rooms. The rooms are small, but comfortable. The bathroom has a nice shower/tub and lots of counter space for your stuff. Flat screen TV worked well. And again, having a fridge is a huge plus! Highly recommended very close by: Espresso for coffee around the corner on Stanton Street. And Schiller's Liquor Bar on Rivington for dinner (I made reservations for me, a college friend, and his NYC friends - and we were all super impressed by the decor and food). And Katz Deli at the end of the block is an experience - a delicious, diet-ruining one! Am hoping to go to NYC again in June or July and will probably stay here again.

“Clean, spacious room, convenient location” The staff was very helpful and nice. When I checked in I was given a room upgrade to what they called a "suite" (see pictures that I've posted). Paid $140/night including tax and free parking. Clean room, spacious, comfortable bed. My room had a view of the parking lot, but since you're in a city I'm guessing that none of the rooms had much of a view besides the buildings across the street. The room had a microwave & a refrigerator (and a safe, I think). The TV was not a flat screen, but had a decent selection of channels, ESPN, showtime, etc. I saw no sign of communal bathrooms mentioned in other reviews. My room had a private bath (#322) and I saw no communal bathrooms in the entire 3rd floor hall (at least on my side of the building).

“Great hotel, exceptional service” Have stayed in Boston many times but usually stay at the Lenox. This time we booked this trip through a price comparison site as we were also going to Cape Cod for a week and this hotel was on as a special deal. I knew that it was in a great location and the reviews were quite good. When we booked we knew that it was just a standard room and expected it to be quite small. When we got there the receptionist told us that we had been upgraded to a king size room which was a great surprise. The room was huge with a big bathroom and one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in but the best thing about this hotel was the service which was excellent. Everyone was really friendly and nothing was a bother even when my husband locked us out of the bathroom at 11.30pm. Plently restaurants nearby. Trinity Church on the door step.

“Nice hotel, very responsive staff” Rooms are large and clean with a great shower! My first room was near the pool which was too loud too late for me. (Pool closes at 10pm) They accomodated me by making a room right across the hall available for me to move into the next day. The food at the evening reception has great opportunities for improvement. I will be staying here again on my next business trip.

“generally good” Generally, a good stay. Central location on side street just east of Grand Central. Pros: homey room; excellent housekeeping; nice linens/towels Cons: officious service; staffing of front desk is spotty; no ice machine (need to call room service); bed too soft

“Great Location for Business in the Financial District, Quiet & Comfortable” I really love this hotel for Convience to financial firms located here. The room is one of the quietest rooms In which I have ever stayed. Upon checking in and going to my room which was immediately off of the elevator bank, I almost asked for another room but decided to give the room a try. To my total surprise, I never heard anyone getting off the elevators or even talking in the hallway. Complete quiet, and I don't believe I have ever experienced this type of quiet. My room overlooked the Statute of Liberty which wais quite beautiful and comforting. I checked in on 9/11 and thought the view was fitting as a statement to our continued freedom. Service seems to be good, as all was in order upon my return from meetings in the evening. Shower is nice and bed is extremely comfortable. Room is large by NYC standards with lots of work space. Great home away from home! I highly recommend this hotel for the business traveler, as well as it would nice for families or couples.

“Perfect for Broadway/Midtown” The Sofitel is an excellent hotel. It has an understated/european charm, feels upscale yet laid-back, and is perfectly situated for being a tourist in the City. It generally has a quiet, unhurried feel to it. The lobby is fairly small, and never feels like its crowded with people. The bar/restaurant that's attached is first-rate. The hotel is part of a French chain, and the artwork around the hotel is either Manhattan- or Paris-themed (a nice touch). It's only 2 blocks from many Broadway theaters, and is in easy walking distance to many other popular destinations (ie Radio City, Rockefeller Center, 5th Ave shopping) and restaurants (ie Four Seasons, Gilt, Le Bernardin). We stay here every year for an end of year trip. Its a little pricey, but it feels like its worth it.

“Concept: 5; execution: 3” Stayed here to be close to a business meeting in the mid-East Side. From the website photos, it looked like it was trying to be sorta hip, sorta European boutique but still suitable for business travel. i was disappointed. First, I paid extra for an Executive Room, giving me access to breakfast and what i thought would be an afternoon reception. Perhaps I misread the website but nothing was offered in the afternoon. The breakfast was o.k. Fairly limited and nothing to write home about. Second, the extra I paid was not evident in the room I was given. It was probably the smallest room I have stayed at in NYC. This was were European standards were unfortunately applied. I made sure the check in folks knew I had Silver Reward status and that they knew I had reserved an Executive Room so if this is what I got, it must mean that the ordinary rooms are closet sized. the room also was on a very low floor even though i had indicated in "comments" a preference for a higher floor. The furnishings were newish/upscale, so that was nice. But the bed had a hard wooden platform and i ran into it with my leg one night. Ouch! Given the tight quarters, i can only assume i wasn't the only one to do this. The sink was Euro-hip but totally dysfunctional. The sink was basically a flat-sided basin and the spout extended below the lip. that made it very awkward when trying to cup one's hands below the spout and then to bring one's hands up to wash one's face. See photos. All in all, I felt I paid too much for not enough. i will stay elsewhere next time.

“Great stay for an excellent price!” Pulling up to the hotel it looked a little plain, but don't judge a book by its cover. The inside was very nice! The lobby was well appointed and the front desk staff was very friendly. Check-in was quick and we were on our way to our room in no time. There was free parking that is under the building and a few spots around the front door area. We never had a problem finding a spot. Our room was clean and roomy. We had a double room with two queen beds. The linens were fine and the towels seemed new. Our room also had a table with two chairs, flat screen TV, microwave, refrig, and coffee maker. We were in a corner room and faced the building next door. You can see the Space Needle from the parking lot in front of the hotel, and some of the rooms on the front of the hotel probably get a view of it. The bathroom was large with the toilet and shower in their own room and the sink just outside of it, but around a wall so it wasn't open to the rest of the room. The water pressure was good from the double shower head. We were there for three nights and had breakfast there each morning. There are waffles (yum!), pancakes (eh), and something else hot (biscuits and gravy two of the days, breakfast burrito one day). There's also bread, muffins, hard boiled eggs, cereal, and oatmeal. They also have cookies for you in the lobby at night. There's also a Whole Foods about a block away for picking up some supplies or a quick dinner. This hotel really isn't within easy walking distance of the waterfront attractions of downtown. We drove our car to the waterfront and parked in a garage there. From there we walked to Pioneer Square, then back up to Pike Place Market. We parked some where in the middle of those two. I think it was around $25 for just over 6 hours of parking. We had a great time in Seattle, beautiful weather and pretty much everyone we interacted in the city was very friendly. We would definitely stay here again!

“Great stay, courteous staff” We are a family of 4 and we arrived at 2am because of our flight delay. Had to book a Madison suite as I waited too long to get a Berkshire suite. Great room. Wonderful staff at the front desk while checking in. They suggested we get a roll away as we have 2 daughters. They brought it promptly up to our room. Have to agree with a previous post that getting a taxi at the hotel is hard especially around 6-8pm. A couple evenings we just used a private car that happened upon the hotel (I know they must sit around there knowing the taxi situation). One evening we shared an SUV with a couple and split the cost which worked out fine as they were going in the Broadway area too and it was raining. Loved the location as its easy to walk around to eat and shop and sightsee. Only minor problem we had is when we were checking out and wanting to leave our bags at the hotel since our fight wasn't until 8pm. We called and no one came for 30 minutes. My husband finally decided to call again and they had never received a message to come up. They promptly came up within a couple minutes. We would stay at the Omni again for sure.

“Tired and Worn, Needs Interior Improvement” I paid for three nights via "name your price" on Priceline and for the price I paid I feel I got what I paid for, but I would not pay full price for this place. Therefore, I would only recommend it if you pay a discounted rate. It's a pretty hotel but is pretty worn out and needs new carpet and refurbishing. I watched a few maids at work and they appear to be rushing to clean the room. In my room specifically, there was this oily smell like the cheap perfume of a previous guest, it thought to complain to the front desk but I didn't find them particularly warm or welcoming when I arrived so I thought what's the point. Later, when passing through the hallway, I noticed the same oily smell and it occurred to me that perhaps the entire hotel was this stinky. Some of the rooms (including the one I got) face the central courtyard which has a lovely pool. You enter these rooms through a pair of French doors and when you get inside they double as a window and you are supposed to close the shades so that no one can look inside. I don't like this design of room and I'm not sure you will unless you are an exhibitionist and don't care if anyone sees your laptop or other valubles in view when they pass by your room. The bedding was very good. I slept very good on the mattress and the pillows were feather down (or felt like it) and extremely comfortable. There was a refrigerator and microwave in the room, both in good working order. To give you an idea of the lack of attention to detail, the "energy saver star rating" label was left on the fridge, there was a piece of wallpaper peeling off the wall in the bathroom that any cleaning attendant should have noticed if they cleaned the room. The internet is only free in the lobby and atrium which I think is silly when one considers that free internet is almost deriguer at any 3 plus star hotel. Two final observations: the front doors are pulled by handles so it makes it extremely inconvenient to enter the hotel when carrying bags in the absence of vigilant or helpful staff. I literally had two bags in one, pulling my Samsonite in the other, and both a security guard sitting on a concrete bench and a hotel employee just watched me struggle to open the door. When you have a hotel this shabby there are two things you must be sure to do: keep it very clean and have courteous, pleasant, and cheerful and welcoming staff. I feel that this hotel is lacking these two aspects and consequently is missing opportunities to please guests. To the manager or to whomever, keep the cookies and give me a smile and a nice attitude upon check-in, it goes a long way.

“Solid Kimpton in NYC” Still good after all these years. Excellent service from check in to check out. The rooms are decent size for NYC standards and quiet as well. Great location midtown, as I was able to walk to most of my meetings. Nice touch as they also have a wine reception hour in the evenings. Highly recommend this hotel and I ll be back next trip to NYC.

“Not planning to go back” After really enjoying a stay here a couple years ago, my boyfriend and I decided to stay here for 2 nights from March 18-20. This time, we were not very pleased. Our biggest complaints revolve around the bathroom. When we first checked in, there was a used washcloth and hairs all over the bathtub. Also, the sink, toilet, and bathtub were all backed up, or at least EXTREMELY slow to drain. This made using the sink and taking a shower disgusting. Also, perhaps this is a bit too vulgar for an online post, but the toilet was so bad that it stopped up (without good reason I might say) and we embarrassingly had to call the front desk to come and fix it (to their credit, they did send someone up quite fast and were very nice about it.) the bathroom in this room was old, dingy and cracked looking. i think the one we stayed in during our previous visit was nicer and had been remodeled. also, when we checked in, there was a thick smell of smoke and ashes in the ashtray on the counter, which was also dirty (we are non-smokers and can't stand smoke). we parked in the garage next-door for 2 nights, resulting in a hefty charge of $40 total ($20 per night, i think it came out to $44 with some fees). the valet staff burn rubber and act like they are in the indianapolis 500 when they bring your car down. nevertheless, when we checked out a little before noon on sunday, there was a crowd of people all waiting for their cars to be brought down, most all of them unhappy with how they or their cars had been treated. (another warning: when we had temporarily parked around the block on March 19, with our meter paid up until almost the 8:00 p.m. free parking time, we were issued a $20 ticket when we went back to the car just a few minutes late. of course this is our fault, just a warning that you should be careful and strictly abide by the parking regulations. parking around the hotel is also extremely difficult to find.) of secondary importance, our view was not that great this time- we overlooked an industrial-looking roof and some construction. last time we had a great view of ben franklin parkway. to their credit, the staff at Hotel Windsor were very pleasant and accomodating. However, for our next visit to Philly, we will be looking for suburban accomodation that is inexpensive and has free parking. we no longer feel it is worthwhile to stay at Hotel Windsor.

“Central City Location - Convenient to Attractions & Restaurants” Marriott's location is tremendous - just one-block from City Hall! Convenient to Historical attractions ( 7 blocks to Independence Hall, Liberty Bell, Betsy Ross House, etc.); shopping (Macy's right across the street), Reading Terminal Market across the street, next to the Convention Center and connected by walkway; and many restaurants. Art museum is just a short cab ride away. Bed was very comfortable and made for a good night's sleep. The room was quiet and not city sounds were heard. Room had a nice sitting chair and a desk. Room was clean. One disappointment with the room is the old televisions they have in the rooms. The picture is not crisp and appears they have been in the rooms for quite a while. Note that parking is not free. It runs $36 per night. If you have the time, about 20 blocks away is Eastern State Penitentiary. It was used from 1830's till 1971 and is now open for tours at a cost of $12 (audio tour). It is now a stabilized ruin and well worth the entry fee. Took about 90 minutes to go through it.

“Consistant quality, cleanliness, friendliness, and service” I am usually a Hilton customer, staying in one of their family of hotels about 2 days per week on average. Because of attending a class, in Austin, where this hotel was mandated for lodging, I begrudgingly gave up the opportunity to earn HHonors points for my stay, and stayed at this Hyatt. Though not happy about getting Hyatt points, instead of Hilton, I am very pleased with this hotel. Pros: Spacious room. Well appointed kitchen (minus an oven). Comfortable king size bed. Large screen LCD television with connections to connect your laptop or other device. DVD Player. Very friendly staff. Efficient maids. Free hot breakfast. On Mon - Thursday free "dinner" with Shiner Bock and Lone Star beer included (wine too). Outdoor pool. Small laundry and gym (very small gym). The biggest pro is that they are a consistent performer. Free shopping service to get food for you from local store. Free internet (but kind of slow at 50kB/s down). Free local calls. Environmentally friendly lighting and HVAC.
