Attractively furnished rooms. Several nearby restaurants and shopping venues. Quiet (even though they stuck me right next to the elevators). Free parking. Cons: No all day coffee service. Gym is tiny (2 bikes, 2 treadmills, and an elliptical).

“I Love an Old Hotel” Just spent a long weekend at the Biltmore. Pluses: Staff was friendly and helpful. Room was surprisingly huge and quiet. Valet parking efficient and quick. The afternoon tea a delight. The gym and indoor pool a time machine. Great for exploring and people-watching. Convenient to everything downtown. Minuses: Nonexistent water pressure in the shower. A lovely view of an airshaft. The price of the valet parking. Overall: I couldn't recommend it more highly, and would definitely stay there again.

“Clean Rooms and Nice Views but not actually on the waterfront” Stayed here for a conference at a nearby hotel that's actually on the waterfront. The hotel is adjacent to the new convention center but that is the only thing convenient about the location of the hotel for a business traveler. Restaurants require a bit of a hike to get to - as those restaurants are actually on the waterfront. As others mentioned - no shuttle to the airport is a real drawback (as most business travelers seem to go to and from the airport from this hotel). The hotel itself had very nice rooms - very comfortable bed, clean sheets, showers with dual shower heads, climate control, and a nice touch with the semi-transparent pull down shades. However, it's missing the finer touches I'd expect with a 4-star at the rate that I paid. Was not able to find the concierge from time to time, limited staffing at the check-in desk (I saw two people manning the desk even though there were a multitude of people waiting), and just did not get the personal and feel that I would have expected - but I will give them the benefit of doubt as the hotel was at full capacity the whole time I was there and multiple conferences were being hosted simultaneously. For those that utilize the gym, the gym was very nice (updated equipment) and there was adequate room in the gym for calistenics (sp?) and a nice indoor pool. I'd like to add, internet is a bit pricey compared to other hotels.

“Excellent and very centrally placed” We went there on our honeymoon, we found the hotel very comfortable , clean , staff very pleasant.As with most places in U.S.A it was room only, this was not a problenm as plenty places nearby to dine at .Hotel was very busy when we were there but staff were always polite and willing to help us .Hotel got us tickets to go and see a basketball game which worked out expensive, if wanting to do same i would reccomend going to Times Square where tickets for everything availableat a fraction of the price.

“Gets the job done at PHL” As I mentioned in another review, I flip back and forth between this and the Sheraton Suites depending on price and both get the job done for Airport Hotels. Admittedly PHL does not have the nicest options for Hotels when compared to other Airports like ORD. If I am arriving very late the Aloft is my preferred choice due to the Grab and Go in the lobby. Rooms are fine but have a bit of a cold modern feel often associated with W/Aloft Brand. If price is similar or within $10 I usually choose the Sheraton Suites which is right next door. For one night it is not the best hotel in Philly but certainly not the worst choice either.

“Very Good Hotel” Spent 4 nights here. With my dog, Goose. The desk staff was very friendly, totally professional & they all seem to love dogs, which helps. Most of the door guys are cool & friendly & helpful. The room was very comfortable, the bed is outstandng & the view (Hudson side) was mesmerizing. The restaurant is really good (lower level); run by a tv show chef. The bar on the roof employs several bartenders who you may want to just smack on the noggin, because they have an arrogant, pouty, you-owe-me attitude. Always odd to encounter that from someone in the hospitality / service biz. There's a difference between being a tool & being insouciant: these boys haven't figured out what it is yet. In any event, the bar gets packed with see & be-seens. Worth going once for a drink, then spending your time, and money, elsewhere. Tons of restaurants close by, obviously tons of shopping in Soho. Room was quiet, clean. Definitely would recommend for a stay if you want to be near Soho.

“Extras, Extras, Extras” We stayed at this hotel to attend an OSU football game. We usually stay at a hotel on Olentangy River Rd. but the cost was too much, lucky for me I found an alternative. We were impressed with the location within walking distance of the Nationwide arena area, North Market and the Short North area therefore lots of places to eat and shop! We were only 5 min. from the OSU campus. The rates per night were great especially impressed with the decor and cleanliness of the hotel along with the security. They do charge for parking but the only way in or out is with a hotel key card for extra security better than parking in an open lot. The elevators you even have to use your key card to get to the room floors. The pool is an indoor/outdoor pool with jacuzzi. We were by a highway exit ramp but heard no noise. Everyone at the hotel was very friendly. We had a marble entry way and bathroom in our room along with fridge and microwave. The extras were impressive: free alcoholic drinks and snacks reception in the evening (limit 3 free drinks) and free popcorn and sodas all evening. The breakfast buffet had more than the norm with waffles, eggs, biscuits/gravy, sausage, etc. They also had free internet and local calls. I would highly recommend a restaurant that is to the east of the hotel across the street called the Flatiron bar and grill very good!

“Nice Hotel” The Century Plaza is a very fine choice. The public areas are nice, with interesting architectural details. The rooms are good sized and comfortable, and the restaurant is very good. I should add that the staff is helpful and responsive.

“Quick trip to Houston” We are in Houston at least once a month. This was our first time to stay at this hotel. It was perfect. Just north of the Beltway, which was good for us, easy access. The hotel met all of our criteria, very clean, great service, the bed & pillows very comfortable, and 24 hour fresh hot coffee. They had free breakfast and it looked very good when I went for coffee, but I didn't eat on this trip. It was also close to fast food & other nicer restaurants. I was very impressed. We normally stay at another hotel north of here, but this hotel was about $50 less per night and was probably better than the other place we normally stay.. This is now our "north" end hotel for trips to the Houston area.

“Not horrible, but I wouldn't stay here again” My husband and I live in NYC, but stayed at the Westin Times Square last Thursday night for a "night out." The room was so-so. The outlet in the bathroom is over the toilet, so you literally have to blow your hair dry over the toilet. Another problem - you get no cell phone reception in the hotel, so you have to use the hotel phone to make all of your calls and they charge several dollars for each call (I think about $5 per call with taxes, but can't recall for sure), so it adds up quickly. Also, no cell phone service means no blackberry service, so I had to log on to my computer (pay $15 for internet service) just to see if I had received e-mails. The bed was comfortable and we got a good night sleep even though you can hear noises from other rooms (people sneezing, flushing the toilet, etc., but no street noise). We went to the hotel's bar for a drink and got great service and good drinks. However, the hotel service is not so great - we called the front desk three times and asked for laundry bags, but they were never delivered.

“Stayed here May 28” We really enjoyed our stay at the Seattle Waterfront Marriott. The room was very nice. The lobby was beautiful. Everyone was super nice & helpful. The hotel restaurant is Todd English's Fish Club. We had a very nice breakfast there. The service was also very good in the restaurant.

“Nice place...” My wife and I spent four nights at the Hilton Houston Westchase in mid-May of 2005, and we had a very pleasant stay. The lobby is beautiful, with an attractive piano lounge. The room was beautiful, clean, and functional. The only potential draw-back to this hotel is the location, which requires a bit of driving time to get to most Houston attractions. But, it is located right off of Beltway 8, and its location on Westheimer means that there is certainly no shortage of restaurant and shopping options. When we returned home, I received a credit bill with an inappropriate charge from Hilton Houston Westchase. After e-mailing the hotel staff, they immediately refunded the amount. I was impressed with their integrity and responsiveness. Though this hotel did not blow us away, it was a nice place, especially for the $40 per night that we paid through Priceline. I would confidently recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Great Location and hotel for families” This is the place to stay if you are a family visiting New York. It is right in the middle of Time Square which for some may be a plus and others a minus. There are massive amounts of people out which can make getting to and from this hotel difficult. The rooms and views are excellent. The rooms are huge and very well appointed for a Doubletree. Staff are friendly enough, but very busy. We received the breakfast for free being Diamond members, but the regular price for the buffet is expensive. It is brunch priced everyday of the week. When we bring the family to New York, this is where we stay, but when it is just my husband and me, we go for something quieter.

“Nice hotel, great location, hit or miss on the staff” I stayed here two nights on business. It's a full-service hotel in a great location (Union Square/Downtown) with tons of shopping & dining. Saks & Macy's are just one block away, great sushi, Indian, Thai, pub food, etc. all within a block or two. Cabs are very easy to come by. Nice lobby & decor (marble & columns & such). There's a small bar with seating both inside & on the sidewalk. It's open to the lobby & doubles as a breakfast area serving baked goods in the morning (for a fee - this is upscale & NOT a free breakfast kind of place). There's a restaurant visible to the lobby (glass wall) that appeared to be upscale dining - I didn't check out the menu. No valet is available, so I don't know what you do for parking if you bring a car as there doesn't appear to be any nearby. Garages? A business center with two or three workstations is available downstairs near the elevators, including a printer. The rooms are small, as is completely expected in an older hotel. Beds & pillows are comfy, linens are decent, but I thought the comforter was a bit thin. There did not appear to be any deferred maintenance issues & they definitely keep this looking nice. I liked the room decor - it was old-school class with modern touches married together perfectly - understated elegance done quite well. I requested a room facing the street as I like to hear the trolley bell (it's right on the trolley line), street musicians (LOTS of that), & street noise, but be forewarned that if you are a light sleeper or need peace & quiet, you DO NOT want to stay on the street side. It's noisy at all times of day & night. The other side should be just fine. The bathrooms are tiny with pedestal sinks. The main issue I had with the bathroom was that there's no counter space or shelving on the sink side - shelves are above the toilet, which makes getting ready a bit less convenient. Rooms have free wifi that's pretty fast & reliable. Window opens only a crack, and you have a window unit AC/heater. There's no gift shop in the hotel, but there is a little store just across the street that will have the basics a traveler might need. Room service only goes 'til 10 PM, and there's no late night dining. There is a mini bar with snacks, soda & alcohol in the room, as well as an in-room safe & a decent desk. Staff was hit or miss. I found the front desk staff to be very helpful & extremely friendly. Half of the time, there was no doorman to be found. They have one, but when I came & went (which was often over a three day period) he was rarely at his post. I think this may be because he doubles as a bellman, so may be gone at times hauling bags, but this is just a guess. I think they need a separate bellman and at least two people at the door. The waitress at the bar was fine at times, at other times snippy. When they were closing up (at 10 PM mind you), we were sitting outside at the sidewalk tables & basically invited to leave while we still had drinks. If you sit outside, you'll be accosted by panhandlers about every three minutes - they are mostly friendly but very aggressive with their efforts. I noted other hotels & restaurants had large men stationed outside who kept the pandhandlers from bothering patrons, but not so here (another reason they need two people at the front door). Overall, a good property, a decent stay, but it didn't wow me. I would stay here again.

“Awesome place” Talk about luxury and convenience, this is the place to stay. I got a weekend rate and had a nice large corner room with a comfy bed. Free shuttle to and from Airport and staff was very friendly. Strongly recommend!!

“Great location, average hotel” The hotel is very conveniently located, directly across from the San Diego convention center with easy access to the dining and shopping options available in the Gaslamp quarter. The room, itself, was average, as was the hotel. We could hear street sounds, even with the windows and sliding door closed, particularly after the baseball game concluded. I would recommend the hotel for its location, and it was decent for the price.

“Great downtown hotel” After staying at the Residence Inn on Walnut, I decided to give this one a try since a) it's in the River North and b) it has a pool. Since the hotel is newer, it's very clean and modern. There a lots of nice, open areas to lounge near the lobby. The room was a standard Res Inn: great kitchen, bath area, cozy beds etc... The breakfast is standard. It does get VERY crowded. But the staff is super friendly and busses tables quickly. I used to live a few blocks away and really enjoy the River North. There are so many great restaurants nearby in different price ranges. It's also near the Red Line and not too far from the others in the loop. It's really easy to catch a cab outside or grab the bus. If you're into chain store shopping, it's good to stay in the River North since Mich Ave is nearby. You're also not far from State/Madison.

“Great location” My wife and I stayed here on 19 and 20 September 2012 at the start of a Cosmos bus tour to Los Angeles. The hotel is very clean with free wifi in the rooms, and a good free breakfast in a very small breakfast room. We were a bit surprised to see that all the cutlery and plates were throw-away plastic and styrofoam, but we came to realize later that this is normal in the US, with huge huge volumes of waste. The room was quite good, and big enough for us, with one queen size bed, a flat screen TV and tea and coffee making facilities. The location is the best feature, so close to Times Square and many theatres and restaurants. As other reviewers have said, there are not enough lifts, and if you're not on one of the highest floors, walking down can save some time. We would stay here again for the excellent location, and it had everything we wanted.

“Had a great stay!!” My daughter and I stayed at this hotel from 30th Dec til 2nd Jan 2010 and had a thoroughly great stay.On arrival we were told we had a smoking room!! then told that there were no other rooms available. I asked for a manager and was asked if I would consider the room for 1 night, after explaining that I had a chest infection she gave us a room on the 11th floor with a view directly across to the USS Midway. Apart from the one slight hiccup we were impressed by the friendly staff in the hotel and enjoyed our stay. The rooms was very nice, beds were fabulous....so comfortable!! a tv in each room and the internet worked perfectly. The daily breakfast was good, we were always up early and did not experience any lines, there was a good selection of items and coffee was good and hot. We managed to to get to the managers nightly reception a few times and were impressed again by the choice of drinks available. Swimming pool was indoors, nice and warm and always quiet in the afternoon. The location had a safe feeling and we were able to walk to the downtown Gaslamp area in 5 minutes. USS Midway was right across from the hotel and the cruise ship terminal is only a few minutes cab ride away.. We intend to stay at the Embassy suites again. on our next visit to San Diego.

“Perfect in downtown!” The location is perfect for the 16th St Mall or the Convention Center. Light rail right in front of the hotel and walking distance to all things downtown. Nice and clean, bright rooms and some of the most helpful and friendly employees ... at every level of staff! Had, of course a two room suite with a flat screen in the living room and one in the bedroom. Full bathroom, plus a sink and mirror in the area between bedrm & livrm. Nice view of downtown Denver from the room and excellent free breakfast each morning ... bacon, eggs, potatoes, fruit, toast, bagels etc. The price was comparible to all the other name hotels, maybe a little less, and well worth it. This is the place to stay!

“A very nice hotel in a wonderful location” We stayed here for an anniversary weekend in early June. The hotel is located somewhat outside the center of the tourist areas (monuments, Smithsonian, etc.) but all of them are very easily reachable in minutes by Metro which stops just outside the hotel. The entry to the National Zoo is just a few blocks away on foot.The neighborhood around the hotel is fairly green and quiet. There are a few blocks full of great restaurants (Lebanese, Afghan, Italian, Indian, Mediterranean, and more...). Our room in the more modern-looking part of the hotel didn't have a great view, but the room itself was very nicely appointed and comfortable. One gripe was the vending machine on our floor that didn't work, but that was a minor inconvenience. Wifi in the room was available but expensive. The housekeeping staff were very friendly and did an immaculate job. Would happily stay here again on a future visit.

“Solid 3* BW with a few nice extras” This Bestwestern is on Hotel Circle, the bargain hotel area of SD. Despite its marine themed name, this is not close to the ocean, but the property has a nice heated pool as well as two hot tubs (one open 24h, the other closes at 10. like the pool). The landscaping is tropical, and pleasant, rooms were clean, two stories throughout, but may have to walk some distance from the lobby to get there. Breakfast was not included in the very reasonable rate, 2 Queen beds, with mirrored wall, good office chair and desk, decent Wifi. There was a public MTS bus from Old Town, stop is directly in front of the hotel. The airport shuttle operates every hour on the hour, a nice bonus (keep in mind it will take ~15 minutes to get to your terminal). Service both at checkin and checkout was much slower than typical for BW, PC with internet had non-working printer in lobby. Would probably stay here again, despite some interstate noise.

“We chose well” we chose this as it was written up in a guide book as having great family rooms, in great location and not prohibitively pricey...the guide book was absolutely right. We had a one-bedroom suite (i think all rooms are 'suites') which had 2 double beds in the bed room, large sitting room, small but adequate bathroom and plenty of extras (extra sink, microwave, coffee perculator, 2 huge TVs, big fridge, etc etc). Hotel's having a bit of a refurb it seems of some of its room but there was little disruption. Had a light lunch in the restaurant one day and that was very good. Staff were generally very good and genuinely friendly (not just on the look out for tips). Location on East 50th between Lexington and 3rd was excellent. Negatives? Front desk was a bit sullen. Hotel only has two small lifts and so waiting for one takes a painfully long time, however they are in the process of adding a third so this should improve things. Generally really very good and if we go to NYC again with the kids, we almost certainly would return.

“Would stay again” 3 of my girlfriends and I spent a girl's weekend in Austin and stayed at this hotel. The location was perfect, within walking distance of 6th street. We had 4 girls in one room and 2 full/queen beds and we had plenty of room! The housekeeping service was great (and we sure needed it after our first night out). The front desk service could have been a little more attentive. At one point when checking in, I had to wait at least 3 mins. before the Guest Service agent got off a personal call. The Business Center is a bit of a joke, it's simply a computer in the lobby. If you need more services, there are computers on the 2nd floor that charge by the minute. Other than that everything was handled well. We enjoyed having a Starbucks in the lobby, but I was told they didn't have the syrup needed to make the drink I liked both night we were in town. I would stay here again, overall, and look forward to my next adventure in Austin.

“cool, hip, nice people work here, but best suited for younger people” My daughter and I had a nice night at Rouge but holy cow...interesting place. The photos don't do it justice. Red leather banquettes, zebra print carpeting and a ton of red paint and mid modern furniture. I think they are going for a 50s mid modern sensibility but for me, it just didn't work. Mind you, it's a Kimpton so the service is very good, the people who work there genuinely want you to have a good time, and they will bend over backwards to help you out. Moreover, red leather/white leather headrests are more a style statement than a hit on their functionability. This is a hotel I think most people under 40 would think was a smashing success and a real hoot too. I just happen to be older than that.

“Up All Night” I'm a Platinum Elite Marriott Rewards member so I've demonstrated a high level of brand loyalty to the Marriott brand over the years and expect to be recognized thusly. I was chagrined to see that the first room assigned (the first of three) was directly across from the ice and vending machines! Hardly a preferred location! The second room I was assigned was a room with a connecting door to the adjacent room and I heard my neighbor coughing as well as opening and closing his drapes. The third room was facing Michigan Avenue and the street noise was intolerable all night - fire engines, ambulances, etc. Additionally, I could hear the elevator going up and down all night through the walls........ The bathrooms were so small that I've seen bigger closets. I had to wait what seemed an eternity for the elevators. The staff is hospitable enough and the location is fabulous, but for my money and piece of mind I left the Marriott early and checked into the Omni down the street. It was blissfully quiet......and I had double the amount of room.

“Okay but a bit expensive for what you get” I'm a faithful Marriott guest / customer and I can tell you there are no surprises waiting for you at this hotel. It's very clean and the beds are super comfortable. I stayed in bed until 9 and that's late for me. The restaurant, called Birch, is quite good and the room service pizza is much better than any of the delivery chains. What I don't like about this hotel is the location- not the part of town but how it's located. It's very difficult to get out of. The price of rooms here is crazy high for some reason. For 120 it would be a deal. For 200 not so much. That's why 3 stars instead of 4.

“Gute Lage, Frühstück wie bei Mc Donalds” Das Hotel ist eher unspektakulär, ein Plattenbau in allerdings guter Lage wenige Blocks vom Times Square entfernt. Das Personal war sehr bemüht und nett, die freie Kaffeeauswahl in der Lobby eine nette Beigabe. Zimmer waren nicht sehr groß, aber ausreichend komfortabel. Sauberkeit war gut. Das Frühstück war deutlich unter dem angestrebten 3-Sterne Niveau, eher wie bei Mc Donalds auf Plastikgeschirr und mit Plastikbesteck. Auswahl war mangelhaft. es gibt fürs gleiche Geld sicherlich bessere Hotels in New York und auch in nicht schlechter gelegen.

“excellent hotel and location” This hotel is in a great location to everything !! Easy walk/water taxi to whatever you want to do ! The hotel is clean, rooms large, clean, bright, comfortable, quiet. The Concierge Lounge also is tops - one of the nicest lounges Marriott has - amazing views. The Staff in the Concierge Lounge are friendly, helpful and nice - otherwise the rest of the staff was pretty stiff and not friendly. The Fitness Center is nice. I would stay here again !!!!! If you pay the additional price for the Concierge Level - be sure to request to be where you can use one set of elevators - I was required to take elevator from 16th floor to 5th floor and transfer elevator banks to the elevator that serves 31st floor. When I asked about it was told "no, that's the only room we have." ( thanks for the great service front desk staff).

“A great hotel and I stay here regularly” I come to Denver often on business and always stay here. I stay in the towers and always go for a club room on the club floor. The rooms are smart, modern and sometimes I luck out and get a very large suite. The club breakfast is excellent and the guy their super friendly and efficient. Location is great and there are lots of eating options around and about. It gets full quickly so book well in advance. The gym is huge and awesome. Sometimes I take a run down to the river.

“Estupendamente situado” Está situado justo al lado del capitolio y a una manzana de Union Station (Estacion central), de donde salen los autobuses turísticos y el metro. Tambien puedes ir andando a todos los museos. Magnifica ciudad para ir de museos. Nuestra estancia ha coincidido con la epoca de los cerezos en flor y la cuidad estaba espectacular. No esperabamos encontrar una ciudad con tantos arboles y ¡todos en flor! El hotel esta bien, como casi todos los hyatt. El personal muy atento y amable. El mayor defecto que le hemos encontrado ha sido la insonorizacion. Desde la habitacion se oye todo lo que pasa en el pasillo, conversaciones, paso de carros, aspiradora, etc. O tienes el sueño muy profundo o te despiertan los numerosos ruidos. Otra cosa que no nos ha gustado es que a las 8:00h empiezan a llamar a las habitaciones para limpiarlas. Si se te olvida poner el cartel de "no molesten" llaman, si no contestas enseguida, entran y te despiertas. De todas formas como oyes que llaman en las habitaciones de al lado tambien te despiertas. Tiene una buena piscina y gimnasio donde relajarte despues de una "dura" jornada de turismo.

“Great Location, But Watch Your Credit Card Statement” My wife and I stayed at the Westin Times Square for 3 nights in late August. The Good: - Location, location, location. Hotel is at 43rd and 8th which is less than a block away from the center of Times Square on 7th Ave. There's also a convenient rear entrance into the hotel on 42nd street through the movie theatre lobby. - Very comfortable beds. Slept very well. - No bed bugs found in room 4207. We checked very thoroughly pulling up mattresses, etc. - Room was clean and well maintained. Had all the amenities we would want. 32" flat screen TV, coffee and tea, free USA Today, nice soaps and lotions, plenty of desk space, free refrigerator upon request (we didn't request one). We had a view on the 42nd floor overlooking the Hudson. Nice view from up there and we rarely heard any street noise. - Concierge really knew her stuff. She was extremely helpful and friendly to all she encountered when I was there. She knew midtown well and was able to make reservations and offer discounts at local restaurants, etc. The Not So Good: - First and foremost, the minibar charges were a problem. We were charged about $8 after the first day for something in the minibar, but we hadn't taken anything. We opened it to see if anything was missing, but couldn't tell. We did notice, however, that there were half full bottles of soda in there. We called the front desk to have the charge removed and report the half full bottles. They removed the charge from our folio. Then the day after we checked out, they charged my credit card $53.90. I called to inquire about this charge and they said it was for the minibar again. The person in accounting submitted a credit back to my card which showed up about a week later. I can see a mistake happening the first time, but the large 2nd charge goes beyond being a mistake. This is the reason I would not recommend this hotel. Wonder how much money they make from people who don't check their credit card statements thoroughly. Based on their reaction, it seems this happens frequently. - The front desk was efficient, but the gentleman who checked us in seemed put off that there was a customer in front of him. I inquired about upgrade availability since I'm an SPG Gold Member. I was told we could get a room on a higher floor (that everyone gets when occupancy is low). When I asked about an atrium room, he said there were some available, but it would be an extra $50/night. Okay, so much for having status at this hotel. I don't know if it was just him or hotel policy not to provide upgrades to their members with status. This wasn't a good first impression. - The bathroom didn't have much counter space, but it was enough for the items we brought. Not a big deal here. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel only because they cannot seem to control the minibar charges. Either that or they use the minibar as a way to steal from their customers. I would hope it's not the latter. Otherwise, I liked the hotel for the comfort and location.

“Great location - questionable service” This hotel is in a great location with easy access - whether by foot, cab or subway - to the major sights and destinations in Washington, D.C. While the location is a plus, I was disappointed with the level of service - especially since I booked the hotel using Priceline's "name your own price" service. At times it seemed like I was treated as a second-class guest because I was only paying $120 per night when most of the other guests were paying double that price - if not more. Upon check-in, I was assigned what had to be the hotel's smallest room. It was literally half the size of the standard hotel room. While the hotel is very nicely decorated and quite traditional (I'm not much for the contemporary hotels), the television was very old, rather small and quite outdated for a hotel at this price point - especially if I had paid the full published rate. And don't bother using the hotel's $13-a-day internet service, as it is a sham and is slower than dial-up access. I went two days without internet access on my laptop and settled for using my BlackBerry phone. While I didn't dine at the hotel, I did enjoy happy-hour cocktails in the pub in the lobby. The service here was very slow with only two bartenders servicing as many as 30 patrons. The worst experience I had was check-out. The hotel wanted to charge me almost $15 for two items from the mini-bar in the room even though I hadn't consumed anything. The front desk clerk practically called me a liar and insisted I must have ordered something. Apparently, they have some sort of electronic sensor that automatically charges your room if something is moved in the mini-bar. I explained I hadn't even opened the mini-bar and it was some sort of mistake. On the whole, the hotel is not worth the published rate, but I would certainly recommend it if it can be found on Priceline.

“Tolle Lage” Top modernes, sauberes Hotel in super Lage. Kleine aber sehr saubere Zimmer. Guter Zimmerservice und jeden Tag aktuelle Zeitungen kostenlos. Mit knapp 50$ pro Nacht ist das parken allerdings sehr teuer. Sehr nette und hilfsbereite Angestellte. Zu Fuss in 3 Minuten am UnionSquare und tolle Restaurants in unmittelbarer Umgebung

“Great room, mediocre staff” This is the third time I've stayed in this hotel in the last six months. I come back because the rates are reasonable and the room, although quite small, is very stylish (if one exempts the old, cracked tile in the bath area). I'm increasingly frustrated with this hotel as it seems to go downhill every time I stay there. First, the public areas of the hotel are usually unkempt and dirty. It looks as if the carpet is only vacuumed once a day or maybe even less. The furniture is usually spread out without any order and the lobby generally looks like it gets the attention of a cheap residential hotel rather than having the attention of a fine hotel. Second, the Front Desk is a pig sty. When one stands there, there are papers, printers, shoes, boxes, magazines and the door to the office is usually open, allowing a view to the chaos behind. It's no wonder the staff is perfunctory if these are the standards that are expected by the management team. Third, the housekeeping is mediocre. In my last three stays, I've complained twice about the poor housekeeping (btw, each time I check in, I find hair in the bathroom. When I call, I've twice been told the tile is cracked and I should look again to make sure it's hair!). This time, I chose not to complain about the gum on the floor my socks kept sticking to, or the hair on the sink and in the tub, rather than deal with the surly response. I also didn't complain about the spinning sink faucets that had to be adjusted just so to stop the water flow. Fourth, the Front Desk staff could not sound less interested in you if they tried. Calls to the Front Desk are answered in a rude tone, the staff seems very eager to get you out from in front of them. They are unprofessional and lack polish. I'm sure they are kind people away from work, but their professional demeanor is sorely lacking. Finally, the rooms are showing dramatic wear. This time, my room had a very damaged desk, peeling wallpaper, scratched up walls, incredibly dusty surfaces. I had to move a table to plug something in and found old food under it where no one had cleaned. I also had two missing light bulbs (and, having learned my lesson, did not complain!). I'm a huge fan of little hotels and this hotel makes me sad. It is beautiful, but so disappointing if one is an experienced traveler. It has all the trappings of a great little boutique, but delivers so poorly that one is unsure if one should return. I just hate to see all the effort of restoring a landmark go to ruin so quickly. Frankly, it's a 3.5 star product with 1.5 star service. I'm really puzzled why one would spend millions on a renovation and not renovate the training level of the staff. I'm undecided if I will stay here again, but, if I do, it will be with great trepidation.

“Nice hotel - but currently only one working elevator” This is your typical Embassy Suites. Nice and free breakfast and happy hour. Only bad news is they currently only have one working elevator so if hotel is crowded you may wait for a minute to ride. We had a room on the top floor facing the mountains. I highly recommended getting a high floor facing the mountains as the view is pretty cool.

“Great location and fabulous bed” Excellent location within walking distance to the Galleria (though situated to what looks like a men's club...so I would not walk at night) and several decent restaurants. Fabulous bed and very clean accomodations. Good breakfast included in the price--overall an excellent value. This is not the Four Seasons, but for the price it was excellent.

“So bad I had to write my first review” I travel weekly for business, and this trip was for pleasure. I selected the hotel with no particular high expectations, a few friends and I were meeting in Chicago from a few different cities to celebrate a birthday. Everything was fine at check it. Upon checkout, my rate was DOUBLE from what my confirmation email from marriott.com provided me. I call the desk just thinking it is a simple mistake and it will get fixed. Front desk person could not fix it, so she informs me the manager will be contacted. The manager calls me back in my room to inform me that it was their mistake, the apologized but were not going to fix the rate. They told me I should have been informed at check in, but they did not, they apologized for that as well. They still were not going to fix my rate. This was the most unethical practice I have ever seen, I cancelled my return reservation for this hotel for a few days later and will be staying across the street.

“Fine hotel, not outstanding.” This hotel was fine, if unremarkable. I would stay there again and I would encourage a friend to stay there as well, but the hotel is lacking in several ways. The rooms, while nice and adequate, were not extra spacious. Though well furnished, they were frankly the size of a Days Inn hotel room. The bathroom, through clean, was of customary small size. I did have a very nice bath mat my first night, but it was subsequently replaced by the standard flimsy mat. I foudn the location to be very, very strange. The Galleria is next door, but it is, despite its size, not a place you are likely to enjoy spending much time. The outdoor shopping located two blocks away is likely far more enjoyable to most people. The hotel staff were very friendly and hospitable. The hotel lobby was smallish and offered several sofas, etc, but did not provide the most inviting location to sit and read or visit. If you are looking for a dependable hotel - this is certainly safe and clean and restful. If you are looking for a hotel expereince, then you probably ought look elsewhere.

“Do not stay here!” I have been many times to New York and travelled extensively both in really expensive hotels and really cheap ones. But this is the least value for money i have ever had. 609 USD plus taxes for a room where the color in the ceiling of the bathroom is falling off, a bathtub dirty and rusty "hole". The wall paper was coming of the seam broken. Dark dungy carpets. Do not stay here. Lousy service at concierge desk unfriendly. The positive was a comfortable bed and central location close to everything. If you want to stay close to good restaurants and fun bars stay in Meatpacking District or Lower East or somewhere in SoHo, Tribecca. This is for tourist with too much money.

“Return Visit was just as pleasant” Similar to my initial review (june 2010). This was once again a pleasurable stay at the Cosmo Hotel. We loaded up a room with several friends and enjoyed see the sights for a weekend. Rooms are understandably small but if we had a normal amount of people in the room (2 people for 2 doubles instead of 5) its actually quite nice. The smallest part of the room is the bathroom, but it gets the job done. Great location, cute little cafe adjacent and within walking to Brooklyn Bridge/World Trade and it is directly over a subway stop which is great for lugging all your stuff to and from the bus depots. Staff usually asks us whether we would like an inside (alley) facing room or a street facing room. First time we did inside and it was a bit dark, city was noisier but not unpleasantly so. Will definitely continue to stay here.

“Nice but over priced” Spent an in town weekend getaway at Stephen F Austin, while entertaining friends from Houston to Stubbs’s live music a few blocks away. Everything was fine and the staff was great, but did not feel the rate justified the experience. Should have used TripAdvisor to find best rate.

“Nice hotel” This was our second visit to this hotel whilst on a tour. No complaints regarding rooms all with a bonus balconey. Short walk to 16th street where most of the shopping is, shops nothing to write home about infact lots our a bit down market. Visited aquarium on previous visit well worth it slightly out of town but walkable. Staff in hotel could have been a bit more friendly, from the front desk to the restaurant who where especially curt and are possibly in the wrong job.

“Good Location, Good Service, A bit pricey” Ok for the not so good news-- the price was $200/night during the week, when there was no major conference in town. Now for the good news -- the hotel was clean, staff was pleasant and accomodating, Philadelphia's downtown is very walkable and despite troubling crime rates...I felt safe walking from my meetings after 10pm nightly. I didn't eat in the hotel (I seldom do in a city the size of Phily) so I can't comment on that. However, several coffee shops and chain restaurants were closeby in the Market Street area. If I stay again, I will shoot for a much better price. It shouldn't be over $149/night.

“Great location, not a boutique hotel” The Quincy advertises itself as a boutique hotel, which I think is the first problem because it raises the expectations for no reason. The hotel is ok, no major complains, the rooms are big, each has its own kitchen, which is convienient for longer states. Staff is nice and helpful. That being said there is nothing unique, special, about it - it is very basic, they don't even offer breakfast so I am not sure where the boutique description comes from. I think they should advertise it as what it is instead of giving misleading information. The location is great tho, right next to the Dupont Circle, which is very convienient.

“Lovely Hotel” Just an overnight but Hotel facilities are very good, Rooms are good sized with nice Hyatt style bathrooms. Bars & restaurants on site are extremely nice & the 1st impression is great. I used the Gym facilities again which were good next to the pool & jacuzzi. Car Park next door & I did manage to get invited to teh business Breakfast which is arranged monthly so complementary breakfast included which was well appreciated.

“Yuck O” Gross Hotel. Way overpriced for what it is. In desperate need of a remodel. The carpet was torn in our room. There was major construction across the Riverwalk that made it hard to hear the TV -- which is part of the reason we stayed there. We had a conference and they were doing a live feed directly into the hotels rooms via the TV -- but with all the noise it defeated the whole purpose of the live feed. Anyway, I would not stay here again if someone paid for my room.

“Monstrously comfortable, historic bank building,” First, don't use the street address in a GPS. There is no indication on Broadway that you've reached the hotel. The actual awning is on 6th, just around the corner, and that is where the valet parking is. Use 1000 6th avenue instead. Once there, though, expect a very comfortable stay, helpful staff. My room, 106, was very spacious, and the king bed was literally the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever experienced (I travel almost weekly). There is a variety of restaurants in close walking distance, though the downtown area nearby is unimpressive. The original character of the bank is maintained, complete with teller windows and a large vault now used as a meeting room. The lobby has been meticulously restored, and it is full of architectural detail. It is ornate yet cozy at the same time and a very nice change from cookie cutter chain properties. My room had plenty of space for an armoir, two overstuffed chairs, an ottoman, desk and office chair. The TV is in the armoir which is at a right angle to the bed. It does not extend out to it is not possible to watch TV from the bed and see the whole screen. Minor issue.

“Great stay - perfect getaway and great location for all things Inner Harbor” We needed a hotel in close proximity to the M&T Bank Stadium for the 2010 NCAA Lacrosse Finals. Well, it really was a great location. Not only was it in walking distance to the stadium, but it was also even more accessible to the Inner Harbor. We never needed our car! The hotel itself was great. I have no complaints at all. The room was nice and comfy - - very nice bathroom, lots of space, comfy beds and we all enjoyed ourselves. The only problem I had, and it was a small one, was that they wanted to charge me an extra $30/night for my 15 yr old son, when I had the room rate confirmed. Good thing I had my blackberry with me. I dug up the confirmation email that Intercontinental sent me and all was fine. So, all in all, I would stay here again.

“A Lovely Hotel, Location and Staff” I was a bit skeptical when my boyfriend booked this hotel for the weekend. Looking at the photos online, felt that maybe this wasnt the place for me, as I was use to more "luxurious" resort type places. BUT, i trusted his judgment, read reviews on here, and felt that maybe he had indeed made the right choice. When we arrived at the hotel, after a stop-and-go drive from Dallas/Fort Worth on a Friday night, I honestly just wanted to get out of the car and get to our room. I pulled up to valet, and was told I was not in the right spot in valet and needed to go back around the block to pull up behind the car in the back of the row. Mind you, this car was already hanging out into the main street. I felt this was inappropriate as I was a paying guest at this hotel, not someone parking to walk across to the Riverwalk. I kept my car where it was, and without arguing with me, he promptly gave me a ticket to park the car. However, after the initial awful experience with the rude valet, we were greeted by the nicest gentleman at the front desk. He gave us a general idea of where all the restaurants were, and helped us print out our tickets for Sea World as their guest computer wasnt working at the moment. This gentleman was so prompt and courteous that upon checkout two days later, he remembered my boyfriends name as we were walking into the lobby. I must say, this was impressive. That alone would get me to return to this hotel. The hallways and elevator were clean heading to our room. Our room was #225. It didnt have a view, but we werent going to be in our room much anyway, other than to sleep. It was a bit on the smaller side, but ive heard that all the rooms are a bit different in size. The bathroom was a decent size, the water in the shower was warm, the bed was very comfortable, sheets were clean, the floors and bathroom were clean, and the air conditioning stayed running constantly. The bar downstairs is really nice as well. The bartender is knowledgeable about the area, the happy hour prices were good, and they allow you to bring the alcohol to your room which is nice. (Not sure if any others allow this as well, but was a nice touch for us) There is a pool, although it is small. You can see pictures of it on their website for reference. Its on the other side of the, but on property nonetheless. We didnt get in so Im not sure if it is heated or not. The hotel is right across from the mall (which is on the Riverwalk.) The hotel is a 3 minute walk to the Riverwalk at the most. Its a good location for getting to multiple restaurants, shopping etc. Although its not ON the Riverwalk, it wasnt inconvenient getting around anywhere. I fully enjoyed my stay at The Crockett, and if i return to San Antonio, will most definitely book here again. Feel free to ask me any questions you might have about the hotel or the area!

“Fabulous Hotel” Perfect location, right near Bryant Park and Times Square. Central to everything! The rooms are fabulous! They are renovated, clean and the beds are so comfortable. The bathrooms are a great size as well. Free wi-fi for Kimpton In Touch members. Wine hour every night in the lobby, you can't beat it! And the lobby and restaurant have just been renovated as well, and are just beautiful! Service is great. I was checked in within minutes and when I forgot my computer cord, they found one in lost and found and brought one to my room immediately for me. I would definitely stay here again!

“Excellent location” Great location walking distance of Broadway, Times square and central park, several breakfast diners nearby, the subway is 2 blocks away we had a 7 day pass ($25) and it was great got us everywhere even went to Coney Island which is worth the visit if you have time and try Nathans hot dogs. I highly recommend Ellens Stardust diner in the evenings it is on the corner a couple of doors from the theatre showing Mama Mia, all the servers sing songs from the shows if you are into musicals you will adore this place, the hotel is very clean and the staff are friendly and helpful the only moan is the elevators, sooo sloooow apart from that it ticks all the boxes for me.

“Wonderful from the moment we checked in” After a bad experience at a Doubletree property in Pittsburgh, I was very wary about choosing this location. Yet a good rate on the Doubletree web site, combined with the location, convinced me to give the brand another try. I am so delighted that I did, as it provided a perfect location for a shopping trip with a friend. We were greeted so warmly at check-in by Jose. You would think we had booked a penthouse suite -- he treated us like 5-star guests and was very helpful. I can't remember another check-in where I was made to feel like such a truly valued guest, and it started our visit on a wonderful note. We went upstairs to a partial lakeview room that did not disappoint and was a good size for two, with very comfortable beds. In the rest of the hotel, the lobby was cozy with a cute little bar (and, conveniently, free internet access). And the Einstein's bagel shop in the lobby was super convenient to pop down for delicious bagels and coffee to bring back to the room for breakfast. Our positive experience extended to check-out and beyond, when we needed to leave bags due to a few hours lag time before our flight out. The bellman, whose name unfortunately I have forgotten, was very helpful and accommodating; we felt totally comfortable leaving our bags with him -- and, like our check-in, as though it was a pleasure to for him assist us. The only downside in the stay was having to pay for internet in the room -- and being presented with fees not by room but separately for each device -- a drag with two laptops and two iPods, which would have cost a fortune if we bought 4 separate internet plans. This really needs to be revisited to take into account the way people travel in 20111 (this is also the only reason I didn't give 5 stars). Despite this single caveat, this was really a pretty hotel with exceptionally well-trained and accommodating staff, and an unexpectedly great find. Travel surprises are rarely pleasant -- this was that rare surprise that really made our trip.

“Great location and hotel” This hotel is connected to Terminal A at Logan which is great if you are a Delta flier. The rooms are very nice with a beautiful view on one side of the hotel of Boston downtown and harbor. The other side has a street view which is not as nice - request downtown view if possible. The hotel is big and has a great exec floor lounge as well as a nice sports bar/restaurant downstairs. Pricey though for a stay, but definitely worth it if you are a hilton gold member or above so you get free wifi and exec lounge. The convenience of being connected to the airport is great.

“Enjoyed my stay” Just a little walk to various means of public transportation. Friendly staff. Some rooms along staircase may experience noise. All rooms open to outside of building. Room was nice, comfortable. Slight stale odor in mine (fixed with air freshener). Has elevator. Would choose again.

“Many positives, but service was lacking” I was provided with a very comfortable and roomy room. The room was spotless and the cleaning staff was great. There are several things that limit this to a 3 star status at best in my opinion. In house dining is very limited. One night I called to order a bottle of wine from room service at 12:07. I was informed that room service stopped at midnight. I do not recall seeing anything about this on the menu, nor was it pointed out upon check in. The bell staff was very quick, but many times no one was on duty, or just not paying attention when we required a cab. Breakfast is advertised to 11:30, but it was not pointed out that the buffet shut down just after 10:30. The breakfast we ordered and the service was very good, but it put us a little behind schedule due to ordering v. the buffet. I repeat it was a very nice room, and if you are prepared for the shortcomings the price and location would be far more appreciated.

“Older rooms need updating” Recently stay at the Catamaran Resort for three nights. Check in clerk was friendly and efficient. Was assigned to an unit in an older building on the ground floor facing the parking lot. The room appeared to be clean, however the bedspread appeared to be worn out. The room was good in size and despite being next to the parking lot, it was pretty quiet. The bed was comfortable and the shower had good water pressure. Had a friend staying in the tower building and when I checked it out, it was ten times better than my room. His room appeared to be more open and it even had a full size refrigerator inside. I was definitely jealous and to think we even pay the same price for our rooms. Despite that, most of the employees I saw were friendly and professional. If I stay here again, I definitely would want a tower room. Even though its marked three stars, it should be 3 1/2 stars.

“Great location, under construction” I booked this location because of the great reviews I saw on Trip Advisor, I'd always wanted to stay at the Peabody but this was cheaper and better rated. The hotel was nice and clean, the staff was polite and efficient. Our room was amazing, even for a standard, it was larger than I expected, it had an odd shape, curved because it was located in that curve you see on the pictures. The balcony was nice, we could hear live blues music playing the evening we were there but it did not go on past about 9pm. I did hear some construction noise shortly after check-in and some after breakfast but it wasn't too bad. The decor was clean and fresh. I would definitely recommend this location to others and also stay here again unless I can get Peabody to beat their rate which I don't see happening! There is a continental breakfast served on premise but we ate at Zac's in the hotel instead wanting a something a little more substantial. Zac's was very good also.

“Good Location” We only stayed one night in the hotel but enjoyed our stay. The hotel is conveniently located just of I-35. We didn't realise that it was valet parking only ($15 a night). We usually like to leave stuff in the car that we don't need and go back to the car on a needs basis however Valet parking meant we couldn't do this. Valets were friendly. Check-in was quick and hassle free. We asked if there was a room on the Club floor and got upgraded free of charge to a King Suite. The best part of this room is the fantastic bathroom (although the jacuzzi bath was v. noisy). At check-in we were also given vouchers for complimentary cocktails that night in the hotel bar (18th floor - great views of the city) and vouchers for full complimentary breakfast. All in all we thought we got good value for money. We didn't use the pool at the hotel instead drove to Bartons Spring Natural Pool in Zilker Park (only 5-10mins away). This pool is fantastic and is a must on a visit to Austin.

“Great Hotel, Great Service!” I LOVE this hotel. I've been staying at this hotel sporatically over the past 12 years or so. Not sure if I like it so much because it has a lot of sentimental value to me (my now husband and I stayed there when we got engaged back in September 2000) or because it is a reliable hotel. My office also used to be right across the street from it, so I stayed there a lot because of that. The rooms are small (even for NYC), but very updated and comfortable. Great shower, bed and bedding. Room temperature is always perfect and TV channels are great. I had a corner room this time, so I had great light from the many windows. Their bath products are amazing. I'm a marketers dream. I buy the products because I like them so much using them at the hotel! Staff is friendly and accommodating. Keep doing what you are doing!

“STAY AWAY FROM THERE!” We understood that in that days the hotel was fully booked but the rooms that they gave to us were really bad and unpreseantables as the pictures attached shows. As one of our relatives suffers diabetes he needs a refrigerator to keep his medicine at the right temperature but they don ́t provide in any way. We ́re really disappointed with this lack of kindness especially with guests with medical problems. REALLY TERRIBLE HOTEL! STAY AWAY FROM THEM!

“Great Management and Service” The staff and management of the Le Meridian could not have been more lovely and accommodating. Due to a death in our family we were required to make extensive modifications to our reservation, Kathryn (one of the managers) was most helpful and went out of her way to assist us. The location can't be beat, located at the intersection of the Embarcadero, China Town, and the Financial District.
“Didn't change the sheets” The room appeared to be very clean and the bathroom was very clean but I don't believe they changed the sheet before I arrived. There was evidence.

“Good location, small rooms” This is billed as a resort, I suppose because they have two pools. However, I have stayed in larger rooms in Manhattan. The basic rooms are cramped, especially with two beds. On the positive side, the TVs are among the best I've ever found in a hotel--so good that we stayed in two nights to watch movies in the room. Located on the bay but not on the beach. Should you be going to Sea World, this would be a good location with a free shuttle.

“Good Experience” I found the room to comfortable and well furnished. The staff was attentive. If you are arriving via the subway from the airport you will need to take a cab from the nearest station (Grand) to the hotel if you have bags. I don't care for the fact that they charge for internet access--a nickle and dime affair.

“Felt like home away from home” I had stayed at the Hotel Rex about 7 years ago and had good memories of it... I just stayed there again for a week and quickly fell in love again. My particular room was a little bit of a cave..with only a brick wall for a view, so therefore was a little dark and I didn't get cellphone signal in the room.. BUT it was very quiet and cozy. The staff are lovely and helpful. A great hotel all around.

“Huge Hotel--Good All Around” I have been frequenting Dallas on business recently and have stayed here three times over the past two months. Have previously stayed at the Magnolia (the place is needs new leadership and a face lift) and the Embassey in Addison (OK for business). The Anatole is massive with two buildings and another separate fitness club building. I am Hiton Diamond but tend to be frank. The rooms I have stayed in were all upgrades including two suites. Rooms have been massive, clean and consistent with my Hilton experiences. Bathrooms are small but all functional. Executive lounge is a misnomer. Bars are well stocked and there are plenty of them. Ate one night at Nana's and if you are on a corporate expense account, go for it. If not, ask the concierge for help. Good solid place to stay just outside the downtown area.

“格式高い老舗ホテルの立地は最高、サービスは改善の余地あり” アッパーイーストサイドにあるカーライルは古くから世界中のVIPが定宿としていたことで知られています。 クラシックルームに泊まりましたが、1泊USD600代でかなり割高です。アメニティなども充実していますが、サービスは劣ります。オペラの予約を取ってもらうべく、コンシェルジュに直接出向いて頼み、外出から帰って来るまでに何らかのフォローがあるかと思いましたが、結局連絡はありませんでした。 これだけの宿泊料金をチャージするのであれば、老舗の名声にあぐらをかくことなくサービスも向上してもらいたいですね。

“Surprisingly large room at a great price” I was very surprised to find not only a large bedroom, but an attached small sitting room upon check in. I found this to be a great bargain for a Michigan Avenue Chicago hotel based on other stays in this city. The check in staff were very friendly, maid service prompt and thorough. I stayed there due to a conference and the conference room was comfortable, as well as the lunches that were served excellent. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room was very quiet. Great central Michigan Avenue location. I will definitely stay here again when given the opportunity.

“Made for the Young and Hip, not for Older people” First of all, the staff was great and the location was excellent!. However, the beds and furniture in the rooms were very low and made it difficult to arise. Secondly, there was NO coffeemaker! I can not tolerate a hotel without cofffee making accoutrements. The lobby was lovely but it was always so crowded with young revelers, that we had to go elsewhere to have a drink and conversation. Turn up the lights for goodness sake! BTW, the bed was not that comfortable and the room was small and had atrocious lighting. Our view was of rusted stairs next door....not good at all.

“Can't believe stains on a bathroom's wall!” Ok where do I begin...hotel location and SPG brand has always been my favorite. The room was spacious but the bathroom was tiny but the worst thing is stains on a bathroom's wall. I thought it was some sort of design at first but when I took a good look, seems like they tried really hard to clean it but it won't come off. I didn't want to imagine what it was. Bathroom itself was too small and got no room to move. The floor plan was poorly design as it took forever to get to the room and I got no view. Location itself was perfect as it's only a short walk from the pier. Staffs were friendly and they got free wifi in a lobby.

“Nothing special but a good option in expensive Boston” The hotel is just a short walk from the Freedom Trail on the opposite side of the river to Downton Boston in Chalestown. You are away from the hustle and bustle of the main tourist areas and at night the area can feel a bit desolate and lifeless - walk up along Warren Street in Charlestown for more life and eating/drinking options. But you can walk pretty much everywhere and if you want to stay in Boston this is a good budget end choice. Leaving aside the fact that this is an expensive city for accomodation, I thought the standard wasn't great. Previous reviewers commented on it being like a YMCA. I would agree. Corridors and rooms are a bit institutional but our room was very clean. Bed was very uncomfortable (too soft) and only had a sheet and the bedspread. 2 pillows between us and the 3rd one in the closet had no cover on it (and was stained and old). Our room had a full size oven, fridge/freezer, microwave, sink etc. We were only staying for one night so had no use for them but with no utensils or crockery provided I can't see how they are much use to the casual tourist. Also, the fridge/freezer was right at the end of the bed and was quite noisy - we had to turn it off during the night. We had a minor issue with noise in the corridor outside our room but the front desk staff dealt with it promptly at 12am. Can't comment on the leisure facilities. Probably wouldn't choose this place again.

“Average, at best” I agree with the other reviews that the room was dated. Had several small problems and, except for the Director of Facilities (who couldn't have been nicer or more helpful), the other staff looked bothered or distracted each time I went to the front desk. Maybe they need more help? 45 mins after checking in, housekeeping opened my door without knocking. Also, had problems with the wireless.
“Wonderful place” We stayed only one night on our return from Beijing. Our room was spotless and very quiet. Highly recommended. M

“Had a spider in my room!” Check-in was fine, the front desk was helpful and checked us in promptly. The elevator floors could've used some good cleaning and the halls are a bit dingy. Got into the room and was cold, so turned on the heater. The units are under the window and the window had a curtain, so when the warm air was blowing out - the air would blow into the curtain, which in turn would not circulate in the room. So, in order to get the room warmer had to crank up the heater. And that's when I saw the spider on the curtain! I first thought it was dead so didn't touch it. Then afterwards when I was sitting on my bed - I saw it moving onto the ceiling and then the wall!! Ended up killing it with my slipper! Didn't want to move room as we had already showered and were comfortable in bed. The room was shabby with an outdated tv. Bathrooms were not clean at all. Toilet didn't look like it was cleaned so couldn't really sit on it and the shower wasn't clean either. They should really look into what their housekeeping does. Seems to me that they pay housekeeping to do nothing at all. Breakfast wasn't bad - but it shuts down around 9am! So better wake up early to eat. Choices were good and the area was clean. The hotel is located off the freeway and that was the best part of it.

“Great Value if you get a good deal!!!” The Renaissance New York Hotel 57 was a great hotel and a tremendous value. My wife and I stayed there for a weekend in April and I got a room for an incredible price via their website. The location was great and close to several subway lines. The room was extremely small (just a full size bed) but was definitely modern and nicely maintained. For the value, I definitely give this hotel five stars.

“Okay, would try another property for next LAX overnight” The property was okay. There will, of course, be some noise next the airport, but I found this property to carry more airport and internal hotel noise than other places I've stayed at near LAX. The food was average, and overall I'd consider this an average property.

“Refreshingly glamourous and petfriendly” I had a wonderful stay here and was surprised to find this hotel to be very glam. The bed was beyond comfortable, room service very efficient, front desk staff friendly and a great value to boot. And it is walkable to everywhere in the city.

“Great location; small room” The location is awesome - convenient to Newbury Street, Fenway Park, and connected to a shopping at Copley Plaza. Starbucks in the lobby is good for our morning coffee fix. The room was very small though. Barely enough room for the two full size beds (which is hard with 2 kids and 2 adults) and not much room to move around.

“Interessante Location - für Touristen ideal” Das Sheraton at Wharf ist ein typisches Touristen Hotel am Wharf in San Francisco. Man trift hier auf allerlei amerikanische College Kids, italienische Großfamilien und englische Hochzeitspaare. Allerdings ist der Hotel so groß (ein kompletter Block), dass man nur schwer mehrmals ins Gespräch kommt. Highlight ist sicher die Location (allerlei Attraktion in Gehweite). Die Zimmer sind renoviert und zweckmäßig. Frühstück ist nicht zu empfehlen (viel Auswahl in der Nähe). Vorsicht: Parken pro Tag ab 45$

“Great staff and frill free hotel” We stayed here the evening before our international flight to Japan. The staff were wonderful. I had a 2:30 am shuttle to the airport with a lot of luggage and a crated cat. The driver was super helpful with our bags. The front desk let us store our excess luggage in a closet off of the lobby so that we didn't need to haul it up to our room, which was really nice. The room was very basic, but clean and comfortable. For the price, it is perfect. They have upgraded rooms with microwaves and fridges, too.

“Marriott Marquis on Broadway” If you told anyone that you were visiting New York and staying in Times Square/Broadway, they'd say "You lucky Devil!" The hotel was clean and pleasant enough but it just didn't like up to my expectations. Actually, for the "cheap", tacky location of Times Square/Broadway, it fit right in. I would never have chosen this place (and I didn't, I was put up here with other business colleagues) and it was a world of difference from the last Marriott that I stayed in, in Tyson's Corner, VA, which was way, way better, as a hotel. The place looked tired and my room was a hotchpotch collection of furniture that didn't quite fit. All in all, I felt a bit tacky staying here, yet I'm sure many people would love the place in the heart of this loud, glitzy and grubby area.

“Great Location -- Great Staff! (Small rooms & noise)” I was in town for a conference and stayed 5 nights at the Ramada Inn. The reviews are pretty accurate on this property. The rooms are on the small side but clean -- Tue/Wed/Thursday the hotel was pretty quiet but on Friday & Sat night the party starts in Gaslamp and it does get noisy. I had ear plugs and it helped! The front desk staff & bellman were outstanding! I spoke to the hotel Manger during my stay due to an issue with my room and he immediately addressed the issue and "made it right". (Thank you!) If you want a "resort hotel" I would recommend not staying here -- if you want a reasonably priced room without a lot of "fluff" and a great staff -- give it try.

“wonderful!” Got through Priceline as a 3 star and it was wonderful!! a super friendly desk clerk.. my room was amazing! clean, great bed, great bath.. super nice. My only issues were: one of the phones didn't work, the ice machine didn't work on the floor, and you could hear people slamming their doors. But - for $61 - this was a great place to stay!!!

“Great Staff” We stayed here in November 2003 and thoroughly enjoyed it. The staff were so friendly and helpful. It's a fun hotel - kind of funky decor and we enjoyed the evening wine reception. We got a great rate and would definitely consider staying here again - our kids complained a little about the walk back to the hotel - but the exercise is good for you!

“Ci tornerei subito!” Carino e pulito, personale cordiale. Il bagno non è un granchè ma la è posizione ottima per girare la città a piedi (a SF non ci sono parcheggi e quelli che ci sono, sono carissimi) infatti è a 5 minuti a piedi dalla fermata Powell del Cable car e Union Square. L'hotel è particolare, con le stanze dedicate ai film ambientati a San Francisco. Colazione abbondante, e saletta cinema che ogni sera propone un film girato nella città! Ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo.

“Middle Town -Top Lage - Gay Area” das holiday inn hat die optimal lage um philadelphia zu fuss zu entdecken. es liegt direkt im zentrum und gleich in der gay area :-) zimmer inklusive frühstück, man sollte sich aber vom breakfast nichts erwarten, amerika eben. der check in war genail rasch, superfreundliches personal. free w-lan vorhanden. die garage ist beim hotel jedoch zu bezahlen und kostet 22 U$ pro nacht. zimmer sehr gross, flat tv, klimaanlage, tolle betten , gute schlag garantie :-)), leider keine mini bar vorhanden, dafür kaffeemschine und kaffee. würd das hotel sofort wieder nehmen.

“Nice Place Comfortable beds” It was a nice place. Has an Oceans 11 feel. Only complaints are they seemed to be doing some work in the next room and it was annoying and they could kick up the cleaning of the bathroom a notch.

“Nice Hotel” I stayed at the city club for the first time in March. The small hotel is very nice, quite and has a feel of quality - the reception staff was delightful. The room was a little dark for working but high on design....the bath room was the best. Overal this was a great find in a city where it is sometimes had to sleep

“Like Sleeping In A Shoe Box” Truly the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. The bathroom is smaller than those found in travel trailers and requires a dangerous step up on a narrow tread. The advertised refrigerator is actually a cooler that will not keep milk cold. Even the toilet is a small round type barely large enough to perform its function with a slow refill rate. The window looks out onto a brick wall. The rugs were last replaced in 1985. The hall corridors are not wide enough for two children to pass each other side by side. The bed was comfortable and the in-room internet connection does work as does the television in every other room that you can hear through the walls. I thought I found a downtown bargain at $159 but I will gladly stay somewhere else for more money my next trip.

“Spent 5 nights at this location” Though I am not a big fan of the location, the hotel was clean, comfortable and stress free. The room I had seemed a little small if you are traveling with a family, but after the family left it was fine. I stayed on points and felt the point to dollar ratio was a value. Not sure if I would stay there paying their sheet price. Do not let the average score fool you, I would stay here again, but it is just not Awesome, rather simply nice enough.

“Great location” I enjoyed my stay at the Marriott City Center in Uptown Charlotte. The hotel is located right on "The Corner" which is the center of the Charlotte business district. It is across the street from the Bank of America Tower and other major office buildings. The Uptown area is full of dinning and was filled with people during the evenings, I felt quite comfortable walking around after dark. The cab ride from the Charlotte airport was $20, for the return trip I asked the bellman to get me a cab and was a little apprehensive ($$$) when he took my bag to one of the black Lincoln Towncars which service the hotel, the car service picked by the bellman was great and only slightly greater ($25 fare to CLT) than the ratty cab I had taken in the night before. The property was well decorated and spotless. The rooms were comfy with a quality bed and work area. The hotel has in-room high speed internet but annoyingly the service is $9.99/day. I was not able to pick up any free signals from neighboring properties either. The hotel has an indoor pool and exercise area with an outdoor rooftop patio for relaxing. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was pricey, around $14 for the buffet (which was fine, no complaints on the quality or quantity of food available). I will probably check out the Omni nearby for comparison next time I'm in Charlotte but would not hesitate in the least to stay here again.

“Unacceptable” I had an unpleasant experience at this motel and will not be returning. However, I acknowledge the motel had some good points, which I list first. It may be possible to have a decent experience here if you stay on the side furthest away from the Denny's, and if you check the plumbing first to make sure it works properly, and if you find the room to be acceptably clean. But with so many hotel choices nearby, I wouldn't chance it. Positives (or Neutral) : * Unusually firm mattress * Refrigerator in room next size up from tiny * Microwave in room * Swimming pool that's larger than what you'd expect in such a small motel. * Although the room is small, the decor is neutral and pleasant. * My partner found the breakfast acceptable. It included: 2 kinds of cereal, waffles, muffins, toast, 2 kinds of juice, and coffee. And now the negatives which greatly outweighed the positives for me: * Dirty bathroom with many hairs on the floor. Yuck. * Shower water temperature varied wildly from hot to cold. * No cold water in the bathroom faucet. My partner and I had to quickly wash our hands before the water completely warmed up, or we would have been scalded. A child could have easily been scalded. * VERY LOUD. We were in room 210, two rooms away from the Dennys which shares the parking lot. I was kept up in the middle of the night (3:30 to after 4 am) by people blasting car radio and having loud conversations in the parking lot. I had no idea Dennys is open 24 hours a day, but found out the hard way. * A too small, tight parking lot. We were okay b/c we were there on a Sunday night, but had we been there Saturday night when they were sold out, we would have had a problem. * I noticed a flea jumping on the bed. And as Dr. Phil said, "for every one you see there's a hundred you don't." That may have explained why a previous reviewer's family was bitten up at night. The cost was $96 a night (AAA discount), before taxes and fees. In my experience, motels in the L.A. area that cost under $100 are dives. I recommend staying away.

“Not what I expected” My family visits downtown Fort Worth/Sundance Square several times a year. I was really excited when this hotel opened as Sundance Square was in need of more lodging options. If you are expecting this to be like other Embassy Suites....it's not. Don't get me wrong, there are some nice qualities to the hotel but overall I would not stay here again for the price per night ($189). Upon arriving we were greeted at the door with 6 or 7 people in suits and uniforms welcoming us to the hotel although no one really offered to help with bags. They seemed to be cluttering up the already small lobby. Check in took longer than expected as well. The hotel is well appointed, rooms are nice and comfortable. Most of the areas felt very clean and almost new. The lobby is very small as well as the hallways and elevetors. It was almost impossible to navigate a luggage cart from the front door to your room. There is no self parking and the valet parking is chaotic. There is no room to leave your car, so often you are blocking traffic while waiting for someone to get your car. It took between 10-20 minutes to get our car, even when calling to the lobby before going down. The manager's reception in the afternoon was nice as well as having breakfast provided. The problem was that they kept running out of food and the cooked to order line took over 20 minutes to get through. We were there over a weekend and it was pretty crowded. The elevators took an incredible amount of time to get to the lobby. Again, the hotel was nice, but I would probably stay elsewhere next time in Fort Worth.

“Served our needs for two night stay” This hotel worked well for us for a short two night stay. We had a hard time finding a hotel in Philadelphia with good Trip Advisor reviews and reasonable rates and settled on this hotel after finding a discounted rate that included parking (still high in our opinion, but took some of the sting off the high overnight parking rates that are common throughout the city). As many have mentioned on Trip Advisor, this hotel has been recently renovated. We did not find the fancy "key needed to run the lights" system as annoying as others. Seems like a perfectly reasonable addition. One thing about the room that we did not like were the bed frames...they stuck out much past the mattress and my husband and I both smacked our knees pretty good. I'm embarrassed to even mention that in a review, but for a newly renovated room, it's poorly designed. The water also takes quite a while to warm up for the shower. Despite having a car, we took cabs around the city and the valet attendants were the saving grace for the staff at this hotel-nicest I've every experienced. The front desk staff were a bit cold. Cabs were almost always lined up outside this hotel which was nice. We ventured down to the SEPTA stop nearby once, couldn't find a ticket machine and came back for a cab. With some better research on our part the SEPTA would have been a good option for getting around the city from this hotel as well. Overall this is a lovely hotel and I give the Hilton additional props for the free Wi-Fi in the rooms.

“Amazing Hotel” My husband and I spend four amazing days at the InterContinental in Chicago.
