We booked it through a third party provider and expected to get the smaller room or one beside the ice machine. Before leaving home, I contacted the hotel directly and requested a non-smoking room with a king sized bed. I got an immediate response to my request and was also informed, to my delight, that we were booked into a room in the Historic Tower. When we arrived, we were provided with efficient, friendly service. The room was larger than I had expected and very clean. We read about the history of the hotel and later during our stay went on a tour of this historic building. It is absolutely amazing, if you are interested in older buildings staying in this hotel is an absolute MUST. It was like taking a step into the past. In addition, it was right on Michican Avenue, so we were in the heart of Chicago. We certainly reommend this hotel to anyone wanting to experience Chicago in style!!! Sandra, Ontario

“Will be a showpiece - when the teething problems are fixed” Previous reviewers have commented on the degree to which this new hotel has opened without really having everything checked and working - and our experience was no different. It should be a flagship for Holiday Inn Express - an elegant bank building that has been sensitively refurbished with a particularly large and elegant lobby space. It also has a first rate staff team. The neighbourhood is 'up and coming', which means that it has a slightly edgy feel, but it is close enough to the Inner Harbor - about five blocks - to be confident that improvement will continue. Besides, it is only about one block from a major police post and patrol cars are constantly in evidence. However, what we Brits call the "snagging" process at the end of a big construction job has plainly not been done satisfactorily, if at all. Our room had a chipped bath, a badly scratched side panel on the bath, a loose faucet over the bathroom sink (tap over the basin), power circuit that did not function and rendered two lights inactive, and a loose leg on the studio chair. We were staying over a weekend so it was not unreasonable that some of these could not be fixed by maintenance, but they do raise issues both about building management and construction quality. If a plumber got away with fitting a chipped bath, or dropping a wrench into it and not replacing it, what does this say about construction standards - and what other problems are lurking? The front desk were charming and thanked us for our courteous reports - if we didn't tell them about problems, they couldn't be fixed. Well, there are consultants in the hotel business who do that sort of pre-occupancy checking - and I don't think they would miss a chipped bath. Is it really fair to expect customers to do that checking for you? Is it really appropriate to charge them quite a full rate for being the test-drivers? I do think this is a hotel with a good future - but I would track its reviews quite carefully to be sure that the problems reported by this, and other early reviewers, do actually get fixed. By the way, if you are there on a weekend, there is a really good farmer's market on Sunday morning just one block down the street.

“Disappointed” We had tickets to a show and decided to stay in town rather than drive home. We had stayed at the Hotel Icon before and loved it but wanted to try a different downtown hotel. There was no bell service at check-in we unloaded our own bags since there is no driveway and we were blocking traffic while waiting. After check in a bellhop appeared with a cart for our one bag. The elevators are small so we had to wait 3 times because there wasn't enough room for the bellhop, the cart, and us - if anyone else needed a ride up. The room was small. There were no drawers to unload our clothes into. The closet was SO small that we couldn't unload our hanging clothes and hang the hanging bag - and this was for a one night stay. The furniture was threadbare, not charming antiques but garage sale castoffs. The bathroom was stark and uncomfortable I didn't like being in it. It didn't look or feel clean. I sent in the comment card but with mildly stated details of my disappointment and no one has ever called to discuss. Also, small uncomfortable bed. No coffee maker in room or morning coffee in lobby. There wasn't a trashcan in the room or bathroom - I had to call to get one brought up and she told me she had to get it from another room (uh- I didn't want to know that!) We paid more to stay here than at the Hotel Icon - please no one else make the same mistake.

“Nice Convenient Location within walking distance and close subway stop” We stayed here three nights in late July with our three kids. We booked via priceline and were pleasantly surprized. Although the rooms were a bit cramped (all hotel rooms in NYC are smallish), the location and service of the staff made up for the lack of space. This hotel is within walking distance of all the city's major attractions. There are several subway stops close by which made traveling south to Battery Park ,or North to the Natural History Museum very convenient. Tony who works the front door was very friendly and willing to assist with directions whenever we needed them. Mary the conceirge made great restaurant recommendations!

“Good hotel, great location!” Stayed here with my spouse and another couple for a football game. We had a 2 bedroom suite. It was perfect for us. There is a a grocery store quite close. The place was clean and comfortable. The bed was also comfortable. Staff friendly and accomodating. The price great for a suite in downtownish Seattle. The only thing that was strange was no A/C in main living room. In the bedrooms only and it got a little warm. The bedroom A/C was loud but drown out other noise.

“90% EXCELLENT - 10% NOT GOOD” I arrived on May 12, just before 3:00 pm and was warmly greeted by the door gentleman and checked in with Kyria, who was professional, friendly and helpful at the front desk. I was staying from May 12 until May 16, 2010. She went one step further in service when she asked Martin to bring my suitcase up with me up to my room (#601). SInce this was my first visit to this hotel, he showed me some of the features (clock, phone, television, mini fridge, lighting, etc.) of this room. The room was beautifully appointed with a special robe, soft, white towels, bath products from England, LG Flat Screen television, which was easy to operate, Keurig coffee maker, etc. My room was super quiet and faced an office building, which was nice, no street noise or sirens were heard. This hotel was in a great location, close to restaurants and stores. Leonard, from Security always had a kind and welcoming word each time we passed in the lobby. There were two computer systems and a printer which were nicely placed in a side area near the front desk. So, I found 90% of this hotel, excellent. As I am writing this review, I trying to focus mostly on the Excellent qualities of this hotel. The 10% Not Good was Housekeeping area but more directly to the turn down service, which was not only non existent but the woman was rude to me. In a nutshell, the timeline goes like this: May 12th, no turn down service, May 13th, no turn down service, May 14th, at 7:30 p.m., a knock at the door where this woman (I did not catch her name) asked me if I wanted any extra towels. I mentioned that I was okay with the towels and she left. My last night, May 15th, I heard her go into the next room, knocked on the door and called out for her and she stepped out so I could ask her if there was any turndown service for the guests that I did not get that service provided. She basically said "ok", over and over again. I thought there may be a language barrier here. She told me that she had asked me the night before if I needed towels, She actually explained to me the turndown service and was not friendly at all about it. Little did I know as i guest that if I refused more towels that meant no turndown either for me. At this point, I did not want her in my room and put a Do Not Disturb sign on my door knob and went out for a walk - it upset me to be spoken like that. In closing, Lynda, who is super professional and kind, helped check me out and had been helpful earlier in the stay when Housekeeping had the wrong check out date for me. In all honestly, Sandra of Housekeeping was very efficient and friendly. Each day I left a tip to show my gratitude for her cleaning my room. As I was brought out to the curb, one of the good points of this hotel is Eddie, who hailed a cab for me and loaded my suitcase in the trunk, thanked me for my stay and said that the staff would all be here when I returned on my next visit to NYC. That is Customer Service!

“Good location, small rooms” My husband and I stayed here for a little weekend getaway. It's a beautiful hotel with lavish decor, however I found the rooms to be a bit on the small side. Our king room was basically just big enough for the bed and to walk around it. The bathroom however was huge with lots of room on the counter. Nice hotel with lots of character, but I would probably opt for a more practical hotel next time. Definitely too expensive for the size of room you get.

“Good hotel then rates went up” I had stayed at the hotel about 5 or 6 times in the past 10 years and have to say for a historical hotel I was quite satisfied, the hotel wasnt perfect, there were some quirks (things that didnt work) The hotel though all of a sudden increased rates drastically (by booking through the hotel) and this was just to much to pay for the hotel, and so my family figured that since there are so many good Boston hotels we found hotels for the same price in the heart of the city. The location is great for this hotel (There is a Radisson around the corner that is much cheaper also)

“Adequate” The HGI is located in the Baymeadows/South Side area of Jacksonville right off South Side and in walking distance of a large movie theatre and various restaurants. Many more restaurants and a grocery store are within a five minute drive. Typical HGI lobby, wide open, lots of tables and chairs as well a decent sized breakfast area. Check in was fast, friendly and efficient and room requirements were met. The room features a mini-microwave, fridge and coffeemaker, which is covenant for longer stays. There is a nice table and ergonomic chair for getting work done and a wired/wireless connection available. The closet had ample hangers and a clean iron and ironing board. The bed was not very comfortable at all. The middle sloped down a bit, was kind of lumpy, and I didn't sleep well. The linens were clean, however was interesting since they were using the Hampton Inn duvet. TV was older and so-so, channels were fine. No CC unless you used the mute button. Had a very nice view of a creek/lake behind the hotel and didn't hear really any outside noise. Inside noise was minor, little bit of TV, but wasn't too bad. I didn't care much for the bathroom, as the shower curtain smelled mildewy, which stunk up the room if you didn't keep the bathroom door closed and the grout wasn't super-clean. The sink had a crack in it and the fixtures felt kind of grimy, just wasn't the picture of clean. They give you nice amenities, shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash and lotion, and are a decent size. The hotel has a nice exercise room (two treadmills, bike and a weight machine) and an outdoor pool. Business center has one computer with a printer. I didn't eat meals there, so can't rate those, however there is an excellent Sushi restaurant called Sushi Crazy that is across South Side to the right of the hotel. St. John's Town Center is within a five minute drive and has some excellent dining/shopping options (and growing!). When in Jacksonville I usually stay at the Radisson or Hampton Inn. With my company rate, I didn't feel like this hotel was really worth the money paid and will try somewhere else next time. If you aren't picky, is more than adequate. It still is a three, average. Maybe with some renovations to the bathroom and beds, would be a better stay.

“Excellent service, OK location” stayed here on recommendation of client I was meeting with. The hotel is old, but well maintained. The service was excellent from the friendly front desk staff, to the very helpful valets and parking attendants. As other travelers have pointed out, the hotel is not on the Riverwalk as you imagine the Riverwalk. I didn't really have much free time this trip anyway, but next time would probably stay at one of the hotels on the main part, as I have in the past. This one is away from everything, so we ended up eating in the hotel restaurant, as opposed to getting outside and exploring as we had planned to do. There is a self parking garage across the street from the hotel, which is about $10 cheaper per day than valet service. The valets were very kind to let us park for 10-15 minutes while running up to room, which was much appreciated.

“Palomar Service Cannot Be Beat” I stayed at The Palomar for my wedding weekend and also booked my wedding guest block there. Every single employee I interacted with along the process was helpful and friendly. The meeting coordinator Kristen Sudela answered my multiple emails about wedding guest blocks and helped me coordinate the logistics for out of town guest bags (and even out of town doggie gift bags). The Palomar even stepped up to ask about the itinerary for my guests so the concierge would be in the loop about the wedding shuttle bus, etc. I felt that The Palomar went above and beyond their duties as a hotel to make me feel completely at ease about my guests staying there. There were 4 other wedding blocks staying at The Palomar that weekend but you certainly couldn't tell any signs of chaos! We stayed in the Presidential Suite for the weekend, which is a great treat with the huge living/dining area and 3 separate bathrooms. We even received a bottle of champagne and fresh strawberries upon returning to the hotel room after our wedding reception, great ;) We heard nothing but positive comments about The Palomar from our guests, who took advantage of everything from the evening wine reception, to the complimentary Lexus SUV transportation, to the pet friendly policies (we had several guests bring their dogs). I am so glad we chose The Palomar for this occasion. I knew from the get go that this would be one wedding vendor I didn't have to worry about at all, and I was right.

“The Westin is a way better choice!” I stayed here for 3 days as part of a business trip. I had stayed at the Westin for 2 days prior to checking in to this one. The moment I checked in, I knew I made a mistake by switching hotels. The front desk staff was unfriendly and although the hotel seemed very quiet, I did not get a room upgrade despite my platinum membership. The room was ok but not as good as the one I had at the Westin. This hotel is not horrible but if I had a choice, I would definitely stay at the Westin for sure!

“great location” I have stayed at the Georgetown Inn on previous occasions and I have not been disappointed. The location is great, right in the heart of Georgetown. The staff is very welcoming and professional, from the front desk to the bellman to the valet. The rooms are clean and comfortable. After a busy day of sight-seeing it is great to be able to walk out the front door and be in the middle of many great restaurants, shops, bars, all in an area that is safe and vibrant.

“Every Room is Pet Friendly--Really?!” Beautiful historic hotel, fantastic staff but every room is pet friendly! We spent three nights here on business. Every room is pet friendly--not only pet friendly, but pet friendly up to 75 lbs pet friendly! If you have allergies, think twice about this hotel. Our first room was a mini-suite that wasn't remodeled and obviously housed many pets as evidenced by my allergy to pet dander. We moved to a beautifully remodeled standard room on a lower floor which was much better. The only reason I was able to stay the night in this room was because it was remodeled only two months prior and obviously didn't have very many pets spending the night in it. Due to the fact that the hotel is so large, I'm not sure why the hotel doesn't designate pet floors instead of allowing pets in every room. I'm not anti-pet, just very allergic to them. The hotel staff was very accommodating to relocate us to a newer room. The hotel gym was amazing! Probably the nicest hotel gym I've ever had the pleasure of using.

“Is this "THE PLAZA"??” The lobbies and ground floor areas are amazing, just like you would hope. We had reservations for 2 rooms and they kept assigning us to used/dirty rooms. Finally, after speaking with the MOD we were assigned to rooms where housekeeping had cleaned. Ownership at this hotel has changed over the years, and sadly is reflected in the rooms and service

“Nice Hotel in SOMA” Rooms were comfortable. Walking distance to the Moscone Center and shopping. Close to public transportation. Only negative was that there was no wifi in the rooms. Would have been nice to have that.

“Loved the Updates” It has been a couple of years since I stayed here, and got it for a night last weekend on Hotwire. I paid only $100 and stayed a Saturday night. I was very impressed with the redecorating done to the hotel. The lobby has always been great, but the rooms were a little shabby in the past. Not any more, as the hotel has been redecorated in the last few years. The location is still amazing, and with the Berghoff open again, there is a great restaurant within walking distance.

“Still love this wonderful hotel” I have stayed at this wonderful hotel last year . Upon arrival I was greeted with a friendly doorman and receptionist. I stayed in an executive room which was very nice. The lounge was good with a very friendly lady on at breakfast time. I needed an American sim card for my phone so I asked the lady on at the Concierge table where I could get one. I walked about 5 mins and due to the hot weather went back to her and asked how I could get one without having to walk in the boiling hot weather she said she would go and get it for me. What great service. I highly recommend this friendly nice hotel.

“Nice views and location” First, this isn't a hotel in the heart of tourists. It is located across for the WTC and near Wall Street. Busy yes. Times Square no. That being said, it is by plenty of subway stops so it is easy to get in and out. The hotel is a tall (55 floors) and skinny hotel. It feels modern and the rooms are nice. I had a small corner suite but the room felt large because of the large windows. The bathroom was nice size with plenty of room. Downsides: the hotel is in the process of upgrading the Internet so not all of the floors have Internet. Also, the construction at WTC does create some noise. I was on the 32nd floor and didn't hear enough to be bothered. However, I would imagine a lower floor might get some extra noise. If you are looking for a hotel on this side of NYC it is worth a look. The views are great and it is a modern hotel.

“Nice but...” As you would expect, the Omni is a beautiful hotel, both in the public spaces and the guest rooms. All the staff were great. Very friendly and helpful. I stayed in a king room, which was nice but the bathroom was TINY. The pedestal sink had been cracked, making it unattractive for a hotel of this quality. The shower head wasn't fully attached to the wall and didn't have a lot of water pressure. There was a lot of noise in the hallway at night and in the early morning. There are many nice restaurants within walking distance.

“Better than expected” After reading the reviews, I was notably wary as a female business guest travelling alone. However, I felt safe at the hotel and the front desk staff was very courteous. I stayed here as part of the American Heart Association convention, so there were plenty of travellers here. Maybe that was the difference. The room was very spacious and clean. The free internet service worked without a problem. The room smelled fresh, the fridge worked great, and I didn't have a problem with the TV reception at all. The continental breakfast was good with a wide selection of food, about $8, and $2 extra for the hot items. The one reviewer was right -- there really are no close restaurants within walking distance and it is a little confusing getting on and off the highway. If I'm in Dallas again for a convention, I would definitely consider staying here again.

“Just OK...” Great location and hotel seems like it would be great with room rize and hotel set up. Not into the atrium thing with hallways open to lobby. Room was a bit noisy. Can hear people watching TV. If you aren't a light sleeper this hotel is ok but city has much better

“Wonderful Stay At The Fairmont” Recently stayed in a room with a bay view in The Fairmont Tower. Loved it. Amazing view. Very good service. The main bar/restaurant is quite nice. Did not have the food but did have drinks there. Great setting. The food at the restaurant in the lower level is not very good so stay away. The fitness facilities at nicer hotels always amaze me. I find them inadequate. This was no exception. They have an arrangement with a local gym that is housed in the lower level. Not very impressive at all but I don't expect much from hotel gyms. Overall a wonderful stay in a great setting!

“Great Value(Expedia)Large and Nice Room- needs some tlc” The hotel is not bad, the rooms are abnormally large and the staff friendly..Just at closer look the rooms need a little upkeep, nothing major. Location is out of the way a bit which is fine for me. Very small tv in bedroom- had to change rooms as the initial room had a tv in living room but not bedroom...need tv to sleep for me, especially when traveling.

“Good Hotel, & Getting Better” This hotel is in a great location, but needs a little attention. There are updates and repairs that need attention, and the parking is almost non-existent, but the staff is friendly and helpful.

“Wasn't what I expected!!!” At first the room was small and the bed sheets were totally covered eith stains and service was terrible and the staff at check in were so slow and there was one person in front of me and it took a hour to get checked in and at first they gave us the wrong room and we didn't ask for that room but other than that stuff sandiego was awsome!!!!

“Nice place on Michigan Avenue” The Westin is a nice hotel a block away from the John Hancock building on North Michigan Avenue. It's convenient to the shopping on the Magnificent Mile, and not horrendously far from the Red Line stop on the El. It's about a 10-15 minute walk to the Chicago River. We stayed for four nights in May. Got a south-facing room. Not much of a view from our 25th-floor room--the side of the Hancock building was it. The ice-machine room on the north side of the hall had a great view of a beach and Lake Michigan--we'll ask for a north-side room the next time. The bed was Heavenly, and the bathroom was very nice. Not as much water pressure in the shower as I like, but adequate. There's free Wi-Fi in the lobby, but there's a charge for Internet access in the rooms. A free USA Today was waiting outside our door each weekday morning. My only two complaints are: (1) The seat of the desk chair was flimsy--collapsed in when you sat down on it, providing no support. A new chair, or at least new padding, would be great. (2) There are three drawers for clothes in the TV unit. This might not be enough for more than one or two people. The closet near the door was very narrow, but it proved adequate for our needs. We saw the Florida Marlins checking out of the hotel the same day we did. If the Westin is good enough for an MLB team to stay at, it's probably good enough for common rabble like us.

“Everything you need” The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance of Times Square and all the great theaters,. We arrived early so our room was not available but not to worry, had a complimentary breakfast with coffee to go. Off to Rockefeller Christmas Show while the hotel stored our bags. Our room was ready once we got back. Two queen comfy beds and a flat screen tv with a large desk. Free internet is a plus. Bathroom is big enough and clean. The price was expensive but it was Dec 28th so every hotel was charging more. Had dinner at John's Pizzeria (8thAve & 44th st) which serves the most delicious food and was worth the 20 min wait for a table.

“Decent hotel in great location” This was our second stay at this hotel. Both times we came for a Conference. Our room, 1411, was a clean, comfortable room with a small sofa, small cocktail table, and large desk. Although it faced another building, off to the left was a limited view of the harbor. The room itself had excellent lighting, but the bathroom (toilet & tub area) was very dim. The sink and closet was in an open area off the foyer with no door for privacy. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel is located in the wonderful Harbor East area, surrounded by good restaurants and within a short walking distance to Fell’s Point, which has even more restaurants. It is a very easy walking distance to the Inner Harbor and a manageable walking distance to the Convention Center for those with comfortable shoes and who love to walk. We did not take breakfast in the hotel & therefore cannot comment on it. I recommend this hotel for its proximity to excellent restaurants, the Inner Harbor & the Convention Center.

“Excellent Staff, Great Value!” I stayed at this hotel one night on February 16 and it was fantastic! I had a studio room and it was very spacious with a fully stocked kitchen and a large living area with bathroom. I have stayed at the Residence Inn before and I find all their rooms to be spacious, clean and comfortable. Scott, at the front desk was especially helpful and recommended many restaurants where I could order food since I got into Charlotte very late at night and was starving. I would definitely stay at this location again, and I was especially pleased at the low rate of $89/night. Perfect room, great value, helpful staff--I couldn't have asked for a better stay!
“やはり・・・狭い。” 狭いのは承知してましたが、一人で外出ばかりしいたので(寝るだけであれば)問題はなく、1階のカフェ(24h free space)は開放的でよかったです。

“nice character great staff” my best travels are where there is some character and charm but it is not over the top pretentious and expensive. This is a very nice boutique hotel with great staff from the doorman to the housekeeping . It may be a bit worn in places per other reviewers but I did not notice that and not everything has to be perfectly updated to feel clean and comfortable from my standard. I find Washington DC to be a daunting concrete city and while interesting and exciting I like coming back to a place that is personal and welcoming . It has no chain hotel feel and even with the better chains sometimes that just feels like same old same old . I would return .

“About what one expects from a Holiday Inn” Rooms have been freshly remodeled, and are quite nice and well appointed. Hotel is located on I35, and there is easy access. A few problems, though. The first room to which I was assigned on the 14th floor had a strong chemical odor. I noticed it upon leaving the elevator on the 14 floor, and the strong smell was noticable in the room. I called the front desk, and asked for another room. The desk representative was very pleasant, apologetic, and prompt about my reassignment. I was relocated to a room on the 11th floor in the other tower, and found there was no air conditioning in the hallways on floor 11! My room was large and well appointed, with a great view of a nearby lake. The panel covering the room air conditioning unit was not properly attached, and loose. Breakfast not included even for Plat level guests. Restaurant looks quite nice, although I did not use it. Free parking (with a garage!) free internet, shuttle to airport.

“Fan of the Club Quarters” -Very efficient do yourself check in service. I liked this... no need to sign or show ID. -Rooms are small but but very comfortable. There is a help yourself closet on everyfloor so you can get more pillows, blankets, ironing board, etc. I really apprciated this... no calling downstairs (or tipping!) -There is also a help yourself water bottle area. love it-- -There is water and coffee set out in the lobby -They had 35% off the parking structure across the street (where you will park if you arrive with a car) -Location was pretty good..close to ritten house square. But I found that Philadelphia was a very walkable city... just about anywhere would be a "good location". Over all I would recommend this hotel to travelers, couples or singles. I would not recommend to famiies wanting extra space and ammenities.

“Ok for the price.” This Microtel is in a good safe location that is nearby virtually anything that one would need. The exterior of the property is well maintained. Inside the hotel is average for it's class. It is in need of some work inside as it is aging but by no means is a bad hotel. Bed is comfortable. Room is tiny. Great feature is the seating area in the window where you can sit or partially lie down in the window. The windows open which is great to me as it is great to get fresh air into any hotel room. Housekeeping was a little below standard. The night front desk lady was very good. I recommend this hotel. Not spectacular, could use some minor work but not bad by any means

“Okay, but Issues!” Myself and 4 other friends stayed at the Mariott for Labor Day weekend. This was our 2nd time staying here, and the location of the hotel is perfect...it's close to everything on Michigan Ave and the North Ave beach down the street. The issues, however, began with check-in. We were a party of 5 and we got a room with one bed! After calling and getting attitude from the operator, we got a different room w/ 2 full beds and rollaway. 2 Full beds are barely enough for 2 people to sleep on, but we dealt with it anyways figuring we're only sleeping there. Aside from check-in, everytime I would call guest svc's for something, it took them at least an hour and half to bring it up. I'd have to call twice for everything, like extra towels. Aside from these minor difficulties, the hotel's location is the best thing about it. The rooms are way small and are barely enough for 2 people, let alone 5.

“Worth the money.” First, let me say that when you're in NYC, perhaps more than any other city, you're paying for a place to sleep. There is just far too much to do to be worrying about all the little amenities. My main cares when in NYC are that I have a semi-quiet place to sleep, it's clean, and it's safe. If those are fulfilled, I"m happy. I'll save the fretting over marble countertops and deluxe lobbies to when I'm elsewhere. This hotels is basically "no frills" in that the rooms are pretty tiny, the TV is pretty small, and the view wasn't really great. Plus, the bathrooms are realllllly small. But, it was clean, the people were very friendly, the part of town was pretty nice and quiet, and the breakfast was good. All this for 130 bucks a night in Manhattan. How could I complain?

“Wonderful amenities and a great location” Stayed three nights at a grand total cost of $618 for two-persons with a king bed. Room included full bath, phone, TV with 39 cable channels, temperature control, and free wi-fi. Hotel has an exercise room, an outdoor pool (available Memorial Day to Labor Day), and a computer room with two free PC's with internet access and a printer. Hotel was clean, well-maintained, and surprisingly quiet for being next to a freeway. Staff was VERY friendly and willing to assist with our visit. Within the hotel building is a chain pizza place that featured a bar, a full hot breakfast buffet (not included in room price), a pizza and pasta lunch buffet on week-days, and dinners. A convenience store was five blocks away, and several restaurants were a little beyond that. I noted that onsite, outdoor parking would be $16 per day, and nearby covered parking is $9 per day. However, since a 72 hour pass for unlimited rides on the CTA is only $12 per person, it is clearly best to not use a car when visiting Chicago. Hotel is located just a couple blocks from both the Amtrak Station and the bus station. The neighborhood is sufficiently safe that even a late night arrival would not be a problem -- just be aware of exactly how to get to the hotel, as Chicago's grid system makes all streets look alike. The hotel is also just a block from the "Clinton" stop on the CTA Blue Subway Line, meaning you can go from O'Hare Airport direct to the hotel -- and Midway Airport would require one change of train. You can easily either walk or ride the subway to the Loop, and the McCormick Center is a couple miles away. For us, the location was perfect.

“Clean, comfortable, great location, but a bit smelly and noisy!” We arrived at the hotel mid afternoon and check in was quick and easy, staff were polite and friendly, as they were throughout the whole stay. Our room was small but big enough, there was plenty of storage room and a clean but small bathroom. The decor was clean and modern. The location was seen, walking distance to all of the main attractions and sights. The only issues we had were noise, smell and temperature. It can be noisy on a weekend as it is right above a bar. There was also an awful smell, I suspect it was sewage from the drains outside, this lasted for the whole of our stay but there were workers around who seemed to be trying to fix the problem. The room was also cold at night, our bed was right beneath two windows and it was really drafty. We also didn't receive room service once during our stay, this wasn't a problem as we just asked when we needed clean towels etc but I expect to receive room service at least once in a 7 night stay. Despite the little issues we really enjoyed our stay here, the great location, security, free Internet and tv were great and if we returned to Philadelphia we would be sure to stay again.

“Beautiful hotel but noisy!” This hotel is fairly new in San Diego and it's right in the action of the Gaslamp and across the street from the Convention Center. If you are planning to stay at the Omni b/c of business (ie. tradeshow at the Convention Center) ask to get a room on the bayside on a higher floor (above 15th floor). Due to the location of the hotel, one side faces the bay/convention center and the other side faces the Gaslamp/ballpark. Here are the issues with both: Facing the bayside - I've heard this is very quiet if you are on a high floor. If you are not on a high floor (below approx 15th floor) you end up getting major tooting from the trolly/train that passes right in front of the hotel. People staying in higher floors don't appear to hear it as much. Facing the Gaslamp - This faces right into the Hard Rock Hotel which has an awesome, very trendy, 4th floor bar/club. The catch - the bar is all OUTSIDE so if it's Friday or Saturday, you are sure to have the music so loud that your room in the Omni will start to rumble. Very fun when you are on business and trying to get some sleep at midnight. It's so loud that I don't think a high floor is going to help. Then the real fun starts when the bars let out at 2am and people are screaming outside.... Overall fantastic hotel, beautifully appointed beds and bathrooms. Very clean and modern with great amenities. The bar downstairs has a great happy hour menu with good drinks. If you are vacationing, this is a great hotel for you as it's close to the Gaslamp, Seaport Village, shopping, etc. If you are on business, I'd consider the Hilton or Marriot which is still very close to the convention center (the Hilton is actually slightly closer than the Omni, but not by much) and you will not have a room that faces the dreaded Hard Rock Hotel.

“thanks trip advisor friends for great rec of the doubletree” after research and reading here, we booked the doubletree for 6/19-24 . The location was great, almost no cab fares and got breakfast items at the food emporium a few blocks away, frig held doggie bags from dinner enjoyed next day,mcdonalds next door a nice stop for evening ice cream!tourist info next door was great with free internet, subway station also at the door/fyi: cabbies do not know anything without the EXACT address, did not know pier 83, even times square hotel/3 hour circle line boat tour highly rec first activity, great look at the city, helped us get around later, hairspray great show, ave q 2 but adults only/ try getting a letterman lottery ticket ,line up at 9: 30 and see if you can get a lottery seat, one day we were there they were looking for 600 guests,great rest:un,du, tio(1, 2 3 in French) a couple of blocks away, have fun!

“Best value in New York City” The hotel is VERY good and for its price ($250 after taxes in June) it is just great. The room is spacious and ideally clean, the bath is great. It is very close to the Times Square and all the theaters, but its location behind the Bus Terminal is not so nice - you can find a lot of creapy characters outdoor at night time.

“This is one of the finest hotels EVER!” I just can not say enough positive things about this hotel. Your stay will be worth every single penny. The service is impeccable (this is my favorite thing about the hotel), the rooms incredibly clean and comfortable and the location is PERFECT! We come to Dallas at least twice a year and I sometimes hesitate on if I want to spend that much money on a hotel but I have now decided this is my go-to hotel for Dallas. It really doesn't get any better than this. The only hotel experience that I have had that rivals this hotel was the Ritz Carlton in Grand Cayman - and they are a resort!! But the quality service is the exact same. I absolutely love this hotel!

“HAD A GREAT TIME, but had to fight for.” When I booked the hotel I requested an upgrade for a suite, but when I checked in this was not available, at least that was the information I got. I felt unwelcome and made a complaint to the reception manager asking to refund me and that way I could go to another hotel. In minutes, this manager resolved the situation and I was accommodated in a great suite. The hotel has a very special charm, but the executive lounge was very, very poor and crowded, the most crowded I had been at the Hilton Hotels and you also have to pay for alcoholic beverages. The hall of entrance is splendid and full of history and also there are many tourists 9non guests) taking pictures. The Hotel is downtown and from there you can go everywhere in Chicago. My time in Chicago, at the Palmer House (forgetting the check in stress) was amazing.

“Fine, but I don't get the hype” I stayed for three nights in July and was generally not impressed. Hotel security is non-existing; delivery guys come and go as they please, and as long as someone carried a pizza carton or a plastic bag with take-out chinese, no staff cared much about them. The reception is bureaucratic, and the porter by the door most often was more busy with his own business than greeting hotel guests, let alone opening doors, calling cabs or helping out. That being said, location is good as it is between Chinatown and Union Square. Wifi worked spotlessly. And the rooms were clean and nice. I'll probably stay somewhere else next time.

“A Great Find in a Fun Manhattan Neighborhood” Having stayed in mid-town seemingly every single team I had ever been to New York I wanted to try something different. Settled on the Four Points in Chelsea because I could use Starwood points to stay here for free. Boy was I glad I did. The location is fabulous, near lots of things but in a far less congested neighborhood than midtown. The room was actually bigger than those at the Sheraton in midtown and it was well appointed. The free water and wi-fi were a nice touch as well. The only complaint I have is that the hotel has only two elevators, which means you can have to wait a bit at times but this is a minor complaint. I can happily say that this hotel will be my new first choice when I return to NYC.

“Tiny or Cozy?” Everything is tiny. Tiny lobby, tiny rooms and even on a seemingly tiny street. Yet the decor and the staff manged to turn this all into a plus. Decor had a very hip feel to it yet was very comfortable and soothing. Staff was incredible and the complimentary wine hour and cont'l bkst added to the welcoming atmosphere. Really enjoyed the atmosphere in the Ruby Room and the menu and food was great. Even though it comes across as "light fare", the quality, service and portion size made us turn it into dinner. Only drawback would be some tourists may be put off by its unusual location. The neigborhood is a bit gritty but you're within walking distance to Fanueil Hall, Fleet Ctr events and the North end. Have also stayed at its sister Hotel - the Marlowe and found it equally as enjoyable.

“Double Tree/Hilton Hotel San Jose CA” Interesting property. Nice location, lobby area is welcoming and staff are wonderful - they make this hotel! This hotel is probably the oldest I have ever stayed in - the rooms are large but the wallpaper is peeling, the decor needs some major changes and the doors to the suite and bathroom need to be replaced - mine in Rm 704 had wood chipped off in places and a huge burn mark?? The staff from room service and front desk were very friendly and went above and beyond to help me with any questions I had.

“Loved the Affinia Chicago” This Affinia is in a prime location right off MIchigan Avenue. There are restaurants and cafes right near it so you don't have to cross the crowds on that busy shopping street unless you want to. The front desk were very welcoming and the room was great. I had a drink in the fancy bar/restaurant downstairs and really liked it. I have stayed in many hotels in Chicago and can recommend this one if you are looking to be near Michigan Avenue. The red line is a reasonable walk away and that will take you to the Loop or MiIlennium Park. Otherwise, you can walk to the river in about 10 minutes and get there on your own.

“Good Center City Choice, Needs Some Updating” The RI Center City is well located near the Convention Center, City Hall, and the Reading Terminal Market. Lots of Marriott choices nearby, with a nice Courtyard conversion next door and a full service Marriott a block away. This is a garden variety RI with a nice "Hearth Room" comprising an entire florr, but still crowded every day at breakfast, and not completely clean either. The food selection was very average and the cereals surprisingly stale, with the staff indifferent. We had a two bedroom suite which was nice sized and well laid out, but needs some serious updating from a 1980s look. The bar area is bizarre (enclosed in the Hearth Room -- Penn liquor license issue?) and not staffed when the sigh said it would be open. Nice guest laundry, exercise room, and small business center although the printer was broken. Overall the hotel wins on location, and just average on most other things.
“Old school hotel with interesting decor and good location” High marks for value but I was on a special biz rate.

“Excellent” This Hampton fits its surroundings, easily the nicest Hampton I've ever stayed in. Beautiful hotel, spacious rooms, close to everything in South Park. The only thing that wasn't an upgrade from the typical Hampton was the breakfast. Great choice for a night away from the kids.

“Another fabulous Kimpton” Our family of three stayed for three days during Spring break. I chose this hotel based on tripadvisor's rating and the guests' great reviews. It was everything we'd hoped for. Luxurious, elegant (without being stuffy) and it immediately felt like home. Terrific staff from the valet to the front desk to the bartender in the beautiful bar just to the side of the lobby. Can't wait to return. Thank you Hotel Palomar and thank you, once again, to tripadvisor, for making my travel decisions so easy!

“Rough start, but great overall experience.” I grew to adore the Mokara. When my flight was delayed, I called the front desk to reconfirm my room and was told I had no reservation for that evening. When I arrived, the front desk attendant eventually worked out the problem. We very much enjoyed the hotel- the carpet & room design are beautifully done, the layout and furniture are spacious and classic. Hallways and rooms are quiet and the bathroom was luxurious and deluxe. This is a four to five star hotel, hands down. The fresh organic apples, coffee, and fresh fruit juice in the lobby were greatly appreciated small touches, and the valet and desk staff are all top notch. I'll be back!

“Enjoyed our stay” We did not have any problem with the age or cleanliness of the room as some have reported. Ours was typical Embassy Suites in terms of layout. Service was reasonably friendly. The morning breakfast was excellent. The afternoon reception was beneath the standards of other Embassy hotels and did not fit with the price being paid. The hotel does not have its own pool or fitness center, you have privileges to use such facilities of a club located on the top floor. The staff there was unfriendly such that you felt hotel guests to them were more of a bother. The hotel is in a mall that has as its best feature direct access to the DC Metro Underground. This allows you to tour the city easily-best bet, the daily pass that allows unlimited riding. There is also a Cheesecake Factory in the mall but there are better and more reasonable alternatives nearby on the outside. Its also a short train ride to local restaurants in areas such as Dupont Circle. So you can stay here and avoid driving/parking to see the sights, though they do charge $15/day for garage parking. For these reasons, its very convenient, but it comes at a price. We enjoyed our stay, but if it weren't for the metro station it wouldn't be worth it.

“The reviews are true: a wonderful place to stay” I chose this hotel for my friends and I who were staying overnight in Seattle for an event. I wanted somewhere that had a good location (its right next to Westlake center, can't get a better location than that!) with good service. I found a package on the hotels website that included free parking (otherwise yes, it will cost you but its in downtown. Parking will cost you no matter what) and free breakfast for two in the morning. I wanted to check in early or at least park my car and check in later. The stuff was willing to help me in anyway and I was able to check-in early enough to drop of my luggage before heading to my event. I had a corner room on a high floor. The room was nice and clean. All of the staff that we encountered were friendly and very helpful. The breakfast the next morning was delicious and we did use the bar in the evening for a few drinks while planning dinner. I will stay here again when going to downtown. The service and location cant be beat. Check their websites for specials. The bed was a little hard but doable for an over-nighter. Wonderful stay!

“Ok, if you're in a bind” Paid in full for room and checked in after midnight with a front desk agent that said "I was just in the process of cancelling your reservation for good tonight". Too tired to argue I just took the room key and went to sleep. Housekeeping started knocking on doors around 7am and chattering loudly in the hall. Room was decent with an old tv and there was a big balcony. Morning breakfast was ok but uncomfortably packed with people. You can do much better in San Diego for the $$
“Exceptional Hotel” Location, service, wonderful room. No complaints at all regarding this hotel.

“Excellent Accommodations in an Excellent Location” We recently stayed at this hotel for a long weekend visit to NYC. The hotel has a great location with beautiful views of Central Park. Understated elegance and top-notch service access to concierge lounge was great with varied food and beverage presentations thoughout the day. Dinner at BLT Market was great; they sent our dessert up to our room for us. The room and bathroom were spacious and beutiful; the only fault we could find wiht the room was that the TV was too high which makes for akward viewing form the bed.

“Unique and Genuine Property in a Great Part of the City” This is my second trip to the Back Bay Hotel in approximately two years. This visit again was great, and even better than the first time around. We stayed for three nights over Labor Day Weekend. The hotel is located in the great Back Bay area of the city. You are so close to so many great restaurants, Boston Public Garden, the start of the Freedom Trail, Charles River, Beacon Hill and so much more. We arrived late on a Friday evening and were checked in by a friendly person at the front desk. The hotel is as I remember it; however, the front lobby is decorated beautifully and better than before. I got to admit though, it was disappointing to see the water wall at the entrance not working at all during our weekend. (Of course, that didn't sour my view of the hotel). We had a deluxe standard room on the 2nd level of the hotel. You do not stay at the Back Bay Hotel for the views, as most rooms face an internal roof or the street/alley as did ours. However, the room was beautifully decorated! It had subtle tones and the decor was casual-elegant. The amenities in the room were great. These included robes, slippers, Napresso machines, great LCD TV with a wide selection of channels, a super comfortable bed, refrigerator, plenty of outlets, a great working A/C Unit, complimentary bottled water and so much more. The bathroom was great with elegant lighting including under vanity lighting when you approached the bathroom, heated towel racks, great water pressure and more. We were also very pleased with the housekeeping and the nightly turndown service. The property has a really nice workout facility/room for a mid-sized property. There is a bar on property, which we did not utilize; however, we did have breakfast all three mornings in the Stanhope Grill, the on-site restaurant. The breakfast buffet was excellent and including yogurt, cereal, fruit, cold meats, pastries, scrambled eggs, eggs benedict, potatoes, bacon, sausage, pancakes. You could also order omelettes and waffles at no extra cost. The cost of the buffet also included juice and coffee/tea. Some people say it is expensive; however, I would say it is on par for a in-hotel restaurant in that area of the city. One final thought, for those who complain of noise. Boston is an urban area. You will have some noise. The noise was not bad and we were on the second floor. For those that complain of the noise, try a suburb. Seriously though, you will enjoy your stay at The Back Bay Hotel.

“Typical Hyatt...highly recomended!” Typical Hyatt! Great location with the Arena, convention center and food court nearby, right in the heart of downtown Columbus. Only complaints was a very slow elevator (I was on the 10th floor and sometimes it was faster to walk down to lobby rather than wait for elevator) and horribly stained chair inside the room. I wpuld recomend this hotel to others!

“Fab airport hotel” My husband loved this hotel and choose to stay here every time the day before his return to Sydney. The rooms are spacious and the restaurant faces the beautiful harbor. Service is always top notch. Rates are reasonable through Priceline.

“Nice stay, decent service, okay room” My wife, two year old son and I were concluding our road trip by staying 2 nights at the Downtown Marriott. Location off the freeway was easy to find. Valet parking and luggage handling was a joy after 6 hours of driving. Check in was smooth. Room, well, it was tiny. King bed with the wonderful revive sheets and comfy bed were a plus and the bathroom was a good size. No seperate dressing area as is the standard at other Marriotts we stayed at, but overall, was okay. Our room was above the trolley line on the 3rd floor and same as the swimming pool, hot tub, suana. This was fine for us, but for those who need quiet, this is the wrong floor and side of the hotel for you. We used the front desk for help once and they guided us to a resturant that recently closed, so that was dissappointing. Marriott still charges for Internet access which is dissapointing since it is free at Fairfields. Room service is expensive, but the breakfast buffet at $15 a person was a good value with fresh fruits, omlets, waffles, etc. Trolley line access to Beale St is great. Overall, a pleasent, expensive stay, that was decent, but for the money / value, could have been better.
“This place fit the bill.” For a last minute overnight inthe SD area...clean, well maintained rooms and got a deal on Priceline. Nice place.

“Check out the Library, You're Overdue” On the corner of Madison and 41st (entrance on 41st) is the LIbrary Hotel, a slim, handsome 14 story building with partial views of the NY Public Library a half block away on Fifth. Pretty from the outside, and a bustling Madison & Vine restaurant on the ground floor, the lobby was a stylish, high-ceilinged retreat from the hustle. The Library theme begins with a giant card catalogue behind the reception desk and a wall of borrowable books and DVD to the left. My check in staff was very friendly and took a few moments to explain the hotel's amenities, in particular, the 2nd floor lounge (more on that in a bit). The Library theme, which is never kitschy or overdone, continues to the rooms. Each floor is a "theme" based on the Dewey decimal system, and each room is an individual topic. I was on 3, Social Sciences, in the Economics room. My room was the basic one, and it was snug. Done in gold with dark brown wood furniture, it was well designed, maximized storage, and had a split bathroom with nice fixtures and decent shelf space. The two south-facing windows (overlooking the office bldg across 41st street) provided good light and the high ceiling gave the room a more spacious feel. Free water and a good turndown service with chocolates were added perks. But the edible perks did not stop with turndown chocolate. On the 2nd floor is a lounge open 24hrs a day. They put out an expanded array of continental breakfast items in the morning, and a cheese, crackers, fruit & wine reception in the evening. In between, coffee, tea, cookies and fruit were available. This was a lifesaver when you wanted a little snack or cup of espresso between outings. It's the kind of perk that is both practical, enjoyable and sets the hotel apart from the pack. All in all, I was very impressed with this hotel. It's location, facilities, and amenities make it a standout worthy of its high rankings here at Tripadvisor. It's not a luxury hotel in vibe or fittings, and yet was the true definition of luxury in practice.

“A very good experience” The room was very large and well maintained though sparsely furnished.. The staff were consistently friendly. The shower was fantastic. Everything worked as it should. We would definitely stay there again.

“Beware-no hot water-poor A/C-aging hotel” I had clients booked at this hotel. Upon arrival last night, the clerk had no reservation. They called me and I referenced the confirmation numbers to the call center. The call center indicated the HOTEL cancelled the reservations on April 29. No reason for the cancellation was stated. One client complained of poor A/C in his room and they both had no hot water this morning. The hotel did give them 10,000 bonus points for the inconvenience. I have conducted several events in this hotel in the years past and never had problems. I must agree with other reviews that the hotel is aging.

“Stay here - it's (almost) perfect” The location can't be beat, so can't staff attitude. We had a King Premier facing the inner pool courtyard. Definately ask for one of those as outside facing rooms must be terribly noisy and the lower room categories seem to be a mixed bag . That said, our Premier Room was just perfect: spacious, clean, comfortable, nicely furnished (great bed), free WiFi and morning newspaper. The only downpoints: front desk was very busy at check-in and had to answer several calls during the check-in process which made it pretty lengthy. Furthermore, my request for a non-connecting room (made when making reservations) could not be honoured (the hotel was fully booked) and given the famous paper thin U. S. doors, we were witnesses of some interesting things going on next door (luckily the people - they changed daily - were silent at night - don't they get that when they can hear US, we can hear THEM?) In general, the hotel is not for the extremely noise sensitive: even in our room facing the inner courtyard, there was a constant vent noise and you cound hear the toilet flushing from other rooms. But that said, if your a good sleeper, go there. It's one of the best bets around.

“Outstanding Hotel” Attended a meeting here and stayed for 4 nights. I had an amazing time. From check in to check out, I don't think I have ever stayed at a hotel where the service has been so on top of things. Meeting AV personnel were on top of everything and the meeting went off without a problem. Beautiful grounds to the point where I for got I was in DC. Located within walking distance of a large number of good restaurants. Metro is 4 blocks away. Great areas to walk, national cathedral, naval observatory, embassy or all close. The national zoo is maybe 10 blocks away. Great hotel, staff and location.

“Adequate, but a bit of a disappointment” After all the rave reviews of the Lenox, I was prepared to be delighted, but unfortunately it was just okay. The location is great, certainly, and the hotel looks good. The staff were friendly and pleasant, but there were no special touches beyond what you'd expect at any hotel. Our room was attractive, but really quite small, with a small double bed - we rather felt it was a room they reserved for Priceline customers - and we were both unimpressed. We had good quality sleep though, with comfortable bed, darkness, and quiet. As for the bathroom, it was tiny with a miniature shower cubicle (no bath). And in the morning of check out, the maid started loudly knocking on our door to clean our room at 9:45am! It was a shame as it was my partner's birthday and I thought this would be somewhere special. It wasn't. Don't pay over $200 for this one!

“Don't walk....run away from this hotel!!!!” At first glance from the outside, this hotel looked acceptable....although there was a lot of trash scattered in the parking lot. The gentleman that checked us in seemed like we were inconviencing him. The rooms were so-so. There was a lot of "riff-raff" hanging around the side doors of the building. When we went out a side door in the morning an individual let in a good 10 people ( young adults/teen).....not sure what that was about, but I'm sure a free breakfast was had by all. I did not feel safe in this hotel at all and would highly recommend staying somewhere else.....a few miles north would be a smart choice!!!

“Can people really be this nice?” I go to Philadelphia frequently as my son goes to school there. Usually stay at Four Seasons. Wanted to try Palomar because of all the good Trip Advisor reviews. As an aside, they are certainly not shy about advertising their Trip Advisor status. It is even on their mini bar key rings. I say good for them! My son and I were staying just one night for a good rest before a long (16 hour!) car drive home. Let me just say customer service and friendliness go a long way. From when we first pulled up looking like the Beverly Hillbillies in my son's rather beat up, dirty Honda stuffed to the gills with college paraphernalia and two cases of beer (hey, you can't get Yuengling where we live!), and were greeted warmly by the amazingly welcoming and wonderful bellman (so sorry, forgot your name, but know you are from Liberia) to the nice check in (noting that I am a Kimpton member and like a quiet room) to the room service delivery person, the valet the next morning... WOW. Can people really be this nice? The atmosphere is modern and kitschy. I love the elevators with the fake fireplace and moustachioed painting, as well as the distressed wooden floor. The room was small, and modern, and the bathroom was nice and large, with a nice pocket door. I particularly liked the note in the bathroom about being able to easily get things you forgot by just calling downstairs... nice! Beds and linens were very comfortable. Thanks for double sheeting the comforter, a must in my book. I also got a kick out of the leopard robes. Minor quibbles: yes, the room is small. I actually knocked my shin against one of the bedframes (that sticks out farther than the mattress) trying to get around. One problem that I should have solved myself: the room was warm when we checked in so we turned down the a.c. During the night it would cycle on and off every minute or so... not good for light sleepers. If I hadn't been so tired I would have called down for a fan (offered on the "stuff you may have forgotten" sheet in the bathroom) and the problem would have been solved. Note to self for next time. I also wish there were a fan in the bathroom. One other note: the room service breakfast menu door hanger said they started serving at 7 a.m. I was disappointed as we needed breakfast earlier. The next morning I looked at another breakfast menu on the desk, and it said they started serving at 6:30. I called as soon as I read this, but it was already 6:30 so breakfast came at 7. Would have liked it earlier. Also, is there someone out there who could design hotel doors that shut quietly and not bang? Someone should invent one and patent it! So, have they won me over from Four Seasons? If they stay a little less expensive than FS, definitely yes. Priced same as FS, Hmmmm...I do like friendly...

“Great Getaway!” Pros: Beautifully weird decor. Nicely spaced room. Delicious slice of chocolate cake since we were celebrating a birthday. The swimming pool area is gorgeous but I wish that the actual size of the deeper pool was bigger. Staff was professional and attentive. Complimentary wifi and water if you are an SPG member. Great location - a 3 minute walk to Beverly Center and Matsuhisa. Delicious drinks and tapas at The Bazaar by Jose Andres. Cons: The brown leather couch in the room was a stained. Housekeeping need to check on the lighting before we checked in because 2 of the light bulbs went out and we were going crazy trying to find the switch for it. SLS is a dog friendly hotel, and a few rooms across from us had a dog, and the dog was barking nonstop.

“Excellent location -- terrible front desk staff” The location is great -- next to the Hancock and Water Tower and all of the shopping goodness that the Mag Mile has to offer. The front desk staff is terrible. For the amount of money that the room costs and the amount the valet parking costs, you would think they would be better at being more friendly and helpful. Although the front desk staff service is appalling, the breakfast/evening meal ladies are great! They go out of your way to make you feel at home.

“Comfortable rooms and friendly staff” The room was what I expected from a Hampton Inn: comfortable bed and pillows, clean and basic. The front desk staff were extremely kind and friendly, and the location was convenient. The only problem I had was that the water in the shower was never very warm. It was always just lukewarm at the hottest. The hotel was under construction at the time, so perhaps it had something to do with that? None-the-less, if I am in the area again I would happily stay in this hotel.

“Small accomodations but overall nice” Awesome location for this modern, boutique hotel. Right across the street from Time Warner Center. The staff members at this hotel were fantastic - from the doormen, to the front desk - all seemed to work on the guest's behalf almost effortlessly. The room (superior queen) was fine for 2 adults but a bit small. The bathroom was modern and nice. We were on the 6th floor and our view was of the HVAC system - not surprising for NYC. The hotel was perfect for us. I would certainly stay here again and would highly recommend to my friends. I wouldn't recommend to someone expecting a large, full service (restaurants, gym, etc) hotel.

“Excellent location, nice staff, cool historic hotel” This beautiful historic, non-descript hotel is great if you need to be near Times Square or the NY Public Library but want to save a little money. I highly recommend getting the junior suite, however, because the standard rooms are very, very small. Great bar/restaurant on ground floor, cool libraries all over and a great, creepy feel in the hallways. Marble and wood everywhere. Downside: window-unit A/C, little view, very small rooms, no ice machine/iron (would bring up to room upon request), very small bathroom, no large mirror in bathroom (shaving mirror instead). Positives: Clean, minimal decoration, free internet, minifridge (stocked but some room for your own stuff), great room service menu, gym, Aveda toiletries. Good for business/travelling alone (unless you get a bigger room).

“Average at Best. Great Location. Too Noisy & Low Service.” I stayed here one evening, Saturday 8/20/11. I had read many reviews on here and was originally concerned about bedbugs, which I am happy to report I did not experience in my room. Pros: - Awesome location two blocks from the White House. Right near St. Regis and Hay Adams hotel. - Nice shower with good pressure and hot water (this place strikes you as old so I was happy the water worked). - AC worked well. Cons: - LACK OF SERVICE: Arrived at 2pm (check-in at 3pm) and after relinquishing my car for $42 for the valet to park it, the front desk person barely looked my name up before saying "the room type you reserved is not ready yet and should be available at around 3pm". There was no acknowledgement of Hilton Gold status and she was more eager to get onto the next guest then to assist me further. So I got to sit in the lobby for 45 minutes and watch several others get checked in (to queen size rooms, same as what I booked). I finally got up and asked them at 2:45pm to do something since I could not leave my work laptop with the concierge and I had to be somewhere at 3:30pm. The new desk agent then told me she would try...and eventually she came up with a room on the 5th floor (apparently I was blocked in a room on 6, never considered for an upgrade nor ever offered one). No mention of gold status or acknowledgement of Hhonors loyalty, and the attitude was more along the line of she was doing me a favor which I quickly got tired of. In the end she sent me to an average room, but I was happy to get in so I could get my laptop in the safe and get out to meet the others I was meeting up with. I was told I would have access to the Executive lounge for breakfast (which was true...she actually said I forgot to add it onto your key so I will add it). No mention of free internet either so I had to call down to figure that out and get some secret passcode to get logged in that supposedly was on my keypacket (it wasnt). - Very long hallways, room was very far in. Big place. - VERY NOISY. Other guests are right, the walls are thin and my room had connections on both sides so I could hear everything next door, and I heard lovely crowds screaming outside at 2am. Not a good night's sleep which annoyed me most the next morning. - PARKING: $42 per night. Ouch. Yes there are garages nearby cheaper, but many were closed on sundays (I was there on a Saturday night). So I chalked it up. Need to plan 20 mins in advance before you actually need your car so they can go fetch it. - Note I saw a prior review where manager said he would post on the website the hours for the Exec lounge. That hasn't happened yet. Although I went up there briefly Sat. night around 8pm and it was open with an attendant, and was a nice setup. I did not get to have breakfast there the next morning due to schedule. I was annoyed enough with the check-in experience and the noise to leave a message during my stay for GM Gary (I think that;s the guy who responds to these). Gary was probably off Saturday but he did call me on Tuesday. Overall - this place bills itself as a HILTON (not a Garden Inn, not a Hampton). I think the location and size causes the staff to get into "mass production" mode and treat guests without the level of service and appreciation I have experienced in almost all of the other Hilton's I have visited. I will not be returning to this hotel and would never recommend this for a business traveler due to the insane level of noise in the rooms (from hallway and adjoining rooms). Personally though, the lack of service is what makes me decide to never return for pleasure either. I'm rating it average but was highly disappointed.

“Very Pleased with this Hotel” We were a bit nervous that this hotel might be disappointing given it doesn't have the highest of T/A ratings. However, we were very pleasantly surprised. Our room was great - extremely comfortable and clean (I believe they're renovating so that should make the rooms even better). I didn't give 5 stars because the air conditioning was very loud, but that didn't really bother us and we slept soundly. All the staff were extremely helpful and welcoming and breakfast (which was included in our room rate) was really good. Lovely cookies and cool drinks in the afternoon and take away coffee in the morning - most welcome. We ate at the restaurant for dinner one night and that was good and we also enjoyed being able to buy ice cream from the pantry to tuck into while watching tv in our room after dinner. For us though, the real plus came from the location. I can't tell you how wonderful it was to step off the metro and into the hotel after exhausting days of walking around the sites of DC. When you can't walk another step, having the hotel so close to the metro is pure gold!!! I'd stay at this hotel anytime, just for that luxury!!! Highly recommend the Hilton Garden Inn Downtown.

“Decent staff, hotel itself left more to be desired” This was my third "Hilton" branded hotel in 3 days during a recent visit to the Los Angeles area, and this hotel definitely was my least favorite. I thought it was a 4* hotel, but I would rate it about a 2.5 or 3*. To begin with, there seemed to be some security issues inside the hotel. We encountered a strange interaction on the 17th floor between a man and a woman which concerned us. We also noticed a uniformed Hilton security guard standing near the front desk. The room was shabby, with outdated furnishings and a toilet that didn't work. Thank heavens we had access to the exec lounge as we used the toilet there rather than wait for ours to be repaired. An electric outlet we tried to use in our room also did not work. The TV was not flat screened - I can't even remember when I last stayed at ANY hotel that did not have a flat screen TV. Yes, I am aware that the hotel is renovating its rooms, but for me it was too late. The exec lounge was OK - nothing exciting about it and the food offerings were average at best. Now for the good points: The bed was comfy and the view of the airport was great. Would I stay here again??? Definitely not. I'm a Hilton Diamond member and stay at a lot of Hiltons and would not stay here again. At checkout, I was not asked about the stay and when I reported the toilet as not working I was simply told "oh, I'll make a not of that." No apology, etc. We couldn't wait to check out!!!

“Better than average W hotel with great restaurant and bar” I have stayed at a number of W hotels with widely variable experiences. The W Dallas is definitely on the better end of the spectrum. The hotel is relatively new, very clean and had well-furnished and designed rooms. There were plenty of outlets, a large flat-screen TV and internet that worked as promised. Room service was prompt and accurately delivered (note - why is it normally so difficult to get proper ice coffee in the South?). The bed is very comfortable and even though I was on a high floor (close to the top floor club) I had no problems with noise. The bathrooms are also well furnished. Most surprising for a W was that I experienced excellent service. Faxes and car valet were promptly delivered and wakeup calls/room service occurred when scheduled. Further, the receptionist offered an upgrade based on my Gold SPG status. The Craft restaurant downstairs was excellent and the club was busy (this on a Tuesday night). I would definitely stay here again.

“Very good NYC hotel” Pleasantly surprised by my Priceline win..got a spacious, very clean king room with a great bed. The location is great, but as others have noted, easy to miss, as it has a very small street entry that leads to elevators that wisk you up to the lobby. OK view on the 25th floor.. use the 41st Street entrance if you are driving in...valet will park your car, and it was ready when we needed it. all staff, very pleasant and helpful...Clean decent bath..perfect location for walking NYC. we will add this to our list of NYC faves.

“Wonderful Westin in a great location...will return” What a great hotel with a great view of the city. I have stayed here three times in the last year (a total of 15 days). The staff has always been very polite and the maid staff fantastic. The hotel itself is beautiful and in a very nice location in Seattle. There is a cafe down stairs that is quite reasonably priced for a Westin ($10.00 for an Omelet + toast or a Salmon Salad) and the work out room is decent, though not quite up to the Westin St Francis and West Kierland Resort and Spa. Seattle is a great walking city and this hotel is convenient to everything. Internet in your room is a little pricy....but it is very fast and better than the free connections I get a HI Express, BW, etc. Buy the muti-day packages if you will be there for 3 or more days. There is free Wi-Fi in the lobby, but it is quite slow...at least it was for me. Really considerate staff! Would definitely recommend this Hotel. Nice job Westin Seattle staff.

“Overpriced, stuffy, mediocre service and teeny, tiny rooms!” Based on the reco of a fellow Trip Advisor reviewer, I booked our room in the Towers section of the hotel. The first 2 nights we had a King bed on the 15th floor with access to the "lounge" (which, by the way, has very limited hours - and NO weekend hours at all! What is THAT about?!). This room was so small that my husband and I were literally tripping over each other. To open the closet, the dresser drawers had to be closed! We did call up for a refrigerator and they brought it relatively promptly, thought. On the third night we switched to a double-bedded room, also on the 15th floor- which was MUCH bigger. The parking is $44 a night. We parked across the street for 2 of 3 nights and paid $20 for 12 hours. The concierge only works until 7:30PM on a Saturday night - strange considering this is in the heart of Back Bay. And charging $11 for Internet is beyond ridiculous. Unlike most, we had no problem with the HVAC, but I'm not at all sure the Towers Level was worth it.

“The Conrad -- A perfect choice for so many reasons!” I'm a travel agent, and The Conrad is definitely a place I would recommend. I have been to NYC many times, but I had never stayed in lower Manhattan & near the Financial District. By staying here, I had a completely different and unique NY experience and I loved it. It was so close to Soho & Tribeca{some of my favorite areas} that I was sorry I had overlooked this area for so long. The views over the Hudson are spectacular and you will enjoy walking along the waterfront if you find the time. I must add that this would be a great choice for a romantic NYC getaway because of the waterfront location alone. This is an area that most people miss{including myself} because NYC has so much to see and its hard to see it all! This trip was a 'girl's weekend' and it was a perfect choice for many reasons. I had a free morning to explore the neighborhood and I saw a lot of young families walking and playing, some really nice restaurants, the very popular Shake Shack, a cute French bakery directly across from the Conrad{facing the Hudson} and I grabbed breakfast and a coffee about a block away at Whole Foods. The doorman ~ at the Conrad were kind and always eager to open a door, hail a cab, or just say hello. One gentleman rushed over to us offering 4 umbrella's for us to use on a rainy afternoon. The front desk staff were definitely not overly-friendly or helpful like the doorman or luggage handlers were, but, I never saw the front desk staff more than once, so they were easily forgotten. The rooms ~ are huge by NYC standards. There is a separate sitting room(lounge area), with a second TV and coffee table, a working desk, & two end tables and still room to walk around. This is a great place{room} to store extra luggage{as we did} too. And this extra room really made my stay in NY extra special. I never felt claustrophobic or felt like bolting out of the room for air or light, like you usually do in NYC hotel rooms. At the Conrad we found ourselves lounging in our extra sitting room and talking before we headed out! The sitting area has a sliding door which closes the room off from the bedroom and bathroom. This is especially great for families. I was not traveling with my children on this trip, but, the separate door for napping or sleeping makes this an EXCELLENT choice for families with children too. And children love extra large rooms like this. The shower and bathroom layout is a little odd because the shower is located next to the bedroom and you must walk out of the bathroom and then through a small hallway to enter the shower. It definitely becomes a privacy issue{cover-up with a towel :) }, but because you have the separated sitting area, it is fine. And the Conrad NY has a shower head that you will love and the softest most plush bathrobes to go with it. Trust me, you will forget the odd layout of bathroom + shower. ;) The hotel lobby ~ is over-the-top large, very modern and very white, but the rooms and staff were warm and inviting and that is what I liked. Hilton had remodeled this building and I think they did a great job with the foundation they had to work with. I must also add the most important thing ~ This hotel is spotless. From rooms to floors, elevators and escalators ~ we did not see a single piece of anything out of place or not cleaned. Thank you Conrad for a fabulous experience! See you soon!

“March 2004 stay @ Courtyard Midtown East” Just back from New York...thanks to all who take the time to write reviews. They are always informative and helpful when trying to choose a hotel. I agree with all the past writings and I too would like to add that the staff at this hotel is outstanding. They went out of their way to be helpful. We arrived early and (10:00AM) were given a room right away. We thought we would just check luggage and come back later. Instead we checked into our room, unpacked and had the rest of the day.We had breakfast at the hotel each morning and the staff each morning, made it a pleasure to be there. Buffet is $14.95 but you can also order off the menu. The room was very spacious and a comfy bed, room decor is not fancy more"business" like. Clean and everything needed for your stay. We forgot and left a privacy sign on the door one day so housekeeping never made it in.
