They called while we were out and that evening brought clean towels, emptied the garbage and made sure we had what we needed. The staff really makes this courtyard. Location was great for us because we went downtown and uptown, so to be in the middle worked. We used the bus and walking distance to a lot of attractions. Great stay and would definitely return. Enjoy NY we did!

“Another fantastic Monaco. Ten thumbs up!” I grew up in Philly and have about five family overnights per year there as many of my relatives remain there. I have stayed at all the major hotels in Philly, previously settling on the Sofitel before moving on to the Palomar as our goto hotel. Kimpton is my favorite hotel operator by a mile, and I always try to stay in Monacos and Palomars when I travel for business. So you can imagine how pleased I was to find out that a Monaco was opening in Philly. I immediately snagged reservations there over Thanksgiving and Xmas. For Thanksgiving we secured corner suite for our family of four and a basic King room for my mother-in-law. The hotel was new, and the restaurant newer, when we stayed over Thanksgiving. My expectations were high, and they were exceeded. The Philly Monaco is now my favorite Monaco (Baltimore, of all places, and Portland are now runners up). It is also my favorite hotel. Period. Design: Like other Monaco's I've stayed in, the building is landmark-esque and has high ceilings. As per the Monaco brand I guess you can call it maximalism - flamboyant yet classy, modern yet warm. The pictures capture the gestalt of the design but not the quality and distinctiveness of every piece of furniture. The lobby is wonderful and very chill. It’s a good place to read the paper, get some free morning coffee, or meet up with others before going out. Rooms: Wow. Even my hard-to-please, design-obsessed mother in law was blown away. Our suite had one nice touch after another, so much so that it’s hard to pick favorites. The sectional white leather couch, half of which opened up into a sofabed, and the adjacent comfy white leather chair, was mine. The bathroom with soaking tub my wife’s favorite. The location is ideal even if you’re not a sightseer. The area west of Broad Street (which is about seven blocks up) has better shopping but is more 'generic city,' while the Society Hill area in which this hotel is located is distinctively colonial, charming, and rich with history. We managed to spend some in-between time throwing a football right in front of the hotel, in the expansive independence park, with the liberty bell on one side and independence hall on the other. View: We had a direct view of Independence Park, with a view of Independence Hall (where it all began) if I were to sit in the comfy white leather chair in one corner of the room. I think that some reviewers who complained thought that they’d be gazing directly on Independence Hall. Service: Check-in was very smooth. That evening the ‘turndown specialist’ came up within minutes of our requesting to have our sofabed made up. She couldn’t have been more personable, professional, and efficient.. The real test came at checkout. The hotel was very crowded (Black Friday), we had lots of baggage to load into two cars, and we had to transfer a large rug between the cars before departing (long story). They handled it all perfectly, and with a smile. Amenities: the fitness room is brand spanking new with good equipment, TVs, and peaceful view with the occasional passing horse drawn carriage. We did have an unfortunate experience with room service , and service at the restaurant, but I’m chalking that up to the newness of the place (even relative to the hotel), but in the spirit of the holidays I will give them a chance to redeem themselves over Xmas, after which I’ll submit a follow-up review. In sum, the Monaco has the coolness of the coolest design hotels without the pretentious and indifferent staff that sometimes comes with the territory. It adds to that the grandeur and elegance of a luxury hotel, but without the stuffiness. Our family can’t wait to return over Christmas.

“Beautiful view, perfect for business” I stayed here when working next door at the AON center. Perfect location for work and walking distance to many Chicago attractions and restaurants. The room was beautiful, clean and the perfect size. The wine and cheese in the front lobby were delicious. The staff let me check in at 7 am which was very much appreciated after an early morning traveling! Beautiful hotel, I will definitely stay again when in town for business.

“It was OK” Stayed at the Courtyard from 5/9-5/10. I guess I wound up on the smoking floor even though I'm a non-smoker because I wanted to check in early (12 PM), but truth be told, the check in clerk never asked me if I wanted smoking or non. The room stank like smoke, the toilet wouldn't flush properly until the 3rd try, and the a/c is pretty loud. Also, the pillows were "mushy." That sounds picky, but think of a pillow that's overly soft and then mushes down so much that it's really thin and hard. The hotel was about what you'd expect for a business traveler's hotel, but it just didn't have any charm. I found it somewhat depressing, actually.

“What a great hotel and price” I stayed one night at Days Inn for a conference at the convention center. I am a little skeptical about Days Inn due to previous experiences. However this one was just as good as any Hilton hotel. Checkin was friendly and quick, room was clean and nice fitness center. I ate breakfast in the hotel and it was very good also. Would definitely return and recommend.

“A local favorite” I'm a bit reluctant to write this review, as I don't want everyone to find out about my favorite SF hotel for business trips. But it's a big placel, I suppose there's room for everyone. This Westin is fantastic: staff is great, rooms are lovely (recently redone, I believe), the SPG rooms in particular have stunning floor to ceiling views of the bay, food is good, prices are good...and the location is perfect for my purposes. Close to my office, and if you're in town for something at Moscone, you can SEE it. Plus, you're also close to Market Street and Union Square for all your shopping needs. I am a regular. At this price point, there is no cleaner hotel, and that means a lot to me. A couple of (small) cons: they do charge for internet access. Also, room service ends at 10 PM, though there's plenty in the neighborhood if you get home late. All in all, this is a gem of a hotel in this area. I'll definitely be back!

“Photos don't do this hotel justice. Great hotel staffed by great people.” I felt like a VIP from the moment my cab dropped me off. Everyone here has passed customer service school with flying colors. My room was meticulously detailed and gave me the feeling I was the first person sleeping in it. I had a great view of the Hollywood sign from the patio. Would I stay here again? The question should be, "Would I stay anywhere else if I return to LA?" My answer to the latter question would be - wouldn't even consider another hotel. About me: I stay in 8-10 hotels of varying quality per year for combined leisure and business pursuits. This hotel is the finest I've stayed at in the US.

“very good location!” this hotel is located in a good area and it is very close to downtown. There was a good price deal and parking is free so it was excellent for us. The hotel offers a pricey breakfast so we didnt eat there. overall it was a good stay and since there are so many places and bakeries in houston we didnt mind having our breakfast out of the hotel.

“good stay with the kids” overall a good hotel...good value and kid friendly. We stayed four nights with the kids and had a good time. Upgraded to the club level which gave us access to the lounge for breakfast. service was great. front desk was helpful and the wait staff attentive. only downside was the road noise from the freeway close by as you were trying to sleep.

“The perfect place to stay in the Upper East Side” I'm trying hard to find a flaw in the Affinia Gardens hotel and it is not easy. Everything was functional, staff was incredibly helpful, the room was huge.... I mean really giagantic with a kitchenette. The air conditioning was the quietest, best functioning unit I have ever experienced in a hotel room. Very small criticisms might include: an older tube type TV instead of a large flat screen as you might expect; the stairway from floor to floor was kind of unpleasant, but we only used it once. Also, I continue to be frustrated by the $15 per day charge for internet access. It seems to be typical of many hotels to extract this extra fee, and Affinia Gardens is no different, but it still bugs me. There is no contenetial breakfast, just continuously available tea in a small room off the lobby, but we were fine with that. I was perplexed about the "gardens". The name implies that there are gardens, but if there are, we never found them.

“Ok if you can get the $99 rate-ask for the coffee maker” Everything everyone else has said is true-this is a Holiday Inn trying to disguise itself as a W. The hotel is nicely located near Union Station, which is convenient for dining and the Metro. The rooms are kind of small, but the beds are very comfortable and the flat screen TV is nice. I do want to say that the hotel staff was very accommodating, and one of the biggest plusses. The hotel is clean, and the pool area is quite nice, one of the best things the hotel has going for it. However, on the negative side, there is no coffee maker and no refrigerater. I can do without the fridge, but not the coffee maker. I was there for a week and only found out by accident by talking to another guest five days into the stay that they had them, but you had to ask, and if they had one available, they'd provide it. This is nonsense. A four-star hotel should automatically provide a coffee maker, or they should provide all guests with a list of items you can request at check in if they want to play the asking game. I guess they want you to order the $8 coffee in the morning. All the food and drink is extremely expensive, don't eat there. A glass of wine at the pool was $15.00. And $40 to park overnight is insanity. When I arrived on Sunday, the trendy pool party was in full swing, and to be frank, the way the 20-something girls were dressed and parading around the lobby and outside the hotel, I originally mistook them for hookers. It was only when I found out it was a pool party that I understood why they were dressed like that. All in all, if you can get the $99 internet rate, and you don't bring a car or eat in the hotel, it is not a terrible place to stay if you spend most of the day outside the hotel. If they just worked on a couple of things, I could really recommend it.

“Always a delight” I've stayed here many times and honestly - this is well worth the money and a great delight every time. The location is midtown. While many people prefer other areas for better access to downtown, etc, I dont care. This hotel is worth it. And it's close to Central Park, etc. Great for me. Anyway, this hotel is simply comfortable and delivers great service every time. It's not showy or over the top, but clean, comfortable, and the employees are all courteous, solicitious, and happy to help. I was there this past weekend for a family reunion in New York. I was in a King room. First off, the bed is just exceedingly comfortable. I slept well both nights. Then the bathroom - I love how it's all marble. Just feels luxurious. The towels and the robes are all plush, the toiletries nice, and the water pressure just perfect. What I also like about the Omni chain is the loyalty program. Just for signing up you get a number of great perks, such as free wireless internet in your room, daily morning beverages delivered to your room, and certain late check out privileges. Those all come in very handy. Overall, I really like this hotel. It's comfortable, convenient, and my preferred choice for NYC.

“Westin for New Year's Eve” We stayed at the Westin New Year’s Eve as it was within walking distance to the Orpheum Theater where we were attending a concert. The hotel is new and is located within a building that is shared with corporate offices unassociated with the Westin. When we arrived it initially took a few moments to realize that the valet parking turn in was on the west side of the building and not at the south facing entrance. Once we found the turn-in the valet staff was very pleasant and helpful to instruct us how to reach the lobby. A note, the hotel is valet only, no self parking unless you park off-site. The check-in was smooth and the young brunette woman (wish I could remember her name) was most pleasant and helpful. She asked if we needed dinner arrangements and offered to assist with reservations or suggestions. Once she found that we were attending the concert she offered directions or any other additional information. The room was much nicer and larger than we had anticipated. The floor-to-ceiling windows were stunning and we enjoyed the view watching the sunset. The extended ceiling height also adds greatly to the room along with a well appointed bathroom and terrific shower. There was enough room for both of us to move around and get ready for the evening without a problem with an extremely comfortable bed, additional seating area and ample work desk. A quick call to guest services and we received additional pillows within minutes. We did not eat at the hotel restaurant however we did order room service for breakfast which was tasty and delivered promptly and professionally. All of the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful and we would not hesitate to stay at the Westin in the future.

“Huge impersonable expensive hotel, great location” We stayed at this hotel on a vacation to New York City. The single best thing about this hotel is the location. It is located in a very central area and most convienent. The price of the room was acceptable by New York standards, breakfast was a tad expensive. I did not like that bell service was not offered at check in, and that after checking out, you had to PAY for each bag to have them stored in an empty conference room. For 2 hours? Really unacceptable!

“Keep at bay” This is a tired medium sized hotel located on the I45 north of Houston. The rooms were adequate but the sheets had cigarette burn holes in. The bathroom area and water pressure was good. I checked in with a prepaid voucher and handed my passport in, the next day the same person knocked on the room to say he hadn’t any record of me here and asked if I had registered! I told him I had with himself. The free breakfast was okay but basic. Both vending machines were inoperable as they had been vandalised. I wouldn’t stay here again. There is no problem with parking and its free. There is also free wi-fi available.

“Expensive, but great location/” My wife and I spent a night here in December to take in the City's Holiday sights and sounds. This is a very expensive hotel, and I used my Marriott points for the night, but even that was expensive! Check-in was very quick and easy. The rooms are typical NYC hotel rooms, on the small size. But the views looking south or west are spectacular. The location is what I liked best about this hotel. Especially around December time. You are literally 50 feet from 5th Avenue (the entrance is on 40th Street.) Seeing the windows on Fifth, going to Macy's, going to see the tree at Rock Center as well as taking in a Broadway or Radio City Music Hall show, are all an easy walk away. Plus, if you did want to go further, the Lexington Avenue Subway line, with connections to other major subway lines is a short walk away at Grand Central Station. And restaurants? Fuggedaboutit! They're all over the place. My wife and I always spend one night in the city at Christmastime every year. This is the first time we've stayed at this hotel and it ha snow become our favorite and the one we will attempt to stay at every year now.

“Great hotel, did not want to leave at the end of our trip!” I made this reservation as a blind bid and was so happy with both reviews prior to staying and our time at this location. I can't say if I paid full price if I would be as happy; but what we received relative to our rate was fantastic! Pros - Great sized room with a living room/kitchen room and a separate bedroom/bathroom area. Both the living and bedroom had good sized flat screens in them. The living room had a small couch to relax on which always beats using your bed constantly. We didn't use the kitchen, but it seemed well prepared to handle a meal. Did use the ice machine and it was nice having it directly in your room. Overall the room was very clean and nicely furnished with up to date pieces. City hall was right outside our window and a good view around the immediate area. This location is convenient to both subway lines (right across the street!) and is a very easy walk to just about anywhere you want to go in the area. There is free Wifi (always nice!) and we did use the self-serve laundry to have a mid-trip wash. The facilities were nice and a real convenience. Hands down the two best features of this hotel are the staff and the breakfast. We never had a single rude encounter with a staff member; seriously the City of Brotherly Love! And the breakfast was out of this world in terms of choices and getting your fill. There is cold stuff (yogurt, breads, pastries, cereal, fruit) and hot items (waffles, eggs, potatoes, bacon/sausage, a rotating hot item each day). It was a great way to start your morning before walking all over the place. For us, only one thing was not that great - the bed wasn't king size, but I can overlook that considering the room was still a great sleep and comfortable. If you are driving, something to consider is the parking rate. We did not come with a car, so it did not apply to us. But I remember seeing the parking rate and thinking it was really high. We did have an issue of the family in the room next to use being really loud and screaming late at night, but again, the hotel's awesome staff took my phone call and took care of my concern. Except for that one incident, the whole hotel is very calm and quiet. If I had the same rate for this hotel, I would definitely stay again. We 100% enjoyed our time!

“Mixed bag” My wife and I spent 2 nights at this Sheraton. It was truly a mixed bag......When we arrived we were shocked by the length of the check in line. Probably 20 people in line, 2 people working check in. Took forever! although they gave us a bottle of water and a snack for waiting. We then waited several minutes for the elevator, sadly this was a recurring problem. We were pleased w the deor of the room. Comtemporary furniture, comfortable bed, nice shower product. Although the room was no smoking it certainly smelled like someone just got done smoking a pack!! At some point later that night, we discovered black lace panties hanging on the chair, they were not ours. My wife was horrified! We called housekeeping who promised to get rid of them ASAP. Well ASAP to the sheraton must mean 24 hours later, My wife was not pleased. Suffice to say we will NOT be staying here again.

“Exceeded Every Expectation, and Then Some” Location, Location, Location. Upon reading most reviews this is pretty well all I seem to hear about, and please don't me wrong the location is amazing. You are basically right in Time Square, a minutes walk from the Time Square subway hub, and a few blocks from nearly every major theater on Broadway. Within 10-15 minutes in any direction you have the Empire State Building, 30 Rock, New York Library, Macy's, Time Square, Bryant Park, Broadway, MOMA, and on and on. For whatever extra I paid for the rooms to be right in the heart of the city I made up in the first day for what I would have spent on cabs carting around everywhere. However I find far to few reviews give praise to the hotel itself. The check staff are very friendly and made sure that I secured a room that suited my needs, they were even kind enough to upgrade me to a room with a nice view on a higher floor. The Rooms were very nice, the beds were newer and very comfortable with a series of different pillow types which is appreciated. There was very little street noise or anything that would have interrupted my sleep which can be a rarity among New York hotels. Highly Highly Recommended.

“Good Location close to Metro” The hotel was clean, the 1 bedroom suite was a good size, the included breakfast was good, and the metro was out the front door and turn left and left again. Very very convenient. The underground parking garage was tight and $30 nightly. We visited just before New Years and left on New Years day. The hotel was absolutely overrun with families and kiddies. The breakfast area was a little hectic because of all of the kids. It's a buffet and kids naturally want to hold their own plate and scoop their own oatmeal...even though they may not actually be tall enough or strong enough to do that. Some parents were not very good about attending to their little ones and long lines would form because junior was straining to reach the oatmeal container. It would be better if parents would just supervise their kids a bit better...not the hotel's fault. The pool was clean, the 2 internet computers in the lobby worked well. There was really nothing to dislike about this hotel. The only slight problem we had was the maid refused to leave enough towels for us. We had 4 people but she would only leave 2 towels. Also the bathroom vent did not work very well.

“Overpriced and not a busines hotel” There's nothing terribly wrong with the Doubletree Club Hotel San Diego. But nothing really great, either. For $199 (rack rate $499), it's not a good value. The parking garage is aged, with narrow turns and safety railings that look like they were designed to meet bare minimum standards. Stairwells connecting parking to hotel are dark. Parking is $10/day with no clear reason why a non-hotel guest would park there. Internet is $10/day, and wired only (in the rooms; there is wireless in the lobby). Rooms were spacious, clean, and comfortable. Families with kids enjoyed the pool, and a high school sports team was having a meeting in the lobby. Laundry was stacked up outside the lower level's elevator, which you exit in order to access the game room and fitness room. The trolley stop is indeed 10 minutes away, but only via car. Walking is not an option (no sidewalks). I did not get the standard Doubletree chocolate chip cookie. Didn't see anyone else with one, either. The hotel is located in an area of mid-range, older, unattractive but probably perfectly functional hotels. There's nothing overly wrong with this hotel, but it's not a good value for the money. It's not what I would expect from a Doubletree. There was a very large conference in San Diego at the time of my travel, so it raised prices.

“Relaxing Stay” This was my second time to stay at the Hotel Whitcomb. Both stays have been very relaxing and enjoyable. I always love to go to the Starbucks in the lobby for breakfast. A fun staff. Both my check in and check out went smoothly. I found the employees to be friendly and professional. The room was comfortable and quiet. I like the location next to the BART and MUNI entrance so i can pretty much get anywhere I want to in San Francisco. I cannot wait til my next trip.

“Great location, Ok to good hotel” HOTEL REVIEW # 172 Hyatt Embarcadero MY TRAVEL STYLE: If possible, I try to stay away from business hotels and strongly prefer resorts that resemble the Four Seasons, Aman, and Oberoi but try to find similar properties at lower cost. I seek out the “wow” experiences and I encourage you to view hotels I have stayed at and their respective reviews (by clicking on my name). LOCATION: Excellent. More quiet than Union Square and just 20 minute walk or 5 minute cab ride away. The farmers market is across the street with some nice options for meals. Pier 39 is about a 25 minute walk from the hotel. TYPE OF ROOM: Concierge level; upgraded room. BED/SHEETS/PILLOW: Very good but not dreamy. Sheets are of good enough quality but they could have been better. Pillows are very nice down. LIGHTING: Room is a bit dark even with all of the lights on and the bathroom is better. BATHROOM/SHOWER: Shower door doesn’t close well, water pressure is medium with consistently hot water pressure. Mirror in bathroom has a TV in it that blocks most of the mirror for shorter people. The fan in the bathroom will not turn off and it’s a bit loud. TOILETRIES: Nice, may be worthy of taking home. CLEANLINESS: Room is clean. A/C: Quickly gets the room cool, but it’s definitely louder than average. CLOSET SPACE: More than average and two people may be able to pack most items. STYLE OF ROOM: Newly renovated room still looks like it could use an upgrade. Some of the décor are peeling off, the TV is out of place and the ceilings are low. Also, the view is somewhat blocked by the concrete on the outside of the building. COMMON AREA: Not impressive. Looks like an Embassy Suites from the 70s. Fake plants line each level. The tiled flooring is old and the carpeting in the hallways are some of the ugliest I have seen in a hotel. QUIET/MORNING LIGHT: Room was quiet but the A/C and the bathroom fan were a bit too loud. Also the mini-bar was beeping all night and kept me awake until I unplugged it. FOOD: Room service Caesar salad was ok and a drink at the bar was not good.. TV/INTERNET: Many channels on the flatscreen TV which is a very nice size for the room. Didn’t use the internet but it is available at a charge. SERVICE: Staff was not impressive as many requests were not delivered and a few issues went unresolved. SUMMARY: The location is very good but just across the street is a much better hotel, Vitale. I would suggest staying there. The best feature of this hotel is the nice view of the water the the concierge level has an outstanding view of the bay bridge and water which makes for an excellent place to hang out after a long day of walking. I still think the best hotel is the St Regis. If you are looking for nightlife, I would suggest staying at the Hotel Monaco or in that area. Shopping is best at Union Square (which is also walking distance from Monaco area). There are definite better hotels to stay at so I wouldn’t recommend this one unless the price is right.

“bon rapport qualité prix” tres bon hotel pas trop cher pour un hotel asez bien mis par rapport a times squares. les chambres sont bien meublé ?la salle de bain est assez petite et pas terrible en comparaison a la chambre.

“nice all around” We are Residence Inn fans, and this may have been a step above the typical. Quick shuttle to the airport. Very nice pool and hot tub. Cute open "mini rooms" adjacent to the dining area if you want some privacy for a small group of 4-6. Helpful front desk. A great idea that should be copied is their dining guide. They list the close restaurants in many categories, their distances, and then list the best in three different price ranges. What a great idea! We can vouch for the Chinese restaurant directly across the street.

“Very good Courtyard property for business travel” I stayed here for about a week on business. The hotel is large and appeared to be recently renovated. The hotel staff was great on check in. The rooms are large and comfy and had a fridge and microwave in room. The hotel is about 10-15 minutes from downtown and just a few minutes from the fancy Cherry Creek shopping area. The hotel has a good onsite restaurant and bar. I had dinner one night at the restuarant and it was great. There are multiple restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. Overall this was a good hotel. If you are looking for something in downtown than this isn't the hotel for you. The hotel is located very close to the freeway for easy access.

“Good hotel. Great location.” In this price range, it's the best hotel I found so far in NY. It's a good value! Great location, 1 block from Empire State Building. Lobby really small for the amount of people there. The front desk guy was rude but the rest of the staff was nice and friendly. Nice, clean and big room with a separate living area (with "sofa bed"). Small bathroom but this was not a problem. Elevator small and slow. Overall I good stay.

“Book one of the larger rooms.” We stayed for 4 nights mid July. We booked a single room with a queen bed. To be honest of the 7 hotel rooms we stayed in on our USA trip this was the worst. It was very small and the door didnt even open completely, it hit the wall at about 3/4 open. The furniture consisted of a QB, 2 bedsides, a chest of drawers with a flat screen TV on it and a small glass desk and plastic chair. Cleanliness was not wonderful with large dirty stains on the carpet at the entrance and a bit line of dirt at the top of the tiles in the bathroom. The bed was very hard and I did not find it comfortable but my partner was ok with it. Our room was facing the street and it was quite noisy as was the airconditioner. The bathroom had a pedestal basin and it also had 2 orange shelves about 12 inches lower than the basin on each side which was a bit makeshift and unusual. Having said all that you can see I didn't enjoy the room but the service and the staff were very good. Breakfast was enjoyed and we also made use of the laundry, the WIFI, the snacks, the DVDs and the friendly front desk staff also happily booked several tickets for us. We enjoyed dinner and show at the magic castle club. The hotel is in a good location and would be a great place to stay with kids. I think I would have enjoyed one of the larger suites better.

“A Real Treat” In the middle of a business trip I somehow ended up at the Warwick. I rolled up in jeans and a t-shirt and was overwhelmed with the elegance of the place. It was the first time I felt under-dressed for a hotel lobby. Vintage is not usually my aesthetic, but it is a lovely contrast to the rest of Dallas, which seems to have been built entirely in the 80's. More importantly, I forgot how wonderful it is to have solid wood doors, real windows, and a room that is almost totally soundproof. And you don't have to make any compromises with bathroom fixtures or an internet connection. All in all a lovely stay. I hope I get more surprises like this down the road.

“Same Marriot chain?” First off let me start by saying its in a very good location. The entrance is huge clean and classy. The room we stayed in was average; pretty small. Complaints to housekeeping the coffee wasn't refilled the creamer was spoiled there was no soap in the bathroom or any toiletries in the bathroom. The beds are very uncomfortable which is new to me since I've stayed at various Marriott s worldwide and they have never been uncomfortable.

“Basic Marriott Hotel” This is an older Marriott. The location is good. Close (10 minute drive) to the airport. Rooms are dated as well as the lobby. Staff is friendly and make you feel welcome, but not too knowledgeable about the area. When asked for a drug store, I was sent to a super market. Food city. CVS was very close, 1 block away.

“I think they did me a favor by steering me elsewhere.” My girlfriend and I booked The Standard to celebrate an anniversary. We were attracted to the location (in the Meatpacking District, over the Highline), the views, the sexy atmosphere and the architecture. Our room was a superior queen, about 230 square feet, but although space was used wisely, it felt a bit cramped. We only stayed for 2 nights, so we had enough room in the closet, but we used all of the table space for our luggage. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom, although small, was adequate. The rain shower and large tubs were nice amenities. We liked the 2 black bathrobes but never used them. The large TV set at the foot of the bed gave us an error code and didn’t work but we never bothered to get it fixed. There was a letter from Ian, who has answered several disparaging reviews on this forum. He reminded us that the windows were transparent and we should therefore use discretion. I am still confused as to whether the hotel wants us to perpetuate or dispel the voyeuristic and exhibitionistic reputation. I am guessing that there is a fine line somewhere and the hotel is straddling it without direction. We had a reservation for the Boom Boom Room and with anticipation we took the elevator up. The elevator had a video that seemed entertaining at first, but after a few trips to our room and upstairs, the video got tiresome and made the ride seem even longer. And now we must tell our velvet rope story. We went up to the Boom Boom Room and had 2 drinks each and shared a pate appetizer. The tab came to $110 before tax and tip. We would have spent more but the staff insisted that we leave before 10 PM so that the Boom Boom Room, hot tub bar and rooftop bar could open as an invite-only club. We asked if we could gain an invite but were told that we would not be offered one. Now this must be a very good marketing ploy because the best way to get someone to want something is to tell them that they couldn’t have it. We went to a late night show at the Duane Park Café and then returned to see if we could get past the velvet rope. Despite us being hotel guests and dressed to the nines (girlfriend had a gold sequined form-fitting Barbie Doll dress) we were not treated as invitees and were not given the privilege of waiting on a line for about an hour to pay $20-$25 for drinks. So next night, we didn’t try. After a Broadway show we ended up at Dizzy’s Coca Cola in the Time-Warner Building. There the cover was $5. We were able to walk right in and the jazz music was amazing. And the really good drinks were very reasonable. The setting was absolutely beautiful (makes the Boom Boom Room look like a corner deli) and the acoustics were perfect. I can't understand why people would prefer something like the Boom Boom Room. So the Standard did us a favor by not inviting us upstairs after 10 PM. And we won’t return. Ian, I don’t want to hear from you what the limited schedule is for facility use by hotel guests. And I don’t want to hear how you hope we will return and give you a chance to show us that our initial impressions were not really true. Your set up made us feel like second-class guests. Next time we will look for a place next time that makes us feel like we booked a first class ticket. If you want my partner and I to return, then ask Andre to contact us on this forum to discuss what it would take to make us come back. Allowing us to wait on line for an hour to get upstairs on an off night will not cut it.

“Acceptable, clean hotel” I stayed in this hotel for one week recently on a business trip. The hotel is located in the West End of Dallas, which is less impressive than it was 5-10 years ago. However, the location is still near several restaurants (the ones that haven't closed - a sign of the economic times and the other areas of downtown Dallas that are 'up-and-coming') and is within walking distance of most downtown buildings (probably between half a mile and one mile of most of downtown). The hotel is clean, but seems a little older. When you exit the elevator, instead of carpet you are greeted with older tile which transitions to carpet. Also, there were minor issues with my bathroom (e.g., chipped tiles, water temperature control not functioning well as it was mostly scolding hot, and only one light which did not extend into the shower very well - I felt like I was showering in the dark). The room was spacious, with one (older) TV and couch. The internet is free (and fast) and the refridgerator was chilled and ready to be used. There is a nearby CVS that you can use to stock up on items. My room did not have a view, but the room was quiet. I understand that the other side of the hotel may have some views of downtown, but I was warned (by colleagues) that birds from the nearby Acquarium make noises in the early morning. All in all, this is not a bad hotel (for a government rate), but other hotels in the area (if you can get a good price), are probably nicer.

“This property has went downhill.” I've stayed at the Sheraton Seattle numerous times on business over the last 3 years. I used to really enjoy it, but it has progressively gone down hill in my opinion. Unfortunately,. my last stay will likely be my last, despite the location, which is closest to my office. This last visit the hotel was packed, so there was a huge wait to check in, even late at night, and with my SPG status. The room I received was one of the larger suites, but it was really just a huge waste of space. The layout of the furniture was spartan at best. Most disturbingly, the room reeked of mildew and the linens seemed old and tired, long overdue for replacement. This property is undergoing an expansion, so construction noise was also a problem. After 1 night, the mildew was aggravating my allergies, so i asked to be switched to a different room. The room I was moved to was tiny, cramped and dark, and the view looked out on to a lower rooftop, where at 6 am, a construction crew convened. At $279 a night, I expect more. I won't be staying at this Sheraton again anytime soon.

“Excellent location, bring a flashlight, and come prepared for a small room” We won this hotel via Priceline. I figured I couldn't go wrong with a 4* hotel in NYC, and my heart kind of sank a bit when I came here after winning the hotel. However, after reading the reviews, we prepared ourselves for a small room and that's exactly what we got. Yes, the room is small. It will hold no more than two people. We didn't find the hotel staff very snobby -- we only went to them twice -- once to check-in, and once to check-out. They were friendly and quickly performed both tasks. Yes, the minibar is motion sensored -- so don't touch anything in that area and you'll be fine. In regards to the lighting -- it's bad. No way around it. It's one thing to be hip, modern, and cool, but none of that works if you can't see it. The only option for the window shade is a thick fabric shade that lets in NO light. The bathroom lighting was also inadequate. Somebody mentioned the lighting in the elevators -- I'm not sure if the W put more light in there, but we didn't find that too dark. You do need a room key to use the elevator though. Overall, not a bad hotel. We've paid more and received a lot less in our years of travel. Just come prepared and you'll be fine.

“Pleasantly surprised” I've been staying at the Hotel Gansevoort for work since it first opened. I haven't been back in a couple of years though and was expecting the worst--worn rooms and an aging hotel trying to be hip. I found just the opposite: a helpful and friendly staff, spotless & very quiet rooms with updates, and a super comfy bed. The location can't be beat. The neighborhood and rooftop bar are always a scene; even on a rainy night last night, there was an episode of HBO's "Girls" being filmed outside, but once I was inside my room, it was very peaceful and I had a wonderful view uptown from the 10th floor. Expensive, yes, and the rooms are not big (even an upgraded room) but I think it's still a very fair value for NYC.

“Old charm hotel-needs a little updating here and there” Classic hotel with old school cha. Ceiling in lobby is beautiful. Needs a few tweaks here and there but a classic property. Service in the bar in the lobby was very slow. Hotel staff good in some areas. Needs a little more consistency.

“Cracking location but an empty feeling” The Club Quarters sits in an enviable location smack bang in the centre of Boston's financial district - it's a doodle to get anywhere from here, south station is a couple of mins walk and it's a 15min max bus ride to the airport from there. Checking in and out and the feel of staying here is somewhat odd, you actually don't need to speak to anyone at all if you know how to use the machines, and I did feel like I wasn't really a guest, more a client. But then again, it is a business hotel. That said, the room was spotless, comfortable and had a power shower, coffee maker and great bed. Coffee also to hand in the lobby lounge, and next door is the Elephant & Castle pub serving meals and a fantastic cooked to order breakfast menu. The walls are thin however, and I was forced to move rooms at 1am due to neighbour noise (group party) but once in a quieter spot I slept like a log. It's good value for the location, but if you prefer to be treated like you're a guest you may not like the experience.

“Great Location; Good Price” Stayed there for a week in February 2005 during a business trip. The location is wonderful. You're within easy walking distance of a lot of attractions, including the cable car stations. Lots of shopping in nearby Union Square. I flew in from Oakland and found the BART perfect -- drops you a block from the hotel at the Powell Street station. The nightly wine tastings in the library were a real treat. Well attended while I was there and a great way to meet others. Missed the Wednesday night book reading. I signed up for the morning continental breakfast and think I got my money's worth. $6 doesn't buy you much elsewhere in SF. Downsides if you're there for business: Wireless service was lousy. My cell didn't work well in my room, which faced the courtyard. Too much concrete between me and the cell tower. Also, they offer high speed thru wireless but I needed a special device that they were out of the week I was there so I couldn't do my work at night, had to find another location. The price was right; the staff superb. Highly recommend it, especially for pleasure travelers.

“Fantastic, Some room for improvement, but excellent” I surprised my wife with a night here for our anniversary. It was an excellent choice. We stayed on Friday night, booked it on Thursday and got a hefty discount for a last minute booking. Brought my poodle along as well. Westin is the most pet friendly hotel chain I have ever seen. They provide a pet bed and allow you to leave the pet in the room alone (if quiet). I checked in prior to arriving that afternoon so that I could leave some champagne to be waiting in the room on ice, and there was no problem. The parking/valet was bad. As with most downtown hotels, the check-in drive up was very small, but no valet person approached the car, so....I parked it on the curbing and went inside the check-in. Came out, still there of course, but no one ever said anything. The parking garage was convenient enough, $18/night for the garage seemed a bit high. As a SPG we were automatically upgraded to the suite, before I even asked to be as intended. That was a nice corner suite with two bathrooms and living area. There isn't a bad view from a single room in the hotel in my opinion. The light rail station is located at the hotel which is only a couple stops away from the convention center and the nightlife (so the idea that there is nothing to do close by is ridiculous). The epicentre has a movie theater that is designed for adults with bars, etc. Very nice. The room was perfectly clean and well appointed. They failed to mention that my room key would get me out of the parking garage the next morning, so I decided to personally check-out to find out what i needed to do. At 9:30am (a pretty normal check-out time in my mind), they only had one front-desk agent. I waited 30 minutes in a check-out line because there were these ridiculous pagent mothers (they were using the hotel for the competitions) that expected to be able to check into rooms at 9:30am to dress their girls...ridiculous. That's my only real complaint. Still, we were very happy with our stay, the hotel was almost full, but was still able to accomodate our every need... Also a pet peeve but not really a complaint...Room service...We decided not to order breakfast because a normal hot breakfast would have been about $60 for the two of us plus a 20% fee, 8.5% tax and $6.00 automatic tip....that means breakfast for two would have been $84....for a pancake haha.

“Great Hotel, Great Location, great price!” Stayed here a few nights while attending a conference. The price was so cheap i was really almost scared to stay there. But the rooms were clean, comfortable, and the area seemed safe. Right off I-45 so very convenient to anywhere. Will definitely stay there again! Great free breakfast too. Hot waffles, etc.

“expensive and disapointing” The only good thing about this hotel -and I admit it is important- is the location. If you are spending a few days in NYC you are close to 5th Ave. etc- But it is extremely expensive in comparison to the quality and size of the rooms, the carpets are old, and it is not as clean as it should be. I wouldn't recommend it to any friend.

“great deal on priceline, but hotel too old!” the price is right (i booked it through priceline). the location is great. the front desk guy was very nice. there is free parking. but the hotel is just too old. the place feels like it needs a major renovation.

“Amazingly quiet” I stay in hotels 60+ nights a year and am a huge hotel snob. The CP was amazingly quiet--the quietest hotel room I've ever stayed in--despite it's location right in Times Square!! The beds are great, too. Would definitely return.

“Nice for the Discounted Price” I got a $199/night room special at the Algonquin's website. The hotel is gloriously old fashioned and located just a few blocks east of Times Square, with a parking garage across the street. A very convenient midtown location. The hallways are narrow and the room i got was quite small (10x12') with a small bathroom (stall shower), wall mounted LCD TV, a small desk and a view of a brick wall. Definitely fine for the reasonable price but not a room to hang out in, just one to sleep, shower and launch from. A nice touch- on the first night they threw in a complimentary continental breakfast (why only one night I'll never know but it's better than none!) Two sore spots: no written info on WIFI internet was available in the room, though there was an ethernet cable in a box. Thank god I called the front desk and found out the WIFI was free but plugging in to the ethernet was $10 /day. A simple sign on the ethernet cable box would be a nice idea! Then I asked for a NY Times in the lobby and they said they only get 50/day and they run out early. Hmmm....how about ordering 75 papers then? All in all, a fine hotel for $199/night. If I had to pay more I would look elsewhere, though.

“No surprises here” Pretty much what you expect from a Courtyard by Marriott. Good service, clean comfortable room, above average price. This particular hotel has a very good location for restaurants and it is easy to catch the trolley to the downtown area. We spoke to others that stayed in the hotel and the rooms at the front have a good view of Lake Union but traffic noise is a problem. We had a view of a usually empty parking lot next to the hotel but our room was quiet and really how much time do you usually spend looking out the windows of hotel rooms. The room rates are high and the parking fee is very high in my opinion but there is no free parking in Seattle. I did like the free wireless, which had decent speed. The computer in the business center is an antique and should be recycled. By the way, plentiful parking is cheaper in the lot right behind the hotel and the area seems safe enough

“A Budget Hotel that Delivers” My friend and I stayed at Hotel 31 over the Memorial Day weekend for 2 nights in a Double, Shared Bath. We knew what to expect and were pleased overall with the experience. We arrived in the city around 11AM and were able to check into our room right away. On first impression, it's an older building but clean and well-maintained. The elevator is older and requires a pull gate. Our room had a double bed, nightstand, lamp, sink, desk, chair, clock, hairdryer and tv. There is no ironing board or iron. The shared bath was rarely busy and kept pretty clean. The sheets on our bed smelled of bleach (which is always comforting). The towels are rather thin and sparse. There is a window A/C unit and it kept the small room pretty cool. Overall, for the $110 a night we paid for it, it was exactly what we needed. It's located on a residential street, so it was always super quiet and in a VERY safe area. We parked the car on the street a block over on 30th for 3 days and it was free and perfectly fine. It's only 2 blocks from the 33rd and Park Ave subway stop and lots of conveniences around too (Dunkin Donuts, Starbucks, Cosi, etc). If you're looking in Manhattan and would rather spend your money on sights and dining, I would recommend crashing here. It's not the Ritz, but it's a clean place to sleep.

“top notch” 4 nights at the palmer house was a real treat. room was large, well appointed ,clean and classy. the beds were very comfortable and everyone was courteous,helpful and professional. the lobby is awesome.the ceiling is a work of great beauty. they have this huge work out facility on the 8th floor which i think occupies 10000 sq ft. the pool is good. i swam laps 7 strokes end to end so its not nor does it claim to be a lap pool...and they keep the temp at a comfortable setting not near boiling like some places. the palmer house gets highest marks. not cheap altho great rates are possible anywhere with a little luck(pricelinefor ex) and skill.(trip advisor is a great resource) with chicago right outside yr door a trip to skydeck of sears tower (lgt building in no. america) incredible architecture (caf boat tours are outstanding) millenium pk world class city pizza at giordanos on jackson downtown was fabulous. and i know pizza! go / bring lots of money stay at the palmer house. youll love it

“Disneyworld in the Hills” Maybe an average rating isn't fair. My room was really nice, with a balcony and a big new HD TV, and a pleasant sitting area. The bathroom has a separate shower and tub and the tea-making facility is top notch. Turn down service and a smiling and attentive staff abound. The gym sports hot washcloths, fresh towels, and a bowl of fruit. The gift shop has everything you could want from yogurt to beer. When I complained about a room charge it was promptly deleted. The sports bar has the biggest screens I've ever seen. The elevators arrived instantly. The downside for me? The feel of the place is kinda fake. There's a big water park, outside music speakers, gas fireplaces everywhere, and plenty of fountains. I'm thinking many people who find it perfect.

“As usual the FS delivers” Stayed at Four Seasons in Georgetown.The hotel is understated from the outside but luxurious on the inside. Excellent location. Great room in a "renovated" wing - clean well decorated and a wonderful bathroom. The staff is extremely friendly and efficient. We needed contact solution at 11pm, of course it was delivered in less than 10 minutes. This was my boyfriend's first stay at an FS- they have another devoted fan. The entire chain manages to deliver a level of service and luxury that sets the benchmark. Another great Four Seasons experience.

“location is it” You're probably here for the location, which is the top selling feature of this hotel. THE hotel in the heart of Times Square. Really, right outside, TKTS booth steps and the area where everyone congregates to hang out and take photos. You're across the street from The Lion King, and eventually Evita will be downstairs, and Ghost the Musical will also be across the street. You can't get any more central than this. The room was fine. I did not ask for a TS view, so looked more into the office building across the street. The elevator system is probably the most entertaining thing (kids will likely love to play here). At the large bank of elevators (in a semi-circle), you enter your floor number, and it tells you which letter elevator to go to. This computer elevator traffic control is handy for such a big hotel. Also, the elevators are see-through, so you can watch the outside floors pass by quickly. Probably not great for those with fear of heights or vertigo, but entertaining and kind of a rush. For me, however, I think this is probably too big a hotel. It felt more like an office building than hotel. You enter from TS and need to take the elevator to the 8th floor for the Lobby. I prefer either more of a boutique hotel, or one with a real lobby as you walk in from the street. But perhaps a minor thing.

“Showing some wear, but a class act” I used to stay at the NY Palace all the time on business 5-8 years ago, and now usually stay at other hotels. I stayed there last week for the first time in a while due to the convenience of its location. I always enjoy seeing the familiar faces of the doormen, porters and other professional staff members at this very solid hotel. I will say, however, that the decor is starting to wear down. Carpet, upholstery and paint were all showing signs of heavy use over the years in my room and on my floor. With numerous fresher options in Midtown, and standard rooms running easily $700/night all-in, I think the management should really consider a freshening program. Even the elevator buttons are scratched up.

“In the heart of the city” I recently stayed at the Novotel NY for three times through a Priceline booking. I paid a bit more than I usually like since it seemed a higher quality hotel. The location is very tourist-friendly, right off 7th Avenue north of Times Square. The lobby and restaurant/bar area are very chic and modern, but the hotel floors and rooms were dated. My king room was large, with a pull out sofa. Great view of the river and other buildings, especially when the sun was coming up. Mattress was hard and pillows flat. Bathroom looked part-way remodeled, in that there were a couple different decor themes in there. The room-service menu was relatively reasonably priced, although with all the great restaurants on 8th, I never felt the need to try the food. Staff was very accomodating (there was a problem with my priceline booking) and quickly upgraded me to resolve the situation.

“Comedy of Errors at the Fairfield Inn Downtown Indy” My last stay at the Fairfield Inn Downtown Indianapolis was not as nice as my two previous stays, and was full of hilarity. I booked a room with two double beds rather than the suite I had on previous stays, and while cheaper, the room was not as nice. I am fairly easy to please, but you must understand that at least some of the double rooms have very oddly configured bathrooms. As my friend said, "it is great that you can fit in a cow in the bathroom." Seriously, the bathroom was full of useless empty space; it was not a handicapped room as there were no bars to help anyone, and the bathroom was huge. What was even odder was that there was no towel hook anywhere near bathtub. You had to walk across the giant room to get your towel after exiting the shower. Seriously, a terrible room design. The hotel was also very, very loud. Earplugs and a white noise generator were required to sleep! The other problem I had is that the towels were removed from my room, and not replaced. So the next morning we had to call for towels. Hilariously, the front desk guy came up and handed me what I thought were two towels, but ended up being about 15 washcloths--I suppose I was supposed to sew the washcloths together to create one towel. This was definitely the highlight of my trip. I ended up having to go to the front desk to pick up towels. I also found the parking garage annoying with more empty valet spots than regular spots. In fairness to the staff, the hotel seemed busy and there may have been teenagers staying there for Prom or something like that, and the staff all seemed tired. It's a fine hotel, but nothing really went right this weekend in the hotel. One other silly gripe: I am a Marriott Gold member and did not feel like I was treated as one--no upgrade, no towels, nothing. It doesn't really matter, but I am not in a hurry to remain a Gold member because only once while staying at a Marriott has it made a difference in my stay.

“Terrific hotel to explore downtown Seattle” I had been to Seattle many times in the past and always stayed down near BFI or SEA. Occasionally if time allowed I would take the subway into downtown to visit Pike's market etc. I've always told myself that I would stay downtown someday -- unfortunately downtown hotels have always been outside of my company's hotel budget guidance. On this trip, however, I started watching the rates at the Crown Plaza about a week prior to the trip. It was just $9 over our budget and I had high hopes that the rate would drop. Sure enough, a few days prior to the trip the rate fell within guidance and I quickly booked it. I chose not to rent a car this trip due to the hotel's $35/night parking fee. We took a cab to the hotel which was $20 from BFI and took about 15 minutes. Upon check-in the front desk staff quickly recognized our Priority Club Platinum status and upgraded us to mini-suites and provided access to the club level lounge. They also gave us coupons for free internet (lightning fast!), discounted breakfast buffet at the hotel restaurant, and a free drink. The room was a two-room suite right next to the elevators, but I never heard any elevator noise <phew!>. The "living room" included a comfortable couch and chair along with an LCD television and a refrigerator stocked with two bottles of water. The desk was adequate and included 3 electrical outlets and a desk-light. The only complain I have about the workspace is the desk-chair. I am 5'10" and even with the desk chair extended to as high as it would go, the top of the desk came up to my chest. This made it difficult to get some work done. I think the Crowne Plaza would be well served replacing these chairs by something a little more work-friendly. (or I suppose I could have sat on a phone book...) The bedroom includes a very nice, very comfortable king-sized bed. There is another LCD television on the wall, and a deep closet. I questioned how well the room had been cleaned because there was trash and an empty glass underneath the bed (yuck). The bathroom is small, but clean and adequate. Both rooms feature HUGE plate-glass windows that span the entire wall and overlook the city. Just beautiful! The club lounge on the 32nd floor is small but very well appointed. The staff is professional, friendly, and unobtrusive. I haven't had a chance to visit it for breakfast but the evening cocktail hours were nice. They had fresh baked pizza, fruit, vegetables, and warm cookies. Soda and water were free, however beer and wine were available for purchase. (in fairness they did have a nice selection). Tully's coffee was also available in the entryway. The hotel is located between 5th and 6th street. The walk to Pike's market is easy and takes only about 10 minutes. I would love to come back to this hotel with my family because Seattle is such a cool city and, quite honestly, I think that this hotel is better suited for family/tourism than it is for working. At this price point I would not hesitate to come back here again and I intend to write a similar review for our company's internal hotel recommendation message board so that other employees who are looking for hotels in Seattle may take advantage of this great property and convenient location.

“Train tracks behind hotel.” Nice clean accommodations. Small bathroom. Close to airport. Only drawback was the train blew its horn and the train tracks are behind hotel and it woke us every time it went by and blew its horn. Parking is $14 a day, and we had no parking available, but they did comp the parking when we told them. I would personally not stay here again. Not after flying for six hours. Bed was okay.

“Trendy and comfy” Trendy lobby with noisy bar. Try the Lemon Drop in the bar, but beware of slow service. Well-equipped, fairly large rooms. Nice, flat-screen tv. Internet speed barely decent. Nice bed and quiet rooms makes for good sleep.

“Nice hotel but victory park is lacking” W Victory Park was built to be the prime hotel in the victory park neighborhood. It is right next door to the american airlines center. Victory park is basically the name for this area and it looks like an attempt was made to make it a sort of upscale disctrict near downtown Dallas. The problem is that just because you have expensive hotels, expensive office buildings, and a state of the art arena does not mean it actually becomes a cool/hip/trendy place. Since Victory Park has not yet achieved this goal the W actually feels a bit out of place here. You can walk to the Hard Rock Cafe or Hooters but that is really it- if you arent going to a game the location stinks. The hotel itself is your typical W with a flew more flaws. For one the walls here are really thin. I have stayed at other W's on weekends and not been woken up by people talking in the hallways and slamming doors before. Also their housekeeping was inconsistent. One day they forgot to give me bath towels. Another day they forgot to give me soap. On yet another day they threw out my unfinished cashews that I bought from their mini-bar. Oh yes and this is something else. This W's minibar was for many items double what they are in other hotels. 7 bucks for a soda which expired in october 2008??? yup. I should also mention the 'ghost bar' is supposde to be a pretty awesome spot. I did not make it there during my week at this hotel though.

“All Around Good Hotel” Yes, it's perfect for people who are connecting from Logan, but it's also a nice hotel. I've brought my toddler there when we were picking up loved ones, and find it to be family friendly. The facility is very quiet considering it's next door to the airport. I have never heard the sound of a plane when I've been there. The fitness center is great and there's a pool. The bell staff and concierge are fabulous. The restaurant is only average, I think there's room for improvement there. The place is always packed, the menu is basic and it is usually a wait for the food to come out. The wait staff is great though and you can tell that everyone who works at the hotel is well trained in hospitality.

“ボストンらしい滞在” 予定よりかなり遅く到着してしまいましたが、温かい歓迎を受けて安心しました。 受付して下さったスタッフは、ホテルのフロントデスクのスタッフというよりむしろアパートの管理人さんという表現のほうがぴったり。 「ボストンは初めてですか?」 「日本のどちらからいらっしゃったのですか?」 これからしばらくの間、我が宿(アパートメント)に滞在する外国人との会話を楽しんでいるように感じました。B&Bのような小さな宿泊施設では、こういった地元の人との触れ合いがあって大好きです。 事務所で宿泊の手続きを済ませた後、別の棟に車で案内されました。 客室のあるアパートは、事務所が入っている建物のある通りとはまた別の通りにもあって、 私たちが泊まったのは事務所から徒歩2,3分位のところにある3階のstudioタイプ。 建物用と部屋用の2つの鍵が渡されて、まさにアメリカのアパートを借りているといった感覚でした。 毎日外出先から帰って来ると、まず建物の玄関を入って、かわいらしい花柄に囲まれたらせん階段を3階まで上りドアの鍵を開けます。日を追うごとになんだかそこが本当に自宅のような気がしてきて、まさにボストンの住人になった気分でした。 お部屋の半円形に突き出た部分の窓越しからは通りが一望出来ました。 犬の散歩やランニングをする人の姿を見かけたりと、地元の人の暮らしが身近に感じられます。ある日、日中ぼうっとしてテレビを見ていたら、遠くからサイレンが聞こえてきて、消防車が向かいの家の前に止まったこともあって驚きました。 建物自体はここボストンにあるほかのアパートと同様古くからのもので、そのため階段が傾いていたり床が多少軋んでいたりしましたが、全く気になりませんでした。 お部屋にはキチネットがついていて、こちらは大型冷蔵庫にオーブン、おなべや他のキッチン道具から食器に至るまでフルにそろっていて、本格的に料理が出来ました。 ボストンには、クインシーマーケットやシーフード、イタリアンなどの美味しいお店がたくさんあって外食が滞在の楽しみの一つでもあるのですが、今回は長期滞在で料理を作れて助かりました。スーパーマーケット(Shaws)が歩いていける距離にあってとても便利です。 バスルームはホテルと比べて狭めで簡素な感じでした。アメリカにある一般的なアパートにあるバスルームと一緒です。お掃除はハウスキーピングに来てくれるので心配いりませんが、お洗濯は事務所の向かい辺りにあるコインランドリーまで行く必要があります。 ホテルのような快適さを求める方には向きませんが、長期滞在の方や観光でボストンらしい滞在をしてみたいという方にはお薦めです。 Prudential Centerがある広い通り(Huntington St.)は、交通量も多く地下鉄も通っていて全くの都会の雰囲気なのですが、そこから路地を一本入ったコープリーハウスのある一帯は閑静な住宅街でした。ホリデーシーズンのボストンでとても素敵な滞在が出来ました。

“Amazing exercise facility, parking too expensive” I could never afford the $250 pricetag they wanted, but a 3rd party site helped me get down to $100 a night. But, the parking is ridiculous: $18 a day for self park and $22 for valet. If you self park, it's a hike to get back to your room. What did I actually like? The beds were comfortable and the hotel on the whole is very well-kept. The gym was the highlight for me. Individual tv screens for each cardio machine! They had weights and stability balls, with a scale. One night they couldn't get the doors to open, and I was desperate to work out. They graciously called my room as soon as the problem was fixed, so that was a very nice gesture. What I didn't like? The parking rates are too high, daily internet charges are ridiculous, the restaurant, Spencer's, is exceedingly expensive but was good food. This hotel is not worth the $250-$300 a night pricetag.

“Modest exterior, but great value and comfort” Walking up to the River Inn from the nearby Foggy Bottom Metro station, I was taken aback. You might expect a lovely old building with immaculate grounds, or something chic in a hip neighborhood. Instead, you'll see what looks like a bad Sixties apartment building plunked on a quiet residential street near George Washington University. I didn't have high hopes based on that, so the room was a great surprise. It must have been a reasonable studio apartment at one time. Good size, laid out well so that there was comfortable space for seating. We wished we had time and forethought to take advantage of the kitchenette even. The room decor was entirely pleasant. Not memorable, but in good condition. Important for me: the pillows on the bed were substantial. I slept well. We wish we'd had a view of something other than the alley and adjacent apartment building. One whole wall had a strip of windows, so we had light and fresh air, but we also had to close the curtains lest we give the neighbors an unintended show. Other small things: more towels would be great. Nice to have Aveda supplies in the bathroom, though. Also good to have free Internet connection - I expect that from hotels, and they delivered. We didn't try the restaurant, Dish, but it looked very appealing. We will go back. The price was very good, the room was attractive and allowed us to spread out and relax. The location is quite good as well. We're glad we overlooked the frankly plain and uninspiring exterior and enjoyed our stay.

“Probably the best hotel location on the Riverwalk” Very, very nice... We stayed here for a four day weekend, no business, just being tourists. The Hyatt sits at a bend in the Riverwalk, and is truly in the center of the restaurant/bar area. Of course, the whole Riverwalk is easy walking, but the Hyatt's location is the best. The hotel staff was very good, although the Concierge desk was pretty busy during the day. The new Dasa spa was nice, but expensive. Didn't have drinks at the bar, but got Starbucks there each morning. As Hyatt lobby bars go, it was small and out of place, but with so many other bars within 100 feet of the hotel door, I understand why they wouldn't invest heavily in a lobby bar. The lobby atrium does merit mention. We were in a tenth floor room, with direct view of the lobby windows and the Riverwalk below. I'll agree with the other posters that the atrium is a chimney for noise. We happened to be there at the same time as a Tattoo Artists Convention (fascinating attendees...), and these guys can party... until 5am, they can party. The hooting and hollering continued throughout the night, and it was really loud. Rooftop pool was nice, and there was a bar open on Saturday during the day. Weight room also nice, with chilled water on hand, nice towels, etc. The rooms were very nice, new Hyatt beds, soft sheets, thick towels, Portico soaps, etc. A rollaway for Kiddo was brought and set-up happily. Please note, though, that the in-room minibar has one of those mechanisms that charges your room as soon as something is moved. I rearranged some beer cans to make room for her milk and apple juice, and got charged everytime I shifted things around. Overall, a very good stay in a solid Hyatt with a great location. Would stay again... just not during the Tattoo Convention.

“Nice Stay.” We stayed 3 nights this past Columbus Day Weekend. The check in staff were prompt and professional. I booked this on a travel site and was not treated any differently. I was given an early checkin and a nice room. This hotel has an elegant feel to it and deserves a 4 star rating. Hotel is near public transportation from the airport. Check out was prompt and professional also.

“Amazing Experience” After my plans to run the NY Marathon were scuttled by Hurricane Sandy, I decided to treat myself and my husband to a weekend in town instead, and booked the Liberty Hotel easily by using my Starwood Points. We were upgraded at check-in to a Courtyard View King on the sixth floor. I was greeted with the customary glasses of champagne, which the Liberty offers to all its guests upon check-in, and it was great. I had left my car with the Valet, and was about to head up to the room when I realized I had left my cell phone in the car and would probably need to call the valet to retrieve it. No need: after they parked my car, they saw my phone in the console and realized I'd probably be looking for it, and almost on cue they appeared at the top of the escalator and handed me my phone without me even asking. While chatting with the the front desk clerk I mentioned we were also celebrating our first wedding anniversary that weekend, and the hotel promptly sent us up a bottle of Prosecco and bowl of strawberries to congratulate us! I was surprised because we had booked the room using points and thus, the hotel was not making money off of us (at least off the sleeping room rate) so I was kind of expecting the bare minimum. The room was spacious, the view was nice (if looked to the side you see across the Longfellow Bridge). The bathroom was phenomenal, with nice bath products included. The only negative was there was one small sticky spot on the carpet where a previous guest must have left gum or candy. It didn't bother us, but I'm trying to provide an objective review as possible. Our stay included the morning of switching clocks back at the end of Daylight Savings Time, and when we got back to the room, along with the turndown service with a letter reminding us to set our watches back (but also letting us know the bedside clock/docking station would automatically adjust its time, no need for us to do it), along with a brief history of daylight savings time. We had drinks and apps in the lobby bar, and while the drinks are pricy ($15) they're worth it. For out of towners, the cost of valet parking ($42 per night) might also seem steep, but it's actually mostly in line for overnight parking in Boston. The hotel is directly across from the Charles/MGH station on the Red Line, so you really don't even need a car to explore the city. At night, the lobby and the associated bars/restaurants turn into quite the scene, reminiscient of a W hotel, with a line of patrons just waiting to get into the lobby to have a drink! It was nice just showing my room key and feeling like I had some kind of priority access walking past all the people waiting in line LOL. Accordingly, if you have little kids with you, this hotel might not be the most kid-friendly. However, they are VERY pet friendly, and we saw a handful of guests with dogs. Checkout was efficient, and I had a final folio in my e-mail inbox shortly thereafter. I would stay at the Liberty again, and would recommend it to others.

“Don't waste your time here” I stay here often for work, and have found that quirky does not begin to explain this hotel. Everything is inconsistent, sometimes the valet is great and helpful and sometimes they act as if you've greatly imposed on them. The idea that you walk in the street level and there is a huge fountain you have to circle, then go up one floor, circle back around the fountain to check in is dumb. I dont know who laid this hotel out but it was not thought through well. The hallways and rooms are DARK, I have a hard time seeing in the hallway. The rooms have no light switches, so you have to walk to each lamp to light the room which is a burden. The rooms are also very loud at night. I have stayed here 5-6 times and each time the rooms are loud no matter which sie of the hotel I stay on. The property also isnt on the riverwalk, from 4-5 corner rooms you can see the river, but to actually get to the riverwalk you have to walk a ways. If traveling to San Antonio, there are several better hotels with better rates. This hotel is caught up on themselves and their rates are way TOO high, go elsewhere.

“Comfy bed, bad food, stayed 3 nights” If I'd paid full price for the room I would complain. Fortunately, I got the room for $60/night through Priceline. The bed was clean and comfortable. The chocolate chip cookies on check-in is a nice idea but would rather they spend more time/effort on developing a menu for room service that works. I ordered the crab cakes and a cup of the clam chowder. Campbells does a better job on the chowder and I couldn't choke down a second bite of the crab cakes. Bathroom was very clean as were the linens. Staff was friendly. We stayed in the old part of the hotel, not the newer tower, but the rooms were fine. We overlooked the lake or retention pond, whatever it is. It would have been nice if there were chairs on the balconies. Free wi-fi in the public areas was nice. I would stay there again, but not at the full rack-rate. The only real complaint is the balcony areas (stayed in 2 different rooms) - they are chock full of spider webs and the entire outside needs a good scrub. Same goes for the tired carpeting in the halls and rooms. But the for price we paid, it is a good value.

“It'll do the job” I stay here numerous times a year and for the location, it's awesome! You are within walking distance of some of Seattle's greatest offerings. From Pike Place Market, the pier, Westlake mall, it's wonderfully located. What I don't like is how evidently old the building must be. The heating cooling system is ancient, and some rooms have the analog control on the wall which is fine (though I prefer the digital controls like a lot of hotels have) but some rooms have a wall heater that you raise the cover too and it always looks broken, like it either won't close all the way or open all of the way. Some knobs may be missing, hard to turn, etc. My other gripe is the towels. Can they not afford Downy?! Or any fabric softener?! Those things will rub your skin off. Food in the bar is pricey late at night. A basket of french fries was $6.95?! $12 burgers don't come with a side? If this was Boston or NY I could understand, but when there are good eats just footsteps from your property, you would expect better pricing. The beds are comfy though and they use white duvet covers and that's HUGE for me. I need to know that my linens from top to bottom have been washed.

“Cheated on Starwood but it Was Worth it” I have stayed in nearly every Starwood hotel in Chicago and don't get me wrong, I'll always be loyal to them, but I recently stayed at the public as part of a company meeting and was pleasantly surprised. It actually has a feel of a W, but less stuffy, or maybe that's just Chicago. From the second the door of your cab is opened, the staff are great, directing you to checkin and the woman there was really nice and quick. The room itself is really modern, super low bed, desk and massive closet. The bathroom is a bit on the small side and the sink area a bit oddly designed so difficult to spread out your toilettries, but overall it the room was really comfortable and I liked the design. So my one complaint, yes, I literally think I found just one thing I would recommend for them to change - get body lotion in the bathroom! All 3-star+ hotels have this now and when I called down to get some, they checked and offered to run out and get me some, but that wasn't necessary. A hotel of this calibre should have body lotion in the room. Perhaps they had run out or hadn't gotten it in yet, I know this is a new hotel, but that was the thing I noticed. As far as our meeting went, I had 2 days in the conference rooms and everything was great. There were plenty of healthy options at breakfast - yogurt and berries, my standard breakfast, and everything was really fresh. There were more choices on other days too and really fresh orange juice. We didn't have any technical problems and everything was set up nicely. We did turn on the heat at one point and it smelled weird, but I guess it was probably the first time of the season that the heat had been used so that's normal. The lunch we had was really good, although the dessert portions, 3 huge donuts each, were a bit much :) I'm not too familiar with this part of Chicago, but we were able to walk to restaurants, even though when you're driving up to the hotel, it appears that it's at the edge of a neighborhood. Overall, I would highly recommend this place. I'm impressed they were so buttoned up, especially service-wise, for being so new.

“Comfort and a big flat screen TV” I stayed there two nights for a business seminar and the staff was friendly, efficient and accomodating to my requests. The room was immaculate, large and comfortable. Even though I did not watch much TV, I enjoyed the fact that the huge flat screen had numerous inputs for various media like my laptop. The price is very reasonable for the high quality provided. The bars and activity are a short trip up the interstate to down town.

“Solid Nice Hotel” Stayed here for one night on a quick business trip to Boston. When I arrived a room was not available (got in around noon), so I went to the restaurant for lunch. No one was there but I had a very good meal---food is above average. The front desk called me on my mobile to tell me my room was ready. Was upgraded to a room that had a panoramic view of the area--very nice. Went to the restaurant for breakfast in the am and the buffet was very good. A quick walk thru the Sheraton to Copley plaza and cab service is quick. Would recommend a stay for business

“One of Our Favorite Hotels” This is one of our favorite hotels. It’s got such great personality. The lobby is warm and inviting with lots of funky spaces to relax. As far as rooms go, we love the one bedroom jacuzzi suite complete with leopard and zebra robes and two flat screen TV’s. . The service is so friendly and the wine hour is a nice touch. We booked a special that included two drinks and an appetizer per night in the lounge. Delicious! We love the location – walking distance to the theater and to great shopping on State Street. Some of our favorite restaurants nearby include Siam Rice, De Cero taco bar, and the Walnut Room in Macy’s. We can’t wait to return!

“Excellent decor” Like everything in Newyork, the hotel is on the expensive side . The hotel is very close to the times square, so ideal for tourists and business travellers. The staff was very accommodating and helpful. The lights are dimmed and some people might not like it. At least it is different from the standard.

“What More Could You Ask For” As a frequent traveler through Dallas to other destinations, I've experienced the usual-come-with-the-gig travel snafus. This is now my defacto first call. Even if my luggage made it to the last flight to Vancouver, I know that I can get a ditty bag of essentials (better then any at any other hotel I know of) and can be in the hotel and in my room in 15 minutes. It doesn't get better then that. I *am* disappointed that they've made restaurant adjustments. The sushi bar was outstanding. The food is still outstanding, but I miss the sushi.

“FANTASTIC stay at the Magnolia” My wife and I went to Texas for some sightseeing as well as meeting up with some friends.
