While in Dallas we stayed at the Magnolia (this was our first trip to Texas). I booked the room from Expedia so I cannot remember the exact charge for the room since it was a package. The Magnolia definately goes the extra mile in making their guests feel welcome. Upon arrival which I was able to get into my room around 12:30 I was greeted by the manager and girl at the front desk. The manager made sure to let me know all the services the Magnolia had to offer as well as the times to utilize those. We were given a free upgrade to a queen suite. The suite had flat screens in the bedroom and living room. We had a full kitchen. The room was very clean, comfortable, and felt very homey. The bed was very comfortable. Overall I was very impressed with the accomodations. Amenities: well it started with the complimentary happy hour from 5:30-6:30. Jon the bartender (who was fantastic) served guests with free draft beer, and free wine during that hour. We did not stay after that hour so I am not sure of the prices after that. Jon was very helpful in sharing about local places to visit. From 8-10 each evening they have complimentary milk and cookies. They have about 3-4 different types of cookies for your pleasure. Finally each morning they have a breakfast which has eggs, potatoes, and a meat. The breakfast was excellent and a great way to start the day. We did walk into the weight room which looked nice, but the hot tub was TOO hot. They do have a business center with printers on the second and third floors. The people here are outstanding! Everyone from the manager to the valets were very friendly, helpful, and all around welcoming! The walk to some of the attractions range from 5-15 minutes. We did all the tourist stuff (JFK 6th Floor Museum, Southfork, Dealey Plaza, Fort Worth). Hofbrau Steaks is excellent (short walk), Sonny Bryans was very good too. I cannot say enough about this hotel. The only drawback could be the parking which is 22.00 per day plus tax. It does have in/out privledges and I was able to get my car very fast. Going to other large cities, that is a fair price, but downtown Dallas parking seems pretty cheap, and the cars are parked off-site. Thanks again Magnolia!

“Good stay!” I really would give this 4.5 of 5 stars if I could. We had a club level room which I would recommend. The staff was helpful and courteous at all times. The happy hour was great. We had a problem getting our wireless internet to work but we called down and they brought us a bridge which worked like a charm. I only have a few nitpicky issues... first of all, there is not enough seating in the club lounge. People were balancing their plates on their knees during the breakfast and a lot of people were having a hard time trying to find a place to sit. The lounge atmosphere is great with the large chairs, etc., but it's really not practical for breakfast. Also, the food at the breakfast was not that impressive--just a lot of carb-loading! Bagels, bread, cereal, and pastry. Finally, I agree with one reviewer who said the sheets were a little scratchier than what you might expect at a supposedly fairly luxurious hotel. As you can see, these are minor issues and they would not prevent me from staying there again. Overall I thought it was great!

“Elegant!” I travel frequently to Chicago and have my usual hotels that I frequent. I thought I would try the Hotel Palomar and I don't regret the decision in the least. The location off of Michigan Avenue is in the heart of it all with quick access to mass transit. The property is gorgeous and the rooms are surprisingly spacious for a boutique property. Furnishings were modern, clean, and created an environment of elegance of luxury. Hotel staff graciously accommodated my early check-in. Unlike other properties, the Hotel Palomar (and perhaps all Kimpton properties) provide complimentary internet with registration in their frequent guest program. This is an important amenity for me that I truly appreciate. The Etro bath products were sensational...what a joy! I will certainly return to the Hotel Palomar in the future and I hope to have time to check out the bar and the pool (too busy with work on this trip).

“How much you like it depends on where your room is located” The low score is because of the poor service which is not normally Hyatt. We are owners with Hyatt and requested an upper floor. We were put on the first floor and it was very noisy at night and in the early morning so sleeping late is not an option.. Our balcony looked out onto the expressway which was also noisy so sitting outside is not really an enjoyable option. The property is very poorly planned getting to your room with luggage as the walkways meander rather than let you go directly to your room. We were upset about the room and requested to speak to the manager on duty we have yet to hear from them. The room physically was nice and well furnished but very dark even in the middle of the day. Lots of dark wood and dark shades make it dark at all times even when light is coming into the room. If you have kids the water slides , pools and lazy river are unmatched. They are aimed at children though as there is no pool bar or food service. However the staffing is spotty. The employees were all in one towel hut and not on property .There were not employees or staff at the Lazy River. The lack of good management or organization was consistent Lots of employees not being properly utilized to improvie the guest experience. There were no floats you had to go in to the water and walk along the lazy river to find a float rather than get one at the starting point. Ok for a short stay would not want to spend a lot of time here unless I had lots of kids in the party. .

“Very Accomodating accomodations!” Called the hotel before we stayed here and request a room on the higher floors (non smoking only goes to 11th floor). They accomodated. Our room on the 10th floor(1012) had very new surfaces in entire room. Yes, a few stains in the hallway carpet, but this place is Busy, and it was not that bad. Our reservation was posted to them on the Wrong date by "Last Minute Travel", so be sure to print out and take your receipt. We did, and Freddie, at the front desk ,did a great job getting us in, no matter what it said in the computer. For our Entire stay, Freddie was a wealth of help, information and friendly service, as was Everyone at this hotel! Our room had no view, but everything else was perfect, and the bed was Heavenly! Maid service was good, as well. No vending in the hotel, so go to the small uptown grocery stores and quick stops near the hotel for drinks and snacks. They will bring ice to your room and were very prompt ; we tipped 2 dollars-very worth it! Concierge Ron found us an awesome place to eat a special dinner out, and took it upon himself to tell them of our honeymoon at Spiaggia, and we got extra special treatment there too. Location of this hotel is Prime to shopping, sights and eateries, too. (You HAVE to go to Sarah's bakery off of Rush street, about a 2 block walk from the hotel! :) Doormen and bellmen were friendly and helpful at All times, and we agreed we would definitely stay here again, as we encountered NO problems of any kind at the Whitehall; just a great group of people who went out of their way to make our stay a Pleasure, in a very nice place!

“What are people raving about?? It is a cheap old motel.” I guess after reading the reviews on here I was expecting something a little better. Lets just get to the point. Its a seedy old motor lodge. Yup it is cheap and you get exactly what you pay for. The rooms are tacky and old. Carpets are worn and mattresses are lumpy. Its good enough to just stay the night if you looking for something cheap and no frills but you don't wanna spend any extra time there. Plus if you want extra towels they charge for that. oh and if you check in early there's a 10 dollar fee.

“Super Hotel” We stayed a couple nights at the Hyatt at Olive 8 in Seattle while looking at some colleges. I found out later that its not the best area, but we never felt unsafe. In fact, we walked around qauite a bit. There was a lot of shopping and food choices within a short walk. I thought the rooms were very pretty. They beds were comfy, and the sheets felt crisp and clean. The bathroom was pretty standard, but clean and all the amenities we needed. Staff was helpful and friendly. We asked for more towels and they were brought to us within 10 minutes of asking. The pool area was nice, we didnt go in, but walked by and people seemed to be enjoying it. There seemed to be plenty of chairs by the pool, too. We liekd the gym. Felt up-to-date. it was clean, and cool inside. I dont have anything negative to say about the place.

“Very nice and comfortable rooms in the heart of Japan town.” Really nice hotel with Japanese gardens. Rooms are spacious with very comfortable beds. Nice decks with amazing views of the city. Close to great shopping on Fillmore street and excellent Asian food.

“Life is good in Indy at the Conrad!” I read the most recent review about not having the breakfast vouchers. If not for seeing that and knowing to ask for them, I, too, would have been missing them. I checked in and they had me booked in the wrong program, so I was not offered any of the amenities that I was expecting. I didn't completely realize this until later in the afternoon when I realized my check-in materials didn't include the expected breakfast vouchers or the spa certificate. Once I pointed this out to them later in the day, they promptly accommodated me, and upgraded me to a one bedroom suite. Now, the rest of the review is stellar for this beautiful, well-located property. I was able to check in at 11:30am. . .no questions asked. The first room I was shown to was quite nice: large, comfortable accommodations, Molton Brown bath amenities, soaking tub, separate shower, tv in the bathroom, comfortable couch and armchair, nice working desk (FREE internet!) and 42" plasma screen tv (with dvd player). Simply lovely. When I was upgraded to the one bedroom suite--a large living room, another 42" plasma, a guest bathroom (with another tv), and the same amenities as the regular room. The "newness" shows. The hotel restaurants are quite nice, and offer a nice selection for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The $35 prix fixe menu for dinner at Restaurant du Soleil is an absolute bargain! Spa Chakra was lovely. Great prices, that actually already include gratuity (a nice surprise!) and a wonderful assortment of services. Loved the 24 hour pool and sauna. I found everyone very nice. . .the bellmen, the concierge, the front desk people, the restaurant staff. . .very pleasant and knowledgable. The hotel is connected to the Convention Center via a mall with a very nice Nordstrom and an as-expected Parisian. There is also a pretty nice food court, not to mention some higher end restaurants all within a block. There is absolutely NO need to rent a car here. . .everything is easily accessible via car and a reasonable cab ride to the airport (less than the daily $25 cost of the valet at the hotel). I definitely look forward to my next stay!

“Ok experience, would not stay again.” We picked this hotel due to the location and the amenities. Having a toddler the kitchen is a HUGE help! The hotel is in a great location at broad and market, convenient to many shops, restaurants etc. The bellman upon arrival was extremely helpful with our enormous amount of luggage that required 2 luggage carts! However the remainder of the staff was pleasant enough but certainly not "hospitable." To park there it it $40 a day an it takes 30-45 min for them to get your car if you need it.....insane. The beds were very comfortable we had a one bdrm with 2 bds and a pull out sofa. One strange factor was you can hear water flowing though pipes at all times.....sounds like someone is taking a shower right above you for hours!!! I felt an overall sense of uncleanliness in the rooms....maybe just older furnishings?? Not sure. I would not stay here again. There are other options in the city that offer the same amenites with a greater level of service.

“Expected more from JW Marriott” I have to admit I was expecting a lot more from the upscale JW brand. Every time I asked for something like a king bed for example, I was told no. For the prices charged there should be more yes's for simple requests like a king bed or a more quiet room.

“Clean and Comfortable” This room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Why would I not give it an above average rating then? Well, the entire hotel is in need of updating. Although my bathroom was clean, it was also pink/salmon with a pink shower curtain to match. The television was the smallest I've seen in any hotel I have ever stayed at - maybe 13 inch. They can also use some tips on professionalism. Also, like someone else said, you will pay for everything else. I ordered room service - fruit bowl, pancakes, and O.J. and it was $27. It was good, but I thought $27 was pretty expensive for what I got. Don't get me wrong, my stay wasn't bad, it's just that the hotel is average. I would probably stay there again if at the Van Nuys airport.

“Nice Hotel Close to Union Square” I stayed at Hotel Nikko as part a lastminutetravel.com package - I'm not sure what the hotel portion came out to be, but the room was probably less than $100/night. The hotel is in a great location, close to union square and shopping! I got a room on the 20th floor and was able to check in upon arrival in the morning (which was a nice surprise!). There was a semi-view if you looked right or left. otherwise you were facing another hotel (but not too close, so you didn't feel closed in). The rooms are simple and comfortable. They have all the toiletries and amenities that you would expect. The decor is fine - nothing to write home about but certainly not offensive. My only interactions with staff were at check-in and check-out. Totally uneventful, so that's a good thing. The hotel had good temperature control so I never got too hot or cold, and it was also very quiet despite the fact that my room was across from the elevator. This was a nice hotel, and I would stay here again - it lacks the personality of some of the smaller boutique hotels, but it makes up for it in price and accessibility.

“cool new hotel” The Mondrian Soho has just opened and still feels very new. Cool design throughout the hotel, bright and airy white/blue/marbe color scheme in the rooms with floor-to-ceiling windows. Despite its young age, the hotel has already managed to attract a good crowd to its restaurant/bar/lounge on the ground floor nightly, creating a vibe that is pretty cool and not as drab as most hotel bars. On the flip side, while the decor of the rooms looks good, it is not very practical in many respects. Tiny sinks on top of the mini bar right next to the door with bad lighting serve as the bathroom. Closet is so close to the bed that it is basically inaccessible. Rooms are small even by New York standards. No serious sound proofing, street noise could be heard loudly even on the 22th floor, wide gap under door letting all conversations and service elevator clanking from the hallway into the room, and thin walls. However, overall this is a good place to be, and with the current pricing one of the best choices in New York.

“Avg stay at the Westin...” Wow...this was my 3rd stay at the Westin Times Square, and unlike the prior visits, this one was disappointing. Perhaps it was because of the apparent 100% occupancy across the city, but in the end, the service was avg to poor. The reasons: 1) Upon checking in, the desk informed me that I had a fax and kindly indicated they would deliver to my room. It never arrived. When I called back, the operator claimed there was no fax and then sternly asked what "EXACTLY" did the receptionist say. She later figured out that it was at the business center and would have security find and bring it up to me. The kicker...I received a message late that night saying they could not find it and that I needed to call them up again in the AM. Huh? 2) The room itself, on a club floor, had an awful odor when I checked in. The A/C was not turned on as usually done to circulate air, which may have caused the problem. When I called "Service Express", they indicated that there were no other rooms available! I was there at 5PM and surely not everyone had arrived by that time. They then offered to "ozonate" the room, which would require me to leave the room for 30 mins. I finally convinced them to also re-clean the bathroom from where the odor seemed to originate. Odor was never fully removed... Beyond the service issues, room itself was still comfortable. Heavenly bed is awesome as always. However, room showed some wear with the furnishings as well. I'm guessing this hotel went under a management change as this experience (3 star at best) was dramatically different from my previous 5 star rating visits. Hope they get back on track as it's been a great property in the past in a great location.

“it was poor” I booked that hotel using price line . When i saw the hotel and its room i was shocked . rooms were tinny and old furniture. Pool was dirty and also in some out side location from hotel. after watching this i left the hotel and book another in down town chicago. And they did not refund me my money.

“Different; trendy; dorks, geeks and models” I've stay here a few times. My experience has been remarkably consistent. The hotel is an upscale boutique hotel, a converted former jail. The service is typical "hotel trendy" (pleasant, but cool, no follow-through. Examples: room not ready; they take your cell, promise to call--don't. Concierge-not present or too busy; they do like to offer champagne, which is nice). The hotel is next to Massachusetts General Hospital and is convenient to dowtown Boston, Beacon Hill, and the MIT/technology complext just across the river. It also has a popular bar/nightclub. Thus, it has an interesting, mixed ambience and clientele: dorky academics and doctors; technogooks, and beautiful people/models etc. Rooms are sparse and modern. Fitness center is decent. The Red Line part of the "T" is right out the door. Each time I've stayed here has been fine, but I usually prefer top-notch service, thus my rating.

“Get a suite, amazing views!” We booked a junior suite, which was a one-bed room apartment with a corner view on the 30th floor. This was a great hotel, with helpful people if you're a tourist. Nearby there are many good restaurants, and the swimming pool is ok. It has the weirdest Finnish sauna i've ever seen, one where you can't throw water on the stove. That's like a restaurant where it's forbidden to eat! We would happily come back if there's business in the financial district.
“A touch of class in everything” Top class hotel with excellent location. Elegance and personal touch make this hotel the best choice in San Francisco

“Nice hotel, downtown location, lots of convention visitors” I was booked here for three nights on business. My company travel agent booked it for about $230 a night. Location: Hotel is right downtown next door to the SJ Convention Center. There was a convention in town when I was there and no one seemed to be too raucus until the last day of the event. You can't hear it from the room, but folks seemed to be having a lot of fun elsewhere. It is accessible by light rail from the airport and Cal train Station. Two rail lines meet here so I suppose its could be ok for tourists. But probably not your best option in that case. Parking is valet only at $25 a day. Check in: Quick. They have toiletries at the front desk if you need them. I never actually say the concierge on duty although they have a large book of menus at the concierge desk. Lots of staff around the hotel to greet you, but no concierge. Room: Large. One of the larger rooms I had stayed in a Marriott. Not really well laid out. Small work desk and its tough to see the TV if you are sitting there. And they charge $13 for internet access that is not wireless. For that kind of money, wireless would be nice. The bathroom was really big. Not sure why. The bed is firm, very firm. Amenities: The restaurant has a pretty good breakfast in the mornings. Its $18 for the full buffet and $15 for the cold buffet. The valet service can be a bit slow in the mornings if lots of people are trying to get their cars. You get a USA Today at your door (sometimes) and the Journal and Financial Times are available in the lobby. There is a convenience store to get donuts or bagels, but nothing to get something hot if you need to run out quickly. I ended up going to McD's for a quick sandwich. Overall: Not sure I would pay $230 to stay there again. It was convenient for me since we had a lot of site visits in the South Bay. But the same could be said for other downtown hotels. I don't think staying there at the same time as a convention is necessarily bad, but I suppose it could get out of hand. I just don't like the work area for what should be a business hotel. The valet service has the potential to be slow if you are there at the wrong time.

“Worth the price to park----barely.” Paid $78 to park car 16 days and stay here one night beforehand. Amateurish, clueless staff--run down hotel that probably should be torn down. Thought we were going to have to get out and push the van that picked us up at airport on way back----unsafe junk. Didn't see any bedbugs--so I guess, maybe, it was worth it.

“Beware valet” I've stayed at Ritz Carltons all over the world, well over 20 years. I was elated, in 2007, when the Dallas property opened. As a Dallas local, I do not have the opportunity to stay at the hotel very often, but go there often to enjoy their most excellent restaurant, Fearings. I encountered a problem last night, however with the valet parking services contracted by the hotel. In a word, the valet released my new Mercedes Benz to an unauthorized person who did not have a claim check to my car. When I left the restaurant, I presented my claim check to the valet. After considerable confusion, they informed me that they delivered my car to someone else and were not in possession of my car. I immediately summoned the Dallas police. The police were on the scene promptly and the car was located abandoned some time later. This morning, I personally met with the GM of the Ritz Carlton, Dallas, a very subdued, indifferent Mr. Daryl Roberts. He offered his apologies, stating this was "the first time this had ever happened" at their hotel. He offered no explanation, no compensation; nothing. The entire saga was taken so seemingly flippant, I vow to never return to the hotel and encourage others to heed my advise. I am in the process of taking this matter to a higher level, but felt it my responsibility to warn others of this serious, grave occurrence. Do not park here thinking your vehicle is secure; ever.

“Nice if you get the right room” I've stayed here twice so I know what everyone's talking about regarding the small rooms. The first time I stayed here, I had a tiny room with a tiny bathroom. The furnishings were nice but it was a bit difficult moving around in that room. The second time I stayed here, I received an average size room (which I would consider large for this hotel). I was able to move around the room comfortably and the bathroom was large. Very clean and contemporary furniture. The lobby is cozy and warm with a nice fireplace and modern furnishings. There is a little bar located there where you can grab a cocktail or a glass of wine. I have mixed feelings about the front desk staff. I had a nice person who worked with me but noticed another staff member being a bit terse with another guest. I don't think it compares with the other four star properties rated by Priceline. Think it is more of a 3 1/2 star.

“Excellent hotel” We booked this hotel via priceline bidding and paid 189 USD for 2 nights. They gave us a KING bed and the front desk was very friendly. We parked our car in the garage (not valet) which was convenient. The concierge advised us about NO-GO areas nearby which was really helpfull. The hotel is in good walking distance for the major city things. You can even walk to Union station.

“There are Better Hotel Choices in LA than this Place” I stayed here for one night recently while attending a meeting at UCLA. I was really glad that my stay was limited to one night because I really did not like this hotel at all. The room was decent, and the hotel had a fun bar on the top floor, but those are the only positives. What I didn’t like about the hotel was: The Location -. LA has a reputation as not a walker’s town. While this is true compared to a cities such as NY and Chicago, there are many part of LA that are great for walking. However, this particular location, by the 405 freeway (which I could hear and look out on from my room) in Brentwood, was not at all friendly to walkers. While the hotel did have a free shuttle that would take you to nearby places, I would say that ff you want to stay on the Westside of LA, Westwood, Century City, or Beverly Hills are much better options. Amenities – The pool and gym were really tiny. I stay in a lot of hotels, and their gym was one of the smallest I have ever seen. Key system – The worst thing about this hotel was their key system for the guest rooms. The green light on the door mechanism would turn green when I inserted my key, but the door wouldn’t open. This happened every time I used it! Furthermore, problem this wasn’t just isolated to my room. One of my co-workers had the same problem. Next time I go down to LA and have a choice of what hotel to choose, I guarantee that it will not be the Hotel Angeleno

“Location! Location! Location!” We stayed for one night at the Hotel Indigo. It's across the street from the Alamo and close to the Riverwalk. The hotel itself is an old office building. The doors of the old elevators stand in front of the new elevators. Very nicely done. The hallways are, I think, original as well. My compliments to the architect who melted a great hotel with an old office building. The room was bright, clean and quiet. Big enough. The bed was wonderful. The bathroom was bright, clean and had every thing you need. Breakfast is good as well. Loved it. When returning to San Antoio, we will defenitely stay here again.

“Business Stay - Very Pleasant” I travelled to Philly for a business trip and was super pleased with my experience here. This hotel is beautiful inside, and had everything I needed: spacious room, great gym, and good food nearby. The staff was really friendly as well and the location was good enough for my needs. The only thing I thought was a little much was the parking ($40 per night), but that isn’t going to change. I would definitely stay here again.

“Ideal Hotel in downtown San Diego” This Residence Inn is a newer Hotel in the Gaslamp district just minutes from the convention center and Petco park. It is ideally located in the Gaslamp allowing you to walk everywhere including dining and shoping. The staff was exceptional from the breakfast servers in the morning to the manager and even the GM. They are all extremely well trained. This was my second stay here and I would not stay anywhere else in downtown San Diego during future visits.

“Amazing pool, spa and workout facility” This is a great hotel. It's not going to be some cool, trendy place to party at, but it is going to deliver on customer service and relaxation. The staff are super friendly and helpful. I wanted to go for a bike ride and they put me in touch with a shop that found me a bike, picked me up at the hotel and took me to the shop. The hotel kept my bike overnight and the shop picked it up the next day. Again, great service. I also found the workout facility to be top notch as I watched cheesy girl movies while doing the treadmill. Then, I took a warm dip in their heated pool while watching the lights of Austin twinkle from the rooftop. I also ordered a lot of room service, and the food was all quite tasty.

“Great holiday stay!” Stayed 4 nights over Thanksgiving weekend. The hotel has an excellent breakfast buffet, with scrambled eggs, meat (sausage or turkey canadian bacon), usually breakfast potatoes and pancakes, fruit, yogurt, waffles, donuts, breads, juices. Probably the best Res Inn breakfast I have seen. Very roomy gathering place, fireplace, pool table near front desk. One night offered a managers reception of chili, soft drinks, beer. Good wifi speed as well. Stayed in a 2 room suite - the 2 room suites have a 4 setting kitchen with an oven (only a cooktop & microwave in the 1 bedroom suites). Workout facility open 24 hours with one eliptical, all purpose workout machine, two treadmills, multiple free weights. Pool & hottub only open Memorial Day to Labor Day (recommend that management enclose this area - would increase winter stays). Location next to White Marsh Mall - many shopping & food options. Easy to get in & out of property. Some problems with efficiency of checkin staff - but overall a great stay.

“Busy hotel close to everything” The Hyatt is a good business hotel in Chicago. It is very centrally located, though the Wacker Drive location feels a little isolated, it is actually a short walk to Millenium Park, Naby Pier, and shopping / restaurants. The rooms are comfortable and modern, though a little dimly lit. There are a number of restaurants in the two building complex, and the staff was friendly and efficient. It's a five-ten minute ride to McCormick Place via regualrly available cabs. The hotel is okay for families too, but there are probably better choices like the Embassy Suites across the river (with an AMC theater attached to it) and others if you are traveling with kids.

“Consistently excellent” I have to travel to DC frequently for work, and this has become my hotel of choice. The location is excellent, the rooms very comfortable and stylish, the wifi is free and strong, and the nightly wine hour is a nice touch. The location would be perfect for any vacationer, and business travelers in Dupont Circle couldn' do any better. The pool and exercise room are small, but other than that there are negatives about this place.

“Only stay if you get a discounted rate” THE GOOD-- Concierge staff was nice if slow. Water pressure in hotel was good. Lighting in bathroom was decent. Cute hotel upon entering. Coffee/tea maker in room was very nice and clean. THE BAD-- Overall the staff is just incompetent, inattentive, and uncaring about service in almost every area. Very poor service from front office staff. They act clueless, act like you're bothering them and go out of the way not to be helpful with even the simple things. Very strange. Bell staff couldn't even be bothered to get my luggage out of cab or open a door. It was very clear they were helping some people and totally ignoring others but I couldn't figure out how they picked. (VIP's? Big tippers?) Gift shop person was reading a paper and only put it down when I stood there for a while and said 'excuse me' 3+ times. Business center was just as bad with service and prices were high for no real reason. They also advertised supplies they did not have. Room service food was good, but server forget items on every order every time for us. And the hotel needs to invest in tables vs. balancing a meal for 3 people on a tray. It's not like there is a table in the room to eat on. Bathrooms in rooms were tiny. Literally stepped out of the tub and had to be careful not to step into toilet. And if you missed the toilet you hit the sink. I've honestly never seen a bathroom so small in a normal size room. Location of hotel is not convenient to touring city. I would only stay here if my convention used it as a headquarters again. Otherwise no way. I honestly never found the gym because everytime I asked where it was I got the worst directions. It was ridiculous and frustrating. (this is a big hotel even though most is a waste of space) I believe they have bed bugs. They also don't use proper sheets so when you move all the sheets move. Phone in my room was broken and carpet needed shampooing. Honestly I could go on but I'm already frustrated for no reason and you get the point.

“Great Location” I have stayed at this property a couple of times in the last decade, but this was my first stay where I was actually attending an event in the hotel. The hotel is located one block away from the NASCAR Hall of Fame and the Charlotte Convention Center making it one of the most convenient hotels in the city if you are attending events at the CC. My room was great. I loved the 42" flat screen television mounted on the wall as opposed to being stored in a cabinet as most hotels still house their sets even in a flat screen world. The work desk was great and allowed me to spread out all my digital gear with ease. While there is a restaurant in the hotel, there are a plethora of choices for dining within a 2-3 walk block of the hotel from fast food to fine dining. And unlike when I first visited the city more than a decade ago, the downtown is no longer a Monday-Friday office worker centric area, and has a pretty vibrant nightlife. Even the bus station isn't as scary as it used to be. The hotel staff was friendly and courteous, and due to the heavy bookings at the time they weren't able to accommodate my request for a late check-out. I used to avoid staying in the city because of the lack of amenities and how dead the area was on the weekends, but now I will make it a priority as long as the price is right and the Hilton will be near the top of my list.

“Location, Quality, Service, Value.” Mansfield is well-located more or less between Times Square and Grand Central Station - thus, easy access to east and west side trains. Rooms are quaint, quiet and clean. The bar is comfortable and the sitting room with the espresso machine was a great way to start the day. This was a great value delivered via Priceline ($150/night). I hope to stay there again sometime. Their people just added to the experience. My colleague left a check and some other items in the Library one morning, and that evening we went to the front desk to ask if they'd been found. The Gentleman behind the desk said they had not, but he came into the library to help us look for them. No luck. The next morning, we discovered they had been turned in. A great inconvenience avoided. The hotel staff seemed to genuinely care about our experience.

“Wonderful Hotel” I was arriving in New York by train, and wanted a hotel close to Penn Station. The New Yorker is one block away, and it is a truly great hotel. It was busy when I arrived, but I was rapidly checked in by a very friendly, very professional desk clerk. I was assigned Room 4003 on the 40th floor, and it is no exaggeration to say this was the greatest hoel room I have ever stayed in. Room 4003 had views of the Hudson River to the west, and views of downtown New York to the south. It was amazing. I had a refrigerator and a sink area, and the living room had two chairs, a sofa, and a desk with chair. The televsion was a 33 inch flat screen. The sofa made into a bed, and there was an additional coset in the living area. You go through double doors to the bedroom, and I am a stickler for a comfortable bed, and the bed was wonderful. The thread count in the sheets and linen were high. The bathroom was small, but it made up for it with a large shelf above the toilet and sink. The towels were very thick. The location is great. You are across the street from Penn Station and the subway, and Times Square, Chelsea, the Theatre District, Macy's, the Empire State Building are short walks away. This hotel is really a first class hotel, and I will stay here again.

“average” I specifically booked a one bedroom suite with a double sized sofa bed as my husband and I were sharing the room with my mother. My mother was to get the bedroom and we were to go on the sofabed. When we checked in and went to the room, we did have a one bed suite, but it was tiny, very worn and tired and only had a single person sofa bed. After several phone calls and going back down to the front desk we finally got the room we booked. However, we had to move our baggage to our new room ourselves. All of this made us late for our evening reservations. This room was much larger and nicer. However, it is still worn and tired decor wise. The kitchen areas are pretty old!! The heating controls are also extremley outdated as well. My mother said the bed was very comfortable but the sofa bed was not. The bathroom was on the small side, but thats no suprise in NY. In future, I will stay in a smaller room in a nicer hotel.

“Just great” Stayed here for a week-long vacation and had a wonderful time. Other than the construction in the building next door, did not see any issues with the overall maintenance of the property. Staff was courteous and helpful - so the reviews otherwise are a bit of a surprise. The restaurant is terrific and worth visiting, which is not always the case for hotels. But it was also nice to be one block away from Union Station so lower-priced dining options were also available. I would stay here for either personal or business, and I can't always say that about every place.

“Good biz stay if you're at the SJ Convention Center” My company put on an event at the SJ Convention Center, note that the Mariott is attached to it, hence it's an incredibly short walk to the venue. Stayed at the hotel for four nights, overall was a fine stay, room was clean, great work space and was quiet. Since our event served breakfast and lunch, really only had drinks/snacks at the hotel in the hotel bar, which were fine. Service at the hotel was great. The hotel's pool area felt pretty spartan, but, got good sun, and felt a bit like a solar oven with the sun relecting off the hotels windows in the late afternoon.... Overall, if I'm attending an event at the SJCC, will definitely be back at the SJ Mariott.

“Very romantic rooms” I live in suburban Philadephia, and wanted to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday with a romantic night in the city. Last year we had stayed at the Sofitel, which has many things to recommend it (great location, luxe rooms and bath). This year I chose the Penn's View mostly because of its proximity to Old City, and the associated restaurant Panorama. I had booked a regular queen room, but decided to look at other rooms when I arrived. I'm glad I did, because I decided on a king room with fireplace and jacuzzi, with a view of the river. Gorgeous, gorgeous room, with hardwood floors, fine rug, silky linens, and a beautiful bathroom with raised relief tiling, and orangey-gold wallpaper with white Pegasus horses flying on the walls. If you might be bothered by traffic noise, book a room further back from Front St. The jacuzzi and gas fireplace were so pleasing on this winter evening we almost decided to order room service, but stayed with our plans to enjoy a flight of wine at Panorama, followed by dinner on the Mosholu, the tall ship on the Delaware River, not far from the restaurant. Please don't imaging that the Mosholu is a tourist trap -- not only was the river view wonderful, the food was fantastic. A slightly smoky lobster bisque will bring me back. All in all, it was a wonderful evening, and I highly recommend the Penn's View Inn for unusually luxurious rooms, and a fine location.

“Stay at the new Phoenix Westin” I am a frequent business traveler and am starting to provide reviews so others know the great and not-so-great. I would call this place "incredibly average". I don't think I stay at the nicest places, but I will admit I'm getting so I expect some things that I call basic... like a towel rack, enough hangers, and a safe. Am I asking too much? Pros: - Very nice check in and concierge and operator... very nice people - Quick and easy change to get a late check-out an hour after normal time - Great downtown location - Comfortable bed and pillows - Plug on bedside lamp (this is very nice) and 2 plugs on lamp on table (If you think this obsession with plugs is weird, try staying in a room where it's hard to find a single one and then you'll realize how many things you need to plug in (esp if you're working there for several hours) - Ginger-scented Hyatt bathroom amenities smell nice (I'm reaching for compliments here) Cons: - 50 mins room service, at 4:00 pm (!!), for one caesar salad and one bottle of water - Room service salad was incredibly average - TV has an HDMI input but the "input" button on the TV doesn't actually work, so the input is moot - TV remote is so worn, only the number "5" can be seen - TV doesn't swivel all the way to be seen on the bed, and there is only one small armchair otherwise - Bathroom is tiny. Has NO towel racks at all... just ONE hook. One? - Not enough hangers in the closet - No drawers, only open shelves - No refrigerator or mini bar (I usually empty it, get my own sodas as I don't drink coffee, and get milk for morning cereal to try to counter the "fat traveler effect"... no luck on this trip) - No in-room safe - Desk is too small to comfortably fit a laptop and a room service tray - Tub shower (vs. a nice tiled "walkin" shower)... - A lot of activity on my floor - people in and out all night. It was if they put everyone on one floor to make all their work easier. Not great for noise although not too disturbing (just odd). More: - I didn't try internet as I have an aircard - Colleagues said fitness room is nice but I walked instead, so can't verify I recently stayed at the new Phoenix Westin and it was DIVINE!! Standard room came with a couch, chairs, huge desk, empty refrigerator, lots of coffee, huge foyer, huge bathroom, walk-in shower you could switch between "rain" and "regular", great TV with HDMI input, etc. Tons of public sitting areas to have a business chat as well. I would HIGHLY recommend it over this worn Hyatt.

“Perfection” I stayed at the Ritz as part of an overnight spa escape for myself and a friend. We were treated like royalty from start to finish. I have stayed at many Ritz Carltons and this is probably my favorite one in terms of service. All of the staff members, from the valets to the bellhops to the front desk and room service staff, were genuinely friendly and went out of their way to make sure our stay was perfect. We were upgraded to a beautiful corner room on the club floor, which was unexpected but certainly appreciated. The food presentations in the club lounge were decadent, and the club lounge host/concierge was wonderful. Our time in the spa was relaxing and we enjoyed our top quality treatments. We checked out the hotel's bar and patio, which was very lively on a Friday night, and we walked to a couple of other nearby hot spots as well. We ordered late night room service and the food was delivered promptly, with a smile. The next day we were given a late checkout so that we could enjoy a couple hours of sunshine at the pool, which was on the small side but still very pleasant. When we reluctantly checked out, we felt truly relaxed and pampered. Kudos to the staff at this Ritz for getting everything right! We will be back.

“Good Renovation, Average Stay” So it appears that some La Quinta's are getting a makeover, and this one is one of them. It was actually being worked on while I was staying there, but that wasn't so bad. It smelled like fresh paint, and they were replacing tile and furniture in the breakfast room, but the guest room was already finished. I think they're going for the clean look with the bedding, but there isn't really a comforter, just a thick blanket that I can't imagine can be washed very easily. Other than that, the room is comfortable. Breakfast doesn't have much of a selection, and the internet was pretty slow most of the time. Also, the service is a little less than desirable. The front desk seemed to be overly concerned with answering phone calls rather than helping people actually at the counter. Check in took a long time, and at one point I saw 6 people waiting in line.

“Wonderful & Romantic” After receiving a special rate notice from Travel Ticker that offered this hotel at $90+ a night I was a little skeptical since this is more than 60% discounted so I consulted with my "travel friends" at Tripadvisor. Much to my surprise, this hotel was rated #1 in Phoenix by reviewers. And boy were they not wrong! This is a beautiful property located within luscious gardens of palms, flowers and gorgeous foilage! Unfortunately, we were not able to see flowers as it was 116 degrees. All trails lead to "casita" style accomodations. The property gives the feel of a luxury old fashioned mediterranean home (mansion) instead of a commercial type hotel. Upon our arrival, we were greeted by the excellent valet staff who took our luggage and escorted us to the front desk. The front desk staff was very very attentive to our every need. Check in was smooth and we were greeted with a "happy anniversary" - we were celebrating our 27th wedding anniversary. In addition, the hotel presented us with a gift platter of cheese and fruit for the occasion sent to our room. LOCATION: Location is great - it is actually a few blocks from The Phoenician and very close to Scottsdale. Malls, Restaurants, Nightlife and other entertainment. ROOM: We were assigned Casita #112 - no two casitas are alike so this review is based only on this casita. Although I booked this as a "designer" casita (at a higher than the "special $90" rate), after entering it mostly resembled a "southwestern" style casita. I didn't confirm this with the front desk as it was lovely anyway. The decor was of mediterranean and spanish style. Very comfy and well appointed bed (king) and two nice chairs with a table. A soft chair with ottoman was provided facing the TV and a mini-bar. The casita has a door leading to its own private courtyard in the back that is furnished with two chairs and a table surrounded by a small flower and plant garden. Very private. The room also has double french doors with plantation shutters leading to a front courtyard also furnished with patio furniture. In-room internet ethernet, two two-line telephones, LCD TV, clock radio with nice smoothing spa music cds, candles and matches, in-room coffee and tea are provided. Also provided is an iron, ironing table, shoe shining kit (although the hotel provides complimentary daily shoe shine) and daily paper. Minibar items are for purchase. Turn down service nightly. On our first night, we had a Rose Petal Heart placed on the bed upon turn down (this was ordered in advance). The bathroom is very large with a very very large shower. My only concern is the bathroom has no a/c vent - only a small window and a skylight that at 116 degree temperature this becomes intolerable to be in there. An exhaust is provided but does not do the job of removing the extreme heat. Blow dryer, lighted mirror , many towels, slippers, robe and shower amenities is provided. The shower gels, soaps and shampoos are all orange blossom oil based - wonderful! Bought a bottle of lotion at the spa to take home (@$22USD). DINING: Dined on Jul 19 at T.Cook's - the hotel restaurant - a fantastic experience. Very quiet and romantic atmosphere. Inside or outside patio choices - with the heat we chose inside. Our server, John, was excellent - tended to our every need. The food and dessert were of first class. We were a party of four each having, Ribs, Poulet Chicken, and Fish and lobster. Highly recommend the restaurant - reservations prior to hotel arrival is suggested. SPA: We had a couple's massage which was excellent. The spa facility is very beautiful. We did not use the pool as it was very hot during the day but found the poolside area as lovely as the rest of the property. PROBLEM: We did encounter problems with the housekeeping department. Our room was never cleaned unless we called and then we still waited for them to appear. We would leave our room around 10am and return on average about 3 to 3:30pm where we would find our room in the same condition it was left in. On the third evening we informed the front desk of this problem and experienced some difficulty with the front desk staff - Ms. Jennifer. She appeared not to know how to handle this complaint. When we requested to speak to the manager, she informed us that the manager was -conveniently for her - not available and a message would be relayed. We never heard from the manager that evening. The following morning upon check out we informed the front desk staff who immediately referred us to the front manager, Ms. Beth Friddle who quickly apologized for the lack of service of housekeeping and the behavior of Ms. Jennifer. Ms. Friddle is a professional at her job. This is the only problem we encountered at this establishment. OVERALL: For a wonderful romantic experience, I highly recommend this hotel with its majestic views, surroundings and fantastic staff! We certainly will be returning in the near future. Keep in mind that the hotel charges a $25 daily resort fee that includes valet parking. Cars are garage kept. I have posted some pictures for your viewing.

“Convenient airport hotel” The Fairfield Inn is a very good option if you look for a reasonably priced airport hotel. The pluses are the shuttle service, the pool and the complimentary breakfast. Location: The Fairfield Inn belongs to a cluster of airport hotels which is a 10-minute-drive from the airport. The hotel shuttle runs every 15 minutes, day and night, and offers some of the best service I ever experienced. Rooms: The rooms are typical for this class, functional and agreeable. Amenities: The well-heated indoor pool is great after a long flight and especially the beautful tiled spa. Breakfast: Complimentary breakfast is good, with warm oatmeal and sausage gravy and with stuffed biscuits to heat the up in the microwave oven. The minus was that they had a water problem on several levels and had huge fans installed to dry the walls. Another minus are the paper-thin walls. We heard our neighbor's alarm clock at 6:15 and were able to understand each single word which was spoken from his bedside radio. We heard him coughing, however not severe.

“Great location and weekend bargains” My wife stayed here for a convention in 2008, so we decided to stay there following the 4th of July fireworks on The Mall. We got a very good weekend rate about three weeks in advance. The room was fantastic, with a comfortable bed, nice furnishings and a kitchen with a full size refrigerator, stove, microwave, and plenty of dishes and cookware. We brought dinner and breakfast with us, so the facilities were perfect. The Foggy Bottom Metro station is about 2 blocks away. Since we were there for the fireworks, we walked straight down 23rd Street to the Lincoln Memorial, which took about 20 minutes. Parking at the hotel, as with most DC hotels, is very expensive (~$30). However, there is a Ritz Carlton a few blocks away where the public parking is $6 per day on the weekends. My only complaint about this hotel is that the front desk staff is not well equipped to deal with problems. It was necessary to contact the General Manager to resolve a pricing issue, and he took care of the problem in a highly satisfactory way. We will definitely include this among our list weekend getaway hotels. Others include the St. Gregory and the Hilton Garden.

“Love the DoubleTree chain, but not this location” There was a convention at the DT this weekend. The guests were extremely rude running up and down the halls all night. The pool hours were posted as 8am to 11pm, which is WAY too late if you have a room facing the pool. Guests were in the pool before 6am making noise! I called down to the front desk and was told the pool opened at 6am! The property itself is very old. The rooms have not been updated in quiet a while (albeit they have nice flat screen tv). The interior doors are ugly brown with cheap wood veneer paneling that is chipping and peeling. Guests are allowed to smoke on the verandas but the smoke just blows right back into the rooms and the hallways. The hallways reeked of marijuana this morning when we went down for breakfast. I complained to the front desk and I did receive compensation; however, that DID NOT help the lack of sleep! i will not stay at this location again. I am a Hilton-diamond

“Good Hotel, Wayfinding Difficult” Recently stayed over at the Renaissance Center, it was an enjoyable stay. The hotel/location where the hotel is at is HUGE. This was good and bad. On the good side, you literally have a ton of dining/eating options without having to weather the normally bad weather during the winter. Theres fancy establishments, mid-priced and a fast food area down on the bottom floor. They also had a small shopping area for those into that sort of thing. The hotel lobby itself is on the 3rd floor, deep inside the huge complex. I almost wished they had a valet for getting from the front door to the lobby rather than just valet's for parking your car. It was very challenging reaching the lobby and then reaching the front door again from your room. Its a maze of floors and the signage kind of sucks. If you do manage to get through the maze, the rooms themselves are quite nice. The beds are comfortable, the view of the city skyline, particularly from the high floors are great. Room service was good and helpful. My only gripe with our room was that it did not have any closets. I found that wierd, and annoying as i had nowhere to hang my jacket. It really wouldnt have killed them to have atleast a tiny closet. There is room for it. On the plus side, the TV had HD programming and the dresser it sits on has all sorts of easy to access jacks, so if you want to plug in your ipod and other media you happen to have with you its great. They have ample power outlets which is rare and the layout of the room aside from the missing closet is well thought-out. I'd probably stay there again, I would not recommend it to anyone who doesnt like to travel light.

“Great hotel in a great location” I've stayed quite a few times and while the elevators and slow and a couple of the reception staff aren't very friendly, I have enjoyed the clean comfortable rooms and nothing beats the location. Parking is a short walk. Loading and unloading in front of the hotel is not easy but one only does that upon arrival and departure. Close to shops and restaurants.

“One of the better Four Points” I was hesitant to stay at this hotel based on recent TripAdvisor reviews mentioning renovation and construction noise from across the street. However, upon staying here on a weekday, there was no renovation (it may be complete as of this posting?) and there was no construction going on across the street (though this could have been a one day anomaly). We received a room that faced the courtyard with no views beside overlooking the HVAC units. We didn't get too much street noise, but we could hear the light hum of traffic from the main street nearby. The room appeared clean and pretty nicely renovated. Parking was $12, which appears to be average for that area. The hotel is located a few blocks from a 24 hour grocery store as well as some really nice restaurants. It is also close enough to walk to the Seattle Center to visit the museum and/or the Space Needle. Definitely would stay here again for the price.
“Great deal at San Diego's Pacific Beach!” Well worth looking at for your San Diego vacation. Family friendly. Good value. Right on the Beach.

“Kleines Hotel in Manhattan” Das BW Convention Center Hotel liegt in der Nähe des Hudson River in Midtown, Manhattan. Zu Fuss sind es etwa 15 min zum Times Square. Die nächste Subway-Haltestelle (Portauthority) liegt etwa 10 min entfernt. Das Hotel ist mit 10 Stockwerken eines der kleineren Hotels in Manhattan. Die Zimmer und Badezimmer sind sehr sauber, allerdings auch sehr klein. Aber in New York ist man ohnehin ja nur zum Schlafen da. Das Frühstück ist typisch continental. Bagel, Danishes, Marmelade und Cereals sowie Kaffee und Orangensaft. Reicht für einen Start in den Tag auf jeden Fall aus. Wer keinen großen Wert auf eine Lage absolut im Zentrum legt, für den ist dieses Hotel sicherlich eine gute Wahl.

“Great Location” Right in theater district. Waling distance to all theaters. Request a room in back so as to avoid the noise on 8th Ave. If you are a Hilton Honors Gold, you will get free breakfast vouchers for restaurant next door. Good. Staff VERY helpful.

“Great location, beautiful room, good food” I stayed here for 4 nights in early August 2012. I had a good rate from Expedia. I was upgraded from a Queen to a King bedded room. The room was large, well furnished, with lots of closets with full length mirrored doors and a huge bathroom with both separate shower and bathtub. The toiletries are high-end French. The bed is bit too soft and fluffy for my taste but that is just a personal preference and not a criticism of the room. I loved the location just off Times Square for the convenience to multiple subway lines, shopping on Fifth Ave. and the numerous good dining options (DB Bistro Moderne almost next door and a good diner just a half block away). I had breakfast and dinner at the hotel's French restaurant and it was not expensive and very good. Housekeeping was extremely efficient. Everytime I put out the make-up the room sign, it seems the room is always made up within the hour or so that I am away from the room. There is also a good sized gym in the basement with enough equipment for a good workout even if you prefer weight training to cardio like I do. All in all, I had a great stay, no complaints and would definitely stay at the Sofitel again as long as the price was right.

“Would stay here again” This was a nice hotel, right downtown, where I needed to be for a meeting at the Convention Center. The room was large. It had a refridgerator AND a microwave oven. You need that to heat up your leftovers...there's no morning room service. There is FREE high-speed internet access!! Colleaugues who stayed at the Marriot had to pay $10/hour for internet. One negative...the fitness center was mediocre at best. One working treadmill, one old, tired weight machine thing and some other aerobic machines. Okay, so there were TVs in the fitness room. Extra bonus, the people in Philadelphia that I met (Hilton hotel staff, street vendors, taxis, museum workers, etc.) were ALL friendly. What a pleasnt city!

“Great value” The room was clean, the furniture was shabby but serviceable, the bed very comfy, and the shared bathrooms clean but basic and small. The hall to my room smelled strongly of cigarette smoke, fortunately my room did not. The staff was about average, the continental breakfast less than average. Messages and mail delivered promptly, bags stowed without complaint. The location was ideal. Being a residential street meant that it was so quiet you didn’t even realize you were in a big city. I can understand why this is a residential hotel, the neighborhood is very inviting. It is an easy walk to the heart of the village and to Washington Square, lots of good restaurants and bars to keep you entertained and convenient public transportation. I’d return simply because it was above average for the price.

“Absolutely perfect for my needs” This hotel had everything I needed for a quick (two-night) business trip: * Free Wi-Fi (which worked flawlessly) * Clean, quiet and comfortable room * Up-to-date furnishings (no worn-out floral bedspreads!) * Good lighting and plenty of counter space in the bathroom * Fitness room with a choice of a few cardio machines * Free and well-stocked breakfast * Very friendly staff * Free business center with two computers and printer (which I used) * Great location -- convenient to Times Square and surrounding locations Here's a tip -- I almost didn't find this hotel because I was using Expedia to search for two rooms, and it didn't come up in the listings. I think that's because the Comfort Inn system only lets you book one room at a time. In the future I'll search for single rooms...

“W gets a B” W is doing something right. Once a trendsetter in popularizing boutique hotels, W is now on the tamer side of progressiveness, but don’t tell that to the mob in the lobby. While some hotels are conceived as a home away from home, I think of the W as a nightclub with beds upstairs. From the moment you walk in (and regardless of the hour) you’re enveloped by the thump-thump-thumping of music, an organic lounge seating area that begs you to check out who’s who, and no shortage of hipsters who collectively turn and check you out as you pass through the door and then dismissively return to their small talk. You don’t get that at the Westin across the street. In San Francisco, the W will always be relevant because of its location. I stayed there because it was directly across from Moscone, and for a convention there’s simply no better place. The dichotomy between badge-wearing conventioneers and twentysomethings is a little awkward, but it makes for interesting social mixing. If you’re going boutique, I’d put the W SF several rungs below the Hudson in NY or Delano in Miami Beach or any of their brethren. It remains more homey, however, than the stark modernism of the new St. Regis next door or Intercontinental one block down. The room worked for me. Smallish (no surprise), it was more residential and quirky than I expected. I liked the playful accessories – the foot massager under the desk (every hotel should have one), the glowing Buddha, the kaleidoscope, the bench running the width of the room along the window with the block of wood as a step, the wealth of stationery and things with clever phrases on them. The bathroom was fine – I like the Bliss products – tangy without being silly. The bed was heavenly as expected. On the other hand, the plantation shutters make absolutely no sense in a city hotel – you’re stuck with them blocking your view in the middle of the window if you open them, they don’t black out the light, and they’re a pain if you’re sitting on the bench presumably trying to look out the window at the fantastic skyline. The clock radio was too cool for its own good – I prefer digital clocks with the correct time that I can read in the dark instead of a 50’s style form-follows-form piece. The room was too dark and turning the lights on (and the Buddha off) required more reconnaissance than necessary. And finally, the $14.95 for internet access in Downtown San Francisco is frankly insulting to Steve Jobs and everyone else who made Silicon Valley what it is - even a B&B in Vermont gives it to you for free these days. Guys, charge another buck at the bar if you have to. Downstairs, the food was good in the restaurant and the prices reasonable, the fitness center serviceable, the pool a welcomed surprise and their kiosk to print out boarding passes very handy. The service was fine, nothing exceeded my expectations but no disappointments either. The free Acura shuttle was perhaps the most memorable part of my stay, they swept me away to an outstanding Greek restaurant for dinner - Kokkari Estiatorio – splendid lamb chops. My one recommendation to W is to change up the music in the morning so that it doesn’t feel like I have a hangover in Vegas when I’m coming down in the elevator. All in all, a pretty seamless stay. All the reliability of a Starwood corporate standard with a touch of edginess for the young and the young at heart.

“A good place to stay in NYC” Several improvements are being made to this hotel..the lobby , rooms, eating areas...etc...so you may see some constructions through July I am told. I stayed in one of the renovated rooms, with the new decor and furnishings. The rooms are much more functions with access to at least 10 electrical outlets, and inputs into the TV. Speaking of the TV, there are flat screens, but now HD channels. The beds are extremely comfortable, great pillows too.There is also now a small refrigerator in the room as well. As with other stay in this hotel, the bathrooms are very small, barely enough room for one person to maneuver in (something that really cant be fixed)..more shelve space than the past but it blocks access to the sink, in order to rinse my face after shaving I had to get back in the shower...crazy stuff...The drawers in the cabinet are very small, and there is no suitcase rack that will fit a larger suitcase, so I had to use the desk chair. The couch in the new sitting area is uncomfortable, more for looks I guess I would gladly stay here in the future and expect to in late June, hopefully I dont get a room below a floor being renovated as that woke me up each morning at 7am or earlier.

“Nice hotel” This is the second time at this hotel. Service was very good, room was well appointed and clean. Beds were comfortable. Used the pool during a previous visit and it also has a great layout. Entrance area and lobby area are updated and very inviting.

“First-rate service” The Blackwell adjoins the OSU Business school and is within sight of the stadium. First-rate rooms & service. I didn't sample any of the nearby restaurants, but can testify that the rooms are huge, everything works, tea & coffee apparatus in each room and a very helpful staff.

“The Best!” Needed one night close to airport. The price was right and the Hyatt was amazing! The price was lower than a lot of lower class hotels. Great staff, loved the room, quiet, quick trip to airport, safe location.......I plan to stay again next weekend.

“It truly was a home away from home experience.” We had to book a hotel on the north side of Indianapolis because my son was having surgery at the Methodist Sports Medicine hospital. We booked the Homewood Suites because I knew it was like an apartment with a separate bedroom and sitting room plus a full kitchen because I knew we wouldn't be able to eat out after the surgery. But we ended up not needing the kitchen because this hotel provided COMPLIMENTARY breakfast AND dinner (called the manager's reception which is only Mon-Fri). I can't tell you how great it was just to go downstairs to fix a plate for my son while my husband watched over him. And the food was GREAT! For breakfast....name something, they had it. (Try the blueberry scones!) Dinner that night was lasagna, garlic bread and veggies. Salad had plenty of extras and a variety of dressings. They had fresh lemonade....and free beer and wine. It was incredible. What a value! The cost of the room is what you'd pay for any decent hotel with complimentary breakfast so to get two really decent meals and very nice rooms with great beds....well you're not going to get better than this. My husband travels alot for business and has a bad back...so is extremely picky. He was very happy with this hotel. The couch and chair in the sitting room isn't the greatest but the beds are very good, high quality. The rest of the furnishings are beautiful....bathroom is huge, water is hot, lighting and internet are great. A/C runs quiet. Every member of the staff we ran into were friendly and helpful. We especially appreciated the front desk letting us check in early....we had just flown in and were tired. The drive to the airport from this hotel is not bad either because the hotel is right off the freeway exit. Of course you'd never know it while you're inside the hotel because it's so quiet. There was construction going on on 465 S so it slowed us down so it took us about 1/2 hour. But I wouldn't do the drive in rush hour. When we left the hospital to go to the Homewood Suites (which is just a couple miles away from it) it was 5 pm and the traffic was horrendous on that freeway. Also you are across the parking lot from Cracker Barrel which always has great food. Considering the stress of the trip (worrying about my son and his pain), this was a GREAT experience. It was as close you could be to being home....a really nice home!

“Great room, Bad services and Weird elevators!” We has a reunion at the hotel. We loved the location, very conveniently connecting to Galleria Mall. The rooms were spacious with comfy beds and roomy bath. The flaw of the hotel was its personnel. Front desk clerks did not know where the pool is, unhelpful with arranging for transportation to airports. Concierge men showed non guests how to use the weird elevators to get to the floors without concerning of safety. The elevators had no button inside. No compliment WIFI either !!!

“Heavenly Hyatt - Room Upgrade Worth Every Penny” When I arrived to this hotel (which is the largest hotel on the Eastern side of the US - like a Las Vegas hotel it's so big!!) I was offered an upgrade to a room with a view for $20. I reluctantly took it but was so glad I did - the river view was absolutely breathtaking. I loved EVERYTHING about my room. The darkening curtains, the amazingly comfortable bed, the renovated room ... it was all perfection. Some things you'll probably want to know about: - internet was $16/day which was pretty pricey ... they said there was free wi-fi in the lobby but I never had any luck. I went to the corner bakery just a few steps away though and had a great salad and free wi-fi - The breakfast buffet is amazing and for $15 for continental it's actually not a bad value considering how much other than cereal and breads were available. I was very happy plus there's a great store/coffee shop in the main level that sells yogurt parfaits, cereals, coffees, and snacks for a decent price. - The location is awesome. Boat tours across the street, Michigan Mile across the street and easy access to lots of theatre and culture. The sunset tour boat cruise was AWESOME. $28 for 2 hours on the boat and I learned so much about the interesting buildings. - The gym is massive - LOTS of cardio equipment and weights. If there is a big conference in town I could see how the gym could be super busy but it was ok when I was there. My only complaint is how you have to parade through the hotel to get to it - down the escalators and through a bunch of doors and down a hallway but it was a great gym. If you want a small cozy hotel this is NOT your place. With over 2000 rooms it's seriously massive - but the staff were friendly (one guy even escorted me to the gym the first time when I got lost), and it's truly beautiful and convenient.

“Decent Hotel...room less so” This is not your typical Marriott Renaissance. The place has been remodeled. That said, a new rug, paint and headboards do not equal 'new'. Overall the experience was ok. Check in went quickly. There were two clerks. Lots of activity in the hotel as it was the day before the Super Tuesday Primary (this hotel is right around the corner from the Ohio State Capital.) The lobby is clean, no complications get tot eh desk, get the keys and move to the elevators. Te elevators were apparently not part of the multimillion dollar refurbishment- they had scratches and dings, even on the ceiling. The ride was quick and direct. I was assigned a room on the 12th floor. All rooms are within a quick walk of the elevator. The initial entry way of the room was dark, and uninviting. There was the coffee pot and 2 water bottles (for $5). The rooms are configured very tight. See the photos. Desk, TV, sitting area are all within 7 feet!! The rooms HVAC was sub-par. It could not get warmer no matter how hhigh the setting was placed. And it was loud. The fitness room was great, clean, comfortable. Sauna, it was worth the workouts. Plenty of machines to keep the place moving. Bathroom is really a tight fit. sink, shower (no bath) toilet on top of each other. It is so close that the rom has a split door because the room cannot accommodate a regular door. The shower water was cold at 6am. That is unacceptable. The lobby restaurant Latitude 41 is a exceptional restaurant. Small plates (i.e., mix and match your entrees) with reasonable prices and a continental trained Chef. Service could have been more attentive, but heck, for the prices this place has for the quality of the food, I'll take it.

“Felt welcomed and good customer service.” This hotel has recently added some upgrades to the suites and it shows. Flat screen TVs are in both the "living room" and the bedroom. There is a min fridge and microwave in the rooms. Recently added, in the last month are iPod docking stations. This was much appreciated after a long day of driving and listening to my iPod. I was able to charge it overnight and not have to search for my charger immediately. Mattresses could use an upgrade though. Not the best. Some fun restaurants are in walking distance along with places for shopping and if you don't want to walk to catch a baseball game there are other available means to get you there. Beware of the $32.00 a day for parking. While this does entitle one to leave as often during the day as needed, it is a little inconvienent and the added expense of tipping the Valet. Customer service was great. I called once there to get exact directions and they were very helpful and then I checked out a day earlier and no charges were applied for the day I cancelled. Would stay here again.

“Tolles Hotel in hervorragender Lage” Da US gRant liegt mitten im Herzen von San Diego. Von hier aus läuft man nur über die Strasse in das Gas Lamp Quarter hinein und ist mitten in der Restaurant und Barszene gelandet. Per Auto erreicht man alle anderen Sehenswürdigkeiten ebenfalls bequem in kurzer Zeit. Die Zimmer sind toll und die Eingangshalle ist beeindruckend.

“Quality Service and Common Space but rooms lacking” This hotel has a very historic building with great character. The common areas and service levels were all very nice. The level of service from staff is quality and as expected from Ritz. That said, the rooms were lackluster at best. Not only were they lacking in the quality one might expect from a room rate of 400/night. In addition to being extremely loud rooms (traffic noise etc) the bathrooms were very odd in that they had no tables to lay out your personal items, etc. I would not stay here again as the quality was not there for me for the cost, however, if you seek high service levels...this is a certainly present.

“Location and service exceed expectations” My husband and I stayed here 4 nights and were very impressed with the room size, service, free amenities and location. The hotel has no in house restaurant but can arrange dinner at the Magic Castle Club (including free transportation) and it is a block to Hollywood Blvd. and many, many restaurants. Free continental breakfast is offered every morning. The bed was very comfortable and the suite was very clean. Dinner and shows at the Magic Castle Club are recommended to all ages - the shows are unbelieveable!! This is not a luxurious place but definitely a 'home away from home' with better service!

“Loved the Dumont” What an awsome place to stay!!! Four of stayed at the Dumont from 6/11-6/17/08 and the service can not get any better anywhere. The rooms are huge by NYC standards. They gave us a beautiful view on the 33rd floor of the river. It was breathtaking!!! Rooms are so clean and the kitchen is an extra bonus. Nice to have a place to keep bottled water cold and left over food. Sara Candee you are a wonderful person and so caring. Thank you for all you did for us. We will be staying with you when we return to NYC hopefully during the holidays. Everybody at this hotel gives top notch service. They give you good choices of where to eat. The location is awsome right in the heart of Murray Hill. Close enough to TImes Square, but enough distance to enjoy some down time when returning to your room. Thank you for an awsome stay!!! The Toth's

“Successful mix of traditional and trendy” If you've stayed at other W Hotels, you know that they are trendy. This one is a bit more interesting because the structure (old Hotel Washington I think) is very traditional. But it works and it is a very cool place. Pros: Stylish, comfortable and clean rooms. Decent bathroom with cool shower. Amazing views (Monuments, memorials, White House) from the penthouse level lounge. Outstanding staff that manage to be friendly and professional at the same time. The proximity to the Metro was pretty good (couple of blocks). Cons: The room is small. If you are looking for space, you might need to think about a different hotel. The location is both a positive and negative. It's centrally located, but the area itself is not the best DC neighborhood for dining or just getting a snack. Overall, if the smaller room size doesn't bother you, it's a great place to stay in DC.

“Predictably Hyatt Place. That's good.” I'll preface this review by saying I'm unfamiliar with Memphis; my visit was part of a road-trip focused on sampling BBQ in as many Southern states as possible. (Prince Pit BBQ in Bardwell, Kentucky and Payne's in Memphis - do it if you can, friends.) The property isn't particularly convenient to anything except St. Francis Medical Center, directly across the street. There may well be better-located lodgings for your needs. Still, Memphis isn't LA, and driving downtown or to other destinations in town wasn't a big deal. If you're not familiar with the Hyatt Place formula, it's easy to distill: Hyatt Place is to Best Western what Target is to WalMart. The "gallery" includes the front desk, and features a bar, limited menu, grab-n-go and a decent continental breakfast. There are comfortable places to relax, socialize or work. Rooms are nicely updated, and the living / seating area is actually comfortable and useable enough to keep me working there instead of from bed. Staff is great. Friendly, helpful and casually professional. Next trip to Memphis, I'll consider another hotel closer to the things I plan to visit. I certainly wouldn't be unhappy at this hotel, though, and with the internet-only rate it's a solid value. Free wifi, but it can be a bit slow.

“Good Business Traveler Choice” This a good choice considering its a Four Points and not a Ritz Carlton. Pros: Free parking, free internet, newly appointed rooms, brand new workout room, close to airport, 10 minutes from downtown, and next to light rail. Cons: Uncomfortable pillows, no quality dining options nearby, small bathroom and was difficult to find hotel since its behind an office strip mall. There's not many quality hotels near the airport but this one works and would stay again.

“Modern, Clean, Reliable Business-Oriented Hotel, but Slightly Noisy” I stayed here for three nights in the summer on vacation and was pleased overall with my stay. This is the best hotel I've stayed in looking back over recent years, and I'm glad I shelled out the extra dollars. There were some small nuances and quirks about the location which prevented me from giving it an "excellent" rating, but I would definitely be willing to recommend this hotel depending on what a traveler is in Denver for. The location has it's good and bad parts. One good part is that it is near the 16th Street Mall, and the 16th Street Mall has free shuttles that run up and down the long road all day long. So, if you're walking around downtown and are getting tired, as long as you can make it to the 16th Street Mall, you can hop on the shuttle and get off on the street that the Residence Inn is on. The whole area has plenty of food options, mostly chain restaurants and lunch places like The Cheesecake Factory and Corner Bakery.
