There is a 711 right across the street from this hotel and a Walgreen's is nearby, so you won't have to worry about going without any toiletries you may have forgotten to pack. The bad part in my opinion is that the 16th Street Mall has its mix of people and to me looked like it could be very shady at night. Sometimes even during the day when walking back to my hotel there would be pretty rough looking individuals waiting for the bus. I figured the area would be filled with business travelers since the description on the hotel's website makes it seem like it's right next to the convention center. I think the Grand Hyatt was closer to the convention center, but yes, you can walk there. As for the hotel itself, it's a real convenience to have a microwave and refrigerator, something most regular hotels don't have nowadays or want to charge for. My studio suite was huge. The bathroom is narrow, but it is long and fairly clean. The kitchen was clean besides some filth between the refrigerator and counter space (something most people wouldn't even notice). These are very small issues that were not worth complaining about, but one of my bathroom towels did have specks of hair in it, the bathroom floor had a strand of hair on it, and the remote was kind of grimy. I just made sure to not put my hand all over the remote, and I asked the front desk for another bath towel. It was sort of annoying that the front desk staff person claimed they had no towels at all back there, but I used my other ones and the next day got some more. For the money paid it would be nice if their staff made sure hair wasn't in the towel, but I guess that's why these places are called hotels and not homes. In general, it was a clean room with a couple of quirks. The bed seemed fine and comfy enough and my windows had the refreshing view of downtown highrises versus what I'm used to getting stuck with like looking at some garbage or heater. My biggest issue was the noise in the building; I think this is one of the noisiest hotels I've stayed in, and I don't mean hearing people talking. I kept hearing what I would liken to someone dropping a bag of basketballs, but it sounded like the sound was coming from beneath me which is odd. There was a gym on the floor below me (which was pretty nice) but it seems odd that even if people are dropping weights that I'd hear it that well vs. the people on the 7th floor (the gym is on the 8th floor and I was on the 9th). This sound was pretty constant and got worse from the day into the night, really drumming up after 10 pm and I'd gone to the gym at night before and not seen anyone in there. I would also hear what sounded like water running, A LOT. The first night it was bearable, but the second and third night it was miserable. It would wake me up around 6:00 AM. I didn't complain for a new room because by the time it really began to annoy me I didn't have much left of my stay. I'm not sure if it was the gym or housekeeping staff or just other guests. I guess the walls are pretty thin; maybe it depends on which side of the hotel you are on and what floor. I think I may have used my earplugs one night. Besides the hair in the towel and noise I was happy with my stay, but probably wouldn't come back to this particular hotel because I prefer to sleep in peace and quiet. The continental breakfast spread is so-so, I thought it could have had more variety for the rate of the hotel, but it was better than others and maybe they figure guests can cook too since they have a kitchen. I guess I was there during many business trips because the space was kind of tight where they keep the food in the kitchen behind the hotel bar. There is juice, tea, coffee, meat, cereal, oatmeal, and mix to make waffles. They also have complimentary light finger foods and wine and beer in the evening which I thought was awesome. I didn't eat the food, but enjoyed the fact that it was there if I wanted it. There is a Caribou nearby for any coffee drinkers who don't like the hotel's coffee. It was a little irritating that you have to re-sign back in to the wifi network every 24 hours, but I guess it's a security precaution so I should be more patient and understanding. Overall, no big complaints and a successful stay.

“EXCELLENT” a bit over priced but a super nice place. Home of the parker house rolls, and boston cream pie. walking distance to almost anything you could want to see. 3-4 blocks from Cheers, 6 blocks Quincy market

“Pricy, Pretty Hotel with a few flaws” My wife, teenage daughter and I stayed at the new Hotel Wilshire over Christmas, 2011. We basically liked the place, but my wife was very disappointed at the short, shallow pool. She needs to swim several times a week for health reasons, and felt that the picture of the pool on the website had been misleading (as they so often are). It's more of a recreational pool for people at the rooftop bar (nice view, pricy drinks, didn't try the restaurant with the celebrity chef). Otherwise, the place was pretty good. We had a minisuite with a sofabed, for which we paid well north of $200, listed as a discount rate--it was sort of a special occasion trip for us. But the main bed was big and very comfortable, even the sofabed wasn't bed--though it left a very tight passage in the room when it was open. The "rain" shower was excellent, and the bathroom area was helpfully divided up into shower stall, toilet room, and a sink/dressing area--though the shower and toilet didn't have opaque doors (there's a sliding door between the whole bathroom and the rest of the room). There were two giant TVs with plugs for video devices. A refrigerator but no microwave, and no radios or clocks! We had to light up our cell phones to check the time in the middle of the night. Parking was $26, plus 10% parking tax. Ironically, we had to park there because we'd driven down but were trying to do as much of the visit car-free as possible--we did that for most of it. If we'd been using the car constantly we could have parked in a two hour parking spot on a neighboring street--not on Wilshire Boulevard. Transit service is good there, with frequent buses along Wilshire Boulevard out to Beverly Hills and Santa Monica and in to Koreatown and Downtown, and good service on Fairfax Ave. (one long block away) as well. The hotel is across the street from a minimall with numerous restaurants--including pretty good Caffe Latte--but because we arrived at Christmastime they weren't open much. The Farmers Market (and Grove Shopping Center) is a bit under a mile walk, certainly possible if you're a reasonably good walker.

“Charming Characteristic With Convenience” The Prescott Hotel in San Francisco definitely is a small hotel situated near Union Square. The building is about 7 floors high which doesn't have a great view at all. You will have to keep your curtain drawn for privacy. Otherwise, the people in the building next door can look through their windows to see your every move. I have heard a lot of negative feedback about the Prescott Hotel which even made me more curious to find out if the claims of previous guests are true. Because this hotel is fairly small compared to other hotels in the area, you can be guaranteed that the service provided by their staff is of the highest level possible. Some people have said that the hotel rooms are so small. True, SOME rooms are rather small. However, they also have bigger rooms, ie, Executive King Suites and more. Ever wonder why this hotel can charge a lot for a small room? BECAUSE THE PRESCOTT HOTEL IS VERY LUXURIOUS AND YOU CAN BE SURE THAT YOUR PROBLEM IS DEALT WITH EXPEDIENTLY. Just a quick tip: Ask for Patricia at the front desk. She is very professional and she makes sure that your issue gets resolved immediately. The other Asian front desk clerk needs more training. She has no customer service skill. She had me standing right in front of her while she answer the phone, and when she is done with the phone she starts calling someone on her walkie talkie and answers another phone call and carried on another conversation through her walkie talkie. I was standing in front of her for a good 20 minutes without talking to me. When Patricia saw me waiting, she immediately helped me with my request and inquiry. It only took a couple of minutes. Overall, my experience at the Prescott hotel was above average. All the other extra amenities made my hotel stay very nice. I will definitely stay at the Prescott Hotel again. THANKS TO PATRICIA.

“Really great design hotel with tons of nice little extras” I can only second the great reviews. Excellent designed room with a little sofa and a super-comfortable bed. Yes, the bathroom is a bit small, but the sink, shower and everything are nicely designed and the water pressure is good. There was no shower gel in my bathroom, only soap, but when I asked with a little note, next day there was. There is even an international plug adapter in the room, bathrobes, an ipod docking station, minibar. The reception desk is happy to call jazz clubs and restaurants for you to make a reservation and is helpful with personal suggestions that go beyond the usual "Blue Note" and "Cipriani" suggestions heard elsewhere. Breakfast buffet really good for a buffet included in the price! Bagels, cereals, fruit, yogurt, juice, all there. Free newspaper in the morning, and free Time Out and other magazines. E-mail with discounted upgrade offer two days before arrival. My only criticism: I do not think that it is appropriate to charge $10 for wireless for 24 hours. But thanks to the level of design and particularly all these other little extras, for once I am not complaining at all. Fully recommended! Particularly at that price!

“"Soaking in Seattle"” This is a great hotel that is located in the central area of downtown Seattle. The staff are superb, helpful and very polite. The room I had was very spacous and clean and the bed was to die for. Would I stay here again if I were coming back to Seattle, no doubt I would. Located beneath the hotel is the Elephant & Castle pub, the food here is very good, wholesome and filling, the bar staff helpful, polite and very friendly, a great place to go. A tip about coming to Seattle, pack an umbrella in your bag.

“Cancelled flight. Saved by the Sheraton.” Our flight to DFW (Dallas) was cancelled at 1615. Because we booked through that flight and hotel through Expedia and not through the property directly, we still had to pay for the room (Comfort Inn) in Dallas (Expedia DID try to appeal the decision with the hotel). We decided to book Sheraton in Houston on our own and will think twice about third party, pre-charged bookings (as the savings were not that significant anyway). Good location and not riddled with aircraft flying overhead. Check-in was fast. Lobby bar had festivities from 1800-1900hrs. Excellent food and great service in the lounge. Decent restaurant on site. Health club was good, though runners complained it was too hot (it was unseasonably hot in Houston). The indoor pool was too short for me for swimming lengths, so it's more of a splash around pool. Bed was good, lots of pillows. USA Today delivered in the AM. Shuttle on-time at 0440hrs for the airport. I would stay here again.

“Fit for a King” The Lobby is a bit dated. The reception desk is overstaffed and that was great. The staff is a bit detached for such an outstanding property. The rest is royally great! The room is well appointed and very large. Everything works properly it has a remote control system which turns all lights off and even lets the housekeeping know if service or privacy are desired. They shine your shoes for free every night. The bed is as comfortable as there is. The location is outstanding with easy access to the best of Manhattan.

“Pool ist absolut toll” Dieses Holiday Inn hat meiner Meinung nach einen durchschnittlichen Service zu bieten. Die Zimmer sind nicht gerade neu, aber einigermassen gut eingerichtet und sauber. Was ich bei diesem Hotel absolut zu schätzen mochte ist der grosse Pool auf der Terrasse im 17. Stock des Hotels. Das hat nicht manches Hotel in New York zu bieten.

“Great Location and nice hotel” The actual hotel is situated in an old building but has oviously been renovated to bring it up to date. Personally we like this type of hotel as they maintain more character than some of the modern types of building. Our room was well maintained and clean but decoration wise it looked basic and a little tired. Our king size bed was comfortable and the en suite bathroom was a decent size.We purchased our deal on an air/hotel package and elected to pay a little more for a deluxe room in order to have a little more space than normally acquired from a standard New York hotel room. The deal was well worth the money for our three night stay and the extra room cost was well spent. The hotel lobby is spacious, and the staff who we met were helpful and courteous. Within the lobby there is a restaurant area as well as a bar. We did not use the restaurant but I did have a small beer at the bar and even based on New York prices the cost for this appeared to be expensive. Like some other older hotels it is built on a two wing basis, east & west so make sure that you enter the correct elevator for your room area. Again like older hotels the west wing elevators could only be reached by using a small flight of stairs so beware if you have a lot of luggage. Nothing to worry about but a ramp would be of some assistance. Location wise it is situated between Park Avenue and Lexington in mid town Manhattan and is therefore well appointed for all of the tourist sites whether it be on foot or by transport. There is a subway station situated within a five minute walk and Grand Central is virtually on the doorstep. We find that New York is best explored on foot but do not be afraid to use the subways as taxi rides can take a while to get through the traffic. All in all we enjoyed our stay at the Intercontinental Barclay but I can see that it would not be to everyone's taste.

“Nur wenn man die Gegend kennt!” Einen Tag bevor wir im Palomar ankamen wollten wir eine Auskunft via Mail erhalten. Nach einem Mail an den Concierg und einem Mail an das Hotel und keiner Antwort musste ich 3 Mal dort anrufen, da ich immer wieder aus der Leitung gekickt wurde. Diese Anruferei kostete mich 18$, aber das schien dem Hotel egal. Als wir am nächsten Tag eine Erkundungstour machen wollten und einige spezifischen Auskünfte einholen wollten verbrachten wir ca. eine halbe Stunde am Front Desk, ohne ein Resultat erhalten zu haben. Nicht einmal richtige Gebietskarten o.ä. sind ausgedruckt und für die Gäste als Beschreibungshilfe bereit. Zimmer sind schön, sauber und trendy. Lichtblick war Putzfrau die uns bei ihrem ersten Tag ein Zettelchen hinterlegt hat und uns einen schönen Aufenthalt wünschte. Ich kann dieses Hotel nur empfehlen, wenn man die Gegend kennt oder man dort geschäftlich zu tun hat.

“Perfect convention property” Stayed here April 7 - 11. Attended a conference held in the hotel. This property is in a great location in downtown Seattle, in easy walking distance to Pike's Place Market, Pacific Place shopping, the Convention Center, and the monorail to the Space Needle. It is an older property, but the only way to guess that is due to the slightly smaller bedroom and bathroom sizes, along with the narrow corridors on the floor levels, along with the small number of rooms on each floor. All walls, tiles, linens and furnishings were clean and modern, presenting a nice decor. Bathrooms were equipped with Crabtree & Evelyn Le Source toiletries (my favorite!). Rooms start on floor 14 (which I was on) and run through floor 28, with the restaurant on the 29th floor. Three elevators provided smooth and speedy service. Another plus - to access any guest floor, and room key was required, helping make a single traveler feel safe. The meeting rooms were spacious and the hotel staff kept refreshments aplenty. Breakfast and lunch each day in the restaurant was an unexpected gourmet treat - much more elegant than normally required for informal meals. The restaurant had a spectacular view of Puget Sound and when the sky was clear, the Olympic Mountains. The view was easily seen from any seating area. The bar area also had a menu but I didn't eat there - but the bar was large with a cozy decor. The concierge was friendly and helpful. One night she made a reservation for me at Cutter's Restaurant, making sure the restaurant would provide me complimentary transportation for my return to the hotel. At the restaurant, I was given an appetizer, courtesy of the concierge. Also, I needed a 4:15am town car pick up for the airport my last day and the concierge booked me with a company, saving me $15 off the most affordable transportation I found on my own on the internet. My only disappointment was the business center - very small and a $6 fee for use. Most hotels now offer this as a complimentary service. Maybe the Seattle Hilton will change this soon. Thanks for a great four nights, I slept very well!

“A little tired but Impeccable service makes this gem still sparkle!” I used to be a Regency regular from the mid-90s 'til about 2001 so I couldn't wait to return nearly a decade later to see what, if anything had changed. Some recent snotty reviews on Trip Advisor had me worried. I was relieved to discover that many of my favorite room service and bell staff are still working at the hotel, a sign that The Regency must be a good place to work - having a content and stable staff is paramount to creating a hotel experience that feels like home... The lobby and gym are every bit as nice as I'd remembered and while I did see the same scuff marks that several guests have complained about, I really didn't mind that the room looked a bit tired and worn. I'd liken it to visiting NYC and staying with your favorite old, monied yet slightly hip uncle - sure, things aren't going to be totally brand new, but that's part of the charm. And just like that favorite uncle, the staff welcome you with a smile and a welcome back - I was surprised that even the male room service operator remembered me and asked how I'd been doing (even though we haven't talked in at least 7 or 8 years!) From the front desk staff to the maids, the impeccable staff makes this place a winner... And if you don't mind lots of Texans with giant fur coats on the elevator this time of year, The Regency will no doubt leave you with a smile. The one disappointment was that they've somehow changed the receipe of their once renowned crab cakes to the point that they were inedible on the room service menu. And I don't understand how they feel like it's okay to charge more than $20 for a bowl of berries for breakfast! That said, everything else I ordered was perfect and delivered in a prompt and courteous way. I look forward to my next trip... it feels like you're seeing old friends and family when you walk through the doors of the Loews Regency Hotel!

“LOCATION” Location is perfect, but not all the rooms are fine. The first day we were on a room on the 3rd floor with an ugly interior view, no hot water, and they were not able to change the room till the next day,we had an interior regular view on the 10th floor, and everything was ok, nice amenities and free soft drinks on the fridge. Bad wi fi signal on both rooms. Jummeirah essex house is a much better option with same location and very similar prices.

“Many Issues, but a Great Location. OK (loud) Rooms, Good Service” Intercontinental Hotels are usually above average. The service, food choices and great location make this a crowded and popular hotel. The problem is pretty IMPORTANT though... most rooms are very dated and can be very very loud. Upgraded to a renovated "old tower" room and it was still pretty dated and LOUD. The micro-thin windows served as little protection (even on 15th floor) from the extreme street noise that echoed off the u-shaped building. I rarely wake up to street noise--but some rooms here can get very loud. The bed was so-so and I did not find it a great sleep. For an upgraded King room--it was still quite small. With a room service cart in the room, I had trouble moving around. TV is newer, internet was good. Staff was very friendly. I ordered rooms service a couple times and the food was good, well above average. They messed up one of my orders (Coke vs. Diet Coke), but I was generally impressed with the room service and staff. GREAT location on Michigan Ave near lots of SHOPPING and river cruises. Nordstrom is right across the street. If you want a 5-Star experience in Chicago, do the Peninsula or Ritz or Four Seasons. But for a business hotel, this one is pretty standard. It just can't give more than three stars to a hotel where I get a really bad nights rest. The primary point of a hotel. Michael Jordan Steakhouse is in lobby and there is a lot nearby too. If you stay here--be aware of these items and make sure you get a good rate. Otherwise, there are better options.

“great hotel, great location” Loved this place. The hotel is brand new, so everything looks good. Staff was great. I was expecting the free daily breakfast to be bagels and coffee. Not at all. It's way better than any free hotel breakfast I've ever had. Only complaint I can come up with is the A/C vent in the room is located in the back corner of the bedroom, so it doesn't circulate very well throughout the suite. That's the only complaint I can think of though, which means we loved it. The location is outstanding. A block and a half from 16th street and less to the convention center. I definitely recommend this place.

“Great Value for the $$$” The Empire is a gem. The location is fabulous - near Central Park (and away from the Times Square madness) plus great shopping nearby. Very friendly and professional staff from the front desk to the bartender - everyone was terrific. It's extremely clean and quiet. Comfortable bed, great linens, good workout room, LOVED the free Wi-fi. The Empire is a great value for the price especially in New York. The only negatives were the teeny tiny bathroom with the teak shower floor and the fact that my room was quite warm. I would give it a 5 for cleanliness, but that shower floor :(. I think it's supposed to be chic, but I'm not a fan. That said, I'd definitely visit again. For a more detailed review & photos please check my blog at www.tripscout.blogspot.com.

“Nice place to stay” I have stayed at the Columbus Easton Hilton a couple of times over the years. Overall I think it is one of the nicest hotels in Columbus. My room was clean and the bed was comfortable. I am a big fan of the huge bathroom and shower with nice strong water pressure. Also the towels weren't the typical thin cheap things you get at most hotels anymore, but thick and high quality. I did not interact much with the staff, but when I did they were polite and friendly. That having been said I have a few negatives: One, I have to agree with the previous poster who said the place has gone down slightly over the years. I noticed that the rooms seem a little worn and could use an update. Except for the bathrooms, which are still really good. My biggest complaint is the noise. As others have said, the noise carries into the room and I found it really annoying. You can hear eveything, every door that shuts, every conversation...everything. The walls must be paper thin.

“Great Hotel/Staff is questionable” Location, location, location! If you are in NYC to see the sights and don't mind the crowds of Time Square, this is a great place to spend your time. Affordable rates are avialable via their website and the rooms are very roomy and comfortable for the value. The beds & bath products themselves are reason to stay but be sure to set the alarm or you may sleep your day away. Views are minimal so the extra $$ for a balcony is liklely not worth it. I was surpised to see so many others rave about the service at this hotel. From the concierge to housekeeping, I felt that they were pretentious, uniformative and not very helpful. (yes - we tipped everyone from the moment we arrived and it didn't help) Our maid misplaced personal items in our room and denied touching them, the concierge told us to "walk around" when I asked about someplace with a good wine list, the front desk asked me to bring proof downstairs about our being charged a rate $60 higher than my e-mail confirmation and it took us 3 days and 4 phone calls to recieve the tickets arranged for us by the hotel for a broadway show. (they finally arrived 3.5 hours before curtain but were paid for in full over a week before we arrived) The rooms are a great find but don't expect much from the staff.

“Just Average” We've been to New York several times, but this was our first stay at this W. We had stayed at the Times Square location and we were very impressed with that hotel. This was just an average hotel. It didn't look as modern as some of the newer W hotels, but the price was lower than the others and it's a convenient location. This is the oldest of the W hotels and it's starting to show. The staff were friendly, but not anything near the customer service we experienced at other W hotels. They were just average. The rooms were somewhat disappointing, especially the size. The bed was almost the length of the room. We had the WOW room and it was really tight. The furniture and the bedding looked okay, but again, not as nice or upscale as some other W hotels. The air condition was not very good and the paint around it was peeling. The desk was fine and the bed was comfortable, as usual. The bathroom was small too, and looked somewhat worn. There were some tiles and wallpaper that had been replaced, but the quality of work was very poor. All in all, our stay here was fine, but not as good as you would expect for a W hotel. You might want to consder paying extra for a larger room. We might stay here again, but there are other hotels that we consider as well.

“Would be perfect if it wasn't for the noise” We stayed at the Angeleno for one night. The hotel is conveniently located at the crossing of I-405 and Sunset Blvd. from where you can quickly reach both Santa Monica and Beverly Hills. The convenience of the location comes with the disadvantage of 24/7 noise, though. Upon arrival we were greeted by the friendly valets who took care of our car free of charge (tips excepted of course). As soon as we entered the hotel we were positively impressed by the lobby and by the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff. We were informed about the free wine at 5.30pm every night in the lobby which is a nice touch for a hotel of this category. Having read the reviews before our stay, we asked for a room away from 405 and we were given room 1206 on the 12th floor. It wasn't completely on the other side of the freeway, but almost so. Nevertheless, the noise was noticeable even with the balcony door closed. The room was very nice with the most comfortable bed ever, flat-screen TV, desk, chair, balcony, spacious bathroom with upscale toiletries. It was as good as in most 5 star hotels. When we got back to the room at night, noise had diminished, but only marginally. We could sleep without any problem, though. On the following morning we visited the 17th floor restaurant for breakfast. We found the food to be of great quality and at great price. The views from the restaurant are stunning and we suggest everybody to visit it at least for a drink. The only negative were the 4$ charged for coffee and juice, as others have said, which we found a bit on the steep side. All in all the Angeleno is a very nice property which would deserve a five-star rating, but the noise really is a factor, even if you are not a light sleeper. With better insonorization it would be one of the best hotels in LA for sure.

“Good for Leisure, average for Business Traveleres” There are basically 3 types of Sheratons: 1- Old and not renovated 2- Old but renovated 3- New style Sheratons. This is a new style Sheraton about 4 years old. These new Sheratons are basically glorified upper level motels, and they compete with Marriott Courtyard's and the like. The positive is that they are relatively new and consistent accross properties. If you are on leisure travel then they are ok because you can ignore the negatives, as you are probably getting a good deal on the hotel. If on business...there are shortcommmings. Positives: 1- Friendly front desk 2- Friendly bar/restaurant staff 3- New rooms with large tv's and stand up showers, vs the old tubs 4- Complementary coffee and tee in the lobby in the morning 5- Good location next to a large shopping area (new) 6- VERY comfortable beds and pillows (like all Sheratons!) Negatives: 1- Club not open on Sundays, and *very* minimal service/food items on weekdays, no water 2- Walls paper thin, expect to hear *everything* next door 3- Excersize room is small, and when we were there, no towels 4- No A/C in the elevator, which is a MAJOR problem in Florida where it is routinely high 90's. This is just plain inexplicable. It is close to 100 degrees in that elevator all the time 5- Speaking of A/C's, motel style A/C's in the room, which are noisy. Overall the stay was ok, but I am not a huge fan of these new style Sheratons.

“Great Experience” Too short a visit but great staff, accommodations, service. Will choose Fairmont next time in Dallas! Easily accommodated family of 4 with 2 adjoining rooms. Join the President's club for free internet.

“Am Flughafen, aber auch am Highway” Für eine Nacht habe ich hier im Januar 2012 übernachtet. Nun man bekommt, was man bucht, es war also wirklich ok. Allerdings war es laut, das liegt nicht am nahen Airport, sondern daran, dass es direkt an einem Highway liegt. Die Zimmer sind ok, mehr aber auch nicht, da habe ich schon schönere HIE erlebt. Der Giftshop ist super bestückt zur Nahversorgung und preislich ok!

“Unbeatable!” I stayed at the Gem Hotel and, truly, it was a gem! The staff were very congenial and helpful. It is clean, quiet and well priced. A quick walk gets you to any number of great restaurants. I really hate to share this fantastic spot but if I don't, they may leave. So, when staying for fun or business, they have earned my allegiance as they will earn yours if you stay here.

“An average hotel in a great location” I travel quite regularly on business, which is often in top-notch hotels like the Ritz, Westin and Fairmont. On personal travel, with my family, my choices are quite different...often Embassy Suites, Marriotts, condos, or other suite hotels. I offer this information so that others can assess the range of hotels with which I am familiar. This Marriott has some strong assets: location and view. The noise from the nearby train is not horrendous, at least if you are on the bayside and used to urban sounds. The pool area is quite beautiful, but there is no view of the bay. And seagulls and ducks are the most frequent swimmers in the pool. It is not quite disgusting, but knowing the germs such birds carry, I would personally not allow my children to swim in such a pool. Food is average, as is room size. The North Tower bay room, with a terrace, is pleasant though and appears relatively updated. Bathrooms are very average. View from the terrace is great. Service is fast and solid. Value for the dollar is below average to average.

“Not bad” What one should expect of a Comfort: Wi-Fi and breakfast included, clean enough rooms. Stayed here because it was a about a mile away from where I had business. I'd stay again when in the area, although I would not seek it out. I have no complaints, nothing to brag about either.

“Good value, good location, tired around the edges” I chose this property based upon TripAdvisor reviews and had my expectations adjusted accordingly for a budget experience at $50 per night. On the plus side, the hotel is conveniently located in a city in which car is king ("lonelier than a pedestrian in Dallas" should become a new expression). Staff are very helpful and friendly, for example, a room was not ready when I arrived early and I received a cellphone call just as soon as one was. The room was spacious and clean, the bed was comfortable, the free WiFi speedy, the included breakfast buffet a nice touch. On the minus side, there are signs of wear and tear everywhere. In room 114 the upholstery on the arms of the desk chair is frayed and torn. The plastic bathtub surround has a large, crudely repaired crack around the faucet, which is loose. The public hallway carpet has so many stains it's beginning to look like a leopard print. In sum, come with a "you-get-what-you-pay-for" state of mind and you'll be fine here. Interestingly, the Grand Hotel Dallas (ROFLMAO) just across LBJ Freeway looks just as nice for $40 a night.

“Regency Club is like a 5 star Hotel with in a 4 star Hotel. Great Job Hyatt SF” I had 7 faster free nights that I needed to use before Feb. 28. So I took the Cal Train into the city and spent 9 nights at they Hyatt Regency. As a Hyatt Diamond Member I was upgraded to the Regency Club Level, Balcony Bay View, and I loved every second of it, was hard to leave. The Regency Club Rooms occupy the top 2 floors, and the club is on top of the hotel with an awesome views of the Bay Bridge, The Bay, and the Financial District. Each night the club had a wonderful spread of hous D'oenuvers, and in the morning a generous continental breakfast. The rooms have been renovated and are tastefully decorated with large plasma tv in the room, and a tv located in the bathroom mirror. The staff was friendly, accommodating, and professional. I would like to spend a special thanks to the housekeeping staff for the friendly 5 star service they provided. Every morning when I returned from breakfast my room was clean!!! Amazing it like they knew my schedule. I've stayed at almost every Hyatt, and one of my pet peaves is not having my room cleaned by 12 noon, and encountering a cold housekeeping staff. Thanks again Hyatt Regency San Francisco, you have the best Regency Club and Housekeeping Staff, it was an experience I will never forget.

“Excellent Hotel” This one of the better hotels by the airport, if not the best of them all. The rooms are newly done and with very comfortable bedding and pillows. Extremely comfortable beds. The desk area, entertainment center, furniture and the rest are very nicely and tastefully done. They have obviously made the improvements that have been mentioned in prior reviews which rip this hotel to shreds. The Bar and Restaurant is very "sports" oriented. The lobby is very spacious and inviting, with a sunken gathering area and business center with two computers. The gift shop has all the possible amenities a business or tourist traveler could possibly need. Room service is top notch and is available 24/7. The garden/pool/hot tub area in the center of the hotel property is really stunning and very well landscaped. Staff are so friendly and accomodating. The shuttle driver to the airport was very nice and got me to my terminal is no time. Kudos to the staff at the Doubletree.

“Amazing Hotel!” The Knickerbocker hotel is fantastic! It's an old hotel with updated rooms - so you get the old-timey charm and fresh comfort all at once. The hotel has a fabulous location. It's a one minute walk to the Cheesecake Factory and Bloomingdales, and about a 5 minute walk to Einstein Bagel Company (the best bagels and cream cheese EVER), Macys and Saks. This location can't be beat. You're at one end of the magnificent mile, so it makes for easy strolling, as you don't start in the middle and then backtrack. The hotel staff are super helpful and friendly. Checking in and out was very smooth, and the concierge (Cheryl) was amazing. She booked all our dinner reservations and activities for us, and recommended an incredible restaurant called Carmines which was a 5 minute walk. It was the greatest italian restaurant I have ever been to, and I can't recommend it more. The rooms are small but not too small. We had a beautiful big samsung flat screen, cordless phones, a rain shower, ample clean towels, and beautiful marble countertops. The hotel rooms have european charm to them and made me feel like I was at a 5 star hotel in Europe. The beds are very comfortable and the duvet is soft like butter. The only complaint I had was that housekeeping woke us up at 8:30 one morning when the knocked on our door despite the fact that we had the do not disturb sign on. When we answered and asked her to come back later she seemed a bit miffed. The issue was corrected, though, and it didn't happen again during our 4 night stay. The hotel has some unique items on their room service menu - ie - grilled cheese with mini tomato soup for dipping. Very cute. Their late night menu, however, is lacking. It would have been nice to see some soup on there. That being said, I RARELY order from room service when on vacation, so I really don't see that being a big deal. Overall I would recommend this hotel without hesitation. I think we paid about 130 a night and I would say it was worth far more than that. We had a wonderful experience and I truly look forward to staying there again....wouldn't stay anywhere else!

“Hollywood in the Old Tradition” Sure, you could stay at the more exalted Beverly Hills Hotel, but if you want the quintessential Hollywood experience, this is the place! I have stayed both in the pool cabaña villa and in the main tower. I much prefer and would recommend the cabaña; as the room is much more spacious and comfortable, not to mention quiet, except for pool noise which might be a problem in summer. The hotel is a historic wonder and is strategically placed in the heart of Hollywood Blvd. with Graumann's Chinese theater and other attractions, Walk of Fame within easy walking distance. The lobby area has the old Hollywood flavor coupled with 1920's style architecture and Spanish influences throughout; the hotel dates from 1927, the year of the first "talking" picture. The mezzanine level is a tribute to Hollywood history and is worth a look in itself. The famed Cinegrill in the Blossom Room was the site of the first Academy awards back in the late 1920's or early '30s. This hotel was literally a clubhouse for the likes of Errol Flynn who purportedly invented his recipe for gin in the backroom of the ex-barbershop. Nearly every star has trysted here, including Marilyn Monroe and the hotel has attracted famous politicians and literary figures like Ernest Hemingway. All in all, a fascinating place to stay and good service as well. Remember, get a room in the cabaña area; it's the best.
“Out dated” I was in this hotel in 2006 and I reported it as excellent. Last experience has not been the same. Rooms are out dated, and need to be upgraded.

“Best Club Quarters I've stayed at” I've been to a lot of Club Quarters as part of my business travel. They are usually cramped rooms with very few amenities in the hotel, earning them the unofficial nickname "Club Closet". This one breaks the mold. The rooms are actually fairly large by NYC standards. The hotel is pretty new, so that's probably a big part of why it seems so nice. The lobby has a great lounge area, with cappuccino machine, newspapers, magazines, TV, internet stations and ample seating. On the roof they have an open and airy restaurant, which has a bar for the evening and breakfast buffet in the morning. There is also a rooftop patio to lounge in the warmer months, or just get a good view of the surrounding area. If you are planning to visit the 9/11 memorial, you can get much closer than this. In fact you can see the hotel in the pictures on the memorial website (http://www.911memorial.org/explore-memorial, it's the white building in the back left of the photo). Our room faced the memorial, which is lit up at night. I do strongly suggest visiting it, the tickets are free. If you are driving in, I suggest using the parking lot they are affiliated with, which is on Albany St a block away. If you "self park" it's $37/day, compared to the $50 or so at other garages. They will also bill the charge directly to your room. You can find the address for the garage on the directions page of the Club Quarters website. When you get there, it looks closed, but if you tell the guard you are staying at Club Quarters he will remove the various security measures and let you in. I probably shouldn't let out the secret, but unlike most NYC hotels, the room rate at the Club Quarters actually DROPS on the weekend. They get most of their business during the week from business travelers, and so the weekend is pretty dead. As part of their business model though your company needs to be a member in order to make a reservation here. But if you know someone whose company is a member, they can make a reservation for you. I'd definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Very nice hotel, dated decor in some respects” We stayed in the Atherton Suite for 2 nights in June 2008. We booked this hotel (and this room) because we got a great rate on Expedia during one of their 60% off one-day sales. Check in was fast, courteous, and very efficient. We were given detailed directions on getting from the check-in area to our room which was in the tower addition. The first thing we noticed upon entry into our room was the fact that there was a strange juxtaposition between very dated furniture and fixtures, and the modern. There was a big flat panel television, but some couches done up in fabrics clearly from the early 80s. The curtains were heavy, and gold-colored, but the bed was almost brand new, plush, and comfortable. There was an iPod dockable clock-radio in the bedroom. The bathroom was fantastic, reminiscent of the setup of the Intercontinentals we've stayed at: nice deep bath on one side, shower on the other (this one with a rain shower head). The bathroon was spacious, and the tub had great water pressure for producing an excellent bubblebath (did I mention it was deep?) There were sliding doors to block off the sitting area from the sleeping area, which was nice, and also separate temperature controls. Being in a corner suite, due to the hotel's layout, we had no neighbors on any side -- so our room was wonderfully quiet. We didn't eat any meals at the hotel, but we did check out the Tonga Room (kitschy) -- drinks and the "buffet" were pretty expensive and not really worth the atmosphere, we thought. We did enjoy the Laurel Court bar, which was quieter, and had more comfortable seating on couches and such. Overall, the hotel definitely lives up to its reputation. We likely won't stay at the Fairmont again, unless Expedia has another sale like they did! -- and if we did stay again, we'd probably try to check out a room in the main building.

“Best located hotel in new york.” Have stayed here at least six times since 2004.you could not ask for a better location in new york city.walk out the hotel and your are in the middle of times square.the hotel itself is very big and very busy which is the way i like it as you are anonymous.rooms are large,clean and when you shut your door it is complete silence.have been lucky and had a view basic priced rooms with a stunning view of times square,but you can pay more to guarantee this.staff are friendly,helpful and efficient.all in all a great place to stay.not cheap but worth every penny.

“Holiday Stay” We had a great stay at the Hilton Times Square. You can't beat the location if you are if you don't mind crowds. We visited NYC the week between Christmas and New Years. The location is easily accessible to subway and also the Hop On/Hop Off bus. The staff was very nice and helpful. Rooms were clean.

“Okay but could be great” The hotel is in a good location and at one time it was a nice hotel but time and changing owners have not been kind. I don't think I would stay here again because. Our first room was at the back of the hotel with a view of the service entrance. We asked to be moved after we were woken up with a loud bang and crash of the trash can and trash truck at 4:00 am. We were moved to an inside courtyard view. The room was the same but the toilet did not flush correctly, the bathroom was dirty and the AC was weak. We reported the toilet and AC problem but it was never fixed after a few calls and I just gave up. I'm surprised this is a Hilton and maybe they will remodel soon.

“not to bad at all” stayed here for a trade show oct. 16, 17 18 hotel is classic 60's art deco and has been refurbished quite nicely room was a bit smaller than average but clean, well appointed and bathroom was same we were facing the street and there was some road noise as were were on the third floor, ate at the breakfast buffet which was ok, but not great....... hotel is a bit of a walk via the river walk to the busier section but very pleasant walk I would give it an above average rating and the desk staff was very nice.........

“Great Location near Ferry Building with lots of amenities at a reasonable price” We stayed 2 nights @ the Hyatt Regency SF and wish we could have stayed longer. The hotel was lovely. The location was convenient. Right across the street from the Muni (local train) and BART (regional train) especially if you fly into the SFO airport. You can get on the BART and arrived across the street from the Hyatt Regency in about 30 minutes. The California cable car originates in front of the Hyatt. The Ferry Building is one block away. Here you can get the tram or bus. A perfect location if you plan on using the public transportation system which takes you where ever you want to go. Fisherman's Warf is a short ride away. The rooms were spacious and clean. The beds were very comfortable. There were lots of pillows, towels etc. The bathroom was large and clean with nice amenities. There was a mini bar (cost) and flat screen TV. This hotel has a lot of amenities including valet parking and a Budget rental car location on sight which was very convenient for us. The staff was efficient and helpful, the concierge knowledgable and check in quick. And the price was very reasonable. We paid around $140 a night plus tax on Orbitz. which is about what we would have paid for a much lesser hotel in the same location. I'd love to stay here again when I come to San Francisco.

“Nice little hotel in perfect location” I was a bit worried about booking our trip at STAY hotel after reading some of the reviews, but I did it anyway, and I don't regret it. The first night I was by myself, so I had booked a queen rom. Not much place, but for a solo traveller just fine. Very clean and cozy room (and it was noisy yes, and with jet-lag it wasn't much sleep to get staying on the 3rd floor, so ask for high floor!). The day after my boyfriend came and joined me, and for $20 more per night we had a king room on 8th floor (no noise), which is what I would say a normal hotelroom in size compared to Europe standard. We slept really well, but don't eat your breakfast at the hotel. Too expencieve and just not worth it! Over $30 for a not so good omelette, an orange juice and a black coffe! No thank you! We had some drinks in the bar every day, yes, again expencieve, but we were on holiday, staying in Times Sq. and knew it would be pricey, and we couldn't really care if it was some dollars more. All the bar-staff was really helpful in suggesting other bars/clubs to go to. Reseption staff excellent! Always helpful for maps, directions and restaurant suggestions. For a first time visitor to NY, you can't beat the location, the rooms or the price. PS. Last tip: We went to have som sushi at Omida, which was great! Cool interior, fantastisc staff and the sushi was out of this world! It is on Broadway between 53 & 54 (if I'm not wrong). Just 5 minutes walk from the hotel.

“Nice hotel, with awesome location” As a hotel, it was slightly above average. The rooms were standard size, but very clean and kept up nicely. A nice perk was the hotel has a full gift/amentities shop and restaurant. The pool, which is an outdoor pool on the roof, was large and well maintained. The big plus for this hotel is the LOCATION. Ben Franklin's grave is literally right behind the hotel, Betsy Ross' house is one block the other way and all the major sites of Independence Park are 5 minutes walk or less. Seeing all of Independence Park involves a lot of walking and it was invaluable to be able to come back to the hotel, relax for a while and recharge to see more of the incredible landmark sights in American History.

“Bed bugs. Otherwise, nice.” I know what leaving a review titled bed bugs can mean for a property so I don't leave this post without reservations. Yes, I was eaten alive during my recent trip. Back and legs, all swollen red. Now, that aside, this is a nice hotel. Rooms are comfy and the location can't be beat. For the tall people, this may not be your ideal property and sheets are short. By short I mean they only go up 3/4 of the length of the bed. I'm 6'1" and they were half up my chest. You will have to use to available blanket. Staff is very nice and the gym was amazing.

“not bad, just not great” I stayed here for a conference, so I didn't really have a choice in which hotel. I stayed on the 14th floor and had an average view. The room was dated and small (two queens). Bathroom wasn't the cleanest and the sink had a slow drain (I hate when no one checks that stuff in a hotel...). It was nice to sit on the "boardwalk" and watch the people on the river and the location wasn't bad. I spent the weekend in Chicago - but at a different hotel (that cost more than the conf rate) and I was glad I'd booked the other place.

“Will Return” My husband and I travel to New York each summer and have tried some fine hotels. But the fact that the Muse was a Kimpton sealed the deal. They are always artistic and quirky. The Muse was elegant and gracious andwe have absolutely no complaints. We were allowed to use our room before noon, and the 9 PM happy hour was incredible. Everyone couldn't be nicer. Thank you, Trip Advisor and Kimpton hotels.

“Better than the Westin” I've got the top tier status with Marriott and Westin. Having recently stayed at the Westin at LAX I thought I'd give the Marriott a try. While I was underwhelmed with rooms at both properties I was struck by a few things at the Marriott that give it an edge over the Westin: -The staff really is on the ball at the Marriott. They acknowledged my status and gave me a top floor and access to the lounge on 16 - I can remember the Westin guy almost asleep at check in. -Hallway carpet is 70's Vegas, but the room was slightly nicer and less worn than the Westin. -Westin lounge was tired and lame - Marriott had a nice spread of food and beverage options.

“great room, no maid service” I booked online prepaid and got a 197/night rate. Room was ready when I arrived at 9pm sunday night. Room was half way up the tower with a glimpse of the lake between the buildings. It was near the elevator but very quiet. The room is a two room suite with a living room with desk, flat screen tv, wetbar, and sofa. The bedroom had a king bed. This room was excellently outfitted for the business traveller. It was the first room I stayed in where I could work on the laptop, eat room service, and channel surf through the TV, all at the same time from one sitting location. The desk was large and had a pull out table for dinner. So no clearing off the desk for the dinner. Moreover, the TV was on a wall next to the desk so I could watch the tube inbetween emails and bites of dinner. The bedroom was small, just big enough for the king bed and too small for a regular door. Mine had skinny french doors which was odd, but they worked fine. The bathroom was spacious and everything worked well. My only complaint was that they forgot to make up my room while I was gone all day at work. I came back at 9pm the next night to find the room as I left it in the morning. I called the operator and the maid service was sent immediately and they quickly replaced my towels etc. The rooms are recently renovated and they look really nice. Also the hotel has windows that open which means you can get fresh air. This is getting more unusual these days for high rise hotels and it was much appreciated by me, especially since the new furniture and carpet in the room still has an odor and thus the rooms can use a bit of airing out from the new materials. Another small issue was that I needed a credit card receipt because I paid in advance. Hilton did not email me any receipt and the hotel could not give me the information. So I had to call Hilton after my stay and ask for a receipt. They were able to email me the receipt within an hour of my phone call and I was able to submit with my business expenses. Staff was friendly and helpful. I would stay there again on another trip.

“Good hotel; great location” This was my first stay at the L'Enfant Plaza, and I actually plan to stay there again in about one month. The hotel is a bargain considering the price of other hotels of its status in D. C. The location is perfect for both visiting the museums and connecting with the Metro for business appointments or other venues in the D.C. area. The room was spacious and clean; the bed was very comfortable; the shower was great. The hotel is beginning to show its age, as other reviewers have noted, so I expect there will be some renovations in the future. There are really no good restaurants in the area, so expect a long walk, a taxi ride, or a Metro jaunt to your favorite D. C. dining establishments. A good brunch is of course an easy walk to any of the museum cafes in the Mall area. The restaurant in the hotel is of average quality and overpriced (no surprise there).

“Great stay (one night)” I can easily recommend this hotel. Perfect location, particularly for guys interested in 17th Street establishments. "P" is growing too in the Whole Foods block, not to mention 14th street. Steph-Vog (intentionally truncated) is one of the managers and is very friendly and accomodating. It is great to see a Euro-trained, educated manager on-site. The decor? I will repeat I'm not into Red! It makes me feel soooo cheap. I would redecorate in muted colors, "green" for instance. This hotel has fantastic proximity to the Dupont and Logan neighborhoods. It's not really a hotel for the Air & Space middle-schooler crowd, although there's nothing wrong with that. I paid $109 + $30 for parking + Taxes, ending up at about $158, I believe.

“Clean New Hotel; but needs some bugs fixed” The hotel is new...clean and very nice looking rooms with hdtv flat screens...lobby is beautifully decorated...buuuuuuuuuut thats where it ends for the compliments...onto the negatives...the hotel is in a deserted location when it comes to restaurants and bars and shops so you would think that the property would have more than an overpriced critically bashed restaurant as a place to eat when visiting. Sauciety is a 1 1/2 star rated restaurant not worth your cash...just take a $10 cab into the middle of boston and eat at a real restaurant like Umbria for example...their starbucks closes at 7pm?!?!? no yellow pages in the room so you have to order from their room service...again overpriced crap...the cleaning service was loud slamming doors repeatedly...very annoying...no bottle opener for the wetbar and also no list of prices for the bar...wont stay here again...i guess great for business travelers using the convention center...but for families and couples who want a boston experience...skip this hotel!

“Little Italy” Weekend trip with wife and 7-year old. Room 511 on top floor, east wing of hotel. Big room, 2 queen beds, small armoire and dresser. Large bathroom with full bath/shower but only a pedestal sink...no extra countertop was frustrating. Wet bar in room was useless. Included minifridge but no microwave. No pool or spa. PV is perfectly located for Little Italy, SD Zoo, Gaslamp and quick hop onto/off I-5. Construction next door but we were not bothered by any noise at all. Hotel bar is fancy but the weekend crowd gets noisy. All rooms open in toward first level parking lot, which meant we got to hear lots of drunk yelling and partying as bar patrons were leaving. Front desk staff was great, but every taxi we called took almost 30 mins to arrive. Suggest instead walking down one block to catch cabs on Grape or Hawthorne. $10 cab to Gaslamp, $18 cab to SD Zoo. Make a point to eat at Cafe Zucchero, less than a block from Porto Vista.

“Not up to Hampton standards” This was first Hampton Inn that I did not find up to standards. Prior to checking in I advised the front desk that I was a Hilton Gold which should communicate that I was a regular traveler. Unlike other Hamptons I have stayed in, the fabric on the furniture was very frayed and there was someone else's hair in the bathtub. It is not my practice to complain, but at breakfast the (very friendly) breakfast manager inquired about my stay and once I related the problems she and the front desk clerk visited my room. They were sincerely apologetic and promised me a coupon for a free night's stay. I do believe that this might have been a (bad) luck of the draw since the standards of Hamptons are usually pretty good and since I am regular visit to Charlotte I will give them another chance in the future.

“great location; nice room” We stayed between Christmas and New Years. Got an amazing deal at Hotels. Room was very nice. Concierge was extremely helpful. Location was excellent. Parking was a rip-off. Park across the street for 1/3 the price. Also the front desk upon check in offered us a room upgrade - the "upgrade" had a view of a construction site. We asked for our Hotels room and it was a better view and just as nice a room (just a bit small). This is a great deal for SF if you get a discount room and park elsewhere.

“Nice Hotel, But Can Be Noisy” We stayed in room 310 and paid a premium for a "lakeside" location. While the room was spacious with a separate living room, the hotel is across a fairly busy street from Lake Union. The view of the lake was limited at best and I wouldn't call it a particularly beautiful lake in any event. There is a seaplane base on the lake and we were disturbed at night by planes taking off. They are apparently building a streetcar line in front of the hotel which could well add additional noise. The hotel offered the standard Residence Inn breakfast and also offers a free shuttle every 30 minutes to a number of points in the Seattle area, including the Space Needle. Other than the noise and a limited lake view, we were happy with our stay.

“Overworked, but handled themselves well.” Arrived to find we'd been overbooked for the night - they gave us a cash refund plus a taxi to their other premises near Ground Zero. Came back to a really apologetic staff the next day who put us in a good room on the 6th floor. Had wrong luggage delivered to our room as well - this was corrected quickly but it could have ended badly had we been dishonest! I had no problems with noise and the room was well-sized to relax in - though unfortunately we were not in too often! Great location too - mixed opinions on other rooms though so I strongly think it depends what room you get...

“A Hotel Geared Toward Conventioneers” Not a bad stay -- simply a typical Marriott experience -- nothing overwhelming about the experience. The hotel's location is one of its strong points, Back Bay, connected to Copley Place, Prudential Center's Marketplace and the Hynes Convention Center. I was there during a cold spell (2 degrees outside) so it was nice not having to walk outside to get places. The room was decent - fairly modern decor with comfortable beds. The hotel, I believe, is or will be, undergoing a room renovation. It needs it, as my room on the 28th floor had a big nasty yellow stain on one of the walls.
“Great Location” We stayed here between Christmas and New Year's. Everything was great. The staff was wonderful and it was nice to be able to use the fitness center.

“Good Location, Very different from your normal hotel” When i arrived, and walked in, I knew that prior to arriving I would expect to see a renovated bank. Thats exactly what I got. BUT i love the uniqueness of it. I appreciate the work of a company that takes the time to renovate but not remove all the original aspects of the building. The service was excellent. If you valet your car, make sure to call ahead. It can take about 15 minutes to get your car since they park offsite. Also be prepared that there is no pool...so this may not be the best place for a week long vacation. The beds were really comfortable. From what I understand most of the rooms are different sized considering they are old renovated offices. You just have to know what to expect when walking into a place like this, and certainly not to expect the Ritz Carlton, but for the price and location, its a good deal.

“Westgate Rates A-” On the plus side: Excellent car valet service; good front desk staff; beautifully appointed rooms; a most comfortable bed; extraordinary shower pressure; great room service (although the order was incomplete at delivery) On the minus side: No ice machines - must call room service (very inconvenient); no coffee machines in room; rooms could use more pieces of furniture, e.g., a table; inconsistent housekeeping- items were removed and not replaced. Overall: One of the better hotels in San Diego - I would stay there again.

“Good hotel - Clean and great breakfast” Stayed for business on 183 corridor. Great location. Right across from mall. Plenty of parking. Convenient parking. Tread mills in workout room were nice and in good working order. Can't ask for more from a Holiday Inn.

“Nice hotel in downtown LA” I joined my husband as he was attending a conference at the la convention center. We chose the Omni over other the conference hotels based on TripAdvisor reviews. We were upgraded to a room on the 16th floor which was quiet, spacious and very nicely appointed. This room came with access to the club floor for free breakfast, drinks, etc. The entire Omni staff we encountered were courteous, helpful and friendly. I used the fitness room, which was a decent size and had decent equipment as well as the pool. The pool area is a little small and the pool itself is narrow and shallow. It was perfectly fine for a quick dip but not a "lap pool" if you are a serious swimmer. Downtown la is kind of a wasteland, especially during the weekend, but the Omni is a very nice oasis. I would definitely stay here again if I had business in downtown LA and would recommend it to others.

“Spacious & Gracious” We had a 2 bedroom junior suite. Loved it!! Clean, extremely roomy, and friendly staff. We were welcomed with our name as an honors member. Pool to ourselves, close to the airport. Breakfast variety including scrambled eggs, turkey sausage, waffles & all the other typical fare. I would definitely go back! What an awesome room to earn for free (with points accumulated).

“Hated everything about it” Everything about this establishment is horrific.. From the janitor closet size rooms to the obnoxious staff, the late president would be aghast at what this place has become. I won't even approach the dining in this place- the food and beverage director is so far out of touch with reality regarding priciing, its a joke. As far as in room TV and internet service goes, they seem to get good cheap deals on used 20 yr old TV's and an outdated dial up service-ripping you off again. Stay far away from this dump. Unfortunately having booked on Priceline, no refunds allowed. Stay at a Hilton Inn or Courtyard for a slightly higher price.

“Pricey With An Excellent Location! Staff gets an A+” Third trip to the area (2nd this year) and stayed 2 nights in this "Category 7" Hotel, The location is almost dead center for most of Chicago's Big Ticket tourist attractions like the Navy Pier, Millennium Park, Lincoln Park Zoo, Willis & Hancock towers, train stations and of course shopping. You can't beat the location for the price as it sits on the magnificent mile. So this trip we decided on the Chicago's First Lady Architecture tour, beach, the zoo and the aquarium as our highlights. So back to the hotel, if your new to the area you will need to know up front that taxes and parking are high (roughly 10%). For this hotel you can tack on $30 - $50 a day for extra taxes and $51 a day for the valet parking. We chose valet parking over the $36 "on your own"... the parking lot is literally right across the street. So in the future, I would recommend saving your money and opting for the $36 a day version. You must pay for parking somewhere, so it might as well be there close to the hotel. If you’re not an elite member the internet will cost you $15 a night, they have a nice lobby and restaurant with room service. Our room was on the 41st floor facing east towards the lake and we had a spectacular view. On night we even watched the Fireworks from the Navy Pier. So for me it was worth the extra $30 a night above most hotels in the area on or around the mile. Bedding was soft and comfortable room amenities etc were great. We honestly didn't spend much time in the room. My only complaint to note was the "Fire Hose" water pressure from the shower. It was literally stingy when we showered at night. But other than that, I would stay here again for the view and amenities. Hope it helps and Thanks for reading. I have room videos on YouTube. Pros - Great Location and View from higher floors - Fast WIFI Internet - Location (about 2 miles to most Tourist Spots) - Full service restaurant with room service Cons - Fire Hose Water Pressure in Shower Marriott Gold Rewards Member RetiredArmyRANGER

“Great value & services” Stayed in the room at the end of the corridor therefore it's more spacious and not square-shaped feeling. Not much view from my side of the building but others were great nonetheless. Great attentive staff from valet (though expensive parking) till very helpful and friendly check-in. Internet always free at Kimptons upon request which no exception here. Room was lovely decorated, very upscale and beautiful. Bed and pillows were fantastic and very clean. Mini-bar items are in good selection and at acceptable prices. Compliment coffee till 9am. was nice as well as juices. Tried breakfast on E&O which also great and reasonable price. I have absolutely nothing negative to say about this hotel and will certainly check on this first for the next time in Baltimore.

“It's the service which counts!” We reserved our room over the hotel's own web site and secured a discounted rate provided that we prepay in full--no changes or refunds. We had our own "reservations" about this ploy but were glad we made them because when we checked in, the hotel was fully booked. Three days before our visit, the hotel concierge telephoned not only to confirm our reservation but to inquire whether there was anything she might do. Being a Hilton Honors member paid off here! In addition, our room was ready when we checked in at 2:30 (normal check-in is at 4:00). Although there is a $22 parking fee, the in and out privileges and the promptness/courtesy iof the valet staff more than compensated. In fact, when we first arrived, Albert promptly escorted us and our bags to the front desk and within minutes we were looking at the bay and Coronado Bridge. Wonderful! Drinks at 5:30--7:30 with accompanying niblets. The Greek Taverna, enthusiastically recommended by our Concierge turned out to be OK--tentative service but good drinks and wines available. Mopussaka was so-so (bland) but the lamb was excellent. Enough to bring back to the hotel to warm up for lunch! Breakfast was quite good. True, the orange juice must be poured into styrofoam containers and the coffee mugs are plastic, but this prevents broken glass and theft. An outstanding addition to the breakfast scene was the cappuccino machine with latte, hot chocolate, and of course cappuccino. The area was well maintained with pleasant staff constantly cleaning and replacing food. New flat screen TVs were welcome although a CD system would have been nice. A final note: driving in downtown San Diego is a breeze compared to anywhere in the North Bay. Also, our concierge meticulously mapped out directions for negotiating exits and locations. A job well done!

“Always a great stay” We've stayed here numerous times over the past few years. We've enjoyed each stay and never have had a problem. The rooms and bathrooms are always super clean. Lots of great amenities in the bathroom. The bathroom towels are huge!! We've also been upgraded to a suite a few times as platinum SPG members which is always appreciated. Valet here is expensive - $40 per day. The Dupont Circle Metro is close by.

“Excellent Hotel in Perfect Location” I was in town for work at the University of Texas and stayed here and was very, very pleased. The rooms are in good shape, nice bathrooms, and clean. There is a nice lobby bar in the atrium, which was nice and airy. The hotel restaurant was also not bad. The best part is the location of the hotel. You are within walking distance to a lot of great restaurants and bars. Since there seems to be something always going on in Austin, this is a big plus. Maybe the only drawback is there really isn't a lobby convenience store. Since the hotel is in a building that also shares its space with offices, there is only a convenience store that is in the atrium and run separately. So the hours aren't terribly convenient. Added to that, the fitness center I believe is also used by people who have membership, so not only hotel guests. The one evening I had to wait a bit for a machine to open up.

“Nice Stay.” I stayed for three nights with 20+ colleagues. They are typically a picky group, but I heard no complaints - so that says a lot. Spent much time in the adjoining wine bar, everyone enjoyed and the food/service was excellent. Rooms were clean/modern. I read reviews about the lack of horizontal surfaces for storage, but I didn't have an issue. Sink is very shallow (form over function) but it looked cool. Wireless internet was a bit wonky. I had an upper room facing 24th street (at the end of the hall) and it was quiet as long as the air conditioner was running. Comfortable bedding. Friendly staff. Conference/Bfast room has great view and nice deck.

“Take Advantage of Car Service” My wife and I stayed there for a wedding in September 2008, so really don't have that much to offer about the hotel, itself. But one thing we would want to point out is that they do have a complimentary car service to anywhere within 3 miles of the hotel. They don't make that especially well known, which is why I am writing this, so that Trip Advisor users know about it. Given the fact that the hotel is somewhat isolated, and it's a good half hour walk (in the heat) to the nearest commercial area (for eating, etc).,the car service is good to know about. I heard that the food prices are very expensive for breakfast at the hotel, so going to that commercial area is a nice diversion. There is a Rice Food Emporium in that area, which is a very nice and upscale gourmet market, as well as other restaurants. A positive of the hotel is that we found the rooms to be quiet.

“Superb Place to Stay” We stayed here 2 nights as part of a tour. This was the best hotel we stayed in on all of the tour - it was outstanding. Our room was huge and very lavishly appointed in tasteful browns & beige. The beds were extremely comfortable and there were abundant white fluffy towels. There was coffee making facilities along with an iron & ironing board and a hairdryer. The pool was absolutely fabulous! We ate in the hotel one night on the patio and the meal was superb - faultless. It's interesting being next to such a busy little executive airport (the USA's busiest private airport we were told) where the final scenes of 'Casablanca' were filmed. We were told John Travolta, Pamela Anderson and various other stars walk through the hotel lobby sometimes when using the airport. The scale model of the Pan Am jumbo in reception is most impressive. The location is good for Hollywood, Beverly Hills, the Getty Museum & Santa Monica, also Universal Studios. The entire hotel exuded class and the staff were friendly, helpful & courteous. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

“ottimi servizi ma stanze un pò piccole” l'hotel è bellissimo ed il personale molto attento. le stanze sono pultissime e la moquette rossa sembra appena messa. Tuttavia mi aspettavo stanze un pochino più spaziose, ed invece sono conformi alo standard americano che tende al piccolo (tra il letto e la finestra laterale non ci sono due metri). sono appena stato al Palomar che, per un prezzo inferiore, propone stanze un pò meno scintillanti ma decisamente più spaziose. il wifi è gratuito.

“Comfortable and not nearly as bad as some reviews indicate” I don't doubt that the folks that have written negative reviews of L'Enfant Plaza Hotel had bad experiences, and maybe they lowered my overall expectations, but I found my 4 night stay to be very comfortable and enjoyable. I must admit something up front - I stayed at this hotel for free. There was a travel website that was running a promotion where, at random points during the day, all hotels were free for up to 7 nights. It hid the actual name of the hotel until after I booked, but it really didn't matter much to me since I wasn't paying for the stay. We drove to Washington for our 4 night vacation (leaving the kids with grandma!); parking in D.C. is a nightmare and we had read the reviews on here saying how expensive it was at the hotel, so we ended up parking at the Franconia-Springfield Metro station in multi-day parking and riding the train in. It's about 20 minutes from the Pentagon station on the blue line, and then you can switch over to yellow and the next stop is L'Enfant. As others have stated, the metro station is a huge plus for this hotel as (I believe) four out of D.C.'s five lines run through there (the red line being the exception - only two stops away). Check-in was easy, staff was friendly. Our room was on the 11th floor, looking south towards the Potomac and Reagan National Airport. I imagine views from the other side were quite nice. The room was clean and much larger than expected - two double beds with a desk in between that left a lot of room between the beds. I can see where some might be a little disappointed with some nit-picking (some wallpaper peeling in the bathroom near the floor, a slight stain on the ceiling, etc), but I was pleasantly surprised with the room overall as it was not "dirty" or "dingy" as others had apparently experienced here. The TV was small and the reception on some stations was unimpressive, but it was never a real problem as we weren't in D.C. to watch TV. We utilized the metro for most of our travel ... the mall ("La Promenade" I believe) is a little creepy after the stores & eateries close (they cater to work-week employees in the area, not to tourists) as it's deserted and the 70's soft rock hits echo throughout the corridors. The National Mall, and specifically the Air & Space Museum, are VERY easy to walk to from the hotel (just a few blocks), with other attractions like Engraving & Printing and the Holocaust Museum (highly recommended) just a bit further in the other direction. Of course, it was a little annoying that a hotel of this caliber would nickel-and-dime for things like wireless internet, breakfast, etc, but it wasn't a huge issue since I wasn't there on business. I would've been annoyed to pay $10 a day for wifi though. The gift shop charges like $2.50 for a 20 oz. soda, so be prepared for that as well. Starbuck's cart in the lobby was nice to have in the mornings, although a free continental breakfast would've been better ;-). Overall, I was pleased with the stay and would consider staying again. I'd say it's not quite as nice as they'd lead you to believe (they bill themselves as 4-star, which they're just not), but definitely not as bad as some reviews would indicate either. A high 3-star stay, at least from my experience, and recommended for folks looking for easy access to all D.C. has to offer.

“Great hotel” When driving up to the hotel, I was worried because the building looks really old. But it is deceiving because the interior is first class. It is clean and the rooms are nice. The bathroom, especially bathtub, needs updating. The surrounding area is great with many places to eat within walking distance.
“Really amazing” Privacity, good location, spacious, clean and comfortable. It has everyting. We ́d stay again.

“Quiet, unique rooms and great service” Stayed at the Monaco in early June. The rooms are not the standard generic hotel fare. They are interestingly decorated and fun to stay in. My room was very quiet and the wifi signal was good. This was my first time at a Kimpton hotel and now I am hooked! Will definitely return.

“Decent Hotel Despite a Bit of Dust” This was my first visit to Indianapolis. My colleague recomended the Marriott as the best option in the area, close to the client site we were visiting. I was able to secure a room at the end of the hallway with a great view of the lake. Two problems with the room though: First, the bed was somewhat soft...I always have this complaint. I need a good firm bed for back problems and the only thing I can do is sleep on the side of the bed that is least likely to get the most use. The other problem was that the room hadn't been dusted too well. There were some cobwebs in the bathroom and a layer of dust on the bathroom vanity. I don't think that room was used very much. In all fairness to the Marriott, I brought this to the attention of the front desk upon check-out and they "made it right" for me, which I greatly appreciated. But I am always surprised that hotel housekeeping doesn't keep a more careful eye on such a basic issue. One suggestion: rent a car if you are staying on this side of Indy. The cab ride was $80 from the airport and there is no shuttle available at this hotel even though there is a large mall with a Nordstrom just a few blocks away. A hotel shuttle to the mall would have been a nice amenity but I guess most guests drive. Next time, I will rent a car because the Indy airport is really easy to navigate and the rental car lots are right at the airport, no rental car shuttles necessary. I did like the workout room very much. Nicely equipped and open 24/7. I didn't have to wait for a cardio machine. Yes, I will return to this Marriott if I need to come back to this area next time. The front desk team was excellent and attentive. Bell staff very friendly, too.

“A New One To me - And I Will Be Back!” I can not believe that I have never stayed here before. It is in a great location (44th between 5th and 6th) and a very personable boutique hotel environment. If you need big crowds and big lobbies, don't go here, but if you like a nice room, nice people, a good locations, try it. My room was big for NYC standards and had a king size bed, a big table, nice comfy chair and a window seat. The TV was like a 47" or 50" set too! :). Bathroom well equiped - big shower and big sink, you weren't balancing your stuff on top of things you would rather not touch... Only complaint was that the room was warm even with AC cranked, but I would go here every time my budget allowed!

“Not equal to the competition.” I have stayed at numerous hotels in downtown Boston over the last few years.
