Most experiences have been good to excellent, Back Bay, previously known as Jury's falls short. The carpet in our room was dirty. We asked to be moved, something we almost never do, and the "better" room had carpet that was just as dirty. The shower had mildew problems and the smell was bad. On the plus side, the staff couldn't be nicer. It's like a beat up old car with a nicely appointed chauffeur. The public areas are nice but a bit dowdy. At these prices, I think you are owed something better.

“Only 1 real complaint!” Picked this Motel 6 because of it's location, price and the fact that it has been remodeled. The look of the room was actually nice but it's still a small space and most importantly, a BAD BED! It was only a mattress on a board. So uncomfortable! Staff was friendly and all was clean, but just couldn't get a good nights sleep.

“The Hotel is a dark disco” Firstly the positives. The service at this hotel is fantastic expecially around the pool area. This hotel is aimed at cashed up young trendy set not for a middle aged couple like us. We arrived at 10pm to a red carpet dark noisy entrance. I actually thought I had arrived to a disco. Upon entering it was just as dark and walked up to reception. They gave me my room key. I went to sleep to be kept up all night by this very loud sounding jumbo jet noise. By 4am I rang downstairs and they sent up a maintence guy who said yes it is noisy we can change your room. I said maybe at 8am I will change rooms which I did. The noise apparantly was vents above that room. (this room was a Premier room not a standard room) I changed rooms after not sleeping all night. The rooms are also just as dark as the lobby. At check out they actually wanted me to pay extra for the change of rooms are you kidding they should have offered me some kind of compensation for my lack of sleep the first night. I have very mixed feelings about this hotel. As service is very good. It is certainly very different to anything I have ever stayed at but I doubt I will be back

“Fabulous Property In An Excellent Location” I stayed at the Belvedere from 2/26-2/29, 2004 and absolutely loved the property. The rooms were very clean, comfortable, well-equipped and modern. The heat/ac systems could use some work, but they functioned well. The lobby and guestrooms are absolutely beautiful but the corridors are showing some signs of wear. I stayed with a group, so I'm not quite sure what the room rate was, but I did hear that it was around $135 for a triple! This is absolutely outstanding value for New York...especially since we were within walking distance of Times Square and the midtown attractions. Meals were (although a good value for New York) quite pricey. You're better off hitting a Deli or Bagel cart for breakfast and picking up lunch and dinner off property as well. But the ambience of the restaurant is very unique and enjoyable for those willing to spend the extra money. I work for a Hotel in Niagara Falls, NY and can receive deep discounts on hotel rooms in my chain. However, I was so pleased with The Belvedere that I will be glad to spend the extra money to stay there each time I'm in New York. Stay at the Belvedere...you won't be disappointed.

“View! Location! Beautiful, large room and a heavenly mattress!” OK, it was a little weird that our king bed appeared to be a Murphy, but after we finished scratching our heads about that, we turned around and noticed that Puget Sound, Queen Anne Hill and the Space Needle were staring at us through our wall to wall, floor to ceiling windows (and then, oddly, we forgot all about the funky bed frame). The windows and the amazing mattress had only the luxurious bathroom to compete with for our attention while at the Seattle Westin. This place was so impressive - beautiful lobby, super attentive front desk staff, concierge and bellmen, an extra large room with huge windows, nice sofa and chairs, large closet, etc. We were really blown away. Terrific location, right in the middle of everything that is downtown Seattle. It was truly painful to leave that room...

“The Waldorf is the Wonderful!” I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria this last week and was extremely pleased with the whole experience. The Hotel is a true piece of history, wonderful to explore and enjoy. The rooms are lovely and well maintained. The staff is helpful and kind. I would recommend the Waldorf to anyone planning to visit New York and want a memorable stay there.

“Decent but dated” Stopped in for one night with a room booked via my Starpoints. Nice and close to LAX, fast, convenient shuttle, everything you'd really want for an airport hotel. Rooms however do feel a bit dated - if you've stayed in various Sheratons, you'll know that whilst the services are usually quite similar, the rooms can vary depending on how old the hotel is, and this was on the lower end of the scale. Both room and bathroom showing signs of wear+tear, and could use a bit of a makeover. Few lights etc not working in room, but no biggie. On a happier note, we did get upgraded to a suite (which wasn't much bigger than a room), and enjoyed a decent meal at the steakhouse on the ground floor which is pretty good. All in all, a decent airport stopover.

“Beautiful, Historic, and convenient” My wife and I had a great time. Highly recommended. It is close to the German Village, Arena District and the Capitol. Columbus is a clean and vibrant city. The only negative thing I would say is that they charge $20 for parking, which was not told to me when I booked, nonetheless, still reasonable. The service at the front desk was top notch! I plan on going back soon!

“Sofitel sooths” Stayed here during peak Christmas season. There are many good writeups on here about this hotel. I agree with all the ones that define the hotel as an excellent one. Some pointers: Try to get upgraded to a king room. They are on the higher floor. We did so after one night in a standard room and were not disappointed. Had a nice view of the Chrysler building; close enough to see the gargoyles. As mentioned earlier, the higher you are in this hotel, the better. The staff here is very friendly and goes out of their way to make you happy. This statement does not apply to the inept servers at the hotel bar however. Go elsewhere for libations. Regarding the glowing writeups of the 'Red Flame Diner', I just don't get it. The place is o.k. for breakfast and they are certainly fast with delivery, but it is nothing special. A more interesting choice for breakfast and fast is 'Dishes'. Great quality food, even if the atmosphere is 'cafeteria-ish'; two blocks away. Ask the concierge. We ate at DB bistro (two doors down from hotel) and were sorely disappointed, especially after having eaten at the flagship Daniel two nights before. Of course it is much cheaper, but you can do much better for the money. For those from out of town, NYC water is terrific. It comes from upstate New York and does not have to be treated. Drink it from the taps, you are wasting money otherwise. Yes, it was expensive at $500 a night with tax, but my friends stayed at the Roosevelt for $300 and hated it. This hotel is so worth it. Planning to return in early summer; tres bon.

“Just right for us” To me location is paramount. The best hotel far away from where I want to be means nothing when I can't find a parking spot within blocks (or miles) in a town I'm not familiar with. The Hampton Inn Downtown was within walking distance of the bay, of the tour stops and of the great eating places in Little Italy. Sitting on Pacific Highway it was also a great jumping off place for other locations. The room was roomy, nice and clean. The staff was courteous and helpful. The trains took some getting used to but were not nearly as annoying to me as the increasingly horrible instances of loud drunks and groups of teenagers going room to room all night, that I've found in other even nicer hotels all over the country. And I haven't even mentioned the breakfast which was consistently good and saved me 25-30 dollars each day.

“Vaue for money in an excellent Location” This was my second visit to Chicago having stayed at the Conrad on Michigan Avenue previously. I wanted to stay closer this time to the shopping and dining venues and chose the Sutton for that. It is ideally situated a block away from Oak Street Beach and The Magnificent Mile and well surrounded by restaurants and has a tremendous Pancake House restaurant right across the street. The rooms are comfortable and clean and bathrooms were spacious , having a separate shower and tub which I prefer. The hotel is 3-4 star and therefore not luxurious but we were very satisfied for the price we paid.Staff were always obliging. I would recommend this hotel to others.

“Great stay downtown.” Can get to from both airports relatively easily - either orange to red from midway or blue to red from ohare. We trained in and out (walked from state lake orange stop) with luggage and was fine. Is adjacent to red line and is right in the thick of all the tourist stuff. Navy pier, portillos, geno's east, al's, Ed debevics, watertower place, Chicago river, Billygoat and Hancock all within a few block walk. Room was clean - though beds aren't queen - are doubles - which kind of sucked. Breakfast was good. Mgr reception is crowded as well- but most everything free is. Has a small indoor pool and hot-tub. Also business center to print boarding passes etc. There is a jewel osco and trader joes within 2 blocks of the hotel if want to stock up on groceries or just want some water. Parking is $50 a night (hence the train in) so be aware of that. Is one of the nicer places downtown and they seem to price it accordingly. We paid $290 a night marathon weekend. Overall great stay.

“Close Enough To Downtown without the Downtown Prices” My daughter and I were in Austin/San Antonio to look at some schools. For the latter part of our trip, we decided to stay at the Doubletree Downtown. First thing I realized was that if not for my GPS, I would not have found this place! Parking is free in the ramp which is unusual for downtown properties anywhere. This place was close to the downtown attractions but I would not say close enough to walk. The rooms were as I would expect from Doubletree. Very comfortable and clearly has been renovated recently. I believe this property was not originally Hilton/Doubletree. The pool courtyard was very nice and would be great in the hot, Texas sun later in the spring and summer. The small bar proved to be a good watering hole and the breakfast was good. I am not sure I would pay their price if I had to though. Overall, I would definitely stay here again.

“Free internet, free parking and free shuttle to the airport” Although this hotel was located in a location a little far from the airport there was a free shuttle that the hotel operated on request and even when I returned the car at the airport, the hotel sent the shuttle bus to pick me up from the airport car rental company location. The room was very spacious and very clean and while the hotel looked a little rundown from the outside, the inside of it was more than satisfying. The free internet was also very helpful especially for an overseas traveller. I really liked this hotel and I have no problem recommending it.

“Wonderful stay, fantastic location, great staff” Stayed here for 3 nights (during the week) while in Philadelphia on business. Picked the hotel primarily based on location, price, and overall prior TripAdvisor reviews. Short Review: Stay was great, staff across the board were really professional, courteous, and competent. Restaurants (Standing O and Academy Cafe) were above average for hotel restaurants, fitness center was amply set, and location was near perfect. Cleanliness and noise were non-issues. Long Review: Everyone with whom I dealt (with hotel operator one time being the exception) was very friendly, courteous, competent, and professional. From check-in to bell stand, to restaurant staff, to concierge staff, to hotel manager and security (someone turned in my coat, and they got it from lost-and-found for me) - not overstating this - they were all way above average in terms of customer service. The room was decent; not huge, but certainly more than adequate size. Plenty of room to work at the desk, and it was NOT right next to the AC/Heater vent which so many of them are (don't like it when the air is blowing directly on you while you try to work). The hotel architecture is also kind of interesting in that all rooms have kind of a "corner view" with the angled windows. They jut out some so that you can see more than if it was just a set of flat windows. Also the room was very quiet - didn't notice noise issues of other reviewers, although a lot of that can depend on the people in other rooms. The rooms - and the rest of the hotel - had been updated recently. There was a sign/picture in the lobby that stated the renovation completed in June, 2009 (I believe). The hotel and rooms especially had kind of a contemporary clean look to them. They have pictures/drawings of this type on most of the hotel floors as well. All in all the hotel seemed quite clean, although yes, there were a few marks in the carpets here and there, but seldom do you find a hotel without that. I ate at both restaurants, the Academy Cafe (2nd floor) for breakfast each day, and the Standing O which is in the lobby. The Academy Cafe has fairly priced ($8 - $13) menu selections, or the continental/buffet breakfast you can choose. The wait staff did a great job of service and keeping things moving. It was nice to see, at the Standing O, that there were theater patrons who would have lunch or dinner there before/after a show. Must be pretty decent if it attracts people outside the hotel regularly. It's got kind of a sports bar setup in the front, then regular restaurant seating in the back. Same here, prices pretty good for hotel prices (esp. in downtown Philly). They also have a gift shop in the lobby that sells some snacks as well as the ubiquitous T-shirts and other souvenir type items. I used the fitness center every day as well; good setup with 4 treadmills, 2 ellipticals, 1 stationary bike, then free weights and a nautilus machine. On the same floor, all in very close proximity were the pool, hot tub, and sauna (across the hall). Having the 4 treadmills was nice since those are usually the first things to get used; I never had to wait for one, either in the morning or the afternoon. Got to try out the concierge lounge - they had light breakfast in the morning and light snacks in the evening; it took up a smaller area on two floors, the uppermost of which was also a "business center" with a workstation, printer, and free internet. The staff there were very competent and friendly, and it was open every day (maybe this is just during the week not on weekends, not sure about what another reviewer mentioned). The location was near-perfect if you are staying downtown. The surrounding area is great - it's right in the heart of the theater district, and within walking distance of many other attractions, the downtown businesses, and literally hundreds of places to eat. There are several great places within just a few block radius, and all different types of food. I didn't have a car, just took the shuttle to the hotel from the airport and walked everywhere I needed to go. Shuttle/cab note: The hotel recommends Lady Liberty shuttle vans to/from the airport. They are constantly at the airport - didn't have to wait but about 5 minutes, and then they stop at the Double tree every half hour on the :00 and :30. It's only $10 each way, and the cab is $28 each way (fixed price). Have cash for the shuttle van - they say they take credit cards, but the driver gets you to the hotel front door, hands you your bag(s) and no cc reader in sight. So, it's a lot less expensive, but you also have to wait (both ways) while the van picks up enough people to fill it up (holds 8 or 9) and then go the circuitous route to get/drop off everyone. Net - about $25 rt with shuttle and $64 rt with cab. So if you don't mind it taking an extra 30 - 40 minutes, you can save ~$40. Net it out - this was the kind of stay that was so rewarding that I hope to get to Philadelphia again just so I can stay here. Not trying to snow any readers, but this particular stay was that good. Didn't notice the problems of other reviewers, maybe it was just luck, but I don't think so - the fact that really every facet of the stay was far above average made me feel that this is the norm rather than the exception.

“Good hotel, central location” I agree with many of the positive comments on here. Stayed here for 3 nights while on a short vacation. Very friendly staff, clean, good rooms and a very central location. Also good value for money given alternatives.

“Nice Hotel, Friendly Staff, Centrally Located” San Francisco is a great town with a lot of character. This hotel matches the town. It's very big, has a lot of rooms and has a lot of character. Sadly there is no executive lounge, but they provide gold members with vouchers for the Starbucks in the lobby. The line can be long, but it moves along. The people that work at the Starbucks are very efficient and very nice. The front desk staff is very helpful including the concierges. If your not from a big city, you might interpret their efficiency as disinterest. Not the case. They're just dealing with people as quickly and politely as possible so that the people in line behind you don't have to wait too long. We obtained excellent recommendations from the concierge desk. The gym is above average in size and well equipped with many elliptical machines and treadmills. The pool is outdoor and on the roof. My wife did some laps before too many people arrived and although it was short, she enjoyed her swim. We stayed on an upper floor with a beautiful view of the city. All in all a great stay and we would return there.

“Great hotel and staff” Held two meeting here, one in August and the second one in Oct. Meet with Casey who handles the meeting arrangements. Everything was perfect on first request and second meeting two months later was set up exactly as requested with no additional communication necessary. She handles the events flawlessly! The hotel is beautiful and clean. Staff is excellent to work with and very dependable. I own a small business in Greenwood and its the best location hands down to hold your next meeting or event! Enjoy!

“Best Days Inn” This is a great hotel. The rooms are small (European style) but the housekeeping is first rate. The staff are very accommodating and helpful and the hotel is extremely well managed. It's in a lively location, convenient if you're traveling by bus. Bus 22 and 36 stop right on the corner as does 76. From O'Hare, take the Blue line to Logan Square then the 76 bus to the hotel. With all the subway construction on the Brown line, it's just not practical to take the subway to get to the hotel. One word of CAUTION! There are about four rooms that do not have the combo heat/AC units installed yet. If you're "lucky" enough to get one of those rooms, you probably should request a room change. Those rooms have a small air conditioner in the window with side panels that let the cold winter air right through. Supposedly the steam radiator provides heat but it "cycles" on and off and no one seems to know whether it will cycle on during your stay (or even your lifetime) and it does get cold in Chicago during the winter. But if you get one of the other 120 or so rooms you will find a modern HVAC unit that will keep you comfortable all winter long. Not sure why the hotel has not installed these in all rooms yet.

“Hotel lujoso en excelente ubicacion que con algunos detalles seria perfecto” Ubicacion inmejorable, cerca de todo, vida nocturna, Magn Mile, etc comodo, limpio, con tv por cable, con lujos, amplias habitaciones Falencias no hay internet gratis en ningun lugar del hotel (llamativo en un hotel de esta categoria) , sin cafetera, hay frigobar,

“inDeCent exposure” The proprietor of this location owes a huge apology not just to the guests, but also to the staff. I have rarely stayed at a place where everyone was as keen as these people to make sure I was happy. It is also in a fantastic location: four blocks from the convention center. An easy walk to the National Mall or public transportation. But here's the let down: the rooms. OK, they're small. Not a deal breaker. But they're dismal. I couldn't tell if the carpet and bedding were old, or just not well kept. The wallpaper was scarred, peeling, and bubbling - not just in the bathroom, but the main room, too. The paint on the bathroom ceiling was bubbling: the sign of painted over mold. Then there's the smell. The first day it just seemed stale. But as the days progressed, my room had a growing sense of damp. A colleague had an even worse odor in his room. Another oddity was the placement of the hair dryer - right over the sink. One last oddity - a lamp on the desk wouldn't work and i assumed it was the bulb. Investigating a couple of days later, I discovered that it wasn't plugged in ... as there was no outlet anywhere near the lamp. The positives ... the bed was very comfortable. And the lounge/dining area in the basement was well decorated. The pictures on the hotel's website were obviously taken the day the renovations were completed - however many years ago that was. This could be an excellent place to stay. But it isn't.

“Budget and Comfort” I stayed for 6 nights at the hotel in a non-smoking room and paid their seasonal weekly rate. Since the hotel doesn't have 24-hr desk service, I received an email reminder and instructions for late check-in about a week before my arrival. I didn't have any problems checking in and getting settled. I completed my check-in the following morning. Some comments: There was a strong offensive smell when I first entered my room on the fourth floor even though the windows were open. I guessed that it was cigarette smoke from previous occupant/s. After the first couple of evenings or so, the smell has gone away. I didn't get hot water during the second evening of my stay and when I called the manager the following morning, it seemed that the whole building's hot water was shut off. There were apologies made and was assured that hot water was being returned accordingly. I got through with a very cold (and quick!) shower before then but got warmed up pretty quickly because my room's overall temperature was warm and cozy. There was regular hot water since then. Housekeeping and linen change occurred on the third day as advertised; meanwhile, I had to be responsible for room upkeep during those days without maid service. Guests have the option to get fresh towels before then to exchange with their unclean ones. Pets are allowed in the hotel and the next room had a dog. (I think there were a couple of dogs on my floor on the 4th). I never saw them but heard them bark a few times or make door-scratching noises. The barks behind closed doors would startle me every once in a while so if I return to this hotel for another extended SF stay, I would request a room away from pet owners. Summary: Overall, I felt safe and comfortable in this smaller establishment., located just a few blocks from Union Square. I walked a lot to explore the city and used accessible public transit (mostly from Powell/Market Street area) to take me places. I'm out most of the day so coming back to my room at night was like going home to a cozy apartment. (Guests are given a front-door building entry code). I liked the kitchenette and walk-in closet. Although the private bathroom with the claw-foot tub was rather small, it was functional. I had the TV throughout the time I was in the room for news and to watch some of my favorite shows. The hotel's amenities were adequate for my needs and the cost was reasonable. The managers were friendly and responsive to my queries since I first came upon their website information from my own SF hotel/lodging internet search. I don't know if Halcyon Hotel is for everyone so I can not make a recommendation either way. (Note: I didn't need any computer connection or access so its unavailability was a non-issue for me; it may be for others). From my experience, my expectations were met (safety, budget, comfort) and have no major complaints. Just as any lodging in a major city, be reasonably alert and use common sense when venturing the streets. Have fun!

“Off the beaten path, but a very nice hotel.” I stayed in this hotel for 4 nights while in Chicago for a conference at the Chicago Hilton. This hotel was only 2 miles away and considerable cheaper than the rooms at the Hilton. While very close to downtown, the South Loop Hotel is in an area that is still revitalizing. So there's not much directly around the hotel, but there is a bus stop across the street that takes you right into downtown on State Street. The hotel is also walking distance from Chinatown, but I'd be a bit cautious about walking this distance alone or at night. Despite having to take the bus into downtown, the hotel was very nice. The rooms are spacious with a flat screen TV and a nice bathroom with better than your standard bath tiles and flooring. The lobby was quite nice and the staff was very friendly. One of the best things about this hotel making it an extraordinary deal is the free parking. Free parking this close to downtown Chicago is unheard of! There were only 3 bad points in my stay. The AC did not work very well, but the temperatures during my stay did not warrant blasting the AC so I was still confortable. On my last morning there, the hot water did not work, so no shower for me. Also, the maid service was a bit lax in the bathroom. There was a smudge from some moisterizer that I accidently dropped on the counter my first day in the room and it stayed there during my entire stay. Clearly no one was wiping down the bathroom sink and counter. However, I can't complain to much because, let's face it, I don't wash my bathroom counter every day at home. Would definitely stay here again. It's quite a convenient location for Soldier Field and not too far from downtown. If you are willing to take the bus, it's very convenient.

“Not a 5-star, but fine anyway” The Omni is the old Four Seasons, and it does show its age a little. The service is very good but not outstanding, and the rooms are upscale but not opulent. As some of the other reviewers have commented, the hike to the hotel from the self-park facility borders on the absurd, winding past an office building, down a hill, through the pool area and up some stairs. It's free, though, for hotel guests. Don't pay a 5-star price for this hotel or expect a 5-star facility and you should be satisfied.

“Good place, more than what I expected” Stayed here for one night on business, it is a little hard to find from the highway, especially at night. Room was a good size, clean. No problems with staff. I left my cell phone in the room and was unable to collect it until early afternoon and then had it right there at the desk.

“Newer Hotel - Decent Neighborhood” Spent one night here in Late July 2010. Didn't spend a lot of time here as we arrived late afternoon and left the following morning. This is a clean, well kept Hampton Inn, located near the hospital and a little ways from the main part of downtown Boston. Saw some complaints earlier about the neighborhood and the noise. I found neither to be as bad as others made it out to be. Granted I was here only 1 night, but anytime you stay in a hotel within a busy city, you have to deal with noise and other people. In fact the morning of my meeting was so nice, I walked the 1.5 miles to their building on Washington St, though I could have easily taken a bus, which has a stop 2 blocks from the hotel. Good parking set up as well for a city based hotel, with the deck right across the street and no valet to bother with. Breakfast was the standard Hampton Inn affair, which has improved in recent years. Only complaint would be that the kitchen area gets a little tight during prime time. I would happily return to this property in the future.

“Absolutely Outstanding!” I recently spent two nights at the Ritz-Carlton Georgetown while on a business trip. It was very hard to leave. The hotel itself is built in what used to be the area's incinerator. As a result, the layout is not at all traditional. One gets to the rooms through a smallish tunnel that was most probably used for stoking the fires. Red brick is everywhere. It's not a typical Ritz-Carlton. Guest rooms are lovely. I was fortunate to be able to stay in a suite but the "standard" guest rooms are anything but standard. They're top-flight. Couple that with high-end Bulgari toiletries and outstanding service, and you have a definite winner! The service was impeccable! I had a couple of occasions to call the front desk and the responses were almost immediate. Very impressive! The only tiny hiccup was that my appointment with the hotel's sales manager ran about 1/2 hour late However, that was because Brittany Spears and the Pussycat Dolls had spent the night at the hotel post-concert and had needed some special attention before they depatured. Hey, sometimes you're out-ranked! I ate breakfast and lunch at Fahrenheit, the on-site restaurant, and enjoyed both. While prices reflect the convenience (which is to say they're higher than an off-site restaurant), both the food and service were excellent. The Eggs Benedict -- my standard for judging a restaurant's breakfast prowess -- were the best I've had in a long time. The Hollandaise sauce could have had a bit more lemon punch for my taste, but the English muffins were more like crumpets: very tender and delicious. For lunch, I had tastes of their fire-roasted tomato soup, the roast butternut squash soup with candied walnuts, and a simple Turkey Club with fries. All were tasty and well-prepared. If you dine at Fahrenheit, be sure to get a window seat, which will give you a great view of the smokestack. Another note regarding the excellent service: just before leaving for a brief appointment, I called housekeeping to ask that my room be made up while I was gone. (Call me fussy, but I hate coming back to an unmade room.) They were very prompt and had almost completed their service when I returned to the room. The attendants were both polite, but one really got my attention when she addressed me by asking, "How are you, Mr. Carl?" (My last name is a bit unusual and gives some people difficulty.) The fact that she had my name at her disposal -- and, more importantly, USED it -- earns her very high marks in my book. Finally, the hotel is close to the last vestiges of the Chesapeake and Ohio lock-and-canal system that George Washington envisioned as something of an interstate highway system. Very historic and very interesting! You can read more on my travel blog, TravelPro55.blogspot.com, but all I can say is this: if you have the opportunity to stay at the Ritz-Carlton Georgetown, TAKE IT! You won't be disappointed.

“Does the job of an airport hotel well but nothing out of this world” Nice hotel though the shuttle to and from the airport is a bit hit and miss given the sheer number of folks who want to take it, the fact that it only runs twice an hour and that the alternative involves a $16 cab ride (minimum fare to and from the airport - what a rip-off). I stayed in a room far away from the registration desk which I didn't mind given the peace and quiet that it afforded me, plus the four minute walk did me good. The room was ok; nice bed, workspace and TV but alas with the tiniest bathroom you have ever seen. I managed to use it ok but it did feel cramped. Dinner at the restaurant was nice and the servers smiled continually throughout their service. The bar serves a great margarita, too. The gym on the ground floor, while not huge, did the job well and was not too busy at 6am. The executive floor lounge serves an OK breakfast. Unfortunately, it offers lots of processed food, but also fresh coffee and a nice fruit platter (though it does take a while to get replenished, so be quick!). I didn't have time to use the pool, but should I return, I will do next time. In all, it is a good hotel that serves the Sky Harbor PHX hotel well. I would just question whether it is worthy of a Hilton status and should be rebranded as a Hilton Garden Inn.

“Unbelievable, unacceptable” The Courtyard Boston Downtown/Tremont is very conveniently located in the theater district. Access to I-95 is a few blocks away, and the neighborhood seemed quite safe with plenty of restaurants in the area. That exhausts my list of positive things to say about the Courtyard. As others have noted, the parking is a startling $43/night even though the garage is across the street. My room was very small, which is understandable since this is a fairly old property. What was not understandable was the utter lack of intelligence displayed in the layout of the room. The desk area that occupied the outside wall of the room had a set of 3-4 drawers along the right hand side. The drawers, however, could not be opened because they were blocked by the bureau that sat next to the bed - see the picture below. This bit of room design failure would probably have escaped my notice (I rarely use the drawers in hotels) if it weren't for the fact that the desk was not level and the drawers slid open on their own and came to a rest against the side of the bureau even after being closed. The bathroom is also extremely small - there's just enough room for the toilet and a sink. There's not even a vanity on which to place one's toiletries. Hopefully my room is not representative of others in the building. In short, I simply cannot recommend the Courtyard Boston/Tremont.

“Very cool fun hotel.” I came here for my birthday this year and I was really happy with the choice to stay at the Intercontinental. The place looks awesome! Very well decorated. The room was awesome too except for that the bathroom was really weird. There was a window above the bed that didn't lock or anything and it slid open to the bathroom. Awkward. But other than that it was great! There is a cool bar downstairs, a place to get sushi and then a restaurant. Couldn't be better! I had an awesome time and I can't wait to go back!

“So So” We got a great rate, and were told all of the renovations (pool, club floor, lobby) would be done by our visit. One out of 2 happened! Good: At the end of ped. mall, with a free bus and many restaurants, and near the capitol. Room had an incredible view of the mountains and comfy beds. Bad: Many of front desk staff were hum-ho, ask for a manager for all issues as others seem not to care. Pool and club floor not completed. Promised bkfst and evening appetizers on floor, instead given coupons to go to lobby restaurant (had really wanted the club floor reception space as many in our party). Bathroom small! Rooms look renovated but common sense items not there - no refridge, no listing of hotel ammenities or hotel info, not a stick of stationery or notepad to jot on. Gift shop items on floor for renovations, out of newspapers at 9:30am on a Sunday. Took 20 hours and 3 phone calls to get AC working (squealed like a car alarm on arrival) - Guest Relations did keep checking on it and were apologetic. The concierge works like 3 hours a day, no brochures by desk. The front staff could answer no ?s on Denver - both times another guest in line was super helpful. They send you on this confusing walk thru empty, eerie feeling convention floor to get to the second building (reeked of cigars) - use the walkway on the 2nd floor. We did get a reasonable refund on our already great priced room, with very little complaining - get the feeling they are used to people complaining as you would expect more of this chain. Would stay here again, if negotiated super rate but would assume it to be average at best.

“Not bad but keep searching, you'll get a better deal elsewhere.” I gave this hotel a second chance recently for business, and it was marginally better than the last time I stayed. The location is good, ample parking, and the a/c kept the room nice and cool. I found the decor very dated, and the fact that they let people smoke on my floor disgusted me because it stunk up the entire area. Who lets *anyone* smoke in a building anymore? Gross. Bring your own l Lysowipes and give the room a good wipe down- it's hurriedly cleaned at best. (This applies at most hotels, mind you). I did take advantage of the food here and there out of desperation or extreme hunger, but it was not remotely imaginative- they could learn from European counterparts how to ensure guests partake. It's worth a short term stay if you get it for a decent price. It certainly isn't worth the corporate rate they charge my company so I've found higher star hotels in the same area for at least 40-60 dollars less.

“Awesome mid-town location.” After reading some of the other reviews - you may be having doubts about the Roosevelt. Don't believe the hype - The Roosevelt is a sure bet for an extended stay in NYC. We stayed for 5 days and throughly enjoyed every moment. The hotel is in the BEST location !! Walking distance to the highlights of NYC. Fifth Av - one block, Grand Central - one block, Chysler building - one block, Times square - two blocks, ESB - a few blocks, etc etc etc !!! It is one of the greatest feelings to walk out the front door of your hotel and be right in the middle of the action. While you are in NYC you don't want to waste time travelling. The rooms are cosy (re - small) but very adequate - let's face facts - who goes to NYC to spend time in their hotel room ? Great TV and a clean functional shower. All you need. Remember - this is New York - space is at a premium. The hotel bar is very plush and a great place to have a drink before heading out on the town. The hotel is quite large so is normally busy at most times but the staff are helpful and professional. There are about 6 elevators so getting in and out usually takes minimal time. All in all a great choice for a stay NYC !

“A curate's egg!” The Edgewater is a really quirky hotel. Strange combination of brushed metal and log exterior. Very keen staff, tiny rooms. great location on the waterside, terrible location on the train track side. Very tidy rooms but they are tiny. Superb bathroom but no storage space. Every good point is really good, every bad point is pretty bad. The staff try really hard and overall the stay was OK. I couldn't give it a terrible review, nor a great one!

“Consistently excellent” I've stayed at the London approximately 10 times over the past few years. The rooms are fantastic. Each room is a suite, with a large working area, separated by a door to the bedroom. The bathroom is great, too, with an excellent shower. The furnishings are lovely, the bed is so, so comfortable. It can be pricey, but you can get really good deals, especially mid-week. The location is great if you need to be in midtown. The people are remarkably friendly for such a trendy place - they always smile and welcome me back at the front desk. Bottom line: I have no complaints about this hotel. it's near-Ritz quality, and generally much more affordable (but not inexpensive).

“Just an average Days Inn” I stayed in this hotel only one day when returning from Indianapolis to Moscow, so I didn't pay a whole lot of attention to choosing. The place was neat and well-kept, but don't get fooled about the location. It's quite far from the central parts of Manhattan, and the northern part of Broadway where it's located is in fact quite gloomy and without much places of interest (or, even, places to eat or have a drink). Surrounding streets are just an average quiet New York neighborhood. And it takes a long walk South for the impression to change. The hotel itself is quite standard, with standard features and polite staff. Nothing exciting. May be a good stay if you're okay with the location.

“Great stay at a great Chicago hotel” AC POWER Suite, had power at the desk, and some at the night stands, but still found myself running an extension cord to get the laptop to the bed. BATHROOM Spacious, clean, had a bathtub and walk-in shower. Plenty of nice smelling toiletries. BEDDING Comfortable, clean. CLEANLINESS Found the whole suite to be very clean. INTERNET Internet had average connection speeds. LOBBY Welcoming, with easy access to the Nordstrom stores. PARKING Expensive, even for Chicago, valet parking and self park in a mall across the street. Had to circle several times to find a self park spot. STAFF Very nice, not rude at all. Front desk staff was very accomodating. TELEVISION Widescreen large LCD with decent digital channel selections

“A+” We stayed at the Mansion during the Final Four tournament last week and had a wonderful time. As eveyone says, the hotel is on the smaller, more romantic side, and not big and boxy like a Marriott or Hilton. It is in an excellent location and also as mentioned has a parking garage right across the street, where we were only charged $6 a day. The hotel pool is small and quiet, with a bar and lounge chairs. The bar area has coffee and pastries in the morning and is a nice alternative to the rather pricy restaurant. Rooms are on the smaller side (we had a Courtyard/Poolside room) but are very comfortable and well appointed. I would only suggest an upgrade in the shampoo, conditioner items, as what they offer is a bit below the quality one would expect in a nice hotel like this. We did not experience much noise at all, and were pleasantly surprised given that the hotel was full and very busy. One night there were some conversations in the hall outside our room, which we could hear, but they were not overly loud or disruptive. There is a business center, which charges $6.95 for $15 minutes (another thing that could be changed would be to provide free internet!) and a spa in the hotel across the street, which we did not visit. The Alamo is a 10 minute walk, as is the Rivercenter mall and almost all the downtown sites. VERY convenient to everything! Check in and out were perfect and we found the staff to be very pleasant. We would definitly return.

“Wonderful Hotel, Amazing People” We were moved into this hotel after the Hilton Garden Inn gave away my room due to a mix-up. I am SO grateful that happened. In town over the weekend of August 28 to move my daughter into NYU, and yes....Hurricane Irene hit us. The hotel itself is lovely, and when you step into teh door it is af the noise of Times Square no longer exists. Take the elevator up to the sky lobby and it's a lovely space with a nice bar and restaurant. The check in staff could NOT have been nicer, especially considering that our fligth from Los Angeles was delayed and it was 2:30 in the morning. The room was quite large by New York standards, 2 double beds and plenty of space to move about it. I have been in much more expensive rooms that were waaaay smaller. The hotel staff is the best I've ever come across. It was a crazy weekend with hurrican e bearing down, all transportation halted, a skeleton staff of mostly management, and yet you would have never known it. Staff was unfailingly pleasant and maintained a great sense of humor throughout the weekend, the concierge was really helpful with all the travelers who were trying to rearrange air and train travel. They really went above and beyond to reassure guests and make us feel comfortable. I will recommend without hesitation the Hilton Times Square, and I plan to stay there whenever I'm in town visiting my daughter.

“Grand lobby, small rooms, pitiful service” Just completed a 4 night stay at this hotel (stayed here last year for 1 night). Grand Lobby- the hotel is very proud of its heritage (a tv channel dedicated to it). the lobby is grand- from a past era. the rooms were recently renovated, but they're really tacky (peacocks on the carpets, green silky/satin cheap pillows, lime green velvet chairs, etc). The rooms are the size of closets. To the point where they feel unsafe because the hallway door opens directly next to your bed. needless to say, even at 12AM when I tried to sleep, i could hear everything in the hallway and surrounding rooms. its like there is no privacy what so ever. I can get over the small rooms since its an old hotel, but the service is seriously awful and amateur. 1). To use hotel wireless (at $14.95 per day- even for HH Diamond members such as me) you have to get this UFO device from the Front Desk. I inquired, they gave me the device, I had to fill out a waiver, then the desk agent went on a 7 minute search for the instructions. Finally, i told her to stop looking and just had them keep it. seriously, a 12 minute ordeal to pay them $14.95 per day. And, they never offered this at C/I. 2). At checkout, i was charged 8 times for the $14.95 internet. Was charged $85 for the restaurant- which was not my charge- and when I brought it up to the FD, they said it couldn't be fixed until Tuesday- that is, if they decided that I wasn't the one who spent the $85. Why don't they read the folios before they put them under your door- internet charge twice a day for four days?! 3). On day 3, the housekeeper came to my room at 8:30AM, opened the door while i was asleep...i asked her to come back later....left for the day, returned at 6pm, and room hadn't been cleaned. 4). I had access to the exec lounge- it was pitiful. dirty tables, dirty dishes everywhere. only used it one time in 4 days and that was just for coffee and an apple. the food offerings were gross (the turkey on a deli plate was green). So, overall, don't go here. it's just a hassle. there are so many better hotels in this city. i'm a hilton diamond member and won't be back.

“At Library Hotel Home away from Home” I stayed at Library Hotel 4 nights during Independence day weekend. This Hotel is in perfect location and in the vescinity of many attractions. I booked ahead of arrival the day tours as well as g Broadway shows for each evening there - 15 minutes walk to theaters saved me a bundle on taxis. Passed by every night through beautiful Times Square. The Saturday Broadway show was canceled and I did not book any day tour for Saturday, so I had an opportunity to enjoy the Hotel whole day. Let me tell you guys, the minute I walked out of taxi, early in the morning, I walked into Heaven. I came early because I had a tour booked for the morning of my check in. The staff was extremely curtious, beyond any Hotels expectations. Even if I would forgotten anything they would be there to remind me /ask if I needed any reservations or suggestions etc. Take advantage of it, it put my mind at ease. I normally don't mingle or commune much with the hotel employees as they are busy and even if there are no people at front desk does not indicate that they are just there standing and doing nothing, in fact they are busy with checking and ensuring that each guest is expected and accommodated accordingly and in timely manner and much more. When I arrived early in the morning, my luggage was stored, and in a minute I was in the taxi and off to my tour. I arrived back at check in and in a minute was accompanied into my room. The front desk staff was always there for me even if I did not bother to ask. The girls in the kitchen knew I was looking to toast my roll and would do that for me every morning or helped me with peanut butter (I had no glasses and could not see well small prints). This was my first time single on vacation and I was a little not at ease, but the hotel staff made me feel comfortable and accomadated to all my needs, like getting a taxi for me or finding a book, I loved being pampered. I could write forever about every detail, but check it out for yourself. My room was cozy and the bed was the most comfortable I ever slept on and that alone was a big plus after a long day of sight seeing-s and shows. I loved the way the room was designed - piece of art, oh and I always found a place to sit during breakfast or wine and cheese. I extend my appreciation to Igor, Mike, Billy and the Hotel Manager. And I wish I knew the girls' names in the kitchen thank you so much for being there for me and offering to help even if I did not ask for. Back home my mind was still on vacation. I came back and had so much to share and talk about the good time I had at Library Hotel and tours and shows. It took me a week to get back to reality. Oh, and if you are a smoker, they have an excellent garden terrace on 14th floor beautifully decorated and landscaped, and one last thing I enjoyed playing the baby grand piano every evening after coming back from theaters.

“Not For Me.” Guided by previous reviews, I was expecting something really special from this hotel. We booked one of the "Prestige Suites" directly through Sofitel. These rooms are all at the front of the hotel. We were on Floor 8 of 14. Don't expect much of a view. There is major refurbishing work going on directly opposite the hotel ,so expect noise from 7am onwards (mainly from rubbish being thrown into the back of skips from a great height). No warning or mention of this inconvenience anywhere on the hotel website. This work looks like going on for many months yet. One bedroom suites are large, clean and chilled with a huge bathroom and plenty of wardrobe space, with loads of gadgets like a Bose sound system that I never worked out how to operate. On the whole, the reception staff seem to feel that they have that air of superiority. Continential breakfast included in the price was hugely disappointing. This consisted of two croissants and a slice of bread per person with fruit juice and tea/coffee. We were expecting cereal as well as cold meats/cheese like at other hotels, but this was all extra. Be aware that the "a la carte" breakfast during the week could turn out to be very expensive.

“Beautiful hotel, nice location, great food, spotty service...” We arrived at the Joule Hotel around 4:00am after a lengthy drive from Memphis. Check in was a little spotty, as the overnight desk agent seemed bothered by our interruption of his evening and failed to make eye contact with us even once. The valet was present when we arrived, which was a nice thing to not have to search for someone to take our car. We booked a package that included valet parking and breakfast - although no one was quite sure of the breakfast procedure. We received a note at check in stating to call in-room dining and place our breakfast order - none the less everyone seemed confused about if to or if not to present a voucher and where we might obtain those vouchers from. Our breakfast came to the room incomplete and took nearly 55 minutes. The excuse given by the representative when we called to inquire about timing was that the hotel was sold out - a bit confusing - isn't that what the ideal situation is for a hotel? We needed to run some early morning errands and waited approx 20 minutes to obtain my car from valet. There were 3 parkers on duty and they did not seem busy. I'm not certain where the garage is for this property, but it must be a long haul, as it took a great deal of time for our car on both occasions. I mentioned the above concerns to the morning manager on duty, Shirecka, who was very kind. I explained to her that I did not want a discount, but simply to resolve the issues going forward. I don't mind paying for services, but I'd like to not have to worry about the services being upheld at every whim. She did a fantastic job of apologizing and even sent me a nice note and amenity to our hotel room. The pool is fantastic and our server (I don't recall her name) was excellent. Despite the large crowd throughout the day, she never let our drinks get empty and provided the most kind and efficient service I have seen in quite some time. The hotel restaurant is great and the quality of the food in room service is excellent. I might note that the banana ice cream should not be missed if they have it... All in all a nice experience, but some service training to work on...

“Nice - but worth the high rate?” I stayed one night previous to this at another property but moved to the Sofitel because it was the location of my meeting. The previous night, I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn as it was much cheaper and my Hilton Rewards are better. I moved to be onsite for my meeting. The rates are high but you do get a little more. The shower and separate tub are great. The room amenities are fantastic. The internet is not free which always dissapoints me. The bed rivals any of the Hilton "The Bed" rooms I have been in around the US. Very plush sleeping accomodations. The guest service is above and beyond when it comes to concierge, business services and personal waitstaff/bar service. The food is extremely overpriced and therefore I did not eat here. The Sofitel is 2 blocks from the White House and several places to eat in the DC area. McPherson Square subway station is 1 block away and I found the trains to be clean and easy to get around on. If I visited for business, I would stay again but I think the difference in rate to other similar properties is worth the change. The difference in amenities and service do not quite warrant the substantial increase in rate per night.

“Hôtel un peu daté, mais très bien situé et offrant de magnifiques vues” Chicago, détruite par un incendie ravageur à la fin du XIXème siècle, a dû se rebâtir, et pour ce faire a été un riche laboratoire urbanistique, architectural et social de la métropole moderne. Se promener dans la "Windy City", c'est l'occasion de découvrir toute la richesse et l'héritage d'une ville, tant sur le plan artistique que de l'art de vivre. Pour partir à la découverte de la ville que les Américains décrivent volontiers comme "aussi trépidante que New York City, mais avec des gens sympas", l'hôtel Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza constitue un bon point de départ. Par son emplacement, il rend accessible à pied ou en métro les principaux points d'attraction de la ville. La station de métro Merchandise Mart est immédiatement à proximité de l'hôtel, que l'on peut rejoindre directement par un couloir. En outre, des taxis sont toujours présents en bas de l'immeuble. L'hôtel est logé du quinzième au vingt-troisième étage du W Mart Center, ce qui vous obligera à faire une halte dans le lobby, pour ensuite rejoindre votre chambre par un second ascenceur. L'hôtel est quelque peu daté, et dans un style typiquement nord américain, c'est-à-dire confortable mais pas exactement d'avant garde. Les chambres supérieures sont de taille moyenne, et décorées de façon un peu désuète. Les lits sont confortables, et l'ensemble est propre mais manque certainement de fraîcheur . Les salles de bains sont plus vieillottes encore, et nécessiteraient sans doute quelque programme de rénovation. Le point fort des chambres supérieures dites avec vue est précisément la magnifique perspective qu'elles offrent sur The Loop. Le buffet de petit déjeuner, proposé à 17 dollars dans le lobby, est complet et de bonne qualité. La piscine couverte est de taille réduite, mais agréable. Le personnel de l'hôtel est véritablement chaleureux (comment résister à une réceptionniste, typique Big Mama noire américaine, qui vous appelle sweet honey, ou à un vieux serveur d'origine grec qui s'enquiert pendant le petit déjeuner de la vie politique française!), et fait facilement oublier le standing de l'hôtel qui est un peu défaillant. En résumé, l'hôtel Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza est un établissement un peu décati mais finalement très honnête, dont les deux principaux attraits sont la situation et la bonne humeur du personnel. Il peut à ce titre constituer un bon point de visite de la ville, à condition de ne pas être trop exigeant sur les infrastructures.

“Great hotel; great value” I booked our room on Hotwire for $67/night. My main goal was to get a hotel with free parking that was not too far from the Riverwalk. I was pleasantly surprised with this hotel. The carpet and linens appeared to be brand new. The room was very clean spacious with two twin beds, a sitting area with a pullout couch, chair, coffee table and desk with free high-speed internet access. The kitchenette had a small frig, microwave and coffee maker. The trolley to the tourist attractions stopped at the corner and was very easy to navigate. The complimentary breakfast was excellent. The pool was a little small but there were always towels available and it was clean.

“Great Stay/Great Service” I stayed at the InterContinental for 4 days with my teen-aged son, and had a wonderful stay. Despite some negative reviews about the newer tower, our room as spacious, well appointed, with a great view. The staff at the hotel went out of their way to make us feel welcome, and we especially enjoyed the comfortable beds. The location was perfect and we were able to geet around easily from the hotel. Victor was especially accommodating, and arranged to have a refrigerator delivered to the room at no charge. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay!

“Great” If you want to pay 350-400/ night to stay in downtown San Francisco look elsewhere. I agree with all the other favorable reviews. For a little over100$/night this hotel is a bargain. Great location to everything Bart,muni,cable cars restaurants. Very nice staff,and the entire hotel is very clean and smoke free. Would certainly stay again.

“Always a Delight!” One of our favorite hotels in Manhattan! We love all of the Library Hotel Collection properties, but this is the most quaint. The DVD and books selection were a bonus, especially to help with unwinding after a bustling day in the city. The rooms are modern and well-appointed. The location is convenient and the wine and cheese reception is devine. The hotel offers complimentary Contintental breakfast, too! This is a wonderful boutique hotel.

“The Michelangelo Has some Of the Nicest Rooms in NYC” I've stayed here several times most recently this past March for 4 nights. The hotel is just north of Times Square and close to everything mid-town has to offer. It's also very convenient to the subway so the location is very good. Mid town gets very crowded and noisy at night but the Hotel is situated in such a way that the rooms are relatively quiet for Manhattan. The rooms are well furnished and very comfortable and among the largest you'll find in a NYC hotel. They serve a small continental breakfast in the lobby every morning. The workout room is very small and in the basement. Overall I would say the staff is OK, not overly welcoming but they get the job done.

“Good Place to Stay” We enjoyed our nicely decorated and comfortable room which we booked at the very good senior rate Marriott often offers. I was especially pleased that the manager remembered my name and greeted us in a friendly manner.

“Really liked this hotel!” We really liked this hotel. Stayed on the 17th floor of the main building and had no trouble with elevator availability. The morning breakfast and evening manager reception were really great touches. Lots of options for breakfast, although we did miss having bacon (but the sausage and pancakes were quite good). The "extras that aren't extra" are really appreciated. Room wasn't really big, but more than enough for two, with a large bathroom. Loved the restored bank building. Wish we'd made use of the rooftop terrace - especially when we moved to a hotel that didn't have one. Pools were small and filled with kids and teenagers, so we didn't use them, plus the color of the pool itself made the water look murky. Great downtown location. This hotel sold me on the Drury brand, though.

“One of my fav hotels in NYC!” I stayed there for 3 nights over the summer during a business trip. The hotel was top notched on many levels! You cannot beat this location in NYC! It is right in the meatpacking district which is close to many great restaurants and shops. The staff were friendly and helpful. The rooftop was beautiful. My room was spacious by New York standards. I will stay there again for sure!

“Gutes Hotel nach oder vor dem Flug” Zum Hotel: nettes Haus in einer inselartigen Ansammlung von Hotels etwa 15 Fahrminuten vom Flughafen und 5-10 Fahrminuten von den Mietwagenverleihs entfernt Positives: + Hotel war sehr ruhig und sauber + schönes großes Zimmer mit sehr bequemem King Size Bett + sehr freundliches Personal an der Rezeption und beim Frühstück + einfaches kontinentales Frühstück im Zimmerpreis enthalten (leider alles auf Plastikgeschirr) Negatives: Nichts Fazit: als preisgünstiger Übernachtungsstopp in unmittelbarer Nähe des Airports durchaus in die engere Wahl zu ziehen.

“Great location” Excellent location for the the touristy stuff: Macy's, the Empire State Bldg, Herald Square, Times Sq, just walking about Manhattan. Thomas, the friendly, professional concierge, is a wealth of local info, hit him up for what you need. Make sure you hit Brendan's on 35th, just up the block from the hotel, on Thursdays (only Thursdays!) for the most incredible corned beef sandwich I've ever had. No kiddn. This stuff is sublime. Only served 1x per week. A couple of Guinnese brews & heaven has called. Hotel design is kinda urban bland monster (whoever designed this hotel really blew a great opportunity to make a cool design statement....I mean, isn't that what these designer people are supposed to do ?!) with no soul. Housekeeping is cool, front desk worked to get me in early check-in (thank you!), all in all a good hotel featuring an above-average staff of professionals with quiet rooms in a central location.

“Excellent for airport and business” This is a nice big Hilton. It has the big grand entrance and lobby with lots of staff available to assist. I would stay here again. I ended up in a huge suite - so while this might not be too helpful for others, it is quite impressive. Very very large space and nicely apponited. The lounge on 16 was nice. The bed and sheets were excellent and comfortable. If I were going to pick something that wasn't just perfect it would be the air conditioning. It didn't seem able to keep the room really cold - but it wasn't a problem (because it was March - might be a bigger issue in August). It is very easy to get to the airport - but much nicer than the usual airport chain hotel. Yes you are next to Greenspoint mall. In the daytime that can be a good thing. At night I wouldn't go for a run in the area. However, the hotel is across a large divided road and insulated from any real concerns. The parking lot seemed maybe a little tight. I found a space but there weren't too many to choose from. If I were planning to travel into town I would look for something closer in - this would be on a main corridor into the city which means heavy traffic at peak times. However, if I needed an airport hotel I would stay here agian.

“Location Bargain” Terrific central walking distance location. Excellent windows - I think any view is buildings. Atypical of many NY hotels - larger walkin shower bathroom. I was happy with my high floor, next to the elevator noiseless king. This property exceeded my expectation. It is an absolute first consideration for my next visit.

“Hotel der Spitzenklasse” In beste Lage direkt am Times Square. Ich hatte ein Zimmer im 33. Stock mit einem Super-Blick. Das Hotel kann man mit gutem Gewissen weiter empfehlen. Sehenswürdigkeiten wie das Rockefeller Center, Grand Central Station sowie das Empire State Building und viele andere Sehenswürdigkeiten, sind nur ein paar Gehminuten entfernt.

“Excellent, Convenient Location and Pleasurable Stay” The Westin San Francisco is well-situated, 1 block from the BART Montgomery station. At $8.10, the ride from San Francisco Airport (SFO) to the hotel is a steal. The hotel is located in Union Square with an abundance of restaurants and shopping in close proximity. For business travelers, it's only a short walk to Moscone Center. It's also near the MUNI (to go elsewhere in SF) and within walking distance of Chinatown (10 minute walk). Geraldine at the front desk was absolutely fantastic and gave us a room on the 35th floor. The rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows, so the view was spectacular. The shower had a soothing double shower head. Decor was modern and clean. Beds were comfortable. The concierge was also helpful and friendly. I enjoyed my stay here and would definitely come back.

“We will definitely stay here for our next Chicago trip” We stayed at the Fairfield for 5 nights on our Fall Break, and had a wonderful time. First, when it says it is conveniently located to Michigan Avenue - it is true. It is about a block and a half off of Michigan Avenue right in the middle of miracle mile. I traveled with my husband and my 9 year old daughter, and we walked to Navy Pier, the Watertower (many trips to American Girl), to Grant Park, and to the Art Institute. We drove to Field Museum which we could have walked to had we been a little more ambitious, but I am glad that we drove because we were exhausted when we left. We took a $9 cab ride to Willis (Sears) tower and to the theater district (saw Lion King). Second, the rooms are clean and quite spacious! Third, the staff was wonderful and the breakfast was huge (a couple of days we skipped lunch). There is a 7-11 about a block away where we would pick up soft drinks and snacks on the way back to the hotel. The only downside was the cost of parking. We did valet because no in/out charge - regular parking did not have in/out privileges. There is a wonderful (beautiful) cafe at the corner of Michigan Ave (Grand Lux Cafe) which was recommended to us by our bellboy. We loved it and it had a wonderful kids friendly menu for my picky daughter.

“awesome location...good fit for this trip” as soon as i was able to move my room from next to the elevator (i can hear the cables moving) i was more confident at having a good night's sleep. the downside was that the room away from the elevator shaft was way smaller than the one by the elevator...so if you have a hearing deficiency, go for the bigger room! rooms were clean and staff was efficient. location was great!

“Vitale is overrated - needs a little more value. . .” The Hotel Vitale is overrated in my opinion. It's lacking in some very nice touches such as an array of toilet items (free), papers left by the door and free coffee in the room. The operative word here is "free". The Vitale is set up to encourage you to spend more money. The room's array of treats - chocolates, etc. are in full view to entice you into eating and buying. Bath items for sale are displayed in the bathroom. The view is fabulous and the location is good. But, the staff is not trained properly - does not know the menu at the hotel (room service), does not know the room configurations and is not particuarly warm. The Hotel decor is very modern but kind of cheesy. The Meridan in Vienna is very modern and sleek and expensive and wonderful. While staying at the Vitale I thought I was trapped in a popular design on the cheap show on TV. The wall art is made up of pictures wrapped around wood blocks and the overall effect in my opinion did not give the hotel a 5 star aura. The free workout room is very, very small cramped and dark. I'm glad I tried the Vitale but I'll be staying elsewhere in the future where there's more value for my dollar.

“Empfehlenswert” War übers Wochenende da (Ende März 2012), da die Preise doch sehr günstig (für New Yorker Verhältnisse) waren. Nach dem ersten Ärger, dass ich kein Raucher-Zimmer hatte, obwohl ich es bei Expedia angegeben hatte und das nun nur gegen Aufpreis/Upgrade gehen sollte, war ich doch positiv überrascht. Großes, modernes Zimmer mit einer guten Rauchfilter-Anlage, die zwar laut war, aber ich hatte Sie nur an, wenn ich unterwegs war. Das Upgrade wurde mir übrigens dann doch nicht berechnet.

“Just what we wanted” I was a little apprehensive about the place since it's pretty large -but the location just off of Times Square was perfect. When we checked in - after two canceled flights - somewhat haggard from the trip, we were greeted by Enrique at the front desk who could not have been nicer or more welcoming. I had booked the room on TravelZoo and got a really good rate for a high demand weekend so was expecting the worst. However, we were offered a room in the Premier - the sort of mini-hotel within the Millenium. It has it's own entrance across from the main lobby and feels like you're leaving all the chaos of Times Square behind. Somewhat oddly shaped room, but very comfortable with large bathroom, flat panel TV, fax machine, robe, etc. The fitness center is in the main Millenium tower, so if you're in workout gear, you have to cross through the main lobby and take the elevator up. But it's a very nice facility and was immaculate. Housekeeping was great, friendly and unobtrusive. I'd stay here again in a second if I could be guaranteed a room in the Premiere.

“Schoen” Ich war im July 2010 fuer 5 Naechte im Hotel New Yorker, es war sehr sauber und Personal war auch sehr zuvorkommend und hilfsbereit, die Baeder waren nicht greade die modernsten und schoensten, aber okay. Klimaanlage etwas laut und Heizung etwa aus den 1970er Jahren, aber trotz alle dem war das Hotel sehr schoen.

“Reasonbly Priced, Great Location for First Timers” This hotel was a great find last minute. With a trip to NYC booked less than 3 weeks out in the fall, there weren't many recommendable options for less than $250-300 @ night. If you've been to NYC before and are interested in more than just the Square, I'd recommend staying somewhere else, but if this is your first time, you can't go wrong with this place! The only negatives I have are not real negatives, rather nit-picky annoyances. First, have to take an elevator up 20 floors from the entrance, to reach the lobby, then you take another set of elevators to your room. (the elevators are fast and there's not much of a wait, but if you get out to the street and realize you forgot something, you gotta go back up an elevator, through the lobby, up another elevator, then vice versa. Next, anytime you come into the hotel there's a guard asking to see your room key. I'm sure this is to make sure only guests use the hotel facilities, though it didn't appear there were many non-guests attempting to get on the elevator. I used the iron and ironing board the first night and housekeeping never put it away, which I thought was kinda strange. Also, housekeeping comes a bit early... 9-ish or so. It's fine if you're up and at 'em, but if you're out till 4 or 5 each night like we were, it's kinda early, so remember to put out the DND sign. Like I said, these aren't really negatives, but may be helpful to know for some folks. The other reviews have all hit on the positives, so I'll just echo those. The hotel is immaculately clean. The staff is knowledgable, friendly and helpful. Especially the guard Sarito. There are umpteen places to eat, drink, shop, gawk, etc within steps of the hotel. There are subway stations on either corner - ACE to the west, BDNQ to the east. If possible, ask for an even numbered room. There are no poor views - the odd rooms have views of the Hudson, New Jersey, Reuters Building and Theatre District. The even rooms have a view of the Hudson as well, but also the Empire State Building and South Manhattan. The only other thing I can think of is the price of the hot buffet breakfast - $18. If you don't have a voucher for it, there's no reason to pay for it, unless you just love buffets. There are too many other places to eat in the City.

“Good value, excellent service” Overnight stay after cruise and before an early morning flight. Shuttle was convenient. Check in at 2PM, front desk clerks were very efficient and used your name, which is nice. Room was clean and comfortable, but a little dated. If you are on the street side the traffic noise can be heard, but I just put the ac fan on and slept well. Several fast food places within a block. Left before breakfast. Needed to print a boarding pass, the lobby computer was out of order but the desk clerk cheerfully volunteered the front desk one and I printed off my pass. Would stay again if I was overnight at LAX. Price was very reasonable. One odd thing was that the soda machine doesn't take cash, only debit or credit cards.

“Great Location for Universal Exploration” My girlfriend and I recently visited LA and stayed at the Hilton Universal City during our trip. We wanted to be close to Universal Studios to make the most out of our visit and figured that the Hilton would be a good choice. The hotel itself is in a great location, around 5-10 minutes walk away from University Citywalk. We used the valet parking when arriving at the hotel and there were plenty of bell staff to help unload our luggage and get us to the check in desk. Throughout the entire stay the staff at the hotel were really very helpful. They did pretty much everything to make our stay enjoyable. When we checked in we were given access to the executive lounge (as I'm a Hilton HHonors member which was a nice touch) and were escorted to the elevator with our luggage by the check in clerk. The room was large and well appointed, with an excellent work area - which I felt a little odd as I didn't expect business people to check in to a hotel so close to an obviously touristy area. The room was clean and had a nice seating area away from the main sleeping area. The bathroom was also nice and very clean, although the shower was quite dated. After sorting out our things we visited the executive lounge on the 21st floor as they were serving evening appetisers. The executive lounge was a good size, although owing to the appetisers was quite busy. We found ourselves a table near the window and helped ourselves to the meatballs, cheese and bread snacks on offer. Overall I was really impressed with the executive lounge and the staff who made sure everyone had what they needed. When we returned to our room it was really hot inside. We made sure that the air conditioning was on full (which it was) and, as the sun was shining directly on our room we closed the curtains to try and cut out some of the heat. We went down to the pool for an hour to give the room time to cool down. The pool area was overrun with children. It wasn't a relaxing area, but given that we were close by Universal City we expected it to be busy. There were a number of sun loungers and gazebos available for use and plenty of towels available poolside. The pool itself was quite large with a deep area and two shallow areas to swim in. The deeper area was roped off and this encouraged younger children to stay in the shallow areas to play. When we got back to the room the temperature was still pretty warm and we noticed that a fruit basket had been delivered as a welcome gift - this was a nice touch. As we went out to eat on the Universal Citywalk and asked someone at reception to check our air conditioning was functioning correctly and explained that the room was quite hot When we got back the room was still quite warm, but the temperature was a lot cooler than before we went for food. We were assured by the hotel staff that there wasn't a fault with the air conditioning and were offered to move rooms if it was still too hot. As the temperature was bearable and given we were only staying 1 night we decided to stay in our current room and turn in. In the morning we had a quick breakfast in the executive lounge and checked out of the hotel. At the reception desk the clerk apologised for the initial problem with the room temperature and asked whether we'd had any further problems with the temperature of the room. This was a nice touch and showed us that our earlier enquiry had been taken seriously. Overall the Hilton Universal City was a good hotel in a great location for visiting Universal Studios. I would certainly consider this hotel again if visiting Universal Studios, but I don't think I'd stay here if visiting other areas of LA on business owing to the large number of children in the hotel.

“Its not the worst and not the best!” The room was clean although when we opened the dresser drawer someone elses socks were in it. The a/c worked well and the room was quiet. The elevator has a strong smell of deoderant in it but the room didnt. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was clean and had enough towels.The pool was nice and clean (outdoor). The breakfast waffles tasted terrible. I threw it away and then one of the staff members came and had one and he told the breakfast keeper to throw the batter away. Otherwise the breakfast was apples, oranges, 4 kinds of cereal, toast, bagels, baking powder bisquits and baked eggs and sausages. Orange and cranberry juice. A good selection of rolls and small muffins.

“Typical business class hotel” The staff was very friendly and professional, restaurant & bar were good. The rooms are nice but ordinary and the bathrooms are very small. Internet worked great, check-out easy, etc. The hotel was easy walking distance to our meeting and the door staff helpful in directing us to our destination. The bed was comfortable and I liked that the duvet was not overly warm, which was helpful since it was difficult to get the room cool enough to sleep. This isn't unusual at large hotels. No problems, I'd go back.

“prepare to be disappointed” We booked two rooms at the Hyatt through Priceline. We recently stayed at the Hyatt in Lexington, KY - which is only given *three* stars, but is a much superior hotel. We are not the type that are easily annoyed -- I know there are plenty of those on Tripadvisor. But even so, our brief visit was tainted by a few annoyances too much to overlook. First, the good - * The beds are very comfortable * The lobby and atrium is very impressive * The front desk and bellhops are very friendly and helpful * Right in the middle of everything in downtown Now, the bad - * The pool/hot tub is tiny, and closes at 10pm. Worse, the next morning it was also closed with no explanation given. At noon, it was still closed. We could only speculate that they had water quality problems, as the pool was very cloudy. * Rooms feel cramped. * We noticed black mold in the shower. * As others mentioned, Wi-Fi is nowhere to be found except high-priced T-mobile pay service. * The parking garage has a 6'-2" limit. If you have a luggage carrier, you are classified as an oversized vehicle and must pay the $27 valet fee. Overall, it is a pretty nice property that would sit firmly in the 3-star category. Just because a hotel has a great lobby/atrium and location does not make it 4-star if it has all of the shortcomings we found. Unless you are here for a conference or something else, I would recommend trying another location.

“Don't be fooled by the lobby..It's actually very nice..” The hotel staff were courteous, alert and acknowledging of your presence. Never failing to offer assistance when asked or if you looked confused. I never had to deal with bad customer service or bad attitudes. It was all smiles and helpfulness. I personally felt the room was quite impressive. Two chairs, Two Sleep Number Beds, restroom with shower/tub combo, external sink and mirror (not inside the bathroom), plenty of counter space and room for your belongings. It even had a closet. The room was very nice..A++++ When I first saw the lobby I was afraid I would be turning around and not coming back, but after seeing the room, I'm glad I stayed.
