I would describe this hotel as warm and welcoming. Great customer service and very very clean! Pros: Excellent customer service, shuttle, room service *20% gratuity and a delivery charge though are a little over the top in my opinion, but it's a nice option*, very clean, very safe, pool, quiet, yet accessible to many restaurants and shopping..I could go on and on.about the positives of this hotel and I will Definitely stay here again. Cons: No mini fridge/microwave and in my opinion the sleep number beds were not all that great comfort wise, but I do appreciate the effort though. I rested well, but I wasn't impressed with sleep number beds I guess. I don't like firm beds. The lobby is ugly.

“Highly Recommended Hotel at a Great Location” We stayed at this hotel for a few nights and had a very positive experience. The room and bathroom were very large and well-appointed with quality furnishings and products. I needed to purchase a souvenir from the hotel store and would have come back to the hotel late, well after the store closing, and the reception staff arranged to hold the item for me. I really appreciated this. The location of the hotel is very convenient as a base for exploring San Francisco. Should you have a rental car, be forewarned that the hotel and area parking options are quite pricey. There are some terrific restaurants in the area.

“Not worth the price unless you get a REALLY good deal” The main reason I booked this hotel was the $109 per night price I got through another travel website. It was a steal for the $400 per night price tag they normally charge. I knew it was a good jaunt from the heart of D.C. but the subway ride was really fast and the Woodley Park/Adams Morgan station is literally around the block from the hotel. Here are some points from my trip Oct. 2-9, 2008: - Did the online check in but the room and key weren't ready when we arrived. We were confirmed for 1 queen and ended up with a room with 2 full beds instead. - Hotel staff never discussed the hotel amenities and when I needed a computer a few days into my stay I read about the business center in the black info book in the room. When I asked the concierge for directions to the room they never told me I would need both my room key and credit card to access the computers/internet. They charge $9.95 (plus TAX) for 15 minutes of internet access PLUS charge you for any and all printing. Although I did find out after the fact that you can print your boarding pass for free. Staff never told me that. - They charge you $0.95 for every local phone call even if you acciedentally dial the wrong number and hang up and re-dial. You'll be charged for two calls plus tax. - The elevators are extremely slow. Be prepared to take the stairs often. - Received USA Today every morning during the week. - We had to call for toilet repairs twice because the toilets were horrible. I put one single Kleenex tissue in the toilet and it wouldn't flush! - Room was clean but the A/C was the loudest I've ever heard and the television channels were limited. If you're looking for more than a news station or the weather channel you're out of luck. - Unlike another reviewer, we did have a full-length mirror in our room although the lighting in the room is terrible. - I felt like the housekeeping staff was nothing to write home about. We came back once to find that a wet towel was left in the middle of the floor in our room. Another time they didn't remove all the room-service items/trays. They took the bath rug out but didn't replace it with a fresh one. One morning I was awoken really early by extremely loud talking and laughing out in the hall. When I stuck my head out the door I realized it was two members from housekeeping, and I had to ask them to please keep it down. - The front desk staff member was very helpful with teaching us how to navigate the subway systems; however, she also recommended several near-by restaurants one block down Calvert Street. We walked out of two of those restaurants in one night due to horrible service. The only neighborhood restaurant I recommend (highly) is Open City. - The gentlemen at the front doors sometimes paid attention and opened the door upon our arrival but they often ignored us and kept talking to one another as though they never even saw us. Just rude. I don't need someone to hold the door for me but it's polite to greet your guests upon arrival and if it's your job to open the door for your guests you should do so. It makes the guests feel welcome rather than a bothersome pest. - We had the worst experience ordering room service our first night. They said we would have over an hour wait after placing our order. It was after 9:00 p.m. at that point but we said okay. By 10:30 p.m. we still didn't have our food and had to call and complain before we received it. When the order did arrive we noticed several things we paid for weren't included and some of the order that was received was wrong. Not a nice thing to do to your guests who've been traveling all day and just want a hot meal. I expected way more for the price of that dinner. - The only redeeming quality was the hotel somehow knew the date of our anniversary and delivered complimentary champage, chocolate-covered strawberries and sliced oranges. It still didn't make up for everything the hotel lacked during our stay. All in all, I wouldn't stay here again unless I got another exceptional deal. I'd never pay full rate. It's a far cry from the likes of the Four Seasons or The Wynn. Omni Shoreham needs to working on polishing their guest services skills.

“Another great stay” We often stay at this Hilton property and are never disappointed. The bedding is so comfortable and the staff is never anything but friendly. Herb the bartender and Morris the grill cook were fun and great to chat with. The hotel was super busy this past weekend yet all the staff members we came in contact with - and there were lots! - were great!

“Not bad ... but need to do better to get me back” We chose this hotel partly because of its location and partly because it had good reviews. The hotel is in a good location on 17th Street – just one street back from the 16th Street Mall. The hotel room was nice – a king size bed, large flat screen TV and free WiFi. There was a coffee making machine but no sachets of milk – just powdered creamer which doesn’t taste nice in tea which is my preferred hot drink. The bathroom had a huge bath which we would have liked to have used but couldn’t as there was no plug. The vanity basin comprised of a modern porcelain basin which was huge but quite shallow. The sink almost took up the whole width and depth of the wooden stand ... however it was totally impractical and difficult to use as you had to bend much further forward just to clean your teeth over the basin rather than the wide “rim” ... in fact the basin took up so much room that the shaving mirror could not fit on the wooden stand. We found the process of check in a bit odd. The woman printed off a sheet of paper with writing on it and asked us to initial all the paragraphs and then sign the bottom. Turns out one of the paragraphs was about the guest agreeing to pay all charges listed below ... but there were no charges listed below. I told them I wasn’t signing a “blank cheque” and they needed to list the charges. The receptionist found that odd. While the hotel was nice, aspects of the room noted above annoyed me as did the check in process. Even the concierge sitting outside the restaurant didn’t have a sign – again, odd IMO. I thought he might be taking bookings for the restaurant until I asked if he was the concierge. As a guest paying a reasonable amount for a room for the night, I don't think I should have to guess who the concierge is tucked far away from reception and nor do I think it's reasonable for reception to request that I agree to pay charges with listing so much as the room charge for the night ! And further more, when a guest contacts housekeeping and gets the front desk, switching through to another department without hearing the full request and thereby necessitating another call ... not great customer service IMO. While the rooms were nice, I don’t think I would return to this hotel – there are plenty of others in Denver to choose from.

“Very Nice Hotel!” I stayed at this hotel this past weekend. It's not a huge hotel. The elevators are very small. They only hold 8 people. The rooms are a decent size. The beds are very plush and comfortable. The bathrooms are nice and they give you plenty of towels. The only problem I had was that there was no light over my closet door. There was a light switch, but not light. Strange. The restaurant, 'Franklin Exchange' was good. The staff was very friendly. We had a drainage problem with the bathtub, and it was fixed promptly. The hotel is located downtown. We were able to walk to the Covention Center, Georgia Brown restaurant, and down to the Smithsonian and Washinton Monument(15 min walk). I recommend it, and would stay here again!

“Good location, reasonable price” Stayed 2 nights in early October 2011. I stay at Club Quarters in NYC & DC - my employer has a great rate, so this property was better priced than any others available. Next to Farragut West metro station. If you have a car the hotel has a discounted rate with Central Parking, entry on 18th St NW between K & L streets, with elevator to 1020 Connecticut Ave (about 3 blocks away). Great wifi, acceptable workout room with a treadmill, elliptical, bike, some weights. Stay away from the connected restaurant - overpriced with poor service (separate company I think). Hotel staff mentioned a different place a block behind hotel. Rooms are small but clean and well lit. Club Quarters has a 'Night on the House' program for certain nights in various cities (slow dates) in DC, Boston, NYC, SFC, Chicago, Philly, Houston, London.

“Not worth the money” I was "upgraded" and although the room was fairly large by NYC standards it was not really in very good condition and not particularly clean. Location was good. Reception seemed to be a school desk in an empty room. This was a business trip but I believe the price was around $600 per night and it was certainly not worth anything like that.

“Teeny rooms so be prepared” I read previous reviews of this hotel which were quite positive and I decided to stay here for one night for business. On the positive side, It was quite clean, renovated and the lobby was basically a place to check in with an elevator....the restaurant was off the lobby. It's in a great location off Fifth Avenue and 40th Street. I was shocked at how small this hotel is in comparison to other Courtyards/hotels I have stayed at in Manhattan and other large cities. I am actually a New Yorker so I am very familiar with Manhattan and this hotel was located very close to where I had an early business meeting so I thought I would spend the night rather than having to take a very early train in from the suburbs. I checked in about 9PM and the room had a queen size bed, a credenza with a flat screen TV, two night tables and a small bathroom (usually considered the size of a "half bath"). This was the entire room for $419 per nite (including all taxes). It was a good thing I only needed to sleep here and check out since there was no chair (other than the desk chair) to even sit on and you bumped into the bed each time you tried to move around the room! So.....I still say this location is great but be prepared to be claustrophobic in the "queen size" room or book a King or double bed room for a bit more money to have more space.

“excellent hotel” We stayed at the Doubletree Mission Valley Hotel in San Diego on May 6, 2006. It is an excellent facility. The hotel, the room, the grounds and pool area are exceptionally clean. It is a highly recommended place to stay as far as I am concerned.

“Best Service in Chicago” This might not be the newest, swankiest hotel in Chicago, but you cannot beat the Peninsula service. From the doorman to the servers in the restaurant, concierge, room service staff, and housekeeping, the service just shines here. The location of the hotel is perfect for shopping and restaurants. We had afternoon tea at the Lobby, which was just divine. The rooms were not exactly modern, but spatious and decorated with warm tones. TV in the bathroom made a lot of sense as we caught up on morning news while getting ready. I would definitely come back here when I return to Chicago.

“Great renovated rooms and extra Gold/Diamond HHonors benefits” Stayed on the newly renovated 20th floor on the city side. Great rooms that are fully high tech, with better bathroom fixtures, extras like a fridge, safe, bathrobe, etc. See the attached photos. Balconies are nice and terrific views at that level even though I was facing away from the river. No executive floor but Gold/Diamond receives the usual free breakfast buffet (or the 1000 HHonors points), free internet, etc., but here they also add discounts on self/valet parking and 25% off most property restaurants. Location is superb.

“Conrad - Not so rad” I stayed at the Conrad hotel in downtown Chicago, selected for its 5 star rating and attractive low rates. In comparison to most other 5 star hotels in Chicago, this is one of the best properties for the money, which is why I booked here. The location is good, especially in winter months. It is located right across from a mall, so you can enjoy nearby shopping and dining. From the time I stepped out of the cab, I was greeted by a friendly and professional doorman, leading me to the elevator for the reception area. The reception area is neat and informal. This wasn’t the opulent, grand experience like most 5 star places, but it is simple, efficient, and worked well. I would say the décor is modest and uneventful. Although nice, you won’t find much of a WOW factor here. (Until you see their breakfast prices...I will get to that.) My check in went smoothly, and I informed the hotel that I had 2 separate reservations that needed to be merged together. I informed them I would be staying 2 nights, not one. The friendly check in reception gentleman told me that this would be no problem, and the following day, to just come down to reception to have my keys recoded so that they would still work. No problem. I made my way up to the rooms where on my way, I found the elevator areas adorned with beautiful potted orchids; the look was very beautiful and elegant. Once inside my room, I noticed 2 things. (1) The bathrooms are really beautiful, big, and full of amenities. They are marble, gorgeous and complete with matching bathrobes. (2) The TV is huge. The not so great thing was that my view was directly into an office building. I literally could see what they were eating for lunch, etc, so it wasn’t just barely visible. It was like I was in there with them. No bother. I drew my blinds and moved on. (When you check in, ask for a view of NOT into an office building.) A small perk of this hotel is that they do a complimentary tea service each morning until 10 AM, which we used and enjoyed. At night, they put out hot coco and marshmellows for guests, which is cute and a nice touch. We did like that. What sort of struck me as funny at this hotel is that they pride themselves on having a pillow menu, where I think you can pick between 4 different kinds of pillows delivered free to your room, plus others at an additional cost. The irony in this is after waking up, I had concluded that the Conrad pillows were the least comfortable I had ever experienced in a hotel. Funny. (Maybe I should have ordered up a special pillow?) Downside to the room – I didn’t like that the once stocked mini bars are all empty now. The only use for them now is to put your leftovers in. Me? I like to be able to grab a snack or a drink from the mini bar. I found it strange that this was a 5 star hotel with a little, pathetic, empty fridge. Despite this, however, all in all, the room is quite suitable, I think most people wouldn’t have much an issue. Here is where you may take issue with this hotel...breakfast prices. Wow. For a complete breakfast in the dining room ,it is $24-$32, depending on which “breakfast meal” you get. It is very pricy on this, (but delicious and well prepared / served.) However, as good as it was, it just wasn’t “$60 for breakfast for 2” good. My opinion is, there are nearby places that you can find that are a nice walk for $28 for 2. We asked the front desk for a recommendation and he said that Yolk was good. (Most Nordstrom’s have a café, and had I thought of it, you probably could have gotten something awesome and cheap there, inside, right across the street from the Conrad.) All and all, I simply found the breakfast menu to be a turn off all together. Breakfast at the Park Hyatt, arguably a nicer and more upscale hotel, is less at $16 for room service complete breakfast, just for perspective. My opinion is that the Conrad should consider their cost of stay vs their cost of breakfast and maybe consider reducing. Here’s where my stay got kind of annoying. The housekeeping belted on the door at 8 AM on a Friday morning. A little early, don’t you think? We told them to come back later, and we got out of bed and hung the DND sign on the door. Fine. Jet lagged and needing a nap, we retired back to the bed, only for the bellman to WALK IN to our room at 2 PM WITH THE DO NOT DISTURB sign on the door. Have you ever even heard of such a thing? We yelled out, “We are staying another day,” from the bed and he left. We drifted back to sleep when...RING RING. Are you kidding me? We are being woken up again. It is the front desk, now calling to apologize for the bellman walking in. They caught the error in the computer now, where the hotel room bookings had not been merged like I had asked them to at check in. Now, I am really pissed. It was just all the getting woken up. The only point of booking the room was to have a luxurious sleep after a 16 hour nonstop flight. This rather ruined it. I wished this hotel could have been a little more organized and perhaps have housekeeping come by at 10 AM instead of 8 AM on the dot. Just too early for folks that are here to relax and unwind. I would describe this hotel as quiet, tranquil, spacious, unfussy, unpretentious, classic, non-trendy, simple, elegant, and calm. It really just depends on what you are looking for. This property competes in price point with the Sofitel and overall, I would stay at the Sofitel over this hotel for the money. This is a decent property, but didn’t blow me away. I would describe it as luxury on a budget. Affordable rooms, but you can probably do better if you are patient and look.

“Great for a night at the theater” The best thing about the Paramount Hotel is it's location and price compared to other downtown hotels. It's perfect if you have tickets to the nearby Paramount Theater and want to spend the night in Seattle. It's a Coast Hotel and the service standards are higher than most hotels. Designwise, it could be any hotel in any city. The corner rooms are the nicest and have nice city views.

“Good value, nice water park” Upon arrival we were upgraded to a Casita. The room was spacious and clean with a frig and microwave. We came here b/c of the mini water park and it did not disappoint. The pool was grea, as was the lazy river, and water slide. The also had mini-golf as an option as well. The workout area was well equiped and spacious. The staff was very professional and attentive throughout the resort . Our $89 package came with breakfast, which was average at best. The only thing I would warn anyone on is the prices by the pool for food and drink, but than again that's to be expected. This hotel was a great value during the hot summer and we will be back as my children loved the water park.

“A nice place to stay, but plan for breakfast elsewhere!” My wife and I stayed here when our price was accepted on Priceline. I was able to upgrade to a King size bed at no additional cost. The room was a bit dated, but had a large flat screen tv, refrigerator, microwave and coffee maker. The bed was fairly comfortable. The down sides to the room was that there was a huge mirror on one wall, next to the bed. This might be a plus for some, but I didn't appreciate it at all. Another down side was that the air conditioning had to run all night to cool the room down. Suggestion would be to arrive early if you can, and turn it on before you go out for the evening. Breakfast-I have seen reviews that were positive. We did not have that experience. Yes,they had waffles, toaster waffles. not fresh. The breakfast room was very small with minimal seating. There were guests there that took up all the space and I had to reach around them often to get food that I had left on the counter. They ran out of decaf coffee, orange juice and the milk was hidden in the refrigerator. We would have had a more relaxing and enjoyable breakfast somewhere else, but since it was included in the room price, it was okay. Went to IKEA in Burbank later and got a good cup of coffee there before shopping! I would probably stay at this motel again, it was quiet, despite being right next to a freeway, but would probably skip the breakfast. I didn't have a need to use the WiFi so I can't comment on that. .

“Great river walk location, Great Hotel” Great place to stay on the river walk. Very close to the better restaurants on the river. The rooms were very comfortable and clean. Slight problem with the valet. Needed to pick up my car early in the morning, and it took almost 10 minutes for them to retrieve it. Then, when they finally brought it, it had a large dent on it. Still waiting to see if they are going to accept responsibility.

“fun hotel for travelling with kids” The Argonaut is a first-rate hotel in a great location - if you have kids. It is right near Ghiradelli (1 block) and a few blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. I wouldn't have stayed there without kids but the nautical decor, a bit over the top, was a hit with our boys and the location was great for fun, touristy things. Nob Hill or Union Square would be better suited to an adult vacation. The staff treated our kids like they were VIP's and even remembered their names! The doorman (nicknamed "door dude" by my son) was very friendly and helpful. The front desk staff couldn't do enough but the conceirge was a bit disappointing. I was surprised at how little they knew about the city. They could hardly answer any of our questions. When we asked for recommendations they were OK but I got the impression that everyone was sent to the same 3 restaurants. I asked for somewhere that was not touristy and they recommended a place at Fisherman's Wharf! The rooms were spotless and very comfortable although tiny in comparison with just about every other hotel I've been in. One person could hardly fit between the end of the bed and the wall. The washrooms had sliding doors that our kids got a kick out of - I guess it was suppose to make you feel like you are on a boat. The wine reception at 5-6pm was nice - complimentary glass of wine to relax with in the lobby or take to your room. We are walkers so we walked just about everywhere in the city but the cable car turnaround is just across the street from the hotel and the "F" line bus that goes to Union Square (much cheaper than the cablecars) is only two blocks away. This was a fun place to stay and I would have no trouble recommending it but I think I would pick a different, more central location next time. The Wharf is fun but you can only take so much of it!

“Small rooms. Great location” I'm writing this review solely based on room and location. I hardly had any interaction with the staff or used any od the hotel services. Originally I was meant to stay at The Westin Grand Central but there wasn't any power. The hotel is also undergoing renovations so the lobby was smaller than I think it will be. That's all if e but the hallways in the floors were so dark! Everyone waiting for elevators on my floor would comment about the same thing. Dark carpet, dark walls and low lighting. The room was tiny, tinier than almost all the other rooms I've stayed in in the city. The room had two beds. The bathroom door couldnt open completely as it hit the bed. No dresser or desk. Tiny but functional bathroom. Water pressure was fine. Towels were fine. Bed was comfy enough. My biggest grip was the temperature control. The unit didn't work. Heat was blasting so much that we had to open the window and turn off the unit to get the room to decent temp. Location is excellent. However I think you can find slightly larger rooms for a comparable price near by.

“freundliches Personal, weit weg von Downtown” Sehr freundiche Begrüssung, fühlte mich gerade sehr herzlich empfangen. Zimmer war gross, sauber und ruhig gelegen. Leider weite Fahrt bis man downtown ist. Sehr hohe Preise.

“Most Fantastic Hotel Stay Ever!” We stayed for 2 nights to celebrate my son's 8th birthday before spending Thanksgiving w/family in the suburbs. Wow, did everything about this place make it a spectacular trip to remember for all of us! Suite 1211 was amazing - 4 window seats of fantastic views of the city. We spent most of our waking time in the window seats relaxing. Our two boys, age 8 and 9, slept in them - what a treat! The staff went out of their way to do several special things to make my son's birthday special - a suite w/a spectacular view on a high floor, goldfish and birthday cake made out of guest towels waiting in room upon arrival, cupcakes for everyone late that night, balloons tied to a bottle of his favorite soda the next day. It goes without saying that the room was beautifully furnished and decorated, spotless and the bed was super comfy. The Starbucks coffee and pastries in the AM was beyond what we expected. Hot chocolate till 11 with toppings was a treat, as well as the wine hour at night which also included delicious hot apple cider. You can't go wrong by joining Kimpton In Touch - free wireless and $10 mini bar credit is a complimentary treat. We were so sad to leave - I hope we get to go back one day. This is our 2nd Kimpton Experience and we are hooked. The location of this hotel was ideal - close to everything but not in the middle of chaos. Many great places to grab a bite to eat of coffee steps away. Thanks Monaco for a great trip!

“By far and wide, the best!” We love staying at the Renaissance Chicago. The staff is always so attentive, and the property is as crisp as ever. Everything about this hotel says Chicago. From the architecture, to the artwork, and even to the names of the suites. The rooms are HUGE for a Loop property, and all of them offer swollen puffy beds for your relaxation and enjoyment. The location is also great, as it is situated at the HEART of chicago (1 W Wacker, at the corner of Wacker and State... you can't get much more Chicago!) with easy access by L, cab or foot to any other point in Chicagoland. This is my fav Chicago hotel, and I put all of my out of town guests up here, because you have every option in Chicago, from dining, to sightseeing to clubbing at your very doorstep, and when you're done, you have a pristine oasis awaiting you!

“Location, location !” Hotel Penn is situated at an ideal location to base a trip to explore NYC. It is across the road from the Penn Station, a massive hub of subway and rail. From there you can pretty much go anywhere in the city. Also it is close to a large shopping district, featuring the massive Macy's NYC and other specialty stores. The Empire State Building is also only 2 blocks away. Times Square is a short 10 minute walk or if you're lazy, a quick trip on the subway! The hotel entrance and lobby looks spectacular and is very large. We were given a room on the 15th floor which looks like it hadn't been upgraded yet. Hallways and rooms both looked dated. The room itself was spacious and clean. The shower was a little bit cramped but with a working shower and toilet it served its purpose. Being a historic building, there were no ceiling lights and we only had desk and table lamps. We ended up living in semi-darkness as we had to unplug some of the lamps to make room for our chargers as there were not enough power points. Hotel Penn did not have free wi-fi and charged by the minute in their business centre downstairs. Not to worry, as Borders, McDonalds and Starbucks are just outside the hotel so internet access is not a big issue as long as you have a laptop or smartphone. They do not allow early check-in and charge for baggage holding, $4 a bag. We were lucky enough to avoid long check-in queues as mentioned on this website however we did spot long queues during our stay at various hours of the afternoon. I recall seeing a long line at about 7pm one evening and there was only 1 check-in counter opened, thats pretty poor considering the size of the hotel. If you manage to get a good sale rate on a room here, then I recommend Hotel Penn as accommodation in NYC can be costly. The location makes up for any minor complaints.

“Huge difference!” I've stayed at The Plaza several times before they renovated and downsized. What a huge improvement they've made! I was a little surprised for a weekend in August the hotel didn't have the usual busy buzz, but I much preferred that than sifting my way through a busy lobby with lots of tourists snapping pictures. The hotel did a fantastic job keeping the beautiful aspect of the iconic hotel's old world charm and infusing the new at the same time. I spent a great deal of time in the bathroom, how can one not when the tub is so massive. The one small problem, it's not like the Four Seasons where the tub fills up in 60 seconds. It took a very very long time for it to fill. The gold plated faucets didn't look so tacky offset with the white. Bathrobes were plush and comfortable. I didn't take advantage of the vast array of services the hotel offers, but then when you're in NY you want to do more outside than hide in a hotel. I would definitely check out Todd English's food outlet in the basement. It's a great place to grab something quick to eat. The concierge recommended a French Bistro that we were not overly impressed with. It's a very pricey hotel, I would only recommend it for those who want to stay for a special occasion.

“Personable Hotel With Great Location” The hotel was centrally located in downtown San Francisco, which made it easy to walk to surrounding shops and restaurants. It's location also meant that a busy bus stop was right outside the front door but generally the traffic was manageable. The cold and flavored water in the lobby was a nice touch as well as the wine hour on the fifth floor lounge that had complementary coffee in the morning. The "Deluxe King" room which we stayed in was small in size but had good functionality and a decent view of the courtyard and Old Navy store below. Parking was $42/night, which is typical for a downtown hotel, but be prepared to pay the extra fee.

“Fine for business, but not up to Hyatt standards” I've stayed at this hotel a number of times over the past year on quick business trips to Denver. Overall, it is fine. Nothing fancy, but functional. However, it is not up to the standards I'd expect of a Hyatt. Rooms are dated and dingy. Carpet stained. Poor lighting. Bathrooms out of date. Wireless internet is weak in some rooms. Parking is a pain and overpriced for the area. That being said, it is quiet and well located in the Tech Center. Staff is very friendly and helpful.

“Trendy and fun hotel with fantastic rooms” My husband and I spent five nights at the W Westwood and enjoyed the hotel immensely. The hotel is very modern and trendy but not inclusive, they make sure guests feel comfortable and welcome! We tried every amenity except the spa including room service, the restaurant 930 and the gym. Room service for dinner and breakfast was really tasty. We ate at 930 for dinner once and breakfast three times, everything was great, particularly the service and the french toast. The gym was small but well equipped with water, towels and fresh fruit. We stayed in a Wonderful Suite which was a lot larger than I was expecting and was a good value. The bathroom was well stocked with Bliss Beauty products. The bed was very comfortable and we slept like babies all week! The location was perfect with easy access to the freeways and lots of restaurants and shops within walking distance. We would definitely stay here again the next time we are in LA

“Best Hotel Room EVER” My room at the Drake Hotel in downtown Chicago was absolutely the best hotel room I've ever stayed in. It was huge .. it had lots of windows, and was very regal. The staff was great, the hotel was beautiful. And for the price, (given downtown Chicago prices) it was actually a great value. Highly recommended to anyone .. it's also a Hilton network hotel which is why I chose it.

“Maybe 3.5 Stars......” I've stayed at many Drury Inns across the US, so I'm a fan. This Drury is up to par in every respect, but it's right on Highway 6 and Interstate 10, so there's more road noise than I'm used to. Other than that, it's great. Rooms are well equipped with micro, fridge, wide-screen TV, good bedding, above average towells, etc. Staff is excellent which I've come to expect at this chain. Breakfast at Drury's is above average and pretty standard at all the hotels - sausage, eggs, waffles, french toast, bagels, yogurt, fruit, etc, etc. The dining area in this hotel is smaller than in the new Drurys but it works. Happy hour snacks are pretty good, dining next door (Cattleguard) and across the street (Brothers Pizza) is really good.

“Great Hotel and Location” My husband, along with my mother and her friend, stayed at this hotel recently prior to flying out of Detroit early the next morning. I chose the Westin as it has a Park and Fly option whereby you leave your vehicle with the Valet, and they park it for up to 10 days while you're traveling. This has been convenient in the past as well, and it usually ends up being far cheaper than parking your car at the airport or even remote lots. In addition, it's far more convenient in winter weather. When you arrive back at the airport, all you have to do is go to the valet station at the hotel and they get your car. By the time your luggage is loaded, your car has warmed up and you're ready to go. We just leave our winter coats in the car as well. In addition, the rooms are very nice and comfortable, and we even enjoyed a dessert in the dining room before heading to bed for the night. The beds are super comfortable. My only complaint this trip would be that my room did not overlook the airline terminal...it actually looked into the Delta SkyClub. Had we not been checking bags, we would have taken advantage of the security entrance into the terminal rather than going up to the ticket counters. I hope to take advantage of this option another time. This was my 3rd stay at the Westin Detroit Metro hotel, and I can definitely recommend it to other travelers. Regardless of whether it's a business or leisure stay, they definitely take care of you here. Check-in was a breeze as usual as well as check-out. And there are Delta check-in terminals right in the lobby.

“I'd Stay Again” We've stayed at the Westin a few times. It's a great location and the beds are very comfortable. However I have always gotten my rooms via Priceline (less than $100 a night) and probably wouldn't pay more.

“Substitute Hotel Turns Out to be Okay” We booked a 4-night stay online at the sister property to the Springhill, the Fairfield. When we arrived, they had overbooked, and we didn't get the suite we had booked. After spending one night at the Fairfield, management transferred us to the SpringHill, giving us our first night at half price and a $10 discount on our final two nights. I must say, the Marriott Corporation's management team does go the extra mile to make sure their guests are compensated. The room was larger and nicer, and the breakfast was better than at the Fairfield, so we got a better deal. This is the second time we have had a problem at a Marriott property, and both times we were satisfied with the way management handled the situation and the level of compensation for our troubles. Kudos to the manager, Daniel. The SpringHill Suites rooms were well appointed. I have stayed In more spacious rooms in downtown San Antonio, but it was comfortable. Only negative was the small sink area. A word of caution, there are only about 5 employees in the valet parking department that services both the Fairfield and the SpringHill. Give them ample time to retrieve your car. Poor guys are overworked! This is a management problem, so don't take it out on the valet. This property is located at a busy intersection in an very busy city. Expect street noise. It is unavoidable. If you want to stay downtown, there aren't too many places you can stay that are quiet. I know. I have stayed in over 14 of the downtown hotels. For the area (downtown San Antonio), the price was good. I felt I got what I paid for.

“super Lage, super Komfort und sehr freundliches Personal!” Wir haben dieses Hotel nach einer 9-tägigen Rundreise an der Ostküste gebucht um relativ zentral übernachten zu können - und wir wurden in keinster Weise enttäuscht. Kurz den Mietwagen vor der Türe geparkt um einzuchecken, danach das Fahrzeug in der Downtown-Station am BatteryPark entsorgt. Von dort aus ging es zu Fuß mit einer kleinen Runde Sightseeing zurück zum Hotel. Das Zimmer in einem der oberen Stockwerke hat keine typischen New York-Klänge hereingelassen. Es war ein super Schlafkomfort. Wie in vielen New Yorker Hotels war das Hotelzimmer nicht übermäßig groß, war aber mit allen Notwendigkeiten ausgestattet. Fußläufig ist Chinatown in wenigen Minuten erreicht, Little Italy und natürlich SoHo sind ebenfalls um die Ecke. Der öffentliche Personennahverkehr ist von diesem Hotel aus perfekt zu erreichen. Man kommt überall ohne Probleme hin (Canal Street - Metrostation) Gerne kommen wir wieder, es war super. P.S. mit dem Concierge über die Abreise sprechen und nicht über den Terminal die Abholung per Auto/Van buchen... Er hat noch einige Tipps in petto!

“very convenient, great value” I would return here for a clean, safe, comfortable place in an ideal central location for touring, with great service at the front desk. We stayed at the Peninsula a few years ago and that is a knock-your-socks-off world class luxury hotel. This is not -- it's a nice business class Hilton family property. But I would actually prefer to return to this one, instead of the Peninsula, because it is more centrally located, and I don't need to pay for all that luxury when we are out touring all day. We like to walk, and we were able to walk to the boat tours, the old Marshall Field in the Loop, Berghoff, the Sears Tower, Navy Pier, the Magnificent Mile and the Hancock building, all from the HGI. The Peninsula was a little bit further north, less convenient to the Loop, and so we found ourselves using many more cabs. We had a great lunch at Berghoff (weekday lunches on the main floor are as good as ever, including the homemade root beer) and we also had a lot of fun at dinner and great traditional food in a German neighborhood place to the north, the Chicago Brauhaus in Lincoln Square.

“Good, Bad, and Ugly” The Good: Only a block from Central Park and within walking distance of Museum of Natural History Quiet Charming Street and right around the corner from The Dakota (John Lennon's Home) Lots of restaurants within 2 blocks (PINK BERRY!) The Bad: Smallest room I've ever had in any hotel. Even for NYC this was small. Claustraphobic lobby and breakfast room The UGLY: 9-10 angry red bites on my upper body showed up msyteriously after staying here. I would not stay here again, even though the location was perfect for vistiing my friends who live a couple blocks away.

“Quality atmosphere” My husband and I stayed at the resort for a winter golf break. I returned a week later to stay for a few more days with my sister. the room was clean and comfortable and we enjoyed the pool and the service was excellent - only problem we had was noise - a young woman with triplets (toddlers) was booked in to the room next to us. Management was great about listening to concerns. Will return again.

“Good Location, Great View, Friendly Staff” We stayed here for a long weekend in May to take in a few baseball games and the sites. This hotel was in an ideal location for our touring needs. The staff was friendly and very accommodating. The room was clean and comfortable. We would stay here again if we visited chicago.

“Great hotel, top location” This is a great hotel in the center of Boston. Rooms are a bit small, but fully equipped. Newbury Street is right behind the hotel, and all other things worth seeing (ie. Freedom Trail) are within walking distance. We parked our car at Boston Commons for $10 a day. It's a short walk to the hotel and you can unload your luggage before parking. If you're looking for a great hotel in the center, for a reasonable price, look no further!

“What a place!” Usually very expensive, but found a deal through Expedia and directly through hotel. Rooms are some of the nicest I have stayed in - LCD TV, sofa, nice bathrooms. Wish I had more time to spend there.

“Well maintained clean hotel, with very helpful staff, great breakfast” Got this 3-star hotel using priceline and was very satisfied for the price. the staff were very helpful, the rooms, while a bit dated, provided all you need. Internet connection speed was good and allowed some work from room, Very good breakfast served. Hotel was quiet at night and allowed a good nights sleep,

“Pop art style” The Bristol is right in the centre of San Diego and is very convient for sightseeing. The main thing that sets this hotel apart from the others is it's funky decor. OK maybe not high on people's wants when choosing a hotel but it definately added a dimension to our two night stay and made it truly memorable. Look for the original Lichtenstien at reception ! The bed was very suberb and the room had all the features (great telly, minibar etc) to make your stay comfortable. Excellent hotel - highly recommended

“This hotel should receive four circles, but....” I liked everything about the Sofitel Hotel in Philadelphia. I walked into the establishment and immediately felt as if I had stepped back to Europe. The attendent at the front desk spoke with a French accent. My room had a velvet feel with its brown tones and big comfy bed. And, then there was the bathroom - it was perfect. Just the right size, it included both a shower and bath with ample counter space for the sink area. I even ordered room service and had an omelette with fries, which were quite good. Then, I fell asleep and sometime around four in the morning I found out that the walls are paper-thin. The guests next door from me must have arrived from an evening of partying, and I could clearly hear their loud conversations and laughing. I called the front desk, and thankfully, they sent a security guard to take care of the situation within minutes. So, what do I have to say about this hotel? I love it, except for the thin walls. I spend a lot of time in Philadelphia for business and my sleep is very valuable to me during those trips, so I would have to say that I will think twice before I reserve a room at the Sofitel again. Otherwise, everything else is quite delightful at the hotel. Also, it is a convenient distance to so many interesting places - Rittenhouse Square, City Hall, John Wanamaker building, Kimmel Center and Comcast Center.

“Very satisfied customer, thrifty shopper” We were in Houston for our wedding anniversary weekend. Booked the hotel through Hotwire, got a SUPER great rate. Was leary after reading some reviews here. But have to say our stay was VERY good. Room was super, clean, beds were comfortable, granite countertops throughout. Lobby facility was beautiful, all 4 elevators were functioning and were brightly lit and very nice. (We didn't use the fitness center, pool/spa, or restaurant.) Parking, $8/day, was easy in and out, well lit. Location of this hotel is great. NOTE--at check-in, we requested a room away from the freeway and they accommodated us. I'd be leery of having a room that fronts I-59 for traffic noise. Overall, a great stay. (We were on 4th floor, no smells, not musty. No construction that I could see. Several wedding parties going on, but no problem.)

“Great Downtown Detroit Hotel with Top-Notch Service” I've stayed at the Westin Book Cadillac numerous times during the summer and fall months of 2010 on business trips and it is by far, my favorite place to stay in downtown Detroit. Classy hotel with top-notch service from check-in to check-out. Rooms are always very clean and very quiet. Room service is also very good, but expensive. Security is also tops here, because you need to enter your room key in the elevator to access your floor. Workout facilities and pool are also very nice, although the pool is a little chilly for my liking. Valet service can be a little slow, but I've found that to be the case at other downtown hotels as well. I would highly recommend this hotel to others staying in the downtown area, whether for business or pleasure.

“Service and comfort” Don't usually stay in large franchise hotels but the Post Oak could change my mind. Room was large, the exterior window actually opened! Hotel staff very accomodating and helpful.

“Would stay here again in a minute” The staff was all very friendly (even with the small kids) and knowledgable about local attractions. Rooms were nice and requests (for a high floor) were honored. Definately would recommend to others as a fine place to stay in Chicago.

“Needs updates and renovation” This is an older hotel with charm but the room we stayed in needed updates and a thorough clean! The best thing about our room on the 8th floor were the comfortable beds (2 doubles even though we requested a king) and the fact that there were 2 bathrooms. I also appreciated the black out blinds and the Keurig coffee maker. The cons.. peeling paper in both bathrooms and sockets that did not work. A noticeable accumulation of dust/dirt around the edges of the bathroom. Fixtures were clean but dated and/ or damaged (mirror was watermarked? bathroom socket was hidden behind a tissue box and didn't work). I tried to plug the hairdryer into 2 different sockets that didn't work and one of these was coming away from the wall. We arrived late on the Friday night and there were no rooms left with king beds.

“Very good, but could be improved” I stay at the Wardman Park at least half a dozen times a year, primarily for weekends with my wife. Obviously, I really like the hotel and its location at the edge of the Adams Morgan neighborhood. But anything that is good could always be better, so a few areas for improvement. Wireless. The good thing is that every room has wireless computer access. The downside is that service runs at the level of a dialup connection from the 1990s. Also, logging in takes forever, perhaps because of the slow connection speed. Fitness Center. The fitness center is substandard. The machines are old, poorly maintained, and equipped with TVs that seldom work. You struggle to get through a workout. Service. Service is normally quite good, but missed items in the room and a phone line to valet parking that is not answered need attention. Having said that, I will be back. I like Wardman.

“Glad to have a quiet comfortable room” My previously booked accommodations fell through at the last minute. This property was willing to take our group for a three-day stay during a busy week in August. We had been planning on a 1B, but the hotel staff hustled and found us a roll-away so we could squeeze our group into a typical 2Q room. The room was clean and set up with a micro and coffee station which was helpful. Pro: Staff are friendly and accommodating. The room was quiet (recommend getting a room at the end of the hall - a long walk but much quieter), clean and comfortable. The AC was a bit noisy, but very effective and refreshing during a hot week. There is a laundry room in the building which was also a plus. There is ample parking, which is very convenient. Reasonable cost. Con: the public areas are not well maintained. The vending and ice machines were removed from our floor, leaving a depressing gaping space which we passed on a daily basis. The housekeepers were not organized, on several days we were in the room in the morning and they just never came back. When I asked for some coffee since we didn't get room service, they promised to bring it and I noticed later they put it on someone else's door. Neutral: We were never able to make it down in time for breakfast, so I can't comment on the quality. We ended up at the nearby Wyndham for breakfast (walking distance). They have a full service restaurant and a Starbucks which was handy. Similarly, I saw the pool outside, but did not try it. We had a car, so we also didn't have the opportunity to use the airport shuttle, although a good feature. Please note - Google was a bit confused about the location of the hotel. I drove back to the CVS and Marsh grocery store and the nav system sent me to the wrong side of the highway. not a big deal, but recommend you use the actual address when navigating.

“Good service, nice stay” Stayed here a week while visiting Denver on business. I was originally given a double room but the front desk gave me a king room after I requested the change. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was good. The location was also close to several good restaurants.

“Would definitely recommend!” I spent one night at the Parker Meridien while in NYC with my husband for a concert at Lincoln Center. The location was great - close not only to Lincoln Center but also Carnegie Hall, Central Park and Broadway. The rooms were large enough, beds very comfortable and nice Peter Thomas Roth products in the bathroom. There wasn't a coffee maker in the room, but there's a Starbucks directly across the street! Staff was very pleasant and I'd definitely stay there again.

“Sweet Home Chicago at the Hotel Palomar” Practically perfect in every way. From "D" the doorman to the burger at the fantastic Sable Kitchen & Bar, the Hotel Palomar is the place to stay in Chicago. Immaculate, quiet, fantastic location and very professional staff- you really can't go wrong. Please see a detailed review on my blog at www.tripscout.blogspot.com.

“Showing some wear but I still have a soft spot for the Madera...” We just returned from a long weekend at the Hotel Madera in Washington DC. We travel to the DC area often for work and for pleasure and have stayed at the Madera 5 or 6 times throughout the years. It is one of the older Kimpton hotels in the DC area and is showing some wear. I’m thinking they may be close to requiring a bit of updating. We had a spacious room on the 10th floor with a balcony. The rooms are still very stylish however; much of the furniture was a little scuffed and I had forgotten how small the bathrooms are. They no longer offer personal Aveda bath products and have opted for the bulk bottles of shampoo, conditioner, and shower gel screwed to the wall in the shower. This I did not like. Yuck. Reminds of being at the gym and for some reason I feel it’s a bit unsanitary. Glad we brought our own bath products. The room was clean and the bed was dreamy with great Kimpton linens. Front desk service was decent but not great. They were courteous but not very friendly and we really did not feel very “welcomed” as we generally do at Kimpton properties. The Madera is located in the DuPont Circle area and is close to the Metro. It’s kind of a residential/Embassy area with plenty of really cool restaurants and bars all within walking distance. A friend told us about an Italian place called La Tomate. It was excellent. We also recommend the Double Decker “Hop on Hop off” red bus. Very cool. For $35 you can travel around the DC area on three different routes for 48 hours. It’s a great way to see the sites, especially when the weather is great. Even with the hotel issues described herein, the Madera is one of the first DC area hotels we stayed in some 6 to 8 years ago and introduced us to the Kimpton hotel family. I have a soft spot for it and would still recommend it especially if the price is right. However, I really hope they give it some needed TLC...

“A Good Hotel With A Lot of Potential” The Crowne Plaza has secured the perfect location for all types of travelers to Philadelphia. The hotel is on Meeting St. and is in walking distance to almost everything you could want. The historic district is about a 15 minute walk, the high end shopping neighborhood is a ten minute walk, and beautiful parks and grand old building are always within view. The hotel is now undergoing a few minor renovations, like the elevators but the rooms seem new and are very comfortable - full of the usual high-class amenities and the bed is very comfortable. The hallways are outdated and ugly, but the hotel makes up for this with an ultra-friendly staff who is willing and ready to answer any request with a smile! I would also add that for a busy part of town this hotel was very quiet. All aound great hotel if you can score a deal for under $150.00

“A Major Star in Hollywood” Just recently stayed at this boutique hotel for business purpose and little site seeing. The hotel is a about a good 5 min walking distance to all of the main shops and points Hollywood Blvd. Accommodation wise the hotel is very clean and well maintained. Staff is wonderful and friendly especially the front desk. You get free Internet access during your stay and also they provide you with free drinks and snacks 24 hours. The beds are very clean and comfortable, I felt like I can stay indoors all day long. The bathroom is also well kept especially the clean showers. Also they have a washer and dryer facility on the bottom floor if you need to clean your clothes. If you are looking for a great place to stay with a comfort feeling. Look no further. Magic Castle Hotel is your star in the sky for your stay in Hollywood.

“Great Location” We have stayed at this property a handful of times, and each time it has been great. Their service is consistently excellent. The rooms are always clean. We slept like babies on the uber comfortable beds. Our rooms have always been on at least the 12th floor and the views of the city both during day and night are fantastic. Ask for a room on the side of the Boston Public Library. The bathrooms have tubs that are great for soaking. During check-in, the line moves fast (there is usually a small line) and they offer snacks and flavored water upon check-in. There is a Starbucks directly outside of the hotel property, which is right in Copley. The property is incredibly clean and the staff (cleaning, check-in, etc.) cares about their jobs. The negatives about this property: ridiculous amount for internet ($16?!) and they do not validate parking. The only parking available near this property is at least $15-30/per 24 hours. This is a great location for business, sightseeing, or anything as its right in the middle of everything.

“Cool Hotel with unique Location” My friend and I were in the Los Angeles area for four days and decided to stay in LA on our last day before taking our early flight out of Burbank Airport. We picked Dragon Gate Inn b/c of the Trip Advisor reviews and we were not disappointed! First of all, they let us check in early and the staff at the front desk gave helpful info on where to eat and how to get around using transit. This is right in Chinatown with shops and markets very nearby--the Post office is right on the hotel premises for mailing off all your postcards. The LA Union Station is a nice 10-15 minute walk or you can take the 25 cent DASH bus to the station and other points around the City. Highly recommend checking out historic Olvera Street which is by Union Station. The rooms were clean and spacious (double queen standard room). There is supposedly wifi and dsl available, but we did not have a chance to check this out. The Dragon Gate rates low on providing all the bells and whistles/complimentary stuffs other hotels may provide. But for the value and location, it cannot be beat (only a 25 minute supershuttle ride to Burbank airport for us). I know my friend and I will make it a point to come to Dragon Gate again. As first time visitors to LA, the Dragon Gate Inn really made an impression on us.

“Not up to Westin standards” We stayed one night at the Westin LAX prior to a flight. Our room had no hot water that night. At 9pm, a trio of strangers entered our room--the hotel had assigned our occupied room to them. This woke up our small children and was upsetting. At 11pm, housekeeping attempted to enter our room. Again it woke up our children. Probably won't return to this particular Westin.

“Tiny rooms don't justify the price” The decor of the lobby, bar, and restaurant are VERY cool. The staff at the reception friendly. However despite having reserved a room with a ling-size bed I ended up getting a room with a queen-size bed, which was so small, that a bigger bed would have not fit. This was also the first hotel I have ever stayed that didn't have glasses in the room, not even plastic cups. I finally got a bigger room, on the 2nd floor which was extremely loud all night. After breakfast in the hotel restaurant, where the waiter jelled at me at almost assaulted me (and other guests), I check out and moved to the Millenium Broadway a few blocks away, same price and standard, bigger rooms and quiet.

“Great Deal!” Got a great deal at the Holiday Inn Express Midtown this past weekend, which included breakfast, parking and tickets to a local exhibit. The rooms were clean and spacious and more that adequate. The free continental breakfast featured cheese omelets, cinnamon buns, muffins, bagels, cereal etc. The location is great...right in the middle of everyhing. Would definitely stay again.

“I was wowed” We stayed at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront for 3 nights over 4th of July weekend. Two episodes in the hotel lobby set the whole tone for me. First, the desk clerk was happy to see us. Not because it was in her script. And not with a paste-on-smile. She sincerely enjoyed her work, and wanted to make sure that we enjoyed our stay. ( I wish I could remember her name, but her badge said she was from Ohio) A few feet away, they had a kid's check-in. 2 hotel staff, both with polo shirts rather than blazers and ties, were giving the kids grab bags and talking up the weekend. The kids in the elevator couldn't wait to show us their new sunglasses, etc. It's a big hotel, located next door to the convention center. But, they make a big hotel feel personal, not corporate. I was wowed. Only shortcoming: the parking ramp is not well marked. We moved the car 2x each day, and had trouble remembering where we parked. The hotel doesn't own the lot, so I can't fault them...but even putting A, B, C on the posts would allow us to remember where on the 3rd floor we left the car.

“Good Solid Place to Stay” As others have commented, the rooms are small. The hotel makes up with a great location (between 5th & 6th Aves) and great staff. Basic but very clean rooms. If you are staying awhile and have a lot of luggage, that could be a problem as there is a very small wardrobe and no real place to store your bag. I was there the 4 days and could barely hang all of the clothes I needed to. Note there is construction going on right next door starting around 7am. I was on the 16th floor, not facing the street (1604) and I heard no noise but once outside the building, it was there. For a business trip or a short stay, this is a good place to stay.

“Nice hotel, very well located” First, the location: the Grand Hyatt is located in the perfect place in downtown Seattle, close to all the main shopping centres, 10 minutes walk to the Pike Market and 3 minutes walk to the monorail station, leading to the Seattle centre and space needle. Also, about 2 minutes walk to the light train station, going to the airport. This is a very convenient and cheap way to go to the airport. Single ticket only cost $2.75 and it takes about 25-30 minutes to get to Seattle TAC airport. The room itself was very large, with a very large bathroom containing a shower cubicle and also a bath tub. When I booked the room, there was a promotion for three nights for the price of two. The promotion also included breakfast. When I arrived, they told me that breakfast would be room service. I was not sure how much I could spend each day, but had some eggs, toast and coffee each day, and all was included. They also gave me access for free to the lounge on the 27th floor, which has a nice view and some free drinks and appetizers. Tip: Wifi at the hotel is very expensive. However, you can get free wifi from all the Starbucks in town. There is a Starbucks coffee place inside the hotel, so you can easily use one of the comfortable hotel sofa just outside of Starbucks and use their network for free.

“Don't get the room above the dumpsters.....” Location: great, easy walking distance, even in miserable weather, to the Convention Centre, stores, restaurants, etc. Inconspicuous doorway on Chestnut into a lobby and you take the elevator to the 2nd floor to check in. Room: Given room on 2nd floor. Expressed concern about noise, told it was a "very quiet room". Not on main street but buffered by an open car park, back of another building and an alley. However in that alley are at least 8 dumpsters and it's used by very large delivery trucks. You don't need an alarm clock as you'll be woken up easily by 6 a.m. even on Saturday. Why didn't I complain? Because I assumed that the dumpster noise would be one morning not all three. Cross eyed with fatigue, tried to take afternoon nap - thwarted by noise from dumpsters with stores discarding garbage and lots and lots of breaking glass bottles. Yes, the room was quiet but only at certain times of day/night. Room small, fine for one person, updated bathroom, very clean, comfortable bed. Free wireless that worked well= big plus. Took ages for shower water to run semi-hot, felt guilty as they have a "green" policy and lot of water wasted. Staff very friendly.

“Good Location - Friendly - Good Stay” I stayed here for 5 nights recently and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The hotel is located in a place where I hadn't stayed before so I was unfamiliar with the area. There are some nice restaurants, a great authentic Chicago bar - Kasey's Tavern nearby. The rooms are VERY spacious,nice and clean. The rooms are open and large and don't feel cramped at all. The restaurant attached - Custom House - is very good for drinks and dinner... although not the best for breakfast - but there are plenty of other choices for breakfast. The staff was friendly and helpful. This hotel is on my list for a return visit.

“Great Staff, decent location” Had a quick overnight stay for business at this Hampton in November 2011. The front desk attendant and housekeeping staff were very friendly and strived to make sure you were satisfied with your stay. It had all the standard Hampton amenities, the room was spacious, modern and clean. One elevator was out of service the limited time I was there. One quirk in the layout was that you had to walk past the laundry room/cleaning HQ between the front desk and guest rooms, not a bad thing, but usually they tend to hide this loud, humid area from guests. Location - It is right off of I-35 and my room looked right at it. The Alamo & Riverwalk area are located a few blocks over a down, but still pretty walkable. One thing I did notice on my walk there was the birds. Wow, were they noisy! Hundreds of these black birds sqawking everywhere you go. All in all a decent place to stay if you're passing thru town and want to see the downtown sites.

“Beware of construction and inconveniences” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Islandia for two nights to attend a business meeting. As has been noted by other reviewers, this property is undergoing a major renovation and it is a construction site with all the usual inconveniences -- passageways are blocked off, noise from the work going on, limited amenities. If you don't mnd any of these distractions, you will be OK here. While I am not at all fussy or persnickety about accommodations, I think this hotel would be better off closing entirely until the renovation is complete. I have stayed here before and enjoyed it very much. With the renovation going on, a guest has to contend with a "restaurant" set up in one of the ballrooms, with a limited menu. The lobby is in a temporary location and the buildings with the guest rooms are in various stages of construction. There is no pool at the hotel (unspeakable in San Diego!) and guests have to go to a nearby hotel if they want a swim. My room was in the Tower, and was one of the newly renovated rooms. It was very nicely appointed, with Art Deco style furniture, a flat screen TV, and a balcony (Which I couldn't use during the day because of the noise and dust of the construction), but had no coffeemaker. You should also know that this hotel is out on the Bay, and is a $25 or so cab ride to downtown San Diego, making it one of the more inconvenient places to stay right now if you get cabin fever. Once the renovation is complete, the hotel is supposed to be a luxury resort with $300 per night rooms. I will probably not stay here ever again, in that case. I should also note that the hotel staff performed their duties with great courtesy and professionalism despite all the racket and confusion going on.

“Great location” On my last visit to NYC, my boyfriend picked the Chambers Hotel because of its location. I have had drinks in the bar area a few years ago , but I never stayed at the hotel. The front desk people where amazing and helpful. It was a pleasant arrival. The room was a bit small , but cute. It had a sketch pad on a desk in the sitting area. The bed was comfortable and the pillows where down. The room was very clean. The bathroom was small, but what I didn't like, was that it wasn't really that private. There wasn't a bathroom door ,just sliding cabinets that separate the bedroom from the bathroom. The lighting was awful , So it was hard to get ready to go out. It was located close to shopping and the appointment that my boyfriend had. It worked out ok for the two nights we stayed there but we both agreed we would not be staying there again. The hotel did not have a gym. You would have to go out and walk to the closest gym. The restaurant at the hotel was really nice. I did enjoy that. But I have stayed at a lot of better hotels so I'm a little spoiled . I like a makeup area, which this one did not have.

“A bit on the "tired" side...” This Marriott's a bit on the "tired" side -- public spaces are OK, but elevators had no air or air-conditioning (frankly, they were like a sauna). The place is just a little beat up and in need of a renovation. It's probably time for Marriott to "rebrand" this one as one of their other hotels (if it was a Hilton, they would've made it a Doubletree by now). However, Marriott already has a Courtyard, Residence Inn, Fairfield Inn, and Springhill Suites practically next door, so I'm not sure what they'd rebrand it to! On the "plus" side, front desk folks were efficient and competent and the rooms were standard for a Marriott.

“Great Location, Rooms Need Some Work” Location could not have been better for my needs, very short cab ride to anywhere I needed to go. Parking of $35 a day seemed to be a bit excessive but what are you going to do. Person who parked the car and checked us in was very courteous and nice, no problems with the staff at all. The room on the other hand needed some work (see photos), tub filled as you showered, by the time you were down you were ankle deep in water, porcelain on the tub was badly chipped and the tub should be replaced. The pub that is off the lobby was very lively every time I when in, bar staff was very friendly.

“Another stay which was fine” Popped back in last Saturday for another night stay visiting Chicago for dinner with a friend. Slight delay at check in less than 5 minutes. Got to the room and it was fine. The only issue was the thermostat for the air conditioner needed a bit of work to sort it out. Bathroom was clean and the decor was ok. I'm not over enthused with views from rooms as I tend to treat the room as a place to get changed and sleep in - nothing more, I am not known to lift the bed to check for things. I paid $180 for the night, my companion quite liked it and we have to remember this was not purpose built as an hotel so the construction aspect of the property is not as good as say the 4 Seasons (which I find pretentious and unfriendly) or the Westin (which I found soulless). So choose which you prefer. I like the Palmer and the Silversmith but they are too far away when you only have 36 hours to meet up, shop and get on your way. So all in all I was happy.

“Confortable room--Expensive parking” Our single king room on the 8th floor was large, quiet, and comfortable with a coffee maker but no refrigerator. The room was clean and newly renovated. Bed and sheets were comfortable, but the towels were rough. We only stayed Saturday night, and heard zero construction noise. The room had a large desk and comfortable office chair, but the small light on one side did not provide adequate illumination. I thought the room rate of $134 plus tax was a bargain for the area, but parking was $46 plus $6 tax. The nearby Sutter Stockton garage ($33.50) is an option, especially for longer stays.

“Great for business travel” This is an excellent business hotel, centrally located in the dupont circle area and within walking distance to many attractions, restaurants, bars. The rooms are a bit boring, but impeccably clean and the service is great; breakfast buffet is overpriced and with limited choices; m brasserie has decent (and expensive) food- pleasantly surprised; there is also illy coffee shop serving excellent expresso; overall, a convenient chain business hotel, but a bit overpriced ( internet should be included when you pay 289 per night for a standard room) and lacking character.

“Un hotel para gente chic.” Me encanto the james. Es como un hotel boutique. No tienes que caminar por grandes vestíbulos para llegar a tu habitación.esta decorado con muy buen gusto. Moderno. Con camas y almohadas deliciosas. El primer dia tuvimos algunos desperfectos en la habitación. A la regadera le salían chorros de agua por todos lados. Se mojo todo el baño. El espejo de aumento del baño estaba roto. Y el sofá de la habitación estaba muy sucio. Pero hable a la recepción y inmediatamente arreglaron todos los desperfectos de la habitación. A los huéspedes que les molesta el ruido de la calle les proporcionan tapones para los oídos. Los porteros del hotel Lucas y Alejandro son una maravilla. Te solucionan todos tus problemas. Y la hacen de traductores. Son los únicos que hablan español en el hotel. La ubicación del hotel es maravillosa, esta entre el loop y la zona de las tiendas. El bar del hotel es muy ambientado. Necesitan una limpieza las alfombras de los pasillos. Los closets son muy chiquitos. Si regresaría al james. Es todo mi estilo de hotel Es un hotel diferente.

“Gorgeous historic renovation in downtown Chicago” The former Reliance Building, an iconic early skyscraper, has been renovated as the Hotel Burnham. If you love historic reuse, this is a top notch project. Many of the building's original details remain, such as an iron interior staircase, the mosaic floors, the original office doors, etc. The rooms are the usual chic Kimpton decor, customized for the building's era. Excellent restaurant, although the menu is limited. But there is all of Chicago out the door so that wasn't a problem. Very nice staff, especially Darnell at the front desk. The only negative is the rooms are smallish, because of the vintage of the building. Very well done within the space, but if a lot of room to spread out is important, book at least the King size room.

“Like Walking Into a Black & White Movie Set” This hotel is really amazing! I felt like I was walking into an old black and white Hollywood movie set. It's small and hidden right off of the noise of Broadway. The building was originally designed by Gilded Age Architect and Designer Stanford White, the scandalous architect of the original Madison Square Gardens (and was also famously shot to death by the husband of one his lovers on its roof top theater) so it's steeped in some fun history. The overall theme of the hotel is art deco and it's completely perfect. The furniture has a luggage inspired feel, the bedding is masculine and streamlined and the rooms are very large by NYC standards. The bathroom was better than any I've seen in NYC. It had a heated toilet seat, spa tub and 12" rain shower head. The room is controlled via the phone so you can adjust your lighting, room temperature and drapes with a push of the button on the phone. The hotel also lends out ipads and ipods for free. The art deco bar on the second floor is really swanky. I would skip breakfast at the Lamb's club. They seemed to be going for something unique, which I appreciate, but the unique ingredients were utilized at the expense of taste.
“No complaints” Great location, wonderful room, fantastic food. Simply put - one of my favorite hotels in the US (and I get around).

“What do the words "reservation" and "confirmation" mean?” Reservation Details • Confirmation Number: 80426899 • Your hotel: Courtyard Denver Cherry Creek • Check-in: Friday, August 5, 2011 (03:00 PM) • Check-out: Saturday, August 6, 2011 (12:00 PM) • Room type: 1 Bedroom 2 room Suite, 2 Queen, Sofabed • Number of rooms: 1 • Guests per room: 5 • Guest name: • Reservation confirmed: Friday, August 5, 2011 (18:01:00 GMT) • Guarantee method: Credit card guarantee, Visa Above is the confirmation/reservation I received via e-mail. Notice the room type - 2 beds and one pull-out sofa. What was delivered to us was a single King Bed Room, so instead of needing one pull-out sofa, we needed two. Hardly the end of the world, and the accommodations are fine - not great and not terrible - and yet, I find myself wondering what does it mean to make a hotel reservation? Given that we had made the reservation earlier that day, we would have chosen a different hotel had we known this would be the case. Two things: 1. Please don't tell the customer you have something to deliver when you don't; and 2. please just be up front in the communication. the clerk was about to send me to the king room w/out the courtesy of telling me it was not what we had reserved. The only reason I found out was because i saw the look of concern on her face and asked about it. She told me the two bed rooms had all been taken by guests already at the hotel (again, why did they tell me earlier in the day they had the room I requested?) and that if the room they WERE offering me was not acceptable, I could connect with the hotel manager about in about 20 minutes. Hm. It's 11:30 pm, I have three tired kids to get to bed and I want to spend time chatting with the hotel manager about something he could not fix? I am thinking a bit of basic customer service training could help. The experience: a mid-level chain hotel experience. Nothing more, and maybe a little less.

“Romantic hotel, great location” The staff at this hotel is very courteous and helpful. The room was a little smaller than other hotels, but it was charming and the beds are very comfortable. Our room had a bay view and it was very romantic to wake up to that every morning. This hotel is close to many attractions at the Wharf and the cable car turnaround is next door. My only complaints were the lukewarm water (we were told the pipes were being worked on) and the high parking cost.

“Perfect location” You can't do better than this if you want to be central - steps away from the start of the Freedom Trail. The hotel is as you'd expect from Kimpton, quite buzzy and stylish but still friendly. We were there during Hurricane Sandy and they organised movies and an extended wine hour whilst we were stuck in watching the rain go past - I thought this was a great touch. Breakfasts and room service meals were good quality and the service was always friendly. Yes, it's expensive. But you get what you pay for!

“One of the best locations in Austin” I enjoyed my stay at The Intercontinental. The location is perfect for downtown activities. It was a short walk to the Capitol for business and a short walk out to dinner at night. There were two drawback, the rooms are small and the gym never seemed to have drinking water available. Both of these issues did not distract from my trip. I would stay there again.

“perfect location to Convention Center” Stayed at Hampton Inn for a convention being held at The Pennsylvania Convention Center. The hotel was around the corner from the Convention Center entrance so it was an easy walk. I drove and used the valet parking. I didn't need my car until checkout so I'm not sure how easy it was to retrieve your car if you needed something in it. The staff was very friendly and responsive. Despite the large number of guests, we never had to wait for elevators or in the breakfast area. The food selections at breakfast were good. The room was a good size and the shower had great water pressure. Always ice in the ice machine. We didn't get to use the pool or fitness room but we saw others who had used it. I think the pool opened at 7am. FOOD:There was a great little pizza shop one block over (cheese-steaks, pizzas, beer) and the Sheraton had a small restaurant/bar,one block over in the other direction. The Reading Terminal (across from Convention Center) was AMAZING-more food choices in one place than I've ever seen! It closes at 6 pm but we went there for lunch each day/ The Hampton Inn is in a perfect location for us and the value was great. It is the city so there is alot of people milling around but we never felt unsafe. I would definitely return there.

“Been here twice, always nice” I've had the pleasure of staying at the new Wit twice since its opening in May of 2009. Overall, the hotel is a welcome addtion to Chicago's Loop, both in terms of additional hotel rooms as well as the fantastic Roof and great restaurants. I live in Chicago so I have a pretty good sense of what works in this fabulous city. The Wit is perfectly located for people in town on business, who want to be close to Millenium Park and the Art Institute or people wanting to be in the heart of the theater district. Shopping on North Michigan Avenue is an easy walk, as is both the Sears...I mean Willis...Tower and the Hancock Building/Water Tower (ahem, American Girl). One can also get to Navy Pier on foot or by a very short cab ride. Rooms are on the modern side. Many will have a bright neon stripe running diagonally across the windows, which can be blocked using the drapes. Beds are very comfortable and the TV is quite nice. Amenities are good. My only complaint on the room is the oversized, shallow sink which creates a challenge for someone trying to wash their face. Definitely an example of form over function.
