The rooftop bar "Roof" is not to be missed. It has quickly become one of the most desired spots on the nightlife scene as evidenced from the long lines down Lake Street on several nights per week. There is a large outdoor space with good views of downtown Chicago as well as enclosed space to protect against the elements. You can also have a small group occupy a private area which extends out from the building--not for the faint of heart. There are fire pits in the outside area to warm the bodies in non-summer months. Drinks are not cheap, but the wine list is nicely diversified and the cucumber mojitos are quite yummy. Both restaurants are excellent. I had breakfast only twice at State and Lake--both times the food was great. This venue also does a pretty good later bar and grill business. The second floor creative Italian restaurant Cibo Matto, takes a very unique view of Italian cuisine and is a great pre or post theater choice. My only other complaint is the lack of on site self parking. Valet is available, however it is less expensive (at least by a little) to park in one of the many self park garages located within 1-2 blocks of the hotel. The hotel is also easily accessible from both O'Hare and Midway via the El. The Blue Line from O'Hare stops about 4 blocks from the property; the Orange Line from Midway stops almost on top of the hotel. Make sure upon check in you get a VIP pass for Roof if you are there on the weekend. The place is so popular that they have restricted access quite considerably--if its very crowded, a room key may not suffice. Last note, if you are Hilton Gold/Diamond, make sure you get free breakfast coupons for State and Lake. I noticed that they weren't automatically given out. Overall, one of the most dynamic, vibrant hotels to hit Chicago in quite a while!

“ビジネスにもドライブ観光にもゆっくり休めるホテル” 2011年5月に、仕事の関係で2泊しました。 ロケーションは、サンディエゴ・リンドバーグ国際空港から5号線を北に17マイルほどのところ。渋滞がなければ、車で30分ほどの距離です。 2 QUEEN BEDのベーシックな部屋でしたが、アメリカのホテルとしては標準的な(つまり日本人には十分な)広さで、部屋の清潔感やタオル、アメニティーなども満足できるものでした。Advanced Prchaseで、1泊US$160(税・サ別)ほどでした。 フリーウエイの5号線と、56号線のジャンクションのそばですが、フリーウエイからは十分距離があり、車の騒音も部屋の中からは全く気になりません。今回は仕事のため残念ながら使いませんでしたが、中庭には雰囲気の良いプールもあり、また、西側は自然公園を間にすぐ太平洋岸のビーチがあり、サーフボードを抱えたゲストも泊まっていました。 サービスは、可もなく不可もなくですが、静かで落ち着いた雰囲気のたたずまいで、旅の疲れをいやすには良いホテルだと思います。郊外のDoubleTreeということで、室料もあまり高くありませんので、出張や、ラ・ホーヤ観光、カリフォルニア西海岸ドライブなど、この地域を訪れる方には重宝するホテルだと思います。

“No one would miss it” If this hotel were to vanish, no one would miss it. This hotel is far from being a jewel of the Hilton family crown. I found it long-in-the-tooth. My room carpet had a very pronounced grease stain and the temperature was difficult to control. The room was pooly lit. Taking the elevators is a thrill ride in itself: half the time the floor number display in the elevator didn't work, or missed a digit, sometimes the elevator would rocket past my floor only to open its inner doors while still in motion to the next floor making it paticularly worrisome for someone with a small child. The interior elevator doors were scratched with grafitti. The businessman's continental breakfast was never in the same place twice making one play detective each and every morning. Sometimes the breakfast was held in the tiniest of "conference" rooms, sometimes next to the gym. Internet service in the room was often off-line, yet refunds were never offered - one would have to ask for them specifically. The parking garage is horrendous - caution do NOT rent a large, long vehicle you'll never make it on the U-turn required on the second floor. Chances of me staying here again: Zero.

“Great stay” I gambled with Hotwire and the Red Roof Inn, downtown San Antonio was my prize at a pretty good price. I then looked up the hotel on this site and it did not look good, but the credit card was already charged. Finding the hotel was a breeze, it is located right off I-37 near downtown. This is not a fancy hotel and it is not an expensive hotel. It is clean and the shower was great. If you want high end then don't be a cheap skate and spend two or three hundred a night for a riverwalk hotel and you will get what you pay for. The hotel is four or five blocks from the Alamo and the riverwalk. The city trolley stops on the street by the hotel so getting to Market Square is convienient. I parked the car and never moved it for the couples of days stay. The parking is excellent and convienent, the multi-level parking garage makes it possible to park on the same floor as your room. The staff were friendly and helpful. If you are looking for the convienience of a downtown/riverwalk hotel and you don't want to pay the high prices then I recommend you stay at the RRI.

“Best of Seattle” Stayed at Pan Pacific on front end of Alaskan cruise trip and Fairmont at back end; which was a smart choice for a day in Seattle after a week on the sea. The Fairmont is a superior hotel and situated (downtown) perfectly for a visit to Seattle. Rooms are truly luxurious and the indoor pool complex is top-rate and a perfect way to sit and relax, read, use the oversized whirlpool, or the health club. Lobby is spacious, rooms and hallways are brightly and exquisively decorated, and the hotel has a nice bar, breakfast room, and restaurant. Bargain rates can be gotten by surfing the various websites. I am a very discriminating traveler and this hotel met my highest expectations.

“Basic Room” I really enjoyed the attention and kindness from the Phoenix Park Staff. Very prompt in answering my questions and willing to provide the extra touches. However, the Phoenix is a straight up and down functional room. Not a place to roost for more than two nights. My room was very small and claustrophobic. The room also happened to be freezing cold; slept with my robe on. Had a business call in early evening and my next door neighbor and I could hear each other through the walls. Would be a great hotel to be a spy! Had room service sent up from the Dubliner Pub and it was prompt, economical and good grub. I chose this hotel because it was near the 20 F Street Conference Center.

“Very good place to stay for a tourist” The decoration of the hotel is very modern, in sharp contrast with the building itself, which is one of the oldest and tallest skyscraper made of stone (beautiful architecture!). I do like the room a lot, as you can tell from many details that they do care about their guests. Every staff has been very friendly and attentive. The location is great: right across the street to the old state building on the freedom trail and the metro, and 3 min walk to Quincy market. As a result, we had no difficulty walking a significant portion of the freedom trail at the night of our arrival and had dinner in Quincy Market. Will consider coming back if the price is reasonable :)

“Decent Hotel but not necessarily worth the $$” I stayed at the Marriott Downtown on New Years eve for a one night get away. The lobby is very nice, and the restaurant has a great morning buffet, however the rooms are just average and laid out in a funny manner. I would probably recommend the residence inn or courtyard right next door as they are equally as nice but lesser priced. I must mention however the staff was very friendly and accomodating, which makes up for some of the room issues.

“Tiny bathroom and windows don't block out noise.” Spent 3 nights on the 3rd floor of the hotel facing the street. Paid $335 with tax on a corporate account. The bathroom was tiny, even by NY standards. The room was plagued by quite a bit of street noise. The carpet in the room had ink stains. The staff were friendly and very helpful. The room had a large flat screen TV and was pretty well sized. The hallways were small and somewhat dingy. There was a large stain outside the room and we always seemed to be walking around the housekeepers carts. The hotel is in a good location, but unless you secure a good rate you can do better.

“Pleasantly surprised.” Haven't stayed at this hotel for a couple of years, and as the Gateway was sold out, i thought that i would try it again. New carpets in the lobby, and the room looked refreshed. Great beds. The front desk was a bit slow, but the service was excellent. Convenient self park located on the premises. Friendly service at the bar and restaurant. Will definitely return.

“Don't Expect a Five Star Hotel” I spent a leisurely weekend at the Whitehall Hotel after a week business stay at the neighboring Westin. Aside from the great location of both hotels there is no comparison. The Westin is a modern luxury hotel with modern amenities and the Whitehall Hotel is a moth-balled museum of vintage Chicago hotel history. A repairman was in my room repairing the HVAC system as I checked-in and for the remainder of the trip I noticed that the room felt colder than usual. The rooms are very small and there is barely enough room to squeeze between the bed and the television. The television is standard definition, the showerhead is too low to be useful and the closet was extremely small. This hotel is worth it if you can find it on Hotwire or Priceline for $100 or less - or if location is the most important thing for you.

“Large Rooms, but it ends there” Let me first say we never stay in Midtown, but we had 2 Broadway shows in 1 weekend, so decided to stay in touristville and the London had nice reviews on T.A. The rooms at the The London are very spacious, almost empty, no artwork or prints on the wall, very cold and sparse. Terrible check in. Young girl checked us in, telling us our room was not available at 4 pm, because the current guests have not checked out as of yet. ?????? Well then, it's a 500 room hotel, find us another room. Duh! She was a dope. No customer service or smile or kindness and no upgrade. Made us stand there while she called a someone. No HD tv's in the room, and the wireless had to be hooked up by calling an outside I.T. tech that was not located in the hotel. More headaches. Last thing, I am a New Yorker and have never spent $21. on a cocktail in my life. Even in Paris or London. Can you say RIP OFF? Bar is filled with guests in sweat shirts and hoodies, while other people are having high tea. Makes no sense. How about a dress code? Gordon Ramsey would be appalled. If you are looking for a $349. bargain price and close proximity to the theatres and midtown, then this is a fine choice, if you like mediocrity. I suggest you stay at the Trump Soho and take a cab to your show, same price and a fabulous hotel who appreciates their guests. PS. the lights on the desk did not work either. Such a shame. The Rhiga Royal was a swanky place.

“Great location, huge rooms!” This is one of the nicer hotels I have ever stayed at. It's price is in line with other hotels but you get a small suite with a full kitchen, 2 TVs, and even a blu-ray player which I have never seen in a hotel before. It is only a little over a block from a metro stop and is just a few blocks from the White House and National Mall area. The Lincoln Memorial is about a 20 minute walk from here. Staff gave me handy map and good bar/restaurant recommendation. Area seemed safe at night as well. Highly recommended!

“Disappointed with 1 night stay for business” Stayed for one night on business with colleagues and this review is for business travelers who might consider the Hilton Squaw Peak vs. families or vacationers as we did not use the pool. The hotel was at least 1/2 empty being a Monday night in Phoenix in the summer after the kids have returned to school. We arrived to only one person working the front desk who was assisting a guest without a reservation. We had to wait for some time while the front desk clerk explained all the rooms, rates, etc. and then spent considerable more time offering various upgrades. No apology was offered for the wait once it was our turn to check-in. We were also offered an "upgrade" to a king suite. What a disappointment! The rooms have balconies and the view from our rooms faced the laundry facility, which not only was an eyesore but loud with the machines running around the clock. For a half-empty "resort" and an "upgrade" for a Hilton Diamond member, this was extraordinarily disappointing. One would think the hotel would like to earn return business and take the opportunity to offer rooms to its loyal Hilton customers that at least had a "resort" type view. Even a room with a view of the parking lot would have been better. This was a boneheaded move on Hilton's part. The room itself was fine. The bathroom had been updated with nice granite counters and tilework. Flat screen TVs in both the sitting area and bedroom were nice. Bed was comfortable. The hotel offers a continental breakfast in the gift shop, which is as odd as it sounds. It's not really a continental breakfast but a coffee shop with overpriced pastries and nowhere to sit. When checking out the next morning, we commented on the terrible location of our "upgraded" rooms and were again offered no apology by the front desk personnel. Will not return in the future and would not recommend to other business travelers.

“Expensive and nice” We stayed in a Century Suite and it was really comfortable, quite and spacious. Be careful with the minibar in the room, because you have to pay for items at the moment you move them. But in spite of that I would come back to the same room and I recommend it.

“XL size hotel” I tagged along with my husband, who attended a convention there. Yes, it's a convention hotel, which means it's supersized so nothing is personal. Good thing was that the Metro is right outside the hotel and it took 5 minutes to get to Downtown, where I went to work everyday. Area seemed safe enough when I came back from work close to midnight one night. If I had the choice, I wouldn't stay there again, whether it be for work or play, unless I'm attending a convention there. It's not within walking distance from downtown (work) and it's too busy to relax (vacation).

“Avoid the 5th floor” I have stayed here twice. The first time I was impressed with the service. We came in very early and they gave us our room. The room was not very high up and was on the street so it was really noisy even though it was a holiday. Then the next time I stayed, I got a room on the 5th floor and the room was right across the hall from the fitness room. At 4am I hear this loud thumping that kept on going. When I got up in the morning I saw the room was directly across the hall from the fitness room. At check out I mentioned this to the front desk and was just dismissed as so what. I won't stay here again. I feel like when you book on alternative web sites rather than the hotel's web site you get a better price but a lousy room. The second time I didn't even get a good price.

“Great Location for Layover, Good for a night” Stayed here on a lay over with my family. Was picked up by the Shuttle at the International Terminal and quickly dropped at the hotel. Bellmen helped with our bags. Check in was super easy and bags were waiting for us when we got to our room. We had two rooms, that adjoined. Rooms and bathroom are pretty small. Typical for an airport/business type hotel but had a great rate through Marriott that could not pass up. Beds very comfortable and heating control seemed to work just fine. The room was quite with the exception of the loud party going on down the hallway....Did not hear any LAX noise and had a room facing LAX. The room was cramped but very modern and updated. Nice Flat screen TV's in each room. There is a burger King directly across the street which was a life saver as my little ones don't do well off the room service menu. Only big negative was the return shuttle to the airport. apparently the entire hotel (or at least 35 of us) wanted to get on the 6:45 AM shuttle to LAX. Instead of ordering another empty shuttle, the literally jammed everyone into this one shuttle like a circus car. The shuttle bus actually bottomed out as it left the parking lot. Not safe at all. I was pretty disappointed that this was allowed, but really needed the ride to catch our flight. I would hope in the future they would not over stuff a bus like they did. Once we got the airport it was even more trouble as we tried to get off the bus, and have the correct bags passed out..brutal. All in all I would stay here again as the price was right.

“Slightly above average-but needs definite improvement” I came to the Raffaelo with slightly above average expectations and they managed to just barely meet even those expectations. Below is a breakdown of the good, the bad and the lack of common sense: The good: It is in a good location on North Michigan Ave. close to a lot of shops and sights The décor creates nice ambiance The bar upstairs is a fun place to hang out with a nice view The bad: The rooms are tiny The elevators are broken The service is severely lacking The lack of common sense: There was NO OUTLET in the TINY BATHROOM to use the blowdryer they provide. Try blowdrying your hair in the bedroom without a mirror, it doesn't work

“Adequate size room - bizarre furnishings” Contrary to some previous reviews, I found my room to be small but adequate in size. The furnishings, however, were another story. A large marble table was at the end of the bed with barely enough room to get in and out of the chair. Two low chairs that looked like they belong in the children's furniture section at IKEA were also in the room as was a bench that was totally incongruous. In fact the furniture was probably the ugliest I have ever encountered in a hotel room. On a more positive note, the staff was superb, the lobby attractive and the breakfast area especially nice. The hotel's wi-fi had the best signal I have ever found in a hotel. The in-room safe was another good feature. So for a well located River North hotel and a reasonable rate, Hotel Cass is recommended, as long as you don't mind the bizarre furnishings.

“Perfect” We got this hotel on priceline for $96 per night and it exceeded our expectation by a long way. Some of the other reviews complain about the view or the price they paid, they obviously can't afford the room and did not look at the hotel from the outside. The hotel is surrounded by buildings and of course would not have a view unless you were overlooking the front street. We had a brick wall to look at but it really did not make a difference. If you are looking for a view you should book at a hotel known for the view...lol. The service was amazing, we were greeted every time we got in or out of the elevator, they offered to move our bags several times for us and the concierge (Shamus) was extremely helpful. I would stay here again and recommend this hotel to anyone. Also, the bathroom was small, but the room we had was just as large as most other hotel rooms I have stayed in.

“Not the best...not the worst” I spent 2 nights at the Palmer House Hilton. A famiily member was staying there for a business conference so it was a good time to check the place out. Unfortunately we stayed in one of the older rooms (apparently there are some newly remodeled ones) Our room was small, but did include 2 double beds, desk, chair, tv and average sized bathroom. The room however had an old smell to it, musty and caused sinus congestion every morning. So if you have allergies or sinus problems I would suggest requesting a newer room. The Lobby on the other hand was beautiful! Living up to its historical significance, and seeing why famous visitors such as Ulysses S. Grant and Charles Dickens stopped in. But overall I wasn't too impressed. There was a not so exciting small gift shop and restaurant/bar on the ground floor. However, there is a Corner Bakery, CVS, Walgreens and White Hen close by for quick breakfasts and coffee. The hotel is located in a great location if you plan to go to the theater, or shopping on State Street. It is close to restaurants too. There are plenty of taxi's and its along the bus routes. Easy walking distance to Millenium Park. Note however, that on Sundays a lot of the small food joints and shops in the loop area are closed, including some Walgreens. For being a Hilton, I was disappointed in the quality of the room, especially for the price, but the location is great depending on the types of activities you plan to do in Chicago.

“Why #3 hotel in Denver?” I'm confused as to how this hotel could be ranked #3 in Denver. Is this a case of hired bloggers? I've stayed at 8 different hotels near DIA and this one ranks in the mid to low range. It was fine, just nothing great. Bed was OK, room was definitely very clean. Nothing special about room or decor. And the price seems a bit out of line.

“Great location, perfect for pets!” This hotel is in a great location in Center City - easy walk to Reading Terminal Market, the Constitution Center and Independence Hall, City Hall, and great shopping, restaurants, and bars. Our room was very clean and nice. Pets are welcome at the hotel and even get their own room service menu!

“Location Location Location” The location just rocked. The trolley runs right in front of the hotel, which is kinda cool. If you're a tourist, then you'll love the experience. Lots of restaurants and shops within walking distance. The room was comfortable, too.

“Great Place” Had a one night stay in July of 2003 and what a suprise we had. We had a corner room with a view of the city and water. At night the view was out of this world and could't keep the window treatments closed. The room was very large for myself, my wife and the kids and the room extras (Large desk, movies ,robes, free cookies, soda, and water was great) Note: sign up as a Wyndham member before you book to get the upgrade and free stuff. Staff was great anf the walk to the historic area was very close and no problem at all. All in all we will be back soon for more than one night.

“Good but not great” Stayed here for a builder's convention....nice beds, good location. That is about it. Oh, there is a Starbucks downstairs....besides that this hote has no charm and must be located near a fire station because I heard sirens a lot more than when I used to stay at the Grand Hyatt up the street on Stockton. During our stay I threw a party in the Presidential Suite for my company and the room was so poorly decorated it was straight out of a 1980's movie. Just outdated and poor use of space. If you are staying in the city and want a great hotel, go to the Hotel Vitale. Way worth the money!!!!

“Couldn't have been happier with my choice of the Blackstone” I could not have been any happier with my choice of the Blackstone! Whenever I go back to Chicago this will be my number one choice to stay! The hotel is not too far from public transport...about a ten minute walk from the Red Line (we could have just hopped on a bus but decided to walk instead.) Upon entering the hotel we felt like we were taken back to the roaring 20's. The lobby is very dark, atmospheric.. definitely has a very retro feel to it. The room was a little on the small side but BEAUTIFULLY decorated. I absolutely fell in love with the bathroom though as a previous reviewer said, the bathroom doors slide out of the wall and are not wide enough so that when you close the bathroom door all the way, there is an inch wide gap through which you can see into the bathroom. We had a wonderful view of Chicago from our room (and we weren't even in an upgraded room) Great location... Michigan avenue and a short walk to both Millennium Park and Buckingham Fountain. We did not visit the bar/restaurant or order room service but the front desk agents were very welcoming and personable. All in all this is a great choice, albeit a place I would mostly recommend to couples, groups of friends travelling... would not really recommend to families with children.

“Good but needs a little updating” I've stayed at this hotel a few times and have always had a good experience. On our most recent trip, we noticed that the floor smelled very musty. Our room was good but some of the wallpaper was peeling off of the wall and that it generally needed a little TLC.

“Highlight of our trip to Austin” I had a room booked at the Four Seasons because the Hotel San Jose was full, but a room there opened up a couple of days before our trip, so I cancelled the FS and am so glad I did. The South Congress neighborhood is definitely a better place to stay than downtown. Lots of fun shops and restaurants. The San Jose is really cute, they did a great job reinventing the old motel it once was. The rooms are pretty basic but not boring. The first night we were in a standard room, it was small but adequate. The next two nights we moved to a standard plus, i think it was called. Definitely worth the extra $30 a night. We were on the second floor with a shared patio. The pool/lounge area was nice, with heated lamps, seemed like locals came there to hang out too, not just hotel guests. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We didn't get room service at all, Jo's next door had great coffee and snacks. In my opinion, the San Jose lived up to all the hype surrounding it.

“Great NYC hotel if you get a good rate!” This is a solid NYC 4* hotel if you get a good rate. No executive floor like the Hilton New York, but I still prefer this hotel for a number of reasons. 1) Proximity to times square and theatres if that's your thing 2) smack above 42nd street subway - quick and easy access to subway, JFK and the port authority bus terminal (EWR, etc) 3) Quick access to food options - they're at your door step 4) The breakfast - it's super, compared to say the Doubletree Lower Manhattan, Hampton Inns - i love the breakfasts still after 10 years it's great 5) The views - every room basically has an amazing view - i've stayed once facing 42nd, and once looking at lower manhattan and both views were great 6) upgrades - as a diamond, have been given nice rooms both times - once a larger corner room and second time a corner room (with two windows). They also do listen to your preferences unlike many hilton hotels - ie high floor, away from lifts - yes you read my prefs! The gym also in this property is solid, with a proper machine weight selection. They offer time out in the rooms where as other properties charge. Just a great hotel all round, my only criticism, and it is slight is that I may not choose it over say the Hampton Inn Times Sq North or the Hilton Garden Inn Times Sq North because sometimes it can be a 30% premium but then again if it's only a 5% premium, it's definitely my choice over these properties - for the breakfast alone ;-). And also it is looking slightly worn around the edges (but given it's age and use it's still superb) but nothing bad just a little bits and pieces, they've done very well with the decor and it's made it still look amazing after 10 years. Finally, just a tiny bit of nickle and diming - i thought they could have at least included Peter Thomas Roth bodywash in the rooms, then again they did offer mouthwash and a shoe mitt which was helpful.

“Good for business, so so for tourists” If you are in town for business in the downtown/financial district and need a more budget-conscious option, this is a great choice. It's just outside of downtown, in the theater district and a short walk to the red, green or orange lines of the MBTA as well as a quick walk to most any location downtown. The rooms have gorgeous furniture, a nice large desk and free internet. The fitness room is decent and you can run in the Commons/Public Garden nearby. The front desk was also very accommodating, getting me into my room when I arrived from a red eye, 4 hours ahead of check-in. For tourists, there's certainly a lot to recommend it - again, close to the T and the theaters, as well as a short walk to Newbury St/Copley Sq. And because of the theater crowd, plenty of generic, mid-priced (PF Changs, Rock Bottom) food options just out the door. However, there are a few reasons to stay elsewhere if you are primarily in town for leisure. First, the rooms are SMALL. Totally adequate for a single, a bit cozy for a couple, can't imagine cramming any kids in there. Second, it's LOUD. On Thu, Friday and Saturday a large crowd of folks will be at Caprice/The Roxy on the lower level of the hotel. The people waiting outside in line are noisy, and I could hear the DJ as if he were in the room next door (I was on the 7th floor). But, overall, I had a very positive stay. I'd heartily recommend it for business and I'd still recommend it for tourists, just with those caveats.

“If you like boutique/special hotels, you'll likely love this” They gave me an upgrade to a King room for the Queen price as they were sold out of Queen and I really did not want the twin size/Petite bed so that was a good start :) Just there for a sat. eve meeting a friend from out of town - I am in DC. I have wanted to stay here for a LONG time and it's always booked so I was excited about this stay. It's clean, beautiful, very comfy and cozy. The rooftop garden is ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC - 5 stars for that! Lovely 2nd floor has books on various subjects, comp. breakfast/wine for happy hr and is really great for just hanging out 24/7. The bedroom itself was large as I understand it's recognized as a jr. suite. The bathroom was clean, modern, for NY, fine in size. It's just a nice modern layout with the book selection being great. My biggest problem is that the view overlooks 41st St and with the blinds, you'll get quite a bit of light in. Also, I had expected more comfy beds - the mattress is quite hard. I've stayed in other hotels, same price level with comfort/style levels being much more comfortable bed wise. otherwise, it's great! ipod speakers in room which was also enjoyed by me :) But you know, they give you a lot of comps - wifi and the happy hr/breakfast so it could be worse :)

“Needs to be Imploded or Completely Overhauled” This hotel is like a blast from the 1980's. All the furniture is cracked, dented, semi broken. Walls are banged up, decororations are garish. Wonder if they ever charge the $450 rate that is quoted on the door panel. In Las Vegas they just blow up the hotel when they are past their prime. That is my suggestion for this place.

“Good value, convenient to the Metro” Stayed here on a family vacation to DC. Location: Hotel is convenient to the Metro which makes it easy to go anywhere within the city. The immediate neighborhood is actively under construction, but it seems to be an "up and coming" neighborhood with plenty of places to grab a light breakfast or a quick snack. The supermarket was great with plenty of takeout choices. If you want a more substantial meal, you'll need to hop on the metro. Hotel: Staff was friendly and rooms were new and clean. We ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant 1 day. Typical buffet with plenty of choices. Nothing to write home about and a little expensive. We found the nearby coffee shop to be a better option! All in all, the hotel was a good value for the price and a good place to stay as long as you don't mind riding the metro everywhere. I would stay there again!

“Excellent Stay” Like most SpringHill Suites this is a nice property with everything you would expect. Nice clean, large rooms. Comfortable and quiet. Even the breakfast buffet is pretty good and if you read my reviews that is usually a complaint I have about most that offer free breakfast. Room service is available form the Marriott located next door. The only complaint I would have is that the whirlpool was not working.

“Dirty. Worn. Pathetic.” I booked this hotel after looking at the TripAdvidor rating. I was wrong. Checkin took some 30 minutes for me and my two coworkers. The guy at the front desk was confused and inept. Then finding the room was almost impossible due to the confusing room numbering and lack of signage. You can make also a budget hotel like this inviting or at least value for money. This is neither. The room was dirty with some cuttings of computer cable in the middle of the floor. It was not possible to bolt the door. The bathroom mirror was cracked. The bed-lamp did not work since plug was not connected. And finally, the bed was badly creaking.

“Wonderful hotel” Just got back from 3 nights at this hotel and it was great. With it's waterfront location, fabulous beds, and outstanding service, this year old hotel is a good choice. They have 2 concierge floos that give you access to a lounge that includes breakfast, afternoon snacks, beverages, and evening deserts. We were upgraded to this floor, upon asking, at no extra charge because we are Marriott Rewards members. A definite plus. Concierge was very helpful in planning activites and dinner reservations. Our favorite meal was right across the street at Anthony's on Pier 66. They brought us a complimentary appetizer and said it was from the concierge at the Marriott. Very impressive. Will defintiely stay here again.

“Not a Fan” We're a Hilton loyal family. We've been Diamond or Gold members for the better part of the last few years. We've always been shown the friendliest service and decent hotel rooms. Well, this experience left us seriously disappointed. We walked into the hotel with the room dripping all over the place, towels scattered around to sop of the wet and buckets littering the floor. It was slick. It was terribly ugly and it wasn't what I was expecting at all. I walked up the the desk to check in and was told that I couldn't because my husband's name was on the reservation. Seriously, we have checked into many Hilton family hotels and NEVER once was I turned away because I am the Mrs. I have the same credit card and I have the same HHonors ID number on my card. It was raining outside and I had two grumpy children, but I had to trapse out there and have my husband return to get the keys. UGH. Then we had booked a reservation that was to include a 50 dollar voucher. They couldn't find them. (It was dinner time mind you.) UGH. Now not everything was horrible. Our room was nice and it had been upgraded to a Jr Suite. It was clean and comfortable. We were annoyed that we couldn't find a printer to print a document that we needed, that we paid for internet that was slower than the dial up that I had in 1997 and that the staff never brought the promised dinner voucher. (My husband did eventually get one from the desk himself.) I wouldn't ever stay in this Hilton hotel again. There are too many better options.

“No Longer A Favorite” I have visited this hotel many times over the years and I used to enjoy it immensely, but after recent visits I find that it's no longer on my "favorite" list. It still has the advantage of a nice location and large rooms with kitchens, but something has been lost along the way,. The hotel seems to have a new ownership structure. Reservations are made collectively for both hotel properties, and calls are taken with a hint of frostiness. Upgrades to regular clients that used to be cheerfully offered are no longer available, and if you ask for one, the frosty attitude turns downright rude. I recently called from overseas to reserve a room and when I had a special request, the reservations clerk insisted that I had to hang up and call again in order to speak with her manager. Sigh. Room rates are dramatically higher, but there haven't been any significant upgrades to the furnishings to indicate what the money is being spent on. The wifi internet connection is weak and uses an obsolete password system that many hotels abandoned years ago -- it means your internet connection will time out frequently and you'll have to go back and log in again. A small irritation, but one that should be fixed. The front desk staff is new and undertrained, there is no breakfast available, and the hotel's restaurant (The Circle Bistro), apparently gets written up in the local magazines, but is trendily overpriced, so is not convenient for a tired traveler who just wants a sandwich and a beer. The hotel offers less but charges more. It's now my "stand by" hotel, that I'll only call when other, better hotels are not available.

“Understand what you're getting.” We took a room at the Moore when it seemed that all rooms in Seattle were taken. It has both good and bad features. The accommodations are Spartan but clean and spacious. The location is great except for the drug and alcohol recovery center next door, which results in individuals of questionable character loitering on the street day and night. (These folks can be avoided by walking on 3rd St. or on the west side of 2nd St.) We appreciated the kitchenette, but had to request a microwave, which was provided. There were very few cooking utensils, but nice tableware. There were no knobs on the cooktop, and none could be found by the staff. Electrical wiring was stapled to the walls, and there was no clock or clock radio. We were on the street side, 2nd floor, and there was considerable street noise (much of it from the rehab folks next door.) Free wi-fi worked well. Would we stay here again? Probably. If you limit your expectations, the Moore provides acceptable, spacious, but spartan accommodations.

“Great Location but Beauty is in the Eye of the Beholder” I will give you a decent perspective on this hotel. I like it - didn't love it. My wife hated it.. We both love the location. We stayed here as the price was right. The suites are not much different from the one bedroom aprtments our friends had in Manhattan just after college. Unfortunately, we have grown beyond that. Clean me: Yes Wife: yes Spacious me: yes wife: yes Room in good condition me: It's ok but getting a bit long in the tooth. Wife: Totally unacceptable. Cheap furniture when new. Even worse now. Homey: me: not really - but serviceable wife: Awful - uncomfortable - for all the room, not enough comfortable furniture to sit on. Location: me: Great - love Little Italy and Soho Wife: Same Bottom line: - Do not expect miracles here. You are not paying for them. If I had this apartment fresh out of college, I'd have been happy. However, college was a while back and my wife and I have come to expect more. I would return to this hotel as the location is so amazing that it more than makes up for the only fair but clean rooms. However, I will not be returning except perhaps for the occasional guys weekend, as my wife will not.

“Not bad if you are doing business in the city” This hotel has a really good location as it is 2 blocks from Union Square and only 4 blocks from the Moscone Center. We stayed here while we were attending a conference in San Francisco for the week and it was adequate. It is a very small hotel and the amenities are limited (the "breakfast room" is pretty much a closet but it is fine to grab a quick bagel and coffee to go in the morning). The good: Cheap valet parking - $25/night with unlimited in and out Great location Nightclub attached to the hotel with AWESOME food (make sure you try to stay on a high floor so you don't get the noise from the club in the evenings. Great rates! (we got it for $89/night during the week of a major conference in SF) The not-so-good: Small hotel with small rooms No wireless internet (but free wired internet. in my case this means I had a huge cable running from the telephone jack behind the bed to the desk at the other end of the room. Overall it is fine as a centrally located hotel to grab some rest after meetings and conferences while staying in San Francisco.

“Funky Fun Hotel” The Topaz, like other hotels has a funky, fun decor. My room was spacious and comfortable. Only drawbacks were lack of fitness room and not enough room for my toiletries on the bathroom countertop. The free wine hour (and passes to the nearby "Y") made up for that. Staff were very helpful.

“Great location, loved the suite we stayed in.” My family just returned from a 4 night stay at the Warwick. We booked this hotel based on family recommendations. I did ask for an outside room in an upper floor but unfortunately got the 4th floor, our room faced the Museum of Modern Art which was fine. There was very little street noise and still offered some view of the street. The Hilton is directly across the street and is very busy which can help when looking for a cab because there are so many parked there at all times. The check in process was very easy, they did not offer to take our bags to the room but I didn't really need them to. We did get free Wifi because we were in a suite but the service seemed to cut in and out. Our room had a very large living room with a table and chairs, large sofa and two chairs. The sofa is a pull-out which would be nice if you needed extra space. The bedroom had two doubles and plenty of space although the bathroom is a little small for being a suite. We did not eat at the hotel but it does have a nice bar and restaurant to eat at, the prices seemed a little high for breakfast but there is a Starbucks across the street and an Au Bon Pain nearby which we frequented for coffee and breakfast. We walked to Times Square and Rockefeller Plaza very quickly, the location is hard to beat unless you want the noise of staying in Times Square. We did eat a late dinner at the Irish Pub just a few doors down and it was just fine and there are pizza places on the next block for a quick lunch too. If I had any complaint it might be that the staff didn't go out of there way to greet us on our coming and goings but that may just be New York. The room was nice, beds comfortable and maid service did a nice job every day. We had a great time in New York and would stay here again.

“Lovely place” We stayed at the Morris house hotel for two nights in June. The place is so beautiful and the location is superb. The only bad points are that the staff is not as friendly as we were expecting and the breakfast is not great. As for our bedroom, garden and downstairs rooms they are amazing. If we come back to Philadelphia we will stay here again.

“Expected a little more” The Hilton Chicago has a lot of history, and they teach you that in the elevator with small TV screens. I was expecting more based on the history, but it seemed to be an old hotel with some fix-ups. Check-in was fast as a Diamond member, and I was upgraded to the Executive Floor. Unfortunately, the room was less impressive.. very small. They've obviously tried to make it more than it really is. The bathroom had marble and gold-plated fixtures, but still appeared old and boring. THe most annoying thing was a computer monitor with some new touch-screen features that kept coming on at 4 AM to wake me up despite my attempts to turn it off (there was no "off" button). While it was great to have 2 phones in such a small room, the cordless phone didn't work at all. I always love coffee makers in the room, but they didnt refill my coffee one day. The beers were $7 in the bar. I could buy a 6-pack for the cost of one beer. Parking was very expensive. Definitely not worth the expense of this hotel. Next time, I'll try the Palmer Hilton. It's just as far to the darn convention center.

“Not bad... but won't come back here” I wrote a review for the Trump Plaza in Vegas that be relevant for this one: it's all about expectations. Sorry to say this hotel didn't meet my--not too high--expectations. I'll say off the bat, however, that I booked thru the American Express Travel website as a combination (air-hotel-car) deal, so I don't know how much the hotel cost by itself. That's important because it would normally help me assess what to expect (vs. what I get) to measure my level of satisfaction. The hotel is nice: fairly clean, located conveniently (not too far away from downtown, but not too close either), and the rooms were ok. As usual with Hilton hotels, the beds were awesome. Unlike other Hiltons, though, the bathroom and the TV were small, the room was ordinary and the hotel itself looked slightly unkempt (not dirty, mind you, just not 100% tidy). The cookie--though always nice to get one--was probably a couple of days old... As many other choices as there are in San Diego, I find it hard to recommend this property to a friend. But if someone already booked there, I wouldn't tell him/her to change, either.

“Underwhelmed” Recently spent six nights at the Fairmont for a first trip to Chicago. Have experienced Fairmont in Canada which were superb, so had very high expectations for this Chicago property. We got a very good deal so were greatly looking forward to our stay. However, it was just all very ordinary, unspectacular and even drab. We had a 'Stepford Wife' at check-in who we felt sure was on a remote control (she was there seven days later at check out, same fixed grin and glassy stare!). She gave us a large sized room that had all the amenities you could wish for. However, it was gloomy and souless, the contemporary furnishings adding nothing to a feeling of comfort or cozyness. We did have a bay window which was a nice feature but did not allow any more daylight into the room which remained gloomy despite the daily brilliant sunshine outside. The bathroom was large and well fitted but with no magnifying shave/make up mirror. The WC was in a tiny separate cubicle within the bathroom and was a squeeze to use. Toiletries were good quality. A 42" HD TV, swish coffee maker and complimentary mineral water ticked the right boxes too. And yet..... Public areas were stark and gloomy and the bedroom corridor, at least on our floor, was shabby and in need of a make over. We never ate in the hotel. It looked over priced for what was on offer and a menu with the pre-fix 'fusion' never works in our experience. We were concerned that the location was going to be out on a limb but were pleased to find that once we'd got the lay of the land, it was a good, central position for all that (fabulous) Chicago has to offer. And the CVS pharmacy in front of the hotel and Bockwinkles supermarket behind were very useful. I just wish I could get more enthused by this Fairmont property but it left me flat.

“Excellent hotel in Great Location” The Westin on Michigan Avenue is right in the heart of downtown and across from the John Hancock building. Most Westins are above the fray and this is no exception. Although, not lavishing, the lobby is modern and quaint. There is a Starbucks and a restaurant off the lobby but did not eat at the restaurant - ate at Gino's East which was fair) off the lobby. The staff was polite and helpful. The rooms are nice size for big city hotel. HD TV, nice bathroom, great bed. The price was under $120 for mid-week - amazing value. I would give this hotel an 4 1/2 star rating and is a great choice to see the city of Chicago.

“Excellent Location and Great Value” My 3 sons and I spent our annual out-of-town baseball weekend in Denver in mid-June. We decided to stay at the downtown Courtyard Marriott due to its location on the 16th street pedestrian mall as well as being walking distance to Coors Field. We booked 2 rooms each with 2 queen beds. Our room package included complimentary valet parking, which is a $20+ cost savings/day. Internet access was complimentary as well. The rooms definitely met our needs. Large enough to accomodate the two queen beds with room to spare. A nice working area and flat screen TVs. The bathrooms a bit on the small side, but what the hey, good enough for boys. The hotel provided complimentary coffee in the lobby and if you needed to feed your Starbucks fix, a door directly from the hotel to a Starbucks. I found the hotel staff to be friendly and helpful. The only negative was the overwhelming number of seedy, lowlife folks that seem to wander the 16th street mall. I can't imagine what a visitior from another country would think of the cultural state of affairs in the USA. This must be a weekend phenomenom as I don't recall the same when I've stayed downtown Denver for business during the week. Nevertheless, the Courtyard Marriott met our needs and for a fair room rate.

“Great location” This was the first time I stayed at a Westin. It was nice! I only have one complaint when you call for a late check out the girl who answered just said one o'clock and hung up!! This hotel was busy, but if you are looking for more action stay at the W!!

“Mediocre Marriott” This hotel is in a great location in downtown Chicago. The room is really nothing special. The bathroom is extremely tiny. The beds are very comfortable and four pillows per bed. Cleanliness is good. The front desk staff was very friendly and efficient. They don't have a traditional front desk but "pods" and the agent will step out in front of the pod and ask if they can help you and then escort you to their pod. Quite friendly service. The breakfast buffet was quite good and the Executive Chef took my order for an omelette. Breakfast food was very good. The biggest complaint I have is the room doesn't have a mini-bar and the AC seems to be strained to keep the room cool. The shower was a delight.

“Very pleasant surprise” I am a loyal member of Hilton Honors and frequently book travel in a Garden Inn since these properties are consistently reliable. This property clearly didn’t start life as a Garden Inn. It is an all suites property and the rooms have the feel of a Homewood Suites (or similar). The extra space was a pleasant surprise! Check-in was effortless. Early check-in was requested and accommodated. Justin, the front desk clerk, is still in school studying hospitality management and, based on what I saw, he should go far. A true professional! Property is well maintained. Rooms were spacious with a separate living/dining area. Room was extremely comfortable. Even though the hotel is a short distance from the airport, it is situated in such a way that it is very quiet. Had two breakfasts with good quality food and professional service. Overall, I recommend this property to anyone needing accommodations at the Sky Harbor International Airport.

“Good Hotel for Business, Families and Mag Mile Shoppers” We stayed here over the weekend in November 2011. We usually stay at the Best Western River North, but I decided to bid on Priceline to save money and my bid got us into the Residence Inn. The hotel was cheaper, until you added the $35/night parking fee. Then it was exactly the same as The BW River North (which has free parking). The hotel is nice and clean with lots of amenities in the rooms. Had we been traveling with the children we would have appreciated the kitchen more. The hotel is only a couple blocks from the John Hancock Tower and it's just east Michigan Avenue shopping. Since we are not shoppers that wasn't a draw for us. We were also farther away from some of the restaurants and clubs we enjoy than we would have liked. It's all about what you are in town for. Although I found the parking fee high, I have to say that the valet service was excellent and we were easily able to get our car when we wanted it. Overall a nice hotel, just not suited to our needs.

“Perfection Execution of Holiday Inn Express” If you want to go to a hotel that does everything right for what the chain is trying to be, this is the hallmark of Holiday Inn Express hotels. Rate was reasonable. Rooms were large and comfortable. Desk staff was knowledgeable. Breakfast was hot and plentiful and ready more than 30 minutes early. This hotel staff clearly understands what Holiday Inn Express intends to be and excutes across the board.
“Not bad” Clean place with friendly staff. I would only stay there again if it was the cheapest in chicago. My wife would prefer a little more luxurious. No hot tub. Sheets were very soft & comfy.

“Great hotel in Boston” Stayed at Jury's Boston with my Mum in December 2008 and would definitely stay there again. Great location - an easy walk to Boston Common, Boylston Street and the Theatre District. In fact we walked everywhere easily. On one of the four days we were there, we walked from the hotel to the start of the Freedom Trail, had a good look around Quincy Market and Fanueil Hall, continued on the Freedom Trail to the end, then walked all the way back to the Prudential Centre for cocktails at sunset. It was a heavy day on the feet, but certainly manageable. The room was large and clean with lovely comfy beds, big soft feather pillows and crisp, white linen and warm comforters. Great furnishings all round really. We had a massive bathroom with separate shower and bath. They supplied lovely toiletries. The business centre had two PC's with free internet access and free wireless internet. The downstairs bar was nice and served lovely desserts, which on one night I took up to the room. Very lovely! The restaurant off the bar was expensive, but given it was absolutely freezing and blowing a gale one night we were there, we opted to eat in and chose lovely home-made soup and crusty bread. Try Bangkok Blue next to the Charlesmark Hotel on Boylston for cheap and cheery Thai and the Irish bar MJ O'Connors about a five minute walk from the hotel for good hearty pub grub. Also try a Boston Cream Puff at Mike's Pastry shop on Hanover Street. If you're there in December, I'd highly recommend a visit to the Boston Holiday Pops at Symphony Hall - very Christmassy! Really great hotel and good value booking through expedia.com.au. Would highly recommend.

“Lots of positives but a few negatives” We just returned from a two-night stay at this Comfort Inn in NYC. There are many positives about this hotel but a few negatives, too. First of all the location is great, the rooms are clean, the staff is friendly and the rates are good - BUT ... the hotel is incredibly noisy. We didn't spend a lot of time in our room, but when we did, we were hoping to get a good nights sleep after a full day in Manhattan. We were on the second floor just above the lobby, and on the first night we could hear people talking on the street below at 3 a.m. (for about an hour) just like they were in our room. The snow plow came by three times, we could hear the elevator going up and down, and the heater in our room clicking on and off made a ton of noise. On the second night, someone on our floor (who had a few too many) was moaning and yelling, the garbage truck parked right outside our window and loaded up for a good hour and that elevator and heater continued to make a lot of noise. We found the breakfast pretty brutal, too. Luke-warm coffee, boiled eggs that you found difficult to cut with a knife, dry croissants. If you stay here, be prepared for the noise. I don't know if requesting a room on a higher floor at the back of the hotel would help, but this is what I would do. We had a terrific time in NYC, but sleep would have been nice, too!

“Small room but great hip location” This is a hip place to stay...there always seems to be something going on. The night club can get really crazy and there is always some fun people watching. I have stayed here many times and it is nice. The best part is that you are centrally located but not stuck in the craziness of Times Square. And if you want to walk to Times Square you can be there in 5 minutes...not bad and then once you get to Times Square you will wish you were back at the Hudson. There is a great rooftop bar...drinks are pricey...my Martini was 20 bucks after a tip but it was good! The sunset was great from up there. The restaurant has amazing Mac and Cheese too. Now to save some money for dinner and drinks just walk around the corner and you will find a ton of places. We found some great Happy Hours too...$10 Martini's...buy one get one free! What! Now we are talking! On the bad side the rooms are small...but hey this is New York. What do you expect? And it is so dark too...after a week here you start to feel like a vampire living in a cave and you just want to know what you look like...but hey vampires are hip right now...so that could be a selling point for the hotel. I've flown in early and a room has always been available for me. I have been very lucky. Also, I've upgraded my room to a Queen for only $15 a night. Not a bad up charge if you ask me. Staff is super friendly and are always protecting me from the Europeans that stay here. It is really annoying but when you are at the front desk...the Europeans will walk right up and stand on your back while you are checking in or trying to pay your bill. The Hudson Staff always comes to my rescue by asking them, "Excuse me are you with this gentleman?" After they say, "No!" The staff will ask them to stand back and wait for an available staff member. And they call Americans Ugly when they travel! Ha!

“Very comfortable.” Room was clean and well appointed. Staff was attentive. Entry was awkward with too many levels and steps, but there are plenty of staff to help. While room was slightly cramped, it was very comfortable, had every amenity one might need, wireless access was instant. Spa treatments excellent. Room service prompt and tasty.

“A first class, service oriented hotel.” Excellent location near Union Square. Gracious staff at check in and a very "in the know" concierge that will recommend quality restaurants at a great price, not just the "hip" place to be seen at. Rooms are small but functional, bathrooms are elaborate and bath products are nice. Walls a little thin, but what else is new. Room service was prompt and food was warm, pricey of course. Very clean hotel with friendly staff. Taj Hotels has really relayed their hospitality culture into this hotel. Great job.

“Perfect Location.” Walk right out the back door and you are in SeaPort Village which has many quaint little shops and some great restaurants. Most rooms have a great view of both the beach and the downtown area. Great neighborhood. I felt comfortable walking alone. I love the location because it's on the beach, but close to the airport.

“Comfortable hotel at a good location” I stayed at the Back Bay for 4 nights. The hotel was very neat and the staff were very helpful. The rooms were a little small but I guess that's all the real estate space that you can get in downtown Boston. High speed internet was complimentary which was a good deals since many pricey hotels do not give you this comfort. the beds were very comfortable. The only little grouse I had was that this was probably the only hotel that I have stayed where they did not have a coffee maker. It really is scary to wake up and not have a cup of coffee ready. But I guess the nearby Dunkin Donuts make heavy wind of this loss. Overall the hotel stay was pleasant.

“Good for a business trip” I recently stayed at the Allerton Hotel while attending a meeting held on-site. My stay was short, only two nights, but the experience was positive. My first impressions, however, were not so positive as registration is on the second floor and I found very limited signage where I entered on the first floor to direct me up to the second. Also, the first floor lobby is quite small, one small room and a narrow hallway for the elevators (I later noticed that this lobby got quite crowded if a few groups of people entered at the same time). Once I got to the second floor, things got better (though the second floor lobby was also small). Check-in was quick and staff were friendly and polite. My corner room was small, about 10’ by 13’, with nice, up-to-date furnishings in good condition. I would have preferred a firmer mattress on my full-sized bed, but it wasn’t bad. The desk was narrow (some of us still use paper and like to spread our papers out!), and the chair not so comfortable. There was a flat-screen TV. Wi-fi worked well though it was slow (512K). The closet was tiny. I wasn’t disturbed by noise from the hallway or the street. The bathroom had a shower only. Water pressure in the shower was acceptable and there was plenty of hot water. Toiletries were very nice. There was a pedestal sink with just a small shelf nearby so not the best set-up for early morning grooming. The bathroom was very clean as was the room. The meeting rooms were fine and had working wi-fi. The chairs, however, were very uncomfortable especially for all day meetings! I had lunch in the hotel restaurant one day and thought it was fine. The hotel is located in a nice area with many restaurants nearby. It is also five (short) blocks from the CTA, which made travel between O’Hare and the hotel easy and inexpensive. I was busy with work during most of my stay and happy to be able to relax in my pleasant room in the evening. I would happily stay at the Allerton again.

“Great Value in Philly” Just got back from a 4 night stay at the Travelodge in Philadelphia. Great value hotel based on the price. Nice room. Clean and new with a nice working shower. Perfect for 2 people. Asked for extra pillows on our second night and they were there for the rest of our stay. Front desk was friendly and helpful. We were even able to check in 3 hours early on our arrival day - a big plus! Breakfast was just enough to get you off and started on your day (milk, juice, coffee, bagels, danish, fruit, and some days cereal). The Travelodge was in walking distance to the historic area and near public transportation (main reason we picked this hotel). Serveral days, we'd go out and then stop back for a break before heading out again. There was also a restaurant Penn View Inn right on the corner serving good and inexpensive dishes for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. We enjoyed our stay and if returning to Philly would pick the Travelodge again.

“A true find” We stayed 2 nights at the beginning of our California coast tour. The hotel is in a great location, nestled between Hollywood and Beverly hills. Walking distance to the Farmers market. We stayed in a suite and it was very spacious and especially super clean! The room was right beside the elevator, but we never heard a thing, it was a very quiet room. the breakfast is quite big and has a lot of choices. The room has a coffemaker, minibar, safe and a small balcony overlooking the courtyard. The bed was very comfortable and we got little chocolates every day. The best thing is the staff, whatever the request they go out of their way to accomodate you, with a big smile on their face.Thank you Michael and Michael and Paolo. We would return here anytime we are in L.A., it's truly a find and very reasonable rates, including free wireless and the breakfast.

“Cramped for 4 adults” My family (4 adults + a 1-year-old) stayed here for 3 nights the week between Christmas and New Year's Eve. I pushed for this hotel since I had stayed at (and loved) the adjoining Residence Inn a couple of years ago with friends and loved it...however, our room at Springhill Suites seemed a bit inferior and was cramped for us. The fact that this hotel had a sofa bed as well as the king size bed was a selling point for us, but the sofa bed wound up not being used - we unfolded it and discovered the mattress couldn't be more than 3-4 inches deep, and would definitely not be comfortable to sleep on, so we slept on the couch instead. Another issue we had with the room was that, despite having the air conditioning on and set at 68 in December, the room was still quite warm, mostly due to the fact that there was only one vent that we could find, and it was way over by the window, not allowing for adequate air flow. Breakfast was delicious, convenient and filling - if you got down there early enough to not have to spend a lot of time in line or trying to find a place to sit. The fact that there was an indoor swimming pool at this hotel was also a selling point, as it is hard to find downtown Chicago hotels with one, but when my family went to the pool to swim, they couldn't stay in the water longer than 10-20 minutes because it was so cold. The location of the hotel was excellent; there are 2 Starbucks within a block and a half radius of the hotel, several sit-down restaurants (including Harry Caray's and Rosebud Trattoria on the same street) and a few casual dining places nearby as well. The red line is a few blocks northeast and you can get on the purple and brown lines a couple of blocks west. The Magnificent Mile is not a far walk to the east, either. All in all, I would recommend this hotel for groups that wouldn't need the sofa bed - I would come back and stay by myself, for example, but I wouldn't stay here with my family again. Just much too crowded for more than two people.

“What we expected, and then some!” Check out the clerk's hair! Am I allowed to comment about that? It has to take a long time to prepare that look... Awesome! Animal print bathrobes, a comfy bed & walking distance from the best of Seattle! Pricey, but a great location & a ton of fun!

“My Favorite Airport Hotel” Walking distance from the connected airport, comfy beds and not a plane to be heard. The lobby and rooms are beautiful and service is good. Travel wouldn't be so bad, if all airport hotels were this great.

“Nice property, but had a noise issue” My wife and I stayed one night at the Renaissance Boston Waterfront. We were spending very little time in Boston, so I chose the location because of its proximity to Menton restaurant, where we had a dinner reservation. Several bars and restaurants are within walking distance. The hotel is close to the Boston convention center, and the area definitely has that kind of "feel" to it. Our room had a nice harbor view and was generally very good. We only had issues with the shower, which was awkward in that it was necessary to get inside in order to turn on the water, which means you'll get an initial blast of cold water. The shower also leaked through the door onto the bathroom floor. During the day, beginning at around 9am, was a repetitive loud banging noise. It seemed to come from outside, but I wasn't sure. I recommend checking with the hotel about noise issues if you intend to sleep in during your stay. Staff treated us well. My wife's recent Marriott Rewards status upgrade wasn't appearing in their system for some reason. The front desk did not give us a room upgrade, but provided us with club access and refunded our wireless internet charge, which should have been included anyways due to my wife's status. Breakfast in the club was only served until 9:30am, at least on weekdays. Our room was booked as an award stay, which made it a pretty good value for us. I saw what the regular rate was for our stay and would have considered it a poor value at around $500 per night.

“Great for business trips - very good for couples” I've reviewed this hotel previously as I stay at it frequently as a business traveler - I think it a great hotel for the business traveler if your business is in San Francisco's Financial District - see my previous review regarding this. This trip my wife and I used the hotel as our starting point for a driving trip up the Northern Califoria coast. We had a Balcony King room on the top floor with a Bay View. You couldn't ask for a better view and having the balcony to sit on, have a sip of wine and some cheeze and fruit from the HHonors lounge set a very romantic start to our trip. While we did not use any of the hotel's facilities, we found it an ideal location to use as a starting point for most of our sight seeing and evenings out. As I described in my experience as a business traveler, the staff here is first rate and the hotel is spotless. This is not the 4 Seasons or the Ritz - but it is a solid 3+ to 4- property with nice rooms (baths are a little on the small side) that is very good value for very expensive San Francisco. For the tourist it is right on the edge of China town, fifteen minute walk to South Beach, the Embarcadero and Ferry building, South of Market Restaurants and a quick cab or BART ride to Union Square.

“The only conventional motel near Castro Street.” I've been staying here for years, and they've made some major improvements in the last couple of years--better security, high speed internet, new paint, etc. It's a three story motel--straight out of 1960--on Market Street just above Sanchez. Two blocks to Castro Street. One block to a Muni Metro (Light Rail) station (Church Street), and the F-Market Streetcar goes right out front. But if you drive, they have free parking--a real bonus in this area. The rooms are comfortable, but nothing special. Each has a fridge and coffee maker (those awful one cup makers that make it hard to use your own coffee). Most rooms are not air-conditioned, but in San Francisco you rarely need air conditioning, and each room does have a fan for the unusual hot day. The staff is friendly, and some of the other guest can be entertaining too, but I've never felt unsafe here. It can be expensive (or sold out) on the popular weekends, such as Gay Pride, Folsom Street Fair, Castro Street Fair, or New Years, but at other times the rates are competitive with other San francisco motels.

“good stay” This hotel is in a great location close to lots of places to eat.The rooms are modren decor.Beds are comfortable and clean.The bathroom is small but clean.If traveling with older folks tub is quite high to get into.The front staff is not very friendly or helpful.Overall good value for the money.Pool is very small and cloudy looking did not venture to use it.

“Four star location, one star service” The palomar is an elegant hotel with a good central downtown location. The restaurant is rated highly by a number of gourment magazines and rooms are pleasant if on the small side. However the front desk staff have no interest in helping customers outside of routine check in and check out. Service is more akin to a 1 star hotel. I would rate the hotel 4 stars for location and 1 star for service

“Convenient Hotel to Major Attractions” I stayed at this hotel for a major conference. It sits downtown, across the highway from the San Diego Convention Center. I am usually not a fan of Marriott Hotels, but this particular location was well appointed. The hotel definitely had a boutique feel from the lobby to the modern rooms. The negatives to this hotel would be the lack of a pool and the restaurant which is overpriced. We received a pass to swim at the Marriott Towers nearby on the water, but it was a good 6+ block walk in a swimsuit and that pool was so packed with people you couldn't move. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant (only once), which was more than $10 for a danish and orange juice about the same quality as the 7-11 sells for $1.49. We never made it to the rooftop bar, but I understand that is quite popular during the evening. Fortunately the hotel sits at the beginning of the Gaslamp Quarter, so you can walk to many nearby restaurants that cost less and taste better than the hotel food. Probably the best reason to stay at this hotel is to see a San Diego Padres baseball game. Their beautiful new stadium sits right next to this hotel, so you can definitely walk over and enjoy all the beer you want before safely returning to your room. This hotel had valet parking, but we were also allowed to self-park at the garage directly across the street and had no problem with that. Easy to access, except maybe on a game day. Besides walking to the Gaslamp Quarter, you can also walk 4 or so blocks from this hotel to the convention center and a bit farther down the water to Seaport Village for more shopping. You wouldn't really need a car at this hotel to see several major downtown attractions, but it's good to have one for going out to Balboa Park, the zoo, Seaworld, Old Town, the beaches, etc. If you can get a good rate at this hotel, book it. Can't imagine anything more convenient.

“Great location - this is the place to stay” You are sure that you're in San Francisco when you stay at Tuscan Inn. The hotel is located near Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39, cable cars and just a walk from the view of Golden Gate Bridge. Lots of restaurants and shops (and tourists) near by. Be aware that valet parking is expensive (about 50 USD pr night). The breakfast at the restaurant at the hotel is also quite expensive and nothing speciel. We didn't try the restaurant at lunch or dinner. The rooms were clean, and the service was great. We would stay there again.
“Knickerbocker is a dump!” I am not sure what is the best hotel I have visited recently, but I am clear on the worst. The Knickerbocker is a dump! Whoever gave this 4 diamonds should be shot!

“Bowling Trip” We stayed here twice in 2 weeks-excellent front desk staff especially the lady with the accent & big smile-she went above & beyond-the rooms are clean & have the extra ammendities-bathroom is large with separate sink area to get ready-4 ladies stayed & we were pretty comfortable-location is close to airport and not far from shopping, airport, etc-pool & excercise room are efficient

“No glitz or glamour... but gets the job done.” Nothing fancy.. but good value in a good location. Very big hotel, so can be crowded with tour groups.. (I had a huge group of high school girls who didn't have a lot of experience traveling/using elevators, etc.. but wasn't super imposing... not a super nuisance, but not the kind of thing you necessarlly run into at smaller hotels.)

“Great location, wonderful staff” We arrived before the July 4 holiday weekend and check-in was a breeze. The ladies and gentlemen of the Ritz-Carlton are always extremely friendly and helpful. The room was on the club level (floor 12) which is the top floor of the hotel. We did see several guests use the elevator for club access, so I assume you can purchase the club level room without staying on the club floor. Room keys are required for access. The location is wonderful - extremely close to Boston Common and the Public Gardens. Easy access to the T and close to several Boston tour trolley stops. There are lots of restaurants within walking distance, as well as Chinatown and the Theater district. The room was average in size with a separate bathtub and marble shower. I like the added touch of a mirror in the shower, as well as full length mirrors in the closet doors. We were traveling with a baby and the hotel provided a crib with bumper pads and a clean sheet as well as a small baby kit with shampoo, lotion, etc, and baby safety items (outlet covers, etc). The view was a city view but overlooked a modern rooftop garden display. We have previously stayed on other RC club level floors and the service here is excellent, however, I did notice a few things. The Boston club level closes at 10 p.m. sharp and is locked at that time. Other clubs we have visited were a bit more lenient, allowing guests to gather in this space without RC attendants, some even leave beverages out for guests to enjoy. Also, while the club level offers complimentary alcoholic beverages, the selection is limited. When a travel companion asked for a popular after-dinner drink, the attendant said the ingredients were not available and I ended up purchasing the drink downstairs in the restaurant bar and bringing it up. The food presentations were impressive with gorgeous desserts, a great breakfast selection, and filling mid-day snacks. You could easily eat all three main meals in the club. The concierge and club level attendants were extremely helpful in making dinner reservations. There is a house car with limited hours of operation so do inquire about it during your stay. The hotel also offers tea service with their special "cupcake tea" for guests of all ages. The hotel has a relationship with the sports club next door, so you can use their gym facilities and spa if you wish. Club level includes free high-speed internet and other services such as daily paper, garment pressing, etc.

“A review from your long term business traveler” New. Clean. modern. The "suites" are very spacious and nicely appointed too. Hotel has a great workout room. Location is near a strip mall with several dining options close by. In general the area is in a nice suburban location in southern Jacksonville. But there were a couple of issues that could improve: The hotel's internet service was so slow most the time in the evenings it was unusable. I had to call their tech support each night to just get the service in the usable category. Their internet service is inadequate for the hotel's capacity including "casual browsing and email". Forget business use like VPN. The free breakfast is a nice touch. But it has room for quality improvement with the eggs and entrees. Lastly the front desk staff were very friendly and remembered my name -even before I had met some of them. "Jesse" was thoughtful to get me into a Honors upgrade room, but he could be a little less pretentious.

“Skip the Hawthorne Suites Here.......” Overview: Family member was having a procedure at the hospital and they had special rates here - think it was about $90 per night. GOOD: - Pretty close to the hospital. - In accordance with the suite concept, the rooms were pretty large with a full kitchen (looked out of the 80s), living room w/ TV, Couch, and Desk, and bedroom, bathroom. - Breakfast buffet was nice with pre-made omeletts, giant sausage patties, biscuits, gravy, oatmeal, etc. Nice! BAD: - Not a great part of town. We actually had some "working girls" in this hotel who had different men with them every morning at breakfast. Beer bottles, trash, etc was strewn about the perimeter of the property. - Not a clean and fresh room. The carpet had stains, the bathroom was small and old, the kitchen was old, and I found old medicine cups behind the drapes. Let's just say I didn't take off my socks and kept my suitcase off the ground. BOTTOM LINE: There are a lot of other hotels in the area, and even the hospital had rates for about $10 higher at other places. Next time, spend a little extra and get a LOT more.
“Great” Great hotel with top notch sevice. I liked the breakfast

“Not great” Rooms were OK but worn. Service OK. Location is good for the airport. I think the recent reviews sum it up. By the way, the polo teams were somewhat noisy during breakfast... By the way, the 200 characters rule is not helpful...

“Immaculate hotel in San Diego with Gorgeous Views” We stayed for two nights at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront in October, 2011. We had taken the Amtrak down from LA so that it would feel like a real getaway. The downtown Trolley took us from Santa Fe train depot to the "Gaslamp" stop, which was a short walk from the hotel. The hotel is very modern, with sleek lines and large, open spaces. The atmosphere is a little cold because of the modern style, but that is made up for by the warm customer service. At check-in, the lady at the front desk was friendly and professional. I had booked a Bay-City view King room, and I requested a room with more of a bay view, if one was available. She assigned us to Room 1602, which was on the very end of the hotel, overlooking San Diego Bay. What an amazing view! (See the picture I took from my window.) Our room was immaculately clean, and very comfortable. The bathroom had gorgeous lighting, and the water pressure in the shower was very strong (which is unusual for a hotel). I wanted to take that shower home with me! The room was very quiet, and I never heard any noise from the hallway. The pool area is nice, with a gorgeous view of the bay. A large container ship was unloading right outside of the hotel, but is was cool to watch. If I was trying to relax all day, the noise from the ship might have been a little annoying, but that is beyond the control of the hotel. I would have preferred a little more greenery by the pool area, but again, it was in keeping with the cool, modern architecture. We had drinks at the "Odysea" bar off of the lobby, which had a lovely view of the sunset at Happy Hour (discounted beer and well drinks). The service was again friendly and professional.
