Afterwards, we headed to the Gaslamp district for dinner, which is a short stroll from the hotel. I would be happy to stay at the Hilton Bayfront again.. There were no conventions in town, so we didn't have to contend with large crowds anywhere. This, and the wonderful San Diego weather, contributed to my 5-star rating.
“Great location......BUT.....” We would never stay here again. This place needs some TLC. how does it get four stars?

“so unique !” the staff is simply great, as soon as you arrive you feel at home. Rooms are clean, quiet and modern. Breakfast is ok, good quality. The batroom is a bit small, but still ok. Good to have a small fitness room. I can only recommand this place. And a big thank you to the team!

“For an in transit hotel: Reliable and pleasant” I needed an overnight in Los Angeles and was looking for convenience, affordability and good room. I got all three. Shuttle to the airport was convenient and quick. Restaurant was adequate (not a stellar breakfast), internet services were good quality. Hotel room was pleasant and clean. Noise from the hallways at 3 a.m. was unfortunate, but all in all, a good, reliable place to stay in transit if you're not looking for "an experience". My star rating is based on my expectations for an in-transit hotel.

“Another great stay at the James Hotel” This was our second stay at the James NYC (I have previously stayed at their Chicago hotel) and it was as welcoming and comfortable as I remember. The rooms are so comfortable in every sense - size, linen, bathroom etc. We were in a King Guestroom on the 11th floor. The room was immaculately cleaned every morning and turned down every evening. The cleaning staff do a great job. I must say the free wifi is great, it is a service that ALL hotels should offer for free but for some reason do not. We were welcomed with a box of macaroons which was sweet and yummy chocolates were left with every turn down. There is no attitude that comes with this stylish hotel which is one of the main reasons why we returned. They seem to have the combination right. Please do not change James Hotel. Stay grounded, stylish and cool in every way.

“Grande tradition hôtelière au sommet de Nob Hill” Au sommet de l'élégante Nob Hill est perché le majestueux InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco, accessible par les fameux cable cars, qui passent juste devant l'hôtel. Héritier de la grande tradition hôtelière (avec The Fairmont San Francisco, son voisin immédiat, ou le Palace Hotel / The Luxury Collection, plus en contrebas, à proximité du district financier), le vénérable Mark Hopkins offre aux voyageurs les plus exigeants un service d'exception et raffiné. Jouissant d'une situation privilégiée, l'hôtel est à immédiate proximité de Union Square, point central de la ville, de l'incroyable China Town, ville dans la ville, et à moins de 400 mètres du Financial District. Les chambres Executive sont de taille généreuse. Décorées de façon classique, elles disposent de tout l'équipement requis et sont très confortables. Les salles de bains sont également spacieuses et très soignées. Les chambres situées dans les étages supérieurs offrent une très belle vue sur la baie, nappée en matinée de la fameuse brume chère à Hitchcock. Le Club InterContinental, situé au rez-de-chaussée, est très spacieux et élégant : canapés de velours vert sombre, meubles anciens, bibliothèque, parquet. Il propose des hors-d’œuvre de belle qualité tout au long de la journée, ainsi que deux ordinateurs avec accès Internet, des journaux et même une série de jeux de société. Le personnel y est d'une rare courtoisie et gentillesse. Le fitness centre est de taille raisonnable, et dispose d'un équipement complet de dernière génération. Le petit déjeuner est servi au restaurant Top Of The Mark qui, comme son nom l'indique, se situe au sommet de l'hôtel, au seizième étage. Il offre ainsi une vue panoramique époustouflante sur la ville. Le petit déjeuner est parfait par la qualité et la diversité des produits proposés, le service très professionnel, et l'ambiance réellement très cosy. Un seul point noir : comme le vent souffle souvent très fort sur Nob Hill, la salle est réellement froide, même en plein été. Montez donc avec une petite laine pour profiter pleinement de l'endroit. La chaîne InterContinental propose des hôtels qui sont souvent de qualité, mais dont la plupart sont davantage des business hôtels de très bon standing que de véritables palaces. L'InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco est une heureuse exception : c'est une perle, qui mérite d'être visitée pour apprécier plus encore la très belle ville de San Francisco. Quelques conseils : - Ne manquez pas de visiter le magnifique SFMoMa Center, logé dans un batîment de l'architecte Mario Botta. Il sagit de l'un des meilleurs musées d'art moderne et contemporain au monde, avec une magnifique et très riche collection permanente. - A deux pas du SFMoMa Center se trouve South Park, petite place au charme européen où florissent les start-up high tech, les restaurants et les bars les plus en vue de la ville.

“Nice remodel” We stayed at the Parc 55 May 13-15 at the end of a trip to the Wine Country. Got the hotel for $86/night on Priceline and we were very happy with the accommodations for the price. The hotel went through a remodel that was finished about 6 weeks ago and it's very sleek and modern looking right now. Definitely a nice surprise, especially for the price we paid. Location is great; walking distance to several restaurants, Union Square and the cable car/BART stop. The only negative was that the bathroom was a little small. Other than that, great hotel, we'd definitely stay again!

“Great Low-Cost Accomodation” The Days is a nice affordable lodging option located on I-5 and Interurban. Based on what others have said, maybe it is an airport hotel although I would never know that being as that my approach led to no indication of an airport nearby. Despite it being right off of the interstate, the road noise is decently muffled due in part to the trees that line the property. The rooms are what you would expect of a Days Inn. Not too large, not too small. Not plush, but clean and functional. It's got a tv and fridge... I'm good to go. There is free internet and free breakfast in the office lobby. Within 15 minutes of any direction, you can easily come upon supermarkets, restaurants, shopping centers, and the ubiquitous coffee shacks that make Seattle well, Seattle. Southcenter mall is also not too far away. So if you come with Hyatt expectations, then yes you will be disappointed. But for what it is, you can't be wrong. I recommend this hotel.

“I'm having mixed feelings” This is my 2nd night of a 3-night stay for business. The office I'm working in is a 4-minute walk, so that's wonderful. The breakfast buffet is quite expensive, $16.25 for food that was simply mediocre. Dinner, on the other hand, wasn't overpriced. I had seafood linguini for $21. The only thing is, it wasn't fantastic by any stretch. One thing I'm very impressed with is the service and the attitude of the staff: absolutely wonderful! Right now it's 8:40 p.m. on a Wednesday night and in my 2nd floor room I have been hearing the sounds of a jazz band playing downstairs for the past couple of hours. I can even feel the bass through the floor. I'm hoping it ends soon. Definitely ask for a higher floor. The rooms are just OK. Fine, but nothing exciting. One cool thing is that there's a mini fridge in each room. Another great thing is there's free Internet in every room. The rooms definitely have a 1990s feel to them. No flat panel TVs, peeling wallpaper, an alarm clock that's completely uncomprehensible. One more thing: You can hear doors slamming at night. My recommendation is putting a bathroom towel under the door (there's a large gap).

“Hotel idéal pour une famille à Chicago” Nous avons séjourné 4 nuits dans cet hotel. Il est très bien situé, proche de Michigan avenue, du Loop et face à une station de métro. Navy Pier est accessible gratuitement par une navette. Les suites sont très spacieuses et très calmes, parfaitement adaptées à une famille (les lits queen sont un peu petit). Le petit-déjeuner est gratuit, ainsi qu'un diner light certains jours de la semaine, ce qui est très appréciable. La piscine offre une très belle vue sur la ville, mais elle est peu profonde. Le personnel est très accueillant. La cuisine est très spacieuse et très pratique. Elle permet de bonnes économies de restauration, même si de nombreux restaurants entourent l'hotel. Je recommande vivement pour une famille.
“great value very clean” Very nice and extremely clean, for the money it is a great value.

“Definitely a Winner” Great location, clean and comfortable rooms and friendly service. Breakfast area is spacious and food selection is very good. No complaints at all, just a very nice place to stay if you want to be in Center City.

“Brand New Marriott in San Diego, more like a full service!” I recently stayed at the Brand New Courtyard by Marriott in San Diego, this property is more like a full service Marriott than a courtyard. Except it does not offer Conceirge or any much marriott elite benefits. That said, this is a really nice Courtyard. It is in a good location and has above-average amenities (pool, restaurant, lobby) for this level of a property especially. Was able to get a rate for around 120 and for SD, that is cheap. The property is located minutes from the bay and equal distance from the Mission Valley, Seaworld and the Mountains. I am frequently in San Diego and hotels are always expensive for what you get, even the best of them, but this hotel met expectations. You can tell the staff is new, the refinement is not there yet and they are not as friendly as other properties in San Diego and they get flustered easy. Parking is onsite and they charge for it, which is odd for the type of property (but again it is San Diego). If you are in SD for biz or a quick weekend, this Brand New Marriott in San Diego, is less courtyard and more like a full service!

“No problems” The Garden Inn is a fewer frills brand for Hilton and that's exactly what I found. The location is good, not great, near the Reading Terminal and the Convention Center. It sits right next to Chinatown. Other reviews have complained about the neighborhood. The reality is that Philadelphia is a gritty big city, not some Disneyfied interpretation. As a result there are people around who are homeless, dirty, smelly and don't look like people fresh out of the suburbs. But I did a good bit of walking after dinner and never felt threatened or in danger. The hotel is a strange design, built on top of the large parking garage for the Convention Center. As a result you check in on the first floor but levels 2-6 don't exist. There is a decent restaurant on the 10th floor with preditable hotel restaurant quality and prices. There are huge windows that make you wish the city was prettier. Our conference group rate was $200 per night, which seemed high for what we got, but it seemed to be in keeping with the marketplace in Philly. Parking is $33 a day with no valet.

“Great location, good price” I stayed for two nights as a weekend away with my daughter. Room rate was $189. Total price with taxes was $215. That didn't include another $16/day for wireless internet access. I wasn't thrilled about paying that much for something that could just as easily be included in the room rate I was already paying. The room was nice - very typical of a Sheraton. It is a low building (3 storeys max?), so you're always near the ground, but we were on the 2nd floor and I don't remember any street noise. The location is only a couple easy blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39 - a couple more to the Alcatraz ferry. It is close enough to public transit to get just about anywhere. There is so much to do in SF, we could easily have been there a week. My only complaint was that the outdoor pool doesn't have a hot tub/whirlpool, which would have been nice in November. The staff were friendly and helpful (e.g., arranging airport transfer). I would stay there again, although I could be tempted by an equivalent property with a better pool set-up.

“Functional, but executive offerings were less than stellar” This hotel was not the nicest Hilton I've ever been to, but my overall experience was not negative. The staff was helpful, particularly the concierge who gave me directions to a nearby jogging path, and also a coupon for a free margarita at a nearby Mexican cantina. Very friendly people working there; couldn't have been nicer. Also true of the in-lobby Starbucks, which opened the very day I arrived. I was disappointed that, although I have Diamond VIP status, I was given a room on a regular floor and not an Executive room. The room was quite large although the view was nothing spectacular. I was given a key to the Executive Lounge, but travelers accustomed to HHonors amenities would not be impressed with this facility. It was a dark library-type room in which the breakfasts and snacks were sub-par. Also, evening drinks are no longer offered. Besides the disappointment with the Executive offerings, it wasn't a bad stay. I don't think the hotel is worth the asking price, and I would stay elsewhere on my next trip to Fort Worth, but nothing was so terrible that would have me telling people to run the other way.
“Good hotel for the area” This is a great hotel to stay at when in the Galleria area of Houston. It is not as pricey as some and is even fairly close to the medical district.

“Great location, good value for money.” I stayed here with my husband for 5 nights. Its not the Hilton - our room was a little on the shabby side. But the room was exceptionally clean and the bed was comfortable. And the location was just amazing - just a couple of blocks from Metro Center, about 20 minute walk from the Capitol/Supreme Court and the National Mall. For what we paid, and the prices of other hotels in Washington DC, the Harrington represents great value for money. We didn't have much interaction with the staff at the hotel, but on check in and check out they seemed pleasant enough. Plus, I'd emailed the hotel about a week before we arrived to ask whether or not I'd booked a room with a refrigerator or not, as I couldn't remember. They responded that I hadn't, but that they would put a refrigerator in our room for no extra charge, which I thought was very nice of them. The Harrington has two restaurants and a gift shop on site but we didn't eat/shop there at any time so I can't comment on these. Overall this place is great value for money.

“Nice stay, would stay again!” My husband and I stayed here for Valentine's Day this year. The first night we stayed in a Jr Suite which was very big. The decor was very modern which I liked! The bad thing about this night was that apparently the hotel had been robbed in the middle of the night and police officers went door to door banging on everyone's door in the middle of the night which scared us like crazy. It's was around 2-3am and being awoken by a banging on your door can really rattle you. I expected at least an apology from the front desk in the morning or something to say sorry for the awful night but no one even mentioned it, it was as if nothing happened. I know it wasn't their fault they were robbed but it did happen in their hotel so I just thought they'd want to assure their guest that this never has happened before and we're so sorry but didn't get anything out of them. The staff was nice enough but not at all what I would call warm and friendly. Did do a very good job at giving off a welcoming feeling. The second night we stay in an actual suite. It was a very nice room however it smelled like cigerette smoke badly (in this non smoking room). I called down to the front desk to let them know and was told house keeping would be up with an air purifier but they never came. We eventually left to start our day and didn't complain any further when we returned. The hotel itself is nice... I'd say a 3 star but with the staff I would take it down to maybe a 2-2.5 star. I would stay again if I need a room in the area but to plan another trip to stay the specifically, not going to happen!

“Likeable but did not meet my expectations” I suppose I expected more from this place. The location was okay, but when I arrived to the front desk, they mentioned that it would not be safe for us to walk alone (two young professional females one of whom was raised in VERY urban areas including NYC) in the neighborhood at night. I know DC isn't supposed to be a safe city, but I couldn't even walk to a restaurant unless in Union Station!! This was a bit frustrating, especially when I had paid $33 to park the car! From there we ordered delivery, and ran into the dilemma of where to pick from. That was easily solved by calling a variety of restaurants we had found in the phone book that we were "too far away" for delivery. I ended up going to the concierge desk to see where would deliver, very minimal (2) options. The room was beautifully decorated, but the toilet did not work. It took about 20 minutes to come and fix. Breakfast was supposed to be included in my room (I was told a full, warm breakfast) but I only got items from the "cold" side. Overall, I wouldn't return here because of the location issue. I like to go out a restaurant in the area to where I am staying. Furthermore, my room faced the fire house which luckily I didn't hear since I slept pretty heavy. This could be a problem for other people.

“Ausgezeichnet auf der ganzen Linie” Sensationelle Lage direkt neben dem Whitehouse und weiteren DC "Attraktionen". Mit ÖV gut erreichbar. Ein absoluter Höhepunkt ist die POV (Point of View) Bar/Terasse, falls man eine Sitzgelegenheit möchte/braucht empfiehlt sich allerdings eine Reservation - am Besten eine Woche im Voraus via [--] buchen, die POV ist ein echter Hotspot zu welchem man als Hotelgast zwar direkten Zugang hat, ein Platz ist jedoch nicht garantiert. Ansonsten ist das Hotel dem W Standard gerecht ausgestattet - Design, design, design.

“Loud but lovely location” I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights while conducting business at NYU. Clearly the location cannot be beat if you are visiting NYU or the West Village. The hotel sits right on the corners of Washington Square North and West and is 1 block from a subway and just a few blocks from several other subways. In addition to being right on NYU’s campus, there are numerous restaurants, bars, jazz clubs and interesting shops within walking distance. The hotel itself is somewhat charming with the themed artwork and old NYC charm. The rooms are very small, as to be expected in a downtown NYC hotel, but space is used well. The bathrooms had vintage black and white subway tile but modern amenities. The front desk staff was pleasant and seemed to remember each patron. My only challenge was that I experienced quite a bit of noise even after I told the front desk clear that I was a light sleeper and needed a low traffic area. My room was on the first floor and faced the street and full of the sounds of NY. As well, I could hear the sounds in the lobby and patrons passing my door on the way to breakfast. So if you are looking for old NY charm, with some noise and a great location- This may be the place for you.

“Absolutely fabulous!” We loved the room, the view, and everything about our stay (except perhaps the price : ) It made our mother's day stay with my young daughters perfect! There is a rotating restaurant on top. Again really cool, but quite pricey. this is a great location to stay and feel like you really are "doing" New York city. Within walking distance to the Rockefeller, American girl, etc. We loved our view facing south looking down at the downtown financial disctrict, particularly at night. We even had a glimpse of the river. It was so pretty, we left the drapes open all night to admire the view from our bed.
